definitions.definition: has

a var. an₁ pf. privative or negative; forms compound stantivistic nouns; (rare) before a verbal form, gives a sense of blame || gr. alpha, alpha nu; lat. in; ang. un; fr. a, an. apacasi you don't know how to cook. a forms adjectives (with vṛddhi of the theme) and patronymics.

áṃśa |act. aś₁| m. (that which is obtained) part, portion, share, division, share of inheritance | lit. division, volume of a work | myth. ved. np. d'amsa "Dispenser", radiant |āditya| minor personifying divine retribution — ifc. a little bit of, a zest of iic. — v. [11] pr. (amsayati) v. [11] pr. r. (amśayate) divide, distribute. amśīkr share. amśena avatr myth. ["partially descend"] is said of Vishnu incarnating a part of Himself on Earth as an avatar; cf. kalā.
amśavāda | vāda | m. phil. doctrine of the part and the whole.
aṃśahara | hara| amnf aṃśaharā who receives a share.
aṃśaka₁ [agt. aś₁] ifc. amnf aṃśikā which is part of (iic.).
aṃśaka₂ [aṃśaka] m. part | astr. degree of latitude or longitude | ["who must have his share"] heir (legal).
aṃśāṃśi [red. aṃśa] adv. part by part.
aṃśú m. ved. fiber, stems or juice of the soma plant; fiber, filament; thread | ray of light.
amśuka |ka| n. fabric, clothing.

amśumát [mat] amnf amśumatī radiant, shining — m. the Sun | myth. np. of King Aṃśumān "radiant", son of Asamañjā, father of Dilīpa₁; he discovered the ashes of the 60,000 sons of his grandfather Sagara, and obtained from Kapila that his grandson Bhagīratha could purify them by the descent of the Ganges on Earth.
amsa m. shoulder; shoulder blade | corner of a quadrilateral | arch. part (in calculation of proportions of the āyādi system) | of. aṃsau soc. the two corners of an altar | lat. umerus; all. amsa.
áṃsadaghná [daghna] amnf aṃsadaghnā who has (water) up to her shoulders.
aṃsalá [aṃsala] amnf aṃsalā muscular, strong; robust | tender (said of meat).
aṃsya [aṃsaya] amnf aṃsyā concerning the shoulder.
amhati [related to amhas] f. anxiety, anguish | gift, donation — f. amhatī present.
ámhas n. narrowness, suffocation; strangulation, asphyxiation | anxiety, anguish | phil. sin, Evil; cf. nirrti | gr. αψος; lat. angor; fr. angoisse; all. Angst.
aṃhīyas [compar. aṃhu] amnf amhīyasī narrower.
aṃhu [related to aṃhas] amnf narrow — n.
amhú [abl. amhós] ved. anxiety, distress.
amhubheda [bheda] amnf amhubhedī with a narrow slit — f. amhubhedī (woman) who has a narrow vagina.
amhri [related to anghri] m. foot; root of a tree.
amhripa [pa₁] m. tree ["that drinks through the root"].
aka [opp. ka₂] n. misfortune. akam adv. Wrong. °সক aka verse | form of agt. mr. with f. enikaa; cf. nvul.
akaca [priv. kaca] amnf akacā bald — m. myth. n.p. of Akaca, epith. of Ketu.
akatuka [priv. katuka] amnf akatukā not spicy | not impetuous, calm | not tired; tireless.
akaṭhora [neg. kaṭhora] amnf akaṭhorā soft, weak | immature.
ákathita [neg. kathita] amnf akathitā not mentioned, implied | gram. refers to the secondary object of a verb governing two accusatives.
ákanistha [neg. kanistha] amnf akanisthā who is not the youngest. akanişthatā [tā] f. seniority (the state of being the oldest).
ákanyā [opp. kanyā] f. woman who is no longer a virgin.

akampana [neg. kampana] amnf akam panā who does not tremble — m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the ogre [rākṣasa] akampana "Brave", son of Sumāli and the gandharvī Ketumatī₁; sole survivor of the 14000 ogres of Khara exterminated by Rāma, he left the Janasthāna to inform Rāvaṇa of the rout; he was killed by Hanuman, before whom he trembled.
ákampya [neg. kampya] amnf akampyā imperturbable, immovable.
akaruṇa [priv. karuṇā] amnf akaruṇā without pity; merciless.
akarunatva [tva] n. cruelty; lack of pity.
ákarṇa [priv. karṇa] amnf akarṇā without ears | deaf.
akarṇadhāra [priv. karṇadhāra] amnf akarņadhārā without a helmsman, without a pilot.
akartavya [neg. kartavya] amnf akar tavyā impossible.
ákartṛ [neg. kartṛ] amnf akartrī non-creator, non-author; inactive.
akartṛtva [tva] n. state of inaction.
ákarmaka [neg. karmaka] amnf akar mikā inactive | gram. (verb) intransitive; opp. sakar maka.

ákarman [priv. karman] amnf akarmaṇī inactive — opp. n. inactivity, inaction. সকলত্ন ákalanka [priv. kalanka] amnf akalankā immaculate; irreproachable | hist. np. of the Jain logician "the immaculate" Akalanka or Akalankadeva; he lived in the Deccan in the 8th century; he established The logical foundations of agnosticism [syādvāda] and opposed Kumārila and the Buddhists.
akalpita [opp. kalpita] amnf akalpitā not manufactured, not artificial | natural, authentic.
akalmaşa priv. kalmaşa amnf akalmaṣā spotless, immaculate; without stain — m. myth. np. of Akalmaşa "immaculate", 4th Manu.
akava |neg. kava| amnf akavā non-stingy (called marutas).
akavāri | ari | m. myth. | "whose enemies are powerful" | epith. of Indra.
akavitva [neg. kavitva| n. the state of not being a poet.
ákasmāt [neg. kasmāt] adv. without parent cause; all at once, suddenly; unexpectedly; accidentally, by chance; in vain.
akasmādāgantu [āgantu] m. fortuitous arrival, unexpected guest.
ákāṇḍa |priv. kāṇḍa| amnf akāṇḍā without trunk | unexpected, without reason. akāṇḍe adv. sudden, without reason; in a tense manner.

akāmá |priv. kāma| amnf akāmā without desire, indifferent; not enamored of, who does not take pleasure in | unintentional; reluctant | gram. qualifies the sandhi which elides a final 'r' before an initial 'r'.
akāra [(a)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'a'.
akārapraślesa [praślesa] m. gram. elision of an initial letter 'a', marked in writing by the avagraha.
akārānta [anta] amnf akārāntā gram. (word stem) ending in 'a'.

akāraņa [priv. kāraņa] amnf akāraņā without reason, without motive, without cause — n. absence of motive. akāraņam var. akāraņāt, akāraņe, akāraņena adv. without reason. akāraņamitrah disinterested friend. akāraņatva [tva] n. state of being without cause; absence of motivation.
akārya [neg. kārya] amnf akāryā which must not be done; bad, forbidden, prohibited — n. bad action.

akāla [priv. kāla₁] amnf akālā inop portun; at the wrong time; out of season — m. unfavorable weather, setback. akāle adv. at the wrong time; at the wrong moment; out of season | without delay. durjanairucyamānāni sasmitāni priyānyapi | akālakusumānīva bhayam samjanayanti hi || [Hit.] The words of the wicked, even accompanied by smiles and pleasantries, frighten you like flowers out of season.
akālahīnam [hīna] adv. without wasting time, immediately.
akālya [ya] amnf akālyā out of season.
akālakalita [neg. kālakalita] amnf akālakalitā not limited by time | phil. [Trika] qualifies the experience of the Supreme [Anuttara].
akālakṣepa [priv. kālakṣepa] m. absence of delay, promptness. akālaksepam adv. without delay, without loss of time.
akālakṣepārha [opp. kālakṣepārha] amnf akālaksepārhā which does not suffer from delay.
akiṃcana var. akiñcana [priv. kiṃcana] amnf akimcanā poor, indigent ["who has nothing"].
akiṃcit var. akiñcit [neg. kiṃcit] adv. nothing, none.
akimcijjña [jña] amnf akimcijjñā ignorant ["who knows nothing"].
akimcitkara [kara₁] amnf akimcitkarā powerless ["who does nothing"].
akiśora [priv. kiśora] amnf akiśorā not accompanied by her young. akiśorā dhenuh mare without her foal.
akīrti [opp. kīrti] f. shame, dishonor, disgrace, infamy.
akīrtikara [kara₁] amnf akīrtikarī dishonorable, degrading, shameful.
akuțila [neg. kuțila] amnf akuțilā straight, not curved.
akutra [opp. kutra] adv. nowhere.
akudhryāc |akutraac| amnf akudhricī who goes nowhere; lost — ind. var. akudhryāk without aim.
akupya |opp. kupya| n. precious metal, gold or silver.

Akula [priv. kula] amnf akulā vile, of bad family — m. myth. np. of Akula "outside the clan", epith. of Shiva — f. akulā myth. np. of akulā, epith. of Pārvatī | astr. said of the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th, 11th, and 13th days | tithi| of a half-moon.
akulaka [priv. kulaka] f. pitted akulakā (fruit).
akuśala [neg. kuśala] amnf akuśalā bad — n. evil.
akūpāra [priv. kūpāra] amnf akūpārā ved. Unlimited — m. the ocean | myth. np. of akūpāra, epith. of Vișnu "the Unlimited", incarnated as a cosmic tortoise supporting the world; cf. Kūrma.
ákṛta [neg. kṛta] amnf akṛtā non com mis, not done, not accomplished; uncreated | unprepared; incomplete; not ripe; uncooked.
ákṛtabuddhi | buddhi | amnf whose mind is uninformed.
ákrtabuddhitva |vat| n. ignorance.
Akṛtavraṇa [vraṇa] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the brah mane Akrtavrana, friend of Jāmadagnya.
akṛtārtha | artha | amnf akṛtārthā unsuccessful, which failed, which did not achieve its goal | not its goal.
akṛtāstra [neg. kṛtāstra] amnf akṛtāstrā not trained in the use of weapons.
akṛtya [neg. kṛtya] n. evil; that which is forbidden.
akṛtrima [neg. kṛtrima] amnf akṛtrimā not artificial; natural. akṛtrimalāvaṇyaṃ vapuḥ a naturally graceful body.
akrtvā [neg. krtvā] ind. not having done.
ákṛtsna [neg. kṛtsna] amnf akṛtsnā in complet. সক্ষ ákṛṣṭa [neg. kṛṣṭa] amnf akṛṣṭā uncultivated; which grows in the wild.
ákṛṣṭapacyá [neg. kṛṣṭapacya] amnf akṛṣṭapacyā (plant) adventitious, uncultivated | (soil) which produces without being plowed.
akeśa [priv. keśa] amnf akeśī Bald | myth. np. d'akeśa "the Bald", epith. of Ketu.

Akkā [telugu] f. [sg. voc. akka] mother (contemptuous) | elder sister | hist. np. of Akkā Mahādevī, 12th century śaiva mystic; she wrote 430 lessons [vācana] in telugu; she traveled and begged naked while preaching the love of Siva; she experienced mystical union with SivaMallikārjuna at Srīśaila.

aktá [pp. añj] amnf aktā anointed, made up; humide — n. oil, ointment. aktādhikaraņa [adhikaraņa] n. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] "Section on moisture", where it is debated whether the initial injunction aktāḥ śarkarā upadadhāti (we have the wet pebbles) prevails over the final declaration of praise tejo vai ghrtam (clarified butter is the Force itself).
aktú [aktau] m. pomade, makeup | light, ray, glow | end of night (just before dawn). aktubhis adv. of the night.
akná |pp. añc| amnf aknā bent, folded.
akrama [priv. krama] amnf akramā out of sequence; unexpected — m. disorder, confusion. akramam adv. without proceeding by degrees, simultaneously.
akramatā [tā] f. absence of sequence; disorder.
akravyād [neg. kravyād] amnf [“who does not consume flesh”] epith. of Agni | vegetarian.
akriya [priv. kriyā] amnf akriyā inactive |soc. who does not follow the rites; impious — opp. f. akriyā inactivity.
akriyamāṇa [neg. kriyamāṇa] amnf akriyamāṇā not being accomplished.

akrūra [neg. krūra] amnf akrūrā not wicked, gentle, kind — m. myth. np. of the Yādava prince akrūra "Benevolent", eldest son of Svaphalka and Nandinī₁; [Mah.] he commanded the army of the Yādavās; he is a sage among the descendants of Vṛṣṇi [vāṛṣṇeya]; he is the paternal uncle and friend of Kṛṣṇa; sent by Kamsa to invite Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma to the festival of Cāpapūjā in order to kill them, he understood the plot, warned Kṛṣṇa and advised him to kill Kaṃsa; with his friend Kṛtavarmā, he incited Śatadhanvā to assassinate Satrājit so that he would seize the magical jewel Syamantaka, before he entrusted it to them; they then went to do penance in Kāśī; akrūra returned to Dvārakā to end a famine, and Kṛṣṇa and Balabhadra decided that he would keep the jewel; his wife is Sutanu, his sons Devaka₁ and Upadevaka.

akrodha [priv. krodha] amnf akrodhā without anger — m. suppression of anger. সক্রিষ্ট aklista [neg. klista] amnf aklistā fresh, refreshed, rested; serene | impeccable | bed. natural, without artifice.
aklībatā [opp. klībatā] f. virility.
akledya [neg. kledya] amnf akledyā which should not be moistened.
akleśa [opp. kleśa] m. absence of difficulty. akleśāt adv. without difficulty.
√ মা aks [related to as₁] v. [1] pr. (aksati) pft. (ānaksa) aor. [5] (ākṣīt) ved. reach; cross, penetrate — v. [5] pr. (akṣṇoti) mutilate — pr. r. (akṣṇute) mark (not. cattle by the ear).

ákṣa |agt. akṣ| m. car axle, rotating object; chariot | astr. latitude | akṣá die (ivory cylinder with a square cross-section, rolled to choose a number from 4) | cube | | rudrākṣa | seed of bot. Elæocarpus sphæricus used in rosaries | bio. bot. Terminalia bellirica; cf. vibhītaka | myth. cf. akṣakumāra — f. akṣī ifc. one who has the eye (2nd century) | lat. axis; ang. axle; fr. axe.
ákṣakarṇa [karṇa] m. math. hypothenuse | astr. angle between the gnomon of a sundial and its shadow.
akṣakumāra | kumāra | m. myth. | Rām. | np. of the young rākṣasa akṣakumāra "Eye", younger son of Rāvaṇa and Mandodari; he was killed by Hanuman.
akṣakuśala | kuśala | amnf akṣakuśalā soc. skilled at the game of dice.
akṣadāya |dāya₁| m. the act of passing the dice to the next player.
akṣadevana | devana | n. the act of betting on dice.
akṣádyūta [dyūta] n. the act of betting in dice games.
akṣadrugdha [drugdha] amnf akṣadrugdhā |"hated by the dice"| unlucky at gambling.
áksadhur [dhur] f. axle bar.
akṣádhūrta | dhūrta | amnf akṣadhūrtā dice cheat.
akṣanaipuṇya |naipuṇya| n. skill at the game.
akṣapaṭala [paṭala] n. soc. ["dice shelter"] room located generally south of the royal palace, where account books were checked.
akṣápari [bet] adv. missed by one die.
akṣapāta [pāta] m. dice throwing.
akṣapātana [pātana] n. the act of throwing dice.
akṣapāda [pāda] m. hist. np. of the ancient philosopher akṣapāda Gautama, or Gotama₁, ancient logician, founder of the Nyāya doctrine, of controversial date.
akṣápriya [priya] amnf akṣapriyā | "beloved of dice" happy at games, lucky, given to games, gambler — m. myth. epith. of Shiva “given to dice”.
akṣámada [mada] m. passion for the game.
akṣámālā |mālā| f. rosary | myth. n.p. of Akṣamālā, avatar of Arundhatī.
akṣarakṣitṛ |rakṣitṛ| m. soc. | "guardian of the dice" | royal officer, in charge of the akṣapaṭala.
akṣaśauṇḍa |śauṇḍa| amnf akṣaśauṇḍā expert at dice games.
akṣáhṛdaya | hṛdaya | n. expertise in dice games.
akṣāvāpá [āvāpa] m. soc. ["who throws the dice"] director of the games room, important title in the king's entourage | ratnin |.
akṣaṇa |neg. kṣaṇa| amnf akṣaṇā inop portun — n. obstacle.
akṣata |neg. kṣata| amnf akṣatā unstruck, uninjured, unharmed; unbroken — m. pl. akṣatās unwinnowed grains (not. of barley or rice). akṣatāṃ ca samarpayāmi soc. I offer grains of rice.

akṣán [related to akṣa] n. eye | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the sense |buddhīndriya| of sight; its regent [niyantr] is Aditya; the associated perception [tanmātra] is the form [rūpa]; syn. cakṣus | var. ákṣi id. | du. akṣī the (2) eyes | ved. the Sun and the Moon — f. akṣī ifc. (woman) with the gaze (iic.) | lat. oculus; ang. eye; fr. œil.
akṣaṇvat |vat| amnf akṣaṇvatī ved. endowed with eyes.
akṣama |neg. kṣama| amnf akṣamā inca pable de (loc. inf. iic.); which is not suitable | envious, impatient — opp. f. akṣamā envy; impatience. tasyā vikāro vilambākṣamaḥ his illness suffers no delay.
akṣamavat [vat] amnf akṣamavatī impatient.
akṣaya [priv. kṣaya₂] amnf akṣayā imperishable, incorruptible, rot-proof inexhaustible, inexhaustible — m. astr. 20th year of the life cycle.
akṣayatā [tā] f. imperishability.

akṣayatṛtīyā [tṛtīyā] f. soc. 3rd day of the clear fortnight of the month vaiśākha; it is presumed to have been the first day of the satyayuga; it ensures the permanence of actions performed on this day; this festive day is popular for weddings and for buying gold; the birthday of Parasurāma is celebrated on it; on this day Kṛṣṇa multiplied rice with the akṣayapātra; it opens the mango season.
aksayatva [vat] n. imperishability.
akṣayapātra [pātra] n. myth. [Mah.] inexhaustible pot of rice, which Kṛṣṇa fills from a single grain of rice, so that he can feed all the visitors of the Pāndavās during their exile.
akṣayya [neg. kṣayya] amnf akṣayyā in destructible. akṣayyam ind. adr. wish for unalterable prosperity.

akṣára |neg. kṣara| amnf akṣarā imperishable, unalterable; eternal — n. sound; phoneme, syllable | letter, character | phon. the sacred syllable om | phil. [Vedānta] the imperishable, supreme creative principle — f. akṣarī ifc. (formula) in (iic.) syllables. etaj jyotir etad akṣaram etat satyam etad brahma phil. |Vedānta| behold the Fire, behold the Word, behold the Truth, behold Brahman.
akṣaracyutaka [cyutaka] n. game consisting of finding a missing syllable in a sentence.
akṣaradhāman [dhāman] n. mod. ["imperishable paradise"] temple of the sect of Svāminārāyaṇa, not. in Delhi or Gandhināgara in Gujarat.
akṣaranyāsa [nyāsa] m. writing.
akṣaramuṣṭikākathana [muṣṭikākathana] n. the art of speaking with one's fingers, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
akṣaravṛttā [vṛttā] f. Vedic metric, based on the alternation of long or short syllables; opp. mātrāvṛttā.
akṣarasamāmnāya [samāmnāya] m. gram. [Mahābhāṣya] sequence of phonemes in the śivasūtrāņi.
akṣarābhyāsa [abhyāsa] m. learning to write.
akṣarāvali [āvali] f. string of characters.
akṣānti [opp. kṣānti] f. impatience, in tolerance; irritability.
akṣāra [neg. kṣāra] amnf akṣārā non caustic, non bitter; non spicy.
akṣārālavaṇa [alavaṇa] amnf akṣārālavaṇā (food) neither spicy nor salty.
akṣārālavaṇāśin [āśin] amnf akṣāra alavaṇāśinī who abstains from eating spicy and salty food.
aksi cf. aksan.
áksigata [gata] amnf akṣigatā visible |horrible. akṣigato'ham tasya I am a horror in his eyes. akşipakşman | pakşman | n. cil.
áksibhruva [bhruva] n. the eyes and eyebrows.
ákṣita [neg. kṣita] amnf akṣitā in alterable — n. water.
ákṣiti [opp. kṣiti₂] f. unalterability. aksitisravah ved. imperishable glory.

ákṣīyamāṇa [neg. kṣīyamāṇa] amnf aksīyamānā inexhaustible, inexhaustible. yasya trī pūrņā madhunā padāny akṣīyamāṇā svadhayā madanti [RV.] (Viṣṇu) whose three steps, filled with inexhaustible honey, take pleasure in their free unfolding.
akṣudra [neg. kṣudra] amnf akṣudrā not small; large | not vile, not vulgar. aksudraksudhā Great hunger.

Akṣobhya [neg. kṣobhya] amnf akṣobhyā serene, unshakeable, imperturbable — m. bd. np. of Akṣobhya "the Unshakeable", jina guardian of the East in the Mahāyāna pantheon, represented in gen. as bhūmisparśamudrā; he is the bodhisattva of the Prajñāpāramitā — n. math. one hundred thousand billion.
aksobhyatīrtha [tīrtha] m. hist. np. of Akso bhyatīrtha (14th century), disciple of Anandatīrtha Madhva then pontiff of his order; Jayatīrtha was his disciple.
akṣauhiṇī [akṣaūhinī] f. complete army of 10 divisions [anīkinī] comprising 21870 elephants and chariots, 65610 cavalry and 109350 fan tassins.
akṣauhiṇīpati | pat | mr. general in chief.
akṣṇá [akṣsna] amnf akṣṇā oblique.
akṣṇayā [akṣṇayā] adv. ved. crookedly, diagonally; in a crooked manner | badly, wrongly.

akhaṇḍa [neg. khaṇḍa] amnf akhaṇḍā whole, undivided; global; integral; uninterrupted, continuous. akhandam adv. without interruption. akhandā dvādaśī 12th day of the clear fortnight of the month mārgaśīrṣa .
akhandajyotis [jyotis] n. soc. Uninterrupted fire in a temple.
akhaṇḍatā [tā] f. phil. indivision: continuity.
akhandatva [tva] n. phil. id.
akhandana [na] n. nondivision; act of leaving in thirds | phil. non-refutation.
akhandapakṣa [pakṣa] m. gram. [Bhartrhari] doctrine of the primacy of the sentence as a unit of meaning. eko 'navayavah śabdah gram. [Bhartrhari] the sentence is an indivisible symbol.
akhandapadasphota [padasphota] m. gram. synthetic understanding of the meaning of the word.
akhandabhārata [bhārata] n. Great India; eternal India.
akhaṇḍavākya [vākya] n. gram. indivisible sentence, continuous speech.
akhandavākyasphota [sphota] m. gram. Bhartrhari's linguistic theory, positing the indivisibility of the meaning of the sentence.
akhandopādhi [upādhi] m. phil. [Nyāya] global imposed property, not analyzable.
akhaṇḍala [opp. khaṇḍala] m. myth. epith. of Indra "the Indivisible". akhandalah sahasrāksah virūpāksas trilocanah In dra has a thousand eyes, Śiva has three eyes.
akhandita [neg. khandita] amnf akhanditā intact, whole | phil. unrefuted.
akharva [neg. kharva] amnf akharvā not mutilated, not shortened; important.
akhidra [priv. khidra] amnf akhidrā in tiresome.
akhila [priv. khila] amnf akhilā whole, integral, complete ["without gap"]; All. akhilena adv. entirely.
akhyāti [opp. khyāti] f. phil. [Trika] nes cience; syn. avidyā.
aga [aga₁] m. ["immobile"] mountain; tree arch. inaccessible part.
agaṇita [neg. gaṇita] amnf agaṇitā in numerous.
agaṇya [neg. gaṇya] amnf agaṇyā in numerous.
agata |neg. gata| amnf agatā not gone.
agatāsu [neg. gatāsu] amnf living.
agati [priv. gati] amnf arrested; impotent inaccessible.

agadá [priv. gada₂] amnf agadā [“not sick” | healthy, well — m. good health | remedy, medicine; not. antidote — v. [11] pr. (agadyati) to be in good health; to recover. cintāviṣaghno'gadaḥ remedy against anxiety.
agadatantra [tantra] n. med. the science of antidotes, a section of Ayurveda.
agadaveda [veda] m. medicine.
agamya [neg. gamya] amnf agamyā impenetrable, inaccessible — f. cf. agamyā.
agamyā [f. agamya] f. soc. woman with whom one should not have sexual relations.
agamyāgamana [gamana] n. incest.
agarīyas [neg. garīyas] amnf agarīyasī not esteemed; despised.

agásti [related to aga] m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Agasti or Agastya "who moves mountains"; born in a jug | kumbhayoni | from the mixed sperm of Mitra and Varuṇa spilled in the sight of the nymph Urvaśī, he is of small stature; he represents the devouring energy of the Sun; he digested the ogre [rākṣasa] Vātāpi, who disguised himself as a sacrificial goat to make those who ate it burst, and reduced to ashes his brother and accomplice Ilvala, whose riches he took; he then settled in a cave in this place, since named Vātāpi₁ (mod. Badāmi); He dried up the ocean by swallowing it in one gulp at Indra's request, to fight the asura Kāliya who was hiding there; the resulting drying up of the Earth was remedied by Bhagīratha, who brought down the Celestial Ganges to Earth; [SkP.] he went to Kailāsa to ask Shiva for holy water to consecrate a holy place [tīrtha]; Shiva gave him the water from Kāverī in his water pot; Agastya went south, and overcame many obstacles; the asura Krauñca blocked his path by transforming into a mountain and causing a storm; with a few drops of holy water, Agas tya cursed him with a mantra so that he would remain mountain until he received an arrow from Skanda; When he arrived at the Vindhya mountains, they, which Narada had made jealous of Mount Meru's supremacy and filled with pride, rose up to block his path; Agastya became a giant and flattened them; having reached the South, he was meditating on Mount Brahmagiri, when Ganesha, changed into a crow, landed at Indra's request on his water pot, and by tilting it, gave birth to Kaveri; it is said in the North that he conquered and civilized South India, where he introduced Brahmanism; in the Dravidian tradition, he is said to be first among the accomplished siddhas, and that he taught yoga in North India; he is reputed to be the author of Vedic hymns; He was an unsurpassed archer, and he gave his magic bow to Rama, whom he sheltered during his exile in his hermitage in the Pañcavațī forest; after Rama's victory over Ravana, he told him the epic of the vampire king and the story of Hanuman; Drhadasyu is his son by his wife Lopāmudrā; he is depicted as white and bearded, with a large belly, holding a water pot [kamandalu]; at his death, he was fixed in the southern sky as the very bright star Canopus (alpha of Carina), of which he is the astrological regent; it is said that polluted waters are purified at its rising | bio. bot. Sesbania grandiflora, tree with palmette-like compound leaves of 30 to 60 lobes, red or pink papilionaceous flowers, fruits in long pods of 15 to 50; used in medicine | var. Agastya myth. id. etāvad uktvā vacanam maitrāvarunir acyutah | samudram apibat kruddhah sarvalokasya paśyatah | [Mah.] Having said these words, the unwavering Agasti (son of Mitra and Varuna), in anger, drank the ocean in one gulp in the sight of the whole world.
agastiprokta [prokta] n. lit. np. of the agastiprokta "Promulgated by Agasti", treatise on gemmology |ratnaśāstra| of uncertain period, cited by Mal linātha₁.
agastimata [mata] n. bed. n.p. from the Agasti mata "Reflections of Agasti", gemmo treatise
logy [ratnaśāstra]; it forms a section of the Brhatsamhitā; it is later than the 6th century.
agastya cf. Agasti.
agastyatīrtha [tīrtha] n. geo. np. of the great agastyatīrtha basin at Vātāpi₁Badāmi.
agastyasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. [Tantra] np. of the agastyasamhitā, compendium of ritual, not. concerning initiation.
agādha [neg. gādha] amnf agādhā pro fond, where one does not have a foothold.
agādhatā [tā] f. depth.
agāra var. āgāra mn house, dwelling; abode.
aguṇa |priv. guṇa| amnf aguṇā without quality, without value, bad — m. bad quality, defect; demerit, fault.
aguṇajña [neg. guṇajña] amnf guṇajñā who does not recognize merit.

aguru [neg. guru] amnf agurvī light phon. light vowel — m. bio. bot. Aquilaria agallocha, Agar tree — n. soc. Agar tree wood or Tibetan incense, a psychoactive remedy used in Ayurvedic medicine; used in fumigation as a perfume. itarendhanajanmā yo dhūmah so'gurubhavo
dhūpaḥ [Aryāsaptaśatī] That which is only smoke when coming from another fuel is incense when coming from Agar.
agocara [priv. gocara] amnf agocarā which is not of the domain; which is not within reach, inaccessible.
agotra [priv. gotra] amnf agotrā phil. [MO.] which cannot be classified.
agopa [absence gopa] n. absence of herdsman.
agoṣpada [opp. goṣpada] n. pl. agoṣpodāni desert places.
agnā iic. agni.
agnāmarut [marut] m. of. agnāmarutau ved. agni and marut.
agnāviṣṇu |viṣṇu| mr. of. agnāviṣṇū myth. agni and Visnu.

agni m. Fire | myth. ved. np. of agni the Fire, an āngirasa god; he is said to be the son of his radiance Angirā or begotten by Brhaspati (or sometimes by his son Samyu); he is also called Tanūnapāt the Self-Begotten and Apānnapāt "born of the waters"; he has many aspects [āpryas] by which he can be invoked; he eats the offering to carry its fragrance to the gods, and as such is the intermediary between men and gods; the offering [Svāhā] is said to be his wife; he protects from darkness and guards the hearth; he is Atithi the Host; he is the
guardian [dikpāla] of the Southeast direction; his mount is the ram [meṣa]; he is Rohitaśva, who owns red horses [arusa]; it is said that he has 7

languages [saptajihva]; astr. he presides over the nakshatra of the Krttikās; phil. [Sāmkhya] he is the regent [niyantr] of the faculty of speech [vāc]; he is invoked by conciliatory prayers [āpryas]; cf. Atithi, Anala, Jātavedā, Dahana, Pāvaka, Bharata, Mātariśvā, Vasu, Vahni, Vaiśvānara, Soṣaṇa, Havyavah, Hu tabhuk, Hutāśana | phil. [āyurveda] the hot principle, opp. to the cold principle [soma] | math. symb. the number 3, symbolizing the 3 fires of the Vedic sacrifice. (gārhapatya, āhavanīya and dakṣiṇāgni) || Latin: ignis; French: agile, ignition. agnaya idam na mama This is for agni, not for me (recited by the patron of the sacrifice). agam nayati iti agnih [Nirukta] agni Is the one who carries the immobile.
agnikana [kana] m. spark.
agnikunda [kunda] n. pit to receive the Fire
sacred | agnihotra |. agnikșetra [kṣetra] n. soc. location of the Vedic Fire altar.
agnikṣetropadhāna [upadhāna] ved. n. preparation of the sacrificial space.
agnicayana [cayana] n. soc. stack of bricks for the Vedic Fire altar [uttaravedi]; it comprises 10800 bricks; it is a model of the cosmos soc. rite of construction of this altar.
agnicit [cit₃] amnf soc. who builds (by stacking bricks) the altar of the Vedic Fire.
agnija [ja] amnf agnijā born in the Fire; produced by the Fire — f. agnijā brown cow.
agnitva [tva] n. igneous quality.
agnídagdha |dagdha| amnf agnidagdhā burned by Fire.
agnidāha [dāha] m. burn.
agnídūta |dūta| amnf agnidūtā véd. who has agni as messenger.
agniparīkṣā [parīkṣā] f. soc. trial by Fire, ordeal by Fire | myth. |Rām.| not. ordeal of Sītā for having been approached by Rāvaṇa.
agnipurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. of the agnipurāṇa, mythical encyclopedic text, hybrid Vaishnava śaiva, in 383 chapters |adhyāya|.
agnímát |mat| amnf agnimatī possessing Fire; near Fire; in Fire | soc. that maintains a sacrificial Fire.
agnímantha | mantha | m. bio. | "Fire stick" | bot. Premna serratifolia, labiate, shrub with greenish flowers in malodorous umbels, abundantly used in medicine (roots and leaves); syn. ganikārikā.
agnímáya |maya| amnf agnimayī of the nature of Fire; ardent, blazing; burning, incandescent.

agnímitra [mitra] m. bed. n.p. of king Agnimitra "the friend of agni", son of Puṣyamitra Suṅga₁ whom he succeeded in 151 BC; he is the hero (from the time when he was viceroy of Vidiśā) of the drama Mālavikāgnimitra by Kālidāsa.
agnivamśa [vamśa] m. myth. ksatriya lineage of Fire, resulting from a Vedic sacrifice; cf. sūryavaṃśa, somavamáa.
agnivarṇa [varṇa] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā Agnivarņa "Color of Fire", son of Su darśana₂, father of Sīghraga.
agnivāyu |vāyu| mr. of. agnivāyū myth. agni and vāyu.
agnivelā [velā] f. ["hour of the Fire"] hour to rekindle the sacred Fire | afternoon.

agniveśa [veśa] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the hermit Agnivesa "Clothed in Fire"; Agasti taught him the art of arms, which he taught to Drona and Drupada; Atreya taught him the medical science [Ayurveda] which he had learned from his master Bharadvāja; Caraka claims to have received his teaching.
agniśakaṭī [śakaṭī] f. portable stove.
agniśaraṇa [śaraṇa] n. ved. place where the sacred Fire is maintained.

agniśikhā [śikhā] f. flame — m. Agniśikha lit. [KSS.] np. from the rākṣasa Agnisikha “Crowned with flames”, which ravaged the kingdom of Vīrabhuja in the form of a gigantic heron; Prince Srngabhuja struck it with his father's golden arrow and pursued it; it reached the city of Dhūmapura where it met the beautiful Rūpaśikhā, daughter of Agnisikha, who fell in love with it; the treacherous Agniśikha sent it to his brother Dhūmaśikha to have it killed, but it survived thanks to the magic of Rūpaśikhā, whom it married.
agnistut [stut] f. soc. hymn of praise to agni, sung on the first day of the Agnistoma rite.
agnistoma | stoma | mr. soc. the Agnistoma "praise to agni", a Vedic rite. of the soma.
agnisamvartaka |samvartaka| m. myth. clouds of Fire of the apocalypse.
agnisāt |sāt| ind. (deposited) to the Fire (with kṛ₁, bhū₁). agnisātkuru delivers it to the Fire.
agnistoka | stoka | m. a little bit of Fire.

agnihotra [hotra] n. Vedic. offering to agni (not. of fresh milk); it is performed morning and evening by the Brahmins | Soc. Perpetual sacred fire, preserved in the agnikuṇḍa; the initiated Brahmin must honor it three times a day after bathing and keep it perpetually lit.
agnihotrahavanī [havanī] f. ved. oblation spoon.
agnihotrin |in| amnf agnihotrinī who holds a sacrificial fire — m. [nom. agnihotrī] ved. priest practicing agnihotra.
agnīdh [idh] m. ved. priest in charge of stoking and maintaining the sacrificial fires; he is the first assistant of the adhvaryu.
agnīya [īya] amnf agnīyā concerning the Fire.
agnyādhāna [ādhāna] n. ved. establishment of the sacred Fire; syn. agnyādheya.
agnyādheya [ādheya] n. ved. installation of the sacred Fire.
agnī iic. agni.
agnīndra [Indra] m. du. agnīndrau ved. the agnīndrau couple of agni with Indra.
agnīvaruṇa [varuṇa] m. of. agnīvaruṇau véd. Agni and Varuna.
agnīṣoma [soma] m. du. agnīṣomau myth. the agnisoma couple, symbolizing the union of the opposites of Fire and water, and the ardent nature of soma.
agnīsomīya [īya] amnf agnīsomīyā ved. sacred to agni and to soma; qualifies an animal sacrifice on the 9th day of the agnicayana rite.

ágra n. point, summit, extremity | above or in front of something; front; surface; facade | purpose — f. agrā ifc. the best of (iic.). ágram opposite; before, in front of. ágrena opposite, in front of (acc.). ágre opposite, in front of; in the presence of g. | first, originally; before (abl.) | lit. below. agratás at the head; in front of something (g.); before oneself; in the presence of (g.) | at the beginning, first; before, in advance. agratah kr to put forward.
agraja |ja| amnf agrajā elder | "born in the first mier"] — m. elder brother (opp. anuja) — f. agrajā elder sister.
agrajanman | janman | m. firstborn | soc. brah mane (the brahmins having been created first, from the head of Purușa). agraņī |nī₂| amnf who takes the lead; first among the (iic.).
ágranāsikā | nāsikā | f. tip of the nose.
agrabhojana [bhojana] amnf agrabhojanā who presides over the meal.
agravat |vat| amnf agravatī which is at the summit met.
ágrasás |sas| adv. from the beginning.
ágrasara [sara] amnf agrasarā who takes the initiative, who puts himself forward.
ágrasūcī [sūcī] f. point of a needle.

ágrasena [senā] m. myth. np. of the sūryavaṃśin king Agrasena "Whose army is at the head"; he established his capital at Agroha (mod. ruins near Hisar in Hariyāṇa); he had 18 sons, and conducted 18 sacrifices [mahāyajña] to create 18 clans [gotra] of merchants, forming the rich agratahvamśa caste (mod. Agrawal); the legend of King Agrasena is recent, to give a mythical origin to the caste.
agrahāyaṇa [hāyana] mn ["best month of the year"] epith. of mārgaśīrṣa (November December).
agrahāra | hāra₁ | m. soc. donation of land or villages made by the king to a community of brahmans | village of brahmans, exempt from taxes.
agrāśana |aśaná₂| amnf agrāśanā who eats first; who eats before (abl.).
agraha [opp. graha] m. phil. non-apprehension, non-perception.
agrāhya [neg. grāhya] amnf agrāhyā phil. that which cannot be perceived.
agrima [agra] amnf agrimā which precedes, which is at the head | which is found lower (work) | elder; principal — f. agrimā bio. anone, fruit of the bot. Annona reticulata.
ágru m. single — f. agrū virgin.
agre [loc. agra] ind. before; in front, at the head; first; at the edge of.
aggregate |ga₁| amnf agregā véd. who walks in the lead.
agrevana [vana] n. ["in front of the woods"] at the edge of the forest.
agryá [agraya] amnf agryā who is in the lead, the best; eminent.

aghá amnf aghā bad, impure; evil-watchful; fallen (from his caste) — n. impurity, fault; sin, evil; punishment, suffering — m. myth. [BhP.] np. of the demon | asura | Agha, defeated by Kṛṣṇa in child — v. [11] pr. (aghāyáti) to do harm; to threaten, to have bad intentions; to sin | lat. ango; all. Angst; fr. angoisse. bhuñjate te tvagham pāpā ye pacantyātmakāranāt [BhG.] They eat only filth, the sinners who cook only for themselves.
aghamarṣaṇa [marṣaṇa] n. soc. rite of absolution of sins, performed by exhaling through the nostrils over a container of water.
aghaṭatva [neg. ghaṭatva] n. lack of pot quality.
aghṛta [priv. ghṛta] amnf aghṛtā without butter.

Aghora [aghora] amnf aghorā very horrible — m. phil. [śaivasiddhānta] np. of Aghora, vi violent sage of SadāśivaBhairava, turned towards the South, associated with the world of knowledge [vidyā], with the element of fire and the color black.
aghoraghanta [ghantā] m. bed. [Mālatīmādhava] np. from kāpālika aghoraghanta; cf. Mālātī.
aghoraśiva [śiva] m. hist. n.p. by aghoraśiva ācārya, author of the Mrgendravrttidīpikā paddhati, manual of śaiva ritual (12th century).
aghorasādhanā [sādhanā] f. soc. path of realization through asceticism in the crematorium fields.
aghoracakṣus [neg. ghoracakṣus] amnf aghoracakṣuṣī who does not have the evil eye.
aghoṣa [priv. ghoṣa] amnf aghoṣā phon. voiceless (consonant); opp. ghosavat, ghosin.
ághnya [aghnya] amnf aghnyā that must not be killed — m. bull — f. aghnyā cow.

aṅká [act. añc] m. hook; curve; curve of the hips, flank, lap, breast; knee; neighborhood sign, mark; number, seal; act (of a play) | number (from 1 to 9) | math. symb. the number 9 | soc. marking ceremony, prelude to the minting of gold coins for the year — v. [11] pr. (ankayati) pp. (ankita) pfp. (ankya) to brand, to stamp | to seal, to stamp || lat. uncus. pituranke upaviśati he sits on his father's lap.
ankakarana [karana] n. branding with a hot iron.

ankapāta [pāta] m. count, enumeration | geo. np. of the ankapāta spring, at the āśrama of Sāndīpani near Ujjayinī; he had engraved there the first 100 numbers; it was there that his student Kṛṣṇa washed his slate.
ankabhrt [bhrt] amnf that fits in its lap.
ankayantra [yantra] n. phil. [Tantra] diagram bearing a magic square, often dedicated to a
planet | graha|.
ankana [act. anc] n. act of marking, sealing, stamping; writing, cipher — f. ankanī mod. pencil.
aṅkita [pp. aṅka] amnf aṅkitā marked; withered | printed. rāmanāmānkitam cedam paśya devi angulīyakam |Mah.| See, Queen, this ring marked with the name of Rāma.

ankura [ancura] m. bud; young shoot; offshoot | var. ankūra id. yathā bhūmistathā toyam yathā bījam tathā'nkuraḥ | yathā deśastathā bhāṣā yathā rājā tathā prajā | As the land, so the water; as the seed, so the bud; as the country, so the language; as the king, so the subjects. ańkurita |ita| amnf ańkuritā germinated, sprouted.

aṅkuśá [añcuśa] m. croc; not. croc used by the mahout to guide an elephant, and which can be used as a weapon | phil. it symbolizes the means of stimulation opposing the forces of inertia [tamas]. ańkuśadhāriṇam myth. bearing the croc as an emblem (said of Ganesha). ańkuśagraha [graha] m. ["croc-bearer"] nac. ańkuśamudrā [mudrā] f. soc. ritual gesture used as a blessing; the middle finger is extended vertically towards the ground, the other fingers are folded.

ankola m. bio. bot. Alangium hexapetalum, sage-leaved greuvier; plant of the forests of southern India, with alternate leaves, white flowers in fascicles, blue berries; used in medicine | var. ankolla id. ańkolaka [ka] m. id. সহ্বা aṅkya [pfp. [1] aṅka] amnf aṅkyā to mark; to stigmatize.
ankha [vn. anka] v. [11] pr. (ankháyati) pf. (bet) to hook, to spear.
√ ang v. [1] pr. (angati) to go, to move — ca. (angayati) to mark.

ánga₁ [agt. ang] n. limb; part of the body; the whole body; the person, the form part, portion, subdivision; annex | phil. one of the 6 subsidiary disciplines of the Veda; cf. vedānga math. (by ext.) symb. the number 6 | phil. one of the 5 subdivisions of evocation [mantra]; we distinguish: the means of initialization [karmaṇāmārambhopāya], the provisioning of men and materials [puruṣadravyasampat], the distribution of space and time [deśakālavibhāga], the reaction to disaster [vipattipratīkāra] and the

success [kāryasiddhi] | phil. one of the 8 practices of rājayoga; cf. astāngayoga | jn. one of the 12 chapters of the Jain canon: ācārānga monastic discipline, sūtrakṛtāṅga refutation of heretical arguments, sthānānga the set of 10 doctrinal subjects, samavāyānga the development of these, vyākhyāprajñapti legends and dialogues concerning dogma, nyāyadharmakathā series of apologues and various sermons, upāsakadaśā biographies of lay disciples, antakṛddaśā biographies of saints, anuttaropapātikadaśā lives of perfect celestial beings, praśnavyākaraņa questions on virtues and faults, vipākaśruta consequences of good and bad deeds, and dṛṣṭivāda collection of different doctrines | gram. root, theme (strong), inflectional base (uninflected form) | mus. subdivision of a rhythm [tala]; there are 3: light [laghu] (one strike of the instrument and a counting with the fingers), accompanied [druta] (one strike and a wave) and short [anudruta] (one strike) — m. geo. np. of Anga₁, region of southern Bihāra, vassal of Magadha; its capital was Campā | pl. aigās geo. Bengal; its inhabitants, the Angas | myth. np. of the king Anga₁ of Bengal, son of Dīrghatamā and Sudeṣṇā — ifc. annex of, part of (iic.) | gram. auxiliary to; caused by (cf. antaranga, bahiranga) — amnf angā subdivided | contiguous — f. angī ifc. (woman) whose members are (iic.). angīkr to give one's share, to concede; to consent, to put.
ángaja [ja] amnf angajā born of the body; ornamental | soc. produced by an additional ceremony — m. son | myth. np. of Angaja, epith. of Kāma — n. blood — f. angajā daughter.

ángada |da| n. bracelet worn on the arm — m. lit. |Rām.| np. of the princely monkey Angada, son of King Vālī and Tārā₂; upon the death of his father, he was declared heir to the throne conquered by Sugrīva; he fought Rāvaṇa alongside Rāma, and served as a mount for Lakşmana to cross the ocean.
angadesa | desa | m. geo. Bengal.
anganyāsa [nyāsa] m. soc. [Tantra] transfer of the power of a mantra onto the body by ritual gesture.
angabhū | bhū₁ | amnf born (of the body or spirit) of (iic.) | son.
angarāga | rāga | m. soc. application of cosmetics on the body after bathing; not. designs painted on the chest of women with sandalwood paste and saffron.
angavikāra [vikāra] m. infirmity.

angavidyā [vidyā] f. one of the 64 arts; syn. kalā not. palmistry | bed. n.p. from the angavijjā, a Jain text for divining personality traits through behavior, compiled in the 4th century pkt. angavijjā.
angaśikhara | śikhara | mn arch. reduction of pa villon in a pyramidal roof; syn. uruśrnga.
angasukha | sukha | n. pleasure of the body.
angahāra | hāra₁ | mr. gesticulation; mime.
angahīna [hīna] amnf angahīnā mutilated, without limbs | incorporeal — m. myth. epith. of Kāma the "incorporeal".
angāngi | red. | adv. member to member; mutually; reciprocally.

angāngibhāva | bhava | m. mutual relation; correlation. সঙ্গ anga₂ part. affirms, confirms, or expresses desire or impatience; good, agreed; certainly, truly; please; quickly | just; only. kim anga how much better, really. te'nga them alone. so'nga him alone. yad anga just when.
angana [act. ang] n. action of walking | cour ["place where one walks"] | angana cour, area — f.

aiganā ["who has a beautiful form"] woman; wife. prāyeṇaite ramaṇaviraheṣvaṅganānām vinodāḥ [MD.] These are, often, the games of a beautiful woman away from her lover. kulānganā hi caramam śāyinyah prathamam prabodhinyaś ca bhavanti Mothers of families are the last to go to bed and the first to get up.
angam [acc. anga₁] iic.
angamejayá |ejaya| m. that makes the limbs tremble with fear.
aṅgāra m. charcoal, coal; good burning char, ember | ang. coal.

angāraka |ka| m. myth. np. of influence [graha] Aṅgāraka “(of the color of) burning coal”, regent of the planet Mars; cf. Kuja, Bhūmija, Mangala | lit. [KSS.] np. of the daitya angāraka₁; he caused disorder in Ujjayinī; King Candamahāsena killed him, having learned his weak point in the left hand; then he married his daughter Aṅgāravatī, following the prophecy of Caṇḍī; in her honor, he instituted the water festival. angāraparņa [parṇa] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the king

centaur [gandharva] Aṅgāraparṇa "with wings of embers"; he possessed the science of extralucid vision [cākṣuṣī]; he taught it to Arjuna who had defeated him in battle; in return he obtained the weapon āgneyāstra; cf. Citraratha.

angāravat [vat] amnf Angāravatī rich in embers — f. aigāravatī lit. [KSS.] np. of queen Aṅgāravatī "Ardente", daughter of daitya Aṅgāraka₁, wife of king Candamahāsena, mother of princess Vāsavadattā₂.
aṅgāri [f. aṅgāra] f. portable earthen hearth.

aṅgārika [aṅgāraika] amnf aṅgārikā who makes burn — m. charcoal burner — f. aigārikā sugar cane stalk (for burning). mālākāropamo rājan bhava māngārikopamaḥ [Mah.] O king, be the best weaver of garlands, and not the best kindler of pyres (advice from Bhīşma to Yudhişthira).
aṅgāritá [aṅgāraita] amnf aṅgāritā grilled, roasted | burned — f. angāritā cf. angāri.
angin [anga₁in] amnf anginī having members; subdivided, principal | bodily.
aṅgir m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Aṅgī; he received the sacred knowledge [brahmavidyā] from Atharvā and trans it to Satyavāha, who taught it to Angirā.

áṅgiras [related to agni] m. [nom. aṅgirās] myth. ved. np. of the progenitor [prajāpati] Angirā "the Sparkling One", manifestation of agni as the power of illumination, symbolized by the light of lightning; born from the mouth of Brahmā, he married Sraddhā, Devotion personified, from whom he begot Utathya, Brhaspati and Samvarta; Vayasya, Sānti₁, Ghora, Virūpa, and Sudhanvā are also sometimes mentioned; he is sometimes confused with Atharvā, or said to be his disciple; qqf. it is an epithet of Bṛhaspati; [Mah.] as he illuminated the sky, men turned away from agni, who hid himself in the forest; Without fire, the world was desolate, and Angirā came to pray to Agni to take his place, acknowledging that he himself was only his eldest son; |VP.| by a wife Smrti he had 4 daughters, including Anumati pl. angirasas myth. the singers, a class of sages | rṣi|; begotten by Aṅgirā, they are associated with the songs of the Atharvaveda; cf. Kapi, Gautama, Bhāradvāja, Virūpa; with Bṛhaspati at their head, they helped Indra release the waters; cf. vala | soc. by extension, Brahmanical clan bearing this name of gotra.
angirasvat |vat| adv. ved. in the manner of Angirā.
angī iic. anga₁.
angīkarana [karana] n. act of promising; concession.
angīkāra [kāra] m. promise.
angīkṛta [kṛta] amnf angīkṛtā promised.
angīkṛti [kṛti] f. promise, commitment.
anguri [related to anguli] f. finger; toe | var. angurī id.
angurīya |īya| mn ring. aṅgurīyaka | ka | n. ring.
angula [related to anguli] m. finger; thumb | unit of length, size the width of the thumb (approximately 19 mm).
aṅgúli var. aṅguri [aṅg] f. finger; toe; thumb, big toe | measurement of finger length var. angulī id.
angulitra [tra] n. finger protector (archery) | glove.

Angulimāla [mālā] m. bd. np. of Angulimāla "who wears a garland of fingers", son of the chaplain of King Prasenajit; at his birth omens foretold his destiny as a thief, and his father named him Ahimsaka to counter them; he made brilliant studies at Takṣaśilā, but was slandered by his fellow students, and his guru demanded as payment for his studies 1000 right hand fingers; he became a brigand, and wore as a garland the fingers of his victims; in the year 999, Buddha appeared to him, performed a miracle, and recruited him as a monk; the king pardoned him, and he found liberation, but continued to suffer the fruits of his actions |karman| by being beaten by the crowd.
angúlisanga [sanga] m. finger contact — amnf anguliṣangā that sticks to the fingers.
angúlisamdesa |samdesa| m. the act of snapping one's fingers as a signal.
angúlisphotana |sphotana| n. finger snap.
angulī iic. anguli.
angulīya [īya] mn ring.
angulīyaka |ka| n. ring.
angulīvesta [vesta] m. glove. সঙ্গুষ্ট aṅguṣṭha [aṅgulistha] m. thumb; big toe.
angusthamātra [mātra] amnf angusthamātrī the size of a thumb | lit. [KU.] se made of the self per
sonnel | puruṣa |, which resides in the heart. সিফ্লি áṅghri m. foot; foot of a seat; root of a tree. sahasrorvanghribāhvakṣa amn which has a thousand thighs and feet and hands and eyes.
ac [añc] ifc. after (anu, apa, arva, ava, ut, tiras, dadhi, ni, parā, pra, prati, visu, sadhri, sam, sarva) amnf acī turned towards, directed towards (iic.).
ac₁ nota. phon. [pratyāhāra] list of vowels. aci loc. gram. before a vowel.
acakita [neg. cakita] amnf acakitā firm, assured (not. walk).
acakṣuḥśrotra [priv. cakṣuḥśrotra] amnf acakṣuḥśrotrā phil. [MO.] who does not perceive — n. phil. the ineffable, which is not perceptible by sight or hearing.
acakṣus |priv. cakṣus| amnf without eyes, blind.
acatura |priv. catura| amnf acaturā deprived of four.
acara [neg. cara] amnf acarī immobile — m. plant.
acala [neg. cala] amnf acalā immobile, immutable; stable, unshakeable; imperishable; per manent — m. mountain | bd. np. du vidyārāja acala "Unshakeable king of light".
acit [priv. cit₂] amnf ignorant; senseless; stupid.
acitti [opp. citti] f. stupidity.
acintya [neg. cintya] amnf acintyā inconceivable, unimaginable; unthinkable; incomprehensible.
acintyatva [tva] n. phil. inconceivableity.
acira [neg. cira] amnf acirā brief. aciram acc. adv. in a moment, in a short time, before soon, shortly | recently; recently. acirāt abl. adv. id. acirena i. adv. id.
acetana [neg. cetana] amnf acetanī in conscious, insensible, inanimate; opp. sacetana. cetanācetanesu in animate or inanimate beings.
acetas [priv. cetas] amnf unconscious; insensitive; deprived of understanding. স ভ্য accha₁ amnf acchā bright, clear; trans parent, pure — m. crystal.
acchabhalla | bhala | mr. organic. zoo. bear.

acchoda [uda] amnf Acchodā with clear waters — n. |acchodasarovara| geo. np. of the lake Ac choda "with crystal waters", located in the Himālaya, formed by the river Acchodā (mod. Acchāvat in Kaśmīra); it is celebrated in the Kādambarī — f. Acchodā geo. np. of the river Acchodā in the Himālaya.
accha₁ cf. acchā.

ácchā adv. ved. towards acc. loc. (with vb. movement) — ind. cl. accha₁ id. acchā_i var. acchāgam var. acchācar var. acchānaś₁ to reach, to go towards. acchā dru var. acchādhanv to run towards. acchā nī to lead towards. acchā vac to invite.
achāvāká [vāka] m. soc. the "inviter", seated priest of the hotr in the Vedic sacrifice.
acchedya [neg. chedya] amnf acchedyā impossible to cut; indivisible.

Acyuta₁ [neg. cyuta] amnf acyutā firm, unshakeable; constant, imperishable; that which cannot fall | math. infinite | myth. np. of Acyuta₁ "the imperishable", epith. of KṛṣṇaViṣṇu as supreme principle | hist. np. of Acyuta₁ Piṣāroṭi, grammarian and astronomer, guru of Nārāyaṇa₃ Bhatta (17th century).

Acyutadeva [deva] m. hist. np. of Acyutadeva Rāya, emperor of Vijayanagara (1529–1542); he succeeded his brother Kṛṣṇadeva Rāya; his son Venkața succeeded him, only to be immediately assassinated by his maternal uncle the tyrant Salakarāyu Tirumala; then his nephew Sadāśiva₁ ascended the throne.
acyutapreksa [preksā] m. hist. n.p. of Acyutapreksa "of the Fixed Gaze", master [guru] of Madhva; the latter to deny converts him to dualism | dvaita |.
√ aj v. [1] pr. (ajati) pr. r. (ajate) pf. (ut, sat) ved. lead, push, lead gr. ; lat. ago.

Aja₁ [agt. aj] m. leader, chief | myth. [Ragh.] np. of Aja "Guide", son of Raghu, (or [Rām.] of Nābhāga); one day in the forest he was attacked by a wild elephant; he struck it with an arrow, and it revealed itself as the gandharva Priyamvada cursed by Matanga; he married Indumatī who bore him Dasaratha | myth. np. of Aja₁, son of Jahnu, also called Sindhudvīpa₁; Balākāśva is his son | myth. epith. of Indra, of Rudra, of Agni | animal leading a flock | goat — f. cf. ajā lat. agnus; fr. lamb. ajāvayas the goats and the sheep.
Aja₂ |neg. ja| amnf ajā unborn; uncreated that exists from all eternity — m. time | myth. epith. of Shiva, Vishnu, Brahma or Kama — f. ajā ignorance | myth. np. of ajā "Eternal", epith. of Maya.
ajakṣīra [kṣīra] n. goat's milk.
ajágará [gara] m. bio. ["that can swallow a goat" | python.
ajagarakāya [kāya] m. myth. "with the body of a ser pent", epith. from Nahuşa.

ajamīdha |mīdha| m. myth. np. of King Pau rava Ajamīdha "Ram", son of Brhatputra; Jahnu is his son by his wife Keśinī; he is the author of hymns of the RV. | myth. |Mah. | np. of King Ajamīḍha₁, son of Hastī; Ŗkṣa is his son.

ajaikapad [ekapad] m. myth. np. of Ajaikapād "One-legged guide", or Ekapād, one of the 11 divine breaths [marut], form of Shiva Bhairava; he personifies the sacrificial pole; he is often represented in ūrdhvalinga, with only one leg; astr. he presides over the nakṣatra Pūrvaproṣṭhapadās (of Pegasus) | var. ajaikapada id.

Ajagava var. Ajakava [Aja₂] m. myth. n.p. of Ajagava or Ajakava, arch of Siva [Saivacāpa] made by Viśvakarmā in order to destroy Tripura; after his unsuccessful fight against Vișnu, Siva gave him to his disciple Devarāta Janaka; later king Janakarāja inherited it, and at the svayamvara of his daughter Sītā, prince Rāma broke it; cf. Pināka.
ajada [neg. jada] amnf ajadā animated, sensitive | awake, reactive.
ajaná [priv. jana] amnf ajanā desert — m. insignificant person.
ajapa [priv. japa] amnf ajapā who does not pray | not pronounced — f. cf. ajapā.
ajapā [f. ajapa] f. soc. the mantra 'haṃsa' (ventilating in silence).
ajapājapa [japa] m. phil. breakdown of the hamsa mantra.
ajaya [neg. jaya] m. defeat — amnf ajayā undefeated; invincible — f. cf. ajayā.
ajayakośa [kośa] m. bed. n.p. from the ajayakośa, dictionary of homonyms due to Ajayapāla.
Ajayapāla [pāla] m. hist. np. of Ajayapāla, Bengali lexicographer of the 12th century, author of the glossary Nānārthasamgraha and of the dictionary of ho monymes ajayakośa.

ajayameru | meru | m. geo. np. of the city of Ajaya meru, mod. Ajmer in Rājasthāna; it was founded in the 7th century by King Ajayarāja Simha, of the dy nastie rājput Cāhuvāṇa; in 1193 it was conquered by Muhammad the Ghoride and attached to the Sultanate of Delhi; it was attached to Mewar in 1365, to Mārvār in 1532, and conquered by Akbar in 1559.
ajayā [f. Ajaya ] f. Indian hemp.
ajára [neg. jara] amnf ajarā that does not age; ageless; indestructible, unalterable.
ajarāmara | amara| amnf ajarāmarā ageless and immortal.
ajarāmaravat |vat| adv. as if ageless and immortal.
ajaryá [neg. jarya] amnf ajaryā imperishable, unalterable.
ájasra [neg. jasra] amnf ajasrā that does not cease, that does not die out; perpetual (not. fire). ajasram var. ajasrena perpetually, for all days.
ajahat |neg. jahat| amnf ajahatī without abandoning | gram. non-exclusive.
ajahatsvārtha [svārtha] amnf ajahatsvārthā which retains its original meaning — f. ajahatsvārthā gram. derivation | vrtti | of a compound which preserves the denotations of its constituents.
ajahallakṣaṇā [lakṣaṇa] f. gram. refers to an interpretation [vṛtti] of inclusive metonymy; opp. jahallakṣaṇā. kuntāḥ praviśanti (men armed with) spears enter.
ajā [f. aja₁] f. goat.
ajāpayas | payas | n. goat's milk.
ajāputra | putra | m. kid.
ájāta [neg. jāta] amnf ajātā unborn; not yet born | not yet developed. ájātaloma [loman] mf ajātalomā prepubescent.
ájātavyañjana [vyañjana] mf ajātavyañjanā im pubescent.
ájātavyavahāra [vyavahāra] m. minor of 15 years, still under guardianship.

ájātaśatru [śatru] amnf who has no enemy; peaceful — m. ved. [BU.] np. of Ajātaśatru₁ king of Kāśi; Drptabālāki Gārgya taught him brahman | myth. [Mah.] np. of Ajātaśatru₁ "whose enemy is yet to be born", epith. of Yudhisthira | hist. np. of the king of Magadha Ajātaśatru₁, son of Bimbisāra and a princess of Videha; first regent of Anga in Campā, he ascended the throne in Rājagṛha by assassinating his father in 491 ante; contemporary of the Buddha, he patronized Buddhism; He fought his maternal uncle Prasenajit to seize the region of Kāśī; he defended himself against the Licchavi clan by fortifying the village of Pāṭaligrāma, which he made his capital Pāṭaliputra; a great warrior, he is credited with the invention of the Scythian chariot; he subdued the Licchavi republics and established the regional supremacy of Magadha; he converted to Buddhism and founded numerous stupas and monasteries; he was assassinated by his son Udayibha in 459 BCE.
ajāti [opp. jāti] f. imposture; false — amnf gram. not denoting a species; not. adjective. ajātivāda phil. doctrine of cosmic illusion.
ajānat [neg. jānat] amnf ajānatī not knowing; ignorant.
ajāmi [neg. jāmi] amnf soc. non appa renté — n. incest.

Ajāmila [la] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of the Brahmin Ajāmila of Kānyakubja, who lived piously until his encounter with a drunken prostitute; he went astray by frequenting this prostitute whom he took as a servant, and forgot all his duties, stealing and cheating at cards; he had 10 sons, and named the youngest Nārāyaṇa, at the instigation of Nārada; he grew old, fell ill, and at the hour of his death saw the hideous assistants of Yama [yamadūta] come to take him; he called his young son, and at this sacred name the emissaries of Vișnu [vișnudūta] rushed to save him and take him to heaven, for the call of the Lord, even fortuitous, washes away all sins.
Ajita [neg. jita] amnf ajitā undefeated — m. myth. n.p. of Ajita "the Invincible", epith. from Vişnu.
ajitanātha [nātha] m. jn. np. d'ajitanātha "Invincible Master", 2nd mythical tīrthankara; his body is golden, his symbol is the elephant.
ajitapīda [pīdā] m. hist. n.p. of Ajitapīda, king of Kaśmīra from 838 to 850.
ajína [ajina] n. skin, not. of black antelope or goat.
ajinayajñopavīta [yajñopavīta] n. soc. sacred cord cut from a deerskin.
ajinaratna [ratna] n. lit. [DKC.] magic purse, invented by Apahāravarmā to explain the fruit of his plundering.

ajinavat [vat] amnf ajinavatī wearing the antelope skin — f. ajinavatī lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī ajinavatī, daughter of Dhanavatī who descended from heaven with her to present her to Na ravāhanadatta as his wife.
ajinavāsin [vāsin₂] amnf ajinavāsinī dressed in an antelope skin — m. ved. epith. of a patron of solemn sacrifice |dīkṣita|.
ajirá [ajira] amnf ajirā agile, swift — n. court; arena, place of combat, battlefield — v. [11] pr. r. (ajirāyate) to be swift; to run away || lat. agilis; fr. agile. ajiram quickly.

ajihma [neg. jihma] amnf ajihmā not curved, straight | honest. istam vānistam ādistam gurunā yattu gurvapi | tva rayā parayā kuryādbuddhyā samyagajihmayā 📗 [Prapañcasāra] What has been prescribed by the master, whether permitted or forbidden, must be executed immediately, completely, intelligently and with complete uprightness.

ajīgarta [priv. jīgarta] m. lit. [AB.] np. from the Brahman ajīgarta "who has nothing to swallow"; he had three sons, Śunaḥpuccha, Śunaḥśepa and Sunolāngūla; he sold Sunahsepa for 100 cows to King Hariścandra to serve as a substitute for his son Rohitāśva as a sacrifice to Varuna; for 100 more cows he tied him to the sacrificial post, and for another 100 cows he took the executioner's knife; ajīgarta is sometimes assimilated to Rcīka.
ajīrņa [neg. jīrņa] amnf ajīrņā undecomposed | med. undigested — n. med. indigested tion.
ajīva [neg. jīva] amnf ajīvā inanimate — n. jn. the category of inanimate substances [dravya₁]; opp. jīva.
ajjhala m. glowing coal, embers. সর ajña [neg. jña] amnf ajñā ignorant; stupid, stupid | unconscious ; devoid of conscience — m. fool.
ajñatā [tā] f. ignorance.
ájñāta [neg. jñāta] amnf ájñātā unknown; unexpected; incognito | ignorant || lat. ignotus; fr. ignorant. ajñātam adv. without knowing, in ignorance of.
ajñātakula | kula | amnf ajñātakulā whose family is unknown.
ajñātakulaśīla [śīla] amnf ajñātakulaśīlā whose family and character are unknown.
ajñātajñāpaka [jñāpaka] amnf ajñātajñāpakā researcher, discoverer, innovator.
ajñātavāsa [vāsa₁] m. incognito stay | myth. [Mah.] 13th year of exile of the Pāṇḍavās, where they lived incognito at the court of King Virāţa.
ajñāti [opp. jñāti] m. stranger, person without kinship ties || hi. ajnabī.
ajñātvā [neg. jñātvā] adv. without knowing.
ajñāna [priv. jñāna] n. ignorance | phil. ne science. ajñānāt var. ajñānatas adv. through ignorance.
ajñānadhvāntadīpikā [dhvāntadīpikā] f. bed. n.p. of the ajñānadhvāntadīpikā of Somanātha₂.

√ ষূ ancient v. [1] pr. (ancati) ps. (acy idea) pp. (añcita) pf. (ut, ni) v. [1] pr. (ácati) pp. (akná) pf. (ā) to bend, to bend — pr. r. (añcate) to bow, salute, honor — ca. (añcayati) ca. r. (añcayate) to unfold; produce gr. ; lat. uncus; eng. ankle; all. Enkel; fr. angle, anchor.
anca [act. anc] ifc. m. act of standing up; cf. romāñca.
ancana |act. anc| n. act of bending, of curving; inclination, flexion.
añcala [añcala] m. fringe of a garment (of a woman), of a scarf | wink.
añcita [pp. añc] amnf añcitā curved; curly (hair); erect | honored.

√স্থ añj v. [7] pr. (anakti) pp. (akta) abs. (aktvā, añjya) pf. (abhi, ā, vi, sam) to anoint, to coat; to adorn — pr. r. (ankte) to coat oneself, to anoint oneself with; to make up oneself — ps. (ajyate) to be made up, to be beautiful — ca. (añjayati) to anoint, to coat | lat. ungo; fr. oindre, ointment.

añjana [act. añj] n. ointment, eye drops, cosmetic — m. myth. np. of the celestial elephant añjana "made up", diggaja of the West — f. Añjanā myth. np. of the nymph [apsaras] Añjanā "eye drops", reincarnation of Puñjikasthalā changed into a monkey by the curse of a rși whom she had insulted; her husband was the monkey Kesarī; to have a son, she prayed to the god Wind |Pavana| whose seed she received in her ears, and thus gave birth to Hanuman.
añjanaśalākā [śalākā] f. jn. rite of painting the eyes of an idol [mūrti] for the purpose of consecrating it.
añjanābhyañjaná [abhyañjana] n. sg. (collective) makeup products.

añjalí [añj] m. two-handed posture [saṃyutamudrā] of greeting: open hands joined in homage, raised before the chest (equal), the forehead (guru), or above the head (god); cf. mastakāñjali |soc. ritual gesture [mudrā] of greeting (fingers separated, cupped palm animated by a vibratory movement) | soc. gesture of the two hands joined in a cup to offer an oblation. añjalim kṛ to greet in the añjali posture. prāñjali adv. in the añjali posture. añjalinā juhoti he offers the oblation with both hands joined in a cup. añjalinā sūryam upatiṣṭhate he honors the Sun with joined hands.
Añjalika |ka| mr. myth. |Mah.| n.p. of Añjalika, magic arrow with which Arjuna killed Karna.
áñjas [abstr. añj] n. ointment, salve — adv. quickly, instantly, immediately; suddenly | easily.
añjaḥsava |sava₁| m. rapid pressing (not. of soma).
añjasa [añjasa] amnf añjasā straight, direct; honest.
añjasā |i. añjas| adv. straight; with straightness; precisely, correctly; really, exactly | quickly; instantly; easily.
añjīra [Persian] n. organic. bot. Ficus oppositifolia; syn. kākodumbara.

√ aṭ v. [1] pr. (aṭati) pp. (aṭitá) pf. (pari) al to wander here and there, to roam; to set off on an adventure — intens. r. (aṭāṭyate) to wander endlessly — des. (aṭiṭiṣati) to desire to wander. mṛgayām aṭ to chase. bhikṣām aṭa pars to beg!
aṭana [act. aṭ] n. wandering; walk; journey — f. atanī notched end of a bow.
aṭavī [aṭ] f. forest; jungle, tribal area.
aṭṭa amnf aṭṭā high, elevated; strong, brilliant, excessive; noisy — m. observation tower | terrace mus. rhythmic cycle [tāla] comprising 2 laghu and 2 druta | [haṭṭa] market.
attaśūlā [śūlā] f. food sale.

attahāsa [hāsa] m. burst of laughter | myth. epith. of ŚivaBhairava "with thunderous laughter". attahāsabhinnah myth. broken by the burst of laughter of Bhairava. an nota. gram. primary suffix |krt₂| denoting activity (ifc.).
aṇaka amnf aṇakā insignificant; contemptible. anakabhāryā contemptible wife.
Aṇahila m. hist. np. of Aṇahila, minister of Vanarāja in the 8th century.

Anahilapāṭaka [pāṭaka] n. geo. np. of the city of Anahilapāṭaka, ancient capital of the Cāpa dynasty, founded in 746 by Vanarāja; it is named in honor of his minister and friend Anahila; after 974 it was the capital of the Solankī dynasty; it was sacked in 1024 by Mahmud of Ghazni; it was the capital of the Caulukya dynasty in the 12th century; mod. Paṭṭana or Pāṭana in Gujarāt.
anahilapura [pura] n. geo. np. of the city of anahilapura Paṭṭana; cf. aṇahilapāṭaka.
animan [anuman] m. tenuity; atom; smallness | phil. [yoga] the power to shrink, an astasiddhi. স্থাতিষ্ট aṇiṣṭha [super. aṇu] amnf aṇiṣṭhā extremely small.
aṇīyas [compar. aṇu] amnf aṇīyasī smaller.

áṇu amnf aṇvī fine, tenuous, minuscule; weak, insignificant; subtle — m. atom; infinitesimal unit of time or space | phil. [siddhānta] soul. aņubhāsya [bhāsya] n. lit. np. of the Aņubhāsya, commentary by Vallabhācārya on the Brahmasūtra.

anumātra [mātra] amnf anumātrī ["having the dimension of an atom"] minuscule. aņuvrata [vrata] n. pl. jn. the 5 minor vows of a Jain disciple: nonviolence [ahiṃsā], sincerity [satya], probity [asteya], chastity [brahmacarya], and
nonattachment | aparigraha |. aņuvratapañcaka jn. list of the 5 wishes of the jaina.

anuśakti [śakti] f. mod. atomic energy. স্তুত্ত anda mn egg | testicle | arch. dome. brahmāṇḍa phil. ["cosmic egg"] the universe. andam hiranmayam madhye samudram rudrasya vīryāt prathamam babhūva tasmin brahmaviṣṇū jāyete jātavedāh iti śrutau The golden embryo first appeared in the middle of the ocean, by the energy of Rudra; from it were born Brahmā and Viṣṇu; together they revealed the Vedas to the World.
andakosa [kosa] m. scrotum.
aṇḍaja [ja] amnf aṇḍajā born from an egg; oviparous — m. bird.
aṇḍadala [dala] m. eggshell.
at form of active ppr. (parasmaipada).
ata forme des a.
atattvavid [neg. tattvavid] amnf phil. who does not know the truth (i.e. the identity of ātman and brahman).
atathya [neg. tathya| amnf atathyā false; unreal; not really such.
atadartha [neg. tadartha] amnf tadarthā who does not deserve this. atadartham unjustly.

lect [manas]), karman the action (acted by the hand [hasta]), and nāman the name, (acted by the voice [vāc]).

átra₁ | ayamtra| adv. here | towards here | in this case; in this regard; on this point | in this place (loc.) | meanwhile; on this occasion, then. atraiva adv. right here. atra sarasi adv. in this pond. atra vastuni adv. in this matter. atrārthe adv. on the same subject. atra vişaye adv. in this regard. atrāntare adv. in the meantime.

átri [related to atti] m. myth. np. of the sage Atri "Devourer", son of the spirit of Brahmā [mānasaputra], patriarch [saptarṣi] and progenitor [prajāpati]; his wife is Anasūyā; doing harsh penances, tears came to his eyes, the radiance of which filled the universe and gave birth to Candra; he is associated with the star Megrez of the Great Bear; Anasūyā obtained that the trimūrti be reincarnated as his children Candra, Dattātreya and Durvāsā; cf. Ugraśravā; [RV.] he is father of Apālā; [Rām.] he is also said to be father of Bharadvāja. সেবেক্স atvákka [atvacka] amnf atvakkā without skin.
