atharva iic. atharvan.

atharvaveda [veda] m. the atharvaveda, the fourth veda, which comprises 731 hymns, distributed in 20 books; it consists of incantations, songs, magic charms and prayers; it is known by two recensions, called śaunaka and paippalāda; cf. angirasas.

atharvasiras [siras] n. lit. np. of the esoteric lesson [upanisad] Atharvasiras; it describes not. the observations of the doctrine pāśupata | pāśupatavrata | ; also called Atharvasikhā or Atharvasīrṣa; later versions exist, dedicated to the 5 gods of the pañcāyatana, not. the Gaṇapatyatharvaśīrṣa.
Atharvaśīrṣa [śīrṣa] n. bed. n.p. of the Atharvaśīrṣa; cf. Atharvasiras.

átharvan m. myth. np. of Atharvā, first progenitor | prajāpati | from the mind of Brahmā, priest founder of sacrifice in fire; he is also called Angirā | pl. Atharvāņas soc. family of Vedic brah manes, descendants of Atharvā, guardians of the atharvaveda | lit. the hymns of the atharvaveda.
primary athu, form of the s. of state.
ada [agt. ad₁] ifc. amnf adā who eats (iic.).
adaṃṣṭrin [neg. daṃṣṭrin] amnf adamstrinī (elephant) without tusks.
adaḥkṛtya |adaskṛtvā| ind. having done this.
adaka [agt. ad₂] ifc. amnf adikā who eats (iic.).
adakṣiṇa [neg. dakṣiṇa] amnf adakṣiṇā clumsy, awkward, awkward; bad | soc. who does not give the dakṣiṇā to the priest.
adakṣiṇatva [tva] n. clumsiness.
adatta | neg. datta | amnf adattā not given.
adambha |priv. dambha| amnf adambhā sincere.
adambhitva [opp. dambhitva] n. sincerity.

adarśana [priv. darśana] amnf adarśanā Invisible; latent — n. the state of not seeing; the state of neglecting or ignoring | non-appearance; absence, disappearance | gram. mutism. adarśanībhū to become Invisible.
adarśanīya |īya| amnf adarśanīyā Invisible — n. invisibility.
adás pn. start. n. |sg. name. acc. adas; pl. name. acc. ammūni; other cases cf. asau| that; this, this, these (over there) — ind. Thus ; there — mr. cf. asau — f. cf. asau.
adādi [(ad₁)ādi] m. gram. ["which begins with ad₁"] qualifies the second class [gaṇa] of the present tense of verbs; its characteristic marker [vikarana₂] is luk.
adāhya |neg. dāhya| amnf adāhyā in combustible.

Aditi [opp. diti] f. myth. ved. np. of Aditi "the Undivided", mother goddess, personifying Undivided Nature, boundless space, pure and free universal energy; by her husband Kasyapa she is mother of the radiant [Aditya], and notably of Daksa the skillful magician, who is also her father; Nārāyaṇa taught her payovrata so that she would give birth to Vāmana; she presides over the nakṣatra of the Punarvasū (Gemini).
adīna [neg. dīna] amnf adīnā valiant, not defeated.
adīnātman |ātman| amnf adīnātmanī d'hu meur vaillante.
adīrghasūtra [neg. dīrghasūtra] amnf adīrghasūtrā non dilatory; expeditious.
adurmangala [neg. durmangala] amnf adurmangalī that does not bring bad luck. সমুষ adușța [neg. dușța] amnf adușțā undefiled, uncorrupted, unimpure | pure, innocent.
adustatva [tva] n. innocence.
adūra [neg. dūra] amnf adūrā near — n. proximity. adūre var. adūrāt, adūratas adv. in the vicinity.
adūratā [tā] f. proximity. pūrvānubhavasaṃskārabodhinī yadi adūratā lit. [KD.] When there is proximity (of the same sound), one is aware of the impression of a previous perception.
adūrabhava [bhava] amnf adūrabhavā located near (of (iic.)).
adṛśya [neg. dṛśya] amnf adṛśyā invisible; latent.

adṛśyantī [related to adṛśya] f. myth. np. of Adráyantī "the Invisible", wife of the rși Sakti₁, mother of Parāśara. সহুষ্ট adrsta [neg. drsta] amnf adrstā unnoticed, not yet seen, new; unobserved, unattested,

unknown | Invisible | occult; supernatural | that which cannot be seen; unauthorized | phil. that which cannot be understood by ordinary perception and simple reasoning — n. unforeseen calamity; tragic fate | miracle; divine surprise | phil. |Vātsyāyana₂| imperceptible attribute; not. accumulation of merits and faults during past existences [karman]. adrstam kr to make oneself Invisible.
adrstakāma | kāma | m. love towards someone not yet met.

adṛṣṭārtha | artha | amnf adṛṣṭārthā whose merit, meaning or purpose is hidden, occult, or invisible; of incomprehensible purpose; whose designs are impenetrable | phil. which concerns the supernatural world; syn. alaukika.
adeva [priv. deva] amnf adevā non divine | without god, impious | Vedic qualifies the barbarians [dasyu] "who do not honor the gods" (not. Indra, cf. anin dra).
adeśa [priv. deśa] amnf adeśā (document) not legal.
adga |ad₁| mr. soc. cake offered as an oblation.
addhā adv. manifestly; certainly, truly.
adbhis [i. ap] adv. by the waters.
adbhuta [atibhūta] amnf adbhutā extraordinary, Marvelous; supernatural, miraculous — m. lit. the feeling of the Marvelous, one of the 9 modes
artistic [rasa]; it is associated with the color yellow and the deity Brahmā | myth. [Mah.] np. of Adbhuta, the celestial fire "Marvelous" — n. marvel, prodigy | bd. miracle.
adbhutarūpa | rūpa | amnf adbhutarūpā of prodigious beauty.
adbhutasāgara | sāgara | m. lit. np. of the Adbhu tasāgara "Ocean of wonders", astronomical treatise due to the Jain king Vallālasena (13th century).

adyá |div| adv. today; now || lat. hodie; fr. aujourd'hui. adyāpi adv. at this very moment; to this day; so far; today; still today. adya niśi adv. last night. adya prabhrti adv. from today onwards. adya yāvat adv. until today.
adyatana [tana] amnf adyatana of today | contemporary, modern — m. today, the present day — f. adyatana gram. tense of the aorist [lui], which indicates a recent completed past.
adyatva [tva] n. the present time. adyatve nowadays.
adyārabhya [ārabhya] amnf adyārabhyā from now on, henceforth.
adyotaka [neg. dyotaka] amnf adyotikā gram. grammatical word, mottool; opp. vācaka.
adravya [opp. dravya₁] n. insignificant thing, worthless object.

ádri m. stone, rock; mountain | ved. millstone, not. used for pressing soma | projectile stone | math. symb. the number 7 (for the 7 mountains) mountain-shaped cloud formation. paśyasyadrau jvaladagnim na punah pādayoradhah You see the fire burning on the mountain, but not the one under your feet!
adrivat |vat| amnf adrivatī armed with a sling.

adrikā f. myth. [Mah.] np. of the mermaid nymph adrikā; this apsara was cursed by a brahmin, and condemned to become a fish in the Yamunā; there she ate the sperm of King Uparicara to give birth to MatsyagandhīSatyavatī and Matsya₁.
adroghá [neg. drogha] amnf adroghā right, sincere, true. ádrogham adv. with uprightness, sincerely.
ádroghavāc [vāc] amnf sincere, reliable; of good word.
adroha [opp. droha] m. benevolence, goodwill; loyalty.
advaya [neg. dvaya] amnf advayā without equal, unique — n. phil. nonduality; identity (of mind and matter) | ultimate reality.
advayavādin [vādin] amnf advayavādinī Buddhist soc.; monist.
advitīya [neg. dvitīya] amnf advitīyā without second, without equal; unique. ekam eva advitīyam [ChU.] (Being is) truly unique, without second.
adveṣṭṛ [neg. dveṣṭṛ] amnf dveṣṭrī non-enemy; ally.
ádvaita [opp. dvaita] n. phil. nonduality; philosophical doctrine preached by Sankara₁; it postulates the identity of paramātman, the Universal Soul, with jīvātman, the individual soul.
advaitavādin | vādin | amnf advaitavādinī phil. one who adheres to non-duality; one who teaches it; monist.
advaitasiddhi |siddhi | f. lit. np. of the Advaitasid dhi "Perfection of nonduality", phil. work of Madhusūdana₁ Sarasvatī₂, which forcefully refutes dualistic theories.
Advaitānanda |ānanda| m. hist. np. of Ad vaitānanda, Bengali Vaishnava monist author of the late 15th century; he is the author of the Brahma vidyābharaņa; also called Advayānanda.
advaitin [in] m. cf. advaitavādin.
ádha [related to atha] conj. Vedic. then; thus; moreover | var. adhā Vedic. id. adhayad just when.
adhah cf. adhas.
adhaḥprastara [prastara] m. soc. layer of grass
kuśa |darbha|.
adhaḥśākha |śākhā| amnf adhaḥśākhā having the branches at the bottom; cf. ūrdhvamūla.
adhaḥśāyin [śāyin] amnf adhaḥśāyinī who sleeps on the ground.
adhana [priv. dhana] amnf adhanā poor.
adhanya [neg. dhanya] amnf adhanyā poor.
adhamá [great. adhas] amnf adhamā lowest, very low, worst; vile | lat. infimus; fr. tiny.
adhamakāvya | kāvya | n. lit. inferior quality poem | learned poetry with multiple interpretations, wordplay.
ádhara |compar. adhas| amnf adharā below, lower, inferior | (direction) downwards — m. lower lip; lip | nadir || lat. inferus; ang. under; all. unter; fr. inferior. ádharatas adv. below, from below.
adharastāt |tāt| adv. below.
adharahanú | hanu | f. lower jaw. adharāraņi | araņi | f. lower part of a fire stick.
adharottara [uttara₁] amnf adharottarā better and worse; upside down, in order in verse — n. top and bottom; question and answer.
adharostha |ostha| mr. lower lip var. adharaustha id.
adhare [loc. adhara] ind. in either one.
adharedyús [dyu] adv. the day before yesterday.

ádharma [opp. dharma] m. Injustice, wrong; Evil, fault; demerit; sin, immorality | myth. np. of Adharma, personification of Evil; he presides over Vice and Injustice, with his consort Nirrti (or sometimes Himsā or Mithyā); they engender the Sins: Anṛta, Dambha, Darpa, Nikṛti | subterfuge; syn. chala. adharmena adv. in a faulty manner, wrongly. nisiddhakarmajanyas tvadharmah [Tarkasamgraha] Demerit is that which is produced by the prohibited act.
adharmacārin₁ [cārin| amnf adharmacāriṇī that does harm.
adharmajugupsu [jugupsu] amnf who hates injustice; who feels disgust for sin.
adharmajñá₁ [jña] amnf adharmajñā who knows how to circumvent the law, expert in fraud.
ádharmacārin₂ [opp. dharmacārin] amnf adharmacārinī who does not behave well.
ádharmajña₂ [neg. dharmajña] amnf adharmajñā who does not know the law.
adharmya [neg. dharmya] amnf adharmyā improper, illegitimate; wrongful.
adhas adv. under g. ; below, downwards; on the ground, on the soil. adhah kr to surpass; to bring down; to overturn, to turn upside down; to overthrow, to engulf. tarūṇāmadhaḥ under the trees.
adhaścaranam [carana] adv. at the feet of.

adhaścaraṇāvapāta [caraṇaavapāta] amnf adhaścaranāvapātā who throws himself at the feet of. adhaścaraṇāvapātam adv. rushing to the feet of. lāngūlacālanam adhaścaranāvapātam bhūmau ni patya vadanodaradarśanam ca | śvā pindadasya ku rute gajapungavastu dhīram vilokayati cātuśataiśca bhunkte | [PT.] Stretched out on the ground at his master's feet, wagging his tail, showing his muzzle and belly, so acts the dog; while the elephant, examining him from afar, only consents to eat after a hundred caresses.
adhastāt |tāt| adv. down, below, down | under (iic.), below (g.).
adhokṣá [akṣa] amnf adhokṣā under the wheel; smaller than the wheel | not visible.
Adhokṣaja |ja| m. myth. np. of Adhokṣaja "Inaccessible to the senses", epith. of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu as Transcendent God.
adhodhas | red. | adv. lower and lower.
adhonilaya [nilaya] m. hell ["underground abode"].
adhonivīta | nivīta | amn who wears the sacred cord low.
adhomukha | mukha | amnf adhomukhī who lowers his head | head down.
adhā cf. adha.

adhātu [opp. dhātu] m. gram. (morpheme) non-root. স্থা ádhi adv. on, above (loc.) | superior; in addition, besides | outside (abl.) | concerning (acc.) in comparison with. adhi pañcālesu brahmadattah Brahmadatta is the chief of the Pañcālās.
adhigopam |gopa| adv. on the cowherd.

adhipāṇi [pāṇi] adv. on the hand. সাধিক adhika [adhika] amnf adhikā addi tional, augmented by, in excess, extra; excessive, extreme; redundant | eminent, excellent; superior to (abl.) — iic. astr. lunar month [māsa] intercalary of the amānta calendar allowing the lunar year to catch up with the sidereal solar year [nirayana]; it occurs at an interval between 28 and 35 lunar months, i.e., 7 intercalary months every 19 years; cf. śuddha, kṣaya₂ | lit. figure of speech indicating that the content is greater than the container — n. surplus; more — num. separates the hundreds; example: catuhsastyadhikadviśatatama two hundred and sixty-fourth | in excess of 1; opp. ūna. adhikam very; too much, in surplus; more. astādhikanavatih 98. ekādhikam śatam 101.
adhikatara |tara| amnf adhikatarā compar. larger; very large.
adhikatā [tā] f. addition; excess; preponderance; redundancy.
adhikatva |tva| n. id.
adhikadeśa | deśa | iic. in general.
adhikadeśavrttitva | vrttitva | n. being current; opp. alpadeśavrttitva.
adhikarūpavat [rūpavat] amnf adhikarūpavatī of stunning beauty.

adhikasaṃgamā [saṃgama] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of Adhikasaṃgamā, first wife of King Pa rityāgasena, mother of the twins Indīvarasena and Anicchāsena by trickery, to the detriment of Kāvyālaṃkārā; she had been Adityaprabhā in a previous life.
adhikānurāga [anurāga] m. extreme affection.
adhikārtha [artha] amnf adhikārthā exaggerated.
adhikārthavacana [vacana] n. exaggeration; hy perbole.

adhikaraṇa [act. adhikṛ] n. supremacy, government; judgment, tribunal, court of justice | report; case; domain, substrate, support; receptacle; place | phil. substrate; category; syn. ādhāra | gram. government, dependence; mutual relation between words in a sentence; not. the role | kāraka | locative, but also samāna₂, coreference lit. rhet. theme, subject; thematic section of a treatise (itself divided into chapters |adhyāya|) — agt. f. adhikaraṇā ifc. that which governs, in charge of (iic.).
adhikaraṇaka [ka] ifc. amnf adhikaraṇakā [NN.] which has as support or locus (iic.).
adhikaraṇatā [tā] f. phil. [NN.] fact of being a locus or subject of predication; opp. ādheyatā.
adhikaraṇatva [tva] n. gram. the state of being the place of an action.
Adhikaraṇamālā [mālā] f. bed. of np. the Adhikaraṇamālā, compendium of notions of Vedānta due to Bhāratītīrtha.
adhikaranika [ika] m. soc. magistrate, judge.
adhikaranya [ya] n. power, authority.

adhikāra [act. adhikṛ] m. office, charge, employment; administration | authority; jurisdiction; power, government, royal office; right, property; title, rank, position | soc. privilege; priority | phil. [Nyāya] main rule; prerequisite | lit. subject of a work; theme | [theatre] possession by the hero of the desired fruit | gram. rule governing a section; scope of this rule soc. ritual qualification | phil. spiritual qualification.
adhikārapramatta [pramatta] afmn adhikārapramattā negligent in his duty.
adhikāravidhi [vidhi] m. phil. [mīmāṃsā] injunction of ritual qualification.
adhikārin [agt. adhikr] amnf adhikāriņī employee, attendant; officer | proper to, authorized; disciple | phil. |Vedānta| aspiring to liberation | trusted person; person in authority.
adhikṛ [adhikṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (adhikaróti) pp. (adhikṛta) to entrust a charge, to appoint; to place in charge of, to put at the head of (loc.).
adhikṛta [pp. adhikṛ] amnf adhikṛtā charged; qualified — m. chief; employee, attendant.
adhikṛtya [abs. adhikṛ] ind. with regard to (acc.). adhi krtvā having done above (adhi prep. rather than preverb).
adhikṣip [adhikṣip] v. [6] pr. (adhikṣipati) pp. (adhikṣipta) to insult; to slander. kimasmān saṃbhṛtadoṣairadhikṣipatha Why do you overwhelm us with slander?
adhigata [pp. adhigam] amnf adhigatā approached, found, obtained, attained; acquired, received; perceived, understood — n. discovery, understanding.
adhigatya [pfp. [1] adhigam] amnf adhigatyā to be attained, to be understood.

adhigam [adhigam] v. [1] pr. (adhigac chati) pf. (sam) pp. (adhigata) pfp. (adhigatya, adhigamya) to approach; to find, obtain, reach, attain; to receive | to realize, perceive, understand. artham adhigacchati he becomes rich.
adhigama [act. adhigam] m. acquisition, obtaining | mastery; knowledge, understanding | profit.
adhigamya [pfp. [1] adhigam] amnf adhigamyā attainable; perceptible.
adhigā [adhigā₁] v. [3] pr. (adhijigāti) to initiate; to resolve to | to study, to read.
adhiguṇa [adhiguṇa] amnf adhiguṇā which possesses superior qualities.
adhijya [adhijyā₃] amnf adhijyā who pulled the string of his bow.
adhityakā f. country on the slopes of the mountain, foothills; plateau; opp. upatyakā.
adhideva [adhideva] m. tutelary deity.
adhidevatā [tā] f. quality of tutelary deity.
adhidaiva [adhidaiva] n. tutelary deity phil. the divine.
adhidaivika [adhidaivika] amnf adhidaivikā phil. spiritual; supernatural.
adhinātha [adhinātha] m. commander-in-chief.
adhipa [adhipa₂] m. cf. adhipati.

adhipati [adhipati] m. master, chief, superior; prince, supreme master, king | myth. sovereign god; notably used for Indra, Varuna, Agni | phil. [Nyāya] preponderant cause of a phenomenon. bhūmeradhipatih soc. Lord of the earth (royal title).
adhibhū [adhibhū₂] m. master, dominator.
adhibhūta [adhibhūta] n. phil. spiritual substratum of material elements; Supreme Spirit pervading Nature | phil. macrocosm (opp. adhyātma).
adhimāsa [adhimāsa] m. astr. intercalary month.
adhimukta [pp. adhimuc] amnf adhi muktā bd. inclined to, attracted by, tending towards, applies itself with regard to (iic. loc. acc.).
adhimukti [act. adhimuc] f. bd. inclination, tendency to (iic. loc. acc.).
adhimuc [adhimuc₁] v. [1] pr. (adhimuc cati) pp. (adhimukta) bd. to appreciate, to be attracted to, to take pleasure in.
adhiyajña [adhiyajña] m. soc. principal sacrifice | phil. ritual work, mediation between microcosm and macrocosm.

Adhiratha [adhiratha] amnf adhi rathā who is on a chariot — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Adhiratha "Chariot-bearer", prince of Anga, driver of the chariot [sūta₁] of King Śūra; he is the husband of Rādhā₁, the nurse of Karņa.
adhirāj [adhirāj₂] m. superior king; king of zerain; emperor | var. adhirāja id. | var. adhirājan id.
adhiruh [adhiruh₁] v. [1] pr. (adhirohati) pr. r. (adhirohate) to mount, to get on, to climb (loc.); to arrive at — ca. (adhirohayati) var. adhiropayati to raise, to put on.
adhirop [ca. adhiruh] v. [10] pr. (adhiro payati) to raise, to put on.
adhilaya [adhilaya] m. bd. calumny. pratisedhayāmi nāham | pratisedhayasītyadhilaya eșa tvayā kriyate | Nāgārjuna I deny nothing; you slander me by saying that I deny it.
adhivaktṛ [agt. adhivac] amnf adhi vaktrī lawyer.
adhivac [adhivac] v. [2] pr. (adhivakti) by ler in favor of.
adhivas₁ [adhivas₁] v. [1] pr. (adhivasati) to live acc. .
adhivas₂ [adhivas₁] v. [2] pr. r. (adhivaste) to cover oneself (with clothing); to dress oneself.
adhivāsa₁ [agt. adhivas₁] m. inhabitant, resident | dwelling, residence.
adhivāsá₂ [obj. adhivas₂] m. coat — n. adhivāsas id.
adhivāsita [adhivāsita] amnf adhivāsitā perfumed; imbued with, influenced by (i. ifc.
adhivāsin [agt. adhivas₁] amnf adhivāsinī who lives | mod. aboriginal.
adhiviś [adhiviś₁] ca. (adhiveśayati) pp. (adhiveśita) install.
adhiveśana [act. adhiviś] n. facility; session.
adhiśī [adhiśī₁] v. [2] pr. r. (adhiśete) pp. (adhiśayita) to rest, to lie on (acc. loc.). grāmam adhisete he sleeps in the village.
adhiśrayana [adhiśrayana] n. act of putting in the fire — f. adhiśrayaṇī hearth; oven.
adhişavana [act. adhişu] n. ved. manual press to extract the soma. adhişavanaphalaka [phalaka] n. of. adhişavana phalake cf. adhisavanya.
adhisavanya [ya] m. of. adhisavanyau |adhi savaṇaphalake] ved. the two parts of a soma press. স্থিমু adhiṣu [adhisu₂] v. [5] pr. (adhiṣunoti) pp. (adhisuta) ved. press the soma for sacrifice.

adhisthā [adhisthā₁] v. [1] pr. (adhitisthati) pr. r. (adhitisthate) pp. (adhisthita) to settle on, to mount on; to stand on, to stand above (acc.) | to govern, to direct, to have predominance over | to come to; to seize. grāmam adhitisthati he rules the village.

adhişthātṛ [agt. adhişthā] amnf adhisthātrī who governs, who presides; tutelary — m. governor, president; leader, chief; protector | phil. Supreme being — f. adhiṣṭhātrī myth. tutelary goddess of a village or town.
adhisthātrtva [tva] n. quality of ruler; supremacy.
adhiṣṭhāna [adhiṣṭhāna] n. base, foundation | seat, place, domain, location; settlement, agglomeration | (figuratively) person who supports; government, authority, power.
adhiṣṭhita [pp. adhiṣṭhā] amnf adhisthitā populated, inhabited | governed, directed, regulated appointed (to a position).
adhiṣṭheya [pfp. [2] adhiṣṭhā] amnf adhistheyā to govern.
Adhisīmakṛṣṇa m. myth. [BhP.] np. of king Adhisīmakrsna, son of Śatānīka₁.
adhisenāpati [adhisenāpati] m. soc. commander-in-chief of an army.
adhistri [adhistri] adv. concerning a woman or wife.
adhistrī [adhistrī] f. superior woman.
adhihari [adhihari₂] adv. concerning Vishnu.
adhihasti [adhihasti] adv. on the back of an elephant.

adhī [adhii] v. [2] pr. r. (adhīté) pp. (adhīta) abs. (adhītya) to repeat; to read; to study | to learn, to announce | to come across, to notice — v. [2] pr. (adhyeti) to remember — ca. (adhyāpáyati) to teach (2 acc.) — ps. (adhīyate) to be taught. adhīye I study. adhītya after the study. adhīyan sakalam śāstram who studies the whole treatise without difficulty. vedam adhīyīyota tarkam adhīyīya should I study the Veda or logic? ekam śāstram adhīyāno na gac checchāstranirṇayam He who masters only one subject cannot claim to be an authority on any subject. yadyapi bahunādhīṣe tathāpi paṭha putra vyākaraṇam | svajanaḥ śvajano mā bhūt sakalaṃ śakalam sakrchakṛt || [SRBh.] O son, although you have studied much, you must now learn grammar; one must say svajana and not śvajana, sakala and not śakala, sakṛt and not śakrt.
adhīkāra [adhikāra] m. administration of, supervision of loc. | authorization; capacity.
adhīkṣaka [adhiīkṣaka] m. supervisor.
adhīta [pp. adhī] amnf adhītā instructed | learned, studied — n. study.
adhītaveda [veda] amnf adhītavedā who has studied the veda; whose studies are completed.
adhītin [in] amnf adhītinī educated, competent (in loc. ). adhītī vyākaraņe who has studied grammar.
ádhīti [act. adhī] f. study.

adhīna [adhiīna] ifc. amnf adhīnā situated upon, placed upon, resting upon (iic.) | subordinate to, subject to, dependent upon (iic.). sa daivādhīnah kṛtaḥ he was left to his fate. sarvam daivādhīnam everything rests upon destiny. aham tvadadhīno'smi I am at your service. daivādhīnam jagat sarvam mantrādhīnam tu dai vatam | tan mantram brāhmaṇādhīnam brāhmaṇo mama daivatam || The Universe is under divine law; yet, divinity is animated by mantra; and this mantra itself depends upon the Brahmin, therefore the Brahmin is my God.
adhīnatā |tā| f. dependence, subjection.
adhīnatva [tva] n. dependence, subjection.
adhīyat [ppr. adhī] amnf adhīyatī remembering | learner, student.

ádhīra [nég. dhīra₁] amnf adhīrā im patient; impulsive; reckless | anxious; confused; unstable; capricious | lacking control, ex citable; choleric | unfixed; mobile — f. adhīrā lightning | choleric, jealous or capricious mistress; virago | lit. type of heroine expressing her jealousy or grievances.
adhīratā |tā| f. anxiety; lack of confidence.
adhīśa [adhiīśa] m. supreme master (of (iic.)).
adhīṣ [adhiiṣ₁] v. [1] pr. r. (adhyeṣate) dear dear, to solicit.
adhīṣṭa [pp. adhīṣ] amnf adhīṣṭā sol licitity, consulted (teacher) — mn instruction; solicitation, request.
adhunā adv. now. adhunaiva kuru do it now!
adhura |priv. dhura| amnf adhurā not burdened.

ádhṛta |neg. dhṛta| amnf adhṛtā without support; unsupported, free; uncontrolled | restless, agitated — m. myth. np. of Adhṛta, epithet of Viṣṇu "without constraints". সমূহ ádhṛṣṭa [neg. dhṛṣṭa] amnf adhṛṣṭā reserved, modest | invincible, irresistible.
adhṛṣya [neg. dhṛṣya] amnf adhṛṣṭā reserved, modest | invincible, irresistible; inapprochable.
ádhenu [neg. dhenu] amnf ved. (cow) not giving milk.
adhairya [opp. dhairya] n. lack of self-control; excitation — amnf adhairyā who lacks self-control; excitable.
adhyaṃsa [adhiaṃsa] amnf adhyaṃsā placed on the shoulder.

ádhyakṣa [adhiakṣa] amnf adhyakṣā perceptible, observable | "under the eyes" | who oversees, who presides — m. observer, witness | soc. inspector; superintendent; president. dharmādhyakṣah director of the legal department. kiśoravadavāgomahiṣājāvikādhyakṣaḥ superintendent of foals, mares, cows, buffaloes, goats and sheep.
adhyayana |act. adhī| n. soc. reading, personal study (not. of the Veda), one of the 6 duties of a brahmin [saṭkarmāni].
adhyayanatapas | tapas | n. of. adhyayanatapas ī study and asceticism.
adhyavasā [adhiavasā] v. [4] pr. (adhya vasyati) pp. (adhyavasita) to undertake; to accomplish; to consider, evaluate, examine; to determine.
adhyavasāna [act. adhyavasā] n. effort; energy, perseverance | lit. direct and vigorous style lit. absorption of a figure [lakṣaṇā] (distinct from simple superimposition [āropa]).
adhyavasāya [act. adhyavasā] m. effort; energy, perseverance | resolution; determination; certainty.
adhyavasāyin [agt. adhyavasā] amnf adhyavasāyinī determined; resolved.
adhyavasita [pp. adhyavasā] amnf adhyavasitā examined, evaluated, apprehended.
adhyaśana [adhiaśaná2] n. the act of eating too soon after the last meal.
adhyas [adhias₂] v. [4] pr. (adhyasyati) pp. (adhyasta) to place or throw on | wrongly imputed.
adhyātma [adhiātma] n. phil. the supreme Being or soul | phil. microcosm (opp. adhibhūta) — amnf adhyātmā proper, individual.
adhyātmam adv. concerning the individual personality or the soul.
adhyātmajñāna [jñāna] n. phil. knowledge of the Self.
Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa [rāmāyaṇa] n. bed. n.p. of the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa; King Rāma embodies the Supreme Being; it is part of Brahmāndapurāna, and is attributed to Vyāsa.
adhyātmavidyā [vidyā] f. phil. science of Being, knowledge of the Self.
adhyātmika |ika| amnf adhyātmikī phil. which concerns the supreme soul; spiritual.
adhyātmikavidyā [vidyā] f. knowledge of the supreme soul; spiritual knowledge.
adhyāp [ca. adhī] v. [10] pr. (adhyāpayati) to teach (2 acc.).
adhyāpaka |agt. ca. adhī| amnf adhyāpikā who teaches — m. professor — f. adhyāpikā (woman) professor.
adhyāpana [act. ca. adhī] n. soc. teaching (not. of the Veda), one of the 6 duties of a brah mane |saṭkarmāni|.

adhyāya [act. adhī] m. recitation, reading (notably of the Veda); lesson; study | lit. chapter (the Rigveda has 64, each composed of about thirty sections [varga]) | lesson, subdivision of a book [kāṇḍa] of the Satapatha brāhmaṇa; it consists of chapters [brāhmaṇa] | Vedic language; opp. bhāṣā — agt. amnf adhyāyī ifc. one who recites — f. adhyāyī ifc. lit. chapter of (2nd century). vedādhyāyaḥ one who studies the Veda.
adhyāyin [agt. adhī] amnf adhyāyinī who recites, who studies — m. student.
adhyāruh [adhiāruh] v. [1] pr. (adhy ārohati) to mount, to ascend — ca. (adhyāropayati) to mount.
adhyāropa [act. adhyāruh] m. phil. |Vedānta| erroneous attribution, incorrect analogical inference.
adhyās [adhiās₂] v. [2] pr. r. (adhyāste) pp. (adhyāsita) to remain; to settle; to visit; to take office | to put on, to slip on (shoes, etc.). parvatam adhyāste he is sitting on the mountaintop.
adhyāsa |act. adhyas| m. soc. rit. imposition | phil. superimposition; wrong attribution; erroneous interpretation, false idea.
adhyāhāra [adhiāhāra] m. act of joining; supplement; inference | gram. paraphrase substituting for the omitted terms of an ellipsis.
adhyudātta [adhiudātta] m. gram. initial accent.
adhyustra [adhiustra] m. merchandise transported by camel.
adhyeṣaṇa [act. adhīṣ] n. solicitation, request; not. request for teaching.
adhruva [neg. dhruva] amnf adhruvā mobile bile. সধ্ব adhva iic. adhvan.
adhvaga [ga₁] amnf adhvagā traveler — n. act of travelling — f. adhvagā geo. epith. of the river Gangā "that which travels".
adhvagabhogya |bhogya| m. bio. |"that which delights travelers" epith. of bot. Spondias Man gifera, the wild mango tree.
adhveśa [īśa] m. soc. ["guardian of the public way" | police officer.
áadhvan m. path | journey, route; distance and time (of a journey) | phil. [siddhānta] procession; world (subtle or material); cf. śuddhādhvan.
adhvanīna [īna] amnf adhvanīnā fit to travel; syn. adhvanya.
adhvanya [ya] amnf adhvanyā traveler; syn. adhvanīna.

adhvará |priv. dhvarā| amnf adhvarā that does not harm — m. soc. rite, nonviolent sacrifice; not. soma sacrifice — v. [11] pr. (adhvaryáti) v. [11] pr. (adhvarīyáti) to perform the sacrifice or divine service.
adhvarakarman | karman | n. soc. performance of an adhvara sacrifice.
adhvaraga [ga₁] amnf adhvaragā soc. intended for sacrifice.
adhvarastha |stha| amnf adhvarasthā soc. who is in sacrifice.
adhvarin [adhvarain] m. (priest) performing a sacrifice.

adhvaryú [adhvarayu] m. Vedic priest officiating at the solemn sacrifice, in charge of the ritual acts; he builds the altar, prepares the ritual instruments and the hearth, brings and sacrifices any necessary sacrificial animals; he pronounces the formulas of the yajuḥsaṃhitā; he makes the butter offering |ghṛta| in the āhavanīya fire; he is accompanied by the hotr and the udgātr, all supervised by the brahman; his three assistants are the pratiprasthātr, the potr, and the neṣṭr; syn. yajyu — f. wife of an adhvaryu priest. an₁ pf. privative a before a vowel. anaśva who is not a horse.
anakṣara [priv. akṣara] amnf anakṣarā mute; who cannot speak.
anakṣíka [an₁akṣika] amnf anakṣikā without an eye.
anagha |priv. agha| amnf anaghā without fault; irreproachable.

Ananga | priv. anga₁ | amnf anangā in corporeal — m. myth. np. of Ananga "the Incorporeal", epith. of the god Kāma (whose body was consumed by the fire of Shiva's anger, whose asceticism he had disturbed).

anangaprabhā [prabhā₂] f. lit. [KSS.] np of the vidyādharī anangaprabhā "Light of Love", daughter of King Samara; out of pride she refused all marriage; her father cursed her to become human under the name of anangarati and to marry many men whom she would hate; she married the brah mane Jīvadatta and left him for King Harivara, whom she left for the dance master Labdavara, whom she left for the player Sudarsana, whom she left for the merchant Hiranyagupta, whom she left for the fisherman Sāgaravīra, whom she left for the kṣatriya Vijayavarmā, whom she left for King Sāgaravarmā, to whom she gave a son Sa mudravarmā; Shiva revealed to her in a dream that she was vidyādharī, and that Sāgaravarmā was the vidyādhara Madanaprabha, thus ending their curse.
Anangabhīma [bhīma] m. hist. np. of King Anangabhīma III, of the Ganga dynasty; he reigned over Kalinga from 1211 to 1238; he established the state cult of Purusottama (later called Ja gannātha).
Anangaranga [ranga] m. bed. n.p. of the Anangaranga "Theater of Love", or erotic drama due to Kalyāṇa₁ Malla; cf. strīpurusasāmānyasāmudrikalaksaņa.

anangarati [rati] f. lit. [KSS.] np of the princess anangarati "Love's Pleasure", daughter of King Mahāvaraha of Sūrapura and Queen Padmarati; she was the vidyādharī anangaprabhā cursed to be reborn human; she refused four suitors from various castes, and died at 16; the brah mane Jīvadatta could not resurrect her, but obtained a magic sword to find her again as anangaprabhā.
anangavajra [vajra] m. hist. [Vajrayāna] np. of the master anangavajra, author of the Prajňopāyaviniścayasiddhi; Indrabhūti was his student.

anaḍváh [anasvah₂] m. [fb. anahud; obl. anaduh; sg. name. anadvān, acc. anadvāham, i. anaduhā, voc. ánadvan; of. name. acc. anadvāhau; pl. name. anadvāhas, acc. anaduhas] ox (which pulls the cart) | bull; astr. the constellation Taurus.
anaṇīyas [neg. aṇīyas] amnf anaṇīyasī not at all minuscule; vast, powerful.
anati [an₁ati] pf. not completely (ifc.).
anatidūra [neg. atidūra] amnf ana tidūrā not particularly far away.
anatipraudha [neg. atipraudha] amnf anatipraudhā not fully developed; young, growing.
anativṛtti [neg. ativṛtti] f. state of being in agreement.
anaddhā |neg. addhā| ind. not really.
anaddhāpuruṣa [puruṣa] m. ved. useless man (no longer celebrating sacrificial rites).
anadyatana [neg. adyatana] amnf ana dyatanā gram. refers to a time (past or future) that does not apply to the present day.
anadhikarana [neg. adhikarana] n. phil. [Nyāya] non-substrate.
anadhikāra [opp. adhikāra] m. absence of authority; incompetence.
anadhikārin [neg. adhikārin] amnf anadhikāriņī unauthorized; unfit, incapable, incompetent. anadhikārivedānta the philosophy of fools.
anadhigata [neg. adhigata] amnf anadhigatā not approached, left aside; not studied; not reached.
anadhigataśāstra [śāstra] amnf anadhi
gataśāstrā ["who neglected his studies"] uncultured, uneducated.
anadhīta [neg. adhīta] amnf anadhītā uncultured, ignorant.
anadhyayana [opp. adhyayana] n. soc. in interruption of Vedic studies; vacation
anadhyavasāya [opp. adhyavasāya] m. irresolution, hesitation.
anadhyavasita [neg. adhyavasita] amnf anadhyavasitā irresolute, hesitant.
anadhyāya [opp. adhyāya] m. absence of study; period of interruption of studies.
ananuṣṭhāna [opp. anuṣṭhāna] n. inac fulfillment; negligence (not. of one's religious duties).

anantá [priv. anta] amnf anantā in infini, Unlimited; eternal — n. eternity — m. myth. np. of Ananta "Eternal", epith. of the dragon of eternity [nāga] Šeṣa, son of Kaśyapa and Kadrū; during creation he remains in the underworld [pātāla] and at the end of the World [kalpānta] Rudra emanates from his heads to destroy the Universe; he incarnated on Earth as Ba larāmaSaṃkarṣaṇa; Vāsuki is his brother, Manasā his sister | hist. np. of King Ananta₁ of Kaśmīra, son of Samgrāmarāja whom he succeeded in 1028; he laid waste to the kingdom; His wife, Queen Suryamatī, made him abdicate in favor of their son Kalasa in 1063, who proved unfit; Ananta₁ committed suicide in 1081. anantā vai vedāḥ [Indra] The Vedas are truly eternal.
anantacaturdaśī | caturdaśī | f. cf. anantavrata.
anantanātha [nātha] m. jn. np. d'anantanātha "Master of Eternity", 14th mythical tīrthankara; his body is golden, his symbol is a falcon or a bear.

anantápāra | pāra | amnf anantapārā without limits. anantapāram kila śabdaśāstram svalpam tathāyurbahavaśca vighnāḥ sāraṃ tato grāhyam apāsya phalgu haṃsair yathā kṣīram ivāmbumadhyāt || The science of language is indeed without limits, but life is short and the obstacles numerous; thus one must grasp the essential while leaving the superfluous, as geese make milk mixed with water.
anantamūla |mūla| mr. organic. bot. Hemidesmus In dicus, Indian sarsaparilla, gentian creeper; the root of this sarmentose shrub is used medicinally; syn. śāribā.
anantavat [vat] m. phil. [ChU.] the Unlimited or partition [pāda] of brahman into four spaces: the Earth [Pṛthivī], the Atmosphere [Antarikṣa], the Sky [Dyau] and the Ocean [Samudra].

anantavarman [varman] m. hist. np. of King Anan tavarmā Codaganga (1078–1147); originally from the Ganga dynasty of Karnata, he conquered Kalinga around 1108 as Gangesvara; he established his capital at Kaṭaka (mod. Cuttack), and had the temple of Jagannātha built at Purī | lit. [DKC.] np. of the young king of Vidarbha Anantavarmā₁, son of Punyavarmā; he was a poet and artist ignorant of politics, poorly advised by his confidant in pleasures Vihārabhadra, then by Prince Can drapālita who incited him to hunting, gambling, women, alcohol and despotism; the kingdom, delivered into chaos, declined; Vasantabhānu incited King Bhānuvarmā to attack him; Anantavarmā₁ fell in love with the dancer Kṣmātalorvaśī, whom he raped; Vasan tabhānu persuaded Avantideva and other vassals to attack Anantavarmā, and took all his possessions; his wife Vasumdharā had to flee with her children Mañjuvādinī and Bhāskaravarmā.

anantavāsudeva [vāsudeva] m. myth. n.p. of Anan tavāsudeva, epith. of Balarāma son of Vasudeva and incarnation of Ananta | geo. n.p. of the vish nouite Anantavāsudeva temple built on the banks of the Bin dusarovara in Bhuvaneśvarī₁ in 1278.
anantavijaya [vijaya] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Anan tavijaya, conch of Yudhisthira.
anantavrata [vrata] n. soc. festival of Vișnu Anantaśāyin, celebrated on the 14th day [caturdaśī] of the month of bhādra; in Mahārāṣṭra, it ends with the im
mersion | visarjana | of an idol of Ganesa, installed 10 days earlier for gaņeśacaturthī.

Ananta Sayana | Sayana| n. geo. np. of Ananta Sayana, capital of Kerala, named in honor of Sri Padmanabhasvami, whose temple is in the center of the city; it was known as Thiruvi Thamkur Travancore, then as Trivandrum, and since 1991 as Thiruvananthapuram. Ananta Sayanasamsrtagranthāvalli series of works in Sanskrit published in Trivandrum.
Anantaśāyin |śāyin| m. myth. np. of Anantaśāyin, epith. of ViṣṇuNārāyaṇa "resting on Ananta".
anantásīrṣā [śīrṣa] f. myth. np. of Anantaśīrṣā "Dawn of Eternity", wife of the serpent king Sesa.
anantasūtra [sūtra] n. soc. sacred cord; cf. upavīta, yajñasūtra.

ananteśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of the ananteśvara temple dedicated to Shiva in Avantipura, built by King Avantivarmā (9th century) | geo. np. of the ananteśvara₁ temple in Udupī; it is said that Viṣṇu in his primordial form resides in his linga.

anantará [priv. antara] amnf anantarā that follows immediately (in time, space, rank); without interval or pause; adjacent — n. contiguity. anantaram adv. immediately after, then; after which, from there | right next to — prep. cl. immediately after (g. abl. iic.).
anantarakālīna [kālīna] amnf anantarakālīnā which occurs at another time.
anantarakālīnatva [tva] n. gram. act of marking progression in time.
ananda [priv. nanda] amnf Joyless Anandā — f. Anandā phil. the "joyless world" Anandā where those who do not reach brahman die.
anandatva [tva] n. sadness.
anannāsa n. bio. bot. Ananas comosus, Pineapple; also called bahunetraphala.
ananyá [neg. anya] amnf ananyā not different, not other; identical | without second; unique; alone | having no other interest.
ananyamanas [neg. anyamanas] amnf ["having nothing else on one's mind"] entirely attentive, completely involved
ananyamānasa [neg. anyamānasa] amnf ananyamānasā id.
ananyārtha [neg. anyārtha] amnf ananyārthā not subject to another object, principal gram. not ambiguous, without misinterpretation.
anapatya [priv. apatya] amnf anapatyā without descendants.
anapara |priv. apara₂| amnf anaparā without other | alone, isolated.
anapavrjyá [neg. apavrjya] amnf anapavrjyā that must not be abandoned (not. path); without end (not. road) | that must not be finished; inexhaustible.
anapāya [priv. apāya] amnf anapāyā without obstacles; prosperous — opp. m. absence of dan ger.
anapāyin [neg. apāyin] amnf anapāyinī that does not go away; stable, permanent; invariable.

anapekṣa [priv. apekṣā] amnf anapekṣā without regard, without consideration; irrelevant, unjustified — opp. f. anapekṣā inattention, negligence; disregard. anapekṣam without consideration; carelessly, without serious examination.
anapekṣatva [tva] n. irrelevance; negligence. anapekṣatvāt adv. due to having no relation to.

anapekṣita [neg. apekṣita] amnf anapekṣitā neglected, ignored | unnecessary, unjustified; unexpected | phil. not supported by justification; unchecked. nānapekṣitam ucyate |Mallinātha₁| One should not state anything without justification.
anapekṣitaparapīḍa [parapīḍā] amnf anapekșitaparapīdā which does not take into account the suffering of others.
anapekṣitahetu | hetu | amnf which does not take the cause into account.
anapekṣya [opp. apekṣya] amnf anapekṣyā not to be taken into consideration; undesirable — abs. ind. without taking into account. anapeksyam state this should not be taken into consideration.
ánapeta [opp. apeta] amnf anapetā not disappeared | which does not deviate from (abl. iic.).
anabhijña [opp. abhijña] amnf anabhijñā ignorant | unfamiliar with (g. iic.).

anabhidhāna [opp. abhidhāna] n. the act of not expressing | gram. unauthorized form; form without denotation; unattested form; form not in accordance with usage. anabhidhānāt gram. |Patanjali₁| it is not said.
anabhimukha [neg. abhimukha] amnf anabhimukhā indifferent to (g.). anabhimukhaḥ sukhānām he does not pay attention to pleasures.
anabhiṣikta [opp. abhiṣikta] amnf anabhiṣiktā soc. not having received the royal anointing.

anabhiṣvaṅga [opp. abhiṣvaṅga] m. absence of attachment (to (loc.)). asaktiranabhişvangah putradāragrhādişu | nityam samacittatvamistānistopapattisu | [BG.] ca detachment, absence of attachment towards son, wife, home, etc. and constant equanimity towards events, be they pleasant or unpleasant.
anabhisambandha var. anabhisam
bandha [priv. abhisambandha] amnf anabhi sambandhā not connected — absence m. lack of connection.
anabhisneha [priv. abhisneha] amnf abhisnehā without affection; without desire; without passion.
anabhihita [opp. abhihita] amnf anabhihitā not expressed. anabhihite gram. [Pāṇini] when (the role [kāraka]) is not already expressed (it can be expressed by the following ending rules).
anabhīṣṭa [neg. abhīṣṭa] amnf anabhīṣṭā unwanted, undesirable.
anabhyantara [opp. abhyantara] amnf anabhyantarā not contained in (iic. loc. g.) | not initiated into, not familiar with loc. g. .
anabhyupāya [priv. abhyupāya] amnf anabhyupāyā gram. [Patañjali] inoperative.
anamīvá [priv. amīvā] amnf anamīvā without illness or discomfort, in good health — n. well-being.
anayā [i. iyam] ind. by this | gram. follows a passive form to indicate the sense of cause [karaṇa]; syn. anena.

anaraṇya [priv. araṇya] amnf anaraṇyā civilized — m. myth. np. of the king anaranya "civilized", son of Trasadasyu of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa]; he is father of Haryaśva | myth. [Rām.] np. of the king anaranya₁, son of Bāṇa₁, father of Prthu₁; he fought in vain Rāvaṇa, and dying in battle cursed him for being defeated by Rāma.
anargala [priv. argala] amnf anargalā without hindrance, without obstruction; free, licentious.
anargha [priv. argha] amnf anarghā in estimable; without price.
anargharāghava [rāghava] n. bed. n.p. from Anar gharāghava, a play by Murāri₁ dealing with the story of Rāma.
anarghya [neg. arghya] amnf anarghyā inestimable; priceless.
anarghyatva |tva| n. state of being inestimable.
anartha [priv. artha] amnf anarthā without purpose, useless; unfortunate, which brings misfortune — m. disadvantage; misfortune, misfortune, calamity.
anarthaka [ka] amnf anarthakā useless, worthless; without purpose; absurd, without meaning; gratuit, without aim. anarthakā hi mantrāḥ [Kautsa₁] Vedic mantras are meaningless.
anarthakāra [kāra] amnf anarthakārī who does useless or worthless or harmful things.
anarthatva |tva| n. uselessness.
anarthadandavrata [dandavrata] n. jn. the absence of gratuitous sin, a meritorious vow [guṇavrata].
anarthyá [neg. arthya] amnf anarthyā useless, worthless; without purpose; without meaning; syn. anarthaka.
anarha [neg. arha] amnf anarhā unworthy; undeserving.
anarhat [neg. arhat] amnf anarhantī who does not deserve (punishment or reward) | unworthy; inadequate.

Anala [an₁alam] m. myth. ["insatiable"] np. of Anala, the Fire, one of the 8 Treasures [vasu]; epith. of Agni symbolizing the power of duration | astr. np. of Anala "Longevity", personifying the 50th year of a life cycle [saṃvatsara] | med. digestion; gastric juice. jatharānalajīrņavātāpidānavasya [K.] (Agasti) whose gastric juice digested the demon Vātāpi.
analoṣṇa [uṣṇa] amnf analoṣṇā burning like Fire.
analpa |neg. alpa| amnf analpā |“not just a little” | many, numerous; very.
analpaghoṣa [ghoṣa] amnf analpaghoṣā very noisy.
analpamati [mati] amnf excessively intelligent.
analpamanyu [manyu] amnf very angry.
anavakāśa [priv. avakāśa] amnf ana vakāśā inopportun; which does not occur | gram. inapplicable.
anavakāśatva |tva| n. gram. inapplicability.
anavagīta [neg. avagīta] amnf ana vagītā not blamed, not ridiculed | not timid.
ánavacchitti [opp. avacchitti] f. uninterrupted.
anavacchinna [neg. avacchinna] amnf anavacchinnā uninterrupted | math. not intersected without limit; immoderate | indiscriminate. anavacchinnahāsa continuous or excessive laughter.
anavaccheda [priv. avaccheda] amnf avacchedā not delimited, not circumscribed; indiscriminate. anavacchedena adv. entirely, without discrimination.

Anavatapta [neg. avatapta] m. bd. np. of a mythical serpent | bd. np. of the marvelous lake Anavatapta "which does not warm up", located in the Himālaya (Mānasasarovara); it gives birth to 4 rivers (not. the Satadru) "whose waters release mud of sins"; also called Rāvaṇahrada; it is represented at Angkor by the Neak Pean.

Anavatapta [gāthā] f. bd. np. of the Anavatap tagāthā "Songs of Lake Anavatapta", a collection of autobiographies of disciples of the Buddha explaining the evolution of their karma in previous existences.
anavadyá [neg. avadya] amnf ana vadyā irreproachable, immaculate, without defect, without reproach.
anavadyānga [anga₁] amnf anavadyāngī whose body is without defect.
anavabodha [opp. avabodha] m. in understanding.
anavama [opp. avama] amnf anavamā not inferior | elevated; high; noble.
anavamarśam [neg. avamarśam] adv. in order not to come into contact.
anavayava [neg. avayava] amnf ana vayavā unbreakable; primitive.
anavara [neg. avara] amnf non-inferior anavarā | excellent.
anavarata [neg. avarata] amnf anava ratā incessant. anavaratam adv. incessantly.
anavalokayat [neg. avalokayat] amnf anavalokayatī without observing, without looking.
anavasara [opp. avasara] m. unfavorable moment; not. intercalary period of doubling of the month āṣāḍha; during this period the deities of Purī are confined, between snānapūrņimā and rathayātrā.
anavasāda |opp. avasāda| m. accomplishment of one's tasks without allowing oneself any rest.
anavasthā |opp. avasthā₂| f. instability; chaos | phil. infinite regression.
anavasthāna [priv. avasthāna] amnf anavasthānā unstable — m. wind — n. instability.
anavasthiti [opp. avasthiti] f. grammatical instability, vicious circle, infinite regression.
anavāpta [neg. avāpta] amnf anavāptā not obtained.
anavāpti [opp. avāpti] f. non-obtaining.
anavāyá [priv. avāya] amnf anavāyā uninterrupted; who does not submit.

anavekṣa [priv. avekṣā] amnf anavekṣā rude, inconsiderate | inattentive — f. anavekṣā lack of consideration. anavekṣam adv. in a thoughtless manner; without taking into account. anavekṣamāṇa amn inattentive; indifferent; inattentive.
anaśana |opp. aśana₂| n. fasting; suicide by fasting — priv. amnf ánaśanā who does not eat, who fasts.
ánaśanatā [tā] f. fasting.
ánaśita [opp. aśita] n. young.
ánaśnat [neg. aśnat] amnf anaśnatī not eating.
anaśrú [priv. aśru] amnf without tears; who does not cry.
anaśvá [priv. aśva] amnf anaśvā without a horse.
anașța [neg. nașța] amnf anașțā which is not lost; not destroyed, unharmed — iic. which is not deprived of (ifc.).
anastapasu | pasu | amnf whose herd is unaffected.
ánas [abstr. an₂] n. char; chariot, cart (for heavy transport) | lat. onus; fr. onereux.
anasūya [neg. asūya] amnf anasūyā not envious; benevolent — f. cf. anasūyā.
anasūyaka [ka] amnf anasūyikā not envious; benevolent.

anasūyā [f. anasūya] f. absence of greed, covetousness, jealousy; benevolence | myth. np. of Anasūyā "Benevolent" daughter of Dakṣa, wife of Atri; [BrP.] she appeased Śīlavatī who, to spare Ugraśravā, had prevented the rising of the Sun; as a reward, the trimūrti was reincarnated as her children Candra, Dattātreya and Durvāsā; |BvP.| Brahmā, Hari and Sambhu visited Atri to grant his wishes, but he was immersed in the contemplation of brahman; They fell in love with Anasūyā and tried to seduce her, but she cursed them to be the laughingstock of men until they were reincarnated as her sons.
anasūyu |neg. asūyu| amnf not envious.
anasta |neg. asta | amnf anastā non dis paru; unrecumbent (star) | uninterrupted.

anastaruc | ruc₂ | amnf whose brilliance does not weaken. tam śriyā ghanayānastarucā sāratayā tayā | yātayā tarasā cārustanayānaghayā śritam | | [SPV.] II (Kṛṣṇa) was embraced fervently by Srī who arose swiftly, she the irreproachable one with the lovely breast, with unalterable beauty (palindrome in syllables).
anahaṃvādin [neg. ahaṃvādin] amnf anahaṃvādinī without pride.
anahamkāra var. anahankāra opp. ahaṃkāra m. absence of selfishness, humility — priv. altruistic amnf anahamkārī; modest.
anahamkṛta var. anahankṛta |neg. ahamkṛta] amnf anahamkṛtā without pride.
anahamkṛti var. ahankṛti absence of selfishness, humility.
anā form of the names of causes f.
anāgacchat [neg. āgacchat] amnf āgacchantī by not coming.

anāgata |neg. āgata| amnf anāgatā not (yet) happened; to come, future; imminent | bd. |Mahāyāna| qualifies a coming buddha, such as Maitreya | that has not happened, avoided — n. the future; opp. yāta. astyatītām astyanāgatam [buddha] The past exists, the future exists.
anāgatavaṃśa | vaṃśa | mr. bd. chronicle of the future Buddha Maitreya.
anāgatavaṃśadeśanā [deśanā] f. bd. n.p. from the Anāgatavaṃśadeśanā “Announcement of the coming of the future Buddha (Maitreya)”, text from the Mahāyāna.
anāgatavat [vat] amnf anāgatavatī relating to the future.
anāgatavidhātṛ | vidhātṛ | amnf anāgata vidhātrī organizer of the future | foreseeing, who foresees future needs — n. premonition.
ánāgas [priv. āgas] amnf without sin, innocent.
anāgastvá |tva| n. innocence, absence of sin.
anācāra [opp. ācāra] m. bad conduct; immorality; repugnant custom | soc. custom particular to a community, but not in conformity with the teachings of smṛti .
anāḍhya [neg. āḍhya] amnf anāḍhyā poor.
anādhyatā [tā] f. poverty.
anātma iic. anātman.
anātmajña [jña] amnf anātmajñā who lacks wisdom; ignorant | foolish; stupid. mā tāvat anātmajñe Foolish one! What have you done?
anātmalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. lit. np. of the Anattalakkhanasutta, "Proof of the Non-Existence of the Self", work of the bd. pāli canon.
anātmavāda [vāda] m. bd. doctrine of the non-existence of the Self.

anātman [neg. ātman] m. that which is not Self; another | bd. non-existence of the Self; bd. doctrine of the denial of the Soul; syn. nairātmya — priv. amn non-spiritual, material | devoid of consciousness; devoid of understanding || pali anatta.
anātha [priv. nātha] amnf anāthā without a guardian, without a protector; orphan | without resources, poor, indigent — f. anāthā widow.

anādara [opp. ādara] m. disinterest; in difference | lack of consideration, contempt; defiance; insult. anādare adv. notwithstanding; although; despite, disregarding. saṣṭhī ca anādare gram. [Pāṇini] The genitive (absolute) can also be used in the sense of "in spite of".
anādi [priv. ādi] amnf without beginning (said not. of the Veda); existing from all eternity | gram. said of a suffix not mentioned in the class of primary affixes uṇādi.
anāditva [tva] n. phil. the state of existing from all eternity.
anādinidhana | nidhana | amnf anādinidhanā phil. which has neither beginning nor end; eternal.
anādimat [mat] amnf anādimatī phil. which has no beginning.
anādividyā [vidyā] f. phil. original ignorance.
anādṛtya [neg. ādṛtya] amnf anādṛtyā not respectable — abs. ind. without paying attention to.
anādyanta |priv. ādyanta| amnf anādyantā without beginning or end — m. myth. epith. of Śiva.
anādhṛṣṭi [priv. ādhṛṣṭi] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the "unassailable" prince vṛṣṇi anādhṛṣṭi, son of Ugrasena.
anādhṛṣyá [neg. ādhṛṣya] amnf anādhṛṣyā unapproachable, unassailable.
anāmaka [neg. nāmaka] amnf anāmakā anonymous | infamous, unspeakable — m. intercalary month (to catch up with the solar year) — n. hemorrhoids.
anāman [priv. nāman] amnf anāmnī anonymous | infamous, unspeakable.
anāmatva [tva] n. anonymity.
anāmayá [priv. āmaya] amnf anāmayā well, in good health | healthy, wholesome — mn good health. apyanāmayam rājñah how is the king?
anāmayitnú [neg. āmayitnu] amnf that does not make sick; healthy | that heals; curative.
ánāmikā [anāmika] f. auricular ["the anonymous"].
anāmiṣa [priv. āmiṣa] amnf anāmiṣā without fruit, fruitless, sterile; disinterested | without meat, non-meat.
anāyaka [priv. nāyaka] amnf anāyakā which has no leader | anarchic.
anāyatta [neg. āyatta] amnf anāyattā independent.
anāyattavṛttitā |vṛttitā| f. fact of having an independent existence.

anāyāsa [opp. āyāsa ] m. ease, comfort | idleness — priv. amnf anāyāsā easy, comfortable. anāyāsena adv. easily. anāyāsena maraṇaṃ vinā dainyena jīvitam | antakāle ca Govinda smaraṇaṃ dehi me tava || O Govinda, grant me a peaceful death, a life without distress, and on the day of my death the remembrance of You.
anāyudhá [priv. āyudha] amnf anāyudhā without weapons, without defense.
anāyuṣya [neg. āyuṣya] amnf anāyuṣyā unhealthy; poisoned, deadly, fatal.
anārabhya |neg. ārabhya| amnf anārabhyā which should not be undertaken |impossible to undertake. hi vacanaśatenāpy anārabhyo'rthah śakyo na
vidhātum [Sābarabhāsya] One cannot enjoin someone to perform an impossible act, even with 100 in conjunctions.
anārambha [priv. ārambha] amnf anārambhā without beginning — absence m. absence of origin; no beginning.
anāruhya [neg. āruhya] adv. without having mounted.

anārya [neg. ārya] amnf anāryā disloyal, treacherous; ignoble, vile, base | foreign, barbarian | soc. person of low caste, who cannot offer Vedic sacrifice. anāryāh kutra vasanti where do the excluded live?
anāryajuṣṭa [opp. āryajuṣṭa] amnf anāryajustā not suitable for a nobleman.

anāvṛta [neg. āvṛta] amnf anāvṛtā uncovered; undressed | open, not concealed | unlimited; free. yatra sthitamidam sarvam kāryam yasmācca nirga tam | tasyānāvṛtarūpatvānna nirodho 'sti kutracit | [Spandakārikās] That in which this All is established, and from which it is issued, by its free nature, it can encounter no obstacle.
ánāvṛtta [neg. āvṛtta] amnf anāvṛttā not agitated; intact.
anāvṛtti [opp. āvṛtti] f. rnonetour; non repetition.
anāvṛṣṭi [opp. āvṛṣṭi] f. absence of rain; drought.
anāśin₁ [neg. nāśin] amnf anāśinī imperishable.
anāśin² [neg. āśin] amnf anāśinī who does not eat.
anāśramin [neg. āśramin] amnf anāśraminī soc. who does not follow the stages of Brahmanical life.

anāśrita [neg. āśrita] amnf anāśritā detached, disengaged; delivered; free | independent, autonomous — m. phil. [Tantra] np. of Anāśritaśiva, the free Subject, ultimate mode of existence [tattva] |Anuttara|.
anāsadita [neg. āsadita] amnf anāsaditā not met; not obtained | that which did not happen, that which did not occur; non-existent.
anāstha [priv. āsthā₂] amnf anāsthā unexpected.
anāsvādita [neg. āsvādita] amnf anāsvāditā not tasted, not appreciated.
anāhata [neg. āhata] amnf anāhatā "unstruck" (said of a primordial sound); inau dible, ineffable — m. phil. the Subtle sound; its seat is anāhatacakra.

anāhatacakra [cakra] n. phil. [Tantra] 4th chakra of yoga, located at the level of the heart; it is represented by a lotus of 12 golden petals; two interlaced triangles there symbolize the element of air, and bear the bījamantra 'yam'; this chakra controls the sense of touch; from this center emanates the Subtle sound.
ani forms names f. from the full degree [guna] of a root.
anicchā [opp. icchā] f. absence of desire; indifference.
Anicchāsena [senā] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Anicchāsena, younger brother of Indīvarasena; he had been the vidyādhara Rūpasena in a previous life.
anit [priv. it] nota. gram. said of roots conjugated without an intercalary 'i' (opp. set).

anitya [neg. nitya] amnf anityā perishable, destructible; ephemeral, impermanent; inconstant; instantaneous | uncertain; indefinite; indecisive gram. irregular | pali anicca. anityam adv. from time to time, exceptionally | always, eternally; continuously, regularly, every day. sarvasamskārā anityāh bd. [Sarvāstivāda] all phenomena are impermanent.
anityatā [tā] f. bd. impermanence | gram. optionality.
anityatva |tva| n. impermanence; indecision, in uncertainty, indefiniteness gram. presumed optionality of a sūtra.
anidra [priv. nidrā₂] amnf anidrā awake; sleep-deprived — f. anidrā waking state; lack of sleep.
anityasamāsa [samāsa] m. gram. compound word fa optional, whose paraphrase composes the meaning of the components; opp. nityasamāsa, syn. vaikalpika samāsa.
anindita [neg. nindita] amnf aninditā irreproachable; virtuous.
aninditatva [tva] n. state of irreproachability.
anindra [priv. Indra] amnf anindrā véd.
barbarian [dasyu] "who does not honor Indra".
anibhṛta [neg. nibhṛta] amnf anibhṛtā public, blatant | immodest; bold, intrepid violent, intense.
animiṣa [priv. nimiṣa] amnf animiṣā who does not blink; with a fixed gaze; vigilant — m. myth. god ["with a fixed gaze"] | fish. animisam with vigilance.
animisalocana [locana] amnf animisalocanā whose eyes do not blink.
animiṣākṣa [akṣa] amnf animiṣākṣī with a fixed gaze (said of the gods).
animeṣa [priv. nimeṣa] amnf animeṣā cf. animişa. animeșam with vigilance. animesalocanah with a fixed gaze.
aniyata [neg. niyata] amnf aniyatā irregular; uncontrolled, unregulated; indeterminate, am bigu | uncertain, lax, doubtful; incorrect | gram. (dependency) unilateral; syn. utthāpya₁.
aniyama [opp. niyama] m. absence of rule, non-obligation | non-compliance with discipline; irregularity; uncertainty.
aniyāmaka [neg. niyāmaka] amnf aniyāmikā phil. [Nyāya] which does not control.
aniravasita [neg. niravasita] amnf aniravasitā soc. non excluded (said of a śūdra or respectable stranger, whose touch does not permanently pollute a container).
anirukta [neg. nirukta] amnf aniruktā unexplained; indistinct, structureless, indefinite; unlimited | ved. the ineffable, 1st level of language — n. cf. aniruktagāna.

aniruktagāna [gāna] n. ved. chants of the Sāmaveda intoned with meaningless syllables to hide their meaning from the uninitiated | soc. inarticulate sounds emitted in trance during the rituals of returning to the original chaos of the embryo during carnival periods.

Aniruddha [neg. niruddha] amnf ani ruddhā autonomous, free to act, who does not encounter an obstacle | myth. np. of Aniruddha "who manifests himself without obstruction", son of Pradyumna; he married Uṣā₁, and Vajra is their son; in the pañcarātra tradition he is deified as an aspect [vyūha] of VāsudevaViṣṇu; in the spiritual heaven he is the direction of the North | hist. np. of Aniruddha₁, author of a commentary [vṛtti] on the Sāṃkhyasūtra | bd. np. of Aniruddha₂, 21st Kalkī king of Sambhala, supposed to be our contemporary.

anirdiṣṭa [neg. nirdiṣṭa] amnf anirdiṣṭā unspecified, unspecified; indefinite. kvānirdistakāraņam gamyate where are you going without a defined purpose? anirdistāh pratyayā bhāve bhavanti [Paribhāsendu śekhara Unless explicitly specified, a suffix denotes the completed action of the verb.
anirdeśya [neg. nirdeśya] amnf anirdeśyā inexplicable; indefinable.
anirvacanīya [neg. nirvacanīya] amnf anirvacanīyā inexplicable, indescribable, impossible to specify | phil. of which nothing can be affirmed; not. brahman | of which one should not discuss.
anirvacanīyakhyāti [khyāti] f. phil. [Vedānta] theory of the perception of the inexplicable (only the absolute substrate | brahman | being real).
anirvacanīyatā [tā] f. phil. [Vedānta] inexplicability of the world; illusion of the phenomenal world |phil. uncertainty about the existence or non-existence of the created Universe.
anirviṇṇa [neg. nirviṇṇa] amnf anirviṇṇā not discouraged; not depressed; serene. sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo 'nirvinnacetasā [BhG.] Yoga should be practiced with resolve and in a serene state of mind.
anirveda [opp. nirveda] m. self-confidence; assurance. anirvedah śriyo mūlam Courage is the main attraction in the eyes of women.
anila [an₂ila] m. Wind | myth. np. of anila, the Wind, one of the 8 Treasures [vasu]; cf. Vāyu, Pavana, marut | med. rheumatism, disorder of the humors.
anivārita [neg. nivārita] amnf anivāritā not prevented, permitted.
anivārya [neg. nivārya] amnf anivāryā which must not be prevented; inevitable, irresistible.
aniviśamāna [neg. niviśamāna] amnf aniviśamānā without rest.
aniveśaná [priv. niveśana] amnf aniveśanā homeless, which is not established.
aniśa [priv. niśa] amnf aniśā ininter
broken ["without night"]. aniśam adv. always (without stopping). সনিষ্ট aniṣṭa [neg. iṣṭa₁] amnf aniṣṭā undesired; unpleasant | bad, wrong, faulty; disapproved; forbidden.
anistacintana [cintana] n. bad thought.
anistatva [tva] n. undesirability; fault; prohibition gram. non-derivability by grammar.
aniṣṭvā [neg. iṣṭvā] adv. without having sacrificed.

ánīka [an₂īka] n. face, countenance; (figuratively) face | cutting face (of a knife, of an axe) | forehead; (synecdoche) troop, army corps. anīkavidāraņa [vidāraņa] m. [“that which breaks an army” | np. of prince.
anīkinī [in] f. army division, comprising 2187 (3⁷) elephants and chariots, 6561 cavalry and 10935 fan tassins (i.e. 27 battalions [vāhinī]).
ánīḍa [priv. nīḍa] amnf anīḍā which has no nest | not localized; incorporeal | myth. epith. of Agni the incorporeal.
anītijña [neg. nītijña] amnf anītijñā ill-mannered, indiscreet, who behaves badly.
anītiśāstrajña [neg. nītiśāstrajña] amnf anītiśāstrajñā ignorant in politics.
anīdṛśa [neg. īdṛśa] amnf anīdṛśī different. na kadācid anīdrśam jagat phil. [Nyāyamañjarī] The world is never different from what we see of it.
anīpsita [neg. īpsita] amnf anīpsitā unwanted, undesirable | gram. qualifies an object [karman] discarded.
anīya forms pfp. of obligation or necessity.
anīyar nota. gram. suffixe kṛt₂ du pfp. en anīya.
anīśa [priv. īśa] amnf anīśā who is not master of (g.); powerless | who has no master; free — f. anīśā powerlessness.
ánīśvara [priv. īśvara] amnf anīśvarī without master; atheist | supreme | non-divine.

Anu adv. along, towards; behind, following, with, according to, after, in accordance with, in imitation of (acc.) | later, behind; again, then. . ācāryam Anu following the master. anujyestham beginning with the eldest. nadīm Anu sthitā senā the army stands along the river. anvarjunam yoddhārah the warriors are inferior to Arjuna. homam Anu vṛṣṭo devaḥ it rained, following the offering.

Anu₁ |Anu| m. man nonārya | myth. np. of King Anu or Anudruhyu "younger brother of Druhyu", son of Yayāti and Sarmiṣṭhā, younger brother of Puru and elder of Druhyu; he received as his share the North | pl. myth. the Anavas, the foreigners of the North; the Iranians.
anuka [ka] amnf anukā who has a keen desire for — m. lover.
anukath [Anukath] v. [10] pr. (anuka thayati) pp. (anukathita) repeat.
anukamp [Anukamp] v. [1] pr. r. (anukam pate) pp. (anukampita) to feel compassion for, to take pity on someone.
anukampā [act. anukamp] f. compassion, pity. anukampāyām gram. with a sense of compassion. śrīvyā anukampayā by the grace of the Goddess.
anukampin [agt. anukamp] amnf anukampinī compassionate, one who shows compassion.
anukaraṇa [act. anukṛ] n. imitation; res semblance | gram. onomatopoeia.
anukarṣa [act. anukṛṣ] m. attraction | invocation | gram. attraction of a sūtra by a later sūtra | procrastination; delay.
anukarṣaṇa [act. anukṛṣ] n. cf. anukarṣa.
anukāra [act. anukṛ] m. resemblance; imitation.
anukārin [agt. anukṛ] amnf anukāriņī imitator, copyist; who conforms to (iic.).
anukārya [pfp. [1] anukṛ] amnf anukāryā to imitate; (theatrical role) to play, to interpret — n. affair which follows.
anukīrṇa [pp. anukṛ] amnf anukīrṇā full; piled up; in a crowd.
anukīrt [anukīrt] v. [10] pr. (anukīrtayati) to mention, to tell.
anukīrtana [act. anukīrt] n. publication, narrative; representation.

anukūla [anukūla] amnf anukūlā "on his side" | favorable, pleasant, in accordance with, kind; gentle, friendly, amiable; opp. pratikūla | astr. said of a favorable celestial conjunction — ifc. in accordance with, in agreement with, favorable to, which helps (iic.) | gram. [Nyāya] in order to (in semantic analysis [śabdabodha]) — n. act of following the current or the slope | favor.
anukūlatva |tva| n. kindness; friendship; favor; conformity.
anukūlatva [tva] n. id.
anukṛ [anukṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (anukaróti) pp. (anukṛta) pfp. (anukṛtya) to imitate, to copy (acc. g.); to equal; to return the favor.
anukṛ [anukṛ] v. [6] pr. (anukirati) pp. (anukīrṇa) to scatter around, to fill.
anukṛta [pp. anukṛ] amnf anukṛtā imitated, copied; made similar to.
anukṛti [act. anukṛ] f. imitation; copy; conformity.
anukṛtya [pfp. [1] anukṛ] amnf anu krtyā which can be imitated.
anukṛṣ [anukṛṣ] v. [1] pr. (anukárṣati) pr. r. (anukarṣate) pp. (anukṛṣṭa) drag, pull; attract — ca. (anukarṣayati) to attract.
anukṛṣṭa [pp. anukṛṣ] amnf anukṛṣṭā attracted, uprooted; plowed | gram. implied by a later sūtra.
anukta [opp. ukta] amnf anuktā which is not said.
anukram [anukram] v. [1] pr. (anukrāmati) pp. (anukrānta) to go towards; to follow (a path) to enumerate.
anukrama act. anukram m. succession, list; order, method | table of contents of a work. anukramam var. anukramāt, anukrameņa adv. se lon the rank, in the correct order.

anukramaṇa [act. anukram] n. the act of following methodically, enumeration — f. anu kramanī lit. index of Vedic hymns, giving the first word of each hymn, the number of verses, the name of the poet, the deities invoked, and the meter. anukramaņikā |ika| f. cf. anukramaņī.
anukrānta [pp. anukram] amnf anukrāntā who makes a decision | enumerated, listed; done in order; read | mentioned in the anukramaṇī.
anukriyā [act. anukr] f. imitation.
anukrīḍ [anukrīḍ] v. [1] pr. r. (anukrīḍate) to play.
anukrośa [anukrośa] m. tenderness; pity.

anuvyavasā [anuvyavasā] v. [4] pr. (anu vyavasyati) pp. (anuvyavasita) to perceive.
anuvyavasāya [act. anuvyavasā] m. phil. [Nyāya] awareness of cognition; reflective cognition.

Anuvyākhyāna [anuvyākhyāna] n. lit. section of a brāhmaṇa text explaining an obscure passage from another section | lit. np. of the Anuvyākhyāna, supplement to the Vaishnava commentary on the Brahmasūtra by Madhva; cf. Nyāyasudhā.
anuvraj [anuvraj] v. [1] pr. (anuvrajati) pp. (anuvrajita) to follow; to accompany; to pay homage to. mṛgā mṛgaiḥ saṃgamanuvrajanti ["the deer seem with the deer"] that which resembles itself seems.
ánuvrata [anuvrata] amnf anu vratā faithful to his vow, to his commitments; loyal, obedient; devoted to (acc.).
anuśatika [anuśatika] amnf anuśatikā (bought) with a hundred.

anuśáya [act. anuśī] m. importance (attached to); attachment, dependence | phil. consequence of an act causing the transmigration of the soul | regret, repentance, remorse; resentment, hatred; annulment of a contract.
anuśáyāna [agt. anuśī] amnf anuśayānī who repents, who regrets — f. anuśayānā lit. heroine of the theatre who suffers from the absence of her lover.
anuśās [anuśās] v. [2] pr. (anuśāsti) pp. (anuśiṣṭa, anuśasta) to teach, to advise.
anuśāsana [act. anuśās] n. teaching; advice; instruction | precept, commandment — ifc. treatise on; rule concerning (iic.).
anuśāsanaparvan [parvan] n. bed. n.p. of the Anuśāsanaparva, 13th book of the Mah., “of instruction”.
anuśāsita [pp. anuśās] amnf anuśāsitā directed, governed | defined by a rule.
anuśāsitṛ [agt. anuśās] amnf anuśāsitrī who governs, who directs; who instructs.
anuśikṣ [anuśikṣ] ca. (anuśikṣayati) pp. (anuśikṣita) to instruct; learn something. to sb. (2 acc.
anuśiṣṭa [pp. anuśās] amnf anuśiṣṭā taught, revealed.
anuśī [anuśī₁] v. [2] pr. r. (anuśete) v. [1] pr. r. (anuśayate) pp. (anuśayita) to lie down on; to rest in; to attach importance to | to feel remorse, to regret.
anuśīlana [anuśīlana] n. practice assi due, incessant study (not. of knowledge [śāstra]); devotion.
anuśuc [anuśuc₁] v. [1] pr. (anuśocati) pp. (anuśocita) to weep, to bitterly regret someone. (acc.) | to sympathize with, to lament for (acc.) — ca. (anusocayati) to deplore.
anuśoka [act. anuśuc] m. sorrow, grief | regret; repentance, remorse.
anuśocita [pp. anuśuc] amnf anuśocitā deplored, regretted. अनुসূ anuśru [anuśru] v. [5] pr. (anuśṛṇoti) pp. (anuśruta) to hear repeatedly (not. Veda).
anuśruta [pp. anuśru] amnf anuśrutā transmitted by the Veda.
anuṣakta [pp. anuṣañj] amnf anuṣaktā that attaches to; linked to, connected to.
anuṣaṅga [act. anuṣañj] m. adhesion; connection; association, coalition | gram. co occurrence phil. causality, cause-and-effect relationship.
anuṣaṅgika [ika] amnf anuṣaṅgikā which follows | connected; inherent; concomitant.
anuṣaṅgin [agt. anuṣañj] amnf anuṣaṅgiṇī attached to, connected to | common, usual.

anuṣañj [Anusañj] pp. (anuṣakta) ps. (Anușajjate) to be attached to, to take care of (loc.). anuṣṭubh₁ [Anustubh₁] v. [1] pr. (anustobhati) Vedic to celebrate together (not. a sāman). anuṣṭubh₂ [Anustubh₁] f. [nom. anuṣṭup] family of homosyllabic phonic meters |samavṛtta| of 4 lines of 8 syllables; it is the meter of the śloka, the epic verse par excellence; in its usual form, each pāda has its 5th syllable short, the 6th long and the 7th alternating long and short | math. symb. the number 8 | myth. n.p. of the horse Anustup, harnessed to the chariot of Sūrya. pañcamam laghu sarvatra saptamam dvicaturthayoḥ | guru ṣaṣṭhaṃ ca jānīyāt śesesvaniyamo matah | [Chandomañjarī] self definition of anustubh₂.

anuṣṭhā [Anusthā₁] v. [1] pr. (anutiṣṭhati) pr. r. (anutisthate) pp. (anusthita) pfp. (anustheya) to follow, accomplish; to obey, execute. anutisthātmano niyogam accomplish your task; do your work. anuṣṭhātukāmaḥ (I, you, he) desires to proceed to (acc.).
anuṣṭhāna [act. anuṣṭhā] n. accomplishment, execution; cf. svānusthāna | soc. devotion; observance, rite; religious practice; not. tantric rite of supernatural possession.
anusthāyin [agt. anusthā] amnf Anușthāyinī who acts, who accomplishes.
anuṣṭhita [pp. anuṣṭhā] amnf anuṣṭhitā practiced, carried out, accomplished, executed; established.
anustheya [pfp. [1] anusthā] amnf anuṣṭheyā to execute; to accomplish — n. ["that which must be executed" | commission, mandate.
anusvadhám [Anusvadhā] adv. of his own free will.
anusaṃkal var. anusaṅkal [Anusaṃkal] v. [10] pr. (anusaṃkaláyati) pp. (anusaṃkalita) to lead, to lead.
anusáṃtati var. anusantati [act. anusamtan] f. continuation, diffusion, expansion.
anusaṃtan var. anusantan [Anusaṃtan] v. [8] pr. (anusamtanoti) pp. (anusamtata) to proliferate; to spread, to extend.

anusaṃdhā var. anusandhā [Anusaṃdhā₁] v. [3] pr. (anusaṃdadhāti) ps. (anusaṃdhīyate) to explore, inspect; to inquire about; to attend to; to consider, deliberate; to compose, prepare, arrange; to aim; to plan. prakṛtam prastutam anusaṃdhā to get to the point of discussion.
anusamdhāna var. anusandhāna [act. anusandhā] n. investigation, inquiry, inspection; arrangement, planning | plan, scheme; connection; determination.
anusaṃdheya var. anusandheya [pfp. [1] anusandhā amnf anusandheyā which deserves to be investigated or inspected.
anusara [agt. anusr] amnf anusarī that accompanies; that conforms to.
anusaraṇa [act. anusr] n. act of following; act of conforming, agreeing; commitment, agreement | act of seeking, following trail; pursuit — ifc. conformity to (iic.); consequence of (iic.).
anusār [ca. anusr] v. [10] pr. (anusārayati) to pursue.

anusāra [act. anusr़] m. act of following; custom; natural condition | established order, common practice; conformity | authority, legality; prescription. anusāreņa prep. cl. in accordance with, as a result of, according to (g. iic.). tadvacanānusāreņa in accordance with his instructions.
anusāraka [agt. anusr] amnf anusārikā who follows; who conforms to | who investigates, who examines.
anusārin [agt. anusr] amnf anusāriņī which follows; which corresponds, which resembles.
anusṛ [Anusṛ] v. [1] pr. (anusarati) pp. (anusṛta) to follow; to head towards — ca. (anusārayati) to continue. prakṛtaṃ prastutam anusṛ to get to the subject of the discussion.
anusṛta [pp. anusṛ] amnf anusṛtā followed; to what or whom one conforms. jaiminiranusṛtaḥ he conforms to Jaimini.
anusṛti [act. anusṛ] f. conformance; act of following.
anustaraṇa [act. anustṛ] n. soc. funeral ceremony, where the body of the dead is covered with the limbs of a sacrificed cow — f. anustaraṇī soc. sacrificial cow.
anustṝ [Anustṝ] v. [5] pr. (anustṛṇóti) pr. r. (anustṛṇuté) pp. (anustīrṇa) to cover the limbs of a dead person (not. the limbs (i.) of an animal sacrificed during the funeral ceremony).

anusmṛ [anusmṛ] v. [1] pr. (anusmarati) pp. (anusmṛta) to remember; to recall (acc.) — ca. (anusmarayati) ca. (anusmārayati) pp. (anusmārita) to remind someone of something (acc.). tasmāt sarvesu kālesu mām anusmara yudhya ca [BhG.] Thus at every moment think of me, and fight.
anusmṛta [pp. anusmṛ] amnf anusmṛtā remembered; of which one keeps the memory.
anusmṛti [act. anusmṛ] f. (good) memory lit. np. of the Anusmrti, episode of the Mah. (Southern recension) | bd. practices of evocation not. of the pali Buddha anusatti.
anusyūta [anusyūta] amnf anusyūtā intertwined.
anusvāra [anusvara] m. gram. ["(sign) after the vowel"] nasalization phoneme, written in devanāgarī by a dot [bindu] above the syllable, and represented in transcription by m; cf. parasavarņa.
anuhrāda [anuhrāda] m. myth. np. of anuhrāda "who makes a continuous noise", asura son of Hiranyakasipu.
ánūka [related to anvac] mn spine; back, spine | race; family; character | lit. second part of a Vedic stanza [kaṇḍikā]; it follows the in
cipit | pratīka|.
anūkta [pp. anuvac] amnf anūktā recited, studied; heard.
anūcāná [ppft. mo. anuvac] amnf anūcānā scholar; who knows the Veda; who knows how to repeat the Veda and The vedaṣaḍaṅga.
anūccāraṇa [anuuccāraṇa] n. recitation by repeating after the master; opp. pārāyaṇa.
anūdya [pfp. [1] anuvad] amnf anūdyā to explain — m. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] predication of an injunction.
anūpa [anuap] amnf anūpā situated near water; wet, lacustrine, marshy — m. bio. wet ground, marsh; mangrove; riverbank; opp. sthala, jāngala.
Anūru [priv. ūru] amnf without thighs — m. myth. np. of Anūru the "Cripple", epith. of Aruņa charioteer of Sūrya, personifying the dawn.

anūrusārathi [sārathi] m. bed. n.p. from anūrusārathi, epith. of the Sun "whose chariot is driven by Anūru”. tiraścīnamanūrusāratheh gatam prasid dhamūrdhvajvalanam havirbhujah patatyadho dhāma visāri sarvatah kimetadityākulamīkṣitam

janaih | | [SPV.] The Sun travels across the heavens, while it is notorious that the flame of the sacrificial fire rises; but here the light descends, diffusing from all sides; what can this be? This apparition fills the observers with confusion.
anṛṇá [priv. ṛṇa] amnf anṛṇā free from debt or obligation.

ánṛta [priv. ṛta] amnf anṛtā false, men to dream; contrary to the universal order — n. falsehood, lie; bad action, sin | soc. agriculture (which harms the Earth); it is an unsuitable means of subsistence for a brahmin; opp. rta gleaning — m. myth. np. of Anṛta "lie", son of Adharma.
anṛśaṃsa [neg. nṛśaṃsa] amnf anrśamsā sweet, good.
anrśamsya [ya] n. gentleness, kindness.
aneka [neg. eka] pn. mnf anekā [“not unique” | multiple, numerous | pl. anekās several.
anekakleśa [kleśa] m. various ills; various troubles pl. numerous ills.
anekakṣaṇa [kṣaṇa] m. more than once | on numerous occasions.
anekatā |tā| f. multiplicity; diversity.
anekatva [tva] n. multiplicity; plurality.
anekadhā [dhā] adv. several times; often.
anekavat |vat| adv. as plural. anekavarņa [varņa] amnf anekavarņā of numerous colors | math. operation (ifc) with many unknowns.
anekaśas |śas| adv. in large numbers.
anekasamaveta [samaveta] amnf anekasama vetā phil. inherent to multiple entities.
anekasamavetatva [tva] n. phil. property of being present in multiple entities.
anekārtha [artha] amnf anekārthā with varied uses | gram. homophone, homonym; po lysemic. anekārthā hi dhātavah The verbal roots are in fact polysemous.
anekārthaka [ka] amnf anekārthakā lit. qualifies Homonym dictionaries; opp. samānārthaka.
Anekārthakośa | kośa | m. lit. dictionary of homonymes | lit. not. np. of the Anekārthakośa of Mańkha, also called Mankhakośa.
anekārthatilaka [tilaka] m. bed. n.p. from Mahīpa's anekārthatilaka dictionary of homonyms.
anekārthatva [tva] n. gram. polysemy. dhātunām anekārthatvam polysemy of verbal roots.
anekārthadhvanimañjarī [dhvanimañjarī] f. lit. np. from anekārthadhvanimañjarī or Anekārthamanjarī, dictionary of homonyms due to Mahākṣapaṇaka.
anekārthanāmamālā [nāmamālā] f. lit. np. from the anekārthanāmamālā "Garland of homonyms", lexicon of homophones due to Dhanañjaya₁.
Anekārthasamgraha [samgraha] m. bed. n.p. from the Anekārthasamgraha, catalog of homonyms due to Hemacandra.
Anekārthasamuccaya [samuccaya] m. bed. n.p. from the Anekārthasamuccaya, catalog of homonyms due to Sāśvata (6th century?).
anekārthasāra [sāra] m. bed. of np. the Anekārtasāra, dictionary of homonyms due to Dharanidāsa.
anekaśabdadarśana [opp. ekaśabda darśana] n. gram. point of view according to which there are homophones of different meanings; opp. ekaśabdadarśana.
anekānta [neg. ekānta] amnf anekāntā non-exclusive; impartial; uncertain.
anekāntajayapatākā [jayapatākā] f. bed. n.p. from the anekāntajayapatākā "Victory Banner of Impartiality", work of the Jain logician Haribhadra Sūri.
anekāntatā |tā| f. jn. non-exclusivity of points of view, Jain agnosticism.

anekāntavāda [vāda] m. uncertainty, doubt | phil. skepticism, agnosticism | jn. doctrine of the multiform nature of reality by perspective; it postulates that every linguistic expression of reality is necessarily incomplete, and that the different partial points of view [saptabhangī] are mutually inconsistent; it has developed the doctrine of points of view [nayavāda], and opposes the eternalism [nityavāda] of Vedānta and the bd. doctrine of the transient nature of all things [kṣaṇikavāda].
anekāntavādin [vādin] m. skeptic; agnostic; Jain; materialist | ājīvika |.
anekāntaśāsana [śāsana] n. phil. doctrine of Jain agnosticism.
ánedya [nég. nedya] amnf anedyā who should not be blamed; without fault, innocent.
anena [i. ayam] ind. by this, by this — adv. because of this. anena ... vivaksitah gram. by this one means ... anena ... iti vivaksyate gram. id. anena ... sūcitah gram. by this one suggests ...
anenás [priv. enas] amnf not guilty — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Anenā "innocent", son of Kakutstha of the solar lineage |sūryavaṃśa|; he is father of Pṛthulāśva.
anehás [priv. ehas] amnf without rival, incomparable; unattainable — m. [nom. anehā] time.
anaikāntika [neg. aikāntika] amnf anaikāntikā variable, unstable; multiforction — n. phil. [Vaiśeṣika] paradox of the ambiguity of the middle member.
anaiśvarya [opp. aiśvarya] n. weakness | phil. [Sāṃkhya] state of mind [buddhi] of dejection.
anaisthurya [absence naisthurya] n. absence of rudeness.
anoṃkṛta [neg. oṃkṛta] amnf anomkrtā not accompanied by om.
anaucitya [opp. aucitya] n. impropriety, impropriety.

ánta m. proximity, proximity | limit; edge, border, end, end; death; deliverance, solution, outcome — ifc. ending in, which concludes in (iic.); the last of the (iic.) | which has as its purpose or outcome (iic.) | ang. end; all. Ende. ante adv. finally, at the end. antevāsin m. ["who lives in the vicinity"] pupil (living near his master's house).
ántakara | kara₁ | amnf antakarā which marks the end; mortal, destructive.
ántakaraṇa [karaṇa] amnf antakaraṇā mortal; destroy — n. causing death, destroying (iic.).
ántakārin [kārin] amnf antakārinī which causes death; mortal.
ántakāla [kāla₁] m. hour of death; death.
antakṛt | kṛt₂ | amnf which ends — m. dead.
ántakṛddaśā [daśā] f. pl. lit. 8th text of the Jaina canon, biography of lay disciples.
ántagata [gata] amnf antagatā gone to the end, reached the end. yeṣām tvantagatam pāpam but of those whose sin has been eradicated.
ántapāla | pāla | m. road official; border guard | harem guard.
ántavat [vat] amnf antavatī which has an end; limited, perishable — adv. like the end | gram. according to the final (of a word).
ántasvarita | svarita | m. phon. grave accent |svarita| on the last syllable of a word — n. gram. word thus accented.
antādi [ādi] m. du. antādī the beginning and the end | soc. variety of literary game [prahelikā] where one must cite from a large number of sources |samayocitapadyamālikā|.
antah iic. antar.

antaḥkaraṇa [karaṇa] n. phil. [Sāṃkhya] "the inner instrument", consisting of the 3 psychic senses or intellectual functions: the Mind | manas|, the Intellect | buddhi|, and the Self | ahamkāra|; cf. tattva phil. |Vedānta| we add Consciousness |citta|, and we then speak of antahkarana catustaya, the fourfold inner instrument.
antáḥpātá |pāta| m. soc. post in the center of a sacrificial area | gram. insertion of a letter.
antáḥpātin |pātin| ifc. amnf antáḥpātinī inserted, included in | which appears inside of.
antáḥpātrá [pātra] n. interior of a container.
antaḥpihita [pihita] amnf antaḥpihitā hidden inside.
antaḥpīṭha |pīṭha| amnf antaḥpīṭhā soc. which is inside the sacred field.
antaḥpura [pura] n. citadel | soc. private apartment of a prince; harem, women's chamber. sodaśāntahpurah m. (king) who has 16 wives in his harem.
antaḥpurikā |ika| f. woman of the harem.
antaḥsāra [sāra] amnf antaḥsārā solid inside; healthy of heart — n. inner strength.
antahstha [stha] amnf antahsthā median, in intermediate; located in (g. iic.) — m. phon. semi-vowel.
