antodātta | udātta | amnf antodāttā gram. (word) bearing the acute accent at the end.
ántaka [antaka] amnf antakā finalizer; that prepares Death — m. myth. np. of Antaka, Death personified — ifc. that ends; killer of, that eliminates (iic.).
antakatva |tva| n. state of being mortal.
ántama [super. anta] amnf antamā closest, very close; following — m. intimate friend, companion | lat. intamus; fr. intime.

antár [anta] adv. inside, between, in the middle, within | in, between, among, internal to, inside of (loc.) — iic. (ifc.) internal | lat. in ter; fr. interne. antárbhū to be contained; to be inherent; to be in trinsic. antarbhāva included, contained in (loc.); internal; inherent; intrinsic. dantāntah between the teeth.

antaranga [anga₁] amnf antarangā interior, internal; close; essential; intrinsic — n. phil. the internal organ | inner circle, community of intimates; opp. bahiranga | gram. said of a rule whose causes of application are internal to the word, and which has priority over a more external rule called ba hiranga. asiddham bahiraigam antaraige gram. The internal rule has priority over the external rule.
antarangatva |tva| n. gram. metalinguistic rule [paribhāṣā] stipulating that an internal rule [antaranga] takes precedence over a rule
external | bahiranga |.
antarangāri [ari] m. jn. ["enemy from within"] one of the 4 passions [kaṣāya]: anger [krodha], pride [māna₁], confusion [māyā] and greed |lobha|.
antarjāla |jāla| n. mod. Internet.
antarjñāna [jñāna] n. phil. inner knowledge; mystical knowledge.
antarjñānasādhaka [sādhaka] m. mystical.
antardhana [dhana] n. inner wealth; hidden treasure.
antardhí | dhi | m. ved. rim of a wheel; disc of the Moon.
antarbāṣpa | bāṣpa | amnf antarbāṣpā who holds back his tears.
antarbheda | bheda | mr. internal division. antarbhedākulam gṛham house divided into apartments.
antarbhauma [bhauma] amnf antarbhaumī underground.
antaryāga [yāga] m. phil. internal sacrifice.
antaryāmin [yāmin] m. phil. ["internal control"] the soul; [Vedānta] epith. of brahman.
antarlajjā [lajjā] f. modesty, intimate shame.
antarvaktra [vaktra] n. inside of the mouth.
antarvāspa [vāspa] amnf antarvāspā who holds back his tears.

antarvedi [vedi] amnf located inside the sacrificial area — adv. in the sacrificial area — f. geo. delta, not. of the Godāvarī — f. antarvedī geo. region between the Gangā and Yamunā rivers (mod. Doab).

ántara [compar. anta] amnf antarā interior; near, intimate | internal — n. interior, place; middle, contents; interval, difference; distance between two things; period, passage occasion, occurrence, circumstance | safety; guarantee — n. ifc. other than, different from (ii.); other; syn. anya. antaram var. antare adv. inside, between, among; because of, with reference to, with regard to g. acc. . antarena adv. id. | except (acc.). antaratas adv. internally; inside (of g. ). jalāntare adv. in the water. rājāntaram n. another king. gṛhāntarāṇi n. other houses. nyāyāntareņa according to other principles. vanāntarasaṃcārī m. that moves in the woods. nūnam sa lubdho nopāyamantarena vadhyah syāt Truly this beast can only be killed by a stratagem.
antarávāsaka | vasaka₂ | n. bd. monk's underwear; cf. triīvara.
antarātman | ātman | n. phil. the soul; the heart. jāto mamāyam viśadah prakāmam antarātmā my heart is completely satisfied with that.
antarāla |āra| n. Intermediate space | arch. not. vestibule between the garbhagrha and the mandapa of a temple in North India.
antarālaśabda [śabda] m. gram. [Bhartṛhari] component of the principle of meaning |sábda| of a
phrase [vākya] evoked by a word [pada].
ántaratama [super. antara] amnf an taratamā immediate; internal; intimate.
ántaratara [compar. antara] amnf an taratarā closer; very intimate.
antaraya [act. antari] m. impediment, obstruction.
antarayaṇa |act. antari| n. disappearance.

antarā [antar] adv. in the middle; inside; between the two; among; between; on the way | meanwhile; from time to time; for a while | between, during (acc. loc.). antarāntarā from time to time. triśankurivāntarā tiṣṭhan that balances between two positions (like Triśańku). antarā tvām ca mām ca kamandaluh the pitcher is between you and me.
antarābhava | bhava | m. phil. intermediate state (between death and rebirth) | bd. yoga of the intermediate state, a saddharma.
antarābhavadeha [deha] m. phil. [Sāṃkhya] state of the soul between death and reincarnation.
antarāśṛṅgam |śṛṅga| adv. between the horns.
antarāya [agt. antari] m. obstacle.

antari [antari] v. [2] pr. (antareti) pr. r. (antarite) pp. (antarita) to go to the middle; to make di version; to withdraw, to hide; to omit | to exclude from the angle abl. g. | to disappear — v. [1] pr. (antarayati) to interpose; to conceal, to make disappear.
antárikṣa var. antarīkṣa [antarīkṣa] n. at mosphère (Intermediate space between Heaven and Earth) — m. myth. np. d'Antarikṣa the Space, personified as one of the 8 Treasures [vasu].
uro | antarikṣam || ved. O large Space.
antarikṣaga [ga₁] amnf antarikṣagā that goes in the air — m. bird.
antarikṣaloka [loka] m. phil. the world in intermediary between Earth and Heaven.

antárita [pp. antari] amnf antaritā internal; hidden, concealed, protected | gone, disappeared; excluded, prevented — m. math. arithmetic remainder. antariteșu kapoteșu the pigeons having disappeared.
antargaṇa [antargaṇa] n. gram. gaṇa in inclu dans un autre.
antargata [pp. antargam] amnf an targatā part inside, internal; intimate; hidden, disappeared; forgotten | let go (impropriety).
antargam [antargam] v. [1] pr. (antargac chati) pp. (antargata) to interpose | to be included, to be included in | to disappear.
antargāmin [agt. antargam] amnf antargāminī that interposes | included in; internal; hidden, secret | disappeared; forgotten.
antardhā [antardhā₁] v. [3] pr. r. (an tardhātte) to deposit, receive; to hide, conceal. upādhyāyād antardhatte chāttrah The student hides from the master.
antardhāna [act. antardhā] n. disappearance; invisibility; hiding place — m. myth. np. of An tardhāna, son of Pṛthu; Havirdhāna is his son. antardhānam i disappear.
antarhan [antarhan₁] abs. (antarhatya) to save. antarhatya sthitaḥ khalaḥ the wicked left him alive.
ánti [antai] prep. in front of, in front of; Before ; in the presence of, close to, near (g. iic.) | gr. αντι; lat. ante; eng. answer.

antiká [antika] amnf antikā near; in the vicinity | in the vicinity of, in the presence of, beside (abl. g. iic.) — ifc. which completes (iic.) — n. neighborhood; presence; syn. samīpa. antikam adv. up to, near, in the presence of g. iic. . antikāt adv. coming from the vicinity of (g. iic.) | in comparison with (g.). antike adv. near, in the vicinity of, in the presence of (g. iic.). antikena adv. near g. . grahaṇāntika amn ["who completes the acquisition (of knowledge)" | who has finished their studies.
ántigṛha [antigṛha] m. ved. neighborhood of the house; neighbor; extended family.
ántitama [super. anti] amnf antitamā very close; which stands very near.
antitara [compar. anti] amnf antitarā just opposite.
ántitas [adv. anti] adv. very close.
antimá [super. anti] amnf antimā the last || fr. ultimate.
ante [loc. anta] iic.
antevāsa [vāsa₁] m. neighbor; companion.
antevāsin [vāsin₁] amnf antevāsinī who lives at the end; neighbor — m. soc. pupil living near his master's house — ind. antevāsi with the status of pupil.
antya [antaya] amnf antyā last; the lowest; the latest | soc. of the lowest caste; syn. asprśya — ifc. immediately after (iic.) — n. math. ten thousand billion.
antyakarman | karman | n. soc. funeral rites.
antyakriyā | kriyā | f. soc. funeral rites.
antyaja | ja | amnf antyajā soc. of the lowest caste — m. syn. śūdra.
antyajāti [jāti] amnf soc. of the lowest caste.
antyajātitā |tā| f. condition of antyajāti.
antyastrī [strī] f. woman of the lowest caste.

antyānuprāsa [anuprāsa] m. lit. [śabdālaṃkāra] stylistic figure of speech involving the repetition of suffixes, creating a rhythmic effect. antyești [iṣṭi₂] f. soc. funeral ceremony rite; after the deceased is washed, they are dressed in a new garment and adorned with a garland of flowers; they are carried on a stretcher to the cremation ground [śmaśāna] where they are cremated on a pyre lit by the eldest son; an earthenware pot filled with water and pierced is carried by a relative who circles the pyre three times, then it is broken; syn. mṛtyusaṃskāra. স্থান antra n. intestine | pl. antrāṇi bowels, entrails.
andu f. elephant's foot chain | anklet | var. andū id...
andolana n. swaying.

andhá amnf andhā Blind; blinded; that which prevents seeing | dark; secret, occult — ifc. blinded by (iic.) — n. darkness — m. pl. the people of the Andhās — v. [11] pr. (andhayati) to blind. andhīkr to make Blind. andhībhū to become Blind.

Andhaka |ka| amnf andhakā Blind — m. myth. np. of the asura Andhaka "Blind", born from a drop of Shiva's sweat when Parvati covered his eyes with his hands; he was raised by Hiranyaksha, and was crowned king of the demons [asura]; his cousins having conspired to dethrone him, he performed great penances, fasting standing on one leg for 1000 years; he implored Brahma to regain his sight and to be inviolable, both by man, demon, and god, even Vishnu himself; moreover, every drop of his blood shed would recreate him; Brahma granted him this wish, provided that he stated the circumstances of his own death; he chose to die if he fell in love with his mother; He then became a tyrant over the three worlds for millions of years; [Haravijaya] one day he visited Mount Mandara where Shiva was with Parvati; at the end of a long battle Shiva pierced him with his trident, while Devi drank his blood; his desiccated skeleton became Bhrangi; cf. Haravi jaya | pl. race of warriors — f. andhikā night.
andhákāra [kāra] mn blinding darkness.
andhagaja [gaja] m. (copulative) the Blind Man and the Elephant.

andhagajanyāya [nyāya] m. phil. ["maxim of the Blind Man and the Elephant" it explains the contradictions of different blind men in describing an elephant by its parts; Tārānātha Tarkavācaspati says that it expresses the diversity of views on god [Iśvara] by ignorant people.
andhagolāngūla [golāngūla] n. (copulative) the Blind Man and the Cow's Tail.

andhagolāngūlanyaya [nyāya] m. ["maxim of the Blind Man and the Cow's Tail"] parable of a Blind Man looking for his way, to whom a wicked man puts the tail of a cow in his hands, assuring him that it will lead him to his village; it is used to denounce false preachers.
andhátā [tā] f. blindness.
andhátāmisra [tāmisra] m. darkness of the soul — n. myth. [PP.] np. of Andhatāmisra "Darkness", one of the 7 hells.
andhatva [tva] n. blindness.
andhapangu [pangu] m. phil. maxim [nyāya] of the blind and the paralytic; it advocates cooperation between men.

andhaparamparā [paramparā] f. phil. a series of blind speakers transmitting color information | (figuratively) sheep following Panurge. andhaparamparānyāya phil. a metaphor of the blind man leading the blind, which explains that logical reasoning, however correct, does not guarantee the validity of premises; generally applies to people following a common opinion without thinking.
andhavat [vat] adv. like a blind man.
ándhas₁ [abstr. andha] n. ved. darkness; blindness.
ándhas₂ n. ved. soma plant or juice | grassy ground; riverbank | food.

andhu m. well. Andhra m. geo. name of the Andhra country of southern India (Telugu country) | pl. Andhrās its people, the Andhrās | lower caste of hunters — f. andhrī woman of the Andhra country. সেম ánna [ad₁na] n. food, nourishment; boiled rice; cereal | lat. annona; ang. oat. jñānam annam [SS.] Knowledge is nourishment.
annadāna |dāna| n. gift of food; meal of fert.

annadosa | dosa₂ | m. soc. fault committed by violating a food taboo. annapūrņa [pūrṇa] amnf annapūrṇā full of food — f. annapūrņā myth. np. of An napūrņā, epith. of Durgā "Nurse" | geo. mountain range of the Himalayas, which culminates at 8091 in West Nepal.
annaprāśana [prāśana] n. soc. first meal of a child with rice, saṃskāra performed in the sixth month.
annamaya [maya] amnf annamayī formed from food, material.
annamayakośa [kośa] m. phil. [Vedānta] the material envelope, forming with prāṇamayakośa the gross body [sthūlaśarīra].
annarasa [rasa] m. flavor of food | med. [Ayurveda] juice extracted from food; nutrient.
annavat |vat| amnf annavatī provided with food.
annavyavahāra | vyavahāra | mr. soc. permission to share a meal.
annādya |ādya₁| n. food; food brought to prayer.
annādyakāma [kāma] amnf annādyakāmā who wants food.

annambhaṭṭa var. annambhaṭṭa m. hist. np. of the scholar annambhatta; he lived in Andhra in the 16th century; he is the author of the condensed treatise of Vaiśesika and nyāya Tarkasamgraha, and of its commentary the Tarkadīpikā; he is also credited with the Mitākṣarā, commentary on the Aṣṭādhyāyī, and the Ud dyotana, commentary on the Mahābhāṣyapradīpa.
annārthin [arthin] amnf annārthinī who asks for food.

anyá pn. mn anyad f. anyā other, other than (abl. iic.); another, that other one | stranger; different (from (abl.)) | lat. alius; ang. alien; fr. aliéner. anyac ca adv. in addition, moreover. anya ... anya adv. one ... the other. eka ... anya adv. one ... the other. anyasas another, that other one. yad anyat kimcana whatever else.
anyacitta [citta] amnf anyacittā who is thinking about something else, whose mind is elsewhere.
anyatama [tama] amnf anyatamā super. one (among several).

anyatará [tara] pn. mn anyatarad f. anyatarā one of two; either one. anyatarátas adv. on one side or the other; in one way or another | optionally. anyatarasyām gram. by choice; either one. tāsāmanyatarā one of them. grhyatāmanayoranyatarā that one of the two be accepted.
anyatarābhāva [abhāva] m. phil. [nyaya] negation of the alternative (neither one nor the other).
anyathirthikī [tīrthika] amnf anyathirthikī soc. who belongs to another sect; heterodox.
anyadā [dā] adv. at another time, another time | sometimes, occasionally; once | in another case.
anyapada [pada] n. gram. (external) word qualified by a bahuvrīhi compound. anyapadapradhāna gram. exocentric (said of a bahuvrīhi compound).

anyapadārtha [padārtha] amnf anyapadārthā gram. which has another meaning (than the composition of that of its parts); said of a compound word [dvandva] exocentric [bahuvrīhi], but also of certain suffixes forming exocentric derivatives; opp. svārtha.
anyapadārthapradhāna [pradhāna] amnf anyapadārthapradhānā gram. is said of a compound word whose main meaning is exocentric |bahuvrīhi|.
anyapusta | pusta | m. bio. | "fed by another" | Indian cuckoo; syn. kokila.
anyabhṛta [bhṛta] m. bio. ["raised by another"] Indian cuckoo; syn. kokila.
anyamanas | manas | amnf who is thinking about something else, absent | possessed.
anyamanaska |ka| amnf anyamanaskā id.
anyamānasa [mānasa] amnf anyamānasā cf. anyamanas.
anyayoni | yoni | amnf lit. (subject of poetry) "that which has its source elsewhere"; borrowed; opp. ayoni.
anyavāpa [vāpa₂] m. bio. ["that lays eggs in others"] zoo. Eudynamis Orientalis, Indian cuckoo; syn. kokila.
anyaśabdasannidhi | śabdasamnidhi | mr. gram. co rental.
anyahrada | hrada | m. another basin.
anyāpadeśa [apadeśa] m. lit. allegorical epigram.
Anyāpadeśaśataka [śataka] n. bed. n.p. from the collection of poetic allegories Anyāpadeśaśataka by Nīlakantha₂ Dīkṣita.
anyāpoha [apoha] m. phil. [Dinnāga] doctrine of the exclusion of others, defining the reference of a universal by exclusion of particular objects not corresponding to its determination.
anyāpohaviśiṣṭa [viśiṣṭa] amnf anyāpoha viśiṣṭā phil. [bd.] (real object) distinguished among the possible references of a universal, by exclusion of all other concepts.
anyārtha | artha | amnf anyārthā which has another object | gram. which has another meaning — m. matter of another — n. gram. use of a word in an unusual sense.
anyokti [ukti] f. bed. rhet. figure of speech [alamkāra] of indirect praise; syn. aprastutaprasamsā.
anyat iic. anya.
anyatkāma | kāma | amnf anyatkāmā who desires something else.
anyatsthāna |sthāna| amnf anyatsthānā which is located elsewhere.
anyatare [loc. anyatara] ind. in either one.
anyataredyús |dyu| adv. one or the other day.
anyátas [adv. anya] adv. in another direction, otherwise; from another source; in another place, elsewhere — iic. having (ifc.) only on one side.
anyataḥkṣṇút |kṣṇut| amnf sharpened on one side.
anyatodvāra [dvāra] amnf anyatodvārā having doors only on one side.
anyatā [ anyatā ] f. difference.

anyátra | anyatra | adv. elsewhere (than ⟨abl.⟩); in another place, in another | otherwise (than (abl.); in the other case | (ifc.) at another time than (iic.). yadihāsti tadanyatra yannehāsti na tatkvacit [Mah.] What is here is found elsewhere, what is not here is found nowhere. anyatra dharmādanyatrādharmādanyatrāsmātkrtākrtāt anyatra bhūtācca bhavyācca yattatpaśyasi tad vada | [KU.] (Naciketā to Death) That which is outside of good, outside of evil, outside of effect and cause, outside of past and future, this, as you understand it, explains the self.
anyatva [ anyatva ] n. difference.
anyáthā [ anyathā ] adv. otherwise; in another way; in another case; otherwise than it really is, falsely. anyathā bhū to become different; to be altered. nānyathā not otherwise; precisely.
anyáthākhyāti [khyāti] f. phil. [nyāya] theory of error (not. of perception, taking one thing for another); syn. viparītakhyāti; opp. asatkhyāti.
anyáthāvādin [vādin] amnf anyathāvādinī who speaks differently | who speaks of something else; who avoids the subject.
anyáthāsiddha [siddha₁] amnf anyathāsiddhā demonstrated otherwise | falsely established.
anyáthāsiddhi [siddhi] f. false demonstration.
anyāya [priv. nyāya] amnf anyāyā in just; illegal; improper; illogical — m. illegality, irregularity; disorder.
anyāyavartin [vartin] amnf anyāyavartinī who acts unjustly.
anyāyavṛddhi | vṛddhi | f. soc. usurious interest rate.
anyūna [neg. nyūna] amnf Anyūnā par fait — f. Anyūnā myth. np. of the nymph [apsaras] Anyūnā "Perfect".
anye [loc. anya] ind. in another.
anyedyús [dyu] adv. the following day, the next day another day.
anyonya [red. anya] amnf anyonyā each other; reciprocal — n. soc. scholarly debate on the Veda. anyo'nya id. anyonyam var. anyonyatas adv. mutually. anyonyam pratihrcchayah reciprocal love.
anyonyābhāva [abhāva] m. phil. [NN.] ("mutual absence") distinction, non-identity; relative difference; incompatibility; negation |abhāva| as mutual contradiction; opp. tādātmya.
anvac var. anváñc [anuac] amnf
anūcī [m. nom. anvai; n. nom. anvak] directed towards; behind; that follows. anvak adv. behind; coming from the rear — prep. behind, after (acc.).

anvaya [act. anvi] m. succession; descent, family; race; genealogy | connection, association, dependence; correlation; causality | phil. logical chain of causes and effects; inference gram. logical rearrangement of the words of a sentence into phrases; paraphrase of prose verse by simple movement of constituents continuation. viśesanam puraskrtya viśesyam tadlaksanam | kartrkarmakriyāyuktam etad anvayalakṣaṇam | gram. By indicating first the adjectives, then the qualified noun, the agent-patient-verb arrangement characterizes the prose paraphrase.
anvayakleśa [kleśa] m. lit. use of a word order that is difficult to understand.
anvayamukhī [mukhī] f. gram. grammatical commentary using a prose translation with canonical constituent order; cf. daṇḍānvaya.
anvayaracanā [racanā] f. gram. structural analysis of a sentence.

anvayavat [vat] amnf anvayavatī that follows, that derives from | of the same family or race — adv. in view of, in connection with. anvayavyatireka vyatireka n. agreeable and disagreeable | phil. [Nyāya] positive and negative
proposition | rule and exception | gram. contrasting pair | phil. [Jayanta₁] search for the causes and treatment of diseases by dialectic combining positive and negative correlations.
anvayavyatirekin [vyatirekin] amnf anvaya vyatirekinī phil. [Nyāya] which uses both positive inferences and proofs by contradiction.

anvayavyāpti [vyāpti] f. phil. [Nyāya] positive inference; opp. vyatirekavyāpti. yatra yatra hetuh tatra tatra sādhyah phil. (inevitable concurrence between the reason and the goal to be demonstrated) Every instance of the cause entails the corresponding instance of the thesis.
anvayānupapatti [anupapatti] f. gram. inapplicability of the syntactic relationship between words based on their literal meaning, requiring recourse to the
metaphor | lakṣaṇā|.
anvayin [agt. anvi] amnf anvayinī in duit (as a consequence); caused | soc. of the same family.
anvartha [anuartha] amnf anvarthā in accordance with meaning | whose meaning is evident; intelli gible, clear | gram. term whose meaning is in accordance with its etymology.
anvarthagrahana [grahana] n. gram. use of a word in accordance with its meaning.
anvarthanāman [nāman] n. significant name — amnf anvarthanāmnī whose name is significant.
anvarthasamjñā [samjñā₁] f. gram. technical term whose formation conforms to its meaning.

anvākhyā [anuākhyā₁] v. [2] pr. (anvākhyāti) pp. (anvākhyāta) to relate; to explain; to enumerate. saṃskṛtaṃ nāma daivī vāganvākhyātā maharşibhih [Daṇḍī₁] Sanskrit is called the divine language explained by the ancient sages.
anvākhyāna [act. anvākhyā] n. gram. literal explanation; fine analysis.
anvākhyeya [pfp. [1] anvākhyā] amnf anvākhyeyā to describe, to explain.

anvācaya [anuācaya] m. gram. statement of a secondary rule (preceding the default rule) gram. coordination of an action with the main action. anvācaye adv. gram. use of ca for the coordination of verb forms.
anvācayaśiṣṭa [śiṣṭa₂] amnf anvācayaśiṣṭā gram. specified as secondary; opp. pradhānaśiṣṭa.
anvāje adv. in support. anvājekṛ to help, to come in support of.
anvādiś [anuādiś] v. [1] pr. (anvādiśati) pp. (anvādiṣṭa) to show again, to mention again | to repeat, to say again.
anvādiṣṭa [pp. anvādiś] amnf anvādiṣṭā (word) already mentioned, already used gram. anaphora.
anvādeśa [act. anvādiś] m. act of mentioning again; repetition, reiteration | gram. anaphora.
anvādeśaka [agt. anvādiś] amnf anvādeśikā gram. which refers to an antecedent; anaphoric.
anvās [anuās₂] v. [2] pr. r. (anvāste) pp. (anvāsita) abs. (anuvāsya) to sit beside; to live beside | to pay homage; to serve.
anvāsana [act. anvās] n. act of serving someone.
anvāhārya [anuāhārya] m. soc. funeral meal in honor of the manes | pitaras |.
anvāhāryapacana | pacana | m. soc. southern fire of Vedic sacrifice; it is used for the anvāhārya rite; syn. dakṣiṇāgni.
anvi [anui] v. [2] pr. (anvéti) pr. r. (anvite) pp. (anvita) pf. (sam) to follow, to accompany; to imitate; to be guided by (acc.) | to seek; to reach, to touch the goal; to know.
anvita [pp. anvi] amnf anvitā joint, linked to, accompanied by; endowed with, possessing (i. iic.) | which follows; imitated.
anvitābhidhā [abhidhā₂] f. gram. meaning of a sentence from the meaning of words in mutual relation according to their dependencies.
anvitābhidhāvāda [vāda] m. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] school of linguistic philosophy of Prabhākara [prābhākara]; opp. abhihitānvayavāda.

anvitābhidhāna [abhidhāna] n. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] theory of denotation of Prabhākara; it improves the abhihitānvaya doctrine by explaining that the meaning of the sentence is a synthesis which dominates the meaning of the words constituting it.
anvitābhidhānavāda [vāda] m. phil. Prabhākara's doctrine of denotation.
anvitābhidhānavādin [vādin] amnf an vitābhidhānavādinī phil. adherent of this doctrine.

anviṣ [anuiṣ₁] v. [6] pr. (anvicchati) v. [4] pr. (anvisyati) pp. (anvista) to desire, to seek; to aim at. nipuṇamanviṣya seeking carefully. pitaramanviccha seeks your father. sarvato jayam anvicchet | śiṣyādicchet parājayam || One should always seek victory (in debate); but one should desire to be surpassed by one's student. সন্বিষ্ট anviṣṭa [pp. anviṣ] amnf anviṣṭā sought.
anvīkṣ [anuīkṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (anvīkṣate) to follow with eyes, to fix with one's gaze; to keep in sight.
anvīkṣā [act. anvīkṣ] f. examination, investigation | meditation.
anveṣa [act. anviṣ] m. research, investigation.
anveṣaṇa [act. anviṣ] n. research (from g. iic.) — f. anveṣaṇā id.
anveṣin [agt. anviṣ] ifc. amnf anveṣiṇī who searches (iic.).

ap var. ab f. pl. āpas [noun. āpas, acc. Apas, i. adbhis, dat. abl. adbhyas, g. apām, loc. apsu ved. n.p. by Apas The Naiads, water divinities | phil. Waters, one of the 9 substances | dravya₁ | of the vaisika | phil. |Sāmkhya| the |bhūta| element water; his pañcabhūtasthala is Jambukeśvara | lat. aqua; fr. water; hi. Doab, Punjab. āpo jyotir āpo 'mṛtam [Sirā] The waters are Light, The waters are Immortality.
apa pf. separately, out of; without; from; emanating from; opp. upa || gr. alpha pi o; lat. ab; ang. of.
apakarṣa [act. apakṛṣ] m. act of tearing away, removing; suppression; omission; diminution, wear | decline; inferiority; disgrace, infamy | gram. cataphora.
apakāra |act. apakṛ| m. offense, insult; wrong, damage; injury.
apakārin | agt. apakṛ | amnf apakāriṇī that which aggresses, that which causes harm.

apakṛ [apakṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (apakaróti) pp. (apakṛta) pf. (prati) to dismiss; to insult, to offend; to harm someone. (g. loc. acc.) — ca. (apakārayati) to do harm. āpadi yenāpakṛtaṃ yena ca hasitam daśāsu viṣamāsu | apakṛtya tayor ubhayoḥ punar api jātam naram manye | [PR.] I think that the man who returns evil to the one who wronged him in distress, or who mocked him in difficult circumstances, comes back to life, so to speak.
apakṛta [pp. apakṛ] amnf apakṛtā done wrongly; done to hurt or offend | committed as an impure act — n. to hurt; offense.
apakṛṣ [apakṛṣ] v. [1] pr. (apakaṛṣati) pp. (apakṛṣṭa) to tear off; to lay down; to humiliate.
apakṛṣṭa [pp. apakṛṣļ amnf apakṛṣṭā low, vile; insignificant.
apakram [apakram] v. [1] pr. (apakrāmati) pp. (apakrānta) to move away from, to withdraw, to give way.
apakva [neg. pakva] amnf apakvā cru phil. not prepared by yoga; opp. paripakva.
apakṣī [apakṣī] ps. (apakṣīyate) decline; deteriorate; wane (not. moon).
apakhyāti [apakhyāti] f. disgrace; bad reputation, indignity.
apagata |pp. apagam| amnf apagatā gone. mārgenāpagatah left by the way.
apagam [apagam] v. [1] pr. (apagaccati) pp. (apagata) pf. (vi) move away, disappear. apagaccha imp. go away! disappear! apagamyatām asmāt sthānāt leave here!.
apagara [agt. apagr] m. soc. ceremonial invective (of the chief priest during a sacrifice); opp. abhigara | ved. function of invectiver during a sacrifice.
apaguh [apaguh] v. [1] pr. (apagūhati) pp. (apagūdha) to hide, to conceal.
apagṛha [apagṛha] amnf apagṛhā outside the house.
apagṛ [apagṛ₂] v. [9] pr. (abhigṛṇāti) invecti ver.
apagrāma |apagrāma| amnf apagrāmā excluded, banished from a village.
apacá [priv. paca] amnf apacā who doesn't know how to cook.
apacar [apacar] v. [1] pr. (apacarati) pp. (apacarita) to leave | ["to deviate"] to miss, to make a mistake, to sin.
apacarita [pp. apacar] amnf apacaritā gone; disappeared; dead — n. fault, sin; offense.
apacāra [act. apacar] m. departure; absence; defect | sin, crime; misfortune; improper regime.
apaci [apaci] ps. (apacīyate) pp. (apacita) to decrease, to diminish.
apacchid₁ [apachid₁] pp. (apachinna) re decide.
apacchid₁ [obj. apacchid₁] f. portion; co skin.
apaccheda [obj. apacchid₁] m. act of cutting again; cutting, separation.

apacchedanyāya [nyāya] m. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] "Principle of interrupting the chain"; it specifies that a later rite has precedence over an earlier rite, because information cancels out contradictory prior knowledge.
apaṇḍita [neg. paṇḍita] amnf apaṇḍitā sot, ignorant.
apatantra | apatantra | m. med. hysterical attack.
apatantraka |ka| m. id.
ápatighnī [opp. patighnī] f. soc. woman who does not murder her husband.
ápatya [apatya] n. offspring, direct descendants, child; young animal. gargasya apatyam gārgyaḥ Gārgya is a descendant of Garga.
apatyatā [tā] f. childish condition.
apatrap [apatrap] v. [1] pr. r. (apatrapate) to turn away with shame or embarrassment.
apatha [priv. patha] amnf apathā impassable (without path) — n. dead end, bad path. apathodeśah virgin land, without paths.
apathya [neg. pathya] amnf apathyā inappropriate, unsuitable | unhealthy, unsanitary abnormal, incoherent.
apád [priv. pad₂] amnf [m. name. apāt; f. name. apāt, noun. apadī ved. without foot.
apada [priv. pada] amnf apadā without foot gram. (word) uninflected — n. bad place or time.
apadāna [apadāna] n. glorious act; noble work | gram. the thematic role [kāraka] of origin (out of, in the ablative).
apadiś [apadiś₁] v. [1] pr. (apadiśati) pp. (apadiṣṭa) pf. (vi) to indicate, to designate | to claim, to pretext. śiraḥ śūlasparśanamapadiśan pretexting a headache as an excuse.
apadeśa [act. apadiś] m. pretext; disguise, appearance | designation, denomination. apadesena adv. under the pretext of (iic.). anāmayāpadeśena adv. under a pretext of health.
apadravya [apadravya₁] n. bad thing or substance | small object.
apadru [apadru₁] v. [1] pr. (apadravati) to run away.
apanayana [act. ca. apanī] n. removal, extraction; setting aside.
apanī [apanī₁] v. [1] pr. (apanayati) pp. (apanīta) to lift, remove, steal, snatch; to set aside, take away; to extract, draw out — ca. (apanayayati) to remove, set aside, reject, expel.

apanīta [pp. apanī] amnf apanītā stolen, plundered; removed, set aside; deprived (of (abl.)). svamāmsāsrgapanītakṣutpipāsām whose hunger and thirst (have been quenched) by taking his own flesh and blood.
apanutti [act. apanud] f. act of removing, sending away | soc. expiation.
apanud [apanud] v. [6] pr. (apanudati) to raise, to reject.
apanuda [agt. apanud] ifc. amnf apa nudā who removes (iic.).
apapāṭha [apapāṭha] m. lit. erroneous reading of a text. prārthayadhvam ityapapāṭhaḥ prārthayadhvam is an incorrect reading.
apapāda [apapāda] amnf apapādā who has bad feet | without shoes.
apapradāna |apapradāna| n. bribe; corruption.
apabhī [apabhī₂] amnf ["who is without fear" | fearless, courageous.

apabhraṃś [apabhraṃś] v. [1] pr. r. (apabhramsat) v. [4] pr. (apabhrasyati) pp. (apabhraṣṭa) to fall from (abl.), to fall; decay — ca. (apabhramśayati) pp. (apabhramśita) to cause to fall or decay; degrade.

apabhraṃśa [obj. apabhraṃś] m. bed. ["degraded Sanskrit"] is said in Middle Indian dialects | gram. vernacular or non-Sanskrit word (opp. tadbhava); cf. tatsama. apabhramśastu yacchuddham tattaddeśesu

bhāṣitam [Vāgbhaṭa₂] Apabhraṃśa is the purified language spoken in various countries. bhāṣā saṃskṛtāpabhraṃśaḥ bhāṣāpabhraṃśastu vibhāṣā sātattaddeśa eva gahvaravāsināmca prakṛtavāsināṃca | [Abhinavabhāratī] The language
vernacular [bhāṣā] is a dialect [apabhraṃśa] of Sanskrit; the dialects of the language are the
patois [vibhāṣā]; depending on the respective countries, the language of the inhabitants may seem natural or obscure.
apabhramsita [pp. ca. apabhrams] amnf apabhraṃśitā discharged (from a function); deposed.
apabhraṣṭa [pp. apabhraṃś] amnf apabhraṣṭā fallen; deposed | provincial, non-grammatical, incorrect (language) — m. gram. solecism; incorrect use of language.
apaman [apaman] ca. (apamānayati) to despise.
apamāna [act. apaman] mn contempt; humiliation. varam mrtyuh na punarapamānah death is preferable to humiliation.
apamukha [apamukha] amnf apamukhī with a deformed face.
apamūrdhan [apamūrdhan] amnf apamūrdhnī decapitated.
apamṛj [apamṛj] v. [2] pr. (apamārṣṭi) pp. (apamṛṣṭa) erase by rubbing, wipe, clean.
apamṛtyu |apamṛtyu| m. accidental death such; sudden death — adv. by sudden death.
apayaśas [ apayaśas ] n. dishonour.
apayā [apayā₁] v. [2] pr. (apayāti) pp. (apayāta) to go away, to flee.
apara₁ |neg. para| amnf aparā without cond, without rival; unsurpassed.

apara₂ [compar. apa] amnf aparā com par. later, later, beyond, after, which follows; to the West; opp. pūrva | junior, smaller, lower; inferior | other, foreign — pn. m. the other; another pl. apare the others — f. aparā the West [[aparāśakti] phil. [Trika] aparā, individual vital energy — f. aparī pl. the coming days, the future | German aber; English after. aparatas adv. elsewhere. aparathā adv. otherwise. eka ... apara₁ ... one ... the other ... eke ... apare ... some ... others ... aparam ca conj. moreover, in addition. api ca aparam ca bargaining. aparabhāryā second wife.
áparatā [tā] f. distance | posteriority | opposition; difference | proximity.
aparatra [tra] adv. in another place; elsewhere on the other hand (corr. with ekatra on the one hand).
áparatva [tva] n. distance; proximity | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] the property [guṇa] of proximity.
aparavaktra [vaktra] n. phon. name of a varṇavṛtta meter, of patterns na na ra la ga, na ja ja ra; the corresponding mātrāvṛtta meter is the syn. vaitālīya.
aparavidyā [vidyā] f. phil. inferior or erroneous knowledge.
aparaśikha |śikhā| amnf aparaśikhā soc. who wears the reserved lock back (in a ponytail); opp. pūrvaśikha.
áparaspara [para] m. pl. aparasparās one after the other; each other. aparasaparāḥ gacchanti they go one after the other.
Aparāditya [āditya] m. hist. np. of Aparāditya "other Sun", epith. of King Aparārka.
aparānta [anta] m. geo. westernmost region; syn. Konkana — amnf aparāntā who lives in Konkana.
aparāntaka |ka| amnf aparāntikā who lives in the western regions.
aparāpekṣā [apekṣā] amnf aparāpekṣā dependent on another.

Aparārka [arka] m. hist. np. of Aparārka Aparāditya "other Sun", king Šilāhāra of the early 12th century; he is the author of the commentary Aparārkayājñavalkīyadharmaśāstranibandha. Aparārkayājñavalkīyadharmaśāstranibandha [yājñavalkīyadharmaśāstranibandha] m. lit. np. of the Aparārkayājñavalkīyadharmaśāstranibandha, enormous commentary on the Yājñavalkyasmṛti due to king Aparārka; in it he declares the śaiva sects unorthodox.
aparāhṇa [ahna] m. afternoon (last watch of the day); syn. parāhņa.
aparasparasambhūta [opp. paraspa rasambhūta] amnf aparasparasambhūtā not produced one after the other, not produced in order.
aparānmukha [neg. parānmukha] amnf aparāmukhī who does not turn away, who does not turn their back; who faces.
Aparājita [neg. parājita] amnf Aparājitā unconquered; Invincible — m. myth. np. of Aparājita "Invincible", epithet of Viṣṇu or Shiva | myth. np. of Aparājita₁ one of the 4 elephants

cosmic |gajapati| supporting the world — f. aparājitā the direction [diś₂] of the Northeast | myth. np. of aparājitā, epith. of Durgā the Invincible; she is celebrated at mahānavamī | bio. bot. Clitoria terna tea, climbing legume with blue-violet flowers; it is sacred to Shiva; syn. girikarnikā.
aparājitapṛcchā [pṛcchā] f. lit. np. of the Aparājitaprcchā, treatise on architecture.
aparājitavarman [varman] m. hist. n.p. of King Pal lava Aparajitavarmā (885–903), son of King Kampa varmā.
aparāddha [pp. aparādh] amnf aparāddhā who missed the goal; who committed a fault (in reverse g. ); guilty — m. sinner, guilty.
aparādh [aparādh] v. [5] pr. (aparādhnóti) v. [1] pr. (aparādhati) pp. (aparāddha) miss the mark, offend, insult, fail to, wrong (g.).

aparādha [act. aparādh] m. fault, offense; transgression, sin; error. aparādham kṛ to offend (g.). naiṣa sthāṇor aparādho yad enam andho na paśyati [Nirukta] It is not the fault of the post if a blind man does not see it (maxim of the blind man and the post).

aparādhakṣamā | kṣamā | f. pardon of sins; expiation | soc. posture of asking for forgiveness: the right hand grasps the lobe of the left ear, the left hand that of the right ear, the standing penitent makes a series of flexions by bending the knees.
aparādhin [agt. aparādh] amnf aparādhinī who offends | criminal | guilty. taih so'parādhī sthāpitah they judged him guilty.
aparādhitā [tā] f. guilt; criminality.
aparādhitva [tva] n. guilt; criminality.

aparigraha [priv. parigraha] amnf aparigrahā independent; indifferent to material goods — m. deprivation of goods; refusal of gifts; frugality; renunciation of fortune, vow of poverty | phil. the absence of covetousness, one of the virtues [yama₁] of yoga | jn. the absence of attachment, a minor vow [anuvrata].
apariccheda [opp. pariccheda] m. uncertainty.
aparijāta [neg. parijāta] amnf aparijātā not fully developed (not. em bryon); premature; stillborn.
apariṇīya [neg. pariṇīya] ind. not having married.
áparimita [neg. parimita] amnf áparimitā not measured; unlimited.
aparimeya [neg. parimeya] amnf apa rimeyā not measurable; unlimited.
apariśuddha [neg. pariśuddha] amnf apariśuddhā impur | gram. qualifies an invalid principle of rule interpretation.
aparihāra [opp. parihāra] m. act of not avoiding; obligation.
aparihārya [neg. parihārya] amnf aparihāryā inevitable; inescapable; obligatory, that which cannot be omitted. aparihārye'rthe na tvam śocitum arhasi [BhG.] You must not lament the inevitable.
aparīkṣita [neg. parīkṣita] amnf aparīkṣitā untested, unexamined | inconsiderate.
aparīksitakāritva [kāritva] n. "Reckless conduct", title of the 5th book of the Pañcatantra, which shows the danger of haste.
aparuddha [pp. aparudh] amnf apa ruddhā chased away, banished. aparuddho rājā soc. king in exile.
aparudh [aparudh₂] v. [7] pr. (aparuṇaddhi) v. [6] pr. (aparundhati) pp. (aparuddha) to drive out, banish.
apare [loc. apara₁] ind. in either one.
aparedyús |dyu| adv. the day after.

aparokṣa [neg. parokṣa] amnf aparokṣā close, direct, manifest, perceptible; present, actual | phil. of which one has direct experience — v. [11] pr. (aparokṣayati) to make perceptible | to apprehend acc. . aparokṣam in the presence of (g.). aparokṣāt in a perceptible way, in a manifest way.
Aparokṣānubhūti [anubhūti] f. lit. np. of the Aparokṣānubhūti "direct experience", phil. work wrongly attributed to Sankara₁.
aparodha [act. aparudh] m. exclusion, banishment; prohibition.
aparodhya [pfp. [1] aparudh] amnf aparodhyā to exclude; which must be banned or prohibited.
aparṇá₁ [priv. parṇa] amnf aparṇā without leaves.
aparṇa₂ [apaṛṇa] amnf aparṇā without debts.
aparyāpta [neg. paryāpta] amnf aparyāptā incomplete, imperfect | unlimited, innumerable.
aparyāptavat |vat| amnf aparyāptavatī in competent to (inf.).
apavad [apavad] v. [1] pr. (apavadati) to speak ill of; to insult — pr. r. (apavadate) deny, contradict. dhanārthī nyāyam apavadate The miser denies justice.

apavarga [act. apavṛj] m. completion, end phil. emancipation of the soul from the body; liberation, final deliverance, salvation; cessation of transmigrations. dvāram apavargasya [Bhartrhari] leads to liberation (said of grammar).
apavarjita [pp. apavṛj] amnf apa varjitā abandoned; discarded; thrown away | fulfilled (promise); settled (debt).
apavarta [act. apavṛt] m. math. division; reduction of fraction.
apavartana [act. apavṛt] n. removal, deletion | math. division; reduction of fraction.
apavartita [pp. apavṛt] amnf apavar titā removed; deleted | math. reduced by division of the gcd (fraction).
apavah [apavah₁] v. [1] pr. (apavahati) pp. (apodha) to carry off; to deduce — ca. (apavāhayati) to cause to be carried off; to drive away.

apavāda [act. apavad] m. blame; insult; contradiction | gram. rule that is an exception to the default rule [utsarga] | phil. [Nyāya] objection. lokāpavādo balavānmato me I attach great importance to popular censure. apavādairivotsargāh kṛtavyāvṛttayaḥ gram. as general rules are limited by exceptions.
apavādatva [tva] n. gram. condition for the application of an exception.
apavādasūtra [sūtra] n. gram. exception to the general rule (opp. utsargasūtra).
apavāraņa [apavāraņa] n. cover; disguise; concealment.
apavārita [apavārita] amnf apavāritā covered; hidden. apavāritam adv. (theatre) aside; opp. prakāśam.
apavāha [act. apavah] m. [“that which makes (water) evacuate” canal, drain | deduction, subtraction.
apavāhana [act. apavah] n. evacuation.
apavitra [neg. pavitra] amnf apavitrā impure, polluted.
apaviddha [pp. apavyadh] amnf apa viddhā pierced; rejected, abandoned, suppressed.
apaviddhaputra [putra] m. soc. child abandoned by his parents and adopted by strangers.
apavṛkta [pp. apavṛj] amnf apavṛktā finished, completed.
apavṛkti [act. apavṛkta] f. completion, termination.

apavṛj [apavṛj] v. [7] pr. r. (apavṛṅkte) pp. (apavṛkta) to extinguish; to discard, to drive away; to exclude; to tear away — ca. (apavarjayati) to abandon, to get rid of; to turn away from | to transmit, to bequeath; to give. adhvānam apavrj to choose the way.
apavrjya [pfp. [1] apavrj] amnf apavrjyā which must be abandoned; which must be terminated.
apavṛt [apavṛt₁] v. [1] pr. r. (apavar tate) pp. (apavrtta) to leave, to go out of; to move away; to slip away — ca. (apavartayati) to drive out | math. divide; reduce (fraction).
apavyadh [apavyadh] v. [4] pr. (apavid hyati) pp. (apaviddha) throw away, reject, abandon.
ápavrata [apavrata] amnf apavratā unfaithful to his commitments; disloyal, disobedient; opp. anuvrata | stubborn.
apaśabda [apaśabda] m. vulgarity, obscenity; slander | gram. improper grammatical form, barbarism. mleccho ha vā eṣa yad apaśabdaḥ |Mahābhāsya| An incorrect word is truly a barbarism.
apaśu [neg. paśu] amnf that is not a domestic animal.
apaścima [neg. paścima] amnf apaścimā who is not the last | who has no one behind him; last.
apaśyat [neg. paśyat] amnf apaśyantī not seeing; without perceiving | without looking.
apaṣṭhu [apastha] amnf contrary, op posed; false; left; perverse — m. antonym — adv. in a perverse manner; evil.
apás₁ cf. ap.
ápas₂ n. work; activity || lat. opus.
apasada [apasad₁] m. child or man rejected, social outcast — ifc. the last of the (iic.).
apasalavi [apasalavi] adv. left; opp. prasalavi; syn. avasalavi | to the left; levorotatory; opp. pradaksina.
apasidh [apasidh₂] v. [1] pr. (apasedhati) pp. (apasiddha) to repel, to push away.

apasṛ [apasṛ] v. [1] pr. (apasarati) pp. (apasrta) to move away, to flee, to disappear; to escape from (abl.) — ca. (apasārayati) to drive away, to remove. ayam eti putro rājñaḥ puruṣo 'pasāryatām gram. (ambiguity of the genitive) Here is the prince, remove the man/Here is the son, remove the king's servant.
apasṛta [pp. apasṛ] amnf apasṛtā freed from; disappeared; elapsed (time).
apasṛp [apasṛp] v. [1] pr. (apasarpati) quit ter, to move away. yā chāyeva na tatpārśvātkṣaṇamapyapasarpati KSS. Like her shadow, she does not move away from her for a single moment.
apaskṛ [apakṛ] v. [6] pr. r. (apaskirate) to scratch the ground (said of animals). apaskirate vrsabhah the bull scratches the earth.
apastamba m. hist. np. of the mathematician apastamba (600–540 ant.), author of the apastamba śulbasūtra.
apasmāra [apasmāra] m. epilepsy.
apasmārapuruṣa [puruṣa] m. myth. np. of the dwarf Apasmārapuruşa "Epileptic", symbolizing ignorance, depicted holding a snake and trampled underfoot by ŚivaNatarāja in the nadānta dance posture.
apasmārin |in| amnf apasmāriņī epileptic.
apasvara [apasvara] m. bad note (mus.); unpleasant sound.
apaha |agt. apahan| ifc. amnf apahā that repels (iic.); that removes, that destroys (iic.).
apahan [apahan₁] v. [2] pr. (apahanti) pp. (apahata) to remove, withdraw; to repel; to destroy (by removing) | to affect (disease).
apaharaṇa [act. apahṛ] n. act of carrying off, seizure; theft.
apaharaṇīya [pfp. [2] apahṛ] amnf apaharaṇīyā to take away, to steal.

apahartṛ [agt. apahṛ] amnf apahartrī who steals (acc. g. iic.) | who atones (for sin). annam apahartāra āhvarakā bhavanti śrāddhe sid dhe The outcasts steal the food offering as soon as the ritual is finished.
apahas [apahas] ca. (upahāsayati) to mock, ridicule.
apahasita [apahasita] n. laughter without reason, silly laughter; huffing | roar of laughter, with tears in the eyes.
apahasta [apahasta] m. position of gripping the collar | person thus seized | forceful eviction — v. [11] pr. (apahastayati) to evict, to repel.
apahā [apahā₁] abs. (apahāya) to fall behind; not to reach the goal — ps. (apahīyate) to decrease, diminish.
apahāya [abs. apahā] ind. abandoning, avoiding | except, except.
apahāra [act. apahr] m. theft; suppression; embezzlement or squandering of wealth; dissimulation. ātmāpahāram kṛ to conceal one's true nature.

apahāravarman [varman] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Prince Apahāravarmā, "Protected by theft", one of the 10 heroes of the Daśakumāracarita; he is the son of King Prahāravarmā of Videha; he went to Campā, where he led a life of cheating and thieving; he met Kulapālikā, and accompanied him to his sweetheart Udāraka; he advised the latter to pretend to have a magic purse, which he would secretly fill with the fruits of his plundering, so that Kuberadatta would agree to give him the hand of his daughter Kulapālikā; he seduced the young Rāgamañjarī, killed the policeman Kāntaka, and finally obtained the hand of Princess Ambālikā₂.
apahāraka [agt. apahṛ] amnf apahārikā who seizes; who steals — m. thief.
apahārin [agt. apahṛ] amnf apahāriṇī who seizes; who steals — m. thief.
apahāsa [act. apahas] m. mockery, affront.
apahi [apahi₂] pp. (apahita) to reject, to get rid of.
apahita [apahita₂] amnf apahitā com mis, investi | accused (of a crime).

apahṛ [apahṛ₁] v. [1] pr. (apaharati) pp. (apahṛta) to take, remove, seize; to steal, take hold of, snatch. apahriye pariśramajanitayā nidrayā I am overcome with sleep because of fatigue. apaharati ca vātyeva śuṣkapatram sa mudbhūtarajobhrāntir atidūram ātmecchayā yauvanasamaye puruṣaṃ prakṛtiḥ [K.] At puberty, man is carried away, according to his own nature (troubled by passions), like the wind blows the dead leaf (in a whirlwind of dust).
apahṛta [pp. apahṛ] amnf apahṛtā stolen, robbed, carried off.
apahnu [apahnu] v. [2] pr. r. (apahnuté) pp. (apahnuta) to conceal; disguise; deny | to excuse oneself.
apahnuta [pp. apahnu] amnf apahnutā concealed; denied.

apahnuti [act. apahnu] f. dissimulation of the truth | lit. rhet. (figure of speech) deceptive words, dissimulation; disguised description; denial; the concealed fact must be suggested but denied; syn. vyājokti . ākṛṣyādāvamandagrahamalakacayam vak tramāsajya vaktre kanthe lagnah punarapi ku cayordattagādhāngasangah | baddhāsaktirnitambe patati caraṇayoryaḥ sa tādṛk priyome bāle lajjāpraņastā na hi na hi kutile colakah kim trapākṛt | [SRK.] I like the way he's drawn to me, first grabbing my hair, then caressing my face, pressing himself to my mouth and neck, then insistently clinging to my chest, finally after embracing my hips falling at my feet; young girl, you have lost all modesty; not at all, it is you who have a dirty mind, what shame is there in putting on a leotard?
apāka [neg. pāka] amnf apākā raw; unripe | uncooked; uncooked.
apākaraṇa [act. apākṛ ] n. refutation.
apākariṣṇu [agt. apākṛ] amnf [“that which leaves behind”] that which surpasses.
apākṛ [apaākṛ] v. [8] pr. (apākaróti) pp. (apākṛta) to remove; to reject, abandon | to pay, to leave.
apānkteya [neg. pānkteya] amnf apānkteyā soc. not acceptable, deprived of his caste | var. apānktya f. apānktyā id.
apāniga [apaaniga₁] m. outer corner of the eye.
apāc var. apāñc [apaac] amnf apācī [m. nom. apān; n. nom. apāk located behind; turned towards the rear | turned towards the West. apāk adv. towards the West.

apāṇinīya [neg. pāṇinīya] amnf apāṇinīyā gram. not in accordance with Pāṇini. siddhyaty evam apāṇinīyam tu bhavati gram. |Patanjali₁| Thus the correct result is established, but it is not in accordance with Pāṇini.
Apāṇinīyapramāṇatā [pramāṇatā] f. gram. np. of the Apāṇinīyapramāṇatā, work of Nārāyaṇa₃ Bhatta justifying the attested constructions of great poets not conforming to the grammar of Pāṇini.
apāṇipāda [priv. pāṇipāda] amnf apāṇipādā phil. [MO.] ["without hands or feet"] that does not act.
apātra [absence pātra] n. inadequate utensil; useless object | undeserving.

apādāna [apaādāna] n. deviation | gram. |Pāṇini| thematic role |kāraka| generally expressed in the ablative: point of the situation from which the action moves away, or object of fear, or actant from which one hides, or origin of the agent or of its information.
apāna [related to apāc] m. [apānavāyu] phil. |yoga| the excretory breath, one of the 5 breaths vi
rate [prāṇa]; cf. mūlabandha — n. anus | phil. perfume, substance perceived [atigraha] by smell (conceived as emanation of a fragrant object).
apānodgāra [udgāra] m. fart.
apāpa |priv. pāpa| amnf apāpā without sin; virtuous, pure.
apām [g. pl. ap ] iic. apāmnapāt var. Apānnapāt [napāt] m. ved. np. of Apānnapāt, epith. of Agni "Coming from the waters"; it figures lightning coming from the storm | lat. Neptunus.
apāya [act. ape] m. disappearance; that which is lacking to reach the goal (cf. upāya ) | danger; disadvantage; diminution.
apāyin [agt. ape] amnf apāyinī that goes away, that leaves, that disappears; perishable.

apārá [priv. pāra] amnf apārā [“without opposite bank”] unlimited; infinite — opp. m. bank on this side of a river. apāre kāvyasamsāre kavireva prajāpatih [Dhvanyāloka] The poet is the master of creations in the endless flow of poetry.
apāramārthika [neg. pāramārthika] amnf apāramārthikī phil. which does not concern the supreme truth; false, illusory.

apāla |priv. pāla| amnf apālā Defenseless — f. apālā ved. np. d'apālā "Defenseless", daughter of Atri; [RV.] her husband repudiated her for her skin disease; JB. she found a soma stalk in the river and chewed it; Indra ran to drink the soma from her mouth.
apāvṛ [apaāvṛ] v. [5] pr. (apāvṛṇóti) pr. r. (apāvṛṇuté) pp. (apāvṛta) to open, discover, unveil. pratnakīrtim apāvṛṇu Discover the glory of the past!
apāśraya [act. apāśri] m. refuge, refuge | part of the bed where the head rests | veranda.
apāśri [apaāśri] v. [1] pr. (apāśrayati) pr. r. (apāśrayate) pp. (apāśrita) pf. (vi) to have recourse to, to use, to practice.
apāśrita [pp. apāśri] amnf apāśritā which has recourse to, which relies on.
apās [apaas₂] v. [4] pr. (apāsyati) pp. (apāsta) reject, get rid of | repel | abandon; ignore.
apāsana [act. apās] n. rejection; abandonment; suppression.
apāsta |pp. apās | amnf apāstā dismissed; thrown away, abandoned; dismissed; ignored.
apāsya [abs. apās] ind. having abandoned, having dismissed.

api part. cl. and, also, still, equally; even | yet, however, although, despite this | (after num.) expresses totality | (after interr.) expresses the indefinite | interr. (at the beginning of a sentence) is it that? | would to heaven that (opt.)! perhaps — pf. on, near (sometimes abbreviated to pi). api ... api as well ... as; at the same time ... and. api ca even; and moreover | lit. link between two discontinuous stanzas. api you but yet. kutrāpi anywhere. kenāpi for some reason. ko 'pi someone, a certain; something, I don't know what. na ko 'pi nothing, nobody. cāpi and. tathā 'pi var. tadapi nevertheless, however. dvāvapi both of them. nāpi neither, and not, but not, either. yo 'pi anyone. vāpi or. na ... nāpi neither ... nor. na ... vāpi neither ... nor. sarve 'pi all absolutely. mām api me too. kadā cid api na absolutely never. svam apīta that which is his. apih samuccaye gram. The word api is used to denote conjunction. api stuyād vṛṣalam He would even praise an outcast. paśyannapi śrnvannapi aśnannapi gacchan napi śvasannapi naiva kiñcit karomīti cintayati viśuddhātmā although seeing, although hearing, although eating, although walking, although breathing, he whose soul is purified thinks that he is doing nothing at all.
apigam [apigam] subj. (ápigman) ved. to approach.
apidhā [apidhā₁] v. [3] pr. (apidadhāti) pp. (apihita) to close, cover | hide.
apīḍayat [neg. pīḍayat] amnf apīdayatī who does not oppress.
apīḍā [opp. pīḍā] f. non oppression. apīdayā adv. in a consenting, voluntary manner.
aputra |priv. putra| amnf aputrā Without sons.
apunar [opp. punar] ind. phil. Without recurrence; only once.
apunarāvṛtti [opp. punarāvṛtti] f. non-return; absence of reincarnation.
apunarbhava [opp. punarbhava] m. phil. non-rebirth; liberation.
apūjya [neg. pūjya] amnf apūjya which should not be honored or worshipped.
apūpá [apūpa] m. cake, biscuit; bread | wheat. apūpān iva bhakṣayati māṣān He eats beans like cakes.
apūpavat |vat| amnf apūpavatī accompanied by a cake.
apūpīya [īya] amnf apūpīyā which is used to make cakes.
apūpya [ya] amnf apūpyā which is used to make cakes — m. flour.

apūrņa [neg. pūrņa] amnf apūrņā not yet accomplished; incomplete | deficient — n. math. non-integer number. apūrņakāla [kāla₁] amnf apūrņakālā premature — m. insufficient time. apūrņakhyāti [opp. khyāti] f. phil. incomplete knowledge.

apūrvá [neg. pūrva] amnf apūrvā Without predecessor, Without precedent; new; original; innovative, groundbreaking; incomparable; extraordinary — m. novelty, innovation | phil. [Mīmāṃsā] ["that which did not exist before"] force initiated by the effective rite; benefit of a ritual action; its influence on individual karma; causality (linking the rite to its benefit).
apūrvatā [tā] f. state of being unprecedented, new beauty; incomparability; originality.
apūrvatva [tva] n. id.
apūrvavat [vat] adv. in a singular way; as never before.
apṛkta [opp. pṛkta] amnf apṛktā gram. unmixed, uncombined.
ape [apai] v. [2] pr. (apaiti) pp. (apeta) pf. (vi) to leave, to disappear. apaişyāmi I intend to leave.

apekṣ [apaīkṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (apekṣate) pp. (apekṣita) pf. (ā, vi) to respect, to take into account, to expect; to have in mind, to desire. pade tu samhitā nityā nityā dhātūpasargayoh samāse ca tathā vākye sā vivakṣām apekṣate || gram. [Rūpāvatāra] The meaning of an utterance is respected by omitting the sandhi between words, even compound words, but not between a root and its preverbs.

apekṣā [act. apekṣ] f. act of looking around; consideration | regard, consideration, respect for (iic. g.) | desire, expectation, hope; prerequisite | phil. [Nyāya] dependence on (iic.); connection between cause and effect, between the individual and the species. apekṣayā adv. ifc. out of regard for, concerning (iic.). mamāpekṣayā kaniṣṭhaḥ vā He is my junior.
apekṣābuddhi [buddhi] f. phil. [Vaiśeṣika] faculty of being careful, methodical, rigorous, clear.

apekṣita [pp. apekṣ] amnf apekṣitā considered, respected; desired, wished for; required. apekṣitam vā what do you desire? kati phalāni apekṣitāni how many fruits do you desire? kim īśvarānapekṣitam āhosvid īśvarāpekṣitam Is it independent of God or dependent on God?
apekṣin [agt. apekṣ] amnf apekṣiṇī who respects; who waits.
apekṣya [pfp. [1] apekṣ] amnf apekṣyā to be taken into consideration | to be sought; desirable — abs. ind. having considered; with reference to.
apeta [pp. ape] amnf apetā part, disappeared | set aside from, who departs from (abl. iic.).
apaiśuna [opp. apaiśuna] n. noncalumny.
apogaṇḍa [neg. pogaṇḍa] amnf apogandā prepubescent; young boy; childish, juvenile infirm.
apodha [pp. apoh] amnf apodhā set aside, removed, carried away (by abl. ) — ifc. exempt from iic. . kalpanāpodha phil. exempt from conceptualization (said of perception).
apoddhāra [apauddhāra] amnf apoddhārā gram. fine analysis of the structure of compound words.
apoddhārapadārtha [padārtha] m. gram. meaning of a word obtained analytically; opp. sthitalakṣaṇa.
apobdha [pp. apombh] amnf apobdhā bound.
apombh [apaumbh] v. [6] pr. (apombhati) pp. (apobdha) to bind; chain.
apoh [apaūh] v. [1] pr. (apohati) pp. (apodha) pf. (ava, vi) to dismiss — pr. r. (apohate) to contest, to object.

apoha [act. apoh] m. act of contesting, act of denying; objection, contestation | phil. [Dinnāga] elimination, differentiation; mode of meaning of a name by exclusion of opposites; this theory bd. of conceptual exclusion replaced the doctrine of universals of Nyāya.
apohaprakarana [prakarana] n. bed. n.p. from the apohaprakarana, comic text. of Jñānaśrīmitra of philosophy of language.

apohavāda [vāda] m. contestation; exclusion phil. deconstruction | bd. doctrine of discriminating nominalism; this interpretation of notions by double negation postulates that categorization by universals is only the exclusion of contrary properties, and is essentially arbitrary; it was advanced by Dinnāga, and developed by Dhar makīrti.
apohasiddhi [siddhi] f. lit. np. of the apohasiddhi "Knowledge of exclusion", bd. text due to Rat nakīrti; it comments on and summarizes the Apohaprakaraņa of Jñānaśrīmitra.
apohana [act. apoh] n. objection, contestation; denial | phil. clarification.
apauruṣa [opp. pauruṣa] n. quality surhu maine.

apauruseya [īya] amnf apauruseyā of non-human nature, not created by man | phil. said of the Veda, revealed by Brahmā; cf. śruti . apaurușeyatva [tva] n. phil. doctrine of the absence of a human author of the Veda.
apnas [abstr. āp] n. ved. acquisition; possession, property | offspring | lat. ops.

appayya [dravidian] m. hist. np. of the mystic appayya Dīkṣita, born Vināyaka Subrama nian in Adayapalam near Arcot in Tamil Nadu (1520–1593); he is the author of an imposing work (104 texts), notably of texts of Vedānta doctrine opposed to Madhva, such as the Madhvatan tramukhamardana, the Madhvamatavidhvamsana, the Upakramaparākrama, the Nyāyarakṣāmaṇi; his Sivārkamaṇidīpikā and Parimala₁ are his commentaries on the Brahmasūtra; his Atmārpaņastuti is a mystical poem; His Vidhirasāyana is a manual of hermeneutics [Mīmāmsā]; it was opposed by Vijayīndra, but influenced Bhattoji Dīkṣita. appayyadīkṣitendrān aśeṣavidyāgurūn aham vande | yatkṛtibodhābodhau vidvadavidvadbhājakopādhī | [Bhattoji] I pay homage to the great appayya Dīkṣita, my master in all disciplines; knowledge and ignorance of his work characterize respectively the learned and the ignorant. śaivādvaitaikasāmrājyah śrīmān appayyadīkṣitah [Sevappa] Glorious appayya Dīkṣita, sole emperor of śaiva monism.
appayyakapolacapetikā | kapolacapetikā | f. lit. np. of the Appayyakapolacapețikā "Slap to appayya Dīkṣita", work of Vijayīndra coming in defense of Madhva.
apyaya |apiaya| m. end, disappearance; destruction.
aprakaṭa [neg. prakaṭa] amnf aprakaṭā non-manifest, invisible.
aprakatalīlā [līlā] f. myth. transfiguration of Kṛṣṇa into non-visible immanent manifestation; opp. prakatalīlā.

aprakāśa [neg. prakāśa] amnf aprakāśā not bright, dull, dark | not manifest; in visible, secret — m. darkness | phil. [Trika] fluctuating phenomenon, which does not participate in the universal consciousness of Shiva. aprakāśam adv. in secret.
aprakṛta [neg. prakṛta] amnf aprakṛtā non-main; secondary (opp. primary prakṛta) occasional; unnatural; irrelevant. aprakṛtam state it has nothing to do with it.
aprakṛtārtha [artha] m. gram. secondary meaning; opp. prakṛtārtha.
apragalbha [neg. pragalbha] amnf apragalbhā timid, fearful, timid.
apraja [priv. prajā] amnf aprajā without posterity | var. aprajā id. — f. aprajā (woman) sterile.
aprajñāta [neg. prajñāta] amnf aprajñātā not recognized; unknown.
apratarkya [neg. pratarkya] amnf apra tarkyā unimaginable, inconceivable.
aprati [aprati] amnf without equal.
apratikāra [priv. pratikāra] amnf apratikārā without remedy; without relief | var. apratīkāra f. apratīkārā id.
apratikārin [in] amnf apratikārinī méd. (pa tient) refusing care.
apratipatha [opp. pratipatha] m. im proper way back.
apratima [priv. pratimā₂] amnf apra timā without equal; unsurpassed.
apratistha [priv. pratisthā₂] amnf apratiṣṭhā unstable; without solid base; without value.
apratihata [neg. pratihata] amnf pra tihatā that cannot be repelled; invincible.
ápratīta [neg. pratīta] amnf apratītā unapproachable, unassailable, invincible | misunderstood, unused (expression); disapproved | dissatisfied, sad.
apratta [neg. pratta] amnf aprattā not granted; not promised in marriage.
apratyakṣa [neg. pratyakṣa] amnf apratyakṣā invisible, imperceptible. alpam pratyakṣam analpam apratyakṣam There is little visible and much invisible. na hi yad giriśṛṅgam āruhya gṛhyate tad
apratyakṣam [Kumārila] Even if one had to climb to the top of a mountain to understand it, it would not be imperceptible.
apratyaya [opp. pratyaya] m. distrust, doubt | gram. (morpheme) non-suffix | gram. (word) lacking a suffix. ātmanyapratyayam cetah the mind distrusts itself.
apradhāna [neg. pradhāna] amnf apradhānā auxiliary; secondary, subordinate gram. not. subordinate semantic role of accompaniment (argument of saha₂, marked by the i.).
apramattavirata [opp. pramattavirata] n. jn. state of renunciation with full awareness, 7th stage of spiritual development [guṇasthāna].
apramā [opp. pramā₂] f. incorrect knowledge, error | phil. [TkS.] cognition shown to be false by experience | incorrect rule.
apramāṇa [opp. pramāṇa] n. gram. (rule) that does not apply; worthless judgment.
aprameya [neg. prameya] amnf apra meyā not measurable; unlimited; unfathomable.
aprayukta [neg. prayukta] amnf aprayuktā not used, unused | gram. not tested | (rhetoric) faulty.
áprayucchat [neg. prayucchat] amnf aprayucchatī attentive.
aprayoga [opp. prayoga] m. the act of not applying oneself. uktārthānām aprayogah gram. |Patañjali₁| One should not use a form for meanings already expressed.
apravāsa | priv. pravasa | amnf apravāsā | soc. who does not leave their place of birth.
apravṛtti [opp. pravṛtti] f. inertia, inaction; resorption.
aprasāda |opp. prasāda| m. disapproval; disfavor. yasyāprasādān na gatih kuto 'pi with disapproval (from the master) it is impossible to progress.
aprasiddha [neg. prasiddha] amnf apra siddhā not established | unknown; non-existent | unusual; unpopular.

aprastuta [neg. prastuta] amnf aprastutā not mentioned, omitted; implied | secondary, irrelevant — n. beginning, undertaking; object | lit. object of a comparison with its contextual elements; opp. prastuta. aprastutam kimiti anusamdhīyate why are you beating around the bush?
aprastutapraśaṃsā [praśaṃsā] f. bed. rhet. figure of
[alamkāra] style of indirect praise; syn. anyokti.
aprastutaprasanga [prasanga] m. inconsequential event.
aprahṛṣṭa |neg. prahṛṣṭa| amnf aprahṛṣṭā sad; unhappy.
áprāpta [neg. prāpta] amnf aprāptā not obtained, not accomplished, not derivable | inappropriate, unsuitable | gram. impossible to derive.
aprāptakāla [kāla₁] m. inappropriate tense.
aprāpyakārin [neg. prāpyakārin] amnf aprāpyakāriņī phil. ["not in direct interaction"] refers to the senses of sight and hearing; opp. prāpyakārin.
aprāmāṇya |neg. prāmāṇya | amnf aprāmāṇyā not justified, not founded, without proof, which is not authoritative | not to be taken literally — n. lack of proof.
aprāśana |opp. prāśana | n. young.
aprāsangika [neg. prāsangika] amnf aprāsangikā inopportun, inappropriate, irrelevant. alamaprāsangikena enough digressions.
aprāstāvika [neg. prāstāvika] amnf aprāstāvikā inopportun; inappropriate; irrelevant.
ápriya [neg. priya] amnf apriyā unloved, undesirable; unsympathetic, disagreeable — opp. m. enemy.

apsarás [apsaras] f. myth. celestial nymph; the apsarasas are daughters of Kaśyapa, or come from the churning of the ocean of milk |kṣīrodamathana|; they are companions of the centaur musicians |gandharvās|, lovers of the gods |deva| as well as of

titans | asura | ; they cause the sages | ṛṣi | to spread their seed; their magic veil | tiraskariṇī | conceals them from mortals; tradition says that there are seven, or ten, or divided into 14 families; cf. Añjanā Punjikasthalā, Anyūnā, Urvasī, Ghṛtācī, Citra lekhā, Jānapadī, Tilottamā, Devarati, Puņḍarīkā, Pūrvacitti, Pramlocā, Budbudā, Manoramā, Me nakā, Rambhā, Latā, Varānanā, Vargā, Samīcī, Sugandhā, Supriyā, Suratamañjarī₁, Stāvā, Sau rabheyī, Hemā — c. [11] pr. r. (apsarāyate) behave like a nymph.
apsu [loc. pl. ap] adv. in the waters.
apsuyoni [yoni] amnf derived from the waters.
aphala [priv. phala] amnf aphalā infruc tueux; infertile; vain, unproductive.
aphalaprepsu [neg. phalaprepsu] amnf who does not desire a reward.
aphalākāṅkṣin [neg. phalākāṅkṣin] amnf aphalākānkṣiṇī who does not desire the fruits of action. अब् ab iic. after
abindhana [indhana] m. myth. ["whose fuel is water" | underwater fire; cf. Vaḍabāgni.
Abja |ja| amnf abjā born in the water — n. lo tus; syn. ambuja, ambhoja, kamala — n. math. one billion — m. myth. np. of Abja, epith. of Brahmā "Born of the waters" | cf. abjadeva.
abjadeva | deva | mr. myth. n.p. of abjadeva "Divine from the primordial ocean", epith. of Dhanvantari.
ábda | da | m. | "that which brings water" | rainy season year.
abdaka [ka] ifc. amnf abdikā aged (iic.) so many years.
abdhi |dhi| m. pond; lake; ocean | math. symb. the number 4.
ábaddha |neg. baddha| amnf abaddhā loose, untied, detached; loose, free | absurd, meaningless.
abaddhamukha | mukha | amnf abaddhamukhī bad mouth.
abaddhavākya | vākya | amnf abaddhavākyā med. who speaks incoherently — m. delirium.
abalá [neg. bala] amnf abalā weak — n. weakness — f. abalā woman.

abādha |neg. bādha| amnf abādhā unrestricted; Without objection, Without obstruction | cf. abaddha — m. ifc. absence of obstruction to (iic.). arthābādhaḥ gram. |yogyatā| absence of obstruction to the meaning.
abādhita [neg. bādhita] amnf abādhitā not hindered; not oppressed | gram. not obstructed, not prohibited | phil. [Nyāya] not contradictory; irrefutable; compatible.
abādhitatva [tva] n. phil. [Nyāya] absence of contradiction; compatibility, coherence.
abuddha [neg. buddha] amnf abuddhā senseless; stupid.
abuddhatva [tva] n. stupidity.
abuddhi [opp. buddhi] f. incomprehension; ignorance; stupidity — priv. amnf ignorant; stupid. abuddhyā adv. inadvertently; unintentionally.
abuddhimat [neg. buddhimat] amnf abuddhimatī stupid; imprudent.
abodha [opp. bodha] m. unconsciousness; ignorance. abodhapūrvam adv. Without prior knowledge.
abrahmanya [neg. brahmanya] amnf abrahmanyā unfavorable to brahmins | impious. abrahmanyam interj. Heavens! Woe! Sacrilege!
abrāhmaṇa [neg. brāhmaṇa] mf abrāhmaṇī soc. who is not a brahmin.
abhakṣya |neg. bhakṣya| amnf abhakṣyā inedible, which must not be eaten — n. that which must not be eaten.
abhagna |neg. bhagna| f. abhagnā intact; in third | uninterrupted.
abhagnamāna [māna₁] amnf abhagnamānā whose honor is preserved.
abhanga [priv. bhanga] amnf abhangā Without caesura, continuous | lit. form of devotional poem [bhakti] Marathi, perfected by Nāmadeva and Jñānadeva.

abhangaślesa [ślesa] m. lit. figure of speech of double meaning in which the ambiguity rests on homophony and not on division into words; opp. sabhangaślesa. rājā harati lokasya hrdayam mrdulaih karaih The King delights the heart of the people with his moderate taxes/The Moon charms the heart of the world with its gentle rays.
abhangura [neg. bhangura] amnf abhangurā invariable; imperishable; eternal.
abhadra [neg. bhadra] amnf abhadrā bad, unfortunate; wicked; dirty — n. evil, wrong; bad intention.

ábhaya [priv. bhaya| amnf abhayā ras suré, Without fear | safe, Without danger — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of abhaya "Without fear", one of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; he was killed by Bhīma — n. safety, security; serenity | absence of fear, an āyādi arch. bot. Terminalia chebula, the chebulic myrobolan tree; its wood is used in Kerala to build temples, its resin used for varnish and mortar.
ábhayadakṣiṇā [dakṣiṇā] f. promise of protection; safe-conduct. svāminah sakāśādabhayadakṣiṇā dāpayitavyā tvayā |PT.| You must assure me of my safety from your master.
abhayapradāna [pradāna] amnf abhaya pradānā which ensures security.

abhayamudrā [mudrā] f. [iconography] gesture that dispels fear (hand at chest level, palm forward, fingers towards the sky); bd. it evokes the gesture of the buddha during the miracle of the furious elephant; cf. Nālāgiri.
abhayavana [vana] n. forest animal reserve.

Abhayākaragupta [ākaragupta] m. hist. np. of Abhayākaragupta, bd. monk and tantric master [vajrācārya] of the late 11th century, died in 1125; he was abbot of Vikramaśīla, and taught the VajrayānaMadhyamaka doctrine; the Vajrāvalī is attributed to him.
abhava [opp. bhava] m. non-existence, destruction, end of the world.
abhavanīya [neg. bhavanīya] amnf abhavanīyā that which should not exist; that which will not come to pass.

abhavya [neg. bhavya] amnf abhavyā that which should not be; improper, bad; unhappy, miserable | that which will not happen; not predestined | jn. said of a soul which cannot attain deliverance; opp. bhavya.

abhāva [opp. bhāva] m. non-existence; absence, lack | destruction, death | phil. [Mīmāṃsā] means of knowledge [pramāṇa] postulating that what we have no means of knowing does not exist, by appealing to common sense | phil. [Nyāya] negation as absence; Kumārila distinguishes 4 categories: prāgabhāva prior absence, pradhvamsābhāva subsequent absence, atyantābhāva constant absence, and anyonyābhāva mutual absence. tadabhāve in its absence. putrābhāve having not produced a son. gatyantarābhāvāt in the absence of an alternative. abhāvapratinidhidravya med. a substitute substance for an unavailable compound.
abhāvatva |tva| n. phil. quality of being absent.
abhāvavat [vat] amnf abhāvavatī phil. [Nyāya] characterized by the absence (of g. iic. ).
abhāvīya [īya] amnf abhāvīyā phil. concerning non-existence.
abhāvayat [neg. bhāvayat] amnf abhāvayatī unconscious; insane.
abhāvin [abhāvain] amnf abhāvinī that which should not be; that which will not occur.
abhí pf. towards; about, concerning | facing, against | superior to, intense; supreme | gr.; lat. ambi; all. um. abhyagni adv. in the direction of the fire.
abhika [ka] amnf abhikā voluptuary; lascivious, libidinous; syn. abhīka₂ — m. lover.
abhikapracāra [pracāra] m. soc. licentious conduct.
abhikamp [abhikamp] v. [1] pr. r. (abhi kampate) pp. (abhikampita) to tremble strongly.

abhikāś [abhikāś] intens. (abhicākaśīti) to illuminate, to radiate | to observe attentively, to pierce, to see. tayor anyah pippalam svādvatti | anaśnannanyo abhicākaśīti | [MO.] One of them eats the sweet berry, the other, without eating, observes intensely.
abhikṛ [abhikṛ₁] abs. (abhikṛtya) to act in reference to or on behalf of. abhikrtya prep. in reference to.
abhikram [abhikram] abs. (abhikramya) to approach; tackle.
abhikrama [act. abhikram] m. approach; attack; attempt.
abhikramaṇa [act. abhikram] n. approach.
abhikruddha [pp. abhikrudh] amnf abhikruddhā angry.
abhikrudh [abhikrudh₁] v. [4] pr. (abhi krudhyati) pp. (abhikruddha) to be angry with acc. . putram abhikrudhyati he is angry with his son.
abhikhyā₁ [abhikhyā] v. [2] pr. (abhi khyāti) pp. (abhikhyāta) to perceive — ca. (abhi khyāpayati) to make known.
abhikhyā₁ [obj. abhikhyā₁] f. beauty, splendor; fame.

abhigam [abhigam] v. [1] pr. (abhigac chati) pp. (abhigata) pf. (sam) to go towards, to approach, to follow; to meet, to visit, to cohabit; to have sexual relations with | ved. to understand — ca. (abhigamayati) to study.
abhigama [act. abhigam] m. approach; vi site | sexual approach.
abhigamana [act. abhigam] n. ap near, visit | soc. the approach of the divinity, a pañcopāsana according to Rāmānuja; one cleans and purifies one's access path with cow dung.
abhigará [abhigr] m. soc. ceremonial approval (from the head priest during a sacrifice); opp. apagara.
abhigā [abhigā₁] v. [3] pr. (abhijigāti) ap to approach, to come to obtain; to experience. śramam abhigā to experience fatigue.
abhigupta [abhigupta] amnf abhi guptā guarded, hidden.
abhigrhīta [pp. abhigrah] amnf abhigrhītā seized.
abhigṛ [abhigṛ₂] v. [9] pr. (abhigṛṇāti) to address (with approval) to; to welcome, to praise; to approve, to acquiesce to, to authorize.
abhigrah [abhigrah] v. [9] pr. (abhigṛhṇāti) pr. r. (abhigṛhṇīte) pp. (gṛhīta) to seize; to pull (from the ground); to accept, to receive — ca. (abhigrāhayati) to surprise, to take by surprise.
abhigraha [act. abhigrah] m. act of seizing; attack; theft, pillage.
abhigrahaṇa [act. abhigrah] n. flight.
abhigrāhita [pp. That. abhigrah] amnf abhigrāhitā seized; surprised. rūpābhigrāhita caught in the act.
abhighāta [act. abhihan] m. strike, at attack; the act of wounding, damaging | response to an attack, retaliatory blow — n. phon. combined irregular sound of consonants. kaśābhighātah whipping.
abhighṛ [abhighṛ] pf. (prati) [unused without pf.].
abhicar [abhicar] v. [1] pr. (abhicarati) pp. (abhicarita) pf. (vi) to act badly towards; to behave badly; not. (for a woman) to be unfaithful to subjugate, enchant, bewitch.
abhicāra [agt. abhicar] m. soc. power [siddhi] of destruction of enemies; incantation, magic (for evil purposes); sorcery; its use is a minor crime [upapātaka].
abhicārin [agt. abhicar] amnf abhicārinī magician, enchanter; sorcerer.
abhijan [abhijan] v. [4] pr. r. (abhijāyate) pp. (abhijāta) to be born, to be born again; to be of the destined.
abhijana [abhijana] m. family; race; descendants; ancestors | head of family; noble origin; land of origin; notoriety.
abhijanavat [vat] amnf abhijanavatī of noble origin.
abhijaya [act. abhiji] m. conquest; complete victory.
abhijāta [pp. abhijan] amnf abhijātā well born, of noble origin; beautiful, lovable — n. noble birth.
abhiji [abhiji] v. [1] pr. (abhijayati) pp. (abhijita) to conquer completely, to acquire by victory — des. (abhijigīṣati) to try to conquer, to attack.

abhijít [agt. abhiji] amnf Victorious | born under the sign of Vega — m. astr. np. of Abhijit "Victorious", 20th lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the star Vega of Lyra; Brahmā presides over it; its symbol is a nut | astr. name of the 8th moment of the day [muhūrta], around noon | phil. [Tantra] point of equilibrium of breathing between inhalation [apāna] and exhalation [prāṇa]; opp. viṣuvat.
abhijillagna [lagna] amnf abhijillagnā at noon sharp (auspicious moment).
abhijita [pp. abhiji] amnf abhijitā conquered.
abhijña [agt. abhijñā₁] amnf abhijñā₁ experienced, knowledgeable; skillful | who knows, familiar with (g. iic.).
abhijñā₁ [abhijñā₁] v. [9] pr. (abhijānāti) pr. r. (abhijānīté) pp. (abhijñāta) pf. (prati) to know, to recognize, to know well; to concede.

abhijnā₂ [act. abhijnā₁] f. memory, recall | bd. supernatural faculty of the Buddha; there are five: power to appear in any form, hearing or seeing at any distance, influence over a person's thoughts, knowledge of their condition and antecedents || pali abhiññā.
abhijñāna [act. abhijñā₁] n. recognition; sign of recognition | soc. permit of passage; safe-conduct.

Abhijñānaśakuntalā [śakuntalā] f. lit. np. of the Abhijñānaśakuntalā "śakuntalā recognized", famous drama [nāṭaka] by Kālidāsa inspired by an episode from the Mah. (śakuntalā is recognized by the ring that King Dusyanta had given her as a token of recognition after marrying her "in the gandharva fashion"); two recensions of it are known, one from Bengal, the other from Kaśmīra — n. abhijāānaśakuntala lit. it is also called abhijñānaśakuntala "recognition of Sakuntalā".
abhitas [adv. abhi] adv. near, in front of (acc.) | on both sides; on all sides; all around | entirely, completely.
abhitvaramāṇa [abhitvaramāṇa] m. soc. courier, letter carrier.
abhidā [abhidā₁] v. [3] pr. (abhidadāti) ac corder (for a reason).
abhidru [abhidru₁] v. [1] pr. (abhidravati) pp. (abhidruta) to run, to chase after, to run towards; to infest — ca. (abhidrāvayati) to put to flight.
abhidruh [abhidruh₁] v. [4] pr. (abhidru hyati) pp. (abhidrugdha) to harm, to be angry with; to seek to injure (acc. dat.); to offend.
abhidrohá [act. abhidruh] m. offense.
Abhidharma [abhidharma] m. phil. metaphysical; collection of comic dogmas. | bd. n.p. of Abhidharma, high philosophy || pali abhidhamma.

Abhidharmakośa [kośa] m. lit. np. of the Abhidhar makośa or Abhidharmakośabhāsya "Compendium of philosophy", major work of the Norse school of Hīnayāna in Sanskrit, due to Vasubandhu; it revises the Samyuktābhidharmahrdaya of Dhar matrāta.
Abhidharmakośabhāṣya [bhāṣya] n. bed. text of Vasubandhu's Abhidharmakośa (c. 380); it consists of a gloss [bhāsya] and stanzas [kārikās]; Yaśomitra commented on it |vyākhyā₂|.
abhidharmakośavyākhyā |vyākhyā₂| f. bed. n.p. of the abhidharmakośavyākhyā, commentary on the Abhidharmakośa due to Yaśomitra.
abhidharmasamuccaya | samuccaya | m. lit. np. of the abhidharmasamuccaya "Compendium of Metaphysics", bd. work due to Asanga.

abhidharmahrdaya [hrdaya] n. bed. n.p. of the Abhidharmahṛdaya₁, first summary of the bd doctrine. vaibhāṣika, due to Dharmottara₁ | bed. n.p. of the Abhidharmahrdaya₂, extended version due to Upaśānta.

abhidhā₁ [abhidhā₁] v. [3] pr. (abhidhā₁) dadhāti) pfp. (abhidheya) pp. (abhihita) ved. cou vrir, protect | explain, say, express; address oneself to; name — ps. (abhidhīyate) to call oneself, to name oneself mer. abhidhitsita gram. that which one wishes to express. sa pitāmahanāmnā'bhidhīyate he is called by his grandfather's name. idam eva ca punah punar abhidhīyate because it must be repeated again and again.

abhidhā₁ [agt. abhidhā₁] f. designation, name; denotation; syn. ākhyā₂ | gram. direct denotation, literal meaning of a word; it precedes metaphors and other secondary meanings [guṇavṛtti]; opp. vyañjanā | phil. [mīmāṃsā] expressive power of an utterance. višesyam nābhidhā gacchet kṣīṇaśaktir višeṣaṇe [Kumārila] A noun is not a reference; its expressive power is limited to specifying.
abhidhābhāvanā [bhāvanā] f. phil. [mīmāṃsā] modal realization of the sentence (order, wish, etc.).
abhidhārtha [artha] m. gram. direct denotation, literal meaning of a word; syn. mukhyārtha.

Abhidhāvṛttimātṛkā [vṛttimātṛkā] f. lit. np. from the Abhidhāvṛttimātṛkā "Fundamentals of the Denotative Function", a work of rhetoric by Mukula Bhatta; it recognizes only two modes of signification, the literal sense [mukhyārtha] and the figurative sense [lakṣaṇa], denying the autonomy of meaning
suggested [vyañjanā] postulated by Anandavardhana with the concept of dhvani.

abhidhātṛ [agt. abhidhā₁] amnf abhidhātrī speaker. daivī vāg vyatikīrņeyam aśaktair abhidhātṛbhiḥ anityadarśinām tvasmin vāde buddhiviparyayaḥ || [Vākyapadīya] This divine language has been corrupted by incompetent speakers; but those who maintain that it is not eternal hold an opposite opinion.

abhidhāna [act. abhidhā₁] n. designation, name | gram. morphological expression of a semantic role [kāraka] | soc. “name” of a mantra, expressing its purpose; syn. sādhyanāma — agt. ifc. whose name is (iic.) | bed. glossary, vocabulary of (iic.).
abhidhānakośa | kośa | mr. lexicography, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
abhidhānacintāmaṇi [cintāmaṇi] m. bed. n.p. from the Abhidhānacintāmaņi “Treasure of names”, dictionary/thesaurus [nāmamālā] due to Hemacandra.
abhidhānacūḍāmaṇi [cūḍāmaṇi] m. bed. n.p. from the Abhidhānacūdāmani, Narahari dictionary; cf. Rājanighantu.
abhidhānaratnamālā [ratnamālā] f. bed. n.p. from the abhidhānaratnamālā, Sanskrit lexicon due to Halāyudha₁.
abhidhānābhidheya [abhidheya] n. of. phil. [Dharmakīrti] designation and designated.
abhidhāv [abhidhāv₁] v. [1] pr. (abhidhāvati) pp. (abhidhāvita) pf. (sat) run towards.
abhidheya [pfp. [1] abhidhā₁] amnf abhidheyā to mention, to express — n. gram. meaning, sense | gram. noun.

abhidheyasambandha [sambandha] m. gram. [Abhidhāvṛttimātṛkā] variety of metaphor [lakṣaṇā] involving a lexical relation. turangakāntānanahavyavāhah lit. [Siśupālavadha] underwater fire (from the mouth of the mare, constructed by analogy with baḍavāmukhāgni).
abhidhyā₁ [abhidhyā] v. [1] pr. (abhidhyāyati) pp. (abhidhyāta) to meditate; think about (acc.).
abhidhyā₂ [act. abhidhyā₁] f. desire.
abhidhyāna [act. abhidhyā₁] n. act of thinking about; meditation; aspiration.

abhinand [abhinand] v. [1] pr. (abhinan dati) pr. r. (abhinandate) to rejoice in, to find pleasure in (acc.) | to approve | to welcome, to praise, to congratulate, to compliment; to welcome (acc.) — ca. (abhinandayati) to rejoice. na te vaco'bhinandāmi I do not approve of your speech. abhinandya bravīti having offered his compliments, he said.

abhinánda [act. abhinand] mf abhinandā pleasure, voluptuousness — m. hist. np. of Abhinanda, Gauda Brahmin scholar of Kaśmīra of the late 9th century, author of the Kādambarīkathāsara and the Laghuyoga vasishta | hist. np. of Abhinanda₁, poet of the late 9th century at the court of Prince Pāla Hāravarṣa; he is Sātānandi, son of Satānanda; he is the author of the mahākāvya Rāmacarita — ifc. desire for (iic.).

Abhinandana [act. abhinand] n. rejoicing, joy | congratulations, praise, celebration — m. jn. np. of Abhinandana "Master of Bliss", 4th mythical tīrthankara; his body is golden, the monkey is his symbol. abhinandanam congratulations! abhinandanagrantha volume in honor of a master.
