abhinandanīya [pfp. [2] abhinand] amnf abhinandanīyā worthy of praise; that which should be congratulated.
abhinandin [agt. abhinand] amnf abhinandinī who finds pleasure in; who praises, who declares himself satisfied with.
abhinabhas [Abhinabhas] adv. in the sky.
abhinabhyam [Abhinabhas] adv. towards the sky; in the clouds.
abhinaya [act. abhinī] m. expression, gesture; play, performance by an actor; pantomime, theatrical performance | soc. ritual gesture. sābhinayam adv. by gestures.
Abhinayadarpana [darpana] m. bed. n.p. from the Abhinayadarpana "Gesture Mirror", nāṭyaśāstra manual attributed to Nandikeśvara₁.
abhinava [Abhinava₁] amnf abhinavā brand new; fresh; renewed; modern.

abhinavagupta [gupta] m. hist. n.p. of Rājānaka abhinavagupta, important Kaśmīra philosopher of the end of the 10th century, student of Utpaladeva; he is the author of numerous works of śaivasiddhānta, not. of the Īśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinī; we also owe him a commentary [locana] on the Dhvanyāloka discussing the aesthetics of figures of speech in literature, and the Abhinavabhāratī, commentary on the Nātyaśāstra; he taught at Srinagara the practice of transgression sacrifice [kulayāga], and was considered the incarnation of Bhai rava; Ksemarāja was his disciple; cf. Kramastotra, Gītārthasamgraha₂, Tantrāloka, Paramārthasāra, Parātrimśikāvivarana, Paryantapañcāśikā, Bodha pañcadaśikā, Bhairavastotra, Vivarana₂.
Abhinavabhāratī [bhāratī] f. bed. n.p. from the Abhina vabhāratī, commentary on the nāṭyaśāstra by Abhi navagupta.
Abhinavaśākaṭāyana [śākaṭāyana] m. hist. np. of Abhinavaśākatāyana "new Sākatāyana", epith. of the grammarian Śākatāyana₁ to distinguish it from the ancient Sākaṭāyana₁.

abhinidhā [Abhinidhā] v. [3] pr. (abhini dadhāti) pp. (abhinihita) to place on or in (loc.) — ps. (abhinidhīyate) to be in close contact with (i.) (said from the sandhi between final e/o and initial a).
abhinidhāna [act. abhinidhā] n. phone. sandhi of contact between final e/o and initial a.
abhiniviś [Abhiniviś] v. [6] pr. r. (Abhi nivisate) pp. (abhinivista) to devote oneself to, to dedicate oneself to (acc.) | to unload (river).
abhiniviṣṭa [pp. abhiniviś] amnf abhiniviṣṭā occupied; obstinate; obsessed with, fixed on.

abhiniveśa [act. abhiniviś] m. inclination, obsession, ardent desire; affection towards, devotion towards (loc. iic.) | determination, tenacity, obstinacy; project | phil. [Yoga] attachment to existence; cf. abhiniveśakleśa | med. anxiety; phobia; obsessive disorder.
abhiniveśakleśa | kleśa | m. phil. | Yoga | affliction of attachment to life; fear of death.
abhiniveśin [agt. abhiniviś] amnf abhiniveśinī devoted to, obsessed with; who adores (iic.) obstinate.
abhinihita [pp. abhinidhā] amnf abhinihitā in contact with, touched by (i.) | phone. is said of the contact sandhi between final e/o and initial a; cf. avagraha.
abhinī [Abhinī₁] v. [1] pr. (abhinayati) mi sea, to represent.
abhinetṛ [agt. abhinī] amnf abhinetrī dancer.
abhineya [pfp. [1] abhinī] amnf Abhi neyā to be represented (in the theatre). tasyaikadeśah abhineyārthah kṛtaḥ a portion of it has already been adapted for the theatre.

abhinna [neg. bhinna] amnf abhinnā undivided, unbroken; uninterrupted | unchanged, invariable; constant | math. integer (number) | not different from (abl. iic.) | gram. which is none other than (to paraphrase a semantic role that might not be explicitly expressed). kleśaleśairabhinna not tired in the least. abhinnapada gram. homonymous.
abhipūrṇa [pp. abhipṛ] amnf abhipūrṇā full of (ig).
abhipūrvam [abhipūrvam] adv. in succession.
abhipṛ [abhipṛ] v. [9] pr. (abhipṛṇāti) pp. (abhipūrņa) to fill — ca. (abhipūrayati) to fill, to give in abundance.
abhipravṛt [abhipravṛt] v. [1] pr. r. (abhi pravártate) pp. (abhipravrtta) move forward until.
abhipravṛtta [pp. abhipravṛt] amnf abhipravṛttā being produced; moving forward, on the way | busy with.
abhiprāya [abhiprāya] m. plan, intention, design, project; opinion. etadabhiprāya for this purpose.
abhiprekṣ [abhiprekṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (abhiprekṣate) pp. (abhiprekṣita) to look, see, contemplate.
abhiplava |agt. abhiplu| m. soc. 6-day ceremony, performed 5 times during the gavāmayana sacrifice; cf. āyuḥṣṭoma.
abhiplu [abhiplu] v. [1] pr. r. (abhiplavate) pp. (abhipluta) pf. (sam) to swim or sail towards | to overflow — ca. (abhiplāvayati) to flood.
abhipluta [pp. abhiplu] amnf abhiplutā overwhelmed; flooded | overwhelmed by, drowned under (i.).
abhibhavá [agt. abhibhū] amnf abhib havā powerful, dominant — act. m. predominance defeat; submission to, domination by (i. abl. iic.) lack of respect, contempt | humiliation, mortification.
abhibhāvin [agt. abhibhū] ifc. amnf abhibhāvinī which prevails over, which subdues (iic.).
abhibhāṣ [abhibhāṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (abhibhāṣate) pp. (abhibhāṣita) to speak to, to address, to approach (acc.).
abhibhāṣin [agt. abhibhāṣ] amnf abhibhāṣiṇī who addresses, who approaches.
abhibhū [abhibhū₁] v. [1] pr. (abhibhavati) pp. (abhibhūta) to surpass, dominate, prevail over; to subjugate, subdue, master; to conquer.
abhibhūta [pp. abhibhū] amnf abhibhūtā vanquished, defeated; subjugated, subjugated; humiliated | possessed by (i. iic.). śivaḥ katham abhibhūtaḥ pārvatyā How was Shiva defeated by Pārvatī?
abhibhūti [act. abhibhū] f. superiority.
abhibhūtyojas [ojas] amnf who prevails by force.
abhimata [pp. abhiman] amnf abhi matā desired, esteemed, dear, precious; agreeable — n. desire, wish — m. lover.
abhimatatā [tā] f. state of being pleasant or desired; charm | desire, love. cārutābhimatatām upaninye [Kir.] Their charms made them even more lovable.
abhimati [abhimati] f. infatuation; the act of referring to oneself | arrogance.

abhiman [abhiman] v. [4] pr. r. (abhimányate) v. [8] pr. r. (abhimanuté) pp. (abhimata) to desire; to have bad intentions, to threaten; to hurt | to believe, to presume; to have a high opinion of oneself, to be proud.
abhimantr [abhimantr] v. [10] pr. r. (abhi mantrayate) pp. (abhimantrita) soc. to consecrate with a mantra | to invite a guest with a formula.

abhimanyu [abhimanyu] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the valiant abhimanyu "proud", son of Arjuna and Subhadrā, and therefore also called Saubhadra; he married Uttarā who gave him his son Parīkṣit; on the 13th day of the great battle he succeeded in penetrating the powerful entrenchment [cakravyūha] of the Kauravās army, killed Lakṣmaṇa₁ son of Duryodhana, but was finally treacherously killed by the son of Duḥśāsana at the age of 16; in a previous life [pūrvajanman] he had been Varcā, sent by the gods to Earth to serve the dharma for 16 years before being reunited with his father Candra.
abhimarda [act. abhimrd] m. act of violence, attack.
abhimardana [act. abhimṛd] n. oppression; destruction — agt. amnf abhimardanā who uses violence.
abhimardin [agt. abhimrd] amnf abhimardinī who uses violence — ifc. who press (iic.).
abhimāti [act. abhiman] f. attack plan — agt. amnf insidious | enemy.
abhimāna [act. abhiman] m. pride; arrogance; selfishness; prejudice | phil. erroneous belief.
abhimānacihna [cihna] m. lit. np. from abhimānacihna "who signs with pride", to the author of a dictionary of prākṛta (prior to the 12th century).
abhimānavādin [vādin] amnf abhimānavādinī soc. holding on to the importance of family pride; opp. gotravādin.
abhimānin [agt. abhiman] amnf abhimāninī proud, arrogant — ifc. full of possession, imagining oneself to be or to possess, claiming to be (iic.).
abhimārutam [abhimāruta] adv. against the wind.

abhimukha [abhimukha] amnf abhimukhī turned towards, heading towards (dat. acc.); imminent — ifc. ready to, disposed to (iic.). udagabhimukham me grham my house faces North. abhimukhīkṛ attract attention. abhimukhīkaraṇam gram. act of attracting attention, primary intention of the vocative |sambodhana|. abhimukhībhūta being in the presence or facing (destiny) being favorable to. nikāmadāruņair vāgankuśapādapātair abhi

mukhīkṛtaḥ [DKC.] He rained down upon him a terrible volley of cries, fangs, and kicks. dvīpād anyasmād api madhyād api jalanidher diśo 'py antāt | ānīya jhatiti ghatayati vidhir abhimatam abhimukhībhūtaḥ | [Rat.] If fate turns in your favor, it will procure for you the object of your desires, be it from the ends of the earth, from the heart of the ocean, or even from another continent.
abhimṛd [abhimṛd₁] v. [9] pr. (abhimṛdnāti) v. [1] pr. (abhimardati) to treat violently, to destroy.
abhiya [agt. abhiyā₁] amnf abhiyā approaching; who attacks.
abhiyantṛ [abhiyantṛ] m. mod. engineer; technician.
abhiyā₁ [abhiyā₁] v. [2] pr. (abhiyāti) pp. (abhiyāta) to attack, assail | to approach, obtain; to devote oneself to undertaking — ca. (abhiyāpayati) to bring near.
abhiyāna [act. abhiyā₁] n. approach; the act of attacking.
abhiyukta [pp. abhiyuj] amnf abhiyuktā applied to, competent in (loc.); appointed attacked; blamed soc. (law) accused, charged.
abhiyuktatamā super. the most competent; very competent.

abhiyuktatara [tara] amnf abhiyuktatarā compar. more competent. yatnenānumito yo'rthaḥ kuśalair anumātṛbhiḥ | abhiyuktatarair anyair anyathaivopapādyate [Vākyapadīya] Even a fact carefully demonstrated by expert logicians can later be established differently by others even more competent.

abhiyuj [abhiyuj₁] v. [7] pr. r. (abhiyunkté) pp. (abhiyukta) to summon, invite to (dat.) | to undertake, to begin to; to prepare for (acc. inf.), to apply oneself to — v. [7] pr. (abhiyu nakti) to order, to charge with (loc.); to meet, to attack. vayam svakarmanyabhiyujyāmahe we apply ourselves to our task.
abhiyoktavya [pfp. [3] abhiyuj] amnf abhiyoktavyā (right) accused.
abhiyoktṛ [agt. abhiyuj] amnf abhiyoktrī who attacks — m. enemy | soc. (right) plaintiff.
abhiyoga [act. abhiyuj] m. effort, exercise; perseverance; continuous practice (of (loc. inf.)) assault | soc. (law) complaint, charge, accusation.
abhirakṣ [abhirakṣ] v. [1] pr. (abhirakṣati) pp. (abhiraksita) to defend, to guard; to watch.
abhirakṣita [pp. abhirakṣ] amnf abhirakṣitā guarded, monitored.
abhirata [pp. abhiram] amnf abhiratā who takes pleasure in, who takes care of, who devotes himself to (loc.).
abhirati [act. abhiram] f. pleasure found in loc. .
abhiram [abhiram] v. [1] pr. r. (abhira mate) pp. (abhirata) to be delighted; to take pleasure; to rest — ca. (abhiramayati) to rejoice.
abhirāma [abhiram] amnf abhirāmā pleasant, agreeable; pretty, desirable — ifc. pleasure to (iic.). abhirāmam adv. to please (iic.).
abhirāmatā [tā] f. charm; beauty; good disposition towards.
abhiruc [abhiruc₁] v. [1] pr. r. (abhirocate) pp. (abhirucita) to shine, to gleam; to please (to (dat.)) — ca. (abhirocayati) to enchant, to amuse.
abhirucita [pp. abhiruc] amnf abhi rucitā pleasant, agreeable | satisfied; who appreciates (loc. iic.).
abhiruh [abhiruh₁] v. [1] pr. r. (abhirohati) pp. (abhirūḍha) pf. (sat) ride on; climb.
abhirūpa [abhirūpa] amnf abhirūpā handsome; educated, cultured; loved.
abhilaṣ [abhilaṣ] v. [1] pr. (abhilaṣati) pp. (abhilasita) to desire, to wish.

abhilaṣita [pp. abhilaṣ] amnf abhilaşitā desired — n. desire, wish. abhilaşitārtha [artha] amnf abhilaşitārthā wish-fulfilling. abhilařitārthacintāmani [cintāmani] m. lit. np. of the Abhilasitārthacintāmani, epith. of the encyclopedic work Mānasollāsa "Jewel that satisfies all desires" of the 12th century; it is authoritative in śilpaśāstra .
abhilāṣa [act. abhilaṣ] m. longing, desire; pen song, affection — f. abhilāṣā ifc. desire for (iic.).
abhilāṣaka [agt. abhilaṣ] amnf abhilāṣikā who wishes, who desires (acc.).
abhilāṣin [agt. abhilaṣ] amnf abhilāṣiṇī who wishes, who desires (loc. iic.).
abhilikh [abhilikh] v. [6] pr. (abhilikhati) pp. (abhilikhita) to paint; engrave, inscribe.
abhilikhita [pp. abhilikh] amnf abhilikhitā inscribed, engraved.
abhilī [abhilī] v. [4] pr. r. (abhilīyate) pp. (abhilīna) to attach to, to adhere to (acc.).
abhilīna [pp. abhilī] amnf abhilīnā which adheres to, attached to (acc.).
abhivad [abhivad] v. [1] pr. (abhiva dati) to address someone, to speak to someone. (acc.) — ca. (abhivādayati) to greet, to welcome.
abhivadana [act. abhivad] n. soc. greeting, address.
abhivand [abhivand] v. [1] pr. r. (abhivan date) pp. (abhivandita) to greet respectfully, to pay homage to (acc.).
abhivāñch [abhivāñch] v. [1] pr. (abhivānchati) pp. (abhivānchita) to wish, to aspire to.
abhivāñchā [act. abhivāñch] ifc. f. desire, longing for (iic.).
abhivāñchita [pp. abhivāñch] n. desire, longing.
abhivād [ca. abhivad] v. [10] pr. (abhivādayati) pfp. (abhivādya) to greet, to gather | to have recited; to interpret. abhivādaye devadatto'ham (polite greeting) I, Devadatta, greet you respectfully.
abhivāda [act. ca. abhivad] m. respectful greeting, welcome; opp. ativāda | meaning, interpretation.

abhivādana [act. ca. abhivad] n. soc. act of welcoming and respectful greeting a person: one says their gotra and name, and pronounces "namah"; it is preceded by the pratyutthāna, and may be followed by the upasamgrahana | interpretation.
abhivādin [agt. abhivad] amnf abhivādinī who welcomes [["who explains"] interpreter, commentator.
abhivādya [pfp. [1] abhivad] amnf abhivādyā to greet — abs. ind. having greeted.
abhivijval [abhivijval] v. [1] pr. (abhivi jvalati) to lick with flames, to throw flames.
abhividhā [abhividhā₁] v. [3] pr. (abhivi dadhāti) to put in contact with acc. .
abhividhi [abhividhā] f. inclusive interval of its bounds; it can be temporal [kālika] or spa
tial [daiśika].
abhivīkṣ [abhivīkṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (abhivīkṣate) pp. (abhivīkṣita) to see, to look; to perceive; to consider.
abhivṛ₁ [abhivṛ₁] ca. (abhivārayati) to set aside, to stop.
abhivṛ₂ [abhivṛ₂] v. [9] pr. r. (abhivṛṇīte) to choose, to prefer.
abhivṛt [abhivṛt₁] v. [1] pr. r. (abhivartate) pp. (abhivrtta) to go to; to approach, to go towards (acc.).
abhivrdh [abhivrdh₁] v. [1] pr. r. (abhi vardhate) pp. (abhivrddha) to grow, to expand, to become important — ca. (abhivardhayati) to increase, to strengthen.

abhivṛṣ [abhivṛṣ] v. [1] pr. (abhivarṣati) pp. (abhivṛṣṭa) to rain; to water. iṣuvarṣeṇābhivarṣan by raining down arrows. abhivarṣati kāmairyah parjanyam pṛthivīmiva | sa kāmapāśaparyasto mahātejā mahīpatiḥ | [Rām.] This illustrious king (Dasaratha), who waters the Earth with favors like Parjanya, is now trapped in the snares of passion.
abhivyakta [pp. abhivyañj] amnf abhivyaktā revealed; manifest, evident. abhivyaktam adv. manifestly.
abhivyakti [abhivyakti] f. appearance, manifestation.
abhivyañj [abhivyañj] pp. (abhivyakta) p.s. (abhivyajyate) to reveal oneself, to manifest oneself.
abhivyañjaka [agt. abhivyañj] amnf abhivyañjikā which manifests, which reveals; which indicates, which shows.
abhivyañjana [act. abhivyañj] n. act of making manifest.
abhivyāpaka [abhivyāpaka] amnf abhivyāpakā gram. (rule) including (acc.).
abhivyāhāra [agt. abhivyāhr] m. enunciation; sentence.
abhivyāhṛ [abhivyāhṛ] v. [1] pr. (abhivyāharati) pp. (abhivyāhṛta) pf. (sam) to pronounce, to say; converse.
abhivyāhṛta [pp. abhivyāhṛ] amnf abhivyāhṛtā pronounced, said | addressed — n. that which has been said | that which is said.
abhiśap [abhiśap] v. [1] pr. (abhiśapati) pp. (abhiśapta) to curse, to utter a curse, to launch an imprecation — ca. (abhiśāpayati) to conjure, to solemnly implore someone.
abhiśapta [pp. abhiśap] amnf abhiśaptā cursed | slandered.
abhiśāp [ca. abhiśap] v. [10] pr. (abhiśāpayati) to conjure, to solemnly implore someone.
abhiśāpa [act. ca. abhiśap] m. bewitchment, spell; curse, imprecation; anathema, interdict.
abhiśiras [abhiśiras] amnf who has their head turned towards (acc.).
abhiśuc [abhiśuc₁] v. [1] pr. (abhiśocati) pp. (abhiśocita) to bitterly regret, to mourn acc. .
abhiṣava [act. abhiṣu] m. soc. ritual pressing of soma | fermentation; distillation | ritual ablution.
abhiṣávaṇa [act. abhiṣu] n. soc. ritual pressing of soma — agt. f. abhiṣavaṇī pl. utensils for pressing soma.
abhiṣikta [pp. abhiṣic] amnf abhiṣiktā anointed, sprinkled.
abhiṣic [abhisic] v. [6] pr. (abhiṣiñcati) pp. (abhisikta) to consecrate; to give royal anointing, to consecrate — ca. (abhisecayati) to consecrate.
abhiṣu [abhisu₂] v. [5] pr. (abhiṣunoti) pp. (abhisuta) ved. press the soma for sacrifice.

abhişeka [act. abhişic] m. consecration; ritual water; ritual ablution, ritual bath; consecration. kṛtābhiṣekaḥ having received royal anointing | initiated into a religious path. nābhiṣeko na saṃskāraḥ siṃhasya kriyate vane There is in nature neither consecration nor anointing of the lion. abhişekanāṭaka [nāṭaka] n. lit. np. of the abhişeka nāṭaka, a play by Bhāsa based on the Rāmāyaṇa. abhişekavidhi [vidhi] m. soc. rite of initiation.
abhiṣec [ca. abhiṣic] v. [10] pr. (abhiṣecayati) pfp. (abhiṣecanīya) to consecrate.
abhiṣecana [act. abhiṣic] n. ritual sprinkling.
abhiṣecanīya [pfp. [2] abhiṣic] amnf abhișecanīyā concerning the royal consecration worthy of the royal anointing — m. ved. sprinkling consecrating the king in the rājasūya ceremony.
abhiṣṭambh [abhistambh] v. [5] pr. (abhistabhnoti) v. [9] pr. (abhistabhnāti) pp. (abhiṣṭabdha) to immobilize.
abhistava [obj. abhistu] m. lit. praise, eulogy. স্পিষ্ট abhiṣṭu [abhistu] v. [2] pr. (abhiṣṭauti) pp. (abhistuta) to praise, celebrate, glorify.

abhiṣṭuta [pp. abhiṣṭu] amnf abhiṣṭutā celebrated, glorified; consecrated. স্থানিষ্ঠা abhiṣṭhā [abhisthā₁] v. [1] pr. (abhitiṣṭhati) pr. r. (abhitisthate) pp. (abhisthita) to trample, trample | to dominate, to conquer; to spread over (acc.); to advance towards, to march upon (acc.).
abhíṣṭhita [pp. abhiṣṭhā] amnf abhisthitā trampled, crushed; subdued, defeated. vasisthābhisthitāh led by Vasistha.
abhiṣyand [abhisyand] v. [1] pr. r. (abhisyandate) to gush forth, to overflow (liquids) | to invade (vines).
abhiṣyanda [act. abhiṣyand] m. effusion; gushing | med. discharge from the eyes.
abhisyandin [agt. abhisyand] amnf abhisyandiṇī med. that causes discharges; effusion, fluxion.
abhiṣvaṅga [act. abhiṣvañj] m. affection towards, great attachment to (loc. i.).
abhiṣvaṅgin [agt. abhiṣvañj] amnf abhisvanginī intensely attached to, crazy about (loc. i.).
abhiṣvañj [abhisvañj] v. [1] pr. r. (abhisvajate) pp. (abhisvakta) to embrace, to hug, to press in one's arms.

abhisaṃviś [abhisaṃviś] v. [6] pr. (abhisamviśati) to become incorporated into, to merge into, to dissolve into. ānandāddhyeva khalvimāni bhūtāni jāyante ānandena jātāni jīvanti | ānandaṃ prayantyabhisamviśantīti || From joy itself all creatures are engendered, by joy beings live, by returning to joy (at their death) they merge into it.

abhisaṃsmṛ [abhisaṃsmṛ] v. [1] pr. (abhisaṃsmarati) pp. (abhisaṃsmṛta) to remember, to recall (acc. g.); to think of — ca. (abhisaṃsmārayati) to remind someone of something (acc.) to someone. acc. g. .
abhisamdhā₁ var. abhisandhā₁ [abhi saṃdhā₁] v. [3] pr. (abhisaṃdadhāti) pp. (abhisamhita) to aim; to have in mind, to think of deceiving.

abhisaṃdhā₂ var. abhisandhā₂ [abhisamdhā₁] ifc. f. affirmation, word. pratijnābhisamdhāmpālayati he keeps his word. abhisaṃdhāna var. abhisandhāna [na] n. connection; word | deception, art of deceiving.
abhisamdhi var. abhisandhi [abhisamdhi] m. deliberate declaration; intention, design agreement, convention | deception.
abhisamaya [act. abhisami] m. agreement | bd. intuitive understanding.

Abhisamayālankāra [alankāra] m. bd. n.p. the Abhisamayālankāra "Presentation of clear understanding", commentary on the Prajñāpāramitā. abhisamayālankāranāmaprajñāpāramitopadeśaśā stra lit. n.p. from the Abhisamayālankāranāmaprajñā pāramitopadeśaśāstra, text by Maitreyanātha.
abhisami [abhisami] v. [2] pr. (abhisa meti) pp. (abhisamita) ved. to gather, to meet, to assemble (at (acc.)).
abhisambandh var. abhisambandh [abhi saṃbandh] v. [9] pr. (abhisaṃbadhnāti) pp. (abhisambaddha) to refer to (acc.), to mean.
abhisambandha var. abhisambandha [act. abhisambandh] m. relation with (i.); link (not. sexual) | gram. word order in the sentence.
abhisārikā [abhisārikā] f. libertine; adulterous woman | lit. type of libertine heroine of Indian theatre, who goes out at night to meet her lover.

abhisārikāvañcitaka [vañcitaka] m. lit. np. from the drama abhisārikāvañcitaka "Deceived by the liber tine", attributed to Viśākhadeva; it tells how Padmavatī, a wife of King Udayana, is wrongly exiled for killing one of her sons, and becomes a tri bale in the forest; the king meets her during a hunt, does not recognize her and falls in love; her innocence is eventually established.
abhisṛ [abhisṛ] v. [1] pr. (abhisarati) pp. (abhisṛta) to approach.
abhisneha [abhisneha] m. affection; desire.
abhihata [pp. abhihan] amnf abhi hatā struck, attacked; wounded, killed | beaten (drum) | math. multiplied.
abhihan [abhihan₁] v. [2] pr. (abhihanti) pp. (abhihata) to strike, to knock down; to kill | to beat (drum).
abhihāra [act. abhihṛ] m. snatch theft; sudden attack.
abhihāsa [abhihāsa] m. joke.

abhihita [pp. abhidhā₁] amnf abhi hitā said, signified; expressed, designated; explained; expli cite | gram. actant whose role | kāraka | is expressed by the predicate, and put in the nominative case to agree as subject.
abhihitatva [tva] n. gram. the state of being expressed or named.
abhihitānvaya [anvaya] m. gram. compositional meaning of a sentence from the meaning of its words by their rearrangement into syntagms.
abhihitānvayavāda [vāda] m. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] school of linguistic philosophy of Kumārila [bhāṭṭa]; opp. anvitābhidhāvāda.
abhihitānvayavādin [vādin] amnf abhi hitānvayavādinī phil. [Mīmāṃsā] supporter of this school.

abhihṛ [abhihṛ₁] v. [1] pr. (abhiharati) pp. (abhihrta) to offer | to remove, to snatch, to tear away — ca. (abhihārayati) to present, to bring. abhī₁ [abhii] v. [2] pr. (abhyeti) pr. r. (abhīte) pp. (abhīta₁) to approach, to go towards, to join; to become incarnate in.
abhīkṣṇa [abhikṣaṇa] amnf abhīkṣṇā constant; perpetual. abhīkṣṇam repeatedly, constantly, perpetually.
abhīkṣṇaśas [śas] adv. constantly.
abhīta₁ [pp. abhī₁] amnf abhītā ap proxi.
abhīta₁ [neg. bhīta] amnf abhītā without fear; who is not afraid.
abhītavat [vat] adv. without fear.
abhītta [abhī₃datta] amnf abhīttā conferred.
abhīps [des. abhyāp] v. [1] pr. (abhīpsati) pr. r. (abhīpsate) pp. (abhīpsita) to seek, to desire, to wish.
abhīpsu [agt. des. abhyāp] amnf desirous of obtaining, who seeks (acc.).
abhīśu [related to abhyaś] m. bridle | pl. reins | rays of light.
abhīṣ [abhiiṣ₁] v. [6] pr. (abhīcchati) pp. (abhīṣṭa) aim at, tend to.
abhīṣu [abhīśu] m. id. mucyantām abhīṣavaḥ loosens the reins!
abhīṣumat |mat| amnf abhīṣumatī brilliant.
abhīṣṭa [pp. abhīṣ] amnf abhīṣṭā desired, loved, dear — n. wish.
abhīṣṭadevatā | devatā | f. phil. goddess of choice (invoked especially at the moment of dying).
abhukta [neg. bhukta] amnf abhuktā not consumed; not eaten; not enjoyed or used; unused | that which has not been consumed.
abhūta [neg. bhūta] amnf abhūtā inexis tant; which has never existed.
abhūtatadbhava | tadbhava | m. gram. emergence of new language forms; standardization of a dialect.
abhūtaparikalpa [parikalpa] n. bd. [vijñānavāda] consciousness (which imagines the non-existent).
ábhūti [opp. bhūti] f. non-existence; misery | misfortune, calamity.
abhūtitā [tā] f. condition of nonexistence.
abhūmi [opp. bhūmi] f. unsuitable place for, unfit for, beyond the reach of (g.) thing or event beyond (g.). sa satkāro mama manorathānāmapyabhūmiḥ This reception exceeded all my expectations.
abheda [opp. bheda] m. absence of distinction, non-difference; identity | atomicity, indivisibility | phil. monism. vabayorabhedah phon. absence of distinction between the sounds 'va' and 'ba'.
abhedagraha [graha] m. phil. [Nyāya] perception of nondifference; opp. bhedāgraha.
abhedavākya [vākya] n. phil. verbal expression of nondifference.
abhedānanda | ānanda | m. undivided joy.
abhedopacāra [upacāra] m. gram. process of indistinction; it allows the distinction between subject [viśesya] and predicate [viśesana] to be relaxed in a nominal sentence.

abhedya [neg. bhedya] amnf abhedyā that which must not be divided or broken; indivisible | that which must not be revealed (secret). ācāryavāgabhedyā the word of the master must not be refuted | 1434160 [kaṭapayādi]; interpreted in numbers of years from the beginning of the kaliyuga, year 825 of the Gregorian era; it is associated with Shankara₁.
abhoga [priv. bhoga₂] m. lack of enjoyment; frustration (of (loc.)). abhogādiṣṭe vastuni by the frustration of the object of desire.
abhojana [absence bhojana] n. fasting — neg. amnf abhojanā inedible.
abhojyānna [neg. bhojyānna] amnf abhojyānnā soc. unfit to prepare the meal of a brāhmaṇa (said of an impure śūdra).
abhautika [neg. bhautika] amnf abhautikī phil. non-material; immaterial; subtle.
abhyakta [pp. abhyañj] amnf abhyaktā anointed; adorned, decorated | soiled.
abhyagni [abhiagni] adv. towards the fire. abhyagni śalabhāh patanti the moths are attracted to the flames.
abhyanga [act. abhyanj] m. anointing; oil massage | ointment.
abhyangasnāna [snāna] n. soc. perfumed bath, taken on the day of dhanvantaritrayodaśī (mod. Dhanteras).

abhyañj [abhiañj] v. [7] pr. (abhyanakti) pp. (abhyakta) to anoint; to adorn — pr. r. (abhyankte) to anoint oneself. yā'nkte tasyai kāṇaḥ | yā'bhyankte tasyai duścarmā She who adorns herself becomes one-eyed; She who adorns herself too much becomes leprous.
abhyáñjana [act. abhyañj] n. anointing; my ointment | ointment; cosmetic.
abhyadhika [abhiadhika] amnf abhyadhikā additional; in addition.
abhyanujñā₂ [abhianujñā₁] v. [9] pr. (abhyanujānāti) pr. r. (abhyanujānīte) to approve, permit, consent, authorize; to let go, to give leave.
abhyanujñā₂ [abhyanujñā₂] f. assent; consent, permission; leave.

abhyantara [abhiantara] amnf abhyantarā interior, contained within (iic. loc. g.) | secret; initiated into (loc. g.) — m. close, intimate, confidential; opp. bāhya — n. interior; interval, space. abhyantarīkṛ initiate; introduce. sarvaviśrambheṣvabhyaṃtarīkaraṇīyā She must have access to all confidential information.
abhyarc [abhiṛc₁] abs. (abhyarcya) to celebrate; to revere.
abhyarcana [act. abhyarc] n. celebration, reverence.
abhyarth [abhiarth] v. [10] pr. r. (abhyar thayate) pp. (abhyarthita) to ask, solicit, implore.
abhyarthita [pp. abhyarth] amnf abhyarthitā prayed.
abhyarh [abhiarh] v. [1] pr. (abhyarhati) pr. r. (abhyarhate) pp. (abhyarhita) to honor — ca. (abhyarhayati) (addressed to a friend in correspondence) to pay respects to.
abhyarhaṇa [act. abhyarh] n. homage; reverence.
abhyarhaṇīya [pfp. [2] abhyarh] amnf abhyarhanīyā which must be revered; venerable.
abhyarhita [pp. abhyarh] amnf abhya rhitā most honored; venerable.
abhyavahārin [agt. abhyavahr] amnf abhyavahārinī who gorges himself; glutton.
abhyavahārya [pfp. [1] abhyavahr] amnf abhyavahāryā edible — n. food. sarvatraudarikasya abhyavahāryam eva visayah For the glutton, everything is food.

abhyavahr [abhiavahr] v. [1] pr. (abhya vaharati) pp. (abhyavahṛta) pfp. (abhyavahārya) to enjoy, to eat; stuff yourself — ca. (abhya vahārayati) to eat; to eat. satrnam abhyavaharati he swallows everything, stuffs and balls. odanam bhunkṣva saktūn piba dhānāḥ khādetyevāyam abhyavaharati Eat rice! Drink orgeat! Devour roasted barley! This is how he stuffs himself. te ca dvidhārocakinaḥ satṛṇābhyavahāriṇaśca lit. [KM.] (Poetry lovers) are of two kinds: those who are picky, and those who swallow everything, stuff and ball.
abhyaś [abhiaś₁] v. [5] pr. (abhyaśnóti) pr. r. (abhyaśnuté) to reach, to gain; to dominate.
abhyas₁ [abhias₁] opt. (abhiṣyāt) ved. on pass | dry down. yad atra mām abhisyāt so that it resonates with me.
abhyas₂ [abhias₂] v. [4] pr. (abhyasyati) pp. (abhyasta) pf. (sam) to throw towards | to apply oneself to, to devote oneself to, to practice; to study, to learn, to repeat.
abhyasana [act. abhyas₂] n. practice, exercise.
abhyasanīya [pfp. [2] abhyas₂] amnf abhyasanīyā which must be practiced or studied | gram. which must be duplicated.
abhyasitavya [pfp. [3] abhyas₂] amnf abhyasitavyā which must be practiced or studied.
abhyasūya [abhiasūya] v. [11] pr. (abhyasūyati) v. [11] pr. r. (abhyasūyate) to be indignant.
abhyasūyaka |ka| amnf abhyasūyakā indignant; hateful.
abhyasūyā [act. abhyasūya] f. indignation; anger, hatred.

abhyasta [pp. abhyas₂] amnf abhyastā accumulated | practiced, exercised; repeated, learned by heart, studied | gram. duplicated (said of verbal roots) — n. gram. duplicated part of a verbal base (like dadā).
abhyāgata |pp. abhyāgam| amnf abhyāgatā arrived; manifested — m. unforeseen guest (opp. atithi invited guest). kramāt abhyāgata inherited.
abhyāgam [abhiāgam] pp. (abhyāgata) to approach; to visit | myth. said of Vișnu manifesting himself as (not. Kṛṣṇa). cintām abhyāgam to come to mind, to occur to oneself.
abhyātma [abhiātma] amnf abhyātmā directed towards oneself. abhyātmam adv. towards oneself.
abhyāp [abhiāp] v. [5] pr. (abhyāpnóti) pr. r. (abhyāpnuté) pp. (abhyāpta) to reach — des. (abhīpsati) to seek, to wish — ca. (abhyāpayati) to cause to reach the goal; to go to the end.
abhyāvartam [abs. abhyāvṛt] ind. repeatedly.
abhyāvartin [agt. abhyāvṛt] amnf abhyāvartinī that approaches; that returns repeatedly | that returns (days).
abhyāvṛt [abhiāvṛt₁] pp. (abhyāvṛtta) to approach (acc.) — ca. (abhyāvartayati) to repeat.
abhyāvṛtti [act. abhyāvṛt] f. repetition.
abhyāśa [act. abhyaś] amnf abhyāśā near; imminent — m. proximity, neighborhood. abhyāśam var. abhyāse in the neighborhood (from g. abl.).

abhyāsa [act. abhyas₂] m. repetition, recitation; diligent exercise, study, application, usage, practice, habit | soc. regular spiritual practice | gram. reduplication (in a base verb); not. its first syllable | lit. repetition of a word. avicchedena śīlanamabhyāsaḥ lit. [KM.] Diligent exercise consists of practicing without ceasing.
abhyāsavat [vat] amnf abhyāsavatī accustomed; practiced, trained.
abhyutkram [abhiutkram] v. [1] pr. (utkrāmati) ca. (abhyutkramayati) to make go away.

abhyutthā [abhiutthā] v. [1] pr. (abhyuttiṣṭhati) pp. (abhyutthita) to rise To welcome (acc.) | to enter into rebellion; to abstain from abl. . te nābhyuttiṣṭhanti gurūn they do not rise to welcome their elders.
abhyutthāna [act. abhyutthā] n. act of standing up out of politeness | rebellion | acquisition of authority, effectiveness; manifestation (destiny).
abhyutthita [pp. abhyutthā] amnf abhyutthitā raised to welcome | manifested; ready.

abhyudaya [act. abhyudi] m. act of rising; not. rising of a star; beginning of a phenomenon, not. twilight | happiness, prosperity; fortune; success; heroism; triumph | soc. social utility; social benefit; pious work | religious festival, celebration. śāstrapūrvake prayoge 'bhyudayaḥ Success is achieved by studying theory before practice.
abhyudi [abhiudi] v. [2] pr. (abhyudéti) pp. (abhyudita) to rise (celestial bodies); to engage in combat; to prosper.
abhyudita [pp. abhyudi] amnf abhyu ditā risen (sun); engaged in battle; prosperous.
abhyudyata [abhiudyata] amnf abhyudyatā raised | offered | ready to, engaged in (inf. dat. loc. iic.).
abhyupagata [pp. abhyupagam] amnf abhyupagatā approached; arrived | consented, agreed; admitted — n. concession.
abhyupagantṛ [agt. abhyupagam] amnf abhyupagantrī who consents, who admits, who concedes.
abhyupagam [abhiupagam] v. [1] pr. (abhyupagacchati) pp. (abhyupagata) to move towards (acc.) | to grant, consent, admit.
abhyupagama [abhyupagama] m. act of approaching, of arriving at | agreement, contract; assent, concession.
abhyupāya [act. abhyupe₁] m. commitment, promise | effective means.

abhyupāyana [act. abhyupe₁] n. incentive. abhyupe₁ [abhiupe₁] v. [2] pr. (abhyupaiti) pp. (abhyupeta) to approach, go towards; to go into, enter into such a state; to choose, consent to — ps. (abhyupeyate) to be approved, be admitted. abhyupe₁ [abhiupe₁] v. [2] pr. (abhyupaiti) to approach, come towards. śaranam abhyupe₁ to seek refuge.
abhyupeta [pp. abhyupe₁] amnf abhyu petā approached; consented, promised.
abhyūh [abhiūh] v. [1] pr. (abhūhati) pp. (abhūdha) pfp. (abhyūhya, abhyūhitavya) to infer; to guess.
abhyūha [act. abhyūh] m. inference, deduction; reasoning.
abhye [abhie] v. [2] pr. (abhyéti) to approach, to go towards, to head towards; to join.
abhrá [apbhara] n. rain cloud, fog; cloud, cloud; atmosphere, sky | math. symb. the number zero — v. [11] pr. r. (abhrāyate) to be covered with clouds | lat. imber, umbra; fr. ombre.
abhrāvakāśika [avakāśika] amnf abhrāvakāśikā which exposes itself to the rain.
abhrita |ita| amnf abhritā covered in clouds.
abhram |acc. abhra| iic.
abhramliha [liha] amnf abhramlihā ["who licks the clouds" | who touches the sky; grandiose.
abhrānta [neg. bhrānta] amnf abhrāntā phil. [Dharmakīrti] not erroneous; correct.
abhrānti [opp. bhrānti] f. phil. absence of error or perplexity.
√ am v. [1] pr. (ámati) aor. [3] (āmamat) pp. (amita₂) ved. to go towards | to hurt, to harm — ca. (āmáyati) to make sick | to be sick.
amangala [priv. mangala] amnf amangalā which is not of good omen; unfavorable — n. misfortune. pratihatam amangalam misfortune is averted (formula to ward off a bad omen).
amada [priv. mada] amnf amadā without passion, impassive; without joy.
amanas [priv. manas] amnf without perception; without thought | silly.
amanaska [ka] amnf amanaskā id.
amanaskayoga [yoga] m. phil. yoga of the cessation of thought | lit. np. of amanaskayoga, text attributed to Goraknātha (11th-12th centuries).
amanībhāva [amanasbhāva] m. phil. [yoga] state of cessation of thought.
amantu [priv. mantu] amnf without intention.
amantra [priv. mantra] amnf amantrā not accompanied by Vedic texts | not authorized to know Vedic texts
ámanda [nég. manda] amnf amandā ac tif; joyful, blossoming; intense |abundant; important. amandam adv. intensely. amandānandasandoham vindate he obtains the abundance of intense joy.
amára |priv. mara| amnf amarā immortal — m. god.

amarakantaka [kantaka] n. geo. np. of the "peak of the immortals" Amarakantaka, in the Vindhya Mountains, where the Narmadā and Soṇā rivers originate; it is an important pilgrimage site. Amarakoșa |koșa| m. lit. np. of the Amarakoșa or "Thesaurus of Amarasimha", principal Sanskrit lexicon by Amarasimha (6th century); also called Nāmalingānuśāsana and Trikāndaśeṣa. Amarakoșodghāṭana [udghāṭana] n. lit. np. of the Amarakosodghāṭana "Revelation of the Lexicon", commentary on the Amarakoșa by Kṣīrasvāmī.
amaratā [tā] f. phil. immortality; divine condition.
amaratva |tva| n. id.
Amaranātha | nātha | m. geo. np. of Amaranātha "Immortal Lord", Shaivite sanctuary cave in Kaśmīra, housing an ice linga .
amaravat [vat] adv. like the gods.
Amaraśakti [śakti] m. lit. [PT.] np. of King Amaraśakti "Eternal Power", who asked Vișnuśarmā to educate his three idiotic sons.
Amarasara [sara] m. bed. n.p. of Amarasara, abbreviated from Amarakoșa due to MS Gole and KG Oka (1915).

amarasimha [simha] m. hist. np. of amarasimha "Immortal Lion", Buddhist lexicographer, author of the Amarakoşa, also called Nāmalingānuśāsana; he is said to have been one of the nine jewels [navaratna] of King Vikramāditya's court. amarasimho hi pāpīyān sarvam bhāsyam acūcurat amarasimha, truly what a scoundrel, he stole the whole language!
amarārāma [ārāma] m. geo. de np. l'amarārāma, one of the 5 sanctuary-gardens śaiva [pañcārāmakṣetra] at Amarāvatī₁; it is said that his śivalinga amareśvara was installed there by Indra.

Amarāvatī₁ [vat] f. myth. np. of Amarāvatī₁, "the mortal Im" capital of Indra; she moves in the air geo. np. of Amarāvatī₁, capital of the country of Andhra on the river Kṛṣṇā; there is a stūpa from the 2nd century; it is a great place of pilgrimage śaiva, with the amarārāma temple | geo. np. of the principality of Amarāvatī₁ of the Hinduized kingdom of Campā₁ in South Vietnam.
amareśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of the amareśvara, śivalinga installed by Indra at the amarārāma temple.
amarottama [uttama] amnf amarottamā supreme among the gods.

amaropama | upama | amnf amaropamā sem blable to a god. Amaru m. lit. np. of King Amaru or Amaruka, presumed author of the Amarusataka; he is said to have lived in the 8th century; a legend tells that Sankarācārya magically entered his dying body to experience sexuality with his wives.

amaruśataka [śataka] n. lit. np. of the amaruśataka, a collection of 100 poems attributed to King Amaru; of erotic flavor [śṛṅgārarasa], it deals with the game of love; Ravicandra gave a hidden ascetic interpretation of it, attributing the poem to Sankarācārya incarnated in Amaru.
ámartya [neg. martya] amnf amartyā immortal.
amarṣa [priv. marṣa] amnf amarṣā impa tient; qui ne pene pas (iic.) — m. impatience; colère.
amarṣaṇa [neg. marṣaṇa] amnf amarṣaṇā impatient, irritable; irritable — opp. n. im patience of.
amarşin [neg. marşin] amnf amarşin्ī impatient, irritated; who doesn't let anything pass.
amala [priv. mala] amnf amalā clean, impeccable; immaculate, pure — m. crystal — n. talc — f. amalā myth. np. of amalā, epith. of Lakṣmī "the immaculate one".
Amalānanda [ānanda] m. hist. np. of the Vedantic philosopher Amalānanda Sarasvatī₂, author of the Kal pataru, commentary on the Bhāmatī.
amahātman [priv. mahātman] amn without greatness of soul, without nobility; petty.
amā |related to asau| adv. at home, together. amā kṛ to stay at home. amā vas to live together.
amānta [anta] amnf amāntā which ends with the new moon — m. astr. calendar whose beginning of the month starts at the new moon; it is used in South India; syn. amāvāsyānta; opp. pūrnimānta.
Amāvasu |vasu| m. myth. np. of Amāvasu, son of Purūravā and Urvaśī; he founded the kingdom of Kanyākubja.
amāvāsyā [vāsya₁] f. astr. ["when the moon and the sun dwell together"] neomenia, (night of) new moon | var. amāvasyā id.
amāvāsyānta [anta] m. astr. calendar of South India, where the months begin at the new moon; syn. amānta; opp. pūrnimānta.
amāmsa [absence māmsa] n. absence of meat — priv. amnf amāmsā without flesh.
amāṃsāśana [neg. māṃsāśana] amnf amāṃsāśanā who abstains from eating meat.
amātṛka [amātṛka] amnf amātṛkā who has no mother.
amātya [amātya] m. who lives in the same house; close relative; companion | soc. ["who is of the royal household"] minister, advisor to the king. amātyadevadatta the minister Devadatta.
amāni iic. amānin.
amānitā |tā| f. modesty; humility.
amānitva [tva] n. id.
amānin [neg. mānin] amnf amāninī modest, humble.
amānuṣa [neg. mānuṣa] amnf amānuṣī ["non-human"] of animal nature | of divine nature.
amāya [neg. māya] amnf amāyā that does not deceive — f. amāyā absence of deception; sincerity. amāyayā sincerely.
amāyika [neg. māyika] amnf amāyikā that does not deceive; sincere | not illusory, real.
amita₁ [neg. mita₁] amnf amitā immeasurable, indefinite; immense, boundless, infinite.
amita₂ [pp. am] amnf amitā wounded; my lade.
amitagati [gati] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara king amitagati of Vakrapura, ally of Na ravāhanadatta, to whom he gave as a wife his daughter Sulocanā₁.
Amitābha [ābhā₂] m. bd. np. of Amitābha "Eternal Light", guardian jina of the West in the Mahāyāna pantheon, represented in gen. in dhyāna mudrā; his paradise is Sukhāvatī₁.
amitāyus [āyus] m. bd. np. of Amitāyu "the Eternal", epith. of Amitābha.
amitaujas [ojas] amnf whose energy is limitless.
amítra [priv. mitra] amnf amitrā enemy — v. [11] pr. (amitrayati) to be hostile towards.
amitrakhāda [khāda] amnf amitrakhādā "devourer of enemies", title of glory, notably of King Bindusāra.
amitraghāta | ghāta | amnf amitraghātī | "killer of enemies" | title of glory, notably of King Bindusāra.
amitrasenā [senā] f. enemy army.
amithuna [neg. mithuna] amnf ami thunā not composed of pairs; not paired.
amī [nom. pl. asau] ind. those.
amībhis [i. pl. asau] ind. by those.
amībhyas [dat. pl. asau] ind. to those — abl. of those.
amīmāṃsya [neg. mīmāṃsya] amnf amīmāmsyā indisputable, which cannot be doubted.
Amīla m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the daitya king Amīla, son of Hiranyākṣa, father of Kalāvatī.
amīva [am] n. sorrow, pain — m. evil spirit — f. amīvā disease; scourge, plague.
amīvacātana [cātana] amnf amīvacātanī that wards off disease, that heals.
amīvahan [han₂] amnf amīvahanī that soothes the pain | that kills the evil spirit.
amīṣām [g. pl. adas] ind. of those.
amīṣu [loc. pl. adas] ind. in those.
amu iic. adas.
amuka |ka| amnf amukā so-and-so |something; thing, whatchamacallit.
amútra |tra| adv. over there, there; opp. iha | up there, in the other world, in the beyond.
amukta |neg. mukta| amnf amuktā not freed, captive | phil. not freed from reincarnation (not freed from Rāhu) eclipsed (Moon) — n. weapon not thrown (that one keeps in hand).
amútas [adv. adas] adv. from there; opp. itas [in that direction, by that way, towards there.
amunā [i. adas] ind. by that.
amum |acc. asau| ind. that.
amuyā [i. asau] ind. by that — adv. Thus.
amuyos [g. du. adas] ind. of these two, of those two — loc. in these two, in those two.
amuṣmāt [abl. adas] ind. of this.
amuṣmin [loc. adas] ind. over there.
amuşmai [dat. adas] ind. to this.
amuṣya [g. adas] ind. of this.
amuṣyām [loc. asau] ind. in that one.
amuṣyās [abl. asau] ind. of that one — g. id.
amuṣyai [dat. asau] ind. to that one. amū [nom. du. asau] ind. those two; those two — acc. those two.
amūḍha [neg. mūḍha] amnf amūḍhā without perplexity; with clear ideas — n. pl. phil. |Sāṃkhya| the 5 subtle elements of perception |tanmātra|.
amūn [noun. pl. asau] ind. those.
amūbhis [i. pl. asau] ind. by those.
amūbhyas [dat. pl. asau] ind. to those — abl. of those.
amūbhyām [i. du. asau] ind. by these two; by those two — dat. to these two; to those two — abl. of these two; of those two.
amūm [acc. asau] ind. that one.
ámūrta [priv. mūrta] amnf amūrtā in corporeal; informal | phil. immaterial — m. myth. np. of Amūrta epith. of Shiva the "Incorporeal".
amūrtatva [vat] n. phil. [Pratyabhijñā] incorporality, a concept developed in the Sivadṛṣṭi of Somānanda.
Amūrtarajas [rajas] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the king Amūrtarajas or Amūrtarajasa, son of Kuśa₁; he founded the city of Dharmāranya.
amūrtārtha [artha] amnf amūrtārthā gram. (word) not denoting a substance.
amūlá [priv. mūla] amnf amūlā without foundation; without authority, without proof, unjustified — f. amūlā bulbous plant.
amūlya |neg. mūlya| amnf amūlyā which is priceless.
amūṣām [g. pl. asau] ind. of those.
amūṣu |loc. pl. asau| ind. in those.
amūs [nom. pl. asau] ind. those — acc. id.

amṛta [neg. mṛta] amnf amṛtā immor tel; imperishable — m. myth. epith. of various gods, of Dhanvantari, etc. — n. immortality; pa radis; eternity | myth. Nectar, ambrosia, source of immortality of the gods; beverage brought by Dhanvantari during the churning of the ocean of milk |kṣīrodamathana|, it was distributed to the gods by Mohinī | voluntary alms, suitable means of subsistence for a brahmin |satkarman| — f. amṛtā bio. bot. Tinospora cordifolia; cf. guḍūcī | name of various plants, women and goddesses | gr. o ; fr. ambrosia.
amṛtatvá [tva] n. immortality.
Amrtananda [nanda] m. hist. np. of Amrtananda Yogi, rhetorician of the 13th century; we owe him the Alankārasamgraha.
Amrtapura [pura] n. geo. np. of Amrtapura, village of Karṇāṭa near mod. Tarikere where the temple of Amrtesvara is located.

Amṛtaprabha [prabhā₂] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara king Amṛtaprabha; he helped Na ravāhanadatta to go to Kailāsa to meet Šiva who enthroned him emperor of the magic genies; then he made him meet the sage Vāmadeva₃.
amrtaphala [phala] m. pear tree — n. pear | fruit of the myrobalan; syn. āmalakaphala.
amṛtabindu [bindu] mn drop of ambrosia | lit. np. of the Amrtabindūpanisad.

amrtabīja [bīja] n. phil. [Trika] the four phonemes 'r', 'r', 'l' and its long form are said to be seeds of immortality; they are the resting place of Self-consciousness; they produce nothing and do not change.
amṛtamathana [mathana] n. cf. kṣīrodamathana.
amṛtamaya [maya] amnf amṛtamayī made of Nectar.

amṛtavarṣin [varṣin] amnf amṛtavarṣiṇī who distributes ambrosia — f. amṛtavarṣiṇī (mus. car natique) mode [rāga] intended to make it rain; myth. Rāvaņa played it on his vīņā to extinguish the fire when Hanumān set fire to Lankā with his tail; called mallāra in North India.
amṛtavelā [velā] f. hour before dawn.
amṛtasaras [saras] n. geo. np. of the city of amṛtasaras "Lake of Nectar" in Pañjāb (mod. Amritsar); it possesses the golden temple, sacred to the Sikhs.
Amṛtasiddhi [siddhi] f. lit. np. of the Amṛtasiddhi "Nectar of supernatural powers", tantric text of the 11th century; it discusses in particular the impositions ri
tuelles [mudrā]; along with the Amṛtasiddhimūla (preserved in Tibetan), it is one of the earliest texts of hathayoga.
Amṛteśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of the temple of Amrtesvara of the Hoysala period, built in 1196 at Amrtapura; its sculptures inspired by epic tales are renowned.
amṛṣyamāṇa [neg. mṛṣyamāṇa] amnf amṛṣyamāṇā not being able to bear it.
amedhya [neg. medhya] amnf amedhyā unfit for sacrifice; impure; harmful — n. filth, excrement.
amogha [neg. mogha] amnf amoghā ef ficace; infallible (said not of the vajra of Indra) | that which succeeds | happy, productive, fertile.

Amoghavajra [vajra] m. hist. np. of Amoghavajra "Flawless Diamond" (705–774), monk and master of Vajrayana; born in Lanka (or Samarkand), at the age of 14 he followed Vajrabodhi to Srivijaya and then to Luoyang to assist him in translating the Sutras into Chinese; he collected and translated numerous works, notably the Tattvasamgraha; a protégé of the Tang emperors, he advised placing the empire under the protection of Mañjuśrī; his disciples created the Mantra School (Zhenyan), and following him, Kūkai founded the Shingon school, which venerates him as its 6th patriarch. Amoghavarșa | varșa | m. hist. np. of Emperor Raṣṭrakūṭa Amoghavarṣa₁ (9th century); he succeeded Govinda₃ in 814 at the age of 14; a Jain, he was an expert in Sanskrit and Kannada and a patron of the arts; he established peaceful relations with neighboring kingdoms; he moved the capital from Mayūrakhandī to Mānyakheta; Kṛṣṇa₂ succeeded him in 878 | hist. np. of King Raṣṭrakūṭa Amoghavarṣa₂ (10th century); he succeeded Indra₃ in 927; his younger brother Govinda₄ betrayed him and succeeded him in 930 | hist. np. of King Rāṣṭrakūṭa Amoghavarṣa₃ (10th century), half-brother of Indra₃; he succeeded the incompetent Govinda₄ in 936; his son Kṛṣṇa₃ succeeded him in 939.
amoghavrtti [vrtti] f. gram. np. of the Amoghavrtti, commentary on the Sabdānuśāsana grammar of Sākaṭāyana₁, probably also by him.
amoghasamkalpa [samkalpa] will m. irresistible. carati amoghasamkalpo devavac cākhilam jagat [Suśruta] He travels the whole world with an irresistible will, like a god.
amoghasiddhi [siddhi] m. bd. n.p. of Amoghasid dhi "the Infallible", jina guardian of the North in the Mahāyāna pantheon, represented in gen. in abhayamudrā.
ámba cf. Ambā.
ambaka n. eye.
ámbara |anuvr| n. clothing | sky, space, ether | math. symb. the number 0 — ifc. clothed in (iic.).

Ambarīṣa₁ m. myth. np. of the rājarṣi Ambarīṣa₁, author of hymns of the Rigveda; cf. Sunaḥśepha₁ | myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā Ambarīṣa₁, son of PraśuśrukaPrasuśruta, father of Nahuşa₁. সদ্ৰম্ভ ambaṣṭha |ambastha| m. name of a country and its inhabitants | soc. son of a man of the brāhmaṇa class and a woman of the vaiśya class | soc.
physician [vaidya] who emigrated from South India to Bengal. ambaşthānām cikitsitam [Manu] Medicine belongs to the ambasthās.

Ambā f. mother | myth. [Mah.] np. of Ambā, eldest daughter of the king of Kāśi; betrothed to King Sālva, she was abducted by Bhīşma and then, once released, repudiated by Sālva; she asked in vain all the princes to fight Bhīṣma; by great penances she obtained the pity of Subrahmanya, who offered her a garland of eternally fresh lotus which would allow whoever wore it to defeat Bhīṣma; she again begged all the princes in vain, especially King Drupada; leaving the latter's palace she left the garland at his door; she then asked for vengeance from Rāma₁ Jāmadagnya who fought Bhīṣma without success; She went to the Himalayas to perform terrible penances, and Shiva granted her rebirth as a transsexual, like Sikhandī, to kill Bhīşma; she built a great pyre on the banks of the Yamunā, into which she threw herself, saying, "Death to Bhīṣma"; she was reborn as the daughter Sikhandinī of King Drupada; one day she found the garland at the gate of her palace and put it around her neck; through penances, she changed her sex and became Sikhandī — voc. amba adr. Madam; mother | tamil ammaa. ambādā f. mother | ambālā id. Ambālikā₁ f. Little mother (affectionate term) | myth. np. of Ambālikā₁ "Little Mother", epith. of Durgā | myth. [Mah.] np. of Ambālikā₁, 3rd daughter of the king of Kāśi, abducted by Bhīṣma to marry Vici travīrya; widowed without heir, she was made to marry the ascetic Vyāsa; being white with fear at their union, her son Pāṇḍu was born white | lit. [DKC.] np. of Ambālikā₁, princess of Anga; she married Apahāravarmā.

ambikā [ika] f. Little Mother (affectionate term) myth. np. of ambikā "Little Mother", terrible aspect of Durgā, śakti of Rudra | myth. [Mah.] np. of Am bikā₁, 2nd daughter of the king of Kāśi, abducted by Bhīşma to marry Vicitravīrya; widowed without heir, she was made to marry the ascetic Vyāsa; having closed her eyes at their union, her son Dhṛtarāṣṭra was born blind; solicited again by Vyāsa, she had her disguised servant take her place, from whom Vidura was born | jn. np. of the yakṣī ambikā₁, revered as śāsanadevatā of Neminātha.
ambu var. ambhas |abhra| n. water.
ambuga [ga₁] amnf ambugā aquatic, which lives in water.
ambuja | ja | n. | "born of water" | lotus; syn. abja, ambhoja, kamala — mf ambujā proper noun.
ambutā [tā] f. aquatic nature.
ambudhi [dhi] m. ["receptacle of water"] ocean; syn. abdhi | math. symb. the number 4.
amburāśi [rāśi] m. ["pool of water"] mer. ambuvācī f. soc. four-day festival, beginning on the tenth day |daśamī| of the fortnight

dark | kṛṣṇapakṣa | of the summer month āṣāḍha; the menstruation of the goddess Kāmākhyā is celebrated at Kāmagiri; during this period the land is impure, and agriculture is prohibited; the temple is closed for three days, and reopened on the fourth with a great fertility festival.

ámbhas [abhra] n. water; not. the celestial waters | power; capacity | pl. ambhāṃsi myth. the 4 powers: the gods | devās|, the men | narās|, the manes [pitaras] and the titans [asurās] | sg. math. symb. the number 4.
ambhaḥpati | pati | m. myth. np. of ambhaḥpati, epith. of Varuna "Master of the waters".
ambhoja [ja] n. ["born of water"] lotus (of day); syn. abja, ambuja, ambhoruha, kamala.
ambhojanman [janman] n. cf. ambhoja.

ambhodhi [dhi] m. ["receptacle of the waters"] ocean. kāmāre kālakūṭaviṣāśana gaurīvallabha māmuddharāpadambhodhestripuraghna antakāntaka || O lover of Gaurī, enemy of Kāma, you who swallowed the poison Kālakūta, extract me from the ocean of difficulties, you destroyer of the triple city (of demons), you who put an end to death.
ambhoruha [ruha] n. ["that grows in water"] lotus.
amla amnf amlā acid — m. acidity; vi sour, sorrel, acidic substance | phil. [Nyāya] acidity, a type of taste [rasa]; [Bṛhajjātaka] it is associated with the planet Venus [Sukra] | hi. imlī.

amlaka |ka| m. bio. bot. Artocarpus lakuca, a moraceae tree, sought after for its quality wood; its acidic fruit is used as a condiment and in medicine; its boiled bark is used as a vermifuge — f. amlikā acidity | med. stomach ailments mac | bio. bot. Tamarindus indica, tamarind tree; it is used in medicine | var. amlīkā id.
áya |agt. i| ifc. amnf ayā who goes to (iic.) | the act of going to (iic.) | chance.
ayah iic. ayas.
ayaḥśūla |śūla| n. iron stake.
ayajña [priv. yajñá] amnf ayajñā soc. who does not practice Vedic sacrifice — m. miserable sacrifice.
ayata |neg. yata| amnf ayatā uncontrolled, without constraint.
ayati [opp. yáti₂] m. nonascetic.
ayatna |opp. yatna| mr. absence of effort. ayatnena var. ayatnāt adv. effortless; without constraint.
ayathā |neg. yathā| adv. improperly; not in accordance.
ayathāmātram [mātra] adv. phon. improperly visàvoir de la mesure (fault of pronunciation of a vowel).
ayathāvat |vat| adv. incorrectly.

áyana [act. i] n. path, journey, route | astr. half-year (the Sun's journey from one solstice to the other); solstice; cf. uttarāyaņa, dakṣiṇāyana. ayanaghoşa | ghoşa | m. myth. |GG. | np. of Ayanaghoşa, cowherd of Vrndāvana, husband of Rādhā.
ayanacalana [calana] n. astr. precession of the equinoxes.
ayanāmśa | amśa | m. astr. precession of the equinoxes (difference between the tropical zodiac [sāyana] and the sidereal zodiac [nirayana]); syn. ayanacalana.
ayanānta | anta | mr. astr. solstice.
avoirrita [neg. yantrita] amnf ayan tritā who does not control her behavior.

ayám [m. idam] [sg. nom. ayam, acc. imam, i. anena, dat. asmai, abl. asmāt, g. asya, loc. as min; du. nom. acc. imau, i. dat. abl. ābhyām, g. loc. anayos; pl. nom. ime, acc. imān, i. ebhis, dat. abl. ebhyas, g. eṣām, loc. eṣu] this, that, these (here); this one; here, what follows | he; it. ayam janah this person here; myself. ayam asmi here I am. ime smah here we are. mām imam I am here. ko 'yam āyāti who comes here? so 'yam vidūṣakaḥ ce vidūṣaka ici-même. krodhameṣām nāvagacchāmi I do not understand their anger.
ayamita [neg. yamita] amnf ayamitā uncontrolled; unmastered.
ayamitanakha [nakha] amnf ayamitanackā who has uncut nails.
ayaśas [opp. yaśas ] n. infamy, ignominy. ayaśah pramrstam the ignominy was washed away.
áyas mn véd. bronze, copper; metal; mine rai | (after 1200 ant.) iron ore | lat. aes; ang. ore; fr. airain.
ayaskāra | kāra | mr. black-smith.
áyasmáya [maya] amnf ayasmayī ved. of iron; made of metal, metallic — f. ayasmayī myth. np. of Ayasmayī "Of iron", one of the 3 cities of the anti-gods | asura | ; cf. Tripura.
ayoguda | guda | mr. iron ball.
ayodanda |danda| mr. iron bar.
ayomaya |maya| amnf ayomayī made of iron. ayomuşti | muşti | amnf with fists of steel.
ayasa |ayasa| ifc. n. iron (so (iic.)).
ayā adv. ved. in this way, thus. ayā soma lit. beginning of the Ayāsomīya, group of hymns of the SV.
ayās ind. ved. (a.) agile | (n.) fire.
ayi interj. hey! holà! please! oh là là!
áyukta [neg. yukta] amnf ayuktā not connected; not united | not prepared; not attentive | inadequate, non-compliant; unworthy; unreasonable, absurd.
ayuktatā |tā| f. inadequacy; mistake.
ayuktatva [tva] n. id.. upajīvyavirodhasyāyuktatvam One does not bite the hand that feeds you.
ayugapad [neg. yugapad] adv. not simultaneously; separately.
ayugma [opp. yugma] amnf ayugmā math. odd (number).
ayugmacchada | chada | mr. cf. saptacchada.
ayúj [neg. yuj₂] amnf unpaired; (in number) odd; syn. ayuja.
ayujá [ayuja] amnf ayujā id.
áyuta [neg. yuta₁] amnf ayutā without limits, free; unlimited, innumerable | inseparable, indissoluble — n. ayúta math. ["without limits"] ten thousand; a myriad.
ayutasiddha [siddha₁] amnf ayutasiddhā phil. |Vaiśeṣika| inseparable, indissolubly united; added in quantity (opp. yutasiddha) | intrinsic.
ayutasiddhi [siddhi] f. phil. [Vaiśeṣika] knowledge that objects or notions are intrinsically linked and cannot be separated.
ayutāyus [āyus] m. myth. np. of Ayutāyu "Infinitely aged", king of ayodhyā, son of Sindhudvīpa, father of Rtuparna, ancestor of Raghu and therefore of Rāma var. ayutāyu id.
áyuddha [neg. yuddha] amnf ayuddhā unconquered; Invincible, irresistible — n. absence of combat; state of peace.
aye interj. oh! ah! (surprise) |eh! holà! (call).
ayo iic. ayas.
ayogava [gava] mf ayogavī soc. mixed caste; said of the descendant of a śūdra man and a vaiśyā woman; not. caste of carpenters.

ayoga [opp. yoga] m. separation; disjunction separation from a loved one | non-conformity; uselessness, ineffectiveness; impossibility | inappropriate medical treatment | astr. unfavorable conjunction of stars.

ayogakevalin [kevalin] amnf ayogakevalinī jn. to be accomplished [arhat], in the brief state of passive omniscience, at the 14th stage of spiritual development [guṇasthāna]; bodily activity then ceases, and nirvāṇa is attained; opp. sayogakevalin.
ayogavāha [vāha] m. phon. ["not listed with other phonemes"] denotes the anusvāra, the visarga and their variants; syn. parāśraya; opp. yogavāha.
ayoddhr [neg. yoddhr] amnf ayoddhrī noncombatant; coward.
ayodhya [neg. yodhya] amnf ayodhyā Invincible — f. cf. ayodhya.

ayodhyā [f. ayodhya] f. geo. np. of the city of ayodhyā "the Invincible", founded by Iksvāku, capital of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa] and notably of King Rāma; it is one of the 7 sacred cities [saptapurī]; the Sarayū river flows through it; mod. Oudh, near Faizabad in Uttar Pradesh | pali Ayojjhā. daśarathaputrorāmo'yodhyānagare kośāddhastena brāhmaṇāya dhanaṃ dadāti Rāma, son of Daśaratha, gives money from his purse to the brahmin in the city of ayodhyā (grammatical example showing the use of all semantic roles [kāraka]).

ayoni [priv. yoni] amnf outside the matrix; spontaneous, original; without precedent | phil. Uncreated; without beginning | lit. unpublished poetic subject; opp. anyayoni — m. myth. epith. of Brahmā "the Uncreated".

Ayonija [ja] amnf ayonijā who was not born of the maternal womb | myth. np. of Ayonija, epith. of Hariharaputra "Conceived without a womb"; it is said that he was taken in as a child by King Rājaśekhara₁ of Pandalam in Kerala, a descendant of the Pāndya dynasty, who adopted him as his heir; under the name of Ayyappā (ViṣṇuŚiva), he is the object of an important cult in Kerala, not. at Sabarimala; cf. Manikantha — f. ayonijā myth. ["immaculate conception"] epith. of Sītā, of Draupadī, etc.
ayonisambhava [sambhava] amnf ayonisamb havā cf. Ayonija — m. spontaneous generation.

ará [agt. ṛ] amnf arā swift — m. spoke of a wheel | jn. division of time | jn. np. of the master Ara; cf. Aranātha. aram adv. ready, well disposed; quite, suitable. aram kr prepare. aram gam attend to. dvādaśāram nahi taj jarāya vartati cakram pari dyām rtasya | RV. | The wheel with the 12 spokes of the Sun travels across Heaven without ever wearing out.
araghatta [ghatta] m. well wheel or pulley.
aranātha [nātha] m. jn. np. d'aranātha "Master of Time", 18th mythical tīrthankara; his body is golden yellow, his symbol is a fish; he is also associated with the nandyāvarta diagram.
áraṇa [priv. raṇa] amnf araṇā withdrawn, foreign; remote, distant; isolated — n. refuge.
aráni [rani] f. fire stick | its upper part, in acacia wood [śamī] | of. aranī its two parts — m. organic. the bot tree. Premna serra tifolia; syn. agnimantha.
áranya [araṇaya] n. wood, (large) forest; wild nature | isolated place, desert; cf. dharmāranya | pl. aranyanī deep forest. aranye rud to moan in the desert.
aranyagavaya [gavaya] m. organic. zoo. Bos Gaurus, wild gaur.
aranyarājya |rājya| n. sovereignty over the forest.
aranyarudita [rudita] amnf aranyaruditā ["gemi in the woods"] preached in the desert.
aranyarodana [rodana] n. ["weeping in the woods"] the act of preaching in the desert.
aranyavāsin | vāsin₁ | amnf aranyavāsinī who lives secluded in the forest.
araṇyānī [ānī] f. large forest; wild nature.
aranye [loc. aranya] iic.
aranyetilaka | tilaka | m. pl. wild sesame | unexpected event ["like sesame seeds in the forest"]. araņyemāṣa [māṣa] m. pl. bio. wild beans.
arati [priv. rati] amnf discontented — f. displeasure, pain; anxiety; distress; sorrow, regret,
grief | anger | biliary disease.
aratni m. cubit, ell; unit of length, of 24 fingers [angula] (approximately 46 cm) — f. elbow.

arapacana m. hist. syllabary of 42 letters, whose name comes from its first five letters: 'a', 'ra', 'pa', 'ca', 'na'; it was used to write the Gāndhārī language in Kharoṣṭhī script for the purposes of Mahāyāna texts; this word is also a mnemonic for the doctrine bd. and is associated with Mañjuśrī. om arapacana dhīḥ mnemonic mantra of five aspects of the concept of dharma in Mahāyāna doctrine.
arapás [priv. rapas] amnf without infirmity; unharmed; healthy.
aravinda [aravinda] n. bot. Nelumbium speciosum, pink lotus; syn. kamala.
aravindanābhi [nābhi] m. myth. np. of Aravin danābhi, epith. of ViṣṇuNārāyaṇa "whose name shines with a lotus".
arasá [priv. rasa] amnf arasā tasteless, insipid; bland; weak | lacking a sense of taste — m. absence of sap, absence of juice.
arasajña [neg. rasajña] amnf arasajñā who has no taste for; who is not interested in.
arasajñatā [tā] f. med. loss of the sense of taste, ageusia; syn. rasājñāna.
arāga [priv. rāga] amnf arāgā free from passion.
arāgadvesa [dvesa] iic. neither passion nor hatred.
arāgadveṣatas [tas] adv. without love or hate.
arājaka [priv. rājaka] amnf arājakā without a king — absence n. absence of a king, anarchy. arājake janapade when the country is in a state of anarchy.
arājakatā [tā] f. state of anarchy.
arājalakṣman [neg. rājalakṣman] m. not wearing the insignia of royalty.
árāti [opp. rāti] f. disfavor; enmity, hostility | pl. arātayas witches — priv. m. enemy.
arātribhojana [opp. rātribhojana] n. jn. prohibition of taking a meal in the evening, a major observance [mahāvrata] of the Jaina renunciants.
arāddhi [opp. rāddhi] f. failure, failure.
arāla [araala] amnf arālā curve; in curved | curly (hair) — m. ritual gesture [mudrā] of the curved hand (fingers folded under the vertical palm) — f. arālā soc. disloyal woman — f. arālī id.
arí [agt. r] amnf faithful; zealous, fervent, pious | greedy; envious | hostile — m. enemy.
aritā [tā] f. state of being an enemy.
aritva [tva] n. id.
ariṣadvarga [ṣadvarga] m. phil. the 6 enemy passions, preventing liberation [mokṣa]: desire
sexual [kāma], anger [krodha], greed [lobha], attachment to the phenomenal world [moha], gold
pride [mada] and jealousy [mātsarya].
arisamāsa [samāsa] m. gram. ["gathering of enemies"] irregular compound (e.g., of Sanskrit and Prakrit).
arisūdana [sūdana] m. myth. np. of arisūdana, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "who destroys the enemy".
arikta [neg. rikta] amnf ariktā not empty who does not have empty hands.
aritṛ [agt. ṛ] amnf aritrī rower.
aritra [instr. r] amnf aritrā that propels, that guides — m. oar; rudder.
arin [agt. r] n. ["which has spokes"] wheel | myth. not. cakra of Viṣṇu — m. ari₁ id.
arim [acc. ari] iic. arimdama var. arindama |dama| amnf
arimdamā ["who subjugates his enemy"] victorious.

áriṣṭa [neg. riṣṭa] amnf ariṣṭā ved. in demne, safe and sound | of ill omen; disastrous — n. favorable sign, luck | Misfortune, bad omen — m. myth. np. of the demon [asura] Arista "Misfortune", son of Bali, in the form of an enormous furious bull; he was defeated by Kṛṣṇa, who stabbed him with his own horn.
aristátāti | tāti | f. happiness; health; luck.

Aristanemi [nemi] amnf whose wheel rim is intact — m. ved. np. of Aristanemi, associate of Tārkṣya, father of Sumati₂; later he was identified with Garuda as son of Vinatā; a hymn of the RV is attributed to him; cf. Parapurañjaya | jn. epith. of Neminātha, 22ᵉ tīrthankara.
aru m. the sun — acc. arum [arus] cf. arumtuda.
aruci [opp. ruci] f. lack of appetite, disgust | aversion (towards upari, .

aruja [priv. ruj₂] amnf arujā that does not cause suffering (tumor) | healthy, not sick | cheerful — m. bio. bot. Cassia fistula, tree with compound leaves, with pretty yellow flowers in hanging clusters, used in medicine; syn. āragvadha, kṛtamāla.

aruṇá amnf aruṇā f. aruṇī reddish; red (color of the Dawn) — m. the pinkish-red color; the Dawn | myth. np. of aruna, demigod personifying the Dawn, charioteer of Sūrya; he is the crippled son of Kaśyapa and Vinatā and the elder brother of Garuḍa; his wife is Syenī; Sampāti and Jaṭāyu are his sons — n. ruby.
aruṇastambha [stambha] m. arch. column bearing aruna in añjali position, facing a temple of Sūrya; that of the temple of Koṇārka was moved to face the temple of Jagannātha at Purī.

Aruṇācala [acala] m. geo. n.p. from Aruṇācala "Mount of Fire", hill in Tamil Nadu near mod. Tiruvannamalai bearing a temple dedicated to Siva Sankara in the form of the tejolinga Arunācaleśvara; cf. Ramaṇa | geo. n.p. of Aruṇācala₁ "my tagne lit by dawn", mountainous region in the extreme North-East of India, to the East of Bhutan.

Aruṇācaleśvara [īśvara] m. myth. n.p. of Aruṇācaleśvara, "Lord of the pillar of Fire", igneous form [tejolinga] of Siva; his Eastern shrine at Tiruvannamalai in Tamil Nadu; It is the pañcabhūtasthala associated with the element Fire [tejas].
aruṇānuja [anuja] m. myth. "younger brother of Aruṇa", epith. of Garuda.
aruṇi m. bed. n.p. of the muni Aruṇi.
arudra [priv. Rudra] amnf arudrā other than Rudra.

arundhatī [neg. rundhat] f. bio. medicinal climbing plant | myth. np. of arundhatī "Discovery", wife of Vasistha; at wedding ceremonies the groom invokes her as an example of marital fidelity and the priest shows the bride-to-be the star Alcor which symbolizes her; she is also associated with kuṇḍalinī and medicinal plants; cf. Maitrāvaruņī, Akṣamālā | astr. the star Alcor of the Great Bear; barely visible, she is discovered by designating her indirectly by her companion, the main star Mizar, which symbolizes her husband Vasistha; cf. Krttikās. This divine Arund hatī is tiny; he who cannot see it will die within 6 months.

arundhatīdarśananyāya [darśananyāya] m. phil. ["rational of the vision of arundhatī"] rhet. method of indirect explanation by approximation (one shows the star Alcor by first showing the Great Bear, then Mizar).
arușá [related to aruṇa] amnf arușī reddish — m. sun | pl. myth. the red horses of Agni.
árus amnf wounded — n. scar, injury. arūkr to wound.
arumtuda | tuda | amnf arumtudā which causes suffering, which torments.
arūpa |priv. rūpa| amnf arūpā formless | formless; deformed — n. phil. emancipation; syn. nirvāna.
are [voc. ari] interj. (call) hey! Hello! well!
aretáska [aretaska] amnf aretaskā without sperm.
aroga [priv. roga] amnf arogā bien por tant, en bonne santé — m. santé.
arogya [ya] amnf arogyā healthy, well — m. health.
arogyatā |tā| f. health.
arocaka [opp. rocaka] amnf arocakā which disgusts; unpleasant — m. lack of appetite; indigestion.
arocakin [opp. rocakin] amnf roca kinī who lacks appetite | lit. (criticism) who is picky.

arká [agt. rc₁] m. Vedic. ray, lightning | Sun; fire | math. symb. the number 12 (for dvādaśārka) | bio. bot. Calatropis gigantea, medicinal plant also used in magic rituals and in alchemy; its lanceolate leaves evoke flames, and serve as offering supports | soc. hymn, song of praise; ceremony associated with the aśvamedha myth. np. of Arka "Radiant", epith. of Sūrya or Indra | var. arkka id. gato'stam arkah the Sun is setting (standard example of suggestive meaning [vyañjana], e.g. can mean that it is time for the voyage woman to meet her lover).
arkamani [mani] m. solar jewel.
argala m. bolt, bar (of a door) | obstacle, impediment | myth. [PP.] np. of argala, one of the 7 hells. argalam dā pull the bolt. argalaniruddham pakṣadvāram the side door was locked.
argalastotra [stotra] n. soc. laudatory hymn of protection; not. [Devīmāhātmya] hymn to Caṇḍikā in 24 verses.
argalita [argalaita] amnf argalitā rusty, closed ver.
√ argh [related to arh] v. [1] pr. (arghati) to be worth.
arghá [obj. arh] m. value, price | honorific gift.

arghya [pfp. [1] arh] amnf arghyā which has value; esteemed; which deserves to be offered — n. soc. perfumed homage water presented to the host |atithi|; his vessel; oblation to Sūrya, to the pitaras, etc.
arc cf. rc₁.
arcaka [agt. rc₁] amnf arcakā who honors; who worships — m. worshipper | soc. temple officiant.

arcana [act. arc] nf arcanā homage rendered (to a divinity, a superior) | soc. ceremony at the temple where the celebrating priest pronounces the name, the nakṣatra of birth and the gotra of the faithful for the purpose of blessing — amnf arcanī ifc. one who honors, who adores, who venerates (iic.).
arcanīya [pfp. [2] ṛc₁] amnf arcanīyā to honor; venerable.
arcā [act. rc₁] f. cult, adoration | idol.
arci [act. rc₁] m. ved. ray, flame.
arcita [pp. rc₁] amnf arcitā honored, considered.
arcís [abstr. rc₁] n. ved. ray, flame | splendor.
arcya [abs. rc₁] ind. having honored.
arj cf. rj.
arjana [act. rj] n. gain, acquisition.
arjita [pp. ṛj] amnf arjitā acquired.
arjin [agt. rj] amnf arjinī acquirer.

Arjuna [rjuna] amnf arjunī white, clear, silvery; bright — m. bio. bot. Terminalia arjuna, Arjuna tree, a combretaceae; it is used in medicine to reduce cholesterol; syn. marudha | geo. middle mountain range in Maharashtra | myth. [Mah.] np. of the hero Arjuna "Immaculate", one of the 5 Pandhavas, son of Pandu of the Bharatās clan; he was conceived from the union of the god Indra and Kunti, and thus called Partha; he represents Man as his maternal cousin Krishna represents god, according to the duality of the twins NaraNārāyana; An unsurpassed archer, he possesses the magical Gāṇḍīva bow of Varuṇa, which Agni had given him; he carries Hanuman on his

standard [kapidhvaja]; he was the best student of his weapons master Drona, who gave him the brahmaśiras weapon; to pay his master he subdued King Drupada, then he conquered many other kingdoms; he fought the gandharva Angaraparna, who taught him the science of clairvoyant vision |cakṣuṣī|; at the svayaṃvara of Princess Draupadī, disguised as a brahmin, he won the contest, which consisted of shooting an arrow into the eye of a son fish at the top of a mast, while looking at its reflection in a mirror; Upon his return, his mother Kuntī or decreed that he share his prize with his brothers, and Draupadī was to become the common wife of the five Pāṇḍavās, thus fulfilling the promise made in a previous life to Indrasenā₁; his cousin Kṛṣṇa gave him his sister Subhadrā in marriage, whom he married after abducting her, according to the Kṣatriya marriage custom; he also married Citrāngadā, with whom he had a son, Babhruvāhana; he united with the

nymphserpent [nāgī] Ulūpī, whose son was Irāvān; he followed his brother King Yudhisthira into exile, along with his brothers and their common wife Draupadī; in their 13th year of exile, he disguised himself as the transvestite Bṛhannaḍā at the court of King Virāṭa; he prepared for the fratricidal battle, notably by staying 5 years in the heavens with Indra; SivaPinākin taught him the use of the weapon Pāsupata; Krishna served as his charioteer in the battle of Kuruksetra, where He revealed His divine nature to him in the Bhagavad Gita, which is a dialogue between God and Man receiving his duty [dharma] to realize himself through righteous action [karmayoga]; during the battle, he knocked his ancestor Bhisma from his chariot; he had to fight his guru Drona; he fought the invincible Karna, and killed him when his chariot became bogged down; for these negative acts he is Bibhatsu "He who is averse to the task"; after the great battle, he followed the sacrificial horse of Yudhisthira to subdue all the kings of the Earth; at Manipura he challenged his son Babhruvahana, who pierced him with arrows; he was resurrected by Ulupi; When Dharmarāja decided on their renunciation | tyāga|, he followed his brothers and their common wife on their journey to Heaven, clothed in bark; in the forest, Agni asked him to return the Gāndīva bow by throwing it into the river, so that it would return to Varuna; he died on the way, his dharma not being perfect, for he had boasted of killing all his enemies in a single day; cf. Irāvān, Aindri, Kirītin, Gudākeśa, Jaya, Jiṣṇu, Tāpatya, Devadatta, Dhanañjaya, Nandighoṣa, Pa rantapa, Phālguna, Bhārata, Vānaraketu, Vijaya, Svetavāhana, Savyasācī | myth. np. of Arjuna₁ Kārtavīrya, son of king Kṛtavīrya | lat. argentum; fr. money.
arṇa mn flow, current, wave; sea | phon. syllable.
arṇava [va] amnf arṇavā agitated by waves, swell, bubbling; watery, marine — m. sea (swell); waves, swell, foam — ifc. "flow of (iic.)", title of works.
arti [related to ārti] f. suffering.
artihara [hara] amnf artiharā That which removes suffering.
√ arth [vn. Artha] v. [10] pr. r. (artháyate) pp. (arthita) pfp. (arthanīya) pf. (abhi, pra, prati, sam) to ask, to solicit (2 acc.); to implore | to give the meaning of — ca. (arthāpayati) to ask.

ártha [rtha] m. purpose, cause, motive; intention; meaning, significance | thing, object; substance; to do; fact, reality | reward; utility, interest possession, property, goods, wealth, having; advantage, profit (of (i.)); power | soc. the acquisition of material goods, one of the aims of existence [puruṣārtha]; myth. he is personified as Artha the Rich | soc. subject of a dispute; legal case | gram. meaning, significance of a word; notion expressed; communicative purpose | gram. one of the three uses of a word: literal meaning |abhidhā₂|, figurative meaning [lakṣaṇā] and suggestive meaning [vyañjanā] pali attha. artham var. arthāya, arthe, arthena adv. because of; in order to, so as to, to obtain; for the use of; in the manner of, as (g. iic.). arthāt adv. as the case may be | in fact; that is to say. árthatas adv. with a view to; for this purpose; for the benefit of, concerning | in fact, really | gram. as regards meaning. arthekr to do for a purpose, with a view to an advantage, to make oneself useful. ko 'rtho (i.) what for? kimartham adv. why do? for what purpose? tadartha amn Having such an object, useful for that; Existing with a view to. evamartham in this way; to this end. yathārtham according to meaning. udakārtham in order to obtain water. dhanārtham as regards money. tatsādhanārtham in order to prove that. ācārapuspagrahanārtham to bring flowers, as is the custom. arthasya puruso dāso dāsas tvartho na kasya cit [Mah.] Man is the slave of power, but power is not the slave of anything. arthena balavān sarvo 'py arthād bhavati paṇḍitaḥ [PT.] It is through money that every man is strong, it is from money that even the pandita comes. yasyārthās tasya mitrāni | yasyārthās tasya bāndhavāḥ | yasyārthās sa pumān loke | yasyārthās sa ca paṇḍitaḥ | [PT.] He who has money has friends; He who has money has family; He who has money is a man in this world; He who has money is even a great scholar.
arthakāma [kāma] m. du. wealth and pleasure — n. id. — amnf árthakāmā Who desires wealth Who wishes to be useful.
arthakārin [kārin] amnf arthakārinī useful; professional.
arthakriyā [kriyā] f. action aimed at a goal.

arthatattva | tattva | n. true nature of the matter.

arthanirdhāraṇa | nirdhāraṇa | gram. n. determination of meaning.

arthapati | pati | m. rich man | lit. | DKC. | np. of arthapati "Businessman", rich caravan trader, competitor of Dhanamitra, tricked by Apahāravarmā | hist. np. of arthapati₁, son of Kubera₁, father of Ci trabhānu, grandfather of Bāṇa₂.
arthapara [para] amnf arthaparā ["devoted to money" | interested, stingy; Businessman.

árthapāla [pāla] m. lit. np. of Arthapāla, one of the 10 heroes of the Daśakumāracarita; son of the love of Kāmapāla and the princess Kāntimatī, he was abandoned in the woods, and taken in by the yakṣī Tārāvalī, before being adopted by Queen Vasumatī to serve as a comrade to her son Rājavāhana; he went to Kāśī where he freed his father who was wrongly condemned; he married his cousin Princess Manikarnikā.

árthaprakṛti [prakṛti] f. principal instrument for accomplishing a goal | lit. [dramaturgy] one of the 5 dramatic types of the Nātyaśāstra: bīja the seed at the origin of the action, bindu the resumption (metaphor of the drop of oil that forms a sheet on the water), patākā the chain of episodes, prakarī the singular incident, and kārya the denouement; they correspond to the 5 moral situations [avasthā₂]; a canonical dramatic narrative must use these means of action by passing through the stages of unfolding | kāryāvasthā|; cf. pañcasandhi.
arthaphala | phala | n. fruit of a transaction.
arthaphalabhogavirāga [bhoga₁virāga₁] m. phil. [Vedānta] disinterestedness in the fruits of action, qualification of the aspirant for liberation a |sādhanacatuṣṭaya|.
arthamātra [mātra] amnf arthamātrā perti nent to the matter itself | lit. considered from the angle of meaning — n. property, wealth.
arthamātraka [ka] amnf arthamātrakā lit. (poet) concerned first with meaning.
artharūpa [rūpa] amnf artharūpā consisting of.

arthalobha [lobha] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Artha lobha "greedy for riches", greedy doorkeeper of King Bāhubala; his wife was the beautiful Mānaparā; he made her negotiate his affairs, and sent her to bargain with the rich Sukhadhana; the latter, having fallen in love with Mānaparā, promised riches to spend a night with her; arthalobha having approved him, Mānaparā decided to leave him for Sukhadhana; arthalobha tried in vain to fight him, and the king confiscated his goods and dismissed him.
árthavat [vat] amnf arthavatī rich; meaningful; valid, useful | gram. having meaning, signifying | phil. real — adv. according to need; with a view to the goal.
arthavattā [tā] f. wealth; usefulness, importance; significance.
arthavattva [tva] n. id.

árthavāda [vāda] m. phil. gloss (not. of Vedic hymns); description of the purpose of a rite, for the purpose of praising (or blaming) it | lit. text linking the ritual to its mythical or cosmological justification in brāhmaṇa literature; opp. vidhi.
árthavijñāna [vijñāna] n. phil. fine understanding of teaching.
árthavyakti | vyakti | f. lit. clarity of feeling expressed in poetry.
arthaśakti [śakti] f. gram. power of the signified.
arthaśaktimūla [mūla] amnf arthaśaktimūlā gram. ["which has its origin in the power of meaning"] refers to a suggested meaning [dhvani] derived from the signified; opp. śabdaśaktimūla.

árthaśāstra [śāstra] n. political management, administration of the kingdom; economy; morality | lit. np. of the Arthaśāstra, treatise on political economy by Kauțilya Cāṇakya, minister of Candragupta )() Maurya (?313–289 ant.); it comprises 15 sections [adhikarana].
árthaśūnya |śūnya| amnf arthaśūnyā phil. [Dinnāga] meaningless (said of proper names).

árthasaṃgraha [saṃgraha] m. accumulation of rich chesses; treasure | lit. np. of the Arthasamgraha "re collection of semantics", text of pūrvamīmāṃsā Laugākṣi Bhāskara (1882), based on the of Mīmāmsānyāyaprakāśa.
árthasambandha | sambandha | mr. possession of wealth.
árthasambandhin [sambandhin] amnf artha sambandhinī interested in a matter.
árthasādhaka [sādhaka] amnf arthasādhikā responding to a need; useful, effective, profitable.

arthādhikāra [adhikāra] m. gram. semantic injunction of a suffix taddhita; it is a sentence whose predicate is that of the meaning of the word produced, the subject being a pronominal form serving as an anaphora to the word producer, the suffix applying to its theme.
arthādhyāhāra [adhyāhāra] m. gram. resolution of an ellipsis by the meaning, rather than by supplementing the words of a paraphrase; this is the view of the prābhākara school.
arthāntara | antara | n. different circumstance; other case; similar occasion | different meaning; opposite meaning.
arthāntaranyāsa [nyāsa] m. lit. figure of speech of substantiation; act of corroborating, illustration by an example; provision of a general case.

arthāpatti [āpatti] f. phil. implicature, reasoning by presumption; it postulates knowledge of a fact explaining what would otherwise be inexplicable and seeks implicit causes; Sabara distinguishes dṛṣṭārthāpatti and śrutārthāpatti.
arthābādha [abādha] amnf arthābādhā gram. absence of incompatibility between words in a sentence; component of the notion of congruity | yogyatā|.
arthārjana [arjana] n. acquisition of an object.

arthālaṃkāra [alaṃkāra] m. lit. ["embellishment of meaning" | poetic figure of speech that depends on meaning, rather than sound; cf. utprekṣā , upamā ₂; opp. śabdālaṃkāra. 1(
arthāśraya |āśraya| amnf śabdāśrayā gram. which is based on meaning; opp. śabdāśraya.

arddha gem. ardha.
