ardhá amnf ardhā half, semi — mn the Half | a part — iic. (with ordinal) reduced by a Half. ardhe adv. in the middle. ardhatṛtīya two and a half. sarvanāśe samutpanne ardham tyajati panditah ["the wise man leaves the Half rather than lose the whole" A good bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

ardhakukkuṭīnyāya [kukkuṭīnyāya] m. phil. ["maxim of the half-chicken"] saying [subhāṣita] requiring consistency of rhetoric. na hi kukkutyā ekadeśah pacyata ekadeśah pra savāya kalpate [Kumārila] ["one cannot have one's cake and eat it too" | One cannot have one's cake and eat it too.
Ardhagangā [Gangā] f. myth. np. of Ardhagangā "Half of the Ganges", epith. of the Kāverī, Half separated from the Gangā by Jahnu.

Ardhanārī | nārī | f. myth. np. of Ardhanārī "half-woman", epith. of Śivaardhanārīśvara | arch. it is one of the 16 aspects of Śiva.

ardhanārīśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Ard hanārīśvara the "Androgynous Lord", epith. of Śiva "half-woman"; he represents the fusion between Shiva and Pārvatī; his image is masculine on the right and feminine on the left; a shrine is dedicated to him at Tiruchengode in Tamil Nadu; married women without children pray there for their fertility; cf. Bhrngī.
ardhanāriśvarastotra [stotra] n. lit. np. of the Ard hanāriśvarastotra "Ode to the Androgyne God", mystical poem by Kalhana.
ardhamandapa [mandapa] mn (arch.) entrance hall to a temple.
ardhamāgadhī [māgadhī] f. soc. dialect of the māgadhī language, spoken by Mahāvīra₁, and used for the sacred texts of the jaina tradition.
ardhárcá [rca] mn gram. hemistich, half stanza (marked by a pause [avasāna] in the recitation, with absence of liaison [sandhi]).

group [gana] of words used in the neuter as well as in the masculine.

árbuda n. countless quantity; 10 million | tumor, swelling; multitude, troop — m. ved. np. of Arbuda₁, demonhydra [nāga] defeated by Indra; he descends from Kadrū [kādraveya] | geo. np. of Mount Arbuda₁, mod. Mount Abū, on a plateau at 1200 in Rājasthāna, near Gurjara; it is an important Jain pilgrimage site. arbudadhā adv. by the millions.
arbudaparvata [parvata] m. geo. np. of Mount Arbuda₁, highest point (1722 m) of the Arāvalī chain, west of the Deccan; mod. Mount Abū; it is an important place of Jain pilgrimage.
arbudaśikhara [śikhara] m. cf. arbudaparvata. arbudāraņya [araṇya] n. geo. np. of the Ar budāranya, forest site of Mount Abū [Arbuda₁]; it is the region of origin of the gurjarās.
árbha amnf arbhā véd. small, insignificant — m. arbhá véd. boy, child || gr. ορφανος; lat. orbus.

arbhaká [ka] amnf arbhakā small; fragile — m. boy, child; young animal. namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhyo namo yu vabhyo nama āśinebhyaḥ [RV.] Homage to the great, Homage to the small, Homage to the young, Homage to the old.
árma m. pl. armās ruins.

aryá [pfp. [1] r] amnf aryā ["who serves zealously" devoted, faithful, loyal; favorable, attentive — m. árya ved. free man | noble, master | soc. )2 man of the 3rd caste [varna]; syn. vaiśya. ko'ryastasyā darśanena what good is seeing her?

aryamán [aryaman] m. close, intimate; best man | myth. ved. np. of Aryamā "by rain", radiant [āditya] minor, assistant to Mitra, guarantor of the order of ārya society, patron of marriage; he notably guards exogamy: one must marry outside one's clan |gotra|; he presides over the manes [pitaras] and protects the roads; he symbolizes hospitality, and is the god of Customs; astr. he governs the nakṣatra Uttaraphalgunī (of Leo). aryamnáh pánthās astr. the Milky Way ["path of Aryamā"].
arva iic. ready, close.
árvat [aravat] amnf arvatī rapid, swift — m. horse; courier — f. arvatī mare — m. arvan id.
arvāk [nom. arvāc] adv. this way; this way; in front of | near, beside (loc.) | from abl. . arvāk kṛ put in front. arvān nud push forward, downward.
arvākkālika [kālika] amnf arvākkālikā closer in time; later.
arvākkālikatā [tā] f. posteriority.

arvācin [arvācin] amnf arvācinī turned towards.
arvācīná [arvācīna] amnf arvācīnā turned towards, lover of (iic.); who prefers (iic.) amateur, neophyte | recent. arvācinam adv. on this side of (abl.) | forward.

ars cf. rs.

(arháyati) to give the right to, to authorize, to permit. ... arhasi adr. please, deign, I beg you to ... (inf.). bhavān mām moktum arhati you must release me.

(woman) worthy of taking care of a task. pūjārhā f. (woman) who deserves respect. aham kartum arhah I am able to do. indratvamarho rājāyam tapasā |Mah.| This king, through his penances, deserves the rank of Indra.

arhat [ppr. arh] amnf arhantī deserving, good; worthy, honorable, respectable — m. bd. venerable, holy; the Mahāyāna establishes the list of 16 meritors: Pindola Bha radvāja, Kanakavatsa, Kanaka Bharadvāja, Sub hinda/Nandimitra, Nakula, Bhadra, Kalika, Vajri putra, Supaka/Jīvaka/Gopaka, Panthaka, Rāhula, Nāgasena, Aṅgida/Aṅgaja, Vanavāsa, Asita/Ajita, and Cuda Panthaka | jn. saint; syn. tīrthankara || Pali arahā .
árhattva [tva] n. aptitude; respectability; eligibility to (iic.).
sambandhārhattvam [Nyāya] ability to establish a relationship. ala n. scorpion's sting; bee's sting. ala form of agt.

Alakanandā [nandā] f. little girl between 8 and 10 years old geo. np. of the Alakanandā river, in the Himālaya, main tributary of the Ganges; it originates on Mount Badarīnātha, and joins the Bhāgīrathī at Devaprayāga to form the Gangā.
alakapurī [purī] f. myth. n.p. of alakapurī, capital of Kubera.
alakta m. red lacquer of resin or coche nilles (women use it to paint the palms of their hands and the soles of their feet).

alamkariṣṇu [agt. alaṃkṛ] amnf who likes to be adorned; desirous of adornment | who is accustomed to adorning; who decorates (acc.). kanyām alamkariṣṇuḥ who knows how to adorn a young girl.

(pronounced during the sprinkling [abhiseka] of the linga) Vișnu is honored by the ornament, Siva is honored by the sprinkling. alaṃkārarahitā vidhavaiva sarasvatī [AP.] Poetry without ornaments is like sarasvatī made a widow. alamkāracūdāmaņi [cūdāmaņi] m. lit. np. from the Alamkāracūdāmani "Summit of Poetic Art", commentary by Hemacandra on his Kāvyānuśāsana, itself followed by his Viveka₁.
alamkāratilaka [tilaka] m. bed. of np. the alamkāratilaka “ornament of figures of speech”, an aesthetic work by Bhānudatta.
alamkāraprabhā [prabhā₂] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of alamkāraprabhā, wife of the vidyādhara prince Hemaprabha, mother of Ratnaprabhā₁.

alamkāravat [vat] amnf Alamkāravatī decorated — f. alaṃkāravatī lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī Alamkāravatī, daughter of the king alamkāraśīla; she married Naravāhanadatta.

alaṃkāraśāstra [śāstra] n. lit. poetics; aesthetics; literary theory.

alaṃkārasarvasva [sarvasva] n. lit. np. of the alamkārasarvasva, a work on aesthetics by Ruyyaka (Kaśmīra, 12th century); cf. Vimarśinī₂. সলক alaṃkṛ [alamkṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (alaṃkaroti) pp. (alamkṛta) pf. (sam) to prepare, to adorn. kanyām alamkṛtya after having adorned the young girl.

avaman [avaman] v. [4] pr. r. (avamányate) v. [8] pr. r. (avamanute) pp. (avamata) abs. (ava matya, avamanya) to despise.
avamanya [abs. avaman] ind. having despised.
avamanyaka [ka] amnf avamanyakā who despises (g.).

avamarśa [act. avamṛś] m. touch; contact [avamarśasandhi] lit. [dramaturgy] dramatic turn of events; it is one of the 5 articulations of dramatic narratives [pañcasandhi] — f. avamarśā ifc. contact with (iic.). avamárśam adv. in order to make contact.
avamāna [act. avaman] m. contempt | self-contempt.
avamih [avamih] v. [1] pr. (avamehati) to urinate on. .0
avamukta |pp. avamuc| amnf avamuktā released; freed.
avamuktopānatka | upānatka | amnf avamuk topānatka who took off his shoes.
avamuc [avamuc₁] v. [6] pr. (avamuñcati) to release; to free; to unharness.
avamṛj [avamṛj] v. [2] pr. (avamārṣṭi) erase cer, clean.
avamṛja [imp. avamṛj] ind. clean up!
avamṛś [avamṛś] v. [1] pr. (avamṛśati) pp. (avamṛṣṭa) pf. (practice) touch.
avamocana [act. avamuc] n. release; letting go [["where the horses are unharnessed"] halt, resting place.

avayava [obj. avayu] m. part, member, portion; opp. samudāya | phil. [Nyāya] element of a syllogism — f. avayavā ifc. part of, portion of; member of (iic.). avayavāvayavibhāvaḥ gram. relationship between part and whole; metonymy.
avayavadharma | dharma | m. phil. characteristic property of a part.
avayavaśas [śas] adv. member to member.
avayavin [in] amnf avayavinī which has subdivisions; composite; whole — f. avayavinī phil. syllogism.
avayu [avayu₂] v. [3] pr. (avayuyoti) to separate (from (abl.)) — ca. (avayāvayati) to set aside, to keep at a distance.

ávara [neg. vara₂] amnf avarā low, inferior | junior, more recent | which precedes, inferior to (abl.); opp. para — n. ifc. (fine) of at least (iic.) (paṇa). ávaratas adv. under | at least. avarena adv. below (acc.). gopālācchyāmo'varaḥ Syāma is better than Gopāla.
avaraja [ja] amnf avarajā second-born, younger — m. younger brother (opp. agraja, syn. anuja) — ifc. younger brother of iic. — f. avarajā younger sister.
avarapara [para] amnf avaraparā which precedes and follows. avaraparam one on top of the other; in succession.
avarava | varna | mr. soc. lower social class — amnf avaravarṇā lower class; syn. śūdra.
avarata |avarata| amnf avaratā which stops.
avarati [avarati] f. cessation.
avaruddha [pp. avarudh] amnf ava ruddhā detained, arrested, stopped | placed incommunicado; em prisoner; banished — f. avaruddha cf. avaruddhastrī.
avaruddhastrī |strī| f. soc. cloistered woman at the ha rem.
avaruddhikā |ika| f. soc. woman cloistered in the harem.
avarudh [avarudh₂] v. [7] pr. (avaruṇaddhi) pp. (avaruddha) to retain.
avaruh [avaruh₁] v. [1] pr. (avarohati) pr. r. (avarohate) pf. (prati) to descend | to fall — ca. (avarohayati) pfp. (avaropya) var. avaropayati to bring down; to deprive of (abl.), to diminish.
avarodha [act. avarudh] m. seclusion, isolation | gynoecium, harem | pl. avarodhās the women of the harem.
avaropita [pp. ca. avaruh] amnf avaropitā that one has brought down (from (abl.)) demoted, degraded; fallen (not. from his state of prince).
avaropya [pfp. [1] ca. avaruh] amnf avaropyā which must have descended — abs. ind. having been descended or fallen.
avaroha [act. avaruh] m. descent | mus. des cente de ton | aerial roots (not. du banian) climbing vine.
avarohaṇa [agt. avaruh] amnf avarohinī who descends — act. n. descent; descent from (abl.) | place of descent.
avarohin [agt. avaruh] amnf avarohin्ī that descends — m. bio. banyan tree.
avarṇa [priv. varṇa] amnf avarṇā soc. outside the system of the 4 classes.
avarṣa [absence varṣa] n. absence of rain.
avalagna [avalagna] amnf avalagnā which hangs from (iic.) — mn size.

avalamb [avalamb] v. [1] pr. r. (avalam bate) pp. (avalambita) pfp. (avalambitavya) to hang on, to rely on; to resort to, to come to such a state; to affect; to attach oneself to, to depend on, to devote oneself to. dhairyam avalamb to gather one's courage. vaiklavyam avalamb to become discouraged. jaṃghām avalamb to flee.

avalamba [agt. avalamb] amnf ava lambā that hangs from, attached to (iic.) — obj. m. support, point of support. dattahastāvalamba to whom one extends a helping hand. lakṣmīnṛsiṃha mama dehi karāvalambam [Sankara₁] O LakṣmīNṛsiṃha give me the support of your hand.
avalambana |act. avalamb| n. support, support.
avalambita [pp. avalamb] amnf ava lambitā leaning on, leaning on; one who gives oneself to; attached to, hanging from. yena nairāśyam avalambitam he who has no more hopes.
avalambitaka [ka] m. earring.
avalambitavya [pfp. [3] avalamb] amnf avalambitavyā on whom one can rely; on whom one depends.
avalambin [agt. avalamb] amnf ava lambinī which relies on.
avalip [avalip] v. [6] pr. r. (avalimpáte) pp. (avalipta) to anoint oneself with; (figuratively) to be imbued with one's person.
avalipta [pp. avalip] amnf avaliptā arrogant ointment; self-important, proud.
avaliptatā [tā] f. pride.
avalih [avalih₁] v. [2] pr. (swallowedḍhi) pr. r. (avalīḍhé) pp. (avalīḍha) lick, lap.
avalup [avalup] v. [6] pr. (avalumpati) pp. (avalupta) to destroy, to tear out; to extinguish; to absorb, to make disappear.
avalupta [pp. avalup] amnf avaluptā uprooted, destroyed, devastated. avaluptabhavanadāḍimīphalaiḥ kapibhiḥ [K.] The pomegranates uprooted by the monkeys from the trees of the palace.
avalumpana [act. avalup] n. assault; the act of pouncing on prey and escaping with it.
avalepa [act. avalip] m. pride, arrogance; vanity.
avalepamudrā [mudrā] f. sufficient posture; air va niteux.
avalok [avalok] v. [1] pr. r. (avalokate) pp. (avalokita) to see, to look — ca. (avalokayati) id. to observe, to consider.
avaloka [act. avalok] m. glance; show l bed. n.p. of the avaloka, commentary on the Daśarūpaka by Dhanika (c. 1025).
avalokana [act. avalok] n. look; observation, contemplation — ifc. appearance of (iic.).
avalokayat [ppr. That. avalok] amnf avalokayantī by observing.
avalokita [pp. avalok] amnf avalokitā seen, observed — n. action of looking.
avalokiteśvara [īśvara] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] np. of the perfect [bodhisattva] avalokiteśvara, "the Lord who watches over us"; cf. Padmapāṇi, Manipadmā.

avalokiteśvaragunakarandavyūha [guna karandavyūha m. lit. np. of the Avalo kiteśvaragunakarandavyūha "Conceptual Exposition of the Qualities of Avalokitesvara", esoteric work |sūtra| of the bd. Mahāyāna; an early version is in prose, a more recent one in verse | śloka | ; also called Kārandavyūha.
avaśá [priv. vaśa] amnf avaśā independent, free; rebellious, insubordinate, disobedient; uncontrolled.
avaśiṣ [avaśiṣ] ps. (avaśiṣyate) pp. (avaśiṣṭa) to remain; to stay, to remain, to survive.
avaśiṣṭa [pp. avaśiṣṭ amnf avaśiṣṭā spared, remaining, surviving — ifc. of which there (only) remains; remainder of (iic.). kiyadavaśiṣṭaṃ rajanyāḥ how much night remains?

avaśeṣa [agt. avaśiṣ] n. remains — ifc. of which (only) remains (2nd ed.). avasesam adv. so as to remain in remainder — ifc. until (2nd ed.) (not inclusive). kathāvaśeṣaḥ | "of which only his story remains" | deceased.
avaśeṣatā |tā| f. fact of being left over.
avaśya [neg. vaśya] amnf avaśyā insou mis, rétif. avasyam adv. necessarily; certainly, without a doubt; naturally; willingly.
avaśyā | avaśyā | f. dew; frost.
avaśyāya [avaśyāya] m. dew; frost.

avastabdha [pp. avastambh] amnf avaṣṭabdhā that stands firm | supported by, resting on, leaning on (acc.) | seized, arrested | near; next; imminent — amn avastabdha f. avas tabdhā stiffened, seized by the cold.

avaṣṭambh [avastambh] v. [5] pr. (avaṣṭabhnoti) v. [9] pr. (avaṣṭabhnāti) pp. (avastabdha) to lean on, to rely on, to trust in | to seize; to stop. dhairyam avastambh to gather his courage. avastabhya dandam leaning on his staff.
avaṣṭambha [act. avaṣṭambh] m. the act of relying on; the act of having recourse to, the act of applying (acc.) | self-confidence, resolve. dhairyāvaṣṭambhaṃ kṛ to gather one's courage.
ávas₁ [abstr. av] n. favor, protection; grace, appreciation, pleasure; desire, wish.
avás₂ [ava] adv. ved. down | at the bottom of abl. i. .
avástāt |tāt| adv. below; under (g.) | before, prior to (g.).
avasá |avasa| n. food, provision, via tique — m. king.

avasad [avasad₁] v. [1] pr. (avasīdati) pp. (avasanna) to succumb, to fall into misfortune — ca. (avasādayati) to calm; to exhaust; to sink; to ruin, to destroy. yadi nāvasīdati guru prayojanam provided that no important matter suffers.

avasanna [pp. avasad] amnf ava sannā sunk, sunk; pressed; collapsing (under a burden) | deep (wound); opp. utsanna | depressed, discouraged; afflicted, unhappy | finished; abolished (not. a blind person's vision) | soc. (law) who has lost a case. prabalakṣudhāvasanna amn suffering from terrible hunger. avasannaprāyāṇi me gātrāṇi I am about to collapse.

avasara [avasara] m. rain ["descent (of water)"] | propitious place | happy occasion, favorable moment | phil. [Nyāya] opportunity to further the investigation. avasare on this happy occasion. yáthāvasaram according to the circumstances. grhītāvasarah the act of seizing an opportunity.
avasarga [act. avasṛj] m. act of relaxing; relaxation | act of following one's inclination.
avasarpa [agt. avasrp] m. spy.
avasarpaṇa [act. avasṛp] n. myth. place where Manu placed his foot when descending from the ark.
avasarpita [pp. That. avasrp] amnf ava sarpitā which was made to flow back.
avasarpin [agt. avasrp] amnf avasarpiṇī which decreases, which ebbs — f. avasarpiṇī jn. descending cycle, cosmic period of gradual descent; opp. utsarpiņī.
avasalavi [avasalavi] adv. left; opp. prasalavi; syn. apasalavi.

avasā [avasā₁] v. [4] pr. (avasyati) pp. (ava sita) pf. (adhi, nis, pari, vi) to finish, to end; to come to an end, to cease — ca. (avasāyayati) abs. (avasāyya) to cause to settle, to cause to take up residence (loc.).
avasāda [act. avasad] m. lack of energy or stamina; weariness, fatigue, exhaustion, defeat | med. depression.

avasāna |act. avasā| n. end, term, extremity ["where the horses are unharnessed"] halt, resting place; residence | phon. pause; it is noted in writing by the daṇḍa | phon. hiatus, pause in speech; it is marked by a space in the written text gram. end of a word; right part of a compound; end of a sentence — f. avasānā ifc. conclusion, end tion, cessation of (iic.).
avasāya [pfp. [1] avasā] amnf avasāyā to destroy; to finish — act. m. termination; completion, conclusion, end | determination.
avasāyin [agt. avasā] ifc. amnf avasāyinī who establishes his residence at, who settles at (iic.).
avasikta [pp. avasic] amnf avasiktā poured on; sprinkled.
avasic [avasic] v. [6] pr. (avasiñcati) pp. (avasikta) to sprinkle, to water; to pour on acc. loc. .

ávasita [pp. avasā] amnf avasitā ter miné, completed; finished; determined, fixed; understood ved. that which has settled, that which has taken as residence — n. residence. gangām anvavasitā purī the city is situated on the banks of the Ganges.

avasṛj [avasṛj₁] v. [6] pr. (avasṛjati) pp. (avasṛṣṭa) to release, to spread; to cause to flow, to let fall | to abandon (one's anger, one's life, etc.) | to give birth; to produce; to release. rudhiraughān avāsrjan | Rām. | (The rākṣasās) caused torrents of blood to rain down.
avasṛp [avasṛp] v. [1] pr. (avasárpati) to set (sun); to withdraw (sea at low tide) to approach secretly.
avasṛṣṭa [pp. avasṛj] amnf avasṛṣṭā released: sent — ifc. fallen from; fell on (iic.).
avaskand [avaskand] v. [1] pr. (avaskan dati) pp. (avaskanna) to jump out, to come down from (abl.) | to spring out of (abl.) | to rush upon, to pounce on, to attack acc. .
avaskanda [act. avaskand] m. assault, attack.
avastu [opp. vastu₁] n. thing without value phil. insubstantiality; immateriality; unreality of matter. nāvastunah vastusiddhih phil. [Sāmkhya] No material object can come from the immaterial.

avasthā₁ [avasthā₁] v. [1] pr. (avatisthati) pr. r. (avatisthate) pp. (avasthita) pf. (pari, vi, sam) to take place, to stand, to stop | to establish oneself; to inhabit, to remain; to exist, to be stable — ca. (avasthāpayati) to cause to stop | to fix, to place (on (loc.)).

avasthā₂ [act. avasthā₁] f. condition, degree; stage; state, situation [lit. [theatre] moral situation through which the hero passes; the Nāṭyaśāstra distinguishes 5 of them: the undertaking |ārambha|, the effort of progress | prayatna|, the hope of success | prāptyāśā|, the certainty of success [niyatāpti] and the success [prāptyāśā].
avasthātraya [traya] n. phil. the three states of consciousness: waking |jāgrat|, dreaming |svapna| and deep sleep |susupti|.
avasthāntara | antara | n. difference of state; different state, other state.
avasthāna [act. avasthā₁] n. the act of standing; situation, condition; establishment | stay, residence; stability.
avasthāpana [act. That. avasthā₁] n. ex position (not. of goods for sale) — ifc. avasthāpanna gram. expressing (iic.).
avasthita [pp. avasthā₁] amnf avas thitā present, who stands ready; determined | standing, firm, stable.
avasthiti [act. avasthā₁] f. stability.
avasru [avasru] ca. (avasrāvayati) pf. (sam) to make flow downwards.
avahat [neg. vahat] amnf avahatī that does not flow; that remains at rest.
avahan [avahan₁] v. [2] pr. (avahanti) knock down; beat (grain). vrīhīn avahanti we beat the rice.
avahanana |act. avahan| n. threshing.
avahāra |act. avahṛ| m. act of carrying off, vol.
avahāsa | avahāsa | m. joke; humor; derision.
avahāsya [avahāsya] amnf avahāsyā risible; ridicule.
ávahita [pp. avadhā] amnf avahitā at tentif. avahitaih sthītayām tenez-vous prêt.
avahittha n. dissimulation phil. [aesthetics] transient feeling [vyabhicāribhāva] related to dissimulation when secretly looking at the sexually desired person [śṛṅgārarasa] — f. avahitthā id.
avahṛ [avahṛ₁] pf. (abhi, vi) [unused without pf.].

avāc var. avāñc [avaac] amnf avācī [m. nom. avān; n. nom. avāk] turned downwards, directed downwards | turned towards the South; southern — f. avācī downward direction. avāk adv. down, downwards; in depth.
avācya [neg. vācya] amnf avācyā which should not be spoken of.
avāntará |avaantara| amnf avāntarā
intermediate | respective | var. avāntarām between. avāntaram adv. differently from (abl.).
avāntaradīkṣā [dīkṣā] f. soc. consecration in intermédiaire.

avāp [avaāp] v. [5] pr. (avāpnoti) pr. r. (avāpnuté) pp. (avāpta) to obtain, attain; to meet, to fall upon | math. to obtain as a quotient to take upon oneself; to attract, to suffer; to incur. bhāryām avāptavān he took a wife. atha cettvamimam dharmyam samgrāmam na kariṣyasi | tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi | [BhG.] Thus, if you do not take part in this just struggle, then you will lose your duty and your honor and you will incur sin.

avāpoh [avaapoh] abs. (avāpohya) to discard. śarīre caiva śāstre ca dṛṣṭārthaḥ syād viśāradaḥ drstaśrutābhyām sandeham avāpohyācaret kriyāh | Suśruta The specialist must recognize the object both in the organism and in the manual; one must take action after removing doubts concerning what is observed and heard.
avāpta [pp. avāp] amnf avāptā which has reached | obtained — n. math. ["obtained by division"].

avāptavat [ppa. avāp] amnf avāptavatī who obtained or attained. kaścit sārthavāhaḥ 'tītāśītivarṣaḥ prabhūtam vittam dattvā tarunīm bhāryāmavāptavān A caravan driver over 80 years old obtained a young wife after paying a large sum.
avāpti [act. avāp] f. obtaining | math. what holds.
avāya [act. ave] m. act of descending (to the river, etc.) | submission.
avāsas [priv. vāsas] amnf without clothing, naked.
avāsastva |tva| n. absence of clothing; nudity.
avi [avi] m. sheep — f. sheep || lat. ovis; eng. Ewe; fr. sheep.
avika [ka] m. sheep — f. avikā sheep.
avigostha [gostha] n. sheepfold.

avimāraka [māraka] n. lit. np. of the avimāraka, a play by Bhāsa inspired by the Bṛhatkathā — m. lit. np. of Prince Avimāraka, son of King Savīra, hero of this drama; during his father's exile due to a curse, he saves a princess from a furious elephant; at the end of complex intrigues they are reunited.
avyáya₁ |aya| amnf avyayā ved. concerning the sheep | made of sheepskin | ved. not. filter used to prepare soma.
avikala [neg. vikala] amnf avikalā not mutilated; whole, complete; normal, in order.
avikalpa [opp. vikalpa] m. absence of alternative; uniqueness of decision — priv. amnf avikalpā not distinguished, not particularized | not pro crastinant. avikalpam adv. without hesitation.
avikalpaka |ka| amnf avikalpakā who does not hesitate | phil. non-conceptual (said of perception).
avikāra [priv. vikāra] amnf avikārā constant; invariable — absence m. absence of change; non-alteration.
avikārya [neg. vikārya] amnf avikāryā constant; invariable.
avikṛta [neg. vikṛta] amnf avikṛtā inva riable, unalterable | firm in convictions, faithful | without change; without deformation.
aviklava [priv. viklava] amnf aviklavā without fail, without hesitation.
Avikṣit [avikṣita] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the king Avikṣit "the Indestructible", son of Karand
hama [Kārandhama], whom he succeeded at the beginning of the tretāyuga; he had 100 horse sacrifices celebrated by Angirā; his son is Marutta.
avigīta [neg. vigīta] amnf avigītā non contradictoire.
avigraha [priv. vigraha] amnf avigrahā gram. is said of an idiomatic compound word that cannot be paraphrased, such as aśvakarna.

avighāta [priv. vighāta] amnf avighātā unobstructed; without hindrance — opp. mr. absence of obstacle. সবিঘ্ন avighna [priv. vighna] amnf avighnā without obstacle; uninterrupted — n. absence of obstacle. avighnena adv. without encountering any obstacles. avighnamastu (introductory invocation of a work) may our path be without obstacle.
avicalita [neg. vicalita] amnf avica litā that does not deviate; that remains concentrated (mind) that does not deviate from (abl.).
avicāra [opp. vicāra] m. lack of discernment; lack of reflection. avicāram adv. without hesitation.
avicāraramaṇīya | ramaṇīya | afmn avicāraramaṇīya unconditionally satisfied; naive.
avicāraramaṇīyatva [vat] n. naivete.
avicāraṇa [absence vicāraṇa] n. absence of deliberation; absence of hesitation. avicāranāt adv. without hesitation.

avicāraṇīya [neg. vicāraṇīya] amnf avicāranīyā which does not require deliberation; peremptory | inconceivable (said of the gods). ājñā gurūṇāṃ hyavicāraṇīyā the order of the elders must not be questioned.
avicārita [neg. vicārita] amnf avicāritā that has not been discussed | that does not merit discussion; indisputable; certain, clear. avicāritam adv. without hesitation.
avicārya₁ [neg. vicārya₁] amnf avicāryā indisputable.
avicārya₂ [neg. vicārya₁] ind. without discussion; not having reflected.
avicālin [neg. vicālin] amnf avicalinī constant, fixed, invariable.
avicchindat [neg. vicchindat] amnf avicchindatī which does not separate, which does not interrupt.
avicchinna [neg. vicchinna] amnf avicchinnā without limitation; not separated, ininter broken; continuous. avicchinnaparamparā unbroken lineage.
áviccheda [opp. viccheda] m. state of being uninterrupted; continuity. avicchedāt var. avicchedena without interruption.
avicchedin [in] amnf avicchedinī who works tirelessly, relentlessly.
avijña [neg. vijña] amnf avijñā ignorant.
avijñatā [tā] f. ignorance.
ávijñāta [neg. vijñāta] amnf avijñātā unknown | uncertain, doubtful; forgotten (author).
ávijñātagati [gati] amnf whose route is unknown.
avijñāya [neg. vijñāya] ind. not having discerned.
avijñeya [neg. vijñeya] amnf avijñeyā indiscernible, imperceptible | that which cannot be known, incomprehensible.
avita [pp. av] amnf avitā protected.

avitatha [neg. vitatha] amnf avitathā not erroneous; correct | not futile; relevant. var. avitathena not to avitatham wrong; in accordance with the truth. avitathīkr validate; make effective; execute (order). avitathamāha Priyamvadā Priyamvadā is right. .5
avidagdha [neg. vidagdha] amnf avi dagdhā unburned; undigested | ignorant; stupid. muñca mām avidagdhas tvam [KSS.] Leave me alone, you are a fool.
avidāsin [neg. vidāsin] amnf avidāsinī that does not run out; that does not dry up (pond); perennial.
avidita [neg. vidita] amnf aviditā in known | who does not know, ignorant of g. . avidite in ignorance of (g.). aviditam without knowing ((g.)) | so that no one knows.
aviddha [neg. viddha] amnf aviddhā not pierced, not perforated.
aviddhakarna [karna] amnf aviddhakarnī whose ear is not pierced — m. hist. np. of the logician [naiyāyika] bd. Aaviddhakarņa (7th century).
avidya [priv. vidyā] amnf avidyā ignorant; uneducated — f. cf. avidyā.
avidyamāna [neg. vidyamāna] amnf avidyamānā non-existent; absent.
avidyamānatā [tā] f. non-existence; absence.
avidyamānatva [tva] n. id.
avidyamānavat [vat] adv. as if he were not there.

avidyā [opp. vidyā] f. ignorance | phil. nescience; syn. akhyāti | phil. [Vedānta] illusion, personified by Māyā; this key concept of advaita was fought in the viśiṣṭādvaita | bd. ignorance, the cause of suffering [pratītyasamutpāda] | pali avijjā.

avidyāgranthi [granthi] m. phil. knot of ignorance. purușa evedam viśvam karma tapo brahma parāmṛtam etadyo veda nihitam guhāyām so'vidyāgranthim vikiratīha somya | [MO.] Only Being is all here below, pious acts as well as penances; the Absolute is the supreme immortal; he who knows this in the depths of his heart destroys the knot of ignorance here and now, dear friend.
avidyāmaya [maya] amnf avidyāmayī made up of ignorance.
avidvas [neg. vidvas] amnf aviduṣī ignorant, imprudent; fool, senseless, stupid. avidvāmsah the ignorant ones.
avidhavā [opp. vidhavā] f. woman who is not a widow.
avidhānatas [opp. vidhānatas] adv. not in accordance with the rules, irregularly.
avidhipūrvakam [opp. vidhipūrvakam] adv. contrary to his duty; irregularly.
avidheya [neg. vidheya] amnf avidheyā disobedient, insubordinate | med. not. sick non do cile (to whom treatment can be refused).
avinaya [priv. vinaya] amnf avinayā ill-mannered, impolite, impertinent — opp. m. bad conduct, impoliteness.
avinābhāva [opp. vinābhāva] m. ["sine qua non"] necessary connection, inseparability; ca inherent character; cf. vyāpti.
avinābhāvin [in] amnf avinābhāvinī necessarily connected; inherent.
avināśa [opp. vināśa] m. nondestruction; non-putrefaction.
avināśita [neg. vināśita] amnf avināśitā not putrefied; healthy.
avināśin [neg. vināśin] amnf avināśinī imperishable | which does not corrupt; im putrescible.

avinīta [neg. vinīta] amnf avinītā ill-mannered, impolite; undisciplined; arrogant, imperti nent — m. hist. np. of King Avinita of the Ganga dynasty in Karṇāṭa (6th century); his son Durvinīta succeeded him.
aviparyāsita [opp. viparyāsita] amnf aviparyāsitā unchanged, unaltered.
avipaścita [neg. vipaścita] amnf avipaścitā ignorant; incompetent; fool.
avipluta [neg. vipluta] amnf aviplutā not defiled, not dishonored.
avibhakta [neg. vibhakta] amnf avib haktā indivisible, not separated.
avibhaktatva [vat] n. phil. the undivided; the undistinguished.
avibhaktadāyāda [dāyādá] amnf avibhak tadāyādā soc. is said of parents [sapinda] who share the offerings [pinda] during a ceremony of homage to the ancestors [śrāddha].
avibhakti [priv. vibhakti] amnf gram. (word) uninflected; theme.
avibhaktinirdeśa [nirdeśa] m. gram. reference to a word without inflection.

avibhāga [opp. vibhāga] m. non-separation; lack of distinction (from g.) | phil. [Vijñānabhikṣu] this absence of difference [abheda] is compatible with difference in the sense of non-identity [vibhāga], allowing the coherence of the formula bhedābheda characterizing the relationship between brahman and ātman. .6 avibhāgena adv. without distinction; in the same way. avibhāge adv. [Bhartrhari] in dream; opp. pra vibhāge.
avibhāvya [neg. vibhāvya] amn avibhāvyā imperceptible, indistinguishable; f. undetectable; indistinct (lyrics).
avibhāvyatā [tā] f. undetectable. avibhāvyatām gata has become undetectable.
avibhinna [neg. vibhinna] amnf avib hinnā not separated from (abl.) | unchanged.
avimarśa [priv. vimarśa] amnf Avi marśā inconsiderate; thoughtless — ifc. who does not take into account, negligent (iic.).
avimukta [opp. vimukta] amnf Avi muktā not released; not abandoned — m. n.p. from Avi mukta, epith. from a tīrtha from the city of Benares "which Siva never abandoned"; designates Kāśī Vārāṇasī.
avimukteśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Avi mukteśvara, epith. of Shiva tutelary of Kāśī.
avirata [neg. virata] amnf aviratā who does not renounce (abl.) | uninterrupted. aviratam adv. without interruption, continuously.

aviratasamyaktva [samyaktva] n. jn. 4th stage of spiritual development, where one reaches the state of rectitude without renunciation; it is the stage of spiritual qualification that a layperson who has not taken vows can reach.
avirala [neg. virala] amnf aviralā dense, compact; contiguous; intense | incessant, numerous. aviralam intensely; in a compact manner.
aviruddha [neg. viruddha] amnf Avi ruddhā not obstructed, not excluded, not prohibited | compatible with (i. iic.).
avirodha [opp. virodha] m. non-opposition to, compatibility with, harmony with (i.e., i.). svārthāvirodhena adv. in accordance with their own interest.

avilamba [neg. vilamba] amnf Avi lambā that does not linger; prompt, without delay. avilambam var. avilambena adv. without delay, immediately | without interval. padānām avilambenoccāraņam gram. utterance of words without discontinuity.
avivakṣā [opp. vivakṣā] f. absence of explicit mention.
avivakṣita [neg. vivakṣita] amnf avivaksitā not signified | phil. [Mīmāmsā] that one does not intend to express literally; fig ratif.
avivaksitavācya [vācya] mn lit. non-literal meaning of an utterance; figurative meaning.

avivikta [neg. vivikta] amnf aviviktā not separated; not discriminated | indistinct; confused phil. undifferentiated (said of a non-conceptualized perception) | not solitary; not withdrawn from the world.
aviveka [priv. viveka] amnf avivekā without discrimination, without discernment; unreasoned — m. phil. [yoga] nondiscrimination between the purusa and the prakṛti.
avivekatā [opp. vivekatā] f. lack of discernment, lack of judgment.
avivekitā [priv. vivekitā] f. lack of discernment, lack of judgment.
aviśańka [priv. viśańkā₁] amnf aviśankā who does not hesitate, decided; without worry, without reservation.
aviśiṣṭa [neg. viśiṣṭa] amnf aviśiṣṭā indeterminate. Avišistalinga | linga | amnf Avišistalingā gram. whose gender is not determined.

aviśesa [opp. viśesa] m. non-discrimination, non-distinction; non-difference — priv. amnf aviśeṣā without difference; uniform | pl. phil. [Sāṃkhya] the 5 subtle substances [tanmātra]. avaiseṣāt var. aviseṣeṇa adv. without making distinction. avisesatas adv. without difference. sarvamaviśesena paśyati he looks at everything without understanding anything (etymology of paśu).
aviśvāsin [neg. viśvāsin] amnf aviśvāsinī distrustful; who does not trust.

aviṣaya [priv. viṣaya] amnf aviṣayā outside the domain, off-screen, beyond the bounds; irrelevant | that which does not concern you, that which is not your business | illegal, impossible, forbidden; unsuitable for g. . sakalavacanānāmaviṣayam tatsthānam this place defies description. tasyāḥ śrīrvacanānāmaviṣayā there are no words to describe its beauty.
aviṣṇu [neg. viṣṇu] amnf not tel to viṣṇu.
avisaṃvāda [opp. visaṃvāda] m. not breaking one's word; not contradicting oneself.
avisaṃvādaka [neg. visaṃvādaka] amnf avisamvādikā which does not contradict.
avisaṃvādakatva [tva] n. phil. [Dharmottara] non-contradiction, coherence. .7
avisaṃvādin [neg. visaṃvādin] amnf avisamvādinī non-contradictory, coherent; reliable.
avisaṃvāditva [tva] n. reliability.
avihata [neg. vihata] amnf avihatā not rejected, not banished; not prevented.
avī [priv. vī₂] f. woman having her period.
avīkṣaṇa [opp. vīkṣaṇa] n. act of not observing.
Avīci [priv. vīci] amnf without wave — m. bd. np. of Avīci, one of the 8 burning hells, where the damned are perpetually roasted in a furnace.
avṛká |priv. vṛka| amnf avṛkā sans dan ger. avrkám adv. safely, without aggression; with love.
avṛtta [neg. vṛtta] amnf avṛttā who has not arrived | still alive | who behaves badly.
avṛtti [opp. vṛtti] f. absence of resources | non-occurrence; non-existence | phil. [NN.] non-localization.
ave [avai] v. [2] pr. (avaiti) pp. (aveta) pf. (vi, prati, sam) approach | consider as; com take, know ((inf.)).
avekṣ [avaīkṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (avekṣate) pp. (avekṣita) pfp. (avekṣya) to consider, observe, notice | to take into consideration, to take into account.
avekṣā [act. avekṣ] f. circular look | regard, consideration.
avekṣya [pfp. [1] avekṣ] amnf avekṣyā worthy of consideration; to be taken into consideration — abs. ind. taking into consideration acc. . anaveksya param without regard for others.
avedayat [neg. vedayat] amnf ave dayantī en ignorant (acc.). śrāntimaveddantī (f.) ignoring fatigue.
avaidika [priv. vaidika] amnf avaidikā not in accordance with the Veda.
avaidikadarśanasamgraha [darśanasamgraha] m. bed. of the avaidikadarśanasamgraha, catalog of non-orthodox doctrines due to Gangādhara₃ Vājapeyī.
avaidharmya [priv. vaidharmya] amnf avaidharmyā phil. which does not differ in an essential way.
avaiyākaraṇa [neg. vaiyākaraṇa] amnf avaiyākaraṇī which is not a grammarian.
avairāgya [opp. vairāgya] n. non renunciation of passions. 1.
avaiṣṇava [neg. vaiṣṇava] amnf avaiṣṇavī nonvishnouite.

avyakta [neg. vyakta] amnf avyaktā invisible, undetectable, imperceptible; unmanifest — m. phil. [Sāṃkhya] the Primordial Nature [mūlaprakṛti] in its form of the unmanifest or indeterminate, subtle spirit from which all the phenomena of the material world of Manifestation derive | vyakta | gram. onomatopoeia. avyaktānukaraņam gram. onomatopoeia.
avyagra [neg. vyagra] amnf avyagrā calm, thoughtful; unoccupied | occupied with one thing — acc. avyagram adv. calmly, deliberately, at leisure.
avyatirikta [neg. vyatirikta] amnf avyatiriktā not distinct from, like (abl. iic.). avyatirikteyamasmaccharīrāt she is not different from me.
avyatireka [opp. vyatireka] m. non-exclusion, non-exception; compatibility.
avyapadeśya [neg. vyapadeśya] amnf avyapadeśyā phil. non-verbalized; unutterable, inexpressible, which cannot be verbalized — f. avya padeśyā myth. np. of avyapadeśyā, epith. of Kālī the indefinable.
avyabhicarita [neg. vyabhicarita] amnf avyabhicaritā phil. [Nyāya] (reasoning) without fail.
avyabhicaritatva [tva] n. phil. [Nyāya] absence of error in an inference.
avyabhicāra [opp. vyabhicāra] m. non-transgression; fidelity | non-failure; absolute necessity — priv. amnf avyabhicārā constant; faithful. avyabhicārāt var. avyabhicāreņa inevitably.
avyabhicāravat [vat] amnf avyabhicāravatī inevitable.
avyabhicārin [neg. vyabhicārin] amnf avyabhicāriņī that does not fail | stable; per manent; faithful. avyabhicārī tadvacaḥ this proposition admits of no exceptions.

avyaya₂ [neg. vyaya] amnf avyayā invariable, unalterable, immutable; constant; indestructible, imperishable | avaricious | gram. indeclinable — m. avarice — n. gram. indeclinable word; invariable nominal compound in all genders and numbers, inheriting its adverbial function from its first member. avyayībhū gram. to become indeclinable (said of a word forming a fixed adverbial compound with an indeclinable first member, such as yathāśakti).
avyayavarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Sāmānyakāṇḍa, dealing with indeclinables.
avyayī iiv. avyaya₂.
avyayībhāva [bhāva] m. gram. ["conversion to indeclinable"] use of a first-member indeclinable nominal compound as a fixed (indeclinable) adverb.
avyavasāyin [neg. vyavasāyin] amnf avyavasāyinī inactive; negligent.
avyavasita [neg. avyavasita] amnf avyavasitā id.
avyavastha [priv. vyavasthā₂] amnf avyavasthā irregular, chaotic; ephemeral — f. avya vasthā irregularity; instability; chaos.
avyākṛta [neg. vyākṛta] amnf avyākṛtā phil. non manifest, non-developed; la tent.

avyāja [priv. vyāja] amnf avyājā that does not pretend, that does not feign; not artificial — opp. m. absence of fraud; non-dissimulation simplicity. avyājamanoharam vapuh a naturally magnificent body.
avyāpanna |neg. vyāpanna| amnf avyāpannā alive.
avyāpta [neg. vyāpta] amnf avyāptā phil. [Nyāya] incomplete.
avyāptavṛtti [vṛtti] f. phil. [Nyāya] incomplete manifestation; non-exclusive property.
avyāpti [opp. vyāpti] f. gram. under generalization; insufficient extension; in completeness; opp. ativyāpti.
avyutpatti [opp. vyutpatti] f. lit. [aesthetics] lack of sound judgment; lack of taste.
avyutpattipakṣa opp. vyutpattipaksa] m. gram. antithesis of the instituting view that every nominal is derived from a verbal root; this view is defended by Pāṇini.
avyutpattipakṣin |in| amnf avyutpattipakṣinī gram. Opponent of the view that every nominal is derived from a verbal root; opp. vyutpattipaksin.
avyutpanna [neg. vyutpanna] amnf avyutpannā non-derived | gram. refers to nouns that cannot be derived from a root. 1.
avyutpannaśabda [śabda] m. gram. noun not derived from a Sanskrit root; word of foreign origin.
avraņa [priv. vraņa] amnf avraņā not wounded, unharmed | intact, without defect (not. weapon).
aśakta [neg. śakta] amnf aśaktā inca pable (de (inf.)) | incompetent (en (loc. dat.)).
aśakti [opp. śakti] f. impotence; incapa cité.
aśaknuvat [neg. śaknuvat] amnf aśaknuvatī incapable of (inf.).
aśakya [neg. śakya] amnf aśakyā impossible.
aśańka [priv. śańkā] amnf aśańkā without hesitation; without worry.
aśańkita [neg. śańkita] amnf aśańkitā confident, without worry | certain.
aśaná₁ |agt. aś₁| ifc. amnf aśanī who has dyed, who obtains (iic.).
aśaná₂ |act. aś₂| n. food; meal — agt. f. aśanā ifc. who eats (iic.) — v. [11] pr. (aśanāyáti) to desire to eat, to be hungry — v. [11] pr. (aśanīyati) id.
aśanāyā [ayā] f. hunger.

aśabdasamjñā [neg. śabdasamjñā] f. gram. A word that is not a technical term of grammar. svam rūpam śabdasyāśabdasamjñā gram. [Pāṇini] A word that is not a technical term of grammar denotes its own form.
aśaraṇa [priv. śaraṇa] amnf aśaraṇā without protection, without defense; without refuge. aśaranīki to deprive of protection.
aśarīra [priv. śarīra] amnf aśarīrā without a body, incorporeal — m. myth. epithet of Kāma — n. gram. absence of a verb in a sentence. .9
aśarīracit | cit₂ | f. phil. intangible consciousness.
aśarīratva |tva| n. phil. |Vedānta| disembodied state; qualifies liberation | mokṣa|.
aśarīrin [in] amnf aśarīrinī incorporeal; said not. of a celestial voice.
aśastra [priv. śastra₂] amnf aśastrā Unarmed.
áśānta |neg. śānta| amnf aśāntā agitated; violent; impatient, irritable.
aśāmya |neg. śāmya| amnf aśāmyā that cannot be appeased; irreconcilable. aśāmyam vairam irreconcilable enemy.
aśāśvata [neg. śāśvata] amnf aśāśvatī non permanent; transient.
aśāstra [priv. śāstra] amnf aśāstrā not in accordance with sacred texts.
aśāstravihita [neg. śāstravihita] amnf aśāstravihitā not prescribed by sacred texts.
aśāstrasiddha [neg. śāstrasiddha] amnf aśāstrasiddhā id.
aśāstrīya [neg. śāstrīya] amnf aśāstrīyā not in accordance with sacred texts.
aśitá [pp. aś₂] amnf aśitā eaten, devoured — n. place of a meal.
aśiras [priv. śiras] amnf Headless.
aśiraska [aśiraska] amnf aśiraskā id.
áśiva [neg. śiva] amnf aśivā wicked, harmful, dangerous | myth. said of hostile supernatural beings. সংখিত aśiṣṭa [neg. śiṣṭa₂] amnf aśiṣṭā ill-mannered;
uncultured | forbidden || fr. incest.

aśiṣya [neg. śiṣya] amnf aśiṣyā which should not be educated | useless to teach. lingam aśisyam [Pāṇini] The gender of nouns is not taught (by grammar, because it is arbitrary and is acquired through use).
asīta [asīti] ifc. amnf asītī ord. 80th.
aśīti [aṣṭati] num. f. sg. eighty.
aśītitama [tama] amnf aśītitamī ord. 80°.
aśīla [neg. śīla] amnf aśīlā ill-mannered, vulgar — n. vulgarity, rudeness, obscenity.
aśuci [neg. śuci] amnf impur.
áśuddha [neg. śuddha] amnf aśuddhā impure | imprecise; incorrect, erroneous.

áśubha [neg. śubha] amnf aśubhā ugly; unpleasant; unfavorable, ominous; bad, wicked — n. impurity; evil, sin; misfortune | bd. spiritual practice of evoking the repugnant aspect of the physical body to control desire || pali asubha.
aśuśrūṣā [opp. śuśrūṣā] f. aversion to study; disobedience; the act of neglecting one's duty.
aśuśrūṣu [neg. śuśrūṣu] amnf who does not like to study; disobedient (inverted (g.)).
aśūdra [opp. śūdra] amnf aśūdrā soc. noble class.
aśūnya |neg. śūnya| amnf aśūnyā not empty; occupied | not neglected; filled, executed. svaniyogamaśūnyam kuru fulfill your task; attend to your affairs.
áśeva [neg. śeva] amnf aśevā non-friendly; hostile.
aśeṣa [priv. śeṣa] amnf aśeṣā Without remainder, whole. aśesena completely. aśesatas adv. entirely, without exception. aśesavidyāgrahanasāmarthyam ability to grasp all kinds of knowledge.

aśoka [priv. śoka] amnf aśokā that does not cause pain; cheerful, that does not experience sorrow; that brings consolation — m. bio. bot. Sa raca Asoka, ashok tree with very fragrant orange flowers in globules, with pinnate leaves; myth. it was in a grove of ashok trees that Rāvaņa imprisoned Sītā; the tree is sacred, and considered to ward off calamities; it is said that it only flowers if it is touched by the foot of a young woman | hist. np. of the emperor aśoka "(given birth) Without pain", of the Maurya dynasty; he reigned in Pāṭaliputra in the 3rd century BC; he established a vast empire, from Kabul to Bengal, from Nepal to almost Madras; He introduced stone buildings, writing, and organized a rational administration; he conquered Kalinga by a bloody war; he subsequently converted to Buddhism under the influence of his wife and had moral edicts inscribed throughout India, notably on monolithic pillars [stambha] of polished stone bearing sculptures; cf. Devānāmpriya, Priyadarśin | pali Asoka.

Aśokadatta [datta] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Aśokadatta, eldest son of the brahmin Govindasvāmī; he became an invincible wrestler, and the king took him as a bodyguard; one day he was lured into a crematorium field by the rākṣasī Vidyucchikhā from whom he took an ankle ring.

Aśokamālā [mālā] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of Aśokamālā, daughter of the vidyādhara king Aśokakara; proud of her great beauty, she refused to marry; her father cursed her to be reborn on Earth where she was married against her will to the hideous brahmin Haṭhaśarmā; pursued by the vengeance of her husband, she took refuge at the court of King Naravāhanadatta where a celestial voice reminded her of her true identity, thus ending the spell.
aśokavana | vana | n. wood of ashok trees.

aśokavanikā [ika] f. grove of ashok trees. aśokavanikānyāya m. maxim of the grove of ashok trees; it applies to an arbitrary choice, such as the fact that Rāvaņa imprisoned Sītā in a grove of ashok trees rather than another species.
aśokāvadāna |avadāna₂| n. bed. n.p. from the aśokāvadāna, comic legend. of Emperor Aśoka.

aśokāṣṭamī [aṣṭamī] f. soc. festival of aśokāṣṭamī, on the 8th day of the bright fortnight of the month caitra, celebrated in Bengal and Orissa; it celebrates the pūjā of Rāma praying to Šiva and Bhavānī in order to defeat Rāvaṇa, at the instigation of Vibhīṣaṇa; it is the occasion of the chariot festival [rathayātrā] of Lingarāja, where SivaCandrasekhara is transported for 4 days to the Rāmeśvara₁ temple.
aśocanīya [neg. śocanīya] amnf aśocanīyā which should not be grieved.
aśocya [neg. śocya] amnf aśocyā id. — n. (impers.) one should not grieve.
aśauca [opp. śauca] n. impurity; malpro preté.
aśnat [ppr. aś₂] amnf aśnatī while eating.
aśnīta [imp. aś₂] ind. eat!

aśnītapibatā [pibata] f. festivity (where one eats and drinks without ceasing); syn. pibatakhādatā. ākhyātamākhyātena kriyāsātatye | aśnītapibatā || gram. The compound word aśnītapibatā is obtained by juxtaposing two verbal forms.
aśma iic. aśman.

Aśmaka [ka] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of King Aśmaka₁ "born (by cesarean section) from a stone", son of King Kalmāṣapāda of the solar lineage |sūryavaṃśa|; he is father of Mūlaka | pl. aśmakās geo. np. of the Aśmaka country in Kerala (region of mod. Travan core/Trivandrum) and of his warrior people the aśmakās.
aśmarī [ra] f. med. calculi.

aśmalostra [lostra] m. stone and clod of earth. aśmalostranyāya saying of the stone and the clod of earth (used to compare the relative importance of two objects). aśmavat [vat] amnf aśmavatī of stone.
aśmasāra [sāra] mn fer.
aśmasāramaya |maya| amnf aśmasāramayī in iron.
aśmāropaṇa |āropaṇa| n. soc. rite of touching a stone with the right foot; not. by the young bride during the wedding ceremony.
áśman m. stone, rock | mineral; not. iron ore | (strike of) lightning | vault of the heavens | gr. ακμων. aśmavat |vat| amnf aśmavatī made of stone.
aśra₁ cf. asra.

aśra₁ ifc. aśri. अশ্বদ্ধ aśraddhá [priv. śraddhā₂] amnf aśraddhā unbeliever; one who does not trust g. — opp. f. aśraddhā lack of trust; unbelief. अশ্বাদ্ধ aśrāddha [nég. śrāddha] amnf aśrāddhā soc. one who does not sacrifice to the shades — n. food not used as an offering to the shades — f. aśrāddhā nonbelief.
aśrapa | pa₁ | amnf aśrapā blood drinker.

aśrāddhabhogin [bhogin₂] amfn aśrāddhabhoginī soc. who has taken a vow to fast during the rite to the manes. সঙ্গি áśri f. angle, corner, summit; edge of a weapon, any sharp object — m. aśra₁ cl. after num. that has so many summits | lat. acer.

aśrita [neg. śrita] amnf aśritā discon necté. aśritakriyāvākya gram. nominal phrase. अস্থ্র áśru n. tear; weeping. aśru kr to weep. aśrupūrņākulekṣaṇam adv. with eyes rolling back and filled with tears.
aśrukantha | kantha | amnf aśrukanthī with tears in her voice.
aśrukanthya [kanthya] amnf aśrukanthyā with a voice choked with tears.
aśrupluta [pluta] amnf aśruplutā flooded with tears.
aśruplutamukha [mukha] amnf aśruplutamukhī with his face flooded with tears.
aśruvindu [vindu₁] m. tear.
aśruvindumat [mat] amnf Aśruvindumatī who makes one cry — f. Aśruvindumatī myth. np. of Aśruvindumatī "who makes one cry", daughter of Kāma, sent by Indra to seduce Yayāti.
áśruta [neg. śruta] amnf aśrutā not heard of; of which one has not heard | not instructed; ignorant. aśrutapūrvam not heard before. aśrutakriyāvākya gram. |Vākyapadīya| phrase no minale.
áśruti [opp. śruti] f. forgetfulness | act of not hearing | lit. (text) unrevealed. aśrutimabhinayati he/she pretends not to hear.
aślīlá [neg. ślīla] amnf aślīlā vul gaire, coarser; fildurier — n. vulgar language; vulgarity.
aślīlátā |tā| f. vulgarity; obscenity, pornography.
aślīlátva [tva] n. id.

aśleṣā [priv. śleṣa] f. astr. np. of aśleṣā, lunar asterism [nakṣatra] of Hydra; cf. Aśleṣās pl. np. of the Aśleṣās, id. (for the 5 stars composing it). अস্ব áśva m. horse | knight in chess [caturangā]; syn. turamga | math. symb. the number 7 (for saptāśva) — f. aśvā mare — v. [11] pr. (aśvāyáti) to look for horses — v. [11] pr. (aśvasyati) to desire the stallion (said of the mare) | lat. eqūs; gr. o ; fr. equidé. aśvavadavam n. sg. (collective) the horses (males and females).

áśvakarna | karna | m. horse ear | bio. epithet of the śāla tree [bot. Shorea robusta], whose leaves resemble a horse's ear. aśvakarṇanyāya gram. [Ṭupṭīkā] horse ear maxim, referring to a word in an idiomatic sense [rūdha]. yathāśvakarņa ityukte vinaivāśvena gamyate kaścid eva viśisto'rthah sarvesu pratyayas tathā phil. [Vākyapadīya] Just as pronouncing aśvakarna does not evoke a horse, generally it is a particular meaning (of a word) that is understood (depending on the context).
aśvakovida [kovida] amnf aśvakovidā skillful rider.
aśvakhura | khura | mr. horse hoof.
aśvagandhā [gandhā] f. bio. bot. Physalis Flexuosa (or bot. Withania somnifera), a solanaceous plant with orange berries inside the calyx; used in medicine to treat anxiety and insomnia.
aśvagopa [gopa] m. groom.
aśvaghāsa [ghāsa] m. fodder for horses.
aśvaghāsakāyastha [kāyastha] m. soc. quartermaster sergeant.

Aśvaghosa [ghosa] m. hist. np. of Aśvaghosa "He who neighs", contemporary poet and playwright of Kanişka₁ (2nd century); he lived in Pāṭaliputra and then in Purusapura at the court of Kanişka₁; son of a brahmin, he converted to Buddhism; he composed the Buddhacarita, the Saundarananda, and the Sāriputraprakaraņa.
áśvatará [tara] m. organic. zoo. mule — f. aśvatarī mule | bardot.
aśvadaghná [daghna] amnf aśvadaghnā f. aśvadaghnī which has (water) up to the height of a horse.
Aśvapati [pati] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of Aśvapati "Master of the horse", king of the Kekayās; his eldest son is Yudhājit, Kaikeyī is his daughter.
áśvamukha [mukha] amnf aśvamukhī who has a horse's head | myth. chimeric celestial being, with a horse's head.
áśvamedhá [medha] m. soc. horse sacrifice, Vedic ceremony of conquest of an empire by run in one year by a horse; it begins on the 8th or 9th day of the clear fortnight of the month phālguna .
áśvamedhika [ika] amnf aśvamedhikā concerning the sacrifice of the horse — m. soc. horse intended for sacrifice.
áśvayuj | yuj₂ | amnf who harnesses or controls horses — f. du. aśvayújau astr. np. du naksatra Aśvayujau "the pair of two Riders"; cf. Aśvinī.
áśvaśaká [śaka₂] n. horse dung.
áśvaśapha [śapha] m. horse hoof.
Aśvaśāstra [śāstra] n. hippology | lit. np. of the Aśvaśāstra, a work of hippology by Nakula₁.

aśvasena [senā] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the serpent [nāga] aśvasena, son of Takṣaka; he escaped the burning of the Khāndava forest thanks to the sacrifice of his mother, in whose body he had hidden; vowing infinite hatred to Arjuna, he slipped like a magic arrow into Karna's quiver, but Kṛṣṇa diverted his chariot in time to prevent his bite, and Arjuna killed him.
aśvahrdaya [hrdaya] n. equestrian expertise — f. aśvahrdayā myth. np. of the mare Aśvahrdayā, reincarnation of the nymph Rambhā cursed by the sage Sthūlaśirā.

aśvāroha [āroha] m. rider. अশ্বক aśvaka [aśvaka] m. small horse, pony bad horse | unknown horse (wild or escaped) | toy horse | sparrow | geo. clan of the kamboja tribe | jade — f. aśvikā small mare. अশ্বৰেথ aśvattha [aśvastha] m. bio. bot. Ficus re ligiosa, sacred fig, pipal ["under which horses take shelter"]; syn. pippala, bodhitaru | fire stick [araṇi], made from its wood — f. aśvatthā full moon [pūrṇimā] of the month āśvina; also called kumārapūrņimā; cf. kojāgara || pali assattha.
aśvatthopanayana [upanayana] n. soc. investiture ceremony of a sacred pipal.

aśvatthāman [aśvasthāman] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the hero Aśvatthāmā "Strong as a horse", son of Drona and Kṛpī; he learned the art of arms from his uncle the master Kṛpācārya; during the great war, after Duryodhana was defeated by Bhīma, and inspired by the night attack of crows by an owl, he surprised the camp of the Pāṇḍavās while they slept, destroyed it, and killed Dhṛṣṭadyumna and the Pañcālās; he fought Arjuna with the celestial weapon brahmasiras, whom he could only stop by cursing the descendants of the Pāṇḍavās; For this misuse, Krishna condemned him to wander in desolate places for 3000 years, with a wound on his forehead (his princely jewel torn out) that would not heal; this is one of the 7 im

mortals [ciramjīvin]; cf. Drauni | myth. [Mah.] np. of the elephant killed by Bhīma, and whose death Yudhişthira announced to Drona, at the suggestion of Kṛṣṇa, making him believe that his son had just been killed in order to demoralize him.
aśvalá [aśvala] m. myth. n.p. of Aśvala, reciting priest [hotṛ] of King Janakarāja. সম্বি aśvi iic. aśvin.

aśviyuj |yuj₂| m. du. Aśviyujau myth. np. of Aśviyujau "the two Horsemen"; designates the gods aśvinau and the naksatra of aśvinī. সম্বিন aśvin [aśvain] amnf aśvinī cava lier | math. symb. the number 2 | ved. offering of milk to the aśvinau in the pravargya rite of the agnicayana; fresh milk is poured into the white-hot mahāvīra pot | du. aśvinau myth. ved. np. of the aśvinau "the two Horsemen", also called Nāsatyau or Aśviyujau "twin horses" (later distinguished as Dasra and Nāsatya); They are sons of Saranyū and Vivasvān; they drank the soma during the yajña that Cyavana performed for King Saryāti, against Indra's will; young twin gods of great beauty, they have as their common wife Uṣā the Dawn or their sister Sūryā; they are patrons of medicine, agriculture, and marriage; they help the needy and the sick; they ride horses, or drive a three-wheeled golden chariot drawn by donkeys [rāsabha] or birds, and swift as thought [manojava]; phil. [Sāṃkhya] they are regents [niyantr] of the sense of smell [ghrāṇa] — f. aśvinī astr. np. of the nymph aśvinī, epith. of Saranyū; It resides in the 27th (later 1st) lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corresponding to the stars of the head of Aries; the aśvinau preside there, its symbol is a horse's head. अস্থ্য aśvya [aśvaya] amnf aśvyā composed of horses | relating to the horse, equine.
aṣāḍha [neg. sāḍha] amnf aṣāḍhā Invin target — f. aṣāḍhā véd. first brick [iṣṭakā] of agnicayana | pl. astr. n.p. Aṣāḍhās “target Invin”; cf. Uttarāṣāḍhās, Pūrvāṣāḍhās. স্থ asta iic. astan.
astacatvārimsa [catvārimsa] afmn astacatvārimśī ord. 48ᵉ.
astacatvārimsat [catvārimsat] f. 48; syn. astācatvārimsat.
astatrimsa | trimsa | amnf astatrimsī ord. 38e consisting of 38 parts.
astatrimśat [trimśat] f. 38.
astatrimśattama [tama] afmn astatrimsattamī ord. 38ᵉ.
astatrimśati [trimśati] f. 38.
astadiggaja [diggaja] m. myth. the 8 elephants supporting the cardinal points | hist. the 8 Te lugu poets from the court of Emperor Kṛṣṇadeva Rāya; cf. Bhuvanavijaya.
aṣṭadhā |dhā| adv. in 8 parts.
astadhātu [dhātu] m. the 8 metals: iron, copper, zinc, mercury, lead, tin, silver and gold.
astanavata | navata | amnf astanavatī 98°.
astanavati [navati] f. 98.
astanavatitama [tama] amnf astanavatitamī ord. 98ᵉ.
astapañcāśa [pañcāśa] amnf astapañcāśī 58°.
astapañcāśat [pañcāśat] f. 58.
astapañcāśattama [tama] afmn astapañcāśattamī ord. 58ᵉ.
astapad [pad₂] m. bio. spider | myth. epith. of śarabha "that which has 8 legs" | var. aṣṭapāda id.
aṣṭapada [pada] amnf aṣṭapadā lit. (meter) which has 8 feet.
astapāda |pāda| amnf astapādī lit. (animal) which has 8 feet — m. organic. spider | myth. epith. of the fabulous animal śarabha .

astapraharī [prahara] f. soc. [8×3 = 24] festival of sacred song [saṃkīrtana] and dance lasting 24 h (not. for dolāpūrņimā) | 24 h ceremony of libation of lustral water on the linga of a shrine by a wife to pray for long life for her husband (not. during śivarātri).
astabhuja |bhuja| amnf astabhujā who has 8 arms — f. Aṣṭabhujā myth. np. of Aṣṭabhujā, epith. of Durgā with four arms; she is worshipped not. at Vindhyācala.
astabhairava | Bhairava | m. pl. geo. the eight temples of Bhairava in Varanasi Benares.

astamá [ma] amnf astamī ord. eighth — f. aṣṭamī the 8th day of a lunar half-cycle [pakṣa] | soc. this day is favorable, and occasion for festivals; cf. not. aśokāṣṭamī, gopāṣṭamī, janmāṣṭamī, jyaisthāstamī, bhīsmāstamī, bhairavāstamī.

astamangala | mangala | n. soc. collection of 8 auspicious objects; notably, the Brahmin, the cow, fire, gold, clarified butter, the sun, water, and the king; or the lion, the bull, the elephant, the water pot, the fan, the flag, the drum, and the lamp; in the Jain religion, one must draw the 8 symbols with grains of rice before the icon of a Tirthankara before paying homage; in the Digambara tradition, these symbols are: the parasol | chattra|, the banner | dhvaja|, the water pot | kalaśa|, the fly whisk | cāmara|, the mi

The throne (darpaṇa), the throne (bhadrāsana), and the fan; in the śvetāmbara tradition they are: the swastika , the śrīvatsa, the nandyāvarta, the vardhamānaka lamp, the throne, the water pot, the mirror, and the pair of peas.
sounds | mīnayugala|.

astamatha | matha | m. pl. geo. the 8 monasteries established by Madhva at Udupī; each was headed by a direct disciple of Madhva, and named after his village of origin; they manage the temple dedicated to Kṛṣṇa at Udupī, according to a principle of rotation | paryāya|.
astavasu [vasu] m. myth. the group of 8 Treasures; cf. vasavas.
astavikṛti | vikṛti | f. phon. the 8 modes of recitation of a Vedic verse, using redundancy to avoid errors; cf. jaṭāpāṭha, ghanapāṭha.
astavikṛtilakṣaṇa |lakṣaṇa| n. lit. np. of the Aştavikṛtilakṣaṇa, listing 17 stanzas [kārikā] illustrating the 8 modes of Vedic recitation [vikrti], appendix to the prātiśākhya of the Suklayajurveda.
astavidha [vidha] amnf astavidhā which occurs eight times; of eight kinds; in eight parts.

astavivāha | vivāha | m. soc. The 8 modes of marriage: marriage "in the Brahmā [brāhma] between two people of the same class, with a dowry for the daughter, and following Vedic rites; marriage "in the deva [daiva] where the father gives his daughter in marriage to a priest in payment for his services; marriage "in the ṛṣi [ārṣa] where the dowry is fixed at a lump sum of a cow and a bull; marriage "in the Prajāpati [prājāpatya], without a dowry; marriage of love "in the gandharva [gāndharva] by mutual consent of the spouses (often clandestine); marriage by sale "like an asura [āsura], where the bride is bought; marriage by abduction "in the rākṣasa", where the bride is abducted; and the unworthy marriage "à la piśāca " | paiśāca | by abusing a sleeping, drunk or weak-minded woman.
astavaidya [vaidya] m. med. physician expert in the 8
branches [aṣṭāṅga] of medicine [Ayurveda] of Kerala according to Vāgbhata; cf. Astāngahrdaya, Rasa vaiśesika.
aṣṭaśata [śata] num. n. 108 | 800.
astasasti [sasti] f. 68 | var. astāsasti id.
astasaptata [saptata] amnf astasaptatī ord. 78ᵉ.
astasaptati |saptati | f. 78.f.
astasaptatitama [tama] amn astasaptatitamī ord. 78°.

astasāhasraka [sāhasraka] amnf astasāhasrikā consisting of 8000 (not. towards [śloka]) — f. astasāhasrikā bd. n.p. of the Astasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā in 8000 formulas [sūtra], the oldest in the tradition (1st century BC).

astasiddhi [siddhi] f. phil. [yoga] one of the 8 supernatural powers of a siddha₁ or Shiva: animan the power to shrink, mahiman the power to grow, laghiman the power to become light and to levitate, kāmāvasāyitā the power to extinguish one's passions, prākāmya omnipotence, vašitva the irresistible will, prāpti super-perception, and īśitva divine supremacy. animā laghimā prāptih prākāmyam mahimā tathā |īśitvaṃ ca vaśitvaṃ ca tathā kāmāvasāyitā || (śloka mnemonic).

aṣṭasthāna [sthāna] n. med. [Ayurveda] the 8 methods of examining the patient described by Bhāvamiśra: inspection of the body [rūpa], palpation [sparśa], examination of the pulse [nādī], study of the voice [śabda], examination of the eyes [netra], of the feces [purīṣa], of the urine [mūtra] and of the tongue [jihvā].

astānga [anga₁] amnf astāngā consisting of 8 parts, which has 8 members, in 8 stages — n. med. [Ayurveda] the 8 branches of medicine according to Vāgbhaṭa: kāya (general medicine, digestive system), bala (pediatrics and obstetrics), graha (spirit possession), ūrdhvānga (organs of the head), śalya (surgery), daṃṣṭrā (toxicology, stings and bites), jara (geriatrics), and vṛṣa (iron, aphrodisiacs); cf. astavaidya.
astāngapāta [pāta] m. soc. prostration on the 8 parts of the body (hands, knees, feet, chest and head), posture of deep obedience.
astāngapranāma | pranāma | mr. id.
astāngapranipāta [pranipāta] m. id.

astāngamārga [mārga] m. bd. "eight-step path" leading to the abolition of suffering, according to the teachings of Buddha: right understanding [samyagdṛṣṭi], right intention [samyaksankalpa], right speech [samyagvāc], right conduct [samyakkarmānta], the proper way of life [samyagājīva], the effort
correct [samyagvyāyāma], strong attention
just [samyaksmṛti], and correct meditation [samyaksamādhi]; cf. āryamārga.

astāngayoga [yoga] m. soc. The 8 practices or stages of rājayoga, codified by Patañjali₂: self-control [yama₁], moral discipline [niyama], control of one's body [āsana], breath discipline [prāṇāyāma], withdrawal of the senses [pratyāhāra], fixation of thought [dhāraṇā], meditation [dhyāna] (or qqf. tarka or vīkṣaṇa) and spiritual communion or enstasis [samādhi]. yamaniyamāsanaprānāyāmapratyāhāradhāranādh yānasamādhayo 'ṣṭāvaṅgāni [YS.] The 8 limbs (of yoga) are yama₁, niyama, āsana, prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhāraṇā, dhyāna and samādhi.
aṣṭāṅgasaṃgraha [saṃgraha] m. bed. n.p. from the Aṣṭāṅgasaṃgraha, a prose manual of medicine and surgery [āyurveda] attributed to Vāgbhaṭa.
astāngahṛdaya [hṛdaya] n. lit. np. of the Astāngahrdaya samhitā, corpus of medicine and surgery [āyurveda] of Vāgbhaṭa, comprising 8000 verses [śloka] divided into 120 chapters, composed around 600.
astācatvārimsat [catvārimsat] f. 48; syn. astacatvārimsat.
astādhyāyī [adhyāyī] f. gram. np. of the Astādhyāyī "Octopartite", grammar [śabdānuśāsana] in eight chapters by Pāṇini, composed around 350 ante in Northwest India; it lists 3996 rules
condensed [sūtra] giving precisely the conditions for constructing a correct and meaningful utterance.

aṣṭāvadhāna [avadhāna] n. soc. ["attention to 8 different things"] memorization exercise for a pandita; he must pay attention to 8 sets of simultaneous events while composing a Sanskrit stanza on a given subject. avadhāna session with 8 questioners [prcchaka] — mf aṣṭāvadhānī who knows how to do 8 things at the same time. aștottara [uttara₁] amnf aștottarā more than 8.

astottaraśata [śata] n. 108. astottaraśatanāmāvali litany of 108 names of a deity. স্থাবন áṣṭaka [aṣṭaka] amnf aṣṭikā 8partite — n. category of 8 objects | bed. not. poem in 8 lines; cf. Madhurastaka, Yamunastaka | book in 8 cha

pitres [adhyāya]; not. aṣṭādhyāyī; the Rigveda contains 8 — m. myth. np. of the rājarṣi Aṣṭaka, son of Viśvāmitra and Mādhavī; he performed a great horse race [aśvamedha] to which all the kings were invited; he took to heaven in his flying chariot his three elder brothers Vasumanā, Pratardana and Šibi; meeting in flight the sage Nārada, they invited him on board; Aştaka asked him whom they should give away if only four of them were allowed to ascend to heaven, and Nārada replied Aştaka, for having boasted of the gift of his cows; if only three, it would be Pratardana, for not having given his horse to a brahmin; If only two, it would be Vasumanā, for having glorified himself with his flowery chariot; but if only one were allowed to go to heaven, it would be Sibi, who at the request of a Brahmin killed his only son Brhadgarbha to serve as his meal — f. aṣṭakā 8th day after the full moon | soc. oblation of this day, a pākayajña; an animal is sacrificed to the shades | śrāddha|. স্থা aṣṭan num. pers. [pl. nom. aṣṭau; en comp. aṣṭā] the number eight || gr. oκτω; lat. octo; ang. eight; all. acht; fr. huit.
aṣṭā iic. aṣṭan.
astādasá |dasa| amnf astādasā 18°.
aṣṭādaśan [daśan] num. pers. 18.
astādaśama [daśama] amnf astādaśamī ord. 18th e.
aṣṭānavati [navati] f. 98.
astāpañcāśat [pañcāśat] f. 58.
astāpada [pada] n. chessboard; chess game.

aṣṭāvakra [vakra] m. myth. [AG.] np. of the young mystic aṣṭāvakra "Crippled eight times", son of the brahmin Kahoda; still in his mother's womb, he listened to his father reciting the Veda, and the horn would sound when he made a mistake; his father told him so, and he was born crippled; at the age of 12 he went to the court of Janakarāja to instruct him on the nature of the Self |ātman|; he obtained to find his father, and straightened his body by taking a sacred bath.
astāvakragītā [gītā] f. lit. np. of the Astāvakragītā [AG.], mystical poem of the advaita philosophy, composed by an anonymous master of the school of Sankara₁; it is also called Aştāvakrasamhitā.
aṣṭāvakrasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. bed. n.p. of the Aṣṭāvakrasaṃhitā; cf. aṣṭāvakragītā.
astāvimsa [viṃsa] amnf astāviṃsī twenty-eighth | in 28 parts.
astāvimsati [vimsati] f. 28. aștāśīti [aśīti] f. 88.
aṣṭāśītitama |tama| amnf aṣṭāśītitamī ord. 88ᵉ.
astāsasti |sasti| f. 68.
astāsastitama |tama| amnf astāsastitamī ord. 68ᵉ.
astāsaptati |saptati| f. 78.
aṣṭāsaptatitama |tama| afmn aṣṭāsaptatitamī ord. 78ᵉ.
aṣṭādaśa |aṣṭādaśan| amnf aṣṭādaśī ord. eighteenth.
astādaśākṣara |akṣara| amnf aṣṭādaśākṣarī consisting of 18 syllables.
astādaśākṣaramantra | mantra | n. 18 syllable mantra used not. for the worship of Jagannātha (klīm kṣṇāya govindāya gopījanavallabhāya svāhā).
astādaśādhikaraṇī [adhikaraṇa] f. lit. [KM.] as a set of the 18 subjects constituting poetics. স্থাষ্ট áṣṭi [act. aś₁] f. success | seed, kernel.
aṣṭhīvát m. du. aṣṭhīvantau les genoux.
asthīvaddaghna |daghna| afmn asthīvaddaghnā f. asthīvaddaghnī who has (water) up to her knees.

√ as₁ v. [2] pr. (asti) pft. (āsa) impft. (āsīt) opt. (syāt) imp. (edhi) ppr. (sat) pf. (abhi, āvis) to be, to exist; to be present; to become; to take place, to inhabit | to fall to, to belong to someone. (g.) || Latin est; English is; German ist; French être. asmi I am. asti adv. there is. asti mama I have. ... asti greetings to ...

astu | imp. | so be it! agreed! let it be so. astināsti more or less; perhaps and perhaps not. evam astu so be it; good. evam syāt it might be. āsa it happened that. āsīt once upon a time. as forms abstract nouns, like manas.
asa form of sm or n.
ásaṃyata [neg. saṃyata] amnf asaṃyatā uncontrolled; without restraint | not closed (door).
asaṃyatātman [neg. saṃyatātman] amnf asamyatātmanī who does not control his mind.
asaṃyuta var. asaṃyutta [neg. saṃyuta] amnf asamyutā not joined, separated. asamyuttahastau hands not joined.
asaṃyutahasta [hasta] amnf asaṃyutahastā refers to a symbolic gesture [mudrā] with one hand; opp. samyutahasta.
asaṃśakti [opp. saṃśakti] f. phil. [YV.] indifference to supernatural powers, 5th level of knowledge [jñānabhūmikā].
asaṃśaya [opp. saṃśaya] m. absence of doubt; certainty. asamśayam adv. without any doubt.

asaṃskṛta [neg. saṃskṛta] amnf asaṃskṛtā unprepared, undecorated; unconsecrated; raw | unrefined, coarse (language) — opp. n. bd. [Mahāyāna] the unconditioned, which is joy, permanence and ultimate reality.
asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā [śūnyatā] f. bd. [Mahāyāna] va cuité de l'inconditionné, deuxième étape de la sa gesse.
asamsthita [neg. samsthita] amnf asaṃsthitā unstable, in motion | unfinished, in aaccomplished | upset.
asaṃhata [neg. saṃhata] amnf asaṃhatā isolated, dispersed; disunited, in disagreement.
asamhrādayat [neg. samhrādayat] amnf asamhrādayatī without rattling.
asakala [neg. sakala] amnf asakalā not complete, not integral.
asakṛt [neg. sakṛt] adv. several times; repeatedly; often | math. by an iterative process, by recurrence.
asakṛtsamādhi [samādhi] m. bd. repeated meditation.

asakta [neg. sakta] amnf asaktā unhindered, unhindered | free, independent | phil. detached from the world and passions. asaktam adv. without obstacle; without resistance | selflessly. tasmād asaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara BhG. Thus, selflessly, always accomplish the necessary action.
asakti [asakta] f. detachment | phil. detachment from the world and from passions.
asaktiyoga | yoga | m. phil. | vaiṣṇava | yoga of non-attachment to the phenomenal world.
asaṃkṣipta [neg. saṃkṣipta] amnf asamkṣiptā lit. non-abbreviated, discursive.
asaṃkhya var. asaṅkhya [neg. saṃkhya] amnf asamkhyā innumerable. asamkhyaśas adv. in countless quantities.
asaṃkhyaka |ka| amnf asaṃkhyakā id.
asaṃkhyāta var. asaṅkhyāta |neg. saṃkhyāta] amnf asaṃkhyātā innumerable.
asamkhyeya var. asankhyeya [neg. saṃkhyeya amnf asaṃkhyeyā innumerable — n. multitude; immeasurable number.

Asanga [priv. sanga] amnf asangā detached, free; independent; moving without hindrance | detached from the world, indifferent, liberated — m. absence of attachment | hist. np. of Asanga "liberated", brother of Vasubandhu, 5th century Buddhist philosopher of idealist doctrine [vijñānavāda]; he was a student of Maitreya₃; we owe him notably the Abhidharmasamuccaya, the Mahāyānasamgraha and the Yogācārabhūmi, including the Bodhisattvabhūmi.
asamgata var. asangata [neg. samgata] amnf asaṃgatā non-conforming, unsuitable; unwelcome, out of place | disorderly, confused.
asacchūdra [neg. sacchūdra] amnf asacchūdrā soc. śūdra of bad conduct.
ásat [neg. sat] amnf asatī bad, unjust, wicked; false, non-existent — n. nothingness; evil, lie | phil. the Nothingness; the unreal — f. asatī unfaithful woman; libertine woman.
asatkārya | kārya | n. reprehensible occupation.
asatkāryavāda [vāda] m. phil. pernicious discourse | phil. [Sāṃkhya] doctrine refuting the necessary pre-existence of an effect in its cause; opp. satkāryavāda.

asatkhyāti [khyāti] f. bd. "knowledge of the non-existent", theory of the perception of the unreal, developed by the mādhyamikās in opposition to the theory of error | anyathākhyāti | of Nyāya realism; it allows to accommodate fictions.
asatkhyātivāda [vāda] m. phil. doctrine of the unreality of what is perceived.
asatpralāpa | pralāpa | m. soc. | Nātyaśāstra | incoherent delirium, comic device used during the burlesque interlude |trigata| in the prologue |pūrvaranga| of a play.
asatya [neg. satya] amnf asatyā false, deceitful — n. falsehood; deception.
asatyavādin |vādin| amnf asatyavādī who lies.
asatyasaṃdha [saṃdhā₂] amnf asatyasaṃdhā ["who does not keep his word"] traitor, disloyal.
asán [related to ásrj] n. [sg. nom. acc. asrk] blood.

asaná [act. as₂] n. act of throwing | bio. bot. Pte rocarpus marsupium, kino tree, papilionaceous with yellow flowers; used medicinally, not. its resin; syn. bījaka — agt. mf asanā which serves to throw | ved. missile; arrow.
asaṃtuṣṭa var. asantuṣṭa [neg. saṃtuṣṭa] amnf asaṃtuṣṭā discontented; unsatisfied. asantusto dvijo nastah An unsatisfied Brahmin is lost.
asamdigdha var. asandigdha [neg. samdigdha] amnf asamdigdhā clear; unambiguous; without confusion — n. gram. absence of ambiguity.
asaṃdeha var. asandeha [opp. saṃdeha] m. absence of doubt.
asaṃdheya var. asandheya [opp. saṃdheya] amnf asaṃdheyā with whom one should not make an alliance or apologize.
asamnikṛṣṭa var. asannikṛṣṭa [neg. samnikṛṣṭa] amnf asamnikṛṣṭā not in contact with, away from.
asapatna [priv. sapatna] amnf asapatnā without rival; without opponent — n. condition of peace.
asapiṇḍa [opp. sapiṇḍa] m. soc. distant relative.
asabhya [neg. sabhya] amnf asabhyā improper, rude, vulgar; indecent — n. vulgar language.
asama [neg. sama] amnf asamā unequal.

asamañjasa |neg. samañjasa| amnf asamañjasā inappropriate, unwelcome; incapable — m. good for nothing — n. impropriety, non-conformity; in opportunity — m. asamañjas var. Asamañja myth. np. of Asamañjā or Asamañja "Impicious", son of King Sagara by Keśinī₁; he was perverse, amusing himself by drowning children in the Sarayū, and was disowned by his father; his son Amsumān was just and good.
asamartha [neg. samartha] amnf asa marthā improper; useless; incapable (of (inf. dat. loc.) | gram. (compound word) not forming a syntactic constituent.
asamarthita [opp. samarthita] amnf asamarthitā unforeseen, unexpected; inadequacy.
asamavāyi iic. asamavāyin. asamavāyikāraņa [kāraņa] n. phil. [Nyāya] accidental cause.
asamavāyin [neg. samavāyin] amnf asamavāyinī phil. [Nyāya] not inherent, not in trinsic; contingent, accidental.
asamāpaka |opp. samāpaka| amnf asamāpikā which does not complete; which does not finish. asamāpikākriyā f. gram. verb having the im perfective aspect.
asamāpta [opp. asamāpta] amnf asamāptā incomplete; not finished, unfinished; not accomplished.
asamīcīna [opp. samīcīna] amnf asamīcīnā incorrect, inexact; inappropriate. tad asamīcīnam bhavati it is not good; it is not suitable.
asampatti var. asampatti [opp. sampatti] f. failure; unfortunate.

asamprajñāta var. asamprajñāta | neg. saṃprajñāta] amnf asaṃprajñātā phil. [yoga] qualifies the state where the yogi, by the cessation of thought, has lost consciousness of the world; cf. cittavrttinirodha.
ásamprati var. asamprati [neg. samprati] adv. not in the present circumstances.
asambaddha var. asambaddha [neg. sambaddha] amnf asambaddhā detached, disconnected; dissociated | incoherent.
asambandha var. asambandha [priv. sambandha amnf asambandhā without kinship; without relation.
asambuddhi var. asambuddhi [opp. sambuddhi] f. gram. exclusion of the vocative.

ásaṃbhava var. asambhava [opp. saṃbhava] m. non-occurrence; absence | inapplicability | soc. impropriety | phil. (logic) inconsistency, impossibility. sākṣād bhajan asambhavat that which should not be practiced in public. gor ekaśaphatvam (prototype of improper definition) the cow is an animal with an undivided hoof.
asambhāvya var. asambhāvya [neg. saṃbhāvya] amnf asaṃbhāvyā which cannot occur; impossible.
asaṃbhūti var. asambhūti [opp. saṃbhūti] f. phil. the unmanifest.
asaṃmūḍha var. asammūḍha [neg. sammūdha] amnf asammūdhā who is conscious of what he is doing; deliberate.
asaṃmoha var. asammoha [opp. saṃmoha] m. calm, serenity; wisdom.

asarūpa [neg. sarūpa] amnf asarūpā different, of another form | gram. formally different; said of particular suffixes which block the general rule. vā'sarūpo striyām Pan (3,1, 94): Except when the fixed af indicates the derivation of a feminine form.
asaha |neg. saha₁| amnf asahā impatient; who cannot bear, who cannot endure (iic. g.) incapable of (inf.).
asahatva [tva] n. inability to bear; the act of not tolerating.
asahana [priv. sahana] amnf asahanā impatient; intolerant | who cannot bear (iic.) — n. act of not tolerating.
asahamāna |opp. sahamāna₁| amnf asahamānā not tolerant.
asahāya |priv. sahāya| amnf asahāyā without companion; solitary.
asahāyatā [tā] f. solitude.
asahiṣṇu [neg. asahiṣṇu] amnf impa tient; qui ne supporte (acc. loc. iic.) | arrogant, quarrelleur.
asahiṣṇutā |tā| f. inability to bear; impatience.
asahiṣṇutva |tva| n. id.
asahya [neg. sahya] amnf sahyā insup portable; intolerable | impossible (from (inf.)) | in distress. drastum asahya invisible.
asātmya [neg. sātmya] amnf asātmyā med. non-compliant, inappropriate; unhealthy.
asātmyendriyārthasamyoga [indriyaartha samyoga] m. med. [Ayurveda] appropriate inap association of a meaning and its object (element of diagnosis).
asādhaka [neg. sādhaka] amnf asādhakā ineffective; inconclusive.
asādhana [priv. sādhana] amnf asādhanā without resources — opp. n. non-effective object.

asādhāraṇa [neg. sādhāraṇa] amnf asādhāraṇī alone of its kind, unique; special, particular, specific | rare, extraordinary | phil. | Nyāya | characterizes perception | pratyaksa | specific; there are 3 kinds: sāmānyalakṣaṇa which uses analogy, and recognizes a universal type by its sign, jñānalakṣaṇa which appeals to knowledge, not. to common sense or memory, and yogaja, perception obtained by yoga — n. specific property.
asādhāraṇadharma |dharma| m. phil. the moral duty specific to the individual.
asādhita [neg. sādhita] amnf asādhitā phil. unaccomplished. nāsādhitam karaņam phil. That which is not an accomplished fact cannot be an instrument.
asādhú [neg. sādhu] amnf bad; wicked; false — m. bad man — n. evil; misfortune; fault — interj. (disapproval) misfortune! shame!. asādhúnā unfavorably. sādhvasādhúnī good and evil.
asādhya |neg. sādhya| amnf asādhyā impossible, unrealizable, that which cannot be overcome | med. (disease) incurable.
asāphalya [opp. sāphalya] n. phil. failure; objection.
asāra |opp. sāra| amnf asārā without substance, without vigor, without value; useless, inadequate — m. uselessness.
asāratā [tā] f. weakness; uselessness; inadequacy.
así [obj. as₂] m. sword, gladius | ved. sacrificial knife | lat. ensis. asinā hataḥ killed by the gladius.
asikalaha [kalaha] m. sword fighting.
asidhārā [dhārā₂] f. edge of the sword.

asidhārāvrata [vrata] n. very difficult vow; difficulty of avoiding sin | lit. [Mahānārāyaṇopaniṣad] like crossing a ditch on the blade of a sword | KSS. not. for a brahmacārin, to spend the night in the bed of a beautiful woman without experiencing desire | lit. |Ragh. | Rāma compares it to Bharata's vow to be a just regent of the kingdom in his absence, living chastely with his wealth.
asídhenu [dhenu] f. ["which is to the sword what the calf is to the cow" | dagger.
asipattra [pattra] n. sword blade — m. ["with sharp leaves" | sugar cane.
asiloman [loman] m. myth. n.p. of the asura Asilomā, prime minister of the tyrant Mahişa.
asiṃhāsana [absence siṃhāsana] n. absence of throne.

Asita₁ amnf Asiknī black, dark | myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā Asita₁ "the dark one", son of Bharata₄, father of Sagara | bd. np. of Asita₁, the hermit who recognized the newborn Siddhārtha as the future Buddha; he wept, saddened that he had to die before he could learn his teachings lit. [KSS.] np. of Mount Asita₁, where the hermitage of Kaśyapa is located; Naravāhanadatta went there to visit Gopālaka — f. Asiknī Night | myth. np. of Asiknī "Night", daughter of the asura Pañcajana, wife of Dakşa, and mother of Satī | geo. np. of the Asiknī₁ river "with dark waters", tributary of the Indus (mod. Chenāb); Alexander crossed it with difficulty (Akesines).
asiddha [neg. siddha₁] amnf asiddhā unfulfilled, unfinished, incomplete; imperfect; unproven; powerless | nonexistent | gram. (rule) not applied in the current context.
asiddhakānda [kānda] n. gram. the last three sections of the Aṣṭādhyāyī (from the second section of the eighth book); syn. tripādī.
asiddhatva |tva| n. gram. situation of non-application of a rule in the current context.
asiddhavat [vat] amnf asiddhavatī gram. (rule) whose application in the current context is unknown.
asiddhi [opp. siddhi] f. failure | phil. [logic] statement not established; incompleteness.
asī f. geo. np. of the small river asī near Benares.
asīma [priv. sīman] amnf asīmā without borders | unlimited.
ásu [as₁u] m. vital breath, vital spirit; life, vigor | pl. ásavas vital impulse: animal instinct.
