asutrp [trp₂] amnf who steals or takes advantage of another's life | epicurean, devoted to the joys of the world.
asutṛpa [a] amnf asutṛpā id.
asutyāga [tyāga] m. suicide.
Asuniti | niti | f. phil. conduct of life in the afterlife | myth. the world of spirits; its personification Asuniti "She who guides the spirits".
asukha [opp. sukha] n. grief.
asutṛp² [neg. sutṛp] amnf insatiable.
asunvá [neg. sunva] amnf asunvā ved. ["who does not press (the soma)"] indifferent to the gods, atheist.

ásura [asura] amnf asurī immaterial, supernatural — m. Vedic ["master of the vital breath"] a titanasura, a supernatural being preceding the organization of the cosmos | pl. asurās myth. the ti tans; among them the radiant |āditya|, notably Varuna and Mitra, ranked among the gods; the others became malevolent beings, enemies of the beings of light [sura]; they disputed in vain with the gods | deva | the elixir of immortality | amṛta | during the churning of the primordial ocean of milk | kṣīrodamathana|; their teacher is Uśanā; cf. daitya, dānava, Naraka, Suṣṇa — f. asurī myth. ti tan female | Avestan ahura; lex. asura.
asuradruh [druh₂] m. ["enemy of the antigods"] syn. deva.
asuravivāha | vivāha | m. soc. marriage method by purchasing the bride.
asuryá [asuraya] amnf asuryā im material; divine | relating to the asurās — n. phil. spirituality; divine nature.

asūya [asuya] amnf asūyā [“Who is angry with life”] envious, malicious | irritated by loc. — f. cf. asūyā — v. [11] pr. (asūyáti) v. [11] pr. r. (asūyate) pf. (abhi) to be impatient; to be dissatisfied; to be jealous; to envy (dat.) | to be angry with (acc.); to be irritated by (acc. g.).
asūyā [f. asūya] f. envy, malice; jealousy | impatience; discontent, indignation; the act of detracting. asūyākuṭilam dṛś adv. to look with frowns of indignation.
asūyu [asūyau] amnf id.
asūrya [priv. sūrya] amnf asūryā in the shadow, in the darkness | demonic, impious; evil.
asūryampaśya [neg. sūryampaśya] amnf asūryampaśyā soc. (woman living in the royal ha rem) Who never sees the sun.
ásṛj n. [sg. name. acc. asṛk] blood.
asṛṣṭa [neg. asṛṣṭa] amnf asṛṣṭā not created; not distributed. अ প্ ছার asrstānna [neg. srstānna] amnf asṛṣṭānnā That which does not distribute food.

asau pn. start. mr. sg. name. asau, acc. amum, i. amuṇā, dat. amuṣmai, abl. amuṣmāt, g. amuṣya, loc. amusmin; of. name. acc. amū, i. dat. abl. amūbhyām, g. loc. amuyos; pl. name. friend, acc. amūn, i. amībhis, dat. abl. amībhyas, g. amīṣām, loc. amīṣu ce, ce, That, that, those (in the distance); opp. idam | such; so-and-so — f. [sg. name. asau, acc. amūm, i. amuyā, dat. amusyai, abl. g. amusyās, loc. amuṣyām; of. name. acc. amū, i. dat. abl. amūbhyām, g. loc. amuyos; pl. name. acc. amūs, i. amūbhis, dat. abl. amūbhyas, g. amūṣām, loc. amūṣu] this, that, those — n. cf. adas. asāv amutra ayam asmin This one in this world, This one in this world.

ásta [pp. as₂] amnf astā launched, thrown; rejected, abandoned — n. sunset; disappearance; end, death | homeland, abode — m. mountain of the setting sun — ind. astam at sunset — f. astā arrow; missile. gato'stam arkah the sun is setting.
astaprahara | prahara | m. soc. sunset guard (from 2 p.m. until sunset).
astamauna [mauna] amnf astamaunā having renounced silence.
astavyasta |vyasta| amnf astavyastā pell-mell; in disorder.
astaṃga [agt. astaṃgam] amnf astaṃgā disappeared behind the horizon, set (sun, moon, celestial bodies) | (in fig.) deceased.
astaṃgam [astamgam] v. [1] pr. (astaṃgacchati) to disappear behind the horizon (sun, moon, celestial bodies) | (figuratively) to die. astaṃgatya ka āgataḥ Who has returned after death?

astaṃgamita [pp. ca. astaṃgam] amnf astamgamitā disappeared; destroyed. śāpena astangamitamahimā [Meghadūta] Whose greatness has been destroyed by a curse (example of an internally dependent compound |asamartha|).
astam [acc. asta] adv. at sunset (prefix (vb. movement)).
astamaya [act. astami] m. sunset disappearance.
astamayana |act. astami| n. sunset.
astami [astami] v. [2] pr. (astameti) pp. (astamita) to set (moon, sun).
asti [as₁] ind. then, there is (at the beginning of fables) — f. existence | myth. np. of asti "existence", daughter of Jarāsandha, wife of Kamsa.
astikāya [kāya] m. jn. physical substance [dravya₁] occupying space; we distinguish: the animate [jīva], material objects [pudgala], movement [dharma], rest [adharma] and space [ākāśa].
astitā [tā] f. existence; reality.
astitva [tva] n. existence; reality | phil. ontology.
ástṛ [agt. as₂] amnf astrī [sg. nom. astā, acc. astāram Who throws.
asteya [opp. steya] n. respect for property, absence of theft, honesty | phil. probity, one of the
virtues | yama₁ | of yoga.
astobha [priv. stobha] amnf astobhā without pause | without interjection.
astra [instr. as₂] n. throwing weapon, javelin, projectile; weapon in gen. | art of the archer | myth. mantra projectile.
astradeva | deva | mr. myth. deification of Siva's trident.
asthán n. bone; skeleton; core | var. ásthi id. gr. ooteov; lat. ossis; fr. os.
asthāna |opp. sthāna| n. state of being transient or ephemeral | unsuitable place for (g.) | impossibility. asthāne adv. in the wrong place; at an inopportune time; unsuitable.
asthāvara |neg. sthāvara| amnf asthāvarā who does not stand upright; who does not stand straight; who moves.
ásthi cf. asthan.
asthisaṃghāta [saṃghāta] m. med. articulation.
ásthira [neg. sthira] amnf asthirā in stable; trembling; weak | transient, temporary | uncertain, doubtful | of a changeable character, which cannot be trusted. athirībhū to weaken.
ásthiratva |tva| n. instability; inconstancy.
aspandana [neg. spandana] amnf as pandanā which no longer moves; which no longer throbs.
asparsá [absence sparsa] n. absence of contact (with i.).
asparśana [opp. sparśana] n. act of avoiding contact; not. of impurities and impure people.
aspṛśat [neg. spṛśat] amnf aspṛśatī not touching; without contact.
aspṛśya [neg. spṛśya] amnf aspṛśyā which must not be touched, untouchable; which must not be mentioned.
aspṛṣṭa [neg. spṛṣṭa] amnf aspṛṣṭā which is not touched; not mentioned, to which no allusion has been made.

asmát |abl. pl. aham| ind. of us | var. as mattas id. | var. asmad gram. 1st person pronominal theme. asmado dvayoś ca gram. (The plural of the personal pronoun) asmad (is optionally valid for one) or two (persons).
asmatputra [putra] m. our son | du. asmatputrau our two sons | pl. asmatputrāḥ all our sons.
asmadīya [īya] amnf asmadīyā our, ours.
asmabhyam [dat. pl. aham] ind. for us.
asmāka |asmākam| amnf asmākā véd. OUR.
asmākam [g. pl. aham] ind. to us, from us — am asmāka f. asmākā ved. id.
asmāt |abl. ayam| ind. of this; from here.
asmādṛśa [asmatādṛś] amnf asmādṛśā like us.
asmān [acc. pl. aham] ind. nous.
asmābhis [i. pl. aham] ind. by us.
asmāsu [loc. pl. aham] ind. in us.
asmitā [asmattā] f. self-awareness; feeling of self, egotism | selfishness | phil. [yoga] pure experience of the self.
asmin [loc. ayam] ind. in this. asmin loke adv. in this world, here below.
asmṛti [opp. smṛti] f. inability to remember; forgetfulness.
asmai [dat. ayam] ind. to this.
asya [g. ayam] ind. of this.
asyavāmīya n. lit. hymn [sūkta] of the RV. (beginning with asyá vāmásya); it glorifies Vișnu traversing the Universe "in three strides" to shelter all living beings.
asyām [loc. iyam] ind. in this. asyām rātryām adv. this night.
asyās [abl. iyam] ind. of this — g. id.
asyai [dat. iyam] ind. to this.
asra [related to asrj] n. var. aśra₁ blood | math. angle. asrapa var. aśrapa [pa₁] amnf asrapā blood drinker — m. myth. vampire; cf. rākṣasa — f. as rapā leech | myth. fury; cf. dākinī.
ásvapat [neg. svapat] amnf who does not sleep.
asvapadavigraha [opp. svapadavi graha] m. gram. compound word [samāsa] whose paraphrase cannot be expressed with its sub-components, such as kākapeyā.
asvargya [neg. svargya] amnf asvargyā which does not lead to Heaven.
asvastha [neg. svastha] amnf asvasthā unhealthy, sick; uneasy | dependent; not in control.
asvāsthya [opp. svāsthya] n. indisposition; discomfort; ill health.
asveda [priv. sveda] amnf asvedā without sweat.
asvedana [priv. svedana] amnf asve danā who does not sweat.

√ ah v. pft. (āha) pf. (pra, prati) to speak; to consider as | to say (something (acc.) to someone (dat. acc.) | Latin aio, adagium; French adage. āha (present) he said. āhur it is said that; they say that. tan mahyam āhuḥ they told me this.
áha₁ interj. certainly, of course, exactly; that is to say.
aha₂ ifc. ahan.
áhata |neg. hata| amnf ahatā not struck | new (said of a garment not yet washed).

áhan var. Ahar n. |sg. nom. Ahar; i. ahnā; loc. áhani; loc. ahni; en comp. aha] Day (opp. night |rātri|) | Day, day | myth. np. of Ahar, the Day personified, one of the 8 Treasures |vasu| — n. áha ifc. ved. Day of (2nd century) — m. ahá ifc. Day of (2nd century). adya caturthe'hani in four days from now.

aham pn. pers. 1st person. |sg. name. aham, acc. mām, i. mayā, dat. mahyam, abl. mat, g. mama, loc. mayi, or cl. acc. mā₅, or cl. dat. g. me, or cl. abl. mattas; of. name. acc. āvām, i. dat. abl. āvābhyām, g. loc. āvayos, or cl. acc. dat. g. nau₂; pl. name. vayam, acc. asmān, i. asmābhis, dat. as mabhyam, abl. asmat asmattas, g. asmākam, loc. asmāsu, or cl. acc. dat. g. nas₁ I, Me; us || lat. ego; eng. me, us; fr. Moi, me. aham kr to be aware of one's individuality.
ahaṃvādin [vādin] amnf ahaṃvādinī [“who speaks only of himself” | vain, boastful.

ahamvimarśa | vimarśa | m. self-examination; introspection; understanding of the Self. ahaṃkāra var. ahaṅkāra |kāra| m. the Self, personality, sense of individuality | phil. self-sertion | egoism, self-love; pride | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the Self, essence [tattva] of the ego; [Vedānta] its seat is the heart, where it contains citta; it is a constituent of the inner instrument [antaḥkaraṇa]. ahaṃkṛta var. ahaṅkṛta | kṛta| amnf ahaṃkṛtā proud, self-absorbed; selfish. ahamkṛti var. ahankṛti [kṛti] f. pride, selfishness.
ahámuttará [uttara₁] n. supremacy.
ahamuttaratvá |tva| n. struggle for supremacy.
ahámparāmarśa | parāmarśa | m. phil. | Trika | awareness of the Self.
ahampratyaya | pratyaya | mr. phil. knowledge of the Self. ahambuddhi var. ahambuddhi [buddhi] f. pride, pride. ahámbhāva var. ahambhāva [bhāva] m. feeling of Self.
ahámahamikā [red. aham] f. feeling of superiority; desire to impose oneself. ahamahamikayā praṇāmalālasāḥ mutual competition to be the first to greet.
áhar iic. haha. aharahah adv. from Day to Day.
áhardivám [diva] adv. of days and nights; Day after Day.
áhardi [diva] adv. Day after day.
aharniśa [niśa] n. a day and a night. aharniśam adv. Day and night; constantly.

Ahalyā [neg. halya] f. myth. [Rām.] np. of the very beautiful Ahalyā "the Immaculate," Indian Eve, first woman created by Brahmā, who placed her under the care of Gautama for many years; the latter having shown no lust, Brahmā gave her to him as a wife; she was seduced by Indra who had taken her form; Gautama, catching them together, cursed Indra to lose his testicles, to bear 1000 vaginal marks on his body [Netrayoni], and turned Ahalyā to stone; she had to wait thousands of years for Rāma to come and restore her to life; a symbol of feminine attraction, her fault deprived her of the privilege of beauty; |Rām.| Satānanda is her son.
áhas iic. ahan.
ahoratna | ratna | n. | "jewel of the Day" | the Sun.
ahorātrá [rātra] n. ["a Day and a night"] duration of a day; it is divided into 30 periods [muhūrta] of 48 minutes | myth. (for the gods) a human year. ahorātram night and Day; continuously.
ahasta [priv. hasta] amnf ahasta without hands.
ahaha interj. misfortune! | joy!
ahārya [neg. hārya] amnf ahāryā that cannot be stolen.
ahāryatva [tva] n. inalienability.
áhi m. serpent | myth. dragon; not. Vṛtra, dragon of the sky | lat. anguis; fr. anguille.
áhigopā [gopā] amf having the dragon as guardian.

ahicchattra [chattra] m. geo. np. of the country of Ahic chattra north of the Ganges, northern part of Pañcāla; myth. |Mah.| Drona confiscated it from Drupada to make his son Aśvatthāmā reign there — f. ahic chattrā geo. np. of Ahicchattrā his capital; mod. Rāmnagar, Bareilly district, Uttar Pradesh.
ahitunda | tunda | n. snake's mouth. áhitundika var. āhitundika |ika| m. snake handler.
ahinakula [nakula] n. sg. (collective of sworn enemies) the pair of the snake and the mongoose.
ahinakulikā |ika| f. innate inamictamy between the snake and the mongoose.
ahiripu [ripu] m. ["natural enemy of snakes"] peacock | myth. epith. of Garuda.
ahivat |vat| adv. like a dragon.
áhihata | hata | amnf ahihatā killed by a serpent serpent.
ahihátya [hatya] n. myth. combat (of Indra) with the dragon (Vrtra); slaying of the dragon.
ahiṃsaka [neg. hiṃsaka] amnf ahimsakā non-violent, non-dangerous — m. bd. np. of ahimsaka "non-violent", birth name of the bandit Angulimāla.

ahimsā [opp. hiṃsā] f. non-harm; non-violence, respect for life; non-resistance to evil through violence; absence of ill intent or harm | phil. Benevolence (in deeds, words, and thoughts), one of the virtues [yama₁] of yoga | myth. np. of ahimsā "Benevolence," wife of Dharma, mother of Nara | safety, absence of danger. ahimsā paramo dharmah sarvaprānabhṛtām
smṛtaḥ [Mah.] It is taught that nonviolence is the first duty of all beings.
ahiṃsra [opp. hiṃsra] amnf ahiṃsrā harmless, not dangerous — n. harmless behavior.
ahita [neg. hita₂] amnf ahitā unpleasant, disadvantageous; enemy, harmful — n. damage caused, harm.
áhima [priv. hima] amnf ahimā non cold hot.
ahimakara [kara₁] m. the Sun "with hot rays"; opp. himakara the Moon.
ahimádīdhiti [dīdhiti] m. "in the warm light", epith. of the Sun; opp. himadīdhiti the Moon.
ahimaraśmi [raśmi] m. the Sun "with hot rays"; opp. himaraśmi the Moon.
ahimaruci [ruci] m. the Sun "hot splendor"; opp. himaruci the Moon.
ahis [nom. ahi] iic.
ahirbudhnya [budhnya] m. myth. np. of Ahir budhnya "sea serpent", one of the 11 divine breaths [marut]; astr. he presides over the nakṣatra Uttaraprosthapadās (of Pegasus and Andromeda).
ahirbudhnyasamhitā [samhitā] f. lit. np. of the Ahirbudhnyasaṃhitā, text of pancarātra tantrism; it promotes a warrior cult for princes, centered on the deities Sudarsana and Narasimha.
áhīna₁ [ahanīna] mn soc. sacrifice for several days — amnf ahīnā (after number) of so many (iic.) days.
áhīna₁ [neg. hīna₁] amnf ahīnā whole, complete; undivided, intact; without defect, excellent | not deprived of (abl. i.).
áhṛṇāna [neg. hṛṇāna] amnf ahṛṇānā ved. not being angry.
ahetu [opp. hetu] m. absence of cause or reason | incorrect reasoning | lit. figure of rhetoric.
ahaituka [neg. haituka] amnf ahaitukī without reason, without cause; unmotivated; disinterested | unexpected.
aho interj. oh! ah! (surprise, joking or not) aho bata alas!
Ahobala m. hist. np. of Ahobala, author of the musical treatise Sangītapārijāta (17th century).
ahna [ahan] ifc. mr. day of (iic.). ahnāya dat. adv. quickly. has
ākaṇṭham [ākaṇṭha] adv. up to the throat. ākantham papau he drank his fill.
ākamp [ākamp] pft. r. (ācakampe) pp. (ākampita) to tremble (earth) — ca. r. (ākampayate) to make tremble.
ākampa |act. ākamp| mr. tremor, vibration.
ākampana [act. ākamp] n. act of trembling.
ākampita [pp. That. kamp] amnf ākampitā agitated, shaken.
ākara [act. ākr] m. ["which gives in abundance this"] accumulation, abundance; mine; origin — ifc. "mine of (iic.)", title of works.
ākaraṇa |act. ākṛ| nf ākaraṇā call; summons.

ākarņa [ākarņa] amnf ākarņī who lends an ear, who listens — v. [11] pr. (ākarṇayati) pp. (ākarņita) pfp. (ākarņya) abs. (ākarņya) to hear; to listen, to lend an ear; to strain one's ears. ākarṇam adv. (arrow shot) from the ear. ākarņyatām ayam śabdah listens to this noise.
ākarṇamūlam [mūla] adv. up to the ear.
ākarṣa [act. ākṛṣ] m. attraction, fascination | magnet | dice game | touchstone (for gold).
ākarṣaka₁ [ka] m. dice expert.
ākarṣakrīḍā [krīḍā] f. dice game, one of the 64 arts |kalā|.
ākarṣika |ika| amnf ākarṣikī using a touchstone.
ākarṣaka₂ [agt. ākṛṣ] amnf ākarṣikā attractive, pleasant — f. ākarşikā "Pleasant" (city name).

ākarṣaṇa [act. ākṛṣ] n. attraction, fascination | soc. [Tantra] invocation of an absent person by a mantra; syn. ākṛṣṭi | act of stringing a bow — ifc. act of pulling by (iic.) (not. hair) — f. ākarṣaṇī pole for picking fruit.
ākarṣin [agt. ākṛṣ] amnf ākarṣiṇī that attracts, that snatches away. ākarṣiṇī siddhiḥ the magical power of attraction.
ākal [ākal] pp. (ākalita) abs. (ākalayya) at to stain; tighten | observe; examine; take into consideration | consider; estimate.
ākalana [act. ākal] n. act of tightening | estimation; consideration.
ākalita [pp. ākal] amnf ākalitā seized; bound, attached | examined; assessed; considered.
ākalpa [ākalpa] m. ornament, attire.

ākāṅkṣ [ākāṅkṣ] v. [1] pr. (ākāṅkṣati) pp. (ākānkṣita) to desire, to wish; to aspire to (acc. g.) gram. to require additional actants to have meaning. সাকাব্ল ākāṅkṣa [agt. ākāṅkṣ] amnf ākāṅkṣā gram. which requires additional actants to have meaning — f. cf. ākānkṣā.
ākāṅkṣā [f. ākāṅkṣa] f. desire, wish |gram. semantic dependence; valence; presupposition; [Nyāya] mutual dependencies | utthita | and unidirectional dependencies | utthāpya₁ | are distinguished.
ākānkṣāśānti |śānti| f. satisfaction of a desire.
ākāṅkṣin [agt. ākāṅkṣ] ifc. amnf ākānkṣiṇī who desires, who hopes (iic.).
ākāṅkṣya [pfp. [1] ākāṅkṣ] amnf ākānksyā desirable.
ākāra₁ [agt. ākṛ] m. form, figure, aspect, exterior; appearance; expression | phil. structured form, direct object of perception.
ākāra₂ [(ā)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'ā'.
ākāraka |ka| amnf ākārakā phil. |Nyāya| which has the appearance of (iic. g.).
ākāravat [vat] amnf ākāravatī well formed, well made, of good appearance.
ākārānta [anta] amnf ākārāntā gram. (word) ending with 'ā'.
ākāraṇa |act. ākṛ| n. gathering; ap pel, invocation.
ākāś [ākāś] v. [1] pr. r. (ākāśate) pp. (ākāśita) to look, to recognize.

ākāsa [act. ākās] mn ["visibility"] es space, air, sky — n. phil. Ether or substance of Space, one of the 9 substances [dravya₁] of the Vaiśeṣika, one of the 5 elements | bhūta | of the sāmkhya; it is omnipresent, unique, and eternal; it is imperceptible; its pañcabhūtasthala is Cidambara Națarāja; [TkS.] ether is the support of sound [śabda] | phil. the primordial Impulse (properly the awakening of Manifestation) | math. symb. zero | mod. (communication) wireless, broadcasting; waves, radiation. ākāśe ca hṛdi phil. [Vedānta] in the Space within the heart. śabdaguṇakam ākāśam phil. [TkS.] The specific quality of ether is sound.
ākāśagata [gata] amnf ākāśagatā came from the sky (voice).

ākāśagarbha [garbha] m. bd. [Vajrayāna] np. of the perfected [bodhisattva] Akāśagarbha "Receptacle of Emptiness"; it is invoked to improve one's memory and intellectual capacities, and to obtain manual dexterity.
ākāśacārin [cārin] amnf ākāśacārinī that moves in the air — m. bird; planet.
ākāśaja [ja] amnf ākāśajā from heaven.
ākāśabhāṣita [bhāṣita] n. (theatre) speech addressed to a character offstage.
ākāśamudrā | mudrā | f. hand gesture where the hand is folded by the thumb, the other fingers being extended.
ākāśisantra | yantra | n. flying machine.
ākāśayāna |yāna| n. celestial vehicle.
ākāśavacana |vacana| n. voice descending from the sky (not. in the theatre).
ākāśavat [vat] amnf ākāśavatī spacious | (said of fingers) spread apart.
ākāśavāṇī [vāṇī] f. celestial voice, voice descending from the heavens | phil. inner voice | mod. ["voice of the air" | radio. iyam ākāśavāṇī mod. here is the radio.
ākāśya [ākāśaya] relating to air.
ākīrṇa [pp. ākṝ] amnf ākīrṇā filled with.
ākuñcana [ākuñcana] n. contraction; act of folding (limb) | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] the activity | karman | of contraction.
ākuñcita [ākuñcita] amnf ākuñcitā re folded (arm, leg); contracted, tight (lips); curled (hair).

ākula [obj. ākṝ] amnf ākulā covered, strewn with; filled with, invaded by (i. iic.); full | (figuratively) troubled, agitated; confused, perplexed; disordered, overflowing — v. [11] pr. (ākulayati) pp. (ākulita) to fill with confusion, to trouble. ākulam adv. in confusion, with trouble. ākulīkṛ to create confusion, to engender disorder. iti pratipāditamākulībhavet this position would be compromised.
ākulita [pp. ākula] amnf ākulitā disoriented, bewildered.
ākulī iiv. ākula.
ākulīkṛta [kṛta] amnf ākulīkṛtā filled with confusion. সাকু ākū [ākū] v. [6] pr. r. (ākuvate) to intend.
ākūta |act. ākū| n. intention. sākūtam mām nirvarņyam by giving me an intentional look.
ākr [ākr₁] v. [8] pr. (ākaroti) pp. (ākrta) pf. (apa, ut, upa, nis, vi) to bring near; to call, to invoke — ps. (ākriyate) to take form — ca. (ākārayati) to bring forth, to create.
ākṛta [pp. ākṛ] amnf ākṛtā built (house) | obstruction; rejection.

ākṛti [act. ākṛ] f. form, exterior, aspect; appearance; behavior; structure; configuration | phil. generic trait; characteristic of a species; form common to a class [syn. jāti]; evocative power; opp. vyakti | gram. universal, opp. individual object | dravya₁|. śobhanākṛti beautiful in appearance. subhagākṛti happy in appearance. daśākṛtikṛte kṛṣṇāya tubhyaṃ namaḥ |GG.| Homage to You, Krishna, for having taken the ten forms.

ākṛtigaṇa [gaṇa] amnf ākṛtigaṇā gram. para digmatic, generic — m. gram. class of words, named by a characteristic member, as prsodara gram. (open) class of words having a grammatical specificity designated by a formal particularity; opp. paripūrņagaņa.

ākṛṣ [ākṛṣ] v. [1] pr. (ākarṣati) pp. (ākṛṣṭa) to attract, to draw towards oneself, to bring to oneself; to draw (not. the arrow on the bowstring) | to extract (from (abl.)) to seduce. সাকৃষ্ট ākṛṣṭā [pp. ākṛṣ] amnf ākṛṣṭā drawn (sword), drawn (bow).
ākṛṣṭi [act. ākṛṣ] f. act of pulling, not. on the bowstring | soc. [Tantra] act of attracting an absent person into one's presence by use of a mantra; this mantra.
ākṛ [ākṛ] v. [6] pr. (ākirati) pp. (ākīrṇa) to spread over, to pour; to give in abundance.
ākailāsāt [ākailāsa] adv. to Mount kailāsa.
ākrand |ākrand| v. |1| pr. (ākrandati) pp. (ākrandita) to cry for help; lament.
ākrandá [act. ākrand] m. appeal to the se cours | soc. [Arthaśāstra] king likely to rescue the rear in the circle of neighboring kingdoms [maṇḍala].
ākrandasāra [sāra] m. soc. [Arthaśāstra] king possible support of the rear relief.
ākrandana [act. ākrand] n. lamentations.
ākrandita [pp. ākrand] amnf ākranditā invoked, beseeched — n. lamentation, supplication.

ākram [ākram] v. [1] pr. (ākrāmati) pp. (ākrānta) abs. (ākramya) to approach, go towards, visit | to trample underfoot; to weigh upon (acc.); to seize, attack — ca. (ākrāmayati) to bring in. tāvat rātrih kramate yāvat sūryah nākramate The night continues until the Sun appears.
ākramya [abs. ākram] ind. having attacked.
ākrānta [pp. ākram] amnf ākrāntā visited, frequented; reached; surpassed | attacked, seized, beaten | marked with, oppressed by, prey to; charged with, filled with (i.).
ākrīḍ [ākrīḍ] v. [1] pr. r. (ākrīḍate) to play, to have fun.
ākruś [ākruś] v. [1] pr. (ākrośati) pp. (ākruṣṭa) to call out; to insult, to curse. সাক্সন্থ ākruṣṭā [pp. ākruś] amnf ākruṣṭā insulted.
ākrośa [act. ākruś] m. verbal aggression; insult, abuse.
ākṣadyūtika [*akṣadyūtaika] amnf ākṣadyūtikā (enmity) related to the game of dice.

ākṣiká [*akṣaika] amnf ākṣikā concerning the game; contracted to the game (debt) | one who plays dice; one who wins at the game; one who loses at the game | won at the game | derived from the fruits of bot. Terminalia bellirica — n. winnings at the game.
ākṣikapaṇa |paṇa| m. wager; bet.

ākṣip [ākṣip] v. [6] pr. (ākṣipati) pp. (ākṣipta) pf. (sam) to remove; to pull towards oneself; to draw from, to extirpate from (abl.); to disperse | to indicate, to refer to, to suggest | phil. to project (the duality of the differentiated world) | to mock; to provoke, to defy — ca. (ākṣepayati) to cause to spill; to overturn. madvacanamākṣipya interrupting me.

ākṣipta [pp. ākṣip] amnf ākṣiptā thrown; hurled to the ground; cast back into the sea | caught, seized; captivated, charmed, transported (by not. beauty) | refused, refuted | phil. posed as an objection | scorned; insulted; challenged to date | gram. implicit; opp. abhihita.

ākṣepa [act. ākṣip] m. removal, snatching | offense, blame; objection | refutation gram. suggestion | hand gesture, used by Vedic reciters to denote the svarita accent. mama tu ākṣepaḥ nāsti I have no objection to it. ākṣepeṣu samādhānam lit. (rhet.) response to objections, scholastic debate technique. padacchedah padārthoktir vigraho vākyayojanā āksepesu samādhānam vyākhyānam pañcalakṣaṇam | [Parāśarapurāṇa] The 5 linguistic information (provided by a commentary) are segmentation, lexical semantics, morphological analysis, structural sentence analysis, and rhetoric.
ākṣepasamādhāna [samādhāna] n. [rhetoric] response to objections.
ākṣepaka [agt. ākṣip] amnf ākṣepikā which indicates, which suggests.
ākṣepaṇa [act. ākṣip] n. objection.
ākṣepin [agt. ākṣip] amnf ākṣepiṇī ifc. which applies to, which concerns; which suggests (iic.). ākṣepiṇī siddhiḥ the magical power of attraction.
ākhaṇḍala [ākhaṇḍala] m. myth. [“who tears to pieces”] epith. of Indra the destroyer.
ākhará |ākhara| m. den, lair, gymnasium; wrestling arena | soc. order of military ascetics.
ākhú [ākhan] mf ["that digs a burrow"] mouse, rat; mole. ākhūtthaḥ proliferation of rats.
ākhudaṃśita [daṃśita] amnf ākhudaṃśitā bitten by a rat.
ākheṭa [ākheṭa] m. hunting.
ākhetaka [ka] m. id.

ākhyā₁ ₁ [ ākhyā ] v. [2] pr. ( ākhyāti ) pp. (ākhyāta) pfp. (ākhyātavya) pf. (anu, prati, vi) to say, to tell; to announce; to call (2 acc.) — ps. (ākhyāyate) to call oneself, to name oneself — ca. (ākhyāpayati) pp. (ākyāpita) to make known. ākhyāpayat amnf ākhyāpayatī by making his presence known. ācakhyau he said.

ākhyā₁ [agt. ākhyā₁] f. noun | account, total; syn. saṃkhyā₂ | appearance, aspect — ifc. of noun (iic.) — mn ākhya ifc. id.; ex. prasangākhya (vice) of noun addiction — i. ākhyayā adv. named. ākarsikākhyā (the city) called Plaisance. umākhyā sā jagāma she was called Umā.
sūta | ākhyāhi kathāsāram | | O bard! Tell us the essence of the story.

ākhyāta [pp. ākhyā₁] amnf ākhyātā said, narrated, announced; utterance | called — n. gram. |Yāska| conjugated verbal form; opp. dhātu (root). catvāri padajātāni nāmākhyāte copasarga nipātaśca gram. [Nirukta] There are 4 ways to generate words: Nominal forms, Verbal forms, Preverbs, and Particles.
ākhyātacandrikā [candrikā] f. gram. n.p. from the Akhyātacandrikā, “Light on Verba Les Forms”, lexicon of verbs [kriyākośa] by Bhattamalla (1997); it is arranged in a thesaurus.
ākhyātavāda [vāda] m. lit. np. of the Akhyātavāda, a work on the meaning of verbal suffixes by Raghunātha₁ Siromani.
ākhyātaśabda | śabda | m. gram. enunciation.
ākhyātārtha | artha | m. gram. meaning of the forms of bales verbs.
ākhyātavya [pfp. [3] ākhyā₁ ₁] amnf ākhyātavyā to say; to declare; to announce, to reveal.
ākhyāti [act. ākhyā₁] f. narrative, report; statement.
ākhyāna | act. | ākhyā₁ | n. tale, story; com communication, exposition | lit. story composed of a mixture of prose and verse — v. [11] pr. (ākhyānayati) com to communicate.
ākhyānaka [ka] n. short story — f. ākhyānakī phon. meter combining the indravajrā and upendra vajrā meters.
ākhyāpita [pp. That. ākhyā₁] amnf ākhyāpitā made famous.
ākhyāyikā [ākhyā₁ika] f. tale, story, narrative | lit. not. genre of dynastic prose poem; cf. Harşacarita — m. ākhyāyika ifc. history of (iic.).
ākhyeya [pfp. [1] ākhyā₁] amnf ākhyeyā to say; to declare; to announce; to reveal, to confess — n. verbal message.
āgacchat [ppr. āgam] amnf āgacchantī coming.
āgaṇḍa [āgaṇḍa] iic. [āgaṇḍam] up to the cheeks.
āgata |pp. āgam| amnf āgatā occurred, arrived | lit. (text) transmitted — n. action of arriving, of occurring; advent, production | event, thing that happened or that occurred; accident.
āgati [act. āgam] f. arrival; advent | origin, creation.
āgantavya [pfp. [1] āgam] amnf āgantavyā where one must go. nagaram āgantavyam one must come to the city.
āgantu [āgamtu] m. arrival; newcomer, guest.
āgantuka [ka] amnf āgantukā accidental, for tuit; dditionnel; nouveauvenu.

āgam [āgam] v. [1] pr. (āgacchati) pp. (āgata) pf. (abhi, upa, prati, sam) to arrive at or into; to come from (abl.) | to go towards; to occur, to happen | to have recourse to; to fall into, to incur. ihāgamyatām come here! paramparayā āgam be transmitted (not. by tradition). āgantavyam bhoḥ come see us. āgacchāmi bhoḥ I will come to see you soon.

āgama [agt. āgam] amnf āgamā that which comes to the shore, that which approaches; that which approaches — act. m. arrival, approach; acquisition | means, access; origin, tradition, knowledge; authority | soc. religious text; revealed literature, not. śaiva of South India or jaina gram. juxtaposition, affixation; opp. ādeśa gram. augment, accretion (by prefix of the pri vative particle 'a/an₁'); modification of a theme in general — n. [śaivāgama] lit. [“that which comes from Śiva”] Shaivite tantra in the form of a dialogue where Shiva answers questions from Shakti; traditionally 28 are counted; opp. nigama | [pañcarātrāgama] lit. Vaishnavite Samhita | bd. collection of the Law | jn. Jain canonical collection. varṣāgame adv. at the approach of the monsoon; the monsoon having come.

āgamadambara [dambara] m. lit. np. of the Agamadambara "Much fuss about religion", satirical play by Jayanta₁ Bhatta, showing the hypocrisy of religious sects and their political influence under King Sankaravarmā.
āgamaprāmānya [prāmānya] n. lit. np. of the Agamaprāmānya, ritual work due to Ya munācārya.
āgamaśāstra [śāstra] n. lit. np. of the Agamaśāstra "Collection of doctrines", phil. work of Gaudapāda; Sankara₁ made the commentary on it.
āgāmika [ika] amnf āgāmikā concerning the future.
āgamana |act. āgam| n. approach, arrival; return. punar āgamanam return.
āgas n. ved. transgression; sin, fault, of fense, evil; punishment.
āgaskṛta [kṛta] amnf āgaskṛtā malevolent.

āgāmin [agt. āgam] amnf āgāminī that comes, that arrives; to come; future | what will happen (tomorrow) | phil. part of the karma to come. āgāminisomavāsare next Monday. sa kathayatyāgāminamapyartham he even predicts what happens in the future.
āgāra [*agāra] n. dwelling, habitation, but sound.
āgāradāha [dāha] m. fire in a dwelling.
āgāradāhin [in] m. incendiary.
āgnika [*agnika] amnf āgnikā ved. concerning the preparation of the sacrificial fire.
āgnimārutá [*agnimarut] amnf āgnimārutā myth. concerning agni and the maru tas — m. myth. patr. of Agastya — n. ved. litany addressed to Fire and Winds.
āgnivāruņá [*agniVaruṇa] amnf āgnivārunā myth. concerning agni and Varuna.
āgniveśyá [*agniveśaya] amnf āgniveśyā relating to agniveśa | refers to a śaiva Brahmin community of the Avadaiyar Ko vil region in Tamil Nadu.
āgniveśyagrhasūtra [grhasūtra] n. lit. np. of the Agniveśyagrhasūtra, text of domestic rites used by the āgnivesya community.
āgniṣṭomika [*Agniṣṭomaika] amnf āgnistomikī soc. who studies the Agnistoma.

āgnīdhra [*agnidhṛ] m. Vedic priest holding the sacred Fire; he is one of the 3 priests who assist the chief priest [brahman] in the Vedic sacrifice | myth. np. of King Agnīdhra "who maintains the Altar", son of Priyavrata; he had 9 sons of the nymph Pūrvacitti, including Kuru₁; [BhP.] his son Nābhi, through his veneration of Visnu, obtained that the latter incarnate as his son Rṣabha, the supreme devotee.

āgneyá [*agnieya] amnf āgneyī flammable | igneous; hot and dry; of ardent character (opp. saumya) | combustible, flammable | astr. describes the half of the year beginning with the month māgha myth. relating to agni or the Sacred Fire | in the SouthEast myth. cf. āgneyāstra — m. myth. epith. of Skanda — n. bed. n.p. of the Agneya purāṇa ; cf. Agnipurāṇa.
āgneyapurāna [purāna] n. bed. n.p. from the Agneyapurāṇa; cf. Vahnipurāṇa.

āgneyāstra [astra] n. myth. np. of the magical weapon Agneya "agni missile"; Sagara received it from Aurva; [Mah.] Arjuna received it from Drona, and used it to defend himself against Angāraparņa before teaching him its use.
āgrabhojanika [*agrabhojanaika] amnf āgrabhojanikā qualified to preside over the meal.

āgrayaṇá [*agraayana] m. ved. first libation of soma in the rite of the agnistoma — n. soc. sacrifice of the first fruits, at the end of the rainy season; the first fruits are offered there — f. āgrayaṇī soc. offering [iṣṭi₂] of the first fruits at the end of the monsoon.
āgraha [āgraha] m. insistence, obstinacy;
whim | seizure, taking | favor, affection. āgrahāt var. āgrahena obstinately.

āgrahāyaṇī [*agrahāyaṇa] f. astr. np. of Agrahāyanī "Best of the year", epith. of the full moon [pūrnimā] of the month mārgaśīrṣa; soc. a pākayajña is practiced there and the birthday | jayantī| of Dattātreya is celebrated | astr. epith. of the lunar constellation [nakṣatra] Mṛgaśiras.
āghāta |act. āhan| m. blow, murder, destruction | pain, bruise | [āghātasthāna] in execution law, slaughterhouse.
āghātasthāna [sthāna] n. place of execution, slaughterhouse.
āghārá [act. āghr] m. ved. sprinkling of butter on the sacrificial fire.
āghṛ [āghṛ] v. [3] pr. (ājigharti) pp. (āghṛta) pf. (vi) ved. sprinkle (not. the sacrificial fire with butter).
āghṛṇi [āghṛni] amnf that shines, that radiates; bright, radiant.
āghra [agt. āghrā] amnf āghrā who smells.
āghrā [āghrā] v. [3] pr. (ājighrati) pp. (āghrāta) pf. (upa) to feel; sniff.
āghrāṇa [act. āghrā] n. the act of smelling (an odor, a perfume).
āghrāta |pp. āghrā| amnf āghrātā felt (smell).
āṅgavidya [*aṅgavidyā] amnf āngavidyā soc. who knows or studies palmistry cie. সাত্নিক āṅgika [*aṅga₁ika] amnf āṅgikā (sens timent) expressed by the movement of the body or gestures.
āngikābhinaya | abhinaya | m. soc. use of body movements by an actor or dancer.
āṅgirasá var. āṅgīrasá [*aṅgirasa] amnf āngirasī myth. descendant of Angirā; cf. angirasas — m. myth. not. epith. by Brhaspati | astr. the planet Jupiter.
āṅgīrasá [related to āṅgirasa] amnf āngīrasī myth. descendant of Angirā — m. astr. np. of Angīrasa, personifying year 6 of a samvatsara life cycle|.
ācakṣ [ācakṣ] v. [2] pr. r. (ācaṣṭe) pf. (prati, vi, sam) to tell, to announce, to say; to speak to someone. (dat. acc.); to call, to name.
ācandra [ācandra] iic. as long as the moon exists in Heaven.
ācandratārakam | tāraka| adv. as long as there is the moon and the stars. ācandram adv. as long as there is the moon.
ācandrārkam | arka | adv. | "as long as the moon and the Sun last" in perpetuity (on a stele with inscriptions mentioning a gift).
ācandrārkakṣiti |kṣiti₁| adv. valid in perpetuity (as long as there is the Moon, the Sun and the Earth).
ācandrārkatārakālīna | tārakālīna | amnf ācandrārkatārakālīnā perpetual ["as long as there is the Moon, the Sun and the stars".
ācam [ācam] v. [1] pr. (ācāmati) pfp. (ācamanīya) to drink | soc. to rinse one's mouth to purify oneself.
ācamata |imp. ācam| ind. Rinse yourself!

ācamana |act. ācam| n. soc. rite of purification of the mouth by drinking water poured into the hollow of the right hand, not. in a temple — f. ācamanī soc. id. | soc. ritual spoon used to pour this water.
ācamanīya [pfp. [2] ācam] amnf ācamanīyā to purify — n. soc. water to purify the mouth — m. soc. container of water used for rinsing.
ācaya |ācaya| m. collection, aggregate; accumulation, multitude. ācīrņa) pf. (sam, ut) to travel; to conduct oneself, to behave; to practice, to begin to; to accomplish.
ācáraṇa [act. ācar] n. approach, arrival (not. dawn) | implementation, celebration, practice | conduct, behavior.
ācaraṇīya [pfp. [2] ācar] amnf ācaranīyā which must be accomplished.
ācarita [pp. ācar] amnf ācaritā tra versed, frequented | practiced, observed | gram. prescribed by a grammar rule — n. approach, arrival conduct, behavior.
ācaritatva [tva] n. custom, usage.
ācarya [pfp. [1] ācar] amnf ācaryā which must be approached | which must be practiced.

ācāra [act. ācar] m. behavior, conduct, practice; approach | custom, rule, rite; common law, usage, tradition | phil. good conduct; conduct as a criterion of moral judgment; opp. vicāra, anācāra — agt. amnf ācārā ifc. whose conduct is of a (i.e., 20th-century) nature. ācārataḥ adv. by virtue of his behavior. sādhvācāraḥ mf sādhvācārā who behaves well. kalyāṇācāra amn who behaves well. nācāram pālayati lakṣmīḥ K. Fortune does not protect tradition. ācāraḥ paramo dharma ācāraḥ paramaṃ tapaḥ | ācāraḥ paramaṃ jñānamācārāt kiṃ na sādhyate Good conduct is the greatest duty, it is the first discipline, it is the supreme knowledge; what cannot be accomplished by good conduct? deśācārastāvat ādau vicintyah deśe deśe yā sthitis saiva kāryā [Varāhamihira] First of all, one must observe local tradition; whatever the country, it is the custom that is good to follow.

ācāravat [vat] amnf ācāravatī who behaves well; virtuous — f. ācāravatī lit. [DKC.] np. of Acāravatī "Virtuous", wife of Candaghosa; she died in childbirth, giving birth to Manikarnikā, whom she had promised as a wife to the son of Kāntimatī by losing at dice with the latter.
ācāravarjita | varjita | amnf ācāravarjitā who does not follow custom; irregular | soc. excluded; outside caste.
ācārahīna [hīna] amnf ācāravarjitā who does not follow the conventions | soc. excluded; horscaste.
ācārānga [anga₁] n. jn. monastic discipline, expounded in the Acārāngasūtra, first chapter |anga₁| of the jaina canon.

ācārya [pfp. [1] ca. ācar] amnf ācāryā who regulates behavior — m. soc. master, spiritual preceptor; professor ["who regulates conduct"]; not. teacher of the Veda; he invests the student with the sacred cord [yajñopavīta] | master craftsman. ityācāryāḥ lit. ["thus says the tradition"] generic mention to present received ideas before giving the author's thesis (as for example iti kautilyah). upanīya tu yaḥ śiṣyaṃ vedam adhyāpayed dvijaḥ sakalpam sarahasyam ca tam ācāryam pracakṣate | [Manu] A Brahmin who initiates a student and teaches him the Veda with the ritual and esoteric texts is called a Master.
ācāryaka [ka] n. quality of master; function of professor.
ācāryadeśīya | deśīya | mr. soc. assistant professor.
ācāryādiparīkṣā [ādiparīkṣā] f. soc. qualification of the celebrant of the installation of a sacred image.
ācāryānī [ācāryaānī] f. wife of the tutor.
āci [āci] v. [5] pr. (ācinoti) pr. r. (ācinute) pp. (ācita) to accumulate; to cover with (i.).
ācita [pp. āci] amnf ācitā accumulated, piled up | filled with, covered with (i. iic.).
ācīrṇa [pp. ācar] amnf ācīrṇā practiced, observed (dharma).
ācrt₁ [ācrt] v. [6] pr. (ācrtati) to attach, to fix.
ācchad₁ [āchad₁] v. [10] pr. (ācchadati) pp. (ācchanna) pf. (sat) cover, clothe ca. (ācchādayati) pp. (ācchādita) id. - That. r. (ācchādayate) to dress.
ācchad₁ [agt. ācchad₁] f. cover. সা ভ্যুন ācchanna |pp. ācchad₁| amnf ācchannā dressed.
ācchād [ca. ācchad₁] v. [1] pr. (ācchadayati) pp. (ācchādita) to cover, to clothe — pr. r. (ācchādayate) to dress oneself.
ācchāda |act. ca. ācchad₁| m. clothing.
ācchādaka [agt. ācchad₁] amnf ācchādikā that conceals, that hides.
ācchādakatva [tva] n. dissimulation.
ācchādana [act. ca. ācchad₁] n. dissimu lation, couverture; fait de cacher | vêtements; manteau, cape | dessus de beds | charpente.
ācchādita [pp. ca. ācchad₁] amnf ācchāditā concealed, hidden; covered | clothed.
ācchid [āchid₁] v. [7] pr. (ācchinátti) pr. r. (ācchintté) pp. (ācchinna) to cut off, remove, take, steal | to break.
āja [*aja₁] amnf ājā from the goat.
ājādi [ādi] m. pl. goats, etc.
ājādimāṃsa [māṃsa] n. soc. meat food (forbidden to ascetics).
ājagara [*ājagara] amnf ājagarā concerning the python | lit. chapter of the Mah.
ājan [ājan] v. [4] pr. r. (ājāyate) pp. (ājāta) to be born.
ājanma |ājanman| adv. of birth, from birth.
ājanmabhāṣitr [bhāṣitr] amnf ājanmabhāṣitrī native speaker.
ājanmaśuddha [śuddha] amnf ājanmaśuddhā pure since his birth.
ājarasám [ ājaras ] adv. until old age — dat. ājarasāya id.
ājāti [act. ājan] f. birth.
ājāna [act. ājan] n. birth.
ājānika [ika] amnf ājānikā original, native.
ājāneya [īya] amnf ājāneyī of noble birth — m. thoroughbred horse.
ājānu [ājānu] adv. up to the knees.
ājānubāhu [bāhu] amnf [Rām.] whose arms descend to the knee (said not. of Rāma).
āji₁ [āji] ppr. (ājáyat) to conquer, to vanquish.
āji₁ [act. aj] m. race; competition; combat, battle | racecourse, battlefield | gr. αγων. ājau in the melee.
ājibhūmi [bhūmi] f. battlefield.
ājiśiras [śiras] n. front (army).
ājīv [ājīv] v. [1] pr. (ājīvati) pr. r. (ājīvate) pp. (ājīvita) to live from.
ājīva [act. ājīv] m. means of subsistence; way of life. ājīvam adv. for life.
ājīvāntam [ājīvānta] adv. until death; for all of life.

ājīvika [ājīvaika] m. phil. [“one who follows the rules of life”] member of an unorthodox sect of materialist renunciants founded by Gośāla; their fatalistic doctrine was based on the strict determinism of fate [niyati] — f. ājīvikā sub sistance. সার্ম ājñapta [pp. ca. ājñā₁] amnf ājñaptā commanded, ordained.

ājnapti [act. ca. ājnā₁] f. command, order. সারা ājnā₁ [ājnā₁] v. [9] pr. (ājānāti) to notice, to hear said — ca. (ājñāpayati) to command, or to give. tathā ājñāpayati devah as His Majesty wishes (a servant's response to a royal order). ājñāpayatvāryah at your service, Sir. সারা ājnā₂ [act. ājnā₁] f. order, command | Authority | cf. ājñācakra.

ājñācakra [cakra] n. phil. 6th cakra of tantric yoga, located between the two eyebrows [bhrūmadhya]; it is represented by a white lotus of 2 petals; a white triangle there symbolizes the mind, and bears the bījamantra 'om'; this cakra controls the mind; it is the psychic center of the Authority of Truth.
ājñārtha [artha] m. gram. imperative mood.
ājya [act. āñj] n. soc. melted butter (for libation), chrism; syn. ghṛta.
ājyaśeṣa [śeṣa] mn soc. residue of melted butter.
ājyahoma [homa] m. soc. oblation of melted butter.
ājyāhutí [āhuti] f. soc. oblation of melted butter; syn. ājyahoma.
ānc [āanc] v. [1] pr. (ācati) pp. (ākta) to bend.
ānj [āanj] v. [7] pr. (ānakti) pp. (ākta) anoint — pr. r. (ānkte) anoint oneself with (acc.).
āñjana [*añjana] n. ointment || lat. unguen; fr. ointment.
āñjanābhyañjana [abhyañjana] n. sg. (collective) balms and creams.
āñjaneya [*Añjanāīya] m. myth. n.p. of Āñjaneya, matr. of Hanumān “son of Añjanā”.
āñjasa |*añjasa| amnf āñjasā immediate, direct.
āñjasya [*añjasaya] n. directly. āñjasyāt var. āñjasyena immediately, without hesitation.
āṭa |agt. aṭ| ifc. amnf āṭā which goes to, which follows (iic.).
āṭaka |agt. aṭ| amnf āṭikā who goes, who travels — m. sparrow.
āṭu m. arch. floor, not. of the roof of a temple.
ātopa m. pl. ātopās swelling, redundancy; pride, self-sufficiency.
āḍambara [āḍambara] m. drum | tumult, uproar; noisy behavior; em phase | trumpeting of elephants; trumpet call for attack — f. ādambarī ifc. im enormity of (iic.); ultimate, sublime; thunderous.

āḍhaka amnf āḍhakī is a qualifier for a volume measure of grain, a quarter; one ādhaka is equal to 4 prastha (approximately 3.5 kg) or 4 puṣkala (256 handfuls); there are 4 in a drona. āḍhakasaktavaḥ is a measure of flour.
āḍḥyá [related to ṛdh] amnf āḍḥyā rich, opu lent; which abounds in (i.) | abundant; copious | math. augmented by (i.). āḍhyaṃkaraṇo mantraḥ magic formula for becoming rich.
āḍhyatama |tama| amnf āḍhyatamā super. richissime.
āḍhyatā [tā] f. opulence.
āḍhyam [acc. āḍhya] iic.
āḍhyáṃkaraṇa [karaṇa] amnf āḍhyaṃkaraṇī that enriches — n. means of enrichment; prosperity. svādhyamkaraņo mantra formula for becoming rich.
āḍhyaṃbhava [bhava] amnf āḍhyaṃbhavā who becomes rich.
āṇava [*aṇu] amnf āṇavā atomic; in finitésimal — n. extreme smallness.

āṇavamala [mala] n. phil. [siddhānta] primary defilement of the soul, which prevents its liberation; its nature is that of ignorance [ajñāna]; it reduces consciousness to a finite limit by obscuring the Self.
āṇavopāya [upāya] m. phil. [Abhinavagupta] "way of the finite being", by which one attains the state of jīvanmukti.
āṇí m. ved. axle pin of a chariot; peg | femur. āṇīmāṇḍavyaḥ Māṇḍavya skewered by the stake.
āt |abl. ayam| conj. on this, then; next; also; moreover. ād id then precisely; it is just at this moment that.
ātaṅka [agt. ātañc] m. illness; fever; apprehension, fear — f. ātankā ifc. id. sātanka frightened, terrified.
āta ildenc [ā extta ildenc] v. [7] pr. (ātanakti) to coagulate; precipitate (liquid).
ātata |pp. ātan| amnf ātatā extended, stretched; taut, pulled (bow, rope).
ātatāyin [āyin] amnf ātatāyinī who has drawn his bow — m. ["ready to kill"] assassin; criminal.

ātan [ātan₁] v. [5] pr. (ātanoti) pr. r. (ātanuté) pp. (ātata) to extend, stretch; to cover, illuminate | lat. extendere; fr. étend. padam ātan to extend oneself, improve one's position. suratam ātan to make love.
ātana |act. ātan| n. extension; expansion, manifestation | visual field; panorama.
ātap [ātap] v. [1] pr. (ātapati) pr. r. (ātapate) pp. (ātapita) to set ablaze.
ātapá |agt. ātap| m. heat of the sun.
ātapatra [tra] n. ["which protects from heat"] pa rasol.
ātapalanghana | langhana | n. sunburn; sunstroke. ātapalanghanāt as a result of sunburn; because of sunstroke.
ātāna [obj. ātan] m. extension, stretching; taut rope.
ātitheya [*atithieya] amnf ātitheyā hospitalier — n. hospitality.
ātithyá [*atithiya] amnf ātithyā hos pitalier — n. hospitality.
ātiśayika [*atiśayaika] amnf ātiśayikā superabundant | extraordinary.
ātud |ātud₁| ppr. (ātudat) to strike, push, shake.
ātura amnf āturā who suffers; sick — m. patient — ifc. afflicted by, who suffers from (iic.) | desirous of (inf.).
āturasannyāsin | sannyāsin | f. āturasannyāsin ī soc. renunciant pronouncing his vows on his deathbed.
ātṛṇṇa [pp. ātṛd] amnf ātṛṇṇā pierced.
ātṛd [ātṛd] v. [7] pr. (ātṛṇatti) pp. (ātṛṇṇa) to divide; to pierce — inf. (ātṛdas) action of piercing. [1
ātrp | ātrp₁ | v. |4| pr. (ātrpyati) pp. (ātrpta) to be satisfied; to take pleasure in (gi); to become joyful.
ātṛpya [pfp. [1] ātṛp] m. organic. ["succulent"] bot. Annona squamosa, custard apple tree — n. organic. its fruit, the custard apple, edible; syn. sītāphala.
ātṛ [ātṛ] v. [1] pr. (ātarati) pp. (ātīrṇa) to tame.
ātodya [pfp. [1] ātud] amnf ātodyā to strike — n. musical instrument (not. dance drum).
ātta |contr. ādatta| amnf āttā taken, removed; received.
ātma iic. ātman.
ātmakathā [kathā₁] f. autobiography. ātmakāraņa [kāraņa] n. personal reason; private matter.
ātmakhyāti [khyāti] f. phil. knowledge of a modality of knowledge.
ātmagata | gata | amnf ātmagatā absorbed in his reflections. ātmagatam (theatre) aside; opp. prakāśam. ātmaguņa [guṇa] n. phil. spiritual attribute.

ātmaguptā [gupta] f. bio. bot. Mucuna pruriens, velvet bean; this climbing legume has clusters of purple flowers, and the pods of its fruits are covered with stinging hairs; it is used as fodder; it is an aphrodisiac, and contains a precursor of dopamine; it is used in medicine, against snake bites, and to relieve Parkinson's disease [kampavāta]; syn. kapikacchu. ātmacchandānucāriņī [chandaanucārin] f. woman of loose morals ["who follows her own desire"].
ātmaja [ja] amnf ātmajā self-born — m. (his own) son — f. ātmajā (his own) daughter.
ātmajña [jña] amnf ātmajñā who knows himself; sage | phil. [Vedānta] who knows the Spirit.
ātmatattva [tattva] n. phil. true nature of the Spirit.
ātmatattvaviveka [viveka] m. lit. np. of the Atmatattvaviveka "Investigation into the true nature of the Mind", work of Udayana₁; also called Bauddhādhikāra "Condemnation of Buddhists".
ātmatattvavivekadīdhiti [dīdhiti] f. bed. n.p. of the Atmatattvavivekadīdhiti, its commentary by Raghunātha₁ Śiromaṇi.
ātmatuṣṭi | tuṣṭi | f. phil. | "that which pleases Oneself" | that which is good, moral or beautiful in conscience.
ātmatva [vat] n. essence, nature.
ātmadāna [dāna] n. phil. gift of Self.
ātmadṛṣṭi [dṛṣṭi] f. phil. profound knowledge of the essence of beings and things; opp. carmadrsti phil. belief in the reality of the Self bd. false vision of the Self.
ātmapakṣa [pakṣa] m. his own party.
ātmaparīkṣā [parīkṣā] f. phil. bd. critique of the self; not. refutation of the personalist viewpoint |pudgalavāda|.
ātmapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. of the Atmapurāṇa, work of Samkarānanda; it gives a versified form of the main esoteric lessons [upaniṣad]; it is also called Upanisadratna.
ātmapradakṣiṇa | pradakṣiṇa | mn the act of turning on oneself.
ātmapradakṣiṇanamaskāra [namaskāra] m. soc. rite of worship by turning on Oneself.
ātmaprabha | prabhā₂ | amnf ātmaprabhā which has its own splendor.
ātmaprasāda [prasāda] m. phil. divine grace of the Self; serenity of the soul.
ātmabandhu [bandhu] m. cousin.
ātmabodha [bodha] m. lit. np. of the Atmabodha "knowledge of the Soul", non-dualistic [advaita] text attributed to Shankara₁.
ātmabhava [bhava] m. spontaneous generation.
ātmabheda [bheda] m. essential difference.
ātmamāṃsa [māṃsa] n. his own flesh.
ātmavát [vat] amnf ātmavatī who has a soul | thoughtful, reserved; prudent — adv. by oneself, as oneself.
ātmavadha [vadha] m. suicide.
ātmavíd | vid₃ | amnf phil. who knows the nature of the Self. tarati śokam ātmavit [ChU.] He who knows the Self overcomes sorrow.
ātmaviśrānti [viśrānti] f. phil. rest in the Self.
ātmaveditā [veditā] f. knowledge of one's true nature.
ātmaśakti [śakti] f. his own power.
ātmaśonita [śonita] n. his own blood.
ātmasaṃskṛti [saṃskṛti] f. perfection of the Self.
ātmasaṃdeha | saṃdeha | m. personal danger, risk to Self.
ātmasamarpaṇa [samarpaṇa] n. phil. abandonment of the Self, surrender of the Self (to God). [2
ātmasampad | sampad₂ | f. personal success | personal excellence; inherent virtue.
ātmasākṣātkāra [sākṣātkāra] m. phil. direct experience of the supreme spirit; syn. ātmībhāva.
ātmasiddhi | siddhi | f. phil. Self-realization.
ātmasiddhiśāstra |śāstra| n. phil. science of Self-realization.
atmahatyā |hatyā| f. suicide.
ātmahita [hita₂] n. his own well-being.
ātmārpaṇa | arpaṇa | n. phil. submission of Self (to the Lord).
ātmārpaṇastuti [stuti] f. lit. of np. The Atmārpaṇastuti, a mystical poem in 50 stanzas by Appayya Dīkṣita, written under the influence of the
datura [mohana]; it is also called Unmat tapañcāsat.
ātmāśraya [āśraya] m. phil. self-dependence; circular definition.
ātmecchā [icchā] f. personal preference.
ātmopaniṣad | upaniṣad | f. bed. of np. Atmopanisad.
ātmaupamya | aupamya | n. comparison to oneself; the act of putting oneself in someone else's place.

ātmaka |ātmaka| amnf ātmikā which ap partent to, which forms the nature of (g.) — ifc. which is of the nature or character of (iic.) | which consists of; composed of (iic.). ekaśabdātmikā māyā One is the symbol of illusion.
ātmakatva |tva| n. quality of being of the nature of (iic.).

ātman [related to an₂] pn. pers. r. [sg. nom. ātmā; acc. ātmānam; en comp. ātma] one, oneself, Self (in the 3rd person) — m. breath | principle of life; soul; mind, intelligence; Self; self | essence, character, nature; particularity; body | phil. [Vedānta] np. of Atmā, "the Self" or universal Soul, immutable essence of Being, microcosmic form of brah man | phil. Vaiśeṣika the Soul, one of the 9 substances [dravya₁] — m. ātma ifc. whose mind is (iic.) || gr. ατμος; all. Odem; fr. soul, atmosphere; pali attā. ātmānam hanti he strikes himself. ātmānam ādarśe paśyati he looks at himself in the mirror. ātmīkṛ to appropriate, to take possession of. ātmībhāvah phil. assimilation to the supreme spirit. ātmā tattvamasi śvetaketo [ChU.] You are that Atmā itself, Ö Śvetaketu.
ātmanā [i. ātman] adv. by Oneself — iic. (with nth ordinal) being Oneself (the nth).
ātmanādvitīya [dvitīya] amnf ātmanādvitīyā being the second.
ātmasāt [sāt] ind. appropriating (with kṛ₁, bhū₁). ātmasāt kṛ to appropriate, to seize | phil. to identify with the supreme spirit. agnīn ātmasāt kṛtvā |YjSm.| Having identified with the fires.
ātmastuti |stuti| f. ved. personification of a god (by the poet/reciter).

ātmastha |stha| amnf ātmasthā phil. that which resides in Self | aesthetic | situated in the Self; said of acts of theatre or poetry evoking the feeling of the Self in the spectator, such as pleasure; qualifies the comic as humor and self-deprecation; opp. parastha. pañca vā ete'gnaya ātmasthāḥ | ātmanyeva juhoti | [Baudhāyana] These five fires reside in the Self (of the sannyāsin); it is in the Self that it makes oblation.
ātmane [dat. ātman] iic.
ātmanepada [pada] n. gram. ["word for Self"] reflexive voice (middle): the action is for its own benefit; opp. parasmaipada.
ātmanepadin [in] amnf ātmanepadinī gram. (said of a verb) conjugated in ātmanepada.
ātmanya [ātmanya] amnf ātmanyā personal.
ātmaṃbhari [ātmanbhari] m. [“who only cares about Himself”] selfish.
ātmaṃbharitva [tva] n. selfishness.
ātmīya [ātmaīya] amnf ātmīyā to Self, in one's own right.
ātyantika [*atyantaika] amnf ātyantikī continual, uninterrupted; perpetual, infinite, without end | total, absolute (qualifies not. the destruction of worlds).
ātyayika [*atyayaika] amnf atyāyikā urgent, admitting no delay | requiring urgent care.

ātreyá [*atrieya] m. descendant of atri | myth. n.p. of the sage Atreya, disciple of Bharadvāja who taught him the science of medicine [Ayurveda]; he had 6 disciples, including Agnivesa. Ātreyaśikṣā var. ātreyaśīkṣā [śikṣā] f. bed. n.p. from the Atreyaśikṣā, a text from the Kṛṣṇayajurveda dealing with
phonetics [śikṣā] and Vedic recitation techniques.
ātharvaṇa [*atharvana] amnf ātharvaṇā which concerns Atharvā or the atharvāṇas — m. descendant of Atharvā | soc. priest whose ritual belongs to the Atharvaveda. [3
ātharvaṇika [*atharvanika] amnf ātharvanikā soc. concerning the Atharvaveda — m. soc. priest instructed in the Atharvaveda.
āda [agt. ādā] ifc. amnf ādā who takes (iic.); who receives (iic.).
ādaghna |ādaghna| amnf ādaghnā f. ādaghnī who has (water) up to her mouth.
ādadāna |ppr. mo. ādā| amnf ādadānā who receives.
ādayas ifc. ādi.
ādara [act. ādr] m. consideration, respect, attention, care; affection | taking into account loc. . ādareņa var. ādarat adr. respectfully; with care, with regard. snehādareņa adr. amicably.
ādaraṇīya [pfp. [2] ādr] amnf ādaranīyā that must be respected, respectable; venerable.
ādarśa [act. ādṛś] m. act of perception by sight | mirror | perfection, ideal — ifc. commentary on, look at, manual of (iic. name of works).
ādáhana |ādahana| n. crematorium field.

ādā [ādā₁] v. [3] pr. r. (ādatte) pp. (ātta) abs. (ādāya₁) pf. (upa, vi) to take, remove (from (dat.); to take with oneself, carry off; to steal; to take back | to accept; to receive (from (loc. i. abl.)) — des. (āditsati) to wish to take. sa lokasya mana ādade he had a hold on people's minds.
ādāna [act. ādā] n. taking, removal; receiving, accepting a gift.
ādāya₁ |agt. ādā| ifc. amnf ādāyā who takes, who seizes (iic.).
ādāya₁ [abs. ādā] ind. having taken; having received with.
ādāyacara | cara | amnf ādāyacarī who leaves taking (the loot).

ādi [act. ādā] m. conception; beginning, start; principle | first, Primordial, supreme | first time; first fruits | myth. symb. the number 1 — iic. supreme — amnf ifc. preceded by, beginning with; and so on | gram. (compound word) beginning with "(iic.)" | gram. root belonging to the conjugation class [gaṇa] ca characterized by the root "(iic.)"; cf. bhvādi — m. ādika id. | du. ādyau the first two | pl. ādayas et cætera; the elements beginning with (iic.) | gram. not. denotes a list of the gaṇapāṭha beginning with "(iic.)" — loc. ādau adv. originally; first, at first. ādau adv. at the beginning, first. āditah adv. at the beginning. ādim ādatte he makes a beginning. ādāv eva adv. just before; right now. indrādayaḥ surāḥ the gods beginning with Indra; Indra and the other gods. bhūvādayas pl. gram. the verbal roots (which begin with bhū₁ in the lexicon |dhātupāṭha|).
ādikavi [kavi] m. myth. n.p. of Adikavi, epith. of Vālmīki the “Primordial Poet”.
ādikāvya [kāvya] n. epithet of the Rāmāyaṇa, the "Primordial Poem".
ādināga [nāga] m. myth. np. of Adināga, Primordial serpent, epith. of Sesa, of his incarnation Ca raka, and of Patañjali; he is represented with an anthropomorphic bust and a serpent's body.

Ādinātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of Adinātha₁ "Primordial Master", 1ᵉr mythical tīrthankara; his body is yellow, the bull is his symbol; also ap pelé Rṣabhanātha, he is said to have created the Jain religion | hist. np. of Adinātha₁, first master of the order of nāthayogin; the Khecarīvidyā, a work of hathayoga, is attributed to him.
ādiparvan [parvan] n. lit. np. of the Adiparva, 1st book of the Mah., "of the beginning".
ādipāda [pāda] m. hist. title of pretender to the throne of the princes of Lankā.

ādipurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. of the Adipurāṇa₁ "Primordial tale of olden times", epith. of the Brahma purāna | lit. np. of the Adipurāna₂, recounting the lives of the 23 Jain saints, begun by Jinasena, finished by his disciple Guṇabhadra.
ādibuddha [buddha] m. bd. n.p. of Adibuddha, the Primordial Buddha.
ādimat [mat] amnf ādimatī which has a beginning.
ādimattva [tva] n. state of beginning; said not. of the vowel 'a' in the pranava om.
ādimadhyānta [madhyānta] iic. beginning, middle and end.

ādimadhyāntanāgeśvara [nāgeśvara] m. [Śivarātrimāhātmya] np. of the temple lit. Adimadhyāntanāgeśvara "Lord of the serpents of the beginning, middle and end", where Sukumāra₁ obtained liberation from his sins during the śivarātri .
ādirāja [rāja] m. myth. mythical king, ancient king; not. Manu, Prthu.
ādivākya [vākya] n. lit. introductory exposition of a work.
Ādiśakti [śakti] f. myth. n.p. of Adiśakti, primordial form of the Goddess; cf. Mangalā.
ādiśeṣa [śeṣa] m. myth. n.p. from Adiśeṣa₁ “Primordial Vestige”; cf. Seşa | hist. n.p. of Adiśesa₁, ancient philosopher, original author of the Paramārthasāra.
ādisiddha [siddha₁] amnf ādisiddhā phil. by fact of all eternity (said of consciousness).
ādisṛṣṭi [sṛṣṭi] f. phil. supernatural reality of myth, operating at a different level than natural reality
turelle |sṛṣṭi|.
ādistotra | stotra | n. lit. fundamental hymn.

ādyanta [anta] ifc. amnf ādyantā beginning and ending with (iic.) | gram. ending with (iic.) etc. — m. du. ādyantau the beginning and the end. kalāvādyantayoḥ sthitiḥ In the Kali Yuga only the first and last classes remain (Brahmins and śūdrās).
ādyantavat [vat] amnf ādyantavatī ["which has a beginning and an end"] finished — adv. as if it were the beginning and the end.
ādyavasāna [avasāna] n. du. ādyavasāne the beginning and the end.
ādyudātta | udātta | amnf ādyudāttā gram. which carries the initial accent.
ādigdha [ādigdha] amnf ādigdhā rubbed with ointment; anointed.

ādityá [*Aditiya] m. myth. Vedic. radiant, sovereign god, son of Aditi and Kaśyapa; there are originally 6 radiant [ādityās]: Varuņa, Mitra, Aryamā, Bhaga, Dakṣa and Amśa, to whom were later added Visnu, Tvastā, Pūsā, Vivasvān, Savitā and SakraIndra | myth. np. of Aditya son of Aditi, the Sun personified in 12 radiant aspects or celestial positions; cf. Sūrya, Ravi | math. symb. the number 12 | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the Sun as regent [niyantr] of the sense of sight [cakṣus].

ādityaprabhā [prabhā₂] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī princess Adityaprabhā "Solar Splendor"; she fell in love with the vidyādhara prince Padmasena, and became his first wife, then quarreled with her friend Candravatī who became his second wife; King Muktāsena punished her by sending her to Earth as the rākṣasī Khaḍgadaṃṣṭrā.
ādityavat [vat] adv. like the Sun.

ādityavarna [varna] amnf ādityavarnā of the color of the Sun. vedāham etam purusam mahāntam ādityavarņam tamasah parastāt véd. I know this Supreme Being, of the radiance of the Sun, beyond the darkness.
ādityahṛdaya [hṛdaya] n. lit. np. of the ādityahṛdaya "Heart of the Sun", Vedic hymn taught by Agastya to Rāma before his final battle with Rāvaņa, in chapter 105 of the Yuddhakānda.
ādits [des. ādā] v. pr. (āditsati) pp. (āditsita) to want to take.
āditsā [act. des. ādā] f. intention to take.
āditsu [agt. of the. ādā] amnf willing to take or obtain | eager for gain.
ādin [agt. ad₁] amnf ādinī who eats, who devours.
ādima [comp. ādi] amnf ādimā first; primitive; original.

ādiś [ādiś₁] v. [1] pr. (ādiśati) pp. (ādiṣṭa) pfp. (ādeśya) pf. (anu, prati, sam) to show, to teach, to indicate; to declare, to announce | to prescribe, to command; to make an offer — ca. (ādeśayati) to indicate, to show, to say.
ādiṣṭa [pp. ādiś] amnf ādiṣṭā instructs, informs, advises; enjoins | announces, indicates, prescribes.
ādīp [ādīp] ca. (ādīpayati) to set on fire, to inflame; to illuminate.
ādīpaka [agt. ādīp] amnf ādīpikā which inflames.
ādīpana [act. ādīp] n. act of setting fire.
ādīpya [abs. ādīp] ind. having set fire.
ādīrgha [ādīrgha] amnf ādīrghā elongated, oval.
ādr [ādr₁] ps. (ādriyate) pp. (ādrta) abs. (ādṛtya) to respect, to have regard for, to pay attention to, to take care of.
ādṛta [pp. ādṛ] amnf ādṛṭā attentive; zealous | respected, esteemed.
ādṛṭya [pfp. [1] ādṛ] amnf ādṛṭyā res pectable — abs. ind. respecting; listening to.
ādṛś [ādṛś₁] ps. (ādṛśyate) to be seen, to appear — ca. (ādarśayati) to show, to exhibit.
ādṛṣṭi [act. ādṛś] f. vision; look, glance.
ādeya [pfp. [1] ādā] amnf ādeyā to appropriate, to take; to receive.
ādevana [ādevana] n. place of play; gambling den.

ādeśa [act. ādiś] m. advice, indication, information | prescription, rule; command, order | gram. substitution (not. of one root by another); opp. āgama, sthānin. ādeśalakṣaṇabhāva gram. permitting an operation conditioned by the given.
ādeśaka [ka] m. commander, organizer; guide.
ādeśya [pfp. [1] ādiś] amnf ādeśyā which must be said or prescribed.
ādya₁ |pfp. |1| ad₁| amnf ādyā to eat; edible — n. food. anyasyādyaḥ (farmer) who provides for another.

ādya₂ [ādia] amnf ādyā first, at the head, at the beginning; primitive | preeminent; excellent — ifc. that begins with (iic.); syn. ādi | immediately preceding (iic.) | previous, earlier, elder — f. cf. ādyā. ekādaśādya 10ᵉ [“that precedes the 11ᵉ”].
ādyatva [tva] n. preeminence; seniority.
ādyā [f. ādyá2] f. myth. np. of Adyā, epith. of Durgā "who is in the lead".
ādyākālikāstotra [kālikāstotra] n. bed. n.p. from the Adyākālikāstotra, praise of the 100 names of Kālī.
ādyābīja [bīja] n. phil. [Tantra] the bijamantra 'krīm'.
ādvādaśam |ādvādaśan | adv. up to twelve.
ādham [ādham] v. [1] pr. r. (ādhamate) pp. (ādhmāta) to swell, to fill up; to be full.
ādharmika [*adharmaika] amnf ādharmikī who does not practice the law; unjust, impious; illegal.
ādharṣa [act. ādhṛṣ] m. attack.
ādhā [ādhā₁] v. [3] pr. (ādadhāti) pp. (āhita) pfp. (ādheya) pf. (upa, vi, sam) place on, put, deposit — pr. r. (ādhatté) accept, receive; gar der.
ādhāna |act. ādhā| n. deposit; act of disposing (not. the ritual fire) | taking; receiving; effort appearance soc. consecration of the Vedic fires.

ādhāra [agt. ādhṛ] m. support, base, ground; foundation; receptacle | lit. role (in a drama) gram. [cāndra] locative | phil. [yoga] support for meditation; cf. sodaśādhāra | phil. [NN.] substrate; syn. adhikarana. ādhārādheyabhāva phil. [NN.] relation between an object and its receptacle or support.
ādhāratā [tā] f. phil. [NN.] capacity to serve as support or receptacle; spatiotemporal locality of residence; syn. adhikaraṇatā.
ādhārādheyabhāva [ādheyabhāva] m. phil. [NN.] relation between the support and the supported object.
ādhārādheyabhāvasambandha |sambandha| m. phil. [NN.] link between the support and the supported object (or its absence).
ādhāraṇa [act. ādhṛ] n. phil. [NN.] the act of serving as a support or receptacle.
ādhāraṇatā [tā] f. phil. quality of being a support.
ādh i₁ [act. ādh ā] m. receptacle; deposit; pledge; rental. ādhīkr to pledge.
ādhi₂ [ādhī₂] f. thought; worry; anxiety | reflection, examination of conscience; hope.
ādhikṣāma [kṣāma] amnf ādhikṣāmā [MD.] emaciated by anxiety.
ādhikārika [*adhikāraika] amnf ādhikārikā relating to an authority; official | lit. |theatre| main subject of a play; opp. prāsaigika — m. phil. supreme spirit.
ādhikya [*adhikaa] n. surplus, excess; superiority, preponderance.
ādhitsu [agt. des. ādhā] amnf who desires to receive (not. a son).
ādhidaivika [*adhidaivika] amnf ādhidaivikī phil. concerning or originating from supernatural beings; opp. ādhibhautika.
ādhipatya [*adhipatiya] n. supremacy; sovereignty.
ādhibhautika [*adhibhūtaika] amnf ādhibhautikī phil. derived or product of natural beings or elements; material; opp. ādhidaivika secular.
ādhī₁ [ādhī₁] v. [4] pr. r. (ādhīyate) pp. (ādhīta) to meditate; to be concerned about, to reflect on. pratipātramādhīyatām yatnah one must reflect carefully on each character.
ādhī₁ [obj. ādhī₁] f. thought; worry; anxiety. te kulasyādhayaḥ they are a plague on the family.
ādhunika [*adhunāika] amnf ādhunikā new, new, recent; current; modern. ādhunikakalpita amn fake, of modern manufacture.
ādhū [ādhū₁] v. [5] pr. (ādhunóti) pp. (ādhūta) pf. (vi) shake, agitate.
ādhūta [pp. ādhū] f. ādhūtā shaken, agitated | disturbed; trembling.
ādhṛ [ādhṛ] v. [1] pr. (ādharati) pp. (ādhṛta) to hold, to serve as support; to contain — ca. (ādhārayati) to bring, to procure — ps. (ādhriyate) to be contained, to exist in (loc.).
ādhṛṣ [ādhṛṣ] v. [5] pr. (ādhṛṣṇoti) v. [1] pr. (ādharṣati) pp. (ādhṛṣṭa) pfp. (ādhṛṣya) attack, assault.
ādhṛṣṭi [ādhṛṣṭi] f. assault, attack.
ādhṛṣya [pfp. [1] ādhṛṣ] amnf ādhṛṣyā which can be attacked; approachable.

ādheya [pfp. [1] ādhā] amnf ādheyā to put down, to place; to give, to confer; to attribute, to concede | that which is received or deposited — n. placement | phil. |NN.| attribute, predicate; opp. adhikarana — ifc. instauration of, installation of (iic.).
ādheyatā [tā] f. phil. [NN.] property of being a predicate; opp. adhikaranatā.
ādhmāta |pp. ādham| amnf ādhmātā swollen, inflated. darpādhmāta puffed up with pride.
ādhyakṣika [*adhyakṣaika] amnf ādhyakṣikā phil. qualifies the skeptical doctrines, which only recognize perception as a means of knowledge [pramāṇa].
ādhyakṣya [*adhyakṣaya] n. supervision, superintendence.

ādhyātmika [*adhyātmaika] amnf ādhyātmikī which concerns the self | phil. which concerns the supreme soul; of a spiritual nature; said not. of the spiritual meaning of esoteric hymns — n. mental illness.
ādhyātmikatā [tā] f. spirituality.
ādhyāna [ādhyāna] n. meditation; rumi nations; regrets; nostalgia.
ādhvarika [*adhvaraika] amnf ādhvarikā soc. which concerns the sacrifice of soma — m. book [grantha] explaining the sacrifice adhvara; priest who knows its ritual.
ādhavaryava [*adhvaryu] n. soc. service of the sacrificing priest.
ānaka [ānī] m. large military drum | storm cloud, accompanied by thunder.
ānakadundubhi [dundubhi] m. myth. np. of Anakadundubhi "celestial drum", epith. of Vasu deva, whose birth was greeted by a divine drum roll.
ānaḍuha [*anaḍvah] amnf ānaḍuhā taurin; which relates to the bull.
ānata [pp. ānam] amnf ānatā bent, inclined | submissive, humble, obedient | greeted with reverence.
ānati [act. ānam] f. act of bowing, of inclining | submission; reverence, greeting.
ānana [āan₂ana] n. ["that by which one breathes"] mouth; face.
ānantarya [*anantaraya] n. contiguity, the state of being adjacent or immediate successor, proximity.
ānantya [*anantaya] amnf ānantyā infinite; eternal — n. infinity, infinitude; eternity | immortality | phil. non-enumeration (of a universal).
ānantyadoṣa [doṣa₂] m. phil. [Nyāya] vicious circle, infinite regression.
ānand [ānand] v. [1] pr. (ānandati) to rejoice; to be happy — ca. (ānandayati) to rejoice, to fill with Joy — ca. r. (ānandayate) to enjoy oneself.

ānandá |act. ānand| m. Joy, bliss; pleasure; beatitude, ecstatic joy | phil. [Vedānta] Joy of Divine union | bd. np. of Ananda "Joyful", young "great disciple" of Buddha; after his parinirvāṇa, he became the guardian of the Dharma, thanks to his exceptional memory | astr. np. of Ananda₁ "Joyful", personifying the 48th year of a life cycle [saṃvatsara] — n. [saccidānanda] phil. [Vedānta] Joy in identification with brahmanātman || fr. anandamide.
ānandakanda [kanda] mn lit. np. of the Anandakanda "Bubble of Joy", enormous tantric work of 6900 verses dealing with alchemy and yoga (12th or 13th century).
ānandagiri [giri] m. hist. n.p. of Anandagiri, 13th century philosopher, author of Sankaravijaya.
ānandacinmaya [cinmaya] m. phil. Pure spiritual joy.
ānandatāṇḍava | tāṇḍava | min cf. nadānta.
ānandatīrtha [tīrtha] m. hist. np. of Anandatīrtha, epith. of the master Madhva "who grants access to bliss".
ānandatva |vat| n. nature of Joy.
ānandapala [pala] m. hist. np. of King Anandapala Sāhī; he reigned in Afghanistan at the beginning of the 11th century; Ugrabhūti was his guru.
ānandabodha [bodha] m. hist. np. of the Advaita philosopher Anandabodha (11th or 12th century); his magnum opus is the Nyāyamakaranda.
ānandabhatta [bhatta] m. bed. n.p. of Anandabhatta (16th century); he is the author of the Vallālacarita.
ānandamaya [maya] amnf ānandamayī fact of bliss; spiritual, ecstatic — f. ānandamayī mod. n.p. of the Bengali mystic Mā Anandamayī, born Nirmalā Sundarī Devī (1896–1982).
ānandamayakośa [kośa] m. phil. [Vedānta] the spiritual or ecstatic envelope, forming the causal or original body | kāraṇaśarīra|.
ānandalaharī [laharī] f. bed. n.p. from the Anandalaharī "Flow of bliss", text of praise [stotra] due to Sankara₁, in śikharinī meter. Ι7

ānandavana [vana] n. geo. np. of Anandavana, large stable |gośālā| located in Pathamedā (mod. district of Barmer, Rājasthāna), also called Godhāma mahātīrtha; according to tradition, it was established by Aniruddha.

ānandavardhana [vardhana] amnf ānandavardhanā which increases joy — m. hist. np. of Anandavardhana, court poet of the king of Kaśmīra Avantivarmā (9th century); he composed the treatise on aesthetics Dhvanyāloka, which establishes that suggested meaning [dhvani] is the essence of poetry, and he is thus called Dhvanikāra "Inventor of suggested meaning"; he is also credited with the Sahrdayāloka which theorizes aesthetic emotion, and the collection of devotional poems Devīśataka.
ānandānugata | anugata | amnf ānandānugatā phil. in a state of grace.
ānandin [agt. ānand] amnf ānandinī who rejoices; joyful | rejoicing.
ānam [ānam] v. [1] pr. (ānamati) pp. (ānata) to bow, to incline | to greet, to honor, to pay homage to.
ānama |act. ānam| m. act of bending, of stretching (bow).
ānaya |agt. ānī| m. that brings; that leads to.
ānayana |act. ānī| n. act of bringing, of bringing | production; calculation.

Ānarta [act. ānrt] m. dance hall, dance academy; theatre | myth. np. of King Anarta, son of Saryāti; Revata is his son | geo. np. of the country of Anarta, in Gurjara (north of modern Gujarat); the yādavās ruled there | pl. the ānartās, its inhabitants; its kings — n. the empire of the ānartās | the dance.
ānartapura [pura] n. myth. np. of Anartapura "Capital of Anarta", epith. of Dvāravatī.
ānila [*anila] amnf ānilī produced by the wind; windy — m. myth. epith. of Hanuman (son of the wind).
ānī [ānī₁] v. [1] pr. (ānayati) pp. (ānīta) abs. (ānīya) pf. (ut, upa, sam) bring, bring.
ānī forms the names f. not. of wives. indrāṇī f. myth. wife of Indra.
ānīta [pp. ānī] amnf ānītā brought; brought.
ānīya [abs. ānī] ind. having brought.
ānīla [ānīla] amnf ānīlā bluish; blackish — m. amethyst.
ānuk nota. accrement of the suffix ānī.
ānukūlya [*anukūlaya] amnf ānukūlyā conformity; adequacy | sympathy, friendship. ānukūlyatas adv. in accordance with his/her wishes.
ānunāsikya [*anunāsikaya] amnf ānunāsikya phon. nasality.
ānupūrva [*anupūrva] n. order, series, succession | soc. order of precedence of castes — f. ānupūrvī gram. sequence of phonemes |varna| of an utterance. ānupūrveņa one after the other, in order.
ānupūrvya [ya] n. order, succession | gram. successive order of words in a sentence or compound word. ānupūrvyāt in order. ānupūrvyeṇa one by one; according to order.
ānulomya [*anulomaya] amnf
ānulomyā ["in the direction of the hair"] natural; in accordance with the law — n. natural direction; natural disposition; favorable direction; prosperity | conformity to tradition; regularity.
ānuśātika [*anuśatika] amnf ānuśātikā proper to that which is (bought) with a hundred. সানুষক্ ānuṣák [*anuṣañj] adv. without ceasing, without interruption; one after the other.

ānuṣaṅgika [*anuṣaṅgaika] amnf ānuṣaṅgikā concomitant, inherent; inevitable | secondary, auxiliary | gram. dependent on an el lipse — n. lit. |theatre| subordinate subject of a play; opp. ādhikārika; syn. prāsangika.
ānūpa [*anūpa] amnf ānūpā (terrain) wet, marshy | (animal) aquatic.

ānṛṇya [*anṛṇaya] n. absence of debt; payment of a debt | acquiescence of a debt or sacred duty; fulfillment of a promise owed | gratification of a desire "with joy". svāsubhirbharturānrņyam gatah he paid his master's debt with his life.
ānṛt [ānṛt] v. [4] pr. (ānṛtyati) to dance towards; to jump towards.
ānṛśaṃsa [*anṛśaṃsa] n. goodness, kindness.

ānṛśaṃsya [*anṛśaṃsaya] amnf ānṛśaṃsyā kind, gentle, benevolent — n. absence of cruelty; gentleness, kindness, kindness, compassion. ahiṃsā satyaṃ sarveṣām śaucam anasūyānṛśaṃsyaṃ kṣamā ca [KA.] Towards all, benevolence, sincerity, purity, absence of covetousness, compassion, and indulgence.
āntara [*antara] amnf āntarā interior; internal; inside of; intermediary | native — m. close friend.
āntarikṣa [*antarikṣa] amnf āntarikṣī atmospheric — n. rain.
āntargaṇīka [*antargaṇaīka] amnf āntargaņīkī included in the numbers (class, troop).
āntrá [*antra] n. entrails, guts.
āndola [ādola] m. swinging; fanning | swing — v. [11] pr. (āndolayati) pp. (āndolita) to swing; shake.
āndolana [act. āndola] n. swing | swing; palanquin.
āndhra [*Andhra] amnf āndhrā relating to the Andhra people, Andhra country.
āndhradeśa | deśa | mr. geo. the Andhra country (mod. Andhra pradeśa).
āndhraśabda | śabda | mr. Telugu.
āndhraśabdacintāmaṇi [cintāmaṇi] m. bed. n.p. from Andhrasabdacintāmaṇi, grammar from Telugu to Sanskrit.
ānvīkṣikī [*anvīkṣāika] f. examination, in rational investigation; analytical philosophy. ānvīksikībuddhih argumentative spirit.

√ āp v. [5] pr. (āpnoti) fut. (āpsyati) pft. (āpa₁) aor. [2] (āpat) pp. (āpta) inf. (āptum) pfp. (āptavya, āptya) abs. (āptvā, āpya) pf. (abhi, ava, pari, pra, vi, sam) to attain, obtain; to accomplish; to acquire, to gain; to submit; to achieve, to put (acc.) — ca. (āpayati) to cause to attain, to make — ps. (āpyáte) to be attained; to be obtained — des. ( īpsati ) cf. īps || lat. apiscor; fr. apte. yah pathet sa āpnuyāt He who studies will succeed.
āp₁ nota. gram. suffix marking feminine themes in 'ā'.
āpa₁ [act. āp] m. obtaining — amnf āpā ifc. (iic.) to obtain.
āpa₁ [related to āpas] m. myth. np. of Apa personifying Water, one of the 8 Treasures |vasu|; he presides over the nakṣatra Pūrvāṣāḍhās (δ of Sagittarius).

āpadeva [deva] m. hist. n.p. of Apadeva, Maratha Brahman from the beginning of the 17th century, author of Mīmāmsānyāyaprakāśa, treatise on pūrvamīmāmsā — f. āpadevī lit. n.p. of Apadevī, epith. of Mīmāmsānyāyaprakāśa.
āpaka |agt. āp| amnf āpikā Who obtains.
āpaṇ [āpaṇ] [unused without pf.].
āpaṇa |loc. āpaṇ| m. market; shop; com merce.
āpaṇīya [īya] amnf āpaṇīyā for sale.
āpaṇika [agt. That. āpaṇ] m. merchant.
āpat [āpat₁] v. [1] pr. (āpatati) pp. (āpatita) pf. (sam) to rush upon, to fall upon, to dash towards.
āpatita [pp. āpat] amnf āpatitā on came; arrived suddenly. iti yasya hṛdaye nāpatitam that did not occur to him.
āpatti [act. āpad₁] f. event, occurrence; attainment of a state | distress.

āpad₁ [āpad₁] v. [4] pr. r. (āpadyate) pp. (āpanna) pf. (vi, sam) to reach, to arrive at, to attain; to fall into, to befall — ca. (āpādayati) to bring about. prakṛtimāpad to return to oneself. ksīram dadhibhāvamāpadyate the milk turns into curd. yauvanadaśāmāpede he reached adulthood.
āpad₁ [act. āpad₁] f. misfortune, accident, calamity; distress, adversity, misfortune — loc. pl. cf. āpatsu. āpatsu adv. in adversity.
āpadupeta [upeta] amnf āpadupetā fallen into misfortune; unfortunate.

āpaddharma [dharma] m. soc. law of time of distress | mod. state of emergency — n. [āpaddharmaparvan] lit. section of the Sāntiparva, 12th book of the Mah., dealing with exceptional laws in a state of emergency.
āpana | act. | āp | n. obtaining.

āpanna [pp. āpad₁] amnf āpannā fallen into; afflicted, unfortunate | happened, occurred; obtained, acquired | One who obtained, One who acquired (iic.). tatsthānāpanne taddharmalābhaḥ One who takes someone's place must also take their function (popular maxim [nyāya]).
āpas [nom. pl. ap] ind. the waters.

āpastamba [*apastamba] amnf āpastambā lit. relating to or composed by Apas tamba; not. the apastamba śulbasūtra, which indicates the measurements of the instruments of sacrifice, not. the sacrificial pole [yūpa] — m. hist. np. of apastamba, ancient philosopher (between 600 and 300 BC), author notably of the apastamba dharmasūtra. catvāro varņo brāhmaņakṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrāḥ tesām pūrvah pūrvo janmatah śreyān | [AD.] there are four social classes: brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya and śūdra; each is superior to the one that follows it.
āpastambīya [īya] amnf āpastambīyā relating to apastamba. [9
āpastambīyadharmasūtra | dharmasūtra | n. bed. n.p. from the Apasambīyadharmasūtra, defining the views of an ārya .
āpā [āpā₁] v. [1] pr. (āpibati) pp. (āpīta₁) to drink, to suck, to sip | (figuratively) to be all ears.
āpāta [act. āpat] m. attack, sudden advance, sudden appearance. āpātaramaṇīya good for the moment.
āpāda [act. ca. āpad₁] m. reward; remuneration.
āpādaka |agt. ca. āpad₁| amnf āpādikā that causes, that performs.
āpādana |act. ca. āpad₁| n. act of bringing to a state; production.
āpāná₁ [agt. āp] amnf āpānī who has reached death.
āpāna₂ |act. āpā| n. act of drinking; feast, banquet | inspiration.
āpānaśālā |śālā| f. tavern, drinking establishment; liquor store.
āpí [act. āp] m. ved. friend, ally — agt. amnf āpi ifc. that which arrives at, that which reaches (iic.).
āpiśala [*āpiśalia] amnf concerning Apiśali — m. student of Apiśali.
āpiśali m. hist. np. of Apiśali, Mairian grammarian predecessor of Pāṇini, author of the Apiśaliśikṣā.
āpiśaliśikṣā [śikṣā] f. phon. np. from the Apiśaliśikṣā, treatise on phonetics by Apisali.
āpī [āpī] amnf increased, enlarged; large.
āpīḍ [ āpīḍ ] v. [10] pr. ( āpīḍayati ) pp. (āpīḍita) to press, to crush. bhujābhyām tāmāpīdya while holding her in his arms; while kissing her.
āpīḍa [act. āpīḍ] m. compression; crushing | rosary tied in a crown on the head as an ornament | phon. name of a meter.
āpīta₁ [pp. āpā] amnf āpītā bu, swallowed; sucked. surapatiprārthanāpītasakalasāgarasalilasya |K.| (Agastya) who at the request of Indra swallowed the entire ocean.
āpīta₁ [āpīta₂] amnf āpītā yellowish.
āpūrta [pp. āpr] amnf āpūrtā satisfied — n. act of satisfying; meritorious act.
āpr [āpr₂] pf. (vi) [unused without pf.].
āpṛcchya [pfp. [1] āpraś] amnf āpṛcchyā about which one should inquire.
āpṛta [pp. āpṛ] amnf āpṛtā occupied.
(āpṛṇāti) v. [6] pr. (āpṛṇáti) pp. (āpūrta) to fill, to satisfy — ps. (āpūryate) to be filled, to be satisfied — ca. (āpūrayati) to fill.
āpekṣ [āapekṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (āpekṣate) pp. (āpekṣita) phil. [Nyāya] to be dependent on.

āptá [pp. āp] amnf āptā obtained, at tinted, received | having attained, having obtained; responsible, exact, faithful, reliable; appropriate, plausible, suitable, adequate; competent, fit; trustworthy — m. close, intimate; trusted person, friend | phil. [Nyāya] seer, person endowed with direct perception and who transmits a teaching — n. mathematical equation | lat. ap tus; fr. apt, adapted. rājah kāmamāptah the king obtained the object of his desire.
āptákāma | kāma | amnf āptakāmā who has satis fulfilled his desires, satisfied | phil. who knows the identity of brahman and ātman.
āptadakṣiṇa [dakṣiṇā] amnf āptadakṣiṇā provided with appropriate gifts.
āptaparīkṣā [parīkṣā] f. lit. np. of the Aptaparīkṣā, work of the Jain logician Vidyānanda.
āptavacana [vacana] n. phil. trustworthy word, a legitimate means of knowledge [pramāṇa]; syn. āptopadeśa | gram. linguistic usage attested by a competent speaker.
āptavākya | vākya | n. cf. āptavacana.
āptavāda [vada] m. cf. āptavacana.
āptopadeśa [upadeśa] m. phil. testimony transmitted by a trustworthy speaker, a legitimate means of knowledge [pramāṇa]; syn. āptavacana.
