āpti [act. āp] f. attainment, obtaining; acquisition, gain; abundance, fortune | connection, report, relationship; aptitude, suitability | pl. āptayas soc. the 12 invocations; the 1st is āpaye svāhā.
āptya₁ [pfp. [1] āp] amnf āptyā ved. to obtain, to attain.

āptya₂ |āpas| m. myth. Vedic. spirit of the waters; the āptyās are charged with washing away ritual impurities, and in particular the blood shed during sacrifices; they are associated with the nadir [adhastāt]; opp. sādhyās; cf. Trita | myth. np. of aptya, epith. of Trita "Scapegoat".
āpya₁ |pfp. |1| āp| amnf āpyā ved. to obtain, to attain.
āpya₂ |*apya| amnf āpyā relating to water; aqueous; liquid | made of water | aquatic | pl. myth. class of aquatic deities.
āpyā [āpyā] v. [1] pr. r. (āpyāyate) pp. (āpyāna) to grow, swell, inflate; fatten; strengthen, profit | enlarge, make grow; increase, reinforce; confirm.
āpyāna |pp. āpyā | amnf āpyānā aug menté; grosi; fort; réjoué — n. augmentation; cor pulence.
āpravas [āpravas] v. [1] pr. (āpravasati) pp. (āproṣita) to return (from a journey, from abroad, from exile); to return home.
āpravāsa |act. āpravas| m. return to one's home, to the country; immigration.

āpraś [āpraś] v. [6] pr. r. (āprccháte) pfp. (āprcchya) to take leave, to say goodbye | to greet (vi siteur); to invoke (god) | to ask, to inquire about. āpṛcchasva sahacaram say goodbye to your friend.
āprī₁ [āprī] v. [9] pr. (āprīṇāti) pp. (āprīta) to rejoice, to please, to satisfy.

āprī₁ [āprī₁] f. soc. ved. conciliatory ritual prayer of the vedic sacrifice, invocation of an aspect of Agni | pl. āpryas soc. the invocations or aspects of Agni; their list depends on the schools of ritual; e.g. Vaiśvānara "He who is of all men", epith. of the Sun or of the fire āhavanīya; Tanūnapāt the "Self-begotten"; Narāśaṃsa "Praise of men"; Mātariśvā "(fire of sperm) which swells in the mother"; Susamiddha "Well-inflamed".
āplu [āplu] v. [1] pr. r. (āplávate) pp. (āpluta) pf. (sam) to wet, bathe, flood; to plunge.
ābaddha [pp. ābandh] amnf ābaddhā bound, attached | produced, exhibited — n. bond, attachment ornament — m. affection. tasyāh ābaddhadhāramaśru prāvartata her eyes poured torrents of tears.
ābaddhadṛṣṭi [dṛṣṭi] amnf who has their eyes fixed on.
ābanta |āp₁anta| note. gram. family of the 3 suffixes 'tāp', 'dāp' and 'cāp' marking feminine stems in 'ā'.
ābandh [ābandh] v. [9] pr. (ābadhnāti) pp. (ābaddha) to bind, to attach | to tie together; to combine; to grasp | to concentrate on.
ābila cf. āvila.
ābdika [*abdaika] amnf ābdikā annual — ifc. yearly; which lasts for so many years. ābrahmabhuvanāt

ā brahmabhuvana ind. until the world of Brahmā. সামত ābhada m. hist. np. of Abhada, son of Jain merchants from Anahilapāṭaka; orphaned and ruined at 10 years old, he made his fortune by finding an emerald which he gave to King Jayasimha₄; his golden legend is told in the Jain hagiographic tales |prabandha|.
ābharaṇa [ābhṛ] n. [“that which is worn”] ornament, costume, jewelry.
ābhā₁ [ābhā₁] v. [2] pr. (ābhāti) pp. (ābhāta) to shine, to illuminate | to resemble, to have the appearance of.
ābhā₁ [agt. ābhā₁] f. brightness, beauty, appearance, color — m. ābha ifc. that has the appearance of (iic.).
ābhāṇaka |ābhāṇaka| mr. saying, pro verb.
ābhāta [pp. ābhā₁] amnf ābhātā that shines | visible.
ābhāti [act. ābhā₁] f. splendor, light; shadow.
ābhāṣ [ābhāṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (ābhāṣate) pp. (ābhāṣita) to speak to, converse; call. সামাষ ābhāṣa [obj. ābhāṣ] m. speech; address, com
command | saying, proverb | introduction, preface.
ābhāṣaṇa [act. ābhāṣ] n. act of addressing, conversation with.
ābhāṣita [pp. ābhāṣ] amnf ābhāṣitā to whom one addresses oneself; to whom one has spoken.
ābhās₁ [ābhās₁] v. [1] pr. r. (ābhāsate) pp. (ābhasita) to appear, to resemble; to have the (deceptive) appearance of.
ābhās₁ [agt. ābhās₁] f. splendor.

ābhāsa [agt. ābhās₁] m. splendor; aspect, appearance; emanation, manifestation | phantom; illusion, deceptive appearance; seeming | phil. sophism, paradox | phil. [aesthetics] seeming or pretense of an emotion [bhāvābhāsa] or a mood [rasābhāsa]. turagābhāsa image of a horse in a painting. hāsyābhāsa seeming of humor.
ābhāsatā [tā] f. state of being an illusion.
ābhāsatva [tva] n. state of being an illusion.
ābhāsana [na] n. illumination; illusion.
ābhāsavāda [vāda] m. phil. [śākta] ontological theory of physical reality as an aspect or illusion of absolute Reality.
ābhāsin [agt. ābhās₁] ifc. amnf ābhāsinī which has the appearance of (iic.).
ābhāsvara [ābhās₁vara] amnf ābhāsvarā which shines — m. myth. illusion, class of minor deities, subclass of the gaṇa; there are 64 ābhāsvarās.
ābhidharmika [*Abhidharmaika] amnf ābhidharmikā bd. relating to the scholastic doctrine of Abhidharma.
ābhiprāyika [*abhiprāyaika] amnf ābhiprāyikā phil. intentional; opp. neyartha.
ābhiprāyikavacana [vacana] n. language intention nel.
ābhiṣeka [*abhiṣeka] amnf ābhiṣekā relating to the sacred.
ābhis [i. pl. iyam] ind. by these.
ābhīkṣṇa [*abhīkṣṇa] amnf ābhīkṣṇā repeated; frequent.
ābhīkṣṇya [*abhīkṣṇaya] n. repetition | gram. repetitive action. ābhīkṣṇye ṇamul ca Pan (3,4, 22): we repeat with the absolutive in 'am' (like pāyam pāyam we drink and we drink).

ābhīra m. geo. name of a people of herders, originating from the East of Pañjāb | cowherd, herder | soc. mixed caste, resulting from the marriage of a brāhmaṇa and a woman of ambaṣṭha caste — f. ābhīrī woman of ābhīra caste | language of the ābhīra people.
ābhū₂ [ābhū₁] v. [1] pr. (ābhávati) pf. (pari, prati) to be present; to be near; to attend; to exist; to continue to exist | to be produced by, to come from; to begin to exist.
ābhū₂ [agt. ābhū₂] amnf present; near; who assists, who helps | who approaches; who turns towards (not. divinity) — m. assistant.
ābhṛ [ābhṛ] v. [1] pr. (ābhárati) pp. (ābhṛta) to bring; to approach, to bring; to carry with oneself to produce to fill; to attract the attention of.
ābhṛta [pp. ābhṛ] amnf ābhṛtā brought; brought; procured; produced | filled; full.
ābhogá₁ [ābhoga₁] m. curve, turning, the | circuit, circumference; development, expansion | snake; cobra's hood.

ābhogá₂ [ābhoga₁] amnf ābhogā ifc. one who eats, who enjoys — m. enjoyment, pleasure; completeness, satiety | lit. [advaita] np. from the commentary [vākya] Abhoga of the Kalpataru, due to Lakşmīnṛsimha.
ābhyantara [*abhyantara] amnf ābhyantarā internal, located inside; opp. bāhya.
ābhyantaraprayatna [prayatna] m. phone. intraoral vocal process; opp. bāhyaprayatna.
ābhyas [abl. pl. iyam] ind. of these — dat. to these.
ābhyām [i. du. iyam] ind. by these two — abl. of these two — dat. to these two.
ābhyāśika [*abhyāśaika] amnf ābhyāśikā near, close; near.
ābhyāsika [*abhyāsaika] amnf ābhyāsikā resulting from practice; obtained through study | lit. [KM.] characterizes the industrious poet.
ābhyudayika [*abhyudayaika] amnf ābhyudayikā which brings prosperity — n. soc. śrāddha ceremony performed on the occasion of a happy event.
ām₁ interj. ah! yes!
ām₂ [ca. am] v. [10] pr. (āmayati) to be ill.
ām forms the perfect tense. Ind. to be composed with an auxiliary verb in the perfect tense. āsāmcakre hvayāmāsa ca he sat down and he called.
āmá [agt. That. am] amnf āmā raw [“uncooked”] | green ["unripe"] (opp. pakva) — act. mr. illness | gr. ωμος; lat. amurus.
āmarakta [rakta] m. med. dysentery.
āmavāta | vāta | m. med. intestinal pain, flatulence; constipation.
āmaśūla |śūla| n. med. colic.
āmād |ad₂| amnf who eats raw meat; who eats uncooked food.
āmādya |ya| n. condition of eating raw meat.
āmāśaya [āśaya] m. med. stomach.

i>āmantr [ āmantr ] v. [10] pr. r. (āmantrayate) pp. (āmantrita) to address, greet, speak to; summon | say goodbye to, take leave of. āmantrya ind. having paid his respects to, having greeted | having taken leave of. āmantrayasva sahacaram say goodbye to your friend. āmantrayāmcakre he summoned.
āmantraṇa |act. āmantr| n. address, invitation; welcome, greeting; (formula of) greeting gram. syn. sambodhana.
āmantrita [pp. āmantr] amnf āmantritā addressed, to whom one speaks; from whom one takes leave — n. address; conversation | gram. nominal form in the vocative.
āmandra [āmandra] amnf āmandrā which emits a low, muffled sound (like thunder).
āmaya [āmaya] m. illness | destruction.
āmayitnú [āmayitnu] amnf which makes one sick.
āmaraṇam [āmaraṇa] adv. until death.
āmaranānta [āmaranānta] amnf āmaraṇāntā which lasts until death.
āmarda [act. āmrd] m. crushing.
āmardaka [agt. āmrd] m. myth. epith. of Bhairava "who destroys" | hist. np. of Amardaka, founder of a dualistic śaiva sect (8th century); he founded an eponymous monastery [maṭha] at Ujjayinī.
āmarśa [act. āmṛś] m. contact | proximity.

āmalaka [*amlaka] mf āmalakī bio. bot. Emblica officinalis, myrobalan tree; syn. dhātrī— n. |āmalakaphala| fruit of the myrobalan, Indian gooseberry; its transparency is used as a metaphor for extrasensory vision, notably of the Buddha; med. it is used notably to treat bile |pitta|; cf. triphalā | arch. motif crowning the śikhara of certain temples in North India (in the shape of the āmalaka fruit).
āmāvāsyá [*amāvāsyā] amnf āmāvāsyā relating to the new moon | born under the new moon — n. soc. new moon offering.
āmíkṣā f. ved. curdled milk, cottage cheese.
āmitra [*amitra] amnf āmitrī ved. in friendly; odious | belonging to an enemy.
āmiśra [āmiśra] amnf āmiśrā mixed.
āmiṣa [āmaiṣa] n. meat, flesh; food, prey; desired booty | object of desire; pleasing object; ardent desire, passion. siṃhávyāghrāmiṣīkṛ to be prey for lions and tigers.
āmiṣāśin |āśin| amnf āmiṣāśinī carnivore.
āmis [āma] n. raw flesh; flesh.
āmīkṣā f. mixture of hot milk and curd.
āmukta [pp. āmuc] amnf āmuktā mis (clothing); dressed | removed; undressed | released; thrown, sent — n. cuirass.
āmukha [āmukha] amnf āmukhā before the eyes | at the level of the face — n. beginning; prelude, prologue. āmukham adv. in front, visibly. āmukhīkr to make visible. āmukhībhū to become visible.
āmuc [āmuc₁] v. [6] pr. (āmuñcati) pp. (āmukta) to put on a garment, to dress | to take off a garment, to undress | to let go; to throw.
āmuṣyakulikā [*amuṣyakulika] f. the state of being from such a family.
āmuṣyaputrikā [*amuṣyaputrikā] f. daughter of So-and-so.
āmuṣyāyaṇá [*amuṣyaāyana] amnf āmusyāyanī of such and such descent; son of So-and-so.
āmūlam [āmūla] adv. from the beginning; wholeheartedly; thoroughly, radically ["to the root"] | var. āmūlāt id. āmūlācchrotumicchāmi I want to hear from the beginning.
āmṛd [āmṛd₁] v. [9] pr. (āmṛdnāti) to grind, crush; to destroy by rubbing.
āmṛś [āmṛś] v. [6] pr. (āmṛśati) to touch, feel; to taste; to enjoy (not. of a woman) | to consider, to reflect.
āmóda [āmoda] m. joy; scent.
āmnā [āmnā] v. [1] pr. (āmanati) pp. (āmnāta) pf. (sam) to mention, to cite; to learn.
āmnāta [pp. āmnā] amnf āmnātā trans mis, taught.
āmnāya [pfp. [1] āmnā] m. [“that which must be learned” sacred doctrine; Veda | tradition; traditional teaching; sect.
āmnāyapīṭha [pīṭha] m. religious teaching center; the 4 main ones are pūrvāmnāya in Purī, dakṣiṇāmnāya in Śṛṅgeri, paścimāmnāya in Dvārakā, and uttarāmnāya in Badarīnātha.
āmra m. bio. bot. Mangifera indica, mango tree — n. mango.
āmravaṇa [vana] n. mango wood.
āmred [āmred] ca. (āmredayati) pp. (āmredita) repeat.
āmreda [act. āmred] m. repetition.

āmredita [pp. ca. āmred] amnf āmreditā repeated — n. gram. reduplication; in a reduplicated word (e.g., divedive), qualifies the second occurrence. tasya dviruktasya param āmreditam gram. Pan (8,1, 2): The last (word) of a duplicate is qualified as "repeated".
āmla [*amla] mf āmlā bio. bot. Tamarindus indica, tamarind tree — n. acidity.
āya [act. e] m. arrival; income, gains, profit; opp. vyaya | arch. the gain in the āyādi system.

āyādi [ādi] n. arch. [Mayamata] system of evaluating proportions in the architecture [vāstuśāstra] of Kerala; it comprises several lists of parts [varga] determining favorable proportions by remainders of whole divisions; āya is determined to be gain (favorable) and rṇa or vyaya to be loss (unfavorable); the nine parts [amsa] are taskara the thief, sukha happiness, śakti power, dhana wealth, rāja the king, sandha the eunuch, abhaya recklessness, vyaya adversity and āya success; The eight matrices (yoni or guhya) corresponding to the orientation of the axis of the land or building: dhvaja the standard in the East, dhūma the cloud in the Southeast, siṃha or mrga the lion in the South, śvan₁ the dog in the Southwest, vṛṣa the bull in the West, khara the donkey in the Northwest, gaja/ibha/hastin the elephant in the North and kāka/vāyasa the raven in the Northeast; the 27 asterisms (udu, rkṣa or nakṣatra), the 15 days
lunar [tithi], and the 7 solar days [vāra]; finally āyus or vayas₁ the age.
āyādiṣaḍvarga |ṣaḍvarga| m. arch. the 6 formulas of harmonious proportions of the āyādi system: the
gain [āya], expenditure [vyaya], the nine parts [aṃsa], the eight matrices | yoni|, the 26 asterisms | rkṣa|, the 15 lunar days | tithi|, the 7 solar days | vāra| and age | vayas₁|.
āyaḥśūliká [*ayaḥśūlaika] amnf āyaḥśūlikā who uses violence; assassin.
āyat₁ [ā extyat₁] v. [1] pr. r. (āyatate) pp. (āyatta) to arrive, to reach | to be at the disposal of, to depend on (loc.) — ca. (āyātayati) to cause to arrive, to cause to reach.
āyat₁ [ppr. e] amnf āyatī upon arriving, upon approaching.
āyata |pp. āyam| amnf āyatā stretched, al elongated | extended, long, large | math. oblong.
āyatalocana |locana| amnf āyatalocana who has almond-shaped eyes.

āy atana | act. āy at₁ | n. dwelling, residence, homeland; seat, refuge | soc. sanctuary, temple "dwelling of god"; location of the sacred hearth, altar | phil. site of sensory perception or thought; cf. sadāyatana.
āyatanavat [vat] m. phil. [chu.] the Cognitive or
partition [pāda] of brahman into four cognitions: the vital breath [prāṇa], sight [cakṣus], hearing [śrotra] and the mind | manas|.

āyati [act. āyam] f. extension, lengthening; length | time to come or future | phil. the future | posterity, lineage; son, offspring, descendant hope | myth. np. of Ayati, daughter of Meru and wife of Dhātā like her sister Niyati.
yatta [pp. āyat₁] amnf āyattā dependent; available, ready; prudent. ayamarthastvadāyattah this matter is at your disposal.
āyana₁ [act. e] n. act of approaching, arrival.
āyana₂ [*ayana] amnf āyanā relating to the solstice.
āyana descendant of (patr. form).
āyani descendant of (patr. form).
āyanya [*ayanaya] ifc. m. son of (patr. form).

āyam [ āyam ] v. [1] pr. ( āyacchati ) pp. (āyata) pf. (vi) to extend, lengthen — pr. r. (āyacchate) to restrain, stop (one's action); to control, restrain, master — ca. (āyāmayati) to restrain, restrain.
āyama [act. āyam] m. extension, length, constraint; control, mastery; maintenance. nāyame kāntaḥ niyamaḥ This is not an absolute rule.
āyas [āyas] v. [4] pr. (āyasyati) pp. (āyasta, āyasita) to strive, to tire oneself, to exhaust oneself — ca. (āyāsayati) to tire, to torment.
āyasá [*ayasa] amnf āyasī of iron, made of iron; metallic — n. metal; iron — f. āyasī cuirass (metallic), armor, chainmail.
āyasākṣara [akṣara] n. mod. metallic printing character. āyasākṣarair mudritam printed with metal characters.
āyasita [pp. āyas] amnf āyasitā fa tgué.
āyasta [pp. āyas] amnf āyastā performed with difficulty | who tires; zealous; anxious; tired, weary — n. energy; energetic act.
āyā [āyā₁] v. [2] pr. (āyāti) pp. (āyāta) pf. (sam) to arrive; to come to such a state.
āyāta [pp. āyā] amnf āyātā arrived, come; due — n. abundance; superabundance.
āyāti [act. āyā] f. arrival; occurrence, event.
āyāna [act. āyā] n. arrival; temperament, natural disposition.
āyāma [act. āyam] m. extension; stretching; stretching posture; used by Vedic reciters for the acute accent [udātta] | extent; length.
āyāsa [act. āyas] m. effort, work; fatigue, toil.
āyin [agt. e] ifc. amnf āyinī who hurries towards (iic.).
āyú₁ [*iu] amnf active; living — m. man, humanity; descendant, offspring; lineage, family | phil. vital force | myth. cf. Ayu — n. life, duration of life.
āyu₂ |āyu₁| v. |6| pr. r. (āyuvate) pp. (āyuta) ved. to pull towards oneself; to seize, to take possession of; to stir; to mix.
āyukta |pp. āyuj| amnf āyuktā charged with — m. employee.
āyuktaka [ka] m. person exercising an office, official.
āyuj [ āyuj₁ ₁] v. [7] pr. ( āyunákti ) pr. r. (āyunkté) pp. (āyukta) pf. (sam) to join, attach; to accommodate — ca. (āyojayati) to constitute, form, organize.
āyuta [pp. āyu₂] amnf āyutā melted; mixed — ifc. combined with (iic.) — n. melted butter.
āyudh [āyudh₁] v. [4] pr. (āyudhyati) pr. r. (āyudhyate) pp. (āyuddha) to fight; to attack, to oppose.
āyudha [instr. āyudh] n. weapon — ifc. armed with (iic.).
āyudhajīvin | jīvin | amnf āyudhajīvinī who lives by the profession of arms — m. warrior.
āyudhapuruṣa [puruṣa] m. arch. anthropomorphic representation of a weapon of a god.
āyudhapūjā [pūjā] f. soc. ceremony to bless weapons, performed at vijayadaśamī; mod. one blesses working tools, vehicles, etc.
āyudhavidyā [vidyā] f. soc. science of weapons. gato'si sarvāsvāyudhavidyāsu parām pratisthām You have attained perfect mastery of all weapons.
āyudhāgāra [āgāra] n. armory, arsenal.
āyudhāgāranara [nara] m. governor of a national arsenal.
āyudhika [āyudhaika] amnf āyudhikā concerning weapons | who lives by the trade of arms — m. warrior, soldier — n. arms trafficking.
āyudhīya [āyudhaīya] amnf āyudhīyā who lives by the profession of arms — m. warrior, soldier.
āyur iic. āyus.
āyurda [da] amnf āyurdā which gives life; which gives long life.
āyuryoga [yoga] m. astr. conjunction of planets used in predictive astrology.

āyurveda [veda] m. medicine ["science of vital force"] | lit. Ayurveda, a treatise on traditional medicine, an upaveda, considered as an anexe of the Atharvaveda; it comprises 8 sections [aṣṭānga]: śalya the extraction of foreign bodies (thorns, arrows), śālākya eye and ear surgery, kāyacikitsā body medicine, bhūtavidyā psychiatry or the science of evil spirits, kaumārabhṛtya pediatrics, agadatantra the science of antidotes, rāsāyanatantra the science of elixirs, and vājīkaraņatantra the science of aphrodisiacs; cf. Dhanvantari, Bharadvāja, Atreya, Ca raka, Vāgbhaṭa, Suśruta.
āyuṣ iic. āyus.

āyuṣmat [mat] amnf āyuṣmatī well for so long; endowed with long life; aged, venerable — m. adr. Your Eminence, Venerable | myth. np. of the asura Ayuşmat "Longevity", son of Samhrāda. bho āyuşmān edhi Devadatta (in return to a salut) long life to you, Devadatta (if Devadatta is of good caste [trivarna], one must stress and lengthen his last syllable).
āyuṣya [āyusya] amnf āyuṣyā which gives long life, healthy, vital — n. vital force, Longevity.

āyus [abstr. i] n. age, Longevity, lifespan; life, health; vigor, vitality | the living | age, an āyādi; syn. vayas₁ | phil. youthfulness — m. myth. np. of Ayu "the Vigorous", 3rd king of the lunar lineage, son of Purūravā and Urvaśī, father of Nahuṣa; he went to the East, and his descendants populated the Indo-Gangetic Plain, while his brother Amāvasu remained in the West | gr. αιον; lat. aevum; fr. âge. āyurghṛtanyāya phil. maxim of Longevity and butter, evoking the relationship between cause and effect.
āyuḥṣṭoma |stoma| m. soc. rite to obtain a long life, part of the abhiplava ceremony.
āyoga [act. yuj₁] m. yoke of cattle | accomplishment of an action; performance | docking quay.
āyogava var. ayogava mf āyogavī soc. descendant of a śūdra and a vaiśya woman; char pentier; cf. sairamdhra.
āyodhana [act. āyudh] n. combat; battlefield.
āyodhyika [*Ayodhyāika] amnf āyodhyikā born, residing, or located in Ayodhyā.
ara n. brass; iron | corner; corner — m. cavity — f. ārā punch, peak; probe.
ārāvalī [āvalī] f. geo. ["range of peaks"] np. of the Arāvalī mountain range in Rājasthāna, between Mount Abū [Arbudāranya] and Delhi; its summit is Guruśikhara (1722 m).
ārakta [ārakta] amnf āraktā reddish — n. red sandalwood.

āragvadha m. bio. bot. Cassia fistula, leguminous tree with compound leaves, with pretty bright yellow flowers in hanging clusters, used in medicine, not. as a laxative; syn. aruja, kṛtamāla, jatharanud — n. its fruit, a pod.
āranya [*aranya] amnf āranyā relating to the forest, woodland; wild; opp. grāmya — m. pl. āraņyās wild beasts.

āranyaka |ka| amnf āranyikā of the forest, wild — m. forest dweller, hermit — n. lit. a kind of esoteric Brahmanical texts ["to be read in secret in the solitude of the forest"; cf. Brhadāraņyaka, Taittirīyāranyaka — f. āranyikā lit. np. of Aranyikā, epithet of Princess Priya darśikā "found in the forest". āranyakam parva lit. "the book of the forest", 3rd book of the Mahābhārata.
āranyakabhikṣu [bhikṣu] m. hermit living in the woods.
āranyavāsin | vāsin₁ | amnf āranyavāsinī who lives in the forest.
āranyaharidrā [haridrā] f. organic. bot. curcuma aromatica, wild turmeric; it is used in medicine.
ārata |pp. āram| amnf āratā which has ceased; appeased, tranquil — n. soc. variety of coitus.
ārati [act. āram] f. stop, cessation.
ārabdha [pp. ārabh] amnf ārabdhā en trepris; commencé.
ārabdhavya [pfp. [1] ārabh] amnf ārabdhāvyā which must be undertaken. adhyayana ārabdhavye kimiti krīdasi why are you playing instead of studying?
ārabh [ārabh] v. [1] pr. r. (ārabhate) pp. (ārabdha) pfp. (ārabhya) pf. (pra, sam) to hold firm; to undertake; to begin.
ārabhaṭa [ārabh] m. entrepreneur; courageous man — f. ārabhaṭī fearlessness; heroism | soc. [theatre] style of representation of heroic, violent or supernatural events.
ārabhya [pfp. [1] ārabh] amnf ārabhyā to undertake — abs. ind. having been started | from (abl. acc.).
āram [āram] v. [1] pr. (āramati) pp. (ārata) to stop | to rejoice, to take pleasure; to enjoy.

ārambhá [act. ārabh] m. undertaking; beginning, commencement, origin; haste, effort | lit. [theatre] initial moral state [avasthā₂] of the hero of a drama in the Nāṭyaśāstra, gripped by the urgent desire for a coveted object. ārambhaḥ kadā bhavati when does it begin? kimārambhastvam what are you doing?
ārambhopāya [upāya] m. initialization.
ārambhaka [agt. ārabh] amnf ārambhikā that causes to undertake or begin — ifc. that begins (iic.).
ārámbhaṇa [act. ārabh] n. act of seizing | place of grasping; handle | beginning, between grip, commencement. vācārambhaṇamātra phil. |Vedānta| only ver bal (said of the illusory effect of brahman).
ārambhaṇīya [pfp. [2] ārabh] amnf ārambhaṇīyā which must be undertaken | that with which one must begin.
ārambhin [agt. ārabh] amnf ārambhinī entrepreneur.
ārāt adv. from afar; far from acc. abl. | in the vicinity of; next to.
ārātrika [ārātrika] n. soc. ceremony of saluting a deity by rotating a flame of
camphor | karpūra |, not. at dusk | | hi. āratī.
ārādh [ārādh] ca. (ārādhayati) pp. (ārādhita) pfp. (ārādhya, ārādhanīya) pf. (sam) to satisfy, win, appease; to solicit; to honor, venerate | to deserve.

ārādhana |agt. ārādh| amnf ārādhanī who makes himself favorable — act. n. homage, service; the act of winning someone to one's cause |soc. adoration (idol) | implementation; obtaining — f. cf. ārādhanā.

ārādhanā [f. ārādhana] f. jn. tradition jn. of fulfillment of religious duties, not. of the choice of the end of life; doctrinal text dealing with the end of life and modes of suicide; cf. Mūlārādhanā | soc. homage to a deceased person.
ārādhanākathā [kathā₁] f. lit. edifying story on the approach of death in the jn tradition.
ārādhanākathākośa [kośa] m. jn. collection of such stories; cf. Brhatkathākośa.
ārādhanīya [pfp. [2] ārādh] amnf ārādhanīyā whose favor must be won; whom must be honored.
ārādhita [pp. ca. ārādh] amnf ārādhitā reconciled; solicited; honored, revered accomplished, performed.
ārādhya [pfp. [1] ca. ārādh] amnf ārādhyā whose favor one must or can gain | to honor; to accomplish.
ārāmá [act. āram] m. pleasure, delight; rest, pleasant place, place of rest; garden.
ārāmakṣetra [kṣetra] n. holy place of rest; garden temple; cf. Dakṣārāma. সাংক āruka n. organic. bot. Prunus domestica, plum; the plum tree is grown at altitude, in the Mountains
Blues [Nīlagiri₁] and in the Himalayas.
āruj [āruj₁] v. [1] pr. (ārujati) to break, demolish; to interrupt.
āruṇa |*aruṇa| amnf āruṇī concerning Aruna.
āruṇaketuka | ketuka | m. ved. np. of the Arunaketuka fire altar; its construction is specified in the Taittirīyāraņyaka.

āruṇi [*aruṇi] m. phil. [ChU.] patr. of Uddālaka Aruņi, son of Aruņi. Āruņeya [eya] m. bed. n.p. of the Āruņeya upaniṣad phil. [BU.] np. of Aruṇeya, patr. of Svetaketu, son of Uddālaka Aruni. সাহহয় ārurukṣu [agt. of the. āruh] amnf who desires to rise.
ārúṣī f. myth. np. of Aruṣī "Furie", daughter of Manu, wife of Cyavana; persecuted by the kṣatriyās, she took refuge pregnant in a cave, where she gave birth to Aurva through the thigh.

āruh [āruh₁] v. [1] pr. (ārohati) pp. (ārūḍha) abs. (āruhya) pf. (adhi, upa, sam) to climb, to ascend (acc.); to climb, to rise up, to place oneself on, to ascend (acc.) — ca. (ārohayati) var. āropayati to raise, to erect; to raise up (acc.); to cause to grow; to place (in a high position) — ca. r. (ārohayate) to be mounted by | to attach (not. a string to a bow) — des. (ārurukṣati) to desire to rise. vṛkṣam āruh to climb a tree. bhava khatvārūḍhaḥ ["Climb on the bed"] va dor mir. yauvanapadavīm ārūḍhaḥ he reached his majority. āruha mama śroṇīṃ neṣyāmi tvāṃ vihāyasā |Mah.| Climb on my hip, I will carry you through the air (ogress).
āruhya |abs. āruh| ind. having overcome, having attained.
ārūḍha [pp. āruh] amnf ārūḍhā who has mounted, who has climbed on; who has succeeded | reached, has caladed — ifc. having as a mount (iic.).
ārogya [*arogaya] n. good health.

ārop [ca. āruh] v. [10] pr. (āropayati) pp. (āropita) to raise, erect; to mount (acc.); to cause to grow; to place (in a high position) | to attach (not. a string to a bow). idam vrttam lekhyam āropaya put this matter in writing.
āropa [act. ca. āruh] m. imposition; charge, allocation; act of placing high | gram. on
imposition [upacāra] of a figure [lakṣaṇā]; is distinct from absorption [adhyavasāna].
āropana [act. ca. āruh] n. act of raising my ter on (not. the funeral pyre) | action of raising, erecting | action of equipping a bow with its string.
āropita [pp. ca. āruh] amnf āropitā raised; placed on; superimposed.
āropya [pfp. [1] ca. āruh] amnf āropyā to place on; to raise, to train; which must be raised — abs. ind. having been raised.
āroh [ca. āruh] v. [10] pr. (ārohayati) pr. r. (ārohayate) cf. ārop. kareņur ārohayate niṣādinam The elephant lets itself be ridden by its driver.
ārohá [agt. āruh] m. who has mounted on, rider — act. m. ascension; pride; altitude, eminence — obj. m. rump, hips of the woman (serving as a seat for her young child).
ārohaṇa [act. āruh] n. ascension.
ārohin [agt. āruh] amnf ārohiṇī who climbs, who ascends; not. rider.
ārjava [*rjva] amnf ārjavā honest, sincere — n. uprightness, rectitude, sincerity.
ārjīka [*r̪jīka] m. ved. region rich in soma; soma container.

ārta amnf ārtā afflicted by, oppressed by (iic.) | fallen into misfortune; afflicted; tormented | wounded; suffering, sick; unhappy — f. ārtā state of affliction; suffering. ato 'nyad ārtam [BU.] Any other (state than that of absorption in brahman) is suffering.
ārtatā [tā] f. state of affliction; suffering.

ārtadhyāna [dhyāna] n. jn. the meditation of suf france; it is of four kinds: thinking about painful things and desiring to get rid of them, thinking about diseases and desiring to be cured of them, thinking about obtaining pleasant things and sensations, practicing penances with the desire to be reborn like Indra or a cakravartin [nidāna].
ārtavá [*ṛtua] amnf ārtavī seasonal relating to menstruation — m. part of the year — n. menstruation — f. ārtavī woman during her period | mare.
ārtāyani [*ṛtāyana] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of ārtāyani, patr. of Salya "Whose ancestors followed the right path".
ārti [ārtai] f. pain, suffering (physical or moral).
ārtināśana [nāśana] n. destruction of French suffering.
ārtikya n. mod. cf. ārātrika. ārtikyam pratigrhyatām soc. he must receive the homage of fire || hi. ārati.
ārtnī f. ved. end of the bow, where the string is fixed to the notch.

ārtha [*artha] amnf ārthī concerning a thing or object; material, concrete; relating to a possession | gram. relating to meaning, semantics | lit. philosophical remark in a commentary — m. gram. the signified (opp. śābda the signifier).
ārthiká [*arthaika] amnf ārthikā signi
faithful | rich | substantial, real.

ārdrá [*ardra] amnf Ārdrā wet, moist; fresh, green, new | tender, soft, sensitive; soft, flaccid | soc. (sin) deliberate; opp. śuska — f. Ārdrā astr. np. of Ardrā "the Fresh", 4th lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the star Betelgeuse; Ru dra presides there; its symbol is a precious stone; cf. Bāhū. ārdrīkṛ to make moist; to moisten; to refresh | soc. to welcome a guest with water. ārdrīkṛta soc. welcomed as a guest. pratyārdrīkṛta lit. |Kir.| erased.
ārdraka [ka] n. organic. bot. Zingiber officinale, gin ginger | its root, used as a condiment in its fresh state (opp. śuṇṭhī) || hi. adrak.
ārdratā [tā] f. humidity | Coolness; sweetness, tenderness.
ārdratva |tva| n. id.
ārdrávāsas [vāsas] amnf who has wet clothes.

ārdhadhātuka [*ardhadhātuka] amnf ārdhadhātukā gram. ["applicable to a shorter form of the verbal base" refers to the endings of the perfect and benedictive, and of certain suffixes |pratyaya|; opp. sārvadhātuka.
ārbhava [*ṛbhua] amnf ārbhavī ved. concerning the rbhavas; sacred to the rbhavas.

ārya [pfp. [1] r] amnf āryā where one must go | ["with high aspirations"] Noble, generous; respectable | Noble, of Aryan race, well-born; said of the Arya people, who migrated from Central Asia to āryāvarta; they are said to be descended from the mythical ancestor Puru | class society [varna] brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya or vaiśya — m. master, head of household; honest man | adr. Your Excellency, Noble, Honorable — f. cf. āryā || pkt. ayya, ajja, ayyo; pali ariyo; fr. aryen; celte erinn; perse Iran; tamil Iyer; telugu Iyengar. jayatvāryah long live His Excellency. kim atra āryasya (polite) What can I do for His Excellency? | (abrupt) What are you doing here? āryā vāk f. Vedic Sanskrit. kṛṇvantu viśvam āryam [RV.] Make this world Noble (motto of the Aryasamāja). jāto nāryām anāryāyām āryād āryo bhaved guņaih | jāto 'pyanāryād āryāyām anārya iti niścayah || MS. An individual born to a Noble man |ārya| and a non-Noble woman can become Noble through his virtues, but an individual born to a non-Noble man and a Noble woman is certainly not Noble.
āryaketu [ketu] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Aryaketu, wise minister of Mitravarmā, then of Bhāskaravarmā thanks to Viśruta.
āryajusta | justa | amnf āryajustā suitable for nobles.

āryadāsī [dāsī] f. lit. [DKC.] np. of the farm girl [gopakanyā] Aryadāsī "Noble Servant", previous incarnation of Tārāvalī; she was the lover of Saunaka₂ and Sūdraka₂; she conceived by the latter a boy who was abandoned, taken in by Vinaya vatī, and who returned to the world as Arthapāla.

idá [m. Idā] m. ved. n.p. of Ida, epith. of Agni "who carries the libation".
idavidā var. ilavilā f. myth. n.p. of Idavidā or ilavilā, daughter of Tṛṇabindu, wife of Viśravā, mother of Kubera.
iḍas [g. iḍ ] iic. .
idaspati [pati] m. ved. np. of Idaspati, epith. of Pūṣā "master of libations".

Idā [id] f. refreshment, comfort | libation; (figuratively) a flood of praise | soc. part of the offering that the participants in a sacrifice consume in common | myth. np. of Idā "libation", daughter of Manu Vaivasvata; [BhP.] Manu had asked Agas tya to perform a yajña to the two Mitrāvaruṇau to obtain a son; he was astonished to Vasistha to have obtained a daughter; the sage used his great powers to transform her into a boy, who was then called Sudyumna; this boy, having grown up, went hunting in the Kumāravana forest, unaware of the curse that afflicted it, and which made him become a woman again; Sudyumna thus became the beautiful Idā again, with whom Budha fell in love and made his wife; Purūravā is their son, who founded the lunar lineage [somavaṃśa]; Idā has Ikṣvāku as his brother, who founded the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa] | phil. [yoga] ca nal psychic lunar [candranādī] on the left side, representation of Gangā in the microcosm; it originates from the right testicle; cf. Pingalā, Susumņā. it nota. gram. [Aṣṭādhyāyī] nonterminal metalinguistic marker; cf. anubandha. tit gram. which possesses the marker [anubandha] 't'. apit gram. which does not possess the marker [anubandha] 'p'. it (sf. primary av. guṇa) forms agents in the fem.
ita |pp. i| ifc. amnf itā went to (iic.).
ita ta av. i euphonic (form of pp.) | (taddhita itac) form of a. meaning "equipped with", "containing".
itara | idamtara | pn. mnf itarā the other (of 2); another; the rest; remaining | different from (abl.); low, common — ifc. other than, inverse of (iic.) lat. iterum; fr. other; eng. other.
itaratra |tra| adv. elsewhere; otherwise, if not.
itaravāraka [vāraka] m. phil. |Nyāya| presence of a superfluous element in a 5-part syllogism
members [pañcāvayava].
itaretara [red.] amnf itaretarā mutual, one another.

itaretaradvandva [dvandva] m. gram. compound dvandva coordinative, denoting the union of its members, like gandharvayakşa; its number is dual or plural, its gender is that of its last element; opp. samāhāradvandva.
itaretarāśrayadoṣa [āśrayadoṣa₂] m. gram. para dox of circular dependencies.
itare [loc. itara] ind. in either one.
itaredyús [dyu] adv. another day.
itás [adv. idam] adv. from here; here; of this world; opp. amutas | in this direction, this way, towards here | from now on. itas tatas adv. here and there, in such and such a circumstance.

íti [related to idam] part. cl. thus, there you have it, in these terms; namely, that is why, that is how; to that end | he said (closes an implicit quotation); saying, speaking; saying to himself, thinking | even (underlines the preceding word); under the name of, here is the meaning of gram. denotes the meaning of the preceding word (autonymy) | according to, in accordance with (before an author) || Latin itidem. iti kṛtvā adv. therefore; this done; having thus decided. ityuktvā var. uktveti adv. having said this. śrutveti adv. at these words. kim iti why then? under what pretext? iti devā akurvan thus did the gods. iti dhāranā thus is the rule. āgacchāmah iti vadanti "we arrive," they say. thinking he will speak again, they wait. As I am a stranger, I ask you. It must be said: "Here I killed the beloved." [Vedanta] This too, that too (this formula evokes the omnipresence of Brahman in all things) | Ved. marks a quotation within another. Thus, according to Pānini. Such is the meaning (after a para-phrase in a commentary). Gives the idea (after a para-phrase). To be precise; clearly (after a para-phrase). In essence; is the intention (after paraphrase). iti tātparyaḥ lit. rhet. gives the general meaning; is meant (after paraphrase). ityāśayah lit. rhet. gives the author's intention (after paraphrase). iti jñeyam gram. rhet. this should be understood as. iti dik gram. rhet. this is the general idea. iti bhāvaḥ gram. rhet. the intention is that. iti yāvat gram. rhet. this amounts to saying that. iti rahasyam gram. rhet. in fact; this is the important point. iti cet na lit. rhet. (after pūrvapakṣa) if (one speaks) thus, (we respond): No! kriyanta iti karmani gram. the kriyante form is in the passive.
itikartavya | kartavya| amnf itikartavyā necessary to accomplish in such circumstances — n. obligation; duty.
itikartavyatā [tā] f. necessary measure; action appropriate to the situation.
itikartavyatāmūḍha |mūḍha| amnf itikar tavyatāmūdhā who does not know what to do; bewildered, embarrassed, astonished.
itikṛtya |kṛtya| amnf itikṛtyā to do in such circumstances — n. obligation, duty.
itikramena | kramena | adv. in this way.
itivat |vat| adv. in the same way; how.
itivrtta [vrtta] n. occurrence, event; episode [[theatre] knot of a plot.
itiha [ha] adv. thus indeed; thus, once; according to tradition.
itihāsá |āsa| m. lit. |"once upon a time" | legend, saga, epic (not. the Mah. and the Rām.).
ityādi [ādi] adv. cl. (after a series of s.) and so on, and so forth — amnf which begins thus.
ityukta [ukta] n. ["thus spoken"] information, report | bd. explanatory work of the doctrine.
itthám [related to idam] adv. thus; like that; in this way; so much | lat. item.
itthā |related to idam| adv. Vedic. thus; like that; truly, in truth; under these conditions | certainly (emphatic of the following word) | lat. itā.
itthādhī |dhī₂| f. Vedic. sincere devotion — amnf Vedic. very pious.
itya |pfp. |1| i| amnf ityā where one must go — f. ityā litter, palanquin.
Ityaka |ka| m. chamberlain.

Ityoka m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara Ityoka, son of Madanavega and Kalingasenā; at his birth the gods substituted Mada namañcukā, incarnation of Rati; he was raised Madanavega; he attempted to abduct Sura by tamañjarī after his marriage to Avantivardhana, claiming that his mother had promised her to him.

itvará [i(t)vara] amnf itvarī who goes; who travels | who passes; transitory — m. stray bull or horse — f. itvarī unfaithful woman. id [contr. idam] part. cl. ved. certainly, precisely, indeed, exactly (underlines the preceding word) || lat. id.

idám pn. dem. nm ayam f. iyam |sg. nom. acc. idam; du. nom. acc. ime; pl. nom. acc. imāni; other cases cf. ayam this; this, that, these here (opp. asau); that which follows (opp. etad) | he, his, their — n. this world — adv. thus; now; here; next. idam sarvam adv. here below; in the world. tad idam that very thing. idam viśvam bhuvanam This whole world. tad idam vākyam the speech that follows. śrutvaitad idam ūcuḥ having heard them say this.
idā [idam] adv. ved. now | in the Veda.
idānīm [idānīm] adv. now, at this moment; precisely. idānīmeva at this very moment.
iddhá [pp. indh] amnf iddhā lit (fire); blazing | bright, clear; intense, violent — n. light; heat.
idh | agt. indh | ifc. amnf which lights (iic.).
idhmá [indhma] m. combustible; not. wood for sacrificial fire.
idhmaciti | citi₁ | f. pile of wood for the fire.
Idhmavāha [vāha] m. myth. np. of Idhmavāha "who feeds the sacred fire", epith. of the sage Dṛḍhadasyu, son of Agasti and Lopāmudrā; cf. Tri dasyu.
iná [agt. in] amnf inā capable; strong, then sant; brave, energetic, audacious — m. lord; king | the Sun.
ina na av. i euphonic.
√ ind v. [1] pr. (indati) pp. (indita) to be then healthy.
indirā [indira] f. myth. np. of Indirā "Splendor", epith. of Lakṣmī emerging from a lotus during the churning of the primordial ocean | kṣīrodamathana |.
indirālaya [ālaya] n. organic. ["receptacle of Lakṣmī"] bot. Nymphaea stellata, blue lotus.
indīvara var. indīvāra n. (flower of the) blue lotus — m. bee.

indīvarasena [senā] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of indīvarasena "Armed with the blue lotus", eldest son of King Parityāgasena and Queen Adhikasaṃgamā; with his younger brother Anicchāsena he set out to conquer the World; Kāvyālamkārā wanted to have them assassinated, by falsifying an order from the king; warned, they prayed to Ambikā, who gave them a magic sword; they reached the golden city of Sailapura, where reigned the rākṣasa Yamadaṃṣṭra, who had devoured the legitimate king Vīrabhuja and taken his wife Madanadamstrā; indīvarasena killed him with the magic sword, and married his sister, the beautiful Khadgadamṣṭrā; but he deceived her with Madanadamstrā, and Khadgadamstrā in spite put his sword in the fire, causing him to lose consciousness; Anicchāsena prayed to the goddess, indīvarasena recovered, found his sword, conquered the World, gave it back to his father, and then remembered his previous existence as the vidyādhara Padmasena, cursed by his father for complaining about his domestic problems.
Indu m. ved. drop (not. of soma ) | moon | math. symb. the number 1. indrāyendo parisrava [RV.] O drop of soma, flow for Indra.
indukānta [kanta] m. moonstone — f. in dukāntā night.

indukāntaghṛta | ghṛta | n. med. moon butter remedy, a fever-reducing antirheumatic. pūtīkadārudaśamūlakaṣāyasiddham sakṣīraṣatpalayutam grham indukāntam med. Moon butter is a decoction of orne, deodar cedar, and the ten roots, to which milk is added with the six peppers and salt. indumat [mat] m. myth. ritual name of Agni (whose invocation includes the word "Indu") — f. Indu matī full moon day | lit. [Ragh.] np. of Indu matī "Like the moon", princess of Vidarbha; at her svayamvara she chose Aja as her husband; Shortly after the birth of their son Dasaratha she was killed by the fall of a celestial garland adorning the vīṇā of Nārada.
induvrata [vrata] n. soc. ["lunar vow"] fasting graduated according to the phases of the moon.
induśekhara [śekhara] m. myth. np. of Indusekhara, epith. of Śiva "Crowned by the moon".

Indra | Indra| m. Vedic np. of Indra, Mughal god, who separated heaven and earth; he is the first recipient of solemn sacrifices. Later, the eldest of the 33 sons of Aditi and Kaśyapa; battle god of the storm, lord of the sky svarga, he is the king of the gods; he is drunk with soma; his capital is Amarāvatī; his aerial chariot | vimāna₁ | is drawn by the horse Uccaiḥśravā, his charioteer is Mātali, his attendants are the Treasures [vasavas]; he loves bay horses [haripriya] which he rides [Harimān]; later, his mount is the elephant Airāvata; his weapon is the

missile-thunder [vajra], forged by Tvaṣṭā; his magic bow is the rainbow | śakradhanus | ; he killed Tvāṣṭra Viśvarūpa, synthetic son of Tvaṣṭā, with the help of Trita; but by this brahmanicide [brahmahan] he lost his majesty | tejas | to the benefit of Dharma; Tvastā took revenge by creating the asuradragon Vrtra who held the waters captive; Indra fought him in vain: |Mah.| Vișnu advised him to make a pact with Vrtra, who asked not to be killed by dryness or wetness, by day or night, on land or sea; One evening, at twilight, by the sea, Indra invoked Vishnu and in a mass of foam Indra hurled his vajra, into which Vishnu had entered, and killed him; by killing Vjra, Indra freed the waters and allowed life; by this new crime he lost his strength to the benefit of Vayu; he took refuge in the waters, and the gods chose Nahusa as king; taking the appearance of his master Gautama, Indra abused his wife Ahalya; by this rape he lost his beauty, which passed to the two Nasatyas; Gautama stigmatized him to bear 1000 vaginas on his body, which the Brahmins transformed into as many eyes, and made his testicles fall off, which the gods and the shades replaced with those of a ram; He killed the demons Namuci, Bala, and Sambara; he transformed himself into a falcon [śyena] to steal the soma guarded by the centaurs [gandharva] in order to give it to Manu, narrowly escaping Krishna's arrow; [Rām.] during the sacrifice of Marutta, he hid from Ravana in the womb of a peacock; as a reward, peacocks bear his 1000 eyes on their tails; [Rām.] he was defeated by Meghanadaindrajit who took him prisoner to Lanka, and he was only freed when the gods paid his ransom; SacīIndrānī is his wife, Jayanta is his son, Jayantī is his daughter; he incarnated on Earth as King Gādhi; To punish him for his arrogance, Shiva threw him into a dungeon where four Indras of olden times already languished, who, as punishment, would have to be incarnated as warriors (they would be the Pandavas) only to return to Indra's paradise upon their death; he is the guardian [dikpala] of the direction of the East; phil. [Samkhya] he is the regent [niyantr] of the faculty of prehension [pani]; astr. he presides over the nakshatra Citra (Ear of the Virgin) as well as that of Jyeṣṭha (Antares), and sometimes that of Satabhişak (of Aquarius); cf. Jīmūtavāhana, Devapati, Parjanya, Purandara, Pūrudaṃsā, Ba lasūdana, Maghavā, Vāsava, Vijayanta, Vṛtrahan, Sakra, Satakratu, Sutrāman | hist. n.p. of the emperor Rāṣṭrakūṭa Indra₃; he succeeded Kṛṣṇa₂ in 914; Amoghavarsa₂ succeeded him in 929; cf. Trivikrama₁ Bhatta | math. symb. the number 14 | [indradvīpa] myth. One of the 10 continents [dvīpa] forming the jambudvīpa — ifc. the best of, the leader of, the prince of (iic.).
indrakīla [kīla] m. myth. [Mah.] np. from Mount In drakīla in the Himalayas, where Arjuna went to obtain the weapon Pāśupata from Siva.
indragopa [gopa] amnf indragopā protégé of Indra — m. organic. zoo. ladybug.
indragopaka [ka] m. organic. ladybug | organic. ver him health.
indracāpa | capa | min | "bow of Indra" | rainbow.
indrajāla |jāla| n. myth. Indra's net, weapon used by Arjuna | magic, sorcery; juggling, illusionism. indrajālapuruṣāḥ sarve gacchantu bhavanta iti [DKC.] Magical creatures, disappear all of you.
indrajit [jit] m. myth. np. of indrajit, epith. of Me ghanāda "Victor of Indra". indrajyeştha [jyeştha] amnf indrajyeşthā who has Indra as leader.
indratūla |tūla| n. cotton flake.
indratva [tva] n. dignity of Indra | kingship.
índradatta [datta] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the Brahmin magician Indradatta; cf. Vyādi₂.

Indradyumna | dyumna | m. myth. | SkP. | np. of King Indradyumna "adorned with the glory of Indra"; he reigned in Avantī; a wandering ascetic told him of the holy place Purușottamakșetra, where the sacred hill Nīlagiri, dedicated to Nīlamādhava, was located; on the advice of Nārada, he went there to found the city of purī; Jagannātha appeared to him in a dream and instructed him to gather his wooden body on the beach of purī and to lock it away from all eyes; the impatience of Queen Gundicā caused the premature interruption of the divine apparition, which only had time to create his face but neither arms nor legs to be able to help humanity in this ka liyuga; Jagannātha can thus only contemplate the sins of the World while awaiting its destruction; [BhP.] to punish him for his pride, Agastya condemned him to be reborn as Gajendra.
índradvista [dvista] amnf indradvistā myth. hated by Indra; cf. Baṅgāsvana.
indradhanus [dhanus] n. rainbow.
indradhvaja [dhvaja] m. soc. Indra's victory standard; it is represented in the theatre by the jarjara during the prologue of a performance | prastāvanā|.
indranīla [nīla] m. variety of sapphire.
indrapatha [patha] m. secret passage.
indrapālita [pālita] m. bed. [DKC.] np. of In drapālita, minister of King Vasantabhānu; Can drapālita Is his son.

indrapurī [purī] f. myth. np. of indrapurī "capital of Indra", epith. of the divine city Amarāvatī | phil. [Vedānta] seat of the Soul [ātman] in the Heart; cf. ānandamayakośa — n. indrapura geo. np. of the principality of indrapura, in the north of the hin douïsé kingdom of Campā₁ in South Vietnam.
indrapurogama [purogama] amnf indrapuro gamā preceded by Indra, led by Indra.

indraprastha [prastha] n. myth. [Mah.] np. of Indraprastha "plain of Indra", magnificent capital of the Pāṇḍavās during their exile, ancient Delhi; the rumor of its splendor attracted the visit of Du ryodhana, who visited their palace; he fell into a pool mistaking the water for a crystal floor, and attracted the mockery of Draupadī who evoked the blindness of his father; he returned furious to Hastināpura, and Sakuni proposed that he take revenge by gambling his kingdom with Yudhisthira.
Indrabhūti |bhūti| mr. hist. n.p. of the master Vaj rayāna Indrabhūti, student of Anangavajra; he is the author of Jñānasiddhi.

indraloká |loka| mr. paradise of Indra; syn. svarga. indravajra [vajra] n. myth. lightning as Indra's weapon — f. indravajrā phon. epic meter of 4 feet of 11 syllables [triṣṭubh], of tatajagaga motif, with pause after the 5ᵉ and 11ᵉ syllables. syādindravajrā yadi tau jagau gaḥ (self-definition of the indravajrā meter).
indravarman [varman] m. hist. np. of the Khmer king Indravarmā₁, who reigned over Hariharālayapura from 877 to 889; his son Yaśovarmā₁ succeeded him.
indravirocana [virocana] m. du. indravirocanau myth. [ChU.] Indra and virocana together, went as students to the hermitage of Brahmā to understand the Atmā.

índraśatru [śatru] amnf myth. |bahuvrīhi| vic time d'Indra, vanquished by Indra; said not. of Vrtra var. indraśatrú myth. [tatpuruṣa] who vanquishes Indra (which Tvașțā wished for his creature Vrtra, asking the officiating priests to utter in draśatrurvardhasva (may the enemy of Indra prosper), but they pronounced it with the initial accent, prophesying the destruction of Vrtra by Indra) myth. [Rām.] np. of Indrasatru, epith. of Me ghanāda "Victor of Indra"; cf. Indrajit. atha yad abravīd indraśatrur vardhasveti tasmād u hainam Indra eva jaghāna lit. [Satapatha] Then, having said "prosperity to Indra's enemy", thus truly it was Indra himself who killed him.

Indrasena [senā] amnf Indrasenā who serves as Indra's weapon — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of In drasena "Indra's Missile", charioteer of Yudhisthira — f. Indrasenā myth. np. of Indrasenā "Indra's seductive weapon", nymph commissioned by In dra to divert ascetics from their penances | myth. |Mah.| np. of Indrasenā₁, chaste wife of the hermit Maudgalya; when he became decrepit and foul-smelling, she remained very devoted to him; when he became leprous, and one of his fingers fell into his rice, she continued his meal; he then granted her a wish, and she asked him to make love continuously; After thousands of years, Maudgalya grew tired of it and resumed her life as a hermit, but she complained about it, and he declared that she should be reborn with 5 husbands to satisfy her great sexual appetites; she then performed great penances [pañcatapas], and Shiva appeared to her, promised that she would be reborn with 5 husbands as powerful as Indra, and sent her to Ganga; at that time the gods were gathered for a yāga at Naimiṣāranya; Indra, intrigued by flowers floating on the Ganga, went up to its source and found the young woman; he went to find Shiva, but the latter was busy playing dice with Pārvatī, and faced with Indra's arrogance he locked him in a cave where four Indras of olden times were already prisoners; IśānaŠiva then predicted to Indra senā₁ that she would be reborn as the daughter of the king of the Pañcālās, and that the 5 Indras would be reborn in the lunar race as her husbands; so she returned to Earth as PāñcālīDraupadī, and Vyāsa explained to her father Drupada why she had to marry the Pāṇḍavās.
indrāgní [agni] m. du. indrāgnī myth. np. d'indrāgnī, Indra and agni associated; astr. they preside over the double nakṣatra Viśākhe (Libra).
indrābṛhaspati [bṛhaspati] m. du. indrābṛhaspatī myth. Indra and Brhaspati associated.
indrāyudha [āyudha] n. myth. the rainbow, Indra's weapon; syn. indradhanus — m. bed. [K.] np. of the horse indrāyudha "rainbow" of prince Candrāpīda₁; he reincarnates the ascetic Kapiñjala.
indrāvaruṇa [varuṇa] m. of. indrāvaruṇau myth. n.p. of indrāvaruṇau, Indra and varuṇa together.
indrotsava [utsava] m. soc. festival of Indra, instituted by Uparicara.
Indrāṇī [Indraānī] f. myth. n.p. of Indrāṇī,
power [śakti] of Indra, a saptamātṛkā; she is embodied by Sacī, daughter of Pulomā₁.

indriyá [Indraiya] amnf indriyā myth. relating to Indra — n. ved. physical force, then sance | sense, faculty of perception corr. to a sense organ; cf. buddhīndriya | faculty of action corr. to a physical organ; syn. karmendriya | phil. [Sāṃkhya] one of the 10 principles [tattva] of interaction, comprising the 5 senses [buddhīndriya] and the 5 faculties of action [karmendriya]; [yoga] causal energy | bd. faculty; There are 22 physical or mental faculties, including: the bases or sites of perception [āyatana]: the eye [cakṣus], the ear [śrotra], the nose [ghoṇā], the tongue [jihvā], the body [kāya], and the mind [manas]; the natures [bhāva]:
femininity [strītā] and masculinity [puruṣatā]; sensations and feelings [vedana₁]: vitality [jīvita], pleasure [sukha], physical pain [duḥkha], the
gaiety [sumanastā], sadness [durmanastā], and in
difference [upekṣā]; the psychic faculties [bala]: faith [śraddhā₂], vigor [vīrya], sincerity [satya], the faculty of meditation [samādhi], and the sa

gesse | prajñā₂|; and three spiritual faculties: the assurance of attaining knowledge on the path of truth [sattvāpatti], the capacity to reap its fruits, and the attainment of the state of insight | arhat | | bd. |pañcendriya| the 5 foundations of moral virtues: faith | śraddhā₁|, vigor | vīrya|, the
gesse | prajñā₂|.
memory (smṛti), meditation (samādhi), and sa
indriyagrama | grāma | mr. set of senses.
indriyanigraha | nigraha | m. phil. | yoga | withdrawal of the senses.
indriyámocana [mocana] n. abandonment to its senses.
√ indh var. idh v. [7] pr. r. (inddhé) pft. (īdhé) was. (indisyáte) pp. (iddha) pf. (Sat) light up — ps. (idhyate) to be kindled, to consume, to burn | lat. aestus; eng. oast.

índha [agt. indh] amnf indhā that kindles, that consumes; fire, combustion — m. phil. |Vedānta| awakened aspect of consciousness, knower of material reality; cf. Vaisvānara | myth. np. of the rṣi Indha.
indhaka [agt. indh] amnf indhikā which lights.
indhana |act. indh| n. act of lighting or maintaining a fire | fuel, wood to burn.
√ inv [related to in] v. [1] pr. (invati) ved. to lead; to send | ved. to take by force; to have in one's power.
ibha m. bio. elephant | math. symb. the number 8 (for the 8 astadiggaja) — f. ibhī female elephant lat. ebur; fr. ivory.
imán gram. form of secon nouns
daires | taddhita | meaning quality after an a...
imam cf. ayam.
imān cf. ayam.
imām cf. iyam.
imās cf. iyam.
ime cf. ayam.
iya ya av. i euphonic.
iyat [idamyat] amnf iyatī in such quantity, as much; such number, so many; so great; no more than. iyacciram adv. for as much time. iyantaṃ kālam adv. for as much time.

iyam [f. idam] pn. start. f. [sg. name. iyam, acc. imām, i. anaya, dat. asyai, abl. g. asyās, loc. asyām; of. name. acc. ime, i. dat. abl. ābhyām, g. loc. anayos; pl. name. acc. imās, i. ābhis, dat. abl. ābhyas, g. āsām, loc. āsu this, these (here); she | | pṛthivī| this land — m. cf. ayam — n. cf. idam. iyam prthivī this land. iyamaham here I am. so'yam vidūşakah this vidūşaka right here.
ira ra av. i euphonic.
iras [abstr. r] n. hostility; anger — v. [11] pr. (irasyati) to be ill-disposed; to show one's anger | lat. īra ; fr. irascible.
irasyā | iras | f. enmity, hostility.
Irā [related to idā] f. that which is drunk; edible fluid; food; comfort, pleasure | water; milk; word | the earth | myth. np. of Irā, epith. of Sarasvatī "whose words are drunk".

irāvat |vat| amnf Irāvatī abundant in nourishment; that which satisfies; that which comforts — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Irāvān "Comfort", son of Arjuna and the serpent princess |nāga| Ulūpī; he was beheaded at the beginning of the great battle by Alambusa; in Tamil tradition, he is called Kūttantavar or Aravān and is the patron of transsexuals, called aravani or ali; he sacrifices himself to the goddess Kālī in order to ensure victory, after having married Kṛṣṇa in the form of Mohinī; after his beheading, his severed head watches the course of the battle; In Kūvagam (Viluppuram district) an 18-day festival is dedicated to him; the alis ritually marry him and then mourn widows; his severed head is represented in temples | myth. primordial ocean of milk — f. Irāvatī myth. np. of Irāvatī, epith. of Durgā "who brings abundance" | lit. np. of Queen Irāvatī₁, character in the Mālavikāgnimitra | myth. np. of the elephant Irāvatī₂, daughter of Bhadramātā; Airāvata is said to be her son | geo. np. of the Irāvatī₃ river; mod. Rāvī in Pañjāb | geo. np. of the Irāvatī₄ river in Burma; mod. Irrawaddy | bed. [KSS.] np. from the city of Irāvatī₅, capital of king Parityāgasena.

iva | related to idam | part. cl. like, as if, just as | which resembles (nom.) | seems, so to speak, in a way | quite | (interr.) therefore; is it? candra iva mukham face resembling the moon (in its beauty). kim iva how then? what then? atīva cf. atīva.

The six traditional calamities are torrential rain, drought, rats, locusts, parrots, and the proximity of kings.

[nom. र्रिं] master, dominator phil. Supreme God, lord; not. epith. of Shiva (qqf. Viṣṇu or Brahmā); chosen deity, inner God; cf. īśvara . īśā (i.) by the lord. [agt. र्हिंग] m. master, dominator, lord; possessor of | myth. np. of Isa "lord", epith. of Śiva guardian [dikpāla] of the Northeast, symbolizing sovereignty.
[i. र्रं₂] ind. by the lord. īśā vāsyam idam [Iśā] Everything here below is hosted by the lord.
īśāvāsyopaniṣad | vāsya₁upaniṣad | n. bed. ["teaching beginning with īśā vāsya₁"] cf. Iśā.
īśopaniṣad [upaniṣad] f. bed. n.p. of Iśā, or Isopanisad.

Īśāna [agt. īś₁] amnf īśānī rich, powerful, reigning — m. lord | myth. np. of Iśāna or Iśa "lord", aspect of SivaRudra; [Mah.] Vyāsa explained to Drupada that his daughter Draupadī was destined to marry the 5 Pāndavās because of a curse from Isana to Indra who disturbed him during a game of dice with Pārvatī to marry Indrasenā₁, and that he locked in a cave with 4 other Indras of olden times in order to be reborn on Earth to marry the same woman, incarnation of Srī | phil. [śaivasiddhānta] np. of Iśāna, face of Sadāśiva, turned towards the Zenith, associated with the transcendent world [śāntyatīta], with the element of space and the translucent aspect — f. īśānā myth. epith. of Durgā "Sovereign" — f. īśānī bio. bot. Bom bax heptaphyllum, cotton tree (kapok tree); syn. śālmala — act. n. splendor, majesty. [agt. र्रिंग] f. phil. ["who controls (the three aspects of the triad)", epith. of the Goddess [Sakti/Iśvarī] in the Trika system of Kashmira Shaivism.
[र्रिंत(i)tva] n. superiority, supremacy phil. [yoga] divine supremacy, an astasiddhi; this power allows one to create and resurrect.

īśvará [īś₁vara] amnf Īśvarī rich, powerful ["who rules what surrounds us"] | capable of (inf.) — m. lord, master; rich; king | myth. np. of Iśvara "lord", one of the 11 divine breaths [marut] | phil. Supreme God, lord; epithet of Shiva, more rarely of Vishnu or Brahma; astr. he personifies the 11th year of a life cycle [samvatsara] soc. title of the deity of a Shaivite temple, symbolized by its sign [linga] | phil. [yoga] chosen deity, inner God; one evokes him in meditating on om — f. Īśvarī myth. np. d'Iśvarī, a name of Durgā, Lakshmi, or a goddess [śakti] in general | bot. plant whose root is an antidote to snake venom. īśvarīkṛ to make a lord of.
īśvarakṛṣṇa [kṛṣṇa] m. hist. np. of the philosopher Iśvarakrṣṇa, author of the Sāṃkhyakārikās, a text prior to the 4th century; first editor of the sāmkhya doctrine, he was an atheist.
īśvarágītā [gītā] f. lit. np. from the Iśvaragītā, section of the Kūrmapurāna. īśvarátā [tā] f. supremacy, superiority. īśvarátva [tva] n. supremacy, superiority.
īśvarapraṇidhāna [praṇidhāna] n. phil. piety, faith, consecration/submission to God (devotion to the Lord, i.e., to one's chosen deity), one of the dis
disciplines [niyama] of yoga.

Īśvarapratyabhijñā [Pratyabhijñā₂] f. phil. [śaivasiddhānta] np. of iśvarapratyabhijñā, the doctrine of “Recognition of the Lord”, founded by Utpaladeva (Kaśmīra, 10th century) and developed by Abhinavagupta.
īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā [kārikā] f. pl. bed. n.p. of the Iśvarapratyabhijñākārikās “Stanzas of Reknowledge of the Lord”, numbering 244; cf. Iśvarapratyabhijñāsūtra.
īśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinī [vimarśinī] f. bed. n.p. of the Iśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinī, commentary on the Stances on the Recognition of
lord [Iśvarapratyabhijñāsūtra] by Abhinava gupta (1015).
īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛti [vivṛti] f. lit. np. of the Isvarapratyabhijñāvivṛti, detailed commentary on the Stanzas on the Recognition of the Lord of the Stanzas by Abhinavagupta.

Īśvarapratyabhijñāsūtra [sūtra] n. pl. bed. n.p. from the Iśvarapratyabhijñāsūtra “Stances on the Recognition of the Lord”, founding work [prasthāna] of the school of Recognition [Pratyabhijñā], due to Utpaladeva (Kaśmīra, 10th century).
īśvaráprasāda [prasāda] m. divine grace.
īśvarávāda [vāda] m. phil. debate on the existence of God; not. section of the Tattvacintāmaņi.

īśvarasamhitā [samhitā] f. lit. np. of the Iśvarasamhitā, Vaishnava tantric text of the pāñcarātra doctrine, from the 8th or 9th century; it is followed not. for the ritual of the Nārāyaṇasvāmī temple of MelukoteYādavācala.
īśvarasādhanadūṣaṇa [sādhanadūṣaṇa] n. bed. n.p. of the Iśvarasādhanadūṣaṇa of Ratnakīrti.
īśvarasiddhi [siddhi] f. bed. n.p. of the Iśvarasiddhi of Utpaladeva; he gives a proof of the existence of God, using arguments from the Nyāya.
īśvarādvaya |advaya| n. phil. monism.
īśvarādvayavāda [vāda] afmn īśvarādvayavādā phil. monistic theist.
īśvarādhīna |adhīna| amnf īśvarādhīnā subor given by the Lord.
īśvarīya [īya] amnf īśvarīyā concerning the Lord.

Ugraśravas [śravas] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Ugraśravā "of terrible renown", son of the sūta₂ Lomaharṣaṇa (and thus called Sauti₂); he is the second reciter of the Mah. among the brahmins gathered for a sattra in the Naimișa forest; [BrP.] his wife is the faithful Sīlavatī; one day when she was taking him to a prostitute, he saw Māndavya impaled by order of the king, and mocked him; the latter cursed him, and uttered that he would die before the next sunrise; Śīlavatī uttered in return that the sun would not rise the next day, which caused the gods concern; Brahmā, Vișnu and Maheśvara were mandated by them, and asked Anasūyā to intercede with Sīlavatī, who retracted his curse with the assurance that Ugraśravā would not die; as a reward for his help, Anasūyā asked that the trimūrti be reincarnated as her children Candra, Dattātreya and Durvāsā.

Ugrasena [senā] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the Yādava prince Ugrasena "of the terrible army", king vṛṣṇi reigning in Mathurā, brother of Devaka; his wife Karņī was very beautiful, and a demon appeared to her in the guise of Ugrasena to deceive her; from this union was born Kamsa who dethroned his father and imprisoned him; Kṛṣṇa restored his kingdom to him after killing Kamsa; the heroes Kanka₁, Sanku₁ and Anādhṛṣṭi are his sons | myth. |Mah.| np. of Ugrasena₁, epith. of Citrasena₁.
