uccātana [act. ca. uccat] n. dismissal, banishment; destruction, eradication | phil. | Tantra | loss of employment by bewitchment — m. myth. np. of uccāṭana, one of Kāma's arrows.
uccāya |act. ucci | m. gathering (by hand, without stealing). phaloccāyah fruit gathering.
uccār [ca. uccar] v. [10] pr. (uccārayati) pp. (ucārita) to pronounce, to say; to emit | to evacuate; to defecate.
uccārá [agt. ca. uccar] amnf uccārā which rises — act. m. discharge; evacuation, emission; excrement | gram. enunciation.
uccāraṇa [act. ca. uccar] n. act of pronouncing cer, enunciation; recitation; act of making audible.
uccāraṇajña [jña] m. linguist.

uccāraṇārtha [artha] amnf uccāraṇārthā gram. useful for pronunciation (said of a letter inserted to facilitate the pronunciation of a word); syn. mukhasukhārtha. uccāraṇārtham gram. for the needs of pronunciation.
uccārita [pp. uccar] amnf uccāritā pro pronounced, uttered, articulated; manifested (his) | who relieved his bowels — n. defecation. uccāritena gram. by his enunciation.
ucci [utci] v. [5] pr. (uccinoti) pr. r. (uccinute) pp. (uccita) pf. (sat) to gather, to bring together; stack.
uccais [i. ucca] adv. up; loudly; very, strongly, intensely — iic. highly ifc. . uccaistarām adv. higher. atyuccais adv. very loud (voice, noise).
uccaiḥśabdam |śabda| ind. aloud, in a loud voice.
uccaiḥśiras [śiras] amnf ["who holds their head high"] person of high rank.

uccaiḥśravas [śravas] m. myth. np. of the marvelous white horse Uccaiḥśravā "Most Glorious", born from the churning of the ocean of milk [kṣīrodamathana]; he is the ancestor of the horse race; Indra appropriated him to drive his chariot; [Mah.] seeing him from afar, Kadrū and Vinatā wagered on the color of his tail, with the enslavement of the loser as the stake; Vinatā, having wagered black, tried to sort things out by asking her serpent sons to cover his tail; upon their refusal, she condemned them to perish in the sacrifice of Janamejaya; changing their minds, they allowed Vinatā to win her bet, but Kadrū was saved from slavery by her son Garuda who stole the ambrosia [amṛta] at the request of the snakes | var. uccaihśravasa id.
uccaiḥstara [tara] amnf uccaiḥstara quite high; very high.
uccaiḥstarām [tarām] adv. in a very loud voice.
uccaiḥsthāna [sthāna] amnf uccaiḥsthānā of high rank, of noble family; of great stature — n. high place.
ucchal [utśal] v. [1] pr. (ucchalati) pp. (uc chalita) to jump, to spring up; to overflow; to fly away.
ucchalita [pp. ucchal] amnf ucchalitā sprung.

ucchid [utchid₁] v. [7] pr. (ucchinátti) pr. r. (ucchintté) pp. (ucchinna) to remove, destroy; ex to terminate. ucchedyatām prajāpīdakah Down with the tyrant! বিভিন্ন ucchinna [pp. ucchid] amnf ucchinnā cut off, removed; destroyed — m. soc. peace obtained by cession of territory.

ucchilīndhra [utśilīndhra] amnf uc chilīndhrā covered with fungi. বিভিন্ন ucchis [utśis়] v. [7] pr. (ucchinaṣṭi) pp. (ucchista) to leave as leftovers; to reject; to remain as leftovers. বিভিন্ত úcchiṣṭa var. uñśiṣṭa [pp. ucchiṣ] amnf ucchistā left (as leftovers), rejected, spat out, vomited; spoiled, damaged — m. (man) ritually impure (not. not having rinsed his mouth and hands after a meal) — n. leftovers (from a meal, from a sacrifice). nocchiştam kasyacid dadyāt [Manu] (The Brahmin) must not give any of his remains. na spršet pāṇinocchiṣṭo vipro gobrāhmaṇānalān [Manu] (A defiled Brahmin) must not touch with his hand a cow, a Brahmin or the fire.
ucchiṣya [pfp. [1] ucchiṣ] amnf ucchiṣyā to leave some remainder
ucchuṣ [utśuṣ₁] v. [1] pr. (ucchuṣyati) pp. (ucchuska) to dry out — ca. (ucchosayati) to dry out; parchment. বহুপুৰু ucchuṣka [pp. ucchuṣ] amnf ucchuṣkā sec; dried; shriveled.
ucchuṣma [ucchuṣma] amnf ucchuṣmā emitting flames — m. bd. np. du vidyārāja Ucchuşma "Burning".
ucchūna [utśūna] amnf ucchūnā swollen, inflated; puffy; bloated.
uccheda [act. ucchid] m. action of cutting, of uprooting; destruction | act of putting a stop to; abbreviating | soc. excision.
ucchedavāda [vāda] m. phil. materialist doctrine, postulating that death produces annihilation.
ucchedana [act. ucchid] n. cutting; destruction.
ucchedin [agt. ucchid] amnf ucchedinī which destroys.
ucchesa [obj. ucchis] m. stay; waste.
ucchoṣaṇa [agt. ucchuṣ] amnf ucchoṣaṇī that dries out | myth. epith. of the burning of love [dahana], arrow of Kāma — act. n. desiccation.
ucchraya [act. ucchri] m. lifting, elevation; height | growth, increase; intensity.
ucchrāya |act. ucchri| m. act of rising;
height | rising (planet) | growth, increase; intensity.
ucchrāyin [agt. ucchri] amnf uc chrāyinī which rises; elevated, high; imposing.
ucchri [utśri] v. [1] pr. (ucchrayati) pp. (uc chrita) raise, erect — pr. r. (ucchrayate) to get up.
ucchrita [pp. ucchri] amnf ucchritā raised, erect, high; exuberant.

ucchvas [utśvas₁] v. [2] pr. (ucchvásiti) pp. (ucchvásita) to breathe, to blow; to whistle, to pant; to catch one's breath — ca. (ucchvāsayati) to make breathe, to make catch one's breath; to loosen; to calm, to relax.
ucchvasita [pp. ucchvas] amnf ucch vasitā that breathes, that throbs; calm, comforted — n. vital breath, sigh.
ucchvāsa [act. ucchvas] m. respiration; deep inspiration; pause to breathe | lit. chapter of a work (e.g. the Daśakumāracarita and the Harsacarita).
ucchvāsita [pp. ca. ucchvas] amnf ucchvāsitā untied, detached; restored to health, joyful out of breath.
ucchvāsin [agt. ucchvas] amnf uc chvāsinī who breathes | who sighs | who swells, who rises | at the pause.
uj cf. ut.
ujjan [utjan] v. [4] pr. r. (ujjāyate) pp. (ujjāta) ved. to be born; to be from (abl.).
ujjayin [agt. ujji] amnf Ujjayinī victo rieux — f. cf. Ujjayini .

Ujjayini [f. ujjayin] f. geo. np. of Ujjayini "victory", sacred city on the Sipra, capital of Malava, first called Avantika, north of modern Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh; it was a renowned artistic center under the Gupta dynasty; it was the capital of Vikramaditya, who conquered it by his victory over the Sakas; myth. it is said that Shiva defeated the demons [asura] of Tripura there; it is a pilgrimage city, notably of Kumbhamela, and one of the 7 sacred cities [saptapuri]; cf. Mahakaleshvara gr. O. র্বাজ্য ujji [utji] v. [1] pr. (ujjayati) pr. r. (ujjayate) pp. (ujjita) to conquer, to conquer. রতিজয় ujjighra [utjighra] ifc. amnf ujjighrā which feels (iic.).
ujjīv [utjīv] v. [1] pr. (ujjīvati) pp. (ujjīvita) to revive, to come back to life — ca. (ujjīvayati) to revive, to bring back to life.
ujjīvana [act. ujjīv] n. renaissance; resurrection.
ujjīvita [pp. ujjīv] amnf ujjīvitā re came back to life.
ujjṛmbh [utjṛmbh] v. [1] pr. r. (ujjṛmbhate) pp. (ujjṛmbhita) to open, to half open; to appear.
ujjṛmbhita [pp. ujjṛmbh] amnf ujjrmbhitā half-opened; appeared.
ujjval [utjval] v. [1] pr. (ujjvalati) pp. (uj jvalita) to ignite, to shine — ca. (ujjvalayati) to flame, to illuminate.
ujjvala |agt. ujjval| amnf ujjvalā brilliant, radiant.
ujjvalatā [tā] f. radiance; splendor, beauty.
ujjvalatva [tva] n. radiance; splendor, beauty.
ujjvaladatta [datta] m. hist. n.p. of the grammarian ujjvaladatta (13th century), author of the Uṇādivṛtti.
√ ujjh v. [6] pr. (ujjhati) pp. (ujjhita) pf. (pra) to move away from, to leave, to abandon; to renounce, to avoid.
ujjha [agt. ujjh] amnf ujjhā who gives, who renounces.
ujjhita [pp. ujjh] amnf ujjhitā left, abandoned; discharged, issued.
ujjhitavat [ppa. ujjh] amnf ujjhita vatī who left. sā taṇḍulān ātapāyojjhitavatī she left the rice exposed to the sun.
√ বঙ্গু uñch v. [1] pr. (uñchati) inf. (úñchitum) pfp. (unchya) pf. (pra) collect, gather, glean || eng. wash. ব্ৰুক্ত uñchá |act. uñch| mr. gleaning, grain gathering.
uñchana |na| n. gleaning.
uñchanaka |ka| amnf uñchanikā gleaner; neck fear of grass.
uñśiṣṭa cf. ucchiṣṭa. ਤਟ uṭa m. grass; thatch, straw. ব্ৰু udu f. star — n. lunar asterism | the asterism, an āyādi; syn. nakṣatra.
udupa |pa₁| mn boat, skiff; raft | the Moon.
uduloma [loman] m. myth. np. of the wise Uduloma "with star-shaped hair".

udupī f. geo. n.p. from Udupī, a pilgrimage town on the coast of Karṇāṭaka [Karāvalī]; its Candramaulīśvara₁ temple is dedicated to Siva "carrying the Moon in his diadem"; its Anantesvara₁ temple is syncretistic; Vișnu in his primordial form is said to reside in the linga; Madhva founded the Srīkṛṣṇamaṭha there, which became a center of philosophical debates in the 9th century.
udumbara m. cf. udumbara.
uḍḍayana [act. uḍḍī] n. rise; flight; elevation.
uḍḍāmara [utḍāmara] amnf uḍḍāmarā extraordinary; magical.
uddāmareśvara [īśvara] m. myth. n.p. of uddāmareśvara, epith. of Siva “master of magic”.
Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra [tantra] n. lit. np. of the Uddāmareśvaratantra, Shaivite tantra of Kaśmīra dealing with magic and enchantment |vaśīkaraṇa|, in 15 sections [pātāla].
uḍḍiyāna [act. uḍḍī] n. flying posture region of the body between the sex and the navel. uddiyānajayo bandhaḥ [Yoga] contraction of the abdominal belt.

uḍḍī [utḍī] v. [4] pr. r. (uḍḍīyate) v. [1] pr. r. (uddayate) pp. (uddīna) to fly, to take flight, to rise. uddītumabhivānchanti bālā vihagadharmiņah [Yogavāsiṣṭha] Children, like birds, yearn to take flight.
uṇ nota. gram. primary affix [kṛt₂].

uṇādi [ādi] m. pl. uṇādayas gram. class of primary fixed affixes [kṛt₂] (starting with uṇ); these specific affixes are non-compositional: they form ready-made themes that cannot be analyzed semantically; they are listed in the treatises pañcapādī and daśapādī.
uṇādikośa [kośa] m. cf. uṇādisūtrāṇi.
Uṇādigaṇasūtra [gaṇasūtra] n. gram. np. of the Uṇādigaṇasūtra of Hemacandra, which gives 759 rules, prescribing 325 suffixes of primary nominal formation | kṛtpratyaya |.
uṇādivṛtti [vṛtti] f. gram. n.p. of the uṇādivṛtti of Ujjvaladatta.
uṇādisūtra [sūtra] n. pl. uṇādisūtrāṇi gram. for mular of non-compositional primary affixes, starting with un; its original is attributed to Sākatāyana.
ut var. uc, uj, ud, un pf. upwards, out of; escaping, tending towards superiority over; cessation of | ang. out; all. aus. udvikramādityam adv. manifesting (the name of) Vi kramāditya.

uccāvacá [caavaca] amnf uccāvacā high and low, small and large; multiform; heterogeneous, irregular | varied, diverse, of all kinds. uccāvacam upside down. uccāvacā janapadadharmā grāmadharmāśca [Āśvalāyanagṛhyasūtra] Peoples have varied customs and traditions.

utá ₁ conj. cl. and; in truth (emphasis or vow participle) | also, or, even; or else (interr.) | (av. opt.) undoubtedly. uta ... uta at the same time ... and. uta vā or even. kimuta all the more so, all the more so since; all the less so since. apyuta also. pratyuta on the contrary, but rather. uta kuryāt he does it undoubtedly.
utá₂ var. ūta [pp. vā₃] amnf utā woven.
Utathya m. myth. np. of Utathya, son of Angirā and Śraddhā, elder brother of Bṛhaspati; his wife is Mamatā, Dīrghatamā is their son; he taught royal duty [rājadharma] to Māndhātā.

utka [utka] amnf utkā who ardently desires | who hopes, who desires (inf.) | who thinks of something else, absent-minded — mn desire | opportunity, occasion — v. [11] pr. (utkayati) to arouse desire; to make regret.
utkatā |tā| f. state of ardent desire | bio. bot. Scin dapsus officinalis, philodendron, vine climbing along tree trunks; its fruits, fragrant, are used in medicine; syn. gajapippalī.
utkaca | utkaca | amnf utkacā bald.
utkaṭá |utkaṭa| amnf utkaṭā abundantly endowed with; immense, gigantic; excessive, excessive. utkaṭam adv. violently, excessively.

utkaṇṭh [vn. utkaṇṭha] v. [1] pr. r. (utkanthate) pp. (utkanthita) to raise one's neck; to desire; to long for, to be in love with | to regret (g. dat.); to grieve — ca. (utkanthayati) to excite the desire for | to inspire tender emotions.

utkantha [utkantha] amnf utkanthā ["who stretches his neck"] voluntary, enthusiastic; eager melancholic, regretting the absence of a loved one — m. sadness of absence, regret — f. cf. utkanthā. utkantham adv. eagerly.
utkaṇṭhaka [agt. utkaṇṭh] amnf utkanthikā which excites desire.
utkaṇṭhā [f. utkaṇṭha] f. intense desire for the absent loved one.

utkanthita [pp. utkanth] amnf utkanthitā who desires, who regrets, who feels pain; enamored of (iic.); nostalgic for (iic. g.) — f. utkaṇṭhitā woman suffering from the absence of her lover. tatratyātmīyalokasyāham atīvotkaṇṭhitaḥ I miss you all very much.
utkamp [utkamp] v. [1] pr. r. (utkampate) pp. (utkampita) to tremble; to shudder — ca. (utkam payati) to agitate, to shake; to make tremble.
utkampa |agt. utkamp| amnf utkampā trembling, shivering — act. m. agitation; shiver.
utkampana |act. utkamp| n. act of trembling or shivering; agitation.
utkampita [pp. utkamp] amnf utkam pitā trembling, agitated; unstable.
utkampin [agt. utkamp] amnf vikam pinī trembling, agitated.
utkara [obj. utkr] m. waste; embankment | heap; multitude.
utkarīya [īya] amnf utkarīyā relating to a pile.
utkarna [utkarna] amnf utkarnī who has pricked ears | who listens intently, attentive.
utkarṣa [obj. utkṛṣ] amnf utkarṣā superior, eminent, excellent; very; excessive — act. m. elevation, extraction | excellence; eminence; prosperity, abundance; boastfulness.
Utkala m. geo. np. of Utkala, ancient name of the coastal part of Orissa; it is one of the five countries of North India [pañcagauda] | pl. utkalās its inhabitants.
utkalikā [utkalikā] f. lit. the act of regretting the absence of a person.
utkaṣaṇa [utkaṣaṇa] n. plowing.
utkira [agt. utkṛ] ifc. amnf utkirā who piles up; who pours (iic.).
utkīrṇa [pp. utkṛ] amnf utkīrṇā piled up hollowed out; engraved.
utkīrt [utkīrt] v. [10] pr. (utkīrtayati) pro to proclaim, promulgate | to celebrate, to cover with praise.
utkīrtana [act. utkīrt] n. proclamation. ajātaputranāmotkīrtananyāyaḥ maxim of the proclamation of the name of a son not yet born; it corresponds to Perrette and the pot of milk.
utkuc [utkuc] v. [6] pr. (utkucati) to bend upwards; to open, to bloom (flower).
utkuṭaka [utkuṭaka] amnf utkuṭikā croupi.
utkuṭakāsana |āsana| n. squatting position.
utkula [utkula] amnf utkulā rejected from his family, disowned, fallen; degenerate.
utkṛ [utkṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (utkaroti) to get rid of, to extirpate — v. [8] pr. r. (utkurute) to blame. utkurute śatrūn he blames the enemies.
utkṛt [utkṛt₁] v. [6] pr. (utkṛntati) pp. (utkṛtta) to cut, slice, dice.

utkṛṣ [utkṛṣ] v. [1] pr. (utkarṣati) pp. (utkṛṣṭa) to draw, raise; to extract, to pluck out — ca. (utkarṣayati) to raise, increase, make eminent. বক্ষ utkṛṣṭa [pp. utkṛṣ] amnf utkṛṣṭā extracted, plucked out | superior, eminent.
utkṛ [utkṛ] v. [6] pr. (utkiráti) pp. (utkīrṇa) scatter upwards; pile up, stack | dig; engrave.
utkoca [agt. utkuc] amnf utkocā which meanders — m. corruption; bribe, dirty money.

Utkocaka [agt. utkuc] amnf utkocikā corrupt; who accepts bribes — n. myth. |Mah.| np. du tīrtha Utkocaka "Whose water serpent te"; there was the hermitage of Devala and Dhau mya; at the suggestion of Citraratha, the Pāṇḍavās went there to name the latter their lain chape.

utkram [utkram] v. [1] pr. (utkrāmati) pp. (utkrānta) pf. (abhi, vi) to climb on foot; to rise; to ascend | to take a step aside; to move away, to go away; to pass away | to omit, to neglect; to transgress. ūrddhvam prāṇā hyutkrāmanti [MS.] For the vital spirits are exhaling.
utkramá [act. utkram] m. ascension; exit reverse order; deviation, deviation; transgression.
utkrámana [act. utkram] n. ascension; flight | exit, return excess | end of life, death; ritual suicide.
utkramaṇīya [pfp. [2] utkram] amnf utkramanīyā to abandon.
utkliś [utkliś] v. [9] pr. (utkliśnāti) pp. (utklista) to be uneasy; to be tormented — ca. (utkleśayati) to excite; to expel.
utklista [pp. utkliś] amnf utklistā in distress.
utkleśa [act. utkliś] m. torment, affliction med. indisposition; nausea.
utkṣip [utkṣip] v. [6] pr. (utkṣipati) pp. (utkṣipta) to throw into the air; to set up, to raise.
utkṣepa [act. utkṣip] m. act of lifting, raising, throwing into the air | thing thrown.
utkṣepaṇa [act. utkṣip] n. elevation | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] the activity [karman] of elevation.
utkhan [utkhan] v. [1] pr. (utkhanati) pp. (utkhāta) to unearth; to excavate, to dig; to pull out, to uproot, to pull out of.
utkhāta |pp. utkhan| amnf utkhātā dug, excavated; uprooted, torn out, pulled | pulled, brandished (sword) | destroyed — n. hole, cavity; torn-up ground.
utkhid [utkhid] v. [6] pr. (utkhidati) pp. (utkhinna) extract.

Uttanka m. myth. |Mah.| np. of the rṣi Uttanka, a Brahmin companion in Vedic studies of Jana Mejaya; Gautama was his guru and cherished him; he remained in his service until a great age; then Gau Tama restored his youth and offered him his daughter as a wife; in order to fulfill his studies |gurudakṣiṇā|, he wanted to offer Gau Tama's wife the queen's magical earrings, which protected against hunger, thirst, and all dangers; according to the versions, the king is Pausya or Saudāsa; on the way to the king, a man forced him to eat the excrement of a bovine and drink its urine, and he did not purify himself properly; only after purification could he meet the queen, who gave him her jewels, coveted by the

dragons |nāgās|; their king Takṣaka, disguised as a Buddhist renunciant, stole them from him; with Indra's help he dug down to the underworld [Pātāla] to find him; there he found a rider [Indra] who told him to blow into the anus of his horse (Agni in disguise) which emitted flames and smoked out the snakes, until they gave up the jewels; he made Janame jaya make his great sacrifice of snakes, by telling him that Takṣaka had killed his father Parīkṣit; after the great war, Kṛṣṇa returning to Dvārakā met him; upon hearing of the massacres, he blamed Kṛṣṇa for not having been able to restore peace; This one showed him his theophany, and he prostrated himself asking as a blessing never to lack water; later, thirsty while crossing a desert, he invoked this gift, and a man of low caste [cāndāla] came with water, which he refused; Kṛṣṇa humiliated him by revealing that the man was Indra in disguise offering him the nectar of immortality against his will; then he performed a miracle, creating a cloud of rain in the desert.
uttankamegha | megha | m. rain cloud in the desert.
uttan [uttan₁] v. [8] pr. (uttanóti) pr. r. (tanutated C) pp. (uttata) to extend upwards, to stretch.

uttap [uttap] v. [1] pr. (uttapati) pp. (ut tapta) to heat, burn; to torment, to cause suffering — pr. r. (uttapate) to warm up; to be burning hot — ca. (uttāpayati) pp. (uttāpita) to warm, heat; to excite. uttapate ravih the sun shines. ਤਜ਼ਸ uttapta [pp. uttap] amnf uttaptā burned; heated red-hot, burning hot | tormented, burned with a red-hot iron — n. great heat.
uttabhita [pp. uttambh] amnf uttabhitā supported, sustained. satyenottabhitā bhūmiḥ [RV.] The Earth is supported bare by the truth.

uttama [super. ut] amnf uttama the highest, the principal | Supreme, extreme, superior, eminent; excellent, very beautiful, very good | last, final | superior to (g.) — ifc. form of superlatives: the most, the Supreme (iic.) | the chief of, the best of (iic.) — m. gram. first person (listed last in Sanskrit) | myth. np. of Uttama the Supreme, son of Priyavrata Uttānapāda and Suruci, (half) brother of Dhruva; cf. Auttami. uttamam adv. to the highest degree. sarvesām purusāṇām rāma uttamaḥ rāma is the best among all men. vidyāyā buddhir uttama [PT.] Intelligence is superior to knowledge.
uttamagandha [gandha] m. fragrance, sweet smell.
uttamagandhahya [āḍhya] amnf Uttama ganddhahya which exhales sweet perfumes.
uttamapurusa [purusa] m. gram. 1st person (listed last in Sanskrit).
uttamādhama [adhama] amnf uttamādhamā high and low; better and worse.
uttamādhamamadhyama [madhyama] amnf uttamādhamamadhyamā the best and the worst and the middle; from the highest to the lowest.
uttamādhikārin [adhikārin] amnf ut tamādhikāriņī who has the Supreme authority.

uttamaujas [ojas] m. lit. [Mah.] np. d'utta maujas "of great value", Pañcāla warrior who protected the wheels of Arjuna's chariot with his brother Yudhāmanyu; they both perished in the burning of the camp after the victory.
uttambh [utstambh] v. [9] pr. (uttabhnāti) pp. (uttabhita) to support, to bear — ca. (uttamb hayati) to lift, to raise, to erect | to honor.

úttara₁ [compar. ut] amnf uttarā higher, superior; opp. adhara | northern | later, future; subsequent, last; in addition; opp. pūrva | better, more important; victor | myth. [Mah.] np. of Prince Uttara "victor", son ca det but favorite of King Virāṭa; he is frivolous and not very bold, although he is adorned with the title of Bhūmiñjaya and boasts of being the equal of Arjuna; when the Kauravās raided Virāṭa's cattle, while the army was away fighting the Trigartas, he found himself alone in the harem, and used the pretext of not having a charioteer to avoid fighting; The hairdresser Mālinī₁ (Draupadī) persuaded him to let the transvestite Bṛhannaḍā (Arjuna) drive his chariot; the latter routed the army of the Kau ravās; warrior | ratha | of the matsyās, he is in the service of the Pāṇḍavās in the great war; mounted on an elephant, he fought King Salya but was pierced by his javelin — ifc. followed by; formed from (iic.) gram. form of comparatives — n. the north | the left | answer to a question; result | gram. last element of a greeting phrase | lit. np. of the |khaṇḍa| Uttara part of a purāṇa dealing with metaphysics — acc. uttaram adv. finally, lastly — f. cf. uttarā || ang. outer. úttarena adv. to the north — prep. to the north of (acc. g. abl. iic.). uttaratás adv. towards the north, to the north — prep. to the north of g. .
úttarakāṇḍa | kāṇḍa | n. lit. last chapter; not. of the Rām., of the Padmapurāņa, of the Sivapurāņa.
uttarakāla [kāla₁] amnf uttarakālā later, future; after (iic.) — m. future time | astr. time counted from the full moon. uttarakālam later, after. uttarakālatas id.
uttarakāśi | kāśi | f. geo. np. d'uttarakāśi "northern kāśi", sacred city on the banks of the upper course of the Ganges |Bhāgīrathī|, in Uttarākhaṇḍa (alti tude 1160 m).
uttarakuru | kuru | m. pl. name of a people and a Nordic country (Tibet, Assam?).
Uttaragītā [gītā] f. lit. np. of the Uttaragītā, text where Kṛṣṇa teaches the nature of brahman to Arjuna; it is considered a supplement to the Mah.
uttaratantra [tantra] n. soc. later section of an Atharvaveda rite | bd. n.p. of Uttara tantra; cf. Ratnagotravibhāga.
uttaradāyaka [dāyaka] amnf uttaradāyikā who answers; who contradicts; impertinent.
úttaranārāyaná [nārāyana] m. lit. second part of the hymn to the Purușa [purușasūkta].
úttarapakṣa [pakṣa] m. north side; left side | thesis refuting the antithesis; refutation; opp. pūrvapakṣa | good argument; valid thesis; final thesis, conclusion.
úttarapakṣin |in| amnf uttarapakṣinī supporter of the uttarapakṣa; respondent. úttarapatha var. uttarāpatha | patha | m. geo. northern India | hist. the northern route of the empire of Aśoka.
uttarapada [pada] n. gram. second term of a compound [samāsa]; opp. purvapada.
uttarapadapradhāna [pradhāna] n. gram. prima tie semantique du second term de un compound.
uttarapadalopa |lopa| m. gram. drop of the second member of a compound.
uttarapadalopin [lopin] amnf uttarapada lopinī gram, is said of a compound whose second member is implied; for example śākapārthiva si meaning śākabhojipārthiva.
uttarapadārtha [artha] m. gram. meaning of the second term of a compound. uttarapadārthapradhāna cf. uttarapadapradhāna.
uttarapaścima [paścima] amnf uttarapaścimā in the northwest.
uttarapurastāt | purastāt | adv. to the northeast | northeast of g. .
uttarapaundra [paundra] m. geo. north Bengal.
Uttarapaundrakhanda [khanda] m. lit. np. the Uttarapaundrakhanda, including the Paundraksetramāhātmya (60 verses) and the Karato yāmāhātmya (25 verses), prior to the 12th century.
uttarapraśna [praśna] m. lit. poetic figure of speech, where the answer forms the question; opp. praśnottara.

uttaraprosthapadā | prosthapadā | f. pl. astr. np. of Uttaraprosthapadās "the back feet of the bed", 25th lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the stars of Pegasus and Andromeda; Ahirbudhnya presides over it; its symbol is a double face; later also called Uttarabhādrapadās.
uttaraphalgunī [phalgunī] f. astr. np. of Uttara phalgunī "the second Reddish", 10th lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the star of Leo (Dene bola); Aryamā presides over it.
uttarabasti | basti | m. med. vaginal douche; cleaning of the urethra.
Uttarabhāga | bhāga | m. lit. np. of the Uttarabhāga, second part of the Kādambarī, completed by Bhūṣaṇa, son of Bāṇa₂.
uttarabhādrapadā [bhādrapadā] f. pl. astr. np. du nakṣatra Uttarabhādrapadās "the auspicious rear feet (of the bed)"; cf. Uttaraprosthapadās.
uttaramantrin | mantrin | mr. soc. prime minister of a king.
uttaramīmāmsā [mīmāmsā] f. phil. syn. vedānta.
uttararāmacarita [rāmacarita] n. bed. n.p. of Ut tararāmacarita, Bhavabhūti's sophisticated drama; it tells the story of Rāma after his coronation on his return from Lankā; cf. jṛmbhaka.
úttaraloma [loman] amnf uttaralomā who has erect hair.

uttaravedi [vedi] f. soc. northern altar of the solemn Vedic ritual, situated on a raised square mound, and bearing the sacred fire [nāciketa]; it may take the form of a stack of bricks in the shape of a falcon with outstretched wings [śyenacit]; cf. agnicayana.
uttarāmnāya [āmnāya] m. soc. "doctrine of the North", order of Sankara₁ whose jyotirmatha is located in Badarīnātha.

uttarāyaṇa [ayana] n. astr. period (favorable) between the winter solstice and the summer solstice (when the sun appears to move north, and the days lengthen); summer solstice; syn. udagayana; opp. dakşināyana. uttarāraņi | araņi | f. upper part of a fire stick; syn. pramantha.

uttarārtha [artha] amnf uttarārthā gram. which concerns The later rules [sūtra] — m. gram. meaning of the second term of a compound. uttarārthapradhāna gram. which has as its predominant notion its second member (said of a tatpurușa compound).

uttarāṣāḍhā [aṣāḍhā] f. pl. astr. np. of Ut tarāṣāḍhās "The Later Invincibles", 19th lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the star sigma of Sagittarius; The Viśvedevās preside there; its symbol is a bed of rest.
uttara₁ [agt. uttr] amnf uttarā which crosses.
uttara [f. uttara₁] f. the direction of the north myth. np. of uttara "the Nordic woman", daughter of King Virata, wife of Abhimanyu with whom she bore Pariksit.
úttarākhaṇḍa [khaṇḍa] m. geo. np. of Ut tarākhanda, a state in northern India, middle part of the Himalayas, west of Nepal; it is a region of important pilgrimages.
uttarānga [anga₁] n. arch. lintel.
uttarādi [ādi] m. geo. np. of the uttarādi maṭha founded in Karņātaka by Padmanābhatīrtha, disciple of Madhva.
uttarādhyayana [adhyayana] n. jn. n.p. from the text śvetāmbara uttarādhyayana "Supreme Study", in ardhamāgadhī, in 36 sutra-style chapters || pkt. uttarajjhayana.
uttarāpatha | patha | n. geo. the northern road, which connected Gandhāra to Pāṭaliputra; the northern country which it crossed.
uttarārdhá | ardha | mn upper part (of the body); posterior part (opp. pūrvārdha) | north side.
uttarārdhya [ya] amnf uttarārdhyā on the north side.
uttarāsanga [sanga] m. bd. monk's robe; cf. triīvara.

uttarottara | red. | amnf uttarottara very high, higher and higher — n. gram. response to a response | chatter. uttarottaram adv. higher and higher. uttarottaram munīnām prāmānyam gram. [Kaiyaṭa] The three sages of grammar are authoritative, each superior to the preceding one. pūrvaparanityāntarangāpavādānām uttarottaram balīyah gram. anteriority, posteriority, exclusivity, centrality, specificity, are in ascending order The preponderant criteria (for selecting a rule of Pāṇini's grammar).
uttarīya [uttara₁īya] n. garment of the shoulders, jacket, coat; fabric worn around the shoulder, shawl, veil.
uttare [loc. uttara₁] ind. in either one.
uttaredyús [dyu] adv. the following day.
uttāna [agt. uttan] amnf uttānā unfurled, open; stretched out on its back; with the opening at the top; concave | (liquid) spreading on the surface | [stretched] ready to, brought to.

uttānapāda [pāda] m. myth. [BhP.] np. d uttāna pāda "Giant", epith. of Priyavrata, son of Manu Svāyambhuva; he is father of Dhruva by Sunīti and of Uttama by Suruci; he personifies the star Kochab (β of the Little Bear).
uttāpita [pp. ca. uttap] amnf uttāpitā heated, warmed; burning | excited; incited.
uttār [ca. uttṛ] v. [10] pr. (uttārayati) abs. (uttarya) to bring out, to extirpate from | to deliver, to run | to vomit.
uttāra | act. ca. uttṛ | m. crossing; arrival, landing; deliverance, survival | discharge; vomit ment.
uttāraņa [agt. ca. uttr] amnf uttāraņī that comes out of; that crosses — act. n. exit from (not. water); act of landing, of disembarking.
uttārya [pfp. [1] ca. uttṛ] amnf uttāryā to make dock; to eject; to deliver; to vomit — abs. ind. having delivered, etc.
uttāla [uttāla] amnf uttālā grand, strong; high; abundant; excellent | impetuous, impetuous, violent — m. monkey.
uttinga [utdinka] m. organic. louse.
uttij [uttij] ca. (uttejayati) pp. (uttejita) ex cite, stimulate, incite; instigate, encourage.

uttīrṇa [pp. uttṛ] amnf uttīrṇā crossed who has crossed, who has overcome; experienced. uttīrņe ca pare pāre naukāyāḥ kiṃ prayojanam [SRBh.] What use is the boat after it has taken you across? বিরুদ্ধ uttunga [uttunga] amnf uttungā high, erect.

uttṛ [uttṛ] v. [1] pr. (uttarati) pp. (uttīrṇa) to cross, emerge from, come out of, overcome; escape from; reach | conquer; unload, abandon; disembark — ca. (uttārayati) to bring out, extir per de | deliver, rescue | vomit.
uttejaka [agt. uttij] amnf uttejikā who instigates, who stimulates.
uttejana [act. uttij] nf uttejanā incitement, instigation, encouragement; provocation | inspiring or stimulating speech.

uttejita [pp. ca. uttij] amnf uttejitā incited, excited, stimulated | sharpened; polished — n. incitement. ਤਵਪ uttha [agt. utthā] ifc. amnf utthā arising from, produced from, derived from (i.e.) — act. m. the fact of arising from (i.e.). (uttisthate) pp. (utthita) abs. (utthāya) pf. (abhi, prati, vi, sam) to rise, to get up (out of (abl.)) to wake up; to come from, to derive; to be born, to occur; to be resurrected — ca. (utthāpayati) pp. (utthāpita) the worm, to raise, to erect; to animate, to produce. śayyāyā utthāya having risen from the bed. śayyotthāyam dhāvati gram. He rushes out of bed (illustrates the use of the absolutive namulanta in 'am' to denote haste). uttisthamānah satruh a nascent enemy.
utthāna [act. utthā] n. awakening, rising; rising of the sun or moon; resurrection | activity, effort.
utthāp [ca. utthā] v. [10] pr. (utthāpayati) pp. (utthāpita) pfp. (utthāpya₁) to raise, to set up, to erect; to animate, to produce.
utthāpaka [agt. ca. utthā] amnf utthāpikā that makes rise, that raises | that animates, that excites.

utthāpana [act. ca. utthā] n. elevation; the act of erecting, setting up; the act of raising (a banner) instigation; the act of bringing forward, putting forward; these sation | math. answer to a problem — f. utthāpanī is said of a final verse [rc₂]. nāhamātmavināśāya vetālotthāpanam karisyāmi I will not raise a specter for my own destruction.
utthāpanīya [pfp. [2] ca. utthā] amnf utthāpanīyā which must be raised or made to be raised |capable of raising or animating.

utthāpya₁ [pfp. [1] ca. utthā] amnf utthāpyā to raise, to erect | to send back | math. (result) to produce by substitution | gram. |Nyāya| refers to a unidirectional dependency |ākānkṣā| (like the dependency of an adjective on a noun).
utthāpya₂ |abs. ca. utthā| ind. having raised; having produced.
utthāpyākānkṣā |ākānkṣā| f. gram. semantic dependence arising from the structure of discourse.
utthāya [abs. utthā] ind. having risen.
utthāyin [agt. utthā] amnf utthāyinī that rises, that appears; active.

utthita [pp. utthā] amnf utthitā raised; recovered (from illness) | elevated, high; eminent | produced, born, derived, arrived; returned (returned) | gram. [Nyāya] refers to a mutual dependency [ākānkṣā] between words in a sentence; opp. utthāpya₁.
utpaț [utpaț] ca. (utpāṭayati) pp. (utpāṭita) to pluck; to strip | to draw (a sword from its scabbard) | to open (the eyes); to bloom (a flower).
utpat [utpat₁] v. [1] pr. (utpatati) pp. (ut patita) pf. (sat) to fly away; get up.
utpata [imp. utpat] ind. jump!
utpatanipatā [nipata] f. continuous series of ups and downs.
utpatana [agt. utpat] amnf utpatanī that which takes flight; that which makes fly — act. n. flight; jump; ascent, rise | production. utpatanī vidyā soc. charm enabling one to fly or levitate.
utpatāka [utpatāka] amnf utpatākā with the banner raised.
utpatti [act. utpad] f. birth; production, creation; appearance, manifestation | phil. manifestation of what is created (opp. vyakti manifestation of what was veiled).
utpattiprakarana | prakarana | n. bed. n.p. of Utpattiprakarana, 1st section of Moksopāya.
utpattimat [mat] amnf utpattimatī produces, creates. vipadutpattimatāmupasthitā Death awaits those who are born.
utpattividhi | vidhi | m. phil. | Mīmāmsā | principal ritual injunction; it prescribes an act not mentioned previously.
utpattisthāna | sthāna | n. phon. position of articulation of sounds.

utpad [utpad₁] v. [4] pr. r. (utpadyate) pp. (utpanna) pf. (vi, sam) to start, to occur, to appear, to arise; to arrive, to manifest, to exist — ca. (utpādayati) to cause to occur, to provoke, to create, to cause. tasya ca mama ca pauradhūrtairvairamudapādyata [DKC.] These swindlers provoked our mutual hostility. ਤਰਾਸ utpanna |pp. utpad| amnf utpannā arose, emerged; produced, manifested.

Utpala [utpala] n. organic. (flower of the) lotus bot. Nymphæa nelumbo or blue lotus; we compare to him The eyes, The clouds, the tail of peacocks; syn. nīla hist. n.p. by Bhatta Utpala, 10th century astronomer; cf. Bhattotpala.
Utpalaka |ka| mr. myth. n.p. of Utpalaka, one of the 8
dragonkings [nāgarāja].
utpaladeva [deva] m. hist. n.p. of Utpala deva "Lord of the blue lotus", śaivasiddhānta philosopher of Kaśmīra from the 10th century; student of Somānanda, he founded the doctrine of Re
knowledge [Pratyabhijñā]; he is the author of the Iśvarapratyabhijñāsūtra and the Iśvarasiddhi; Abhinavagupta was his student; he is also called Utpalācārya.
Utpalācārya [ācārya] m. cf. utpaladeva.
utpalin [in] amnf Utpalinī abundant in lotus — f. Utpalinī lotus-covered pond | lit. np. from the Utpalinī dictionary of Vyādi₁.

utpaś [utpaś] v. [4] pr. (utpaśyati) to look upwards | to recognize, to perceive (acc.) in (loc.) to foresee; to anticipate. cakitaharinīpreksite dṛṣṭipātam utpaśyāmi [MD.] I recognize your gaze in The eyes of the timid gazelle.
utpaśya |agt. utpaś| amnf utpaśyā who looks upwards.
utpā [ utpā ₁] v. [1] pr. ( utpibati ) to drink until the end, to drink in one gulp.
utpāṭa |act. ca. utpaṭ| m. tearing out. kīlotpāṭaḥ m. lit. [Pañcatantra] (reckless monkey) who tore out the wedge (now the cleft in the trunk on which he sits).
utpāṭana [act. utpaṭ] n. uprooting; destruction; the act of uprooting; eradication | the act of banishing, dethroning.
utpāṭita [pp. ca. utpaṭ] amnf utpāṭitā torn up; destroyed, uprooted, eradicated | driven out, banished; dethroned.
utpāṭin [agt. utpaṭ] ifc. amnf utpāṭiṇī that tears out, that destroys (iic.).
utpāta [act. utpat] m. flight upwards;
jump | ascent, rise | sudden event; unexpected arrival | triggering of a cataclysm; calamity. pātotpātau var. vyasanodayau The highs and The lows.
utpād [ca. utpad] v. [10] pr. (utpādayati) to cause to happen, to bring about, to create, to cause. bhagavān viśvam udapādayat God created the World.
utpāda [act. ca. utpad] m. production; creation.

utpādaka |agt. ca. utpad| amnf utpādikā that produces, that engenders | productive; ef ficace; inventive, creative — m. progenitor; producer, generator. santi śvāna ivāsankhyā jātibhājo grhe grhe utpādakā na bahavah kavayah śarabhā iva || [Harşacarita] Ordinary poets are countless, like dogs barking from house to house, while creative ones are as rare as the griffin, with its paws on its back.
utpādakatā [tā] f. phil. generation function.
utpādana [act. ca. utpad] n. procreation.
utpādya [pfp. [1] ca. utpad] amnf utpādyā to produce, to create | produced, created; artificial, fictitious | lit. novelistic, pertaining to fiction.
utpiba [utpiba] amnf utpibā who drinks in one gulp.
utpiș [utpiṣ] v. [7] pr. (utpinaṣṭi) pp. (utpiṣṭa) to crush; to destroy.
utpiṣṭa [pp. utpiṣ] amnf utpiṣṭā reduced to powder.
utpīḍ [utpīḍ] v. [10] pr. (utpīḍayati) pp. (utpīdita) to press against, compress, crush; to extract from.
utpīḍa [agt. utpīḍ] m. act of pressing; pressure | explosion of tears.
utpīḍana [act. utpīḍ] n. act of pressing.
utpīḍita [pp. utpīḍ] amnf utpīḍitā pressed, crushed.
utpuccha [utpuccha] amnf utpucchā that raises its tail (bird) — v. [11] pr. (utpuc chayati) pr. r. (utpucchayate) raise its tail.
utpeșa [act. utpiș] m. act of pounding, crushing.
utprāsa [utprāsa] m. act of throwing far away, of throwing | burst of laughter; derision, joke.
utprekṣ [utprekṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (utprekṣate) pp. (utprekṣita) to look up, to observe, to consider | to imagine, to guess.
utprekṣā [act. utprekṣ] f. lit. elaborate metaphorical figure of speech, poetic comparison poetic imagination lit. poetic genre of marvelous fiction.
utprekṣāvallabha [vallabha] m. hist. n.p. of the poet Utprekṣāvallabha, author of the Maṇḍanapaddhati on jewels (16th century).
utprekṣita [pp. utprekṣ] amnf utpreksitā imagined.
utplu [utplu] v. [1] pr. r. (utplávate) pp. (ut pluta) to jump, to leap.

utphal [utphal] v. [1] pr. (utphalati) fut. (phalisyati) pp. (phalita) to open, to burst. उন্দেল্ল utphulla [agt. utphal] amnf utphullā wide open, burst forth. harșotphullanayanah with eyes wide with joy. tasya vahanam harsotphullam babhau he looked delighted.
útsa |agt. und | m. source; fountain; well | rain cloud.
utsanga [utsanga] m. lap, hip | flat surface; terrace, roof; layer; hollow place.
utsangavat [vat] amnf utsangavatī deep; rooted.
utsad [utsad₁] v. [1] pr. (utsīdati) pp. (ut sanna) to rise | disappear — ca. (utsādayati) to lift up, remove, destroy.
utsanna [pp. utsad] amnf utsannā high; opp. avasanna | abolished, suppressed.

utsarga [act. utsṛj] m. rejection, excrement; cessation, abandonment | production; offering, gift | gram. producer rule applicable by default, except in exceptional situations [apavāda]. utsargalakṣaṇapratiṣedha gram. prohibition of an operation conditioned by the data.
utsargasūtra [sūtra] n. gram. general rule, expressing a regularity (opp. apavādasūtra, viśeṣasūtra); productive construction.
utsargāpavāda | apavāda | m. gram. rule control by exception/default.
utsarjana [act. utsrj] n. abandonment, cessation; suspension of the reading of the Veda soc. end of Vedic studies; cf. upākarman.
utsarpa [agt. utsrp] m. that rises gently | that swells.
utsarpaṇa [act. utsṛp] n. act of rising; rising tide.

utsarpin [agt. utsrp] amnf utsarpinī which rises, which swells — f. utsarpiṇī jn. ascending cycle, cosmic period of gradual elevation; opp. avasarpiņī. utsarpinah khalu ete manorathah These are certainly very high ambitions.
utsavá [utsava₂] m. enterprise, commencement | celebration, holiday, festival; joy, happiness | soc. festival associated with a temple | elevation; ex hubérance, passion.
utsavamūrti [mūrti] f. soc. movable temple statue; syn. calantī pratimā₁.
utsah [utsah₁] v. [1] pr. r. (utsáhate) pp. (utsodha) pf. (pra) to endure, to bear; to act courageously.
utsaha |agt. utsah | ifc. amnf utsahā who supports, who endures (iic.).
utsādá |act. utsad| m. cessation; disappearance; ruin.
utsādaka [agt. utsad] ifc. amnf utsādikā which destroys, which cancels (iic.).

utsādana [act. utsad] n. cessation; act of removing, erasure; disappearance | interruption; omission | destruction; annulment, opposition | med. cure, healing (wound, disease); friction, anointing (ointment) | ascension; elevation; act of raising.

utsāha [act. utsah] m. strength of soul; determination, resolution; drive; enthusiasm; in enterprise | phil. courage, a stable emotion [sthāyibhāva]. utsāho balavānārya nāstyutsāhāt param balam sotsāhasya hi lokeṣu na kiñcidapi durlabham || [Rām.] Courage is strong, my dear, nothing is stronger than courage; truly, for the courageous, nothing is impossible in this world. utsāhaśauryadhanasāhasavat amn having courage, heroism, wealth, and boldness.
utsāhavat [vat] amnf utsāhavatī energetic; enthusiastic; persevering.
utsāhaka [agt. utsah] amnf utsāhikā 1( active; persevering.
utsāhin [agt. utsah] amnf utsāhinī active, energetic; enthusiastic | persevering. rūpayauvanotsāhī with the ardor of youth and beauty.
utsikta [pp. utsic] amnf utsiktā puffed with pride; hautein — ifc. overflowing with, made gold guileful by (iic.).
utsic [utsic] v. [6] pr. (utsiñcati) pp. (ut sikta) to overflow by pouring — ps. (utsicyate) to rise (liquid); to overflow | to swell with pride.
utsidh [utsidh₂] v. [unusual without pf.].
utsuka [utsu₁ka] amnf utsukā worried, anxious, melancholic | longing for, preoccupied with, straining towards (i. loc.).
utsūra [utsūra] m. time of the setting sun.
utsṛ [utsṛ] v. [1] pr. (utsarati) pp. (utsṛta) pf. (pra) to escape, to run away — ca. (utsārayati) to remove, to send away, to exile; to take away | to send away; to make go out.

utsrj [utsrj₁] v. [6] pr. (utsrjati) pp. (utsṛṣṭa) pf. (pra, sam) to let go, to release, to let escape; to throw | to reject, to deposit; to produce, to spread; to vomit, to exhale | to raise one's voice.
utsrja |imp. utsrj| ind. spread!
utsrp [utsrp] v. [1] pr. (utsarpati) pf. (sam) to rise gently; to rise (sun); to rise (sea).
utseka [agt. utsic] m. abundance; excess, pride.
utsekin |in| amnf utsekinī proud, who takes pride in; excessive.

udayagiri [giri] m. Eastern mountain (behind which the sun rises) | geo. n.p. from the fortified town of udayagiri, capital of Lāngūla Gajapati, in the Andhra country; its citadel, deemed impregnable, was conquered by Kṛṣṇadeva Rāya in 1513, after a siege of 18 months; a local tradition associates it with Mount Mahodaya where Hanumān found the herb of resurrection [saṃjīvanī] | geo. n.p. from udayagiri₁ hill, in Orissa; cf. Puspagiri | geo. n.p. the udayagiri₂ hill, twin of that of Khandagiri, 8 km north of Bhubaneśvar, Orissa; It is a site of caves dug by Jain monks (2nd century BC); the cave [gumpha] of the queen [rānī] contains sculptures; the cave of the elephant [hāthīgumpha] bears an inscription of King Khāravela | geo. np. of the hill udayagiri₃ of Vidiśā.

udáyana [act. udi] n. rising (not. of the sun) | exit; result, conclusion — agt. m. myth. np. of Udayana₁ "rising sun", king of the Vatsa country, son of Sahasrānīka, presumed descendant of the Pāṇḍavās; [KSS.] the legend tells that his mother Queen Mṛgāvatī was taken by a bird which abandoned her in the woods, and taken in by Jamadagni in his hermitage, where she gave birth to a son of marvelous beauty whom she named Udayana₁ "Rising Sun"; one day, Udayana₁ while hunting met a mountain man who had captured a snake, which he released in exchange for a gold bracelet that his mother had entrusted to him; The serpent, a nāga named Vasunemi, gave him the marvelous lute Ghoṣavatī and taught him the art of weaving garlands that never fade; the mountain man sold the bracelet, engraved with the name of Sahasrānīka, which allowed his father to find him; later Sahasrānīka abdicated in his favor and retired to the Himalayas; this mythical king is inspired by a historical figure, a contemporary of the Buddha, of whom it is said that he was a disciple [upāsaka]; he reigned in Kauśāmbī around the 5th century BC; [KSS.] he thought only of hunting, wine, and women; he charmed wild elephants with his magic lute; the Kathāsaritsāgara and the Priyadarśikā boast of his conquests; King Pradyota Caṇḍamahāsena of Avanti wanted him to marry his daughter Vāsavadattā₂, and built a wooden elephant full of soldiers to capture him and take him to Ujjayinī; he then promised Udayana₁ his life if he taught the princess music with his magic lute; having fallen in love with Vāsavadattā₂, Udayana₁ escaped by abducting her and married her; Naravāhanadatta Est was their son; Udayana₁ was known to be fickle, and many love stories are attributed to him, not. the Ratnāvalī₁; cf. Svapnavāsavadatta, Abhisārikāvañcitaka | hist. np. Udayana₁ or Udayanācārya, "Master of Inference," a celebrated logician of the 11th century (~1050–1100), a precursor of the Navyanyāya school; he unified Nyāya epistemology and logic with Vaisesika ontology; he is the author of numerous works, notably the Kiraņāvalī, the Lakṣaṇāvalī, the Nyāyakusumāñjali, and the Nyāyavārttikatātparyapariśuddhi or Nibandha; his Atmatattvaviveka is a refutation of Buddhism. strīmadyamrgayāsakto niścinto hy esa tisthati lit. [KSS.] He (Udayana₁) leads a carefree life, preoccupied only with hunting, alcohol, and women.

maternal | cavity; interior || lat. uterus. udare inside. udarapūram adv. | "until the belly is full" | to satiety.

(udghaṭate) pp. (udghaṭita) to open — ca. (udghāṭayati) to open; to peel. sa peṭikāṃ kuñcikayodghāṭayati he opens the casket with the key.

uddharṣa [agt. uddhṛṣ] amnf uddharṣā joyful; happy, satisfied — m. gushing forth (fire); great joy | soc. religious festival.

Uddhava₁ [uthava] m. sacrificial fire; festival; joy | myth. [BhP.] np. of Uddhava₁, cousin, childhood friend and confidant of Kṛṣṇa; he informed Vi dura of the latter's death, and urged him to meet the sage Maitreya₁ in Haridvāra to learn divine cosmology | hist. np. of the religious order |sampradāya| Uddhava₁ founded by Rāmānanda₁ Svāmī in Gujarāt in the 18th century; it was continued by the order founded by his student Svāminārāyaṇa.
Uddhavagītā [gītā] f. myth. np. of the Uddhavagītā "Gesture of Uddhava₁", where Kṛṣṇa reveals his last words to Uddhava₁ before leaving this world; it is part of the BhP.
uddhā [uthā₂] v. [3] pr. r. (ujjihīte) ppr. r. (ujjíhāna) to rise; to stand up | to open (door) | to leave from.

uddhāra |act. uddhṛ| m. act of pulling, of tearing out; rescue | math. subtraction | part; not. 1/6th of war booty, reserved for the prince | discernment, choice, selection; deduction; redemption; exception.
uddhāraṇa [act. uddhr] n. act of tearing off, lifting, removing | act of removing one's clothes | eradication, extermination, destruction vomiting.
uddhū [utdhū₁] v. [5] pr. (uddhunoti) pp. (uddhūta) pf. (sam) to agitate, excite; to lift, throw into the air.
uddhūta [pp. uddhū] amnf uddhūtā agitated; thrown into the air; scattered | revived (fire); excited; doped; exalted; exuberant | shaken; detached; thrown.
uddhṛ [uthṛ₁] v. [1] pr. (uddharati) pp. (uddhṛta) pf. (sam) to pull, extract; to snatch away from danger (not. from flames); to rescue, save | to raise up; to honor.
uddhṛta [pp. uddhṛ] amnf uddhṛtā pulled, extracted, torn out, removed | rescued, saved. )7 uddhṛtaudanā sthalī container from which rice has been removed.
uddhrtānekamahānāgadaśanam [K.] Who tore off the tusks/hooves of many elephants/snakes.
uddhṛtasneha [sneha] amnf uddhṛtasnehā from which the oil was extracted.
uddhṛtoddhāra [uddhāra] afmn uddhṛtoddhārā except exception; exceptional.
uddhṛṣ [utdhṛṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (uddharṣate) to rejoice; to take joy in — v. [4] pr. (uddhṛṣyati) to be joyful; to flourish — ca. (uddharṣayati) to rejoice: to encourage.
uddhvaṃs [utdhvaṃs] v. [1] pr. r. (uddhvamsate) to be affected by (disease) — ca. (uddhvamsayati) to affect, afflict.
uddhvamsa [act. uddhvams] m. med. affec tion; infection; epidemic.
uddhvaṃsana [act. uddhvaṃs] n. med. id.
udbāṣpa [utbāṣpa] amnf udbāṣpā filled with tears.
údbāhu [utbāhu] amnf udbāhukā with outstretched arms. údbāhuka | ka | amnf udbāhukā id.
udbuddha [pp. udbudh] amnf udbuddhā
woken up | excited | reminded; remembered; brought to mind.
udbudh [utbudh₁] v. [4] pr. r. (udbudhyate) pp. (udbuddha) to awaken — ca. (udbodhayati) to make understood; to inform; to instruct.

udbhaṭa m. hist. np. of the poet Bhaṭṭa Udbhața or Bhațțodhbața, director of the Academy |sabhāpati| of the king of Kaśmīra Jayāpīḍa; first theorist of aesthetic experience |rasa|, he is the author of the Kāvyālankārasārasangraha, and of a commentary on the Nātyaśāstra now lost; he gave an interpretation of Pāṇini independent of the Mahābhāṣya; cf. sthāyibhāva. ব্রব udbhava [agt. udbhū] m. birth, origin; homeland, place of birth — ifc. coming from, having as its origin (iic.).
udbhavatva [tva] n. origin of birth. ব্রহাব udbhāva [act. udbhū] m. production, act of engendering | intensification (sound).
udbhāvana [act. udbhū] n. act of raising | act of ignoring, not paying attention, neglecting announcement, communication | manifestation.
udbhās [utbhās₁] v. [1] pr. (udbhāsati) pp. (udbhāsita) to shine, to illuminate.
udbhāsa [act. udbhās] m. splendor; brilliance.
udbhāsavat [vat] amnf udbhāsavatī brilliant, brilliant.
udbhāsita [pp. udbhās] amnf udbhāsitā surgi, paraît | illuminé; splendid; orné.
udbhāsin [agt. udbhās] amnf udbhāsinī brilliant, shining | emerging, illuminating.
udbhid₁ [utbhid₁] v. [7] pr. (udbhinátti) pr. r. (bhintté) pp. (udbhinna) arise; become visible.
udbhíd₂ [agt. udbhid₁] amnf That penetrates; That overflows; That germinates; abundant — f. germ, bud; shoot.
udbhijja [ja] amnf udbhijjā That which germinates, That which grows.

udbhida [agt. udbhid₁] amnf udbhidā Who germinates, Who grows — n. fountain, source. রিম údbhinna [pp. udbhid₁] amnf udbhinnā arisen, appeared; discovered | abundant. বিহুস udbhuja [utbhuja] amnf udbhujā Who has his arms raised.

udbhū [utbhū₁] v. [1] pr. (udbhavati) pp. (udbhūta) pf. (sam) to reach, equal | to rise; to emerge, appear, become visible; to grow — ca. (ubbhāvayati) to produce, create | to explain, make ap relative; to mention, consider. সহুব udbhūta [pp. udbhū] amnf udbhūtā pro duit, appeared, born; emerged; raised, pushed, grown; perceptible.
udbheda [act. udbhid₁] m. appearance, germination, emergence.
udbhedana [act. udbhid₁] n. act of piercing, of germinating; emergence, gushing forth | source, resurgence.
udbhram [utbhram] v. [1] pr. (udbhra mati) v. [4] pr. (udbhrāmyati) pp. (udbhrānta) to rise, to stir in the air, to be brandished — ca. (udbhrāmayati) to brandish.
udbhrānta [pp. udbhram] amnf udbhrāntā mounted, perched; agitated, brandished | troubled; perilous — n. act of brandishing (not. a sword).
udya [pfp. [1] vad] amnf udyā Which must be pronounced; to say.
udyata [pp. udyam] amnf udyatā raised, high; active, ready to act.

udyam [utyam] v. [1] pr. (udyacchati) pp. (udyata) pf. (sam) to raise, to lift; to undertake, to begin | to strive to (dat. acc.). udyacchati cikitsām vaidyah the physician devotes himself to medicine.
udyama |act. udyam| m. act of lifting; not. )8 of raising one's hands to begin work; act of undertaking; undertaking, attempt; effort, zeal. udyamena by zeal.
udyamabhrt | bhrt | amnf who makes an effort; zealous, enterprising.
udyamana |act. udyam| n. act of rising effort, application.
udyā [utyā₁] v. [2] pr. (udyāti) to rise (So leil); to ascend; to come from | to go out, to depart; to depart from | to excel; to surpass (acc.). sūrya udyati at sunrise.

udyāna |act. udyā| n. elevation | exit | (place of exit) garden, park, promenade; not. palace garden | geo. np. of the udyāna or Uddiyāna or Oddiyāna, country of the North of the Indus valley (mod. Swat valley and Kashmir); it was a center of diffusion of bd. (1st century), associated with Gandhāra; in the 11th century it was a center of teaching of tantrism with Tilopa.
udyukta [pp. udyuj] amnf udyuktā active, enterprising, diligent, zealous; ready, active.
udyuj [utyuj₁] v. [7] pr. (udyunákti) pr. r. (udyuńkté) pp. (udyukta) to undertake, to prepare for, to be active — ca. (udyojayati) to incite, to activate, to stimulate.
udyoga [act. udyuj] m. zeal, effort, diligence; preparation; undertaking.
udyogaparvan | parvan | n. lit. np. from the udyoga parva, 5th book of the Mah., "of negotiations", recounting the preparations for war.
udyogin [agt. udyuj] amnf udyoginī diligent, active, energetic; entrepreneur.
udyojaka [agt. udyuj] amnf udyojikā entrepreneur.
udyojita [pp. ca. udyuj] amnf udyojitā excited, activated; gathered (clouds).
udrá [udara] m. bio. otter | sea lion — n. water.
udraśmi [utraśmi] amnf that radiates, that emits rays.
udrikta [pp. udric] amnf udriktā prominent, which stands out | increased, augmented; improved; abundant; predominant | in excess; excessive; residue.
udriktacitta | citta | n. great soul, great spirit — amnf udriktacittā proud, arrogant, self-important.
udriktacetas | cetas | amnf with lofty thoughts, haughty.
udric [utric] ps. (udricyate) pp. (udrikta) excel, distinguish oneself | increase; abound in | let go, release, empty; evacuate, release — ca. (udre cayati) improve; increase.
udreka [act. udric] m. abundance; excess; overflowing | superiority, prominence; preponderance, predominance.
udvát [utvat] f. summit, hill, elevation; opp. nivat — n. lit. np. of the Utvat, a sāman.
udvad [utvad] v. [1] pr. (udvadati) to raise one's voice; to proclaim — ca. (udvādayati) to make proclaim mer.
udvam [utvam] v. [1] pr. (udvamati) pp. (udvānta) to vomit, to spit.
udvarta [agt. udvṛt] amnf udvartā su perflu, redundant, en excès | abundant — m. left as remainder; excess, surplus.
udvartaka [agt. udvṛt] amnf udvartikā that makes grow, that makes rise — ifc. that spreads (iic.).
udvartana [act. udvṛt] n. act of rising; as cension; jump; act of germinating, of growing | act of swelling, of overflowing, of flooding | spreading of a guent, massage.
udvartin [agt. udvṛt] ifc. amnf udvartiṇī which spreads, which massages with (iic.).
udvas [utvas₁] v. [1] pr. (udvasati) to dwell outside of — ca. (udvāsayati) to banish, exclude; to remove; to uproot (tree).

udvah [utvah₁] v. [1] pr. (udvahati) to raise, to draw out; not. to draw arrows from a quiver; to marry | to bring; to manifest, to show. tava mukham kamalaśriyamudvahati your face has the beauty of the lotus.

udvahá [agt. udvah] amnf udvahā that carries in the air; that carries far away eminent, superior — m. act of bringing home the new wife, marriage | son; offspring | myth. np. of Udvaha, one of the 7 celestial Winds; he supports the lunar houses [nakṣatra] and ensures their rotation.
udvahana [act. udvah] n. transport; act of lifting, carrying | transport by (i.) | marriage arch. pillar support.
udvādana |act. udvad| n. proclamation.
udvāpa [utvāpa₂] m. act of throwing, of removing
ver | ejection | phil. [Nyāya] non-existence of a consequence in the absence of a hypothesis | gram. rejection of a meaning of the preceding word. āvāpa udvāpa gram. contrasting pair.
udvāspa [utvāspa] amnf udvāspā who sheds tears. )9 udvāspe nayane jāte with eyes filled with tears.
udvāsa |act. udvas| m. exile; abandonment | the act of dismissing.
udvāsana [act. udvas] n. retraction; withdrawal (not. from fire) | abandonment; the act of banishing; the act of going out to execute.
udvāha [act. udvah] m. soc. ["act of bringing the new bride" marriage.
udvigna [pp. udvij] amnf udvignā ef frayé; anxious, afflicted.
udvignacitta [citta] amnf udvignacittā an xieux, in pain.
udvignamanas | manas | amnf terrified; anxious, in pain, in distress.
udvij [utvij] v. [6] pr. r. (udvijate) v. [6] pr. (udvijati) v. [7] pr. (udvinakti) pp. (udvigna) to tremble, to fear (abl.) — ca. (udvejayati) to frighten, to frighten, to terrify; provoke disgust.
udvīkṣ [utvīkṣ] pf. (sat) observe.
udvṛt [utvṛt₁] v. [1] pr. r. (udvartate) pp. (udvrtta) overflow, rise, swell (floods); inon der | be arrogant.
udvṛtta [pp. udvṛt] amnf udvṛttā swollen, agitated; which overflows; unleashed | extravagant; inso slow, rude. udvṛttagaṅgā the Ganges in flood.
udvega [act. udvij] m. excitement, disturbance; nervousness; agitation, trembling | anxiety; distress, pain of separation from a loved one. udvegam kr to disturb. sodvegam adv. with nervousness.
udvegakara | kara₁ | amnf udvegakarī which causes anxiety.
una gram. forme des adjectives de partir de racines.

√ und v. [7] pr. (unátti) pp. (unna, utta) to wet, to water; to gush, to flow; to make wet, to bathe; to flood | Latin unda; Slavic voda; English wa ter; German Wasser; French onde. বন্ধ unná [pp. und] amnf unnā wet, wet. বন্ধব unnatá [pp. unnam] amnf unnatā high, tall, great; noble.
unnatakāla [kāla₁] m. measurement of time by a sundial.
unnatatama |tama| amnf unnatatamā great. the biggest.
unnatatara |tara| amnf unnatatarā compar. greater (than (abl.)). vrkṣata unnatataraḥ larger than a tree.
unnatatva [tva] n. magnitude; elevation.

Unnati [act. unnam] f. elevation; prosperity, grandeur | myth. np. of Unnati "prosperity", daughter of Daksa, one of Dharma's wives. বস্তু unnaddha [pp. unnah] amnf unnaddhā bound | unbound; unlimited; immeasurable, excessive; arrogant.
unnam [utnam] v. [1] pr. (unnamati) pr. r. (unnamate) pp. (unnata) pf. (sam) to rise, to stand up ser — ca. (unnamayati) to erect, to set up. unnamatyakāladurdinam an unseasonal storm is brewing.
unnaya |act. unnī| mr. lifting.

unnayana [act. unnī] n. act of lifting, of raising | act of removing a liquid; the container from which it is taken | parting of the hair, not. ritual | phil. inference. বিষ্ণ unnah [utnah] v. [4] pr. (unnahyati) pr. r. (unnahyate) pp. (unnaddha) pf. (sam) to bind, to gird, to free oneself from one's bonds, to escape.
unnidra [utnidrā₂] amnf unnidrā awake, awake; one who renounces sleep | open (flower).
unnī [utnī₁] v. [1] pr. (unnayati) to raise, to erect; to put above | to separate; to detect; to infer.
unnīya [unnī] amnf unnīyā to drive up.
unmajj [utmajj] v. [6] pr. (unmajjati) to emerge — ca. (unmajjayati) to bring forth, to bring to the surface.
unmajjana [act. unmajj] n. emergence.
unmatta [pp. unmad] amnf unmattā bewildered, frantic; mad, demented; intoxicated, drunk.
unmattagangam [ganga] adv. geo. where the Ganges is wild.
unmattadarśana |darśana| amnf unmatta darśanī with a panicked look.
unmattadaśānana [daśānana] m. bed. n.p. from the Un mattadaśānana “Rāvaṇ was driven mad”, 4th act of the Vi kramorvaśīya.

Unmattapañcāsat [Unmattapañcāsat] f. bed. n.p. from the Unmattapañcāsat “Fifty stanzas of madness”, epith. from Appayya Dīksita's Atmārpaņastuti, a mystical poem composed under the influence of the da
tura | mohana |.
unmattavat |vat| adv. like crazy.
unmattavrata [vrata] n. soc. "vow of madness" of tantric sects.
unmad [utmad₁] v. [4] pr. (unmādyati) pp. (unmatta) to go mad, to panic; to get drunk.
unmada [agt. unmad] amnf unmadā mad, furious | that intoxicates, that drives mad — m. madness, )() dementia.

unmanas [utmanas] amnf perplexed; agitated, excited, exalted; violently desiring — v. [11] pr. r. (unmanāyate) to take an interest in. unmanīkṛ to excite, to drive out of one's mind. unmanībhū to worry, to fret.
unmanaska [unmanaska] amnf unma naskā agitated, exalted.
unmanaskā [tā] f. perplexity.
unmanaskatva [vat] n. trouble of mind.
unmā [utmā₁] v. [3] pr. r. (unmimīte) to measure the height.
unmāda |act. unmad| m. intoxication, madness; insanity, drunkenness, passion.

unmādin [agt. unmad] amnf Unmādinī who drives mad — f. Unmādinī lit. [KSS.] np. of the beautiful Unmādinī "beautiful enough to drive mad", daughter of a rich merchant of Srāvastī, who offered her to King De vasena as a wife; the latter sent brah manes to check if she bore auspicious signs [sulakṣaṇa]; at the sight of her, they feared that the king would neglect his duties; they lied, and Unmādinī married the commander-in-chief; one day the king saw her on his balcony, and he died of grief.
unmāna [act. unmā ] n. altitude, height | thickness.
unmārga [utmārga] m. detour, wrong way | deviant behavior — amnf unmārgā who takes the wrong path | perverse.
unmārgagāmin [gāmin] amnf unmārgagāminī misguided, lost | evildoer. unmārgagāmī abhūt he lost his way.
unmārgavṛtti [vṛtti] amnf deviant, who behaves badly; rebellious.
unmiș [utmiș] v. [6] pr. (unmișati) pp. (unmișita) open the eyes; lift the eyelids; open (eyes, buds); be born, develop; become bright.
unmișita [pp. unmiș] amnf unmișitā open (eye, flower); smiling (face) — n. act of opening the eyes.
unmīl [utmīl] v. [1] pr. (unmīlati) pp. (unmīlita) pf. (sam) open the eyes, blink; close the sea (eyes, flowers).
unmīlana [act. unmīl] n. opening of the eyes; not. during the ceremony of consecration of an idol. caksūnmīlanam n. soc. ceremony of opening the eyes of an idol.
unmīlita [pp. unmīl] amnf unmīlitā open (eyes); blooming (flowers) || pkt. unmilla.
unmukta [pp. unmuc] amnf unmuktā untied; removed; thrown | freed from (iic.).
unmukha [utmukha] amnf unmukhī who raises his head, who looks upwards | who anticipates, who waits | near, imminent. maranonmukhah whose death is imminent.
unmukhatā |tā| f. state of anticipation.
unmuc [utmuc₁] v. [6] pr. (unmuñcati) pr. r. (unmuñcate) pp. (unmukta) to untie, unzip;
open | undress | release, send away.
unmūla [utmūla] amnf unmūlā torn up; uprooted; eradicated — v. [11] pr. (unmūlayati) ar to tear up; to eradicate; to extirpate; to destroy.
unmṛj [utmṛj] v. [2] pr. (unmārṣṭi) pr. r. (unmṛṣṭe) pp. (unmṛṣṭa) to rub, polish, clean; to buff; to erase — pr. r. (unmrjate) to pull towards oneself.
unmṛja [imp. unmṛj ] ind. rub!
unmrjāvamrjā [avamrja] f. action of rubbing continuously up and down.
unmṛjā [act. unmṛj] f. cleaning.
unmeṣa [act. unmiṣ] m. act of opening the eyes; act of looking | act of blooming (flower) | appearance, development | lit. volume of a periodical.
unmeṣaṇa [act. unmiṣ] n. development; appearance; emergence.
unmocana [act. unmuc] n. act of untying, of detaching.
unmocanīya [pfp. [2] unmuc] amnf unmocanīyā which must be untied.
úpa pf. near, towards, up to (acc.); under; in (loc.); opp. apa | near, beside, towards, close, contiguous;
subordinate | pf. of homage | pf. of cadet, junior name || gr. o; lat. sub. upa govardhanam śābdikāh grammarians are inferior to Govardhana₁.
upo [u] adv. (pragrhya) and verses.
upakakṣa [upakakṣa] amnf upakakṣā under the armpits — n. tuft of hair under the armpits saddles.
upakakṣadaghna [daghna] amnf upakakṣadaghnā f. upakakṣadaghnī who has (water) up to their armpits.
upakaniṣṭhikā [upakaniṣṭhā] f. (av. anguli) annular.
upakarana | act. upakr | n. aid, assistance tool, machine, device, instrument | expedient, )1 resource, means of subsistence | manufactured object.
upakartṛ [agt. upakṛ] amnf upakartrī who does a good deed; benefactor.
upakarṣaṇa [act. upakṛṣ] n. act of pulling towards oneself. edhopakarşanam act of bringing logs near the fire.
upakalpana |act. upaklp| nf upakalpanā preparation.
upakāra [act. upakṛ] m. service (rendered), help, care; benefit, favor; kindness ornament, decoration (garlands, etc.) | gram. fine subdivision of semantic roles [kāraka].
upakāraka [agt. upakṛ] amnf upakārikā helpful, assisting; appropriate benefactor; required, necessary; subsidiary, accessory. sarvaśāstropakāraka useful to all sciences.
upakārakatva [tva] m. gram. act of coming to the aid (of ⟨iic.⟩).
upakārin [agt. upakṛ] amnf upakāriņī helpful, who helps; benefactor.
upakumbham [upakumbha] adv. near the jug. upakumbhād āgataḥ came from near the jug.
upakurvāṇa [ppr. mo. upakṛ] m. soc. ["one who renders service"] Brahmanical student |brahmacarya| opting at the end of his studies for family life [grhastha]; opp. naisthika.

upakṛ [upakṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (upakaróti) pp. (upakṛta) pf. (prati) to assist, to serve; to help, to care for, to do good; to oblige, to render a service to someone. g. loc. — v. [8] pr. r. (upaskurute) pp. (upaskṛta) to make an effort; to transform; to supply (a missing proposition). guṇānām upaskurute it confers new qualities.
upakṛta [pp. upakṛta] amnf upakṛtā aided, served; benefited | rendered as a service — n. aid, relief; favor, service; benefit.
upakṛti [act. upakṛ] f. help, aid, assistance; service rendered or received.
upakṛtin [agt. upakṛ] amnf upakṛtinī who renders service, who helps.
upakṛṣ [upakṛṣ] v. [1] pr. (upakarṣati) to pull towards oneself.
upakṛṣṇam [upakṛṣṇa] adv. near kṛṣṇa.
upakṛṣṇāt [upakṛṣṇa] adv. having taken kṛṣṇa as a refuge.
upakṛ [upakṛ] v. [6] pr. (upakirati) to scatter; to water — v. [6] pr. (upaskirati) to cut, split, damage.
upaklp [upaklp] v. [1] pr. r. (upakalpate) pp. (upaklpta) to serve (dat.); to take the form of — ca. (upakalpayati) to prepare, equip; arrange; provide, procure.
upakośā [upakośa] f. bed. [KSS.] np. of upakośā, who married Vararuci.

upakram [upakram] v. [1] pr. (upakrāmati) pp. (upakrānta) to approach; to arrive | to throw oneself upon, to attack | med. to treat, to care for (a patient) — pr. r. (upakramate) to approach, to have recourse to, to begin to (acc. dat. inf.).

upakrama [act. upakram] m. approach; commencement; undertaking, plan | means, expedient; stratagem | med. remedy; medical treatment | phil. [Mīmāṃsā] introduction of a section of text; opp. upasamhāra.
Upakramaparākrama [parākrama] m. lit. np. of the Upakramaparākrama "Supremacy of the introduction (of a text)", polemical text by Appayya Dīkṣita aimed at refuting Vyāsatīrtha.
upakramopasamhāra [upasamhāra] m. du. lit. in introduction and conclusion of a section of text.
upakramopasamhāraikarūpya [ekarūpya] m. phil. coherence of the beginning and end of a section of text, a tātparyalinga.
upakriyā [upakriyā] f. aid, help; favor, service; benefit | means, expedient | med. remedy.
upakrī [upakrī₁] v. [9] pr. (upakrīṇāti) to buy.
upakṣī [upakṣī] ps. (apakṣīyate) pp. (upakṣīṇa) decline; deteriorate; exhaust.
upakṣīṇa [pp. upakṣī] amnf upakṣīṇā exhausted, consumed; gone.
upagangam [upagangā] adv. near the Ganges.
upagaṇa [upagaṇa] amnf upagaṇā which forms a small group — m. gram. subclass of a group of words.

upaguh [upaguh] v. [1] pr. (upagūhati) pp. (upagūḍha) to hide, to conceal — v. [1] pr. r. (upagūhayate) to embrace. upaguya ind. having concealed; having embraced.

tuel [snāna], clothing [vastra], the wearing of the sacred horn [yajñopavīta], perfume [gandha], the

upadiṣṭa [pp. upadiś] amnf upadiṣṭā in diqué, conseil; enseignant | gram. emploi (par un speaker cultivé [śiṣṭa₂]). yathopadistam gram. en le sol c'est essayé par un parleur cultivé. en le sol c'est essayé par un parleur cultivé.

[Padakṛtya] The application expresses the attainment of the essence of the subject by the proof of the discriminating quality of the expressed inherence.

Atmapurāna.

upanīti [act. upanī] f. cf. upanayana.
upanetram [upanetra] adv. within sight.
upanyas [upanyas] v. [4] pr. (upanyásyati) pp. (upanyasta) to put forward, to mean; to mention, to announce | to suggest, to explain.

upapatham |upapatha| adv. beside the road.

(upapādayati) to put (acc.) in the state of (acc.); to bring about (acc.) (loc. dat.); to accomplish, to produce; to justify. doşamapi gunatvamupapādayitum to make the best of a bad situation.

layer [Śayyabhoga], incense [Dhupabhoga], and the
women |Yosidbhoga|.

upamanyú [Upamanyu] amnf eager, zealous, obedient — m. myth. np. du rși Upamanyu "Obedient", pupil of Dhaumya; he gave to his master the food he received in alms; the latter ordered him not to beg for his own account, nor to drink the milk of cows, nor even the foam of milk from the muzzle of calves; he ate from a poisoned bark, became blind, fell into a well, and recovered his sight by praying to the Aśvinau; it is said that he is son of Vyāghrapāda, and that as a baby he obtained by praying to Siva the sea of milk as food.
