Rcīka [rc₂īka] m. myth. np. of the rsi Rcīka "Verse", son of Aurva Bhārgava; in his old age he married Satyavatī₁, giving his father Gādhi a thousand white horses with one black ear [śyāmakarṇāśva], which Varuṇa had caused to emerge from the Ganges at his prayers; Satyavatī₁ prayed to him to give her a son, and wished that his mother also had a son so that she herself might have a brother; Rcīka made a Vedic sacrifice |homa| and prepared two rice balls, into which he had breathed resp. the effulgence of

brahmins [brahmatejas] and the effulgence of the princes | kṣātratejas |; the first was intended for Satyavatī₁, the second for Gādhi's wife, but the latter switched the foods, causing the confusion of castes |varnasamkara|; Satyavatī₁ gave birth to Jamadagni, his mother obtained Viśvāmitra as a son; |Rām.| Ŗcīka is assimilated to Ajīgarta, in a variant where he sells his son Sunaḥśepha₁ to King Am barīṣa; After his victory over Shiva, Vishnu gave his victorious bow to Rika, who gave it to Jamadagni, who gave it to his son Parasurama, who used it to confront Rama upon returning from the svayaṃvara of Sita.
rcchā [r] ifc. f. cf. yadrccha.

√ rj v. [1] pr. (árjati) pp. (árjita) pf. (upa) to obtain, acquire, procure — ca. (arjayati) id. — pr. r. (árjate) to stand straight, to be upright; to be direct, to be firm, to be strong — v. [6] pr. (rñjáti) pr. r. (rñjáte) to reach; to extend.
rjīṣá [rjīṣa] n. ved. residue from pressing soma.
rjīṣin |in| amnf rjīṣiṇī véd. which receives the residue from pressing the soma.
rjú [rju] amnf rjvī straight; upright, honest; opp. vrjina | lat. rectus; all. recht; ang. right; fr. direct, droit. rjū kṛ straighten; correct. rjū bhū straighten oneself.
rjútva |tva| n. uprightness, probity, honesty; sincerity.
rjurekhā [rekhā] f. math. right.
rjusūtra |sūtra| n. just rule | jn. one of the seven argumentative viewpoints [naya].

rṇá [r] amnf rṇā flight; guilty of transgression; fugitive — n. lack; debt, obligation; guilt | loss, an āyādi; syn. vyaya. rnam kr to contract a debt. rṇaṃ dā to repay a debt. rnam prāp to go into debt. rņam yāc to solicit a loan.
rṇágraha [graha] amnf rṇagrahā qui em prunte; qui contracte une dette — m. emprunt (fait d'emprunt).

rṇatraya [traya] n. phil. the "triple debt" of man to the gods [deva], the sages [rsi] and the manes [pitr]; it is discharged respectively by sacrifice, Vedic recitation and the procreation of posterity.
rṇádātṛ [dātṛ] amnf rṇadātrī who repays a debt.
rṇádāna |dāna| n. repayment of a debt.
rṇádāyin [dāyin] amnf rṇádāyinī who rem bourse une dette.
rṇádāsa [dāsa] m. soc. ["slave in debt"] who pays off his debt by becoming a slave to his creditor.
ṛṇānubandha | anubandha | m. bond related to a debt; obligation towards one's lender.

rtá [pp. r] amnf rtā clear, true, pure; suitable, correct; regular — n. moral rule, right; established order, justice | sacred custom; pious work; prayer, faith | exact arrangement; divine law, cosmic order; supreme truth | gleaning, a suitable means of subsistence for a brahmin [satkarman]; opp. anṛta agriculture — v. [11] pr. (ṛtāyáti) v. [11] pr. r. (rtayáte) to observe the established order. rtena rightly; correctly. rtasya yoni heart of the sacrificial area; altar; holy of holies. rtasya sadana id.
rtádhāman |dhāman| amnf rtadhāmanī who accepts divine law.
rtasáp [sap₂] amnf virtuous.
rtāyana | ayana | n. phil. correct way.
rtam [acc. rta] iic.

rtambhara [bhara] m. myth. np. of Rtambhara, epith. of Brahmā "Bearer of the supreme truth", or of Vișnu "who maintains cosmic order" — f. rtambharā phil. [yoga] concentration of the mind bringing the infallible divine light.
rtaṃbharaprajña [prajñā₂] afmn rtambharaprajñā phil. (yogin) having supreme knowledge.
rtā iic. rta.
rtāvan [van] amnf rtāvarī in accordance with the cosmic order (said of recurring phenomena such as dawn) | of good morality, pious; just | soc. that performs sacred acts; that accepts them (God).
rtāvrdh | vrdh₂ | amnf virtuous.
rti [act. r] f. misfortune; suffering — m. as enemy, assailant.
rtikara | kara₁ | amnf rtikarī which does harm.

rtú [rtu] m. epoch, period; agreed time, appropriate time, favorable time (not. for a sacrament); fertile period, menstruation (for a woman) time of year, astral season. 2-month season; there are 6: vasanta spring, (months of caitra and vaiśākha) grīṣma summer, (months of jyaiṣtha and āṣādha) varṣā rainy season, (months of śrāvaṇa₂ and bhādrapada) śarad autumn, (months of āśvina and kārttika) hemanta winter, (months of mārgaśīrṣa and paușa) and śiśira cold season (months of māgha and phālguna) | fertile period of a woman after her menstruation | math. symb. the number 6 || lat. artus. rtușu adv. in the favorable period (not. for conception). saṃvatare ṛtavaḥ ṣaṣ there are 6 seasons in the year. rtuparņa | parņa | m. myth. np. of the king of Ayodhyā Rtuparņa, son of Ayutāyu, father of Sarvakāma, ancestor of Raghu and therefore of Rāma; [Mah.] Rtuparņa is also called Bhāngāsuri "son of Bhangāsura"; on the advice of Karkoṭaka, King Nala went incognito to the court of rtuparna to become his master of the stables, under the name of Bāhuka; On their way to Damayantī's svayamvara in Vidarbha, the king showed his powers by counting very quickly the leaves and fruits of a vibhītaka tree, and thus by playing dice [akṣahṛdaya]; Nala exchanged his knowledge for his own equestrian expertise [aśvahrdaya]; as soon as he had the power of the dice, Nala expelled from his body the demon Kali who vomited the poison of Karkoţaka; finally Damayantī recognized him, and they were reunited.

rtumat [mat] amnf rtumatī which occurs at the appropriate time | according to the season — n. myth. np. of the sacred grove Rtumat where Varuna resides, in the Trikūṭa mountains — f. rtumatī ["who has her period"] pubescent girl | woman During her fertile period.
rtusamhāra [samhāra] m. lit. np. from the Rtusamhāra "The Round of the Seasons", a lyric poem attributed to Kālidāsa.
prep. rte without, except, to the exclusion of (abl. acc.
rtvik iic. rtvij.
rtvíj [rtuij] m. [sg. nom. rtvik] soc. ["who offers at the appointed time"] Vedic officiant, priest; according to his functions he is called hotr, adhvaryu, udgātr or brahman.
rtviya [rtuiya] m. ved. (officiant) following the ritual.
rddha [pp. rdh] amnf rddhā prosperous, abundant; rich — n. stored grain | phil. conclusion demonstrated. rddheşu bhuñjāneşu daridrā āsate While the rich eat, the poor remain seated.

rddhi [act. rdh] f. abundance, prosperity, wealth; blessing; fortune; success | perfection; supernatural power; magic | myth. np. of rddhi "prosperity", wife of Kubera | bio. bot. Habenaria edgeworthii orchid with yellowish flowers, whose tubers are used in medicine.
rddhiprāpta [prāpta] amnf rddhiprāptā who has attained perfection | soc. refers to the ārya people of pure stock.
rddhiprāptārya |ārya| amnf rddhiprāptāryā jn. ārya superior.
√ rdh v. [4] pr. (rdhyati) v. [5] pr. (rdhnoti) pp. (rddhá) pf. (sam) to grow, to prosper, to succeed — ps. (rdhyáte) to prosper — ca. (ardhayati) to satisfy.
rdhak [related to ardha] adv. separately; apart; one by one.

rbhú |rabh| amnf intelligent; skillful; prudent — m. craftsman, blacksmith; artist | ved. np. of Rbhu, divine craftsman, creator of the chariot | ratha|, father of the wheelwrights [rathakāra] | pl. ṛbhavas ved. the three divine artists: Ŗbhu, Vāja and Vibhvā; they represent the three seasons; they inhabit the solar sphere; they fashioned the bay horses of Indra, and the chariot of the Aśvinau; the gods sent them Agni with the cup of Tvașțā, to make 4 copies of it; they were then admitted to join them as companions of Indra and to drink the soma with him.
rbhukṣin [Rbhu] m. myth. one of the three rbhavas, not. Rbhu | myth. np. of Rbhuksin, epith. of Indra.
rśya var. rṣya m. organic. zoo. antelope cervica pra, male antelope.

rśyaśrnga [śrnga] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the ascetic Rśyaśrnga "(who bears an) Antelope Horn", born from the seed of his father Vibhāṇḍaka absorbed by an antelope; he had a small Horn on his forehead; he spent all his youth as a hermit [vānaprastha] without seeing any woman; a terrible drought having broken out in the Anga country following a transgression committed by King Romapāda, the latter tricked Ráyaárnga out of his hermitage by courtesans to make him cease his penances and thus make the rain fall; he gave him his daughter Sāntā in marriage, in order to restore the dharma; King Daśaratha summoned him for his horse sacrifice; He added to the sacrifice a special offering intended to provide him with sons. tasyarsyaśrigam śirasi rājan | āsīn mahātmanah tenarşyaśṛṅgamityevam tadā sa prathito'bhavat || |Mah.| Sire, this holy man wore an antelope horn on his head; for this reason, he became known as "Antelope Horn".
√ ṛṣ var. arṣ v. [1] pr. (árṣati) aor. [5] (ārṣīt) pp. (ṛṣṭa) ved. to flow, spread; to impregnate — v. [6] pr. (rṣati) to move, push | pierce; stab.

ṛṣabhá [ṛṣ] m. Bull [“that which fertilizes”] | male animal in general | myth. np. of Rṣabha “Bull”, epithet of Nandī | myth. np. of Rṣabha₁ “Male”, one of the 4 master elephants [gajapati] supporting the World | myth. [BhP.] np. of King Rṣabha₂, a form of Vishnu incarnated as the son of Nābhi, symbolizing the perfect devotee; after instructing his 100 sons in the supreme truth, he became a wandering ascetic and traversed the World, naked, with a stone in his mouth to quench his thirst; after placing his eldest son Bharata on the throne, he renounced life and sacrificed his body in a forest fire | lit. [KSS.] np of Mount Rsabha₃, where Naravahanadatta was crowned emperor of the vidyadharās | mus. 2nd note of the Indian octave — ifc. the best of (iic.) ("a Bull among The") — f. ṛṣabhī woman with masculine characteristics | widow.
rṣabhagītā [gītā] f. lit. [BhP.] np of the Ḥṣabhagītā, song of glory to the Lord of Rsabha₂.
rṣabhátara [tara] m. young Bull.
rṣabhatā [tā] f. eminence, superiority. rşabhatva [tva] n. id.
rṣabhadeva [deva] m. cf. ṛṣabhanātha.

rṣabhanātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of rṣabhanātha "Master of the Bull", 1ᵉr mythical tīrthankara; his body is yellow, the Bull is his symbol; also called Adinātha, he had 100 sons, including Bharata₂ and Gommata.

ṛṣi [ṛṣi] m. myth. singer-author of Vedic hymns (which "he spreads"); poet; seer | myth. demiurge; progenitor [prajāpati]; patriarch, old sage; cf. saptarși, devarși, brahmarși, rājarṣi, maharṣi | myth. sage, ascetic, hermit; saint, venerable; The rsayas acquire great powers through their penances; they receive revelation through their vision of the Veda; whoever disturbs their meditations exposes himself to their wrath, even if he is a god; cf. Agasti, Angirā, Aurva, Kakṣīvān, Kaṇva, Kāmanda, Kutsa, Garga, Gālava, Gṛtsamada, Cyavana, Jahnu, Tittiri, Dadhīci, Dīrghatamā, Durvāsā, Devala, De vasthāna, dharma, Nārada, Parāśara, Bharadvāja, Mandu, Matanga, Mārkandeya, Mudgala₁, Mṛkaṇḍa, Medhātithi, Yājñavalkya, Vālmīki, Viśravā, Vyāsa, Sibi. rṣirāśidṛtigranthikrimidhvanibalikaulimauliravikavi kapimunayah gram. The nouns ṛṣi, rāśi, dṛti, granthi, krimi, dhvani, bali, kauli, mauli, ravi, kavi, kapi and muni (are used only in the masculine).
rsika [ka] m. sage of lesser importance | pl. geo. people of the Ŗṣikās, in South India — f. ṛṣikā geo. np. of the Ŗṣikā river.
rsyādi [ādi] n. soc. component of a mantra, including the author [ṛṣi], the meter [chandas], the deity |devata|, the syllable germ |bīja|, the energy |śakti|, the
point [kīlaka] and use [viniyoga].
rsyādinyāsa [nyāsa] m. soc. rite of imposition of the elements of a mantra. 報と ṛṣṭā |pp. ṛṣ| amnf ṛṣṭā issued, launched | pushed.
rṣṭi [act. rṣ] f. spear; sword.
ṛṣya [ṛśya] m. bio. zoo. male antelope.
rsyamūka [mūka] m. [rsyamūkācala] myth. [Rām.] np. of Mount Ŗṣyamūka; there was the hermitage of the sage Matanga | lit. domain of the accompanies
folds [siddha₁] where Naravāhanadatta takes refuge with Prabhāvatī.
rṣyaśṛṅga [śṛṅga] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the young ascetic Ŗṣyaśṛṅga "who carries an antelope horn"; cf. Rśyaśrnga.
rṣvá amnf rṣvā elevated; noble, virtuous; sublime. 雅 r
!kāra [(!)kāra] m. the sound or letter '!'. ए е
e [āi] v. [2] pr. (aiti) imp. (ehi) pp. (eta) pf. (abhi, upa, prati, sam) to approach, to arrive, to come (here). punar e to return.

éka pn. mnf ekā sg. one, the one, unique; alone, solitary, only | a certain, such a | pl. eke some, certain | |ekatāla| mus. rhythmic cycle | tāla | minimal repeating a laghu — n. unit. eke some; certain. ekeṣām according to some. ekaika one by one. eke vadanti some say. ekīkṛ combine, associate, unify. ekībhū combine, come together, unify. eka ... anya ... one ..., another ... eka ... dvitīya ... the first ..., the second ... eka ... para ... one ..., the other ... eke ... eke ... some ..., some ... ekam ca ... aparam ca on the one hand ... on the other hand.
ékakāla | kāla₁ | amnf ekakālā simultaneous. ekakālam only once; once a day.
ekakālatva [tva] n. simultaneity.
ekakūṭa |kūṭa| amnf ekakūṭā arch. is said of a temple with a single sanctuary.

Ekacakra | cakra | amnf Ekacakrā which has only one wheel | Vedic epith. of Surya's chariot — f. eka cakrā geo. |Mah.| np. of the city of Ekacakrā, of the land of the Kīcakās; the Pāṇḍavās lived there incognito, disguised as Brahmins, after the burning of the lacquer palace of Vāraṇāvata; cf. Baka₁.
ekacatvārimsat | catvārimsat | f. 41.
ekacatvāriṃśattama |tama| amnf eka catvārimsattamī ord. 41ᵉ.

ekacitta [citta] amnf ekacittā ["who fixes his attention" absorbed, attentive — n. unanimity; consen sus. ekacittībhū to reach unanimity, to reach a consensus. ekacittībhūya having reached an agreement.
ekacittatā [tā] f. concentration; unanimity. ékajāta | jāta | amnf ekajātā of the same family; born of the same parents. ékajātīya | īya | amnf ekajātīyā of the same species; of the same family.
ékajāti [jāti] amnf ["born only once"] śūdra; opp. dvijāti.
ekatatpara [tatpara] amnf ekatatparā devoted exclusively to.
ekatama |tama| pn. mnf ekatamā one (among several).
ekatara |tara| pn. mnf ekatarā one (of 2) | one among others | unichord musical instrument of the Baul tradition; syn. gopīyantra.
ékatāna | tāna | amnf ekatānā obsessed with an object, absorbed in an occupation; very attentive — m. attention fixed on a single object.
ékatāla [tāla] m. harmony; unison — f. ekatālī metronome.
ekatin [tin] amnf gram. "which has a unique verbal form", definition of the sentence by Kātyāyana.

ekatra [tra] adv. in one; in a single place | in one place; in the same place | on the one hand (corr. with aparatra on the other hand). grahaikatvanyāyaḥ maxim of wiping a single one (soma ladle); it justifies that a specified action of one object actually applies to all: all the cups used in the ritual must be rinsed.
ékatrimśa | trimśa | amnf ekatrimśī ord. 31ᵉ.
ékatrimásat | trimásat | f. pl. 31.
ekatva [tva] n. unity, identity; union, coincidence gram. the singular | state of being alone; solitude, isolation.
ékadamstra | damstra | mr. myth. n.p. of Ekadamstra, epith. of Ganesa "who has only one defense".
ekadanta | danta | mr. myth. n.p. of Ekadanta, epith. of Ganesa "who has only one defense".
ekadā |dā| adv. once, one day; sometimes, occasionally; only once; once upon a time, long ago simultaneously.
ekadiś [diś₂] amnf in the same direction.
ekadeśa [deśa] m. a place; a certain passage; on one side | part (of a whole) | math. factor — amnf ekadeśā at the same place. ekadeśena partially; opp. krtsnena.
ekadeśin |in| amnf ekadeśinī phil. who argues a point of view; who has a partial view of the truth — m. protagonist of a debate.
ekadvyādi [dviādi] iic. math. ["1,2, etc."] natural numbers
ekadvyādilagakriyā [lagakriyā] f. phone. [Vṛttaratnākara] Pascal's triangle; cf. meru prastāra.
ekadhā [dhā] adv. simply; only together, at the same time, at once | in one way.
ékanaksatrá | naksatra | n. astr. lunar asterism with a single star, or whose name appears only once.
ékanavata [navata] amnf ekanavatī ord. 91ᵉ.
ékanavati | navati | f. 91.
ekanavatitama |tama| amnf ekanavatitamī ord. 91ᵉ.

ekanātha [nātha] m. hist. np. of ekanātha, brahmin of Pratisthāna, great-grandson of Bhānudāsa (1533–1599); he left his family to become a disciple of Janārdana Svāmī at Daulātābad, who initiated him into the Vārkarī school of which he became an important poet.
ekanivāsa [nivāsa₁] m. common residence. ekanivāsatah adv. by cohabitation.
ekapañcāśá [pañcāśa] amnf ekapañcāśī 51ᵉ.
ekapañcāśat [pañcāśat] f. 51.
ekapañcāśattama |tama| fnam ekapañcāśattamī ord. 51ᵉ.
ekapatnī [patnī] f. faithful woman |sole wife |pl. ekapatnyas wives of the same man.
ekapatnīka |ka| amnf ekapatnīkā monogamous.
ekapatnīvrata | vrata| amnf ekapatnīvratā who has vowed fidelity to his wife (said not. of Rāma faithful to Sitā).
ekapad [pad₂] m. myth. n.p. of Ekapād "the Unijam be", ithyphallic form of SivaBhairava; cf. Ajai kapād.

ekapada | pada | amnf ekapadī that takes a step | that has only one foot | gram. consisting of a single word — n. a single place | gram. a single word. ekapade adv. immediately, in the heat of the moment.
ekapari | bet | ind. missed by one (not. in the game pañcaka).
ekaparigrahā [parigraha] f. soc. prostitute tied to a single client.

ekapinga | pinga | m. myth. np. of ekapinga, epith. of Kubera "having only one (yellow) eye"; [Rām.] he committed the offense of looking at Pārvatī with his left eye; she burned it and made the other eye yellow.
ekapriyadarśana [priyadarśana] amnf eka priyadarśanī loved by all.
ekaphala | phala | amnf ekaphalā which has the same effect.
ékabhakṣa | bhakṣa | ifc. amnf ekabhakṣā who feeds only on; who eats (iic.) alone.
ékabhāva [bhāva] amnf ekabhāvā unanimous; sincere — m. unity; sincerity.
ékamati [mati] amnf unanimous.
ékamukha [mukha] amnf ekamukhi having a mouth or a head; having a head | with the face turned in the same direction; of the same category.
ekamukhalinga [linga] m. arch. śivalinga bearing engraved the face of Shiva.
ekarasa | rasa | amnf ekarasā who has only one object of affection; who finds pleasure only in one thing or person; faithful, constant | phil. homogeneous.
ekarāj [rāj₂] m. [sg. nom. ekarāt] soc. ["only king"] royal title.
ekarūpa | rūpa | amnf ekarūpā uniform; of the same color or shape — n. unique form. ekarūpatas adv. in a single form; uniformly.

ekarūpatā |tā| f. uniformity; equanimity. udaye savitā rakto raktaścāstamaye tathā | sampattau ca vipattau ca mahatāmekarūpatā || The Sun is red at sunrise, and red at sunset as well; likewise great souls show equanimity in success as in adversity.
ekarūpatva |tva| n. uniformity.
ekarūpya [ya] n. phil. coherence of meaning.
ekarca [rca] amnf ekarcā consisting of a single verse.

Ekalavya [lavya] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Ekalavya "whose (thumb) had to be cut off", young orphan son of a tribal chief [niṣāda] of Mount Raivata₂; he wanted to learn archery, and chose Drona as his instructor, but was rejected by him as a student because of his low birth; he became a master by training alone, revering a clay idol of Drona that he had made; he was noticed by Arjuna by mutilating a dog just enough to prevent it from barking, and surpassed all the princes who came to challenge him; in order not to compromise the supremacy of his student Arjuna, Drona demanded that he mutilate his right thumb; it symbolizes blind obedience to the authority of the master and submission to
duty [dharma] of his caste; [BhP.] fighting alongside King Jarāsandha, he was killed by Kṛṣṇa; this act ultimately caused Kṛṣṇa's accidental death at Jarā₂.
ekavacana [vacana] n. gram. singular.
ekavat [vat] adv. as singular; as if unique.
ekavadbhāva [bhāva] m. gram. collective aggregate of entities, in the singular. ékavarņa [varņa] amnf ekavarņā of a single color; (coat) unspotted — f. ekavarņī musical instrument.
ekavākya [vākya] n. gram. utterance of a sentence; the same sentence — amnf ekavākyā unanimous.
ekavākyatā |tā| f. unanimity | gram. |Mīmāṃsā| syntactic coherence | lit. faithful transmission of texts, not. of the Veda.

ekavākyatva [tva] n. id. ekavākyatvānusamdhānadaśā gram. stage of verifying the coherence of a sentence. ékavimsá vimsa amnf ekavimsī ord. 21° consisting of 21 parts — m. lit. np. of the Ekavimsa stoma. ékavimásat vimásat f. pl. 21.
ékavimsati [vimsati] f. pl. 21; collection of 21 objects.
ekavimśatitama [tama] fanm ekavimásatitamī ord. 21ᵉ.

Ekavīra | vīra | m. myth. Revanta, friend of Indra, once saw Vaikuntha on the horse Uccaihśravā; Lakṣmī was captivated by the beauty of the horse and its rider, and paid no attention to Viṣnu who was speaking to her; the latter exiled her to Earth as a mare, to return only after giving birth to a son as glorious as Viṣṇu himself; there she did penances for 1000 divine years; at her prayer Shiva and Pārvatī interceded with Viṣnu, who descended to Earth in the form of a horse; when Lakṣmī gave birth to a son she returned to Vaikuntha, and the child was adopted by King Satajit under the name of Ekavīra "First Hero"; as he was born of a horse [haya] he is also called Hehaya; he is the ancestor of the Haihayās and not. of Krtavīrya; cf. Vītahavya.
ékaśapha [śapha] amnf ekasaphā bio. soliped, ungulate animal with undivided hoof.
ekaśabda [śabda] m. gram. uniqueness of the meaning of a phonetic realization.
ekaśabdadarśana [darśana] n. gram. viewpoint according to which there is a single word for a given sequence of phonemes, possibly polysemous; opp. anekaśabdadarśana.
ekaśas [śas] adv. one by one.

Ekaśilā [śilā] f. geo. np. of the city [nagara] of Ekaśilā "Monolith", rich fortified capital of the Kākatīyās, carved from a single rock (mod. Waran gal, Telangāna); it was besieged by the Delhi Sultanate, and sacked in 1323 by Prince Ulugh Khan; among its many treasures, the Kohinoor diamond was taken to Delhi; it was recaptured by the nāyaka Kāpaya in 1326, and annexed to the Bah mani Sultanate in 1370.
ekaśriga |śriga| m. myth. unicorn | bd. epith. of Ráyaárnga; its story was transmitted to China by the monk Hiuen Tsiang (7th century).

ekaśesa [śesa] amnf ekaśesā gram. residual mono (process explaining a du. or pl. as a coordinating compound from which only one stem is retained) phon. said of a sandhi replacing two vowels by a single one. ekaśesavrtti vrtti f. gram. the act of expressing the meaning of several words by a single one (like "dogs" for "dogs and female dogs").

ekaśruti | śruti | f. phon. monotonous recitation of the Veda (without accents); this is the mode used for sacrificial rites | gram. absence of accent mark |svara| for class 10 roots |curādi| in the dhātupāṭha. ekaşaşti [şaşti] f. 61.
ékasaptata [saptata] amnf ekasaptatī 71ᵉ.
ékasaptati |saptati| f. 71.
ekāṃśa [aṃśa] m. a single part.
ekākṣa [akṣa] amnf ekākṣā which has only one axis | which has only one eye — m. crow (which is supposed to have only one eye).
ekākṣara [akṣara] amnf ekākṣarā monosylla bique — n. gram. a single syllable; labial monosyl word | the sacred syllable om.
ekākṣarakoṣa [koṣa] m. lit. vocabulary of monosyllabic words; this kind of lexicon is used by poets to facilitate the composition of interlacing
ments | śleṣa |, or to explain esoteric meanings in Tantra; not. np. of the ekākṣarakoṣa of Purușottamadeva.
Ekākṣaranāmamālā [nāmamālā] f. bed. glossary of monosyllabic words | n.p. from the Ekākṣaranāmamālā₁ of Sudhākalaśa Gaṇī | n.p. from the Ekākṣaranāmamālā₂ of Kālidāsa₁.

ekāgra [agra] amnf ekāgrā attentive, concentrated; who has sustained attention on one thing | who has a single goal; absorbed in (loc.) | phil. yogic attention; myth. [Mah.] this is the reason for Arjuna's supremacy as an archer.
ekāgratā [tā] f. phil. perfect mental concentration, necessary for the fixation of thought | dhāraṇā| in yoga, or [bd.] for the contemplation of emptiness [śūnya].
ekāñjali [añjali] m. a handful.
ékādaśan [daśan] num. pers. eleven.
ekādaśadhā [dhā] ind. 11 times | in 11 parts.

ekādaśarudra [Rudra] m. pl. myth. [Mah.] The ekādaśarudrās are the 11 aspects of Rudra; they are the winds or currents of vital energy [prāna], identified with the breaths or principles of immortality |marut|: Mṛgavyādha "Hunter", Sarpa "Sea Serpent", Nirṛti₁ "Calamity", Ajaikapād "One-Legged Guide", Ahirbudhnya "Sea Serpent", Pinākin "Archer", Dahana "Burning", Iśvara "Lord", Kapālī "Skull Bearer", Sthāņu "Pillar", and Bhaga₁ "Fortunate".
ekādeśa |ādeśa| m. gram. |Pāṇini| coalescence of two sounds into one (e.g., in the sandhi between vowels).

ekānta [anta] amnf ekāntā exclusive, absolute |"having only one purpose"| — m. solitary place; single purpose; necessity, exclusivity | phil. devotion to a single object, monotheism. ekāntam var. ekāntena, ekāntāt adv. absolutely, exclusively, completely | invariably, necessarily. ekānte adv. alone, in private; secretly, apart. ekāntatas adv. in solitude | only, exclusively; invariably.
ekāntanaṣṭa [naṣṭa] amnf ekāntanaṣṭā lost forever.
ekāntavāda | vāda | mr. phil. exclusive point of view; opp. anekāntavāda.
ekāpāya [apāya] m. decrease of one.
ekāmra [āmra] m. geo. np. d'ekāmra "The man guier", former name of the site of Bhuvaneśvarī₁.
ekāmrakṣetra | kṣetra | n. geo. n.p. from ekāmrakṣetra "Field of the mango tree", former name of the region of Bhuvaneśvarī₁.
Ekāmreśvara | īśvara | m. geo. np. of Ekāmreśvara, shrine of Shiva located in Kāñcīpura; it is the pañcabhūtasthala associated with the earth element |pṛthivī|.
ekāyaná | ayana | n. narrow path | only conduit to
hold | policy | focus on a single goal.
ekāyanaveda [veda] m. lit. [pañcarātra] hy pothétique unique veda original.

ekārtha [artha] amnf ekārthā gram. of the same meaning, synonym | having only one principal meaning — m. a single and the same purpose | lit. [Daṇḍa] tautology, a poetic fault | doșa₂|. ekārthībhū gram. to agree the meaning of co-denoting words. ekārthībhāvaḥ gram. expression of a single meaning by all the constituents of a compound.
ekārthatā [tā] f. fact of having a single purpose | gram. fact of having a single referent.
ekārthatva [tva] n. id.

ekāvalī [āvalī] f. single row of pearls | lit. figure of style of sequences of predicates where the theme of one clause becomes the object of the next | lit. np. of the ekāvalī, treatise on poetics by Vidyādhara, in kārikā style, with gloss; Mallinātha₁ made a commentary on it.
ekāśīta |aśīta| amnf ekāśītī ord. 81ᵉ.
ekāśīti |aśīti| f. 81.
ekāśītitama |tama| amnf ekāśītitamī ord. 81^ e.
ekāśva |aśva| amnf ekāśvā to a horse. ekāśvo rathaḥ chariot to a horse.
ekāstakā [astakā] f. astr. 8th day after the full moon | soc. not. festival of the month of Maghās.
ekāhá |aha| m. period of a single day.
ékaika [red.] amnf ekaikā one by one; one at a time; just one; both of them; each only once; each. ekaikam adv. one by one.
ekaikaśas |śas| adv. one by one; one after the other, multiplely.
ekoddista | uddista | n. soc. funeral rite | śrāddha | for an unrelated person who recently died; it is celebrated notably on the occasion of bhīsmāstamī.
ekona | ūna | amnf ekonā of which one is missing; (ifc.) minus one (before a number of tens).
ekonavimsati | vimsati | f. 19; syn. ūnavimsati.
ekonasaptati [saptati] f. 69; syn. navasasti.
ekaka [ekaka] amnf ekikā alone of its species, isolated.
ekata [ekata] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of ekata "First", son of Gautama, unworthy brother of Trita; he was transformed into a monkey.
ekatas [adv. eka] adv. on one side; on the one hand (anyatas on the other hand).
ekākín [red. eka] amnf ekākinī all alone; solitary.

ekādaśá [ekādaśan] amnf ekādaśī ord. eleventh — f. ekādaśī astr. the 11th day of a lunar fortnight | soc. it is auspicious, and a day of celebration; it is dedicated to Viṣṇu, and fasted; cf. vaikunthaikādaśī, nirjalaikādaśī; Māndhātā.
ekādaśādya [ādya₂] amnf ekādaśādyā ord. 10th ["which precedes the 11th"].
ekāra [(e)kāra] m. the sound or the letter 'e'.
ekārthī iiv. ekārtha.
ekārthībhāva [bhāva] m. gram. unity of meaning of the constituents of a compound or a secondary derivative authorizing their compositionality.
√ ej v. [1] pr. (ejati) pp. (ejita) pfp. (ejita vya) to move; to tremble — ca. (ejayati) to shake, to make tremble.
ejaya |agt. ca. ej| ifc. amnf ejayā that makes tremble (iic.). kālimejaya that makes tremble Kālī.
eji [ca. ej] v. [10] pr. (ejayati) to shake, to make tremble.
eḍa amnf eḍā deaf; syn. badhira.
edamūka | mūka | amnf edamūkī deafmute.
eṇa mf eṇī bio. zoo. Antelope cervicapra, an tilope noire (adulte); cf. harina.
eṇamada | mada | m. musc.
eta [pp. e] amnf etā f. enī who emerges, who runs away | variegated — m. organic. suede.
state iic. etad.
etatsamīpa |samīpa| n. presence of this one.
states [abl. etad] ind. of that; of these two; death.

etád var. etat pn. dem. nm eṣa₁ f. eṣā this, this, this one (close to the speaker); here is | what precedes; what has just happened; what has just been mentioned | (rarely) what follows — adv. thus, then; first. etad A idam B for what precedes A, for what follows B. tadetat satyam phil. |MO.| this very thing is the truth.
etadartham | artha| adv. for this purpose, to this end; thus, therefore.

etadyoni | yoni | amnf of this origin. etadyonīni bhūtāni sarvānīty upadhāraya | aham kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā || [BhG.] Realize that all these creatures are from this source; I am the origin of the totality of this universe and its dissolution.
etam [acc. eṣa₁] ind. ce.
etayos [g. du. etad] ind. of these two — loc. du. in these two.
etárhi [etad] adv. nowadays; now; at this moment | |correl. of yarhi| then.
etavya [pfp. [3] i] amnf etavyā which must or can go.
etasmāt [abl. etad] ind. of that.
etasmin [loc. etad] ind. in that.
etasmai [dat. etad] ind. for that one.
etasya [g. etad] ind. of that.
etasyām [loc. eṣā] ind. en celle — abl. de celle.
etasyās [g. eṣā] ind. of that.
etādṛś [etaddṛś₂] amnf such; such as; thus done; in this way — amn etādṛśa f. etādṛśī id.
etān |acc. pl. state| ind. these.
etābhis [i. pl. eṣā] ind. by these.
etābhyas [dat. pl. eṣā] ind. for these — abl. pl. of these.
etābhyām [i. du. etad] ind. by these two — g. du. of these two — abl. du. of these two.

etāvat [etadvat] amnf etāvatī also large, of such extent; of such quality; of this kind, such — adv. as much; to such an extent. etāvān eva puruso yaj jāyātmā prajā A complete family man, with wife and children.
ete [nom. pl. etad] ind. ces — nom. acc. du. ces deux (f. ou n.).
etena [i. etad] ind. by this. etena ... vivakṣitaḥ gram. by this we mean...
etebhyas [dat. pl. etad] ind. for these — abl. pl. death.
eteṣām [g. pl. etad] ind. of these two.
eteșu [loc. pl. etad] ind. in these.
was [i. pl. etad] ind. by these.

vice [nom. du. etad] ind. these two. dh v. [1] pr. r. (edhate) pp. (edhita) pf. (sam) to grow, increase, augment; to rejoice; to prosper, succeed | to gain ground, expand (fire, passion); to swell (waters); to intensify; to become insolent — ca. (edhayati) to make prosper; to bless.
édha [obj. indh] m. combustible, firewood fage, log — act. ifc. conflagration of (iic.) — n. edhas combustible.
edhita [pp. edh] amnf edhitā increased, augmented, extended; full of (i.).
ena pn. 3rd person. mn enad f. enā₁ cl. after ayam, eṣa |sg. acc. enam, i. enena; of. acc. enau, g. loc. enayos; pl. acc. enān] he, him, the (anaphoric, nominal, unstressed).
enad [n. ena] pn. 3rd person. n. cl. after ayam, eșa |sg. acc. enat, i. enena; of. acc. ene, g. loc. enayos; pl. acc. enāni he, the, in (anaphoric).
enas [abstr. in] n. fault, sin; act of violence, crime | evil, misfortune, calamity.
enasvat |vat| amnf enasvatī guilty; criminal.
enā₁ [f. ena] pn. 3rd pers. f. cl. after ayam, eșa [sg. acc. enām, i. enayā; du. acc. ene, g. loc. enayos; pl. acc. enās she, the (anaphoric).
enā₂ adv. in this way, thus; then, at this time | here; there. enā paras moreover. para enā beyond here; beyond (i.). yátra ... enā from there ... to.
enī [f. eta] f. variegated | antelope.
ebhis [i. pl. ayam] ind. by these.
ebhyas [abl. pl. ayam] ind. of these — dat. to these.

emuṣá |am| amnf emuṣā ved. having gone towards — m. emūṣa ved. |RV.| np. of the celestial boar emūṣa, hero of a particular creation myth; he guarded the nourishing dish of rice and milk |odana| behind a mountain; Indra struck the mountain with his arrow to release the milk, at the instigation of Visnu | myth. [SB.] divine boar who performed the "cosmogonic dive" to retrieve the Earth from the bottom of the Waters; later identified with the avatar Varāha.
eyá form of possessives.
er [āīr] ca. (erayati) ved. to bring, to bring; to procure — ca. r. (erayate) to procure, to obtain.
eraṇḍa m. organic. bot. Ricinus communis, castor oil.
ervāru cf. urvāru.
elavālu |telugu| n. bio. fragrant bark of the kapittha.
elā f. bio. bot. Elettaria cardamomum, a large herbaceous plant with palmate leaves; its fruit is cardamom — n. elāka id. — f. elākā small cardamom. elālatāvanam grove of cardamom vines.

evá [āiva] part. cl. only, however; just, hardly, only | even, still | precisely, precisely, exactly; in fact, really, quite | for (part. often expletive); just | participle or abs.) at the very moment when; immediately after having | (negation) really not. caiva also. eva ca and likewise. jīvaiva adv. all living things. tatraiva adv. right here. tathaiva adv. likewise, also; exactly so. naiva adv. not even; in no way. etad eva precisely that one. eka eva completely alone. saiva the same, himself. sarvaiva adv. all absolutely. nāstyeva adv. certainly not. anda eva blind immediately. vasudhā eva the whole Earth. mṛtyur eva certain death. pumāmsa eva only men. mūsika eva krtah changed into a mere mouse. cintayann eva just when he was thinking. uktam eva mayā just when I tell you. lokaih kimcid vaktavyam eva people will surely say something. tvamevāham You are none other than myself (said by Sarasvatī to Kālidāsa, surprised that she had declared Dandī the best poet).
evam iic. evam.
evámyuktam | yukta | ind. in this way.
evámrūpa [rūpa] amnf evamrūpā of this form, of this kind.
evamvāc | vāc | amnf speaking like this.
evamvid [vid₃] amnf knowing this; fully aware of the facts.
evamvidha | vidha | amnf evamvidhā in such a way, such.
evaṃbhūta | bhūta | amnf evaṃbhūtā tel.

evam [eva] adv. thus; like that; in this way | certainly, assuredly. evam uktvā having thus spoken. evam evaitat it is so. evam astu var. evam bhavatu so be it. astyevam it is so. maivam not at all! yadyevam if it is so. kim evam why? what is it? ya evam veda who knows this. yathā ... evam ... so that ...
evamartha [artha] amnf evamarthā for this use, of such use; proper for this, which serves this purpose; intentional.
evamarthīya |īya| amnf evamarthīyā intended for this use.
evamādi |ādi| m. this and others.
eṣa₁ |m. etad| pn. dem. m. this, that; this one (near); that which precedes — f. eṣā this; that one. ্দ éṣa₂ [agt. iṣ₁] amnf eṣā ifc. who seeks (iic.) — act. m. search, quest — f. eṣā wish.

eṣaṇa [agt. iṣ₁] amnf eṣaṇī who wishes, who desires — act. n. desire; solicitation; the act of imploring, of begging — m. jn. appropriate attitude for begging for food — f. eṣaṇā desire; soll citation, request | impulse | med. natural instinct, temperament; Caraka distinguishes three of them: prāṇa, dhana and paraloka.
eṣām |g. pl. ayam| ind. of these.
eṣin [agt. iṣ₁] ifc. amnf eṣinī who seeks, who desires (iic.).
eşu |loc. pl. ayam| ind. in these.
estavya [pfp. [3] is₁] amnf estavyā desirable; that which should be sought.
esyat [pfu. i] amnf esyantī imminent, future.
ehá |agt. īh| amnf ehā who desires; who wishes haite — n. ehas anger; emulation, rivalry.
ehi [imp. e] ind. (hortative particle) approach! ehi manye go, I think. ehi manye odanam bhoksyáse I suppose you will eat the rice (ironic, when the rice has already been eaten).
ehisvāgatā [svāgata] f. ["enter, welcome"] tradition of hospitality.
ehīha [iha] n. manual labor (characterized by the words: come here).
ai
aikadhya [*ekadhāya] n. uniqueness of time; the act of occurring only once. aikadhyam all at once; in one go; together.
aikamatya [*ekamatiya] n. unanimity — amnf aikamatyā of the same opinion, in agreement. asminvisaye sarvesām tesāmaīkamatyam they are all in agreement on this point.
aikāntika [*ekāntaka] amnf aikāntikī necessary; absolute; exclusive — m. necessity; exclusivity. aikāntikam adv. necessarily.
aikāntya [*ekāntaya] n. necessity; uniqueness; exclusivity.
aikāra [(ai)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'ai'.

Aikya [*ekaya] n. unity, harmony; coherence; equality, identity | phil. identity of the human soul with the divine absolute | aggregate; sum, union | math. Product of the length and depth of excavations | soc. np. of the svayaṃbhūliṅga Aikya at Kudālasaṃgama, where Basavaṇṇa and Siva are identified in Sangamanātha.
aikṣvāká [*ikṣvāku] amnf aikṣvākī myth. descendant of ikṣvāku — m. myth. epith. of the line of the kings of Ayodhyā, of the solar line |sūryavaṃśa|; |Rām.| not. epith. of Daśaratha — m. aiksvāku id.
aicchika [*icchāika] amnf aicchikā op tionnel; arbitrary | at will.
aiṇa [*eṇa] amnf aiṇā relating to the black antelope (male) — amn aiņeya f. aiņeyā id. (fe melle).
Aitareya [*itaraīya] m. myth. n.p. of Aitareya, patr. of Mahidāsa, author of the eponymous brāhmaṇa of the Rgveda | bed. n.p. of the Aitareyabrāhmaṇa and the Aitareyopanișad, attributed to Aitareya.
Aitareyabrāhmaṇa [brāhmaṇa] n. bed. n.p. of the Aitareyabrāhmaṇa of the Rgveda; he describes not. the aindramahābhiṣeka.
aitareyāranyaka |āranyaka| n. bed. n.p. of the Aita reyāranyaka. aitareyopanişad [upanişad] f. bed. n.p. of the Aitareyopanisad, attributed to Aitareya.
aitihāsika [*itihāsáika] m. soc. storyteller of old legends | phil. historical point of view of the Veda.
aitihya [*itihaya] n. oral tradition; traditional instruction | legend; belief; rumor.

aindrá [*Indra] amnf Aindrī myth. relating to Indra; similar to Indra; derived from Indra — m. gram. school of grammar prior to Pāṇini; [HC.] Śiva ended it by instructing Pāṇini — n. astr. the nakṣatra Jyeṣṭhā — f. Aindrī myth. np. of Aindrī, mother goddess personifying the power [śakti] of Indra.

aindramahābhiṣeka [mahābhiṣeka] m. soc. "great anointing of Indra", consecration ceremony of a king; [AB.] King Anga₁ gave his officiant 2 million cows, 88000 horses, 10000 slave girls and 10000 elephants.
aindrajāla [*indrajāla] n. magic, witchcraft, illusionism; it is one of the 64 arts [kalā].
aindrajālika [ika] amnf aindrajālikī relating to magic; gifted with magic — mr. magic. aindrajālikavidyākovidah m. expert in magical arts.
aindrābārhaspatyá [*indrābṛhaspati ya] amnf aindrābārhaspatyā myth. which concerns Indra and Brhaspati.
Aindri [*Indrai] m. myth. descendant of Indra myth. [Mah.] np. of Aindri, epithet of Arjuna "son of Indra".
aim part. phil. [Tantra] sound of vāgbhavabīja, bījamantra of evocation of Sarasvatī.
Airāvaṇa cf. airāvata.

airāvata [*irāvata] m. myth. np. of airāvata or Airāvaņa "Produced by the primordial ocean", or "son of Irāvatī₂", three-headed white elephant; born from the churning of the sea of milk [kṣīrodamathana]; former chief of the dragons [nāga], it is the mount of Indra (post-Vedic); it is sometimes assimilated to the rainbow; it is the diggaja of the East; cf. Aryaka, Kauravya, Dvipendra, Suragaja | var. airāvaņa id.
airāvateśvara |īśvara| m. geo. np. of the Cola temple of airāvateśvara (12th century), in Darasuram (modern Tamil Nadu).
aiśa [*īśa] amnf aiśā phil. derived from Shiva, similar to Shiva | divine, supreme.
aiśya [*īśaya] n. supremacy, power.
aiśvara [*īśvara] amnf aiśvarā powerful, sovereign, majestic.
aiśvarayoga [yoga] m. phil. [yoga] ritual spiritual realization by way of identification with the inner form of God.
aiśvarya [*īśvaraya] n. grandeur, majesty; sovereignty, empire; supremacy | phil. | yoga | superhuman power, an aṣṭasiddhi.
aiśvaryamatta | matta| amnf aiśvaryamattā drunk with power.
aisámas adv. This year; in the current year.
aihika [*ihaika] amnf aihikī of this right, from here; of this world; local; temporal. om cf. om.
oká [agt. uc] m. refuge, asylum — n. ókas house, dwelling; at home; refuge.
okāra [(o)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'o'.
ogha [vah₁] m. flow, rapid current; multitude, mass.

ójas [abstr. vaj] n. force, energy, power; splendor, majesty | med. vital energy | lit. luxury; vigorous style of poetry |kāvyaguṇa|, com bearing complex compound words and the use of retroflex consonants | lat. augustus.
ojasvin |wine| amnf ojasvinī robust, strong, vigorous.
ojodā [dā₁] amnf which gives energy; fortifying.
ojiṣṭha [super. ugra] amnf ojiṣṭhā the strongest, the most powerful.
ojīyas [compar. ugra] amnf ojīyasī stronger, more powerful.
odra [telugu] m. geo. name of the country and people of the Odra (mod. Orissa); cf. Utkala | pl. odrās ses inhabitants.
odradeśa | deśa | mr. geo. n.p. from odradeśa (mod. Orissa).
oḍhra var. oḍra m. geo. name of the country and people Odhra (mod. Orissa).
odhramagadha [magadha] m. du. geo. the Eastern region (odra and magadha).
ota [pp. āvā] amnf otā intertwined; braided; sewn.
otaprota [prota] amnf otaprotā sewn lengthwise and widthwise.
otsūryám [āutsūraya] adv. ved. until sunrise.
odaná [obj. und] mn cooked rice (in water or milk); opp. grain rice |taṇḍula| | porridge, (rice) gruel.
odanapac | pac₁ | amnf | sg. nom. odanapak | who cooks rice.
odanápāṇinīya [pāṇinīya] m. food grammarian ["who studies Pāṇini for the sole purpose of earning a plate of rice".
odanapinda | pinda | m. cooked rice ball.
odanavat [vat] amnf odanavatī provided with cooked rice.

opaśá [upaśī] m. cushion, pillow | plume | braid of hair — n. support. om part. phil. sacred syllable Om which can be divided into the sounds 'a', 'u' and 'm', and sometimes considered to symbolize the trinity of Brahmā, Vișnu and Shiva; om is the primordial manifestation of the Word, origin of divine power [śakti]; [Vedānta] the sound 'a' corresponds to the waking state [jāgrat], the sound 'u' to dreaming [svapna], the 'm' to deep sleep [suṣupti], and the silence that follows to the 4th state [turīya] of liberation; pronounced before a mantra, it expresses that the reciter knows its meaning; the Tantric tradition substitutes the bījamantra 'hrīm' for it; cf. akṣara, praṇava, udgītha | yes (solemn, in ritual). omityetadakṣaramidam sarvam [MU.] This syllable Om Is all this. om itīdaṃ sarvam [TU.] all this world Is but Om. om tat sat (mantra) So be it. om manipadme hum bd. "O you who bear the jewel and the lotus," Buddhist invocation [mantra] invoking Avalokiteśvara in her feminine form Manipadmā in the vocative; it is called the 6-syllable formula [vidyāṣaḍakṣarī] (often incorrectly explained as locative tatpurușa "the jewel Is in the lo tus").
omkāra [kāra] m. phon. pronunciation of the syllable om; letter representing it; cf. māṇdūkyopaniṣad.

Omkāreśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of Omkāreśvara, one of the 12 radiant signs of Shiva [jyotirlinga], established on an island of the Narmadā, in Madhya Pradesh, at the confluence with the Kāverī₁, 60 km southeast of Indore, an important place of pilgrimage [tīrtha]; it is said that it was established as an earth linga |pārthiva| by Mount Vindhya, humiliated by Nārada for not having the grandeur of Mount Meru, in order to pray to Shiva to become the greatest mountain on earth; granted, it grew until it obstructed the Sun; The gods implored Shiva to end the burning of the earth, and he sent Agasti who demanded that Vindhya bow down to his wise step, and remain bowed down until his return, which never came; the surrounding country [pañcakrośī] is called Omkāratripurī "Triple City of the Sacred Syllable", comprising Brahmapurī, Viṣṇupurī and Sivapurī.
omkrta [krta] amnf omkrtā accompanied by om.
oman m. favor; protection | óman friend, protector.

aurva [*ūrua] m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] aurva "Born from the thigh" or Urva, son of Cyavana and Aruṣī; the Bhārgavās brahmins having been made rich by Kṛtavīrya, they aroused the jealousy of the kṣatriyās who oppressed them, and they had to take refuge in caves; there, Aruṣī who was pregnant tried to hide her son in her thigh, but was denounced, captured, and from her thigh came out aurva, so radiant that he blinded the kṣatriyās; they had to prostrate themselves before him in order to regain their sight; aurva did penances such that the whole World began to burn; The spirits [pitaras] begged him to stop and Aurva put the ardor of his penance to the bottom of the ocean like the inextinguishable underwater fire Baḍavāgni; he helped King Sa gara regain his throne thanks to the āgneyāstra; he is the father of 100 sons, including Rcīka.

ka₁ |m. kim| pn. m. |pl. nom. ke| interr. who? Which? | lat. quis; ang. who; all. wer; fr. qui. kānicitad ... kānicitad ... some ... others ... |n.|. kānicid ... kānicid ... id. yat kim ca any, anything. yasyai kasyai ca devatāyai to any deity whatsoever. kecana some; a few. ko 'pi someone, a certain; something, I don't know. Which. ko nāma who then? ko nu who really? ko vā who could? na ko 'pi nothing, nobody. kah svid anyone. ko 'yam āyāti who comes here? ko harim nindet who could blame Hari? kān kān which of them? What could the opposing archers do against me? How could you run against me? Which book should be read by whom? Whose son is he? It is not known whose son he is.

ka₂ m. myth. epith. of Ka "him", the Creator Prajāpati — n. joy, happiness | water | head | math. symb. the number 1. kasya paridadāmi soc. I entrust (it) to Prajāpati (formula pronounced during the upanayana).

kaṭapayādi [ṭapaya] m. math. coding of numbers by phonemes, attributed to Vararuci₁; the kādinava series 'ka' ... 'ña' represents 1,2, ..., 9,0, the tādinava series 'ta' ... 'na' also, the pādipañca series 'pa' ... 'ma' the numbers 1 to 5, the yādyasta series 'ya' ... 'ha' the numbers 1 to 8; vowels code 0; by this coding every syllable codes a number, only the last consonant counts; successive syllables of a word count the powers of 10; thus jaya gives 8+1×10 = 18, the number of books of the Mah. and of sections of the Gītā; This coding is also used in Carnatic music to determine the scale of a musical mode |rāga|. °ক ka form of the agt. | ifc. after s. of kinship in r | ifc. m. of a theme in ī | diminutive.

kaṃsá mn drinking utensil; goblet, cup (in metal) | (collective) utensils (in metal); brass, bronze — m. myth. |Mah.| np. of the cruel Kamsa, son of a demon with the features of Ugrasena, king of Mathurā; he married Asti and Prāpti; he embodied the asura Kālanemi, and Nārada had prophesied to him that he would be killed by a son of his cousin De vakī; he imprisoned Devakī and Vasudeva he had his first 6 children killed, but the 7th, Balarāma, escaped [Saṃkarṣaṇa] by being transferred by Magic |Yogamāyā| into the belly of Rohiņī; On the 8th, Krishna, incarnating Vishnu, was miraculously abducted by Vasudeva and secretly raised by the shepherd king Nanda and his wife Yaśodā; later Krishna dethroned and killed him; cf. Asti — f. kaṃsā myth. |BhP.| np. of Kaṃsā, sister of Kaṃsa.
Kamsavadha | vadha | m. lit. np. of the Kamsavadha "Slaying of Kaṃsa", poem by Kṛṣṇa Seṣa₂ written for Govārdhanadhāri, son of Ţoḍara Malla.

kaca m. hair | scar; stitching; strip of fabric, hem | myth. np. of kaca "with the beautiful hair", eldest son of Brhaspati; he was of great beauty, and the favorite of the gods; [Mah.] the gods wanted to know the secret of immortality [samjīvanī] that Sukra used to bring demons [asura] back to life; kaca became Sukra's pupil for 1000 years, whose daughter, the beautiful Devayānī, fell in love with him; the demons [asura] killed him while he was tending his flock, but Devayānī begged her father to resurrect him; the demons killed him again, and made a paste of his body which they threw into the sea; Sukra resurrected him again; the demons ground him into powder, and made Śukra drink it mixed with wine; Śukra then gave him the secret of immortality, so that he could be reborn from his stomach, and in turn give him life; Sukra then forbade the brahmins to drink the deceptive wine; when his apprenticeship was finished, kaca took leave of Sukra, but refused to take Devayānī as his wife "because he had become like her brother"; she cursed him for not being able to use for himself the art of samjīvanī, which he nevertheless taught to the gods.

kacchapajātaka [jātaka] n. bd. story of the tortoise, told by the Buddha; in a previous life he was the chaplain Takkāriya of the verbose king of Kāśī, whom he taught to speak only at the appropriate time; a tortoise lived in the Himalayas; it made friends with two wild geese, who offered to show it a golden cave on Mount Citrakūta; they would transport it through the air by having it hold a stick between its teeth, it would only have to remain silent during the journey; which they did; above Benares, some children exclaimed at the sight of them; the tortoise could not refrain from calling them importunate scoundrels, dropped the stick and crashed in the courtyard of the royal palace; The king asked the reason, and Takkāriya explained that the cause of her downfall had been that she had spoken unwisely, and that sometimes silence is golden. ক ভ্ ন kacchū [kas] f. scabies; skin disease; itching | kacchu id.

kañcuka [kañcuka] m. jacket, leotard, horn set; breastplate; garment; cover | organic. molt of a snake | phil. | śaiva | limiting envelope; there are six: niyati (limitation of space), kāla₁ (limitation of time), rāga (limitation of attachment), vidyā (limitation of knowledge), kalā (limitation of action), and māyā (limitation of individuality). asti grīvā śiro nāsti dvau bhujau karavarjitau | sītāharaṇasāmarthyo na rāmo na ca rāvaṇaḥ || [SRBh.] He has a neck but no head, two arms without hands, is fit to remove Sitā (to protect from the cold) but is neither Rāma nor Rāvaņa (riddle [prahelikā] of kañcuka answer).

kaṇādarahasya |rahasya| n. bed. n.p. from the kaṇādarahasya "Secret doctrine of kaṇāda", nyāyavaiśeṣika manual due to Saṃkara₂ Miśra.
kánapa m. mace.
kaṇika [kaṇaika] m. grain, ear (of wheat) | drop; small particle — f. kanikā ear of wheat | drop; small particle; small spot | meal of dried grains.
kaṇin [kaṇain] ifc. amnf kaṇinī carrying particles of (iic.) (snow).
Kane, ind., in ardent desire.
kaṇehan [kaṇehan₁] v. [2] pr. (kaṇehanti) abs. (kanehatya) to satisfy an ardent desire ad libi tum. kanehatya payah pibati he drinks from the bed to his heart's content.
kanta m. thorn.

kantakāra | kāra | amnf kantakārī thorny — f. kantakārī bio. bot. Solanum xanthocarpum, a spiny nightshade with purple flowers and yellow fruits; this medicinal plant, used against coughs, is one of the 5 small roots | hrasvapañcamūla | ; syn. duḥsparśa. কত্বক kántaka | kantaka | m. thorn, splinter; point, needle; sting, edge | rebel, bandit, enemy | acute pain.
kántakavat |vat| amnf kantakavatī which bears thorns | bristly, covered with erect hairs.
kantakavrntākī [vrntākī] f. bio. bot. Solanum jac quini, small spiny solanaceous plant with purple flowers and yellow fruits, used in medicine; syn. kantakāra.
kantakaśodhana [śodhana] n. lit. np. from the Kantakaśodhana "Punishment by suffering", 4th book of the Arthaśāstra.
kantakoddhāra | uddhāra | m. removal of a thorn or splinter.
kantaki iic. kantakin.
kantakikṣīrin [kṣīrin] m. pl. thorny plants and succulent plants.
kaṇṭakitá [kaṇṭakaita] amnf kaṇṭakitā thorny, prickly; full of thorns | bristling; horrified.
kaṇṭakin [kaṇṭakain] amnf kaṇṭakinī thorny, prickly — m. thorny plant.
kaṇṭhá m. neck, throat.
kanthatālavya [tālavya] amnf kanthatālavyā phon. gutturalopalatal (said of the vowels e, ai).
kanthadaghna [daghna] amnf kanthadaghnā f. kaṇṭhadaghnī who has (water) up to her neck.
kanthabhūṣaṇa [bhūṣaṇa] n. ["throat ornament" | necklace | refers to a highly regarded poem. satām kanthabhūṣaṇam (poem) adorning the throats of scholars.
kanthastha [stha] amnf kanthasthā ["in the throat" | said of memorized knowledge, judged superior to knowledge read in a book [granthastha]; syn. mu khastha | (text) learned by heart.
kanthābharana |ābharana| n. necklace.
kanthosthya [osthya] amnf kanthosthyā phon. gutturalolabial (said of the vowels o, au).
kanthe [loc. kantha] iic.

kanthekāla | kāla₁ | amnf kanthekālī who has a black throat; syn. kālakaṇṭha — m. myth. epith. of Siva. কত্তা kanthya [kanthaya] amnf kanthyā relating to the throat | phone. ["pronounced in the throat"] guttu ral — m. velar or guttural (postpalatal) phoneme (k, kh, g, gh, n) — ifc. who has (iic.) in the throat.
kaṇḍana [act. kaṇḍ] n. winnowing; the act of grinding — f. kandanī grain mortar.
kaṇḍarā f. med. tendon | vein, artery.

kaṇḍikā [agt. kaṇḍ] f. kaṇḍikā lit. Vedic stanza, consisting of a first line | pratīka | ending with the half-pause [daṇḍa], followed by a second line |anūka| ending with the pause |pūrṇavirāma| marked by the double daṇḍa; the pratīka is short (on average 8 syllables), and may interrupt the first sentence; it serves as an incipit. কত্ত্ব kaṇḍu [kaṇḍu] mf itch — ifc. violent desire to (iic.) — f. kandū itch, pruritus — v. [11] pr. (kaṇḍūyati) (se) gratter — v. [11] pr. r. (kandūyate) déitcher. kandūkr irritate, causate pruritus. kandūjus sentir une itche, une pruritus.
kaṇḍūti [ti] f. itch | (figuratively) sexual desire (for a woman).
kaṇḍūmat |mat| amnf kaṇḍūmatī which itches.
kaṇḍūyā [ya] f. itching; tickling.

kaṇḍvādi [ādi] m. gram. [Kaumudī] "which begins with kaṇḍū", designates the [gaṇa] class of nominal verbs. কण্ব káṇva m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Kaṇva₁, son of Medhātithi, author of Vedic hymns; his āśrama on the banks of the Mālinī was a place of peace; he is husband of Gautamī and adoptive father of Sakuntalā | myth. np. of Kaṇva₁ Kāśyapa | hist. np. of the Kanva dynasty, founded by Vāsudeva₂ around 71 BC; it succeeded the Sunga dynasty — n. sin — v. [11] pr. r. (kaṇvāyate) to commit a sin.
kánvatama |tama| m. Kanva in person; a true Kanva.
kataka m. bio. bot. Strychnos potatorum, a shrub with orange fruits that have medicinal properties; the powder from its seeds is used to purify water, and it is used to coat the inside of jars.
katama |super. ka₁| pn. mn interr. which one? who? — f. katamā which one? katamaś cana none (in negative sentence). katamo 'pi id. yatamát katamác ca any one.

katara [compar. ka₁] pn. mn interr. which one (of the two)? — f. katarā which one (of the two)? kataratas on which of the two sides? kataro bhavatoh paṭuh which of you two is ma lin? nakataroścana neither of the two. ° কনা katā in a Navyanyāya compound, expresses the suffix tā after a bahuvrīhi compound.

káti [kim] pn. pers. num. [pl. nom. acc. voc. kati, i. katibhis, dat. abl. katibhyas, g. katīnām, loc. katișu interr. how many? how many? | lat. quot; fr. daily. katyapi a few, several. bhavān kati kadalīphalāni krīnāti how many ba nanes do you want to buy?
katicit [cid₁] pn. pers. num. some, several — adv. often. katicit stutah often celebrated.

katipaya [kati] amnf katipayī a few, some; a certain number, several — n. ifc. a little, a small bit of (iic.) | pl. katipayās a few. katipayāt adv. with difficulty, barely. katipayena adv. id. udaśvitkatipayam a little udaśvit. katipayenāhargaņena after a few days.
√কল্থ katth v. [1] pr. r. (katthate) pp. (katthita) pf. (vi) to boast, to glorify oneself | to praise | to blame, to despise. katthase satyavādī |Rām.| You boast of speaking the truth.
katthita [pp. katth] amnf katthitā van tard — n. boasting. ° কবে katva in a compound Navyanyāya, ex prime the suffix tva after a compound bahuvrīhi.

√ kath [vn. katham] v. [10] pr. (katháyati) impft. (akathayat) aor. [3] (acakathat) pp. (kathita) pf. (anu, pra, sam) ["to give the how"] to say, to tell, to explain (acc.) (to (dat.)) | to converse with (i.) | to speak to, to call (dat.); to admit — ps. (kathyate) to be considered as, to recognize oneself as | ang. quote. uttaram kath tell the answer, give the solution. kathaya me kathām tell me the story. কথক kathaka [agt. kath] amnf kathikā who tells, who recites — m. narrator; storyteller; reciter | speaker of a monologue; principal actor | myth. member of Skanda's retinue.
kathana [act. kath] n. act of telling, story.
kathanīya [pfp. [2] kath] amnf ka thanīyā which deserves to be told; to be mentioned.

kathám adv. interr. how? in what way? katham nu adv. how then? katham etat how is that? katham rūpa of what form? kathaṃ vīrya of what strength? kathaṃkathā var. kathaṅkathā | Kathā₁ | f. question and answer. kathamcana var. kathancana | cana | adv. somehow; however well, little. kathamcit var. kathamcit | cid₁ | adv. barely, with difficulty; somehow.
kathamapi [api] adv. barely, with difficulty; somehow. candram kathamapi paśyāmi I can barely make out the Moon. katham kathamapi muktaḥ he escaped by the skin of his teeth.
kathaṃbhūta [bhūta] amnf kathaṃbhūtā of what kind? how did this happen?
kathambhūtinī [in] f. lit. refers to a method of teaching by questions and answers; cf. khandānvaya.
kathayitavya [pfp. [3] kath] amnf kathayitavyā which deserves to be told (to (dat.)); to be mentioned. idam tvayā mahyam kathayitavyam you should have told me about it.

Kathā₁ |obj. kath| f. explanation, discourse; narrative, History (the "how" of an event); tale, fable, deed | the act of speaking about; interview, conversation; recitation; debate | [kathāsaritsāgara] lit. np. of Kathā, the Great History. kā Kathā what can be said of (g. loc.)? all the more so; not to mention. kathīkṛ reduce to a mere tale.
Kathā₂ [ka₁thā] ind. ved. why? how? (for katham). yathā Kathā ca in one way or another; by whatever means.
kathākusuma [kusuma] n. selected tale | lit. np. from the kathākusuma, a selection of 25 Tales; its author is Pandit Ambikādatta Vyāsa (1858–1900).
Kathākusumadvāṣaṣṭi [dvāṣaṣṭi] f. bed. n.p. from the Kathākusumadvāṣaṣṭi “62 Selected Tales” by Ra sarājaviracitā.
kathākusumasaurabha [saurabha] n. lit. np. from kathākusumasaurabha "perfumes of the bouquet of Tales", which presents the 25 Tales of kathākusuma in 9 forms, for the purpose of learning Sanskrit.

kathākeli [keli] m. np. of kathākeli, a style of ritual dance-drama from Kerala, accompanied by drums; the plays are in manipravala; it dates from the 17th century. kathāchala var. kathāchala [chala] n. semblance of history, cover; teaching disguised as a fable.
kathāpīṭha |pīṭha| n. lit. |"origin of the Great History" first book of the kathāsaritsāgara. kathāpravacana pravacana n. recitation/explanation of texts.
kathāpravacanakāra [kāra] amnf kathāpravacanakārī traveling storyteller.
kathāpravacanaparamparā [paramparā] f. tradition of oral transmission of texts.
kathāmātra [mātra] n. lit. ["just the Story"] simple plot of a work, without its stylistic devices.
kathāmukha [mukha] n. lit. prologue of a tale | not. second section [lambaka] of the kathāsaritsāgara.
kathāvatāra [avatāra] m. bed. incarnation of Great History.

kathāsaritsāgara [saritsāgara] m. lit. np. from kathāsaritsāgara "Ocean of Rivers of Tales", version of the Brhatkathā in Sanskrit by Somadeva Bhatta, composed between 1063 and 1081 to entertain Queen Sūryamatī; this collection of Tales of 24000 verses inspired the Tales of the Arabian Nights; it contains not. the Vetālapañcavimśatikā; it is divided into 18 sections | lambaka | and 124 chapters | taramga |.
kathodghāta [udghāta] m. lit. [theatre] opening of a play by a character who takes up the words of the prologue by the sūtradhara.
kathita [pp. kath] amnf kathitā said, mentioned, recounted — n. story.
kad |n. ka₁| iic. gives a pejorative meaning.
káduṣṇa [uṣṇa] amnf kaduṣṇā lukewarm — n. lukewarmness.

kadamba [Tamil] m. bio. bot. Nauclea cadamba, kadamba tree with dense, spherical, orange flowers, very fragrant, blooming with the arrival of the rains; it is a Rubiaceae; myth. it was on a kadamba that Krishna hung the garments of the cowherds [gopi] who were bathing; the vrksasthala of the temple of Minaksi Sundareshvara is a kadamba; tantr. its flower is associated with the cult of Lohitaya; lit. [Aryabhatia] the Earth is compared to its flower; syn. nipa | astr. ecliptic pole var. kadamba hist. np. of the kadamba or kaḍamba dynasty which reigned in Karṇāṭa (345– 525); it was founded by King Mayūraśarmā; its capital was VaijayantīVanavāsī; Jainism was encouraged there; a later dynasty of the same name reigned in the 12th century; cf. Kāmadeva₁ — n. mul titude, collection, grouping, troop, flock (plural form).
kadambaka |ka| n. the kadamba flower; it is sacred to the Goddess, who wears a garland of it | group, troop, flock.
kadara m. saw | elephant tusk | corn, callus — n. curdled milk.
kadartha [kadartha] m. useless thing or fu neste — v. [11] pr. (kadarthayati) to despise, to lie, to treat harshly, to disregard. kadarthīkr to despise.
kadarthana |na| n. trouble, torment.
kadarya [kadarya] amnf kadaryā stingy, greedy | despicable, evil; ignoble.
kadala mf kadalī bio. bot. Musa sapientum, plantain banana; its stem is a symbol of fragility and grace.

kadalīgarbha | garbha | m. bio. heart of the banana tree — f. Kadalīgarbhā lit. [KSS.] np. of Kadalīgarbhā, daughter of Mankanaka disturbed in his penances by the nymph Menakā and losing his seed in a banana tree; she was very beautiful, and King Dṛḍhavarmā fell in love with her and married her; she was the target of the jealousy of a rival, accused of witchcraft, and returned to her father, who restored the truth.
kadalīpāka | pāka | n. lit. poetry fairly easy to understand (like bananas are easy to access); opp. drākṣāpāka, nārikelapāka.
kadalīphala | phala | n. organic. banana.
kadā |ka₁ dā| adv. interr. when? || Latin quando; Slavic kogda; French quand. yadā ... kadā ca as many times as possible.
kadācana [cana] adv. sometimes, occasionally; once. na kadācana adv. never.

kadācit [cid₁] adv. sometimes, occasionally; once, one day; at a certain time. na kadācit adv. never. kadācid api na adv. never. pūrvam kadācit adv. once upon a time; formerly. kadācid gośabdena budhyeta he might wake up with the sound of cows.
kadāpi [api] adv. once; one day; sometimes; from time to time.

kádru amnf Kadrū red, brown; bronzed, tanned — f. Kadrū myth. np. of Kadrū "the Brown one", daughter of Dakṣa (or [Mah.] Prajāpati), wife of Kaśyapa and mother of the thousand dragons |nāga|; she is also said to be the daughter of Kaśyapa and Krodhavaśā; she opposed her sister Vinatā; cf. Uccaiḥśravā | ved. soma (brown) container.
√ kan var. kā [related to kam] v. pft. (cākana) pft. r. (cake) aor. [5] (akānīt) ved. to be satisfied, to appreciate; to accept, to agree | to shine; to desire.
kana [agt. kan] amnf kanā young; small (substituted for alpa for the compar. and the super.).
kanakhala [khala] n. geo. np. of the tīrtha kanakhala on the banks of the Ganges, at the foot of the Mts Śivālika, near Haridvāra; mod. village of Kantchal. anukanakhalam adv. towards kanakhala.
kánaka [agt. kan] n. or — amnf kanakā in gold; Golden — f. kanakā myth. "Golden", np. of one of the 7 languages of Agni.
kanakagamana [gamana] m. bd. np. of Kanakaga mana "Golden Rain", mythical buddha of the 23rd previous life [jātaka] of buddha, second of our
era [kalpa]; a shower of gold fell upon India at its birth | pali Konagamana.
Kanakadhārā [dhārā₁] f. lit. np. of the Kanakadhārā "Golden Rain", devotional hymn [stotra] to Lakṣmī attributed to Sankara₁.

kanakapurī [purī] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the divine City of kanakapurī "Golden City"; Princess Kanaka rekhā only wanted to marry a man who had visited her; Saktideva presented himself, but was found to be a liar; humiliated, he set out in search of the find; from the island of Utsthala, he succeeded, and there met the vidyādharī Candraprabhā, daughter of King Sasikhanda; after many adventures, he became the vidyādhara king Saktivega.
kanakaprabhā [prabhā₁] f. “Splendor of gold”, np. of woman.
kanakamañjarī [mañjarī] f. phone. n.p. of a meter of 11 syllables, used in the Gopīgīta.
kanakamaya [maya] amnf kanakamayī made of gold.
kanakamṛga [mṛga] m. myth. [Rām.] golden deer, into which Mārīca metamorphosed to attract Rāma; syn. māyāmrga, hemamrga.

Kanakarekhā [rekhā] f. bed. [KSS.] np. of Princess Kanakarekhā, daughter of King Paropakārī and Queen Kanakaprabhā of Vardhamāna; she only wanted to marry a man who had visited kanakapurī; cf. Candrarekhā, Śaktideva.
Kanakalekhā [lekhā] f. lit. [DKC.] np. of the princess Kanakalekhā, daughter of King Kardana of Kalinga; she married Mantragupta.
kanakasūtra [sūtra] n. gold chain.
kanakastambha [stambha] m. golden column. [3
kanakastambharucira | rucira | amnf kanakas tambharucirā which shines with its golden columns.
kanat [ppr. kan] amnf kanantī brilliant.

Kaniska m. hist. np. of King Kaniska₁ who founded the Kuṣāṇa dynasty in northern India in the early 2nd century; his capital was Purusapura (mod. Peshāwar); he promoted the expansion of Buddhism; he founded the Saka era | hist. np. of Kanişka₂, Kuṣāṇa king who reigned around (226–240).
kaniṣṭha [super. kana] amnf kaniṣṭhā the youngest, the cadet; opp. jyeṣṭha — f. kaniṣṭhā auricular.
kaniṣṭhaka [ka] amnf kaniṣṭhikā the smallest — f. kanisthikā Little finger.
kanisthaprathama | prathama | amnf kanisthaprathamā having first the smallest.
kanīna [kanaīna] amnf kanīnī young — f. kanīnī pupil of the eye.
kanīnaká [ka] m. young boy — f. kanīnakā young girl; Virgin — f. kanīnikā pupil of the eye Little finger.

kánīyas [compar. kana] amnf kanīyasī younger, younger; opp. jyāyas | lesser; insigni fiant — f. kanīyasī younger sister of the wife. kanīyān rājakumārah lit. The Little Prince, a work by Saint Exupéry translated into Sanskrit by Gopa bandhu Miśra.
kanta var. kaṃta [kamta] amnf kantā happy.
kanti [kamti] amnf happy.
kantu [kamtu] amnf happy — m. myth. np. of kantu "happy", epith. of Kāma.
kanthā f. rag, patched garment (not. worn by an ascetic) — n. kantha ifc. city || lat. cento.
kanda mn bulb, onion.
kandala |la| n. bio. banana flower — f. kandalī bio. bot. Musa sapientium, banana tree.
kandara [kam₁dara] n. cave, ravine.
kandu [skandu] m. metal cooking utensil; saucepan, frying pan, sauté pan, pot | oven.
kanduka m. ball (to play with); balloon — v. [11] pr. r. (kandukāyate) to be like a balloon. kandukena krīḍ to play with the ball.
kandukakrīdā [krīdā] f. ball game, balloon game |soc. iconographic theme of the young woman playing with a ball.
kandukanṛtya [nṛtya] n. lit. [DKC.] ball dance, performed by Princess kandukavatī to obtain a husband during the kandukotsava festival.

kandukavat [vat] amnf kandukavatī who holds a ball — f. kandukavatī lit. [DKC.] np. of the princess kandukavatī "Ball-bearer", daughter of King Tungadhanvā; she danced for Somāpīdā at the kandukotsava; she married Mitraupta.

kandukotsava [utsava] m. bed. [DKC.] ball dance festival. কন্নত Kannada m. geo. Dravidian-speaking Kannada country and people of Karnātaka; corrupted into Kanara by the Portuguese to designate its coastal strip Karāvalī.
kanya [great. kana] amnf kanyā the Smallest; opp. uttama — f. cf. kanya.

kanyakā [ka] f. young girl. kanyakubja var. Kanyākubja [kubja] n. myth. np. of kanyakubja, ancient kingdom founded by Amāvasu; cf. Kanyākubja. Kanyakumārī var. kanyākumārī [kumārī] f. myth. np. of Kanyakumārī or kanyākumārī "young girl", epith. of DurgāPārvatī | geo. pilgrimage city of Tamil Nadu, in the extreme South of India; Pārvatī is venerated there (mod. Cape Comorin).
kanya [f. kanya] f. young girl, Virgo; woman; daughter; female astr. zodiacal sign [rāśi] of Virgo. devakanyā young goddess. rājakanyā princess.

Kanyākubja | kubja | n. myth. np. of kanya kubja or Kanyākubja, ancient kingdom founded by Amāvasu; [Rām.] Gādhi, then his son Viśvāmitra, were its kings — f. kanyākubjā geo. its capital kanyākubjā, a very large city on the Ganges; it owes its name "Hunchbacked Daughter" to the legend of King Kuśanābha, whose 100 daughters were made hunchbacked by Vāyu for not yielding to his desires; it is also called Mahodayā and Gādhipura; it was renowned for its perfumes and the knowledge of its brahmins; it was the capital of Yaśovarmā in the 8th century; It was later the object of struggles between the Rāstrakūtās of the Deccan, the Pratīhārās in the west and the Pālās in the east; it was abandoned after the raids of Mahmud of Ghazni in the 11th century; only a huge field of ruins remains near modern Kannauj, 80 km northwest of Kanpur.
kanyākumārī [kumārī] f. cf. Kanyakumārī.
kanyādāna [dāna] n. soc. gift by the father of his daughter in marriage to his son-in-law; it is one of the marriage rites | vivāha|.
kanyādūṣaṇa [dūṣaṇa] n. rape.
kanyapura | pura | n. soc. women's apartment; harem.
kanyāratna [ratna] n. ["a girl's jewel"] pretty girl, beauty.

kapata mn deception, fraud. kapaṭāt adv. ifc. under the appearances of (iic.). asuragrhītāmṛtāpaharaṇakṛtakapaṭapaṭuvilāsinīveṣa [K.] (Hari) cleverly disguised under the appearance of the seductive (Mohinī) to take back from the demons the elixir of life which they had stolen.
kapaṭaprabandha | prabandha | m. serial frauds; machination, conspiracy.
kaparda m. shell, seashell; not. zoo. Cy praea moneta, whose shell is used as currency; there are 80 in a pana | bun | ang. cowrie.
kapardin [in] m. myth. np. of Kapardī, epith. of Siva "with hair braided in a bun".

kapāṭa m. leaf; door (of temple, city). anāvṛtakapāṭam dvāram dehi opens the door. udghāṭayet kapāṭaṃ tu yathā kuñcikayā haṭhāt | kundalinyā tathā yogī mokṣadvāram vibhedayet || VM. The door should be opened using the key; similarly, by the force of kuṇḍalinī, the yogi opens the door to liberation.
kapāṭikā [ika] f. mod. storage unit.
kapāla [kampāla] mn cup, bowl, dish; alms bowl; lid | skull, head — n. co eggshell — f. Kapālī soc. skullcap used as an alms bowl by an ascetic lat. caput; fr. cap; all. Kopf.
kapālakundala [kundala] m. bed. [Mālatīmādhava] np. of the kāpālika Kapālakundala; cf. Mālātī.
kapālakuhara [kuhara] n. palatal cavity; cf. khe carīmudrā.
kapālabhātī [bhāti] f. phil. [yoga] exercise alternating breath and breath retention; forced exhalation in bursts.

kapālamocana [mocana] n. geo. sacred site of kapālamocana, located at a bend of the Ganges at Kāśī; myth. it was at this place that Sivakāpālika was freed from his curse and threw the 5th head of Brahmā; the Omkāra temple is located there.

kapālavrata [vrata] n. soc. ["vow of the skull"] transgressive behavior of Shaivite ascetics who clothe themselves in bones and other impurities, accompanied by a black dog, and consume alcohol in excess.

kapālasphota [sphota] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the rākṣasa Kapālasphota into which the young Vi jayadatta was transformed, when the bursting of a skull on a crematorium field caused him to ingest the brains of a dead man.

kapālin [in] m. myth. np. of Kapālī "Skull-bearer", aspect of Rudra, one of the 11 divine breaths [marut] | myth. Shiva as an ascetic begging for alms with a skullcap — f. Kapālinī myth. np. of Kapālinī, epith. of Kālī "who wears the garland of skulls".

Kapāleśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of the temple of Kapāleśvara, located in mod. Mylapore, south of Chennai; myth. his linga was established there by Brahmā to repent after Shiva cut off his 5th head; the original temple was built by the Pallavās in the 7th century, then destroyed by the Portuguese; the current temple dates from the 16th century; it is the site of many festivals.
kapí [kampi] m. monkey | myth. n.p. of Kapi, a rsi among the angirasas — f. var. kapī female monkey | gr. κηπος; eng. ape.
kapikacchu [kacchu] f. organic. bot. Mucuna pruriens, velvet pea; syn. atmaguptā | kapikacchū id.

kapittha |stha| m. bio. bot. Feronia elephantum or bot. Limonia acidissima, tanka tree "where monkeys perch"; it can reach 8 m; its trunk is covered with thorns; its resin is used as varnish, and its bark as a cosmetic [elavālu]; its fruit, 5 to 9 cm in diameter, has a very hard rind; the pulp is eaten, and is also used to make syrup, jelly, and sorbet; it is used medicinally; it cures impotence and restored Varuna's lost virility; syn. tanka — n. its fruit the elephant apple; its brown, edible pulp is astringent
gente | grāhiphala | ; Gaņeśa is fond of it.
kapitthaka [ka] m. bio. bot. Feronia elephantum — n. its fruit the elephant apple — m. ritual gesture [mudrā] of Feronia (index and middle fingers raised, other fingers folded).
kapitva [vat] n. monkey nature.
kapidhvaja [dhvaja] m. myth. epith. of Arjuna "who carries Hanuman on his standard".
kapíśīrṣa [śīrṣa] n. arch. cornice.
kapiśīrṣaka [ka] m. id.
kapísthala | sthala | mr. ved. n.p. of the rsi Kapisthala.
Kapisthalasamhitā [samhitā] f. lit. np. of the Kapisthalasamhitā, Vedic text close to the Kāthaka samhitā
Kapisura [sura] m. myth. n.p. of Kapisura, epith. of Hanumān the “Godusinge”.

kapíñjala m. bio. capercaillie, pheasant, partridge | lit. [K.] np. of the young ascetic Kapiñjala, follower of Pundarīka₂ during his encounter with Mahāśvetā; he is reincarnated as the horse Indrāyudha, and takes on human form during the lethargy of Candrāpīda₁; he recounts having followed Candra when the latter abducted Pundarīka₂, who taught him the mutual curses that afflicted them, and suggested that he go to see Svetaketu; on the way an irascible sage cursed him to be reborn as a horse, at least until the death of his rider; In return, he begged him not to be separated from Pundarīka₂, who would become Vaiśampāyana₁, best friend of Prince Candrāpīda₁, his rider.
kapiñjalakulakalakūjitam [K.] the murmur of a brood of partridges.

kapilá [kampila] amnf kapilā brown, reddish, reddish ["the color of monkeys"] — m. the color brown; brown animal | myth. np. from the rși Kapila "the redhead"; he reduced to ashes with a glance the 60,000 sons of King Sagara for disturbing his meditation; he is considered the founder of the Sāṃkhya system; |BhP.| he was born to the prajāpati Kardama and his wife Devahūti at the manvantara of Svāyambhuva; he is the supreme
devout |mahābhakta| but also the supreme sage [paramarși] who gave their name to things; his divine status is varied; the Baudhāyana dharmasūtra says he is the son of Prahlāda — f. kapilā brown cow.
Kapilavastu [vastu₁] n. geo. n.p. from Kapilavastu, birthplace of the Buddha, in southern Nepal.
kapilasmṛti [smṛti] f. lit. np. of the kapilasmṛti, a collection of rules to be respected by a brahmin in the kaliyuga, in 1002 verses of anuştubh₂ meter, composed between 800 and 1200.
kapilendra | Indra | m. hist. np. of the Gajapati king Ka pilendra, who reigned in Kalinga (1435–1467) after overthrowing King Ganga Bhānudeva; his son Purușottamadeva₁ succeeded him.
kapileśvara |īśvara| mr. geo. kapileśvara temple, built in the 14th century in Bhubanesvar by king Ka pilendra.

kapiśá [related to Kapila] amnf kapiśā brown, reddish, russet ["the color of monkeys"] — m. the color brown — n. a type of rum — f. kapiśā var. kapiśī id. | geo. np. of the town of kapiśī, 60 km north of Kabul (mod. Bagram)
kapúcchala [ka₁pucchala] n. tuft of hair hanging behind the head.
kapóta m. Pigeon, dove — f. kapotī pi geon female. varam adya kapotah śvo mayūrāt [Nītivākyamṛta] "a pigeon today is better than a peacock." A good bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
kapotasandeśa [sandeśa] m. lit. np. du Kapota sandeśa "Messenger Pigeon", contemporary poem by K. Sudhākara Rao.
kapola m. cheek (not. man or elephant) — f. kapolī kneecap. unmadamātangakapolasthalagalitamada
salilasiktena [K.] Car mois du suint liquide efflowe de la surface des temples de l'éléphant furée.
Kapphiṇa m. bd. np. of the (mythical) king Kapphina of Kaśmīra; the Kapphinābhyudaya relates his war against King Prasenajit₂, and his conversion by the Buddha himself.
kapphinābhyudaya [abhyudaya] m. bed. n.p. from the mahākāvya Kapphinābhyudaya "Triumph of King Kapphina", Buddhist poem by Bhatta Šivasvāmī (Kaśmīra, 9th century).
kapha m. med. phlegm, one of the three humors [tridoṣa]; syn. khaṭa, śleṣman.
kaphoni mf elbow.

kábandha mn barrel; pot-bellied container | belly; potbelly | Decapitated human trunk | myth. epith. of Rāhu "Decapitated" | large cloud, especially at sunset — m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the dānava Kabandha "Trunk"; born Viśvāvasu as the son of a king of the gandharvās, he was a giant of prodigious beauty, and Brahmā had foretold a long life for him; full of pride, he challenged Indra to combat, and received from the latter a blow that drove his head and legs into his body; he had very long

[Yojanabāhu] had arms, a large, hungry mouth on his belly, and a single eye that shot flames; he terrified the worlds and devoured travelers; he captured Rāma and Laksmana in exile in the forest, but they cut off his arms, and he explained his curse to them; he could only regain his divine form after being killed by them and burned with the rites; thus he regained his splendor, and thanked Rāma by advising him to make a friend of Sugrīva.
kabara [related to kavara] amnf kabarā miscellaneous; mixed (color); inlaid — m. lecturer, preacher — f. kabarī braid of hair.

√ kam v. pft. (cakame) pp. (kāntá) pf. (ni) to desire, to love, to be in love with — ca. r. (kāmayate) ca. (kāmayati) id. | to inspire love, to make someone love. kāmaye dātum I wish to give. na dhanam kāmaye I do not desire wealth. so'kāmayata |BU.| He desired.

kam₁ [acc. ka₂] part. cl. himself (underlines the preceding word) | truly (intensive expletive at the end of pada) | what? (interrogative of surprise or of re close at the beginning of the sentence) — iic. head | water | bliss. kamja var. kañja [ja] m. ["produced by the head"] hair | myth. np. of kamja, epith. of Brahmā "born of the waters" — n. ["born of the water"] lotus.
kandarpa [darpa] m. love; sexual desire | myth. np. of kandarpa "Mad Desire", epith. of Kāma.

Kandarpaketu₁ | ketu | m. myth. | Hitopadeśa | np. of Kandarpaketu₁ "who has love as his banner", king of the celestial genies [vidyādharās]; he is son of Jīmūtaketu | lit. np. of the charming prince Kandarpaketu₁ "Champion of love", hero of the romance novel Vāsavadattā by Subandhu; perfect son of the perfect king Cintāmaṇi₂, he saw in an erotic dream the princess Vāsavadattā₁; leaving his palace with his friend Makaranda, he met a parrot who led him to his betrothed, who had had the symmetrical dream.
kaṃdhara | dhara | m. | "that which bears the head" | neck | | "that which contains water" | ocean. valitakamdhara amn that has an inclined neck.
kamaṇḍalu mn water pot used by ascetics.
kamana |agt. kam| amnf kamanā experiencing desire; lustful | desirable, charming — m. epith. of the god Kāma.
kamanīya [pfp. [2] kam] amnf kamanīyā desirable; charming, pretty.
kamanīyatā [tā] f. charm, beauty, desirability.
kamanīyatva [tva] n. id.

kámala |kamala| amnf kāmalā pale rose — mn bio. bot. Nelumbium speciosum, rose lotus; it opens during the day; it is compared to the face of women, their lips, their hands and their feet; syn. nalina, padma, pankaja, ambuja, amb hoja, abja, aravinda | bio. sweet orange (manda rine) — f. cf. kamalā.
kamalaśīla [śīla] m. hist. np. of the philosopher Ka malaśīla (740–795), student of Sāntarakṣita; he is credited with the analytical commentary Panjika of the Tattvasamgraha.
kamalākara |ākara| mr. pond full of lotuses.
Kamalākṣa [akṣa] amnf kamalākṣā who has lotus eyes; said not. of Kṛṣṇa — m. myth. np. of Kamalākṣa "with lotus eyes", son of Tāraka; cf. Tripura.
kamalāyudha [āyudha] m. hist. np. of the poet Ka malāyudha, of the court of Yasovarmā in Kanyākubjā (late 7th century).
kamalālaya |ālaya| m. lotus field | geo. | "lotus country" region of the Cauvery delta in Tamil Nadu — f. kamalālayā myth. epith. of Lakṣmī "surrounded by lotus".

Kamalālayakṣetra | kṣetra | n. geo. np. of the city of Kamalālayakṣetra "Chief of the land of the lotus", in Tamil Nadu (mod. Thiruvarur); it was a capital of the Cola kingdom, then in the 13th century was disputed between the Pāndya kingdom and the Hoysala empire; it became a cultural center of the Vijayana gara empire; its Tyāgarāja temple is famous for its chariot festival.
kamalinī |in| f. organic. bot. Nelumbium speciosum, pink lotus | pond covered with pink lotuses.
