kamalā [f. kamala] f. myth. np. of kamalā "rose lotus", epith. of Lakṣmī; [Tantra] she is one of the 10 powers [mahāvidyā] of the Goddess [Śakti]; she is also called Siddhilakṣmī | lit. [Rājataraṃgiṇī] np. of kamalā₁, dancer of the temple of Kārttikeya in Pundravardhana; she seduced King Jayāpīda.
kamalābīja [bīja] n. phil. [Tantra] bijamantra 'śrīm' of evocation of Sarasvatī.
kamitṛ [agt. kam] amnf kamitrī amorous; sexually attracted — m. male; husband.

√ kamp v. [1] pr. r. (kampate) pft. r. (cakampe) was. r. (kampisyate) aor. [3] (acakampat) aor. r. [5] (akampiṣṭa) pp. (kampitá) inf. (kámpitum) abs. (kampya) pf. (anu, abhi, ā, ut, pra, vi) to tremble; to agitate | to be frightened — ca. (kampayati) to shake.
kampa [act. kamp] m. trembling, agitation, fear.
kampavāta [vāta] m. med. Parkinson's disease; cf. atmaguptā.
kampana [agt. kamp] amnf kampanī trembling, unstable | that which makes tremble; that which shakes.
kampita [pp. kamp] amnf kampitā trem blant.
Kampila m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Kampila; his hermitage was located in Kāmpilya.

kampili m. geo. np. of the small kingdom of kampili in the Deccan; it comprised the districts of Gulbarga and Raichur in modern Karnaka; it was founded by the dissident Hoysala commander Singeya Nayaka (1280–1300), who was succeeded by his son Kam Pilideva; it was taken over by the Delhi Sultanate, before being integrated into the Vijayanagara Empire.

kampilideva | deva | m. hist. np. of King Kampilideva of Kampili; he allied himself with King Ramadeva of De Vagiri against King Hoysala Ballala III and welcomed the dissident cousin of the Sultan of Delhi, Muhammad ibn Tughluk; the latter sent his general Malik Kafur who took the fort of Kummata, seized Kampili in 1327, and had Kampilideva beheaded.
kampya [pfp. [1] kamp] amnf kampyā to shake; to move aside, to chase away.
kambalá mn blanket or woolen cloth — m. fanon; syn. sāsnā.
kambalya |ya| n. measure of wool weight.
kambu m. shell, seashell, conch shell bracelet | kambū thief.
kambukantha [kantha] amnf kambukanthī who has a neck wrinkled like a conch; syn. kambugrīva.

kambugrīva [grīvā] amnf kambugrīvā who has a neck pleated like a conch shell; syn. kambukantha — m. lit. [PT.] np. of kambugrīva, tortoise who was carried into the air holding onto a stick by its mouth, could not restrain himself from getting angry at the mockery, and thus crashed to the ground. buddhimān nītimān vāgmī śrīmān śatrunibarhaṇah vipulāmsah mahābāhuh kambugrīvah mahāhanuh ca [Rām.] (Rāma) Is intelligent, sagacious, eloquent, glorious, he exterminates his enemies; He has broad shoulders, powerful arms, a muscular neck similar to a conch shell, and a powerful jaw.
Kamboja m. pl. geo. ved. royal clan [kṣatriya] Kamboja of the śakās; country and people of the extreme northwest of India, north of Gandhāra | their king | horse or elephant of the country.
kamra [kamra] amnf kamrā in love; enamored | desirable; pretty, charming — f. kamrā a type of musical instrument.
káyā [i. kā] adv. by what?
kayāpi [api] adv. by some. na kayāpi kanyayā saha saṃvadati he does not speak to any girl.
Kayādhu | related to kravyād | f. myth. n.p. of Kayādhu "Vampire", wife of Hiraņyakaśipu.

kará₁ [agt. kṛ₁] amnf karī ifc. that which does, that which acts, that which usually produces (iic.) | that which causes, that which gives (iic.) | that which takes pleasure in doing (iic.) — ins. m. hand; trunk (of the elephant); pincers (of the crab) ray of light — mf karā ifc. craftsman of (iic.) lat. cerus. kara'kamala | kamala | amnf karakamalā | "that which has lotus hands" | graceful; revered.
karákisalaya [kisalaya] mn hand closed like a bud | the "thumb of the hand" | finger.
karákosa [kosa] m. cup-shaped hand.
karatala | tala | m. palm of the hand. karatalīkr to take in the palm of one's hand.
karatalatāla | tāla | m. act of clapping one's hands in rhythm.
karatāla | tāla | m. cymbal — n. act of beating time by clapping one's hands — f. karatālī cymbal.
karatālaka [ka] n. cymbal — f. karatālikā claps hands in rhythm.

Karatoyā |toya| f. geo. np. of the Karatoyā River "whose water flows from the hand (of Śiva)"; formerly an important sacred river of Bengal, it flowed at Pundranāgara, between the Gangā and the Brahmaputra; it is said to have originated from the water poured on the hand of Shiva at his marriage to Pārvatī; it marked the eastern boundary of Aryāvarta (with the Sindhu to the west and the Narmadā to the south); it is now dislocated into several channels in the Ganges delta.
karatoyāmāhātmya | māhātmya | n. lit. np. of the Ka ratoyāmāhātmya, description of the sacred places of the Karatoyā basin; cf. Uttarapaundrakhanda.
karada₁ |da| amnf karadā who gives a hand.
karada₂ [da] amnf karadā who pays the tax.
karanyāsa [nyāsa] m. phil. [Tantra] transfer of the power of a mantra onto the hand by ritual gesture.
karáruha [ruha] m. ["that grows from the hand"] nail.
kararuhapada | pada | n. nail mark on the skin.
karavāri [vāri] n. water poured from hand.

karavīra [vīra] m. bio. bot. Nerium odorum, oleander; this apocine, very toxic, is used variously in medicine; cf. vadhyamālā myth. magic formula to summon a celestial weapon — n. bio. flower of the oleander.

karavīrapura [pura] n. myth. np. of the city of Ka ravīrapura where Lakṣmī took refuge, displeased that Bhrgu had struck Vișnu at the place of the Śrīvatsa where she liked to rest; [HV.] Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma took refuge there, pursued by Jarāsandha; they met Parasurāma there | geo. it is identified with the modern Kolhāpūra in the southwest of Mahārāṣṭra, which has a large temple of Mahālakṣmī.
karāgra [agra] n. fingertip; end of elephant's trunk.
karāgraja [ja] m. nail.
karāvalambana | avalambana | n. act of holding by the hand.
kara₂ |act. kr| m. tribute, toll, tax, levy. karīkṛ to offer as tribute.
karaka m. water pot of an ascetic | coconut shell | hailstone | tax; levy.
karakāvṛṣṭi |āvṛṣṭi| f. hail shower.
karakāsāra [āsāra] m. hailstorm.
karańka m. skull; head | coconut used as a cup or container | container; not needed for betel | tāmbūla| | skeleton; bones.

kárañja m. bio. bot. Pongamia glabra, glabrous tree with brown bark speckled with russet, leaves arranged in palmettes, violet papilionaceous flowers, fruits in pods of one or two seeds; used medicinally; it is associated with Saramā.
karața | kara₁ | m. elephant temple | crow | impious man | pl. geo. name of the karaṭās people; their royal dynasty — f. karaţā elephant temple — f. karaţī crow.
karaṭaka [ka] m. crow | lit. [PT.] np. of the jackal Karataka, advisor to the lion king Pingalaka₁ with his brother Damanaka.
karaṭin [karaṭain] m. elephant — f. karaṭinī female elephant.

karaṇá |agt. kṛ₁| amnf karaṇā that does, that causes; active, effective, efficient; skillful — m. karana agent; craftsman; scribe | soc. member of the craft caste — act. n. kárana does, accomplishes, performs, act | soc. ritual action | penitential posture; sexual posture | instrument, means of action; charm, incantation | muscle, tendon; gold

gane | gram. | Pāṇini | thematic role | kāraka | generally expressed in the instrumental case of the principal effective cause [sādhakatama] of the action | phon. [Patañjali₁] internal effort of articulation | soc. mixed caste; not. son of a Kṣatriya father and a Vaiśya mother | astr. practical work for performing astronomical calculations | pl. karaṇās astr. subdivisions of time corresponding to 1/2 a lunar day [tithi]; there are 11; the first 7 are in order: bava or vava, balava or valava, kaulava or kau laba, taitila, gara, vanija and visti; they are called mo

biles [adhruva] and are repeated 8 times from the first half of the new moon day; the last 4 are called fixed [dhruva] and fill the rest of the lunar month: kimtughna or kimstughna, śakuni, nāga and catuspada; thus we obtain 7×8 + 4 = 2×30 half-days in a 30-day lunar month — f. karanī math. irrational number; side of a square. karanena var. karanāt prep. because of.
karaṇatā [tā] f. causality.
karanatva |tva| n. causality; instrumentality |phil. |Raghunātha₁| the category |padārtha| of causa lities.
karanapaddhati [paddhati] f. bed. n.p. from the Karanapaddhati, an astronomical text by Putumana Somayājī (16th century).
karanahetu | hetu | m. phil. physical cause (opp. jñāpakahetu logical reason).

karaṇīya [pfp. [2] kṛ₁] amnf karaṇīyā that which must be done, which must be accomplished; to do — n. duty. lokahitam mama karanīyam I must do good in this world. yathā tu vācā dattam anyathā na karaṇīyam [VC.] What has been promised must not be called into question.
karanda mnf karandī basket, basket in
willow | honeycomb | duck; syn. kāraṇḍa.

karandaka [ka] mnf karandikā small wicker box (not. containing an amulet). doṣakaraṇḍikā phil. ["basket of sins"] sin ori ginel due to individual karma . puspakaraṇḍikā phil. |"basket of flowers" | garden of Eden of original innocence.
karandavyūha [vyūha] m. basket bed arrangement. conceptual exposition.
karabha [kara₁bha] m. young camel | trunk; young elephant.
karabhoru [ūru] amnf karabhorū ["with the thighs of a young elephant" | said of a beautiful woman.

karam [acc. kara₁] iic. karamdhama var. karandhama | dhama | m. myth. |Mah.| np. of the king karandhama "who blows on his hand" to obtain armies and riches at kṛtayuga because of his dharma; his son is Avikṣit Kārandhama.
karambhá m. barley gruel, porridge soc. not. porridge given as an offering to Pūṣā, who has no teeth | var. karamba id.
karasna |kara₁sna| mr. forearm.

karāla [kara₁āla] amnf karālā gaping, wide open (not. wound) | large; imposing; spacious | with an open mouth; ferocious; frightening, terrifying | serrated; bristling; deformed — m. bio. musk deer; syn. kastūrīmrga | black basilisk — f. karālā myth. np. of Karalā, epith. of Durgā “ready [9 to devour” — f. karālī myth. “devouring”, np. of one of the 7 languages of Agni.
Karālanarasimha [Narasimha] m. myth. np. of Karālanarasimha, fierce form of Narasimha; Bhīma assumed it to kill Duḥśāsana.
karālamukha [mukha] m. lit. [PT.] np. of the crocodile dile karālamukha "with the frightening mouth", who took advantage of the credulity of the monkey Raktamukha.

Karāvalī f. geo. np. of the coastal band Karāvalī of karņātaka, of the TuluKannada people; cf. Konkana; tradition attributes to Parasurāma the fact that he brought it out of the waters [paraśurāmasṛṣṭi].
kari₁ [agt. kṛ₁] ifc. amnf that which makes, that which forms, that which accomplishes (iic.).
kari₁ iic. karin.
karikara | kará₁ | m. elephant trunk.
karikarakrīdā [krīdā] f. erotic game (manipulation of the vagina with three fingers).
karikumbha [kumbha] m. frontal hump of the elephant.
karināyaka | nāyaka | m. elephant driver | | fr. cornac.
karin [kara₁in] m. [name. karī] elephant [“which has a trunk” | — f. kariṇī elephant.
kariṣṇú [agt. kṛ₁] ifc. amnf which does (iic.).
kariṣya [kariṣyat] amnf kariṣyā which will be accomplished. karisye we are taking care of it.
kariṣyat [pfu. kṛ₁] amnf kariṣyantī who will do.
karīndra [karinIndra] m. war elephant; chief of the elephants | myth. elephant of Indra.
karīndrakumbha | kumbha | m. frontal hump of a fighting elephant.
karīra mn pousse (not. of bamboo) — m. water pot | bio. bot. Capparis aphylla, ar thorny shrub of the desert on which camels feed; its root has medicinal virtues — n. bio. its fruit, a caper.
kárīṣa [kṛīṣa] mn manure; dried cow dung.
kárīṣagandhi [gandhi] amnf who smells like cow dung — m. nickname for a man.

karúṇa [kṛuna] amnf karúṇā lamentable, pitiful; melancholic, sad; pitiable, touching — m. lit. the pathetic, one of the 9 artistic modes |rasa|; it expresses the irreparable loss of a loved one; it is associated with the color ash and the deity Yama — f. cf. karuṇā — v. [11] pr. r. (karuṇāyate) to feel compassion. karuņavilāsa | vilāsa | n. lit. np. of the karuņavilāsa, 3rd section of the Bhāminīvilāsa, of a pathetic nature.
karunasāgara [sāgara] m. myth. n.p. from karuṇasāgara "Ocean of compassion", an epith. of Rama.
karunin |in| amnf karuninī pitiful.
karuṇā [f. karuṇa] f. pity, compassion | phil. compassion, one of the four moral qualities |brahmavihāra|.
karuṇāpara | para | amnf karuṇāparā compa weaver; kind. ক ৰুপ karūṣa m. geo. [Mah.] name of a country and a people | pl. karūṣās its inhabitants.
kareņu [kara₁] mf elephant — f. var. kareņū female elephant.
karoṭā mf karoṭī cup | skullcap used as a container | var. karoți id.
karká [kṛ₁] amnf karkī white; excellent — m. crab; syn. karkata | jewel — f. karkī bio. female crab.

karkaṭa [karka] m. bio. zoo. crab; crayfish astr. zodiacal sign [rāśi] of Cancer — f. Karkaṭī bio. female crab | myth. np. of the ogress [rākṣasī] karkațī "Cancer"; she lived in the Himalayas where she could not find food, and she implored Brahmā with long penances; he finally granted her a wish; she wished to become as thin as a needle [sūcī] to slip in like a lady and kill people; Brahmā granted her to be Viṣūcīkā, cholera vibrator, and to infect people who have poor hygiene and the wicked, but to spare the good people; he also gave her a healing mantra; After killing countless sick people, she grew weary and regretted her original fate; after many more penances, she succeeded in persuading Brahma to restore her to her original form; he allowed her to roam the world and eat people of ill repute; she entered a forest, where she met the King of the Foresters and his minister; the King agreed to answer her questions, and through his answers, she progressed spiritually in the knowledge of Brahman; he offered her the opportunity to come to his court, take those condemned to death, and carry them to the Himalayas to devour them. | bio. bot. Cucu mis utilissimus, gourd; its fruit is the cucumber; syn. urvāru || gr. καρκινος; lat. Cancer; fr. crab.
karkaṭaka [ka] mf karkaṭakī crab; crayfish.
karkándhu [karkaandhu] mf karkandhū bio. bot. Zizyphus jujuba, jujube tree; syn. badara — n. jujube berry.
karkaśa [karka] amnf karkaśā hard, harsh, rough; hoarse — m. sword, scimitar. kākānām svarah karkaśah crows have a hoarse cry.
karketana [karka] m. chrysoberyl.
karkoṭa m. myth. n.p. of Karkoṭa, nāga of Pātāla; cf. Karkota.

Karkoṭaka [ka] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the nāga Karkotaka; he was cursed by Nārada for deceiving him, and was to remain in the fire; he was delivered from it by King Nala, lost in the forest after leaving Damayanti; on his promise of help, Nala took him from the fire when he had shrunk to the size of a thumb; at the tenth step, Karkotaka bit Nala, who became deformed with small arms and a blue body; Karkotaka reassured him, gave him a marvelous scarf allowing him to regain his normal appearance, told him that he should present himself to King Rtuparna as an expert on horses under the name of Bāhuka, and that he should exchange his expertise for the king's knowledge of dice; then he would be reunited with his family | pl. hist. np. of the Karkoţakās people.

kárṇa m. ear |rudder |math. hypotenuse of a triangle | myth. [Mah.] np. of Karna "ear (of gold)", secret elder brother of the Pāṇḍavās, son of Kuntī and the god Sūrya, raised in secret by the sūta₁ Adhi ratha and Rādhā₁; his divine birth being ignored, he was called Sauti₁; kind-hearted hero of the Kau ravās, he is impetuous and boastful; he was invincible target with his breastplate [kavaca] and his golden earrings [kundala] which he had from birth; He possessed the Vijaya₄ bow that Viśvakarmā had made for Indra, and that Jāmadagnya had given him when he visited him on Mount Mahendra₁ to learn the science of weapons, after Drona had refused him as a student; there he was cursed by a Brahmin for accidentally killing his cow's calf, and condemned to die in battle, his chariot wheel stuck in the mud; he joined Duryodhana, and helped him commit the abduction of his wife; he succeeded Drona as commander-in-chief of the Kauravās; he was possessed by the asura Naraka; he is also Mahādānī, the one who gives all that he possesses; he thus gave his attributes to Indra, although he knew he would have to die for it; He killed the monster Ghatotkaca, but to do so he had to use the magical weapon [brahmāstra] given to him by Jāmadagnya, which he intended for Arjuna; his charioteer was King Salya, with whom he quarreled; during his battle with Arjuna, driven by Kṛṣṇa, the wheel of his chariot became stuck in the mud, and Arjuna killed him with the magical arrow Añjalika; Vṛṣasena is his son; cf. Rādheya, Vaikartana — f. cf. karņī — v. [11] pr. (karṇayati) to pierce, to dig. karne adv. in the ear, aside. karnam dā to lend an ear; to listen. karnam āgam to return to the ears; to circulate.
kárnaka [ka] m. handle (on the side of a usten sile) | ring — f. karņakā ear ornament; not. earring | protuberance; central point.
kárnaja [ja] m. cerumen.
kárṇajāpa [jāpa] m. whispering in the ear | slander, calumny.
karnadeva |deva| m. hist. np. of the Solankī king Karnadeva, who succeeded Bhīmadeva in Aņahilapāṭaka (11th century); he conquered the city of Aśapalli, which he renamed Karnavatī.
karṇadhāra [dhāra₁] m. ["who holds the rudder"] helmsman, pilot.
karnapattrabhanga | pattrabhanga | mr. the ornament and fragrance of the ears, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
karṇaparvan [parvan] n. bed. n.p. of the Karṇaparva, 8th book of the Mah., "of Karņa".
Karṇapūraka [pūraka] m. lit. np. of Karṇapūraka, servant of Vasantasenā in the Mṛcchakaṭikā.
karṇaprayāga [prayāga] m. geo. np. of Karņaprayāga, city of Uttarākhaņda at the confluence of the Alakanandā and the Pindara; myth. it is the presumed place of the cremation of Karna by Kṛṣṇa.

karṇabhāra [bhāra] n. lit. np. from karṇabhāra "Karņa suffering his fate", one-act drama by Bhāsa, based on the Mah.; it evokes Indra's theft of Karna's armor before his fight with Arjuna, in order to fulfill Paraśurāma's curse.

karnavat [vat] amnf karnavatī having ears | with long ears — f. karnavatī geo. np. of the city of karnavatī, on the banks of the Sabarmatī in Gurjara; it was conquered by King Solankī Karnadeva in the 11th century; in 1411 Sultan Ahmed Shah founded his fortified capital Ahmedabad nearby. karnavedha [vedha] m. soc. rite [saṃskāra] of piercing the earlobes of a child.
karṇābharaṇa [ābharaṇa] n. ear ornament. ^51
karṇāmṛta |amṛta| n. lit. (poetry) nectar for the ear.
Karṇāmṛtaprapā [prapā₂] f. lit. np. of the Karṇāmṛtaprapā, "Fountain of nectar for the ear", anthology of 217 didactic verses collected by Someśvaradeva.
karnāvatamsa [avatamsa] n. earring.
karṇākarṇi [red. karṇa] adv. ear to ear.
Karṇāṭa m. geo. name of the country Karṇāṭa (mod. Karņātaka) in the Deccan; its capital was Vi jayanagara | pl. karņāṭās its inhabitants. karņātaka [ka] m. geo. the Karņātaka.
karnāṭakasaṃgīta [saṃgīta] n. soc. Carnatic chant.
karni iic. karnin.
karnikāra [kāra] m. bio. bot. Pterospermum aceri folium, large tree of the southern Himalayas; its white flower has an unpleasant odor.
karņika [karņaika] amnf karņikā equipped with ears; with large ears | at the helm — m. helmsman — mn pericarp (not. of a lotus) — n. type of arrow (with a notched point).
karṇin [karṇain] amnf karṇinī who has ears or ear-shaped appendages; who wears an earring.
karnilá [karnaila] amnf karnilā who has big ears.
Karṇī [f. karṇa] f. type of arrow (with serrated points) | myth. [Mah.] np. of Karṇī, wife of Ugrasena, mother of Kamsa.
karnīsuta [suta₂] m. myth. matr. of Kamsa "son of Karņī" | lit. [K.] np. of the famous thief Karņīsuta; his companions are Vipula and Acala, Sasa is his guru; he is identified with Mūladeva.
karņe [loc. karņa] iic. karņejapa [japa] amnf karņejapā ["who whispers in the ear" accuser.
kartá [obj. kṛt₁] m. trench, ditch.
kartana [act. kṛt₁] n. act of cutting, excision — ins. f. kartanī scissors.
kartanaka [agt. kṛt₁] amnf kartanikā that cuts — m. med. incisive.
kartari [instr. kṛt₁] f. scissors, knife, cut; cutting instrument | var. kartarī id.
kartarikā [ka] f. id.
kartarīphala | phala | n. knife blade.
kartarīmukha | mukha | m. ritual gesture | mudrā | of the hand in scissor blades (fingers joined horizontally, little finger raised).

kartávya [pfp. [3] kṛ₁] amnf kartavyā to be done, to be accomplished; to do — n. duty, obligation, task. mayā kartavyam it is my duty, I must do it. yatnam kartavyam gram. there is an effort to be made (to understand the rule).
kartavyatā [tā] f. the act of being to be done. kartavyatām brūhi tell me what I must do.

kartṛ [agt. kṛ₁] amnf kartrī [sg. nom. kartā; acc. kartāram] that makes, that acts, active; creator, author — m. soc. officiating priest | gram. thematic role |kāraka| of independent agent [svatantra] — f. kartrī creative — v. [11] pr. (kartrīyati) to wish for a creator. śraddham kartā who performs the funeral rite. karttā kaṭān who makes mats. kartari prayogah gram. ["in active process"] use of the active voice, where the personal suffix of the verb denotes the agent of the action; opp. use of the passive voice |karmani prayogah|.
kartṛka |ka| ifc. amnf kartṛkā id.
kartṛtā [tā] f. gram. quality of being the agent of an action.
kartṛtva |tva| n. gram. the state of being the agent of an action.
kartṛṣādhana |sādhana| n. gram. agent name.
kartṛstha [stha] amnf kartṛsthā gram. which resides in the agent.
kartṛstakriya [kriyā] amnf kartṛstakriyā gram. said of a root whose action is located only in the agent; opp. karmasthakriya. kartṛstakriyaka amnf kartṛstakriyakā id.
karttr gem. kartr.
Kardana n. borborygmus — m. bed. [DKC.] np. of King Kardana of Kalinga; he granted his daughter Ka nakalekhā to Mantragupta.

kardama m. mud; dust, dirt; mythical sin. [BhP.] np. of the prajāpati kardama, an aspect of Vișnu that appeared at the manvantara of Svāyambhuva, emerging from the shadow of Brahmā; with his wife Devahūti he traveled in a flying palace; they had 9 daughters and one son, the rṣi Kapila, who taught them liberation [vairāgya] through devotion [bhakti]; the BhP. contains a dialogue between Manu and kardama.
karpaṭa n. rag.
karpaṇa m. throwing weapon, forked javelin.
karpara [related to kapāla] m. cup, bowl, cup, skull, tortoise shell.
karpāsa mn bio. bot. Gossypium herba ceum, cotton | gr. καρπασος; lat. carbasus.
karpūra [kṛp] mn Camphor (plant and resin) — m. hist. np. of the karpūra family of physicians of Vāraņasī (17th century) — f. cf. Karpūrā | ang. camphor; fr. Camphre.
Karpuraka |ka| mr. bed. |KSS.| n.p. of Karpūraka, king of the country Karpūrasambhava — f. Karpūrikā np. of his daughter, the beautiful Karpūrikā.
karpūrapaṭa [paṭa] m. bed. [Hit.] np. from the dyer Karpūrapata.
karpūramañjarī | mañjarī | f. bed. n.p. from the Karpūramañjarī "Bouquet of Camphor", sattaka type drama in 4 acts in Prakrit by Rājaśekhara.
karpūravarṣa [varṣa] m. bed. [Viddhaśālabhañjikā] np. from the imaginary land karpūravarṣa.
Karpūravilāsa [vilāsa] m. bed. [Hit.] np. from the dyer Karpūravilāsa.
Karpūrasambhava [sambhava] m. bed. [KSS.] np. from the Karpūrasambhava country “from Camphor”.
karpūrastotra [stotra] n. bed. n.p. from the karpūrastotra; cf. karpūrādistotra.
Karpūrā [f. karpura] myth. [Tantra] n.p. of Karpūrā, Goddess Camphor.

karpūrādistotra [ādistotra] n. lit. np. from karpūrādistotra "Fundamental Hymn to the Camphor Goddess", an elegant Sanskrit poem composed by an anonymous Bengali scholar of the 17th century; it describes extreme tantric practices.
karbura amnf karburā variegated, variegated purple.
karma iic. karman.
karmakara [kara₁] amnf karmakarī who does work — m. soc. worker.

karmakartṛ [kartṛ] m. gram. thematic role [kāraka] of self-object agent, also called intransitive reflexive use. karmakartari loc. gram. in the reflexive voice; said of a sentence where the agent is its own object, such as odanah pacyate.
karmakartrprakriyā [prakriyā] f. gram. formation of the intransitive reflective mode.
karmakānda [kānda] n. lit. section of the Veda relating to sacrificial rites | lit. set of the 12 main chapters of the Mīmāṃsāsūtra, as opposed to the 4 supplementary chapters of the Samkarṣakāṇḍa.
karmakāra [kāra] amnf karmakārī who works — m. soc. free worker, craftsman.
karmagṛhīta |gṛhīta| amnf karmagṛhītā caught in the act.
karmaceṣṭā [ceṣṭā] f. activity; voluntary action.
karmaja | ja | amnf karmajā which results from an action | phil. (merit/demerit) produced in a life.
karmatā [tā] f. effect of an action; activity | gram. nature of object.
karmatva |tva| n. id.
karmadosa | dosa₂ | m. sin of action; fault, error; vice | phil. demerit produced in a life.

karmadhāraya [dhāraya] m. gram. ["that which carries the role"] appositional or descriptive compound, where the first word is an attribute of the second (separately, they would decline similarly, as they are codenotative); when the 1st term is a number name, the compound is called dvigu.

karmapravacanīya [pravacanīya] amnf karma pravacanīyā gram. ["which serves to express the act"] used by Pāṇini to qualify prepositions not attached to a verbal form, and other particles like api and su₁.

karmaphala | phala | n. | "fruit of action" | result or consequence of an act; reward phil. consequences of action; we distinguish between immediate [prārabdha], potential [saṃcita], and future [āgāmika] consequences | bio. fruit caram bole; cf. karmaranga.
karmaphalatyāga [tyāga] m. phil. [BhG.] renunciation of the fruits of action.
karmabhūmi [bhūmi] f. place of activity, place of work | epith. soc. of India [Bhāratavarṣa] as "Land of Rituals".

karmamārga [mārga] m. phil. ["way of action"] individual destiny due to the accumulation of merit from the actions of previous lives; one is freed from it through asceticism [tapas], leading to detachment from actions and to the
liberation [mokṣa].
karmamāsa [māsa] m. 30 day calendar.
karmamīmāṃsā [mīmāṃsā] f. phil. [“examination of action” philosophical doctrine pūrvamīmāmsā of Jaimini, exegesis of the Veda and explanation of the Vedic ritual.

karmamīmāṃsādarśana [darśana] n. lit. np. of the Karmamīmāmsādarśana, a phil. at work attributed to Jaimini in 12 chapters, also called Mīmāṃsāsūtra; Sabara₁ Svāmī made the commentary on it; it is completed by the 4 chapters of the Samkarşakānda.
karmamudrā [mudrā] f. bd. [Kaula] np. of the kar mamudrā, or sexual practice of tantric yoga of Tibet.

karmayoga [yoga] m. phil. spiritual realization through action; this discipline of action is preached by Kṛṣṇa in the Bhagavadgītā; cf. sādrśya, sādharmya | active life, work; industry, commerce, agriculture.
karmaranga | ranga | m. bio. bot. Averrhoa ca rambola, a bushy tree with alternate compound leaves; its star-yellow fruit is the carambola |karmaphala|, edible and used medicinally.
karmavacana | vacation | n. bd. ritual.
karmavajra [vajra] amnf karmavajrā ["whose weapon is work"] is said of the śūdrās.
karmavaśa [vaśa] m. phil. influence of past actions — amnf karmavaśā that which is subject to this influence.
karmavipāka [vipāka] m. phil. ["maturation of actions" | good or bad consequences in this life of actions performed in previous lives; the Sātātapasmṛti gives a list of 86 | pali kammavipāka.
karmavibhanga [vibhanga] m. phil. liberation from the bonds of karma | lit. np. of a work bd.
Karmavibhangopadeśa [upadeśa] m. bed. n.p. from the Karmavibhangopadesa “Classification of Acts”.
karmavyatihāra [vyatihāra] m. reciprocity of action. ic karmavyatihāro gram. Pan (5,4, 127): the suffix "ic" indicates the reciprocity of the action.
karmaśobhā [śobhā] f. masterpiece. karmasamtati var. karmasantati [samtati] f. phil. continuity of actions.
karmasādhana [sādhana] n. gram. noun of object.
karmastha [stha] amnf karmasthā gram. which resides in the object.
karmasthakriya [kriyā] amnf karmasthakriyā gram. refers to a root whose action is located in the object (and not only in the agent); opp. kartrstakriya. karmasthakriyaka amnf karmasthakriyakā id.
karmānusthāna [anusthāna] n. soc. practice of one's duties; execution of the rites prescribed by one's caste.
karmānuṣṭhānin [in] amnf karmānuṣṭhāninī soc. who practices his duty, who performs the prescribed rites.
karmānta | anta | m. accomplishment of an action work, action; conduct.
karmāra [āra] m. blacksmith | craftsman, mechanic; artificer || pali kammāra.

karmendriya [indriya] m. phil. [Sāṃkhya] one of the 5 faculties of action: vāc the voice (faculty of speech), pāṇi the hand (faculty of grasping), pāda the foot (faculty of walking), upastha the genital organ (faculty of copulation) and pāyu the anus (faculty of excretion).
karmaka [karmaka] ifc. amnf karmikā active; that which does.
karmathá [karma] m. good worker.

kárman [kṛ₁man] n. act, action, work; deed, execution, operation; ceremony, sacrifice; work; occupation, profession; destiny | individual function, duty of one's caste | phil. accumulation of merits and faults during past lives; pious work, effective influence, retribution for previous acts | supreme act, holy work | practice (opp. theory); syn. prayoga | gram. the role

thematic [kāraka] of object or purpose (indicated by the accusative in active voice, the nominative in passive voice, or the genitive of an action noun); we distinguish the created object [nirvartya], the transformed object [vikārya], the intended object [prāpya] and the discarded object [anīpsita] [phil. [Vaisesika] the category [padārtha] of activities; tradition gives 5: utksepana the raising, avakṣepaṇa the lowering, ākuñcana the contraction, prasāraņa the expansion and gamana the displacement — n. karma ifc. execution of; destiny of (iic.) | pali kamma. karmaṇi prayogaḥ gram. ["in passive process"] use of the passive voice, where the personal suffix of the verb denotes the object or purpose of the action; opp. kartariprayogah.
karmavat [karmavat] amnf karmavatī busy with his work; employed as a worker gram. used in the role of object.
karmavadbhāva [bhāva] m. gram. use of the subject in the nominative case in the role of object of a verb of progressive action conjugated in the reflexive voice [ātmanepada]; cf. karmakartr.
karmika [karmaika] amnf karmikā active, which acts.
karmin [karmain] amnf karminī active, acting; busy, at work. pāpakarmiņah evildoers.
karmma gem. karma.
karş [ca. kṛṣ] v. [10] pr. (karṣayati) pp. (karṣita) to extract, to tear off; torment.

karşa [act. kṛṣ] m. act of pulling, dragging, or snatching | agriculture — mn weight of gold or silver (a gold coin, about 8 g); there are 4 in a pala; syn. suvarna. pañcaguñjāpramānam tu māṣa ityabhidhīyate māsaih sodaśabhih karsah palam karsacatustayam iti karşalakşanam || It is said that a bean [māṣa] is worth 5 grains [guñjā], a crown [karṣa] 16 beans, a pala 4 crowns, this is the definition of karşa.

karṣaṇa [act. kṛṣ] n. act of pulling, dragging, attracting towards oneself; extraction | act of tormenting extension; prolongation (time, sound) | plowing, cultivation; cultivated field | soc. agriculture; it is an unsuitable means of subsistence for a brahmin | satkarman |.
karṣita [pp. kṛṣ] amnf karṣitā pulled, ar plowed; plowed. tvayā svahastenāmgārāh karsitāh | "you pulled the embers with your own hands"] you brought about your own ruin.
karşin [agt. kṛṣ] amnf karṣinī who pulls, who extracts, who tears out — m. plowman; peasant.
kárhi adv. when? at what time?
karhicit [cid₁] adv. anytime | (with na) never | ang. where.
karhyapi |api| adv. id.

√ kal v. [10] pr. (kaláyati) pr. r. (kalayate) pp. (kalita) pf. (ā, sam) to incite; to excite; to bear | to do, to accomplish, to perform, to produce; to emit (a sound), to murmur | to consider, to observe, to notice; to count, to measure; to know; to believe — ca. (kāláyati) ca. r. (kālayate) to incite; to put forward; to lead (a herd) | to pursue, to chase; to persecute. mūrchām kal to faint. culukam jalasya kal to take a sip of water. কল kala [agt. kal] amnf kalā hoarse, indistinct, weak | inarticulate, low; soft, melodious (voice) — m. cowardly — f. cf. kalā. kalam adv. softly; pleasantly.
kalakala [red.] m. confused noise, hubbub, clamor; not. rumbling of a crowd, cries of impatient children, chirping of birds.
kaladhauta | dhauta | n. ruddy.
kaladhautamaya [maya| amnf kaladhauta mayī golden.
kalamūka | mūka | amnf kalamūkā deafmute.
kalahaṃsa | haṃsa | mf kalahaṃsī organic. zoo. Anser Anser, goose.
kalakatā f. mod. Calcutta. কলঙ্কু kalańka [kalańka] m. stain; mark; rust mark | mark of infamy, blame | (poetry) stain of the Moon — v. [11] pr. (kalankayati) pp. (kalankita) to stain; to defame.
kalankita [pp. kalanka] amnf kalankitā stained; defamed.
kalacuri m. hist. n.p. of the [saṃvat] kalacuri or Kalacūri dynasty, founded in 249; the capital was Māhiṣmatī; cf. Kṛṣṇarāja. কলের kalatra n. woman, wife | female; rump; vagina | citadel.
kalana |agt. kal| amnf kalanā that produces, that causes (iic.) — act. f. kalanā incitement; production.

kalandaka m. bio. zoo. Funambulus palma rum, Indian squirrel (chipmunk) with 3 (or 5) stripes; myth. |Rām.| he helped Rāma build the bridge to Lankā by carrying grains of sand; to thank him, Rāma blessed him with his hand, origin of the stripes.
kalabha [related to karabha] m. young elephant (under 30 years old).
kalabhaka [ka] m. baby elephant

kalama [kal] m. rice harvested in winter | calamus, reed pen | soc. np. of the Ksatriya Ka lama clan of the Kosala country, in the time of Bimbisāra; its members lived in the city of Keśaputra; bd. Bud dha, who preached there, taught them to be wary of established dogmas, scriptures, traditions and received ideas | mod. pen | gr. o; lat. calamus.
kalavinka m. sparrow | cuckoo. কল্ম kalaśa mn vase, pot, cup, jug; syn.

kumbha | churn | jn. sacred symbol of the water pot associated with two divine eyes; cf. aṣṭamaṅgala | arch. pinnacle of a temple (in the shape of a vase) | var. kalasa id. — f. kalaśī water pot, jar; churn | var. kalaśi id. | gr. καλιξ; lat. calix; fr. calice.
kalaśayoni [yoni] m. myth. epith. of Agasti “born in a pot”. কল্ ह kalaha [kalahan₂] m. dispute, litigation, quarrel; fight, brawl | deception; lie — v. [11] pr. r. (kalahāyate) to quarrel.
kalahakāma [kāma] amnf kalahakāmā quarrel them.
kalahakutūhalin [kutūhalin] amnf kalaha kutūhalinī quarrelsome, fond of fights; |Bālarāmāyaṇa| epith. of Nārada.
kalahapriya [priya] amnf kalahapriyā fond of quarrels; myth. is said of Nārada.
kalahaśīla |śīla| amnf kalahaśīlā quarrelsome.

kalā [f. kala] f. small part of a whole, portion, element, atom; sixteenth part | not. sixteenth part of the lunar circle, cf. candrakalā | unit of time (approx. 1 min) | astr. 1 degree of arc (not. of the zodiac) | phon. time of a syllable in prosody | phil. atom of matter | phil. [ChU.] quarter of one of the four quadripartitions [pāda] of brahman | phil. sixteenth part of the complete divine manifestation |pūrṇāvatāra| | math. simb. the number 16 | one of the 64 arts; syn. angavidyā; cf. catuḥṣaṣṭikalās | lit. np. of the Kalā, commentary on the Vaiyākaraņasiddhāntamañjūṣā by Bālambhatta.
kalākāra | kāra | mr. artist.
kalāvat [vat] m. astr. moon (which has phases) — f. Kalāvatī reads. [KSS.] np. of Kalāvatī, daughter of the daitya king Amīla, who granted her as wife to Sūryaprabha.

Kalāpa [Kalāāpa₁] m. ["that which holds together" bond, bundle, bundle; quiver | peacock's tail; ornament in general | totality; collection of objects held together; not. book | lit. quadruple of stanzas [śloka] syntactically connected | gram. np. of the Kalāpa grammar system of the Kātantra — f. kalāpī bundle of grass. kuntalakalāpaḥ who has disheveled hair.
kalāpavat [vat] amnf kalāpavatī gathered in a bundle; forming a sheaf | untied (hair).
kalāpasūtra [sūtra] n. lit. np. of the kalāpasūtra, text of the grammar of the Kātantra; [KSS.] it was said to have been revealed to Sarvavarmā by Kārttikeya.
kalāpin [in] m. bio. zoo. peacock | ved. np. from the scholar kalāpī.

káli [kali] m. losing throw of the dice (of 1) | myth. [Mah.] its personification kali "Bad luck", es pris Mauvais who helped Puşkara win his brother Nala's possessions at dice | dispute, discord; Bad object among several.
kálikāla [kāla₁] m. phil. age of kali: syn. kaliyuga.
kálikālasarvajña [sarvajña] m. hist. n.p. from Ka likālasarvajña "All-knowing of the era of kali", title of the Jain scholar Hemacandra Sūri (11th century).

káliyuga [yuga] n. phil. 4th age of the world, iron age; tradition sets its beginning at the presumed death of Kṛṣṇa in the year 3102 ant.; its king is Jagannātha; [Rām.] the śūdrās acquire the right to practice asceticism [tapasya]; [Mah.] it is embodied by Duryodhana.
kalivarjya [varjya] amnf kalivarjyā soc. (rite, practice) to be avoided in this degraded age | obsolete, outdated.
kalivarjyavinirnaya [vinirnaya] m. bed. n.p. of the Kalivarjyavinirnaya of Dāmodara₁ Bhatta, precisely setting out the prohibitions of kaliyuga.
kalividambana [vidambana] n. lit. np. from the satirical poem Kalividambana, by Nīlakantha₂ Dīkṣita; it is a satire of society, and not. of astrologers.
kalikā [kalika] f. 16th of the moon (unit of time) | bud (of flower); bud.
kálikātā [related to kālīghaṭṭa] f. geo. np. of the city of Kalikātā in Bengal (mod. Calcutta).

kalinga m. geo. np. of the Kalinga country and its people, the Kalingās, on the Coro Mandel coast, extending south of Kataka; Emperor Aśoka conquered it after a bloody war; its capital is Puri; mod. southern Orissa | myth. [Mah.] Sahadeva conquered it so that it would pay tribute to Yudhisthira | myth. np. of the Kalinga king, son of Dīrghatamā and Sudesnā. gato'ham kalingān I went to Kalinga.
kalingadatta [datta] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of kalingadatta, bd. king reigning in Takṣaśilā; his wife Tārādattā gave birth to the princess Kalingasenā, incarnation of the fallen nymph on abhidattā.

Kalingasenā [senā] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the princess Kalingasenā, daughter of king kalingadatta and queen Tārādattā, reincarnating the fallen nymph Surabhidattā, of extraordinary beauty; she became friends with Somaprabhā, who showed her king Udayana, with whom she fell in love, preferring him to the old Prasenajit₂ who had asked for her hand; the young king vidyādhara Madanavega fell in love with her, and by his magical powers impersonated Udayana to abuse her; from this union was born a boy, to whom on the order of Siva was substituted a girl, incarnation of Rati, to become the wife Madanamañcukā of Naravāhanadatta, in incarnating Kāma.
kalita [pp. kal] amnf kalitā incited; led; produced | held (not. sword) | divided, separated.
kalinda m. geo. np. of Mount Kalinda, from which the Yamunā originates | pl. geo. np. of the people and country of the Kalindas .
kalindavarman [varman] m. bed. [DKC.] np. of Ka lindavarmā, king of the Kāmarūpās; Kalpasundarī is his daughter.

kalila [kalila] amnf kalilā full of, green neck of | impenetrable — n. thicket; heap; embarrassment. কলুম kaluṣa amnf kaluṣā dirty, troubled, tur belly, muddy; impure | hoarse (voice) — m. buffalo — f. kaluṣā buffalo — n. dirt, impurity | fault, sin — v. [11] pr. (kaluṣayati) pp. (kaluṣita) to soil, pollute, contaminate — v. [11] pr. r. (kaluṣāyate) to become troubled, soiled. kaluşīkṛ to pollute, soil. krodhena kaluṣīkṛtaḥ |Rām.| choked with anger. kaluşībhū to become disturbed; to become dirty.
kalevara mn body | lat. cadaver. কল্ক kalka m. residue; deposit, dregs; paste, filth, dirt, hypocrisy, falsehood, deceit.

kalkin [kalkain] m. [nom. Kalkī] myth. np. of Kalkī, 10th avatar of Vishnu as a horseman of the Apocalypse; he will come to destroy the universe at the end of the Kali Yuga; he is represented as a white rider on a black horse, or as a black rider on a black horse (Jagannātha) accompanied by a white rider on a white horse (Balabha dra) | bd. [Kālacakra] designates one of the last 25 kings of the mythical kingdom of Sambhala; the first is Mañjuśrīyaśā, the second is Pundarīka₄ | var. kalki id.
kalp [ca. klp] v. [10] pr. (kalpayati) pr. r. (kalpayate) pp. (kalpita) to make, to produce; to order, to appoint (to a function). bhāgaśas kalp var. bhāgam bhāgam kalp to divide into parts.

kálpa |agt. klp| amnf kalpā feasible, possible, practicable | skillful; suitable for, apt for g. inf. rangle act. m. production, manufacture | means, process; precept, rule, law; ritual — ifc. similar to, approaching, almost (iic.); approximately, roughly; model of (iic.) | phil. great cosmological cycle of creation, where the material Uni is created, degrades and is annihilated during the kalpānta | myth. cosmological period of one (half-day) of Brahmā, duration of a creation of the universe, worth 1000 great eras [mahāyuga] (approximately 4.32 billion years); each kalpa consists of 14 eras of Manu [manvantara]; 100 Brahmic years form one mahākalpa | phil. The ritual, one of the 6 limbs of the Veda [vedānga] | alternative; syn. pakṣa | investigation, research; determination. Astral work, thorough work, not. tantraparīkṣā med. treatment of the sick, therapy; preparation of remedies, pharmacy | lat. corpus; pali kappa. sa mrtakalpah he is almost dead. svakarmani na kalpah incompetent in his function. yadā na śāsitum kalpaḥ if he is incapable of governing. bhikṣukalpaḥ who is not quite a monk. trnakalpah which consists almost entirely of grass. rājakalpo devadattah Devadatta is almost a king.

Kalpataru | taru | mr. myth. cf. kalpavrksa | bed. n.p. from the Kalpataru, commentary on the Bhāmatī, due to Amalānanda Sarasvatī₂; cf. Abhoga, Parimala₁ |lit. n.p. from Kalpataru₁, cf. Kṛtyakalpataru.
kalpadru [dru₃] m. cf. kalpavṛkṣa. Kalpadrukośa kośa m. bed. n.p. from Kalpadrukośa, dictionary of synonyms due to Keśava₄.
kálpadruma [druma] m. cf. kalpavṛkṣa.
kalpadrumakalikā [kalikā] f. jn. n.p. of the Kal padrumakalikā or Kalpadrukalikā "Bud of the Tree of Plenty", which forms the Jain Kalpasūtra.
kálpalatā [latā] f. myth. fabulous vine, which accompanies all desires.
kálpavrksa [vrksa] m. myth. magic tree that grants what one desires; it is one of the 5 trees of the
Indra's paradise [Svarga]; in its shade Kāmadhenu rests; cf. pañcavṛkṣa, Cūṭa | bio. by extension coconut palm.

kalpasundarī [sundarī] f. lit. [DKC.] np. of the beautiful kalpasundarī "Accomplished Beauty", daughter of King Kalindavarmā; she was married to the ugly Vikațavarmā, whom she hated; she fell in love with Upahāravarmā, helped him kill the tyrant, and married him.
Kalpasūtra [sūtra] n. pl. soc. collection of ritual injunctions; the injunctions of the Kalpasūtra form the vedānga of the ritual; collections of rites are distinguished
solemn [śrautasūtra] of those concerning the rites

domestic [smārtasūtra]; cf. Kāśyapakalpasūtra, Baudhāyana, Pārāśarakalpasūtra | lit. sacred writing of the śvetāmbara jaina canon, in the ard hamāgadhī language; it comprises three sections: the lives of the saints [Jinacaritra], the homage to the masters
ancients [Sthavirāvalī] and monastic discipline [Sāmācārī].
kalpasūtratīkākāra |tīkākāra| mr. bed. commentator on the Kalpasūtra.
kalpānta [anta] m. myth. end of the World (end of the present kalpa); cf. Ananta.
kalpana [act. klp] n. formation, fabrication; invention; ornament, adornment — f. cf. kalpanā.

kalpanā [f. kalpana] f. fabrication, preparation | disposition, arrangement, composition supposition, hypothesis; imagination, illusion, fiction; invention | phil. |Dinnāga| construction of a concept by perception.
kalpanāgaurava | gaurava | n. phil. complexity of a description.
kalpanāpodha [apodha] amnf kalpanāpodhā phil. devoid of construction (said of a non-conceptualized perception). kalpanāpodham abhrāntam phil. direct perception free from error.
kalpanāmaṇḍitikā [maṇḍitikā] f. lit. np. of the kal panāmaṇḍitikā, bd. work of Kumāralāta.
kalpanālāghava [lāghava] n. phil. principle of economy of hypotheses | gram. minimal presupposition of an utterance.
kalpanāśakti | śakti | f. power of imagination; in inventiveness.
kalpanīya [pfp. [2] kļp] amnf kalpanīyā which can be accomplished; practicable, possible | which must be assumed; which must be arranged.
kalpita [pp. That. klp] amnf kalpitā ima giné — n. bed. (philology) conjectured text.
kalpitatva [vat] n. imagination; fiction.
kalpitavrtta [vrtta] n. lit. novel; fictional narrative.

kalmaşa [related to kaluşa] amnf kalmaşā dirty, soiled; impure; evil — n. stain, dirt; impurity, defilement | (figuratively) sin. yotsye vigatakalmaşah lit. [Mah.] Yudhişthira: I want to fight without sin.
kalmāṣa amnf kalmāṣī variegated, variegated; spotted, speckled; black — f. kalmāṣī myth. epith. of kalmāṣī "Variegated", cow of plenty of Jama dagni.
kalmāṣadhvaṃsa | dhvaṃsa | m. destruction of sin.
kalmāṣadhvaṃsakārin [kārin] afmn kalmāṣadhvamsakārinī which causes the destruction of sin | which avoids crime.

kalmāṣapāda [pāda] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā kalmāṣapāda "with stained feet"; he is Saudāsa "son of King Sudāsa₁" of the solar dynasty, also called Mitrasaha; he was cursed by his pu rohita Vasistha for refusing priority to his son Sakti₁ and striking him; Vasistha sent him the evil spirit Kimkara; one day, a brahmin came to him asking for a mutton meal; the king had a man killed, whom he served as a meal; the brahmin cursed him, and condemned him to become a vampire [rākṣasa]; he devoured the 100 sons of Vasiṣṭha, then tried to devour Vasistha himself, who finally exorcised him; During his curse [śāpa], he had surprised a Brahmin couple making love, had devoured the man, and had been cursed by the woman, condemning him to sterility; he asked Vasistha to cure the queen, who became pregnant by him; as she still had not given birth after 12 years of pregnancy, she opened her belly with a cutting stone to deliver her son Aśmaka₁; he continued the dynasty; King Dilīpa₂ is his descendant; cf. Prayrddha.

kalya [pfp. [1] kal] amnf kalyā well-being, healthy; vigorous; strong | pleasant, auspicious; instructive | ready; prepared for (loc. inf.) — n. health dawn, morning; yesterday lpl. geo. people of the Kalyās, brahmins of Kaśmīra origin | gr. o ; ang. whole. kalyam var. kalye adv. at dawn; in the morning | tomorrow.

Kalyāṇa [kalyaana] amnf Kalyāṇī beautiful, excellent, happy, noble; amiable — voc. adr. term of politeness for a person (present or absent) — n. happy event; good fortune, happiness, prosperity | good, virtue (opp. pāpa); advantage, salvation | myth. wedding ceremony; cf. Jāmbavatī — m. mus. name of a nocturnal musical mode [rāga] | arch. np. of Kalyāṇa, epith. of Shiva "accompanied by Gaurī"; it is one of the 16 aspects of Shiva | hist. np. of the Kalyāna₁ dynasty of the Western Cālukyās; from the name of their capital Kalyāṇī | hist. np. Kalyāṇa₂ Malla, court writer to the Afghan prince of Oudh Lāḍkhān, around 1500; he is the author of the Anangaranga and the Sulaimac caritra — f. kalyānī cow | geo. np. of the city of Kalyānī in Karņātaka (mod. Basavakalyāna in the district of Bidār); it was founded by King Someśvara₁; Basavanna taught there. kalyāṇabhogamokṣam lit. [Srīnātha] sweetness of pleasures and freedom.
kalyāṇaka [aka] amnf kalyāṇikā prosperous, happy; favorable | effective — f. kalyāṇikā arse nic.
Kalyāṇakaṭaka [kaṭaka] mn geo. np. of the land of Kalyāṇakaṭaka, "Jolival".
kalyāṇakāraka [kāraka] n. lit. np. from kalyāṇakāraka, a Jain medical work by Ugrāditya (circa 800) dealing in particular with personal hygiene.
kalyāṇamalla [Malla] m. hist. n.p. by kalyāṇamalla, author of the Anaṅgaraṅga "Erotic", (16th century).
kalyāṇamitra [mitra] n. esteemed friend; noble advisor | person of good counsel; opp. pāpamitra.

kalyāṇasaugandhika [saugandhika] n. bio. bot. Hedychium coronarium, white ginger lily, with a sweet fragrance | myth. [Mah.] Bhīma went in search of these flowers at the request of Pāncālī/Draupadī; on the way, he met his half-brother Hanumān disguised as an old monkey, blocking the road with his tail; Bhīma could not move it despite his Herculean strength; Hanumān then told him about his origins; this is a favorite theme of Kathākeli theatre in Kerala.
kalyāṇācāra |ācāra| amnf kalyāṇācārā who behaves well.
kalyāṇin |in| amnf kalyāṇinī happy, chan those, prosperous; illustrious; virtuous — f. kalyāṇinī bio. bot. Sida cordifolia, white mallow; it contains ephedrine, it is medicinal.
kallața m. hist. [Trika] np. of the Kaśmīra philosopher Kallata Bhatta, student of Vasugupta (late 8th century); under his direction he composed the Span dakārikās.
kallola m. vague.
kallolinī [in] f. torrent, river.

kalhaṇa m. hist. np. du paṇḍita kalhaṇa, son of Campaka, poet and historian of Kaśmīra of the 12th century, author of the dynastic epic Rājataramginī; he is also credited with the Ode to God An drogyne Ardhanāriśvarastotra.
kava [related to ku₁] pf. (pejorative particle) bad, bad; small; worn, deficient — amnf kavā stingy.
kávaca mn cuirass, armor; corset, jacket | mushroom — n. soc. piece of bark bearing a magic formula; mystical syllable in an invocation; amulet — f. kavacā ifc. armor of (iic.).
kavacamantra [mantra] n. soc. [Tantra] magical formula of protection; it is worn as an amulet in a small metal box around the neck.
kavacin [in] amnf kavacinī who wears a rough leather.
kavayitṛ [agt. That. kū] m. poet — f. kavayitrī poetess.
kavara [ka₁vara₁] amnf kavarā various; mixed (color); inlaid — m. lecturer, preacher — f. kavarī braid of hair.
kavarga [(ka)varga] m. phone. the guttural class.
kavala m. mouthful, mouthful — v. [11] pr. (kavalayati) ["to make a mouthful"] to swallow, to devour. kavalīkṛ to swallow; to devour.

kaví [agt. kū] m. poet; bard | inspired; skillful; wise, prophet | ved. visionary poet; singer of revealed hymns myth. np. of Kavi "Poet", epithet of Sukra | pl. Kavayas myth. np. of the Kavayas, spirits of the sages of old; they gravitate around the Sun — v. [11] pr. (kavīyati) to act like a poet; to pretend to be a poet.
kavikanthābharana [kanthābharana] n. lit. np. from the Kavikanthābharana "Collar of the poet", manual of poetic composition due to Kşemendra.
kavíkalpadruma [kalpadruma] m. gram. n.p. from the Kavikalpadruma, treatise on the Sanskrit verb due to Vopadeva.
kavíkāmadhenu [kāmadhenu] f. lit. np. of the Ka vikāmadhenu "Treasury of the poet", commentary on the Amarakoşa by Subhūticandra, composed between 1050 and 1120.
kavíkratu | kratu | amnf phil. who possesses omniscient divine vision.
kavítā [tā] f. poetry; state of being a poet. uttamā kavitā first-rank poetry.
kavitāvali |āvali| f. bed. n.p. from the kavitāvali, a theology of poetry in 325 verses by Tulasīdāsa.
kavítvá |tva| n. poetic art; quality of poet.
kavípraśasti [praśasti] f. lit. praise of poets.
kavímānin [mānin] amnf kavimāninī who thinks he's a poet.

kavírahasya [rahasya] n. lit. np. of the Kavirahasya₁ "Secret Poetry" of Halāyudha₁; it is a grammar of Sanskrit disguised as a royal panegyric l lit. np. of the Kavirahasya₁, first book (and only completed) of the Kāvyamīmāmsā of Rājaśekhara.

kavírāja | rājan | m. hist. np. of Kavirāja, title of "King of Poets"; cf. Viśvanātha₁ | hist. np. of Ka virāja₁, court poet of Kāmadeva₁ in Vanavāsī (12th century); he is the author of the Rāghavapāṇḍavīya; in it he develops a theoretical analysis of the mode of conarration with ślesa .
kavirājamārga [rājamārga] n. bed. n.p. from the Ka virājamārga "Royal Way of Poets", poetic treatise in Kannada language due to King Amoghavarşa₁ (850).
kavísasta [sasta₁] amnf kavisastā recited by the cantor (said from a mantra). kavíšikṣā [śikṣā] f. bed. manual of poetic composition.
kavisamaya [samaya] m. lit. poetic convention; poetic license cf. Rājaśekhara.
kavisamavāya [samavāya] m. meeting of poets; poetic competition.
kavisamāja [samāja] m. poetry competition.
kavisammelana [sammelana] n. meeting of poets, improvisation contest.
kavisārvabhauma [sārvabhauma] m. lit. "Emperor of poets", self-proclaimed title of Śrīnātha.
Kavīndra [indra] m. title of Kavīndra "prince among poets".

kavīndrācārya |ācārya| m. hist. np. du paṇḍita kavīndrācārya Sarasvatī₂; he lived at the Mughal court around (1600–1675); he is the author of the Kavīndrakalpadruma (in Hindi) and the collection of poems Jagadvijayacchandas.
kavim [acc. kavi] iic.

kavimmanya | manya | amnf kavimmanyā (pej.) who thinks he is a poet; syn. kavimānin. kavimmanyasya hi puratah sūktamaranyaruditam syādviplaveta ca [KM.] (Reciting) a beautiful word before a so-called poet is to groan in the desert, and (only lead to) confusion.

kavyá [pfp. [1] kū] amnf kavyā ved. sage; priest in charge of sacrifice — n. offering to the shades. কাষা káśa m. whip; reins — f. káśā whip; rope; bridle, rein. কিষ্পু kaśipu mn cushion, pillow; mat, mattress.
kaśipūpabárhaná | upabarthana | n. sg. (collective) cushions and rugs.

Kaśeru var. kaseru mn spinal column myth. one of the 10 regions | dvīpa | forming the jam budvīpa, south of Mount Meru | bio. rhizome of the tuberous bulrush bot. Cyperus esculentus, water plant used in medicine — f. kaśerū myth. np. of Kaśerū, daughter of Tvaṣṭā; [Mah.] kidnapped at 14 years old by the asura Naraka, she was freed by Kṛṣṇa whom she married.
kaścana |ka₁cana| mnf someone, whoever. tatra kaścana brāhmaņo vasati a certain brah mane lives there. na kaścana person, no one. na kaścana śrnoti mām nobody listens to me.
kaścit [ka₁cid₁] mnf someone, whoever; a certain; whoever. na kaścit person, no one. na kaścid api absolutely no one.
kaśmala [ka₁mala] amnf kaśmalā f. kaśmalī dirty, impure | timid, pusillanimous — n. dirt; impurity, sin — mnf kaśmalā stupefaction; weakness, lack of courage.
kaśmīra m. geo. np. of kaśmīra (Cache mire), country of Northwest India, foothills of the Himalayas | pl. kaśmīrās its inhabitants — f. kaśmīrī the kaśmīrī language.

kaśyápa |related to kacchapa| m. tortoise | myth. np. of Kaśyapa₁, first of the saptarși; |Mah.| he is son of the brahmarși Marīci; he is a prolific universal progenitor; he married 13 of Daksa's daughters; he is father of the gods |deva| and later of Vāmana (by his wife Aditi), of the demons |daitya| (by his wife Diti), of the undines [dānava] (by his wife Danu), of Aruna and Garuda (by his wife Vinatā), of the dragons [nāga] (by his wife Kadrū), of the winds [rudra] and of Rohinī₂ (by his wife Surabhī), of the centaur genies [gandharva] and gnomes |yakṣa| by his wife |Munī|, and wild animals (by his wife Krodhā); he embodies the divine power of procreation; [HV.] guru of Varuna, he stole the cows of his sacrifice to give them to Surabhī and Aditi; Varuṇa having complained to Brahmā, the latter proposed to Nārāyaṇa that as punishment Kaśyapa₁ should descend to Earth as the cowherd Vasudeva, to marry Surabhī incarnated as Rohinī₃ and Aditi incarnated as Devakī; [Mah.] Takṣaka paid him so that he would not go to the aid of Parīkṣit | hist. np. of the philosopher Kaśyapa₁, founder of the Vaiśesika system, known as Kaṇāda || pali Kassapa.
kaśyapaparivarta [parivarta] m. bed. n.p. from the kaśyapaparivarta, text from the comic. Mahāyāna in for
mules [sūtra] (before the 7th century); a later version contains parts in verse in an archaic style.
kaśyápasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. bed. [Tantra] n.p. from the Kaśyapasamhitā, a demonology text.
kaśyápasūnujyeṣṭha [sūnujyeṣṭha] m. myth. “eldest son of Kaśyapa₁”, epith. of Hiranyākṣa.

√ কিছ্ kaş v. [1] pr. (kaşati) pr. r. (kaşate) fut. (kasisyati) pp. (kasita) pf. (ni) to rub, scratch, scrape | to injure; to destroy — pr. r. (kaṣate) to scratch; to itch — ca. (kāṣayati) to injure. ক্স kaṣa [agt. kaṣ] ifc. amnf kaṣā that scratches, that rubs (iic.).
kaṣaṇa | act. kaṣ| n. act of rubbing, scraping | not. gold testing by touchstone.

kaṣāya [related to kaṣ] amnf kaṣāyā astrin gent | orange; red; brown — mn phil. |Nyāya| astringent, a type of taste [rasa]; [Bṛhajjātaka] it is associated with the planet Saturn |Sani| | dark red color (not. of monastic robes) herbal decoction, infusion; potion; ointment, balm; gum, resin | application of cosmetics and perfumes | impurity, dirt; defect; sin | emotion, passion | phil. pollution of thoughts by desires | jn. attachment to actions. kaṣāyīkṛ to redden, to dye red. kaṣāyīkṛtalocana amnf kaṣāyīkṛtalocanā one who has reddened eyes.
kaṣāyaprabhṛta [prabhṛta] n. lit. np. from the kaṣāyaprabhṛta "Treatise on the Passions", sacred Jain text of the digambarās.
kaṣāyita [kaṣāyaita] amnf kaṣāyitā rougi; coloured, dyed.

kaṣita [pp. kaṣ] amnf kaṣitā scratched, rubbed; wounded. কষ্ট kaṣṭa |pp. kaṣ| amnf kaṣṭā bad, wicked; severe, rigorous; painful; dangerous, fatal | inaccessible — n. evil, misfortune; in fortune, misery; difficulty; fatigue, stress — v. [11] pr. r. (kaṣṭāyate) to strive to commit evil. kaştam alas! misfortune! misery! woe is me! kanyāpitrtvam khalu nāma kastam [PT.] To be the father of a daughter is certainly a calamity.
kaṣṭáśrita [śrita] amnf kaṣṭaśritā who is in a distressing situation; unhappy | doing penance.
kaṣṭāṅka |aṅka| m. degree of difficulty.
√ kas v. [1] pr. (kasati) pp. (kasta, kasita) ca. (kāsayati) pf. (nis, vi) [unusual without pf.].
kasun nota. gram. kṛt₂ suffix 'as' used for the infinitive.
kaseru cf. kaśeru.
kastūrikā [kastūrīka] f. bio. zoo. musk deer | musk.
kastūrī f. musc.

kastūrīgandha | gandha | amnf kastūrīgandhī musky — f. kastūrīgandhī myth. [Mah.] np. of kastūrīgandhī "with the scent of musk", epith. of Sa tyavatī after Parāśara had changed his fishy odor into the odor of musk; cf. Gandhavatī.
kastūrīmīga [mrga] m. organic. zoo. Moschus moscife rus, musk deer.
kásmāt [abl. ka₁] adv. why? how? from where? || pali kamhā kasmād agacchasi where do you come from?
kásmin [loc. kim] adv. in whom, in what?
kasmimścit [cid₁] adv. in some place; nowhere. kasmimścin nagare vasati sma nrpah the king lived in a certain city.
kásmai [dat. kim] adv. to whom, to what?
kasya | g. ka₁ | ind. from whom.
kasyacit [cid₁] adv. of whoever.
kasyām [loc. kā] ind. in something (f.).
kasyāñcit [cid₁] adv. in whatever (f.) it may be. kasyāñcidavasthāyām in whatever situation it may be.
kahlāra |ka₂hlād| n. bio. bot. Nymphæa lo tus, White water lily | "that loves water" |.
kā [f. kim] pn. f. interr. who? which? — iic. part. pejorative.

Kātantra [tantra] n. [kātantravyākaraṇa] lit. np. of the Kātantra "abridged system", Simplified Sanskrit Grammatical Treatise, without treatment of Vedic forms, due to Sarvavarmā; also called Kaumāra and Kumāravyākaraņa.

Kātantrakaumudī [kaumudī] f. bed. n.p. of the Kātantrakaumudī, commentary on the Kātantra due to Govardhana₁. kātantraparišista [parišista] n. bed. n.p. of the kātantrapariśiṣṭa, supplement to the Kātantra due to Śrīpatidatta. kātantravyākaraņa [vyākaraņa] n. bed. n.p. from Kātantravyākaraņa, Grammatical Treatise of Sarvavarmā.

kārohaṇa | rohaṇa | n. geo. np. of kārohaṇa, a locality in southern Gujarāt, the origin of the pāśupata movement in the 7th century; it is venerated as the place of manifestation of Shiva in every cosmic age.
kāṃsya [*kaṃsaya] amnf kāṃsyā in copper, in brass — n. brass; brass goblet gong (struck with a stick). veņumrdangakāmsyam (collective) the flutes, the drums and the gongs.
kāṃsyabojana | bhojana | n. meal eaten from a copper bowl.

kāṃsyabojananyāya [nyāya] m. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] analogy of a meal eaten from a copper bowl; it explains the master's use of a copper bowl so that his student can fulfill his ritual duties by eating his leftovers; it justifies adapting a primary rite to perform a non-contradictory secondary rite. কাক kāka [onomatopoeia] mf Kākī bio. zoo. cor neille; corbeau; syn. vāyasa | (pej. metaphorically) scoundrel, untrustworthy person; cripple arch. the raven, a matrix [yoni] of the āyādi system — f. Kākī myth. [Mah.] np. of Kākī, one of the 7 "(dangerous) mothers to children" [śiśumātaras] associated with Skanda. kākah kṣīram pītvā kokilah na bhavati A crow does not become a cuckoo by drinking milk. na tvā kākam manye You are no better than a crow.
kākaguha [guha] m. ["hidden from crows"] sesame.
kākatāla [tāla] m. of. crow and palmyra fruit.

kākatālīya [īya] amnf kākatālīyā (unexpected event) "as in the fable of the crow and the palmyra"; accidental, due to fate — n. [kākatālīyanyāya] lit. fable where a crow lands on a palmyra just as its fruit falls and kills it. kākatālīyam suddenly; by accident.
kākatālīyavat [vat] adv. ["as in the fable of the crow and the palmyra" accidentally.
kākati [ti] f. myth. np. of kākati, form of Durgā venerated at Ekasilā.

kākatīya [īya] m. soc. worshipper of kākati | Hindu dynasty of the Deccan; it reigned between the 12th and 14th century in Ekaśilā; cf. Rudrāmbā, Pratāparudra₁ | pl. kākatīyās geo. np. of the people of the kākatīyās, in Telugu country [Andhra].
kākapakṣa [pakṣa] m. ["raven's wing"] curls on the temples of young men, the rest of the head being shaved.
kākapakṣadhara [dhara] afmn kākapakṣadharī who wears curls at the temples; adolescent.
kākapada | pada | n. mark of a crow's foot; V-shaped figure.
kākapeya [peya] amnf kākapeyā (water) no
potable ["only a crow would drink it"] | (water) little
deep ["the crow can drink from it (by touching the bottom)"] — f. kākapeyā river whose water is murky.
kākarava [rava] amnf kākaravā who cries like a crow | coward — m. soc. coward; ba nal man.
kākala [the] mn larynx; Adam's apple.
kākalaka [ka] n. id. kākaśańkin [śańkin] amnf kākaśańkinī wary as a crow.
kākākṣi |akṣi| n. crow's eye (presumed unique, and passing from one orbit to the other) gram. constituent shared by two contiguous phrases.

kākākṣinyāya [nyāya] m. gram. rule of linking a constituent both to the left and to the right. kākākṣinyāyena var. kākākṣinyāyāt adv. gram. by being linked by the preceding word and by the following word.
kākākṣivat [vat] adv. ["like a crow's eye looking from right to left" in two ways; in a double dependence
kākodumbara [udumbara] m. organic. bot. Ficus op positiveolia, fig tree with opposite leaves.
kākolūka [ulūka] n. the crow and the owl (as a pair of sworn enemies).
kākolūkikā |ika| f. enmity between the crow and the owl.
kākolūkīya [īya] m. lit. "(War) of the crow and the owl", title of the 3rd book of the Pañcatantra, which teaches the danger of trusting strangers.
kākaṇī f. sou, small coin; cf. kākiņī | [Mayamata] area measure, of 8 fathoms [danda] squared (approximately 2.5 ares); there are 4 in a māṣa .
kākiṇī f. sou, small coin (quarter of a paṇa) | guñjā seed used as a measure of weight | var. kākinī id.

kākiṇīka [ka] amnf kākiṇīkā which is worth a kākiņī. কাকু kāku f. intonation; accent, emphasis | gram. tone of voice, not. interrogative | lit. rhetorical question cry of distress; lamentation, complaint; murmur.
Kākutstha [*kakutstha] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of Kākutstha "Descendant of kakutstha", patr. not. of Raghu, Daśaratha, Rāma and his brothers.
kākúd [*kakud] f. palace (mouth) — n. kākuda id.
kākola [kākala] m. crow | var. kākāla id. kālakākolavalayam a flock of black crows.
kākṣīvata [*kakṣīvata] amnf kākṣīvatī relating to, derived from, composed by Kakṣīvān.
kāgada n. paper.
kāgadapattra | pattra | n. sheet of paper.
√ kāṅkṣ [related to kam] v. [1] pr. (kāṅkṣati) v. [1] pr. r. (kānkṣate) pp. (kānkṣita) pf. (ā) to desire, to hope; to aspire to (acc. dat.).
kāṅkṣā [act. kāṅkṣ] ifc. f. desire, wish.
kānkṣita [pp. kānkṣ] amnf kānkṣitā desired, hoped for — n. desire, wish.
kāṅkṣin [agt. kāṅkṣ] amnf kāṅkṣiṇī who desires, who wishes; who waits.
kācá m. glass; crystal; quartz | pl. glass beads.
kācábhājana | bhājana | n. glass container, crystal cup, goblet.
kācámaṇi [maṇi] m. rock crystal; quartz.
kācana n. string for holding a package or for binding the pages of a manuscript.
kācanaka |ka| n. id.
kāñcana [agt. kāś] amnf kāñcanī in gold; gold color — n. gold — f. kāñcanī turmeric.
kāñcanadaṃṣṭra [daṃṣṭrā] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara king Kāncanadamṣṭra, enemy of Na ravāhanadatta.

kāñcanaśṛṅga [śṛṅga] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the mythical city Kāncanaśrnga "Golden Horn" in the Himalayas, capital of the vidyādhara prince Hema prabha; it is also that of the vidyādhara king Sphatikayaśā.

Kāñcī [*kañc] f. belt (not. of woman) | geo. np. of Kāñcī or Kāñcīpura, in Tamil Nadu; it is one of the 7 sacred cities [saptapurī] | lit. [alaṃkāra] variety of yamaka where the repetition occurs at the beginning of each line of a stanza.
Kāñcīpura [pura] n. geo. np. of the city of Kāncīpura, in Tamil Nadu; cf. Kāncī.
kāñjika var. kāñjīka n. gruel, fermented rice porridge — f. kāñjī id.

Kāṭvā f. geo. np. of the city of Kāṭvā in Bengale; Caitanya received her initiation [dīkṣā] there by Keśava₁ in January 1510; on the site stands the temple of Gaurānga, a Vaishnava pilgrimage site. কাতক Kāṭhaka [*kaṭhaka] m. inhabitant of kaṭha |pl. the people of kaṭhākās — n. lit. np. of the Kāṭhaka, recension of the Black Yajurveda attributed to Katha; cf. Kāthakagrhyasūtra, Mādhyamikā — amnf kāthakā hist. attributed to Katha.
kāthakagrhyasūtra [grhyasūtra] n. lit. np. of the Kāthakagrhyasūtra, a collection of hymns for mestic use.
kāthakasamhitā [samhitā] f. lit. np. of the Kāthakasamhitā, collection of the first brāhmana texts.
kāthina [*kathina] n. hardness; rigidity.
kāṭhinya [*kaṭhinaya] n. hardness; rigidity; severity; firmness | difficulty; obscurity (of style).
kāṇá [related to kaṇ] amnf kāṇā f. kāṇī one-eyed; pierced, punctured, perforated (by (i.)); blind. akṣṇā kāṇaḥ one-eyed.

Kāṇabhūti [bhūti] m. lit. [KSS.] np. du piśāca Kāṇabhūti "Blind Destiny", Earth incarnation of the yakṣa Supratīka₃ by Kubera's curse; he received the Bṛhatkathā from Puṣpadanta₃ incarnated in Vararuci; his curse will end when he tells the story to Mālyavān₂ incarnated in Guṇāḍhya.

kāṇāda [*kaṇāda] amnf kāṇādā phil. ["belonging to kaṇāda"] logic. kāṇādam pāṇinīyam ca sarvaśāstropakārakam Logic and linguistics are prerequisites for all science. কাণ্ড kāṇḍa [act. khaṇḍ] mn segment; not. portion of bamboo stalk between two nodes lit. chapter, division, section of a work; not. book of the Satapatha brāhmaṇa, which comprises 14; it is divided into readings | prapāṭhaka | and lessons [adhyāya] | soc. division of a sacrificial rite heaven | department, division, subject | trunk (tree), branch, stem (plant) | sheaf, bundle, pile; multitude of bones of the arm or leg; not. femur | reed, bamboo; arrow — f. kāṇḍā ifc. section of, etc. — f. kāṇḍī ifc. id.
kāṇḍabhagna | bhagna | n. fracture.
kāṇḍamaya |maya| amnf kāṇḍamayī made of reed or bamboo — f. kāṇḍamayī variety of lute.
kāṇḍalāva |lāva| amnf kāṇḍalāvī reed cutter.
kāṇvá [*kaṇva] amnf kāṇvā relating to Kanva — m. descendant of Kanva.
kānvaśākhā [śākhā] f. bed. recension of the vājasaneyisaṃhitā (white Yajurveda) attributed to Kanva.
kāt [kad] pf. pejorative (before kṛ₁ and its derivatives, to insult).
kātkṛta [kṛta] amnf kātkṛtā insulted, dishonored.
kātara [*katara] amnf kātarā timid; fearful; cowardly | confused; perplexed; embarrassed; fearful (loc. inf. iic.).
kātaratā |tā| f. cowardice; timidity; confusion.
kātaratva |tva| n. id. | discouragement.
Kātya [contr. Kātyāyana] m. hist. np. from the ancient lexicographer Kātya; cf. Kātyāyana.

Kātyāyana [*Katiāyana] m. "descendant of Kati" | Hist. np. of Kātyāyana, grammarian of the 3rd century BCE, author of commentaries [vārttika] on the aphorisms [sūtra] of Pāṇini, trans. by the Mahābhāsya of Patañjali₁ | Hist. np. of Kātyāyana₁, mathematician (around 200 BCE), to whom we owe a treatise [śulbasūtra] later than those of Baudhāyana and Apastamba | Hist. np. of Kātyāyana₂, specialist in law [vyavahāra], author of the Kātyāyanasmṛti; he lived between 300 and 600 BCE | bd. np. of Kātyāyana₃, disciple of Buddha — f. Kātyāyanī myth. np. of Kātyāyanī, tantric form of frightening Durgā, brandishing a sword; she is celebrated on the 6th day of navarātra | lit. np. of Kātyāyanī₁, one of the two wives of Yājñavalkya.
kātyāyanasmṛti [smṛti] f. lit. np. of the kātyāyanasmṛti, important legal text |vyavahāra| composed between 300 and 600.
kādamba [*kadamba] m. bio. kind of goose with grey wings; syn. kalahamsa — n. bio. flower of the ka damba.
kādambara [*kadambara] mn skin on milk or cream — f. cf. Kādambarī.

Kādambarī [f. kādambara] f. juice of the flowers of the kadamba; intoxicating liqueur obtained by its distillation; myth. AdyāKālī drinks it in a skull |liqueur in gen. |lit. |K.| np. of the nymph |apsaras| Kādambarī "the Intoxicating One", daughter of the gandharva king Citraratha and the nymph Madirā; she swore not to marry any boy as long as Mahāśvetā mourned the suicide of Puṇḍarīka₂; when Prince Candrāpīda₁ visited her, they fell in love, but they had to wait for the resolution of many dramas to finally know love [lit. A romantic tale [kathā₁] bearing the same name as Bāṇa₂ Bhaṭṭa, in which she is a heroine, written in prose, within the Sanskrit literary genre of fiction.
marvelous [utprekṣā]; this labyrinth of intrigues, twists and turns, is a masterpiece of interwoven stories and poetic turns [alankāraśāstra], notably of

metaphors [upamā₂] In his description of Ujjayinī and Lake Acchoda; the erotic atmosphere, the irony emanating from the dithyrambic techniques, and the subtly maintained suspense make this novel captivating; Bāna₂ composed the first part [Pūrvabhāga] during his lifetime; the second part [Uttarabhāga] was completed by his son Bhūṣaṇa according to his plans; cf. Pundarīka₂, Candrāpīda₁ | lit. kadamba flower sent as an arrow of desire by Kāma to King Śūdraka₂ | myth. [BhP.] np. of the Kādambarī₁, a river in Jambudvīpa originating from a kadamba trunk, flowing westward. kādambarīrasajñānām āhāro'pi na rocate The lover of Kādambarī (or kadamba alcohol) even forgets to eat. yuktam kādambarīm śrutvā kavayo maunam āśritāḥ | bāṇadhvanāvanadhyāyo bhavatīti smṛtir yataḥ || [Kīrtikaumudī] It is appropriate for poets to remain silent when listening to Kādambarī, because according to tradition the recitation should be interrupted (at the sound of the arrow/at the hearing of Bāṇa).
kādambarīkathā [kathā₁] f. bed. history of Kādambarī.
kādambarīkathāsāra [sāra] m. lit. np. of the Kādambarīkathāsara "Essence of the tale of Kādambarī", epic poem by Abhinanda presenting more simply the complicated plot of the novel of Bāna₂.
kādambinī [*kadambain] f. cloud, bank of clouds.
kādraveyá [*Kadrūīya] m. myth. ["son of Kadrū"] refers to certain dragons [nāga] such as Ar buda.
kān [acc. pl. ka₁] ind. such.
kāṃskān | red. | ind. such and such. kāṃskān bhojayati he feeds such and such.
kānac nota. gram. primary suffix [kṛt₂] ' āna' used for the middle perfect participle, like dadāna.
kānana [act. ca. kan] n. wood, forest, grove.
kāni [nom. pl. kim] ind. which ones? yāni kāni ca mitrāņi all friends without exception. kānicit [ cid₁ ₁] n. pl. any of them. yāni kānicit anything.

kānīná [*kanīna] amnf kānīnī born of a young wife | soc. (pej.) born before marriage; born out of wedlock — m. myth. np. of Kānīna, epith. of Vyāsa, of Karņa, of the three princes Pārtha and not. of Arjuna.
kāntá [pp. kam] amnf kāntā beloved, cherished | pleasant, handsome, magnificent — m. husband; beloved — f. kāntā beloved; mistress.

Kāntaka [ka] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Kāntaka "Charming", chief of police of Campā; he captured Apahāravarmā, made him dig a tunnel to reach the princess he believed was in love with him, and ended up stabbed.

kāntāra |āra| mn thick forest; virgin forest, jungle. vindhyakāntāram Vindhya mountain forest. kāntārevanadurgesu krcchrāsvāpatsu sambhrame udyateşu ca śastreşu nāsti sattvavatām bhayam In the virgin forest, In the thickets, In unfortunate accidents, In troubled situations, and when swords are raised, the brave know no fear.
Kānti [act. kam] f. charm, beauty, grace; radiance, splendor | myth. np. of Kānti, epith. of Lakṣmī “the Splendid”.

kāntipura [pura] n. geo. np. of the City of kāntipura "City of Grace", in the valley of Nepal; it was founded by King Gunakāma deva in 724; then it federated the authority of 12 lords |thakkura|; Ratna Malla seized it at the end of the 15th century by having them all poisoned, creating the Malla dynasty, which lasted until the Gur kha conquest; the City was renamed Kāsthamandapa (mod. Kathmandu) in the 16th century.

kāntimat [mat] amnf kāntimatī charming; splendid — f. kāntimatī lit. np. of a poetic meter | lit. [DKC.] np. of the princess kāntimatī, daughter of the king of Kāśī Caṇḍasiṃha; reincarnation of Vinayavatī, she was seduced by Kāmapāla, and gave birth to Arthapāla | lit. [KSS.] np. of the princess kāntimatī₁, daughter of kāntisena, sixth wife of Sūryaprabha₁.
kāntisena [senā] lit. [KSS.] np. of king kāntisena of Srikantha₃, father of kāntimatī₁.
kānyakubja [*kanyakubja] n. geo. np. of the City of kānyakubja; cf. Kanyākubjā, Kuśasthala, Kauśa — amnf kānyakubjī ha bitant de Kanyākubjā.
kāpaya m. hist. np. du nāyaka kāpaya ou Kāpanīdu; he recaptured Ekaśilā from the Muslims in 1326, and was defeated by Singama in 1370.
kāpāla [*kapāla] amnf kāpālā relating to the skull — m. soc. renunciant heretic; cf. kāpālika.

kāpālika [*kapālaika] m. myth. np. of kāpālika, epith. of ŠivaBhairava, cursed for having cut off the 5th head of Brahmā to wander in crematorium enclosures and to beg with a skullcap | soc. wandering ascetic śaiva living in imitation of Bhairava, not. by frequenting crematorium enclosures; he carries an alms bowl made of a skullcap, and a staff surmounted by a skull [khaṭvānga] | pl. Shaivite sect of such renunciants; the lākulapāśupata sect has similar practices, as do some followers of śākta tantric rites.
kāpiśa [*kapiśa] n. kind of rum — f. Kāpiśī np. of the City of Kāpiśī.
kāpiśāyana [*kapiśaāyana] amnf kāpiśāyanī from Kāpiśī. kāpiśāyanī drākṣā grape from Kāpiśī.
kāpuruṣa [kāpuruṣa] m. coward, coward.
kāpeya [*Kapieya] amnf kāpeyī cf. kāpya.
kāpota [*kapota] n. group of pigeons.

kāpya var. kāpeya |*Kapia| amnf kāpyā grandson of Kapi; descendant of Kapi | soc. ap belonging to the clan of cantors |angirasas| — mr. soc. n.p. of gotra of priests celebrating the songs of the Atharvaveda, not. in mod. Orissa || tamil kaap piya. Kāma |act. kam | mr. wish, desire; designed piscence | soc. pleasure, one of the goals of existence

tence [puruṣārtha] | [kāmadeva] myth. np. of Kāma "Desire", ever-young god of amorous desire; in poetry his weapon is the Hasita bow made of sugar cane and whose string is made of bees, and he possesses 5 flower arrows | puspabāṇa | with which he excites amorous desire: amorous turmoil | ketaka|, the burning of love [dahana] (or saṃdīpana), sexual desire [bilva], the pleasure of sex [mohana], and sexual enjoyment [harṣaṇa]; Vedic. he is identified with the form of Agni of the devouring fire of passion; he is the son of Dharma and Śraddhā; his body was consumed by the anger of Shiva whose asceticism he had disturbed; His wife, Rati, personifies pleasure; his other wife, Prīti, personifies love; his daughter Aśruvindumatī seduced King Yayāti; his mount |vāhana| is a parrot, his emblem the makara; cf. Ananga, Uccāṭana, Kantu, Kandarpa, Kusumāyudha, Jhasaketana, Pañcabāṇa, Pañcayuddha, Pradyumna, makara ketana, Madana, Manmatha, Mādana, Sukavāha,

Smara | myth. | harivamśa | son of Kṛṣṇa and Rukminī — n. beloved or desired object; the agreeable | semen — ifc. (iic.) ad libitum, at will, at choice — agt. amnf kāmā ifc. who desires (inf.) (the inf. iic. elises the final 'm') — f. kāmā desire. kāmena adv. out of affection. kāme adv. according to the desire of, out of affection for g. dat. māṃsakāma amn who desires meat. kāmo me bhuñjīta bhavān I wish you to eat. vaktukāmah who desires to speak. tyaktukāmah who aspires to renunciation. dātukāmo bhava be inclined to give.
kāmakandalā [kandala] f. lit. np. of the courtesan kāmakandalā; cf. Mādhavānalakathā.

kāmakāra [kāra] amnf kāmakārī who satisfies the desires of g. — m. act of following one's inclination; free will. kāmakārāt adv. according to one's own desire; spontaneously, voluntarily. kāmakāratas id. kāmakāram kr to act as one pleases.

kāmakārin [kārin] amnf kāmakāriņī amoral — m. myth. servant of Kāma. kāmakoți [koți] f. geo. np. of the sanctuary |pīṭha| kāmakoţi of Kāñcī, dedicated to KāmākṣīDurgā; it is the seat of a monastery [matha], whose foundation is attributed to Śańkarācārya.
kāmaga |ga₁| amnf kāmagā Who leaves of their own free will.
Kāmagiri [giri] m. geo. np. of Kāmagiri, hill near Guwahati in Assam; there is the temple of Kāmākhyā.

kāmacāra [cāra] amnf kāmacārī One who follows one's own pleasure — m. spontaneous behavior; unconstrained movement | the act of following one's own pleasure; sensuality; selfishness. kāmacāratas adv. voluntarily; according to one's own pleasure. kāmacūdāmaņi [cūdāmaņi] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of kāmacūḍāmaṇi, daughter of Sumeru; she married Sūryaprabha, and became empress of the vidyādharās.
kāmachattra | chatra | n. clitoris.
Kāmaja [ja] amnf kāmajā produced by desire; lustful — m. myth. np. of Kāmaja, "from Kāma", epith. of Aniruddha.
kāmajajvara [jvara] m. med. mental illness related to romantic passion.
kāmatattva [tattva] n. sexual enjoyment, or gasm; by extension, the panting sound produced during orgasm.
kāmada |da| amnf kāmadā Who grants wishes, Who fulfills desires — f. kāmadā cf. Kāmadhenu.
kāmadugha [dugha] amnf kāmadughā fa vorable, Who grants wishes, Who fulfills desires — f. kāmadughā myth. np. of kāmadughā, Cow of abundance of Vasistha; cf. kāmadhuk, Kāmadhenu.
kāmadughadhenu | dhenu | f. myth. Vasistha's Cow of Abundance; cf. kāmadhuk.

kāmaduh [duh₂] amnf [sg. nom. kāmadhuk] Who grants all wishes — f. myth. np. of the Cow of Abundance kāmadhuk "Who grants wishes", epith. of the mythical Cow Nandinī, daughter of Rohinī₂ (or born from the churning of the sea of milk [kṣīrodamathana]), given to the sage [ṛṣi] Vasiṣṭha; she grants all his wishes to the one Who milks her; she is also called Kāmadhenu, kāmadughā.
kāmadeva | deva | m. myth. np. of kāmadeva, the god Kāma | hist. np. of the king kāmadeva₁ of the late nastie kadamba dy; he reigned from 1181 to 1197 in Vanavāsī.
Kāmadhenu [dhenu] f. myth. np. of the Cow of Abundance Kāmadhenu; cf. kāmadhuk | lit. name of works; not. Kāvyālamkāravrtti.

Kāmapāla |pāla| m. myth. epith. of Viṣṇu "He who sustains human desires"; also epith. of Siva | lit. |DKC.| np. of Kāmapāla "Shepherd of Desire", son of the Brahmin minister Dharmapāla₂; despite the advice of his half-brother Sumitra₁ he led a dissolute life; having arrived in Kāśī he seduced the princess Kāntimatī, daughter of King Candasimha; the child born of the union was abandoned in the woods, where he was taken in by the yakṣī Tārāvalī; Kāmapāla was captured, condemned to death, but killed his executioner and escaped; He met Tārāvalī, who told him that he had taken in the child, whom his father Manibhadra brought to Kubera, who taught him the lineages of various reincarnations, and ordered that the child be entrusted to Queen Vasumatī, wife of Rājahamsa, to serve as a companion to their son Rājavāhana; Tārāvalī, several times lover of Kāmapāla in previous lives, built him a palace of love by her magical powers; Kāmapāla summoned him to take revenge on King Candasimha, entered his apartments, and threatened him; the king apologized, allowed him to marry Kāntimatī, and appointed him prime minister before dying of fatigue; The heir Candaghosa, an inveterate reveler, died in turn, and Kāmapāla enthroned the young Simhaghosa as king; when the latter grew up, his advisors told him that his minister had poisoned Candasimha and Candaghosa; when Tārāvalī, jealous of Kāntimatī, left the court, Kāmapāla was arrested and condemned to have his eyes gouged out; his son Arthapāla, who was the abandoned child and who had learned of Pūrnabhadra's deeds, saved him by trickery, having him bitten by a venomous snake for which he had the antidote; Kāmapāla was in previous lives Saunaka₂ and Śūdraka₂, both husbands of Aryadāsī, previous incarnation of Tārāvalī; Aryadāsī conceived by Śūdraka₂ a boy Who was abandoned, taken in by Vinayavatī, and Who was reborn as Arthapāla, son of Kāntimatī, reincarnation of Vinayavatī.
kāmabala [bala] n. sexual potency; strength of libido.
kāmabīja [bīja] n. phil. [Tantra] bijamantra 'klīm' of evocation of Kāma.
kāmamañjarī | mañjarī | f. lit. | DKC. | np. of kāmamañjarī "Bouquet of love", courtesan who won the bet to seduce the ascetic Marīci.
kāmayuj |yuj₂| amnf that grants the wish.
