kāmarūpa |rūpa| amnf kāmarūpā which changes shape at will — m. pl. geo. np. of the country and people of the Kāmarūpās, in southern Bengal and Assam; cf. Prāgjyotisa.
kāmarūpin |rūpin| amnf kāmarūpiņī which changes shape at will.
kāmavṛtti | vṛtti | amnf independent, free of spirit — f. free will. na kāmavrttirvacanīyamīksate [KuS.] A free man does not need to justify his actions.
kāmaśāstra [śāstra] n. phil. science of erotics.
kāmasakta [sakta] amnf kāmasaktā who indulges in lust; lascivious, lewd.
Kāmasāra [sāra] m. bed. n.p. from the Kāmasāra, summary of sexology in 41 verses, due to Kāmadeva.
Kāmasūtra [sūtra] n. lit. np. of the Kāmasūtra, treatise on erotics by Vātsyāyana₁; cf. Jayamangalā.
kāmākṣī [akṣī] f. myth. np. of the goddess kāmākṣī "with the gaze of desire", form of Durgā; she is the tutelary goddess of Kāñcīpura, in Tamil Nadu; cf. Kāmakoţi.

kāmākhyā [ākhyā₁] f. myth. [Tantra] np. of kāmākhyā, epithet of Durgā "she who answers desires"; [Kālikāpurāṇa] she is Mahāmāyā, first among the tantric goddesses [yoginī]; she is invoked in the formulas [mantra] of
subjugation [vaśīkaraṇa]; its main temple is at Kāmagiri; it is a highly revered pīṭhasthāna (that of Satī's yoni); its menstruation is celebrated there at the ambuvācī festival; cf. daśamahāvidyā.
kāmāgni [agni] m. fire of desire.
kāmānkuśa [ankuśa] m. ["spur of desire"] penis; clitoris.
kāmātman |ātman| amnf kāmātmanī whose mind is invaded by desire.
kāmāri [ari] m. myth. np. of kāmāri, epith. of Shiva "enemy of desire" | arch. it is one of the 16 aspects of Shiva | med. pyrite for medicinal use.
kāmāvasāyin | avasāyin | amnf kāmāvasāyinī which suppresses desire.
kāmāvasāyitā [tā] f. phil. [yoga] the power to subdue one's passions, an astasiddhi.
kāmāvasāyitva |tva| n. id.
kāmepsu |īpsu| amnf who seeks sensual pleasures.
kāmeśvara |īśvara| m. myth. np. of kāmeśvara, epith. of Kubera — n. geo. np. of a tīrtha — f. kāmeśvarī myth. np. of the goddess kāmeśvarī.
kāmana [agt. kam] amnf kāmanā who desires; sensual, lascivious — act. f. kāmanā desire; su hait.
kāmanda m. myth. |Mah.| np. du rsi kāmanda ou kāmandaka.
kāmandaka [ka] m. myth. id. — f. Kāmandakī lit. np. of the nun bd. Kāmandakī, skillful go-between of the Mālatīmādhava.
Kāmandaki m. hist. np. of Kāmandaki "son of Kamandaka", father of Sekhara, author of the Nītisāra, inspired by his master Cāṇakya.
Kāmandakīya [īya] amnf kāmandakīyā relating to or composed by Kāmandaki — mn lit. np. of the Kāmandakīya Nītisāra.

kāmam [acc. Kāma] adv. at pleasure, at will; willingly | freely, according to one's desire; with pleasure, joyfully | (assent) very well, agreed, certainly, of course; please | in any case; to tell the truth, indeed | even if; supposing that; nevertheless, in any case; although, even though, by putting that. kāmam ... na rather ... than. kāmam you ... na you if he pleases ... but in any case.
kāmayā [i. kāmā] adv. according to the desire of, out of love for (g. dat.) | (with brūhi) supplication. kāmayā me brūhi deva kastvam out of love for me, O god, tell me who you are.
kāmayitr [agt. ca. kam] amnf kāmayitrī concupiscent, lustful.
kāmala [Kāmala] amnf kāmalā lascivious, libidinous — mf kāmalā med. form of jaundice; excess or obstruction of bile — f. kāmalī myth. epith. of Renukā "Concupiscent".
kāmi iic. kāmin.
kāmijana | jana | m. in love.
kāmitā [tā] f. state of being in love, desire.
kāmitva [tva] n. id.
kāmika [Kāmaika] amnf kāmikā desired, loved; hoped for | that satisfies desires — n. [kāmikatantra] lit. np. of the kāmika Tantra, foundation of the dualistic Shaivite doctrine Siddhānta.
kāmin [Kāmain] amnf kāminī affect killer, affectionate; desirous, amorous, loving — m. lover — f. cf. kāminī.
kāminī [f. kāmin] f. loving wife, lover; lascivious woman.
kāminīsakha |sakha| am in the company of his wives.

kāmuka [kāmauka] amnf kāmukā amou reux | soc. lascif; it is a defect contrary to the views of the sādhaka — m. lover — f. kāmukī lover myth. np. of kāmukī, aspect of Durgā; Gand hamādana is his devīpīṭha.
kāmukatva [tva] n. lasciviousness; sexual desire.
kāmpila [*kampila] m. geo. n.p. of the kāmpila country — f. Kāmpilī np. from the city of Kāmpilī, its capital.

Kāmpilya [*kampilaya] m. geo. n.p. from the Kāmpilya country of North India, southern part of Pañcāla; it is inhabited by the Pañcālās; myth. Brah madatta and Drupada were kings — f. Kāmpilyā geo. n.p. from Kāmpilyā, its capital, near the Ganges; it was a rich and superb city; a canal connected the Ganges to the royal palace; [Mah.] it was the capital of king Drupada; his daughter Draupadī celebrated her svayamvara ceremony there; mod. Kampil in Uttar Pradesh, village near Farrukhabad.
kāmpilyaka [ka] m. inhabitant of Kāmpilya.
kāmboja [*kamboja] m. geo. country of Ka boul; its horses were renowned | pl. kāmbojās its inhabitants.
kāmya [pfp. [1] kam] amnf kāmyā sou haité, désirable; amiable, désirable; beau, charming | soc. (rite) "according to his desire" or optional, opp.
obligatory [nitya] or occasional [naimittika] — ifc. suffix for forming denominative verbs of sou hait; cf. putrakāma, rathakāma.

kāmyaka [ka] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the kāmyaka forest "Pleasant", where the Pāṇḍavās remained during their exile (except Arjuna, then in Heaven |Svarga| of Indra); Jayadratha abducted Draupadī there.
kāmyakarman [karman] n. self-interested act.
Kāmyakarmakamalā [kamalā] f. bed. n.p. from the Kāmyakarmakamalā, liturgical text [paddhati] on the worship of the Goddess Tripurasundarī, by Prānamañjarī.
kāya [act. ci] m. body (human) | trunk (of a tree) | body of a lute | gathering, collection, multitude | funeral pyre | bd. cf. trikāya.
kāyakalpa [kalpa] m. body care, hygiene; gymnastics | med. [Ayurveda] anti-aging treatment; rejuvenation cure.
kāyacikitsā | cikitsā | f. medicine.
kāyasiddhi [siddhi] f. phil. power to protect the body.

kāyastha |stha| m. phil. the Supreme Spirit "that resides in the body" | Vedic np. of the Indo-European clan kāyastha | myth. descendant through Bhattika of Citragupta, brought forth from the body of Brahmā at the request of Yama to administer justice; [Bhavişyapurāṇa] Brahmā brought forth Citragupta from his body, and thus named him kāyastha and assigned him to the service of Yama | soc. (man of the) caste [jāti] of scholars; scribe, secretary, administrator; the kāyasthās were often descended from unions of princes [kṣatriya] and handmaids [śūdrā]; they appeared under the Maurya dynasty as administrators and other subordinate officers of the princely courts; they flourished in the Muslim and later the Anglo-Saxon period; Their educational tradition made them the principal community of intellectual elites of modern India, such as Subash Chandra Bose, Rajendra Prasad, but also spiritual masters such as Vivekananda, Aurobindo, and Maharshi Mahesh Yogi — f. kayastha soc. woman of this community.
kāyāgni [agni] m. ["body fire"] digestion | motor impulse.
kāyotsarga | utsarga | m. jn. standing meditation position, not. of Jain masters | tīrthankara|.

kāyaka [kāyaka] amnf kāyikā concerning the body; corporeal — m. kāyaka ifc. body of — f. kāyikā soc. interest | vṛddhi | on a fixed capital, livestock or other; yield (not. of a cow); opp. kālikā. kāyikā vṛddhi soc. simple interest on a pledged good.
kāyika [kāyaika] amnf kāyikī made by the body; bodily — ifc. bd. which concerns a multitude of (iic.).

kār [ca. kṛ₁] v. [10] pr. (kārayati) pp. (kārita) to have done, to have executed — pr. r. (kārayate) to have executed for oneself | (with mithyā) to repeat. kaṭhaṃ kārayate he has a carpet made for his own use. padam mithyā kārayate he repeats the word incorrectly.

kāra [agt. kṛ₁] ifc. amnf kārī he or she who does, that which does (iic.); author of (iic.) act. m. execution, action of (iic.) | gram. designates the sound, the letter or the word (iic.), like akāra | effort, penance; determination; religious rite. kumbhakārah potter. andhakāraḥ blindness; darkness. kimceti cakārārthaḥ gram. the meaning of the particle "ca" is "moreover".

kāraka |agt. kṛ₁ | amnf kārikā ifc. that which makes, that which creates, that which produces, that which acts, that which accomplishes (iic.) | that which causes the action; author — act. n. gram. semantic role of a word in a sentence; not. role of a noun phrase in relation to the process expressed by the verb; We distinguish: apadāna, the role of origin (out of, from, because of, in the ablative case); sampradāna, the role of destination (for or towards, in the dative case); karana, the role of instrument (by, in the instrumental case); adhikaraṇa, the role of support (on or in, in the locative case); karman, the role of object or purpose (accusative in the active case, nominative in the passive case); kartr, the role of agent (nominative in the active case, instrumental in the passive case); and hetu, the role of cause (nominative case governed by a causative verb) — cf. kārikā. vivakṣātaḥ kārakāṇi gram. The semantic roles depend on the speaker's intention.
kārakatva [tva] n. gram. the state of being a participant in an action.

kāraṇa |act. kṛ₁| n. reason, cause, motive, origin; occasion; principle | sign, mark | means; instrument | father (cause of conception); god (cause of creation) | phil. necessary cause | justification of an opinion or judgment | lit. origin or plot of a poem or play | soc. [Tantra] fermented drink consumed during the ritual cakrapūjā — f. kāraṇā pain; agony. kāranībhū to be a necessary cause. niṣkāraṇa amn without cause; spontaneous. kasmāt kāraņāt for what reason? mama kāraṇāt for my own use. yena kāraņena because. yasmin kāraņena for this reason, thus.
kāraṇatā [tā] f. causality. kāraņatva [vat] n. id.
kāraṇamālā [mālā] f. lit. figure of speech of guir lande of causes.

kāraṇavat [vat] amnf kāraṇavatī having a cause — n. myth. the primordial water, origin of all waters kāraņavihīna [vihīna] amnf kāraņavihīnā without cause; unreasonable. kāraņaśarīra [śarīra] n. phil. [Vedānta] causal or original body of the soul, formed from the ānandamayakośa.
kāraṇānanda |ānanda| m. soc. tantric union rite during the śrīcakrapūjā, with intoxication from kāraņa wine.
kāranānandajāpeṣṭā [jāpaiṣṭa₂] f. myth. "worshipped by reciting the mantra of the kāraṇānanda rite", epith. of Lalitā.
kāraṇḍa |*karaṇḍa| m. bio. zoo. duck, coot; goose. kāraņdava |va| m. id.
kāraṇḍavyūha [*karaṇḍavyūha] m. lit. np. of the Kārandavyūha, contracted title of the Avalo kiteśvaragunakarandavyūha.
kārandhama |*karandhama| mr. patr. from kārandhama "son of karandhama"; cf. Avikṣit.
kāram [abs. kṛ₁] ind. having done.

kārayitr [agt. ca. kṛ₁] amnf kārayitrī who incites action; creative — m. soc. officiant of a religious ceremony — f. kārayitrī lit. [KM.] qualifies the creative inspiration of the poet; cf. pratibhā₂.
kāravella m. bio. bot. Momordica charantia, bitter gourd; it is used in medicine || hi. karelā.
kārā f. restraint, imprisonment; prison, jail.
kārāpāla [pala] m. prison guard.
kāri [agt. kṛ₁] m. craftsman; artist; technician — f. action, work (in questions).
kāritva [tva] n. conduct, action, commitment.
kārikā [f. kāraka] act. f. activity; com merce; interest | phil. summary of doctrine, mnemonic stanza effectively condensing a philosophical or linguistic teaching; opp.
bhāsya | pl. kārikās | harikārikās | gram. versified stanzas from Bhartrhari's Vākyapadīya.
kārikāvalī [āvalī] f. lit. np. from the kārikāvalī "Garland of Stanzas", a manual of Nyāyavaiśeṣika philosophy attributed to Viśvanātha₂, also called Bhāṣāpariccheda.

kārita [pp. ca. kṛ₁] amnf kāritā that which is made to be done, whose creation has been ordered; caused, oc casioned, provoked — n. gram. causal form of a verb — f. kāritā soc. interest [vṛddhi] specified by contract, higher than the usual usurious rate. tena sa praṇāmaṃ kāritaḥ he made him obey.

kāritra [instr. kṛ₁] n. bd. [Sarvāstivāda] internal activity at a moment of consciousness [dharma] of the present; it is opposed to its capacity [sāmarthya] to interact causally with moments of the past or future.
kārin [agt. kṛ₁] amnf kāriṇī ifc. that which does, that which causes (iic.) | agent, active, doing, producing; acting; actor — m. craftsman; merchant.
kārīra [*karīra] amnf kārīrī relating to bamboo shoot or bush karīra.
kārīrīsti | isti₁ | f. soc. rite to make rain, using the bot fruit. Capparis aphylla.

kārīṣa [*karīṣa] amnf kārīṣā concerning cow dung — n. dried cow dung (used as fuel). kārīso 'gnir adhyāpayati Dung fire allows one to study. কাহ kārú₁ [*kṛ₁u] amnf that works; that makes — m. worker, craftsman, artist | myth. epith. of Viśvakarmā, architect of the gods. কান্ত kāru₂ [*kr₂u] m. Vedic ["one who sings praises" | poet. কাংক kāruka |ka| mf kārukā craftsman | soc. secta teur śaivapāśupata, considered impure. kāpālikāḥ pāśupatāḥ śaivāśca saha kārukaiḥ | dṛṣṭāśced ravim īkṣeta spṛṣṭāś cet snānam ācaret | The kāpālikās, pāśupatās, śaivās and other kārukās (are impure); at the sight of them, one must look at the Sun (to purify oneself); at the touch of them, one must take a bath.
kārukasiddhāntin [siddhāntin] pl. m. kārukasiddhāntinas soc. śaivapāśupata sect, whose members were considered impure.
kāruņika [*karuṇaika] amnf kāruṇikā compassionate. kāruņikatā [tā] f. compassion.
kāruņya [*karuṇaya] n. compassion.
kārkaṭa [*karkaṭa] amnf kārkaṭā relating to the crab or the sign of Cancer.

Kārkoṭa [*karkoṭa] m. myth. np. of the serpent genius [nāga] Kārkoṭa or Kārkoṭaka | hist. np. of a royal dynasty of Kaśmīra (7th-9th centuries), established by Muktāpīḍa; they established many temples of Vaishnava obedience.
kārkotaka [ka] m. myth. cf. Karkotaka.

Kārtavīrya [*Kṛtavīrya] m. myth. [Mah.] patr. of Prince Arjuna₁ Kārtavīrya, king of the Hai hayās, son of Kṛtavīrya; to reward his piety, Dattātreya gave him a thousand arms [sahasrabāhu] to defend the dharma, eternal youth, a golden chariot that moved at will, and sovereignty over all the Earth; his capital was Mahismatī; he abused his power by oppressing the gods and the sages [ṛṣi] and disturbed Indra in his intimacy with Sacī; [Rām.] while bathing in the Narmadā with his thousand wives, he made a dam of his 1000 arms, and caused a wave that drowned the offerings of Rāvaṇa who was bathing not far from there; Rāvaṇa and all the vampires [rākṣasās] com defeated the army of Arjuna₁; the latter managed to capture Rāvaṇa by binding him with his 1000 arms, and only released him at the prayer of Pulastya; visiting the hermitage of Jamadagni, dissatisfied with the reception of Renukā, he stole the calf of his dairy cow |homadhenu|; Jamadagni ran after him, cut off his thousand arms, and delivered him to his death; He was avenged by his thousand sons, provoking the extermination by Paraśurāma of the entire princely class | kṣatriyās | ; his 5 surviving sons from Parasurāma's massacre are Jayadhvaja, Sūrasena₁, Vṛṣabha₂, Madhu and Urjita; Kārtavīrya is invoked when one loses an object; BhP. in a variant of the myth, he stole Kāmadhenu and was killed by Paraśurāma; in South India, he appears as the demon king Kātavarāyan, who abducted the Brahmin Ariyamālai and was impaled on Shiva's orders. kārtavīryārjunanāma rājā bāhusahasravān | tasya smaranamātreņa gatam nastam ca labhyate || Hom mage to the thousand-armed king Kārtavīrya Arjuna₁, by his invocation we find what was lost.

kārttika [*kṛttika] m. the month of kārttika (October-November), when the moon is full in the Pleiades; cf. kaumuda. kārttikapūrņimā [pūrņimā] f. astr. full moon of the month of kārttika; ŠivaTripurāntaka and VișnuMatsya are celebrated; the marriage of the tulasī with the śālagrāma [tulasīśālagrāmavivāha] is celebrated; the Sikhs celebrate the birthday of Guru Nānaka soc. festival [melā] and important cattle fair at the Hariharaksetra pilgrimage (mod. Sonepur in Bihāra).

Kārttikeya [*kṛttikaīya] m. myth. matr. of Kārttikeya "Raised by the Pleiades", epithet of Skanda, son of Shiva, commander-in-chief of the army of the gods; his mount [vāhana] is the peacock Pa ravāni; his image is generally placed to the west of sanctuaries; cf. Kumāra, Subrahmanya. śṛṇudhvaṃ munayaḥ sarve kārttikeyasya sambha vam | brahmanyatvam samāhātmyam vīryam ca tridaśādhikam | Listen, all you wise ones, to the story of Kārttikeya's birth, his devotion to the Brahmins, his greatness and heroism which surpasses even that of the gods.
kārtsna [*kṛtsna] n. totality.
kārtsnya [*kṛtsnaya] n. totality. kārtsnyena in totality, completely.
kārpaṭa [*karpaṭa] amnf kārpaṭā ["in rags" | beggar, beggar.
kārpaṭika [ika] m. pilgrim; traveler; beggar | soc. vassal (said of a poor man tearing his rags in the presence of his future master).
kārpaṇya [*kṛpaṇaya] n. poverty, misery; pitiful condition | avarice | compassion.
kārpāsa [*karpāsa] amnf kārpāsī in cotton tone; cottony — mn cotton | cotton paper — f. organic kārpāsī. bot. Gossypium herbaceum, cotton plant.
kārpāsapaṭa | paṭa | mr. cotton fabric; cotton paper.
kārma [*karman] amnf kārmī ["accustomed to acting" | active; worker | accustomed to.
kārmaṇa [*karmana] amnf kārmaṇī re latif to an action or to a work | that brings its task to completion — n. magic, sorcery.
kārmuka [*karmanuka] amnf kārmukā effective — n. arc. prāsakārmukabibhrat carrying the javelin and the bow.

kārya [pfp. [1] kṛ₁] amnf kāryā that which must be done, instituted or accomplished, obligatory that can be fulfilled, feasible; just, suitable | gram. produced, created; artificial; opp. nitya — n. | "that which must be done" | matter, occupation, work; labor; interest; task, duty, responsibility; urgency; the good | legal action, trial effect, result; motive, aim, purpose, object | phil. effect resulting from a causality | gram. performative sense of an utterance | gram. grammatical operation | lit. [theatre] subject of a play, main goal set by the hero | ang. care. kāryavaśāt for my own guidance; as far as I am concerned. asmābhiḥ sahaikakāryāṇām who made common cause with us.
kāryákara | kara₁ | amnf kāryakarī effective.
kāryakaraṇa [karaṇa] n. the act of doing one's duty phil. the cause and its effect.
kāryakaraṇabhāva | bhāva | m. phil. relation between cause and effect; theory of causality.
kāryakartṛ [kartṛ] m. agent working on behalf of g. .
kāryákārin [kārin] amnf kāryakārinī who performs a job.
kāryakāla |kāla₁| m. time to act | gram. time when an operation is carried out.

kāryakālapakṣa [pakṣa] m. gram. viewpoint according to which operations [sūtra] are prescribed everywhere in grammar where they are implied, not. meta-rules [paribhāṣā] and conventional rules [samjñā₁]; opp. ya thoddeśapaksa.
kāryátā [tā] f. fact of being an effect.
kāryátva [tva] n. id.
kāryaśabda [śabda] m. gram. language generated by grammar, through the operation of synthesis vrtti.
kāryaśabdavādin [vādin] m. gram. proponent of the theory affirming the construction of compound words by synthesis | vṛtti | of their components; opp. ni tyaśabdavādin.
kāryaśabdika |ika| amnf kāryaśabdikā gram. which holds the language as a creation of the gram mayor; opp. naityaśabdika.
kāryahantṛ | hantṛ | m. obstructor, disruptor.
kāryākṣama [akṣama] amnf kāryākṣamā in fit for work.
kāryāgāra [agāra] n. mod. desk.
kāryānuśāsana [anuśāsana] n. teaching of what should be done; action of administering justice.
kāryāntara [antara] n. break from work; leisure | another matter.
kāryāntarasaciva [saciva] m. soc. leisure companion of the prince.
kāryālaya [ālaya] mn mod. bureau. kāryālayasya samāptih kadā when is your office closed?

kāryāvasthā [avasthā₂] f. lit. [aesthetics] one of the 5 stages of unfolding a dramatic narrative: ārambha beginning of an undertaking, yatna effort to overcome difficulties, prāptyāśā hope of reaching the goal, niyatāpti assurance of success by overcoming an obstacle, and phalāgama/phalayoga attainment of the goal; cf. arthaprakṛti, pañcasandhi.
kāryaikya [aikya] n. phil. [Nyāya] coherence of causality of two adjacent sections.
kāryin [kāryain] amnf kāryiṇī assidu; industrious | looking for a job | gram. operand; awaiting an affix.
kārrya gem. kārya.
kārśya [*kṛśaya] n. thinness | med. [Ayurveda] cachexia; opp. sthaulya.
kārṣa [*karṣa] m. peasant — f. kārṣī ifc. (iic. gomaya) dried cow dung cake.
kārṣaka [ka] m. id.

kārṣāpaṇa [āpaṇa] mn soc. ["of the weight of a karșa"] coin whose value depends on the metal used: in gold, 16 beans [māṣa]; in silver, 16 stakes [pana]; in copper, 80 seeds of raktikā — n. money, coin — ifc. worth so much (iic.). nahi kākinyām naṣṭāyām tadanveṣaṇam kārṣāpaṇena kriyate (maxim) A man who has lost a penny does not spend a crown to find it.
kārṣṇa [*kṛṣṇa] amnf kārṣṇī bio. rela tif à l'antelope noire | astr. concernant la fortune sombre | relative à kṛṣṇa ou à Vyāsa/Dvaipāyana₁.

kāla₁ [*kala] m. time; moment; hour, day, season; occasion, circumstance | not. time of the meal (2 times a day) | interval of time, period, appropriate time for (g. dat. loc. iic. opt.yad) period of the day, comprising 3 moments [muhūrta] (2 h 24 min); there are 5 in the daytime; cf. prātastana, saṃgava | phil. time, one of the 9 substances [dravya₁] of the vaiśesika | destiny, Death | myth. np. of kāla₁, epith. of YamaMṛtyu, the god of Death, in his aspect of the time of the destroyers — loc. kāle adv. ifc. at the time of || lat. kalandae; fr. calendrier. kālam adv. for a certain time. kālāt adv. in time. kālena adv. on time, at the appointed time; in time. mahāntam kālam for a long time. nityakālam always; constantly. kālam i to die. kālam kṛ id. gacchatā kālena over time, in time. kāle adv. on time, appropriately, at the right moment. kāle kāle adv. always on time | from time to time. tatra kāle adv. at that time; at that time. caturthakālam the evening of the second day (at the 4th meal). kriyākālaḥ time to act. kālah prasthānasya time to leave. ubhau kālau morning and evening (the two meal times). şaṣṭe kāle on the evening of the 3rd day (after 6 meals). saste kāle 'hnaḥ at noon (the 6th hour of the day). ṣaṣṭānnakāla amn who only eats at the 6th meal (while fasting for two and a half days). nāyam kālo vilambitum [Nalopākhyāna] This is not the time to linger. kālo bhoktum It is time to eat. kālo 'yam yad bhuñjīthāḥ Here is the time to feed. abhyadhāvata prajāḥ kāla ivāntakaḥ [Ram] He attacked men like destructive weather.
kāla₂ amnf kālī Black — m. black color | myth. np. of kāla₂ "the Black", epith. of Shiva — f. cf. kālī. kālīkr to blacken.

kālakañjá [kañja] m. pl. myth. ["hair of time" race of demons [asura]; they made a tower of bricks to reach the Heavens; Indra, disguised as a brahmin, placed his brick at the bottom; when they arrived at Heaven, he removed his brick, and the tower collapsed; the Kālakañjās fell back to Earth in the form of spiders, except for two, who managed to jump to Heaven to become the spotted dogs |śabalau| of Yama.
kālakalita | kalita | amnf kālakalitā limited by time.

kālákrama | krama | m. interval of time | phil. progression of time. kālakrameņa adv. over time, gradually. ācāryāt pādamādatte pādam śisyah svamedhayā | pādaṃ sabrahmacāribhyaḥ pādaṃ kālakrameṇa ca | The student acquires a quarter (of his knowledge) from his teacher, a quarter of his own intelligence, a quarter from his fellow students, and a quarter from life experience.
kālákriyā [kriyā] f. astr. measure of time.
kālákṣepa [kṣepa] m. delay, postponement ["waste of time" | pastime, leisure. akālakṣepam adv. without delay, without wasting time.
kālakṣepārha | arha| amnf kālakṣepārhā which justifies a delay.

kālácakra | cakra | n. phil. time, symbolized by a Wheel that turns continuously; its cycle | jn. the Wheel of Time; the period of its revolution is estimated at 2 million billion oceans [sāgara] of years | bd. tantric philosophical system of the Kālacakra; cf. Paramārthasevā.

kālacakratantra [tantra] n. bd. np. of the kālacakratantra, teaching of the Kālacakra system | lit. not. its exposition by Mañjuśrīyaśā, the Laghutantra, and its commentary Vimalaprabhā by Pundarīka₅.
kālájña [jña] amnf kālajñā who knows the festive seasons or the seasons | who knows the opportune moment; who knows not to disturb — m. astrologer.
kālanāśa [nāśa] m. myth. np. of kālanāśa, epith. of Shiva "who destroys time" | arch. it is one of the 16 aspects of Shiva.
kālanirnaya [nirnaya] m. bed. n.p. of the Kālanirnaya, precise of smrti of Mādhavācārya.
kālanemi [nemi] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the asura kālanemi "Rim of the Wheel of Time"; he was defeated by Viṣṇu in a celestial battle before incarnating as Kamsa, killed by kṛṣṇa.
kālaparyāya [paryāya] m. passage of time.
kālaparyāyadharman [dharman] m. temporary destiny. dehasya kālaparyāyadharma (temporal destiny of the body) Death.
kālapāśa | pāśa | m. claws of Death.
Kālayukta | yukta | amnf kālayuktā of season; appropriate to the present time | astr. np. of Kālayukta "whose time has come", personifying year 52 of a life cycle |samvatsara|.

kālárātrī [rātrī] f. myth. [Mah.] np. of Kālarātrī "Night of Time", magical weapon made by Tvaṣṭā for Iśāna; Yudhiṣṭhira used it to kill Śalya | var. kālárātri myth. np. of Kālarātri Night of the end of time, personified by Durgā | lit. |KSS.| she guards the cave of Triśīrṣa.
kālávakrokti [vakrokti] f. bed. [Vakroktijīvita] oblique use of time, a poetic quality.
kālavarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Svargādikāṇḍa, dealing with time.
kāláśakti [śakti] f. phil. destructive power of time. kālātikramaņa [atikramaņa] n. delay; loss of time.
kālātipāta | atipāta | m. delay; loss of time.
Kālāri [ari] m. myth. np. of Kālāri "Enemy of Death", epith. of Shiva striking Yama who came to seek Mārkandeya.
Kāleśvara₁ [īśvara] n. geo. n.p. from the Shivaist shrine of Kāleśvara₁ in Ujjayinī; cf. Mahākāleśvara | geo. n.p. of the Kāleśvara₁ trilinga, at the confluence of the Godāvarī and the Prāṇahitā.
kālocita [ucita] amnf kālocitā whose time has come; opportune, in season.
kālottara [uttara₁] amnf kālottarā which occurs upon completion of the required time.
kālottarajñāna [jñāna] n. phil. [śaiva] knowledge revealed when the time has come to understand it.

kālakaṇṭha | kaṇṭha | amnf kālakaṇṭhī who has the black throat — m. bird with a black throat, like the peacock or the sparrow | myth. epith. of Shiva. kālakūţa [kūţa] m. myth. ["Black Mystery"] np. of the poison kālakūṭa, resulting from the churning of the sea of milk [kṣīrodamathana]; it was swallowed by ŠivaNīlakaṇṭha whose throat turned blue; syn. Halāhala.
kālapānīya [pānīya] n. mod. coffee.
kālapuccha [puccha] m. bio. animal of wet zone mide, with black tail, like the barasingha ruru deer|.
kālapucchaka |ka| n. id.
kālabhairava | Bhairava | m. geo. np. of the temple of kālabhairava, in Ujjayinī; dedicated to Bhairava "Black"; alcohol is offered to him.
kālamukha [mukha] amnf kālamukhī who has the Black face | soc. similar to Shiva/Bhairava; said of pāśupata sectarians — m. pl. soc. np. of the pāśupata kālamukha or Kālāmukha sect in Karṇāṭaka.
kālasūtra [sūtra] n. black rope | bd. np. of kālasūtra, one of the 8 burning hells, where the body of the damned is marked with black lines, indicating where to cut the flesh.

kālahastīśvara [hastiīśvara] m. geo. np. of kālahastīśvara, sanctuary of Sivavāyu "Master of the Black Elephant", located in Śrīkālahasti 36 km from Tirupati on the Svarnamukhī River; this enormous temple is carved into a hill; its construction began under the Pallavās, it was rebuilt by the Colās in the 10th century, the enclosure with its 4

portals [gopura] date from the 12th century; Krishnadeva Raya built the 100-pillar mandapa and the Rajagopura in 1516; it is the pañcabhūtasthala associated with the element of air [vāyu]; it is called the Dakṣiṇa Kailāsa. কালক Kālaka |kāla₂ka| amnf kālikā dyed or painted black — m. beauty mark — f. cf. kālikā.
kālakavana [vana] m. geo. np. of the Kālaka forest, to the East of Prayāga; it formerly marked the Eastern boundary of the Arya country.
Kālañjara m. geo. np. of the sacred mountain Kālanjara, place of penance (mod. Kalinjer in Bundelkhand) | lit. [KSS.] King Udayana ended his life there by throwing himself into the void.
kālaśeya [*kalaśaīya] amnf kālaśeyā which is found in a jar or churn — n. whey.
kālāpa [*Kalāpa] m. student of the grammar mayor Kalāpa | pl. ved. school of Kalāpī.

Kālāpaka [*Kalāpaka] n. gram. Kālāpaka system of Kātantra grammar, revealed by Kārttikeya to Sarvavarmā. madvāhanakalāpasy nāmnā kālāpakam tathā lit. [KSS.] (Kārttikeya) It will be called Kālāpaka in homage to my vehicle, the peacock.

kālika [kāla₁ika] amnf kālikī concerning time; which depends on time; periodic; seasonal | which lasts a long time; durable (not. ini mitié) | phil. [Nyāya] temporal — ifc. which lasts as long as (iic.). māsakālika monthly.

kālikā [f. Kālaka] f. ink | rust spot; flaw in gold | mass of black clouds | line of hair between the navel and the pubis | soc. interest | vṛddhi| paid at regular intervals, not. monthly; opp. kāyikā myth. np. of Kālikā, epith. of Kālī as a cosmic aspect [mahāvidyā]; she is worshipped in the Mahānirvāṇatantra | soc. 4-year-old girl personifying the Goddess at the Durgā festival. kālikāpurāņa | purāņa | n. lit. np. of the Kālikāpurāņa or Kālikopapurāṇa; it is dedicated to the worship of Kālī; It lists 108 ritual gestures | mudrā|.
kālikāvṛddhi [vṛddhi] f. soc. monthly interest rate.
kālikāstotra | stotra | n. bed. n.p. from the Kālīkastotra, a hymn of adoration to Kālī.
kālinga [*kalinga] amnf kālingī originating from kalinga — m. prince of the kalingās — n. watermelon.

Kālidāsa [Kālīdāsa] m. lit. np. of Kālidāsa "Servant of Kālī", famous poet and dramatic author of the 5th century (controversial); tradition says that he was one of the 9 jewels [navaratna] of the court of King Vikramāditya in Ujjayinī; orphaned, he was said to have been raised without education by a cowherd, then deceitfully married to a princess as a scholar, before receiving intelligence at the temple of Gaḍhakālikā (from which his name derives); He is credited with the plays Abhijñānaśakuntalā, Mālavikāgnimitra and Vikramorvaśī, the epic poems Raghuvamśa and Kumārasambhava, and the lyric poems Me ghadūta and Rtusamhāra; he is celebrated as the unsurpassed poet; many other texts are attributed to him, such as the collection of erotic poems Srigāratilaka | hist. np. by Kālidāsa₁, author of the Ekākṣaranāmamālā₂ (17th century).
kālinda [*kalinda] amnf kālindī relating to the land of the kalindās | from the Yamunā — n. watermelon — f. cf. kālindī.
kālindaka [ka] n. watermelon.

kālindī [f. kālinda] f. geo. np. of kālindī, epith. of the Yamunā "sister of Mount kalinda" | lit. |K.| np. of the mynah kālindī₁, jealous of the sentimental deviations of her husband Parihāsa | lit. [DKC.] np. of kālindī₂, daughter of an asura king annihilated by Viṣṇu; a siddha₁ told her that she would marry the king of Rasātala, where Rājavāhana found her.
kālindīkarṣaṇa [karṣaṇa] m. myth. epith. of Ba larāma "who diverts the course of the Yamunā".

kāliya var. Kāleya m. myth. [BhP.] np. of the dragon |nāga| kāliya or Kālīya or Kāleya; he poisoned the water of the Yamunā; inaccessible to Garuda because of a curse of the sage Saub hari, he was vanquished by Kṛṣṇa as a child, and had to go to the bottom of the ocean; cf. Agasti.

Kālī [f. kāla₂] f. myth. np. of the goddess of destruction Kālī "the black one", a terrifying aspect of Durgā, one of the ten powers |mahāvidyā| of Sakti; she is depicted as black, grimacing, dripping with blood, with fangs and a lolling tongue; she carries a garland of 51 skulls |muṇḍamālā| and wanders in crematorium enclosures; originally a tribal deity, she was first regarded as a flying demon with her tongue, catching the fat of the sacrifice, then was deified as the flame of the sacrificial fire; she is one of the 7 tongues of Agni [saptajihva]; [Tantra] humiliated by the gods for having had to show her sex to Mahisha to defeat him, Durga brought forth Kali from her anger; worried by her destruction, the gods asked Shiva Mahadava to interpose; walking on her chest in the crematorium enclosure, Kali recognized her husband and stuck out her tongue in ecstasy; buffaloes and goats are sacrificed to Kali; she is offered red hibiscus flowers [japa]; she is attended by furies [dakini] feeding on human flesh | myth. np. of Kali₁ "Black woman", epith. of Matsyagandhi | lit. [DKC.] np. of Kali₂, first wife of Satyavarma.
kālīkrama | krama | m. soc. extreme tantric doctrine of the "Kālī series"; hideous goddesses are worshipped in crematorium fields and impure transgressions are committed.
kālīghatta [ghatta] m. geo. steps of the temple of Kālī on the Ganges in Calcutta || Bengali Kolkata.
kālīna [kāla₁īna] ifc. amnf kālīnā ap proprié to time (iic.).
Kālīya cf. kāliya.
Kāleya cf. kāliya.
kālpanika [*kalpanāika] amnf kālpanikā imaginary, fictitious; invented; artificial, fabricated.
kālpanikatā [tā] f. state of being fictitious.
kālpanikatva [tva] n. id.
kālpasūtra [*kalpasūtra] amnf kālpasūtrā soc. which studies the injunctions of the Kal pasūtra.
kālya |kāla₁ya| amnf kālyā in time, at the right moment; in season; auspicious — f. kālyā cow ready for the bull.
kāvera n. saffron — f. cf. kāverī.

kāverī [f. kāvera] f. turmeric | courtesan, prostitute | geo. np. of the kāverī, great river of the Deccan, flowing from West to East; cf. Śrīranga | myth. [SkP.] The sage Agastya went to Kailāsa to ask Shiva for sacred water to consecrate a tīrtha; the kāverī was there in prayer; Shiva gave Agastya the water of the kāverī in his water pot [kamaṇḍalu]; Agastya went South, and he was meditating when Ganesha, changed into a raven, landed at Indra's request on the water pot which, by overflowing, gave birth to the river | myth. |HV.| daughter of Yuvanāśva, wife of Jahnu, changed by her father's curse from half of the Gangā into the kāverī river, and thus called Ardhagangā | geo. np. of the kāverī₁, river of Madhya Pradesh, flowing into the Narmadā, at Oṃkāreśvara.

kāverīstuti [stuti] f. lit. hymn of praise to the kāverī. kāverī nimnagā vārilaharīpāpahārinī | tārinī pāpināmenām bhaje'ham pāpahārinīm The kāverī that rushes down like a wave of water carrying away sin, she who liberates us from sins, I revere her as the liberator from sin.

kāvyá [*kavia] n. poem, poetry | literary or lyrical work; a distinction is made between narrative [śravya] and drama [dṛśya] — m. myth. np. of Kāvya, title of Sukra "the Bard" || pkt. kavva. kāvyam gadyam padyam ca lit. [Vāmana₃] Poetry includes prose and verse. kāvyaguņa [guṇa] m. lit. [Kāvyadarpaṇa] style of poetry; three are distinguished: mādhurya, ojas and prasāda.
kāvyacandrikā [candrikā] f. bed. n.p. from the kāvyacandrikā, Treatise on poetic composition due to Kavicandra Datta (Bengal, 16th century).
kāvyátā [tā] f. essence of poetry; poetic nature of a composition.
kāvyátva [tva] n. id. kāvyadarpaņa |darpaņa| m. lit. du np. Kāvyadarpaṇa "Mirror of Poetry", Treatise on Sanskrit poetics, composed in Kaśmīra in the 11th century by Rājacūdāmani Dīksita.
kāvyadoṣa [doṣa₂] m. lit. poetic error.
kāvyapāka [pāka] m. lit. [KM.] poetic maturity.

kāvyapurusa [purusa] m. lit. [KM.] np. of Kāvyapuruṣa, mythical incarnation of poetry, son of Sarasvatī, presented as one of the 64 disciples of Shiva; he received the poetic science of Prajāpati, which Rājaśekhara wanted to expound in The 18 Books of the kāvyamīmāmsā, but of which only the first appeared as Kavirahasya₁.
kāvyaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. from the np. kāvyaprakāśa "Splendor of poetry", Treatise on Sanskrit poetics, composed in the 11th century by Mammata.
kāvyamīmāṃsā [mīmāṃsā] f. lit. np. of the kāvyamīmāmsā "Investigation of Poetry", composed in the 10th century by Rājasekhara Yāyāvara.
Kāvyarākṣasa [rākṣasa] n. lit. np. of the Kāvyarākṣasa or Rākṣasakāvya "Damonic Poem"; this sylvan poem of 20 stanzas in enigmatic style is attributed to Ravideva of the Malaya country (before 1000).
Kāvyalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. lit. np. from the manual of poetics Kāvyalakṣaṇa "Instructions to the poet", by Dandī₁; cf. kāvyādarśa.
kāvyaśāstra [śāstra] n. lit. poetic | of. The arts and The sciences.

kāvyaśāstravinoda [vinoda] m. entertainment in arts and sciences. kāvyaśāstravinodena kālo gacchati dhīmatām | vyasanena ca mūrkhāṇām nidrayā kalahena vā || Scholars spend their time entertaining themselves with poetry and science, while fools spend it sleeping and quarreling.
kāvyaśobhā [śobhā] f. lit. poetic beauty.
kāvyasamasyā [samasyā] f. lit. poem to be completed. kāvyasamasyāpūraņa [pūraņa] n. poem completion game, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
kāvyātman |ātman| n. lit. essence of poetry.

kāvyādarśa [ādarśa] m. lit. np. from kāvyādarśa "Mirror of Poetry", Treatise on Sanskrit poetic composition by Daṇḍī₁ (7th century), also ap pelé Kāvyalakṣaṇa; in it he defines The two styles [mārga] vaidarbha and gauḍa; he describes 35 poetic figures of style [arthālamkāra] and deals in detail with Euphonic figures of style [śabdālaṃkāra]; he divides the vernacular language [prākṛta] into three categories: tatsama, tadbhava and deśī; he had an enormous influence on the poetry of Indian languages in general; Ratnaśrījñāna made the commentary Ratnaśrī on it.

kāvyānuśāsana [anuśāsana] n. lit. np. of the kāvyānuśāsana "Treatise on Poetics" due to Hemacandra (12th century), in sūtra style; he gave his commentary Alamkāracūdāmaņi, itself glossed by his Viveka₁, more advanced | lit. np. of the kāvyānuśāsana₁ "Treatise on Poetics" of Vāgbhaṭa₃ in sūtra style with commentary.
kāvyārtha [artha] m. poetic matter.
kāvyārthacaura | caura | mr. plagiarist.
kāvyārthatattva [tattva] n. lit. [Anandavardhana] essence of poetry.

kāvyālaṃkāra [alaṃkāra] m. lit. np. of the Kāvyālaṃkāra₁ "Ornaments of Poetry", manual of poetic style due to Bhāmaha (7th century) lit. np. of the Kāvyālamkāra₁ manual of poetics due to Rudrața (9th century); it contains the first known turaga padabandha — f. kāvyālaṃkārā lit. [KSS.] np. of Kāvyālaṃkārā, second wife of King Pa rityāgasena; jealous of her rival Adhikasamgamā, she tried to have her sons assassinated; in a previous life, she had been the vidyādharī Candravatī.
Kāvyālamkāravṛtti [vṛtti] f. lit. np. of the Kāvyālamkāravrtti (or Kāvyālamkārasūtravrtti), commentary of Vāmana₃; also called Kāmadhenu; Sahadeva₃ made a commentary on it.

kāvyālamkārasārasaigraha [sārasaigraha] m. lit. np. from the Kāvyālankārasārasangraha "Compen dium of the principal figures of style", treatise on dramaturgy and poetics by Bhatta Udbhata (8th century); Pratīhārendurāja commented on it.

√ kās v. [1] pr. r. (kāsate) pft. (cakāse) pp. (kāśita) pf. (abhi, ava, ā, pra, vi, sam) to appear, to manifest, to shine, to gleam — ca. (kāśayati) to cause to manifest — intens. (cākaśīti) intens. r. (cākaśyáte) to shine intensely; to observe attentively.

kāsía | agt. kāś| m. aspect of (2nd century); appearance, visibility; splendor | myth. np. of King Kāśa, who gave his name to his capital Kāśi₁, descendant of Purūravā; he is father of DhanvāDīrghatapā | bio. bot. Saccharum spontaneum, tall grass (up to 6 m), wild form of sugarcane; its flowers are purplish-white; it is used for weaving mats and roofs; myth. this plant is personified, with the kuśa grass, as a servant of Yama — n. its flower.
kāśakṛtsna [kṛtsna] m. hist. np. from the ancient grammarian kāśakṛtsna.

Kāśi₁ [kāśi] m. the Sun | myth. np. of Kāśi₁ "Bright", son of Suhotra, ancestor of the kings of Kāśi₁; [HV.] he is said to be grandfather of Dhanvantari — f. var. Kāśī geo. np. of the city of Kāśi₁ or Kāśī "City of lights", mod. Vārāṇasī (Benares); it was attached to Magadha by Ajātaśatru₂. kāśyām hi kāśate Kāśī Kāśī sarvaprakāśikā [Manīṣāpañcaka] Yes indeed, to Kāśī Kāśī shines forth, Kāśī who illuminates all.
kāśírāja [rāja] m. king of Kāśi₁ | myth. cf. Pratar dana.

kāśika [*Kāśīka] amnf Kāśikā₁ f. kāśikī from Kāśi₁ — f. Kāśikā₁ [kāśikāvṛtti] lit. np. of the Kāśikā₁ "Gloss of Benares", commentary [vrtti] on the Aştādhyāyī; its first 2 books are by Jayāditya, the last 3 by Vāmana₂ (7th century); its main commentaries are the Nyāsa and the Pa damañjarī | lit. np. of the Kāśikā₁, "Brilliant" Gloss of the Slokavārttika by Sucarita Miśra.
Kāśikāvivaraṇapañjikā [vivaraṇapañjikā] f. bed. n.p. of the Kāśikāvivaraṇapañjikā, analytical commentary on the Kāśikā₁, due to Jinendrabuddhi, also called Nyāsa (8th century).
Kāśī iic. Kāśi₁.
kāśīkhaṇḍa [khaṇḍa] mn lit. np. du kāśīkhaṇḍa, section of the Skandapurāṇa glorifying the sacred city of Benares and Visvanātha.
kāśmīra [*kaśmīra] amnf kāśmīrī relating to kaśmīra (Kashmir) — n. saffron. kāśmīrabhūr uttamā [Rājataramginī] The land of Kashmir is supreme.
kāśmīramaṇḍala [maṇḍala] n. geo. the region of Kashmir.
kāśya₁ [pfp. [1] kāś] amnf kāśyā to contemplate, to admire.
kāśya₂ |*kaśaya| amnf kāśyā who deserves the whip.
kāśyapa |*Kaśyapa| amnf kāśyapā relating to Kaśyapa | myth. who descends from Kaśyapa — m. myth. n.p. from kāśyapa, epith. of Kaṇva₁.
kāśyapakalpasūtra [kalpasūtra] n. pl. lit. np. from the kāśyapakalpasūtra, a collection of ritual injunctions attributed to Kasyapa.
kāśyapaparivarta | parivarta | mr. bd. n.p. of the Kāśyapaparivarta, central work of the Ratnakūta, heart of the Mahāyāna canon.
kāśyapaśilpa | śilpa | n. lit. np. from the kāśyapaśilpa, a Southern Shaivite text from the 11th century; it gives the rituals for the consecration of temples.
kāśyapasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. np. of the Kāśyapasaṃhitā, a 7th-century medical treatise aimed at the medical treatment of women and children.
kāṣāya [*kaṣāya] amnf kāṣāyā of saffron color; orange; brown — n. garment (not. monastic) of saffron or brown color.

kāṣāyin |in| m. bd. monk. কাষ্ট kāṣṭhá [kāśtha] n. wood, not. for heating; piece of wood, log, bundle — adv. kāṣṭham (with verb) expresses superiority or excellence. kāṣṭhībhū to become as still as a log. ānandasya param koṭim kāṣṭham adhigatah he was extremely happy.
kāsthacchid [chid₂] m. bio. zoo. woodpecker.
kāṣṭhaccheda [cheda] m. cutting of firewood fage | shortage of wood.
Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa [maṇḍapa] n. geo. np. of Kāṣthamaṇḍapa "Wooden Pavilion", wooden temple built in 1596 in Kathmandu (mod. Durbar Square), and which gave its name to the city.
kāṣṭhavikretṛ |vikretṛ| mr. timber merchant.

kāṣṭhādhyāpaka [adhyāpaka] m. excellent professor. কাষ্টা kāṣṭhā [f. kāṣṭha] f. direction; region of the world | limit, border; mark, goal | upper limit, extremity; summit, climax | racecourse; path (of the wind, clouds) | unit of time; there are 30 in a kalā; approx 2 s. কাষ্টিক kāṣṭhika [kāṣṭhaika] m. woodcutter.
√ kās₁ v. [1] pr. r. (kāsate) to cough. kāsām cakre he coughed.
kās₂ [act. kās₁] f. med. cough.
kāsa [act. kās₁] mf kāsā med. cough.
kāsakara | kara₁ | amnf kāsakarā which makes everyone ser.
kāsaghna |ghna| amnf kāsaghnā which relieves coughs; pectoral.
kāsamarda [marda] m. bio. ["that suppresses cough"] bot. Senna sophera, a bushy legume with yellow flowers, used in medicine, not. against coughs.
kāsamardaka | mardaka | mr. id.
kāsavat |vat| amnf kāsavatī who coughs.
kāhala amnf kāhalā who speaks with difficulty or in an unpleasant manner | large, excessive — m. large drum.
Kim IIc. Kim.
kimrājan | rājan | m. bad king; opp. surājan.
kimrūpa [rūpa] amnf kimrūpā in what form?
kiṃvat [vat] amnf kiṃvatī interr. having what? — ind. like what?
kimvrtta [vrtta] m. common man, brute.

kimśuka [śuka] m. bio. bot. Butea frondosa, Flamboyant tree "like a parrot"; its scarlet flowers appear in spring before the leaves; it is compared in poetry to a warrior or a blood-reddened tiger, or to a fire; syn. palāśa.
kiṃstughna cf. kiṃtughna.

kin iic. kim. kimkara var. kinkara [kara₁] mf kimkarā ser viteur; esclave | myth. [Mah.] np. of the evil spirit kimkara; Vasistha made it possess the king Kalmāṣapāda to punish him for having offended his son Sakti₁ — f. kiṃkarī wife of servant.
kiṃkirāta [kirāta] m. organic. Ashok tree variety (bot. Saraca asoka).
kinkiṇī f. bell | ascetic staff mounted on a metal ring bearing small rings, ringing to announce his presence; it is an attribute of Sani | var. kinkini id.

kiñ iic. kim. kimca var. kiñca |ca| conj. moreover, in addition. kiṃcana var. kiñcana [cana] n. sg. something | pl. kānicana some things. na kimcana nothing. na me nasyati kimcana nothing of me is destroyed. kimcit var. kiñcit [cid₁] n. sg. something, a little, some. mahyam kimcid vadati he/she tells me something. tava kimcid jalam bhavati do you have some water? akimcit nothing. kasmimścinnagare 'vadadrājā The king lived in a certain city.
kimciccalana | calana | n. imperceptible movement; movement in place.
kimciccchesa [śesa] amnf kimciccchesā of which little remains. kimcicccheșajīvita [jīvita] amfn kimciccchesajīvita half-dead; barely alive. kimjala var. kiñjala [jala] m. lotus flower.
kiti m. bio. porc.
Kina m. callus | scar.
kiṇalāñchana [lāñchana] amnf kiṇalāñchanā marked with a callus.
kiṇāṅka [aṅka] m. mark of callus.
kinva n. ferment for the production of alcohol.
kitava [kṛtavat] m. player (not. at dice) | deceiver, treacherous; rogue; brigand.
kitavavyavahāra [vyavahāra] m. game (with bet).
kin iic. kim.

kimtarām [tarām] ind. which one?. kimtu var. kintu [tu] adv. but, nevertheless. kimtughna var. kimstughna [ghna] m. astr. ["that which destroys everything except"] first half-day of the moon [karana] fixed. kimdama var. kindama | dama | m. myth. | Mah. | np. of the muni kimdama; he mated with his companion in the forest in the guise of deer; Pāṇḍu struck him with an arrow; as he died, he told him that he could not make love without dying. kiṃnara var. kinnara [kimnara] mf kinnarī myth. ["anthropomorphic being"] fabulous celestial being with the body of a man and the head of a horse or bird; The kinnarās are associated with the centaurs [gandharvās]; they are servants of Kubera; cf. mayu.
kimnaravarṣa [varṣa] n. myth. np. of the Kimnaravarsa, one of the 9 watersheds [varṣa] of the World, north of the Himalayas; syn. kimpuruşavarşa.

kim pn. nm ka₁ f. kā interr. who? which? which one? | what? why? how? | enough (i.); why then? what's the point (ig)? — (at the beginning of a sentence) is it that? what is it? atha kim certainly. kim atra what's the point? kim anyad what else? kim api rather, preferably. kimartham why? for what reason? kim iti why? kim iva what then? how then? kimu adv. all the more so, especially since. kimuta adv. all the more so, especially since. kim kila what a pity! kim ca moreover, besides. kimcana adv. in a certain way, somehow. na kimcana nothing. kimcit something, a little, some. kim tu var. kintu but, nevertheless. kim nu all the more so | really? how much more? how much less? kim punar all the more so. kim vā all the more so | what's the point (i.)? kim svid why, how then? yat kim ca nonsense. kim aham ajñaḥ am I an idiot? kim yuddhena what's the point of fighting? kim bahunā why so much talk? kim vilambena what's the point of dragging things around? nirujaḥ kim auṣadhaiḥ what good is a remedy to a healthy man? lobhaścedagunena kim piśunatā yadyasti kim pātakaiḥ satyaṃ cettapasā ca kiṃ śuci mano ya dyasti tīrthena kim | saujanyam yadi kim nijaih svamahimā yadyasti kim mandanaih sadvidyā yadi kim dhanairapayaśo yadyasti kim mṛtyunā || [Bhartrhari₁] Look no further for fault if there is greed, look no further for sin if there is wickedness; what good is pilgrimage to a righteous person? Do not suspect selfishness in a generous person; what good is the decoration of an eminent person, what good is wealth to a wise person? Death is nothing compared to dishonor.

kimartha [artha] amnf kimarthā for some purpose. kimartham adv. why? kimarthah varnānām upadeśah gram. [Paspaśā] why must phonemes be taught? kimpurusa var. kimpurusa purusa mf kimpuruṣī myth. ["almost human"] chimera; the kimpuruṣās inhabit the Hemakūṭa and are under Kubera's command; they include the gandharvās and the apsarasas; syn. kinnara. kimpuruşavarşa [varşa] m. myth. np. of the kimpuruṣavarṣa, one of the 9 slopes of the World; syn. kimnaravarşa. kimprabhu var. kimprabhu [prabhu] m. bad master. kimbhṛtya var. kimbhṛtya [bhṛtya] m. bad ser fast.

kímu var. kímuta [kimu] conj. à plus forte rai son, d'autant moins que. yauvanam dhanasampattih prabhutvam avivekitā | ekaikamapyanarthāya kimu yatra catuṣṭayam || [Hit.] Youth, wealth, power, lack of discernment: each of them leads to disaster, all the more so all four together.

kimpunar var. kimpunar [kimpunar] conj. all the more so. ropiteșu tarușu śreyah svayam kimpunarangasambhavesvapatyesu Planting a tree with one's own hands brings happiness; how much more so the coming of one's own offspring.

kíyat [kimyat] amnf kiyatī interr. To what extent? | How big? How much? How far away? | (pej.) Any; small, insignificant — adv. How much? How? How far away? kiyantah m. pl. How much? Syn. kati. kiyantam kālam For how long? kiyacciram For how long? kiyatyadhvani At what distance? kiyadetad How important is it towards (g.)? tena kiyān arthah What benefit is there in it? kiyaccirena In how long? Within what timeframe? kiyaddūre At what distance? kiyad rodimi What good is it to cry? kiyad asubhis What good is it to live? kiyadvakra Slightly crooked. kiyātamcit Of a certain size; at a certain distance. kiyatāpyamśena To a certain extent. kākiyati mātrā teṣām mama I think they are worthless.
kiyaddūra [dūra] n. small distance. kiyaddūre adv. at a short distance.
kiyanmātra [mātra] amnf kiyanmātrī of little importance — n. trifle.
kira [agt. kr] amnf kirā which disperses.
kiráṇa [agt. kṛ] m. dust | ray (of light, of sun, of moon).
Kiraṇavṛtti [vṛtti] f. bed. n.p. from the Kiraṇavṛtti of Bhatta Rāmakantha.

Kiraṇāvalī [āvalī] f. lit. [Nyāya] np. of the Kiraṇāvalī "Collection of Rays", commentary on the Padārthadharmasamgraha by Udayanācārya, which he was unable to complete. kiraņāvalīprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. [Nyāya] np. of the Kiraṇāvalīprakāśa "Splendor of the Collection of Rays", commentary on the Kiraṇāvalī by Vardhamāna₁.
kiranāvalīprakāśadīdhiti [dīdhiti] f. bed. n.p. of the Kiraṇāvalīprakāśadīdhiti, commentary on the preceding one by Raghunātha₁ Siromani.

kírāta m. geo. inhabitant of the mountains of the Himalayas |soc. tribal hunter living in the forest, of Tibeto-Mongole race | pl. kirātās np. of the kirātās people; the Tibetans; the Nepalese; the savages; cf. Yalambara — f. kirātī soc. woman of mountain tribe.

kirātārjunīya [Arjunaīya] n. lit. np. from the mahākāvya kirātārjunīya of Bhāravi; it tells of the fight between Arjuna, who went to Mount Indrakīla to obtain the weapon Pāśupata from the gods, and the god Šiva in the guise of a wild mountaineer [kirāta]; with his bare hands Arjuna managed to seize the god and hold him up off the ground, an exploit marking the culminating point of the heroic feeling [vīrarasa] evoked by the work; Shiva then reveals himself to him and gives him the desired weapon; this motif is represented notably at Prasat Thom in Angkor and at Banteay Srei in Isvarapura.
kirīta n. diadem; crest; tiara.
kirītin [in] amnf kirītinī who wears a diadem — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Kirīṭin, epith. of Arjuna "Crowned (by Indra)".

Kirmīra amnf kirmīrā variegated — m. [Mah.] np. du rākṣasa Kirmīra "Speckled", brother of Baka₁ and friend of Hidimba; he attacked the Pāṇḍavās during their exile in the forest; Dhaumya destroyed his māyā , and Bhīma killed him.

kíla part. cl. certainly, as they say, as is known; so they say; supposedly; apparently; probably, surely |if possible; as I hope | (interr.) isn't it? kim kila what a pity! kim kila sa bhavān surām pāsyati can he possibly drink alcohol? naiva kila certainly not! yadi kila perhaps. smarati kila you remember, don't you? śrūyante kila bhārate as it is said in the Mahābhārata. na śraddadhe kim kila tvam śūdrānnam bhoksyase [SK.] I can't believe you're going to eat śūdrās food.
kilakiñcita [kiñcita] n. [nāṭya] amorous agitation, one of the 10 means of seduction [hāva] of the woman; it includes anger, tears, joy, fear, etc.
kilāsa amnf kilāsī leper — n. leprosy spot; white leprosy — f. kilāsī spotted deer; myth. vehicle of the winds [marut].
kilbiṣa [related to kilviṣa] n. cf. kilviṣa. kilbişin [in] amnf kilbişinī guilty, sinner.
kilviṣa var. kilbiṣa [viṣa] n. fault, sin; offense, injustice; syn. agha — f. kilviṣā ifc. sin of (iic.).
kiśara m. perfumed commodity | var. kisara id.
kiśarika [ika] amnf kiśarikī ["who sells kiśara" perfume merchant.
kiśorá m. foal | boy, prepubescent adolescent — ifc. little of (iic.) — f. kiśorī foal young girl.

kiṣkindha m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the Kişkindha mountain of South India, containing the kiskindhā cave | geo. territory north of My sore, near the sources of the Pampā; myth. it was the kingdom of Sugrīva, usurped by his brother Vālī — f. cf. kişkindhā.
kişkindhā [f. kişkindha] f. myth. n.p. from the Kişkindhā cave, which was the capital of Vālī the usurper, then returned to Sugrīva by Rāma.
kiṣkindhākāṇḍa [kāṇḍa] n. bed. n.p. from Kişkindhākānda, 4th book of Rām., where Rāma meets Hanumān and Sugrīva.
kisalaya n. bud, young shoot.

kīcaka m. bio. bot. Bambusa arundinacea, thorny bamboo; it can reach 30 in height myth. |Mah.| np. of Kīcaka "Bamboo", commander-in-chief of the army of King Virāṭa, and his son-in-law as brother of Queen Sudeșṇā₁; he troubled Draupadī during the 13th year of exile of the Pāṇḍavās, disguised as the sairandhrī Mālinī₁; she sought protection from Bhīma, who massacred him by crushing him into a ball of flesh | pl. geo. np. of the land of the Kīcakās, tribe of the Kekayās.
kīcakavadha [vadha] m. lit. np. of the poem kīcakavadha "The Killing of Kīcaka" by Nītivarmā; it recounts the events of the Virāṭaparva with many interpretive devices
tiple | ślesa |.
kīta mnf kīti insect; worm, caterpillar — ifc. vile, despicable (iic.).
kīṭamaṇi [maṇi] m. bio. zoo. Lampyris noctiluca, firefly, glowworm.
kīdṛś [kimīdṛś] pn. mnf interr. of what kind? resembling what? | excl. what ...! — am kīdrśa f. kīdrśī id.
kīmāśa m. peasant, farmer | commoner, poor person.
kīri [act. kṛ₂] m. one who gives praise.
kīrṇa [pp. kṛ] amnf kīrṇā spread out, scattered, disseminated | covered with, full of.

√ kīrt [vn. Kīrti] v. [10] pr. (kīrtayati) pp. (kīrtita) pf. (anu, ut, pari, pra, sam) mention ner; call; announce, name | commemorate celebrate, glorify (g.); recite, tell — ps. (kīrtyate) to be called.
kīrtana [act. kīrt] nf kīrtanā mention, account; praise, eulogy | litany of praises to a deity; devotional song.

kīrtí [act. kṛ₂] f. mention; glory, fame — m. myth. np. of the asura Kīrti (or Kīrtti) "glo rieux"; with his brother Vāsa he was guardian of the ekāmrakṣetra; he possessed the monster Raktabīja; when Pārvatī visited them, they quarreled over her, and Shiva proposed that whoever took her on his shoulders would win her; with her two heels she sent them underground, assigned to guard the basin of her temples.
kīrtikara | kara₁ | amnf kīrtikaraī which confers glory.
kīrtikaumudī [kaumudī] f. bed. n.p. from the Kīrtikaumudī "Moonlight of Glory", large
poem [mahākāvya] in vaidarbhī style attributed to Someśvaradeva; it is a panegyric of the minister Vastupāla.
Kīrtipatākā [patākā] f. lit. np. of the Kīrtipatākā "Glorious Banner", erotic poem by Vidyāpati₁ in the maithilī language.
kīrtímat [mat] amnf kīrtimatī glorious, re-named.
kīrtimukuṭa | mukuṭa | mn high cylindrical tiara; Vișnu the door.

Kīrtimukha [mukha] n. myth. np. of Kīrtimukha "face of glory", monster born from Shiva's anger at Jalandhara's impudence; it sprang from his third eye to devour Rahu the messenger, who placed himself under Shiva's protection, leaving Kīrtimukha only the possibility of devouring himself; when only the head remained, Shiva honored it by entrusting it with the guard of his sanctuaries; arch. its head is a motif frequently decorating the pediments and lintels in Indian, Indonesian and Khmer temples; it also adorns jewelry such as belt buckles.
Kīrtiratha [ratha] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of King Kīrtiratha Janaka, son of Pratīndhaka, father of De vamīdha.
Kīrtirāta [rāta] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of King Kīrtirāta Janaka, son of Mahīdhraka, father of Mahāromā; he is also called Kṛtirāta.
kīrtilatā [latā] f. bed. n.p. from the kīrtilatā "Glorious Liana", poem in campū style by Vidyāpati₁, in the Maithilī language.
kīrtivāsa |Vāsa₃| mr. of. myth. Kīrti and Vāsa appear in it.

Kīrtivāseśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Kīrtivāseśvara, epith. of Šiva "Victor of Kīrti and Vāsa"; he is worshipped at Bhuvaneśvarī₁ as Lingarāja | myth. epith. of Šiva "clothed in glory", displaying the spoils of the gajāsura.
kīrtisena [senā] m. bed. [KSS.] np. of nāga kīrtisena, nephew of king Vāsuki; cf. Guṇāḍhya.
kīrtita [pp. kīrt] amnf kīrtitā said, named, mentioned; known, famous.
kīrtya [pfp. [1] kīrt] amnf kīrtyā to recite.
√ v. [1] pr. (kīlati) pp. (kīlita) to attach, to tie (to a post); to peg; to pin.
kīla [agt. kīl] m. stake, peg; stake; peg, needle, point; spear; woodcutter's wedge | post; not. post for tying cattle | sundial; syn. mayūkha | weapon; elbow; elbow strike — f. kīlā post; pin.

kīlaka [agt. kīl] m. needle; peg; wedge, stake (in wood); splint | stake for tying cattle soc. stake to delimit a ritual space; e.g., around the hollow made for the hearth of a cremation, dry wooden stakes connected by a red cord are driven in | astr. np. of Kīlaka "Stake", personifying the 42nd year of a life cycle |samvatsara| — n. lit. active syllable of a tantric mantra, conceived as the point possessing its active principle and penetrating into the person or object aimed at; cf. ṛṣyādi — f. kīlikā needle; peg.
kīlana [act. kīl] n. act of piercing, pinning soc. magical rite of immobilization, by piercing a doll with a human bone | action of preventing a mantra.
kīlāla mn sweet drink | myth. beverage of the gods, similar to amrta — n. blood.
kīlālapa |pa₁| amnf kīlālapī who drinks blood; syn. aśrapa — m. myth. cf. rākṣasa.
kīlālapā [pā₄] mf who drinks kīlāla.
kīlita [pp. kīl] amnf kīlitā tied to a post; impaled; pinned; tied, bound, sequestered | erected as a post | soc. | Tantra | (mantra) hindered in its action by a defect (mantradoșa).
ku₁ [ka₁] pf. of interrogation | pejorative particle; bad, evil, wicked, shameful | somewhat, a little, rather | good, well.
ku₂ f. earth.
kuṃśa ifc. mr. cf. bhrūkuṃśa | var. kuṃsa id.
kukavi [ku₁kavi] m. bad poet.
kukavitva |tva| n. state of being a bad poet.
kukavinindā | nindā | f. lit. section of poetry anthologies blaming not. plagiarists.
kukkuṭá |onomatopoeia| m. bio. zoo. rooster — f. kukkutī hen.
kukkuṭaka |ka| m. bio. zoo. Phasianus Gallus, fai san | soc. son of a tribal | niṣāda | by a servant |śūdrā|.
kukkuṭamayūrī | mayūrī | f. male and female peacocks.
kukkuṭāsana [āsana] n. phil. [yoga] posture by so many padmāsana, the hands passing between the thighs and calves to lift oneself from the ground.
kukkura m. dog.
kukkuradru | dru₃ | m. bio. bot. Blumea lacera, herbaceous plant of the family Compositae, with a strong turpentine odor, with yellow flowers; it is used in medicine | var. kukudru id.
kukṣa [kukṣi] m. belly; matrix.
kukşi m. belly, entrails; lower abdomen; my
trice | sheath, scabbard | cavity in gen. | myth. np. of the king kukṣi "Porous", eldest son of Ikṣvāku, also ap pelé Vikukṣi and Śaśāda; Kakutstha is his pali kucchi son.
kuksiroga [roga] m. med. dyarrhea; dysentery.
kukṣim [acc. kukṣi] iic.
kuksimbhari [bhari] m. ["who only cares about his stomach"] glutton.
kunkuma n. organic. bot. crocus sativus, crocus; saffron | Arabic turmeric; gr. κροκος; lat. crocus.
√ kuc [related to kut] v. [6] pr. (kucati) pp. (kucita) pf. (ut, sam) to bend — ca. (kocayati) to make bend.
kuca [agt. kuc] m. breast, chest | of. kucau the (two) breasts (of the woman).
kucabandha | bandha | m. bra.
kucaśāṭī [śāṭī] f. garment covering the chest.
Kucumāra m. bed. n.p. by Kucumāra, author of the Aupanisadādhikarana.
kucela [ku₁cela] n. rag — m. myth. np. of kucela "Poorly dressed", epith. of the poor Sudāma.
kuja [ku₂ja] m. astr. n.p. from kuja “earth-born”, a name for Mars; cf. Angāraka, Bhumija, Mangala.
kuñcana [act. kuñc] n. curvature, contraction.

kuñci [act. kuñc] f. measure of volume of grain, equal to 8 handfuls. astamustirbhavetkuñcih kuñcayo'stau tu puşkalam puskalāni ca catvāri āḍhakaḥ parikīrtitaḥ It is stipulated that the kuñci must be 8 handfuls, the puşkala 8 kuñci likewise, and that 4 puşkala make one āḍhaka.
kuñcita [pp. kuñc] amnf kuñcitā contracted, tightened; curved, twisted.
kuñcitāṅghri [aṅghri] amnf who has a bent foot; said notably of Națarāja. kuñcitānghrim bhaje I worship (Lord Națarāja) with a bent foot.
Kuñcitānghristava [stava] m. lit. np. from the Kuñcitānghristava "Hymn of glory with the bowed foot (of Națarāja)", devotional poem by Umāpati₁ Šivācārya (circa 1300).
kuñja m. bushes, thickets, copse.
kuñjara [kuñjara] m. elephant — ifc. treasure; cf. navakuñjara. mrgapatinakhabhidyamānakumbhakuñjara rasitam trumpeting of an elephant whose temples are being slashed by a lion with its claws.
kuñjarākṣa |akṣa| m. arch. lattice window.
√হৈ kuṭ v. [6] pr. (kuṭati) pp. (kuṭita) to be curved; to bend; to lean; to twist, to twist | to be deceitful, to be dishonest — ca. (koṭayati) ca. r. (koṭayate) to bend.
kuṭa [agt. kuṭ] mn house; family | pitcher; water pot — m. bastion; fort | hammer; axe | mountain.

kutaja | ja | m. bio. bot. Wrightia antidysenterica, mountain jasmine; it is used medicinally against intestinal spasms; it is a rainy season flower; syn. girimallikā | myth. epith. of Agastya "born in a jar".
kuṭaka |agt. kuṭ| amnf kuṭikā curved; twisted — m. kuṭika id. — n. kuṭaka plow — f. kuṭikā hut | soc. funerary hut to shelter ashes.
kuṭi var. kuṭī [act. kuṭ] f. curve | hut; ca bane; stall; tree. kuțicara | cara | m. crocodile | "that carries the hut (into the water)". kuțira |ra| n. small cabin, hut | var. kuțīra id.
kutiraka [ka] n. id.
kuṭitá [pp. kuṭ] amnf kuṭitā curved; twisted.

kuṭila [kuṭila] amnf kuṭilā bent, curved, twisted, arched | tortuous, deceitful; dishonest — mr. myth. n.p. from ṛṣi Kuṭila “Hunchback” — n. organic. bot flower. Valeriana jatamansi; cf. tagara — f. kuṭilā geo. n.p. of the Kuțilā river "Serpentine", epith. of Sarasvatī₁.
kuṭilaka [ka] amnf kuṭilikā bent, twisted | (hunter) on the lookout — m. soc. crook carried by the vidūṣaka during the trigata , and symbolizing Brahmā — f. kuṭilikā tortuous movement.
kuṭī var. kuṭi f. curve | hut; cabin; shop.
kuṭīkṛta [kṛta] n. (fabric) curly; not. woolen garment.
kúṭīnivātam |nivāta| adv. sheltering from the wind in a hut.
kuṭīra [ra] mn small hut.
kutumba n. family, household, home; family responsibilities; family worries | family ties; offspring. kuṭumbārtham adv. on behalf of the family.

kuṭumbaka [ka] n. id. — m. family man. ayam nijah paro veti gananā laghucetasām udāracaritānām tu vasudhaivakuṭumbakam || [Hitopadeśa] This one is one of mine, the other is a stranger, so calculate the petty; while for generous men the whole world is their family.
kuṭumbin |in| amnf kuṭumbinī who lives in a family | member of the household (including servants) | du. kuṭumbinau the father and mother of the family — f. kuṭumbinī mother of the family.
√ crush, grind; pulverize | math. solve.
kuṭṭa [act. kuṭṭ] m. grinding, crushing — ifc. grinding by (iic.).
kuṭṭakāra | kāra | m. math. method of solving simultaneous congruences.

kuṭṭamita [mita₁] n. [nāṭya] feigned anger, one of the 10 means of seduction [hāva] of a woman. কুহুক kuṭṭaka [agt. kuṭṭ] amnf kuṭṭikā ifc. that which cuts, breaks, grinds — m. action of grinding, breaking, cutting; pulverization math. |Bhāskarācārya₂| solving linear Diophantine equations by means of continued fractions.
kuttana [act. kutt] n. action of crushing, breaking, cutting, beating — f. kuṭṭanī kind of spear whore, whore.
kuṭṭanī [f. kuṭṭana] f. whore, damn.

kuttanīmata [mata] n. lit. np. from Kuṭṭanīmata "Advice of the Whore", a libertine narrative poem of the 8th century in verse by Dāmodaragupta, of the erotic-satirical genre (Mālatī, a novice courtesan from Benares, seeks the advice of an experienced professional, who explains to her the art of seducing and stealing from wealthy men).
kuṭṭita [pp. kuṭṭ] amnf kuṭṭitā crushed, ground; beaten | crushed; flattened.
kuttin [agt. kutt] amnf kuttinī that grinds, that crushes.
kuṭṭima [kuṭṭinma] amnf kuṭṭimā paved, tiled; covered with mosaics — mn paved, tiled floor; mosaic tiling | leveled floor for building construction, slab.
kuṭhāra [related to kuṭa] m. axe.
kuṭhārikā [ika] f. hatchet.
kuḍmala amnf kuḍmalā filled with buds — mn bud | arch. top of the floret; syn. mukula.
kuḍya n. wall, partition.
kuṇa m. mite | dust in the navel.
kúṇapa n. corpse; carrion; fertilizer of animal origin | excrement — amnf kuṇapā which stinks like a corpse.
kunapajala [jala] n. manure.

√ kuṇṭh v. [1] pr. (kuṇṭhati) pp. (kuṇṭhita) to be crippled, infirm; to be dull | to be lazy; to be obtuse, stupid — ca. (kunthayati) to dissemble. কুণ্ড kuṇṭha [agt. kuṇṭh] amnf kuṇṭhā dull; without effect | stupid, dull; slow, lazy. vajram tapovīryamahatsu kuntham thunder does not affect those who practice severe penances.
kuṇṭhita [pp. kuṇṭh] amnf kuṇṭhitā blunt; obtuse | indolent; lazy; stupid.
√তু kuṇḍ v. [1] pr. r. (kuṇḍate) to burn — v. [1] pr. (kuṇḍati) to mutilate — ca. (kuṇḍayati) to protect.

kuṇḍa [act. kuṇḍ] mn pot, jar, bowl, pitcher; container; not. water pot — n. pit in the ground, well; basin, sacred body of water | soc. not. brick pit serving as a Vedic altar — m. soc. illegitimate son, bastard — ifc. tuft of (iic.) — f. kuṇḍī bowl-shaped container — f. kuṇḍā burning, mutilation.
kuṇḍapāya | pāya | amnf kuṇḍapāyā soc. (sa crifice) where one drinks (the soma) from a bowl.
kuṇḍaka [agt. kuṇḍ] mn pot — f. kuṇḍikā pot; ascetic water pot.
kuṇḍala [kuṇḍala] mn earring, an neau, bracelet — f. Kuṇḍalī astr. horoscope. kuṇḍalīkṛ to bend into a circle; to wrap; to turn. kuṇḍalīkaraṇa n. action of stringing a bow.

kuṇḍalin [kuṇḍalain] amnf kuṇḍalinī Who has earrings — m. bd. np. du vidyārāja Kuṇḍalī — f. kuṇḍalinī phil. [yoga] "the Coiled One", epith. of the śakti of Shiva in the form of the serpent kuṇḍalinī, psychic force Which rises during kundalinīyoga to successively awaken the 6 energy centers [cakra] by piercing them; cf. Suṣumṇā.

Kuṇḍina₁ m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Kuṇḍina₁, one of the 100 sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — n. geo. np. of the city of Kuṇḍina₁ or Kuṇḍinapura, capital of the Vidarbha country; mod. ruins of Kaundinyapura in the Wardha district in Berar | myth. it was the capital of King Bhīma₁.
kutapa [ku₁tapa] mn blanket made of mountain goat hair.

kútas [adv. ku₁] adv. from where? from Whom? towards where? in what direction? | (figuratively) why? how? | e.g. (abl.); introduces an example of what precedes | in a way; all the more so, far from. kutahkālāt since when? ākutas to where? kuta āgata where does it come from? yathah kutaścit from Whomever. kuto'pi from anywhere; whatever the cause. kuto'pi kāraṇāt whatever the cause. kuta iti that if you ask why. yāvat jīvet sukham jīvet | rṇam kṛtvā ghṛtam pibet bhasmībhūtasya dehasya punarāgamanam kutaḥ [Bārhaspatya] As long as one lives, one must live in joy; one goes into debt, and eats rich food; how could it return, this body reduced to ashes?
kutaścit | cid₁ | adv. of anyone; of anywhere.
kútastya |kutastya| amnf kutastyā ve nant d'où? kutastyo'pi de quelque part ; d'où que ce soit. কুরুক kutuka |kutas| n. curiosity — ifc. desire for (iic.).
kutukita |ita| amnf kutukitā curious; inquisitive.

kutūhala [kutashala] amnf kutūhalā astonishing, surprising; interesting, fascinating; amu sant; excellent — n. desire; attention, curiosity, interest. kutūhalāt out of curiosity. nṛpāṇām tu kumāram dṛṣṭvātyantam kutūhalam bhavati But the kings, seeing the young man, felt an intense curiosity.
kutūhalakṛt [kṛt₂] amnf That which arouses curiosity.
kutūhalavat |vat| amnf kutūhalavatī curious, interested.
kutūhalin |in| amnf kutūhalinī amateur of, fond of, curious about (iic.) | impatient, desirous, avid.
kuttā f. soc. rental contract; lease; life annuity. কুর kútra [ku₁tra] adv. Or? to where?
kutracit [cid₁] adv. somewhere.
kutrāpi [api] adv. somewhere. yatra kutrāpi in one place or another.
√ kuts v. [10] pr. (kutsayati) pr. r. (kut sayate) pp. (kutsita) pfp. (kutsya) to despise; to criticize, to blame; to condemn.

kútsa [agt. kuts] m. ved. np. of the ṛṣi Kutsa “Who blames”, author of hymns of the Ŗgveda; he is a friend of Indra, Who took him one day on his chariot; when the demon Sușna attacked him, Indra defended him and killed the demon | pl. geo. np. of the Kutsās, people of the descendants of Kutsa.
kutsakuśika | Kuśika | n. link between Kutsa and Kuśika.
kutsakuśikakā [aka] f. marriage alliance between the families of Kutsa and Kuśika.
kutsana [act. kuts] n. contempt; blame, re close — f. kutsanā expression of contempt.
kutsā [act. kuts] f. contempt; blame, criticism. kutsayā i. adv. with contempt.
kutsita [pp. kuts] amnf kutsitā despised; blamed, branded | despicable; vile kutsite with an intention of contempt.
Kutha M. carpet.
kuthumin m. hist. np. from the Vedic scholar Ku thumī or Kuthumi.
kudāla m. organic. bot. Bauhinia variegata, mountain ebony.

kudālasaṃgama [saṃgama] m. geo. np. of Kudālasaṃgama, sacred place at the confluence of the Kṛṣṇā₁ and the Malaprabhā in Karṇāṭaka; it is an important lingāyat pilgrimage site since the 12th century; it is the memorial site [samādhi] of Basavanna.
kudṛṣṭi [ku₁dṛṣṭi] f. erroneous view; unorthodox system.
kudeśa [ku₁deśa] m. bad country (where life is difficult).
kudeha [ku₁deha] m. wretched body.
kuddāla mn hoe, spade.
kudhī[ku₁dhī₂] amnf unintelligent, foolish, simpleton; crazy.
kunadikā [ku₁nadikā] f. small river.
kunṛpa [ku₁nṛpa] m. bad king.
kunṛpati [ku₁nṛpati] m. id.
kunta m. barbed arrow, javelin; lance lat. contus; fr. contusion. kuntān praveśaya bring the guards.
Kuntaka |ka| mr. hist. n.p. by Rājānaka Kuntaka, 10th century Kaśmīra poet, author of Vakrok tijīvita.
kuntala [kuntala] m. hair; lock of hair — m. geo. land of the kuntala, ancient name of Karṇāṭa | prince of the Kuntalās | pl. geo. np. of the people of the Kuntalās — f. kuntalā ifc. hair of (iic.).
kuntākunti [red. kunta] adv. in combat spear against spear.
Kunti m. geo. man of a people of the North West | [kuntibhoja] myth. n.p. of Prince Kunti | pl. kuntayas geo. the Kunti people — f. cf. Kunti.

kuntibhoja [bhoja] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Kun tibhoja "Kunti the bon vivant", Prince Kunti of the Yadu dynasty; his mother was the sister of the yādava Sūra, who gave him to adopt her firstborn, his daughter Pṛthā, who thus became Kunti; he fought in the great battle of Kuruksetra alongside the Pāṇḍavās with his brother Purujit.

Kunti [f. Kunti] f. myth. [Mah.] np. of Kunti "(adopted daughter) of Kunti", epith. of Pṛthā daughter of Śūrasena, sister of Vasudeva (and thus paternal aunt of Kṛṣṇa); she received from the sage [ṛṣi] Durvāsā a mantra having the power to invoke the gods to give birth; she tried it at the moment by invoking Sūrya, from whom was born her eldest Karņa; later she became the 1st wife of King Pāṇḍu, who could not have sexual relations under penalty of death; she gave birth to Yudhisthira by Dharma, to Bhīma by Vāyu, and to Arjuna by Indra.
kuntīstuti [stuti] f. lit. [BhP.] hymn of praise to Kṛṣṇa of Kuntī.
√ কুন্থ kunth v. [1] pr. (kunthati) to hurt | to suffer.
Kunthu [kunthu] m. cf. kunthunātha.
kunthunātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of Kunthu or kunthunātha "Martyr", 17th tīrthankara; his body is golden, his symbol is a goat.

kunda m. bio. bot. Jasminum multiflorum, white jasmine; it blooms in spring; in poetry, it evokes the whiteness of teeth — n. white jasmine flower, very fragrant | myth. Sarasvatī wears a garland of them. kundaih savibhramavadhūhasitāvadātairuddyoti tānyupavanāni manoharāṇi | cittaṃ munerapi haranti nivṛttarāgam prāgeva rāgamalināni manāṃsi yūnām | [Rtusaṃhāra] The groves illuminated with jasmine flowers, evoking the immaculate radiance of the smile of attractive young women, disturb even the minds of ascetics who have tamed their passions, and all the more so those of young men just awakened to sensuality.
kundāvadāta [avadāta] amnf kundāvadātā of the whiteness of jasmine (noted teeth).

√ kup v. [4] pr. (kúpyati) pft. (cukopa) pp. (ku pita) pf. (pra) to agitate; to boil | to become irritated with someone. (g. dat.) | to be irritated, to get angry — ca. (ko payati) to irritate | lat. cupio.
kupitá [pp. kup] amnf kupitā irritated, angry. কুপুত্ৰ kupuruṣa [ku₁puruṣa] m. bad man | despicable man; coward.
kupya [pfp. [1] kup] amnf kupyā irritable — n. non-precious metal.
kubuddhi [ku₁buddhi] amnf who has vile feelings; ill-intentioned | stupid — f. erroneous opinion.

Kubera var. Kuvera m. myth. np. of Ku bera "Deformed", born of the progenitor | prajāpati | Pulastya and the Word [Go]; angered by his devotion to Brahmā, from which he was excluded, Pulastya recreated himself in the form of Viśravā to father him with Idavidā; Kubera₁ is the regent of the oceans and rivers; he performed severe penances to obtain from Brahmā the status of protector of the universe | lokapāla|, and to obtain the title of King of Kings [Rājarāja]; he is the guardian [dikpāla] of the direction of the north; the Indian Croesus, Kubera₁ is the god of wealth, guardian of the nine treasures | navanidhi|, chief of the genies | yakṣās| and hidden spirits |guhyakās|; the pre-men [kinnarās] and the chimeras [kimpuruṣās] are his servants; his half-brother Rāvaṇa usurped his throne in Lankā and stole his flying chariot

Flowery | Puṣpaka | ; he established his capital Alakā on Mount Gandhamādana; his magnificent palace was built by Viśvakarmā; his marvelous garden Caitraratha is located on Mount Mandara; he is depicted as deformed and obese | kumbhāṇḍa|, with eyes bulging from alcohol; it is sometimes said that he has one eye [Ekapinga], three legs and eight teeth; he is the friend of Shiva [Harasakhi]; the mongoose [nakula] brings him treasures; his mount is a man | naravāhana|, a horse or a mongoose; Rddhi or Cārvī is his wife; he has sons Nalakūbara and Maņigrīva, and a daughter Mīnākṣī; cf. Dhaneśvara, Nararāja, Mayurāja, Rat nagarbha, Vaiśravaṇa, Pāñcika | hist. n.p. of the brah mane Kubera₁, of the vātsyāyana lineage, father of Arthapati₁, great-grandfather of Bāṇa₂.
kuberadatta [datta] m. bed. [DKC.] np. from the rich merchant of Campā kuberadatta "Don of Kube ra"; Kulapālikā is his daughter.

kuberapūjā |pūjā| f. cf. dhanvantaritrayodaśī. কুজ্ব kubjá amnf kubjā hunchback, bent — m. hunchback; hunchbacks are traditionally used as spies || gr. v ; lat. gibbus. kubjībhū to bend. kubjavāmanakirātāḥ lit. |K.| hunchbacks, dwarves and savages (court jesters).

kubjaka [ka] amnf kubjikā humped, bent; in firme — m. humped | bio. bot. Rosa moschata, musk rose | bio. bot. Trapa bispinosa, aquatic plant of the lakes of Kashmir; its fruit, the sin hara nut, is a food and a medicinal plant — f. cf. kubjikā. কুত্যিকা kubjikā [f. kubjaka] f. myth. [Tantra] np. of the Newar goddess kubjikā, androgynous aspect of Durgā; during her festival in Nepal, she is represented by an 8-year-old girl; her cult is explained in the Manthānabhairava Tantra.
kubjikātantra [Tantra] n. lit. np. of the Kub jikātantra, an esoteric work of the Kaula tradition.
kubjikāmata [mata] n. phil. [Tantra] n.p. of Kub jikāmata, kaula doctrine.

kubjikāyantra | yantra| n. SOC. geometric diagram of kubjikā, support of the ten powers [mahāvidyā] of the Goddess; around the central bindu, seat of Siddhilakṣmī, a triangle then a hexagon carry the other nine.
kumati [ku₁mati] amnf feeble-minded; idiot — f. idiocy; madness.
kumanas [ku₁manas] amnf angry, angry.

kumārá m. boy, young man; son | prince; page; knight | myth. np. of Kumāra "prince", epithet of the (ever young and beautiful) god Skanda Kārttikeya | myth. np. of the [sampradāya] vaiṣṇava Kumāra₁ movement founded by Vallabhācārya and venerating the child Kṛṣṇa; cf. Srīnāthajī — n. pure gold — f. kumārī adolescent girl, young girl | maiden, virgin | myth. np. of kumārī "Princess", epithet of not. Durgā — m. effeminate man.
kumāraka [ka] m. child, boy, young man — f. kumārikā girl, young woman, virgin | myth. one of the 10 regions [dvīpa] forming the jambudvīpa.

kumāragiri [giri] m. hist. np. of King Kumaragiri Reddy of Kondavīdu (1386–1402); a great lover of art, he left the government to his brother-in-law Katayavema, and took care to organize festivals like the vasantotsava; he was nicknamed Karpūra Vasanta Rāyalu; he is credited with the dance treatise Va santarājīya; his court dancer Lakumadevī was renowned.

Kumārajīva [jīva] m. hist. np. of the Brahman scholar Kumārajīva (4th century), who spread Buddhism in Central Asia and China; born in Kucha (on the Silk Road north of the Taklamakan) to the Brahman Kumārāyana and the Kuchian princess Jīvakā, he traveled with his mother to India and was ordained a Buddhist monk in the Mahāyāna tradition; returning home, a celebrated scholar, he was brought to the Emperor of China to lead a team translating Buddhist texts without krits into Chinese; he fixed in Chinese the abhidharma terminology of Mahāyāna.
kumāratantra | tantra | n. lit. np. of the Kumāra tantra, manual of exorcism to cure children possessed by a demon.
kumāratva |tva| n. youth (of a boy).
kumāradatta | datta | m. np. of kumāradatta, man's name "given by Kumāra".
Kumāradāsa |dāsa| m. hist. np. of the Ceylonese prince Kumāradāsa (~517~526), author of the Jānakīharaņa; he is also called Kumārabhaṭṭa.

Kumārapāla |pāla| mr. hist. n.p. of King Caulukya Kumārapāla of Gurjara; he succeeded his uncle Jayasimha₄ Siddharāja in 1143; its capital was Aņahilapāṭaka; Hemacandra Sūri converted him to Jainism; he died in 1173.
kumārapālita [pālita] m. bed. [K.] np. of Kumārapālitā, minister of King Sūdraka₁. kumārapūrņimā [pūrņimā] f. full moon of the month āśvina; Kārttikeya is celebrated there; cf. aśvattha.
Kumārabhaṭṭa [Bhaṭṭa] m. hist. n.p. of the poet prince of Ceylon Kumārabhatta; cf. Kumāradāsa.
Kumārabhīmeśvara [bhīmeśvara] m. geo. np. śivalinga Kumārabhīmeśvara, established from the pañcārāmakṣetra kumārārāma by Kumāra; it is made of white limestone, more than 4 meters high.

kumāravana [vana] n. myth. [BhP.] np. of the kumāravana wood "Skanda's wood", near Mount Kailāsa; it was there that Shiva and Parvati were engaged in marital relations, when a group of sages led by Sunaka went there to honor Shiva; surprised in his amorous encounter, he cursed the forest to turn into a woman any man who entered it; Sudyumna came one day to hunt there, and thus became the beautiful Ida again. kumāravyākaraņa [vyākaraņa] n. lit. np. of the Kumāravyākaraņa "grammar of Kumāra", work of the bd. Śarvavarmā grammarian; cf. Kātantra.
kumāraśramaṇā [śramaṇā] f. young nun.

kumārasambhava [sambhava] m. lit. np. from kumārasambhava "Origins of Kumāra", a poem [kāvya] in the form of a lyric epic by Kālidāsa, composed around 400; it describes the events leading to the birth of Kumāra, who is to be born to kill the demon Tāraka; the gods ask Kāma to make Shiva fall in love with Pārvatī, daughter of Himavān, but the latter's anger, practicing his asceticism, reduced him to ashes; Pārvatī achieves her goal by becoming an ascetic herself, and the poem ends with their union; the poem has 8 cantos | sarga | attributed to Kālidāsa; 9 additional cantos have no certain attribution; cf. Viśausadhi, Sañjīvanī, Vivaraņa₁.

kumārārāma [ārāma] m. geo. n.p. from kumārārāma, a major Shaivite pilgrimage site to Somarla kota in Andhra country, east of the Godāvarī delta; it is one of the five garden sanctuaries | pañcārāmakṣetra|; the temple was built by king Cālukya Bhīma₂ at the end of the 9th century; cf. Kumārabhīmeśvara.

kumāralāta m. hist. np. of the grammarian bd. kumāralāta; he lived at the end of the 2nd century at the Kuṣāṇa court of Takṣaśilā; he founded the bd. sautrāntika school; he wrote a Sanskrit grammar inspired (or originally) by the Kātantra; he is also credited with the Kalpanāmanditikā; he is sometimes identified with Aśvaghosa.
kumāri iic. kumārī.
kumārimata | mata| amnf kumārimatā estimated by kumārī.
