kumārilakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. [Ratiramaṇa] bodily mark indicating the type of a young girl.

kumārila m. hist. np. of kumārila Bhaṭṭa, famous teacher of Mīmāmsā; he lived in South India in the 8th century, and founded the bhattamata school; he refuted the apoha theory of Dinnāga; he mocked the pedantry of grammarians like Patañjali₁; we owe him in particular the Slokavārttika, the Tantravārttika, the Bṛhaṭṭīkā, the Madhyamaṭīkā; he ended his life by immolating himself in a straw fire [tuṣānala].

kumitra [ku₁mitra] m. false friendship. marmāntaḥ parihāso yāvatkriyamāṇabhadrakatvam ca smaranam ca duşkṛtānām trīṇi kumitrasya cihnāni | making jokes to hurt, maintaining relationships as long as they are profitable, remembering only bad times, are the three signs of false friendship.
kumud [Kumuda] n. organic. bot. Nymphaea escu lenta, white lotus.
kúmudvat [vat] amnf kumudvatī abundant in white lotus — f. kumudvatī lotus-covered pond.

kúmuda [ku₁mudā] amnf kumudā [“that which brings such joy” | joyful, pleasant — n. bio. bot. Nymphæa esculenta, night-blooming lotus; it is said to bloom at moonrise; one compares one's teeth to it in a smile — m. camphor | myth. np. of the celestial elephant Kumuda “Joyful”, gar
dien [diggaja] of the SouthWest — f. kumudā myth. n.p. of Kumudā, aspect of Durgā; Prayāga is his devīpītha.

kumudabāndhava [bāndhava] m. lit. [“friend of the white lotus (which blooms at its rising)”] epith. of Candra, the Moon. udayati candrah kumudabāndhavah gram. |Rāmarudrī| The Moon, friend of the white lotus, rises (typical example of apposition between nouns).
kúmudavat |vat| amnf Kumudavatī abundant in white lotus — f. Kumudavatī pond covered with lo
tus | myth. |Rām. | np. of Princess Kumudavatī, wife of Kuśa.
kumudika [ika] amnf kumudikī abundant in white lotus.
kumudinī |in| f. lotus-covered pond.

kumbhá m. jug, potàeau; jar, vase, urn; syn. kalaśa | soc. funerary urn | | kumbharāśi | astr. zodiacal sign [rāśi] of Aquarius | frontal hump of the elephant | myth. sacred vessel containing ambrosia |amrta| from the churning of the sea of milk | kṣīrodamathana | myth. np. of kumbha "jug", son of Kumbhakarņa — f. kumbhā prostitute — f. cf. kumbhī.

Kumbhakarna | Karna | m. myth. | Rām. | np. of the ogrevampire [rākṣasa] Kumbhakarṇa "Jar Ear", son of Viśravā and Keśinī₂, brother of Rāvaṇa, of gigantic size and with an insatiable appetite; he wanted to ask Brahmā as a reward for his penances the destruction of the gods [nirdevatva]; frightened by his voracity, the gods obtained that Saras vatī danced on his tongue when he made his request; she made him make a slip of the tongue and he actually asked for eternal sleep [nidrāvattva]; he only wakes up one day every 6 months; Rāvaṇa made him drink 2000 jugs of alcohol to wake him up and fight Rāma's army; he defeated Sugrīva, but Rāma cut off his head; kumbha and Nikumbha₁ are his sons | hist. np. of King Kumbhakarna₁ of the Rajput Sisodia dynasty of Mewar; he reigned from 1433 to 1468 and fought the sultans of Malwa and Gujarat; he is credited with the fortress of Kumbhalgarh, at 1075 m, with 38 km of walls.
kumbhákāra [kāra] m. potter — f. kumbhakārī potter's wife.

kumbhakoṇa |koṇa| n. geo. np. of the city of kumbhakoṇa, on the banks of the Kāverī (mod. Kumbakonam, district of Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu); Cola capital in the 7th century, it was disputed between the Pallavās and the Pāṇḍyās, conquered by the latter in 1290, then attached to the empire of Vijayanagara; it is a pilgrimage city, with many temples; Rāghavendra Svāmī studied there; the Mahāmaha basin is the object of a large annual pilgrimage.
kumbhadāsī [dāsī] f. prostitute.
kumbhádhara [dhara] m. astr. ["who carries the jar re"] sign of Aquarius; syn. kumbharāśi.
Kumbhamela | Mela | m. soc. major pilgrimage taking place on a 12-year cycle, the period of Jupiter; it takes place alternately at Allahabad | Prayāga|, Harid

war [haridvāra], Ujjain [Ujjayinī] and Nasik [Nāsika]; myth. these are the 4 places where a drop of soma fell to earth which Indra in the form of a falcon carried in the air in the sacred vessel |kumbha|.
kumbhayoni | yoni | m. myth. np. of kumbhayoni, epith. of Agastya "born in a jug".
kumbhárāśi [rāśi] m. astr. sign of Aquarius.
kumbhāṇḍa [aṇḍa] amnf kumbhāṇḍā pot-bellied, pot-bellied | pl. kumbhāṇḍās myth. pot-bellied genies; syn. yaksās.

kumbhaka [kumbhaka] m. ifc. pot of, me sure of (iic.) — mn phil. [Yoga] cessation of res breathing, the mouth closed and the nostrils blocked by the fingers of the right hand | frontal hump of the elephant — f. kumbhikā small jug, pitcher.
kumbhin [kumbhain] amnf kumbhinī that carries a jar; that resembles a pot — m. ["that has a cranial protuberance"] elephant | math. symb. the number 8 — f. kumbhinī the earth.
kumbhila [kumbhala] m. thief, burglar; plagiarist | abortion.
kumbhī [f. kumbha] f. small jug; small jar, small earthenware pot | bd. hell.
kumbhīka [ka] m. soc. eromenos boy.

kumbhīnása [nasa] m. large venomous snake — f. kumbhīnasī myth. n.p. of kumbhīnasī "with pitcher-shaped nostrils", wife of the gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa — m. Kumbhīnasi myth. [Mah.] np. of the demon Kumbhīnasi.
kumbhīpāka [pāka] m. cooking in a pot, food cooked in a pot | myth. [PP.] np. of kumbhīpāka, one of the 7 hells, where the damned are thrown into cauldrons of boiling oil.
Kumbhīpākanaraka [naraka] m. myth. np. of the Kumbhīpākanaraka "burning hell", where the damned are burned in the Pitrloka; also called Pitrtīrtha.

kumbhīra [ra] m. gharial crocodile | bed. [KSS.] np. of King Kumbīra of Kāñcī, father of Varuņasenā. কুংব্ৰ kuranga mf kurangī antelope, deer; not. zoo. Tetracerus quadricorni, cf. catuḥśṛṅga — v. |11| pr. r. (kurangāyate) behave like an antelope.

kuraṇṭa m. bio. bot. Amaranthus caudatus, yellow amaranth; it is considered a bad omen | var. kuranda id. kurantaka var. kurandaka |ka| m. bio. id. কুংৰক kurabaka m. bio. bot. Amaranthus cruentus, red amaranth; it is said to bloom only after a young girl has looked at it | kuravaka id.
kurara mf kurarī bio. zoo. Pandion haliaetus,
osprey | fishing bird of prey | gull.

kúru m. myth. np. of the paurava Kuru₁, king of the lunar lineage; he is son of King Samvarana and Ta patī; he is ancestor of Śāmtanu | myth. his kingdom, the kuruvarșa, one of the 10 subcontinents [dvīpa] forming the jambudvīpa | myth. np. of Kuru₁, son of King Agnīdhra and the nymph Pūrvacitti — mf kurū inhabitant of Kurukṣetra | pl. kuravas myth. the kuravas, ancient people of northern India.

kuruksetra [kṣetra] n. geo. np. of the vast plain of Kurukṣetra, between the Sarasvatī₁ and Dṛṣadvatī rivers, northwest of Delhi | myth. [Mah.] territory of the kuravas; site of the great battle between the Kauravās and the Pāṇḍavās. dharmaksetre kuruksetre [BhG.] on the land of Kuru₁, on the land of Destiny.
kurucara [cara] amnf kurucarī which travels through the Kuruksetra.
Kurujāngala | jāngala | n. geo. np. of Kurujāngala | "land of Kuru₁", in the Ganges valley; its capital was Hastināpura — m. pl. kurujāngalās its inhabitants.
kurunandana [nandana] amnf kurunandanā who brings joy to the Kauravās — m. myth. epith. not. of Yudhisthira.
kurupañcāla [pañcāla] m. pl. geo. the kuravas and the Pañcālās.
kurupañcālatrā [trā] adv. as among the Ku ravas and the Pañcālās.
kuruvarṣa [varṣa] n. myth. land of the kuravas, one of the 9 watersheds [varṣa] of the World.
kuruśrávana [śravana₁] m. ved. [RV.] np. of king Kuruśravana "Glory of the kuravas", descendant of Trasadasyu. কু হকুপ্পা kurukullā f. bd. n.p. of the goddess Tantr. Ku rukullā.
kuruvinda n. cinnabar | type of ruby || fr. corundum.
kurūpa |ku₁rūpa| amnf kurūpā poorly formed, misshapen; ugly.
kurvat [ppr. kṛ₁] amnf kurvantī by noting. by acting as a servant. aśabdam kurvan by not making a noise. kurvadrūpah whose form is efficient.
kurvāṇa [ppr. mo. kṛ₁] amnf kurvāṇā doing — m. he who does — f. kurvāṇā she who does.

√ kul v. [1] pr. (kolati) to accumulate. কুল kúla [act. kul] n. troop, crowd; horde; herd. soc. family; race; clan; tribe, caste; nobility, royal dynasty | family home | phil. [Tantra] doctrine of the good family; [Ānandabhaṭṭa] it prescribes 9 obligations: good conduct [ācāra],
discipline [vinaya], acquisition of knowledge [vidyā], good social standing [pratisthā₁], pilgrimage [tīrthadarśana], obedience to the texts
sacred [niṣṭhā₂], endogamy [āvṛtti], practice of
penances [tapas] and generosity [dāna]; cf. kaula — f. kulā ifc. id. caurasyakulam band of thieves.
kúlagiri [giri] m. myth. main mountain range of a varșa; there are 7 of them; not. for Bhāratavarṣa: Mahendra₁, Sahya, Śuktimān, Ŗkṣa₁, Vindhya and Pāriyātra.
kulaguru [guru] m. soc. family tutor.
kulacaritra [caritra] n. custom. kulacūdāmaņi [cūdāmaņi] n. [kulacūdāmaņi Tantra lit. n.p. from the Nigama Kulacūdāmaņi, late Tantra of the Kaula doctrine (14th century).
kulaja [ja] amnf kulajā of good family | soc. of royal lineage.
kulattha [stha] m. bio. bot. Dolichos uniflorus, a pod-shaped vegetable used to feed livestock.
kuladevatā [devatā] f. soc. tutelary deity of a lineage (opp. istadevatā, chosen deity) |var. ku ladevī id.
kuladharma [dharma] n. soc. family obligations | soc. ["clan religion"] tantric rites; cf. kulācāra.
kulapati | pati | m. soc. head of family; clan chief | school principal; university rector.
kúlaparvata [parvata] m. cf. kulagiri.

kulapālikā [pālikā] f. lit. [DKC.] np. of kulapālikā, daughter of the merchant Kuberadatta, who had promised her to the prodigal son Dhanamitra, but as he had squandered his fortune, he wanted to marry her to Arthapati.
kulaputra | putra | m. son of (good) family.
kulapurāṇa | purāṇa | n. lit. collection of stories and legends concerning the origins of a caste, tribe or dynasty.
kulamuktikallolinī [muktikallolinī] f. bed. n.p. from the kulamuktikallolinī “Clan Liberation Torrent”, śākta text.
kulayāga [yāga] m. phil. [Trika] tantric transgression technique, during the expansion phase [vikāsa] of spiritual realization; the prohibitions of meat, alcohol and sex are ignored; cf. dūtī.
kulavadhū | vadhū | f. soc. respectable wife.
kulavadhūtā [tā] f. quality of a respectable housewife.
kulaśīla [śīla] n. family and character.
kúlaśekhara [śekhara] m. hist. np. of King Kulaśekhara Perumāl, 10th of the ālvār saints; he reigned in Malaya in the 9th century; he is the author of the devotional poem Mukundamālā.

kulasantati [santati] f. phil. [Tantra] the "descent dance of the family", symbolic rite [cakrapūjā] performed by the gesture [mudrā] of touching one's majoryoni with one's thumblinga, evoking the ritual union of one's inner Śakti identified with sakti Caṇḍikā with the Supreme Being SivaBhairava.
kulācāra [ācāra] m. phil. [Tantra] the "way of the clan", doctrine developed in the Kulārņava tan tra, teaching monism through the transgression of opposites; cf. makārapañcaka.

kulādhīna [adhīna] n. soc. monastery [maṭha] of the village of origin of a family, in gen. śaiva. kulārņava [arṇava] n. [kulārṇavatantra] lit. "Ocean of the Way of the Clan", np. of the Kulārṇava Tantra, of non-dualistic kaula Shaivite doctrine; it was compiled in the 12th century — n. [kulārṇavatantra] lit. id.
kulotpanna [utpanna] amnf kulotpannā soc. from a good family — ifc. from gotra (iic.).

kulaka [kulaka] n. kernel of a fruit | gram. sequence of sentences sharing the government of a verb | lit. passage of poetry where several verses are syntactically linked — ifc. multitude of iic. — m. patron of a guild; craftsman of good family.
kulaṭā f. woman of ill repute.
kulāya mn fabric; network | bird's nest; niche; location, place, residence.
kulāyanilāya [nilāya] m. nest rest; brooding.
kulāyanilāyin |nilāyin| amnf kulāyanilāyinī (bird) that broods.
kulāyastha |stha| amnf kulāyasthā |“who has built a nest” | bird. কুলাল kúlāla [kulāla] m. potter | bio. wild rooster, pheasant.
kulālacakra | cakra | n. potter's wheel.
kulika [kulaika] amnf kulikā of good family — m. respectable person.
kulinga [ku₁linga] mf kulingī magpie |sparrow.
kulin [kulain] amnf kulinī of good family — f. kulinī bio. bot. Impatiens balsamina, impatience.
Kulinda m. geo. name of a country in the central Himalayas | hist. np. of Kulinda, princely title of this country | pl. kulindās geo. its inhabitants.
kúliśa m. axe, hatchet — n. var. kulīśa myth. np. of Indra's thunderbolt; syn. vajra | by extension diamond — ifc. lit. title of works.
kuliśamani [mani] m. glans penis.
kulīna [kulaīna] amnf kulīnā noble, of noble origin, of good family — ifc. of the family of (iic.) — m. soc. high-class Bengali brahmin | soc. adept of the left-hand path |kulācāra|; syn. kaula.
kulīya [kulaīya] ifc. amnf kulīyā appar tenant à la famille de (iic.).
kulīra m. bio. crab | astr. zodiac sign of Cancer; syn. karkata.
kulīraka |ka| mr. little crab.

kulphá var. gulpha m. ankle.
kulphadaghná [daghna] amnf kulphadaghnā f. kulphadaghnī who has (water) up to their ankles.
kulya [kulaya] amnf kulyā concerning the family or clan | of good family — m. honorable man — n. friendly request concerning the family; congratulations; condolences — f. kulyā₂ family custom.
kulyā f. stream; channel. কুল্লুক kullūka m. hist. n.p. by kullūka Bhaṭṭa, 15th century commentator of Manu, author of the Man varthamuktāvalī.
kulva amnf kulvā bald | lat. calvus.
kúvala m. bio. bot. Ziziphus mauritiana, jujube — n. its fruit, the jujube or Chinese date, small edible fruit, purple when ripe | bio. bot. Nymphæa nelumbo, blue lotus.
kuvalaya [ya] n. organic. bot. Nymphaea nelumbo, blue lo tus.

kuvalayamālā [mālā] f. bed. n.p. of the Kuva layamālā, a Jaina work in prākṛta by Uddyotana₁ Sūri, composed in Jālore (Rājasthāna) in 778 | bed. |Viddhaśālabhañjikā| n.p. of Kuvalayamālā₁, princess of the country of the Kuntalās with whom king Vidyādharamalla is in love.
kuvalayānanda |ānanda| m. lit. np. from Kuva layānanda "Joy of the blue lotus", treatise on rhetoric by Appayya Dīksita.
kuvalayāśva [aśva] m. cf. kuvalāśva.
kuvalāśva [aśva] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of king Kuvalāsva or Kuvalayāsva "On the blue horse", son of Brhadaśva; he killed the asura Dhundhu |Dhundhumāra|.
kuvid [ku₁id] adv. ved. (interrogation) if? is it that? where then?.
kuvitsa |sa₂| m. ved. whoever; a stranger.
Kuvera [ku₁vera] amnf kuverā Deformed, monstrous — m. myth. np. of Kuvera "Deformed", original form of the later name Kubera.

kuśá m. bio. bot. Desmostachya bipinnata, a herbaceous plant of the grass family, with a large rhizome and sharp leaves; meadow grass; fodder. Sacred herb used in religious ceremonies since the Vedic period, with purifying virtues; syn. darbha; it serves as a meditation couch; ropes are also made from it | myth. [Rām.] np. of Kuśa₁, son of King Rāma, twin of Lava; upon his father's death he became king of Ayodhyā; his wife was Princess Kumudavatī; he was killed fighting the asura Durjaya; [Ragh.] his son Atithi₁ succeeded him. myth. [Rām.] np. of the rājarṣi Kuśa₁, spiritual son of Brahmā; His sons by Vaidarbhī are Kuśāmba, Who founded the city of Kauśāmbī, Kuśanābha, Who founded the city of MahodayāKanyākubjā, Amūrtarajasa Who founded the city of Dharmāranya, and Vasu₃ Who founded the city of GirivrajaRājagṛha — n. water — f. kuśā wooden or metal needle, used as a recitation marker — f. kuśī soc. kuśahasta holding Kuśa₁ by the hand.
kuśadvīpa [dvīpa] m. myth. one of the 7 continents [dvīpa], surrounded by a sea of ghṛta.

kuśadhvaja [dhvaja] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the sage kuśadhvaja "Who has the sacred herb as his emblem", son of Brhaspati; his daughter is the very beautiful Vedavatī, whom he did not want to marry to anyone except Vișnu; the daitya Sambhu₁, furious at not being able to see her married, killed him; his wife threw herself on his funeral pyre, and his daughter took refuge as an ascetic in a forest, where she was attacked by Rāvaṇa | myth. [Rām.] np. of kuśadhvaja₁ Janaka, son of Hras varomā; after the victory of his elder brother Jana karāja over the king Sudhanvā₁ Who had attacked Mi thilā, he obtained his throne and became king of Sāmkāśyā; He had two daughters, Māndavī who married Bharata₁, and Srutakīrti₁ who married Satrughna.

Kuśanābha [nābhi] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of King Kuśanābha, son of Kuśa₁; he founded the prosperous city of Kanyākubjā [Mahodayā]; he had 100 very beautiful daughters by the nymph [apsaras] Ghṛtācī; they were made hunchbacked by Vāyu for not yielding to his desires; he married them to King Brahma datta, and they regained their beauty; he then made a sacrifice to obtain a son like Indra, and Gādhi was born to him.
kuśapiñjūla [piñjūla] n. tuft or armful of grass Kuśa₁.

kuśalava | lava | m. du. kuśalavau myth. np. of the kuśalavau, twin sons of Rāma Kuśa₁ and lava; they were raised by Vālmīki, Who taught them to recite his Rāmāyaṇa in public; they are therefore also Kuśīlavau "the two Bards".
kuśalavopākhyāna | upākhyāna | n. lit. np. du kuśalavopākhyāna "History of Kuśa₁ and lava", late addition to the uttarakānda of the Rām.

kuśásthala [sthala] n. geo. np. of Kuśasthala "where one finds the Kuśa₁ grass", epith. of the city of Kānyakubja — f. Kuśasthalī myth. np. of Kuśasthalī, epith. of the city of Dvārakā | myth. capital of King Revata.

kuśāgra | agra | n. sharp point of grass Kuśa₁ — amnf kuśāgrā cutting; penetrating; perspi cace, Intelligent — m. myth. np. of the king of Magadha kuśāgra "the Intelligent", son of Brhadratha, brother of Jarāsandha.
kuśāgrabuddhi [buddhi] amnf sharp-witted; Intelligent, shrewd, perceptive — f. intelligence; cunning.
kuśāgrīya [īya] amnf kuśāgrīyā sharp as grass Kuśa₁; penetrating. kuśāgrīyā buddhih sharp intelligence.
Kuśāvarta [āvarta] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of a ford on the Ganges | myth. n.p. of the Kuśāvarta muni | pl. kuśāvartās his descendants.
kuśāśva [aśva] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Viśālā kuśāśva, son of Sahadeva₂, father of Somadatta₁.

kuśāsana |āsana| n. soc. small mat of sacred grass, used for meditation. কুখাল kúśala [Kuśa₁la] amnf kuśalā good, just, appropriate to, suitable for (g.) | healthy, prosperous, well | capable, skillful, adept; expert, learned — n. well-being, prosperity, good health. kuśalam adr. well. kuśalam te (hello) how are you? kuśalam asti vā var. kuśalamvā how are you? ... api kuśalam how is ... (g.)? kuśalam iva it's fine. kutra kuśalam how would that be? kuśalamasya he is well.
kuśalin |in| amnf kuśalinī prosperous; well for so much; in good condition.
Kuśāmba m. myth. [Rām.] np. of King Kuśāmba, son of Kuśa₁; he founded the City of Kauśāmbī.
kuśi iic. kuśin.

Kuśinagara | nagara | n. geo. n.p. the City of Kuśinagara, capital of the Malla dynasty; mod. Kasia, east of mod. Uttar Pradesh; Buddha died there; it is a great place of pilgrimage bd. — f. kuśinagarī id.

Kuśiká amnf Kuśikā affected by strabismus myth. Mah. np. of King Paurava Kuśika "Who lou che", son of Balākāśva, descendant of Bharata; he did penance to obtain an invincible son, the equal of Indra; touched by his devotions, Indra was incarnated in his son Gādhi | myth. [Rām.] "son of Kuśa₁", epith. of Kuśanābha, father of Gādhi.
kuśikaputra | putra | mr. myth. [Rām.] “descendant of Kuśika”, patr. of Viśvāmitra.

kuśe [loc. Kuśa₁] ind. in the grass Kuśa₁.
kuśeśaya [śaya] amnf kuśeśayā lying in the grass Kuśa₁ — n. lotus ["spread out on the water"].

kusīda [related to kuśīda] amnf kusīdā pa resseux, inerte — n. usury; loan at interest.
kusīdapatha | patha | m. usurious interest.
kusīdavṛddhi [vṛddhi] f. interest on a sum lent.
kusīdin |in| amnf kusīdinī moneylender.
kusuma n. flower | fruit — v. [11] pr. (Kusu mayati) pp. (kusumita) cover with flowers.
kusumadhanus [dhanus] m. myth. n.p. of Kusu madhanu, epith. from Kāma "flower archer".

kusumadhanvan [dhanvan] m. myth. np. of Ku sumadhanvā, epith. of Kāma "flower archer" lit. [DKC.] np. of Kusumadhanvā₁, king of Kosala, father of Vasumdharā by his wife Sāgaradattā, and therefore grandfather of Bhāskaravarmā.
Kusumapura [pura] n. geo. np. of Kusumapura, epith. of Pāṭaliputra "City of flowers".
Kusumabāṇa | bāṇa | mr. myth. n.p. of Kusumabāṇa, epith. of Kāma "with flower arrows". kusumamārgaņa [mārgaṇa] m. myth. n.p. from Kusu mamārgaṇa, epith. of Kāma "with flower arrows".
kusumaśara [śara] m. myth. np. of kusumaśara, epith. of Kāma "with flower arrows".
kusumasukumāra [sukumāra] amnf kusuma sukumārā tender as a flower.
kusumāñjali |añjali| m. soc. offering of flowers in the hollow of joined hands.
kusumāyudha [āyudha] m. myth. np. of Ku sumāyudha, epithet of Kāma "armed with flowers". )1 kusumeșu [ișu] m. myth. np. of Kusumaśara, epithet of Kāma "with flower arrows".
kusumita [pp. kusuma] amnf kusumitā in bloom, covered with flowers, flowering.
kusumbha m. organic. bot. Carthamus tincto rius, saffron | ascetic water pot.
kustubha [ku₂stambha] m. myth. n.p. from kustubha, epith. of Viṣṇu "who supports the earth".
kustumburu |ku₁tumburu| mr. coriander — n. coriander seed.
kuha m. deception — v. [11] pr. r. (kuhayate) to astonish by a magic trick or cheating.
kuhaka [kuhaka] m. cheat; prestidigita teur; impostor — nf kuhakā magic trick; cheating, deception | stimulus of laughter, tickling.
kuhana [kuhana] amnf kuhanā envious, hypocritical — m. np. of man "Tartuffe" — f. ku hanā hypocrisy; false piety; envy — n. kuhana goblet (of earthenware or glass).
Kuhanāgopa [gopa] m. myth. np. of Kuhanāgopa, epith. of Kṛṣṇa as Bhagavān "claiming to be a cowherd".
kuhara [ku₂hara] n. cavity, cavern; hole, burrow.
kuhū₁ f. myth. np. of kuhū₁, the new moon, personified as daughter of Angirā | new moon day.
kuhū₁ [onomatopoeia] ind. cuckoo call [kokila].
√ kū v. [6] pr. r. (kuvate) pp. (kūta) pf. (ā) make a sound, utter a cry — intense. r. (kokūyate) to shout.
kūcī f. brush; pencil.
kūjana [na] n. id.
kūjita [pp. kūj] amnf kūjitā filled with murmurs or moans — n. bird cry; chatter, cooing, warbling.

kūṭá amnf kūṭā false, liar, deceiver — mn point, summit, eminence; front, horn | heap; multitude | arch. sanctuary; cf. ekakūṭa, dvikūṭa, trikūṭa | trap, concealed weapon; enigma | illusion, fraud; falsehood.
kūṭakāraka [kāraka] m. liar; false witness.

kūṭakārṣāpaṇa |kārṣāpaṇa| n. counterfeit money. kūṭakārṣāpaṇanyāyaḥ maxim of counterfeit money; it dictates that one who realizes that he has counterfeit money must immediately refrain from using it; it is used as a metaphor for erroneous teachings.
kūṭalekha |lekha| m. falsified document, forgery.
kūṭaśālmalī [śālmalī] f. myth. [PP.] np. d'kūṭaśālmalī "Tricky", one of the 7 hells.
kūṭastha [stha] amnf kūṭasthā which is at the summit; at the head of | phil. unalterable, inamo visible, fixed; uniform, constant; absolute, supreme — n. phil. the soul, the Self [Ātmā].
kūṭasthatā [tā] f. state of being invariable; fixity; uniformity.

kūtasthanitya [nitya] amnf kūtasthanityā phil. eternally invariable; opp. parināmanitya; [Sāṃkhya] qualifies the Being [Puruṣa]; [Vedānta] qualifies the brahman | gram. [Patañjali₁] absolute and invariable; opp. pravahanitya.
kūṭākṣara [akṣara] n. consonants joined in a syllable; ligature.
kūṭiyāṭṭa [malayalam] n. traditional theater of Kerala.
kūḍu m. arch. horseshoe-shaped roof ridge vent.
kūpa m. pit, cavern; well, cistern; fountain. kūpe toyam there is water in the well.
kūpaka [ka] m. hole, cavity; cellar | small well.

kūpakhānaka [khānaka] m. well digger. kūpakhānakanyāyaḥ maxim of the well digger (who uses the water from the well he dug to clean his dirt); by analogy, the study of grammar serves to acquire merit by purifying one's speech.
kūpamandūka [mandūka] amnf kūpamandūkā ["well frog"] sedentary, homebody; whose horizon is limited; syn. udapānamaṇḍūka.
kūpāra m. ocean.
kūbara mnf kūbarī timon.

kūrcá mn bundle, sheaf; sheaf or handful of grass kuśa | brush | part of the human body, limb | place between the eyebrows; beard | plow. gesture pinching the end of the medium with the tip of the thumb | fraud; hypocrisy.
kūrcaka |ka| m. brush, paintbrush; pencil; toothbrush.
kūrcin [in] amnf kūrcinī bearded.
kūrpāsa m. cuirass; padded jacket.

kūrmá m. turtle | myth. np. of Kūrma "Tor kills", 2nd avatar of Viṣṇu, who supported the axis of the churn during the churning of the ocean of milk |kṣīrodamathana|; cf. Akūpāra, Mandara, Vāsuki — f. kūrmī female turtle.
kūrmápurāṇa [purāṇa] n. bed. n.p. from Kūrmapurāṇa or Kaurmapurāṇa, tantric mythological text.
kūrmáprstha | prstha | n. turtle shell.
kūrmāñcala |añcala| m. geo. np. of the Kūrmāncala country in the Himalayas (mod. district of Ku maon in Uttarākhanda).
kūla n. slope, bank, shore, bank, edge.
kūlaṃkaṣa [kaṣa] amnf kūlaṃkaṣā [“who carries its banks” impetuous (torrent).
kūlacara [cara] m. bio. class of animals "living on the banks"; not. elephant [ruru], gaur [gavaya],
buffalo [mahisa], deer [ruru], yak [camara], wild boar [varāha], rhinoceros [khadgin], otter [udra].
kūṣmāṇḍa cf. kuṣmāṇḍa.

√東kṛ₁ v. [5] pr. (kṛṇóti) pr. r. (kṛṇuté) v. [8] pr. (karóti) pr. r. (kurute) imp. (kuru) was. (kariṣyati) pft. (cakāra) pft. r. (cakre) aor. [3] (acīkarat) aor. [4] (akārṣīt) aor. r. [1] (akṛta) cond. (akariṣyat) pp. (kṛta) ppr. (kurvat) ppr. p.s. (kriyamāṇa) ppft. (cakṛvas) inf. (kartum) pfp. (kārya, karaṇīya, kar tavya, kṛtya) abs. (kṛtvā, kṛtya, kāram) pf. (adhi, anu, apa, abhi, alam, ava, ā, āvis, ut, upa, tiras, ni, nis, parā, pari, puras, pra, prati, bahis, vi, sat, sam) to do; accomplish | cause; produce, create; undertake; prepare, make | express, my (familiarity, compassion, love, contempt, etc.) | make (acc.) such as (acc.) — ps. (kriyáte) to be done, to be accomplished, to be created — ca. (kārayati) pp. (kārita) to cause to be done, to cause to be carried out; to ensure — des. (cikīrṣati) des. r. (cikīrṣate) pp. (cikīrṣita) to do | lat. creare; fr. créer. kartā he will do. kartāsmi I must do, I will do. mā kārṣīḥ inj. do not do. mā krthāh inj. do not do. kālam kr to die ["to have fulfilled one's time"]. ciram kr to linger, to be late; to be slow. dandam kr to inflict punishment, to punish. pūjam kr to honor. manasā kr to think, to consider. rājyam kr to rule. vaśīkr to submit to one's will. kanyām kṛ to rape a young girl. sakhyam kṛ to make friends. alam kr to prepare, to adorn; cf. alamkr. padam kurute he takes a step; he puts his foot down. yatheccham kuru do as you please. kuru kurviti karoti do! do! he tells himself as he does (he works hard). kim karavāni te (subj.) what can I do for you?
√ 東 kṛ₂ v. aor. [5] (ákārīt) intens. (cárkarti) to mention, to praise, to celebrate. কুক kṛka m. throat; larynx.
kṛkaṇa |na| m. bio. partridge; pheasant | geo. np. of a locality.
kṛkalāsá [lāsa] m. organic. lizard; chameleon.
kṛkalāsatā [tā] f. chameleon state.
kṛkalāsatva [tva] n. id.
kṛkavāku [vāka] m. rooster | peacock | chameleon — f. chicken.

kṛcchrá [kṛśra] amnf kṛcchrā difficult, troublesome, dangerous; bad (illness) — n. difficulty, need, danger; pain; sin — v. [11] pr. r. (kṛcchrāyate) to experience difficulties | to make difficult. kṛcchreṇa var. kṛcchrāt, kṛcchratas adv. with difficulty.
krcchrakarman | karman | n. arduous work.
kṛcchrátā |tā| f. med. painful state; bad condition.
kṛcchramūtra |mūtra| amnf kṛcchramūtrā med. who suffers when urinating.
kṛcchramūtratva [tva] n. med. difficulty urinating.
kṛcchramūtrapurīṣa | purīṣa | amnf kṛcchramūtrapurīṣā med. who has difficulty urinating and defecating.
krcchramūtrapurīṣatva |tva| n. med. difficulty urinating and defecating.
kṛcchrāt |abl. kṛcchra| iic. (pp.) with difficulty.
kṛcchrādavāpta | avāpta | amnf kṛcchrādavāptā obtained with difficulty.
kṛcchrin [kṛcchrain] amnf kṛcchrinī who experiences difficulties; who struggles, who suffers.

√ krt₁ v. [6] pr. (krntati) pft. (cakarta) aor. [5] (akartīt) pp. (kṛtta) pf. (ava, ut, ni, nis, vi) to cut, divide, slice | to cut off | (figuratively) to destroy || Latin: culter; French: couteau; English: to cut.

krt₂ [agt. kr₁] ifc. amnf who has done, who has accomplished, who has executed (iic.); author of (iic.) | gram. suffix [pratyaya] primary (form of nouns, participles and indeclinable nouns from the root); opp. taddhita. sukṛt who acted well. karmakrt who did the work. pāpakṛt who committed a sin. mantrakṛt to whom a mantra was revealed. punyakrt who did a good deed. karmakṛt who did the work. śāstrakṛt who made treaties. bhāṣyakṛt who made a commentary.
krtpratyaya | pratyaya | mr. gram. primary noun formation suffix.
kṛtvan |van| ifc. amnf kṛtvarī who acts, who performs. pūrvakāmakṛtvan amn véd. having granted wishes in the past.

kṛdanta | anta | m. gram. primary derivative. bhūte kṛdantaḥ gram. passive past participle; it agrees with the sole actant of an intransitive verb |akarmaka| and with the patient of a transitive verb sakarmaka].
kṛdantarūpamālā |rūpamālā| f. gram. list of declined forms of primary derivatives.
kṛdvṛtti |vṛtti| f. gram. formation of primary nominal theme, obtained by the action of a suffix kṛt₂ on a root.

kṛtá |pp. kṛ₁| amnf kṛtā done, accomplished; finished; well done, perfect | prepared; obtained — ii. who has done; accomplished in — ifc. who is the object of, become, made such to (ii.) — n. deed, action, act; good deed, benefit | soc. (lucky) roll of the die of 4; side of the die marked 4 | myth. 1st age | yuga | of the world, golden age. kṛtam adv. enough (i.), that cease, not ... kṛtaṃ saṃdehena enough hesitation. kṛtametādṛśena asaṃgatena pralāpena Stop speaking in this absurd manner. krte var. krtena ind. for; on behalf of, because of (g. ii.) | having accomplished (iic.). mama kṛte for my account. asmatkrte for us. amīṣām prāṇānām kṛte for this life.
kṛtakarman | karman | amnf kṛtakarmaṇī who has performed the rites; who has done his duty — n. act performed.

kṛtakṛtya |kṛtya| amnf kṛtakṛtyā who has accomplished his task, satisfied — n. phil. | "achievement of the goal" serenity; liberation; feeling of having accomplished all that had to be accomplished | what is done and what remains to be done.
kṛtakṛtyatā [tā] f. condition of having accomplished one's task.
kṛtákrudha [krudhā] amnf kṛtakrudhā angry, upset.

kṛtaghna |ghna| amnf kṛtaghnā | "who destroys what has been done"] who forgets the good deed, ungrateful; opp. kṛtajña. kṛtajña [ jña ] amnf kṛtajñā ["who knows what has been done"] grateful; opp. kṛtaghna.
kṛtánāmaka |nāmaka| amnf kṛtánāmikā named.
kṛtánāmadheya [nāmadheya] amnf kṛtanāmadheyā to whom the name was given.
kṛtániścaya | niścaya | amnf kṛtaniścayā who made his decision; resolved | determined to (dat. loc. inf. iic. | assertive; certain. martavye kṛtaniścayaḥ resolved to die.
kṛtániścayin [niścayin] amnf kṛtaniścayinī who made his decision; resolved.
kṛtaprayatna | prayatna | amnf kṛtaprayatnā to whom efforts have been devoted.
kṛtabuddhi | buddhi | amnf resolved.
kṛtamada [mada] amnf kṛtamadā which excites passion — m. in rut (elephant).
kṛtamāla |mālā| m. bio. spotted antelope | bio. bot. Cassia fistula, tree with compound leaves, with pretty yellow flowers in hanging clusters, used in medicine; syn. aruja, āragvadha, jaṭharanud.
kṛtamauna | maunah | amnf kṛtamaunā who remains silent.
kṛtayuga [yuga] n. phil. 1st age of the world, golden age; syn. satyayuga; its king is Narasimha; only brāhmaṇās can practice asceticism |tapasya| there.

kṛtávarman [varman] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Krtavarmā "Protector of good", prince [kṣatriya] friend of Kṛṣṇa who went to war on the side of Duryodhana; he will be the only survivor of the Kauravās camp, with the brahmins Kṛpa and Aśvatthāmā; 36 years later, he fought with Yuyudhāna in the fratricidal drunken battle that ended the yādava line, fulfilling the curse of Gāndhārī; cf. Bhoja, Akrūra.
kṛtávīrya [vīrya] m. myth. np. of Prince Kṛtávīrya "the Vigorous", king of the Haihayās; for his education he gave a fortune to his guru, making the Bhārgavās rich; he is father of Kārtavīrya.
kṛtásaṃkalpa [saṃkalpa] amnf kṛtasaṃkalpā resolved.
kṛtasaṃketa |saṃketa| amnf kṛtasaṃketā having agreed; having agreed on a meeting. kṛtasaṃdhi var. kṛtasandhi [saṃdhi] amnf gram. where the sandhi has been performed. )4

kṛtākṛta |akṛta| amnf kṛtākṛtā done and not yet done; partly done | optional, indifferent — n. that which is done and that which remains to be done | phil. that which has been accomplished and that which has not yet been accomplished | phil. |Vedānta| the effect and the cause.
kṛtāñjali |añjali| amnf in añjali posture.
kṛtānurāga | anurāga | amnf kṛtānurāgā fell in love.
kṛtānta |anta| amnf kṛtāntā that ends, that concludes — m. phil. inevitable result of past actions; destiny | myth. epith. of Yama, death personified | conclusion; dogma.
kṛtāntasaṃtrāsa |saṃtrāsa| mr. bed. |KSS.| n.p. from rākṣasa Kṛtāntasaṃtrāsa “Terror of death”; cf. Mṛgāṅkavatī.
kṛtānná | anna | n. prepared food.
kṛtāpakṛta |apakṛta| amnf kṛtāpakṛtā done and done badly. kṛtāpakṛtam neither done nor to be done.
kṛtārtha | artha | amnf kṛtārthā who has achieved his goal; who has fulfilled his role; who has succeeded | effective; skillful.
kṛtāvajña |avajñā₂| amnf kṛtāvajñā despised.

kṛtāvadhāna [avadhāna] amnf kṛtāvadhānā absorbed; concentrated, attentive. kṛtāvadhānaṃ jitabarhiṇadhvanau surakta gopījanagītaniḥsvane | idam jighatsām apahāya bhūyasīm na sasyam abhyeti mṛgīkadambakam || Kir. A herd of deer, absorbed by the graceful songs of the cowherds, so much more pleasant than the cries of the peacocks, having forgotten their hunger, does not approach the crops.
kṛtāstra | astra | amnf kṛtāstrā skilled with the bow; skilled in the use of weapons.

kṛtaka |kṛtaka| amnf kṛtakā fabricated, artificial, fake; false, feigned | soc. unnatural, adopted. kṛtakakalahaṃ kṛtvā having feigned a quarrel. kṛtakam maunam feigned silence. kṛtakaṃ kopaṃ kṛtvā pretending to be angry.
kṛtakakopa | kopa | mr. feigned anger.
kṛtakatva [tva] n. artificiality; the act of simulating.
kṛtávat [ppa. kṛ₁] amnf kṛtavatī who did; having done || pkt. kitava. kim yūyam kṛtavantaḥ what have you done? sa tat krtavān he did that.

kṛti [act. kṛ₁] f. fabrication, composition; production; action, activity | creation, work; literary work; musical composition | phil. resolution, point of view | lit. devotional words addressed to Vishnu | magic | phon. Vedic meter of 2 lines of 12 syllables and one line of 8 syllables; also of 4 lines of 20 syllables | math. symb. the number twenty | math. square of a number | myth. |BhP.| np. of Kṛti "Ma gie", wife of Samhrāda, mother of Pancajana.
kṛtimat [mat] amnf kṛtimatī who creates.
Kṛtirāta [rāta] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of King Kṛtirāta Janaka "Given by magic", son of Pratīpaka, father of Mahāromā; [Rām.] also called Kīrtirāta.

kṛtin [agt. kṛ₁] amnf kṛtinī who acts; active | expert, skillful, gifted, learned (in (loc. iic.)) virtuous, pure, pious; obedient | who has accomplished a goal or obtained an object; satisfied — m. myth. np. of Kṛtī "Accomplished", son of Cyavana, father of Uparicara Vasu₂.
kṛtta [pp. kṛt₁] amnf kṛttā cut, re severed. akṛttanābhi whose umbilical cord has not been cut.
kṛtti [act. kṛt₁] f. action of cutting, splitting, slicing, dismembering — obj. f. bark; birch bark; bark garment | skin; animal skin; antelope skin | lat. cortex.

kṛttika [ka] amnf kṛttikā cutting — f. kṛttikā pl. myth. np. of the Kṛttikās "the Cutting Ones" or group of the 6 Pleiades; they form with Arundhatī the wives of the 7 sages [saptarsi]; Agni appeared to each in the guise of her husband to abuse them; only Arundhatī detected the deception and remained faithful, avoiding her banishment from the Great Bear; they were the nurses of KārttikeyaSkanda and were then fixed in Heaven as

constellation [nakṣatra]; they are sterile by a curse of Dakṣa | astr. first lunar asterism [nakṣatra] symbolizing them cosmically, corr. to the 6 stars of the Pleiades, and whose symbol is a knife; Agni presides over it || gr. o ; fr. critique ; ang. critic.
kṛttivāsas [vāsas] amnf clothed in skin — m. myth. np. of Kṛttivāsā, epith. of Siva "clothed in a tiger skin".
kṛtnú |agt. kṛt₁| amnf active; capable, ha bile, who has the know-how — m. skilled craftsman, good worker.

kṛtya [pfp. [1] kṛ₁] amnf kṛtyā to be done, to be accomplished; just, fitting — n. matter, occupation, work; interest; task, duty, responsibility; the good (opp. akṛtya evil) | effect, result; motive, purpose, design, object | that which concerns (g.) (about (i.)) — m. gram. suffix of the pfp. (tavya, anīya, ya) — f. kṛtyā action, accomplishment. kṛtyapratyayānta gram. form of the pfp.
Krtyakalpataru [Kalpataru₁] m. lit. np. of the Krtyakalpataru, a manual of jurisprudence due to Lakṣmīdhara (12th century); also called Kalpataru₁.
kṛtyavat |vat| amnf kṛtyavatī who has something to do, busy.

kṛtríma [kṛ₁trima] amnf kṛtrimā artificial, fake, false, falsified; accessory | adoptive (in child) — m. soc. adopted son | phil. |advaita| image, effigy, representation — n. cf. vida. saṃskṛtaṃ kṛtrime lakṣaṇopete |Amarakoṣa| Sanskrit is marked with the sign of the artificial.
kṛtrímatā |tā| f. cunning; sagacity.
kṛtrímatva |tva| n. artificiality; falsehood.
kṛtvas [kṛ₁] ifc. adv. (iic.) times. daśakrtvas 10 times. bahukrtvas many times.
krtvā [abs. krt₁] ind. having done. iti kṛtvā adv. therefore, this being; this done.
kṛtsa n. water | totality; multitude.
kṛtsná amnf kṛtsnā complete, whole; overall; all — n. totality. kṛtsnena adv. partially; opp. ekadeśena.
kṛtsnakāraka | kāraka | amnf kṛtsnakārakā that anyone is capable of doing.
kṛtsnátā |tā| f. totality; completeness.
kṛtsnátva |tva| n. id.
kṛtsnávat [vat] amnf kṛtsnavatī similar to the whole.
kṛtsnávid |vid₃| amnf omniscient.
kṛntatra |instr. kṛt₁| n. plow.
kṛntana [act. kṛt₁] n. act of cutting, dividing.
√ krp v. [1] pr. r. (krpate) ved. to complain, to lie to oneself; to be in pain — ca. (kṛpáyati) to pity, to have pity on | lat. crepo.

kṛpa [agt. kṛp] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of kṛpa "Mercy", descended from the sage Śaradvān; he was found with his sister in a clump of reeds [śarastamba] by King Sāmtanu who took them in out of compassion [kṛpā]; later he was part of the council of Has tināpura, and as an expert archer was master-at-arms of the Kauravās; also called Kṛpācārya; he is one of the 7 immortals [ciramjīvin] | myth. [Mah.] np. of the Brahmin kṛpa Gautama, father of Saradvān (and thus grandfather of the former) — f. Kṛpī myth. np. of Kṛpī "compassion", twin of kṛpa; she married Drona, from whom she conceived Aśvatthāmā.

kṛpaṇá [agt. kṛp] amnf kṛpaṇā unhappy, miserable; poor, weak, lamentable avaricious, stingy — m. miserly — act. n. kṛpáṇa misery; misfortune — v. [11] pr. r. (kṛpaṇāyate) to lament. krpanam adv. in a lamentable way. sa mahātmā vayam kṛpaṇāḥ [PT.] He is a lord and we are poor.
kṛpā [act. kṛp] f. compassion, pity, tenderness. kṛpayā adr. ["out of pity"] please. guru kṛpā hi kevalam The master is nothing but compassion.
kṛpāṇa [kṛpā] m. ["that which delivers the final blow"] sword | sacrificial dagger — f. kṛpāṇī scissors; dagger, knife.
kṛmi [kram] m. insect; worm, vermin, maggot; spider, louse; silkworm; ant | carmine (produced by the cochineal insect) | lat. vermi; fr. vermine.
kṛmija [ja] amnf kṛmijā produced by an in sect; not. silk — f. kṛmijā carmine dye (produced by cochineal) | gr. ; lat. carmine; fr. carmine; eng. crimson; Arabic qirmiz.
kṛmiparisṛpta | parisṛpta | amnf kṛmiparisṛptā covered in swarming vermin.
krmimat [mat] amnf krmimatī infested with worm mine; teeming with maggots.
√ কুষ্ kṛś v. [4] pr. (kṛśyáti) pft. (cakárśa) pp. (kṛśitá) to lose weight, to weaken | astr. wane (moon) — ca. (karśáyati) to make thin, to waste away | lat. graciles; fr. gracile.
kṛśá |agt. kṛś| amnf kṛśā thin, lean, emaciated; weak, puny; small, insignificant; haggard. kṛśīkṛ to make thin. kṛśībhū to lose weight.
kṛśatā [tā] f. thinness, gauntness.
kṛśatva [tva] n. id.
kṛśāṅga |aṅga₁| amnf kṛśāṅgī thin, slender; lean, emaciated.

Kṛśāśva [aśva] amnf kṛṣ́āśvā who has thin hair — m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the progenitor [prajāpati] Kṛśāśva; he married Jayā and Suprabhā, of whom he had 50 sons by each; each of them was a weapon of great power; Viśvāmitra acquired these weapons by his penances, and transmitted them to Rāma and Lakşmana.
kṛśodara | udara | amnf kṛśodarā who has a slim waist.
kṛśaka [agt. kṛś] amnf kṛśikā thin, slender — f. organic kṛśikā. bot. Salvinia cucculata, water lilt.

kṛśānu m. Fire of the lightning; myth. a name of Agni the Fire | myth. np. of kṛśānu "He who draws the bow", centaur | gandharva | sagittarius Who shot with the bow against the falcon | śyena | into which Indra had transformed himself, to try to prevent him from giving the divine soma to Manu the Man; he is armed with the lightning |vidyut₂|.
kṛśānuretas | retas | m. myth. np. of kṛśānuretas, epith. of Shiva "with the semen of Fire".

(anu, apa, ava, ā, ut, upa, ni, nis, pari, Pra, vi, sam) drag, train, pull — v. [6] pr. (kṛṣáti) pr. r. (kṛṣate) to plow — ca. (kaṛṣayati) to extract, to tear off; torment; torture.
kṛṣa [agt. kṛṣ] m. plow. কৃষক kṛṣaka [agt. kṛṣ] amnf kṛṣikā Who plows, Who cultivates — m. plowman; farmer, cultivator | plow; ox — act. f. kṛṣikā plowing, cultivation.
kṛṣi [act. kṛṣ] f. agriculture, plowing | var. kṛṣī field.
kṛṣiparāśara | parāśara | m. lit. du np. kṛṣiparāśara, manual of agriculture attributed to parāśara; also called Kṛṣisaṃgraha, to Krşipaddhati and Krşitantra.
kṛṣībala |bala| m. ploughman, peasant | var. kṛṣīvala id. ক্ষ kṛṣṭa |pp. kṛṣ| amnf kṛṣṭā dragged, pulled, drawn (by (iic.)); uprooted | ploughed, cultivated (land) — mn arable land.
kṛṣṭaja |ja| amnf kṛṣṭajā cultivated (plant).

kṛṣṭapacya | pacya | amnf kṛṣṭapacyā cultivated (plant). কৃষ্টি kṛṣṭi [act. kṛṣ] f. plowing, cultivation; cultivated land; harvest | settlement | pl. the people; people, race, humanity. páñca kṛṣṭáyas myth. the 5 tribes of the descendants of Yayāti | humanity.

kṛṣṇá [kṛ₁sna] amnf kṛṣṇā Black, blue Black — m. black color | bio. black antelope | myth. np. of Kṛṣṇa₁ "the Black", multiform deity; in the Vedic period, asura representing the Dravidian peoples, he is black in color; 9th avatar of Viṣṇu, he was born in Mathurā to Prince Vasudeva of the Yādava lineage and Devakī; Mah. Devakī's cousin, the cruel Kaṃsa king of Mathurā, knowing that one of her sons would kill him, had his first 6 children killed; on the 7th, Balarāma escaped, and on the 8th, Kṛṣṇa₁, was secretly raised by the king of the shepherds Nanda and his wife Yaśodā; [BhP.] a mischievous baby, he drank Yaśodā's butter and was of Herculean strength; as a child, he defeated the demons Tṛṇāvarta, Agha, Ariṣṭa, Kāliya, Keśī, Baka and Sakaṭa; he saved the village of Govardhana from the flood caused by Indra by raising his hill above his head; he courted thousands of herdswomen |gopī| of Vṛndāvana, among whom his favorites were Rādhā and Rukminī; As a teenager, he dethroned and killed the cruel King Kamsa; his teacher was the wise Sāndīpani; having become king of Dvārakā, he married Rukmiņī, taking her from the evil Siśupāla; he is the father of Pra dyumna; he fought Jāmbavān, from whom he took the jewel Syamantaka; he married Jāmbavatī, who conceived Sāmba by him; he married Satyabhāmā, with whom he had 10 sons, and who helped him defeat the asura Naraka and his ally Mura; he gave his sister Subhadrā in marriage to Arjuna; [Mah.] he participated with Arjuna in the writing of the Mahābhārata alongside the Pāndavās; At the beginning of the battle, as Arjuna's charioteer, he exhorted him to fulfill his duty [karmayoga] by revealing his divine nature to him in the Bhagavadgītā; but he did not take part in the war himself, ensuring the fairness of the fight by his neutrality; at the death of his brother Balarāma, the last survivor of the yādavās, he was meditating on the sadness of existence, when he was killed by the arrow of the hunter Jarā₂ Who had mistaken him for a deer, and Who struck him in the heel, the only vulnerable place on his body; from this wound sprang a śālagrāma at his death; his birthday is celebrated at the janmāṣṭamī festival; cf. Acyuta, Adhokṣaja, Arisūdana, Giridhara, Gopa, Gopāla, Gopīnātha, Gopendra, Govinda, Jagannātha, Pārthasārathi, Madhudvit, Madhusūdana, Mādhava, Mitravindā, Murāri, Vāsudeva, Viṭṭhala, Hṛṣīkeśa, vṛṣṇi | of. kṛṣṇau myth. Kṛṣṇa₁ and Arjuna, representing God and Man together | epith. of Vyāsa/Dvaipāyana₁ hist. n.p. of King Raṣṭrakūṭa Krishna₁ (8th century); he succeeded his father Dantidurga upon his death in 756 and had the Kailāsa₁ temple built, carved into the rock at Ellora; Govinda₂ succeeded him in 774 | hist. np. of King Raṣṭrakūṭa Krishna₁ (9th century); he succeeded Amoghavarsa₁ in 878; Indra₃ succeeded him in 914 hist. np. of King Raṛṣṇa Krishna₁ (10th century); he succeeded his father Amoghavarsa₃ upon his death in 939; he invaded the Cola country in 949, and conquered Kāncī and Tanjavūr; his half-brother Khoṭṭiga )7 succeeded him in 967; he encouraged the culture of Sanskrit hist. np. of the pandita Kṛṣṇa Śeṣa₂, grammarian and poet of the 16th century | hist. np. of Kṛṣṇa Dai vajña, astronomer of the 17th century | hist. np. of śrī Bhāratī Kṛṣṇa Tīrthajī Mahārāja, śamkarācārya of the mațha of Govardhana₃ in Purī (1884–1960); He is the author of a method of mental calculation called "Vedic mathematics" — n. darkness; black heart — m. black pepper; iron; black antelope; black spots of the moon, etc. — f. Kṛṣṇā₁ myth. np. of Kṛṣṇā₁, epith. of Draupadī "dark-skinned" | myth. one of the 7 languages of Agni [saptajihva] | geo. np. of the river Kṛṣṇā₁, which crosses the country of Andhra — f. kṛṣṇī night — v. [11] pr. r. (kṛṣṇāyate) to blacken — v. [11] pr. (kṛṣṇayati) to act like Kṛṣṇa. kṛṣṇastu bhagavān svayam [BhP.] Kṛṣṇa is God in person.
Kṛṣṇakarṇāmṛta [karṇaamṛta] n. lit. np. Krsnakarnāmrta, a set of verses

Devotionals [bhakti] of worship to Krishna due to Līlāśuka. Krishnakānta hist. np. of the logician Krishnakānta Vidyāvāgiśa (18th-19th century); we owe to him the Krishnakāntīṭīkā, commentary on the Sabdaśaktiprakāśikā.
kṛṣṇagītā [gītā] f. lit. text where Kṛṣṇa teaches Ar juna; refers especially to the triad Bhagavadgītā, Anugītā and Uttaragītā.
kṛṣṇajanmāṣṭamī | janmāṣṭamī | f. soc. day anniversary of Kṛṣṇa; 8th day of the dark fortnight of the month śrāvaṇa₂.
kṛṣṇatama [tama] amnf kṛṣṇatamā super. the blackest.
kṛṣṇatara [tara] amnf kṛṣṇatarā compar. blacker.
kṛṣṇatā [tā] f. blackness | astr. waning phase of the moon.
kṛṣṇatva [tva] n. blackness | myth. the nature of Kṛṣṇa.
kṛṣṇadāsa [dāsa] m. hist. n.p. by the author ben gali kṛṣṇadāsa, author of the Caitanyacaritāmṛta (16th century).

kṛṣṇadeva [deva] m. hist. np. of the emperor kṛṣṇadeva Rāya, who reigned over Vijayanagara from 1509 to 1529, succeeding his elder brother Vīra₁ Narasimha₆; his reign is the apogee of this Karṇāṭa empire; he defeated the Sultan of Bahmani at Bīdar, and reinstated him as a vassal, giving himself the title of Establisher of the King of the Muslims; he allied himself with the Portuguese against the Sultan of Vijaya pura (Bijapur); he defeated the Sultan of Golconda, and took Telangāna from the Gajapati kings; he took the citadel of Udayagiri in 1513 after an 18-month siege; He took the fort of Rāyacūru (modern Raichur, Karnataka), conquered its doab in 1520, and razed the fortress of Gulburga; it is said that every morning after his massage, he practiced weightlifting, swordsmanship, and wrestling, then rode his horse before taking his bath; he encouraged the arts at his court, notably Sanskrit, Kannada, and Telugu literature; he notably patronized a court of 8 poets |astadiggaja|; Vyāsatīrtha was his rājaguru; he had the titles of Kāvyanāṭakamarmajña "Expert in poetry and dramatic art", Kavitāprāvīnyaphanīśa "Patañjali of poetic virtuosity", and Sakalakalābhoja "Expert in all the arts like King Bhoja₁"; He composed the drama Jāmbavatīpariņaya in Sanskrit and the poem Amuktamālyada in Telugu; he donated the village of Mattur to a Vedic community, which has kept Sanskrit as its vernacular language to this day; he built a new go pura at the temple of Virūpākṣa; in 1513 he erected the temple of Kṛṣṇasvāmī, to serve as a shrine to the image of Bālakṛṣṇa which he had brought back from Udaya giri; in 1516 he built the Rājagopura of the temple śrī Kālahastīśvara; his brother Acyutadeva Rāya succeeded him.
kṛṣṇapakṣa [pakṣa] m. astr. "dark fortnight", period (unfavorable) between a full moon [pūrnimā] and a new moon [amāvāsyā]; opp. śuklapaksa.
kṛṣṇapratipad [pratipad₂] astr. day [tithi] following a full moon.
kṛṣṇamaṭha [maṭha] mn geo. n.p. of the Kṛṣṇamaṭha or Śrīkṛṣṇamaṭha temple, founded by Madhva in Udupī, in Karņāṭaka.
kṛṣṇamitrācārya [mitraācārya] m. hist. np. of the philosopher kṛṣṇamitrācārya (early 19th century); cf. Durbalācārya.
kṛṣṇamiśra [miśra] m. hist. n.p. of the ascetic [yati₂] kṛṣṇamiśra, author of the allegorical drama Prabod hacandrodaya (11th century).
kṛṣṇayajurveda [yajurveda] m. bed. n.p. black kṛṣṇayajurveda or yajurveda; opp. Suklayajurveda; cf. Taittirīya, Kāthaka.

Kṛṣṇarāja₁ [rāja] m. hist. np. of King Kṛṣṇarāja₁ Ka lacuri of Māhiṣmatī; he reigned around (550–575) | hist. np. of King Krsnarāja₁ Wodeyar III, Mahārāja of Mysore (1794–1868); he was a scholar and patron of the arts; he commissioned the Śrītattvanidhi.
kṛṣṇarāma | rāma | mr. of. kṛṣṇarāmau myth. Kṛṣṇa and rāma.
kṛṣṇalīlā [līlā] f. myth. erotic play or frolic of Kṛṣṇa.
kṛṣṇalīlāśuka [śuka] m. lit. np. of the poet kṛṣṇalīlāśuka "Kṛṣṇa's Play Parrot"; he lived in Kerala in the 13th century, and composed the Durgāstuti.
kṛṣṇavartman [vartman] m. fire [“that blackens its passage”].
kṛṣṇaśakuni |śakuni| m. crow.
kṛṣṇasarpa [sarpa] m. organic. ["black snake"] zoo. Coluber Naga, very venomous cobra.
kṛṣṇasarpavat [vat] amnf kṛṣṇasarpavatī (venomous, deadly) like the cobra.

kṛṣṇasvāmin [svāmin] m. geo. np. of the temple of Kṛṣṇasvāmī at Vijayanagara; it was erected by Kṛṣṇadeva Rāya in 1513, to serve as a sanctuary for the image of Bālakṛṣṇa which he had brought back from Udayagiri.
kṛṣṇājiná [ajina] n. black antelope skin (which serves as clothing and seat for an ascetic) — amn covered with a black antelope skin.
kṛṣṇāyas |ayas| n. iron ; syn. śyāmāyas.

kṛṣṇāṣṭamī [aṣṭamī] f. myth. anniversary of Kṛṣṇa; cf. kṛṣṇajanmāṣṭamī | soc. 8th day of the dark fortnight of any month. কুষ্ণাল kṛṣṇala [Kṛṣṇala] n. black berry of the Abrus Precatorius used as a unit of weight, not. of gold.

√ klp v. [1] pr. r. (k 'alpate) pft. (caklpe) fut. r. (kalpsyáte) aor. [3] (acīkļpat) pp. (kļptá) pf. (kalpáyati) ca. r. (kalpayate) pp. (kalpita) to make; to arrange; to order, to appoint (to a function); to equip with (i.) | to consider (acc.) as (acc.) || ang. help; all. helfe. idam me istasiddhaye kalpeta this suits me. mātaram enām kalpayantu that they consider her as their mother.

ke [noun. pl. ka₁] ind. what?
kecana [cana] m. pl. some; a few.
kecit [cid₁] m. pl. id. kecit ... kecit ... some ..., others ...

Kekaya m. geo. name of the Kekaya country west of the Sutlej, and of its warrior people; mod. it corresponds to the districts of Jhelum, Shahpur and Gujrat in Punjab; cf. Aśvapati | pl. Kekayās its inhabitants, the Kekayās.
kekara amnf kekarī qui louche.
kekaralocana [locana] amnf kekaralocanā id.

kekaralohita [lohita] m. myth. [VAa.] np. of the nāga kekaralohita; he attacked the sage Cyavana bathing in the Narmadā at the ford [tīrtha] of Na kuleśvara; his poison did not attack the sage in meditation, who visited the Pātāla, found Prahlāda in his palace to describe to him all the sacred places of the World, and returned from there.
kekā [onomatopoeia] f. cry of the peacock.
kéta [agt. cit₁] amnf ketā who knows — act. m. desire, intention; will | dwelling, shelter; mark, form

ketaka [agt. cit₁] m. bio. bot. Pandanus odo ratissimus, pandanus tree; thorny plant with yellow leaves and fragrant flowers (on male plants) — f. ketakī the pandanus flower, with a sweet fragrance; myth. it is one of Kāma's [puṣpabāṇa] arrows, because it "stirs up trouble in the blood"; the ketakī is cursed by Šiva, because it was produced as a witness by Brahmā claiming to have seen his face, when he sought the top of the pillar of fire [tejolinga]; it is also said that Pārvatī disturbed Śiva's asceticism by adorning himself with ketakī, provoking his curse and banishment; hateful to Siva [śivadviṣṭā], one cannot offer it to him; In poetry, it symbolizes the pain of the
separation [viraha] from the loved one. mukhena sā ketakapattrapāṇḍunā |Ragh.| her wise vi was pale like the pandanus flower.
ketana [act. cit₁] n. seat, residence; mark, attribute; sign, standard, flag.

ketú [cit₁u] m. lamp; torch | splendor; mark, symbol; sign, flag, banner arch. emblem | astr. shooting star; comet | myth. np. of Ketu "Meteor", son of Rsabha, deity of the winter solstice, tail of the "descending dragon" Rāhu; he is nicknamed the bald one (Muṇḍa or Akeśa) pl. rays | ang. hood; all. heit.
ketumat [mat] amnf Ketumatī made of splendor — m. myth. n.p. of Ketumān "the Splendid", son of Dhanvantari, father of Bhīmaratha — f. Ketu matī geo. n.p. of Ketumatī "the Splendid", epith. of
Benares [Kāśi] | myth. [Rām.] np. of the gandharvī Ketumatī₁, daughter of Narmadā, wife of the rākṣasa Sumāli; she gave birth to Akampana and Kaikasī.
ketumāla | māla | m. | ketumālavarṣa | myth. one of the 9 watersheds [varşa] of the World, located in the West.

kedāra m. meadow, irrigated field; basin surrounded by dikes, rice paddy | [Kedāranātha] myth. np. of kedāra, epith. of Siva "Master of the rice paddies" | | kedārabhaṭṭa | hist. np. of the mathematician kedāra₁ Bhatta, prior to the 15th century; he founded binary combinatory in his work on prosody Vrttaratnākara.

Kedāranātha | nātha | m. geo. np. of Kedāranātha, an important pilgrimage site at 3583 altitude north of Uttarākhanda, in the Badarīnātha mountain range, accessible in summer by a 14 km mountain path from Gaurīkuṇḍa; one of the 12 radiant signs of Shiva | jyotirlinga| is venerated there; the Mandākinī₁ river originates nearby.
kéna [i. kim] adv. how? why?
kenāpi [api] adv. in a certain way. yena kenāpyupāyena in one way or another; at all costs.
kenopanisad [upanisad] f. bed. n.p. of the esoteric lesson [upaniṣad] Kena or kenopaniṣad (starting with Kena); this short text is part of the Talavakārabrāhmaņa of the Sāmaveda.
kenopaniṣadbhāṣya [bhāṣya] n. bed. n.p. of the Kenopanisadbhāsya, his commentary, attributed to Śańkara₁.
kendra n. center of a circle | gr. o ; ang. center; fr. centre.
kembuka n. cabbage | areca nut kernel.
keyūra mn bracelet (arm ornament, above the elbow).
Keyūraka [ka] m. lit. [K.] np. of the young gandharva Keyūraka "with the ruby bracelet", bearer of vīņā of Kādambarī.
keyūradharā [dharā] f. bed. n.p. of the apsaras keyūradharā "who wears an arm ornament".
keyūrin |in| amnf keyūrinī who wears a bra celet on her arm.
kerala n. geo. np. of the Kerala country on the Malabar coast; its capital is Anantasayana (Trivan drum) — m. its people; its king | pl. keralās its inhabitants — f. keralī woman of Kerala.
kelā [vn. keli] v. [11] pr. (kelāyati) to have fun.
keli mf amusement, pleasure; game, pastime; erotic frolic | disguise.
kevárta var. kaivarta m. fisherman.

kévala amnf kevalā f. kevalī alone, isolated; exclusive, proper; pure, unmixed; abstract | absolute, whole | selfish — m. ifc. a simple (iic.) — n. phil. doctrine of the unity of the Spirit. kevalam adv. only, solely, entirely, purely, completely, exclusively. na kevalam ... api adv. not only ... but also. na kevalam ... kintu id.
kevalanaiyāyika [naiyāyika] m. a simple logician (ignorant of other sciences).
kevalapramāṇa [pramāṇa] n. phil. main evidence of a cognition; opp. anupramāṇa. kevalavaiyākaraņa [vaiyākaraņa] m. a simple grammarian (ignorant of other sciences).
kevalavyatirekin [vyatirekin] amnf kevala vyatirekiņī phil. [Nyāya] refers to an inference [anumāna] that uses only proofs by contradiction.
kevalavyatirekiprakarana [prakarana] n. phil. [Nyāya] demonstration by negation; this method of proof is explained in the Tattvacintāmaņi.
kevalādin [ādin] amnf kevalādinī who eats all alone.
kevalādvaita | advaita | m. phil. nonduality according to Śańkara₁.
kevalānvayin [anvayin] amnf kevalānvayinī phil. [Nyāya] refers to an inference [anumāna] that uses only positive inferences. )()
kevalin |in| amnf kevalinī alone, isolated; exceptional — m. meditating ascetic.
kéśa m. hair, mane; head of hair — amnf Keśī ifc. who has hair (iic.). keśān dhṛ to let one's hair grow.
keśapakṣa | pakṣa | m. lock of hair from the temples.
keśapāśa | pāśa | m. hairstyle with knots in the hair.
keśavat |vat| amnf keśavatī poilu.
keśavāpana | vāpana₁ | n. the act of shaving the hair.
keśaśmaśrú |śmaśru| n. sg. (collective) facial pi system.
keśaśmaśrulomanakha [lomanakha] n. pl. hair and nails.

keśānta | anta | m. terminal line of hair on the front, fringe | long lock, braided hair, etc. | soc. rite [saṃskāra] of shaving the head and body hair; it is performed at 16 years [brāhmaṇa], 22 years [kṣatriya] or 24 years [vaiśya]; syn. godāna.
kéśara [keśara] m. cf. kesara.

keśarin [in] amnf keśarinī who has a mane — mf keśariṇī lion | myth. n.p. of the monkey Keśarī or Kesarī "mane", husband of Añjanā | hist. n.p. of the Keśarī₁ dynasty of kings of Kalinga; cf. Kesarī₁.

Keśava [keśava] m. myth. np. of Keśava, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "long-haired" or "For cleaver of the demon Keśī"; a temple in So manāthapura is dedicated to him | hist. np. of Keśava₁ Bhāratī, a māyāvādin; Caitanya became sannyāsin (took the habit [veṣa]) under his guidance | hist. np. of Keśava₂ Bhāratī, a poet challenged and humiliated by the young Caitanya in Māyāpura | hist. np. of the logician Keśava₃ Miśra (13th century); he is the author of the Tarkaparibhāṣā | hist. np. from the lexicographer Keśava₄ Miśra (17th century), author of the Kalpadrukośa. ākāśāt patitam toyam yathā gacchati sāgaram | sarvadevanamaskāraḥ keśavam pratigacchati || As the water that descends from the sky goes to the ocean, so prayers to all the gods return to Kṛṣṇa.

Keśavadāsa | dāsa | mr. hist. n.p. of Keśavadāsa "Servant of Kṛṣṇa", poet and grammarian of the 16th century, author of the first grammar of Hindī |Brajbhāṣā|, of the Rāmacandracandrikā, a treatise on Sanskrit metrics, and of the Rasikapriyā.
keśavadeva [deva] m. geo. np. of the great temple of keśavadeva, in Mathurā; it was destroyed by Aurang zeb in 1669.
keśavasvāmin |svāmin| mr. hist. n.p. of the lexicon Keśavasvāmī, whose patron was a 3( king Cola Rājarāja (12th century); he composed the Nānārthārnavasamskepa.
keśākeśi [red. keśa] adv. by grabbing each other's hair.
keśi iic. keśin.
keśiniṣūdana | niṣūdana | mr. myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa “who killed Keśī”.

Keśin [keśain] amnf Keśinī, hairy; bearing a mane — m. myth. np. from the dānava Keśī "mane"; during the war with the gods, he attempted to abduct the two celestial beauties Dai tyasenā and Devasenā; the former agreed to be his wife, but the latter cried for help and was saved by Indra, who gave her in marriage to Skanda; an asura Keśī, an ally of Kaṃsa, went to Gokula in the form of a horse to kill Kṛṣṇa, but was destroyed by the latter, who thus acquired the name Keśava — f. Keśinī, myth. np. from Keśinī "beautiful-haired", wife of Ajamīdha, mother of Jahnu | myth. np. of Keśinī₁, daughter of the king of Vidarbha, first wife of Sagara, mother of Asamañjā | myth. np. of Keśinī₂, epith. of the rākṣasī Kaikasī, wife of Viśravā, mother of Rāvaņa, Kumbhakarņa, Khara and Vibhīṣaṇa. tapoviśesapariśankitasya уā su kumārampraharaṇam mahendrasyapratyādeśaḥ rūpagarvitāyāḥ śriyaḥ alaṃkāraḥ Svar gasyasānah priyasakhyurvaśī kuberabha pratinivartamānāsamāpattidṛṣṭena vanāt keśinādānavenacitralekhādvitīyā ban

digrāhaṃgṛhītā [Kālidāsa] Our dear friend Urvaśī, the youthful weapon of Mahendra, he who is afraid of severe penances, who eclipses even Srī proud of his beauty, and who is an ornament of the heavens, was captured, with Citralekhā, by the demon Keśī who saw her by chance as she was returning from the house of Kubera.
kesara var. keśara [related to keśa] n. eyebrow; hair | fiber; stamen (not. of lotus) | bio. bot. Crocus sativus, saffron | yak tail (used as

fly whisk [cāmara]) — m. mane (horse, lion) | [nāgakesara] bio. bot. Mesua Ferrea, tree with reddish bark, very dense wood, and very fragrant white flowers with numerous stamens, giving red berries; it is used in pharmacopoeia — n. its flower | ang. hair; all. haar; lat. cae saries.
kesarāgra | agra | n. end of the mane.

kesarin [in] amnf kesarinī equipped with a mane — m. lion | myth. np. of the monkey Kesarī; cf. Keśarī )1 | hist. np. of the Kesarī₁ or Keśarī₁ dynasty "Lineage of the lion", which ruled the Kalinga from the 5th to the 12th century; its founder is Yayāti₁; it replaced the Ionian rulers | yavanās|, and Buddhism was abandoned for the worship of Shiva — f. kesarinī lioness || lat. caesar; all. Kaiser; ru. tsar.
kaikaya [*Kekaya] amnf kaikayī relating to the Kekayās | from the Kekaya country.
Kaikasī f. myth. np. of the rākṣasī Kaikasī, daughter of Sumāli and Ketumatī₁, wife of Viśravā, mother of Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Khara and Vibhīṣaṇa; cf. Keśinī₂.

kaikeya [kaikaya] m. prince of the Kekayās; said not. by Dhṛṣṭaketu | pl. geo. people of the Kaikeyās or Kekayās — n. language of the Kekayās — f. Kaikeyī myth. [Rām.] np. of Queen Kaikeyī, daughter of King Asvapati, favorite wife of Dasaratha, mother of Bharata₁; cf. Manthara.
kaitabha m. myth. n.p. of the asura Kaiṭabha; cf. Madhu₁.
kaitava [*kitava] amnf kaitavī deceiver, cheat — m. patr. of Ulūka (son of Sakuni the cheat) — n. stake; gambling; deception, trick — f. kaitavī deception, fraud.
kaimutika [*kimutaika] iic. relating to "com much more".
kaimutikanyāya [nyāya] m. a for tiori argument. kaimutikanyāyāt adv. a fortiori.
kaiyata m. hist. np. from the grammarian kaiyata (11th century), originally from Kaśmīra; he is the author of the commentary Pradīpa on the Mahābhāṣya, which is based on the gloss Mahābhāṣyadīpikā.

kailāsa m. geo. np. of Mount kailāsa, which rises to 6638 in the Himalayas, southwest of Tibet; myth. it is the abode of Shiva and Kubera, and is an important place of pilgrimage; it can be circled by a high mountain circuit of 52 km; no one has climbed Mount np. of the temple of kailāsa₁, excavated from the rock at Ellora during the reign of King Rāstrakūta Kṛṣṇa₁ (8th century).

Kailāsanātha₁ [nātha] m. myth. of np. Kailāsanātha₁, epithet of Shiva "Lord of the kailāsa" geo. np. of the Kailāsanātha₁, śaiva temple of Kāncīpura, built by King Narasimhavarmā₂. kailāsoddhāraņa [uddhāraṇa] n. lit. np. of the Kailāsoddhāraņa, myth. episode where Rāvaņa finds Mount kailāsa in his path and moves it; it is a classic of Kūdiyattam theatre in Kerala. 3(
kaivarta var. kevárta mf kaivartī fisherman.
kaivalya [*kevalaya] n. act of isolating oneself, detachment from all ties | singularity | phil. [yoga] state of bliss, liberation, salvation.
kaivalyapāda | pāda | m. phil. | yoga | np. of the Kaiva lyapāda, section of the Yogasūtra dealing with the Way of salvation.
kaivalyamukti [mukti] f. phil. eternal liberation (from rebirths); ultimate goal of rājayoga.
kaivalyāśrama [āśrama] m. hist. n.p. by Kai valyāśrama, kaula author.
kaiśora [*kiśora] n. adolescence (between 10 and 15 years old).
kaiśorya [ya] m. véd. patr.
ko [ka₁] pf. of appreciation or depreciation.
kóka [onomatopoeia] m. wolf | red goose; cuckoo; frog | lat. occa; fr. goose.
kokanada [nada] n. red lotus flower | myth. np. of kokanada, servant of Shiva | pl. geo. np. of the Kokanadava people.
Kokila [onomatopoeia] mf kokilā bio. zoo. Eudynamis Orientalis, Indian cuckoo; (poetry) its
cri [kuhū₂] awakens amorous desire; cf. anyapuṣṭa, anyabhṛta, syn. anyavāpa, parabhṛta.
kokilasandeśa [sandeśa] m. lit. np. from Kokila sandesa "Message of the cuckoo", love poem by Uddanda Sāstrī.

konkana m. geo. name of the country konkana (Western Dec, towards mod. Goa) | pl. konkanās geo. his people — f. konkanā woman from the konkana myth. n.p. of Konkanā, epith. of Renukā — f. konkanī language of konkana.

kojāgara [ka₁jāgara] mf kojāgarī soc. festival of the full moon [pūrnimā] of the month āśvina; various games are celebrated, notably dice games, to keep one awake, and Lakṣmī is celebrated, who is said to have appeared saying: Who is awake? [ko jāgarah], to promise wealth to those who keep watch; the moonlight is supposed to be beneficial on that night; a jar of milk is left to soak in it, at midnight the reflection of the moon on the milk is looked at before drinking it.
kotara n. tree hollow; cavity. viśvam tisthati kuksikotare The whole universe rests in the hollow of the matrix.
koți f. end, extremity, point; horn (of the moon); summit; excellence | ten million; multitude, immeasurable number | math. vertex of a tri-angle | hi. crore.
koṭijīvā [jīvā] f. math. cosine of an arc of a circle. koţijyā [jyā₃] f. cf. koţijīvā. )2
kotiphala | phala | n. astr. zenith of the Sun; opp. bāhuphala.
kotisas [sas] adv. by the millions, in innumerable quantities. koțiśo dhanyavādaḥ adr. a thousand thanks.
koṭika m. frog | ladybug — f. koṭikā ifc. the most despicable of (iic.). koțikāsya |āsya| m. myth. np. of Koțikāsya "Frog Head", son of a Suratha king.
koṭṭa m. strong | var. koṭa id.
koṭṭapāla [pāla] m. commander of a fort.
kona m. corner, angle | math. angle | point car dinal | math. symb. the number 4 | stick, rod; drumstick. trikonah triangle. konatah konam ["from one corner to another"] from this to that.

Koṇārka | arka | n. geo. np. of the temple of Koṇārka "Place of the Sun", on the shore 35 km east of Purī, built by King Narasimha₂ to honor Sūrya the Sun (circa 1250); the temple is in the form of a chariot of the Sun 30 high, with twelve pairs of enormous wheels, drawn by 7 stone horses; the śikhara was nearly 70 m; it bears statues of Sūrya and frames of green chlorite; the main sanctuary | devakula | is collapsed, only the jaganmohana remains; a dance pavilion | nāṭamaṇḍapa| precedes it to the East; between the two stood an aruṇastambha, which was moved to Purī.
koṇaspṛgvṛtta m. math. circumscribed circle.
koṇika [koṇaika] amnf koṇikā lateral.
Kondabhatta m. hist. np. from the grammarian Kondabhatta; cf. Kaundabhatta.
kodanda [kodanda] m. arc.
kodaṇḍāṭanī |aṭanī| f. notched end of a bow.
kodaṇḍin [in] amnf kodaṇḍiṇī armed with the bow — m. myth. epith. of Siva or Rāma.
kodrava [kodrava] n. bio. bot. Paspalum scrobiculatum, variety of millet | millet broth (eaten by the poor).
kopa [act. kup] m. anger; passion, rage, fury | med. hypochondria | incompatibility | phon. elision of visarga before a vowel. kopāt of anger; with anger.
kopākula [ākula] amnf kopākulā seized with anger; full of fury.
kopaka [agt. kup] amnf kopakā irascible | rebellious, inciting to revolt. 3(
kopana [agt. kup] amnf kopanā irascible; angry, furious | irritating — act. n. med. hypochondria, irritation of the humors.
kopākopi [red. kopa] adv. angry mu tuellement.
kopita [pp. ca. kup] amnf kopitā enraged, furious.
kopin [agt. kup] amnf kopinī who gets irritated, irascible, choleric.
komala amnf komalā tender, sweet; pleasant, agreeable, charming; pretty.
komalānga [anga₁] m. with a charming body.
koraka mn bud; flower bud.
kola [agt. kul] m. pork, boar, wild boar; syn. kroda — n. jujube — mn weight of a tola (1/2) karşa, approximately 4 g) | black pepper — f. organic kolā. bot. Ziziphus mauritiana, jujube tree.
kolabrūka m. hist. n.p. by Henry Thomas Colebrooke (1765–1837), pioneer of Sanskrit philology.

kolāhala [onomatopoeia] mn growl, roar; buzzing (bees); confused noise, tumult, uproar, din — m. myth. np. of Mount Kolāhala "Tumultuous" in Ma gadha; seized by desire for the Suktimatī River, he diverted it; upon his disappearance, the inhabitants complained to King Uparicara Vasu₂, who gave the mountain such a kick that it split it in two, freeing the river, and two children born of their union; the son became commander of Uparicara's army, who married the daughter Girikā as queen — f. kolāhalā mus. name of a mode [rāga]. kolāhale kākakulasya jāte virājate kokilakūjitam kim | parasparam samvadatām khalānām maunam vidheyam satatam sudhībhih || When a gathering of crows creates a din, what good would it do the cuckoo to answer them with cooing? Thus, in situations of bad disputes, the wise person is always well advised to remain silent.
kovida [kovida] amnf kovidā experienced, competent, skillful | who knows well, expert in, adept at (g. loc. iic.) — ifc. soc. title of beginner scholar in (iic.). jyotisakovida beginner in astronomy.

kóśa m. case, sheath, purse; vase, receptacle, box, container; shell | bud, flower bud; cocoon, notably of a silkworm; membrane, scrotum | treasure; lexicon | phil. [Vedānta] one of the five sheaths of the soul, which are: annamayakośa the material sheath )3 | "that which feeds" | and prāṇamayakośa the sheath of vital breaths, forming the gross body

sier [sthūlaśarīra]; manomayakośa the thought envelope and vijñānamayakośa the discernment envelope, forming the subtle or intellectual body [sūkṣmaśarīra]; and finally ānandamayakośa, the spiritual or ecstatic envelope forming the cau sal or original body [kāraṇaśarīra] | var. koṣa id.
kośaka [ka] m. testicle.
kośakāvya [kāvya] n. lit. anthology of poetry.

Kośadāsa [dāsa] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Kośadāsa, son of the rich caravanner Arthadāsa; he was in love with Candrasenā, captive of Bhīmadhanvā; he met Mitragupta who became his friend and helped them to be reunited.
kóśastha [stha] m. bio. shelled animal: conch, snail, etc. | chrysalis, cocoon.
kośāmra [āmra] m. bio. bot. Mangifera sylvatica, Himalayan mango — n. its fruit, the Nepal mango, used in medicine.
Kośāvatamsa [avatamsa] n. bed. from np. Kośāvataṃsa, dictionary due to Rāghava Kavi (early 19th century).
kośala m. cf. Kosala.

koşa cf. kośa. koşakalpadruma [kalpadruma] m. lit. np. from the Koṣakalpadruma, dictionary by Viśvanātha₃. কাষ্ট kostha [related to kośa] m. stomach, belly; viscera (heart, lung, liver, etc.) | inner apartment — n. attic, store; cassette, chest, treasure; ca raptor | enclosure wall; enclosure, inner courtyard; central part of a dwelling | frame; square (not. of chessboard).
kosthaka |ka| mn receptacle; granary, maga sin | enclosure wall; enclosure, inner courtyard — f. kosthikā pot.
koṣṭhikāyantra [yantra] n. (alchemy) horned.

Kosala m. geo. np. of Kosala, country of North India on the banks of the Sarayū, having as its capital Ayodhyā (mod. Oudh); its capital became Srāvastī during the Buddhist period of King Srāvasta; in the 4th century BC it was absorbed by the neighboring Ma gadha | myth. kingdom of the solar dynasty [sūryavaṃśa] of Daśaratha and Rāma — f. kosalī its language, a dialect of Hindi.
kaukkuṭika [*kukkuṭaika] m. [“who keeps their eyes lowered in the limited space of a hen's flight”] is said of a mendicant monk or a hypocrite. 3(
kaukṣeya [*kukṣieya] amnf kaukṣeyī which is in the belly — m. ["in the scabbard"] sword.
kaukseyaka [ka] m. sword; scimitar; dagger.
kaunkuma [*kunkuma] amnf kaunkumā with a saffron complexion.
kaucumāra [*Kucumāra] amnf kau cumārā relating to Kucumāra.
kaucumārayoga [yoga] m. erotic magic of yoga according to Kucumāra; the art of disguise, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.
kauta [*kūṭa] amnf kauṭā dishonest, fraudulent | self-employed — n. fraud, deception; lie.
kautalya m. cf. Kautilya.
kautilika [*kutilikā] m. (path) full of detours.
kauṭilīya [*kuṭilaīya] amnf kauṭilīyā relating to Cāṇakya; qualifies not. his Arthaśāstra.

Kautilya [*Kutilaya] amnf kautilyā who is of the lineage [gotra] of Kutila — m. hist. np. of Kautilya Cāṇakya, brahmin born in Kāñcī (?313–289 ant.); he helped Candragupta Maurya to overthrow the Nanda dynasty and was his minister in Pāṭaliputra; he is the author of the treatise on political economy Arthaśāstra; the Cāṇakyanīti is attributed to him; this theorist of pragmatism, a fine diplomat, is compared to Machiavelli — amn (by extension) devious, Machiavellian — n. twist, curvature; the state of being curly (hair) | cynicism, Machiavellianism.
kautilyaśāstra [śāstra] n. diplomacy; politics.
kauṭumba [*kuṭumba] amnf kauṭumbā relating to the family — n. family relationship.
Kauṭhāra [*kuṭhāra] m. geo. np. of the principality of Kauthāra of the Hinduized kingdom of Campā₁ in South Vietnam.
kauṇḍa [*kuṇḍa] amnf kauṇḍā relating to pot — m. hist. n.p. of Kauṇḍa Bhaṭṭa; cf. Kaundabhatta.

Kaundabhatta [bhatta] m. hist. np. of Kaundabhatta, grammarian of the 17th century, nephew of Bhattoji Dīkṣita; he is the author of the treatise on the philosophy of language Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇa, and of its summary the Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra.
kauṇḍinya [*Kuṇḍina₁ya] amnf kaundinyā originating from Kundina₁ — m. hist. np. of kaundinya "originating from Kundina₁", author of the Pañcārthabhāsya (4th-5th century).

kautuka [*kutuka] n. curiosity; impatience, desire (for (iic. loc.)) | curious object, marvel )4 | entertainment, amusement; sport, spectacle; pleasure, happiness | soc. festival, Festival; not. wedding bracelet ceremony | cotton ribbon, dyed red and yellow, used in rituals. kautukāt adv. out of curiosity; impatiently, ardently.
kautukaratnākara | ratnākara | mr. bed. n.p. from the Kau tukaratnākara "Mine of amusements", satirical work by Laksmana Mānikyadeva of Bhuluya (16th century).
kautukasūtra |sūtra| n. soc. yellow woolen cord tied by her mother to the bride's wrist before the wedding.
kautūhala [*kutūhala] n. curiosity | interest in, violent desire for (loc. pratiacc. inf.) curious spectacle.

Kautsa [*kutsa] m. lit. [Ragh.] np. of the brah mane Kautsa; at the end of his studies, he wanted to give his salary [dakṣiṇā] to his guru Varatantu; the latter initially told him that his successful completion of the studies was his reward, but at Kautsa's insistence asked him for 140 million gold coins (one koți for each of the 14 sciences taught); Kautsa went to see King Raghu, who asked Indra for the gold, who ordered Kubera to rain the gold coins down on Ayodhyā | hist. patr. of Kautsa₁, ancient skeptical philosopher; cf. anarthaka.
kauthuma [*kuthumina] m. patr. of the descendants of Kuthumī | pl. vedic school of Kuthumī; not. Samaveda school of chanting.
Kauthumaka [ka] n. bed. n.p. of Kauthumaka, brāhmana of the school of Kuthumī.
kauddālika [*kuddālaika] amnf kauddālikā who uses a hoe.
kaunteya [*kuntīeya] m. myth. [Mah.] “son of Kuntī”, matr. of Yudhiṣṭhira, of Bhīma, or of Arjuna.
kaunda [*kunda] amnf kaundī relating to jasmine.
kaupa [*kūpa] amnf kaupī coming from a well or cistern — n. well water.
kaupīna [*kūpaīna] n. ["worthy of being thrown into the well"] fault, sin | genitals | piece of cloth to cover them.

Kaumāra [*kumāra] amnf kaumārī juvenile, virginal | myth. relating to Skanda — n. childhood; youth, adolescence; virginity | lit. np. of Kaumāra, epith. of the Kātantra "Inspired by kumāra" — f. kaumārī myth. np. of kaumārī, śakti of Skanda, saptamātṛkā symbolizing youthful energy.
kaumārabhrtya [bhrtya] n. med. pediatrics, one of the 8 subdivisions [aṣṭānga] of Ayurveda.
kaumāralāta [lāta] m. gram. np. from kaumāralāta "received by Skanda", ancient grammatical text precursor of the Kātantra.
kaumārahara [hara] m. who takes virginity.
kaumuda [*kumuda] m. the "joyful" month kārttika — f. cf. kaumudī.
kaumudika [*kumudaika] amnf Kau mudikā rich in lotus — f. kaumudikā np. of woman.

kaumudī [f. kaumuda] f. moonlight | lit. "clarification" (not. from Pāṇini's grammar); not. the Siddhāntakaumudī or kaumudī of Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita (17th century) and its abridged version Laghukau mudī of his disciple Varadarāja₁, which give a simplified grammatical system for beginners; see also Tarkakaumudī.
kaumudīmahotsava [mahotsava] m. bed. n.p. from the kaumudīmahotsava "Joyful Festival", play by Princess Vijayabhaṭṭārikā (7th century).
Kaumodakī [*kumudaka] f. myth. np. of Kaumodakī "who brings joy to the Earth", club
scepter [gadā] of Viṣṇu, given by Varuṇa; cf. Gadādevī.

kaurava [*kurua] amnf kauravā myth. descendant of kuru | pl. kauravās myth. [Mah.] the kauravās, royal family of the descendants of kuru; this designates in particular the descendants of King Sāmtanu: the eldest Bhīṣma, his half-brothers Citrāngada and Vicitravīrya, who died without descendants, then the children of the widows of Vicitravīrya by the ascetic Vyāsa: Dhṛtarāṣṭra the blind and Pāṇḍu who reigned before renouncing the crown, which was taken up by Duryodhana, eldest son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; In the ensuing fratricidal war, the kauravās referred to the men of Duryodhana's clan, as opposed to that of his cousins, the Pāṇḍavās.

Kauravya [*kuruya] amnf kauravyā myth. descendant of kuru; patr. of kings of the lunar lineage, and not. of Śāmtanu and his lineage; syn. kaurava | myth. [Mah.] np. of the nāga king Kauravya, of the lineage of Airāvata; he is the father of Ulūpī.
kaurma [*Kūrma] amnf kaurmā relating to the tortoise or the avatar Kūrma.
kaurmapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. cf. kūrmapurāṇa.

kaula [*kula] amnf kaulī familial; which concerns the family — m. phil. [Tantra] worshipper of )5 SaktiBhairava and the fierce powers | yoginī| following the "left-hand" ritual, having as its ideal the virile hero [vīra] — n. this ritual; cf. kulācāra.
kaulajñāna [jñāna] n. phil. ["clan gnosis"] doc trine kaula associated with tantric rites.
kaulajñānanirnaya [nirnaya] m. bed. n.p. from the Kau lajñānanirṇaya “Exposition of the kaula doctrine”, by Matsyendranātha (10th century); it served as the basis for the yoginīkaulamata doctrine.
kaularahasya | rahasya | n. bed. n.p. of the Kaularaha sya, presentation of the esoteric kaula doctrine.
kaulācāra [ācāra] m. soc. [Tantra] correct behavior of a kaula devotee.
kaulava var. kaulaba n. astr. third half lunar day [karaṇa] (mobile).
kaulālá [*kulāla] n. pottery.
kaulālacakra [cakra] n. potter's wheel.
kaulālaka [*kulālaaka] n. pottery.
kaulika [*kulaika] m. weaver | phil. [Tantra] adept of kulācāra; syn. kaula — f. Kau likī phil. [Tantrāloka] supreme energy of the non

manifested [akula], capable of unfolding the totality [kula]; [Jayaratha] these two inseparable aspects emanate from the unsurpassed light [anuttara] of Ultimate Reality which freely decides to manifest itself in Shiva and Shakti; its experience is instantaneous
tanée | sadyah|.
kaulikasiddhi [siddhi] f. phil. [Trika] power of totality; syn. kaulikī.
kaulīka [kaulika] m. organic. bayā, passerine tis serand; cf. pītamuṇḍa.

klība var. klīva m. transvestite; homosexual (not sif) | eunuch — impotent amn; castrated | effeminate; timid; weak; coward | (cloud) not bearing rain | gram. (noun) of neuter gender — n. [klībaliṅga] gram. neuter gender — v. [11] pr. r. (klībāyate) to be a coward — v. [1] pr. r. (klībate) to behave like a eunuch.

kled [ca. klid] v. [10] pr. (kledayati) pp. (kle dita) to moisten, to wet; spoil.
kleda [act. klid] m. moisture | seepage; pu runence; putrefaction.

kledya [pfp. [1] klid] amnf kledyā to water.
kleśa [act. kliś] m. torment, difficulty; suffering, affliction; passion | phil. factor of affliction; vice; |Yoga| The 5 afflictions are: ignorance
rance |avidyā|, selfishness |asmitā|, attachment [rāga], aversion [dveṣa] and existential anxiety [abhiniveśa] | bd. defilement; mental affliction.
kleśin [agt. kliś] amnf kleśinī which causes torment, which makes one suffer.
