kloman mn med. right lung | pl. klomānas lungs || lat. pulmo. kva adv. where? in what place? in what state? to what degree?

kvaca | ca | part. (after negation) nowhere; but. yatra kvaca anywhere; anytime. kvaca ... kvaca ... one must choose between ... and ... kva ... kvaca ... what is the relationship between ... and ...? kva tapaḥ kvaca ruditam One cannot be an ascetic and weep.
kvacana | cana | adv. somewhere; anywhere; in any case; sometimes. yatra kvacana anywhere; anytime.

kvacit [cid₁] adv. somewhere; anywhere; in any case; sometimes. na kvacit adv. nowhere; never. kvacit ... kvacit sometimes ... sometimes; here and there, variously. yad ihāsti tad anyatra yan nehāsti na tat kvacit [Mah.] What is here is found elsewhere, what is not here is found nowhere.
kvasvit [svid₁] adv. anywhere.
kvāpi [api] adv. anywhere.
√ kvan v. [1] pr. (kvanati) pp. (kvanita) to make noise, to ring; to buzz; to make a noise of chains — ca. (kvanayati) to ring; to make produce a sound (by a musical instrument (i.)).

kvanitavenu [venu] amnf who played the flute. .1
√ kvath v. [1] pr. (kvathati) pp. (kvathita) to cook, boil | digest — ca. (kvāthayati) to cook; to prepare a decoction, an infusion. kvatha [agt. kvath] m. decoction over low heat.
kvathita [pp. kvath] amnf kvathitā cooked, boiled; hot (by cooking) — n. mead. ক্লমু kvasu nota. gram. primary affix [kṛt₂] producing ppft. like vidvas.
kvātha |act. kvath| m. cooking; boiling | med. decoction | (in fig.) pain, distress.
kvip nota. gram. primary affix [kṛt₂]; form of the agents ifc. from the root.
kṣa [obj. kṣi] ifc. mr. field.

kṣaṇa mn second, instant, moment; leisure, occasion; measure of time (approx. 4/5 second) — iic. temporarily (ifc.). kṣaṇam adv. for an instant; in an instant. kṣaṇam kuru wait an instant. kṣaṇena var. kṣaṇāt adv. at the moment; right away. kṣaṇeṣu immediately, at once. kṣaṇāt in an instant, instantly. kṣaṇāt kṣaṇāt at this precise moment. kṣaṇe kṣaṇe at any time | from time to time; as the opportunity arises.
kṣaṇadā |da| f. night | "that which gives leisure" |.
Kṣaṇadācara [cara] m. myth. n.p. of the vampire | rākṣasa | Kṣaṇadācara “Night owl”.
kṣaṇabhaṅga [bhaṅga] m. bd. continuous destruction of the universe.
kṣaṇabhaṅgavāda [vāda] m. phil. thesis bd. according to which the universe is continually destroyed and recreated.
kṣaṇabhaṅgavādin [vādin] afmn kṣaṇabhaṅgavādinī phil. supporter of this thesis.
kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi [siddhi] f. bed. n.p. of Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi, comic work. of Ratnakīrti.
kṣaṇaviyoga [viyoga] m. momentary separation.
kṣaṇārdha [ardha] n. ["half of a kṣaṇa"] very short instant, second.

kṣaṇika [kṣaṇaika] amnf kṣaṇikā fleeting, momentary; instantaneous | lasting only an instant, ephemeral; temporary | having leisure, taking advantage of an opportunity — f. kṣaṇikā flash. annadānam param dānam vidyādānam atah param annena kṣaṇikā tṛptiḥ yāvajjīvam ca vidyaya || The giving of food is a great charity, but the giving of knowledge surpasses it; with food satisfaction is momentary, with knowledge it lasts a lifetime.
kṣaṇikatva |tva| n. fugacity | phil. dogma bd. of universal fugacity, or ephemeral nature of phenomena.
kṣaṇikavāda |vāda| m. phil. doctrine bd. by teaching the transient nature of all things |kṣaṇikatva|; it was refuted by the Brahmasūtra of Bādarāyaṇa.
kṣatá |pp. kṣan| amnf kṣatā struck, wounded, broken; annihilated — n. wound, contusion.
kṣati [act. kṣan] f. act of injuring; injury | damage | defect; fault; error — ifc. suppression of (iic.).
kṣattṛ [agt. kṣad] amnf kṣattrī ved. one who cuts or distributes — m. waiter; carver |soc. bailiff, high-ranking person belonging to the circle

royal [ratnin]; [Mah.] Vidura had this title | soc. son of a śūdra and a kṣatriyā. ধ্বৰ ksatrá [instr. kṣi] n. temporal power, dominion, nobility, sovereignty; supremacy, authority | soc. dominant principle of the nobility of the sword; class [varna] noble of warriors; one of its members | Persian shah.
kṣatradharma | dharma | mn duty of the noble caste; royal ethic | warrior aptitude; courage.
kṣatrapa [pa₂] m. governor || fr. satrap.
kṣatrabandhu [bandhu] m. soc. member of the kṣatra class, noble.
kṣatrasama [sama] amnf kṣatrasamā soc. equal to a kṣatriya.

kṣatríya [kṣatraiya] amnf kṣatriyā who governs — n. sovereignty; nobility of the sword — mf kṣatriyā soc. member of the 2nd class [varṇa], warrior, prince, noble | pl. kṣatriyās soc. the class of princes — f. kṣatriyī wife of a kṣatriya || pali khattiya.
kṣatríyatā [tā] f. soc. nobility; rank of nobility.
kṣatriyayuvan | yuvan | mr. young warrior.
kṣatriyavarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Bhūmyādikānda, dealing with warriors.
√ kṣad v. [1] pr. r. (kṣádate) to cut (not. meat), dissect; divide | distribute food; eat.
√ kṣan v. [8] pr. (kṣaṇóti) pp. (kṣata) to strike, to injure — pr. r. (kṣaṇuté) to injure oneself.
kṣantavya [pfp. [3] kṣam] amnf kṣantavyā which must be endured or borne | which must be forgiven — n. (impers.) it must be pardoned by (g.) for (abl.).
√ kṣap₁ v. [1] pr. (kṣapati) pr. r. (kṣapate) to be abstinent; to fast; to do penance.
kṣáp₂ f. ved. night; darkness | duration of 24 h || fr. twilight. kṣapaḥ var. kṣapā adv. at night.
kṣapaṇa [act. kṣap₁] n. abstinence — m. mendicant monk bd. or jn.
kṣapaṇaka |ka| m. jn. mendicant monk | hist. np. of kṣapaṇaka, one of the nine jewels |navaratna| of the court of King Vikramāditya.
kṣapā |kṣap₁| f. night.
kṣapāha |ahan| n. one day and one night (24 h).
kṣapita [pp. ca. kṣī] amnf kṣapitā destroyed; ruined; diminished; suppressed.
kṣapitavya [pfp. [1] ca. kṣī] amnf kṣapitavyā to finish, to delete.

(kṣamiṣyati) pp. (kṣānta, kṣamita) to be patient, to endure, to bear | to allow; to forgive, to be lenient towards | to forgive something (acc.) to someone (g. dat) — ca. (kṣamayati) ca. r. (kṣāmayate) to ask someone for forgiveness (acc.) for (acc.). kṣamyatām var. kṣamatām adr. excuse me. kṣamasva me tat adr. excuse me for that.
kṣam₁ [agt. kṣam] f. the earth. kṣamā i. adv. on earth; on the ground.
kṣamá [agt. kṣam] amnf kṣamā patient, capable of enduring; able to (loc. inf.) | bearable, tolerable — f. cf. kṣamā. kṣamībhū become capable of (dat.). kartum kṣamaḥ capable of doing.
kṣamatā |tā| f. capacity, aptitude.
kṣamatva |tva| n. capacity, aptitude (at ⟨iic. loc.⟩).
kṣamavat [vat] amnf kṣamavatī knowing what is appropriate or adequate.
kṣamā [f. kṣama] f. patience; indulgence, by giving | the earth. kṣamām kr to be indulgent. kṣamām karotu adr. excuse me. kṣamāṃ prārthaye adr. excuse me.
kṣamādaṃśa [daṃśa] m. bio. bot. Moringa olei fera, horseradish tree; it is cultivated as a medicinal plant to combat diabetes; its leaves and fruits are rich in nutrients and used in cooking.
kṣamāvat [vat] amnf kṣamāvatī patient; tolerant; who endures | domesticated (not. elephant).
kṣamita [pp. kṣam] amnf kṣamitā par donné.
kṣamitṛ [agt. kṣam] amnf kṣamitrī while lasting; patient.
kṣamin [agt. kṣam] amnf kṣaminī who forgives.
kṣamya [pfp. [1] kṣam] amnf kṣamyā to forgive.
kṣáya₁ [agt. kṣi] amnf kṣayā who lives, who resides — m. dwelling, residence.

kṣayá₂ [act. kṣī] m. ruin, loss, destruction; misfortune | decline, decay, decay; decrease; opp. vrddhi | end, fatal illness; not. phthisis, tuberculosis | | kṣayamāsa | astr. orphaned lunar month, framing a short solar month without a new moon; such a month is always preceded and followed within three months by an intercalary month [adhika], which allows it to be named; the Eastern school omits the second intercalary month, the Northwest school omits the first; the Southern school keeps both, but doubly names the orphaned month which is called

double | yugma | math. negative quantity; opposite astr. np. of Kṣaya "at the end of life", personifying year 60 of a life cycle [samvatsara]. kṣayaṃ gam decrease; come to an end, perish. kşayam i id. kşayam yā id. kṣayam nī destroy. kulakṣaya ruin of a family. lokakṣaya end of the world. jīvitakṣaye adv. at the end of life. dinakşaye adv. at the end of the day. vrddhiksayau growth and decline.
kṣayin [agt. kṣī] amnf kṣayiṇī perishable; sick; that which goes out (light).
kṣayya [pfp. [1] kṣī] amnf kṣayyā which can be destroyed.
√ kṣar v. [1] pr. (kṣarati) pft. (cakṣāra) pp. (kṣaritá) pf. (vi) to flow, to run | to melt, to liquefy | to escape, to be lost | to spread | to expel.
kṣara [agt. kṣar] amnf kṣarā that flows; perishable — n. body.

kṣarita [pp. kṣar] amnf kṣaritā flowed; liquefied; oozed.
√ ধ ল্ kṣal [related to kṣar] ca. (kṣālayati) pp. (kṣālita) pf. (pra) to wash, rinse; to clean | to bathe, to purify with water. hastau pādau cākṣālayat he washed his hands and feet.
kṣáva [act. kṣu] m. sneezing; cough | black mustard; syn. rājika. .3
kṣavathu [kṣuathu] m. sneeze.
√ &T kṣā v. [4] pr. (kṣāyati) pp. (ksāṇa) to burn — ca. (kṣāpayati) to cause to burn.
kṣātra |*kṣatra| amnf kṣātrī proper to the warrior | kṣatriya | — n. state of chief, privilege of the prince, dignity of warrior.
kṣātratejas [tejas] n. phil. effulgence of princes; cf. Rcīka.
kṣānta [pp. kṣam] amnf kṣāntā patient bearable, forgiven — n. patience.
kṣānti [act. kṣam] f. patience, indulgence; constancy | bd. tolerance, one of the 6 perfections |pāramitā| of an accomplished |bodhisattva|.
kṣāmá amnf kṣāmā burned; emaciated, thin; weakened | weak; infirm.
kṣāra [agt. kṣar] amnf kṣārā caustic, corrosive; acrid, bitter, salty — mn soda, potash; acid | ang. caustic; fr. caustique. kṣate kṣāramiva (maxim) like salt on a wound.
kṣāla |act. kṣal| m. cleaning, washing.
kṣālana |act. kṣal| n. cleaning, washing — agt. amnf kṣālanā ifc. that washes, that cleans, that wipes (iic.).
kṣālita [pp. kṣal] amnf kṣālita washed, cleaned | erased.

√ kṣi v. [2] pr. (kṣeti) pf. (pari) ved. to possess, to govern; to be master of (g.) — v. [1] pr. (kṣáyati) ved. id. — v. [6] pr. (kṣiyáti) to inhabit, to remain, to reside | to be quiet; to be hidden.
kṣit [agt. kṣi] ifc. amnf who resides in, who governs (iic.).
kṣitá [pp. kṣī] amnf kṣitā cf. kṣīṇa.
kṣitāyus [āyus] amnf whose existence is miserable | whose life is wasted.
kṣití₁ [act. kṣi] f. dwelling, dwelling | land, soil; the land.
kṣitikampa |kampa| m. earthquake. kṣitikampavighūrṇitamm overturned by an earthquake.

Kṣitigarbha |garbha| m. bd. np. of the perfect [bodhisattva] Kṣitigarbha "Seed of the Earth"; he is the patron of children and travelers; he is depicted holding the staff |khakkhara| in his right hand. kșititala | tala | n. surface of the ground. kșitipa [pa₂] m. king ["who protects the earth"].
kṣitibhuj [bhuj₃] m. king ["who enjoys the land"].
Kṣitīśa [īśa] m. king ["master of the land"] | hist. np. of King Kṣitīśa of Kānyakubja.
kṣitīśavaṃśāvalīcarita |vaṃśāvalīcarita| n. bed. n.p. from the Kṣitīśavaṃśāvalīcarita “Dynastic Chronicle of Kṣitīśa”, from the end of the 18th century.
kṣíti₂ [act. kṣī] f. ruin, destruction | end of the world; destruction of the universe.

√ kṣip v. [6] pr. (kṣipáti) pr. r. (kṣipate) pft. (cikṣepa) pp. (kṣiptá) abs. (kṣiptvā, kṣipya) pf. (adhi, ava, ā, ut, ni, pra, prati, vi, sam) to throw, to hurl; to propel | to plunge into (2 acc.); to reach (with a thrust) | to throw away; to discard, to get rid of | to blame (loc.) | to despise; to insult; to strike; to destroy — ca. (kṣepáyati) to cause to throw; to send down; to bring down. kṣāraṃ kṣate kṣip ["to throw salt on the wound"] ag to engrave an offense.
kṣipa [agt. kṣip] amnf kṣipā ifc. who throws (iic.) — m. thrower of (iic.) — act. f. kṣipā act of throwing; throw.
kṣipaka [agt. kṣip] m. archer.
kṣiptá [pp. kṣip] amnf kṣiptā thrown, launched; rejected — n. distraction, forgetfulness.
kṣiptáyoni [yoni] amnf soc. of bad birth; said of a person for whom a brah mane cannot officiate as a priest | rtvij|.

kṣiptálaguḍa [laguḍa] amnf kṣiptalaguḍā having thrown the club. ধিমু kṣipnu [agt. kṣip] amnf [“who throws obstacles in the way” | who obstructs | who despises; who insults; syn. nirākariṣṇu. ਖਿਸ kṣiprá [kṣipra] amnf kṣiprā that rebounds; elastic (bow) | lively; quick — f. kṣiprā geo. np. of the river kṣiprā “quick”, flowing at Ujjayinī; cf. Siprā. kṣipram adv. quickly, fast, immediately. kşiprasamdhi var. kşiprasandhi [samdhi] m. phon. case of liaison between vowels, where the first is changed into the corresponding semivowel.

√ k sī v. [5] pr. (k sinoti) v. [9] pr. (k sināti) pp. (kṣīṇa) pf. (apa, upa, pra, sam) destroy, damage, diminish; strike, kill — ps. (kṣīyate) perish; pass (said of time) — ca. (kṣapayati) destroy, ruin, finish off.
kṣīṇá [pp. kṣī] amnf kṣīṇā diminished, weak; worn out, exhausted; destroyed, ruined; poor, miserable.
kṣīṇátā [tā] f. exhaustion; decrease, wear, corruption, rupture.
kṣīṇátoya [toya] amnf kṣīṇatoyā tari (river, source).
kṣīṇávat [vat] amnf kṣīṇavatī worn out, exhausted; corrupted. .4
kṣīṇávṛtti [vṛtti] amnf without employment; who no longer has means of subsistence | phil. [YS.] (thought) whose fluctuations have been suppressed.
kṣīṇáśakti [śakti] amnf exhausted, who has no more strength.
kṣība amnf kṣībā drunk, intoxicated — m. drunkard.
kṣīyamāṇa [ppr. ps. kṣī] amnf kṣīyamāṇā which withers away; which is exhausted.
kṣīrá [kṣarīra] n. milk; water, juice, sap — v. [11] pr. (kṣīrasyati) to desire milk || hi. khīr.
kṣīrataraṃgiṇī [taraṃgiṇī] f. gram. n.p. of the Kṣīrataraṃgiṇī, lexicon of roots |dhātuvṛtti| due to Kṣīrasvāmī.
kṣīranīra [nīra] iic. (copulative) milk and water.
kṣīranīranyāya [nyāya] m. maxim of milk and water, simili of two things difficult to separate |nīrakṣīraviveka|; opp. tilataṇḍulanyāya.
kṣīrapāka |pāka| amnf kṣīrapākā cooked with milk.
kṣīrapāna |pāna| n. act of drinking milk — m. container for drinking milk | var. kṣīrapāṇa id. (tribe) milk drinker.
kṣīramahārṇava [mahārṇava] m. cf. kṣīroda.
kṣīrasagara [sagara] m. myth. ocean of primordial milk; syn. kṣīrodadhi.

ksīrasvāmin [svāmin] m. hist. np. of the grammarian Kṣīrasvāmī (11th century); he lived in Kaśmīra at the court of Jayāpīḍa, to whom he taught the grammar of Sanskrit; he is credited with the Amarakosodghāṭana, commentary on the Nāmalingānuśāsana, and the commentary Ksīrataramginī, of the pāninīya Dhātupātha.

kṣīrārāma |ārāma| m. geo. np. of kṣīrārāma, great Shaivite pilgrimage site at Palakollu in Andhra, west of the Godāvarī delta; great Shaiva pilgrimage site at Rāmacandrapura; it is one of the five garden shrines [pañcārāmakṣetra].
kṣīrārāmeśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of kṣīrārāmeśvara, śivalinga of kṣīrārāma; it is said that it was installed by Visnu.
kṣīroda [uda] m. myth. primordial ocean of milk lit. [K.] np. of the chamberlain Kṣirodha, sent by Citraratha to Mahāśvetā to console Kādambarī; he brought Taralikā back to the latter.

kṣīrodamathana [mathana] n. myth. churning of the ocean of milk; the gods [deva] and the demons [asura] joined forces to churn the primordial sea of milk, with Mount Mandara as the churn, the dragon [nāga] Vāsuki as the rope, and Viṣṇu Kūrma as the support; all the treasures of the Earth came out of it, including Surabhī, Vārunī, Lakṣmī, the pārijāta tree, Uccaiḥśravā, Airāvata, Sudarśana, Kaustubha, and finally Dhanvantari carrying the urn [kumbha] of ambrosia [amrta] which the gods and the ti tans fought over; Vișnu transformed into Mohinī subjugated them with his magic [māyā] and served the 33 gods, Vāyu the first; the titan [asura] Rāhuketū stole some and began to drink, but Vișnu decapitated him into an eternal head Rāhu, and an ephemeral body Ketu; from it also came evils, such as Jyeṣṭhā the evil elder sister of Lakṣmī, and the poison Halāhala which destroys everything, and which was swallowed by Śiva whose throat turned black |Nīlakantha|.
kṣīrodaka | udaka | n. milk and water | cf. kṣīroda.
ksīrodakaśāyin [śāyin] m. myth. np. of Kṣīrodakaśāyī epith. of cosmic Viṣṇu, resting on the primordial waters.
kṣīrodadhi | udadhi | mr. myth. ocean of primordial milk; syn. kṣīroda.
kṣīrin [kṣīrain] amnf kṣīriṇī which gives milk; succulent (plant).
√ kṣu v. [2] pr. (kṣauti) pp. (kṣuta) to sneeze; to blow one's nose | to cough — des. (cukṣūṣati) to feel like sneezing or coughing.
kṣuṇṇa [pp. kṣud] amnf kṣuṇṇā crushed, ground, pulverized; broken, pierced; trampled | violated (vow).
kṣut iic. kṣudh₂.
ksutksāma [kṣāma] amnf kṣutkṣāmā emaciated by hunger.
kṣutpipāsā |pipāsā| f. hunger and thirst.
kṣutpipāsita [ita] amnf kṣutpipāsitā who is hungry and thirsty.
kṣuta |pp. kṣu| amnf kṣutā who sneezed — m. mustard — n. sneezing — f. kṣut id.
kṣutābhijana [abhijana] m. ["that makes you sneeze"] black mustard; syn. rājika.
kṣutavat [ppa. kṣu] amnf kṣutavatī who sneezes.

kṣudrá [kṣudra] amnf kṣudrā small, insignificant; low, vile, bad — n. small thing, baseness | pl. kṣudrāṇi phil. [ChU.] the lower beings who revolve in the cycle of samsāra, unlike the realized ones who have freed themselves from it. .5
kṣudraka |ka| amnf kṣudrikā weak, small | med. difficult (breathing).
kṣudrapanasa | panasa | m. bio. bot. Artocarpus communis, breadfruit tree, a moraceae; large tree with grey-yellow bark, used medicinally — n. its fruit, edible.

kṣétra [instr. kṣi] n. property, domain; field, plain, countryside | place, location, spot; geometric figure; place of pilgrimage | wife; body | phil. the object; opp. kṣetrajña the subject || Pali khetra. kșetrīkṛ to take possession of, to become master of (land). kṣetrīkaraṇam n. occupation, possession | alchemy.

kṣetrajña [jña] amnf kṣetrajñā ["who knows his domain" | skillful, expert, adroit — m. soul, conscience | phil. spiritual conscience animating the body and the mind | phil. the conscious subject, who contemplates the object |ksetra|. kṣetrakṣetrajñau phil. the subject and the object.
ksetrapa |pa₂| m. soc. (title) guardian of the king's fields. kșetrapati | pati | m. soc. landowner; farmer.
kṣetrin [in] amnf kṣetrinī who owns a field | concerning agriculture | landowner; farmer.
ksetriya [iya] m. adulterous man.
kṣepa [act. kṣip] m. throw, shoot | offense, insult — v. [11] pr. r. (kṣepāyate) to insult.
kṣepaka [agt. kṣip] m. lit. interpolated or doubtful passage — f. kṣepikā ifc. that throws, that sends back (iic.) | that insults, that shows disrespect towards | lit. inserted, interpolated.
kṣepaṇa [act. kṣip] n. action of throwing, moving, propelling — f. kṣepaṇī oar; rowing. kṣepaṇe gram. (action) in the sense of throwing.
kṣépiṣṭha [super. kṣipra] amnf kṣépiṣṭhā the fastest.
kṣépīyas [compar. kṣipra] amnf kṣepīyasī faster. kṣepīyas acc. adv. as quickly as possible.

kṣéma [kṣiman] amnf kṣemā habitable; safe, comfortable, serene, tranquil — mn ved. settled period | place of rest; peace, tranquility; security, well-being, happiness, prosperity myth. [SP.] np. of Kṣema "prosperity", son of Siddhi₂ and Gaņeśa | myth. son of Titikṣā | ang. home.
kṣématara [tara] amnf kṣematarā compar. more peaceful — n. more comfortable situation, greater happiness.
kṣemayoga |yoga| m. du. kṣemayogau tranquility and action; rest and effort.

Kṣemarāja [rāja] m. hist. n.p. of Kṣemarāja, 11th century Kaśmīra philosopher, prolific student of Abhinavagupta; he is the author of the Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya, the Vimarśinī₁ exegesis of the Śivasūtra, the Spandanirṇaya commentary on the Spandakārikās, and commentaries on the Stava cintāmani, the Svacchandatantra, the Netratantra and the Spandasamdoha.

Kṣemendra [indra] m. hist. n.p. of Kṣemendra, 11th century Kaśmīra poet, student of Abhina vagupta; he is the author of numerous works, not. composition manuals [kaviśikṣā] like the Aucityavicāracarcā, the Kavikaņṭhābharaṇa and the Suvṛttatilaka; his Bṛhatkathāmañjarī is a Sanskrit version of the Bṛhatkathā; He is also the author of satirical works such as the Sa mayamātrkā and the Narmamālā, and didactic works such as the Lokaprakāśa and the Nītikalpataru, devotional works such as the Daśāvatāracarita, or satirical works such as the Desopadesa; he is also credited with the Rāmayaṇamañjarī and the Barathakathāmañjarī, abridged versions respectively of the Rām. and the Mah.; also the Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā and the Sevyasevako padeśa; he bore the title of Vyāsadāsa.
kṣemam [acc. kṣema] iic.
kṣemaṃkara [kara₁] amnf kṣemaṃkarī who brings serenity, who comforts — f. kṣemaṃkarī myth. np. of Kṣemaṃkarī, favorable aspect of Durgā "the Comforter".
kṣémīśvara [kṣemaīśvara] m. hist. np. of Kṣemīśvara, dramatic author of the 9th-10th century; he is credited with the dramas Candakauśika₁ and Naisadhānanda.
kṣemyá [kṣemaya] amnf kṣemyā at rest, at ease, comfortable; serene, tranquil | soothing; prosperous (region) — n. rest — m. myth. epith. of Śiva — f. kṣemyā myth. epith. of Durgā.
kṣeya [pfp. [1] kṣī] amnf kṣeyā which must be destroyed. ধীস kṣaitra [*kṣetra] n. group of lands; territory.
kṣaipra [*kṣipra] amnf kṣaiprā phon. qualifies the ksiprasamdhi, carrying the accent svarita — n. speed.
kṣodiṣṭha [super. kṣudra] amnf kṣodiṣṭhā the smallest; the finest extremely small, minuscule.
kṣodīyas [compar. kṣudra] amnf kṣodīyasī even smaller; finer.
kṣobha [act. kṣubh] m. trembling, agitation; disturbance, worry, emotion | strong current of water, torrent, swell.
kṣobhya [pfp. [1] kṣubh] amnf kṣobhyā agitated, troubled, worried.
kṣaudra [*kṣudra] mf kṣaudrā soc. mixed caste man vaidehamāgadhī — n. honey.
kṣaura [*kṣura] amnf kṣaurā done with a razor — n. shaving; not. the act of shaving one's head — f. kṣaurī razor. kşauram kr to shave. kşauram kār to get shaved.
kṣaurakaraṇa | karaṇa | n. shaving.
kṣaurakarma | karma | n. shaving.

kṣṇutá [pp. kṣṇu] amnf kṣṇutā sharpened — ifc. ksnut id. k ā f. the Earth gr. ; fr. chthonic, to chthonic.
kṣmātala [tala] n. soil of the Earth.
kṣmātalorvaśī [Urvaśī] f. lit. [DKC.] np. of the beautiful kṣmātalorvaśī "Urvaśī on Earth", Avantideva's personal dancer; Anantavarmā₁ the viola.
√ kṣviḍ v. [1] pr. (kṣveḍati) pp. (kṣveḍita) ca. (kṣveḍayati) to emit an inarticulate sound; to buzz, to murmur, to grunt, to roar, to hiss.
kṣveḍa [act. kṣviḍ] m. hiss, noise — f. kșvedā roar; battle cry.

khá [obj. khan] n. hole, cavity; opening; not. one of the 9 openings of the human body | sense organ; wound | hub of a wheel | empty space, air, ether; sky | math. symb. the number 0 | [lex.] humor; cf. duhkha, sukha — loc. cf. khe. khapuṣpāṇi ci ["to pluck flowers in the void" | to build castles in the air.
khaga [ga₁] amnf khagā that moves in the air, that flies — m. bird; flying insect | sun; air, wind | myth. np. of khaga the moving sun, a name of Sūrya.
khagasthāna | sthāna | n. tree hollow where a bird lives.

khagama | gama | amnf khagamā that moves in the air (said notably of gandharvās and missile weapons) — m. bird; flying insect | myth. [Mah.] np. of the Brahmin Khagama; one day while he was officiating at the agnihotra, his friend Sahasrapāda playfully placed a straw snake around his neck; he cursed him to become a snake [dundubha], and to be able to regain human form only at the sight of the ascetic Ruru. khagoda m. bio. bot. Saccharum spontaneum, a species of reed.
khácara [cara] amnf khacarī that flies, that moves in the air — m. bird | planet; the sun; cloud; wind; celestial aerial being | math. symb. the number 9 (for the 9 planets).
khajyotis [jyotis] m. organic. glow worm; syn. kha dyota.
khadyota | dyota | mr. organic. zoo. Lampyridae firefly, glow worm; syn. khajyotis.
khayoga [yoga] m. astr. cf. yogas.
khasūci [sūci] amnf ["needle to pierce space" | open door pusher; stupid person. .7
vaiyākaraṇakhasūciḥ | Mah. | An incompetent grammarian.
khakāra [(kha)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'kha'.
Khakkhara m. bd. Buddhist monk's staff; it bears rings that announce his imminent arrival.
khacita ifc. amnf khacitā inlaid with (iic.). manikhacita inlaid with jewels.

(ni, nis, pari, vi) to burn, consume, set on fire | (figuratively) to destroy — ps. (dahyate) to be consumed | to be burning hot — v. [4] pr. (dahyati) to burn, to be on fire | (figuratively) to be consumed | to grieve, to be tormented — ca. (dāhayati) to set on fire — intens. (dandahīti) to destroy by fire ang. day; all. Tag. dagdhukāmaḥ who wants to set on fire.
khañj₂ [agt. khañj₂] amnf [nom. khan] who limps.
khañja [agt. khañj₂] amnf khañjā lame; syn. pangu — m. myth. |Hayaśīrṣapancarātra| epith. of Sani — f. khañjā phon. family of meters. pādena khañjaḥ who limps on one leg.
khañjatā |tā| f. lameness.
khañjatva [tva] n. id.
khañjana [act. khañj₂] n. act of limping — m. bio. zoo. Motacilla alba, wagtail.
khaṭa m. phlegm; syn. kapha, kheṭa.
khataka |ka| mr. closed hand; hand position pulling the string of a bow.
khaṭakāmukha |āmukha| amnf khaṭakāmukhā (archery) refers to the position of the archer ready to shoot, with the hand pulling the string brought to the level of the face.
khaṭvā f. bed, couch; swing, hammock.

khaṭvāṅga [aṅga₁] mn soc. ["in the shape of a bedpost" | mace combining a skull and a humerus, weapon of Bhairava, and of the ascetics of the bhai rava sect | bd. tantric symbol of Vajrayāna, trident of Padmasambhava; it bears three severed heads — m. myth. [BhP.] np. of King Khaṭvāṅga "Armed with a mace", son of Mūlaka of the solar lineage |sūryavaṃśa|, also called Dilīpa₂. khaţvātale |tala| loc. adv. under the bed.
khaṭvārūḍha |ārūḍha| amnf khaṭvārūḍhā
lazy ["mounted on the bed"]; said especially of a student who has not finished his studies, and who should sleep on the floor. khatvārūdhah jālmah the lazy person is despicable.

khaḍa |obj. khaṇḍ| amnf khaḍī broken, shattered | cracked, fissured; having holes, gaps — m. division; section | math. term in an equation — f. khadī chalk — v. [11] pr. (khadayati) to break, shatter, divide. hāte khadi soc. ceremony marking the beginning of primary school studies, around 4 or 5 years old, on the day of vidyārambha; the teacher gives a stick of chalk to the student and begins to teach him to write.
khadadevakula | devakula | n. temple in ruins.
khaḍana |agt. khaṇḍ| amnf khaḍanā that breaks, that shatters — act. n. break; shatter; destruction.

khadgachinna | chinna | amnf khadgachinnā cut by the sword. khadgachinnārikantha who cuts the necks of enemies with the sword.

khadgadamstrā [damstrā] f. bed. [KSS.] np. of the rākṣasī Khadgadaṃṣṭrā “Bite of the sword”, sister of Yamadamṣṭra; Indivarasena married him after killing him; she is the vidyādharī Adityaprabha punished by his jealousy.

khadgabandha | bandha | mr. bed. geometric poem [citrakāvya] in the shape of a sword. khadgarāvaņa [rāvaṇa] m. phil. [Tantra] n.p. of Khadgarāvana, divinity mantra; His cult was celebrated in India from the 10th to the 13th century.
khadgin [in] m. organic. zoo. rhinoceros; syn. gandaka.
khaḍgākhaḍgi [red. khaḍga] adv. en com bat sword against sword.
√ khaṇḍ v. [1] pr. r. (khaṇḍate) v. [10] pr. (khandayati) pp. (khandita) pf. (ava, pari) break, shatter; cut, divide; crush | tear to pieces, rip; destroy, suppress | refute; disturb.
khaṇḍa [obj. khaṇḍ] amnf khaṇḍā broken, shattered, cracked; mutilated, crippled; deficient; castrated— mn part, fragment, piece, shard, gap lit. section, chapter, division.
khandakāvya [kāvya] n. lit. minor poem, small poem.
khandakhādya [khādya] n. delicate dish; pleasant thing.

khaṇḍagiri [giri] m. geo. np. of the hills of khandagiri, site of caves dug by Jain monks (2nd century BC), 8 km north of mod. Bhubaneśvar in Orissa; it is twin to the hill of Udayagiri₂, which bears an inscription of King Khāravela.

khandadeva [deva] m. hist. np. of the philosopher mīmāṃsaka Khaṇḍadeva of Kāśī (1575–1665); he is the author of the Bhāṭṭatantrarahasya and the Bhāṭṭadīpikā; he enriched the Mīmāṃsā using the conceptual calculus [Navyanyāya] of Gangesěa; he undertook a commentary Mīmāmsākaustubha of the .8 Pūrvamīmāmsāsūtra; he became sannyāsin under the name of Srīdhara Yatindra.
khandamañjūṣā [mañjūṣā] f. lit. varied collection.
khaṇḍasādhaka [sādhaka] m. expertise in weapons.

khandānvaya [anvaya] m. gram. style of grammatical commentary at the structural level [vākyayojanā] starting from the verb, then filling the roles of its dependencies by the noun forms, the adjectives being attached afterwards to the nouns they qualify; it is appropriate to the dialectical method by question and answer [kathambhūtinī]; opp. dandānvaya.
khandānvayapaddhati [paddhati] f. gram. vaiyākaraṇa method of grammatical analysis, where the verb is considered first.
khaṇḍaka [agt. khaṇḍ] amnf khaṇḍikā ifc. that destroys, that breaks (iic.) — obj. m. fragment, piece, chunk | not. sugar cubes | ang. candy.
khandakāluka |āluka| n. sweet potato.

khaṇḍana [act. khaṇḍ] n. destruction, fragmentation, shattering; beating | the act of wounding (not. with the teeth) | interruption; frustration; opposition, rebellion; insurrection | refutation of an argument, contradiction; deception, trickery lit. [bhāṣya] demolition of the opposing thesis — f. khaṇḍanā rejection — agt. amnf khaṇḍanā ifc. that which breaks, that which divides (ii.c.); that which destroys, that which suppresses (ii.c.).

khandanakhandakhādya [khandakhādya] n. lit. np. from the Khandanakhandakhādya "Sophism Treats", a philosophical work by Śrīharṣa; it aims to criticize the realism of the logicians [naiyāyika] of the Gotama₁ school, and not. Udayana₁, by refuting any attempt to define reality, the world being essentially inexplicable [anirvacanīya]; cf. Dīdhiti.
khaṇḍala [khaṇḍala] mn piece.
Khaṇḍika [khaṇḍaika] m. [“who learns section by section” | student | hist. np. of Khandika, founding master of a school of the Black Yajurveda.
khandikopādhyāya [upādhyāya] m. school classroom teacher. khandikopādhyāyah śisyāya capetam dadāti | Mah. | The teacher slaps the student.

khaṇḍita [pp. ca. khaṇḍ] amnf khaṇḍitā broken, shattered, in pieces |destroyed, in ruins; lost, damaged — f. khaṇḍitā soc. woman furious at the sight of another woman's nail or tooth marks on her husband's body.
khaṇḍin [khaṇḍain] amnf khaṇḍinī in pieces, divided.

khandobā m. myth. np. of Khaṇḍobā "Father with the sword", pastoral Dravidian deity of the Dhangar community of Mahārāṣṭra; he is identified with Rudra and then with Shiva as Mārtanda Bhairava; he is depicted on horseback, carrying the sword, with a dog.

khadirá m. bio. bot. Acacia catechu, the tree from which catechu is produced; its very hard wood was used as the core of clay icons and as a sacrificial pole; Vedic. 100 needles of khadira wood are sacrificed for long life. kanţakavān khadirah the khadira bears thorns.

khanitṛ [agt. khan] amnf khanitrī who digs, who spades.

khára amnf kharā hard, Rude; rough, rugose; harsh; acidic; unpleasant | dense; solid; opp. drava | cutting; dangerous; offensive — m. bio. zoo. donkey (because of its braying); syn. gar dabha, rāsabha | soc. quadrangular mound of earth used to receive the vessels of the Vedic sacrifice | construction platform of a dwelling | myth. [Rām.] np. of Khara "Rude", vampire ogre [rākṣasa], younger brother of Rāvaṇa; he lived in Janasthāna in the Daṇḍakā forest with his sister Sūrpaṇakhā; at the head of an army of 14000 ogres, he was killed by Rāma; Khara had been Madhu₁ in .9 a previous life | astr. np. of Khara₁ "Rebel", personifying year 25 of a life cycle [samvatsara] — f. cf. kharī. kharībhū med. (disease) to worsen.
kharavat [vat] adv. like a donkey.

kharosthī [oṣṭhī] f. hist. ancient Indian script, adapted from the Aramaic script of the Achaemenid Empire, under the reign of Ashoka; it was written from right to left; it was replaced from the 3rd century by brāhmī .
kharī [f. Khara₁] f. bio. zoo. donkey | female mule.
kharīvātsalya [vātsalya] n. soc. ["maternal love of a mule"] unwanted motherhood.
kharu [Khara₁u] amnf idiot; pervert; sa dique — f. soc. (woman) who chooses her own husband.
kharkhoda var. khārkhoṭa n. exorcism.
kharjūra m. organic. bot. Phoenix sylvestris, date palm — f. kharjūrī wild date palm — n. kharjūra date.

kharjūrapura [pura] n. geo. np. of the City of kharjūrapura "City of dates", cultural capital of the rājput Candela dynasty (9th to 12th centuries), also called Kharjuravāhaka; it has many temples, Jain and Hindu; mod. Kha jurāho, in Madhya Pradesh.
kharpara m. skull; cranial cap | alms bowl.
kharbūja [Persian] n. watermelon; syn. tarambuja.
kharvá amnf karvā mutilated; disabled; dwarf — mn math. ten billion | myth. the "innumerable"
treasure [nidhi] guarded by Kubera; cf. navanidhi.

khála amnf khalā wicked — mn ground; location | granary; threshing floor; cake — mf khalā wicked person. khale kapotanyāyaḥ maxim of pigeons on the threshing floor; it evokes the production of an effect by many simultaneous causes.
khálapū |pū₂| mnf sweeper.
khalatí amnf bald — m. baldness.
khali [khalai] m. crab.
khalina mn bride; brake — n. khalīna id.

khálu adv. indeed; certainly, in truth; definitely | behold; now | let us cease (abs.). na khalu adv. not at all, certainly not. atha khalu adv. now. kim nu khalu adv. it may indeed be that. susthu khalu most certainly. dārunah khalvasi you are truly cruel. kāpālikah khalu eşah that man is certainly vile.
khalla m. paper or fabric pouch; leather gourd | spice mortar.
khálva m. bot. Dolichos spicatus, legume whose lentils are edible | spice mortar; syn. khalla.
khalvāṭa amnf khalvāṭā bald || lat. calvus; fr. bald, baldness.
khasa m. itching; scar | man from the land of the khasās | pl. khasās this land, in northern India.
khasatila [tila] m. organic. bot. Papaver somniferum, poppy; syn. khaskhasa.
khasabīja [bīja] n. organic. bot. Papaver somniferum, poppy; syn. khasatila.
khasṛma m. myth. [HV.] np. of daitya khasṛma, son of Vipracitti and Siṃhikā.
khaskhasa [related to khasa] m. organic. bot. Papa worm somniferum, poppy; syn. khasatila.
khā [act. khan] ifc. f. digging.

khāṇḍava [*khaṇḍava] mn Sugar candy, sweet — n. myth. [Mah.] np. of khāṇḍava “(forest of) Sugar”, sacred wood of Kuruksetra, symbolizing the desire to enjoy the world of dualities | fr. candi; ang. candy.
khāṇḍavadahana [dahana] m. myth. [Mah.] incen die par Agni, aided by Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, de la forêt khāṇḍava.
khāndavaprastha | prastha | m. myth. | Mah. | np. of Khāndavaprastha, "Plateau of Khāndava", City founded by the Pāṇḍavās in the khāṇḍava forest; its architect was Maya.
khāṇḍavāyana [*khaṇḍaāyana] m. soc. family of brahmins, descendants of the officiants of Parasurāma at his great sacrifice, so named because they shared |khanda| the altar of Kaśyapa.
khāṇḍika [*Khaṇḍika] n. hist. school of the black Ya jurveda founded by Khaṇḍika — m. merchant of Sugar and confectionery.
khāndikīya [īya] m. pl. Khandika students | var. khāndikeya id.
Khāṇḍikya [*Khaṇḍikaya] m. bed. [VP.] np. of Khāṇḍikya, a Janaka king.
khātá |pp. khan| amnf khātā dug; excavated, unearthed | buried — m. pit, ditch — n. ditch; canal, moat; well, basin, pond | excavation; ca verne | digging — f. khātā artificial pond.
khātaka |ka| amnf khātikā who digs — m. excavator; debtor — n. ditch; dike — f. khātikā ditch.
khātámūla |mūla| amnf khātamūlā from which the root is pulled out.
khātra |instr. khan| n. shovel; spade | dug basin.
khādá [agt. khād] ifc. amnf khādā who devours (iic.).
khādaka |agt. khād| mf khādikā who eats, who devours — act. m. act of eating, meal.
khādata [imp. khād] ind. eat!
khādatamodatā [modata] f. festivity (where one eats and rejoices continuously). atra khādatamodatā vartate "eat and rejoice" is the rule here.
khādatavamatā [vamata] f. festive excess (where one eats and vomits continuously).
khādatācamatā [ācamata] f. feast (where one eats and rinses one's mouth constantly).
khādana [act. khād] n. act of eating; chewing | meal — obj. n. food; victuals — ins. m. dent.
khādí m. bracelet; ring | ankle ring.
khādita [pp. khād] amnf khāditā mangé.
khāditavya [pfp. [3] khād] amnf khāditavyā which must be eaten.
khāditṛ [agt. khād] amnf khāditrī [sg. nom. khāditā, acc. khāditāram] who eats, who devours; hungry.
khādirá [*khadira] amnf khādirī prove nant de l'arbre khadira.
khādirágṛhasūtra |gṛhasūtra| n. bed. n.p. of the Khādiragrhasūtra.
khādirásāra |sāra| mr. resin from the khadira tree, used to prepare cachou.
khādya [pfp. [1] khād] amnf khādyā man geable; comestible — n. food; provisions, vic tuailles.
khānaka [agt. khan] amnf khānakā ifc. who digs (iic.) — m. burglar, thief.
khāni [loc. khan] ifc. f. mine of (iic.).
khānya [pfp. [1] khan] amnf khānyā which must be unearthed | obtained by digging.
khāra m. minot, measure of grain; it is worth 3
bushels [droṇa] (about 40 l) — f. khāri id. — f. khārī id.

Khāravela m. hist. np. of King Khāravela, who reigned in Kalinga in the 2nd century BC; he was of the Meghavahana lineage; under his reign the bd. site of Tosalī prospered, as did the Jain monasteries; he favoured all religions; he extended his empire over a large portion of East and South India.
khārim [acc. khāri] iic.
khārimpaca [paca] amnf khārimpacā refers to a 40-litre pot (capable of holding a khāri).
khārkhoṭa var. kharkhoda n. exorcism.
√ khid v. [6] pr. (khidáti) pp. (khinna) pf. (ut, bet) to press; to squeeze, torment — ps. (khi dyate) to get tired, to be depressed — ca. (khedayati) to torment, molest.
khidra [khidra] m. unhappy | illness — n. burden.
khinna [pp. khid] amnf khinnā depressed, tired; suffering, uneasy, disturbed. ratikhinna amn exhausted from sexual pleasures.

khilá amnf khilā insufficient; incomplete; insoluble — m. wasteland; wasteland between cultivated plots; desert land — n. interval; gap; supplement, remainder | math. insoluble problem | pl. khilāni lit. additional hymns of the Rigveda. khilīkī to make desert-like; to render powerless. khilībhūta amn abandoned.
khiladhātu [dhātu] m. gram. irregular verbal root.
khilaparvan [parvan] n. lit. np. of the Khilaparva "Additional Section" of the Mah., also called Harivamśa.
khilya [khilaya] m. wasteland; mass, heap.
khura m. hoof (of a horse).

khe [loc. kha] ind. in the air. khecara var. khacara [cara] amnf khecarī that flies, that moves in the air — m. bird | mythical planet gandharva or vidyādhara or other divine messenger — f. cf. khecarī.
khecaratva [tva] n. (magical) power to fly.

khecarī [f. khecara] f. myth. np. of a vidyādharī | phil. [yoga] supernatural power [siddhi] of levitation | esoteric teaching; cf. khe carīmudrā | phil. [Trika] np. of Khecarī, śakti of Maheśvara | bd. [Tantra] Celestial goddess of the triad of the three worlds; cf. Bhūcarī, Pātālavāsinī.

khecarīmudrā [mudrā] f. phil. [yoga] position where the tongue, turned back to the back of the palate, enters through the gate of Brahmā | brahmadvāra | into the palatal cavity |kapālakuhara| to drink the amrta. kapālakuhare jihvā pravistā viparītagā | bhruvor an targatā dṛṣṭir mudrā bhavati Khecarī | [GS.] with the tongue turned back towards the top of the palate and the gaze directed on the space between the eyebrows, this posture is the Khecarī.

Khecarīvidyā [vidyā] f. lit. np. of the Khecarīvidyā, tantric work of haṭhayoga attributed to Adinātha₁; the teaching is revealed therein by a dialogue between Siva and Devī; it is prior to the 13th century, and has 4 sections | paṭala|.
khecarīsamatā [samatā] f. phil. [Trika] identification with Universal Consciousness.
khecarīsiddhi [siddhi] f. phil. [yoga] magical power to move in space (inner levitation); state of yogic hibernation, allowing one to live in long-term isolation.
kheṭa m. village, hamlet | med. phlegm; glands | myth. np. of Kheṭa, club of Balarāma — ifc. wretched (iic.).
khetaka [ka| m. small village, hamlet | inhabitant of a hamlet.
kheda [act. khid] m. fatigue; penalty; depression.
khedavaśa [vaśa] amnf khedavaśā under the worst of pain or fatigue; depressed.
kheya [pfp. [1] khan] amnf kheyā to dig — n. ditch.
√ khel v. [1] pr. (khelati) to tremble, to stir, to agitate; to sway | to play — ca. (khelayati) to agitate, to shake.
khela [agt. khel] amnf khelā that trembles, that stirs — act. f. khelā game, sport — v. [11] pr. (khelāyati) to play, to practice a sport.

khelana [act. khel] n. act of shaking, of fluttering | blinking (of the eyes) | pastime, game — f. khe lanā back-and-forth movement — f. khelanī piece in the game of chess. kavitvam kiyadaunnatyam cintāmanimanīsinah nipītakālakūṭasyaharasyevāhikhelanam | [Raghu nātha₁] He who is an expert in Cintāmaņi reaches the heights of poetry, as Shiva, having absorbed the black poison, plays with the serpents.

khottiga m. hist. np. of King Rāṣṭrakūṭa khottiga, half-brother of Kṛṣṇa₃ whom he succeeded in 967; his kingdom was invaded by King Paramāra Harşa₁ Sīyaka who sacked Mānyakheṭa in 972; his nephew Karka succeeded him briefly in 973, only to be dethroned by King Cālukya Tailapa₂.
khola mn casque; fabric head covering.
kholaka |ka| m. helmet.

√ khyā v. [2] pr. (khyāti) pft. (cakhyau) aor. [2] (akhyat) pp. (khyāta) pfp. (khyātavya) pf. (abhi, ā, pra, vi, sam) to look, to see — ps. (khyāyate) to be named, to be called — ca. (khyāpáyati) to make known, to say, to announce, to declare — des. (ci khyāsati) to mean, to mean to explain.
khyāta [pp. khyā] amnf khyātā named; called; known; famous, celebrated. devadattah iti khyātah named Devadatta.
khyātavya [pfp. [3] khyā] amnf khyātavyā to name; to say; to celebrate.

khyāti [act. khyā] f. declaration, assertion; opinion, view, idea | perception, knowledge notoriety, Fame, celebrity | myth. np. of Kyāti, Fame personified, daughter of Daksa, wife of Bhṛgu; Dhātā and Vidhātā are her sons.
khyāna [act. khyā] n. perception, knowledge | phil. conceptualization by naming.
khyāp [ca. khyā] v. [10] pr. (khyāpayati) pp. (khyāpita) to make known, to say, to announce, to declare.
khyāpaka [agt. ca. khyā ] ifc. amnf khyāpakā who makes known, who indicates; who confesses (iic.).
khyāpana [act. ca. khyā] n. declaration; disclosure; act of making known confession | celebration.
khyāpanīya [pfp. [2] ca. khyā] amnf khyāpanīyā which must be revealed; which must be confessed.
khyāpita [pp. ca. khyā] amnf khyāpitā declared; announced; confessed; denounced | celebrated.
khyāpin [agt. ca. khyā] ifc. amnf khyāpinī which reveals (iic.).
g
ga₁ |agt. gam| ifc. mf gā that goes to, that is in (iic.); that moves in (iic.) | place or season of, that relates to (iic.).
ga₂ [agt. gā₂] ifc. mf gī who sings (iic.) — nf gā song. sāmagaḥ singer of the Sāmaveda.
ga₃ [contr. guru] nota. phon. notation for a long syllable [guru] of one meter.
gakāra [(ga)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'ga'.
gagana n. sky | math. symb. the number 0. gaganakusumāni ci ["to pluck flowers from the sky"] to build castles in the air.
gaganaparidhāna [paridhāna] amnf gagana
paridhānā ["who has the sky as underwear"] completely naked.
gaganāravinda | aravinda | n. | "lotus in the sky" | non-existent thing; cf. śaśaviṣāṇa.
gagane [loc. gagana] iic.
gaganecara [cara] amnf gaganecarī who goes in the air — m. bird | planet.
ganga m. kind of suede | hist. n.p. of the ganga dynasty | iic. for Gangā.

gangadatta [datta] m. lit. [PT.] np. of gangadatta "Gift of the Ganges", king of frogs. [PT.] gangadattah punareti kūpam na ["gangadatta does not return to the well"] One does not make the same mistake twice.

gángā f. geo. np. of the Ganges river | myth. [gangādevī] the goddess Gangā who personifies it, eldest daughter of Himavān and Menā; her mount is the makara; she is represented holding a pūrņakumbha vase; she is often associated with Yamunā; cf. Jāhnavī, Bhāgīrathī, Varuṇa; she courted King Pratīpa by sitting on his thigh, but he declared that this place was reserved for his daughter or his son's wife; thus she married his son King Sāntanu, to fulfill the curse of the vasavas by Vasistha; she drowned her first 7 sons at birth, and left Bhīṣma alive so that he would embody Dyau.
Gangādāsa | dāsa | mr. hist. n.p. of Gangādāsa, to the creator of Chandomañjarī (14th century).

gangādevī [devī] f. hist. np. of gangādevī, poetess of the 14th century; she is credited with the poem Madhurāvijaya, which tells of the victory of her husband Kumāra Kampana over the Muslims at Madhurā; she is also called gangāmbikā.
Gangādvāra [dvāra] n. geo. np. of Gangādvāra "Gate of the Ganges", epith. of Haridvāra.

gangādhara [dhara] m. myth. np. of gangādhara, epith. of Shiva "Receiving the Ganges" (on his hair to prevent it from shattering the Earth); he caused the descent of the celestial Ganges [mandākinī] to Earth at the request of Bhagīratha; cf. Națarāja | hist. np. of the mathematician gangādhara₁, author of a commentary on the Līlāvatī | hist. np. of the poet and rhetorician gangādhara₂ Miśra (16th century) | hist. np. of the scholar gangādhara₃ Vājapeyī (17th century), author of the Avaidikadarśanasamgraha.
gangādharamūrti [mūrti] f. geo. bas-relief from Mahābalipuram representing the descent of the celestial Ganges.
gangāmbikā [ambikā] f. hist. n.p. of princess gangāmbikā; cf. gangādevī.
gangāyamunā [Yamunā] f. brass and copper alloy of the gangāyamune geo. the Gangā and the Ya munā.

gangālaharī [laharī] f. lit. np. of the poem gangālaharī "The Wave of the Ganges", which tells how its author Jagannātha₁ Paṇḍitarāja was washed clean of the sin of marrying a Muslim princess by the Gangā which carried him away in its waves while he was reciting it; at each stanza of the poem that he recited, a step became covered with water.
gangāvatara [avatara] m. myth. descent of the celestial Ganges to Earth; cf. Bhagīratha.

Gangesa [īśa] m. hist. np. of Gangesa or Gangesopādhyāya "Master of the Ganges", philosopher of the late 13th century originating from Bengal; he taught in Mithilā; he investigated the notions of truth and logical inference [prāmānya]; he is the author of the Tattvacintāmani, and thus founder [mūlagranthakāra] of the school of semiotics or new logic [Navyanyāya] of Mithilā; Vard hamāna₁ is his son.
Gangeśvara |īśvara| m. hist. np. of King Gangeśvara of Kalinga; cf. Anantavarmā. gangaikonda m. hist. np. of Gangaikonda, title of glory of King Rājendracola "who conquered the Ganges" (Tamil).
Gangaikondacolapura [colapura] n. geo. n.p. from Gangaikondacolapura, new capital of King Rājendracola, famous for its temple.
gangotrī [uttr̄] f. geo. np. of gangotrī, place of pilgrimage and glacier in the north of Uttar Pradesh, from which the Ganges originates; cf. Gomukha.
gangodaka | udaka | n. water of the Ganges. গ্ৰু gaccha [pr. gam] m. jn. family, race; Jain monastic order.
gacchat [ppr. gam] amnf gacchantī while going. gacchati kale var. dinesu gacchatsu over time.
√ gaj v. [1] pr. (gajati) pft. (jagāja) bellow, trumpet.
gaja [agt. gaj] m. elephant | math. symb. the number 8 (for the 8 celestial elephants) — f. gajī female elephant.
gajagati | gati | f. elephant's gait; (poetry) majestic gait | phon. name of a 4-foot, 8-syllable meter of the nabhalaga pattern. nabhalagā gajagatiḥ The gajagati meter is of the nabhalaga pattern.
gajagāmin |gāmin| amnf gajagāminī who has the (majestic) gait of the elephant — f. ga jagāminī woman with a majestic gait.
gajagraha | graha | mr. myth. [BhP.] np. crocodile

dile | makara | gajagraha, who attacked the elephant Gajendra; he was the gandharva king Huhu, cursed by the sage Devala for pulling his leg while he was invoking Surya during his sacred bath; he was freed from his curse by being beheaded by the cakra of Vișnu invoked by Gajendra.
gajatā [tā] f. elephantine condition | pl. multitude of elephants.
gajadaghná |daghna| amnf gajadaghnā f. gajadaghnī which has (water) up to the height of an elephant.
gajadanta | danta | m. elephant tusk; ivory | myth. epith. of Ganesa.
gajadantamaya [maya] amnf gajadantamayī in ivory.
gajadāna [dāna] n. bio. liquid exuding from the temples of the elephant in rut.

gajapati | pati | m. hist. np. of gajapati "Master of the elephants", dynastic title of the kings of Kataka, in Kalinga; cf. Pratāparudradeva | myth. |BhP.| one of the 4 cosmic elephants established by Brahmā to maintain the balance of the world: Rṣabha₁, Puṣkaracūḍa, Vāmana₁ and Aparājita₁; they stand on the Lokāloka mountain delimiting the world.
gajapippali | pippali | f. organic. bot. Scindapsus offi cinalis, philodendron, liana climbing along tree trunks; its fragrant fruits are used in medicine; syn. utkatā.
gajapṛṣṭhakṛṭi [pṛṣṭhakṛṭi] f. arch. “elephant-back” apse.

Gajamukha | mukha | amnf gajamukhī who has an elephant's head — m. myth. np. of Gajamukha, demon [asura] with an elephant's head; by his penances, he obtained a vow from Shiva, and asked him to live in his belly; Viṣṇu delivered him from it.
gajamedha [medha] m. soc. elephant sacrifice.
gajamela | mela | m. soc. gathering of elephants, a festival in Kerala, in January, not. in Kochi.
gajayuddha | yuddha | n. combat using an elephant. gajayuddhesu kuśalah expert in elephant combat.

gajalakṣmī [Lakṣmī] f. myth. "Lakṣmī with elephants", iconographic representation of the lustration of Lakṣmī by two elephants, representing the treasures of Kubera Padmanidhi and Sankhanidhi; it is generally found on the pediment of the threshold of access to the main sanctuary [garbhagrha] of a temple.
gajaśāstra [śāstra] n. lit. (veterinary) science of elephants.
gajasimha [simha] m. arch. motif of the lion overpowering the elephant, symbol of the victory of Hinduism over Buddhism.

Gajasūtra [sūtra] n. gram. np. of the Gajasūtra "Rule of the Elephant", np. of sūtra 1.3.67 of the Astādhyāyī, which prescribes the middle of the causative when the object of the verb becomes the agent in the causative.

gajānana [ānana] m. myth. np. of gajānana, epith. of Ganesa "elephant-headed". gajānanam bhūtaganādisevitam ka pitthajambūphalacārubhakṣanam śokavināśakārakam umāsutam namāmi vighneśvarapādapankajam || I honor you, elephant-headed master of the hordes of creatures, taking pleasure in eating the fruits of kapittha and jambu, son of Umā, destroyer of pains, lord of obstacles with lotus feet.
gajāsura [asura] m. myth. elephant demon Gaya₁, killed by Shiva; cf. Dārukavana | myth. elephant demon Nīla, killed by Ganesha.
gajāsurasamhāra [samhāra] m. myth. destruction of the elephant demon by Shiva; in iconography, Shiva is represented wearing its skin.

Gajendra [indra] m. chief of the elephants | myth. [BhP.] np. of Gajendra, king of the elephants of the Rtumat forest; went to bathe in the lake, he was seized by the leg by the crocodile [makara] gajagraha; unable to free himself, he implored Vișnu, who freed him and taught him that in a previous life he had been Indradyumna, cursed for having failed to respect Agastya; he symbolizes the man blinded by his pride and freed by faith [bhakti].

gajendramoksa [moksa] m. myth. [BhP.] liberation of the elephant Gajendra, trapped and threatened by a crocodile; he prayed to Vișnu for his salvation, and upon his arrival, gave him the lotus he had plucked with his trunk; it symbolizes the liberation of the devotee through prayer; cf. Hariharanātha — n. [gajendramokṣastotra] cf. gajendrastuti.
gajendramokṣaṇa [mokṣaṇa] n. bed. [Mah.] np. of the gajendramokṣaṇa, episode of the liberation of Ga jendra.

gajendrastuti [stuti] f. lit. hymn to the glory of Vishnu, invoked by the captive Gajendra; also ap pelé gajendramokṣastotra; it is the first śloka of the Visnusahasranāmastotra. śuklāmbaradharam viṣṇum śaśivarṇam caturb hujam | prasannavadanam dhyāyeta sarvavigh nopaśāntaye | [gajendrastuti] Be contemplated, O Vishnu with four arms, with the complexion of the moon, clothed in white, with a serene countenance, so that all obstacles may be lifted.

gañja | Persian | mn treasure room, casket, jewelry box — m. cattle market — f. gañjā tavern; liquor goblet | bio. bot. cannabis sa tiva, Indian hemp | soc. intoxicating mixture of resinous cannabis buds, ritually smoked in a clay pipe.
gada m. barrier | ditch. गাৰু gadu m. bump; goiter | superfluous or unsightly growth | bed. blister in poetry | hunchback.
gaḍḍārikā f. very slow river | sheep leading a flock.
gaddārikāpravāha | pravaha | m. flock of sheep in single file.
gaddārikāpravāhanyāya | nyāya | m. maxim equivalent to the sheep of Panurge.
gadha [Persian] n. fort, fortified city.
Gadhakālikā |kālikā| f. geo. np. of the temple of Gadhakālikā at Ujjayinī; it is said that Kālidāsa, as an idiotic child, received intelligence there.

√ gan v. [10] pr. (ganayati) aor. [3] (ajīgaṇat) pp. (gaṇita) pfp. (gaṇeya, gaṇya) abs. (gaṇayya) pf. (ava, vi) to count, enumerate, evaluate (à (i.)) to appreciate, count, estimate | to impute something (acc.) to someone (loc.) | to consider (acc.) as (acc.) | to attribute to (loc.) — ps. (ganyate) to be counted, to be valued. na gan not to care about, to neglect. na gaṇayāmi taṃ tṛṇena |Mah.| For me, it's not worth much.

gaṇá [act. gaṇ m. number; enumeration] troop, multitude; clan, tribe; crowd (of friends); group, class, suite | trade guild; not. guild of horse dealers | company, army division of three platoons [gulma], comprising 27 (3³) elephants and chariots, 81 cavalry and 135 infantry; cf. vāhinī | myth. the Gaṇa, troop of Shiva's servants; Ganesha is its leader; cf. Kuṣmāṇḍa | gram. present tense class of a Sanskrit verb; there are 10 of them | gram. class of words obeying a common rule; cf. gaṇapāṭha | phon. foot of measure, prosodic pattern of 3 syllables; There are 8 (2³), memorized by the formula yamātārājabhānasa lagā; thus 'ya' is the shortlonglong pattern (bachée), 'ma' the longlong pattern (molosse), 'ta' the longlongshort pattern (antibhachée), 'ra' the longshortlong pattern (amphimacre), 'ja' the shortlongshort pattern (am phibraque), 'bha' the longshortshort pattern (dactyl), 'na' the shortshortshort pattern (tribraque), 'sa' the shortshortshort pattern (anapeste), to which are added: 'la' the short syllable [laghu], and 'ga' the long syllable [guru]; thus the homosyllabic meter gajagati has 4 feet of 8 syllables of the same pattern nabhalaga. gaņakārikā [kārikā] f. pl. lit. np. of the Gaņakārikās of Haradattācārya, which expound the pāśupata doctrine; Bhāsarvajña made a commentary on it.
gaṇátā [tā] f. the act of forming a class or a multitude | the act of belonging to a party | classification | math. arithmetic.
ganátva |tva| n. id. |myth. belonging to Gana.
ganadhara | dhara | m. jn. leader of an assembly of wise men | rsi |.
gaṇanāyaka | nāyaka | mr. cf. Gaṇapati.
ganapati [pati] m. myth. np. of Ganapati, epith. of Ganesa, "the leader of the troop", who directs the Gana.
ganapatyatharvaśīrṣa [atharvaśīrṣa] n. lit. np. du gaṇapatyatharvaśīrṣa, late text glorifying Gaņeśa.
ganapātha |pātha| m. gram. collection of 261 word classes subject to idiosyncratic treatment in the tradition of Pāṇini.
Ganaratnamahodadhi [ratnamahodadhi] m. lit. np. from the Ganaratnamahodadhi "Ocean of treasures of lexical paradigms", gaṇapāṭha composed by Vardhamāna₁ in 1140.

ganasamgha [samgha] m. soc. chieftaincy, republican clan system of government; it appeared in the Ganges plain in the 6th century BC, and persisted until the middle of the 1st century when it was supplanted by a more centralized royal system [mahājanapada].
gaṇasūtra [sūtra] n. pl. gram. rules of inflection of word classes in the Aṣṭādhyāyī.

gaṇaka [agt. gaṇ] m. calculator, mathematician; astronomer — f. gaṇakā mathematician; female astronomer — f. gaṇakī wife of an astronomer — amnf gaṇikā bought at a high price — f. ganikā (rich) courtesan.
ganakayantra [yantra] n. mod. calculator; computer.
gaṇana [act. gaṇ] n. account, calculation, enumeration; taking into consideration — f. cf. gaṇanā.
gaṇanā [f. gaṇana] f. account, calculation, enumeration | taking into consideration; supposition; taking into account (g.). rājeti kā gaṇanā mama, what does it matter to me that he is king?
gaṇanāpati [pati] m. accountant.
gaṇanīya [pfp. [2] gaṇ] amnf gaṇanīyā calculable; possible to estimate.
gani iic. ganin.
ganipitaka [pitaka] n. jn. set of the 12 sacred works of the jaina canon |anga₁|.
gaṇikā [f. gaṇaka] f. (rich) courtesan | bio. cf. gaņikārikā.

ganikārī [ari] f. bio. bot. Premna corymbosa, a small tree of the verbena family, with simple opposite leaves, small greenish flowers in corymbs with a fetid odor; it is one of the 5 major medicinal roots | bṛhatpañcamūla|; syn. agni mantha | var. gaṇikārikā id. gaņikāvṛttasaṅgraha [vṛttasaṅgraha] m. lit. np. from the Ganikāvrttasangraha "Catalogue of the customs of courtesans", a collection of texts in Sanskrit dealing with prostitution.
gaṇita [pp. gaṇ] amnf gaṇitā counted, enumerated; calculated — n. sum, account; calculation; arithmetic.

Gaṇitakaumudī [kaumudī] f. lit. np. of the Ganitakaumudī "Clarification of Calculation"; this Treatise on mathematics is the work of the pandita Nārāyaṇa₂ (1356); this work is a precursor of combinatorial analysis.
ganitatilaka [tilaka] m. bed. n.p. from the mathematical text Gaņitatilaka, due to Srīpati₁; Simhatilaka Sūri commented on it.
ganitanyāya [nyāya] m. math. np. from the Ganitanyāya "Logic of calculation"; cf. Gaņitayuktibhāṣā.
ganitisantra [yantra] n. mod. computer.

ganitayuktibhāṣā [yuktibhāṣā] f. math. np. of the Ganitayuktibhāṣā "Demonstration of Calculation", Treatise on analysis and astronomy in Malayālam from 1530 due to Jyeşthadeva, expounding the theory of Mādhava₁, and dealing not. with trigonometric series; very ahead of its time, it provides proofs of the theorems.
ganitaśāstra [śāstra] n. math. science of calculation; computer science; mathematics.
ganitasāra [sāra] m. [“essence of calculation”] mathematics.
ganitasārasaigraha [saigraha] m. bed. n.p. from Mahāvīrācārya's Ganitasārasaigraha "Treatise on Mathematics" (c. 850).
gaṇín [agt. gaṇ] amnf gaṇinī who has an audience; who has helpers; surrounded by (i. iic.) — m. ["who has students"] teacher | jn. np. of Gaṇī, title of teacher.

gaṇeśa [gaṇaīśa] m. myth. np. of gaṇeśa "the Lord of Gana", god of knowledge and success, son of Shiva and Parvati; Parvati fashioned him into a little boy from the foam of an oil massage, and gave him life; he forbade Shiva from entering his bath, who in anger cut off his head; at Parvati's prayer, Shiva reattached the head of the first young animal found in the forest, which happened to be a baby elephant; he is invoked at the beginning of every undertaking, for "he triumphs over obstacles" [Vighnāntaka]; he is the patron of scholars, merchants and thieves; he is represented with a large belly and an elephant's head [Gajānana], often in a dancing pose, or seated as a scribe; In his right hand he holds the end of one of his tusks, used as a stylus (notably for writing the Mah. under Vyāsa's dictation), and in his left hand a sweet [modaka] of which he is greedy, or the plow [lāngala] which he took from Balarāma (during a battle where he broke his tusk); he also sometimes holds an axe [kuṭhāra] or a mahout's hook [ankuśa]; he has the rat [mūṣa] as his mount [Mūṣikavāhana]; his curved trunk symbolizes om; he must be worshipped first in the pradakṣiṇā; Candra having mocked him, he curses those who look at the moon on the day of ganeśacaturthī; As a brahmacārin, he is often depicted covered in vermilion [sindūra];

sometimes [SP.] he is said to be married to Buddhi and Siddhi₂; cf. Gaṇapati, Grāmaṇī, Vakratuṇḍa, Vighneśvara, Vināyaka, Heramba | hist. n.p. by Gaņeśa₁ Daivajña, 16th century astronomer, author of the Grahalāghava and the Buddhivilāsinī. namo ganeśāya vighneśvarāya lit. (preliminary invocation of a work) Glory to you, Ganesa who removes obstacles.

gaṇeśacaturthī | caturthī | f. soc. festival commemorating the birth of Ganesha, on the 4th day of the bright fortnight of the month bhādra; sweets [modaka] are prepared; clay statues of the god are carried in procession, which are then thrown into the river or the sea; it is said that whoever looks at the moon on this day incurs as a curse the suffering of false accusations; thus Kṛṣṇa was suspected of having stolen Syamantaka. gaņeśanāmāvali [nāmāvali] f. lit. litany of the 108 names of Ganesha.

ganeśavisarjana | visarjana | n. soc. rite of abandonment of the idol of Ganesa to the sea to the Mahārāṣṭra, during the anantavrata. ganesavesa vesa m. soc. decoration of the idols of Purī so that together they evoke Ganesa, after their ritual bath of snānapūrņimā; syn. hāthīveśa.

gaṇḍa m. cheek; side of the head, temple | gland, swelling, pimple; tumor; protuberance; goiter; viscera; bladder — mn lit. rhet. rapid exchange of questions and answers, characteristic of the dramatic style vīthi — ii. excellent, the best of the ifc. .

gandaka [ka] m. bio. zoo. rhinoceros; syn. khadgin — f. gandakī geo. np. of the gandakī river, which descends from the border with Tibet to flow through Nepal and then Bihar and join the Ganges at Hariharakșetra near Pațnā.
gandabheda [bheda] m. purse cutter.

gandabherunda [bherunda] m. myth. np. of gandabherunda "The most terrible", two-headed raptor born from the anger of Narasimha enraged after he had disemboweled Hiranyakasipu; at the request of the gods Shiva assumed the form of the śarabha to try to control it; after an 18-day battle Narasimha managed to overcome his anger, and the two gods resumed their identities | hist. two-headed eagle, emblem of several dynasties of South India, not. of the Wodeyar line of the kings of Mysore; it symbolizes strength, and is often depicted holding elephants in its talons; it appears on coins of Vijayanagara.
gandavyūha [vyūha] m. bed. n.p. of Gandavyūha, a bd dharmasūtra. |Mahāyāna|; his hero South Hana, disciple of Mañjuśrī, tours India to learn.
gaṇḍi [gaṇḍai] m. tree trunk | arch. (Orissa) syn. śikhara — f. gaṇḍī soc. wooden gong, used for rites bd.
gáṇya [pfp. [1] gaṇ] amnf gaṇyā to calculate; to consider | made up of sequences or lines (not. hymn).

gatá [pp. gam] amnf gatā gone, left (to (acc.); past, bygone; lost, absent; come, arrived | that goes as far as, going to (acc.); out, coming from (abl. iic.) | fallen into the condition of (loc. iic.) — n. setting out, departure; arrival | march, movement | the past — ifc. that is in or on (iic.); concerning. ātmagatam var. svagatam adv. apart, separately. evam gate adv. in this case. nagaram gatah went to town. snātum gatah went to bathe. gatagatā she has gone, alas! hastagata that is in the hands. kṣetragatā vṛkṣāḥ The trees in the field. bhāryāgatā cintā worry about her women.
gatatrapa [trapā] amnf gatatrapā who has no shame; who has no fear; bold.
gataprāṇa [prāṇa] amnf gataprāṇā ["whose breath has departed" | expired, dead.
gatáśrīka |śrīka| amnf gataśrīkā who has lost his prosperity, ruined.
gatasamkalpa |samkalpa| amnf gatasamkalpā without use.

gatāgata [āgata] amnf gatāgatā part and ar landed; one who enters and leaves; one who goes back and forth — n. act of going back and forth; repeated movement | astr. appearance and disappearance (star); growth and decline. gatāgatān kṛ enter into negotiations.
gatānugata [anugata] n. act of following custom, or the latest opinion.
gatānugati [anugati] f. act of following the preceding; act of following The old ruts.
gatānugatika |ka| amnf gatānugatikā who follows blindly. gatānugatiko lokaḥ [PT.] People are sheep of Panurge.
gatāyus |āyus| amnf death | "whose vital energy has departed".
gatārtha | artha | amnf gatārthā meaningless; without purpose.
gatāsu [asu] amnf ["who has expired"] death. gatāsūn agatāsūmsca nānusocanti paņditāḥ [BhG.] The wise do not mourn the dead nor the living.
gatavat [ppa. gam] amnf gatavatī who passes; who feels.

gáti [act. gam] f. walk, gait, pace; course, destination; power; progress | access, exit, refuge; means; expedient | origin, source; state, condition; situation (in a future life), destiny | gram. preposition used as a coreferential preverb to the action of the verb; also gati are some particles like alam, those of the genus |gaṇa| sākṣāt, and the inchoative forms |cvi| in ī or ū || ang. gait. grahāṇām gatiḥ astr. path of the planets. anyā gatirnāsti there is no other alternative. jagāma gatim agacchat he returned to his birth condition.
gatika |ka| n. movement, pace; course; condition.
gatikatva |vat| n. route potential. ananyagatikatvāt in the absence of an alternative.
gaticitra | citra | n. lit. variety of citrakāvya, where the poem is read by a series of movements in rows of letters; cf. gomūtrikā.
gatitva |tva| n. mobility.
gatipracāra [pracāra] m. practice of postures (of dance, yoga, rites, etc.) | lit. section of the Nāṭyaśāstra on postures.
gátimat |mat| amnf gatimatī that moves, mobile | gram. equipped with a preverb.
gatisamāsa |samāsa| m. gram. compound word formed with a prefix gati.
gátihīna [hīna] amnf gatihīnā abandoned, without refuge.
gatyartha | artha | amnf gatyarthā gram. is said of verbs of motion.

√ ; gad ; v. ; [1] ; pr. ; (gadati) ; pft. ; (jagāda) ; fut. ; r. (gadisyate) pp. (gadita) pfp. (gadya) pf. (ni) by ler; to say something to someone. (2 acc.) — ca. (gadayati) ton ner — des. (jigadiṣati) to want or wish by ler — intens. r. (jāgadyate) to speak forcefully or repeatedly. gad gad |onomatopoeia| imitates the cry not. of geese.
gada₁ [obj. gad] m. word, phrase | lit. [Mah.] np. of gada₁, son of Vasudeva, younger brother of Kṛṣṇa — f. gadā discourse.
gada₁ m. disease — n. poison | club — f. cf. gadā.
gadayitnu [yitnu] amnf loquacious, talkative; li bertin — m. myth. epith. of Kāma.
gadana |act. gad| n. act of speaking, of telling.
gadā [f. gada₁] f. club; mace; scepter | myth. not. scepter of Vișnu; cf. Kaumo dakī.
Gadādevī | devī | f. myth. np. of Gadādevī, personification of Kaumodakī, scepter of Viṣṇu; she is represented associated with CakrapurușaSudaréana.

gadādhara [dhara] m. hist. np. of the Bengali logician [naiyāyika] gadādhara Bhaṭṭācārya "(Master) bearer of the scepter" (17th century); he is the author of the semantic treatises Saktivāda, Muktivāda and Vyutpattivāda; he is also credited with numerous commentaries, known collectively as the Gadādharī | hist. np. of gadādhara₁ (15th century), author of traditional works [smṛti] hist. np. of gadādhara₂ Bhaṭṭa, son of Gauripati of Mithilā (17th century), author of the Rasikajīvana.
gadi [act. gad] m. discourse, language | sectarian tradition.
gadita [pp. gad] amnf gaditā spoken; said, uttered | to whom one addressed oneself | called, named — n. word.
gadin [gadāin] amnf gadinī who carries a staff (said not. of Kṛṣṇa).
gadgada [red. gad] amnf gadgadā stutterer — n. stuttering; incomprehensible speech — v. [11] pr. (gadgadyati) to stutter.
gadya [pfp. [1] gad] amnf gadyā which must be spoken or pronounced — n. lit. prose (opp. padya). gadyam kavīnām nikaṣam lit. |Vāmana₃| Prose is the touchstone of poets.
gadyakāvya | kāvya | n. lit. prose literature (not. poetry).

gantavya [pfp. [3] gam] amnf gantavyā that towards which one goes; where one must go; to be attained; that which must be accomplished or undertaken or suffered; with whom one can have carnal relations; that which can be accused of (i.) | that which will occur, imminent; inevitable | (impers.) one must go there. gantavyam let's go. mayā gantavyam I must go there.
gántu₁ [gamtu] m. way, route | traveler.
gantu₂ [inf. gam] iic. leave.
gantukāma [Kāma] amnf gantukāmā who is going to leave; about to leave.
gantumanas [manas] amnf who intends to leave. gantumanā'pi pathikah sankocam naivasithilayati [Bharścu] Although intending to leave, the traveler does not loosen his bedding.
gántṛ [agt. gam] amnf gantrī walker; who moves; who arrives at (acc.) | who goes towards a woman (loc.) for sexual purposes.

gandhá m. odor, scent; perfume | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the odor, perception [tanmātra] of the sense of smell [ghrāṇa]; it is governed [niyantr] by the pair of Aśvinau | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] the quality [guṇa] of the odor; 9 kinds of odors are characterized: iṣṭa₁ (pleasant), anista (unpleasant), madhura (sweet), kațu (acrid), nirhārin (diffusing), samhata (dense), snigdha (oily), rūkṣa (rough), viśada (pure); amla (acidic) is sometimes added — f. gandhā ifc. that which has the odor of just a Perfume of; small quantity of; small | relation, connection | pride; arrogance — f. gandhā cf. gandhapalāśī — n. Gandha smell.
gandhakuṭī [kuṭī] f. bd. chamber of the principal buddha of a monastery.
gandhagaja |gaja| m. elephant in rut.
gandhaghrāṇa [ghrāṇa] n. the act of smelling an odor.
gandhapalāśī | palāśī | f. organic. bot. Turmeric zedoa ria, ginger variety.

Gandhamādana [mādana] amnf gand hamādanā whose Perfume intoxicates — m. myth. np. of Mount Gandhamādana "with intoxicating perfumes"; east of Mount Meru, covered with a forest by smoke; it bears the palace of Kubera; Bhīma fought its guardians to bring back to Draupadī Fragrant Lotuses [saugandhika]; it is the devīpīṭha of Kāmukī; cf. Jaṭāsura | lit. [K.] np. of gand hamādana₁, elephant of the palace of King Tārāpīḍa — n. forest that covers Mount Gandhamādana.
gandhayukti [yukti] f. the composition of perfumes, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
gandhavat |vat| amnf gandhavatī Perfumed — f. gandhavatī myth. [Mah.] np. of Gandha vatī "the Perfumed One", epith. of Satyavatī after Parāśara had rid her of her fishy odor; cf. Kastūrīgandhī.
gandhavattva [tva] n. quality of being fragrant. gandhavattvam pṛthivyā lakṣaṇam phil. [Nyāya] The quality of having a smell is the characteristic sign of the earth.
gandhavaha [vaha] m. wind ["that carries odors"].
gandhaśāstra [śāstra] n. lit. science of cosmetics and perfumes.
gandhahastin [hastin] m. royal elephant Perfumed; cf. Gandhamādana.
gandhaka [Gandhaka] amnf gandhikā ifc. which has the smell of (iic.) — m. Perfume | sulfur.
gandhana [Gandhana] n. act of diffusing an odor.

gandharvá [Gandhava] m. Vedic np. from gand harva "Fragrant One", guardian of soma; he stands on the firmament and reveals Divine Truth in the form of a celestial rain; he dug the herb that cured Varuna of his impotence and revealed the Veda to Vāk | myth. (later, collectively) a centaur genius, celestial musician of Indra's paradise; the gandharvās were the guardians of soma, in the mythical time preceding Creation; Vāyu (or Varuna) is their king; they are sons of Kaśyapa and Munī (or sprung from the nose of Brahmā), and tireless lovers of the nymphs [apsarasas]; they are experts in medicine, and can possess humans (notably through epilepsy); they are associated with the fetus, and are invoked in marriage rites; Their mode of marriage [gāndharva] is clandestine love; they are depicted with a human torso and the body of a bird or horse; they inhabit the sky, regulate the course of the stars, and are associated with the nakṣatrāṇi; cf. Angāraparņa, Kṛśānu, Caṇḍavega, Citraratha, Citrasena, Tisya, Tumburu, Priyamvada, Bhrāja, Viśvāvasu, Sikṣa, Sāta, Supriya, Hāhā, Huhu; cf. kimnara — f. gandharvī myth. female gandharva; cf. Dundubhī, Puranjanī, Somadā | myth. np. of gandharvī, daughter of Surabhī; she gave birth to the race of horses | gr. Κενταυρος; fr. centaur; pali gandhabba.
gandharvagṛhīta [gṛhīta] afmn gandharvagṛhītā possessed by a gandharva; in a trance | epileptic.
gandharvagraha [graha] m. phil. [Tantra] possession by a centaur.

gandharvadatta [datta] amnf Gandharvadattā given by the gandharvās — f. Gandharvadattā lit. [Kathāsaritsāgara] np. of the beautiful Gandharvadattā, lover of Prince Naravāhanadatta, who won her in a vīṇā contest.
gandharvanagara [nagara] n. myth. splendid celestial city of the gandharvās | mirage.

gandharvayakṣā [yakṣa] m. pl. gandharvayakṣās myth. the genii of heaven [gandharva] and earth |yakşa|. gandhāra m. geo. land of gandhāra, in the northwest of ancient India, from the Ky ber pass to the Indus; its capital was Puṣkarāvatī, then Purușapura; its university of Takșaśilā was renamed; Pāṇini lived there; myth. king Subala reigned there | minium; vermilion; syn. sindūra | pl. gandhārās its inhabitants.
gandhālu [Gandhaālu] fragrant; Perfumed — m. perfumed rice.
gandhi [gandhin] ifc. amnf Perfumed with, smelling of (iic.) | evocative of, containing only traces of (iic.); (iic.) only of name.

gandhin [Gandhain] amnf gandhinī perfumed; fragrant — ifc. that smells of, perfumed to evoke of, that contains only traces of (iic.); (iic.) only by name. mātrgandhinī a mother only by name. ਸਮ gabhá [related to jabh₂] m. vulva.
gábhasti m. ray (of sun, of moon). ravigabhastayah rays of sunlight.
gabhastimat [mat] amnf gabhastimatī bright, resplendent — m. sun | myth. one of the 10 regions [dvīpa] forming the jambudvīpa.
gabhīrá var. gambhīra [gamīra] amnf gabhīrā deep; grave | serious; sagacious; so lennel, mysterious, secret | dense, impenetrable; inscrutable; unfathomable | (time) inexhaustible, inexhaustible.

(ati, adhi, anu, antar, apa, api, abhi, ava, astam, ā, ut, upa, ni, nis, parā, pari, pra, prati, vi, sam) to go, to move, to walk; go into | go towards; become, fall into (acc.); get; to arrive at, to access, to reach (loc.); to encourage | to leave, to go away, to disappear — ca. (gamáyati) ca. r. (gamayate) to make go, to set in motion, to lead, to send | to communicate (idea); to explain (meaning), to denote | to pass (time, days) — ps. (gamyate) to have gone, to have left; to be understood — des. (jigamiṣati) des. r. (jigamiṣate) des. (jigamṣati) des. r. (jigamṣate) to want to go | to aim for, to strive to obtain; to want to bring — intens. r. (jangamyate) to walk in a crooked manner | lat. ve nio; all. kommen; ang. to come; fr. venir. gamyatām please go. tvam grāmam gaccheh go to the village. astam gam disappear behind the horizon; to lie down (star). to prostrate oneself. to perceive. to beg. to ask for alms; to beg. to die. to faint. when the time comes. who is old enough to approach a woman. to be able to approach a woman. to lead us from nothingness to Being; to lead us from darkness to Light; to lead us from death to Eternity.

gama |act. gam| m. course; walk; journey | departure of abl. | sexual intercourse with iic. — agt. f. gamā ifc. that which goes to, that which becomes (iic.); that which goes by, that which rides (iic.) | having as first, preceded by (iic.).
gamāgama |āgama| m. back and forth; coming and going | pl. negotiations, discussions.
gamāgamika |ika| m. soc. police officer monitoring the comings and goings in a city.

gamaka |agt. gam| amnf gamaikā that clarifies, that explains, that makes intelligible; convinces cant | that indicates (g.) — m. phil. sign provoking the understanding of the object to be understood [gamya] — n. (mus.) grave tone.
gamakatā [tā] f. the state of being convincing intelligibility.
gamakatva |tva| n. id.

gamana [act. gam] n. ["act of going"] walk, gait; departure; movement, journey | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] the activity [karman] of movement — ifc. (agt. (g.)) going to (iic.) — agt. amnf ga manā ifc. who has sexual relations with (iic.). rāmasya vanagamana departure of Rāma for the woods.
gamanāgamana [āgamana] n. round trip; back and forth.
gamanīya [pfp. [2] gam] amnf gamanīyā where one can or should go; accessible — ifc. which consists of, relating to (iic.).
gamin [agt. gam] ifc. amnf gaminī who has to go, who is going to go to (acc. iic.).
Gambhan n. depth.
gambhára [gambhanra] n. depth.

gambhārī f. bio. bot. Gmelina arborea, gamhar tree, of the verbena family, with opposite heart-shaped leaves, with brownish-yellow spike flowers; it can reach 20 m; it is one of the 5 major medicinal roots [brhatpañcamūla] | its flower; its fruit; its root.
gambhiṣṭha [super. gambhīra] amnf gambhisthā the deepest.

gambhīrá var. gabhīra [gamīra] amnf gambhīrā profound; grave, impenetrable, respectable; solemn, mysterious, secret — m. geo. np. of the gambhīra temple in Purī, where Caitanya spent the last years of her life — f. gambhīrā geo. [MD.] "Deep", np. of the gambhīrā river in Mālava. trigambhīra amnf trigambhīrā is said of a man whose navel, voice, and character are profound.
sakalakalāgamagambhīrah [Bāṇa] (family) having a deep knowledge of all the arts or (ślesa) (flow of the celestial Ganges) deep in its tumultuous fall.
gambhīratā [tā] f. depth.
gambhīratva [tva] n. id.
gambhīriman [iman] m. depth.
gambhīreśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Gambhīreśvara "Lord of the depths", epith. of Shiva.
gamya [pfp. [1] gam] amnf gamyā that one can frequent; dissolute | perceptible; accessible; understandable | phil. that must be understood; opp. gamaka.
gamyatā [tā] f. accessibility; the state of being perceptible, intelligibility.

gáya [obj. ji] m. ["that which has been conquered"] property, goods, riches | myth. np. from the rājarṣi Gaya "Spoils"; he celebrated many sacrifices [yajña] in all the holy places; [Mah.] he offered the Pāṇḍavās five aśvamedha on the banks of the Payoṣṇī | myth. np. from the asura Gaya₁; he manifested himself in the form of a furious elephant that attacked some sages [muni]; they took refuge in a shrine of Shiva; Shiva killed the elephant with his trident and draped himself in its hide as in a cloak; cf. Dārukavana, gayāsura — f. cf. Gayā.
gáyadāsa [dāsa] m. hist. n.p. by the physician Gayadāsa, author of a commentary on the Suśrutasamhitā.

Gayā [f. Gaya] f. geo. np. of the city of Gayā "Richness", famous pilgrimage site in Bihāra (mod. Bodhgayā); soc. one must practice the śrāddha rite to his manes [pitaras] at least once in one's life; bd. Buddha received Enlightenment [bodhi] there.

gayāsura [asura] m. myth. [AP.] np. of the demon gayāsura, who had acquired great power by the rigor of his penances; Vișnu granted him the vow that his residence [Gayā] should become the most sacred place of pilgrimage; he placed his foot on his chest to subjugate him; this place, marked with the imprint of Vișnu's foot in a block of ba salte, is revered in the temple of Visnupada.
gara [obj. gr₁] mn ["that which is swallowed"] drink its poisoned | astr. fifth lunar half-day [karana] (mobile).
garaṇa [act. gr₁] n. action of swallowing.
gariman [guruiman] m. weight, heaviness; importance, respectability — f. garimā phil. [Yoga] the power to become heavy, a siddhi.
gariṣṭha [super. guru] amnf gariṣṭhā very heavy; the heaviest | very important; the most important.

garīyas [compar. guru] amnf garīyasī heavier than, greater than, more important than (abl.); more expensive than | very heavy, very large; very venerable — n. great weight; importance. padagauravād yogavibhāgo garīyān |Nāgoji| The multiplication of rules is more costly than the prodigality of words. apisvarṇamayī laṅkā na me Lakṣmaṇa rocate | jananī janmabhūmiśca svargādapi garīyasī || |Rāma| Even if Ceylon were all gold, O Laksmana, it could not please me, for the mother and the homeland are preferable even to paradise.

garīyastara |tara| amnf garīyastarā compar. extremely heavy; very important. ন্ত garuḍa [gr̄1] m. myth. np. of the mythical eagle Garuda "(Sun) that Devours", son of Kaśyapa and Vinatā, younger brother of Aruṇa [aruṇānuja]; at his birth he frightened the gods by his brilliance; he is king of birds and destroyer of serpents of which he is affamé (Nāgāntaka, Nāgāśana); [Mah.] Kaśyapa showed him at the bottom of a lake an elephant and a tor tue engaged in fighting over an inheritance, and which he devoured; He stole the ambrosia [amṛta] to give it to the serpents who held his mother captive, but a trick allowed Indra to get it back; he is the
mount [vāhana] of Viṣṇu from whom he obtained immortality provided that he did not drink amrta; he is father of Vālmīki and Dīpaka; he protects from poisons; cf. Tārkṣya, Vainateya, Suparņa.
garudadhvaja [dhvaja] m. arch. Garuda support column.

garudapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. soc. du np. Garuḍapurāṇa or Gāruḍapurāṇa, traditional encyclopedic work of Vaishnava obedience, in 200 chapters [adhyāya] (between 6th and 11th century); it deals with rites and festivals, expiatory ceremonies, the glorification of holy places, but also with science, medicine, divination, grammar and politics; cf. sāttvika.
garut mn aile.
garútmat [mat] m. eagle | myth. np. of Garutmān, great eagle, epith. of Garuda.

garga m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] garga Bhāradvāja; [BhP.] he was chaplain [purohita] to the Yādavā princes, and dedicated the children Kṛṣṇa and Ba larāma to Vraja | hist. np. of garga₁, ancient astronomer/astrologer (1st century), author of the Gārgīyajyotiṣa; he is also called Vṛddhagarga; this name probably covers several people; 34 works of jyotisa are associated with this name — f. gargī [gārgī] lit. [BU.] np. of gargī, ancient philosopher, daughter of the sage Vacaknu; she posed the most difficult questions about the Absolute [brahman] to Yājñavalkya.
gargasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. bed. n.p. of the Gargasaṃhitā, compendium of astronomy later than the Gārgīyajyotişa.
