√ garj v. [1] pr. (garjati) pp. (garjita) to rumble (thunder); growl, roar, trumpet.
garja [agt. garj] m. elephant (that trumpets) | trumpeting; rumbling (storm).
garjana [act. garj] n. rumble of thunder, roll of thunder | growl; trumpeting, roaring.
garjita [pp. garj] amnf garjitā who growled or growled — n. thunder; cry, growl; trumpeting.
gárta [gṝ₁ta] mnf gartā hole, pit; terrier; ditch; cave.

gartavartin | vartin | amnf gartavartinī (ani mal) residing in its burrow. gartavartigodhāmāṃsāvibhajananyāyaḥ maxim of sharing the flesh of an iguana while it is still in its burrow; equivalent to selling the bear's skin before killing it.
√ gard v. [1] pr. (gardati) to shout; bray.
garda [agt. gard] amnf gardā who cries; who brays.

gardabhá [bha] m. bio. zoo. donkey; syn. khara, rāsabha — f. gardabhī bio. jenny — n. bio. sca rabée dung beetle. ghatam bhittvā patam chittvā kuryādvā gar dabhasvanam | yenakenāpyupāyena prasiddhaḥ purușo bhāva || By breaking pots, tearing their clothes, or even braying like a donkey, in one way or another everyone strives to find a way to become famous.
gardebhakṣīra [kṣīra] n. donkey milk.
gardebhila m. hist. n.p. of gardabhila or Gardabhilla, father of Vikramāditya | pl. hist. dy nastie of the Gardabhilās.
gardha [act. gṛdh] m. desire, longing (for (iic.)) | greed. atigardhena through excessive greed.
gardhin [agt. gṛdh] amnf gardhinī eager for; who desires; who longs for.

gárbha [gr̄1] m. interior of something; private apartment; sanctuary | womb; maternal breast; living germ; embryo, fetus. Soc. consecrated deposit in a temple under construction | [jalagarbha] va atmospheric fears, dew | riverbed | [garbhasandhi] lit. [theater] knot of the plot; it is one of the 5 articulations of dramatic narratives [pañcasandhi] — ifc. containing, enclosing, full of, heavy with (iic.) | all. kalb; ang. calf. garbham dadhānāh bearing fruit. kṣīragarbhaṃ ghaṭam a pot full of milk. ratnagarbhah syūtah a bag full of jewels. abde garbhād ekādaśa in the 11th year after conception.
gárbhagrha | grha | n. interior apartment; sanctuary of a temple, cella.
gárbhatā [tā] f. the state of being impregnated [jalagarbhatā] with the moisture of dew.
gárbhatvá [tva] n. id.
garbhanirodhaka [nirodhaka] m. mod. condom.
gárbhapurodāśa [purodāśa] m. soc. cake of offering for the embryo, offered after a paśupurodāśa if the sacrificial animal is pregnant.
garbhavatī [vat] f. (woman) pregnant; (cow) full.
garbhavadha | vadha | mr. abortion.
garbhastha [stha] amnf garbhasthā inside the womb (embryo) | inside g. .
garbhasthasamāsa [samāsa] m. gram. compound word internal to another compound word (this one being called samāsagarbhita).
garbhasrāva [srāva] m. miscarriage.
garbhahatyā [hatyā] f. abortion.
garbhānka [anka] m. lit. [theatre] interlude; play within a play.

garbhādhāna [ādhāna] n. impregnation (of (loc.)) soc. reception of the embryo, a rite [saṃskāra] of fertility between spouses performed before conception soc. rite of consummation of the marriage, after her menarche, of a woman previously ritually married before her puberty.
garbhāvakrāntisūtra [avakrāntisūtra] n. bd. n.p. of the Garbhāvakrānti sutra relating to conception.
garbhāśaya [āśaya] m. med. uterus.
garbheśvara [īśvara] amnf garbheśvarī rich by birth — m. prince by birth — f. garbheśvarī princess by birth.

garbhodaka [udaka] n. med. amniotic waters myth. np. of garbhodaka, great primordial ocean of the Universe, where Seșa remains after the annihilation of the worlds | pralaya|; | BP.| Hiranyākṣa plunged the Earth into it, which was saved from the Waters by ViṣṇuVarāha.
garbhodakaśāyin [śāyin] m. myth. np. of Garb hodakaśāyī, epith. of Viṣṇu "Resting on the Primordial Waters".
garbhita [garbhaita] amnf garbhitā in terne; nested; embedded, inserted, encapsulated — ifc. filled with, containing (iic.). garbhitāḥ śālayaḥ ripe rice.
garbhitatā [tā] f. gram. rhet. embedding of one sentence within another.
garbhitatva [tva] n. id.
garbhin [garbhain] amnf garbhinī filled with (acc. i.); fertilized — f. garbhiṇī pregnant woman — f. garbhiṇī ifc. beast (iic.) fertilized female. gogarbhinī f. pregnant cow.
garva m. pride; arrogance, vanity; arrogance | [theatre] arrogant speech — v. [11] pr. (garvayati) pp. (garvita) to make proud — v. [11] pr. r. (garvāyate) to be proud, to be vain; to be arrogant.
garvabandha | bandha | mr. humiliation.
garvita [pp. garva] amnf garvitā or proud, vain, haughty; proud of (i. iic.) — n. pride.
garvin [agt. garva] amnf garviṇī vain man; fat. alpavidyo mahāgarvī | SRBh. | Fools are excessively vain.
√ garh v. [1] pr. r. (garhate) v. [10] pr. (ga rhayati) aor. r. [5] (agarhiṣṭa) pp. (garhita) pf. (vi) to complain about (to (dat.)); to reproach; to accuse, to blame.
garhaṇa [agt. garh] amnf garhaṇā implying a reproach — act. n. blame, reproach; censure — f. garhaṇā id. garhaṇāṃ yā to incur the reproach.
garhaṇīya [pfp. [2] garh] amnf garhanīyā blameworthy; to be blameworthy.
garhita [pp. garh] amnf garhitā blamed (by (ig loc. iic.)); despised.

√্যাল্ gal v. [1] pr. (galati) pp. (galita) pf. (vi) to flow, to drip, to leak, to escape; to drip, to flow | to vanish, to disappear | to swallow — ca. (gālayati) to drain, to filter, to press — intens. (jalgalīti) to swallow repeatedly, to lap up.
gala [agt. gal] m. ["who swallows"] throat, neck. pāśārpitagala amn with the rope around the neck.
galagraha [graha] m. act of seizing by the throat | sore throat | throat-irritating sauce | embrace.

galita [pp. gal] amnf galitā that drips, fallen, run off; exhausted, weakened; degraded, rotten; lost | lit. qualifies dubious passages of the Veda. angam galitam palitam mundam dasanavihīnam jātam tundam | vṛddho gṛhītvā daṇḍam tadapi na muñcati āśā piṇḍam || [Saṅkarācārya] His body has slumped, his hair is gray, his teeth have fallen out, the old man walks with a stick, and yet he does not renounce his desires.
galitaka |ka| m. gesticulation | lit. towards prakrit uti reading the ambiguity visàvoir du sanskrit.
galitakuṣṭha [kuṣṭha] n. med. advanced leprosy, where the fingers and toes fall off.
√ galbh v. [1] pr. r. (galbhate) pf. (pra) to be resolute; to be bold, to be intrepid.
galla |gaṇḍa| m. cheek.
gavi iic. go.
gavaya | aya | mr. organic. zoo. Bos Gaurus, wild gaur; zoo. Bos Frontalis, gayal; zoo. Bos gavaeus, domestic ox | lat. gavaeus. aranyagavayah organic. wild gaur.
gavis | is₃ | amnf eager, anxious, fervent.
gavisti [iṣti₁] f. ardor, fervor | desire to fight; conflict, battle; war. gaveșa [eṣa₂] ifc. amnf givenṣā who seeks, who desires.

gávyūti |yūti| f. ved. pasture | district; territory; place of residence | measure of distance; cf. gavyūta — n. gavyūta surveying measure, worth 8 leagues | krośa | or 4000 fathoms | daṇḍa | (approximately 8 km).
gava [go] f. gavī ifc. cow of (iic.) — iic. (iic.) of cow.
gavākṣá |akṣa| mn arch. bull's-eye, circular decorative element of a pediment or a niche; decorative trellis, louvers | mesh (of chainmail).
gavākṣajāla |jāla| n. trellis; grid; openwork wall.
gavāhnika [āhnika] n. ration (of fodder) for one day for a bovine.
gavendra [indra] m. bull.
gavām [g. pl. go] iic.

gavāmayana [ayana] n. astr. ["journey of the cows"] period of one year, journey of the sun through the different signs of the zodiac | soc. great sacrifice of soma [sattra] of one year; it ends with the ceremony of the mahāvrata followed by the atirātra; cf. abhiplava | soc. collective sacrifice marking a sotice sol.
gavāśva [aśva] n. sg. (collective) cows and horses.
gaves [vn. gavesa] v. [1] pr. r. (gavesate) pp. (gaveṣita) v. [10] pr. (gaveṣayati) to seek; inquire about (acc.).
gaveṣaka [agt. gaveṣ] amnf gaveṣikā dear choir — f. gaveṣikā mod. search engine.
gavéṣaṇa [agt. gaveṣ] amnf givenṣaṇā Who ardently desires | ved. Who desires to fight — act. n. quest, search; ardent desire; not. desire for combat — f. gaveṣaṇā id.
givenṣaṇīya [pfp. [2] gaveṣ] amnf givenṣanīyā Worthy of being sought.
gaveṣita [pp. gaveṣ] amnf gaveṣitā re cherché.
gaveṣin [agt. gaveṣ] ifc. amnf gaveṣiṇī Who seeks (iic.).
gaveṣṭha [great. go] m. myth. n.p. of dānava Gavestha | var. gavesthin myth. n.p. of the dānava gaveșțhī "to the Supreme Word", son of Prahlāda; he is father of Sumbha and Nisumbha.
gávya [goya] amnf gavyā from the cow; bovine, relating to cattle | One who honors cattle — n. herd of cows | cow's milk; beef — f. gavyā desire for cow or milk.
gavyacikitsā | cikitsā | f. veterinary medicine of livestock.
gavyú |u| amnf Who desires or appreciates the cow or the milk | ved. Who desires the fight.
√ gah [related to gāh] v. [10] pr. (gahayati) to sink deeply into it.

gáhana [agt. gah] amnf gahanā thick, deep; impenetrable; confused, incomprehensible; inexplicable — n. hiding place, thicket; inaccessible place — v. [11] pr. r. (gahanāyate) to wait in the shadows with ill intentions. gahanīkṛ to make inaccessible. karmano gahanā gatih the ways of fate are impenetrable.
gahanatva |tva| n. inaccessibility.

gáhvara [gahvara] amnf gahvarā f. gah varī deep; unfathomable, impenetrable; unexplain cable, obscure — m. arbor, grove — n. hiding place, thicket; cavern; abyss | secret; enigma; hy pocrisia — f. gahvarī cave, cavern.

√ gā₁ [related to gam] v. [3] pr. (jigāti) aor. [1] (agāt) pfp. (gāya) pf. (ati, adhi, abhi, pari) to go, to come; to arrive, to leave | to approach (acc. loc.) || ang. to go. mā gāḥ inj. does not go.

√ gā₂ var. gai v. [1] pr. (gāyati) pft. (jagau) pp. (gīta) ppr. ps. (gīyamāna) pfp. (geya) pf. (ut, upa, pra, vi, sam) to sing; to celebrate by singing — ps. (gīyate) to be sung, to be invoked — intens. r. (jegīyate) to be praised by song | to be affirmed obstinately. gāyam gāyam having sung and sung.
Gānga [*gangā] amnf gāngī on the Ganges, near the Ganges; concerning the Ganges — m. myth. np. of Gānga, matr. of Bhīsma or Kārttikeya Skanda.
gāṅgāyani [*gaṅgāāyani] m. myth. epith. of Bhīṣma or KārttikeyaSkanda "from the Ganges".
gāṅgeya [*gaṅgāeya] amnf gāṅgeyā re latif au Gange — m. myth. épith. de Bhīṣma "son of gangā" | épith. de Skanda "descended from the Ganges".
gājara m. mod. bot. Daucus carota, carrot.
gāḍha [pp. gāh] amnf gāḍhā plunged, im merged | fixed, tight, held; intense. gādham adv. closely, firmly | very, strongly; intensely.
gāna [gā₂na] n. chant.
gāṇapatya [*gaṇapatiya] amnf gāṇapatyā relating to Gaṇeśa | devotee of Gaṇeśa — n. command of a troop.
gānika [*gaṇaika] amnf gāṇikā myth. Relating to Gana.
Gāṇḍīva [gāḍha] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Gāṇdīva "Held firmly", magic bow of Varuna; he held it from Soma, and gave it to Agni to lend to Arjuna | var. gāndiva id.
gāṇḍīvadhanvan [dhanvan] m. myth. epith. of Ar juna "Who has Gāṇḍīva as his bow".
gātu₁ [gā₁tu] m. movement; trajectory; space where to move; place of residence; refuge | progress; well-being.
gātu₂ [gā₂tu] m. singer — angry amnf.
gātṛ |agt. gā₂| f. gātrī cantor.
gātra [instr. gā₁] n. member ["instrument of movement"; body.
gātravat [vat| amnf gātravatī Who has a beautiful, slender body.
gātha [gā₂tha] m. singing | verse, stanza — f. cf. gāthā.
gātháśravas | śravas | m. myth. epith. of Indra "whose glory is celebrated by hymns".
gāthaka [agt. gā₂] amnf gāthikā singer (by profession).
gāthā |f. gātha| f. hymn; sacred song; lyric stanza | lit. meter of poetry of the prakrit, comptant the prosodic patterns |gana| | lit. section of the Avesta (Mazdaean sacred text of ancient Persia).
gāthāratnakośa [ratnakośa] m. bed. n.p. from Gāthāratnakośa, an anthology of Prakrit verses in Gāthā style by Jineśvara (1194).
gāthālakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. lit. np. from gāthālakṣaṇa "Definition of gāthā", treatise on metrics by Nan ditādhya (10th century).

gāthāsaptaśatī [saptaśatī] f. lit. np. of the gāthāsaptaśatī or Saptaśataka collection of poems in prākṛtī of the Mahārāṣṭra, dealing with the torments of love, in a pastoral setting; attributed to King Hāla, they are prior to the 6th century; 7 recensions are known.
gāthín [gāthain] amnf gāthinī familiar of hymns, Singer — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Gāthī "Singer", father of Viśvāmitra; cf. gādhi |pl. gāthinas myth. the descendants of Gāthīgādhi.
gādha [related to gāh] amnf gādhā shallow, where one can stand — n. ford | lat. vadum; fr. gué.
gādhi iic. gādhin.
Gādhipura [pura] n. geo. np. of the city of Gādhipura, presumed capital of the gādhi king, and birthplace of Viśvāmitra [Rām.]; cf. Kanyākubjā.

gādhin [related to gāthin] m. Singer | gādhi myth. [Mah.] np. of the king gādhi "Singer", in incarnation of Indra, son of KuśanābhaKuśika, king of Kānyakubja; he is father of Satyavatī₁ and Viśvāmitra; in his old age he left his crown to Viśvāmitra, and retired to the hermitage of his son-in-law Ŗcīka | pl. myth. descendants of gādhi.
gāna [gā₂na] n. chant, song.
gāndinī f. myth. np. of gāndinī, princess of Kāśī, wife of Svaphalka and mother of Akrūra; cf. Nandinī₁.

gāndharva [*gandharva] amnf gāndharvī relating to the gandharvās soc. describes the mode of marriage of love "in the gandharva style", by mutual consent of the lovers (often clandestine) — n. music, song, concert. gāndharvarākṣasau kṣatre dharmyau tau mā
viśankitāḥ [Mah.] It is undeniable that marriages in the style of the gandharvās or rākṣasās are appropriate to the warrior class.
Gāndharvaveda | veda| m. lit. from the np. Gāndharvaveda "Science of music", an upaveda; it has its origins in the Sāmaveda.
gāndharvavedasāra [sāra] m. bed. n.p. from gāndharvavedasāra, a short musical treatise by Dattila.

gāndhāra [*gandhāra] m. geo. the country of Gandhāra | minium; vermilion | (mus.) 3rd note of the Indian octave | pl. gāndhārās the inhabitants of Gandhāra — f. gāndhārī hist. language and culture of Gandhāra | myth. [Mah.] np. of Gāndhārī, daughter of King Subala of Gandhāra, wife of the blind King Dhṛtarāṣṭra; out of respect for her husband, she lived with a blindfold over her eyes; the sage Vyāsa had promised her that she would have 100 sons; After a two-year pregnancy, she gave birth to a solid lump of flesh, which Vyāsa distributed among 100 jars, resulting in 100 sons (plus one daughter, Duḥśalā, from the remnant); her eldest, Duryodhana, became the leader of the Kauravās army; through her devotion to Shiva and her vow of blindness, she had acquired great powers; one day a hole in her headband revealed Yudhisthira's toe, which turned black; she cursed Kṛṣṇa for the loss of her 100 sons, prophesying the end of the Yādava line; she ended her life in the Himalayas with her husband and her devoted daughter-in-law, Kuntī; they perished in a forest fire.
gāndhika [*gandhaika] m. perfumer | soc. mixed-caste man; employee — f. gāndhikī perfumer.

gāmin [agt. gam] amnf gāminī who goes everywhere — ifc. who goes, who leads to, who reaches, who obtains (iic.) | who moves like (iic.) | directed towards; related to (iic.) | vassal of (iic.). hamsagāmin amn who walks like a goose.
gāmbhīrya [*gambhīraya] amnf gāmbhīryā which is in a deep place — n. depth; thickness (water, sound) | depth of character; dignity, calm, height of view.
gāya [gā₁ya] ifc. amnf gāyā who goes, who travels.
gāyaka |agt. gā₂| amnf gāyikā who sings — m. singer — f. gāyakī singer.
gāyakavāda [marathi] m. hist. np. of the Marathi clan Gāyakavāḍa, which conquered the state of Vado darāBaroda in 1721; mod. Gaekwad.
gāyatra [*gāyatrīa] n. song, hymn in gāyatrī meter.

Gāyatrī₁ [contr. gāyantamtrāyate] f. Vedic meter (3 times 8 syllables) | lit. one of the most sacred hymns of the Rigveda, by Viśvāmitra, praising Savitā the rising sun at dawn; it is called sāvitrī at midday, and sarasvatī at sunset; every Aryan must recite it evening and morning, facing the sun |saṃdhyā|; it is also recited during the |saṃskāra| ceremony of initiation |upanayana| | myth. np. of Gāyatrī₁ "She Who Sings", divine incarnation of this liturgical formula, patroness of poetry, wife of Brahmā; cf. sarasvatī | myth. np. of the horse Gāyatrī₁, harnessed to the chariot of Sūrya. tát savitúr várenyam bhárgo devásya dhīmahi dhíyo yó nah pracodáyāt | [RV.] Let us meditate on the resplendent light of the divine sun, so that it inspires our thoughts.
gāyana [agt. gā₂] mf gāyanī singer.
gāruda [*Garuda] amnf gārudā relating to or from Garuda — n. emerald.

gāruḍatantra [tantra] n. lit. [Ayurveda] np. of the Gārudatantra, a branch of literature of śaiva obedience associated with Garuda, and dealing with antidotes to snake bites and other poisons, and their treatment by recitation of formulas [mantra] and preparation of remedies based on plants and minerals.
gārudapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. cf. garudapurāṇa.

gārga [*garga] amnf gārgī composed of garga — f. gārgī soc. wife of a Gārgya₁ | lit. [BU.] np. of gārgī Vācaknavī, Who embarrassed Yājñavalkya with his questions; also called Gargī — m. gārgi soc. son of garga.
gārgi [*gargai] m. son of garga.
gārgīya [*gargaīya] amnf gārgīyā relating to garga or garga₁.
Gārgīyajyotisa [jyotisa] m. astr. from the np. Gārgīyajyotisa, a treatise on astrology from the 1st century due to garga₁, also called Vṛddhagargasaṃhitā.

Gārgya₁ [*gargaya] m. soc. np. patr. of Gārgya₁ "descendant of garga" (from the grandson); this name gotra is valid for an ancestor [vrddhi], but is pejorative for a young [yuvan] emancipated during the lifetime of his father | hist. np. of Gārgya₁ Bālāki — ifc. soc. (after num.) bought in exchange for as many women from the clan of garga.

Gārgyāyaṇa [*Gārgya₁āyana] mf gārgyāyaṇī myth. np. patr. of Gārgyāyaṇa "son of Gārgya₁"; it also applies to a younger brother [yuvan] if his elder brother Gārgya₁ is alive, or has honorific value for a Gārgya₁.
gārdabha [*gardabha] amnf gārdabhā relating to donkeys.
gārbha [*garbha] amnf gārbhā relating to the embryo, to pregnancy.
gārbhika [ika] amnf gārbhikā relating to the matrix; prenatal.
gārṣṭeya [*gṛṣṭieya] amnf gārṣṭeyī (calf or young animal) firstborn of a heifer.
gārha iic. grha.
gārhamedha [medha] m. soc. domestic sacrifice.
gārhapata [*gṛhapati] n. soc. rank of master of house.

gārhapatya [*gṛhapatiya] amnf gārhapatyā relating to the master of the house — m. soc. domestic sacred fire; it is lit to the west of the sacrificial area ved. | vedi | with the fire stick | arani | ; it must burn day and night; during the agnihotra, the milk is heated in it before being offered in the fire āhavanīya; during the sacrifice [iṣṭi₂] the wife of the master of the house [yajamānī] makes the offerings there — n. state of master of the house.
gārhastha [*gṛhastha] amnf gārhasthā relating to the master of the house — n. soc. state of head of family, 2nd stage [āśrama] of the brahmanic life.

gālava [*galava] m. bio. bot. Symplocos ra cemosa, tree whose bark is used for dyeing and in medicine | myth. np. from ṛṣi gālava "He who has (the rope) around his neck", son of Viśvāmitra; in times of famine, and while his father had gone to do penance on the banks of the Kauśikī, his mother took him to the market to sell him, with a kuśa rope around his neck; he was rescued by Prince Satyavrata₂; when his father returned he educated him; one day Dharma, disguised as Vasistha, came to the hermitage to test Viśvāmitra; the latter came out to welcome him with rice, but he had disappeared in the meantime, and the hermit waited for him for 100 years; Since gālava had taken good care of him, he wanted to spare him the cost of his education [gurudakṣiṇā]; at gālava's insistence on paying for it, his father asked him for 800 horses with a black ear [śyāmakarṇāśva]; Garuda assisted him and led him to Yayāti's palace; Yayāti promised him the horses if he helped him marry off his daughter Mādhavī; he took her to King Haryaśva, who was doing penance to obtain a son; Haryaśva agreed, but only had 200 suitable horses; Mādhavī then revealed that a sage had granted her the ability to regain her virginity even after giving birth; After giving a son to Ha ryaśva, she did the same with Divodāsa, king of Kāśi, then with Uśīnara, King of the bhojās; Gālava thus had 600 horses, and Garuda advised her to give them to her father, with Mādhavī as an addition; Viśvāmitra was satisfied, and Mādhavī gave her his son Aṣṭaka; |PP.| One day when Gālava was saying her Sandhyā prayers, a spittle from Citrasena fes toying in the air fell on the offering; Gālava complained to Kṛṣṇa who promised her head; Nārada informed Citrasena, who sent his wives Sandhyā and Ratnāvalī to plead with Subhadrā, who granted them the wish to live long with their husbands [mangalyabhikṣā]; Arjuna fought Kṛṣṇa, Subhadrā intervened, Kṛṣṇa then asked Citrasena to pay homage to Gālava who forgave him; |Mah.| Nārada recounts his propensity to accomplish impossible projects, such as traveling to inaccessible lands on Garuda.
gāvas cf. go.
gāvī [pkt. go] f. [apabhraṃśa] cow.

√ gāh v. [1] pr. r. (gāhate) v. [1] pr. (gāhati) aor. [3] (ajīgahat) aor. r. [4] (agāḍha) aor. r. [5] (agāhiṣṭa) pp. (gāḍha, gāhita) pf. (ava, vi) to plunge into, to sink into, to penetrate into (acc.) to cross, to traverse. mano me samśayameva gāhate my mind Is in vahi by doubt.
gāha |agt. gāh| amnf gāhā ifc. plunged into, immersed in — m. depth, interior, heart — f. gāhī id.
gāhana [agt. gāh] amnf gāhanā deep; difficult, from which one cannot extract oneself — act. n. plon geon, immersion.
gāhita [pp. gāh] amnf gāhitā immersed, plunged into — n. depth, interior.
gāhitṛ [agt. gāh] amnf gāhitrī that plunges into; that immerses itself | that penetrates.
gír [agt. gr̄2] f. [nom. gīr; en comp. gīr] invocation, praise | word, language; voice, Song — m. gira ifc. word, voice.
girīśa₁ [īśá] m. myth. np. of girīśa₁, epith. of Brhaspati "Master of the word".
girí [related to gur] m. mountain, Mount | hill, plateau | math. symb. the number 7 (cf. kulagiri).
giríkarnikā [karnika] f. bio. bot. Clitoria ternatea, climbing legume with bright blue flowers; syn. aparājitā.
giríja | ja | amnf girijā from the mountains — n. talc — f. girijā myth. epith. of Pārvatī "daughter of the mountains".
girínadī [nadī] f. [girinadī] torrent.
girínadī [nadī] f. mountain torrent | giriṇadī id.
girídvāra [dvāra] n. mountain pass.
girídhara [dhara] m. myth. np. of Giridhara, epith. of the young KṛṣṇaGovardhana "who carries the mountain" to protect the shepherds of Vṛndāvana from the torrential rains sent by Indra.

Girínagara | Nagara | n. geo. np. of the town of Girínagara, at the foot of Mount Vimalādri, in southern Gujarāt, near Jūnāgaḍha (mod. Girnār); it is sacred to Hindus, Buddhists and Jains; it is said that Dattātreya stayed there; there is an edict of Aśoka on a rock, and a fort built by Candragupta Maurya; one goes around Mount Parikrama by a 3-day pilgrimage.
giripatana | patana | n. act of throwing oneself from the top of a cliff, a method of suicide; syn. bhrgupāta.
girimallikā [mallikā] f. organic. bot. Wrightia antidy senterica, mountain jasmine; syn. kutaja.
girírāj [rāj₂] m. myth. np. of Girirāj, epith. of Himavān "King of the mountains".
girirājkumārī [kumārī] f. myth. n.p. from Gi rirājkumārī, epith. of UmāPārvatī “daughter of Hi mavān”.

girívraja [vraja] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the city of Girivraja "Encircled by mountains" epith. of Rājagrha, capital of Magadha founded by Vasu₃; [Mah.] it was the capital of King Jarāsandha; it was surrounded by 5 hills, including Caityaka; at its foot flows the Sumāgadhī.
giriṣṭhā [sthā₂] m. ved. inhabitant of the mountain (said of Vișnu, of the marutas).
girīśa₂ [īśa] m. myth. np. of girīśa₂ epith. of Hi mavān "Lord among the mountains" or of Siva "Lord on the mountain".

girika [girika] amnf girikā like a mountain (said of the heart of the gods) — f. girikā myth. np. of the queen girikā "daughter of the mountain"; she is the daughter of the river Suktimatī diverted by the mountain Kolāhala; Uparicara Vasu₂ married her; Brhadratha is one of their sons | mouse.
gila [related to gira] ifc. amnf gilā who swallows.
gīta [pp. gā₂] amnf gītā Sung — n. Song — f. cf. gītā.

gītáGovinda |Govinda| n. lit. np. from the Gītagovinda kāvya "Song of Govinda", erotic mystical poem by Jayadeva (12th century); it describes the loves of the young Kṛṣṇa and the shepherdesses [gopī]; it is immensely popular in East India; an edict of King Pratāparudradeva (1499) mandates that it be the only song permitted in the temple of Jagannātha in Purī.
gītajayantī | jayantī | f. soc. festival of the gītā; it is celebrated on the 11th day [ekādaśī] of the clear fortnight [śuklapakṣa] of the month mārgaśīrṣa (around the beginning of December).
gītākāra | kāra | mr. | nāṭya | choir.
gītārtha₁ [artha] m. ascetic who has completed ("sung") his studies.
gītārthasaṃgraha₁ [saṃgraha] m. lit. np. from the Gītārthasaṃgraha₁ "Compendium of the ascetic ac compli", work of Yāmunācārya.
gītālaṃkāra [alaṃkāra] m. lit. np. of the Gītālamkāra, the oldest known Indian treatise on musicology, attributed to Bharata₃.
gītaka [gītaka] nf gītikā chant, hymn; song.
gītā [f. gīta] f. chant, song, hymn, stanza, poem | lit. np. of the gītā, epith. of the Bhaga vadgītā.
Gītābhāṣya |bhāṣya| n. lit. np. of the Gītābhāṣya, commentary on the gītā due to Rāmānuja.
gītārtha₁ | artha| m. explanation of the gītā.
gītārthasaṃgraha₂ [saṃgraha] m. bed. n.p. of the gītārthasamgraha₁, śaiva commentary on the Bha gavadgītā of the Kaśmīra, due to Abhinavagupta.
gīti [act. gā₂] f. chant, song.
gītikāvya [kāvya] n. lyric poetry.
gīyamāna [ppr. ps. gā₂] amnf gīyamānā being sung.
gīr iic. gir. gīrvāṇa var. gīrbāṇa [vāṇa] amnf gīrvāṇā “whose arrow is speech” (said of the gods).
gīrvāṇapadamañjarī [padamañjarī] f. cf. pa damañjarī.
gīrvāṇabhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. Sanskrit "language of the gods". śivo rakṣatu gīrvāṇabhāṣārasāsvādatatparān [Kālidāsa] May Shiva bless the lovers of Sanskrit.
gīrnā₁ [pp. gr₁] amnf gīrnā swallowed, engulfed.
gīrṇa₂ [pp. gṝ₂] amnf gīrṇā praised — m. praise, eulogy — f. gīrņi praise; celebrity.
gu ifc. go.

gúggulu n. bio. bdellium, resin of the balsam tree bot. Commiphora mukul; Indian myrrh, used as perfume and in medicine, with triphalā |var. gúlgulu id. মূ ভ guccha var. gutsa m. bush; thicket | bouquet, sheaf; bundle, armful; group | necklace (not. of pearls).
gucchaka |ka| m. id.; not. small bouquet of fragrant flowers | lit. collection of works.
gucchagulma [gulma] n. (collective) bushes and shrubs.
√ guñj v. [1] pr. (guñjati) pp. (guñjita) bour give; yelp.

guñja |act. guñj| m. buzzing | bio. bot. Abrus precatorius, leguminous liana — f. guñjā bio. its fruit, a red (or white) seed, used for rosaries | jewelry weight measure, which is worth two grains [yava] (approx. 0.85 g). মূভ guḍa m. ball, lump |molasses (from cane juice); brown sugar (from palm) — f. guḍā ball, lump; pill.
gudaka |aka| mr. ball — f. gudikā pill.
gudajihvikānyāya [jihvikānyāya] m. (sugar and tongue saying) transient impression, momentary opi nion.
Guḍākeśa [keśa] m. myth. [BhG.] np. of Guḍākeśa, epith. of Arjuna "Thick-haired".
guḍākeśatā [tā] f. bd. property of having curly hair, one of the minor signs of the Buddha.
guḍūcī f. bio. bot. Tinospora cordifolia, dioecious liana menispermaceae With cordiform leaves, With small red berries in clusters, bitter plant widely used in medicine; syn. amṛtā.

guṇá m. thread; string (of a bow, a musical instrument, a necklace) | constitutive quality, property, attribute | subdivision, kind, category, species | merit; high quality, excellence | lit. literary quality; factor of poetic beauty | kāvyaśobhā| phon. increase of a vowel in the 1st degree: the guṇa of ('a', 'i', 'u', 'r', 'l') is resp. ('a', 'e', 'o', 'ar', 'al') | phil. [Sāṃkhya] quality characterizing one of the three essences of nature: the Good or Pure Essence of Being sattva (purity, truth), Passion rajas (strength, desire), and Darkness tamas (ignorance, inertia); These three qualities are balanced in things, whose nature is characterized by their respective relationships | lit. the 3 qualities of a poetic work [kāvya]: the art of simile [upamā₂] typical of Kālidāsa, the density of expressed meaning [arthagaurava] typical of Bhāravi, and the grace of the

vocabulary [padalālitya] typical of Daṇḍī₁ | math. symb. the number 3 | phil. [Vaisesika] the category [padārtha] of properties; Kaṇāda enumerates 17: rūpa aspect, rasa taste, gandha smell, sparśa touch, samkhyā₂ number, parimāṇa dimension, prthaktva singularity, prayatna volition, buddhayas perceptions, and 4 pairs of

opposites [dvandva]: saṃyogavibhāgau contact and separation, paratvāparatve distance and proximity, sukhaduḥkhe pleasure and suffering, icchādveṣau desire and aversion; the Tarkasaṃgraha lists 24, adding: gurutva heaviness, dravatva fluidity, sneha viscosity, śabda sound, dharma good, adharma evil, and saṃskāra disposition | math. multiplier coefficient — ifc. form of multiples: triguna the triple. gunátas adv. according to its qualities; according to its merits phil. according to the proportion of the three essences. guṇībhū to be subordinate to (g.). guṇāh pūjāsthānam guṇiṣu Among people of merit, qualities are the object of devotion. guņákiraņāvalīprakāśa [kiraņāvalīprakāśa] iic. phil. [Nyāya] quality of the Kiraṇāvalīprakāśa. guņakiraņāvalīprakāśadīdhiti [dīdhiti] f. lit. [Nyāya] np. of the guṇakiraṇāvalīprakāśadīdhiti "Praise of the Qualities of the Splendor of the Collection of Rays", commentary by Raghunātha₁ on the Kiraņāvalīprakāśa.
guṇákeśī [keśa] f. myth. [Mah.] np. of the beautiful Guṇakeśī "with beautiful hair", daughter of Mātali; she married the nāga Sumukha.
gunágana | gana | m. number or series of virtues. guņágāņa | gāṇa | n. panegyric.
gunágrahana [grahana] n. act of appreciating merit.
guṇajña [jña] amnf guṇajñā who recognizes merit.
gunátā |tā| f. subordination, dependence | fact of being a quality | possession of qualities; excellence.
guṇátva [tva] n. id.
gunadeva [deva] m. bed. [KSS.] np. of gunadeva, student of Guṇādhya.
gunádosa [dosa₂] m. du. vice and virtue — n. sg. id.

gunádharma | dharma | m. virtue or duty implied by a quality; e.g., clemency is the duty of a king. guņapatākā | patākā | f. lit. np. of Guņapatākā "Emblem of Qualities", prostitute receiving lessons in eroticism [kāmaśāstra] from Mūladeva in an eponymous work whose author may be Mūladeva himself.
Gunaprabha [bhadra| m. hist. np. of the monk bd. Gunaprabha (550–630), who attempted to introduce the sarvāstivāda doctrine into China; he is the author of a vinayasūtra.
Gunabhadra | bhadra | mr. hist. n.p. of the Jain master ācārya guṇabhadra (10th century), disciple of Jina sena; he completed his Adipurāṇa₂.
gunabheda | bheda | mr. classification of character or quality. gunabhedatas according to the subdivision into characters.

guṇamaya [maya] amnf guṇamayī in thread |endowed with qualities, deserving. gunávacana vacana n. gram. "word expressing a quality"] qualifying adjective — amnf gunavacanā gram. (word) that denotes a quality; used as an adjective.
guṇavat [vat] amnf guṇavatī deserving, deadly worm, having qualities; excellent | equipped with a rope. dravyam eva gunavat only substances possess qualities.
Guṇavārā [vāra] f. bed. [KSS.] np. of Guṇavārā, favorite wife of king Vīrabhuja, mother of Srngabhuja.
gunavrtti [vrtti] f. phil. secondary condition; opp. mukhyāvṛtti | gram. figurative meaning of a word (opp. meaning
literal [abhidhā₂], suggested meaning [vyañjanā]); metaphorical meaning [upacāra]; connotation; specialized technical meaning [lākṣaṇa].

guṇavrata [vrata] n. jn. meritorious vows, Jain ritual observance; there are three of them: limited activity [digvrata], limited consumption [bhogopabhogavrata] and absence of gratuitous sin [anarthadandavrata].
guṇaśabda [śabda] m. gram. word denoting an intrinsic quality; adjective. guņaśālin [śālin] amnf guņaśālinī virtuous; excellent.

guṇasaṃdrāva [saṃdrāva] m. phil. confluence of qualities, characterizing an individual object [dravya₁]. anvartham khalvapi nirvacanam gunasamdrāvo dravyam iti phil. [Patañjali₁] An individual object is a confluence of qualities whose explanation is evident.
guṇasamanvita |samanvita| amfn guṇasamanvitā endowed with virtues.
gunasamudāya [samudāya] m. phil. collection of qualities. gunasamudāyo dravyam phil. |Patanjali₁| An individual object is an aggregate of qualities.

gunásthāna [sthāna] n. jn. stage of spiritual development; Jainism distinguishes 14 of them, in order of decreasing sin and increasing purity; the first four concern rationality: the ignorant state of the brute [mithyātva], the state of remembering having tasted true faith [sasvādana], the mixed state of partially rational beliefs [miśra], the state of rectitude without renunciation [aviratasamyaktva]; the following are determined by conduct: the state of partial renunciation [deśaviratasamyagdriṣṭi], is obtained by taking one's minor vows [anuvrata]; the last 9 require having taken one's major vows | mahāvrata | : the state of complete renunciation with relaxation [pramattavirata], the state of conscious renunciation [apramattavirata], the state of meditative recollection [apūrvakaraṇa], the advanced meditative state "of no return" [anivṛttikaraṇa], the state of almost total absence of passion [sūkṣmasamparaya], the state of tranquility without passions [upasantamoha], the state of total absence of delusion [kṣīṇamoha], the state of active omniscience [sayogakevalin], attained by the
saints [arhat], and the brief state of passive omniscience [ayogakevalin], where bodily activity ceases, and nirvana is attained.
gunasthānaprakarana | prakarana | n. jn. n.p. from the Jain work Gunasthānaprakarana.

Guṇāḍhya [āḍhya] m. hist. Tradition attributes to Gunādhya the authorship of a collection of tales, the Brhatkathā; his historical existence is not demonstrated | lit. [KSS.] np. of Guṇāḍhya "Killer Worm", born of Srutārthā seen during the bath by the nāga Kīrtisena; a heavenly voice announced at his birth that he was a brahmin and rich in virtues; he acquired all the sciences, became famous, and was appointed minister by King Sātavāhana at Supratisthita; he is the incarnation on Earth of the gaṇa Mālyavān₂, punished for having supported the guilty Puspadanta; He must hear the Brhatkathā of the piśāca Kānabhūti to be freed, and will himself be freed by transmitting the story; King Sātavāhana, having been corrected by his wife for making a grammatical error, was promised to be taught by the scholar Sarvavarmā in 6 months; Guṇāḍhya made a bet to renounce the 3 languages (saṃskṛta, prākṛta and bhāṣā) if he succeeded; having lost his bet he withdrew to the Vindhya mountains; on the directions of Vind hyavāsinī he met Kāṇabhūti who told him the Kathā; it took him 7 years to transcribe his 7 tales in the language of the spirits | paiśācī|, giving birth to the 700,000 verses of the Bṛhatkathā which he wrote with his blood; he offered it to King Sātavāhana, who refused it; he then put it in the fire, except for the chapter on Naravāhanadatta, and freed from his fate returned to heaven.
guṇānvita | anvita | amnf guṇānvitā endowed with qualities; excellent | auspicious (star).
guṇābhāsa [ābhāsa] m. illusion of quality (of (iic.)).
guṇābhāsakara [kara₁] amnf guṇābhāsakarī which causes an appearance of quality.
guṇābhāsakaratva [tva] n. ability to simulate a quality.
gunopeta [upeta] amnf gunopetā endowed with qualities.
guṇaka [guṇaka] amnf guṇikā ifc. which has the quality (iic.) — m. calculator; accountant.
guṇana [guṇana] nf guṇanī math. multiplication; enumeration; repetition.
guṇanapālita [pālita] m. bed. [Kuṭṭanīmata] np. of guṇanapālita, friend of Sundarasena.
guṇanaphala | phala | n. math. product of a multiplication.
guṇanikā [guṇanaika] f. repetition; repeated study; syn. gunanī. hetuh paricayasthairye vakturgunanikaiva sā [SPV.] Repetition serves to increase the reciter's knowledge.
guṇanīya [guṇanaīya] amnf guṇanīyā to repeat, to multiply — m. repeated study — n. math. multiplicand.
guṇita [guṇaita] amnf guṇitā multi folded (with (i. iic.)) | increased; intensified; practiced frequently | connected with (iic.).
guṇin [guṇain] amnf guṇinī deserving, virtuous, endowed with qualities | equipped with a rope. varam eko guṇī putro naca mūrkhaśatānyapi [Hit.] Better one intelligent son than a hundred fools.
guṇī iiv. guṇa.
guṇībhāva [bhāva] m. gram. (term) subordinate (opp. pradhānabhāva principal).
guṇībhūta [bhūta] amnf guṇībhūtā subor given to (g.); secondary | invested with attributes.

guṇībhūtavyaṅgya [vyaṅgya] amnf guṇībhūtavyaṅgyā lit. [Ānandavardhana] whose suggested meaning is secondary (said of poetry |kāvya| which does not have the development of an emotion [rasa] as its main purpose, and whose use of suggestion is a simple figure of speech); opp. dhvani.
√ guṇṭh var. guṇḍ v. |10| pr. (guṇṭhayati) pp. (gunthita) pf. (ava) to cover, to wrap.
√ guṇḍ [related to guṇṭh] v. [10] pr. (guṇḍayati) pp. (guṇḍita) to cover, to wrap; to hide | to reduce to powder.
guṇḍa |agt. guṇḍ| m. soc. protective capsule, not. of the portable linga of the Vīraśaiva sect.

guṇḍicā f. geo. np. of the temple of guṇḍicā at Purī, summer residence of Jagannātha for 9 days during the great procession [rathayātrā], symbolizing the return of Kṛṣṇa to Vṛndāvana; it is named after the wife of Indradyumna.
guṇḍita [pp. guṇḍ] amnf guṇḍitā reduced to powder.
gunya [gunaya] amnf gunyā endowed with qualities or virtues | to be enumerated | according to the quality math. multiplicand.
gutsa m. cf. guccha.
gudá n. anus — mn intestine, entrails — f. gudā ifc. id. | pl. intestines, viscera.

√ gup v. pft. (jugopa) aor. [4] (agaupsīt) aor. [5] (agopīt) pp. (Gupta, gupita) ca. (gopayáti) to guard, protect, defend — des. r. (jugupsate) to defend oneself against (abl.); to feel disgust for | to be on one's guard; to distrust, avoid, hate, despise acc. .

Gupta |pp. gup| amnf guptā protected, defended; hidden, secret — m. hist. np. of the first emperor of the Gupta dynasty, the famous |śrī| king Gupta, who founded the dynasty [samvat] of the same name, under the title Candragupta₁ in 320; he reigned over a large part of the Ganges valley; his son Samudragupta succeeded him | Gupta era, beginning in 319 — ifc. soc. form of the np. of the Vaishya class: "protector of the (iic.)". guptam in secret. gupte in a hidden place. guptīkr to conceal, hide.
guptaka [ka] m. conservative.
guptácara | cara | mr. spy, secret agent.
guptátama [tama] amnf guptatamā super. very hidden.
guptádāna |dāna| n. donation made in secret.
gupti [act. gup] f. protection, preservation, act of hiding | military defense | rampart; prison.
gum [onomatopoeia] iic. buzzing of bees.
guṃkāra |kāra| m. humming | gram. pro nunciation of the anusvāra; sometimes made explicit in recitation as gum or gvam.
gumānī m. hist. np. of the poet gumānī, to the author of the collection of sayings Upadeśaśataka.
√ gumph v. [6] pr. (gumphati) pp. (gumphita) to string, to assemble into a necklace or garland.
gumpha |act. gumph| m. arranged in a row; as sembling a garland; bracelet.
gumphana [act. gumph] nf gumphanā making of a garland | lit. [KM.] the interlacing of words, a poetic quality.
gumphita [pp. gumph] amnf gumphitā arranged in order, in row, aligned.
√ gur v. [6] pr. r. (gurate) to lift, raise; to weigh | to make an effort.

gurú [gr̄2] amnf gurvī heavy, grave, res respectable, venerable; great, important | phon. long (vowel or syllable); opp. laghu | difficult to digest (food) — m. soc. tutor, spiritual guide, master; divine guide; God incarnate | myth. np. of Guru, abbreviation of Suraguru "Preceptor (of the gods)", epithet of Brhaspati who teaches the Veda to the gods; astr. he personifies the planet [graha] Jupiter | pl. guravas (respectful address) Master, Venerable | lat. gravis; fr. grave. gurau in the master's house; in the case of a master. gurūṇām guruḥ master of masters. gururbrahmā gururviṣṇuḥ gururdevo maheśvaraḥ | gurussākṣāt parambrahmā tasmai śrīgurave namaḥ | [Srīgurustotra] The Master is Brahmā, the Master is Vișnu, the divine Master is Shiva; truly the Master is God: let us revere the Master.
gurukula |kula| n. soc. master's house, hermitage; his family and the students of his school live there | mod. traditional Sanskrit teaching school.
Gurugītā [gītā] f. lit. np. of the Gurugītā "Praise to the Master", dialogue between Pārvatī and Siva teaching how to revere his Guru; it is an annex of the SkP.
gurugrāma | grāma | m. geo. np. of the town of Gu rugrāma "Village of the master (Droṇa)"; mod. gur gaon in Hariyāna.
gurutattva [tattva] n. phil. principle of divine guidance.
gurutama [great. Guru] amnf gurutamā the heaviest.
gurutara |compar. Guru| amnf gurutarā heavier.
gurútalpa [talpa] m. soc. adultery with the master's wife; it is one of the 5 great sins |mahāpātaka|.
gurútalpaga |ga₁| m. soc. refers to a student who deceives his teacher.
gurutalpagāmin |gāmin| mr. id.
gurutā |tā| f. heaviness, weight | importance; respectability, dignity | soc. qualification of a spiritual preceptor.
gurutva [tva] n. heaviness, weight | mus. length of a vowel | burden, boredom | med. severity (treatment) | grandeur, magnitude | respectability, dignity soc. qualification of a spiritual preceptor.
gurudakṣiṇā [dakṣiṇā] f. soc. fees paid by the student to his master at the end of his studies.
gurudatta [datta] amnf gurudattā given by the master.
gurudattamantra [mantra] n. soc. mantra given by the master.
gurudeva |deva| m. phil. master venerated as a living god.
gurudvādaśī [dvādaśī] f. soc. festival in honor of Dattātreya, on the 12th day of the dark fortnight | kṛṣṇapakṣa | of the month kārttika; Val labhācārya is also celebrated there.

gurupañcamī | pañcamī | f. cf. śrutapañcamī. gurupūrņimā [pūrņimā] f. full moon day of the month āṣāḍha, syn. āṣāḍhī; soc. on which the sage Vyāsa is celebrated, and by extension his own spiritual ritual teacher; it marks the return of the rains, and the beginning of spiritual exercises |sādhana|.
gurubandhu [bandhu] amnf who has the same master as (iic.) — m. fellow student, comrade.

gurumukha [mukha] amnf gurumukhī from the mouth of the master — f. gurumukhī hist. gurmukhī script used in Pañjāb from the 14th century, evolved from devanāgarī; it was used notably for the holy book of the Sikhs (Guru Grantha Sahib).
gurumukhopadeśa [upadeśa] m. soc. initiation by the master.
gurulāghava [lāghava] n. relative importance; the pros and cons | "the heavy and the light" |.
guruvaktra [vaktra] n. mouth of the master. guruvaktratas adv. (learned) from the mouth of the master.
guruvat [vat] adv. like a master | as for a master.
guruvāra [vāra] m. Thursday, the day of Jupiter [Bṛhaspati]; it is sacred to Lakṣmī.
guruśikhara [śikhara] mn geo. n.p. Gurusikhara peak (1722 m), summit of the Arāvalī mountain range; there is a sanctuary of Dattātreya there.
guruśisya [śiṣya] amnf guruśiṣyā soc. which relates to the relationship between master and student.
guruśisyasaṃvāda [saṃvāda] m. lit. np. from the Guruśisyasamvāda "Dialogue between the master and the student", Philosophical dialogue due to Caranadāsa.
guruśisyasambandha [sambandha] m. soc. link between master and pupil.
gurvaparādha [aparādha] m. soc. offense to the master.
gurjará var. gūrjara m. geo. the Gurjara country, mod. Gujarat; cf. Dvārakā | pl. gurjarās its inhabitants.
gurjaradesa | desa | mr. geo. the country of the gurjarās, mod. Gujarat.
gula |guḍa| m. ball; not. brown sugar ball;
candy | glans of the penis | clitoris — f. gulī pill.
gulikā [ika] f. small ball; rifle bullet | toy ball | pearl; pill.
gulphá var. kulpha m. ankle.
gulphadaghná [daghna] amnf gulphadaghnā f. gulphadaghnī who has (water) up to her ankles.
gúlma m. bush; shrub; grove, clump of trees | platoon, army unit comprising three sections [senāmukha]; cf. gaṇa | med. abdominal tumor | med. spleen.
gulmasthāna [sthāna] n. soc. police station.
gulmin [gulmain] amnf gulminī (army) comprising several sections | bushy, thick — f. gulminī creeping plant covering the ground.
√ guh v. [1] pr. (gūhati) pft. (jugūha) aor. [7] (aghukṣat) pp. (gūḍha) pfp. (gohya, guhya) pf. (apa, upa, ni) cover | hide, conceal — ca. (gūhayati) hide, conceal.

Guha₁ |obj. guh| m. myth. np. of Guha₁, epith. of Skanda "raised in secret" | myth. [Rām.] np. of Guha₁, Niṣāda king; his capital was Sṛṅgavera, on the banks of the Gangā; he made heroes cross the river; Rāma was his friend, and embraced him (despite his caste) | pl. guhās geo. tribe of South India — f. cf. guhā — adv. guhā in secret, secretly; opp. āvis.
guhā [f. Guha₁] f. hiding place, cavern; den, burrow | arch. niche.
guhāśaya [śaya] amnf guhāśayā who lies in a den.
gúhya [pfp. [1] guh] amnf guhyā which must be hidden, secret, mysterious — n. secret, mystery, magic formula — m. sexual organ | the womb, an āyādi ; syn. yoni .
guhyatama [tama| amnf guhyatamā great. the most secret.
guhyasamāja |samāja| m. bd. np. of the Gu hyasamāja, esoteric community, school of interpretation of bd. tantr. Vajrayāna; cf. Aryadeva.
guhyasamājatantra | tantra| n. bd. np. of the Gu hyasamājatantra, teaching of the Guhya samāja system; also called Śrīsamāja; it describes secret rites and reprehensible practices.
Guhyasiddhi |siddhi| f. lit. np. of the Guhyasiddhi, an esoteric work by Padmavajra, written in style
obscure [sandhyābhāṣā].
guhyaka [Guhyaka] m. myth. hidden spirit, guardian genius of Kubera's treasures; the leader of the guhyakās is Revanta; cf. Nalakūvara, Maņigrīva.
guhyatama |great. Guhya| amnf Guhya tamā the most secret.

guhyatara |compar. Guhya| amnf Guhya tarā more secret. মূভ gūḍha |pp. guh| amnf gūḍhā hidden, secret — n. secret place, hiding place. tama āsīt tamasā gūḍham agre |RV.| In the beginning, darkness was hidden by darkness.
gūdhajatru | jatru | amnf with a powerful neck ["whose neck is hidden (by the muscles)"].
gūdhārtha | artha | m. phil. esoteric sense, mystical sense; hidden sense — amnf gūḍhārthā phil. whose meaning is hidden.
gūḍhārthadīpikā [dīpikā] f. bed. of np. Gūdhārthadīpikā, commentary on the Gītā of Madhusūdana₁ Sarasvatī₂.
gūrjara m. cf. gurjara.
gṛ cf. jāgṛ. সৃস্কন gṛñjana m. red onion (non-vegetable)
killer [sāttvika]) | resinous cannabis buds chewed as an intoxicant — n. meat of an animal badly killed by a poisoned arrow.
gṛtsa amnf gṛtsā skillful, adroit; wise, prudent; judicious — m. sage.

grtsamadá [mada] m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Grtsamada; first son of Sunahotra of the lineage of Angirā, but by Indra's decree transferred to the lineage of Bhrgu as son of Saunaka; most of the hymns of the 2nd mandala of the Rigveda are attributed to him. myth. np. of Gṛtsamada₁, son of Vītahavya. myth. np. of Grtsamada₂, son of Queen Mukundā, deceived by Indra who had taken the form of her husband Rukmāngada; he became an unsurpassed scholar. সূদ্ধ grddha [agt. grdh] amnf grddhā who desires; eager for (loc.).
gṛddhin [agt. gṛdh] amnf gṛddhinī ifc. who covets.

√ਸੁਖ਼ grdh v. [4] pr. (grdhyati) aor. [2] (agrdhat) pp. (grddha) to desire, covet; to be greedy for (loc. acc.) — ca. (gardhayati) to be greedy; to cause to be coveted — ca. r. (gardhayate) to deceive | all. gier; ang. greed; fr. gredin. mā grdhah kasyasvid dhanam Does not covet the wealth of others. śiśum gardhayate he deceives the child. মুখ্য grdhra [grdhra] amnf grdhrā ifc. greedy for (iic.) — mf gṛdhri bio. zoo. vulture.
gṛdhrakūṭa |kūṭa| m. geo. np. of the gṛdhrakūṭa “Peak of the Vultures”, summit near Rājagṛha.
gṛbh cf. grah.
grbhīta var. grhīta [pp. grah] amnf gṛbhītā taken, seized; acquired, obtained, received. সৃষ্টি gṛṣṭí f. young heifer, having had only one calf — ifc. young female animal.
gṛh cf. grah.

gṛhá [agt. grah] n. sg. house, dwelling, home; apartment, room — m. servant, servant | pl. gṛhās house, hearth, apartments; penates, family estate; servants; wife all. kirche; ang. church. grham gam to return home. grhe grhe in every house.
grhákapota [kapota] m. domestic pigeon.
gṛhákuliṅga [kuliṅga] mf gṛhakuliṅgī house sparrow.
gṛhatyāgin [tyāgin] amnf gṛhatyāginī who left his home.
gṛhánīḍa [nīḍa] amnf gṛhanīḍā ["who makes his nest in the house" sparrow.
grhápati [pati] m. master of the house; head of the family — f. gṛhapatnī wife of the master of the house, mother of the family. grhapraveśa praveśa m. moving into a new home; housewarming.
grhábali [bali] m. domestic offering; leftover food offered to animals or gods. [3
grhabalibhuj [bhuj₃] m. ["who eats leftovers"] sparrow | crow.
grhámedhá | medha | m. domestic sacrifice.
grhámedhín [in] m. ["who performs the domestic sacrifice" | (brahman) head of household.
grhaśrama [śráma] m. domestic labor.
grhaśramavrata [vrata] n. conjugal duty.
grhasūtra [sūtra] n. soc. sūtra describing domestic rites.

grhastha [stha] m. master of the house; syn. grhapati | soc. 2nd stage [āśrama] of Brahmanic life (active adult life, practice of a profession, establishment of a family); the associated puruṣārtha is kāma — f. gṛhasthā his wife.
grhasthatva [tva] n. state of head of family.
gṛhasthāśrama [āśrama] m. soc. role of family father, 2nd stage [āśrama] of Brahmanic life.
gṛhasvāmin [svāmin] m. master of the house, head of the family — f. gṛhasvāminī mistress of the house.
gṛhín [in] amnf gṛhiṇī who owns a house — m. master of the house — f. gṛhiṇī mistress of the house. yuvatayo gṛhiṇīpadaṃ yānti young women attain the position of mistress of the house.
grhaikatva [ekatva] n. phil. ["unity of the family"]
[nyāya] rule of generalization: the predication of an element of a class holds for all elements of the class.
grhopakarana | upakarana | n. domestic utensils.

gṛhīta var. gṛbhīta [pp. grah] amnf gṛhītā taken, seized; acquired, obtained, received — iic. who took or received (ifc.) || pkt. gahia. gṛhītaikacakraḥ myth. epith. of the demon Baka₁ “who took the city of Ekacakrā”.
gṛhītavidya |vidyā| amnf gṛhītavidyā who has acquired knowledge; scholar. grhītasamjña var. grhītasañjña [sañjñā₂] amnf gṛhītasaṃjñā who has received the signal.
gṛhītārtha | artha | amnf gṛhītārthā which takes the meaning; conscious, lucid.
gṛhītvā [abs. grah] ind. having seized; having obtained.

gṛhya₁ [pfp. [1] grah] amnf gṛhyā to be taken; perceptible | that which must be admitted or recognized; that which must be believed; reliable — ifc. to be taken with (iic.) | of the party of, in connection with, connected to (iic.) — abs. ind. cl. having taken (iic.). gunagrhyah friend of virtue. grāmagṛhyā senā army quartered outside the village. hastagrhya having taken the lead.
gṛhya₂ [gṛhaya] amnf gṛhyā domestic — m. domestic animal — n. |grhyakarman| domestic rite — f. gṛhyā domestic rules.
grhyaka |ka| amnf grhyakā (animal) captive, domestic.
grhyakarman [karman] n. soc. domestic rite.
grhyaprayoga [prayoga] m. soc. practice of domestic ritual.
gṛhyasūtra |sūtra| n. lit. text of aphorisms of domestic ritual.
gṛhyāgni |agni| m. soc. domestic fire.

√ gr₁ v. [6] pr. (girati) pp. (gr₁ pf. (ava, ut, ni, sam) to swallow, absorb, gulp down | vomit — ca. (girayati) ca. (gārayati) ca. (gālayati) to make swallow — des. (jigariṣati) to want to swallow — intens. r. (jegi lyate) (av. ni) to gorge oneself | lat. glutio, gula, vorare; fr. engloutir, glutton, gueule, vorace.
√ gr₂ v. [9] pr. (gṛṇāti) pr. r. (gṛṇīte) pf. (apa, abhi, prati, sam) to call, to invoke, to pray; to proclaim; to sing, to praise, to celebrate | lat. garrio.
geya [pfp. [1] gā₂] amnf geyā to sing.
geyagarbha [garbha] m. lit. melodramatic recitation.
gehá [pkt. gṛha] n. house, dwelling.
gehin [gehain] m. master of the house; syn. gṛhin — f. gehinī mistress of the house.
gehe [loc. geha] adv. at home, at one's own place.
gehemehin [mehin] m. ["who pees at home"] (pej.) lazy person.
gehevyāda | vyāda | m. | "salon tiger" | (pej.) my tamore, braggart.
gai cf. gā₂.

go m. sg. nom. gaus, acc. gām, i. gavā, dat. gave, abl. g. gos, loc. gavi; du. nom. acc. gāvau, i. dat. abl. gobhyām, g. loc. gavos; pl. nom. gāvas, acc. gās, i. gobhis, dat. abl. gobhyas, g. gavām, loc. goșu; en comp. gava ox, bovine | (pej.) stupid person, beast of burden | pl. gāvas cattle; herd | ved. milk — f. cow | word | ved. ray of the sun (they form the celestial herd) | the Earth (cow of kings) the hairs of the human body myth. np. of Go "word", epith. of Sarasvatī, goddess of sacred speech, śakti of Brahmā — mnf gu ifc. whose cow is; cf. citragu | who has num. iic. cows; cf. dvigu — v. [11] pr. (gavyati) to wish for a cow | lat. bos; ang. cow; all. Kuh; fr. bœuf. go'śvapuruṣahastiśakunimrgabrāhmaṇāḥ |Patanjali₁| The cows, The horses, The men, The elephants, The kites, The deer and The Brahmins. gó_agra [agra] amnf go_agrā ved. who puts The cows in the lead.

Gokarna | Karna | m. geo. np. of Gokarna "Cow's Ear", pilgrimage site on the West Coast, north of Karṇāṭaka; myth. Ravana had stolen the linga into which Rudra had transformed; Ganesha tricked him into carrying it during his prayers, but instead placed it on the ground at Gokarna, from where Ravana could no longer lift it | myth. [Srīmadbhāgavatamāhātmya] np. of the killer worm Gokarna₁, brother of the criminal Dhundhukārī, whose wandering spirit he only managed to appease by leading a saptāha | bio. zoo. Boselaphus tra gocamelus, nilgai; cf. nīlānga.
gókāma |kāma| amnf gokāmā who desires cows.
gókāmyā | kāmya | f. desire to acquire cows.
gókula | kula | n. herd of cows, cattle; stable myth. np. of Gokula "Dairy", village near Mathurā where Yaśodā lived and where Kṛṣṇa was raised as a child.

gokulāṣṭamī [aṣṭamī] f. soc. Krishna's birthday; syn. janmāṣṭamī. gokșura [kṣura] m. cow's hoof | bio. bot. Tribulus terrestris, a herbaceous plant of the Zygophyllaceae family with yellow flowers and fruits in five spiny, caltrop-like pods; its thorns are formidable to humans and livestock; it is one of the five medicinal roots.
neures | hrasvapañcamūla|.
gogostha |gostha| n. stable.
gógranthi | granthi | m. dried cow dung.
góghātá [ghāta] m. cow killer.
góghná |ghna| amnf goghnā who kills the cattle — m. host ["for whom the cow is sacrificed"].

gócara | cara | amnf gocarā perceptible, visible, attainable by (g.); accessible to the senses — ifc. frequented by; connected to; obeying (iic.); accessible to, perceptible to (iic.) | gram. usable in the sense of (loc.) — loc. m. pasture, grazing land; do maine, province | reach, influence, reach; access route — v. [11] pr. (gocarayati) to be observable, to be common. locanagocaram yā to become visible, to be within sight. śravanagocare tistha remains within earshot. mṛtyuocaram gataḥ in The Claws of Death. gocarīkī to reach by the senses | to be subject to, to feel. glānyā gocarīkṛ to be weary, to feel fatigued. gocarīkṛta amn in the field of observation. nivṛttam abhidhātavyam nivṛtte cittagocare phil. [Nāgārjuna] What words can express stops where the grasp of the mind stops.
gócāratā [tā] f. state of being subject to (iic.).
gócāratva [tva] n. id.
gócāraṇa | cāraṇa | n. care of cows.
gójāta [jāta] amnf gojātā is said of the gods ["born of the cow".
gotīrtha | tīrtha | n. geo. Oxford.
gotva [gotva] n. stupidity ["cow nature"].
goda |da| amnf godā which gives cows.
Godāvarī [vara₂] f. geo. n.p. of the Godāvarī river, crossing the Deccan from West to East and having its delta on the coast of Golconda [saptagodāvara].
godāvarīkhanda [khanda] n. bed. n.p. of Godāvarīkhanda, autonomous section of Skāndapurāṇa; Srīnātha made a version in Sanskritized Telugu language.
godāna [dāna] n. gift of a cow | soc. rite of shaving the head and body hair; it is a saṃskāra performed at the age of 16 for the brah manes; syn. keśānta.

godānamantra | mantra| m. pl. lit. [Matsyapurāṇa] formulas of praise of the cow. hiranyagarbhagarbhastham hemabījam vibhāvasoh anantapunyaphaladamatah śāntim prayaccha me Golden embryo of the divine womb, golden seed of the Sun's radiance, which always rewards good deeds, thus grant me your blessing.
goduh |duh₂| m. |nom. godhuk| cowherd |"who milks"].
godoha [doha] m. milking. godoham ind. as long as the milking of the cows lasts.

godohana [dohana] mf godohanī milk | milk pail. godohananyāyaḥ m. maxim of the milk pot; it is said that a yajamāna desiring cows must bring his water in a milk pot; by analogy, the milk pot evokes an occasional accessory of a ceremony.
godhāman [dhāman] n. geo. np. of Godhāma "Delight of the cows", large stable [gośālā] of Anandavana.
godhūli [dhūli] f. misty moment of the morning in the hot season; it is a favorable period.
godhenu [dhenu] f. dairy cow.

gónarda | narda | m. myth. | "who roars like a bull"] epith. of Shiva | geo. np. of the village of Gonarda, where Patañjali₁ was born, between Ujjayinī and Vidiśā | pl. geo. np. of the Gonardās people.
gónardīya |īya| m. hist. | "originating from Gonar da", epith. of Patañjali₁.
gónasa [nasa] m. bio. a kind of large snake "with a cow's nose".
gópati | pati | m. soc. clan chief | myth. np. of Gopati "chief", epith. of Indra, Kṛṣṇa, etc.
gopatha | patha | m. cow path; pasture lit. np. of the Gopatha brāhmaṇa; it is the only brāhmaṇa genre text associated with the Atharvaveda.
gópada | pada | n. hoofprint of a cow.
gópávana [pavana] m. myth. np. of the ṛṣi Gopavana, of the family of Atri.
gópaśu [paśu] m. soc. bovine intended for sacrifice.
gopā [pā₃] m. herdsman, shepherd | guardian, protector — v. [11] pr. (gopāyati) to act like a herdsman; to protect, to preserve.

gopānasī [nasa] f. bamboo frame of a thatched roof. gopānasīsu ksanamāsthitānāmālambibhiscandrakiņā harinmaniśyāmatṛṇābhirāmairgṛhāṇi kalāpaiḥ nīdhrairiva yatra rejuḥ || [ZPV.] There, the houses seemed adorned with an overhanging eaves of fresh, emerald-colored grass, formed from the drooping tail feathers of the peacocks that were perched at that moment in their frame.

Gopāla [Pāla] m. cowherd | caste name [jāti] vaišya (herders/farmers) | myth. np. of Gopāla "Cowherd", epithet of Kṛṣṇa as a youth; he enchanted the cowherd girls [gopī] with his flute [venu], and played at hiding their clothes in the trees while they bathed | hist. np. of Gopāla₁, first Pāla king of Bengal, elected to end anarchy; he reigned from 750 to 770; he encouraged Buddhism, and protected scholars like Prajñāvarmā; his son Dharmapāla₁ succeeded him | hist. np. of the mathematician Gopāla₂ (circa 1135) | hist. np. of Gopāla₃ Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī [1501–1591], one of the six pastors of Vṛndāvana, Bengali disciple of Caitanya.
gopālaka [ka] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of gopālaka, eldest son of King Candamahāsena; upon the latter's death, he renounced the throne in favour of his younger brother Pālaka₁ and retired to Mount Asita₂.
Gopālārcana [arcana] n. lit. np. from the Gopālārcana "Adoration of Kṛṣṇa", treatise on vaiṣṇava ritual. gopuccha mn cow tail.
gopucchāgra [agra] n. end of a cow's tail; [Nāṭyaśāstra] Bharata compares it to the denouement of a good play, revealing a bouquet of surprises.
gopura | pura | n. porte cochere, fortified gate of a city, monumental gate of a temple in South India.
gophana [phana] m. sling — f. gophanā med. facial bandage with a hole for the nose.
gobrāhmaṇa | brāhmaṇa | m. soc. the brahmin with his cow.

gomat |mat| amnf Gomatī₁ who possesses herds, rich | made up of cattle — n. possession of cattle — f. Gomatī₁ region of herds | geo. np. of the Gomatī₁ river in Uttar Pradesh, tributary of the Ganges; cf. Naimișa myth. np. of Gomatī₁, daughter of Vasistha (or form of Gangā); Kṛṣṇa officiated at her marriage to the Ocean [Sāgara]; she has a sanctuary at Dvārakā, on the seashore.

gómáya [maya] mn cow dung — v. [11] pr. (gómayati) to coat with cow dung — v. [11] pr. r. (gomayāyate) to resemble cow dung; to be tasteless. khyātah sarvarasānām hi lavaņo rasa uttamah | grhņīyāt tam vinā tena vyañjanam gomayāyate [Hit.] Of all spices, salt is recognized as supreme; a sauce used without it is destined to be tasteless.
gomayanikāya | nikāya | m. pile of cow dung.

gomātr [mātr] amnf myth. ["having a Cow as a mother"] is said of the marutas — f. myth. ["mother of cows"] np. of Gomātā "Mother Cow", who brings abundance; epith. of the Cow of abundance in Nandinī; she is venerated not. at the Godhāma mahātīrtha.
gomāyu [māyu₂] m. ["that bellows like cattle"] frog | jackal.
gomin |min| m. cattle owner | bd. secular Buddhist.

Gomukha₁ [mukha] amnf gomukhī who has a cow's head — mn cor, trunk | geo. np. of Gomukha₁ "Cow's Head", chasm of the Gangotrī glacier in northern Uttar Pradesh from which the Ganges originates — m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Gomukha₁, son of the chamberlain Nityodita, born at the same time as Na ravāhanadatta; he became his chamberlain and confidant; separated from his companions, he is taken by a celestial woman to the hermitage of Nāgasvāmī — f. gomukhī channel for the flow of lustral waters north of a sanctuary. gomukhaḥ vyāghraḥ | "cow-headed tiger" | underestimated difficulty.
gomukhāsana |āsana| n. phil. |yoga| posture as seated where the legs cross, the right heel along the left side and vice versa (the feet evoke the horns of a cow).
gomūtra | mūtra | n. cow urine.

gomūtraka [ka] amnf gomūtrikā ["like a cow that pees" | which goes in a zigzag — f. gomūtrikā zigzag | math. method of positional multiplication due to Brahmagupta | lit. variety of gaticitra poem, with zigzag reading.
gomeda [medas] m. organic. hyacinth quartz, a
orange gem [uparatna].
gomedha | medha | mr. soc. sacrifice of a cow.
goyakṛdrasa | yakṛtrasa | m. med. extract of cow liver.
goyukta |yukta| amnf goyuktā harnessed to an ox (cart).

Gorakṣa [rakṣa] amnf gorakṣā who tends cattle — m. cowherd | Nepali; disciple of Gorakṣanātha | hist. descendant of Prince Bappa Rawal, founder of the House of Mewar; not. member of the Nepali royal family | hist. np. of the monk-soldier Gorakṣa; cf. Gorakṣanātha | hist. np. of the śaiva philosopher Gorakṣa₁; cf. Maheśvarānanda mod. mercenary soldier (Gurkha in the British Army and in Singapore, Gorkha in the Indian Army); they speak Nepali; they carry the curved machete [khukurī], and are renowned for their courage — f. gorakṣā cattle herder || ang. gurkha.

Gorakṣanātha [nātha] m. hist. np. of Gora kṣanātha or Gorakṣa "Protector of Shepherds", Guru of the nāthayogin of the 11th century, student of the mahāsiddha Matsyendranātha, author of several treatises of hathayoga, not. the Goraksasataka, the Vi vekamārtanda and the Yogabīja; according to legend, this soldier-monk was meditating in the desert in Rājasthāna when he met his first disciple, the young rājput prince Bappa Rawal, whom he enthroned as the first gorakșa, and whom he encouraged to liberate Afghanistan from vahi by the Muslims; he is also called Guru Goraknātha, the cities of Gorkha in Nepal and Goraksapura in India are named in his honor; Siddhasiddhāntapaddhati is attributed to him || hi. Goraknath.
gorakṣaka [rakṣaka] amnf gorakṣikā cf. gorakşa.
gorakṣapura | pura | n. geo. np. of the city of Goraksapura in Kosala (mod. Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh, near Nepal); named in honor of Gorakṣanātha, it houses his mausoleum |samādhi|.
gorakṣaśataka |śataka| n. bed. n.p. of the Gorakșaśataka "Centurie of Gorakșa", hathayoga work by Gorakşanātha.
gorakṣāsana [āsana] n. phil. [yoga] posture (a smiling version of bhadrāsana); seated, legs folded or fully extended, arches of the feet opposite, hands holding opposite ankles, torso straight.
goraksya [raksya] n. livestock protection; syn. gorakṣā | var. gaurakṣya id.
gorasa [rasa] m. milky taste; dairy product, milk; milk. vinā gorasam ko raso bhojanānām Without dairy, what would the taste of food be?
górocanā [rocanā] f. yellow ointment made from cow bile, used in dyeing, painting, and to mark the sign on the forehead [tilaka]; also medicinal remedy.
gólakṣaṇa |lakṣaṇa| n. marks on the coat of a cow.
gólāngūla [lāngūla] n. cow's tail — m. ["who has a cow's tail" langur monkey.

góvardhana [vardhana] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of Mount Govardhana "where cows thrive", near Vṛndāvana; it was raised by the child Kṛṣṇa to protect his Shepherds from the storm of Indra; cf. Giridhara, Nagarājadhara | hist. np. of Govardhana₁, court poet of the Bengal king Lakshmanasena (12th century); he is the author of the collection of poems Aryāsaptaśatī; Jayadeva considers him a master of erotic composition; he is also credited with the Kātantrakaumudī, commentary on the Kātantra | hist. np. of the pandita Govardhana₂, author of the Nyāyabodhinī | geo. Govardhana monastery, founded by Saṃkara in Purī.
govardhanapūjā [pūjā] f. soc. festival in honor of Kṛṣṇa, celebrated on the 3rd day of dīpāvali.
govardhanamaṭha [maṭha] m. geo. np. of the monastery Govardhana₃, founded by Saṃkara₁ in Purī.
govaśā | vaśā | f. sterile cow or one that has not yet calved.
govrndāraka | vrndāraka | m. choice bull.
govrsa [vrsa] m. bull.

gośālā [śālā] fn Gośāla stable — m. Gośāla hist. np. of Makkhali Gośāla "(born in) the stable"; he was born in Magadha in the mankha mendicant caste, in the 5th century BC; he was a student and then rival of Mahāvīra, and founded the sect of the materialist renunciants |ājīvika|; he lived naked and begged for his food in his hand; he professed the predestination of a deterministic fate | niyati |; he denied the doctrine of retributions | karman | and free will.

gósakhi |sakhi| m. ved. |"friend of cattle" | rich in cattle. gosthá stha mn stable, cattle pen fair, meeting place, gathering place — n. conversation; speech; short one-act drama — f. goșthā stable — f. gosthī assembly, association, company; guild; partnership | conversation, dialogue; debate; not. scholastic debate (between historical or mythical scholars); symposium | mod. club of (2nd century) enthusiasts.
goṣṭhalīlā [līlā] f. games in the stable.
gosthaśva [śvan₁] m. farm dog that barks for no reason | (figuratively) person who spends their time denigrating others.

gospada | pada | n. cow hoofprint; puddle | inhabited place (marked with hoofprints). agospadāni desert places. gospadapūram vṛṣṭo devaḥ it rains so hard it fills the hoofprints. yāny ujjahāra bhagavān vyāso vyākaraṇāmbudheḥ tāni kim padaratnāni bhānti pāṇinigoṣpade || [Nārāyaṇa₃] How could these jewels of speech, extracted by the Venerable Vyāsa from the ocean of grammars, shine in the puddle of Pāṇini?
gosamdāya [saṃdāya] amnf gosaṃdāyā which confers a cow.
gosava |sava₂| m. soc. rite ekāha where the sacrificer receives an aspersion |abhiṣeka| of cow's milk; it is prescribed as a remedy for the crime of brahma hatyā.

gosvāmin [svāmin] m. owner of a cow; one who has cattle | phil. master of his passions | soc. religious title of Gosvāmī "Shepherd" ["one who controls his senses"] in the Gaudīya tradition of Caitanya pl. gosvāminas hist. the six shepherds of the Vṛndāvana, Bengali disciples of Caitanya; cf. Rūpa, Rag hunāthadāsa, Jīva, Prabhupāda₁ || pkt. gosain. gosvāmīmahārāja soc. Vaishnava religious title; cf. gaudīya.
gohita [hita₂] amnf gohitā good for cows.
goṇa [pkt. go] m. ox, bovine — f. goṇī cow large grain sack — m. goni ifc. which is worth (iic.) cows. pañcagoni amn bought for five cows.

gótama [gotama] m. ved. np. of the ṛṣi Go tama "of the High Word", son of Rahūgaņa of the āngirasa clan, author of hymns of the Rgveda | hist. np. of Akṣapāda Gotama₁, ancient logician (between the 6th and 3rd century BC); the origin of the Nyāyasūtra is attributed to him.
gotara [gotara] m. bovine that can pull a cart like a plow — f. gotarā cow that calves a cow every year.
gotā [pkt. go] f. cow.

gotrá [gotra] n. stable | family, exogamous clan, lineage; patronymic | soc. Brahmin lineage name, generally corresponding to a mythical sage [rsi]; originally eight (linked to the Saptarși and Agastya), the lineages have subdivided extensively; they are traditionally grouped into 49 ancestral groups [pravara₁]; a Kṣatriya's gotra is transmitted to him by his puro hita. pacati gotram (pej.) he uses his gotra for nutritional purposes.
gotraja |ja| amnf gotrajā born in the family — m. parent.
gotravādin [vādin] amnf gotravādinī soc. holder of the importance of lineage; opp. abhimānavādin.
gotraskhalana [skhalana] n. the act of being called by someone else's name.
godhā f. tendon | leather bracelet on the left arm preventing injuries from a bowstring | bio. monitor lizard; lizard, iguana.
godhūma m. organic. ved. bot. Triticum aesti vum, wheat; syn. sumana.

gopá [gopa₂] m. herdsman, cowherd, herdsman | protector, guardian | myth. np. of Gopa, epith. of the young Kṛṣṇa "Master of the herds" — f. gopī cowherd, shepherdess | myth. one of the many cowherds who were lovers of Kṛṣṇa | var. gopā id. | bd. np. of gopā, wife of Prince Siddhārtha.
gopakanyā [kanyā] f. farm girl, cowherd.
Gopāditya [āditya] m. hist. np. of Gopāditya, king of Kaśmīra (5th or 6th century); he restored the brahmanic order there | varṇāśramadharma|.

gopāṣṭamī [aṣṭamī] f. soc. 8th day of the clear fortnight of the month kārttika; on this day we celebrate the promotion of Kṛṣṇa to the rank of guardian of the flock; the cows are honored; they are washed, adorned with flowers, and offerings are made to them.
gopendra | indra | m. myth. np. of gopendra epith. of Kṛṣṇa "Best herdsman".
gópaka [agt. gup] mf gopikā guardian; not. herdsman.
gópana [act. gup] n. guard, protection; preservation | concealment.
gopī iic. gopa.
gopīcandana [candana] n. soc. white clay pro coming from Dvārakā used for face decoration by devotees of Vaishnava.
Gopīnātha [nātha] m. myth. np. of Gopīnātha, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "Master of the cowherds".

gopīyantra [yantra] n. mus. ["instrument of the herdsman" monochord instrument of the Baul tradition, consisting of a gourd fixed to a bamboo handle of about one meter, connected by a string; it holds the tonic; syn. ekatara.
gopotalikā [related to go] f. (vulgar) cow.
goptṛ [agt. gup] amnf goptrī that protects, protector — ifc. that hides, that conceals (iic.).

gommața m. jn. np. of the mythical ascetic Gommata, second son of Rsabhanātha, also called Bāhubalī; he is the object of a cult in Karnātaka; at Sravanabelagolā, a monolithic statue 19 cm high is the destination of a pilgrimage festival [kumbhamela], the mastakābhiṣeka, every 12 years. gommațeśvara [īśvara] m. jn. np. of the mythical renunciant gommața, deified as gommațesvara.
gola [related to guḍa] m. ball; sphere; globe |astr. celestial globe; terrestrial globe | soc. bastard son of a widow — f. golā playing ball, balloon.
golakrīdā [krīdā] f. soc. ball game.
golayantra [yantra] n. astr. instrument simulating celestial movements.

golādhyāya [adhyāya] m. lit. np. of the golādhyāya, chapter of the Siddhāntaśiromaņi dealing with the terrestrial and celestial globes | lit. np. of the golādhyāya₁, chapter of the Sarvasiddhāntarāja dealing with trigonometry.
golaka [golaka] m. ball, balloon | glans of the penis | soc. bastard son of a widow.

Govinda [govinda] m. myth. np. of Go vinda, epithet of the young Kṛṣṇa "Master of the skin holes" | hist. np. of Govinda₁ Dīkṣita, scholar at the court of Thanjavur from 1575 to 1634; he was an expert in advaita vedānta, astronomer, musician; he composed the Saṅgītasudhā for his pupil King Raghunātha₂ Nāyaka | hist. np. of Emperor Rāṣṭrakūṭa Govinda₂ (8th century); he succeeded his father Kṛṣṇa₁ upon his death in 774; Dhruva₁ succeeded him in 780 | hist. np. of Emperor Rāṣṭrakūṭa Govinda₃; he succeeded his father Dhruva₁ upon his death in 793; he extended the empire to the Gangetic Plain and conquered Kanyākubjā; Amoghavarṣa₁ succeeded him in 814 hist. np. of Emperor Rāstrakūta Govinda₄ (10th century); he intrigued to succeed his elder brother Amoghavarșa₂ in 930; incompetent, he was deposed by his loyalists and replaced by Amoghavarșa₃ in 936.
govindacandra [candra] m. hist. np. of King Govin dacandra; he reigned (~1114–1156) in Kanyākubja and Vārāṇasī, and fought the Ghaznavids and the Pālās; his son Vijayacandra succeeded him.
govindadāsa | dāsa | mr. hist. n.p. from govindadāsa, ascetic name of Yādavaprakāśa when he converted to the doctrine of Rāmānuja.
govindanātha [nātha] m. hist. np. of the philosopher govindanātha, disciple of gauḍapāda (8th century); Sankarācārya was his student.
govindabhāsya [bhāsya] n. lit. np. du śrī Go vindabhāṣya, commentary on the Vedāntasūtra due to Baladeva₁ Vidyābhūṣaṇa.
govindasvāmin [svāmin] m. lit. [KSS.] np. du brah mane Govindasvāmī; he left for Vārāṇasī with his sons Aśokadatta and Vijayadatta; the latter came to Rākṣasa by accident.
govindānanda [ānanda] m. hist. n.p. of the Bengali scholar Govindānanda (16th century); we owe him the Ratnaprabhā, commentary on the Sānkarabhāṣya, and the varşakrtyakaumudī.

Gauda [*guda] amnf gauda made of sugar, molasses — n. rum — m. [gaudada] geo. ["land of sugarcane"] name of the country Gauda (Central Bengal); its capital was Lakshmaṇavati soc. doctrine of the movement [sampradaya] of the

Bengal [gaudīya] | var. gaudī lit. poetic style [rīti] of the Gauda, bold and spirited, with long compounds; opp. vaidarbhī | pl. Gauḍās the Gauḍās, inhabitants of West Bengal | soc. (in a broad sense) Brahmins of the North of the Vindhya Mountains; cf. pañcagauda.
gaudadeśa [deśa] m. geo. Bengal.

gaudapāda [pāda] m. hist. np. of the Bengali philosopher gauḍapāda (8th century), commentator of several esoteric lessons [upanisad], close to Buddhism; he was the preceptor of Govin danātha; he is a precursor of the ad vaita idealism of Sankara₁; we owe to him notably the teaching of the Gaudapādakārikās, the Māndūkyakārikās, and the Agamaśāstra.

gaudapādakārikā [kārikā] f. pl. lit. np. of the Gaudapādakārikās, a collection of 215 verses teaching Vedānta and explaining advaita by the universality of the ātman; they are attributed to Gaudapāda.
gaudapādīya [īya] amnf gaudapādīyā lit. relating to Gauḍapāda; says not. of his kārikās, cf. Gaudapādakārikās.
gaudapādīyabhāsya [bhāsya] n. lit. np. of the Gaudapādīyabhāsya, commentary on the kārikās of Gaudapāda, attributed to Sankara₁ (controversial).
gauḍika [*guḍaika] amnf gauḍikā good for sugar (sugar cane).

gauḍīya [gauḍaīya] amnf gauḍīyā relating to Bengal |soc. refers to the Bengali Vaishnava [saṃpradāya] movement advocating devotion [bhakti], initiated by Caitanya; the main doctrinal work of this sect is the Bhāgavatapurāna.

gauṇa [*guṇa] amnf gauṇī relating to the three qualities [guna] | accessory, secondary | gram. (stantive noun) secondary purpose of a sentence; opp. pradhāna lit. metaphorical — f. Gauņī lit. meaning [vṛtti] metaphorical of a word. simho devadattah |Kumārila| Devadatta has the character of a lion (classical example of metaphorical transfer [gaunī vṛtti]).
gauṇakarma [karma] mn gram. secondary purpose semantic role (of verbs with two accusatives); opp. mukhyakarma.
gaunatva [tva] n. subsidiarity.
gauṇārtha [artha] n. gram. metaphorical sense of a word; opp. mukhyārtha — amnf gauṇārthā gram. used in its metaphorical sense.
gauṇika [*guṇaika] amnf gauṇikī re latif aux trois qualités | possessing subsidiary qualities.

Gautam₁₁á [*Gotama] m. myth. (patr.) descendant of Gotama | myth. np. of the saptarși Gautama₁, son of the angiras Dīrghatamā; he was the guru of Indra; he married Ahalyā, whom he cursed after she committed adultery with Indra; he cast a spell on the latter, whose body became covered with 1000

vaginas [yoni], which the Brahmins transformed into 1000 eyes; he also made his testicles fall off, which were replaced by the gods with those of a ram; Satānanda is his eldest son; cf. Trita, Tryam bakeśvara soc. lineage name [gotra]; cf. Akṣapāda, Kakṣīvān, Kṛpa, Hāridrumata | bd. not. family gotra of Prince Siddhārtha, future Buddha Sākyamuni | lit. np. of Gautama₁, vidūṣaka of the Mālavikāgnimitra — f. cf. gautamī.
gautamadharmasūtra [dharmasūtra] n. bed. n.p. from the gautamadharmasūtra, a text of laws attributed to Gau tama.

gautamī [f. Gautama₁] f. myth. np. of Gau tamī "(daughter) of Gautama₁", wife of Kaņva, adoptive mother of Śakuntalā | hist. np. of gautamī₁ Balaśrī, mother of Śālivāhana | geo. np. of the river gautamī₂, epith. of the Godāvarī.

gautamīputra [putra] m. hist. matr. of Gau tamīputra Śātakarņī, of the Indoscythian king [Śaka] Gautamīputra Śātakarņī (78–102), son of Śātakarņī of the line of the Sātavāhanās; kṣatrapa of Ujjayinī, he was crowned emperor as Śālivāhana in 78, founding the Saka era; his son Vasisthīputra₁ Śrīpulamāvi succeeded him in 102.
gaupavana [*Gopavana] amnf gaupa vanā who descends from Gopavana — m. pl. gaupa vanāh the descendants of Gopavana.
gaurá amnf gaurī white, pale; fair-skinned; yellow, blond; tawny; Brilliant — m. gars, friend (familiar address) | bio. zoo. Bos Gaurus, gaurus ox — f. cf. gaurī.
Gaurakṛṣṇa |kṛṣṇa| m. hist. np. of Gaurakṛṣṇa "Kṛṣṇa the clear", epith. of Caitanya.

Gauracandra [candra] m. hist. np. of Gauracandra, epith. of Caitanya "Bright as the moon". gaurapūrņimā [pūrņimā] f. soc. festival celebrating the birth of Caitanya; it is held at the beginning of March, at the full moon of phālgunī; cf. vasantotsava.

gaurānga [anga₁] amnf light-bodied gaurāngī; with Brilliant body — m. hist. n.p. from gaurānga, epith. by Caitanya “With the body of gold” | geo. his eponymous temple at Kāṭvā in Bengal — f. gaurāṅgī carda mome.
gaurakṣya cf. gorakṣya.

gaurava [*guru] amnf gauravā relating to the master [guru]; relating to Jupiter — n. weight, mass; gravity; importance, respectability; dignity | phon. the fact of a vowel or syllable being long; opp. lāghava | gram. heaviness, verbosity — ifc. res pect pour (iic.). pūrnatā gauravaya [Meghadūta] Full respect for the master (motto of the Sanskrit University of So manātha).
gauravasaṃvatsara [saṃvatsara] m. astr. [“year of Jupiter”] time of Jupiter’s transit through a sign of the zodiac [rāśi].
gauri iic. gaurī.
Gaurimunda [munda] m. bed. [KSS.] np. of king vidyādhara Gaurimuṇḍa, opponent of Na ravāhanadatta; cf. Matangadeva.
gaurirūpā [rūpa] f. similar to Gaurī₂.

Gaurī₂ [f. gaura] f. girl (not nubile); not. 8-year-old girl | bio. gaur cow | myth. np. of Gaurī₂, epith. of Pārvatī "with the milky complexion" | lit. |K.| np. of the nymph | apsaras | Gaurī₂, mother of Mahāśvetā | lit. [DKC.] np. of Gaurī₂ "White", second wife of Satyavarmā, mother of Somadatta₂.
gaurīpūjā |pūjā| f. soc. rites of worship of Pārvatī; cf. Rauravāgama.

gaurīvrata | vrata | n. soc. observance of Gaurī₂, observed notably in Gujarāt; Young girls fast for 5 days with a diet of milk, fruit and cereals, to obtain a good husband; sprouted barley is offered to the Goddess to implore fertility.
gaurīśankara [śankara] m. geo. np. of Mount Gaurīśaṅkara of the Rolvāliṅga range of the Himālaya (7134 m).
gaulakṣaṇiká [*golakṣaṇaika] amnf gaulakṣaṇikī soc. who studies the markings on the coat of a cow.
gaulmika [*gulmaika] m. soc. head of section.
gnā f. ved. female divinity | ang. queen.
grathana [act. granth] n. to bind, to attach — f. grathanā id.
grathitá [pp. granth] amnf grathitā bound, tied; bundled | arranged, classified | | theatre | composed (plot) | with knots; knotty.
√ granth var. grath v. [9] pr. (grathnāti) pr. r. (grathnīte) pp. (grathita) to join, unite; to attach, to bind lit. to compose, to arrange; to write — ps. (gra thyate) to be composed.

grantha |act. granth| m. act of binding together; bound collection; knot |literary work, text, book (on birch bark or palm leaf); not. ritual book | prayoga | | not. sacred literature of the Sikhs (Guru grantha Sahib) | script [lipi] used not. in Tibet for Sanskrit.
granthakāra [kāra] m. author (of a work) | var. granthakartr id.
granthakṛt [kṛt₂] m. author (of a work)
granthagranthi [granthi] m. lit. thorny stanza [śloka] of the Mah.; it is said that Vyāsa created them as soon as Ganesa threatened to catch up with him by writing the epic; there are 8800 in total.
granthadhāraka [dhāraka] m. editor, proofreader.
granthapāla | pāla | m. librarian.
granthapraśasti [praśasti] f. prologue of blessing of a work.
granthamālā |mālā| f. series of works.
granthastha [stha] amnf granthasthā refers to knowledge read from a book, considered inferior to memorized knowledge | kanthastha |.
granthālaya [ālaya] mn library.
granthāvali [āvali] f. series of works.
granthana [act. granth] ifc. nf gran thanā composition, arrangement of (iic.); binding (book).
