granthí [act. granth] m. knot; joint, articulation; bamboo stem knot | garment knot serving as a purse | protuberance, bundle | med. gland | tight knot; difficulty | lit. thorny stanza [śloka] of the Mah.; it is said that Vyāsa created them as soon as Ganesa threatened to catch up with him by writing the epic; there are 8800 in total.
granthiparna [parna] mn bio. bulbous plant.

granthiparnaka [ka] mn bio. odo rférante plant. nepālyo vallabhaih sārdhamārdraiņamadamandanāh granthiparnakapālīsu nayanti grīsmayāminīh [KM.] Nepalese women, adorned with fresh musk, spend summer nights with their lovers in the granthiparnaka avenues.
granthibandhana [bandhana] n. act of tying a knot | soc. not. act of tying together The clothes of the bride and groom during the wedding ceremony.
granthibheda [bheda] m. purse breaker.
granthirasa | rasa | m. med. hormone.
granthihara [hara] m. suppression of difficulties minister.

granthika [granthaika] m. narrator, scholar; astrologer, diviner | myth. [Mah.] np. of gran thika "scholar", false identity of Nakula disguised as master of horses [sūta₂], to hide at the court of King Virāṭa during the 13th year of exile of the Pāṇḍavās.
granthin [agt. granth] amnf granthinī Learned.
grabh cf. grah.
√ fat v. [1] pr. (grásati) pr. r. (grasate) pp. (grasta) to seize in one's mouth; to swallow, devour, gulp down; to make disappear; to eclipse (said of Rāhu) lat. grāmen; all. grasen; ang. grass.
grasana [act. gras] n. mouth, maw | act of seizing; act of swallowing, of gulping down.
grasiṣṇú [agt. gras] amnf that devours continuously. ^51
grasta [pp. gras] amnf grastā swallowed, devoured; seized; eclipsed; possessed (by a demon) — ifc. affected by, tormented by (iic.); implicated in (iic.). vādagrasto'rthaḥ a controversial point.
grastacetana | cetana | amnf grastacetanā rendered unconscious.

√ grah var. grabh v. [9] pr. (gṛbhṇāti) v. [9] pr. (gṛḥṇāti) pr. r. (gṛḥṇīté) pft. (jagrāha) aor. [3] (ajigrahat) aor. [5] (agrahīt) pp. (gṛhīta, gṛbhīta) abs. (gṛhītvā, gṛhya) pfp. (grāhya, gṛhya) inf. (grahītum) pf. (ati, anu, abhi, ut, upa, ni, pari, pra, prati, vi, sam) to take, seize, take possession of, acquire; to hold in hand; to grasp by (loc.) to apprehend, understand; to learn | to receive, accept; to take possession of; to obtain, gain | to eclipse; to steal | to capture, take prisoner; to overpower — ps. (gṛḥyate) to be taken, to be seized — ca. (grāhayati) to cause to be taken, to give, to render; to make understood — des. (jighṛkṣati) cf. jighṛkṣ || Eng. to grab; Ger. greifen; Fr. agripper, griffe. nāma grah to mention the name of. pāṇim grah soc. to take the hand (in the wedding ceremony). hastagrāham grah to hold by the hand. gṛhītā keśeṣu to seize by the hair. grhyatām dhanuḥ seize your bow. nātra munirdoṣaṃ grahīṣyati the wise man will find no fault in it. alamanyathā gṛhītvā do not misunderstand me. idam suvarnakankanam grhyatām [Hitopadeśa] Receive this gold bracelet. grhnīdhvam jyesthakanisthakramena [Vikramacarita] Share among yourselves according to seniority.

gráha [act. grah] m. action of seizing, grasping; taking, capture; confiscation, imprisonment phil. apprehension (by the senses); understanding | resolution possession, magical influence eclipse — agt. m. crocodile | ved. spoon, ladle, cup; not. soma ladle; spoonful, (contents of a) ladle phil. organ of apprehension; there are 8: the 5 sensory faculties [buddhīndriya] of hearing [śrotra], touch [tvak], sight [cakṣus], taste [jihvā] and smell [ghrāṇa], to which are added the intellect [manas], the hand [hasta] and the voice [vāc]; they are associated with the 8 respective sensations [atigraha] myth. abducting genie, astral influence; not. epith. of the dragon Rahu, the eclipsing asura; cf. navagraha ast. planet or star in general; cf. navagraha math. symb. the number 9 | phil. |Tantra| possession by a supernatural being; it can affect any adult male, except devotees of Mahādeva diton; cf. devagraha, pitrgraha, siddhagraha, rāksasagraha, gandharva Graha, yakṣagraha, piśācagraha — ifc. that which seizes, that which takes hold of (ii.). graham gam to be taken prisoner. hastagraham grah to hold by the hand.
grahadoṣa |doṣa₂| mr. astr. astral misfortune.
gráhapati | pati | m. myth. np. of Grahapati, epith. of Candra "chief of the planets".
grahalāghava | lāghava | n. astr. n.p. from the Gra halāghava, treatise on the movement of the planets by Gaņeśa₁ Daivajña.

gráhavarman | varman | m. hist. np. of King Graha varmā Maukhari of Kanyākubjā (late 6th century); he married Rājyaśrī, daughter of King Prabhākara₁; he was killed in a surprise attack by King Devagupta of Mālava.
grahaśānti |śānti| f. soc. rite of pacification of malignant influences.

gráhaṇa [agt. grah] amnf grahaṇā that holds, that seizes (iic.); that persists — act. n. act of seizing; taking; acquisition | possession (by a demon); eclipse | acceptance; act of assuming a form; taking of a garment | phil. (seized by the spirit) perception; acquisition of knowledge.
grahi [agt. grah] ifc. amnf who holds (iic.).
grahītṛ [agt. grah] amnf grahītrī who takes, who seizes | who perceives, who understands.
grābhá |agt. grabh| amnf grābhā that seizes — m. ved. demon causing diseases.

grāma m. Vedic. group of related families [sajāta], semi-nomadic, headed by a chief [Grāmaṇī] responsible to the tribal chief | hamlet, village; inhabitants, people; crowd, multitude — ifc. set of (iic.) | (music) tone, scale; (math.) symb. the number 3 || Pali gāma. grāmatas adv. from the village. grāme grāme in each village. grāmāt pūrvaḥ parvataḥ the mountain is to the east of the village.
grāmakāma [kāma] amnf grāmakāmā who loves the village.
grāmacaṭaka | caṭaka | mf grāmacaṭikā house sparrow.
Grāmaṇī [nī₂] m. village chief; chief in gen. | soc. clan chief member of the royal circle |ratnin| | myth. n.p. of Grāmaṇī, epith. from Gaṇeśa "the leader".
grāmaṇīputra | putra | mr. soc. son of the village chief | var. grāmaniputra id.
grāmatakṣa | takṣan | mr. village carpenter.
grāmatā [tā] f. pl. group of villages.
gāmatva |tva| n. landscape of villages.
grāmadeya | deya | n. soc. donation of the revenues of a village to sponsor a religious building or a ceremony.
grāmadevatā [devatā] f. soc. village deity; we celebrate our cult at the edge of the habitat | var. grāmadevatī soc. id.
grāmabāhya |bāhya| amnf grāmabāhyā who lives outside the village; opp. grāmavāsa var. grāmavāhya f. grāmavāhyā mod. id.
grāmavāsa [vāsa₁] amnf grāmavāsā who lives in a village; opp. grāmabāhya.
grāmavāsin [vāsin₁] mf grāmavāsinī who lives in a village.
grāmika [grāmaika] amnf grāmikī rural, rustic — m. villager; village chief.
grāmín [grāmain] amnf grāminī rural, rustic — m. villager; village chief.
grāmīṇa [grāmaīna] amnf grāmīṇā f. grāmīṇī proper to the village; specific to a rustic, coarse, vulgar village — m. villager, peasant.
grāmyá [grāmaya] amnf grāmyā rela tif to a village; produced by a village | rustic; vulgar | domesticated; cultivated; opp. āranya — m. villager — n. patois | village terroir | country food.
grāmyátā [tā] f. rusticity; vulgar language, patois.
grāmyátva [vat] n. id. agrāmyatvam urbanity.
grāmyádharma | dharma | m. destiny of a villager | soc. ["right of a villager"] (opp. the duty of a recluse) practice of sex.
grāmyádharmin |in| amnf grāmyadharminī soc. afflicted with sexual addiction.
grāva iic. grāvan.
grāvarohaka [rohaka] amnf grāvarohakā which grows on stones — m. bio. bot. Physalis flexuosa.
grāvastút [stut] m. ved. priest assisting the hotr in the solemn sacrifice "who praises the soma millstones".
grāvan m. stone; not. ved. millstone for pressing soma. grāvni rekheva as if engraved in marble.
grāsa [obj. gras] m. mouthful, morsel; nour riture. prathame grāse makṣikā pātā | "at the first bite, a fly falls" | We are immediately upset.
grāsatrpti [trpti] f. satiety | du. grāsatrptī phil. [Abhinavagupta] joy of realization in the present, enjoying a time without division between past and future.
grāsāmbu | ambu | n. to eat and drink.
grāh [ca. grah] v. [10] pr. (grāhayati) pp. (grāhita) to make take, to give, to render.

grāhá |agt. grah| amnf grāhī that seizes, that captures, that takes, that receives (iic.) | monster; bird of prey; crocodile, shark — act. m. capture, seize; disease, paralysis. grāham adv. ifc. in order to take (iic.).

grāhaka [agt. grah] amnf grāhikā who takes, who captures; who holds captive | who receives; who buys | who perceives | bd. (aspect) subjective (of perception); opp. grāhya — ifc. who seizes (iic.) — m. phil. subject (who perceives) | falcon, bird of prey | myth. epith. of Rāhu the eclipse.
grāhi iic. grāhin.
grāhiphala [phala] n. bio. elephant apple, "astringent fruit" of the kapittha.
grāhita [pp. ca. grah] amnf grāhitā who has been forced or invited to take.

grāhin [agt. grah] amnf grāhiṇī ifc. that takes (iic.); that accepts (iic.); that holds, that catches (iic.) | that obtains; that keeps, that retains (iic.) | that scrutinizes, that spies; that perceives (iic.) | that attracts the attention of, that fascinates (iic.) | med. astringent; constipating.
grāhya [pfp. [1] grah] amnf grāhyā that must be received; that can be grasped; perceptible | bd. (aspect) objective (of perception); opp. grāhaka.
grīva m. cou.
grīvadaghná [daghna] amnf grīvadaghnā f. grīvadaghnī who has (water) up to their neck.
grīvā [f. grīva] f. neck, nape | pl. id.
grīṣmá [gras] m. the hot season [ṛtu], summer (month of jyaistha and āṣādha).
grīṣmaprāvṛṣa [prāvṛṣ] n. sg. summer; including the monsoon.
grīṣmavasanta |vasanta| m. of. summer and spring time.
graiva [*grīvā] amnf graivā concerning the nape of the neck or the neck — n. ["located at the nape of the neck"] collar.
graiveya [*grīvāīya] n. [“located at the nape of the neck”] collar — m. chain around the neck of an elephant.
graiveyaka |ka| n. necklace — m. chain around the neck of an elephant | pl. jn. class of 9 deities forming a necklace around the neck of Lokapurușa.
graisma [*grīṣma] amnf graismī summer; concerning summer | not. sown in summer.
graiṣmaka [*grīṣmaaka] amnf graiṣmikā sown in summer | (debt) due in summer. নল gla [agt. glā] amnf glā tired.
√ glah [related to grah] v. [1] pr. r. (glahate) to bet; to play (dice) with (i.) to (acc.) | win at the game. ন্লিছ gláha [act. glah] m. dice throw; dice game; dice stake | bet.
gláhana [act. glah] n. the act of playing dice.
√ glā v. [4] pr. (glāyati) pr. r. (glāyate) pp. (glāna) to be tired, to languish; to wither | to feel aversion for (i. abl.) — ca. (glāpayati) pp. (glāpita) to exhaust, to wither; to cause to perish.
glāná [pp. glā] amnf glānā exhausted, worn out; emaciated; withered; failing; sick — n. exhaustion, languor; illness; decline.

glāni [act. glā] f. weariness; exhaustion, languor; depression; debility, illness | decline, decay. yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati Bhārata abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānam srjāmyaham | [BhG.] Whenever, O Bhārata, justice declines and injustice increases, I manifest myself.
glāpita [pp. ca. glā] amnf glāpitā emaciated.
glau [glā] m. ball | the Moon.
gh

gha [agt. han₁] ifc. amnf ghā that strikes, that kills (iic.) — f. ghā blow. ঘ gha₁ nota. gram. fictitious word designating The secondary suffixes of superlatives and comparatives tara and tama, as well as rūpa, and the suffixal use of kalpa, that, bruva, etc. | gram. substitute iy of the v of the secondary suffix vatup after kim and idam.
ghakāra [(gha)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'gha'.
ghañ nota. gram. primary suffix krt₂ denoting activity; it forms action nouns like bhāva.

√ ghat v. [1] pr. r. (ghatate) pp. (ghatita) pf. (ut, vi, sam) to be busy, to work; to apply oneself, to strive to; to achieve (loc.) | to function correctly — ca. (ghaṭayati) ca. (ghāṭayati) to procure, to produce; to accomplish; to make, to fashion, to assemble | to unite, to connect; to render service (acc.) to (g.) — intens. (jāghaṭīti) to put all one's efforts into acc. . ghaṭamānaḥ m. lit. said of a poet who practices with talent but does not publish his verses. tadubhayathāpi ghaṭate Both are possible; it works in both cases. na ghatetārthasambandhaḥ One should not work with a view to getting rich. ਬਟ ghaṭa [agt. ghaṭ] amnf ghaṭā very busy with (loc.) — m. pot, jug, jar, earthenware vessel | (in fig.) head | bio. frontal sinus of the elephant | phil. the perishable body (as a vessel containing the soul [ātman]) — f. ghaṭī small jar | clepsydra, clock | 24-minute time measure; cf. ghațikā — f. cf. ghaṭā. ardho ghaṭo ghoṣamupaiti nūnam [SRBh.] Half-empty pots really do make a lot of noise (Fools are noisy).

ghaṭakañcuki [kañcukin] n. soc. sexual rite tāntrika and śākta; the bodice |kañcuka| of different women is placed in a jar; The men present at the ceremony draw one at random, then couple with the woman thus chosen.

ghaṭakarpara [karpara] m. hist. np. of the poet Ghataparpara, one of the nine jewels | navaratna | of the court of King Vikramāditya; he composed a very artificial eponymous poem. ghațatva [tva] n. quality of pot. ghațatvatva phil. [NN.] specifier of the quality of pot.
ghaṭapradīpa [pradīpa] m. du. the pot and the lamp.

ghaṭapradīpanyāya [nyāya] m. lit. maxim of the pot and the lamp; Abhinavagupta uses it to explain the relationship between the literal and suggested meanings of the phrase, which are not as different as the pot and the lamp. ghațavat [vat] amnf ghațavatī who possesses a pot. ghaṭavadbhūtalam n. phil. [NN.] ground on which a pot rests.
ghatastha | stha| amnf ghatasthā phil. residing in the physical body.
ghatasthayoga | yoga | m. phil. preparation of the body by hathayoga. ghaṭasthayogasādhanā soc. practice of physical yoga.

Ghatotkaca [utkaca] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Ghatotkaca "Egghead", son of Bhīma and the rākṣasī Hidimbā; by his magic | māyā | he knew how to make himself invisible and gigantic; Kṛṣṇa sent him to fight Karna, who had to use the magical weapon that Indra had given him and that he intended for Arjuna to kill him; Barbarīka is his son by his wife Maurvī | hist. np. of the king Ghatotkacagupta, who reigned at the beginning of the 4th century; Candragupta₁ succeeded him.
ghatodara | udara | mr. myth. epith. by Ganeśa “Ventripotent”.

ghaṭaka |agt. ghaṭ| amnf ghaṭikā that applies, that works, that takes pains — m. pot, jar | matchmaker — f. ghaṭikā jar | water clock, clepsydra | astr. period of 24 minutes, dividing the day into 60 equal parts, also called nādī; it comprises 60 divisions | vinādīkā|.

ghaṭana [act. ghaṭ] n. connection with (i. ii.) — f. ghaṭanā manner of acting; occupation (with the angle loc. iic.); work | act of procuring; contribution. ghatanām nī to accomplish. ghaṭanāṃ yā to take effect; to succeed. yā ghaṭanā samāpatat what happened to him.

ghaṭā [f. ghaṭa] f. effort | crowd, gathering; assembly | collection, assembly | troop of war elephants assembled to fight. madajaladurdināndhakāragajaghaṭitaghanaghaṭāpa prapalāyate K. Despite being defended on all sides by the compact troop formed of elephants blackened by the downpour of their rutting exudate, (fortune) flees.
ghațita [pp. ghaț] amnf ghațitā planned, foreseen; attempted | arrived — ifc. produced by; made of (iic.); connected with, involving (iic.).
√ ghaṭṭ v. [1] pr. r. (ghaṭṭate) pf. (vi, sam) ca. (ghattayati) to rub, touch; to strike, move; to agitate, shake | to have a bad influence on (acc.) | to insult, slander.
ghatta [obj. ghatt] m. quay, jetty; ford; bathing place; steps leading down to a river, pond or basin || hi. ghaț.

ghantaka [related to ghantā] m. bio. bot. Bi gnonia suaveolens, trumpet vine (with bell-shaped flowers) — f. ghantikā small bell, bell. ਬਾਟਾ ghaṇṭā f. jingle bell, bell, gong. ghantākarņa [karņa] m. myth. [Harivaṃśa] np. from the piśāca Ghaṇṭākarṇa, devotee [bhakta] śaiva "wearing a bell in his ear" (to avoid hearing the name of Vișnu pronounced); Kṛṣṇa meets him at Ba darī when he goes to pray to Siva to grant Rukmiņī a son equal in qualities to himself; Meanwhile, the piśāca, desiring liberation, is on the road to Dvārakā to pray to Kṛṣṇa at the suggestion of Siva; Kṛṣṇa reveals himself to him and liberates him; it is explained that his concern not to hear the name of Vișnu made him have him constantly in mind, deserving liberation through this permanent meditation on the Lord.
Ghaṇṭāpatha | patha | mr. bed. n.p. of the Ghaṇṭāpatha, commentary on the mahākāvya Kirātārjunīya of Bhāravi by Mallinātha₁.

ghanṭāmāgha | Māgha | m. lit. "Bell-belled Māgha", epithet of Māgha for having composed the verse (4.20) of the Śiśupālavadha that follows. udayati vitatordhvaraśmirajjāvahimarucau hi madhāmni yāti cāstam | vahati giririyam vilambighantādvayaparivāritavāraņendralīlām lit. [ZPV.] when the Sun rises, a burning splendor darting upwards the strings of its rays, and the Moon sets with its cold brilliance, this mountain [Raivataka] evokes the grace of a royal elephant encircled by a bell hanging on each side.
ghaṇṭārava | rava | m. bell sound.

ghaná [agt. han₁] amnf ghanā Vedic destroyer thick; compact, solid; dense, massive; broken | deep (sound); dark (color) — ifc. filled with; consisting solely of (iic.) | (iic.) in its pure state — m. thick cloud; solid body; mace, hammer, metal club | med. two-month-old embryo | lit. mode of recitation [pāṭha] complex of Vedic texts | math. cube (number); solid body, volume — n. metallic percussion instrument, gong, bell | metal; iron | darkness | cf. ghanapāṭha — f. ghanā type of woman small, plump, dark-skinned, sexually active; opp. ślathā. ghanam adv. massively. ghanam dhvan to resound with a deep sound. ghanībhū to thicken, condense, solidify; freeze. ghanīkr to solidify; freeze. ghanīkṛta solidified; frozen. ghanībhūtam ice. vijñānaghanaḥ pure knowledge. abhraghanah mass of clouds. ghanam dadhi curdled milk. ghane niśīthe in the dark night.
ghanakapha [kapha] m. hail.
ghanatā [tā] f. density | condensation.
ghanapāṭha [pāṭha] m. phon. "compact" recitation of the Veda [vikṛtipāṭha]; it iterates the pattern: AB, BA, ABC, CBA, ABC, pause.
ghanapāṭhin |in| m. Vedic scholar mastering the 11 modes of recitation; title linked to a first degree in the traditional teaching of the Veda.
ghanamūla |mūla| n. math. cube root.
ghanarasa [rasa] concentrated extract; decoction | organic. latex plant | |"cloud juice" | water, rain.
ghanaśyāma [śyāma] amnf ghanaśyāmā black as a storm cloud — m. myth. epith. of Krsna.
ghanasāra | sara | amnf ghanasārā firm, solid — m. camphor.
ghanasāravilepa [vilepa] m. myth. np. of Gha nasāravilepa, epith. of Hanumān "Anointed with camphor".
ghanāghaná | red. | amnf ghanāghanā who strikes hard; quarrelsome; unleashed; ved. said of In dra | compact, thick (cloud) — m. storm cloud elephant in rut.
ghanānta [anta] m. ["end of clouds"] autumn.
gharghara [onomatopoeia] amnf ghargharā f. ghargharī which gurgles — m. geo. np. of the Ghar ghara, tributary north of the Gangā; mod. Gogra.
gharmá [ghṛma] m. burning heat, hot season; inner fire; sweat | gr. o ; lat. for mus ; ang. warm.
gharmāṃśu [aṃśu] m. sun (with burning rays); opp. śītāṃśu.
√ ghas v. pft. (jaghasa) aor. [2] (aghasat) (pr. cf. ad₁) to eat, to devour — des. (jighhatsati) to want to eat. mā gdha (prohibitive) does not eat.
ghasa [agt. ghas] m. that which devours | myth. devouring demon.
ghasana [act. ghas] n. action of devouring.
ghasmara [ghasmara] amnf ghasmarā voracious — ifc. passionate about (iic.).
ghāṇṭika [*ghaṇṭāika] m. soc. minstrel accompanied by a bell; processional reciter ringing a bell in front of idols.
ghāt [ca. han₁] v. [10] pr. (ghātáyati) to put to death; to cause to be killed.
ghāta [act. han₁] m. blow, wound, murder — agt. f. ghātī ifc. that kills (iic.). ripughātaḥ mf ripughātī that kills the enemies. mātrghātah matricide.

ghātaka [agt. han₁] amnf ghātikā meur trier | pilld. kākadadhighātakanyāyaḥ maxim of the crow that steals the curd, a synecdoche; the curd must be protected from all animals, not just the beautiful crow.
ghātana [agt. han₁] amnf ghātanā who kills — act. n. murder; immolation.
ghāti [act. han₁] f. blow, wound | bird hunting; bird net.

ghātin [agt. han₁] ifc. amnf ghātinī who killed, murderer of (iic.). kumāraghātī who kills a child or a prince. śīrṣaghātī who kills by beheading. pitrvyaghātī who killed his paternal uncle. mātulaghātī who killed his maternal uncle. pitrvyaghātī putro janitā A son will be born who will kill his uncle.
ghāsá [obj. ghas] m. food; pasture, meadow; grazing, hay, fodder. ghāsād ghāsam little by little, gradually.

ghi nota. gram. [saṃjñā₂] fictional word designating a class of nouns (ending in i or u and not having feminine declension), such as agni or viṣṇu ; they must be put first in a copulative compound; sakhi, although masculine stem, is not in this class, nor is pati.
ghinun nota. gram. primary suffix [kṛt₂] of agent noun formation in in.
ghu nota. gram. [saṃjñā₂] refers to verbs derived from the roots dā₁, dā₂, dhā₁ and dhā₁.
√ ghuṭ v. [6] pr. (ghuṭati) v. [1] pr. r. (ghoṭate) to resist.
ghuṭa |agt. ghuṭ| mf ghuṭī ankle.
ghuṇa [agt. ghūrṇ] m. forest insect, woodworm.
ghuṇākṣara [akṣara] n. pattern hollowed by a worm in wood or a book, resembling writing; fortuitous event, coincidence.
ghurghur [onomatopoeia] ind. neighing, hissing, whining.
√ ghus v. |1| pr. (ghoṣati) pp. (ghuṣṭa, ghuṣita) pf. (ut) to make noise; to resound; to ring out; to declare, to proclaim — ca. (ghoṣayati) to cause to be proclaimed.
ghuṣita [pp. ghuṣ] amnf ghuṣitā noisy; proclaimed. ঘুষ্ট ghuṣṭa |pp. ghuṣ| amnf ghuṣṭā noisy; proclaimed | filled with clamor.
ghusrna [obj. ghṛṣ] n. saffron || pkt. ghuṣiṇa.
ghūka m. bio. owl.
ghūkāri |ari| m. | "enemy of the owl" | crow.
√ ghūrn v. [6] pr. (ghūrnati) v. [1] pr. r. (ghūrṇate) pp. (ghūrṇita) pf. (vi) to move, to stir.
ghūrṇa [agt. ghūrṇ] amnf ghūrṇā Who comes and goes, Who is restless.
√ ghr v. [3] pr. (jigharti) v. [1] pr. (gharati) aor. [4] (aghārṣīt) pp. (ghṛta) pf. (abhi, ā) ved. shine, illuminate; burn | sprinkle; humidify — ca. (ghārayati) id.
ghṛṇā [ghṛna] f. pity, compassion, tenderness.
ghṛṇi [ghṛni] m. ved. light; flame; Sun; day | passion.
ghṛṇin [ghṛṇāin] amnf ghṛṇinī compa tissant.

ghṛtá [pp. ghṛ] amnf ghṛtā sprinkled — n. melted butter, clarified butter; syn. ājya | (figuratively) symbol of abundance || hi. ghī. āyur ghṛtam butter gives strength. yad aghṛtam abhojanam tat Without butter, nothing is food.
ghṛtapaśu | paśu | m. soc. animal made of butter for sacrifice.
ghṛtapīta [pīta₁] amnf ghṛtāpīta Who drank melted butter.
ghṛtapūra | pūra | m. | "full of butter" | a sweet made from flour, milk, coconut and butter.
ghṛtávat [vat] amnf ghṛtavatī full of butter; well greased — adv. like butter.
ghṛtaścút [ścut₂] amnf ved. oozing with butter.

ghṛtācī [ac] f. ["filled with ghī"] oblation spoon myth. [Mah.] np. of the nymph [apsaras] ghṛtācī "Who bows before the butter of sacrifice"; her sight caused the ṛṣi Bharadvāja to spill his seed to give birth to Drona; she appeared in the form of a magnificent parrot to Vyāsa, and he spilled his seed to give birth to Suka; [Rām.] she gave 100 very beautiful daughters to King Kuśanābha.
√ঘৃষ্ ghṛṣ v. [1] pr. (gharṣati) pp. (ghṛṣṭa) pf. (ava, ni, sam) to rub; to grind || ang. crush; fr. écrase. ঘৃষ্ট ghṛṣṭa [pp. ghṛṣ] amnf ghṛṣṭā rubbed, polished; worn; ground.

ghṛṣṇeśvara [ghusṛṇaīśvara] m. geo. np. of ghṛṣṇeśvara, one of the 12 radiant signs of Śiva [jyotirlinga], created by Pārvatī by rubbing his hands with saffron; it is established at the temple of the village of Verul near Ellora in Mahārāṣṭra.
ghota m. horse.
gotaka [ka] m. horse — f. gotikā mare.
ghoṇā f. nose; nostril; beak.

ghorá amnf ghorā ved. venerable, sublime (said of gods, singers | angirasas | ) | terrible, frightening, violent — n. horror, terror |soc. black magic; poison — m. myth. np. of Ghora "Terrible", son of Angirā — f. ghorā night. ghoram adv. terribly; very.
ghorácakṣus | cakṣus | amnf ghoracakṣuṣī Who has the evil eye.
ghorátara |tara| amnf ghoratarā compar. more terrible; terrifying.
ghoratā |tā| f. the state of being terrifying.
ghoravīrya | vīrya | amnf ghoravīryā whose strength is terrible.
ghorākṛti |ākṛti| amnf in terrifying form.
Ghorāhi [ahi] m. myth. n.p. of Ghorāhi, epith. of Kāliya "terrible serpent".
ghóṣa [act. ghuṣ] m. noise, cries, sounds; rumbling (thunder); rumor; tumult; proclamation | soc. hamlet | phon. voiced phoneme. gangāyām ghoṣaḥ hamlet near the Ganges.
ghoṣavat [vat] amnf ghoṣavatī phon. voiced (phoneme); opp. aghoșa — f. Ghoșavatī myth. np. of the magical vīṇā ghoṣavatī, offered by the nāga Vasunemi to King Udayana for having saved him.
ghoṣaka [agt. ghuṣ] amnf ghoṣikā ifc. Who proclaims — m. bio. climbing gourd, like the sponge gourd bot. Luffa fætida.
ghoṣaṇa [agt. ghuṣ] amnf ghoṣaṇā retaining — act. n. proclamation — f. ghoṣaṇā id.
ghosanasthāna [sthāna] n. soc. place of proclamation (not. of a sentence).

Ghoșita m. hist. np. of Ghoșita, treasurer of King Udayana of Kauśāmbī (6th century), contemporary of Buddha; he built for his own use the Ghoșitārāma monastery, which was destroyed in the 5th century by King Hūṇa Toramāṇa.

ghoṣin [agt. ghuṣ] amnf ghoṣiṇī noisy, resounding; sonorous | phon. (phoneme) sonorous; opp. aghosa | Who proclaims; herald. ਬੁ ghna |agt. han₁| ifc. amnf ghnā Who strikes, Who kills, Who fells, Who destroys, Who suppresses (iic.).
ghnát [ppr. han₁] amnf ghnatī by killing, by destroying.
ghnī cf. han₂.
ghnya |han₁| ifc. mf ghnyā to be slaughtered.
√ ghrā v. [1] pr. (jighrati) pft. (jaghrau) pp. (ghrāta) pf. (ā) to sniff, smell, smell — ca. (ghrāpáyati) to make sniff | lat. fragrare; fr. fra grance; ang. fragrant; hollandais geur.
ghrāṇa [instr. ghrā] n. nose | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the sense [buddhīndriya] of smell; it is governed [niyantr] by the Aśvinau; the associated perception |tanmātra| is smell |gandha|.
ghrātá [pp. ghrā] amnf ghrātā smelled, sniffed. n
nīp var. nīs nota. gram. suffix giving the feminine theme in ī.

c ca conj. cl. and, also, as well as | but, on the other hand, although; if | even; precisely, only || lat. that. api ca even. ca ... ca and ... and; not only ... but also; hardly ... than. caiva also. tathā ca and; likewise, also. na ... ca neither ... nor; and not ... not || lat. neque. ca ... naca however ... nevertheless. naca ... ca nevertheless ... yet. ... varam na ca rather ... than; better ... than. táva ca máma ca to you and me. na pūrvāhņe na ca parāhņe neither in the morning nor in the afternoon. rāmah Sitā ca vanam gacchati Rama and Sitā go to the woods (example showing that in Sanskrit the verb agrees with the last component of a subject conjunction).

√c sad₁ v. [1] pr. (sīdati) pft. (sasāda) pp. (sanna) pf. (ava, ā, ut, upa, ni, pari, pra, prati, vi, sam) to sit, to be seated | to be enthroned, to reside | to slump, to faint; to wither, to succumb; to despair — ca. (sādáyati) to seat, to make sit; to place in or on (loc.) | to ruin, to overthrow, to destroy, to cause to perish, to reduce to nothing — intens. r. (sāsadyate) to slump | gr. εζομαι; lat. sedeo; all. sitzen; ang. to sit. sīdanti me aṃgāni I am going to faint.
cakāra (ca)kāra m. the sound or letter 'ca' gram. coordinating conjunction 'ca'.
Cakārakukṣi |kukṣi| m. lit. np. of Cakārakukṣi "who has a belly full of 'ca'", ironic epith. of Vyāsa.
√ cakās [pft. kās] v. [2] pr. (cakāsti) pft. perished. (cakāsām)(cakāra) shine.
cakita amnf cakitā trembling, fearful, frightened, intimidated — n. timidity; anxiety; alarm. cakitam trembling, with fear. cakitam nrpasya pārśvam upaimi I approach the king with fear.
cakṛvas [ppft. kṛ₁] amnf cakruṣī having done — n. gram. perfect (of any verb).
cakora m. bio. zoo. Perdix rufa, red partridge or rock partridge; it is said to feed on moonlight, and that its eyes turn red in the presence of poisoned food.
cakoralocana [locana] f. "with partridge eyes", epith. of pretty woman in poetry.

cakrá [pft. kṛ₁] n. wheel, circle, disc; cycle, circular movement | the royal wheel, emblem of sovereignty; army | region, country; sovereignty | myth. flaming disc, solar weapon of Vishnu; cf. Sudarśana | phil. [Tantra] mystical circular diagram phil. [yoga] center of psychic energy, the 7 principal ones being: mūlādhāra, svādhisthāna, maṇipūra, anāhata, viśuddha, ājñā₂ and sahasrāra || lat. circus; fr. cercle; pali cakka. cakram car to travel by chariot.
cakrakrīdā [krīdā] f. soc. ["circular meeting"] secret krama ritual of collective orgy; syn. cakrame laka, vīramelāpa.
cakratīrtha [tīrtha] n. myth. [VAP.] np. of Ca kratīrtha, best holy place of Pātāla according to Cya vana.
cakradhara | dhara | amnf cakradhara who carries the wheel — m. soc. emperor; king.

Cakrapāṇi₁ [pāṇi] m. myth. n.p. of Cakrapāṇi₁, epith. of Vișnu “who has the disc in hand” | hist. n.p. by Cakrapāṇi₁ Datta, 11th century Bengali physician, main commentator on Caraka, author of the Ayurveda manual Cikitsāsaṃgraha.
cakrapāda [pāda] m. ["circular foot"] elephant.
cakrapurusa [purusa] m. myth. np. of cakrapurușa, personification of Sudarsana, flaming disk of Vișnu; he is represented associated with GadādevīKaumodakī.
cakrapūjā [pūjā] f. soc. [Tantra] rite of symbolic union.
cakramukha [pāda] m. ["circular snout"] san glier.
cakramelaka [melaka] m. soc. ["circular meeting"] secret krama ritual of collective orgy; syn. ca krakrīdā, vīramelāpa.
cakravartin [vartin] m. emperor, master of the universe; sovereign ["who turns the wheel of the universe"]

veraineté [ratnacakra]"] | king of the line of twelve kings beginning at Bharata | bd. the Buddha in my jesté, “who turns the wheel of the Dharma” || pali cakkavatti. ubhayacakravartī m. sovereign of the two worlds.

cakravāka [vāka] mf cakravākī bio. ["whose cry makes the sound of a chariot wheel" zoo. Tadorna fer ruginea, shelduck, a kind of duck of dark orange color, with a black collar, and white wings, living in pairs; but the pairs must separate at night, because of the curse of a sage, and they utter heart-rending cries in the evening; they evoke in poetry conjugal attachment, and the pain of separation from a loved one; the breasts of beautiful women are compared to a pair of these birds; syn. cakrānga, rathānga. cakravākīm ivaikām She remains solitary like the shelduck. esā cakravākī priyeņa vinā rajanīm gamayati [AS.] The shelduck spends the night without its companion.
cakravākasamśayākārapayodharā |DKC.| (She) who wears breasts that evoke a pair of shelducks.
cakravāla [vāla] amnf cakravālā circular, cy clique — n. circle | lit. [alaṃkāra] variety of yamaka where each second verse begins with the end of the previous verse.
cakravrddhi | vrddhi | f. soc. compound interest.
cakravyūha | vyūha | m. circular encircling battle order; [Mah.] Drona used it for the Kauravās army; Abhimanyu was treacherously trapped in it, causing his death.
Cakrākṣi |akṣi| m. myth. np. of Cakrākṣi, epith. of Jagannātha "with round eyes"; its decoration represents the face of God contemplating The sins of the world in the kaliyuga .
cakrāṅga [aṅga₁] mf cakrāṅgī [“with a curved neck”] goose | bio. zoo. Tadorna ferruginea, red duck; syn. cakravāka, rathānga.
cakreśvarī [īśvarī] f. phil. [Tantra] divinity presiding over a mystical diagram | jn. np. of the yakṣī cakreśvarī, revered as śāsanadevatā of Adinātha.
cakraka |cakraka| amnf cakrikā circular.

cakravat [cakravat] amnf cakravatī equipped with wheels | circular, wheel-like — m. oil mill | sovereign, emperor | myth. by extension Viṣṇu — adv. like a wheel; rotating. cakravat parivartante sukhāni ca duḥkhāni ca Good fortune and misfortune follow one another like a turning wheel.
cákri [red. kṛ₁] amnf that does; that performs (acc.); active.

cakrin [cakrain] amnf cakriṇī who has wheels; who drives a chariot | who carries the disc; np. of Cakrī, epith. of Kṛṣṇa — m. sovereign potter; provincial governor | tightrope walker; cheat; informant.
cakrīvat [cakravat] amnf cakrīvatī with wheels | going in a cart — n. cart.

caks [red. kāś] v. [2] pr. r. (caste) v. [1] pr. r. (cakṣate) imp. (cakṣva) inf. (cakṣtum) pp. (caṣṭa) pf. (ā, pari, pra, vi) see, perceive, look, announce; say, speak of (acc.) — ca. (cakṣayati) show.
cakṣas [abstr. cakṣ] n. ved. gaze; eye.
cakṣuḥ iic. cakṣus.
cakṣuḥpīḍā [pīḍā] f. med. eye condition.
caksuḥprīti | prīti | f. love at first sight.
cakṣuḥśravas [śravas] m. ["who hears with his eyes" | snake.
cakṣuḥśrotra | śrotra | n. phil. vision and hearing.
cakṣur iic. cakṣus.
cakṣurdhātu [dhātu] m. bd. organ of sight.
cakṣurvijñāna [vijñāna] n. bd. faculty of sight.
caksurvisaya [visaya] m. field of vision; syn. darśanapatha, nayanapatha | visible object. caksurvisaye in view of; in the presence of.
cakṣuṣ iic. cakṣus.
cakṣuṣka [ka] ifc. amnf cakṣuṣkā who only has eyes for (iic.); who takes the point of view of (iic.).
cakṣuṣmat |mat| amnf cakṣuṣmatī endowed with vision; having eyes; seeing.
cakṣuṣmattā |tā| f. faculty of vision.
cakṣuṣmattva |tva| n. id.
cakṣus [abstr. cakṣ] n. eye; sight, vision | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the sense [buddhīndriya] of sight; its regent [niyantr] is Aditya; the associated perception |tanmātra| is the form |rūpa|; syn. akṣi.
cakṣuḥprīti | prīti | f. | "affection through the gaze" | first stage of love.
cakṣū iic. cakṣus.
cakṣūrāga [rāga] m. thunderbolt.
caṅkram [intens. kram] v. pr. (caṅkramīti) always dominate — v. pr. r. (cankramyáte) to stroll, to wander.
cankrama [act. cankram] m. place of pro menade — f. cankramā promenade | bd. first walk of the Buddha after his Enlightenment.
√ cañc v. [1] pr. (cañcati) pp. (cañcita) to jump; to move, to hang, to waver, to be unstable; to tremble, to throb.
cañca m. wicker basket — f. cañcā wicker or cane object; basket | puppet | scarecrow.
cañcala [intens. cal] amnf cañcalā agitated; unstable, inconstant; fluctuating; trembling, wavering — m. wind | libertine. manaścańcala with an unstable mind.
cañcalatā [tā] f. instability, inconstancy; agitation.
cañcalatva |tva| n. id.
cañcita [pp. cañc] amnf cañcita trem blant, palpitating.
cancu amnf ifc. famous for iic. — m. deer — f. bird's beak.
caṭaka [agt. caṭ] m. sparrow [pl. soc. nickname of the students of Vaisampāyana — f. caṭikā f. caṭakā female sparrow.
caṭu mn amorous chirping | flattering speech, compliments.
catula [la] amnf catulā trembling, unstable graceful, charming — n. pl. caṭulāni sweet words, flattery.
caṇa amnf caṇā ifc. renowned for (iic.); syn. cuñcu — m. chickpea. vidyācaņa renowned for his knowledge.
caṇaka [ka] m. organic. bot. Cicer arientinum, chickpea.

cáṇḍa amnf caṇḍā f. Caṇḍī hot, ardent impetuous; impetuous, ferocious, cruel, furious, violent circumcised — m. myth. np. of Caṇḍa₁ "furious", one of the two guardians [dvārapālau] of Shiva; his companion is Pracanda | myth. np. of the muni canda₁ "the terrible" Kauśika, son of Kakṣīvān Gautama; cf. Brhadratha | myth. [YV.] np. of the raven canda₂, mount of the mātrkā Alambuṣā₁, and father of Bhuśunda | hist. np. from the grammarian canda₃, to the author of the grammar of prakrit Prākṛtalakṣaṇa; its date is controversial — f. cf. candā — f. cf. candī.
candakauśika [kauśika₁] m. myth. n.p. of Candakauśika "full of fury", son of ŗși Kakṣīvān Gautama; cf. Caṇḍa₁ — n. bed. n.p. of Candakauśika₁, drama due to Kṣemīśvara.

Candaghosa [ghosa] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Prince Candaghosa "with cries of fury", son of candasimha and Līlāvatī₁; he died of exhaustion from his dissolute life; his wife Acāravatī died in childbirth, giving birth to Manikarnikā.
candapota [pota] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Candapota "furious young male", war elephant of Candavarmā.

Caṇḍamahāsena [mahāsena] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the king of Avanti Candamahāsena "mahāsena the slow vio"; he offered Caṇḍikā his own flesh to obtain a magic sword and his wife Angāravatī; Gopālaka is their eldest son, Pālaka₁ their younger son, Vāsavadattā₂ their daughter.

Candarava [rava] m. lit. [PT.] np. of the jackal Candarava "with the ferocious cry"; having fallen into a vat of indigo, he came out blue, and took advantage of this to make himself feared by the other animals, and become their king; having driven his fellows away from his court, they howled together, and by atavism he howled in turn, was unmasked and torn to pieces.
candavarman [varman] m. bed. [DKC.] np. of "fiercely protected" Candavarmā, nephew of King Mānasāra, regent of Mālava.

candavega [vega] amnf candavegā impetuous course (said of the sea, of the weather, of an army) myth. np. of Candavega "Furious Torrent", chief of the gandharvās who plundered the kingdom of Purañjana.

candasimha [simha] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of candasimha "Furious Lion", king of Kāśī; by his wife Līlāvatī₁ he is father of Caṇḍaghoṣa and Kāntimatī | lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara candasimha₁, son of Dhanavatī.
candesa [īśa] m. myth. n.p. of Candesa, epith. of Siva "Lord of canda".
Candeśānugraha [anugraha] m. arch. n.p. of Candeśānugraha, one of the 16 aspects of Siva.
candeśvara [īśvara] m. myth. n.p. from candeśvara, epith. by SivaCandesa.
caṇḍā [f. Caṇḍa₁] f. myth. np. of caṇḍā, fierce aspect of Durgā; cf. Caṇḍī.

caṇḍāla [Caṇḍa₁āla] amnf caṇḍālā cruel; savage — mf candālā soc. pariah, outcaste (not. son of a servant [śūdra] and a brāhmaṇī); untouchable taking care of the preparation and cremation of the dead, or of the execution of criminals — f. candālī bd. yoga of ardent fervor, cf. saddharma.
caṇḍālatā [tā] f. soc. pariah condition.
caṇḍālatva [vat] n. soc. pariah condition.
caṇḍika [Caṇḍa₁ika] amnf Caṇḍikā cir concise — f. cf. candika.
candikā [f. candika] f. myth. np. of Candikā "the Furious One", one of the 10 terrible powers [mahāvidyā] of the Goddess [Sakti]; cf. Caṇḍī.
caṇḍita [Caṇḍa₁ita] amnf caṇḍitā arch. said of a grid diagram — m. arch. not. grid diagram of side 8, with 64 squares; syn. mandūka.
caṇḍiman [Caṇḍa₁man] m. choleric character.

Caṇḍī [f. Caṇḍa₁] f. myth. np. of Caṇḍī or Candikā "the Furious One", epith. of a terrible aspect [mahāvidyā] of the Goddess [Śakti]; she is patroness of the tribal hunters | sabara | who offer her human sacrifices; she is tutelary deity of Kaṭaka | lit. np. of the Caṇḍī₁, part of the Mārkaṇḍeya purāṇa which describes the glorious deeds of the Goddess; she is recited not. during the durgāpūjā | furious woman, virago.
Caṇḍīśataka |śataka| n. lit. np. of the Caṇḍīśataka, poem in praise of Caṇḍī₁Durgā due to Bāṇa₂.
√ cat v. [1] pr. (c stati) pp. (catt st) ppr. (c stat) to leave, to hide — ca. (cātáyati) to frighten; to shoot, to chase away.
catasṛ [f. catur] num. pers. pl. [name. acc. catasras, i. catasrbhis, dat. abl. catasrbhyas, g. catasṛṇām, loc. catasṛṣu four.
catuḥ iic. catur.
catuḥśata |śata| n. ved. 104 — amnf catuḥśatā 400 — f. Catuḥśatī lit. np. of the Catuḥśatī, tantric poem "in 400 stanzas".

catuḥśataka [śataka] n. lit. np. of the catuḥśataka, a philosophical poem in 400 stanzas |kārikās| by Aryadeva (3rd century); it defends the doctrine of Nāgārjuna against the other bd. and brahma schools; it forms the philosophical basis of the bd. Mahāyāna school; Dharmapāla and Candrakīrti commented on it in the 6th century — f. catuḥśatikā var. catuhśatī lit. id.
catuḥśāla [śālā] amnf catuḥśālā arch. (building) with 4 rooms — m. traditional house of Kerala, with 4 building sections.

catuhśriga [śriga] m. organic. zoo. Tetracerus quadri cornis, tetraceran antelope || hi. causingā. catuhsasti var. catussasti |sasti| f. 64. catuļsastikā var. catussastikā [kalā] f. pl. catuḥṣaṣṭikalās soc. the 64 arts or knowledge
annexes [angavidyā]: the Kāmasūtra lists: song [gīta], music [vādya], dance [nṛtya] and theatre [nāṭya], drawing, painting and the

calligraphy [ālekhya], face and body adornment [viśeṣakacchedya], altar decoration with rice and flowers [taṇḍulakusumavalivikāra], flower arrangement [puṣpāstaraṇa], teeth, limb, and clothing coloring [daśanavasanāṅgarāga], gemstone mosaic making [maṇibhūmikākarma], bed arrangement [śayanaracana], music with a water pot [udakavādya], water play [udakāghāta], various [citra] kinds of magical yoga, garland making [mālyagrathanavikalpa], diadem arrangement | śekharāpīḍayojana | and flowers in the ears and hair, the art of grooming [nepathyaprayoga], ear ornamentation [karṇapattrabhaṅga], the art of perfume and cosmetics [gandhayukti], the art of adornment [bhūṣaṇayojana], juggling and circus arts [aindrajāla], the art of disguise [kaucumārayoga], magic [hastalāghava], the art of preparing food [vicitraśākayūṣabhakṣyavikārakriyā], the art of preparing drinks [pānakarasarāgāsavayojana], sewing [sūcīvānakarmāṇi], the art of puppetry [sūtrakrīḍā], the lute and drum

bourin [vīṇāḍamaruvādyāni], the art of riddle-telling [prahelikā], the art of reciting verses backwards [pratimālā], the art of pronouncing difficult words [durvācakayoga], the art of deciphering manuscripts

writing [pustakavācana], theatre and storytelling [nāṭakākhyāyikādarśana], the game of poem completion [kāvyasamasyāpūrana], weaving and caning [pattikāvetravāṇavikalpa], spinning [tarkukarmāṇi], carpentry [takṣaṇa], architecture [vāstuvidyā], the appreciation of coins and precious stones [rūpyaratnaparīkṣā], metallurgy and alchemy [dhātuvāda], the knowledge of gems [manirāgākarajñāna], horticulture [vṛkṣāyurvedayoga], the organization of animal fights [meşakukkutalāvakayuddhavidhi], the training of parrots and mynahs [śukasārikāpralāpana], the art of rubbing, massaging and curling hair (utsādane saṃvāhane keśamardane ca kauśalam), the art of finger storytelling [akṣaramuṣṭikākathana], knowledge of foreign languages [mlecchitavikalpa], mastery of dialects

regional [deśabhāṣāvijñāna], the arrangement of a flower cart [puṣpaśakaṭikā], knowledge of magical diagrams and amulets [yantramātṛkā], mnemonics [dhāraṇamātṛkā], the recitation of the Veda in unison [sampāthya], mental poetry (mānasī kāvyakriyā), lexicography
phie [abhidhānakośa], prosody [chandojñāna], rhetoric [kriyāvikalpa], the art of rhetorical devices

magic [chalitakayogās], the art of dissimulation in one's clothing [vastragopana], games of chance [dyūtaviśeṣa], dice games [ākarṣakrīḍā], children's games [bālakrīḍanakāni], and the military knowledge of discipline [vainayikī], strategy [vaijayikī], and physical culture [vyāyāmikī]; these are the principal arts [mūlakalā] of the Šaivatantra; other sources mention other arts, such as the science of theft | cauravidyā|. catuhsastikalāgamaprayogacaturah [Daśakumāracarita] Gifted in the acquisition and practice of the 64 arts. catuhsastiyoginī var. catussastiyoginī [yoginī] f. pl. phil. the 64 divine powers; they are represented, associated with Bhairava and Kātyāyanī, in circular open-air temples (around the 9th century).
catuhsana [sana₂] m. pl. cf. sanakādi.
catuḥsaptata [saptata] amnf catuḥsaptatī ord. 74ᵉ.
catuḥsaptati [saptati] f. 74.
catuḥsaptatitama |tama| afmn catuhsaptatitamī ord. 74ᵉ.
cátuḥsahasra [sahasra] n. 1004.

catúr num. pers. pl. |m. name. catvāras, acc. caturas, i. caturbhis, dat. abl. caturbhyas, g. caturṇām, loc. caturṣu; f. name. acc. disasters; n. name. acc. catvāri | Four — adv. catus Four times — n. cf. catvāri — f. cf. catasṛ || lat. quartet; fr. Four.
caturakṣa |akṣa| amnf caturakṣī | "who has 4 eyes" | with piercing gaze | myth. epith. of the dogs of Yama, or of Agni "who see all".

caturanga [anga₁] amnf caturangā formed of 4 parts; said not. of an army comprising chariots, elephants, cavalry and infantry — n. [caturangabala] army — f. caturangā [caturangābalā] id. | game of chess; its pieces are: the king [rājan], the minister [mantrin] (for the queen), the elephant [hastin] (for the bishop), the horse [aśva] (for the knight), the chariot [ratha] or the boat [naukā] (for the rook) and the infantryman [padāti] (for the pawn).
caturangakrīdana [krīdana] n. chess game.

caturangadīpikā [dīpikā] f. lit. np. of the Ca turangadīpikā, treatise on the game of chess attributed to Sūlapāṇi; this ancestor of the modern game was played by 4 players, the players on opposite sides being allies; the moves were determined by the throw of two dice.
caturaigākrīdā [krīdā] f. game of chess.
caturadhyāya [adhyaya] amnf Caturadhyāyī consisting of 4 lessons — f. Caturadhyayī phon. n.p. from the Caturadhyāyī or caturadhyāyikā or Ca turādhyāyikā, treatise on phonetics of Saunaka₁.
caturadhyāyika [ika] nf caturadhyāyikā cf. ca turadhyāyī.
caturartha [artha] m. gram. 4 senses; 4 uses.
caturaśīta [aśīta] amnf caturaśītī ord. 84°.
caturaśīti [aśīti] f. 84.
caturaśītitama |tama| amnf caturaśītitamī ord. 84ᵉ.
caturaśra | aśra₂ | amnf caturaśrā quadrangu laire; quadrilateral; rectangular, square; regular — m. rectangle, square.
caturaśratā [tā] f. regularity, harmony; symmetry.
caturaśri | aśri | amnf whenrangular. caturādhyāya amnf caturādhyāyī cf. catu radhyāya.
caturādhyāyika |ika| nf caturādhyāyikā id.

caturānana₁ [ānana] amnf caturānanā who has Four faces — m. myth. np. of caturānana₁, epith. of Brahmā "with Four faces" | myth. four-headed representation of Vișnu with the faces of Varāha, Narasimha, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa; cf. vaikunthacaturmūrti.
caturāśrama [āśrama] mn one of the 4 stages of brahmanical life: brahmacarya, grhastha, vānaprastha and sannyāsa; cf. puruṣārtha.
caturthá [tha] amnf caturthī ord. fourth — f. caturthī gram. dative (4th case of declension) soc. fourth day of the lunar month; ganeśacaturthī lat. quartus; hi. chautha. caturtham adv. the 4th time.
caturdaśan [daśan] num. pers. fourteen.
caturdiśam [diś₂] adv. in the 4 directions, towards the 4 cardinal points.
caturdhara | dhara | mr. hist. n.p. by Nīlakantha₄ Ca turdhara.
caturdhā |dhā| adv. in 4 parts. caturdhākṛ divide into 4 parts. caturdhābhū be divided into 4 parts.
caturdhākaraṇa [karaṇa] n. division into 4 parts.
caturdhāvihitá [vihita] amnf caturdhāvihitā division into 4 parts.
caturnavata [navata] amnf caturnavatī ord. 94ᵉ.
caturnavit | navati | f. 94.
caturnavatitama [tama] amnf caturnavati tamī ord. 94ᵉ.
caturpada | padah | amnf caturpadī quadruped.
caturbāhu |bāhu| amnf which has 4 arms (epith. of representations of deities).
Caturbhāṇī [bhāṇa] f. bed. n.p. from the Caturbhāṇī, collection of 4 dramas in bhāṇa style, including the Ubhayābhisārika, the Padmaprābhṛtaka, the Dhūrtaviṭasaṃvāda and the Pādatāḍitaka.

cáturbhuja |bhuja| amnf caturbhujā which has 4 arms (epith. of representations of deities) | math. quadrilateral. tricaturbhuja m. math. [Brahmagupta] triangle completed by a point on its circumcircle.
caturmāsa | māsa | n. period of 4 months, corresponding to the rainy season | myth. period of sleep of Vișnu of 4 months; it ends at the full moon |pūrṇimā| of the month kārttika.
caturmukha | mukha | amnf caturmukhī which has 4 faces — m. epith. of Brahmā.
caturyuga [yuga] n. astr. the 4 ages of the World; syn. mahāyuga.
caturvarga [varga] m. group of 4 objects | lit. or work in 4 parts.
caturvarna [varna] m. soc. the 4 Vedic classes. caturvargacintāmaņi |cintāmaņi | mr. bed. n.p. from the Caturvargacintāmani "Quadripartite Treasure", my manual of rituals [vrata] of Hemādri₁.
caturviṃśa [viṃśa] amnf caturviṃśī ord. 24th bed. stoma made up of 24 parts.
caturvimást | vimást | iic. twenty-four | made up of 24 parts.
caturviṃśaccata | śata | n. 124.
caturviṃśati [viṃśati] num. f. twentyfour.
caturvidya [vidyā] amnf caturvidyā soc. who masters the 4 Vedas; syn. caturvedin.
cáturvidha [vidhā₂] amnf caturvidhā of 4 kinds; quadripartite.
caturvedin | vedin | amnf caturvedin soc. who masters the 4 Vedas (form of the np. of brahmins); syn. caturvidya.
caturvyavasita | vyavasita | n. [caturvyavasitayamaka] lit. variety of yamaka in which the four lines of a stanza are homophones.
caturvyūha [vyūha] m. myth. the 4 divine emanations of the Vaishnava mystical tradition: Vāsudeva, Sankarşana, Pradyumna and Aniruddha.
caturhāyaṇa [hāyana] amnf caturhāyaṇī aged 4 years.
cáturhotṛ |hotṛ| m. pl. caturhotāras ved. the 4 priests who sacrificed for whom? (classic question of a ritual riddle |brahmodya|).
catuścatvārimśá [catvārimśa] amnf catuścatvāriṃśī ord. 44ᵉ | made up of 44 parts (not. stoma).
catuścatvāriṃśat | catvāriṃśat | f. 44.

catuska [ka] amnf catuskā quadripartite; square | consisting of 4 elements; not. swastika — n. quadruple | intersection of two roads, crossroads soc. square of honor drawn to receive a guest | 4-row collar — amnf catuṣkī pond qua drangular; mosquito net; 4-row collar. catuskoți |koți | f. bd. | "tetralemma" | logical principle in 4 parts, expressing the totality of the disjoint sum of the four classes A and not B, not A and B, A and B, and not A and not B. sarvam tathyam na vā tathyam tathyam cātathyam eva ca | naivatathyam naiva tathyam etad buddhānuśāsanam | [Mūlamadhyamaka] Everything exists, or does not exist, or both exists and does not exist, or neither exists nor does not exist; this is the teaching of the Buddha.
cátustaya |taya| amnf catustayī quadruple, quadripartite — n. tetrad | all four at once. catuștva [tva] n. the state of being quadruple.
catuṣpañcāśa | pañcāśa | amnf catuṣpañcāśī ord. 54ᵉ.
cátuṣpañcāśat [pañcāśat] f. 54.
cátuspañcāśattama [tama] amnf catuspañcāśattamī ord. 54ᵉ.
catuspatrī [patra] f. organic. bot. Marsilea quadrifolia, water clover; syn. sunisanna.
catuspathá | patha | m. crossroads, intersection of two roads.
catuspad | pad₂ | amnf catuspadī | nom. catuspād quadruped — n. the quadruped people; (collective) the animals.
cátuspada | pada | amnf catuspadī quadripar tite | (stanza) of 4 feet [pada]; consisting of 4 words — n. astr. last fixed lunar half-day [karaṇa].
catuspari | pari | ind. missed four (not. in the game pañcaka ).
catustriṃśa [triṃśa] amnf catustriṃśī ord. 34ᵉ | made up of 34 parts.
catustriṃśat | triṃśat | f. 34.
catūrātrá [rātra] mn soc. four-day ceremony. catūrātram for four days.

catura [catura] amnf caturā skillful, adroit; ingenious; quick, fast; charming — m. soc. | nātyaśāstra | ritual hand gesture (horizontal palm, 4 fingers raised, thumb inclined towards the middle finger, symbolizing truthfulness).
caturaka [ka] amnf caturikā skillful, skillful — m. bed. |PT.| n.p. of the caturaka jackal.
caturānana₂ [ānana] amnf caturānanā au vi sage rusé.

caturdaśa [caturdaśan] amnf caturdaśī ord. 14ᵉ — f. caturdaśī fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the lunar month (new moon) soc. It is auspicious, and a day of celebration; cf. dīpāvali [vaikunthacaturdaśī], nṛsiṃhacaturdaśī, śivarātri, anantavrata.

catvara | caturvara | n. crossroads; square place; district | soc. leveled square of ground for a sacrifice. dūrvācatvaram soc. square of ground covered with grass dūrvā for sitting during a sacrifice.
catvāras cf. catur.
catvāri [n. catur] num. pers. pl. [name. acc. catvāri; other cases cf. catur | Four. catvāryāryasatyāni bd. the Four Noble Truths |āryasatya|.
catvārimsá [dasa] amnf catvārimsī ord. 40°.
catvāriṃśát [daśat] f. sg. forty.

Caná [cana] part. cl. not even | gram. gives an indefinite value to pr. and a. interr. kaścana someone, whoever. na kaścana person. kimcana something | pl. kānicana some things. na kimcana nothing. kvacana somewhere; anywhere.
canas n. pleasure, satisfaction; food.
√ cand v. [1] pr. (candati) pp. (candita) shine, shine | lat. candeo; eng. candle; fr. candle, candid, fire.
canda |agt. cand| m. moon | hist. np. of King Soma canda, who founded the eponymous kingdom in Kūrmāncala (11th century).
candasimha [simha] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of King vidyādhara Candasiṃha, son of Siṃha₁ and Dhana vatī, ally of Naravāhanadatta.

Candeśvara [īśvara] m. soc. np. of Candeśvara, one of the 63 Tamil nayanar saints; he is depicted at the northeast entrance of a śaiva shrine as a curly-haired young boy, arms in añjali, or carrying an axe; according to legend, this young Brahmin incurred the wrath of his father for spoiling milk as an offering to an earth linga; by destroying the linga, the father awoke his meditating son who smashed his leg with an axe; Shiva then manifested himself and appointed him guardian of the treasure.
candana [agt. cand] mn bio. bot. Sirium myrtifolium, tree or sandalwood; it is said that he is loved by snakes | lat. sandalum; eng. sandalwood; fr. sandalwood.

candananagara [nagara] n. geo. np. of the village of candananagara in Bengal, on the Ganges 30 km upstream from Calcutta, founded as a French trading post (Chandernagor) by Duplessis in 1674, annexed to India in 1950; mod. Candanna gar.

Candala [candala] m. hist. n.p. of the Candala or Candela dynasty, founded by Nannuk, head of a Rājput clan who Sanskritized his lineage, making it descend from the moon [candravaṃśa]; the Can dalās reigned from the 9th to the 12th century in Khajurāho, then in Mahoba; they were initially vassals of the Pratīhārās; they patronized the arts and letters, and built numerous Hindu and Jain temples.

candrá [candra] amnf candrā Bright, illuminating — m. the moon ["that shines"] | myth. np. of the god Candra "Bright", personifying the moon; as Soma he is the vessel of the amrta; he was born from the churning of the sea of milk [kṣīrodamathana], but also from the tears of Atri as the son of Anasūyā, and is therefore doubly said

born [dvija]; he is the guardian [dikpāla] of the northeast direction; as Oşadhipati he rules over plants; his chariot is drawn by 7 sacred geese [hamsa]; he married 27 daughters of Daksha, identified with the asterisms or lunar mansions |nakṣatra|; as he neglected them in favor of Rohinī₁ alone, they complained to Daksha who cursed him and condemned him to decay; he implored Shiva, who commuted the sentence to periodic decay; he is the star king Tārakārāja, his beauty is celebrated; after performing the rājasūya sacrifice of royal consecration, he became arrogant and abducted Bṛhaspati's wife Tārā; a war with the gods [tārakāmayayuddha] ensued; Candra was cut in two by Shiva's trident, and had to surrender Tārā, from whom he had obtained as a son Budha myth. one of the 10 regions [dvīpa] forming the jambudvīpa | math. symb. the number 1 | eye of a peacock feather | [candragomin] gram. school of the grammarian Candragomī | lit. cf. Candraka — ifc. the best of (iic.) — n. ved. or. kṣīrodārṇavasaṃbhūta atrinetrasamudbhava grhāṇārghyam mayā dattam rohinyā sahita u sasin || (said while making an offering of milk to Candra during kṛṣṇāṣṭamī) O you product of the foam of the sea of milk, coming from the eye of Atri, you who carry the hare, accompanied by the red star, accept the oblation that I offer you.

candrakalā | kalā | f. quarter moon, sixteenth part of the lunar circle | phil. [Tantra] one of the 16 associated female divinities | astr. crescent moon one day before or after the new moon | crescent-shaped mark on the nail.

candrakānta [kānta] amnf candrakāntā dear to the moon | charming as the moon — m. lit. moonstone, a gem |mani| reputed to melt in the moonlight; syn. candropala | bio. bot. Nymphæa esculenta, White Water Lily (Which blooms at night); syn. kumuda — n. sandalwood — f. Can drakāntā night.
candrakānti | kānti | f. moon's luster; Moonlight | moon's disk on the 9th day.

Candrakīrti₁ [kīrti] m. hist. np. of the monk bd. Candrakīrti₁ (early 7th century), abbot of the university of Nālandā, commentator of Nāgārjuna; his Madhyamakāvatāra is an introduction to the Madhyamaka system; cf. Prasannapadā | hist. np. of Candrakīrti₁ "Glory of the moon star", prince of Ujjayinī.
Candraketu₁ | ketu | m. np. of prince Candraketu₁ "He who has the moon on his banner" | myth. [Rām.] np. of Candraketu₁, son of Lakshmana.

Candragupta [Gupta] m. hist. np. of King Candragupta Gupta Maurya, rebel general who overthrew the Nanda dynasty in Magadha and founded the Maurya dynasty in 321 BC; his court was held at Pataliputra, Kautilya was his mentor and prime minister; he is known to the Greeks as Sandrakottos, and Plutarch says (according to the Greek historian Megasthenes) that he met Alexander in Punjab in 329 BC; after conquering an empire extending to Gandhara, he became a Jain renunciant, and abdicated in 297 BC in favor of his son Bindusara, father of Emperor Ashoka; cf. Canakya, Mayuraposha, geo. np. of King Candragupta₁, the first true emperor of the Gupta dynasty; his accession to the throne in 320 marks the beginning of the Gupta era [saṃvat]; he gave himself the title of Mahārājādhirāja; his son Samudragupta succeeded him | np. of King Kumāra Candragupta, younger son of Samudragupta; he succeeded his elder brother Rāmagupta after assassinating him, and reigned as Candragupta₂ (~380–415); cf. Vikramāditya.

candragomin [gomin] m. hist. np. of the Bengali scholar Candragomī (around the 5th century); he is the author of the Sanskrit grammar Cāndravyākaraņa, with its gloss [vrtti]; he is also credited with the play [nāṭaka] Lokānanda, and many other works.
candragrahana | grahana | n. lunar eclipse.
candracūda [cūdā] m. myth. ["Who wears the moon as his crest"] epith. of Siva; cf. candramauli.
Candrajanaka [janaka] m. np. of Candrajanaka, epith. of the ocean "where Candra was born".
candranādī [nādī] f. cf. idā.
candrapālita [pālita] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Can drapālita, son of the minister Indrapālita; he went to Kundinapura, claiming to have been banished by his father.

candraprabha [prabhā₁] m. jn. np. of Candra prabha "Moonlight", 8th tīrthankara mythic; his body is white, his symbol is a crescent moon; he is associated with pure meditation [śukladhyāna] [lit. [KSS.] np. of the king candraprabha₁ of Sākala; his son Sūryaprabha₁ was destined by Šiva to become emperor of the vidyādharās; Maya revealed to him that in a previous life he was his eldest son the dānava Sunītha₁, as his son Sūryaprabha was his younger son Sumundīka — f. candraprabhā lit. [KSS.] np. Princess Vidyādharī Candraprabhā, eldest daughter of King Sasikhandapada of Kanakapurī; her sisters Candra Rekhā, Šaśirekhā, and Šaśiprabhā, for having defiled an ascetic, were cursed to marry a human; she welcomed Saktideva to Kanakapurī and fell in love with him. Candrabindu [bindu] m. phon. sign of nasalization, to indicate the change of a silent na to anusvāra before a semivowel |anunāsika|.
candrabhāgā [bhāga] f. geo. np. of the Can drabhāgā river at Pañjāb (mod. Chenāb, confluence of the Candrā and the Bhāgā) | var. candrabhāgī id.
candramandala [mandala] n. moon disk.

candrámas [mās] m. moon | hist. n.p. from Can dramā "moon", epith. of king Samudragupta, son of Candragupta₁, father of Vikramāditya — f. Candra masī myth. n.p. of Candramasī, epith. of Tārā “Ra life by Candra”. sūryācandramasau du. the Sun and the moon.
candrámāsa [māsa] m. astr. lunar month.
candrámukuṭa [mukuṭa] amnf candramukuṭā myth. n.p. of Candramukuṭa, epith. of Siva "Who has the moon as a diadem".
candrámukha [mukha] amnf candramukhī whose face is like the moon (poetic praise).
candrámauli [mauli] m. myth. ["who has the moon for a diadem" | epith. of Siva; cf. candracūḍa.
candramaulīśvara [īśvara] m. geo. n.p. of Candra maulīśvara, crystal linga of the Ci dambara sanctuary | geo. n.p. of candramaulīśvara₁, temple dedicated to Siva in Udupī.

Candrarekhā [rekhā] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī Candrarekhā, sister of Candraprabhā, cursed to become human in the form of Princess Kanakarekhā of Vardhamāna; she married Saktideva with her three sisters.
candrávaṃśa [vaṃśa] m. cf. somavaṃśa.

candravat [vat] amnf Candravatī like the moon — f. Candravatī lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī Candravatī "beautiful as the moon"; ja louse of her friend Adityaprabhā, she got herself married as Padmasena's second wife, causing disputes; King Muktāsena punished her by seeing her on Earth as Madanadamstrā.
candravarna [varna] amnf candravarna of brilliant color.

candravarman | varman | bed. mr. [Viddhaśālabhañjikā] np. of Candvararmā, king of the Lāṭās, vassal of Vidyādharamalla; he passed off his daughter Mṛgānkāvalī as the crown prince Mṛgāṅkavarmā, whom he handed over to Vidyādharamalla as tribute.

candravākya [vākya] n. lit. manual of mnemonic phrases in kaṭapayādi code due to Vararuci₁, allowing the calculation of the position of the Sun and the moon (tithi, nakṣatra) on any day of the year; syn. vararucivākya .

candrasekhara [sekhara] amnf candrasekharā myth. n.p. of Candraśekhara, epith. of Śiva "who wears the moon in a diadem"; a temple was built for him in 1246 by King Narasimha₂ on the Kapilas hill 25 km from Dhenkanal, Orissa.
candrásimha [simha] m. hist. np. of the pandita Candrasimha, author of the Padakṛtya (17th century).

candrasena [senā] m. lit. [Mah.] np. of Prince Can drasena, son of King Samudrasena — f. Candrasenā lit. [DKC.] np. of Candrasenā, foster sister and confidante of Princess Kandukavatī; she was in love with Kośadāsa, but held captive by Prince Bhīmadhanvā.
candráhāsa [hāsa] m. myth. np. of the sword Can drahāsa "Moon Laughter", which Shiva gave to Ravana to reward him for his 1000 years of penance |tapas|.

Candrāditya [āditya] m. hist. np. of Candrāditya, eldest son of King Cālukya Pulikeśī₂; he fought his 4 brothers; at his death, his wife Vijayabhaṭṭārikā ensured the regency of the empire until the accession of Vikramāditya₁.
Candrānanda |ānanda| mr. hist. n.p. of the philosopher Candrānanda (10th century), author of the Vaiśesikasūtravṛtti.

Candrāpīḍa₁ [āpīḍa] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Candrāpīḍa₁ "Horned by the Moon", son of Janame jaya | lit. [K.] np. of Prince Candrāpīḍa₁, son of King Tārāpīda and Queen Vilāsavatī; at 16 years old he is enthroned as crown prince, then sets off to conquer the world; he gets lost and finds at Lake Acchoda the beautiful Mahāśvetā who tells him of her unhappy love affair with Pundarīka₂, the latter's suicide and her Ascent to Heaven with Candra; she takes him to Mount He makūṭa and introduces him to Kādambarī; they are seized by passion for each other; but Candrāpīda₁ must return to the palace on his father's orders, and they are separated; he goes in search of his friend Vaiśampāyana₁ and falls into a great lethargy upon learning of his sad end; he is the incarnation of Candra struck by a curse from Pundarīka₂ who is reborn as the sad king Sūdraka₁, while his friend Vaiśampāyana₁ is reborn as the narrating parrot.
candrāmṛta [amṛta] n. liquid moistening the palatal cavity; fountain of youth.
candrodaya [udaya] m. moonrise.
candropala [upala] m. bed. moonstone, cf. Can drakānta.
candraka [Candraka] amnf candrikā sem blable to the moon — m. peacock feather eye; nail hist. np. of the Kashmiri dramatic poet Can draka (1st century ant.) — n. pepper — f. cf. candrikā.
candrakavat [vat] m. peacock.
candrakin |in| m. id.
Candrața m. med. n.p. of Candrața, 10th century doctor, son of Tīsaṭa, on whose Cikitsākalikā he commented; we also owe him Suśrutapāthaśuddhi.

candrikā [f. candraka] f. moonlight phon. name of a meter | organic. bot. Rauvolvia ser pentina, apocynaceae shrub with black berries; its roots are used medicinally; syn. sarpa gandha — ifc. splendor, clarity of; elucidation of (iic.) | bed. clarification on (name of works) [tātparyacandrikā] lit. n.p. of the candrikā of Vyāsatīrtha; cf. tātparyacandrikā.
candrikācārya |ācārya| mr. hist. n.p. of Can drikācārya "Master of the candrikā", title given to Vyāsatīrtha.
candrikācvatī [vat] f. bed. [KSS.] np. of Princess Candrikāvati, daughter of Subhaṭa₁, second wife of Sūryaprabha₁.
candrimā [candra] f. moonlight.
Cannibhatta m. hist. np. of the logician Cannibhațța, author of the Tarkabhāṣāprakāśikā (14th century).

capala [related to kamp] amnf capalā mobile, agile, unstable | hesitant; capricious, changeable; ti mide | inconstant, giddy; mischievous — f. capalā lit. modulating prakrit verse, indicating an alternation of rhythm; we distinguish the mukhacapalā of the first verse and the jaghanacapalā of the second.
capalatā [tā] f. inconstancy; scatterbrainedness.
capeta mf capetā slap. mukhe capeţām dā slap. capețikā [ika] f. id.
√ cam v. [1] pr. (camati) v. [1] pr. (cāmati) pft. (cacāma) pfp. (camya) pf. (ā) [unused without pf.].
camat ind. excl. of surprise or appreciation (with a click of the tongue).

camatkāra [kāra] m. astonishment, surprise; wonder, rapture | lit. not. sudden pleasure caused by a literary composition; it is the essence of rasa. yatpratipāditārthavisayakabhāvanātvam ca matkārajanakatāvacchedakatvam tattvam
kāvyatvam [Rasagangādhara] Only words that inspire wonder belong to poetry.
Camatkāracandrikā [candrikā] f. bed. n.p. from the Camatkāracandrikā, a treatise on poetic analysis by Viśveśvara₁.
camatkāratva |tva| n. lit. state of wonder.
camana [act. cam] n. the act of taking a sip
camara mf camarī bio. zoo. Bos grunniens, Tibetan white yak | bio. its tail, from which fly whisks are made | ang. chowrie.
camasá [camasa] mnf camasī ved. square wooden cup with a handle, used for drinking soma at solemn rituals.
camasādhvaryu [adhvaryu] m. ved. priest officiating at soma rituals, in charge of the cups.
camū f. army; syn. senā.

campa m. bio. bot. Bauhinia variegata, a shrub of the Fabaceae family with large bright pink or white flowers with a sweet fragrance — f. campā geo. np. of the city of campā, capital of the Anga country (mod. Bhagalpur in Bihāra); it was an important trading city [mahānagara] | myth. [Mah.] capital city of Lomapāda and Karņa | geo. np. of the Hinduized kingdom of campā₁ in South Vietnam; it had its apogee from the 8th to the 11th century; it comprised the principalities (from North to South) of Indrapura, Amarāvatī₂, Vijaya₆, Kauthāra and Pāṇduraṅga₁.

campaka |ka| m. bio. bot. Michelia champaka, a bust of the magnolia family; its bright yellow flowers with a sweet fragrance are sacred to Shiva; an oil is extracted from it to perfume the hair hist. np. of campaka, minister of King Harsa₂ (11th century); the poet Kalhaṇa is his son || hi. cāmpnā; ang. shampoo; fr. shampooing.
campakavat [vat] amnf campakavatī (place) rich in campaka — f. campakavatī geo. n.p. of the campakavatī forest.
Campakā [f. campaka] f. bed. [Hit.] np. from the town of Campakā "with the scent of magnolia".
campū f. lit. [kāvya] style of elaborate literary composition in which the same theme is treated successively in prose [gadya] and in verse [padya]; cf. Rāmāyaṇacampū, Yaśastilakacampū, Nalacampū.
caya |act. ci| m. heap, pile, mass; sheaf, bouquet, collection, assembly; gathering; multitude | pile of earth; earthwork, foundation, wall; fortification, glacis.
cayana |act. ci| n. pile of wood, pyre | altar.

√ car v. [1] pr. (c 'arati) pr. r. (carate) pft. (cacāra) aor. [5] (acārīt) aor. [3] (acīcarat) pp. (ca rita, cīrṇa) ppr. (carat) abs. (caritvā) pf. (ati, anu, apa, abhi, ā, ut, upa, nis, parā, pari, pra, vi, sam) to go, walk, stroll; to graze | to travel, follow (a path); to behave as; to live | to begin, to engage in, to occupy oneself with, to exercise | to observe (if lence), to practice; to accomplish, to commit, to do; to act | to continue to do, to pursue | to bring someone (acc.) to (acc.) — ca. (cārayati) to make move, to make practice | to be recognized by a spy (i.) — ca. r. (cārayate) to reflect, hesitate, have doubts about (loc.) — des. (cicarișati) to try to go; to wish to have a certain conduct | to try to have sexual relations with (i.) — intens. (carcarīti) to hurry, to come and go, to parade | to strut; to behave provocatively || gr. κολος; lat. curro, carrus; fr. char; ang. car. bhaikṣam car to ask for alms; to beg. mārgam car to make one's way. vighnam car to oppose an obstacle. bhaikṣam car to beg. mithunám car to have sexual relations with someone. (i.). mṛgayāṃ car to chase. vratam car to observe a vow. sasyam because to feed on wheat. caraiveti let's go, let's move forward. arcantas cerur they continued to honor. svāminam avajñāya caret he will continue to despise his master.

cara [agt. car] amnf carī mobile; animated, moving — ifc. that goes into, that inhabits (iic.); that which is sent to (iic.) | place of living of (iic.); formerly inhabited by (iic.) — m. animal (opp. plant) | emissary, es pion; wind, breath. brāhmaṇacaraḥ which was formerly the possession of the brahmins.
carācara | acara | amnf carācarā mobile as well as immobile — n. ["the mobile and the immobile"] all creatures; the universe.

cáraka |agt. car| m. nomadic student; ascetic, wandering monk; spy | myth. np. of the ancient physician Caraka, son of a muni; he is the incarnation of Sesa, moved by a visit to Earth where he witnessed the ravages of disease; he synthesized the medical knowledge of Agnivesa and the other disciples of Atreya in the carakasamhitā.

carakasamhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. np. of the carakasamhitā, a treatise on medicine [Ayurveda] in 120 chapters attributed to Caraka; it was probably composed between 100 and 400, and revised by Drdhabala.

cáraṇa [act. car] mn foot; leg | section, division | gram. quarter of a stanza; syn. pāda | ved. Vedic school — n. conduct, way of being, practice; accomplishment; pilgrimage. prathamacalitadakṣiṇacaraṇaḥ one who sets out beginning with the right foot (auspicious). guroś caraṇam hariḥ śaraṇam practice of guru, protection of Viṣṇu (postyoga mantra).
caraṇadāsa [dāsa] m. hist. n.p. of the philosopher Caranadāsa, author not. of Guruśisyasamvāda.
carat [ppr. because] amnf carantī while walking, going, wandering.
caramá [super. cara] amnf caramā last, final. caramā kriyā funeral ceremony. caramam kim and what else?
caramávayas [vayas₁] amnf ["in the last stage of life" | aged.
caramaśloka | śloka | m. epitaph | lit. last line (18.66) of the BhG.

caritá [pp. car] amnf caritā done, accomplished; practiced — n. action accomplished, thing done; past | conduct, behavior, way of acting; deeds and gestures; practice, exercise of a function; present | set of acts, life; existence; exploits, adventures | ang. care; fr. charité.
caritavrata [vrata] amnf caritavrata having fulfilled her marital duty.
caritāmṛta | amṛta | n. bed. | "nectar of acts" | name of biographies; not. Caitanyacaritāmṛta.
caritārtha [artha] amnf caritārthā who has achieved his goal, who has succeeded.
caritārthatā [tā] f. success.
caritra [instr. car] n. conduct, action, practice; work; saga, adventures, exploits.
caritrabandhaka [bandhaka] mn ready; pledge, hy pothèque.
cariṣṇú [agt. car] amnf mobile, in motion | unstable; who wanders, who roams — m. myth. np. of Carișnu, son of Manu Sāvarņa.
caru [caru] m. oblation consisting of a porridge of rice, barley and peas cooked in milk cauldron used for its preparation.
√ carc v. [10] pr. (carcayati) pp. (carcita) repeat (a word, not. when reciting the Veda) | discuss, deliberate — pr. r. (carcayate) study.
carca [act. carc] m. discussion, deliberation — f. cf. carcā.
carcaka |agt. carc| mf carcikā who studies, who repeats the Veda — act. m. repetition of a word (while reciting the Veda) — f. carcikā cf. carcā.
cárcarī [intens. car] f. cries and songs of joy, festive procession | flattery.
carcā [f. carca] f. preoccupation | discussion; investigation | recitation with repetition of the Veda (not. inserting iti). carcām kr to be preoccupied with, to be concerned about.
carcāpāṭha [pāṭha] m. soc. recitation of the Veda in the manner of carcā.
carcāpāra |pāra| amnf carcāpārī who studies carcāpāṭha in depth.
carcāviṣaya [viṣaya] m. object of discussion.
carcita [pp. carc] amnf carcitā repeated; said especially of the recitation of the Veda with particle iti of citation.
carpața m. palm of the hand.
carma iic. carman.
carmakāra | kāra | m. curroyeur, cordonnier, tan neur, leather worker | soc. man of low class, not. son of a candālā or vaidehī or niṣādī woman — f. carmakārī tanner's wife || hi. camār.
carmaja | ja | amnf carmajā made of leather — n. hair of the skin.
carmadanda |danda| m. whip.
carmadṛṣṭi [dṛṣṭi] f. phil. superficial knowledge of the appearance of beings and things; opp. ātmadṛṣṭi.
carmanāsikā [nāsikā] f. whip.
carmamuṇḍā |muṇḍa| f. cf. cāmuṇḍā.

carmaranga [ranga] amnf carmarangā which dyes leather — f. carmarangā bio. bot. Cassia auri culata, bushy shrub with compound leaves, with bright yellow flowers in corymbs, used in tanning and medicine; syn. āvartakī.
carmin [in] amnf carminī made of leather | armed with a shield.

cármaṇvat [carmanvat] amnf carmanvatī filled with hides; supplied with leather — f. carmanvatī geo. np. of the Carmanvatī River "full of carcasses"; [Mah.] it is so named because of the many cattle sacrifices of King Rantideva; mod. Chambal, which flows from the Mts Vind hya towards the Northeast to the border between Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, before flowing into the Yamunā.
carman [carman] n. skin, leather; shield (of leather) | soc. antelope skin of a brahmacārin.
carya [pfp. [1] car] amnf caryā which must be practiced or accomplished — n. ifc. transport by — f. cf. caryā.

caryā [f. caryā] f. walk, journey, means of locomotion | behavior, conduct, occupation; practice, observance (of (i. iic.)); not. observance of monastic rules and religious rites | office, service, ministry.
caryāgīti [gīti] f. lit. mystical poem sung in the Bengali sahajayāna tantric tradition; cf. Caryācaryaviniścaya.
Caryācaryaviniścaya [ācaryaviniścaya] m. bd. np. from the Caryācaryaviniścaya, a collection of poems
mystics [caryāgīti] in Old Bengali; syn. caryāpāda.
caryāpāda [pāda] m. lit. collection of mystical poems [caryāgīti] in Bengali expressing the mystical experience in bd. tantr. sahajayāna, composed between the 8th and 12th centuries.

Caryāmelāpakapradīpa [melāpakapradīpa] m. lit. np. of the Caryāmelāpakapradīpa "Explanation" integrating the practice", bd. [Vajrayāna] work of Aryadeva; it is the foundation of the esoteric guhyasamāja school.
√ carv [related to cūrṇa] v. [10] pr. (carvayati) pp. (carvita) inf. (carvitum) chew, chew; ron ger.
carvana [act. carv] n. mastication | solid food — f. carvaṇā tasting | molar.
carvaṇaka [agt. carv] amnf carvaṇikā who chews — m. molar.
carvita [pp. carv] amnf carvitā masticated, chewed.
carvitacarvaṇa [carvaṇa] n. ["mastication of chewed" | tedious repetition.

carṣaṇi [kṛṣani] amnf Carṣaṇī active, in dustrious, busy; agile, gifted — f. Carṣaṇī myth. np. of carșanī "the Sower", wife of Varuna and mother of Bhṛgu | pl. carṣaṇyas the sedentary, the farmers, the workers.

√ cal [ reli 'e à car] v. [1] pr. (c 'alati) pp. (ca lita) pfp. (calitavya) pf. (pra, vi, sam) to move, to stir, to be agitated | to set off; to depart, to deviate; to tremble, to throb — ca. (cālayati) to agitate, to shake, to stir | to turn away from, to expel from (abl.), to drive out — intens. r. (cañcalyate) to be unstable | lat. callis. Mālatī mūrdhānam cālayati Mālatī nods his head.
cala [agt. cal] amnf calā mobile, moving; fragile, unstable; trembling, confused; inconstant. calīkr to move.
calatā [tā] f. act of moving, of trembling.
calatva [tva] n. id.
calācala | acala | amnf calācalā unstable, changing, constantly moving — m. myth. np. of calācala, epith. of Šiva "Perpetually changing" | ["mobile and immobile"] plants and animals.
calat [ppr. cal] amnf calantī while moving; mobile. calantī pratimā soc. movable temple image, used for processions; it is called utsavamūrti in South India.
calana |agt. cal| amnf calanā mobile, mouvant — act. n. motion, putting into motion; action of walking | vibration.

calita [pp. cal] amnf calitā trembling, moving; agitated, unstable | disturbed, shaken, deviated; diverted from (abl.) — n. act of moving, stirring; displacement; dance. prathamacalitadakṣiṇacaranah who moves starting from the right foot (auspicious ritual).
calitavya [pfp. [3] cal] amnf calitavyā who must leave | (impers.) we have to leave.
cavarga [(ca)varga] m. phone. the class of palatals.
cavika nf cavikā cf. cavya.
cavī f. cf. cavya.
cavya n. bio. bot. Piper brachystachyum, wild pepper.
caṣaka mn cup, goblet, glass.
caṣāla mn boar's snout | soc. ved. octagonal wooden ring crowning the post sa
crificiel |yūpa|.
cākacakya n. radiance; beauty | var. cākacikya illusion; error of perception.
cākrika [*cakraika] amnf cākrikā circular | concerning a wheel, a disc or a circle — m. chariot driver; potter.
cākṣuṣá [*cakṣusa] amnf cākṣuṣī relating to the eye or vision — m. myth. np. of cākṣuṣa "the Visionary", 6ᵉ Manu of the kalpa — f. cf. cākṣuṣī.
cākṣuṣátva [tva] n. the state of being visually perceptible.
cākṣuṣī [f. cākṣuṣa] f. myth. [Mah.]
science [vidyā] of extralucid vision; the gandharva Angāraparna, who possessed it, taught it to Arjuna who had defeated him in battle.
cākṣuṣīvidyā [vidyā] f. id.
cāta m. mercenary; bandit.
cāṭu [*caṭu] mn flattery, words of love; ten dresse; caresses.
cāṇakya [*caṇakaya] m. hist. n.p. from cāṇakya, patr. of Kauṭilya, minister of Can dragupta Maurya; he is the subject of numerous legends; cf. Viṣṇugupta, Mudrārākṣasa.
cāṇakyanīti [nīti] f. lit. np. of the cāṇakyanīti or Cānakyarājanītiśāstra, a work attributed to Kautilya intended for the teaching of princes, close to the Brhaspatisamhitā of the Garudapurāņa.
cāṇūra m. myth. [BhP.] np. of the wrestler cāṇūra, in the service of Kaṃsa; he was defeated by Krsna as a child.

cānūramardana [mardana] m. myth. np. of cāṇūramardana, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "conqueror of Cānūra". vasudevasutam devam kamsacānūramardanam de vakīparamānandam kṛṣṇam The divine Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva, supreme joy of Devakī, conqueror of the Cānūra of Kamsa.
cāṇḍālá |*caṇḍāla| m. outcaste, pariah; syn. caṇḍāla — ifc. the worst of (iic.) — f. cāṇḍālī outcaste woman.
cāṇḍālaka |*caṇḍālaka| n. thing done by a caṇḍāla.

cātaka [agt. ca. cat] mf cātakī bio. zoo. Cucculus melanoleucus or zoo. Clamator jacobi nus, Jacobin cuckoo, black and white bird; always thirsty, it is said to feed on raindrops, which it must seize before they fall to the ground; syn. sāraṅga .
cātakāstaka [astaka] n. lit. np. from the poem cātakāṣṭaka, of unknown date, celebrating the cātaka.
cātana [agt. ca. cat] amnf cātanā that chases away, that drives away; that suppresses.
cātura [*catura] amnf cāturī intelligent, ingenious — f. cāturī intelligence, skill.

cāturarthiká [*caturarthaika] amnf cāturarthikā gram. is said of a suffix [pratyaya] usable as taddhita in one of the 4 senses: originating (from a country), built (by a person), residence (of a being or people) and proximity (of a river).

cāturmāsya [*caturmāsaya] n. soc. beginning of a period of 4 months; sacrifice made on this occasion; these three seasonal rituals are called vaiśvadeva, varuṇapraghāsās and sākamedhās — amnf cāturmāsyā quadrimonthly (sacrifice).
cāturya [*caturaya] n. skill; charm, amiability; coquetry.
cāturvarnya [*caturvarnaya] n. soc. as a set of the four Vedic classes. cāturvarņyam mayā sṛṣṭam guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ [BhG.] I created the four classes in retribution for merits and deeds.
cāturvaidya [*caturvidya] amnf cāturvaidyī soc. who masters the 4 Vedas; syn. ca turvedin.
cāndra [*Candra] amnf cāndrā lunar; related to Candra | gram. related to the grammar of Candragomi — f. cāndrī lunar light.
cāndrapañjikā [pañjikā] f. gram. np. of the Cāndrapañjikā, commentary on the grammar of Candragomī due to Ratnamati.
cāndramāna [māna₂] amnf cāndramānā (ca calendar) lunar (opp. sauramāna).
cāndramāsa [māsa] m. lunar month.
cāndrayoga [yoga] m. astr. cf. yogas. 7()
cāndravatsara | vatsara | m. lunar year.
cāndravyākaraṇa [vyākaraṇa] n. gram. np. from the Cāndravyākaraņa "grammar of Candragomi", from the 5th century; it is a Sanskrit grammar intended for Buddhists.
cāndravyākaraṇavṛtti [vṛtti] f. bed. n.p. from the Cāndravyākaraṇavṛtti, his self-commentary; cf. Sumatipañjikā.
cāndrasaṃvatsara [saṃvatsara] m. lunar year.
cāndramasá [*candramasa] amnf lunar cāndramasā.
cāndrasenīya [*candrasenaīya] amnf cāndrasenīyī of the lineage of candrasena | soc. class of kāyasthās claiming ksatriya status.
cāpa mn arc; rainbow | hist. n.p. of the cāpa or Cāvaḍā dynasty in Gujarat, established around 690; cf. Vanarāja | math. arc of circle. cāpapāṇiḥ m. who holds the bow in his hand (said not. of Rāma).
cāpaguṇa | guṇa | mr. bowstring.
cāpadhara | dhara | amnf cāpadharā who holds a bow.
cāpapūjā |pūjā| f. myth. np. of the cāpapūjā archery festival to which Kamsa invited Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma in order to kill them; cf. Akrūra.
capin |in| m. archer.
cāpala [*capala] n. lightness, agility, liveliness | frivolity, carelessness, recklessness; childishness; insolence.
cāpalya [*capalaya] n. mobility | agitation; instability, inconstancy.
