cāmara [*camara] amnf cāmarā relating to the yak — n. fly whisk, plume (in yak tail, symbol of royalty) — m. shell zoo. Cy praea moneta, used as money — f. cāmarī id. || hi. kaurī .
cāmaragrāhiṇī [grāhin] f. soc. suite appointed to fan the king with a yak tail fly whisk.
cāmīkara n. or.
cāmuṇḍā [contr. carmamuṇḍā] f. myth. np. of Cāmuṇḍā "Bald Skin", one of the ten powers

terrible [mahāvidyā] of the Goddess [śakti]; black, desiccated, old and hideous, she has a lolling tongue; her mount is a corpse [śavārūḍha]; she is classified as saptamātṛkā as śakti of Rudra | var. cāmuṇḍī myth. she is also called Cāmuṇḍī.
cāra [agt. car] m. spy — act. m. movement, course; journey | practice, exercise.
cāraka [agt. car] amnf cārikā that sets in motion | lit. composed by Caraka | associate, companion — m. cārika ifc. that practices (iic.) — f. cārikā lady-in-waiting.
cārakīna [*Carakaīna] amnf cārakīnā good for nomadic students.

cāraṇa [agt. ca. car] amnf cāraṇī ved. relating to a Vedic school | myth. celestial musicians and singers of Indra's court — mf cāraṇī minstrel, wandering singer | mod. caste of Gujarāt and Rājasthāna; its members are respected for their courage and loyalty; they are prized as hostages; betrayed, they practice self-immolation | lime.

cārāyaṇa [*caraāyana] m. hist. patr. of cārāyaṇa, ancient grammarian mentioned by Patañjali; he is also the promoter [pravaktr] of the eponymous school [cārāyaṇīya] of the Black Yajurveda | lit. [Viddhaśālabhañjikā] np. of the Brahmin cārāyaṇa₁,
jester [vidūṣaka] of King Vidyādharamalla.
cārāyaṇīya [īya] amnf cārāyaṇīyā relating to Cārāyana | phil. school of the black Yajurveda. kambalacārāyaṇīya (pej.) student cārāyaṇīya for the benefit of a cover.
cāritra [instr. car] n. conduct, behavior, attitude | Good conduct, correct attitude; Good reputation | observance; custom.
cārin [agt. car] amnf cāriṇī who does, who acts, who practices; who moves, who circulates — m. infantryman.

Cāru [related to canas] amnf cārvī serene, gentle, kind | beautiful, pleasant, agreeable, charming, graceful, pretty | appreciated, esteemed, dear — m. myth. np. of Cāru "Charming", son of Kṛṣṇa and Rukmiṇī | myth. epith. of Bṛhaspati — f. cārvī pretty woman | myth. np. of cārvī "Charming", wife of Ku bera — n. splendor, charm — adv. in order to please (to (dat.)); agreeably; gracefully | lat. carus; fr. cher.
cārucaryā [caryā] f. lit. np. from the cārucaryā "Good conduct", treatise on hygiene and good manners in 100 verses by Kşemendra.
cārutama |tama| amnf cārutamā super. The most charming, the most beautiful; the best loved.
cārutara [tara] amnf cārutarā compar. plus Charming; very graceful, very beloved.
cārutā |tā| f. beauty, grace; charm; elegance.
cārutva [tva] n. id.
cārutvapratīti | pratīti | f. expression of beauty (essence of poetry according to Abhinavagupta).

cārudatta [datta] m. lit. np. of cārudatta "Endowed with grace", ruined brahmin, principal character of the Mrcchakatikā; the vidūṣaka Maitreya₂ Is his friend, the courtesan Vasantasenā Is in love with him; the child Rohasena Is his son by his wife Dhūtā lit. np. of cārudatta₁, dramatic play by Bhāsa, precursor text of the Mṛcchakaṭikā.
cārudarśana | darśana | amn of pleasant appearance.
cārvakṣara [akṣara] amnf cārvakṣarā (scribe) with beautiful handwriting.
cārvāc [vāc] amnf who speaks kindly.
cārma [*carman] amnf cārmā in leather | (cart) covered in leather.
cārya [pfp. [1] ca. car] n. espionage.

Cārvāka [cārvāc] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the vampire [rākṣasa] Cārvāka₁ "of pleasant speech", friend of Duryodhana; he disguised himself as a mendicant brahmin during the triumphal return of Yudhisthira to Hastināpura to insult him, but was recognized, burned alive and reduced to ashes by the gaze of the brahmins | hist. np. of Cārvāka, probably mythical skeptical philosopher, professing materialism [lokāyata] | pl. cārvākās The materialists, followers of Cārvāka; they are atheists [nāstika] and believe only in the testimonies of their senses; They admit only direct observation through perception as a legitimate means of knowledge [pramāṇa]; they are hedonistic and seek to lead a pleasant life, symbolized by butter [ghṛta]; they reject the transmigration of souls and the afterlife, the authority of the Veda, and caste distinctions; they elevate freedom of thought to a fundamental principle; cf. Brhaspati₁. lokavyavaharasiddha iti cārvakāḥ phil. [Nyāyakusumāñjali] Materialists believe only in worldly affairs.
cāl [ca. cal] v. [10] pr. (cālayati) to agitate, to move again; to turn away from (abl.), to chase away.
cāla [agt. cal] amnf cālā that moves; mobile.
cālaka |agt. cal| amnf cālikā conductor — f. cālikā female conductor.
cālana |act. ca. cal| n. action of stirring, agitation | driving force.

Cālukya m. hist. name of the Cālukya dynasty of the Deccan; it was founded in Karṇāṭa by Prince Jayasimha in the 5th century, at Aryapura (mod. Aihole), cradle of Cālukyā art; in 525 King Rāṇāranga built the sanctuary of Mahākūṭeśvara; King Pulakeśī₁ moved the capital to Vātāpi₁ (mod. Badāmi) in 550; Pulakeśī₂ extended the empire to the South at the expense of the Pallavās and to the East; he stopped Harşa in the North with a victory on the banks of the Narmadā; King Vikramāditya₁ established the chronicles of the dynasty in 658; He captured Kāñcīpura in 671; the last Cālukya of Badāmi was defeated in 753; The Eastern Cālukyās maintained a capital kingdom of Vengī; later (10th century) The Western Cālukyās established their capital at Kalyāṇī; their king Vikramāditya₆ founded the Vikra macālukya era in 1075.
cāṣa m. organic. zoo. Caracias indica, blue jay.
cāhuvāṇa m. hist. np. of the Rajput dynasty Cāhuvāṇa, claiming descent from the Fire lineage |agnivamśa|; it was the last Hindu dynasty to rule Delhi and Ajmer in the 12th century | pkt. chauhan.

√ ci v. [5] pr. (cinóti) pr. r. (cinuté) pft. (cikāya) aor. [1] (acet) aor. [4] (acaiṣīt) pp. (cita) abs. (citvā, citya) pf. (apa, ava, ā, ut, upa, nis, pari, pra, vi, sam) to heap up, accumulate, pile up; to gather, assemble | to search, dig; to note, observe — aor. ps. (acāyi) to increase — ps. (cīyate) to be heaped up, to be gathered together | to prosper, grow (opp. apaci) — ca. (cayayati) ca. (capayati) ca. (cāyayati) ca. (cāpayati) to heap up, assemble — dés. (cikīṣati) dés. (cicīṣati) to want to gather. pușpāṇi ci to pick flowers. agnim ci to maintain the Fire, to stoke ["to gather the embers"].
cikitvas [ppft. cit₁] amnf cikituṣī having observed | attentive, observant; understanding; competent, skillful; wise.
cikits [des. cit₁] v. pr. (cikitsati) pp. (cikit sita) to take care of, to cure; to procrastinate.
cikitsaka [agt. cikits] m. doctor — f. cikitsikā female doctor.
cikitsana [act. cikits] ifc. n. cure of, remedy for.
cikitsā [act. des. cit₁] f. practice of medicine; medical, therapeutic treatment.
cikitsākalikā [kalikā] f. med. np. from the cikitsākalikā "Bottles of Medicine", treatise by Tīsaṭa (10th century), also called Yogamālā; his son Candrața made a comment on it.
cikitsāmṛta [amṛta] n. med. n.p. from the cikitsāmṛta “Nectar of medicine”, an Ayurveda treatise of 2500 verses due to Milhana (Delhi, 1224).
cikitsālaya [ālaya] mn hospital.
cikitsāsaṃgraha [saṃgraha] m. lit. np. of the Cikitsāsamgraha or Cikitsāsārasamgraha "Essential Therapeutics", Ayurveda treatise by Cakrapāṇi₁ Datta.
cikitsita [pp. cikits] amnf cikitsitā cared for; cured — n. medicine.
cikīr ₁ [des. k₁] v. pr. (cikīr ₂ pp. (cikīrṣita) ppr. r. (cikīrṣamāṇa) to want to do.
cikīrṣ₁ [agt. cikīrṣ₁] amnf who wants to do.
cikīrṣaka [agt. cikīrṣ₁] amnf cikīrṣikā who wants to do.
cikīrṣā [act. des. kṛ₁] f. intention, goal; desire to do (g. iic.).
cikīrṣita [pp. cikīrṣita amnf cikīrṣitā (goal) sought (by action); willed, intentional — n. intention.

cikīrṣu [agt. des. kṛ₁] amnf who intends to do, who wants to practice (acc. iic.). cūrņīcikīrṣuḥ desirous of pulverizing. cikīrṣur lokasaṅgraham myth. |BhG.| desire (of Kṛṣṇa) to act for the good of the worlds.
Cikura amnf cikurā rude, impolite — m. hair | myth. [Mah.] np. of the nāga Cikura, son of Aryaka, nāga prince of the line of Airāvata; he married a daughter of Vāmana, their son is Sumukha.
ciketa [pft. cit₁] ind. which included
cikroda m. organic. Indian squirrel, chipmonk. चিস্কা ciñcā f. organic. bot. Tamarindus indica, tamarind tree; its fruit is medicinal.
ciñcāphala | phala | n. its fruit (astringent and laxative).

√ cit₁ v. [1] pr. (cetati) pft. (ciketa) pp. (citta) abs. (cetitvā) pf. (pra, vi) to notice, observe, per cevoir — ca. r. (cetayate) to think, reflect, understand; to know, to be aware of — ca. (cetayati) to point out, to remind; to make understood, to instruct — des. (cikitsati) cf. cikits — intens. r. (cekite) to reflect deeply, to ponder.

cit₂ [agt. cit₁] amnf ifc. who thinks (iic.) — obj. f. thought, intellect; consciousness | knowledge. om cidānandarūpam šivo'ham šivo'ham šivo'ham [mantra] Om Of consciousness and joy is my form, Shiva I am, Shiva I am, Shiva I am. cicchaktiḥ sarvatra bhavati The power of consciousness is everywhere.

cit₃ [agt. ci] ifc. amnf who stacked (2nd century) (not. the bricks of the altar) | ved. (fire altar [uttaravedi]) stacked in the shape of (2nd century). agnicit who stacked (the bricks for the altar) of fire. śyenacit (fire altar) built in the shape of a falcon. kankacit (fire altar) built in the shape of a heron. rathacakracit (fire altar) built in the shape of a chariot wheel.
citcamatkāra [camatkāra] m. phil. joyful wonder of the conscious being.
cítsabhā [sabhā] f. geo. shrine of Siva Natarāja at Cidambaram.

cítsukha [sukhā] m. hist. np. of the master [ācārya] Citsukha, disciple of Śaṃkara₁, author of the Bhāvatattvaprakāśikā, commentary on the Naiskarmyasiddhi of Sureśvara, and of the Citsukhī, commentary on the Nyāyamakaranda.
quote [pp. ci] amnf citā gathered, reunited, piled up — f. cita funeral pyre.
citapuspa | puspa | amnf citapuspā who picked the flowers.
cíti₁ [act. ci] f. heap; not. pile of wood; funeral pyre | collection; multitude.
citi₂ [act. cit₁] f. understanding — m. intel lect.
citt a [pp. cit₁] amnf cittā thought, noticed, understood — n. knowledge; thought; mind, intelligence, reason; heart, wisdom | phil. [Vedānta] l'es

sense [tattva] of consciousness, 4th constituent of the internal instrument [antaḥkaraṇa]; it stores memories in the mind and determines tendencies; its symbolic seat is the Heart, where it is associated with the Soul [jīvātman].
cittanāśa [nāśa] m. phil. [Yoga] cessation of mental activity.
cittamātra [mātra] n. bd. doctrine of the single thought, school of the bd. Mahāyāna; cf. vijñaptimātra.
cittávat [vat] amnf cittavatī qualifies a conscious being.
cittávatkartrka | kartrka | amfn cittavatkartṛkā gram. which is used with an animate agent.
cittáviprayukta [viprayukta] amnf cittavi prayuktā phil. outside of thought; external to the mental image.
cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra [saṃskāra] m. phil. mental pressure from external influence.
cittaviprayuktasaṃskāradharma | dharma | m. phil. ethics of behavior towards others.
cittávibhrama | vibhrama | mr. med. mental disorder; madness.

cittávrtti | vrtti | f. state of mind, emotional state; disposition | imagination, conscious thought; cogi tation | impression, afterthought | phil. | yoga | cognitive process, concept formation; [YS.] fluctuation of thought; judgment is distinguished
valid [pramāṇa], erroneous judgment [viparyaya], conceptualization [vikalpa], loss of attention [nidrā₂], and appeal to memory [smṛti] | lit. psychological modality; opp. śabdavrtti.

cittavrttinirodha [nirodha] m. phil. ["repression of the movements of thought" | control of the mind, cessation of thought; stage of yoga necessary for the attainment of asamprajñāta samādhi; this is the goal of yoga according to the Yogasūtra (I, 2).
yogaścittavrttinirodhah [YS.] Yoga suppresses the fluctuations of the mind.
cittavrttibheda [bheda] m. phil. id.
cittākūtá [ākūta] n. sg. (collective) thoughts and desires.
cittānubodhaśāstra | anubodhaśāstra | n. sg. lit. np. from cittānubodhaśāstra, a philosophical treatise by Bhāskarakantha.
cítti [act. cit₁ ₁] f. thought, intention; understanding, wisdom | pl. thoughts.
citya [pfp. [1] ci] amnf cityā véd. to pile (bricks, sacrificial fire) — n. soc. pile of crematorium wood.

citrá [instr. ci] amnf citrā excellent; remarkable | varied, multifaceted; brilliant; multicolored, variegated | soc. qualifies an execution with various means of torture | astonishing, strange, marvelous — n. representation; drawing, painting, picture | lit. illustration, figure | marvel, prodigy | myth. [Mah.] np. of Citra₁, son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; cf. Citrasena₁ | myth. [Mah.] np. of King Citra₂, hero fighting alongside the Pāndavās in the great battle; he was killed by Prativindhya — f. citrā astr. np. of citrā "the Brilliant One", 12th lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the Ear of Virgo; Indra presides there; its symbol is the pearl | phon. designates various poetic meters, of 4 lines of 16 or 15 syllables | myth. np. of citrā₁, epithet of Subhadrā "born under the sign of citrā" — v. [11] pr. r. (citrīyate) to astonish, to amaze; to perform a miracle; to bewitch. citram adv. in various ways, diversely. citrīyate hemamṛgaḥ the golden deer mystifies. naitaccitram that's not surprising. kimatra citram what's so surprising about that? kañcanacitra (ifc) with gilded illustrations.

citrakāvya [kāvya] n. lit. poetry with graphic support | lit. [Anandavardhana] poetry without suggested meaning | lit. 19th century work of poetic puzzles, by śrī Sundapalayam Ramabhadrachariar (1840-1904).
citrakuṣṭha | kuṣṭha | n. scab leprosy.

citrakūṭa [kūṭa] m. myth. [Rām.] np. from the hill of Citrakūta, where the hermitage of Vālmīki was located; this is where Rāma settled with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa at the beginning of his exile || Pali Cittakūta.
citrakṛt [kṛt₂] amnf astonishing; astounding.

citraketu [ketu] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of Prince Sūrasena citraketu, king of the vidyādharās; he desired a son from his wife Krtadyutī; the sage Angirā promised him one, but at his birth his son was poisoned by the king's other wives, and could not be brought back to life; citraketu became a great adolescent of Visnu; having witnessed Shiva's frolicking with Pārvatī, he mocked it, and Pārvatī cursed him to be reborn like the demon Vrtra, who at the time of his battle with Indra gave a sermon on devotion to the Lord.
citragu |gu| amnf who owns a cow with a spotted coat — m. myth. np. of citragu, son of Kṛṣṇa.

Citragupta | gupta | m. myth. np. of Citragupta "of the many secrets", accountant of the actions |karman| of men at the tribunal of Yama, born from the body of Brahmā; father of Bhattika, he is the patron of scribes [kāyastha]; very meticulous, he keeps track of every action of beings, for their examination on the day of their judgment; a great temple honors him at Khajurāho; he is represented at Prasat Thom, temple of Yama at Koh Ker (near Angkor).
citragrīva [grīva] m. lit. [PT.] np. of the pigeon Ci tragrīva "with a colored throat"; caught in a hunter's nets, it is rescued by Hiranyaka.
citrapañjī [pañjī] f. mod. photo album.
citrapatamga [patamga] m. organic. butterfly.
citrápada [pada] amnf citrapadā peppered with astonishing or graceful words — amnf citrapadā phon. variety of meter anustubh₂.
citrapaddhati [paddhati] f. bed. ["amazing journey"] cf. turagabandha.
citrapura [pura] n. geo. np. of the monastery [maṭha] of citrapura in Kanara (coast of Karṇāṭaka); it is a community of sārasvatās; cf. Bhavānīśankara.
citrabandha | bandha | m. lit. variety of citrakāvya, where the poem is drawn on an image, not. of lotus |padmabandha| or of cobra; syn. bandhacitra.

citrábhānu |bhānu| amnf bright, sparkling (said especially of fire or the Sun) — m. astr. np. of Citrabhānu "Sparkling", personifying the 16th year of a life cycle |saṃvatsara| | hist. np. of Ci trabhānu₁, father of Bāṇa₂; he was a brahmin
scholar | pandita | of gotra vātsyāyana.
citrámīmāṃsā |mīmāṃsā| f. bed. n.p. from Ci tramīmāmsā, a poetic treatise by Jagannātha₁ Panditarāja.

Citraratha | Ratha | amnf Citrarathā with the resplendent chariot — m. myth. epith. of the Sun, Surya myth. np. of the Gandharva king Citraratha₁, epith. of Angāraparņa "with the chariot set on fire (by Arjuna)"; |Mah.| After their flight from the lacquer palace, the Pandavas arrived at the forest where they killed Hidimba and Baka₁; traveling along the Ganges at night, they saw Angāraparņa bathing there with his wife Kumbhīnasī; the Gandharva, guardian of the forest, fought Arjuna, who burned his chariot with the Agneya weapon and took him prisoner; on the advice of Yudhisthira, Arjuna released him; Citra Ratha then taught him the science of extrasensory vision

lucid [cākṣuṣīvidyā], and in return Arjuna taught him the use of the Agneya missile; Citraratha₁ told him that he was descended from Tapatī, and advised the Pāṇdavās to take Dhaumya as their chaplain [purohita] | myth. [Mah.] np. of Citraratha₁, king of Mārttikāvata; while bathing in the river he inspired a guilty desire in Renukā | myth. name of many characters; not. father of Sasabindu.
citrarūpa [rūpa] amnf citrarūpā multiforme; multi-colored.
Citralakṣaṇa | lakṣaṇa | n. lit. np. of the Citralakṣaṇa, treatise on painting by Nagnajit₁.

citralekhā | lekhā| f. myth. np. of the nymph [apsaras] citralekhā "Who draws wonderfully"; she helped Uṣā₁ to recognize her lover Aniruddha by a portrait which she animated to materialize it phon. np. of a meter of 4 verses of 15 syllables of maramayaya pattern.
citravadha | vadha | m. soc. capital execution with torture.
Citravāhana | vāhana | m. myth. | Mah. | np. of Ci travāhana "with the shining chariot", king of Maṇipura, father of Citrāngadā.
citraśālā |śālā| f. picture gallery, room decorated with paintings.
citraśravas | śravas | amnf whose glory is brilliant.
citrasūtra |sūtra| n. lit. np. of the citrasūtra, section of the Vișnudharmottara dealing with painting.

Citrasena [senā] m. myth. np. of the Gandharva king Ci trasena "with the marvelous weapon"; he embodies Brahmā punished by a curse; Sandhyā and Ratnāvalī are his wives; |Mah.| when Arjuna ascended to heaven following his penances, he studied singing and dancing with him, and became his friend; Arjuna saved him from a curse of Kṛṣṇa, his spittle having fallen on the ascetic Gālava performing his Sandhyā rite; during the exile of the Pāṇdavās, he was bathing in a pond near their hermitage with his Gandharvā companions, when Duryodhana arrived at the head of a troop, and ordered them to leave; Citrasena took him prisoner, and released him at the request of Arjuna | myth. | Mah. | np. of Citrasena₁, son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, killed by Bhīma; cf. Ugrasena₁ myth. np. of many other characters.

citrāngada [angada] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of citrāngada "of the shining bracelet", son of King Sāṃtanu and Satyavatī; crowned king of Has tināpura by his half-brother Bhīşma, who had renounced the throne; he lived in pleasure without worrying about producing an heir, and was punished for this 3 years later by an eponymous gandharva, who killed him in battle; the crown passed to his younger brother Vicitravīrya — f. citrāngadā myth. [Mah.] np. of Citrāngadā, princess of Manipura, daughter (and sole heir [putrikā]) of Citravāhana; Arjuna married her, and she had a son, Babhruvāhana.
citrācārya |ācārya| m. master of graphic arts.
citrādvaitaprakāśavāda [advaitaprakāśavāda] m. bed. n.p. from citrādvaitaprakāśavāda, phil. work. of Ratnakīrti.
citrotpala | utpala | amnf Citrotpalā Which has lotuses of all colors — f. Citrotpalā geo. np. of the river Citrotpalā.
Citrotpalāvalambitaka [avalambitaka] m. bed. n.p. from Citrotpalāvalambitaka, a romantic comedy by śrī Sankuka, now lost.

citraka [Citraka] m. painter | bio. bot. Plum bago indica, shrub with bright red flowers, used in medicine; syn. dahana — n. ifc. marked by, characterized by; decoration of | sectarian mark on the forehead | decoration; painting.
citrin [Citrain] amnf citrinī with salt and pepper hair — f. citriṇī [kāmaśāstra] one of the 4 types of women.

cid₁ var. cit part. cl. one, some, one of (gives an indefinite meaning to interrogative pronouns) lat. quid. kaścit someone, whoever; whoever person. kasmimścit in some way; in any way; anywhere. na kaścit person, no one. na kaścid api absolutely no one. katicit some, several. kimcit something, a little, something. na kimcit nothing. na kimcid api absolutely nothing. yat kimcit any thing, whatever it may be. yaḥ kaścit whoever, anyone, whoever. kecit some, certain. kecit ... kecit ... some ..., others ... kathamcit in some way. kaccit is it that? perhaps? isn't it true that? kadācit sometimes, occasionally; once, one day. na kadācit never. kutracit somewhere. kvacit somewhere; sometimes. na kvacit nowhere; never. kvacit ... kvacit ... sometimes ... sometimes ...
cid₂ iic. cit₂.

Cidambara [ambara] m. myth. n.p. of Cidambara "Pure spirit", linga of Space [ākāśa], hidden behind a curtain in the sanctuary [citsabhā] of Siva Națarāja; it is the pañcabhūtasthala dedicated to the ether |ākāśa|; cf. Candramaulīśvara — n. geo. n.p. from the town of Cidambaram in Tamil Nadu; cf. dīkṣita.
cidātman |ātman| mr. phil. pure consciousness.
cidānanda [ānanda] m. consciousness and joy | hist. np. of the philosopher cidānanda, philosopher of language, author of the Nītitattvāvirbhāva.

cidānandadaśaślokī [Daśaślokī] f. lit. np. of the cidānandadaśaślokī or Daśaślokī "10 verses on consciousness and joy", work of Śamkara₁; also called Cidānandastavarāja or Nirvānadaśaka; the Siddhāntabindu is a commentary on it.
Cidānandastavarāja [stavarāja] m. bed. n.p. of Cidānandastavarāja; cf. cidānandadaśaślokī.
cidghana [ghana] m. phil. ["compact mass of thought"] pure consciousness.
cidrūpa [rūpa] amnf cidrūpā formed of pure thought; syn. cinmaya — n. phil. the Supreme Being as formed of pure thought.
cin iic. cit₂.
cinmaya [maya] amnf cinmayī phil. made of pure thought; [Vedānta] qualifies the undifferentiated universe.

Cinmayānanda [ānanda] m. hist. np. of Svāmī Cinmayānanda "Bliss of pure consciousness", born Balakṛṣṇan Menon in Kerala (1916–1993); after a brief career as a journalist, where he joined the movement to fight for Indian independence, he became a disciple of Svāmī Sivānanda; he spent 12 years in the Himalayas to follow the teachings of Svāmī Tapovana Mahārāja; he then preached Vedānta throughout the world by establishing the "Chin maya Mission".
cinmātra [mātra] amnf cinmātrī phil. [Vedānta] made of pure consciousness; syn. cinmaya.
cinmudrā [mudrā] f. symbolic gesture of wisdom; cf. mudrākhya.

√ cint [related to cit₁] v. [10] pr. (cintáyati) pp. (cintita) ppr. r. (cintayāna) pfp. (cintya, cin tanīya) abs. (cintayitvā, cintya) pf. (anu, pari, vi, sam) to think, reflect, meditate; to consider; to think about, to attend to (acc.) | lat. sentio. cintayāmāsa he/she thought. iti cintayatas tasya (g. absolute) while he was engaged in these reflections. na kimcid api cintayet [BhG.] One should not think of anything.
cintaka [agt. cint] ifc. amnf cintikā who thinks about, who reflects on; who is concerned with; familiar with. sṛṣṭicintaka phil. [MU.] creationist.
cintana [act. cint] n. act of thinking, reflection; preoccupation; consideration — f. cin tanā id.
cintayāna [ppr. mo. cint] amnf cin tayānā reflecting, considering.

cintā [act. cint] f. thought, reflection; meditation, reverie | worry, preoccupation; in quietude, anxiety (about (g. loc. iic. upari)) matter for reflection, examination, suspicion. cintayā by the mere thought of. cintām dhā to think about, to be preoccupied with (loc.). cintā māstu var. cintā mā kuru do not worry. cintākrtya having reflected.
cintākavi |kavi| m. lit. category of poet using reflection.

Cintāmaṇi |maṇi| m. variety of fabulous jewel, which changes its appearance according to the thoughts of its possessor | myth. np. of the Cintāmaṇi "Mirror of Thoughts", fabulous jewel which grants all the wishes of its possessor; it belongs to Brahmā | hist. np. of the nāthayogin Cintāmaṇi₁, author of the Hathayogapradīpikā; he took the religious name of Svātmārāma; he was honored with the title of yogīndra | lit. [Vāsavadattā] np. of King Cintāmaṇi₁ of Kusuma pura, father of Kandarpaketu₁ — ifc. lit. "treasure of (iic.)", name of works; cf. Tattvacintāmaņi. cintāmanim parityajya kācamanigrahananyāyah maxim of abandoning the magical jewel Cintāmaņi for a piece of quartz; it is equivalent to "letting go of the substance for the shadow". cintāmaņisāraņikā [sāraņikā] f. lit. np. of the Cintāmaņisāraņikā, an astrological work by Daśabala (11th century).
cintāmaya [maya] amnf cintāmayī consisting of ideas; imagined; reflected.
cintāratna [ratna] n. wish-fulfilling jewel; syn. Cintāmaṇi₁ — pp. (cintāratnāyita) (impers.) represented as a wish-fulfilling jewel.
cintita [pp. cint] amnf cintitā thought, meditated, imagined | something that has been reflected upon; investigated; found — n. intention.
cintya [pfp. [1] cint] amnf cintyā which must be meditated upon, which deserves reflection; which can be conceived or seen | subject to caution, debatable — n. necessity of thinking about g. .

cirá [cira] amnf cirā long (time), which lasts a long time — v. [11] pr. (cirāyati) to take a long time; to delay. ciram adv. a long time. cirasya var. cirasya kālasya adv. after a certain time. cirena adv. for a long time. cirāt adv. a long time ago; for a long time; in the end, finally. cirāt drśyate it has been a long time since we last saw each other.
cirakāla [kāla₁] amnf cirakālā ancient — acc. cirakālam adv. for a long time — abl. cirakālāt adv. taking into account the antiquity — dat. cirakālāya adv. for a long time.
cirajīvin [jīvin] amnf cirajīvinī cf. ciramjīvin.
cirátama |tama| amnf ciratamā super. the most extended (time); the slowest. ciratamena more slowly.
cirátara |tara| amnf ciratarā compar. longer (time); very slow. cirataram for a very long time. ciratarena more slowly.
cirátā [tā] f. Long duration.
ciranavīna |navīna| amnf ciranavīnā eternally young.
cirabilva | bilva | m. bio. bot. Holoptelea integrifo lia, tree with yellowish bark, a toxic ulmaceae; it is used in medicine.

cirāyus [āyus] amnf who has a Long life — m. crow | lit. [KSS.] np. of the city cirāyus "Long life" and of its king, who had reached the age of 800 years thanks to the elixir of his minister Nāgārjuna₄.
ciram [acc. cira] adv. for a long time; for a long time.
ciraṃjīva [jīva] amnf ciraṃjīvā [“who has a long life” | affectionate term of address for a child.

ciramjīvin [jīvin] amnf ciramjīvinī who lives long; eternal | soc. destined for a Long life (used to wish Long life to the young groom during the marriage rite) | myth. epith. of Viṣṇu, of Vyāsa, of Mārkandeya or of Jāmbavān | myth. one of the 7 immortals: Aśvatthāmā, Bali, Vyāsa, Hanuman, Vibhīṣaṇa, Kṛpācārya, and Paraśurāma; they will be the saptarși of the 8th manvantara | bio. beautiful horn (symbol of longevity).
cirāyita [pp. cira ] amnf cirāyitā late. kimiti cirāyitam tvayā why are you late?
cilla amnf cillā chassieux — m. organic. zoo. black kite, peregrine falcon. bandhanabhraṣṭo gṛhakapotaścillāyā mukhe
patitali ["like the dove which escapes captivity only to become prey for the falcon"] fallen from Charybdis to Scylla.
cilli [cilla] m. bio. falcon, bird of prey.
cihna n. mark, stamp; sign, characteristic, symptom | banner, sign — f. cihnā ifc. sign of (form of signatures).
cīt [onomatopoeia] iic. brrr, pschitt.
cītkāra [kāra] m. noise, screams.
cīna var. cīṇa m. lead | pl. cīnās geo. the Chinese; China.
cīnapaṭṭa [paṭṭa] m. Chinese silk (opp. in silk
dienne | kauśeya|).
cīnapiṣṭa [piṣṭa] n. minimum.
cīnāṃśuka [aṃśuka] n. ["Chinese fabric"] silk.
cīnaka [cīnaka] m. pl. geo. the Chinese.
cīra [cira] n. garment made of plant material or bark, for a renunciant or a brahmacārin — ifc. (iic.) in rags.
cīrṇa [pp. car] amnf cīrṇā practiced, observed (vow, penance) — n. conduct.
cīvara n. bd. monk's garment; cf. tricīvara rags.
Cuñcu [related to cañcu] amnf ifc. renowned for — m. myth. np. of King Cuñcu "Famous", of the solar lineage | sūryavaṃśa|, son of Rohitāśva; Su deva is his son. vidyācuñcu renowned for his knowledge.
√ cud v. [1] pr. (codati) pp. (cudita) pf. (pra, sam) ved. to offer — ca. (codáyati) ppr. (codayat) to incite, excite, urge; to press, solicit. codayāt (benedictive) may he incite.
√ cumb v. [1] pr. (cumbati) pp. (cumbita) pf. (bet) kiss, kiss.
cumba [act. cumb] m. kiss, embrace.
cumbaka [agt. cumb] amnf cumbakā who embraces a lot — m. loving.
cumbakamani | mani | m. lodestone.
cumbakeya [īya] amnf cumbakeyā magnetic.
cumbana [act. cumb] n. kiss.
cumbita [pp. cumb] amnf cumbitā em brewed.
cumbin [agt. cumb] ifc. amnf cumbinī who kisses (iic.) | busy with (iic.).
√ cur v. [10] pr. (corayati) aor. [3] (acūcurat) pft. (corayāmāsa) pp. (corita) to steal, to rob,
to plunder | to make disappear | to steal (Romani)
curā [act. cur] f. vol.
curādi [(cur)ādi] m. gram. ["which begins with cur"] qualifies the tenth class [gaṇa] of the present tense of verbs; its characteristic marker |vikarana₂| is nic.

Culuka mn, a hollowed hand for drinking water (myth. np.) of King Culuka, presumed founder of the Caulukya dynasty. culukam jalasya kal, to drink a sip of water. culukīkṛ, to swallow in one gulp | to make disappear.
cūcuka n. teat.
cūṭa m. myth. [YV.] np. du kalpavṛkṣa Cūṭa of Indra's paradise, with gold and silver leaves; it shelters the raven Bhuśuṇḍa.
cūḍa m. crest (rooster, peacock) | diadem; capital (column) — f. cf. cūdā.

cūḍā [f. cūḍa] f. tuft of hair at the top of the skull, tuft, crest. soc. lock reserved during the tonsure of a brāhmaṇa, not. during the upanayana or mourning; syn. śikhā || hi. curkī, cuṭiyā. cūdākaraņa [karaṇa] n. soc. tonsure (preserving the cūḍā); not. saṃskāra of first tonsure of a child, in his 3rd year; syn. cūdākarman, caula.
cūḍākarman [karman] n. cf. cūḍākaraṇa.

cūdāmani [mani] m. jewel worn on the top of the head | astr. favorable conjunction of the sun and moon (solar eclipse on a Sunday or lunar eclipse on a Monday) — ifc. (in fig.) best of, jewel of, crowning achievement of (ii.) | soc. np. of cūḍāmaṇi, honorific title of scholar; cf. Janakīnātha Bhaṭṭācārya.
cūdāratna | ratna | n. cf. cūdāmani.
cūḍāla [la] amnf cūḍālā who has a crest; who wears the lock; syn. cūḍāvat.
cūdāvat [vat] amnf cūdāvatī who has a crest; who wears the lock of hair — m. young boy.
cūdin [in] amnf cūdinī who wears the lock [cūḍā].

Cūta m. bio. bot. Mangifera indica, mango tree | myth. [YV.] np. of the immense Cūta tree of Indra's radish, whose leaves and flowers shine like jewels; it is inhabited by sages, including the raven of eternity Bhusunda.
cūtavṛkṣa [vṛkṣa] m. mango tree.
cūrṇa [related to carv] mn powder; dust; flour; sandalwood powder | chalk; limestone powder used for making the

betel [tāmbūla] | plaster — v. [11] pr. (cūrṇayati) pp. (cūrnita) to reduce to powder, to pulverize. cūrnīkr to reduce to powder, to pulverize, to crush. cūrņīkṛta pulverized. cūrṇībhū to become dust; to be crushed. cūrņavṛddha [vṛddha] m. lit. [Mṛcchakaṭikā] np. of cūrṇavṛddha, friend of Cārudatta. cūrņaśas [śas] adv. in powder. cūrņaśah kr to reduce to powder.
cūrṇi [f. cūrṇa] f. gram. scholastic analysis drowning in details, splitting hairs | var. cūrnī id. || pkt. cunni.
cūrṇin [cūrṇain] amnf cūrṇinī (cake) obtained by mixing powdered substances.
cūrti [car] f. act of walking.
cūlavaṃśa m. lit. np. of the Cūlavaṃśa, the most recent part of the Mahāvaṃśa chronicle of the kings of Laṅkā.
cūlā f. cf. cūḍā.
cūlin [cūlāin] amnf cūlinī who carries the

lock [cūdā] | which bears a crest; whose crown is adorned — m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the ṛṣi Cūlī; the gandharvī Somadā was very devoted to him; by thought he impregnated her to give birth to the sage Brahmadatta.
√ cūs v. |1| pr. (cūsati) pp. (cūsita) pfp. (cūṣaṇīya, coṣya) to suck; to aspirate; to dry | ang. suck.
cūṣaṇa [act. cūṣ] n. suction (not. leech).
√ crt v. [6] pr. (crt st i) pp. (crt ta) pf. (ā, ni) to bind — ca. (cartayati) to bind — dice. (cicartișati) to want to bind.
cekitāna [ppr. mo. intens. cit₁] amnf cekitānā intelligent — m. myth. np. of the prince cekitāna "the Wise", ally of the Pāṇḍavās.
ceta mf cetī servant; slave.
cet₁ [ca. cit₁] v. [10] pr. (cetayati) to point out, to make perceived; to remind; to instruct — pr. r. (cetayate) to think, to reflect, to understand; to know, to understand.
cet₂ iic. ced.

Cetaka [agt. cit₁] amnf cetakī that gives thought, evocative; that makes one think; endowed with thought — m. hist. np. of Cetaka "Strategist", chief of the Licchavi clan; he reigned in Vaiśālī₁ in Bihāra in the 5th century BC, and fought Ajātaśatru₂ — f. cetakī bio. bot. Jasminim grandiflorum, jasmine; syn. mālatī | lit. |poetic| the scent of the jasmine flower |cetakī| evokes the beloved.

cetana [agt. cit₁] amnf cetaníi conscious, sensitive, sensible, intelligent — m. intelligent man | mind, thought, consciousness — act. n. intelligence, soul — f. cetanā consciousness, sensitivity; understanding, intelligence. cetanībhū to become aware of.
cetanatva [tva] n. sensitivity, conscious state.
cetaya [agt. ca. cit₁] amnf cetayā which makes
to perceive | sensitive | that brings back to life.
cetas [abstr. cit₁] n. conscience, mind, heart, wisdom, thought.
ced var. cet₂ [ca] conj. cl. si, provided that, in case (what precedes). atha ced but if. na ced otherwise, unless; so that not ... not. yadi ced if. iti cenna if (one speaks) thus (we answer) no!

cedi m. geo. n.p. from a country south of the Ya munā (mod. Bundelkhand); Śuktimatī₁ was its capital | myth. n.p. of cedi, founding ancestor of a royal dynasty [samvat] (around 249) | pl. cedayas his people, the cedayas; cf. Uparicara, Damaghosa, Dhṛṣṭaketu, Siśupāla, Subāhu₂.
this n. clothes | (figuratively) appearance — f. celī ifc. (pej.) semblance of, parody of, poor (iic.) — m. slave.

√ cest v. [1] pr. (cestati) pr. r. (cestate) aor. [5] (aceṣṭīt) aor. [3] (aciceṣṭat) pp. (ceṣṭita) pfp. (cestavya) pf. (vi) to gesticulate, to stir, to agitate — ca. (ceṣṭayati) to set in motion, to excite; to exhort.
ceșța [agt. ceșt] m. bio. type of fish — act. nf ceṣṭā Gesture; movement, effort, activity; execution, conduct | lat. gestus; ang. gesture; fr. Geste.
cestaka [agt. cest] amnf cestikā who makes an effort.
cestana [act. cest] n. effort; agitation; movement — agt. amnf ceṣṭanā that is agitated.

cestita [pp. cest] amnf cestitā put into motion — n. movement of the body; effort, action; manner of acting. loke gurutvam viparītām vā svacestitānyeva naram nayanti It is his own actions that lead man to a high position in the world or to adversity.

Caitanya [*cetanaya] n. mind, consciousness, sensation | phil. [yoga] eternal consciousness, spiritual ritual | phil. [Vaiseșika] consciousness of the sensible world — m. soc. title of novice [brahmacārin] of the Bhāratī order | phil. np. of Kṛṣṇa Caita nya "consciousness of Kṛṣṇa" (1486–1533), Vaishnava mystic, born Viśvambhara Miśra son of Ja gannātha₂ in Māyāpura near Navadvīpa north of the Ganges in Bengal; his mother Sacī Devī called him Nīmāya (Nimaï); he was an expert in Sanskrit and rhetoric [pandita] from a very young age, and trained many students; He married at the age of 15; following an ecstatic experience in 1509, he was

initiated [dīkṣā] by Keśava₁, a monk of the Bhāratī order of Sankara₁, but followed a doctrine close to that of Rāmānuja; he preached devotion [bhakti] to Kṛṣṇa through devotional chanting [kīrtana], recitation of the mahāmantra and ecstatic dancing; he was of radiant beauty [Gaurānga]; he retired as a sannyāsin to Purī in 1515; he represents Kṛṣṇa reincarnated as his own disciple, and is venerated as Mahāprabhu; he is depicted in a pose of ecstatic dancing, with his arms raised to heaven; Viśvarūpa₂ was his elder brother; Nityānanda (Nitai) was his friend and disciple; cf. Gauracandra, Prabhupāda, Siksāstaka.
caitanyacaritāmṛta [caritāmṛta] n. bed. n.p. from Cai tanyacaritāmṛta “Nectar of the Gesture of Caitanya”, by Kṛṣṇadāsa (Bengali, 1581).
caitanyabhāgavata [bhāgavata] m. lit. np. of the Cai tanyabhāgavata, biography of Caitanya.
caitanyasvarūpa [svarūpa] n. phil. conscious state.
caitya₁ [*cit₂ya] m. individual soul.
caitya₁ [*citāya] mn funerary monument; chapel annexed to a temple | soc. object of worship; sacred tree; sacred stone | bd. Sanctuary; prayer hall | jn. representation [mūrti] of a saint [jina].

Caityaka [ka] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Caityaka "Sanctuary", one of the 5 hills surrounding the city of Girivraja; it bore a Sanctuary where three drums made with the skin of rākṣasās were beaten; it was by this route that Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna and Bhīma arrived when they attacked Jarāsandha.
caityavandana [vandana] n. soc. veneration of icons and temples.

Caitra [*citrā] m. month of citrā (March-April); it begins the lunar year | soc. wandering monk bd. or jaïne | common man's name; "So-and-so" | soc. patr. Caitra "son of citrā"; np. of a son of Buddha — f. caitrī soc. its full moon; a pākayajña is practiced there; it is the birthday [jayantī] of Hanuman.
caitraratha [*citraratha] m. myth. np. of caitraratha "fruit of the work of citraratha", the ancient garden of Kubera on Mount Mandara; its gardener is citraratha.
caila [*cela] amnf cailā made of fabric |[“raised in a cocoon”] butterfly, insect — n. piece of fabric; garment; shawl — f. cailā ifc. clothed in (iic.).
coca n. bark, not. of cinnamon.
coda [related to cūḍā] m. prince of the Coḍās | pl. geo. np. of the people of the Codās.
codaganga [gangā] m. hist. n.p. from the Codaganga dynasty of Kalinga (12th century); cf. Ananta varma.
cod [ca. cud] v. [10] pr. (codáyati) to incite, ex cite, urge; to press, solicit.
codá [agt. cud] amnf codā that animates, that inspires, that incites — m. goad, whip.
codaka [agt. cud] amnf codikā instigator; conductor — m. invitation.
códana [agt. cud] amnf codanī which obliges — act. n. injunction, rule — f. cf. codanā
codanā [f. codana] f. injunction, rule.
codanālakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] amnf codanālakṣaṇā phil. bounded by rules (said not. of dharma). codanālakṣaṇe'rthaḥ dharmaḥ |Mīmāṃsāsūtra| The dharma aims to respect the (Vedic) injunctions.
coditá [pp. ca. cud] amnf coditā enjoined, urged; invited; ordered | informed; about which one has been informed.
codya [pfp. [1] cud] amnf codyā which must be incited | to criticize — n. questioning incitement to controversy.
codyaparihāra [parihāra] m. bd. refutation of criticisms.
corá [agt. cur] mf corī thief; plagiarist.
corabhaya [bhaya] n. fear of thieves.
corita [pp. cur] amnf coritā stolen, robbed — n. vol.
coritaka [ka] n. well stolen — m. petty thief.

Cola m. blouse, jacket | pl. colās geo. name of the Colā people of the Coromandel Coast |colamandala| | hist. ancient royal Cola dynasty of the Kāverī Valley, ruling much of South India from the 9th to the 13th century; their capital was Thanjavur; cf. Rājarāja₁.
colamandala [mandala] mn geo. Cola country, on the South coast of the Coromandel | topo. Coromandel.
colaka [Colaka] m. blouse, jacket; dress | cuirass — n. bark.
cauḍa var. caula [*cūḍā] n. soc. saṃskāra of tonsure of a child; cf. cūdākaraṇa.
caura [*cora] m. thief, brigand; swindler, usurper, plagiarist — f. caurī thief.

caurapañcāśikā [pañcāśikā] f. lit. np. of the caurapañcāśikā “50 stanzas of the abductor” (also Caurīsuratapañcāśikā “50 stanzas of the abductor’s loves”), an erotic poem by Bilhana; its 50 stanzas in vasantatilakā meter, of which there are two recensions, all begin with “Even today” [adyāpi]; they evoke the poet’s love for a princess from whom he is now separated, in the register of the pain of thwarted love [vipralambha]; legend tells that a king Vīrasimha had a daughter Śaśikalā of exceptional intelligence by his wife Sutarā; he entrusted her to the Kashmiri scholar Bilhana to educate her; The master and his pupil fell in love, were caught in the act, and Bilhana was condemned to the scaffold; he recited his poems as he ascended the steps, and the king, moved by their beauty, pardoned Bilhana and granted him his daughter's hand in marriage. Even today I remember her, petite, her face radiant like the full moon, her hair flowing in disarray, her body wild with passion, bending under the weight of her heavy breasts and thighs, leading the frenzied dance of love.
caurabhaya | bhaya | n. fear of the thief.
cauravidyā [vidyā] f. science of flight, one of the 64 arts | kalā].
cauravīra | vīra | mr. pl. cauravīrās underworld.
cauraka [agt. cur] m. thief — f. caurika thief.
caurya [cauraya] n. cheating, theft.
cauryarata | rata | n. illicit sexual pleasure.
cauryavidyā |vidyā| f. art of theft | lit. np. of the cauryavidyā, treatise on the art of theft, attributed to Yogācārya, who received it from Kārttikeya.
cauryavṛtti [vṛtti] amnf who is in the habit of stealing; who lives by stealing — f. practice of stealing.
cauryaśāstra [śāstra] n. science of flight; cf. Sanmukhakalpa.
caula [*cūḍā] n. soc. saṃskāra of tonsure of a child; cf. cūdākarana.
Caulukya [*Culukaya] m. n.p. from the Caulukya dynasty "Descendant of King Culuka"; she reigned at Anahilapātaka in Gurjara from 940 to 1244; cf. Kumārapāla, Siddharāja.

cyávana [agt. cyu] amnf cyavanā fallen; that which makes fall; that which shakes; that which helps to give birth— m. myth. ved. np. of the sage [rṣi] Cyavana or Cyavāna "Premature", son of Bhṛgu, born in the forest after the abduction of his mother Pulomā₂ by the demon Pu lomā₁; he practiced great penances at a very young age, and his motionless body was covered with earth and vegetation; when he was very old, King Saryāti came one day to picnic with his family in the forest; his daughter, the pretty Sukanyā, went with her friends to the mound where he was buried, and from which emanated a strange radiance; Sukanyā dug out of curiosity, and Cyavana's voice ordered her to stop, but she continued, saw two bright spots, and drove thorns into them, blinding the sage; Cyavana, in great suffering, continued his asceticism without cursing Sukanyā, but this injustice caused great misfortunes in the land; neither man nor beast could defecate or urinate anymore; to cause these disorders, King Śaryāti conducted an inquiry, and Sukanyā confessed his evil deed; Šaryāti came to prostrate himself before the sage, and begged his forgiveness; the sage, decrepit, ugly and blind, asked for the hand of the beautiful woman, to the despair of the king who had to accept; Sukanyā became a devoted wife to her old husband; at that time Indra had forbidden the Aśvinau to drink the soma |somapāna|; These men met Sukanyā, were dazzled by her beauty, and offered to leave Cyavana to marry one of them; upon her indignant refusal, they explained that they were divine physicians and could prepare a rejuvenating bath that would make Cyavana as young and desirable as themselves, provided that in the end she chose between the three of them; they plunged with the old hermit into the river, and returned as identical triplets, young and desirable; by praying to the Goddess to make her choose her true husband, Sukanyā correctly identified Cyavana; he thanked the Aśvinau by forcing Indra to allow them to participate in a soma ceremony to which he invited all the gods; when Indra brandished his vajra he paralyzed it, and drew from the sacrificial fire a Mada demon capable of killing all the gods; These fled, and the paralyzed Indra had to surrender and apologize; Cyavana tore Mada into 4 demons of possession: Gambling, Hunting, Alcohol and Women; Pramati is the son of Cyavana and Su kanyā; Cyavana is also father of Aurva by Aruṣī, daughter of Manu; cf. Kekaralohita — n. movement; descent | jn. fall from divine existence to the human condition | bd. death — ifc. fall from; deprivation of (iic.).
cyávāna [ppr. cyu] amnf cyavānā ved. that moves; active — m. myth. np. of Cyavāna, son of Bhrgu; cf. Cyavana.

√ cyu v. [1] pr. r. (cyávate) v. [1] pr. (cyávati) pp. (cyuta) to stagger, fall, decline; to move; to come and go; to fidget | to move away, disappear, appear, fail — ca. (cyāváyati) to agitate, shake; to drive away abl. | to deprive someone acc. of something acc. . vṛṣṭiṃ cyāvayati to make it rain.
cyut [cyuta] ifc. amnf that makes fall (iic.).
cyuta |pp. cyu| amnf cyutā fallen, deposed; past; expelled; deprived of (abl.) | reached maturity (said of a fruit that falls from the tree when ripe). cyutādhikāra amn having lost his job.
cyutaka [ka] ifc. n. Game consisting of finding a missing element (iic.) in a sentence.
cyuti [act. cyu] f. banishment, degradation; fall; expulsion | disappearance, loss; death. garbhasya cyuti abortion.
cli nota. gram. modifier [vikarana₂] of generic formation of the aorist, to be substituted by sic, ksa, can, an or cin.
cvi nota. gram. inchoative formation in ī or ū used as a verbal prefix |gati| of the auxiliaries kṛ₁ (to bring into the state of), bhū₁ (to become), and (rarely) as₁ (to be).
ch
chakāra |(cha)kāra| m. the sound or letter 'cha'.
chaga |related to chāga | m. bio. goat.
chagalá |la| m. id. | myth. np. du muni Chagala — n. goat.
chaṭā f. agglomerate; mass.
chattra |instr. chad₁| n. parasol, umbrella; parasol (insignia of royalty, symbolizing the protection of the people) | var. chatra id. chattrīkṛ use as a parasol.
chatropānahapriyaḥ [Mah.] (A student) who cherishes the parasol and the clogs.

Chattrapati [pati] m. soc. officer holding the royal parasol | hist. np. of Chattrapati "Master of the parasol", royal title; not. title of the Maratha king Chattrapati Sivajī at his coronation in 1674.
chattravat [vat] amnf chattravatī equipped with a parasol.

Chattrasāla |śāla| m. hist. np. of Mahārāja Chat trasāla (1649–1731), who fought Aurangzeb and established an independent kingdom in Bundelkhand; his palace is in Dhubela, near Khajurāho; Sabhāsimha is his son.

chattrin [in] amnf chattrinī equipped with a para sol — m. arch. pavilion surmounted by a dome, used as a decorative element of a palace, temple or cenotaph | geo. prince's cenotaph, not. in Rajasthan | jn. cenotaph honoring a
superior [bhattāraka].
√ chad₁ v. [1] pr. (chadati) pp. (channa) pf. (ā, pari, pra, sam) ca. (chādáyati) to cover, to wrap; to hide, to keep secret.
chad₂ [agt. chad₁] ifc. amnf which hides (iic.).
chada [agt. chad₁] amnf chadā that covers — m. cover; wing; leaf — n. plumage.
chadana |act. chad₁| n. veil, covering.
chadi [chadin] ifc. amnf that covers (iic.); that forms a roof over (iic.). návacchadi with 9 roofs.
chadin [agt. chad₁] ifc. amnf chadinī which covers (iic.).
chadís [abstr. chad₁] n. roof, thatch.
Chadma IIc. Chadman.
chadmatāpasa | tāpasa | m. alleged ascetic.
chadmarūpa |rūpa| amnf chadmarūpā disguised. chadmarūpeņa adv. incognito; under a disguise.
chadmarūpin | rūpin | ifc. amnf chadmarūpinī disguised as (iic.).
chadman [chad₁man] n. disguise; mask | pretext; deception, cheating; betrayal, treachery, perfidy — ifc. disguised as (iic.). tāpasacchadmanah disguised as ascetics.
chadmin [chad₁min] ifc. amnf chadminī disguised as (iic.).

chand v. [1] pr. (chandati) pp. (chandita) pf. (upa) to please (dat. acc.), to satisfy — v. [1] pr. r. (chandate) to be satisfied with (acc.); to take pleasure in (acc. loc. rangle — ca. (chandayati) to be favorable to, to gratify someone (acc.) with (i.).

chánda [act. chand] m. intention, desire, will; pleasure, predilection; whim. chandátas adv. according to one's desire, according to one's intention; at will | according to the will of g. . yaste chandaḥ as you wish. chandataḥ kriyā action according to one's good pleasure. ন্তবেক Chandaka |agt. chand| ifc. amnf chandikā ifc. that which enchants (iic.) — m. bd. np. of Chandaka, charioteer of Sākyamuni.
chandana |agt. chand| amnf chandanā pleasant, charming.

chándas |abstr. chand| n. desire, will | Vedic hymn, meter; a distinction is made between Vedic meters, based on the alternation of long or short syllables [akṣaravṛttā], and those based on the alternation of long or short vowels [mātrāvṛttā], used only in Classical Sanskrit | phil. metrics or prosody, one of the 6 supplementary treatises of the Veda [vedānga] | gram. Vedic language (opp. bhāṣā) mus. rhythmic harmony. chandasi loc. adv. gram. in Vedic texts. chandaḥ padau tu vedasya [Pāṇinīyaśikṣā] The meter gives the Veda its legs.

Chandaḥśāstra [śāstra] n. phil. prosody | lit. np. of the Chandaḥśāstra or Pingalachandaḥsūtra, a work of prosody attributed to Pingala₂ (3rd century BC); also a later text (6th century) by Jayadeva₁. yamātārājabhānasalagām math. [Chandaḥśāstra] mnemonic sūtra representing all the triplets of short and long syllables [gana] (sequence B (2,3) of N. de Bruijn); thus ya 11 is the foot bac chius, mā 111 is the molossus, tā 110 is the antibac chius, rā 101 is the cretic, ja 10 is the amphibrach, bhā 100 is the dactyl, na 0 is the tribrach, and sa 1 is the anapest.
Chandaḥsūtra [sūtra] n. lit. np. of the Chandaḥsūtra, treatise on prosody by Pingala₂.
chandogá [ga₂] m. soc. hymn singer.
chandojñāna [jñāna] n. metric [chandojñāna], one of the 64 arts [kalā].
chandonuśāsana | anuśāsana | n. lit. np. from the Chan donuśāsana, an encyclopedic collection of meters by Hemacandra.
chandobhanga | bhanga | m. phon. non-compliance with meter. chandobhangavat who makes a proso error die.
chandomañjarī [mañjarī] f. phone. n.p. from the Chan domañjarī, a work of prosody by Gaṅgādāsa.
chandomaya [maya] amnf chandomayī consisting of hymns.
chandomāṇikya [māṇikya] n. lit. from the np. chandomāṇikya, a work of prosody by Tathāgatadāsa (11th century).
chandoratnākara [ratnākara] m. lit. du np. chandoratnākara, a work of prosody by Ratnākaraśānti, improving the Chandaḥśāstra of Jayadeva₁.

Jagadīśa₁ [īśa] m. myth. np. of Jagadīśa₁ "Lord of the universe", epith. of Brahmā, Šiva, or Vișnu | hist. np. of Jagadīśa₁, neologism of the 17th century, student of Rāmabhadra₁ Sārvabhauma; we owe him the Tattvacintāmanidīdhitiprakāsikā, also called Jagadīśī, commentary [tīkā] of the Tattva cintāmaṇidīdhiti of Raghunātha₁; we also owe him the Šabdaśaktiprakāśikā and its gloss [vṛtti], and the Tarkāmṛta.

Jagadīśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Jagadīśvara "Lord of the universe", epith. of Shiva, of Indra, or of kings | hist. np. of Jagadīśvara₁ Bhattācārya, to the comic author of the 14th century; cf. Hāsyārṇava.
Jagaduddhāra [uddhāra] m. phil. salvation of the mythic world. np. of Jagaduddhāra "Savior of the World", epith. of Kṛṣṇa or of Shiva.

jagaddala |dala| n. geo. np. of the monastery bd. Ja gaddala, founded in Varendra₁ by King Rāmapāla (11th century); it was destroyed in 1207 by the Muslim invaders; cf. Vidyākara.
jagaddhātṛ [dhātṛ] m. myth. n.p. from jagaddhātṛ, epith. of Viṣṇu “Creator of the World” — f. ja gaddhātrī myth. n.p. of Jagaddhātrī, epith. of His rasvatī “Nurse of the World”.

jagannātha [nātha] m. myth. np. of jagannātha "Master of the universe", epith. of KṛṣṇaViṣṇu; phil. jagannātha is the gaze of God upon the sins of the World; his principal idol, at the shrine of the temple of jagannātha at Purī (Orissa), carved from a nīma tree trunk and painted in black, yellow and red, as an abstraction of the face of Kṛṣṇa, with large round eyes [cakrākṣi]; the idol contains in a cavity a divine substance [brahmapadārtha] which no one can see without risking death, and sacred basil [tulasī] which does not wither; It is placed on a throne [simhāsana] covered with sacred ammonites [śālagrāma], alongside other wooden idols representing Balabhadra, Subhadrā and Sudarśana; jagannātha takes a ritual bath during the festival of snānapūrņimā, and is struck with fever; the idols are then repainted and the shrine is closed; they are then moved for 9 days to their summer residence Gundicā in a procession of three chariots [rathayātrā] which is the object of a great pilgrimage at the beginning of the monsoon, at the āṣāḍha śukla dvitīya; the idol is renewed every 12 or 19 years [navakalevara]; cf. Indradyumna | geo. name of the linga of the double shrine of the temple of Jagannātha₁ | hist. np. of Jagannātha₁ Paṇḍitarāja (1590–1665), illustrious Sanskrit poet, Brahmin of a family of orthodox Vedic tradition originating from Venginādu in Andhra; he was court poet of Emperor Shah Jahan; he was a master of classical rhetoric [alankāra] and a severe literary critic, opposed to metaphorical usage [dhvani]; he wrote the treatises on the aesthetics of poetry Rasagangādhara and Citramīmāmsā, royal eulogies such as the Prāṇābharaṇa, and poems such as the Sudhālaharī; He traveled throughout India, and is credited with praise from the kings of Udai, Delhi, and Assam; he married a Mughal princess by winning a game of chess; after her untimely death, he dedicated his erotic poem Bhāminīvilāsa to her, and committed suicide in the Ganga while reciting the Gangālaharī, washing away the sin of having married a Muslim princess | hist. np. of Jagannātha₁ Miśra, father of Caitanya | hist. np. of the Telugu scholar Jagannātha₁ (early 17th century), theorist of the mystical rasa | hist. np. of the mathematician Samrāt Jagannātha₁ (1652–1744), astronomer to King Jayasimha₆ (18th century); cf. Yan tramandira | du. jagannāthau phil. Viṣṇu and Siva "ruling the Universe together" | ang. juggernaut.

janaká [agt. jan] amnf janikā producer, progenitor — m. father | np. of the Janaka lineage, dynastic title of the kings of Videha | myth. |Rām. | notary paternal of the philosopher King Sīradhvaja Janakarāja, father of Sītā | myth. np. of his ancestor the rājarṣi Mithi Janaka "Progenitor", from the thigh of Nimi; first King of Videha, he gave his name to the dynasty, whose capital Mithilā he founded; Udāvasu is his son | myth. paternal of King Devarāta Janaka — ifc. He who produces, He who engenders; He who causes (iic.) — f. janikā mother.
janakatanayā | tanaya | f. myth. "daughter of Janaka", epith. of Sītā.
janakatā |tā| f. paternity; production.
janakatva [tva] n. productivity; generation.

Janakarāja [rājan] m. hist. np. from the rājarṣi Jana karāja, son of Hrasvaromā, King of Videha, reigning in Mithilā, around the 7th century ante; he was renowned as a disinterested sage; at his court philosophers such as Yājñavalkya and Gārgī disputed doctrines; [Rām.] while plowing the sacrificial ground with his plow, he caused his daughter Sītā to emerge from the furrow; he carries the plow on his standard [Sīradhvaja]; he was the custodian of the Ajagava bow of Shiva, and had promised the hand of Sītā to Whoever could wield it; King Sudhanvā₁ came to attack him to take it, but he killed him and gave his capital Sāṃkāśyā to his younger brother Kuśadhvaja₁; the young Rāma came to Mithilā, accompanied by Viśvāmitra, managed to string the bow and broke it, causing an earthquake; the King then held a great ceremony, where Rāma was united with Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa with his 2nd daughter Urmilā, and their two brothers Bharata₁ and Satrughna with the two daughters Māṇḍavī and Srutakīrti₁ of Kuśadhvaja₁; his chaplain [purohita] was Satānanda; Janakarāja represents the ideal of the Vedic King, imbued with sacrifice; [Bṛhadāraṇyaka] he received the teaching of Yājñavalkya; [AG.] the young sage Astāvakra instructed him on the nature of the Self [ātman]; [BhG.] Kṛṣṇa cited him as a model for his karmayoga; he received a visit from Suka, and lavished his wisdom upon him.
janakīnātha m. hist. np. of the logician Ja nakīnātha Bhaṭṭācārya Cūḍāmaṇi (16th century); he is credited with the Nyāyasiddhāntamañjarī; Rāmabhadra₁ Sārvabhauma is his son.
janatā | Janatā| f. people, people; humanity.
janana [agt. jan] amnf jananī ifc. Who begets, progenitor; Who produces — act. n. birth, existence; production — f. jananī mother.
jananāntara [antara] n. phil. birth or prior existence.
jananīya [pfp. [2] jan] amnf jananīyā to produce.
janam [acc. Jana] iic.

jánamejayá [ejaya] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Ja namejaya "He Who Makes Men Tremble", son of Parīkṣit, King of Hastināpura; to avenge the death of his father, killed by a snake bite, and urged on by the sage Uttanka, he made a great sacrifice of snakes [sarpasattra] and conquered the nāga people of Takṣaśilā; Vyāsa asked Vaiśampāyana to recite the Mah. to him; Candrāpīḍa is his son; cf. Pārikṣita, Sarpasattrī, Jaimini | lit. [KSS.] Janame jaya is said to be the father of Satānīka, King of Kauśāmbī, and of Parapuṣṭā | myth. np. of Janamejaya₁, son of Pūru; he is the 12-generation ancestor of King Dusyanta.
janayitr [agt. ca. jan] m. progenitor; father — f. janayitrī mother.
janas [abstr. jan] n. kind, class (of beings); race | cf. janarloka.
janarloka [loka] m. cf. Janaloka.
jani [agt. jan] f. woman; wife | birth; production.
janitṛ [agt. jan] m. progenitor, father || lat. ge nitor.
janitva [jan] m. du. janitvau [“the two progenitors”] the parents.
janīya [Janaīya] amnf janīyā beneficial for the people.
Janus |abstr. Jan| n. birth; creation, pro
duction | genus, class | lat. genus. januṣā adv. of birth; by nature; essentially; necessarily. pratijanus adv. at each birth.
jantu |jantu| m. being, creature, person.
janma iic. janman.
janmakuṇḍalī | kuṇḍalī | f. astr. birth horoscope.
janmadina | dina | n. birthday of birth.
janmadivasa [divasa] m. birthday.
janmapattra [pattra] n. horoscope.
janmapatrikā | patrikā | f. horoscope.
janmabhāj [bhāj] amnf possessing life — m. living being.
janmabhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. mother tongue.
janmabhūmi [bhūmi] f. place of birth; na tale land, homeland.
janmamṛtyujarā |mṛtyujarā| f. birth, death and old age.
janmamṛtyujarāduḥkha [duḥkha] n. pain of birth, old age and death.
janmāntara | antara | n. phil. each subsequent birth.

janmāṣṭamī [aṣṭamī] f. soc. 8th day of the dark fortnight of the month śrāvaṇa₂, where the birthday of Kṛṣṇa is celebrated; one must observe the fast until midnight, the hour of his birth; syn. gokulāṣṭamī.

jánman [janman] n. birth, origin; existence, life — m. progenitor, father — m. janma ifc. born of (11th century) — f. janmā ifc. born of (11th century) || Pali jamma. janmatas adv. according to birth | according to the stage of life. janmato jāyate śūdrah samskārāddvija ucyate One is śūdra by birth, one is called dvija by the ceremony (of the upanayana). punarjanman n. phil. rebirth, new birth.

janya₁ |pfp. |1| ca. jan| amnf janyā that is born; that comes into existence; born of, produced by (iic.) — m. progenitor; father. janyajanakabhāva gram. relation between parent and child (marked by the g.).

jánya₂ [janaya] amnf janyā of the same country; national | relating to men, coming from the people — m. man of the people | soc. relative or friend of the fiancé | public rumor — n. people, community, nation; people.
√ jap v. [1] pr. (jápati) pft. (jajapa) aor. [5] (ajapīt) pp. (japta) to whisper, murmur (prayers); to recite or pray in a low voice — ca. (jāpayati) to have recited.
japa [act. jap] m. whisper | soc. recitation in a low voice of sacred words — agt. f. japā ifc. who murmurs (at ⟨iic.⟩ loc.).
karnejapah ["who whispers in the ear"] informer.
japamālā |mālā| f. rosary.
japā var. javā f. bio. bot. Hibiscus Rosasinen sis, Red Hibiscus; its flower is offered to Kālī.
japāpuspa [puṣpa] n. flower of the red Hibiscus, rose of China.
jabālā f. lit. [ChU.] np. of jabālā, daughter-mother of Satyakāma; she taught her son that respect for the truth was the best nobility |brāhmaṇya|.
√ jabh₂ v. [1] pr. r. (jabhate) to bite, to snatch; to crunch; to snap | to open the jaw | to bark, to yell.
√ jabh₂ [related to yabh] v. [1] pr. (jabhati) inf. (jabhitum) to have sexual relations.
jabhya [pfp. [1] jabh₂] amnf jabhyā that bites, that crunches — m. granivorous insect — VOC. adr. (impers.) one must open the mouth wide.
√ jam v. [1] pr. (jamati) ppr. (jamat) ppr. in tens. (jājamat) to eat, to have as food.
jamat |ppr. jam| amnf jamantī while eating giant.

jamadagni |agni| m. myth. np. of the ascetic Jama dagni "Devouring Fire", one of the saptarsi, descendant of Bhṛgu; he is the son of R̄cīka and Satya vatī₁, last brāhmaṇa of his lineage as a result of the confusion of castes | varṇasaṃkara | ; his knowledge of the Veda was unsurpassed; ally of Viśvāmitra, he opposed Vasistha; he married Renukā with whom he had 5 sons, Rumaṇvān, Suhotra₁, Vasu₁, Viśvavasu and Paraśurāma; he possessed the Kalmāṣī cow of plenty; Renukā having sinned by watching King Kārtavīrya bathe, he condemned her to wander as a leper; she returned to him after being cured by her devotion to Shiva, but he then ordered his sons to behead her; the elders having disobeyed him, only the youngest Parasurāma left; he cut off King Kārtavīrya's thousand arms and delivered him to death; he was killed in turn by the latter's sons, and avenged by Parasurāma who killed all the princes [kṣatriyās] to return the earth to the Brahmans.
Jamba m. mud; clay.
jambāla [jambaala] mn clay, clay; mud — m. organic. bot. Pandanus odoratissimus, pandana tree; syn. ketaka.
jambīra [jambaīra] m. organic. bot. Citrus li mon, lemon tree — n. organic. lime.

Jambu f. bio. bot. Eugenia jambolana, jamblon tree or jamelonguier; its purple fruits, resembling a small plum, are edible — mn myth. np. of the Jambu, mythical river | divyagangā| from the juice of the fruits of the Jambu crowning Mount Meru — f. jambū myth. the jambū river, id. | fruit of the jamblon; Ganesha is fond of it.

Jambudvīpa [dvīpa] m. myth. n.p. Jambudvīpa, the most central of the 7 mythical continents surrounding Mount Meru, surrounded by the Lāvaṇa ocean; it is itself subdivided into 10 regions [dvīpa]: kuru, candra, varuņa, saumya, nāga, kumārikā, gabhas timat, tāmraparņa, kaśeru, Indra | geo. greater India, the Indian subcontinent.
jambūnadī | nadī | f. myth. n.p. of the jambū river. ज দ্ৰুক jambuka m. organic. zoo. jackal — f. organic jambukā. female jackal.

jambukeśvara |īśvara| m. geo. np. of Jam bukeśvara, sanctuary of Šiva located in Tiruvanaikka near Srīranga, on an island of the Kāverī; it is the pañcabhūtasthala associated with the water element |ap|; a natural spring waters it.

jámbha [agt. jabh₁] m. tooth, tusk | pl. jambhās jaws | jambhá myth. demon devourer myth. n.p. of the asura jambha, desecrator of his sacrifices; at the head of the anti-gods, he stole the amrta from Dhanvantari; |Mah.| n.p. many asurās, killed by Indra, Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna.
jámbhaka |agt. jabh₁| amnf jambhakā that destroys, that devours | myth. evil spirit animating magical weapons.
jámbhana₁ |agt. jabh₁| amnf jamb hanī who destroys, who devours — m. organic. bot. Ca lotropis gigantea, milkweed shrub, with milky juice, woolly leaves; medicinal plant; cf. śivapuspaka.
jámbhana₁ [act. jabh₂] n. copulation.
jámbhala [jambhala] m. bd. np. of the yakṣa Jambhala, god of wealth or king of the North (equivalent bd. of Kubera or his commander-in-chief); his wife is Hārītī; cf. Vaiśravaṇa.

jaya [act. ji] m. victory, Conquest — agt. m. Conqueror, victor | myth. [Mah.] np. of jaya, epith. of Arjuna "the Victorious" | myth. [Mah.] name assumed by Yudhişthira during the exile of the Pāndavās in the kingdom of Virāta; Arjuna was Vi jaya, Bhīma was Jayanta, Nakula was Jayatsena, Sahadeva was Jayadbala, and Draupadī called them all jaya | myth. np. of jaya₁, one of the two dvārapālau of Viṣṇu | lit. np. of jaya₂ "victory (of dharma over adharma)", epic poem of 8800 verses, attributed to Vyāsa; It became the Bhārata₁ of 24,000 verses, recited by Vaisampāyana, then finally the Mah. (100,000 verses) | astr. np. of jaya₃ "Conqueror", personifying the 28th year of a life cycle [saṃvatsara] — ins. m. means of obtaining victory — f. cf. jayā — f. jayā ifc. Victorious over, who conquers (2nd century). jáyo'svah victory horse.

jayátīrtha [tīrtha] m. hist. np. of the philosopher śrī Jayatīrtha, born near Pandharpur (1343–~1388), disciple of Akşobhyatīrtha, and his successor as pontiff of the Madhva order; he was vigorous and rode a horse; he was the master commentator [tīkācārya] of the dvaita doctrine; he is the author not. of the Nyāyasudhā, the Tattvaprakāśikā, the Prameyadīpikā, the Pramāṇapaddhati and the Rgbhāsyatīkā.
jayadatta | datta | m. myth. np. of jayadatta, son of Indra, presumed author of a text on economics
litique [arthaśāstra].

jayádeva [deva] m. hist. np. of Jayadeva₁ "god of victory", poet of Orissa (~1150~1210); he lived at the court of King Laksmanasena of Bengal; he is the author of the Gītagovinda | hist. np. of the Jain Jayadeva₁ (6th century), author of a work on prosody; cf. Chandaḥśāstra | hist. np. of Jayadeva₁ Pakṣadhara, famous logician of Mithilā (15th century) | hist. np. of the poet and logician Jayadeva₁ Pīyuṣavarṣa, author of the Prasannarāghava and the Candrāloka.
jayádhvaja [dhvaja] m. myth. np. of King Jayadh vaja "Banner of Victory", eldest son of Kārtavīrya; Tālajangha is his son.
jayapatākā [patākā] f. victory banner.
jayápattra | pattra | n. soc. royal edict; edict of a court declaring the victory of a party | soc. sign attached to the forehead of a horse chosen for the aśvamedha.
jayapura | pura | n. geo. np. of the city of jaya pura in Rājasthāna, founded by King Jayasimha₆ in 1727 to serve as his capital (mod. Jaipur).

jayámangala | mangala | m. royal elephant | (mus.) kind of measure — f. Jayamangalā lit. np. of the Jayamangalā, commentary on the Kāmasūtra by Yaśodhara₁. jayayakşa [yakşa] m. hist. np. of Jayayakşa Malla, king of Nepal (1428–1482); he fortified the city of Bhaktapura and built the temple of Pasupatinātha, as well as the royal palace with 55 carved wooden windows; he divided his kingdom between his sons; Rāya Malla became king of Bhaktapura, Ratna Malla became king of Kāntipura.
jayaratha | ratha | m. hist. np. of Rājānaka Jaya ratha, scholar of Kaśmīra under Rājadeva (early 13th century), brother of jayadratha₂; we owe him not the Tantrālokaviveka and the Vimarśinī₂.
Jayarāśi | rāśi | m. hist. np. of Jayarāśi Bhaṭṭa, skeptical philosopher of the early 9th century (South India); he is credited with the Tattvopaplavasimha.

jayávarman | varman | m. hist. np. of Jayavarmā "Protector of victory", name of kings not. at Angkor; Jayavarmā₁ (650) was king of Zhenla; Jayavarmā₂ (802) was king at Angkor, as was his son Jayavarmā₃ (835); Jayavarmā₄ (928) reigned at Lingapura (mod. Koh Ker); there he built the Pra sat Thom, temple of Shiva and Yama; Jayavarmā₈ (1280), Buddhist, reigned at Angkor Thom; he built the Bayon temple with face towers.

jayáśrī |śrī| f. goddess of victory. jayásimha simha m. hist. np. of Prince Jayasimha "Victorious Lion"; he created the Calukya dynasty of the Deccan in the 5th century; its capital was Aryapura (modern Aihole) | hist. np. of King Jayasimha₁, of the Eastern Calukya dynasty; he reigned from 641 to 673 | hist. np. of King Jayasimha₂, of the Eastern Calukya dynasty; he reigned from 706 to 718 | hist. np. of King Jayasimha₃, of the Western Calukya dynasty; he reigned from 1015 to 1042; his son Someśvara₁ succeeded him | hist. n.p. of king Jayasimha₄ Siddharāja, of the Cau lukya dynasty; he reigned in the 12th century at Anahilapātaka in Gurjara; Hemacandra Sūri worked at his court; he made an expedition to Avantī in 1140; when he died in 1143, he was succeeded by his nephew Kumārapāla | hist. n.p. of Jayasimha₅ (Jai Singh I), King of Amber, general of Shah Jahan (1611–1667) | hist. n.p. of the mahārāja of Amber Jayasimha₆ (Jai Singh II, [16881743]), descendant of Jayasiṃha₃; son of Maharaja Bishan Singh, he ascended the throne at age 11 in 1699, and obtained the title of Savai (best of 1/4) of Aurangzeb; he founded a new capital in 1727 at Jayapura (modern Jaipur); he was keen on mathematics, and built several observatories, first at Uj Jayini (1719), then at Delhi (1724), then at Jayapura the Yantramandira (1728) for his astronomer Samrat Jagannatha₄ | hist. np. of the king of Kashmira Jayasimha₇ of the Lohara dynasty (1128–1149); he was the last great Hindu king of Kashmira.
jayasimhakalpadruma [kalpadruma] lit. mr. n.p. from jayasimhakalpadruma, the dharmaśāstra work of Ratnākara₃.
Jayāditya |āditya| m. hist. np. of the grammarian Jayāditya, first author of the Kāśikā vṛtti (7th century).
Jayānanda | ananda | m. hist. np. of Jayānanda, scholar of Kaśmīra (12th century); he is the author of a commentary | bhāsya | of the Madhyamakāvatāra of Candrakīrti.

jayāpīḍa |āpīḍa| m. hist. np. of the king of Kaśmīra jayāpīḍa "Crowned by Victory" (reign 776–807); he was the grandson of Lalitāditya, whom he succeeded; he patronized the arts and sciences, and was an expert in Sanskrit grammar; he was given the title of pandita; he founded a school of literary criticism at his court, headed by Udbhața; the poet Dāmodaragupta was his minister; cf. Rājataramginī.
jayat [ppr. ji] amnf jayantī conqueror, victor.
Jayatsena [senā] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Jayatsena "to the victorious army", the name of Nakula's exile in the kingdom of Virāta.
jayadbala [bala] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Jayad bala "Force of victory", name of Sahadeva's exile in the kingdom of Virāţa.

jayadratha [ratha] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of jayadratha "of the victorious chariot", king of Sindhu [Saindhava], chief of the sauvīrās; he is the son of the old sage Vrddhaksatra, who had made the prophecy at his birth that whoever put his head on the ground would have his skull burst into 100 pieces; he attended the svayamvara of Draupadī without being chosen, and swore a hatred for Arjuna; when the Pāṇḍavās went into exile, crossing the Kāmyaka forest they went hunting, leaving Draupadī alone in a hut; jayadratha abducted her, with the help of his brother Balāhaka₃; He was overtaken by the Pāndavās who tore his army to pieces, and he was shorn by Bhīma; he was released on the orders of Yudhiṣṭhira; he did penance at Gangādvāra, and Śiva granted him the power to see all pāndavas, except Arjuna, defeated in battle; during the great battle he allied himself with the Kauravās, having married Duḥśalā, the only daughter of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; he won many battles; on the 14th day of the battle he treacherously lured Abhimanyu into a cakravyūha trap to kill him; Arjuna swore that he would kill him the next day to avenge his son; Krishna taught the latter the prophecy of Vddhakshatra; then he simulated a sunset by creating an eclipse with his chakra, in order to deceive Jayadratha's guards; Arjuna cut off his head with an arrow that made it fall onto his father's knees in meditation; the latter awoke and rose, saw his son's severed head rolling to the ground, and his skull exploded, fulfilling his own prophecy | myth. np. of King Jayadratha, son of Bhatkaya, descendant of Hasti | hist. np. of Jayadratha, philosopher of Kashmira in the 13th century under Rajadeva; he bore the titles Rajanaka and Mahāmāheśvara; he is the author of the Haracaritacintāmaṇi; cf. Jayaratha.
jayadrathayāmala [yāmala] n. lit. np. of the jaya drathayāmala, a work of Kaula tradition (10th century).

jayanta |jayat| amnf jayantī Victorious — m. myth. np. of jayanta "the Victorious", son of Indra; he attacked Sītā in the form of a beautiful horn, and Rāma gouged out one of his eyes | myth. [Mah.] name of exile of Bhīma in the kingdom of Virāṭa | hist. np. of jayanta₁ Bhatta, grammarian of Kaśmīra (late 9th century); he bases the semantics of the sentence on the
logic [Nyāya]; we owe him not. the Nyāyamañjarī and the Nyāyakalikā, as well as the satirical play Agamadambara | epith. of many gods and kings — f. cf. jayantī.
jayantī [f. jayanta] f. myth. np. of jayantī, daughter of Indra, wife of Sukra | soc. anniversary festival (not. of Kṛṣṇa [janmāṣṭamī], of Ha
numān [caitrī], from Buddha [vaiśākhī], from Bhai
rava [bhairavāṣṭamī], from Dattātreya [āgrahāyanī], from Madhva | vijayadaśamī|).
jayantīkalpa |kalpa| m. lit. np. of the jayantīkalpa, giving the ritual of the festival of Kṛṣṇa | janmāṣṭamī|, due to Madhvācārya.

Jayā₁ [f. jaya] f. myth. np. of Jayā₁, daughter of Dakṣa; she married Kṛśāśva, by whom she had 50 very powerful sons, destined to serve as magical weapons to fight the asurās lit. [KSS.] np. of Jayā₁, cham bellan of Pārvatī, wife of the gaṇa Puspadanta₃.
jayin [agt. ji] amnf jayinī who conquers — m. conqueror; victor — ifc. who overcomes (iic.); who wins (a lawsuit, in games, in sports, etc.).
jayiṣṇu [agt. ji] amnf Victorious.
jayya [pfp. [1] ji] amnf jayyā which can be defeated.
jára [agt. jr] amnf jarā Old, aged; which ages — act. m. aging, wear — f. cf. jarā.
jaraņá var. jīraņa [agt. jr] amnf jaraņā Old, worn | that dissolves, that aids digestion — act. n. maturation — mn cumin seeds; di verses spices.

járat [ppr. jr̩] amnf jaratī Old, worn, decrepit; infirm | outdated; ancient, out of service (temple); dry (grass) — m. old man | gr. γεροντος; fr. géronte. jarannaiyāyikah m. phil. ["Old ratiocina teur" (pej.) adept of traditional logic |prācīnanyāya|. jaranmīmāṃsaka m. phil. | "Old casuist" | (pej.) adept of the doctrine of traditional ritual |pūrvamīmāṃsā|.

jaratkāru [kāru₁] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the ascetic jaratkāru "who saves his ancestors"; he lived as a wandering brahmacārin [yāyāvara]; during a pilgrimage, he saw his ancestors hanging from the top of an abyss by a rope gnawed by a rat, for lack of offspring; he then decided to marry Ma nasā, sister of the dragon [nāga] Vāsuki, who conceived Astika.
jaradgava [gava] m. Old bovine | lit. [Hit.] np. of the vulture jaradgava — f. jaradgavī Old cow.
jarás [agt. jr] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of jarā₂ "the Old Man", hunter who mistook Kṛṣṇa for a deer and fatally struck him in the heel, the only vulnerable spot on his body; cf. Sāmba.

jarā [act. jr] f. old age | bd. decrepitude, 12th cause of suffering [pratītyasamutpāda] | myth. [Mah.] np. of the rākṣasī jarā₁ "the Old Woman"; she gathered the half-abortions of Brhadratha and fused them into jarāsandha; she was killed with her offspring by the magic club of jarāsandha deflected by Baladeva armed with the weapon sthūṇākarṇa.
jarāyu [āyus] amnf that has run its course, perishable — n. snake molt | placenta.

jarāyujá |ja| amnf jarāyujā viviparous; syn. yonija. jarāsaṃdha var. jarāsandha |saṃdhā₂| m. myth. [Mah.] np. of jarāsandha "United by jarā₁", son of Brhadratha and his two twin queens, monster obtained by fusion of two half-abortions by jarā₁; he was invincible in battle; he became king of Ma gadha, his capital was Girivraja; he married his daughters Asti and Prāpti to King Kaṃsa, and fought 18 times Kṛṣṇa who had killed his son-in-law; he imprisoned many kings with a view to sacrificing them; he challenged Karna to a duel, but conceded their equality in combat; Krishna came to his court with Arjuna and Bhima, all three disguised as snataka brahmins; they challenged Jarasandha, who chose to fight Bhima; the duel lasted 14 days; finally, Krishna advised Bhima to separate Jarasandha into his two halves in order to kill him; his son and heir Sahadeva pledged allegiance to Krishna and ascended the throne. [Myth. [Mah.] Name of a son of Dhtarastra.
jarita [pp. ca. jṛ] amnf Jaritā aged, decrepit; spoiled, rotten — f. cf. Jaritā.
Jaritā [f. jarita] f. myth. [Mah.] np. of the oi bucket female wasp-eater [śārṅgikā] Jaritā; impregnated by the sage Mandapāla in order to ensure his salvation, she gave birth to the four śārngakās.
Jaritāri [ari] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Jaritāri, eldest of the śārngakās.

jarjara [red. jara] amnf jarjarā decrepit, infirm, damaged; broken, twisted, pierced | torn to pieces; divided (kingdom) — m. soc. bamboo cane of 5 segments symbolically representing the banner of Indra [indradhvaja] during a theatrical performance; cf. pūrvaranga. jarjarīkṛ to tear to pieces. jarjarībhū to deteriorate, to wear out.
jarjaratva [tva] n. decrepitude.
jarjarapūjā [pūjā] f. soc. [theatre] homage to the banner of Indra.

[KSS.] np of the hideous brahmin jīvadatta "by Whom life is given", claimant of Anangarati; he knows how to resurrect the dead by invoking Cāmuṇḍā; he is in fact the gaṇa Vikatavadana, cursed by the hermit Kapilajata; he obtained a magic sword which allowed him to conquer Anangaprabhā, but upon returning to Earth it left him.

Jaimini m. myth. Patr. of the sage [ṛṣi] Jai mini, disciple of Vyāsa, priest-chanter [udgātr] at the sacrifice of snakes [sarpasattra] of Janamejaya; he is said to be the founder of the pūrvamīmāṃsā doctrine; the Mārkaṇḍeya purāṇa was said to have been transmitted to him by four wise birds; he is the author of a treatise on domestic rites |gṛhasūtra|; and of the Pūrvamīmāmsāśāstra; it is said that he died trampled by wild elephants.

jaivali m. lit. [ChU.] np. of King Jaivali; he questioned the young Svetaketu on 5 metaphysical questions to which he could not answer; his father Uddālaka asked the king to instruct them, and he explained to them the doctrine of the 5 fires: the gods offer devotion in the fire of Heaven to obtain the Moon; then the Moon in the fire of the clouds, to obtain rain; then rain in the fire of Earth, to obtain food; then food in the fire of man, to obtain sperm; finally sperm in the fire of woman, to obtain the embryo.
joda ifc. m. menton.

[Sāṃkhya] the Thinking Mind Puruṣa | myth. np. of Jña, epith. of Budha "who has knowledge".
