takrakauṇḍinyanyāya | nyāya | m. gram. maxim of the exception to a general rule, by analogy to the kaundinya brahmins, who are entitled to whey rather than cream.
√ takṣ v. [1] pr. (takṣati) pp. (taṣṭa) to cut (with an axe), to carve, to split; to shape.
takṣa iic. takṣan.

takṣaśilā [śilā] f. geo. np. of takṣaśilā "City of stonemasons", capital of eastern Gandhāra, center of medical and Buddhist teaching until the 2nd century; Emperor Ashoka studied there; its name was corrupted to takṣilā or Taxila by the Greeks and became Takkasilā in pāli; the City was destroyed by the Huns | var. takṣilā id.
takṣaká [agt. takṣ] m. carpenter | myth. [Rām.] np. of Takṣaka "Slayer", dragon king [nāga] brother of Seṣa, ally of Rāvaṇa | myth. np. of the cobra surrounding the arm of Siva.
takṣakacūdāratnālamkāra [cūdāratnaalamkāra] m. myth. jewel adorning Takṣaka’s diadem.
takṣaṇa [agt. takṣa] m. that cuts, that cuts; )8 chisel | math. divider — act. n. cutting, carving, shaping.
takṣan [agt. takṣ] m. woodcutter, carpenter myth. np. of Takṣā "carpenter", eldest son of Bharata₁ — iic. cf. takṣa.
tagara mn bio. bot. Valeriana jatamansi, herbaceous plant from the Himalayas; its root has many medicinal properties.
tac iic. tad.
tacca [ca] adv. and this.
tacchīla |śīla| amnf tacchīlā having this habit; of this nature.

√ ta ~nc [reli 'ea tak] v. [7] pr. (tan₁ 'akti) pf. (a) (av. ā) to contract, reduce; to coagulate. ਰਟ tața m. bank, shore, bank; declivity, slope, ta lus | edge, side (not. of the body) — f. taṭī ifc. id.
tatastha [stha] amnf taṭasthā who stands on the bank or shore | ["who does not get involved"] indifferent person.
√ taq v. ca. (tāqayati) pp. (tāqita) abs. (tāḍayitvā) pf. (pari, vi) to hit, to strike, to beat; to winnow; to punish | to hit (in a ball); to beat (the drum) — ps. (tāḍyate) to be beaten, to be hit.
taḍāka mn cf. taḍāga.
taḍāga var. taḍāka mn mare, étang, Réservoir.
tadāgādividhi [ādividhi] f. ved. np. of the Tadāgādividhi, dealing with the ritual of consecration of basins and ponds, appendix | parisista | of the Atharvaveda.
tadít [agt. tad] f. lightning, thunderbolt.
Taṇḍu |taḍ| m. myth. np. of Taṇḍu "Drummer", guard of Shiva, who taught him the art of mime and dance; he in turn taught it to Bharata₃.

taṇḍulá [taḍ] m. grain rice (winnowed); grain of rice; opp. cooked rice [odana] | unit of weight, not. of gems; it is worth 8 mustard seeds [sarṣapa] | pl. taṇḍulās rice to be cooked. taṇḍulān pacati he cooks rice.
tandulákana [kaṇa] m. grain of rice.
taṇḍulakusumavali [kusumavali] f. stripes made with flowers and grains of rice, not. to decorate temples and the thresholds of houses.
taṇḍulakusumavalivikāra [vikāra] m. art of decorating with flowers and grains of rice, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.
taṇḍulavaicārika [vaicārika] n. med. np. of the Taṇḍulavaicārika (pkt. Tandulaveyālika), small 4( Jain medical treatise, part of the Prakīrņaka, dealing not. with embryology.
tat iic. tad.
tatkara | kara₁ | amnf tatkarā who does this.
tatkāla [kāla₁] amnf tatkālā at that time; just; immediately, simultaneously. tatkālakṛṣṭa which has just been plowed.
tatkriya | kriyā| amnf tatkriyā cf. tatkara.
tatpara [para] amnf tatparā who follows him; who takes him as his goal; who is totally devoted to him | who devotes himself to (loc. iic.) — ifc. adept of (iic.).
tatparatā |tā| f. intention; goal; tendency devotion, addiction (reverse loc. ).
tatparatva |tva| n. id.

tatpurusa [purusa] m. his servant | gram. determinative compound word (like the word tatpurusa); the 2nd term is determined by the 1st, by a case relation or by an attributive relation in the case of a descriptive compound [karmadhāraya] | phil. the supreme Spirit | phil. [śaivasiddhānta] np. of tatpurușa, face of majesty of Sadāśiva Mahādeva, turned towards the East, associated with the world of
peace [śānti], to the element of air and to the color gold.
tatpūrva [pūrva] amnf tatpūrvā which arrives for the first time. tatpūrvam thus for the first time.
tatprakāra | prakāra | amnf tatprakārā of this kind. tatprakāraka id. tatprakārakaśabdabodhe śaktijñānasya hetutvam Knowledge of meaning is the reason for understanding sentences.
tatprakṛta [prakṛta] amnf tatprakṛtā makes of this.
tatpratikāra [pratikāra] mn preventive measure.
tatprathamá [prathama] amnf tatprathamā who does this for the first time. tatprathamam cf. tatpūrvam.
tatphala [phala] amnf tatphalā who has this result; who obtains this fruit or this reward.
tatsad [sad₂] amnf sitting there.
tatsama [sama] amnf tatsamā similar; like him; as is — m. word assimilated to Sanskrit, sanskritization | word borrowed as is from Sanskrit; cf. tadbhava.
tatstha |stha| amnf tatsthā gram. which remains there (said of a quality [guna] presented as distinct from its object, as gandha).
tata₁ [pp. tan₁] amnf tatā extended, stretched, )9 stretched (bow); spread out | accomplished (sacrifice) — n. stringed instrument.
tatá₂ m. ved. father, dad — voc. adr. little father, my little one, my darling, son.

tátas |adv. tad| adv. substitute for the abl. of tad or another pronoun | |correl. of yatas| from here, from here | then, after; henceforth | therefore, thus, consequently, that is why, it follows that. itas tataḥ adv. here and there, in such and such a circumstance. tátas tatah adv. here and there, on one side and the other; from all sides; everywhere | and what follows | lit. (theater) what happens then? yatas ... tatas ... as ... it follows that ... tátah katham but how is it that? tátah kṣaṇam var. tátah kṣaṇāt immediately after. tátah páram var. tátah paścāt moreover | on this; nextly. tátah pára moreover. tátah prabhṛti from then on; from there. tato'nyatas var. tato'nyatra in another place. tato'param then; on another occasion. tasmai deyam tato grāhyam Offerings must be made to him, his gifts may be accepted.
táti [related to tad] conj. [correl. of yati₁] as much — f. crowd, quantity.

tattva [tadtva] n. reality, truth | essence, essential principle | phil. [Sāṃkhya] primary element or substance; there are 24 or 25 of them: the original Nature prakṛti, and its 23 transformations [vikāra] manifesting creation [sarga]: the 3 psychic senses or intellectual functions composing the inner instrument [antaḥkaraṇa] (buddhi, ahaṃkāra, manas, to which Vedānta adds citta at the beginning), the 10 faculties of perception and action [indriya], the 5 subtle elements [tanmātra], and the 5 elements

gross [bhūta]; this evolution [pariṇāma] of the tattvāni occurs under the influence of the Purușa | phil. [Abhinavagupta] category of existence; there are 36 of them: the 5 gross elements [mahābhūta]; the 5 subtle elements [tanmātra], the 10 faculties of perception and action [indriya], the 3 intellectual functions buddhi, manas, ahamkāra, Nature prakṛti, the Cosmic Person puruṣa, Illusion māyā accompanied by its 5 armors [kañcuka], Pure Knowledge śuddhavidyā, the Lord Iśvara, the Eternal Sadāśiva, Anāśritaśiva and his Sakti math. symb. the number 25 | var. tatva id. tattvam phil. [Vedānta] "you are that" (mahāvākya). tattvena adv. in truth, precisely, exactly. tattvatas adv. id.

tattvakaustubha | kaustubha | n. lit. np. from the Tatt vakaustubha, a philosophical work by Bhattoji Dīkṣita; in it he criticizes the Vedānta school of Madhva. tattvacintāmaņi [cintāmaņi] m. lit. np. from the Tatt vacintāmaņi "Jewel of Truth", a foundational work of the Mithilā [Navyanyāya] school of logic, a monumental work by Gangesa (14th century); in it he expounds the theory of the 4 means of knowledge [pramāṇa], and proposes 5 definitions [pañcalakṣaṇī] of inevitable concomitance [vyāpti]; in the īśvaravāda section he demonstrates the existence of God; This text is also called Pramācintāmaņi and Manigrantha; it comprises 4 books [khanda], named Pratyakṣa, Anumāna, Upamāna and Sabda.

tattvacintāmaṇidīdhiti [dīdhiti] f. lit. np. of the tattvacintāmaṇidīdhiti, commentary on the Tatt vacintāmani, principal work of Raghunātha₁ Siromani; Jagadīśa₁ made the commentary tattva cintāmaṇidīdhitiprakāśikā; cf. Jāgadīśī.
tattvacintāmaniprakāśa [prakāśa] m. bed. n.p. of the Tattvacintāmaņiprakāśa, commentary by Vard hamāna₁ of his father's Tattvacintāmaṇi.

tattvacintāmanimayūkha [mayūkha] m. lit. np. of the Tattvacintāmaņimayūkha "Axis of the Jewel of Truth", commentary on the Tattvacintāmaņi by Samkara₂ Miśra. tattvacintāmaņirahasya [rahasya] n. lit. np. of the Tattvacintāmaņirahasya "Secret of the tattva cintāmaņi", work by Navyanyāya of the logician
Mathurānātha₁ [Māthurī].

tattvajñāna [jñāna] n. phil. knowledge of essential principles; true knowledge of reality, syn. samyagdarśana. tattvațīkā [tīkā] f. lit. np. of the Tattvatīkā, commentary on the Srībhāsya of Rāmānuja due to Vedāntadeśika.
tattvatā [tā] f. truth; reality.
tattvadīpikā [dīpikā] f. bed. n.p. of the tattvadīpikā of Baladeva₁ Vidyābhūṣaṇa.

tattvanirnaya [nirnaya] m. lit. from the np. Tattvanirnaya of Madhu; cf. Tattvasankhyāna. tattvaprakāśa prakāśa m. lit. np. from the tattva prakāśa "Lights on Reality", phil. at work attributed to King Bhojadeva.
tattvaprakāśikā [prakāśikā] f. lit. np. of the Tatt vaprakāśikā "Lights on Reality", commentary on the Brahmasūtra bhāsya of Madhvācārya, by Jayatīrtha. .0
tattvabindu [bindu] m. lit. np. du tattvabindu "Drop of truth", psycholinguistic treatise on the perception of the meaning of a verbal utterance, due to Vācaspati₁ Miśra (9th century).
tattvabubhutsu [bubhutsu] amnf who seeks the truth.

Tattvabodha [bodha] m. knowledge of the truth lit. np. of the Tattvabodha, an introductory work to Vedānta attributed to Sankarācārya. vāde vāde jāyate tattvabodhaḥ through debate, the knowledge of the truth triumphs.
tattvabodhinī [bodhinī] f. lit. np. of the Tattvabod hinī "Revelation of the principles of grammar", commentary on the Siddhāntakaumudī for the use of beginners, due to Jñānendra Sarasvatī₂.
tattvamīmāṃsā [mīmāṃsā] f. bed. n.p. of the Tatt vamīmāmsā “Investigation of the truth”, sāmkhya treatise due to DurbalācāryaKṛṣṇamitrācārya.
Tattvamuktāvalī [muktāvalī] f. lit. np. of the Tattvamuktāvalī "Pearls of Truth", work of Madhvācārya refuting the māyāvāda doctrine.
tattvaratnāvalī [ratnāvalī] f. lit. np. of the Tatt varatnāvalī of Maitrīpa, incorporating tantric rites into the bd. Mahāyāna doctrine.
tattvavat [vat] amnf tattvavatī which possesses this nature.
tattvavāda [vāda] m. phil. "realism", doctrine of
dualism | dvaita | of Madhvācārya.
tattvavādin [in] amnf tattvavādinī phil. holding the doctrine of dualism |dvaita| of Madhvācārya; opp. māyāvādin .
tattvavid | vid₃ | amnf who knows the nature of g. .

tattvaviveka | viveka | m. phil. | Vedānta | "discernment of reality", monistic doctrine |advaita| teaching that only Atmā is real. ātmā satyastadanyat sarvamithyeti [Śaṅkara₁] Atmā exists, all else is illusion.
tattvavaiśāradī [vaiśāradī] f. bed. n.p. of the Tattva vaiśāradī, commentary on the Pātañjalayogaśāstra due to Vācaspati₁ Miśra.
tattvasankhyāna [sankhyāna] n. lit. np. from the Tatt vasankhyāna, a philosophical manifesto by Madhva giving his views on Vedānta; he insists on 5
fundamental dualities [dvaita], from which his system derives its name; he is also called Tattvanirnaya.

tattvasamgraha [samgraha] m. lit. np. from the tattvasamgraha "Compendium of true principles", philosophical encyclopedia in verse by Sāntarakṣita; it marks the phenomenological turn of bd epistemology.
Tattvasamgrahapañjikā [Pañjikā] f. lit. np. of the Tattvasamgrahapañjikā or Pañjikā, analytical commentary on the tattvasamgraha by Kamalaśīla.
tattvasamāsa [samāsa] m. lit. np. from the Tattva samāsa, manual of sāmkhya philosophy, attributed to Kapila; it is prior to 1600.
tattvasamīkṣā [samīkṣā] f. lit. np. of the Tattva samīkṣā, commentary by Vācaspati₁ of the Brah masiddhi.
tattvānyatva [anyatva] n. of. of such and such a kind. tattvānyatvābhyām anirvacanīya which it is vain to try to specify.
tattvābhiniveśa [abhiniveśa] m. phil. impregnation with the meaning of teaching.
tattvābhiniveśin [abhiniveśin] amnf tattvābhiniveśinī lit. (aesthete) who focuses on the essence of things.
tattvārtha [artha] m. veracity | relevance.
tattvārthadīpa [dīpa] m. lit. np. du tattvārthadīpa nibandha, text of teaching of the śuddhādvaita doctrine and explanation of the Srīmadbhāgavata due to Vallabhācārya.
Tattvārthasūtra [sūtra] n. bed. n.p. of the Tattvārthasūtra, the founding work of Umāsvāmī Jainism; cf. tattvārthādhigamasūtra.
tattvārthādhigama [adhigama] m. jn. relevant knowledge of reality.

tattvārthādhigamasūtra [sūtra] n. jn. np. of the tattvārthādhigamasūtra, work of Umāsvāmī expounding the Jain doctrine; also called Tattvārthasūtra, it is accompanied by its gloss, the Tattvārthādhigamabhāsya.

tattvopaplavasimha [upaplavasimha] m. lit. np. from tattvopaplavasimha "Overturning of all principles", rationalist philosophical work of Jayarāśi Bhaṭṭa (circa 800); it refines the materialism of Cārvāka by justifying atheism through epistemology.

tátra [tadtra] adv. [correl. from yatra] here, there; in this, in this | towards there — (at the beginning of the sentence) among these, one of them — iic. (av. pp.) (ifc.) there. tatra kāle adv. at that moment. tatraiva adv. right here. yatra tatra adv. anywhere. tatra tatra adv. here and there; everywhere. tatrabhuktam consumed there. atra dhūmastatra vahniḥ No smoke without fire. .1
tatratya [ya] amnf tatratyā which is here, which is there.
tatrabhavat | bhavat₂ | mr. adr. Sir (not present, polite form of he) | phil. n.p. of Ta trabhavān "Sir", respectful designation of Bhartrhari by Abhinavagupta — f. tatrabhavatī Madam.
tatraloka |loka| m. the other world.
tatva cf. tattva.

táthā |tadthā| adv. |correl. of yathā| thus, in this way; also, likewise | (part of assent) yes, certainly; agreed; so be it! — iic. of such ...; thus ... tathā bhavatu so be it. tathāstu let it be so. tathā kuru do thus. tathetyuktvā approvingly.
tathākāram [kāra] adv. thus (correl. of yathākāram).
tathākṛta |kṛta| amnf tathākṛtā thus done.
tathāgata [gata] amnf tathāgatā of this nature; arrived in this way — m. bd. epith. of Buddha "thus come" (came like his predecessors).
tathāgatagarbha [garbha] m. bd. Mahāyāna doctrine which postulates that every being is a Bud dha in germ; cf. Ratnagotravibhāga.
Tathāgatabhadra [bhadra] m. bd. n.p. of Tathāgatabhadra, student of Nāgārjuna.
tathāca [ca] adv. even so.
tathātā |tā| f. bd. true nature of things; absolute reality.
tathātva |tva| n. id.
tathātvadārḍhya [dārḍhya] n. phil. [Trika] (stability of reality) light of universal consciousness; cf. spanda.

tathāpi [api] adv. nevertheless, however | [correl. of yadyapi| although ... yet ... yadyapi ayam bahu prayāsam kṛtavān tathāpi parīkṣāyām anuttīrṇaḥ although he made a lot of effort, he failed the exam.
táthābhāva [bhāva] m. the fact being | the fact of being of such a nature; the true nature; the accomplishment.
táthābhāvin |bhāvin| amnf tathābhāvinī when entering such a state.
táthābhūta [bhūta] amnf tathābhūtā of such a nature, of such an essence, of such a nature; having such qualities.
táthāmukha | mukha | amnf tathāmukhī thus oriented | looking in the same direction.
táthārūpa |rūpa| amnf tathārūpā of such form; appearing thus.
táthārūpin [rūpin] amnf tathārūpinī id.
táthāvidha | vidhā₂ | amnf tathāvidhā in such a way; in such a condition; of such quality. tathāvidham in this manner; likewise.
tatheti | iti | adv. that's good, understood, agreed. bhavatu tatheti sa pratyuvāca he replied "very well".
tathaiva | eva | adv. also, likewise; in the same way, exactly likewise. tathaiva ca adv. and likewise; similarly.
tathya |tadya| amnf tathyā | "who is so true, real; truthful — n. truth, reality. tathyena adv. in truth; really, in fact, for real.

tad var. tac, tat, tan pn. 3rd pers. nm sa₂ f. sā₂ |sg. nom. acc. tat, i. tena, dat. tasmai, abl. tasmāt, g. tasya, loc. tasmin; du. nom. acc. te, i. dat. abl. tābhyām, g. loc. tayos; pl. nom. acc. tāni, i. tais, dat. abl. tebhyas, g. teṣām, loc. teṣul it, this, that, that | correl. of yad (he who ...) it | therefore; for this reason; then, in this, it is that. tad etad adv. that very thing. tat tad this and that; such and such; different, varied; respective | phil. [Nyāya] this (ifc.) precisely. tam tam deśam jagāma he went here and there. yat tad whatever, whichever; all. yad vā tad vā this or that, whichever | so much and so much. yadvā tadvā vṛṣṭhiḥ a driving rain. tad yathā adv. notably, as follows. tadapi adv. nevertheless, however.
tadvat |correl. yadvat| conj. thus; like that. tat tvam asi phil. [ChU.] "You are that", mahākāvya summarizing the Advaita doctrine.

tadanantara | anantara | amnf tadanantarā very close to (g.); adjacent, contiguous; which immediately follows. tadanantaram adv. right after, following which, thereupon; it is then that, in the meantime.
tadanya | anya| amnf tadanyā other than that.

tadartha [artha] amnf tadarthā for this use, of such use; proper to this, which serves this purpose; intentional gram. in this sense; with the same meaning — m. this use; this sense. tadartham adv. for this reason; with a view to this object; consequently.
tadarthīya [īya] amnf tadarthīyā intended for this use. .2
tadātman [ātman] amnf tadātmanī of such a spirit, of such an essence; of such a nature.
tadgata | gata | amnf adgatā math. raised to such a power.
taddharma [dharma] amnf taddharmā whose task it is.

taddhita [hita₂] m. gram. ["whose role is to hit (a stem)"] suffix [pratyaya] secondary (forms nouns from nouns); opp. krt₂. taddhitamūdho vaiyākaranah | taddhitamūdho 'vaiyākaraṇaḥ | gram. [Paspaśā] The grammarian has the taddhita suffixes as a burden; one who is ignorant of the taddhita suffixes is not a grammarian.
taddhitapratyaya | pratyaya | mr. gram. secondary noun formation suffix.
taddhitavrtti [vrtti] f. gram. formation of a secondary nominal theme, obtained by the action of a suffix taddhita on a nominal theme.
taddhitānta | anta | mr. gram. nominal derivative se condary.
tadbhava | bhava | amnf tadbhavā derived (from Sanskrit) — m. gram. word of Indoaryan origin; cf. tatsama; opp. apabhramśa.

tádrāja [rāja] m. gram. ["king of such country"] qualifies 5 suffixes taddhita added to the name of a people to form the name of its princes, with elision in the plural. pañcālāḥ the princes of Pāñcāla.
tádrūpa | rūpa | amnf tadrūpā of the same shape or color.
tádvayas | vayas₁ | amnf of the same age.
tadvid | vid₃ | amnf competent, specialist, ex pert.
tadvidya [vidyā] amnf tadvidyā connoisseur, expert.
tadvidyasaṃbhāṣā [saṃbhāṣā] f. consultation of a specialist.
tadā [taddā] adv. [correl. of yadā] then, in this case.
tadātadā |corr. yadāyadā| conj. then (each time).
tadānīm [nīm] adv. then, at that time. nāsad āsīn no sad āsīt tadānīm |RV.| (Nāsādisūkta, Hymn of Creation) At that time, neither nothingness existed, nor even Being existed.
tadryac var. tadyañc [tadac] amnf tadrīcī m. nom. tadryan; n. nom. tadryak in this direction.
tádvat [tadvat] amnf tadvatī of this form; similar to that | phil. [NN.] individual defined by a description — ind. thus, therefore, like (correl. of yadvat) | similarly, also.
tádvattā [tā] f. conformity.
tádvattva |tva| n. id. tadvattvam tadeva phil. |Nyāya| The extension of belonging to a notion is that notion itself (extension axiom).
tan₁ iic. tad.
tannimitta | nimitta | amnf tannimittā caused by this | related to this; in accordance with this.
tannimittatva |tva| n. the fact of being the cause of it.
tanmadhya [madhya] n. in the middle of that. tanmadhyāt among them; out of their ranks.
tanmanas | manas | amnf having this in mind; preoccupied with this.
tanmaya [maya] amnf tanmayī makes of this, of its matter, identical to it; absorbed into; consubstantial. tanmayībhū to become similar, to identify with.
tanmayatā |tā| f. absorption in, identification with; consubstantiality | phil. is said not. of the absorption in the nature of Kṛṣṇa.
tanmayatva [tva] n. id.

tanmātra [mātra] amnf tanmātrī just the amount — n. just a little | phil. |Sāṃkhya| substance [tattva] of perception, one of the 5 subtle elements perceived resp. by the 5 senses |buddhīndriya| : śabda the perception of sound (cf. śrotra), sparśa touch (cf. tvak), rūpa aspect or form (cf. cakṣus, akṣi), rasa taste (cf. jihvā) and gandha smell (cf. ghrāṇa); syn. sūkṣmabhūta; cf. divyaviṣaya.

√ tan₁ v. [8] pr. (tan₁óti) pr. r. (tanuté) fut. (tanisyati) pp. (tata) abs. (tatvā, tanitvā) pf. (ava, ā, ut, pra, vi, sam) to stretch, extend; lengthen to execute, accomplish (the sacrifice) — ca. (tānayati) to cause to lengthen; to cause to accomplish | lat. tendo; fr. tendre. lakṣmīm tan₁ to add to the luster.
√ tan₁ [related to stan] v. [4] pr. (tanyati) ved. thunder | gr. oo ; fr. thunder.
tána [act. tan₁] n. offspring, progeny.
tana forms adjectives from time adverbs, with f. in ī; can be abbreviated to tna.
tánaya [tanaya] m. ["who continues the race"] son — f. cf. tanayā.
tanayā [f. tanaya] f. girl.
tanayitnú var. stanayitnu [tan₁yitnu] amnf thunderous. .3
tanādi [(tan₁)ādi] m. gram. ["which begins with tan₁"] qualifies the eighth class [gaṇa] of the present tense of verbs; its characteristic marker [vikarana₂] is u.
taniman [tanuiman] m. smallness; thinness, slenderness; leanness; weakness | state of being shallow — n. med. liver.
tániṣṭha [super. tanu] amnf taniṣṭhā the smallest, the thinnest.
taniyas [compar. tanu] amnf taniyasī smaller, thinner; very thin, tiny.

tan₁ú [tan₁u] amnf tanū f. tanvī thin, slender, elegant; tenuous, light, fine, lean; clear (li quide); subtle | weak, unimportant, negligible — f. tanvī [élancée] pretty woman | lat. tenuis; all. dünn; ang. thin; fr. ténu. tanūkṛ to thin, shrink; to trim (skin). tanūbhū to thin, shrink; to make smaller.
tanuja [ja] m. son — f. tanujā daughter.
tanujatva [tva] n. quality of son.
tanubhṛt [bhṛt] m. ["who has a body"] living being; man.
tanumadhyama | madhyama | amnf tanu madhyamā with a slim waist, with slim hips.
tanumānasa [mānasa] n. phil. [YV.] the refinement of the mind (by concentration on an object), 3ᵉ ni calf of knowledge [jñānabhūmikā].
tanus |abstr. tan₁ | n. body; person; syn. tanū.
tanū [f. tanu] f. body; person, oneself — m. tanu ifc. whose body is (iic.)
tánūnápāt [napāt] m. ved. ["son of his own body" | np. of Tanūnapāt "the self-begotten", solemn epith. of Agni in the hymns of praise [āpryas].
tanti var. tantī [act. tan₁] obj. f. rope; lunge; line of lunges in a stable — m. weaver.

Tantipāla [pāla] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Tantipāla "Guardian of the tether", false identity of Sahadeva disguised as master of the stables, to hide at the court of King Virāta during the 13th year of exile of the Pāndavās.
tántu [tan₁tu] m. thread, string; cable; fiber | lineage; continuity. tantu kṛ to spin.
tantukarana | karana | n. spinning.
tantukriyā [kriyā] f. spinning work.
tantudhārin | dhārin | amnf tantudhārinī soc. | "cord bearer" | brahmin.

tántuparvan | parvan | n. soc. festival of the cord, celebrating the anniversary of the upanayana of Kṛṣṇa [syn. pavitrāropaṇa]; it is celebrated on the 12th day of the bright fortnight of the month śrāvaṇa₂.
tantuvāya | vāya | m. weaver.
tántutva [tantutva] n. fibrosity.

tántra |instr. tan₁| n. thread; warp (of a fabric); weft; continuity, succession | rule, method; treatise; model, system, doctrine; sectarian writing | soc. not. sectarian work śākta | phil. np. of the tan₁ tra, set of śākta doctrines and practices; cf.

kaula | troop, army | mod. procedure, program, software — f. tantrī lute string | vessel of the body — v. [11] pr. (tantrayati) to maintain in order; to align | to govern, apply a method, perform a tantra. tatra yat sakṛt kṛtaṃ bahūnām upakaroti tat tan₁ tram ityucyate [Sabarasvāmī] Tantra is said to be that which, applied once, serves multiple purposes.
tantraka |ka| amnf tantrikā new (said of a fabric just removed from the weft).
tantradosa | dosa₂ | m. error in a treaty.
tantraparīkṣā | parīkṣā | f. lit. critical work, not. of astronomy [jyotișa].
tantrapāla [pāla] m. soc. army commander.
tantrayukti | yukti | f. lit. rhetorical device; Kauṭilya lists 32 in the Arthaśāstra | scientific validity of traditional legal or medical texts, justified by a set of logical rules.
Tantraratna [ratna] n. bed. n.p. of the Tantraratna, work of Mīmāṃsā of Pārthasārathi₁ Miśra (13th century).
tantrarahasya [rahasya] n. lit. np. of the Tantrara hasya of Rāmānujācārya, which elaborates the Mīmāṃsā according to Prabhākara; cf. Sāstraprameyapariccheda.
Tantravaṭadhānikā |vaṭadhānikā| f. lit. np. of the Tantravaṭadhānikā, work of Abhinavagupta summary of his Tantrāloka.
tantravārttika [vārttika] n. bed. n.p. from the tan₁ travārttika, a gloss by Kumārila Bhaṭṭa of the Pūrvamīmāmsāsūtra with his commentary Mīmāmsāsūtrabhāsya; cf. Tuptīkā.

Tantrasamgraha [samgraha] m. lit. np. of the Tantrasamgraha, a treatise on mathematics and astronomy by Nīlakaṇṭha₃ Somayājī (1500), in 432 verses; it describes a heliocentric planetary model where the 5 planets revolve around the Sun, which itself revolves around the Earth. .4
tantrasadbhāva |sadbhāva| mr. bed. n.p. of the Sadbhāva Tantra, work of the kaula doctrine.
tantrasamuccaya [samuccaya] m. lit. np. from the Tan trasamuccaya "Tantric Breviary", a 14th-century ritual manual used in Kerala.
tantrasāra [sāra] m. bed. n.p. of tantrasāra "Essence of Tantra", work by Abhinavagupta, condensed from Tantrāloka.
Tantrākhyāyika |ākhyāyika| m. lit. np. of the Tantrākhyāyika, ancient version of the Pañcatantra of Kaśmīra.

Tantrāloka [āloka] m. lit. np. of the Tantrāloka "Elucidation of Tantra", major phil. work of Abhinavagupta in 37 chapters; it deals in particular with the ritual of the transgression sacrifice [kulayāga].
tantrālokaviveka [viveka] m. lit. np. of the detailed commentary tantrālokaviveka of the Tantrāloka by Jayaratha.
tantrin [Tantrain] amnf tantrinī which has threads; made of threads, spun, woven | stringed (instrument) — m. musician.
√ tandr v. [10] pr. r. (tandráyate) to tire (to (inf.), in (ppr.)).
tandrā [act. tandr] f. weariness, fatigue; exhaustion; laziness — m. tandri ifc. fatigue of ⟨iic.⟩ — f. tandri ifc. id.
tandrālu |lu| amnf who falls from fatigue.
tandrita [pp. tandr] amnf tandritā las, tired — f. tandritā weariness, need for sleep.
tanmayī iiv. tanmaya.
tanmayībhava [bhava] m. the act of becoming similar to.
tanmayībhavana [bhavana] n. identification; em
pathy | phil. | Trika | depersonalization
tanyatú |Tan₂| mr. ved. thunder.
tapa [act. tap] m. heat; hot season — ifc. that torments (iic.). paramtapah "that torments his enemy", epith. of hero, not. of Arjuna.
tapat [ppr. tap] amnf tapantī heating, burning — f. tapatī myth. np. of tapatī "Heatwave", daughter of Sūrya and Chāyā, wife of Samvaraņa and mother of Kuru; she personifies a river.
tápana [agt. tap] amnf tapanī that heats, that burns, that shines — m. myth. np. of Tapana "Burning", epith. of Sūrya.
tapanīya [pfp. [2] tap] amnf ta panīyā which must be heated | which must be endured (penance) — n. refined gold.
tapanīyamaya |maya| amnf tapanīyamayī in gold.
tapantaka m. lit. [KSS.] np. of tapantaka, son of Vasantaka; he became a pleasure companion of Naravāhanadatta.
tapara [(ta)para] amnf taparā gram. (fixed af) ending with 'ta'.

tapas [abstr. tap] n. heat, ardor; suffering, torment | mortification, penances, asceticism phil. the strength of soul acquired through asceticism, one of the disciplines [niyama] of yoga | observance incumbent upon the caste — m. astr. name of the Vedic month māgha (January-February) | cf. Taparloka — v. [11] pr. (tapasyati) to practice asceticism, to mortify oneself. tapasā i. adv. through penance. pañca tapāmsi soc. the 5 fires of penance: 4 fires in a square around the ascetic, and the Sun above.
Taparloka [loka] m. myth. np. of Taparloka "Heaven of the ascetics", 6th celestial world [loka], where the renunciants dwell | vairāgin |.
tapaskara [kara₁] m. soc. branding, a samskāra of Vishnuite initiation; syn. taptasamskāra.

tapasvin [vin] amnf Tapasvinī who practices penances, ascetic | pious; austere; mented tower | suffering, miserable, unhappy, pitiable — m. ascetic, hermit — f. Tapasvinī poor woman; ascetic woman | myth. np. of Tapasvinī "ascetic", mother of Mātali.
tapodhana [dhana] amnf tapodhanā ascetic (whose only wealth is his penances).
Tapovana [vana] m. hermitage ["ascetic wood"] | hist. n.p. of Svāmī Tapovana Mahārāja (1889–1957); he was the guru of Cinmayānanda.
tapasya [tapasya] n. practice of penance, asceticism, spiritual discipline — m. astr. name of a Vedic month (phālguna, February-March). tapasye bhū to undertake asceticism. .5

tapita [pp. tap] amnf tapitā cf. tapta. ਰਸ tapta var. tapita [pp. tap] amnf taptā heated; hot, ardent; incandescent, reddened by fire; melted, molten | tormented, afflicted; who has practiced penances. taptam taptena sambadhyate hot unites with hot (maxim | nyāya | equivalent to "like attracts like").
taptamudrā | mudra | f. soc. branding on the skin (from an attribute of Viṣṇu); its imposition is one of the 5 rites of vaiṣṇavadīkṣā.
taptamudrādhāraṇa [dhāraṇa] n. soc. wearing the seal of Vișnu imprinted with a red-hot iron, religious sign of the mādhva sect.
Taptavāluka [vāluka] amnf taptavālukā at the Burning Sand — m. myth. [PP.] np. of Taptavāluka "Burning Sand", one of the 7 hells — f. taptavālukā pl. burning gravel.
taptasaṃskāra [saṃskāra] m. soc. branding, a saṃskāra of Vishnuite initiation; syn. your paskara.
√ tam v. |4| pr. (tamyati) pft. (tatāma) pp. (tamita) to be afflicted, to languish, to grieve | to faint, to suffocate.

tama sf. super form. | a. ord. form (i th) (with f. in ī) | (rare) after noun, cf. kaṇvatama | var. tamām intens. after adv., qqf. verbs. 2000 tama varşa the year 2000. pacatitamām he is the best cook.

támas [abstr. tam] n. darkness, gloom, blackness; torpor | [tamoguṇa] phil. [Sāṃkhya] Darkness, 3rd quality [guṇa] of nature, passive essence of ignorance and inertia; its efficacy [arthakriyā] is restriction [niyama] || lat. te mere; all. Dämmerung; ang. dim; fr. ténèbres. andham tamah blinding darkness.
tamasvat |vat| amnf tamasvatī dark, obscure cur — f. tamasvatī night.
támasvin [vin] amnf tamasvinī filled with obs curité — f. tamasvinī night. tamasvinyām adv. in the night.

tamasá [tamasa] amnf tamasā dark, gloomy — m. darkness — n. ifc. blackness of (iic.) — f. tamasā geo. np. of the tamasā river, tributary of the Gangā south of the Yamunā; myth. it was on its banks that Rāma spent his first night of exile, accompanied by many inhabitants of Ayodhyā; Vālmīki had his hermitage on its banks; it was there that Sītā took refuge with her two sons when she was repudiated by Rāma.
tamākhu m. mod. tobacco || eng. tobacco; fr. tobacco.
tamākhunālī [nālī] f. cigarette.
tamākhunālīvikrayaka | vikrayaka | mr. cigarette seller.

tamāla [tamāla] m. bio. bot. Xanthochymus pictorius (var. bot. Garcinia Xanthochymus), black laurel or false mangosteen, a tree of medium altitude, with very dark bark, white flowers, and edible orange fruits; its sap is used to make ink.
tamālavīthikāndhakāraiḥ [K.] with its dark avenues of black laurel.
tamālapattra [pattra] n. black bay leaf |soc. sectarian mark on the forehead.

tamālaka |tamālaka| amnf Tamālikā with black bark or skin — m. organic. black laurel — f. Tamālikā lit. n.p. of Tamālikā "of ebony complexion", servant-messenger of Vāsavadattā₁ | bed. |K.| n.p. of Tamālikā₁, betel bearer |tāmbūlakarankavāhinī| of Kādambarī.
támisra [tamasra] n. darkness; black night; dark fortnight | pl. tamisrāṇi id. — f. tamisrā darkness, black night.
tamo iic. tamas.
tamoguna | guna | m. phil. | Sāmkhya | Darkness, 3rd quality [guna] of nature, passive essence of ignorance and inertia.
tamoguṇamaya |maya| amnf tamoguṇamayī which has the quality of Darkness.
taya sf. forms the adjective npartite after the number n (f. en tayī).
tayā [i. tad] f. by her.
tayos [g. du. tad] mnf of the two of them — loc. in the two of them.
tára [agt. tṛ] amnf tarī that which makes one cross, ferryman; that which saves — ifc. act of overcoming (iic.) — m. crossing, passage — f. tarī boat, ship.
tara sf. form of the comparative a. | qqf. sf. intensive of noun, cf. vrtratara, duḥkhatara | sort of (iic.); cf. aśvatara — ind. (with na) not at all | cf. tarām.
tarákṣu |related to kṣī| m. bio. hyena.
taraṃgita [pp. taraṅga] amnf taraṃgitā that goes back and forth; that undulates; drowned (in tears) — n. movement of waves, of coming and going.

taraṃgin var. taraṅgin [agt. taraṃga] amnf taraṃgiṇī which undulates, alternating; which goes back and forth incessantly — f. taraṃgiṇī river — ifc. lit. form .6 of the names of works, not. biographies.
taraṇa [agt. tr] mf taraṇī raft, boat — act. n. crossing (of (iic.)) | act of overcoming (an obstacle, a misfortune) — m. tarani the Sun.
taraņi [agt. tr] m. the Sun ["which crosses the sky"] | hist. np. of the Tarani scholar Miśra, contemporary of Gangesa who refuted it, author of an unknown Rat nakośa.
taraṇīya [pfp. [2] tr̄] amnf taraṇīyā to cross (river).
taratama tara, tama.

taram [acc. tara] iic. taramga var. taranga [ga₁] m. wave, wave; re soft; comes and goes | bed. chapter of a work, not. Kathāsaritsāgara or Rājataraṃgiņī — c. |11| pr. (taramgayati) to move back and forth.
taraṃgavatī |vat| f. n.p. of the river Taraṃgavatī "which forms waves".
tarambuja [Persian] n. watermelon.
tarala |tṛala| amnf taralā trembling; mobile | sparkling — m. wave; necklace; jewel, not. ruby — f. taralā liqueur.
Taralikā [ika] f. lit. [K.] np. of Taralikā, companion of Mahāśvetā used as a matchmaker by Pundarīka₂.
táras |abstr. tṛ| n. speed, velocity; force, energy, efficiency — amnf fast; energetic. tarasā adv. quickly, directly.
tárasvat |vat| amnf tarasvatī cf. tarasvin.
tárasvín |vin| amnf tarasvinī swift, violent, energetic; bold — m. messenger; runner; hero | wind | falcon; epith. of Garuda.

tarām [acc. pl. tara] ind. intens. after prep., cf. atitarām | adv. (later) intens. after verbal form; (with na) not at all. pacatitarām he cooks better. dadātitarām he gives more. vaktitarām he talks a lot.
tari [instr. tṛ] f. boat; not. ferryman's boat var. tarī id.
tarika |ka| m. ferryman | soc. officer controlling river crossings.
taru [tru] m. tree eng. tree.
taruṣaṇḍa [ṣaṇḍa] n. grove, park.

táruṇa [tṛuna] amnf taruṇī young, juvenile, vigorous; fresh, tender, delicate; just begun — m. adolescent, young man — f. tarunī young girl, young woman (up to 30 years old) — voc. taruṇi adr. Miss — v. [11] pr. (tarunayati) to rejuvenate — v. [11] pr. r. (taruṇāyate) to be young; to remain young || gr. . kūpodakam vatacchāyā tāmbūlam tarunīkucau śītakāle bhaveduṣṇam uṣṇakāle tu śītalam || The water drawn from the well, the shade of the banyan tree, the betel leaf and the breasts of a young woman are warm in the cold season but cool in the hot season.
√ tark v. [10] pr. (tarkayati) pp. (tarkita) pf. (pra, vi) to consider, examine, appreciate, evaluate; to reflect, judge; to conjecture; to suspect, to doubt acc. || gr. ; lat. torqueo.

Tarka [obj. tark] m. subject of reflection, discussion; topic, reasoned notion | supposition, conjecture; speculation, examination, evaluation, discussion, deliberation | reason; reasoning, argumentation, reflection | phil. logic, dialectic; not. reasoning by contradiction, refutation | phil. |Vāgbhata| one of the 6 philosophical systems: jina, sāṃkhya, śiva, bhāṭṭa, bauddha, laukāyata phil. one of the 6 orthodox viewpoints | darśana | | math. symb. the number 6 — f. tarkā phil. reasoning; investigation | pali takka. upasannah te tarkah you saw correctly. tarko'numānameva phil. Tarka is nothing other than reasoning. tarkyate iti tarkah Le Tarka, c'est ce dont en dis cute, le sujet de la discussion.
Tarkakaumudī | kaumudī | f. lit. | Nyāya | np. of the Tarkakaumudī "Light on Logic", work of Laugāksi Bhāskara₂.
tarkatāṇḍava [tāṇḍava] m. lit. np. of the Tar katāṇḍava "Dance of the apocalypse of logic", or work of Vyāsatīrtha in support of Madhva.
Tarkadīpikā |dīpikā| f. bed. |Nyāya| n.p. of the Tarkadīpikā "Exegesis of logic", treatise by Annambhatta glossing his form Tarkasamgraha.
tarkaparibhāṣā [paribhāṣā] f. bed. n.p. from the Tarka paribhāṣā, a treatise on logic by Keśava₃ Miśra.
tarkapāda [pāda] m. phil. section of a work dealing with the rational discussion of the proper subject of the work.
tarkabhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. bed. n.p. from the tarkabhāṣā, an elementary teaching work by Nyāya Vaiseșika of Kesava Misra (end of the 13th century).
Tarkabhāṣāprakāśikā [prakāśikā] f. lit. [Nyāya] np. of the Tarkabhāṣāprakāśikā, a work of logic by Cannibhațța (14th century).
Tarkavāgīśa [vāgīśa] m. hist. n.p. of Ma thurānātha₁ Tarkavāgīśa, son and student of Rāma Tarkālankāra; cf. Mathurānātha₁. .7

Tarkavācaspati | vācaspati | m. soc. title Tar kavācaspati of scholar in logic | hist. np. of Tārānātha Tarkavācaspati, (1806–1885), Bengali scholar, lexicographer, superior of Sanskrit Col lege of Calcutta, author of the Vācaspatya.
tarkavidyā | vidyā | f. phil. science of reasoning; syn. Tarkaśāstra.

Tarkaśāstra | śāstra | n. phil. science of reasoning; cf. Navyanyāya | lit. np. of the Tarkaśāstra, or work of logic attributed to Vasubandhu; the original Sanskrit, lost, was translated into Chinese by Pa ramārtha.

tarkasaṃgraha [saṃgraha] m. lit. [Nyāya] np. of the Tarkasamgraha "Compendium of Concepts", Annambhațța's formulary treatise, the basic work of Nyāya; the Tarkadīpikā of the same author is a gloss on it; the Nyāyabodhinī and the Padakṛtya are commentaries on it.
tarkāmṛta [amṛta] n. lit. np. from the tarkāmṛta "Nec Tar of logic", elementary manual of Jagadīśa.
Tarkālankāra [alankāra] m. hist. n.p. of the gician Rāma Tarkālankāra (16th century), student of Rāmabhadra₁ Sārvabhauma, father of Ma thurānātha₁; he is the author of the Viṣayatāvāda.
tarkaṇīya [pfp. [1] tark] amnf tarkaṇīyā suspect.
tarkita [pp. tark] amnf atarkitā considered as; investigated — n. conjecture.
tarkin [agt. tark] amnf tarkinī imbu de speculation, versed in logic; logician | phil. dialectician; skeptic.
tarku [tarku] mn time zone. tarkukarman n. pl. tarkukarmāṇi the work of spinning, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
tarkya [pfp. [1] tark] amnf tarkyā to consider, to evaluate, to examine; which deserves reflection | doubtful, suspect.
√ tarj v. [1] pr. (tarjati) pp. (tarjita) pf. (pari) to threaten, terrify | to scold, blame; to mock, ridicule — ca. (tarjayati) id.
tarjaka [agt. tarj] amnf tarjikā which naces me.
tarjana [act. tarj] n. act of threatening, grunting, ridiculing — f. cf. tarjanī.
tarjanī [f. tarjana] f. (threatening finger) index finger threatening attitude (not. of sacred images).
tarjanīya [pfp. [2] tarj] amnf tarjanīyā which must be scolded.
tarjita [pp. tarj] amnf tarjitā threatened; scolded, humiliated; ridiculed — n. threat.
tarp [ca. tṛp₁] v. [10] pr. (tarpayati) to satisfy, to please, to rejoice.

tarpaṇa [act. ca. tṛp₁] n. satisfaction, satiety [pitṛtarpaṇa] soc. libation of water to the manes — ifc. act of satisfying; food. āmrasekapitrtarpaṇanyāyaḥ maxim of watering the mango tree and of the libation to the manes: one can make an offering to the manes at the foot of a mango tree, and take the opportunity to water it; it is equivalent to "killing two birds with one stone".
tarṣa [act. tṛṣ₁] m. desire; thirst — ifc. desire for ⟨iic.⟩ — f. tarṣā desire; thirst || pali taḥhā.
tarṣam [abs. tṛṣ₁] ind. having been thirsty.
tarhi adv. [correl. of yadi] then, now, at this moment | consequently.
tarhyeva | eva | adv. only then.
tala mn surface, ground | palm of the hand; sole of the foot; handle. talān dā to slap each other.
talatra [tra] n. glove worn by archers.
talapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. work of mythology of a holy place; cf. sthalamāhātmya.
talavat [vat] amnf talavatī which has a surface.
talānguli [anguli] iic. the palm and the finger.
talāngulitra [tra] iic. (glove) which protects the palm and finger (of the archer).
talāṅgulitravat [vat] m. (archer) wearing the glove.
Talātala [atala] n. myth. n.p. of the world [loka] Talātala, fifth underground hell.
talavá [talava] m. musician.
talavákāra [kāra] m. pl. school of Sāmaveda. talavakārabrāhmaņa [brāhmaṇa] n. bed. n.p. from the Talavakārabrāhmaņa, brāhmaņa text of the Sāmaveda; syn. Jaiminīya.
talātali [red. tala] adv. in hand-to-hand combat.
tálpa mn bed, couch, bench | upper floor | raft — f. talpā couch, lit. talpam adhigam to have sexual relations with (iic.). talpam āvas to desecrate the marital bed.
talpaga [ga₁] ifc. m. who has sexual relations with (iic.).
tava [g. tvad] ind. from you, to you, yours.
tavāsmi ["I am yours"] I surrender (words of surrender from a vanquished man to the victor).
tavat forms ppa. (see ktavatu)
tavarga [(ta)varga] m. phon. the class of dentals. .8
tavás amnf strong, energetic; courageous — m. power, strength, courage.

taviṣá [related to tavas] amnf taviṣī strong, energetic, courageous — m. strength, courage — f. taviṣī id. — v. [11] pr. (taviṣīyáti) v. [11] pr. r. (taviṣīyáte) to be powerful; to show courage. tavisībhis adv. powerfully.
távīyas var. tavyas [compar. tavas] amnf tavīyasī stronger. tavasas tavīyān stronger than the strong.
tavya gram. form of pfp. of obligation or necessity (cf. tavyat).
tavyat nota. gram. primary affix [kṛt₂] of the pfp. in tavya. ਰਣ taṣṭá |pp. takṣ| amnf taṣṭā hewn, cut, shaped; sculpted. hṛdā taṣṭān mantrān Mantras come from the heart.

tas forms adverbs of place or circumstance, forms adverbs of manner meaning "according to", "as a result of", "in the manner of", "respectively to", etc. | ablative sf; cf. tasil. mumbaitaḥ āgatavān he comes from Bombay.
tasil nota. gram. ablative suffix, obtained by affixing to a nominal stem of tas.
taskara m. thief, brigand. apahṛtāni dhanavatām dhanāni taskarādibhiḥ DKC. Thieves and others stole the goods of the rich.

tasthivas [ppft. sthā₁] amnf tasthuṣī having stood, who stood, who was standing; who continues; ready to (dat.) — n. tasthivat the vegetable and mineral kingdom; the immobile (opp. jagat) | phil. the immutable.
tasmāt [abl. tad] adv. [correl. of yasmāt] thus, for this reason.
tasmin [loc. tad] ind. in him, in this.
tasmai [dat. tad] ind. to him, to this.
tasya |g. tad| ind. of him, of this.
tasyām [loc. sā₂] ind. in it, on it.
tasyās [g. sā₂] ind. of her.
tasyai [dat. sā₂] ind. to her.
tā form of the sf. of state; quality of; species denotes a collection of || fr. té.
tācchīlika [*tacchīlaika] amnf tācchīlikā gram. is said of a suffix denoting the habit or the naturalness of an action.
tācchīlya [*tacchīlaya] n. nature ca ractéristique; habit, interest in.
Tājika m. geo. Tajik; Persian; syn. ya vana | hist. n.p. of Tājika, epith. of Tuka, Persian astrologer; by ext. Perso-Arabic astrology; cf. varşaphala.
Tājikatantrasāra [tantrasāra] m. bed. n.p. from the Tājikatantrasāra, an astrological work of Arabic origin by Samarasimha (13th century); also called Karmaprakāśā, Manusyajātaka and Ganakabhūsana.
Tājikamuktāvali [muktāvali] f. bed. n.p. from the Tājikamuktāvali, an astrological work by Tuka.
tājikayogasudhānidhi [yogasudhānidhi] m. lit. np. from the tājikayogasudhānidhi, a work on astronomy by Yādavasūri.

Tāṭakā [*taṭaka] f. myth. [Rām.] np. of the yakṣī Tāṭakā “(Guardian) of the edge of the forest”, daughter of the yakṣa Suketu, “strong as 1000 elephants”; she married the gandharva Sunda₁, and bore Mārīca and Subāhu; after Agastya reduced Sunda₁ to ashes for disturbing his devotions, she attacked his hermitage with her sons, but Agastya cursed them, and she became a hi deuse rākṣasī , haunting a forest south of the Sa rayū; the young Rāma killed her, on the order of his guru Viśvāmitra, although he was loath to kill a woman.
tāṭaṅka n. ear ornament, female symbol; it notably adorns the left ear of Națarāja.
tāṭasthya |*taṭasthaya| n. indifference. mā bhaja mā bhaja durge tātasthyam putrakesu
dīnesu [Durgāstuti] O Durgā! Do not remain indifferent to your children in distress.
tāḍa [act. That. taḍ] m. cut.
tādapattra | pattra | n. palm leaf (for writing).
tādaka [agt. tad] m. murderer — f. tādakā myth. [Rām.] np. of the yakṣī Tāḍakā; cf. Tāṭakā.

tāḍana [agt. ca. taḍ] amnf tāḍanā that strikes, that beats, that wounds — act. n. action of beating, of striking, of whipping | astr. eclipse by tielle — ifc. (after instrument) act of inflicting a correction with (iic.) — f. tāḍanī whip.
tāḍita [pp. ca. taḍ] amnf tāḍitā beaten, struck, punished | struck by lightning, struck by thunderbolt.
tāditaka |ka| ifc. amnf tāditakā struck by (iic.).
tāḍyamāna [ppr. ps. ca. taḍ] amnf tādyamānā being struck, being beaten.
tāṇḍava [*taṇḍua] mn myth. dance ma cabre of SivaBhairava in The Crematorium Enclosures | [ānandatāṇḍava] myth. cosmic dance of Šiva Națarāja; cf. nadānta | by extension frenzied dance, .9 trance.
Tāṇḍya m. lit. patr. of the scholar Tāṇḍya — n. cf. tāṇḍyabrāhmana.
tāṇḍyabrāhmaṇa [brāhmaṇa] n. lit. np. of the tāṇḍyabrāhmaṇa, also called Mahābrāhmaṇa or Pañcavimsabrāhmaņa.
tāt forms adverbs with a locative meaning | stāt id.
tāta [*tata₂] m. father — voc. adr. affectionate towards a male relative, junior or senior; papa | pl. tātās dear all.
tātācārya |ācārya| m. hist. np. of the Vaishnava philosopher tātācārya, of the viśiṣṭādvaita school of Rāmānuja (16th century); he had as his patron Sevappa Nāyaka of Tanjavūr.
tāti [act. tan₁] f. continuity; descent.

tātparya [*tatparaya] amnf tātparyā having as its purpose; aimed at — n. act of devoting oneself to it | reference to (loc.); intention; aimed purpose | gram. [Mīmāṃsā] transmission of the speaker's intention — ifc. lit. work about (iic.).

Tātparyacandrikā₁ [candrikā] f. bed. n.p. of the Tātparyacandrikā₁ "Light on the intention of the lo cutor", commentary [tīkā] of the Gītā due to Vedāntadeśika, following Rāmānuja | bed. n.p. from the Tātparyacandrikā₁ of Vyāsatīrtha, commentary on the Tattvaprakāśikā of Jayatīrtha; it earned him the title of Candrikācārya.
tātparyajñāna [jñāna] n. gram. intention of the speaker.
Tātparyaṭīkā [ṭīkā] f. bed. n.p. of the Tātparyaṭīkā, glossed by Vācaspati₁ Miśra of the Nyāyabhāsya.

tātparyanirṇaya [nirṇaya] m. determination of intention; motivation | lit. np. of the tātparyanirṇaya of Madhva, which presents the philosophical purpose of the stories of the Mah., the Rām., the Harivaṃśa and the mythological collections [purāṇa], in 5180 stanzas |śloka|.
tātparyalinga [linga] n. phil. [Mīmāmsā] index of the speaker's intention, a hermeneutic tool of Prakāśātmā, who lists six: coherence of the
discourse [upakramopasaṃhāraikarūpya], repetition [abhyāsa], innovation [apūrva], benefit [phala], factual description [arthavāda] and plausibility [upapatti].
tātparyaśakti [śakti] f. gram. [Jayanta] power of words to account for communicative intention.
tātparyārtha [artha] m. gram. meaning of a word intended by the speaker, communicative intention.

tātparyārthānupapatti | anupapatti | f. gram. in incompatibility of the literal meaning of a word with the intention of the speaker. chattrino yānti a group of people moves, some (but not all) carrying an umbrella.

tādarthya [*tadarthaya] n. state of being appropriate; usefulness; relevance | gram. similarity of meaning, synonymy | gram. semantic role [kāraka] of usefulness, marked by the dative. tādarthyeṇa with this intention; for this purpose; in this sense. tādarthye caturthī vācyā gram. Usefulness is indicated with the dative.
tādātmya [*tadātmanya] n. auto coincidence; coherence | phil. [Nyāya] similarity or identity of nature (with (i. loc. iic.)); opp. anyonyābhāva.
tādrs [*taddrs₂] amnf [correl. of yādrs] of this sort, similar; like, such — amn tādṛśa f. tādṛśī id. — amn tādṛkṣa f. tādṛkṣī id.
tāna [agt. tan₁] m. fiber | tone, resonance | gr. τονος; fr. your.
tāni [nom. pl. tad] ind. them, these, they.
tāntrika [*tantraika] amnf tāntrikā taught in a tantric soc. manual — m. phil. adept of tantric doctrines.
Tāntrikābhidhānakośa [abhidhānakośa] m. bed. n.p. from Tāntrikābhidhānakośa “Vocabulary of tantris me”.
tāp [ca. tap] v. [10] pr. (tāpayati) pp. (tāpita) to cause suffering, to burn.
tāpa [act. tap] m. torment; pain (moral and physical) | soc. branding with the cakra and the śańkā on the shoulders of renunciants of the pañcarātra lineage of Rāmānuja.

tāpatraya [traya] n. phil. the three kinds of evils: [ādhyātmika] internal torments of the body and mind (hunger, thirst, anger, jealousy, confusion), [ādhibhautika] external secular evils (attacks by animals or enemies, wars)
and [ādhidaivika] the evils due to natural or supernatural calamities (storms, earthquakes, epidemics).
tāpaka [agt. tap] amnf tāpikā that heats, that inflames; that torments — m. fever |furnace — f. tāpikā frying pan.
tāpatya [*tapatī] m. myth. [Mah.] np. from tāpatya "descendant of tapatī", matr. from Kuru; epith. of Arjuna.

Tāpana [agt. tap] amnf tāpanī that burns, that causes suffering — m. the Sun | the heat wave — n. burn; torment lit. [theatre] distress, perplexity | bd. np. of Tāpana, one of the 8 burning hells, where the damned are impaled by a white-hot spit — f. tāpanā asceticism.
tāpasa [*tapasa] m. ascetic, hermit.
Tāpasavatsarājacarita [vatsarājacarita] n. bed. n.p. of the nāṭaka Tāpasavatsarājacarita, due to Mātrarāja; it is freely inspired by Svapnavāsavadatta.
tāpiccha [contr. tāpinaṃchādayati] m. organic. ["which provides shade to those suffering from the heat"] bot. Xanthochymus pictorius, syn. tamāla var. tāpiñcha id.
tāpita [pp. ca. tap] amnf tāpitā heated,
inflamed | tormented, wounded | converted.
tāpin [agt. tap] amnf tāpinī that causes suffering | suffering from the heat; suffering.
tām [acc. sā₂] ind. she, this.

tāmasa [*tamas] amnf tāmasī ["whose predominant guna is tamas" | dark, gloomy; ignorant, asleep; passive, inert — m. wicked | myth. np. of tāmasa "from darkness", 4th Manu of the kalpa — f. tāmasī night.
tāmasika [tāmasaika] amnf tāmasikā relating to tamas, of the nature of tamas; inert, passive.
tāmisra [*tamisra] amnf tāmisrā dark astr. (fortnight [pakṣa] where the Moon is waning) — m. phil. [Sāṃkhya] anger, one of the 5 forms of ignorance | avidyā| | cf. andhatāmisra.
tāmbala amnf tāmbalī made of hemp.
tāmbūla m. bio. bot. Piper betle or betel vine, a type of pepper plant — n. betel leaf, not. to be chewed with areca nut [pūga] — f. tāmbūlī betel.
tāmbūlakaranka [karanka] m. necessary for betel.
tāmbūlakarankavāha [vāha] m. soc. servant of a prince charged with carrying his betel.
tāmbūlakarankavāhinī [vāhinī] f. soc. attendant of a princess charged with carrying her betel.
tāmbūlabhoga | bhoga₂ | m. betel pleasure.
tāmbūlika [ika] m. betel seller.

tāmrá amnf Tāmrā coppery, dark red — n. copper; copper vessel — f. Tāmrā myth. [Rām.] np. of Tāmrā "the red one", daughter of Dakṣa; by Kaśyapa she gave birth to five daughters who in turn gave birth to the five races of birds — f. tāmrī in copper.

Tāmradvīpa [dvīpa] m. geo. np. of Tāmradvīpa, Ceylon the "Copper-colored Island"; known to the Greeks as Taprobane, to the Arabs as Serendib, to the Portuguese as Ceilão, to the English as Cey lon; syn. Svarņadvīpa, śrī Laṅkā; myth. Rāvaņa established his capital Lankā there; bd. it was near its shores that the ship of Simhala sank with his 700 companions | pali Tambapanni.
tāmrapaṭṭa | paṭṭa | mr. cf. tāmrapattra.

tāmrapattra | pattra | n. copper sheet for writing | soc. land title deed written on a copper sheet. tāmraparņa | parņa | n. myth. one of the 10 regions [dvīpa] forming the jambudvīpa — f. tāmraparņī geo. np. of the Tāmraparņī River, in southern Tamil Nadu; it is renowned for pearl fishing.
tāmrapraśasti | praśasti | f. soc. copper plaque recording a royal donation.
tāmramūlā [mūla] f. bio. bot. Rubia munjista, high-altitude rubiaceae liana; this madder is used in dyeing and medicine; syn. mañjisthā.
tāmralipta | lipta | mr. pl. geo. n.p. of the people and country of the Tāmraliptās, west of the Ganges delta — f. Tāmraliptā f. Tāmraliptī their capital, Tāmraliptā/Tāmraliptī.
tāmraśāsana [śāsana] n. inscription on copper plate.
tār [ca. tṛ] v. [10] pr. (tārayati) pfp. (tārya) inf. (tārayitum) to make cross, to lead; to save, to rescue | to free from (abl.).
tāra [agt. ca. tṛ] amnf tārā that makes cross ser; savior, liberator | bright, resplendent; high, piercing (sound) — m. brilliance; strident sound — n. silver — f. cf. tārā || ang. star.

tāraka [agt. tār] amnf tārikā that which makes cross, that which transports; savior, liberator — m. myth. np. of tāraka "Star", daitya who through his penances acquired great powers and threatened the three worlds; he obtained that he could only be killed by a son of Shiva; Agni, solicited by the gods, hid; an elephant denounced him, and Agni cursed the elephants for not being able to stick out their tongues; a parrot denounced him, and Agni cursed the parrots for not being able to speak distinctly; he was defeated by Indra with the help of KumāraSkanda; his three sons Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī and Kamalākṣa took refuge in the triple fortress Tripura — n. Star; meteor — f. cf. tārakā.
Tārakākṣa [akṣa] m. myth. np. of Tārakākṣa “who has stars in his eyes”, son of tāraka; cf. Tri pura.
Tārakārāja [rāja] m. myth. np. of Tārakārāja, epith. of Candra "King of the stars".
Tārakā [f. tāraka] f. star; syn. Tārā₁ | myth. n.p. of Tārakā "Star", another name for Tārā₁ | astr. main star of a nakṣatra; syn. yogatārā.
tārakāmaya [maya] amnf tārakāmayī relating to Tārakā.
tārakāmayayuddha | yuddha | n. myth. | VP. | war over Etoile, caused by the abduction of Tārā₁ by Candra.
tārakitá |ita| amnf tārakitā étoilée (said of the early night sky).

Tāraṇa [agt. tṛ] amnf tāraṇī that makes one cross, that helps one to pass; savior, liberator | myth. epith. of Shiva or Vishnu "savior" | astr. np. of Tāraṇa "Salvation", personifying the 18th year of a life cycle [samvatsara] — n. the act of getting out of a difficulty; crossing, passage; Salvation.
tāratamya [*taratamaya] n. gradation, proportion; difference, inequality. tāratamyena adv. to varying degrees; more or less.

Tārā₁ [f. tāra] f. star, celestial body, meteor | myth. np. of Tārā₁ "Star", wife of Bṛhaspati; she was abducted by SomaCandra, with whom she had a son, Budha; cf. Candramasī | phil. [Tantra] np. of Tārā₁ "liberator", one of the 10 powers [mahāvidyā] of the Goddess [Sakti]; she is depicted as blue, with her tongue hanging out [lolajihvā], blood flowing from her mouth, her foot on the chest of the reclining Shiva. myth. [Rām.] np. of Tārā₁, wife of the Monkey King Vālī, and mother of Angada; upon Vālī's death, she married his half-brother Sugrīva; She cursed Rama for losing Sita after he found her | bd. name of various goddesses; not. the white Tara and the green Tara. tārāgaņa [gaṇa] m. multitude of stars.
tārādattā [datta] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of Queen tārādattā "gift of Tārā₁", wife of King Kalingadatta, mother of Kalingasenā.
Tārānātha [nātha] m. SOC. np. of Tārānātha "Master of the stars", title of scholar [pandita].
tārāpīḍa [āpīḍa] m. lit. [K.] np. of the King of Uj jayinī Tārāpīda "Crowned with stars", father of Candrāpīda₁.

tārāvalī [āvalī] f. line of stars | lit. [DKC.] np. of the yakṣī princess tārāvalī "Lineage of stars", daughter of King Manibhadra; she took in Arthapāla, fruit of the love of Kāmapāla and Kāntimatī | lit. |KSS.| np. of the princess tārāvalī₁, daughter of Rambha, eighth wife of Sūryaprabha₁.
tārin [agt. tṛ] amnf Tāriṇī that makes one cross; savior, liberator — f. tāriņī myth. np. of Tārinī, epith. of Durgā "liberator".
tāruṇya [*taruṇaya] n. youth; freshness.
tārkika [*tarkaika] amnf tārkikā relating to logic | phil. qualifies rationalist doctrines — m. dialectician; logician; rationalist reasoner, rationalist philosopher.
Tārkikarakṣā [rakṣā] f. bed. [Nyāya] np. from the Tārkikarakṣā, work of Varadarāja Miśra (12th century).

tārkṣya m. ved. np. of tārkṣya, solar deity, first a horse (also called Aristanemi), then a bird, later identified with Garuda. svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ svasti | naḥ Pūṣā viśvavedāḥ svasti | nastārkṣyo ariṣṭanemiḥ svasti | no brhaspatirdadhātu || ved. [RV.] May Indra of high renown favor us, may Pūṣā the most generous favor us, may tārkṣya whose wheel (of the solar chariot) is indestructible favor us, may Brhaspati favor us.
tārya [pfp. [1] tār] amnf tāryā to cross, to traverse.

tāla [*tala] m. lock; bolt | bio. bot. Bo rassus flabelliformis, ronier or palmyra, a species of wine palm with a straight trunk; its sweet sap is drunk; its dates are edible, and it provides a choupalmiste; its leaves are used for writing; myth. it is the emblem of BhīṣmaTālaketu | the act of clapping one's hands, of beating time; cymbal; rhythmic movement (not. of an elephant's ears) | mus. rhythm (given by striking the strings of an instrument with the palm); rhythmic cycle; In Carnatic music, there are 7 basic rhythms, given with their constituents [anga₁]: dh ruva (1 laghu, 1 druta and 2 laghu), matya₁ (1 laghu, 1 druta and 1 laghu), rūpaka (1 druta and 1 laghu), jhampa (1 laghu, 1 anudruta, and 1 druta), triputa (1 laghu and 2 druta), atta (2 laghu and 2 druta) and eka (1 laghu) | pitch measure, equals 12 inches | angula| (approximately 23 cm); syn. vitasti — f. cf. tālī.
Tālaketu [ketu] m. myth. np. of Tālaketu, epith. of Bhīşma "carrying the palm tree on his banner".
tālaghāta | ghāta | m. slap.

Tālajaigha [jaighā] m. myth. np. of the valiant King Tālajangha "Palm Leg", son of Jayadh vaja; he was defeated by Paraśurāma; the eldest of his 100 sons, Vītihotra, took refuge in the Himalayas | pl. myth. np. of the Haihaya tribe of the Tālajanghās, his descendants
ashes [lit. [KSS.] np. bhūta Tālajangha₁; cf. Hariśikha.
tāladhāraka [dhāraka] m. conductor, who beats the beat; syn. śailūṣa | dancer, who keeps the beat.
tāladhārin | dhārin | m. | nātya | cymbal player.
tāladhvaja | dhvaja | m. myth. np. of tāladhvaja, epith. of Balarāma "carrying the palm tree on his standard" | soc. np. of Balarāma's 16-wheeled chariot at the Jagannātha rathayātrā festival.
tālamāna | māna₂ | n. iconometry; canonical rules governing iconographic measurements in the śilpaśāstra .
tālaka [tālaka] m. venomous insect — n. orpiment — f. tālikā palm of the hand.
tālavya [tāluya] amnf tālavyā phon. palatal — m. phon. palatal phoneme.

tālī [f. tāla] f. bio. bot. Corypha umbraculi fera, talipot palm, native to Malabar, with large umbrella-shaped leaves; it can reach 25 in height; its leaves are used for writing and for covering roofs, its sap is fermented to make palm wine | palm alcohol | ang. toddy.
tālīpattra | pattra | n. talipot palm leaf.

tālīśa [related to tālī] m. bio. bot. Flacourtia jangomas, tree cultivated for its plum-like fruits; it is used in medicine; sacrificial spoons are made from its wood; syn. sruvavṛkṣa, vikankata, prācīnāmalaka.
talu n. palate (of the mouth).
tāvaká [*tavaka] amnf tāvikā f. tāvakī ton; here.

tāvat [*tadvat] amnf tāvatī as large, as numerous, as long, as much — adv. |correl. of yāvat| as much, so much, as, for as long | first; only; so be it! | (interr. or imp.) therefore | (fut. pr.) then (indicates that the action will take place). tāvatā i. adv. to that extent | meanwhile; in the meantime. tāvati loc. adv. so far; until then, meanwhile. na tāvat not yet; not for the moment. mā tāvat never in my life; God forbid! itas tāvat come here first. gatā tāvat she has indeed left. dṛḍhas tāvad bandhaḥ the knot is indeed tightly tied. tāvannāpina not just no but, but no, plain and simple. tisthatu tāvat put it aside for a while.
tāvatika |ika| amnf tāvatikā bought for such and such a sum.
tās |noun. pl. sā₂| ind. they.
tāsi nota. gram. modifier [vikaraṇa₂] of future stem formation | lṛṭ|.
ti (primary) form of action sf | [Nyāya] rather denotes the object resulting from the action | (num.) form of tens.
tikta [pp. tij] amnf tiktā amer — m. phil. [Nyāya] bitterness, a type of taste [rasa]; |Bṛhajjātaka| it is associated with the planet Mars.
tiktaka |ka| amnf tiktakā bitter — n. bitter substance — m. organic. bot. Terminalia catappa; cf. inguda.

tigmá [tijma] amnf tigmā pointed, sharp, keen (weapon, flame, ray of light) | acidic, pi quant, spicy, burning | violent, intense, passionate, rapid — m. myth. epith. of Indra's thunderbolt [vajra] — n. causticity.
tigmága [ga₁] amnf tigmagā vitece.
tigmáśrnga [śrnga] amnf tigmaśrngā with a pointed horn.

tin nota. gram. personal ending; conjugation suffix [pratyaya]. ekatin vākyam gram. the sentence has a single conjugated verb form. tvam pāsi hamsi tanuse manuse bibharsi vibhrājase srjasi samharase virausi | āsse nirasyasi sarasyasi rāsi lāsi sankrīdase vrudasi medhasi modase ca || [KM.] You protect, you strike, you extend, you think, you support, you shine, you create, you absorb, you howl, you sit, you destroy, you are passionate, you give, you take, you amuse yourself, you hide, and in the marrow (of the sacrificial victim) you rejoice.
tinanta [anta] n. gram. finite conjugated form of a verb; syn. kriyāpada; opp. subanta.
tinvibhakti [vibhakti] f. gram. personal ending.

√ tij v. [1] pr. r. (téjate) pp. (tikta) pf. (ut) to be acute, to be pointed — ca. (tejayati) pp. (tejita) to sharpen; excite, incite — dice. r. (titiksate) to desire to remain firm; endure — intense. r. (tetikte) sharpen | gr. ; lat. instinctus; all. stretch; eng. stick; fr. instinct, distinct, stigma.
tita_u mn véd. crible.
titikṣ [des. tij] v. pr. r. (titikṣate) to bear patiently, to endure.

Titikṣā [act. des. tij] f. endurance, patience phil. [Vedānta] longanimity, one of the 6 cardinal virtues | saṭsampad | myth. np. of Titikṣā, patience personified, daughter of Dharma, mother of Ksema. na titikṣāsamamasti sādhanam [Kir.] There is no virtue like patience.
titikṣu [agt. dés. tij] amnf enduring, patient.
titīrṣ [des. tṛ] v. pr. (titīrṣati) pr. r. (titīrṣate) to desire to cross.
titīrṣu [agt. dés. tr] amnf who wishes to cross.
tittirá [onomatopoeia] m. bio. partridge | var. Tittiri bio. id. | myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Tittiri "Per drix", student of Yāska, presumed founder of the taittirīya school.
tittirikalmāṣa | kalmāṣa | amnf tittirikalmāṣī with a spotted coat (horse).
Titha m. fire; time.
tithi [tithai] f. astr. lunar day, 30th part of a lunar month; there are 15 in each half

lunation [pakṣa]; the favorable days are nandā (1, 6 and 11), bhadrā (2, 7 and 12), vijayā (3, 8 and 13) and pūrņā (5, 10 and 15); the riktā days (4, 9 and 14) are unfavorable | the lunar day, an āyādi; syn. yoni | math. symb. the number 15 — f. tithī id.
tithikṣaya |kṣaya₂| mr. astr. new moon day.
tithitattva | tattva | n. bed. n.p. from the tithitattva of Raghunandana₁ Bhaṭṭācārya.

tilalipa [lipa] m. hist. np. from the Bengali pandita Ti lopa, born Prajñābhadra (988–1069); after his Vedic studies he became a Buddhist monk; he received the teachings of the Mahāmāyātantra and the texts of Nāgārjuna; after 12 years of hard practice he became an accomplished [mahāsiddha]; it is said that he received the Vajrayāna initiation directly from Vajradhara; he practiced tantrism with a yogini daughter of a sesame merchant, was expelled from his monastery, and became a miller himself in Udyāna, hence his epith. of tilalipa "sesame miller", popularized as Tilopa; SamantabhadraNāropa was his disciple.

tilottamā [uttama] f. myth. np. of the nymph [apsaras] tilottamā "Bellississie" ["whose beauty cannot be surpassed even by an iota"]; she was created by Viśvakarmā from the pretty parts of all things animate and inanimate, then fantasized by Pradhā, to create discord between Sunda and Upasunda so that they would kill each other; it is also said that Brahmā created her from diamond dust, hence her name of "(Made of) the best particles"; on the eve of her departure to Earth she bid farewell to the Devaloka, where she went around the gods to honor them; bewitched by her beauty, Shiva could not take his eyes off her, and four faces grew on him; Indra not having enough eyes to look at her, his face became covered with a thousand. বিলক tilaka [tilaka] m. bio. bot. Zanthoxylum armatum, Rutaceae shrub used in medicine | myth. np. of the Gandharva Tum buru "Dancing Drum"; he was the music and dance master of the nymphs [apsarasas]; his consort was Dundubhī; one day when the nymph Rambhā was dancing at Indra's court, Purūravā mocked her; Tumburu punished him by decreeing his separation from Urvaśī until he did penance; [Rām.] one day Kubera required him to bring Rambhā to him; Having failed within the allotted time, Kubera cursed him to be reborn like the rākṣasa Virādha; he would only be freed by the sword of Rāma.

turagabandha | bandha | m. Hamiltonian circuit of a knight on a chessboard; it is implied from verses 929 and 930 of the Pādukāsahasra, which can be obtained from one another by a permutation describing such a path; before him Ratnākara₂ had defined such a circuit in verses 145 and 146 of chapter 43 of his Haravijaya "Triumph of Śiva"; a Hamiltonian path of half a chessboard was already known from verse 15 of chapter 5 of Rudrata's Kāvyālankāra₂.

tulasī f. bio. bot. Ocymum sanctum, holy basil, white-flowered labiate; myth. it comes from the churning of the ocean of milk [kṣīrodamathana]; it is offered to Viṣṇu; syn. vṛndā; soc. the union of tulasī with śālagrāma is celebrated by the rite of tulasīśālagrāmavivāha at kārttikapūrņimā myth. np. tulasī, daughter of King Dharmadhvaja and Mādhavī, reincarnation of Lakṣmī; she did penances at Badarīnātha praying that she could marry Viṣṇu; Brahmā asked her to marry the asura Sankhacūda; When Shiva went to fight the asura, Vishnu manifested himself to her in his likeness, and asked her to return to Vaikuntha as Lakshmi, remaining on Earth in the form of the sacred ba silic.

tejolinga [linga] n. myth. the linga of Fire, the ar dente form of Shiva; [SP.] Brahma and Vishnu, discovering a pillar of Fire, decided to seek its ends, the former flying on his swan Hamsa, the latter plunging in the form of the boar Varaha; they could not, the pillar being infinite, and retraced their steps to meet; Brahma lied and declared that he had reached the summit, on the faith of the ketakī flower which claimed to descend from Shiva's head; Shiva revealed himself before them as Arunakaleshvara, emerging from the pillar of Fire [lingodbhava]; he granted each of them a wish; Brahma asked to have Shiva as a son; outraged by this audacity, Shiva decreed that he would not be the object of worship on Earth; Vishnu asked to be a servant at Shiva's feet; He thus obtained the ability to incarnate himself as Shakti.
