daṇḍakāṣṭha |kāṣṭha| n. soc. brah macārin stick.
daṇḍádhāra₁ |dhāra₁| amnf daṇḍadhārā who administers justice — m. king | myth. epith. of Yama.
daṇḍádhāraka |dhāraka| amnf daṇḍadhārikā who administers justice.
dandádhārana | dhārana | n. carrying of the scepter or staff | "administration of the staff" | punishment.
dandana |na| m. punishment.
dandanīti [nīti] f. administration of punishment maintenance of order; justice administered by the king political.
dandápāni [pāni] n. one who has the Scepter in hand; one who holds a stick — m. policeman. daņḍápāruṣya [pāruṣya] n. brutal punishment, severe justice.
daṇḍápāruṣyavat [vat] amfn dandapārusyavatī which inflicts a severe punishment.
dandápāla [pāla] m. soc. superintendent of punishments; executioner.
dandápranāma [pranāma] m. prostration face down on the ground as a sign of submission.
dandábhaya [bhaya] n. fear of the stick; fear of being punished.
dandábhāj [bhāj] amnf receiving punishment (by (g.)).

dandavat |vat| amnf dandavatī who carries a staff | equipped with a handle | stiff as a staff having a large army — adv. like a staff in a straight line. dandavat pranam to prostrate oneself face down (lying flat on the ground, arms outstretched and crossed at the wrists).
dandavadha [vadha] m. death penalty.
dandaviveka [viveka] m. bed. n.p. from Dandaviveka, a treatise on criminology by Vardhamāna₂.

dandānvaya [anvaya] m. gram. style of grammatical commentary at the structural level [vākyayojanā] using a prose translation with canonical constituent order; syn. an vayamukhī; opp. khaṇḍānvaya. ādau kartrpadam vācyam dvitīyādipadam tataḥ ktvātumunlyap ca madhye tu ante kriyāpadam 🗀 gram. [Samāsacakra] Starting with the agent, followed by accusative words and others, with absolutives and infinitives in the middle, and the verb at the end (definition of dandānvaya).
dandānvayapaddhati | paddhati | f. gram. naiyāyika method of grammatical analysis, where the subject of the sentence is considered first.
daṇḍāpūpa [apūpa] m. of the. stick and cake.

daṇḍāpūpanyāya [nyāya] m. lit. ("who can do the most can do the least") wisdom evoked by the example of the mouse, which, having eaten a stick, will surely eat a cake. daņdāsana |āsana| n. phil. |yoga| seated posture, legs extended on the floor, hands on either side of the body, fingers pointing forward.

daṇḍakā [f. daṇḍaka] f. geo. np. of the forest | araṇya | daṇḍakā, in the Deccan, between the Nar madā and the Godāvarī (mod. Madhya Pradesh); lit. [Rām.] Rāma lived there as a hermit during his exile with Sītā and Lakshmana.
dandakāranya [aranya] n. geo. the Dandakā forest.
dandakāvana [vana] n. geo. the Dandakā forest.
daṇḍanīya [pfp. [2] daṇḍa] amnf daṇḍanīyā which must be punished.
daṇḍādaṇḍi [red. daṇḍa] adv. stick against stick (in hand-to-hand combat).
daṇḍika [daṇḍaika] amnf daṇḍikā equipped with a stick.

daṇḍin [daṇḍain] amnf daṇḍinī who holds a staff; armed with a staff | who carries the scepter of justice; who carries the pilgrim's staff | brahmin at the 4th stage of ascetic life [sannyāsin] | mendicant order founded by Sankara₁; cf. daśanāmīdandin — m. myth. np. of Dandī "Justiciar", servant of Sūrya; he punishes sinners and defends divine justice | hist. np. of Daṇḍī₁, poet of the late 7th century, at the Pallava court of Kāñcī; he is the author of the prose adventure novel Daśakumāracarita; His treatise on literary composition, Kāvyādarśa, became an authority among poets, complementing Bhāmaha's Kāvyālamkāra₁; he is also the author of the kathā₁ Avantisundarī; he is renowned for his mastery of sandhi, morphology, and rhetoric, his long compounds, and his long sentences. Dandinah padalālityam [Rājaśekhara] Dandī₁ is the master of wordplay.
dát |related to danta| m. dent.

dattá [pp. dā₁] amnf dattā given, granted, provided, offered; received as a gift — n. gift, donation, present — m. soc. (Bengal) Datta title of physician [vaidya] — ifc. given by (iic.) | given to (iic.) | who has received, endowed with (iic.); form of the np. not. of vaisya — iic. to whom one has given (ifc.) | pali dinna. dattavadhyacihnah who bears the mark of the condemned.
dattávat |vat| amnf dattavatī who gave. sā taṇḍulān sūryātape dattavatī she exposed the rice to the sun.
dattásamjña [samjñā₁] amnf dattasamjñā to whom the name of was given.

dattātreya [ātreya] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of the sage | ṛṣi| Dattātreya "Born of Atri", son of Anasūyā as an incarnation | avatāra | of Viṣṇu; he became a sage from a young age near the Narmadā; he granted Arjuna₁ Kārtavīrya 1000 arms, and eternal youth to defend the dharma; he is considered the patron of scholars [pandita]; he is also called Guru Datta, and he is celebrated at gu rudvādaśī; his festival | jayantī| is at the Agrahāyaṇī; he has a shrine on the summit of Gurusikhara 15 km from Mt Abu; the Avadhūtagītā is attributed to him.
dattila m. hist. n.p. of dattila, expert in prosody and singing before the 7th century; he is the author of the Gāndharvavedasāra and the Yatyu padeśopanisad.
dattvā |abs. dā₁| ind. having given.
dad cf. dā₁.
dada | agt. dā₁ | ifc. amnf dadā who gives (iic.). dhanamdadā f. bd. goddess granting wealth.
dadat [ppr. dā₁] amnf dadatī by giving.
dadru m. bio. turtle — f. dadrū dermatosis; leprosy.
dadruka |ka| mr. dermatosis; leprosy.
dadhan [dhā₁] n. [sg. name. acc. dadhi, i. dadhnā, dat. dadhne, abl. g. dadhnas, loc. dadhni] curdled milk, little butter; yogurt || hi. dohi. dadhnā juhoti curd is given as an oblation.
dadhāna [ppr. mo. dhā₁] amnf dadhānā in holding, in carrying.
dadhi iic. dadhan.
dadhikrā [krā] m. ved. [RV.] np. of the celestial horse dadhikrā or Dadhikrāvā; it personifies the rising sun | var. dadhikrāvan id.
dadhipayas [payas] n. du. dadhipayasī milk and whey.

Dadhivāhana [vāhana] n. bd. np. from the Jātaka Dadhivāhana; a king cultivates a mango tree with whey to obtain sweet fruit; his gardener plants neem trees [nimba] around it so that its fruit becomes bitter; the king removes them and waters the tree with sweet water so that it bears sweet fruit again. dadhyac var. Dadhīca [ac] m. myth. Vedic np. of the sage | rṣi | Dadhyan "He who spreads the dadhi"; cf. dadhīci.
dadhyodana | odana | n. mixture of cooked rice and curdled milk.
dadhyonna [anna] n. id.

Dadhīca var. dadhīci [dadhiac] m. myth. ved. np. of the sage [rṣi] Dadhīca or dadhīci or Dadhyan "He who loves or spreads the dadhi", son of Bhṛgu |Mah.| or Atharvā [BP.]; he lived on the banks of the Sabar matī; Indra revealed to him mysteries which he was not to divulge under pain of having his head cut off; the Twin Horsemen |Aśvinau| gave him a horse's head, and he taught them to find the soma in the house of Tvașțā and to reconstitute the decapitated Makha sacrifice; when Indra cut off his head, the Aśvinau restored his original head; he gave the bones of his horse's head to Tvașțā to forge Indra's vajra which was used to kill Vrtra; He sacrifices himself for just causes; he is credited with the invention of honey; when Vișnu tried to attack him with Sudarśana, the latter lost its sharpness and became as harmless as a potter's wheel.
dadhṛṣ [red. dhṛṣ] amnf [nom. dadhṛk] audacious. dadhrk adv. ved. with audacity.
Danāyu | related to danu | f. myth. | ved. | np. of Danāyu, daughter of Dakṣa; she had as sons by Kaśyapa the demons | asura | Vala, Vikṣara₁, Vīra and Vrtra.

dánu |dānava| f. myth. np. of danu or Danū "Naiad", daughter of Dakṣa, mother of the undine demons | dānavās | by Kasyapa; she is a water deity; she is also called Danāyu, and is said to be the mother of Vṛtra — m. myth. np. of danu₁, epith. of the dānava ViśvāvasuKabandha.
danuja [ja] m. myth. ["from danu"] syn. dānava.
danta var. dat |daṃśta| m. tooth | elephant tusk | math. symb. the number 32 | lat. dens; ang. tooth; all. zahn; fr. dent.
dantakāra [kāra] m. ivory craftsman.
dantakāṣṭha [kāṣṭha] n. toothpick.
dantacchada [chada] m. lip ("That which covers the teeth") — f. dantacchadā epith. of the bimbā (whose red fruit is compared to lips).
dantajāhá [jāha] n. dental root.
dantadhāvana [dhāvana₂] n. brushing teeth.
Dantapura [pura] n. geo. np. of the holy city bd. Dantapura "city of the tooth (relic of the Buddha)", ancient capital of Kalinga; mod. Purī.

dantavakra [vakra] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the dānava dantavakra (or dantavakra), king of the karūṣās, friend of Śiśupāla; he opposed Krsna Who killed him with his club, causing his release, and ending the curse of the guardian of Vaikuntha Vijaya₁ that he had been in a previous existence.
dantavīṇā [vīṇā] f. noise made by clacking teeth. dantavīṇām vād to clatter teeth.
dantaharṣa [harṣa] amnf dantaharṣā That which irritates the teeth.
dantādanti [red. danta] adv. tooth against tooth (in combat).
danti iic. dantin.
dantidurga [durga] m. hist. np. of the king dantidurga, founder of the Rāṣṭrakūṭa dynasty (733–757); his son Kṛṣṇa₁ succeeded him.
dantin [dantain] mf dantinī ["Having tusks"] elephant | myth. epith. of Ganesa.
danturá [danta] amnf danturā with prominent teeth | jagged, irregular; ugly — v. [11] pr. (danturayati) to fill with (i.).
danturaka |aka| amnf danturikā having prominent teeth.
danturita [pp. dantura] amnf danturitā ifc. filled with, full of (iic.).
dantya [dantaya] amnf dantyā ["in the teeth" | dental — m. phon. dental phoneme. dantyosthya osthya amnf dantyosthya phon. dentalolabial (said of the semivowel v).
√ dabh var. dambh v. [1] pr. (dábhati) to deceive, to disappoint.
dabhrá var. dahara [dabhra] amnf dabhrā small, tiny; disappointing; deficient, puny — m. lit. the ocean.
dabhram adv. barely.

√ dam₁ v. [4] pr. (dāmyati) pp. (dānta) abs. (damitvā, dāntvā) to control, tame, discipline, subdue; to master, subdue, punish — ca. (damayati) id. || gr. δαμνημι; lat. domo; ang. to tame; all. zähmen; fr. dompter. dāmyata datta dayadhvam [BU.] Discipline yourselves, be charitable, have compassion.
dam₂ [dam₁] iic. ved. house.
dampati [pati] m. du. dampatī ["the two masters of the house" | the couple, husband and wife.

dáma [act. dam₁] mn house, dwelling self-mastery, self-control, mastery of one's passions | discipline, firmness; domination, taming; punishment | phil. [Vedānta] asceticism, including abstinence, one of the 6 cardinal virtues [satsampad] | myth. [Mah.] np. of Dama, son of King Bhīma₁ — ifc. He who tames, He who masters, He who controls (iic.) | gr. δομος; lat. domus; ang. to tame; german. zähmen; fr. dompter, domaine, domicile.
dámaghosa | ghosa | mr. myth. | Mah. | n.p. of Damaghosa, prince of the Cedayas, father of Sisupāla.
dámaghosaja [ja] m. myth. n.p. of Damaghosaja, epith. of Siśupāla "born of Damaghosa".
dámaghosasuta [suta₂] m. myth. of np. Damaghoṣasuta, epith. of Siśupāla “born of Damaghoşa”.

Damana [agt. dam₁] amnf damanī That which represses, that which subdues, that which prevails — m. tamer, coachman | bio. bot. Artemisia indica, Indian mugwort; it is used in medicine to control the vata and kapha humors; it is sacred to Shiva.
Nepal | myth. | Mah. | np. of the brahmarşi Damana; he allowed King Bhīma₁ to procreate | myth. |Mah.| np. of Damana₁, younger son of King Bhīma₁ — act. n. discipline; taming; repression, punishment.

damanaka [ka] m. lit. [PT.] np. of the jackal damanaka "Manipulator", advisor to the lion king Pingalaka₁; his bad influence prevails over the wise counsel of his brother Karataka. damanāropaņa |āropaṇa| n. SOC. np. of an initiation ceremony, the 12th day of the clear fortnight of the month caitra.

damayat [ppr. ca. dam₁] amnf da mayantī Who tames (not. her passions); Who dominates — f. damayantī myth. [Mah.] np. of the princess damayantī "Who dominates (in beauty all her rivals)", daughter of King Bhīma₁ of the country Vidarbha, of very great beauty; she married King Nala.
damin [agt. dam₁] amnf daminī Who controls, Who dominates.
dambh cf. dabh.
dambha [act. dabh] m. deception, fraud, hypocrisy myth. np. of dambha "Hypocrite", personifying deception, son of Adharma and Mṛṣā, father of Lobha by Pușți.
dambhin [agt. dabh] amnf dambhinī Who deceives — m. Hypocritical.
dambhitva [tva] n. deception, hypocrisy.
√ day v. [1] pr. r. (dayate) pp. (dayita) com to suffer; to share; to have pity on, to feel compassion for (acc. g.) | to feel sympathy or affection for (acc.); to love gr. δαιοω.

Dayā [act. day] f. compassion, Pity; Pity in verse (loc. g. iic.) myth. [BhP.] np. of Dayā "Pity", daughter of Daksa, one of the wives of Dharma | myth. np. of Dayā₁ "compassion", wife of Venkaṭa. dayām kr to take Pity on (loc. g.).

Dayānanda [ānanda] amnf dayānandā Who experiences the Joy of compassion | hist. np. of Dayānanda "Joy of compassion", name of renunciant; mod. not. the Svāmī Dayānanda₁ Saras vatī₂ (1824–1883), born in Gujarāt, Who founded the Hindu revival movement Aryasamāja in 1875; he is the author not. of the Satyārthaprakāśa; his master was the Svāmī Virajānanda Sarasvatī₂.
dayāvat [vat] amnf dayāvatī compassionate, merciful.
dayāvīra | vīra | mr. heroism of compassion.
Dayāśataka [śataka] n. lit. np. from the collection of devotional poems Dayāśataka by Vedāntadeśika, dedicated to Dayā₁ and Venkaṭa.
dayālu [dayālu] amnf compassionate, sympathetic, kind. hare dayālo | naḥ pāhi | | [SK.] O kind Hari, have mercy on us.
dayālutā |tā| f. compassion, Pity.
dayālutva [tva] n. id.
dayita [pp. day] amnf dayitā beloved, well-loved, cherished — m. beloved, spouse — f. cf. dayitā.
dayitā [f. dayita] f. beloved, wife.
dayitāmaya [maya] amnf dayitāmayī totally devoted to his beloved.
dara [agt. dr] amnf darā ifc. That which tears, That which splits, That which destroys (iic.) — act. m. cavity, cave,
cavern | conch; navel | fear — f. darī cavity, cavern.
darada n. vermilion — m. pl. geo. np. of the people of the Daradās, of the region of modern Peshāwar.
dáridra [agt. daridrā] amnf daridrā er rant; poor, needy — m. wretched; vaga bond, wandering beggar.
dáridratā [tā] f. indigence, shortage; state of being deprived of (iic.).
dáridratva [tva] n. id.
daridrā [intens. drā₁] intens. (dáridrāti) to be poor, to be miserable; to wander as a beggar. daridrāmcakara he became miserable.

Dardura [dṛura] m. ["He who breaks the ears"] frog | musical instrument; not. drum | cloud | geo. np. of the Dardura rock, near Mount Malaya — f. dardurā myth. epith. of Caṇḍikā “He who destroys demons”.
darp [ca. dṛp] v. [10] pr. (darpayati) to intoxicate, to make proud. 17
Darpa [act. dṛp] m. pride, vanity; arrogance, folly | myth. np. of Darpa, pride personified, son of Adharma.

Darpasāra [sāra] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Prince Darpasāra "Flow of Vanity", heir son of King Mānasāra; he entrusted the regency of Ujjayinī to his cousins Caṇḍavarmā and Dāruvarmā and went to do penance in the Himalayas.
darpādhmāta |ādhmāta| amnf darpādhmātā swollen with pride.
darpaṇa [agt. ca. dṛp] m. mirror [“that which renders vain”] — ifc. lit. form of book titles ["reflection on (i.e.)"] || pkt. dappaṇa. svamukham darpane paśya (ironic) look at yourself in the mirror!
darbhá [obj. dṛbh] m. soc. ved. sheaf of kuśa grass used in ritual; cf. prastara.
darbhavāhaṇa |vāhana| n. ved. cart of grass.
darbhaśara [śara] n. sg. (collective) of grass and reeds.
darbhānkūra [ankūra] m. blade of grass kuśa; syn. sūca.
dárvi [dru₃] f. ["wooden"] spoon, spatula; ladle | var. darvī id. darvī pākarasaṃ yathā [Mah.] Like a wooden spoon in soup (although immersed in it, it ignores the taste).
darvihoma | homa | m. ved. simple oblation of a ladle of boiled rice.
darś [ca. dṛś₁] v. [10] pr. (darśayati) to show, to display — ps. (darśyate) to be shown.
darśa [act. drś₁] m. ifc. vision of; look at, contemplation of — m. appearance (not. of the new moon) astr. new moon soc. rite celebrated at the new moon.

darśapūrṇamāsa [pūrṇamāsa] m. du. pūrṇamāsau the new moon and the full moon | soc. new and full moon ceremonies; [ChU.] clarified butter is poured into the fire dakṣiṇāgni to serve as food for the moon. idam aham anṛtāt satyam upaimi |SB.| (vow [vrata] pronounced by the sacrificer [yajamāna] at the beginning of the ritual) I, here and now, abandon falsehood to attain truth. idam aham ya evāsmi so'smi [SB.] (pronounced at the end of the ritual) I, here and now, become just who I am.

darśaka [agt. dṛś₁] amnf darśikā who sees, who looks; who seeks (iic.) | who shows, who clarifies — m. spectator | lit. [Svapnavāsavadatta] np. of the darśaka prince of Magadha, brother of Padmāvatī₂.
darśatá [darśata] amnf darśatā visible; to be seen; worthy of being seen.

darśana [act. dṛś₁] n. view, vision; aspect | visit; spectacle | soc. vision of the idol in the sanctuary of a temple | phil. method, doctrinal point of view, school of thought, philosophical system, doctrine of salvation; one distinguishes the schools ni

hilist [nāstika] and positivist [āstika] schools; cf. saddarśana | math. symb. the number 6 | soc. large flat earring identifying a nāthayogin || pali dassana. cārudarśana of pleasant appearance. punar darśanāya (adr.) goodbye.
darśanapatha | patha | mr. field of vision; syn. caksurvisaya, nayanapatha. mama darśanapathamāgataḥ he came into my sight.
darśanamārga [mārga] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] 3rd stage on the path of knowledge, where one sees reality directly; one acquires the title of Arya.
darśanīya [pfp. [2] dṛś₁] amnf darśanīyā visible; that which should be seen, that which deserves to be seen | pleasant to see, agreeable, pretty, beautiful.
darśin [agt. dṛś₁] ifc. amnf darśinī who sees, who looks, who observes, who examines (iic.); who understands, who knows (iic.).
√ , dal , v. , [1] , pr. , (dalati) , fut. , (dalisyati) , pp. , (da lita) pf. (ut, vi) to burst, to burst; to split, to open suddenly; to bloom.
dala [agt. dal] n. petal, leaf; bud, young shoot | fragment, piece, portion | math. half.
dalana [act. dal] n. bursting, rupture [action] of splitting, bursting, breaking; destruction.

dalita [pp. dal] amnf dalitā split, burst; open, blossomed (bud), burst (bour geon); unfolded, unfurled | broken, crushed; scattered, pulverized, destroyed, torn to pieces | to powder | mod. oppressed; qualifies the untouchables without reference to their caste (Ambedkar).
dalmi [dal] m. myth. weapon of Indra; syn. vajra.
dava [agt. du] m. fire, blaze; combustion; burn, heat; fever.
davadahana [dahana] m. forest fire.
davāgni | agni | m. fire, forest fire.
davathu [duathu] m. torment, vexation.
daviṣṭha [super. dūra] amnf daviṣṭhā the furthest.
davīyas [compar. dūra] amnf davīyasī further.
daśa |daśan| f. daśī ifc. which has ten (iic.) | (after num.) form of ordinals.
Daśaka |ka| amnf daśikā consisting of 10 components — n. ten, decade; category of 10 objects | lit. not. poem in 10 verses | lit. np. of the Daśaka, attributed to the sage Vyāghrapāda.
Daśakantha [kantha] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of Daśakantha, epith. of Rāvana "of the ten gorges" | thai thoskonth.

Daśakumāracarita | kumāracarita | n. lit. np. of the Daśakumāracarita "Adventures of the Ten Princes", novel of Adventures and Emancipation of Dandī₁; cf. Rājavāhana, Somadatta₂, Puspodbhava, Dhana mitra, Apahāravarmā, Upahāravarmā, Arthapāla, Pramati, Mitragupta, Mantragupta, and Viśruta.
daśakuśala [kuśala] n. bd. the 10 virtues according to Sāntarakṣita; opp. daśākuśala.
Daśagaṇī [gaṇa] f. gram. the ten classes of the present of the roots | lit. np. of the Daśagaṇī section of the Siddhāntakaumudī.
daśagītikā [gītikā] f. bed. n.p. of the daśagītikā, section of the Aryabhatīya.
daśaguṇa | guṇa | amnf daśaguṇā ten times; tenfold. daśagunam adv. ten times.

daśagrantha | grantha | mr. pl. bed. the ten books essential to Rgvedin: saṃhitā, brāhmaṇa, āraṇyaka, śikṣā, kalpa, vyākaraṇa, nighaṇṭu, nirukta, chandas and jyotiṣa; or the 4 Vedas and the 6 vedāṅgas.
daśagranthin [in] amnf daśagranthinī soc. refers to a brahmin who has studied the 4 Sciences |Veda| and the 6 related disciplines |vedānga|.

daśagrīva [grīvā] m. myth. [Rām.] np. from daśagrīva, epith. of Rāvaṇa "with ten heads". Daśagrīvarākṣasavadhacarita |rākṣasavadha carita n. bed. np of the Daśagrīvarākṣasavadhacarita, version of the rāmakathā at the end of the Agneyapurāṇa.
dáśataya [taya] amnf daśatayī in ten parts; by ten — n. ten — f. daśatayī pl. lit. the 10
collections [maṇḍala] of stanzas [rcas] from the Rigveda.
daśadhā [dhā] ind. 10 times | in 10 parts.
daśanāma [nāman] amnf daśanāmnī which has ten names.
daśapādī [padī] f. gram. formula of non-compositional primary affixes | unadi | in 10 sections; they are arranged by suffix of their formation, respecting the order of the older pañcapādī.

dasapura | pura | n. geo. np. of the city of Dasapura "Decapolis" in Mālava, (mod. Mandasor); it was the capital of King Rantideva; there is a column commemorating the victory of Yaśodharmā over Mihirakula in 528, and a temple of Pasupatinātha.
daśapuruṣam | puruṣa | adv. across generations.
daśapeya [peya] n. soc. solemn rite of drinking soma by a group of brahmins.
daśamá [ma] amnf daśamī ord. tenth — f. daśamī astr. the 10th day of a lunar fortnight; cf. vijayadaśamī, sāmbadaśamī. daśamyām putrasya soc. the son is named on the 10th day after birth.
daśamāṃśa [aṃśa] m. tithe.

daśamahāvidyā [mahāvidyā] f. phil. [kaula] the ten terrible aspects or cosmic powers of the Goddess [Šakti]: KālīKālikā, Tārā₁, Şoḍaśī (or Rājarājeśvarī), Bhuvaneśvarī, Bhairavī, Chin namastā (or CaṇḍīCaṇḍikā), Dhūmavatī, Va galā, Mātaṅgī, and KamalāSiddhilakṣmī; sometimes we also list Cāmuṇḍī, and TripurasundarīLalitā; these goddesses have sanctuaries not. in Kāmākhyā myth. n.p. of daśamahāvidyā, epith. of Durgā "of the ten great powers".
daśamūla [mūla] n. med. tonic preparation mixing the 5 large roots | bṛhatpañcamūla| and the 5 small roots [hrasvapañcamūla].

Daśaratha [ratha] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of Daśaratha "of the victorious chariot in the ten directions of space", king of Kosala, son of Aja of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa]; at the age of 60,000 years, despite his 3 wives, he had no heir; for his virtuous conduct he received a fertility porridge which he shared between his wives; his first wife Kausalyā received half of it, and gave birth to the eldest Rāma, incarnation [avatāra] of Viṣṇu; his second wife Sumitrā, who received a quarter and an eighth, gave birth to the twins Lakshmana and Satrughna; his third and favorite wife Kaikeyī, who received an eighth, gave birth to the youngest Bharata₁; In his old age he made Rama his heir; but his favorite Kaikeyī, reminding him of his old promise to fulfill a wish, forced him to bequeath the kingdom to her son Bharata₁, who would reign in Rama's name; Rama having gone into exile with his twin brothers and his wife Sita, Daśaratha died of
grief [putraśoka]; cf. Śravanakumāra | hist. np. of Daśaratha₁ Maurya, grandson of Aśoka whom [9 he succeeded, from 232 to 224; he patronized the materialist ascetics [ājīvika] of Bihar.

daśarātrá [rātra] amnf daśarātrā which lasts ten days — m. soc. period of ten days ending the Vedic year. | gavāmayana|; on the last day, the mahāvrata is celebrated; on the last night in the East, the atirātra.

daśarūpa | rūpa | amnf daśarūpā which has 10 aspects | myth. The 10 aspects of Viṣṇu; by extension, epithet of Viṣṇu "of the ten aspects" | lit. The 10 principal genres of literary composition; cf. daśarūpaka.
daśarūpāvaloka [avaloka] m. lit. np. from daśarūpāvaloka "Analysis of the ten dramatic genres"; cf. daśarūpaka.

daśarūpaka [rūpaka] n. lit. np. from the daśarūpaka "The Ten Dramatic Structures", a work of aesthetic rhetoric by Dhanañjaya₁; it discusses dramatic composition and narrative structure, not. the theory of the 5 articulations |pañcasandhi|; also called daśarūpāvaloka.
daśalakāra | lakāra | m. pl. gram. The 10 indicators of tense, aspect or mood of a verb.
daśalakṣa [lakṣa] num. n. pl. a million; syn. prayuta.
daśaśatī | śata | f. ten hundred.
Daśaślokī [śloka] f. bed. n.p. from the Daśaślokī of Śaṃkara₁; cf. Cidānandadaśaślokī.
daśasahasra [sahasra] num. n. pl. ten thousand.

daśaharā [hara] f. geo. ["she who removes the 10 sins"] epith. of the Gangā soc. festival in honor of the Gangā, on the 10th tithi of the clear fortnight of the month jyaistha | soc. np. of the festival of Dasaharā in honor of Durgā, on the 10th tithi of the clear fortnight of the month āśvina (mod. Dassera); cf. navarātra. śuklapaksasya daśamī jyesthe māsi dvijottamāh harate daśa pāpāni tasmād daśaharā smṛtā || The tenth (tithi) of the clear fortnight of the month of jyestha removes the 10 sins; That is why, O brahmins, she is known as daśaharā.
daśahotr [hotr] m. pl. daśahotāras ved. The 10 priests who sacrificed for Prajāpati (classic question of a ritual riddle [brahmodya]).
daśākuśala [akuśala] n. pl. bd. The 10 sins according to Sāntarakṣita; opp. daśakuśala.
daśākṣara [akṣara] amnf daśākṣarī consisting of 10 syllables.
daśākṣaramantra [mantra] n. mantra of 10 syllabes used not. for the vibhūtipañjaranyāsa (gopījanavallabhāya svāhā).
Daśānana |ānana| m. myth. |Rām.| np. of Daśānana, epith. of Rāvaṇa "of the ten mouths".
daśārṇa [arṇa] m. pl. geo. ["ten lakes"] np. of the country and people of the Daśārṇās, in the south-East of Madhyadeśa; cf. Hiranyavarmā.
daśārha [arha] m. pl. myth. [Mah.] np. of the Daśārhās, The 10 Meritors of the vṛṣṇi clan; Daśaratha Is one of them.

daśāvatāra [avatāra] m. myth. epith. of Viṣṇu "of the ten avatars" | pl. daśāvatārās myth. The ten incarnations of Viṣṇu: Matsya the Fish savior of the Veda, Kūrma the Tortoise, foundation of the world, Varāha the Boar, savior of the Earth, Narasimha the Lion-Man who destroys injustice, VāmanaTrivikrama the Dwarf with three cosmic strides, Parasurāma the Brahmin with the Axe, Rāma the Charming King, Krsna the Black Prince, Balarāma the White Prince and Kalkī the Horseman of the Apocalypse; sometimes Balarāma is replaced by Buddha | geo. np. of the daśāvatāra temple "of the ten avatars" (of Viṣṇu), from the Gupta period (5th century), in the pañcāyatana style; it is located in the fortified village of Deogarh (in the south of modern Uttar Pradesh).

Daśāvatāracarita [carita] n. lit. np. from the Daśāvatāracarita, work of Kṣemendra (1066); it describes in ten cantos The ten incarnations of Vișnu; the 9th describes the Buddha as personification of Kṛṣṇa.
Daśāśvamedha [aśvamedha] m. geo. np. of the quay [ghatta] Daśāśvamedha on the Ganges at Benares, so named because bathing at this spot is worth "10 sa horse crifices".
daśāsya |āsya| amnf daśāsyā which has 10 mouths — m. myth. np. of daśāsya, epith. of Rāvaṇa “with ten heads”.
daśāha [aha] m. ten days | soc. (10th day) festival of victory of Rāma over Rāvaṇa; it closes the festival of durgāpūjā; cf. navarātra, vijayadaśamī, āyudhapūjā || hi. daśāra.
daśaika [eka] amnf daśaikā pl. eleven.
daśaikādaśa [ekādaśan] n. ["eleven to the ten"] (loan) which yields ten percent.
daśaikādaśika |ika| amnf daśaikādaśikī | "who lends at ten percent" | usurer.
daśat [daśan] f. ten.
daśan num. pers. [sg. nom. acc. daśa; pl. other cases] the number ten || gr. ; lat. decem; ang. ten; all. zehn; fr. dix.
daśana [agt. daṃś] m. tooth; dentition.
daśanavasanāngarāga | vasana₂angarāga | m. the coloring of teeth and clothes, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.

daśanāmī [f. daśanāma] f. soc. order men diant śaiva founded by Śankara₁; at his initiation [dīkṣā] the renunciant receives a name among 10: Giri, Purī, Bhāratī, Vana, Parvata, Araņya, Sāgara, Tīrtha, Aśrama, Sarasvatī.
daśanāmīdaṇḍin [daṇḍin] m. soc. mendicant of the daśanāmī order.
daśanāmīsampradāya | sampradāya | mr. śaiva doctrine of the daśanāmī order.

daśā |act. daṃś| f. fringe of weft threads; lamp wick | (in fig.) condition, state, destiny; circumstance, age of life | astr. birth configuration in predictive astrology | jyotiṣa | ; cf. ulkā. nīcairgacchatyupari ca daśā cakranemikrameṇa Life has its ups and downs, like the rim of the wheel turns.
daśāpavitra | pavitra | n. ved. wool filter. daśāpavitreņa graham sammārṣṭi The ladle (at soma) is wiped with a wool filter.
daśin [daśain] amnf daśinī consisting of 10 parts.
daṣṭa |pp. daṃś| amnf daṣṭā bitten, stung.
√ das v. [4] pr. (dásyati) v. [1] pr. (dāsati) pft. (dadāsa) aor. [2] (ádasat) pp. (dastá) pf. (vi) to be in lack of; to be exhausted — ca. (dāsáyati) pp. (dāsita) to exhaust.
dasta |pp. das| amnf dastā exhausted.
dasyú [Persian] m. enemy of the gods, impious | savage, barbarian; thief, brigand, scoundrel; outcast, commoner; syn. dāsa.
dasyusāt |sāt| ind. given over to the barbarians (with kṛ₁, bhū₁). loko'yam dasyusādbhavet [Mah.] This country would be given over to the barbarians.
Dasra [dasra] m. myth. ved. np. of Dasra, an aśvin, physician of the gods | math. symb. the number 2.
dah₁ [agt. dah₁] ifc. amnf [nom. dhak] that burns (iic.); (iic.) burning. grāmadhak that burns the village.
dahat [ppr. dah₁] amnf dahantī ardent. dahannaiva diśo daśa myth. BhP. Burning in all directions (said of the fever that Shiva sent to Krishna, who sent him back a freezing fever |śīta|).

dahana |agt. dah₁| m. fire | myth. np. of Da hana "Burning", one of the 11 divine breaths |marut|; epithet of Agni | bio. bot. Plumbago indica, shrub with bright red flowers with 5 petals, used in medicine; syn. dāhaka — act. n. action of burning, combustion | myth. "burning of love", one of the 5 arrows
erotic [puṣpabāṇa] of Kāma — ifc. that which burns, that which consumes, that which calcines, that which destroys (iic.) | setting on fire of (iic.).

dahara var. dabhra amnf daharā small, thin; tiny | young — m. little brother; child; little animal tit. atha yad idam asmin brahmapure dahanam puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma | daharo'sminnantar ākāśaḥ | tasmin yad antas tad anvestavyam | | [ChU.] Well, in this citadel of Brahmā there is a little lotus, a receptacle; inside, there is a tiny space; one must look for what is inside.
daharādhikaraṇa [adhikaraṇa] n. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] "section on the minuscule space", hermeneutic controversy between Advaita Shaivism and Dvaita Shaivism.
√ dā₃ v. [1] pr. (dāyati) pp. (dāta) pf. (ava) [unused without pf.].

√ dā₁ v. [3] pr. (dadāti) pr. r. (date) imp. (dehi) v. [1] pr. (dádati) v. [2] pr. (dāti) was. (dāsyati) pft. (dadau) aor. [1] (adāt) aor. [3] (adīdadat) aor. [4] (adāsīt) pp. (datta) ppr. (dadat) pfp. (dātavya, dānīya, deya) abs. (dattvā, dāya) pf. (anu, abhi, ā, pari, pra, prati, sam) to give, grant, provide, offer something. (acc.) to sb. (dat. g. loc.) — ps. (dīyate) to be given — ca. (dāpayati) aor. [3] (adīdapat) to cause to be given, to cause to be paid, to recover — des. (ditsati) to want to give, to be ready to give | lat. do; fr. donner. agnīn dā to arrange the sacrificial fires. anuyātrām dā to accompany. argalam dā to draw the bolt. avakāśaṃ dā to make room, to let pass. ājñāṃ dā to give an order. ātmānam dā to sacrifice oneself | to devote oneself to, to dedicate oneself to (dat.). ^51 āsanam dā to give up one's place. rṇaṃ dā to pay one's debt. karnam dā to lend an ear; to listen. jānu dā to kneel | to put one's knee on the body. talam dā to slap. dandam dā to pay the fine | punish. dṛṣṭiṃ dā to glance. mano dā to fix one's mind on (loc.). mārgam dā to give way. vacam dā to say a word, speak. varam dā to bestow a gift. viśam dā to poison. śabdam dā to raise one's voice, call out. śokam dā to cause grief. samdeśam dā to give information, inform. samayam dā to propose an agreement, agree. prema bhikṣāṃ dehi Give us Divine Love as alms.

√ dā₂ v. [2] pr. (dāti) v. [4] pr. (dyati) pft. (da dau) aor. [1] (adāt) pp. (dita) pf. (ava, ni) divi ser, divide | cut; tear to pieces, rip, destroy | bind — ps. (dīyate) be rejected | lat. dae mon; fr. to strike, damage, condemn. deyāt that he divides.
dā fois (form of time adverbs).
dākṣa [*Dakṣa] amnf dākṣī myth. relating to Dakṣa | southern — mn the South.
dākṣāyaṇá [*Dakṣaāyana] amnf Dākṣāyaṇī myth. descendant of Dakṣa; relating to Dakṣa — f. Dākṣāyaṇī myth. np. of Dākṣāyaṇī "daughter of Dakṣa", epith. not. of Satī and of the nakṣatrāṇi; cf. Auṣadhī.
dākṣi [*Dakṣa] mf dākṣī₂ [gotra] descendant of Daksa.
dākṣiṇá [*dakṣiṇā] amnf dākṣiṇī soc. relating to the fees of the priest — f. dākṣiṇā geo. South India, the Deccan.

dākṣiṇātya [*dakṣiṇātya] amnf dākṣiṇātyā of the South, southern; not. from the Deccan | lit. [KM.] refers to the southern [rīti] style, with an abundance of secondary nominal derivatives [taddhitānta] | pl. inhabitants of the Deccan. priyataddhitā dākṣiṇātyāḥ [Patañjali₁] The South Indians are fond of secondary suffixes.
dākṣiṇya [*dakṣiṇāya] amnf dākṣiṇyā which concerns or which deserves the payment of ritual fees — n. dexterity, skill, address (in verse (loc. g. iic.) | politeness, consideration, piety.
dākṣya |*Dakṣaya| n. dexterity, skill, dexterity; ability; zeal.
dāḍima mf dāḍimī bio. bot. Punica grana tum, pomegranate — n. [dādimaphala] pomegranate. dāḍimāni daṃś ["to bite into a pomegranate"] to do a chore, to have an impossible task.
dādimaphala | phala | n. grenade.

dādimabīja [bīja] n. pomegranate seed. harinakharabhinnamattamātangakumbhamukta raktārdramuktāphalatvisi khanditāni dādimabījāni [K.] I crunched pomegranate seeds the color of red beads of blood released from the temples of furious elephants lacerated by the claws of lions.
dātavya [pfp. [3] dā₁] amnf dātavyā which must be given or offered.
dātṛ [agt. dā₁] amnf dātrī [sg. nom. dātā, acc. dātāram] who grants, who permits; who gives, who lends; liberal, generous; donor, patron, founder; lender, creditor — f. dātrī generous, donor.
dātrtva |tva| n. generosity.
dātra |instr. dā₂| n. knife; sickle. dātreņa lūnavān by cutting with the sickle. dātrākarņa [karņa] amnf dātrākarņī (cattle) with ears marked with a sickle.
dāda [dā₁] m. gift; present.
dādada |da| amnf dādadā who gives gifts.

dāná [act. dā₁] n. gift, the act of giving; generosity, liberality; charity; abandonment | bd. generosity, one of the 6 perfections |pāramitā| of an accomplished [bodhisattva] — obj. n. gift, present | communication, teaching | reimbursement | math. addition | bribe | [kanyādāna] soc. offering of one's daughter in marriage | [gajadāna] bio. ichor or fron taline, liquid exuding from the temples of the elephant in rut.
dānadharma [dharma] m. soc. duty of charity.
dānavīra [vīra] m. heroism of charity.
dānasāgara [sāgara] m. lit. np. from the dānasāgara "Ocean of gifts", compendium of rituals of the nation due to King Vallālasena (1168).
dānastuti [stuti] f. lit. [RV.] praise of gifts, not. from kings to brahmins.
dānāstakakathā [astakakathā₁] f. jn. np. of the dānāṣṭakakathā, śvetāmbara collection of eight stories about the gift.
dānin [in] amnf dāninī who Gives; generous.

dānavá [dānu] mf dānavī myth. ["son of Da nu" undine demon, variety of aquatic asura under the orders of Rāhu; cf. Vṛṣaparvā | pl. dānavās the class of these demons; they are sons of Kasyapa and Danu; Indra asked Dușmanta to fight them; cf. Vrtra | myth. cf. Danu₁.
dānavapati | pati | m. myth. np. of dānavapati, epith. of Rāhu "King of the dānavās".
dānīya [pfp. [2] dā₁] amnf dānīyā which must be given or offered.
dānu |agt. dā₁| amnf liberal | courageous; valiant, victorious, conquering — m. donor prosperity | wind, draft of air | water, current of fluid.
dāntá [pp. dam₁] amnf dāntā tamed, trained | who has tamed his passions | myth. [Mah.] np. of Dānta, son of King Bhīma₁.
dāp [ca. dā₁] v. [10] pr. (dāpayati) to make give, to make pay, to recover.
dāma iic. dāman₂.
dāmalipta | lipta | nf dāmaliptā geo. | DKC. | np. of the city of dāmalipta in the Suhma country.

Dāmodara | udara | m. myth. np. of Dāmodara, epith. of Kṛṣṇa as a child "tied by a rope around his waist" (by his nurse Yaśodā for his mischievousness) | hist. np. of Dāmodara₁ Bhaṭṭa, scholar of North India (late 16th century); to him is the author of the Yantracintāmaņi and the Kalivarjyavinirņaya | lit. np. of the young vidyādhara prince Dāmodara₂, supported by Vișnu, adversary of Sūryaprabha.
dāmodaragupta [gupta] m. hist. np. of dāmodaragupta, poet and prime minister of the King of Kaśmīra Jayāpīda (late 8th century); he is the author of the satire of manners Kuṭṭanīmata.
dāmodarāṣṭaka |aṣṭaka| n. soc. festival celebrating KṛṣṇaDāmodara, on the 8th day of the month kārttika; cf. gopāstamī.
dāman₁ |dā₁man| m. giver; generous man.
dāman₂ [dā₂man] n. bond, rope, restraint; belt | garland; necklace, rosary — f. dāmnī ifc. (after num.) tied by (num.) cords. dvidāmnī tied by two cords.
dāya₁ | agt. dā₁ | amnf dāyā ifc. who gives (iic.) — act. m. gift, present | soc. dowry; gift to the master after studies.
dāya₂ [act. dā₂] m. portion, part; share of inheritance | division; destruction — ifc. division into (iic.) parts.
dāyábhāga | bhāga | m. soc. division of an inheritance | lit. Hindu treatise on inheritance.
dāyabhāgaprabodhinī | prabodhinī | f. lit. np. of the dāyabhāgaprabodhinī "Manual of Inheritance Law" by Srīkṛṣṇa Trakālankāra, commentary on the preceding.
Dayavibhāga | vibhāga | mr. bed. n.p. of the Dāyavibhāga, chapter on the transmission of the heritage of the Mānavadharmaśāstra.
dāyādá [āda] m. heir (of (g. loc iic.)) — f. dāyādā heiress — f. dāyādī id.
dāyādya [ya] n. inheritance.
dāyaka [agt. dā₁] amnf dāyikā that gives; that grants — ifc. that causes, that permits, that affects (iic.).
dāyi iic. dāyin.
dāyitva [tva] n. donor status.
dāyin [agt. dā₁] ifc. amnf dāyinī that gives, that grants, that communicates (iic.) | that abandons, that yields, that permits (iic.). dāyīkṛ to make a gift.
dāra [instr. dr] m. wife (rare) | pl. dārās (collective) The wives; (arbitrary gender and number) the wife. darān kṛ var. darānprakṛ to take as a wife, to marry.
dāraka [ka] m. young son, boy | du. dārakau boy and girl — f. dārikā girl.
dārakācārya |ācārya| m. schoolteacher.
dāragava [gava] n. the wife and the cows. dāraguņa [guṇa] m. the virtue of the wife. kim grhinah priyahitāya | dāraguṇāh | | [DKC.] What pleases the master of the house? The qualities of the wife.

dāridrya [*daridraya] n. poverty. bho dāridrya namastubhyam siddho 'ham tvat prasādatah | paśyāmyaham jagatsarvam na mām paśyati kaścana | O poverty, glory to you! By your grace I have acquired magical powers: I see the whole world, but no one sees me!
dāru var. dru₃ [dr̄u] mn wood; piece of wood; post | bio. deodar cedar.
dārubrahmā [brahman] m. myth. np. of Dārubrahmā, epith. of Jagannātha "the God of wood".
dārumaya |maya| amnf dārumayī in wood. dārumayī pratimā wooden idol.
dāruvarman [varman] m. bed. [DKC.] np. of Dāruvarmā, brutal younger brother of Caṇḍavarmā; he tried to seduce Bālacandrikā, and was killed by Puspodbhava.
dāruśilā [śilā] f. wood and stone.
dāruśilāgrahaṇa | grahaṇa | n. soc. criteria for selecting materials intended for sacred images.
dāruka [dāruka] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of dāruka, driver of Kṛṣṇa's chariot — n. organic. bot. Cedrus deodara, Himalayan cedar — f. dārukā wooden doll.
dārukavana | vana | n. myth. np. of the dārukavana cedar forest, where many er lived

mites [rsi]; they were infatuated with their Vedic rituals and worshipped only Sabdabrahma; Shiva visited the hermitage as a naked beggar in his Bhikṣāṭana form, to humiliate these heretics; the wives of the sages fell in love with his great beauty; the sages wanted to make him disappear, and made a tiger appear, which he killed and whose skin he adorned himself with; they made a deer appear, which he took in his left hand as an attribute; they produced a red-hot iron, which he kept in his hand as a weapon; an elephant demon [gajāsura] named Gaya₁, having acquired great powers through his penances, made the sages flee to Vārāṇasī, where they took refuge in a temple of Shiva; He killed the demon-elephant with his trident, and adorned himself with its carcass as with a cloak.
dāruņa [*dr̄una] amnf dāruņā f. dāruņī hard, rough; severe, implacable; intense; cruel, violent | painful, distressing; frightening, terrible, dreadful — n. hardness, roughness, severity; horror.
dārdhya [*dṛḍhaya] amnf dārḍhyā soli dité, resistance; stability.
dārteya [*dṛtiīya] amnf dārteyā which is found in a wineskin.
dārdurika [*darduraika] amnf dārdurikā which makes a drum-like noise.
dārva [*dāru] amnf dārvī in wood.
dāva [agt. du] amnf dāvā that burns | forest, park — act. m. fire, not. of a forest.
√ dās₁ v. [1] pr. (dāsati) pft. (dadāsa) ved. to honor a god (acc. dat.) with (i.) | ved. to give, to grant to (dat.) — ca. (dāśayati) to offer, to give.
dās₁ [act. dās₁] f. soc. ved. cult, veneration — agt. m. soc. devout.
Dāsa |dās₁| m. recipient (to whom one gives) fisherman; boatman; cf. Dāsa.
dāśaratha [*daśaratha] amnf dāśarathā relating to daśaratha — m. myth. n.p. of dāśaratha, patr. of Rama.
dāśarathi [*daśarathai] m. myth. descendant of daśaratha | patr. of Rāma or Lakṣmaṇa of. dāśarathī Rāma and Laksmana.

dāśarājña [*daśarājan] m. ved. “(battle) of the 10 kings”, won by King Sudāsa, chief of the Bharatās tribe, with the help of Rṣi Vasiṣṭha; these kings led 5 Aryan tribes and 5 non-Aryan tribes respectively; the battle took place near the Paruṣṇī River; it gave the Bharatās sovereignty over Kurukșetra.
dāsas [g. dās₁] iic.
dāśaspati [pati] m. soc. ["master of offerings"] great donor.
dāśaspatya [a] amnf dāśaspatyā prolific; not. good milk producer (cow).
dāśvás [dāś₂vas] amnf dāśvasī ved. devout, pious — m. ved. qualifies different gods.

Dāsa [related to dasyu] m. slave, servant | fisherman | soc. ["servant of god"] np. of Dāsa, fixed suf of the name of renunciants of the devotional current [bhakti] of the vaiṣṇava tradition — f. cf. dāsī.
dāsakarmakara [karmakara] m. pl. soc. serfs and free workers.
dāsarāja | rāja | m. myth. | Mah. | np. of dāsarāja, "chief of the fishermen" of the Yamunā, who raised Sa tyavatī and gave her in marriage to King Sāṃtanu.
dāsya [ya] n. slavery, servitude.
dāsita [pp. ca. das] amnf dāsitā exhausted.
dāsī [f. Dāsa] f. female slave, servant | fisherman's wife.
dāsīka |ka| n. suite of servants.
kvacitpragītadāsīkam | KSS. | there sang servants.
dāsīputra | putra | m. son of a servant, bastard (in jure).
dāsīmāṇavaka [māṇavaka] n. (collective) the servants and the children.
dāsīsuta [suta₂] m. id.
dāsyās |g. dāsī| iic. dāsyāḥputra var. dāsīputra | putra | m. son of a ser vante, bastard (insult).
dāha [act. dah₁] m. fire; burning.
dāhaka [agt. dah₁] amnf dāhikā that burns, that sets on fire — m. bio. bot. Plumbago indica, ar bust with bright red flowers with 5 petals, used in medicine; syn. dahana.
dāhin [agt. dah₁] amnf dāhinī that burns, that sets on fire | that torments.
dāhya [pfp. [1] dah₁] amnf dāhyā to burn; combustible.
dik iic. diś₂.
dikkarin | karin | mr. myth. elephant of car dinal points; syn. diggaja.
dikcakra [cakra] n. ["circle of the orients"] horizon.

dikpāla | pāla | m. myth. deity governing one of the 8 directions of space: Indra (or Sūrya) in the East, VahniAgni in the Southeast, Yama in the South, Nirṛti₁ (or Sūrya) in the Southwest, Varuņa in the West, Pavana Vāyu in the Northwest, Kubera (or Rudra) in the North, and IśaIśāna (or SomaCandra) in the Northeast; each of them is associated with a diggaja; syn. lokapāla bd. epith. of Avalokiteśvara.
dig iic. diś₂.
diganta [anta] m. horizon; the distance.
digambara | ambara | amnf digambarā jn. nu ["clothed in sky"], epith. of the Jain sect of the digam barās, whose monks live naked; opp. śvetāmbara.

diggaja |gaja| m. myth. mythical elephant supporting the world at one of the cardinal points: Airāvata in the East, Pundarīka₁ in the Southeast, Vāmana₁ in the South, Kumuda in the Southwest, Añjana in the West, Puṣpadanta₁ in the Northwest, Sārvabhauma in the North, and Supratīka₁ in the Northeast; each of them is associated with its dikpāla; cf. diśāgaja and gajapati for other lists.
digjaya | jaya | m. complete conquest | "in all directions".
digbhāga | bhāga | m. direction, cardinal point. prāguttaradigbhāge in the direction of the Northeast.
digbhrama [bhrama] m. disorientation; loss of way; syn. dinmoha.
digvāsa [vāsa₂] amnf digvāsā ["clothed in sky"] naked.

digvijaya [vijaya] m. total victory ["all azi muts"]; tour of conquests | lit. np. of the Digvi jaya, work of Sankarācārya describing his victory over other sects | title of a section of the Mahābhārata.
digvrata | vrata | n. jn. observance of limitation of activity, a meritorious vow [gunavrata].
digdha [pp. dih] amnf digdhā coated, anointed; soiled, smeared, poisoned.
dignāga cf. dinnāga.
din iic. diś₂.

Dinnāga [nāga] m. myth. syn. diggaja | bd. np. of Dinnāga or Dignāga, Buddhist religious figure and philosopher of the 56th century (480-540), born in Kāncīpura, disciple of Vasubandhu; he headed the university of Nālandā where he founded a school of logic [Nyāya]; he refuted Vātsyāyana₂; he is the author, notably, of the Pramāṇasamuccaya, the Hetucakraḍamaru, the Nyāyamukha, and the Traikālyaparīkṣā; he professed that the meaning of language was made up of concepts, abstract constructs independent of reality
objective |apohavāda|, and developed the notion of constructive force of reason [vikalpavāsanā]; this Buddhist nominalism was refuted by Kumārila, but defended by Jayanta₁.
dinmārga [mārga] m. path going far (in one direction) | pl. dinmārgās paths in all directions.
dinmoha | moha | m. disorientation; syn. digbh rama.
Dinka m. bio. lice lice lice.
dita [pp. dā₂] amnf ditā divided, torn.
Diti [act. dā₂] f. myth. np. of Diti "Division", daughter of Dakṣa and mother of the daityās by Kaśyapa; she was killed by Indra.
dits [des. dā₁] v. pr. (ditsati) pp. (ditsita) to want to give, to be ready to give.
ditsā [act. des. dā₁] f. intention to give.
ditsu [agt. dés. dā₁] amnf desirous of giving or sacrificing.
didṛkṣ [des. dṛś₁] v. pr. (didṛkṣati) to wish to see — pr. r. (didṛkṣate) to hope to see, to desire.
didṛkṣā [act. des. dṛś₁] f. phil. desire to see.
didṛkṣu [agt. dés. dṛś₁] amnf phil. who wishes to examine.
didyu m. ved. weapon, arrow, missile.
didhiṣ [des. dā₁] v. pr. (didhiṣati) to want to give — pr. r. (didhişate) to want to obtain.

didhiṣú [agt. des. dā₁] amnf didhiṣū who seeks to obtain — m. courtier, suitor; lover; 2ᵉ husband — f. var. didhiṣū widow remarried elder sister married after her younger sister younger sister married before the elder.
dina [div] n. day, daytime || lat. dies; fr. quo tidien. dine dine adv. day by day, every day; tou jours. pratidinam adv. each day, daily.
Dinakara [kara₁] m. the Sun ["that makes the day"] myth. np. of Dinakara, the Sun, epith. of Sūrya — f. dinakarī lit. np. of the dinakarī, commentary on the Siddhāntamuktāvalī.
dinakrt [krt₂] m. the Sun ["that makes the day"].
dínapati [pati] m. Sun ["master of the day"].
dinayāminī [yāminī] f. du. dinayāminyau day and night.
dinānta | anta | m. evening.
dinārdha [ardha] m. midday; half-day.
dineśa [īśa] m. Sun ["master of the day"].
dineśvara [īśvara] m. Sun ["master of the day"].
Dilīpa₁ [dillipa₂] m. myth. np. of King Dilīpa₁ "Protector of Delhi", son of Amsuman of the lineage

solar [sūryavaṃśa], father of Bhagīratha | myth. np. of King Dilīpa₁, epith. of King Khaṭvāṅga of the solar lineage | sūryavamśa|, descendant of Aśmaka₁ and therefore of the previous one; |Raghuvamsa| he had visited Indra at Svarga, but on the return he neglected to honor SurabhīKāmadhenu, who cursed him with sterility; he went with his wife Sudakṣiṇā to the hermitage of Vasistha to take care of his calf Nandinī; Surabhī tested him with the illusion of a lion to which he offered his life to save that of Nandinī; gaining Surabhī's forgiveness, he obtained Raghu as a son.

div [agt. dīv₁] m. [sg. nom. dyaus, acc. divam, i. divā, dat. dive, abl. g. divas, loc. divi; pl. nom. divas dyāvas, acc. divas, i. dyubhis ved. sky myth. np. of Dyau, the sky. Personified Light, a Treasure [vasu]; cf. dyaus — mn day — f. sky || gr. Z epsilon v sigma; lat. diu; fr. diurne, god. divā adv. of day, during the day. dyauḥ pitā m. myth. [Jupiter] Father sky. rātriṃdivam adv. night and day.
divá [agt. dīv₁] n. iic. sky; Light, day. divedive every day, daily.
divaukas [oka] m. ["who lives in heaven"] god; planet var. divaukasa id.
divah [g. div] iic.

Divodāsa₁ [dāsa] m. ved. np. of the sage |rājarṣi| Di vodāsa "Servant of Heaven", king of Kāśī, son of Bhīmaratha; [RV.] he was imprisoned by Sambara, whose fortresses he destroyed with the help of Indra; [SkP.] Shiva had granted Divodāsa₁ to rule in Kāśī; when he wanted to rule there himself, he sought to restrict his dharma in order to supplant it; the gods he sent (Sūrya, Brahmā, etc.) did not succeed; only Viṣṇu succeeded, disguised as a Buddhist monk, because Buddhist doctrine disorganized the kingdom which Divodāsa₁ eventually abandoned; cf. Nikumbha for another version; he married Mādhavī, by whom he had a son Pratardana, for the price of 200 śyāmakarṇāśva in Gālava; renowned for his hospitality, he was called Atithigva | hist. [RV.] np. of King Divodāsa₁, king of the Bharatās, father of King Sudāsa.
divasa [divasa] mn day, daytime. ekasmin divase adv. one day, once upon a time. pratidivasam adv. every day, every day. anudivasam adv. each day. divasīkṛ to change night into day.
divasīya [īya] ifc. amnf divasīyā relating to a period of (num. iic.) days.
divaseśvara [īśvara] m. the Sun.
divā [i. div] adv. of day; opp. naktam | daily | day.
dívākará [kara₁] m. the Sun ["that makes the day"]; cf. niśākara | hist. np. of the mātanga Divākara, esteemed poet of the court of King Harşa.
Divākarasuta |suta₂| m. myth. np. of Divākarasuta, epith. of Śani "son of the Sun" — f. divākarasutā myth. np. of divākarasutā, epith. of the Yamunā "daughter of the Sun".
divākīrtya | kīrtya | amnf divākīrtyā to be recited during the day.
divākṛta |kṛta| amnf divākṛtā made during the day.
divātana [tana] amnf divātanī of the day.
divānaktam | nakta| adv. night and day.
divānidrā | nidrā₂ | f. siesta.
divāniśam [niśa] adv. night and day.
dívāndha [andha] amnf divāndhā blinded by the day — m. bio. owl.
dívāmanya [manya] amnf divāmanyā (night) that pretends to be day.
divārātram [rātra] adv. night and day.
divādi [(dīv₁)ādi] m. gram. ["which begins with dīv₁"] qualifies the fourth class [gaṇa] of the present tense of verbs; its characteristic marker [vikarana₂] is śyan .
divi m. bio. zoo. blue jay.
divya [divya] amnf divya divine, celestial; opp. manusya | marvelous, magical; splendid, radiant — m. celestial being | divine year — n. divine judgment; the divine world | the divine.
divyaksetra | ksetra | n. sacred land.
divyáGangā [Gangā] f. myth. celestial river; [Mah.] 7 are listed: Nalinī, Pāvanī, Sarasvatī₁, Jambu, Sītā, Gangā and Sindhu.
divyácaksus [caksus] n. divine vision — amnf divyacakṣuṣī who has divine vision.
divyádrsti [drsti] f. divine vision; syn. divyacaksus.
divyadeśa | deśa | m. Vaishnava shrine, notably in South India; 108 are reputed to be venerated by the 12 Tamil poet-saints |alvar|.

divyaprabandha | prabandha | m. soc. ritual recitation of the Vaishnava devotional hymns — n. lit. np. of the Divyaprabandha, corpus of devotional songs of the tradition of the Tamil saints ālvār, collected by Nāthamuni.
divyarūpa [rūpa] amnf divyarūpā of divine beauty.
divyarūpin |in| amnf divyarūpinī id.
divyaviṣaya [viṣaya] m. phil. the set of 5 subtle elements or perceptions |tanmātra|.
divyānganā | anganā | f. cf. apsaras.
divyāvadāna |avadāna₂| n. lit. np. of the divyāvadāna "Divine Exploits", bd. collection from Nepal; it dates from around the 2nd century.

√ dis₁ v. [6] pr. (disati) fut. (deksyati) pft. (dideśa) aor. [3] (adīdiśat) aor. [7] (adikṣat) pp. (diṣṭa) inf. (diṣṭum) pfp. (deṣṭavya, deśya) abs. (diṣṭvā, diśya) pf. (apa, ā, ut, upa, ni, nis, pra, sam) to show, to make visible; to indicate | to exhibit, to produce; to demonstrate; to produce (a witness) | to make an offer; to pay (tribute) — ps. (diśyate) to be shown — ca. (deśayati) to show, to make visible; to expound, to explain, to teach; to communicate; to confess — des. (didikṣati) to want to show; to be willing to show lat. dico, index; all. zeigen; fr. afficher, index. śriyam diś to bring fortune.

diś₂ [agt. diś₁] f. [nom. dik; en comp. dik, dig, din direction, sense, cardinal point; region, quarter of the sky; place, location; sky, space | phil. space, one of the 9 substances | dravya₁ | of the Vaiseka | pl. Diśas the heavens; the horizon, the distant, mythical space. the 6 Disas or directions of space, personifying the 4 cardinal points: prācī the East, dakṣiṇā the South, pratīcī the West and udīcī the North, plus ūrdhvā the zenith and dhruvā the here | phil. [Sāṃkhya] these directions are regent [niyantr] of the sense of hearing |śrotra|. caturdisam adv. in the four directions. anudisam adv. in all directions. diśi diśi adv. in all directions, from all sides. diso disas adv. here and there. diso prayā to spread out in all directions. iti dik this is the general direction (said notably by a pandita after giving instructions on a technical point).
diśā [obj. diś₁] f. direction, cardinal point; region | one of the 10 directions of space (with ūrdhva and adhara) | math. symb. the number 10.

diśāgaja [gaja] m. myth. [Rām.] mythical elephant supporting the world at one of the cardinal points: Virūpākṣa₂ in the East, Mahāpadma in the South, Saumanasa in the West, and Bhadra in the North; they die at Rasātala; cf. diggaja for another list. বিষ্ট dista [pp. diś₁] amnf diṣṭā shown, indicated; fixed, determined; mentioned, explained — n. assigned place, purpose; indication, instruction, order | destiny, fate. diṣṭā gatiḥ ["at the appointed time"] death.

disti [act. diś₁] f. indication, instruction, prescription | destiny, fortune, chance | fr. destin. distyā adv. by chance, fortunately; thank God, thank God. distyā vrdh to congratulate (for (i.)). distyā vardhase congratulations! be congratulated! good luck! (wish of prosperity ["be favored by fortune"). sutamukhadarśanenāyuṣmānvardhate distyā congratulations on the birth of a son.

√ dih v. [2] pr. (dégdhi) aor. [3] (adīdihat) aor. [7] (adhikṣat) pp. (digdha) pf. (pra, sam) to coat, anoint | to soil, defile, pollute | to increase; to accumulate — ps. (dihyate) to be coated, to be soiled — ca. (dehayati) to cause to be coated or soiled | lat. fingo; all. Teig; ang. dough.
√ dīkṣ v. [1] pr. r. (dīkṣate) pp. (dīkṣita) to be initiated, to be consecrated; to prepare for a religious ceremony — ca. (dīkṣayati) to consecrate; to consecrate (king).
dīkṣaṇa [act. dīkṣ] n. consecration; initiation; execution of the dīkṣā.

dīkṣā [act. ca. dīkṣ] f. soc. preliminary observances to sacrifice, consecration of the sacrificer; religious observance | soc. initiation; investiture of the sacred cord; rite in general | religious conversion | exclusive occupation; intensive preparation (not. for battle).
dīkṣāguru [guru] m. master who initiates (opp. śikṣāguru, who teaches).
dīkṣādarśa [ādarśa] m. bed. n.p. of the dīkṣādarśa, work of Vedajñāna.
dīksāmandala [mandala] mn soc. ritual diagram of three concentric circles, bearing the symbols of the zodiac, drawn on the altar by the master for Vaishnava initiation.

dīkṣita [pp. dīkṣ] amnf dīkṣitā consecrated, initiated (to (dat. i. iic.)); prepared — m. ved. patron of a solemn sacrifice [yajamāna] | soc. designates certain Shivaite Brahmins, not. the priests of the Națarāja shrine (Cidambara temple, Tamil Nadu) soc. n.p. from dīkṣita, title of scholar in grammar; cf. Nāgoji, Nīlakaṇṭha₂, Bhaṭṭoji, Hari₁.

Dīdhiti [red. dhīti] f. religious reflection, devotion, inspiration | lit. np. of the Dīdhiti, commentary by Raghunātha₁ Siromani of the Khandanakhandakhādya of Srīharşa | light, splendor; ray of light.
pīyūṣadīdhitiḥ [Murāri] the moon star “with rays of nectar”.
dīna amnf dīnā sad, dejected, depressed; desolate, afflicted, miserable; poor; ruined; unhappy, lamentable | timid, frightened. dīnam adv. sadly.
dīnavrajyā [vrajyā] f. lit. ["wandering of the disinherited"] category of verse in anthologies.
dīnāra m. gold coin (of variable value depending on the era) | lat. denarius.

√, q, pr, v. [4] pr. r. (dī pyate) pft. (didī pe) aor. [3] (adidīpat) aor. [5] (adīpiṣṭa) aor. p.s. (adīpi) pp. (dīpta) pf. (ā, ut, pra, sam) to shine, to shine, to be Luminous; burn, flame, blaze — ca. (dīpayati) to illuminate, to illuminate — intense. r. (dedīpyate) to shine; shine permanently; be excessively bright.

dīpa [agt. dīp] m. light, brightness; lamp, dim light; torch, beacon. dīpād dīpāntaram yathā like a lamp lit from another lamp. dīpakarņi [karņin] n. lit. [KSS.] np. of King Dīpakarņi, without an heir; he saw Shiva in a dream telling him to go into the forest to find a boy chasing a lion who would become his son; the lion was the yakṣa Sāta punished for having sinned with the daughter of a sage; the king named the boy Sātavāhana and adopted him.
dīpamālā [mālā] f. illumination (by a string of lamps).
dīpalakṣmī [Lakṣmī] f. statuette of a woman carrying an oil lamp.
dīpaśikhā [śikhā] f. lamp flame.

Dīpāvali [āvali] f. illumination (by a row of lamps) | soc. festival of Dīpāvali "Festival of Light", celebrated for 4 days from the eve of the new moon of kārttika [caturdaśi]; it celebrates the victory of Kṛṣṇa over the asura Naraka | narakacaturdaśī|, evoked by a fireworks display, the triumphant return of Rāma with Sītā to Ayodhyā after his victory over Rāvaṇa, and the visit of Lakṣmī anticipating the awakening of Vișnu from his 4-month sleep, 12 days later; it begins at dhan vantaritrayodaśī, celebrating the advent of Lakṣmī and Dhanvantari during the kṣīrodamathana; on the second day, at the new moon [amāvāsyā], we celebrate

Lakṣmī [lakṣmīpūjā]; it also celebrates the victory of Vișnu over the tyrant Bali, relegated to the underworld; the third day commemorates the annual return to Earth for one day of King Bali, people rise before dawn [brahmamuhūrta], forget enmities, and in the evening lamps are lit everywhere to dispel darkness and ignorance; it also celebrates go vardhanapūjā; on the fourth day the sisters invite their brothers to their homes |yamadvitīya| || hi. dīvali.
dīpoddīpana [uddīpana] n. mod. ceremony of lighting the lamp, as a prelude to a scholarly meeting.
Dīpaka [agt. dīp] amnf dīpikā Luminous; that illuminates, that lights up; that inflames — m. lamp, light | myth. np. of Dīpaka "Luminous", son of Garuḍa — f. cf. dīpikā.

dīpana [agt. dīp] amnf dīpanī that kindles the fire, that ignites | that stimulates; that aids digestion — act. n. ignition, setting alight | med. tonic; digestive. kopodīpanāya alam this will serve to provoke his anger.

dīpikā [f. Dīpaka] f. lamp, lantern; torch; light | lit. exegesis; ifc. title of works of exegesis | lit. poetic figure |alaṃkāra| where the syntactic parallelism highlights the similarity |rūpaka| between the upameya and the upamāna.
dīpikādhāriṇī [dhāriṇī] f. lamp bearer.
dīpita [pp. dīp] amnf dīpitā burning, in flames; bright, luminous, illuminated; flamboyant, resplendent | agitated, excited, ardent.
dīpitṛ [agt. dīp] amnf dīpitrī that illuminates; luminaire.
dīpin [agt. dīp] amnf dīpinī that kindles the fire, that kindles; that excites.
dīpta [pp. dīp] amnf dīptā burning, in flames; bright, luminous, illuminated; flamboyant, resplendent | agitated, excited, ardent | exposed to the sun.
dīptarasa [rasa] amnf dīptarasā lit. which develops a brilliant aesthetic experience.
dīptarasatva [tva] n. lit. [Vāmana₃] splendor of poetic style.
Dīptāgama [āgama] m. lit. np. of the Dīptāgama, Shaivite treatise [śaivasiddhānta] of rituals of consecration of images, iconography, and sacred architecture.
dīpti [act. dīp] f. brilliance, radiance; splendor, beauty.
dīptimat [mat] amnf dīptimatī brilliant; splendid | myth. n.p. of Dīptimān, son of Kṛṣṇa.
dīpra [dīpra] amnf dīprā that shines; that blazes — m. fire. agnidīpramgeham the house was on fire.

dīrghá amnf dīrghā long, elongated, extended (space or time) | phon. (vowel or syllable) long; opp. hrasva — acc. dīrgham adv. long time, far || gr. δολιχος. dīrghīkṛ to lengthen, prolong. dīrghībhū to lengthen. dīrghībhāva m. gram. lengthening (vowel). dīrghībhūta amn gram. lengthened (vowel).

dīrghakaṇtha [kaṇtha] amnf dīrghakaṇthī long-necked — m. myth. np. of the dānava Dīrghakaṇṭha "long-necked". dīrghakarņa [karṇa] amnf dīrghakarṇī long-eared — m. lit. [Hit.] np. of the cat Dīrghakarna.
dīrghakāya [kāya] amnf dīrghakāyā | "with an outstretched body" | large; giant.
dīrghakāla | kāla₁ | m. long period of time. dīrghakālam adv. for a long time.

dīrghajihva [jihvā] m. serpent ["who has a long tongue"] — f. dīrghajihvī myth. [JB.] np. of the rākṣasī dīrghajihvī "with the long tongue", with the many vaginas | yoni | ; Indra gave Sumitra the corresponding penises, so that he could kill her while they were united.
dīrghatapas [tapas] m. myth. np. of Dīrghatapā "who did a long asceticism (to obtain an heir)", epith. of King Dhanvā, son of Kāśa; his son is Dhanvantari₁.

dīrghatamas [tamas] m. myth. ved. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Dīrghatamā "who sees far in the darkness", son of Utathya and Mamatā, born blind by the curse of Brhaspati trying to rape his mother when he was already conceived; his mother abandoned him in the forest, the gods gathered him up and gave him to King Bharata who named him his heir Vitatha, making him a kṣatriya; he married Pradveṣī, and Gautama is one of their sons; he grew into a vicious and odious old man, was banished by his wife and children, and sent on a raft into the Ganges; King Bali recognized him and asked him to father intelligent sons for his queen Sudeṣṇā; The queen, not liking this decrepit old man, took advantage of his blindness to have herself replaced by a wet nurse, who bore him Kakṣīvān and ten other sons, all great scholars; the king, having learned of the super-darling, asked the queen to comply, and she bore him five sons, Anga₁, Vanga, Kalinga₁, Pundra and Sunga, who founded the eponymous kingdoms; [Bṛhaddevatā] the gods restored his sight and he is thus "he who remained long in darkness"; cf. Bharadvāja₁ | lit. author of the cryptic hymns 140 to 164 of the first mandala of the RV.

dīrghadarśin [darśin] amnf dīrghadarśinī who sees far — m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Dīrghadarśī, mi nistre of king Yaśaḥketu; he takes leave of the king to make pilgrimages; on going to Suvarṇadvīpa he spots the beautiful Mṛgāṅkavatī; on his return, the king disguised as an ascetic went in search of her.
dīrghábāhu [bāhu] amnf who has long arms. dīrghavarņa [varņa] m. phon. long vowel.
dīrgháśriga [śriga] amnf dīrghaśrigī which has long horns.
dīrghásūtra [sūtra] amnf dīrghasūtrā [“who unwinds a long thread” procrastinator; dilatory.
dīrghásūtrin [in] amnf dīrghasūtriņī who procrastinates, who procrastinates. dīrghasūtrī vinašyati the indecisive runs to his ruin.
dīrghāgama [āgama] n. bd. sacred text bd. dīrghāyus var. dīrghāyusa [āyus] amnf who lives long — m. myth. np. of Dīrghāyu, epith. of Mārkandeya "the Eternal".
dīrghatama [super. dīrgha] amnf Dīrghatamā furthest away; syn. drāghiṣṭha.
dīrghatara [compar. dīrgha] amnf dīrghatarī further away; syn. drāghīyas.
dīrghikā [dīrghaika] f. pond or elongated lake; water point, well. dīrghikāvalokanagavākṣagatā sitting at the window overlooking the well.
dīrṇa [pp. dṛ] amnf dīrṇā split, cracked,
torn | scattered (army) | frightened.
dīrṇāṅga [aṅga₁] m. epith. of the planet Saturn "with the dispersed body".
dīv₁ [act. dīv₁] f. ved. game (not. dice bet). pratidīvnā by the opponent in the game.

√ dīv₁ v. [4] pr. (dīvyati) pr. r. (dīvyate) pft. (dideva) pp. (dyūtá) to play, to have fun; to make fun of (acc.) | to bet, to play for gain, to wager (g. dat. i.) | to shine, to gleam | to be joyful; to be drunk — ca. (devayati) to make shine — dés. (didevișati) dés. (dudyūṣati) to want to bet. dīvyāva let's both play. akşair dīvyati var. akṣān dīvyati to play dice. akṣairmā dīvya One must not play dice.

√ of v. |5| pr. (dunóti) ps. (dūyate) pp. (duta, dūna) pf. (pra) to burn, consume; to be afflicted, to suffer, to be consumed with grief | to afflict, to torment someone (acc.) — ca. (dāvayati) to burn, to torture — des. (dudūṣati) to want to suffer. sacetasas kasya mano na dūyate what man of heart would not have a tormented mind?

duḥkhá [duskha] amnf duḥkhā painful, disagreeable, distressing; difficult, awkward | "whose axle turns with difficulty" | — n. misfortune, evil; suffering, pain, sorrow (opp. sukha) | phil. |Vaisesika| the property | guna | of suffering | phil. |Sāṃkhya| suffering, categorized into its three causes; cf. duḥkhatraya — v. [11] pr. (duḥkhīyati) to be unhappy — v. [11] pr. (duḥkhyati) to cause pain — v. [11] pr. r. (duḥkhāyate) to experience pain, to be unhappy. duhkhena var. duskhena with pain; painful ment. duḥkhaduḥkhena with great difficulty. duhkham kr to afflict, to sadden, to cause pain. sarvam duḥkham bd. (1ᵉ Noble Truth [āryasatya]) All is suffering.
duḥkhákara |kara₁| amnf duḥkhakarī that causes pain (to (g.)), that afflicts.

destiny [ādhidaivika], or by our body or mind [ādhyātmika]; syn. tāpatraya.
duḥkhaprāya [prāya] amnf duḥkhaprāyā sub mergé de douleur.
duḥkhabahula [bahula] amnf duḥkhabahulā overwhelmed with pain.
duḥkhabhāj [bhāj] amnf unfortunate.
duḥkhavighāta [vighāta] m. phil. [Sāṃkhya] pain relief.
duḥkhaviśrāma [viśrāma] m. relief of pain. duḥkhaviśrāmam to ease the pain.
duḥkhākula [ākula] amnf duḥkhākulā led astray by grief.
duḥkhānarha [anarha] amnf duḥkhānarhā who does not deserve to suffer | unaccustomed to suffering France. duhkhānarham sukhocitam unaccustomed to hardship and accustomed to comfort.
duḥkhānubhava | anubhava | m. feeling of suffering; pain.
duḥkhānta [anta] m. phil. state of liberation, considered as the end of suffering.
duḥkhārta |rta| amnf duḥkhārtā overwhelmed with grief.
duḥkhālaya |ālaya| m. the world, here below | "the valley of tears".
duḥkhita [pp. duḥkha] amnf duḥkhitā afflicted, dejected.
duḥkhin [duḥkhain] amnf duḥkhinī af fligé, soiné.
duḥśaka |dusśaka₃| amnf duḥśakā im possible.
duḥśakatva [tva] n. impossibility.

Duḥśala [dusśala] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Duhśala, "evil spear", one of the 100 sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, killed by Bhīma — f. duḥśalā myth. [Mah.] np. of duḥśalā, only daughter of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, wife of Jayadratha.

duḥśāsana [dusśāsana] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of duḥśāsana "Bad advice", one of the 100 sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; he insulted Draupadī by undoing the braid of his hair |veṇīsaṃhāra|; Bhīma killed him to fulfill his vow to drink his blood — n. Bad teaching.
duḥṣanta cf. duṣyanta. ব্ৰঃ duḥṣṭhu [dusstha] amnf who behaves badly; opp. susthu — adv. badly, in a bad way.
duḥsaṃdhāna var. duḥsandhāna [dus saṃdhāna amnf duḥsaṃdhānā difficult to counter; difficult to gather.
duḥsampāda [dussampāda] amnf duḥsampādā difficult to obtain.
duḥsaha [dussaha₁] amnf duḥsahā unbearable.
duhsādhya [dussādhya] amnf duhsādhyā difficult to accomplish | difficult to achieve; difficult to cure; difficult to conquer.
duḥsūta [dussūta₂] m. Bad chariot driver.
duḥstha [dusstha] amnf duḥsthā in bad condition; opp. sustha.
duḥsthita [dussthita] amnf duḥsthitā in a bad situation.
duḥsparśa [dussparśa] amnf duḥsparśā painful to the touch — m. bio. bot. Sola num xanthocarpum, small spiny solanaceous; syn. kantakāra.
duḥspṛṣṭa [dusspṛṣṭa] m. phone. im perfect contact.
duḥsmara |dussmara| amnf duḥsmarā whose memory is painful.
duḥsvapna |dussvapna| m. bad dream. বুকুল dukūla n. silk fabric; muslin; fine garment.
dukūlapaṭṭa | paṭṭa | m. silk strip for tying a turban.
dugūla n. cf. dukūla.
dugdhá |pp. duh₁| amnf dugdhā draw, drawn (milk) | extract, sucked, exhausted, emptied — n. milk; milky juice.
dugdhadoha [doha] amnf dugdhadohā trait, from which milk was drawn.
dugdhaphenī | phena | f. organic. bot. Taraxacum officinale, dandelion.
dugdhin |dugdhain| amnf dugdhinī which has milk; milky — n. bio. calcite.
dugdhodadhi [udadhi| mr. myth. primordial ocean of milk; syn. kṣīroda .
dugha |agt. duh₁| amnf dughā ifc. that which milks | that which gives (like milk); that which grants — f. dúghā dairy cow.
duṇḍuka amnf duṇḍukā fraudulent; malicious.
duṇḍubha m. organic. lizard | duṇḍubhi id.
duta |pp. du | amnf dutā burned, consumed; afflicted, desolate.
dundubha var. duṇḍubha m. organic. water snake, non-venomous.

dundubhí [onomatopoeia] f. mus. bass drum — m. myth. |Rām.| np. of dundubhi, giant buffalo asura, son of Maya and Hemā; Shiva having given him great powers, his pride knew no bounds, and he fought all those he met; on the edge of the ocean he provoked Varuṇa, who sent him to Himavān; the latter sent him to the kingdom of the king of the monkeys Vālī, who defeated him thanks to the power of a golden necklace that Indra had given him; the fight lasted for a whole year in the cave Kişkindhā; when the blood of dundubhi gushed out of the cave, Sugrīva, believing his brother dead, walled up the entrance with a large stone, provoking the anger of Vālī; a little of dundubhi's blood fell on Matanga's hermitage, provoking the latter's anger, who cursed his superior to die if he came to Rsyamūka; Sugrīva took refuge there. astr. np. of dundubhi₁ "Irascible", personifying the 56th year of a life cycle [samvatsara] | lit. [KSS.] np. of dundubhi₂, king of the genies [yakṣās]; Mada namañjarī is his daughter — f. dundubhī myth. [Mah.] np. of the gandharvī dundubhī, companion of Tum buru; On Brahmā’s instructions, she incarnated on Earth as the hunchback Mantharā in order to incite Kaikeyī’s jealousy, to provoke Rāma’s exile, and finally to trigger the war that caused Rāvana’s death.
dundubhilepa | lepa | m. paste for coating drums for magical purposes.
duratikrama [dusatikrama] amnf of the ratikramā difficult to overcome. svabhāvo duratikramaḥ it is impossible to change its nature.
duratyaya [dusatyaya] amnf duratyayā inaccessible | unfathomable.
duranvaya [dusanvaya] amnf duranvayā difficult to accomplish, to find or to imagine — m. gram. faulty agreement | [logic] erroneous deduction.
durāgama [dusāgama] amnf durāgamā difficult to approach; unintelligible — m. illegitimate gain.
durācāra [dusācāra] m. bad conduct — amnf durācārā unbeliever, wicked; impious — m. lit. np. of durācāra "Rogue", pupil of the beggar Viśvanagara in the Dhūrtasamāgama.
duratman [dusatman] amnf
durātmanī ["of an evil nature"] bad, wicked, criminal; opp. mahātman.
durādharṣa [dusādharṣa] amnf durādharṣā unassailable, invincible; dangerous arrogant — m. white mustard.
durāpa [dusāpa₁] amnf durāpā difficult to obtain; inaccessible.
durāroha [dusāroha] amnf durārohā difficult to climb — m. palm tree — f. durārohā kapok tree; syn. śālmala.

durāśaya |dusāśaya| amnf durāśayā wicked, ill-intentioned. durāśayam adv. in a bad sense. tasya vacasi durāśayam mā kalpaya var. tasya va casi durāśayam mā āropaya do not take his pa roles in a bad sense.
durāsada |dusāsad| amnf durāsadā ["difficult to encounter"] unheard of.

duritá [dusita] n. difficulty; hazard; evil, sin — amnf duritā difficile; wrong; bad. kṣipto hastāvalagnah prasabham abhihato 'py ādadāno 'mśukāntam grhņan keśeṣv apāstaś carananipatito neksitah sambhramena | ālingan yo 'vadhūtas tripurayuvatibhih sāśrunetrotpalābhih kāmīvārdrāparādhah sa dahatu duritam śāmbhavo vaḥ śarāgniḥ | [Bāṇa₂] The young women of Tri pura, with lotus eyes filled with tears, repel the fire of Sambhu's arrow as they would a lover eager to be forgiven; though rejected, he takes their hand; though violently struck, he grasps the edge of their sari; though pushed aside, he seizes them by the hair; though ignored, he stretches out at their feet; though pushed back, he embraces them; may this fire of Shiva consume your sins.

durukta [dusukta] amnf duruktā badly said, badly pronounced | bad word, hurtful or insulting remark, defamation, lie — f. duruktī myth. np. of duruktī, Insult personified, daughter of Krodha and Himsā.
duruta [dusuta₂] amnf durutā poorly woven fig. ill-bred, uncultured.
duruttara [dusuttara₂] amnf duruttarā difficult to cross.
durūha |dusūha| amnf durūhā difficult to understand.
durūhaka [ka] amnf durūhakā id.
dureva [duseva] amnf durevā malevolent; criminal.

durga [dusga₁] amnf durgā of difficult access, inaccessible, impenetrable, unapproachable — mn difficult, dangerous passage; fortress, citadel, stronghold | Difficulty, obstacle, danger, calamity, distress — f. cf. durgā.
durgata [dusgata] amnf durgatā poor, needy.
durgati [dusgati] f. misfortune, misery, distress, poverty; difficult situation | lack of ⟨g.⟩.
durgandha [dusgandha] amnf dur gandhā stinking, foul-smelling — m. bad smell, stench.
durgama [dusgama] amnf durgamā difficult to traverse; unattainable, inaccessible incomprehensible — mn difficult situation.

durgā [f. durga] f. myth. np. of durgā "the Inalienable", epith. of the Goddess, śakti of Śiva; the lion Manastāla is her mount; she killed the asurabuffol Mahişa with the weapons of all the gods combined; she killed the brothers Sumbha and Nisumbha with the divine wrath Kālī that came out of her forehead; cf. Annapūrņā, Am bikā, Astabhujā, Adyā, Irāvatī, Iśvarī, Umā, Kālī, Gaurī, Candī, Cāmundā, Tripurasundarī, Tvaritā, Daśamahāvidyā, Devī, Dhūmavatī, Pārvatī, Bha drakālī, Mātaigī, Mātā, Lalitā, Sakti, Sākaṃbharī.
Durgāparameśvarī | parameśvarī | f. myth. Durgā as supreme deity.
durgāparameśvarīstotra [stotra] n. bed. n.p. from durgāparameśvarīstotra; cf. Durgāstuti.
durgāpūjā [pūjā] f. cf. navarātra.
Durgāmbā [ambā] f. myth. np. of Durgāmbā "Mother Durgā".
Durgāstuti [stuti] f. lit. np. of the Durgāstuti, poem by Kṛṣṇalīlāśuka; it is recited to ask for the protection of the Goddess.
durgraha [dusgraha] m. spasm, cramp | obstinacy in, insistence on (loc.); stubbornness; monomania, addiction — amnf durgrahā difficult to grasp; difficult to achieve, accomplish or understand.
durgrāhya [dusgrāhya] amnf durgrāhyā difficult to grasp; difficult to attain, to accomplish or to understand.
durgrāhyatva [tva] n. Difficulty in grasping or understanding.

Durghața [dusghața] amnf Durghațā difficult to accomplish; difficult to reconcile. Durghațavrtti [vrtti] f. lit. np. of the Durghațavrtti "Morphological Difficulties", work by Saranadeva discussing problematic grammatically correct usages visàre de Pāṇini (1172); this catalogue of disputes between grammarians adopts a question-and-answer style setting out the various points of view.
durjana [dusjana] amnf durjanī wicked, vile, evil — m. wicked man, odious person; the wicked one.
durjanatā [tā] f. wickedness.
durjanatva [tva] n. wickedness.
durjaya [dusjaya] amnf durjayā invin target — m. myth. n.p. from the asura durjaya “Invincible”; he killed Kuśa in battle.
durjāta [dusjāta] amnf durjātā malchan those; miserable | bad, false — n. misfortune, adversity; calamity | maladjustment. durjatabandhuh a friend in need.
Durjñeya [dusjñeya] amnf durjñeyā in comprendre — m. myth. np. of Durjñeya, epith. of Shiva "Unknowable".
durṇāman [dusnāman] amnf durṇāmnī who has an ugly name.
Durdama [dusdama] amnf durdamā difficult to master; indomitable — m. myth. [HV.] np. of Prince Durdama, son of Vasudeva and Rohiņī₃.
durdarśa [dusdarśa] amnf durdarśā difficult to see, difficult to encounter | whose sight is painful.
durdaśā [dusdaśā] f. misfortune, distress, misery; calamity.
durdaśāpanna [panna] amnf durdaśāpannā fallen into misfortune; fallen into misery.

durdānta [dusdānta] amnf durdāntā indomptable — m. lit. [Hit.] np. of the lion durdānta; a hare made him believe in a rival lion by showing him its reflection at the bottom of a well, and caused his downfall.
durdina [dusdina] n. rainy day, stormy day; bad weather — amnf durdinā rainy, wet, dark — v. [11] pr. r. (dur dināyate) to start to rain, to become overcast (weather).
durdaiva [dusdaiva] n. bad luck, in fortune.
durdaivavat [vat] amnf durdaivavatī infor tuné.
durdhara [dusdhara] amnf durd harā difficult to bear | irresistible; inevitable; inescapable; inexorable | gram. (suffix) necessary — m. mercury | myth. np. of durdhara, demon ally of Mahisa.
durdharma [dusdharma] amnf durd harmā of bad morals.
durdharsa [dusdharsa] amnf durdharsā inaccessible, inviolable; dangerous, horrible haughty, distant — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Durdharșa, one of the 100 sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
durdhī [dusdhī₂] amnf ["mal penser"] weak-minded | ill-intentioned, wicked.
durnaya [dusnaya] m. bad conduct; imprudence.
durnāman [dusnāman] amnf durnāmnī who has an ugly name; syn. durṇāman
durnimitta [dusnimitta] n. bad omen.
durnirīkṣaṇa [dusnirīkṣaṇa] amnf durnirīkṣaṇā difficult to observe.
durnirīkṣya [dusnirīkṣya] amnf dur nirīksyā difficult to observe.
durnivāra [dusnivāra] amnf durnivārā difficult to contain; irrepressible.
durnivāratā [tā] f. irrepressibility.

durbala [dusbala] amnf durbalā weak, puny; sickly, ill, impotent | frail, thin, emaciated; precarious. durbalībhū to become weak or ineffective. aśvam naiva gajam naiva vyāghram naiva ca naiva ca | ajāputram balim dadyād devo durbalaghātakah [Cāṇakya] One must not sacrifice the horse, the elephant, or especially the tiger, but only the kid to God who kills the weak.

Durbalācārya |ācārya| m. hist. np. of the philosopher Durbalācārya (early 19th century); he is notably credited with the Tattvamīmāmsā; he is also the author of the Kuñcikā, commentary on the Vaiyākaraņasiddhāntamañjūṣā; also called Krsnamitrācārya.
durbuddhi [dusbuddhi] amnf fool, stupid; weak-minded, imbecile — f. ignorance; stupidity.
durbodha [dusbodha] amnf durbodhā incomprehensible, unfathomable.
durbhāgya [dusbhāgya₁] amnf durbhāgyā unlucky; unfortunate — n. misfortune.

durbhāvanā [dusbhāvanā] f. evil thought, evil inclination — m. durbhāvana ifc. vicious. devaranyāyadurbhāvanāparatantrah lit. [Bhīmeśvarapurāṇa] vicious practitioner of illicit levirate marriage (imprecation of SivaViśvanātha to Vyāsa).
durbhikṣa [dusbhikṣā] n. famine; misery. durbhiksam adv. in times of famine.
durbhida [dusbhidā] amnf durbhidā difficult to destroy.
durmangala [dusmangala] amnf durmangalī which brings bad luck.
Durmati [dusmati] amnf insane — m. astr. np. of Durmati "Senile", personifying the 55th year of a life cycle [samvatsara].
durmanas [dusmanas] amnf sad, sorrowful, ill-disposed — n. bad mood, melancholy.
durmanastā [tā] f. sadness; opp. sumanastā || pali domanassa.
durmitriya [dusmitriya] amnf durmi triyā unfriendly.

Durmukha [dusmukha] amnf durmukhī ugly-faced | rude-speaking; insulting — m. astr. np. of Durmukha "Rude", personifying year 30 of a life cycle [samvatsara] | myth. np. of Durmukha₁, horrible demon allied with Mahişa.
durmedha [dusmedha] amnf durmedhā stupid; ignorant; cretin — amnf durmedhas id.

duryodhana [dusyodhana] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of duryodhana "the Invincible", eldest son of King Dhrtarāstra and Gāndhārī, commander-in-chief of the Kauravās army; he embodies the kaliyuga; he insulted and mistreated Draupadī, dragging her by the hair; after the battle he hid in Lake Dvaipāyana₂ to rest; he was killed in single combat with a club by Bhīma; his son Lakṣmaṇa₁ was killed by Abhimanyu; cf. Suyodhana.
durlanghya [duslanghya] amnf durlanghyā difficult to overcome or transgress; insurmountable.

durlabha [duslabha] amnf durlabhā inac transferable; unfindable, rare, extraordinary | difficult to find; difficult to (inf.) || pkt. dullaha. durlabhībhū become inaccessible. bodhidurlabha jn. rarity of supreme knowledge, a circumspect canonical instruction [anuprekṣā]. durlabham bhārate janma It is a great fortune to have been born in India.
durlabhatama |tama| amnf durlabhatamā great. the rarest; extremely rare.
durlabhatara [tara] amnf durlabhatarā com par. more rare; very rare.
durlabhatā [tā] f. rarity.
durlabhatva [tva] n. id.
durlalita [duslalita] amnf durlalitā (en fant) spoiled, badly behaved; rascal, rogue.
durvaca [dusvaca] amnf durvacā who speaks Bad | difficult to pronounce or explain — n. in insult, injury; bad words.
durvacana [dusvacana] n. pl. bad words; oaths, insults.
durvacas [dusvacas] n. id. — amnf who speaks maliciously; who swears or insults.
durvācaka [dusvācaka] m. pun.
durvācakayoga [yoga] m. the art of wordplay, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
durvārttā [dusvārttā] f. bad news durvārtā id.
