durvāsa [dusvāsa₂] amnf Durvāsā Ill-dressed — m. var. durvāsas myth. np. of the irascible sage [ṛṣi] Durvāsā "the Ill-dressed"; he is the son of Atri and Anasūyā as an incarnation of Shiva; his nature is intolerance [akṣānti]; he is green and swarthy, emaciated, has a long beard, is dressed in rags; he curses those who insult him; [Mah.] as a reward for his patience and hospitality, he gave Kunti a mantra having the power to invoke the gods to conceive; He gave Krishna the rest of his rice gruel to cover his body with as protection, and blessed him, saying that he could not fear death from the coated parts, but "that he should have covered the soles of his feet with it," prophesying his death by Jarā₂'s arrow; for not having been received with respect at Kanva's hermitage, he cursed Duşyanta with amnesia, causing his tragic misunderstanding with Sakuntalā; he performed the sacrifice for Svetaki; [VP.] he cursed Indra, full of pride in his riches, who had scorned the garland of heavenly jasmine [pārijāta] that he had offered him; all the wonders disappeared into the ocean, including Lakṣmī, only to return to the churning of the primordial Ocean |kṣīrodamathana|; He visited Pitrloka, and was surprised by the cries of pain emanating from Pitrtīrtha; Yama told him that it was hell where the wicked were tormented; he asked to visit it, and the ashes covering his body transformed it into paradise.
durvidagdha [dusvidagdha] amnf dur vidagdhā narrow-minded, stupid — m. false scholar.

Durvinīta [dusvinīta] amnf durvinītā undisciplined, ill-bred; brutal; rebellious — m. hist. np. of Durvinīta "Rebellious", who fought his younger brother favored by their father Avinita and became king of the Ganga dynasty of Karṇāṭa in 529; his capital was Talakadu on the Kāverī; one of his daughters married Pu lakeśī₂ and gave birth to Vikramāditya₁.
durvipāka [dusvipāka] m. unfortunate result, harmful consequence — amnf durvipākā that has bad consequences. aho dāruņo daivadurvipākah alas! the harmful consequences of fate are terrible.
durvivaktṛ [dusvivaktṛ] amnf durvi vaktrī bad referee.
durvṛtta [dusvṛtta] amnf durvṛttā wicked, vicious — m. the wicked one.
durhṛd [dushṛd] amnf hard-hearted; wicked — m. enemy.
duścara [duscara] amnf duścarā difficult to perform or to cross | that moves with difficulty | that behaves badly.
duścaratva [tva] n. difficulty to perform.
duścarita [duscarita] n. bad conduct; sin | pl. bd. the 10 deadly sins: murder, theft, adultery, lying, slander, obscenity, wickedness, covetousness, jealousy, heresy.
duścarman [duscarman] m. leper.
duścarmaka [ka] n. leprosy.
duścintya [duscintya] amnf duścintyā difficult to understand.
duśceṣṭā [dusceṣṭā] f. bad conduct, bad action.
duścheda [duscheda] amnf duśchedā difficult to decide.
duśchedatā [tā] f. difficulty in deciding.
√ duș v. [4] pr. (dușyati) pp. (dușța) pf. (anu, pra, vi, sam) to spoil; to be bad, corrupt, impure, contaminated, ruined | to sin, to make a mistake, to be wrong — ca. (dūṣayati) cf. dūṣ.
duṣkara [duskara₁] amnf duṣkarā difficult to do, arduous — n. difficulty.
duṣkaraṇa [duskaraṇa] n. arduous work; drudgery.
duṣkarman [duskarman] n. sin; arduous task — amnf duṣkarmaṇī wicked, criminal. ব্ৰুজুল duṣkula [duskula] n. bad family; low birth.
duṣkṛta |duskṛta| amnf duṣkṛtā who acts badly, guilty | poorly organized, poorly applied, poorly done — n. bad action, sin; guilt. mithyāsmi duskrtam I am wrong.
duṣkṛti [duskṛti] amnf who acts badly.
duṣkṛtin [duskṛtin] amnf duṣkṛtiṇī who acts badly.

duṣkhá |duskha| amnf duṣkhā cf. duḥkha. ਫੁੲ duṣṭa [pp. duṣ] amnf duṣṭā spoiled, defiled; contaminated, impure, tainted | corrupted, depraved, vicious; vile, base, bad, wicked | faulty, guilty | slandered, debased, insulted — ifc. defiled with (iic.) — m. villain, criminal; lit. role of the villain in the theater — n. sin, crime, defilement; guilt; outrage, rape; perversion — f. duṣṭā depraved woman. duștatā [tā] f. wickedness, vice; fault, violation, crime. duștatva |tva| n. wickedness, vice; fault, violation, crime.
dustabatuka |batuka| m. dirty kid, bad boy, thug. duştahrdaya | hrdaya | amnf duştahrdayā wicked, bad, hard-hearted.
duṣṭātma [ātma] amnf duṣṭātmā to the broken soul; whose nature is evil.
duṣṭara |dustara| amnf duṣṭarā cf. dus tara.
duṣṭi [act. duṣ] f. corruption; defilement; vice infection (wound).
duṣṭhu adv. cf. duḥṣṭhu.
duspīyamāna [duspīyamāna] amnf duspīyamānā drank with difficulty.
duṣpūra [duspūra] amnf duṣpūrā difficult to fill; difficult to satisfy.
dusprayukta [dusprayukta] amnf dusprayuktā badly arranged, disorderly; misused.
duspraveśa [duspraveśa] amnf duspraveśā difficult to penetrate — f. duspraveśā bio. bot. Opuntia, prickly pear.
duṣprāpa [dusprāpa] amnf duṣprāpā difficult to obtain.
duṣprāpya [dusprāpya] amnf dusprāpyā difficult to obtain.
dușmanta cf. dușyanta.

dusyanta var. Duḥṣanta, duṣmanta m. myth. np. of the king dusyanta (or Duhsanta or Dusmanta), of the lunar lineage [somavamsa], descendant of Pūru, husband of Haṃsavatī then of Sakuntalā and father by the latter of Bharata; he was invited to heaven [svarga] by Indra, who sent his charioteer Mātali to fetch him, in order to fight the demons | dānavās | lit. he is the hero of the drama Abhijñānaśakuntalā by Kālidāsa.
dus var. dur, duś, duṣ, duḥ pf. mal, mauvais, difficile, dangereux, inférieur | fr. dys.
dustara var. duṣṭarā [dustara] amnf dus tarā difficult to cross.
dustarka [dustarka] m. incorrect reasoning; bad argument.
dustyaja |dustyaja| amnf dustyajā which is difficult to give up.

√ duh₁ v. [2] pr. (dogdhi) aor. [7] (adhukṣat) v. [4] pr. (duhyati) pr. r. (duhyate) aor. ps. (adohi) pp. (dugdha) pfp. (duhya, dohya, dohanīya) inf. (dogdhum) pf. (sam) to milk (cow, udder); to take advantage of (acc.) | to draw, extract (milk, soma, good things); to express (sap) | to extract acc. from acc. — pr. r. (dugdhé) to give milk; to emit, to make flow; to provide, to grant — ca. (doháyati) to milk — dés. (dudhukṣati) to want to milk ang. dug. devā aduhra véd. the gods granted abundance. The cow gives milk of her own accord. Devadatta left when the cows were being milked and returned once they were milked. Devadatta left when the cows were about to be milked.
duh₁ [agt. duh₁] ifc. mf [noun. dhuk] which treats (iic.) | who grants (iic.) — m. duha id.
duhitṛ [agt. duh₁] amnf [sg. name. duhitā, acc. duhitaram | who treats — f. girl | “the one who milks” | eng. daughter; all. Tochter.
duhya |pfp. |1| duh₁| amnf duyā to milk, that which must be milked.
duhyamana |ppr. p.s. duh₁| amnf of the hyamānā which is milked.
dū |act. du| f. pain; distress.
dūdhī |dhī₂| amnf véd. malevolent.
dūda |da| amnf dūdā enemy; oppressor.

dūtá amnf dūtī messenger, envoy, emissary; ambassador; negotiator — f. dūtī soc. matchmaker | phil. [Trika] sexual partner of a kulayāga | myth. follower of Durgā. agnim dūtam puro dadhe [RV.] I appoint Agni as first ambassador.
dūtaka |ka| amnf dūtikā messenger; ambassadress.
Dūtakāvya [kāvya] n. lit. poetic genre, like the Meghadūta | lit. np. of the Dūtakāvya of Nārāyaṇa₃ Bhaṭṭa, which evokes the role of mediator of Kṛṣṇa between the Pāṇḍavās and Duryodhana.
Dūtaghatotkaca [ghatotkaca] n. lit. np. of the Dūtaghatotkaca, a play [nāṭaka] by Bhāsa based on the Mahābhārata. dūtapresaņika [presaņika] m. soc. officer managing the messengers.
Dūtavākya [vākya] n. lit. np. of the Dūtavākya "Tale of the Messenger", play [nāṭaka] by Bhāsa based on the Mahābhārata; it is also performed in the Kūṭiyāṭṭam genre in Kerala.
dūtavāsa [vāsa₁] m. mod. embassy.
dūtyá [dūtaya] n. embassy; message.
dūná [pp. du] amnf dūnā burned; afflicted, depressed.

dūrá amnf dūrā distant, remote, far away — n. remoteness, distance, long road, great duration. dūrāt adv. far, far away; a long time ago. dūram adv. far away; far from (abl. g.); very high or very low | a long time ago | enormously. dūratas adv. from afar, at a distance; far; very. dūram kṛ to outdistance, to surpass. dūrīkṛ to set aside, to distance, to banish. dūrībhū to move away, to withdraw. dūre kṛ to move away, to separate. dūre tisthatu adv. never mind, let's not talk about it anymore. dūre bhū to move away, to be absent, to go far away. durādvaram from afar preferable.
dūrágata [gata] amnf dūragatā gone far away very committed. dūragatamanmathā sā she is very much in love.
dūrádarśana [darśana] m. ["who sees far"] vulture — n. ability to see far | mod. television.
dūrádarśin | darśin | amnf dūradarśinī who sees far — m. prophet, seer | vulture.
dūradarśitā [tā] f. quality of seeing far; ability to foresee. dīrghadūradarśitā quality of foreseeing in the long term.
dūrábhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. mod. radio.
dūrávāṇī [vāṇī] f. mod. telephone.
dūrārūḍha |ārūḍha| amnf dūrārūḍhā risen high; very advanced; attained a high position. dūrārūdhāh khalu ete manorathāh These are indeed very high ambitions.
dūrārohin [ārohin] amnf dūrārohinī id.
dūrakta [dusrakta] amnf dūraktā badly painted; badly tinted.
dūraksya |dusraksya| amnf dūraksyā difficult to protect.
dūrvā f. bio. bot. Cynodon dactylon, panis, couch grass; this dark green creeping herb is used in offering rites. dūrvāvaņa | vana | n. ved. dūrvā herb thicket.

dūș [ca. duș] v. [10] pr. (dūṣáyati) pp. (dūṣita) abs. (dūṣayitvā) to corrupt, defile, vitiate, spoil; to damage, harm; to dishonor, violate; to falsify, slander; to insult, outrage someone. (g.) | to blame, disapprove; to object, refute. svam dūṣayati he dishonors himself.
dūṣa |agt. ca. duṣ| amnf dūṣā who defiles — ifc. defiled by (iic.).
dūṣaka [agt. ca. duṣ] amnf dūṣikā who breaks, who defiles, who outrages; vicious, Bad, impure | seducer; slanderer — f. dūṣikā impure, filth; chassie.

dūṣaṇa [agt. ca. duṣ] amnf dūṣaṇī harmful, disastrous, Evil; unjust; plundering — act. n. defilement, sin, fault; outrage, insult, rape phil. criticism, refutation — m. myth. np. of dūṣaṇa, epith. of Rāvaṇa "the Evil One" | myth. np. of the asura Dūsana₁, who persecuted Vedapriya; cf. mahākāleśvara.
dūṣita [pp. ca. duṣ] amnf dūṣitā defiled, corrupted, damaged; slandered, outraged — n. calom denie, insult.
dr₂ cf. dr.
√ dr₁ ps. (driyáte) pfp. (drtya, daranīya) pf. (ā) unusual without pf...
dṛṃh cf. dṛh.
drk cf. drś₂.
drkpāta [pāta] m. act of casting a glance.

dṛḍha |pp. dṛh| amnf dṛḍhā firm, fixed; stable, constant | solid, massive; hard, dense; thick; rigid | strong, resistant; tenacious, unwavering; rigorous. dṛḍhībhū to strengthen. drdham kr to make firm. bhāvam dṛḍham kṛ to take a firm resolution.
dṛḍhatara |tara| amnf dṛḍhatarā compar. very strong; very violent.
dṛḍhatā [tā] f. firmness; hardness; solidity; perseverance.
dṛḍhatva [tva] n. id. Drdhadasyu var. drdhasyu |dasyu| m. myth. np. of the sage Drdhadasyu "Inflexible towards the impious", son of Agasti and Lopāmudrā, also called Idhmavāha or Tridasyu.
dṛḍhaniścaya | niścaya | amnf dṛḍhaniścayā established; certain | resolved.
drdhabandha | bandha | m. rigorous imprisonment | lit. rigid rules of poetic composition.
dṛḍhabala [bala] m. hist. n.p. of the doctor Dṛḍhabala; he revised the Carakasaṃhitā.
dṛḍhabhakti | bhakti | amnf whose affection is solid.
drdhabhaktika |ka| amnf drdhabhaktikā id.
drdhamati | mati| amnf firm-minded; committed, resolute.
dṛḍhamanaska | manaska | afmn drdhamanaskā id.
dṛḍhamūrkha [mūrkha] amnf dṛḍhamūrkhā fieffé imbécile.
dṛḍhavrata [vrata] amnf dṛḍhavratā [“firm in his vows” who follows his resolutions; who is firm in his asceticism | devoted to, who perseveres in (iic. loc.).
dṛḍhasyu cf. dṛḍhadasyu.

dṛti [act. dṛ] m. (tanned) skin, leather | leather bag; leather bag. na hi pūtam syādgokṣīram śvadṛtau dhṛtam Even milk spoils when kept in a dog-skin bag; this maxim is used by Kumārila to condemn the teaching of the Dhist Buddhists.
drtihari [hari₁] m. ["carrion carrier" | dog.
rp v. [4] pr. (drpyati) pp. (drpta) to go mad, to ramble | to become proud, to be proud — ca. (darpayati) to drive mad, to make proud.
drpta | pp. drp | amnf drptā mad, frenzied proud, arrogant, presumptuous.
drptabālāki |bālāki| mr. ved. |BU.| n.p. of the scholar Drptabālāki; cf. Gārgya₁ bālāki.
dṛprá |dṛpra| amnf dṛprā arrogant | strong.
dṛbdha [pp. dṛbh] amnf dṛbdhā tied, at stained; in bundles, in sheaves.
√ dṛbh v. [6] pr. (dṛbháti) pp. (dṛbdha) ca. (darbhayati) to bundle, to tie, to bind.

√ drs₁ var. pas v. [4] pr. (pasyati) fut. (drakṣyati) pft. (dadarśa) aor. [2] (adarśat) aor. [3] (adīdṛśat) aor. [4] (adrākṣīt) inf. (dráṣṭum) pp. (dṛṣṭa) ppft. (dadṛśivas) pfp. (dṛṣ́ya, darśanīya) abs. (dṛṣṭvā) pf. (anu, ā, upa, ni, pra, prati, sam) see; discern | look | go see, visit (acc.) — ps. (drśyate) be seen; to appear, to manifest, to reveal oneself; to prove to be, to seem to be (impersonal) it is observed — ca. (darśayati) to show, to display — intens. r. (darīdṛśyate) to be always visible; to be constantly evident, to be very often seen | to be seen repeatedly — des. (didṛkṣati) pp. (didṛkṣita) to wish to see — des. r. (didṛkṣate) to hope to see, to desire. punah draksyāmah adr. see you soon. na dráyate it does not seem (that this is the case).

dṛś₁ [agt. dṛś₁] amnf ifc. [nom. dṛk; en comp. drk, drg | who observes, who understands, who knows (iic.) | similar to, such as (iic.) — f. look, sight, vision; eye | aspect, appearance, point of view, doctrine.
dṛśa |act. dṛś₁| ifc. amnf dṛśī which has the appearance of, similar to (iic.). īdṛśa var. etādṛśa, tādṛśa amn such. kīdṛśa amn what, of what nature, of what use? mādrśa such as me.
dṛśi [act. dṛś₁] f. vision; faculty of sight.
dṛśya [pfp. [1] dṛś₁] amnf dṛśyā visible; to see, pleasant — n. visible object | lit. drama (opp. śravya).
drśyakāvya | kāvya | n. bed. pra krit theater dialogue; opp. drśyakāvya.
dṛśvan |agt. dṛś₁| ifc. amnf dṛśvarī who saw (iic.); familiar with (iic.). merudṛśvā who saw Mount Meru. paralokadṛśvā who saw the beyond. pāradṛśvā who saw the other shore.
dṛṣád f. stone, rock; millstone (lower, for so much the stone [upalā]); syn. śilā.
dṛṣadupala | upala | n. condiment millstone — f. dṛṣadupalā du. dṛṣadupale the two stones of the millstone.
dṛṣadvat [vat] amnf dṛṣadvatī full of stones — f. dṛṣadvatī geo. np. of the river dṛṣadvatī "which carries stones" (mod. Ghaggar, on the border between Pañjāb and Hariyāṇa?).

dṛṣadolūkhala [dṛṣadulūkhala] n. mortar and pestle. yonirulūkhalam śiśnammusalam | mithunam praja nanam | [SB.] The vulva is the mortar, the penis is the pestle; coitus leads to procreation. ਵੁষ্ট dṛṣṭá [pp. dṛś₁] amnf dṛṣṭā seen, observed, noticed, perceived | visible, apparent, manifest, real, evident | experienced, understood; recognized, valid. dṛṣṭavīryo me rāmaḥ Rāma witnessed my exploits.
dṛṣṭathā |thā| adv. according to the point of view. anayā dṛṣṭathā considered in this light.
dṛṣṭádoṣa [doṣa₂] amnf dṛṣṭadoṣā considered guilty, erroneous or wrongful. dṛṣṭadoṣā mṛgayā hunting is considered a sin.
dṛṣṭanaṣṭa |dṛṣṭanaṣṭa| amnf dṛṣṭanaṣṭā previewed.
dṛṣṭapūrva [pūrva] amnf dṛṣṭapūrvā déjà vu.
dṛṣṭādṛṣṭa |adṛṣṭa| amnf dṛṣṭādṛṣṭā more or less visible — n. ved. the seen and the unseen.

dṛṣṭānta | anta | m. example; instance; illustration | analogy, parable, metaphor | phil. [Nyāya] example in support of the syllogism [pañcāvayava]; it must verify the thesis [sapakṣa]. dṛṣṭāntatas adv. for example. hetoh pratibandhāvadhāraņam dṛṣṭāntah phil. [Nyāyamañjarī] The supporting example is the affirmation of the implication of the cause.
dṛṣṭārtha [artha] amnf dṛṣṭārthā whose merit, meaning or purpose is evident | who knows the true meaning of things | phil. which concerns the visible world; syn. laukika.
dṛṣṭārthāpatti [arthāpatti] f. phil. [Kumārila] implicature arising from perception; opp. śrutārthāpatti.

dṛṣṭi [act. dṛś₁] f. sight, vision; glance, look, eye | phil. notion, point of view | understanding, intelligence; knowledge | phil. yoga point of ocular focus; the nine principal ones are: the tip of the nose, the space between the eyebrows, the thumb, the hand, the foot, the top, the right side, and the left side. dṛṣṭiṃ dā to look (loc.); to glance. mama dṛṣṭyā in my opinion. lokadrstyā in the public eye. lokavyavahāradrstyā from a practical point of view.
dṛṣṭikṣama [kṣama] amnf dṛṣṭikṣamā worthy of being seen.
drstidosa [dosa₂] m. soc. spell cast by the gaze, evil eye.
dṛṣṭinipāta |nipāta| mr. cf. dṛṣṭipāta.
dṛṣṭiparihāra [parihāra] m. protection against the evil eye.
dṛṣṭipāta [pāta] m. look ["fall of the gaze"]; glance | phil. |Netratantra| evil eye.
dṛṣṭimanohara [manohara] amfn dṛṣṭimanoharā pleasing to the eye.
dṛṣṭivāda [vāda] m. lit. 12th text of the Jaina canon, collection of different doctrines.
dṛṣṭiviṣa [viṣa] amnf dṛṣṭiviṣā myth. ["with a poisoned gaze" | that poisons by the mere gaze.
dṛṣṭisambheda |sambheda| m. exchange of glances.
dṛṣṭisṛṣṭi |sṛṣṭi| f. phil. Advaita doctrine of observation and manifestation.
√ dṛh var. dṛṃh v. [1] pr. (dṛṃhati) pp. (dṛḍha) consolidate, strengthen — pr. r. (dṛṃhate) be firm, be strong.
√ dr var. dr₂ v. [9] pr. (drṇāti) ca. (dārayati) pf. (vi) to split, tear, break — ps. (dīryate) pp. (dīrṇa) to burst, split, tear, fall to pieces | gr. δερω; ang. to tear; all. verzehren.

déya [pfp. [1] dā₁] amnf deyā to give. deyamārtasya śayanam pariśrāntasya cāsanam | tṛṣitasya ca pānīyam kṣudhitasya ca bhojanam || We must give a bed to the sick, a seat to the exhausted, water to the thirsty, food to the hungry.
deyadharma [dharma] m. bd. ["duty of giving"] charity, donation | var. devadharma bd. donation; not. in the case of the image of a god.
√ dev v. [1] pr. (devati) ca. (devayati) pp. (dyūna) pf. (bet) [unusual without pf.].

devá [agt. dīv₁] amnf devī brilliant | divine — m. god | "being of light" | phil. personification of a manifestation of divine power; aspect of the transcendent | pl. devās myth. the gods; tradition gives a conventional list of 33 [trayastriṃśa] | King, his majesty — f. cf. devī — v. [11] pr. (devayati) to worship, to pray, to make devotions; to be pious | lat. divus; fr. divin; Avestan daeva. devau the King and the queen.
naradevah ["god among men"] King. jayatu devah long live the King! devagandharvamānusoragarākṣasāh the gods, the genies gandharvās, the men, the serpent spirits and the demons rākṣasās.
devakula [kula] n. temple ["house of god"] — f. devakulā small temple, chapel.
devakulāvāsa |āvāsa| mr. pl. outbuildings of a temple.

devagiri [giri] m. geo. np. of the city of devagiri in Mahārāṣṭra; it was the capital of the Rāṣṭrakūṭās in the 11th century, then of the Yādavās in the 12th century, from Bhillama; it was taken by Alauddin Khalji in 1294, then definitively by Kutubuddin Mubarak Khilji in 1318; its King Harapaladeva was flayed alive there; in 1327 Mohammad Tughluk, sultan of Delhi, renamed it Daulatābād and tried to make it his capital; its fortress was impregnable, with 4 walls of fortifications encircling a fort established on a rock 200 high, accessible only by a dark labyrinth carved into the rock; Ahmad Nizam Shah captured it in 1499; mod. ruins of Daulatābād, 13 km west of Aurangābād; cf. Rāmacandra₁.

devagupta | Gupta | m. hist. np. of King Deva Gupta of Mālava, eldest son of Mahāsena Gupta (late 6th century); he attacked King Grahavarmā of Kanyākubjā, killed him and imprisoned his wife Rājyaśrī; he was defeated by Rājya Vardhana₁ and his property confiscated; by treachery Saśānka, King of Gauda, killed Rājya, but his brother Harşa avenged him and seized Mālava which he annexed to his empire.

devagrha [grha] n. ["house of god"] temple, sacred city | king's palace | geo. n.p. many localities or forts in India (mod. Deogarh); not. holy city of Jharakhanda (Vaidyanātha temple), city in Uttar Pradesh southwest of Lalitpur (Daśāvatāra temple, complex of Jaina temples and monasteries), city of Orissa east of Sambalpur, city of Rājasthāna north of Udaipur, and temple in Gwalior.
devagraha [graha] m. phil. [Tantra] possession by a god.
Devacandra | candra | m. hist. np. of the Jain monk Devacandra (11th century); Hemacandra was his disciple.
devacarita | carita | n. conduct of the gods. na devacaritam caret Do not behave like a god.
devajaná [jana] m. divine being; divinity | pl. Deva janās the divine beings: gods, spirits, serpents, etc.
devatrāsa | trāsa | m. fear of the gods.
devatvá |tva| n. divine state, divinity.

Devadatta [datta] amnf devadattā given by the gods; desired (may God give it to us) | myth. human being begotten by gods, such as Bhīṣma — m. lit. np. of Devadatta "God-given", prototype character used by rhetoric, like So-and-so | myth. |Mah. | np. of the Devadatta₁ conch of Arjuna, given by Maya | bd. np. of a treacherous cousin of the Buddha; cf. Nālāgiri.

devadattahantrhatanyāya [hantrhatanyāya] m. gram. maxim of the death of the murderer of Deva datta. nahi devadattasya hantari hate devadattasya prādurbhāvo bhavati It is not the death of Devadatta's death that restores Devadatta's life.
devadāru [dāru] mn bio. bot. Cedrus deodara, Himalayan deodar cedar; syn. Sarala; this large conifer can reach 85 m; myth. [KuS.] Siva meditates under a cedar tree.
devadāruvāna [vana] n. myth. n.p. from the Devadāruvana cedar forest where Šiva humiliated the heretical ascetics; cf. Darukavana.
devadāsa [dāsa] m. hierodule, temple or monastery servant | np. de devadāsa "servant of god", name of various characters — f. devadāsī sacred prostitute in a temple.
devadrāc [ac] amnf devadrācī turned towards the divinity.
devanāgarī [nāgarī] f. ["of the divine city"] syllabic script of North India, used not. for writing the Sanskrit language (late use for city writing [nāgarī]).
devapati [pati] m. myth. np. of devapati, epith. of Indra "King of the gods".
devapāla [Pāla] m. hist. np. of King devapāla, son and successor of Dharmapāla₁; he reigned from 810 to 850 over the Pāla empire of Bengal.
devapūjā [pūjā] f. soc. rite of divine worship, one of the 6 duties of a brahmin [satkarmāni].

Devaprabha [prabhā₂] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the great harva Devaprabha, cursed by an ascetic to incarnate himself as King Ratnādhipati for having suspected him of lust towards his wife Rājavatī; Somaprabha is his younger brother; cf. Śvetaraśmi.
Devaprayāga [prayāga] m. geo. np. of the holy city of Devaprayāga in the Himālaya; the Alakanandā joins the Bhāgīrathī there to form the Gaṅgā.
Devabodha [bodha] m. hist. np. of the poet and dramaturge Devabodha (circa 11th century, North India); he is the author of the Jñānadīpikā.
devamandira [mandira] n. temple.
devámaya [maya] amnf devamayī consisting of divinities; comprising The gods.
devamāya [māya] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of King vidyādhara devamāya, Who guards the cave Triśīrṣa; defeated by Naravāhanadatta, he sides with him.
devamīdha [mīdha] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of King devamīdha Janaka, son of Kīrtiratha, father of Vi budha.
devaya |ya₂| amnf devayā Who seeks the gods, Who goes towards the gods.
devayajñá [yajña] m. soc. [SB.] ved. sacrifice to the gods, one of the five major rites [mahāyajña].
devayajya [yajya] n. soc. [SB.] ved. sacrifice to the gods — f. devayajyā id.

devayāna [yāna] amnf devayānī That which leads to the gods — n. path to the gods; divine vehicle | phil. liberation from death, by the "path of the gods", opp. pitṛyāna — f. devayānī myth. np. of devayānī "That which leads to the gods", daughter of SukraUśanā, wife of Yayāti, mother of Yadu and Turvasu.

devayoni [yoni] mf myth. to be of divine lineage. vidyādharāpsaroyakṣāh rakṣogandharvakinnarāh | siddhaguhyakabhūtāśca piśācā devayonayaḥ [KM.] The vidyādharās, The apsarasas, The yakṣās, The rakṣās, The gandharvās, The kinnarās, The siddhās, The guhyakās, The bhūtās and The piśācās are of divine lineage.
devarata [rata] amnf devaratā Who loves the gods; pious.
devarati | rati | f. myth. np. from the apsaras devarati "Delight of the gods".
Devarāja [rāja] m. King by divine right | myth. np. of Devarāja, epith. of Indra "King of the gods".

Devarāta [rāta] m. myth. np. of King Devarāta "Given by the Gods", epithet of Sunahsepha₁ son of Ŗcīka, taken in by Viśvāmitra and who became King of Mithilā under the title of Devarāta Janaka; Shiva gave him the Śaivacāpa bow, which his descendant Jana karāja inherited | myth. [BhP.] np. of King Devarāta Janaka, son of Suketu₁, father of Brhadratha₂. devarși [ṛṣi] m. sage |ṛṣi] divine; epithet not. of Nārada, Vasistha.
devarsitva [tva] n. quality of divine sage.
devaloka |loka| m. myth. np. of devaloka, the Heaven of the gods; cf. Svar.
devavat |vat| amnf devavatī guarded by the gods, surrounded by gods | like a god — adv. in the manner of a god.
devavāṇī | vāṇī | f. divine voice | | "language of the gods" | Sanskrit.
Devavrata | vrata | amnf devavratā Who serves the gods, pious — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Devavrata "the pious", eldest son of King Sāṃtanu by Gaṅgā; cf. Bhīşma.

devaśayana | śayana | n. myth. 4-month sleep of Viṣṇu — f. devaśayanī soc. festival of the beginning of Viṣṇu's sleep, on the 11th day [ekādaśī] of the clear fortnight of the month āṣāḍha (around the beginning of July); he wakes up 4 months later, at prabodhanī; cf. śayanaikādaśī. devásilpin | silpin m. myth. np. of Devasilpin, epith. of tvașțā "the craftsman of the gods".

devasenā [senā] f. myth. [Mah.] np. of devasenā "Divine Army", daughter of Dakṣa (or Prajāpati); with her sister Daityasenā they were of great beauty; Keśī tried to abduct her, but she called upon In dra for help Who saved her, to become the first wife of Skanda — m. Devasena lit. [KSS.] np. of the King of Srāvastī Devasena; cf. Unmādinī.
Devasomā [soma] f. bed. n.p. by Devasomā, partner of Satyasoma in the play Mattavilāsa.

Devasthāna [sthāna] n. divine residence; temple — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the rṣi Devasthāna "He who speaks in the name of the gods"; he taught Yudhisthira the necessity of royal temporal power [danda].

devasmitā [smita] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of devasmitā, daughter of the merchant Dharmagupta; when Dhana datta, a merchant from Tāmraliptī, came accompanied by his son Guhasena to ask for her hand, her father refused, but having fallen in love with Guhasena she ran away to marry him; he was away on a mission to the island of Kaţāha, she was worried; Siva provided each of them with a red lotus Which would only wither in case of infidelity of the other; Guha sena, drunk, revealed the secret to four sons of merchants, Who entered her house through the nun Yogakarandikā; devasmitā intoxicated them with dhattūra and Made them mark with śvapada.
deváhūti [hūti] f. invocation of the gods | myth. np. of Devahūti, wife of Kardama, mother of Kapila.
devahūya | hūya | n. Vedic. invocation to the gods. devāmśa amśa m. myth. partial incarnation of a god.
Devākara |ākara| m. lit. np. of the Jaina logician Sid Dhasena Devākara (around the 1st century); he is credited with the Nyāyāvatara.
devālaya |ālaya| mn temple | “stay of god” | ; arch. main sanctum of a temple || hi. deval; oriya deul.
devāvasura | asura | m. du. devāvasurau myth. RV. the two titans who became gods, epith. of Mitrāvaruņau.
Devendra | Indra | m. myth. np. of Devendra "Chief of the gods"; it qualifies Indra, and also Shiva.
devendrabuddhi [buddhi] m. hist. n.p. from the philosopher bd. devendrabuddhi (7th century), disciple of Dharmakīrti.

Devaka₁ [agt. div] amnf devikā celestial, divine — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the king vṛṣṇi Devaka₁ "divine", son of Ahuka, elder brother of Ugrasena, father of devakī | myth. np. of Devaka₁, elder son of Akrūra.

devakī [f. Devaka₁] f. myth. [Mah.] patr. of devakī "daughter of Devaka₁"; wife of Vasudeva, she is mother of Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa (respective incarnations of a white hair and a black hair of Viṣṇu, or of Śeṣa and Nārāyaṇa); she is a magician; she is also called Sahadevā; |HV.| she incarnates on Earth Aditi.
devakīnandana | nandana | m. myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa "son of devakī".
devakīputra | putra | m. myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa "son of devakī".
devatā [devatā] f. divinity, deity; divine being | [devatapratimā] image of a god.
devatādhikaraṇa [adhikaraṇa] n. phil. relation to the gods, mediation with the gods | lit. section of the Pūrvamīmāmsāśāstra relating to the gods.
devatāpratimā [pratimā₁] f. soc. representation of the deities.
devana [act. dīv₁] m. dice — nf from vanā dice game; game; sport | playing field; garden occupation; service; profession.
devayú [devayu] amnf devoted to the gods; devout, pious.
devara [related to dīv₁] m. brother-in-law (younger brother of her husband); syn. devr
devaranyāya [nyāya] m. soc. levirate.
Devala [devala] m. soc. officiant of an idol; pious man | myth. np. of the rsi Devala; his hermitage was the tīrtha Utkocaka, where he lived with his younger brother Dhaumya; cf. Huhu.
devalaka [ka] m. soc. itinerant servant of an idol, which he carries on his head; he goes from house to house to present it and thus earn his subsistence.
devānām [g. pl. deva] iic.

devānāmpriya [priya] amnf devānāmpriyā Beloved of the gods; (figuratively) simple-minded — m. hist. np. devānāmpriya "Beloved of the gods", (pāli Devānampiya), honorific title of kings, which King Aśoka notably called himself.

devāpi m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the prince kau rava devāpi "Close to the gods"; eldest son of King Pratīpa, he renounced the throne to become a hermit; it is said that he still lives; his brother Sāmtanu became king in his place.
devī [f. deva] f. goddess | soc. queen | phil. np. of devī, the Goddess.
devīkālottarāgama [kālottaraāgama] n. lit. np. of the devīkālottarāgama, śaiva mystical work giving the way of kālottarajñāna.
Devīkṛti [kṛti] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the marvelous sea garden Devīkṛti at Pratiṣṭhāna, created by an ascetic with the help of the Goddess.

devīcandragupta [Candragupta] m. lit. np. from devīcandragupta "The Queen and Candragupta", dramatic play [prakaraṇa] attributed to Viśākhadeva; it tells of the misfortunes of King Rāmagupta who lost his wife Dhruvadevī to an enemy Saka; his younger brother freed her before murdering her to ascend the throne under the name of Candragupta₂.
devīpīṭha [pīṭha] n. myth. one of the 51 (or 64, or 108) sacred places where the pieces of Satī's corpse fell; syn. pīṭhasthāna.
Devīpurāṇa [purāṇa] n. bed. n.p. of Devīpurāṇa.
devībhāgavatapurāna [bhāgavatapurāna] n. bed. n.p. of Devībhāgavatapurāna.
Devīmāhātmya [māhātmya] n. lit. np. of the Devīmāhātmya "Glorification of the Goddess", a 7th century work celebrating Durgā and Kālī, inserted in the Mārkandeya purāņa; cf. Śrīdurgāsaptaśatī.
devīśataka [śataka] n. lit. np. from the devīśataka, a collection of 100 poems about the Goddess of Anandavardhana.
devṛ [agt. dīv₁] m. brother-in-law (younger brother of her husband); syn. devara.
deś [ca. diś₁] v. [10] pr. (deśayati) to show, to make visible; to expose, to explain, to teach.
deśá [obj. diś₁] m. point indicated; place, location, spot; region, province, country, land | soc. evidence, document produced in court of justice — ifc. (after body part) indicates its location.
deśaguna [guna] m. regional particularity; neck local tumor.
deśaja | ja | amnf deśajā local; native; of gram origin. regional
deśajāta | jāta | amnf deśajātā local; native; original | gram. regional
deśabhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. regional language, vernacular.
deśabhāṣāvijñāna | vijñāna | n. understanding regional languages, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
deśasātmya |sātmya| n. med. the state of being appropriate to the place.
deśastha | stha| amnf deśasthā residing in a country | soc. designates a community of brah manes originating from Mahārāṣṭra.
deśānantara [anantara] n. foreign country.
deśāvakāśika [avakāśika] n. jn. observance of the avoidance of certain places, a śikṣāvrata .
Deśopadeśa | upadeśa | mr. bed. n.p. from Deśopadeśa, a satirical poem by Ksemendra.
deśaka [agt. diś₁] amnf deśikā ifc. which indicates, which shows — m. indicator; instructor.
deśanā [act. diś₁] f. direction, instruction.
deśika [deśaika] amnf deśikā familiar of places, guide | title of spiritual master | lit. cf. Vedāntadeśika.
deśin [agt. diś₁] amnf deśinī who shows the way, guide | (in fig.) spiritual master — f. deśinī index (finger).
deśī [f. deśa] f. vernacular regional particularism; provincialism | neologism not derivable from Sanskrit grammar.
deśīnāmālā [mālā] f. bed. n.p. of the deśīnāmālā, dictionary of barbarisms and neologisms attested in prākṛta, due to Hemacandra, in 8 sections | varga|.

deśīya [īya] amnf deśīyā autochthonous, local, native; regional, provincial — ifc. native of (iic.) | compatriot of | neighbor of; approximately; almost, by a short time. pañcavarṣadeśīyaḥ of about 5 years. abdeśīyam grtam of almost liquid butter. ācāryadeśīyah m. approximate teacher.
deśīśāstra [śāstra] n. soc. regional custom.

deśya [pfp. [1] diś₁] amnf deśyā to show; to select; remarkable; standard | present; witness; native, regional — n. proposition to prove, conjecture | accusation to establish — ifc. approximately (iic.); which leaves something to be desired. pacatide syam he cooks in a way that leaves something to be desired.
destr [agt. diś₁] amnf destrī indicator, pointer.
deṣṭrá [instr. diś₁] n. indication, direction.
deṣṇá [dā₁sna] n. Don; gift.

deha [obj. dih] mn body; form; mass | human body; person, individual | phil. the carnal form of man; opp. that which animates it [dehin] | appearance; manifestation (of (iic.)) — ifc. having the appearance of (iic.) — f. dehī mound; dike; rampart, fortification.
dehavedha | vedha | mr. phil. transubstantiation of the body (simili of lohavedha).
dehalī f. threshold of the door; cornice of the entrance threshold.
dehalīmuktapuṣpaiḥ [MD.] with the flowers that fell from the cornice.
dehi cf. dā₁.
dehin [dehain] amnf dehinī living being, man | phil. [BhG.] ["that which animates the body and survives it"] soul; syn. ātman.
daiteya [*Ditiīya] amnf daiteyī myth. descendant of Diti — m. cf. daitya | myth. matr. of Rāhu.
daitya [*Ditiya] m. myth. son of Kaśyapa and Diti, asura disturbing the sacrifices; Bali is the king of the daityās — amnf daityā relating to Diti and his sons.
Daityasenā [senā] f. myth. np. of Daityasenā "Army of demons", daughter of Daksa, sister of De vasenā; Keśī abducted her to make her his wife.
daidhiṣavya [*didhiṣū] m. soc. son of a widow's second marriage.
daina [*dina] amnf dainī of day, diurnal; daily.
dainam [acc. daina] iic.
dainamdina [dina] amnf dainamdinī daily dien.
dainika [*dinaka] amnf dainikī per day; by day; daily.
dainya [*dīnaya] m. sadness, discouragement; distress | weakness, cowardice.
dairghya [*dīrghaya] n. length.

daiva [*deva] amnf daivī divine, celestial, pro coming from the gods; fatal — m. ["that which proceeds from the divine"] divine will; destiny, fate; chance, fatality | lat. divinus; fr. devin. daivī vāk the language of the gods (Sanskrit).

Daivajña [jña] m. diviner, seer ["who knows destiny" | astr. np. of Daivajña, title of predictive astrologer. cārān vicārya daivajñairvaktavyam bhūbhujām phalam | grahacāraparijñānam | [Nīlakaṇṭha₁] To predict the king's future, it is essential for the seer to consult spies before analyzing the course of the stars.
daivahata | hata | amnf daivahatā struck by fate.
daivahataka [ka] amnf daivahatakā struck by fate — n. stroke of fate | tragic destiny.
daivata [*devatāa] amnf daivatā which concerns the gods — n. divinity; idol | lit. np. of the daivata, section of the Nighanțu dealing with divinities — ifc. that which worships (iic.).
daivika [*devaika] amnf daivakī divine — n. fatality.
daivya [*devaya] amnf daivyā divine — n. divine power | destiny. daivyā hotārā ved. the two divine priests.
daiśika [*deśaika] amnf daiśikā spatial.
daihika [*dehaika] amnf daihikā concerning the body; bodily.
daihya [*dehaya] amnf bodily daihyā.
dogdhr [agt. duh₁] amnf dogdhrī that milks — f. dogdhrī that nurses; dairy cow; wet nurse.
dola [related to tul] m. swaying, oscillation — f. cf. dolā — v. [11] pr. (dolayati) pp. (dolita) to sway.

dolā [f. dola] f. swing; cradle; swing, transport platform; palanquin | (figuratively) hesitation, uncertainty. dolāpūrņimā [pūrņimā] f. astr. full moon phālgunī soc. festival corr., the 14th of the month phālguna, where an effigy of Kṛṣṇa is swung to celebrate his youth and his games with the gopī; in the evening fires are lit celebrating the Holikā pyre; cf. vasantot sava.
dolāyātrā | yātrā | f. soc. spring festival; syn. holākā, phālgunotsava.
dolita [pp. dola] amnf dolitā balancé.
doṣa₁ [m. doṣā] m. evening, darkness; darkness | myth. np. of dosa, personifying the night sky, a vasu.

dosa₂ [act. dus] m. defect, vice, fault, error | transgression, evil, sin, crime, outrage | med. affection, disease; bodily humor (cf. tridoșa) | accusation, reproach | lit. aesthetic defect of a work. naisa dosah there is no harm. kotra dosah what is the problem? doșajña [jña] amnf doșajñā one who knows the faults of (iic.) | one who knows how to guard against evil; prudent, wise — m. physician; scholar; wise man. doșadrști | drști | f. search for faults; discovery of fault.
doṣabhāj |bhāj| amnf sinner, unbeliever. sarvathā tvamevātra dosabhāk the fault lies entirely with you.
doṣabhājana |bhājana| amnf doṣabhājanā who indulges in vices — n. blameworthy behavior. doșabhājanam bhavati he incurs blame. doșarohitā [rohita] amnf doșarohitā free from error, without defect.
dosavat [vat] amnf dosavatī faulty; defective; blameworthy, guilty | harmful; criminal.
doṣaṇa [act. ca. duṣ] n. imputation of a crime, indictment.
doṣán [back-bound] n. arm, forearm | math. symb. the number 2.
dosā f. darkness; night — adv. of night. dosām adv. of night.
doṣin [doṣa₂in] amnf doṣiṇī defective; faulty; blameworthy, guilty.
dós n. arm, forearm | math. symb. the number 2.

dóha [agt. duh₁] amnf dohā ifc. who benefits from — act. mr. milking, extraction; milk; advantage, gain; success | (in fig.) taking advantage of (g. iic.) — f. moral dohā of a tale, supplicatory verse of a hymn.

dohada m. pregnancy woman's desire; the desires are supposed to emanate from the will of the embryo, and announce the qualities of the child to come |morbid desire (For (loc.)) |lit. (poetry) desire of a plant to be touched by the foot or mouth of a pretty woman in order to flower.
dohána [agt. duh₁] amnf dohanī that gives milk; that brings profit — act. n. milk — f. dohanī milking pail.
dohánīya [pfp. [2] duh₁] amnf dohanīyā which must be treated.
dóhas [abstr. duh₁] n. deals.
dohita [pp. duh₁] amnf dohitā trait.
dohīyas [compar. doha] amnf dohīyasī which gives more or a lot of milk.
dohya [pfp. [1] duh₁] amnf dohyā to milk, that which must be milked — n. animal giving milk.
dauhṣanti [*Duḥṣanta] m. myth. n.p. by Dauhsanti, patr. of Bharata "son of Duhsanta".
dautya [*dūtaya] n. messenger's charge; mes sage, mission.
daundubhi [*dundubhi] f. deception | var. daundubhī soc. journey of the betrothed to the house of his wife.
daurātmya [*durātmanya] n. wickedness, harshness; depravity.
daurjanya [*durjanaya] n. wickedness; bad nature.
daurbalya [*durbalaya] n. weakness; inca pacity.
daurhdrda [*durhrda] n. hardness of heart; wickedness | desire of a pregnant woman. daurhdalakṣaṇaṃ dadhau she was showing signs of pregnancy.
dauhitra [*duhitṛa] m. grandson (son of a daughter) — f. dauhitrī granddaughter (daughter of a daughter).
dyāvā [nom. du. div] iic.
dyāvāpṛthivī [pṛthivī] f. du. dyāvāpṛthiyau ved. the sky and the Earth.
dyāvābhūmī | bhūmi | f. du. ved. heaven and Earth.
dyu [div] m. ifc. sky of; day of — iic. of the sky || fr. diurnal.
dyukāma | kāma | amnf dyukāmā who desires heaven.

√ dyut₁ [related to dv₁] v. [1] pr. r. (dyotate) aor. [2] (adyutat) aor. [3] (ádidyutat) ppr. (dyumat) pf. (ut, pra, vi) to shine, to gleam — ca. (dyotayati) to illuminate, to radiate | to explain, to elucidate, to make clear.
dyut₂ [agt. dyut₁] f. ray, burst of Light.
dyuti [act. dyut₁] f. brilliance, splendor; majesty, glory.
dyutimat |mat| amnf dyutimatī resplendent health.
dyumat [ppr. dyut₁] amnf dyumantī lu minous, resplendent, splendid; glorious.
dyumna |dyut₁mna| n. splendor, brilliance; my jestery, glory; vigor | fortune, wealth.
dyūtá [pp. dīv₁] amnf dyūtā played — n. dice game; bet, game of chance; competition | winnings at the game, loot.
dyūtakuśala [kuśala] amnf dyūtakuśalā skilled at the game.
dyūtaparvan [parvan] n. bed. n.p. of the Dyūtaparva, section of the Mah. recounting the game of dice between Yudhişthira and Sakuni, part of the Sabhāparva.
dyūtamandala [mandala] n. soc. circle of play.
dyūtaviśesa [viśesa] m. the knowledge of games of chance, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.
dyot [ca. dyut₁] v. [10] pr. (dyotayati) to illuminate, to radiate | to explain, to make luminous; to reveal.
dyota [agt. dyut₁] m. Light, brightness.
dyotaka [agt. dyut₁] amnf dyotikā that illuminates, that shines; that suggests | gram. said of a grammatical word, not. preverbs [upasarga], part
cules | nipāta|, suffixes svārthika; opp. vācaka — m. explanation; sens — ifc. that clarifies, that explains (iic.).
dyotakatva [tva] n. gram. Patañjali₁'s theory of meaning; it explains morphological formation by semantic composition.
dyotana [agt. dyut₁] amnf dyotanī that shines, that illuminates | that explains — m. lamp — act. nf dyotanā act of shining; illumination | gram. act of suggesting.
dyotita [pp. dyut₁] amnf dyotitā ex plique | gram. expressed; expressed; suggested.

dyotya [pfp. [1] ca. dyut₁] amnf dyotyā to be explained; which must be expressed or suggested — m. gram. connotation; implication. dyotadyotakasambandha gram. relation between the notion to be suggested and the suggesting notion.

dyaus [nom. div] ind. myth. np. of Dyau, the sky. Personified light, a treasure [vasu]; pṛthivī is his wife; [Mah.] to punish him for stealing his cow Nandinī, Vasiṣṭha condemned him to incarnate on Earth as Bhīṣma; cf. Gaṅgā.
dradhistha [super. drdha] amnf dradhisthā the most solid, the strongest.
dradhīyas [compar. drdha] amnf draḍhīyasī more solid, stronger; very solid, very strong.

√ dram [related to drā₁] v. [1] pr. (dramati) to run, to flee — intens. r. (dandramyate) to run around, to wander. avidyāyām antare vartamānāh svayandhīrāh paṇḍitammanyamānāḥ | dandramyamāṇāḥ pa riyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ | [KU.] Moving about in the midst of ignorance, believing themselves learned, taking themselves for a master, running around in all directions, the fools go round and round like blind men led by blind men.
drava [agt. dru₁] amnf dravā that runs | that flows, that oozes; liquid, fluid, molten; opp. khara — act. n. flow; fluid, secretion. dravīkṛ to liquefy. dravībhū to become fluid.
dravatva |tva| n. phil. |Vaiśeṣika| fluidity, a quality [guna].
drávat | ppr. dru₁ | amnf dravantī current; rapid | having a leak — f. dravantī np. of rapid river — adv. dravat quickly, fast — v. [11] pr. (dravatyati) to become fluid.
Dravida m. myth. np. of Dravida "the Ta moul", son of Krishna | pl. name of the people and the country
Dravidians [drāviḍa] on the Coromandel coast south of the Godāvarī.
draviņa [related to dravya₁] n. possession, wealth; property, fortune; power, prowess — m. pl. draviņās goods.
dravī iiv. drava.
dravīkaraṇa [karaṇa] n. melting; liquefaction.
dravībhāva [bhāva] m. melting; liquefaction | (figuratively) softening.
dravībhūta | bhūta | amnf dravībhūtā melted tenderly. mama vacasā tasya hṛdayaṃ dravībhūtam my words touched his heart.

drávya₁ n. substance, object, matter; thing substance of (iic.); material | suitable, useful or valid object | property, goods, riches; for tune | soc. oblatory matter of the sacrifice ved. | phil. |Vaiśeṣika| the category |padārtha| of the 9 elementary substances: of which 5 tangible substances [bhūtadravya]: Earth [pṛthivī], Waters [āpas], Fire [tejas], Wind [vāyu], Ether [ākāśa], and 4 subtle substances [sūkṣmabhūta]: Time [kāla₁], Space [diś₂], Soul [ātman] and Spirit [manas]; cf. mūrtadravya | jn. physical substance; We distinguish six types: the animate [jīva] and five categories of inanimate [ajīva]: material objects [pudgala], movement [dharma], rest [adhrma], and

pace [ākāśa] and time [kāla₁]; all except the last occupy Space [astikāya] | phil. [Bhartṛhari] matter; it cannot be apprehended by speech [śabda], and can only be designated indirectly by its attributes [upādhi] such as jāti, guṇa, kriyā, etc. dravyasyāvyapadeśyasya ya upādīyate gunah | bhedakah vyapadeśāya tatprakarşo'bhidhīyate phil. |Bhartrhari| The best way to designate a matter, impossible to express by speech, is to indicate its discriminating quality. lingasamkhyānvitam dravyam gram. Is dravya₁ that which possesses gender and number. vastūpalakṣaṇam yatra sarvanāma prayujyate dravyam iti ucyate so'rtho bhedyatvena vivaksitah gram. [VAK.] The word dravya₁ expresses the meaning of a differentiated object, which can be designated by a pro noun.
dravyatva [tva] n. phil. [Vaiśeṣika] substantiality, materiality.
dravyamaya [maya] amnf dravyamayī material.

dravyasamuddeśa [samuddeśa] m. gram. np. from the dravyasamuddeśa "Exposition on nouns", second chapter of the Prakīrņakānda section of Bhartrhari's Vākyapadīya; the Prakīrņaprakāśa is a commentary on it.
dravya₁ [dru₁ya] amnf dravyā relating to the tree — n. resin, gum, lacquer.
dravyavana | vana | n. revenue forest.
drastu [inf. drś₁] iic. (inf.) see.
drastukāma [kāma] amnf drastukāmā eager to see.
drastumanas [manas] amnf inclined to see.
drastuśakya [śakya] amnf drastuśakyā able to see.
drastr | agt. drś₁ | amnf drastrī | sg. nom. draștā, acc. draștāram, g. draștur who has good sight, seer; spectator, contemplator, eyewitness | just; who decides; judge | who goes to see.
√ drā₂ v. [2] pr. (drāti) to run, to flee — ca. (drāpayati) to make flee — intens. (dáridrāti) pp. (da ridrita) to be miserable (to wander without a fixed address). daridrāmcakāra he became poor.
drāk [drā₂ac] adv. quickly; fast; soon.
drāgbhṛtaka [bhṛtaka] n. water just drawn from the well.
drākṣā f. bot. Vitis vinifera, vine; grape — amn drākṣa f. drākṣī made from grapes.
drākṣāpāka [pāka] n. lit. poetry very easy to understand (like grapes that can be eaten without preparation); opp. kadalīpāka, nārikelapāka.
drākṣāphala | phala | n. grapes.
drākṣāmat |mat| amnf drākṣāmatī provided with grapes.
drākṣārasa | rasa | m. grape juice; wine.
drākṣālatā [latā] f. vine.
drākṣāvana | vana | n. vineyard.
drākṣāsava [sava₁] m. med. [Ayurveda] wine, marc.
√ drāgh [related to dīrgha] v. [1] pr. r. (drāghate) to stretch, to lengthen — ca. (dhrāgayati) to stretch, to go; to delay, to be slow | ang. drag; all. tragen; lat. trahere; fr. tracter.
drāghiṣṭha [super. dīrgha] amnf drāghiṣṭhā the longest; the furthest; syn. dīrghatama.

drāghīyas [compar. dīrgha] amnf drāghīyasī longer; further away; syn. dīrghatara. yad drāghīyas tat tadeva hrasīyo yan nedīyas tad davīyas tadaiva | yat kṣodīyas tan mahīyas tadānīm citrākāram dṛśyate viśvam etat | [Bhāvanāpuruṣottama] What is very long is in fact very short; What is very near is suddenly very far; what is tiny is now immense; thus everything can be seen in various ways (like a painting).
drār [ca. druh₁] v. [10] pr. (drārayati) endure.
drāv [ca. Dru₁] v. [10] pr. (drāvayati) to make run, to put to flight, to chase away | to make flow, to melt.
drāva |act. Dru₁| mr. leak.
drāvaṇa |agt. drāv| amnf drāvaṇī that makes run, that puts to flight — act. n. act of putting to flight | diluent.
Drāviḍa [*draviḍa] amnf drāviḍā relating to the Dravidians; not. Drāvida country on the Coromandel coast south of the Godāvarī | pl. drāviḍās its inhabitants; their mythical ancestor is Yadu.
drumat [mat] amnf drumatī supplied in wood | made of wood.
drugdha [pp. druh₁] amnf drugdhā haï; offended, violated. drugdham (impers.) there has been damage.

druta [pp. Dru₁] amnf drutā rapid; agile | fluid | phon. tempo of pronunciation too fast; opp. vilambita — n. phon. measure of time of a half mora [mātrā], worth 2 breves [anudruta] mus. accompanied rhythm (a strike of the instrument and a wave). drutam adv. rapidly.
drutatara [tara] amnf drutatarā compar. faster. drutataram adv. very quickly; as fast as possible.
drutavilambita | vilambita | n. lit. poetic meter "alternating fast and slow".

Drupada [Dru₃pada] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Drupada "Pillar" son of Pṛṣata, king of the Pañcālās; his capital was Kāmpilyā; he studied at the hermitage of Bharadvāja with Drona; he wished for a son, and made great penances to pray to SambhuSiva who announced to him that he would have a daughter who would become a man; he spilled his seed in the sight of the nymph Menakā; a very pretty girl was born to him, for whom the rites were performed as for a boy under the name of Sikhandī; Drona taught her the art of war; then she was married to the daughter of King Hiranyavarmā, who, learning of the deception, wanted to wage war against Drupada; Sikhandinī withdrew to a forest where the yakṣa Sthūṇakarṇa agreed that they would exchange sexes; thus war was avoided and Sikhandinī became an illustrious warrior alongside the Pāṇḍavās; upon his accession to the throne, Drupada despised his former fellow student Drona, who was only a poor Brahmin; the latter, with the help of the Pāṇḍavās, took him prisoner and confiscated the part of his kingdom north of the Ganges; he implored revenge by a Vedic crucifixion, in the fire of which Drau padī and Dhṛṣṭadyumna were born, destined to kill Drona; he participated in the war alongside the Pāṇḍavās and was killed by Drona; cf. Yajñasena, Pārṣata.
drupadaputra | putra | mr. myth. | Mah. | n.p. of Dru padaputra, epith. of Dhṛṣṭadyumna “son of Drupa da”.
Druma [Dru₃ma] m. tree |myth. n.p. of Druma, king of almost men |kinnarās| | gr. δρυμος.
druh₁ [agt. druh₁] amnf [sg. name. dhruk] hostile, enemy.

√ druh₁ v. [4] pr. (drúhyati) pp. (drugdha) pf. (anu, abhi) to be hostile to, to hate, to want to harm; to seek to harm, to do violence to, to offend (dat. g. loc. acc. rangle — ca. (drārayati) to support || lat. trux.
druhyú |yu₃| m. myth. np. of Druhyu "the Stranger", eldest son of Yayāti and Sarmiṣṭhā, brother of Puru and Anu | pl. myth. the people of the druhyavas or strangers of the East.
drógha [agt. druh₁] iic. ill-intentioned; false.
droghavāc | vāc | amnf whose word Is deceptive.

dróṇa [dru₁na] m. bucket, trough, container (made of wood); soma bowl | bushel, measure of capacity and weight of grain; a Drona is worth 4 quarts |ādhaka| (about 14 l); there are 3 in a minot [khāra] measure of area (the area of a field sown with a Drona of wheat) | myth. [Mah.] np. from the Brahmin Drona "(Born in a) cup", from the seed of the hermit Bharadvāja poured in the sight of the nymph | apsaras | Ghṛtācī; he is an incarnation of Brhaspati; he acquired the science of weapons from his father and the hermit Agnivesa; he married Kṛpī who bore him a son, Aśvatthāmā; He met Paraśurāma on Mount Mahendra₁; the latter gave him his weapons and taught him the art of archery |dhanurveda|; very poor, he went to the Pañcālās to ask for assistance from King Drupada, his former companion in study, but the latter rejected him; he then went to Hastināpura, where, upon hearing of his exploits, Bhīṣma engaged him as tutor and master of arms to the princes Kauravās and Pāṇḍavās; as a price for his lessons, he demanded the capture of Drupada, whose half of the kingdom he confiscated; Having predicted that no archer would be better than his pupil Arjuna, he learned that Ekalavya had surpassed him by training alone before a statue of himself, even though he had refused to teach this low-caste hunter [niṣāda]; he then demanded, as the price of his knowledge, that he mutilate his right thumb; he made Arjuna swear that he could face him in combat without feeling remorse for fighting his master; when the conflict broke out between the cousin princes, he favored the Pāndavās and gave his blessing to Yudhisthira, but he had sided with the Kauravās, whose general he became in

leader [senādhipati] after the defeat of Bhīṣma; he annihilated the army of the Pāṇḍavās and killed many heroes, including Drupada and Virāṭa; he was invincible as long as he wielded his weapons; discouraged by the false news of the death of his son Aśvatthāmā (a half-truth by Yudhisthira, at the instigation of Kṛṣṇa, announcing to him the death of a mononymous elephant killed by Bhīma), he laid down his arms, entered a state of yoga, and was instantly beheaded by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, who thus fulfilled his father's curse; his son Aśvatthāmā avenged him with a general massacre. [Mah.] np. of Drona, one of the śārngakās — f. dronī gutter | container; bucket.
dronaparvan [parvan] n. bed. n.p. of Dronaparva, 7th book of Mah., "of Drona".
droṇi [dru₁ni] f. tub; bucket, bucket.
droha [act. druh₁] m. hostility, hatred, ill will; treachery, perfidy, betrayal.
drohavacana [vacana] n. abusive language.
drohin [agt. dru₁] amnf drohinī malevolent | treacherous towards, hostile towards g. iic. .
Drauni [*Drona] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Drauni, patr. of Aśvatthāmā "son of Drona"; at the end of the war, he massacres in their sleep all the sons of Draupadī, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Sikhaṇdī.

Draupadī [*Drupada] f. myth. [Mah.] patr. of the princess Draupadī "daughter of King Drupada", of the country pañcāla [Pāñcālī]; she was born from the fire sacrifice sky, with her brother Dhṛṣṭadyumna, in the pit of the altar [yajñakuṇḍa] of a sacrifice of Drupada; she embodies the goddess Srī; she is also called Kṛṣṇā "dark-skinned"; at her svayamvara in Kāmpilya she chose Arjuna, but became the common wife of the Pāṇḍavās to fulfill the promise of Iśāna to In drasenā₁, and by order of Kuntī that her son Ar juna share his property with his brothers; She had 5 sons: Prativindhya by Yudhisthira, Srutasoma by Bhīma, Srutakīrti by Arjuna, Satānīka by Nakula and SrutakarmāSrutasena by Sahadeva; when King Yudhisthira lost his kingdom at dice, she was insulted and humiliated by Duḥśāsana in front of her husbands; during exile with King Virāta she disguised herself as the sairandhrī Mālinī₁, and was assaulted by Kīcaka; all her sons were killed by Aśvatthāmā at the end of the war; when Dharmarāja decided on their renunciation [tyāga], she followed her husbands on their journey to heaven, but died on the way, her dharma not being perfect, for she secretly preferred Arjuna; cf. Pārsatī, Yājñasenī.
draupadeya [Draupadīeya] m. pl. drau padeyās myth. [Mah.] the 5 sons of Draupadī: Prativindhya, Šrutasoma, Šrutakīrti, Šatānīka and Srutasena.
dva cf. dvi.

dvandvá var. dvaṃdva [red. dva] n. pair, couple; duality | quarrel, fight, duel; alternative, dilemma — m. [dvandvasamāsa] gram. copulative compound word (dual or plural); not. pair of opposing notions. dvandvam var. dvandve, dvandvena adv. in pairs, two by two, face to face | aside, secretly. sāmānyabhūmipau du. (copulative compound) the common and the king. aśvāvyustrāh pl. horses, sheep, and camels.
dvandvagīta [gīta] n. duet singing.
dvandvamoha [moha] m. phil. illusion of dualities.
dvandvavāda [vāda] m. dialectic.
dvandvasamāsa [samāsa] m. gram. copulative compound word (dual or plural); not. pair of opposing notions.
dvandvin var. dvaṃdvin [dvandvain] amnf dvandvinī forming a pair | adversary, op posing, antagonist. āvām pratidvamdvinau bhavāva Let's organize a competition between the two of us.
dvaya | dvaya | amnf dvayī double; of two kinds — n. pair, couple — ifc. the two, the pair of (iic.) — f. dvayā ifc. id. dvayam adv. doubly. daladvaya n. the two pieces (sg.).
dvayasá ifc. amnf dvayasī of the size of, of width, of depth, up to (iic.).
dvayos [loc. dva] ind. gram. refers to a word usable with the masculine and feminine genders.
dvā iic. dva.
dvācatvāriṃśa [catvāriṃśa] amnf dvācatvārimsī ord. 42ᵉ.
dvācatvāriṃśat [catvāriṃśat] f. pl. 42 | var. dvācatvārimsati id.
dvātrimsá | trimsa | amnf dvātrimsī ord. 32nd made up of 32 parts.
dvātriṃśat [triṃśat] f. pl. 32.
dvātriṃśatputtalikā [puttalikā] f. bed. n.p. from the Dvātriṃśatputtalikā, Tale of the Thirty-Two Statues of the Throne of Vikramāditya; cf. Simhāsanadvātrimsikā.
dvātriṃśati | triṃśati | f. collection of 32 elements.
dvātriṃśikā [triṃśikā] f. collection of 32 elements.
dvānavata [navata] amnf dvānavatī ord. 92°.
dvānavati [navati] f. pl. 92.
dvāpañcāśa [pañcāśa] amnf dvāpañcāśī ord. 52^ e.
dvāviṃśá [viṃśa] amnf dvāviṃśī ord. 22ᵉ.
dvāviṃśati |viṃśati| f. pl. 22.f.
dvāviṃśatitamī [tama] amn dvāviṃśatitamī ord. 22ᵉ.
dvāṣaṣṭá |ṣaṣṭa| amnf dvāṣaṣṭī 62°.
dvāsasti |sasti| f. 62; syn. dvisasti.
dvāṣaṣṭitama |tama| amnf dvāṣaṣṭitamī 62°.
dvāsaptata |saptata| amnf dvāsaptatī ord. 72ᵉ.
dvāsaptati |saptati| f. 72; syn. dvisaptati.
dvāsaptatitama |tama| amnf dvāsaptati tamī 72ᵉ.
dvāh iic. dvār. dvāḥstha var. dvāstha |stha| mr. doorman, guard.

dvādaśá [dvādaśan] amnf dvādaśī ord. 12ᵉ | in 12 parts; 12 times; augmented by 12 — n. dozen — f. dvādaśī astr. 12th day of a fortnight soc. festival day of the 12th day of the bright fortnight | śuklapakṣa|, preparing for the full moon festival; it is dedicated to the tulasī; phālgunī dvādaśī inaugurates the festival of holī | soc. festival day of the 12th day of the dark fortnight [kṛṣṇapakṣa]; cf. gurudvādaśī.
Dvādaśalakṣaṇī [lakṣaṇa] f. bed. n.p. from the Dvādaśalakṣaṇī or dvādaśādhyāyī, forming the Mīmāmsāsūtra “in twelve chapters” of Jaimini; it is also called Tantrakānda.
Dvādaśastotra [stotra] n. lit. np. of the Dvādaśastotra, devotional poem in 12 parts by Madhvācārya in adoration of Kṛṣṇa.
dvādaśādhyāyī [adhyayī] f. bed. n.p. from the dvādaśādhyāyī of Jaimini; cf. Dvādaśalakṣaṇī.
dvādaśānta [anta] m. phil. [Trika] psychic center [cakra] located 12 fingers above the brahma randhra.
dvādaśāra | ara | amnf dvādaśārā (Wheel) with 12 spokes.
Dvādaśāranayacakra [nayacakra] n. lit. np. of the Dvādaśāranayacakra "Wheel of 12 Viewpoints", work of the jaina Mallavādī, also called Nayaca kra.
Dvādaśārka [arka] m. myth. np. of Dvādaśārka or Dvādaśāditya, combining the 12 aspects |āditya| of the Sun.
dvādaśāhá |aha₂| amnf dvādaśāhā which lasts 12 days — m. soc. rite of 12 days of purification of a yajamāna during his dīkṣā to participate in the śrauta ritual.
dvādaśan [dvadaśan] num. pers. pl. twelve | lat. duadecim.

dvāpara [dvaapara₂] m. soc. throw of a 2; side of the die marked 2 | lit. [KSS.] np. of the evil genius dvāpara, demon of the game like Kali; he possesses the body of Puşkarākhya, younger brother of Nala, as Kali possesses that of Nala — n. cf. dvāparayuga.
dvāparayuga [yuga] n. phil. 3rd age of the world, bronze age; its king in it is Krishna; |Ram.| the vaishyas acquire the right to practice asceticism |tapasya|; |Mah.| he is personified by Sakuni.
dvār f. door, gate; entrance | (in fig.) opportunity, means | gr. v ; lat. fores; ang. door; all. Thor. dvārā adv. ifc. by means of (iic.).

dvāra [dvāra] n. door, portal; entrance, opening | passage; means of access | phil. [Yoga] door of perception of the human body; there are 9: 2 eyes, 2 ears, 2 nostrils, mouth, anus, urethra plus the fontanelle; each door accesses a psychic channel |nādī|. dvāreņa adv. ifc. by means of, according to (iic.).

dvāraka [ka] n. gate, portal — f. cf. Dvārakā. dvārapaņdita [paṇḍita] m. bd. scholar's title "Master of the Gate" at Vikramaśīla monastery; there were 6 of them; in the 11th century, they were: Ratnākaraśānti to the East, Vāgīśvarakīrti to the West, Ratnavajra and Jñānaśrīmitra at the central gates, Nāropa to the North and Prajñākaramati to the South.

dvārapāla [pāla] m. gatekeeper, guard | arch. guardian of the gate of a sanctuary | myth. yakṣa guardian of the. dvārapālau myth. Jaya₁ and Vijaya₁, the two guards of Vișnu, at the entrance to the Vaikuntha; one day they refused access to the four eternally young [sanakādi]; the latter threw them as

The curse [abhiśāpa] of having to relive the experience on Earth; Vishnu gave them the choice between being reborn six times like his servants, or three times like his enemies; to shorten the ordeal they chose the second path, and returned to Earth, first as Hiranyakasipu and Hiranyākṣa in the kṛtayuga, then as Rāvaņa and Kumbhakarņa in the tretāyuga, and finally as Siśupāla and Dantavakra (or Kaṃsa) in the dvāparayuga. | myth. Nanda and Sunanda, guardians of Shiva's temple. The two guardians are depicted on either side of the entrance to the sanctuary.
dvārapālikā | pālikā | f. arch. guardian of the door of a sanctuary.
dvārabali |bali| m. leftover food deposited near the door.
dvārabalibhuj [bhuj₃] m. ["who eats leftovers"] crow; sparrow.
dvārarakṣa | rakṣa | m. gatekeeper.

dvāravat |vat| amnf dvāravatī with many doors — f. dvāravatī name of city capital myth. n.p. from dvāravatī, capital of Kṛṣṇa; cf. Dvārakā | geo. n.p. from dvāravatī₁, capital of the Mon empire, to Nakhon Pathom in mod. Thailand (7th to 11th centuries).
dvārastha | stha | amnf dvārasthā who stands at the door — m. doorkeeper, usher.

Dvārakā [f. dvāraka] f. myth. [Mah.] np. of the city of Dvārakā "with the great gates", capital of the kingdom of Kṛṣṇa after he was driven out of Ma thurā by demons, located west of Gurjara; it is also called dvāravatī and Anartapura; it is said to have been swallowed up by the waters seven days after the death of Kṛṣṇa; near it is the seat of the paścimāmnāya maṭha founded by Saṅkara₁; it is one of the 7 sacred cities |saptapurī|.
dvārakānātha [nātha] m. hist. np. of the mathematician dvārakānātha (16th century), author of the Śulbadīpikā, commentary on the Baudhāyana śulbasūtra.
dvāstha |related to dvār| m. gate.
dvi num. pers. du. [m. nom. dvau; f. nom. dve; n. nom. dve; en comp. dvā, dvi deux || gr. δvo; lat. duo; ang. two; all. zwei; fr. deux.
dvikaraṇī [karaṇī] f. math. diagonal of a square.
dvikarmaka [karmaka] amnf dvikarmikā gram. refers to a verb admitting two accusative complements; one is called the main [mukhya], the other
secondary [gauna].
dvikūṭa [kūṭa] amnf dvikūṭā arch. refers to a temple with two sanctuaries.
dvigangam [gangā] ind. at the confluence of the two Ganges.
dvigata | gata | amnf dvigatā ambiguous.

dvigu [gu] amnf at the price of two cows | who has two cows — m. gram. [generic] category of appositional compound [karmadhāraya] whose first term is a number, like dvigu in the sense of a value; on the other hand, in its possessive sense, it is a bahuvrīhi. dviguņa [guṇa] amnf dviguṇā double; of two kinds | folded (clothing) | twice as much, twice as large as (abl.) | (music) in the upper octave — adv. dviguṇā doubly; twice as much. dviguņākṛ to plow twice. dvigunāya to become double. dvigunīkr to double. dvigunībhū to become double; to increase. dvigunībhāva (music) passing in the upper octave.
dvigunita [gunita] amnf dvigunitā doubled.
dvicatvārimsat [catvārimsat] f. 42.

dvija [ja] amnf dvijā twice born — m. soc. Aryan man, from one of the first 3 |varna| classes, having accomplished upanayana; cf. brahma janman | bird, oviparous animal in gen. | tooth | myth. the Moon; cf. Atri.
dvijottama | uttama | amnf dvijottamā super. the best of the brahmins | soc. chief priest.
dvijāti [jāti] amnf of Aryan origin. dvijātīnām adhyayanam ijyā dānam The Aryans must study the Veda, perform the Vedic rites and give to the Brahmins.
dvijānu [jānu] amnf (water) up to both knees.
dvijihva [jihvā] amnf dvijihvā [“who has two tongues” | liar.
dvitala | tala | amnf dvitalā arch. two-story.
dvitra |tri| amnf dvitrā pl. two or three.
dvitri | tri | amnf pl. two or three.
dvidandin [dandin] amnf dvidandinī who carries two sticks (said of beggars).
dvidaśa |daśan| amnf dvidaśī pl. two dozen; 20.
dvidhāra |dhāra₂| amnf dvidhārā divided into two streams.
dvinavata | navata | amnf dvinavatī ord. 92ᵉ.
dvinavati | navati | f. 92.
dvinavatitama [tama] amnf dvinavatitamī ord. 92ᵉ.
dvipa |pa₁| m. elephant |"that drinks in 2 drinks" | (with the trunk and the mouth).
dvipendra [indra] m. myth. np. of dvipendra, epith. of Airāvata "King of elephants".
dvipañcāśa | pañcāśa | amnf dvipañcāśī ord. 52ᵉ — n. 2 times 50.
dvipañcāśat [pañcāśat] f. 52.
dvipañcāśattama [tama] famn dvipañcāśattamī ord. 52ᵉ.
dvipád [pad₂] amnf [nom. dvipāt] biped.

dvipada | pada | amnf dvipadā gram. consisting of 2 words; containing 2 words | two feet long (brick) | biped — m. ["two-legged beast"] (pej.) man — f. dvipadā stanza [rc₂] two feet — f. dvipadī phon. ved. meter prākṛta; verses in this meter | female biped.
dvipari |pari| ind. missed bet of two (not. in the game pañcaka).
dvípāda | pāda | amnf dvipādā which has two feet.
dvipādya [ya] amnf dvipādyā which is worth double — n. double punishment.
dviprahara | prahara | mr. soc. morning shift (8 a.m. to 11 a.m.).
dvibhuja | bhuja | mr. math. corner.
dvimīdha [mīdha] m. myth. np. of Dvimīdha, second son of Brhatputra.
dvimuni | muni | ind. gram. (n.) The two Sages of the Sanskrit grammatical tradition (Pāṇini and Patañjali₁).
dvirada [rada] amnf dviradā which has two tusks — m. elephant.
dvirūpá [rūpa] amnf dvirūpā which admits two forms; double; bicolor | (word) written in two different ways.
dvirūpakoṣa [koṣa] m. lit. lexicon of orthographic variants; not. np. of the dvirūpakoṣa of Purusottamadeva.
Dvirūpadhvanisamgraha [dhvanisamgraha] m. lit. np. from the lexicon of orthographic variants Dvirūpadhvanisamgraha from Bharatamal lika/Bharatasena, (Bengal, around 1600).

dvirepha [repha] m. bio. ["shaped like 2 letters 'r'"] | large black hymenopteran; bee. dvayor eva nāmni rephayor bhavād bhramaram dvi repha ityācakṣate Because there are two 'r's in its name, the bee [bhramara] is called 'double'.
dvivacana [vacana] n. gram. dual and its declension suffixes. dvivarșa | varșa | amnf dvivarșā aged two years — f. dvivarṣā two-year-old heifer.
dvividha [vidha] amnf dvividhā of two kinds — adv. dvividhā in two ways.
dviveda [veda] amnf dvivedī who masters 2 Vedas.
dvivedin [vedin] amnf dvivedinī who masters 2 Vedas.
dviśata [śata] n. 200 — f. dviśatī id.
dvisasti [sasti] f. 62; syn. dvāsasti.
Dvisandhāna [sandhāna] n. amalgamation of two compounds | lit. poetic device with a dual purpose, invented by Dhanañjaya₁ and theorized by Bhoja₁.
dvisandhānakavi [kavi] m. "poet of the double narration", epith. of Dhanañjaya₁.

dvisandhānakāvya [kāvya] n. lit. poem narrating two stories simultaneously; not. np. of the dvisandhānakāvya or Dvisandhāna mahākāvya of Dhanañjaya₁, combining the Mah. and the Rām. through the process of coalescence | ślesa | ; cf. dvyar thakāvya.
dvisandhi | sandhi | amnf composed of two parts | gram. which admits an ambiguous sandhi.
dvisaptata |saptata| amnf dvisaptatī ord. 72ᵉ.
dvisaptati |saptati| f. 72.
dvisaptatitama |tama| amnf dvisaptatitamī ord. 72ᵉ.
dvisapha | śapha | amnf dvisaphā bio. ungulate animal with divided hoof.
dvihāyana [hāyana] amnf dvihāyanī two years old — f. dvihāyanī two-year-old cow.
dvihrdayā [hrdaya] f. pregnant woman.
dvika [dvika] amnf dvikā double; doubled augmented by two | which arrives for the 2nd time.
dvitá [dvita] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Dvita "Second", son of Gautama, unworthy brother of Trita; he was transformed into a monkey.
dvitaya [dvitaya] amnf dvitayī [m. pl. nom. dvitaye dvitayās] double, consisting of two parts; the two — n. pair, couple.
dvitā [dvitā] f. fact of being double; duality — adv. all the more reason; precisely; certainly, especially.

dvitīya [dviīya] amnf dvitīyā ord. second, Second | astr. (month) intercalary — ifc. having for Second, accompanied by, provided with (iic.) — m. second son of the family | phon. second phoneme of a varga (voiceless aspirated consonant) — n. ifc. half of — f. dvitīyā accompanying, close friend; wife (other self) | gram. accusative (2nd case of declension) | astr. second tithi of a pakṣa.
dvitīyaka [ka] amnf dvitīyikā which needs to be done twice | (fever) manifesting every two days. dvitīyakam granthagrahanam acquisition of a knowledge to see on the second reading.
dvitīyatatpurusa [tatpurusa] m. gram. compound determinative word derived from the accusative of its first member, like grāmagatah.

dvitīyarājataranginī [rājataranginī] f. lit. of the dynastic epic of Kaśmīra np. Dvitīyarājatarangiņī of Jonarāja (1412), also called Rājāvali; it follows the Rājataraṃgiņī of Kalhaṇa; it was continued by his student Srīvara (1477).
dvitva [dvitva] n. phil. duality | gram. dual.
dvitvavat [vat] amnf dvitvavatī possessing a double character.
dvidhā [dvidhā] adv. doubly, 2 times; in 2 parts; in 2 ways.
dvir iic. dvis.
dvirukta [ukta] amnf dviruktā repeated.

dviṣ₁át [ppr. dviṣ₁] amnf dviṣatī hateful; hostile to, enemy of (acc. g.) — m. enemy. caurasya dvisan var. cauram dvisan who hates the thief. ਫ਼ਿੲ dviṣṭa [pp. dviṣ₁] amnf dviṣṭā hated, detested, odious, hostile. dvis [dvi] adv. twice, on two occasions | ang. twice.

dvīpa [dviap] mn island | myth. continent; mythical geography lists 7: in the center the jambu, then the kuśa, the plakṣa, the śālmali, the krauñca, the śāka₁ and the puṣkara | one of the 10 regions forming the Jambudvīpa.
dvīpin [dvīpain] amnf dvīpinī spotted ["having islands (on the skin or fur)"] — m. leopard, panther, tiger.
dvedhā [dvidhā] adv. doubly, 2 times; in 2 parts; in 2 ways; syn. dvidhā.

dveṣa [act. dviṣ₁] m. hatred; disgust, aversion (opp. icchā) | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] the property [guṇa] of aversion — ifc. antipathy for, aversion to (iic.). dvesam kr to manifest one's aversion towards dat. .
dvesabhakti [bhakti] f. phil. hatred turned into devotion; cf. vairabhakti.
dveṣaṇa [act. dviṣ₁ɪ] n. hatred; disgust, aversion (towards (g. iic.)) — agt. amnf dveṣaṇā ved. enemy.
dveṣas [abstr. dviṣ₁] n. aversion, hatred.
dveṣin [agt. dviṣ₁ɪ] amnf dveṣiṇī enemy; hostile (towards (g. iic.)).
dvestr [agt. dvis₁] amnf dvestrī enemy; hostile (towards (iic.)).
dveṣya [pfp. [1] dviṣ₁] amnf dveṣyā to abhor rer, to hate; odious, detestable — m. enemy — n. nutmeg.
dvesyatā [tā] f. state of being odious; disfavor, rejection.
dvesyatva |tva| n. the state of being odious; disfavor, rejection.
dvaitá [*dvita] n. phil. dualism, duality; triune doctrine preached by Madhva.
Dvaitavana | vana | n. bed. | Kirātārjunīya | n.p. from the Dvaitavana forest where the Pāṇḍavās spent their exile.
dvaitavādin | vādin | m. soc. follower of dualism; not. disciple of Madhva.
dvaitādvaita [advaita] n. phil. duality in non-duality, doctrine preached by Nimbārka.
dvaitin [in] m. cf. dvaitavādin.

dvaidha [*dvidhā] amnf dvaidhā double; bipartite — n. duality; duplicity; division; separation into two | dispute; argument; doubt, uncertainty | duplicated object; reserve. dvaidham in two parts; doubling; in two ways. dvaidhībhū to separate into two.
dvaidhī iiv. dvaidha.

dvaidhībhāva [bhāva] m. division into two parts; choice between alternatives | not. division of troops, one of the 6 acts of a king in war [sadguna]. dhṛtadvaidhībhāvakātaram me manaḥ my mind is seized with anxiety due to uncertainty.
dvaipa₁ [*dvīpa] amnf dvaipā relating to an island, inhabitant of an island.
Dvaipāyana₁ [āyana] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Dvaipāyana₁ "Born on an island", epith. of Vyāsa (born on an island of the Yamunā).
dvaipa₂ [*dvipa] amnf dvaipā relating to elephants.
Dvaipāyana₁ [āyana₁] n. myth. [Mah.] name of Lake Dvaipāyana₁ "where elephants go to drink"; Du ryodhana took refuge there after losing the great battle.
dvaipya [*dvīpaya] amnf dvaipyā who has bitten an island.
dvaividhya [*dvividhaya] n. double nature, duplicity; variance.
dvy iic. dvi.
dvyartha | artha | amnf dvyarthā with a double meaning.
dvyarthakāvya [kāvya] n. lit. poem with double meaning, using the ślesa process; syn. dvisandhānakāvya; cf. Dhanañjaya₁, Rāmacarita₁.
dvyaśīta | aśīta | amnf dvyaśītī ord. 82ᵉ.
dvyaśīti [aśīti] f. 82.
dvyaśītitama |tama| amnf dvyaśītitamī ord. 82^ e.
dvyasta | astan | n. copper.
dvyahá [ahan] m. period of 2 days — amnf dvyahā which lasts 2 days — adv. for 2 days; after 2 days. dvyahatarşam | tarşam | adv. having been thirsty for 2 days.
dvyahātyāsam | atyāsam | adv. two days later | every three days. dvyahātyāsam gāḥ pāyayati He waters the cows after a period of two days.
dvyāyuṣa |āyus| n. double human lifespan.
dvyāhika [āhika] amnf dvyāhikā (recurrent fever) every two days. dh
dhakāra |(Dha)kāra| mr. the sound or letter 'Dha'.
dhattūra m. bio. |bot. datura alba| datura, a solanaceous plant whose root contains a hallucinogenic drug; its flower is associated with Shiva; cf. mo hana — n. bio. its fruit || lat. datura.
dhattūraka [ka] mf dhattūrakā decoction of datura for the purpose of intoxication. dhattūrakasaṃyuktam madyamānayata drutam lit. KSS. Quickly bring wine mixed with datura.

dhána [act. dhā₁] n. goods, possessions; wealth | wealth, an āyādi — v. [11] pr. (dhanāyati) to desire money — v. [11] pr. (dhanīyati) to desire to be rich. dhanam ji to win the prize; to win the battle. yato dharmastato dhanam |SRBh.| Where justice reigns, there is prosperity. vidyādhanam sarvadhanapradhānam Knowledge is the most important wealth.
Dhanaka [ka] m. avarice, greed | lit. [DKC.] np. of Dhanaka, eldest of the three rich men of the country Trigarta; his brothers are Dhānyaka and Dhanyaka.
dhanatrayodaśī [trayodaśī] f. cf. dhanvantari trayodaśī.
Dhanapati [pati] m. myth. np. of Dhanapati "Master of treasures", epith. of Kubera.
dhanapatisakha [sakhi] m. myth. epith. of Siva "Friend of Kubera".
dhanamitra [mitra] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Dha namitra "Friend of riches", son of a rich merchant; he squandered his fortune through generosity |Udāraka|; he is the Friend of Apahāravarmā.
dhanalubdha [lubdha] amnf dhanalubdhā greedy for riches.

dhanavat [vat] amnf dhanavatī rich, wealthy — f. dhanavatī lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī Dha navatī, wife of King Siṃha₁, mother of Candasiṃha and Ajinavatī, whom she gave as a wife to Na ravāhanadatta.
dhanavrddha | vrddha | amnf dhanavrddhā rich, fortunate.
dhanasampatti |sampatti| f. abundance of wealth.
dhanāgama [āgama] m. revenue ["acquisition of wealth".
dhanādhipati [adhipati] m. myth. “master of wealth”, epith. from Kubera.
dhanādhyakṣa [adhyakṣa] m. soc. superintendent of the treasury | myth. epith. from Kubera.
Dhaneśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Dhaneśvara, epith. of Kubera "Lord of treasures".

dhanam [acc. dhana] iic. dhanamjaya var. dhanañjaya [jaya] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of dhanañjaya, epith. of Arjuna "Conqueror of riches" | hist. np. of dhanañjaya₁, Digambara Jain poet who lived in the Deccan around 800; he invented the style of double narration [dvisandhāna] with his poem Dvisandhānakāvya which combines the Mah. and the Rām. thanks to the double meaning [śleṣa]; He is also credited with the Nāmamālā lexicon, the Anekārthanāmamālā homonym lexicon, the devotional poem Viṣāpahārastotra, and the rhetorical work Daśarūpaka in which he develops a theory of the 10 dramatic genres | hist. np. de dhanañjaya₂ Bhaṭṭācārya, author of the synonym dictionary Paryāyaśabdaratna.
Dhanika [dhanaika] amnf dhanikā riche — m. hist. n.p. of the scholar Dhanika (11th century); we owe him the Avaloka, commentary on the Daśarūpaka. janmanā dhanikaḥ rich by birth.
dhanin [dhanain] amnf dhaninī rich.
dhanistha [great. dhanin] amnf dhanisthā very rich — f. dhanistha astr. n.p. of Dhanisthā "Richest", 22nd nakṣatra; cf. Śravisthā.
Dhanu [dhanus] m. arc | astr. zodiacal sign [rāśi] and constellation of Sagittarius; syn. taukṣika | sandy shore, beach — f. dhanū id.
dhanuyātrā [yātrā] f. soc. (Orissa) a week-long festival during the month of Pausa; it celebrates the visit of Krishna to Mathura; it ends with the sūryapūjā, on the day of Sāmbadaśamī.
dhanuḥ iic. dhanus.
dhanuḥśālā [śālā] f. hall of the archers.
dhanur iic. dhanus.
dhanurāsana [āsana] n. phil. [yoga] prone posture where one grasps one's toes with the hands to bring them to the ears while bending the body like a bow.
dhanurgraha [graha] m. ["who carries the bow"] Archer.
dhanurdanda [danda] m. of. the bow and the club.
dhanurdhara [dhara] m. Archer.
dhanurmāsa [māsa] m. astr. month of the solar calendar, beginning around December 15, and ending at makarasaṃkrānti.
dhanurveda [veda] m. bed. n.p. of dhanurveda or archery, a minor art | upaveda|.

dhanus iic. dhanus. Dhanuşmat [mat] m. ["equipped with a bow"] Archer. ekam hanyānna vā hanyādisuh ksipto dhanusmatā | prājñena tu matih kṣiptā hanyādgarbhagatānapi | | Arthaśāstra | The arrow shot by the Archer may kill a man or not; but the reflection of an intelligent man may kill even men yet to be born.

dhánus n. arc | astr. zodiacal sign [rāśi] and its constellation Sagittarius | [śakradhanus] myth. the rainbow, attribute of Indra | length measure, equal to 4 arms [hasta] (approximately 180 cm) — m. myth. np. of Dhanu/Dhanvin, epith. of Shiva "the Archer".

dhánya [dhanaya] amnf dhanyā who brings abundance | rich; happy; lucky charm — ifc. rich in (iic.) — n. felicity; blessing; rich fortune — f. dhanyā bio. bot. Coriandrum sativum, coriander | phil. [Tantra] np. of dhanyā, one of the 8 divine powers | yoginī|. dhanyo'si adr. blessed soistu.
dhanyaka [ka] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of dhanyaka, younger brother of the three rich men of the country Trigarta; his brothers are Dhanaka and Dhānyaka, his wife Dhūminī.
dhanyavāda [vāda] m. thanks; compliment, praise. dhanyavādāḥ adr. thank you!
dhanyāka [ka] n. coriander.

dhanvan [dhanus] n. bow | rainbow — ifc. who carries a bow (iic.) — m. myth. np. of Dhanvā, son of Kāśa, king of Kāśi; long without an heir, he prayed to Abjadeva for many years, and obtained a son whom he named Dhanvantari₁; cf. Dīrghatapā.

Dhanvantari | tari | m. myth. np. of Dhanvantari "He who crossed the rainbow", divine physician, born from the churning of the ocean of milk [kṣīrodamathana], carrying the urn [kumbha] of ambrosia [amṛta]; he is said to have brought Ayurveda; born after the gods, he cannot be rewarded by sacrifice |yajñabhāga| like them, but can be invoked as Abja deva; Viṣṇu resurrected him at the dvāparayuga as the son Dhanvantari₁ of King Dhanvā; he taught Ayurveda to his disciples, notably Suśruta; Ketumān is his son | hist. np. of Dhanvantari₂, medical author, one of the nine jewels [navaratna] of the court of King Vikramāditya. dhanvantaritrayodaśī var. dhanatrayodaśī [trayodaśī] f. soc. 13th day of the dark fortnight |kṛṣṇapakṣa| of the month of kārttika; it is a festive day, preceding the festival of dīpāvali; it celebrates the primordial churning [kṣīrodamathana], where Lakṣmī and Dhanvantari appeared; Lakṣmī is invoked on this day to wish for prosperity; mod. Dhan teras; it is a favorable day for business, for buying gold, jewelry, and new clothes; Kubera | kuberapūjā | is honored on this day; houses are decorated and domestic utensils are renewed; cf. Hima. dhanvantarinighanțu | nighanțu | m. lit. np. from the Dhanvantarinighantu, medical glossary attributed to Dhanvantari.
dhanvin [dhanusin] amnf dhanvinī Who holds a bow; Archer | myth. np. of dhanvin, epith. of Shiva "the Archer".
√ dham var. dhmā v. [1] pr. (dhamati) pft. (dadhmau) pp. (dhmātá, dhamita) pf. (ā, upa, pra) to blow; fan the fire by blowing; forge — ca. (dhmāpayati) to blow.
dhama [agt. dhmā] ifc. amnf dhamā Which blows (iic.).
dhammilla mn women's hairstyle composed of braids wrapped around the head.
dhaya [agt. dhā₂] ifc. amnf dhayā Who drinks (iic.). uddhaya amn Who drinks in one gulp. vidhaya amn Who drinks excessively.

Dhara |agt. dhṛ| amnf dharā ifc. That which bears, That which supports; That which transports; That which preserves — m. |bhūdhara| mountain | myth. epith. of Viṣṇu Kūrma; cf. Śrīdhara | myth. np. of Dhara the Earth, personified as one of the 8 Treasures | vasu| — f. cf. dharā.
dharaṇa [agt. dhṛ] amnf dharaṇī That which carries, That which supports; That which provides — m. dike — mn unit of weight (of various value) — f. cf. dharaṇī.
dharani [agt. dhr] f. myth. np. of Darani, the earth, personified as the wife of Dhruva.
dharanikśa | kośa | mr. bed. cf. Anekārtasāra.
dharanidāsa [dāsa] m. hist. np. of Dharanidāsa, poet of East India (early 12th century); he is the author of the dictionary of homonyms Anekārtasāra.
dharaṇī var. dharaṇi [f. dharaṇa] f. the earth.
dharanīdhara [Dhara] amnf dharanīdharā That which supports the earth — m. myth. np. of dharaṇīdhara, epith. of Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa or Seṣa "That which supports the earth".
dharaṇīmaṇḍala [maṇḍala] n. the terrestrial globe.
Dharasena₁ [senā] m. hist. n.p. of a Dha rasena line of kings of Vallabhī (7th century) | jn. n.p. of Dharasena₁, ancient Digambara ascetic, presumed author of the Şatkhandāgama.
