dharā [f. Dhara] f. the earth.
dháritrī [instr. dhṛ] f. ["She Who supports"] the earth.
dharúṇa [dhṛ] amnf dharuṇī That which carries, That which supports — n. base, foundation | the earth; the sky | container — f. dharunī receptacle.

dhárma [dharman] mn law, condition, inherent nature | physical law, natural order | soc. duty; legislation | religious duty; good, virtue; uprightness, rectitude; Justice, merit; ethics | phil. merit acquired by an act in accordance with the revealed word [śruti] | soc. the duty of one's caste, one of the aims of existence [puruṣārtha]; dharma is the traditional morality of India; it is codified in the laws of the dharmaśāstra; cf. svadharma, sādhāraṇadharma | phil. duty, right, and justice | phil. [Nyāya] trait; landmark; particularity; property, predicate | human quality | bd. the law, teaching of Buddha, one of the three Treasures [triratna] | bd. [abhidharma] analytical category of intrinsic existence; their interaction by causation explains conventional events | myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] dharma "the Just" personifying Justice and natural order; he is said to have sprung from the right nipple of Brahmā; [BhP.] he married 13 daughters of Dakṣa: Śraddhā, by whom he had sons Nara and Kāma, Maitrī, Dayā, Sānti, Puṣṭi, Tuṣṭi, by whom he had son Saṃtoṣa, Kriyā, by whom he had sons Danda, Naya and Vinaya [VP.], Unnati, Buddhi₁, Medhā, Titikṣā, Hrī and Mūrti; he is also said to be the husband of Ahiṃsā; [Mah.] Kuntī invoked him to conceive Yudhisthira, who was thus Dharmarāja, the Sovereign of dharma; he transformed himself into a dog to test him before his admission to Heaven; by the curse of Māṇḍavya, he himself was reincarnated as the śūdra Vidura | myth. epith. of Yama "the Judge (of the dead)" | pl. dharmās soc. civic and religious duties | bd. |Madhyamaka| phenomena, things (non-intrinsic designations) | lat. firmus; pali damma. dharmeṇa var. dharmāt according to the rule; regularly; justly; by the nature of the thing. dharmataḥ adv. according to one's duty. dharmam because to behave well. dhāraṇātmika iti dharmaḥ bd. Dharma is that which carries its own essence. Where Krishna is, there is righteousness; where righteousness is, there is victory. I know what is right, yet I do not do it; I know what is wrong, yet I do not refrain. Merit is that which is produced by the prescribed act.
dharmaka |ka| ifc. amnf dharmakā whose duty is (iic.).
dharmakartr | kartr | mr. soc. mod. administrative manager of a temple.
dharmakāya [kāya] m. bd. the "essential body", symbolizing the absolute Being present in the spiritual nature of every man; syn. vajrakāya.

Dharmakīrti [kīrti] m. bd. np. of Dharmakīrti "whose glory is the law", Buddhist philosopher and logician yogācārin of the mid-6th century, disciple of Dharmapāla at Nālandā; he is the author of influential works of epistemology, such as the Nyāyabindu, the Pramāṇavārttika, the Hetubindu and the Pramāṇaviniścaya; in them he elaborates and clarifies Dinnāga's theory of the means of knowledge; he discusses the bd. theory of impermanence in the Santānāntarasiddhi; he is also the author of the Sābdikābharaņa lexicon; he denied the principle of the plurality of causes, and the divine origin of the Veda; It is said that he won a debate with Śaṅkara₁ who threw himself into the Ganges; he is also credited with poems; cf. svabhāvahetu, vādanyāya | hist. np. du grammai rien Dharmakīrti₁ (Ceylon, 11th century), author of the Rūpāvatāra.
dharmakriyā [kriyā] f. soc. pious practice.
dharmakṣetra [kṣetra] n. myth. [Mah.] the Land of Duty; cf. kuruksetra. dharmaksetre kuruksetre |BhG.| on the Land of Kuru, on the Land of Duty.

dharmaguptaka | guptaka | m. bd. Dharma Guptaka school of Buddhism originating in Gandhāra, around the 1st century; it taught in gāndhārī (kharoṣṭhī script); via Khotan and the Silk Road it penetrated into China, Vietnam, Korea and Japan, while the Kuṣāṇa empire favoured the Sarvāstivāda sect.
dharmagrantha | grantha | m. lit. sacred book | mod. Bible.
dharmacakra [cakra] n. bd. "wheel of the law", symbol of Buddhist doctrine and of the universal dissemination of the Buddha's teachings | Pali dham macakka; Thai thammachak.
dharmacakrapura [pura] n. geo. n.p. by dharma cakrapura, bd site. from Telangāna, active from the 2nd to the 4th century; mod. Phanigiri hill, Surya pet district.

Dharmacakrapravartana | pravartana | n. bd. "setting in motion of the wheel of the law", episode of the Buddha's first sermon at Sāranātha; it is represented in iconography by a wheel with 8 spokes | lit. np. of the Dharmacakrapravartana sūtra, canonical teaching text by the Buddha of the Noble Path [āryamārga].

dharmacakramudrā [mudrā] f. bd. gesture of preaching, or of "starting the wheel of the law", evoking the Buddha's first sermon at Sāranātha (two hands in front of the chest, right palm outwards, thumb and index finger together, touching a finger of the left hand, whose palm is inwards, thumb and index finger together); cf. Vai rocana.
dharmacārin [cārin] amnf dharmacāriṇī who follows the law; who practices his duty.

dharmaja | ja | amnf dharmajā produced by justice | soc. specifically describes a judgment by trial: the Judge writes dharma on one piece of paper, adharma on another, and the accused will be declared innocent or guilty according to his choice.
dharmajijñāsā [jijñāsā] f. phil. search for the order of things; opp. brahmajijñāsā.
dharmajña [jña] amnf dharmajñā versed in the law; who knows duty.
dharmatā [tā] f. essence; inherent nature | bd. justice.
Dharmatrāta [trāta] m. hist. n.p. from the philosopher bd. Dharmatrāta of the 4th century, author of the Samyuktābhidharmahrdaya.
dharmatva [tva] n. essence; inherent nature; characteristic | soc. morality; piety.
dharmadughā [dughā] f. soc. cow whose milking is reserved for the needs of worship.
dharmadhvaja [dhvaja] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of the King of Mithilā dharmadhvaja Janaka "who has the law as his standard", son of Kuśadhvaja₁.
dharmanātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of dharmanātha "Master of the law", 15th mythical tīrthankara; his body is golden, his symbol is a lightning bolt; cf. Dharmaśarmābhyudaya.
dharmanibandha [nibandha] m. lit. genre of texts on dharma.
dharmaniyama [niyama] m. ["limitation for the sake of good"] meritorious discipline.
dharmapatnī [patnī] f. wife according to law.

dharmaparīṣā [parīṣā] f. lit. jaina treatise analyzing the inconsistencies of narratives in order to establish their credibility; a version of it is known in apabhramśa (988) and one in sanskrit (1014).

dharmapāla [Pāla] m. hist. np. of dharmapāla "Guardian of the Law", 6th century Buddhist religious and philosopher, born in Kāñcīpura, disciple of Dinnāga whom he succeeded as head of the University of Nālandā | hist. np. of King dharmapāla₁, who reigned from 770 to 810 over the Pāla Empire of Bengal founded by his father Gopāla₁; he founded the universities of Vikramaśīla, Somapura and Uddāntapurī; his son Devapāla succeeded him | lit. [DKC.] np. of dharmapāla₂, wise minister of King Rājahamsa; He is the father of Sumitra₁, Sumantra₁ and Kāmapāla.
dharmaputra [putra] m. myth. [Mah.] np. from dharmaputra, epith. of Yudhisthira “son of Dhar ma”.
dharmapramāṇa [pramāṇa] n. investigation of the law.
dharmapravicaya [pravicaya] m. bd. investigation of dharma.
dharmaprekṣā [prekṣā] amnf dharmaprekṣā who is concerned with righteousness.
dharmabhāṇaka [bhāṇaka] m. bd. reciting words of the Buddha.
dharmamegha [megha] m. phil. [yoga] ["cloud of virtue"] state of samādhi, giving perfect knowledge of prakrti .
dharmayuddha | yuddha | n. rules of ethics of fair combat; law of war | fight for justice; just war.

dhármarāja | rāja | mr. myth. n.p. of Dharmarāja, epith. of Yama "the Supreme Judge" | myth. [Mah.] epith. by Yudhisthira “King of Duty” | bd. holy King of Sambhala | var. dharmarāj id. | var. dharmarājan id.
dhármavat [vat] amnf dharmavatī ["respectful of dharma"] virtuous; pious; just.
dharmavattva [tva] n. state of virtue. parasparaanvayaprayojakadharmavattvam gram. [yogyatā] aptitude to promote a mutual relationship.
dhármavardhana | vardhana | amnf dharma vardhanā which makes virtue and justice prosper; myth. epith. of Shiva | lit. [DKC.] np. of King Dhar mavardhana of Śrāvastī; he is father of Navamālikā.
dhármavāṇijaka [vāṇijaka] m. religion merchant.
dhármavāṇijyaka [vāṇijyaka] m. religious merchant.
dharmavāda | vāda | m. legal discussion | soc. religious controversy.
dharmavijaya [vijaya] m. equitable conquest free from territorial greed.
dharmavid [vid₃] amnf who knows the law, who knows his duty | virtuous, just; pious.
dharmavīra [vīra] m. heroism of piety.
dharmavrddhi [vrddhi] f. soc. legal interest rate.

dharmavyādha [vyādha] m. lit. [Mah.] np. of dharmavyādha "whose duty is to hunt", wise game merchant of Mithila, who explains to the brahmin Kauśika₁ that moral obligations are relative to the situation, and not absolute.
Dharmaśarmābhyudaya [śarmaabhyudaya] m. bed. n.p. of Dharmaśarmābhyudaya, mahākāvya of Ha ricandra evoking the life of dharmanātha, in 21 cantos.
dharmaśālā [śālā] f. tribunal [“hall of the law”] | hospice, pilgrimage accommodation (mod. dharamśālā).
dharmaśāstra | śāstra | n. soc. code of good conduct | collection of laws, legal treatise and penal code; law; cf. manusmṛti, viṣṇusmṛti.
dharmasamkata [samkata] n. endangering the moral order. dharmasāvarņa [sāvarņa] m. myth. n.p. of Dhar masāvarņa, 11ᵉ Manu of the kalpa.
dharmasuta [suta₂] m. myth. [Mah.] np. from Dhar masuta, epith. of Yudhisthira “son of dharma”.
dharmasūtra |sūtra| n. bed. text of aphorisms of socio-religious laws [smrti].
Dharmasūri [sūri] m. hist. n.p. by the poetry theorist Dharmasūri (16th century), author of the Sāhityaratnākaramīmāmsā.
dharmahīna [hīna] amnf dharmahīnā contrary to the law; prohibited (said not. of pra tiloma marriages).
dharmātman | ātman | amnf dharmātmanī ver tueux, juste; bien intentionné; opp. pāpātman.
dharmādharma [adhrma] m. du. phil. good and evil; justice and injustice.
dharmādharmajña [jña] anfm dharmādharmajñā phil. one who knows how to discern good and evil.
dharmādhyakṣa [adhyakṣa] m. soc. chief judge.
Dharmānubandhiślokacaturdaśī [anubandhin ślokacaturdaśi f. lit. np. la de Dharmānubandhiślokacaturdaśī "14 verses justifying duty" de Śeṣakṛṣṇa.
dharmānusāra | anusāra | m. conformity to the law; prescription of duty; practice of virtue.
dharmāraṇya [araṇya] n. ["wood of duty"] hermitage; sacred grove myth. [Mah.] np. of a sacred forest of Madhyadeśa | myth. [Rām.] np. of the city of dharmāraṇya, founded by King Amūrtarajasa.
dharmārtha | artha | m. du. phil. religious duty and social success. dharmārtham adv. according to one's duty | to acquire religious merit.
dharmārthakāmamokṣa | kāmamokṣa | m. pl. phil. the 4 goals of existence: duty, wealth, pleasure and liberation.
dharmāsana [āsana] n. ["seat of the law"] tribunal.

dharmottara [uttara₁] m. hist. n.p. from the philosopher bd. dharmottara₁ or Dharmaśrī (4th century), author of the Abhidharmahrdaya₁ | bd. n.p. of dharmottara, 8th century logician; we owe him commentaries on Dharmakīrti, not. the Nyāyabinduṭīkā, commentary on the Nyāyabindu.

dharmán [dhṛman] m. Vedic. support, maintenance — n. dhárman support; foundation | phil. established order, natural law | myth. divine decree (not. of Mitra or Varuna) | law, rule, duty; practice, custom; cf. dharma. pratyakṣadharmāṇaḥ (sages) having direct vision of the dharman.
dharmi iic. dharmin.
dharmigrāhaka [grāhaka] m. phil. [Nyāya| that which establishes the existence of the locus.
dharmigrāhakapramāṇa [pramāṇa] n. phil. [Nyāya] means of knowledge associated, argument giving both proof of existence and characteristic of a thing.
dharmika [dharmaika] ifc. amnf dhar mikī which follows the rule of (iic.).
dharmitva [dharmatva] n. fidelity to one's own; virtue — ifc. fact of being obliged to or charged with (iic.).
dharmin [dharmain] amnf dharmiṇī faithful to his duty, just, virtuous; pious | legitimate — ifc. who follows the law of; subject to — m. phil. [Nyāya] locus.
dharmistha [super. dharmin] amnf dharmiṣṭhā very just, very virtuous; absolutely legal.
dharmya [dharmaya] amnf dharmyā suitable, legitimate, legal; in accordance with duty; just, virtuous.
dharṣ [ca. dhṛṣ] v. [10] pr. (dharṣayati) pp. (dharsita) to attack, assault; destroy | rape (a woman).
dharṣa [act. dhṛṣ] m. recklessness, audacity; imprudence | arrogance, insolence; violence; rape.
dharṣaṇa [act. dhṛṣ] n. attack, outrage, insult; attack, assault.
dharsita [pp. dhars] amnf dharsitā at taqué, malmené; violé, outrageé.

dharşin [agt. dharş] amnf dharşinī who attacks, who submits (iic.) | arrogant. durdharadharṣiṇī f. myth. epith. of Durgā "who subdues the demon Durdhara". ধব dhavá₁ m. organic. bot. Anogeissus latifolia, large tree used for its resin.
dhavá₂ m. husband; lord.
dhavala amnf dhavalā White, of a brilliant whiteness | pretty, pleasant — m. the color white. dhavalīkṛ to whiten.

Dhavalagiri [giri] m. geo. np. of the "White Mountain" Dhavalagiri, which rises to 8167 in the Himalayas (mod. Dhaulagiri) | geo. np. of the hill of Dhauli in Orissa, 6 km south of Bhubanesvar, site of the Battle of Kalinga; on a rock there is an inscription of Aśoka.
dhavalatā [tā] f. whiteness.
dhavalatva [vat] n. whiteness.
dhavaleśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of the Dha valesvara temple, at the top of Dhauli Hill in Orissa; it dates from the Bhaumakara period.

dhā₃ |agt. dhā₁| ifc. amf that which places, which sets, which supports (iic.) | that which gives (iic.). ratnadhā ved. that which confers the reward. ੰਬਾ dhā forms with numerals adverbs signifying repetition ((iic.) times) or division (into (iic.) parts).

√ dhā₁ v. [3] pr. (dadhāti) pr. r. (dhatte) imp. (dhehi) fut. (dhāsyati) pft. (dadhau) aor. [1] (adhāt) inf. (dhātum) pp. (hita₂) ppft. (dadhivas) pfp. (dheya) abs. (dhāya) pf. (antar, api, abhi, ava, ā, upa, tiras, ni, pari, pi, puras, pra, vi, śrat, sam) to place, lay, install, put (on (loc.)) | fix on, direct towards (dat. loc.) | produce, engender, create; execute, perform | establish; destine to, grant to (loc. dat. g.) | soc. confer the charge of (acc.) on acc. — v. [1] pr. (dádhati) pr. r. (dadhate) id. — pr. r. (dhatté) to have, to hold — ps. (dhīyate) to be placed, to be set — ca. (dhāpayati) to cause to be set — dés. (dhitsati) dés. r. (dhitsate) to want to set — dés. (didhisati) to want to give — dés. r. (didhisate) to want to obtain | lat. dare; ang. to do; all. thun. mano dhā to think about, to meditate on (loc. dat. prati inf. daṇḍaṃ dhā to punish (loc. g.). tatpadavyām padam dhā ["to follow in the footsteps of" | to follow, to imitate. dharme dadhyān manaḥ [MS.] Let him direct his mind towards duty.

dhātakī f. bio. bot. Woodfordia fruticosa, a flamboyant shrub from North India with numerous bright red flowers in clusters, used in medicine, with opposite lanceolate leaves in palmettes; syn. madahetu, madanīyahetu.

dhātu [dhā₁tu] m. seat, foundation | primordial element, elemental substance; mineral ingredient, metal, ore; cf. aṣṭadhātu | phil. element | gram. verbal root | bd. one of the 6 elements: ākāśa the Ether or Space, anila the Air, te jas the Fire, jala the Water and bhū₂ the Earth and vijñāna Knowledge | bd. constituent element of the body; ashes, relics | [dhātugarbha] bd. central reliquary of a stūpa, at the base of the stone pillar [yaṣṭi].
Dhātukāvya [kāvya] n. lit. np. of the didactic poem Dhātukāvya by Nārāyaṇa₃ Bhaṭṭa; it recounts the killing of Kamsa by Kṛṣṇa, illustrating in turn the uses of the roots of the dhātupātha.
dhātugarbha [garbha] m. bd. reliquary of ashes (pāli dhātugabbha, which became dāgoba in Ceylon, occi dentalized into a pagoda).

Dhātupāṭha |pāṭha| m. gram. recitation of verbal roots | lit. np. of the Dhātupāṭha, a traditional work listing verbal roots, and indicating their inflected forms | anubandha | and their meaning |dhātvartha|; there are many versions of it from various times.
dhātupradīpa [pradīpa] m. gram. n.p. from dhātupradīpa, lexicon of roots [dhātuvṛtti] of Maitreyaraksita (12th century).
dhātumaya [maya] amnf dhātumayī in metal. dhātumayī pratimā metal idol.
Dhāturatnākara [ratnākara] m. gram. np. from Dhāturatnākara, dictionary of conjugated forms of Sanskrit roots, by Muni Lāvanya Vijaya Sūri (1992).
dhāturūpa [rūpa] n. gram. conjugated form of a root.
dhāturūpaprapañca [prapañca] m. gram. np. from dhāturūpaprapañca, dictionary of conjugated forms of Sanskrit roots, by NVP Unithiri and OK Munși (2006).
dhāturūpāvali [āvali] f. gram. list of conjugated forms of Sanskrit roots; cf. Brhaddhāturūpāvali.
dhātuvāda [vāda] m. metallurgy; alchemy, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
dhātuvṛtti [vṛtti] f. gram. commentary on a lexicon of roots [Dhātupāṭha], manual for the use of verbal roots; cf. Mādhavīya, Kṣīrataramgiṇī, dhātupradīpa.
dhātusaṃgraha [saṃgraha] m. lit. np. from the Dhātusamgraha "Collection of roots", by Srīla Jīva Gosvāmī.
dhātusūtra [sūtra] n. gram. grammar rule applicable to a set of roots.
dhātvartha [artha] m. gram. action as a sense of a verbal root | lit. list of words giving this sense in the dhātupātha.
dhātvādeśa [ādeśa] m. gram. substitution of one root for another.

dhātṛ [agt. dhā₁] amnf dhātrī [sg. nom. Dhātā, acc. dhātāram] founder, creator, author; compiler; patron | ved. np. of Dhātā "the Shaper" or "Orderer", demiurge of creation, son of Bhṛgu by Kyāti, associated with PrajāpatiBrahmā; Niyati is his wife; [Mah.] the rși Uttanka had the vision of the Wheel of Time rolling in a cavern where Dhātā and his brother Vidhātā stood in the form of two old women weaving the destinies of the World | astr. np. of Dhātā₁ "Creative", personifying year 10 of a life cycle [saṃvatsara] — n. providence — f. cf. dhātrī.
dhātrī [f. dhātr] f. nanny, adoptive mother; midwife | organic. bot. Emblica officinalis, my robolan tree; syn. āmalaka.
dhātreyī [*dhātrīeya] f. milk sister | wet nurse.
dhātreyikā |ka| f. milk sister; confidante.
dhāna |act. dhā₁| n. container, receptacle; residence — f. dhānī ifc. residence of (iic.) — f. cf. dhānā
dhānaka [ka] n. coriander — m. coin, worth 4 crowns [kārṣāpaṇa].
dhānikā [ika] f. receptacle.
dhānā [f. dhāna] f. seed; shoot, bud coriander | pl. cereal grains; grains in gen.
dhānurdaṇḍika [*dhanurdaṇḍaika] amnf dhānurdaṇḍikī who makes a living from the profession of arms.
dhānyá [dhānaya] n. cereal; not. wheat, rice | wealth, prosperity | coriander.
Dhānyaka [ka] m. grain; wheat | lit. [DKC.] np. of Dhānyaka, rich burgher of the country Trigarta; his brothers are Dhanaka and Dhanyaka — n. coriander.
dhānyakalka [kalka] m. straw.
dhānyakhala | khala | m. threshing floor.
dhānyaphalanyāya | phalanyāya | m. maxim of grain and straw, a laukikanyāya (one does not have grain without having straw with it).
dhānyabīja [bīja] n. coriander.
dhānyamaya [maya] amnf dhānyamayī which consists of grains.
dhānyavat |vat| amnf dhānyavatī rich in grains — adv. like grain.
dhānyārtha | artha | m. income from the harvest; wealth acquired through agriculture.
dhāma iic. dhāman.
dhāmacchad [chad₂] amnf myth. said of Agni "who changes his dwelling".

dhāman [dhā₁man] n. Vedic. site of the sacred fire and soma | dwelling; abode | delight, pleasure, established order, norm; institution, establishment; condition, nature; manner, mode; faculty | strength, power; majesty, splendor, brilliance | phil. the sacred felt as divine presence | Lat. famulus; Eng. fame; Fr. fameux. priyam dhāma favorite place; favorite thing, pleasure; status; faculty. abhayadhāman place of safety. dhāmāni trayāni bhavanti sthānāni nāmāni
janmānīti [Yāska] The word dhāman has three meanings: place, name and race.
dhāya [agt. dhā₁] amnf dhāyā that supports — f. dhāyī ifc. that has, that possesses (iic.) — act. m. gift, present; inheritance.

dhār [ca. dhṛ] v. [10] pr. (dhārayati) pp. (dhārita) abs. (dhārayitvā) to hold firmly, rete nir, to support, to bear, to bear | to preserve, entrete nir, to keep, to possess | to repress, to stop, to suppress; to impose, to decide | to owe something to someone. (dat.). viprāya śataṃ dhārayati he owes 100 (coins) to the priest.
dhāra₁ [agt. ca. dhṛ] ifc. amnf dhārī that which carries, that which holds, that which supports, that which sustains (iic.).
dhāra₁ |dhāv₁| amnf dhārā which falls as rain or as a stream — mn stream; torrent — f. cf. dhārā₁.
dhāraka [agt. dhṛ] amnf dhārikā which carries.

dhāraṇa |agt. dhṛ| amnf dhāraṇī that holds, that carries; that guards, that protects | that restrains, that restricts — act. n. support, guard; endurance; memory, memorization — f. cf. dhāraṇā — f. dhāraṇī bd. kind of mantra.
dhāraṇamātṛkā |mātṛkā| f. mnemonics, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.

dhāraṇā [f. dhāraṇa] f. action of maintaining, enduring, memorizing; rule, law | memory; perfect understanding, certainty | phil. [yoga] concentration of the mind with cessation of breath, or fixation of thought, 6th stage of rājayoga, ob held by ekāgratā; cf. aṣṭāṅgayoga — f. dhāraṇī bd. secret formula [mantra] learned from the master; its indefinite repetition leads to spiritual realization [siddhi].
dhāraṇātmaka [ātmaka] amnf dhāraṇātmikā phil. whose nature is intrinsic.
dhāraya [agt. ca. dhṛ] amnf dhārayā that holds; that supports.
dhārayat [ppr. That. dhṛ] amnf dhārayantī who holds, who possesses — ifc. paid in (iic.).
Dhārayadvasu | vasu | m. hist. np. of the Persian emperor Dhārayadvasu "(Darius) the Fortunate".

dhārā₁ [f. dhāra₁] f. flow, current; running water; stream, torrent; drop, downpour | (figuratively) rain of (arrows, etc.) | soc. particular libation to Agni | leakage (of a pitcher, etc.) | trot (of a horse) | uniformity, continuity; usage, custom; lineage | geo. np. of the city of dhārā, in Mālava (mod. Dhar in Madhya Pradesh); in the 9th century, King Vairisimha of the Paramāra dynasty transferred his capital there; it became a center of learning under the reign of King Bhojadeva, who had the Bhojaśālā, a Sanskrit university and temple of Saras vatī, built there.
dhārā₂ [dhāv₂] f. edge, margin; cutting edge, edge, blade | ridge of a mountain; rim of a wheel; rim of an ear | summit; glory, excellence.
dhārāgṛha |gṛha| n. bathroom, shower room.
dhārānipāta | nipāta | mr. downpour.
dhārāsampāta | sampāta | mr. downpour. aviralavāridhārāsampātaḥ heavy rain shower.
dhārāsāra |sāra| mr. downpour. paturdhārāsāraḥ piercing rain.

dhārin [agt. dhṛ] amnf Dhāriṇī which carries; who owns; who remembers (of (iic. g.)) — f. Dhāriṇī the earth | bed. n.p. of Queen Dhāriṇī; cf. Mālavikāgnimitra. tāpasarūpadhāriṇaḥ disguised as ascetics.

Dhārtarāṣṭra [*dhṛtarāṣṭra] amnf dhārtarāṣṭrā relating to dhṛtarāṣṭra — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Dhārtarāṣṭra "son of dhṛtarāṣṭra", patr. of note. Duryodhana | pl. the Kuravas, who left without dhṛtarāṣṭra.

dhārmika [*dharmaika] amnf dhārmikī one who practices the law; just, virtuous, proper, pious | in accordance with justice — m. devout, religious; pious man; man of duty | soc. monk | pkt. dhammia. dharmo rakṣati dhārmikam Justice protects the just. brāhmaṇāya gām dadāti dhārmikah The just man gives a cow to the Brahmin.
dhārya [pfp. [1] dhṛ] amnf dhāryā that one must wear, hold or bear | to keep; to follow; that one must remember — n. clothes.

√ dhāv₁ v. [1] pr. (dhāvati) pr. r. (dhāvate) pp. (dhāvita) abs. (dhāvitvā) pf. (anu, abhi, upa, nis, pari, pra, vi) to go away; to run, to save oneself; to escape || gr. . mṛgayāṃ dhāv | "to run after game" | to go hunting.
√ dhāv₂ v. [1] pr. (dhāvati) pp. (dhauta) pf. (pra) to wash, clean, purify, rinse; to polish, scour, shine — pr. r. (dhāvate) to rub, clean oneself. dato dhāvate he brushes his teeth.
dhāva |agt. dhāv₂| ifc. amnf dhāvā that washes, that cleans (iic.).
dhāvat₁ |ppr. dhāv₁ | amnf dhāvantī running.
dhāvat₂ [ppr. dhāv₂] amnf dhāvant while washing.
dhāvana₁ [act. dhāv₁] n. race.
dhāvana₂ [act. dhāv₂] n. washing, cleaning, polishing, whitening | the act of rubbing. ਬਿ dhi [act. dhā₁] ifc. m. receptacle of (iic.).
dhik ind. excl. of distress, reproach or contempt; alas! woe! poor me! woe to, shame on, cursed be (acc.). hā dhik what woe! what shame! dhik kṛ to blame; to reproach.
dhikkāra [kāra] m. reproach; contempt; satire.
dhikkrta [krta] amnf dhikkrtā reprimanded; stigmatized, despised — n. reproach; contempt.
dhikpralāpa [pralāpa] m. withering words.
dhigdanda [danda] m. soc. reprimand; public denunciation.
dhita [pp. dhā₁] amnf dhitā [hita₂] placed, put; granted.
dhits [des. dhā₁] v. pr. (dhitsati) to want to pose.

dhişana amnf dhişanā intelligent, its vant; wise — mr. master, spiritual guide | myth. n.p. of dhisana, epith. of BrhaspatiGuru — n. understanding; intelligence — f. Dhiṣaṇā ved. soma container | myth. n.p. of Dhiṣaṇā, descended from Agni, wife of Havirdhāna — ifc. knowledge of (iic.).

dhísnya amnf dhiṣṇyā ved. attentive; benevolent (said of the Aśvinau) — m. ved. at the secondary tel, annex hearth of the vedic altar; it consists of a mound of earth covered with sand on which the hearth is placed; there are 8 of them — n. place, spot, site; residence; region | star, meteor.
√ dhī v. [4] pr. r. (dhīyate) pp. (dhīta) pf. (ā) to think, to meditate; cf. dhyā.

dhī₂ [act. dhī₂] f. Vedic. vision of the sages [rsi] | phil. np. of dhī₂, self-understanding of the Creator, first and supreme creative principle | thought (not. mystical), meditation; devotion, prayer | intelligence, understanding; knowledge, wisdom; syn. buddhi.
dhī₃ cf. dhā₁.
dhīmat [mat] amnf dhīmatī wise, sensible, thoughtful, intelligent; learned. dhīmānnaraḥ an intelligent man.
dhīmattama [tara] amnf dhīmattamā great. the wisest.
dhimattara |tara| amnf dhīmattarā compar. wiser; smarter.
dhīvarga [varga] m. bed. section of the Svargādikāṇḍa, dealing with the intellect.
dhītá [pp. dhī₁] amnf dhītā thought; weighed, analyzed, reflected — n. pl. dhītāni thoughts; reflection, meditation.
dhīti [act. dhī₁] f. thought; reflection, meditation | contemplation; devotion; prayer.

dhīmahi [aor. dhā₁] Vedic (benedictative, aorist of the middle optative) may we establish | (later, interpreted as a form of dhī₁) let us meditate, invoke, honor. satyam param dhīmahi (motto of Ut Kala University) Let us seek the supreme truth.

dhīra₁ [dhā₁] amnf dhīrā firm, stable, constant; wise, tranquil; tenacious, obstinate | grave, solemn | energetic, resolute; courageous; intrepid — m. man of firm character — f. cf. dhīrā — v. [11] pr. (dhīrayati) pp. (dhīrita) pf. (ava) to encourage; to strengthen; to comfort. dhīram adv. quietly.
dhīra₂ [dhī₂ra] amnf dhīrā intelligent, insightful; wise, learned; skilled in, versed in (loc.) | lit. expert in the art of poetry.
dhīratara |tara| amnf dhīratarā compar. firmer; very firm.
dhīratā₁ [tā] f. courage; firmness of character.
dhīratā₂ [tā] f. wisdom.

dhīralalita [lalita] m. lit. type of hero [nāyaka] brave and joyful.

Dhundhu m. myth. n.p. of the asura Dhundhu; he was killed by Kuvalāsva.

dhundhukārin [kārin] m. myth. [Srīmadbhāgavatamāhātmya] np. of the unbeliever Dhundhukārī; he expelled his father from his own house, made his mother fall into a well, led a criminal life and was murdered by prostitutes; his wandering spirit haunted his virtuous brother Gokarna₁, who only succeeded in appeasing it by leading a recitation of the Bhāgavata [saptāha].
Dhundhumāra [māra] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Dhundhumāra "who slays Dhundhu", epith. of the king Kuvalāśva, son of Brhadaśva₁; or |Rām.| son of Triśańku and father of Yuvanāśva.

dhúr [dhṛ] f. [in comp. dhūr; nom. dhūs] pole, yoke, shaft | place of honor; summit, peak. dhuri at the head, in the place of honor, in the first rank. dhuri kīrtanīyaḥ that which must be put at the head. dhuram vah to be in the place of honor, to be the first. sa sarveṣāṃ dhuri tiṣṭhati he is above all.
dhura [dhura] m. yoke, stretcher — f. dhurā burden, load.

dhurīya [dhurīya] amnf dhurīyā proper to a charge; having important responsibilities — m. beast of burden | businessman.
dhurya [dhurya] amnf dhuryā at the head, best, eminent; who assumes responsibilities — m. beast of burden.

dhūma [dhū₁ma] m. smoke; vapor, fog | arch. the cloud, a matrix | yoni | of the āyādi system — v. [11] pr. r. (dhūmāyate) to emit smoke | gr. θυμος; lat. fūmus; fr. fume, perfume. dhūmāyate 'gniḥ fire makes smoke.
dhūmapa [pa₁] amnf dhūmapā ["who inhales smoke"] smoker.

Dhūmapura [pura] n. bed. [KSS.] np. from the town of Dhūmapura, capital of rākṣasa Agniśikha.
dhūmala [la] amnf dhūmalā smoke color; violet, mauve — m. the violet color.
dhūmavat [vat] amnf dhūmavatī who smokes — f. dhūmavatī phil. [Tantra] n.p. of dhūmavatī "the Widow", one of the 10 powers [mahāvidyā] of the Goddess [Sakti].
dhūmavattva |tva| n. emission of smoke.
dhūmavarti [varti] f. aromatic plant cigar.
dhūmaśakaṭa |śakaṭa| n. mod. train, railway.
Dhūmaśikha₁ [śikhā] m. bed. [KSS.] np. of rākṣasa Dhūmaśikha₁, brother of Agniśikha | bed. [KSS.] np. of king vidyādhara Dhūmaśikha₁, ally of Mandara deva.
dhūmahetu | hetu | m. cause of smoke.

dhūmita [pp. dhūma] amnf dhūmitā which has the smell or taste of smoke | smoky; obscured.

dhūmin [agt. dhūma] amnf dhūminī that emits smoke or vapor — f. dhūminī myth. one of the 7 languages of Agni [saptajihva] | lit. np. of dhūminī, cruel wife of Dhanyaka; she cheated on her husband with a cripple, pushed him into a well, and falsely denounced him.
dhūmra [dhūmara] amnf dhūmrā smoke color; grey, violet | darkened — m. camel | incense | the violet color. dhūmrávarņa [varņa] amnf dhūmravarņā ["smoke color"] grey, dark red.
dhūmrāśva [aśva] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Viśālā dhūmrāśva "with the grey horse", son of Sucan dra, father of Srñjaya.
dhūr iic. dhur. Dhūrjați [jați] m. myth. n.p. of Dhūrjați, epith. of Siva "with the heavy frizzy bun".
dhūrta [pp. dhvṛ] amnf dhūrtā cunning, cunning; cheat, dishonest (in (iic.)) — m. rogue, scoundrel; swindler, trickster. akṣadhūrtaḥ cheat at dice.
dhūrtamayūra [mayūra] m. peacock thief.
dhūrtasamāgama [samāgama] m. assembly of evildoers | lit. np. from dhūrtasamāgama "a band of thieves", comedy by Kavisekhara Jyotīśvara (14th century).
dhūli [dhū₁] f. dust; dusty ground; powder; pollen.
dhūsara [dhvaṃs] amnf dhūsarā grey, obs curci, dust-colored — m. the grey color || ang. dust. dhūsarīkr to make grey. pakṣair dhūsaraih with grey wings (said of the kalahamsa).

dhṛt [agt. dhṛ] ifc. amnf that carries, that supports (iic.); support, support of (iic.).

dhṛtániścaya [niścaya] amnf dhṛtaniścayā firmly resolved to (dat.). )2

Dhṛtarāṣṭra₁ [rāṣṭra] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Dhṛtarāṣṭra₁ "of the firm kingdom", son of Vyāsa and Ambikā₁, half-brother of Pāṇḍu and Vidura, blind king of the Kauravās; his wife is Gāndhārī; the eldest of his 100 sons is DuryodhanaSuyodhana; others are called Abhaya, Kundina, Citra₁, Jarāsandha, Duḥśāsana, Durdharṣa, Pramatha, Yuyutsu, Vikarņa, Šala, Ṣaṇḍha, Subāhu₂, Sulo cana; His daughter is Duḥśalā — f. dhṛtarāṣṭrī myth. |Mah.| np. of dhṛtarāṣṭrī, daughter of Kaśyapa and Tāmrā; Haṃsa is his son | myth. | Mah. | np. of Dhrtarāstrī₁, daughter of Dakṣa, wife of Kaśyapa; she bore Sukī | myth. [Mah.] np. of the great harva Dhṛtarāṣṭra₁, sent as a messenger to King Marutta to persuade him to take Brhaspati as officiant for his great sacrifice.
Dhṛti [act. dhṛ] f. firmness, constancy, resolution, courage, myth. np. of the goddess Dhrti "Resolution" phon. class of meters of 4 times 18 syllables | math. symb. the number 18.

(ā, ut, pra) to dare, to be audacious; to risk; to be reckless | to be insolent; to aggress, to attack, to assail — ca. (dharṣayati) at to attack, to assault; to destroy | to rape (a woman). ধুপু dhṛṣu [dhṛṣu] amnf courageous — m. group, multitude. ধৃষ্ট dhṛṣṭá [pp. dhṛṣ] amnf dhṛṣṭā Bold, daring; reckless, adventurous | brazen, insolent. dhṛṣṭam adv. with boldness.

Dhṛṣṭaketu |ketu| m. myth. |Mah.| np. of Dhṛṣṭaketu "Bold in character", king of the Ce dayas, ally of the Pāṇḍavās | myth. [BhP.] np. of king Dhṛṣṭaketu₁ Janaka, son of Sudhṛti, father of Ha ryaśva₁.

Dhṛṣṭadyumna [dyumna] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Dhṛṣṭadyumna "Glorious Daring One", son of Dru pada, born in a Vedic sacrifice with his sister Draupadī; he was commander-in-chief of the army of the Pāṇḍavās; realizing the fruit of the sacrifice of his birth, he killed Drona during the great ba taille, taking advantage of his dejection at the (false) news of the death of his son; then he was killed by Aśvatthāmā attacking him in his sleep; cf. Pārsata.
dhṛṣṭi [act. dhṛṣ] f. audacity, courage.
dhṛṣṇu [agt. dhṛṣ] amnf bold; courageous.
dhṛṣya [pfp. [1] dhṛṣ] amnf dhṛṣyā to agres ser.

dhenú [agt. dhā₁] amnf that gives milk — f. dairy cow | mare — ifc. female of (iic.) — ifc. cow made of (iic.) (offered as a gift to a brahmin) | by extension diminutive. savatsā dhenuḥ the cow and her calf. sakiśorā dhenuh the mare and her foal.
dhenuka |ka| m. myth. np. of the asura dhenuka "disguised as an archer", killed by Balarāma — f. dhe nukā dairy cow.
dhenúdugdha | dugdha | n. cow's milk.
dhenubhavyā | bhavya | f. future dairy cow.

dhenum [acc. dhenu] iic.
dhenumbhāvyā [bhāvya] f. intended to be a dairy cow.

dheya [pfp. [1] dhā₁] amnf dheyā which must be placed, installed, put in place; which must be applied — n. offering, gift — ifc. (iic.) by convention; attributed as (iic.).

dhairya [*dhīra₁ya] n. firmness, resolution, constancy; dignity; courage | calm, composure, patience, endurance. dhairyam nidhehi hrdye regain courage. tasya dhairyam na hīyate courage did not fail him.
dhaivata [*dhīvan] n. (mus.) 6th note of the Indian octave.
dhoyin m. hist. np. of the poet Dhoyī of the court of Laksmanasena (12th century), author of the Pa vanadūta.
dhauta [pp. dhāv₂] amnf dhautā washed, cleaned, purified; polished, buffed, lustrous, shiny — n. washing, laundering.
dhautavastra [vastra] n. clean garment.
dhautātman |ātman| amnf dhautātmanī with a pure heart.
dhauti [act. dhāv₂] f. [yoga] cleansing of the esophagus with a strip of cloth swallowed and then removed from the mouth | var. dhautī id.

dhaumya [*dhūmaya] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the hermit dhaumya "Born from smoke", younger brother of Devala; at the suggestion of Citraratha, the Pāṇḍavās chose him as chaplain | purohita | by visiting his hermitage of Utkocaka; he married them successively to Draupadī; he gave the royal anointing to Yudhişthira at his coronation |rājasūya|.
dhmā |agt. dham| ifc. amf that blows into (iic.); that stirs, that breathes, that animates (iic.).
dhmātá |pp. dham| amnf dhmātā into which one has blown; kindled (fire); sounded (not. conch |śaṅkha|).
dhmāna |act. dham| n. action of blowing; swelling.
dhyāta [pp. dhyā] amnf dhyātā meditated, imagined; what one thinks about | revealed by meditation.
dhyātvā [abs. dhyā] ind. having meditated.
dhyāna |act. dhyā| n. meditation, mental contemplation | phil. meditation, the 7th stage of rājayoga; cf. aṣṭāṅgayoga | bd. meditation, one of the 6 perfections [pāramitā] of an accum

fold [bodhisattva] | jn. Jain tradition recognizes four kinds of meditation, two good: dharma (pious) and śukla (pure) and two bad: ārta (painful) and raudra (harmful) | lit. introductory invocation of a work || pkt. jhāna; Japanese zen.
dhyānanimagna [nimagna] afmn dhyānanimagnā absorbed in meditation.
Dhyānaratnāvalī [ratnāvalī] f. bed. n.p. of the Dhyānaratnāvalī, a śaiva hymn [stotra] which prescribes the canonical visualizations of the cult of Sadāśiva, due to Trilocanasiva ācārya.
dhyānaśloka [śloka] m. lit. meditation verse.
dhyāni iic. dhyānin.

dhyānibuddha [buddha] m. bd. "spiritual buddha", neologism (due to BH Hodgson) To designate the five regents of a paradise in the Mahāyāna pantheon: the accomplished [jina] directional guardians Aksobhya, Amitābha, Amogha siddhi, Ratnasambhava, and at the center Vairocana.
dhyānibodhisattva [bodhisattva] m. bd. "spiritual bodhi sattva", neologism (due to BH Hodgson) To personify the qualities of a dhyānibuddha; cf. Samantabhadra.
dhyānimudrā | mudrā | f. bd. meditation gesture, right hand on left hand, placed flat on the lap, palms towards the sky; generally associated with padmāsana; also called samādhimudrā.
dhyānin [dhyānain] amnf dhyāninī who contemplates; who meditates.
dhyāyat [ppr. dhyā] amnf dhyāyantī who contemplates; who meditates.

dhyeya [pfp. [1] dhyā] amnf dhyeyā to meditate on, to consider; imaginable.
dhyai cf. dhya. ধ্ব dhra [contr. dhara] f. dhrā ifc. who holds, who supports (iic.).

Dhruvá [Dhruvá] amnf Dhruvā firm, solid, fixed; permanent, perpetual, immutable, eternal; sure, certain — m. myth. np. of Dhruvá "the immutable", one of the 8 Treasures | vasu|, personifying the pole star; [VP.] he is the son of Uttānapāda and Sunīti; Uttānapāda's favorite, Suruci, had a son Uttama preferred to Dhruvá; Dhruvá finally withdrew to the woods, and through his penances was raised by Vishnu to his celestial position; soc. the pole star is shown to the wife at her ma

marriage [vivāha] So that she may be firm in her attachment to her new family | hist. np. of the emperor Rāṣṭrakūṭa Dhruvā₁ (8th century); he succeeded Govinda₂ upon his death in 780; he conquered all the territory between the Kāverī and the Vindhya mountains; his son Govinda₃ succeeded him in 792 — n. certainty — f. dhruvā the here, indicated by the direction [dik] of the nadir | mus. first verse repeated as a refrain, recurring melody; rhythmic cycle |tāla| comprising 1 laghu, 1 druta and 2 laghu. dhruvam adv. firmly, solidly; surely, certainly; constantly, eternally. dhruvā dik the here. jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtyasya ca [BhG.] For him who is born death is certain, For him who is dead birth is certain.
dhruvagopa [gopa] m. ved. guardian of the soma in the solemn sacrifice.
dhruvadevī [devī] f. hist. np. of Queen Dhruva devī, wife of Rāmagupta then of his brother who )4 freed her from the Sakās, and reigned like the emperor Candragupta₂.
dhruvapada | pada | n. style of music and song.
dhruvasandhi [sandhi] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā dhruvasandhi, son of Susandhi, father of Bharata₄.

dhvaṃsin [agt. ca. dhvaṃs] amnf dhvamsinī that destroys, that disperses.

dhvajá mn flag, banner, standard | badge, emblem, attribute (not. of a deity); pillar of glory; mark, ensign (not. of a temple) | sexual organ | sign of penitence, mark of an ascetic | (figuratively) pride; arrogance — ifc. ornament of (iic.) — f. dhvajā ifc. id.
dhvajastambha [stambha] m. soc. standard pillar or banner pole of a temple; it stands in the 1st enclosure, opposite the divinity of the sanctuary.
dhvajin |in| amnf dhvajinī who carries a standard; bearing the mark of (not. a crime) — f. dhvajinī army.
√ dhvan v. [1] pr. (dhvanati) pp. (dhvanita, dvāntá) to emit a sound, to resonate, to make noise; to rumble (thunder); to echo — ca. (dhvanayati) pp. (dhvānita) to make a noise, to resound.

dhvani [act. dhvan] m. sound, resonance, noise; rumble (of thunder); voice; reverberation, echo lit. rhet. suggested meaning; suggestion, evocation, connotation; trope | gram. presupposition; implicature; innuendo | lit. school of poetic composition, established by Mammata, from the aesthetics of Anandavardhana; it defines dhvani as preponderance of the suggested meaning [vyañjanā] over the literal meaning |abhidhā₂|.
dhvanikāra [kāra] m. lit. np. of Dhva nikāra "Inventor of suggested meaning", epith. of Anandavardhana.
dhvanikāvya [kāvya] n. lit. [Anandavardhana] poetry where the suggested meaning is predominant.

Dhvanyāloka [āloka] m. lit. np. from the Dhvanyāloka "Illumination of Suggested Meaning", a work of literary aesthetics by Anandavardhana (circa 875); it includes a collection of verses [kārikā] condensing the teaching, and a commentary [vṛtti] in prose interpreting it; Abhinavagupta made a commentary [locana] on it; in it he distinguishes 4 powers of speech, or levels of expression of meaning: denotation [abhidhā₂], communication of the speaker's intention [tātparya], metaphorical use [lakṣaṇa] and suggestion [dhvani].
dhvanyālokalocana [locana] n. bed. n.p. of the Dh vanyālokalocana, commentary on the Dhvanyāloka by Abhinavagupta.

√ nakṣ v. [1] pr. (nakṣati) aor. [4] (anakṣīt) to approach, to arrive at, to reach. নিধ্ব nákṣatra [instr. nakṣ] n. star, celestial body | celestial vault; (collective) the stars | astr. celestial position of the full moon, lunar asterism, lunar mansion; there were first 27 nakṣatrāṇi, then 28 with the addition of Abhijit; each nakṣatra actually designates a 13° 20' division of the ecliptic; each is divided into 4 quarters [pāda] of 3° 20' | myth. (collective) personified lunation, daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Can dra; they are called: Kṛttikās (Pleiades), Rohinī₁ or Brāhmī (Aldebaran), Mrgasiras or Agrahāyaṇī (Baldric of Orion), Ardrā or Bāhū (Betelgeuse), Punarvasū or Yamakau (Castor and Pollux), Pusya or Tisya or Sidhya (Cancer), Aśleṣās (Hydra), Maghās (Regulus), Pūrvaphalgunī (δ of Lion), Uttaraphalgunī (β of Lion), Hasta (Raven), Citrā (Ear of Virgo), Svāti or Svātī (Arcturus), Viśākhe or Rādhā₂ (Libra), Anurādhās (delta of Scorpio), Jyestha (Antares), Mūlabarhaņī (epsilon of Scorpio), Pūrvāṣāḍhās (delta of Sagittarius), Uttarāṣāḍhās (sigma of Sagittarius), Abhijit (Vega), Śravaṇā (Altaïr), Śraviṣṭhā or Dhanisthā (of the Dolphin), Satabhisak (of the Bucket Worm), Pūrvaprosthapadās or Pūrvabhādrapadās (αβ of Pegasus), Uttaraprosthapadās or Utta rabhādrapadās (of Pegasus and Andromeda), Revatī (zeta of Pisces), A u₀0e₁vinī or A u₀0e₁viyujau (u₀0beta zeta) of Aries) and Bharanī (Arietis). nakṣatrapathavartinā rājñā [Kāvyādarśa] By a king who follows the path of the stars (or who does not follow the path of heroes).
nákṣatranātha | nātha | m. "master of the stars", epithet of the moon.
nákṣatrarāja |rāja| m. "king of the stars", epithet of the moon.

nakhá mn nail; claw | dagger with a claw-shaped blade | pl. claws, talons; pincers | lat. ungula; fr. ongle; ang. nail; all. Nagel. nakhāni kṛ to cut nails. nakhāni kļp id. katitataniviştaratnanakhah [DKC.] (man) carrying a jewel-encrusted dagger at his hip.
nakhamuca [muca] m. ["which frees the nail"] arc.
nakhará [ra] m. nail; claw, spur — amnf nakharā curved, hooked.
nakhalekhaka [lekhaka] m. manicure.
nakhānakhi [red. nakha] adv. claw against claw (in combat).
nága [naga₁] m. ["to be immobile"] mountain tree.
naganagarī [nagarī] f. geo. n.p. from the walled city of naganagarī in Kashmir.
nagarāja [rājan] m. big mountain.
nagarājadhara [dhara] m. myth. np. of Na garājadhara "Supporting the great mountain", epith. of Kṛṣṇa supporting Mount Govardhana.
nagavāsa [vāsa₁] m. ["that lives in trees"] peacock.
nagendra [indra] m. ["king of the mountains"] Himālaya | [MD.] Kailāsa.
nágara mn town, city; capital — f. nagarī id.
nagarakāra | kāra | mr. architect; urban planner.
nagarakīrtana | kīrtana | n. SOC. devotional street procession, with songs and dances; cf. Caitanya.
nagaraśobhinī | śobhinī | f. soc. | "urban adornment" | courtesan (not. in the time of Buddha).
nagna amnf nagnā nu; desert, arid — m. soc. monk wandering naked; sadhu fighter | eng. naked; all. nackt; fr. naked; hi. nagā.

nagnájit [jit] amnf ["victor over a naked opponent"] athlete — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Nagnajit₁ of Gandhāra; Kṛṣṇa subdued his sons and married one of his daughters | hist. np. of Nagnajit₁, expert in arts |śilpaśāstra|, author of the Citralakṣaṇa.
nagnátva [tva] n. nudity. nagnámușita [mușita] amnf nagnamușitā completely stripped.
nagnam [acc. nagna] iic.
nagnamkarana [karana] amnf nagnamkaranā which undresses.

naciketas var. naciketa [naciketa] m. phil. [BrP.] np. of Naciketā, a young Brahmin "who did not understand" (why his father was freeing himself from all his possessions); [KU.] he was cursed by his father Vājaśravasa, who is suitable for Gautama, irritated by his question "Father, to whom will you give me?", who sent him to Death; he went to the underworld, and waited for Yama for 3 days; Yama, to apologize for not having received him immediately, granted him the fulfillment of 3 wishes: his father's forgiveness, immortality, and knowledge of the Self [ātman]; then he taught him how to build the Vedic altar |agnicayana| to celebrate the sacred fire that would be named after him [nāciketa].
nácira [nacira] amnf nacirā not long; short. nacirāt adv. soon. nacirādiva adv. very soon, right away.
nañ nota. gram. mark of the negation 'na', and of the prefixes a and an₁. nañau prakṛtārthaṃ gamayataḥ dvau Two negations are equivalent to an affirmation.
nañartha [artha] m. gram. meaning of the particle 'na'.
nañtatpuruṣa [tatpuruṣa] m. gram. compound privative determinative word, like abrāhmana.
nañbahuvrīhi [bahuvrīhi] m. gram. exocentric privative compound word, like aputra.
nañvāda [vāda] m. bed. n.p. from the nañvāda “Discussion on Negation”, work by Navyanyāya Raghunātha₁ Śiromaṇi; also called due to Nañarthavivṛti, Nañvyutpatti and Nañviveka.
√ naṭ [related to nṛt] v. [1] pr. (naṭati) to dance; to mime — ca. (nāṭayati) to act; to mime.

nața |agt. naț| m. dancer, actor, comedian, mime — f. națī actress; courtesan. națarāja [rāja] m. myth. np. of Națarāja, epith. of Shiva in his cosmic aspect of the "King of the dance", dancing in the posture of nadānta tāṇḍava, after the submission of the sages | rṣi | heretics of the cedar forest TaragamDevadāruvana to the prayer of the dragon [nāga] Ananta, this dance was replayed before the gods at Cidambaram, in Tamil Nadu.
nataśekhara | śekhara | m. myth. np. of Națasekhara "Pinacle of the dance", star dancer of the daityās; to surpass him, Indra asked Nandikeśvara to compose the Abhinayadarpaṇa.
nateśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Nateśvara, epith. of Shiva in his cosmic aspect of the "Lord of the dance"; cf. Națarāja; Śivakāmasundarī.
nad iic. nada.
nadvat [vat] amnf nadvatī covered with roses
nadvala |vala| amnf nadvalā covered with reeds — n. wet place, marsh. nadvalodakam pādarogah (maxim) one catches diseases of the feet by walking in marshes.
naḍá [related to nala] m. bio. bot. Arundo tibialis, variety of reed.

natá |pp. nam| amnf Natā bent, twisted; leaning, inclined; flattened, sunken; prostrate | phon. said of the nasal n changed into the cerebral n — n. astr. inclination — f. Natā myth. [Mah.] np. of Natā, daughter of Sukī₁; Vinatā is his daughter. natāśubhāśunāśakah epith. of Ganesha "who swiftly destroys the sins of those who prostrate themselves before him".
natabhrū [bhrū] amnf with arched eyebrows — f. woman raising her eyebrows.
natonnata [unnata] amnf natonnatā with ups and downs.
natonnatabhūmibhāga [bhūmibhāga] m. bumpy ground.
nati [act. nam] f. curvature; inclination, greeting; humility | gram. retroflexion of a dental into a cerebral.
natu [natu] conj. rather than, and not; although, nevertheless. varam buddhir natu vidyā Wisdom is better than knowledge.

√ nad v. [1] pr. (nádati) pp. (nadita) pf. (anu, ni, pra, vi) to murmur; to rustle, to resonate, to make a sound; to cry out, to howl, to neigh — ca. (nādayati) ca. (nadáyati) )7 to make resound, to fill with noise or cries — des. (ninadișati) to want to cry out — intens. (nānadati) to howl.
nadá [agt. nad] m. river | to be noisy (not. cloud, horse, bull) — f. cf. nadī.
nadanadī | nadī | iic. all the rivers.
nadanadīpati | pati | m. lord of all rivers, epith. of the Indus |Sindhu|.

nadānta [anta] m. myth. cosmic dance of Shiva Națarāja, who makes the "silence" of the universe cease at its final dissolution; represented in bronze idols in South India, notably in the Cola period (11th century); Shiva in Gangādhara holds in his upper right hand a drum [damarin] symbolizing the primordial sound, in his upper left hand a flame symbolizing the destruction of the world, his lower right hand is in abhaya mudrā symbolizing divine protection, his lower left hand shows his raised left foot symbolizing the hope of liberation, the right foot resting on the epileptic dwarf Apasmārapurusa symbolizing ignorance; all surrounded by a halo of fire [prabhāvali]; this dance is also called ānandatāndava.
nadikā [nadaika] ifc. f. river.
nadī [f. nada] f. river, current | med. blood circulation; tension. nadyāstīre at the riverbank.
Nadīja [ja] amnf nadījā from the river — m. myth. np. of Nadīja, epith. of Bhīsma "son of Gangā" — nf nadijā bio. lotus.

nadīya [īya] amnf nadīyā region "around the river" in Bengal, of capital Navadvīpa, where Rag hunātha₁ Siromaṇi founded the nadīyā university in the 15th century, an important center of dialectic, logic and law.
nadīsaṃgama [saṃgama] m. geo. confluence of two rivers.
naddhá |pp. nah| amnf naddhā attached, bound; assembled, joined; equipped, girded — ifc. fixed to (iic.) — n. link, attachment, restraint; knot.
nanandṛ cf. nanāndṛ.
nanā f. mother, mom.
nanāndṛ f. sister-in-law (husband’s sister) | var. nanandr id.
nanāndrpati | pat | mr. husband of his sister-in-law.

nanú [nanu₂] adv. no, not at all; never (insistent question or statement) Isn't that so? Isn't it true that? | certainly, indeed, undoubtedly; of course | (imp. interr.) please, I beg you | adr. expresses kindness, closeness, or perplexity. nanūcyatām please tell us. nanūpaviśāmah well, we'll sit down.

√ nand v. [1] pr. (nandati) pr. r. (nandate) pfp. (nandya) pf. (abhi, ā, prati) to rejoice; to rejoice in (acc.) — ps. (nandyate) to be rejoiced; to enjoy — ca. (nandayati) to rejoice, to fill with joy.

nánda [act. nand] m. joy, pleasure, happiness | myth. |Mah.| "Joyful", proper noun of Nanda Mahārāja, king of the shepherds, who raised Kṛṣṇa with his wife Yaśodā in Vraja | myth. [Mah.] name of a drum of Yudhişthira | myth. proper noun of a dvārapāla (its double being called Sunanda) | hist. name of the Nanda dynasty of Magadha; it was overthrown by Candra gupta who founded the Maurya dynasty | math. symb. the number 9 (for the nine Nanda kings) | myth. proper noun of Nanda₁, one of the 8 dragon kings [nāgarāja] | hist. proper noun of Nanda₂, half-brother of Buddha — f. Nandā bliss, joy, happiness; prosperity | geo. np. of the mountain Nandā devī, 7816 peak of the Himalayas, in the mod. state of Uttarākhaṇḍa; myth. she embodies Pārvatī; her East peak, 7434 n high, is her companion Sunandā devī — f. nandī blessing.
nandagopa | gopa | mr. myth. n.p. of nandagopa, husband of Yasodā in Vraja; cf. Nanda.
nandatanuja | tanuja | mr. myth. n.p. of Nandata nuja "(adoptive) son of Nanda Mahārāja", epith. of Kṛṣṇa.
nandapadra | padra | min geo. n.p. from the town of Nandapadra (mod. Nandod, near Baruch in Gu jarāt).

nandaka [agt. nand] amnf nandikā Joyful, happy — ifc. who takes pleasure in (iic.) myth. np. of nandaka "Joyful", sword [khadga] of Viṣṇu — act. m. joy, pleasure. nandakah nom. (blessing) may he rejoice — f. nandakā may she rejoice.

nandana [agt. nand] amnf nandanā that rejoices, that makes happy — m. son | astr. np. of nandana "happiness", personifying the 26th year of a life cycle [samvatsara] — act. n. bliss [[nandanavana] myth. np. of the nandana₁ park, paradisiacal stay of Indra in Svarga.
nandanavana [vana] n. myth. np. of the Nanda navana park, Indra's paradisiacal abode in Svarga.
Nandi [act. nand] mn joy; game — m. myth. np. of Nandi "Joyful", epith. of various gods — f. joy, happiness.
nandigrāma | grāma | m. geo. | Mah. | np. of the village of nandigrāma, where Bharata₁ ensured the regency of the kingdom while awaiting the return of Rāma.

nandighosa [ghosa] m. cries of joy, joyful music soc. proclamation by a herald or panegyrist myth. np. of nandighosa, chariot of Arjuna | soc. np. of the 18-wheeled chariot of Jagannātha at the festival of rathayātrā.
Nandirudra | rudra | mr. myth. n.p. of Nandirudra, Joyful aspect of Siva.

Nandivardhana₁ [vardhana] amnf nandivard hanā which increases joy, which brings happiness (of (g.)) — m. myth. [BhP.] np. of the nandivard hana king Janaka of Mithilā, son of Udāvasu, father of Suketu₁ | np. of many characters | geo. np. of the city of Nandivardhana₁, capital of the Vākāṭakās dynasty (3rd century); mod. Nagardhan at 28 km from mod. Nagpur.
nandivarvarman [varman] m. hist. n.p. of king Pal lava Nandivarvarmā II; he reigned in Kāñcī from 731 to 795.
nandīśvara [īśvara] m. myth. n.p. from nandīśvara, epith. of Siva | myth. epith. of Nandī, Siva's first assistant.
nandyāvarta [āvarta] m. jn. ["whirlwind of joy"] diagram symbol of the tīrthankara Aranātha, formed of a swastika extending in Greek into a square.
nandika [nandaika] m. myth. n.p. from Nan dika “Merry”; cf. Nandī.

Nandikeśvara₁ [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Nan dikeśvara, form of Nandī musician; he is represented with a bull's head and a human body with 4 arms, The superiors holding the axe [paraśu] and the gazelle [mṛga], The inferiors playing the mrdanga | hist. np. of Nandikeśvara₁, presumed author of the Abhinayadarpaṇa, which he composed at the request of Indra as an abridgment of the Bharatārṇava composed according to the rules of Bharatamuni.
nandikeśvarakāśikā [kāśikā] f. bed. n.p. from the Nan dikeśvarakāśikā, grammatical work.
nandikeśvarasamhitā [samhitā] f. bed. n.p. from the nandikeśvarasamhitā, collection of Shivaist ritual; cf. Sivadharma.

Nandin [agt. nand] amnf Nandinī Joyful, rejoicing — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Nandī "Joyful", member of the gaṇa, follower of Shiva, armed with a spear [śūla]; later identified with his mount [vāhana] the bull Vṛṣabha; cf. Ḥṣabha, Basava — f. Nandinī myth. np. of Nandinī "joyful", cow of plenty | kāmadughadhenu | of Vasiṣṭha; she is daughter of Surabhī; also called Sabalā | myth. np. of Nandinī₁, daughter of a king of Kāśī, wife of Svaphalka and mother of Akrūra.
nápāt m. ved. descendant; grandson, son || lat. nepos; ang. nephew; all. Neffe; fr. neveu, nepotism.
napumlinga [contr. nastrīpumlinga] n. gram. gender neutral.
nápuṃs [contr. nastrīpuṃs] m. eunuch; effeminate man | nápumsa id.
nápuṃsaka [aka] amn ["neither male nor female"] hermaphrodite, androgyne — m. eunuch — n. gram. neuter gender.
napuṃsakanāman | nāman | amnf napuṃsakanāmnī which has a neutral name.
napuṃsakaliṅga [liṅga] anfm napumsakalingā gram. gender neutral.
napuṃsakalingatā [tā] f. gram. state of being of neuter gender. kriyāvišeṣaṇānām karmatvam napumsakalingatā ca gram. Adverbs have an object role and are of neuter gender.
náptr | related to napāt | m. | sg. nom. naptā, acc. naptāram grandson; cf. pautra, dauhitra — f. naptrī granddaughter.
√ nabh v. [1] pr. r. (nábhate) to be swollen; to burst.

nábhas |abstr. nabh| n. sky, celestial vault; at mosphère | cloud, mist, vapor — m. astr. name of a Vedic month (śrāvaṇa₂, July-August) | var. nabha id. | gr. ; lat. nebula; all. Nebel; fr. nuage, nébuleux; ru. nebo. nabhastas adv. coming from the sky. tārakitam nabhaḥ the starry sky. nabhaḥspṛśaṃ dīptam [BhG.] In incandescence I touch the sky (modern motto of the Indian Air Force).
nabhaścara | cara | amnf nabhaścarī | "who goes to heaven"] aerial; celestial — m. bird; cloud; star | math. symb. the number 9 (for navagraha).
nabhastva |tva| n. cloud state; vaporous state; nebulosity.
nabhasmaya |maya| amnf nabhasmayī nua geux, vaporeux; brûmeux.
nabhasvat [vat] amnf nabhasvatī id. — adv. like steam.
nabhasá |nabhasa| amnf nabasā nua geux; vaporeux — m. sky, atmosphere | humid season. )9
nabhasyá [nabhasya] amnf nabhasyā cloudy, misty — m. astr. name of a Vedic month (bhādrapada, August-September).
nábhrāj | nabhrāj | m. cloud | ved. divine being, guardian of the soma.

√ nam v. [1] pr. (námati) imp. (nama) pft. (nanāma) aor. [6] (anaṃsīt) pp. (nata) pfp. (na manīya, namitavya) abs. (natvā, nátya, namya) pf. (ava, ā, ut, upa, pari, pra, vi) to bend, incline, lean | to bow, stoop | to greet, honor, pay homage to; to submit to, yield to | gram. to change a dental into the corresponding cerebral — ps. (namyate) to be bent; to submit, yield — ca. (namayati) ca. (nāmayati) to incline, bend; to cause to bend || gr. o ; lat. nemus. namate dandah the stick bends.

namanīya [pfp. [2] nam] amnf namanīyā Who must be greeted.

námas [abstr. nam] n. salute, homage, adoration; prostration; obedience — ind. glory to (dat.); I bow before (dat.) — v. [11] pr. (na masyati) to pay homage to (acc.), to honor, to greet; to revere, to adore.

namaste ["I greet you"] greetings; hello, welcome; good evening. om namah śivāya [pañcākṣarī] glory to Shiva! śrī gaņeśāya namaḥ in homage to Gaņeśa (invocation at the beginning of a Sanskrit work). haraye namah greetings to Hari. śrī śrī gurave namah in homage to the revered master (invocation at the beginning of a Sanskrit work). namo'stu te Ö (voc.) I give you thanks; glory to you (invocation in a prayer). namo namaḥ greetings. namaskr to pay homage to, to worship. namasyati devān he worships the gods.
namaskāra [kāra] m. greeting, homage; adoration (performed with the head bowed in the hands in añjali mudrā, and pronouncing namaḥ). namaskāram adr. welcome; greetings; good morning, good evening.
namaskṛta [kṛta] amnf namaskṛtā adored.
namita [namita] amnf namitā curved, inclined.
namitavya [pfp. [3] nam] amnf nami tavyā Who must be greeted.
naminātha var. niminātha m. jn. np. of naminātha, 21st mythical tīrthankara; his body is golden, his symbol is the blue lotus.

namuci [namuc₂] m. myth. [MkP.] np. from the dānava namuci "Who does not deliver"; Indra had promised not to attack him by day or by night, nor with dry or wet weapons; taking advantage of Indra's drunkenness, he stole half of his strength; Indra regained it with the help of Sarasvatī and the Aśvinau, and killed namuci "by churning his head with foam"; cf. Vṛtra.

Nambuthiri var. nampūtiri [malayalam] m. geo. np. Nambuthiri of a community of Brahmans from Kerala originating from the Cola kingdom in Tamil Nadu; they preserve to this day the Vedic śrauta rites, not. the agnicayana and the agnistoma.
namya [pfp. [1] nam] amnf namyā that one must honor; venerable.
namrá [namra] amnf namrā inclined, bent, leaning; deferential, humble | adr. your servant — ifc. submitted to (iic.). bhavanti namrāstaravaḥ phalāgamaiḥ the trees bend under the weight of the fruits.
namrátā [tā] f. act of bowing | act of bowing before (loc. iic.) | humility, deference; submission.
namrátva [tva] n. id.

naya [agt. nī₁] m. One who leads (not. an army) myth. np. of naya "Guide", son of Dharma and Kriyā — act. m. conduct, way of acting; governance, policy | prudence, wisdom, skill | foresight, purpose, plan; method, doctrine | jn. argumentative point of view; 7 are distinguished: nai gama, saṃgraha, vyavahāra, rjusūtra, śabda, sa mabhirūḍha and evaṃbhūta; the nayacakra distinguishes 12 — iic. with wisdom. nayeşu adv. with prudence.
nayacakra [cakra] n. jn. n.p. from the nayacakra of Mal lavādī; cf. Dvādaśāranayacakra.
nayavāda [vāda] m. jn. doctrine of viewpoints; it accounts for the multiform nature of reality [anekāntavāda] by proposing a modal logic according to different modes of predication [syādvāda].
nayat |ppr. nī₁| amnf nayantī by leading, by driving.
nayana | act. nī₁ | n. conduct, behavior | the act of directing — agt. n. eye — f. nayanā f. nayanī pupil of the eye. nayane the two eyes.
nayanajala [jala] n. tear. )()
nayanapatha | patha | mr. field of vision; syn. caksurvisaya, darśanapatha.
nayanaputa [puta] mn eyelid.
nayanavat [vat] amnf nayanavatī provided with eyes.
nayanavisaya [viṣaya] m. field of vision; horizon. nayanavişayībhāva m. being in sight.
nayanaviṣayamavatīrṇaḥ ["he came into my field of vision"] I suddenly saw him.
nayanonmīlana [unmīlana] n. soc. rite of consecration of an idol by "opening of its eyes".
nayanar m. hist. saint devotional poet shaiva of Tamil Nadu; The 4 principal ones are Appar, Sundarar, Sambandhar and Manikkavacakar; there are 63 of them.
nayavat |nayavat| amnf nayavatī skilled in politics; shrewd, wise.

nára | related to nṛ | m. Man, male, person myth. np. of Nara, the primordial Man, son of Dharma and Ahimsā, often associated with his twin Nārāyaṇa; Arjuna is his incarnation on Earth | pawn in the game of chess | pl. narās people, folk, humanity.
narakapāla |kapāla| n. human skull. lokah pibati surām narakapāle'pi People drink alcohol even from a human skull.
naratva [tva] n. quality of being a Man, humanity.
náranārāyaṇa |Nārāyaṇa| m. myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa "the Lord made Man" | du. na ranārāyaṇau myth. Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa.
náranārī [nārī] f. du. naranaryau Man and woman.
nárapati [pati] m. cf. nṛpati.
narapatipatha [patha] m. royal road.
nárapaśu [paśu] m. brute in human form | Man victim of a sacrifice.
nárabali | Bali | mr. soc. human sacrifice; syn. na ramedha.
náramedha | medha | m. soc. human sacrifice; syn. narabali | soc. funeral cremation.
nárarāja [rāja] m. myth. np. of Nararāja, epith. of Kubera "Master of men (slaves of riches)".

naravarman [varman] m. hist. np. of Naravarmā "Protector of Men", King Paramāra, prince of Mālava, son of Udayāditya; around 1100 he renovated the temple of Mahākāla at Ujjayinī; he encouraged the study of Sanskrit. 5(
naravahana [vāhana] m. myth. np. of Na ravahana, epith. of Kubera "who has Man as a mount".

Naravāhanadatta [datta] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Prince Naravāhanadatta "gift of Kubera", mythical son of King Udayana and Vāsavadattā₂; the Brhatkathā, transcribed by Guṇāḍhya, recounts his loves, and how he became emperor of the magic genies | vidyādharās | ; Vasudeva replaces him in the Jain version Vasudevahindi. nárasimha var. nṛṣiṃha [siṃha] m. myth. np. of Narasimha or Nrsimha "Lion-Man", 4th avatar of Vișnu, who destroyed the daitya Hiranyakasipu by tearing out its entrails; he is the King of the kṛtayuga ; cf. Karālanarasiṃha | Hist. np. of Narasimha₁, son of Vișnuvardhana, King of Hoysala from 1152 to 1173 | Hist. np. of Narasimha₂, King of Kalinga from 1238 to 1264, descendant of Anantavarmā Codaganga; he built the temples of Konārka and Candrasekhara | Hist. np. of Narasimha₃, King of the Deccan dynasty in the 15th century | Hist. np. of Saluva Narasimha₄, King of Vijayanagara (1486–1491); he fought many rebel leaders, and was taken prisoner by Gajapati Purusottamadeva₁; he traded his freedom for the surrender of the citadel of Udayagiri; Narasa Nāyaka was his minister and commander of the armies; in 1496 he made a long campaign to subdue the kings of the South (Cola, Hoysala, etc.), and he held King Ganapati at bay in the North; at the death of the emperor he ensured the regency | hist. np. of Narasimha₅ Rāya, son of Saluva, King of Vijayanagara (1491–1505) | hist. np. of Vīra₁ Narasimha₆, eldest son of Narasa Nāyaka; he became King of Vijayanagara (1505–1509), inaugurating the Tuluva dynasty.
narasimhagupta | gupta | mr. hist. n.p. of Emperor Narasimhagupta of North India (early 6th century).
narasimhadīkṣā [dīkṣā] f. soc. Royal consecration rite of the Vaisnava Pañcarātra tradition.
narasiṃhapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. bed. n.p. of Narasimhapurāṇa, an upapurāṇa.

narasimhavarman [varman] m. hist. np. of the King of the Pallavās Narasiṃhavarmā₁, who reigned in Kāñcīpura (630–668) | hist. np. of Narasimhavarmā₁, who reigned in Kāñcīpura around 700, and had the Kailāsanātha temple built there.

Narahari [hari₂] m. hist. np. of Narahari, lexicographer of Kaśmīra of the 15th century, author of the Rājanighaṇṭu (Kaśmīra, 18th century) | hist. np. of )1 18^ e Narahari₁, author of the Bodhasāra (Kaśmīra, century).
narādhipa [adhipa] m. king ["master of men"].

nárāśaṃsa [śaṃsa] m. ved. [RV.] np. of Narāśaṃsa "who receives the praise of men", form of Agni who first receives the offering to the gods; he is born from Tanūnapāt conceived in the mother | arani | to become nir Mātariśvā, the first breath [marut] of the winds; it is said that he commands the wives of the gods.
Narendra₁ [Indra] m. king ["lord of men"] | hist. np. of King Rājarāja Narendra₁ of the Eastern Cālukyās dynasty (11th century); his capital was Rājamahendrapura.
nareśa [īśa] m. king ["lord of men"]. kāśinareśa title of king of Benares; during śivarātri he is the only one to officiate in the sanctum of the Viśvanātha.
nareśvara [īśvara] m. king ["lord of men"].
Narottama [uttama] m. the best of men | myth. np. of Narottama, epith. of Viṣṇu "the Supreme Being" | bd. epith. of Buddha.

náraka [naraka] mn myth. hell (guarded by naraYama) | bd. hell where the damned are tortured; [Abhidharmakośa] there are 8 glacial ones, and 8 burning ones | myth. np. of the titan [asura] Naraka "Infernal", son of VarāhaViṣṇu and Bhūmi; at Bhūmi's request, Viṣṇu had granted him the all-powerful weapon vaisnavāstra, to protect him from both the devās and the asurās; he reigned in Assam over Prāgjyotisa guarded by Mura; through his penances he acquired great powers from Brahmā and became a tyrant; he stole Varuna's royal parasol and Aditi's earrings; he had obtained the right to be killed only by his own mother; He was defeated by Satyabhāmā, reincarnation of Bhūmi, and finished off by Kṛṣṇa; he was reincarnated as Karṇa; [Mah.] the mighty warrior Bhagadatta is said to be his son; he is considered the ancestor of the Kāmarūpās kings; cf. Bhauma₁, dīpāvali.
narakakunda [kunda] n. myth. well of torture of the wicked in hell; there are 86 of them.
narakacaturdaśī [caturdaśī] f. soc. fourteenth day of the clear fortnight of the month kārttika, commemorating the victory of Kṛṣṇa over Naraka, also called vaikunthacaturdaśī; cf. dīpāvali.
narakavarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Svargādikānda, dealing with hell.
nart [ca. nṛt] v. [10] pr. (nartayati) pp. (nartita) to dance.
narta [act. nṛt] m. dance.
nartaka [agt. nṛt] m. dancer, actor; dance master — f. nartakī dancer, actress
nartana [agt. nṛt] m. dancer — act. n. dance, dramatic art.
nartananirnaya [nirnaya] m. lit. np. from the Nartananirnaya, treatise on dance and dramatic art by Puṇḍarīka₅, written at the request of Emperor Akbar (16th century).
nartita [pp. nart] amnf nartitā that one makes dance — n. dance.
√ nard v. [1] pr. (nardati) pft. (nanarda) pp. (nardita) inf. (narditum) to bellow; roar; shout.
narda [agt. nard] amnf nardā who bellows, who roars; noisy.

nardana [act. nard] n. bellow; roar; cry | praise, celebration.
nardita [pp. nard] amnf narditā who has bellowed, who has cried out — n. bellow; roar; cry — m. soc. winner at the game.
Narma IIc. Narman.
narmada [da] amnf Narmadā amusing, pleasant; who entertains — f. cf. Narmadā.
narmabhāṣita [bhāṣita] amnf narmabhāṣitā said in a joking manner.
narmamālā [mālā] f. bed. n.p. from the narmamālā “Comic Garland”, a work of social satire by Ksemendra.
narmasaciva |saciva| m. soc. playmate of a prince.
Narmadā [f. narmada] f. geo. np. of the Narmadā, river which originates at the Amarakantaka peak of the Vindhya mountains and flows into the Gulf of Khambhāta (mod. Nerbudda); cf. Revā.
narmadāparikrama [parikrama] m. geo. pilgrimage of the Narmadā; it follows the form of the symbol om; cf. Omkāreśvara.
narmadeśvara | īśvara | mr. soc. quartz pebble sacred to Siva, originating from Narmadā; syn. bāṇaliṅga.
narman [nṛman] n. [en comp. narma] amu sement, pleasure; entertainment, pastime; game, sport; joke.

Nala [related to nada] m. bio. bot. Amphidonax karka, a species of large reed | lit. [Mah.] np. of the hero Nala "Reed", king of the Niṣadhās, son of Vīrasena; handsome, brave, and generous, he fell in love with Princess Damayantī who chose him as her husband; for this, she had to thwart, with the help of Sarasvatī, the deception of the cardinal gods Indra, Agni, Yama, and Varuna, who had all taken on the appearance of Nala; Nala was dispossessed of his kingdom by the treachery of his brother Puşkara and by the gambling demon Kali, and he abandoned Damayantī to the dangers of the forest, but they will happily be reunited at the end of the story; cf. Karkotaka, Naisadhacarita; Yama inspired him with the Pākadarpaṇa | myth. np. of Nala₁, 3rd son of Yadu | myth. [Rām.] np. of the monkey Nala₂, son of Viśvakarmā, having inherited his architectural gifts; he built for Rāma the jetty |setu| allowing him to invade Lankā — n. smell, perfume — f. nalā myth. [Mah.] np. of nalā, daughter of Kaśyapa and Tāmrā; she bore Vinatā. āsīd rājā nalo nāma vīrasenasuto balī | upapanno guņair istai rūpavān aśvakovidaḥ | [Nalopākhyāna] He was a king, called Nala, son of Vīrasena, then sant, endowed with all desirable qualities, of fine bearing and consummate horseman.
nalakīla [kīla] m. knee.

nalakūbara [kūbara] m. var. Nalakūvara myth. np. of the genius | guhyaka | nalakūbara or Nalakūvara, son of Kubera; he married the nymph | apsaras | Rambhā; she having been raped by Rāvaṇa, nalakūbara cursed him so that he could not touch a non-consenting woman without dying, thus contributing to the protection of Sitā; [BhP.] he got drunk on vāruņī with his brother Maṇigrīva, and they danced naked with nymphs before Nārada; he condemned them to become arjuna trees for 100 heavenly years; Kṛṣṇa as a child freed them by uprooting the trees.
nalacampū [campū] f. bed. n.p. of the nalacampū, first campū style poem, due to Trivikrama₁ Bhaṭṭa (10th century); also called Madālasācampū.
nálada [da] mn bio. bot. Nardostachys ja tamansi, Indian nard; valerianaceae plant of the Himalayas with aromatic fibrous rhizome used in perfumery; syn. jaṭāmāmsī.
nalapāka | pāka | m. lit. | Mah. | gift of making tasty food, given by Yama to Nala as a reward for her role as messenger.
nalapākaśāstra [śāstra] n. lit. np. from Na lapākaśāstra "Science of food", teaching the art of preparing dishes.
Nalasetu [setu] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the Nalasetu "Nala Bridge₂", built by the monkeys so that Rāma's army could invade Lankā.
Nalābhyudaya |abhyudaya| mr. bed. n.p. from Nalābhyudaya "Triumph of Nala", poem by Vāmana₄ Bhatta Bāṇa. 5(
Nalopākhyāna [upākhyāna] n. myth. np. from the Na lopākhyāna (story of Nala), section of the Mah. which Brhadaśva tells to Yudhisthira to show him that his misfortunes could be much worse.
nalaka [Nalaka] n. long bone (hollow like a reed); not. tibia — f. nalikā vessel of the body; syn. nādī | quiver.

nalina n. organic. bot. Nelumbium speciosum, pink lotus; syn. kamala — f. nalinī pond covered with lotus | myth. n.p. of the nalinī, a divyagangā; it is a branch of the Milky Way or celestial Ganges [Mandākinī].
nalva m. length measurement, approximately 200 m.
náva₁ amnf navā new, new, recent, fresh, young | fresh, uncooked (not. earthenware pot) || gr. ; lat. novus; ang. new; all. neu; fr. neuf, nouveau. navīkṛ to rejuvenate, refresh, renovate; revive.
navakarmika [karmika] m. architect.

navakalevara [kalevara] mn soc. ceremony of the new body, ritual of renewal of the idol of Jagannātha at Purī on the occasion of a double month āṣādha; the consecrated nīma tree is found by divi nation of a priest of Mangalā; the ritual occurs at intervals of 9, 12 or 19 years; one does not marry during the year in which it occurs.
navatara |tara| amnf navatarā compar. younger, fresher, more recent syn. navīyas. vrkso vrkņo rohati mūlān navatarah punah A cut tree grows back from its root, rejuvenated anew.
navatā [tā] f. novelty; freshness.
navatva [tva] n. novelty; freshness.
navanagara [nagara] n. geo. n.p. from the town of nava nagara, near Dvārakā in Gurjara; cf. Šatruśalya.
návanīta [nīta] n. butter (fresh).
navanītagopāla [gopāla] m. myth. representation of Kṛṣṇa as a child stealing butter.
navanītagola [gola] m. ball of butter.
navabaddha [baddha] amnf navabaddha recently attached.
navaśaśibhṛt [śaśibhṛt] m. myth. epith. of Shiva "who bears the crescent moon".
navāhnika |āhnika| n. lit. section of the Mahābhāsya.
navotthāna [utthāna] amnf navotthānā nou vellement levé (astre) — m. renaissance.
nava₂ iic. navan.

navakuñjara | kuñjara | m. myth. | BhG. | the ''nine treasures' chimera formed of 9 animals (elephant, snake, bull, horse, peacock, lion, tiger, rooster and )3 parrot) in which Kṛṣṇa manifested himself before Arjuna to establish his supremacy during the episode of khāndavadahana.
navagraha [graha] m. pl. astr. the 9 astral influences, including the Sun |Sūrya|, the Moon |Candra|, the 5 planets Mars [Angāraka], Mercury [Budha], Jupiter [Bṛhaspati], Venus [Śukra] and Sa
turne [Sani], and the two demons of the eclipse Rāhu and of the comet Ketu; they are often depicted sculpted on the lintel of the sanctuary of a temple.
navacatvāriṃśa [catvāriṃśa] amnf nava catvārimśī ord. 49ᵉ.
navacatvārimsat | catvārimsat | f. 49.
navajala [jala] n. new water.
navajalamaya [maya] amnf navajalamayī made of new water.
navatrimśa [trimśa] amnf navatrimśī ord. 39ᵉ consisting of 39 parts.

navatrimsati [trimsati] f. 39.
navadaśa [daśa] amnf navadaśī ord. 19ᵉ.
navadaśan |daśan| num. pers. 19.
navadvāra [dvāra] amnf navadvārā which has nine orifices — n. the human body (compared to a city with 9 gates).

navadvīpa | dvīpa | m. geo. np. of the city of Na vadvīpa "Formed of nine islands" on a branch of the Ganges in Bengal, 130 km north of Calcutta (Nadīyā district); it was the capital of the Sena dynasty in the 12th century, and an important center of learning; Caitanya was born there and lived there in his youth; it is a place of pilgrimage of the gaudīya sampradāya.
navadhā |dhā| adv. nine times; in nine parts; in nine ways.
navanavati [navati] num. f. 99 | ved. [RV.] large number.
navanavatitama [tama] amnf navanavati tamī ord. 99ᵉ.

navanidhi [nidhi] m. myth. [Tantra] the 9 hidden treasures, guarded by Kubera: kacchapa the tortoise, ma kara the crocodile, mukunda the jewel, nanda good fortune, kharva the countless, nīla the sapphire, śankha the conch, padma the lotus or padmarāga the ruby and mahāpadma the great lotus, each guarded by a yakṣa or a nāga.
navapañcāśa | pañcāśa | amnf navapañcāśī ord. 59^ e. 5(
navapañcāśat [pañcāśat] num. f. 59.
navapattrikā [pattrikā] f. soc. "the 9 leaves", rite of celebration of the durgāpūjā, where the Goddess is worshipped in the form of the leaves of nine plants.
navapallava | pallava | n. bud, new shoot.
navapāṣāṇa [pāṣāṇa] n. alloy of 9 metals.
navama [ma] amnf navamī ord. ninth — f. navamī soc. festival on the 9th day of a lunar half-month; cf. rāmanavamī.
navamallikā [mallikā] f. organic. bot. Jasminum sam bac, white jasmine, with a sweet scent.
navamālikā [mālikā] f. lit. [DKC.] np. of the princess navamālikā, daughter of King Dharmavardhana of Srāvastī; she married Pramati₁.
navamukha [mukha] amnf navamukhī which has nine orifices.
navaranga | ranga | m. pl. astr. the nine colors of gems associated with the influence of a star; cf. navaratna | arch. room located in the center of a temple.

navaratna [ratna] n. pl. navaratnāni astr. the nine gems associated with the influence of a celestial body [navagraha]: the ruby [māṇikya] to the Sun [Sūrya], the pearl [muktā] to the Moon [Candra], the coral to Mars [Mangala], the emerald [marakata] to Mercury [Budha], the topaz [puṣyarāga] to
Jupiter [Guru], diamond [vajra] to Venus [Sukra], sapphire [nīla] to Saturn [Sani], lapis
lazuli [rājāvarta] at the eclipse [Rāhu], and quartz

hyacinth [gomeda] to the comet [Ketu] | hist. ["the nine jewels of the court"] the nine illustrious poets/scholars traditionally associated with the court of King Vikramāditya in Avanti: Dhanvantari₂, Kṣapaṇaka, Amarasimha, Sanku, Vetālabhaṭṭa, Ghataparpara, Kālidāsa, Vararuci and Varāhamihira lit. the nine main works of Rāmānuja: śrī Bhāsya (commentary on the Brahmasūtra), Vaikunthagadya, Śrīrangagadya, Śaranagatigadya, Vedārthasangraha, Vedāntasāra₁, Vedāntadīpa, and Gītābhāsya (commentary on the Gītā).

navarātra [rātri] m. nine-day period | ved. his soma cry with 9 days of extraction [sutyā] — n. soc. festival of durgāpūjā of the Bengal region Orissa; it celebrates the victory of Durgā over the buffalo asura Mahisa; it is held on the first 9 days of the bright fortnight [śuklapakṣa] of the month āśvina (September-October); colored clay statues are built showing his victory over Mahisa; on the 9th day the mahānavamī festival takes place, where DurgāAparājitā is celebrated; on the 10th day [daśaharā] his clay idol is immersed in the river, symbolizing his return to Shiva; This is the festival of Durgā's Victory [vijayadaśamī]; during this festival the epic of Rāma [rāmalīlā] is played out, and on the 10th day effigies of Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa and Meghanāda are burned || hi. navarātri.
návavimsa [vimsa] amnf navavimsī ord. 29th made up of 29 parts.
návavimásti [vimásti] f. 29.
Navavihāra [vihāra] m. geo. n.p. du grand monastery bd. Navavihāra, in Bactres, capital of Bactria (mod. Balkh, in northern Afghanistan).
Navavṛndāvana |vṛndāvana| n. geo. n.p. of Navavrndāvana, place of memory, where the ashes of 9 disciples of Madhvācārya rest in a park of cenotaphs on an island of the Tungabhadrā, near mod. Hampi.
navaśata | śata | n. 109 — amnf navaśatā pl. 900.
navasasti |sasti| f. 69; syn. ekonasaptati.

navasāhasānka [sāhasānka] m. hist. n.p. from Na vasāhasānka "new Vikramāditya", title of King Sindhurāja of Mālava.

navasāhasānkacarita | carita | n. lit. np. of the epic poem Navasāhasānkacarita "Exploits of King Sind hurāja" by Parimala Padmagupta, in 18 cantos (circa 1005); it mixes a historical chronicle with the myth of the vidyādharī princess Saśiprabhā.
navāśīti [aśīti] num. f. 89.
navāśītitamī [tama] amnf navāśītitamī ord. 89^ e.
navata [navati] ifc. amnf navatī ord. 90th.

navan num. pers. the number nine | lat. novem; ang. nine; fr. neuf.
naviṣṭha [super. nava₁] amnf naviṣṭhā the most recent, the youngest; the last — m. myth. epith. of Agni or Indra.
navī iiv. nava₁.
navīkṛta [kṛta] amnf navīkṛtā rejuvenated, refreshed, renovated.
navīna [nava₁īna] amnf navīnā new, new — m. pl. navīnās logicians of the navyanyāya. 5(
navīya [nava₁īya] amnf navīyā véd. nou calf, new.
navīyas [compar. nava₁] amnf navīyasī new, fresh, young, recent — adv. recently. navīyasā adv. recently.
návya [contr. navīya] amnf navyā new, nine.

navyanyāya [nyāya] m. phil. np. of navyanyāya, dialectical semiotics or "new logic" (opp. old logic [prācīnanyāya]); the founder of this school [mūlagranthakāra] is Gangesěa; it discards notions of general philosophy to refocus on dialectic and reasoning [tarkaśāstra]; it has developed a relational calculus of notions formalized in compound words, usable by all sciences [śāstra]; its principal operators are conjunction [avacchedaka], the
disjunction [nirūpaka] and negation/complement [pratiyogin].
navyanyāyaparibhāṣā [paribhāṣā] f. phil. technical language of navyanyāya, conceptual calculus of a relational nature, based on the elaboration of unambiguous para phrases.

Navyanyāyabhāṣāpradīpa [bhāṣāpradīpa] m. phil. np. from Navyanyāyabhāṣāpradīpa "Light on the Language of Navyanyāya", a didactic work by Maheśacandra Nyāyaratna (late 19th century). navyavyākaraņa [vyākaraņa] n. phil. np. from Na vyavyākaraņa, a modern development of grammar, using the language of Navyanyāya.
