nahi [nahi₁] adv. no, not at all, not in the slightest.

náhuṣa [nahusa] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Nahuṣa₁, 4th king of the lunar lineage, son of Āyu and father of Yayāti; he seized the throne of Indra when the latter had to hide to atone for the murder of Vrtra; the assembly of sages | rṣi | carried his chariot into the air, but his foot having touched Agastya, the latter transformed him into a serpent, and he was forced to live on earth for 100,000 years | myth. [Rām.] np. of King Nahuṣa₁ of Ayodhyā, son of Ambarīṣa₁, father of Yayāti₁.
náhus [abstr. nah] m. neighbor; one's fellow man; man | pl. nahuṣaṣ ved. humanity.
nā cf. nṛ.
nāka m. myth. vault of the heavens, firmament.
nāku n. anthill | mountain | myth. np. of the muni nāku.

nāga [*naga] m. serpent, cobra | myth. hydra, dragon, serpent genie with a human face, subterranean helper of the gods or local deity, sometimes mythical aboriginal ancestor of a royal lineage; descendants of Kaśyapa and Kadrū, the nāgās inhabit the marvelous subterranean city of Bhoga vatī; cf. AnantaŠeṣa, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Kārkoṭa, 5( Bhujanga, Sankhapāla | [nāgahasta] elephant myth. race of divine elephants, equipped with wings, and associated with clouds; they bring prosperity and fertility to humans; cf. Airāvata | myth. one of the 10 regions [dvīpa] forming the jambudvīpa | astr. third fixed lunar half-day [karaṇa] — f. nāgī myth. nāgī princess, of the dragon race; cf. Manasā — amnf nāgā f. nāgī concerning snakes or elephants || fr. naja. karena rājate nāgah [Rasagangādhara] The elephant is distinguished by its trunk (example of disambiguation) (mutual of kara and nāga). sāgram śatasahasram tu nāgānām bhārata | nāge nāge rathaśatam śatam cāśvā rathe rathe | [Mah.] There were more than one hundred thousand elephants, O Bharata, for each elephant there were one hundred chariots, for each chariot one hundred horsemen.
nāgapañcamī [pañcamī] f. soc. festival in honor of Manasā, where cobras are honored; it is held on the 5th day of the dark fortnight of the month āṣāḍha; syn. manasāpañcamī.
nāgapura | pura | n. geo. n.p. from the city of nāgapura to Vidarbha (mod. Nagpur to Mahārāṣṭra).
nāgapuspa [puṣpa] m. bio. bot. Mesua nagassa rium, a tree with brown bark, large fragrant white flowers, and hard oval fruits; it is used in medicine.
nāgábandha | bandha | m. phon. name of a meter imitating the rings of a snake.
nāgabhata [bhata] m. hist. np. of King Nāgabhata I (~730–760), founder of the Pratīhārās dynasty; he reigned in Ujjayinī; he repelled a Muslim invasion; he was subdued by the Rāṣṭrakūṭa Dantidurga.
nāgabhūṣaṇa [bhūṣaṇa] m. myth. epith. of Shiva "adorned with serpents".
nāgamātṛ [mātṛ] f. myth. Mother Serpent deity; cf. Manasā.
nāgaranga |anga₁| mr. organic. orange tree.
nāgarangaka [ka] m. id.
nāgarāja [rāja] m. myth. dragonoid; there are 8 in the comics tradition. of the lotus sutra: Nanda, Upananda, Sāgara, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Anavatapta, Manasvī and Utpalaka.

nāgalinga [linga] n. bio. bot. Couroupita guianen sis, a tree flowering in March, with large pink or orange flowers in large fragrant clusters along the trunk; its heavy brown fruits are spherical, and burst when they fall to the ground (they are compared to cannonballs); the tree, sacred to Shiva, is used in medicine.
Nāgasena₁ |senā| mr. bd. n.p. of the monk Nāgasena₁, contemporary of King Milinda; Rohana was his master; cf. Milindapraśna | bed. n.p. of Nāgasena₁, bd monk. from the play Mattavilāsa.

nāgasvāmin [svāmin] m. lit. [KSS.] np. du brah mane Nāgasvāmī; asking for alms, he received from a witch a red lotus, in fact a man's hand, to possess; he is protected by a cow, then by a pāśupata , then by the yakṣinī Su mitrā₁, who is just waiting to unite with such a mor to end a curse; when she joins Heaven, she enjoins him not to enter a room of her palace; there he finds a horse, which sends him in a kick as a hermit to a temple of Shiva where he acquires great powers; there he shelters Gomukha₁.
Nāgānanda [ānanda] m. lit. np. of the Nāgānanda, a drama of King Harșa, whose subject is the sacrifice of Jīmūtavāhana.
Nāgāntaka [antaka] m. myth. np. of Nāgāntaka, epith. of Garuda "Snake Killer".

Nāgārjuna₁ [arjuna] m. bd. np. of Nāgārjuna₁ "Silver Serpent", master bd. (150 250), author of the Madhyamakaśāstra (or Mūlamadhyamaka) of the Sūnyatāsaptati, the Vigrahavyāvartanī and the Vaidalyaprakaraṇa; the Ratiśāstra is also attributed to him; cf. mādhyamika | hist. np. of Nāgārjuna₁, presumed author of the Yogaśata | hist. np. of Nāgārjuna₁, author of the Yogaratnamālā | hist. np. of the alchemist Nāgārjuna₁, author of the Rasa ratnākara (between the 8th and 10th centuries) | lit. [KSS.] np. of Nāgārjuna₁, minister of King Cirāyus, who had conceived an elixir of long life; at the request of the gods, he renounced making an elixir of immortality; Prince Jīvahara asked him for his head, in order to be able to reign; Nāgārjuna₁ gave his head, as he had done in 99 different existences, and attained the state of buddha.

nāgārjunakuṇḍa |kuṇḍa| n. geo. np. of nāgārjunakuṇḍa, ancient site of the Andhra country on the banks of the Kṛṣṇā₁; it included many monasteries bd. and a large stūpa from the 2nd to the 3rd century, under the Ikṣvāku₁ dynasty; the site is now under the waters of a dammed lake.
Nāgāśana [aśana₂] m. myth. np. of Nāgāśana, epith. of Garuda "Snake Eater".

Nāgeśa [īśa] m. hist. n.p. of the grammarian Nāgeśa Bhaṭṭa, also called Nāgoji Dīkṣita 5( (1730–1810); he lived in Vārāṇasī; he fixed a collection of metalinguistic rules [paribhāṣā] associated with Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī in his Paribhāṣenduśekhara; he is also the author of the treatise on the semantics of the language Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntamañjūṣā, its summary the Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntalaghumañjūṣā, and the Vaiyākaraņasiddhāntaparamalaghumañjūṣā which condenses it Furthermore, he is also credited with the Sphotavāda explaining the doctrine of evocative power, the Sabdendusekhara, a commentary on the Siddhāntakaumudī, the Chāyāvyākhyā, a commentary on the Yogasūtra, the Paramalaghumañjūṣā, a treatise on lexical semantics, and the Uddyota, a commentary on the Pradīpa of Kaiyaṭa.
nāgeśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of nāgeśvara, one of the 12 radiant signs of Śiva [jyotirlinga], established in Kumbakonam in Tamil Nadu.

nāgara [*nagara] amnf nāgarī urban, ci tadin | polite, refined, courteous | clever, skillful, cunning — m. city dweller, citizen — f. nāgarī city girl | North Indian syllabic script for Sanskrit; cf. from vanāgarī.
nāgarakhaṇḍa |khaṇḍa| min reads. n.p. of Nāgarakhaṇḍa, section of Skandapurāṇa.
nāgaraka [*nagaraka] amnf nāgarikā who lives in town or village; opp. āraņyaka | urban; cultured | clever, skillful, cunning — m. aesthete | citizen; hero | policeman, city official.
nāgarika [*nagaraika] m. cf. nagaraka.
Nāgoji cf. Nāgeśa.

nāciketá [*naciketas] amnf nāciketī relating to Naciketā — m. phil. [KU.] the Sacred Fire with the three Vedic altars, whose order [agnicayana] was revealed by Yama to Naciketā. trināciketa m. phil. [KU.] who performs the triple sacrifice of the Fire through meditation, identifies with Virāt, and attains immortality.
nāciketopākhyāna [upākhyāna] n. bed. [KU.] history of Naciketā.
nāṭ [ca. naṭ] v. [10] pr. (nāṭayati) to act; to mime.
nāṭa [act. naṭ] mn dance; theatre.
nāṭamaṇḍapa | maṇḍapa | mn arch. dance pavilion, in a temple complex; cf. Koṇārka.

nāṭaka [agt. naṭ] amnf nāṭakī who dances; who plays in the theatre — m. dancer; actor, mime, singer — n. drama, dramatic work; dramatic genre of heroic comedy | theatrical performance — f. nāṭikā secondary dramatic work )7 |uparūpaka|. nāṭakīkṛ to transform into comedy.
nāṭakākhyāyikādarśana [ākhyāyikādarśana] n. soc. theatre and storytelling, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
nāṭya [pfp. [1] nāṭ] n. that which relates to the theatre, dramatic art, theatre; dramatic work, social performance of a drama; it combines simple recitation with mime |nrtya| with the
dance | nrtta|.
nātyavarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Svargādikānda, dealing with dramaturgy.

nātyaveda [veda] m. myth. [Nātyaśāstra] At the end of the krtayuga, when Vaivasvata was preparing the tretāyuga, Indra, leading the gods entering the Jam budvīpa, asked Brahmā to utter a 5th veda which would be permitted to be heard by all castes for their relaxation; Brahmā took the words of the Rgveda, the songs of the Sāmaveda, the rites of the Ya jurveda, and the magic of the Atharvaveda to compose the Nātyaveda "Knowledge of mime and dance", which he taught to Bharatamuni.

nātyaśāstra [śāstra] n. dramaturgy, art of classical dance | lit. np. of the Nātyaśāstra, great treatise on classical dance, attributed to Bharatamuni, and thus called Bharataśāstra; it is earlier than the 6th century, and even the 2nd century for its oldest parts; this encyclopedic treatise on the art of dance, theatre and music comprises 36 volumes; cf. Abhinavabhāratī.

nāṭyasaṃgraha [saṃgraha] m. [nāṭyaśāstra] collection of the components of theatre and dance. rasabhāvābhinayadharmivrttipravrttayah | siddhih svaras tathātodyam gānam rangas ca samgrahah The artistic mode, the emotion conveyed, the interpretation, its accuracy, the plot and its unfolding, the skill, the music, as well as the instruments, the song and the stage are the components (of theatre).
Nāṭyotpatti [utpatti] f. lit. np. of the Nāṭyotpatti, chapter of the Nāţyaśāstra.
nātyotsava | utsava | mr. soc. dance festival.
nāḍa [*naḍa] n. hollow stem — f. cf. nāḍi — f. cf. nādī.
nāḍi [f. nāḍa] f. tube, pipe; vein, artery, vessel.

nādikā [ka] f. hollow rod; pipe | drain pipe of a clepsydra |ghaṭikā| | time measure of a moment of day, equal to half a 5( muhūrta (24 minutes); 30 moments are counted, from sunset to sunrise; syn. ghațikā.
nāḍikāccheda [cheda] m. end of a 24-minute moment; it is sounded by the paṭaha drum.
nādijaigha [jaighā] m. myth. n.p. of the nādijangha vulture, friend of Virūpākṣa₁.

nāḍī [f. nāḍa] f. tube, pipe, channel; vessel, vein, artery; hollow stem, flute | phil. [yoga| sympathetic or psychic channel; the three principal ones are Idā, Pingalā and Susumņā; there are 10 or 14 of them; they are associated with the sites of perception | dvāra | astr. period of time of 24 minutes, equal to half a muhūrta ; also called ghaṭikā .
nādīprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. np. from the Nādīprakāśa "Explanation of the vessels", a medical work by Samkarasena.
nādīvraṇa [vraṇa] m. med. ulcer; fistula.

nāth v. [1] pr. (nāthati) pr. r. (nāthate) to ask for protection or help, to implore, to beseech; to desire, to solicit (dat. g.) | to dominate, to be master of all. Not. sarpiso nāthate he desires butter.
nātha |agt. nāth| m. master, lord; protector, husband.
nāthatva |tva| n. protection, patronage.

nāthadvārā [dvāra] f. geo. np. of the nāthadvārā shrine of Kṛṣṇa as a child [Srīnāthajī]; his idol, originally installed in Vṛndāvana, was moved to Rājasthāna 48 km northeast of Udaipur in the 17th century to protect it from Aurangzeb; this pilgrimage city is the main center of the |sampradāya| Kumāra₁ movement founded by Vallabhācārya.

nāthamuni [muni] m. hist. np. of nāthamuni, disciple of Nammālvār (10th century); he collected the Di vyaprabandha, corpus of devotional hymns of the Tamil Vaishnava tradition of the 12 saints "immersed (in divine experience)" [ālvār]; his work was continued by his grandson Yāmunācārya.

nāthayogin [yogin] m. hist. np. of a medieval tantric sect; their followers are strictly vegetarian and abstinent; they wear large flat [darśana] or cylindrical | kundala | earrings; at their initiation their ears are split open, hence their Hindi name kānphaṭa (pierced ear); cf. Adinātha₁, Gorakṣanātha.
nāthavat [vat] amnf nāthavatī who has a protector; subordinate — f. nāthavatī married woman.
nāthahari [hari₁] m. ["who takes away the master (of the flock)"] lion. )8
nād [ca. nad] v. [10] pr. (nādayati) pp. (nādita) to resound, to fill with noise or cries.
nādá | act. nad | m. resounding noise, tumult; cry, howl | phil. nasal in a mystical sound of yoga | lit. resonance. hastinādah trumpeting.

Nādaprada | prada | m. bd. np. of Nādaprada "He who transmits the roar (of the Buddha's teaching)", epith. of the Bengali mystic Saman tabhadra (1016–1100); student of Tilopa, pandita of Nālandā, he transmitted Buddhism to Tibet through his student Marpa; he is known as Nāropa; mod. Naropa University (Boulder, Co lorado) is named in his honor.
nādávat |vat| amnf nādavatī phon. sound.
nādasvara | svara | n. Carnatic musical wind instrument, a type of oboe; it is used notably at weddings.
nādi [(na)ādi] amn Which begins with the letter 'na'.
nādiphānta [phānta] amn Which begins with the letter 'na' and ends with the letter 'pha'.
nādiphāntakrama | krama | m. phil. | Tantra | enumeration of the letters of the alphabet, with their imposition in 49 points of the body by nyāsa , invoking the goddess Mālinī₂.
nādita [pp. ca. nad] amnf nāditā that one makes ring — ifc. resonating with (iic.) — n. sound, noise.
nādin [agt. nad] amnf nādinī That which rings, That which resounds; That which cries out, That which howls; That which trumpets.
nādeyá [*nadīeya] amnf nādeyī [“Belonging to the river” | fluvial, aquatic — m. bio. bot. Saccharum spontaneum, reed, sugar cane | river fish; opp. sāmudra₁.

Nānaka m. hist. np. of Guru Nānaka, 1st Guru of the Sikhs: born in 1469 in a village in Pañjāb, son of a civil servant, he became a mystic and founded in Kartarpur the community of Sikhs, neither Hindu nor Muslim; he died in 1539, after declaring his disciple Lehna as his successor under the name of Guru Angād; his birthday is celebrated in kārttikapūrnimā.
nānā adv. diversely | separately, distinctly (of (abl. i.)); otherwise than — iic. varied, diverse, of all kinds.
nānārūpa [rūpa] amnf nānārūpā multiforme — m. different forms.

nānārūpadhara | dhara | amnf nānārūpadharā Who assumes multiple forms. 5( antah śāktāh bahih śaivāh sabhāyām vaisnavāh matāh nānārūpadharāh kaulāh vicaranti mahītale Above all, faithful to the Goddess, outwardly Shaivite, collectively following Vishnuite rites, in multiple forms the Tantric adepts circulate on Earth.
nānārtha | artha | amnf nānārthā gram. Which has another purpose or object or meaning; polysemous — m. gram. homonymous.
nānārthavarga | varga | m. lit. section of the Sāmānyakāṇḍa, dealing with homonyms.
Nānārthaśabdakośa [śabdakośa] m. lit. np. from the dictionary of homonyms Nānārthaśabdakośa, due to Medhinīkara, also called Medinīkośa.
nānārthasaṃgraha [saṃgraha] m. bed. n.p. from the glossary nānārthasamgraha of Ajayapāla.
nānārthārṇavasaṃkṣepa [arṇavasaṃkṣepa] lit. np. from the dictionary of homonyms m. Nānārthārnavasamskepa de Keśavasvāmī, en 5801 vers.
nānārthodayasāgarakoṣa [udayasāgarakoṣa] m. bed. n.p. from the dictionary of homonyms Nānārthodayasāgarakosa due to Ghāsīlālajī Mahārāja (1988).
nānāvidha [vidha] amnf nānāvidhā of various kinds; multiform, varied.
nānāndra [*nanāndr̩] m. son of a sister of her husband — f. nānāndrī daughter of a sister of her husband.

nāndī [nand] f. joy, satisfaction, pleasure | soc. praise of a deity; not. recitation of a propitiatory stanza calling for the grace of a deity upon the audience, at the beginning of a theatrical performance.
nāndīmukha [mukha] amnf nāndīmukhī smiling, radiant | pl. nāndīmukhās soc. manes [pitaras] To Whom a śrāddha is offered.

nāpitá m. barber — f. nāpitī wife of the barber. nṛpanāpitaputranyāya | "saying of the king and the barber's son"] everyone sees noon at their own door, like this barber Whom the king had asked to bring him a pretty boy, and Who returned with his own hideous son.
nāpitáśālā [śālā] f. barbershop.
nābha ifc. nābhi.
nābhāga m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā nābhāga, son of Yayāti₁, father of Aja.

nābhi mf navel; umbilical cord | hub of a wheel, center; apex of a conch | myth. [BhP.] np. of nābhi, son of King Agnīdhra; through his devotion to Vishnu, he obtained that the latter be incarnated )9 as his son Rṣabha₂, the best of devotees — m. nābha ifc. whose navel is (iic.) || lat. umbi licus; ang. navel; all. Nabel; fr. nombril.
nābhikṛntana [kṛntana] n. cutting of the umbilical cord; syn. nābhivardhana.
nābhigandha [gandha] m. musk odor. surabhitasilam nābhigandhair mṛgāṇām |MD.| whose deer perfume the rocks with their musk.
nābhijanman [janman] m. ["from the navel (of Viṣṇu)"] epith. of Brahmā.
nābhidaghna [daghna] amnf nābhidaghnā f. nābhidaghnī who has (water) up to her navel.
nābhimūla [mūla] n. part of the body under the Name bril (euphemism for sexual parts).
nābhivardhana [vardhana] n. cutting of the umbilical cord; syn. nābhikṛntana.
nāma₁ [nāman] prep. cl. certainly, indeed, of course; in truth, certainly, of course | yet,
nāma₁ iic. nāman.

nevertheless | of Name (iic.) | (interr.) I beg you. kim nāma₁ what then? katham nāma₁ how then! api nāma₁ perhaps; Provided that, would to heaven that opt. mā nāma₁ Provided that ... not .... mayā nāma₁ jitam [Vi.] Truly I have conquered. apy eṣa nāma₁ phalam icchati [MK.] Perhaps this man wants a reward. api nāmaivam syāt If only it were so. mā nāma₁ akāryaṃ kuryāt Provided that he does no wrong.
nāmaka [ka] amnf nāmikā named — ifc. of Name (iic.).
nāmakaraṇa [karaṇa] n. soc. naming rite of a child on its 10th day, a samskāra | soc. bestowing of the secret Name of a newborn son during the jātakarman. nāmakaraṇam kṛ perform the naming rite.

Nāmadeva [Deva] m. hist. n.p. of Nāmadeva "Master of (God's) Name", Maratha tailor-poet (1275–1350), worshiper of Vitthala [Haridāsa]; tradition says that he accompanied Jñānadeva on his tour of India, and settled at Pandharpur; he perfected continuous devotional poetry [abhanga].
nāmadhātu [dhātu] m. gram. denominative verb. nāmadhātuprakriyā gram. use of a denominative verb.
nāmadheya [dheya] n. appellation, Name; title |soc. ceremony to give one's Name to a child — ifc. who has for Name (iic.). pātaliputranāmadheyam nagaram a city called Pāṭaliputra.
nāmapada [pada] n. gram. | "action word" | verb, verbal form; syn. subanta.
Nāmamālā [mālā] f. lit. lexicon; not. np. of the Nāmamālā "Garland of Words", lexicon due to Dhanañjaya₁.
nāmamālikā [mālikā] f. lit. np. from the small lexicon of synonyms nāmamālikā of Bhoja, also called Bhojanighantu.
nāmarūpa | rūpa | n. du. phil. the Name and the form, the (illusory) individuality | bd. the illusion of existing as an individual, the 4th cause of suffering |pratītyasamutpāda|.
nāmalinga [linga] n. gram. kind of a Noun.

Nāmalingānuśāsana [anuśāsana] n. lit. np. of the Nāmalingānuśāsana "Teaching of the gender of names", lexicon of Amarasimha also called Amarakosa; it comprises 3 chapters [Trikāṇḍaśeṣa]: Svargādikāṇḍa, Bhūmyādikāṇḍa and Sāmānyakānda.
nāmastotra | stotra | n. litany of names (of a deity or saint).
nāmārtha [artha] m. gram. meaning of a word.
nāmāvali [āvali] f. litany of names (not. of the 108 names) of a deity | dictionary.

nāman [jnā₁man] n. [sg. Nom. acc. nāma₁] characteristic mark, form | Name, appellation; Personal proper name (opp. gotra) | soc. imposition of a religious name (not. dāsa in the devotional [bhakti] current of the Vaishnava tradition) gram. noun — acc. nāma₁ prep. ifc. cf. nāma₁ — mf nāmnī ifc. named, of Name (iic.) — i. nāmnā prep. of Name (iic. g.) | (interr.) I beg you, please | lat. nomen; ang. name; all. name; fr. Nom. nāmatas adv. namingly. nāmataḥ kṛ to name, to call someone. by his Name (2) acc. nāmatah praś to inquire about someone's Name. acc. . nāma₁ grah to mention the Name of. mama nāma₁ devadattah my name is Devadatta. devadatto nāma₁ puruṣaḥ a man named Deva datta. devadattanāmā puruṣaḥ the man whose name is De vadatta. kādambarīnāmnī kanyakā a young girl named Kādambarī. viṣṇuśarmānāma paṇḍitaḥ The scholar Viṣṇuśarmā. .0 bhagavatah nāmni pūjām karomi I celebrate the homage in honor of God.
nāmika [nāmanika] amnf nāmikā relating to the noun.
nāy [ca. nī₁] v. [10] pr. (nāyayati) to cause to lead, to cause to drive — ps. (nāyyate) to be caused to drive.
nāya |agt. nī₁| m. guide; chief — act. m. political.

Nāyaka |agt. nī₁| amnf nāyikā Who leads, Who guides — m. chief, captain, leader | hist. not. military leader of the Andhra country; cf. Kāpaya; after the conquest of Ekasilā by the Sul tanat of Bahmani, the nāyakās founded the Vijayanagara empire; the Nāyaka dynasty replaced the Colās in Thanjavur around 1532 | hist. cf. Bhattanāyaka | hero, leading man (first male role in a drama) | central jewel (of a necklace) — f. nāyikā noble lady | theatrical heroine, leading lady; not. abhisārikā | courtesan. nāyikānāyakabhāvah behavior of lovers.
nārá [*nara] amnf nārī relating to Man, human; mortal — f. nārī woman, wife; female being.
nāranga m. oranger || pt. naranja; fr. orange.

Nārada [*naradā₂] m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Nārada "Who divides men", progenitor |prajāpati| son of Brahmā; on his refusal to procreate, his father condemned him to live a dissolute life of 100,000 years as a gandharva before being reborn as the son of a servant; a young adolescent of great beauty, perfect worshipper of the Divine, master of yoga, he is messenger of the gods, celestial musician and patron of bards; he invented the vīṇā (cf. Mahatī); it is an oracle, which informs men of their destiny; he notably informed Kamsa that he would be killed by a son of his cousin Devakī; His curse of Sāmba caused the death of Kṛṣṇa and the extinction of the yādavās; he is talkative, and provokes quarrels by his indiscretions; he is said to be fond of quarrels [kalahapriya], or even [Bālarāmāyaṇa] fond of fights [kalahakutūhalin]; the esoteric lesson [upaniṣad] Nāradaparivrājakā, the Nāradapurāņa, and other works are attributed to him; [MP.] he entrusted to Vișnu the secret of his Māyā; the latter told him to plunge into a basin, where he became Suśīlā₂; [BhP.] Curious to know how Krishna could satisfy his 1008 wives, he visited them all, and at each one found Krishna — f. nāradī myth. np. of nāradī, Narada transformed into a woman by Vishnu for boasting of his celibacy; she made a king fall in love with her, who married her and bore her sixty sons, who name the years of a life cycle; cf. samvatsara. nāradāya rocate kalahaḥ Quarrel pleases Narada.
nāradajayantī [jayantī] f. soc. Nārada festival, the 1st day of the dark fortnight of the vaiśākha month.
nāradapañcarātra [pañcarātra] n. bed. n.p. from the nāradapañcarātra, collection of Vaisnava ritual.
Nāradaparivrājakā | parivrājaka | f. lit. np. of the esoteric lesson | upaniṣad | Nāradaparivrājakā, at tribuée à Nārada.
nāradapurāna [purāna] n. lit. np. from the nāradapurāṇa, mythological collection of Vaishnava obedience; cf. sāttvika.
Nāradasmṛti [smṛti] f. lit. np. of the Nāradasmṛti, detailed law text, later than the Manusmrti.
nārasiṃha [*narasiṃha] amnf nārasimhā myth. relating to Narasimha — m. astr. np. of the 6th cosmological cycle [kalpa] | myth. Vișnu as Narasimha.
nārāca m. iron arrow; arrow in gen. — f. nārācī goldsmith's balance.
nārācadurdina [durdina] n. rain of arrows.

nārāyaṇá [nāraāyana₁] amnf nārāyaṇī phil. in Whom men find Refuge | myth. np. of Nārāyaṇa "Refuge of men", ancient water divinity, twin brother (or son) of nara; the nymph [apsaras] Urvaśī was born from a flower placed on his thigh | myth. Viṣṇu sleeping on the primordial waters between two eras, resting on the coils of the serpent SeșaAnanta; the creation of the world came from his navel, from which a lotus bearing Brahmā rises (cf. Anantaśāyin, Aravin danābhi, Jalaśayana, Padmanābha); it represents the awakening of the Divine Manifestation | phil. God in Man; by invoking it one can worship God in human form, not. Krishna | lit. the hymn to the Puruṣa [puruṣasūkta] (attributed to Narayana) | hist. patr. of Narayana₁, 12th century Bengali writer, compiler of the Hitopadesa | hist. np. of Narayana₂ Paṇḍita, 14th century mathematician; he is the author of the Ganitakaumudī | hist. patr. of Narayana₃ Bhatta, 16th-17th century grammarian from Melputtur in Kerala; He is the author of the Prakriyāsarvasva, the Dhātukāvya, and the Apāṇinīyapramāṇatā; he is also the author of the Nārāyaṇīya, a poem sung to this day, the Rājasūyacampū, the Srīpādasaptati, and the Dūtakāvya | hist. np. of Nārāyaṇa₄ Paṇḍita, author of the Vivarana₁ commentary (late 16th century) | hist. np. of Nārāyaṇa₅ Sāstrī (17th century), author of the Nārāyaṇīya₁ commentary of the Pradīpa | hist. np. of the devotional poet Bhatta Nārāyaṇa₆, author of the stotra Stavacintāmaņi (late 9th century) | hist. cf. Svāminārāyaṇa | pl. nārāyaṇās myth. [Mah.] cowherds soldiers of the troop | arbuda | of Kṛṣṇa, whom he incited to fight on the side of Duryodhana, Arjuna having preferred the presence of neutral Kṛṣṇa at his side; they fought Arjuna fiercely but all perished in the great war excl. soc. said while yawning (so that the soul does not escape) — f. Nārāyaṇī myth. np. of Nārāyaṇī epith. of Durgā or Lakṣmī "In Whom men take refuge". nārāyaṇam namaskṛtya | naram caiva narottamam | devīm sarasvatīm caiva | tato jayamudīrayet || (in vocation before the recitation of the Mah.) having honored Nārāyaṇa, Nara, Narottama, and the goddess Sarasvatī, let the song of victory now be proclaimed.
Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha |kaṇṭha| mr. hist. n.p. of the Kaśmīra philosopher Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha (10th century); he made a commentary on the Mrgendratantra.

nārāyaṇasvāmin [svāmin] m. geo. np. of the temple of Nārāyaṇasvāmī of the fort of Melukoṭe, established on Mount Yādavācala 40 km northeast of mod. Mysore in Karņāṭaka, of obedience pāñcarātra; the cult of Celuva or Sampatkumāra "(Viṣṇu) young and beautiful" is celebrated there; it is also called Celu vanārāyaṇa Svāmī and Tirunārāyaṇa; the site of the fort contains many other Vaishnava temples.

Nārāyaṇīya |īya| amnf nārāyaṇīyā concerning Nārāyaṇa — n. lit. np. of the Nārāyaṇīya, a sung poem by Bhatta Nārāyaṇa₃, which summarizes the Bhāgavatapurāṇa | gram. np. of the Nārāyaṇīya₁, commentary on the Pradīpa by Nārāyaṇa₅ Sāstrī (17th century) | lit. np. of the Nārāyaṇīya₂, portion of the 12th book of the Mah..
Nārikela var. nārīkela [related to nālikera] m. coconut tree; coconut | var. nārikera id. — f. nārikelī coconut | var. nārikerī id.

nārikeladvīpa [dvīpa] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the marvelous island of Nārikela "Coconut Island", where four divine beings reside: Rūpasiddhi who can change his appearance, Pramāṇasiddhi who can measure all things, Jñānasiddhi who knows the past, present and future, and Devasiddhi who can invoke divine powers; they took Naravāhanadatta to Švetadvīpa to meet Hari, who granted him four apsarasas as wives.
nārikelapāka [pāka] n. lit. poetry difficult to understand (like coconut pulp is difficult to access); opp. drāksāpāka, kadalīpāka.

nārikelaphala [phala] n. coconut. antah kaulo bahih śaivo lokācāre tu vaidikah sāram ādāya tiṣṭheta nārikelaphalam yathā || Inwardly tantric, outwardly Shaivite, behaving in life like a brahmin res pectuate of the Veda, he keeps the essential within himself, in the manner of a coconut.
nārī cf. nāra.
nārīkavaca | kavaca | m. myth. np. of nārīkavaca, epith. of king Mūlaka "having women like a cream".

nārīdūṣaṇa |dūṣaṇa| n. soc. female vice; there are six of them: drinking alcohol, keeping bad company, leaving one's husband, loitering outside the home, spending the night at a stranger's house and residing there.
nārpatya [*nṛpatiya] n. state of king.
nāla [*nala] amnf nālī made of reeds — m. tube, pipe; vein — n. ifc. stem; handle — f. nālī pipe, conduit; vein, vessel; enema.

nālaka [nālaka] amnf nālikā ifc. stem of (plant); tube of (iic.) — f. nālikā lit. rhet. insinuation, innuendo | soc. [nātya] riddle [prahelikā] humorous used by the vidūṣaka of the rant the comic trilogue |trigata| | period of 24 minutes; syn. nādikā.

Nālandā f. geo. np. of the city of Nālandā, site of a Buddhist University 90 km south of Pāṭaliputra (mod. ruins near the village of Bar gaon south of Paṭnā in Bihāra), founded in 427; it was an important cultural and scientific center for 7 centuries; Samantabhadra was its abbot in the 11th century; it was destroyed by the Turk Bakhtiyar Khilji around 1193.
Nālāgiri [nālagiri] m. bd. np. of Nālāgiri, furious elephant sent by the traitor Devadatta against his cousin the Buddha; the latter appeased the ani mal, who knelt at his voice.
nālika amnf nālikā describes a posture
seated [āsana] — ifc. period of 24 minutes.
nālikera m. coconut tree; coconut | var. nālikela id.
upalabhagnanālikerarasasnigdhasilātalam [K.] greasy stone slabs from the juice of coconuts broken on the millstone.
nālī [nādī] f. vessel of the body; vein, artery — ifc. period of 24 minutes; syn. nālika.

nālījaigha [jaighā] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of the old Nālījangha, faithful servant of Vasumdharā; he saved Bhāskaravarmā from the cruel Mitravarmā, but fell into a well to make him drink; he was saved from it by Viśruta.
nāvika [nau₁ika] amnf nāvikī relating to the boat | boatman; navigator, captain.
nāvya [nau₁ya] amnf nāvyā navigable — f. nāvyā navigable river.
nāś [ca. naś₁] v. [10] pr. (nāśayati) pp. (nāśita) to cause to perish, to destroy; to turn away from (abl.); to forget; to renounce (acc.).
nāsa [act. nas₁] m. loss, ruin, destruction, annihilation. cittanāśaḥ phil. [yoga] cessation of mental activity.
nāśaka [agt. naś₁] amnf nāśikā that destroys, that eliminates (g. iic.) | that wastes.
nāśana [agt. naś₁] amnf nāśanī that destroys — act. n. annihilation, ruin, destruction, loss.
nāśita [pp. nāś] amnf nāśitā destroyed, ruined, lost | excluded — m. soc. outcaste.
nāśin [agt. naś₁] amnf nāśinī perishable — ifc. that destroys, that removes (iic.).
nāsat |naasat| ind. the non-existent | "did not exist"|.
nāsadīya [īya] n. [nāsadīyasūkta] lit. [RV.] np. from nāsadīyasūkta, Hymn of creation.

nāsatya amnf nāsatyā helpful, friendly — m. du. ved. np. of Nāsatyau "the two Friends", formula designating the Aśvinau — m. myth. (lately) np. of nāsatya "the Friend", one of the Aśvinau, distinguished from his twin Dasra.
nāsā [nas₂] f. nose, nostril | of. ved. id. —ifc. cf. nasa | lat. nāsus; eng. nose; all. Nase; fr. nose.
nāsāgra | agra | n. tip of the nose.

nāsāgradṛṣṭi [dṛṣṭi] f. phil. [yoga] "fixation of the tip of the nose", yogic eye concentration — amnf in eye concentration. nāsāgradṛṣṭir ekākī prāṇayāmaṃ samabhyaset [GS.] with one's gaze directed towards the tip of the nose, one must practice breath control in solitude.

nāsika [*nas₂ika] mn geo. np. of nāsika, sacred city on the Godāvarī, center of pilgrimage, not. of kumbhamela (mod. Nāsik or Nāsik, north of the Mahārāṣṭra); myth. [Rām.] its name comes from the fact that it was here that Lakshmana is said to have cut off the nose of the rākṣasī Śūrpaṇakhā; cf. Tryambakeśvara — f. cf. nāsikā.
nāsikā [f. nāsika] f. nostril, nose.
nāsikāgra [agra] n. tip of the nose.
nāsti [naasti] ind. there is not.
nāstitā [tā] f. non-existence.
nāstitva [tva] n. non-existence.
nāstika [naāstika] amnf nāstikī atheist, unbeliever | phil. qualifies nihilistic doctrines; a distinction is made between skeptics [ādhyakṣika] and rationalists
lists | tārkika | | phil. non-orthodox sectarian not recognizing the authority of the Veda; the nāstikās include atheist materialists (cārvākās, bārhaspatyās), Jains and Buddhists.
nāstikatā [tā] f. atheism.
nāstikatva [tva] n. atheism.
nāha [act. nah] m. act of attaching, of binding.
nāhuṣa [*Nahuṣa] m. myth. n.p. of nāhuṣa "(son of) Nahuṣa", patr. of King Yayāti.
nor pf. inside, below, under | lack of, devoid of, cessation of.
neither variant nor form of the sm
niḥkṣatra [niskṣatra] amnf niḥkṣatrā not having a military caste.
niḥśaṅka [nisśaṅkā] amnf niḥśaṅkā fearless; intrepid | risk-free, safe — ifc. who is not afraid of (iic.) — f. niḥśaṅkā absence of hesitation. niḥśankam adv. safe; without fear.
niḥśabda [nisśabda] amnf niḥśabdā silent; quiet — mn silence. nihśabdam silently. niḥśabdam kṛ not to make a noise.
niḥśītam [nissītā] adv. with cessation of the cold.
niḥśeṣa [nisśeṣa] amnf niḥśeṣā without remainder; finished | complete, whole, all. niḥśeṣam var. niḥśeṣeṇa completely, in total. nihśesam kr to destroy completely.
niḥśeṣita [nisśeṣita] amnf niḥśeṣitā which has nothing left; completely consumed, finished or destroyed.
niḥśrīka [nisśrīka] amnf niḥśrīkā ugly unfortunate.

niḥśreyasa [nisśreyasa] amnf niḥśreyasī unsurpassed; excellent, best — n. the best; beatitude; felicity | phil. attainment of the supreme good, ultimate personal goal; emancipation, personal fulfillment, faith; salvation.
niḥśvas [nisśvas₁] v. [2] pr. (niḥśvásiti) pp. (niḥśvásita) pf. (vi) to breathe in; to sniff; to sigh.
niḥśvásita [pp. niḥśvas] amnf nihśvasitā aspirated, inspired — n. expiration; sigh.
niḥśvasya [abs. niḥśvas] ind. having sighed.
niḥśvāsa [act. niḥśvas] m. expiry; sou pir — f. nihśvāsā ifc. id.
niḥśvāsāndha | andha | amnf niḥśvāsāndhā made opaque by (the mist of) breathing (mi roir).
niḥsaṃkhya [nissaṃkhyā₂] amnf nihsamkhyā gram. devoid of number.
niḥsaṅga [nissaṅga] amnf niḥsaṅgā disinterested.
niḥsaṃjña [nissaṃjñā₂] amnf
niḥsamjñā ["who no longer knows himself"] unconscious, outside of himself.

niḥsattva [nissattva] amnf niḥsattvā non-existent, non-substantial | without energy, weak; infirm, miserable | devoid of inhabitants | insignificant, bad — n. lack of energy; insignificance; non-existence.
niḥsattvatā [tā] f. lack of energy, weakness.
niḥsattvatva [tva] n. non-existence.
niḥsara [niḥsṛ] amnf niḥsarā which comes out.
niḥsaraṇa [niḥsarana] n. exit, evacuation; departure — ifc. means of getting rid of (iic.). āhāraniḥsaraṇamārga anus.
niḥsārita [pp. ca. niḥsṛ] amnf niḥsāritā evacuated, sent away.
niḥsṛ [nissṛ] v. [1] pr. (niḥsarati) pp. (niḥsṛta) to go out, to withdraw from, to flow out of — ca. (niḥsārayati) pp. (niḥsārita) to bring out, to evacuate (from (abl.)) | to conclude.
niḥṣṛta [pp. niḥṣṛ] amnf niḥṣṛtā exited, gone (out of (iic. abl.)) | bulging (eye).
niḥsneha [nissneha] amnf niḥsnehā not greasy, not unctuous, not oily; dry | not affective, insensitive, cold; indifferent | unloved; lacking affection, ignored; hated.
niḥsnehatva [tva] n. state of being dry | lack of affection.
niḥspanda var. niṣpanda [nisspanda] amnf nispandā immobile.
nihspandatva [tva] n. immobility.
niḥspṛha [nisspṛhā] amnf niḥspṛhā free from desires, indifferent, detached.
niḥsphur [nissphur] v. [6] pr. (niḥsphurati) v. [6] pr. (niḥsphurati) to throw far away.
niḥsvana [nissvana] amnf niḥsvanā silent — ifc. noise emitted by (iic.).
niḥsvabhāva [nissvabhāva] amnf niḥsvabhāvā devoid of its own nature.
niḥsvādu [nissvādu] amnf niḥsvanā tasteless, without taste.
nikaṭa [nikaṭa] amnf nikaṭā near, close to (g.) — mn proximity. nikațe adv. near. nikaţāt adv. far from. nikaṭībhū to approach.
nikam [nikam] pft. (nicakame) to desire, to covet.
nikara [nikara₂] m. heap; pile; collection; large quantity; multitude | substantial fee, gift | treasure; not. Kubera's treasure | var. nikāra the act of heaping or winnowing grain.
nikarsa [act. nikṛṣ] m. lowering; reduction; decrease.
nikarṣaṇa [act. nikṛṣ] n. surroundings of a village; courtyard at the entrance of a dwelling; neighborhood.
nikaṣ [nikaṣ] v. [1] pr. (nikaṣati) pp. (nikașita) to rub, to scratch — pr. r. (nikașate) to rub oneself.

nikaṣa [act. nikaṣ] m. act of rubbing, of anointing touchstone — n. trace of gold on the touchstone — f. nikaṣā myth. [Rām.] np. of the rākṣasī nikaṣā, mother of Rāvaṇa; cf. Kaikasī — v. |11| pr. r. (nikaṣāyate) to serve as a touchstone; to serve as a test. nikaṣāyamāṇa amn (pprm.) that establishes the stan dard, that defines the norm — ifc. that serves as a test to (iic.).
nikaṣaṇa [act. nikaṣ] n. erasing, polishing.
nikaṣā [related to nikaṣ] adv. near (acc.); in the middle, between.
nikāmá [act. nikam ] m. desire; covetousness. nikāmam adv. according to one's pleasure, at one's own will; at will | excessively.
nikāya [nikāya] m. heap, mass, accumulation; group, association, brotherhood | bd. congregation, school | pl. lit. the 5 lists of precepts [sūtra] (bd. pāli canon) | house, residence; funeral pyre.

Nikumbha [nikumbha] m. myth. [HV.] np. of Nikumbha, a member of the gaṇa, sent by Śiva to Vārāṇasī to provoke Divodāsa; he granted all wishes, except Divodāsa's wish to have a son; the latter wanted to expel him, but Nikumbha₁ mau said the city for 2000 years, so that Shiva could benefit from it | lit. [Rām.] np. of the rākṣasa Nikumbha₁, son of Kumbhakarna.
nikumbhilā [nikumbhila] f. myth. |Rām.| np. of the nikumbhilā grove, at the western gate of Lankā, place of sacrificial rites of the rākṣasās.
nikṛ [nikṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (nikaróti) pp. (nikṛta) to lower, to humiliate; to dominate, to conquer.
nikṛt var. niṣkṛt [nikṛt₁] v. [6] pr. (nikṛntati) pr. r. (nikṛntate) pp. (nikṛtta) to cut, slice, re-cut, divide. nakhāni nikṛntate he cuts his nails.
nikṛta [pp. nikṛ ] amnf nikṛtā humiliated, offended, insulted; deceived | base, vile, wicked — n. humiliation.
Nikṛti [act. nikṛ] amnf dishonest, disloyal — f. baseness, vileness, disloyalty | myth. np. of Nikṛti "Deception", daughter of Adharma.
nikṛtta [pp. nikṛt] amnf nikṛttā cut, recut, hewn.
nikṛntana [act. nikṛt] n. act of cutting (hair, nails, head) | destruction of enemies | instrument for cutting — f. nikṛntanā ifc. that cuts, that destroys (iic.).

nikṛṣ [nikṛṣ] v. [6] pr. (nikṛṣati) pp. (nikṛṣṭa) pf. (sam) to pull down, to withdraw — ps. (nikṛṣyate) to be carried away by the current of a river. নিক্ষ nikṛṣṭa [pp. nikṛṣ] amnf nikṛṣṭā lowered, degraded; debased, despised; outcast.
niketa | niketa | mn dwelling, house.
niketana [niketana] n. dwelling, house.
niktá [pp. nij] amnf niktā washed, cleaned, purified | clean, pure.

nikṣip [nikṣip] v. [6] pr. (nikṣipati) pp. (nikṣipta) to throw, overturn; to discard, abandon, repudiate; to throw into, pour into | to entrust, deposit, stipulate; to impute (acc.) to (loc.). haste nikṣip to entrust (task) (to (loc.)). ayam janah kasya haste niksiptah into whose care this person has been entrusted. kasmin doṣam nikṣipāmi to whom should I impute the fault?
nikṣepa [act. nikṣip] m. deposit; consignment abandonment jn. aspect of reality: four are distinguished: nāman the name, sthāpanā the representation, dravya₁ the substance, and bhāva existence.
nikṣepavāda |vāda| m. jn. doctrine of renunciation of the oneness of reality; syn. nyāsavāda.
nikhan [nikhan] v. [1] pr. (nikhanati) pp. (nikhāta) to bury, to sink.
nikharva [nikharva] n. math. one hundred billion.

nikhila [nikhila] amnf nikhilā complete, whole, complete. nikhilena adv. completely, totally. নিমতত nigantha m. hist. n.p. of nigantha Nātaputta, name of Mahāvīra₁ in comic literature. in Pāli | (ext.) jaïne.

nigad [nigad] v. [1] pr. (nigadati) pp. (ni gadita) pf. (pra) to recite, proclaim, announce, declare; to say something to someone. (2 acc.) — ps. (Niga dyate) to be called, to be named — ca. (nigadayati) to make recite — intens. r. (nijāgadyate) to declare forcefully or repeatedly.
nigadá [act. nigad] m. audible recitation, not. of a ritual formula | mention | speech.
nigadana [act. nigad] n. recitation from memory.
nigadita [pp. nigad] amnf nigaditā recited; pronounced, mentioned.
nigam [nigam] v. [1] pr. (nigacchati) pp. (ni gata) to go near, to go towards (acc. loc.) | to reach such a state — ca. (nigamayati) to conclude, to deduce; to derive.

nigama [instr. nigam] m. tradition, doctrine; knowledge; certainty | passage from the Veda; sacred tradition; revered words | lit. Shaivite tantra (in the form of a dialogue where Shakti answers questions from Shiva); opp. āgama | gram. root; ifc. derived from (2nd century) | phil. [Nyāya] conclusion of a syllogism | access, road; trade, market, town; caravan of merchants.
nigamajñāna [jñāna] m. hist. np. of Niga majñāna₁, philosopher of the 16th century, who propagated the śaivasiddhānta doctrine | hist. np. of Niga majñāna₂, nephew and disciple of the former.
nigamana [act. nigam] n. deduction; logical conclusion | phil. [Nyāya] conclusion of the syllogism [pañcāvayava]; it is a repetition of the

thesis [pratijñā₂], confirming it. pakṣe sādhyasya abādhitatvapratipādakavacanam nigamanam phil. [Padakṛtya] The conclusion ex primes the explanation of the coherence of the predicate with the subject.
nigaraṇa [act. nigṛ] n. act of swallowing, of eating — m. throat.
niguh [niguh] v. [1] pr. (nigūhati) pp. (nigūdha) to cover, hide, conceal — ca. .5 (nigūhayati) to hide, conceal; to keep secret.
nigūḍha [pp. niguh] amnf nigūḍhā hidden, concealed; secret | obscure, esoteric. nigūdham in secret.
nigūdhārtha | artha| amnf nigūdhārthā in the hidden or mysterious sense; occult | lit. refers to esoteric texts |Tantra| which are read allegorically.
nigṛhīta [pp. nigrah] amnf nigṛhītā phon. contracted || pali niggahīta.
nigṛ [nigṛ₁] v. [6] pr. (nigirati) to swallow, to gitter, to gulp down — ca. (nigārayati) ca. (nigālayati) to make swallow — intens. r. (nijegilyate) to gorge oneself.
nigrah [nigrah] v. [9] pr. (nigṛḥṇāti) pr. r. (nigṛḥṇīté) pp. (nigṛḥīta) pf. (sam) to restrain, res to restrain; to restrain, to repress, to constrain; to stop. krodham nigṛhāṇa restrain your anger.

nigraha [act. nigrah] m. restriction, repression, punishment; opp. anugraha | coercion, constraint; subjugation | phil. [Tantra] possession by a yogini | defeat, rout, destruction, arrest, capture, immobilization | med. cure, healing of an illness | confinement, imprisonment
nement | reprimand, blame | aversion, disgust | phil. [Nyāya] fault of reasoning; refutation | handle; grasping device — f. nigrahā ifc. id. || pali niggaha.
nigrahasthāna [sthāna] n. phil. [Nyāya] rhet. im possibility of argumentation by disagreement on basic principles; stumbling block | defeat, situation of failure of an opponent in a debate.
nigrahaṇa [agt. nigraha] amnf nigrahaṇī ifc. that which restrains, that which suppresses — act. n. constraint; retention, repression, suppression | capture; punishment tion, imprisonment.
nigrāha [act. nigrah] m. repression; suppression; punishment | var. nigrābhá ved. act of lowering the ritual spoon.
nighanta m. gram. lexicon; vocabulary.

Nighanțu [related to Nighanța] m. lit. glossary lit. np. of the Nighanțu, an ancient glossary of Vedic words arranged by synonyms; it comprises 3 sections [khanda]: the Naighantuka (synonyms), the Naigama (homonyms) and the Daivata (names of deities); Yāska made the commentary on it Nirukta pl. nighantavah id. samāmnāyaḥ samāmnātaḥ tam imam samāmnāyam nighantavah iti ācakṣate [Aupamanyava] Any catalogue listing the vocabulary of sacred texts is called a nighanṭavaḥ.
nighaṇṭuratnākara [ratnākara] m. lit. np. from the Nighanturatnākara "Lexical Mine", work
medical | Ayurveda| late.
nighantuśesa [śesa] m. lit. np. from the Nighantuśesa "Supplement to the Nighantu", dictionary of botanical terms due to Hemacandra.
nigharṣa [act. nighṛṣ] m. erasure, scraping; grinding.

nighṛṣva [nighṛṣva] m. ["which crushes"] hoof — n. hoof print. নিম্ন Nighna [agt. nihan] m. myth. n.p. of king Nighna "Killer", father of Satrājit and Prasena.

nicaya [nicaya] m. heap; pile; quantity, multitude; reservoir | provisions; collection; assembly. pravaranarapatimukuṭamaṇimarīcinicayarañjitacaraṇayugalaḥ lit. [PT.] His feet were illuminated by the multitude of rays emitted by the jewels adorning the diadems of the greatest kings.
nicula m. bio. bot. Calamus rotang, reed used for rattan. sthānāt asmāt sarasaniculāt utpata [MG.] leaves this place covered with reeds full of sap.
nicṛt₁ [nicṛt] v. [6] pr. (nicṛt₁áti) pp. (nicṛtta) insert; untie.
nicrt₂ [act. nicrt₁] f. gram. defective meter. nicrdgāyatrī lit. adaptation of the gāyatrī not respecting its meter.

√ nij v. [2] pr. r. (ninkte) v. [3] pr. (nénekti) pr. r. (nenikté) pp. (niktá) to wash, clean; to wash oneself, to purify oneself — ps. (nijyate) to be cleaned — ca. (ne jayati) to have cleaned — intens. (nénijīti) to clean thoroughly — des. (nenikṣati) to want to clean.

nijá [nija] amnf nijā innate; his own, own; native | of the same country, fellow citizen; of the same party; relative. nijoripuh traitor in his own camp. nijam dhairyamadarśayat he showed his courage.
nitamba m. (erotic) pelvis, hips, buttocks (of the woman).
nitambinī [in] f. pretty woman [“who has a pretty butt”], callipyge; syn. suśronī.
nitarām [nitarām] adv. downwards much, entirely, completely; .6 especially; excessively | in any case, in every way.

nítya [nitya] amnf nityā constant, fixed; invariable, permanent, continuous; essential; perpetual, eternal, indestructible | daily, regular, ordinary; innate; native | necessary; obligatory | soc. (rite) obligatory; opp. kāmya optional gram. a rule A is nitya visàver of a rule B if A is applicable whether B is or is not, but not the reverse; it has precedence over a rule anitya — ifc. constantly engaged in (iic.); devoted to, accustomed to (iic.) — n. inescapable act; necessary rite — f. nityā myth. np. of nityā, epith. of Durgā the Eternal. nityam adv. always, eternally; continually, regularly; every day. na nityam adv. never. śabdo 'nityaḥ phil. [Nyāya] Sound is not eternal. śabdo nityaḥ phil. [Mīmāṃsā] Sound is eternal.

nítyakarman [karman] n. soc. obligatory ritual observance, daily or occasional [naimittika]; it includes the five major rites [mahāyajña] | lit. np. of the Nityakarmā ritual, which describes the observances of the brahmin, not. the sandhyāvandana.
nityagrantha | grantha | m. lit. np. from the Nityagran tha, a text regulating the rites of purification, worship and meditation, attributed to Rāmānuja.
nítyatā [tā] f. perpetuity, eternity | eternal return of (iic.).
nítyatṛpta |tṛpta| amnf nityatṛptā eternally satisfied.
nítyatva |tva| n. perpetuity, eternity.
nítyadā [dā] adv. eternally, perpetually; always, constantly.
nityanarta [narta] amnf nityanartā who dances without ceasing — m. myth. epith. of Shiva.
nityaprajalpita [prajalpita] amnf nityaprajal
pitā ["who talks incessantly"] talkative.
nityaprahasita | prahasita | amnf nityapraha sitā who always laughs.
nityabrahmacārin [brahmacārin] amnf nitya brahmacāriņī who does not experience carnal desire — m. myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa "eternally chaste".
nityamukta [mukta] amnf nityamuktā phil. eternally free.
nityavastu |vastu₁| n. phil. |Vedānta| permanent reality, eternal brahman.
nityavāda | vāda | m. phil. | Vedānta | Eternalism, doctrine of the permanence of reality; it opposes the doctrine of the transience of all
things | kṣaṇikavāda|.
nityavrata [vrata] n. eternal vow (for life).
nityaśabda [śabda] m. gram. ["eternal language"] language as existing from all eternity.
nityaśabdavādin | vādin | m. gram. proponent of the theory affirming the indivisibility of compound words; opp. kāryaśabdavādin.
nityaśas [śas] adv. eternally, in perpetuity.
nityasamāsa [samāsa] m. gram. idiomatic compound, whose meaning is not the composition of the meanings of its constituents; opp. vaikalpikasamāsa.
nityasumangalī [sumangala] f. soc. sacred prostitute [syn. devadāsī] of South India.

Nityānanda₁ [ānanda] m. hist. np. of śrī Nityānanda₁ Prabhu "Eternal Joy", Vaishnava mystic of Bengal [gaudīya], born in 1474, friend and disciple of Caitanya; he is considered in the gaudīya tradition as a reincarnation of Balarāma; his name is shortened to Nitaï, and with CaitanyaNīmāya they form the eternal brother couple Nimaï and Nitaï; Vīrabhadra₂ Prabhu is his son | hist. np. of Nityānanda₁, 17th century mathematician, author of the Sarvasiddhāntarāja and the Siddhāntasindhu.
nityānitya [anitya] n. opposition perma nent/impermanent, eternal/ephemeral.
nityānityavastuviveka [vastu₁viveka] m. phil. [Vedānta] discernment in reality between the permanent and the ephemeral, first of the qualifications of the aspirant to liberation [sādhanacatuṣṭaya].
nityānumeya [anumeya] amnf nityānumeyā phil. ["always (only) inferable"] refers to a hidden Veda, implicit through its presumed influence in revealed texts.
Nityodita [udita₁] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Nityodita, chief of the chamberlains [ityaka] of King Udayana; his son Gomukha₁ became chamberlain and companion of Naravāhanadatta.
nidarśaka [agt. nidṛś] amnf nidarśikā who perceives, who has the intuition of | who announces, who proclaims.

nidarśana [agt. nidṛś] amnf nidarśanī that indicates, that teaches — act. n. aspect, appearance; vision; proof, evidence; example; sign, indication, index, symptom — f. nidarśanā lit. rhet. figure of speech [alaṃkāra] exhibiting an object and its reflection. .7
nidarśita [pp. nidṛś] amnf nidarśitā presented, offered (seat) | given as an example.
nidarśin [agt. nidṛś] amnf nidarśinī who perceives, who has an intuition of; familiar with, knowledgeable, who is suitable for.
nidah [nidah₁] v. [1] pr. (nidahati) pp. (ni dagdha) to burn, to be consumed.
nidā [nidā₂] v. [4] pr. (nidyati) to bind.
nidāghá [agt. nidah] m. heat; heat wave | the hot season, summer (May-June) | sweat, perspiration.
nidāghakāla [kāla₁] m. the hot season, the heat wave.

nidāna [instr. nidā] n. link, cord | cause, origin (not. of a disease); symptom | med. diagnostic; therapeutic; cf. Mādhavanidāna | phil. link between microcosm and macrocosm, effective mantra; cf. bandhu | bd. one of the 12 factors in the chain of causalities or occasions of production of existence | lit. introduction; preliminary statement.
Nidānasthāna [sthāna] n. med. study of the diagnosis; pathology | lit. np. of the Nidānasthāna of Caraka; cf. Carakasamhitā.
nídigdha [nidigdha] amnf nidigdhā soiled; coated; poisoned | filled — f. carda mome.
nidigdhikā [ika] f. organic. bot. Solanum xanthocar pum; syn. kantakārī | cardamom.
nididhyās [d. nidhyā] v. pr. r. (nor didhyāsate) pfp. (nididhyāsitavya) to desire to meditate; meditate carefully. ātmā vā are drastavyah śrotavyo mantavyo ni
didhyāsitavyaḥ [BU.] In truth, faithful one, it is the Self that one must look at, that one must listen to, that one must contemplate, on which one must desire to meditate.
nididhyāsana [act. nididhyās] n. phil. [yoga] intense meditation technique.
nidiś [nidiś₁] v. [6] pr. (nidiśati) to order, to give instructions.
nidṛś [nidṛś₁] ca. (nidarśayati) to show, to point out, to indicate; to advise, to teach; to demonstrate, to announce, to proclaim.

nideśa [obj. nidiś] m. order, command; instruction, directive; explanation | neighborhood. nidese adv. near, close to g. . nidesatas adv. on the order of, according to the instructions of (i.e. g.). nideśam kṛ var. nideśamvṛt, nideśamsthā to carry out the orders, to obey.
nidrā₂ [nidrā₂] v. [1] pr. r. (nidrāyate) to sleep, to sleep.
nidrā₂ [act. nidrā₂] f. sleep, drowsiness | phil. [yoga] loss of attention, a cittavṛtti. nidrām gam to fall asleep.
nidrānāśa | nāśa | mr. med. insomnia.
nidrāmagna [magna] amnf nidrāmagnā pro fundamentally asleep.
nidrāvaśa [vaśa] amnf nidrāvaśā under the influence of sleep.
nidrālú [nidrā₂ālu] amnf asleep; sleepy.
nidrālutva |tva| n. drowsiness.
nidritá [nidrā₂ita] amnf nidritā in slept.
nidritavat [vat] amnf nidritavatī who slept.

nidhána [act. nidhā ] n. receptacle; conclusion sion, end; final | destruction, death; demise | soc. fi nal, 5th part of a sāman song | myth. np. of the rudra Nidhana or Nidhanesa "the Lord who destroys", aspect of Shiva who delivers the soul by destroying the cause and effect of samsāra | lat. offendo.

nidhā [nidhā₁] v. [3] pr. (nidadhāti) pp. (ni hita) abs. (nidhāya) pf. (abhi, pra, prati, sam) to deposit, lay down, place; to place in (loc.); to reserve, hide | to offer, entrust to (dat. loc.) — ps. (nidhīyate) to be contained or absorbed in (loc.). ātmānam nidhā to entrust oneself to (loc.). kriyām nidhā to take pains to (loc.). dṛśaṃ nidhā to fix one's eyes on (loc.). bhūmau nidhā to bury. maulau nidhā to place on the head; to receive with res pect. padam hi sarvatra gunairnidhīyate Merits always confer distinction.
nidhāna [nidhāna] n. receptacle, deposit; reserve, treasure.
nidhāya [abs. nidhā] ind. having deposited. nidhāya manasi having in mind, reflecting on acc. .
nidhi [act. nidhā] m. distribution of food | receptacle | treasure | myth. one of the 9 treasures of Kubera; cf. navanidhi | math. symb. the number 9.
nidhuvana [nidhuvana] n. trembling; agitation | coitus.
nidhuvanayudh [yudh₂] f. ["fight of love"| sexual act; syn. ratikalaha.
nidhyā [nidhyā] v. [1] pr. (nidhyāyati) pp. (nidhyāta) to observe, perceive; to contemplate; .8 to meditate — des. r. (nididhyāsate) to meditate with attention.
ninad [ninad] v. [1] pr. (ninadati) pf. (pra) to rustle, to resound; to shout — ca. (ninādayati) pp. (ninādita) to make resound, to fill with noise or shouts.
nināda [agt. ninad] m. noise; her; cries, go carme.
ninitsu [agt. des. nind] amnf desirous of denigrating or blaming.
ninī sā [act. des. nī₁] f. desire to lead or bring.
ninī su [agt. dés. nī₁] amnf who wants to lead or bring (acc.).

√ nind v. [1] pr. (nindati) pft. (nininda) pp. (nindita) pfp. (nedya) pf. (prati) to blame; reproach; criticize, accuse; denigrate, mock; ridicule | punish; despise, humiliate; curse — des. (nínitsati) to want to denigrate or blame.
nindaka [agt. nind] amnf nindikā who is in the habit of blaming.
nindā [act. nind] f. blame, reproach; censure; controversy, defamation, insult; outrage.
nindāstuti [stuti] f. false praise, ironic praise; irony.
nindita [pp. nind] amnf ninditā blamed; blameworthy, despicable; prohibited, forbidden.

nipat [nipat₁] v. [1] pr. (nipatati) pp. (nipa tita) pf. (upa, pra, vi, sam) to descend, to swoop down, to throw oneself upon; to fall | to land (bird) | to fall, to be lost — ca. (nipātayati) to bring down, to knock down.
nipata [imp. nipat ] ind. fall!
nipatana [act. nipat] n. fall, descent | flight.
nipatita [pp. nipat] amnf nipatitā fallen, descended | degraded, corrupted. nabhonipatita descended from the heavens. dṛṣṭir nipatitā it was noticed, it was observed.
nipalāśam [nipalāśa] adv. as gently as the falling of leaves from trees.
nipā [nipā₁] v. [1] pr. (nipibati) to drink from; to suck; to absorb, to dry.
nipāt [ca. nipat] v. [10] pr. (nipātayati) pp. (nipātita) to bring down, to knock down.
nipāta [act. nipat] m. descent, fall; downfall, ruin; death | act of rushing, attack; overthrow, destruction, murder | gram. irregularity, exception | gram. particle.
nipātana [agt. nipat] amnf nipātanī that overturns, that destroys — act. n. overturning, destruction, murder | fortuitous occurrence | gram. ex ception; fixed expression, idiomatic form.
nipātanasūtra [sūtra] n. gram. rules of grammar specifying set forms and other exceptions.
nipātita [pp. ca. nipat] amnf nipātitā that one has brought down (on (loc.)) | struck down; beaten, destroyed | gram. irregular, exceptional.
nipātin [agt. nipat] amnf nipātinī that falls, that flies | that strikes, that destroys.
nipāna [act. nipā] n. act of drinking, of soaking watering trough; reservoir, pond.
nipīḍ [nipīḍ] v. [10] pr. (nipīḍayati) pp. (nipīdita) to press against, to press together; com to prime | to torment, to oppress | astr. to eclipse. dantān nipīdayat grinding his teeth.
nipīḍita [pp. nipīḍ] pressed, pressed; em brewed.
nipuṇa amnf nipuṇā intelligent, educated; skillful, subtle, clever; adroit, precise, exact.
nibaddha [pp. nibandh] amnf nibaddhā bound, attached, chained; fixed on (loc.) | covered by, veiled by (i.) | accompanied by, decorated by, inlaid with (i.) | composed (text).

nibandh [nibandh] v. [9] pr. (nibadhnāti) pr. r. (nibadhnīté) pp. (nibaddha) to attach, bind, fix to (loc.); to tie, chain, hinder; tighten | stop, capture, take; restrain, restrict; obstruct | fix in writing, draft, compose — ca. (nibandhayati) pp. (nibandhita) to cause to be tied up, to cause to be captured. kācam maṇikāñcanamekasūtre bāle nibadhnāsi ki matra citram | vicāravān pāṇinirekasūtre śvānam yuvānam maghavānamāha || young girl, why are you threading a glass bead, a jewel, and a gold ornament onto the same cord? She replied: the wise Pāṇini indeed placed a dog, a young man, and Indra in the same rule!
Nibandha [agt. nibandh] m. link, chain, in

work | origin, cause | title of ownership, deed of gift; legal texts in general | phil. attachment to the world of the senses, slavery to one's desires composition, literary work ["leaves bound together" | lit. not. np. of the Nibandha of Udayanācārya; cf. Nyāyavārttikatātparyapariśuddhi.
nibandhakāra [kāra] m. literary author.
nibandhana [agt. nibandh] amnf ni bandhanī that which binds, attaches; that which hinders — act. n. bond, chain, hindrance | support, aid; cause, origin, foundation | literary work, treatise. .9
nibandhin [agt. nibandh] amnf ni bandhinī that binds, that attaches; that hinders — ifc. connected to (iic.).

nibarhaṇa [agt. nibṛh] amnf nibarhaṇī that destroys, that crushes — act. n. destruction; ex termination. নিৰিভ nibiḍa [nibila] amnf nibiḍā without interstice; continuous; compact, dense, firm | full of (iic. i.) | with a hooked nose — n. the fact of having a hooked nose — v. |11| pr. (nibidayati) to strengthen, to tighten. nibidīkṛ to strengthen; to bend (bow).
nibudh [nibudh₁] v. [1] pr. (nibodhati) pr. r. (nibudhyate) pp. (nibuddha) to pay attention to (acc.), to learn from. nibodha imp. pay attention, listen carefully.
nibṛh [nibṛh₂] v. [1] pr. (nibṛhati) pf. (sam) to overthrow, to destroy. ਜਿਮ nibha [nibha] amnf nibhā similar to, like (iic.) — mn appearance; pretext.

nibhṛta [nibhṛta] amnf nibhṛtā carried or placed under; hidden; secret | modest; silent, solitary | firm, fixed; settled, ordered, decided; closed (door) — ifc. filled with (iic.) — n. humility, modesty. nibhṛtam adv. quietly, silently; secretly.
nimagna [pp. nimajj] amnf nimagnā plunged, immersed; absorbed; drowned.
nimajj [nimajj] v. [6] pr. (nimajjati) pp. (nimagna) to plunge, submerge | to be submerged, to sink; perish — ca. (nimajjayati) to immerse, to drown.
nimantr [nimantr] v. [10] pr. r. (niman trayate) pp. (nimantrita) pf. (upa) to invite, to join from (loc. inf.).
nimantraṇa [act. nimantr] n. injunction, command | soc. invitation | āmantraṇa | which cannot be refused.
nimaya [act. nimā₁ 2] m. exchange, barter.
nimā₁ [nimā₁] v. [3] pr. r. (nimimīte) pp. (nimita₁) to measure.
nimā₁ [nimā₄] v. [1] pr. r. (nimayate) pp. (nimita₂) to exchange, to barter (for (i.)).
nimi m. myth. np. of the emperor nimi "Wink", younger son of Ikṣvāku; he wanted to celebrate a

sacrifice [yajña] of 500 years, and asked his tutor Vasistha to direct it; the latter, having pledged himself to Indra for the same service, ordered him to wait; but nimi had the sacrifice carried out by Gautama in his place; on the return of Vasistha, the latter cursed him, condemning him to lose his body |videha| and to live only in the eyes of mortals; there he directs forever the blinking of the eyes [nimisa]; his body was embalmed, and the sages |rsi| churned his thigh to give birth to King Mithi Janaka, founder of the dynasty of Mithilā.
nimita₁ [pp. nimā₁] amnf nimitā measured.
nimita₂ [pp. nimā₁] amnf nimitā exchanged.

nimitta n. mark, sign; omen, augury | purpose, target | material cause, means, motive | (oblique cases) because of | phil. [Nyāya] effective cause (opp. upādāna , material cause) | gram. cf. pravṛtti, vyutpatti — amnf nimittā ifc. caused by. nimittena adv. for this reason. kim nimitta for what purpose? nimittam yā to be the cause of. nimittīkr to consider as the cause; to use as a means. nimittīkṛtya as a consequence of, because of (acc.). nimittībhū to become the cause of (loc.). nimittam sūcayan (theater) pretending to have an omen. nimittakāraņa [kāraṇa] n. phil. effective cause (notably God as Creator); instrumental cause (e.g. the potter's stick [daṇḍa] to make the pot |ghaṭa|).
nimittanaimittika | naimittika | n. of. phil. cause and effect.
nimittasaptamī | saptamī | f. gram. locative of motive.
nimittin [nimittain] amnf nimittinī having a cause; conditioned.
niminātha cf. naminātha.
nimiṣ [nimiṣ] v. [1] pr. (nimiṣati) pp. (nimișita) to wink.

nimiṣa [act. nimiṣ] m. blink of an eye | instant. nimiṣārdhena in a fraction of a second (the Sun travels 2202 stages [yojana]); this commentary by Sāyana on hymn I50 of the Rigveda gives an estimate of the distance from the Earth to the Sun.
nimișita [pp. nimiș] n. eye movement; wink; the act of closing the eyes.

nimīl [nimīl] v. [1] pr. (nimīlati) pp. (nimīlita) to close one's eyes, to fall asleep; to close (eyes, flowers); to die, to disappear. sā locane nyamīlayat she closed her eyes. nimimīla narottamapriyā The king's beloved closed her eyes (as she died).
nimeṣá [act. nimiṣ] m. blink; wink; a very brief measure of time (approximately a quarter of a second). nimeṣād iva adv. in the blink of an eye. nimesam nimesam adv. at any moment.
nimná [nimna] amnf nimnā deep, low, hollow — ifc. inclined towards (iic.) — n. depression in the ground, cavity; depth. nimnaih adv. downwards.
nimnonnata | unnata| amnf nimnonnatā mo delé (hollow and raised); bumpy (top and bottom).
nimba var. nīma m. bio. bot. Azadirachta indica, neem tree or neem tree, a member of the meliaceae family; its flowers are violet, its leaves are doubly pinnate; an oil is made from its bitter fruits

medicinal | taila|; its bark and leaves also have medicinal uses; its young branches serve as toothbrushes; its leaves are chewed at funeral ceremonies; the idol of Jagannātha is made of its wood; cf. prabhadra || hi. nīm.

nimbaka |ka| m. id. śatāyurvajradehāya sarvasampatkarāya ca sarvāristavināśāya nimbakam dalabhakṣaṇam By chewing the buds of the nīm tree, fortune smiles upon you, difficulties vanish, and until one hundred years the body remains as strong as a diamond (sung at the New Year |yugādi|, the mixture of bitter nīm and sweet guḍa symbolizing the sorrows and joys to come).
nimbataila [taila] n. neem oil.
nimbadala [dala] n. nimba inflorescences. nimbadalam gudam ca svīkarotu Please take nimba buds with brown sugar (formal New Year's Day ritual [yugādi]).

nimbārka [arka] m. hist. np. of the master [ācārya] nimbārka "Who made the sun appear from the neem tree [nimba] (to receive his Jain opponent refusing his hospitality after sunset)", born in Dravidian country in the 11th century; he was an ascetic at Nan dagrāma near Govardhana; he preached the doctrine of duality in nonduality [dvaitādvaita].
nimbū [related to nimba] m. organic. bot. Citrus acida, lemon | var. nimbūka id.

níyata [pp. niyam] amnf niyatā restrained, repressed, prevented; chained | bound to, connected with, contained in (loc.) | limited, disciplined, mastered, controlled; tempered, moderate | fixed, determined, invariable, permanent, usual; certain, established | marked by destiny — m. gram. sandhi de ās before voiced phonemes. niyatam adv. always, inevitably; with certainty | it is certain.
niyatabhojana | bhojana | amnf niyatabhojanā One who eats in moderation — n. diet.
niyatamānasa [mānasa] amnf niyatamānasī Who controls his thoughts — n. repression of the mind.
níyatamaithuna | maithuna | amnf niyatamai thunā Who abstains from carnal intercourse — n. sexual abstinence.
niyatayukta |yukta| amnf niyatayuktā Who controls meditation — n. phil. continuous or controlled yoga.
níyatavrata [vrata] amnf niyatavratā Who observes his vows; pious — n. piety; observance of vows.
níyatāñjali [añjali] amnf ["Who observes the añjali" | Who greets by joining hands.
níyatātman [ātman] amnf niyatātmanī [“Who controls his character” self-master, disci pliné.

níyatāpti [āpti] f. lit. [theatre] certainty of success: the fact that the hero overcomes an obstacle, giving hope of achieving the goal; it is one of the 5 stages of the unfolding of the action [kāryāvasthā].
niyatendriya [indriya] amnf niyatendriyā Who controls his senses — n. control of the senses.

niyati [act. niyam] f. necessity; inexorable force | order of things; fate, destiny | phil. determinism of destiny according to the materialists [ājīvika] | myth. np. of niyati, daughter of Meru and wife of Dhātā like her sister Ayati.
niyativāda [vāda] m. phil. doctrine of predestination or fatalism, taught notably by Gośāla.

niyantṛ [agt. niyam] amnf niyantrī Who governs, Who represses, Who restricts; governor — m. phil. [Sāṃkhya] regent of a faculty [indriya]; the 5 regents of the senses [buddhīndriya] are the Diśas, Vāyu, Aditya, Varuņa and the pair of the Aśvinau; the 5 regents of the faculties of action [karmendriya] are Agni, Indra, Vișnu, Prajāpati and Mitra.
niyantra [niyantra] v. [11] pr. (niyantrayati) to restrict, repress; control.
niyantrana [act. niyantra] n. restriction, limit, constraint | gram. restriction to a particular meaning; definition.
niyantrita [pp. niyantra] amnf niyan tritā restricted, controlled; attached, confined; placed on banks (river) | gram. restricted to a particular sense | governed by, dependent on (i. iic.).
niyam [niyam] v. [1] pr. (niyaccati) pp. (niyata) pf. (vi, sam) to restrain, repress, restrict; govern, discipline, regulate, fix — ca. (niyamayati) id. vācam niyaccha hold your tongue!

niyama [act. niyam] m. repression, restriction, limitation, abstinence; restraint, reserve; discipline, observance, penance; practice resulting from a vow | soc. moral discipline, the second stage of rājayoga, consisting of the practice of spiritual exercises to acquire five virtues: purity [śauca], moderation (frugality) [samtoṣa], fortitude (acquired through asceticism) [tapas], knowledge (acquired through the reading of sacred texts) [svādhyāya], and faith (acquired through meditation) [īśvarapraṇidhāna]; cf. aṣṭāṅgayoga | pl. niyamās rules; regulation. niyamena generally; certainly, surely under certain conditions. niyamāt generally; certainly, surely.
niyamavidhi [vidhi] m. phil. [Mīmāmsā] restrictive ritual injunction.
niyamasūtra [sūtra] n. gram. restrictive rule in Aştādhyāyī.
niyamana [agt. niyam] n. that which dominates, that which represses, that which tames — obj. n. domination; humiliation | restriction, limitation | regulation.

niyamita [pp. ca. niyam] amnf niya mitā controlled, repressed; limited, confined; attached to (iic.) | stopped, removed; determined, fixed; intended for (inf.) | governed, guided; regulated, prescribed; stipulated; agreed.
niyamya [pfp. [1] niyam] amnf niyamyā to control, to repress; that which must be limited; to define — abs. ind. having restricted, having limited.
niyāma [act. niyam] m. cf. niyama | sailor, navigator.

niyāmaka [agt. niyam] amnf niyāmikā that restricts, that controls, that represses | restrictive, limiting, defining | phil. [Nyāya] that delimits; syn. avacchedaka — m. guide, leader | chariot driver; navigator | phil. [Nyāya] guiding principle.
niyāmakatā [tā] f. restriction; control; direction.
niyāmakatva [tva] n. id.
niyu [niyu₁] v. [2] pr. (niyauti) pp. (niyuta) to attach, to unite.

niyukta [pp. niyuj] amnf niyuktā at taché, attelé, fettervé; fixe; assigned to (loc.); pres crit, ordained | charged with (dat. inf. iic.); employee, attendant — m. official. niyuktam certainly; necessarily.
niyukti [act. niyuj] f. prescription; order, injunction; charge, employment.

niyuj [niyuj₁] v. [7] pr. (niyunákti) pr. r. (niyuńkté) pp. (niyukta) pf. (vi, sam) to order, to sign, to designate, to charge with, to entrust something (acc.) to someone (loc.) | to put under the yoke, to subjugate; to put under; to discipline, to govern, to tame — ca. (niyo jayati) to attach to; to charge someone (acc.) with (loc.) to lay (a trap), to set (a snare).
niyuta [pp. niyu] amnf niyutā fixed, at stained — n. one hundred thousand.
niyuddha [niyuddha] n. pugilism; close combat; unarmed combat.

niyoga [act. niyuj] m. assignment, employment, charge, instruction; order, mission | [niyogadharma] soc. levirate, duty of a childless widow to marry her husband's brother. vyāsaniyogah myth. [Mah.] the obligation that Vyāsa had to ensure the descendants of his mother Satyavatī's sons, to father Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu.
niyogin [agt. niyuj] amnf niyoginī appointed, assigned; assigned to a mission — m. functionary, official; minister.

niyojya [pfp. [1] ca. niyuj] amnf niyojyā which must be attached, fixed | to employ, to use; to equip with (i.) — ifc. which must be employed to, which deserves the charge of, which must be ordered to (iic.) — m. official, servant; employee, servant.
nir cf. nis.
nirakṣara [nisakṣara] amnf nirakṣarā illiterate.
niragni [nisagni] amnf without fire; who does not maintain his fires.
niragha [nisagha] amnf niraghā without sin; not guilty.

Nirañjana [nisañjana] amnf Nirañjanā immaculate; pure, unmixed | without emotions, passionate dis — m. myth. np. of Nirañjana, epith. of Śiva "the immaculate" — f. Nirañjanā full moon; syn. pūrnimā | myth. np. of Nirañjanā, epith. of Durgā "the immaculate".
nirata [pp. niram] amnf niratā content, satisfied; delighted by | devoted to, engaged in, absorbed by (loc. i. iic.).
niratı [act. niram] ifc. f. enjoyment of; attachment to.
niratiśaya [nisatiśaya] amnf ni ratiśayā unsurpassable.
niranunāsika [nisanunāsika] amnf niranunāsikā phon. is said of semivowels without nasalization; opp. sānunāsika.

nirantara [nisantara] amnf nirantarā compact, dense; uninterrupted, continuous | perpetual; constant, faithful; sincere — ifc. full of; filled with (iic.). nirantaram adv. closely, firmly without interruption, continuously; perpetually immediately, at once.
nirantarāya [nisantarāya] m. absence of obstacle.
nirantarāyatva [tva] n. phil. state of consciousness where one is free from all obstacles.
niraparādha [nisaparādha] amnf ni raparādhā who does not make a mistake; not guilty; irreproachable.

nirapekṣa [nisapekṣā] amnf nirapekṣā indifferent to, without regard for, independent of (iic. loc.) | indifferent; disinterested; impartial; opp. sāpekṣa — f. nirapekṣā indifference. nirapekṣam adv. with indifference; notwithstanding; without paying attention, accidentally.
nirapekṣatā [tā] f. indifference, disinterest; impartiality; tolerance.
nirapekṣatva [tva] n. id.
nirapekṣin [in] amnf nirapekṣinī indifferent.
nirabhilāṣa [nisabhilāṣa] amnf ni rabhilāṣā not desiring, not seeking; without covetousness, indifferent.
niram [niram] v. [1] pr. r. (niramate) v. [1] pr. (niramati) pp. (nirata) to cease, to stop | to find pleasure in, to be attached to — ca. (niramayati) to stop; to satisfy, to please.

niraya [nisaya] m. ["bad luck"] hell myth. np. of niraya, hell personified, son of fear and death. nirayah yas tvayā vinā Hell is your absence. vedānām lekhakāścaiva te vai nirayagāminah [Mah.] He who writes the Veda in truth goes to hell.
nirayana [nisayana] n. astr. zodiac
sidereal ["without movement"], related to the constellations; opp. sāyana.
nirartha [nisartha] amnf nirarthā ["without wealth"] poor | useless, vain; absurd.
nirarthaka [ka] amnf nirarthikā useless, vain; absurd. nirarthakam adv. in vain, uselessly.
niravagraha [nisavagraha] amnf nira vagrahā gram. without the avagraha sign.
niravacchinna [nisavacchinna] amnf niravacchinnā phil. [Nyāya] not delimited; not determined, not discriminated.
niravadya [nisavadya] amnf niravadyā irreproachable — n. Excellency.
niravadyatva [tva] n. irreproachability.
niravadyavat [vat] amnf niravadyavatī ex cellent.

niravadhi [nisavadhi] amnf unlimited, without end; infinite. kālo hyayam niravadhirvipulā ca pṛthvī [Mālatīmādhava] Time is endless and the world is vast (and so the day will come when my fellow man will appreciate these verses).
niravayava [nisavayava] amnf nira vayavā phil. indivisible, indivisible (said not. of Brahman).
niravalamba [nisavalamba] amnf ni ravalambā without support, without support.
niravalambana [nisavalambana] amnf niravalambanā without support, without backing | which belongs to no one.
niravasā [nisavasā] v. [4] pr. (niravasyati) pp. (niravasita) to reject.
niravasita [pp. niravasā] amnf nira vasitā soc. excluded, rejected (said of an outcaste or an untouchable śūdra, whose touch permanently pollutes a food container, e.g. a cāndāla).
niraśana [nisaśana₂] amnf niraśanā who fasts — n. fasting.
niras [nisas₂] v. [4] pr. (nirasyati) pp. (ni rasta) pfp. (nirasya) reject; drive out, expel, banish nir; renounce (acc.); refute | tear out, destroy, annihilate.
nirasta [pp. niras] amnf nirastā rejected, banished, refused; that which has been renounced; omitted | launched (arrow, throwing weapon) | vomited — n. bad pronunciation.
nirasya [pfp. [1] niras] amnf nirasyā to reject; to banish; to refute — abs. ind. having rejected.
nirahamkāra var. nirahankāra nis ahamkāra] amnf nirahamkārā without ego.
nirākaraņa [act. nirākṛ] n. rejection; ex pulsion; repudiation | opposition; contradiction, negation | forgetfulness; neglect (not. of religious duties).
nirākariṣṇu [agt. nirākṛ] amnf who rejects, who repudiates; who drives away, who banishes | who obstructs, who prevents (abl.); envious.
nirākānkṣa [nisākānkṣā] amnf nirākānkṣā gram. (word) without (other) dependency, or whose dependency is already satisfied.

nirākāra [nisākāra₁] amnf nirākārā formless; incorporeal (said of brahman); without content; undetectable | phil. devoid of aspect | insignificant, without importance; without object; opp. sākāra — m. myth. epith. of Shiva | phil. the Heavens; the Supreme Being.
nirākāravāda | vāda | m. bd. idealist doctrine teaching that consciousness is without external object; cf. Ratnākaraśānti.
nirākṛ [nisākṛ] v. [8] pr. (nirākaroti) pp. (nirākṛta) to undo, separate, detach; to set aside, expel, repudiate | to reject, refuse, neglect; to contradict, deny.
nirākṛta [pp. nirākṛ] amnf nirākṛtā repudiated, banished; omitted, forgotten; removed; destroyed; refuted — ifc. deprived of (iic.).
nirākrti₁ [act. nirākr] f. obstruction — agt. amnf that prevents, that obstructs.
nirākṛti₂ [nisākṛti] amnf formless (said not. of Viṣṇu) | ugly — m. soc. person neglecting his duties; not. brahmin ignorant of the Veda.
nirākṛtya [pfp. [1] nirākṛ] amnf nirākṛtyā to reject; to banish; to refute — abs. ind. having banished, having refuted (acc.).
nirātanka [nisātanka] amnf nirātankā without apprehension; without fear | not feeling embarrassment; at ease.
nirātman [nisātman] amnf nirātmanī soulless; without individuality.
nirāmaya [nisāmaya] m. good health — amnf nirāmayā well, in good health | intact; in working order. nirāmayasya kimāyurvedavidā For a healthy man, what use is a doctor?
nirālamba [nisālamba] amnf nirālambā independent, autonomous, self-sufficient isolated, solitary.
nirālambana [nisālambana] amnf nirālambanā deprived of support, without support; lacking a basis | phil. ["without support in reality"] imaginary, illusory.
nirāloka [nisāloka] amnf nirālokā dark.
nirāśa [nisāśā₂] amnf nirāśā indifferent, without desire; depressed, hopeless. nirāśībhū to give in to despair. nirāśībhūta hopeless. nirāśībhāva despair.
nirāśin [in] amnf nirāśinī desperate.

nirāśis [nisāśis₁] amnf [sg. nom. nirāśīs; en comp. nirāśīr] without desire; indifferent without hope. nirāśīrnirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvarah [BG.] Having become without personal desire and without attachments, struggles in indifference.
nirāśraya [nisāśraya] amnf nirāśrayā without refuge; without protection | without attachment; without need; independent.
nirāsa₁ [act. niras] m. rejection, exclusion, refusal; expulsion | the act of vomiting | elision (of a sound); faulty pronunciation.
nirāsa₁ [nisāsa₂] m. without seat; without shelter.
nirāhāra [nisāhāra] amnf nirāhārā who fasts.
nirīkṣ [nisīkṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (nirīkṣate) pp. (nirīkṣita) to look at carefully, to examine, to scrutinize; to contemplate.
nirīkṣaka [agt. nirīkṣ] amnf nirīkṣikā who looks, who sees; who visits — m. inspector.
nirīkṣaṇa [agt. nirīkṣ] amnf nirīkṣaṇī who looks, who sees (iic.) — act. n. view; look, observation | overview; investigation, study astr. aspect of the planets — f. nirīkṣaṇā id.
nirīkṣā [act. nirīkṣ] f. examination, observation (not. of the stars).
nirīkṣya [pfp. [1] nirīkṣ] amnf nirīkṣya which must be examined.
nirīśvara [nisīśvara] amnf nirīśvarā phil. atheist; opp. seśvara | soc. not. qualifies an atheist branch of Sāṃkhya.

Nirukta [pp. nirvac] amnf niruktā pro noncé, expliqué, expliqué — n. explication, in interprétation, étymologie | phil. l'herméneutique, ou sémantique phonologique, interprétation du glossaire des termes vedics, un des 6 traité annexes du Veda [vedānga] | lit. np. du Nirukta, ouvrage d'herméneutique vedic dû de Yāska; c'est un commentaire de son glossaire Nighantu ; il y a 3 commentaires de l'on vrtti Rjvartha de Durga/Durgasimha, avant le 6e siècle, la Ni ruktabhāṣyatīkā de Skanda Svāmī et Maheśvara, et le Niruktavārttika de Nīlakantha₆.
niruktatara [tara] amnf niruktatarā articulated, explained.
Niruktavārttika [vārttika] n. bed. from np. Niruktavārttika of Nīlakantha₆; cf. Nor ruktaślokavārttika.
Niruktaślokavārttika [ślokavārttika] n. bed. n.p. of the Niruktaślokavārttika, commentary on the Nirukta due to Nīlakantha₆ (before the 14th century).

Nirukti [act. nirvac] f. gram. etymological interpretation of a word | artificial derivation of a word; np. of the Nirukti cf. Nirukta | soc. (theatre) communication that an event has just taken place || pali nirutti.
niruttara [nisuttara₁] amnf niruttara which has no superior | which has no answer.
niruddha [pp. nirudh] amnf niruddhā obstructed, stopped, held back, blocked; besieged | prevented, sidelined, rejected, excluded; suppressed.
nirudyama [nisudyama] amnf niru dyamā who does not make an effort; inactive; lazy.
nirudyoga [nisudyoga] amnf niru dyogā who does not make an effort; inactive; lazy, discouraged. nirudyogaih asmābhih avasthātum ayuktam It is not good for us to remain inactive.
nirudh [nirudh₂] v. [7] pr. (niruṇáddhi) pr. r. (nirunddhé) pp. (niruddha) pf. (sam) to obstruct, block, enclose; to restrict; to hide | to exclude, repress, keep in check.
nirupadrava [nisupadrava] amnf ni rupadrava out of danger, safe; peaceful.
nirupama [nisupama] amnf nirupamā unsurpassed; unsurpassable; supreme.
nirupāya [nisupāya] amnf nirupāyā without means; powerless; unable to succeed.
nirūḍha₁ [pp. nirvah] amnf nirūḍhā drawn, separated; evacuated; purged; eviscerated — m. soc. unmarried, single.
nirūḍha₁ [nirūḍha] amnf nirūḍhā developed, wall, adult | gram. of conventional acquired meaning — m. gram. use of words according to their natural or conventional meaning.
nirūdhapaśubandha | paśubandha | m. ved. independent animal sacri fice.
nirūdhalakṣaṇā [lakṣaṇā] f. gram. secondary meaning of a word which has become principal, such as kuśala fixed metaphor.

nirūp [nirūp] v. [10] pr. (nirūpayati) pp. (nirūpita) pfp. (nirūpya) to observe, examine, consider | to determine, decide; to assign to. loc. inf. | lit. to represent (not. on stage), to express by gestures | phil. [Nyāya] to determine, to describe. rathavegam nirūpya (coachman in the theater) miming a chariot at high speed.
nirūpaka [agt. nirūp] amnf nirūpikā ob servator, examiner | phil. [Nyāya] descriptor, restrictor — ifc. described by (iic.).

nirūpaṇa [agt. nirūp] amnf nirūpaṇī ifc. that which determines, that which defines — act. nf nirūpaṇā act of ruling | research, investigation, examination | form, appearance — ifc. lit. form of book titles "in investigation de (iic.)".
nirūpaṇīya [pfp. [2] nirūp] amnf nirūpanīyā which must be investigated, which must be examined.
nirūpayitavya [pfp. [3] nirūp] amnf nirūpayitavyā to be determined; to be estimated.

nirūpita [pp. nirūp] amnf nirūpitā describes, observed, examined, evaluated; determined, assigned, designated, chosen, elected | phil. [NN.] determined by, described by, restricted by (iic.) (specifies the target of a relation) — n. state of having been examined. ghațanirūpitādhraṇatā f. phil. fact of being a support conditioned by a pot. nirūpitapitrtva n. ifc. quality of father determined by (iic.). nisthaputratva n. ifc. quality of son inherent in (iic.).

nirūpya [pfp. [1] nirūp] amnf nirūpyā to consider, to examine; to determine, to choose | what is described, what is observed. nirūpya nirūpaka bhāva phil. relation between the observer and the observed.
nirūha [nisūha] m. med. administration of a non-oily enema based on plant decoctions.
nirūhana [na] n. id.
nirṛ [nisṛ] v. [1] pr. (nirṛcchati) pp. (nirṛta) to fall, to be deprived of; to fall apart, to disintegrate, to rot.
nirṛṇa [nisṛṇa] amnf nirṛṇā without debt.
