nirṛta [pp. nirṛ] amnf nirṛtā destroyed, demolished, corrupted.

Nirṛti [act. nirṛ] f. destruction, dissolution, decline, corruption, decomposition | calamity, curse; abyss | phil. Evil; syn. amhas | disorder, entropy | myth. np. of Nirrti "Calamity", universal force of destruction, wife of Adharma, associated with Mṛtyu; she is the mother of
ogre-vampires [rākṣasās] — m. myth. np. of the divine breath |marut| Nirṛti₁; it is one of the 11 forms of
Rudra [ekādaśarudrās]; guardian [dikpāla] of the South West, he reigns over the spirit of the dead [bhūta].
nirodha [act. nirudh] m. imprisonment, detention; restriction, restraint, obstruction; obs tackle; repression, suppression | bd. Noble Truth āryasatya of the cessation of suffering.
nirodhaka [agt. nirudh] ifc. amnf nirod hikā which obstructs (iic.); who prevents, who suppresses (iic.).
nirodhana [agt. nirudh] amnf nirodhani that obstructs; that prevents, that suppresses — act. n. detention; restriction, restricted, obstruction; repression, suppression
nirgata [pp. nirgam] amnf nirgatā gone, gone; disappeared | appeared.
nirgam [nisgam] v. [1] pr. (nirgacchati) pp. (nirgata) pf. (vi) to go away, to leave; to disappear; to go out (from (abl.)); to appear. nidrām nirgam to fall asleep.
nirgama [act. nirgam] m. departure, disappearance; cessation, end; exit.
nirgamana [act. nirgam] n. exit.
nirgarbha [nisgarbha] amnf nirgarbhā without private apartment | without matrix; without em bryon.

nirguṇa [nisguṇa] amnf nirguṇā without string (bow) | devoid of qualities, evil, vicious phil. without attributes, undifferentiated (opp. saguna). nirguna brahman phil. the transcendent, unmanifested divine.
nirguṇaguṇī [red.] amnf phil. ["with and without qualities" qualifies the dual divine nature, both immanent and transcendent.
nirguṇatā [tā] f. phil. absence of attributes; undifferentiation | absence of good qualities, defectiveness, wickedness.
nirgunatva |tva| n. id.
nirguṇātmavādin [ātmavādin] amnf nirguṇātmavādinī phil. holding a posi doctrine
tivist [āstika] believing in an indescribable transcendent reality; opp. saguņātmavādin.
nirguṇḍī f. organic. bot. Vitex negundo; cf. sin duvāra | var. nirgundi id.
nirgundīpuspa [puṣpa] m. bio. its flower, used in medicine.
nirgrantha [nisgrantha] amnf nir granthā without attachments, free from ties — m. er mite withdrawn from the world, wandering ascetic | naked Jain beggar — n. soc. Jainism.
nirghṛṇā [nisghṛṇā] amnf nirghṛṇā cruel, merciless.
nirghrnatā [tā] f. cruelty.
nirjana [nisjana] amnf nirjanā ["without men" solitary; uninhabited.
nirjanasthāna [sthāna] n. uninhabited place.
nirjaya [act. nirji] m. conquest; complete victory, triumph.
nirjara [nisjara] amnf nirjarā that does not age; always young; unalterable, imperishable; immortal — amnf nirjaras id. — m. god; syn. deva, amara.
nirjala [nisjala] amnf nirjalā dry, arid; desert.
nirjalaikādaśī [ekādaśī] f. soc. 11th day of the clear fortnight of the month jyaiṣṭha ; one fasts on it without food or water.
nirji [nisji] v. [1] pr. (nirjayati) pr. r. (nirjayate) pp. (nirjita) abs. (nirjitya) to overcome, conquer; to subdue, subjugate.
nirjita [pp. nirji] amnf nirjitā subjugated, subjugated; conquered, defeated | owed (interest, rent).
nirjhara [nisjhara] m. waterfall, cataract; torrent | lit. alliteration.

nirṇaya [act. nirṇī] m. act of carrying off, removing | decision, determination | phil. deduction, inference; conclusion; demonstration; solution | soc. sentence, verdict; decree | discussion, consideration — ifc. lit. names prescriptive works, not. summaries of smrti. tava nirnaye sthāsyāmi I submit to your decision. tava nirnayah pramānam your decision is authoritative.
nirnayaka [agt. nirnī] amnf nirnayikā which is authoritative.
nir n ī [nisn ī₁] v. [1] pr. (nir nay ati) pp. (nirnīta) pf. (vi) to take away, carry off | to deduce; to conclude, to determine, to decide, to establish, to fix.
nirṇīta [pp. nirṇī] amnf nirṇītā determined, deduced, established; decided, concluded.
nirṇud [nisnud] v. [6] pr. (nirṇudati) to repel, to set aside; to reject; to repudiate; to banish.
nirdaya [nisdayā] amnf nirdayā cruel, merciless; violent; passionate, excessive. nirdayam adv. ruthlessly; violently; passionately. nirdayataram adv. very cruelly.
nirdayāślesa [āślesa] m. passionate embrace.
nirdah [nisdah₁] v. [1] pr. (nirdahati) pp. (nirdagdha) burn completely, consume.
nirdākṣiṇya [nisdākṣiṇya] amnf nirdākṣiṇyā impolite; without consideration.
nirdiś [nisdiś₁] v. [1] pr. (nirdiśati) pp. (nirdiṣṭa) pf. (vi) to designate, stipulate, prescribe; to specify, define, name.
nirdiṣṭa [pp. nirdiś] amnf nirdiṣṭā in diqué, annonce; designated, specified.
nirduḥkha [nisduḥkha] amnf nirduḥkhā without pain.
nirduḥkhatva |vat| n. absence of pain.
nirdeva [nisdeva] amnf nirdevā aban given by the gods; without gods.
nirdevatva |tva| n. absence of gods.
nirdeśa [act. nirdiś] m. indication, instruction (for (i.e.)); order, command | description, specification; special indication.
nirdeśya [pfp. [1] nirdiś] amnf nirdeśyā to determine, to define; to establish, to prove — m. math. statement of a problem (find ... such that).
nirdoṣa [nisdoṣa₂] amnf nirdoṣā without fault, impeccable; without sin, innocent. nirdosīkr to exonerate.
nirdvandva [nisdvandva] amnf nird vandvā indifferent to alternatives | phil. that has transcended opposites | that does not take sides; independent | without question; without alternative.
nirdhana [nisdhana] amnf nirdhanā without possessions, poor | volunteer.
nirdhanatā [tā] f. poverty.
nirdhanatva [tva] n. id.
nirdharma [nisdharma] amnf nirdharmā impious; unjust, unfair; unnatural | phil. indes indescriptible (said of absolute reality).
nirdharmatva [tva] n. phil. absence of properties of absolute reality.
nirdhāra [act. nirdhṛ] m. act of defining, determining; evaluation.

nirdhāraṇa [act. nirdhṛ ] n. act of defining, determining; evaluation | gram. segregation of an element (outside of a set g. loc. ), not. for the superlative. kṣatriyo manuṣyāṇāṃ śūratamaḥ the kṣatriya is the bravest of men.
nirdhāryamāṇa [ppr. ps. ca. nirdhr] amnf nirdhāryamāṇā selected | gram. segregated element (of a whole).
nirdhāv [nisdhāv₁] v. [1] pr. (nirdhāvati) to spring from, to escape from, to run away from abl. .
nirdhū [nisdhū₁] v. [5] pr. (nirdhunoti) pr. r. (nirdhunute) pp. (nirdhūta) shake, agitate; scatter, disperse; remove.
nirdhūta [pp. nirdhū] amnf nirdhūtā agitated, shaken | deprived of (ifc.); abandoned.
nirdhūtakalmaṣa [kalmaṣa] amnf nirdhūtakalmaṣā whose sins have been erased.
nirdhūma [nisdhūma] amnf nirdhūmā without smoke.
nirdhṛ [nisdhṛ] v. [1] pr. (nirdharati) pp. (nirdhrta) to evaluate; to determine.
nirnimitta [nisnimitta] amnf nir nimittā without reason, without motive; without cause selfless. nirnimittam adv. without cause.
nirnimeṣa [nisnimeṣa] amnf nirnimeṣā whose eyes do not blink (said of the gods). nirnimeṣam adv. without blinking.
nirbandh [nisbandh] v. [9] pr. (nirbadhnāti) pp. (nirbaddha) insist, persist.
nirbandha [act. nirbandh] m. insistence, perseverance; tenacity, obstinacy. alam nirbandhena enough of your obstinacy.
nirbādha [nisbādha] amnf nirbādhā without hindrance, without obstruction.
nirbīja [nisbīja] amnf nirbījā [“without germ” infertile, sterile (opp. sabīja).
nirbuddhi [nisbuddhi] amnf senseless; ignorant; stupid.

nirbhaya [nisbhaya] n. absence of fear; security — amnf nirbhayā without fear, fearless; tranquil; safe — m. hist. np. of Nirb haya, epithet of King Mahendrapāla₁ "the Bold" (late 9th century). nirbhayam adv. without fear, in a fearless manner.

nirbhara [nisbhara] amnf nirbharā ["without measure"] excessive, violent; deep (som meil); narrow (embrace) — ifc. full of (iic.). nirbharam adv. excessively, violently; completely, thoroughly; deeply. nirbharam prasuptah deeply asleep.
nirbharts [nisbharts] v. [10] pr. (nirbhart sayati) pp. (nirbhartsita) to threaten.
nirbhartsana [act. nirbharts] n. threat.
nirbhid [nisbhid₁] v. [7] pr. (nirbhinatti) pr. r. (nirbhintte) pp. (nirbhinna) to split, break, divide, open, pierce | wound; destroy — ps. (nirbhi dyate) to be split.
nirbhinna [pp. nirbhid] amnf nirbhinnā opened, bloomed (flower) | divided, separated | pierced, penetrated, discovered, betrayed.
nirmakṣikam [nismakṣikā] adv. without flies.
nirmagna [pp. nirmajj] amnf nirmagnā flooded; sunken.
nirmajj [nismajj] v. [6] pr. (nirmajjati) pp. (nirmagna) to flow under, to sink; to sink; inon der.
nirmama [nismama] amnf nirmamā disinterested; without selfishness | indifferent to (loc.).
nirmamatā [tā] f. disinterestedness; indifference.
nirmamatva [tva] n. id.
nirmala [nismala] amnf nirmalā spotless, pure, immaculate; brilliant; virtuous.
nirmalatā [tā] f. cleanliness, purity; the state of being immaculate.
nirmalatva |tva| n. id.

nirmā [nismā₁] v. [3] pr. r. (nirmimīte) v. [2] pr. (nirmāti) pp. (nirmita) pf. (vi) to measure; to construct, shape, make; to create | to produce, cause, determine; to establish. citram nirmā to paint a picture. dharmam nirmā to establish a law.
nirmāṇa [act. nirmā] n. measure; scope, extent | construction, creation, formation, composition; form; work — ifc. made of (iic.).
nirmāṇakāya [kāya] m. bd. the "created body", symbolizing the physical form of Being present in the sensual nature of man.
nirmāna [nismāna₁] amnf nirmānā without assurance; without pride.
nirmānuşa [nismānuşa] amnf nirmānuṣā uninhabited; desert, desolate.

nirmālya [nismālya] amnf nirmālyā discarded from a garland; rejected, expired; (clothing) worn the day before — n. soc. garland offered in his crucifixion; remainder of a sacrifice, consecrated food; not. sacred preparation of the temple of Jagannātha at Purī, consisting of a net containing consecrated grains of rice; one must eat one a day.

nirmita [pp. nirmā] amnf nirmitā made, constructed, fashioned, manufactured, formed, created; made by (i. i. ic.) with (abl. i. i. ic.) | established, fixed; (judgment) rendered; (rite) performed | chosen, determined, reserved (animal for sacrifice) | pl. nirmitās bd. [Mahāyāna] class of deities || pali nimitta.
nirmitavat [ppa. nirmā] amnf nirmi tavatī author.

nirmukta [pp. nirmuc] amnf nir muktā made free; liberated | deprived of (abl. i. iic.) abandoned; lost; disappeared | deprived of everything; without any possessions | (snake) having just shed its skin.
nirmuktadeha [deha] amnf nirmuktadehā freed from his sensual desires.
nirmuktasanga [sanga] amnf nirmuktasangā free from attachments to the world.
nirmukti [act. nirmuc] f. liberation, deliverance (from (abl. iic.)).

nirmuc [nismuc₁] v. [6] pr. (nirmuñcati) pp. (nirmukta) pf. (vi) to free; to deliver from (abl.) — ps. (nirmucyate) to be freed from; to free oneself, to get rid of (abl.); to be deprived of (i.); to molt (ser pent) — ca. (nirmocayati) to make free; to release from (abl.); to disengage.
nirmūla [nismūla] amnf nirmūlā ar torn out; eradicated | without base; without foundation — v. [11] pr. (nirmūlayati) to tear out, to extirpate; to eradicate, to annihilate.
nirmūlana [act. nirmūla] n. act of uprooting, extirpating.
nirmoka [obj. nirmuc] m. liberation | molting of a snake.
nirmokṣa [act. nirmuc] m. liberation, deliverance (from g. iic.).
nirmocana [act. nirmuc] n. liberation; deliverance.

niryā₁ [nisyā₁] v. [2] pr. (niryāti) to go out; to go out from (abl.) (to go to (acc)) | to depart for (dat.) | to depart for the afterlife, to die | to pass (time) — ca. (niryāpayati) to cause to go out; to expel from (abl.). yuddhāya niryā to go out for battle. digjayāya niryā to go out for conquest. bhikṣārtham niryā to go out to beg. mrgayām niryā to go out for hunting.
niryā₂ [nisya₂] f. malfunction; defect; not. fault during a rite.
niryāṇa [act. niryā₁] n. exit; outcome | departure; rout (army); departure (of the herd for transhumance) | disappearance | death (departure from life) exit road of a city.
niryānādhyāya [adhyāya] m. lit. np. from the Niryāṇādhyāya, chapter of the Bṛhajjātaka dealing with the prediction of death and the transmigration of the soul.
niryātana [nisyātana] n. return; restoration; replacement; payment (debt) | retaliation, revenge.
niryūtha [nisyūtha] amnf niryūthā separated from the flock or the herd.
niryogakṣema [nisyogakṣema] amnf niryogakṣemā phil. freed from the acquisition and preservation of goods.
nirlakṣaṇa [nislakṣaṇa] amnf nirlakṣaṇā undistinguished, commonplace; without distinction; insignificant | incapable, good for nothing | unnoticed.
nirlakṣya [nislakṣya] amnf nirlakṣyā undetectable; invisible.
nirlajja [nislajjā] amnf nirlajjā who is not ashamed. nirlajjam adv. shamelessly.
nirlajjatā [tā] f. lack of shame; impudence.
nirlinga [nislinga] amnf nirlingī gram. devoid of gender.
nirlunth [nislunth] v. [1] pr. (nirluntati) pp. (nirluthita) to plunder, to steal.
nirvac [nisvac] pfp. (nirvacanīya, nirvācya₁) pp. (nirukta) ps. (nirucyate) declare, state; in interpret, explain; derive | derive from (abl.) forbid from, warn against, order to leave abl. .
nirvacana₁ [nisvacana] amnf nirvacanā silent, saying nothing | irreproachable, beyond reproach. nirvacanam adv. in silence.
nirvacana₁ [act. nirvac] n. saying, proverb; explanation | gram. interpretation, etymology; cf. nirukta | meaning of a word in accordance with the speaker's intention.
nirvacanaśāstra [śāstra] n. phil. traditional science of etymology and semantic interpretation; syn. nirukta.

nirvacanīya [pfp. [2] nirvac] amnf nirvacanīyā to explain, to specify; syn. nirvācya₁. nirvana [nisvana] mn country without forest; bush. nirvane adv. in open countryside. nirvana [nisvana] amnf nirvanā without forest; outside the woods; in open countryside.

nirvap [nisvap₂] v. [1] pr. (nirvapati) pp. (ni rupta) to pour, to spread; to sprinkle | to offer (not. a libation) (to (dat)) — ca. (nirvāpayati) to sow. agnaye tvā justam nirvapāmi [Veda] O Agni I make this offering to you.
nirvápana [act. nirvap] n. act of pouring, of spreading; watering, scattering | soc. offering; not. libation to the manes | gift; donation — ifc. scattering of, pouring of (iic.).
nirvarn [nisvarn] v. [10] pr. (nirvarnayati) to look, observe, contemplate, examine.
nirvart [ca. nirvrt] v. [10] pr. (nirvartayati) pfp. (nirvartya) abs. (nirvartya) to accomplish; stop, finish.
nirvartin [agt. ca. nirvṛt] amnf nirvar tinī who accomplishes, who does (iic.) | who behaves or acts badly.
nirvartya [pfp. [1] nirvart] amnf nir vartyā to accomplish, to do | gram. qualifies an object | karman | created by action.
nirvah [nisvah₁] v. [1] pr. (nirvahati) pp. (nirūdha) to lead out of, to save from (abl.); to flow out of (abl.) | to accomplish; to succeed, to overcome
obstacles | survive by (i.) | be up to the task — ca. (nirvāhayati) accomplish, fulfill. te svakarma sādhu niravahayanācaran they fulfilled their task well.

nirvahana [act. nirvah] n. completion, ac completion | bed. [theatre] denouement or catastrophe of a drama; syn. upasamhrti | retrospective account by the actor of the origin of his character | mod. management.
nirvahni [nisvahni] amnf smokeless; cf. nirdhūma.
nirvā [nisvā₂] v. [2] pr. (nirvāti) pp. (nirvāta) to cease breathing; to go out, to be extinguished | to be calmed, to be comforted.
nirvācya₁ [nisvācya] amnf nirvācyā ["that which should not be spoken of in slander"] irreproachable | that which should not be spoken of.
nirvācya₁ [pfp. [1] ca. nirvac] amnf nirvācyā to be explained, to be specified.

nirvāṇa [agt. nirvā] amnf nirvāṇī extinguished, dead, gone; appeased — act. n. extinction, disappearance, rest, dissolution, annihilation phil. ["extinction of the fire of passions"] liberation; cf. mokṣa | bd. state of final liberation; final emancipation; beatitude, supreme bliss || pali nibbāna. nirvāṇam kṛ reduce to nothing. nirvāņatīkā [tīkā] f. lit. np. of the nirvāņatīkā, commentary by Bhāskarakantha on the nirvāņaprakaraņa.
nirvāṇadaśaka [daśaka] m. bed. n.p. of nirvāṇadaśaka; cf. Cidānandadaśaślokī.
nirvāṇadīkṣā [dīkṣā] f. soc. initiation rite of śaiva Tantricism.
nirvāṇaprakaraṇa [prakaraṇa] n. bed. n.p. from nirvāṇaprakaraṇa, 6th section of Mokṣopāya; cf. Nirvāņatīkā.
Nirvāṇasūtra [sūtra] n. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of nirvānasūtra; cf. Mahāparinirvānasūtra.
nirvāpa [act. nirvap] m. act of spreading; sprinkling | soc. offering (not. to an ancestor).
nirvāpaṇa [act. ca. nirvap] n. act of spreading, dispersing, sowing | offering. kartavyāni duḥkhitaiḥ duḥkhanirvāpaṇāni the afflicted must relieve themselves of their suffering.
nirvārāṇasi [nisvārāṇasī] amnf who left Benares.
nirvāri [nisvāri] amnf without water, arid.
nirvārideśa | deśa | mr. country without water.
nirvāha [act. nirvah] m. accomplishment, completion; perseverance; subsistence | evacuation.
nirvāhaka [agt. nirvah] amnf nirvāhikā that performs, that accomplishes — f. nirvāhikā med. diarrhea.
nirvāhakaikya [aikya] n. phil. [Nyāya] coherence of termination of two adjacent sections.

nirvikalpa [nisvikalpa] amnf nirvi kalpā undifferentiated; non-conceptual | which admits no alternative; indisputable | phil. [yoga] qualifies samādhi where identification with the object occurs by losing consciousness of its identity; opp. savikalpa phil. [NN.] refers to a perception that does not conceptualize its object. nirvikalpam adv. without a doubt.
nirvikalpaka [ka] amnf nirvikalpakā phil. evident, indisputable — n. [nirvikalpakajñāna] phil. knowledge not based on perception [phil. [Nyāya] non-discriminating knowledge; opp. savikalpaka.
nirvikāra [nisvikāra] amnf nirvikārā unchanged; uniform; normal.
nirvighna [nisvighna] amnf nirvighnā which is not hindered; without obstacle. nirvighnam adv. without obstruction.
nirvicāra [nisvicāra] amnf nirvicārā without reflection, without hesitation (opp. savicāra). nirvicāram adv. without reflection, in a thoughtless manner.
nirviṇṇa [pp. nirvid] amnf nirviṇṇā discouraged; pained, depressed; disgusted (with (abl. ig loc. iic.).

nirvitarka [nisvitarka] amnf nirvitarkā irrational, without reflection | phil. [yoga] qualifies the second stage of samādhi, where the yogi directly feels the object of his meditation, without recourse to thought.
nirvid [nisvid₂] v. [2] pr. r. (nirvitte) pp. (nirvinna) to get rid of, to give up, to throw away (g. acc. | to be depressed; to be sick of (abl. i.); to despair.
nirvinoda [nisvinoda] amnf nirvinodā without entertainment; who is bored.
Nirvindhyā [nisVindhya] f. geo. name of the Nirvindhyā river "originating from the Vindhya mountains".
nirvibhakti [nisvibhakti] f. gram. absence of flexion.
nirvibhaktika [ka] ifc. amnf nirvibhaktikā gram. which does not carry flexion.
nirviś [nisviś₁] v. [6] pr. (nirviśati) pp. (nirvista) to enter into, to penetrate into (acc. loc.) to settle in, to become master of a house to take pleasure in (acc.).

nirviśeṣa [nisviśeṣa] amnf nirviśeṣā not different; which makes no difference — ifc. not different from, identical to (iic.) — n. absence of distinction, identity. nirviśesam var. nirviśesena adv. without distinction, indifferently; just as (iic.).
nirviśesatva [tva] n. identity.
nirviśeṣaṇa [nisviśeṣaṇa] amnf nirviśeṣaṇā without attributes.
nirviṣa [nisviṣa] amnf nirviṣā without poi sound.
nirviṣaya [nisviṣaya] amnf nirviṣayā detached from pleasures | gram. which does not admit an object, intransitive (verb); opp. savisaya; syn. akar maka.
nirvīrya [nisvīrya] amnf nirvīryā not manly, impotent; cowardly, weak — m. effeminate, weak, cowardly.
nirvīryatā [tā] f. weakening, exhaustion; im. power. nirvīryatām i. to become powerless.
nirvṛ [nisvṛ₁] v. [5] pr. (nirvṛṇóti) pr. r. (nrivṛṇuté) pp. (nirvṛta) to deliver.

nirvṛt [nisvṛt₁] v. [1] pr. r. (nirvartate) pp. (nirvṛtta) to occur, to take place; to be accomplished, to be completed; to stop — ca. (nirvartayati) to accomplish; to stop, to end. yad gatvā na nivartante once gone there, there is no going back.
nirvṛta [pp. nirvṛ] amnf nirvṛtā calm, peaceful; content, satisfied; ceased, finished. aham nirvṛtaḥ I am at ease.
nirvṛti [act. nirvṛ] f. pleasure, contentment, happiness; serenity, beatitude | phil. [Somānanda] the force | śakti | of aesthetic pleasure | extinction, ac fulfillment.
nirvṛtta [pp. nirvṛt] amnf nirvṛttā developed, become, accomplished, made, ready — ifc. which comes from (iic.). kuśāmbena nirvṛttā nagarī a city built by Kuśāmba.
nirvṛtti [act. nirvṛt] f. provenance; development, accomplishment, completion.

nirvedá [act. nirvid] m. indifference; detachment from the world; renunciation | phil. [aesthetics] absence of passion | repulsion, disgust (of (loc. g. iic.)); depressive state | self-deprecation, shame. nirvedam āyāt phil. [MO.] Manage to detach yourself from the world!
nirveśa [act. nirviś] m. access, installation; the act of taking pleasure.
nirvaira [nisvaira] amnf nirvairā non hostile, friendly — n. absence of animosity (reverse (i.⟩).
nirvyāja [nirvyāja] amnf nirvyājā that does not deceive; honest. nirvyājam without deceit.

nirvyājatā [tā] f. honesty, rectitude. a nirvyūḍha [pp. nirvyūh] amnf nirvyūḍhā dismissed, rejected | executed, finished, accomplished | justified, defended. nirvyūdhaste'patyasnehah your parental affection has been fully defended.
nirvyūh [nisvyūh] v. [1] pr. (nirvyūhati) pp. (nirvyūdha) to set aside, to dismiss from (abl.) | to arrange in battle order.
nirvyūha [act. nirvyūh] m. gate, barrier.
nirvraṇa [nirvraṇa] amnf nirvraṇā without injury, without wound; restored.
nirhan [nishan₁] v. [2] pr. (nirhanti) to pull out, remove (tooth, eye); destroy — ca. (nirghātayati) id.
nirharaṇa [act. nirhṛ] n. extraction; evacuation; expulsion; destruction; transport of corpse.
nirharaṇīya [pfp. [2] nirhṛ] amnf nirharaṇīyā which must be extracted or evacuated.
nirhāra [act. nirhṛ] m. booty | evacuation (excrement); transport (corpse) | deduction | penetrating odor.
nirhārin [agt. nirhr] amnf nirhārinī diffusing (odor) | that comes and goes | rich.

nirhṛ [nishṛ₁] v. [1] pr. (nirharati) pp. (nirhrta) to carry away; to pull, to extract (from (abl.)); to remove, to destroy | to export (goods); to transport (corpse) | to bleed; to evacuate; to purge — pr. r. (nirha rate) to exclude or deliver from (abl.); to get rid of; to change (clothing).
nirhrād [nishrād] ca. (nirhrādayati) to make noise; to beat (drum).
nirhrāda [act. nirhrād] m. noise, tumult; rumbling (thunder).
nirhrādin [agt. nirhrād] amnf ni rhrādinī noisy, deafening.
nilambita [nilambita] amnf nilambitā detached; removed from (i. iic.).
nilaya [act. nilī] m. stay; abode, residence; refuge.
nilayana [act. nilī] n. act of settling, of settling | hiding place.
nilāya [act. nilī] m. refuge.
nilāyin [agt. nilī] amnf nilāyinī who settles, who takes refuge (in (iic. loc.)).
nilī [nilī] v. [4] pr. r. (nilīyate) pp. (nilīna) pf. (sam) to take refuge, to crouch, to hide.
nilīna [pp. nilī] amnf nilīnā carpet, hidden; under the shelter of (i.) | applied; devoted to, immersed in loc. .
nivac [nivac] aor. [2] (nyavocat) dire.
nivacana₁ [nivacana] n. absence or obstruction of speech. nivacane adv. in silence; without speech. nivacanekr to act in silence.
nivácana₁ [act. nivac] n. speech; salutation, address | turn of phrase; saying, proverb.
nivát [nivat] f. hollow, valley; opp. udvat. nivatā adv. down; down.
nivap [nivap₂] v. [1] pr. (nivapati) pp. (ni vapta) to overturn, to spread; to scatter | to offer a libation to the shades; to scatter ashes.
nivartaka [agt. nivṛt] amnf nivartikā who returns, who turns back; who retreats, who flees who abolishes, who suppresses who stops, who abstains from.
nivartana [act. nivṛt] n. return; about-turn; retreat, flight | impediment, suppression; act of abstaining from (abl.) | inactivity | measure of land area (approx. 1 ha).
nivaśa [nivaśa] amnf nivaśā weak, without will, who is not in control of himself.
nivas₁ [nivas₁] v. [1] pr. (nivasati) pp. (nivasita₁) to inhabit, to stay, to live, to choose as residence | to cease inhabiting — ca. (nivāsayati) ex pulser (de (abl.)); banish.
nivas₂ [nivas₂] v. [2] pr. r. (nivaste) pp. (ni vasita) to dress — ca. (nivāsayati) to put on.
nivasita₁ [pp. nivas₂] amnf nivasitā expelled, banished.
nivasita₁ [pp. nivas₂] amnf nivasitā dressed in (i.).
nivah [nivah₁] v. [1] pr. (nivahati) to lead down; to bring to (dat. loc.) | to flow | to transport — ca. (nivāhayati) to set in motion.
nivaha [agt. nivah] amnf nivahā which brings — m. multitude, quantity | myth. np. of Ni vaha, one of the 7 celestial Winds.
nivāta [nivāta] amnf nivātā sheltered from the wind, calm.

nivātakavaca [kavaca] m. myth. ["whose armor protects from the wind"] category of titans [asura] com fighting the gods; the capital of the nivātakavacās is the rich Manimatī, object of the covetousness of Rāvaņa who fought them for centuries, before Brahmā reconciled them.
nivāpa [act. nivap] m. sown field | soc. libation of water to the manes | soc. scattering of ashes.
nivāra [agt. nivṛ] amnf nivārā that which restrains, that which represses, that which keeps at a distance.
nivāraka [agt. nivṛ] amnf nivārikā defender (of (iic.)).
nivāraṇa [act. nivṛ] n. suppression, removal; impediment; disturbance.
nivārita [pp. ca. nivṛ] amnf nivāritā prevented, held back, excluded.
nivārya [pfp. [1] nivṛ] amnf nivāryā to prevent, to ward off.
nivāsa 1 [act. nivas₂ 1] m. the act of dwelling | dwelling, residence, place of stay; night stop, refuge. nivāsatah adv. by its origin.
nivāsa₂ [agt. nivas₂] ifc. amnf nivāsā dressed in (iic.).
nivāsin [agt. nivas₂] amnf nivāsinī inhabitant.
nivāhá [act. nivah] m. act of leading downwards.

nivid₁ [nivid₁] v. [2] pr. (nivetti) v. [1] pr. (nivédati) pp. (nividita) pf. (vi) to say, announce— ca. (nivedayati) pp. (nivedita) inf. (nivedayitum) to say, announce, make known, communicate; inform (dat.) | to offer, present (not. request, complaint). ātmānam nivid to present oneself, to offer oneself. doșam nivid to impute the fault to (dat.). tasmai nivedayāmāsa he informed him. rājakule rājñe nyavedayat he filed a complaint with the royal court.
nivid₂ [act. nivid₁] f. instruction; information | soc. form of liturgical invocation.

niviś [niviś₁] v. [6] pr. r. (niviśate) pp. (niviṣṭa) ppr. ps. (niviśamāna) pf. (abhi, vi, sam) to halt, camp; to settle; to establish a home | to concentrate, to be attentive to — ca. (niviśyati) pp. (niveśita) to deposit, leave in a place; to bring, to transfer; to entrust to (loc.) | to introduce, to install; to make sit or lie down. sa punarapi svakārye mano nyaveśayat He applied himself again to his task.
niviśamāna [ppr. p.s. niviś] amnf niviśamānā while resting.

niviṣṭā [pp. niviś] amnf niviṣṭā installed; fixed, placed; located (city); assigned (guard); deposited occupied, colonized, cultivated (country) | put into service, inaugurated (city, reservoir) | seated (on (loc. iic.)).
nivīta [nivīta₂] amnf nivītā worn around the neck — n. worn as a necklace, not. of the sacred cord this cord; syn. upavīta.
nivṛ [nivṛ₁] ca. (nivārayati) pp. (nivārita) to hold back, repress, set aside.

nivṛt [nivṛt₁] v. [1] pr. r. (nivartate) pp. (nivṛtta) pf. (prati, vi, sam) to return, to come back from (abl.) to (acc.); to retrace one's steps, to go back, to return home | to revive, to be reborn, to become again | to cease, to disappear, to withdraw; to fail, not to exist, not to occur. na cedānīm ācāryāh sūtrāņi kṛtvā nivartayanti gram. [Paspaśā] But the masters do not go back on the rules once they are composed.

nivṛtta [pp. nivṛt] amnf nivṛttā re returned to (acc.) | disappeared, gone away; past, over, ceased; set (sun) | indifferent; who has renounced (abl. iic.); rid of, deprived of (abl.); withdrawn from the world; disinterested (act).
nivṛttamāṃsa [māṃsa] amnf nivṛttamāṃsā who has renounced meat.

nivṛtti [act. nivṛt] f. cessation, disappearance; abandonment, abstinence; abstention from (abl.) detachment; rest, inactivity, contemplation phil. withdrawal from the world, contemplative path; opp. pravṛtti | phil. [śaivasiddhānta] aspect of the bindu as associated with SadāśivaSadyojāta | myth. np. of Nivṛtti "Contemplation", personifying the energy of the mind or the Mind at rest, wife of Manas, mother of Viveka.

nivedana [agt. nivid₁] amnf nivedanī who announces, who proclaims — act. n. proclamation, publication; information, communication | offer; dedication; preface — f. nivedanā lit. foreword. ātmanivedana is the act of presenting oneself.
nivedayitvā [nivedayitvā] ind. having presented.
nivedita [pp. ca. nivid₁] amnf niveditā divulged, announced; published, communicated | presented; offered.
nivedin [agt. nivid₁] amnf nivedinī who knows, informed of (iic.) | who informs, who communicates.
nivedya [pfp. [1] nivid₁] amnf nivedyā which must be announced; which must be offered — n. soc. food offered to an idol — abs. ind. having offered.
niveśa [act. niviś] m. act of entering; settlement; encampment, stopover; dwelling, residence. niveśam kṛ to settle.
niveśana [act. niviś] n. installation; encampment; shelter, hiding place, lair | dwelling, house, residence; living room | settlement (of a country).
niveśita [pp. ca. niviś] amnf niveśitā introduced, placed in or on, installed; located at (iic.).
niveśin [agt. niviś] amnf niveśinī which rests on; based on.
nivyadh [nivyadh] v. [4] pr. (nividhyati) pp. (nividdha) to strike, to hit (with an arrow); per cer.
niś [related to nakta] f. [except noun. acc. voc. niśā₂] night. niśi adv. of night. aharniśam adv. day and night. niśi niśi adv. every night.
niśam [niśam₂] ca. (niśāmayati) pp. (niśāmita) abs. (niśamya) pf. (anu) to perceive, to tend to; to learn, to hear said; to convince oneself of.
niśamana [act. niśam] n. perception; listening.
niśamaya [agt. niśam] amnf niśamayā who perceives | who comes into contact with (iic.).
niśā₂ ₁ [ niś ] f. night; dream — n. niśa ifc. id. niśāyām adv. in the night.
niśā₂ [niśā] v. [4] pr. (nisyati) pp. (nisita, niśāta) to sharpen.

niśākara | kara₁ | m. the moon | "that makes the night" | ; cf. divākara | myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] niśākara; his hermitage was in the Vindhya mountains; he took in Sampāti, who had burned his wings to protect Jaṭāyu from the heat of the Sun.
niśācara | cara | m. ghost, specter; night monster, night prowler.
niśāniśam | red. | adv. every night.
niśānta₂ | anta| mn | "end of the night" | dawn.
niśāprāṇeśvara [prāṇeśvara] m. moon | "husband of the night" |.
niśāta [pp. niśā₂] amnf niśātā sharpened.
niśāna [act. niśā₂] n. act of sharpening; stimu lation; observation, perception.
niśānta₂ [niśānta] amnf niśāntā calm, tranquil usual, traditional — n. dwelling, but sound; harem.
niśāma [niśāma] m. observation; perception.
niśāmana [niśāmana] n. id.
niśāmya [abs. ca. niśam] ind. having learned, having heard.
niśita [pp. niśā₂] amnf niśitā sharp, cutting; sharp | excited, eager for (loc.).
niśītha [niśī₁] mn midnight | (time) night. niśīthe at midnight.
niśumbh [niśumbh] v. [1] pr. (niśumbhati) to crush.
niśumbha [act. niśumbh] m. destruction, murder | myth. [Devīmāhātmya] np. of the asura niśumbha "Murderer", son of Gaveṣṭhī, killed with his brother Sumbha by Kālī emerging from the front of Durgā.

niścaya [act. niści] m. investigation; firm opinion, conviction; certainty | resolution, decision; ruling, sentence | phil. [Nyāya] certainty, tautology. niścayena var. niścayāt adv. certainly. iti niścayah here is the decision. iti me niścayah this is my conviction. niścayam kr to settle one's opinion, to make a decision. niścayam jñā to assess the certainty of, to convince oneself of. niścayah nāsti it is not certain. kṛtaniścayaḥ determined to (dat. loc. inf. iic.). tasmāduttistha kaunteya yuddhāya krtaniścayah [BhG.] Thus arise, son of Kuntī, firmly resolved to fight.
niścayaka [agt. niści] amnf niścayikā that determines, that decides; decisive.
niścayakatva |tva| n. quality of decision-maker.

niścayin [agt. niści] amnf niścayinī of firm resolve. নিশ্বং niścar [niscar] v. [1] pr. (niścarati) to advance, to come out of, to appear — ca. (niścārayati) to bring out, to make appear. নিস্থল niścala [niscala] amnf niścalā immobile, immutable, unshakeable; imperishable.

niści [nisci] v. [5] pr. (niścinóti) pr. r. (niścinuté) pp. (niścita) abs. (niścitya) pf. (vi) to check, to reflect on, to convince oneself of; to consider as certain | to settle one's opinion, to determine, to decide, to conclude.
niścita [pp. niści] amnf niścitā convinced, determined; resolved, decided to (dat. loc.) | established, certain — n. certainty, decision. niścitam adv. certainly, surely, decidedly, without a doubt.
niścitārtha | artha | amnf niścitārthā who has convinced himself of, who has made a decision about loc. .
niścitya [abs. niści] ind. having ascertained, having formed his opinion; having made his decision; with the conviction or certainty (that someone (acc.), of something i.).
niścinta [niscintā] amnf niścintā without worries | carefree, indifferent; who does not think.
niścintatā [tā] f. indifference, indifference.
niśchidra [nischidra] amnf niśchidrā without tear, without gap; without opening; without hole, without defect.
niśvas [niśvas₁] v. [2] pr. (niśvasiti) pp. (niśvasita) to breathe in; to sigh; to grunt, to hiss. dīrgham niśvasya with a deep sigh.
niśvasita [pp. niśvas] n. inspiration; breathing.
niśvāsa [act. niśvas] m. inspiration; respiration; sigh.
niśvāsatattvasamhitā [tattvasamhitā] f. bed. n.p. from the niśvāsatattvasamhitā, ancient tantra (7th century) of the mantramārga śaivasiddhānta.
niśvāsamukhatattvasamhitā [mukhatattva samhitā] f. lit. np. of the Niśvāsamukhatattva samhitā, introductory chapter of the Niśvāsatattva samhitā.
niśśreyasa [nisśreyas] n. absolutely pro pice.

niṣakta [pp. niṣañj] amnf niṣaktā hung, attached, bound, fixed to (loc. iic.). tad eva saktah saha karmanaiti lingam mano yatra nişaktam asya [BU.] The man of desire goes, by virtue of his actions, to the goal to which his mind has attached itself. নিষ্ট্ন niṣaṅga [act. niṣañj] m. attachment; the act of binding | quiver.
niṣaṅgathi [niṣaṅga] amnf that embraces — m. embrace | chariot shaft; quiver.
niṣañj [nisañj] aor. r. [4] (nyasakta) pp. (niṣakta) to hang; fix, bind.
niṣaṇṇa [pp. niṣad₁] amnf niṣaṇṇā seated; lying down | soc. (sattra) performed seated. gaur niṣaṇṇā the cow is lying down.
niṣád₁ [nisad₁] v. [1] pr. (niṣīdati) pft. (niṣasāda) pp. (niṣaṇṇa) pf. (sam) to sit, to be seated | to stretch out, to lie down, to rest.
nisad₂ [agt. nisad₁] amnf seated quietly; seated near (not. altar) | lit. said of a style of composition.
niṣada [act. niṣad₁] m. musical note; cf. Niṣāda.
niṣadvará [niṣad₁vara] amnf niṣadvarā seated; resting; seated near (not. altar) — f. niṣadvarī the restful night.

Niṣadha m. geo. country of northwest India | myth. [Mah.] np. of King Niṣadha, title of Vīrasena, king of the Niṣadha country; also his son Nala | pl. np. of the Niṣadhās people, dark-skinned mountain tribes — f. niṣadhā myth. [Mah.] np. of niṣadhā, capital of King Nala.

nisādá [agt. nisad₁] m. Vedic non-Aryan native | soc. member of a tribe of wild hunters | hunter; man fallen from his caste; thief; man hardened in sin (such as the hunter who killed the male of a pair of birds in the Ram.); cf. Ekalavya, Guha₁, Vena; syn. bhilla | pl myth. [Mah.] fishermen of an island, given as food to Garuda by his mother Kadrū | (mus.) 7th note of the Indian octave — f. niṣādī soc. tribal woman. mā Niṣāda pratiṣṭhām tvam agamaḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ | yat krauñcamithunād ekam avadhīḥ kāmamohitam | [Rām.] Fi, Niṣāda, you will have no rest for all eternity, you who killed one of these two herons, while they were led astray by their amorous passion.
niṣādin [agt. niṣad₁] amnf niṣādinī who sits on, who rests on — m. elephant driver.
niṣikta [pp. niṣic] amnf niṣiktā watered, infused, irrigated.
niṣic [nisic] v. [6] pr. (niṣiñcati) pft. (niṣiṣeca) pp. (niṣikta) to sprinkle; to pour into; to irrigate; to soak in — ca. (niṣecayati) to rig; to wet, to impregnate.
niṣiddha [pp. niṣidh] amnf niṣiddhā res restricted, forbidden, prohibited; forbidden (of (inf.)). nişiddhākṣarī [akṣarī] f. soc. ordeal of
memorization [avadhāna] where one must construct a poem without using certain letters.

nisidh [nisidh₂] v. [1] pr. (nisedhati) pp. (nișiddha) to repel, to keep away; to prevent from (abl.) surpassing — ca. (niṣedhayati) to prohibit, to forbid. tat ko nu khalvevam nisidhyate So who could it be that is being prevented from entering?
niṣūd [nisūd] ca. (niṣūdayati) pp. (niṣūdita) to kill, to destroy.
niṣūda [act. niṣūd] m. destruction; murder.
niṣūdaka [agt. niṣūd] ifc. amnf niṣūdikā killer of (iic.).
niṣūdana [agt. niṣūd] mf niṣūdanī ifc. iic killer. — act. n. destruction of iic. . keśiniṣūdanaḥ myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa “who killed the demon Keśī”.
niṣūdita [pp. niṣūd] amnf niṣūditā killed, massacred; destroyed. śūlāyām niṣūdita impaled.
niṣeka [act. niṣic] m. watering; infusion; as persion; dripping | soc. seminal infusion, impregnation | washing water, rinsing.
niṣektavya [pfp. [3] niṣic] amnf niṣektavyā (loc.) that needs to be watered.
niṣecana [act. niṣic] n. act of pouring, watering, sprinkling.

niṣedha [act. niṣidh] m. prohibition, inter diction; contradiction, negation; exception | phil. [Mīmāmsā] injunction of prohibition, prohibition | gram. negation (with particle na); exception, in terdiction; opp. vidhi.
niṣedharthavāda [arthavāda] m. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] discourse with a negative purpose; opp. stutyarthavāda.
niṣedhana [act. niṣidh] n. prohibition, interdict.
niṣedhya [pfp. [1] niṣidh] amnf niṣedhyā to prohibit, to forbid.
niṣev [nisev] v. [1] pr. r. (niṣevate) pp. (nișevita) to frequent, to inhabit; to seek, to visit | to serve, to honor, to devote oneself to; to cultivate | to follow, to practice, to execute.
niṣeva [agt. niṣev] amnf niṣevā who practices, exercises, observes (iic.) — act. f. nisevā exercise, practice, service | employment, utilization tion | adoration, worship.
niṣevaka [agt. niṣev] amnf niṣevikā who practices, who exercises, who observes, who appreciates (iic.).
niṣevaṇa [act. niṣev] n. visit, attendance; practice, performance: use, employment; devotion.
niṣevita [pp. niṣev] amnf niṣevitā visitation, frequented; busy; practical; observed; served, honored, obeyed. নিষ্ক niṣká mn gold coin; gold ornament; gold. নিষ্কাতক niṣkaṇṭaka [niskaṇṭaka] amnf
niṣkaṇṭakā ["without thorn"] safely, without troubles |lit. without difficulties.
niṣkampa [niskampa] amnf niṣkampā who does not tremble; who acts with certainty | immobile; immutable.

niṣkarman [niṣkarman] n. phil. cessation of acts. নিষ্কর্ষ niṣkarṣa [act. niṣkṛṣ] m. extraction | essence; extract; summary; main point — n. the act of burdening one's subjects with taxes. niṣkarṣāt adv. principally concerning (ii.). esa tava vacaso niskarsah this is the essence of your speech.
niṣkarṣaṇa [act. niṣkṛṣ] n. extraction; under traction.
niskalmasa [niskalmasa] amnf niskalmaṣā without impurity; without defilement; pure.
niṣkas [niskas] ca. (niṣkāsayati) to send back, expel; exile.
niṣkāñcana [niskāñcana] amnf niskāñcanā devoid of gold.
niṣkāma [niskāma] amnf niṣkāmā disinterested, without desire — m. phil. state of suppression of desires.
niṣkāmakarman [karman] n. phil. disinterested act.

niṣkāraṇa [niskāraṇa] amnf niṣkāraṇā without reason; without necessity | disinterested. niṣkāraṇam var. niṣkāraṇāt adv. without motive; in a disinterested manner. nişkāraņo bandhuh disinterested friend.
niṣkāsa [act. That. niṣkas] m. exit.
niṣkāsita [pp. ca. niṣkas] m. expelled | placed, deposed; assigned.
niskimcana [niskimcana] amnf niskimcanā who has nothing; poor. নিজ্কুত niṣkuṭa [niṣkuṭa] m. garden or field outside the house | harem.

niṣkuṣ [niskuṣ] v. [9] pr. (niṣkuṣṇāti) pp. (niskusita) to extract; to tear out, to slash. নিজ্ক niskr [niskr₁] v. [8] pr. (niskaroti) pr. r. (niskurute) pp. (niskrta) to extract; to remove, to undo | to prepare.
niskrt var. nikrt [niskrt₁] v. [6] pr. (niskṛntati) pp. (niskṛtta) to cut, slice, recut, divide.
niṣkṛtá [pp. niṣkṛ] amnf niṣkṛtā sup prize; dispatched; banished; expiated | phil. reviewed, revised — n. expiation; revision.
níṣkṛti [act. niṣkṛ] f. suppression; act of avoiding, neglecting | acquittal; expiation; res toration, healing | complete development (fetus).
niṣkṛpa [niskṛpa] amnf niṣkṛpā merciless, cruel.
niṣkṛṣ [niskṛṣ] v. [6] pr. (niṣkṛṣati) pp. (niskṛṣṭa) to extract, to pull. নিজ্ঞ niṣkṛṣṭa [pp. niṣkṛṣ] amnf niṣkṛṣṭā ex trait.
niṣkram [niṣkram] v. [1] pr. (niṣkrāmati) pp. (niṣkrānta) abs. (niṣkramya) to go out, to leave, to go away. naitāvatā pīḍāṃ niṣkrāmati evil does not stop there.
niṣkrama [act. niṣkram] m. exit; departure from (abl.) | soc. first outing of a 4-month-old infant to see the Sun | soc. degradation (class); inferiority (tribal).
niṣkramaṇa [act. niṣkram] n. exit; departure of abl. | soc. first outing of a 4-month-old infant to see the Sun | soc. degradation (class); inferiority (tribal).
niṣkriya [niskriyā] amnf niṣkriyā inac tif | soc. who neglects his religious duties, non prati quant — n. phil. the Supreme Being ["absolutely im passible".
niṣkriyatā [tā] f. inactivity — ifc. neglect of (iic.).
niskriyatva [tva] n. id.
niṣkrī [niṣkrī₁] v. [9] pr. (niṣkrīṇāti) pr. r. (niṣkrīnīte) pp. (niṣkrīta) to redeem; to redeem oneself; to reimburse; to ransom.
niṣṭap [nistap] v. [1] pr. (niṣṭapati) pp. (niṣṭapta) to burn, to heat; to roast, to fry.
nistarkya [nistarkya] amnf nistarkyā ved. that which lets itself be undone.

Niṣṭigrī f. Vedic np. of Niṣṭigrī, mother of Indra. নিষ্ম níṣṭya [nistya] amnf niṣṭyā foreigner — m. soc. man of low caste; barbarian; cf. candāla, mleccha. ਜਿਲ niṣṭha [agt. niṣṭhā₁] ifc. amnf niṣṭhā₁ situated on, resting on (loc. 11th century) | relating to, concerning; dependent on (11th century); given to, absorbed in (11th century) | leading to, producing (dat.) | phil. |NN.| relating to, residing in (i.e.) (specifies the source of a relation, correlative with nirūpita). Rāmaniṣṭhaputratvanirūpitapitṛtvavān

Daśarathaḥ [NN.] Daśaratha possesses the quality of father, determined by the quality of son residing in Rāma. নিষ্ঠা niṣṭhā₁ [nisthā₁] pp. (niṣṭhita) pf. (pari) to emit, to produce. নিষ্ঠা niṣṭhā₁ [f. niṣṭha] f. state, condition; absorption into (loc.) | certainty, perfected knowledge, faith in (loc.) | conclusion, culmination; completion, end | gram. refers to verbal adjectival suffixes (ta or tavat) indicating the completion of the action | lit. (theater) denouement.
niṣṭhāvat [vat] amnf niṣṭhāvatī completed, full, consummated; perfect | religious.
niṣṭhāśūnya [śūnya] amnf niṣṭhāśūnyā in stable; inconstant; uncertain, indecisive. manah niṣṭhāśūnyam bhramati the mind wanders in the absence of purpose.
niṣṭhita [pp. niṣṭhā₁] amnf niṣṭhitā by done, accomplished | gifted at, expert in, champion of (loc.) | firm, fixed; certain, determined.
niṣṭhīv [niṣṭhīv] v. [1] pr. (niṣṭhīvati) pp. (niṣṭhīvita) to spit, expectorate; ejaculate.
niṣṭhīvana [act. niṣṭhīv] n. sputum, saliva.
niṣṭhura [niṣṭhā₁] amnf niṣṭhurā hard, rough; coarse; severe; cruel (not. words).
niṣṭhurabhāṣin [bhāṣin] amnf niṣṭhurabhāṣiṇī who speaks harshly.
niṣṭhuramānasa [mānasa] afmn nisthuramānasī cruel.
niṣṇā [nisnā] v. [2] pr. (niṣṇāti) pp. (niṣṇāta) to be plunged or absorbed in (loc.).
niṣṇāta [pp. niṣṇā] amnf niṣṇātā versed in, skilled, experienced, learned in (loc. iic.).
nispat [nispat₁] v. [1] pr. (nispatati) pp. (nispatita) to fly from, to arise from, to fall from (abl.) — ca. (nispātayati) pp. (nispātita) to make fall.
niṣpatita [pp. niṣpat] amnf niṣpatitā flown away, fallen.
nispatti [act. nispad] f. completion; generation, production | gram. derivation (not. from a root |dhātu|).

niṣpad [nispad₁] v. [4] pr. r. (niṣpadyate) pp. (nispanna) pf. (pari) to come out, appear, occur; to be born, to originate from (abl.) | to ripen — ca. (niṣpādayati) ca. r. (nispādayate) to accomplish, perform, do. rājyam nispādayati he reigns.
nispanda [nisspanda] amnf nispandā immobile; syn. nihspanda.
niṣpanna [pp. niṣpad] amnf niṣpannā appeared, emerged (from (abl. i.)) | gram. derived from (abl.) effected; accomplished; finished; ready.
niṣpāṇḍitya [nispāṇḍitya] amnf nispāndityā ignorant; uneducated.
nispādaka [agt. ca. nispad] amnf nispādikā that accomplishes, that develops; effective— act. f. niṣpādikā production. padaniṣpādikā gram. production of inflected words.
nispādana [act. ca. nispad] n. production; cause, effect.
nispādakatva [tva] n. effectiveness.

nispis [nispis] v. [7] pr. (nispinásti) pp. (nispista) to crush, grind; to hit; to beat (the laundry) — ca. (nispesayati) pp. (nispesita) to grind, to reduce to powder. karam karena nispis to rub one's hands together. svacaranau nispis to stomp one's feet. roṣāt daṃtairdantānniṣpiṣya while grinding one's teeth in rage.
nisprapañca [nisprapañca] amnf nisprapañcā without development, not manifested;
fictional | of pure essence || Pali Nippapañca.

niṣprayojana [nisprayojana] amnf nisprayojanā without motive; impartial, indifferent | harmless | without purpose, useless, unnecessary. nisprayojanam uselessly; without necessity. নিষ্পল nisphala [nisphala] amnf nisphalā without fruit, without profit, barren.
niṣyand [nisyand] v. [1] pr. r. (niṣyandate) to drip; to trickle into (loc.).
nisyanda [act. nisyand] m. flow, seepage.
nis var. nir, niś, niṣ, niḥ pf. beyond, outwards, outside of, disappearance | deprived of, lacking, without.

nisarga [nisarga] m. evacuation; defecation abandonment; gift, reward | natural condition, innate nature. nisargena var. nisargāt naturally, spontaneously. nisargatas adv. by nature; naturally; spontaneously. nisargaramaṇīyam vapuḥ a naturally graceful body. striyo hi nāma khalvetāh nisargādeva panditāh | puruṣāṇāṃ tu pāṇḍityaṃ śāstrair evopadiśyate || [Mṛcchakaṭikā] Women, in fact, are instructed by nature, while men must acquire knowledge through study.
nistāra [nistāra] m. crossing; rescue; liberation | payment, repayment, release from a debt.
nístejas [nistejas] amnf without energy, without passion; weak; sad.

nistraiguņya [nistraiguņya] amnf nistraigunyā phil. outside the realm of nature. traigunyavisayā vedā nistraigunyo bhavārjuna nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | natural qualities; transcends this realm, Arjuna, outside of duality, firm in truth, indifferent to material goods, master of yourself.
nisneha [nissneha] amnf nisnehā without affection.
nihata [pp. nihan] amnf nihatā launched; touched | wounded, shot down; killed, annihilated; disappeared | phon. without accent; syn. anudātta.
nihatakantaka [kantaka] amnf nihatakantakā whose thorns have been removed.
nihatāri [ari] amnf who eliminates his enemies.
nihatya [abs. nihan] ind. having killed, having struck down.
nihan [nihan₁] v. [2] pr. (nihanti) pp. (ni hata) abs. (nihatya) pf. (pra, vi) to strike, to knock down; to kill, to destroy.
nihantṛ [agt. nihan] amnf nihantrī that kills, that destroys — m. murderer, destroyer | myth. epith. of Shiva.
nihākā f. storm, tornado | bio. Ganges alligator.
nihita [pp. nidhā] amnf nihitā placed, deposited, fixed; given, entrusted.

√ nī₁ [related to nī₃] v. [1] pr. (nayati) fut. (neṣyati) pft. (nināya) aor. [4] (anaiṣīt) pp. (nīta) ppr. (nayat) pfp. (neya) abs. (nītvā, nīya) inf. (netum) pf. (anu, apa, abhi, ā, ut, upa, nis, pari, pra, prati, vi, sam) to lead, to conduct | to bring someone. (acc.) (to (acc.)) | to carry, to bring, to take away, to lead | to bring to completion, to accomplish; to pass (the time) | (acc. abstract noun) to do (causal sense) — ps. (nīyate) to be led — ca. (nāyayati) ps. (nāyyate) to cause to be led, to cause to be led (by (i.)) — des. (ninīṣati) des. r. (ninīṣate) to desire to lead — in tens. r. (nenīyáte) to bring by force. kriyām nī to perform a rite. daṇḍaṃ nī to punish, to exercise authority. duḥkhaṃ nī to cause pain. paritoṣam nī to satisfy, to please. prasādam nī to make favorable. bhasmasān nī to reduce to ashes. vaśam nī to subdue. śamaṃ nī to appease. kālam nī to spend one's time (at (inf. loc.)). samatām nī to share equitably.
nī₂ [agt. nī₁] ifc. mf who guides, who leads, who directs (iic.).
nī₃ [nii] v. [2] pr. (nyeti) pfp. (nyāyya) to enter into.
nī₄ iic. ni.
nī var. ṇī form of the sf
nīca [niac] amnf nīcā low, insignificant; inferior; vile, petty, wicked | short (hair, nails).
nīcakula | kula | n. soc. inferior race.
nīcatā |tā| f. inferiority; condition of servant. nīcatayā yā to squat.
nīcatva |tva| n. inferiority; condition of servant.
nīcavat |vat| adv. like a slave.
nīcais [i. pl. nīca] adv. down, down,
below | modestly | in a low voice; in a serious tone.
nīḍá mn shelter; nest || lat. nidus; eng. nest; fr. nest.
nīdaka |ka| mn bird's nest.
nīḍája [ja] m. [“born from a nest”] bird.
nīḍin [in] m. ["having a nest"] bird.
nīta [pp. nī₁] amnf nītā led, brought; taken away, carried off.
nītārtha [artha] amnf nītārthā ["whose meaning is certain" | evident; established; definitive.

nīti [act. nī₁] f. guidance, conduct; education wisdom, common sense behavior; natural disposition | usage, custom; method, manner | level of language, manner of speaking; style of diction or writing | ethics, morals; politics, government | brass; bell bronze | oxidation of a metal; rust.
Nītikalpataru | kalpataru| m. lit. np. of the Nītikalpataru, didactic work of Vyāsadāsa Ksemendra (11th century).
nītijña [jña] amnf nītijñā well-mannered.
Nītitattvāvirbhāva [tattvaāvirbhāva] m. bed. n.p. of Cidānanda's Nītitattvāvirbhāva.
nītimat [mat] amnf nītimatī wise, prudent; wise, sagacious.
nītivarman [varman] m. hist. np. of the poet Nītivarmā; he lived in the East of India, around the 7th century; he is the author of the Kīcakavadha.
nītivākya | vākya | n. pl. words of wisdom.
Nītivākyāmṛta [amṛta] n. bed. n.p. from the Nītivākyāmrta, a work of political morality by Somadeva₁ Sūri.
nītividyā [vidyā] f. savoirvivre.
Nītiśataka [śataka] n. lit. np. from the Nītiśataka, a collection of 100 poems on the morality of Bhartrhari₁.
nītiśāstra [śāstra] n. lit. treatise on politics, etiquette or morality; cf. Pañcatantra, Hito padeśa.
nītiśāstrajña |jña| amnf nītiśāstrajñā competent in politics.

Nītisāra [sāra] mn lit. np. of Kāmandakīya Nītisāra "Essence of Government", work of nītiśāstra due to Kāmandaki, expounding in verse the doctrines of the Arthaśāstra of his master Cāṇakya, for the use of the education of princes.
nītha [related to nīta] m. guide; leader.
nīdhra n. front roof.
nīpa amnf nīpā located at the bottom — m. region at the foot of the mountain, piedmont | organic. bot. Nauclea cadamba; cf. kadamba.
nīm forms adverbials of circumstance.
nīma m. cf. nimba.
nīmāya [aya] m. hist. np. of nīmāya, epith. of Caitanya "born under a neem tree".
nīya [pfp. [1] nī₁] amnf nīyā to lead, to take, etc.
nīra [nī₁ra] n. ["that which carries"] water — f. Nīrā geo. np. of the Nīrā river in Mahārāṣṭra.

nīrakṣīraviveka [kṣīraviveka] m. phil. power to separate milk from water (that is, to discern truth from falsehood); it is embodied by the haṃsa. nīrakṣīravivekam ca haṃso vetti na ca aparaḥ |GP.| Only the sacred swan knows how to separate milk from water.
nīrakta [nisrakta] amnf nīraktā colorless; whose colors have faded.
nīraja [nisrajas] amnf nīrajā without dust | phil. freed from passions | nīrajas id.
nīrasa [nisrasa] amnf nīrasā insipid.
nīrāga [nisrāga] amnf nīrāgā which is without passion.
nīrāj [nisrāj₁] ca. (nīrājayati) to illuminate, to radiate | soc. to perform the rite nīrājana (on (acc.)).

nīrājana [act. nīrāj] nf nīrājanā soc. ceremony of lubrication of weapons by a king before a battle; consecration of a horse, of an elephant soc. rite of worship of a deity by illumination with a camphor lamp. kvosto kvaca ... nīrājanā what is the relationship between a camel and the lubrication of weapons? (none); this maxim is used when two mentioned notions have no relation to each other.
nīruj [nisruj₂] amnf well, in good health.
nīroga [nisroga] amnf nīrogā bien por tant, en bonne santé.

nīla amnf nīlā f. blue nīlī; dark in color; indigo complexion; midnight blue, purple or black — m. sapphire | myth. n.p. from the demonelephant [gajāsura] nīla “the Black”; he attacked Siva and was destroyed by Gaņeśa — f. nīlā bio. bot. Indigofera tinctoria, in digo — f. nīlī id. —n. nīla dark color; obscurity | organic. bot. Nymphæa nelumbo or blue lotus; syn. utpala | dark substance; indigo, etc. — v. |11| pr. (nīlāyati) v. [11] pr. r. (nīlāyate) become midnight blue or black; blacken | lat. Niger; fr. lilac.

Nīlakaṇṭha [kaṇṭha] amnf nīlakaṇṭhī who has a blue throat — m. peacock; blue jay | myth. n.p. of Nīlakantha "blue throat", epith. of Siva, whose throat turned black after he drank the poi son Halāhala from the churning of the sea of milk [kṣīrodamathana] | hist. n.p. from Nīlakaṇṭha₁, surname of the poet Bhavabhūti hist. n.p. of the scholar Nīlakaṇṭha₂ Dīkṣita (17th century), grandnephew of Appayya Dīkṣita; He is the author of the Paribhāṣāvṛtti, the Kaliviḍambana, and the Anyāpadeśaśataka; he was a minister to the king of Madu rai Thirumalai Nāyaka | hist. np. of the mathematician and astronomer Nīlakantha₃ Somayājī, author of the Tantrasamgraha (1445–1545) | hist. np. of the brah mane Nīlakantha₄ Caturdhara, a Maratha scholar established in Benares (2nd half of the 17th century); he is credited with the Bhāratabhāvadīpa, an influent commentary on the Mah. and the origin of its vulgate edition; he is also the author of numerous other works, notably in the style of mantrarahasyaprakāśikā hist. np. of the jurist Nīlakantha₅ Bhatta (17th century), grandson of Nārāyaṇa₃ Bhaṭṭa, author of the Vyavahāramayūkha | hist. np. of the yajurvedin Nīlakantha₆ Gārgya born in Kontayūr in Kerala, author of the Niruktaślokavārttika (before the 14th century) | hist. np. of Nīlakaṇṭha₇, author of the Mātaṃgalīlā (Kerala) | geo. np. of Nīlakantha₈, summit of the Garhwal range of the Himālaya at 6596 altitude, overlooking Badarīnātha.
nīlakuñcitamūrdhaja | kuñcitamūrdhaja | amnf nīlakuñcitamūrdhajī who has black, curly hair.
Nīlagiri | giri | m. myth. np. of the hill of Nīlagiri, in Purușottamakșetra, sacred to Nīlamādhava; in its center stretched an immense abon tree
dance [kalpavṛkṣa]; the Rohinīkunda liberation fountain was located there; King Indradyumna founded the city of Purī | geo. np. of the Blue Mountains Nīlagiri₁, south of the Western Ghats.

Nīlamani [maṇi] m. sapphire | geo. np. of the Nīlamani, an 89-carat pear-shaped blue diamond adorning the crown of the jyotirlinga of the sanctuary of Tryam bakeśvara since at least 1500; it was confiscated as spoils of the Maratha wars by the East India Company in 1818, recut and sold in London.
Nīlamata [mata] n. lit. np. of the Nīlamata purāṇa; earlier than Kalhana, it describes the ancient history of Kaśmīra and the legends that form the basis of its culture.
Nīlamādhava [mādhava] m. myth. n.p. of Nīlamādhava, epith. of Kṛṣṇa “blue descendant of Madhu”. nīlavarņa [varņa] m. blue.
nīlavarṇatva [tva] n. quality of being blue.

nīlasukhādi [sukhaādi] m. phil. [Tantra] category of felt experiences, including external perceptions or experiences (such as the perception of blue) and internal sensations or experiences (such as pleasure).
nīlānga |anga₁| mr. organic. zoo. Boselaphus tragoca melus, nilgai or blue antelope; cf. gokarna.
Nīlācala [acala] m. geo. np. of Nīlācala "Blue Mountain", ancient name of a hill near the seaside in Orissa, on which the temple of Jagannātha was built; mod. Purī.
nīlācalakhaṇḍa |khaṇḍa| min reads. n.p. of the Nīlācalakhaṇḍa, one of the supplements [pariśiṣṭa] of the Skandapurāṇa, dealing with JagannāthaPurī.

nīlāñjana [añjana] n. ointment Black — f. nīlāñjanā var. nīlājanā geo. np. of the river nīlāñjanā, which joins the Mohanā to form the Phalgu near Gayā in Bihāra; [Buddhacarita] it was on its banks that the future Buddha practiced his penances with five ascetic companions before leaving them and renouncing asceticism; he accepted a meal from Sujātā, and went to meditate under the tree where he experienced Enlightenment [bodhitaru] || pali neranjanā.
Nīlāñjanagiri [giri] m. myth. np. of Nīlāñjanagiri, epith. of Sani "Like a mountain of black ointment".
nīlāṇḍa |aṇḍa| m. bio. antelope (hariṇa) "with blue tusks".
nīlotpala | utpala | n. organic. bot. Nymphæa cærulea, blue lotus (which opens at moonrise) — amnf nīlotpalā (pond) covered with blue lotuses.
nīvāra [nī₄vāra] m. bot. Hygroryza ari stata, wild rice; floating aquatic grass, medicinal | pl. nīvārās grains of wild rice.
nīvī [nivyā] f. loincloth, skirt made from a piece of fabric tied in front | var. nīvi id.
nlhāra [nl₄hāra₁] m. fog — v. [11] pr. r. (nīhārāyate) to make fog.
√ nu₁ v. [2] pr. (nauti) pp. (nuta) pf. (pra) to praise, to acclaim.

nu₂ part. of emphasis of sentences | now; then | isn't it? certainly, undoubtedly, definitely | lat. nunc; all. nun; ang. now. katham nu how so? kim nu what so? why so? na nu isn't it? isn't it true that? definitely. nu ... nu or ... or.
primary form, a. in the sense of habitual agent.
nuti [act. nu₁] f. praise, homage.
nutta var. nunna [pp. nud] amnf nuttā pushed, sent, chased.
√ nud v. [6] pr. (nudati) pp. (nutta, nunna) pf. (apa, pra, nis, vi) to push, excite, hasten | to repel, reject — ca. (nodayati) to excite, stimulate — des. (nunutsati) to want to reject.
nud₁ |agt. nud| ifc. amnf that repels, that suppresses (iic.); that remedies (iic.).
nunuts [des. nud] v. pr. (nunutsati) to want to reject.
nunutsu [agt. of the. nud] amnf nunutsū who desires to incite or reject. নুস nunna |pp. nud| amnf nunnā cf. nutta.
nū [nu₂u] ind. now; then.
nūtana [tana] amnf nūtanī new, new calf; present, recent; fresh, young — v. [11] pr. (nūtanayati) renew.
nūtanatva [tva] n. novelty.
nūtanavarṣa [varṣa] m. New Year.
nūtna [contr. nūtana] amnf nūtnī new, new; present, recent; fresh, young.
nūnam [nū] adv. probably, surely; really, indeed | now, henceforth | therefore. kadā nūnam when then? kva nūnam where then?

nūpura m. ankle ring, periscelide. nr [related to nara] m. [sg. nom. nā; other cases cf. nara; pl. g. nṛṇām nṛṇām man, male; hero | gram. masculine noun. eko nā viṃśati strīṇām snānārtham sarayūm gatāḥ | vimśati pratiyātāḥ caiko vyāghrena bhakṣitaḥ || [prahelikā] A man and twenty women (not nineteen women) went to bathe in the Sarayū; twenty (women) returned and one (the man) was eaten by the tiger.

Nrga [ga₁] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the Yādava king Nrga; by mistake he gave a Brahmin a cow belonging to another Brahmin; when he tried to take it back, he was cursed to be reborn as a chameleon; having fallen into a well, he was rescued by Kṛṣṇa and regained human form. nrgah krkalāsatām agamat lit. [VAD.] Nrga became a chameleon.
nṛnamana | namana | amnf nṛnamanā np. "that which makes men bow down".
nrpa [pa₂] m. prince, king ["protector of men" | the king in chess [caturangā]; syn. rājan.
nrpatva [tva] n. royalty; royal state. nrpati var. narapati [pati] m. prince, king | "master of men". nrpaśu paśu m. bestial man.
nṛmāṃsa [māṃsá] n. human flesh.
nṛmāṃsāśana |aśana₂| n. cannibalism.
nrmná [mna] n. virility.
nryajña [yajña] m. soc. ved. the sacrifice to men, or welcoming of guests, one of the five ma rites
players [mahāyajña]; cf. manuṣyayajña.
nrvarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Bhūmyādikānda, dealing with man.
nrvīra [vīra] m. hero among men.
nṛśamsa [śaṃsa] amnf nṛśaṃsā [“who harms men” | cruel, wicked; vile, abject — m. executioner — n. criminal action.
nṛṣiṃha [siṃha] m. cf. narasiṃha.
nṛṣiṃhacaturdaśī [caturdaśī] f. soc. festival celebrating the appearance of Narasimha, on the 14th day of the clear fortnight of the month vaiśākha.
nṛṣiṃhanātha [nātha] m. geo. temple of Nṛṣiṃhanātha, in the West of Orissa, at the foot of the Gandhamardana Mountains, important place of pilgrimage.
nṛṣiṃhavrata |vrata| n. soc. vow of Narasiṃha, fast performed at nṛsiṃhacaturdaśī.
nṛṣiṃhāśrama [āśrama] m. hist. np. of the philosopher Nṛsiṃhāśrama (16th century); he criticized Madhva in his Bhedadhikkāra.

√ nrt v. [4] pr. (nrtyati) pft. (nanarta) pp. (nṛtta) pf. (ā, pra) to dance — ca. (nartáyati) to make dance — intens. (narīnartti) intens. r. (narīnṛtyate) to gambol — dés. (ninṛtsati) dés. (ninartișati) to want to dance.
nṛtu [agt. nṛt] m. dancer.

nṛttá [pp. nṛt] amnf nṛttā danced — agt. m. myth. np. of nṛtta, epith. of Śiva dancer; arch. it is one of the 16 aspects of Shiva — n. dance; theatre, pantomime | phil. cosmic dance of Shiva. mayūrasya nṛttam peacock dance.
nrttahasta | hasta | m. hand gesture in dance or theatre, with decorative effect; opp. mudrā.
nṛtya [pfp. [1] nṛt] amnf nṛtyā which must be danced — n. pantomime, recitation with mime; this art is combined with dance |nrtta| in the
drama | nātya|.
nṛtyaśāstra | śāstra | n. choreography.
nṛmṇá |nṛ| n. virility; power, strength, courage.
nej [ca. nij] v. [10] pr. (nejayati) to clean.
nejaka [agt. nij] m. cleaner, washer.
nejana [act. nij] n. cleaning.

nejameṣa [related to meṣa] m. myth. np. of nejameșa "Bogeyman", epith. of Viśākha, from the side of Skanda, a ram-headed creature; he is invoked for fertility, but he can also harm children as Skandagraha; cf. Naigamesa, Naigameya.
netavya [pfp. [3] nī₁] amnf netavyā that which must be led or guided; that which must be escorted back.

neti [naiti] adv. not so. netyāha gram. [MB.] it is not so, says (the master). neti neti phil. [Vedānta] Neither this nor that (this formula evokes the incommunicability of the Divine, which can only be characterized by denying that it has any particular property).
netī f. soc. [yoga] cleansing of the nasal passages (by a cloth which is brought out through the mouth).
netr [agt. nī₁] amnf netrī who leads, who guides — m. conductor, guide, leader.
netrtva [tva] n. aptitude for command; quality of guide.
netra [instr. nī₁] m. ifc. conductor, guide, leader — n. eye | math. symb. the number 2 | rope (used to turn the churn or the fire stick) | conduit, pipe.
netrakamala [kamala] m. lotus eye (symbol of beauty).
netrakośa [kośa] m. eyeball.
netratantra [tantra] n. bed. n.p. from the netratantra, a tantric text from the Kaśmīra from the beginning of the 9th century; it deals with witchcraft and demonology; Kṣemarāja commented on it.
Netrayoni [yoni] m. myth. np. of Netrayoni, epith. of Indra cursed to have to bear 1000 vagina marks on his body (later changed into 1000 eyes) after his adultery with Ahalyā; cf. his hasrākṣa.
netrotpāṭana [utpāṭana] n. act of tearing out the eyes.
nédiṣṭha [super. antika] amnf nediṣṭhā nearest; very near. nedistham adv. then; first. nedisthāt adv. in the vicinity.
nédīyas [compar. antika] amnf nedīyasī closer, very close — adv. near; right here.
nedya [pfp. [1] nind] amnf nedyā to blame.

nepathya n. (theatre) ornament, decoration, stage equipment; actor's attire, costume | backstage (separated from the stage [ranga] by a curtain); wings — f. nepathyā ifc. costume of (iic.). nepathye (theatre) backstage. nepathyam kr var. nepathyam grah to disguise oneself, to costume oneself.
nepathyagṛha [gṛha] n. toilet room, dressing room.
nepathyaprayoga [prayoga] m. the art of grooming [nepathyaprayoga], one of the 64 arts [kalā].
nepathyabhrt [bhrt] amnf costumed. udāranepathyabhṛt magnificently dressed.
nepāla m. geo. n.p. from nepāla or Nepal — f. Nepālī the Nepālī language.
nema amnf nemā one; several — iic. half — m. myth. np. of the ṛṣi Nema Bhārgava, author of a hymn of the Rigveda | portion; limit, border.
nemí [nam] f. wheel rim; circumference; edge.
Neminātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of Neminātha "Master of the wheel (of fortune)", 22nd mythical tīrthankara; his body is dark red, his symbol is a marine conch; he is also called Aristanemi.
nemināthacarita [carita] n. bed. n.p. from Ne mināthacarita "Legend of Neminātha", work in apabhramśa by Haribhadra.
nemināthapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. from the Ne mināthapurāna, a collection of Jain tradition.
neya [pfp. [1] nī₁] amnf neyā to lead, to guide | to control; to put in the state of, to subject to (acc.) | to remove; to lead to (loc); to pass (time).
neyārtha [artha] amnf neyārthā phil. whose meaning is to be established; which must be interpreted; opp. ābhiprāyika | whose meaning can only be guessed.
neṣṭā [noun. neṣṭṛ] iic.
nestodgātr [udgātr] m. du. nestodgātārau ved. the two priests nestr and udgātr.
neṣṭṛ [agt. nī₁] m. ved. one of the 3 priests seated at the adhvaryu in the vedic sacrifice; he guides the wife of the sacrificer and prepares the surā.
naika [naeka] amnf naikā not unique, mul tiple; numerous, varied.
naikadhā |dhā| adv. multiplely; in various ways.
naikṛtika [*nikṛtaika] amnf naikṛtikī dishonest; deceitful; false, base, vile.

naigama [*nigama] amnf naigamī rela tif au Veda et à son vocabulaire | lit. np. du Nai gama, section of the Nighantu dealing with homonyms — m. soc. interpreter of sacred tradition | means, expedient; prudent conduct | respectable citizen; wise man; bourgeois, merchant.
naigamakhanda [khanda] mn lit. section of 3 chapters of the Nirukta where Yāska glosses the naigama vocabulary.
Naigameya [īya] m. myth. n.p. of Naigameya "Interpreter of the sacred tradition", aspect and companion of Skanda; cf. naigamesa.
naigameṣa [*nejameṣa] m. myth. np. of Naigameșa "Bogeyman", aspect and companion of Skanda with a ram's head; he seizes children and harms them; cf. Nejameșa, Naigameya.
naighaṇṭuka [*Nighaṇṭuka] n. lit. np. from the Naighantuka, section of the Nighantu dealing with synonyms.
naija [*nija] amnf naijā which belongs to oneself.
naityaśabdika [*nityaśabdaika] amnf naityaśabdikā gram. who holds the tongue as existing from all eternity; opp. kāryaśabdika.
naipuṇá [*nipuṇa] ifc. amnf naipuṇā cf. nipuṇa — n. expertise; syn. naipuṇya.
naipuṇya [*nipuṇaya] n. skill, dexterity; excellence in (g. iic.) | art requiring skill; fullness, totality. naipunyena totally; exactly.
naimitta [*nimitta] amnf naimittā relating to signs — m. diviner ["who explains omens"].
naimittika [ika] amnf naimittikā determined, caused by; accidental, fortuitous, occasional (opp. ni tya) — n. effect — m. diviner.

naimiṣa [*nimiṣa] amnf naimiṣī temporary, momentary; instantaneous — n. myth. [Mah.] np. of the forest [araṇya] and the sacred ford [tīrtha] Naimișa; Ugraśravā Sauti₂ told the Mah. there to the sages [rsi] gathered by Saunaka; [BhP.] Ugraśravā recited the Bhāgavatapurāņa there, composed by Vyāsa at the request of Nārada for the benefit of bhakti; [VAP.] Prahlāda visited it after receiving Cyavana at the Pātāla; it is said that this forest is so named because an army of asurās was defeated there "in the blink of an eye" | geo. mod. Nimsar, on the banks of the Gomati River, in the district of Sitapur in Uttar Pradesh.
Naimiṣāranya [aranya] n. myth. n.p. of naimiṣāraṇya, the naimiṣa forest.
naiyāyika [*nyāyaika] m. phil. logician; follower or doctrinaire of nyāya; we distinguish between the old school [prācīna] and the new school [navya].
nairantarya [*nirantaraya] n. absence of interruption; continuity; compactness. nairantaryena in an uninterrupted manner; continuously.
nairātmya [*nirātmanya] n. bd. doctrine of the negation of the Self; syn. anātman — f. nairātmyā bd. [Tantra] cf. Prajñānairātmyā.
nairātmyavāda [vāda] m. bd. doctrine of the negation of the Self.
nairātmyavādin [vādin] amnf nairātmyavādinī bd. who teaches the doctrine of the negation of the Self.
nairāśya [*nirāśaya] n. indifference, absence of desire or hope; depression, despair.
nairukta [*Nirukta] amnf nairuktā etymological — m. etymologist.
nairṛta [*Nirṛtia] m. myth. [“from Nirṛti”] ogrevampire; syn. rākṣasa.
nairguṇya [*nirguṇaya] n. absence of qualities | absence of good qualities, mediocrity — amnf nairgunyā without connection with qualities.
nairmalya [*nirmalaya] n. impeccability; purity.
nairlajjya [*nirlajjaya] n. absence of shame; immodesty.
naiva [naeva] adv. not even.
naivedya [*nivedya] n. soc. offering of food to an idol.
naiśa [*niśā₁] amnf naiśī nocturnal — m. nocturnal wild animal.
naiśika [*niśā₁ika] amnf naiśikā noc turne — m. nocturnal wild animal.
naiṣadha [*niṣadha] amnf naiṣadhī geo. relating to the country or people niṣadha — m. lit. epith. of Nala, king of the country niṣadha | pl. geo. the people of the Naisadhās or Nisadhās.
naisadhacarita [carita] n. bed. n.p. from the mahākāvya Naisadhacarita of Sriharṣa, also called Naisadhīya; this is a variation of the beginning of Nala's story; cf. Pancanalīya.
Naiṣadhānanda [ānanda] n. bed. from np. Naiṣadhānanda, drama [nāṭaka] due to Kṣemīśvara.
Naiṣadhīya [īya] amnf naiṣadhīyā re relating to the country or the nisadha people — n. [Naiṣadhīyacarita] lit. n.p. from the mahākāvya Naisadhīya or Naisadhīyacarita of Śrīharsa; cf. Naisadhacarita.

naiṣkarmya [*niṣkarmanya] n. phil. non-action, freedom from action. naiskarmyasiddhi phil. perfection of liberation from action | lit. np. of the Naiskarmyasiddhi, a phil. advaita work by Sureśvara. naiṣkarmyasiddhim paramām
saṃnyāsenādhigacchati [BhG.] Through his renunciation he attains the supreme perfection of being freed from his actions.
naiṣkika [*niṣkaika] amnf naiṣkikā at the price of one coin [niṣka].
naiṣkṛtika [*niṣkṛtaika] amnf naiskrtikī cf. naikrtika.

naiṣṭhika [*niṣṭhaika] amnf naiṣṭhikī ter minal, definitive, firm; perfect, complete, superior — ifc. perfect connoisseur of (iic.) — m. soc. ["who makes his final vows"] Brahmanical student [brahmacarya] opting at the end of his studies for a life of renunciation; opp. upakurvāna.
naisthurya [*nisthuraya] harshness.
naisnehya [*nisnehaya] n. absence of affection.
no [nau] part. (pragṛhya) and no. no ced otherwise, so that not ... not. no vā or not.
nod [ca. nud] v. [10] pr. (nodayati) pp. (no dita) to incite, excite, stimulate — ps. (nodyate) to be incited, to be stimulated.
nodana [agt. nud] amnf nodanī that which repels, that which removes — act. n. incitement, impulse.
nodita [pp. ca. nud] amnf noditā incited, stimulated, excited.
nodin [agt. nud] amnf nodinī which grows back.
nodya [pfp. [1] nud] amnf nodyā that must be repelled | that must be incited.
nau₁ f. [acc. nāvam] boat, ship, barque — v. [11] pr. (nāvyati) to wish for a boat || gr. ; lat. navis; fr. nef, navire.
nau₁ cl. āvayos, āvābhyām, āvām.
naukā |ka| f. (small) boat, skiff | piece corresponding to the rook in chess [caturaigā]; sometimes rather ap pelée ratha | lit. name of comments.
naulika n. phil. [yoga] yogic penance — f. naulī id.
nyag iic. nyac.
nyagrodha | rodha₁ | m. bio. bot. Ficus indica, banyan tree ["that grows downwards"]; syn. vaṭa.
nyagrodhapādapa | pādapa₁ | mr. organic. id.
nyańku m. bio. zoo. type of antelope.
nyac [niac] amnf nīcī [m. nom. nyan; n. nom. nyak directed downwards. nyak adv. downwards, below.
nyañc [niañc] v. [1] pr. (nyañcati) pp. (niañcita) lean, hang — pr. r. (nyañcate) to bend down.
nyañcana [act. nyañc] n. curve, hollow | hiding place.
nyaya [act. nī₃] m. destruction, loss.
nyarbuda [niarbuda] n. math. one hundred million.

nyas [nias₂] v. [4] pr. (nyásyati) pp. (nyasta) pf. (upa, pari, vi, sam) to throw to the ground, drop; to place on, deposit | to throw towards, pour into (loc.) | to abandon; to renounce (acc.) | to entrust, leave. manasi nyas to reflect upon, weigh up. śirasi nyas ["to place on the head"] to receive with [3] reverence. pathi nyas to abandon.
nyasana |act. nyas| n. act of depositing, placing, arranging | act of mentioning.

nyasta |pp. nyas| amnf nyastā thrown, launched, placed; set, fixed, inserted | abandoned, to which one has renounced | exposed; put on display | subjected to a mystical imposition — iic. who has renounced (ifc.).
nyastaśastra [śastra₂] amnf nyastaśastrā ["who laid down arms"] opposed to conflict, non-violent, peaceful.

nyāyá |act. nī₃| m. |"original nature"| method, system, rule; plan, model; axiom, law | process; judgment; justice | phil. np. of Nyāya "Dialectic", one of the 6 points of view [saddarśana] of the orthodox philosophical tradition, founded by Akṣapāda Gautama, and based on logical analysis, reasoning and rhetoric; later, the new logic [Navyanyāya] develops a conceptual language that renews traditional logic [prācīnanyāya] | lit. popular maxim, moral drawn from a metaphorical story; custom; cf. ardhakukkuṭīnyāya, ustralagudanyāya, mātsyanyāya, tṛṇabhakṣaṇanyāya, daṇḍāpūpanyāya, andhaga janyāya, maṇḍūkaplutinyāya, rathakāranyāya, sthālīpulākanyāya, sūcikatāhanyāya, vṛddhakumārīvākyavaranyāya, bhūlinganyāya. eso 'tra nyāyaḥ is what is appropriate here.
nyāyákaṇikā [kaṇikā] f. lit. np. of the Nyāyakaṇikā "Seed of Logic", Commentary on the Vidhiviveka due to Vācaspati₁ Miśra.

nyāyákandalī [kandalī] f. lit. np. of the Nyāyakandalī "Flower of Logic", a philosophical work of theistic orientation of the Nyāya and Vaiśesika systems, due to Śrīdhara₁ Bhaṭṭa (991); it is a Commentary on the Padārthadharmasamgraha.
nyāyákalikā [kalikā] f. lit. np. of the Nyāyakalikā, work of Nyāya due to Jayanta₁ Bhatta, commentary on the Nyāyasāra.
nyāyakusumāñjali [kusumāñjali] m. phil. [Navyanyāya] np. from the nyāyakusumāñjali “Of France of Logic”, work by Udayanācārya; he defends the existence of God.
Nyāyakośa [kośa] m. bed. n.p. of the Nyāyakośa, dictionary of technical terms of Nyāya due to Bhīmācārya.
nyāyadarśana [darśana] n. phil. from the np. nyāyadarśana, philosophical point of view of the Nyāya system.
nyāyadharmakathā [dharmakathā₁] f. lit. 6ᵉ text of the jaina canon, series of apologues and sermons in verse.
nyāyanibandha [nibandha] m. bed. cf. Nyāyavārttikatātparyapariśuddhi.
Nyāyapariśuddhi [pariśuddhi] f. bed. n.p. from Nyāyapariśuddhi of Udayanācārya; cf. the Nyāyavārttikatātparyapariśuddhi.
Nyāyapraveśa [praveśa] m. lit. np. from the Nyāyapraveśa "Introduction to Logic", by Sankarasvāmī; it is sometimes attributed to Dinnāga.

nyāyabindu [bindu] n. bd. np. du nyāyabindu "Pearl of Reasoning", a work of logic by bd. Dharmakīrti; it develops the theory that names and relations are imposed by the intellect, while perception reveals the true nature of things; Dharmottara made a commentary on it [Nyāyabindutīkā].
nyāyabindutīkā [tīkā] f. bed. n.p. of the nyāyabinduṭīkā, Commentary on the nyāyabindu due to Dharmottara.
Nyāyabodhinī [bodhinī] f. bed. n.p. from the Nyāyabodhinī, Commentary on the Tarkasaṃgraha of Govardhana₂.

nyāyabhāsya [bhāsya] n. lit. np. of the Nyāyabhāsya, Vātsyāyana₂'s Commentary on the Nyāyasūtra; it reuses the paths of liberation of the Yoga system defined by Patañjali₂ but advocates their commitment to the service of true knowledge samyagdarśana.
nyāyabhūṣaṇa [bhūṣaṇa] n. lit. np. from the nyāyabhūṣaṇa "Commentary on Logic", due to Bhāsarvajña.
Nyāyamakaranda [makaranda] m. lit. np. from the Nyāyamakaranda "Nectar of Logic", Vedānta philosophical treatise by Anandabodha.
nyāyamañjarī [mañjarī] f. phil. np. of the nyāyamañjarī "Sheaf of Logic", a work of semantics by bd. Jayanta₁ Bhatta.
Nyāyamālāvistara [mālāvistara] m. bed. n.p. from Nyāyamālāvistara; cf. Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara.
nyāyamukha [mukha] n. bed. n.p. from the nyāyamukha of Dinnāga.
Nyāyarakṣāmaṇi [rakṣāmaṇi] m. lit. np. from the Nyāyarakṣāmaṇi "Jewel protector of reasoning", hermeneutic work by Appayya Dīkṣita.
Nyāyaratna [ratna] n. bed. n.p. from the Nyāyaratna of Manikantha₁ Miśra.
Nyāyaratnamālā [ratnamālā] f. bed. of np. the Nyāyaratnamālā, work of Mīmāmsā of Pārthasārathi₁ Miśra (13th century).
nyāyaratnākara [ratnākara] m. bed. n.p. from the nyāyaratnākara, work of mīmāṃsā of Pārthasārathi₁ Miśra (13th century).
Nyāyaratnāvalī [ratnāvalī] f. bed. n.p. of the Nyāyaratnāvalī, refutation of the advaita Vedānta of Sankara₁ by Vādirāja.
nyāyalīlāvatī [līlāvatī] f. bed. n.p. of the nyāyalīlāvatī, a work of logic by Vallabha₂; Mathurānātha made a comment [rahasya] on it.

nyāyávārttika |vārttika| n. lit. np. of the Nyāyavārttika or Nyāyasūtravārttika, work of the logician Uddyotakara; he comments on the Nyāyasūtra and justifies the Nyāyabhāsya of Vātsyāyana₂ against the criticism of Dinnaga.
nyāyavārttikatātparya [tātparya] iic. cf. following.
Nyāyavārttikatātparyaṭīkā [ṭīkā] f. bed. n.p. from the Nyāyavārttikatātparyaṭīkā of Vācaspati₁ Miśra; cf. Tātparyatīkā.

nyāyavārttikatātparyapariśuddhi [pariśuddhi] f. lit. np. of the nyāyavārttikatātparyapariśuddhi of Udayanācārya, unification of the Nyāya and Vedānta systems, also called Nyāyapariśuddhi or Ni bandha.
nyāyáśāstra | śāstra | n. phil. cognitive sciences.
nyāyásāra [sāra] m. bed. n.p. from the Nyāyasāra, short text of Nyāya due to the ācārya Bhāsarvajña; the Nyāyakalikā is a commentary on it.

nyāyasiddha [siddha₁] amnf nyāyasiddhā phil. logical, consistent with common sense | gram. says not. obvious meta-rules [paribhāṣā], not explicit in the Aṣṭādhyāyī; syn. yuktisiddha, lo kanyāyasiddha; opp. jñāpakasiddha.
nyāyásiddhānta [siddhānta] m. phil. teaching of logic.
nyāyásiddhāntajana [jana] n. bed. n.p. from the Nyāyasiddhāntajana of Vedāntadeśika.
nyāyásiddhāntadīpa [dīpa] m. lit. np. from the Nyāyasiddhāntadīpa logic treatise by Śaśadhara.
nyāyásiddhāntamañjarī [mañjarī] f. bed. n.p. from the Nyāyasiddhāntamañjarī, a work by Navyanyāya by Janakīnātha Cūdāmaņi.
nyāyásiddhāntamuktāvalī [muktāvalī] f. bed. n.p. of the Nyāyasiddhāntamuktāvalī or muktāvalī, work of Navyanyāya due to Viśvanātha₂ Pañcānana; it is a commentary on the Bhāṣāpariccheda.
Nyāyásudhā [sudhā] f. lit. np. of the Nyāyasudhā "Nectar of Logic", commentary exhaus
tif [tīkā] of the Anuvyākhyāna of Madhva due to Jayatīrtha, who received the title of Ţīkācārya lit. np. of the Nyāyasudhā₁, commentary of the Slokavārttika by Someśvara₄ Bhatta.
Nyāyasūcīnibandhana |sūcīnibandhana| n. bed. n.p. from the Nyāyasūcīnibandhana of Vācaspati₁ Miśra.

nyāyásūtra [sūtra] n. pl. nyāyasūtrāņi lit. np. of the Nyāyasūtra "Aphorisms of Logic", compiled between the 1st century BC and the 2nd century AD; tradition attributes its origin to Gotama₁; its principal commentaries are the Nyāyabhāsya of Vātsyāyana₂ and the Nyāyavārttika of Uddyotakara.
nyāyásūtrabhāsya [bhāsya] n. bed. n.p. of Nyāyasūtrabhāsya; cf. Nyāyabhāsya.
nyāyāmṛta [amṛta] n. lit. np. from nyāyāmṛta "Nectar of logic", a polemical dvaita work by Vyāsatīrtha; in it he attacks the advaita doctrine as unfounded.
nyāyālaya [ālaya] mn court.
Nyāyāvatāra [avatāra] m. lit. np. of the Nyāyāvatāra, a Jaina treatise on epistemology by Siddhasena Mahāmati (8th century).
Nyāyāvali |āvali| f. lit. np. of the Nyāyāvali, a modern collection of maxims and proverbs.
nyāyya [pfp. [1] nī₃] amnf nyāyyā regular, usual, correct, just; appropriate, suitable; legal | authorized to be (inf.); which is suitable for (i.) to be (inf.).
nyāyyatva [tva] n. adequacy, correctness; conformity to the law.

Nyāsa |act. nyas| m. act of placing, of putting; act of writing, of painting | placement, depositing; act of entrusting; submission | abandonment of, renunciation of (g.) | written text, literal, verbatim gram. position, formulation; content of a sūtra lit. commentary on the grammar of Benares [Kāśikā]; not. the Nyāsa of Jinendrabuddhi, also called Kāśikāvivaraṇapañjikā (8th century) | phil. [Tantra] ritual laying on of fingers on parts of the body, associated with a bījamantra; cf. aṅganyāsa, ka ranyāsa, hṛdayanyāsa.
nyāsavāda [vāda] m. cf. nikṣepavāda.

nyūna [niūna] amnf nyūnā inferior, defective; diminished | deprived of (i. iic.); inferior to (abl.) | vile; bad, wicked — n. [nyūnavaraka] phil. [Nyāya] lack of one of the 5 members of the syllogism [pañcāvayava]. nyūnam adv. less.
nyūnatā [tā] f. inferiority (to (abl.)).
nyūnatva [tva] n. inferiority (to (abl.)).
p Į5 Ч pa noted. the number 1; cf. kaṭapayādi.
pa₁ [agt. pā₁] ifc. mf pī who drinks (iic.) — act. mf pā acts of drinking (iic.). surāpaḥ var. śīdhupaḥ drinker of alcohol.

paka₁ | pa₁ ka | ifc. mf pakā who drinks (iic.).
paka₂ [pa₂ka] ifc. mf pakā which protects (iic.).

dish | cooked food | maturation; digestion; perfection.
