paktrima [pactrima] amnf paktrimā cooked to perfection; fully cooked. ча pakvá [pp. pac] amnf pakvā cooked; digested | ripe || hi. pakkā ; ang. pucka.
pakvānna | anna | n. cooked food — amnf pakvānnā (container) for cooking food.
pakvāśaya [āśaya] m. med. intestine.

pakṣá m. wing, feather | side, flank, shoulder | wing or side of a building, gable | faction, party; multitude, troop | point of view, alternative; opi nion, thesis; bias | partisan, adherent, sympathizer; follower | half | astr. half-moon, fortnight; cf. śukla, kṛṣṇa | phil. [Nyāya] hy pothesis; minor term of a syllogism | lit. one of the senses of an equivocation [śleṣa] | math. member of an equation. pakṣāntare in the other case, on the other hand. pakṣīkṛ to appropriate; to take a position. sandigdhasādhyavān pakṣaḥ phil. [Tarkasaṃgraha] The subject is what is conjectured from the predicate.
pakṣaka |ka| ifc. amnf pakṣakā which has the point of view (iic.).
pakṣatā |tā| f. the act of being partisan; adherence to a party | phil. adherence to an argument; defense of a thesis. pakṣatāṃ gam to take the side of (g.).
pakṣatva [tva] n. ifc. adherence to (iic.).
pakṣadvāra [dvāra] n. side door.
pakṣadhara [dhara] m. hist. np. of the logician Jayadeva₂ pakṣadhara of Mithilā (~1424~~1500); Raghunātha₁ Siromaṇi took him as his teacher, after a difficult start due to his insolence.

pakṣadharmatā [dharmatā] f. phil. [Nyāya] The inherent nature of the subject of a predication, showing that the subject verifies the predicate. hetoh pakṣavṛttitvam pakṣadharmatā phil. [Tarkasamgraha] The inherent nature of the subject is the presence of the cause in that subject. vyāptivišistapakṣadharmatā jñānam parāmaršaḥ phil. [Tarkasaṃgraha] Inference is the knowledge of the inherent nature of the subject qualified by inevitable concomitance.
pakṣapāta |pāta| m. partiality, bias | "fall to one side"] | wingbeat.
pakṣavacana | vacana | n. phil. | Nyāya | thesis.
pakṣaṣaṣṭhī [ṣaṣṭhī] f. myth. tantr. winged form of ŞaşthīSakunī.
pakṣāntara | antara | mr. alternative.
pakṣābhāsa |ābhāsa| m. phil. false thesis in a debate.
pakṣavat |pakṣavat| amnf pakṣavatī winged one who belongs to a party.
pákṣas |related to pakṣa| n. wing | side; riverbank | door frame | wing of an army | astr. period of a half-moon, fortnight.
pakşi iic. pakşin.
pakṣiyuddha | yuddha | m. cockfight.
pakṣin [pakṣain] amnf pakṣiṇī winged — ifc. supporter of (iic.) — m. bird — f. pakṣiṇī period of one night, the previous day, and the following day.
pakṣman | pakṣaman | n. | in comp. pakṣma | eyelash; hair | petal.

paksya [pakṣaya] amnf pakṣyā concerning wings | bimonthly | partisan (of (iic.)). পদ্ধ pánka mn mud, mire | paste, ointment | (figuratively) defilement. pańkaja [ja] n. bio. ["born of mud"] bot. Nelum bium speciosum, rose lotus; syn. kamala.
pankalagna [lagna] amnf pankalagnā em mudé.
pańke [loc. pańka] iic. pańkeja [ja] n. cf. pańkaja.

pankti [pancan] f. series of 5, group of 5, pentad | series, collection, group; rank, row (not. for sitting at a meal) | Vedic meter of 5 times 8 syllables | myth. np. of the horse Pankti, harnessed to Surya's chariot. sarpapankti knot of snakes. dantapankti row of teeth.
pangu amnf pangu lame; leg cripple — m. myth. np. of Pangu, epith. of Sani "who drags his leg". andhapangunyāya maxim of the blind and the paralytic.
panguka |ka| amnf pangukā lame.
pangutā [tā] f. lameness.
pangutva [tva] n. id.
pangupāda |pāda| mr. myth. epith. by Sani “boi teux”.

pañca iic. pañcan.

pañcaka [ka] amnf pañcikā consisting of 5 components, of symmetry 5 | of 5 days of age — m. collection of 5 objects — n. pentad, quincunx; category of 5 notions | lit. not. poem in 5 verses; part of a work in 5 chapters | soc. game with 5 dice (where the faces must be equal) | astr. unfavorable conjunction of 5 planets.
pañcakapāla | kapāla | amnf pañcakapālā offered in 5 bowls — m. soc. oblation thus offered.

pañcakarman [karman] n. med. [Ayurveda] the 5 treatments for purifying the body: emetic [vamana], purgative [virecana], sternutative [nasya], and laxative [vasti], with oil [anuvāsana], or with herbal decoction [nirūha].

pañcakṛtya [kṛtya] n. phil. the manifestation of the Supreme Being Shiva, in five activities: sṛṣṭi creation, sthiti preservation, samhāra destruction, tirobhāva illusion and anugraha karaṇa the power of grace or liberation.
pañcakṛtvas [kṛtvas] adv. 5 times.
pañcakola [kola] m. pl. med. the 5 spices: long pepper abies |pippalī|, its root |pippalīmūla|, wild pepper [cavya], red plumbago [citraka], dry ginger [ārdraka].
pañcakośa | kośa | m. pl. phil. the 5 envelopes of the soul; cf. kośa.
pañcakrama | krama | m. soc. way of reciting the Veda in 5 steps | bd. the "way in 5 steps", teaching of Nāgārjuna.
pañcakrośa [krośa] m. distance of 5 leagues (approximately 15 km) — f. pañcakrośī soc. country within a radius of 15 km around a sacred place | tīrtha|, not. at Vārāṇasī and at Oṃkāreśvara.
pañcagata [gata] amnf pañcagatā math. raised to the power of five.
pañcagava [gava] nf pañcagavī collection of 5 cows.
pañcagavya [gavya] n. the 5 products of the cow: milk [payas], curd [dadhan], butter [ghṛta], urine [gomūtra] and dung [gomaya].

pañcagauda [gauda] m. geo. the 5 peoples of North India: Gauda, Kanyakubja, Maithila, Utkala, and Vanga; |Sahyādrikhanda| this subdivision classifies the Brahmins north of the Vindhya Mountains; opp. pañcadrāvida. Ι7 brāhmanā daśadhā proktah pañcagaudaś ca
Drāvidāh [Skanda] It is said that there are 10 kinds of brahmins, 5 from the Gauda countries and 5 from the Drāvida countries.
pañcacatvāriṃśa [catvāriṃśa] amnf pañcacatvārimśī ord. 45ᵉ.
pañcacatvāriṃśat | catvāriṃśat | f. 45.
pañcacūḍā [cūḍā] f. lit. np. of pañcacūḍā, nymph |apsaras| who describes in the Umāsamhitā the bad nature of women.

Pañcajana [jana] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of the demon [asura] Pañcajana "Pentagenes", son of Samhrāda and Krti; he lived in the waters hidden in the conch Pāncajanya, and held captive the son of the sage Sāndīpani who had drowned at Prabhāsakṣetra; he was killed by Kṛṣṇa, who thus fulfilled his duties to his guru by resurrecting his son, with the assistance of Yama: he is the father of Asiknī; cf. Śańkhāsura | pl. pañcajanās myth. the 5 categories of humanoid beings: gods [devās],

Men [janās], celestial beings (nymphs [apsarasas] and centaurs [gandharvās]), dragons [nāgās], and ancestors [pitaras] | society: the 5 gents, made up of the 4 classes [caturvarna] to which are added the tri
leases |niṣāda|.
pañcajñāna [jñāna] m. bd. (buddha) who possesses the 5 knowledges.
pañcatattva [tattva] n. phil. [Sāṃkhya] the 5 gross elements [bhūtatattva] | [Tantra] cf. pañcamakāra.
pañcatattvāprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. np. from the Pañcatattvaprakāśa, a dictionary of synonyms of 400 stanzas by Venīdatta (1644).

pañcatantra [Tantra] n. lit. np. of the pañcatantra, "Five books" of instructive tales intended for princes [nītiśāstra]; attributed to Viṣṇuśarmā, it was composed before the 6th century; it comprises 5 parts: mitrabheda, mitraprāpti, kākolūkīya, labd hapranāśana and aparīkṣitakāritva; it was translated into Arabic in 750 under the name "Kalīla wa Dimna" (adaptation of the name of the jackals Karaṭaka and Damanaka); cf. Tantrākhyāyika, Pañcākhyāna, Hitopadeśa.
pancatantraka |ka| n. bed. id.
pañcatapas [tapas] n. soc. ["the 5 fires"] mortification device, consisting of 4 braziers arranged in a square (plus the burning sun) between which an ascetic exposes himself.
pañcataya |taya| amnf pañcatayī consisting of 5 parts; quintuple. pañcatayam adv. in 5 parts.
pañcatā |tā| f. collection of 5 entities; not. the 5 elements. pañcatāṃ gam var. pañcatāṃ yā | "return to the 5 elements"] die.
pañcatrimsá [trimsa] amnf pañcatrimsī ord. 35ᵉ | made up of 35 parts.
pañcatrimśat [trimśat] f. 35.
pañcatrimśati [trimśati] f. 35.

pañcatva [tva] n. state of being Five [phil. materiality (essence of the 5 material elements [pañcabhūta]). pañcatvam gam die ["return to the 5 elements"]. pañcatvam upagataḥ he died. pañcatvam nī kill.
pañcadaśa [daśa] amnf Pañcadaśī fifteenth — f. Pañcadaśī astr. 15th day of a half-moon, day of full or new moon.
pañcadaśavārṣika [vārṣika] amnf pañcadaśavārṣikī aged 15 years.
pañcadaśika [ika] amnf pañcadaśikā de lon gueur 15; au nombre de 15.
pañcadaśin |in| amnf pañcadaśinī consisting of 15 parts — m. lit. np. of the Pañcadaśī, work of advaita vedānta of Vidyāranya, in 3 parts of 5 chapters each [pañcaka].
páñcadaśan [daśan] num. pers. pl. fifteen.

pañcadevata [devatā] amnf pañcadevatā myth. relating to the 5 deities (Ganesa, Vishnu, Shiva, Parvati, Surya). pañcadevata mantra invocation of the 5 gods; cf. below. namaḥ gaṇe nārāyaṇe rudre ambike bhāskare Glory to Ganesha, Vishnu, Shiva, Parvati, Surya.

pañcadrāviḍa [Drāviḍa] m. geo. the Five Peoples of South India: Gurjara, Mahārāṣṭra, Tailaṅga, Karņāṭaka, and Drāviḍa; [Sahyādrikhaṇḍa] this subdivision classifies the Brahmins of the south of the Vindhya Mountains; opp. pañcagauda.
pañcadhā [dhā] adv. Five times; in five parts; in five ways.
pañcanakha | nakha | amnf pañcanakhā (ani mal) with 5 claws.
Pañcanada [nada] n. geo. np. of Pañcanada "land of the 5 rivers" (SatadruSutlej, Vipāśā Beās, IrāvatīRāvī, CandrabhāgāChenāb and Vi tastāJhelum); mod. Pañjāb.
Nala [pañcanala] m. pl. lit. Nala and the 4 gods who took on her appearance.
Pañcanalīya [īya] n. lit. np. from the Pañcanalīya "History of the Five Nala", episode of the Naisadhacarita in ślesa style.
pancanavata | navata | amnf pañcanavatī ord. 95^ e.
pañcanavati |navati| f. 95.
pañcanavatitama |tama| amnf pañcanavati tamī ord. 95°.

pañcapañcanakha | pañcanakha | m. pl. med. [Ayurveda] The five five-clawed animals that can be eaten: the hedgehog [śvāvidh], the porcupine |śalyaka|, the monitor lizard |godhā|, the hare |śaśa| and the tor
kills | kūrma |. pañcapañcanakhā bhakṣyāḥ (There are only) 5 ani 5-clawed evils that can be eaten.
pañcapañcāśa [pañcāśa] amnf pañcapañcāśī ord. 55ᵉ.
pañcapañcāśat [pañcāśat] f. 55.
pañcapañcāśattama [tama] amnf pañca pañcāśattamī ord. 55ᵉ.

pañcaparvan [parvan] n. astr. the 5 favorable conjunctions and the corresponding festival days: caturdaśī (with not. vaikunthacaturdaśī, festival of dīpāvali, and śivarātri); aṣṭamī (with not. jyaişthāstamī and janmāstamī); amāvāsyā the new moon; pūrnimā the full moon; and ravisamkrānti the entry of the sun into a sign of the zodiac (with not. makarasaṃkrānti, festival of the new year).
Pañcapādikā [pādikā] f. lit. np. of the exegesis Pañcapādikā of the commentary Brahmasūtra bhāṣya of Sankarācārya; its author is Padmapāda.
pañcapādī [padī] f. gram. form of non-compositional primary affixes [unādi] in 5 sections; opp. daśapādī.
pañcabāṇa |bāṇa| m. myth. np. of pañcabāṇa, epith. of Kāma "with the Five flower arrows".
pañcabhūta [bhūta] n. pl. pañcabhūtāni phil. [Sāṃkhya] set of the 5 material elements: ākāśa the Ether or Space, vāyu the Air, tejas the Fire, ap the Water and pṛthivī the Earth.
pañcabhūtamahālinga [mahālinga] m. soc. the 5 signs of Shiva associated with the 5 elements, and with 5 great manifestations of Shiva; cf. pañcabhūtasthala.

pañcabhūtasthala [sthala] n. geo. shrine of Shiva associated with one of the 5 elements: Ekāmreśvara at Kāncīpura for pṛthivī , Jambukeśvara at Tiruva naikka for āpas, Aruņācaleśvara at Tiruvannama lai for tejas, Kālahastīśvara near Tirupati for vāyu and CidambaraNatarāja at Cidambaram for ākāśa.
pañcamakāra [makāra] n. cf. makārapañcaka.

pañcamanuṣyavibhāga [manuṣyavibhāga] m. [BS.] division into 5 types of men for the canonical representation of the plastic arts [citra]: haṃsa, born under Jupiter, of height 96 inches |angula|, śaśa, born under Saturn, of height 99 inches, rucaka, born under Mars, of height 102 inches, bhadra, born under Mercury, of height 105 inches, and mālavya, born under Venus, of height 108 inches; there are other classifications.
pañcamūla |mūla| n. med. the 5 medicinal roots; cf. bṛhatpañcamūla, hras vapañcamūla.

pañcayuddha [yuddha] m. the 5 weapons of Viṣṇu: the mace [gadā], the sword [khadga], the conch [śaṅkha], the disk of Fire [cakra], and the bow [sāraṅga] | myth. n.p. from pañcayuddha, epith. of Kāma "with the Five Weapons" (his flower arrows).

Pañcaratna [ratna] n. lit. np. of the Pañcaratna "Five verses offered as jewels", devotional poem dedicated to Ganesa | collection of 5 episodes of the Mah.: Bhagavadgītā, Bhīṣmastavarāja, Viṣnusahasranāmastotra, Anusmrti and Gajendramoksana.
pañcaratha [ratha] m. arch. temple plan.

Pañcarātra [rātra] amnf pañcarātrā which lasts 5 nights — m. period of 5 nights; not. rite of the 5 nights | soc. Vaishnava tradition instituted by Rāmānuja | pl. pañcarātrās soc. ritual manuals of Vaishnava tradition; cf. Hayaśīrṣapañcarātra, Nāradapañcarātra; they are distinguished from those of the Vaikhānasa ascetic traditions — n. lit. np. of the Pañcarātra nāṭaka, play by Bhāsa taken from the Mahābhārata.
pañcarātrāgama [āgama] n. lit. collection [saṃhitā] of Vaishnava tradition fixing the observances of the cult.
pañcarātrin [in] amnf pañcarātriņī soc. member of the Vaisnava Pañcarātra community.

pañcalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. lit. the 5 subjects treated by the mythological collections [purāṇa]: sarga the creation of the Universe, pratisarga the secondary creations, vamsa the genealogy of the gods and sages, manvantara the creation of the human race and the first men, and vamśānucarita the genealogies and dynastic histories | collection of 5 signs — amnf pañcalakṣaṇī (work) which deals with the 5 philosophical subjects — f. pañcalakṣaṇī phil. not. work of logic [Nyāya], such as the Pañcalakṣaṇīsarvasva. kākacakṣur bakadhyāyī śvānanidras tathaiva ca | alpāhārī grhatyāgī vidyārthipañcalakṣaṇam At tentif like a crow, meditating like a heron, lacking sleep like a dog, content with little and having left his home, these are the five characteristics of a student.
pañcalakṣaṇīsarvasva [sarvasva] n. bed. n.p. from the pañcalakṣaṇīsarvasva, a work of logic [NN.] by Mathurānātha₁.
pañcavaktra [vaktra] amnf pañcavaktrā with 5 faces — m. myth. epith. of Shiva.
pañcavata [vata] m. soc. sacred cord of the brah manes, made up of 5 strands — f. pañcavațī the 5 sacred trees: the pipal |aśvattha|, the Bengal cognac [bilva], the banyan [vaṭa], the myro

bolan [dhātrī] and ashok [aśoka] | geo. np. of the Pañcavațī, forest of South India where the Godāvarī originates; myth. [Rām.] there was the hermitage of Agasti where Rāma stayed during his exile; it was in this forest that Lakshmana cut off the nose of Sūrpaṇakhā; cf. Nāsika.
pañcavarṣa | varṣa | amnf pañcavarṣā aged 5 years.
pañcavarṣaka [ka] amnf pañcavarṣakī aged 5 years. pañcavarṣakadeśīyaḥ approximately 5 years old.
pañcavarṣīya [varṣīya] amnf pañcavarṣīyā aged 5 years. pañcaviṃśa viṃśa amnf pañcaviṃśī ord. 25th made up of 25 parts.
pañcavimśabrāhmaṇa [brāhmaṇa] lit. n. Pañcaviṃśabrāhmaṇa, epith. of the np. Tāṇḍyabrāhmaṇa, ritual text in 25 books.
pañcavimśat [vimśat] num. f. twentyfive.
pañcavimśati [vimśati] num. f. twentyfive.
pañcavimśatika [ka] amnf pañcavimśatikā which consists of 25 parts.
Pañcavimśatisahasrikā [sahasraka] f. bd. n.p. from the Pañcavimśatisahasrikā Prajñāpāramitā “Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 formulas [sūtra]”.
pañcaviṣaya [viṣaya] m. pl. pañcaviṣayāḥ the five objects of the senses: śabda sound, sparśa touch, rūpa form, rasa taste and gandha smell.
pañcavīra [vīra] m. pl. myth. [Mah.] the 5 heroes of the vṛṣṇi clan: Vāsudeva/Kṛṣṇa, Saṃkarṣaṇa/Balarāma, Sāmba/Sāmba, Pra dyumna and Aniruddha.
pañcavrkṣa [vrkṣa] m. myth. the 5 trees of paradise Svarga of Indra: kalpavrkṣa, pārijātaka, mandāra, kalpavṛkṣasaṃtāna, haricandana.

pañcavrtti | vrtti | f. gram. mode of word formation; we distinguish: krt₂ (primary suffix) taddhita (secondary suffix) samāsa (compound) ekaśeṣa (dual or plural form) and sanādyanta (secondary conjugation).
pañcaśata [śata] n. 105 — amnf pañcaśatī pl. 500.
pañcaśataka [śataka] amnf Pañcaśatikā five hundredth — n. set of 500 stanzas — f. Pañcaśatikā bd. n.p. from the Pañcaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā, or Perfection of Wisdom in 500 stanzas.

pañcaśikha |śikhā| amnf pañcaśikhā who has five locks (not. religious hairstyle) — m. lion | myth. np. of pañcaśikha₁, musician of Indra | lit. [Mah.] np. of pañcaśikha, sage expert in Sāmkhya and Yoga; at the court of King Janaka, he is confronted by 100 masters [ācārya] whose doctrines he destroys; he professes a teaching contrary to reincarnation and the transmission of merits, close to the materialist points of view |lokāyata|.
pañcaśīla |śīla| n. bd. the 5 prohibitions of the bauddha doctrine: not to kill, not to steal, not to have illicit sexual relations, not to lie, not to intoxicate oneself.
pañcaśīlasamādhāna [samādhāna] n. bd. commitment to respect the 5 prohibitions.
pañcaṣa [ṣaṣ] amnf pañcaṣā pl. pañcaṣās in number of five or six.
pañcaṣaṣti [ṣaṣti] f. 65.

pañcasandhi [sandhi] m. lit. the 5 articulations of dramatic narratives; they combine a dramatic spring or means of action [arthaprakṛti] and a stage of development [kāryāvasthā]; they are called: mukha "in front" (seed of the plot), pratimukha "to face" (trial to overcome during the crescendo of the action, disruptive incident, epitasis), garbha "matrix" (climax, knot of the plot), avamarsa "contact" (dramatic turn of events), and upasamhṛti/nirvahaṇa "catastrophe" (resolution). nātakam khyātavṛttaṃ syāt pañcasandhisamanvitam It is postulated that dramatic narratives have 5 articulations.
pañcasaptata [saptata] amnf pañcasaptatī ord. 75ᵉ.
pancasaptati |saptati | f. 75.f.
pancasaptatitama |tama| amn pañcasaptatitamī ord. 75ᵉ.
pañcasaptan [saptan] num. pers. pl. 5×7 = 35.
pañcaskandha | skandha | m. bd. the 5 aggregates or constituent factors of the ego: material form [rūpa], sensation [vedanā], perception cog

nitive [samjñā₂], mental formation (emotion, thought, opinion, compulsion) [saṃskāra] and active awareness [vijñāna]; Buddha taught that one must free oneself from them, by realizing their emptiness — f. pañcaskandhī (collective) set of the 5 aggregates.
pañcastavī [stava] f. lit. np. of the pañcastavī, collection of hymns to Tripurasundarī (Kaśmīra, author and date unknown).
pañcahotṛ |hotṛ| m. pl. pañcahotāras ved. the 5 priests who sacrificed for whom? (classic question of a ritual riddle [brahmodya]).
pañcākṣara [akṣara] amnf pañcākṣarī formed of 5 syllables — f. pañcākṣarī soc. [śaiva] formula of worship of Siva om namaḥ śivāya.
pañcākhyāna [ākhyāna] n. lit. np. from the pañcākhyāna "Five stories"; cf. Pañcatantra.
pañcākhyānaka |ka| n. lit. np. of the pañcākhyānaka, version of the Pañcatantra com compiled in 1199 by Pūrņabhadra.

pañcāgni [agni] n. soc. the 5 sacred fires: anvāhāryapacanadakṣiṇa, gārhapatya, āhavanīya, sabhya and āvasathya — amnf soc. one who maintains the 5 fires | one who practices the penance of the 5 fires; syn. pañcatapas | phil. one who knows the doctrine of the 5 fires.
pañcāgnitapas | tapas | n. soc. penance of the 5 fires; syn. pañcatapas.

pañcānga | anga₁ | amnf pañcāngā consisting of 5 parts, in 5 stages — n. astr. almanac ["which deals with 5 subjects"]: solar days [vāra], lunar days [tithi], lunar stations [nakṣatrāṇi], astral conjunctions [yogās], and lunar periods [karaṇās]; cf. pañjī.
pañcānguli [anguli] amnf 5 fingers wide.
pañcāngulika [ka] m. right hand mark imprinted or engraved in the ground of a shrine.

pañcānana [ānana] amnf pañcānanī [“who has 5 faces”] fiery, passionate — m. myth. np. of pañcānana, fierce form of Shiva | lion — ifc. soc. form of scholarly titles; cf. Viśvanātha₂ — f. pañcānanī myth. epith. of Durgā.

pañcāyatana |āyatana| n. arch. temple plan with 5 sanctuaries in a quincunx; they are traditionally dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, Surya, Ganasha and AmbikāDurga | soc. domestic altar including these 5 deities, the principal one being in the center of the square formed by the other 4 | soc. ceremony using 5 symbols | soc. caste or village assembly, led by 5 notables (modern pañcāyat) || hi. pañcāyat.
pañcāyatanapūjā [pūjā] f. soc. daily domestic religious service offered on the altar pañcāyatana; cf. ṣaṇmata.
Pañcāyudha [āyudha] m. myth. np. of Pañcāyudha, epith. of Kāma "of the Five weapons"; syn. pañcabāṇa.

pañcārāmakṣetra [ārāmakṣetra] n. pl. geo. the 5 garden sanctuaries in the land of Andhra; cf. Amarārāma, Dakṣārāma, Somārāma, Kṣīrārāma, and Kumārārāma; myth. the asura Tāraka possessed a linga which gave him omnipotence; Kumāra broke it into 5 pieces, which fell to Earth at the 5 sanctuaries, and were established as śivalinga by respectively Indra, Sūrya, Candra, Visnu and Kumāra.

pañcāvayava [avayava] m. consisting of 5 parts | phil. [Nyāya] the 5-part syllogism: pra tijñā₂ the thesis to be demonstrated, (in the form of the predicate [sādhya] applied to the subject [pakṣa]) hetu the hypothetical reason, udāharaņa the concomitance

inevitable [vyāpti] followed by the supporting example [dṛṣṭānta], upanaya the hypothesis, and nigamana the conclusion. parvato vahnimān dhūmāt yo yo dhūmavān sa sa vahnimān yathā mahānasaḥ tathā ca ayam vah nivyāpyadhūmavān ca ayam parvatah tasmāt tathā dhūmavattvāt ca parvatah vahnimān There is fire on the mountain, because of the smoke; there is no smoke without fire, for example in the kitchen; thus from the existence of smoke one concludes that the mountain is on fire.
pañcāvaraṇastava [āvaraṇastava] n. bed. n.p. from Agoraśivācārya's Pañcāvaranastava, a 12th century South Indian śaiva text, dealing with prescriptions for the representation of Sadāśiva.
pañcāśīta |aśīta| amnf pañcāśītī ord. 85°.
pañcāśīti [aśīti] f. 85.
pañcāśītitama [tama] amnf pañcāśītitamī ord. 85ᵉ.
pañcāsya |āsya| amnf pañcāsyā which has 5 faces or 5 heads | with 5 points (arrow).
páñcan num. pers. [sg. name. acc. pañca; pl. other cases; pl. g. pañcānām] the number Five | gr. πεντε; lat. quinque; all. funf; eng. five, punch; fr. Five.
pañcama | pañcama | amnf pañcamī ord. fifth — m. (mus.) 5th note of the Indian octave phon. 5th consonant of a varga, nasal — f. cf. pañcamī.
pañcamaveda | veda | m. lit. collection of texts
traditional [purāṇa], considered to form the 5th veda.

pañcamahākāvya [mahākāvya] n. pl. lit. the 5 great epic poems: the Kumārasambhava and the Raghuvamáa of Kālidāsa (45th century) Kirātārjunīya of Bhāravi (6th century), the Śiśupālavadha of Māgha (9th century), and the Naisadhacarita of Śrīharṣa (12th century).

pañcamahāyajña [mahāyajña] m. pl. soc. the five major rites of the śrauta ritual: brahmayajña the sacrifice to brahman, devayajña the sacrifice to the gods, manusyayajña/nṛyajña the sacrifice to men, pitryajña the sacrifice to the ancestors and bhūtayajña the sacrifice to the spirits.
pañcamukha [mukha] amnf panñcamukhī which has 5 heads — m. myth. epith. not. of Prajāpati, of Siva, of Hanumān.
pañcārtha [artha] m. pl. phil. [pāśupata] the 5 concepts: effect [kārya], cause [kāraṇa], union [yoga], ritual injunctions [vidhi] and cessation of suffering | duḥkhānta|.
Pañcārthabhāṣya [bhāṣya] n. lit. np. of the Pañcārthabhāsya, commentary on the Pāśupatasūtra due to Kaundinya.
pañcamī [f. pañcama] f. gram. ablative (5th case of declension) | soc. 5th day of a lunar fortnight; cf. vasantapañcamī, raṅgapañcamī.
pañcamītatpurusa [tatpurusa] m. gram. compound determinative word derived from the ablative of its first member, like corabhaya.

Pañcāla m. geo. Pañcāla country, inhabited by a tribe of 6 warrior clans of northern India, east of the Kuravas and Matsyās; its capital was Kāmpilyā | myth. [Mah.] Pañcāla was the kingdom of Drupada; his former fellow student Drona defeated him and confiscated the part of the country north of the
Ganges [Ahicchattra] to make his son Aśvatthāmā | pl. Pañcālās reign there, his people, the Pañcālās or Pañcālās.
Pañcāleśvara |īśvara| m. geo. np. of the cellar of Pañcāleśvara in Puṇe, housing the Pātāleśvara.

Patañjali m. hist. np. of Patañjali₁, grammarian of the 2nd century BC, originally from Go narda; he enjoyed the patronage of Puşyamitra; he is the author of the great Mahābhāṣya commentary on the grammar of Pāṇini and the additional aphorisms of Kātyāyana | hist. np. of the philosopher Patañjali₂, ancient author of the Yogasūtra, a compilation of aphorisms on yoga, of disputed date (4th century?) | lit. nal [syn. prātipadika] weak (before suffixes beginning with a consonant); opp. bha | gram. conjugation form of a verb determining its suffixes (parasmaipada for the active voice, ātmanepada for the middle or reflexive voice) | math. square root; quadrant. padena adv. on foot. padam dā to take a step, to move. padam kṛ to step into (loc.), to enter. kutūhalena tasya cetasi padam kṛtam curiosity came to his mind. padam ātan to extend, to improve one's position. padam dhā to follow in the footsteps of, to compete with. iic. padam nidhā to set foot on (loc.); (figuratively) to make an impression. pade pade adv. with every step; progressively | on every occasion. trīni padāni viṣṇoḥ myth. The three strides of VisnuTrivikrama. viṣṇoḥ pādau myth. The feet of Viṣṇu (placement between the two eyebrows where the sectarian mark [ūrdhvapuṇḍra] of Viṣṇu is affixed, i.e., two vertical marks). suptinantam padam [Pāṇini] A word is a nominal or verbal inflected form. śaktam padam phil. [Tarkasamgraha] A word is that which has expressive power. ākṛtiviśeṣeṣvādaraḥ padaṃ karoti Good manners command respect. kavīnām ca kapīnām ca padānām nāsti bandhanam poets like monkeys we do not restrict the steps/verses.

padārtha [artha] m. gram. meaning, sense; denotation; notion, concept; entity; thing | phil. [Vaisesika] category or modality; there are 6 of them: dravya₁ (substance), guṇa (quality, species), karman (activity), sāmānya (generic substrate), viśesa (discriminative substrate), and samavāya (inherence) | phil. [Nyāya] conceivable and nameable entity; denotable concept category; there are 7 of them: dravya₁ (substance), guna (quality), kriyā (action), jāti (genericity), višesa (individuality), samavāya (inherence) and abhāva (absence); Raghunātha₁ disputes these categories and proposes others, such as karanatva (causality) | phil. [rhet.] method of argumentation; Akṣapāda names 16 at the beginning of the Nyāyasūtra: pramāṇa (means of right knowledge), prameya (object of legitimate judgment), samśaya (point of contention), prayojana (purpose of discussion, motivation), dṛṣṭānta (supporting example), siddhānta (established conclusion), avayava (element of a syllogism), tarka (logical reasoning), nirnaya (the act of carrying the decision), vāda (discussion), jalpa (chatter, ratiocination), vitandā (quibbling), hetvābhāsa (fallacious argument), chala (tomperie), jāti (genericity) and nigrahasthāna (situation of argumentation failure) | phil. [Bhartrhari] ontological category of the lexicon; there are 8: dravya₁, guṇa, kriyā, saṃbandha (relation), sādhana (semantic role), dik (space), saṃkhyā₂ (number) and kāla₁ (time) | phil. [Sivānanda] object that can be conceptualized and named — ifc. gram. category of compound word; Patañjali₁ dis tingue The types pūrvapadārtha, uttarapadārtha, anyapadārtha and ubhayapadārtha, according to the semantic dependence of the compound on its constituents. vyaktyākṛtijātayastu padārthāh phil. [Nyāya darśana] Meaningful entities combine three aspects: generic character [jāti], aspect [ākṛti] and individual object [vyakti].
padārthaka [ka] amnf padārthikā meaning.
padārthakhandana [khandana] n. lit. np. du Padārthakhaṇḍana "Re-examination of semantic categories"; cf. Padārthatattvanirūpaņa.
Padārthakhaṇḍanavyākhyā [vyākhyā₂] f. bed. n.p. of the Padārthakhandanavyākhyā, commentary on the Padārthakhandana due to Raghudeva.
padārthatattva [tattva] n. phil. matter of the meaning of words.

padārthatattvanirūpana [nirūpana] lit. n. np. of the Padārthatattvanirūpaṇa "Investigation of the Meaning of Words", a work of semantics [NN.] by Raghunātha₁ Širomaṇi; also called Padārthakhandana by the commentators. padārthatattvanvivecanaprakāśa [vivecanaprakāśa] m. lit. of the np. Padārthatattvavivecanaprakāśa, commentary on the Padārthatattvanirūpaņa by Rāmabhadra₁ Sārvabhauma.

padārthadharmasamgraha [dharmasamgraha] m. lit. np. of padārthadharmasamgraha "Treatise on the laws of the classification of concepts", work by Praśastapāda commenting on the Vaiśeṣikasūtra, but also bringing important new contributions to the discriminative doctrine [Vaiseșika]; the Nyāyakandalī is the commentary by Śrīdhara₁.
padārthokti [ukti] f. gram. explanation of the meaning of a word.
padāvalī [āvalī] f. bed. series of verses; poetry.
padāvṛtti [āvṛtti] f. repetition of a word.
padoccaya [uccaya] m. lit. [aesthetics] accumulation of chosen words.
padottarārdha [uttarārdha] mn gram. suffix (opp. padapūrvārdha theme).
padottarārdhavakratā [vakratā] f. lit. [Kuntaka] oblique quality of the use of suffixes.
padāti [contr. pādabhyāmatati] m. who goes on foot, pedestrian; foot soldier | chess pawn | caturangā|.

padma mn organic. bot. Nelumbium speciosum, pink lotus; it is a symbol of beauty and purity; syn. kamala — ifc. splendid (iic.) — f. padmā myth. n.p. of padmā, epith. of Lakṣmī “pure as the lotus” — n. math. a billion.
padmakośa | kośa | m. bio. lotus bud | hand gesture |mudrā| in the shape of a lotus bud (fingers joined upwards).
padmagarbha | garbha | m. calyx of the lotus | myth. epith. of Brahmā "born from the lotus"; also of Viṣṇu, Buddha, etc.
padmagupta | gupta | m. hist. np. of the poet Pari mala padmagupta, court poet of King Sind hurāja Paramāra (late 10th century); he is credited with the Na vasāhasānkacarita.
padmacaraṇa [caraṇa] m. cf. Padmapāda.
padmanābha [nābhi] m. myth. np. of Pad manābha, aspect of ViṣṇuNārāyaṇa "whose name shines with the lotus (of Creation)".
padmanābhatīrtha [tīrtha] m. hist. np. of Pad manābhatīrtha, chief disciple of Madhva; at the death of the master, he became the pontiff of the order; he founded the Uttarādi matha.

padmanābhasvāmin [svāmin] m. geo. vaiṣṇava temple of Padmanābhasvāmī, at Anantaśayana (mod. Trivandrum) in Kerala; the original temple is from the 8th century, the gopura built in 1566; the present temple was built in 1750 by King Mārtanda₁ Varmā who took the title, with his descendants, of padmanābha Dāsa; the recumbent statue of padmanābha there is 6 meters long; it is said to be made of 12008 śālagrāma .
padmanidhi | nidhi | mr. myth. n.p. of padmanidhi, one of the 9 treasures of Kubera [navanidhi].
padmapāṇi [pāṇi] amnf who holds a lotus — m. bd. n.p. of Padmapāṇi, epith. of Avalokiteśvara "holding a lotus".
Padmapāda [pāda] m. hist. np. of Padmapāda or Padmacarana "Lotus Foot", disciple of Sankarācārya; he is credited with the Pancapādikā exegesis of his commentary Brahmasūtra bhāsya.

padmapurāna [purāna] n. lit. np. of the padma purāņa or Pādmapurāņa [PP.], enormous mythological collection, in 5 parts [khanda]: Sṛṣṭi, Bhūmi, Svarga, Pātāla, Uttara; it instills the cult of Viṣṇu; there are two recensions of it; its writing extends over several centuries from the 4th, its later parts are later than the Bhāgavatapurāṇa; cf. sāttvika | lit. np. of a sacred Jaina text of the 6th century; it relates the exploits of Rāma.

padmaprabha [prabhā₂] m. jn. np. of padma prabha "Splendor of lotus", 6th tīrthankara mythic; its symbol is a red lotus flower | hist. np. of the Jain astronomer padmaprabha₁ Sūri, author of the Bhuvanadīpaka.
padmabandha | bandha | m. lit. geometric poem |citrakāvya| in the shape of a lotus.
padmabhūṣaṇa [bhūṣaṇa] n. mod. civil decoration (Indian Legion of Honour).
padmarāga [rāga] m. ruby ["of the color of the lotus"] — f. padmarāgī myth. one of the 7 languages of Agni |saptajihva|.
padmavajra |vajra| m. hist. np. from the scholar bd. Pad mavajra (late 7th century); he was the author of Vajrayāna works, notably the Guhyasiddhi, written in an obscure style | sandhyābhāṣā].
padmavat |vat| amnf padmavatī full of lotus flowers. padmavarņa |varņa| amnf padmavarņā with lotus complexion — m. myth. n.p. of Padmavarna, a son of Yadu.
padmavibhūṣaṇa [vibhūṣaṇa] n. mod. civil decoration (officer of the Indian Legion of Honour).
padmaśrī [śrī] m. bd. epith. of Avalokiteśvara "who has the beauty of the lotus" | mod. (title) honorable (civil decoration, Indian merit).

padmasambhava |sambhava| m. bd. np. of Pad masambhava "From the lotus", 8th century bd. master, originally from northern (or eastern) India; according to legend, in Rivālasara he seduced Princess Maṇḍāravā, daughter of the King of Maṇḍī, to initiate her into tantric bd.; the king wanted to burn him, but he survived the pyre, and went with Maṇḍāravā to practice Vajrayāna at the Marātika cave, where they received the vision of Amitāyu, which conferred immortality upon them; He left in 760 for Tibet to found the monastery of Samye with Sāntarakṣita at the request of King Trisong Detsen, to establish the Tibetan alphabet and translate Buddhist texts there; he is known in Tibet as Guru Rinpoche, and considered the founding monk of the Nyingma sect of the red hats in Tibet; he is depicted with the khatvānga.

Padmasundara [Sundara] m. hist. n.p. of the Jain scholar Padmasundara Sūri (16th century); he was honored by Akbar; we owe him not. the Hāyanasundara (astrology), the Akabarasahiśringāradarpaņa (poetics), the Pramāṇasundara (logic) and the Sundara prakāśaśabdārṇava (lexicon).

Padmasena [senā] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara Padmasena "Armed with the lotus", eldest son of King Muktāsena; the vidyādharī princess Adityaprabhā fell in love with him and he married her; his jealous friend Candravatī also wanted him as a husband; Adityaprabhā harassed him, he complained to his father, who sent him to Earth as Indīvarasena with his twin brother Rūpasena, to find his wives there as vampires [rākṣasī]; cf. Pa rityāgasena.

Padmāvatī [vat] f. myth. np. of Padmāvatī, epith. of Lakṣmī "bearing the lotus" | hist. np. of Padmāvatī₁, a wife of Aśoka | lit. [Svapnavāsavadatta] np. of Padmāvatī₂, Pradyota princess of Magadha, sister of King Darśaka; she married King Udayana as his favorite wife after many adventures.
padmāsana [āsana] n. phil. [yoga] posture of crossed legs "in lotus" (left leg folded on the right groin, right leg symmetrically above).
Padmodbhava [udbhava] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Padmodbhava "From the lotus", hereditary minister of King Rājahaṃsa; he is father of Suśruta₁ and Rat nodbhava.
padmin [padmain] amnf padminī who holds a lotus — f. padminī organic. bot. Nelumbium speciosum, pink lotus | excellent woman, noble lady.

pádya [Pad₂ya] amnf padyā relating to the foot; relating to a verse; in verse | bearing footprints | of such length in feet — n. verse; stanza of 4 verses [pāda] | meter; poetry (opp. gadya) — f. padyā pl. footprints; strides. padyacūdāmaņi |cūdāmaņi| m. lit. np. of the Pa dyacūdāmani, a work by Buddhaghosa; it is inspired by the Raghuvamsa, whose themes it takes up.
padyaveṇī [veṇī] f. bed. n.p. from the padyaveṇī, an anthology of 889 verses [subhāṣita] due to Veṇīdatta (1644).
Padra M. village; path.

panasa m. bio. bot. Artocarpus heterophyl lus, jackfruit tree, a moraceae; large tree with black bark, fine-grained yellow wood; it has many medicinal uses — n. |panasaphala| its fruit, a drupe that can weigh up to 25 kg, with a sweet taste and strong smell; it is edible and rich in minerals.
√ panth [related to path] v. [10] pr. (panthayati) pf. (pari) follow the path.
panthan cf. pathin. দ্য panna [pp. Pad₁] amnf pannā fell, gone.
pannaga [ga₁] m. snake.

pampā f. geo. np. of the pampā, a river in southern India; it rises in the Western Ghats (cf. Kişkindha), and flows into Lake Vembanad in Kerala; myth. AyyappāAyonija is said to have appeared as a child to King Rājaśekhara₁ on its banks; one bathes there before making the Sa barimalā pilgrimage; she is personified as the wife of Virūpākṣa | myth. lake near the hermitage of Agastya.
pampāsaras [saras] n. bed. [K.] np. of the pampā₁ lake, on the edge of which was the tree where the pug parrot Vaiśampāyana₁ was born.
paya iic. payas.

Payoṣṇī |uṣṇa| f. geo. np. of the Payoṣṇī river, which descends from the Vindhya mountains; myth. it is said that its water is mixed with soma; [Mah.] King Gaya offered the Pāṇḍavās five aśvamedha on the banks of the Payospī.
payas |abstr. pī| n. milk (freshly drawn); li quide, water, rain | sperm, virile strength — v. [11] pr. r. (payāyate) to taste like milk — v. [11] pr. (payasyati) to spill out.
payasvat [vat] amnf payasvatī juicy; succulent, rich in milk.
payoda |da| amnf payodā that gives milk; that provides water — m. cloud — f. payodā cow.
payodhara [dhara] m. breast ["that which bears milk"].
payonidhi | nidhi | mr. ocean.
payomuc [muc₂] amnf which releases water or milk — m. rain cloud.
payovrata | vrata | n. myth. milk ritual, taught by Nārāyaṇa to Aditi so that she would give birth to Vāmana.

pára pn. mnf parā earlier in time, ancient | further in space | that follows, that comes after (abl.); second, posterior, future; subsequent; last, extreme; excessive | Superior (to (abl.)); principal, supreme, powerful; absolute | other, distant, different; opposite; foreign, adverse; hostile, en nemi — m. the other, the foreigner; the enemy | supreme, absolute spirit — n. furthest point, highest degree; principal occupation — ifc. occupied with, given over to, devoted to, full of, which consists in (iiic.); which has as its principal object (iiic.) — f. parā foreign land | [parāvāc] phil. [Bhartṛhari] the primordial Word, 1st stage of the manifestation of sound [parāśakti] phil. [Trika] np. of parā, the supreme transcendent creative Energy — iiic. supreme (ifc.) | gr. ; ang. far, port. param adv. cf. param. pare adv. later, after; in the future. parena prep. after, later than (abl. g.).
parakāyapraveśana [kāyapraveśana] n. act of entering the body of another (a magical art).
paragata [gata] amnf paragatā associated with another; which relates to another.
paracittajñāna [cittajñāna] n. phil. knowledge of the thoughts of others.
párajāta [jāta] amnf parajātā foreigner | of an inferior race.
páratantra [tantra] amnf paratantrā dependent; relative; subject — n. state of dependence; submission | soc. formula for another rite.
páradāra [dāra] m. soc. wife of another | adultery | pl. id.
páradeśa | deśa | m. foreign country.
páradeśin [in] amnf paradeśinī foreigner — m. foreigner; traveler.

páradhana | dhana | n. soc. another's fortune. mūkah parāpavāde paradāranirīkṣaṇe'pyandhah | panguh paradhanahare sa jayati lokatrayam puruṣaḥ | The man who remains mute to insult another, blind to look at another's wife, and crippled to take another's wealth, this one gains the three worlds.
páranindā | nindā | f. act of vilifying others.
paranipāta [nipāta] n. gram. irregular incidence of a compound member in the later place; opp. pūrvanipāta.
parapura | pura | n. foreign city | foreign body.
párapurapraveśa [praveśa] m. act of entering an enemy city | act of entering the body of another person, possession.
parapurapraveśavidyā | vidyā | f. art of possessing another body, a magical practice.

parapurañjaya [purañjaya] m. myth. np. of Para purañjaya, king of the Haihayās; hunting in the forest, he mistook for a deer the son of the sage Ariștanemi, in meditation under a deerskin; believing he had killed him with his arrow, he asked forgiveness of his father, who showed him his son alive, protected by his tapas.
parapustā [pusta] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the princess Parapuṣṭā, daughter of Janamejaya, seventh wife of Sūryaprabha₁.
parabrahman | Brahman | n. cf. parambrahman.
parabhṛta [bhṛta] mf parabhṛtā bio. ["raised by others"] zoo. cuckoo; cf. kokila.

paramāra [māra] m. myth. np. of paramāra "Superior to death", son of the rși Saunaka; he is given as the origin of the line of the eponymous dynasty of Mālava, and therefore reputed ancestor of Bhojadeva | hist. dynasty of Mālava, of capital Ujjayinī then Dhārā; cf. Vairisiṃha, Bhojadeva.
paramokṣanirāsakārikā [mokṣanirāsa₁kārikā] f. pl. phil. np. of the Paramokṣanirāsakārikās "(59) Stanzas rejecting other views on liberation", work of Sadyojyoti.
Paramokṣanirāsakārikavṛtti [vṛtti] f. bed. n.p. from the Paramokṣanirāsakārikavṛtti “Commentary on the Stanzas of Sadyojyoti” by Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha.
pararūpa [rūpa] n. the sound that follows.
paraloka [loka] m. phil. the other world; the beyond. paralokam adv. towards the other world.
paravidyā [vidyā] f. phil. supreme knowledge.

paravipratisedha [vipratisedha] m. gram. ["act of ignoring a previous rule"] priority of the subsequent rule, metalinguistic rule [paribhāṣā] in grammatical formulas conforming to the paratva principle; opp. pūrvavipratisedha.
paraśarīra [śarīra] mn phil. [śaiva] the body cau sal; cf. kāraņaśarīra.
parasaṃgata |saṃgata| amnf parasaṃgatā associated with another | engaged in combat with another.
parasaptamī [saptamī] f. gram. locative in a temporal sense; opp. viṣayasaptamī.
parasukhā [sukhā] f. happiness of others.
parasukhāsahiṣṇu [sahiṣṇu] amnf jealous of the happiness of others, envious.
parastha [stha] amnf parasthā phil. aesthetic situated in the other; said of acts of theatre or poetry evoking or describing the other, such as beauty; qualifies the comic of satire; opp. ātmastha.
parādvaita [advaita] m. phil. [Trika] tantr doctrine. of “beyond nondualism”; cf. Pra tyabhijñā.
parādhīna [adhīna] amnf parādhīnā dependent on others.
parādhīnatā |tā| f. dependence on others.
parādhīnatva |tva| n. id.
parānta | anta | m. | "last resort" | death.
parāntakāla [kāla₁] m. hour of death.

parāpara [apara₁] amnf parāparā distant and near; before and after; higher and lower; better and worse — n. phil. |trikaśāstra| identity in difference (of God and man) — f. parāparā [parāparāśakti] phil. [Trika] np. of parāparā, the immanent creative divine Energy.
parāparajāti | jāti | f. gram. lexical relation “kind of”.
parāparajña [jña] amnf parāparajña phil. who possesses both transcendent and profane knowledge.
parāparatā |tā| f. greater or lesser degree; greater or lesser priority.
parāparatva |tva| n. id.

parāyaṇa₁ [ayana] amnf parāyaṇā violent (pain) | principal; which constitutes the final goal | which depends on, which entails (g.) — ifc. which has as its principal object (iic.); engaged in, occupied with (iic.) totally devoted to, possessed by, obsessed with, which thinks only of (iic.) — n. final goal; ultimate refuge, last resort | principal object; essence, summary principal occupation; complete devotion; obsession, addiction | med. panacea, (remedy) sovereign. parāyaṇam kṛ to do everything possible for, to give oneself wholeheartedly to.

parārtha [artha] m. most important, most interesting object; primary matter | sexual relations | matter or meaning of another — amnf parārthā which has another object; which concerns something else; dependent on something else | intended for another; for the use of others; opp. svārtha. parārtham var. parārthe adv. for another; for others; for something else.
parārthabhāvinī [bhāvin] f. phil. [YV.] state where one cannot conceive of anything outside of the supreme brahman, 6th level of knowledge [jñānabhūmikā].
parārthānumāna [anumāna] n. phil. [Nyāya] use of reasoning for debate.
parārthābhidhāna [abhidhāna] n. gram. new meaning of a word obtained by synthesis of its
components [vṛtti]; cf. samudāyaśakti.

parārdhá [ardha] m. (poetry) the immeasurable phil. [Vaiśeṣika] the maximum number [saṃkhyā₂] — n. math. one hundred thousand billion (one hundred million billion) | myth. number of earthly days equivalent to 50 years of Brahmā days.
parārdhya [ya] amnf parārdhyā incommen surable; inégalable, indésurpassable — n. ifc. au maxi mum de.

parāvara [avara] amnf parāvarā distant and near; before and after; without exception, one after the other | immemorial, traditional | soc. transmitted from master to disciple | phil. supreme and not supreme — n. cause and effect; totality; the universe — m. ancestors and descendants. parāvare exhaustively.
parāvaratattva | tattva | n. phil. gift of com to take the essence of all things; cf. Yuvanāśva.
paraka [paraka] ifc. amnf parikā gram. next (said in one word). itiśabdaparakah gram. (word) following the word iti.
parakīya [īya] amnf parakīyā belonging to another, foreign; opp. svakīya. parakīya bhava contrary nature.
paratama |great. para| amnf paratamā supreme.
paratara [compar. para] amnf paratarī superior to.
páratas [adv. para] adv. beyond; after (langle abl. rangle); elsewhere; superiorly; differently in an extrinsic way; opp. svatas.
paratra [paratra] adv. elsewhere; in another world | in the future, henceforth.

paratva [paratva] n. distance | phil. [Vaisesika] the property [guna] of distance | gram. principle of priority of the subsequent rule in case of conflict between two rules of the Aṣṭādhyāyī; cf. paravipratisedha.
paratvāparatva [aparatva] n. du. paratvāparatve distance and proximity.

param |para| adv. after, later; beyond, besides | after, following, beyond (abl.) | extremely, quite; willingly | but, however. atah param var. paramatah adv. then. itah param adv. henceforth. tatah param adv. after that, afterwards. na param adv. not only. yadi param adv. perhaps; in any case, however. nāsmāt param that's enough! mattah param after me. param tu var. parantu conj. but, on the other hand, however. param param adv. one after the other. param vijñānāt beyond human knowledge. astamayāt param adv. after sunset. varṣaśatāt param adv. after 100 years. paramtapa var. Parantapa [tapa] amnf paramtapā who torments his enemy (epith. of hero) — m. [Mah.] np. of Parantapa, epith. of Ar juna | [Rām.] epith. of Rāma. parampara var. parampara [red. para] amnf paramparā one after the other, in succession; from father to son | successive, repeated — f. cf. paramparā. paramparam adv. successively; without interruption. parambrahman var. parabrahman [brahman] mn phil. the Supreme Spirit — m. nom. parambrahmā] phil. God; Brahmā.

paramá [super. para] amnf paramā the furthest, the highest, the best, excellent, Supreme, extreme — ifc. that which deals with, that which devotes itself to (iic.); that which consists of (iic.). santosah paramo lābhah satsangah paramā gatih vicārah paramam jñānam śamo hi paramam su kham | [YV.] Contentment is the Supreme gain, good company the Supreme path, reflection the Supreme wisdom, peace yes truly is the Supreme happiness.
paramatā [tā] f. superiority, Supremacy. paramatām gam to attain Supremacy.
paramáprīta [prīta] amnf paramaprītā extremely pleased.
paramabrahman [brahman] n. phil. the Supreme Spirit, undifferentiated cosmic principle pervading the Universe.
paramamāheśvara [māheśvara] m. soc. Supremely devoted to Śiva, royal epith.; syn. atyantamāheśvara.
paramarājya | rājya | n. Supreme kingship. paramarşi [rṣi] m. myth. [Yuktidīpikā] Supreme sage, an epithet of Kapila.

paramalaghumañjūṣā [Laghumañjūṣā] f. gram. n.p. from the paramalagumañjūṣā, a treatise on the semantics of language due to Nāgeśa Bhaṭṭa; it is an abbreviated version of the Laghumañjūṣā; the semantics of negation is distinguished between the types pa ryudāsapratisedha and prasajyapratisedha.
paramavrddhi [vrddhi] f. soc. maximum legal interest mal.
paramahaṃsa | haṃsa | amnf paramahaṃsā soc. "who has Supreme discernment", title of spiritual accomplishment. paramāņu | aņu | m. infinitesimal particle; atom (in the vaiśeșika system).
paramātman [ātman] m. phil. the Supreme Spirit (opp. jīvātman the individual soul); identified with the principle paramabrahman, it is personified by Brahmā.
Paramātmasandarbha [sandarbha] m. lit. np. of the Paramātmasandarbha, treatise by Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī explaining the philosophy of Caitanya.
paramānanda [ānanda] m. Supreme happiness | phil. bliss of refuge in the Supreme Being.
paramānandīya [īya] amnf paramānandīyā procuring Supreme happiness.
paramānandīynāmamālā [nāmamālā] f. bed. n.p. from the Paramānandīyanāmamālā, dictionary of Makarandadāsa (end of the 16th century).

Paramārtha [artha] m. reality, Supreme truth; spiritual knowledge; reality, truth | bd. ultimate truth (opp. samvṛti) | altruistic work; opp. svārtha | hist. np. of the bd philosopher Paramārtha (6th century); he is credited with a life of Vasubandhu; he went to China in 645. paramārthena var. paramārthāt in reality. paramārthatas adv. in reality, truly. paramārthena grah to take to heart.
paramārthavid [vid₃] amnf who knows the Supreme truth — m. philosopher, sage.
paramārthasat [sat] amnf saṃvṛtisatī bd. which ultimately exists, as dharma; opp. samvṛtisat.
paramārthasatya [satya] n. bd. ultimate truth (opp. samvṛtisatya).

paramārthasāra |sāra| mr. bed. n.p. from the Pa ramārthasāra "Essence of the Supreme truth", or concise work of Abhinavagupta giving the philosophical principles of Shaivism of the Kaśmīra [Trika] in 105 verses, taking up an original work by Adisesa₁; he investigates the nature of liberation during his lifetime [jīvanmukti]; Yogarāja wrote a gloss on it |vivṛtti|.
paramārthasevā [sevā] f. bd. np. of the Pa ramārthasevā "Homage to the ultimate truth", early bd. work of the Kālacakra system due to Pundarīka₃.
paramārthika |ika| amnf paramārthikā phil. transcendent, ultimate; of the domain of reality ab solue; spiritual; opp. vyavahārika. paramārthikasat phil. ultimate reality.
paramāvadhi [avadhi] m. extreme limit.
parameśa [īśa] m. myth. n.p. from parameśa, the Supreme Being, epith. of Vișnu or Siva.

parameśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Pa rameśvara, epithet of Vishnu or Shiva in their form as Supreme God | hist. royal title of emperor — f. parameśvarī myth. np. of parameśvarī, Supreme form of the Goddess. atra tatra ca sarvatra vartate parameśvarah anyatra cāpi tatsthānam kutra syād yatra nāsti saḥ || God exists here, there, and everywhere; he also resides elsewhere; where then could he not be?
paramodāra [udāra] amnf paramodārā extremely generous.
parame [loc. parama] iic. parameștha [stha] amnf parameșthā which is at the summit; superior; Supreme — m. myth. "Supreme", epith. of Brahmā, Viṣṇu or Siva.

paramesthin [in] amnf paramesthinī superior; Supreme | soc. ["in preeminent position" | royal title — m. myth. np. of parameșthī "Supreme Being", epith. of Brahmā and various gods | np. of sages or heroes.

paramparā [f. parampara] f. soc. success sion; offspring; lineage | [guruśiṣyaparaṃparā] soc. obedience, school (magisterial lineage from master [guru] to disciple [śiṣya]). paramparayā adv. by tradition; indirectly. iti karnaparamparayā śrutamasmābhih we know it by hearsay.

páramparāprāpta [prāpta] afmn paramparāprāptā received by tradition. evam paramparāprāptam imam rājarṣayo viduḥ [BhG.] Thus the princely patriarchs transmitted this knowledge (of yoga) from master to disciple.
páravat [paravat] amnf paravatī vas sal de, sujet de, dépend de (ig loc. iic.) subordinate; obedient | needy, without resources — adv. like a stranger.

páravaśa |paravaśa| amnf paravaśā sou put to the will of another; subject to, obeying (iic.). ānandaparavaśaḥ mad with joy. anangaparavaśah suratam ātatāna |K.| under the emperor of Cupid he indulged in love.

páravācya | paravācya | amnf paravaśā blameworthy by others — n. blameworthy act of another. paravācyesu nipuņah sarvo bhavati sarvadā ātmavācyam na jānīte jānannapi vimuhyati | |Mah.| while being well aware of the fault of others, one never recognizes one's own fault; while knowing it, one plays the fool.
páravāṇi [paravāṇī] m. the year | myth. np. of the peacock Paravāṇi, mount [vāhana] of Kārttikeya; it is said to kill Time.
páravāda [paravāda] m. reported speech; rumor; slander | objection; controversy.
páravādin [paravādin] m. opponent; creator of controversy.
paraśu m. axe.
paraśucchinna [chinna] amnf paraśucchinnā cut by the axe.

Paraśurāma [Rāma] m. myth. np. of Paraśurāma, "Rāma₁ with the axe", younger son of Jamadagni; he became a warrior [kṣatriya] as a consequence of the ritual error [varṇasaṃkara] of his grandmother Satya vatī₁; on his father's orders, he beheaded his guilty mother Renukā; after the murder of his father, Vișnu incarnated in him as the 6th avatar; he is the unsurpassable master of martial arts; [Rām.] when Ramāma broke the bow of his guru Śiva, he wanted to fight him, but had to recognize his superiority and gave him Vișnu's bow; [Mah.] he gave Indra's bow to Karna; With the magic axe given to him by Shiva, he destroyed 21 generations of princes [kṣatriyās], turning them into three lakes of blood at Samantapañcaka; after a great sacrifice, he restored sovereignty over the Earth to the Brahmins and erected a golden altar at Kasyapa, which was shared by the officiating priests [khāṇḍavāyana]; he then withdrew as a hermit to Mount Mahendra₁, where he taught Karna the science of weapons, and where the Pāṇḍavās visited him during their pilgrimage; it is also said that after giving the Earth to the Brahmins, he brought Kerala out of the waters to live there by throwing his axe from Kanyakumārī to Goa; there he taught the martial arts |kalarippayat| to 21 disciples; |Mah.| He fought unsuccessfully against Bhīṣma, at the request of Ambā, whom the latter had abducted to marry Vicitravīrya; [Bālarāmāyaṇa] was outraged that Rāma had broken the bow of
Śiva [Śaivacāpa], he challenged him to a duel, and lost; he is one of the 7 immortals [ciramjīvin]; his birthday is celebrated at the akṣayatṛtīyā; cf. Jāmadagnya, Bhārgava.

paraśurāmasṛṣṭi [sṛṣṭi] f. geo. “created by Paraśurāma”, epith. of the western coastal strip of southern India, from Karāvalī to Kerala; it is said that Parasurāma brought it out of the waters by throwing his axe.
paraśvas [paraśvas₂] adv. the day after tomorrow. paraśvo bhoktā he will eat the day after tomorrow.
parás [para] adv. on the other side of, far away — pf. beyond, more than, beside | lat. portus.

párastāt [tāt] adv. beyond, further than, far from g. ; opp. avastat | after, later; opp. pūrvam. paraspara var. paraḥpara | para| amnf para sparā mutual, reciprocal — pn. each other. parasparam var. paraspareņa, parasparāt adv. mutually, reciprocally. parasparavadhodyatau du. ready to kill each other. parasparopagraho jīvanam The living owe each other mutual respect (Jain motto).
parasparavirodha [virodha] m. phil. mutual incompatibility. parasparavirodhe hi na prakārāntarasthitah phil. [Nyāyakusumāñjali] In case of mutual incompatibility, there is no possible compromise.
parasparasambhūta [sambhūta] amnf apa rasparasambhūtā produces one after the other, produces in order.
parasparopakāra [upakāra] m. mutual aid.
párasavarṇa [parasavarṇa] amnf parasavarṇā phon. congruent to the following consonant (said of the substitute anusvāra). parasavarṇībhū phon. to become congruent to the following consonant.
párasāt [para] adv. soc. (woman given) in marriage to another (with kṛ₁). parasātkṛtā given in marriage to another.
parasmin [loc. para] adv. there.
parasmai [dat. para] iic.
parasmaipada [pada] n. gram. ["word having as its purpose another" | active voice (opp. ātmanepada).
parasmaipadin [in] amn gram. (said of a verb) conjugated in the active voice.
parahita [parahita₂] amnf parahitā friendly, benevolent — n. well-being of others.
parahyas [parahyas] adv. the day before yesterday.
párā |para| iic. back, in the opposite direction, far, apart, beyond; outside | gr. pi alpha rho alpha.
parāṇa [parāan₂a] amnf parāṇā exhaled, blown away. parāṇam vāyoḥ n. name of a sāman.

parātriṃśikā |triṃśikā| f. lit. np. of the Parātriṃśikā "30 verses on the Supreme", short tantric text of the Trika tradition of Kaśmīra, final section of the Rudrayāmala tantra, summarizing his teaching; it is a śaivāgama, in the form of a dialogue between Devī and Bhairava; it was commented on by Somānanda and then by Abhina vagupta, first in a condensed |Laghuvṛtti|, then in his Vivaraṇa₂; cf. Anuttaraprakriyā, Parātrīśikā.

parātriṃśikāvivaraṇa [Vivaraṇa] n. bed. n.p. of the Parātrimsikāvivaraņa or Parātrimsikāvivrti, commentary [Vivaraṇa₂] of the Parātriṃśikā by Abhi navagupta; it dates from the end of the 10th century.
parātriṃśikāvivṛti [vivṛti] f. cf. parātrimśikāvivarana.
Parātrīśikā [triīśikā] f. lit. np. of the Parātrīśikā "Supreme goddess of the Trinity [Trika]"; cf. Parātrimśikā.
parāvat |vat| amnf parāvatī distant.
Parāvaha | vaha | mr. myth. n.p. of Parāvaha, one of the 7 Heavenly Winds.
Parāśakti [śakti] f. phil. [Trika] np. of Parāśakti, Supreme transcendent creative energy.

parāśraya [āśraya] amnf parāśraya dependent on others; parasite | phon. said of visarga, anusvāra and other letters whose pronunciation depends on the context — m. dependence on others | refuge for enemies — f. parāśrayā bio. parasitic plant.
parāk cf. parāc.
parākaraņa |act. parākr| n. act of setting aside, rejection; disdain.
parākṛ |parākṛ₁| v. |1| pr. (parākaroti) to reject, to discard; to ignore.
parākṛta |pp. parākṛ| amnf parākṛtā dismissed, rejected, scorned.
parākram |parākram| v. |1| pr. (parākrāmati) pp. (parākrānta) to advance furiously, to excel, to distinguish oneself | to invest oneself, to shine in (loc.).
parākrama [act. parākram] m. courage, heroism; power, valor; exploit.

Parākramabāhu [bāhu] m. hist. np. of the bd king Parākramabāhu I who reigned in Ceylon [Lankā] from 1153 to 1186; he undertook a reform of the sangha by a council in 1156; his reign was marked by the production of numerous grammars of Sanskrit and Pali; not. the school of Moggalāna.
parākrānta [pp. parākram] amnf parākrāntā courageous, energetic, heroic; busy with (loc.).
parāga [agt. parāgam] m. ["that which goes far away"] pollen; dust; perfumed powder.
parāgānveṣaṇa [anveṣaṇa] afmn parāgānveṣaṇā in search of pollen.
parāgata [pp. parāgam] amnf parāgatā parti; deceased.
parāgam |parāgam| v. [1] pr. (parāgacchati) pp. (parāgata) to go to the law, to depart; to die.
parānmukha [parācmukha] amnf parānmukhī who turns their face away from, who turns away from, who avoids | hostile to, enemy. parāmukham adv. turning their back.
vanitāsambhogasukhaparānmukhaḥ [K.] who is repelled by the pleasure of love with women.
parāc var. parāñc [paraac] amnf parācī m. nom. parān; n. nom. parāk diverted; directed outwards. parāk var. parān adv. outside, outwards.
parācar [parācar] v. [1] pr. r. (parācarati) to move away from, to leave from.
parācīna [īna] amnf parācīnā diverted; removed from, beyond; indifferent to (abl.); ill-suited. parācīnam adv. far away; beyond (abl.).
parājaya |act. parāji| m. defeat, loss | conquest, victory | desertion. śisyādicchet parājayam One should desire to be sure that one has passed by one's student.

parāji [parāji] v. [1] pr. r. (parājayate) pp. (parājita) to be overcome by, to succumb to (abl.) — v. [1] pr. (parājayati) to overcome, to conquer, to defeat. adhyayanāt parājayate mandabuddhiḥ (The slow-witted student grows weary of study.
parājita [pp. parāji] amnf parājitā defeated, conquered.
parājiṣṇu [agt. parāji] amnf defeated, who succumbs | victorious, triumphant.
parāñc cf. parāc.
parāt |abl. para| iic.
parātpara [para] amnf parātparā superior to the best | superior to the superior.

parābhavá [agt. parābhū] m. disappearance; dissolution | defeat; humiliation; contempt, insult; injury; destruction, ruin | astr. np. of Parābhava "Decrepitude", personifying year 40 of a life cycle |samvatsara|.
parābhū [parābhū₁] v. [1] pr. (parābhavati) pp. (parābhūta) to succumb.
parābhūta [pp. parābhū] amnf parābhūtā disappeared, perished; defeated, beaten; wounded, humiliated.
parābhūti [act. parābhū] f. humiliation; defeat.

parāmarśa [act. parāmṛś] m. grasping, seizing; attack, assault; manifestation | the act of remembering; reference, mention | phil. [Nyāya] substitution, instantiation; the act of considering, reflection; deduction; implication, inference | lit. (theater) denouement. vyāptiviśistapakṣadharmatā jñānam parāmarśah phil. [Tarkasamgraha] Inference is the knowledge of the nature inherent in the subject specified by inevitable concomitance.
parāmarśana [act. parāmṛś] n. act of remembering; reference, mention.
parāmarśi iic. parāmarśin.

parāmarśitva [tva] n. phil. quality of denoting; reference. tatpadasya pūrvaprasaktasya pradhānasyaiva parāmarśitvāt phil. [Nyāya] by reference even to the main antecedent of the pronoun tad (rule of interpretation of a pronominal anaphora taking the subject of the discourse as its antecedent).
parāmarśin [agt. parāmṛś] amnf parāmarśinī which recalls; which designates, which refers, which denotes.
parāmṛś [parāmṛś] v. [1] pr. (parāmṛśati) pp. (parāmṛṣṭa) to touch, feel; to seize, grasp; to violate.
parāmṛṣṭa [pp. parāmṛś] amnf parāmṛṣṭā seized, held, grasped; moved, touched; mistreated; afflicted (illness) | remembered, restored.
parāyaṇa₂ [act. pare₂] departure; final destination.
parāri [related to parā] adv. the year before; two years ago.
parāvarta [act. parāvṛt] m. return; the act of going back restoration; return to tradition.
parāvāk iic. parāvāc.
parāvāgbhūmi [bhūmi] f. phil. level of the supreme primordial speech.
parāvāc [parāvāc] f. [nom. parāvāk] phil. [Bhartrhari] the supreme primordial speech, 1st stage of the manifestation of sound | phil. [Trika] then the manifestation of speech.
parāvrt [parāvrt₁] v. [1] pr. r. (parāvartate) pp. (parāvṛtta) to return.
parāvṛtta [pp. parāvṛt] amnf parāvṛttā turned around; avoided (from (abl.)) | disappeared; overturned (judgment) — n. act of rolling.
parāvṛtti [act. parāvṛt] f. about-turn; return; exchange; barter | reversal of a judgment.

parāśara [agt. parāśṛ] m. destroyer | myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] parāśara "the destroyer", son of Sakti₁ and Adráyantī, grandson of the rṣi Vasiṣṭha; he massacred many ogre-vampires [rāk;sasās] to avenge his father; [Mah.] crossing the Yamunā on Satyavatī's boat, he darkened the sky and granted her his wish to no longer smell of fish; from their union was born immediately Vyāsa, who grew old by his own will and became a hermit; parāśara was lame, and he died attacked by wolves in the forest; He is credited with the Kṛṣiparāśara and the teaching of Vișnupurāna.
parāśaratantra [tantra] n. lit. from the np. parāśaratantra, a work of astronomy from the 12th-14th century.
parāśarapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. from the np. parāśarapurāṇa, an upapurāṇa; it describes not. the structure of a canonical commentary.
parāśaramādhavīya [mādhavīya] n. bed. n.p. parāśaramādhavīya, commentary by Mādhavācārya of the parāśarasmṛti.
parāśarasmṛti [smṛti] f. bed. the of np. parāśarasmṛti, a dharmasūtra.
Parāśaropapurāṇa [upapurāṇa] n. bed. n.p. from Parāśaropapurāṇa; cf. parāśarapurāṇa.
parāśṛ [parāśṛ] v. [9] pr. (parāśṛṇāti) pp. (parāśīrṇa) crush, destroy.
parāhna [paraahna] m. afternoon.

pári prep. around, about, at the end of ⟨acc. abl. | circular movement — pf. var. parī₁ very, completely, abundantly, excessively | around, opposite to; towards, in the direction of — cl. around, on | successively — iic. var. pāri₁ very, abundantly || gr. . vrkṣam pari siñcati he waters each tree one after the other.

parikara [agt. parikṛ] amnf parikarī en tourage; aides, assistants — mf parikarā abon dance; multitude | belt | (theater) suggestion of a future event in the plot | lit. figure of speech accumulating epithets to reinforce a description. parikaram kṛ to prepare for (dat.). parikaram bandh id. baddhaparikarāh te they prepared for the ba size
parikarabandha [bandha] m. harness; preparation (not. for combat).

parikarman [parikarman] m. servant, assistant — n. assistance; adoration | body preparations, ointments, perfumes | purification; preparation; logistics, operations | math. fundamental arithmetic operations; there are 8: addition [samkalita], subtraction [vikalita], multiplication [guṇana], division [bhāgahāra], square [varga], cube [ghana], root
square [vargamūla], cube root [ghanamūla].
parikalpa [act. That. pariklp] n. bd. illusion.
parikalpita [pp. ca. pariklp] amnf parikalpitā determined; accomplished; foreseen | created, ima giné, invented | phil. conceived (doctrine).
parikīrt [parikīrt] v. [10] pr. (parikīrtayati) pp. (parikīrtita) to proclaim, announce, declare, specify; to praise, celebrate, glorify.
parikīrtita [pp. parikīrt] amnf pa rikīrtitā proclaimed, announced; praised; called.
parikṛ [parikṛ₁] v. [5] pr. (parikṛṇoti) pp. (parikṛta) to encircle | to support — v. [5] pr. (pariskrnoti) to prepare, to decorate; to improve, to perfect.
parikṛṣ [parikṛṣ] v. [1] pr. (parikarṣati) pp. (parikṛṣṭa) to lead, to guide, to have authority over acc. | to afflict, torment; to violate, to subdue.
pariklp [pariklp] ca. (parikalpayati) ca. r. (parikalpayate) pp. (parikalpita) to establish, determine; to destine to (acc. loc. inf.) | to execute, accomplish; to distribute; to suppose, imagine.
parikram [parikram] v. [1] pr. (pa rikrāmati) pp. (parikrānta) pf. (anu) to wander, to walk around, to go back and forth; to visit (theatre) to walk to simulate a scene change.
parikrama [act. parikram] m. wandering, peregrination; tour, walk, circuit; circu mambulation, procession | geo. pilgrimage; course of a river | order, succession, series.
parikraya [parikrī] m. salary, wages | redemption.
parikrī [parikrī₁] v. [9] pr. r. (parikrīṇīte) pp. (parikrīta) to buy, acquire; to hire (for i. dat. ). śatena parikrītaḥ var. śatāya parikrītaḥ bought for a hundred (rupees).
parikrīḍ [parikrīḍ] v. [1] pr. r. (parikrīḍate) to have fun around.
parikliś [parikliś] v. [9] pr. (parikliśnāti) pp. (pariklista) to afflict, to torment — ps. (pa rikliśyate) to be tormented.
parikliṣṭa [pp. parikliś] amnf parikliṣṭā tormented, afflicted — n. regret. pariklistam adv. reluctantly, grudgingly.
parikleśa [act. parikliś] m. suffering, torment; pain, fatigue.
parikleṣṭṛ [agt. parikliś] amnf parikleṣṭrī torturer, executioner.
parikṣi [parikṣi] v. [2] pr. (parikṣeti) to extend, to rule over.
parikṣit [agt. parikṣi] amnf that extends, that reigns around — m. cf. parīkṣit.
parikhaṇḍ [parikhaṇḍ] ca. (parikhaṇḍayati) pp. (parikhaṇḍita) to break, shatter, tear to pieces, rip, destroy.
parikhaṇḍana [act. parikhaṇḍ] n. destruction, loss. mānaparikhandanam loss of honour.
parikhā [parikhā] f. trench, ditch; moat. parikhīkṛta transformed into a moat.
parikhid [parikhid] v. [4] pr. r. (parikhi dyate) pp. (parikhinna) to feel tired.
parikhinna [pp. parikhid] amnf pari khinnā tired.

parigata [pp. parigam] amnf parigatā which has been circled; encircled; included possessed by, dominated by, afflicted by (iic. i.) | diffused, spread | deceased | felt; understood; learned from (abl.).
parigam [parigam] v. [1] pr. (parigacchati) pp. (parigata) to turn around; to make the circumambulation of; to surround, enclose; to reach (a state) — ca. (parigamayati) to turn; to pass (time).
parigā [parigā₁] v. [3] pr. (parijigāti) aor. [1] (paryagāt) to surround, encircle; to reach; to spread, to permeate.
parigṛhīta [pp. parigrah] amnf parigṛhītā seized on both sides; surrounded, encircled, wrapped | seized, received, obtained; adopted; followed, obeyed | controlled.
parigṛhītārtha | artha| amnf parigṛhītārthā in former, notified; informed. bhavato'vinayamamtarena parigrhītārthā kṛtā devī The Queen has been informed of your impertinence.
parigrhya [pfp. [1] parigrah] amnf parigṛhyā which must be followed or accepted — abs. ind. having seized; in company with (acc.) | as regards.

parigrah [parigrah] v. [9] pr. (parigṛḥṇāti) pr. r. (parigṛhṇīté) pp. (parigṛhīta) to take, sai sir; to surround, encircle; to take prisoner | to subdue; to surpass | to embrace; to accept, to welcome; to marry "to take as wife". strīgaņair dhanvibhih parigrhyeta |Arthaśāstra| (The King) must be protected by a troop of ama zones.
parigraha [act. parigrah] m. seizure, taking; encirclement, embrace; endorsement, acceptance; marriage | property, goods, harem; entourage, retinue, wife | domination, constraint; desire for power.
parigha [parigha] m. iron bar; lock; gate of a palace, barrier; obstacle | mass of weapons.
paricakṣ [paricakṣ] v. [2] pr. r. (paricaṣṭe) to neglect, ignore; to despise, reject | to condemn, to forbid | to consider; to mention, to call; to address, to answer (acc.).
paricakṣā [act. paricakṣ] f. rejection, disapproval.

paricaya [act. parici] m. study, knowledge; familiarity; intimacy. samastapadaparicayah m. gram. analysis of compound words. atiparicayād avajñā saṃtatagamanād anādaro bhavati | malaye bhillapurandhrī candanatarum indhanam kurute | too much familiarity breeds contempt, and too frequent visits lead to disrespect; the Malaya mountain woman uses the sandalwood tree to make fire.

paricar [paricar] v. [1] pr. (paricarati) pp. (paricarita) to walk around, to go around; to serve, to honor, to be at the service of — ca. (pa ricārayati) to serve, to take care of. sa tayā sārdham paricārayati they made love.
paricaryā [paricarya] f. service; homage, devotion — ifc. circumambulation around (iic.).
paricāra [act. paricar] m. service, tribute.
paricāraka [agt. paricar] m. servant, as sistant; emissary — f. paricārikā servant, sui vante.
paricāraṇa [act. paricar] n. act of serving.
paricārin [agt. paricar] amnf pa ricārinī servant — f. paricārinī servante.
parici [parici] v. [5] pr. (paricinóti) pr. r. (paricinuté) pp. (paricita) to accumulate, increase, augment | to examine; to find, to know, to practice; to become accustomed to.
paricita [pp. parici] amnf paricitā known, familiar; usual | tame. paricitakeśa accustomed to suffering.
paricint [paricint] v. [10] pr. (pa ricintayati) pp. (paricintita) to reflect, meditate; to consider; to remember | to imagine, to invent.
paricintaka [agt. paricint] amnf pa ricintakā who reflects on, who meditates on (iic. g.).
paricumb [paricumb] v. [1] pr. (paricum bati) pp. (paricumbita) to cover with kisses, to embrace passionately.
paricchad [parichad₁] pp. (parichanna) ca. (paricchādayati) to cover, to wrap; to hide, to conceal.
paricchada [act. paricchad] m. cover; clothing | personal belongings; stewardship.
paricchanna [pp. paricchad] amnf pa ricchannā concealed, hidden; disguised. dvīpicarmaparicchannah gardabhah an ass dressed in a tiger skin.
paricchid [parichid₁] v. [7] pr. (paric chinátti) pr. r. (paricchintté) pp. (paricchinna) to cut out, delimit, define; to decide, judge.
paricchinna [pp. paricchid] amnf pa ricchinnā cut out; delimited, defined | phil. bounded, of finite dimensions.
pariccheda [act. paricchid] m. division, separation; section or chapter of a work | exact definition, discrimination, decision; judgment, resolution.
paricchedātīta | atīta| amnf paricchedātīta which defies all definition. mama vikāraḥ paricchedātītaḥ my suffering surpasses all description.
paricchedana [act. paricchid] n. act of discriminating, defining or dividing | division of a work.
paricchedya [pfp. [1] paricchid] amnf paricchedyā to define; to estimate, to weigh, to measure.
parijana [parijana] m. entourage, continued.
parijā [parijā] f. source, origin; place of birth.
párijāta [parijāta] amnf parijātā which descends from (abl.) | fully developed.
parijñā₁ [parijñā₁] v. [9] pr. (parijānāti) pr. r. (parijānīte) pp. (parijñāta) to observe, perceive; to understand | to recognize as 2 acc. .
parijñā₂ [act. parijñā₁] f. knowledge.
parijñāta [pp. parijñā₁] amnf parijñātā recognized, understood.
parijñāna [act. parijñā₁] n. perception; understanding; discernment.

parinata [pp. parinam] amnf parinatā bent, inclined; not. elephant ready to charge with its tusks | bent by (i. ic.); changed, transformed into (i. i. ic.) | developed; ripe; adult; advanced (age); digested (food); elapsed (time) | astr. full (moon); set (sun) | gram. whose form must be adjusted according to the context — n. capital, rich accumulated wealth. pariņatam vayasā var. pariņatavayasi old age has arrived. parinataprāyam ahah the day is drawing to a close.
parinataprajña [prajñā₂] amnf parinataprajñā who has mature knowledge.

parinati [act. parinam] f. act of bending, of bowing | change, transformation, natural development | maturity; advanced age | result, consequence; termination, outcome; the act of fulfilling one's promise | digestion. parinatim yā to reach its final goal. śravanaparinatim yā to eventually reach the ears.

pariṇam [parinam] v. [1] pr. (pariṇamati) pr. r. (parinamate) pp. (parinata) pf. (vi) to bend, to incline forward; to fold | to be transformed into (i.); to arrive; to ripen, to age; to be ripe, to be old — ca. (pariṇāmayati) to ripen; to bring to its end; to pass (night). kṣīram dadhibhāvena parinamate the milk transforms into curd.
pariṇamayitr [agt. pariṇam] amnf pariṇamayitrī which makes bend; which makes ripen.
pariṇaya [act. pariṇī] m. (ceremony of) marriage | soc. transition from student status
single [brahmacarya] to that of master of May his [grhastha].

pariṇāma [act. pariṇam] m. maturity, maturation; decline, aging; change, transformation, evolution | result, consequence; end, denouement | phil. [Sāṃkhya] latent possibility; evolution of substances [tattva] in contact with purusa. pariņāme gram. qualifies the progressive mood of a verb. pariņāmanitya | nitya | amnf pariņāmanityā phil. eternally evolving, transient; opp. kūtasthanitya; [Sāṃkhya] qualifies Nature [prakṛti]; [Vedānta] qualifies the perceived world.
pariṇāmavāda [vāda] m. phil. theory of evolution.
pariṇāya [act. pariṇī] m. movement of a piece (chess); turn in the game. parināyena śārān hanti he throws the die after moving his pawn.

parināha [parināha] m. math. circumference of a circle. caturādhikam śatamastaguņam dvāsastistathā sahasrānām ayutadvayavişkambhasyāsannah vrttapariņāhah math. [Aryabhaṭa] 4 plus 100 times 8, plus 62000, gives approximately the circumference of a circle of diameter 20000 (gives π equal to 3 . 1416).
pariṇī [parinī₁] v. [1] pr. (pariṇayati) pp. (parinīta) to lead around (not. around the fire, in the wedding ceremony) | to marry (said of the husband).
pariņīta [pp. pariņī] amnf pariņītā married. pariņītapūrvā [pūrvā] f. woman previously married.
pariṇīya [abs. pariṇī] ind. having married.
pariņetṛ [agt. pariṇī] m. [sg. nom. pariņetā, acc. parinetāram] spouse.
pariņeya [pfp. [1] pariņī] amnf pariņeyā which must be led around | to marry.
páritakmya [paritak] amnf pari takmyā uncertain, unstable; dangerous — f. pari takmyā journey, peregrination | astr. winter solstice; cf. dakṣiṇāyana, saramā.

paritad [paritad] ca. (paritādayati) to strike all around. modakair deva paritādaya mām [KSS.] Sire, stop splashing me by striking the water! said his favorite to King Sātavāhana at the royal bath; he immediately had sweets [modaka] brought, provoking jeers against his ignorance of Sanskrit. samdhimātram na jānāsi māśabdodakaśabdayoh na ca prakaraṇam vetsi | You don't know how to make the sandhi between the words mā and udaka, nor do you understand their analysis. mūrkhas tvam katham īdṛśaḥ How can you be such an idiot!
paritap [paritap] v. [1] pr. (paritapati) pr. r. (paritapate) pp. (paritapita) to torment.
paritarj [paritarj] v. [1] pr. (paritarjati) pp. (paritarjita) to threaten.
parítas [adv. pari] adv. all around; on all sides; everywhere | around (acc.). na paritas not at all. grāmam paritah vṛkṣāḥ the village is surrounded by trees.
paritāpa [act. paritap] m. heat, torment.
paritus [paritus] v. [4] pr. (paritusyati) pp. (paritușța) to be content, to be satisfied with (i.).
paritoșa [act. paritus] m. satisfaction, contentment. paritosam nī to satisfy, to content.
parityakta [pp. parityaj] amnf pari tyaktā left; abandoned; rejected, repudiated. yadbhāvi tadbhavatu ityuktvā parityaktah he was left to his fate (saying "come what may").

parityaj [parityaj₁] v. [1] pr. (parityajati) pp. (parityakta) pfp. (parityājya) abs. (parityajya) abandon; renounce | soc. repudiate. sthānabhraṣṭā na śobhante dantāḥ keśā nakhā narāḥ | iti vijñāya matimān svasthānam na pari tyajet || Those who leave their place lose their esteem: teeth, hair, nails, and men; knowing this, the wise do not leave their place of origin. sarvadharmān parityajya mām ekam śaranam vraja [BhG.] Renounce all ritual, and place yourself under my sole protection.
parityajya [abs. parityaj] ind. having left, having abandoned | with the exception of (acc.).
parityāga [act. parityaj] m. abandonment, cession; renunciation of, sacrifice, abdication, neglect, omission | pl. parityāgās (acts of) his crifice.
parityāgabhūmi [bhūmi] amnf beneficiary ap proprie.

parityāgasena [senā] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of King Pa rityāgasena "Armed with renunciation"; he reigned in Irāvatī₅ with his two wives, Adhikasamgamā and Kāvyālaṃkārā; to obtain a son, he performed asceticism by praying to Ambikā; she gave him two magical fruits in a dream; he gave one to Adhikasaṃgamā to eat, who stole the other and ate it too, and gave birth to two twins, Indīvarasena and Anicchāsena.
parityāgin [agt. parityaj] amnf pa rityāginī who abandons; who renounces (iic.).
parityājana [act. ca. parityāj] n. act of causing abandonment or renunciation.
parityājya [pfp. [1] parityaj] amnf parityājyā to leave, which must be abandoned; which must be renounced | which must be omitted.
paritrasta [paritrasta] amnf paritrastā extremely frightened.
paritrā [paritrā] v. [4] pr. r. (paritrāyate) imp. r. (paritrāyasva) pp. (paritrāta) to save, defend, protect, rescue. paritrāyatām to the rescue! paritrāyasva nah save us!

paritrāṇa [act. paritrā] n. protection, safeguard, preservation | deliverance from (abl.) | refuge, aid; self-defense. paritrāṇāya sādhūnām vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya saṃbhavāmi yuge yuge | [BhG.] Era after era, I manifest myself for the protection of the righteous and the punishment of the guilty, in order to preserve justice.
paritrāta [pp. paritrā] amnf paritrātā saved; protected, defended.
paridah [paridah₁] v. [1] pr. (paridahati) to burn completely, to destroy by fire — ps. (pa ridahyate) to be completely consumed.
paridā [paridā₁] v. [3] pr. (paridadāti) to give, to offer; to hand over, to entrust.
paridīna [paridīna] amnf paridīnā very downcast, very distressed; completely depressed.
paridev [paridev] v. [1] pr. (paridevati) to lament.
parideva [act. paridev] m. lamentation.
paridevaka [agt. paridev] amnf pari devikā who laments.
paridevana [act. paridev] nf paridevanā lamentation. alamparidevanena what is the point of lamenting?
paridevita [pp. paridev] amnf paride vitā complained, cried — n. lamentation.
paridevin [agt. paridev] amnf paride vinī who laments.
paridveṣa [paridveṣa] amnf paridveṣā [RV.] enemy (who hates).
paridhā [paridhā₁] v. [3] pr. (paridadhāti) to surround, to envelop; to dress, to clothe — ca. (pa ridhāpayati) to make put on, to dress in (2 acc.).
paridhāna [act. paridhā] n. undergarment, draped around the waist; underwear.
paridhānīya [īya] n. underwear — f. pa ridhānīyā soc. verse [rc₂] ending a section of a ritual.
paridhāv [paridhāv₁] v. [1] pr. (pa ridhāvati) pp. (paridhāvita) pf. (vi) to run around; to pursue — ca. (paridhāvayati) to encircle. mrgayām paridhāv to go hunting.
paridhāvana [act. paridhāv] n. escape.
paridhāvin [agt. paridhāv] m. astr. n.p. of Paridhāvī "running in all directions", personifying year 46 of a life cycle [samvatsara].

paridhí [agt. paridhā] m. enclosure, barrier; enclosure wall | soc. sacrificial enclosure made up of three stakes delimiting the sacred fire: to the East, madhyama represents the sacrifice [yajña]; to the South, daksina represents the yajamāna and to the North, uttara₁ represents its opponent [bhrātrvya] | garment; halo around the Moon; horizon; circumference, etc.
paridhvaṃsa [paridhvaṃsa] m. distress,
misfortune | eclipse | soc. loss of caste; mixing of castes; outcaste.
parinirvāṇa [parinirvāṇa] n. bd. death (not. of the Buddha) || pali parinibbana.
pariniṣṭhā [pariniṣṭhā₁] pp. (pariniṣṭhita) to accomplish perfectly.

parinisthita [pp. parinisthā] amnf parinisthitā perfect, accomplished perfectly | expert in, champion of (iic. loc.) | gram. qualifies a form where phonetic operations have been carried out; syn. krtasandhi.
pariniṣpatti [act. pariniṣpad] f. perfection.
parinispad [parinispad] v. [4] pr. r. (parinispadyate) pp. (parinispanna) to become, to change into (noun).
parinispanna [pp. parinispad] amnf parinispannā developed, accomplished; perfect; real.
