parinyas [parinyas] v. [4] pr. (parinyasyati) pp. (parinyasta) to throw over, to spread over.
parinyasta [pp. parinyas] amnf pari nyastā extended.
parinyāsa [act. parinyas] m. development; not. of a seed, of a plot lit. act of completing the meaning of a passage.
paripakva [pp. paripac] amnf paripakvā well cooked; well ripe | phil. well prepared by yoga; opp. apakva.
paripakvatā |tā| f. maturity | perfection.
paripakvaśāli [śāli] m. ripe rice.

paripac [paripac] v. [1] pr. (paripacati) pp. (paripakva) to bring to maturity | to bear fruit; (fig.) to have consequences — ps. (paripacyate) to be cooked; to come to maturity | to roast in hell — ca. (pa ripācayati) to cook; to ripen; to bring to perfection.
paripat [paripat₁] v. [1] pr. (paripatati) pp. (paripatita) to run or fly in all directions, to wander; to fall into (loc.).
paripanth [paripanth] v. [10] pr. (paripan thayati) to obstruct.
paripanthín [agt. paripanth] amnf paripanthinī that obstructs; that gets in the way; enemy.
paripanthika [ka] m. opponent; enemy.
paripā [paripā₂] v. [2] pr. (paripāti) pp. (pa ripālita) to protect on all sides, to defend.
paripāka [act. paripac] m. complete matu
ritual | digestion | result; perfection. paripākāt var. paripākatas as a consequence of which.
paripācana [act. paripac] n. cooking | the act of bringing to maturity or perfecting.
paripārśva [paripārśva] amnf pa ripārśvā near; beside, familiar. paripārśvatas adv. beside, on either side of (g.).
paripālaka [agt. ca. paripā] amnf pa ripālikā who guards, who protects | who takes care of his property.
paripālana [act. paripā] nf paripālanā protection, preservation, conservation | maintenance.
paripīḍ [paripīḍ] v. [10] pr. (paripīḍayati) pp. (paripīdita) to torment.
paripīḍā [act. paripīḍ] f. torture, the act of tormenting.
paripīta [paripīta₁] amnf paripītā completely swallowed or bu. kalaśayoniparipītasāgarah the ocean swallowed by (Agasti) Nédansunpot.

paripūrņa [paripūrņa] amnf pa ripūrņā complete; exhaustive | accomplished; perfect — ifc. completely filled with (iic.). paripūrņagaņa [gaṇa] m. gram. exhaustive list of words having a grammatical specificity; opp. ākṛtigana.
paripṛcchaka [agt. paripraś] m. question neur; investigator.
paripṛcchā [act. paripraś] f. question, request for information; inquiry.
paripraś [paripraś] v. [6] pr. (pariprchati) pp. (paripṛṣṭa) to inquire about (acc.).
paripraśná [act. paripraś] m. question, in interrogation — ifc. examination of, question concerning (iic.). jātiparipraśne gram. to express a question concerning the species.
pariplavá [agt. pariplu] amnf pari plavā who swims; who moves about in all directions — act. m. swimming; flood | disorderly agitation oppression, tyranny.
pariplu [pariplu] v. [1] pr. r. (pariplávate) pp. (paripluta) to swim around, to swim in circles; to fly here and there.
paripluṣṭa [paripluṣṭa] amnf paripluṣṭā burned; reduced to ashes.
paribarha [act. paribṛh] m. procession, pomp.
paribṛh [paribṛh₁] v. [1] pr. (paribṛṃhati) to fortify, to surround.
paribhava [act. paribhū] m. insult; humiliation; rejection; contempt.
paribhavapada [pada] n. object of contempt. na syuḥ paribhavapadaṃ ke vā
niṣphalārambhayatnāḥ [Meghadūta] Anyone whose efforts are fruitless is an object of contempt.
paribhavavidhi | vidhi | mr. humiliation.
paribhāva [act. That. paribhū] m. contempt.
paribhāvin [agt. paribhū] amnf pa ribhāviṇī that insults, that humiliates, that despises — ifc. that defies (iic.). vaidyayatnaparibhāvī gadaḥ a disease that defies the efforts of doctors.
paribhāṣ [paribhāṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (pa ribhāsate) pp. (paribhāsita) to address, warn (acc.); reprimand | teach; explain, define.
paribhāṣaṇa [act. paribhāṣ] n. warn; reprimand.

paribhāṣā [act. paribhāṣ] f. address, discourse; explanation | admonition, reprimand, blame med. prognosis technical discourse, specialized terminology; formalism | gram. metalanguage; not. metalinguistic rule deciding the priority between formulas [sūtra] of the Asṭādhyāyī.
paribhāṣākāra [kāra] m. gram. author of rules of interpretation of the Astādhyāyī.

paribhāṣāvṛtti [vṛtti] f. bed. n.p. from the Pa ribhāṣāvrtti, a grammar work by Nīlakantha₂ Dīkṣita explaining the principles of interpretation of Pāṇini's grammar; other versions are the Laghuparibhāṣāvṛtti of Puruṣottamadeva, the Brhatparibhāṣāvṛtti of Sīradeva, and the Vyādīya paribhāṣāvṛtti.
paribhāṣāsūcanā [sūcanā] f. gram. n.p. of the Pa ribhāṣāsūcanā; cf. Vyādīyaparibhāṣāvṛtti.
paribhāṣāsūtra [sūtra] n. gram. metalinguistic rule of the Aṣṭādhyāyī.
paribhāṣenduśekhara [induśekhara] m. bed. n.p. of the Paribhāṣenduśekhara "Śiva of metalanguage", a grammar work by Nāgeśa Bhaṭṭa establishing the metalinguistic rules of Aştādhyāyī (18th century).
paribhāṣika [paribhāṣāika] amnf paribhāṣikā gram. concerning metalinguistic rules | technical; terminological; specialized.
paribhāṣikadharma [dharma] m. soc. regulations specific to a community; local custom.
paribhāṣita [pp. paribhāṣ] amnf paribhāṣitā explained, taught; stated as (nom.); established | used technically.
paribhāṣin [agt. paribhāṣ] ifc. amnf paribhāṣiṇī who says, who explains (iic.).
paribhū [paribhū₁] v. [1] pr. (paribha vati) pp. (paribhūta) to surpass; to despise, humiliate, mock.
paribhūti [act. paribhū] f. contempt, humiliation, insult.
paribhūṣ [paribhūṣ] v. [1] pr. (paribhūṣati) pp. (paribhūṣita) to turn around, circumambu ler; to honor; to follow, obey | to adorn, decorate.

paribhram [paribhram] v. [1] pr. (paribhra mati) v. [4] pr. (paribhrāmyati) pp. (paribhrānta) to wander, to meander | to circulate, to circle around — ca. (bhrāmayati) to agitate; to rotate. pradakṣiṇaṃ paribhram soc. to perform the ritual circumambulation around a shrine.
paribhrama [act. paribhram] m. wandering, di vagation; confused discourse.
parimaṇḍala [parimaṇḍala] amnf parimandalā round, circular; globular — m. bio. bed bug — n. math. ellipse; globe, sphere; circumference; orbit.
parimaṇḍalatā [tā] f. rotation; circularity, roundness.
parimardana [act. parimrd] n. polishing, cleaning, massage; action of rubbing.

Parimala₁ [pkt. parimrd] m. perfume (not. obtained by crushing odorous substances) | coitus; conjugal pleasure; syn. sambhoga | lit. np. of the Parimala₁, gloss of the Mahārthamañjarī by Maheśvarānanda | lit. [advaita] np. of the commentary [vākya] Parimala₁ of the Kalpataru, due to Appayya Dīkṣita.
parimā [parimā₁] v. [3] pr. r. (parimimīte) v. [2] pr. (parimāti) pp. (parimita) to measure around, to limit; to estimate, to survey.

parimāṇa [act. parimā] n. quantitative measure (of length, weight, capacity, etc.); not. periphery | phil. [Vaiseșika] the property [guṇa] of dimension and weight | gram. sequence of phonemes constituting a nominal stem | prātipadika | ; its length. parimāṇatas adv. in weight.
parimāṇin [in] amnf parimāṇinī measurable gram. said of a noun denoting an object that can be measured.
parimārg [parimārg] v. [10] pr. (pa rimārgati) pr. r. (parimārgate) to look around to strive to; to solicit something (acc.) (from someone (abl.)).
parimārgaṇa [act. parimārg] n. search (from left).
parimārgitavya [pfp. [3] parimārg] amnf parimārgittavyā which must be sought.
parimārgin [agt. parimārg] amnf parimārgiņī ifc. who continues (iic.).
parimārjana [act. parimṛj] n. cleaning, wiping | the act of removing by rubbing.
parimārjita [pp. parimrj] amnf pa rimārjitā cleaned, polished.
parimita [pp. parimā] amnf parimitā measured; limited.
parimukta [pp. parimuc] amnf pari muktā released; freed from (iic.).
parimukti [act. parimuc] f. release.
parimukham [parimukha] adv. in front of around the face; around, concerning (person).
parimugdha [pp. parimuh] amnf pari mugdhā whose beauty bewitches.

parimuc [parimuc₁] v. [4] pr. (parimuñcáti) pp. (parimukta) to free; to deliver from (abl.) to abandon, to separate from; to issue — ps. (pari mucyate) to free oneself; to get rid of (abl. gi) phil. to be freed (from worldly attachments) — ca. (parimocayati) to free, to emancipate.
parimuṣ [parimuṣ₁] v. [9] pr. (parimuṣṇāti) to steal, to plunder; to rob something from someone. 2 acc. .

parimuh [parimuh] v. [4] pr. (parimuhyati) pr. r. (parimuhyate) pp. (parimugdha, parimūdha) to be perplexed, to be troubled — ca. (parimohayati) ca. r. (parimohayate) to perplex, to trouble | to incite, to seduce.
parimūḍha [pp. parimuh] amnf pa rimūdhā perplexed, troubled.
parimṛj [parimṛj] v. [2] pr. (parimārṣṭi) pp. (parimṛṣṭa, parimṛjita) to wipe; to clean, to purify; to touch; to caress; to remove by rubbing, to erase; to remove, to eliminate.
parimṛja [agt. parimṛj] ifc. amnf parimṛjā that which rubs itself, that which cleans itself (iic.).
parimṛd [parimṛd₁] v. [9] pr. (parimṛdnāti) v. [1] pr. (parimardati) to crush, trample, pulverize | to rub, polish; to erase, clean; to wipe away (not. one's tears) | to surpass.

parimṛś [parimṛś] v. [1] pr. (parimṛśati) pp. (parimṛṣṭa) abs. (parimṛṣ́ya) to touch, seize, catch per | to examine, observe; to consider, investigate; to discover. pavanais parimṛśyate to be exposed to the breath of the wind.
parimṛṣ [parimṛṣ] v. [4] pr. (parimṛṣyati) to endure | to be angry towards, to envy (dat.).
parimṛṣṭa₁ [pp. parimṛś] amnf parimṛṣṭā wiped; rubbed; caressed; polished | erased, cleaned, removed.
parimṛṣṭa₂ [pp. parimṛś] amnf parimṛṣṭā caught, taken, discovered | observed | invaded by, filled with (i.).
parimeya [pfp. [1] parimā] amnf pari meyā measurable; limited; rare.
parimocita [pp. ca. parimuc] amnf parimocitā freed; emancipated.
parimoṣa [act. parimuṣ] m. flight.
parimoṣaṇa [act. parimuṣ] n. act of stealing.
parimlā [parimlā] v. [4] pr. r. (parimlāyate) pp. (parimlāna) to wither, to fade; to shrink, to vanish.
parimlāna [pp. parimlā] amnf pa rimlānā faded, withered; emaciated; flaccid | swooning; disappeared — n. depression.
pariyaj [pariyaj₁] v. [1] pr. (pariyajati) soc. obtain by sacrifice | soc. perform a secondary rite.
pariyajña [pariyajña] m. soc. secondary rite.
parirakṣ [parirakṣ] v. [1] pr. (parirakṣati) pp. (pariraksita) to guard, protect, defend against abl., save.
parirakṣita [pp. parirakṣ] amnf parirakṣitā well guarded, well defended.
parirakṣitṛ [agt. parirakṣ] amnf parirakṣitrī [sg. nom. parirakṣitā, acc. pariraksitāram guardian, protector. lokasya pariraksitā protector of the world.
parivad [parivad] v. [1] pr. (parivadati) by speaking about, to speak about (acc.) | to speak ill of; to blame, to censure.
parivarta [act. parivṛt] m. turn, revolution (not. of a planet) | travel time; year | money returned | lit. section of a work.

parivartana [agt. parivṛt] amnf parivartanī that which turns — act. n. rotation; revolution; accomplishment of a period of time | barter; exchange | gram. grammatical turn; evolution of language; diachronicity.
parivartanīya [pfp. [2] parivṛt] amnf parivartanīyā to exchange.

parivartin [agt. parivṛt] amnf pa rivartinī turning, running around; operating its revolution. parivartini saṃsāre mṛtaḥ ko vā na jāyate [Hit.] In this round of transmigrations, who is dead and who is not born?
parivas [parivas₁] v. [1] pr. (parivasati) pp. (paryusita, paryusita) abs. (paryusya) pass, stay; stay (with (i.)) — ca. (parivāsayati) to spend the night.
parivah [parivah₁] v. [1] pr. (parivahati) to lead around (not. the wedding fire); to marry | to overflow.
parivaha [agt. parivah] m. myth. np. of Pa rivaha, one of the 7 celestial Winds; he supports the stars of the Great Bear and pushes before him the waves of the celestial Ganges (Milky Way).
parivādá [act. parivad] m. blame, censure, reproach; calumny, slander about g. | var. parīvāda id.
parivādin [agt. parivad] amnf pa rivādinī who blames, who defames, who speaks ill of, who insults | insulted — m. accuser, complainant — f. parivādinī mus. 7-stringed lute.
parivāra [agt. parivṛ] m. cover; case, sheath; palisade | suite, surroundings, circle, court,
party | family | var. parīvāra id.
parivāraka [ka] m. id..
parivāha [act. parivah] m. overflow, flood | drain; overflow; spillway var. parīvāha id.
parivāhin [agt. parivah] ifc. amnf parivāhinī which overflows with (iic.).

pariviṣ [pariviṣ₁] v. [1] pr. (pariveṣati) pp. (parivista) to serve; to serve food — ps. (parivisyate) to be served | to have a halo (moon) — ca. (pariveṣayati) to be in the service of (acc.); to offer (nour riture) — intens. (parivevești) subj. (parivevișati) to do the service.
páriviṣṭa [pp. pariviṣ] amnf pariviṣṭā ved. encircled, besieged | surrounded by a halo (moon) | offered, presented (food).
páriviṣṭi [act. pariviṣ] f. service, support.
parivṛ [parivṛ₁] v. [5] pr. (parivṛṇóti) pp. (parivṛta) to wrap, to surround — ca. (pa rivārayati) pp. (parivārita) id.
parivṛkta [pp. parivṛj] amnf parivṛktā avoided; abandoned, neglected — f. parivṛktī soc. neglected royal wife; opp. mahiṣī, vāvātā.
parivṛj [parivṛj] pp. (parivṛkta) ca. (pari varjayati) to avoid; to abandon, to neglect.

parivṛt [parivṛt₁] v. [1] pr. r. (parivartate) pp. (parivṛtta) pf. (vi) to turn around, to go around in circles | to return, to come back to; to turn around | to change, to become different — ca. (parivartayati) to turn around, to turn over, to invert; to change, to make different.
parivṛta [pp. parivṛ] amnf parivṛtā en touré par, couvert de, voilelé par (i. iic.).
parivṛtta [pp. parivṛt] amnf parivṛttā turned; revolu — n. rolling.
parivṛtti [act. parivṛt] f. turn, revolution; the act of rolling.
pariveṣa [act. pariviṣ] m. service, presentation (of food) | circle, circumference; disc, halo; crown, aureole | protection (by a guard) | the act of dressing.
pariveṣṭ [pariveṣṭ] pp. (pariveṣṭita) ca. (pariveștayati) to wrap, surround; to cover.
pariveșțita [pp. pariveșț] amnf pariveștitā surrounded (from (i. iic.)); covered.
parivraj [parivraj] v. [1] pr. (parivrájati) pp. (parivrajita) wander; to be a wandering monk.
parivrāj [agt. parivraj] m. [name. parivrāt] wandering monk | var. parivrāja id.
parivrājaka [agt. parivraj] mf pa rivrājikā wandering monk, ascetic.
pariśańk [pariśańk] v. [1] pr. r. (pariśankate) pp. (pariśankita) to doubt; to suspect, to distrust (acc.); to fear something from someone. abl. | to suppose, to believe that something is 2 acc.
pariśańkita [pp. pariśańk] amnf pariśankitā suspicious, who distrusts (abl. iic.); who fears | suspect.
pariśiṣ [pariśiṣ] v. [7] pr. (pariśinaṣṭi) pp. (pariśiṣṭa) to leave, to leave as a remainder — ps. (pariśisyate) to remain; to stay behind.
pariśiṣṭa [pp. pariśiṣ] amnf pariśiṣṭā left as remainder, remained | miscellaneous — n. supplement, appendix (qualifies late ancillary works of ritual treatises [sūtra], not. of the Atharvaveda).
pariśīl [pariśīl] ca. (pariśīlayati) pp. (pariśīlita) to practice, to cultivate; to use frequently; to cherish.
pariśīlana [act. pariśīl] n. touch, contact — ifc. attachment to, sexual contact with (iic.) | practice of, study of (iic.).
pariśīlita [pp. pariśīl] amnf pariśīlitā practiced, employed; pursued, studied.
pariśuddha [pp. pariśudh] amnf pariśuddhā cleaned, purified; pure | acquitted — ifc. diminished by (iic.). raktabhāvam apahāya candramā jāta eşa
pariśuddhamandalah [KuS.] Abandoning its redness, the moon became this immaculate disc.
pariśuddhi [act. pariśudh] f. complete purification; acquittal, exoneration | correction; justice.

pariśudh [pariśudh] v. [4] pr. (pariśudhyati) pp. (pariśuddha) to be cleansed — pr. r. (pariśudhyate) to cleanse oneself, to purify oneself | to justify oneself, to proclaim one's innocence — ca. (pariśodhayati) to cleanse, to purify | to resolve.
pariśuṣ [pariśuṣ₁] v. [1] pr. (pariśuṣyati) pr. r. (pariśusyate) pp. (pariśuska) to dry out completely; to wither — ca. (parisosayati) to dry out completely; to emaciate.
pariśuṣka [pp. pariśuṣ] amnf pariśuskā dried; parchment-like; shrunken; emaciated (face), hollow (cheek) — n. (av. māmsa) dried and spiced fried meat.
pariśodha [act. pariśudh] m. cleaning, purification.
pariśodhana [act. pariśudh] n. cleaning, purification | settlement, the act of paying off.
pariśoṣa [act. pariśuṣ] m. desiccation; evaporation. parisosam gam se dessècher; devenir sec; slender.
pariśoṣaṇa [agt. pariśuṣ] amnf pariśoṣaṇī which dries, which dries out — n. desi cation; the act of losing weight.
pariśram [pariśram] v. [4] pr. (pariśrāmyati) pp. (pariśrānta) to tire oneself, to exhaust oneself — ca. (pariśrāmayati) to tire, to exhaust.
pariśrama [act. pariśram] m. fatigue, effort, labor; uninterrupted study.
pariśrānta [pp. pariśram] amnf pariśrāntā very tired, exhausted, worn out.
pariśri [pariśri] v. [1] pr. (pariśrayati) pp. (pariśrita) to surround, encircle, enclose.
pariśrit [agt. pariśri] f. pl. soc. aligned stones surrounding the Vedic altar, numbering 21.
pariśrita [pp. pariśri] amnf pariśritā surrounded by (i. iic.).
pariṣad₁ [parisad₁] v. [1] pr. (pariṣīdati) to sit around; to besiege, to encircle.
parisád₂ var. parṣad [agt. pariṣad₁] amnf that encircles, that harasses — act. f. assembly, meeting; circle, council; audience.
pariṣkāra [act. pariṣkṛ] m. preparation cu linaire | domestic utensils; instruments; mo bilier | phil. [Nyāya] clarification. rājñah pariṣkāra soc. set of royal attributes.
pariskr cf. parikr.
pariṣkṛta [pp. pariṣkṛtā prepared; improved, embellished, decorated; furnished (by (i. iic.) | cooked, prepared | soc. purified by initiatory rites | phil. clarified.
pariṣṭhā₁ [paristhā₁] v. [1] pr. (paritiṣṭhati) pr. r. (paritisthate) pp. (paristhita) to stand around, to obstruct; to hinder the passage | to form a crowd around.
pariṣṭhā₂ [act. pariṣṭhā₁] f. obstruction.
pariṣvakta [pp. pariṣvañj] amnf parișvaktā embraced, embraced; encircled, surrounded.
pariṣvaṅga [act. pariṣvañj] m. embrace, hug, embrace.
pariṣvañj [parisvañj] v. [1] pr. r. (parișvajate) pp. (parișvakta) to surround, encircle; to embrace, press in one's arms.
parisaṃkhyā₁ [parisaṃkhyā₁] v. [2] pr. (parisamkhyāti) pp. (parisamkhyāta) to count, to enumerate; to add; to delimit.

parisamkhyā₁ [act. parisamkhyā₁] f. enumeration; calculation; sum, total, number phil. exhaustive enumeration; limitation to this enumeration | lit. [Subandhu] "delimitation", suggestive rhetorical device of wordplay.
parisamkhyāvidhi [vidhi] m. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] in ritual junction of exclusion.
parisamkhyāta [pp. parisamkhyā₁] amnf parisamkhyātā enumerated, specified exclusively ment.
parisamkhyāna [act. parisamkhyā₁] n. enumeration; total; exclusive specification | phil. [yoga] method of meditation.

parisamāp [parisamāp] v. [5] pr. (parisamāpnoti) pp. (parisamāpta) to accomplish, complete, fill — ps. (parisamāpyate) to be filled; to be contained in. iti parisamāptam this concludes this document; end.
parisara [agt. parisr़] amnf parisarā ad adjacent, contiguous; neighbor — m. site; proximity, neighborhood; surroundings.
parisarpita [pp. That. parisrp] amnf parisarpitā cf. Parisrpta.
parisāntva [parisāntva] v. [11] pr. (pa risāntvayati) to appease, to calm.
parisāra [act. parisr़] m. perambulation.
parisṛ [parisṛ] v. [1] pr. (parisarati) pp. (parisrta) to turn around, to circumambulate; to go around | to go back and forth, to perambulate.
parisrp [parisrp] v. [1] pr. (parisarpati) pp. (parisrpta) to swarm; to cover by crawling (insects, worms) | to approach by crawling.
parisṛpta [pp. parisṛp] amnf parisṛptā covered in vermin.
paristaraṇa [act. paristṛ] n. soc. act of strewing kuśa grass around the sacrificial fire.
paristṛ [paristṛ] v. [5] pr. (paristṛṇoti) pr. r. (paristṛṇute) pp. (stīrṇa) to spread, to scatter; to envelop per.

parispand [parispand] v. [1] pr. r. (pa rispandate) pp. (parispandita) ppr. r. (parispan damāna) to quiver, throb, vibrate, tremble. aparispandamāna gram. qualifies an action without movement, denoted by a nominal phrase.
parispanda [act. parispand] m. pulsation, vibration, palpitation; movement.
parispardhin [parispardhin] ifc. amnf parispardhinī that rivals, that emulates (iic.).
parisphuța [parisphuța] amnf parisphuțā prominently, visible.
parisphur [parisphur] v. [6] pr. (parisphu rati) to tremble, to throb, to quiver; to vibrate. paryasphuran me daksinabhujah [DKC.] My right arm began to throb (a sign of good fortune).
parisrava [agt. parisru] m. current, stream. garbhaparisrava childbirth, giving birth.
parisru [parisru] v. [1] pr. (parisravati) pp. (parisruta) to flow, to run from or around.
parisruta [pp. parisru] amnf parisrutā that flows, that runs; flowed — amnf paris rut that foams, that ferments — f. parisrut fermented alcoholic drink, beer.
parihan [parihan₁] v. [2] pr. (parihanti) circ to consecrate; to extinguish (fire) — ps. (parihaṇyate) to be altered; to perish.
parihartavya [pfp. [3] parihr] amnf parihartavyā to be avoided. mūrkhaḥ parihartavyaḥ pratyakṣaḥ dvipadaḥ paśuh The fool, who is only perceptible as a bipedal beast, is to be avoided.
parihas [pariHas] v. [1] pr. (parihasati) pr. r. (parihasate) pp. (parihasita) to amuse oneself, to mock, to laugh at (acc.); to ridicule. na parihasāmi I am not joking.

parihā [parihā₁] v. [3] pr. (parijahāti) pp. (parihāṇa) to leave, abandon | omit; neglect, disdain — ps. (parihīyate) to be abandoned, to be cast aside; to be excluded from or deprived of (abl. i.) | decline; wither — ca. (hāpayati) to give up; to interrupt. na tarhi prāgavasthāyāḥ parihīyase you are not then in a worse situation than before. tvatto na kimapi parihāsyate you will lack nothing.
parihāṇa [pp. parihā] amnf parihāṇā private (of (iic. abl.)) — n. state of deprivation; souf france.
parihāṇi [act. parihā] f. loss; deprivation; decline, deficiency.
parihāpaṇīya [pfp. [2] ca. parihā] amnf parihāpaṇīyā which must be omitted.
parihāpita [pp. ca. parihā] amnf pa rihāpitā deprived of, robbed of.
parihāra [act. parihṛ] m. act of avoiding, abandoning, yielding | exemption, privilege, immunity | wastelands around a village or town.
parihāravat [vat] amnf parihāravatī évitable — ind. ifc. as the omission of (iic.).
parihārya [pfp. [1] parihṛ] amnf pa rihāryā to be avoided; which must be omitted.

Parihāsa [act. parihas] m. joke, prank, farce; mockery, ridicule; the act of laughing or making fun of | lit. |K.| np. of the parrot Parihāsa "Joker", fickle husband of the mynah Kālindī₁ | var. parīhāsa id. nāyam parihāsasya samayah I am not in the mood to joke. alam krtam parihāsena quite a joke. parihāsavijalpita said in jest, in a playful manner.

parihṛ [parihṛ₁] v. [1] pr. (pariharati) pp. (parihṛta) pfp. (parihārya) to envelop — pr. r. (pa riharate) to leave, abandon; to avoid, abstain from acc. | refute. mṛgayākṣastrīpānābhiratim pariharet |Viṣṇusmṛti| (The king) must abstain from the pleasures of alcohol, women, gambling, and hunting.
parihṛta [pp. parihṛ] amnf parihṛtā avoided; refuted.
parī [parii] v. [2] pr. (paryeti) pp. (parīta) pf. (vi, sam) to surround, to include; to walk around (not. fire).
parī₁ pf. pari.
parīkṣ [pariīkṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (parīkṣate) pp. (parīkṣita) to look at carefully, to consider; to investigate, to examine; to test, to verify.
parīkṣaka [agt. parīkṣ] amnf parīkṣikā who examines — m. expert; examiner, inspector.

parīkṣā [act. parīkṣ] f. examination, inspection, investigation; verification; evaluation | test; judgment by ordeal. ghatikāvimśati parīkṣā 8-hour examination. ratnaparīkṣā evaluation of precious stones.
parīkṣādhikārin [adhikārin] m. certifying examiner.

Parīkṣit var. Parikṣit [parīkṣita] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the kaurava king Parīkṣit or Parikṣit "who reigns around", son of Abhimanyu and Uttarā; stillborn as a result of a curse from Aśvatthāmā, he was resurrected by₁ Kṛṣṇa having pity on Uttarā and succeeded the Pāṇḍavās on the throne of Has tināpura; Janamejaya is his son; Having received a curse from a young Brahmin to die within the week, he renounced the throne in favor of his eldest son Sala₁ and spent his last days fasting at Śukatīrtha on the banks of the Ganges, where the sage Suka told him the Bhāgavatapurāṇa, inaugurating the tradition of saptāha; he was killed by the nāga Takṣaka.
parīkṣita [pp. parīkṣ] amnf parīkṣitā examined, tested.
parīkṣitavya [pfp. [3] parīkṣ] amnf parīkṣitavyā to try, to test, to verify.
parīkṣya [pfp. [1] parīkṣ] amnf parīkṣyā to try, to test, to verify.
parīta [pp. parī] amnf parītā past, elapsed surrounded by; taken from, invaded by (i. iic.). rosaparīta furious.
párīman [parī₁man] n. abundance, plenitude — adv. in abundance.
parīvāda cf. parivāda.
parīvāra cf. parivāra.
parīvāha cf. parivāha.
parīśāsa [parī₁śāsa₁] m. excision; cut part, skin of the parīśāsau véd horns of an tilopes used as tongs to pour the mahāvīra pot at the end of the pravargya.
parīṣ [pariiṣ₂] v. [1] pr. (paryeṣati) to search, to look for.
parīṣā [act. parīṣ] ifc. f. investigation of (iic.).
parīṣṭi [act. parīṣ] f. research, investigation, inquiry | service, homage.
parīhāsa cf. parihāsa.
appeared [related to para] adv. last year.
paruṣa amnf paruṣā hard, rough, coarse, unpleasant | harsh, stiff; stiff (hair); dirty.
Paruṣṇī [paruṣana] f. geo. np. of the Paruṣṇī river (mod. Rāvī), which flows in Pañjāb; cf. dāśarājña.
pare₁ [loc. para] iic.

pare₂ [parāi] v. [2] pr. (paraiti) pp. (pareta) pf. (anu, vi) to go away, to leave, to go towards (acc.); to rejoin — ca. (palāyati) ca. r. (palāyate) to flee, to flee from, to fly away; to cease, to disappear.
paredyavi [dyu] adv. the day after.
paredyus [dyu] adv. tomorrow.
pareta [pp. pare₂] amnf paretā parti; dead.
paraiya [pfp. [1] pare₂] amnf paraiyā who must leave | soc. outcast; pariah.

parokṣa [parasakṣa] amnf parokṣā out of sight; invisible; opp. pratyakșa | absent; foreign, unknown; incomprehensible; secret | gram. whose etymology is not evident — f. parokṣā gram. perfect tense; its conjugation [vibhakti]; cf. lit — v. [11] pr. r. (parokṣāyate) to act as if out of sight. parokṣam var. parokṣe adv. out of sight | without the knowledge of, in the absence of, behind the back of (ig iic.). parokṣāt adv. secretly, without the knowledge of (i.). paroksena adv. out of sight; secretly, mysteriously. parokṣekṣam adv. behind his back. pārokṣe lit gram. (When the action refers to the past to the exclusion of the present day) and outside the speaker's perception, the perfect tense lakāra is used. parokṣakāmā hi devāḥ The gods love mystery.
parokṣakṛta [kṛta] amnf parokṣakṛtā soc. refers to a hymn in which the deity is addressed to the 3rd person.
parokṣatā [tā] f. invisibility; imperceptibility | gram. condition of use of the perfect tense for a past action which the speaker did not witness.
parokṣatva [tva] n. invisibility; imperceptibility.
parokṣavāda [vāda] m. phil. esoteric doctrine.
parokṣārtha [artha] amnf parokṣārthā phil. whose meaning is secret — m. that which is hidden from sight.
paropakāra [paraupakāra] m. relief, aid, charity; benevolence.
paropakāritva |tva| n. act of coming to the aid of the sow.
paropakārin |in| amnf paropakāriņī chari table.
paropatāpitva [paraupatāpitva] n. act of harming others.
parovaram [parasvara₂] adv. in succession.
parka [act. prc] ifc. mr. mixture of (iic.).
parkața m. heron — n. regret; anxiety — f. parkati bio. bot. Ficus infectoria, Indian fig; syn. plaksa.
parjanya m. cloud (of rain); rain; thunder ved. np. of parjanya "Storm", atmospheric god associated with or confused with Indra.

parņá n. wing, feather; leaf | betel leaf (mod. pāṇ) — m. bio. bot. Butea frondosa, sacred tree (legume) with large trifoliate leaves from which disposable plates are made, and with large clusters of salmon-pink and orange flowers; syn. palāśa — f. parņī ifc. names of trees | ang. fern.
parṇamaya [maya] amnf parṇamayī made of flamboyant wood. parnamayīnyāyah maxim (of the oblation spoon | juhū|) made of flamboyant wood; it is invoked when a prescription is obligatory.
parṇamṛga |mṛga| m. bio. arboreal animal: squirrel, etc.
parṇaśālā |śālā| f. leaf hut.
parṇāśā |āśā₁| f. myth. |Mah.| np. of the river parṇāśā; she had as a son of Varuṇa the king Srutāyudha.
parṇin [parṇain] amnf parṇinī which has feathers, which has wings; leafy — m. bio. bot. Butea frondosa; cf. parna.
parpața m. thin lentil flour pancake, fried or grilled; mod. pappadam.
paryanka [parianka] m. daybed, sofa; bed; palanquin | sitting position on the floor with legs crossed | var. palyańka id. | pali pallańka; fr. palanquin. paryankīkṛta transformed into bed.
paryankabandha | bandha | mr. “sitting cross-legged” posture.
paryankabandhana |na| n. id.
paryankha [pariankha] v. [11] pr. (pa ryankhayati) to kiss, to embrace.

paryaṭ [pariaṭ] v. [1] pr. r. (paryaṭate) pp. (paryatita) to wander; to travel through (acc. loc.). paryaṭaṃś ca diśām antān kālaṃ kañcid avāhayat |Mahārthamañjarī| He spent his time traveling to the ends of the world.
paryaṭaka [agt. paryaṭ] amnf paryaṭikā traveler; vagabond.
paryaṭaṇa [act. paryaṭ] n. wandering; journey mod. tourism.
paryaṭita [pp. paryaṭ] amnf paryaṭitā who has wandered — n. peregrination.
paryadhyayana [pariadhyayana] amnf paryadhyayanā tired of studying.
paryanuyoga [parianuyoga] m. the act of questioning with a view to refutation.
paryanuyojya [parianuyojya] amnf paryanuyojyā which must be censored.
paryanuyojyopekṣaṇa [upekṣaṇa] n. the act of neglecting to point out an error by one's opponent, one of the criteria for losing a debate.

paryantá [parianta] m. limit, border, edge, extremity; circuit, circumference | conclusion — amnf paryantā ifc. surrounded by; extending as far as, to, or as far as | extending in all directions — iic. near, close to. paryantam entirely, completely. paryante at the end. paryantāt paryantam from one end to the other. Xtah Y paryantam mod. from X to Y
Paryantapañcāśikā [pañcāśikā] f. lit. np. of the Paryantapañcāśikā "Fifty stanzas on the Ulti me", phil. poem attributed to Abhinavagupta.

paryaya [act. parī] m. revolution, by course; lapse, period | astr. time of revolution of a planet | change; alteration; inversion deviation, non-conformity to custom; failure to fulfill one's duties gram. polysemy; evolution dia chronicle. kālasya paryayaḥ lapse of time.
paryavasā [pariavasā] v. [4] pr. (paryava syati) pp. (paryavasita) to end by (loc. pratiacc.); to come to its conclusion.
paryavasāna [act. paryavasā] n. concluded sion, outcome; act of returning to (loc.). paryavasānāt as a consequence of.
paryávasita [pp. paryavasā] amnf pa ryavasitā finished, concluded, due; decided, definitive | which comes back to (loc.).

paryavasthā [pariavasthā₁] v. [1] pr. r. (paryavatisthate) pp. (paryavasthita) to firm up, stabilize; to compose itself | to fill, to permeate — ca. (paryavasthāpayati) to comfort, to encourage. sa nādyāpi paryavasthāpayati ātmānam he has not yet recovered.

paryas [parias₂] v. [4] pr. (paryasyati) pr. r. (paryasyate) pp. (paryastá) pf. (vi) to throw around; to distribute, to spread | to encircle, to trap — ca. (paryāsayati) to roll; to make shed (tears).
paryasta [pp. paryas] amnf paryastā thrown around, distributed, diffused | encircled, trapped overturned; reversed.
paryākula [pariākula] amnf paryākulā troubled, agitated; confused — ifc. full of, filled with (iic.).
paryāp [pariāp] v. [5] pr. (paryāpnóti) pp. (paryāpta) to cease, to limit oneself to — des. (parīpsati) to desire, to desire to obtain — pr. r. (paryāpnuté) dear dear to attain.

paryāpta [pp. paryāp] amnf paryāptā obtained, earned; sufficient, abundant; adequate, complete, perfect, finished. paryāptam adv. completely; enough, sufficiently, at will. paryāptamācāmati drink to satiety.

paryāpti [act. paryāp] f. completion; finishing, completion; conclusion | completeness; sufficiency; totality | obtaining, acquisition | adequacy, relevance; the state of being appropriate | phil. distinction of objects according to their properties; intensionality — ifc. proper to, which serves to (iic.).
paryāptiniveśa [niveśa] m. phil. [NN.] insertion of relevance.
paryābhū [pariābhū₁] v. [1] pr. (paryābhavati) to overturn. daksinena ced yāyām tarhi na śakaṭam paryābhavet I prefer to go by the South to avoid the chariot overturning.

paryāya [act. parī] m. turn, revolution, course; repetition, succession; manner of proceeding; period, interval of time; time; recurring sequence; repeated formula | gram. synonym; equivalent term. Normal development of a phenomenon from beginning to end. paryāyeṇa adv. one after the other; successively; alternately. tava paryāyah it's your turn. mama paryāyah it's my turn. caturthe paryāye at the 4th time.
paryāyakrama | krama | mr. order of succession; normal turn.
paryāyacyuta | cyuta | amnf paryāyacyutā who has lost his turn; ousted.
paryāyapada | padah | n. gram. synonymous word.
paryāyabandha [bandha] m. lit. set of independent verses dealing with the same subject.
Paryāyamuktāvalī [muktāvalī] f. bed. n.p. from the Paryāyamuktāvalī, a dictionary of medicinal terms by Haricarana Sena; it is inspired by the paryāyaratnamālā.
paryāyaratnamālā [ratnamālā] f. lit. np. from the paryāyaratnamālā, dictionary of synonyms of botanical terms and medicinal plants due to Mādhavakara (circa 700).
paryāyavakratā [vakratā] f. lit. [Kuntaka] oblique quality of the use of synonyms.
paryāyaśabdaratna [śabdaratna] n. hist. n.p. from the thesaurus paryāyaśabdaratna, due to Dhanañjaya₂ Bhaṭṭācārya.
paryāyaśas [śas] adv. periodically; successively, one after the other.
paryāyārtha [artha] m. bed. dictionary of synonyms.
paryāyokta | ukta | n. lit. figure of speech | alaṃkāra | where the signified fact is evoked by a turn of phrase or a paraphrase.
paryāloc [pariāloc] ca. (paryālocayati) to consider.
paryālocana [act. paryāloc] n. consideration; reflection — f. paryālocanā id.
paryālocita [pp. paryāloc] amnf paryālocitā considered, examined.
paryāvṛt [pariāvṛt₁] v. [1] pr. r. (paryāvartate) pp. (paryāvrtta) to turn around; to turn away from (abl.); to return to (dat.) — ca. (paryāvartayati) to turn around.
paryāsá [act. paryas] m. act of cutting; rotation; resolution | conclusion; not. concluding stanzas of a hymn.
paryāsita [pp. ca. paryas] amnf paryāsitā thrown; destroyed.
paryāhāra [pariāhāra] m. yoke for bearer, palanquin.
paryutsuka [pariutsuka] amnf paryut sukā very excited, feverish | zealous; very eager for, eager to dat. .
paryutsukatva |vat| n. ardent zeal.
paryudas [pariudas] v. [4] pr. (paryuda syati) pp. (paryudasta) to reject, to exclude.
paryudasta [pp. paryudas] amnf pa ryudastā rejected; excluded.
paryudāsa [act. paryudas] m. gram. prohibitive rule, exclusion; exception.
paryudāsapratisedha | pratisedha | m. gram. negation as non-existence or exclusion; the scope of the privative prefix is restricted (opp. prasajyapratisedha).
paryupasthita [pariupasthita] amnf paryupasthitā that surrounds (acc.) | that will occur; imminent | that escapes (word) | desirous of, devoted to (loc.).
paryupās [pariupās] v. [2] pr. r. (pa ryupāste) pp. (paryupāsita) to sit around, to circle; to take part in, to enjoy [acc.] | to honor, to be vir; to seek refuge.

paryupāsita [pp. paryupās] amnf pa ryupāsitā in which one has participated | honored, served. brāhmaṇān paryupāsīta prātar utthāya pārthivaḥ traividyavrddhān vidusas tisthet tesām ca śāsane | [Manu] that the prince, rising early in the morning, honors the wise Brahmins instructed in the three Vedas, and follows their instructions.

paryuṣaṇa [act. parivas] n. jn. Jain festival of preaching and fasting during the monks' residence in the rainy season, during the clear fortnight of the month of bhādrapada; it lasts 8 days for the śvetāmbarās (until caturthī) 10 days for the di gambarās (from pañcamī).
paryuṣita [pp. parivas] amnf paryuṣitā who spent the night (at (iic.)) | stale, windy, past, not fresh. paryusitam vākyam broken promise.
paryuṣṭa [pp. parivas] amnf paryuṣṭā not fresh, stale; faded, wrinkled, old.
parva iic. parvan.
parvadhi |dhi| m. the Moon |"which contains the phases"].
párvata [parvan] m. mountain; mountain range; hill; rock | math. symb. the number 7 (cf. kulaparvata) — f. parvatā ifc. mountain of, heap of.
párvatamastaka | mastaka | mn mountain peak.

párvatavāsin [vāsin₁] amnf parvatavāsinī who lives in the mountains — m. mountain dweller — f. by vatavāsinī bio. bot. Nardostachys grandiflora, Indian spikenard; its rhizome is used for its perfume and in medicine.
parvatāgra | agra | n. summit.
párvan [pṛvan] n. knot (of a stem), joint,

joint | limb | lit. section of a book; not. one of the 18 sections of the Mah.: ādi, sabhā, vana, virāṭa, udyoga, bhīṣma, droṇa, karṇa, śalya, sauptika, strī, śānti, anuśāsana, āśvamedhika, āśramavāsika, mausala, mahāprasthānika, and svargārohaṇa | occasion, favorable moment; decisive day, fateful day | soc. festival, consecrated day; not. festival of cāturmāsya | astr. fortnight (lunar); one of the 4 days marking the phases of a lunar month.
párśu m. ved. rib; sickle.
parṣad [contr. pariṣad₂] f. assembly, meeting; company, society.

parṣadbhīru [bhīru] amnf shy in society. প্ল pala m. straw — n. measure of weight (4 gold pieces, about 40 g) or of volume (about 90 ml); one pala is worth 4 karṣa; there are 32 (or 16) in a prastha, 100 in a tulā | measure of time of 24 seconds; there are 60 in a ghațī | lat. palea; fr. straw.
palāṇḍu [palaaṇḍa] m. organic. bot. Allium cepa, onion.

palāy [related to pare₂] v. [1] pr. (palāyati) pr. r. (pálāyate) pp. (palāyita) abs. (palāyya) aor. r. [5] (palāyiṣṭa) pf. (pra) to flee, to run away, to fly away; to cease, to disappear | ang. to flee. yadā senāpatirhatastadā sainikāh palāyanti When the army commander was killed, the soldiers fled from him.
palāyana |act. palāy| n. flight, retreat; escape.
palāyanamanas [manas] amnf ["who has flight in mind"] who thinks of escaping.
palāyya [abs. palāy] ind. having fled.
palāla |related to pala| mn stem; straw — f. palālī id. — f. Palālā myth. [Mah.] np. of Palālā, one of the 7 "mothers (dangerous) to children" | sisumātaras | associated with Skanda.

palāśa m. bio. bot. Butea frondosa, Palas tree or flamboyant; syn. kimśuka, parna | bio. bot. Curcuma zedoaria | cochineal; red lacquer — ifc. splendor of (iic.) — n. bio. the flamboyant flower, large orange cluster | leaf, petal; foliage — f. palāśī ifc. leaf of (iic.) — f. palāśī variety of climbing plant. palāśakusumabhrāntyā śukatuņde patatyalih Deceived by its resemblance to the flamboyant flower, the bee falls into the parrot's beak.
palitá amnf palitā grey, white; greying, hoary; aged — n. pl. palitāni grey or white hair | gr. πολιος; lat. palleo; fr. pale. palitāḥ grey or white hair (by ellipsis of keśāh).
palitávat |vat| amnf palitavatī who has grey hair.
palī [f. pati] f. mistress of the house; wife | soc. village chief.

Pallava mn bud, shoot, young shoot | turban — m. ritual gesture [mudrā] of the shoot (4 joined fingers raised) | pl. Pallavās geo. name of the people of the Pallavās of the Deccan; the Pallava dynasty reigned in Kāñcī from the 3rd to the 9th century, succeeding the Sātavāhanās — v. [11] pr. (pallavayati) to spread, disseminate, divulge (news).
pallavita [pp. Pallava] amnf pallavitā germinated; budded | amplified; exaggerated | lacquered. alam pallavitena let's stop embroidering.
pallī var. pali f. hut; hamlet; village.

pavana [agt. pū₁] amnf pavanī clean, neat, pure — m. air, breeze, Wind | myth. np. of pavana "Purifier", epith. of Vāyu the Wind; he is father of Hanumān by Añjanā | phil. vital breath; there are 5 [prānās] | math. symb. the number 5 — n. cleaning, purification | instrument of purification; filter, sieve, strainer, winnowing fan — f. pavanā ifc. wind of (iic.).
pávanatanaya [tanaya] m. bed. n.p. from Pavanata naya, epith. of Bhīmasena “son of the wind”.
pávanadūta [dūta] m. lit. np. from the Pavanadūta "The Messenger Wind", poem by Dhoyī (12th century); it is an imitation of the Meghadūta, where a young gand harvī sends a message to Lakṣmaṇasena.
pavanāśana [aśana₂] m. snake ["that feeds on air"]; syn. śvasanabhuj.

pavamāna [ppr. mo. pū₁] amnf pa vamānā being purified; flowing clear (said of soma) — m. ved. song of praise |stotra| sung by the sāmaga during the jyotistoma sacrifice; there are three for each of the three pressings |savana₁|: bahispavamāna, mādhyaṃdina and tṛtīya or ārbhava.
pavarga [(pa)varga] m. phone. biales class.
pavi [agt. pū₁] m. ved. Indra's thunderbolt.
pavidhara [dhara] m. myth. epith. of Indra "lightning bearer".
pavitṛ [agt. pū₁] amnf pavitrī that purifies; purifier.

pavitra [instr. pū₁] n. ["instrument of purification" | sieve, filter, strainer; not. soma sieve, Brahmanic cord; syn. upavīta | purification, soc. purification mantra | soc. (two) stalks of kuśa grass braided into a ring for perching or holding offerings; the priest places it on the middle finger of the right hand — m. soc. festival of tan tuparvan, in honor of Kṛṣṇa — amnf pa vitrā that purifies; that removes sin; sacred — v. [11] pr. (pavitrayati) pp. (pavitrita) to cleanse, purify; to make happy. pavitrīkṛ to cleanse, purify, sanctify. pavitrībhū to purify oneself. na hi jñānena sadršam pavitramiha vidyate [BhG.] There is no better purification than knowledge here below.
pavitratā |tā| f. purity, cleanliness.
pavitrāropaṇa [āropaṇa] n. soc. investiture of the sacred gift; syn. upanayana | not. festival celebrating the initiation of Kṛṣṇa, celebrated at cf. tantuparvan.
pavitrin [in] amnf pavitriņī which purifies, purifying; pure, clear.
pavitrita [pp. pavitra] amnf pavitritā clean, pure; cleansed, purified, sanctified; happy.
pavitra.
pavitrīkṛta |kṛta| amnf pavitrīkṛtā purified, sanctified. dṛḍhadasyunāmnā pavitrīkṛtam Dṛḍhadasyu was his consecrated name.

paśú m. beast, domestic animal; livestock; opp. mrga | soc. sacrificial animal | phil. soul | soc. uninitiated | lat. pecus; ang. fee; all. Vieh. apaśavah vā anye go'śvebhah There is no other livestock than cattle, horses and elephants.
paśutrp [trp₂] amnf cattle lover; cattle thief.
paśutva |tva| n. animal condition; bestiality.
paśudharma [dharma] m. animal behavior, instinct | copulation, bestiality | soc. refers to the remarriage of widows.

paśupati [pati] m. myth. np. of paśupati, the "Master of souls", epith. of Shiva, personification of ritual sacrifice; charged by the gods to stop the primordial incest committed by Brahmā, he cut off his fifth head with the weapon Pāsupata; he is the tutelary deity of Nepal; cf. Lakulīśa.
Paśupatinātha | nātha | m. geo. np. of Paśupatinātha, principal Shaivite sanctuary of Nepal, on the banks of the Vānmatī river.
paśupatimata [mata] n. phil. Saiva doctrine of Pasupati of Nepal.
paśupālya [pālya] n. cattle breeding.
paśupurodāśa [purodāśa] m. soc. cake offered on the occasion of an animal sacrifice.
pasuprerana [prerana] n. cattle herding.
paśubandhá [bandha] m. soc. cattle sacrifice.
paśumat [mat] amnf paśumatī who owns cattle; rich in cattle — m. cattle owner.
pasumāra | māra | m. soc. way of sacrificing livestock.
paśca adv. back, behind, after; to the west — iic. behind (ifc.) — ind. paścā id. opp. purā || lat. post; fr. posterior.
paścānutāpa | anutāpa | m. regret; remorse.
paścārdhá [ardha] m. rear part; occi dental half. paścārdhe prep. behind, west of (g.).

paścāt |related to paśca| adv. backward, from behind, from the back; westward | therefore, then, finally | after, behind (abl. g.). dakṣiṇapaścāt to the Southwest. paścāt kṛ to surpass, to overcome. paścāt tap to repent.
paścāttara [tara] amnf paścāttarā which follows abl. .
paścāttāpa [tāpa] m. ["after the torments (of guilt)"] repentance, regret. paścāttāpam kṛ to repent, to regret.
paścāttāpahata [hata] amnf paścāttāpahatā struck by repentance.
paścādahas [ahas] adv. in the afternoon.
paścādukti [ukti] f. repetition, reiteration.
paścima [super. paśca] amnf paścimā back; last, final; western — f. paścimā the direction of the west. paścimam drś see for the last time.
paścimātāna [ātāna] m. back stretch.
paścimātānāsana [āsana] n. phil. [yoga] posture of stretching the back: legs straight, one takes one's toes with one's hands and places the forehead on the knees.
paścimāmnāya [āmnāya] m. soc. "doctrine of the west", order of Sankara₁ whose matha is located in Dvārakā; the cult of Kubjikā developed there; cf. Manthānabhairava.
paśya [agt. paś] amnf paśyā who looks.
paśyat [ppr. paś] amnf paśyantī seeing, in the act of seeing — f. paśyantī [paśyantīvāc] phil. [Bhartrhari] the word visualized in consciousness,

stage [vapus] of the manifestation of sound | 1st prostitute. paśyatas adv. in the presence of; under the nose of g. . paśyato bakamūrkhasya nakulair bhaksitāh sutāh |Hit.| Her little ones were being eaten by the man goustes under the nose of that idiot heron.
paśyata [paśyata] amnf paśyatā seen; visible, manifest, evident | to see; worth seeing.
pasas n. penis | lat. penis; gr. o.
paspaśa [pft. spaś₁] m. introduction, preface; plan of a work — f. paspaśā gram. n.p. of the paspaśā, introduction to the Mahābhāṣya; syn. paspaśāhnika.
paspaśāhnika [āhnika] n. gram. introductory chapter (1ᵉr āhnika) of the Mahābhāṣya.
paspaśāná [ppft. mo. spaś₁] amnf paspaśānā having observed, having spied.

Pahlava m. pl. Pahlavas name of a people of northwestern India (the Iranian Parthians) | myth. |VP.| They are considered a fallen Kshatriya people; conquered by Sagara, they were forced to wear beards.
pā₃ [agt. pā₂] ifc. mf that which keeps, that which protects (iic.). surāpāḥ that which keeps the alcohol.
pā₄ [agt. pā₁] ifc. mf who drinks (iic.).

√ pā₁ v. [1] pr. (pibati) pft. (papau) aor. [1] (apāt) pp. (pīta₁) ppr. (pibat) pfp. (pānīya, peya, pātavya) abs. (pītvā) pf. (anu, ā, ut, ni, pra) to drink — ps. (pīyate) to be drunk — ca. (pāyáyati) pp. (pāyita) to give to drink, to sprinkle — dés. (pipāsati) ppr. (pipāsat) to desire to drink — intens. r. (pepīpyate) ppr. r. (pepīpyamāna) to drink to excess; to drink continuously | gr. ; lat. bibo; fr. drink, beverage, beer. pītvā hasati having drunk he laughs. pāyam pāyam having drunk again and again.

√ pā₂ v. [2] pr. (pāti) aor. [6] (apāsīt) subj. (pāsati) pf. (anu, pari, prati) to protect, defend — ca. (pāláyati) to keep, protect, save, preserve; to defend against (abl.) — des. (pipāsati) to want to defend — intens. r. (pāpāyate) to defend fiercely | lat. pasco; fr. pasture, shepherd. pāhi mām help! śivah pātu may Shiva protect you. pātu vo dayitāmukham may the favor of your beloved protect you.
pāmsana var. pāmśana [pāmsuna] amnf pāṃsanī despicable; bad — ifc. that defiles (iic.) — nf pāṃsanā contempt.
pāṃsu var. pāṃśu m. pl. dust; sand; sandy soil | manure | pollen.
pāṃsuka [ka] n. pl. dust; sand — f. pāṃsukā impure woman (having her period).

pāṃsulá [la] amnf pāṃsulā dusty; sandy; covered with dust, soiled — ifc. soiled by, withered by (iic.) — m. myth. aspect of Shiva carrying a staff decorated with bones; this staff. ucchuşkamrgakarīşapāmsula soiled with dry deer droppings.
pāṃsúlavaṇa [lavaṇa] n. powdered salt.

pāka [act. pac] m. cooking, maturation; refinement, ripening; maturity | the act of cooking, boiling, roasting, burning | digestion; inflammation | youth, simplicity, innocence | young of an animal; child | myth. np. of pāka "Simpleton", asura killed by Indra | med. syrup | lit. poetic maturation; the KM. distinguishes 9 kinds — f. pākī ifc. cooking of, refinement of (2nd century). pākam kṛ to cook. odanasya pākaḥ cooking of rice.

pākadarpaṇa [darpaṇa] m. lit. np. from the pākadarpaṇa, an ancient cookbook attributed to Nala, who received it from Yama. pākaprakaraņa [prakaraņa] n. lit. np. from the Pākaprakaraņa, a 17th-century culinary treatise.
pākayajña [yajña] m. soc. oblation of cooked food; seven are listed: aṣṭakā, pārvaṇasthālīpāka, śrāddha, śrāvaṇī, āgrahāyaṇī, caitrī, āśvayujī.
pākarasa | rasa | m. sauce of the dish, its taste.
pākaśāsana [śāsana] m. myth. epith. of Indra "who punishes pāka".
pākaśāstra [śāstra] n. culinary art.
pākin [agt. pac] ifc. amnf pākinī that ripens, that cooks (iic.).
pākya [pfp. [1] pac] amnf pākyā which can be cooked; edible; ripe | obtained by cooking or evaporation — n. (salt) from salt marsh.
pākṣika [*pakṣaika] amnf pākṣikā par tisan; partial | subject to an alternative; optional — m. alternative.
pāgala amnf pāgalā deranged, crazy; demented.
pāṅkta [*paṅktia] amnf pāṅktī formed of 5 parts.
pānkteya |īya| amnf pānkteyā soc. respectable, admissible in the ranks of his caste.
pānktya [ya] amnf pānktyā soc. respectable, admissible in the ranks of his caste.
pāc [ca. pac] v. [10] pr. (pācayati) to cook.
pācaka [agt. pāc] amnf pācikā that cooks, that roasts | that aids digestion; that ripens — m. cook — f. cf. pācikā. pācatīti pācakaḥ he cooks, therefore he is a cook.
pācakastrī [strī] f. cook.
pācana |agt. pāc| amnf pācanī that cooks; that ripens; that aids digestion — m. fire; acidity — act. n. cooking | dressing of a wound | digestive.
pācikā [f. pācaka] f. cooking; maturity | cooker.
pācikābhārya [bhāryā] m. husband of a cook.
pājas n. firmness; vigor, strength | brilliance, shine | du. pājasī ved. Heaven and Earth | pl. pājāmsi bright colors.
Pāñcajanya [*Pañcajanaya] amnf pāñcajanyā relating to the five races of humanity — m. myth. np. of Pāncajanya, conch of Viṣṇu "Call of all races"; Kṛṣṇa stole it from Pañcajana.
pāñcarātra [*pañcarātra] n. soc. doctrine of the pāñcarātrās — m. pl. pāñcarātrās soc. vaisnava tantric sect.
pāñcarātrika [*pañcarātraika] amnf pāñcarātrikā which lasts 5 nights (or days) — m. soc. adept of the pāñcarātra doctrine.
pāñcāla [*pañcāla] amnf pāñcālī rela tif au peuple pañcāla | myth. np. du roi pāñcāla, qui eattaque à Saṃvaraṇa — m. pl. Pañcālās princes des Pañcālās; cf. Drupada, Sikhaṇḍī — f. cf. pāñcālī.
pāñcālaka [*pañcālaka] amnf pāñcālikā relating to the Pañcāla people — m. prince of the Pañcālās | doll, puppet — f. pāñcālikā prince of the Pañcālās | doll, puppet.

pāñcālī [f. pāñcāla] f. myth. np. of pāñcālī, epith. of Draupadī "of the pañcāla country" | lit. manner of speaking, style [rīti] of the pañcāla, with few compounds. patipravaratā jyesthe patidevaratānuje | itaresu ca pāñcālyāḥ tritayaḥ tritayaḥ triṣu || (Kālidāsa in response to Vyāsa's challenge to write a verse describing Draupadī's relationships with her 5 husbands and not containing the letter 'ca').
Pāñcika [*pañcaika] m. bd. n.p. from Pāñcika,

genius [yakṣa] of the riches and fertility of the culture of Gandhāra (around the 1st century); he is said to be the commander-in-chief of Kubera's army; his wife is the repentant ogress Hārītī; he is also called Jambhala.
pāt [ca. pat] v. [10] pr. (pātayati) pp. (pātita) to split, tear, rip off.
pāṭa [act. pāṭ] m. width; extension — f. pāṭā series, sequence, succession — f. cf. pāṭī.
pāṭaka [agt. paṭ] amnf pāṭikā that splits, that divides — m. bank, shore; steps descending to a river — act. f. pāṭikā part; partition | incision, laceration.
pāṭana [act. paṭ] n. division; laceration, destruction — f. pāṭanā cut, incision.

pāṭala [pāṭala] amnf pāṭalā pale red, pink, orange — m. the color pink or orange | bio. bot. Stereospermum colais or bot. Bignonia sua veolens tree with yellow flowers edged in red in the shape of a trumpet; it is one of the 5 major medicinal roots [bṛhatpañcamūla] — n. bio. its flower, the trumpet vine, with a sweet fragrance — f. pāṭalā bio. id. — mf pāṭali bio. id. rudhirapāṭala blood red.
Pāṭalika [ka] n. geo. np. of Pāṭalika, epith. of pāṭaliputra "rich in bignonia".
pāṭaligrāma | grāma | m. geo. np. of the village of pāṭaligrāma, in Magadha; it was fortified by Ajātaśatru₂, who made it his capital pāṭaliputra || pali pātaligāma.

pāṭaliputra | putra | n. geo. np. of the city of pāṭaliputra, in the Ganges valley, founded by Ajātaśatru₂; it was the capital of Magadha, then of the Maurya empire (mod. Paṭnā in Bihāra); cf. Kusumapura, Candragupta, Puspapurī. asti mahītalatilakam sarasvatīkulagrham mahānagaram | nāmnā pāṭaliputraṃ pa ribhūtapurandarasthānam | Kuṭṭanīmata Pātaliputra is a great capital, the most beautiful in all the earth; ancestral land of Sarasvatī, it even humbles the residence of Indra.
pāṭavá [*paṭua] amnf pāṭavī ma lin, able, skillful (in (loc.)) — n. acuity, intensity | skill, dexterity in (loc.) — ifc. rapidity, haste in (iic.) | health.
pāṭita [pp. ca. paṭ] amnf pāṭitā split; torn; broken — m. fracture, not. of the leg.

pāṭī [f. pāṭa] f. math. arithmetic. pātīgaņita | gaņita | n. math. n.p. from the Pātīgaņita, arithmetic treatise by Śrīdharācārya (9th century) in 300 verses [Triśatī]; also called Pāṭīsāra, Gaṇitasāra, Triśatīgaṇitasāra, Triśatikā, Śrīdharapātī, Śrīdharīlīlāvatī.
pāṭīra [*paṭīra] m. sandalwood paste.
pāṭh [ca. paṭh] v. [10] pr. (pāṭhayati) pp. (pāṭhita) pfp. (pāṭhanīya, pāṭhya) to make read; to teach; to instruct in (2 acc.) — ps. (pāṭhyate) to be instructed in.
pāṭha [act. ca. paṭh] m. reading, recitation (not. of the Vedas); study; lesson | ved. mode of recitation of Vedic texts; there are 11 of them, 3 of which are called

natural [prakṛti] (saṃhitā, pada, krama), the other 8 are artificial [vikṛti] (jaṭā, mālā, śikhā, rekhā, dhvaja, daṇḍa, ratha, ghana) | gram. re collection of rules of grammar or its appendices; their memorization by recitation | lit. (philology)

variant | |dhātupāṭha| gram. list of roots and their nominal derivatives | [gaṇapāṭha] gram. re collection of classes of morphological exceptions — f. pāthā bio. bot. Cyclea peltata (or Clypea hernan difolia), a menispermaceae liana with heart-shaped leaves; its tuberous roots have numerous medicinal uses.
pāṭhabheda [bheda] m. bed. [philology] correction, variation, interpolation of a text.
pāṭhaśālā [śālā] f. Vedic study hall | mod. Sanskrit college.
pāthaśālāpaddhati [paddhati] f. traditional teaching of Sanskrit by recitation.
pāṭhāntara [antara] n. lit. ["other reading"] a reading of a text. iti pāṭhāntaram according to another reading.
pāṭhālaya [ālaya] mn school.
pāṭhāvalī [āvalī] f. reading manual.
pāṭhaka [agt. ca. paṭh] amnf pāṭhikā reciter, reader — m. student; scholar, tutor, teacher — f. pāṭhikā female student; scholar.
pāṭhakādhama [adhama] m. soc. worst reciter; there are 6 varieties of it; cf. likhitapāthaka.
pāṭhana [act. ca. paṭh] n. recitation, lecture; teaching.

pāṭhanīya [pfp. [2] ca. paṭh] amnf pāṭhanīyā which must be taught; which must be studied. mahārājyam vā pālanīyam mahābhāsyam vā pāthanīyam One must either rule a great kingdom or teach the Mahābhāsya.
pāṭhita [pp. That. paṭh] amnf pāṭhitā in lord.
pāṭhin [agt. paṭh] amnf pāṭhinī competent — ifc. competent in (iic.) — m. student; scholar; teacher | soc. Brahmin who has completed his Vedic classes.
pāṭhīna [pāṭhaīna] m. organic. zoo. Wallago attu, catfish.
pāthya [pfp. [1] ca. path] amnf pāthyā that must be taught | that needs to be instructed.
pāṇavika [*paṇavaika] m. drum player.

pāṇi m. hand; syn. kara₁, hasta | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the faculty [karmendriya] of grasping, whose regent [niyantr] is Indra; its predominant element |bhūta| is vāyu the air; the associated perception | tanmātra | is the tactile sensation | sparśa | which excites the sense [buddhīndriya] of touch [tvak] — ifc. that which holds in hand (iic.) || lat. palma; fr. palm; ang. feel. pāṇim gṛhṇīṣva pāṇinā take his hand in yours.
pāṇígraha [graha] m. soc. ["taking the hand"] ma riage.
pāṇigrahaṇa | grahaṇa | n. soc. rite of the marriage ceremony; the act of getting married. varam te vişabhakşanam na tu pānigrahanam Better poison for you than marriage.
pāṇígrahītṛ [grahītṛ] m. married; husband.
pāṇígrāha [grāha] m. marriage | spouse ["who takes the hand". pānígrāham adv. taking by the hand.
pānígrāhaka [grāhaka] m. married; husband; syn. pānigrahītr.
pāṇígha |gha| m. (music) | "who strikes with the hand" | musician (not. drummer).
pāṇipadma [padma] m. [rūpaka] graceful hand ["like a lotus"].
pāṇipāda | pāda | n. sg. hands and feet — m. pl. id.
pāṇipīḍana |pīḍana| n. soc. act of the husband pressing the bride's hand during the wedding.
pāṇipuṭa [puṭa] mn hollow of the hand (for drinking).
Pāṇivāda |vāda| mr. hist. n.p. of the scholar Rāma Pāṇivāda from Kerala (18th century); we owe him two long poems in vīthī style in prākṛtī , the Candrikā and the Līlāvatī.

Pāṇini m. hist. np. of Pāṇini, grammarian of Sanskrit of the 4th century BC, born in Salātura in Gandhāra (near modern-day Lahore); he developed a grammar of Sanskrit, called the Aṣṭādhyāyī, which remains authoritative to this day; a drama, Jāmbavatīvijaya, is also attributed to him. simho vyākaraņasya karturaharat prāṇān muneh
pānineh [PT.] A lion took the life of the wise Pāṇini, author of the grammar.
pāṇinidarśana [darśana] n. lit. chapter of the Sar vadarśanasamgraha, giving a phil. interpretation of grammatical methods, inspired by the Vākyapadīya.
pāṇinyukta [ukta] amnf pāṇinyuktā gram. said by Pāṇini. pāṇinyuktam pramāṇam gram. the munitraya is authoritative.

pāṇinīya [Pāṇiniīya] amnf pāṇinīyā gram. of Pāṇini or his school; in accordance with Pāṇini — m. expert of the school of Pāṇini — n. phil. linguistics. odanapāṇinīya (pej.) student of grammar for the benefit of meals. siddhyaty evam apāṇinīyaṃ tu bhavati gram. [Mahābhāṣya] One can arrive at it this way, but it does not follow Pāṇini.

pāṇinīyavyākaraṇa |vyākaraṇa| n. gram. grammar according to the school of Pāṇini. pāṇinīyavyākaraṇodāharaṇakośa [udāharaṇakośa] m. lit. collection of examples of grammar according to the school of Pāṇini.
pāṇinīyaśikṣā [śikṣā] f. gram. np. of the pāṇinīyaśikṣā, a treatise on phonetics due to Pāṇini or his disciples.
pāṇḍara [*paṇḍara] amnf pāṇḍarā white, pale. śańkhapāṇḍara white like a conch shell.

pāṇḍava [pāṇḍua] m. myth. [Mah.] patr. of the 5 (adopted) sons of pāṇḍu: the 3 sons of Kuntī: King Yudhişthira son of Dharma, Bhīma son of Vāyu, Arjuna son of Indra, and Nakula and Sahadeva, twin sons of Mādrī and the Aśvinau; with Kuntī they were invited by Duryodhana to a great festival in honor of Siva at Vāraṇāvata where they lived in a lacquer palace intended to be set on fire to kill them; warned of the danger, they escaped through a tunnel, and went to live incognito, disguised as brahmins, at Ekacakrā; From there they went to the svayamvara of Draupadī, where Arjuna won the archery tournament; as a result of a word from Kuntī ordering them to share the prize, all five of them had to marry Draupadī; Dhṛtarāṣṭra divided the kingdom, and they established their capital Indraprastha, where Yudhisthira had himself crowned king [rājasūya]; but he lost his kingdom at dice with the cheat Sakuni, and the brothers had to go into exile for 12 years; in the 13th year, during their exile with King Virāta, they hid under false identities; Arjuna disguised himself as Brhannadā, Yudhişthira as Kanka, Bhīma as Ballava, Nakula as Granthika, and Sahadeva as Tantipāla, while Draupadī disguised himself as the sairandhrī Mālinī₁; on their return the great war broke out with their cousins the Kauravās, whom they defeated with the help of Kṛṣṇa | pl. Pāṇḍavās myth. the five Pāṇḍavās; in gen. their clan, opposed to that of the Kauravās.
pāṇḍitya [*paṇḍitaya] n. erudition, knowledge, competence.

pāṇḍú amnf pale yellow, pale; clear, whitish — m. pallor; jaundice | myth. [Mah.] np. of pāṇḍu "the Pale One", son of the ascetic Vyāsa and Ambālikā₁ his sister-in-law "pale with fear"; king of Hastināpura as a result of the incapacitating blindness of his elder brother Dhṛtarāṣṭra, he led a campaign of conquests establishing the supremacy of the Kauravās; then he renounced the throne by becoming a hermit in the mountain of Sataśriga; there he was cursed by the daimmuni Kimdama whom he killed while he was making love, and condemned himself to die if he made love; His first wife, Kuntī, who had received from the sage [rsi] Durvāsā a mantra with the power to invoke the gods to conceive, gave him his three eldest sons: Yudhisthira son of Dharma, Bhīma son of Vāyu, and Arjuna son of Indra; she then allowed his second wife, Mādrī, to use this gift once; Mādrī cheated by giving birth to twins, Nakula and Sahadeva, by invoking the Aśvinau; one spring day, pāṇḍu could not resist Mādrī's charm and died. || Latin: pallidus; French: pâle.
pāṇdúcchāya [chāya] amnf pāṇducchāyā co colored with white. pāṇḍucchāyopavanavṛtayaḥ ketakaiḥ [MD.] gardens whose groves are colored white by pandana.
pāṇḍútā [tā] f. pallor.
pāṇḍútva [tva] n. id.

pāṇḍuraṅga [raṅga] amnf pāṇḍuraṅgā white; fair-skinned — m. myth. n.p. of Pāṇḍuraṅga, epith. by VitthalaPuṇḍarīka “light-complexioned” | myth. epith. of Siva | geo. n.p. from the principality of Pāṇḍuraṅga₁ of the Hinduized kingdom of Campā₁ in southern Vietnam.
pāṇḍuraṅgamahātmya [mahātmya] n. lit. np. of the Pāṇdurangamahātmya, a poem of devotion to Pāṇḍuraṅga by Tenali Rāmakṛṣṇudu, Te lugu poet of the Vijayanagara court (16th century).
pāṇḍuvaṃśa [vaṃśa] m. hist. Pāṇḍuvaṃśa dynasty of southern Kosala (6th century).
pāṇḍuvaṃśin [vaṃśin] m. hist. n.p. Pāṇḍuvaṃśī of the kings of the Pāṇḍuvaṃśa dynasty.
pāṇḍura [pāṇḍura] amnf pāṇḍurā whitish, pale; pinkish, beige — m. the beige or pinkish color — n. depigmentation, vitiligo.

Pāṇḍya m. name of the land of the Pāṇḍyās of the southern Deccan (Madurai) | myth. [Mah.] np. of King Pāṇḍya "of the land of the Pāṇḍyās"; he fought on an elephant alongside the Pāṇḍavās in the great battle; his emblem was the fish; after a long fight, he was put to death by Aśvatthāmā | his dynasty.
pāṇḍyadeśa | deśa | m. geo. the country of Pāṇḍya (around modern Madurai).
pāt [ca. pat₁] v. [10] pr. (pātayati) pp. (pātita) to knock down, to bring down, to throw.
pāta |act. pat₁| m. flight, fall, descent, sudden arrival; accident; blow (of a sword) | astr. nodal point of an orbit.
pātotpāta | utpāta | mr. ups and downs.
pātaka |agt. ca. pat₁| n. sin, crime | "that causes one to fall (from one's caste)"].
pātañjala |*Patañjalia| amnf pātañjalī relating to Patañjali.
pātañjaladarśana [darśana] n. phil. n.p. of pātañjaladarśana, doctrine of yoga according to Patañjali₂.
Pātañjalayogaśāstra [yogaśāstra] n. lit. np. of the Pātañjalayogaśāstra "Science of yoga taught by Patañjali₂", including the Yogasūtra and its commentary the Yogabhāṣya.
pātañjalayogaśāstravivarana [vivarana] n. bed. commentary on the Pātañjalayogaśāstra; it is attributed to Samkara₁.
pātañjalavṛtti [vṛtti] f. bed. n.p. from the pātañjalavṛtti, a gloss on the Yogasūtra of Patañjali₂ due to king Bhoja deva; cf. Rājamārtaņda.
pātañjalavṛttivivaraṇa [vivaraṇa] n. bed. n.p. of the pātañjalavṛttivivaraṇa, sub-commentary of the Yo gasūtra attributed by some to Sankara₁.

pātana [agt. ca. pat₁] amnf pātanī that which brings down; that which fells (g. iic.) — act. n. act of bringing down, of bringing down | act of humiliating | act of rolling dice; wink | (alchemy) treatment not. of the mer cure. dandasya pātana ["to bring down the stick"] punishment. garbhasya pātana abortion. jalaukasām pātana med. application of leeches.
pātavya [pfp. [3] pā₁] amnf pātavyā that one must drink. rugṇaiḥ auṣadhaṃ pātavyam the remedy must be drunk by the sick.
Pātāla [*pat₁āla] n. myth. np. of the world [loka] Pātāla, seventh subterranean hell; the dra
gons [nāga] dwell there; Bali reigns there | lit. np. from the section [khanda] Pātāla of a purāna dealing with infernal myths.
pātālagaigā [gaigā] f. geo. np. of the Pātālagaigā, lower course of the Kṛṣṇā₁ river; one bathes there before making the pilgrimage to Srīśaila.
pātālabhogivarga | bhogin₁varga | m. lit. section of the Svargādikāṇḍa, dealing with the subterranean regions.

pātālavāsin | vāsin₁ | amnf pātālavāsinī myth. who inhabits the underworlds — m. cf. nāga — f. pātālavāsinī bd. |Tantra| np. of pātālavāsinī, Underworld goddess of the triad of the three worlds; cf. Khecarī, Bhūcarī.
pātāleśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of the pātāleśvara "Lord of the Underworld", 8th century Shaivite shrine, carved into the rock in the cave of Pañcāleśvara in Puņe in Mahārāṣṭra.
pātita [pp. ca. pat₁] amnf pātitā fallen, thrown; struck down; affected, depressed, collapsed.
pātitya [*patitaya] n. soc. loss of status or caste; degradation.
Pātityagrāmanirṇaya [grāmanirṇaya] m. lit. np. of the Pātityagrāmanirṇaya, which deals with communities of fallen Brahmins treated as untouchables; it is part of the Sahyādrikhanda.
pātin [agt. pat₁] amnf pātinī that falls, that flies.
pātṛ [agt. pā₁] amnf pātrī [sg. nom. pātā, acc. pātāram drinker.

pātra [pā₁tra] n. cup, goblet; bowl, vase, pot, (drinking) container | receptacle — m. (person) worthy of, suitable for g. loc. iic.; worthy of receiving | lit. character or theatrical role | soc. royal advisor, minister — f. pātrā ifc. receptacle of — f. pātrī vase, dish, pot. pātrīkṛ to make something a receptacle for (g.) | to honor; to bestow a distinction. pātrībhū to become a person of merit. pañcapātram n. the 5 receptacles.
pātratā [tā] f. fact of being a receptacle for g. iic. | capacity, value; dignity, honor.
pātratva [tva] n. capacity, value; dignity, honor.
pātravidhi | vidhi | m. soc. injunction concerning the purification of the vessel of an ascetic, not. of the pāśupata sect.
pātre [loc. pātra] iic.
pātrebahula [bahula] amn pl. ["often around the dish" | (pej.) parasites.
pātresamita |samita| amnf pātresamitā pl. id.
pāthas [*pathaas] n. water | food.
pātheya [*pathaīya] n. provisions for the journey.
pād [ca. pad₁] v. [10] pr. (pādayati) pp. (pādita) to make go.

pāda [instr. pad₁] m. foot | foot of a tree, column, mountain; position, site, radius (of a celestial body) | quarter, fourth part | verse in a stanza | gram. word, element of a compound word | lit. section of a work; not. grouping of aphorisms [sūtra] | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the faculty [karmendriya] of walking, whose regent [niyantr] is Viṣṇu; its predominant element [bhūta] is te jas, fire; the associated perception [tanmātra] is the as
pect [rūpa], which excites the sense [buddhīndriya] of the

vision [akṣi] | du. pādau the two feet | phil. [ChU.] conceptual division of brahman according to Gautama; there are four: Space [prakāśavat], the Unlimited [anantavat], the Radiant [jyotismat] and the Cognitive [āyatanavat] — ifc. pl. pādās ["at the feet of (iic.) (person)"] expression of respect | gr. o ; lat. pedis; ang. foot; all. Fuss; fr. pied. pādābhyām adv. on foot. śrīpādāḥ soc. ["at the feet of Śrī"] Vaishnavite sectarian symbol, a vertical red line between two white ones, worn as a tilaka. pitṛpādāḥ kathaṃ santi, how is your father?
pādatāditaka [tāditaka] m. bed. n.p. Syāmalika's one-act bhāna-style drama Pādatāditaka; it is part of the Caturbhāṇī.
pādapa₁ [pa₁] m. tree ["that drinks through the root"].
pādapa₂ [pa₂] m. footrest — f. pādapā shoe, slipper.

pādapadma [padma] n. ["lotus among the feet"] (metaphor) pretty foot. pādapūraņa [pūraņa] amnf pādapūraņā that fills a verse; said of expletive particles — n. action of filling a verse with expletive particles | gram. anomalies of sandhi to adjust to the meter.
pādarakṣa | rakṣa | amnf pādarakṣā which protects the feet (not. of the fighting elephant).
pādādi [ādi] iic. starting with the feet.
pādādikeśānta [keśaanta] amnf pādādikeśāntā lit. [kāvya] complete ascending description of a character "from head to toe".
pādādiyamaka | yamaka | n. lit. | alaṃkāra | variety of yamaka where the different lines of a stanza have the same beginning.
pādānta | anta | m. end of the foot | phon. final of a verse |pāda| — n. lit. |alaṃkāra| variety of yamaka where the different verses of a stanza have the same ending.
pādāntāmredita |āmredita| n. lit. variety of ya maka where the different lines of a stanza have the same ending.
pādāhata |āhata| amnf pādāhatā trampled; struck by the foot — f. pādāhati kick.
pādodaka [udaka] n. water for (washing) the feet.
pādaka [pādaka] m. foot — f. pādikā sandal — ifc. foot of (iic.).
pādaśas [pādaśas] adv. gram. (recitation) word by word, following the padapātha | foot by foot; verse by verse; quarter by quarter.
pāduka [pāda] amnf pādukā f. pādukī equipped with feet; who goes on foot, pedestrian — f. cf. pādukā.
pādukā [f. pāduka] f. sandal, slipper; shoe (wooden clog) | soc. footprint in a temple honoring a god or a venerable. gurupādukā phil. holy sandal of the guru; its invocation brings liberation.
pādukākāra [kāra] m. shoemaker.
pādukāpañcaka [pañcaka] n. lit. [Tantra] np. from the pādukāpañcaka, an esoteric text dealing with mystical anatomy.
pādukāsahasra [sahasra] n. bed. from np. pādukāsahasra, 1008 verse poem by śrī Vedāntadeśika celebrating Bharata₁'s worship of Rangarāja's sandals, using citrapaddhati; cf. turagabandha.
pādū [pāda] f. sandal; shoe.
pādma [*padma] amnf pādmā relating to the lotus.
pādmapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. cf. padmapurāṇa.
pādya [pādaya] amnf pādyā relating to feet — n. (water) for (washing) The feet.

pāna [act. pā₁] n. act of drinking (not. alcohol) | (poetry) act of kissing on the lips — obj. n. drink, beverage — ins. m. goblet, cup — m. distiller; tavern keeper. payaḥpānam bhujaṅgānām sukham drinking milk is the pleasure of snakes.
pānaka |ka| mn drink, beverage.
pānakarasarāgāsava [rasarāgaāsava] m. wood, sons, seasonings and liquors.
pānakarasarāgāsavayojana | yojana | n. the art of preparing drinks, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.
pānakumbha [kumbha] m. ["drinking vessel"] go belet, glass.
pānagosthī |gosthī| f. drinking establishment, tavern.
pānagosthīkā [ka] f. id.
pānadoṣa [doṣa₂] m. ["drinking vice"] alcoholism; state of intoxication.
pānī [pkt. pāna] f. water.

Pānīpata [pata] m. geo. np. of the city of Pānīpata on the banks of the Yamunā, on the route between Afghanistan and India (modern Panipat in Haryana, 100 km north of Delhi); 3 major battles took place there; in 1504 Zahir Ud Din Babr (Ba bur) invaded India from Kabul; he reached the Chenāb in 1519, and won the first battle of Pānīpata against Ibrahim Lodi in 1526 thanks to his cannons, inaugurating the Mughal Empire; in 1556 Ak bar defeated the last Hindu king of Delhi, Hemu Vikramāditya; in 1761 the Afghans defeated the Marathas at the third battle of Pānīpata, which resulted in 100,000 deaths.
pānīya [pfp. [2] pā₁] amnf pānīyā po table; to drink — n. beverage; drinking water.
pāntha [*panthan] m. traveler; nomad — f. pānthā ifc. act of accompanying.

pānthatva [tva] n. condition of traveler; nomadism. ЧТЧ pāpá amnf pāpā f. pāpī sinner, evil, wicked, vicious, criminal; fatal — m. unbeliever; wrongdoer, criminal — n. Evil, fault, sin, vice, crime | phil. Evil; opp. punya | lat. peccare; fr. péché. pāpam adv. wickedly, wrongly. śāntam pāpam vade retro, satanas. sadā devā janānmuñcanti pāpāt The gods always deliver men from sins.
pāpaka [ka] n. sin.
pāpákarman [karman] amnf pāpakarmanī evil; criminal.
pāpanāśana [nāśana] n. removal of sin — amnf pāpanāśanā myth. epith. of Shiva "who removes sin".
pāpanāśin [nāśin] amnf pāpanāśinī which removes sins — f. pāpanāśinī geo. np. of the sacred pool of pāpanāśinī, in Bhuvaneśvarī₁; its water "removes sins"; one can bathe in it one day a year.
pāpaniścaya [niścaya] amnf pāpaniścayā dedicated to Evil, criminal.
pāpamitra | mitra | n. friend of debauchery | bad company; opp. kalyāṇamitra.
pāpamitratva [tva] n. friendship with bad people.
pāpayoni |yoni| f. unclean womb (in which one is reborn as punishment for one's sins).
pāparogin [rogin] amnf pāparoginī sick with a disease due to sin, such as leprosy.
pāparddhi [rddhi] f. ["success in sin"] hunt.
pāparddhika [ka] m. hunter.
pāpahara [hara] amnf pāpaharā that removes sin — n. means of removing sin.
pāpātman [ātman] amnf pāpātmanī wicked; sinner; criminal, scoundrel; opp. dharmātman. nāyam pāpātmā mama gatāyā utthitah |PT.| Didn't the scoundrel get up while I was gone?
pāpin [pāpain] amnf pāpinī fisherman; wicked; criminal.
pāpiṣṭha [great. pāpa] amnf pāpiṣṭhā the worst.
pāpīyas [compar. pāpa] amnf pāpīyasī worse; more wicked — m. scoundrel, rogue; great sinner, criminal. māraḥ pāpīyān m. bd. the devil.
pāpman [pāpaman] m. evil; misfortune, infor tune; calamity; crime, sin, wickedness | evil spirit, demon.
pāma iic. pāman.
pāmaghna |ghna| amnf pāmaghnī which heals skin conditions — m. sulfur.
pāmavat [vat] amnf pāmavatī affected by a skin disease.
pāmán m. skin disease; skin rash, pruritus; scar — f. pāmā id.
pāmana [na] amnf pāmanī afflicted with pruritus.
pāmara [ra] amnf pāmarā afflicted with a skin disease; leper — m. wretch, scoundrel; idiot — n. bad conduct.
pāmpa |*pampā| n. pl. pāmpāni geo. (woods) near the pampā.
pāya |obj. pā₁| n. water.
pāyasa [*payasa] amnf pāyasī prepared with milk — n. rice cooked in milk.
pāyin [agt. pā₁] ifc. amnf pāyinī who drinks (regularly) (iic.). kaṣāyapāyino gāndhārāḥ The inhabitants of Gandhāra who regularly drink plant juices to stay healthy.

pāyu [*pā₁u] m. anus | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the faculty [karmendriya] of evacuation, whose regent [niyantr] is Mitra; its predominant element [bhūta] is pṛthivī the earth; the associated perception [tanmātra] is the smell [gandha] which excites the sense [buddhīndriya] of smell [ghrāṇa].
pāyudhvani |dhvani| m. pet.
pāyūpastha [upastha] n. anus and genitals.
pāyya [pfp. [1] ca. pā₁] amnf pāyyā (acc.) to make drink; to drink — act. n. act of drinking — obj. n. water.

pāra |obj. pṛ₁| n. opposite bank, shore; side op placed | end, extremity, limit; goal — agt. amnf pārī ifc. that which crosses, that which overcomes (iic.). pāratas adv. on the other side; on the other bank | beyond g. . pāram gam to attain, to achieve (a goal, a wish, knowledge (g. loc.). pāram nī to complete, to conclude. carcāpārah one who thoroughly studies the carcāpātha.
pārága |ga₁| amnf pāragā gone far away; who has crossed | Accomplished; who knows thoroughly, familiar with (g. loc. iic.); learned.
pārágata [gata] amnf pāragatā who reached the opposite bank (from g. ); who crossed | bd. who attained liberation — m. jn. holy man.
pāragrāmika |grāmika| amnf pāragrāmikī “from another village” | hostile, unfriendly.
pārádṛśvan [dṛśvan] amnf pāradṛśvarī who has seen the other shore; who sees far | scholar Accomplished in (iic. g.). śāstrapāradṛśvā who has mastered all the sciences.

pārāyaṇa | ayana | n. consultation, recitation, study (not. private study of the Veda or a purāṇa) | totality; especially complete text of a tradition — f. pārāyaṇī meditation; elucidation. vedapārāyaṇam soc. complete recitation of the Veda of one's family tradition, at the rate of one lesson per day.
pāraka [agt. pṛ₁] amnf pārikā that makes one cross; savior, liberator.
pārakya [*parakaya] amnf pārakyā ap belonging to another, stranger; syn. parakīya — m. enemy.
pāraṇa |act. pṛ₁| nf pāraṇā execution, ac accomplishment; conclusion; not. end of fast.
pāram [acc. pāra] iic.

pāramgata [gata] amnf pāramgatā who has at teint (a goal, a vow, a knowledge (iic. g. loc.) — m. soc. np. Pāraṃgata "Accomplished", title of scholar. sakalaśāstrapārangatah who has mastered all the sciences.

pāramita | ita| amnf pāramitā reached the opposite shore | that which leads to the goal | phil. transcendent (not. spiritual knowledge) — f. pāramitā perfection, virtue | bd. one of the 6 perfections of an accomplished [bodhisattva]: generosity [dāna], virtue [śīla], tolerance [kṣānti], vigor [vīrya], the
meditation [dhyāna] and wisdom [prajñā₂].
pāramārthika [*paramārthaika] amnf pāramārthikī phil. which concerns the supreme truth; ideal, absolute; absolutely real, essential, true; opp. vyāvahārika | which seeks the supreme truth.
pāramārthikabheda | bheda | m. phil. difference es sentielle.
pārameśvara [*Parameśvara] amnf pārameśvarī which concerns Parameśvara; from Siva.
pāramparya [*paramparaya] n. unbroken succession; tradition. pāramparyeṇa successively, progressively.
pāramparyagata [gata] amnf pāramparyagatā from tradition.
pāramparyopadeśa | upadeśa | m. traditional teaching.
pāraya [agt. pāri] amnf pārayā which crosses.
pārasa amnf pārasī Persian — f. pārasī Persian language || hi. parsi. pārasika var. pārasika [ika] m. Persian | pl. pārasikās the Persians | pl. pārasīkās the Persians.
Pāraskara [*paraskara₁] m. lit. np. of Pāraskara, author of a gṛhyasūtra and a dharmaśāstra.
pārāvata [*parāvata] amnf pārāvatī distant; foreigner — mr. ved. n.p. of the pārāvata tribe of the Yamunā basin | organic. pigeon, dove — f. pārāvatā ifc. id..

Pārāśara [*parāśara] amnf pārāśarā myth. relating to parāśara — m. np. of Pārāśara, patr. "descendant of parāśara" — n. rules of conduct of the order of mendicant ascetics, according to parāśara; syn. Bhikṣusūtra.
pārāśarakalpasūtra [kalpasūtra] n. pl. lit. np. from the pārāśarakalpasūtra, a collection of ritual injunctions attributed to parāśara.
pārāśarin [*parāśarain] amnf pārāśariņī soc. which follows the monastic rules of parāśara.
pārāśarya [*parāśaraya] m. myth. patr. of Vyāsa, "Son of parāśara".
pāri [ca. pṛ₁] v. [10] pr. (pāráyati) to cause to cross; to aid, to protect | to resist, to contend with; to overcome, to prevail over.
pari.
pāribhadra | bhadra | m. bio. bot. Erythrina in dica, coral tree; it loses its leaves in summer and is covered with large purple flowers; cf. bahupuspa, mandāra.
pāriyātra [yātrā] m. geo. np. of the pāriyātra mountains, western part of the Vindhya range.
Pārikṣita [*parikṣita] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Pārikṣita, patr. by Janamejaya | myth. kuru dynasty | var. pārīksita id.

pārijāta [*paramajāta] m. bio. bot. Nyc tanthes arbortristis, Night Jasmine; tree with opposite leaves, with sweetly scented white flowers that bloom at night and fall before dawn; the corolla of its flower has 5 to 8 lobes around an orange center; its flowers decorate sanctuaries; it is used in medicine; syn. sephālikā | myth. "supreme product (of the primordial ocean)" Heavenly Jasmine, one of the 5 trees [pañcavṛkṣa] of Indra's Svarga paradise; it was produced during the churning of the ocean of milk | kṣīrodamathana | ; | Mah. | Nārada brought some of its flowers back to Earth to Kṛṣṇa, curious to see to whom he would offer them; He offered them to Rukminī, and Nārada informed Satyabhāmā of this to arouse her jealousy, while suggesting that she ask Kṛṣṇa to fetch the tree and plant it on Earth; Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā went to steal a branch from the celestial tree, but Indra, informed of the theft by Nārada, fought against Kṛṣṇa; he lost, but cursed the plant never to bear fruit; Kṛṣṇa planted the tree in Satyabhāmā's garden, but in such a way that its flowers fell into Rukminī's garden. Durvāsā offered a garland of it to Indra, who scorned it; In the face of his arrogance, Durvāsā cursed all the celestial treasures to disappear into the ocean, Lakṣmī included; they could only reappear through the churning of the ocean | kṣīrodamathana | | lit. | K. | Puṇḍarīka₂ wore pārijāta flowers on his ear, offered by the fairy guardian of the garden Nandanavana, and their divine scent attracted Mahāśvetā || hi. parjā.
pārijātaka [ka] m. id. pārijātaharaņa | haraņa | n. myth. theft by Kṛṣṇa of the celestial Jasmine from Svarga.
pārita [pp. ca. pṛ] amnf pāritā filled, accomplished; complete; finished.
pāripārśva [*paripārśva] n. soc. retinue of a prince, entourage | soc. extras in the theatre (spectators, servants, courtiers).

pāripārśvaka [*paripārśvaaka] amnf pāripārśvikā soc. servant, valet, member of a prince's retinue — m. pāripārśvika soc. assistant to the theatre director [sūtradhāra]; cf. trigata— f. pāripārśvikā soc. chambermaid.

pāriplava [*pariplava] amnf pāriplavā that swims; that stirs in all directions; unstable — m. soc. cyclic narration of legends undertaken by the hotr during the aśvamedha, repeated for 36 periods of 10 days.

pāribhāṣika [*paribhāṣika] amnf pāribhāṣikī conventional, technical — f. pāribhāṣikī gram. [Praśastapāda] category of technical names. pāribhāṣikī saṃjñā phil. [Nyāya] name introduced by a definition. pāribhāṣikapadārthasaṃgraha [padārthasamgraha] m. lit. of the np. Pāribhāsipadārthasamgraha, work of Nyāya of Kurugunthi Śrīrāma śāstr.
pārimukhika [*parimukhamika] amnf pārimukhikā who is (always) in front (of the master).
pārimukhya [*parimukhamya] amnf pārimukhyā which is in the presence of — n. proximity, presence.
pāriṣada [*pariṣad₂a] amnf pāriṣadā suitable for an assembly | relating to a village — m. soc. member of an assembly; assessor; attendant; spectator.
pāriṣadya [*pariṣad₂ya] m. soc. member of an assembly; advisor; attendant; spectator.
pāruṣṇá [*paruṣana] m. bio. starling; the movement of its flocks is compared to that of fire.
pārusya [*paruṣaya] amnf pāruṣyā du reté, rudeness, rudeness.
pāre [loc. pāra] ind. on the other bank.
pāregangam [gangā] adv. on the other side of the Ganges.
