pārokṣa [*parokṣa] amnf pārokṣā indiscernable; mysterious.
pārokṣya [*parokṣaya] amnf pārokṣyā indiscernible; invisible, hidden — n. mystery. pāroksyeņa beyond direct experience.

Pārtha [*Pṛthā] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Pārtha ["son of Prthā"], matronymic of a pāndava having as mother Kuntī (Yudhisthira, Bhīma or Arjuna); not. Arjuna | prince in gen pārthamādhavau Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna.

Pārthasārathi [sārathi] m. myth. np. of Pārthasārathi, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "Driver of Arjuna's chariot", embodying Vișnu in his role as Savior [guru] of Humanity; he is worshipped at the temple of mod. ChennaiTriplicane | hist. np. of the philosopher of the language Pārthasārathi₁ Miśra, author of mīmāmsā texts (13th century); he is credited with the Nyāyaratnamālā, the Tantraratna, the Nyāyaratnākara and the Śāstradīpikā.
pārthagjanika [*pṛthagjanaka] amnf pārthagjanikā which relates to the man in the street; vulgar, coarse.

pārthiva [*pṛthivīa] amnf pārthivā f. pārthivī earthly; human; royal, princely | earthy; made of earth; said not. of a linga — m. man, mortal; king, prince | astr. np. of Pārthiva "prince", personifying the 19th year of a life cycle [saṃvatsara].

pārvana [*parvana] amnf pārvanī relating to the phases of the moon | soc. concerning religious festivals. pārvaņasthālīpāka [sthālīpāka] m. soc. oblation of rice or barley linked to the phases of the moon, a pākayajña.
pārvatá [*parvata] amnf pārvatī relating to the mountain; mountain dweller, mountainous — f. cf. pārvatī.

pārvatī [f. pārvata] f. myth. np. of the goddess pārvatī "daughter of the mountain", daughter of Himavān and Menā, wife of Siva; she is the reincarnation of Satī; cf. Umā, Durgā, Sailaputrī; she is celebrated at jyaisthāstamī.

pārvatīparameśvara [parameśvara] m. of. pārvatīparameśvarau myth. pārvatī and Siva. pārvatīrukmiņī [rukmiņī] f. of. pārvatīrukmiņyau pārvatī and Rukmiņī. pārvatīrukmiņīya [īya] n. bed. n.p. from the double meaning poem [śleṣa] Pārvatīrukmiņīya "Cohistory of pārvatī and Rukminī" by Vidyāmādhava.
pārvatīya [*parvataīya] amnf pārvatīyā relating to mountains; who lives in the mountain — m. mountain dweller.
pārvatéya [*parvataeya] amnf pārvateyī relating to mountains; born in the mountains; extracted from the mountains — m. mountain prince — n. antimony — f. pārvateyī upper stone of a millstone.

pārśvá [*parśua] n. flank, side; ribs | proximity of (g. iic.) — m. horse on the side of a four-horse team. pārśvayos adv. on both sides. pārśvam prep. towards, in the direction of. pārśve beside, near, towards; opp. dūratas. )1 pārśvāt on the side of, far away. pārśvatas adv. side; beside (of (g. iic.)).

pārśvanātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of pārśvanātha, 23ᵉ tīrthankara; supposed ascetic of the 8th century BC, he is said to have founded an order of 8 communities; his body is dark blue, his symbol is a 7-headed cobra; a large 10th century temple honors him at Khajurāho geo. np. of Mount pārśvanātha₁ (1370 m) in Jharakhanda; at its summit is the Sikharajī temple, an important Jain pilgrimage site.

pārśvābhyudaya [abhyudaya] m. lit. np. du pārśvābhyudaya "Triumph of pārśvanātha", pro dige poetique de Jinasena qui narrate le vie du 23ᵉ tīrthankara en vers ous en hemistiches par les successive verses de la Meghadūta.
pārśvam [acc. parśva] iic.
pārśvamśaya [śaya] amnf pārśvamśayā which lies on its side.
Pārṣata [*pṛṣata] amnf pārṣatī relating to the antelope — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Pārṣata, patr. of Drupada and Dhṛṣṭadyumna — f. pāṛṣatī myth. [Mah.] np. from pārṣatī, patr. of Draupadī.

pārṣada [*parṣada] m. follower, companion; member of the retinue of a king or god (not. Vișnu) | participant in a meeting; spectator — n. gram. grammar manual; not. collection prātiśākhya work relating to a particular school.
pārṣṇi f. heel; back | rearguard | axis connecting the outer horses of a quadriga (the inner horses being harnessed to the pole [dhur] of the chariot).
pārṣṇigrāha [grāha] m. soc. [Arthaśāstra] king likely to attack from the rear in the circle of neighboring kingdoms [maṇḍala].
pārṣṇigrāhasāra [sāra] m. soc. [Arthaśāstra] king potential support of the rear attacker.
pārṣṇitra [tra] n. protedos | reserve army.
pāl [ca. pā₂] v. [10] pr. (pālayati) ppr. (pālayat) pp. (pālita) pfp. (pālya) to keep, protect, save, preserve; to defend against (abl.).

Pāla [agt. ca. pā₂] m. guardian, protector shepherd, herdsman | hist. np. of the Pāla dynasty, which reigned not. over Gauda (~750~1050) in East India; pl. the Pālās; cf. Gopāla — f. pālā ifc. protector of (iic.) — f. pāll₁ wife of herdsman.

Pālaka [agt. ca. pā₂] amnf pālikā who guards, protects, nourishes — m. guardian, protector | adoptive father | prince, king | lit. [Mṛcchakaṭikā] np. of the wicked king Pālaka; the son of the cowherd Aryaka₁ ends his tyrannical reign and dethrones him | lit. [KSS.] np. of Prince Pālaka₁, younger son of King Caṇḍamahāsena of Avanti; Avanti vardhana Is his son | guard, majordomo — f. pālikā guardian.

pālana [agt. ca. pā₂] amnf pālanī that which guards, protects, nourishes — act. n. protection, defense, guard; preservation; care | milk of a recently calved cow. brahmacaryapālana observance of vows of celibacy. pālanī jananī wet nurse.
pālanīya [pfp. [2] ca. pā₂] amnf pālanīyā which must be governed; to be protected.
pālāgalá m. ved. messenger — f. pālāgalī soc. 4th wife of a prince, the least respected.

pāli [act. ca. pā₂] f. var. pālī border, border, margin; edge, border; line | earlobe | row, line, interval | dike, dam; bridge. Food prescribed to a student during their studies by their guru | lap, belly; circumference; louse | [pālibhāṣā] bd. The pāli language is a dialect
Middle Indian [prākrta] used for sacred Buddhist texts.
pālibhāṣā |bhāṣā| f. bd. language of the holy scriptures, Middle Indian dialect resulting from a simplification of Sanskrit; syn. pāli.
pālita [pp. ca. pā₂] amnf pālitā guarded, protected.
pālitasaṃgara [saṃgara₂] amnf pālitasaṃgarā who honors his commitment.
pālin [agt. ca. pā₂] amnf pālin who protects, who guards — m. ifc. ruler, king of (iic.).
pālya [pfp. [1] ca. pā₂] amnf pālyā to protect.
pāv [ca. pū₁] v. [10] pr. (pāvayati) to make clean, to purify; to purify.
Pāvaka [agt. pū₁] m. Fire [Purifier] | myth. np. of Pāvaka "Purifier", epith. of Agni. vasūnām pāvakaścāsmi [BhG.] Among the eight treasures, I am the Purifying Fire.
pāvaki [Pāvakai] m. myth. np. of pāvaki, epith. of Skanda "son of Fire". pāvakeh tam mayūram garjitaih nartayethāh now make the peacock of the son of Fire dance to the rumblings of thunder.
pāvana |agt. pū₁| amnf pāvanī pure, sacred; Purifier — act. n. purification — f. pāvanī myth. np. of the pāvanī, a divyagangā.
Pāvā f. geo. np. of the city of Pāvā, in Ma gadha, near Rājagrha; Buddha gave his last sermon there. )2
pāśa [*paśua] m. bond, cord, chain; lace, collar | myth. Varuna's lace-tamper | knot; loop (of hair) | (figuratively) bond, attachment — v. [11] pr. (pāśayati) to attach, to tie | lat. paciscor.
pāśaka |ka| mr. lace, collar | of.

pāśupata [*paśupatia] amnf pāśupatī sacred to Śivapaśupati | phil. qualifies a doctrine of ascetic emancipation, devotional Śiva triune current created by Lakulīśa — m. soc. follower of Śivapaśupati — n. [pāśupatajñāna] myth. np. of the pāśupata, celestial weapon with which Shiva cut the fifth head of Brahmā, also called brahmaśiras; [Mah.] Śiva revealed its secret to Arjuna, after fighting him; cf. Kirātārjunīya.
pāśupatayoga [yoga] m. bed. n.p. of pāśupatayoga, section of Skandapurāṇa.

pāśupatavrata [vrata] n. soc. observances of the pāśupata doctrine: worshipping Shiva, repeating his name, covering oneself with ashes, transgressing social norms; not. ascetic ritual celebrating Shiva in his paśupati form, given in an appendix | pariśiṣṭa | of the Atharvaveda; cf. Atharvasiras.
pāśupatasūtra [sūtra] n. pl. bed. from np. pāśupatasūtra; Kaundinya commented on it |Pañcārthabhāṣya|.
pāśupālya [*paśupālya] n. breeding (of livestock).
pāścāttya [*paścāttya] amnf pāścāttyā to the West; to the rear; later; last | var. pāścātya f. pāścātyā id.
pāścātya cf. pāścāttya.
pāśyā [pāśaya] f. set of ropes; net.
pāṣaṇḍa [related to parṣad] amnf pāṣaṇḍī heretic, impious — m. impostor; false Hindu; hy pocrite — n. heresy | var. pākhaṇḍa f. pākhaṇḍī id.
pāṣaṇḍatā [tā] f. heresy.
pāṣandastha [stha] amnf pāṣandasthā soc. established in heresy; belonging to a heretical sect; not. Jain, Buddhist.
pāṣaṇḍin [in] amnf pāṣaṇḍinī soc. heretic; not. Jain, Buddhist.

pāṣāṇa m. stone — f. pāṣāṇī small stone used as a measure of weight. na devo vidyate kāṣṭhe na pāṣāṇe na mṛṇmaye | bhāveṣu vidyate devaḥ tasmāt bhāvo hi kāraṇam || God does not reside in the idol of wood, stone, or clay; it is in the heart of man, in truth, that God finds his origin.
pāṣāṇabheda [bheda] m. organic. ["stonebreaker"] bot. Solenostemon Scutellarioides, old boy deadnettle.
pāṣāṇabhedaka [ka] m. id.
pāṣāṇahṛdaya [hṛdaya] amnf pāṣāṇahṛdayā | "with a heart of stone" | insensitive, cruel.
pi pf. cf. api.
piká mf pikī bio. zoo. Cuculus indicus, Indian cuckoo; it is said to like mangoes, and that its beak is red because it tried to eat betel.
pikárāga [rāga] m. bio. ["preferred of cuckoos"] mango tree.
pinga [related to piñja] amnf pingā yellow; reddish-brown, Tanned — m. the yellow color or
brown | mouse | ang. pink.
pingākṣá [akṣa] amnf pingākṣī who has brown eyes. aruņayā pingākṣyaikahāyanyā somam krīnāti véd. Soma is bought with a one-year-old heifer, red with brown eyes.

pingala [pingala] amnf pingalā reddish, coppery, brown, Tanned; golden yellow, Golden — m. the color Golden; name of various animals | myth. np. of pingala "Bronzed", servant of Sūrya; he measures the good deeds and sins of mortals; he is represented bearded | astr. np. of pingala₁ "Tanned", personifying the 51st year of a life cycle [samvatsara] | hist. np. of the mathematician pingala₂ (2nd century BC); nothing is known of his life; he is said to be a reincarnation of the nāga Seṣa; Snakes p 187 he wrote a theory of prosody [Chandahśāstra]; in it he describes the combinatorics of combinations of n long [guru] or short [laghu] syllables — f. cf. pingalā.

Pingalaka |ka| amnf pingalikā yellow, coppery | myth. [Mah.] np. of the yakṣa Piṅgalaka | name of various animals [lit. [PT.] np. of the lion Pingalaka₁ "Tawny"; the jackals Karataka and Damanaka are his advisors.
pingalachandahsūtra [chandahsūtra] n. bed. n.p. from the Pingalachandahsūtra of pingala₂.

pingalā [f. pingala] f. type of bronze | name of various birds | phil. [yoga] the solar psychic channel [sūryanādī] pingalā on the right side, representation of the Yamunā in the microcosm; cf. Idā, Suṣumṇā | phil. [Tantra] np. of Piṅgalā₁ "Golden", one of the 8 divine powers [yoginī] | lit. [BhP.] np. of pingalā₂, rich courtesan of Vidiśā; while waiting for her lover, she was struck by grace, and withdrew to the forest as a hermit; her story was told to King Yadu by a renunciant |avadhūta| who considered her to be one of his guru masters.
pingalāgītā [gītā] f. lit. [BhP.] np. of the pingalāgītā "song of Pingala₂", verse celebrating renunciation. āśā hi paramam duḥkham nairāsyam paramam su
kham [BhP.] Desire is the ultimate misfortune; the absence of desire is the ultimate happiness.
pingalin [pingalain] amnf pingalinī coppery, brown.
picu m. cotton.
picumata | mata | n. bed. | Tantra | n.p. from picumata “cotton doctrine”; cf. Brahmayamala.
picumanda [manda] m. organic. bot. Azadirachta in dica, neem tree; syn. nimba.
picuvaktra [vaktra] n. phil. [Tantra] "cotton mouth", euphemism for the vulva of a yogini.
piccha n. tail feather (not. of peacock) | wing, crest | pl. feathers of an arrow — f. picchā foam (not. of cooked rice) | saliva.
picchala [la] amnf picchalā slimy; viscous; slippery.
picchila [picchaila] amnf picchilā equipped with a feathered tail | slobbering.
piñja n. turmeric.
piñjara [piñjara] amnf golden piñjarā; tanned — n. gold | orpiment — v. [11] pr. (piñjarayati) pp. (piñjarita) dye golden yellow. piñjarīkr dye yellowish red; brown.
piñjarita [pp. piñjara] amnf piñjaritā of golden color.
piñjūla n. armful of grass.
piţa box; basket.

pitaka [ka] mn basket | bd. cf. tripitaka | jn. cf. gaņipiṭaka — f. piṭakā f. piṭikā burn; blister, blister; swelling. gandasyopari piţikā saṃvṛttā ["a blister on a burn" | misfortune never comes alone.
pithara mn pot; hollow utensil — f. pitharī pot, vase.
piṭharapāka |pāka| m. phil. destruction of atoms by cooking.
piṭharapākavādin [vādin] amfn pitharapākavādinī phil. adherent of the doctrine that cooking only changes the quality of objects, without changing their nature; opp. pīlupākavādin.
pidhā f. step, floor | arch. temple with a stepped roof.

piṇḍa mn ball, balloon, lump | dumpling of food, morsel; food, daily bread; alms | soc. offering to the spirits; cf. tripindī body; calf; muscle; not. pl. shoulder muscles embryo | mass, quantity, collection | math. total sum; measure of a sine — f. cf. piṇḍī₁ — v. [11] pr. (pindayati) to make a ball, assemble, join. piṇḍīkṛ to make a ball; to mold, compress, ras to seem, concentrate | to identify with (i.saha₂). pindīkrtya adv. in total. evam pindīkrtya mahyam vimsatim rūpakāndehi give me 20 rupees in total. piṇḍībhū to be balled; to become compact.
pindaka [ka] mn ball, lump; fragment, piece — f. pindikā muscular protuberance; not. calf.
piṇḍada |da| amnf piṇḍadā who offers to the spirits | nourisher; master of the house — f. piṇḍadā mother.
piṇḍadāna |dāna| n. soc. rite of offering to the manes; cf. tripindī.
piṇḍapitṛyajña [piṇḍapitṛyajña] m. soc. [SB.] ved. sacrifice to the manes, one of the five major rites |mahāyajña|.

piṇḍabrahmāṇḍa | brahmāṇḍa | n. phil. nāthayogin doctrine of the equivalence of the microcosm and the macrocosm; it affirms that the yogi attains the pa ramātman by piercing the sahasrāracakra. yathā piṇḍe tathā brahmāṇḍe phil. the microcosm is congruent to the macrocosm.
piṇḍasaṃvitti [saṃvitti] f. phil. yoga understanding of the body.
piṇḍāra |āra| m. religious mendicant |bio. bot. Mal lotus nudiflorus, false teak tree, a euphorbaceous plant — n. its fruit, used in medicine.
piṇḍāraka |ka| n. geo. np. of Piṇḍāraka, place of pilgrimage.
pindālaktaka [alaktaka] m. red pigment, used to decorate the hands and soles of women's feet.
piṇḍi [piṇḍai] f. hub of a wheel.
pindika [ka] n. penis.
pindita [pindaita] amnf pinditā made into a ball, agglomerated; densified | mixed, united with (iic.) | added, collected, piled up — cl. after num. repeated so many times | multiplied.
piṇḍitārtha [artha] m. condensed meaning; summary; main point. This is the essence of your speech. )4
piṇḍī₁ [f. piṇḍa] f. ball, dumpling; morsel (food); pill | soc. gestures accompanying the silent repetition of prayers.
piṇḍītagara [tagara] n. bio. balsam endron, tree with fragrant flowers.
pindīśūra [śūra] m. ["meatball hero"] (pej.) coward.
pindī₂ iiv. pinda.
pindīkaraṇa [karaṇa] n. making a dumpling.
piṇḍīkṛta |kṛta| amnf piṇḍīkṛtā put into a ball, put into a heap; piled up, joined.
piṇḍībhūta |bhūta| amnf piṇḍībhūtā ag glomerated, compactified; put into a ball.
piṇyāka mn sesame cake.
pitari [loc. pitr] iic.
pitariśūra [śūra] m. ["brave before his father"] (pej.) braggart.
pitā [nom. pitr] iic.
pitāputrá | putra | m. of the pitāputrau father and son.
pitāputravirodha | virodha | m. competition between father and son.
pitāmaha | mahat | m. paternal grandfather | myth. np. of pitāmaha "the Grandfather", epith. of Brahmā — f. pitāmahī paternal grandmother.
pitú [pā₁tu] m. juice, drink; food.

pitṛ [agt. pā₂] m. [sg. nom. pitā, acc. pitaram; pl. nom. pitaras, acc. pitrn, g. pitrnām who protects | father | of the. pitarau the parents (father and mother) | pl. pitaras myth. the ancestors; the manes; cf. śrāddha astr. they preside over the nakṣatra of Maghās (Regulus) as well as that of Mūlabarhaṇī (of Scorpio) gr. $ pi au tau eta rho rho; lat. pater; ang. father; all. Vater; fr. père.
pitṛgraha | graha | m. phil. | Tantra | possession by an ancestor.
pitṛtīrtha [tīrtha] m. myth. np. of the pitṛtīrtha "Purgatory", also called Kumbhīpākanaraka, in iron where the damned are tortured in the Pitrloka; it was changed into paradise by Durvāsā.
pitrtva [tva] n. quality of father; paternity.
pitrtvavat [vat] m. who possesses the quality of father. rāmanisthaputratvanirūpitapitrtvavān daśarathah NN. Dasaratha possesses the paternity determined by the quality of son possessed by Rāma.
pitrdeva [deva] m. pl. pitrdevās myth. the gods and the shades.
pitrpakṣa | pakṣa | m. astr. half lunar month after the full moon of the month bhādrapada.
pitṛpaitāmaha | paitāmaha| afmn ancestral pitṛpaitāmahī — m. pl. the ancestors.

pitrmedha [medha] m. soc. oblation to the manes; this rite is performed a year or more after a death; the participants make three turns around the urn containing the ashes of the deceased, at the beginning, middle and end of a summer night; the vīṇā is played, there is singing, and at dawn the remains of the deceased are buried.
pitryajña [yajña] m. soc. [SB.] ved. sacrifice to ancestors, one of the five major rites |mahāyajña|; cf. pindapitryajña.
pitṛyāna [yāna] mn phil. transmigration at death, by the "path of the ancestors", opp. devayāna | var. pitṛyāṇa ved. id.
pitrloka [loka] m. myth. np. of the sky Pitrloka where the manes | pitaras | dwell.
pitrvat |vat| amnf pitrvatī whose father is still alive — adv. in the manner of a father.
pitṛṣvasṛ [svasṛ] f. paternal aunt.
pitrsvasrīya [īya] m. cousin (son of a paternal aunt) — f. pitrsvasrīyā cousin.
pitrsvasrīya [īya] m. cousin (son of a paternal aunt) — f. pitrsvasrīyā cousin.
pitṛṣvaṣṛ [svaṣṛ] f. paternal aunt.
pitṛvya [pitṛ] m. paternal uncle | elderly relative on the paternal side — f. pitrvyā his wife.
pitryyaputra [putra] m. cousin (son of a paternal uncle) — f. pitrvyaputrī cousin.
pittá n. med. bile, one of the 3 humors; cf. tridosa.
pittala [la] amnf pittālā med. bilious; that secretes bile — n. bronze.
pittātisāra [atisāra] m. med. dysrarrhea caused by bile.
pittāśaya |āśaya| m. med. gallbladder.
pitrya [pitṛya] amnf pitryā paternal.
pidhā [pidhā₁] v. [3] pr. (pidadhāti) abs. (pidhāya) pp. (pihita) to close, obstruct, block. dvāram pidhehi closes the door.
pidhāna [act. pidhā] n. obstruction, closure; cover, sheath.
pidhāya [abs. pidhā] ind. having obstructed. karnau pidhāya by plugging his ears.
Pināka mn club, club; bow | myth. n.p. from Pināka, arch of RudraŠiva; cf. Ajagava.
pinākin [in] m. myth. np. of pinākin "the Archer", epith. of RudraŚiva; cf. Tripura.
pipaṭhiṣ [des. paṭh] v. pr. (pipaṭhiṣati) to want to learn. )5
pipās [des. pā₁] v. pr. (pipāsati) to desire to drink; to be thirsty.
pipāsat [ppr. des. pā₁] amnf pipāsantī thirsty.
pipāsā [act. des. pā₁] f. desire to drink, thirst.
pipāsārdita | ardita | amnf pipāsārditā tour menté par la souff.
pipāsitá [pp. des. pā₁] amnf pipāsitā thirsty.
pipāsu [agt. dés. pā₁] amnf thirsty.
pipīla m. ant.
pipīlikā |ika| f. little red ant. svarge'pi pipīlikāḥ santi Even in Heaven there are ants.

Pippala m. organic. bot. Ficus religiosa, pipal or sacred fig tree (because the Buddha received Enlightenment under a pipal tree); syn. aśvattha, bodhitaru | nipple | myth. [BhP.] np. of Pippala, son of Mitra and Revatī | Atharvaveda School; cf. Pippalāda.
pippalaka [ka] n. nipple.

Pippalāda [ada] amnf pippalādā who eats the fruit of the pipal | epicurean | phil. dominated by his passions; [MO.] Two birds perched on a pipal, one eating its fruit, the other only watching it, are comparable to man [jīvātman] consuming the fruit of his actions [karman] and to the Supreme Spirit [paramātman] his impassive witness — m. hist. np. of Pippalāda "Glutton", former master of a school of the Atharvaveda | pl. pippalādās its followers. dvau suparnau sayujau sakhāyau samānam vrksam parisasvajāte | tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvattyanaśnannanyo abhicākaśīti | [MO.] Two close companion birds are perched on the same tree; one of them is eating the sweet pipal berry, the other, without eating, is intensely perceiving.
pippali f. bio. bot. piper longum, long pepper tree; this vine produces a pepper less strong than black pepper [marica] | var. pippalī id. || lat. piper; ang. pepper; fr. poivre.
pippalīmūla |mūla| n. root of the long pepper tree, used medicinally; cf. pancakola.
piba [agt. pā₁] ifc. amnf pibā who drinks (iic.).
pibat [ppr. pā₁] amnf pibantī in the act of drinking, drinking.
pibata [imp. pa₁] ind. drink!
pibatakhādatā [khādata] f. festivity (where one eats and drinks without ceasing); syn. aśnītapibatā.
√ pis₁ v. [6] pr. (pimsati) pp. (pisita) to cut (the flesh of the victims); to trim (meat) to adorn, shape, decorate | gr. ποικιλος.
pis₂ [act. pis₁] ifc. f. ornament, decoration.
piś₁ánga [anga₁] amnf piśangī reddish, brown. piśangīkr dye red.

piśāca [piś₁] m. myth. cannibal demon; ogre, vampire | pl. piśācās myth. the class of cannibal ogres; the piśācās descend from Krodhā — f. piśācā myth. ogress | myth. np. of piśācā, daughter of Daksa, mother of the piśācās ; later replaced by Krodhā — f. piśācī myth. ogress — m. piśāci ifc. ogre.
piśācagraha [graha] m. phil. [Tantra] possession by an ogre.
piśācavelā [velā] f. late at night ["at the hour when demons prowl".
piśitá [pp. piś₁] amnf piśitā prepared, decorated — n. cut meat; flesh.
piśuna [piś₁una] m. traitor, slanderer; nasty | gr. πικρος; all. Fehde.
piśunatā [tā] f. wickedness; slander.
piśunya [piśunaya] n. slander.

√ piṣ v. [7] pr. (pináṣṭi) pp. (piṣṭa) pf. (ut, nis, vi, sam) to grind, pound, crush, grind; destroy — ca. (peṣayati) pp. (peṣita) to crush; grind | lat. pinso. cūrņapeṣaṃ piṣ reduce to powder. ਪਿਣ piṣṭá [pp. piṣ] amnf piṣṭā ground, crushed — n. flour, powder; not. almond powder — f. piṣṭā arch. temple pedestal. na pináști piștam | "he does not grind flour" | he does not do useless work.
piṣṭaka [ka] m. ["made of flour"] cake, pastry, pie.
pistápasu [pasu] m. soc. ["flour cow"] substitute for sacrificial livestock, consisting of vegetables.
pistápesa | pesa | m. | "the act of grinding what is already ground" | useless work; the act of dwelling on things.
pistápesana [pesana] m. id. piştapeşananyāya saying of grinding what is already ground, evoking useless work.
piṣṭāta [piṣṭa] m. perfumed powder; it is sprinkled on oneself at Holī.
piṣṭātaka [ka] m. id.
pihita [pp. pidhā] amnf pihitā closed; hidden, concealed; covered by (i.) — n. lit. figure of speech, where one pretends to know the secrets of one's interlocutor.
√ pr v. [1] pr. r. (payate) pp. (pīna) ved. augmen ter, engraisser; grosir, gonfler, s'enfler; déborder || gr. .

pīṭha n. reclining seat, bench, opp. āsana; throne, pedestal, base | soc. ascetic seat, made of grass kuśa | district; religious center | arch. pedestal; seat of the deity; base of an image | base supporting the linga in a sanctuary; syn. yoni | district; religious center; cf. pīṭhasthāna | altar for offerings | arch. grid diagram with 3 sides, with 9 squares | math. sym. the number 9.
pīṭhaka [ka] mnf pīṭhikā stool, chair; bench; table; pedestal. utpīthikāyām adv. on the table.
pīṭhacakra [cakra] n. chariot with a seat.
pīṭhamarda [marda] m. soc. ["throne breaker"] companion of a prince or of the hero of a play; parasite, jester. pīthamardaviṭavidūṣakāḥ various matchmakers and debauchees.

pīṭhasthāna |sthāna| n. myth. one of the 51 (or 64 or 108) sacred places where the pieces of Satī's body fell when Shiva traveled the Universe like a madman carrying his corpse, which Vișnu cut into pieces with his discus; syn. devīpīṭha; cf. Kāmākhyā, Vajreśvarī | lit. [VC.] np. of the city of pīṭhasthāna, capital of Sālivāhana.
pīṭhādhipati [adhipati] m. soc. pontiff, superior of a religious center.

√ pīd v. [10] pr. (pīdayati) pp. (pīdita) ppr. (pīḍayat) pf. (ā, ut, upa, ni, pari) press, compri mer, crush, grind | torment, mistreat, op primer | besiege (a city); break (a vow); neglect (one's family) — ps. (pīdyate) to be tormented, to be afflicted; to suffer | gr. πιεζω. pīdyate me hṛdayam my heart is in pain.
pīḍaka [agt. pīḍ] amnf pīḍikā oppressor. nipātyantām prajāpīḍakaḥ Down with the tyrant!
pīḍana [agt. pīḍ] amnf pīḍanī that afflicts, that torments, that causes suffering — act. n. pressure; pressing, crushing | oppression, torment; infortune, calamity | press, winepress.
pīḍayat [ppr. pīḍ] amnf pīḍayantī that torments, that oppresses. kālam kālena pīdayan letting time take its course.

pīdā [act. pīd] f. pain, suffering, torment; injury, damage | devastation; restriction, limitation; act of obscuring, eclipse | arch. temple style characteristic of Kalinga, also called bhadra; cf. rekhā, khākhārā. pīdayā adv. reluctantly. mama prsthe pīdā vartate I have a backache.

pīḍita [pp. pīḍ] amnf pīḍitā pressed, crushed; oppressed, mistreated, tormented (by (i.)); afflicted. pīditam adv. pressing; tightly (embracing sade). kṣudhayā pīḍita tormented by hunger. pipāsayā pīdita tormented by thirst.
pīta₁ [pp. pā₁] amnf pītā drunk, absorbed, swallowed | diluted, diluted — ifc. watered, saturated, filled with (iic.). pītā gāvaḥ the cows drank.
pīta₁ amnf pītā yellow (colour of the vaiśyās) — m. yellow colour, topaz; yellow pigment — n. yellow substance; not. or.
pītaśoṇita [śoṇita] amnf pītaśoṇitā [“who drank the blood”] is said of a sword red with blood.
pītakauśeya [kauśeya] n. yellow silk. pītakauśeyavāsas "dressed in yellow silk", epith. of Krsna. pītakauśeyavāsinī "dressed in yellow silk", epith. of Sītā (called by Hanumān).

pītamuṇḍa [muṇḍa] m. bio. zoo. Ploceus philippi nus, bayā, a weaverbird; the male, with a yellow head, weaves hanging nests of woven fibre; this very intelligent bird lives in groups, and chirps frequently; syn. kaulīka.
pītarakta | rakta | amnf pītaraktā orange.
pītarāga [rāga] amnf pītarāgā of yellow color.
pītala |la| amnf pītalā yellow — m. the yellow color — n. brass.
pītavāsas [vāsas] m. myth. n.p. of Pītavāsā, epith. of Visnu "Clothed in yellow".
Pītāmbara [ambara] amnf pītāmbarā dressed in yellow — m. myth. np. of Pītāmbara, epith. of Viṣṇu "Dressed in yellow" — f. pītāmbarā myth. np. of pītāmbarā, epith. of Vagalā.
pītāśman [aśman] m. topaz.
pīti [act. pā₁] f. act of drinking ( acc. g. ) | drawing of a drink | tavern.
pītin [agt. pā₁] amnf pītinī who drinks; who has drunk.
pīna [pp. pī] amnf pīnā swollen, swollen; muscle; thick, fat, big. pīno devadattaḥ divā na bhunkte gram. The fat De vadatta does not eat all day (example of im
folding [lakṣaṇā] suggesting that Devadatta is stuffing himself at night). )7
pīnāyata |āyata| amnf pīnāyatā large and elongated. pīnāyatakarṇau with elongated earlobes (said of Buddha).
pīyamāna [ppr. p.s. pā₁] amnf pīyamānā which is drunk.

pīyūṣa [pī] mn creamy milk; not. of a cow having calved in the week (amouille) | (by ext.) cream, juice, syrup | myth. beverage of immortality, nectar; it was obtained by churning the sea of milk | kṣīrodamathana| ; syn. amṛta.
pīyūṣadhāman |dhāman| n. “receptacle of the nec tar”, epith. of the Moon.
pīyūṣadhārā [dhārā₁] f. "current of nectar", epith. of the Moon.
pīyūṣapāṇa [pāna] n. cf. pīyūṣapāna.
pīyūṣapāna [pāna] n. act of drinking amouille.
pīyūṣavarṣa [varṣa] m. rain of nectar — v. [11] pr. r. (pīyūṣavarṣāyate) become a rain of nectar.
pīlu m. palm; palm | phil. atom.
pīlupāka | pāka | m. phil. destruction of atoms by cooking.
pīlupākavādin | vādin | amnf pīlupākavādinī phil. |Vaiśeṣika| doctrine according to which cooking transforms atoms; opp. piṭharapākavādin.

pīvan [pīvan] amnf pīvarī [sg. nom. pīvān] swollen, puffed up; thick, fat, large; strong, robust — m. wind — f. pīvarī young woman, pretty woman myth. np. of pīvarī "Blossomy", spiritual daughter of the pitaras, wife of Suka.
pīvara [pīvara] amnf pīvarā fat, big, strong; dense — ifc. swollen with, full of (iic.); which abounds in (iic.).
pīviṣṭha [great. pīvan] amnf pīviṣṭhā very big. T pum iic. pums.
puṃyuj |yuj₂| m. connection or relationship with a man.

puṃyoga [yoga] m. connection or relationship with a man. pumyogād ākhyāyām gram. with the intention of designating the wife of a man (the feminine form in ī of the corresponding masculine in a is used, e.g. gaṇakī for the wife of an astronomer).
pumlinga [linga] n. gram. masculine gender.
puṃvat [vat] adv. like a man | gram. (word) used in the masculine.
puṃvadbhāva [bhāva] m. gram. morphological action transforming a word into its masculine stem [bhāṣitapuṃska] to serve as the left part of a compound word.

puṃsavana [savana₂] n. soc. ceremony [vrata] performed during gestation to obtain a son; it is a samskāra. puṃgava var. puṅgava [go] m. bull | male, hero ["strong as a bull"] — ifc. best among, expert in, chief of (iic.). kavipuṃgavaḥ m. expert in poetry. narapuṃgavaḥ m. best among men. munipumgavah m. best among the sages. pakṣipuṃgavaḥ m. ["best among birds"] epithet of Garuda or Jațāyu.
pumnāga [nāga] m. nutmeg.
puṃnāman |nāman| amnf puṃnāmnī which has a masculine name.
puṃś iic. puṃs.
puṃścala [cala] f. puṃścalī ["who runs after men" | prostitute.
puṃścalīputra | putra | m. (vulgar) son of a bitch.
puṃścalīya [īya] m. id.

puṃs m. [sg. nom. pumān; voc. puman; acc. pumāṃsam; i. puṃsā; du. nom. pumāṃsau; i. pumbhyām; pl. nom. pumāṃsas; acc. puṃsas; i. pumbhis | man, male, human being | servant; soul, spirit | | puṃliṅga | gram. (word) of masculine gender culin.
puṃska [ka] ifc. amnf puṃskā gram. (word) in the masculine form.
púṃstva |tva| n. state of being a man; masculi nity; opp. strībhāva | virility; sperm | gram. state of being of the male gender.
puṃsa iic. puṃs.
puṃsavat |vat| amnf puṃsavatī who has begotten a son — adv. like a man.
punkha m. fletching of an arrow | falcon.
punkhita [punkhaita] amnf punkhitā fletched (arrow).

punkhitaśara [śara] amnf punkhitaśarā which has feathered arrows — m. myth. epith. of Kama Madana. পু হন্ত puccha mn tail, behind — ifc. end of (iic.) (not. year) — f. pucchī ifc. which has a tail of (iic.) — f. pucchā ifc. id.
pucchakantaka [kantaka] m. organic. ["whose sting is in the tail" | Scorpio; syn. vișapuccha.
puñja m. heap, multitude — f. puñjā ifc. quantity of, mass of, heap of.
puñjika [ika| m. hail.

puñjikasthalā [sthalā] f. myth. np. of the nymph [apsaras] puñjikasthalā "Squall"; she belongs )8 to the kingdom of Varuna; having insulted a ṛṣi , she was condemned to be reincarnated as a monkey; cf. Añjanā.
√ put v. [6] pr. (puṭati) pp. (puṭita) to fold; to wrap (in (i.)); to embrace | to rub with (i.); to grind — ca. (puṭayati) ca. (poṭayati) to be in contact with.

puṭa [agt. puṭ] mn fold, hollow; envelope, pocket, bag, purse; receptacle; case | free space, fissure, fold (of (iic.)) | [nayanapuṭa] eyelid envelope of a bud | page (of a book) | |pattrapuṭa| container made of leaves.
puṭaka [agt. puṭ] amnf puṭikā which encloses — m. fold, hollow | container — f. puţikā container.

Puṇḍarīka₁ n. lotus flower; not. White lotus flower, symbol of beauty — ifc. beauty of (iic.) | tiger; variety of animals, rice, sugar cane, mango, etc. — m. myth. np. of the saint Puṇḍarīka₁ "immaculate lotus", a young Brahmin who went on pilgrimage on his mule while his elderly parents had to walk behind him; arriving in Pandharpur, he spent the night with a host who shamed him for his conduct, and he settled in this city to take care of his parents; one day when Kṛṣṇa disguised as a young cowherd tried to distract him from his duty, he threw him a brick and told him to stand on it; Kṛṣṇa blessed him and transmitted his divine essence to him, under the name of Vitthala; this saint symbolizes filial piety; He is also called Pundalīka, Pundaranga or Pānduranga | myth. np. of the celestial elephant Pundarīka₁, diggaja of the Southeast | lit. [K.] np. of the beautiful Puṇḍarīka₁ "with lotus eyes", born from the gaze of Ŝrī upon Svetaketu; he falls in love with the nymph Mahāśvetā but is devoted to celibacy by his ascetic vows; accusing Candra of being insensitive to his distress, he curses him never to be able to love through his transmigrations, and ends his life; he was reincarnated as Vaisampāyana₁, then as a parrot, while Candra was reincarnated as Candrāpīda₁ then as Sūdraka₁; In the framing story, the parrot narrates the story to the latter, who then remembers his true nature; after their death they are reborn as Puṇḍarīka₁ and Candrāpīḍa₁ and can both finally experience love | hist. np. of Puṇḍarīka₁, author of the Paramārthasevā (10th-11th centuries) | bd. [Kālacakra] np. of Puṇḍarīka₁ "White Lotus", 2nd Kalkī king of Sambhala (176–76); the Vimalaprabhā is attributed to him; the Dalai Lamas are reincarnations of him | hist. np. of Pundarīka₅ Vitthala, a Jāmadagnya Brahmin born in Karṇāṭa (16th century); he was court poet to Man Singh in Jayapura and then to Akbar; he is credited with the music treatises Sadrāgacandrodaya, Rāgamālā (1576) and Rāgamañjarī, the treatise on drama and dance Nartananirnaya, and the lexicon Sīghrabodhinīnāmamālā — f. pundarīkā myth. [Mah.] np. from the apsaras puṇḍarīkā "Lotus Splendor".
puṇḍarīkanayana [nayana] afnm puṇḍarīkanayanā with lotus eyes (symbol of beauty) — m. epith. of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa “with lotus eyes”.

puṇḍarīkapur [pur] f. geo. np. of the City of Puṇḍarīkapur "City of the White Lotus", in Mahārāṣṭra on the river Bhīma; mod. Paṇḍharpur, named after the saint Puṇḍarīka₁; pilgrimage is made there to ekādaśī in the months āṣādha and kārttika; cf. śayanaikādaśī, Nāmadeva, Tukārāma, Viśvarūpa₂.
puṇḍarīkasūtra [Sūtra] n. pl. bd. n.p. from the puṇḍarīkasūtra “Lotus Sutra”; cf. saddharma.

puṇḍarīkākṣa [akṣa] m. "with lotus eyes" (symbol of beauty) | myth. np. of puṇḍarīkākṣa, epith. of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu. om apavitram pavitro vā sarvāvasthām gato'pi vā yah smaretpundarīkākṣam sa bāhyābhyantāram śucih | Om Whether one is pure or impure, or even fallen into some state, by invoking him with lotus eyes one becomes immaculate, inside and out.

Pundra m. sugar cane | myth. np. of King Pundra, son of Dīrghatamā and Sudeṣṇā, mythical ancestor of the pundrās | people and country corr. to Ben gale | pl. puṇḍrās its inhabitants — mn sectarian mark, line on the forehead; cf. tilaka, tripundra, ūrdhvapundra.

puṇḍranāgara [nāgara] n. geo. very ancient City of Pundranāgara, capital of the pundrās, on the banks of the Karatoyā River in Bengal, also called Paundravardhanapura; its raised plateau protects it from floods; mod. Mahāsthana in Ban gladesh.
puṇḍravardhana [vardhana] n. geo. np. of the Pundravardhana, land of the pundrās in Gauda (northern Bengal); its capital was Pundranāgara; it is also called pundraksetra.

púṇya amnf puṇyā of good omen, fa vorable, happy; good, beautiful, meritorious, just, pure; holy — n. good, justice, act of merit, pious work )9 | phil. the good; opp. pāpa | soc. religious ceremony; not. performed by a woman, to keep the love of her husband and obtain a son.
púnyakāla [kāla₁] m. auspicious time.
púnyajaná [jana] m. honest man | pl. punyajanās myth. class of benevolent genies; yakṣās.
púṇyatama |tama| amnf puṇyatamā great. the purest.
púṇyatara |tara| amnf puṇyatarā compar. purer; holier.
pleasant to look at, of beautiful appearance.
puṇyadhara [dhara] amnf beneficial puṇyadharā.
puṇyanagarī | nagarī | f. geo. n.p. from puṇyanagarī "the Pure City", Maratha capital, mod. Pune in Maharashtra.
puṇyanāma |nāman| amnf puṇyanāmnī of the happy name | myth. np. of Punyanāma, a servant of Skanda.
puṇyapāpa |pāpa| n. du. puṇyapāpau phil. good and evil.
puṇyabhāj |bhāj| amnf who shares the joy, blessed.
punyabhājin [bhājin] amnf punyabhājinī id. puņyabhūmi var. puņyabhū |bhūmi| f. the sacred land.
Punyaraśmi |raśmi| m. bd. np. of Prince Punyaraśmi "Splendor of Goodness", accomplished mythical [bodhisattva] whose jātaka is recounted in the Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā.
puṇyarāja [rāja] m. hist. np. of the grammarian Punyarāja (1112th centuries), author of a commentary [tīkā] on the Vākyapadīya.
puṇyavarman [varman] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Puṇyavarmā "Protected by good", virtuous king of Vidarbha; his son Anantavarmā₁ succeeded him.
Punyastambha [stambha] m. geo. n.p. from the town of Punyastambha, in Mahārāṣṭra; mod. Puntambem, near Ahmadnagar.
puṇyāgni |agni| m. soc. public fire maintained out of charity towards travellers and the homeless in the village or town square.

puṇyāhá [aha] mn auspicious day, favorable day; festive day. puṇyāhaṃ vac (ca.) to wish (acc.) a good day. puṇyāhavācanaphalasamṛddhirastu May prosperity result from the declaration of an auspicious day.
punyāhávācana [vācana] n. wish for a favorable day | soc. consecration of lustral water.
puttala m. puppet; effigy, image — f. puttalī id.; statue; idol.
puttalaka |ka| mf puttalikā id.

puttikā f. puppet; doll | bio. termite. পুর putrá m. son | child; young (of an animal) | math. symb. the number 5 (for the 5 Pāṇḍavās) — ifc. (diminutive) little (i.e.) — voc. (affectionate) my son, little boy — f. putrī daughter | du. putrau son and daughter — v. [11] pr. (putriyáti) to wish to have a son or a child — v. [11] pr. (putrasyati) id. — v. [11] pr. (putrīyati) id. | to treat like a son | lat. puer; fr. puéril; pali putta. putrīkṛ to adopt a son. putrībhū to become a son. putrīyati chātram he treats the student like his son.
putrakalatra | kalatra | m. du. femme et fils.
putrakāma [kāma] amnf putrakāmā who desires a son — v. [11] pr. (putrakāmyati) to desire a son.
putrakāmesti [iṣti₂] f. soc. rite to obtain a son; syn. putrești.
putrajagdhī [jagdha] f. ["who eats her young"] unworthy mother.
putrajāta | putra | m. whose son is born; syn. jātaputra.
putratva |tva| n. quality of sons.
putrábhāva | bhāva | m. filiation.
putravat |vat| amnf putravatī who has a son.
putravadhu | vadhū | f. daughter-in-law, daughter-in-law; syn. snuṣā.
putraśoka [śoka] m. pain of losing one's son or dying far from him; cf. śravaṇakumāra.
putrahata |hata| m. whose sons were killed.

putrādinī [ādin] f. ["eater of your son"] (in sulte) cf. putrajagdhī. putrești [iști₂] f. soc. rite to obtain a son; syn. putrakāmesti. পুরক putraká | putraka | m. young son; little boy, little child; adolescent — f. putrakā cf. putrikā.
putras [putra] v. [11] pr. (putrasyati) to wish to have a son.
putrikā [f. putraka] f. girl | soc. girl chosen to ensure the male offspring of a father having no sons | doll, figurine; statuette — ifc. (di minutif) little girl.
putrikāputra | putra | m. soc. son of putrikā adopted as his own son by his grandfather.
putrin [putrain] amnf putrinī who has one or more sons. )()
putrīya [putraīya] amnf putrīyā relating to a son; That which procures a son — f. putrīyā desire to have a son.

√ puth v. [4] pr. (puthyati) ca. (pothayati) to crush, destroy. পুদুল pudgala amnf pudgalā beautiful, pretty, graceful — m. the body | the personality, the self | phil. the individual and their ego | bd. the person enslaved by their desires | | pudgalāstikāya | jn. material object | bd. [Vātsīputrīyās] material support of personal karma, transmitted by transmigration; it is postulated to be different from the ātman of Vedānta | pali puggala.

pudgalavāda | vāda | m. phil. doctrine of personalism, postulating the existence of pudgala as a principle of continuity of the individual and his ego; it emanates from the non-orthodox bd. schools of the Vātsīputrīyās and the Sammitīyās.
pudgalavādin [in] amnf pudgalavādinī phil. holding the doctrine of personalism; cf. Sam mitīyās, Vātsīputrīyās.
pudgalāstikāya [astikāya] m. jn. material object, one of the 6 types of physical substances | dravya₁|.
punaḥ iic. punar.
punaḥsūti [sūti] f. new production.

púnar adv. again | in return; in response, on the other hand | yet, but; nevertheless. punar api adv. again, but still; on the other hand. punar eva adv. once more. punah punar adv. ceaselessly. atha punar adv. but. kim punar adv. all the more so. punar i return, go back; leave. punar gam id. punar dā return. punar as fall back on. punar bhū go around in circles. punāramate he is still having fun. parehi nāri punar ehi kṣipram [AV.] Vaten, woman; but come back quickly.
púnarāvṛtti [āvṛtti] f. return; reappearance; rebirth.

púnarukta [ukta] amnf punaruktā redit, repeated; superfluous, useless — n. repetition, tautology — v. [11] pr. r. (punaruktāyate) to occur repeatedly. punaruktam adv. repeatedly. punaruktām nī to make superfluous.
púnarjanman [janman] n. phil. rebirth, new birth, reincarnation. mām upetya tu punarjanma na vidyate |BhG.| When I was joined there was no more rebirth.
púnardarśana [darśana] n. act of seeing again. punardarśanāya ind. adr. goodbye.

púnarnava [nava₁] amnf punarnavā renewed; rejuvenated; refreshed — f. punarnavā bio. bot. Boerha via diffusa herbaceous plant with red flowers and a thick root used in medicine as an anti-inflammatory; also a variety with white flowers bot. Boerhavia verticillata.
punarnavatā [tā] f. rejuvenation, renewal. phalena hi punarnavatām kleśah vidhatte [Kumārasambhava] by its fruit, yes indeed hard work brings comfort.
punarbhava | bhava | amnf punarbhavā born again — m. rebirth.
punarbhū | bhū₂ | amnf regenerated; returned to life or youth — f. soc. young widow remarried.
punarmṛtyu [mṛtyu] m. phil. recurrent death.

Punarvasu [vasu] m. du. punarvasū astr. np. of the two punarvasū "Who restore wealth", 5th lunar asterism | nakṣatra|, corr. to Gemini Castor and Pollux; Aditi presides over it; its symbol is a house; cf. Yamakau.
punā iic. punar.
punārāja [rāja] m. new king.
pum iic. puṃs.
pumbhūman [bhūman] m. gram. masculine word used in the plural (like dārās). pumbhūmni adv. gram. masculine plural.
pumāms cf. pums.
pumān cf. puṃs.
pur [agt. pṛ] f. [sg. nom. pūr] rampart, (wall of) fortification; citadel, fortified town | city, town — n. cf. Pura || gr. pi o lambda lambda cong fr. police, politics.
Pura [obj. pṛ] n. fortress; fortified town | city,
City | women's quarters | house, residence | myth. np. of Pura = Tripura, the "City of Three Fortresses" of

demons [asura] — f. purī fortress; city, Town | geo. np. of the holy City of purī, capital of Kalinga (mod. South Orissa, on the coast of the Gulf of Bengale), seat of the cult of Jagannātha — m. puri Town; river.
purajit [jit] m. myth. np. of purajit, epith. of Śiva "victor of Tripura".
puradvis [dvis₂] m. myth. epith. of Siva, enemy of Pura.
puramathana [mathana] m. myth. n.p. of Purama thana, epith. of Siva "Destroyer of Tripura". 1(
puravarga |varga| m. lit. section of the Bhūmyādikāṇḍa, dealing with cities.
purahan |han₂| m. myth. np. of Purahā, epith. of Vișnu "destroyer of Tripura".
purārāti [arāti] m. myth. epith. of Šiva, Enemy of Pura. पुर: puraḥ iic. puras.
puraḥphala | phala | amnf puraḥphalā which will bear fruit.
purahsád |sad₂| amnf seated in the front row; who presides.

puraḥsará |sara| amnf puraḥsarī who walks ahead, who precedes — m. precursor; accompanying, escorting, guiding — f. purahsarā ifc. preceded by; connected with (2nd century). purahsaram adv. among, in the middle of, after, with (2nd century). vasisthapurahsarāh var. vasisthapramukhāh with Vasistha at their head.
purahstha [stha] amnf puraḥsthā in front; prominently, before his eyes.
Purāri [ari] m. [purajit] myth. np. of Purāri, epith. of Shiva "Enemy of Tripura"; arch. It is one of the 16 aspects of Shiva | [purahan] myth. epith. of Viṣṇu.
puraṇa [obj. pr] m. ocean.
puratas [adv. puras] adv. before, in front of, in the presence of (g. iic.). puratah kr to place before; to put forward; to honor.

puram [acc. Pura] iic. puramjana var. Purañjana [jana] m. phil. vital principle, individual soul ["whose body is the city"] | myth. [BhP.] np. of King Purañjana; after sacrificing cows, he went on a journey to the Himalayas, where he found the castle of the beautiful gandharvī Puranjanī, with whom he immediately fell in love; he married her and they lived 100 years of amorous games; he lost his common sense and let his kingdom be plundered by an army of 360 gandharvās led by Candavega, representing the days wasted by man carried away by his passions, in an allegory of human life; he was put to death by wandering cows; His story was recounted by Nārada as a disastrous consequence of his killing sacrificial cows [yajña] — f. puramjanī phil. in intelligence | myth. np. of the gandharvī Purañjanī, wife of King Puranjana. puramjaya var. purañjaya [jaya] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Puramjaya, hero of the Kauravās. puramdará var. Purandara | dara | m. myth. np. of Purandara "destroyer of walls", epithet of In dra; also abbreviated to Puranda | lit. [Kuṭṭanīmata] np. of the Brahmin Purandara, father of Sundara sena.

puramdaradāsa [Dāsa] n. hist. np. of Purandara₁ Dāsa (~1484~~1565), rich diamond merchant from Karņāta who became Haridāsa; he composed devotional songs and is considered one of the founders of Carnatic music.

Puramdarapurī [Pura] n. myth. capital of Indra — f. Puramdarapurī geo. [VC.] np. of the city of Puramdarapurī in Mālava, capital of King Vi kramāditya; cf. Ujjayinī. Puramdhi var. purandhi |dhi| amnf prolific, abundant — f. prodigality, Abundance | myth. [RV.] np. of purandhi "Abundance", goddess personifying fertility; she is associated with Indra. Puramdhri var. purandhri [dhṛ] f. ["she who keeps the house" matron, patroness, mature married woman | var. purandhrī id.
puraś iic. puras.

puraścarana [carana] amnf puraścaranā which prepares; preparatory, introductory, preliminary — n. prolegomenon, preliminary | soc. |Tantra| preliminary rite to the enunciation of a mantra, in order to make it more effective.
purás adv. before; first; in front, opposite, in front of — pf. before | opposite, in the presence of, under the eyes of g. abl. acc. iic. | towards the East | gr. παρος; ang. fore; all. vor.

purastāt [tāt] adv. in front, before, at the head, in first position (before (g.)); in the East. yah purastādyatīnām who is first among the ascetics. purastād uṣitaḥ he lives in the East or in the eastern region | he used to live there. purastād āgataḥ he came from the East. purastād ramyā dik the eastern region is pleasant. purastād ramanīyam it used to be pleasant.
puroga [ga₁] amnf purogā which goes in front, first — ifc. preceded by (iic.).
purogama [gama] amnf purogamā which goes in front, first — ifc. preceded by (iic.). vasisthapurogamāh with Vasistha at their head.
purogāmin [gāmin] amnf purogāminī that goes in front, that precedes — m. leader | dog.
purodāś [dāś₂] m. soc. rice cake offered as an oblation in the sacrificial fire | var. purodāśá soc. id. soc. offering in general or its remains. )2
purottāna [uttāna] amnf purottānā palms up (hand position).

purobhāga [bhāga] m. soc. share set aside, preciput | impudence, indiscretion; envy, jealousy — amnf purobhāgā that which is in front of oneself | annoying, indiscreet; jealous. mama purobhāge in front of me. purobhāgam muc to abandon the game; to be defeated. te parasparayaśaḥpurobhāgāḥ they are envious of each other's glory.
purobhāgin |in| amnf purobhāgiṇī impor tun, cheeky.

puroruc [ruc₂] f. preliminary glow | phil. [ved.] recitation of formulas [mantra] of pa indrome structure of the ABBA type, preceding the reading of hymns [śastra₁] in The Rites of Soma; [KB.] such a formula "shines forth," for it is the breath preceding the body. agnirjyotirjyotiragnih | indrojyotir jyotirindrah | sūryojyotir jyotihsūryah | Agni is Light, Light is Agni, Indra is Light, Light is Indra, Sun is Light, Light is Sun.

puraskāra [act. puraskṛ] m. highlighting; preference; honor, distinction; decoration | the act of accompanying, serving; arrangement, ordering, ranking; enumeration; completion — ifc. preceded by, accompanied by, connected with (iic.); including, including, taking (iic.). sa puraskāramarhati he deserves precedence.
puraskārya [pfp. [1] puraskr] amnf puraskāryā to charge with, to name, who will be assigned to (loc. inf.).

puráskṛ [puraskṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (puraskaróti) pp. (puraskṛta) to put before, to precede; res to respect, to honor; to prefer | to name, to charge with; in to introduce. puraskriyantām that they may be honored.

puráskṛta [pp. puraskṛ] amnf puraskṛtā placed opposite; put before, placed under the eyes | put forward, preferred; honored | accompanied by; occupied with — ifc. preceded by (iic.). ... puraskṛtam adv. among, in the middle of, with ... puraskrtamadhyamakramah who prefers to follow the middle way.
puraskṛtya |abs. puraskṛ| ind. having put at the head. puraskṛtya śatakratum with Indra at the head.

purā [related to puras] adv. before, formerly; formerly, in the past, long ago (gives the present the preterite meaning) | at the beginning, first; early, soon (gives the present the future meaning) | before, except for abl. . na purā adv. never.
purākalpa |kalpa| m. ancient era. purākalpe var. purākalpesu formerly; once upon a time.

purātana |tana| amnf purātanī belonging to the past; ancient, antique | worn — m. pl. purātanās The ancients — n. legend of olden times. purātane formerly, in ancient times. kathām ekām purātanīm lit. a legend of olden times. Purātanaprabandhasamgraha [prabandhasamgraha] lit. m. of the np. Purātanaprabandhasamgraha "Compendium of Ancient Literature", by Jinabhadra (1278).

purāṇa [purāna] amnf purāṇī old, ancient, antique; faded — n. antiquity; old legend, ancient history | lit. "tale of old", mythological and religious collection; a purāna traditionally deals with five subjects [pañcalakṣaṇa]: sarga the creation of the Universe, pratisarga The secondary creations, vamsa the genealogy of the gods and sages, manvantara the creation of the human race and the first men, and vamśānucarita The dynastic histories; cf. mahāpurāṇa, upapurāṇa, sthala purāṇa, kulapurāṇa; Most were composed between 400 and 1200. The five subjects of a purāṇa are...

púrīṣa [pṛīṣa] n. Vedic. earth, clay; fill; daub; mud; not. interstitial clay of the altar of the agnicayana | pottery clay; phil. the sacrificial fire heaven is in a latent state | waste, garbage, excrement; excrement, feces.
purīṣyá [purīṣaya] amnf purīṣyā ved. fire in a latent state in the earth. agnim purīsyam angirasvad acchemah ved. We will extract Agni from the clay, like Angirā.

purú [agt. pṛ] amnf pūrvī numerous, a good deal of, in Abundance, very, often — m. Pūru myth. np. of King Puru or Pūru "Abundance", 6th king of the lunar lineage [somavamśa], youngest son of Yayāti and Sarmiṣṭhā; he received as his share the Central India or ārya country; Janamejaya₁ is his son of his wife Kausalyā₁ | hist. np. of kings of the paurava kingdom, not. Porus who was defeated by Alexander )3 in 326 ant. on the banks of the Hydaspes/Jhelum [Vitastā] (near modern Bhera).
purukútsa [kutsa] m. myth. np. of Purukutsa, son of King Māndhātā of the solar lineage |sūryavaṃśa|; he is father of Trasadasyu.
purújit [jit] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Purujit "of the many victories", brother of Kuntibhoja com fighting alongside the Pāṇḍavās.
purútrā [trā] adv. in various ways; in different directions | many times, often.
purudaṃsas |daṃsas| m. myth. np. of Pūrudamsā, epith. of Indra "of many powers".
purúmīdhá [mīdha] m. myth. np. of Purumīdha, third son of Brhatputra.
purúhūtá [hūta] amnf puruhūtā ved. often invoked; invoked by many — m. myth. np. of Puruhūta, epith. of Indra.

purútáma [super. puru] amnf purutamā very numerous, abundant; frequent, recurrent. পুক্ষ púruṣa [related to puru] m. Man, male, person; hero | official; servant | humanity phil. np. of purușa the Being, the divine spirit, the macrocosm; [Sāṃkhya] the cosmic mind or order, static male principle activated by the dynamic female principle of Nature [prakṛti] | phil. [Vedānta] the personalized self, pure thumb-sized crystal egg [angusthamātra], residing in the heart | gram. grammatical person; cf. prathama, madhyama, uttama | var. pūrusa véd. id. — f. purusī ifc. of a length of (iic. num.) men — v. [11] pr. r. (puruṣāyate) to imitate a Man || ang. person; fr. person; pali purisa. dvipuruṣī parikhā trench of two Man lengths.
puruṣatā [tā] f. masculinity, virility — adv. hu mainement.
puruṣadaghná [daghna] amnf puruṣadaghnā f. puruṣadaghnī at human height.
puruṣaparīkṣā [parīkṣā] f. lit. np. of the purușaparīkṣā, collection of 44 stories by Vidyāpati₁.
Purusapura [pura] n. geo. n.p. from Purusapura "city of Man", capital of Gandhāra; mod. Peshawar.

púruṣamedhá [medha] m. Vedic ritual of symbolic human sacrifice | Soc. ["sacrifice of one's person" | entry into renunciation, where the renunciant gives away all his possessions, his fires, his rites, his caste.
puruṣavakratā [vakratā] f. lit. [Kuntaka] oblique quality of the use of the grammatical person.
púrusavyāghrá [vyāghra] m. tiger among men. purusasimha simha m. lion among men.

púruṣasūkta [sūkta] n. ved. [RV.] hymn to the purușa, in 16 verses; it describes the sacrificial universe resulting from the dismemberment of the purușa; soc. a high-caste Hindu must recite it every morning.
puruṣastrīlakṣaṇa [strīlakṣaṇa] n. pl. puruṣastrīlakṣaṇāni bodily marks of man and woman; cf. strīpuruṣasāmānya | bed. | jyotiḥśāstra | chapter of the Gārgīyajyotiṣa.
puruṣādaka [adaka] m. cannibal | myth. [Rām.] epith. of King Pravṛddha.
puruṣāyuṣa [āyus] n. human lifespan.
puruṣārtha [artha] m. phil. purpose of human existence; tradition defines four: duty [dharma], profit [artha], pleasure [kāma] and the

renunciation [mokṣa], associated with the four stages of Brahmanical life [caturāśrama]; the first three form the trivarga | phil. [Sāṃkhya] striving towards perfection | personal effort, human activity proceeding from free will.

Purusottama [uttama] m. the best of men phil. np. of purușottama "the Supreme Being", synthesis of puruṣa and prakṛti; [bhakti] epith. of Vișnu in his Supreme form | geo. temple of purușottama in Purī, main sanctuary of Ja gannātha. purușottamakșetra [kṣetra] n. geo. np. of purușottamakșetra, region of Purī, in Utkala (mod. Orissa).

purusottamadeva [deva] m. hist. n.p. by purușottamadeva, grammarian of the 12th century, author of the Bhāṣāvṛtti, commentary on the Aştādhyāyī, and numerous dictionaries, not. the Trikāṇḍaśeṣa, the Hārāvalī, the Ekākṣarakoṣa, the Dvirūpakoṣa and the Varṇadeśanā; his patron was the king of Bengal Laksmanasena | hist. n.p. of purusottamadeva₁ Gajapati, son of Kapilendra; he ruled Kalinga from 1470 to 1497; He took Saluva Narasimha₄, king of Vijayanagara, prisoner, and released him in exchange for the surrender of the citadel of Udayagiri; his son Pratāparudradeva succeeded him.
purusottamamāhātmya [māhātmya] n. lit. np. of the Purusottamamāhātmya, a work listing mythological episodes related to the holy places of Orissa.
purū iic. puru. )4

purūravas |ravas| m. myth. np. of King Purūravā "Thunderous", 2nd king of the lunar lineage [somavaṃśa], in the tretāyuga which begins with him; he is Baudha, son of Budha and Idā, and lover of the nymph | apsaras | Urvašī, with whom he had sons Ayu and Amāvasu; the gandharvās taught him how to make fire with the aranī; he is the ancestor of Puru, Duşyanta, Bharata, Kuru, Sāmtanu and Pāndu; the institution of the three Vedic sacrificial fires is attributed to him; he is the hero Vikrama, and his thwarted love with Urvasī is recounted in the play Vikramorvaśī; [Yaśodhara₁] He visited Indra's paradise, where he saw Dharma, Kāma and Artha, personifying the 3 goals of man [puruṣārtha]; as he only revered Dharma, Kāma cursed him for being separated from Urvaśī, and Artha cursed him for accumulating wealth by stealing from his subjects; robbed, the Brahmanes put him to death with the sharp leaves of the kuśa grass.

Purocana m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the archchitecte Purocana, advisor to Duryodhana; he built at his request the lacquer palace [lākṣāgṛha] at Vāraṇāvata in which Kuntī and the Pāṇḍavās came to live, and set it on fire; he is a reincarnation of Prahasta.
purodhas [purodhā] m. cf. purohita.
purodhā [purasdhā₁] v. [3] pr. (puro dadhāti) pp. (purohita) to choose, to prefer; to charge with (not. priesthood), to appoint to.

purohita [pp. purodhā] amnf purohitā appointed to a post, appointed, in charge (not. appointed by the king) — m. soc. | "in charge" | family priest, chaplain, almoner; he is "the one who walks before (the king)" | var. purodhas id. পুল pula amnf pulā wide, spread out — m. horri pilation, goosebumps.

pulakeśin [keśin] m. hist. np. of King Pulakeśī₂ or Pulikeśī₁ of the Cālukya dynasty (6th century); he established his capital at Vātāpi₁ (mod. Badāmi) in 550 | hist. np. of King Pulakeśī₂ or Pulikeśī₂, his grandson, who extended the Cālukya empire to the South, at the expense of the Pallavās, and to the East; during a battle on the banks of the Narmadā he routed the troops of King Harşa with his elephants, and became emperor of a large part of the Deccan, from the Narmadā to the Kāverī; His reign ended in 642 with the capture of Vātāpi₁ by the Pallavās; his eldest son was Candrāditya, whose wife Vijayabhaṭṭārikā served as regent of the empire until the accession of his third son, Vikramāditya₁, who restored the empire; his standard bore Varāha; he was the first king to issue gold coins in South India. পুলক pulaka [pulaka] m. garnet | pl. pulakās horri pilation (of pleasure) — v. [11] pr. (pulakayati) pp. (pulakita) to tremble with pleasure.
pulakita [pp. pulaka] amnf pulakitā quivering with pleasure. pulakitatanuh whose body shudders with pleasure.

Pulastya m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Pulastya, progenitor [prajāpati] born from the mind of Brahmā; [Mah.] he is one of the seven sages [saptarṣi]; |Rāmopākhyāna| he is the father of Kubera by Go Sarasvatī; but, angry that the latter honored his grandfather, he recreated himself | dvija | in the form of Viśravā, begotten by Māninī to serve as a screen for him and that Kubera be Vaiśravana.
pulaha m. myth. np. of the progenitor |prajāpati| pulaha, born from the mind of Brahmā.
pulāka mn swollen grain | cooked rice ball | abbreviation; shorthand; speed, haste.
pulākakārin |kārin| amnf pulākakāriņī who hurries; in a hurry.
pulākodaka | udaka | n. rice cooking water.
pulikeśin cf. pulakeśin.
pulina mn sandbank; islet in the middle of a river; small island; sandy beach; riverbank — f. pulinā ifc. bank of.
pulinavat [vat] amnf pulinavatī sandy.
pulinda m. man of a barbarian tribe of Vindhya | pl. pulindās this tribe.
puloma iic. puloman.
pulomajā [ja] f. myth. n.p. from pulomajā, epith. of IndrāṇīSacī daughter of Pulomā₁.
Pulomajit | jit | m. myth. np. of Pulomajit, epithet of Indra, victor over Pulomajit; he killed his stepfather to avoid his curse following the rape of his daughter
Pulomaniṣūdana [niṣūdana] m. myth. np. of Pulomaniṣūdana, epith. of Indra killer of Pulomā₁.

puloman m. myth. np. of the dānava Pulomā₁; enamored of the beautiful Pulomā₁, he entered in the form of a boar into the hermitage of Bhrgu to abduct her, causing the birth of Cya vana who struck him down with her brilliance; Sacī devī was his daughter, Indra abducted her and killed Pulomā₁ — f. pu lomā myth. np. of the beautiful Pulomā₁ or Pulomī, daughter of AgniVaiśvānara; the demon [asura] Pulomā₁ coveted her; she was married to Bhrṛgu, but the prescribed rites were not performed; Pulomā₁ )5 having learned of this from Agni, he abducted Pulomā₂ who was in the final stages of pregnancy; The embryo (Cyavana) fell to the ground, and its brilliance was such that it reduced Pulomā₁ to ashes; Pulomā₂'s tears became the Vadhūsarā river; Bhṛgu then condemned Agni to eat anything and everything [sarvabhakṣaka] |myth. np. of the asurī Pulomā₃; with his sister Kalakā they performed penances to please Brahmā, who promised them that their sons would be immortal; those
ci |Paulomās| inhabit an indestructible golden city in the air — f. pulomī cf. Pulomā.
pulkasa mf pulkasī soc. mixed tribe im pure; cf. paulkasa.

√ pus₁ v. [4] pr. r. (pusyate) pp. (pusta) to prosper, to be nourished, to enjoy (i.) — v. [4] pr. (puṣyati) to nourish, to increase, to augment — v. [9] pr. (puṣṇāti) to maintain — ca. (poṣayati) to make prosper, to raise, to nourish. পুষ্ pus₂ [agt. pus₁] ifc. amnf that which nourishes, that which makes prosper (iic.).

púṣkara |puṣ₁| n. bio. bot. Nymphæa ne lumbo, blue lotus | bowl of a spoon; drum skin; tip of an elephant's trunk | myth. np. of Puskara₁ "Abundance", mythical continent, one of the 7 continents [dvīpa]; Brahmā presides there geo. np. of the City of Puşkara, place of pilgrimage in Rājasthāna, in the hills 11 km from Ajmer; its lake is sacred; on its shores is a shrine to Brahmā; in the Middle Ages it was a center of teaching of the Jain religion — m. kind of drum | myth. [Mah.] np. of puṣkara "lotus", envious brother of Nala who enlisted the help of the gambling demon Kali to usurp her kingdom by possessing it in a game of dice — v. [11] pr. r. (puṣkarāyate) to resemble a blue lotus. púşkaracūda | cūdā | m. myth. np. of Puşkaracūda | "Lotus-crowned", one of the 4 cosmic elephants
miques |gajapati| supporting the world. puşkarākṣa [akṣa] amnf puṣkarākṣī with lotus eyes (sign of beauty).
puṣkarākhya [ākhyā₂] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Puskarākhya "Called lotus", envious younger brother of Nala; he is possessed by Dvāpara; cf. puṣkara.
puṣkarāvat [vat] f. puṣkarāvatī geo. np. of Puṣkarāvatī "City of blue lotuses", ancient capital of Gandhāra, between Indus and Swat (near modern Peshawar).
puṣkarāvartaka [āvartaka] m. cumulonimbus; black cyclone cloud.

puṣkarikā [ika] f. med. syphilitic chancre lit. [DKC.] np. of puṣkarikā, daughter of the nou nou of Upahāravarmā, whom she helped to conquer his mistress Queen Kalpasundarī. puşkarin [in] f. lotus-covered pond, pond.

puşkalá [related to puşkara] amnf puşkalā numerous, copious, abundant; many copious, rich; splendid, excellent | strong, sonorous, resounding — m. type of drum | myth. np. of the hero Puskala "the Radiant", son of Bharata₁ the half-brother of Rāma; Takṣā is his elder brother — n. measure of volume of grain, equal to 8 kuñci, or 64 handfuls — f. Puskalā myth. np. of Puskalā "Abon dance", first wife of HariharaputraSāstā. puşkalāvata [vat] n. myth. np. of Puşkalāvata, residence of Pușkala — f. pușkalāvatī cf. Puşkarāvatī. পুষ্ট puṣṭa [pp. puṣṭ] amnf puṣṭā well-fed, strong, fat, fat; rich in (i.).
pustavipusta | vipusta | m. pl. the well-fed and the poorly-fed.

puṣṭi [act. puṣ₁] f. growth, development, completeness; prosperity, wealth, opulence, fatness; abundance, fatness | soc. prosperity rite; power |siddhi| of restoring health | myth. np. of Puști "opulence", daughter of Daksa, one of the wives of Dharma; she is also mother of Lobha by Dambha.
pústikara [kara₁] amnf pustikarī that makes prosper; that brings opulence.
pustimat |mat| amnf pustimatī abundant; prosperous, flourishing.
pustimārga [mārga] m. soc. ["path of grace (of Kṛṣṇa)"] doctrine [saṃpradāya] of vaiṣṇava tradition founded by Vallabhācārya; it rejects asceticism and monastic life, and exalts erotic mysticism.
puṣṭimārgīya [īya] amnf puṣṭimārgīyā soc. relating to the pustimārga doctrine.
pustivardhana [vardhana] amnf pustivardhanī that nourishes, that fattens; that increases prosperity.
√ pusp v. [4] pr. (puspyati) pp. (puspita) to bloom, to open | to flower.
púspa [agt. pusp] n. flower | ved. embellishment of a stanza [rc₂] — m. topaz — v. [11] pr. r. (puspāyate) to become a flower.

puṣpaka [ka] n. [puṣpakavimāna] myth. [Rām.] np. of Puspaka "Flowering", aerial chariot of Kubera, built by Viśvakarmā; it is a marvelous sea palace made of gold and jewels, it moved at the speed of thought, it changed shape at the will of its occupants, and it provided for all their desires; it was neither hot nor cold, and its trees bore fruit in every season; Rāvaņa stole it from his brother Kubera, whom he knocked unconscious; he used it to abduct Sītā, and provoke the war that was his downfall; the victorious Rāma used it to return to Ayodhyā with Sītā | portable earthen hearth — f. puspikā tartar; mucus | lit. last lines of a chapter, summarizing the subject matter | colophon.
puspakakunda [kunda] mn flower pot.
puṣpakavimāna [vimāna₁] n. myth. Kubera flower float; cf. Puspaka.
puspakaranda [karanda] n. flower basket | geo. pleasure garden near Avantī.
puspakarandaka |ka| n. id. | bed. name of an ancient royal garden in Mṛcchakaṭikā — f. puspakaraṇḍikā myth. ["basket of flowers"] garden of Eden of original innocence.
puṣpakaraṇḍinī [in] f. geo. np. of Puṣpakaraṇḍinī, epith. of Avantī/Ujjayinī “the well-flowered one”.

puspagiri |giri| m. geo. np. of the university bd. of Puspagiri "Hill of Flowers", 100 km East of Bhubaneśvar, mod. Orissa; it extended over the sites of Ratnagiri, Lalitagiri and Udayagiri₁; it prospered until the 11th century.
puspaguccha | guccha | m. bouquet of flowers.
puspacāpa [cāpa] m. lit. flower bow, an attribute of Kāma | myth. epith. of Kāma "with the flower bow".

púspadanta [danta] m. jn. np. of Puspadanta₁ "ivory flower", 9th mythical tīrthankara; his body is white, his symbol is a makara or a crab; he is also called Suvidhinātha | myth. np. of the celestial elephant Puspadanta₁, diggaja of the Northwest | hist. np. of Puspadanta₁, author of the late 10th century; he lived in Mānyakheṭa | lit. KSS. np. of the gaṇa Puṣpadanta₃ "flower with the tooth"; listening at doors, he heard Shiva telling Parvati the story of the vidyādharās magicians, unknown to all; Back home, he told the story to his wife Jayā₁, who could not keep her tongue, and Pārvatī banished him to earth to become the scholar Vararuci in Kauśāmbī; his curse will end when he tells the story to the piśāca Kāṇabhūti.
púspadruma [druma] m. flowering tree. puspadrumakusumitamukuṭa |kusumita mukuṭa] m. myth. np. of the gandharva king Puspadrumakusumitamukuta "Crowned with flowers like a flowering tree".
puspapurī | purī | f. geo. np. of Puspapurī, epith. of Pāṭaliputra "City of Flowers", capital of Magadha lit. [DKC.] it is the capital of King Rājahamsa.
púspabāna [bāna] m. myth. flower arrow, weapon of Kāma; there are 5 of them: ketaka, dahana, bilva, mohana, harsana; they are associated with love troubles.
puspabhadra | bhadra | mr. arch. pavilion with 62 columns — f. puṣpabhadra geo. n.p. of the Pușpabhadra river "Adorned with flowers".
púspamaya [maya] amnf puspamayī floral, made of flowers.
púṣpamālā |mālā| f. garland of flowers. púșpavat [vat] amnf pușpavatī covered with flowers, decorated with flowers, flowery — f. puspavatī woman having her period — adv. like a flower.
púspavarsa [varsa] n. shower of flowers in homage to a hero.
púspaśakatikā [śakatikā] f. the arrangement of a flower cart, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.

puspāñjali [añjali] m. soc. ritual gesture of offering flowers with hands joined in a cup | lit. form of titles of devotional works. puspāstaraņa [āstaraņa] n. the arrangement of flowerbeds, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
puspāhara [āhara] amnf puspāharā who picks flowers.
puspotkaṭā [utkaṭa] f. myth. [Mah.] np. of Puspotkatā "Gigantic flower", epith. of the rākṣasī Keśinī₂, mother of Rāvaṇa and Kumbhakarna.

Puspodbhava [udbhava] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Puspodbhava "Born of Flowers", one of the 10 heroes of the Daśakumāracarita; he is the son of Ratnodbhava and Suvrttā; after the disappearance of Rājavāhana, he saw a man fall from a cliff, who told him he was his father Ratnodbhava; then he found his mother who was about to throw herself into the fire; the two had not seen each other since their shipwreck 16 years before; then he used magical powers to find hidden treasures, and he joined Candrapāla's caravan going to Ujjayinī; There, he became friends with his father Bandhupāla, and at his home he met the beautiful Bālacandrikā whom he married after killing a rival.
puspitá [pp. pusp] amnf puspitā flowered, in flower.
puspitāgra [agra] amnf puspitāgrā ["with flowery ends"] is said of flowering trees — f. )7 puspitāgrā lit. poetic meter of 2×12+2×13 syllables labes.
puṣpin [puṣpain] amnf puṣpiṇī fleuri — f. puṣpiṇī (woman) having her period.

púṣya [act. puṣ₁] n. flower, cream, best part of — m. astr. np. of Pusya "the Best", 6th lunar asterism | nakṣatra|, corr. to Cancer; Brhaspati presides over it; its symbol is an arrow; cf. Tişya, Sidhya.

puṣyabhūti |bhūti| f. hist. np. of the Pusyabhūti dynasty, founded by Prabhākara₁ in the 6th century; cf. Vardhana₁. pușyamitra | mitra | m. hist. np. of Pușyamitra Sunga₁, general [senāpati] of King Bṛhadratha, last of the Mauryās, whom he assassinated; he then became king of Magadha, and suppressed Buddhism; he performed a horse sacrifice |aśvamedha|, and thus founded the śungā dynasty which ruled over an empire extending over the entire Ganges valley; he reigned from 185 to 151 ante. | pl. hist. np. Puşyamitrāḥ, a tribe from Central India that rebelled against Emperor Skandagupta (5th century)
pusyarāga [rāga] m. topaz.

pustaka [Persian] mn manuscript on parchment min; book — f. pustikā id. satpustaka good manuscript. pustakasthā tu yā vidyā parahastagam dhanam | kāryakāle samutpanne na sā vidyā na taddhanam Knowledge kept in a book is like money in another's hand; when the time comes to use it, there is neither knowledge nor money.
pustakavācana | vācana | n. reading aloud, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.
pustakālaya [ālaya] mn library.

√ pū₁ v. [9] pr. (punāti) pr. r. (punīté) aor. [5] (ápāvīt) pp. (pūta₁) to clean, to purify — v. [1] pr. r. (pavate) to purify oneself — ca. (pāvayati) pp. (pāvita) to have cleaned — ps. (pūyate) to be purified || lat. pūrus; fr. pur. ዧ pū₂ [agt. pū₁] ifc. amnf that cleans, that purifies (iic.).

pūga [related to puñja] m. crowd, multitude, assembly | bio. bot. Areca catechu or areca palm; it can reach 20 m; syn. kramuka — n. its fruit, the areca nut; it contains an excitating alkaloid, slightly addictive, and causes red salivation; it is used ground with hydrated lime, wrapped in a betel leaf [parna], to make betel for chewing [pāṇ] — f. pūgā ifc. quantity of, mass of, crowd of.
pūjaka [agt. pūj] amnf pūjikā who honors, who venerates; who celebrates the pūjā — m. worshipper of g. ifc. .
pūjana [act. pūj] n. honor rendered, homage, adoration (de (g. iic.)).

pūjā [act. pūj] f. soc. daily religious rite, divine service; the rite of pūjā gradually supplanted the solemn rites of Vedic sacrifice [yajña]; cf. devapūjā | adoration, veneration, worship, homage. pūjāyām loc. adv. gram. during worship.
pūjākakṣa [kakṣa] m. soc. place of worship domestic tick.
pūjārtha | artha | amnf pūjārthā honorific; honoris causa.
pūjita [pp. pūj] amnf pūjitā honored (by (g. iic.), because of (iic.)) | recognized, esteemed, consecrated.
pūjya [pfp. [1] pūj] amnf pūjyā that must be respected; honorable, respectable, venerable — m. respectable man. brāhmaṇāḥ pūjyāḥ Brahmins must be respected.

pūjyapāda |pāda| mr. hist. n.p. of the Jain ascetic Pūjyapāda, of the Digambara tradition; he lived in Karņāta in the 5th century (464–524); we owe him the Jainendra grammar, the grammar commentary Sabdāvatāranyāsa, and numerous devotional works.
pūta₁ |pp. pū₁| amnf pūtā cleaned, purified; pure, clear. vastrapūtam jalam pibet dṛṣṭipūtam padam nyaset [Mah.] One must drink filtered water and watch where one puts one's foot.
pūta₂ [pp. pūy] amnf pūtā putrid, fetid; stinking.
pūtana |na| mr. myth. evil spirit; syn. vetāla — f. cf. pūtanā.

pūtanā [f. pūtana] f. myth. np. of the demoness pūtanā "putrid", who personifies infant sickness; wet nurse in the service of Kamsa, she breastfed the newborn Kṛṣṇa to poison him, but he drained her of her vital substance and caused her death.
pūti [agt. pūy] amnf putrid, fetid; stinking — m. pus — act. f. stench. pacati pūti his kitchen is filthy. )8
pūtika |ka| amnf pūtikā id. —n. garbage, excrement.
pūtigandha | gandha | amnf pūtigandhā stinking — m. stench | sulfur.
pūtīka m. bio. bot. Holoptelea integrifo lia, Indian elm; its bark and leaves are medicinal.
pūpa m. cake, biscuit.
pūpaśālā [śālā] f. bakery.
√ pūy v. [1] pr. (pūyati) pr. r. (pūyate) pp. (pūta₂) to spoil; stink || gr. naked pivo; lat. pus; all. faul; eng. foul; fr. stink, pus.
pūya |agt. pūy| mn pus.
pūr₁ [ca. pṛ] v. [10] pr. (pūrayati) pp. (pūrita) to fill (acc.) (of (i.)), to satisfy, to enrich.
pūr₁ cf. pur.

pūra |agt. ca. pṛ | amnf pūrī ifc. filling; satisfying — act. m. act of filling, of brimming; full inspiration; abundance | flow, flood, tide, inundation | river; sea; ocean — ifc. abundance of (iic.).

pūraka [agt. ca. pṛ] amnf pūrikā that fills, that fills, that completes; that satisfies g. iic.) — m. flow, effusion | phil. | yoga | slow inspiration complete through the nose; opp. recaka | gram. complement.

pūraņa [agt. ca. pṛ] amnf pūraṇī that completes, that fills; that satisfies; that performs — m. masculine ordinal number — act. n. completion; filling; inflation; extension of an arc to the maximum | med. injection; nourishment astr. revolution of a star around its orbit — f. pūraṇī feminine ordinal number.
pūrayat [ppr. ca. pṛ] amnf pūrayantī who fills.
purita [pp. That. pṛ] amnf pūritā filled, completed; blown (conch); intensified (sound) | filled with (i. iic.).
pūritaprāṇa | prāṇa | m. phil. | yoga | breath which one has filled the chest by inspiration [pūraka].
pūru cf. puru.
pūruṣa cf. puruṣa.

pūrṇá [pp. pṛ] amnf pūrṇā full, filled; filled with (ig iic.); abundant; fulfilled, satisfied; perfect | accomplished, completed, finished; past (time); satisfied (vow) | infinite — f. cf. pūrṇā. pūr₁ņesu adv. at completion, this accomplished; when the time comes. pūr₁ņam adaḥ pūr₁ņam idam | pūrṇāt pūrṇam udacyate | pūr₁ņasya pūr₁ņam ādāya | pūr₁ņam evāvašisyate | [BU.] and śāntivacana [IU.] This is infinite, this is infinite; Infinity emanates from infinity; even infinity withdrawn from infinity, infinity remains. pūr₁ņákumbha | kumbha | m. full vase (āpam, of water) | arch. ["vase of prosperity"] pot-bellied vase from which lotus flowers emerge, a sculptural motif notably found in Amarāvatī₁; syn. pūrṇaghaṭa. pūr₁ņághata [ghata] m. arch. vase of abundance, a decorative element notably found in Amarāvatī₁; syn. pūrnakumbha. pūr₁ņácandra | candra | m. full moon.

pūrṇácandraprabhā | prabhā₂ | f. full moonlight. pūr₁ņátā [tā] f. fullness; wholeness. pūr₁ņatāvāda [vāda] m. phil. [Trika] doctrine of fullness, which defines liberation as the recognition of the freedom of the Self.
pūrnátva [tva] n. fullness; completeness.

pūrnápātrá [pātra] n. ["a full cup"] measure of capacity (256 handfuls of rice) | soc. full cup of rice offered as a sacrifice | full cup of gifts to be distributed (e.g., at the birth of a son); basket full of gifts. pūr₁ņáprajña [prajña] m. hist. np. of pūr₁ņaprajña, epithet of Madhva "endowed with total knowledge" | soc. by extension, renunciant of the Madhya school. pūr₁ņáprajñadarśana | darśana | n. phil. philosophical doctrine of Madhva. pūr₁ņapratijna | pratijnā₂ | amnf pūr₁ņapratijnā who keeps their promise.

pūrṇábhadra [bhadra] m. hist. np. of śrī Pūrṇabhadra, a Jain scholar [sūri] from Jaisalmer; he compiled the Pañcākhyānaka, a version of the Pañcatantra, in 1199 | lit. [DKC.] np. of the thief pūr₁ņabhadra₁; condemned by Kāmapāla to be executed by Mrtyuvijaya, he put his executioner to flight, was pardoned, and became the minister's confidant; he explained to Prince Arthapāla the successive vicissitudes of his father Kāmapāla. pūr₁ņamāsa [māsa] mf pūr₁ņamāsī full moon | soc. ceremony taking place on a full moon; cf. Vratopāyana. pūr₁ņayoga [yoga] m. phil. spiritual discipline of total yoga, developed by the contemporary philosopher Sri Aurobindo (1872–1950). pūr₁ņavirāma [virāma] m. double daņda ( 1 1 ), indicating the end of a stanza. pūr₁ↁvatāra [avatāra] m. myth. complete divine manifestation, full incarnation of Vishnu; Narasimha is considered pūr₁ņāvatāra, as well as Krishna from his birth; It is said that Rama was born with 14 divine parts |kalā|, and that Paraśurāma acquired 2 parts through his penances [tapas], which he transferred to Rama during Sita's svayaṃvara, so that he might become purnavatara. purnavatara [upamā₁] f. lit. [alaṃkāra] complete simile, possessing the 4 characteristics: subject [upameya], object [upamāna], common property [sādhāraṇadharma|, illuminating element [dyotaka|; opp. luptopamā.
pūrṇā [f. pūrṇa] f. geo. np. of the river Pūrņā in Mahārāstra; it originates in the Arjuna Mountains and flows into the Godāvarī | myth. np. of pūrṇā₁ "Fullness", second wife of HariharaputraSāstā.
pūrṇāhutí [huti] f. ved. "complete oblation", of frande of a full spoonful of butter; it concludes the yajña.

pūrṇimā [pūrṇa] f. astr. day (or night) of the full moon. pūrņimādina | dina | n. astr. day of the full moon. pūrņimānta |anta| amnf pūrņimāntā which ends with the full moon — m. astr. calendar whose month begins with the full moon; it is used in North India; opp. amānta. pūrņimārātri [rātri] f. astr. night of the full moon.
pūrtá [pp. pṛ] amnf pūrtā filled; ac corded, filled, accomplished — n. accomplishment; reward; merit | soc. pious foundation; honor of officiating priest.
pūrtí [act. pṛ] f. completion; finishing | reward, prize | satiety, satisfaction.

pūrva amnf pūrvā at the head, in front, first, initial; ancient, antique, traditional | earlier than, prior to, elder of (abl. iic.); oriental — pn. the elder, the first; the ancient — acc. cf. pūrvam — i. pūrveņa ifc. with; provided with — f. pūrvā the direction [diś₂] of the East — loc. pūrvasyām to the East || pali pubba. pūrvatas adv. formerly; opposite; towards; to the East | first, firstly. pūrvam kadācit adv. once upon a time; formerly. pūrvasmin kāle var. pūrvakāle adv. formerly. pūrvasyām diśi adv. towards the East. pūrvapanditah, a scholar of bygone times. pratyayāt pūrvām gram. (accent) on the final syllable of the stem. samkalpitapūrva var. pūrvasamkalpita, already ima giné, imagined before. kim atrabhavatī mayā pariņītapūrvā, have I married this lady before?
pūrvakalpa [kalpa] m. case or preceding subject. pūrvakalpe var. pūrvakalpeṣu formerly.
pūrvakāya [kāya] m. front half of an animal or a man.
pūrvakāla [kāla₁] amnf pūrvakālā which precedes in time; anterior — m. ancient time. samānakartṛkayoḥ pūrvakāle gram. Pan (III, 4,21): The absolutive shares the agent of the main action.
pūrvakālatā [tā] f. gram. relation of temporal precedence of a verb in the absolutive in relation to the main verb of the sentence.
pūrvakālika [ika] amnf pūrvakālikā concerning past time; ancient.
pūrvakālikakriyā [kriyā] f. gram. absolutive.
pūrvakālīna [kālīna] amnf pūrvakālīnā qui ap partint au temps jadis; ancien.
pūrvakālīnatva [vat] n. cf. pūrvakālatā. pūrvakṛta var. kṛtapūrva [kṛta] amnf pūrvakṛtā already accomplished; done previously.
pūrvakriyā [kriyā] f. past action.
Pūrvacitti [citti] f. premonition | myth. np. of the nymph [apsaras] Pūrvacitti; she gave 9 sons to King Agnīdhra, including Kuru₁.
pūrvajanman | janman | n. phil. previous birth; previous life.

pūrvajanmakṛta | kṛta| amnf pūrvajanmakṛtā phil. committed in a previous life. pūrvajanmakṛtam pāpam vyādhirūpeṇa bādhate [Mādhavācārya] The sin committed in a previous life torments you like a disease.
pūrvatantra [tantra] n. soc. anterior section of an Atharvaveda rite.
pūrvatara [tara] amnf pūrvatarā compar. anterior, previous. pūrvataram before; first; previously.
pūrvatā [tā] ifc. f. the act of being preceded or accompanied by.
pūrvatra |tra| adv. previously; in the preceding section, above | in a previous life. pūrvatrāsiddham gram. [tripādī] The preceding rules of grammar no longer apply.
pūrvatva [tva] n. precedence, anteriority; priority, previous condition.
pūrvadeśa [deśa] m. direction of the East. pūrvadeśe to the East of (abl.) | in the East of the country.
pūrvadeha [deha] m. forebody. pūrvadehe in a previous existence.
pūrvadehika [ika] amnf pūrvadehikā relating to a previous existence. .0
pūrvanipāta [nipāta] n. gram. irregular incidence of a compound member in the front position; opp. paranipāta.
pūrvapakṣa [pakṣa] m. astr. 1st half of the lunar month; syn. śuklapakṣa | phil. opposing thesis of an intellectual school; preliminary thesis; antithesis; opp. uttarapaksa.
pūrvapakṣin | pakṣin | amnf pūrvapakṣinī te nant du pūrvapakṣa; adversary to be refuted. pūrvapaņdita | paņdita | m. scholar of old.
pūrvapāda [pada] n. gram. first term of a compound [samāsa]; syn. prākpada; opp. uttara pada.
