prahlād [prahlād] v. [1] pr. r. (prahlādate) pp. (prahlādita) to refresh oneself, to comfort oneself — ca. (prahlādayati) to refresh, to comfort.

Prahlāda |act. prahlād| m. comfort, consolation, happiness | myth. np. of the asura Prahlāda "Comfort", son of Hiranyakasipu; he was a worshipper of Vișnu, and consequently persecuted by his father, who tried to poison him, to have him killed by snakes, to throw him into a precipice, to have him trampled by an elephant; he was saved by Vișnu Narasimha; he embodies the rewarded patience of the persecuted devotee; after the death of Hiranyakasipu he was crowned emperor of the asuras; he welcomed to Pātāla the sage Cyavana bitten by the nāga Keka ralohita, and asked him to name the best sacred places of the three worlds; the latter cited Naimisa on Earth, Puşkara in Heaven, and Cakratīrtha in Pātāla; Prahlāda went to Naimisa to worship ViṣṇuPuṇḍarīkākṣaPītāmbara; after his bath at the tīrtha he went hunting and reached Sarasvatī where he found a tree full of arrows and two ascetics with the magic bows Sārnga and Aja gava at their sides; he challenged them, but could not defeat them, and invoked Vișnu, who revealed to him that Nara and Nārāyana could only be won through devotion; he implored their forgiveness, and withdrew as a hermit, leaving the governance of his kingdom to Andhaka; after a war won by the gods, his grandson Bali concluded a truce with them and became emperor of the asurās; Prahlāda is father of Gaveṣṭhī and Virocana; [BhP.] it is also called prahrāda; cf. Holikā. ਸ਼ਿਲ੍ਹ prahva [related to hvṛ] amnf prahva inclined; sloping | leaning, inclined (before (g.)) | inclined to, engaged in, devoted to.
prahvāñjali [añjali] amnf bowed with hands joined in a sign of respect. ЯТ prā pf. pra.
prāṃśu [praaṃśu] amnf large, high, long; strong, intense — m. myth. n.p. of Prāmśu, son of ManuVaivasvata.
prāk cf. prāc.
prāktāt |tāt| adv. in front.
prākpada [pada] n. gram. first term of a compound word |samāsa|; syn. purvapada. সাক্ষ prākatya [*prakaṭaya] n. advertisement; demonstration.
prākaraņika [*prakaraṇaika] amnf prākaranikā relevant | relating to the subject.
prākaranikatva [vat] n. relevance; contextuality.

prākāmya [*prakāmaya] n. free will, free choice | phil. [yoga] the astasiddhi of omnipotence, or power to subdue the elements to one's will; it allows one to live underwater, to become invisible, to incarnate in other beings and to enjoy eternal youth.
prākāra |prākāra| m. wall, enclosure wall, rampart | not. temple enclosure with galleries and chapels. mathurāvat pāṭaliputre prākāraḥ There is an enclosure wall at Pāṭaliputra as at Mathurā.
prākārabhañjana [bhañjana] amnf prākārabhañjanā who demolishes walls.
prākāśya [*prakāśya] n. state of being evident or manifest; evidence.

prākṛta [*prakṛtia] amnf prākṛtā origi nal, natural; original, primitive; unaltered | common, ordinary; vulgar | gram. related to the root — nf prākṛtī prakrit dialect, literary language used not. in Sanskrit theatre for dialogues by women and men of the lower class, but also in prakrit poetry (as opposed to Sanskrit, the sacred prescriptive language); cf. pāli, ardhamāgadhī, śaurasenī, paiśācī, apabhraṃśa.
prākṛtacandrikā [candrikā] f. bed. n.p. of the prākṛtacandrikā “Clarification of prakrit”, or grammatical clarification on prakrit attributed to Śālivāhana.
prākṛtadhvani [dhvani] m. phone. phonemic representation of a word; opp. vaikṛtadhvani.
prākṛtaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. bed. n.p. from prākṛtaprakāśa, grammar of prākṛta due to Vararuci.
prākṛtalakṣaṇa |lakṣaṇa| n. lit. np. from prākṛtalakṣaṇa "Definition of prakrit", grammatical work on prakrit attributed to Canda₃.
prākṛtasarga [sarga] m. phil. cycle of first creation, associated with the mahākalpa; opp. pratisarga.
prāg iic. prāc.
prāgabhāva |abhāva| m. phil. |nyaya| negation [abhāva] as absence before the creation of something.

Prāgjyotiṣa [jyotis] amnf prāgjyotiṣā lit by the East — m. geo. np. of the land of Prāgjyotisa or land of the Kāmarūpās, ancient kingdom of As sam (from the 4th to the 12th century) — n. [prāgjyotiṣapura] lit. |Mah.| np. of the city of Prāgjyotiṣa, capital of Naraka and Bhagadatta.
prāgdiś [diś₂] amnf mentioned previously — f. direction of the East.
prāgdeśa | deśa | m. geo. Eastern countries.
prāgdvāra | dvāra | amnf prāgdvārā whose doors face East — n. threshold; door on the East side.
prāgbhakta [bhakta] n. (medicine) to be taken before meals.
prāgbhāra | bhāra | m. mountain slope,
Piedmont | slope | proximity | multitude, quantity, heap.
prāgbhāva [bhāva] m. phil. previous existence | superiority, excellence | phil. [nyaya] negation [abhāva] as absence before the creation of something. prāgbhāvatas adv. by a prior existence.

prāgalbhya [*pragalbhaya] n. audacity; har diesse, courage; resolution, determination | lit. au dace lascivious, a quality of the courtesan [nāyikā]. vacasi prāgalbhyam boldness of speech. সাম prāgra | praagra | n. culminating point, summit.
prāgrahara [hara] amnf prāgraharā [“who takes the best part” principal, chief; the first, the best among (g.).
prāghūrṇa [*praghūrṇa] m. visitor, guest.
prān iic. prāc.

prānmukha | mukha | amnf prānmukhā f. prānmukhī facing East. prānmukham adv. towards the East. prānmukhah upavišya sūtrāni pranayati sma [Patañjali₁] Seated facing East, (Pāṇini) establishes his rules.

prāc var. prāñc [praac] amnf prācī [m. nom. prāi; n. nom. prāk] turned forward, turned toward the East; eastern | to the East of (abl.); preceding, earlier | until (abl.) | soc. who practices the puja with fervor — f. prācī the Orient, the East, the Levant — ind. prāk before, previously, formerly; before something (abl.) — ind. prācā ved. forward; toward the East. prāgeva adv. just before, previously; before all. iti prāñcaḥ according to the ancient authors.
prācīna [īna] amnf prācīnā turned towards the front or towards the East; oriental | former, ancient, old. prācīnam adv. forward, before; formerly; towards the East; to the East of (abl.).
prācīnanyāya | nyāya | m. phil. old school of nyāya (opp. the new school |Navyanyāya|).
prācīnabarhis [barhis] m. myth. [VP.] np. of prajāpati Prācīnabarhi, son of Havirdhāna; He is the father of the 10 Pracetās.
prācīnabhārata [bhārata] m. mod. ancient India.
prācīnavaṃśa [vaṃśa] m. soc. straw hut facing East, containing the sacrificial area ved. |vedi|.
prācīnāmalaka |āmalaka| mr. organic. bot. Flacourtia jangomas, small tree producing round purple edible fruits; syn. sruvavrksa — n. its fruit.
prācārya [Praācārya] m. advanced master; ex excellent teacher.
prācetas [*pracetas] m. myth. np. of Prācetā "From the Pracetās", epith. of the progenitor [prajāpati] Daksa.
prācetasa [*pracetasa] amnf prācetasā relating to Pracetā₁Varuṇa | descendant of the Pra cetās; epith. of Valmīki.

prācya [prācya] amnf prācyā forward; eastern | former; ancient, old | pl. prācyās geo. the eastern region; its inhabitants — f. prācyā [prācyabhāṣā] the language spoken in eastern India. āsuryāh prācyāh the eastern demonic (populations).
prācyabodha | bodha | mr. mod. archeology.

prājāpatyá [*prajāpatiya] m. myth. np. of Prājāpatya "descendant of prajāpati" | soc. form of marriage intra gotra, without dowry; son Born of such a marriage | soc. form of fasting — n. power of procreation.

prājitṛ m. chariot driver; syn. pravetr. সার prājña [*prajña] amnf prājñī wise, intelligent | learned, versed in Sanskrit; graduate of ca pacity in Sanskrit — m. wise; connoisseur, scholar — f. prājñā intelligence, understanding — f. prājñī wife of a wise man.
prājñatā [tā] f. intelligence, wisdom.
Prājya [Praājya] amnf prājyā copious, abundant; great, important; long, lasting; high, eminent | hist. np. of the pandita Prājya Bhatta, author of the Rājāvalipatākā (16th century).
prāñc cf. prāc.
prāñjali [Praañjali] amnf prāñjalī soc. in añjali posture, with hands open in a cup.
prāt iic. prās₂.
prādvivāka [vivāka] m. soc. ["who questions and decides"] judge.
prān₁ [Praan₂] v. [2] pr. (prāniti) to breathe, to exhale; to live — ca. (prāṇayati) to animate, to give breath — des. (prāṇiṇiṣati) to desire to breathe or to live.
prān₂ [agt. prān₁] ifc. breathing amnf (iic.).

prāna |act. prān₁| m. breath, respiration | prāṇavāyu | phil. | yoga | respiration, one of the 5 vital breaths | phil. the principle of life | life, vigor, energy, power | pl. prāṇās phil. | yoga | the 5 vital flows or breaths: the flow of excretion |apāna|, the flow of elevation |udāna|, respiration |prāṇa|, digestion |samāna₁| and the vital breath |vyāna|, which combines the other 4 | [rudraprāṇās] phil. the 11 vital energies of man, corresponding to the 10 vital centers plus ātman the soul; cf. rudra, marut — f. prāṇā ifc. id. gr. φρην. tvam me prāṇaḥ you are as dear to me as life. hṛdi prāṇo gude ápānaḥ samāno nābhisaṃsthitaḥ | udānaḥ kaṇṭhadeśastho vyānaḥ sarvaśarīragah || [TkS.] Respiration resides in the heart, excretion in the anus, digestion in the navel, regurgitation in the throat; the vital breath circulates throughout the body.
prāṇatoṣiṇī [toṣin] f. bed. n.p. of the Prāṇatoṣiṇī, compilation of tantr ritual. (1920) by Rāmatosaņa Vidyālamkāra.

prāṇadhara [dhara] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of prāṇadhara, a carpenter from Kāñcī skilled in making automata; he was extravagant, and to keep a prostitute, he made a mechanical goose, with the aim of stealing the king's treasure; unmasked, he fled on a flying chariot; Rājyadhara is his younger brother.
prāṇanārāyaṇa [nārāyaṇa] m. hist. np. of King prāṇanārāyaṇa of the Kāmarūpās (circa 1600); Jagannātha₁ Paṇḍitarāja wrote his eulogy Prāṇābharaṇa.
prāṇapati | pati | m. soul | "master of vital breaths".
prāṇapratiṣṭhā [pratiṣṭhā₂] f. soc. rite of establishing breath in images to animate them.
prāṇabhṛt [bhṛt] m. ["that breathes"] living being; man.
prāṇamaya [maya] amnf prāṇamayī formed of breath, vital.
prāṇamayakośa | kośa | m. phil. | Vedānta | envelops it with vital breaths, forming with anna mayakośa the gross body [sthūlaśarīra].
prāṇayāma | yāma | mr. cf. prāṇāyāma.
prāṇ₁ávallabhā [vallabhā] f. beloved, dearer even than life.
prāṇavāyu |vāyu| mr. mod. oxygen. karbadviprāņavāyu CO 2.
prāṇ₁ávyaya [vyaya] m. sacrifice of one's life. prāṇavyaye nāpi even at the cost of one's own life.
prāṇ₁ásaṃyama [saṃyama] m. phil. [yoga] the discipline of breathing; syn. prāṇāyāma.
prāṇ₁ásaṃrodha [saṃrodha] m. phil. [yoga] the cessation of breathing.
prāṇ₁ásiddhi |siddhi| f. phil. [yoga] the knowledge of breath.
prāṇ₁áhara [hara] amnf prāṇaharī ["who takes life"] fatal (to (iic.)) — m. capital punishment.
prāṇāgnihotra [agnihotra] n. ved. [“offering in the fire of digestion” ritual of preparation of the dīkṣita who must feed only on boiled milk in the period preceding the solemn sacrifice.
prāṇānta | anta | mr. death | soc. death penalty.
prāṇāntika [antika] amnf prāṇāntikā fatal, mortal; capital (punishment) | for life — n. danger mor tel. prāṇāntikam adv. for life.
prāṇāpahārin [apahārin] amnf prāṇāpahārṇī that takes away life; mortal, fatal.
prāṇāpāná |āpāna₂| n. of. inspiration and expiration.
Prāṇābharaṇa [ābharaṇa] n. bed. from np. Prāṇābharaṇa, eulogy of King Prāṇanārāyaṇa of the Kāmarūpās due to Jagannātha₁ Paṇḍitarāja.
prāṇāyana [ayana] n. sense organ.

prāṇāyāma [āyāma] m. phil. the discipline of breath, 4th stage of rājayoga; the 3 phases of breathing are inhalation [pūraka], retention [kumbhaka] and exhalation [recaka]; cf. aṣṭāṅgayoga soc. one of the 3 acts of purification, with the mantra formula and the gesture | mudrā |.
prāṇeśvara [īśvara] m. soc. husband ["master of life"].
prāṇin [agt. prāṇi] amnf prāṇinī that breathes, living — m. living being; animal.
prātár adv. in the morning; early, at dawn; tomorrow. Morning, tomorrow — m. myth. np. of Prātar, the personified Morning. prātah prātah adv. every morning.
prātaḥprahara | prahara | mr. soc. dawn guard (from sunrise to 8 a.m.).
prātaḥsaṃdhyā |saṃdhyā| f. sunrise, at rore.
prātaranuvāka | anuvāka | mr. soc. morning recitation.
prātarāśa |āśa₂| m. breakfast (first meal of the morning).
prātardoha | doha | m. treatise of the Morning.
prātastána [tana] amnf prātastanī morning — n. astr. small Morning, first of the 5 moments [kāla₁] of the day, just after sunrise; it is followed by samgava.
prātikaṇṭhika [*pratikaṇṭhamika] amnf prātikanthikī which seizes by the throat.
prātijanīna [*pratijanaīna] amnf prātijanīnā good for an opponent | good for everyone; popular.
prātipathika [*pratipathaika] amnf prātipathikā which goes along the path.

prātipadika [*pratipadaika] amnf prātipadikā explicit — n. gram. ["productive word"] nominal stem (uninflected base form). prātipadikānurodhāt adv. explicitly. arthavadadhāturapratyayah prātipadikam gram. [Pāṇini] A nominal stem is a signifier that is neither a verbal root nor a suffix.
prātipadikārtha [artha] m. gram. meaning of a nominal theme.
prātibha [*pratibha] amnf prātibhā in intuitive, immediate — n. intuition; divination, clairvoyance — f. prātibhā intuition, presence of mind.
prātibhāsika [*pratibhāsaika] amnf prātibhāsikī phil. illusory; unreal | which has no meaning, absurd; physically or logically impossible.
prātiveśika [*prativeśaka] m. neighbor.

prātiśākhya [*pratiśākhāya] n. lit. a phonetic-grammatical collection of Vedic texts [chandas] from a sectarian tradition, defined by branch of the Veda [śākhā]; there is one for the Śākalya recension of the RV., two for the Yajur Veda, one for the Atharvaveda; they explain how to pronounce the Vedic texts, and how to obtain their lexical analysis [padapāṭha]; they are the oldest treatises of the Sanskrit grammatical tradition. śikṣā ca prātiśākhyam ca virudhyete parasparam | śikṣaiva durbalety āhuḥ siṃhasyaiva mṛgī yathā If a treatise on phonetics and a prātiśākhya contradict each other, the treatise is considered inferior, like the doe before the lion.
prātiśākhyakṛt [kṛt₂] m. lit. author of a prātiśākhya collection.
prātiśrutká [*pratiśrutka] amnf prātiśrutkā which resonates — n. phon. resonator.
prāthamya [*prathamaya] m. priority | the state of being first.
prādi [(pra)ādi] m. gram. preposition ["(in the list [gaṇa]) which begins with 'pra"'].
prādibahuvrīhi [bahuvrīhi] m. gram. exocentric compound beginning with a preposition.
prādur adv. visibly, obviously; in view. prādur as to be visible, to appear, to reveal oneself. prāduṣkṛ to make visible, to reveal. ete saṃkalpā mama prādurāsan these thoughts came to my mind.
prādurbhāva [bhāva] m. manifestation, mythical revelation. Epiphany, divine manifestation on Earth, note of Vișnu.
prādeśá [praādeśa] m. span (measure of length) | soc. gesture of the master touching the shoulder of the student between the thumb and forefinger.
prādhānaya [*pradhānaya] n. supremacy,

preeminence | chief | lit. [Bhoja₁] preeminence of discourse: it can be the signifier (mantra), the signified (which can be paraphrased), or both (poetry). prādhānyena var. prādhānyāt, prādhānyatas adv. principally, essentially.

prānta | praanta | mn edge, border; margin; extremity, end — m. tip, point. prāntatas adv. at the edge of, at the extremity of | marginally. yauvanaprāntam end of youth. osthāprāntau corners of the mouth.
prāntavṛti | vṛti | f. horizon.
prāntara | praantara | n. long solitary path; long distance.

prāp [praāp] v. [5] pr. (prāpnoti) pr. r. (prāpnuté) fut. r. (prāpsyate) pp. (prāpta) pfp. (prāpya, prāptavya, prāpaṇīya) pf. (anu, sam) at to reach, to arrive at, to participate in; to arrive, to take place; to obtain, to acquire, to catch; to win, to receive; to run from, to undergo — ca. (prāpayati) pp. (prāpita) to bring about; to bring about — ps. (prāpyate) to be obtained — dés. (prepsati) to aim for, to covet. atah kim prāpnoti what does this entail? lekham tasya hastam prāpayisyāmi I will hand him the letter personally.
prāpa [act. prāp] m. obtaining.
prāpaka [agt. prāp] amnf prāpikā that procures; that makes successful.
prāpaṇa [act. prāp] n. obtaining.
prāpaṇika [*prapaṇaika] m. merchant; trader.
prāpaṇīya [pfp. [2] prāp ] amnf prāpanīyā to bring.
prāpita [pp. ca. prāp] amnf prāpitā caused, brought about, led to (acc.) | obtained, procured; due. aham devadattenāvasthāmimām prāpitah it is De vadatta who put me in this situation.
prāpitatva |tva| n. act of occurring; occurrence.

prāpin [agt. prāp] ifc. amnf prāpiṇī that reaches, that obtains (iic.). ਸ਼ਾਸ਼ prāpta |pp. prāp| amnf prāptā reached, found; caught, joined; obtained; arrived | appropriate | phil. obtained at first sight [pūrvapakṣa]. kāle prāpte adv. the time having come; at the appropriate time. iti prāpte phil. this having been obtained at first sight [pūrvapaksa]. vayasi prāpte having reached adulthood ["of age"]. prāptayauvanah having become an adolescent; having reached his majority. lālayet pañca varṣāṇi daśa varṣāṇi tāḍayet | prāpte tu sodase vasse putre mitravadācaret || [Cāṇakyanīti] He should be cherished at 5 years old, and corrected at 10 years old; but when the son is 16 years old he should be treated as a friend.
prāptakāla |kāla₁| m. opportune time, propitious moment; time when — amnf prāptakālā whose time has come; opportune, seasonal.
prāptajīvika [jīvikā] amnf prāptajīvikā who obtained enough to live on.
prāptaprasavā [prasavā] f. parturient. prāptaprasavā tadbhāryā his wife is ready to go to bed.
prāptavyavahāra [vyavahāra] m. soc. ["capable of doing business" major, adult. prāptavyavahāradaśa of age.
prāptāgni [agni] amnf (village, house) affected by fire.
prāptātithi | atithi | amnf (village) which received guests.
prāptodaka [udaka] amnf prāptodakā (village) supplied with water.
prāptavat |ppa. prāp| amnf prāptavatī which has been obtained or attained | gram. not. said of a grammatical form produced by grammar.
prāptavya [pfp. [3] prāp] amnf prāptavyā that which can or should be obtained; destined, due, deserved.
prāptavyam [acc. prāptavya] iic.

Prāptavyamartha [artha] m. phil. destiny appropriated | lit. [Pañcatantra] np. of Prāptavyamartha "Predestined", nickname of a young boy expelled from his father's house for spending 100 rupees on a book containing only one poem, who accepted his destiny with candor, and to whom fortune smiled. prāptavyam artham labhate manusyah lit. A man obtains in life what he deserves (1st line of the poem that Prāptavyamartha recited when asked his name). ਸ਼ਾਸ਼ਿ Prāpti [act. prāp] f. act of obtaining, acquisition, gain, profit | act of meeting, joining, reaching; arrival | phil. [yoga] superperception or "power to reach through the senses", an astasiddhi; this power gives Omniscience and the power of healing; cf. bhagavatprāpti | myth. np. of Prāpti "Omniscience", daughter of Jarāsandha, wife of Kamsa.
prāptyāśā |āśā₁| f. expectation of gain | lit. [dramaturgy] the hero's hope of achieving the goal, one of the 5 stages in the unfolding of a narrative
dramatic | kāryāvasthā|.
prāpya [pfp. [1] prāp] amnf prāpyā to obtain, to attain | gram. qualifies an object [karman] aimed at — n. goal to attain — abs. ind. having obtained.
prāpyakārin | kārin | amnf prāpyakārinī phil. ["in direct interaction"] refers to the senses of smell, taste, and touch; opp. aprāpyakārin.
prābhākara [*prabhākara] amnf prābhākarā relating to prabhākara | phil. qualifies not. the Mīmāmsā doctrine according to prabhākara; it supports the arthādhyāhāra point of view.
prābhūtika [*prabhūtaika] amnf prābhūtikī which says “abundance”.
prāmāṇika [*pramāṇaika] amnf prāmāṇikā forming a measure | authoritative, admitting proof; credible — m. patron of his profession.
prāmāṇikatva |tva| n. authority; credibility.

prāmāṇya [*pramāṇaya] n. measure, height | authenticity; evidence, credibility; authority phil. truth, correct knowledge; validity of a cognition; epistemology. vacanaprāmāṇyāt gram. by reason of the authority of the word (of Pāṇini). yathottaram munīnām prāmāṇyam gram. The Sages are authoritative in the order (Pāṇini, Kātyāyana, Patañjali₁).
prāmāṇyavāda | vāda | m. phil. theory of the validity of knowledge; epistemology.
prāmādika [*pramādaika] amnf prāmādikā erroneous; faulty; false. prāmādikam by mistake. prāmādikah pāthah lit. erroneous reading.
prāmodya [*pramodaya] n. joy, enchantment, ecstasy.
Prāmodyarāja [rāja] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of the accomplished [bodhisattva] Prāmodyarāja.

prāyá [act. pre] m. departure, not. for a battle or a race | (departure from life) death; suicide, renunciation of life (by starvation) | principal or dominant part; habit, condition; majority, general rule | quantity, abundance, wealth; excess | close; similar; almost, as if — agt. f. prāyā ifc. rich in (i.c.); composed principally of (i.c.); almost completely (i.c.); intended especially for (i.c.) | close to, similar to (i.c.); almost, as if (i.c.). prāyeṇa adv. principally, generally probably, undoubtedly. prāyam kṛ renounce life, fast until death. mṛtaprāya almost dead. adhunā prabhātaprāyā rajanī it is almost dawn now.
prāyagata | gata | amnf prāyagatā dying, agonizing.

prāyadarśana [darśana] n. usual phenomenon; first impression. prāyadarśanāt adv. according to the first impression. prāyaśas var. prāyeṇa [śas] adv. ordinarily, generally, mainly; as a rule, for the most part; abundantly | probably, perhaps.
prāyopaveśana [upaveśana] n. ["peaceful waiting for death"] suicide by fasting. mayā prāyopaveśanam krtam viddhi know that I am going to commit suicide by fasting.
prāyaṇa [agt. pre] amnf prāyaṇā that goes forward — act. n. entry, beginning, commencement the course of life departure from life, entry into death. prāyaṇatas adv. at the beginning.
prāyaṇīya [īya] amnf prāyaṇīyā concerning the beginning; preliminary, introductory — mnf prāyanīyā ved. introductory libation, not. the first day of a solemn sacrifice.
prāyaś iic. prāyas.

prāyaścitta [citta] n. soc. [ved.] penance, expiation (for a fault, an error or an accident in the ritual, for a bad omen, for a journey abroad), propitiation; not. sacrifice to Varuna. brāhmaṇasya hanane prāyaścittaṃ nāsti There is no expiation for the murder of a brahmin.

Prāyaścittasamuccaya | samuccaya | m. lit. np. of the Prāyaścittasamuccaya, Shaivite compendium of tantric prescriptions of expiations due to Hṛdayaśiva (North India, 12th century); a contemporary text from South India of the same name is due to Trilocanasiva ācārya.
prāyas [related to prāya] adv. generally, mainly; as a rule, for the most part probably, presumably.
prāyovāda [vāda] m. bed. saying, proverb.
prāyogika [*prayogaika] amnf prāyogikī applicable; used.
prārabdha [pp. prārabh] amnf prārabdhā started; undertaken | who undertook; entrepreneur; syn. prārabdhavat — n. undertaking [prārabdhakarman] phil. immediate benefit of a
action | karmaphala | ; part of karma that has begun to bear fruit.
prārabdhakarman [karman] n. acts undertaken phil. past acts beginning to bear fruit; in influence of the acts of previous existences.
prārabdhakārya [kārya] amnf prārabdhakāryā entrepreneur | phil. bearer of the fruit of his past actions.
prārabdhavat [ppa. prārabh] amnf prārabdhavatī who has undertaken; entrepreneur.
prārabdhi [act. prārabdha] f. commencement; beginning of an undertaking.
prārabh [praārabh] v. [1] pr. r. (prārabhate) to seize, to take charge of; to undertake; to begin, to start (acc. inf.).

prārth [praarth] v. [10] pr. r. (prārthayate) pp. (prārthita) to desire, to want; to aspire to; to run to ask something (acc. loc.) from someone (acc. abl.⟩; to solicit, to pray, to implore. kṣamām prārthaye adr. excuse me. ko'paro niyogo'nuṣṭhīyatāmiti prārthayāmāsa he inquired about the following orders.
prārthana [act. prārth] n. request, desire, solicitation — f. cf. prārthanā.
prārthanā [f. prārthana] f. request, desire, solicitation | soc. prayer to a god. prārthanayā adv. at the prayer of, at the request of (iic.).
prārthanābhanga | bhanga | m. refusal of a request; solicitation in vain.
prārthanāsiddhi [siddhi] f. fulfillment of a desire.
prārthita [pp. prārth] amnf prārthitā desired, requested, solicited — n. object of desire, wish.
prārthin [agt. prārth] ifc. amnf prārthinī who desires, who wishes (iic.). kaviyaśahprārthī who aspires to the glory of the poet.
prālamba [prālamba] amnf prālamī that hangs — m. beaded pendant | female breast.
prāleya [prālaya] n. dew; frost; snow, hail. সাব্ prāv [praav] v. [1] pr. (prāvati) to favor; to be considerate of (acc.) | lat. avere, ave.
prāvīṇya [*pravīṇaya] n. expertise in.
prāvṛṣ [*pravṛṣ] f. [nom. pravṛṭ] rainy season.
prās₁ [praas₂] v. [9] pr. (prāsnāti) pp. (prāsita) to eat, to devour — ca. (prāśayati) to feed, to give food (2 acc.).
prās₂ [act. pras] m. request.
prāsa [act. prās₁] m. the act of eating, meal; food.

prāsana [act. prās₁] n. meal; food; vic tuailles | nutrition; the act of eating (iic.), the act of feeding | soc. first solid meal of a child; cf. annaprāśana — f. prāśanī enjoyment of — m. prāśana ifc. that which feeds on (iic.).
prāśanīya [pfp. [2] prāś₁] amnf prāśanīyā to eat; consumable; served as food — n. food.
prāśita [pp. prāś₁] amnf prāśitā eaten, devoured — n. soc. daily oblation (of rice and water) offered to the manes [pitaras].
prāśitavya [pfp. [3] prāś₁] amnf prāśitavyā edible, edible; succulent.
prāśitṛ [agt. prāś₁] amnf prāśitrī who eats.
prāśnika [*praśnaika] amnf prāśnikā who investigates, who arbitrates — m. investigator, examiner; arbitrator | witness, spectator.
prāśya [pfp. [1] prāś₁] amnf prāśyā to eat; edible, consumable.
prās [praas₂] v. [4] pr. (prāsyati) pp. (prāsta) pf. (anu) to throw, to launch; to throw into (loc.); to overturn, reject, repel.
prāsa |act. prās| m. act of throwing, of launching — obj. m. javelin; dart, spear.
prāsaiga [*prasaiga] m. yoke of cattle.

prāsangika [*prasangaika] amnf prāsaigikā which results from occasional, fortuitous attachment; opportune, appropriate, relevant | inherent, innate | bd. qualifies the school of logic founded by Candrakīrti — m. phil. |Nyāya| corollary | lit. |theatre | secondary subject of a play; opp. ādhikārika; syn. ānuṣaṅgika.
prāsaigya [prāsaigaya] amnf prāsangyā harnessed with a yoke — m. draft animal.

prāsāda [*prasāda] m. [“established on an eminence” palace, temple | terrace, tower, tribune terminal terrace of a building | bd. meeting and confession hall of a monastic community — v. [11] pr. (prāsādīyati) to treat like a palace. prāsādīyati kutyam bhikṣuḥ a beggar considers his hut as his palace.
prāsādalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. arch. characteristic sign of a temple.
prāsta [pp. prās] amnf prāstā thrown, launched | rejected; banished.
prāstāvika [*prastāvaika] amnf prāstāvikā with an appropriate introduction (piece, hymn).
Prāstāvikavilāsa [vilāsa] n. bed. n.p. of Prāstāvikavilāsa, 1st section of Bhāminīvilāsa, of a didactic nature.
prāsravaņa [*prasravaņa] amnf prāsravaņī from a source — m. [plakṣaprāsravaṇa] myth. center of the continent Plakṣa, mythical source of the Sarasvatī₁.
prāh [praah] pft. (prāha) (present) to announce, to say, to declare; to transmit. prāhur they declare; they proclaim.
prāhṇa [praahna] m. beginning of the day; morning. prāhṇam adv. early; in the morning.
prāhṇe [loc. prāhṇa] adv. in the morning. prāhņetana [ana] amnf prāhņetanī matutinal. prāhņetarām [tarām] adv. very early in the morning.

priyá [agt. prī] amnf priyā dear, beloved; friendly, pleasant | dear to (g. loc. dat. iic.) | dear, costly | one who loves, appreciates; enamored of, attached to (loc. inf. iic.) — m. beloved, husband, lover — n. that which is dear, pleasant; desire, pleasure, love; service, favor — f. cf. priyā — v. [11] pr. r. (priyāyáte) to love, cherish. priyena adv. willingly, with pleasure. priyápriyena adv. wholeheartedly. priyaguda amn one who loves molasses; syn. gudapriya. brāhmaṇaḥ bhojanapriyaḥ the Brahmin is fond of food.
priyákarman [karman] amnf priyakarmanī kind, kind.
priyákāmya [kāmya] m. bio. bot. Terminalia ellip tica, large combretaceae tree (30 m) with red wood; it stores water in its trunk — f. priyakāmyā desire to show kindness towards g. .
priyákāra [kāra] amnf priyakārī who does a kindness or a favor towards g. .
priyákāraka [kāraka] amnf priyakārakā that gives pleasure; benefactor. priyákāraņa | kāraņa | n. reason for a favor. priyakāraṇāt in order to do a favor.
priyákṛt |kṛt₂| amnf that does good.
priyákṛttama |tama| amnf priyakṛtamā su per. who does what pleases best.
priyáguḍa [guḍa] amnf priyaguḍā who likes sugar.
priyátā |tā| f. fact of being agreeable; charm — ifc. love of (iic.).
priyádarśa | darśa | amnf priyadarśā pleasing to the eye (of (g.)); pretty, graceful — n. friendly look.
priyádarsana |darsana| amnf priyadarsanī pleasing to the sight (of (g.)); dear | myth. epith. of the gandharva Citraratha. ekapriyadarśana dear to all.

priyádarśikā [darśaka] f. lit. np. of the princess Priyadarśikā "who manifests her love", and of the eponymous court comedy by Harşa; the princess, who was to marry King Udayana, gets lost on the way in the forest and is taken in at court under the name of Aranyikā.
priyádarśin | darśin | amnf priyadarśinī with a friendly look — m. hist. n.p. of Priyadarśin (Pāli Piyadassi), epith. of King Aśoka “with a friendly look”.

priyáprāya [prāya] amnf priyaprāyā always friendly, very polite, refined (not. language) | who expresses himself pleasantly; eloquent — n. eloquence. priyaprāyā vṛttiḥ vinayamadhuro vāci niyamaḥ prakṛtyā kalyāṇī matiranavagītah paricayah | puro vā paścādvā tadidamaviparyāsitarasam rahasyam sādhūnāmanupadhiviśuddham vijayate [Uttararāmacarita] Always amiable in conduct, gentle in behavior, reserved in speech, with noble thoughts by nature, not tiresome in company, face to face as well as in pairs, O you the unshakeable, is the very essence, secret and pure, of the wise, which is victorious.
priyábhāṣaṇa [bhāṣaṇa] n. kind word.
priyábhāṣin [bhāṣin] amnf priyabhāṣiṇī who speaks kindly.
priyamedha | medha | mr. ved. n.p. of the wise | ṛṣi | priyamedha.
prayavayasya | vayasya | mr. dear friend.
priyavāc [vāc] amnf who speaks kindly, politely, sociably — f. kind speech.
priyávādin | vādin | amnf priyavādinī who speaks pleasantly, flattering.

priyávrata [vrata] amnf priyavratā benign, in dulgent; just ["whose orders are appreciated" | | who likes to be obeyed | myth. np. of the primordial king Priya vrata "of the just edicts", son of Manu Svāyambhuva and Satarūpā; this giant [Uttānapāda] distributes the continents and oceans on the surface of the Earth by rolling his chariot over it; he is father of Dhruva by Sunīti, of Uttama by Suruci, and of Agnīdhra; astr. he personifies the star of the little bear.
priyasakhī [sakhī] f. dear friend.
priyasarpiṣka [sarpiṣka] amnf priyasarpiṣkā who loves butter.
priyāpriyá | apriya | n. (collective) things that are more or less pleasant.
priyālāpin |ālāpin| amnf priyālāpinī who says kind things.

priyángu [contr. priyangu] mf bio. bot. Panicum italicum, panic, millet | bio. bot. Sina pis ramosa, black mustard | bio. bot. Callicarpa macrophylla, shrub of eastern India, with pink flowers gathered in globules; it is a medicinal plant | liana, climbing plant (reputed to flower at the touch of a woman).

Priyangumañjarī [mañjarī] f. lit. np. of the princess Priyangumanjarī, daughter of King Vikramāditya; the latter asked Vararuci to find her a suitable husband; the latter, humiliated by the princess, proposed as a learned husband an ignorant cowherd, instructed to remain silent; the princess gave him a manuscript, asking him to revise it; the cowherd erased all the diacritical marks indicating vowels, unmasking the deception. jāmātṛśuddhinyāyaḥ maxim of revision by the son-in-law; it mocks the erroneous opinions of false scholars.
priyátama [super. Priya] amnf Priya tamā favorite, cherished above all — m. beloved, husband, lover — f. priyatamā mistress; favorite wife.
priyátara [compar. Priya] amnf Priya tarā preferred, best loved.
priyam [acc. Priya] iic.

priyámvada [vada] amnf priyamvadā who speaks kindly | myth. [Raghuvaṃśa] np. from the great harva Priyamvada "Smooth talker", son of King Citra ratha; out of pride he had bathed in the Narmadā upstream from the sage Matanga; the latter cursed him to prowl like a wild elephant until he was struck by an arrow from Aja.
priyámkara |kara₁| amnf priyamkarī who acts kindly towards (g.) | pleasant, agreeable; amiable.
priyā [f. Priya] f. beloved, wife.

√ prī v. [9] pr. (prīṇāti) aor. [1] (aprīyāt) aor. [4] (apraisīt) pp. (prīta) pf. (ā, sam) to rejoice, to satisfy, to please; to please, to give pleasure — pr. r. (prīṇīté) to rejoice — ca. (prīṇáyati) to make rejoice, to please, to delight — dés. (píprīṣati) to desire to please ang. friend; all. Freund.
prītá [pp. prī] amnf prītā rejoiced, satisfied, joyful; fulfilled, content | happy with (i. loc. g. iic.) — n. joy, pleasure. prītah bhava be satisfied.
prītātma [ātma] amnf prītātmā rejoiced in his heart.

prīti [act. prī] f. pleasure, satisfaction, joy; af affection, friendship; amiability, favor | joy of (loc. iic.) myth. np. of prīti Love, daughter of Dakṣa, wife of Kāma. prītyā i. adv. with joy, amicably.
prītikara [kara₁] amnf prītikarī who enjoys doing favors.
prītikūṭa |kūṭa| m. geo. np. of the village of prītikūṭa on the Soṇā river; Bāṇa₂ was born there.
prītimat [mat] amnf prītimatī satisfied, content, delighted; favorable, kind; who has affection for (loc. g. acc.).
prītimaya |maya| amnf prītimayī caused by joy (tears).
√ pru [related to plu] v. [1] pr. r. (tie) pp. (pruta) ved. arise, spring forth — ca. (prāvayati) to reach, inon der.
√ prus₁ v. [5] pr. (prusnoti) pr. r. (prusnute) aor. [5] (aproṣīt) pp. (proṣita) ved. to water; to irrigate, to moisten | ang. freeze; all. frieren.
prus₂ [agt. prus₁] ifc. amnf that waters (iic.).

prū [agt. pru] ifc. amnf that arises from (iic.). ਸੇ Pre [prai] v. [2] pr. (praiti) pp. (preta) abs. (pretya) to set out, to advance; to arrive at, to enter into (acc.) | to go away, to leave; to leave (this world), to die | to surpass, to stand out, to protrude.
prekṣ [praīkṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (prekṣate) pp. (prekṣita) pfp. (prekṣya) pf. (anu, abhi, ut, sam) see, look, observe, consider; tolerate.
prekṣaka [agt. prekṣ] amnf prekṣikā spec tateur, observateur — act. m. regard, obser vation.

prekṣaṇa [act. prekṣ] n. gaze; observation appearance | spectacle, representation — f. prekṣaṇī ifc. (woman) in the gaze of (iic.). tanvī śyāmā śikharadaśanā pakvabimbādharausthī madhye kṣāmā cakitahariṇaprekṣaṇī nimnanābhiḥ |MD.| A woman in the fullness of her youth is there, slender, with chiseled teeth, lips red like the ripe fruit of bryony, a fine waist, the gaze of a startled gazelle, a deep navel.
prekṣaṇakūṭa [kūṭa] n. pupil of the eye.
prekṣaṇīya [pfp. [2] prekṣ] amnf prekṣaṇīyā visible, apparent — ifc. that seems, that resembles (iic.) | of good appearance; worthy of being seen; spectacular — n. spectacle.
prekṣā [act. prekṣ] f. spectacle; observation, contemplation (of (iic.)) | circumspection; consideration; reflection, deliberation (on (iic.)) — ifc. that which is to be understood as (iic.).
prekṣāgṛha [gṛha] n. performance hall.
prekṣita [pp. prekṣ] amnf prekṣitā seen, looked at, observed, considered; tolerated — n. look, glance.
prekṣin [prekṣāin] amnf prekṣinī spec tateur — ifc. ayant le regard de (iic.).

preksya [pfp. [1] preks] amnf preksyā vi sible | to see; to consider | worth seeing. ਸੇੜ੍ਹ prenkh [praīnkh] v. [1] pr. (prenkhati) to tremble, to vibrate — ca. (prenkháyati) to swing. ਸੇੜ੍ਹਾਂ prenkha [agt. prenkh] amnf prenkhā trem blant, swaying — m. swing | du. prenkhau po teaux of a swing — f. prenkhā swing; hammock.
prenkhana |na| n. act of swinging | swing.
prenkhanakārikā [kārikā] f. lullaby (servant charged with rocking the women of the harem).

preta [pp. Pre] amnf pretā parti, deceased, dead — m. dead, deceased; spirit | phil. spirit of a dead person before their cremation | wandering spirit of a deceased person whose successive existences were dominated by greed | revenant, evil spirit, phantom || pali petā.
pretakalpa [kalpa] m. soc. ritual of the dead; it is detailed in the Garudapurāna; cf. sapindana.
pretanātha | pretanātha | m. myth. np. of Pre tanātha, epith. of Yama "Lord of the dead".
pretarāja [pretarāja] m. myth. n.p. from pretarāja, epith. of Yama "King of the dead".
preti [act. Pre] f. departure | approach; arrival.
pretya [abs. Pre] ind. being dead; in the afterlife (opp. iha in this world). na ca tat pretya no iha this is neither in this world nor in the next.
pretyabhāva [bhāva] m. phil. existence after death.
preps [des. prāp] v. pr. (prepsati) pr. r. (prep sate) pp. (prepsita) to desire, to obtain, to covet.
prepsu [agt. dés. prāp] amnf who desires to obtain, who covets, who seeks (acc. inf.).
prema iic. preman.
premabandha | bandha | m. attachment of love.
premabandhana | bandhana | n. id.
premarāśi [rāśi] m. accumulation of love. premarāśībhū to become a reservoir of love. abhogādiste vastunyupacitarasāh premarāśī
bhavanti [MD.] The feelings accumulated from the frustration of the object of desire become a reservoir of love.
Premasāgara [sāgara] m. ocean of love | lit. np. of the Premasāgara "Ocean of Love", Hindustani adaptation of the 10th book of the Srīmadbhāgavata.
premán [prīman] mn affection, love, fa veur — m. prema ifc. love for, attachment to — f. premā ifc. who feels love for. premņā i. adv. out of love.

preyas [compar. priya] amnf preyasī dearest, more agreeable, preferred; very dear, beloved — m. lover, sweetheart; dear friend | phil. |KU.| the path of pleasures, which leads to perdition (opp. śreyas the preferable path, which leads to salvation) | lit. the feeling of affection — n. flattery — f. preyasī mistress, beloved.

preyasvat |vat| amnf preyasvatī full of affect | lit. [Udbhaṭa] rhetorical figure of the simple suggestion of an emotion without complete development of the corresponding aesthetic mode [rasa]; opp. rasavat.
prer [praīr] ca. (prerayati) pp. (prerita) to set in motion, to lead (not. a boat) | to incite, to excite.
prerana [act. prer] n. starting up; exhortation, instigation; injunction, command.
prerita [pp. ca. prer] amnf preritā incited, sent.
prelay [il] v. [10] pr. (prelayati) to set in motion.

pres [prais₂] v. [4] pr. (presyati) pp. (presita) pfp. (presya) pf. (sam) to push; to impel; to start (not. a game) | soc. to direct (said of the chief priest signaling to an assistant to start a reading or a rite) — ca. (presáyati) to throw, to launch, to send; to direct the eyes towards.
presana [act. pres] n. charge, service, employment. presanakrt Who performs his service.
presanika [ika] amnf presanikā employee; civil servant.
presita [pp. pres] amnf presitā thrown, in voyé; banned. ਸੇਣ prestha [great. priya] amnf presthā dearest.
presya [pfp. [1] pres] amnf presyā Who can or must be sent — n. servitude | obligation, ser vice — mf presyā servant, slave.
presyavadhū [vadhū] f. servant.
praiṣá [act. preṣ] m. invitation; instruction; order to an assistant or servant | soc. not. order of a priest to an assistant to begin a ceremony.
praisanika [ika| amnf praisanikā Who is at orders — m. factotum.
praiṣyá [*preṣya] mf praiṣyā servant; es claves — n. service; servitude.
prokta [pp. pravac] amnf proktā said, declared; called | promulgated.
prokṣ [praukṣ] v. [6] pr. (prokṣati) pp. (prokṣita) pf. (sam) to sprinkle with sacred water; to consecrate.
prokṣa [act. prokṣ] m. aspersion.

prókṣaṇa [act. prokṣ] n. soc. consecration by sprinkling of an animal intended for sacrifice, or of a corpse before the funeral rites — f. prokṣaṇī soc. container for consecrated water | pl. water for consecrating (mixed with rice and barley).
procear [prauccar] v. [1] pr. (procearati) pp. (proccarita) to emit a sound, to pronounce — ca. (proccārayati) to cause to emit a sound, to make a noise.
proccārita [pp. ca. proccar] amnf proccāritā made resound; noisy.
proceais [prauccais] adv. very loud (noise, song) | to a very high degree, powerfully.
projjh [praujjh] v. [6] pr. (projjhati) to avoid; to erase. likhitamapi lalāte projjhitum kaḥ samarthaḥ |Hit.| Who is able to avoid what is written on his forehead?
proñch [prauñch] v. [1] pr. (proñchati) ba layer; to clean, to erase.
proñchana [act. proñch] n. act of cleaning, wiping, erasing. padaproñchana doormat.
prota [praūta₁] amnf protā sewn; at stained, fixed; skewered — n. fabric; clothing.
protaśūla |śūla| amnf protaśūlā impaled.
prototsādana [utsādana] n. umbrella, parasol.
prottunga [prauttunga] amnf prottungā very high, erect.
protsah [prautsah] v. [1] pr. (protsahati) to take courage; to prepare to (inf.) — ca. (protsāhayati) to exhort, to inspire, to instigate.
protsārita [pp. ca. protsr] amnf protsāritā offered, granted, given | ejected, banished | incited.
protsāha [act. ca. protsah] m. zeal, ardor, incitement; stimulus.
protsāhaka [agt. ca. protsah] m. incita teur, instigator.
protsṛ [prautsṛ] v. [1] pr. (protsarati) pp. (protsṛta) to disappear; to leave — ca. (utsārayati) pp. (protsārita) to cause to leave; to disperse; to destroy | to incite, to exhort | to grant.
protsrj [prautsrj] v. [6] pr. (protsrjati) pp. (protsrsta) to throw. মীব্লিস prodbhinna [praudbhinna] amnf prodb hinnā germinated; budded.
probhūta [praudbhūta] amnf prodbhūtā sprouted; emerged; germinated.
proṣ [prauṣ] v. [1] pr. (proṣati) pp. (pruṣṭa) to burn. সাষ্ট prostha [praostha] m. bench, stool, daybed.

prosthapada [pada] m. foot of stool, bench or bed — f. proṣṭhapadā pl. astr. np. of Prosthapadās "the Bed Feet", lunar asterism [nakṣatra] of the Square of Pegasus, also called bhādrapadā; cf. Pūrvaprosthapadās, Uttaraprosthapadās.
proha var. prauha [praūha] amnf prohā skillful, intelligent, clever — m. logical reasoning.

prauḍha [pp. pravah] amnf prauḍhā fully developed; mature, adult; tall, strong, advanced, confirmed; expert, learned; opp. bāla | bold, cheeky, impertinent — ifc. filled with, full of (iic.) — f. praudhā mature woman. praudhasvaram ind. in a loud voice.
praudhatva [tva] n. effrontery, audacity, impertinence | maturity; expertise.
praudhapriyā [priyā] f. assured mistress, strong woman.

Prauḍhamanoramā [manoramā] f. lit. np. of the Praudhamanoramā "Joy of the connoisseurs", lucid commentary of Bhațțoji Dīkșita on his own grammar Siddhāntakaumudī; his Brhacchabdaratna of Haridīkṣita is a commentary on it.
praudhi [act. pravah] f. complete growth, full development, maturity; perfection, high degree | majesty, dignity; assurance, self-confidence; exuberance; boldness.

Barbarīka [īka] m. myth. [SkP.] np. of Barbarīka "barbarian", son of Ghatotkaca and Maurvī; he had been a yakṣa in a previous life; Shiva gave him three infallible arrows that could destroy the three worlds and return of their own accord to his carquois; in return, he promised to engage in the great battle on the side of the vanquished; a magician, he knew how to distinguish the Pāṇḍavās from the Kauravās, and could therefore kill them all with one arrow; Kṛṣṇa, worried, disguised himself as a brahmin and went to mock him, as an archer with only 3 arrows; he demonstrated his power by piercing with one arrow all the leaves of a pipal, even the one that Kṛṣṇa had hidden under his foot; Krishna then asked for his head as an alms; he accepted, understanding that he would thus obtain liberation, but asked for the grace of being able to attend the great battle; his head was then placed on a pole overlooking the battlefield; when later the Pandavas disputed the victory, he declared that the only victor was Krishna; the latter allowed him to be worshipped under the name of Syama in the Kali Yuga; his story [Barbarikapakhyana] is told in the SkP; he is revered in Khatuśyamaji in Rajasthan, and called Belalasena in Orissa; in Nepal he is associated with King Yalambara of the Kiratas.
barbura m. bio. bot. Acacia arabica, ba boul tree, mimosa with globular yellow flowers, with very hard wood used to make carts; it produces gum arabic, and is used in medicine.

sacrificial | kuśa | arranged in a tablecloth on the altar.

(balati) to breathe, to live. ৰল bala [agt. bal] n. force, vigor, power; vital energy | troop, army | phil. means of subjugating an opponent; there are 4: negotiation |sāman|, bribery |dāna|, treason |bheda| and punishment [nigraha]; cf. upāya — m. raven myth. np. of the asura bala or Balāsura, "Mighty" son of Maya; he invented 96 magical spells which he gave to the asurās; [PP.] he defeated Indra fighting so much Jalandhara; Indra gave him thanks, bala granted him a wish, Indra asked for his body; bala dismembered himself, and his pieces scattered by Indra came from diamond mines | myth. np. of the asura bala, corr. at the ved. Vala, son of Kaśyapa and Danāyu; |Mah.| he became king of the Pāṇḍyās | myth. n.p. of many other heroes or demons | |Balarāma| myth. cf. Balarāma — ifc. strong in (iic.); cf. Vala — f. balā troop; army | soc. name of a spell || lat. va lore; fr. value. balāt var. balatas, balena adv. by force, by force.
balakara | kara₁ | amnf balakarā fortifying.
balada |da| amnf Baladā that makes strong — m. Baladā ved. np. of Baladā, epith. of Indra "that gives strength".

baladeva [deva] m. myth. np. of baladeva "Great God", epith. of Balarāma | jn. eminent person |śalākāpuruṣa| of an epic, in the role of a non-violent saint; not. Rāma, associated with the hero Laksmana and the antihero [pratināyaka] Rāvaņa, and Balarāma, associated with the hero Kṛṣṇa and the antihero Jarāsandha | hist. np. of baladeva₁ Vidyābhūṣaṇa, gauḍīya vaisnava of the 18th century, disappeared in 1768; Facing criticism from the Rāmānandī, he composed a commentary on the Vedāntasūtra, the śrī Govindabhāsya; he then became the pontiff [ācārya] of the gaudīya sam pradāya under the name of śrī Govinda Dāsa; he is the author of numerous works, notably the Tatt vadīpikā.
balabhadra [bhadra] m. myth. np. of Balabha dra "Fortunate", epith. of Balarāma | hist. np. of balabhadra₁, compiler of poetic anthologies of the 17th century.
Balabhid [bhid₂] m. myth. n.p. of Balabhid, epith. of Indra "destroyer of bala".
balayantra [yantra] n. phil. [Tantra] mystical diagram, a kind of simplified śrīyantra with two tri-angles śakti interlaced with a vahni triangle; cf. Bahucāramātā.

Balarāma | rāma | m. myth. np. of Balarāma "rāma₂ the powerful", elder brother of Kṛṣṇa, 8th avatar of Viṣṇu; son of Vasudeva captive of the tyrant Kaṃsa, he was born of Devakī in prison, but was magically transferred into the womb of Rohin₃ who raised him in secret; patron of farmers, his emblem is the plow |hala| with which he guided the waters of the rebellious Yamunā so that he could bathe in its waters; Indian Hercules, his weapon is the club |musala| Kheṭa; he killed the demons Dhe nuka and Pralamba opposed to his brother; he fought the monster Jarāsandha with the weapon sthūṇākarṇa; He is depicted as white and dressed in blue; he is the divine drinker of palm wine, with which he is drunk; he fought with Ganesha, who took his plow; he married the giantess Revatī who came from the previous era; he embodies on Earth AnantaSeşa, and thus represents Creation accompanying his brother Kṛṣṇa the Creator; after the destruction of the yādavās who killed each other in a quarrel born from a curse of Nārada, he went into the forest with Kṛṣṇa, where he died, the nāga Seṣa coming out of his mouth; cf. Pralambāri, Baladeva, Balabhadra, Samkarşana, Sīrī, Halabhṛt, Halāyudha.
balavīrya [vīrya] n. strength and heroism — mr. myth. n.p. of balavīrya, descendants of Bharata.
balavṛtra | vṛtra | mr. of. myth. bala and vṛtra.
balavrtraniṣūdana [niṣūdana] m. ved. ["murderer of bala and Vṛṭra" | epith. of Indra.
Balasūdana [sūdana] m. myth. np. of Balasūdana, epith. of Indra "destroyer of bala".
balopeta [upeta] amnf balopetā full of vigor.
balana [act. bal] n. reinforcement.
balava var. valava n. astr. second lunar half-day [karana] (mobile).

bálavat [balavat] amnf bala vatī strong, powerful, intense; important, main, predominant — adv. strongly, intensely; very. atrabhavatī balavat paritrastā Madam is very frightened. ৰলাক balāka var. valāka [balaāka] m. organic. zoo. Ar dea torra/putea, variety of heron or egret; it broods during the rainy season | zoo. Phoeni copterus ruber, flamingo — f. balākā id. (more common) | mistress, lover.
balākāśva [aśva] m. myth. np. of balākāśva, son of Aja₁Sindhudvīpa₁; Kuśika is his son.
balāt [abl. bala] iic.
balātkāra [kāra] m. use of force; violence; rape | detention for default of debt. balātkāram var. balātkāreņa with violence, rape; by using force.

balāha m. bd. np. of the flying horse balāha, into which the accomplished |bodhisattva| Lokeśvara had changed himself to save the merchant Simhala and his shipwrecked companions off the island of Ceylon [Tāmradvīpa]; he is represented at Angkor at Preah Neak Pean, the fountain of the "Intertwined Serpents" (Nanda₁ and Upananda).

Balāhaka₁ var. valāhaka [vārivāhaka] m. storm cloud, rain cloud | myth. one of the seven clouds of the apocalypse | myth. [PP.] np. of Balāhaka₁ "Hurricane", one of the 4 steeds of Kṛṣṇa's chariot, white in color | lit. [K.] np. of Balāhaka₁, commander-in-chief of King Tārāpīda's army | myth. [purāṇa] np. of Balāhaka₁, nāga guardian of Varuna's audience hall | myth. [Mah.] np. of Balāhaka₁, brother of Jayadratha; he helped him kidnap Draupadī.

balí m. present; offering | soc. oblation, of propitiatory offering; not. offering thrown on the ground or in the air in the bhūtayajña | royal tribute, tax, levy | myth. np. of King Bali "Sacrifice", son of Virocana, king of the demons [daitya]; he is father of Bāṇa by his wife Vindhyāvalī; by the powers acquired by his penances and thanks to the sacrifice of omnipotence [viśvajit] made by his chaplain Sukra who could resurrect him by his samjīvanī power, [HV.] he had defeated Indra thanks to the weapon of Varuna [vārunāstra] and had appropriated the three worlds; he had secured a prosperous reign by celebrating 100 aśvamedha; He was defeated by Vishnu who incarnated as VāmanaTrivikrama, and demoted him to ruler of the underworld [pātāla]; he is one of the 7 immortals [ciramjīvin]; the demon-bull Arista is his son; he gave his wife Sudeṣṇā to the hermit Dīrghatamā so that he would bear her intelligent sons; cf. Mahābali, Vairocana₁.
balíkara₁ [kara₁] amnf balikarī who offers propitiatory sacrifices.
balíkara₂ [kara₂] m. pl. soc. taxes and services.
balíkṛt [kṛt₂] amnf who pays taxes; tri butaire.
balijana | jana | m. soc. man destined to be offered as a sacrifice to the Goddess.

balípīṭha |pīṭha| n. soc. sacrificial altar, flat-topped base, at the entrance to the first enclosure of a temple, in the axis of the sanctuary; it receives offerings and serves to ward off harmful influences from the outside.
balípusta | pusta | m. "fed by oblations", epith. of the raven.
balipratipadā | pratipadā | f. soc. festival of the return of King Bali to Earth, the 3rd day of dīpāvali.
balibhuj | bhuj₂ | m. "oblation eater", epithet of the crow.
balitama [great. balin] amnf balitamā the strongest.
balitara [comp. balin] amnf balitarā more robust.
balín [balain] amnf balinī strong, vigorous, powerful; robust. ৰলিষ্ট baliṣṭha [super. balin] amnf baliṣṭhā very strong; stronger than (abl.).
baliṣṭhatama [tama] amnf baliṣṭhatamā su per. the most powerful.
bálīyas [compar. balin] amnf balīyasī stronger; more important; more effective — adv. more strongly.
balīyastara |tara| amnf balīyastarā compar. stronger; more powerful.
balīyastva |tva| n. predominance; primacy in force.
balya |balaya| amnf balyā fortifying | vigorous.

ballava var. vallava m. cowherd | myth. |Mah.| np. of ballava "Shepherd", false identity of Bhīma disguised as a head cook, butcher and wrestler to hide at the court of King Virāta during the 13th year of exile of the Pāṇḍavās — f. vallavī cowherd.
bava var. vava n. astr. first lunar half-day |karaṇa| (mobile).

Basava |related to vṛṣabha| m. hist. np. of Ba sava, vīraśaiva brahmin born near Bījāpur (1125– 1167); he founded the lingāyat sect; he is credited with a work of free-style mystical poetry in the form of sayings [vacana]; he campaigned against castes, rituals and reincarnation, and for the remarriage of widows; he lived in Kalyāṇī as minister to King Bījala Deva; from whom he was expelled; he is considered an incarnation of Nandī (whose kannara name he bears); he is often affectionately called Basavanna "Brother Basava", or respectfully Basaveśvara "Lord Basava".
basti [vasti] m. med. [Ayurveda] laxative treatment.

bahala [baṃhala] amnf bahalā thick; dense, compact; firm, solid | bushy, ruffled | wide, extensive; intense (color) | numerous; co pious, abundant; syn. bahula — i.e. extremely (ifc.) — i.e. filled with, consisting principally of (iic.).
bahalatā [tā] f. thickness.
bahir iic. bahis.

bahiranga | anga₁ | amnf bahirangā concerning the outside; outside, external; distant; inessential; extrinsic; opp. antaranga — m. external part; foreign | math. external circle | gram. said of a rule whose causes of application are more external than another rule called antaranga having priority.

bahirātmam [ātman] adv. outside of yourself.

bahirbhūta [pp. bahirbhū] amnf ba hirbhūtā gone out, left outside | excluded, dismissed from (iic.) | elapsed (time interval) | inattentive; giddy.

bahiṣkṛ [bahiskṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (bahiṣkaroti) pp. (bahiṣkṛta) abs. (bahiṣkṛtya) to put out, exclude, expel.
bahiṣkṛta [pp. bahiṣkṛtā banished, excluded.
bahiṣṭāt [bahistāt] adv. from outside.
bahís adv. outside, outside, externally — pf. out of (abl. g.) | out of abl. g. .
bahiścara | cara | amnf bahiścarī who goes outside, exterior, external — m. spy.

bahispavamāná [pavamāna] m. ved. ["outer praise of the (soma) purified"] first song of praise |stotra| sung by the sāmaga during the sa crifice jyotistoma for the pressing |savana₁| of the morning, outside the sacrificial area [vedi] to its northeast; it consists of three stanzas | trca|.
bahisprajña [prajña] amnf bahisprajñā phil. whose knowledge is directed towards external objects.

bahú [baṃhu] amnf bahu f. bahvī noun large, abundant; important, large | pl. bahavas many — iic. very, many | which is very, which has many || gr. v ; lat. pinguis. bahu acc. many. bahutas adv. in great number. kim bahunā in short, to make it brief.
bahukaṇṭā [kaṇṭa] f. organic. epith. of bot. Solanum indicum, very thorny plant; syn. bṛhatī.
bahukara | kara₁ | mf bahukarā big worker — m. bio. dromedary.
bahukukkuṭa [kukkuṭa] amnf bahukukkuṭā where there are many roosters.
bahukautuka [kautuka] amnf bahukautukā abundant in wonders. bahukautukah sa deśah this country is rich in curiosities.
bahukṣīrā |kṣīra| f. cow that gives a lot of milk. goșu kṛṣṇā bahukṣīrā among cows, the black one is the most productive in milk.
bahucāra [cāra] m. great journey — amnf bahucārā or one who travels a lot | soc. person of nomadic caste.
bahucāramātṛ [mātṛ] f. myth. np. of the goddess Bahucāramātā, aspect of Tripurasundarī; her vehicle is the rooster, her symbol is the balayan tra; she is the patroness of transsexuals and cases
trats [hijra]; she is worshipped in Bahucāraji in Gu jarāt (distr. Mahsana).
bahucārin [cārin] amnf bahucārinī who travels a lot.
bahujana | jana | m. crowd, multitude.
bahutama [tama] amnf bahutamā super. the most numerous | the furthest. bahutamam adv. to the highest degree; extremely. ā bahutamāt puruṣāt to the furthest descendant.

bahúdhānyaka |dhānyaka| m. geo. np. of Ba hudhānyaka "Fertile", land of the Yaudheyās; mod. Pañjāb.

bahuphala [phala] amnf bahuphalā covered with fruit.
bahubīja | bīja | amnf bahubījā which has many seeds — m. bio. bot. Annona reticulata | bio. bot. Psidium guajava — n. anone, custard apple guava.
bahubhārya | bhāryā| amnf bahubhāryā poly game.
