bahúmāna | māna₁ | m. high esteem; great respect for (loc. g.). sabahumānam with great respect.
bahúrūpá [rūpa] amnf bahurūpā multiform; of varied aspects | myth. said of many gods — f. bahurūpā myth. one of the 7 languages of Agni [saptajihva].
bahuvacana [vacana] n. gram. plural.
bahuvāram [vāra] adv. many times, very often.
bahuvidha [vidha] amnf bahuvidhā miscellaneous.

bahuvrīhi | vrīhi | amnf prosperous, rich | "(who has) a lot of rice"] — m. gram. [generic] possessive compound forming an adjective [viśeṣaṇa] (as for example bahuvrīhi); they are exocentric, the main notion [pradhāna] being outside the compound |anyapada|.
bahúśas [śas] adv. many times, repeatedly, often | in quantity, a lot.
bahúśākha [śākhā] amnf bahuśākhā ["multi branch" | branched; diverse, varied; multiple.
bahuśruta [śruta] amnf bahuśrutā soc. expert in Veda.
bahuśreyasī [śreyasī] m. who has many good wives.
bahusvara | svara | amnf bahusvarā gram. (word) multisyllabic.
bahudhā [bahudhā] adv. in many ways, variously.

bahulá [bahula] amnf bahulā numerous; frequent; abundant; very | thick, wide; ample, spacious heavens | dark astr. (said of the fortnight | pakṣa| when the Moon is waning) | accompanied by | gram. of frequent application; productive. bahulam adv. often, frequently | gram. (rule) with exceptions. bahuletarapakṣayoḥ in the dark fortnight and the light fortnight of the month.
bahv iic. bahu.
bahvre | re₂ | amnf lit. which contains many verses.
bahvṛca |ṛca| amnf bahvṛcā lit. which contains many verses — m. soc. teacher of the Rigveda.
bahvrcopanisad [upanisad] f. bed. n.p. of Bahvrcopanisad.
bāḍhá |pp. baṃh| amnf bāḍhā reinforced, strengthened, consolidated; powerful, strong. bādham adv. surely, assuredly, certainly; of course, so be it, but yes, if done. bādham iti very well, so be it.

Bāṇa₁ var. vāṇa m. reed (serving as an arrow); arrow | myth. np. of the asura Bāṇa₁ "Arrow", eldest son of Bali and Vindhyāvalī; his wealth was fabulous, and all the kings trembled before him; he lived in the "City of Blood" Sonitapura; in return for his penances Shiva had granted him 1000 arms, with which he played the mṛdaṅga when Shiva danced the tāṇḍava; Shiva had revealed to him that he would be defeated by Kṛṣṇa; he became cruel and sequestered his daughter Uṣā₁ so as not to marry her; She, having seen Aniruddha in a dream, magically summoned him to her castle, where Bāṇa₁ held him prisoner; Kṛṣṇa and Pradyumna raised an army and killed him | myth. [Rām.] np. of King Bāṇa₁, son of Vikukṣi, father of Anaranya₁ | lit. np. of Bāṇa₁ Bhaṭṭa, son of Citrabhānu₁, born in Prītikūṭa; he was an important poet of mannered style at the court of King Harşa (7th century) in Kanyākubjā; He is the author of the marvelous novel Kādambarī, the royal panegyric Harşacarita, and the devotional poem Candīśataka; a play Sāradacandrikā is also attributed to him; his son Bhūṣaṇa Bhaṭṭa completed the unfinished Kādambarī, respecting its plan and style | hist. cf. Vāmana₄ Bhatta. bāno balisute śare [Amarakoṣa] (the word) Bāṇa₁ is used in the sense of son of Bali or in the sense of arrow.

bāṇagaṅgā [gaṅgā] f. geo. np. of the Bāṇagaṅgā reservoir on Malabar Hill in Mumbai; [Rām.] Rāma is said to have gone there to receive Gautama's blessing; to quench his thirst, he shot an arrow into the ground, which caused the Bho gavatī to spring forth.
bāṇaliṅga [liṅga] n. soc. quartz egg or ovoid pebble from Narmadā used as a linga in the worship of Siva; syn. narmadeśvara.
bāṇin |in| amnf bāṇinī who carries one or more arrows.
bāṇijá [vāṇija] m. merchant.
bādara [*badara] amnf bādarī concerning the jujube tree — n. jujube — m. (plant of) cotton — f. bādarā id.

bādarāyana [*badaraāyana| m. patr. of various authors | hist. np. of Bādarāyaṇa, author of the Brah masūtraVedāntasūtra; he is said to have lived between 200 and 400; called composer of the Veda [Vedavyāsa], he is sometimes identified with Vyāsa.
bādāma var. vātāma m. almond.

√ bādh v. [1] pr. r. (bādhate) aor. r. [5] (bādhiṣṭa) pp. (bādhiṭa) pfp. (bādhya) pf. (pra, prati, sam) oppress, attack; harass, torment, cause suffering | repress, repel, prevent; infringe | suffer from (acc.) — ca. (bādhayati) op prime, torment — des. r. (bībhatsate) hate; despise; loathe, avoid (abl.) — des. r. (bībādhisate) want to suppress. balavatī śirovedanā mām bādhate I am suffering from a severe headache. tvām bhojanalobho bādhate you are tormented by gluttony. na tathā bādhate śītam yathā bādhati bādhate It is not so much the cold that bothers me as (the faulty word) bādhati (response of a palanquin bearer to a paṇḍita going to a poetry competition of King Bhoja₁ and who asked him "api śītam bādhati" (the cold does not bother you?)).
bādhá [agt. bādh] m. oppressor, tormentor pain, suffering; sorrow; damage, detriment; contradiction — ifc. violation of, exclusion from (iic.) — f. bādhā annulment.

bādhaka |agt. bādh| amnf bādhikā that which prevents, oppresses, causes suffering | that which cancels, suspends, excludes — m. phil. |Nyāya| object; contradiction, paradox. bādhakapramāvirahaḥ gram. [yogyatā] absence of impediment to understanding.

bādhana [agt. bādh] amnf bādhanā that oppresses; that prevents; that refutes — act. n. opposition, resistance oppression; suppression, annulment | gram. hindrance of a rule | phil. fact of being falsified by a superior reason — f. bādhanā discomfort, trouble, pain.
bādhita [pp. bādh] amnf bādhitā hindered; oppressed | gram. annulled, obstructed | phil. [Nyāya] contradictory, absurd, false, incompatible.
bādhitatva |tva| n. the state of being prevented, hindered or excluded.
bādhitavya [pfp. [3] bādh] amnf bādhitavyā which must be oppressed; to exclude, to nullify.
bādhitr [agt. bādh] m. oppressor.
bādhitvā [abs. bādh] ind. having oppressed | gram. by neutralizing the effect of a previous rule.
bādhya [pfp. [1] bādh] amnf bādhyā to oppress, to suppress, to exclude.
bādhyabādhakabhāva [bādhakabhāva] m. gram. blocking relationship.

bāndhava [*bandhua] m. relative (not. on the maternal side); companion, friend — f. bāndhavī relative, close (not. on the maternal side) — f. bāndhavā ifc. friend of. sabāndhavās his/her own, his/her kind.
bāndhavaka [ka] amnf bāndhavikā cognate.
bāndhavajana [jana] m. relatives, kin (collective).
bāndhavatā [tā] f. relationship.
bāndhavya [ya] n. kinship, blood tie.
Bābhravya m. hist. np. from the ancient grammarian Bābhravya, who fixed the kra mapātha recitation method.

bārhaspatya [*Bṛhaspati₁ya] m. myth. "From Bṛhaspati₁", patron saint of Bharadvāja | soc. materialist sect |nāstika|; the bārhaspatyās followed the teaching of Brhaspati₁ — n. lit. np. of the bārhaspatya, treatise on ethics attributed to Bharadvāja.
bārhaspatyasūtra [sūtra] n. lit. np. of the bārhaspatyasūtra, foundational text of the materialists [cārvākās], attributed to Bṛhaspati₁, known only through quotations.

bāla [*bala] amnf bālā young [“who is vigorous”] | childish, candid; simpleton, fool; opp. pandita — m. child, young boy; syn. kumāra, śiśu | soc. minor; opp. vyavahārajña | beginner; opp. praudha — f. bālā little girl, young girl.
Bālakāṇḍa [kāṇḍa] m. bed. n.p. of the Bālakāṇḍa “book of youth (of Rāma)”, first book of Rām.
bālakunda [kunda] m. fresh jasmine. alakam bālakundānuviddham [MD.] whose curls are mingled with fresh jasmine.

Bālakṛṣṇa [kṛṣṇa] m. myth. np. of Bālakṛṣṇa "kṛṣṇa child"; his prodigies are reported in the Bhāgavatapurāna; he is worshipped notably at the temple of Kṛṣṇasvāmī at Vijayanagara, whose image was brought from Udayagiri by Kṛṣṇadeva Rāya in 1513.
bālakrīdana [krīdana] n. child's game.
bālakrīḍanaka [ka] n. children's game | pl. bālakrīdanakāni children's games, one of the 64 arts [kalā] — m. toy; ball.

bālakrīdā [krīdā] f. children's game | hist. np. of the Bālakrīdā, commentary on the Yājñavalkyasmṛti by Viśvarūpa₃ (9th century); the Vacanamālā is a gloss on it. bālagaņa |gaṇa| m. mod. children's class.
Bālagopāla |gopāla| m. myth. np. of Bālagopāla epith. of kṛṣṇa child to Gokula.
bālagopālastuti [stuti] f. lit. np. of the bālagopālastuti, devotional hymn [bhakti] to kṛṣṇa due to Bilvamaṅgala/Līlāśuka.
bālagraha [graha] m. myth. demon seizing children.
bālaghna [ghna] m. myth. child murderer.
bālacandra | candra | m. astr. young Moon — n. arch. niche in a wall.
bālacandrikā [candrikā] f. bed. [DKC.] np. of bālacandrikā "Light of young Moon", friend of Princess Avantisundarī₁; she married Puspodbhava.
Bālacarita | carita | n. lit. np. of the Bālacarita, nāṭaka of Bhāsa based on the story of Kṛṣṇa as a child.
bālatantra [tantra] n. lit. np. from the treatise on pediatrics bālatantra by Kalyāṇa₂ (16th century).
bālatā [tā] f. childhood.
bālatva [tva] n. childhood | inexperience, childishness; foolishness.
Bālamanoramā [manoramā] f. lit. np. of the Bālamanoramā, grammar "pleasant to young people", commentary on the Siddhāntakaumudī due to Vāsudeva₄ Dīkṣita.

Bālarāmāyaṇa [Rāmāyaṇa] n. lit. np. of the Bālarāmāyaṇa "Little Rāmāyaṇa", a drama by Rājaśekhara very loosely adapted from the Rāmāyana, and whose main character is Rāvaṇa; it is characterized by its irreverent tone and the presentation of events through indirect descriptions.
bālarūpin | rūpin | amnf bālarūpinī childlike; said not. of Kṛṣṇa child |Bālakṛṣṇa| or of VișnuUpendra, youngest of Aditi.

bālendu [indu] m. first crescent moon | myth. attribute of Shiva, who wears the crescent moon in his hair. ৰালক bālaka |bālaka| amnf bālikā young, juvenile, childlike — m. Small child, young boy; Young animal — f. bālikā girl.
Bālambhaṭṭa m. hist. n.p. of Bālambhaṭṭa, grammarian from South India (18th century); we not. the Kalā commentary on him owes the Vaiyākaranasiddhāntamañjūṣā.
bālāki m. ved. [Kausītaki] patr. of the scholar Gārgya₁ bālāki; he went to King Ajātaśatru to teach him Brahman, but the king knew more than he did.
bālin cf. vālin.
bālivadha [vadha] n. lit. episode of the Rām. where Rāma treacherously kills the king of the monkeys Bālī/Vālī.
bāliman [bālaiman] m. youth; immaturity, childishness.
bāliśa [bāla] amnf bāliśā childish; simple, naive, puerile — m. fool, imbecile; simpleton.
bāliśatā [tā] f. puerility.
bāliśatva [tva] n. id.
bāliśya [ya] n. puerility.

bālya [bālaya] n. childhood | inexperience, childishness; foolishness. ৰাষ্কল Bāṣkala m. hist. np. of the master Bāṣkala, compiler of the Rigveda; the other recension | śākhā | is due to Sākalya | myth. np. of the asura Bāṣkala₁, son of Samhrāda.
bāṣpa var. vāṣpa m. steam | tears, weeping — v. [11] pr. r. (bāṣpāyate) to weep. bāṣpībhū to emit steam. bāṣpāyate sthālī the pot emits steam.
Bāhādura m. soc. np. of Bāhādura “Hero”, honorific title conferred by Muslim kings.
bāhú m. arm; forearm | myth. n.p. of King Bāhu; cf. Bāhuka | math. side of a figure | of. Bāhū astr. n.p. from Bāhū "the two arms", epith. of nakṣatra Ardrā (Betelgeuse) || gr. πηξυς.
bāhudantin [dantin] m. myth. epith. of Indra "with large teeth".
bāhudantiputra [putra] m. myth. epith. of Jaya datta, son of Indra.
bāhuphala [phala] n. astr. inclination of the Sun; opp. kotiphala.
bāhubala [bala] m. bed. [KSS.] np. of bāhubala "with powerful arms", king of Kāñcī; Prāṇadhara plundered his treasure with a mechanical goose; its gatekeeper was the greedy Arthalobha.
bāhubalin | balin | m. jn. np. of Bāhubalī, epith. of Gommața "with powerful arms".
bāhúmūla [mūla] n. armpit.
bāhúyuddha [yuddha] n. pugilism; unarmed combat.
bāhúyodha [yodha| m. wrestler; boxer.
bāhúyodhin [yodhin] m. wrestler; boxer.
bāhulatā [latā] f. [rūpaka] graceful arm | "like a vine" |.
bāhuśālin [śālin] amnf bāhuśālinī who has big arms.
bāhusahasra |sahasra| n. a thousand arms.
bāhusahasrabhrt [bhrt] m. myth. epith. of king Kārtavīrya “with a thousand arms”. kārtavīryārjunah nāma rājā bāhusahasrabhrt King Arjuna₁ Kārtavīrya has a thousand arms.
bāhusahasravat [vat] m. myth. epith. of the king Kārtavīrya "of the thousand arms".

Bāhuka [Bāhuka] m. ifc. arm of; servant of — amnf bāhukā servile; servant | with deformed arms — m. myth. np. of King Bāhuka or Bāhu "Reduced to servitude", of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa], son of Bharuka; driven from his kingdom by the Haihayās, he took refuge in the forest with his wives; one of them was pregnant, and a rival gave him poison, which delayed by 7 years the birth of his son Sagara, who was born "with the poison" after the death of Bāhu | myth. |Mah. | "Es tropié", borrowed name of Nala under the deformed appearance given to him by a snake to disguise himself; he presented himself to King Rtuparna as an expert in chariots and cooking, to become his charioteer and cook. ৰা <u>র্</u> bāhula₁ [Bāhula] n. arm armor.
bāhula₂ [*bahula] amnf bāhulā multiple — n. multiplicity.
bāhuleya [*bahulaīya] m. n.p. of bull.
bāhulya [bahulaya] n. abundance; multitude; variety | the usual course of things, the ordinary. bāhulyena usually, ordinarily; as a general rule. bāhulyāt id. | in all likelihood.

bāhya [*bahisya] amnf bāhyā external, situated outside (abl. loc.); opp. ābhyantara external, foreign to, contrary to excluded, excom muni; pariah, outcast | in conflict with, opposed to, having nothing to do with (abl. iic.) — m. foreign. bāhye var. bāhyena adv. outside, outside. bāhyāt adv. from outside. bāhyatas adv. outside, outside; externally; out of (g. abl.). bāhyaṃ kṛ to put out, exclude, expel.
bāhyatara [tara] amnf bāhyatarā compar. ex clu, external | excommunicated, outcaste. vedabāhyatara soc. excluded from Brahmanical orthodoxy.
bāhyatā [tā] f. state of being outside; exclusion deviation or divergence from (abl.).
bāhyatva [tva] n. id.
bāhyanāman [nāman] n. address of the recipient (of a letter). adattabāhyanāmā lekhaḥ a letter without a recipient's address. dattalikhitamadbāhyanāma patram presaya see the letter addressed to me.
bāhyaprayatna [prayatna] m. phone. extraoral vocal process; opp. ābhyantaraprayatna.
bāhyalingin [lingin] amnf bāhyalinginī heretic.
bāhyārtha [artha] m. external sense [phil. the external world, reality.
bāhyārthavāda | vāda | m. phil. doctrine according to which the external world is real.
bāhyārthavādin [in] amnf bāhyārthavādinī phil. realist; syn. sarvāstitvavādin.
bāhyārthasiddhikārikā [siddhikārikā] f. pl. phil. np. from the Bāhyārthasiddhikārikās "Stanzas demonstrating the existence of external objects" by Subhagupta.
bāhli m. geo. country of Bactria, mod. Afghan province of Balkh; it is the place of arrival from the North of the Aryan populations — f. bāhlī id.

bāhlika [ka] amnf bāhlikī geo. Balkhi, ha bitant or prince of Bactria | var. Bāhlīka id. | myth. [Mah.] np. of the Kaurava prince Bāhlīka, son of Pratīpa; he left his brother Sāmtanu to reign; So madatta is his son | pl. geo. np. of the country or people of the Bāhlikās or Bāhlīkās, inhabitants of Bactria; their horses are renowned.
bāhlija [ja] amnf bāhlijā born in Bactria | from Bactria; not. breed of renowned horses.
bāhvṛcya [*bahvṛcaya] n. lit. Vedic corpus.
biḍāla var. viḍāla m. cat — f. biḍālā f. bidālī female cat.
Biḍaujas var. biḍojas [viś₂ojas] m. myth. np. of bidaujas, epith. of Indra "with penetrating strength".

bindú var. vindu₁ mn drop | point, mark, spot; sign on the face, fly | pearl | math. symb. zero; point | gram. sign of the anusvāra | phil. symbol of the Absolute | lit. (theatre) reprise; cf. arthaprakrti. jalasyam binduh drop of water.
binducyuti | cyuti | f. the act of shedding a tear | lit. the act of omitting a nasalization, a śabdālaṃkāra.

bindumat [mat] amnf Bindumatī₁ that makes bubbles; granular; speckled — f. Bindumatī₁ myth. np. of Bindumatī₁, daughter of King Śaśabindu, wife of Māndhātā | lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī Bin dumatī₁, cursed for having cut with her teeth the leather cords of her vīṇā to be reborn as the daughter of the fisherman Satyavrata₃; she married Saktideva after making him promise to bring her the embryo of his future wife bindurekhā.

bindurekhā [rekhā] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the princess bindurekhā, daughter of King Candavikrama; she was abducted by a daitya at Kanakapurī; the latter took the form of an enormous boar which Saktideva killed, before marrying her; she became pregnant, and Bin dumatī₁ reminded Saktideva of his promise to pull his embryo from her womb, which became a magic sword while Saktideva was transformed into a vidyādhara, and the curse of Bindumatī₁ came to an end.
bindusaras |saras| n. geo. np. of Lake Bindusara; cf. bindusarovara, Bindusāgara.
bindusarovara [sarovara] n. geo. n.p. from Lake Bindu sarovara; cf. Bindusāgara, Bindusara.
Bindusāgara [sāgara] m. geo. np. of the Bindusāgara or Bindusara or bindusarovara, great sacred pool of Bhuvaneśvarī₁; it is said to contain a drop of all the sacred waters of India.

bindusāra |sāra| m. hist. np. of bindusāra, son and successor of Candragupta Maurya in 297 ant.; it is said that he had 16 wives and 101 sons, including Ashoka who was designated by an oracle as his successor in 273 ant.; cf. amitrakhāda, amitraghāta, vijigīsu.

bindusthāna [sthāna] n. phil. [Tantra] "Abode of the Absolute", the highest point of a sādhaka's subtle body, located 2 inches above the skull; it is there that the añjali of divine invocation is performed, by pronouncing the bījamantra 'hūm'. ৰিন্ত্ৰীক bibboka var. vivvoka n. [nāṭya] feigned indifference, one of the 10 means of seducing [hāva] a woman.
bibhits [des. bhid₁] v. pr. (bibhitsati) v. pr. r. (bibhitsate) pp. (bibhitsita) to want to break; to want to scatter; to want to conquer.
bibhitsā [act. des. bhid₁] f. rage to destroy.
bibhitsu [agt. dés. bhid₁] amnf who wants to destroy acc. .
bibhīṣaṇa var. vibhīṣaṇa m. myth. [Rām.] np. of rākṣasa bibhīṣaṇa; cf. vibhīṣaṇa.
bimba mn disc; not. solar or lunar disc; round shape | mirror; reflection, image — f. cf. bimbā. bimbībhū to reflect.
bimbaka [ka] n. solar disk — f. bimbikā bio. fruit of the bimbā; syn. bimba.
bimbabimbībhāva [bimbībhāva] m. phil. [Vedānta] link between the mirror and the image (used to qualify the relationship between citti and jīvātman).
bimbā [f. bimba] f. bio. bot. Coccinia grandis, a type of climbing bryony with bright red fruits — f. bimbī id. — n. bimba bio. its fruit; in poetry, women's lips are compared to its color.
bimbādhara [dhara] m. lit. woman's lip (red like the fruit of the bimbā).
bimbosthī [osthī] f. woman with bimbā lips.

bimbisāra [bimbīsāra] m. hist. np. of the king of Magadha bimbisāra, of the Haryanka dynasty; a jaina follower, he was a contemporary and patron of the Bud dha; his first wife Kosaladevī brought him Kāśī as a dowry; he reigned in Rājagrha from 543 to 491 ante; he was dethroned by his son Ajātaśatru₂, who had him starved to death in prison; cf. Srenya.
bimbī iiv. bimba.

bimbībhāva [bhāva] m. (that which is reflected) image in a mirror. ৰিল bíla n. hole, orifice, cavity, opening; hollow burrow (of a bowl, of a ladle) | var. vila id. — f. bilā ifc. id. śatamukhabilam burrow with 100 exits.
biladvāra | dvāra | n. access to a burrow.
bilamukha [mukha] n. entrance to a burrow.
bilavāsa |vāsa₁| amnf bilavāsā (animal) that lives in a burrow — m. bio. burrowing animal: porcupine, rat, lizard, etc.
bilavāsin | vasin₁ | amnf bilavāsinī id.
bilaśaya [śaya] amnf bilavayā id.
bile [loc. bila] iic.
bileśaya [śaya] amnf bilevayā cf. bilavāsa.

bilva m. bio. bot. Ægle marmelos, tree of Bæl or Bengal quince; sacred tree whose trilobed leaves [tryambaka] serve as an offering to Shiva; its flower is one of the arrows of Kāma [puṣpabāṇa], for it "redoubles the ardor of the blood" — n. bio. its fruit, a large yellowish berry; Bengali love poetry compares it to a woman's breast; it contains a whitish pulp which is pressed to extract a delicious juice with medicinal virtues; it is one of the 5 major medicinal roots [bṛhatpañcamūla]; syn. rau cya, śrīphala || hi. bela.

Bilvamangala [mangala] m. hist. np. of the mystic Bilvamangala (13th century, Kerala); from a śaiva family, he became a devotee of Kṛṣṇa, and called himself Līlāśuka; we owe him the Kṛṣṇakarṇāmṛta and the Bālagopālastuti.

Bilhaṇa m. hist. np. of Bilhaṇa, famous poet of Kaśmīra (~1050–1100); he travelled extensively, before settling at the court of Kalyāna₁, where he composed the Vikramānkadevacarita in honor of King Cālukya Vikramāditya₆ who conferred upon him the title of vidyāpati; then he fell out of favor, and had to flee; we owe to him not. the series of erotic poems Caurapañcāśikā.
bilhanapañcāśikā [pañcāśikā] f. cf. cau rapañcāśikā.
bilhaṇaśataka [śataka] n. bed. n.p. from Bilhana's century of erotic poems Bilhanasataka; it includes the two recensions of the cau rapañcāśikā.
bísa n. lotus rhizome; it is edible. bisakisalayacchedapātheyavat | kisalayacheda pātheya n. provisions of lotus shoots for the journey.
bisakisalayacchedapātheyavat |vat| amnf
bisakisalayacchedapātheyavatī [MD.] provided with supplies of lotus shoots for the journey.
bisinī [bisain] f. lotus.
Bihāra [pkt. vihāra] m. geo. np. of Bihāra, in the Ganges Valley, country of origin of the bd.; mod. Bihār.
bīja var. vīja n. seed, germ; seed, sperm | first cause, origin, source | (theatre) origin of the plot.
bijaka |ka| mr. organic. bot. Citrus medica, lemon tree; lemon | organic. bot. Pterocarpus marsupium, kino tree; syn. asana.
bījaganita [ganita] n. math. np. from the Bījaganita, a work on algebra by Srīdharācārya, now lost; in it he gives the rule for solving quadratic equations, cited by Bhāskarācārya₂ (1150).
bījapūra [pūra] m. lemon | "full of glitches"].
bījapūraka [ka] m. id.
bījamantra [mantra] n. phil. germinal syllable, primordial paricle of the Word; cf. hrīm, krīm, śrīm, aim, hūm, sauh.
bījākṣara |akṣara| n. phil. first syllable of a mantra.

bījānkura |ankura| m. of. the seed and the bud. bījānkuranyāya maxim of the seed and the bud, paradox of the reciprocal effect and cause, like the egg and the chicken; its effect is to deny the existence of a beginning of the world.
bībhats [des. bādh] des. r. (bībhatsate) to hate, abhor, execrate; despise; loathe, avoid (abl.).

bībhatsa [agt. bībhats] amnf bībhatsā hideous, disgusting, repugnant, odious; cruel, wicked — m. aversion, disgust | hideous aspect; object That inspires aversion | lit. disgust, one of the 9 artistic modes [rasa]; it corresponds to the feelings inspired by the odious, the sinister and the macabre; it is associated with the color blue and the deity Mahākāla — f. bībhatsā aversion, disgust — n. bībhatsa repugnant thing; hideous spectacle. hanta bībhatsamevāgrato vartate oh! there a truly horrible scene is taking place.

Bībhatsu [agt. des. bādh] amnf Who hates; repugnant, disgusted; horrified — m. myth. |Mah.| np. of Bībhatsu epith. of Arjuna "Who is repugnant (to the task he must accomplish, that is, to fight his ancestor Bhīṣma, and later to kill his elder brother Karna)”.

bīrobā [pkt. vīra] m. myth. np. of bīrobā or Bīrappa, pastoral deity of the Dhangar community of Mahārāṣṭra; he is said to be an avatar of Vīrabhadra; he is the Primordial Shepherd, hero of the community. ৰুক্স Bukka mf bukkā heart — m. goat | hist. np. of King Bukka₁ or Bukkarāya, son of Sangama, founder of the Vijayana gara dynasty (14th century) with his elder brother Harihara₁, whom he succeeded as emperor upon his death in 1356; Mādhavācārya, elder brother of Sāyaṇa, was his minister; upon his death in 1377, Harihara₂ Rāya succeeded him | hist. np. of Bukka₂ Rāya, son of Harihara₂, emperor of Vijayanagara (1405–1406) | fr. bouc.
buḍbuḍa [onomatopoeia] ind. imitates the sound of an object sinking into water.

buddhá [pp. budh₁] amnf buddhā awakened, enlightened, learned, wise — m. bd. person who has realized the liberating Awakening | bd. epith. of the buddha Sākyamuni "the Awakened One"; born prince Siddhārtha Gau tama in Kapilavastu of king śākya Šuddhodana and queen Māyā₁ (around 485 ante); at the age of 16 he married princess Yaśodharā with whom he had a son, Rāhula; at the age of 29 he left his palace to practice asceticism as a wandering monk for 6 years; he received Awakening [bodhi] in Gayā; He gave his first sermon proclaiming the Four Noble Truths [āryasatya] in the gazelle park [mṛgadāva] of Sāranātha, and founded the sangha community; he entered parinirvāṇa at the age of 80; he is considered by some devotees of Viṣṇava as his 9th avatāra (because he prepares the end of the kaliyuga by spreading an erroneous doctrine); cf. Ananda, Devadatta, Māra — n. knowledge.

buddhakṣetra [kṣetra] n. bd. universe of a buddha. buddhaghoşa [ghoşa] m. hist. n.p. by Buddhaghoşa "Who proclaims the Buddha", comic book author. from the 5th century; he finalized the Jātakamālā; he is the author of the Pa dyacūdāmaņi, the Viśuddhimārga and the Sumangalavilāsinī commentary on the Dīgha nikāya.
buddhacarita [carita] n. lit. np. of the buddhacarita "Acts of the Buddha", composed by Aśvaghosa; it is one of the earliest bd. works composed in sans krit.
buddhajayantī [jayantī] f. soc. birthday festival of the buddha, at the full moon of the month of Viśākhe [vaiśākhī]; it is the occasion of the Vaiśākha festival.
buddhajñāna [jñāna] n. bd. knowledge of Bud dha.
buddhadharma [dharma] mn phil. Buddhism.
buddhadhātu [dhātu] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] nature of buddha, inherent in every being; this absolute notion treats and refines the doctrine of the tathāgatagarbha; cf. Mahāparinirvānasūtra.
Buddhapādamangala | pādamangala | n. bd. np. of the Buddhapādamaṅgala, a work (in pāli) listing the 108 signs of good fortune on the soles of the feet of the Bud dha.
buddhapūrnimā [pūrnimā] f. bd. full moon of the month of Viśākhe [vaiśākhī]; the birth of the buddha [buddhajayantī] is celebrated during the Vaiśākha festival (May).
buddhabhaṭṭa | bhaṭṭa | m. hist. np. of the ācārya bd. buddhabhatta, author of the Ratnaparīksā; he is earlier than the 6th century.
buddhavacana | vacana | n. bd. teachings of the buddha.
buddhaśrījñāna [buddhaśrījñāna] m. hist. np. of buddhaśrījñāna, master of the bd. Vajrayāna; he is the author of a commentary on the Abhisamayālaṃkāra.

Buddhi [act. budh₁] f. mind, intelligence, reflection; faculty of perception; understanding; wisdom; reason | thought; idea; resolution | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the essence [tattva] of the Intellect, first constituent of the inner instrument [antaḥkaraṇa]; it is the discriminating faculty; syn. mahat, mahātattva; 8 states of mind are distinguished; 4 are of a sāttvika character: dharma, jñāna, vairāgya, and aiśvarya, and 4 are of a tāmasika character, their opposites adharma, ajñāna, avairāgya, and anaiśvarya | knowledge; wisdom, science; syn.

jñāna | bd. Awakening | myth. np. of Buddhi, the personified Wisdom, daughter of Prajāpati; [SP.] she is said to be the wife of Ganesha, by whom she bore Lābha myth. np. of Buddhi₁, daughter of Daksha, wife of dharma | pl. buddhayas phil. | Vaiśeṣika | the property [guṇa] of perceptions. buddhitas by reflection. buddhyā adv. mentally. buddhim kr to determine oneself to. tasmādgardabhād vyāghradhiyābuddhyā paśavah palāyante the animals flee from the donkey, mistaking it for a tiger. buddhiryasya balam tasya knowledge is strength.
buddhiprakāśa | prakāśa | m. lit. np. from the Buddhi prakāśa, treatise on chess by Nīlakantha.
buddhibala [bala] n. chess; syn. caturanga.
buddhimat |mat| amnf buddhimatī intelligent; wise, prudent.
buddhiviparyaya | viparyaya | mr. contrary opinion.
buddhivilāsinī [vilāsinī] f. lit. np. of the Buddhi vilāsinī "Beauty of knowledge", commentary on the Līlāvatī due to Gaņeśa₁ (1545).

buddhistha |stha| amnf buddhisthā present in mind; memorized | gram. (meaning) in accordance with the speaker's intention — n. understanding; knowledge. śabdo 'pi buddhisthaḥ śrutīnāṃ pṛthak gram. [Bhartrhari] Language is only the memorization of speech.
buddhisthārtha [artha] m. gram. meaning evoked by a word or phrase.

buddhīndriya [indriya] m. phil. [Sāmkhya] one of the 5 senses or organs of perception [tanmātra]: śrotra hearing, tvak touch, cakșus or akși sight, jihvā taste and ghrāṇa smell; each is governed by the corresponding regent [niyantr]; syn. jñānendriya.

buddhyapekṣā [apekṣā] amnf buddhyapekṣā phil. which is a prerequisite of cognition. sāmānyam viśeṣa iti buddhyapekṣam [Vaiśeṣikasūtra] The universal inherent in the particular is a prerequisite of cognition.
buddhvā [abs. budh₁] ind. having awakened.
budbudá [onomatopoeia] m. bubble; water bubble, ampoule (symbol of ephemeral things) — f. Bud budā myth. np. of the apsaras Budbudā, companion of Vargā. budbudam adv. boiling.

√ budh₁ v. [1] pr. (bodhati) v. [4] pr. r. (Bud hyate) pft. (bubodha) aor. r. [4] (abuddha) pp. (buddhá) inf. (boddhum) abs. (buddhvā, budhya) pf. (anu, ava, ut, ni, pra, prati, vi, sam) to awaken, rouse, watch | to learn, discover, perceive, notice; to know, understand | to observe, think, reflect on — ca. (bodháyati) pfp. (bodhayita vya) abs. (bodhayitvā) to attract attention; to awaken; to rouse, revive, excite | to make understood, remind, reveal; to advise, inform, counsel; to instruct — ca. (bodháyati) pp. (bodhita) to make known — intens. (bobhudhīti) to reflect intensely — des. (bubhut sati) des. r. (bubhutsate) to want to understand — des. (bubhodhisati) des. r. (bubhodisate) id. | ang. to bid; all. bieten. bodhayati padmam he awakens the lotus.

budh₂ |agt. budh₁| ifc. amnf One who awakens, who understands (iic.); versed in (iic.) | intelligent, enlightened, wise in (iic.). ਕੁਖ Budha |agt. budh₁| amnf budhā scholar, Sage — m. a scholar | myth. np. of Budha "(Mercury) the Sage", illegitimate son of Soma and Tārā, husband of Iḍā by whom he fathered King Purūravā, founder of the lunar lineage | somavamśa | ; he is the influence | graha | of the planet Mercury, of which he is regent; the Rājaputrīya is attributed to him; cf. Jña.
budhavāra | vāra | m. Wednesday, the day of Mercury; syn. jñavāra.

budhasvāmin |svāmin| m. hist. np. of Bud hasvāmī, an author from 8th-century Nepal; he is credited with the Bṛhatkathāślokasaṃgraha, the Nepali version of the Brhatkathā. ৰুণ্ণ budhna [budh₁na] m. ground, soil, depth.
budhnya |ya| amnf budhnyā Who lives in the depths.
bubhukṣ [des. bhuj₂] v. pr. (bubhukṣati) pp. (bubhukṣita) to desire to eat or possess.
bubhukṣā [act. of the. bhuj₂] f. hunger; gluttonous nerie. bubhukṣām jayate yas tu sa svargam jayate dhru
vam [Mah.] He who controls his appetite gains Heaven without a doubt.
bubhukṣājaya [jaya] m. control of one's hunger.
bubhukṣita [pp. bubhukṣ] amnf bubhuksitā hungry.
bubhukṣu |agt. des. bhuj₂| amnf hungry phil. One who desires to enjoy the world; opp. mumukșu.
bubhuts [des. budh₁] v. pr. (bubhut sati) pp. (bubhutsita) to desire to understand; to desire to know; to want to know.
bubhutsā |act. des. budh₁| f. desire to understand; curiosity.
bubhutsu [agt. des. budh₁] amnf Who desires to understand or know; Who wants to know Who wants, Who wants to persuade themselves of (acc.) | myth. "eager to know everything", said of the gods.
bubhūṣā [act. des. bhū₁] f. desire to become.
bubhūṣu [agt. des. bhū₁] amnf Who wants to become (nom.) | Who wants to prevail | Who wishes good for g. .
bṛṃhaṇa [agt. ca. bṛh₂] amnf bṛṃhaṇā That which increases, That which nourishes, That which strengthens — act. n. ren strengthening, increase | med. [Ayurveda] surali mentation; opp. langhana.
bṛṃhita [pp. bṛh₂] amnf bṛṃhitā increased, augmented; fortified — n. bio. grunt of elephants — f. bṛṃhitā myth. [Mah.] np. of Bṛṃhitā, one of Skanda's wet nurses [mātr].
bṛṣī var. bṛṣī, vṛṣī f. grass cushion, not. seat of a budding ascetic dūrvā.
brsī var. vrsī f. cf. brsī. bṛsīkā id.

√ brh₁ [related to vrdh₁] v. [1] pr. (brmhati) pr. r. (bṛṃhate) pp. (bṛṃhita, bṛḍha) v. [6] pr. (brhati) ppr. (brhat) pf. (upa, pari) to increase, enlarge; to grow, to grow; to become strong; to expand — ca. (bṛṃhayati) var. vṛṃhayati to increase, to enlarge; to make grow, to enlarge; to strengthen.
√ brh₂ var. vrh v. [6] pr. (brh ati) pp. (brdha) pf. (ni) to tear, to rip.
brh₃ [act. brh₁] ifc. f. increase in force; power.
bṛh₂ác iic. bṛhat.

bṛhacchabdakusumākara [śabdakusumaākara] m. lit. np. from the Brhacchabdakusumākara "Great mine of linguistic flowers", by Harekāntamiśra (1999); it gives the inflected forms of nouns; its chapter lokoktikośa is a collection of sayings.
Brhacchabdaratna [śabdaratna] n. bed. n.p. of the Brhacchabdaratna, commentary on the Praudhamanoramā due to Hari₁ Dīkṣita.
brhacchabdenduśekhara [śabdenduśekhara] m. gram. n.p. of Brhaccabdenduśekhara; cf. Sabdenduśekhara.
bṛh₂áj iic. bṛhat.
Brhajjātaka | jātaka | n. bed. n.p. from Brhajjātaka, a treatise on predictive astrology by Varāhamihira (6th century); cf. Niryāṇādhyāya.
bṛhajjyotiṣārṇava [jyotiṣaarṇava] m. lit. np. from bṛhajjyotiṣārṇava "great ocean of astronomy", work of Harikṛṣṇa Vyaṅkaṭarāma Sarmā (late 19th century).
bṛhaṭ iic. bṛhat.
bṛhaṭṭīkā [ṭīkā] f. lit. np. of the bṛhaṭṭīkā "great commentary", work of mīmāmsā of Kumārila.

bṛh₂át var. vṛdhát [ppr. bṛh₂] amnf brhatī great, high; vast, abundant; compact, so lide; strong, powerful; principal — n. ved. hymn of praise [sāman] composed in meter bṛhatī — f. cf. bṛhatī || fr. brigand, bourg, Brigitte, Burgundy; all. burgh. brhatī dik zenith.
brhatikā [ikā] f. cloak.

Bṛhatkathā [kathā₁] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the Bṛhatkathā "Great Compilation of Fables", a vast collection of tales in paiśācī attributed to Guṇāḍhya, and undoubtedly fictitious; it notably recounts the adventures of King Udayana and his son Naravāhanadatta, who became emperor of the magicians [vidyādharās]; the Kathāsaritsāgara is the Sanskrit version by Somadeva; the versified Brhatkathāmañjarī is by Kṣemendra; the Vasudevahiṇḍi is the Jain version; the Brhatkathāślokasamgraha, attributed to Budhasvāmī, is a Nepali version. brhatkathākośa kośa m. jn. du np. Brhatkathākośa, collection of edifying stories on the approach of death and the modes of suicide in the jn. ārādhanā tradition; it is due to Harisena (931).
bṛhatkathāślokasaṃgraha [ślokasaṃgraha] m. lit. np. of the Brhatkathāślokasamgraha, Nepali version of the Brhatkathā due to Budhasvāmī (8th-9th century).
brhatkāya | kāya | m. myth. np. of Brhatkāya | "with a powerful body", descendant of Hastī, father of Jayadratha₁.
brhatksatra | kṣatra | mr. myth. n.p. of king Paurava Brhatkṣatra, son of Bharata, father of Hastī.

Bṛhattrayī [trayī] f. bed. n.p. of the Bṛhattrayī, "The three great lyric poems [mahākāvya]": the Kirātārjunīya of Bhāravi, the Siśupālavadha of Māgha, and the Naisadhacarita of Srīharṣa | med. n.p. of the Bṛhattrayī₁, “Great Triad” of the masters of Ayurveda: Caraka, Suśruta, and Vāgbhaṭa; cf. Mādhavanidāna.
bṛhatpañcamūla [pañcamūla] n. med. The 5 major medicinal roots: bilva, śyonāka, gambhārī, pāṭalā and gaṇikārikā.
brhatputra | putra | m. myth. np. of Brhatputra, son of Suhotra, king of Paurava; [AP.] he had three sons: Ajamīḍha, who succeeded him, Dvimīḍha and Pu rumīdha.

bṛhatsaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. np. of the Bṛhatsaṃhitā "great compendium", a 6th century astronomical work by Varāhamihira; the Agastimata, which forms a section of it, deals with the science of gems.
brhatsamhitāvivṛti [vivṛti] f. bed. n.p. of the Brhatsamhitāvivrti, gloss of the Brhatsamhitā by Bhattotpala (10th century).
bṛhatsāman |sāman| n. soc. set of hymns from the Sāmaveda praising Indra; they are sung at the end of the Atirātra.

bṛhatī [f. bṛhat] f. phon. Vedic meter of 36 syllables (4 lines of 9 syllables) | math. symb. the number 36 | lit. np. of the bṛhatī "Great (gloss)", commentary by Prabhākara on the Mīmāmsāsūtra of Jaimini (6th-7th century) | bio. bot. Solanum indicum, Indian bittersweet; it is one of the 5 minor medicinal roots | hrasvapañcamūla | myth. np. of the horse bṛhatī₁, harnessed to the chariot of Sūrya.
bṛhatīdvaya | dvaya | n. med. the pair of medicinal solanaceous plants: bṛhatī and kaṇṭakārī.
bṛhád iic. bṛhat.

brhadaśva [aśva] m. mighty horse | myth. [Mah.] np. of the sage Bṛhadaśva "of the mighty horses"; he told the story of Nala [nalopākhyāna] to the Pāṇḍavās during their exile in the Kāmyaka forest. myth. np. of the king of Ayodhyā Brhadaśva₁, father of KuvalāśvaDhundhumāra.
brhadāranyaka [āranyaka] n. bed. n.p. from the “great text for hermits” Bṛhadāraṇyaka; cf. Yājñavalkya.
brhadāranyakopaniṣad [upaniṣad] f. phil. np. of the associated esoteric lesson Brhadāranyakopanişad.
brhadāranyakopanisadbhāsya [bhāsya] n. lit. commentary on the previous one by Samkara₁.

brhadīśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of the temple of Brhadīśvara, in Tanjavūr (mod. Tamil Nadu); it was built by King Cola Rājarāja₁ and consecrated in 1010; its main sanctuary [vimāna₁], of 12 stories, has a height of 66 m; it is crowned with a monolithic dome of 80 tons.

brhadgarbha | garbha | m. myth. np. of brhadgarbha "Power in germ", son of King Sibi; his father killed him and served him as a meal to appease a brahmin, in fact Brahmā who came to test him; the latter brought him back to life covered in flowers.
brhaddevatā [devatā] f. lit. np. of the Brhaddevatā "Great List of Gods", large work explaining the different gods appearing in the Rigveda; cf. anukramaṇī.

Bṛhaddharma [dharma] n. [bṛhaddharmapurāṇa] lit. np. of the Brhaddharma or Brhaddharmapurāna "great narrative of duty"; it deals not. with the social organisation in Bengal, and with the kulīna caste system with only two classes [varna], brāhmana and śūdra.
brhaddhāturūpāvali [dhāturūpāvali] f. gram. np. from the Bṛhaddhāturūpāvali, "Grand list of conjugated forms of the roots of Sanskrit" by TR Kṛṣṇācārya (Trivandrum, 1924).
brhádbala [bala] amnf brhadbalā who is very strong — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Brhadbala; he is said to descend from Rāma through Lava; he was killed by Abhimanyu.
bṛhadbhāgavatāmṛita [bhāgavataamṛta] n. bed. n.p. from the bṛhadbhāgavatāmṛita, sacred text of the Vaisnava tradition of Caitanya, due to Sanātana₁ Gosvāmī.

brhádrathá | ratha | m. myth. | Mah. | np. of the king of Magadha Brhadratha "of the mighty chariots", son of Uparicara and Girikā; he had two wives, twin sisters, daughters of the king of Kāśi, whom he treated similarly; they remained barren for a long time, until the visit of the muni Canda₁ Kausika, who gave the king a mango on which he had meditated; the king divided it between his two wives, who eventually each gave birth to half a stillborn child, which they abandoned; the rākṣasī Jarā₁ took them in and joined them together into a son who was named Jarāsandha, and to whom the muni predicted to be invincible in battle; the king enthroned him as his successor and withdrew to the forest; Kuśāgra is another of his sons | myth. np. of King Brhadratha₁ of the solar lineage, mentioned in the Maitrī; after long penances, he learned the secret of the soul [ātman] from the sage Sakāyanya myth. [BhP.] np. of King Brhadratha₂ Janaka, son of Devarāta, father of Mahāvīrya | hist. np. of King Brhadratha₃, last of the Maurya dynasty; he was assassinated in 185 ante by his commander-in-chief Pusyamitra Sunga₁.
bṛhan iic. bṛhat.

brhannada | nada | m. large reed — amn that has a long virile member — f. bṛhannaḍā myth. [Mah.] np. of Brhannadā "Long stem", false identity of Arjuna disguised as an effeminate eunuch, master of dance and song of the women of the court of King Virāta, during the 13th year of exile of the Pāṇḍavās.
bṛhannala [nala] m. large reed — f. Bṛhannalā myth. [Mah.] np. from Bṛhannalā, Arjuna's assumed name; cf. bṛhannaḍā.
brhanmatha [matha] mn main monastery of a sect.
Bṛhalī f. myth. [Mah.] np. of Bṛhalī, one of the 7 "mothers (dangerous) to children" [śiśumātaras] associated with Skanda.
bṛhas [g. bṛh₃] iic.

brhaspati [pati] m. myth. ved. ["master of (the prayer that makes) the power (of the gods)"] epithet of Bṛhaspati₁ "Master of Strength", son of Angirā and Sraddhā, first among the fire singers [angirasas]; he is Incantation personified; god of piety, divine priest and magician, he is chape lain [purohita] and preceptor [ācārya] of the gods; in this capacity he is called Guru, Suraguru, Dhisana; he is also the "Master of the Word" Vācaspati, Vāgīśa; he directs the influence [graha] of the planet Jupiter of which he is regent; his chariot is drawn by eight yellow horses; His wife is Tārā, who was brought back to life by Candra, causing a war between the gods and the demons [tārakāmayayuddha]; Kaca, Samyu, Kuśadhvaja are his sons; he incarnated on Earth as Drona; [PP.] he deceived his rival Sukra by taking his place among the demons; he deceived his elder brother Utathya by raping his wife Ma matā; [Mahābhāsya] he attempted to teach Indra the language by reciting the litany of correct words, but a thousand divine years were not enough; astr. he presides over the nakṣatra Puṣya (Cancer) | hist. np. of Bṛhaspati₁, ancient materialist philosopher [Cārvāka]; the Bārhaspatyasūtra is attributed to him; It is said that Cārvāka was his student. bṛhaspatirayam mūrkhaḥ (ironic) this fool is a true Bṛhaspati₁.
brhaspatigranthi [granthi] m. med. thyroid gland.
bṛhaspatisaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. np. of the Brhaspatisamhitā, section of the Garudapurāņa dealing with the education of princes.
bṛhaspatisama [sama] amnf bṛhaspatisamā same as Brhaspati.
brhaspatisava |savá₁| mr. soc. solemn rite of his soma crifice.
bṛhaspatisūtra [sūtra] n. lit. np. of the Brhaspatisūtra, attributed to Brhaspati₁, composed around 600 BCE; it taught the doctrine
materialist [Cārvāka]; it has not reached us.
brhaspatismrti [smrti] f. bed. n.p. of the Brhaspatismrti.
baijaka [*bījaka] amnf baijikā relating to seed, seminal | (original) sin.
baiḍāla var. vaiḍāla [*biḍāla] amnf baidālī relating to the cat, characteristic of the cat; hypocritical feline, impostor.
baidālavrata [vrata] n. imposture, hypocrisy.
baidālavratin [vratin] amnf baidālavratinī false religious, ascetic impostor.
bailva [*bilva] amnf bailvā coming from bilva; in bilva wood.
baiṣka [related to bleṣka] n. meat of an animal killed by a wild beast or caught in a trap.
boddhṛ [agt. budh₁] amnf boddhrī knower, scholar; versed in (loc. iic.).

bodhá [agt. budh₁] amnf bodhā who knows, who understands — act. m. knowledge, perception, consciousness; awakening; intelligence, understanding, science | blossoming; flowering; taking effect phil. Nyāya justification, truth value myth. np. of Bodha, a rṣi among the aṅgirasas . bodham prayā to begin to take effect.

bodhapañcadaśikā [pañcadaśika] f. lit. np. of the bodhapañcadaśikā "Wisdom in 15 verses", an introductory work to the Trika doctrine by Abhinavagupta; it consists of 16 verses, 15 of which are teachings and one last one explaining the purpose of the work.
bodhapūrva [pūrva] amnf bodhapūrvā intentional; conscious. bodhapūrvam intentionally, consciously.
bodhavāsara [vāsara] m. soc. day of the awakening of Vișnu from his 4-month sleep, the 11th day of the clear fortnight of kārttika; cf. prabodhanī.
bodhasāra [sāra] m. lit. np. of the bodhasāra "Nec tar of awakening", spiritual teaching text due to Narahari₁ (1789).
bodhāyana | ayana | m. hist. np. of the philosopher and mathematician bodhāyana author of the Brah masūtra vṛtti , the Baudhāyana śulbasūtra and other commentaries; he lived around 800 ant.

bodhaka [agt. budh₁] amnf bodhikā that awakens, that stimulates; that explains, that instructs — m. instructor, teacher — ifc. that denotes, that indicates, that signifies (ii.). pramāṇam hi sarvam bodhakam eva bhavati na tu ghaṭam iva kaṇṭhe rajjvā baddhvā prameyam ar
payati [AD.] A means of knowledge never does anything but explain; it does not deliver the object to be known like a pot, with a rope tied around its neck.
bodhana [agt. budh₁] amnf bodhanī ex citing, stimulating; revealing, explaining — act. f. bodhanī knowledge, understanding.
bodhanaśāstra [śāstra] n. pedagogy.
bodhayitvā [abs. ca. budh₁] ind. having awakened.
bodhi [act. budh₁] m. accomplished sage; epith. of buddha — f. science, intelligence; perfect knowledge | bd. deliverance, illumination, state of awakening of a buddha.
bodhicarya | carya | m. bd. enlightened conduct of an accomplished [bodhisattva].
bodhicaryāvatāra [avatāra] n. bed. n.p. from bodhi caryāvatāra, philosophical and didactic poem bd. of Śāntideva; Prajñākaramati made an analytical commentary [pañjikā] on it.
bodhicitta | citta | n. soc. | Vajrayāna | sperm. bodhicittam notsrjet Sperm must not be emitted (during ritual maithuna).
bodhitaru | taru | m. bio. bot. Ficus religiosa or pipal, tree under which the buddha attained Enlightenment; its prototype is venerated in Gaya; syn. aśvattha, pippala.

Bodhidharma | dharma | m. hist. np. of the monk Bodhidharma, said to have been born a prince in South India at the beginning of the 5th century; he went to China to teach meditation [dhyāna]; he is considered the transmitter of the Chan tradition in China and Zen in Japan, where he is called Daruma; it is said that he meditated for 9 years facing a wall, and that he cut off his eyelids after 7 years to remain awake; he is the first patriarch of the Bodhidharma lineage, and the 28th in a lineage tracing back to Buddha, through his master Prajñātara. bodhisattva var. bodhisatva [sattva] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] "Awakened Being" accomplished, a person having the essence of a buddha, but delaying his liberation out of compassion in order to devote himself to his fellow man; cf. jātaka, Avalokiteśvara, Mañjuśrī, Maitreya, Lokeśvara, Samantabhadra | pali Bod hisatta.
bodhisattvacaryā [caryā] f. bd. [Mahāvastu] stage on the path to enlightenment; there are 4: prakṛticaryā, pranidhānacaryā, anulomacaryā and anivartanacaryā.

bodhisattvabhūmi [bhūmi] f. lit. np. of the Bod hisattvabhūmi "The Way of the Bodhisattva", a bd. Mahāyāna work from the 5th century, attributed to the school of Maitreya₃ and not. to his student Asanga; it forms the 15th section [bhūmi] of the 1st division of the Yogācārabhūmi.
bodhisattvamārga [mārga] m. bd. path of progress of an accomplished one.
bodhisattvayāna [yāna] n. bd. monastic current bd. of the path of perfect awakening, established in the Ma gadha from the 1st to the 6th centuries, close to the Lokot taravādī school; cf. Mahāvastu.
bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā [avadāna₂ kalpalatā] f. lit. bd. np. of the bodhi sattvāvadānakalpalatā, work of Kṣemendra containing golden legends; it is known by its Tibetan translation.

bodhisena [sena] m. hist. np. of the Buddhist monk bodhisena (704–760), who introduced Chinese Huayan Buddhism to Japan after a long stay in China; born in Madurai, he had the mystical experience of Mañjuśrī and went to China before being invited by Emperor Shomu to teach Sanskrit in Japan.
bodhita [pp. That. budh₁] amnf bodhitā
explained | informed, instructed | reminded.
bodhin [agt. budh₁] ifc. amnf bod hinī warned of, aware of (iic.); familiar with (iic.) making known, revealing, illuminating (iic.) — f. bod hinī lit. title of didactic works.
bauddha [*buddha] amnf bauddhī bud dhist.
bauddhabandhu [bandhu] amnf phil. which has affinities with Buddhists; epith. not. of Prabhākara.
bauddhavacana [vacana] n. Buddhist discourse.
Bauddhādhikāra [adhikāra] m. bed. n.p. from Bauddhādhikāra (or Bauddhādhikkāra) “Condemnation of the Buddhists”, epith. of Udayana₁'s Atmatattvaviveka.
baudha [*Budha] amnf baudhā relating to Budha; concerning the planet Mercury — m. myth. n.p. of baudha, patr. of Purūravā.

baudhāyana [*bodhāyana] amnf baudhāyanī lit. relating to, composed by bodhāyana or baudhāyana — m. hist. patr. of baudhāyana, author of the Kalpasūtra, comprising śrautasūtra, grhyasūtra and dharmasūtra; he is also the author of a formulary [śulbasūtra]; he gave an approximation of the root of 2 accurate to 4 decimal places; he lived around 500. dīrghacaturaśrasyākṣṇayā rajjuh pārśvamānī ti ryanmānī ca yatprthagbhūte kurutastadubhayam
karoti [śulbasūtra] The areas (of the squares) of the length and width of a rectangle taken together equal the area (of the square) of the diagonal (precursor of the Pythagorean Theorem).
baudhya [*bodhaya] amnf baudhyā soc. belonging to the gotra of the descendants of bodha.
braja cf. vraja.
brajabhāṣā |bhāṣā| f. mod. variety of Hindi from the Brajabhūmi region; this dialect, used by certain poets, has been supplanted by the khari boli dialect.
Brajabhūmi [bhūmi] f. geo. n.p. from the Bra jabhūmi region, cultural area around Agarā and Ma thurā. র্ঘ্ধ bradhna m. ved. the Sun.
brahma iic. brahman.

brahmakāṇḍa [kāṇḍa] n. lit. np. of the Brah makānda, 1st section of the Vākyapadīya, also called Agāmasamuccaya; cf. Trikāndī | lit. np. of the Brahmakhanda₁, section of the Skandapurāna; it includes the Setumāhātmya, the Dharmāranyakānda, and the Brahmottarakhanda.

brahmakūrcavidhi [kūrcavidhi] f. ved. np. of the brahmakūrcavidhi, treatise of ritual of purification with The 5 products of the cow [pañcagavya] mixed with a decoction of kuśa herb, appendix [pariśista] of the Atharvaveda.

Brahmagiri₂ | giri | m. geo. np. of Mount Brahmagiri₂ "Brahma Mountain", summit of the Western Ghats (1608 m) on the border between Karnaṭaka and Kerala | geo. np. of Mount Brahmagiri₂, north of the Sahyādri mountain range (mod. Mahārāṣṭra); the Godāvarī originates there at Tryambakeśvara | geo. np. of Mount Brahmagiri₂ (1276 m), southwest of Karnaṭaka; the Kāverī originates there at Talakāverī | geo. np. of the town of Brahmagiri₂ in Odisha, west of Purī.

Brahmagupta [gupta] m. hist. np. of the mathematician Brahmagupta (598–665); he solved quadratic equations by iterative method [cakravāla]; he diri la gea l'observatoire de Ujjayinī; he is credited with the Brāhmaguptasphuṭasiddhānta; he calculated the circumference of the Earth as 5000 steps |yojana|.
brahmagranthi [granthi] m. soc. knot used to tie the 3 strands of grass kuśa in the rite of dīkṣā .

brahmacarya [carya] n. study of the Veda, apprentice sage of sacred science | soc. 1st stage of brahmanical life [āśrama], state of abstinent student learning from his master [guru] | celibacy, chastity, continence | phil. [yoga] chastity, one of the virtues | yama₁|.

brahmacārin [cārin] amnf brahmacāriṇī [“one who practices brahman”] who makes religious studies |chaste, continent — m. soc. brahmanical student, young celibate brahmin; vermilion |sindūra| is his symbol.
brahmajanman [janman] n. soc. "birth to brahman", upanayana ceremony; cf. dvija.
brahmajijñāsā [jijñāsā] f. phil. search for the Brahman; opp. dharmajijñāsā.
brahmajña [jña] amnf brahmajñā who knows the sacred; who has spiritual knowledge | saint.
brahmajñāna [jñāna] n. knowledge of brahman. )2
brahmajñānin |in| amnf brahmajñāninī cf. brahmajña.
brahmatattva [tattva] n. phil. [Sāṃkhya] "essence of brahman", spiritual consciousness which pervades everything.
brahmatā [tā] f. social condition of Brahmin.
brahmatejas [tejas] n. phil. power of Brahmā; effulgence of the brahmins; cf. Rcīka.
brahmatva [tva] n. condition of brahmin | soc. priestly function.
Brahmadanda [danda] m. myth. np. of the Brahmadanda "Scepter of Brahmā", cosmic weapon used by Rāma to part the waters and allow passage to Laṅkā; cf. Marukānta.

brahmadatta [datta] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the sage brahmadatta "gift of Brahmā", son of the ṛṣi Cūlī and the gandharvī Somadā; he was king of the Pañcālās; his capital was Kāmpilyā; |Rām.| King Kuśanābha gave him his 100 hunchbacked daughters as wives, and they regained their beauty | lit. np. of various kings or brahmins.
brahmadeya [deya] amnf brahmadeyā married according to the rites of the brahmins — m. marriage according to these rites — n. gift to the brahmins.
brahmadvāra [dvāra] n. phil. access to Brahmā | phil. [yoga] access to the palatal cavity |kapālakuhara|; cf. khecarīmudrā.
brahmadvís [dvis₂] amnf enemy of the Brah manes.
brahmadhvaja | dhvaja | m. soc. victory standard of Brahmā; it is of yellow brocade, carried by a long bamboo pole; it is honored at the nou vel an |yugādi|.
Brahmanadī | nadī | f. geo. np. of the Brahmanadī, epith. of the Sarasvatī₁.
brahmanirvāṇa [nirvāṇa] n. phil. extinction in the contemplation of brahman.
brahmanistha [niṣtha] amnf brahmanisthā phil. absorbed in the contemplation of brahman; MO. established in brahman (necessary quality of a guru).
brahmapadārtha | padārtha | m. divine substance; not. substance placed in the idol of Jagannātha during its consecration | navakalevara |.

brahmaputrá [putra] m. myth. son of Brahmā; cf. vaidhātra, Vasiṣṭha | geo. np. of the great river Brah maputra, which originates in Tibet and forms a common delta with the Ganges in the Gulf of Ben gale.

Brahmapura | pura | n. myth. np. of Brahmapura "City of Brahmā" in Heaven | phil. [ChU.] the body — f. Brahmapurī myth. np. of Brahmapurī "City of Brahmā" in Kailāsa | geo. epith. of Benares; third of the site of Omkāreśvara soc. Brahmin quarter in a village.

brahmapurāṇa | purāṇa | n. lit. np. of the Brahma purāņa, or Brāhmapurāņa (BP.), late text containing many descriptions of sacred places [māhātmya], especially of Utkala; it comprises 245 chapters [adhyāya]; also called Adipurāṇa₁.
brahmapralaya [pralaya] m. myth. extinction of Brahmā, at the end of a mahākalpa; syn. mahāpralaya.
brahmabandha [bandha] m. soc. knot of the sacred cord of the brahmins |yajñopavīta|.
brahmabandhu [bandhu] m. soc. brahman in worthy or bastard; false brahman.
brahmabhakta [bhakta] m. worshiper of Brahmā.
brahmabhuvana [bhuvana] n. world of Brahmā. ābrahmabhuvanāt adv. to the world of Brahmā.
brahmabhūya | bhūya | n. state of brahmin.
brahmamaya [maya] amnf brahmamayī of the nature of Brahmā | possessed by, proper to a brahmin.
brahmamuhūrta [muhūrta] m. astr. period of a laps [muhūrta] preceding rudramuhūrta (1 and a half hours before sunrise); this time of day |kāla₁| is particularly favorable.
brahmayajña [yajña] m. [SB.] ved. the sacrifice to brahman, or private recitation of the Veda, one of the five major rites [mahāyajña]; it is performed not. during the renewal of the sacred cord.

brahmayāmala [yāmala] m. lit. np. from the Brah mayāmala tantra (towards the end of the 7th century), first text of the transgressive Bhairava tantra tradition; it describes religious observances and tantric sexual rituals, and elaborates the doctrine of the "cotton mouth" [picuvaktra]; syn. Picumata.
brahmayoga [yoga] m. phil. spiritual realization through identification with God.

brahmarandhra [randhra] n. fontanelle, 10th opening of the human body | phil. [Vedānta] "the opening of Brahmā", region of the brain located below the anterior fontanelle, seat of the Spirit [manas], of perceptions [tanmātra], and of the subtle body of the soul [sūkṣmaśarīra]; [yoga] location of the sa hasrāracakra.

brahmarākṣasa | rākṣasa | m. evil spirit | myth. "vampire of knowledge", class of demon into which a scholar | paṇḍita | is reborn who neglected to transmit his knowledge. brahmarși | ṛṣi | m. myth. sage | ṛṣi | of the Brahmanic caste; there are notably 10 of them which correspond to the 10 Vedic clans associated with the collections | maṇḍala | of the Rgveda: Aṅgirā (3619 hymns, note of mandala 6), Kanva (1315.8), Vasistha (1267.7), Viśvāmitra (983.3), Atri (885.5), Bhṛgu (473), Kaśyapa (415.9), Grtsamada (401.2), Agas tya (316) and Bharata (170).
brahmaloka [loka] m. phil. np. from brahma loka "Heaven of Brahmā", where those who are delivered from rebirths are transported; cf. Satyaloka; |Praśnopanisad| it is accessed by chanting om.
brahmavadha | vadha | m. murder of a brahmin; syn. brahmahatyā.
brahmavarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Bhūmyādikānda, dealing with brahmins.
brahmavarcasá [varcasa] n. phil. divine splendor; preeminence in sacred knowledge, holiness; power over human.
brahmavāc |vāc| f. phil. the sacred text revealed by Brahmā; the Veda.
brahmavāda | vāda | m. explanation of sacred texts, not. of the Veda.
brahmavādin | vādin | amnf brahmavādinī soc. who teaches the Veda | phil. who professes the doctrine of vedānta.
brahmavādya | vādya | n. religious controversy.
brahmavíd [vid₃] amnf who knows the Brah man; who understands the vedānta.
Brahmavidāśīrvāda [āśīrvāda] m. lit. np. of the Brahmavidāśīrvāda "Religious Blessing", a small work of religious teaching [paddhati] attributed to Mādhavācārya.
brahmavidyā | vidyā | f. phil. sacred knowledge; knowledge of brahman | |brahmavidyopaniṣad| lit. np. of the esoteric lesson [upanisad] brahma vidyā.
brahmavidyābharaṇa [bharaṇa] n. lit. np. from the brahmavidyābharaṇa, text of Advaitānanda.
brahmavihāra [vihāra] m. phil. pious conduct, moral quality; four are distinguished: the fra

eternity [maitrī], gaiety [muditā], compassion [karuṇā] and equanimity [upekṣā]. brahmavaivarta |vaivarta| n. [brahmavaivartapurāṇa] lit. np. from brahma vaivartapurāna "Narrative of the transformations of Brahmā"; it identifies Kṛṣṇa with Brahmā, offers him praise, and celebrates his loves with the shepherdesses and Rādhā; it also celebrates the worship of Ganesha; it is dated to the 15th or 16th century.

brahmaśiras [śiras] n. myth. [Mah.] "Head of Brahmā", magical celestial weapon of Rudra; with it Pasupati cut off the fifth head of Brahmā; it was taught by Drona to Arjuna; his son Aśvatthāmā also possessed the secret; it is so destructive that it cannot be used against a human being, at the risk of destroying the entire world; syn. Pāśupata.
brahmasāvarṇa [sāvarṇa] m. myth. n.p. of Brah masāvarņa, 10ᵉ Manu of the kalpa.
brahmasiddhi [siddhi] f. lit. np. of the brahma siddhi "knowledge of brahman", philosophical work of Maṇḍana Miśra; Vācaspati₁ made the Commentary Tattvasamīksā.

brahmasūtra [sūtra] n. soc. sacred cord; syn. yajñasūtra | lit. np. of the brahmasūtra, generic term for a collection of Vedānta aphorisms; also called Vedāntasūtra and Sārīrakamīmāmsā; it is attributed to Bādarāyaṇa Vedavyāsa; cf. Bodhāyana, Bhāskara₁, Yādavaprakāśa, Vallabha₁. khalvaham brahmasūtram In truth I am the knowledge of brahman.

brahmasūtrabhāsya [bhāsya] n. lit. np. of the Brahmasūtrabhāṣya₁ or Brahmasūtraśaṅkarabhāṣya "Commentary by Sankara₁ of the brahmasūtra", also called Sārīrakamīmāmsābhāsya | lit. np. of the Brahmasūtrabhāsya₂ or Bhāskarabhāsya, commentary by Bhāskarācārya of the brahmasūtra | lit. np. of the brahmasūtrabhāṣya₃, Commentary by Madhva of the brahmasūtra of Bādarāyaṇa.
brahmasūtravṛtti [vṛtti] f. lit. np. of the Brah masūtravṛtti, Commentary on the brahmasūtra due to Hari₂ Dīkṣita (1736).
brahmasūtraśāṃkarabhāsya | śāṃkarabhāsya | n. cf. brahmasūtrabhāsya.
brahmastena [stena] m. ["sacred thief"] who appropriates Vedic knowledge illicitly.
brahmasthāna |sthāna| n. soc. sacred place; mo nastère | arch. open center of a building.
brahmahatyā | hatyā| f. brahmanicide, the crime of murdering a brahmin; syn. brahmavadha.
brahmahan [han₂] amnf brahmahanī brahma nicide, who kills a Brahmin.
brahmāṇḍa [aṇḍa] n. phil. ["cosmic egg"] the universe; the macrocosm. )4
brahmāndapurāna [purāna] n. lit. np. of the brahmāṇḍapurāṇa, of advaita doctrine, in prakrit sanskritized; it comprises 245 chapters |adhyāya|.

Brahmānanda |ānanda| m. "Joy of the brahman", np. of renunciant | hist. np. of Svāmī Brahmānanda Sarasvatī₂ (1871–1953); he lived as a hermit at Utta rakāśi for many years meditating in silence; in 1941 he became śaṃkarācārya of the jyotirmaṭha of Badarīnātha.

Brahmāvarta | āvarta | m. geo. np. of Brahmāvarta "Holy Land", territory between the Saras vatī₁ and the Dṛṣadvatī | geo. holy place on the Ganges (mod. Bithur) 20 km upstream from the mod. Kan pur; tradition says that it was here that Brahmā unfurled the Universe, and that he celebrated the aśvamedha; not far from tradition says that there is the hermitage of Vālmīki, where the repudiated Sītā raised her sons Kuśa and Lava.

brahmāstra | astra | n. myth. "missile of Brahmā", incantation making a weapon invincible; it was by this means that Lakşmana killed Atikāya, that Rāma killed Rāvaņa, that Bhīsma killed Sveta and that Karņa killed Ghatotkaca; [Mah.] Drona and Dhṛṣṭadyumna invoked it during their fight.
brahmāsvāda [āsvāda] m. phil. enjoyment of brah man.
brahmottara | uttara₁ | amnf brahmottarā Which deals primarily with Brahmā or the brah manes.
brahmottarakhanda [khanda] n. lit. np. from the brahmottarakhanda, chapter of the Skandapurāna.
brahmotsava | utsava | mr. soc. main festival of the temple of a great god of bhakti, not. in Tirupati.

brahmodya [udya] amnf brahmodyā (dis course) relating to the sacred — n. poetic joust; rhetorical challenge, theological debate | ved. riddles of the Veda (in contiguous stanzas forming question and answer) — f. brahmodyā mythological narrative [kathā₁].

brahmaudaná [odana] m. soc. offering of (cooked) rice to the brahmins officiating at the sacrifice. tasmād ādhitsur brahmaudanam pacet | tena pu trotpādakam reta eva dadhāti | ved. [TB.] Therefore, he who desires to beget must cook offering rice; thus he produces seed good for producing a son.
brahmaṇas [g. brahman] iic.
brahmanaspati [pati] m. ved. cf. Brhaspati.
brahmanyá |brahmanya| amnf brahmanyā relating to Brahmā or to the benevolent brahman towards the brahmins; pious — m. myth. epith. of Kārttikeya.
brahmaṇyátā [tā] f. benevolence towards the brahmins; piety.
brahmanyatva |tva| n. id.

bráhman [bṛh₁man] n. [nom. brahma] Vedic [RV.] sacred hymn | the sacred, its manifestations; the word, the Word | sacred science, sacred text, theology; spiritual power | soc. devotion; his cerdoce, holy life, condition or caste of the brahmans | phil. the Absolute, undifferentiated and inqualifiable Supreme Being or Principle; god as the Essence or substratum of the All — m. Brahmán [nom. Brahmā] myth. np. of the demiurge Brahmā, the Supreme Being, the Creator, god personifying the sacred, knowledge and truth; the Veda is his word; he possesses 4 heads [caturmukha] Which speak the Veda in all directions; a fifth head turned towards the sky grew from him, out of shame at his lust for his daughter; SivaPaśupati, charged by the gods to stop the primordial incest, cut it off with the weapon Pāśupata; astr. he regents the nakṣatra Abhijit (Vega); he presides over the Puṣkara₁ and dwells in the heaven [loka] Satyaloka; GāyatrīSāvitrī is his wife, his śakti is Brāhmī or Sarasvatī; Brahmā is born at the awakening of VișņuNārāyaṇa from his cosmic sleep on the primordial waters, seated on the lotus that sprang from his navel, reciting the Veda to the four directions; from his mind |vaidhātra| were born the 4 sages [sanakādi] eternally young and pure, and the 10 progenitors [prajāpati] Who populated the world; Brahmā grants vows to penitents, often in a thoughtless manner; he is boastful and presumptuous, as in the episode of the fire pillar [tejolinga]; for this reason he is not revered in India, except in very rare shrines such as at Puskara₂; he is not eternal, and lives 100 years of Brahmā days | kalpa|; cf. Abja, Pitāmaha, prajāpati, Vidhātā, Vidhi, Vibhu, Virāt, Satarūpā, Srastā, Svayambhū, Hiraņyagarbha | soc. priest, not. chief priest of the Vedic sacrifice; he only observes the sacrifice, to rectify any possible errors and to "cure" it, and he is thus qualified as healer [bhiṣaj]; He has three assistants: the brāhmanācchamsin, the āgnīdhra, and the potr soc. brah mane in gen. ["He who possesses brahman (born in his navel, doubly in his heart)"]; cf. brāhmaṇa || lat. flāmen. aham brahmāsmi [mahāvākya] I am Being. brahmavid brahmeva bhavati He who knows Being becomes Being itself. satyam hyeva brahma [BU.] Being is reality itself. yato vāco nivartante aprāpya manasā saha phil. [TU.] (Brahman) is from whence words return, unable to reach it with the mind.

bráhmistha [super. brahman] amnf brahmisthā soc. brahmin of the highest rank; qualifies as the most pious scholars and princes | myth. Brah most man; qualifies not. Bṛhaspati and Prajāpati. namo vayam brahmiṣṭhāya kurmaḥ gokāmā eva vayam smah [Yājñavalkya] we bow to the best brahmin, but we desire these cows.

brāhmá [*brahman] amnf Brāhmī relating to Brahmā or to brahman; divine, sacred | prescribed by the Veda — m. soc. form of marriage |vivāha| | myth. patr. of Nārada — n. study of the Veda — f. cf. Brāhmī.
brāhmapurāṇa | purāṇa | n. bed. n.p. of brāhma purāņa; cf. Brahmapurāņa.
brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta |sphuṭasiddhānta| mr. astr. n.p. of brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta; cf. brāhma guptasphutasiddhānta.
brāhmagupta [*Brahmagupta] amnf brāhmaguptā math. relating to Brahmagupta.

brāhmaguptasphuṭasiddhānta [sphuṭasiddhānta] m. astr. np. of the brāhmaguptasphuṭasiddhānta, manual of astronomy and mathematics of Brah magupta (628); it uses zero; Pṛthūdaka Svāmī made a comment on it; cf. gomūtrikā.

brāhmaṇa [*brahmana] amnf brāhmaṇī relating to or befitting a brahmin — m. Brahman, person of the first Vedic class |varṇa| | pl. brāhmaṇās soc. the class of Brahmans; priests are part of it, but many are cooks, unable to accept food prepared by people of a lower class; they wear the sacred cord [upavīta] from their
investiture [upanayana] — n. lit. generic name of works supplementing the Vedic samhitā — f. brāhmaṇī brahmin woman. brāhmaṇakṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrāh the four classes of society.
brāhmaṇaka |ka| amnf brāhmaṇakā proper to brahmins | soc. said of a country inhabited by warrior brahmins.
brāhmaṇavat [vat] adv. like a brahmin.
Brāhmaṇasarvasva [sarvasva] n. lit. np. from the Brāhmaṇasarvasva, an encyclopedia of the duties of the brahmin written by Halāyudha₁ for the use of King Laksmanasena at the end of the 12th century.
brāhmaṇasāt [sāt] ind. given to the brahmins (with kṛ₁, bhū₁, as₁). yasya brāhmaņasāt sarvam vittam āsīt |Mah.| Whose entire possessions have been given to the brahmins.
brāhmaṇāt |abl. brāhmaṇa| iic.
brāhmaṇācchaṃsin |āśaṃsin| m. ved. | "He who recites according to brāhmaṇa"] one of the 3 priests assisting the chief priest | hotr| in the solemn sacrifice; he recites the hymns honoring Indra.
brāhmaṇya [brāhmaṇaya] amnf brāhmaņyā Which is suitable for brahmins — n. state, rank of brahmin; nobility.

Brāhmī [f. brāhma] f. myth. np. of Brāhmī, śakti of Brahmā, a saptamātṛkā; she is also SarasvatīVāk, the Word of Brahmā, and Medhāvinī the Learned | hist. ancient indigenous Indian script, ancestor of Devanāgarī, evolved from Kharosthī; it ceased to be used around the 8th century | bio. bot. Hydrocotyle asiatica, water pennywort; herbaceous aquatic plant, with numerous medicinal uses. brāhmīkṛ gram. |Deshpande| to bring the tongue to the standard of the Ganges basin.
brāhmīghṛta [ghṛta] n. med. [Ayurveda] concoction of milk, ginger and juice from a bowl of water; it is given to young boys to improve their intelligence and eloquence.
bruva |brū| ifc. amnf bruvā (pej.) Who claims to be (iic.).

√ brū v. [2] pr. (brávīti) pr. r. (brūté) imp. (brūhi) impft. (abravīt) opt. (brūyāt) v. [6] pr. (bruvati) pf. (ati, pra, vi) to say something to someone (2 acc.); to speak, to tell, to declare | gr. ; fr. phrase. brūmi I say. brūhi tell me. bravītu let him speak! yah paśyati na sa brūte yo brūte sa na paśyati He who looks does not speak, He who speaks does not see. satyam brūyāt priyam brūyān na brūyāt satyam apriyam | priyam ca nānṛtam brūyād eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ | One must speak the truth, one must speak what is good; one must not speak the truth that hurts, nor the lie that flatters; this is the eternal law.
bleṣka m. collar, lace. bh

ਮ bha [agt. bhā₁] ifc. amnf bhā similar to (iic.) | animal name suffix — gram. nota. [samjñā₂] fictitious word, aspect of the nominal theme; intermediate morphological variant. Having a particular behavior in composition; opp. pada— n. star; asterism; syn. nakshatra | math. symb. the number 27 — m. astr. the planet Venus; its regent Sukra — f. cf. bhā₁.

bhakāra [(bha)kāra| m. the sound or letter 'bha'. bhakāraḥ kumbhakarņe'sti bhakāro'sti vibhīṣaṇe | tasmāt rākṣasarājo'yam rābhano na tu rāvanah || There is the sound 'bha' in Kumbhakarna, the sound 'bha' is in Vibhīṣaṇa; thus the king of vampires must be Rābhaṇa rather than Rāvaṇa (scholasticism from a paṇḍita in a legend about the young Kālidāsa).
bhaktá [pp. bhaj] amnf bhaktā devoted to (g.), faithful, loving; devout, pious follower of — m. follower, pious worshipper — n. food, (cooked) rice.
bhaktapura [pura] n. geo. np. of the city of Bhak tapura, ancient capital of Nepal, 13 km east of Kathmandu; it was founded in the 12th century by King Devamalla, and fortified by Jayayakṣa Malla.
Bhaktamāla |māla| n. lit. np. of the Bhaktamāla, a poem in the Braja language by Nābhadāsa (circa 1600); it gives the hagiographies of more than 200 saints.
bhaktavatsala [vatsala] amnf bhaktavatsalā who feels friendship towards devotees.
bhaktavilāsa | vilāsa | mr. bed. n.p. from bhaktavilāsa, a śaiva text attributed to Agasti.
bhaktaśaraṇa [śaraṇa] n. kitchen; syn. mahānasa.

bhakti [act. bhaj] f. love, zeal, devotion, fervor, adoration; fidelity, homage; ecstasy | phil. worship, adoration; not. ecstatic worship of divine love | myth. [Srīmadbhāgavatamāhātmya] np. of bhakti, young woman personifying devotion; she appears to Nārada accompanied by two senile old men Jñāna and Vairāgya presented as her sons; Nārada consults the 4 eternals [sanakādi] who organize a saptāha in order to restore their youth order, series, sequence — ifc. case of, part of (iic.).
bhaktimat |mat| amnf bhaktimatī devoted, attached, faithful to (loc. iic.) | devout; follower of the cult of divine love.
bhaktiyoga | yoga | m. phil. spiritual realization through devotion; cf. sāmīpya, sālokya.
bhaktirasa | rasa | m. taste for devotion.
bhaktírasāmṛta [amṛta] n. nectar of devotion.
bhaktírasāmṛtasindhu [sindhu] m. bed. n.p. from Bhaktirasāmṛtasindhu “River of Nectar of Devotion”, devotional work by Jīva Gosvāmī.
bhaktivedānta [vedānta] m. soc. n.p. bhakti vedānta, title of scholar in the Gaudīya Vaisnava tradition; cf. Prabhupāda.

Bhaktisiddhānta [siddhānta] m. soc. n.p. of Bhaktisiddhānta, title of scholars and historical works. n.p. of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura (1874–1937), Bengali spiritual master; he founded the Gaudīyamatha and initiated many disciples, including Bhaktivedānta Svāmī.
Bhaktisūtra |sūtra| n. lit. np. of the Bhaktisūtra, a collection of devotional aphorisms attributed to Sāndilya.

√ bhakṣ [related to bhaj] v. [1] pr. (bhakṣati) pr. r. (bhakṣate) pp. (bhakṣita) pfp. (bhakṣya, bhakṣanīya) to eat, consume; to drink, absor ber; to devour, engulf; to exhaust, destroy — ca. (bhakṣayati) abs. (bhakṣayitvā) id. ਮੁਲਾ bhakṣa [act. bhakṣ] m. act of eating or drinking | food, drink, provisions — ifc. act of feeding on (iic.) — agt. f. bhakṣī ifc. that which feeds on (iic.).
bhakṣaka [agt. bhakṣ] amnf bhakṣikā eater; voracious, greedy, gluttonous — ifc. man geur de (iic.) — m. food; meal — act. f. bhakṣikā act of eating; mastication.
bhakṣaṇa [act. bhakṣ] n. the act of eating, nourishing oneself; meal, food. Bhakşanam kr to eat, consume.
bhakṣaṇīya [pfp. [2] bhakṣ] amnf bhakṣanīyā which can be eaten, edible.
bhakṣita [pp. bhakṣ] amnf bhakṣitā eaten, consumed, devoured | mispronounced, mar monné (word) — n. fact of having been eaten by (i.).
bhakṣitavat [ppa. bhakṣ] amnf bhakṣitavatī who ate. nāham bhakṣitavānambe ityuktavānchrīkṛṣṇaḥ bhāgavate "I did not eat any, Mother" says śrī Kṛṣṇa in the Bhāgavatapurāṇa.
bhakṣin [agt. bhakṣ] amnf bhakṣiṇī who eats, who devours.

Bhagīratha [ratha] m. myth. np. of Bhagīratha "Chariot of Glory", king of Ayodhyā, son of Dilīpa₁, grandson of Amsumān of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa]; he is the example of the most pious king; following the advice of his spiritual director [guru] the sage Tritula, he followed an ascetic practice, and undertook the sacrifice [yajña] of agnistoma to give away all his possessions; he gave his kingdom to his enemy the neighboring king and became a wandering ascetic, begging for his food, in distant lands where he was unknown; he happened to pass through his former kingdom, was begged to take up the throne again, but resumed his wandering, in the company of Tritula; The minister of a distant kingdom whose king had died without an heir persuaded him to rule there; later, at the death of the king who succeeded him, he returned to rule over his kingdom at the request of his former subjects; [Rām.] through his penances and prayers to Gangādevī he brought down [gangāvatara] the Celestial Ganges [Mandākinī] to earth through the intermediary of SivaGangādhara to create the terrestrial Ganges [Bhāgīrathī] which he led to the Ocean to purify the ashes of the 60,000 sons of his great-grandfather Sagara who had dug it to find the horse of his sacrifice; through his son Śrutanābha (or |Rām.| Kakutstha) he is the ancestor of Raghu and therefore of Rāma.

Bharataśāstra [śāstra] n. lit. np. from the Bharataśāstra, an encyclopedic manual of the art of dance
classical [nāṭyaśāstra], attributed to Bharata₃; cf. Nātyaśāstra.

bharatārṇava [arṇava] m. myth. np. of the Bha ratārņava "Indian Whirlwind", a complete treatise on dance according to Bharata₃, composed by Nan dikeśvara at the request of Indra, who wanted to surpass Națaśekhara; Indra asked for a condensed version, and obtained the Abhinayadarpana. )2
bharad iic. bharat.
bharádvāja [vāja] m. lark | myth. ved. n.p. of

Patriarch [saptarși] Bharadvāja₁ "He Who Holds the (Protective) Strength"; [Rām.] he is said to be the son of Atri; he was a disciple of Vālmīki, and accompanied him when they saw the pair of curlews |krauñca| mourned by the hunter; Indra granted him thousands of years of study of the Veda, and taught him Ayurveda, which he transmitted to the sage Atreya; his hermitage [āśrama] was in Prayāga; Rāma stopped there with Sītā and Lakshmana during his exile; Mah., performing his ablutions on the banks of the Ganges, spilled his seed at the sight of the nymph |apsaras | Ghṛtācī, and collected it in an ablution cup [Drona], where droṇa was found; his wife is Srutavatī, who bore him his son Sunahotra; a friend of King Pṛṣata, he was the tutor [guru] of his son Drupada; [BhP.] after thousands of years of studying the Veda, he asked Indra for an extension, who appeared to him before three mountains and took three handfuls of sand, which he compared to his infinitesimal knowledge of the Veda in relation to the three mountains; Bharadvāja₁ was not discouraged, and continued his study; we owe to him hymns of the Rigveda | myth. np. of Bharadvāja₁ "born of (She Who was) doubly pregnant", epith. of Dīrghatamā, son of Mamatā, who was pregnant and raped by her brother-in-law Bṛhaspati; his mother abandoned him in the forest, the wind spirits [marutas] found him and gave him to Bharata, who named him his heir under the name Vitatha. ਮਿੰਟ bhari [agt. bhṛ] ifc. amnf Who maintains (iic.).
Bharu |bhṛu| m. lord, master; husband |myth. np. of Bharu "lord", epithet of Shiva or Vishnu of the. bharū myth. Shiva and Vishnu together.
bharuka [ka] m. myth. np. of King Bharuka, of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa], son of Sudeva; Bāhuka is his son.
Bharukaccha | kaccha | mn geo. np. of the country and city of Bharukaccha, corruption of Bhrgukaccha "Lord's Shore (Bhṛgu)", at the mouth of the Narmadā; mod. Broach/Baruch in Gujarāt.
bhárga [related to bhargas] m. brilliance, splendor; effulgence | myth. np. of Bharga, epith. of Shiva "Resplendent" — n. bhargas radiance; splendor, glory.
bhargavat |vat| amnf bhargavatī splendid, radiant.
bhárgas [abstr. bhṛjj] n. brilliance, splendor; glory | fire || lat. fulgur; gr. φλεψον; fr. fire, dazzling.

bhartr [agt. bhr] amnf bhartrī [sg. nom. bhartā, acc. bhartāram] Who supports, Who preserves, Who maintains (iic. g.); Who sustains, Who nourishes — m. master, patron, chief; husband — f. bhartrī nursing mother.
bhartrpinda | pinda | mn soc. salary paid by the master to his servants.
Bhartrprapañca | prapañca | m. hist. np. of the philosopher Bhartrprapañca, one of the first commentators on the Brahmasūtra, prior to Saṃkara₁; cf. jñānakarmasamuccayavāda.
bhartṛmatī |mat| f. married woman.
bhartrmentha [mentha] m. hist. np. of the poet Bhartṛmeṇṭha (5th century); he lived in Ujjayinī and Kaśmīra; he is the author not. of the mahākāvya Hayagrīvavadha.
bhartṛsneha [sneha] m. favor of the master.

Bhartrhari [hari₂] m. hist. np. of Bhartrhari "Master Hari", philosopher of language and poet of Ujjayini (5th century); he is the author of an important treatise on the philosophy of language, Vākyapadīya "On the Sentence and the Word" with its gloss [vrtti], and of the commentary Mahābhāsyadīpikā on the Mahābhāṣya of Patañjali₁; he is also credited with the Ṣaḍhātusamīkṣā; cf. Harivṛṣabha; the caves where he is said to have lived as a hermit are shown to Ujjayini | hist. np. of the poet Bhartrhari₁, presumed brother of King Vikramāditya; he returned seven times to his Buddhist vocation; he composed three hundred
ries [Satakatraya] of poems, resp. on eroticism [śṛṅgāra], morality [nīti], and renunciation [vairāgya].
√ bharts v. [1] pr. (bharsati) v. [10] pr. (bhart sayati) pp. (bhartsita) pf. (ava, nis) threaten, insult; scold, scold.
bhartsaka [agt. bharts] ifc. amnf bhart sikā Who threatens, Who insults (iic.).
bhartsana [act. bharts] n. reproach; threat; curse.
bhartsita [pp. bharts] amnf bhartsitā threatened, insulted; scolded — n. threat.

bharścu m. hist. np. of the poet bharścu, guru of Bāṇa₂; also called Bhartsu, Bhatsu, Bharśsu, Bharcu. ਮਲ਼ bhalla m. bio. bear — mnf ballī kind of arrow — amnf bhallā favorable, good to the gure — f. bhallī bio. bot. Semecarpus anacardium, a tree related to the cashew; this rose family member is used in medicine. )3

bhallūka [ūka| m. bio. bear. ਮਰ bhavá |agt. bhū₁| m. existence, state; origin, birth; prosperity, excellence | attainment, acquisition | the world, life here below | phil. quality of feeling expressed by the artist and felt by the viewer of the artwork, one of the 6 aesthetic canons of the visual arts | sadanga silpa | | bd. continuity of existence | myth. np. of bhava "the Being", a name of Shiva | du. bhavau myth. bhava and Bhavānī.

bhavacakra [cakra] m. bd. ["wheel of existence"] representation (not. in Tibet) of the cycle of rebirths [saṃsāra]; this circular diagram has 6 parts, representing the respective realms of gods [deva], demons [asura], specters [preta], infernal creatures [naraka], animals [tiryac] and men | manuṣya| ; cf. saṃsāracakra.
bhávacchid [chid₂] amnf phil. which cuts the chain of transmigrations cleanly.
Bhavatrāta [trāta] m. hist. np. of the ancient scholar Bhavatrāta; we owe him a vrtti of the Jaiminikalpa.
Bhavanātha | nātha | m. hist. np. of the grammarian Bhavanātha Miśra (1460–1530), author of the Prayo gapallava.

bhavabhūti [bhūti] f. prosperity | hist. np. of bha vabhūti "prosperous", poet and playwright of the 8th century; he was born in Padmapura in Vidarbha; he lived at the court of King Yaśovarmā in Kanyākubjā, and bore the name Srīkantha₁ Nīlakantha₁; he is the notable author of the Mahāvīracarita, the Mālatīmādhava and the Uttararāmacarita; he is ranked with Kālidāsa and Bāna₂ among the glories of Sanskrit poetry.
bhavasaṃkrānti [saṃkrānti] f. bed. n.p. from the Bhavasamkrānti, comic text. sutra-style.
bhavānukīrtana [anukīrtana] n. representation of emotions; defines theatre according to Bharata₃.
bhavat₁ [ppr. bhū₁] amnf bhavantī [nom. bhavan] being, existing, present — f. bha vantī gram. present tense; cf. lat. bhavadbhūtabhavye adv. gram. in the present, past, and future.

bhávat₂ [contr. bhagavat] m. [nom. bhavān; voc. bhavan adr. Sir, Your Honor (present tense, polite form of 3rd person) | pl. bhavantas Gentlemen, lords, honorable — f. bhavatī Madam (voc. bhavati). atrabhavat this Sir (here-present tense, polite form of he). tatrabhavat that Sir (non-present tense, polite form of he). ihabhavantah this great man. bhavatah nāma kim adr. What is your name? (to a man). bhavatyāḥ nāma kim adr. What is your name? (to a woman). bhavān kaḥ var. bhavatī kā adr. Who are you? bhavantah pramāṇam It is up to Your Excellency to decide.
bhavad iic. bhavat₁.
bhavadanya [anya] amnf bhavadanyā other than you.
bhavadīya [īya] amnf bhavadīyā your, yours. bhavadīyaḥ adr. Yours truly.
bhavana [act. bhū₁] n. house, dwelling, residence; palace — ifc. seat of (iic.).
bhavanīya [pfp. [2] bhū₁] n. (impers.) it must be.
bhavā iic. bhavat₁.
bhavādṛś [dṛś₂] amnf such as you.
