bhavādṛśa [dṛśa] amnf bhavādṛśī id. rājñāṃbhavādṛśāmagre rahasyaṃ kathamucyate [KSS.] how can I tell this secret before a king such as you?

Bhavānī [bhavaānī] f. myth. n.p. of Bhavānī "existence", peaceful form of the Goddess; epith. of Pārvatī, wife of bhavaSiva. Bhavānī bhāratī lit. n.p. from Bhavānī Bhārati, patriotic poem by śrī Aurobindo (1908); it has 99 verses in tristubh meter.
Bhavānīśankara [śankara] m. geo. np. of Bhavānīśankara "Shiva with Pārvatī"; he is worshipped at the monastery [maṭha] of Citrapura in Karnātaka.
bhavitavya [pfp. [3] bhū₁] amnf bha vitavyā which must be, which must be accomplished.
bhavitavyatā [tā] f. that which must be accomplished, the inevitable | destiny.
bhavitṛ [agt. bhū₁] amnf bhavitrī that which is to be, that which will be; future, subsequent.
bhavin [agt. bhū₁] amnf bhavinī being, living — m. to be alive; man.
bhaviṣṇú [agt. bhū₁] amnf that is about to happen, imminent; future — ifc. (after acc.) in the process of becoming. andhambhaviṣṇuḥ becoming blind. ādhyambhaviṣṇuḥ becoming rich.

bhaviṣya [fut. bhū₁] amnf bhaviṣyā that is about to happen, imminent; future — n. the future, the future nir. )4 bhavişyapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. of the np. Bhavişyapurāṇa "Ancient History of the Future", composed between 500 and 1200; its compiler Vyāsa recounts the kaliyuga according to the prophetic vision of Sūta₁ Gosvāmī; this text interprets the Genesis of the Bible, adapting Adam [Adama] and Eve [Havyavatī], the tree of sin [pāpavṛkṣa], with Kali in the role of the serpent; they begat the race of the mlecchās ; Noah is Nyuha, Vishnu appeared to him in a dream at the time of the Flood, to build the ark; Vikramāditya is then mentioned, then Mahomet [Mahāmāda], illusionist blessed by Shiva; he appeared in a dream to King Bhoja as a specter [bhūta] to announce that he was founding an impious religion; Shiva revealed to him that he was the ghost of Tripura, returned to spread a false doctrine; King Bhoja gave the samskṛta to the Aryans [dvija] and left the prākṛta to the śūdrās; then the Buddhists prospered before leaving for China; Jayadeva is presented as an incarnation of Tvașțā composing the Nirukta then the Gītagovinda; finally the Muslims invade India and destroy the temples.
bhaviṣyát [pfu. bhū₁] amnf bhaviṣyantī imminent; to come; future — n. gram. future tense tur — f. bhaviṣyantī gram. future marker; cf. lṛţ.

bhávya [pfp. [1] bhū₁] amnf bhavyā existing, present, real | that which will be accomplished, that which will occur; future | adequate, opportune; good, just; favorable; happy, pleasant; gracious, excellent | jn. said of a soul that can attain liberation; opp. abhavya — n. existence; future; result, reward; success — m. lit. np. of the scholar bd. Bhavya "Blessed" (500-578), student of Nāgārjuna, also called Bhavyaviveka; he is the author of the Madhyamakahrdayakārikā and its commentary the Tarkajvala | lit. np. of many mythical or historical figures.
√ bhaş v. [1] pr. (bhaşati) to bark, to howl.
√ bhas v. [3] pr. (babhasti) pp. (bhasita) mas tiquer, dévorer; consumer, réduit à cendres.
bhasád f. posterior, buttocks | genitals; glans of the penis. bhasattas adv. below the buttocks | down to the buttocks. ābhasat below the hips.
bhasita [pp. bhas] amnf bhasitā consumed, reduced to ashes — n. ashes.
bhastrā |bhastra| f. off skin | leather bag, satchel; leather water bottle; bellows | var. bhastrī id.
bhastrika [bhastrāika] amnf bhastrikī that carries in a bag — m. [yoga] intensive breathing technique [prāṇāyāma] — f. bhastrikā small bag.
bhasma iic. bhasman.

bhasmasāt |sāt| ind. (reduces) to ashes (with kṛ₁, as₁, bhū₁, nī₁, yā₁). sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute |Mah.| He reduces all deeds to ashes. niyatam bhasmasād yāti [HV.] He is inexorably reduced to ashes.
bhasmānkura | ankura | m. offspring of a śaiva ascetic and a śūdra prostitute.

Bhasmāsura [asura] m. myth. np. of Bhasmāsura, the asura "of the ashes"; he obtained from Shiva a magic wand that could reduce to ashes any being touched by it; he sought to destroy Shiva with it, but was deceived by Vishnu who incited him to try it on himself to find that it was inoperative; producing his downfall.

bhasman [bhasman] n. ashes. bhasmīkṛ reduce to ashes. bhasmīkaraṇam act of reducing to ashes. bhasmībhū be reduced to ashes. bhasmībhūta amn reduced to ashes. bhasmībhāvah condition of being reduced to ashes. bhasmībhāvam gatah reduced to ashes.
bhasmani [loc. bhasman] iic.
bhasmanihuta [huta] amnf bhasmanihutā ["sacrificed in the ashes"] useless.

√ bhā₁ v. [2] pr. (bhāti) pft. (babhau) aor. [6] (abhāsīt) pp. (bhāta) pf. (ā, pra, prati, vi) to shine, to gleam | to appear, to manifest, to be in view | (av. na) to cut a poor figure | to please (g.) — ps. (bhāyate) (impers.) splendor radiates (from (i.)) | gr. ); lat. fāri; fr. phare. ਮਾ bhā₁ |f. bha| f. light, brightness; splendor | shadow of the gnomon.

bhāsarvajña [sarvajña] m. hist. np. of bhāsarvajña, philosopher of Kaśmīra (9th century); he is the author of the Nyāyasāra and the Nyāyabhūṣaṇa; he is also credited with a commentary on the Gaṇakārikās.

bhāgá [obj. bhaj] m. portion, share, fraction, lot, destiny, fate; profit, good fortune | soc. share taken for the king. bhāgān kṛ var. bhāgīkṛ divide into parts, share. mahābhāgaḥ Your Eminence, Your Excellency, Noble Sire ["who has a great destiny"]. yathā bhāgam adv. in accordance with his destiny. )5
bhāgádughá [dugha] m. ved. official distributing gifts or booty; he is part of the royal circle |ratnin|.

bhāgádheyá | dheya | n. Vedic. portion, share; property, goods; fortune, destiny | soc. royal share; tax, levy | prosperity — m. soc. heir, co-heir — amnf bhāgadheyī reverting as a share — f. bhāgadheyā soc. royal tax, levy. bhāgávṛtti lit. np. of the Bhāgavṛtti, commentary on the Kāśikā by Vimalamati (late 9th century); it is known only through quotations.
bhāgásas [śas] adv. by portions; each in turn; gradually. bhāgaśas kalp divide into parts.
bhāgáhara [hara] amnf bhāgaharā that takes its share, that shares — m. math. divisor; denominator.
bhāgáhāra [hāra₁] m. math. division.
bhāgavata [*bhagavata] amnf bhāgavatī myth. relating to Bhagavān, to Kṛṣṇa; relating to God — n. lit. np. of the bhāgavata purāṇa; cf. bhāgavatapurāna.

bhāgavatapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. of the Bhāgavatapurāna "Deed of the Lord", also called Srīmadbhāgavata; it is the legendary life of Kṛṣṇa, told by Suka, son of Vyāsa, to King Parīkṣit; its 12 sections |skandha| are an expansion of the 6 tomes [amśa] of the Viṣnupurāṇa; it was composed mostly between the 8th and 10th centuries in South India; tradition attributes it to Vyāsa; it conforms [sāttvika] to the Vaishnava canon; its 10th chapter (4000 verses out of a total of 18000) is particularly revered.
bhāgavatasaptāha [saptāha] m. soc. recitation of the Bhāgavatapurāna in a 7-day ceremony.

bhāgín [agt. bhaj] amnf bhāginī who has a right to the share; who possesses a share; fortunate — ifc. who shares (iic.); concerned by; who inherits from (iic.) — m. partner; owner; heir | the whole (opp. the parts).
bhāgineya [*bhaginīya] m. nephew (son of a sister); syn. svasrīya — f. bhāgineyī niece || hi. bhāñjā.
bhāgīya [*Bhagaīya] ifc. amnf bhāgīyā which belongs to, connected with (iic.).

bhāgīratha [*Bhagīratha] amnf bhāgīrathī relating to Bhagīratha — f. bhāgīrathī myth. np. of bhāgīrathī, epith. of the Gaṅgā “of the descended upon Earth thanks to Bhagīratha” | geo. Himalayan river forming the upper course of the Ganges, upstream from Haridvāra; it has its source at Gomu kha.
bhāgurāyaṇa m. bed. [Viddhaśālabhañjikā] np. of the Brahmin Bhāgurāyaṇa, minister of King Vidyādharamalla.

bhāgya₁ [bhāgaya] amnf bhāgyā myth. relating to Bhaga | who deserves his share | lucky, fortunate — n. destiny; happy fate, happiness | phil. destiny linked to his merit | karma | in previous existences — f. bhāgyā ifc. chance of; destiny of. bhāgyena adv. by chance, fortunately.
bhāgya₁ [pfp. [1] bhaj] amnf bhāgyā to divide; divisible. ਮਾੜ੍ਹਾ bhāṅgā [*bhaṅgā] amnf bhāṅgā made of hemp — n. hemp field.
bhāṅgāsuri [*bhaṅgāsurai] m. myth. |Mah.| np. of bhāngāsuri, patr. of Rtuparna "son of Bhangāsura".
bhāj [*bhaj] ifc. amnf who has in his share, who possesses, who enjoys | who dwells, who frequents; who worships. śokabhāk afflicted by grief.

bhāja |agt. bhaj| amnf bhājā ifc. that takes part, that participates in; relating to; belonging to— act. n. receptacle, vessel, ship person of great merit, of great virtue or intelligence — f. bhājī rice porridge.
bhājaka |agt. That. bhaj| mr. separation, division.
bhājana |act. bhaj| n. vase, container, pot; receptacle | (in fig.) where a good flows.
bhājin [agt. bhaj] ifc. amnf bhājinī who shares (iic.); who participates in (iic.).

bhājya [pfp. [1] ca. bhaj] amnf bhājyā that one must share — n. math. dividend. ਮਾਣੂ bhāṭṭa [*Bhaṭṭa] amnf bhāṭṭā hist. concerning Kumārila Bhaṭṭa — m. phil. mīmāṃsaka of his school | pl. geo. the people of Bhaṭṭās — n. lit. the work of Kumārila.

Bhāṭṭatantrarahasya | tantrarahasya | n. lit. np. from the Bhāttatantrarahasya of Khandadeva, a work of philosophy of language according to the Mīmāmsā; it establishes creative energy [bhāvana] as the basis of the meaning of the sentence in the optative [lin].
bhāṭṭaīpikā [dīpikā] f. lit. [Mīmāṃsā] np. of the Bhāṭṭadīpikā "Light on the school of Kumārila", work of Khandadeva.
bhāṇa [act. bhaṇ] n. recitation; monologue | soc. theatrical performance in one act in the form of a monologue; cf. Caturbhāṇī | bd. recitation of the Law.

bhāṇaka |agt. bhaṇ| m. reciter; herald — f. bhāṇikā type of drama. ਮਾਾਤ bhāṇḍa [*bhaṇḍa] n. vessel; container, pot, dish, box; tool, instrument, utensil; ornament, treasure — m. pl. goods, merchandise, foodstuffs — f. bhāṇḍā ifc. container of (11th century); testicle of (11th century). bhojanabhāṇḍāni kitchen utensils.
bhāṇḍaka |ka| mn small container, cup, bowl — ifc. goods, quantity of (iic.) — f. bhāndikā tool, instrument.
bhāṇḍaśālā |śālā| f. warehouse || pt. bancasal.
bhāṇḍāgāra [āgāra] n. treasure; collection.
bhāṇḍāra [ra] m. jn. manuscript library; not. in Pattana.

Bhāndārakara [kara₁] m. hist. np. of Rāmakṛṣṇa Gopala bhāṇḍārakara (1837–1925), paṇḍita ma rathe and social reformer, teacher at Dec can College; the Bandharkar Institute in Pune is named in his honour.
bhāṇḍi [bhāṇḍai] f. razor case.
bhāndivāha [vāha] m. barber.
bhāndiśālā [śālā] f. hair salon.
bhāṇḍīra m. bio. bot. Clerodendrum visco sum, a bushy labiate plant with white panicle flowers tinged with purple; it is used in medicine.
bhāta [pp. bhā₁] amnf bhātā Bright, splendid res | having appeared.
bhāti [act. bhā₁] f. brilliance, splendor | evidence; perception, knowledge.
bhādra [*bhadra] m. abbreviation of the month of bhādrapada — f. bhādrī its full moon.

bhādrapada [pada] m. astr. name month of bhādrapada (August-September), month of the of Bhādrapadās; cf. anantavrata — f. bhādrapadā pl. astr. np. of Bhādrapadās "the feet (of the bed) are auspicious", lunar asterism | nakṣatra | of the Square of Pegasus, also called prosthapadā; cf. Pūrvabhādrapadās, Uttarabhādrapadās — f. bhādrapadī cf. bhādrī.
bhāna |act. bhā₁| n. appearance, perception | luster, brilliance.

bhānú [agt. bhā₁] m. appearance; splendor, brilliance, radiance. The Sun king, prince, lord. myth. np. of Bhānu "Brilliant", epithet of Sūrya and of the gods | lit. [Mah.] np. of Bhānu₁, hero of Yādavās; bhānumatī is his daughter | soc. honorific title — f. beautiful wife.
bhānukampa |kampa| m. myth. np. du gaṇa Bbhānukampa, celestial musician who with Bāṇa ac companion Siva dancing the tāndava.
Bhānucandra [candra] m. hist. np. du paṇḍita jaina Bhānucandra (late 16th century); he was patronized by the Mughal emperor Akbar; his student Siddhican dra wrote his biography Bhānucandracarita.
Bhānucandracarita [candra] n. lit. np. of the Bhānucandracarita, biography of Bhānucandra due to Siddhicandra; its last chapter is the author's autobiography.

bhānudatta [datta] m. hist. n.p. of bhānudatta, a 15th century scholarly Brahmin from Videha; he composed works of aesthetic poetry at the court of DevagiriDaulatābād, not. the Rasamañjarī, the Rasataranginī, and the Alamkāratilaka.

Bhānudāsa [dāsa] m. hist. np. of Bhānudāsa, deśastha brahmin of the Vārkarī movement, born in Pratisthāna around 1450; he brought back to Pandharpur the idol of Vithobā which had been hidden from the Khilji armies.

bhānumat |mat| amnf bhānumatī Brilliant — f. lit. [HV.] np. of bhānumatī, daughter of Bhānu₁; during a visit to Piṇḍāraka, Kṛṣṇa organized a drinking festival; the demon Nikumbha took advantage of it to kidnap her; this stemmed from a curse of Durvāsā, which she had not acknowledged during a meeting in the gardens of Raivata₂; but he had nevertheless predicted that she would be saved by Saha deva, whom she would marry, which indeed happened.
bhānuvarman [varman] m. bed. [DKC.] np. of king Bhānuvarmā of Vanavāsī; he attacked Ananta varma₁.
√ bhām v. [1] pr. r. (bhāmate) pp. (bhāmita) to be angry, to be passionate — ca. (bhāmayati) to anger — intens. r. (bābhāmyate) to be furious.
bhāma₁ [bhā₁ma] m. light, splendor | the Sun. ਮਾਸ bhāma₂ [act. bhām] m. anger, passion, rage — f. bhāmā passionate woman | myth. cf. Satyabhāmā.

bhāmat [ppr. bhā₁] amnf bhāmatī Brilliant — f. bhāmatī lit. n.p. of the bhāmatī, "Brilliant" exegesis of the Brahmasūtra bhāsya of Sankarācārya, due to Vācaspati₁ Miśra; by ext. phil school. advaita which arises from it (opp. vivarana); cf. Kalpataru.
Bhāmaha m. hist. np. of Bhāmaha, poetic theorist of Kaśmīra (late 7th century); he is )7 the author of the Kāvyālamkāra₁.
bhāmitá [pp. bhām] amnf bhāmitā véd. angry; in rage.
bhāmin [agt. bhām] amnf bhāminī passionate — f. bhāminī passionate woman; beautiful woman | hist. np. of bhāminī "beautiful", wife of Jagannātha₁ Panditarāja.

bhāminīvilāsa |vilāsa| m. lit. np. from bhāminī vilāsa "Entertainment of bhāminī", famous poem in 384 stanzas by Jagannātha₁ Paṇḍitarāja in memory of his wife who died prematurely; it comprises 4 parts: Prāstāvikavilāsa (didactic), Sringāravilāsa (erotic), Karuņavilāsa (pathetic), Sāntavilāsa (devotional).
bhārá [obj. bhṛ] m. charge, burden; corvée, labor | weight, mass, large quantity | unit of weight, worth 20 tulā || gr. φορος; fr. phore.
bhārahāra [hāra₁] amnf bhārahārā who carries a burden — m. bearer; porter | brute; beast of burden.
bhāraka |agt. bhṛ| amnf bhārikā ifc. charged with (iic.) — obj. mn charge, burden; weight.
bhāraṇḍa mf bhāraṇḍī lit. |PT.| two-headed bulbous bird; cf. bhāruṇḍa.

Bhārata₁ |*Bharata| amnf Bhāratī re latif to Bharata; of the lineage of Bharata; Indian — m. myth. |BhG.| np. of Bhārata₁ "Hero of the bharatās", address of Arjuna by Kṛṣṇa the yādava | |Bhāratavarṣa| cf. bharatavarṣa | pl. the Bhāratās, descendants of Bharata — n. |bhāratākhyāna| lit. np. of the Bhārata₁, poem of 24000 verses, ancestor of the Mah., from the poem Jaya₂ of Vyāsa | [bhāramaṇḍala] ["land of Bharata"] India — f. cf. Bhāratī.
Bhāratabhāvadīpa |bhāvadīpa| m. lit. np. of the Bhāratabhāvadīpa, influential commentary on the Mah. due to Nīlakaṇṭha₄ Caturdhara who fixed the standard text, precursor of the critical edition.
bhārataratna [ratna] n. mod. "Jewel of India", highest Indian civil distinction.
Bhāratavarṣa [varṣa] m. geo. n.p. from Bhāratavarṣa, India; cf. bharatavarșa.
bhāratasamara [samara] m. myth. war between the Kauravās and the Pāndavās.
bhāratānuvarṇana [anuvarṇana] n. bed. n.p. from the bhāratānuvarṇana “Description of India” by Mahāmahopādhyāya T. Ganapati Sāstrī (1905).
bhāratīya [īya] amnf bhāratīyā Indian.
bhāratīyavidvatpariṣad [vidvatpariṣad₂] f. mod. Indian cultural association.

Bhāratī [f. Bhārata₁] f. eloquence; literary composition, dramatic art | soc. np. of the Bhāratī order, one of the 10 orders of mendicant monks founded by Sankara₁; cf. Caitanya | lit. commentary on the Nātyaśāstra. amarabhāratī Sanskrit, the eternal language.
Bhāratītīrtha [tīrtha] m. hist. np. of Bhāratītīrtha, guru of Sāyaṇa; we owe him the Adhikaraṇamālā.
Bhāradvāja [*Bharadvāja] amnf bhāradvājī (patr.) from Bharadvāja | soc. n.p. of
lineage [gotra] Bhāradvāja; cf. Garga, Drona, Śāsa, Sunahotra | pl. soc. np. of a clan of brahmins, of a vedic school; the 6th mandala of the RV. is their work.
Bhāravi m. lit. np. of Bhāravi, poet prior to the 7th century, author of the mahākāvya Kirātārjunīya.

bhāruṇḍa var. bhuruṇḍa m. lit. [PT.] np. of bhāruṇḍa or bhāraṇḍa, two-headed bird; one head ate a delicious fruit without sharing with the other; the other took revenge by eating a poisoned fruit, causing the death of the animal; the fable illustrates the necessity of solidarity — n. soc. variety of Vedic chant |sāman|.

bhārgavá [*bhṛgua] amnf bhārgavī derived from, related to bhṛgu — m. myth. np. of Bhārgava "Of the race of bhṛgu", patron of Paraśurāma, Ja madagni, Sukra, Gṛtsamada, etc. | myth. lineage of the descendants of bhṛgu; the Bhārgavās were the hereditary preceptors [guru] of the Hai hayās kings; cf. Aurva | soc. lineage name [gotra] brah mane | myth. [Mah.] name of a weapon given by Paraśurāma to Karna.
bhārgavárāghavīya [rāghavīya] amnf bhārgavarāghavīyā about Paraśurāma and Rāma.
bhārṅgī [*bhṛṅga] f. bio. bot. Clerodendrum serratum, a verbena-like plant with clusters of blue flowers, attracting bees; it is used in medicine.
bhārya [pfp. [1] bhr] amnf bhāryā to be maintained or fed — m. servant — f. cf. bhāryā.
bhāryā [f. bhārya] f. wife, woman (also collective lective in the plural). bhāryā bhū to marry (for a woman). gatavati vāyau dehāpāye bhāryā bibhyati tasmin
kāye [Bhajagovindastotra] As soon as the breath has left this body, even the wife is frightened.
bhāla n. front.

bhāv [ca. bhū₁] v. [10] pr. (bhāvayati) pp. )8 (bhāvita) pfp. (bhāvya) to cause to manifest; to produce, create, cause | to encourage, comfort; to animate; to promote; to show, manifest; to consider, recognize, know; to honor — des. (bibhāvayiṣati) to want to create.

bhāva [act. bhū₁] m. existence, presence; mode of being; state, condition | state of mind; disposition; temperament | situation; becoming; transition to, transformation into (loc. iic.) | character, nature, essence; reality; truth | phil. profound reason for an argument | behavior, conduct | psychological disposition, feeling; thought, intention | emotion, heart; inclination, affection, love | bd. the instinct for survival and copulation, 10th cause of suffering [pratītyasamutpāda] | gram. result of the process linked to a verb, state resulting from an action | astr. aspect of a planet | astr. np. of bhāva "Affectionate", That which personifies the 8th year of a life cycle [saṃvatsara] | phil. [Nyāya] discriminatory relation (e.g., pitṛputrabhāva) — ifc. state of (iic.) (e.g., bālabhāva youth). xy bhāva link between x and y. bhāvaṃ kṛ to feel affection for (loc.). bhāvam drdham kr to make a firm resolution. bhāve prayoga gram. impersonal voice (use of an intransitive verb in the passive). iti bhāvaḥ lit. it is so (concludes an explanation in a commentary). anyam bhāvam āpadyate he dies. yādṛśena bhāvena in any state of mind. bhāvo bhāvam nigacchati Like attracts like.

bhāváprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. np. of the Bhāvaprakāśa, a work of poetics in chapters by Sāradātanaya: it is also called Bhāvaprakāśana and Bhāvaprakāśikā | med. [Ayurveda] np. of the Bhāvaprakāśa₁, an encyclopedic treatise on Ayurveda by Bhāvamiśra (1550).
bhāváprakāśikā [prakāśikā] f. bed. n.p. Bhāvaprakāśikā, gloss [tīkā] of the Mahābhāratatātparyanirņaya by Vādirāja.
bhāváMiśra [Miśra] m. hist. n.p. of the physician Bhāvamiśra (Vārāṇasī, 16th century), author of the Bhāvaprakāśa₁.
bhāvamūrti [mūrti] f. soc. [bhakti] imaginary collective lective.
bhāvalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. gram. refers to the absolute locative, quantifying the temporal unfolding of the action; syn. lakṣaṇasaptamī.
bhāvávacana [vacana] n. gram. refers to the dative in finial, expressing an action or a state.
bhāvaśakti [śakti] f. phil. natural efficacy.
bhāvasādhana [sādhana] n. gram. noun of action.
bhāvásvabhāva |svabhāva| mr. phil. nature of being.
bhāvasvabhāvanityatva | nityatva | n. phil. in alterability | "eternity of the nature of being" |.
bhāvātīta |atīta| amnf bhāvātītā phil. very cending.
bhāvānubandha [anubandha] m. faithful love.
bhāvābhāsa [ābhāsa] m. phil. [aesthetics] seeming, pretense of an emotion.
bhāvābhinaya [abhinaya] m. gesture of emotion.
bhāvābhivyañjana [abhivyañjana] n. manifestation of emotion.
bhāvārtha [artha] m. gram. gloss, synthetic meaning of a sentence; opp. śabdārtha.
Bhāvārthadīpikā [dīpikā] f. lit. np. of Bhāvārthadīpikā, classical gloss of the Bhāgavatapurāṇa due to Srīdhara₂ Svāmī.
bhāvaka [agt. ca. bhū₁] amnf bhāvikā Who causes, Who performs | Who imagines (g. iic.) | Who has artistic taste — m. appreciator of a work of art, aesthete | feeling; affection.
bhāvakatva [tva] n. creativity | phil. [aesthetics] ability to reproduce (an emotion).
bhāvatas [adv. bhāva] ifc. adv. as a consequence of being (iic.).
bhāvana [agt. ca. bhū₁] amnf bhāvanī That which produces, That which brings forth; producer, creator — act. n. production, creation — f. cf. bhāvanā. bhāvanam bandh fix the imagination on (loc.).

bhāvanā [f. bhāvana] f. production, creation gram. action expressed by the verb; semantic role of a suffix | lit. language efficiency; creative imagination; vision | phil. mental creation, conception, imagination | phil. [Nyāya] intrinsic cause of perceptions and conceptualizations of the self, an ātmaguņa | phil. [Mīmāṃsā] creative energy as support of the meaning of the sentence in
joint [lin] power of speech in general devotion, faith (in loc. ).
bhāvanātva [tva] n. phil. evocative power.
bhāvanāmaya [maya] amnf bhāvanāmayī pro duit par l'imagination | obtained through meditation.
bhāvanāviveka [viveka] m. bed. n.p. from Bhāvanaviveka, a mīmāmsaka work by Mandana Miśra. )9

bhāvanīya [pfp. [2] ca. bhū₁] amnf bhāvanīyā that which must be performed or undertaken | that which must be endured (suffering); that which must be cherished; that which must be conceived or imagined or supposed; that which must be taught.

bhāvayat [ppr. ca. bhū₁] amnf bhāvayantī becoming, developing; producing, creating. parasparam bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha [BhG.] It is by helping one another that you will attain the supreme goal.
bhāvayitavya [pfp. [3] ca. bhū₁] amnf bhāvayitavyā which must be cherished or protected or raised.

bhāvayitṛ [agt. ca. bhū₁] amnf bhāvayitrī that brings into being; that cherishes, that protects, that raises up | that will call to life — f. bhāvayitrī lit. qua lifies the receptive inspiration of the poet; cf. pratibhā₂.
bhāvāganeśa m. hist. n.p. by bhāvāganeśa dīksita, student of Vijñānabhikṣu, author of the Sāmkhyatattvayāthārthyadīpana.
bhāvi iic. bhāvin.
bhāvitā [tā] f. state of becoming; predestination — ifc. fact of conforming to (iic.).
bhāvitva [tva] n. state of becoming | necessity, inevitability.
bhāvika [bhāvaika] amnf bhāvikā real, natural | sensitive; expressive — n. expressive or passionate language | lit. style of describing the future giving the illusion of the present.
bhāvikatva [tva] n. lit. figure of speech [alaṃkāra] where the future is narrated in the present tense.

bhāvita [pp. ca. bhū₁] amnf bhāvitā created, produced, obtained, manifested; exhibited, simulated; transformed into (i. ic.) | well-disposed, joyful, cheerful; honored | occupied with, devoted to, filled with, absorbed by (i. i. ic.). bhāvitaviṣavegaḥ pretending to be under the influence of poison.

bhāvin [agt. ca. bhū₁] amnf bhāvinī ifc. that which exists, that which becomes, that which is accustomed to being, that which behaves as (iic.) | future; imminent; predestined, inevitable | as it should be, well; ca pable; illustrious | that which manifests, that which exhibits — f. bhāvinī beautiful woman; noble woman.
bhāvuka [bhāvauka] amnf bhāvukā becoming; willing to be | connoisseur — ifc. (after acc.) happy to become — n. happiness, well-being. āḍhyaṃbhāvukaḥ becoming rich.
bhāvyá |pfp. |1| ca. bhū₁| amnf bhāvyā which must be done or accomplished — ifc. intended for (iic.) — n. it must be — m. future. sannhitena bhāvyam you must be present.

√ , ,bhāș v. [1] pr. r. (bhāșate) pft. (babhāșe) pp. (bhāṣita) pfp. (bhāṣya) inf. (bhāṣṭum) pf. (abhi, ava, ā, pari, pra, prati, vi, sam) to speak, to tell, to say something to someone. (2 acc.) — ca. (bhāṣayati) ca. r. (bhāṣayate) to make someone speak.
bhāṣaṇa [act. bhāṣ] n. act of speaking; chatter | kind words, pleasantries | lit. (theatre) expression of satisfaction at having achieved a goal — f. bhāṣaṇā ifc. id.
bhāṣā [obj. bhāṣ] f. speech, spoken language; ordinary, vernacular language. bhāṣāyām gram. [Pāṇini] in everyday language; opp. chandasi.
bhāṣācitraka | citraka | n. wordplay; charade.
bhāṣātraya [traya] n. the 3 languages of India: saṃskṛta, prākṛta, and bhāṣā or more precisely apabhramśa (vernacular).
bhāṣādvaya [dvaya] m. pair of tongues.
bhāṣādvayottara [uttara₁] n. lit. poetic figure of speech, where the word forming the answer is the same in a vernacular language.
Bhāṣāpariccheda [pariccheda] m. lit. np. from the Bhāṣāpariccheda "Judgment on the tongue", Nyāyavaiśesika philosophy manual by Viśvanātha₂, also called Kārikāvalī.
bhāṣāpāda [pāda] m. legal complaint.

Bhāṣāvṛtti [vṛtti] f. gram. np. from the Bhāṣāvṛtti "Gloss (of the grammatical rules) of the language", linguistic treatise by Purusottamadeva; it is a free commentary on the Kāśikā limited to the classical language, and not dealing with accents, but giving many examples.
bhāṣāsama [sama] m. lit. utterance that can be interpreted as saṃskṛta or prākṛta.
bhāṣika [bhāṣāika] amnf bhāṣikā concerning the vernacular language — f. bhāṣikā language; speech.
Bhāṣikasūtra [sūtra] n. gram. n.p. of the Bhāṣikasūtra, collection of rules of accentuation of Satapatha brāhmana.
bhāṣita [pp. bhāṣ] amnf bhāṣitā said, spoken, uttered — n. language; not. vernacular pali bhattha.
bhāṣitapuṃska [puṃska] m. gram. masculine theme line of a feminine word used in composition; cf. puṃvadbhāva. .0
bhāṣitṛ [agt. bhāṣ] amnf bhāṣitrī speaker.
bhāṣin [agt. bhāṣ] amnf bhāṣiṇī Who speaks.

bhāṣya [pfp. [1] bhāṣ] n. word, discourse, commentary, annotation; gloss, interpretation. Lit. not. the śrī Bhāsya, commentary on the Brah masūtra | gram. detailed explanation | vyākhyāna | of a sūtra with refutation of opposing theses; cf. Mahābhāsya. bhāsyam sūtroktārthaprapañcakam [Abhidhānacintāmaṇi] The commentary is a detailed explanation of the meaning of the utterance of an aphorism.
bhāṣyakāra [kāra] m. gram. epith. by Patañjali₁, author of the Mahābhāṣya.
Bhāṣyapradīpa | pradīpa | m. lit. of the np. Bhāsyapradīpa "Light on the gloss", commentary on the Mahābhāṣya due to Kaiyaṭa; cf. Uddyotana.
bhāsyapradīpoddyota | uddyota | m. lit. np. of the Bhāsyapradīpoddyota "Revelation of Light on the Gloss", commentary by Nāgoji Bhaṭṭa of Kaiyata's pradīpa commentary on the Mahābhāsya.

√ bhās₁ [related to bhā₁] v. [1] pr. (bhāsati) pp. (bhāsita) pf. (ava, ā, ut, pra, prati) to shine, to splendor; to appear — pr. r. (bhāsate) to become clear, to become evident or manifest, to be understood — ca. (bhāsayati) ca. r. (bhāsayate) to make shine, to illuminate. yatra yat bhāsate tatra tat nāsti All that shines is not gold.
bhās₁ [agt. bhās₁] f. Light, splendor. tasya bhāsā sarvamidam vibhāti [SU.] From such Light truly all shines forth.
bhāsvat |vat| amnf bhāsvatī brilliant, resplendent — m. Sun; glow; Light — f. bhāsvatī myth. n.p. of bhāsvatī, the resplendent capital of Sūrya.

bhās₁á [agt. bhās₁] m. Light, splendor | phil. mental impression, evocation; imagination | bio. zoo. vulture | hist. np. of Bhāsa, important playwright prior to the 5th century; Thirteen plays [nāṭaka] are attributed to him: the Pratijñāyaugandharāyana, the Svapnavāsavadatta and the Avimāraka are taken from the Brhatkathā, the Pratimānāṭaka and the Abhiṣeka from the Rāmāyaṇa, the Madhyamavyāyoga, Pañcarātra, Dūtavākya, Dūtaghatotkaca, Karnabhāra and Urubhanga from the Mahābhārata, the Bālacarita is based on the story of Kṛṣṇa as a child, and the Cārudatta₁ is taken from the folk lore — ifc. semblance of, illusion of; evocation of (iic.).
bhāsura [contr. bhāsvara] amnf bhāsurā brilliant, dazzling; splendid — ifc. excellent in, distinguished by (iic.).
Bhāsuraka [ka] m. lit. [PT.] np. of the lion Bhāsuraka, cruel and stupid; a rabbit persuaded him that he had a rival, inciting him to jump into a well.
bhāsuratva |tva| n. splendor.

Bhāskara [bhās₁kara₁] amnf bhāskarā Who illuminates, bright, luminous — m. the Sun | myth. np. of Bhāskara, epith. of Sūrya "Who illuminates" | hist. np. of the philosopher Bhāskara₁ "Lightly Light" (9th century), author of the Bhāskarabhāsya Sārīrakamīmāmsābhāsya, commentary on the Brah masūtra; he professed the bhedābhedavāda doctrine in its aupādhika form, rejected the theory of illusion [māyā] and believed in evolution [parināma]; he is also credited with the commentary Bhagavadgītābhāsya | lit. np. of the logician Bhāskara₂; cf. Laugākṣi | lit. np. of the philosopher Bhāskara₃ Dīkṣita (17th century) cf. Bhāskarācārya cf. bhāskarakantha.
Bhāskarakaṇṭha [kaṇṭha] m. hist. n.p. of the Shaivite philosopher of Kaśmīra Bhāskarakantha (18th century), author of the Cittānubodhaśāstra and the Moksopāyatīkā.
bhāskarabhāsya [bhāsya] n. bed. n.p. of bhāskarabhāṣya, a gloss of Brahmasūtra due to Bhāskara₁; cf. Sārīrakamīmāṃsābhāsya.
Bhāskararāya [rāya] m. hist. np. of Bhāskararāya, 18th century scholar, specialist in the cult of Sakti; he is the author not. of the Setubandha₂.
bhāskaravarman [varman] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of the young prince of Vidarbha Bhāskaravarmā, brother ca det of Mañjuvādinī; he was taken in by his cousin Viśruta.

Bhāskarācārya [ācārya] m. hist. np. of Bhāskarācārya, 9th century philosopher; cf. Bhāskara₁ hist. np. of Bhāskarācārya₁, 6th century mathematician | hist. np. of Bhāskarācārya₂, 12th century mathematician and astronomer (1114–1185); he directed the Ujjayinī observatory; he is the author of the Siddhāntaśiromaņi.
bhāsvara [bhās₁vara] amnf bhāsvarī brilliant, Resplendent | myth. np. of bhāsvara "Resplendent", a servant of Sūrya.
bhikṣ [des. bhaj] v. pr. r. (bhikṣate) pft. (bibhikṣe) pp. (bhikṣita) to ask something (acc. g.) .1 to ask someone (acc. abl.) | to beg, to seek, to ask for alms.
bhikṣā [act. des. bhaj] f. begging; almsgiving. bhiksām because to ask for alms; to beg. kṛṣito nāsti bhikṣām He who works the land has no need to beg.
bhikṣācara [cara] amnf bhikṣācarī beggar.

bhikṣātana [aṭana] n. state of wandering beggar — m. myth. np. of Bhikṣāṭana, epith. of Shiva "Who wanders as a beggar"; naked, he begs for his food in a skullcap; cf. Dārukavana | arch. it is one of the 16 aspects of Shiva.
bhikṣārtha [artha] m. mendicancy; alms.
bhikṣārthin [in] amnf bhikṣārthinī men diant.

bhikṣu [agt. des. bhaj] m. mendicant | soc. man at the 4th stage of brahmanic life [āśrama], wandering beggar, ascetic; the associated puruṣārtha is mokṣa; cf. sannyāsin | bd. Buddhist monk, living on alms || pali bhikkhu.
bhikṣuka [ka] m. soc. wandering beggar; not. brah mane of a mendicant order — f. bhikṣukī soc. men diante | bd. Buddhist nun.
bhikṣuṇī |nī| f. bd. Buddhist nun.
bhikṣuṇīsaṅga [saṅga] m. bd. congregation of Buddhist nuns; it is extinct today.
Bhikṣusūtra [sūtra] n. lit. np. of the Bhikṣusūtra, a collection of monastic rules promulgated by Parāśara.
bhittí [act. bhid₂] f. (separation) wall, rail, partition; panel.
bhitticaura [caura] m. burglar.
bhitticcheda | cheda | mr. breach in a wall.
bhittirekhā [rekhā] f. graffiti.

√ bhid₂ v. [7] pr. (bhinátti) pr. r. (bhintté) fut. (bhetsyati) pft. (bibheda) aor. [1] (abhidyāt) aor. [2] (abhidat) aor. [4] (abhaitsīt) pp. (bhinna) pfp. (bhedya, bhidya) abs. (bhittvā) pf. (ut, nis, pra, prati, vi, sam) to split, break, pierce, fracture; violate; separate, interrupt; destroy — ps. (bhidyate) to split — ca. (bhedayati) ca. r. (bhedayate) to split, break; destroy; divide; conquer — dés. (bíbhitsati) dés. r. (bíbhitsate) to want to break; to want to scatter; to want to conquer lat. findere; all. beissen; ang. to bite; fr. fendre. sūtram tarhi bhidyate gram. if this is the case, the rule must be formulated differently. sodaśake dravyagane caturvikalpena bhi dyamānānām aṣṭādaśa jāyante śatāni sahitāni 7.
bhid₂ [act. bhid₂] ifc. amnf That which pierces, That which splits, That which destroys.
vimśatyā [BS.] Dividing 16 objects into groups of 4 gives 1820 combinations.
bhidaka [agt. bhid₂] m. ["That cuts"] mythical sword. Indra's thunderbolt.
bhidā [act. bhid₂] f. act of piercing; of truction, bursting | distinction; separation, difference.
bhidura [bhid₂ra] amnf bhidurā That which breaks, That which pierces, That which destroys (iic.) | brittle, fragile.
bhidya [pfp. [1] bhid₂] amnf bhidyā That destroys — f. bhidyā impetuous river.
bhindat [ppr. bhid₂] amnf bhindatī cas sant, piercing, destroying.

bhindipāla [bhid₂pāla] m. javelin | catapult. ਮਿਸ਼ bhinná [pp. bhid₂] amnf bhinnā split, broken, fractured, destroyed; wounded by (i. ii.) | transgressed, violated | divided into parts; burst | disturbed, interrupted; changed, altered | detached; free | separated, differentiated; seduced, corrupted distinct, different from (i. ii. abl) | mixed with (i. ii.) — m. math. fraction — n. fragment, piece | stab wound, stab wound — f. bhinnā bio. bot. Sansevieria roxburghiana, a type of agave; cf. mūrvā. śarabhinnah pierced by an arrow. bhinno'stadhā divided into 8 parts. He is not wise who never changes his mind.
bhinnákata | kata | m. elephant in rut | "whose temples have burst".
bhinnákarata [karata] m. id.
bhinnakarīndrakumbha | karīndrakumbha | m. war elephant in rut. bhinnakarīndrakumbhamuktāmaya makes pearls falling from the frontal humps of war elephants in rut.
bhinnakrama [krama] amnf bhinnakramā gram. whose (normal) order is broken.

bhinnáruci [ruci] amnf Who has a different or varied taste. bhinnarucir hi lokaḥ [Ragh.] All tastes are in nature. athāngarājād avatārya cakṣur yāhīti janyām ava dat kumārī | nāsau na ramyo na ca veda samyag drastum na sa bhinnarucir hi lokaḥ || But the princess (Indumatī) turned her gaze away from the king of the Aṅgās and said to the servant, "not this one"; it was not that he was not a handsome boy, nor that she did not see him correctly, but one does not argue about tastes and colors.
bhinnávarga [varga] m. math. square of a fraction. bhinnávarņa [varṇa] amnf bhinnavarṇā discolored; pale | soc. of a different caste or tribe.
bhinnávrtta [vrtta] amnf bhinnavrttā who forgets his duties; who leads a dissolute life.
bhinnávrtti [vrtti] amnf having various occupations; of a different profession cf. bhinnavṛtta.
bhilla m. geo. name of a montagnous tribal race of the Vindhya mountains | soc. horscaste; son of a śabara and an andhrī — f. bhillī woman of bhilla race.

bhillama m. hist. np. of King Bhillama, of the Yādavās dynasty; he founded the city of Devagiri, where he reigned from 1187 to 1191; he was defeated by Ballala II (1173-1220), son of Narasimha I; his son Jaitugi succeeded him. মিষ্ডা bhiṣáj m. [nom. bhiṣak] physician, healer — v. [11] pr. (bhiṣajyáti) pp. (bhiṣajyita) to treat (med.); to cure | to be a remedy for, to be master of loc. .
bhişajya [bhişajya] amnf bhişajyā that heals; wholesome; healthy, in good health.
bhiṣajyitá [pp. bhiṣaj] amnf bhişajyitā guéri.

√ bhī₁ v. [3] pr. (bibheti) aor. [4] (abhaiṣīt) pp. (bhīta) pfp. (bhetavya, bheya) pf. (vi) to fear (abl. g.); to be frightened of — ca. (bhīṣáyati) ca. r. (bhīṣáyate) ca. (bhāyáyati) ca. r. (bhāyáyate) to frighten, to frighten, to terrify | gr. φοβος; all. beben; fr. phobie. mābhaiṣīḥ var. mābhaiḥ do not be afraid. bibhīmas tava [Mah.] we are afraid of you.
bhī₁ [act. bhī₁] f. fear, dread, fright, terror. yuṣmat bhiyā out of fear of you.
bhīta [pp. bhī₁] amnf bhītā frightened, terrified. na bhīto maraṇādasmi I am not afraid of death.
bhīti [act. bhī₁] f. fear, dread, terror. bhītitas adv. of fear. bhītiḥ māstu do not be afraid.

bhīmá [bhī₁ma] amnf bhīmā formidable; terrible, dreadful, awesome — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Bhīma₁ "Terrifying", brother of Arjuna; cf. Bhīmasena | myth. epith. of RudraŚiva | myth. |Mah.| np. of king Bhīma₁ of the Vidarbha country, father of Damayantī, Dama, Dānta and Damana₁ | hist. np. of king Cālukya Bhīma₁ (892–921); he had the temple of bhīmeśvara built at Dakṣārāma cf. Bhīmadeva.

Bhīmadeva [deva] m. hist. np. of King Solankī Bhīmadeva I, successor of Mūlarāja; he reigned at Anahilapātaka (1022–1064); he built a temple at Sūrya at mod. Modhera; his chief general Vimala Shah built at Arbuda₁ the first of 5 Jain marble temples, dedicated to Rṣabhanātha (1031); his wife Queen Udayamatī had the stepped well Rāṇī kī vāva built in his memory; his successor is Karnadeva.

bhīmadhanvan [dhanvan] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Prince Bhīmadhanvā, son of King Tungadhanvā; he was in love with Candrasenā, whom he held captive; he had Mitragupta thrown into the sea, who eventually drowned him.
bhīmaparākrama [parākrama] m. courage or terrible strength — amnf bhīmáparākramā to formidable heroism.
Bhīmaratha | ratha | m. myth. np. of King Bhīmaratha "of the terrible chariot", son of Ketumān, father of Divodāsa.
Bhīmaśankara [śankara] m. geo. np. of Bhīmaśańkara, one of the 12 radiant signs of Shiva [jyotirlinga], established near Pune in Maharashtra.

Bhīmasena [senā] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Bhīmasena "of the terrible weapon" alias Bhīma₁, second of the 5 Pāṇḍavās, son of the god Vāyu and Kuntī; he is endowed with prodigious strength; he possessed the conch Paundra; he killed the rākṣasās Baka₁, Kirmīra and Hidimba; he united with the sister Hidimbā of the latter, who gave birth to the monster Ghatotkaca; during the exile of the Pāṇḍavās to the court of King Virāta, he hid as the cook Ballava; he massacred the general Kīcaka to defend the honor of Drau padī; during the great battle he killed Duḥśāsana, whose blood he had sworn to drink; at the end of the battle, he fought Duryodhana in single combat with a club and broke his thigh, fulfilling his vow to avenge the insult made to Draupadī, but provoking the anger of Balarāma by this disloyal blow, unworthy of a kṣatriya; when Dharmarāja decided their renunciation [tyāga], he followed his brothers in their march towards Heaven, but died on the way, his dharma not being perfect, for he was gluttonous [Vṛkodara] and selfish; cf. Ballava.
bhīmācārya [ācārya] m. hist. n.p. by mahāmahopādhyāya bhīmācārya Jhallakīkara author of Nyāyakośa (19th century).
bhīmeśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of the śivalinga .3 Bhīmeśvara, established in Dakṣārāma, of great height (2.6 m).

Bhīmeśvarapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. from the Bhīmeśvarapurāṇa of Srīnātha, a poem glorifying the Dakṣārāma; the narrator, Vyāsa, tells Agas tya, whom he met on the banks of the Tulyabhāga, that he was banished from Kāśī by Viśvanātha for having almost cursed the city for three generations under the worst of famine; he took refuge in the Dakṣārāma where Agastya shows him Bhīmeśvara who grants him his grace; During the churning of the ocean of milk [kṣīrodamathana], Nīlakantha had established himself as Bhīmeśvara at Dakṣārāma; there, the asurās prayed to Siva to grant them power and glory, and tormented the gods from their triple city of metal |Tripura|, where they worshipped a great linga; at the request of the gods, Mahādeva destroyed their fortress with a single arrow which was Vișnu; the linga , broken into 5 parts, was distributed among the 5 garden shrines in the land of Andhra |pañcārāmakṣetra|; for their ritual installation, the sages went in search of Vyāsa whom they found at Dakṣārāma with Agastya; Sūrya ins talla Bhīmeśvara, then went to Kailāsa to pray that Siva would incorporate himself entirely into the linga.
bhīrú [Bhī₁ru] amnf bhīrū timid, fearful, timid; cowardly | who fears, intimidated by (abl. iic.) — voc. bhīru f. adr. Mademoiselle (graceful way of approaching a young woman).
bhīruka |ka| amnf bhīrukā timid, fearful; fearful; one who fears (iic.).
bhīrutva |tva| n. timidity; fear of (iic.).
bhīṣ [ca. Bhī₁] v. [10] pr. r. (bhīṣayate) to frighten, to scare, to terrify.
bhīṣaṇa [agt. ca. Bhī₁] amnf bhīṣaṇā ter rible, appalling, horrible — m. lit. the feeling of horror | myth. epith. of Bhairava — act. n. act of terror — f. bhīṣaṇā myth. epith. of Nirṛti.
bhīṣaṇatva [tva] n. state of being terrifying.
bhīṣaṇīya [īya] amnf bhīṣaṇīyā terrifying; horrible.
bhīṣaṇaka [agt. That. Bhī₁] amnf bhīsanikā terrifying; horrible.
bhīṣā [act. ca. Bhī₁] f. act of frightening; intimidation — adv. out of fear of abl. .

bhīṣmá [bhīṣma] amnf bhīṣmā terrible, frightening — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of bhīṣma "the terrible", nickname of Prince Devavrata, eldest son of King Sāmtanu and the goddess Gangā, and as such, gift of Heaven [devadatta]; he is the incarnation of the vasu Heaven [Dyau]; his guru being Parasurāma, he became invincible in arms; to allow his father to marry the beautiful Satyavatī by promising to make her the heir to the kingdom, he renounced the throne and took a vow of brahmacarya; his father rewarded him by giving him the power to choose the hour of his death; after the tragic death of the first heir Citrāngada, he placed the young Vici travīrya on the throne; At his majority, he chose his wives by abducting the daughters of the king of Kāśi during a svayamvara ceremony; the eldest, Ambā, being promised to King Śālva, he married Vicitravīrya to the two younger daughters Ambikā₁ and Ambālikā₁; for having caused the repudiation of Ambā, Paraśurāma fought him unsuccessfully in a titanic battle of 23 days; at the death of Vicitravīrya without an heir, he married the two widows to the ascetic Vyāsa whom Satyavatī had once borne to the sage [ṛṣi] Parāśara; the eldest of this union Dhṛtarāṣṭra being blind, he crowned the younger son Pāṇḍu; When he renounced the throne, the kingdom was contested between his 5 sons, the Pāṇḍavās, and their cousins Kauravās, led by Duryodhana, eldest son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; bhīṣma, the invincible pa triarch of the Kauravās, and their commander-in-chief, was mortally wounded by Arjuna accompanied by Sikhaṇḍī, because he did not want to fight a woman (reincarnation of Ambā); he waited for the end of the war, lying on his bed of arrows, to die at the uttarāyaṇa, after having dispensed his wisdom to the Pāndavās.
bhīṣmápañcaka [pañcaka] n. soc. 5 sacred days to Bhīşma (from the 11th to the 15th day of the clear fortnight of the month kārttika ).

bhīsmápañcakavrata [vrata] n. soc. observance followed during this period. Bhīşmáparvan [parvan] n. lit. np. from the Bhīşmaparva, 6th book of the Mah., "dealing with bhīṣma"; it recounts the battles and death of the patriarch.
Bhīṣmastavarāja [stavarāja] m. lit. np. of the Bhīṣmastavarāja "hymn of praise to Kṛṣṇa of bhīṣma (dying on his bed of arrows)", episode of the Mah. [1247].

bhīṣmastuti [stuti] f. lit. [BhP.] hymn of praise to Kṛṣṇa by bhīṣma. Bhīşmāştamī [aṣṭamī] f. soc. 8th day of the bright fortnight of the month māgha; it is a festival in honor of bhīṣma, who chose this day for his death; the funeral service ekoddista śrāddha is celebrated on it.

Bhīṣmaka [bhīṣmaka] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Bhīşmaka, father of Rukmī and Rukmiņī; he reigned over Vidarbha. ਮੁੱ Bhu [agt. bhū₂] ifc. amnf that which becomes, that which is (11th century); produced by (11th century).
bhukta [pp. bhuj₁] amnf bhuktā that has been enjoyed or used; possessed; eaten — ifc. that feeds on (iic.) — n. food, meal; enjoyment. bhuktavibhuktam half eaten.
bhuktaśesa | Sesa | n. leftover meals.
bhukti [act. bhuj₁] f. profit, possession, consumption; pleasure, enjoyment, usufruct; vic tuailles | phil. attachment to profane pleasures; opp. mukti | astr. path of a celestial object.
bhugna [pp. bhuj₁] amnf bhugnā bent, twisted; furrowed (eyebrows).
√ bhuj₁ v. [6] pr. (bhuj₁áti) pft. (bubhoja) pp. (bhugna) to bend, to fold, to bend, to twist | gr. φευγω; lat. fugio; all. biegen.

√ bhuj₁ v. [7] pr. r. (bhuṅkté) pft. (bubhoja) pp. (bhukta) ppr. r. (bhuñjāna) inf. (bhoktum) pfp. (bhoktavya, bhogya, bhojya) pf. (anu, upa, sam) to enjoy, possess (acc.); to enjoy carnally | to eat, taste; to drink | to use, employ, exploit; to experience — v. [7] pr. (bhunákti) to serve, assist, protect (acc.) | to govern, rule — ca. (bhojáyati) ca. (bhuñjāpayati) to nourish; to feed someone (acc.) with something (acc. i.) — des. (bubhukṣati) to desire to eat or possess | lat. fungor, fructus; fr. fruit. bhavān bhunaktu it's time to eat. bhojam bhojam vrajati he walks after gorging himself. udarapūram bhunkte he eats his fill.
bhuj₁ [agt. bhuj₁] ifc. amnf [nom. bhuk] who enjoys, who loves, who eats (iic.) | who governs, who rules (iic.).
bhuja [agt. bhuj₁] m. arm; elephant trunk; tree trunk — f. bhujā curve, fold; coil of a snake | math. side of a geometric figure | math. symb. the number 2. bhujais tr. to swim across.
bhujaga [ga₁] m. snake ["that snakes"] — f. bhujagī female snake.
bhujabalanibandha | balanibandha | mr. bed. n.p. of Bhujabalanibandha, a work of astrology and ritual attributed to King Bhojarāja.

bhujam [acc. bhuja] iic. bhujamga var. Bhujanga [ga₁] m. snake | soc. companion of debauchery; not. dissolute companion of a prince; libertine; lover; pimp | myth. n.p. of the snake genius [nāga] Bhujaṅga | math. symb. the number 8 math. side of a polygon; not. base of a triangle.
bhujamgaprayāta [prayāta] n. phone. meter of the “gait of the cobra”. bhujamgaprayātam caturbhiryakāraih the bhujamgaprayāta meter consists of four bacchaea (11011011011).
bhujamgavijrmbhita [vijrmbhita] m. meter of the "elongated cobra".
bhujamgama [gama] m. snake.
bhujābhuji [red. bhuja] adv. ["arm to arm"] in unarmed combat.
bhujiṣyá [fut. bhuj₁] m. servant — f. bhujişyā servant.

bhujyú [bhuj₁yu] amnf rich, opulent ved. |RV.| np. of Prince Bhujyu, "the opulent", son of King Tugra; |Sāyaṇa| his father sent him to sea to attack his enemies who had taken refuge on a distant island; having been shipwrecked at sea, he implored the Aśvinau who saved him from drowning.
bhuñjāna [ppr. mo. bhuj₁] amnf bhuñjānā who eats.
bhuruṇḍa m. lit. [PT.] np. of bhuruṇḍa, oi fabulous bucket with two heads; cf. Bhāruṇḍa.
bhúva |bhuvas| mr. myth. n.p. of Bhuva, epith. of Agni the “Uncreated” — n. atmosphere — ifc. cf. Bhu.

bhúvana |act. bhū₁| n. living being, human being, humanity | universe, earth, one of the 3 worlds | tribhuvana | math. symb. the number 14 (7 worlds [loka] and 7 hells [pātāla]) — m. the earth, the World.
Bhuvanakośa [kośa] m. bed. n.p. of Bhuvanakośa, work by Rājaśekhara on the geography of India.
bhuvanagiri [kośa] m. geo. n.p. from the town of Bhuva nagiri, near Cidambaram in Tamil Nadu; it is the birthplace of śrī Rāghavendra Svāmī.
bhuvanatala | tala | n. surface of the earth.
hastasthitasakalabhuvanatalam | K. | Holding the whole earth in his hand.
bhúvanatraya | traya | n. the three worlds, the Uni vers; syn. tribhuvana. svadeśo bhuvanatrayam The universe is our homeland.
bhuvanadīpaka [dīpaka] m. astr. n.p. from the Bhuva nadīpaka, a jyotisa work by Padmaprabha₁ Sūri; Simhatilaka Sūri made a commentary [vṛtti] on it in 1269.
bhuvanapati [pati] m. phil. ved. the Master of the World.
bhuvanapradīpa [pradīpa] m. lit. np. from the Bhu vanapradīpa, a treatise on architecture, notably for the construction of temples. .5
bhuvanavijaya [vijaya] n. hist. n.p. of the Bhuvana vijaya, court of poets of Emperor Kṛṣṇadeva Rāya in Vijayanagara; cf. astadiggaja.
bhuvanābhyudaya [abhyudaya] m. bed. n.p. from Bhu vanābhyudaya "Triumph of the World", court poem by śrī Saṅkuka (c. 850).

bhuvaneśvara [īśvara] m. myth. n.p. from Bhu vaneśvara, epith. of Šiva "Lord of the Universe" — f. bhuvaneśvarī phil. [Tantra] n.p. of bhuvaneśvarī, one of the 10 powers [mahāvidyā] of the Goddess [Sakti] | geo. n.p. of bhuvaneśvarī₁, sacred city of KalingaUtkala (mod. Bhubaneśvar, capital of Orissa); cf. Lingarāja.
bhuvanopari [upari] adv. ved. above the World. ayam viśvāni tiṣṭhati | punāno bhuvanopari | somo devo na sūryaḥ | ved. [RV.] This hurried soma stands above the World like the god Sūrya.
bhuvas [VOC. pl. bhū₂] ind. air, atmosphere
bhuvar [bhuvarloka] myth. np. of bhuvar the "Between heaven and earth", Celestial world [loka] intermediate, where the accomplished [siddhās] dwell; cf. lokatraya, vyāhrti.

bhuśuṇḍī f. kind of weapon | var. bhuśuṇḍi id. — m. bhuśuṇḍa myth. [YV.] np. of the raven Bhuśuṇḍa, a sage of very great age living in the kalpavrkṣa Cūṭa in Indra's paradise; Vasiṣṭha having visited him, he recounted his birth from an orgy where the sacred geese of Brāhmī united with the beautiful horn Canda₂, mount of the mātrkā Alambuṣā₁; he explained to him that his extreme longevity was due to the practice of meditation, and the control of his senses; Vasistha transmitted his teaching to Rāma.

√ bhū₁ v. [1] pr. (bhávati) imp. (bhava) opt. (bhavet) fut. (bhaviṣyati) fut. péri. (bhavitā) pft. (babhūva) aor. [1] (abhūt) cond. (abhaviṣyat) pp. (bhūta) ppr. (bhavat₁) pfp. (bhavanīya, bhavita vya, bhavya, bhāvya) abs. (bhūtvā, bhūya) pf. (ati, anu, abhi, ā, āvis, ut, tiras, parā, pari, pra, bahis, vi, sam) to occur, to take place | to become, to be born | to be, to exist, to be found (to be becoming, opp. as₁ to be realized) | to belong to — ps. (bhūyate) to be created — ca. (bhāvayati) pp. (bhāvita) pfp. (bhāvya) to cause to appear; to produce, create, cause | to encourage, comfort; to recognize, honor — intens. (bóbhoti) intens. (bobhavīti) intens. r. (bóbhūyáte) to be frequently, to be accustomed to | to be transformed into (acc.) — des. (búbhūṣati) des. r. (bubhūṣate) to want to become || gr. ; lat. fui; ang. to be; all. bin; fr. physique. 7. bhavatu adv. be it! well then! deal struck (marks a resolution taken). abhavisyat in the event that; supposing that; if. krtavān bhavisyati you will have done. evam bhavatu so be it. yadbhāvi tadbhavatu come what may. bhavati bhavān yājayisyati it is possible that you may be able to perform a sacrifice. anuvaksyan bhavati he will recite. kim bhāvayet [Mīmāṃsā] what must be done? kena bhāvayet by what means can it be done? katham bhāvayet how should it be done? idam pādodakam bhaviṣyati this will serve as water for washing the feet. ਮੁ bhū₂ [bhū₁] f. [sg. nom. acc. bhūs bhuvam, i. bhuvā, dat. bhuve bhuvai, abl. g. bhuvas bhuvās, loc. bhuvi bhuvām; du. nom. acc. bhuvau, i. dat. abl. bhūbhyām, g. loc. bhuvos; pl. nom. acc. Bhu vas, i. bhūbhis, dat. abl. bhūbhyas, g. bhuvām, loc. bhūṣu] the earth; soil, terrain | region, place, location | the act of becoming or appearing — ind. bhūr |bhūrloka| myth. np. of bhū the earth, first celestial world |loka|; cf. lokatraya, vyāhṛti pl. bhuvas the worlds; VOC. cf. bhuvas — loc. bhuvi adv. on earth. bhūr bhuvar svar by the earth, the worlds and the sky (ritual exclamation |vyāhṛti|); cf. Prajāpati. rahobhuvi adv. in a secret place | in private.
bhūgrha | grha | n. underground dwelling | "gateway" of a mystical diagram [yantra], at the four cardinal points.
bhūgola [gola] m. terrestrial globe; the earth.
bhūcara [cara] amnf bhūcarī who walks or inhabits the earth — f. bhūcarī bd. [Tantra] np. of bhūcarī, earth goddess of the triad of the three worlds; cf. Khecarī, Pātālavāsinī.
bhūtala [tala] n. ground; the earth.
bhūtṛṇa |tṛṇa| mr. cf. bhūstṛṇa.
Bhūdevī [devī] f. np. of Bhūdevī, the nourishing earth, wife of Vișnu.
bhūdhara |dhara| m. myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa “that which supports the earth” | mountain.
bhūdharaja [ja] m. ["born in the mountain"] tree.
bhūpati | pati | m. king | "master of the earth" |.
bhūpāla [pāla] m. king ["guardian of the earth"].
bhūbhuj [bhuj₃] m. king, prince ["who rules the land"].
bhūbhṛt | bhṛt | mr. king | mountain.
bhūrāla [rāla] m. lava. .6
bhūruh [ruh₂] m. ["that grows from the earth"] plant, tree.
bhūruha |ruha| m. id.
bhūlinga [linga] m. organic. bhūlinga bird; cf. bhūlingaśakuni.
bhūlinganyāya | nyāya | m. lit. maxim of the plon geon, who does not follow his own principles, for his cry is mā sāhasam "no recklessness", while he is in the company of crocodiles.
bhūlingaśakuni |śakuni| mr. organic. zoo. Pluvianus aegyptius, Nile loon; he cleans the crocodiles.

bhūsvarga [svarga] m. paradise on earth | myth. epith. of Mt Sumeru — v. [11] pr. r. (bhūsvargāyate) to become a paradise on earth. bhūsvargāyamānametatsthalam var. bhūlokagataḥ svargah this land is a paradise on earth.

bhūtá [pp. bhū₁] amnf bhūtā been; become, that which existed, that which occurred; past; true, real — ifc. that which has become, that which is like, that which consists of (iic.) — n. living being, soul, creature | myth. spirit, phantom, genie | phil. |Sāṃkhya| cf. bhūtatattva | phil. |Vaiśeṣika| cf. bhūtadravya | math. symb. the number 5 — m. myth. spirit of a deceased person, specter; the bhūtās are a class of malevolent beings. ... bhūta being ...

bhūtatattva | tattva | n. phil. |Sāṃkhya | gross element [tattva]; there are 5 of them [pañcabhūtāni]: ākāśa the Ether or Space, vāyu the Air or Wind, tejas the Fire, ap the Water and pṛthivī the earth; they derive from the 5 perceptions [tanmātra]; cf. sūkṣmabhūta, sthūlabhūta.
bhūtatva [tva] n. (past) event.
bhūtadāha |dāha| m. destruction of creatures.
bhūtadāhīya |īya| amnf bhūtadāhīyā ca pable de détruire des créatures.
bhūtadravya [dravya₁] n. phil. [Vaiśeṣika] sub
stance | dravya₁ | tangible; there are 5 of them: earth [pṛthivī], Waters [āpas], Fire [tejas], Air [vāyu], Ether |ākāśa|.
bhūtadhāra |dhāra₁| amnf bhūtadhārā that keeps in mind, that remembers — f. bhūtadhārā the earth ["base of the elements"] | bhūtadhārinī id.
bhūtánātha [nātha] m. myth. np. of Bhūtanātha, epith. of Shiva "Lord of creatures".
bhūtabhavyá [bhavya] n. sg. (collective) the past and the future.
bhūtabhavyabhavat | bhavat₁ | n. the past, the future and the present.
bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhu | prabhu | m. myth. master of the past, future and present; Nahuşa boasted of being so.
bhūtabhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. lit. ["language of spirits"] qualifies the presumed language of the Bṛhatkathā, also called paiśācī .

bhūtabhāṣāmaya [maya] afmn bhūtabhāṣāmayī composed in paiśācī. bhūtabhāṣāmayīṃ tu āhur adbhutārthā Bṛhatkathā |Kāvyādarśa| It is said that the admirable Brhatkathā was composed in the language of spirits.
bhūtayajña [yajña] m. [SB.] ved. sacrifice to the bhūtās spirits, one of the five major rites |mahāyajña|; cf. bali.
bhūtalipi [lipi] f. gram. [Tantra] "alphabet of the elements", a particular arrangement of the Sanskrit alphabet (without long vowels) associated with the evolution of material elements.
bhūtavikriyā [vikriyā] f. possession by evil spirits; epilepsy.
bhūtavijñāna [vijñāna] n. spiritualism; demonology.
bhūtavidyā [vidyā] f. phil. Spiritism or the science of spirits, a literary genre.

bhūtasaṃkhya [saṃkhya] m. chronogram, system of numeration by analogy; e.g. abhra, ambara, ākāśa, kha, gagana, bindu, viyat, vyoman or śūnya for 0, ādi, indu, ka₂, can dra, bhūmi, rūpa or soma for 1, akṣi, ne tra, locana, pakṣa, aśvin, dasra, phaṇīndra, dos, dosan, bhuja, yama₂ or yamala for 2, agni, krama, guņa, grāma, bhuvana, mūrti, rāma or loka for 3, veda, yuga, varņa, abdhi, ambudhi, koņa, śruti, samudra₁ or ambhāṃsi for 4, in driya, bhūta, putra, pavana, vāyu, śara, iṣu or suta₂ for 5, anga₁, rtu, rasa, darśana, or tarka for 6, sindhu, adri, turaga/turamga, giri/parvata, śaila, mahīdhra, muni/ṛṣi, svara or aśva for 7, anuṣṭubh₂, kumbhin, gaja/ibha/mataṃgaja, sarpa/bhujamga, mangala, vasu or siddhi for 8, chidra, randhra, graha, nanda, nidhi, kha cara/nabhaścara, anka, pīṭha or saṃkhyā₂ for 9, āśā₁/diśā, avatāra or rāvaṇaśiras for 10, maheśvara or rudra for 11, āditya, arka, māsa or ravi/sūrya for 12, viśve for 13, manu, indra or bhuvana for 14, tithi for 15, kalā for 16, dhrti for 18, krti for 20, tattva for 25, bha for 27, rada or danta for 32, deva/sura for 33; this system is notably used by Varāhamihira. śūnyarasa math. 60. śarayamarasa math. 625.
śrutīndriyarasair [stela] in the year 654 (from the śāka₃ era).
bhūtārtha [artha] m. deed that took place, real deed. .7
bhūtārthavāda [vāda] m. phil. realism; materialism.
bhūtāvāsa [āvāsa] m. myth. | "refuge" of creatures"] epith. of Vișnu or Siva | bio. bot. Terminalia bellirica, false myrobalan; syn. vibhītaka.
Bhūtāsana |āsana| n. lit. |KSS.| np. of the Bhūtāsana air chariot, built by Sūryaprabha₁ with the help of Maya.
bhūteśa |īśa| m. myth. np. of bhūteśa "Master of spirits", epith. of Brahmā, Kṛṣṇa or Siva.
bhūtokti | ukti | f. phil. infallible divine word.
bhūti [act. bhū₁] f. existence, well-being | happiness, prosperity, fortune, success; salvation.
bhūmá ifc. bhūman. dhruvāya bhūmāya namah Homage to the eternal earth.

bhūman [bhū₁man] n. the earth, the World | territory, soil, land; country, region — m. fullness, abundance; wealth; multitude | phil. [Vedānta] the infinite | gram. plural — ifc. filled with (iic.). bhūmnā adv. generally, in general. bhūmni adv. gram. in the plural.

Bhūmi [bhū₁] f. earth, soil, terrain | place, spot, terroir; location, ground; position, post, location; plan | floor | myth. np. of Bhūmi the earth | role, character | math. symb. the number 1 | math. base of a triangle; opp. bhuja | lit. np. of the [khaṇḍa] Bhūmi section of a purāṇa dealing with myths taking place on earth | bd. stage of perfection; there are 10 or 13 | |vihārabhūmi| bd. stage of perfection of a bodhisattva — ifc. object proper to, receptacle of (iic.) || lat. humus. bhūmau adv. on the ground.
bhūmigṛha [gṛha] n. underground chamber; dungeon; vault — amnf bhūmigṛhā ["whose earth is the residence" death.
bhūmicchattra | chatra | n. mushroom.
bhūmicchidra [chidra] n. clearing, first cultivation of the land.
bhūmicchidranyāya [nyāya] m. soc. right of the land to the one who cultivates it first.
bhūmija [ja] amnf bhūmijā from the earth; born of the ground — m. astr. n.p. from bhūmija "earth-born", a name for Mars; cf. Angāraka, Kuja, Mangala.
bhūmipa [pa₂] m. king ["protector of the earth"].
bhūmipati [pati] m. king ["master (or husband) of the earth".
bhūmipatitva [tva] n. royalty.
bhūmipāla |pāla| mr. king | “protector of the earth” | Thai Bhumibol.
bhūmipūjā [pūjā] f. soc. rite of consecration of the ground of a building, not. of a temple.
bhūmibhāga [bhāga] m. land; portion of land; location.
bhūmimat [mat] amnf bhūmimatī who owns land.
bhūmivarga [varga] m. bed. section of the bhūmyādikāṇḍa, dealing with nature.
bhūmisāt [sāt] ind. flattened, shaved (with kṛ₁).
Bhūmisuta [suta₂] m. np. of Bhūmisuta, epith. of Mangala "son of the earth".
bhūmisparśa | sparśa | m. touching the earth.

bhūmisparśamudrā [mudrā] f. bd. gesture of the "touch dear of the earth", by which Buddha took the earth to witness his merits at the time of his Enlightenment (represented in padmāsana, right hand on the right knee, fingers extended touching the ground).

bhūmihāra [hāra₁] m. soc. class of landowners of the Indo-Angetic plains; they are descendants of Brahmins converted to Buddhism under Aśoka; they make donations, but do not beg, and do not officiate as priests.

bhūmyādikānda [ādikānda] n. lit. np. from the Bhūmyādikānda, 2nd volume of the Amarakoşa; it comprises ten sections [varga]: bhūmivarga dealing with the earth, puravarga dealing with cities, śailavarga dealing with mountains, vanausadhivarga dealing with wild herbs, simhādivarga dealing with animals, nrvarga dealing with man, brahmavarga dealing with brahmins, ksatriyavarga dealing with warriors, vaiśyavarga dealing with merchants, and śūdravarga dealing with servants.

bhūmikā [Bhūmika] f. earth, ground | preface, introduction to a work; (theater) list of actors' roles — ifc. location of (2nd century); ground in (2nd century); floor, story; level. bhūmikāyām adv. ifc. in the role of (2nd century). saptabhūmikāh prāsādah seven-story palace. laksmībhūmikāyām vartamānā playing the role of Laksmī.
bhūmim [acc. Bhūmi] iic.
bhūmimjaya [jaya] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Bhūmiñjaya "Conqueror of the land", title of the Uttara prince.
bhūya [act. bhū₁] n. being, becoming — ifc. the act of becoming (2nd ed.) | state of (2nd ed.). kuśalam bhūyāt adr. wish for prosperity. .8
bhūyaśas [bhūyasśas] adv. mainly; generally | again; still.

bhūyas [compar. bhūri] amnf bhūyasī very numerous, very abundant, very large | which abounds in (i. iic.). bhūyas acc. adv. more, further, still, much, very. bhūyasā i. adv. generally; to the highest degree. kim bhūyas what's the point of further discussion? bhūyo'pi more; even more. bhūyo bhūyas again and again; many times.
bhūyastva [tva] n. profusion, abundance.

bhūyiṣṭha [super. bahu] amnf bhūyiṣṭhā the greatest, the most abundant, principal — acc. bhūyiṣṭham adv. for the most part | to the highest degree. bhūyisthena adv. principally. abhirūpabhūyiṣṭhā pariṣat an assembly composed mainly of learned people. kṣīṇabhūyiṣṭhāyāṃ kṣapāyām the night being almost exhausted. bhūyiṣṭhāṃ te nama uktim vidhema [Iśā] We offer you our best greetings.
bhūr [nom. bhū₁] ind. myth. np. of bhūr the Earth, first celestial World [loka]; cf. lokatraya, vyāhṛti.
bhūrloka | loka | m. the terrestrial world, the Earth.
bhūri amnf numerous, abundant; great, important — m. myth. epith. of Visnu, Shiva, Brahmā, Indra — adv. bhūrī in great numbers, abundantly; often; very. bhūri kṛtvas many times; repeatedly.
bhūriśas |śas| adv. in multiple ways; in abon dance.

bhūriśravas [śravas] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Prince Bhūriśravā "Thunderous", son of Somadatta; he rallied the Kauravās clan as a general [akṣauhiṇīpati]; while he held his compatriot Yuyudhāna at his mercy, Arjuna cut off his arm with an arrow, and Yuyudhāna beheaded him.
bhūrja m. bio. bot. Botula bhojpatra, birch; one writes on its bark — n. birch bark leaf used for writing | document, written contract || ang. birch.
bhūrjapattra | pattra | n. birch bark used for writing.
√ bhūṣ v. [1] pr. (bhūṣati) pp. (bhūṣita) pf. (pari) to make efforts to (dat.), to strive to obtain — ca. (bhūṣayati) pf. (vi) to adorn, to embellish, to decorate; to beautify.

bhūṣaṇa [agt. bhūṣ] amnf bhūṣaṇā ifc. that which adorns, that which decorates — m. myth. epith. of Vișnu — n. lit. ornament, adornment, decoration; poetic style abundant in ornaments [alaṃkāra] | lit. commentary.
bhūṣaṇabhaṭṭa [bhaṭṭa] m. hist. np. of bhūṣaṇa bhaṭṭa, son of Bāṇa₂; after the death of his father, he completed the Kādambarī according to his plans.
bhūsanayojana [yojana] n. the art of adornment, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.
Bhūṣaṇasāra |sāra| n. gram. n.p. from the Bhūṣaṇasāra "Essence of the commentary", from the work Kaundabhatta; cf. Vaiyākaranabhūsanasāra. মুষা bhūṣā [act. bhūṣ] f. ornament, decoration.
bhūṣin [agt. bhūṣ] amnf bhūṣiṇī ifc. decorated with (iic.).
bhūsṇu [agt. bhū₁] amnf that benefits, that grows; prosperous | desirous of prosperity.
bhūstṛṇa [bhūtṛṇa] m. bio. bot. Cymbopogon citratus, lemongrass; this aromatic plant has many medicinal uses; cf. uśīra .

√ bhr v. [3] pr. (bíbharti) ppr. (bibhrat) v. [1] pr. (bhárati) pr. r. (bharate) ppr. (bharat) aor. [3] (abībharat) pp. (bhṛta) pfp. (bhārya, bhṛtya) pf. (ā, pra, sam) to support, to bear; to bear (literally and figuratively); to maintain | to carry on, to have — ca. (bhārayati) to make bear || gr. φερω; lat. fero; ang. to bear; all. gebären; fr. fère. rājyam bhr to exercise kingship. kṛṣṇaścakramabibhararjuno gāṇḍīvam duryodha nabhīmasenau gadāmabibhṛtāmanye sarve yodhāḥ sādhāranam dhanurābibharuh Kṛṣṇa carried the ca kra, Arjuna the bow Gāṇḍīva, Duryodhana and Bhīma carried the mace, all the other warriors generally carried a bow.
bhṛg [onomatopoeia] ind. imitates the crackling of fire

Bhṛgu [bhṛgu] m. myth. np. from the maharṣi Bhṛgu "Crackling", progenitor [prajāpati], born from the trinity of Brahmā, or else born from Agni during a brahmayajña led by Varuṇa; he was raised by Varuna and Carṣaṇī; his wife was the beautiful and virtuous Pulomā₂; he is the father of Sukra and Cyavana; at the wedding of Rcīka, he taught his wife Satyavatī₁ a rite to enable her and her mother to have a son; [Mah.] he officiated at the sacrifice of Dakșa, and Siva plucked out his beard; [SB.] as he considered himself superior in knowledge to his father Varuna, the latter sent him to the afterlife to see the torments of the damned; there he saw a man cutting down another with his axe, a man eating a screaming man and a man eating a silent man; his father taught him that they were respectively the spirit of a tree, that of an animal, and that of a plant, taking revenge on their executioner for what he had made them suffer in this world; [PP.] the sages [rsi], unable to decide which god was most worthy of veneration by the brahmins, asked him to arbitrate; unable to access Shiva, who was occupied with his husband, he condemned him to be worshipped in the form of the linga; despised by Brahma, who was full of his own grandeur, he condemned him not to be the object of worship; Finally, he struck the sleeping Vishnu on the chest with his foot to awaken him; Vishnu nevertheless treated him with respect, thus gaining his approval. Bhrgu had a third eye under his foot, signifying his prideful ego; Vishnu destroyed it and showed him the vanity of his pretension to judge the Trimurti. Bhrgu is the patron of astrologers, and the Bhrgusaṃhitā is attributed to him. [RV.] The Bhrgavas are a race of divine beings associated with fire, which Matariśvā brings them; cf. Bhārgavās. bhrgor caru myth. Bhrgu's ritual porridge, consumed by a wife to conceive a son.

bhṛgukaccha [kaccha] n. geo. np. of the sacred city of Bhrgukaccha "Bank of Bhrgu" on the Narmadā River (known to the Greeks as Ba rygaśa, mod. Broach/Bharuch in Gujarāt), where the temple of bhrgurşi is located; cf. Bharukaccha — f. bhrgukacchā id.
bhrgupati | pati | m. myth. np. of Bhrgupati, epith. of Paraśurāma "Chief of the Bhārgavās".
bhṛgupāta [pāta] m. soc. ritual suicide by throwing oneself from the top of a cliff, not. at the rock of Giri nagara, of a firstborn male promised by his mother to Mahādeva.
bhṛguprasravaṇa [prasravaṇa] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of Mount Bhrguprasravana "Bhṛgu Waterfall", in the Himalayas; Sagara did penance there for 100 years with his wives to obtain sons.
bhṛgurṣi [ṛṣi] m. myth. n.p. of Bhṛgurṣi, the ṛṣi Bhrgu.
bhṛguvallī [vallī] f. lit. 3rd chapter of the TU.
bhṛgusaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. np. of the Bhṛgusaṃhitā, an ancient work of predictive astrology attributed to Bhrgu.
bhṛṅga mf bhṛṅgī bio. zoo. bee, bumblebee; large dark blue hymenopteran | passerine.
bhṛṅgarāja [rāja] m. bio. zoo. Dicrurus paradiscus, forked-tailed drongo.
bhrigasamdeśa [samdeśa] m. lit. np. from the Bhrigasandeśa, a samdeśakāvya type poem by an anonymous author.

bhṛṅgāra [āra] m. myth. gold vase offered by Varuna to Bharatamuni and his sons after their first theatrical performance | soc. purifying vase used during the consecration of a king; it is composed of the 8 alloys [aṣṭadhātu] | soc. [nāṭya] vase used by the theatre director |sūtradhāra| during the prologue [pūrvaranga] of a play to purify the jarjara so that it may serve as a sacred banner [indradhvaja] — n. clove | gold | cf. bhṛṅga.
bhṛṅgi iic. bhṛṅgin. bhrigiriți m. myth. n.p. from Bhrgiriți or Bhrgīriți; cf. Bhrngī.
bhṛṅgirīti [rīti] m. myth. np. of BhṛṅgirītiBhṛṅgī; lit. he is featured in the Bālarāmāyaṇa, as an emissary of Shiva to avoid a fight between Rāvaņa and Paraśurāma which Nārada sought to incite.
bhṛṅgīśa [īśa] m. myth. n.p. of Bhṛṅgīśa, epith. of Siva.
bhṛṅgīśasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. bed. n.p. from the Bhrigīśasamhitā, collection of texts of praise of
pilgrimages [māhātmya] of northern Kaśmīra; cf. Sāradāmāhātmya.

bhṛṅgin [bhṛṅgain] m. myth. np. of the preta Bhrigī, worshipper of Śiva who, having vowed to worship only one god, neglected to honor Pārvatī; unable to circumambulate Shiva alone, embraced by her, he transformed himself into an insect [bhṛṅgī] to do so; Pārvatī cursed him to be reduced to a skeleton; no longer able to support himself, he obtained a third leg from Shiva; to force him to honor Pārvatī, Shiva united with her in the androgynous form Ardhanārīśvara; it is also said that he represents the demon Andhaka drained of his blood; he is depicted as a skeleton; It is also called Bhrgiriti, Bhṛṅgirīti, and other variations.
bhṛj [obj. bhṛjj] ifc. amnf (iic.) grilled.
√ bhṛjj [related to bhṛg] v. [6] pr. (bhṛjjáti) pp. (bhṛṣṭa) to grill, roast; to fry. भূজ্বর bhṛjjata [imp. bhṛjj ] ind. roast!

bhṛt [agt. bhṛ] ifc. amnf that carries, that supports; that has, that has (2nd century). ਮ੍ਰ bhṛta [pp. bhṛ] amnf bhṛtā carried, sup carried, transported; raised | acquired; hired; paid, remunerated — ifc. full of (2nd century) — m. salaried.
bhṛtaka |ka| amnf bhṛtikā drawn, brought (water) — m. domestic, servant; wage earner — f. bhṛtikā hiring; salary.
bhṛti [act. bhṛ] f. maintenance, the act of raising or feeding; food; wages.

bhṛtya [pfp. [1] bhṛ] amnf bhṛtyā to be maintained — m. domestic, servant — ifc. one who raises (iic.) — f. bhṛtyā maintenance, support; wages — v. |11| pr. r. (bhṛtyāyate) to behave like a servant. bhṛtyībhū to become a servant, to enter the service of. ਮੁੱਧ bhṛtha m. ved. oblation (of soma).

bhṛśa [related to bhraṃś] amnf bhṛśā strong, powerful, violent; abundant; intense, excessive — v. [11] pr. r. (bhṛśāyate) to become vigorous; to intensify. bhrśam adv. strongly, powerfully, intensely; much, in great numbers | frequently; again and again | energetically, violently; excessively.
bhráaduḥkhita |duḥkhita| anfm bhrśaduhkhita extremely afflicted. ਮੁਣ bhṛṣṭá [pp. bhṛjj] amnf bhṛṣṭā fried; grilled, roasted.
bheka m. bio. zoo. frog. ਮੇਤ bheḍa m. ram | var. bheṇḍa id. — f. bheḍī ewe.
bhetavya [pfp. [3] bhī₁] amnf bhetavyā to be feared, that which one must dread. na bhetavyam (impers.) one must not be afraid; do not be afraid (of (abl. g.)).

bhedá [act. bhid₁] m. cleft, break; fissure (du. labia of the vagina) | destruction, violation | breach; disclosure | state of being broken; frown (of the brows) | separation; difference; interval | classification; not. phonetic feature | intrigue, discord; corruption, betrayal | math. hypotenuse of a right triangle | phil. duality between God and the Universe (opp. identity of monism |abheda|) gram. violation of a rule; grammatical ambiguity; orthographic variant.
Bhedadhikkāra [dhikkāra] m. lit. np. of the Bhe dadhikkāra "Contempt for the doctrine of difference", a critique of Madhva due to Nṛsiṃhāśrama; cf. Bhe davidyāvilāsa.
bhedavākya | vākya | n. phil. verbal expression of difference.
bhedavāda | vāda | m. phil. doctrine of duality between God and the Universe, due to Madhya.
bhedavidyā [vidyā] f. phil. id.
bhedavidyāvilāsa [vilāsa] m. lit. np. from the bheda vidyāvilāsa "Beauty of the doctrine of difference", defense of Madhva by Vijayīndra in response to the Bhedadhikkāra of Nṛsiṃhāśrama.
bhedāgraha [agraha] m. phil. [bd.] non-apprehension of difference; opp. abhedagraha.

bhedābheda [abheda] m. du. phil. duality and monism mixed; [Vedānta] school professing that Brahman and creation are both separate and linked | phil. |Kumārila| identity and difference; characterizes not. the relationship between quality |guna| and substance [dravya₁]. acintyabhedābhedatattva inconceivable simultaneity of unity and difference between God and the individual soul (summary of Caitanya's doctrine).
bhedābhedavāda [vāda] m. phil. "unity in diversity", doctrine professing both duality and monism; cf. Bhāskara₁, Sālikanātha.
bhedojjīvana [ujjīvana] n. lit. np. from bhedojjīvana "Rebirth of Difference", a small work by Vyāsatīrtha opposing the Advaita doctrine.
bhedaka [agt. bhid₁] amnf bhedikā that pierces, that perforates; that destroys | that distinguishes, that determines, that defines — n. gram. adjective — act. f. bhedikā destruction, annihilation.
bhedana [act. bhid₁] n. act of splitting, breaking, separating; division, rupture | act of betraying (not. a secret (iic.)); act of sowing discord.
bhedya [pfp. [1] bhid₁] amnf bhedyā which must be broken, split or pierced; to open | to contest, to refute; to analyze, to determine, to distinguish — n. gram. substantive.
bhedyatva [tva] n. gram. quality of a noun; act of discriminating.
bheya [pfp. [1] bhī₁] amnf bheyā to be feared, that which must be dreaded — acc. bheyam (impers.) one must fear (abl.). arer bheyam the enemy must be feared.
bherī f. large drum with a deep sound; timpani, bass drum.
bheruṇḍa var. bheraṇḍa amnf bheruṇḍā terrible, formidable, terrifying | bird of prey | carnivorous animal (wolf, jackal, fox, hyena).
bheṣaja [agt. bhiṣaj] amnf bheṣajī that heals, that cures — n. medicine; remedy (against (g. iic.)) | healing charm, not. from the Atharvaveda.
bhaikṣa [*bhikṣa] amnf bhaikṣī who lives on alms — n. begging; begged food. bhaikṣaṃ gam to ask for alms; to beg. bhaiksam car id.
bhaikṣuka [*bhikṣuka] n. crowd of beggars — m. soc. 4th stage of brahmanical life, state of wandering ascetic — f. bhaikṣukī ancient bd. writing.

bhaikṣya [*bhikṣya] amnf bhaikṣyā cf. bhaikṣa. ਮੈਸ bhaima [*Bhīma₁] amnf Bhaimī concerning Bhīma₁; descendant of Bhīma₁ or Bhīma₁ — f. Bhaimī myth. np. of Bhaimī, epith. of Damayantī, daughter of Bhīma₁.

Bhairava [*bhīrua] amnf Bhairavī terrible, formidable, frightening — m. myth. np. of Bhairava "the Terrifying One", epithet of Shiva in his fierce [ugra] form; his mount is a corpse [śavārūḍha] or a dog, and he carries the skull-humerus club [khaṭvāṅga] as a weapon; he is often depicted

ithyphallic [ūrdhvalinga]; he is celebrated [jayantī] in bhairavāṣṭamī; he has 8 temples in Benares [aṣṭabhairava] | soc. yogin of the tantric sect of the worshippers of Bhairava — n. horror, terror — f. Bhairavī phil. |Tantra| np. of Bhairavī "the Terrible", one of the 10 powers [mahāvidyā] of the Force [Sakti].
bhairavatantra [Tantra] n. soc. n.p. from the transgressive bhairavatantra tradition; cf. Brahmayamala.
bhairavastotra [stotra] m. bed. n.p. from Abhinavagupta's Bhairavasto tra (993).
bhairavānanda [ānanda] m. myth. joy of Bhai rava.
Bhairavānandanāṭaka [nāṭaka] n. lit. np. of the drama Bhairavānandanāṭaka, due to Maṇika; its hero is Bhairava, the heroine is the nymph Mada navatī.
bhairavāṣṭamī [aṣṭamī] f. soc. the 8th day of the dark fortnight of the month mārgaśīrṣa ; on this day we celebrate the appearance of Bhairava, who came to behead Brahmā.
Bhaişajya [*bhişajya] n. medicine, remedy (against (g.)); curative efficacy.
bho cf. bhos.
bhoktavya [pfp. [3] bhuj₁] amnf bhok tavyā that which can be enjoyed, that which can be eaten; to be used. bhoktavyam one must eat. asti bhoktavyam there is to eat.
bhoktu [inf. bhuj₁] iic. to speak.
bhoktukāma [kāma] amnf bhoktukāmā who likes to eat.
bhoktr [agt. bhuj₁] amnf bhoktrī who profits; who eats; who feels | who governs, who uses — m. user; beneficiary; possessor; husband; prince | myth. epith. of Vișnu.
bhoktrtva |tva| n. the act of enjoying, taking pleasure, perceiving, possessing.
bhoga₁ [act. bhuj₁] m. ring (of a snake).
bhoga₂ [act. bhuj₁] m. consumption; food; meal, banquet | pleasure, wealth, enjoyment; perception, feeling | sexual pleasure | profit, gain phil. fruit (of an action), reward.
bhogavat [vat] f. Bhogavatī myth. n.p. of the Bhogavatī or underground Ganges river | myth. underground capital of dragons [nāga].
bhogalābha [lābha] m. soc. advantage obtained by a creditor from the return on an asset lent as collateral.
bhogopabhogavrata | upabhogavrata | n. jn. the observance of limited consumption, a vow
meritorious [gunavrata].
bhogin₁ [agt. bhuj₁] mf bhoginī [“who has rings”] snake.
bhogin₂ [agt. bhuj₁] amnf bhoginī jouis seur — f. bhoginī soc. favorite of a prince.

bhógya [pfp. [1] bhuj₁] amnf bhogyā that one should enjoy; worthy of being enjoyed | that one can feed on | useful, profitable | to endure — n. object of pleasure; possession; money — f. bhogyā prostitute.
bhoj [ca. bhuj₁] v. [10] pr. (bhojáyati) to nourish; to gladden. brāhmaṇā bhojyantām let the brah manes be nourished!

bhojá [agt. bhuj₁] amnf bhojā that gives pleasure; liberal | joyful, bon vivant, pleasure-seeker — m. myth. np. of the yādava Bhoja "Epicurean", king of the bhojās, descendant of Vṛṣṇi, father of Hṛdīka | myth. epith. of Kṛtavarmā | hist. np. of the king Bhoja₁ of Mālava; cf. Bhojadeva | pl. bhojās geo. name of a country and its inhabitants, of capital Bhojapurī; cf. Uśīnarās.
bhojajyā [jyā₃] f. math. product of the sine of an arc of a circle by the radius of the circle.

bhojádeva [deva] m. hist. np. of the king of Mālava Paramāra Bhojadeva, eldest son of Sindhurāja; his capital was Dhārā; he reigned from 1018 to 1054; he repelled the Turuṣkās at Dvārakā; he fought, and was finally defeated by the Cālukyās; he was learned, had many poets at his court, and organized poetry tournaments; the Bhojaprabandha made him a golden legend; many works are attributed to him, not. treatises on poetic style in Sanskrit (Sarasvatīkanthābharana₁), on poetry and dramaturgy (Srigāraprakāśa), on hygiene (Cārucaryā), on astronomy (Rājamṛgānga), on philosophy (Tattvaprakāśa); he is credited with the Bhojanighanțu or Nāmamālikā lexicon; his Rājamārtanda is a commentary on the Yogasūtra; his Rāmāyaṇacampū is a classical poem of medieval Sanskrit; finally, he is credited with the grammar of Sanskrit also called Saras vatīkanthābharana₂.
bhojanighantu | nighantu | mr. bed. from np. Bhojanighantu; cf. Nāmamālikā.
bhojápura [pura] n. geo. np. of the city of bho japura, founded by King Bhoja₁ (mod. Bhojpur in Madhya Pradesh, 28 km from Bhopal); cf. bhojeśvara — f. Bhojapurī geo. np. of Bhojapurī, id.
bhojáprabandha [prabandha] m. lit. np. from the Bhoja prabandha "Deeds of King Bhoja₁" by Vallāla; it is a fiction that features many poets (often not contemporary) at the court of King Bho Jadeva.
bhojárāja | rājan | mr. hist. n.p. of king Bhojarāja; cf. Bhojadeva.
bhojávrtti [vrtti] f. bed. n.p. of Bhojavrtti, commentary on the Yogasūtra of Patanjali₂ |Pātañjalavṛtti| owed to king Bhojadeva; cf. Rājamārtanda.

bhojáśālā [śālā] f. hist. np. of the Bhojaśālā "Library of King Bhoja₁", Sanskrit school founded by King Bhojadeva in Dhārā, in the temple of Sa rasvatī; it was looted in 1140 by Siddharāja, who brought back as booty its books, and not. the grammar Sa rasvatīkanthābharana; it was then transformed into a mosque.

bhojeśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of the śaiva bhojeśvara temple of Bhojapura; it was begun by King Bhoja₁ in the 11th century, but never completed; its monolithic linga is 5.5 high and 2.3 in circumference.
bhojosna | uṣṇa | amnf bhojoṣṇā too hot to eat.
bhojana [act. bhuj₂] n. food, nourishment | sustenance, meal — f. bhojanā ifc. nourished by; that which serves as food for.
bhojanapātra | pātra | n. food container; bowl.
bhojanabhāṇḍa [bhāṇḍa] n. kitchen utensil.
bhojin [agt. bhuj₂] ifc. amnf bhojinī who eats; who takes pleasure in, who enjoys (iic.). śīghrabhojī glutton.
bhojya [pfp. [1] bhuj₂] amnf bhojyā that can be enjoyed, consumed; edible; that must be fed; whose food can be eaten by (g.) | that can or must be used — n. food, nourishment, meal.
bhojyānna | anna | amnf bhojyānnā soc. conve nable à préparer le repas (said of a śūdra suitable for preparing the food of a brāhmaṇa).
bhojyosna [uṣṇa] n. something hot to eat.
bhoṭa m. geo. np. of Bhoṭa, Tibet || fr. Bhutan.
bhos [bhavat₂] interj. of respectful address: sir! | oh! (voc.) | var. bho id. bho bhos holà! hear, hear! bho rāma O rāma!

bhauta [*bhūta] amnf bhautī which concerns living beings; which concerns material substances | relating to spirits; possessed by demons; demented, mad; idiot — n. the multitude of spirits — f. bhautī night ["where the spirits roam"].
bhautaśāstra [śāstra] n. mod. physical science.
bhautākhyāna [ākhyāna] n. lit. np. of the literary genre bhautākhyāna or bhautopākhyāna; it consists of satirical anecdotes featuring stupid characters, representing the authors' opponents.
bhautopākhyāna [upākhyāna] cf. n. bhautākhyāna.
