bhautika [*bhūtaika] amnf bhautikī phil. derived from natural elements; material | that which concerns beings — n. pearl — f. bhautikī mod. physical.
bhautya [*bhūtiya] m. myth. n.p. of bhautya "Fortunate", 14ᵉ Manu of the kalpa.

bhaumá [*Bhūmia] amnf bhaumī relating to the earth, terrestrial | made of earth | (income) land relating to the planet Mars; which occurs on Tuesday — m. myth. np. of Bhauma, epith. of Mangala "from the earth" | myth. np. of Bhauma₁, patr. of the asura Naraka, son of Bhūmi | hist. era |saṃvat| of the Bhaumakara dynasty — f. bhaumī myth. np. of bhaumī, epith. of Sītā “from the earth”.

Bhaumakara [kara₁] m. hist. n.p. of the Bhaumakara dynasty, established in 736 in Orissa; of many monasteries bd. were instituted at its beginning; Jajpur was its capital; in the 10th century the Somavamśī dynasty succeeded him.
bhaumika [*bhūmiika] amnf bhaumikī terrestrial | picked up on the ground.
bhaumya [*bhūmiya] amnf bhaumyā terrestrial; of this world.

√ bhramś v. [1] pr. r. (bhramśate) v. [4] pr. (bhraśyati) pr. r. (bhraśyate) pp. (bhraṣṭa) pf. (apa, pra, vi) to fall, to fall to pieces, to fall from (abl.) | to rebound from (abl.) | to decline; to disappear; to escape from (g.) | to be deprived of, to lose (abl.) — ca. (bhramśayati) pp. (bhramśita) to cause to fall or decline, to cause the loss of.
bhraṃśa [agt. bhraṃś] amnf bhraṃśā that falls; that detaches from (abl. iic.) — act. m. fact of falling by detaching; loss, disappearance separation; abandonment; fact of being deprived of (iic.).
bhraṃśita [pp. ca. bhraṃś] amnf bhramsitā that has been dropped; thrown to the ground deprived of (abl.).
bhraṃśin [agt. bhraṃś] amnf bhraṃśinī that falls (from (iic.)) | that withers away; transient.
bhraj [related to bhraṃś] ifc. m. cf. mṛtabhraj.

√ bhram v. [1] pr. (bhramati) v. [4] pr. (bhrāmyati) pft. (babhrāma) pp. (bhrānta) pf. (ut, pari, vi, sam) to wander; to roam, to ramble, to stagger; to move irregularly; to circulate (stars, planets) | to spread (news) | to doubt, to hesitate; to make a mistake — ca. (bhrāmayati) to wave, to brandish — intens. (bambhramīti) intens. r. (bambhramyate) to wander for a long time. bhikṣām bhram to wander as a beggar.
bhrama |act. bhram| m. rambling, wandering; er reur | displacement, rotation; trajectory; rolling (eyes); whirlpool | source, fountain, stream — f. bhramā ifc. id. bhramam dā to swing.
bhramātmaka |ātmaka| amnf bhramātmikā phil. characterizes erroneous cognition [jñāna]; opp. pramātmaka.

bhramaṇa [act. bhram] n. peregrination; wandering; circumambulation around (i.e.) digression; revolution, orbit (planet) | vertigo; dizziness | the act of making a mistake. cakrabhramananyayah maxim of the potter's wheel, which continues to turn; it explains that a jīvanmukta continues to live until the exhaustion of the merits acquired at his birth.
bhramaṇatva [tva] n. act of turning.

bhramara [bhramara] m. bio. zoo. Xylocopa fenestrata, black hymenopteran | bee; flying insect | (poetry) lover ["forager"] | soc. ritual gesture [mudrā] of the hand "in the bee" position (hand raised vertically, index finger folded) — f. bhramarā ifc. bee | climbing plant — f. bhramarī bee. vibhramabhramarī lakṣmīḥ lit. |K.| Fortune is like a bee bustling about.
bhramaraka [ka] mn soc. spinning top; yo-yo; diabolo.
bhramarāmbikā [ambikā] f. myth. n.p. of Bh ramarāmbikā, form of Devī, consort of Mal likārjuna in Srīśaila; it is a śaktipītha.

bhramin [agt. bhram] amnf bhraminī who wanders, who rambles. ਮੋਣ bhraṣṭa [pp. bhraṃś] amnf bhraṣṭā fallen, deposed (from (abl. ii.)); corrupted | vanished; in ruins. mārgāt bhraṣṭa amn phil. having lost his way. adhikārabhrasta amn having lost his job. yogabhrașta amn phil. having lost yogic grace.
bhraṣṭabuddhi | buddhi | perverted amnf.
bhraṣṭamārga | mārga | amnf bhraṣṭamārgā who has lost his way.
bhraṣṭaśrī [śrī] amnf ruined. ਮਣ bhrástra |instr. bhrjj| n. grill; frying pan.
√ bhrāj v. [1] pr. r. (bhrājate) pf. (vi) to shine, to radiate, to sparkle — ca. (bhrājayati) to make shine, to illuminate | gr. ; lat. flagro; ang. bright; fr. flamme.

bhrājá |agt. bhrāj| amnf bhrājā bright; that illuminates — m. epith. of fire or of the Sun | myth. np. of the gandharva Bhrāja, guardian of soma | pl. lit. np. of the Bhrājās, work attributed to Kātyāyana.
bhrājaka |agt. ca. bhrāj| amnf bhrājikā that makes shine — n. med. bile.
bhrātṛ m. [sg. nom. bhrātā, acc. bhrātaram] brother | my brother (close friend) | du. bhrātarau brother and sister || gr. φρατηρ; lat. frater; ang. brother; all. Bruder; fr. frère.
bhrātrjāyā [jāyā] f. sister-in-law (wife of a brother).
bhrātṛtva [tva] n. brotherhood.
bhrātrīya [īya] m. nephew (son of a brother) — f. bhrātrīyā niece.
bhrātṛvya [bhrātṛ] m. paternal cousin | rival, competitor, adversary; enemy | Vedic adversary of the yajamāna in the solemn ritual.
bhrānta [pp. bhram] amnf bhrāntā who wanders; lost, troubled | traversed — n. wandering, digression, tribulation.
bhrānti [act. bhram] f. wandering, rambling; straying; hesitation, doubt, perplexity; trouble, confusion; illusion; error of perception | rolling (wheel); vibration; trembling.
bhrāma [*bhrama] m. confusion, hesitation.
bhrāmara [*bhramara] amnf Bhrāmarī concerning the bee — n. honey — f. Bhrāmarī phil. [Tantra] np. of Bhrāmarī "Buzzing", one of the 8 divine powers [yoginī].
bhrukuṭī [bhrūkuṭ] f. frown. bhrukuṭīṃ bandh var. bhrukuṭīṃ rac to frown.
bhrukuṭīmukha [mukha] amnf bhrukuṭīmukhī who frowns — n. angry or sullen face.

bhruva ifc. bhrū. ¥ bhrū f. eyebrow; cf. subhru || gr. oφρυς; ang. brow; all. braue; fr. frown. bhruvau samkuc var. bhruvau bhid to frown the eyebrows. acaladṛśā paśyanbhruvorantaram [GS.] By having one's gaze fixed on the space between the eyebrows.
bhrūkuṃśa | kuṃśa | mr. soc. transvestite actor | var. bhrūkumsa id.
bhrūkuṭī [kuṭī] f. frown. bhrūkuṭīm kṛ var. bhrūkuṭīm bandh frown.
bhrūbhanga [bhanga] m. frowning. bhrūbhangam kṛ to frown.
bhrūmadhya | madhya | n. space between the eyebrows.
bhrūṇa [bhṛ] n. fetus — m. child, boy | learned brahmin.
bhrūṇaghna | ghna | amnf bhrūṇaghnī murderer of a learned brahmin.
bhrūṇahatyā | hatya | f. abortion.
bhrūṇahan |han₂| amnf bhrūṇaghnī cf. bhrūnaghna.
bhvādi [(bhū)ādi] m. gram. ["which begins with bhū₁"] qualifies the first class [gaṇa] of the present tense of verbs; its characteristic marker |vikarana₂| is śap.
m ॰ਸ my form of a. ord. and sm or n. | superlative (for tama)
√ maṃh [related to mah] v. [1] pr. r. (máṃhate) pp. (mahitá) to give generously, to grant; to offer as a reward — ca. (mamháyati) to cause to be granted.

mákara mf makarī organic. zoo. Crocodilus palustris, river crocodile | myth. makara or sea monster, chimera of dolphin and dile crocodile, mount of Varuna and Gangā, emblem of Kāma | astr. zodiac sign | rāśi | and constellation Capricorn || hi. magar.
mákarakundala [kundala] n. earring in the shape of a makara, male symbol; Națarāja wears one on her right ear.
mákaraketana | ketana | m. myth. np. of Makarake tana, epith. of Kāma "with a standard adorned with a ma kara".
mákaraketu | ketu | m. myth. np. of Makaraketu, epith. of Kāma “with a standard adorned with a makara ”.
mákaraketumat [mat] m. id.
mákaradamstrā [damstrā] f. bed. [KSS.] np. of Makaradamstrā "Crocodile Tooth", real mother of her daughter Rūpiņikā.

mákaradhvaja [dhvaja] m. myth. np. of Maka radhvaja "who has the makara as emblem", epith. of Kāma | ocean | med. [Ayurveda] mixture of sul phide of mercury and gold, produced by sublimation of an amalgam of mercury, sulfur and gold, used not. as a tonic.

makarasaṃkrānti [saṃkrānti] f. soc. New Year festival, at the beginning of the month of māgha; it originally corresponded to the winter solstice [dakṣiṇāyana]; it is now celebrated around January 14, because of the precession of the equinoxes [ayanāṃśa]; it is a day favorable for bathing, not. in Prayāga; it is also called māghamela; this festival is called Pongal saṃkrānti in South India, rice is cooked in milk and a ceremony [pūjā] is dedicated to the Sun.
makaranda [related to makara] m. nectar, pol len, honey | variety of jasmine or mango | lit. [Vāsavadattā] np. of makaranda "Sweet", friend of Kandarpaketu₁.
makarandadāsa [dāsa] m. hist. n.p. by Ma karandadāsa, author of the Pa ramānandīyanāmamālā dictionary (end of the 16th century).
makarandavat [vat] amnf makarandavatī (flower) rich in nectar or pollen.
Makarandikā [ika] f. phon. name of a poetic meter | lit. [KSS.] np. of Makarandikā, daughter of a vidyādhara.
makarandikopākhyāna [upākhyāna] n. lit. np. from the makarandikopākhyāna, an episode from the Kathāsaritsāgara in which Makarandikā is the heroine; the Kādambarī is inspired by it.
makāra [(ma)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'ma'.

makārapañcaka [pañcaka] n. phil. [Tantra] the group of "five m's", ingredients of transgression of kulācāra including alcohol [madya], meat [māṃsa], fish [matsya], sexual union [maithuna] and the laying on of hands [mudrā].
makura [related to makula] m. flower bud (ornament); syn. koraka | bio. tree bot. Mimusops Elengi; syn. bakula | potter's wheel stick | mirror.
makula | linked to makura | mr. | mukula | flower in bud (ornament) | |bakula| organic. bot tree. Mimu sops Elengi.
makṣikā [maśa] f. fly, gnat | var. makṣīkā id. || lat. musca; fr. fly.
makṣū adv. ved. immediately, directly, instantly.

makhá [related to magha] amnf makhā joyful; vigorous, active; turbulent | myth. always in motion; said of the breaths | marutas | or aspects of Rudra — m. festival | soc. Sacrifice, oblation | ved. np. of Makha, god personifying Sacrifice; refusing to share his benefit with the other gods, he was punished by being beheaded with his bow, the string of which was gnawed by ants; his head became the Sun; to restore the completeness of the Sacrifice, Dadhyań taught the Aśvinau how to reassemble it; so as not to be beheaded himself by Indra, he gave the secret with a horse's head as a substitute.
makhi |Makhai| m. soc. title of priest performing a Sacrifice.

Magadha m. geo. np. of the Magadha country (south of modern Bihāra); its capital was Rājagṛha, then Pāṭaliputra from the reign of Ajātaśatru₂ (5th century BC); it is the crucible of the Mau rya empire.

magna |pp. majj| amnf magnā plunged, immersed (in (loc. iic.)) | disappeared (not. said of the moon after its setting); fallen into misfortune; which falls again (not. breasts) | which has penetrated or disappeared into (loc. iic.).

maghá [obj. maṃh] m. gift, reward; booty — f. maghā pl. astr. np. of the Maghās "the Generous Ones", forming the 8th lunar asterism [nakṣatra] corr. to the star Regulus (constellation of Leo); the manes | pitaras | preside there; its symbol is a house.
maghavan [vat] amnf maghonī f. magha vatī liberal, generous — m. maghavan | nom. ma ghavā myth. np. of Maghavā, epith. of Indra "the generous one".

maṅkaṇaka m. myth. [VAP.] np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Mańkanaka, born from the spirit of Kaśyapa; one day taking his bath in the river, he was joined there by the nymph [apsaras] Rambhā and her attendants; he lost his seed, which he divided into 7 portions, giving birth to 7 divine breaths [marut]; having cut his hand with kuśa grass, sap flowed from it, which made him joyful, and his ecstatic dance made the whole universe vibrate, causing the gods to worry; Shiva humbled him, showing him that if he hurt himself it was ash that came; Mankanaka prostrated himself at his feet, and was forgiven; cf. Ka dalīgarbhā.
maṅkṣu [related to makṣū] adv. immediately, directly, instantly | very, excessively, really.

mankha m. soc. member of a mendicant order of Magadha | hist. np. of Mańkha (or Mańkhāka), poet and lexicographer of Kashmira in the 12th century, student of Ruyyaka; he is the author of the mahākāvya Srīkanthacarita and the mankhakośa; he was a minister of King Jayasimha. mańkhakośa [kośa] m. lit. np. of the Mańkhakośa, epithet of the Anekārthakośa, dictionary of homonymous words due to mankha.
maṅkhali [pkt. maskarin] m. hist. n.p. of the materialist philosopher Mankhali or Makkhali; cf. Gośāla.
mankhāka m. hist. np. of mankhāka, scholar from Kaśmīra of the 12th century, student of Ruyyaka, author of the Śrīkanthacarita.

mangala n. blessing, happiness, felicity; prosperity | auspicious sign; lucky charm, good luck charm, amulet; cf. astamangala ceremony, custom, festival — m. astr. np. from the graha mangala "Beneficial", personifying the planet Mars, and red in color [Rudhira]; [SP.] it is said that mangala was born from a drop of sweat of Shiva doing penance after the death of Satī, and collected by the Earth Bhūmi; or that he is the son of Vișnu Varāha and Bhūmi, and thus called Bhūmisuta; it is therefore said that he is Kuja/Bhūmija "Born of the Earth" or Bhauma; he is celibate, he is said to be impulsive and adventurous; he protects property and the wife; astr. in his dark aspect, he personifies war, and is expert in occult sciences; It is associated with copper, fire, coral, summer, and the south; it is honored on Tuesday [mangalavāra]; cf. Angāraka | lit. auspicious verse, prayer to a deity | math. symb. the number 8 — f. mangalā myth. np. of the yoginī mangalā "Favorable", aspect of the Goddess, venerated notably in Orissa as Adiśakti in aniconic form (stones); in Kakatpur it is worshipped in the form of an ancient bd. statue of Tārā, and invoked by divination rites for the construction of the idol of Jagannātha | navakalevara | ; its puja is celebrated every Tuesday for a month, starting from caitrī || thai mongkhon. mangalam bhūyāt good luck! samāptikāmo mangalam ācaret He who wishes to carry out his undertaking must begin by formulating a blessing. mangalo bhūmiputraścarnahartā dhanapradah | sthirāsano mahākāyaḥ sarvakarmavirodhakaḥ || [SkP.] mangala, son of the earth, removes debts and bestows wealth; firmly established, of great stature, he hinders all action.
mangalakalaśa | kalaśa | m. soc. earthenware water pot covered with a coconut, used at the time of festivals, not. in śivarātri and in Jain rituals.

mangalapura [pura] n. geo. np. of the city of mangalapura on the West coast of South India (mod. Mangalore); it was an important bd. center until the 11th century, site of the temple of Mangaladevī Tārā and at the Kadri hill of the temple of Avalo kiteśvara, later converted into Mañjunātha.
mangalavacas [vacas] n. blessing; congratulation.
mangalavat |vat| amnf mangalavatī Which brings luck; blessed.

mangalavāda [vāda] m. blessing; congratulation | lit. not. prayers of blessing at the beginning of a work, aimed at countering obstacles to its proper understanding | lit. not. chapter of the Tattva cintāmani.
mangalavāra [vāra] m. Tuesday, March Day.
mangalaśloka | śloka | m. lit. auspicious stance inaugurating a work.

mangalasūtra [sūtra] n. soc. ["beneficial thread"] a cord that the groom ties around his bride's neck during the wedding ceremony, and which she must keep as long as he lives | lit. verses of blessing at the beginning of a work. mangalācaraņa [ācaraņa] n. soc. blessing, prayer for the success of an undertaking; preliminary invocation | pl. lit. litanies of invocation to the gods serving as an introduction to a work.
mangalārtha [artha] m. meaning of good omen.
mangalika [mangalaika] n. amulet.
mangalya [mangalaya] amnf mangalyā of good omen — n. lucky charm; favorable prayer.
mangalyabhikṣā [bhikṣā] f. soc. gift of a pledge of happiness; not. of living long with one's spouse.
mac iic. mat.
maccitta | citta | amnf maccittā Who has their mind fixed on themselves.
maccharīra | śarīra | n. my body.
majamudāra [Arabic] m. title Majumdār of notary or archivist, used as np. in Ben gale.

√ (majjya) pf. (ut, ni, nis) plunge into (acc. loc.), penetrate; be immersed, sink | drown, perish, fall (into hell) — ca. (majjayati) immerse, drown; flood | cause to penetrate, drive in | lat. mergo; ang. to merge; fr. immerger.
majján [agt. majj] m. bone marrow; sap, juice.
majjana [act. majj] n. immersion, ablution, bath; perdition, fall (into hell).

majjas [abstr. majj] n. marrow — f. majjā id. ਸਡ mañca m. platform, stage; terrace; canopy; pedestal; sentry box | bed, couch. mañcāḥ krośanti the children (on the bed) are crying (classical example of metaphor | lakṣaṇā|).
mañcaka [ka] mn platform, dais, terrace; pedestal, throne | bed, couch.
mañcukā f. cf. madanamañcukā.
mañjara n. cluster of flowers; ear | pearl — f. cf. mañjarī — v. [11] pr. (mañjarayati) to decorate with clusters of flowers.
mañjarika |ika| amnf mañjarikā decorated with clusters of flowers | lit. ["in flowery style"] is said of the verses of the Bhajagovinda.
mañjarī [f. mañjara] f. bouquet, bunch of flowers | flower, bud, shoot — ifc. ["bouquet de"] names literary works.
mañjiṣṭha [super. mañju] amnf mañjisthā dark red, madder red — f. mañjiṣṭhā bio. bot. Rubia munjista, madder.
mañjisthakula [kula] n. bio. family Rubiaceae.
mañjīra n. ankle ring — f. mañjīrā ifc. id.

mañju amnf pretty, pleasant, graceful, charming. mañjughoșa |ghoșa| m. bd. np. of Mañjughoșa "with the melodious voice", civilizing Buddhist saint of Nepal, identified as the accomplished [bodhisattva] Mañjuśrī; cf. vāgīśvara.
Mañjunātha [nātha] m. myth. n.p. of Mañjunātha, identification with Siva of Mañjuśrī; cf. mangalapura.
mañjuvādin [vādin] m. whose speech is gracious — f. mañjuvādinī lit. [DKC.] np. of the princess of Vidarbha mañjuvādinī "Eloquent", daughter of Anan tavarmā and Vasuṃdharā; she married Viśruta.

Mañjuśrī [śrī] m. bd. np. of the accomplished [bodhisattva] Mañjuśrī "Gracious Saint", deification of the monk Manjughosa; eternally young, symbolizing Knowledge [prajñā₂], guardian of the eastern paradise, he is often depicted with an erect flaming sword [jñānakhadga] (Knowledge that cuts through ignorance) and a 5-pointed crown; his mount is a lion; his cult spread in China in the 8th century.
mañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti [nāmansaṃgīti] f. bed. bd. n.p. from the Mañjuśrīnāmasamgīti "Song of the names of Mañjuśrī", text of Buddha's teaching to his divine disciple Vajrapāni.

mañjuśrīyaśas [yaśas] m. bd. of np. Mañjuśrīyaśā, 1st Kalkī king of Sambhala; he would have lived in the 2nd century BC. he is attributed the Laghutantra or Laghukālacakratantra, which establishes the Kālacakra doctrine.
mañjula [mañjula] amnf mañjulā pretty, pleasant, graceful, charming.
Mañjulikā [ika] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of Mañjulikā, borrowed name of the princess Bandhumatī, dis simulated by the queen Vāsavadattā₂; the king Udayana seduced her, but was pardoned.

mañjūṣā f. box, casket, case; chest | lit. collection | gram. cf. Laghumañjūṣā | var. mañjuṣā id. ਸਠ matha mn soc. hermit's cell; cloister, hermitage, monastery, place of residence for renunciants |sannyāsin|; college for young priests. devālayo devagrham caityam āyatanam maṭhaḥ [Nāmamālā] dwelling of God, house of God, sanctuary, temple, hermitage (synonyms). mațhādhipati [adhipati] m. soc. superior of my nastery.
Maṭhāmnāya [āmnāya] m. lit. np. of the Mathāmnāya, text specifying the regulations of a monastery [maṭha], attributed to Śaṅkarācārya.
maní m. jewel, precious stone, pearl, crystal; ornament | glans penis; clitoris | gram. cf. Tatt vacintāmaņi, Siddhāntaśiromaņi.
manikana [kana] m. bed. n.p. from the manikana, a work by Nyāya of unknown author.

Manikantha₁ [kantha] m. organic. blue jay | myth. n.p. of Manikantha₁, epith. of Ayyappā "wearing a jewel around his neck" (on the necklace given at his birth by Mohinī and Šiva) | hist. n.p. by the logician Manikantha₁ Miśra, author of the Nyāyaratna (around 1300). manîkarna [karna] amnf Manikarnī who wears an ear ornament — f. maṇikarṇī myth. n.p. of Manikarnī, tutelary goddess |adhiṣṭhātrī| of Benares.

maníkarnikā [karnika] f. geo. np. of the sacred Manikarnikā pond in Benares; Manikarnī in the East the tutelary goddess | lit. [DKC.] np. of Maņikarņikā, daughter of Prince Candaghoșa and Acāravatī; she was orphaned from birth; King Candasimha ordered that she be raised in secret in an underground palace, which Arthapāla discovered while digging a tunnel; her mother had lost a dice bet with Kāntimatī before her birth, and therefore she was to marry her son Arthapāla.
maṇikarṇikāghaṭṭa [ghaṭṭa] m. geo. np. of the manikarnikāghatta, 2nd place of cremation in Benares.
Manigrīva [grīvā] m. myth. np. of the genius [guhyaka] Manigrīva "with jeweled neck", son of Ku bera; cf. Nalakūbara.

manicūda | cūdā | m. lit. np. of Manicūda "born with a diadem [cūḍāmaṇi]", hero of the Lokānanda; he substitutes for the victim of a human sacrifice, and is taken up to heaven by Garuda; his character is adapted under the name of Jīmūtavāhana in Harşa's Nāgānanda.
manídhanus [dhanus] n. ["jeweled bow"] rainbow.

manípadma [padma] amnf manipadmā por tant le jewelau et le lotus — f. maṇipadmā bd. np. de manipadmā "She who bears the jewel and the lotus", epith. of Avalokitesvara in his feminine form. om manipadme hum bd. "O You who bear the jewel and the lotus", Buddhist mantra evoking manipadmā; sometimes called vidyāṣaḍakṣarī or 6-syllable formula.
manípuskara [puskara] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Manipuskara, conch of Sahadeva.

manípūra [pūra] m. navel — n. geo. np. of the city (mod. Imphal in Manipur) and of the kingdom of Maṇipūra or Maṇipura "Abundant in jewels"; cf. Citravāhana | myth. [Mah.] city of Kalinga, visited by Arjuna | phil. [yoga] 3rd energy center [cakra], located at the level of the solar plexus; it is represented by a blue lotus with 10 petals; in the center, a red triangle symbolizes the element of fire, and bears the bījamantra 'raṃ'; this chakra controls the sense of sight; it is the psychic center of the vital force.
maníprabhā [prabhā₂] f. lit. np. of the Maniprabhā, commentary on the Yogasūtra due to Rāmānanda₂ Sa rasvatī₂.
manípravāla [pravāla] n. ["rubies and coral"] medieval literary language of Kerala, mixture of Sanskrit and Malayālam.
maníbandha | bandha | m. wearing of jewelry | wrist (where jewelry is worn).

maníbhadra [bhadra] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of the yakṣa king Maṇibhadra "fortunate in jewels"; Tārāvalī is his daughter | lit. | KSS. | np. of Manibhadra₁, younger brother of Kubera; Madanamañjarī is his wife.
maṇíbhūmi [bhūmi] f. room in a palace for bathing, with a floor made of a mosaic of precious stones.
maṇibhūmikā [bhūmikā] f. mosaic in precious stones.
maṇibhūmikākarma | karman | n. the making of precious stone mosaics, one of the 64 |kalā| arts.
manimat |mat| amnf manimatī adorned with jewels — f. maṇimatī myth. np. of Manimatī "Full of jewels", rich capital of the nivātakavacās.
manimaya |maya| amnf manimayī made of crystal; made of jewels.
manímālā [mālā] f. necklace of pearls or jewels trace of circular bite on the skin (not. during love games).
manirāga [rāga] m. coloring of a jewel — n. rub bis; syn. mānikya, padmarāga.
maṇirāgākarajñāna [ākarajñāna] n. the knowledge of the colors and places of origin of gems, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
manistambha [stambha] m. post in the center of a pool | crystal pillar.
maṇika [maṇika] m. jewel, gem | hist. n.p. of Manika, maithila theater author (14th); we owe him the drama Bhairavānandanāṭaka.
manita n. cries of pleasure from a woman during intercourse.
maṇiva [maṇiva] m. myth. ["who wears a jewel on her hood"] nāga.
√ maṇḍ v. [1] pr. (maṇḍati) pp. (maṇḍita) to adorn, to decorate — ca. (mandayati) id. ਸਾਤ maṇḍa [agt. maṇḍ] mn scum (from cooking rice, milk, etc.); cream; essence.
maṇḍaka |agt. maṇḍ| mf maṇḍikā pancake, pancake.

maṇḍana act. maṇḍ amnf maṇḍanā which adorns, which decorates (g.) — m. hist. n.p. of Mandana Miśra ācārya, Mīmāmsaka philosopher born in Bihāra (8th century), student of Kumārila; we owe him not. the Mīmāmsānukramaņī, the Vidhivi veka, the Bhāvanaviveka, the Vibhramaviveka and the Sphotasiddhi; cf. Sureśvara | hist. n.p. from Grammai nothing Jain Mandana₁ Mantrī, prime minister of King Hośāmga Ghorī of Mālava (15th century); we owe him the Upasargamandana, supplement to the Kavikal padruma — n. ornament, adornment, decoration — f. mandanā ifc. id.
mandapa mn arch. open hall in a temple, pavilion, pillared porch; tent; greenery cradle. mandapaksetra consecrated territory.
maṇḍapaka [ka] m. id — f. maṇḍapikā small pa villon; shelter, lean-to.

Mandapadurga [durga] m. geo. n.p. the Mandapadurga fort, established on a steep hill in Mālava (mod. Mandu in Madhya Pradesh, 70 km southwest of Indore); the fort has existed since the 6th century, it was the fortified place of the Pa ramāra kings, of which it became the capital in the 12th century; the region was devastated by the Sultan of Delhi Kaljī in 1293; the fort fell in 1305, and Alau'dDin Kaljī an annexed the Mālava kingdom to the Delhi Sultanate; in 1401 its governor Dilawar Khan declared independence, and his son Alp Khan, under the title of Sultan Hoshang Shah, made it his capital and completed the fortifications; Mahmud Shah Kaljī built many monuments there.

maṇḍala mn circle, disc | soc. ritual diagram | group, grouping | lit. one of the 10 divisions of the Rigveda, grouped into hymns [sūkta] | soc. [Arthaśāstra] ["circle of neighboring kingdoms" geometric conception of relations between kingdoms by concentric circles; beyond the immediate enemy [ari], one finds the

allies [mitra], the enemy's allies [arimitra], the allies of allies [mitramitra], and the allies of the enemy's allies [arimitramitra]; in the opposite direction, the rear attacker [pārṣnigrāha], the rear course [ākranda], the support of the attack
quant [pāṛṣṇigṛāhasāra] and the support of the relief [ākrandasāra]. mandalīkr to round off. maṇḍalībhū to bend (arc); to curve; to become circular.
mandalabrāhmaṇa [brāhmaṇa] n. lit. np. of the Mandalabrāhmanopanisad of the Šuklayajurveda; it deals with integral yoga [rājayoga]; the Rājayogabhāsya is a commentary on it.
maṇḍalārādhana [ārādhana] n. soc. worship of a ritual diagram.
mandalin [in] amnf mandalinī circular — ifc. surrounding (iic.).
maṇḍalita [maṇḍalaita] amnf mandalitā coiled. mandalitahastakāndam adv. [DKC.] by making the stem of its trunk whirl.
mandalitahasta [hasta] m. (elephant) with a curled trunk.
maṇḍalī iiv. maṇḍala.
mandalīkarana [karana] n. act of rounding: circular arrangement.
maṇḍalīkāram [kāram] ind. rounding.
mandalīkṛta [kṛta] amnf mandalīkṛtā rounded, curved; curved (arc).
maṇḍalībhāva | bhāva | m. circular form; circu larity.
mandalībhūta [bhūta] amnf mandalībhūtā ar rounded, curved, bent; stretched, bent (bow).
maṇḍita [pp. maṇḍ] amnf maṇḍitā ornate, decorated.
manditastambha | stambha | mr. arch. corner pillar.
maṇḍitikā [ika] f. bed. ornament of (iic.).
mandī f. geo. np. of the sacred city of Mandī, in Himachal Pradesh, on the banks of the Beās River; it possesses not. a Tri lokīnātha shrine.
maṇḍu m. myth. n.p. of the wise |rṣi| maṇḍu.

maṇḍūka mf maṇḍūkī bio. zoo. frog; in poetry it evokes the gregarious instinct and the spirit of parochialism; the croaking of frogs signals the beginning of the monsoon | arch. grid diagram with 8 sides, with 64 squares; it is drawn in rice during the rites of crowning a building; syn. candita. mandūkaparņa [parṇa] m. bio. bot. Oroxylum in dicum, trumpet vine of India, used in medicine — f. mandūkaparnī med. medicinal plant, used to treat cerebral activity.
mandūkapluti [pluti] f. frog jump | gram. discontinuity in the scope of a contextual condition in the anuvrtti.
mandūkaplutinyāya [nyāya] m. gram. maxim of the frog jump, explaining by analogy a discontinuity in the scope of a rule [anuvṛtti].
maṇḍūkayoga [yoga] m. yoga posture of immobility. mandūkašikṣā [śikṣā] f. lit. np. of the Mandūkašikṣā "doctrine of the frog", collection of texts of the Vedic school of the Māṇḍūkās
mat var. mac, mad₂ [abl. aham] ind. of me — iic. me, from me, to me, by me.
matkṛta | kṛta | amnf matkṛtā made by me.
matpara | para | amnf matparā devoted to me.
matputra | putra | m. my son.
matpūrva |pūrva| amnf matpūrvā prior to me.
matsaṃsthā |saṃsthā₂| f. union with me; refuge in me.
mat forms a. (replaces vat after th. in i, ī, u, ū, r, o, is or us).

matá [pp. man] amnf matā thought; believed, imagined, understood | esteemed; desired — n. doctrine, belief, opinion; point of view | resolution; intention; desire, wish | mod. vote. mate according to the point of view of g. . ahameva mato mahīpateḥ [RV.] I am the only one to be considered the king.
matabheda | bheda | m. difference of opinion (with gisaha₂ ).
matávat [vat] amnf matavatī which has a goal; resolved.
mataikya | aikya | n. uniformity of opinion.

matam |acc. mata| iic. matámga var. Matanga [ga₁] m. ["who goes where he wants"] elephant | myth. [Rām.] np. of the ṛṣi Mataṅga; his hermitage was at Rsyamūka; when Vālī killed Dundubhi, some of his blood splashed onto the hermitage; Matanga cursed his superior to die if he came to Ŗṣyamūka; Sugrīva took refuge there; |Raghuvamśa| he cursed the gandharva Priyamvada who had bathed upstream of the river from him; he should prowl like a wild elephant until he is struck by an arrow from Aja.

Matangadeva [deva] m. lit. [KSS.] np. from the vidyādhara Matangadeva, servant of King Gaurimunda; the latter asked him to kill Naravāhanadatta; Šiva cursed him to be cast down to Earth as a candāla with his daughter Suratamanjarī; the curse would end if the father of a suitor of his daughter managed to invite 18000 brahmins to eat at his house as a wedding gift; this would be Pālaka.
matangaparameśvara [parameśvara] lit. m. np. of the Matangaparameśvarāgama, a work of Kashmiri Shaivism from the 10th century; it was commented on by Bhatta Rāmakantha.
matámgaja [gaja] m. elephant; not. one of the 8 elephants of the cardinal points | math. symb. the number 8.

máti [act. man] f. thought, intention, resolution opinion, judgment, belief mind, intelligence; memory | esteem, respect; wisdom | gr. ; lat. mens; ang. mind; fr. mental, demented. mama matyā in my opinion. matim kṛ var. matim dhā to decide to (loc. dat. acc.prati.
matímat |mat| amnf matimatī intelligent, clever, cunning | wise, prudent.
matup nota. gram. secondary formation [taddhita] of adjectives in mat or in vat, meaning "possessing".
matvartha [artha] m. gram. meaning of the suffix mat/ vat; not. abundance, being worthy of praise or blame, permanent presence, excess, and contact.
matkuna [related to kuna] m. insect; not. pu naise (of bed) — n. gaiters.
matta |pp. mad₁| amnf mattā drunk, intoxicated with (iic.); furious; delighted, joyful, passionate; excited in rut (not. elephant).
mattahaṃsasvaraḥ [Rām.] in a voice like the cry of a hamsa in love (said of Rāma addressing his brother Bharata₁).
mattakāla [kāla₁] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of mattakāla, king of the Lāṭās; he besieged Vīraketu, and forced him to give him his daughter Vāmalocanā; he was killed by Somadatta₂.
mattamātaṃga | mātaṃga | m. elephant in rut.
mattamātamgagāmin ["who has the gait of an elephant in rut" | majestic.

mattavilāsa |vilāsa| mr. bed. n.p. from the satirical play [prahasana] mattavilāsa "Drunkards' Games", composed by the Pallava king Mahendravarmā₁ in the 7th century; it mocks the excesses of the pāśupata, kāpālika, and bauddha sects by depicting drunken ascetics.
mattas cl. mat.
matyá₁ n. harrow; roller | leveling of a terrain | mus. rhythmic cycle [tāla] comprising 1 laghu, 1 druta and 1 laghu.
matya₂ [mataya] n. means of knowledge.
matvā [abs. man] ind. having thought.

matsará [mad₁sara] amnf matsarā ved. that which exalts, that which intoxicates | joyful, gay | selfish, in old; jealous, hostile — m. selfishness; envy, jealousy; passion for (loc. iic.) | anger; hostility; rage | soc. ["the intoxicating"] qualifies the soma.
matsaramanas | manas | amnf of selfish disposition.
matsarin [in] amnf matsariņī envious; in old loc. .

mátsya m. Fish | myth. np. of Matsya₁ the Fish, 1st avatar of Viṣṇu, who found in the waters the Veda which had been hidden there by the demon Hayagriva; he saved from the waters the seven sages |saptarși|, who clung to his horn during the primordial flood; he is celebrated at the full moon |pūrṇimā| of the month kārttika | myth. |Mah.| np. of Matsya₁, son of Uparicara whose sperm had been swallowed by the Fish nymph Adrikā; he was found in her womb with his sister Matsyagandhī by the fisherman Dāsarāja — n. lit. cf. Matsyapurāņa | pl. matsyās geo. name of the country Matsya₁ (between modern Delhi and Jaipur) and of its people the Matsyās; cf. Virāţa. matsyā iva janā nityam bhakṣayanti parasparam Like fish, men devour each other endlessly.

matsyagandha [gandha] amnf Matsyagandhī who smells of the Fish — f. Matsyagandhī myth. np. of Matsyagandhī, epith. of Satyavatī found in the belly of the Fish Adrikā by the fisherman Dāsarāja, who collected her; taking the sage Parāśara across the Yamunā, he freed her from her smell in exchange for his favors, which gave birth to Vyāsa; she then married King Sāmtanu mad with her beauty to give birth to the princes Citrāngada and Vicitravīrya; After their death without an heir, she brought Vyāsa to fulfill his duty of niyoga and continue the lineage by fathering Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu, whose descendants would fight in the great fratricidal battle of Mah.

matsyapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. of the Matsya₁ purāṇa or Mātsyapurāṇa "Tale of the time of the Poison," mixed mythological text, in 291 chapters [adhyāya]; its ancient parts are dated to the 3rd century; it relates the flood where Vișnu incarnated as Matsya₁ saved Manu clinging to his horn; of an encyclopedic nature, it includes several sections of vastuvidyā, not. on the construction of temples and their decoration.

matsyamudrā [mudrā] f. soc. gesture of the Fish, performed by the priest on a water pot before offering it to the deity; the two hands are superimposed flat horizontally, right hand on the left, palms towards the ground, thumbs spread apart, other fingers joined and extended; the thumbs are turned to swim.
matsyād |ad₂| amnf who eats fish.
Matsyendra [indra] m. hist. np. of the yoga master Matsyendra; cf. matsyendranātha.

matsyendranātha [nātha] m. hist. de np. matsyendranātha "Born of a fish", accomplished [mahāsiddha] who founded the school of hathayoga in Nepal in the 10th century; he was the master [guru] of Gorakṣanātha; he is revered by Buddhists as well as Hindus as the patron saint of Nepal; he reformed the kula doctrine and established the kaula yoginī; the Kaulajñānanirnaya is attributed to him.
math cf. manth.
matha |act. manth| mr. cf. mātha.
mathana [agt. manth] amnf mathanī that upsets, that destroys — act. n. mathana barat tage; damage, destruction; cf. kṣīrodamathana.
mathin [agt. manth] m. [sg. nom. manthās, acc. manthānam, dat. mathe; pl. acc. mathas, dat. mathibhyas | stick (for churning or making fire).

Mathura (f. geo. np.) of Mathura, a city in the Vrji region of the province of Agra on the right bank of the Yamuna; myth. It was conquered by Satrughna; Krishna was born there; it is also called Madhura, "the gentle city"; it is one of the seven cities
sacred | saptapurī |.

Mathurānātha₁ | nātha | mr. myth. n.p. from Ma thurānātha, epith. of Kṛṣṇa “Lord of mathurā” | hist. n.p. of Mathurānātha₁ Tar kavāgīśa, logician of the Navyanyāya (~1600 ~1675), son of Rāma Tarkālankāra; student of Rāmabhadra₁ Sārvabhauma; he is the author of the Tattvacintāmaņirahasya or Māthurī, the Pañcalakṣaṇīsarvasva and the Vyāptipañcakarahasya.
mathurāvat [vat] amnf mathurāvatī as in mathurā.
mad₁ iic. mat.

√ mad₁ v. [4] pr. (mādyati) aor. [5] (amādīt) pp. (matta) pf. (ut, pra) to get drunk; to be drunk | to rejoice; to get excited — ca. (mad₁áyati) ca. r. (mādayate) to get drunk; to rejoice gr. ; lat. madeo; ang. mad₁.
madartha [artha] m. my own use. madartham var. madarthe adv. for my own use, for myself.
madāśraya [āśraya] amnf madāśrayā who takes refuge in me.
madīya |īya| amnf madīyā poss. my, mine, belonging to me, of me.
madgrha [grha] n. my house.
maddhasta [hasta] m. my hand.
maddhastagata | gata| amnf maddhastagatā which is in my hand. maddhastagatās te dīnārāh these coins are in my hands.
madbhakta | bhakta | amnf madbhaktā who is my follower.
madvacana [vacana] amnf madvacanā who speaks about me, who speaks for me — abl. madva canāt adv. in my name.

Mada | act. mad₁ | m. intoxication | madness, fury; passion for (i.e.); sexual excitement, rut | bio. fronta line, sweat from the temples of the rutting elephant | intoxicating liquor, alcohol | pride, presumption | myth. np. of Mada, pride personified (or intoxication).
mádajala [jala] n. bio. frontaline, serous fluid which oozes from the temples of the elephant in rut; its strong odor is compared to that of the cinchona tree [saptacchada].
madayitnú [yitnu] amnf intoxicant — m. li
queur | drunken man | myth. epith. of Kāma, the intoxicating Love | var. madayisnu id.
mádalekhā [lekhā] f. line on the temples formed by the oozing frontal bone of the rutting elephant | lit. |K.| np. of the nymph Madalekhā, confidante of Kādambarī.
mádavihvala [vihvala] amnf madavihvalā under the influence of passion.
mádavihvalita [vihvalita] amnf madavihvalitā id.
madasthana | sthāna | n. mod. bar.
mádahetu [hetu] m. organic. bot. Woodfordia fru ticosa, flamboyant shrub; syn. dhātakī, ma danīyahetu.
madāndha | andha | amnf madāndhā blinded by pride, desire, drunkenness or anger; unleashed.
madāmada | amada| amnf madāmadā phil. passionate and impassive at the same time (qualifies the dual nature of the Soul [ātman]).
madotkāta [utkata] amnf madotkātā drunk | excited; arrogant; violent — m. lit. [PT.] np. of the lion madotkāṭa; he promised protection to a camel, but his court decided otherwise.

mádana [agt. mad₁] m. Carnal love, passion | myth. np. of Madana Love, a name of the god Kāma — act. n. drunkenness, excitement, intoxication — f. madanā var. madanī intoxicating drink — f. madanā ifc. passion for. madanavahniśikhāvalī f. the flame of the fires of Love.
mádanacaturdaśī [caturdaśī] f. soc. festival in honor of Kāma, on the 14th day of the clear fortnight of the month caitra.
mádanatrayodaśī [trayodaśī] f. soc. festival in honor of Kāma, on the 13th day of the clear fortnight of the month caitra.

madanadaṃṣṭrā [daṃṣṭrā] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of Queen Madanadamstrā "Bite of Love", wife of King Vīrabhuja and then of Rākṣasa Yamadamstra in Sailapura; Indīvarasena married her, provoking the jealousy of Khadgadamṣṭrā; she is the vidyādharī Candravatī punished for her jealousy.
mádanadamana [damana] m. myth. np. of mada nadamana, epith. of Śiva "who tames his passions" by annihilating desire Kāma.
mádanadvādaśī [dvādaśī] f. soc. festival in honor of Kāma, on the 12th day of the clear fortnight of the month caitra.
mádanadhvajā [dhvajā] f. soc. festival in honor of Kāma, on the 15th day of the bright fortnight of the month caitra.

Madanamañcukā [mañcukā] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of Madanamañcukā, daughter of the vidyādhara madanavega and Princess Kalingasenā, incarnation of Rati; she married Naravāhanadatta and became his first wife; she was abducted by Mānasavega but thanks to Vegavatī, was able to find Naravāhanadatta.
Madanamañjarī [mañjarī] f. bed. [KSS.] np. of Madanamañjarī, daughter of Dundubhi₂, wife of Manibhadra₁.
madanamaha | maha | mr. soc. spring festival, in honor of Kāma; syn. madanotsava.

madanamahotsava | mahotsava | m. soc. spring festival, in honor of Kāma; it is described by Harşa in his Ratnāvalī₁, as celebrated at Kauśāmbī in the time of Udayana; the men dance and sing [carcarī], the women throw jets of colored water and green powder at them; syn. madanamaha, madanotsava.
mádanamodaka | modaka | m. stimulant candy made from cannabis.
mádanamohana | mohana | m. myth. np. of Ma danamohana, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "who leads the god Kāma astray".
mádanalekha | lekha | mf madanalekhā love letter.

mádanavat |vat| amnf Madanavatī filled with love — f. Madanavatī reads. n.p. of the nymph [apsaras] Madanavatī, heroine of the drama Bhairavānandanāṭaka | bed. [Viddhaśālabhañjikā] np. of Queen Madanavatī₁, wife of King Vidyādharamalla.
mádanavaśa [vaśa] amnf madanavaśā under the sway of love; in love.

madanavega [vega] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara king madanavega, who impersonated Udayana to seduce Kalingasenā and give birth to Ma danamañcukā; we will learn that in fact Ityoka is their son, and that Madanamañcukā is the incarnation of Rati.
Madanasenā [senā] f. bed. [KSS.] np. of Princess Madanasenā, daughter of Vīrabhaṭa, first wife of Sūryaprabha₁.
madanānkuśa [ankuśa] m. penis.
madanāntaka [antaka] m. myth. n.p. of Ma danāntaka, epith. of Šiva "who destroyed Kāma".
madanāśaya [āśaya] m. sexual desire.
madanikā [ikā] f. exciting woman | geo. type of sculpture of a pretty woman, not. at the temple of Belūr.
madanīya [īya] amnf madanīyā intoxicating; that which excites desire.
madanīyahetu | hetu| mr. organic. bot. Woodfordia fruticosa, flamboyant shrub; syn. dhātakī, mada hetu.
madanotsava | utsava | mr. soc. spring festival, in honor of Kāma; syn. madanamaha, madanamahotsava.
madira [mad₁ira] amnf madirā who intoxicates, exciting — f. cf. madirā.
madirā [f. madira] f. wine, liqueur, alcohol, intoxicating beverage | lit. [K.] np. of the nymph Ma dirā "Intoxicating", first queen of the gandharva king Citraratha, mother of Kādambarī.

madirāvat [vat] amnf madirāvatī containing alcohol; intoxicating — f. madirāvatī lit. [KSS.] np. of the Madirāvatī princess, in love with a Brah Mane; she is the heroine of the eponymous 13th chapter of the KSS.
madgú m. organic. zoo. Anhinga rufa, plon bird
ger | bio. cormorant | water snake | war galley.
madgura [ra] m. type of fish (catfish?).
mádya [pfp. [1] ca. mad₁] amnf madyā intoxicating, euphoric — n. wine, liqueur.
madrá [mad₁ra] m. geo. ["happy country"] np. of Madra, region and people of Pañjāb | its king; cf. Salya | pl. madrās the inhabitants of Madra.
mádvan [mad₁van] amnf madvarī joyful, intoxicated | that rejoices, intoxicating — m. epith. of Śiva.
madhavya | Madhuya | amnf madhavyā made of honey.

mádhu amnf madhū f. madhvī sweet, sugary | pleasant, charming; delicious — n. Sweetness, honey, sugar | Vedic soma, liquor of immortality; the Aśvinau are fond of it — m. epith. of the first month Vedic of spring, caitra | spring | myth. np. of King Madhu, son of Kārtavīrya; Vṛṣṇi is said to be the eldest of his hundred sons | myth. np. of the asura Madhu₁ "Sweetness"; with his brother Kaiṭabha they were born as drops of dew in the primordial lotus that sprang from the navel of Vișnu (or sprang from the earwax of the sleeping Vișnu); they obtained from Devī, through great penances, the right to die only if they wished; they personify pride; Vishnu fought them in vain, then, faced with their arrogance, asked them for a wish that would allow him to kill them; the Earth was formed from their fat; they were reincarnated as Khara and Atikāya | myth. np. of the asura Madhu₂, who was killed by Satrughna | |madhudruma| cf. madhūka | pl. madhavas soc. the people of Madhu; syn. yādavās — v. [11] pr. (madhusyati) v. [11] pr. (madhvasyati) to want honey | gr. ; lat. mel; ang. mead; all. Meth; fr. miel. prasangamadhu spring honey.
madhukara | kara₁ | mf madhukarī bee.
madhukarkaṭī | karkaṭī | f. organic. bot. Carica papaya, papaya.
madhukaiṭabha [Kaiṭabha] m. of. myth. Madhu₁ and Kaitabha.
madhukaiṭabhāri [ari] m. myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa "Enemy of Madhu₁ and Kaiṭabha".
madhudruma | druma | m. cf. madhūka. madhudviş [dviş₂] m. myth. np. of Madhudvit, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "Enemy of Madhu₁".
madhupa [pa₁] m. bee ["that drinks sap"].

madhuparka [parka] m. sweet drink made from fermented milk and honey; soc. its welcoming offering to a guest. samāmsa madhuparka offering to a passing guest of curdled milk with honey accompanied by meat (pres
Vedic [āmnāya] description).
madhupākā [pāka] f. sweet melon.
mádhuphala [phala] m. coconut tree — f. madhuphalā watermelon.
madhumat [mat] amnf madhumatī sweet; sugary — m. (country) where honey is found.
madhumattama [tama] amnf madhumattamā super. very sweet. jihvā me madhumattamā may my tongue be sua vissime.
madhumādhava [mādhava] m. of. the two months of spring, caitra and vaiśākha.

madhumukula [mukula] mn bud of madhūka. nitambah samvādam masrnamanivedyā mrgayate manāggaņdah pāṇdurmadhumukulalakṣmīm tu layati Her rump seeks to equal an altar made of polished pearls; her cheek, which pales a little, equals in beauty the bud of the madhūka.
mádhurasa | rasa | m. sweet taste; pleasure | cane juice; palm wine — f. madhurasā np. of various plants — amnf madhurasā sweet.
mádhulih [lih₂] m. bio. bee.
mádhuvrata | vrata | n. bee.
madhusarpis | sarpis | n. of. madhusarpiṣī honey and butter.

mádhusūdana |sūdana| m. myth. np. of Madhusūdana, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "Destroyer of the asura Madhu₁" | hist. np. of the philosopher Madhusūdana₁ Sarasvatī₂, born Kamalajanāyana in Bengal in the 16th century; he became an ascetic at a young age, his teacher was Viśveśvara Sarasvatī₂; he studied in Navadvīpa, and settled in Vārāṇasī; he was honored at the court of the Mughal emperor Akbar; he is the author of works of Advaita vedānta, and not. of the Advaita siddhi, the Prasthānabheda and the Siddhāntabindu; his Gūdhārthadīpikā is a commentary on the Gītā.
Madhvācārya [ācārya] m. hist. np. and title of the master Madhvācārya; cf. Madhva.
madhuka [Madhuka] amnf madhukā sweet; melodious; honey-colored — m. cf. madhūka.

madhura [Madhura] amnf madhurā sweet, mellow, charming, harmonious | (dishes) tasty; sweet — m. phil. [Nyāya] the sweet, a type of taste |rasa|; |Bṛhajjātaka| it is associated with the planet Jupiter [Guru] — f. cf. madhurā. madhuram adv. pleasantly.
madhuratā [tā] f. Sweetness.
madhuratva |tva| n. id.
madhurāmla | amla | amnf madhurāmlā sour sweet.
madhurālāpa [ālāpa] amnf madhurālāpā of pleasant address; who speaks sweet words — m. melodious song.
Madhurāṣṭaka |aṣṭaka| n. lit. np. of the Madhurāṣṭaka, a collection of 8 devotional verses dedicated to the beauty of Kṛṣṇa due to Vallabhācārya.
madhurokta | ukta | amnf madhuroktā kindly said.

Madhurā₁ [f. madhura] f. geo. np. of Madhurā₁ "the Sweet City", epith. of Mathurā | myth. np. of Madhurā₁, celestial nymph who visited Kailāsa to honor Shiva and who united with him; Pārvatī cursed her to become a frog for 12 years; Shiva promised her that at the end of the 12 years she would become a beautiful young girl and marry a prince; cf. Mandodarī.

madhūka [madhuuka] m. bee | bio. bot. Madhuca Latifolia, large Mahua tree of South India, with pale yellow flowers grouped at the ends of branches, with brown bark; used in medicine, not. Mahua oil extracted from its seeds; its flowers are evoked in poetry as symbols of beauty — n. its seed | beeswax.

mádhya amnf madhyā in the center, in the middle; average; ordinary — mn the middle, the center — n. math. a thousand billion (one million billion) — f. madhyā the middle one — ind. in the middle; among, between (g.) | lat. medius; ang. middle; all. Mitte; fr. médian, milieu. madhyena adv. in the middle of, between (g. iic.). madhye var. madhyāt prep. cl. among, in the middle of (iic.); in the presence of (g.). madhyekrtya adv. with regard to. eka iva mama putrāṇāṃ madhye only one among my sons. āvayormadhye yaścaurastam kathaya | PT. | Let us say which of us two is the thief. teṣām madhyātkākaḥ provāca [PT.] among them, the crow spoke.
mádhyaga |ga₁| amnf mádhyagā located in the middle of iic. g. .
madhyatā [tā] f. mediocrity.
Madhyadeśa [deśa] m. central region; middle of the body, trunk, belly | geo. np. of Madhyadeśa "Central Region (of Aryāvarta)", corr. to the Ganges plain.
madhyastha |stha| amnf madhyasthā |"that which stands in the middle" | indifferent, neutral, impartial; intermediary, middle.
madhyasthatā [tā] f. impartiality. alam sevayā madhyasthatām gṛhītvā bhaṇa enough flattery, speak impartially.
madhyānta [anta] iic. middle and end.

madhyāntavibhāga [vibhāga] m. bd. np. of the madhyāntavibhāga "Distinction between the middle way and the extremes", important work of the bd. Yogācāra; it comprises 112 verses [kārikā]; the original Sanskrit is known from a single manuscript, with a commentary [bhāṣya] by Vasubandhu, and a subcommentary | tīkā| by Sthiramati.
madhyāhna [ahna] m. midday.
madhyāhnasamdhyā [saṃdhyā] f. rite of celebration of the sun at its zenith.
madhyam [acc. madhya] iic.
madhyándina [dina] m. midday |soc. midday offering phil. np. of Madhyandina, disciple of Yājñavalkya.

madhyama [super. madhya] amnf madhyamā in the middle, central, intermediate; median; middle-aged | moderate, impartial, neutral; ordinary — m. [madhyamapuruṣa] gram. 2nd pers. | mus. 4th note of the Indian octave — n. middle of the body, waist, belt — f. cf. madhyamā || pali majjhima.
Madhyamaṭīkā [ṭīkā] f. bed. n.p. of the madhyamaţīkā, work of mīmāṃsā of Kumārila.
madhyamanyāya [nyāya] m. phil. medieval school of nyāya (4th to 12th centuries), with jaina predominance.
madhyamapadalopa | padalopa | m. gram. elision of a medial term in a compound word.
madhyamapadalopin [padalopin] m. gram. compound word [samāsa] with elision of a medial term, like chāyāvṛkṣa "tree (offering) shade".
madhyamaprahara [prahara] m. soc. midday guard (from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m.).

madhyamavyāyoga [vyāyoga] m. lit. np. of the one-act drama madhyamavyāyoga by Bhāsa; this "drama of the middle one" evokes the monster Ghatotkaca, whose mother, the ogress Hidimbā, demanded a human for a meal; he pursued the family of a Brahmin for this purpose; of the three brothers, the eldest was the father's favorite, the youngest the mother's; the middle one sacrificed himself and stayed behind; when Ghatotkaca called him: "O madhyama", it was Bhīma who appeared (he is the middle one of the Pāṇḍavās), and at Hiḍimbā's hermitage she recognized her husband and Ghatotkaca knew that he was his father, a happy ending.

Madhyamaka [madhyamaka] amnf madhyamikā middle | common — m. bd. Madhyamaka doctrine of the middle way of Nāgārjuna, nihilist school of bd. Mahāyāna — n. the inside of something — f. madhyamikā marriageable woman.
Madhyamakavṛtti [vṛtti] f. bd. n.p. from the Madhyamakavrtti, commentary on the Mūlamadhyamaka by Candrakīrti; cf. Pra sannapadā.
madhyamakaśāstra [śāstra] n. lit. np. from madhya makaśāstra "Teaching (of the way) of the Middle place", work of Nāgārjuna, major work of bd. Mahāyāna; cf. mādhyamika , Mūlamadhyamaka.

Madhyamakālamkāra [alamkāra] m. lit. np. of the Madhyamakālamkāra, phil. synthesis due to Sāntarakṣita between the conventional truth of bd. Yogācāra and the ultimate truth of the Madhyamaka, leading to the doctrine of the double truth.
madhyamakāvatāra [avatāra] m. bd. n.p. of the madhyamakāvatāra, commentary [bhāsya] of the Mūlamadhyamaka by Candrakīrti; Jayānanda commented on it.
madhyamā [f. madhyamā] f. the major; the matrix | [madhyamāvāc] phil. [Bhartṛhari] the conceptualized word, 2nd stage [vapus] of the manifestation of sound.
madhyamīya [madhyamaīya] amnf madhyamīyā central.
madhye [loc. madhya] ind. among, in the middle of; in the presence of g. .
madhyegangam [gangā] adv. in the Ganges.
madhyejalāt [jala] adv. out of the water.
madhyenagaram [nagara] adv. within the city.

Madhva [contr. Madhvācārya] m. hist. np. of Madhva or Madhvācārya, born in Pājaka near Udupī (1238–1317), philosopher opposed to the monism of Sankara₁ and Rāmānuja; he was a student of Acyutaprekṣa; he taught at the Kṛṣṇamaṭha of Udupī, south Karņāṭaka; he founded the realistic dvaita doctrine [tattvavāda], based on bhakti to Viṣṇu, who alone liberates by his grace; he is the author not. of the Anuvyākhyāna, the Tattvasankhyāna, the Tattvamuktāvalī and the Pramāṇalakṣaṇa; also of the commentary Brah masūtrabhāsya₃ of the Brahmasūtra, and of the commentary Mahābhāratatātparyanirnaya of the Mah.; his work is collectively called sarvamūla gran tha; he is said to be an incarnation of Mukhyaprāṇa, on par with Hanumān; his disappearance [antardhāna] in 1317 is a mystery; cf. Bhagavadgītābhāsya, Pūrnaprajña, Anandatīrtha, Dvādaśastotra.
madhvatantra [tantra] n. system (dualistic) of Madhva.

madhvatantramukhamardana | mukhamardana | n. lit. np. of the madhvatantramukhamardana "Slap in the face to the system of Madhva", virulent refutation of the doctrine of Madhva due to Appayya Dīkṣita, with his commentary madhvamatavidhvamsana.
madhvamata | mata| n. doctrine of Madhva.
madhvamatavidhvamsana [vidhvamsana] n. bed. n.p. from the madhvamatavidhvamsana "Refutation of the doctrine of Madhva", commentary on the Madhvatan tramukhamardana by Appayya Dīkṣita.

Madhvavijaya [vijaya] m. lit. np. of the Madhvavijaya, which recounts the life of Madhva. [adhva madhvādhvakantakoddhāra kantakoddhāra] of the m. lit. np. Madhvādhvakantakoddhāra "Removal of a thorn from the path of Madhva", work of Vijayīndra in defense of the doctrine of Madhva against the attacks of Appayya.

√ man v. [4] pr. r. (mányate) v. [8] pr. r. (ma nuté) pft. r. (mene) pp. (mata) pfp. (mantavya, manya) abs. (matvā, matya) pf. (anu, apa, abhi, ava, Pra, vi, sam) to think, reflect, judge | to know; to believe, imagine, suppose | to consider as, to hold in high regard (2 acc.) | to consider, to esteem, to value | to think little of dat. — ps. (manyáte) pp. (māna) to esteem highly, to appreciate, to honor — ca. (mānayati) ca. r. (mānayate) to honor, to respect — des. r. (mīmāṃsate) to reflect, to want to understand || gr. ; lat. moneo; all. meinen; ang. to mean. manye I think; it seems to me; it would seem. idam manye that's what I think. laghu man to disregard. sādhu man to approve; to hold in high esteem. sa tvam bahumanyate he has a high opinion of you. manyate caran he thinks he's walking. rājyam tṛṇāya manye I care about the kingdom as much as a straw.
man gram. form of primary nouns [krt₂]; mainly action nouns n. with accent on the root, also agent nouns m. with accent on the suffix.
mana iic. manas. mana_āpa₁ [āpa₁] amnf mana_āpā | "that reaches the heart"] attractive, moving. mana_icchā [icchā] f. intellectual desire.
manarañjana [rañjana] ifc. amnf manarañjanī which enchants the spirit of (iic.).
manah iic. manas.
manaḥśikṣā [śikṣā] f. bed. n.p. from the Manaḥśīkṣā “Spiritual Instruction”, a Vaiṣṇava devotional poem of 12 lines [stotra] by Raghunāthadāsa Gosvāmī.

manahśilā [śilā] fm manahśila yellow of the realgar. manaḥsaṃharaṇa saṃharaṇa n. phil. detachment of the mind from external objects. manaḥsvānin lit. [KSS.] np. of the young brahmin Manaḥsvāmī of Sivapura; he fell in love with the princess Śaśiprabhā₁, whom he saved from a furious elephant; thanks to the magical powers of a pill provided by the magician Mūladeva₁ he was transformed into a woman, and presented to the king by the magician transformed into an old brahmin as the betrothed of his son, whom he went to fetch from afar; the king accepted her guardianship, and admitted Manahsvāmī daughter into the gynaeceum with Sasiprabhā₁; By removing the pill, he became a man again to unite with Sasiprabhā₁, but took the pill again during the day as a woman; Mūladeva₁ returned to see the king with his son Sāśī, in fact Manaḥsvāmī, to reclaim the promised wife; the king apologized for his absence, and to appease Mūladeva₁ offered his daughter Saśiprabhā₁ in his place, which officially united the lovers.
manána [agt. man] amnf mananā thoughtful, prudent — act. n. reflection, meditation; thought understanding. mananāt adv. after reflection; deliberately.
manayī [f. Manu] f. cf. manavī.
manavī [f. Manu] f. myth. n.p. of Ma navī/Manayī, wife of Manu.

mánas [abstr. man] n. thought, mind; faculty of attention; intellect, mental | instinct; advice, opinion; intention, taste, inclination | phil. the thinking and desiring subject | phil. [Vaisesika] the substance [dravya₁] of the mind; [Sāmkhya] the essence [tattva] of the mind, one of the constituents of the instrument in

terne [antahkaraṇa]; it is the decision-making organ; [Vedānta] its seat is the brahmarandhra, in the brain; cf. manomayakośa — m. myth. np. of Ma nas the personified mind, son of Māyā and Iśvara; he has two wives: Pravṛtti and Nivṛtti, personifying respectively the activity and inactivity of the intellect — amnf ifc. who has the mind to (iic. inf.) — v. [11] pr. (manasyati) pr. r. (manasyate) to have in mind, to consider; to reflect. manah kr direct one's thoughts upon, to think of (loc.); to have a taste for (g.). manīkr to take to heart. mano dā to fix the mind upon (loc.). mano dhā to think about, to meditate on (loc. dat. prati inf. mano vidhā to think about, to meditate on (loc. dat. prati inf. manah samādhā to pull oneself together. āsīt me manasi it came to me. manovākkāyakarmabhih in thoughts, words, and deeds. manyate aneneti manah phil. the mind is that by which one thinks. napuṃsakamiti jātvā tāṃ prati prahitaṃ manaḥ ramate tacca tatraiva hatāḥ pāṇininā vayam || |Dharmakīrti| Knowing that the mind |manaḥ| is neutral, I directed it towards her, but it fell in love with her; we are deceived by Pāṇini.
mánaskānta [kānta] amnf manaskāntā pleasing to the mind, agreeable.
mánaskāra [kāra] m. awareness (pain, pleasure) | sustained attention | devotion.
mánastāpa | tāpa | mr. anguish; remorse.
mánastāla | tāla | m. myth. np. of the lion Manastāla "Swift as the mind", mount |vāhana| of Durgā.
mánastusti [tusti] f. satisfaction of the mind; inner peace.
manasvat |vat| amnf manasvatī intelligent.

mánasvin [vin] amnf Manasvinī intelligent, wise | good-humored, joyful — m. myth. np. of Manasvī, one of the 8 dragon kings |nāgarāja| — f. Manasvinī myth. np. of Manasvinī "Serene", wife of Mṛkaṇḍu, mother of Mārkaṇḍeya.
mánasā₁ [i. Manas] adv. by the mind, in imagination; willingly, wholeheartedly; with the permission of g. . manasā kṛ to think, to meditate. manasā man to be inclined to.
manasāyajña [yajña] m. soc. internalized sacrifice.

manasā₂ [manasā₁] f. myth. np. of manasā "Born of the spirit", serpent goddess [nāgamātr], sister of the dragons | nāga | Ananta and Vāsuki; she protects from cobra bites [viṣāpahārī]; she is worshipped not. in Bengal and Orissa; she is the wife of Jaratkāru, and Astika is their son.
manasāpañcamī [pañcamī] f. soc. festival in honor of manasā, where cobras are honored; it is held on the 5th day of the dark fortnight of the month āṣāḍha; syn. nāgapañcamī.
manasāvijaya [vijaya] m. lit. np. from manasāvijaya "Victory of manasā", Bengali poem by Vipradāsa (1495); it describes the cruel way in which the snake goddess establishes her cult.
manasi [loc. Manas] adv. in mind | in the heart. manasi nidhā to picture. manasi kṛ to keep in mind.
manasikāra [kāra] m. act of taking to heart; determination.
manasigangākunda [gangākunda] n. geo. np. of the lake Manasigangākunda near Govardhana; after killing Vatsāsura, Kṛṣṇa came to purify himself there, having summoned the Ganges by thought.
manasija [ja] m. ["born in the heart"] love | myth. epith. of Kāma | myth. spiritual son of Brahmā; cf. sanakādi.
manaska | manaska | ifc. amnf manaska of (iic.) disposition of mind.
manā f. ved. devotion, attachment; zeal; ar deur, enthusiasm; envy.

manāk [manāac] adv. ["perceptibly"] a little; slightly, to a small extent | immediately | only. kālam manāk briefly. na manāk not at all. na manāgapi not in the least. dānam manāgapi a gift, however modest. manāg asmi na pātitaḥ I was not affected by it in the least.
manāpa [mana_āpa] amnf manāpā [“that reaches the heart” attractive, moving.
manīṣā [manasīṣā] f. reflection, consideration; intelligence, wisdom; conception, idea, thought. paro manīṣayā beyond all imagination.

manīṣāpañcaka [pañcaka] n. lit. np. du manīṣāpañcaka "5 reflections" of Sankara₁, inspired by his encounter with an outcast [cāṇḍāla] who reproached him for not putting his philosophy [advaita] into practice.
manīṣikā [manīṣāika] f. wisdom, intelligence. svamanīṣikayā according to one's own judgment.
manīṣin [manīṣāin] amnf manīṣiṇī thoughtful, wise, prudent | learned, erudite; syn. pandita. pravadanti manīsinah thus speak the wise.

mánu [manu] m. Man ["thinking creature"] | myth. np. of ManuSvāyaṃbhuva "the Primordial Man", the first Man of the era, born from the two halves Virāţ and Satarūpā of Brahmā; by Satarūpā he had as children Idā, Priyavrata and the 10 progenitors [prajāpati]; the Laws of Manu [mānavadharmaśāstra] are attributed to him; [SB.] he was saved from the flood by a jhasa fish which Manu made grow to a gigantic size, and which pulled his boat attached to its horn | phil. the Manu of a cosmological era [manvantara]; 14 of them are counted in a kalpa; tradition names them Svāyambhuva, Svārociṣa, Auttami, Tāmasa, Rai vata, Cākṣuṣa, Vaivasvata or Satyavrata (the Manu Yama of today, son of Vivasvān), Sāvarņa, Dakṣasāvarṇa, Brahmasāvarṇa, Dharmasāvarṇa, Rudrasāvarņa, Raucya and Bhautya | math. symb. the number 14 | var. manus id. | eng. man; all. Mann. manur bhava janayā daivyaṃ janam [RV.] Become a Man, so that you can generate the divine race.
manukula | kula | n. humanity. jayatu saṃskṛtaṃ jayatu manukulam The victory of Sanskrit is the victory of humanity.
manubṛhaspatisaṃvāda | bṛhaspatisaṃvāda | m. lit. |Mah.| dialogue between Manu and Brhaspati in the Mokşadharma.
Manusmṛti |smṛti| f. bed. n.p. from the Manusmṛti or Laws of Manu, text of traditional Laws, a dharmaśāstra, in stanzas |śloka|; it is later than Kauṭilya; syn. mānavadharmaśāstra.

manvantara [antara] n. myth. Manu period or cosmological era between two floods, comprising 12000 divine years, or 71 great eras [mahāyuga] (307 million years); the 7th of the current kalpa is in progress, there are 14 in a kalpa | lit. creation narrative of the human race and the first men, a pañcalakṣaṇa.
manvartha [artha] m. phil. interpretation of Manu.
manvarthamuktāvalī [muktāvalī] f. bed. n.p. from the manvarthamuktāvalī, commentary by Manu of Kullūka Bhaṭṭa, closely following Medhātithi.
Manvālaya [ālaya] n. geo. np. of Manvālaya, temple of Manu in the Himalayas, presumed place of landing of his ark after the flood; mod. Ma nali.
manuja [Manuja] m. Man, human — f. manujā var. manujī woman. manujīkr change into Man.
manujanātha [nātha] m. king, prince.
manujapati [pati] m. king, prince.
manujendra [indra] m. king.
manuṣa [manusa] m. Man — f. manuṣī woman | fr. gypsy.
manusya [manusya] amnf manusyā hu hand; relating to Man; masculine — m. Man (human) | all. Mensch; Manouche gypsy.
manusyatā [tā] f. humanity; human condition; the state of being a man. manusyatām i to become a man.
manusyatva [tva] n. humanity; human condition; the state of being a man. manusyatvam yā to become a man.
manusyayajña [yajña] m. soc. [SB.] ved. the sacrifice to men, or welcoming of guests, one of the five major rites [mahāyajña].
manus cf. manu.
mano iic. manas.
manogata | gata | amnf manogatā came to the mind; concealed in thought — n. idea; desire.
manogati [gati] f. desire — amnf that goes where it wants.
manoja [ja] m. ["from the spirit"] Love | epith. of Kāma.
manojava | java | amnf manojavā quick as thought — m. manojavá speed of thought — f. manojavā myth. n.p. from one of the 7 languages of Agni [saptajihva]. manojavam adv. at the speed of thought.

Manobhū [bhū₂] m. myth. np. of Manobhū, epithet of Kāma "born of thought". nāstyasādhyam nāma manobhuvah [K.] Truly, nothing is impossible for Love. śriyam diśatu vah śambhoh śyāmah kantho manob huvā | ankasthapārvatīdrstipāśair iva vivestitah || [KSS.] May Sambhu's black throat, caught in Love's snare in the form of Pārvatī's gaze nestled against him, bring you fortune.
manomathana [mathana] m. myth. np. of mano mathana, epith. of Kāma "that which overwhelms the mind".
manomaya [maya] amnf manomayī spiritual, mental, intellectual.
manomayakośa [kośa] m. phil. [Vedānta] the mental envelopment, forming with vijñānamayakośa the subtle or intellectual body [sūkṣmaśarīra].

manoratha [ratha] m. wish, desire ["that which transports the mind"] | illusion, imagination, dream | hist. np. from the philosopher bd. manoratha (4th century). manorathānāmagatirna vidyate nothing is inaccessible to desire. udyamena hi siddhayanti kāryāni na manorathaih It is by putting oneself to work that tasks are accomplished, and not by dreaming about them.

manorama [rama] amnf manoramā pleasant, charming, attractive; pretty — f. manoramā pretty woman | myth. [Mah.] np. of the beautiful nymph [apsaras] manoramā | lit. [K.] np. of manoramā₁, wife of Sukanāsa, mother of Vaiśampāyana₁ | lit. np. of works.
manorājya | rājya | n. realm of the imagination; land of dreams. manorājyāni kṛ to build castles in the air. manorājyavijrmbhanam kr id.
manovikāra [vikāra] m. change of mind.
manovega [vega] m. speed of thought. manovegena at the speed of thought.
manohara [hara] amnf manoharā ravishing, charming, pleasant, beautiful, captivating | "that which delights the mind".
manohan [manashan₁] v. [2] pr. (mano hanti) abs. (manohatya) to satisfy a desire ad li bitum. manohatya payah pibati he drinks from the bed to his heart's content.
mantavya [pfp. [3] man] amnf mantavyā what one must think about | what one must admit, believe or approve.

mántu [mantu] m. advisor; decision-maker; arbiter | council, deliberation | (result of a deliberation) motion, recommendation; intention, plan | offense; transgression — f. reflection; understanding; intellect — v. [11] pr. (mantūyati) to offend; to become angry.
mantr | agt. man | m. advisor; wise man.

√ mantr [vn. mantra] v. [10] pr. r. (mantráyate) pp. (mantrita) abs. (mantrayitvā) pf. (abhi, ā, ni) to take counsel (from (i.saha₂), concerning (dat.); to deliberate, to discuss — v. [10] pr. (man trayati) pf. (anu, sam) to speak. na tābhirmantrayetsudhīḥ The wise man should not take counsel from them.

mantra [instr. man] mn deliberation, opinion; resolution, counsel, plan; maxim | sacred hymn; mystical formula; magic incantation, phil. charm ["instrument of thought"] mantra or esoteric sacred formula; instrument of knowledge and power, its precise recitation is prescribed by the master [guru].

mantragupta [gupta] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of the young mantragupta, son of the minister Sumantra₁, one of the 10 heroes of the Daśakumāracarita; finding Rājavāhana, he told his story without using labials, having swollen lips after a night of love; he met a rākṣasa sorcerer ordering a servant to kidnap Princess Kanaka lekhā; he killed him, the princess fell in love with him; the king of Andhra who had defeated his father Kar dana fell in love with him; he disguised himself as a sorcerer to pretend to free the princess from a yakşa; he tricked the king of Andhra, made him drown, took his place, and freed Kardana qi who granted him the hand of Kana kalekhā.
mantratantra | Tantra | n. the formula and the treatise | mod. (pej.) esoteric gibberish, abracadabra.
mantradṛś [dṛś₂] amnf who sees (the meaning) of a mantra. mantradoșa | doșa₂ | m. soc. for want of a mantra.
mántrapāṭha |pāṭha| m. recitation of a sacred text.
mantrapuspa | puspa | n. soc. offering of flower while reciting a mantra.
mantramahodadhi [mahodadhi] m. bed. n.p. from Mahīdhara's mantramahodadhi (1588).

Mantramārga [mārga] m. phil. Tantric school of the Mantramārga "way of the formula"; its founder is Sadyojyoti; it developed in Kaśmīra in the 10th century according to two currents, the purely śaiva siddhānta, and the śākta movement dedicated to Bhairava and the Goddess.
mantramuktāvalī [muktāvalī] f. bed. [Tantra] n.p. from the mantramuktāvalī, ritual manual.
Mantrayāna [yāna] n. bd. np. of the Mantrayāna, tantric doctrine bd. of the way of the formula; cf. Va jrayāna.
mantrayoga [yoga] m. phil. [Tantra] incantatory magic.

mantrarahasyaprakāśikā [rahasyaprakāśikā] f. lit. collection of works by Nīlakantha₄ Ca turdhara, selecting Vedic verses to explain the gestures of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa: Mantrarāmāyaṇa, Mantrabhāgavata, Man tramahābhārata, Mantrakāśikhanda.
mantravīrya [vīrya] m. effectiveness of a mantra.
mantraśāstra [śāstra] n. phonematic science of formulas.
mantraśikhā [śikhā] f. soc. "flame" (power) of a mantra.
mántrasaṃskāra [saṃskāra] m. soc. rite of perfecting a mantra.
mantrasādhana [sādhana] n. soc. [Tantra] ritual procedure of initiation.
mántrasiddha [siddha₁] amnf mantrasiddhā accomplished by a charm [mantra] | expert in utterances.
mántrasiddhi [siddhi] f. magical power of a mantra.
mántrasiddhyupāya | upāya | m. soc. means to make a mantra effective.
mantrālaya [ālaya] mn mod. seat of government (not. of the Mahārāṣṭra).
mantroccāraṇa [uccāraṇa] n. recitation of a Man tra, form of worship [vandana].
mantropadeśa [upadeśa] m. soc. gift of a mantra by the dīkṣāguru during initiation.
mantrausadhivasa [osadhivasa] amnf mantrauṣadhivaśā which is resolved by formulas and herbs.
mantrayitvā [abs. mantr] ind. having taken counsel — m. mantrya ifc. having taken counsel from (iic.).
mantri iic. mantrin. mantriparișad | parișad₂ | f. council of ministers.
mantrita [pp. mantra] amnf mantritā deliberate; advised — n. deliberation.
mantrin [agt. mantra] amnf mantrinī advisor to the king, minister; title Mantrī of first
minister | magician | (chess [caturangā]) queen | | fr. mandarin. pradhānamantrī prime minister.
mantrya cf. mantrayitvā.

√ manth var. math v. [1] pr. (manthati) v. [1] pr. (mathati) pp. (mathita) pf. (pra) to shake vigorously; to rub wood (to make a fire); to churn | to upset, damage, destroy | gr. oo ; all. Mangel. sa jāyase mathyamānah saho mahat | tvām āhuh sahasas putram angirah | | ved. You are born by rubbing the fire stick very hard; that is why you are called son of strength, O Angirā.
mantha [act. manth] m. agitation, churning barley porridge mixed with milk | spoon or stick for stirring, churn stick — f. manthā id.
manthan cf. mathin.

manthana [agt. manth] amnf manthanī that stirs, that churns | that kindles fire by friction — m. manthana churn stick; fire stick — act. n. churning | myth. churning of the primordial ocean | production of fire by friction — f. Man thanī churn.

manthara [related to manda] amnf mantharā slow, stupid; cumbersome; cumbersome — f. mantharā myth. [Rām.] np. of the hunchbacked servant mantharā, incarnation of the gandharvī Dundubhī; when King Dasaratha was about to enthrone his elder Rāma as his successor, she aroused the jealousy of Kaikeyī, who reminded the king of his promise to grant him a vow, to demand the exile of Rāma and the coronation of his own son Bharata₁.
Manthāna [mathana] m. fire stick | myth. np. of Manthāna, epith. of Šiva "who churns the Uni vers".
manthānabhairava | bhairava | m. lit. np. of the manthānabhairava tantra, esoteric work of the paścimāmnāya tradition of the cult of Kubjikā.
√ mand₁ | reli 'ea ; mad₁ | v. ; | 1 | ; pr. ; r. ; (mandate) ; to rejoice, to be cheerful; to be drunk or intoxicated | to be splendid — ca. (mandayati) to intoxicate; to rejoice.
√ mand₂ v. to stay, to remain, to pause.

Manda [agt. mand₂] amnf mandā slow, late; opp. śīghra | weak, sluggish; sleepy, lazy, indolent; inactive; apathetic, indifferent to (dat.) | gentle; clumsy; foolish, stupid | astr. np. of Manda, epith. of Sani "slow" — v. [11] pr. (mandāyati) v. [11] pr. r. (mandāyate) to become lethargic, to slow down; to weaken; to drag. mandam adv. slowly, weakly; modestly. mandīkṛ to slow down. mandāyante na khalu suhrdām abhyu petārthakṛtyāḥ Those do not drag their feet, who undertake a task promised to friends.

mandaka |ka| amnf mandakā stupid; simple-minded. śrotriyasyeva te rājan | mandakasyāvipaścitah | anuvākahatā buddhir dharmam evaikam īkṣate || [Mah.] Your Majesty, your mind, like that of a stupid reciter of the Veda, dulled by recitation, is obsessed with morality.
mandakarṇa [karṇa] amnf mandakarṇī hard of hearing. badhirān mandakarṇaḥ śreyān Better to be hard of hearing than deaf.
mandaga [ga₁] amnf mandagā that moves slowly — m. astr. epith. of the planet Saturn [Sani].
mandadhī | dhī₂ | amnf who is slow-witted; unintelligent.

mandapāla | pāla | m. myth. | Mah. | np. of the ṛṣi Man dapāla; after a life of hard penances he died without sons, and for this reason was not admitted to Heaven; he incarnated as a bee-eater [śārṅgaka] to mate with Jaritā and obtain four sons [śārṅgakās]; then he abandoned her immediately for La pitā.
mandabuddhi [buddhi] amnf who is slow-witted. adhyayanāt parājayate mandabuddhiḥ (The student) with a slow mind grows weary of study.
mandabhāgya | bhāgya₁ | amnf mandabhāgyā ["who has little luck"] unfortunate, unlucky — n. misfortune.
mandamati | mati | amnf to the slow mind.
mandavisarpin [visarpin] afmn Mandavisarpiṇī which creeps slowly, which insinuates itself — f. Mandavisarpiṇī lit. |Pañcatantra| n.p. of Mandavisarpinī, royal bedbug.
mandākrānta [ākrānta] amnf mandākrāntā which progresses slowly — f. mandākrāntā phon. name of a homosyllabic meter [samavṛtta] of 17 syllables with 2 caesuras at syllables 4 and 6; cf. Me ghadūta.
mandādara |ādara| amnf mandādarā in different (to (loc.)).
mandānila | anila | m. pleasant breeze.

mandodarī [udara] f. myth. [Rām.] np. of Mando darī "with a painful belly"; in a first life she was Madhurā₁ transformed into a frog by the spell of Pārvatī; she lived for twelve years in the well near which the asura Maya and the apsaras Hemā did penances to obtain a daughter; she was taken in by them when her spell ended; of great beauty, she was noticed by Rāvaṇa who made her his chief queen; she is the mother of Indrajit; she is a perfect wife [pativratā].
mandautsukya [autsukya] amnf mandaut sukyā not inclined to (acc.prati). mandautsukyah asmi nagaragamanam prati I don't want to go to the city.
mandána [agt. mand₁] amnf mandanā gai, joyeux — n. éloge — m. amant.

mandara [Mandara] amnf mandarā large, massive; slow, lazy — m. myth. np. of Mount Mandara "the Enormous", which served to churn the primordial sea of milk [kṣīrodamathana]; cf. Kūrma, Vāsuki | lit. [KSS.] np. of the sage vidyādhara Man dara.
Mandaradeva [deva] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara king Mandaradeva, who reigned over the North face of Kailāsa; he was defeated by Na ravāhanadatta.

mandākinī [Mandaac] f. astr. np. of the mandākinī or Celestial Ganges (Milky Way); myth. it springs from the toe of Vishnu, and flows in the hair of Shiva; syn. chāyāpatha, rasā | geo. np. of the mandākinī₁ river which rises at Kedāranātha; it is one of the tributaries of the Ganges, and it joins the Alakanandā at Rudraprayāga | myth. [BhP.] name of a garden of Kubera in the Himalayas; his sons Nalakūvara and Manigrīva became intoxicated there.

mandāra m. bio. bot. Erythrina indica, coral tree; it loses its leaves in June and is covered with large flowers with long pistils; its leaves are used to make shampoo; 3 varieties are distinguished according to the color of the flowers: yellow, used for tantric puja, black, for the puja to Sani, and coral red ("the color of Kālī's blood") for the puja to Durgā; cf. pāribhadra, bahupuṣpa | myth. one of the 5 trees of Indra's paradise Svarga; cf. pañcavṛkṣa.

mandāravat [vat] amnf Mandāravatī coral green neck — f. Mandāravatī lit. [KSS.] np. of the princess Mandāravatī, daughter of King Mandāradeva of Hamsadvīpa and Kandarpasenā, of unparalleled beauty; she marries Sundarasena after many adventures.
mandira [mand₂ira] n. dwelling, abode, house; palace | [devamandira] temple.
mandirābhyantara | abhyantara | n. interior of the temple, of the palace.
mandurā [mand₂] f. stable | straw mattress.
mandra [mandra] amnf mandrā pleasant, agreeable, charming | low, muffled, grave (said of the voice, the noise of chariots, of the storm).
mandhātṛ [contr. manodhātṛ] m. wise or pious man.
Manmatha [intens. manth] m. carnal love,
passion ["that which overwhelms"] |myth. np. of Manmatha "passion", a name of the god Kāma; he personifies the 29th year of a life cycle [samvatsara].

manya [manya] ifc. amnf manyā who thinks he is; who pretends to be; who resembles (⟨iic.⟩ acc.). panditammanyah who thinks he is an eminent person. paṇḍitammanyā'sau he prides himself on studying. śūrammanyah who thinks he is a hero. darśanīyammanyah who thinks he is handsome; vain. narammanyah who thinks he is a man. rājaṃmanyaḥ who thinks he is the king. śriyammanyah who thinks he is Sri. gāmmanyah who thinks he is a cow. divāmanyah who is considered to be diurnal. doṣāmanyam ahaḥ a day like the night.
mányā f. du. pl. neck muscles.

manyú [manyu] m. mood, temperament; ardor, zeal, passion, virility; courage; syn. ojas indignation; vehemence; anger, fury, rage; cha grin, pain | soc. not. legitimate indignation of a warrior | kṣatriya | | phil. impulse of a being to accomplish its designs; tension of desires; incitement to act; creative impulse | ved. np. of Manyu, the Will personified; it is said to be uncreated [svayaṃbhū]. manyutas adv. with rage, with anger. manyum kṛ vent one's anger on (loc. acc.prati). kasmān manyur na vardhate |Draupadī| Why are you not furious?.
mama var. me [g. aham] ind. to me, of me; mine, mine, mine.
mamaka |ka| amnf mamakā véd. mine.

mamatā [tā] f. interest (en (loc.)); feeling of possession; selfishness; pride, arrogance | myth. np. of mamatā "the Proud One", wife of Utathya; pregnant by her husband, she was raped by her brother-in-law Brhaspati; the embryo protested, and repelled his sperm which fell to the ground; Brhaspati mau said the child, who was born blind, hence his name Dīrghatamā.
mamatva [tva] n. interest, attachment; feeling of possession, act of hoarding. mamatvam kr to be attached to (loc.).

mammața m. hist. np. of mammața Bhațța or mammaţācarya, author of the Kaśmīra of the end of the 11th century; he is credited with the essential part of the Kāvyaprakāśa; and the Sabdavyāpāravicāra; he established the doctrine of the school of evocative poetry [dhvani], following Anandavardhana.

Maya [agt. mā₁] m. myth. np. of the asura Maya "Architect", first among the undines [dānava]; Architect of the devās and daityās, he built sit the triple fortress Tripura; his wife is the nymph [apsaras] Hemā; their sons are Māyāvī and Dundubhi; they adopted Mandodarī as their daughter; [Mah.] during the fire of the Khāṇḍava forest, Maya was hidden there, disguised as Takṣaka; he escaped from it, and by his prayer to Arjuna was saved from the flames of Agni and the cakra of Kṛṣṇa; As a sign of gratitude, he built the city of Khāṇḍavaprastha for the Pāṇḍavās; [KSS.] Sunītha₁ and Sumundīka are said to be his sons by Līlāvatī₂.
Mayamata [mata] n. lit. np. of the Mayamata, treatise on architecture | vāstuśāstra | and urban planning of the 11th century, attributed to Maya Muni.
Maya gram. (form of the secondary a., with f. in mayī) made of, formed from (iic.) | concerning, relating to (iic.).
mayā [i. aham] ind. by me.
mayi [loc. aham] ind. in me.
mayú |mā₁u| m. myth. chimera, celestial being half-man half-beast; cf. kinnara, gandharva.
mayurāja [rāja] m. myth. np. of mayurāja, epith. of Kubera "King of chimeras".
mayūkha m. peg; patère; stake | soc. ved. stake for attaching the sacrificial animal | axis of a sundial; syn. kīla.

mayūra mf mayūrī bio. zoo. peacock | hist. np. of mayūra, mannered poet of the court of King Harṣa, rival of Bāṇa₂ whose sister he had married; he is credited with the Sūryaśataka, praises to the sun for having cured him of leprosy.
mayūrapattra [pattra] n. peacock feather, iconographic symbol of immortality.
Mayūrapoṣaka [poṣaka] m. peacock breeder | hist. n.p. of Mayūrapoṣaka, father of Candragupta Mau rya.
mayuravarman | varman | mr. hist. n.p. of King Mayūravarmā; cf. Mayūraśarmā.
mayūravyaṃsaká [vyaṃsaka] m. peacock thief; syn. dhūrtamayūra | thief like a peacock gram. paradigmatic example of an irregular determinative compound, with inverse dependence.

mayūraśarman [śarman] m. hist. n.p. of King Mayūraśarmā who founded the Kadamba dynasty in Karņāta in 345; its capital was Vanavāsī; he took the name Mayūravarmā to indicate his passage from the brāhmaṇa class to the kṣatriya class.

mayūrāsana [āsana] n. phil. [yoga] peacock pose: lying flat on your stomach, elbows on either side of your navel, supporting yourself with both hands turned backwards, you lift your body while keeping it straight |dandavat|.
mara [act. mr] m. death | the earth ["world of mortals"] | pl. the inhabitants of hell.
