maravijaya [vijaya] m. bd. ["victory over death"] episode of Buddha's Awakening in Gaya, where he overcame demonic temptations and "took the earth to witness" his merits.
maravijayamudrā [mudrā] f. bd. gesture of the "touch dear of the earth" in representations of the Bud dha not. in Thailand; syn. bhūmisparśamudrā.
mara form of a. meaning "that which makes".
marakata n. emerald || lat. smaragdus.
marana |act. mr | n. extinction, agony, death.
maranatva |tva| n. state of death.
maraṇasamaya [samaya] m. moment of death. maranasamaye adv. at the hour of death.
maraṇānta | anta | amnf maraṇāntā ending in death.
maraṇāntika | antika | amnf maraṇāntikā id.
maraṇābhimukha [abhimukha] amnf maraṇābhimukhī on the point of dying, mori bond.
maraṇīya [maraṇaīya] amnf maraṇīyā susceptible to dying; condemned to die.
maranda m. pl. pollen or nectar of flowers.
marāṭha cf. mahārāṣṭra.
marica var. marīca m. organic. bot. Piper nigrum, pepper plant — n. black pepper || hi. mirc.

Marici f. Vedic ray of light (solar or lunar) — m. myth. np. of Marici₁, first progenitor [prajāpati], sprung from the mind of Brahmā [vaidhātra]; Kaśyapa is [Mah.] his son or [Rām.] his younger brother; he is a paragon of virtue, and the Daśakumāracarita recounts his seduction by the court herbalist Kāmamañjarī in order to win a wager — f. burst of light, ray of sunlight; dawn | mirage lit. section of an anthology of myth. poetry np. of Marici₁ "Burst of Light", a name of Uṣā, the Dawn; creation was born from her incestuous, murderous love with her father Brahmāprajāpati; She is sometimes represented as a sow with 7 piglets representing the 7 days of the week | bd. deity of the Lamaist pantheon.
marīcikā [ka] f. mirage.

Marīcikuṇḍa | kuṇḍa | n. geo. np. of the Marīcikuṇḍa, sacred water well of the Muktesvara temple in Bhu baneśvar; its water, which grants fertility, is drawn once a year and auctioned for the Lingarāja chariot festival; cf. Aśokāṣṭamī.

marú | mṛu | m. desert, desert space; ro cher soc. abstinence from drink (form of penance) | pl. maravas geo. ["desert people"] name of the Mārvār people and their country; mod. Rājasthāna | myth. [BhP.] np. of the Maru King Janaka "the Hostile", son of Haryaśva₁, father of Pratīpaka; or [Rām.] father of Pratīndhaka | myth. [Rām.] np. of the Maru King₁ of Ayodhyā, son of Sīghraga, father of Praśuśruka. marū bhū to become desertified. marum sādh to abstain from drink.
marukānta [kānta] m. geo. np. of the "splendid Desert" marukānta, dried from the ocean by Rāma armed with the Brahmadanda (mod. desert of Bikaner and Mārvār).

marudesa [desa] m. geo. desert west of the Aravalli Mountains in Rajasthan. marubhuti var. marubhutika [bhuti] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the Brahmin Marubhuti, son of Yaugand Harayana; he became a minister of Naravahanadatta; he is quarrelsome, a lover of women and drink; after a fight with Manasavega, he was rescued by an ascetic who made him steal the clothes of a nymph at her bath; the nymph united with the ascetic, and at the birth of their child, her curse having come to an end, she went to Heaven; the ascetic cooked the child and ate it to follow her; Ma rubhūti ate two grains of rice from the stew, and his spit turned into gold; he frequented the Sane courtiers; a matchmaker made him spit out the two grains of rice that had become rubies and he lost his power; by praying to Durgā he found his companions again.

marút |mr| m. Wind | phil. divine breath, principle of immortality | pl. marutas myth. ved. np. of the maruta breaths, genies of the winds and storms, forming the troop of young warriors ta pageurs of Indra; they are said to be voracious | praghāsya|; the Mahābhārata lists 11 of them: Mṛgavyādha "Chaser", Sarpa "Serpent", Nirrti₁ "Misfortune", Ajai kapād "Eternal One-Legged", Ahirbudhnya "Sea Serpent", Pinākin "Archer", Dahana "Burning", Iśvara "Lord", Kapālī "Skull Bearer", Sthānu "Pillar", and Bhaga₁ "Lucky"; These are the 11 aspects of Rudra [ekādaśarudrās]; sometimes 48 are listed; their leader is Mātariśvā; they drive chariots drawn by antelopes [śarvarās]; they are symbolized by 11 sacrificial poles, with the main pole IsvaraSiva in the center, and 5 poles of decreasing sizes on each side; they are also represented as 11-headed Shiva; cf. Rudra, prāṇa, vāha, gomātr.

Marutta [datta] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Marutta, son of Avikșit; very pious, he celebrated his countless crucifixions with all the kings; near Mount Meru, armies of goldsmiths made him utensils in gold; he asked Brhaspati to be his chaplain, but Indra opposed it; Narada suggested that he take as chaplain the penitent [tapasvin] Samvarta, who, tired of being thwarted by his brother Brhaspati, wandered naked in the forest; the latter accepted, which displeased Brhaspati who incited Indra to prevent his sacrifice; Agni was dispatched to frighten him, but Samvarta threatened Agni with his powers of asceticism [tapas]; Marutta went to Mount Muñjavān, and Samvarta celebrated a great soma sacrifice there which Indra and all the gods attended; [Rām.] Rāvaņa profaned his sacrifice.
marútputra [putra] m. myth. np. of Marutputra or Marutiputra or Māruti, patr. of Hanumān or Bhīma "son of the Wind".
marútvat |vat| amnf marutvatī myth. in the presence of the marutas — m. myth. np. of Marutvat, epith. of Indra — f. marutvatī myth. np. of Marut vatī, daughter of Dakṣa, wife of Dharma.
marutvatīya [īya] amnf marutvatīyā soc. relating to MarutvatIndra; said especially of the midday rite.
marútsakhi |sakhi| amnf myth. friend of my routes.
Marudvṛddhā [vṛddhā] f. geo. np. of the Marudvṛddhā river, a river in the Himalayas descending from the Amaranātha massif to flow into the Chenāb near Kishtvār; mod. Maru Wardwan.
marudha m. bio. bot. Terminalia arjuna, arjun tree, large combertaceae, with oval leaves arranged in a straight line; it is used in medicine; syn. arjuna.

marudhajalapati [jalapati] m. myth. np. of Ma rudhajalapati or Marudhacalapati, "Master of the water of the marudha", epith. of MuruganSkanda who is said to have caused a spring to gush forth at the foot of an ar jun tree to answer the prayers of a thirsty siddha₁.
markaṭa var. marka m. organic. zoo. monkey.

markatakiśora [kiśorá] m. little monkey [markaṭakiśoranyāya] phil. Northern bhakti doctrine, where the believer seeks help from God as the little monkey clings to its mother's belly; opp. mārjārakiśora .
márta [mṛta] m. mortal; man.
martavya [pfp. [3] mṛ] amnf martavyā mortal; who must die — n. (impers.) one must die. martavya sati death being inevitable. martavya krtaniścayah resolved to die.
mártya [martaya] amnf martyā ["who must die" mortal; human — m. (a) mortal, man — n. the mortal body — f. martyā death.
mártyatā [tā] f. mortality; human condition.
mártyatva [tva] n. mortality; human condition. martyatvam āgataḥ var. martyatām prāptaḥ in his condition of mortality.
mard [ca. mṛd₁] v. [10] pr. (mardayati) to press, crush; to destroy, to kill.
marda [agt. mṛd₁] amnf mardā ifc. that which rubs; that which grinds, that which destroys — act. n. friction, shock; destruction.
mardaka [agt. mṛd₁] ifc. amnf mardikā that crushes, that grinds (iic.); that causes suffering (iic.).
mardana [agt. mṛd₁] amnf mardanī that rubs; that grinds, that destroys — act. n. friction, massage | destruction, ruin.
mardala [mṛd₁ala] m. kind of drum; syn. mrdanga.
mardin [agt. mṛd₁] amnf mardinī that crushes, that grinds; destroyer, annihilator.

Marpa m. hist. np. of the Tibetan mystic bd. Marpa Lotsava (1012–1097), student of Nāropa, great accomplished [mahāsiddha]; he translated the tantric doctrines into Tibetan, and founded the Kagyūpa lineage; Milarepa was his student.
marma iic. marman.
marmaga [ga₁] amnf marmagā ["that goes to the heart"] extremely painful or poignant.
marmajña |jña| amnf marmajñā who knows the sensitive points; expert — ifc. expert in, exceptionally gifted in (iic.).
marmajñāna [jñāna] n. knowledge of a secret.
marmasthala [sthala] n. vital point, vulnerable place.
marmasthāna [sthāna] n. vital point, vulnerable spot.

márman [mṛman] n. vulnerable point (of the body), weak point; joint, vital organ; painful point, raw flesh | secret, mystery, hidden meaning. marmacchit var. marmabhit cutting raw. marmāṇi kṛntat cutting the flesh.
marmara [onomatopoeia] amnf marmarā that makes a rustling noise; that murmurs || fr. murmure.
márya [mṛ] m. mortal; lad; young man, young warrior; courtier | pl. (voc.) people.
maryaká [ka] m. little Man | ved. said of a bull in the middle of cows.
maryā f. limit; border.
maryāda [da] m. ["that marks the border"] ar bitre — f. cf. maryādā.

maryādā [f. maryāda] f. border, limit; purpose; moral limits, customary rules; legal framework; good conduct | agreement, contract. grhyatām pāninā pānirmaryādā badhyatām tvayā [Rām.] hand clasped in the hand, the contract is concluded by you.
maryādāpuruṣa [puruṣa] m. myth. epith. of Rāma "Man of proper conduct".
marśana [act. mṛś] n. touching (of a woman) | examination, inquiry | advice; deliberation; explanation.
marṣ [ca. mṛṣ] v. [10] pr. (marṣayati) pfp. (marṣaṇīya) to bear; forgive. na marş molester.
marṣa [act. mṛṣ] m. patience; endurance.
marṣaṇa [agt. mṛṣ] amnf marṣaṇā who forgives, indulgent — act. n. patience, endurance; indulgence.
marṣaṇīya [pfp. [2] mṛṣ] amnf marṣaṇīyā which deserves indulgence; which must be forgiven.
marșin [agt. mṛṣ] amnf marṣiṇī patient, indulgent.

mála mn dirt, filth; stain, defilement, impurity; poison | med. bodily excretion: phlegm, bile, mucus, sweat, hair, nails, etc. | phil. |śaiva| primordial substance of sin; three are distinguished [trimala]. malam ajñānam icchanti saṃsārānkurakāraṇam phil. [Mālinīvijaya] The fundamental impurity is ignorance; it is the cause of the germ of the flux of becomings.
máladhārin [dhārin] m. soc. ["covered in filth"] renouncing Jain.
málaprstha | prstha | n. outer page of a book (unwritten, because soiled).

Malaprabhā [prabhā₁] f. geo. np. of the Malaprabhā River in Karṇāṭaka, which descends from the Sahyādri Mountains, flows near Vātāpi₁ (mod. Badāmi) and Aryapura (mod. Aihole), and flows into the Kṛṣṇā₁ at Kudālasamgama.
málamallaka [mallaka] m. piece of cloth covering the private parts; syn. kaupīna. aham anayā malamallakaśeṣaḥ [DKC.] She left me with nothing but a rag as underwear.
malamāsa [māsa] m. astr. intercalary lunar month, added periodically so that the lunar cycle catches up with the solar cycle; it is impure, and no religious ceremony should be performed in it.
malaya m. geo. np. of the malaya, region of the Malabar chain, in the Western Ghats, south of Kaveri (mod. Kerala); it is renowned for its sandalwood | pl. its inhabitants.
malayaja [ja] amnf malayajā which grows in Malabar — m. organic. bot. Sirium myrtifolium, sandalwood tree | candana |.
malayadeśa [deśa] m. geo. the Malaya country (mod. Kerala).
Malayavat |vat| amnf Malayavatī born in Malaya, inhabitant of Malaya — f. Malayavatī lit. [Nāgānanda] np. of Malayavatī, wife of Jīmūtavāhana.

malina [mala] amnf malinā dirty, soiled, tarnished; impure | grey — v. [11] pr. (malinayati) to soil, to wither, to defile. malinīkṛ to soil. malinībhū to soil oneself. śisya upadeśam malinayati the student discredits the teaching.
maliṣṭha [super. malina] amnf maliṣṭhā very dirty; excessively impure — f. malisthā menstruating woman.
malīmasa [mala] amnf malīmasā dirty, soiled, impure | dirty grey in color.
malīyas [compar. mala] amnf malīyasī very dirty, infected | very impure; very bad.

Malla₁ m. wrestler; athlete, man of great physical strength | soc. ksatriya outcaste | hist. np. of the Malla₁ dynasty of Nepal (1483–1768) [mallāsura] myth. np. of the demon [asura] Malla₁ "wrestler" | pl. mallās geo. Malla₁ country and people; their capital was Kuśinagara.
mallavādin [vādin] m. hist. np. du phi losphe jaina Mallavādī; he is credited with the treatise Dvādaśāranayacakra, or Nayacakra.
mallaka m. container; packaging.
mallāra m. mus. mode [rāga] intended for the rainy season; cf. amrtavarsin.
malli m. possession, belonging | jn. np. from jina malli; cf. Mallinātha — f. mallī bio. bot. Jas minum sambac, white jasmine, with a sweet fragrance.

Mallinātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of Mallinātha "Master who possesses knowledge", 19th mythical tīrthankara; his body is blue and gold, his symbol is a water jug | hist. np. of Mallinātha₁, Jain scholar of the 14th or 15th century; he notably wrote commentaries on various poems
epics [mahākāvya]; cf. Sañjīvanī, Ghaṇṭāpatha, Sarvankaṣā, Sarvapathīnā.
malliṣeṇa |senā| mr. hist. n.p. of the philosopher jn. mallisena (18th century), author of the Syādvādamañjarī.
mallika m. organic. zoo. kind of goose — f. mal likā organic. bot. Jasminum sambac, white jasmine, with a sweet scent; syn. mallī.

mallikārjuna [arjuna] m. geo. np. of Mallikārjuna, one of the 12 radiant signs of Shiva [jyotirlinga], established at the temple of Śrīśaila; he is worshipped with jasmine; he is a vertex of the trilinga triangle; cf. Bhramarāmbikā.
maśa m. buzzing | mosquito; fly ron.
maśaka |ka| m. mosquito; in general, an insect that stings or bites.
mași mf mașī black smoke mixed with oil, used in cosmetics and as ink for marking writing on palm leaves.
masijala [jala| n. ink.
masibhāvuka [bhāvuka] amnf masibhāvukā which becomes black like ink.
masura m. organic. bot. lens esculenta, lens — f. masurā prostitute, courtesan.
masūra [related to masura] m. organic. bot. lens es culenta, lens — f. masūrā prostitute, courtesan — f. masūrī smallpox.
masūraka [ka] m. id. — f. masūrikā med. (eruption of) smallpox.
masṛṇa amnf masṛṇā finely ground; tender, soft; sweet; smooth; syn. snigdha.
masṛṇatva [tva] n. tenderness, gentleness.
maskara m. bamboo; bamboo cane.
maskarin [in] m. soc. ["who carries a bamboo cane" | mendicant ascetic.
masta n. head, skull.
mastaka [mastaka] mn head, skull; temple summit, upper part, peak. mastakam prep. cl. above (iic.).
mastakaśūla |śūla| n. headache, headache.
mastakāñjali [añjali] m. posture of devotion, hands joined in front of the chest, head bowed.
mastakābhiṣeka [abhiṣeka] m. jn. pilgrimage festival [mela] of Śravanabelagolā (Karnāṭaka), where offerings are poured onto the head of a giant statue of Bāhubalī; cf. Gommața.
mastiṣka [related to mastaka] mn brain medicine affecting the brain.
mástu m. sour cream.
mástulunga | lunga | m. brain.

√ mah v. [1] pr. (mahati) ppr. (mahat) pft. (māmahe) ppr. (mahat) pp. (mahita) abs. (ma hitvā) to rejoice; to exalt, to excite; to increase, to magnify; to honor, to celebrate — pr. r. (mahate) ved. to rejoice — ca. (maháyati) to make grow, to amplify | to rejoice; to exalt; to honor — ca. r. (mahayate) ved. id. || gr. ; lat. magnus; ang. much; fr. to magnify, magnanimous.

maha iic. mahat. maharşi | rṣi | m. myth. great sage; cf. saptarşi | mod. np. of the maharși Maheśa Yogī, title of the spiritual master Maheśa Prasāda Varma (1917– 2008); after studying physics, he became a disciple of the śamkarācārya Brahmānanda Sarasvatī₂ in Badarīnātha; he created the international Transcendental Meditation movement in 1955.

mahát [mahat] amnf Mahatī [en comp. mahā] great (in space, in time, in quantity); high, vast, eminent, important | rich in (i.) — n. important thing; sacred knowledge — m. [mahātattva] phil. [Sāṃkhya] the essence [tattva] of the intellect [buddhi], or power of discrimination; it is the first stage of the evolution of nature |prakṛti|, where the distinction of quality [guṇa] appears | eminent person, great man | soc. superior of a temple or monastery — f. ma hatī myth. np. of Mahatī, lute |vīṇā| of Nārada. mahāntam kālam for a long time.
maháttā [tā] f. grandeur; importance; power.
maháttva |tva| n. id.
mahadvarsah | varsa | mr. heavy rain.
mahannadī | nadī | f. great river.
mahattama [super. mahat] amnf ma hattamā the greatest, the most important.
mahattara |compar. mahat| amnf ma hattarā greater, more important.
mahanīya [pfp. [2] maha] amnf ma hanīya worthy of being honored; glorious, illustrious.
mahanīyakīrti | kīrti | amnf to illustrious glory.
mahanīyamūrti |mūrti| amnf with a splendid appearance.
mahanta | related to mahat | m. soc. superior of a monastery.
mahallaka m. soc. eunuch of the royal harem — f. Mahallikā lit. [KSS.] np. of Mahallikā, daughter of the asura king Prahlāda, who gave her as a wife to Sūryaprabha.
máhas |abstr. mah| n. power, glory, greatness — ind. mahar [maharloka] myth. cf. vyāhṛti. mahobhis adv. powerfully, with greatness.

maharloka | loka | m. myth. np. of mahar or Ma harloka the "Sky of glory", 4th celestial world [loka], above the pole star; Bhrgu remains there, with the sages [ṛṣi] who survive the dissolution of the worlds.
mahā iic. mahat.
mahākarman [karman] n. great work — m. one who accomplishes great works; epith. of Shiva.
Mahākarmavibhanga [karmavibhanga] m. bd. np. of the Mahākarmavibhanga "great classification of acts", treatise on morality bd.; it is represented in stone at Borobudur.

mahākalpa [kalpa] m. phil. great cycle of time of the existence of Brahmā, for 100 brahmic years, i.e. 311000 billion years; it ends with a great extinction |mahāpralaya|; then ViṣṇuNārāyaṇa sleeps on the dragon Vestige, [Seṣa], symbolizing the residue of the Universe burned by cosmic fire, until the next cycle of birth of Brahmā.
Mahākavi | kavi | m. lit. title Mahākavi of "great poet".
Mahākaśyapa [kaśyapa] m. bd. np. of Mahākaśyapa, great disciple of Buddha; after his parinirvāṇa, he became the leader of the community; pāli Mahakassapa.

Mahākāla |kāla₁| m. phil. eternity | myth. np. of Mahākāla "great destroyer" (or "Eternity"), epith. of Shiva in his terrible form of Bhairava; he is represented as black and frightening, accompanied by a black dog; he is notably worshipped as the jyotirlinga Mahākāleśvara at Ujjayinī (in a temple destroyed by Altamish of Selhi in 1235 and restored in the 19th century) and also at the Kālabhairava temple north of the city.
Mahākālabhairavāṣṭaka [Bhairavaaṣṭaka] n. bed. n.p. from the Mahākālabhairavāstaka stotra.

Mahākāleśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of Mahākāleśvara, one of the 12 radiant signs of Shiva [jyotirlinga]; it is said to be the navel |nābhi| at the center of the World; it was established by Vedapriya and his sons to protect themselves from the demon Dūṣaṇa₁; established in the largest temple of Ujjayinī, it is constantly anointed with milk, and is decorated variously according to the festivals; the surrounding country [kṣetra] contains 84 lingasashrines, described in the Skandapurāna.

mahākāvya [kāvya] n. lit. ["great poem"] court epic-lyric poem; it consists of chapters [sarga] bringing together verses of various meters organized into subjects; each verse is an independent poem; the theme is an episode taken from an epic narrative; cf. pañcamahākāvya, brhattrayī.

mahākūṭeśvara [kūṭaīśvara] m. geo. np. of the sanctuary of Mahākūteśvara, built on an arid plateau 10 km west of mod. Aihole, by King Cālukya Rāṇāraṅga in 525; it is the presumed site where the demons Vātāpi and Ilvala are said to have held sway.
mahākriyā [kriyā] f. phil. [kriyāyoga] main action/posture; there are 18 of them.
mahākṣatrapa [kṣatrapa] m. hist. [Saka] Indobacterian royal title; cf. Rudradāmā.
Mahākṣapaṇaka [kṣapaṇaka] m. hist. np. of Mahākṣapaṇaka, scholar from Kaśmīra (10th century?); he is the author of the dictionary of homonyms Anekārthadhvanimañjarī.
mahācīna |cīna| m. geo. Greater China | pl. the Chinese.
mahājada [jada] amnf mahājadā complete idiot, imbecile.
Mahājana [jana] m. populace; crowd | eminent man, great man | soc. ruling society

community [agrahāra] | myth. [VP.] The twelve Eminent Ones are Brahmā, Nārada, Siva, Kumāra, Ka pila, Manu, Prahlāda, Janaka, Bhīṣma, Bali, Suka, and Yama, all pure devotees of Nārāyana | soc. ban quier, usurer | myth. np. of Mahājana "great man", son of Kubera, personifying Avarice; he refused his dakṣiṇā to Kṛṣṇa disguised as a Brahmin by feigning death, and even at the foot of the pyre refused to pay it | pl. soc. Mahājanāḥ are merchants or bankers. mahājane adv. before a crowd; in public.

mahājanapada [janapada] m. bd. one of the 16 great ancient kingdoms of India: Kāśi, Kosala, Anga, Magadha, Vrji, Malla, Cedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Pañcāla, Matsya₂, Sūrasena, Aśmaka, Avanti, Gandhāra and Kamboja.
mahātattva | tattva | n. cf. mahat.
mahātapas [tapas] amnf who practices severe penances — m. great ascetic; qualifies not. Vișnu and Siva.
mahātapaḥsaptamī | saptamī | f. soc. 7th day of a fortnight (pakṣa), devoted to fasting.
Mahātala [tala] n. myth. n.p. of the world [loka] Mahātala, sixth underground hell.
mahātīrtha |tīrtha| n. soc. major place of pilgrimage.
mahātejas [tejas] amnf very glorious; who has a Great spiritual strength.

mahātman |ātman| amnf mahātmanī ma gnanime, noble, wise | eminent; distinguished; powerful — m. phil. the supreme Spirit; being having attained divine realization | mod. np. of Mahātmā "Great Soul", epith. of Gandhi.

mahātmya [ya] amnf mahātmyā magna nime — n. magnanimity | grandeur (of a place or a person) | lit. glorification (not. of places of pilgrimage) | lit. cf. Śrīmadbhāgavatamāhātmya. mahātmyakīrtana n. song of praise.
mahādāna [dāna] n. soc. considerable gift; 16 varieties are listed.
mahādānin [dānin] amnf mahādāninī who gives much — m. myth. np. of Mahādānī, epith. of Karna who gave all his gold ornaments to Indra, although he had to die for it.

mahādeva [deva] m. myth. np. of mahādeva, "Supreme God", epith. of Shiva; he is the patron of grammar | hist. np. of King Māhadeva₁, of the Yādavās dynasty; he reigned in Devagiri from 1260 to 1271; his prime minister was Hemādri₁; Rāmacandra₁ succeeded him | hist. np. of the physician Māhadeva₁ Pandita, author of the Hikmatprakāśa.
mahādevī | devī | f. soc. first queen; she is the mother of the crown prince.
mahādhana [dhana] amnf mahādhanā [“which costs dearly” precious — n. Great wealth.
mahādhanika [dhanika] amnf mahādhanikā extremely rich.
mahānagara [nagara] mn geo. metropolis, Great city; there were 6 of them in the time of Buddha: Srāvastī, Sāketa, Kāśī, Kauśāmbī, Rājagrha and Campā.

mahānadī [nadī] f. Great river | lit. [Mah.] epith. of the Ganges | geo. np. of the "Great River" mahānadī, originating in Bengal, which divides at Kaṭaka in Orissa, forming a large delta flowing into the Bay of Bengal.
Mahānaya [naya] m. Great prudence; Great wisdom | soc. mystical tradition śaiva Mahānaya of Kaśmīra, also called Mahārtha. mahānayam prasādah thank you very much.
mahānavamī [navamī] f. soc. 9th day of the festival of durgāpūjā, where DurgāAparājitā is celebrated by offering him sugar cane; cf. navarātra.

mahānasa [nasa] n. kitchen ["with good smells"] — f. mahānasī cook. mahānasādau phil. [Nyāya] in the kitchen, etc. (example in support [udāharaṇa] in the syllogism using the inevitable concomitance [vyāpti] between smoke and fire).
Mahānārāyaṇa [Nārāyaṇa] m. myth. np. of Mahānārāyaṇa, epith. of Viṣṇu.
mahānārāyanopaniṣad [upaniṣad] f. lit. np. of the Mahānārāyanopanisad, last chapter of the Tait tirīyāranyaka; it contains important hymns [mantras], such as the Medhāsukta.
mahānirvāṇa [nirvāṇa] n. [mahānirvāṇatantra] lit. np. from the mahānirvāṇatantra, esoteric text.
mahānīla [nīla] m. variety of dark blue sapphire.

mahānubhāva [anubhāva] amnf mahānubhāvā very powerful | magnanimous, generous, with lofty ideas | pl. soc. ["the very devout"] np. of a bhakti sect of the Mahārāṣṭra (13th-16th centuries); it wrote its works (in Marathi) in code.
mahānubhāvatā [tā] f. magnanimity, generosity.
mahānubhāvatva [tva] n. magnanimity, generosity.
Mahānuśāsana [anuśāsana] n. lit. np. from the Mahānuśāsana, text specifying the qualifications of a mathādhipati, attributed to Sankarācārya.
Mahāntaka [antaka] m. myth. np. of Mahāntaka, epith. of Shiva "the great destroyer".
mahānyāsa [nyāsa] m. bed. n.p. of the mahānyāsa, compilation of formulas [mantra] of praise of Rudra.
mahāpatha [patha] m. Great road | end of existence | np. of Mount mahāpatha, place of a precipice where the faithful of Shiva threw themselves.

Mahāpadma [padma] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of Mahāpadma "great lotus", diśāgaja of the south | myth. one of the 9 treasures [navanidhi] of Kubera; it is guarded by an eponymous dragon [nāga] — n. math. one billion (thousand billion).

mahāparinirvāna [parinirvānasūtra] lit. n. [Mahāyāna] np. of the Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra, eschatological text bd. which aims to define the nature of Buddha [buddhadhātu] as the principle of salvation; it deals with the cremation of the Buddha and the distribution of his ashes; it dates from the 2nd century, and is known only through its Tibetan and Chinese translations; also called Nirvāṇasūtra || pali mahaparinibbanasutta.
mahāparīkṣā [parīkṣā] f. soc. great scholarly examination, completing 14 levels of study.

mahāpātaka [pātaka] n. mortal sin, sacrilege; the 5 principal ones are: the murder of a brahmin, the consumption of alcohol, theft, adultery with the wife of the master [gurutalpa] and association with anyone who commits these crimes; opp. upapātaka.
mahāpātakin [in] amnf mahāpātakinī coup pable d'un siné mortel.
mahāpātra [pātra] n. soc. prime minister.

mahāpurāṇa [purāṇa] n. bed. one of the 18 main mythological books [purāṇa], attributed to Vyāsa: Brahmapurāņa, Padmapurāņa, Visnupurāņa, Vāyupurāņa (Sivapurāņa), Bhāgavatapurāņa, Mārkaņdeyapurāņa, Nāradapurāņa, Agni purāņa, Bhavisyapurāņa, Brahmavaivartapurāņa, Lingapurāņa, Vārāhapurāņa, Skāndapurāņa, Vāmanapurāņa, Kūrmapurāņa, Matsyapurāņa, Garudapurāņa and Brahmāndapurāņa; opp. upa purāṇa.
mahāpuruṣa [puruṣa] m. great man; eminent person; hero; sage, saint | phil. Supreme being; epith. of Vișnu.
Mahāpuruṣanirṇaya [nirṇaya] m. lit. np. from the Mahāpuruşanirnaya "Demonstration of the existence of God", phil. work due to Yamunācārya.
Mahāprakāśa [prakāśa] m. hist. np. of Mahāprakāśa, śaiva philosopher of the Krama school of the Cola country (around 13th century); Maheśvarānanda was his disciple.

mahāprajñā [prajñā₂] f. bd. Great Wisdom. Mahāprajñāpāramitāśāstra [prajñāpāramitāśāstra] n. bed. n.p. from Nāgārjuna's Mahāprajñāpāramitāśāstra "Treatise on the Great Virtue of Wisdom"; cf. Prajñāpāramitāśāstra.

Mahāpratisarā [pratisarā] f. lit. np. of the Mahāpratisarā "Great protection", text of the Vajrayāna tradition giving protective magical formulas [dhāranī], dating from around the 6th century; also called Mahāvidyārājñī.
mahāpratīhāra [pratīhāra] m. soc. chief doorman.
mahāprabandha [prabandha] m. lit. Great literary work.

mahāprabhu [prabhu] m. soc. (title) great lord, prince | myth. np. of mahāprabhu "great Lord", epith. of Indra, of Shiva or of Vishnu; a name of God | hist. title of Caitanya deified by the Gaudīya sect.

mahāpralaya [pralaya] m. phil. dissolution of the Universe into its original nature [prakṛti] at the extinction of Brahmā [brahmapralaya] (at the end of a mahākalpa, every 100 Brahmic years, i.e. 311000 billion years).
mahāprasthāna [prasthāna] n. great departure, death.

mahāprasthānika [ika] amfn mahāprasthānikā relating to the great departure, which concerns death — n. [mahāprasthānikaparvan] lit. np. from the Mahāprasthānikaparva, 17th book of the Mah., "of the great journey".
mahāprāṇa [prāṇa] amnf mahāprāṇā who has great physical endurance | phon. (phoneme) aspirated; opp. alpaprāṇa — m. phon. aspiration.
mahābala [bala] amnf mahābalā extremely strong; very powerful, very effective — f. mahābalā bio. bot. Sida spinosa, bushy malvaceae with pale yellow flowers, used in medicine.
mahābaleśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of mahābaleśvara, plateau at 1350 in the Western Ghats, 120 km south of Pune, where the Kṛṣṇā river originates. [9

Mahābali [bali] m. myth. np. of Mahābali or great king bali, considered as ideal king of the golden age, condemned to reign in hell by the jealousy of the gods; he is celebrated in Kerala under the name of King Maveli, and the festival of Onam at the Malayālam New Year (at the beginning of the month of cinga, corr. to bhādrapada) celebrates his return to Earth for one day by the favor of Lakṣmī; in North India he is celebrated at dīpāvali.
mahābalipura | pura | n. geo. np. of the city of Mahābalipuram, in Tamil Nadu; its rock-carved temples date back to the Pallava king Ma hendravarmā₁.

mahābāhu [bāhu] amnf ["who has great"] arms"] powerful (said of a warrior). atha cainam nityajātam nityam vā manyase mṛtam | tathāpi tvam mahābāho | naivaṃ śocitum arhasi [BhG.] For if you consider that he is constantly born and constantly dead, O powerful one (Ar juna), then truly there is no reason for you to mourn him.

mahābodhi [bodhi] f. bd. Great wisdom of the Bud dha — m. bd. epith. of the Buddha “great sage” | geo. np. of the temple of mahābodhi in Gayā; it is the first place of pilgrimage bd. in the World; it dates from the 6th century.
Mahābrāhmaṇa [brāhmaṇa] m. (ironic) high brahmin | soc. qualifies the vidūṣaka not. in his role as scapegoat | soc. priest in charge of rites
funeral [śrāddha] at Vārāṇasī — n. lit. np. of the Mahābrāhmaṇa, epith. of the Tāṇḍyabrāhmaṇa.
mahābhakta [bhakta] m. myth. [BhP.] expert in devotion, considered as a path to liberation; cf. Kapila.

mahābhaya [bhaya] n. calamity, catastrophe; great peril. daivānyastau mahābhayāni agnir udakam vyādhir durbhikṣaṃ mūṣikā vyālāḥ sarpā rakṣāṃsīti [Arthaśāstra] The eight calamities of fate are Fires, Floods, Epidemics, Famine, Mice, Wild Beasts, Snakes and Demons.
mahābhāga [bhāga] amnf mahābhāgā very happy, fortunate; eminent; illustrious — voc. adr. Your Eminence, Your Excellency, Noble Sire.

Mahābhārata [Bhārata₁] m. lit. epic narrative [itihāsa] of the Mahābhārata "Great India"; it comprises 90,000 stanzas [śloka] in 18 books [parvan] and 97 appendices [upaparvan] plus a supplement, the Harivaméa; it describes the fratricidal struggle between the Pāṇḍavās and their cousins the Kau ravās; its philosophical message is the Bha gavadgītā; its compilation took place between the 4th century BC and the 4th century AD; myth. it is said that its composer Vyāsa dictated it to Gaņeśa; his disciple Vaiśampāyana recited it to Janamejaya during his sarpasattra, where Ugraśravā Sauti₂ heard it and transmitted it in turn; cf. Bhārata₁ — n. |mahābhāratākhyāna| id.
Mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaya [tātparyanirṇaya] m. bed. n.p. of the Mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaya, commentary by the Mah. by Madhva; Vādirāja glossed it Bhāvaprakāśikā tīkā .

Mahābhāṣya [bhāṣya] n. lit. np. of the Mahābhāṣya "great commentary (on the grammar of Pāṇini)", work of Patañjali₁ (circa 200); it gives the commentary on 1228 rules of Pāṇini, and discusses the supplementary rules [vārttika] of Kātyāyana; it is divided into 85 sections [āhnika].
mahābhāṣyadīpikā [dīpikā] f. bed. n.p. from the mahābhāṣyadīpikā "Clarification of the Mahābhāṣya", name of a grammar treatise by Bhartrhari, of which only an incomplete manuscript survives.
Mahābhāṣyapradīpa [pradīpa] m. lit. np. of the Mahābhāsyapradīpa, commentary on the Mahābhāsya due to Kaiyata; cf. Bhāṣyapradīpa.
mahābhāṣyapradīpaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. bed. n.p. of the Mahābhāsyapradīpaprakāśa, his commentary, by Pravartakopādhyāya.
mahābhiṣava [abhiṣava] m. soc. solemn pressing of the soma.
mahābhiṣeka | abhiṣeka | m. soc. solemn anointing or sprinkling.
Mahābhīṣma [bhīṣma] m. myth. np. of Mahābhīṣma "Father of bhīṣma", epith. of King Sāmtanu.
mahābhūta [bhūta] n. phil. [Sāṃkhya] coarse element; syn. sthūlabhūta; opp. sūkṣmabhūta.
mahāmanas [manas] amnf ["who has a big heart"] magnanimous | ["who thinks highly (of himself)"] proud, haughty; arrogant.

mahāmantra [mantra] mn soc. Great incantation of the Vaisnava tradition. hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare | hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare || bed. |"hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare | hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare | |"] O God kṛṣṇa, O God kṛṣṇa, kṛṣṇa, kṛṣṇa, O God O God, O God rāma, O God rāma, rāma, O God O God; bhakti mantra, to be recited in japa or chanted in procession; its continuous recitation is said to bring liberation.
mahāmantrin | mantrin | m. soc. title of chief minister of a king.
Mahāmayūrī [mayūrī] f. bd. np. of the vidyārājñī Mahāmayūrī "Great Peacock Queen of Wisdom"; she is depicted peaceful, riding a peacock.
mahāmalla | malla | m. soc. np. of mahāmalla, title of "great wrestler"; used not. as a title of glory | viruda | by the Pallava dynasty.
mahāmaha [maha] amnf mahāmahā very powerful — n. geo. np. of the mahāmaha basin of Kumbhakona, place of a great annual pilgrimage.
mahāmahopādhyāya [mahopādhyāya] m. soc. mahāmahopādhyāya "Very great master", title of exceptional erudition.
mahāmātya [amātya] m. soc. prime minister.

mahāmātra [mātra] amnf mahāmātrī in Great quantity; great; excellent — ifc. best among (iic.) — m. soc. high person; mi nistre | elephant driver; elephant superintendent — f. mahāmātrī high-ranking lady; wife of the master [guru] | ang. mahout.
mahāmāna [māna₁] m. pride, arrogance.

Mahāmāyā [māyā] f. myth. np. of Mahāmāyā "the Supreme Illusion", tantric goddess, first yoginī among the 64 | phil. [siddhānta] the pure matter of Śiva's consciousness. namaste'stu mahāmāye śrīpīthe surapūjite Honor to you O Mahāmāyā, you the socleyoni, you worshipped by the gods.

Mahāmāyātantra [tantra] n. bd. np. of the Mahāmāyātantra, short text of the tantric tradition of the Anuttarayogatantra, dealing with contemplative techniques such as lucid dreaming [svapnadarśana] (around the 10th century); it circulated in the monastic circles of the accomplished [mahāsiddha] and was translated in the 11th century into Tibetan.
mahāmāyūrī [māyūra] f. lit. np. of the mahāmāyūrī or sūtra of the Great Peacock, bd. text listing the Indian tutelary spirits [yakṣa], popular in China and Japan.
Mahāmāheśvara [māheśvara] title soc. mr. Mahāmāheśvara of great worshiper of Siva; cf. Jayadratha₂.
mahāmukha [mukha] m. ["Grandgousier"] np. of a king.
mahāmudrā [mudrā] f. bd. esoteric doctrine of the ultimate nature of mind; Tilopa received it from Va jradhara and taught it to Nāropa; it was transmitted to Tibet in the Kagyūpa tradition by Marpa.
mahāmṛtyuñjaya [mṛtyuñjaya] n. [mahāmṛtyuñjayamantra] phil. [śaiva] np. of the Mahāmṛtyunjaya, great mantra "that conquers death"; cf. traiyambakamantra.
mahāmoha | moha | m. phil. Divine Illusion Supreme myth. np. of mahāmoha "the Evil One", symbolizing the divine power of Illusion, son of Manas and Pravrtti.
mahāyajña [yajña] m. soc. [SB.] ved. one of the five major rites of the śrauta ritual prescribed for an accomplished householder [āhitāgni]; cf. pañcamahāyajña.

mahāyamaka [yamaka] n. lit. rhet. figure of speech [alaṃkāra] where the four quarters of a stanza are identical, but of different meanings. vikāśamīyurjagatīśamārganāh vikāśamīyur jagatīśamārgaṇāḥ | vikāśamīyurjagatīśamārgaṇāḥ vikāśamīyurjagatīśamārganāh | [Kirātārjunīya] The arrows of the prince (Arjuna) flashed forth brilliantly, the arrows of the master of the World (Shiva) scattered; the troop (gana) of demon slayers rejoiced, and those who seek God gathered in Heaven (to contemplate).

Mahāyāna [yāna] n. bd. np. of the Mahāyāna "Great Way (of Liberation)" or "Great Vehicle", reformed Buddhist doctrine, opposed to the "Lesser Vehicle" [Hīnayāna]; its philosophical source goes back to Nāgārjuna and Aryadeva; the idealist Yogācāra doctrine and the nihilistic Madhya maka doctrine are distinguished within it.
Mahāyānasamgraha [samgraha] m. bd. np. of the Mahāyānasamgraha, principal collection of the bd. Yogācāra doctrine, due to Asanga.

Mahāyānasūtrālamkāra [sūtraalamkāra] n. lit. np. of the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra "Ornament of the aphorisms of the great Vehicle", bd. work of the 4th century, attributed to Maitreya₃ and possibly due to Asanga; it is inserted in his commentary |bhāṣya|, attributed to Vasubandhu; it expounds in particular the doctrine of the trisvabhāva.

mahāyuga [yuga] n. phil. era, cumulative period of the 4 ages of the World [yuga], worth 12000 divine years, and therefore about 4.32 million human years; there are 1000 in a kalpa. sahasra yuga paryantam ahar yad brahmano viduh [BhG.] It is known that one day (1/2 day) of Brahmā is worth 1000 eras.
mahāranya [aranya] n. Great forest.
mahāratna [ratna] n. precious stone: vajra the diamond, muktā the pearl, māṇikya the ruby, nīla the sapphire and marakata the emerald.
mahāratnakūṭa |ratnakūṭa| n. bd. cf. ratnakūṭa.
mahāratha [ratha] m. great warrior ["who has a great chariot"].
mahārāja [rājan] m. soc. np. of mahārāja, title of great king | soc. title of renunciant; ad. to a brahmin | jn. head of congregation | mod. title of brahmin, not. cook — f. mahārājñī queen.
mahārājādhirāja [adhirāja] m. mahārājādhirāja, title of supreme king of the great kings; cf. Sandra Gupta.

Mahārāṣṭra |rāṣṭra| m. pl. geo. the people of the Marāṭhās — n. geo. np. of the Mahārāṣṭra "great Kingdom"; not. the Maratha country — f. mahārāṣṭrī their language, Marāthī, "best prākṛtī" according to Daṇḍī₁; cf. māhārāṣṭrī.
mahāroman [roman] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of King Mahāromā "with long hair", son of Kīrtirāta, father of Svarnaromā.
mahāraurava [raurava] m. bd. de np. mahāraurava, one of the 8 burning hells, where the damned are devoured by ferocious beasts.
mahārṇava | arṇava | m. ocean.
mahārtha [artha] m. Great matter; deep sense | soc. mystical tradition śaiva mahārtha of Kaśmīra, also called Mahānaya — amnf mahārtha of Great importance; important, deep.
Mahārthamañjarī [mañjarī] f. lit. np. of the Mahārthamañjarī, phil. śaiva work of Maheśvarānanda, who also composed his gloss Parimala.
mahārthavat |vat| amnf mahārthavatī which has a profound meaning; very valid.
mahārbuda | arbuda | n. math. one billion; syn. padma. mahārha var. mahārgha [arha] amnf mahārhā very worthy, very precious.
Mahālakṣmī [Lakṣmī] f. myth. np. of Mahālakṣmī, Lakṣmī in glory, śakti of Viṣṇu | soc. young prepubescent girl of 13 years representing Durgā at the festival of durgāpūjā.
mahālakṣmīdīpadānavidhi |dīpadānavidhi| mr. bed. n.p. of the mahālakṣmīdīpadānavidhi, paddhati on the cult of Mahālakṣmī.
mahālaya [ālaya] m. Large dwelling, palace | temple, monastery, sanctuary, place of pilgrimage — f. mahālayā soc. new moon of the month bhādra, and last day of the calendar; festival cor respondant.
mahālinga [linga] n. soc. sign of Šiva associated with one of the 5 elements; cf. pañcabhūtamahālinga.

mahāvaṃśa |vaṃśa| m. lit. np. of the Mahāvaṃśa "Great Chronicle" of the kings of Lankā, longest epic poem in the pāli language, due to Mahānāma (5th century); it begins with the reign of the mythical king Vijaya₂Simhala and ends with that of King Mahāsena; cf. Cūlavaṃśa.
mahāvakṣas [vakṣas] amnf with a broad chest (said of heroes).
mahāvana | vana | n. Large forest, jungle.

Mahāvastu [vastu₁] n. bd. np. of the Mahāvastu, collection of texts from the vinayapitaka of the Lokot taravādī school of the Mahāsāmghikās, composed between the 1st and 6th centuries in North India in hybrid Sanskrit bd.

mahāvākya [vākya] n. lit. Great literary work gram. discourse, as opposed to the utterance of a sentence without context (vākya) | phil. [Vedānta] important formula of monistic teaching, such as tat tvam asi or so'ham or aham brahmāsmi or neti neti.
mahāvādin | vādin | amnf mahāvādinī bd. title of master in dialectic.
mahāvāyu |vāyu| m. storm.
mahāvidyā [vidyā] f. Great science; supreme knowledge | phil. [Tantra] aspect of the power [śakti] of the Goddess [Durgā]; we traditionally list 10: cf. daśamahāvidyā.
Mahāvidyārājñī [rājñī] f. bed. n.p. of the Mahāvidyārājñī “queen of protective incantations”; cf. Mahāpratisarā.
mahāvidyālaya [vidyālaya] m. college.

Mahāvibhāṣā [vibhāṣā] f. alternative, option | gram. general problem of the optionality of the rules of Pāṇini | lit. np. of the Mahāvibhāṣā "Great Exposition", sarvāstivāda philosophical text from Kaśmīra, known by its Chinese translation.
mahāvihāra [vihāra] m. bd. large monastery; cf. Vikramaśīla, Nālandā, Somapura, Uddāntapurī, Jagaddala.

Mahāvīrá [vīra] m. great hero | Vedic. the Sun; cf. pravargya | myth. epith. of various gods myth. np. of Mahāvīra, epith. of Hanuman the "great Hero" | jn. epith. of the ascetic Vard hamāna Mahāvīra₁, founder of Jainism (~599–527 antecedent); born a prince in Vaiśālī₁ in Bihāra, he left his family at 28 and spent 12 years in penance before attaining liberation [kaivalya]; he then traveled throughout Magadha to preach the doctrine

victorious [Jaina]; according to the śvetāmbara tradition, after her conception by the Brahmin Devānandā, her embryo was transferred into the womb of Princess Triśalā | hist. np. of the Jaina mathematician Mahāvīra₂ or Mahāvīrācārya; he lived in Bihāra in the 9th century; he is the author of the Ganitasārasangraha "Treatise on Mathematics", which revised the Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta and separated mathematical teaching from astronomy; he advanced algebra, and fixed geometric terminology | Vedic pot used for the sacrifice of pra vargya; it is made by hand by the Brahmin using clay, without a potter's wheel, before being placed in the fire and heated white-hot.

mahāvīracarita | charity | n. bed. n.p. from the mahāvīracarita “Exploits of the Great Hero”, famous drama of Bhavabhūti; it tells the story of Rāma until his departure into the forest, by intrigue of Rāvaṇa; Vīrarāghava commented on it.

mahāvīrya [vīrya] amnf mahāvīryā very powerful, of great strength; very effective — m. gentle pa tate | myth. epith. of many gods or heroes | myth. [BhP.] np. of the "very energetic" king mahāvīrya Janaka, son of Bṛhadratha₂, father of Sudhrti.
mahāvedi [vedi] f. soc. ["great altar"] area encompassing the solemn Vedic ritual, to the east of the hut containing the small altar [prācīnavaṃśa].
mahāvyutpatti [vyutpatti] f. lit. np. of the mahāvyutpatti, a bilingual Sanskrit-Tibetan dictionary of basic concepts compiled in Tibet in the 9th century under the patronage of the king.

mahāvrata [vrata] n. phil. [yoga] great vow (of nonviolence, truthfulness, probity, chastity and selflessness) | ved. "great observance" re religious, ved. ceremony of the winter solstice, variant of the Agnistoma ritual celebrated on the penultimate day of the gavāmayana period; it includes the swinging of a priest on a swing, an obscene dialogue between a student [brahmacarya] and a prostitute, ritual copulation between the prostitute and a man from Magadha, the fight of an ārya and a śūdra for a white skin disc representing the sun, and a dance with amphorae practiced by young girls around the fire; Finally, the king, on his chariot, after circumambulating the sacrificial space [vedi], shoots three arrows at a circular hide stretched between two poles to "gain the sun"; there, the sthālīpāka is consumed | jn. Jain ritual observance; the traditional list comprises twelve: the 5 minor vows [anuvrata] of every disciple, the 3 meritorious vows |guṇavrata| and the 4 disciplinary vows |śikṣāvrata| of the renunciant. jātideśakālasamayān avicchinnah sārvabhaumah
tadmahāvratam [YS.] Independent of birth, place, time and circumstances, this is the great universal vow.
mahāśaya [āśaya] m. ["great receptacle"] ocean — amnf mahāśayā who has noble sentiments, respectable.
mahāśāla [śāla] amnf mahāśālā soc. rich master of a house.
mahāśūdra |śūdra| amnf mahāśūdrā f. mahāśūdrī soc. high-ranking servant | cowherd.
mahāśūnyatā [śūnyatā] f. bd. [Mahāyāna] the great emptiness, third stage of wisdom, in which the distinction between the conditioned [saṃskṛta] and the unconditioned [asaṃskṛta] disappears.

mahāśveta [śveta] amnf mahāśvetā of a brilliant white — f. mahāśvetā lit. [K.] np. of the nymph [apsaras] mahāśvetā "Immaculate", daughter of the great harva Hamsa₁ and the apsaras Gaurī₁; she mourns the loss of the beautiful ascetic Puṇḍarīka₂ who preferred death to breaking his vows by giving in to love.
mahāśvetāvṛttānta [vṛttānta] m. bed. n.p. from the mahāśvetāvṛttānta, episode of the Kādambarī.
mahāsattā [sattā] f. phil. absolute existence.
mahāsattra [sattra] n. soc. great sacrifice of soma.
mahāsattva [sattva] m. great creature — amnf mahāsattvā of noble essence: courageous; princely.
mahāsandhivigrahika [sandhivigrahika] m. soc. minister of peace and war.
mahāsamādhi [samādhi] m. death.

mahāsāmghika [sāmghika] m. pl. bd. np. of the bd. school of the Mahāsāmghikās; it flourished notably around Termes (Bactria) from 50 to 650, in opposition to the ancient bd. [sthavira]. mahāsāṃghikalokottaravādin cf. lokottaravādin.
mahāsāmanta [sāmanta] m. soc. great vassal (honorary title).

mahāsiddha [siddha₁] m. accomplished yogi, possessing great powers | bd. perfect accomplished; tradition counts 64; cf. Nāgārjuna, Tilopa, SamantabhadraNāropa, Marpa, Matsyen dranātha, Milarepa, Gorakṣanātha.
mahāsiddhi | siddhi | f. great power of an accomplished yogi | bd. power of a perfect accomplished one.
mahāsubhāsitasamgraha | subhāsitasamgraha | mr. bed. n.p. from the Mahāsubhāsitasamgraha, enormous collection of 14,653 dictors in 8 volumes, edited by Lud wik Sternback (1974-2007).

Mahāsena₁ [senā] amnf mahāsenā who has a Great Army — m. general | myth. epith. of SkandaKārttikeya | hist. np. of the king of Lankā Mahāsena₁ "of the Great Army" (late 3rd century); he attempted to impose bd. Mahāyāna at the expense of the original Theravāda doctrine; he undertook great irrigation works | hist. cf. Caṇḍamahāsena | lit. [KSS.] np. of the king Mahāsena₁ of Alakā₁, husband of Sasiprabhā₂, father of Sundarasena.
mahāsenāpati |senāpati| mr. soc. general in chief. |sthāmaprāpta| Mahāsthāmaprāpta m. |Mahāyāna| n.p. of the bodhisattva bd. Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
mahāsvāda [svāda] amnf mahāsvādā savory, delicious — m. soc. title of a Brahmin temple cook.
mahāhanu |hanu| amnf to the jaw then health.

Mahendra | Indra | m. myth. np. of Mahendra, epith. of Indra "Majestic" | [mahendragiri] geo. np. of the Mahendra mountains₁ (1500 m) south of Orissa (modern district of Gajapati); myth. |Mah.| ParaśurāmaJāmadagnya established his hermitage there and did penance; Karna visited him to learn the science of weapons from him; there he accidentally killed the calf of a Brahmin's cow, who cursed him by prophesying his death in battle, the wheel of his chariot stuck in the mud; Parasurāma revealed to him the secret of the brahmāstra, but realizing that he had lied to him by pretending to be a Brahmin, he drove him away, prophesying that he would forget the weapon mantra during his battle with his principal enemy | hist. np. of the Jain astronomer Mahendra₂ Sūri (14th century); he is credited with the treatise Yantrarāja on the astrolabe.

Mahendrapala [pala] m. hist. np. of Mahen drapala₁, king of the Pratīhārās dynasty; he reigned (885–910) over an empire extending from Gurjara to Bihāra; his capital was Kanyākubjāmahodayā; he patronized his guru the poet Rājaśekhara; he is also called Nirbhaya "Fearless".

mahendravarman [varman] m. hist. np. of the Pallava prince Mahendravarmā₁ or Mahendravikrama varmā, son of Simhaviṣnuvarmā (571630); he reigned in Kāñcī, his title of glory [viruda] was Satrumalla; he protected the arts, and had the first temples carved in the rock executed at Mahābalipuram; he is the author of the satirical play | prahasana | Mattavilāsa.
maheśa |īśa| m. myth. np. of maheśa "great Lord", epith. of Shiva.

Maheśvara [īśvara] m. sovereign, god | myth. np. of Maheśvara "the Supreme Lord", epith. of Shiva (or more rarely of Krishna) | hist. cf. Maheśvarakavi | math. symb. the number 11 (for the 11 aspects of Rudra) — f. Maheśvarī cf. māheśvarī geo. np. of the city of Maheśvarī, on the banks of the Narmadā, 70 km southwest of Indore in Madhya Pradesh; it was the capital of Mālava under the Holkar dynasty in the 18th century.
Maheśvarakavi | kavi | m. hist. np. of Maheśvarakavi, lexicographer of the 12th century; he is the author of the Viśvaprakāśa.
maheśvarakhaṇḍa [khaṇḍa] mn lit. n.p. of maheśvarakhanda, section of Skandapurāna.

maheśvarasūtra [sūtra] n. pl. gram. sequence of phonemes listed in the pratyāhārasūtrāṇi, permet the use of condensed statements in the grammar; these 14 formulas were supposedly revealed by Shiva by sounding the dhakkā drum which he holds in his hand during the ānandatāṇḍava dance.

Maheśvarānanda [ānanda] m. hist. np. of Maheśvarānanda "Bliss of the Lord", initiation name of Gorakșa₁, śaiva author of the Krama school native of the Cola country (around 13th century); disciple of Mahāprakāśa, he is the author of the Mahārthamañjarī.
maheṣvāsa [iṣvāsa] m. master archer.
mahokṣá [ukṣan] m. fat bull.
mahokṣátā [tā] f. quality of a large bull

Mahotsava [utsava] m. soc. big festival | hist. town of Mahotsava, founded by Candravarman around 800; she succeeded Khajurāho as capital of the Candela kingdom; mod. Mahoba — f. mahotsava ifc. soc. great festival of.
mahodadhi [udadhi] m. ocean.

Mahodaya₁ [udaya] amnf mahodayā that gives much (happiness); very prosperous — cl. adr. blessed; very dear; Sir — m. Great prosperity | myth. [Rām.] np. of Mount Mahodaya₁ that Hanuman brought back with his herbs to heal Lakshman of his wounds; cf. Vrşa | myth. [Rām.] np. of the ascetic Mahodaya₁, who refused to attend the sacrifice of Viśvāmitra for Triśanku and was cursed to become an outcast — f. Mahodayā myth. np. of Mahodayā "Prosperous", epithet of the city of Kanyākubjā, capital of Kuśanābha. Devadatta mahodayasya the esteemed Devadatta.
mahodayapura | pura | n. geo. np. of the city of Ma hodayapura; cf. Mahodayā.
mahodara [udara] amnf mahodarī who has a big belly — m. myth. np. of mahodara, epith. of Ganesa "with a big belly".
mahopanisad | upanisad | f. lit. major esoteric lesson [upaniṣad].
mahopādhyāya [upādhyāya] m. soc. "grand master", title of erudition and ritual spiritual accomplishment.
mahoraga | uraga | m. great serpent | jn. a class of demons, the mahoragās.
mahoraska [uraska] amnf broad-chested mahoraskā.
mahaujas |ojas| amnf very strong.
mahi [mahat] ind. ved. great | greatness | [mahī] the earth — adv. very; too.
Mahidāsa [dāsa] m. bed. n.p. of Mahidāsa "Servant of the earth", author of the Aitareya brāhmaṇa of the Rgveda.
abundant mahimat |mat| amnf mahimatī.
máhivrata [vrata] amnf mahivrata which has great powers, powerful.
mahita [pp. mah] amnf mahitā honored, celebrated.
mahima iic. mahiman.

mahimabhatta | bhatta | m. hist. np. of mahimabhatta, theorist of literary aesthetics, author of the Vyaktiviveka (11th century); he denies the autonomy of a semantic function of suggested meaning |vyañjanā|.

mahimán [mahatiman] m. greatness, my jestery; glory | phil. all-greatness, an attribute of Śiva | phil. [yoga] the power to grow at will, an astasiddhi | np. of man mahimā "the great one" — f. cf. mahimā. mahimnā of strength; mightily.
mahimā [f. mahiman] f. grandeur, majesty. gomahimā supremacy of the cow.
mahimādharma [dharma] m. mod. movement of Hindu dissidents born in Orissa in the 19th century, opposed to the worship of idols and not. of Jagannātha.
mahilā [mahila] f. woman; ecstatic or drunk woman | kind of drug | lit. [PT.] np. of the fictional river mahilā "Impetuous".
mahilāropya [āropya] n. lit. np. of mahilāropya "Perched on the mahilā", a fictional South Indian city mentioned in the Nordic recensions of the Pañcatantra.

mahiṣá [mahi] amnf mahiṣī important, powerful — m. buffalo | cf. Mahiṣāsura — f. mahiṣī female buffalo | soc. first queen of a king, high-ranking woman; opp. vāvātā, parivṛktī, pālāgalī | cf. mahisāsurī.

Mahiṣāsura | asura | m. myth. np. of the asura Mahiṣa or Mahiṣāsura, buffalo demon invulnerable to any male; he was defeated by the Goddess Durgā, using the weapons of all the gods combined; the gods had granted him to die only after having contemplated the sex of the Goddess; cf. Kālī, Durdhara, Durmukha₁ — f. mahiṣāsurī myth. (Kerala) np. of the asurī mahiṣī or mahiṣāsurī, sister of Mahiṣa, who to avenge him made such penances that Brahmā granted her kingship over the three worlds, and to be invulnerable to any creature not having the combined strength of Vișnu and Shiva; She was defeated by their synthesis HariharaputraAyyappa, and became a beautiful young girl upon her liberation.
mahiṣāsuramardinī [mardin] f. myth. np. of mahiṣāsuramardinī, epith. of Durgā "Overcoming the buffalo demon" thanks to the weapons of all the gods united.
mahiṣṭha [super. mahat] amnf mahiṣṭhā the greatest.

mahismat [mahisamat] amnf Mahiṣmatī (country) rich in buffaloes — f. Mahiṣmatī geo. np. of the sacred city of Mahismatī "rich in buffaloes", on the banks of the Narmadā; it was the capital of the Haihayās, not. of Kārtavīrya Arjuna₁; it is identified with the island of Māndhātā bearing Omkāreśvara or with Maheśvarī.
mahī₁ [contr. mahatī] f. the land | territory, soil.
mahī₂ [vn. mahat] v. [11] pr. r. (mahīyate) to be honored, to be worshipped; to be happy.
mahītala [tala] n. surface of the earth; soil.

Mahīdhara [dhara] m. ["who supports the earth"] mountain | myth. epith. of Visnu | hist. np. of Mahīdhara, commentator of the Veda of the 16th century; we owe him the Mantramahodadhi and the Vedadīpa.
mahīdhra [contr. Mahīdhara] m. mountain | math. symb. the number 7.
mahīdhraka [ka] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the mahīdhraka king Janaka, son of Vibudha, father of Kīrtirāta.

Mahīpa [pa₂] m. king ["protector of the earth"] | hist. np. of Mahīpa, minister of the king of Nanda padra in the 14th century and lexicographer; he is credited with the Sabdaratnākara and the Anekārthatilaka.
Mahīpakośa | kośa | mr. bed. n.p. of Mahīpakośa; cf. Sabdaratnakara.
mahīpati [pati] m. king, sovereign ["master of the earth".

Mahīpāla [pāla] m. king ["protector of the earth"] | hist. np. of King Mahīpāla of Kanyākubjā, successor sister and probably son of Mahendrapāla₁ (early 10th century); his guru was the poet Rājaśekhara.
mahībhuj |bhuj₃| m. king |"who enjoys the land"|.
mahīyas [comp. mahat] amnf mahīyasī bigger. aņoraņīyān mahatomahīyān ātmā [KU.] The Self, subtler than the atom and greater than the immensity.
mahe iic. mahā.
maho iic. mahā.
mahyam |dat. aham| ind. for me.

mā₂ part. of prohibitive negation (av. inj. or imp. or opt. or subj.) no, do not, so that ... do not (sometimes followed by sma) | (av. ppr.) utterance, insult || gr. ; lat. ne. x mā yy rather than x.
√ mā₃ v. [3] pr. (mimāti) to bellow.
mā₅ cl. mām.
√ ਸਾ mā₄ [related to mā₁] v. [1] pr. r. (mayate) v. [1] pr. (mayati) pf. (ni) to exchange, to barter (for (i.)).

√ mā₁ v. [3] pr. r. (mimīte) v. [2] pr. (māti) pft. (mamau) pp. (mita₁) pfp. (meya) pf. (anu, ut, upa, ni, nis, pari, pra, prati, vi, sam) to measure, delimit, mark; compare with (i.) | (māti) to correspond in measure; to be the size of g.; to fit in loc. | to measure to, to serve as (dat.); to grant | (av. na) not to admit g. | phil. to infer, to conclude — ps. (mīyate) to be measured — ca. (māpayati) to measure; to erect || gr. μετρον; lat. mensura, metor; fr. to measure, meter. guruh praharsah vapusi na mamau He could not contain his great joy.

mo |u| adv. ved. (pragrhya) and not (often followed by sú for su₁). mo sú nah nirrtir vadīt ved. Above all, do not let Nirrti destroy us. māstu do nothing about it. mā bhūḥ do not be. mā bhavatu no, that is not the case. tanmākārṣīḥ do not do that! mākarot let him not do it. maivam certainly not! maivam vocah do not speak like that! mābhaiṣīḥ var. mābhaiḥ do not be afraid. mā nāma ...above all not ... mā nāma rakṣiṇaḥ provided it is not the guards. mā bhūt ... (technique) it is not so, otherwise ... | the rule does not apply to a case such as ... mā bhūd āgataḥ should not be there? mā jīvan may he not live! mā yamam paśyeyam provided that I do not see Yama. paritrāyasvainām mā kasyāpi tapasvinaḥ haste patisyati Protect her, in case she falls into the hands of some ascetic.
māṃs n. |except noun. acc. voc. māṃsa| meat, flesh.

māṃsá |māṃsa| n. meat, flesh | pulp | pl. māṃsāni id. — v. [11] pr. (māṃsīyáti) to have meat alive | lat. limb; eng. member; fr. member; ru. meso; Lithuanian mesa. māṃsátas adv. (skin) on the flesh side; opp. lomatas.
māṃsatattva | tattva | n. soc. subject of meat consumption.

māṃsatattvaviveka [viveka] m. lit. np. from the Māṃsatattvaviveka "Controversy about meat", customary treatise | smṛti| by Viśvanātha₂; in it he justifies the consumption of (non-bovine) meat by the brahmins of North India, and criticizes the vegetarianism of the brahmins of South India as being of Buddhist influence.
māṃsatva |tva| n. state of being of the flesh.
māṃsarasa [rasa] m. broth or meat juice | blood.
māṃsaśoṇita |śoṇita| n. sg. (collective) of meat and blood.
māṃsāśana |aśana₂| n. the act of eating meat; the state of being a carnivore.
māmsāśin [āśin] amnf māmsāśinī carnivorous. māṃsaṃ māṃsāśinām the flesh of predators.
māmsī [f. māmsa] f. cf. jatāmāmsī.

māgadhá [*magadha] amnf māgadhī relating to the country of Magadha — m. prince of Magadha soc. man of mixed caste, not. of Ksatriya mother and Vaishya father | soc. bard; princely panegyrist; spy informant of the king — f. māgadhī language of Magadha; it was the administrative language of the Maurya empire, and the language of Buddha; it is used in Sanskrit theatre for characters of lower rank, not. servants and brigands | princess of Magadha | cumin, fennel, anise and other aniseed spices.
māgadhabhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. language of Magadha, spoken not. by Buddha; syn. māgadhī.

māghá [*magha] amnf māghī relating to the Maghās — m. astr. the month of the Maghās (January-February) lit. np. of Māgha, poet of the 7th or 8th century, author of the mahākāvya Šiśupālavadha — f. māghī astr. the full moon of the month of the Maghās. māghe santi trayoguņāh Māgha's poetry possesses the three qualities (upamā₂, arthagaurava, and padalālitya). navasarge gate māghe nava śabdo na vidyate [Mallinātha₁] He who has read the nine songs of Māgha will find no new word. māghe meghe vayam gatah [Mallinātha₁] We get lost trying to understand Māgha and Me ghadūta.
māghamela [mela] m. cf. makarasamkrānti.
māghya [*maghaya] n. organic. flower of the bot. Jas minimum multiflorum.

māṅgalika [*maṅgalaika] amnf Māngalikā Who desires success | Who brings luck — n. object Who brings luck, amulet — f. Māngalikā lit. [DKC.] np. of Māngalikā, nanny of the princess Ambālikā₂; she made Kāntaka believe that the princess was in love with him, and caused his downfall.
māṅgalya [*maṅgalaya] amnf māngalyā That which brings luck, That which gives fortune or happiness — n. object or ceremony of good omen.
māciram [mā₂ciram] adv. Soon; quickly ["without wasting a moment"].
māñjiṣṭha [*mañjiṣṭhā] amnf māñjiṣṭhā madder red tint — n. red color.

māthara [*mathara] m. soc. superior of a monastery or school | hist. np. of the ācārya Māṭhara; to him is due a commentary on the Sāmkhyakārikās; cf. Mātharavrtti. mātharavrtti phil. np. of the Mātharavrtti, commentary on the Sāṃkhyakārikās due to Māṭhara.
māṇava [*manua] amnf māṇavī ga min, gars; boy; not. young brāhmaṇa | pej. little man, dwarf | ornament of 16 (or 20) rows of beads.

māṇavaka |ka| m. boy, lad; schoolboy, Brahmanical student | 16-strand beaded ornament | lit. np. of māṇavaka, vidūṣaka of the Vikramorvaśīya — n. phon. variety of meter anuştubh₂ — f. māṇavikā young girl, maiden. simho māṇavakah this boy is (brave) like a lion.
māṇavīna |īna| amnf māṇavīnā good for schoolchildren.
māṇika [*maṇika] m. jeweller.
māṇikya [*maṇikaya] n. ruby; syn. maņirāga, padmarāga.
māṇikyapuñja [puñja] m. lit. ["collection of ru bis"] (Rājaśekhara) poetic genre borrowing di vers ingredients from several poems.
māṇḍava [*maṇḍava] n. lit. ["lento"] refers to a hymn [sāman] to be sung slowly — f. māndavī myth. [Rām.] np. of Māndavī, eldest daughter of King Kuśadhvaja₁; she married Bharata₁.

māṇḍavya [*maṇḍuya] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the ascetic māṇḍavya "of the line of maṇḍu"; he was meditating in his hermitage when thieves came to hide their loot there; having taken a vow of silence [muni], he did not answer the questions of the king's soldiers, was accused of the theft, and impaled on a three-pronged stake; seeing that he did not die, and that his anger was great, the king had him untied and apologized for the injustice, but the stake that impaled him could not be removed; Māndavya went to complain of his fate to Dharma, who told him that he had deserved it because, as a child, he had impaled a butterfly on a blade of grass; Māndavya decreed that no one is responsible for their actions before the age of 14, and he cursed Dharma by condemning him to incarnate on Earth as the son of a servant [śūdra]; cf. Vidura.
māṇḍūka [*maṇḍūka] amnf māṇḍūkī lit. concerning the maṇḍūkaśikṣā — m. pl. soc. np. of the Vedic school of the Māndūkās.
māṇḍūkāyana [ayana] amn soc. Who follows the doctrine of the frog [maṇḍūkaśikṣā] | pl. soc. Vedic school of the Māṇḍūkās.
Māṇḍūkeya [īya] m. hist. n.p. of the master Māṇdūkeya — b. his doctrine.
māṇdūkya [*maṇdūkaya] amnf māndūkyā phil. relating to the doctrine of the frog.
māṇḍūkyakārikā [kārikā] f. pl. bed. n.p. of the Māṇdūkyakārikās, commentary on the Māṇdūkyopaniṣad due to Gauḍapāda.

Māṇḍūkyopaniṣad [upaniṣad] f. lit. np. of the Māṇdūkyopaniṣad, esoteric lesson [upaniṣad] of the Atharvaveda; it explains the meaning of omkāra by the triad [avasthātraya] of the three stages of consciousness jāgrat, svapna and suṣupti, and the silence that follows as the turīya state of liberation; cf. Gaudapādakārikās.

mātaṃga var. mātaṅga [*mataṃga] m. elephant | soc. man of impure caste; syn. caṇḍāla, kirāta | jn. np. of the yakṣa Mātaṅga, associated with Mahāvīra₁; he is a god of wealth, analogous to Kubera and Jambhala | lit. |K. | np. of mātanga₁, chief of the tribe of forest hunters | lit. |DKC.| np. of mātanga₂, brahmin turned brigand in the middle of the pulindās of the Vindhya Mountains forest; one day he wanted to save the life of a brahmin, and was killed by the savages; Yama restored him to life, after showing him the torments of hell; He then became a devotee of Shiva, who showed him in a dream a cave containing inscriptions describing a magical ritual, and announced the visit of Rajavahana; when the latter appeared, he went with him to the hell Rasatala, where he recited formulas | mantra |, threw himself into the Fire, and obtained a divine body; immediately the celestial Kalindi₂ appeared, to whom he united and became the king of Rasatala — ifc. the best of (iic.) — f. mātaṃgī elephant | phil. [Tantra] np. of Mātaṅgī or Mātaṅginī "Elephant", a terrible aspect [mahāvidyā] of the Goddess [Sakti] | myth. np. of Mātaṅgī₁, daughter of Kaśyapa and Krodhavaśā; she gave birth to the line of elephants | soc. woman caṇḍālā or kirātī.
mātaṃgalīlā |līlā| f. lit. np. of the Mātaṃgalīlā "Entertainment around the elephant", work of Nīlakantha₇.
mātaṃgaka [ka] m. soc. tribal chief | lit. K. np. of Mātaṃgaka, chief of the savages | śabara | of Lake Pampā₁.
mātara iic. mātṛ.
mātarapitr [pitr] m. of the. mātarapitarau father and mother.
mātari [loc. mātr̩] ind. in the mother.

mātariśvan [śvan₂] m. ved. np. of Mātariśvā “That which swells in the mother”, chief of the breaths [marut], form of Agni personifying the power of procreation, and born in the womb of the Fire staff; Indian Prometheus, he brought Fire [Agni] to men, and entrusted it to the clan of the Bhārgavās.

mātali m. myth. np. of mātali, driver of Indra's chariot, born of a prodigy; the sage Śamika and his wife Tapasvinī having a son, they desired a second; an astrologer predicted to them that by placing their son in a hole in the ground, a twin brother would come to them, which happened; barely born, this one offered to Indra to drive his chariot to wage war against the asurās; the latter accepted and bap tisa mātali; he taught wisdom to Yayāti; |Mah.| he wanted to marry his daughter, the very beautiful Guṇakeśī, to a dragon [nāga]; Nārada took him to visit Bhogavatī, where he met Sumukha, a nāga prince of high lineage; but his father Cikura had just been eaten by Garuda, who had threatened to return to kill Sumukha; mātali then took Sumukha to In dra, where Vișnu gave her ambrosia |amṛta|; full of anger, Garuda complained to Vișnu Who humiliated him.
mātā |nom. mātṛ | iic.
mātāpitr [pitr] m. of. mātāpitarau the parents (in order of respect).
mātāmaha [mahat] m. maternal grandfather — f. matāmahī maternal grandmother.
mātuḥ |g. mātṛ| iic. .
mātuḥsuta [suta₂] m. (pej.) son of his mother.
mātula [mātr] m. maternal uncle | astr. solar year (opp. vimala, lunar year) — f. mātulā maternal uncle's wife | var. mātulī id. | var. mātulānī id. | cannabis smoke.
mātuleya |iya| m. cousin (son of a maternal uncle) — f. mātuleyī cousin.
mātulunga var. lunga m. organic. bot. Citrus medica, lemon tree.
mātulungaphala | phala | n. lemon.

mātṛ [man] f. [sg. nom. mātā, acc. mātaram; pl. nom. mātaraḥ, acc. mātr̄ḥ mother | respectful form of address for a woman of a certain age or rank | phil. np. of mātā the Divine Mother, the Goddess as Universal Mother; cf. Sakti, Durgā | myth. one of the six wet nurses who raised Skanda; cf. Kṛttikās | myth. [Mah.] a "mother to the child," a demonic female being to be pacified to avoid childhood illnesses; cf. mātrgaṇa | myth. a divine energy, associated with a principal god; first in number 7 [saptamātṛkās], then 8, 9 or 16 | matrix of the Fire Staff | var. mātrī id. | gr. ; lat. mater; ang. mother; all. Mutter; fr. mère. mātrībhavati she becomes a mother. vande mātaram "I adore you, Mother (country)", nationalist song by Bankim Chandra Chattopadyaya (1880), adopted as the national anthem of India in 1950. mātṛdevo bhava Treat your mother like a god.

mātṛgaṇa [gaṇa] m. myth. [Mah.] the group of 7 "mothers (dangerous) to children" [śiśumātaras] associated with Skanda: Kākī, Halimā, Rudrā, Bṛhalī, Aryā, Palālā and Mitrā; later they were identified with divine energies [saptamātṛkās].
mātṛtamā |tama| f. the most maternal; the mother par excellence.
mātṛdatta [datta] m. hist. np. of the trivedin Mātrdatta, contemporary and friend of Daṇḍī₁.
mātrbhāṣā |bhāṣā| f. mother tongue. mātrbhāṣā mātrdugdham The mother tongue is like breast milk.
mātrsvasr | svasr | f. maternal aunt.
mātṛṣvaṣrīya [īya] m. cousin (son of my ternal aunt) | var. mātrsvaseya id. — f. mātrsvasrīyā cousin | var. mātrsvaseyā id.
mātṛṣvaṣrīya |īya| mr. cousin (son of my ternal aunt) — f. mātrsvasrīyā cousin. mātṛhan var. mātṛghāta [han₂] m. matricide.
mātṛṣvaṣṛ |svaṣṛ| f. maternal aunt.
mātrarcanā [arcanā] f. veneration of the mother.
mātricchā [icchā] f. mother's desire.
mātrupāsanā | upāsanā | f. submission to the mother.

mātṛka [mātṛka] amnf mātṛkā maternal — m. maternal uncle — n. nature of mother — f. mātṛkā mother | goddess, divine mother; śakti of a god source, origin | alphabet; not. mystical alphabet associated with a diagram | yantra | gram. np. of the mātṛkā, sequence of the 50 phonemes of Sanskrit in canonical order, vowels followed by consonants; it is different from the Mālinī₂ of the Trika system | pl. mātṛkās cf. saptamātṛkās | phon. the 16 sound energies, including the vowels, the anusvāra, and the visarga.

mātra |instr. mā₁| n. small quantity, element, atom — ifc. measure of (20th century); sum, distance, length, depth, time of (20th century) | of only (20th century) — m. soc. (pej.) ((20th century) Brahmin) only by birth — amnf mātrā f. mātrī ifc. of the measure of; as great (high, long, deep, far) as (20th century) | nothing but, only, just after, barely (pp.) — f. cf. mātrā. kroṣāmātre adv. within earshot. māsamātre adv. within a month. bhuktamātre adv. just after eating. granthamātre adv. only in books. angulamātram one inch wide. arthamātram a certain sum of money. bhayamātram some kind of danger. ratimātram nothing but sensuality. rājāmātram only kings. trimātra amn three in number. śatamātram a hundred in number. śabdamātreņa only by a sound. grhamātro gajah an elephant the size of a house. dehamātram caitanyavišistam ātmā phil. The self is just the body qualified by consciousness. guņamātraviṣayā buddhiḥ phil. an idea concerning any quality. jātamātram na yaḥ śatrum vyādhim ca praśamam nayet That which does not suppress the enemy or disease at its onset.
Mātrarāja |rāja| m. hist. np. of the poet Mātrarāja, epith. of the prince Māyurāja, author of the plays | nāṭaka | Tāpasavatsarājacarita and Udāttarāghava.

mātrā [f. mātra] f. measure (size, duration, depth, degree, etc.) | unit of measure | phon. more, time to pronounce a short syllable, worth 2 beats [druta] | glyph of the nāgarī alphabet — ifc. That which has as its measure (iic.) (size, duration, depth, etc.) | the size of, no larger than (iic.); just, only, nothing but, (iic.) pure and simple; as soon as, hardly at all pp. . mātrayā adv. to a small extent. rājeti kā mātrā what does it matter to me that he is king? jālamātreņa vartayan Who lives only on water. uktamātre you vacane the words being barely pronounced.
mātrācyutaka | cyutaka | n. game consisting of replacing a vowel in a sentence to change its meaning.
mātrāchandas | chandas | n. phon. meter based on the length of syllables, rather than on their number; cf. mātrālāghava.
mātrāmeru | meru | m. math. sequence of Fibonacci numbers, studied by Pingala₂ for prosody, then by Gopāla₂ and Hemacandra.
mātrālāghava [lāghava] n. gram. conciseness of expression by brevity of syllables.

mātrāvṛtta [vṛtta] amnf mātrāvṛttā phon. refers to a classical meter, defined by the alternation of long or short syllables — f. mātrāvṛttā metric based on the alternation of long or short syllables; opp. akṣaravrttā.
mātrāsamaka [samaka] n. lit. poetic meter of 16 syllabic beats divided into groups of 4.
mātrāsparśa [sparśa] m. phil. physical perception.
mātrika [mātraika] amnf mātrikā ifc. pl. all kinds of (iic.) | phon. said of meters based on syllabic times; cf. mātrāvṛtta — f. mātrikā phon. prosodic instant, more.
mātrī cf. mātr.
mātsarya [*matsaraya] n. selfishness, envy, jealousy — m. myth. np. of Mātsarya, Envy personified.
mātsya [*matsya] amnf mātsyā relating to the fish or the matsya avatar.
mātsyanyāya | nyāya | m. "maxim of the fish": the biggest eat the smallest; similar to the law of the strongest.
mātsyapurāna | purāna | n. cf. matsyapurāna.
mātha |act. manth| m. act of churning, stirring, destruction.
māthurá [*mathurā] amnf māthurī ori ginary of mathurā — f. māthurī lit. n.p. of the māthurī, commentary by Mathurānātha₁ of the
Tattvacintāmani [Tattvacintāmanirahasya] | gram. np. of the Māthurīvṛtti, ancient oral commentary of the Astādhyāyī.
māda | act. mad₁ | m. drunkenness, intoxication; passion | combat, war.
mādayitnú [yitnu| amnf intoxicant | var. madayişnu id.
mādana |agt. mad₁| amnf mādanā intoxi cant, exciting, intoxicating — m. myth. np. of mādana "the intoxicating one", epith. of Kāma — act. n. intoxica tion, intoxication.
mādin [agt. mad₁] amnf mādinī intoxi cant; narcotic — f. mādinī hemp.

Mādrī [*madra] f. myth. [Mah.] np. of Mādrī, Madra princess, 2nd wife of Pāṇḍu, mother of the twins Nakula and Sahadeva by the Aśvinau, thanks to the mantra that Kuntī had lent her; she made Pāṇḍu's destiny come true by giving herself to him, then threw herself on his funeral pyre as a satī; she is considered an incarnation of Dhrti.

mādhava [*Madhua] amnf mādhavī spring — m. epith. of the second Vedic month of spring vaiśākha; spring | myth. descendant of King Madhu; syn. yādava | myth. not. np. of mādhava, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "descendant of Madhu" | soc. designates a Brahmin descendant of Madhu | myth. relating to the asura Madhu₁ | hist. cf. Mādhavācārya | hist. np. of the mathematician and astronomer mādhava₁, of the Namputiri Brahmin family (1340–1425); he founded a school of mathematics in Kerala, and invented trigonometric series two centuries before Leibniz; He thus calculated an approximation correct to the 11th decimal place; his analytical work is known from the Gaņitayuktibhāṣā of Jyeṣṭhadeva; his works preserved to us are the Venvaroha and the Sphuțacandrāpti, which deal with the calculation of the position of the Moon | med. np. of mādhava₂, author of the mādhavanidāna | lit. np. of mādhava₃, hero of the play Mālatīmādhava — f. cf. mādhavī.
mādhavaka [ka] m. mead — f. mādhavikā bio. bot. Gærtnera racemosa, white jasmine, with a sweet fragrance; syn. mādhavī.
Mādhavakara |kara₁| m. med. np. of the physician Mādhavakara or mādhavacandrakara; cf. mādhava₂.
mādhavacandrakara [candrakara₁] m. med. np. of the physician mādhavacandrakara; cf. mādhava₂.

mādhavanidāna [nidhāna] n. med. np. of the mādhavanidāna, epith. of the Rogaviniścaya of mādhava₂, synthesis of the medical knowledge of India over 2000 years, written between the 8th and 12th centuries; it includes in particular a compilation of the treatises of the Brhattrayī₁, and an important glossary, the Madhukośa.

Mādhavācārya [ācārya] m. hist. np. of Mādhavācārya, minister of King Bukka₁ of Vijayanagara and elder brother of Sāyana (14th century); he served as mentor to three generations of Vijayanagara kings; considered a saint, a temple is dedicated to him; of ad vaita vedānta obedience, he became superior of the monastery [maṭhādhipati] of Śṛṅgerī in 1331; he is the author of the Vedāntādhikaranaratnamālā, the Kālanirnaya, the Parāśaramādhavīya, the Rgbhāsya and the Jai minīyanyāyamālāvistara; He is also credited with the Sarvadarśanasamgraha, the Pañcadaśī, and the Jīvanmuktiviveka; he is also called by his renunciant name Vidyāranya Svāmī.

mādhavānāla [anala] m. lit. np. of Mādhavānala, a young musician from Puspavatī who sings while accompanying himself on his vinā and attracts the love of all the women; King Govindacandra invites him to his court, the queen falls in love with him and the king banishes him; he leaves for Kāmavatī where at the court of King Kāmasena he falls in love with the courtesan kāmakandalā; their love story is told in the Mādhavānalakāmakandalākathā — n. lit. np. of the eponymous tale Mādhavānalakathā. mādhavānālakāmakandalākathā [kāmakandalākathā₁] f. lit. np. from the Mādhavānalakāmakandalākathā "History of Mādhavānala and kāmakandalā"; this love story has been circulating since the 12th century, and exists in many written forms, often richly illustrated.
mādhavīya [īya] amnf mādhavīyā lit. com posed by mādhava or Mādhavācārya | gram. np. of the Mādhavīya dhātuvṛtti; cf. Mādhavīyadhātuvṛtti.
mādhavīyadhātuvrtti [dhātuvrtti] f. gram. np. of the Mādhavīyadhātuvrtti, treatise on the verb roots of Sāyaṇa (dedicated to his brother Mādhavācārya); it restores the dhātuvrtti used by Pāṇini.

Mādhavī [f. mādhava] f. bio. bot. Hiptage benghalensis, a climbing shrub with fragrant white flowers; it is said that this vine only grows around trees with a pleasant scent, such as the mango tree | bio. jasmine; cf. mādhavikā | myth. np. of Mādhavī "Jasmine", daughter of King Yayāti; she lived secluded as a hermit, dressed in a deerskin; she had received the gift of always being a virgin; her father entrusted her to Gālava so that she could marry; so that the latter could pay his student debt [gurudakṣiṇā], she married the king of Ayodhyā Ha ryaśva, by whom she had a son, Vasumanā; then the king of Kāśī Divodāsa, by whom she had a son, Pratar dana; then the king of Bhojapurī Uśīnara, by whom she had a son, Sibi; she finally married Viśvāmitra, by whom she had a son, Aṣṭaka; when her father Yayāti fell from heaven, she granted him half of her merits.
Mādhavya [*madhuya] m. lit. np. of Mādhavya "Spring", jester [vidūṣaka] of the drama of Sakuntalā.
mādhu [*madhu] iic. of the bee.
mādhukara [kara₁] amnf mādhukarī relating to the bee or honey | similar to the bee — f. mādhukarī soc. ["foraging"] giving of food to renunciants or students.
mādhukośa [kośa] m. med. np. from Madhukośa, glossary of Mādhavanidāna.
mādhuparkika [*madhuparkaika] amnf mādhuparkikī soc. presented as a gift to a host with the madhuparka.
mādhurya [*madhuraya] n. sweetness; grace, charm, beauty lit. style of poetry [kāvyaguṇa] graceful, without complex compound words, and with many nasals.
mādhya [*madhya] amnf mādhyā central, median.

mādhyándina var. mādhyaṃdina [*madhyandina] amnf mādhyandinī relating to midday; southern | concerning madhyandina | ved. qualifies the second song of praise [stotra] during the jyotistoma sacrifice for the midday pressing [savana₁].
mādhyandinasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. cf. mādhyandinīyaśākhā.
mādhyandinīya [īya] amnf mādhyandinīyā soc. relating to the midday oblation | phil. relating to the madhyandina school.
mādhyandinīyaśākhā [śākhā] f. bed. review of the vājasaneyisamhitā (white Yajurveda) due to madhyandina.
mādhyama [*madhyama] amnf mādhyamā relating to the middle; middle; central.
mādhyamaka [*madhyamaaka] amnf mādhyamikā middle; central | myth. concerning the atmosphere or intermediate sky — f. mādhyamikā lit. np. of the mādhyamikā, central section of the Kāthaka.

mādhyamika [*madhyamaika] amnf mādhyamikā phil. relating to the Buddhist doctrine of the Middle Way developed by Nāgārjuna; qualifies this school of Mahāyāna — m. pl. mādhyamikās bd. followers of this doctrine.
mādhyamikavṛtti [vṛtti] f. bd. n.p. from the Mādhyamikavrtti, commentary by Candrakīrti on the doctrine of Nāgārjuna; cf. Prasannapadā.
mādhyástha [*madhyastha] amnf
mādhyasthā ["who adopts a middle position"] indifferent, neutral; impartial — n. indifference; neutrality; impartiality.
mādhyásthya [*madhyasthaya] n. in difference; neutrality; impartiality.
mādhva [*Madhva] amnf mādhvā phil. follower of the doctrine of Madhva; cf. Vyāsatīrtha.
mān [ca. man] v. [10] pr. (mānayati) to honor, respect.
māna₁ [act. man] m. opinion, conception | regard, respect, esteem, honor rendered; honor | pride, high opinion of oneself, arrogance; caprice, sulking, jealousy. mānam arhati he deserves respect.
māna₂ [act. mā₁] n. measure; dimension, size, height; extension, length | proportion; white resemblance | phil. demonstration, proof — ifc. (iic.) times.
mānatva [vat] n. arrogance, arrogance.

mānada [da] amnf mānadā that honors. mānada voc. "Your honor", respectful address. yadi tvam bhajamānām mām pratyākhyāsyasi mānada | viṣam agnim jalam rajjum āsthāsye tava kāraṇāt | [Nalopākhyāna] Your honor, if you repudiate me while I love you, because of you I will resort to poison, fire, water or rope.
mānadhmāta [dhmāta] amnf mānadhmātā full of arrogance, self-important.
mānapara [para] amnf Mānaparā puffed with gold guile — f. Mānaparā lit. [KSS.] np. of the beautiful Mānaparā, wife of Arthalobha.

Mānapāla [pāla] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Mānapāla "Guardian of pride", minister of King Vīraketu; he was escorting Princess Vāmalocanā, who had been abducted by Mat takāla, when Somadatta₂ arrived and he armed himself to free her.
mānabhanga | bhanga | m. dishonor; loss of pride.

mānasāra |sāra| mn sufficiency, arrogance — m. lit. [DKC.] np. of the king of Mālava mānasāra "Beggar Gold"; fought by his rival Rājahaṃsa, he implored Śiva who gave him a magical mace enabling him to regain the victory; he named his son Darpasāra crown prince — n. lit. np. of the mānasāra₁, treatise on architecture [vāstuśāstra] and urban planning of the 1516th century.
Mānasāraśilpaśāstra [śilpaśāstra] n. lit. np. from the Mānasārasilpasāstra, treatise on architecture, sculpture and urban planning.
mānadaṇḍa |daṇḍa| mn measuring ruler.
mānādhyakṣa [adhyakṣa] m. soc. superintendent of measurements.
māna var. āna form of the ppr. r. or ps. | form of the pfut. r. | form of the ppft. r.
mānaka [agt. mā₁] amnf mānikā that measures — n. measure.
mānana |agt. man| amnf mānanā that honors, that shows respect — act. mf mānanā marks of respect.
mānavá [*Manua] amnf mānavī human, proper to man | myth. relating to Manu — m. man, human being | pl. humanity; the whole of human races.
mānavaka [ka] m. boy, young man; schoolboy.
mānavagrhasūtra [grhasūtra] n. bed. n.p. of the Mānavagrhasūtra, ved manual. domestic rites; cf. Maitrāyaņīyagṛhasūtra.

mānavadharmaśāstra [dharmaśāstra] n. bed. n.p. from the mānavadharmaśāstra "Laws of Manu", code of traditional Brahmanical Laws, attributed to Manu; it was written between the 2nd century BC. and the 3rd century; Kullūka commented on it Manvartha muktāvalī; syn. manusmṛti.
mānavādhikāra | adhikāra | m. pl. mod. human rights.
