mānasá [*manasa] amnf mānasī men tal, spiritual | in thoughts (not. silent recitation) | present in mind; imaginable, conceivable — m. myth. spiritual son of Brahmā; syn. ma nasija — n. mind, understanding; soul, feelings | [Mānasasarovara] geo. np. of Lake Mānasa or Mānasasarovara "Lake of the Mind", at 4600 m altitude south of Mount Kailāsa, where the Sutudrī (mod. Sutlej) originates; it is there that the wild geese
vages [haṃsa] migrate to mate at the beginning of the rainy season — ifc. lit. ["Spiritual Lake of (iic.)"] name of devotional collections.

mānasaputra [putra] m. myth. one of the 6 "sons of the spirit" (of Brahmā), created to populate the World: Marīci, Atri, Angirā, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu; sometimes the ten progenitors |prajāpati| are included.
mānasapratyakṣa [pratyakṣa] n. phil. [Nyāya] mental perception.

Mānasavega [vega] amnf mānasavegā quick as thought — m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara prince Mānasavega, son of King Vegavat and Pṛthivīdevī, enemy of Naravāhanadatta; he abducted the beautiful Madanamañcukā, with whom the latter was enamored; his sister Vegavatī will help the lovers reunite. vidyādharam iva mānasavegam [K.] Like the vidyādhara Mānasavega, he was quick as thought.

Mānasollāsa₁ [ullāsa] m. lit. np. of the Mānasollāsa₁ "Entertainment of the Mind", an encyclopedic work attributed to King Cālukya Someśvara₃ (1129) it deals with the acquisition and administration of a kingdom, and the entertainments of a king, notably musical, choreographic and culinary; it comprises 5 sections [viṃśati] of 20 chapters [adhyāya] each; it is also called Abhilașitārthacintāmani; cf. Upabhoga, Krīdāviṃśati | lit. np. of the Mānasollāsa₁, an Advaita work by Suresvara.
māni iic. mānin.
mānitā [tā] f. act of believing oneself; act of honoring — ifc. imagination of (iic.).
mānitva [tva] n. pride; arrogance; the state of being honored — ifc. the state one imagines oneself to be (iic.).

mānin [agt. man] amnf māninī proud, haughty — m. man of honor — ifc. who believes himself, who takes himself for, who passes for (iic.) who believes himself to be the (iic.) of (g.) — f. māninī disdainful or sulky woman | lit. woman wounded in her pride; angry woman | myth. np. of māninī "the Proud One", daughter of Tṛṇabindu; she is the mother of Viśravā by Pulastya. panditamānī m. who takes himself for an eminent figure. śūramānī m. who believes himself to be a hero. rājamānī m. who takes himself for the king. darśanīyamānī m. who believes himself to be handsome; vain. ripumānī bhrātuḥ m. (exocentric usage) who believes himself to be the enemy of his brother.
mānīṣā [*manīṣā] f. thought; conception, idea | reflection, consideration; wisdom, intelligence; prayer, request; desire, wish. paro mānīṣayā beyond all conception.
mānīṣin |in| amnf mānīṣiṇī thoughtful, wise.
mānuṣa [*manusa] amnf mānuṣī human, proper to man — m. man — n. human nature; humanity — f. mānuṣī woman. ātmānam mānuṣam manye [Rām.] (Rāma) I consider myself a human being.
mānuṣatā [tā] f. human nature; human condition; humanity | virility.
mānusatva |tva| n. id.
mānuṣya [*manuṣaya] n. beauty, grace, elegance | goodness, generosity | phil. aesthetics.
māntrika [*mantraika] m. spellcaster; magician; sorcerer.
māndāra [*mandāra] m. bio. flower of the coral tree.
māndāraka [*mandāraka] amnf māndārikā bio. concerning the coral tree.
māndya [*mandaya] n. slowness; indolence; laziness | weakness; slowness of mind; indisposition; illness. māndyam kṛ to make oneself ill.
māndyavyāja [vyāja] m. illness simulation.

māndhātṛ [*mandhātṛ] m. myth. np. of King Māndhātā "son of the pious (king)", born from the womb of his father Yuvanāśva as a result of a ritual error; on the advice of his ministers the king abandoned him in the woods, but the gods rescued him; Indra named him Māṃdhātā ( māṃ dhātr ), meaning that he would be his own nurse, and made him suckle his big toe; he grew tall and strong, and ascended the throne upon the death of his father; he conquered kingdoms and terrorized the barbarians [dasyu]; he married the chaste Bindumatī, by whom he had two sons, Purukutsa and Mu cukunda; he reigned wisely and the country prospered; It happened that it did not rain for three consecutive years, and the king consulted the hermits; they explained that a śūdra was doing penance, a prerogative of the brahmins in this krtayuga, and that the rain would return if he were put to death; the king did not want to kill an innocent ascetic, and asked for a palliative; he was instructed to fast for the eleventh days of each fortnight | ekādaśī|; the king and his subjects complied, and the rain and prosperity returned; Māndhātā, who had learned the rājadharma from Uta thya, is the model of the pious and just monarch; [Rām.] he is also said to be the father of Susandhi | geo. np. of the eponymous village in Madhya Pradesh, south of the Narmadā, beginning of the pilgrimage | parikrama | of the island of Omkāreśvara; myth. it is said that King Māndhātā prayed to Shiva there and made it his capital.
mānya |pfp. |1| man| amnf mānyā res pectable, honorable, venerable. mānye adr. Madam.

mānyakheṭa [kheṭa] m. geo. n.p. from the town of Mānyakheta (mod. Malkhed north of Karņāṭaka, 40 km east of Gulbarga); it became the capital of the Rāṣṭrakūṭa empire under Amoghavarṣa₁ (9th century), then of the kingdom of the Western Cālukyās.
mānyatva |tva| n. respectability; the state of being ho noré (by (g.)).
māp |ca. mā₁| v. |10| pr. (māpayati) pfp. (māpya) to measure; to erect.
māpaka [agt. ca. mā₁] amnf māpikā which serves to measure (g.) — m. measuring instrument — f. māpikā balance.
māpana |act. ca. mā₁| m. balance — n. act of measuring or shaping — f. māpanā measure, placement (not. of the sacrificial area).
māpya [pfp. [1] ca. mā₁] amnf māpyā measurable.
mām |acc. aham| ind. me.
māmaka |*mamaka| amnf māmikā f. māmakī véd. my, mine.
māmakīna [īna] amnf māmakīnā my, mine.
Māmateya [*mamatāīya] m. myth. n.p. of Māmateya, matr. from Dīrghatāmā “son of mamatā”.
māya [agt. mā₁] amnf māyī ifc. who measures (iic.) | who creates Illusion, deceiver; said of Viṣṇu — m. mime, juggler, magician — f. cf. māyā. dhānyamāya mf dhānyamāyī who weighs the grain.

māyā [f. māya] f. Illusion, apparition; magic, sorcery; deception | phil. [Vedānta] the world of appearances; the Divine Illusion, created by Vișnu myth. np. of māyā, the Divine Illusion personified; it emanates from Vișnu; cf. Mahāmāyā, Yogamāyā phil. Tantra epith. of the Goddess under her power of illusion | phil. [siddhānta] prime matter of the worlds to which the consciousness of Shiva gives form | hist. np. of Queen Māyā₁, mother of the Buddha. māyedam sarvam [Vedānta] All here below is but illusion.
māyākāya [kāya] m. bd. [ṣaḍdharma] yoga of the illusory nature of the phenomenal world.
māyākāra [kāra] m. magician, illusionist.
māyākrt [krt₂] m. magician, illusionist.
māyādevī [devī] f. hist. np. of Queen Māyā₁, mother of the Buddha.
Māyāpura [pura] n. geo. np. of the village of Māyāpura near Navadvīpa on the Ganges in North Bengal; it is the birthplace of Caitanya (1486).
māyābīja | bīja | n. soc. [Tantra] bījamantra 'hrīm', evocation of Durgā.
Māyāmaya [Maya] m. lit. [Rām.] np. from the rākṣasa Māyāmaya "deed of illusion", emissary of Rāvaņa.
māyāmrga [mrga] m. myth. [Rām.] "deer of illusion", golden deer in which mārīca disguised herself to deceive Rāma; syn. hemamṛga.
māyāyoga [yoga] m. practice of magic or illusion.
māyāyogin [yogin] m. magician — f. Māyāyoginī myth. n.p. from Māyāyoginī, personifying Māyā₁.
māyāyoginīgranthi | granthi | m. med. pituitary gland.

māyāvat [vat] amnf Māyāvatī who causes illusion, who has magical powers; deceiver — f. Māyāvatī myth. np. of Māyāvatī "Magician", wife of Sambara₁; she took in Pradyumna as a child, fell in love with him and later married him; their son is Aniruddha; she is an incarnation of Rati.
māyāvāda [vāda] m. phil. doctrine affirming that the world is an illusion; applies to Vedānta and Buddhism | (pej.) false doctrine (from the point of view not. of Madhva).
māyāvādin |in| m. soc. follower of Vedānta or Buddhism; he shaves his head completely.
māyāvin [vin] amnf māyāvinī who possesses magical powers; who creates illusion; who deceives — m. magician | myth. [Rām.] np. of the asura Māyāvī "magician", eldest son of Maya and Hemā.
māyīya [īya] amnf māyīyā phil. coming from the divine illusion Māyā₁.
māyika [Māyā₁ika] amnf māyikā illu evening, deceptive.
māyín [māyain] amnf māyinī that creates illusion, that deceives — m. magician, illusionist; cheat | myth. epith. of Shiva — n. magic, illusion.
māyu₁ [*mā₁u] m. sorcery. Māyurāja m. hist. np. of Māyurāja, prince Kala curi, identified with the poet Mātrarāja | myth. son of KuberaMayurāja.
māyu₁ [*mā₄u] m. bellowing; bleating.
māyu₁ [*miu] mn bile.
māyūra [*mayūra] amnf māyūrī relating to the peacock.
mār [ca. mr] v. [10] pr. (mārayati) to kill, to put to death. paśumāramamārayat he killed him as one kills an animal.

māra | act. mṛ | m. Death, destruction | obstacle | passionate love | myth. epith. of Kāma (obstacle to liberation) | bd. np. of māra, Death; he is the spirit of evil, and the tempter of the Buddha | fr. Death.
mārajit | jit | m. bd. epith. of Buddha "who conquers māra".
māraripu [ripu] m. myth. epith. of Śiva “enemy of Kāma”.
māravijaya | vijaya | amnf māravijayā bd. refers to the posture of the meditating Buddha, overcoming the temptation of māra, and taking the Earth as a witness to his merits; cf. bhūmisparśamudrā.
mārāri [ari] m. myth. epith. of Shiva "enemy of Kāma".
māraka |agt. mṛ| amnf mārikā murderer — m. deadly disease; plague | falcon — f. mārikā plague.
māraṇa |act. mṛ| n. murder, killing, execution.
mārava [*marua] amnf māravī desert || hi. Mārvār .

māriṣa m. good man; patron | role of troupe director in the theatre — f. māriṣā myth. [Harivamśa] np. of the apsaras māriṣā₁, mother of Dakṣa by the Pracetās | myth. [Mah.] np. of the queen māriṣā₂, wife of Sūra.

mārīca [*marīcia] m. myth. np. of mārīca, patr. of Kaśyapa, son of marīci | myth. [Rām.] np. of mārīca "Master of the mirage", yakṣa magician son of Sunda₁ and Tāṭakā; he became rākṣasa as did his mother by the curse of Agastya; he was an advisor at the court of Rāvaṇa; he transformed himself into a golden deer [hemamṛga] to separate Rāma from Sītā with whom he was in the forest so that Rāvaņa could approach and abduct her | var. mārīci patr. from Marīci — f. Mārīcī bd. np. of the goddess Mārīcī.
māruta [*maruta] amnf mārutī rela tif aux marutas, relating to the Wind; stormy | aerial, celestial; divine — m. breath; respiration | myth. np. of māruta, epith. of Vāyu "Master of the Winds".
Māruti [*marut] m. myth. np. of Māruti, patr. of Hanumān "son of the Wind"; cf. Marutputra.

mārkaņdeya [*mṛkaṇḍaīya] m. myth. Patr. of the sage [ṛṣi] Mārkaṇḍeya; his father Mṛkaṇḍu having long prayed for a son, he was given the choice between many stupid sons or one very intelligent one, but with a life limited to 16 years; having made the latter choice, his wife Ma nasvinī gave birth to mārkandeya, who grew in wisdom until his 16th year; on his 16th birthday, he was worshipping the linga in a shrine of Shiva when Yama came to get him; Shiva, angry, sprang from the linga, struck Yama on the chest, and promised Mārkaṇḍeya that he would remain eternally young; immortal [ciramjīvin], he travels in the body of Nārāyaṇa asleep on the primordial waters, and Vișnu reveals to him the secrets of his māyā; [Mah.] when Yudhisthira in exile complains about his fate, Mārkaņdeya tells him the Rāmopākhyāna; cf. Dīrghāyu, Suratamanjarī₁.

mārkandeyapurāna | purāna | n. lit. np. of the Mārkandeyapurāna, which describes the glorious acts of the Goddess; Jaimini is said to have received the teaching from Mārkaņdeya transmitted by 4 birds; its composition is prior to the 6th century; the part called Candī₁, which is highly revered, is recited during the Durgā pūjā.

√ mārg [related to mrg] v. [1] pr. (mārgati) pr. r. (mārgate) pp. (mārgita) pf. (pari) to seek, to go in search of; to pursue, to chase | to strive to, to try to attain; to ask, to solicit something (acc.) from someone (abl.) — ca. (mārgayati) id.

mārga [*mṛga] amnf mārgā relating to the antelope | gram. conforming to the Sanskrit norm; opp. deśī — m. ["antelope track"] way, path, street, road | lit. mode of expression | bd. stage on the path of knowledge | pali magga. mārgāya in view of (2nd century). mārgeṇa by, through, by way of (2nd century). mārgais across (2nd century). mārgam dā give free rein to. mārgam yam id. mārgeņa yā suffer the same fate as.

mārgadarśaka [darśaka] amnf mārgadarśikā ["who shows the way"] pioneer — m. guide. mārgašīrsa [śīrṣa] amnf mārgašīrsī born under the constellation Mṛgaśiras (Orion) — m. astr. month of the antelope (November-December), when the moon is full in Orion; it is sacred to Viṣṇu; cf. Āgrahāyaṇī — f. mārgaśīrṣī day of his full moon. māsānām mārgaśīrṣo'ham [BhG.] (Kṛṣṇa dixit) Among the months I am Mārgaśīrṣa.
mārgaṇa [agt. mārg] amnf mārgaṇā ifc. who desires, who inquires about, who seeks — m.
beggar | arrow | math. symb. the number 5 (for the 5 arrows of Kāma) — act. n. investigation, research, inquiry | solicitation, request; begging.
mārgaṇatā [tā] f. quality of arrow; possession of arrow. upakṣīṇamārgaṇatā the state of having exhausted one's arrows.
mārgika [*mṛgaika] m. hunter.
mārgita [pp. mārg] amnf mārgitā re sought; solicited.
mārgitavya [pfp. [3] mārg] amnf mārgittavyā that one should seek or desire.
mārgin [agt. mārg] amnf mārgiņī who opens the way; guide — ifc. who follows the way of (iic.).
mārj [ca. mṛj] v. [10] pr. (mārjayati) to rub, polish; to clean, purify; to adorn.
mārja [agt. mṛj] amnf mārjā that cleans — m. cleaner | cleaning; purification.
mārjaka [agt. mṛj] amnf mārjikā that cleans.
mārjana [agt. mṛj] amnf mārjanā ifc. that which erases, that which cleans, that which purifies — m. broom; brush — f. mārjanī washerwoman — act. nf mārjanā wiping, cleaning; purification.
mārjāra [mārjara] m. cat ["who cleans himself"]; wild cat — f. mārjārī female cat.
mārjāraka [ka] m. cat; peacock — f. mārjārikā ci vette.
mārjārakiśora [kiśora] m. kitten [mārjārakiśoranyāya] phil. Southern bhakti doctrine, where the believer surrenders to God like a kitten carried in its mother's mouth; opp. markatakiśora.
mārjāramūṣaka [mūṣaka] n. sg. (collective) the pair of sworn enemies of the cat and mouse.
mārjāla [mārjāra] mf mārjālī cat.
Mārtaṇḍa [contr. mārtāṇḍa] m. Sun |myth. np. of Mārtaṇḍa Bhairava; cf. Khaṇḍobā | hist. np. of King Mārtaṇḍa₁ Varmā (Kerala, 18th century) — ifc. lit. light on (iic.) (title of works).

mārtāṇḍa [*mṛtāṇḍa] m. [“born from an (apparent) dead egg”] bird | Sun (later written mārtanda) | geo. np. of the temple to the Sun Mārtānda, built by Emperor Lalitāditya Muktāpīda in a splendid site in Kaśmīra in the 8th century; it was destroyed by Sultan Sikander in the 15th century; its ruins are located near the village of Mattan.
Mārttikāvata [*mṛttikāvatīa] m. geo. n.p. from the yadu kingdom of Mārttikāvata; cf. Citraratha₁ — f. mārttikāvatī myth. capital of king Śālva in Saubha country.
mārdangika [*mṛdangaika] amnf mārdangikā drummer [mṛdanga].
mārdangikapāṇavika [pāṇavika] n. group of players of mṛdaṅga and paṇava .
mārdava [*mṛdua] n. gentleness, kindness, tenderness; goodness, amiability | (coating) plasticity.
mārmika [*marmanika] amnf mārmikā specialist of, versed in (loc. iic.).
māla m. geo. territory west of Bengal | pl. barbarian people; untouchables — n. field.
mālaka [ka] nf mālakā f. mālakī garland — f. cf. mālikā.

mālatī f. bio. bot. Jasminum grandiflorum; its sweet-smelling white flowers open in the evening; syn. cetakī | virgin girl | moonlight; night lit. np. of Mālātī, heroine of the Mālatīmādhava; she is abducted there by the kāpālika Aghoraghaṇṭa, then by his student Kapālakundala.

Mālatīmādhava [mādhava] n. lit. np. from Mālatīmādhava, a play in the style of comedy | prakaraṇa | in 10 acts by Bhavabhūti; it tells of the love affair of the student mādhava₃ with Mālātī, daughter of a minister.
mālaya [*malaya] amnf mālayā relating to Malabar; derived from Malabar — m. sandalwood — n. sandalwood ointment.

mālava m. geo. np. of the mālava, country of central India, west of the Deccan, north of the Nar madā (mod. Mālva); its capital was Ujjayinī Avanti; cf. Yaśodharmā, Paramāra | prince of the mālava | pl. mālavās its inhabitants — amnf mālavī relating to the mālava.
mālavaka |ka| mr. malava country | soc. bastard śūdra — f. cf. Mālavikā.
mālavīya [īya] amnf mālavīyā from mālava, native of mālava.
mālavya [ya] amnf mālavyā relating to mālava — m. type of man; cf. pañcamanusyavibhāga.
Mālavikā [f. mālavaka] f. bed. n.p. of Mālavikā, heroine of Mālavikāgnimitra.

Mālavikāgnimitra [agnimitra] n. lit. np. of the Mālavikāgnimitra "agnimitra and Mālavikā", Kālidāsa drama (King Agnimitra, in love with the servant Mālavikā, provokes the anger of his wives Irāvatī₁ and Dhāriṇī, but Mālavikā, who turns out to be a princess in exile, is finally accepted as a co-wife, and all's well that ends well).
mālā f. garland, crown | necklace, cape let — v. [11] pr. (mālayati) to crown; to adorn with a garland.
mālākāra | kāra | mr. florist.
mālāphala [phala] n. seed of the Elæocarpus gani trus (from which rosaries are made); syn. rudrākṣa.
mālāyamaka [yamaka] n. lit. [alaṃkāra] repetition of consonants; syn. anuprāsa.
mālopamā [upamā₁] f. bed. (style) litany of comparisons.
mālikā [f. mālaka] f. garland | necklace; sequence, row, alignment.
mālin [mālāin] amnf Mālinī who wears a garland, crowned; girded with (i. iic.) — m. gardener; florist — f. cf. Mālinī.

Mālinī [f. mālin] f. myth. np. of the river Mālinī, on the banks of which lived the sage [ṛṣi] Kaṇva | myth. [Mah.] np. of Mālinī₁ "In garland", false identity of Draupadī concealed as sairandhrī at the court of King Virāṭa | florist; wife of gardener/florist | lit. poetic meter "in garland" | phil. [Trika] np. of the goddess Mālinī₂, personifying the garland of the letters of the alphabet in the order nādiphāntakrama.
mālinīvijaya [vijaya] n. lit. [kaula] np. of the mālinīvijaya tantra, also called Pūrvaśāstra or mālinīvijayottara.
mālinīvijayavārttika [vārttika] n. bed. n.p. mālinīvijayavārttika, commentary on the mālinīvijayottara due to Abhinavagupta.
mālinīvijayottara [uttara₁] n. [mālinīvijayottaratantra] lit. from np. mālinīvijayottara tantra, epith. of mālinīvijaya; he influenced the Tantrāloka.
mālya [mālāya] n. garland, wreath; collar. mālyaguņa [guṇa] m. thread of a necklace, garland, or wreath — v. [11] pr. r. (mālyagunāyate) to be like the thread of a garland
moor | become | appear as.
mālyagrathana | grathana | n. tying a heath garland.
mālyagrathanavikalpa [vikalpa] m. the art of making garlands, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.

mālyavat [vat] amnf mālyavatī crowned with garlands; who wears a garland — m. myth. |Rām.| np. of the rākṣasa Mālyavān, minister of Rāvaṇa | myth. np. of the Mālyavān₁ Mountains, east of Mount Meru; [Rām.] Rāma and Lakshmana spent the monsoon season there after the abduction of Sītā, while waiting for Sugrīva | lit. [KSS.] np. of the gana Mālyavān₂, friend of Puṣpadanta, banished for having forbidden him to become human as Guṇāḍhya; He must hear the story of the magicians of the piśāca Kāṇabhūti in order to free him, and will be freed himself by transmitting the story, which he wrote in the language of the spirits [paiśācī], the mythical Bṛhatkathā — f. mālyavatī myth. [Rām.] np. of the river mālyavatī.

māṣa mn bio. bot. Phaseolus radiatus, bean | gold weight measure, worth 5 kṛṣṇala (about 2 g) | value of this gold weight | [Mayamata] area measure, lot of 4 pieces [kākanī]; (about 10 ares); there are 4 in a vartanaka .
māṣaka |ka| m. bean, bean — n. measure of gold weight, worth 8 guñjā seeds; syn. hema.
māṣavāpana [vāpana₂] n. sowing of beans. māṣavāpin | vāpin | amnf māṣavāpinī who sows beans.
māṣoṇa |ūna| amnf māṣoṇā lesser of a māşa.
māṣona |ūna| amnf māṣonā cf. māṣoṇa. - name. mās moon; month || lat. mensis; eng. month; month; fr. month.
māsa [māsa] mn month; we distinguish between solar [saura], natural [sāvana], stel months

lary [nakṣatra] and lunar [cāndra] | astr. lunar month, divided into 30 lunar days [tithi]; there are twelve of them, each associated with the constellation [nakṣatra] in which the full moon takes place: caitra (March-April), month of Citrā; vaiśākha (April-May), month of Viśākhe; jyaiṣṭha (May-June), month of Jyeșthā; āṣāḍha (June-July), month of the Aṣādhās; śrāvaṇa₂ (July-August), month of Śravaṇā; bhādrapada (August-September), month of the Bhādrapadās; āśvina (September-October), month of Aśvinī; kārttika (October-November), month of the Kṛttikās; mārgaśīrṣa (November-December), month of Mṛgaśiras, also called agrahāyaṇa; paușa (December-January), month of Pusya; māgha (January-February), month of the Maghās; phālguna (February-March), month of Phalgunī; depending on the region of India, the months begin at the full or new moon | Vedic: the twelve Vedic months: madhu, mādhava, śukra, śuci, nabhas, nabhasya, iṣa, ūrja, sahas, sahasya, tapas and tapasya | Math. symb. the number 12. māsena during 1 month. māse after one month. māsam ekam for 1 month.
māsamātra [mātra] m. duration of a month. māsamātre adv. within the space of a month. māsamātram adv. for a whole month; for a length of months.
māsika [ika] amnf māsikī monthly; payable monthly; committed monthly — n. soc. service to the spirits [śrāddha] celebrated at each new moon (money) due at the end of the month.

māhātmya [*mahātmya] n. greatness of soul, magnanimity; majesty, panegyric dignity — ifc. lit. glorification of (iic.) (generic title of works glorifying a divinity, a river or a holy place); section of praises of a work.

māhārāṣṭra [*mahārāṣṭra] amnf māhārāṣṭrī geo. concerning the people and country of the Marāṭhās — f. māhārāṣṭrī their language, Marāṭhī, "best prākṛtī" according to Daṇḍī₁; it replaced śaurasenī in lyric poetry.
Māhiṣmatī [*mahiṣmat] f. geo. np. of the city of Māhiṣmatī; it was the capital of the Ka lacuri kings, not. Kṛṣṇarāja; cf. Mahiṣmatī.
māhisya [*mahisaya] m. soc. member of a mixed caste (son of a kṣatriya and a vaiśyā assigned to the care of livestock).
māheśvara [*Maheśvara] amnf Māheśvarī myth. which concerns Maheśvara; who honors Śiva — m. soc. devotee of Śiva — f. Māheśvarī myth. n.p. of Māheśvarī, śakti of Maheśvara, a saptamātrkā.

√ mi [related to mā₁] v. [5] pr. (minóti) pr. r. (mi nute) pft. (mimāya) pp. (mitá₂) to attach; to establish | to measure, to delimit | to judge, to perceive, to know — ps. (mīyate) to be attached; to be measured; to be known.
mita₁ [pp. mā₁] amnf mitā measured, limited; moderate, modest; short, small.

Mitākṣarā₁ [akṣara] f. lit. np. of the Mitākṣarā₁, commentary on the Aṣṭādhyāyī due to Annambhaṭṭa lit. np. of the Mitākṣarā₁, commentary on the dharmaśāstra of Yājñavalkya due to Vijñāneśvara (12th century).
mitá₂ [pp. mi] amnf mitā attached, established.
mitam [acc. mita₁] iic.
mitampaca | paca | amnf mitampacā | "who cooks lean" stingy.
miti [act. mā₁] f. measure; weight [phil. justification, proof | phil. [Tantra] phoneme 'm', evoking dissolution in the pranava om.

mitrá [instr. mid] n. friendship — m. Friend; ally | myth. ved. np. of the radiant |āditya| mitra “the Friend”; he represents the light side of the divine associated with the Sun, opposed to its dark side, personified by Varuna associated with the Subterranean Waters; he symbolizes the social contract and is the god of Alliances; phil. [Sāṃkhya] he is regent [niyantr] of the faculty of evacuation |pāyu|; astr. he presides over the nakṣatra Anurādhās (delta of Scorpio) | du. mitrā myth. ellipsis for the pair mitrāvaruṇau | hist. np. of the paṇḍita mitra₁ Miśra (17th century), author of the Vīramitrodaya — f. mitrā myth. [Mah.] np. of mitrā, one of the 7 "(dangerous) mothers to children" [śiśumātaras] associated with Skanda — v. [11] pr. (mitrīyati) dear dear to make a Friend; to treat as a Friend; to be friendly Avestan Mithra. mitrīkṛ to make a Friend. mitrīkṛta amn whose friend one has made. mitrībhū to become a Friend (with (i.)).

Mitragupta | gupta | m. lit. | DKC. | np. of the young Mitragupta, son of the minister Sumitra₁, one of the heroes of the Daśakumāracarita; he arrived in Dāmalipta at the time of the kandukotsava, where he met tra Kośadāsa; he fell in love with Princess Kandukavatī upon seeing her dance, and she fell in love with him too; Prince Bhīmadhanvā, her brother, had him thrown into the sea; he was rescued by a foreign ship, which was attacked by a galley of Bhīmadhanvā; he was shipwrecked on an island where a demon posed four riddles to him; finally a rākṣasa flying in the air with an abducted woman was attacked by the demon, and the woman fell into his arms, only to turn out to be Kandukavatī whom he was able to marry; Bhīmadhanvā had to let Kośadāsa marry Candrasenā, and became his vassal, in accordance with the predictions of Vind hyavāsinī.
mitradrúh | druh₂ | amnf | sg. nom. mitradhruk | one who betrays his Friend; hostile towards his Friend — m. traitor; false Friend.
mitrádroha | droha | m. treachery.
mitrádrohin | drohin | amnf mitradrohin cf. mitradruh.
mitraprāpti [prāpti] f. lit. "Acquisition of friends", title of the 2nd book of the Pañcatantra, which shows the benefit of helping one another.
mitrabheda [bheda] m. lit. "Disunion of friends", title of the 1st book of the Pañcatantra, which shows the danger of listening to slander.
mitrámukha | mukha | amnf mitramukhī | "who makes a friendly mouth" | hypocrite.
mitravat [vat] amnf mitravatī who has friends — adv. like a Friend.

mitravarman [varman] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Mi travarmā, king of Māhiṣmatī, half-brother of Anan tavarmā₁; after the defeat of the latter, he took in Vasumdharā and his children; he coveted Vasumdharā, and on his refusal wanted to kill his son Bhāskaravarmā, whom he entrusted to the faithful Nālījaṅgha; Viśruta took him under his protection, and arranged for Vasumdharā to poison Mitravarmā.
Mitravinda [vinda] amnf Mitravindā who possesses a Friend — f. Mitravindā myth. [Mah.] np. of Mitravindā, wife of Kṛṣṇa, mother of Vard hana.

Mitrasaha |saha₁| m. myth. np. of Mitrasaha, epithet of King Kalmāṣapāda "indulgent towards his friends". mitrāvaruņa [varuņa] m. du. mitrāvaruņau myth. [RV.] np. of mitrāvaruņau "mitra and Varuņa together"; first of the radiant [ādityās], they are the titans who became gods |devāvasurau|; they are sovereign [samrāj] over Earth and Heaven, and govern justice, truth, and light; [SB.] mitra is sacred power, Varuna civil power; the effectiveness of the latter depends on the former, as the Brahmin purohita walks before the king; [MP.] One day, when the nymph Urvaśī visited their hermitage, they lost their seed before her beauty; she collected it in a pot, and thus begot Agasti and Vasistha; the former went to spread Brahmanism in South India to become its patron saint, the latter remaining in the North as chape lain [purohita] of the lineage of King Ikṣvāku. kratūdakṣau ha vā asya mitrāvaruṇau véd. [SB.] Mitra and Varuna truly are intelligent intention and effective execution, relative to the Self.
mitrodaya [udaya] m. sunrise.
mitríya [mitraiya] amnf mitriyā friendly var. mitrya f. mitryā id.
√ mith v. [1] pr. (methati) abs. (mithitvā) ren to counter; to pair up; to mate | to confront; to face, to engage in an altercation.
mithas [abstr. mith] adv. in the company of (i.); each other, reciprocally | privately, secretly.
Mithi [related to mathana] m. myth. np. of King Mithi (or Mithila), "Churned" from the thigh of Nimi, founder of Mithilā, ancestor of the Janaka lineage; Udāvasu is his son.

Mithila [Mithila] m. myth. np. of King Mi thila; cf. Mithi | pl. mithilās inhabitants of Mithilā — f. Mithilā geo. np. of Mithilā, capital of Vi deha (45 km northeast of mod. Darbhanga, north of present-day Bihār); its kings were said to be of the ashes of Nimi by Mithi, ancestor of the Ja naka lineage; |Rām.| the young Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, with their master Viśvāmitra, visited King Janakarāja there. mithilāyām pradīptāyām na me dahyati kiṃcana [Mah.] Even if Mithilā was in flames I would not be tormented in the least (Janakarāja showing his detachment from the world).
míthu [mithu] adv. alternatively, contrary dictorily; falsely.

mithuná [mithuna] amnf mithunā for mant couple — n. couple, pair | union, coupling | arch. iconographic theme of the loving couple | astr. np. of Mithuna, zodiac sign [rāśi] of Gemini | gram. combination of a preverb and a root. mithunyas to pair up; to cohabit sexually. mithunīkṛ to pair up; to mate. mithunībhū to be paired. mithunībhāvaḥ m. copulation. mithunīcārin amn that mates.

mithunasamkrānti [mithunasamkrānti] f. astr. passage into the zodiac sign of Mithuna [Gemini], in mid-June; it marks the beginning of the monsoon in Orissa, where the menstruation of the Earth [Rajā] is celebrated, seen as its regeneration.
mithuyā [mithuyā] adv. ved. conversely, contrary; falsely, incorrectly. mithuyākr undo.

Mithyā [contr. mithuyā] adv. backwards, crookedly; wrongly, falsely, badly | apparently, illusorily | in vain, uselessly, sterilely — iic. false; falsely — f. myth. np. of Mithyā "falsehood", his personification, wife of Adharma. mithyākṛ to deny | to break one's word. na mithyākṛ to keep one's word. mithyākār to pronounce badly. Mithyā pracar to act wrongly. Mithyā pravṛt to behave badly. mithyābhū to prove false. Mithyā brū to lie. Mithyā vac to lie (opp. satyam vad). mithyāmaunam false vow of silence. brahma satyam jaganmithyā [Sankara₁] Brahman is the truth, the world is but illusion. sarvam Mithyā bravīmi [Bhartṛhari] everything I say is false (liar paradox). sarvam jñānam Mithyā [Vedānta] All knowledge is false.
mithyākarman | karman | n. error, mistake; slip of the tongue, failure.
mithyākṛta [kṛta] amnf mithyākṛtā is wrongly done.
mithyākopa [kopa] m. feigned anger.
mithyācāra [cāra] m. bad conduct; bad treatment (med.) — amnf mithyācārā who behaves badly; hypocrite.
mithyājalpita | jalpita | n. false news, rumor.

mithyājñāna [jñāna] n. false knowledge, misconception; error, mistake. mithyājñānam adv. by mistake. mithyājñānam viparyayaḥ | yathā śuktau rajatam iti | [TkS.] Mistake is a mistaken knowledge; for example, in the presence of mother-of-pearl, thinking "it is silver".
mithyātva [tva] n. illusion; falsehood | jn. perversion, one of the 18 faults | jn. illusion, state of ignorance of the brute, initial stage of spiritual development | guṇasthāna|.
mithyāpratijña [pratijñā₂] amnf mi thyāpratijñā who does not keep his word, perjurer.
√ mid var. mind v. [1] pr. r. (medate) v. [10] pr. (mindayati) pp. (minna) to be fat — v. [4] pr. (medyati) to fatten, to grow fat — ca. (medáyati) pp. (medita) to make fat.
min cf. in.
minna [pp. mid] amnf minnā became fat, obese.
mim cf. mā₃.

√ mil v. [6] pr. (milati) fut. (milisyati) pp. (mi lita) to meet someone. (i.saha₂ g. loc.) — ca. (me layati) ca. (melāpayati) to make someone meet with someone else (g.). kutra milāmaḥ where do we meet? punah milāmah see you soon, goodbye. sarve militvā sapta vayam there are 7 of us in all.
milana [act. mil] n. meeting; contact.

Milarepa m. hist. np. of the Tibetan mystic Mila Raspa or Milarepa (1040–1123), born in the province of Goungthang to a landowner who died when he was 7 years old; he lived with his mother as a servant of his uncle who confiscated his property; to take revenge, he studied black magic and became a renowned magician, who could conjure hail; he took Marpa as his master, who made him do countless trials; he is an accomplished saint [mahāsiddha] and a poet; he withdrew to a cave near the Lapchi glacier in western Tibet near Everest, it is said that he became green from eating nettles; before his death he dictated his biography to his disciple Retchungpa.
militā [pp. mil] amnf militā met; gathered; accomplished.
Milinda m. bio. bee |hist. np. of the Indo-Greek king Milinda (Menander), originally from Bactria; he reigned in Sākala (Pañjāb) in the 2nd century BC.

milindapraśna [praśna] m. lit. np. from the Milinda prasna "Questions of Menander", a bd. work in pāli on the dialogue between King Milinda and the monk Nāgasena about nirvāņa; this bd. breviary of the Gandhāra culture is probably earlier than the 2nd century || pali Milindapañha.

miśrá amnf miśrā mixed, mingled; varied, mingled; multiple | accompanied by, furnished with (i.samam g. iic.) — iic. adr. (honorific) Honorable (np.) — ifc. pl. id. — m. np. of Miśra, eminent title of Brahmin notably in Orissa — v. [11] pr. (miśrayati) pp. (miśrita) to mix; to combine (with (i.)) | lat. miscere; ang. mix; fr. miscible. miśrībhū to mingle (with (i.)); to couple. āryamiśrāḥ honorable persons; your honor. āryamiśrāh pramāṇam your honor is authoritative.
miśraka [ka] amnf miśrikā mixed; impure not just (song).
miśrana |na| n. mixture.
miśramata [mata] n. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] school of Murāri₂ Miśra.
miśramudrā [mudrā] f. mixed gesture with two hands, where each hand shows a different basic gesture.
miśrita [pp. Miśra] amnf miśritā mixed.

√ miṣ v. [6] pr. (miṣati) pp. (miṣita) ppr. (misat) pf. (ut, ni) to open one's eyes, to blink (used in the simple sense only in the ppr. g. ab solu) | to rival, to emulate. misatas adv. under the eyes of, in the presence of, in spite of (the gaze) of g. . misato bandhuvargasya under the very eyes of the whole group of friends. ਸਿਣ miṣṭa [mṛṣṭá₁] amnf miṣṭā sweet, delicate, pleasant; sugary — n. confection.
mistānna [anna] n. tasty food; sweet dish; confectionery. kim miṣṭamannam kharasūkarāṇām What good is giving jam to pigs?
miṣṭānnapāna |pāna| n. du. miṣṭānnapāne sweet dishes and drinks.
√ mih v. [1] pr. (mehati) pp. (mīḍha) pf. (ava) to urinate, to water; to rain | lat. mingere; fr. miction. mehati it rains.
Mihira M. The Sun.

Mihirakula [kula] m. hist. np. of the hūṇa tyrant Mihi rakula "of the Solar House", son of King Toramāṇa; he conquered an empire in North India at the beginning of the 6th century; he was driven out by King Yaśodharmā of Mālava in 528, and took refuge in Sākala in Kaśmīra, where he died in 533; he was a śaiva , and persecuted Buddhists.
mihirapura | pura | n. geo. np. of the city of Mihi rapura, founded by Mihirakula.
mihirabhoja [bhoja] m. hist. n.p. of king mihirabhoja₁ of the Pratīhārās (836–885).
mihireśvara [īśvara] m. geo. n.p. of the Shivaite Mihireśvara temple, founded by King Mihirakula.
√ mī v. [9] pr. (mnati) v. [5] pr. (minoti) v. [4] pr. r. (mīyate) pp. (mīta) pf. (pra) overthrow, destroy — ca. (māpayati) cause to be destroyed — dés. (mitsati) dés. (mitsate) want to destroy.
mīḍhá [pp. mih] amnf mīḍhā urinated — m. ram — n. competition; prize, reward.
mina m. Fish | astr. zodiac sign [rāśi] of Pisces.
mīnakāra | kāra | mr. fishmonger.
mīnayugala [yugala] n. jn. pair of fish, sym bole of good omen; cf. astamangala.
Mīnarāja [rāja] m. hist. np. of Mīnarāja, astro nome of western India of the 4th century; we owe him the Vrddhayavanajātaka.
Mīnarājajātaka [jātaka] n. astr. n.p. of Mīnarājajātaka; cf. Vṛddhayavanajātaka.

Mīnākṣī [akṣa] f. myth. np. of Mīnākṣī “(the Goddess) with fish-like eyes”, daughter of Kubera, one of the forms of Pārvatī, wife of Śiva, deification of a Pāṇḍya princess venerated in the great temple of MīnāksīSundareśvara in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. 7()
Mīnendra | Indra | m. astr. np. of Mīnendra "King of the fish", epith. of the rāśi makara (Capricorn).
mīmāṃs [des. mān] v. pr. r. (mīmāṃsate) pp. (mīmāṃsita) pfp. (mīmāṃsya) to reflect; to want to understand; to study.
mīmāṃsaka [agt. mīmāṃs] f. mīmāṃsikā examiner, investigator; exegete | phil. follower or doctrinaire of the pūrvamīmāṃsā doctrine — f. mīmāmsikā phil. syn. Mīmāmsā.
mīmāṃsā [act. des. man] f. desire for knowledge; investigation, examination | interpretation, exegesis; casuistry | phil. np. of the philosophical doctrine Mīmāmsā; cf. pūrvamīmāmsā, utta ramīmāmsā.
mīmāmsākaustubha [kaustubha] n. bed. n.p. mīmāmsākaustubha, commentary on the Pūrvamīmāmsāsūtra due to Khaṇḍadeva.
mīmāṃsānukramaṇī [anukramaṇī] f. bed. n.p. from the Mīmāmsānukramanī, work of Mandana Miśra.
mīmāṃsānyāya [nyāya] iic. phil. dialectic of the exegesis of the Vedic ritual.
mīmāṃsānyāyaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. np. of the Vedic exegesis Mīmāmsānyāyaprakāśa of Apadeva; it is also called the Apadevī.
mīmāṃsāśloka [śloka] m. pl. cf. mīmāṃsāsūtra.
mīmāmsāślokavārttika [vārttika] n. bed. n.p. from the mīmāmsāślokavārttika of Kumārila Bhaṭṭa; cf. Ślokavārttika.

mīmāṃsāsūtra [sūtra] n. pl. lit. np. of the mīmāmsāsūtra, a collection of aphorisms condensing the doctrine pūrvamīmāmsā; it is later than the 4th century BC, but attributed to Jaimini; the Samkarşanakānda is an annex to it.
mīmāṃsāsūtrabhāṣya [bhāṣya] n. lit. np. of the mīmāmsāsūtrabhāṣya or Mīmāmsābhāṣya, commentary on the Mīmāṃsāsūtra due to Sabarasvāmī; it was commented on by Kumārila.
mīmāṃsita [pp. mīmāṃs] amnf mīmāṃsitā reflected, weighed.
mīmāṃsin [agt. mīmāṃs] amnf mīmāṃsinī phil. casuistic reasoner.
mīmāṃsya [pfp. [1] mīmāṃs] amnf mīmāmsyā debatable, to be questioned.

mīra mn sea, ocean | drink — f. mīrā hist. np. of the holy mīra or Mīrabai (1498– 1547), Rajput princess, famous for her total devotion to Kṛṣṇa; she composed many devotional poems; her ecstatic conduct caused a scandal in her family.
√ mīl v. [1] pr. (mīlati) pp. (mīlita) pf. (ut, ni) to close the eyes, to blink; to close (eyes, flowers) — ca. (mīlayati) to make close.
mukuṭa mn tiara, diadem, crown (crescent-shaped). mukuțin [in] amnf mukuținī crowned; who wears a diadem.

Mukunda m. precious stone | myth. one of the 9 hidden treasures, guarded by Kubera; cf. navanidhi | myth. np. of Mukunda, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "liberator" — f. mukundā myth. np. of mukundā, wife of King Rukmāngada; she was deceived by Indra having taken the form of her husband, and gave birth to Grtsamada₂.
mukundadeva [deva] m. hist. np. of a princely family of Orissa.
Mukundamālā [mālā] f. bed. n.p. from the devotional poem [stotra] Mukundamālā, by King Kulaśekhara; he glorifies Kṛṣṇa.
mukura var. makura m. mirror | ritual gesture [mudrā] of the hand "in mirror" (index and little finger raised vertically, other fingers folded) | stick for turning the potter's wheel.

mukula mn bud, bud | first tooth | hist. np. of mukula Bhatta, son of Kallaṭa (Kaśmīra, 9th century); he is credited with the Abhidhāvṛttimātṛkā, a treatise on denotative functions criticizing the dhvani concept of Anandavardhana; he is also credited with a commentary on the Spandakārikās (lost) | arch. summit of the floret; syn. kudmala | meatal bud on the linga | ritual gesture [mudrā] of the bud (fingers joined upwards) — v. [11] pr. (mukulayati) pp. (mukulita) close (the eyes); close (like a button).

mukta [pp. muc₁] amnf muktā freed, delivered; abandoned, gone; launched, released, poured out, emitted | phil. freed (from the bonds of transmigration) — loc. mukte prep. cl. excepted, except (i.) — f. cf. muktā || pali mutta. mṛtyumukhānmuktaḥ pulled from the clutches of death. muktairavayavairaśayişi I slept with my limbs relaxed.
muktakantha | kantha | amnf muktakanthī with a free throat. muktakantham loudly, at the top of one's lungs. muktakeśa keśa amnf muktakeśī who has loose hair.
muktagraha | graha | m. the act of letting go.
muktabuddhi [buddhi] amnf whose mind has been liberated; emancipated.

muktāpīda [āpīda] m. hist. np. of the king of Kaśmīra muktāpīḍa (733–769); he established the KārkoṭaNāga dynas and made Kaśmīra a great power, allied with China; he overthrew King Yaśovarmā and became Emperor |sārvabhauma| La litāditya; he built the admirable Sun Temple of Mārtāṇḍa.

mukteśvara |īśvara| m. geo. np. of the śaiva mukteśvara temple in Bhubaneśvar (Orissa), built around 970; in front of its entrance stands an arch | torana|, and it has a maṇḍapa with a sculpted ceiling; in the same complex are the Sid dheśvara temple and the Marīcikuṇḍa well.
muktaka [muktaka] amnf muktakā detached, separate; independent — n. lit. stance |śloka| isolated, quotation | gram. simple prose (without compound words) | lit. isolated verse in an anthology.
muktā [f. mukta] f. ["secreted"] Pearl.
muktākāra [kāra] amnf muktākārī which has the shape of a Pearl.

muktācarita [carita] n. lit. np. from the muktācarita "Story of the Pearls", poem by Raghunāthadāsa; Satyabhāmā asks Kṛṣṇa if pearls grow on trees, and he tells him that he made pearls grow on a tree in Vṛndāvana, back when he was having fun with Rādhā and other shepherdesses |gopī|.
muktāpura [pura] n. lit. [KSS.] np. of the city of muktāpura, in the Himalayas; its king is the vidyādhara prince Muktāsena.
muktāphala | phala | n. Pearl. muktāmaņi [maṇi] m. Pearl.
muktāvali [āvali] f. row of beads; pearl necklace — ifc. bed. name of works | var. Muktāvalī₁ id.; not. n.p. of the Muktāvalī₁ or Nyāyasiddhāntamuktāvalī, and the Muktāvalī₁ or Viśvalocana.

Muktāsena [senā] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara Muktāsena, king of muktāpura; by his wife Kam buvatī he had sons Padmasena and Rūpasena; Adityaprabhā and Candravatī fell in love with Padmasena and quarreled; Padmasena complained to his father, who sent them all to be incarnated as mortals; cf. Parityāgasena.
mukti [act. muc₁] f. liberation | phil. final deliverance, salvation; cf. sālokyādicatustaya. muktaye harim bhajati Liberation is obtained by worshipping Hari.
Muktivāda [vāda] m. lit. np. from the Muktivāda "To see of liberation", treatise on semantics due to Gadādhara.
muktikā [muktika] f. Pearl.
muktikopanisad [upanisad] f. bed. n.p. from the Muktikopanisad “Pearl of Lessons”.
muktikṣetra [kṣetra] n. Sacred place conducive to liberation.

muktisthala | sthala | n. geo. np. of muktisthala "Place of deliverance", Place of pilgrimage associated with Sankara₁ and Nārāyaṇa₃ Bhaṭṭa; mod. village of Mukkuthala in the district of Malappuram in Kerala.
muktvā |abs. muc₁| ind. having released | without, except (acc.).

múkha n. mouth, maw, opening; face, wise face; forehead; front of an army; prow (ship) head, summit; essential part, best part; beginning | edge of a blade | nipple [mukhasandhi] lit. [theater] germ of the plot; it is one of the 5 articulations of dramatic narratives [pañcasandhi] — ifc. which has as its head, which has as its essential or initial part (iic.) — f. mukhī ifc. id. mukhatas adv. by the mouth | at the head; from the beginning. sarve vedā mukhato gṛhītāḥ The entire Veda is retained by recitation. mukhāmukhi var. sammukhām face to face.
mukhakamala | kamala | n. lit. lotus-like face.
mukhaghaṇṭā [ghaṇṭā] f. soc. ululations of joy of women, not. during a wedding ceremony; syn. hulahulī.
mukhacandra | candra | m. lit. "face like the Moon", a sign of beauty.
mukhacandramas [candramas] m. id.
mukhadaghná [daghna] amnf mukhadaghnā f. mukhadaghnī who has (water) up to their mouth.
mukhapadma [padma] n. lit. lotus-like face.
Mukhalinga [linga] m. myth. np. of Mukhalinga, epith. of Shiva "represented by an anthropomorphic linga"; arch. it is one of the 16 aspects of Shiva.
mukhaśalā [śālā] f. entrance hall; waiting room, vestibule.
mukhaśodhana [śodhana] amnf mu khaśodhanā that cleans the mouth | acrid, pungent — m. acrid or spicy taste — n. mouth cleaning.
mukhaśodhin [śodhin] amnf mukhaśodhinī that cleans the mouth — m. lemon.
mukhasaṃdaṃśa [saṃdaṃśa] m. med. forceps.
mukhasukha [sukha] n. ease of pronunciation.
mukhasukhārtha [artha] amnf mukha sukhārtha gram. useful for pronunciation (said of a letter inserted to facilitate the pronunciation of a word); syn. uccāraṇārtha.
mukhastha [stha] amnf mukhasthā memorized. mukhasthā vidyā memorized knowledge (not. by a pandita).

mukhāgni |agni| m. soc. rite consisting of placing a burning brand in the mouth of a dead person at the time of cremation, in order to prevent the explosion of the skull; the eldest son performs it for his father.
mukhebhaga [bhaga] m. homosexual ["who practices fellatio"].
mukhopādhyāya [upādhyāya] m. title of scholars; mod. Mukherji.
Mukhara |mukhara| amnf mukharā ba vard, loquacious; eloquent | that chirps, that sings (bird, bees); that rings (ankle ring) | noisy; coarse — m. crow; (shell of)

conch | chief | myth. [Mah.] np. of the nāga Mukhara — f. mukharī mors — v. [11] pr. (mukharayati) to make speak, to make talkative | to announce, to notify. mukharīkṛ to resound; to dwell on. mukharīkṛtavān talkative, babbling. ata eva mām prayojanaśuśrūṣā mukharayati That is why the desire to know your motives makes me so beardy.
mukharatā |tā| f. chatter.
múkhya [mukhaya] amnf mukhyā at the head, principal, the first; excellent, the most beautiful; preeminent, chief | gram. cf. dvikarmaka — ifc. the best among, principal in (iic.).
mukhyakarma [karma] mn gram. primary purpose semantic role (of verbs with two accusatives); opp. gaunakarma.
mukhyaprāṇa [prāṇa] m. myth. np. of Mu khyaprāṇa, Vāyu in the form of the Supreme Breath; he incarnated as Hanumān, as Bhīma, and as Madhva.
mukhyaviśesya [viśesya] n. gram. theory of the main qualification.

mukhyaviśesyaka [viśesyaka] ifc. amnf mu khyaviśesyakā gram. which admits as a principal qualification. dhātvarthamukhyaviśesyaka gram. refers to semantic analysis [śabdabodha] directed by the meaning of the verb (school of grammarians [vaiyākaraṇa]). prathamāntamukhyaviśesyaka gram. refers to semantic analysis [śabdabodha] directed by the subject (school of logicians | naiyāyika|). bhāvanārthamukhyaviśesyaka gram. refers to semantic analysis [śabdabodha] directed by the consequence of the action (school of exegetes | mīmāmsaka|).
mukhyārtha [artha] n. gram. main or literal meaning of a word; syn. abhidhārtha; opp. gauṇārtha — amnf mukhyārthā gram. used in its literal sense.
mukhyārthabādhā [bādhā] f. gram. inapplica bilice du sens literale; se dit de la metaphor | lakṣaṇa | ; syn. anupapatti.

mugdhá [pp. muh] amnf mugdhā naive, foolish, simpleton, stupid; simpleton; mad | perplexed, bewildered, astonished candid, inexperienced, ingenuous; young, amiable, charming — f. mudghā young silly girl, naive goose.
mugdhabuddhi [buddhi] amnf id. ["who has taken it astray".
mugdhabodha |bodha| n. gram. n.p. from the Mugd habodha vyākaraņa "Instruction of the ignorant", grammar of Vopadeva.
mugdhākṣī [akṣa] f. attractive woman ["who has an ingenuous look".
mugdhābhisārikā | abhisārikā | f. lit. ingénue going to her first romantic date.

√ muc₁ v. [6] pr. (muncati) fut. r. (moksyate) pft. (mumoca) aor. [1] (amok) aor. [2] (amucat) aor. [3] (amūmucat) aor. r. [4] (amukta) pp. (mukta) inf. (moktum) abs. (muktvā) pf. (adhi, ava, ā, ut, nis, pari, pra, vi) to free, to deliver; to let go, to untie, to deliver from (abl.) — ps. (mucyate) to be freed, to be deprived; to free oneself, to abstain — ca. (mocayati) to set free, to untie; to free from (abl.) — des. (mumukṣati) to desire to free | lat. mūcus. prānān muc₁ kill. mukṣīya (benedictative) grant that I may be freed. ámoci (aorist passive) he has been freed. kopam mumoca sā anger passed from him. mā bhavānangāni muncatu do not lose hope. adhunā muṃca śayyām get out of bed now!
muc₁ [agt. muc₁] amnf ifc. that which delivers from, that which liberates from (iic.) — f. liberation
muca [agt. muc₁] ifc. amnf mucī that releases from (iic.) | that releases, that sends (iic.).

Mucilinda m. bd. np. of Mucilinda or Mu calinda, mythical giant cobra, who sheltered Buddha with her hood to protect him from the storm for 7 days while he meditated under the tree of awakening in Gaya | mucalinda id.
mucukunda m. myth. np. of mucukunda, son of king Māndhātā; he assisted the gods in their war against the demons, and obtained eternal sleep as a reward.
mucutī [muc₁] f. med. pair of forceps.

múñja m. bio. bot. Saccharum arundinaceum, ved. reed used for divination and for weaving baskets and ascetic belts | mekhalā| | hist. np. of Muñja, Paramāra king who reigned in Dhārā in the 10th century; this poet-king had the title of Vākpati; he was beheaded by King Kalyāṇa₁ Tai lapa; his younger brother Sindhurāja succeeded him. muñjīkṛ | "to reduce to reeds" | to shred.

múñjavat [vat] amnf muñjavatī overgrown with reeds — m. variety of soma | myth. np. of the marvelous jar din Muñjavān in the Himālaya for the pleasures of Shiva and Kubera, full of gold mines; King Marutta held his great sacrifice there, officiated by Samvarta — ind. similar to the reed Muñja.

muṇḍa amnf muṇḍā Bald; one who has a shaved head | pruned (tree) — m. myth. np. of muṇḍa, epith. of Ketu "the Bald" — f. muṇḍī bio. bot. Sphæranthus indicus, globular aster, medicinal plant — v. [11] pr. (muṇḍayati) pp. (muṇḍita) to shave the head. yavanamundah un yavana Bald (compound in versed).
muṇḍamālā [mālā] f. garland of severed heads.
muṇḍaka [agt. muṇḍa] amnf muṇḍikā shaved; Bald; pruned.

mundakopanisad [upanisad] f. lit. np. of the Mundakopanisad (MO.) "Liberator", esoteric lesson [upaniṣad] of the Atharvaveda; Saṅkara₁ commented on it; it teaches that the Veda only provides superficial knowledge, and that supreme knowledge [Vedānta] comes from the direct experience of the Imperishable Brahman |akṣara| through renunciation.
muṇḍana [act. muṇḍa] n. tonsure |soc. shaving of the head, not. as a sign of family mourning.
muṇḍita [pp. muṇḍa] amnf muṇḍitā who has his head shaved.
√ mud₁ v. [1] pr. r. (modate) v. [1] pr. (modati) pft. (mumude) aor. r. [5] (amodista) pp. (mudita) pf. (anu, pra) to be joyful, to rejoice in (i. loc.) — ca. (modayati) to rejoice, to amuse.
mud₂ [act. mud₁] f. Joy, gaiety; happiness (also pl.) | delirium, intoxication | var. mudā Joy, gaiety; pleasure; happiness | var. mudī moonlight — m. muda Joy personified.
mudita [pp. mud₁] amnf muditā joyful (of (i. iic.)); happy — f. muditā Joy, gladness phil. gaiety, one of the four moral qualities |brahmavihāra|.
mudgá m. organic. bot. Vigna radiata, mung bean; its peas are edible and used medicinally.
mudgayūṣa |yūṣa| n. pea soup.
mudgara m. hammer, mallet.

Mudgala₁ [mudgala] m. geo. [Mah.] np. of the land Mudgala₁; it was conquered by Kṛṣṇa | myth. [Mah.] np. of the sage [rsi] Mudgala₁ or Maudga lya "of Mudgala₁"; he never gave in to anger; Durvāsā visited his hermitage to test him; every day, he took all his food, ate his fill, and wasted the rest by crushing it on his naked body; satisfied that he thus controlled his anger, Durvāsā offered him access to heaven with his mortal body; but the sage refused such a luxurious residence; his wife was Indra senā₁.

mudrā [mud₁ra] f. seal, (ring bearing a) stamp; stamp, printing form | coin, medal; stamp; stamped paper, not a sport | bodily attitude; canonical iconographic gesture | symbolic hand gesture, not. in the theater; the Hastalakṣaṇadīpikā lists the 24 basic gestures; a distinction is made between two-handed gestures |saṃyutahasta| and one-handed gestures |asaṃyutahasta| |bd. commemorative gestures of events in the life of the Buddha; cf. abhaya, añjali, dharmacakra, dhyāna, bhūmisparśa, varada, vitarka | phil. [Tantra] ritual laying on of the fingers for esoteric purposes, such as isolating the subtle body |sūkṣmaśarīra| | "roasted cereals" (interpretation hiding the preceding esoteric meaning, in the enumeration of the 5 transgressions in [makārapañcaka]) | lit. figure of speech where the name of its meter appears in the verse — v. [11] pr. (mudrayati) abs. (mudrayitvā) pp. (mudrita) to put a seal; to print.
mudrākhya [ākhyā₂] m. ritual gesture [mudrā] of the seal (index finger pinching the thumb, other fingers separated); it is the gesture of wisdom [cinmudrā] and knowledge [jñānamudrā].
mudrānkita [ankita] amnf mudrānkitā marked with a seal — n. soc. mādhva initiation ritual consisting of marking the temples of an initiate with the conch [śańkha] and the disc [cakra].

mudrādhāraṇa [dhāraṇa] n. du. mudrādhāraṇe soc. imposition of the seal of Vișnu on the body, a mādhva rite; the śītalamudrādhāraṇa, cold-printed with the gopīcandana, is daily; the tap tamudrādhāraņa, branded with a hot iron, is performed annually at the ekādaśī of the bright fortnight of the month āṣāḍha .

mudrārākṣasa [Rākṣasa₁] m. keeper of the seals | mod. ["demon of the press"] printing error — n. lit. np. of the mudrārākṣasa “the Seal of Rākṣasa₁”, historical fiction drama in 7 acts by Viśākhadatta; it depicts Cāṇakya's policy to win over the minister Rākṣasa₁ to the cause of Candragupta after the latter has overthrown the Nanda dynasty in Magadha.
mudrāvidhāna [vidhāna] n. bed. from np. mudrāvidhāna “Prescription of ritual gestures”, work in Sanskrit and Tamil (1985).
mudrita [pp. mudrā] amnf mudritā tam ponné, cacheté, imprime | marque au fer | scellé; relie — n. impression (on (loc.)) | mod. imprime rie.
mudhā muh adv. in vain; uselessly; without reason | wrongly.

múni m. sage; ascetic, anchorite; hermit who has taken a vow of silence | phil. conscience | pl. munayas myth. the seven celestial sages [syn. saptarși] | astr. the Great Bear | math. symb. the number 7 — f. var. munī myth. np. of munī, daughter of Dakṣa, wife of Kaśyapa, mother of the centaur genies [gandharva] and
trolls |yaksa|. yathottaram munīnām prāmānyam gram. Each of the wise men (of the trimuni) has rank over his predecessor.
munikumāra [kumāra] m. young ascetic.
munitraya [traya] n. gram. the triad of masters of the Sanskrit grammatical tradition: Pānini, Kātyāyana and Patañjali₁; syn. trimuni.
munivara [vara₂] m. soc. title of "best of the sages".
Munisuvrata [suvrata] m. jn. np. of Munisuvrata "Virtuous sage", 20th mythical tīrthankara; his body is brown, his symbol is a tortoise.
mumukṣ [des. muc₁] v. pr. (mumukṣati) to desire to liberate — pr. r. (mumukṣate) to desire deliverance.
mumukṣu |agt. des. muc₁| amnf phil. who wishes for deliverance; opp. bubhukşu.
mumukṣutva [tva] n. phil. [Vedānta] impulse towards liberation.
mumukṣuvyavahāra | vyavahāra | m. phil. question of deliverance.
Mumukṣuvyavahāraprakaraṇa [prakaraṇa] n. bed. n.p. of Mumuksuvyavahāraprakaraņa, 3rd section of Moksopāya.
mumūrṣ [des. mṛ] v. pr. (mumūrṣati) to desire to die | to be about to die.
mumūrṣā [act. des. mṛ] f. desire to die.
mumūrṣu [agt. dés. mṛ] amnf who desires death.

Mura₁ [mr] m. myth. np. of Mura₁ or Murāsura "Slayer", demon [dānava] son of Kasyapa and Danu; to reward him for his penances, Brahmā had granted him the power to kill any being he touched, even immortals; he guarded Prāgjyotiṣa, capital of Naraka, and had 4000 sons; he challenged Indra, who preferred to exile himself to Earth; he disrupted a sacrifice of Raghu, and Vasistha advised him to attack Yama instead; when he came to order Yama to stop killing, Yama told him that he was under the orders of Vișnu; it was then that Kṛṣṇa at taqua Prāgjyotiṣa, where he killed Naraka and Mura₁ | myth. np. of the yādava king Mura₁ or Muru.
muraja [ja] mf murajā type of drum; tam bourin.
murajabandha [bandha] m. lit. drum-shaped geometric poem [citrakāvya].

Murāri₁ [ari] m. myth. n.p. of Murāri₁, epith. by VișnuKrșna "enemy of Mura₁" | hist. n.p. of the poet Murāri₁ (10th century, Orissa), author of the Anar gharāghava | hist. n.p. of Murāri₁ Miśra, who created the miśramata school of mīmāṃsā in the 12th century; we owe him the Ekadaśādhyāyādhikaraṇa.
murala m. pl. geo. np. of the Muralā people in Kerala — f. muralā geo. np. of the Muralā river in Kerala.
muraladesa [desa] m. geo. country of the Muralas in Kerala, north of the Kāverī.
muralī f. flute.
muralīdhara | dhara | m. myth. np. of muralīdhara, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "holding the flute".
muralīmanohara [manohara] m. myth. np. of Mu ralīmanohara, epith. of Kṛṣṇa "who enchants with his flute".
√ muṣ₁ v. [9] pr. (muṣṇāti) pp. (muṣita) pf. (pari) to steal, rob, plunder; to snatch, deceive, trick; to mislead, blind.
muṣ² [agt. muṣ¹] ifc. amnf [nom. muṣt] that steals, that ravishes (iic.).
muṣitá [pp. muṣi] amnf muṣitā stolen, plundered; carried off, snatched, taken away, abducted | deprived of (acc.) | blinded.
muṣka m. scrotum, testicles.
muṣṭāmuṣṭi [red. muṣṭi] adv. in bare-knuckle combat.
muṣṭi [act. muṣ₁] mf theft | closed hand, fist (concealing the theft) | grip | ritual gesture [mudrā] of the hand in a closed fist.
mustika |ka| mr. handle | hand position | pl. muṣṭikās soc. pariahs, outcastes — f. cf. muṣṭikā.
muṣṭikā [f. muṣṭika] iic. with the hands.
muṣṭikākathana | kathana | n. the act of telling a story with the hands.
muṣṭim [acc. muṣṭi] iic.
muṣṭiṃdhama [dhama] amnf muṣṭiṃdhamā
baby ["who blows into his fist"].
baby ["who sucks on his fist"].
muṣṭiṃdhaya [dhaya] amnf muṣṭiṃdhayā
músala mn club; pestle (wooden); bell clapper — f. musalī lizard; chameleon; alligator.
musalāmusali [red. musala] adv. “mass against club” in hand-to-hand combat.
musta mf mustā bio. bot. Cyperus rotundus, sedge; herbaceous marsh plant with rhizomes and tubers, three-cornered stem, flowers in brown spikes; used in medicine.
mustakā |ka| f. id.

√ muh v. [4] pr. (múhyati) pft. (mumoha) pp. (mugdha, mūḍha) pf. (pari, pra, vi, sam) to be confused, to be misled; to be unconscious; to be stupid; to be mistaken, to be led astray; to go astray, to be mistaken; to lose one's head — ca. (mo hayati) to panic, to mislead.
múhur adv. suddenly, all at once | for a moment; repeatedly, frequently; often; constantly. muhur ... muhur sometimes ... sometimes; always and always. bālo muhū roditi the child cries often.

muhūrtá [muhurta] mn minute, moment, period of time equivalent to 48 minutes; there are 3 in a [kāla₁], 30 in a full day [ahorātra]; it is worth two demilaps [nādikā] | one of the 30 moments of the day; cf. brahmamuhūrta, ru dramuhūrta, prātastana, samgava, abhijit; myth. they are personified as the Muhūrtās | astr. appropriate moment to undertake an important act; fateful hour — f. Muhūrtā myth. np. of Muhūrtā, daughter of Dakṣa, mother of the 30 Muhūrtās.
muhūrtaśāstra | śāstra | n. astr. astrological determination of the favorable time to start an enterprise.
mūka amnf mūkā mute; silent — m. fish || gr. v ; lat. ū tus; eng. mute; fr. mute.
mūkabhāva | bhāva | m. state of being mute, muteness.
mūjavat m. geo. np. of the Mūjavān mountain, in the Pamir region; ved. the soma plant is found there || Avestan Muza.

mūḍhá |pp. muh| amnf mūḍhā confused, stupefied, bewildered; fool, simpleton; stupid, idiot, cretin; senseless, mad | adrift; erroneous, misled, out of service, bewildered by, not knowing what to do with (loc. iic.) — m. idiot — n. confusion of mind, bewilderment. yathā kharaścandanabhāravāhī bhārasya vettā na tu candanasyaivam hi śāstrāṇi bahūnyadhītya cārthesu mūdhāh kharavadvahanti [Suśruta] Just as a donkey carries its load of sandalwood without knowing its value, those who have recited the teachings a lot while being inept at understanding their meaning carry them like donkeys.
mūdhácetas [cetas] amnf mūdhacetasā to the disturbed mind. dhigme mandam pitaram mūdhatācetasam |Mah.| (Ambā) Cursed be my foolish father, whose mind is disturbed.
mūdhátā |tā| f. stupefaction; perplexity; confusion; stupidity, madness.
mūdhátva |tva| n. stupefaction; confusion; stupi dité, folie.
mūdhadhī [dhī₂] amnf simpleton, idiot.
mūdháprabhu [prabhu] m. ["king of fools"] cretin.
mūdhámati [mati] amnf idiot, stupid. govindam bhaja mūdhamate pray to Govinda, you fool!
mūdhamanas [manas] amnf idiot, stupid.

mūtra [instr. muc₁] n. urine — v. [11] pr. (mūtrayati) pr. r. (mūtrayate) pp. (mūtrita) uri ner; to urinate against (acc.). mūtram kṛ to urinate. tisthan mūtrayati gauh the ox pees standing up. tisthan mūtrayati yavanah the Greek pees standing up. abrāhmaņo'yam yas tisthan mūtrayati [Mah.] He who urinates standing up is not a Brahmin.
mūtrakṛcchra [kṛcchra] mn med. urinary affection.
mūtrāśaya [āśaya] m. med. bladder.
mūtrita [pp. mūtra] amnf mūtritā who has urinated | urinated; soiled with urine — n. micturition.
mūtrya |mūtraya| amnf mūtryā urinary; concerning urine.

mūrkhá [agt. mūrch] amnf mūrkhā stupid, simpleton; stubborn, obtuse; stupid, imbecile — mr. imbecile, moron; crazy — ifc. an idiot of (iic.). mūrkhāms tyajati panditah The wise avoid fools. tāvacchobhate mūrkho yāvat kiṃcin na bhāṣate |Hitopadeśa| The fool only shines as long as he stays silent.
mūrkhátā [tā] f. foolishness, stupidity, foolishness.
mūrkhátva [tva] n. foolishness, stupidity, foolishness.
mūrkhalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. sign of stupidity.
mūrcchana gem. mūrcchana.
mūrcchā gem. mūrchā.
mūrcchita gem. mūrchita.

√ mūrch v. [1] pr. (mūrchati) aor. [5] (amūrchīt) pp. (mūrchita, mūrta) pf. (sam) to solidify, harden, stiffen; to form, thicken; to clump, coagulate, crystallize; to become a homogeneous mass | to grow, increase; to gain strength, become violent | to penetrate, spread over; to have an effect — ca. (mūrchayati) to shape; to strengthen. mārutasya raṃhaḥ śiloccaye na mūrchati the storm has no effect against a mountain. mūrchantyamī vikārā aiśvaryamatteșu such changes affect those who are drunk with power. niśamūrchatām tamasām of darkness thickening with the night.

mūrchana [agt. mūrch] amnf mūrchanā that stupefies; that anesthetizes (said of a Kāma arrow) — act. n. fainting | (mus.) melodic modulation | vehemence; intensification | var. mūrcchana f. mūrcchanā id. — f. mūrchanā fainting; stupor; hallucination | melody; modulation. bhūyo bhūyah svayam api kṛtām mūrchanam vis
maranti [MD.] She forgets again and again the melody that She Herself chose.
mūrchā [act. mūrch] f. fainting; bewilderment, hallucination | var. mūrcchā id. mūrchām bhaj to faint. mūrchām kal id.
mūrchita [pp. mūrch] amnf mūrchitā stupefied; solidified, frozen; increased, enlarged — ifc. full of, filled with (iic.).
mūrtá [pp. mūrch] amnf mūrtā corporeal, incarnate; substantial.
mūrtatara [tara] amnf mūrtatarā substantial, made concrete.

mūrtadravya [dravya₁] n. phil. [Vaiśeṣika] concrete substance; there are 5 of them, including 4 elements [bhūtadravya]: Earth [pṛthivī], Waters [āpas], Fire [tejas], Air [vāyu], to which we add the Mind or inner sense [manas].

Mūrti [act. mūrch] f. solid body; Matter; form | manifestation; individual; representation, statue, image, idol | math. symb. the number 3 myth. np. of Mūrti "Matter", daughter of Dakṣa, one of the wives of Dharma.
mūrtikāra | kāra | mr. sculptor.
mūrtikumbha [kumbha] m. arch. consecration vase representing a deity, during the rite of installation of a building.
mūrtipūjā |pūjā| f. soc. worship by means of idols.
mūrtimat [mat] amnf mūrtimatī having a form; incarnate.
mūrtiśāstra | śāstra | n. sculpture.
mūrdha iic. mūrdhan.
mūrdhaga [ga₁] amnf mūrdhagā which is on the head of.
mūrdhaja [ja] m. pl. mūrdhajās hair, what you want.
mūrdhābhiṣikta [abhiṣikta] amnf mūrdhābhiṣiktā consecrated | gram. is said not. of the examples of Patañjali₁.
mūrdhāvasikta [avasikta] amnf mūrdhāvasiktā soc. consecrated by royal anointing. rājño mūrdhāvasiktasya vadho brahmavadhād
guruh |BhP.| The murder of a consecrated king is worse than that of a brahmin.

mūrdhán m. head, skull; summit, peak; beginning, origin; crucial thing | phon. place in the palate where retroflex consonants are articulated. mūrdhni adv. at the head sa sarveṣām mūrdhni tiṣṭhati he is above all.
mūrdhanya [ya] amnf mūrdhanyā from the head | phon. (consonant) retroflex or apical — m. apical phoneme (apicoalveolar or retroflex).

mūrvā f. bio. bot. Sansevieria roxburghiana, a plant with fleshy leaves, a type of agave; it is used to make bowstrings and belts [maurvī]; its rhizome is used medicinally against coughs | bio. bot. Chonemorpha fragrans, an apocynaceae shrub with latex, large white flowers with a sweet scent; its roots are used medicinally.

Mūla n. Root; foot (of a tree); Edible root, turnip, radish | base, foundation | origin, cause; principle | main city, capital | edge of the horizon | lit. original text, source; primary work (opp. vrtti) | |mūlabarhanī| astr. np. from the nakṣatra Mūla "Root" | math. Square root — ifc. based on, derived from (2nd century). mūlaskandhaphalapalāśavān (trees) formed from stump, trunk, fruits and leaves.
prācīmūle |MD.| at the edge of the eastern horizon.
mūlakalā [kalā] f. soc. main art; cf. catuļķastikalā.
mūlagranthakāra [granthakāra] m. author founder (of iic. ).
mūlatva [tva] n. Nature of being an origin or a founding act — ifc. fact of resting on (iic.). vedamūlatvāt from the fact that the Veda is the source of all knowledge.

Mūladeva₁ [deva] m. lit. np. of Mūladeva₁, a famous thief and seducer; he is an expert in eroticism [kāmaśāstra], which he teaches to the prostitute Guṇapatākā in the work he dedicated to her; he is Karņīsuta, author of a work on the art of theft l lit. [KSS.] np. of the magician Mūladeva₁, a friend of Manaḥsvāmī; he made a pill to change him into a woman, and another to turn himself into an old Brahmin.
mūlaprakṛti [prakṛti] f. phil. [Sāṃkhya] the Primordial Nature, original cause of the phenomena of the material world; cf. avyakta, pradhāna.
mūlabandha [bandha] m. phil. [yoga] contraction of the perineal muscles aimed at raising the apānavāyu in the channel [mārga] of the Suṣumṇā.
Mūlabarhaṇī [barhaṇa] f. astr. np. of Mūlabarhaṇī "she who uproots", 17th lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the star of Scorpio; the manes |pitaras| preside there; its symbol is a lion's tail.

mūlamadhyamaka | madhyamaka | m. bd. np. of the mūlamadhyamaka "foundation of the Middle Way", work in stanzas [kārikās] by Nāgārjuna, also called Madhyamakaśāstra; it had a strong influence on all intellectual circles; it is also a jewel of elegant poetry.

mūlamantra [mantra] n. soc. [Tantra] Root mantra, dedicated to the Supreme Goddess; it is pronounced as an introduction to offering rites | soc. principal mantra of invocation of a deity | original form of a mantra before its encapsulation by seed syllables [bīja] and other incantations. hrīm śrīm krīm parameśvari svāhā |mūlamantra| Homage to you Supreme Goddess.
Mūlarāja [rāja] m. hist. np. of Mūlarāja, first king of the Solankī dynasty in Gurjara in 940; his capital was Anahilapātaka; Bhīmadeva I succeeded him.
mūlavibhuja |vibhuja| amnf mūlavibhujā who bends the roots — m. cart.
mūlasamhitā [samhitā] f. lit. np. of the mūlasamhitā, presumed original collection of ancient books [purāṇa], attributed to Lomaharṣaṇa; it would be close to the Vāyupurāna.
mūlasarvāstivāda [sarvāstivāda] m. bd. n.p. of the mūlasarvāstivāda, disciplinary code [vinaya] of the sarvāstivāda school.
mūlasarvāstivādin [in] m. bd. adherent of this doctrine.
mūlasūtra |sūtra| n. lit. foundational collection of aphorisms of a tradition | jn. not. class of texts jina.
mūlāgama |āgama| mr. bed. text of the śaiva Siddhānta canon; there are 28 of them.

mūlādhāra |ādhāra| m. phil. | "the support of the foundation"] 1st chakra of tantric yoga, located at the foundation; it is represented by a lotus with 4 red petals; a yellow square there symbolizes the earth, and bears the bījamantra 'laṃ'; the śakti Kuṇḍalinī sleeps there, coiled three and a half times around the svayambhūlinga; this chakra controls the sense of smell; it is the psychic center of the Inciting Awakening.
mūlābhāva [abhāva] amnf mūlābhāvā phil. without foundation.
mūlārādhanā [ārādhanā] f. jn. np. of the mūlārādhanā, doctrinal text jn. on the choice of one's end of life; also called Bhagavatī ārādhanā.

mūlaka [Mūlaka] amnf mūlikā ifc. From; rooted in — mn Root; radish, turnip, swede; sweet potato — m. myth. [BhP.] np. of the king mūlaka "From (the Sun)", son of Aśmaka₁ of the solar lineage |sūryavaṃśa|; he is father of KhaṭvāṅgaDilīpa₂; cf. Nārīkavaca.
mūlakapaṇa [paṇa] m. bunch of radishes.

mūlya [Mūlaya] amnf mūlyā from the root cine, originally — n. market value, cost, purchase price; price | remuneration; gain; capital. amūlya without price. mūlyahīna without value. ekasya mūlyena vyayah śudhyate the sale of a single one covers the expenses.
mūṣ₂ [agt. mūṣ₁] mf ["thief"] mouse | gr. μυς; lat. mūs; eng. mouse; all. Maus. দুপ mūṣa [agt. mūṣɪ] mf mūṣā f. mūṣī rat; crucible mouse.
mūṣavāhana |vāhana| mr. cf. Mūṣikavāhana.
mūṣaka [agt. mūṣɪ] mf mūṣikā thief, plunderer rat, mouse.
mūṣaṇa |act. mūṣ₁| n. flight.
mūṣika [mūṣaika] m. mouse; rat | myth. the

ratmonture [vāhana] of Gaņeśa | pl. geo. name of the country and people of the Mūṣikās, established on the coast of Kerala south of mod. Quilon — f. cf. mūṣikā. Mūṣikavāhana [vāhana] m. myth. of np. Mūṣikavāhana, epith. of Gaṇeśa "who has a mouse as a mount".
mūṣikā [f. mūṣika] f. mouse; rat | med. blood sweat | crucible.

√ mṛ v. [6] pr. r. (mriyáte) pft. (mamāra) pft. r. (mamre) aor. r. [1] (amṛta) aor. [3] (amīmarat) pp. (mṛta) inf. (martum) to die — ca. (mārayati) to cause to die, to kill — des. (mumūrṣati) to be dying; to wish to die — intens. (marīmarti) in tens. r. (memrīyate) to agonize | lat. morior; ang. murder; all. Mord; fr. mort, mourir. adya mamāra he is dead now.
mṛkaṇḍa m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] mṛkaṇḍa, father of Mārkaṇḍeya by Manasvinī | mṛkaṇḍu he is also called mṛkaṇḍu.
√ mṛg v. [4] pr. (mṛgyati) to search, to examine; to chase, to pursue | to desire (acc.) for (abl.).

mṛgá [act. mṛg] m. research, investigation; hunting — obj. m. game, peaceful wild animal; opp. vyāla (wild beast); opp. paśu (domestic animal) | not. antelope, gazelle, deer | lit. in poetry, the antelope or hare visible on the Moon | astr. the constellation

lation | nakṣatra | of Orion; cf. Mṛgaśiras — f. mṛgī wild animal female | myth. np. of mṛgī, daughter of Kaśyapa and Krodhavaśā; she gave birth to the race of antelopes — f. cf. mrgā — v. [11] pr. r. (mrgayate) v. [11] pr. (mrgayati) inf. (mrgayitum) to seek, chase, pursue | to pursue, aim at, strive to (acc.) | to ask, demand (of (abl. g.)) | to explore. mṛgacapalā f. (young girl) timid as a gazelle.
mrgacakra | cakra | n. astr. ecliptic; zodiac.

mṛgacārin [cārin] mf mṛgacāriṇī ["who lives like an antelope"] ascetic secluded in the woods. aham te duhitā rājan | Mādhavī mṛgacāriṇī || lit. [Mah.] (Mādhavī to Yayāti) I am your daughter, O king, Mādhavī, dressed in the skin of the antelope (of the ascetic).
mṛgatṛṣṇā [tṛṣṇā] f. ["gazelle thirst"] mirage (of the desert) | var. mṛgatṛṣṇi id.
mṛgatṛṣṇikā [ika] f. Fata Morgana.
mrgatva [vat] n. wild animal condition.
mṛgadāva [dāva] m. bd. gazelle park of Sāranātha, where Buddha gave his first sermon.
mṛgadṛś [dṛś₂] f. pretty woman [“with the look of a doe”].
mṛgapati [pati] m. lion ["master of animals"].
mrgamada | mada | m. musc.
mrgamanda | manda | m. bio. marsh animal | race of elephants — f. mṛgamandā myth. np. of Mṛgamandā, daughter of Kaśyapa and Krodhavaśā; she gave birth to the race of yaks | camara |.
mrgamandra [mandra] m. prized breed of war elephants.
mṛgarāja [rāja] m. lion ["king of the animals"].
mṛgavana [vana] n. royal hunts.

Mrgavyādha [vyādha] m. hunter | myth. np. of Mrgavyādha "the hunter", personifying the star Sirius, symbolizing Rudra as the divine archer who struck Prajāpati with his arrow while he was committing incest at the dawn of the world; by extension, epith. of Śiva in his role as avenger of primordial unity; he is one of the 11 divine breaths | marut|; syn. Lubdhaka.
mṛgáśāva₁ [śāva₁] m. young fawn.
mṛgáśāvākṣī [akṣī] f. pretty woman ["with the look of a young gazelle".

mrgásiras [siras] n. astr. np. of Mrgasiras "Head of the antelope", 3rd lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the Belt of Orion (Three Kings); Soma presides over it; its symbol is the head of a gazelle; it symbolizes Prajāpati, the primordial victim, pierced by Rudra after the incest of Creation; cf. Rohinī.
mrgáśīrṣá [śīrṣa] n. antelope head | astr. cf. Mṛgaśiras | ritual gesture [mudrā] of the antelope head (index and ring fingers raised like horns, middle finger bent).
mṛgākṣī [akṣa] f. pretty woman ["with the look of a doe" |.
mṛgānka |anka | m. the Moon | "whose spots are shaped like an antelope"].

mṛgāṅkadatta [datta] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Prince Mṛgāṅkadatta "Gift of the Moon", son of King Amaradatta of Ayodhyā; a vetāla predicted that he would marry the beautiful Princess Śāśānkavatī; he went to Ujjayinī disguised as a śaiva ascetic with 10 companions; King Pārāvata cast a spell on them and they were separated; after many trials Mṛgānkadatta married Sāśānkavatī.

mṛgāṅkavat [vat] amnf mṛgāṅkavatī possessing the splendor of the Moon — f. Mṛgānkavatī lit. [KSS.] np. of Mṛgāṅkavatī, daughter of the vidyādhara king Mṛgānkasena; she made the mistake of being late at the temple to honor Gaurī while her father waited for his meal; devoured with hunger, he cursed her to be devoured four nights a month by the rākṣasa Kṛtāntasaṃtrāsa, then he left and left her alone in an underwater palace; she would come out to show herself to the sailors, perched on a wishing tree of coral, singing to the lute the inevitability of the retribution of the act [karman]; She was spotted by Dīrghadarśī and King Yaśahketu plunged into the ocean to follow her, kill Kṛtāntasaṃtrāsa and bring her back as his wife among mortals.

mṛgānkāvalī [āvalī] f. bed. [Viddhaśālabhañjikā] np. of princess Mṛgāṅkāvalī, daughter of king Candravarmā, who passes her off as crown prince Mṛgānkavarmā and sends her as tribute to Vidyādharamalla.
Mrgendra [indra] m. lion ["king of the animals"] | lit. np. of the Mrgendra; cf. Mrgendrāgama.
Mrgendratantra [tantra] n. bed. from np. Mrgendratantra.
mṛgendratā |tā| f. primacy among animals (said of the lion).
Mrgendrapaddhati [paddhati] f. bed. n.p. from the Mrgendrapaddhati, śaiva ritual manual; Vak traśambhu commented on it.

Mrgendrāgama [āgama] m. lit. np. of the Mṛgendrāgama, a śaiva syncretistic work (circa 1000); Mādhava used it to describe the śaiva doctrine in his Sarvadarśanasamgraha; Bhattanārāyaṇakaṇtha made a gloss on it |vṛtti|.
mrgendrottara [uttara₁] m. bed. n.p. of Mṛgendrottara; cf. Mṛgendrāgama.
mṛgayā [mṛgaya₂] f. hunting. mṛgayām dhāv ["to run after game"] to go hunting. śyainampātā mṛgayā falconry.
mṛgayāvihārin [vihārin] amnf mṛgayāvihārinī hunting enthusiast.
mṛgayu [mṛgayu] m. hunter.
mṛgā [f. mṛga] f. female antelope.

mṛgāvat [vat] amnf Mṛgāvatī who has an antelope — f. Mṛgāvatī lit. np. of the Videha princess Mṛgāvatī, who married King Sahasrānīka; taken away by a bird which abandoned her in the woods, she was taken in by Jamadagni, and gave birth to Udayana at his hermitage.
mṛgāvidh |vidh₂| amnf |sg. name. mṛgāvit| which pierces game.
mṛc iic. mṛd₂.

mṛcchakaṭikā [śakaṭikā] f. bed. n.p. from the Mṛcchakaṭikā “The Little Terracotta Cart”, a subversive comedy of Buddhist inspiration attributed to the “king” Śūdraka, of uncertain date; cf. Aryaka₁, Cārudatta, Dhūtā, Pālaka, Maitreya₂, Rohasena, Sarvilaka.

√ mṛj v. [2] pr. (mārṣṭi) v. [1] pr. (mārjati) pr. r. (mārjate) v. [6] pr. (mṛjati) pr. r. (mṛjate) pp. (mṛṣṭa) inf. (māṛṣṭum) pf. (apa, ava, ut, pari, pra, sam) wipe, clean, rub; erase; smooth; massage | mix with (i.) | crush; reduce to powder; trample, destroy | graze; pass through (constellation); surpass — ca. (mārjayati) ca. r. (mārjayate) erase; rub, polish; adorn — intens. r. (marmrjyate) rub vigorously | lat. mulgeo; eng. to milk; all. melken.
mṛja |agt. mṛj| ifc. amnf mṛjā who cleans, who wipes, who rubs (iic.).
mṛjā [act. mṛj] f. cleaning, purification.
mṛṇāla n. stem or root of the lotus (symbol of fragility).
mṛṇālasūtra |sūtra| n. lotus stem fiber.
mṛṇmáya amnf mṛṇmayī cf. mṛnmaya.
mṛt iic. mṛd₂. mrtpindá ball of clay.
mrtpindábuddhi [buddhi] amnf idiot, imbecile, cretin.
mṛtá [pp. mṛ] amnf mṛtā dead, struck down; gone, disappeared, consumed — n. death | begging, suitable means of subsistence for a brah mane [satkarman] || fr. death.
mṛtátithi [tithi] m. anniversary of death.
mṛtápa [pa₂] m. soc. ["guardian of the dead"] in charge of funeral pyres, of impure caste | var. mṛtapā id.
mrtabhraj |bhraj| m. loss of virility; syn. nastavīrya.
mṛtasaṃjīvanī [saṃjīvanī] f. myth. herb of resurrection; cf. samjīvanī | lit. np. Mṛtasaṃjīvanī, commentary on the Pingalachandaḥsūtra due to Halāyudha₁.
mrtānda [anda] n. egg Dead or believed to be Dead — amnf mṛtāṇḍā [Matsyapurāṇa] born from an egg Dead — f. mṛtāṇḍā woman whose offspring are dead.
mrti [act. mr] f. Death; passing away.

mṛtiman [man] m. mortality. nākavitvam adharmāya vyādhaye daṇḍanāya vā kukavitvam punah sākṣān mṛtimāhur manīṣiṇah [Bhāmaha] Not being a poet incurs neither demerit, nor illness, nor punishment, whereas being a bad poet deserves Death on the spot, say the sages.
mṛttikā [mṛd₁ika] f. earth, soil; clay, clod.
mṛttikāghaṭa [ghaṭa] m. earthenware pot.
mṛttikāvat [vat] f. mṛttikāvatī geo. n.p. from the city of mṛttikāvatī “Made of mud”.

mṛtyú [mṛtayu] m. Death | myth. np. of mṛtyu, Death, title of Yama, the first human, who became the god of Death upon his death; his eldest daughter is Sunīthā | lit. |Mah.| mṛtyu is sometimes evoked as a goddess. mṛtyave tvā dadāmi [KU.] I give you to Death. mrtyoh sa mrtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati BU. He runs from Death to Death, he who believes he sees plurality.
mrtyuvañcana |vañcana| n. phil. deception of Death.
mrtyuvañcanopadeśa [upadeśa] m. bed. n.p. from the Mṛtyuvañcanopadeśa "Treatise on how to deceive Death", comic book. of Vāgīśvarakīrti.
mrtyuvijaya [vijaya] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of the executioner elephant mṛtyuvijaya "He who conquers Death"; supposed to execute Pūrņabhadra₁, he was put to flight by him.
mrtyusamskāra [saṃskāra] m. SOC. funeral ceremony rite; cf. antyeșți.
mṛtyuhīna |hīna| amnf mṛtyuhīnā immortal.

mṛtyum [acc. mṛtyu] iic. Mrtyumjaya var. mrtyuñjaya [jaya] amnf mṛtyumjayā ["Who conquers Death"] Who heals (remedy) — m. myth. np. of Mrtyumjaya, epith. of Shiva "Who conquers Death" — n. name of a śloka of the Rigveda; cf. traiyambakamantra.
mṛtsna [mṛd₁sna] mn dust, powder not. perfumed turmeric powder, used for the protection of writing palm leaves — f. mṛtsnā clay; good soil.
mṛdaṅga [mṛd₁aṅga₁] m. double-sided drum, made of clay or jackfruit wood.
mṛdaṅgika [ika] m. [nāṭya] mṛdaṅga player.
mrdā [mrd₁] f. earth, clay.
mṛdiman [mṛduman] m. lightness; lack of consideration, contempt | phil. [yoga] the power to become light, an astasiddhi.

mṛd₁ú [mṛd₁u] amnf mṛdvī soft; tender, gentle, delicate; kind | phon. said of the consonants so nores (including nasals, semivowels, and the pirée a ha); opp. kathora — n. gentleness, delicacy. mrdu adv. gently. mṛdūkṛ soften. mṛdūbhū soften. mṛdubhūtāḥ become soft. mṛdumṛdu very delicately. mṛdu pacati it cooks gently.
mṛd₁útā |tā| f. gentleness; tenderness; weakness. mṛdutām gam to soften, to calm down; to become more supple, to weaken.
mṛd₁útva [tva] n. gentleness; tenderness; weakness.
mṛdupūrva [pūrva] amnf mṛdupūrvā [“Who begins gently”] kind, amiable, tender (not. words). mṛdupūrvam gently; tenderly.
mṛd₁úbhava [bhava] m. gentleness, tenderness.
mṛdubhāṣin [bhāṣin] amnf mṛdubhāṣiṇī with a delicate voice | Who speaks gently.
mṛduviśada [viśada] amnf mṛduviśadā (cooked rice) tender, with the grains well separated.
mṛdusparśa [sparśa] amnf mṛdusparśā soft to the touch.
mṛdula |mṛdula| amnf mṛdulā soft; tender, gentle.
mṛdvīka [mṛduīka] amnf mṛdvīkā sweet, mild — f. mṛdvīkā grape; bunch of grapes.
√ mṛdh v. [1] pr. (márdhati) pp. (mṛddhá) ved. to neglect, to abandon.
mṛdhas |mṛdh| n. disdain, contempt, insult.
mṛdhrá [mṛdhra] n. contempt, insult.
mṛdhrávāc [vāc] amnf abusive, insulting.

√ mṛś v. [6] pr. (mṛśati) pr. r. (mṛśate) pft. (ma marśa) pp. (mṛṣṭa) pfp. (mṛṣya) pf. (ava, ā, parā, pari, vi) to pass one's hand over, to touch | to reflect on, to examine; to deliberate — ca. (marśayati) pp. (marsita) to consider | lat. mulceo.
√ mrs v. [4] pr. (mrsyati) pf. (pari) to forget, to forgive; to excuse; to bear, to tolerate, to accept; to allow (acc. inf.) — ca. (marṣayati) to bear; to forgive. na mṛṣ to molester.

mṛṣā [mṛṣ] adv. in vain, uselessly | falsely, wrongly; deceitfully — act. f. Deception, lie, falsehood | myth. np. of mṛṣā, Deception personified, mother of Dambha by Adharma — v. [11] pr. r. (mṛṣāyate) to be in error. mṛṣā kṛ to feign. mṛṣā jñā to know as false. mṛṣā man to consider as false. varjanīyam mṛṣā budhaiḥ The wise must refrain from lying.
mṛṣātva |tva| n. falsehood, error; injustice.
