mṛṣodya [udya] amnf mṛṣodyā liar | slanderer. ਸ਼ਣ mṛṣṭá₁ |pp. mṛj| amnf mṛṣṭā cleaned, purified; pure | coated with (i.) | appetizing, pleasing (dish).
mṛṣṭáluñcita [luñcita] amnf mṛṣṭaluñcitā ar raché and cleaned (root). ਸੁਣ mṛṣṭá₂ [pp. mṛś] amnf mṛṣṭā touched.
mṛṣṭi₁ [act. mṛj] f. tasty meal.
mṛṣṭi₁ [act. mṛś] f. touch; contact.
mṛṣyamāṇa |ppr. mo. mṛṣ| amnf mṛṣyamāṇā supporting, tolerant.
me cl. mama, mahyam.
mekhalā f. belt; not. belt of a Brahmanical student; strap, baldric; ventriloquist | phil. [Tantra] circle surrounding a geometric yantra.
mekhalin |in| amnf mekhalinī who wears a belt; not. brahmanical student.
megha [obj. mih] m. rain cloud — v. [11] pr. r. (meghāyate) to become covered with clouds.

Meghadūta [dūta] m. lit. np. of the Meghadūta "The Messenger Cloud", a famous poem by Kālidāsa in mandākrāntā meter, of the saṃdeśakāvya genre; it is an elegy evoking the heartaches of a yakşa separated from his beloved, having been banished for a year by Kubera for desertion; there are commentaries on it by Mallinātha₁ and Vallabhadeva.

meghanāda [nāda] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of Me ghanāda₁ "Thunderous", son of Rāvaņa and Mando darī; he defeated Indra [Indrajit] and only released him in exchange for the gift of immortality; he was nevertheless killed by Lakṣmaṇa | lit. |K.| np. of the army leader Me ghanāda₁, son of Balāhaka₁.
Meghapuspa [puspa] m. myth. [PP.] np. of Meghapuspa "Cloud Flower", one of the 4 horses of Krishna's chariot, cloud-colored.
megharekhā [rekhā] f. line of clouds. meghavarņa [varņa] amnf meghavarņā which has a color of storm cloud — m. lit. [PT.] np. of the king of crows Meghavarņa — f. meghavarņā bio. indigo (plant).
Meghavahana [vahana] m. hist. n.p. of the Meghavahana princely line; cf. Khāravela.
meghaśyāma | śyāma | amnf meghaśyāmā black as a cloud.
meghasandeśa | sandeśa | mr. bed. n.p. from the megha sandesa, poem by Kālidāsa; cf. Meghaduta.
meghastanita | stanita | n. thunder.
meghodaka [udaka] n. ["cloud water"] rain.
mecaka amnf mecakā dark blue, black — m. black color | eye on a peacock's tail | peacock — n. blackness.
metha var. meṇtha m. elephant keeper.
medhī cf. methi.
médhra [instr. mih] n. penis | ram.
médhracarman [carman] n. foreskin.
médhraśrigī [śrigī] f. bio. bot. Lannea coroman delica, tree with grey bark used in medicine; its fruit is shaped like a ram's horn; syn. jinginī.
Mentha m. elephant keeper.

methí m. post; not. ved. post for tying the sacrificial animal — f. methī id. var. methikā bio. bot. Trigonella foenumgraecum fenugreek, aromatic alfalfa; its seeds rich in mucilage are used as a condiment and in medicine | var. meḍhī id.
methikā [ka] f. cf. methī.
medas [abstr. mid] n. fat.
medasvin [wine] amnf medasvinī fat, slow body.
medin [agt. mid] amnf Medinī who possesses vigor; energetic — m. friend, companion; by tenary; ally — f. cf. Medinī.
Medinī [f. medin] f. fertile land, fertile soil lit. |DKC.| np. of Queen Medinī "Fertile", wife of King Tungadhanvā.
medhinīkara | kara₁ | m. hist. np. of medhinīkara, lexicographer of the 12th century; he is the author of the dictionary of homonyms Nānārthaśabdakośa, also called Medinīkośa.
medhinīkośa [kośa] m. lit. np. from the dictionary of homonyms Medinīkośa; cf. Nānārthaśabdakośa.
medura [midra] amnf medurā fat; onc killer; smooth, soft | thick; dense; full of (i. iic.).
medo iic. medas.
medodosa [dosa₂] m. corpulence, obesity.
medha m. meat juice, sauce, broth | marrow (not. of the sacrificial victim); sap; essence soc. sacrificial victim; animal sacrifice; not. cf. aśvamedha — n. medhas sacrifice | Avestan Mazda.

medhapati | pati | m. soc. | "master of sacrifice" | deity honored by sacrifice. medhapataye soc. [AB.] (ritual mantra) to honor the master of sacrifice (medhapatibhyām for 2 deities, medhapatibhyah for several).
Medhātithi₁ | atithi | m. myth. np. of the sage | ṛṣi | Medhātithi₁ "the Host of the sacrifice", father of Kaṇva | lit. np. of Medhātithi₁, commentator bd. of Manu.

medhā [manasdhā₃] f. intellectual vigor, intelligence; prudence, Wisdom | pl. medhās opinions myth. np. of medhā "Wisdom", daughter of Dakṣa, one of the wives of Dharma — v. [11] pr. (medhayati) to be quick-witted.
medhāvat |vat| amnf medhāvatī intelligent; wise, prudent.

medhāvín |vin| amnf Medhāvinī₁ intelligent, clever; wise, wise — m. scholar, teacher; syn. paṇḍita — f. Medhāvinī₁ myth. np. of Medhāvinī₁ "Learned", epith. of Brāhmī | lit. [Ratnāvalī₁| np. of Medhāvinī₁ "Cheeky", mynah who overheard the conversation between Sāgarikā and Susamgatā, and who repeats it to King Udayana.

medhāsūkta [sūkta] n. bed. [TA.] np. from the Vedic hymn Medhāsukta. yaśchandasāmṛṣabho viśvarūpaḥ om chandobhyo'dhyamṛtātsambabhūva sa men dro medhayā spṛṇotu | amṛtasya devadhāraṇo bhūyāsam | śarīram me vicarṣaṇam | jihva me madhumattamā | karṇābhyāṃ bhūriviśrutam | brahmaṇaḥ kośo'si medhayā'pihitaḥ | śrutam me

gopāya | om śāntiḥ śāntiḥ | Om, universal hymn, best among all hymns, which emanated from the eternal; he, the superior, delivers me through intelligence; O divine support of the eternal, I give you thanks; let my body be exercised, let my tongue become sweet, let my ears hear all knowledge; let my intelligence receive this reservoir of brahman, let this knowledge protect me.
medhira [medhara] amnf medhirā véd. wise, intelligent; is said of Varuna, Indra, Agni.

medhya [medhaya] amnf medhyā full of sap, vigorous | fit for sacrifice; pure | intelligent. krośamātram tato gatvā bhrātarau rāmalaksmaņau | bahūnmedhyānmṛgānhatvā ceraturyamunāvane || [Rām.] Having traveled a league, the two brothers Rāma and Lakshmana went to the woods by the Yamunā where they killed many vigorous animals.
médhra [instr. mih ] n. penis — m. ram.
médhracarman [carman] n. foreskin.
médhraroga [roga] n. med. venereal disease.

Menakā f. myth. Vedic np. of the nymph [apsaras] Menakā; Indra asked her to seduce the sage [ṛṣi] Viśvāmitra, to distract him from his penances which threatened the gods; she bore him to Sakuntalā. niyamavighnakāriņī menakā nāma apsarāh presitā The nymph Menakā was sent to oppose asceticism.

menā f. ved. woman; female animal | myth. np. of menā, daughter of Mount Meru, wife of Himavān; [Rām.] she is mother of Gangā and UmāPārvatī; or [Vāmanapurāṇa] she is mother of Rāgiṇī, Kutilā Sarasvatī₁, Kālī, and Sunābha | myth. [RV.] epith. of Indra who became wife of Vṛṣaṇaśva.
meya [pfp. [1] mā₁] amnf meyā measurable.

Meru m. myth. np. of Mount Meru, a fabulous mountain, in the center of Jambudvipa, and therefore at the center of the World; an immense Jambu tree crowns it; [Mah.] it rises to 84,000 steps [yojana]; the Ganges falls from the heavens there to subdivide into 4 rivers in the 4 directions; the guardians [dikpāla] of the directions reside there; its slopes are gold in the East, silver in the West, crystal in the Southeast, and agate in the Northwest; it has 4 peaks, the 5th having been cast into the sea by Vāyu to form the island of Lankā; on its slopes are Svarga, the paradise of Indra, and the abodes of the 33 gods |trayastrimśa|; Brahmā reigns at its summit; cf. Sumeru | myth. np. of Meru₁, a cakra vartin.
merutunga | tunga | mr. hist. n.p. of the Jain pontiff Merutunga (early 14th century); we owe him the Pra bandhacintāmani.
meruprastāra | prastāra | m. math. Pascal's triangle (invented by Pingala₂, explained by the commentary of Halāyudha₁).
mela [act. mil] m. meeting, contact | pilgrimage; cf. kumbhamela — f. melā society, company.

melaka [ka] m. meeting, gathering | soc. [Tantra] union with a yogini | phil. | Abhinavagupta | indes incriptible mixture of Shakti and Shiva resulting from their supreme union [saṃghāṭa]; cf. visarga. melakam kr to assemble.
melana [act. mil] n. meeting, gathering.
melāp [ca. mil] v. [10] pr. (melāpayati) to make someone meet with someone from another g. .
melāpa [act. That. millet] m. meeting.
melāpaka [ka] m. meeting, gathering; conjunction | ast. conjunction of planets | soc. Tantral union with a yogini.
meṣá [agt. miṣ] m. ["the one who competes"] ram; sheep | astr. zodiac sign [rāśi] of Aries; cf. meṣasaṃkrānti — f. meṣī sheep.
meṣákambala [kambala] mn sheepskin serving as a blanket or jacket.

meṣakukkuṭalāvakayuddha [kukkuṭalāvaka yuddha m. soc. the fight of rams, roosters or partridges. meşakukkutalāvakayuddhavidhi [vidhi] f. soc. the organization of animal fighting, one of the 64 arts [kalā]. meşapāla [pāla] m. shepherd.
meṣasaṃkrānti [saṃkrānti] f. passage of the Sun in the sign of Aries, in mid-January; it marks the new year in Bengal and Orissa.
meha [obj. mih] m. urine | med. urinary disease; diabetes. meham kr to urinate.
méhala [la] amnf mehalā which has the smell of urine — m. smell of urine.
méhana [act. mih] n. penis | urinary tract urine; micturition.
mehin [agt. mih] amnf mehinī who urinates — m. feline.
maitrá [*mitra] amnf maitrī Friendly — n. friendship || pali metta. sarvabhūtānām maitra friend of all creatures.
maitraka |ka| n. friendship | hist. np. of the maitraka dynasty, which reigned in Vallabhī from the 5th to the 8th centuries.
maitrāyaṇa [ayana] n. good treatment, benevolence — m. soc. name of a school of the Yajurveda — f. cf. maitrāyanī.

maitrāyaṇīya [īya] m. soc. name of a school of the Yajurveda, named after Maitri; syn. maitrāyaṇa — n. [Maitrāyaṇīyagṛhasūtra] lit. np. of the Maitrāyaṇīyagṛhasūtra, Vedic manual of domestic rites; also called Mānavagṛhasūtra.

Maitrāyaṇī [f. maitrāyaṇa] f. lit. np. of the Maitrāyaṇī saṃhitā, late esoteric lesson [upaniṣad] of the maitrāyaṇa school; it is part of the black Ya jurveda | soc. community of brahmins originating from Pañcāla, having migrated to Gujarāt and northern Mahārāstra.
maitrāyaṇīsaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. np. of the Maitrāyanīsamhitā, text of the Kṛṣṇayajurveda.

maitrāvaruņa [*mitrāvaruņa] m. soc. name of the priest first assistant to the hotr; syn. praśāstr myth. np. of Maitrāvaruna or Maitrāvaruni "descended" from mitra and Varuna", epith. of Agasti and Vasistha — m. maitrāvaruņi id. — f. maitrāvaruņī myth. np. of maitrāvaruņī, epith. of Arundhatī "wife of Vasistha".
Maitri m. lit. np. of Maitri, presumed author of the Maitrāyanī.
maitryupaniṣad [upaniṣad] f. bed. n.p. of the Maitryupanisad; cf. Maitrāyanī.
maitrī [f. maitra] f. friendship; benevolence | phil. brotherhood, one of the four moral qualities | brahmavihāra | myth. np. of maitrī, friendship personified, daughter of Dakṣa, wife of Dharma.
Maitrīpa [pa₂] m. hist. np. du phil. bd. Maitrīpa (~1007~1085), author of the Tattvaratnāvalī.

maitreya [*mitraīya] amnf maitreyī Friendly — m. bd. np. of the bodhisattva maitreya, "the Friendly" Buddha of the future; he reigns over the tușita heaven; he is depicted with a stūpa in front of his jațāmukuța headdress, and holding in his hand a sacred water pot [kumbha] | lit. np. of the sage maitreya₁, student of Parāśara in the Viṣṇupurāṇa; [BhP.] he taught divine cosmology to Vidura lit. np. of the jester [vidūṣaka] maitreya₂ in the play Mṛcchakaṭikā | hist. np. of the philosopher bd. maitreya₃ (5th century); Asanga was his student; She is attributed the Yogācārabhūmi soc. declassed caste; cf. maitreyaka — f. maitreyī phil. np. of maitreyī "Friendly", wife of Yājñavalkya.
maitreyaka [ka] m. soc. mixed caste; said of a descendant of a vaideha man and an ayogavī woman; their function is to sing the praises of the powerful and to ring the bell at dawn.
Maitreyanātha [nātha] m. hist. n.p. from the master comics. Maitreyanātha, author of the Abhi samayālankāranāmaprajnāpāramitopadeśaśāstra.
Maitreyaparipṛcchā [paripṛcchā] f. bd. n.p. of the Maitreyapariprechā "Questioning of Maitreya", section of the Pañcavimsatisahasrikā Prajñāpāramitā.

Maithila [*Mithila] amnf Maithilī rela tif à Mithilā — m. inhabitant, king of Mithilā | geo. Maithila, one of the five countries of northern India [pañcagauḍa]; mod. Bihār — f. Maithilī language spoken in Mithilā; this literary language reached its peak in the 14th-15th centuries with Vidyāpati₁ | myth. |Rām.| np. of Maithilī, epith. of Sītā, daughter of Jana karāja, "princess of Mithilā".
maithuná [*mithuna] n. union, association; marriage | coupling, copulation, coitus.

maināká [*menāka] m. myth. np. of Maināka, son of Himavān and of menā; he personifies a mountain north of Kailāsa; when Indra cut the wings of the mountains, he was the only one to keep his own; the asura Krauñca is his son.
mairāvaṇa m. myth. n.p. of the rākṣasa Mairāvaņa. mairāvaņacaritra [caritra] n. bed. n.p. from the Mairāvaṇacaritra "History of Mairāvaņa", text attributed to Jaimini.
maireya [*mīraya] mn alcoholic beverage, not. based on rum [āsava].
maireyaka [ka] mn id.
moka [obj. muc₁] n. skin of an animal.
moktavya [pfp. [3] muc₁] amnf mok tavyā which must be released | which must be renounced | which must be thrown (against (loc. acc.prati)).
moktr [agt. muc₁] amnf moktrī that releases, that liberates.

√ [related to muc₁] v. [10] pr. (mokṣayati) pp. (mokṣita) to free, to deliver from (abl.) — v. [1] pr. r. (mokṣate) to free oneself, to deliver oneself from acc. . aham tvā sarvapāpebhyo moksayisyāmi mā śucah [BhG.] Do not grieve, I will free you from all sins.
mokṣa [act. mokṣ] m. liberation, abandonment | phil. deliverance, salvation; ultimate goal of orthodox doctrine.
mokṣada |da| mr. myth. n.p. from mokṣada, aspect of Visnu "granting liberation".
Mokṣadharma [dharma] m. lit. np. of the Moksadharma "Justice of salvation", section of the Sāntiparva of the Mah. dealing with the philosophy of liberation.
mokṣamūla [mūla] n. foundation of liberation.

Mokṣamūlara [ra] m. hist. np. of Mokṣamūlara "Source of liberation", Sanskritization of the name of Max Müller, Germanic linguist, philologist and Indologist established in England (1823–1900), first editor of the Rigveda.

mokṣopāya [upāya] m. phil. means of deliverance lit. np. of the Moksopāya or Moksopāyaśāstra "obtaining liberation", important or vrage (30000 stanzas [śloka]) of Kashmira Shaivism of the 10th century, of unknown author; it foreshadows the Yogavāsiṣṭha which derives from it; its sections are named Utpattiprakarana, Vairāgyaprakaraņa, Mumukṣuvyavahāraprakaraṇa, Sthitiprakarana, Upaśamaprakarana, Upaśāntiprakaraņa, and Nirvāņaprakaraņa.
Mokṣopāyaṭīkā [ṭīkā] f. bed. n.p. of the Moksopāyatīkā, commentary on the Moksopāya due to Bhāskarakantha (end of the 17th century).
moksana [act. moks] n. obtaining liberation; the act of liberating.
mokṣita [pp. mokṣ] amnf mokṣitā released.

mogha [agt. muh] amnf moghā vain, useless, ineffective, disappointing; erroneous, absurd; abandoned. moghīkṛ to render vain, frustrate; disappoint. moghībhūta rendered vain or useless. tasmāt tasyāḥ kumudaviśadānyarhasi tvam na dhairyān moghīkartum cațulaśapharodvartanaprekṣitāni [MD.] Thus do not allow yourself, through excessive seriousness, to ignore her glances, bright as the night lotus, made of the leaps of her graceful carp.
moc [ca. muc₁] v. [10] pr. (mocayati) to set free, to untie; to free from (abl.).
mocaka [agt. muc₁] amnf mocikā who liberates, who emancipates — m. ascetic, renunciant.
mocana [agt. muc₁] amnf mocanī ifc. that which releases from | that which throws, that which casts — act. n. release; act of unhitching (a cart) — ifc. emission of (iic.); abandonment to (iic.).
mocanīya [pfp. [2] muc₁] amnf mo canīyā which must be released.
moṭṭāyita n. [nāṭya] absorption in the thoughts of the lover when his name is mentioned, one of the 10 means of seduction [hāva] of the woman.
mod [ca. mud₁] v. [10] pr. (modayati) to rejoice, to amuse.
moda [act. mud₁] m. joy, pleasure.

modaka [agt. mud₁] amnf modikā ifc. which rejoices (iic.) — obj. n. sweet, confection; not. rice (or semolina) ball flavored with coconut and cardamom and caramelized; Ganesa is fond of it, and it is prepared to celebrate ganeśacaturthī.
modakapriya | priya | amnf modakapriyā who loves sweets | myth. epith. of Ganesa "Gour mand".
modata [imp. mud₁] ind. Rejoice!
modana [agt. mud₁] amnf modanā ifc. that rejoices (iic.) — act. n. rejoicing.
modayat [ppr. That. mud₁] amnf mo dayantī rejoicing — f. cf. moddantī.
moddantī [f. modayat] f. organic. ["joyful grass"] bot. Trachyspermum roxburghia num, umbellifer used in medicine | var. mo dayantikā id.
modin [agt. mud₁] amnf modinī who rejoices, happy — ifc. who rejoices (iic.). bālamodinī f. children's story.
moṣa [agt. muṣ₁] m. thief | theft; larceny.
moh [ca. muh] v. [10] pr. (mohayati) pp. (vi mohita) to drive mad, to lead astray.

móha [act. muh] m. failure, fainting, syncope | Illusion, bewilderment, confusion, error; stupefaction; hallucination, madness phil. bewilderment due to attachment to the phenomenal world; cf. māyā. moham gam to faint.
móhacūdottara [cūdāuttara₁] n. bed. n.p. from the Mo hacūdottara, text on the architecture of śaiva temples and the installation of the linga .
móhamudgara [mudgara] m. lit. np. from the Mohamud gara "Hammer to strike error", poem attributed to Sankarācārya; it is also called Bhajagovindas totra.

móharājaparājaya [rājaparājaya] m. lit. np. from Moharājaparājaya "Defeat of the Illusion King", a Jain drama by Yaśaḥpāla (Gurjara, 12th century); it is an allegory about the conversion to Jainism of King Kumārapāla.

Mohana [agt. muh] amnf mohanī that which leads astray, that which troubles the mind, that which drives mad — act. n. mental disturbance | Enchantment | pleasure of love | myth. np. of Mohana "Enchantment", name of one of the five arrows of Kāma [puṣpabāṇa] — m. bio. bot. Datura inoxia, a nightshade plant whose root contains a hallucinogenic drug; cf. dhattūra— f. mohanī myth. "She who leads astray", one of the 9 forces [śakti] of Kāma — f. Mohanā geo. np. of the Mohanā river, which joins the Nīlāñjanā to form the Phalgu.
mohita [pp. ca. muh] amnf mohitā stunned, confused, misled, deceived. kāmam mohita blinded by passion.

mohin [agt. muh] amnf mohinī who confuses, who deceives, who leads astray — f. mohinī myth. np. of mohinī "Enchantress", feminine form as sumée by the magic of Vișnu to take back the elixir of life [amṛta] from the demons [asura] who had stolen it, and give it to the gods [deva] to immortalize them, during the churning of the primordial ocean [kṣīrodamathana]; even Shiva fell in love with it; cf. Hariharaputra.
mauktika [*muktāika] n. pearl.
maukha [*mukha] amnf maukhā relating to the mouth; oral | based on oral instruction.
maukhara [*mukhara] m. soc. n.p. of the maukhara breed.

Maukhari [*mukharai] m. patr. | hist. np. of the śaiva Maukhari dynasty of kings of Kanyākubjā (6th century); it succeeded in North India the nasti Gupta dynasty and was followed by the reign of Harşa; cf. Grahavarmā.
maukharya [*mukharaya] m. act of being ba vard or noisy; malfeasance | insult, defamation, slander.
maugdha [*mugdha] n. simplicity, innocence; inexperience, naivety | feminine charm, grace; cunning (not. asking a lover to say what is already known).
maujavata [*mūjavata] amnf mauja vatī originating from Mount Mūjavān | soc. qualifies not. a renowned soma.
mauñjá [*muñja] amnf mauñjī in wicker — m. reed leaf muñja — f. cf. mauñjī.
mauñjī [f. mauñja] f. braid of three reed leaves; not. ascetic belt, sacred cord.
mauñjībandhana [bandhana] amnf mauñjībandhanā who wears the grass cord muñja — n. soc. wearing the grass cord muñja.
maudgá [*mudga] amnf maudgā mixed with beans.
Maudgalya [*mudgalaya] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the ascetic Maudgalya "of the mudgala country"; his wife is Indrasenā₁; cf. Mudgala₁.

Maudgalyāyana [*Mudgala₁ āyana] m. hist. patr. of Maudgalyāyana or Mahāmaudgalyāyana, disciple of the Buddha renowned for his accomplishment in magical powers; he was said to read thoughts, speak with spirits, pass through walls, etc.; he died assassinated | pali Mahāmoggallāna.
mauna [*munia] n. asceticism, state of muni; silence, vow of silence.
maunavratā [vrata] amnf maunavratā who has taken a vow of silence.
maunin [maunain] amnf mauninī silent; mute.
maurya [*muraya] m. hist. np. of the maurya dynas, founded by King Candragupta | pl. mauryās The kings of the maurya dynasty.

maurva [*mūrvā] amnf maurvī made of hemp — f. maurvī bowstring (made of hemp) | soc. ascetic's belt; syn. mekhalā | myth. np. of maurvī, daughter of King Muru; she married Ghatotkaca and had Barbarīka.

maula [*mūla] amnf maulī from roots (not. poison) | antique, immemorial, ancient (not. custom) | hereditary (not. office) | aboriginal, in digene, autochthonous — m. soc. minister having inherited his office from family.
mauli [*mūlai] m. head, summit; principal, chief | diadem, crown; crest; chignon | lock of hair reserved after tonsure; syn. cūdā. maulau nidhā to place on the head; to receive with res pect.
maulimani | mani | m. soc. ornamental turban of the kuṣāṇa nobility, featuring a large circular cockade | hair brooch adorned with a gem.
mauliká [*mūlaika] amnf maulikā who produces roots | who pulls up or sells roots | gram. derived from a root | soc. inferior; opp. kulīna — m. root seller.
Mausala [*musala] amnf mausalā relating to the club.
mausalaparvan | parvan | n. bed. n.p. of Mausala parva, 16th book of Mah., “(from combat) to mass”.
mauhūrta [*muhūrta] m. astrologer.

mauhūrtika [*muhūrtaika] amnf mauhūrtikā momentary, fleeting | related to a particular time | skilled in astrology — m. astrologer | pl. myth. np. of the Mauhūrtikās; cf. Muhūrtās. āyuhpraśne dīrghamāyurvācyam mauhūrtikairjanaih | jīvanto bahumanyante mṛtāḥ prakṣyanti kam punaḥ | [Nīlakaṇṭha₁] When questioned about longevity, the astrologers predict a long life to come; the people remaining alive will be filled with admiration, and the dead will ask no questions. ॰দ্ম mna gram. form of neuter adjectives and nouns.
√ਸ਼ਾ mnā [related to man] v. [1] pr. (manati) aor. [6] (amnāsīt) pp. (mnāta) pf. (ā) [unused without pf.].
mradas [abstr. mrd₁] n. gentleness.
mradiman [mrduman] m. gentleness.
mradistha [super. mrdu] amnf mradisthā the sweetest.
mradīyas [compar. mṛdu] amnf mradīyasī softer.
√ mred ca. (mredayati) pf. (ā) [unusual without pf.].
mla [agt. mlā] ifc. amnf mlā dejected, depressed.
√ਸ਼ਾ mlā v. [4] pr. (mlāyati) pp. (mlāna) pf. (bet) to wither, to wither | to be dejected, to be melancholy || gr. μαλακος; fr. melancholy.
mlāna [pp. mlā] amnf mlānā faded, withered languid, dejected, melancholic.

mlāni [act. mlā] f. fading, withering; decline, decay | depression, melancholy, sadness | decrease, decline; disappearance | impurity, filth; vileness. ਢਿੱষ mliṣṭa var. mlecchita [pp. mlecch] amnf mliṣṭā (language) incomprehensible — n. foreign language.
√ mluc v. [1] pr. (mlocati) pp. (mlukta) pf. (pra) to settle; to rest.

√ mlecch v. [1] pr. (mlecchati) pft. (mimlec cha) aor. [5] (amlecchīt) pp. (mlecchita, mliṣṭa) to speak incomprehensibly; to babble. na mlecchet one should not use the language of barbarians. nāryā mlecchanti bhāṣābhiḥ [Mah.] Aryans do not speak in jargon.

mlecchá [agt. mlecch] m. barbarian non-Arya; foreigner; outcaste; infidel | ignorance of Sanskrit; fault, barbarism | pl. mlecchās The barbarians, The foreigners. gomāmsakhādako yastu viruddham bahubhāsate sarvācāravihīnasya mleccha iti abhidhīyate [Baudhāyana] He who eats cow, who speaks with hostility and whose entire behavior is vulgar, is called a barbarian.
mlecchayajña [yajña] m. soc. [Bhaviṣyapurāṇa] massacre of foreigners offered as sacrifices.
mlecchasamparka [samparka] m. soc. contact with a foreigner (or a Hindu who has crossed the ocean); this prohibition must be expiated.
mlecchita var. mliṣṭa [pp. mlecch] amnf mlecchitā (language) incomprehensible — n. foreign language.
mlecchitavikalpa [vikalpa] m. knowledge of foreign languages, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.
noted it. the number 1; cf. kaṭapayādi.

ya₁ [m. yad] pn. relative m. Who, that || lat. is, ea, id. yaḥ kaścit whoever, Whoever. yasmāt conj. since, because, for, hence, as a result of which; so that. yena conj. where; so that. yo yaḥ all those Who, whatever ... that. yo 'ham me Who. ye ke ca any persons.
ya₂ [agt. yā₁] ifc. amnf yā Who goes towards, Who seeks.

ya gram. (with vṛddhi of the theme) form of possessive a. (belonging to, about, deriving from) form of verbs or conjunctions (class 10) | form of abstract quality sn of an a. | form of past participles with passive sense of obligation, necessity or possibility | form of intensives of repetition; cf. yan | (pej.) in a roundabout or sloppy way.
yak nota. gram. modifier [vikaraṇa₂] of passive formation | gram. primary affix [kṛt₂] of the ppr. ps. (ex. kriyamāṇa).
yakan [related to yakṛt] n. [nom. acc. yakṛt] liver.
yakāra [(ya)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'ya'.
yákṛt n. liver.

yakṣá m. myth. spirit, supernatural being; genie endowed with magical powers; not. servant of Ku bera and guardian of his treasures; tutelary genie; the yakṣās, rustic genies, represent the chthonic forces producing mineral treasures, precious metals and precious stones; they are represented corpulent and with a large belly [kumbhānḍa]; Su ketu is their king, Alakā their capital; the yakṣās are invoked by caravans for the protection of the journey; one can be possessed by a yakṣa, or pretend to be in order to dismiss an unwelcome suitor; they are often associated with a sacred tree; cf. vṛkṣakā, śālabhañjikā, Tāṭakā — f. yakṣī myth. female yakşa, woodland nymph | pali yakkha.
yakṣagraha [graha] m. soc. [Tantra] possession by a genie.

yakṣápraśna [praśna] m. lit. [Mah.] np. from the Yakṣapraśna, an episode from the Vanaparva; at the end of their 12 years of exile, the Pāṇḍavās meet a Brahmin who cannot perform his Vedic rituals because a deer has taken his aranī in its antlers; while searching for the deer, Yudhisthira is thirsty; Nakula goes to a lake to get water, where a crane |baka| tells him that the water will be poison if he does not answer her questions; Nakula drinks it, and dies immediately; his twin Sahadeva suffers the same fate, then Ar juna, and finally Bhīma; Yudhiṣṭhira, going to search for them, arrives at the lake, and asks the crane to question him; The crane turns out to be a genieyakṣa, who poses 18 philosophical questions; Yudhisthira having answered correctly, the yakşa finally identifies himself as Dharma and promises them protection during their year of incognito |ajñātavāsa|.
yakṣiṇī [in] f. myth. syn. yakṣī.
yákṣma m. med. consumption; pulmonary disease, not. tuberculosis | var. yakşman id. yakşmin [in] amnf yakşminī tuberculous.
yan nota. gram. Mark of the intensive or frequentative. yananta anta m. gram. Intensive or frequentative form of a root.
yanantaprayoga [prayoga] m. gram. use of the frequentative or intensive.

√ yaj₁ v. [1] pr. (yajati) pr. r. (yajate) pft. (iyāja) aor. [4] (ayākṣīt) aor. [3] (ayīyajat) fut. (yakṣyati) pp. (iṣṭa₂) abs. (iṣṭvā) ppr. r. (ya jamāna) inf. (yaṣṭum) pf. (pari, pra) to offer one's sacrifice, to sacrifice (for another) | to honor a divinity (acc.) with a sacrifice (i.) | to offer as a sacrifice (acc. i.) | to sanctify a place (acc.) (by a sacrifice (i.) — pr. r. (yajate) to offer a sacrifice (for one's own benefit) | to be sacrificed | to be honored with a sacrifice — ca. (yājayati) to cause to be sacrificed; to offer the sacrifice to (acc.) — ps. (ijyate) to be sacrificed | to be honored with a sacrifice — des. (yiyakṣati) to desire to sacrifice — intens. (yāyajyāti) to sacrifice repeatedly | gr. o. paśunā rudram yajate he sacrifices an animal to Rudra. svargakāmo yajeta He who wants to go to Heaven must offer a sacrifice.
yaj₁ [agt. yaj₁] ifc. mf Who sacrifices to iic. ; Who honors (iic.).
yajat |ppr. yaj₁| amnf yajantī who sacrifices; sacrificing.
yajatá [yaj₁ata] amnf yajatā to whom one must sacrifice; adorable; sublime.
yájatra |yaj₁tra| amnf yajatrā which deserves to be honored or worshipped; venerable — m. cf. agniho trin — n. cf. agnihotra.
yajana [act. yaj₁] n. soc. celebration of the sacrifice as a sacrificer, one of the 6 duties |satkarmāni| of a brahmin | place of sacrifice.

yajamāna [ppr. mo. yaj₁] amnf ya jamānī sacrificing, one who sacrifices (for oneself) — m. soc. sacrificer as patron of the sacrifice, as opposed to the priest who performs the rite of sacrifice for his own benefit; he must be previously consecrated by a ritual observance [dīkṣā] of 12
days [dvādaśāha]; after the sacrifice he must pay their fees | dakṣiṇā| to the priests who officiated — f. yajamānī soc. the wife of the sacrificer, who sponsors the sacrifice with him || hi. jajmān.
yajuḥ iic. yajus.
yajuḥsaṃhitā |saṃhitā| f. phil. cf. yajurveda.
yajus [abstr. yaj₁] n. sacrificial formula in prose (to be murmured) | cf. yajurveda. yajuși loc. adv. gram. in a sacrificial formula in prose.
yajurveda | veda | m. phil. np. of the yajurveda, a collection of ritual formulas [yajus], 3rd veda; one distinguishes between the white yajurveda | śukla | and the yajurveda
black | kṛṣṇa| ; cf. Yājñavalkya, Kaṭha.
yajurvedin [in] amnf yajurvedinī soc. specialist of yajurveda; said of lineages of brah manes.

yajñá [act. yaj₁] m. devotion, prayer; sacred act — m. sacrifice; solemn rite | soc. ceremony of offering of a worshipper [yajamāna] performed by a priest, according to the Vedic rite of sacrifice | adoration; ritual veneration | myth. the sacrifice personified, epithet of Vishnu or Indra | cf. mahāyajña. yajñena yajñam ayajanta devāh [RV.] The gods offered the sacrifice as a sacrifice through sacrifice (Huben) through ritual veneration. The gods venerated ritual veneration.
yajñakarman [karman] amnf yajñakarmanī who performs a sacrifice — n. sacrificial ceremony.
yajñakuṇḍa [kuṇḍa] n. soc. hole in the ground at the foot of the Vedic altar | myth. not. that of the altar at Kāmpilya where Draupadī was born from a sacrifice by King Drupada.
Yajñajātaka [jātaka] n. lit. np. of the Yajñajātaka, account of an earlier birth of Buddha, told in the Jātakamālā of Sūra₁.

yajñádatta [datta] m. np. Yajñadatta "Given as an oblation"; prototype character used in rhetoric, like Devadatta | lit. [Mah.] np. of Yajñadatta₁, young ascetic accidentally killed by Daśaratha; cf. Śravaṇakumāra | bd. [Śūraṃgamasūtra] np. of the madman of Śrāvastī who, looking at himself in a mirror, thought he had lost his head.
yajñádattavadha [vadha] m. lit. "Slaying of Yajñadatta", episode of the Rām.
yajñápaśu |paśu| m. soc. animal intended for sacrifice.
yajñábhāga | bhāga | amnf yajñabhāgā who benefits from sacrifice; said of the gods.
yajñavat [yat] amnf Yajñavatī who sacrifices — f. Yajñavatī [DKC.] np. of Yajñavatī, wife of King Samba; she was reincarnated as Avantisundarī₁.
Yajñavalka [valka] m. hist. np. of Yajñavalka, father of Yājñavalkya.
yajñávedi |vedi| f. altar or sacrificial area | var. yajñávedi id.
yajñasūtra |sūtra| n. sacred cord of the high castes [dvija] (worn between the left shoulder and the right side); it symbolizes the right to celebrate a yajña.
Yajñasena |senā| mr. myth. n.p. of Yajñasena, epith. of King Drupada “(who leads) the Holy Army”.
yajñāgni [agni] m. sacred fire.
yajñārtha [artha] m. ritual occupation. yajñārtham adv. for the purpose of sacrifice.
yajñopavīta [upavīta] n. soc. investiture of the sacred gift of the noble castes [dvija] | this cord; cf. yajñasūtra.
yajñiya [yajñaiya] amnf yajñiyā intended or suitable for sacrifice; sacred | var. yajñīya f. yajñīyā id.
yajya [pfp. [1] yaj₁] amnf yajyā to honor; to whom one must offer a sacrifice.
yájyu [yaj₁yu] amnf devotee; pious — m. soc. adhvaryu priest.
yájvan |yaj₁van| amnf yajvarī sacred; act of sacrificing; one who sacrifices, sacrificing | var. yajvin f. yajvinī id.
yan nota. gram. pratyāhāra des semivowels 'y', 'r', 'l' and 'v'.
yat₁á [pp. yam] amnf yatā held, restrained, maintained, controlled, mastered | moderate — n. control of the elephant by the mahout with his feet.
yatat [yat₁] amnf yatatī véd. One who practices; One who strives, diligent, zealous.
yatātman [ātman] amnf yatātmanī master of oneself.
yatendriya | indriya | amnf yatendriyā in control of his senses; chaste.
yatana |act. yat₁| n. effort, exercise.

yatas [adv. ya₁] adv. [suppl. of tatas] from whence; since when; since where, when for, because. yatas ... tatas ... as ... it follows that ... yatah kṛṣṇastato jayah [BhG.] Where Krishna is, there is victory. yatah satyam tato dharmah [SRBh.] Where there is sincerity there is righteous conduct.
yáti₁ [related to yad] conj. [suppl. of tati] as much as; as often as.

yáti₂ [yat₁i] m. ascetic | myth. [RV.] race of ascetics associated with Bhrgu and said to have participated in the creation of the World | myth. [Mah.] epith. of Shiva | myth. np. of yati, a son of Nahuşa.

yáti₃ [act. yam] f. control, constraint | stop, pause | phon. caesura (prose); breath, pause (verse) | var. yatī widow. yatir vicchedah phon. |Chandaḥsūtra| The pause occurs at the juncture between words. yatir jihvestaviśrāmastānam kavibhir ucyate phon. |Chandomañjarī| Poets rest the language at the pause.
yátidharma [dharma] m. soc. duty of ascetics.
Yatidharmaprakāśā [prakāśa] f. hist. np. of the Yatidharmaprakāśā, manual of rules and rites governing the ascetics, due to Vāsudevāśrama.
Yatidharmasamuccaya [samuccaya] m. lit. np. from the Yatidharmasamuccaya of Yādavaprakāśa, manual of rules governing the behavior of ascetics of Brahmanism (11th century).
yátipātra [pattra] n. ascetic bowl.
yativara [vara₂] m. great among the ascetics.
yatiprabala | prabala | amnf yatiprabalā phon. refers to meters where the caesura is predominant.
yatisthāna |sthāna| n. phon. place of the caesura.
Yatyupadeśopanisad [upanisad] f. phone. n.p. from the Yatyupadeśopanisad "Secrets of the doctrine of the pause", small text by Dattila.
yatta [pp. yat₁] amnf yattā exerted, ap applied; engaged, prepared (to (loc. dat. acc. pratiinf.)) | ready; on his guard; prudent | led, guided (not. chariot).

yatna [act. yat₁] m. effort, energy, zeal, care lit. [theatre] moral state [avasthā₂] of the hero of a drama in the Nāṭyaśāstra, gripped by a feverish impulse towards the object of desire. yatnam kr to apply oneself, to make an effort. yatnena adv. with effort, with care. mahatā yatnena adv. with great effort, with great care. yatnatas adv. carefully.
yatnavat [vat] amnf yatnavatī zealous, diligent.

yátra [ya₁tra] adv. where | because. yatrāsau adv. there. yatrakvacana adv. wherever. yatra tatra adv. anywhere. yatra yatra adv. anywhere; as long as. yatra manaḥ tatra mārgaḥ He who seeks finds the way. yatra yatra manastustir manas tatraiva dhārayet tatra tatra parānandasvarūpam sampravartate || [Vijñānabhairava] Wherever the individual's intellect is satisfied, let him concentrate on it; in all cases the true nature of supreme joy manifests itself.

yathā |ya₁thā| adv. as, according to, since, in accordance with; just as, as if — iic. id. [suppl. of tathā] so that, in order that; those Who. na ... yathā not so much ... that. yathā ... tathā as true as ... yathā hi ... tathā hi it is indeed the fact that ... yathā ... tathā kṛ to make sure that, to arrange for ... yathā tathā any way, however one wants lit. indicates an adverbial value in a comment. yathā kathaṃcit in any case; in one way or another. yathā vā or again. yathaiva just as. tad yathā that is how. yathā śakras tathā tvam You are like Sakra.
yáthākāma |kāma| amnf yathākāmā in accordance with his desires.
yathākāmajyeya [jyeya] afnm yathākāmajyeyā to oppress at will.
yathākāmam |kāma| adv. at will, at his own pleasure.
yathākāram |kāra| adv. in such a way; in any way whatsoever. yathākāram aham bhokṣye tathākāram bhokṣye kim tavānena I will eat as I eat, what's it to you?
yathākālam | kāla₁ | adv. at time | according to the circumstances. yathākālam vyavahara behave according to the circumstances.
yathākṛtám [kṛta] adv. gram. as usual; according to usage.
yathākṣaram |akṣara| adv. gram. syllable by syllable.
yathākhyānam [ākhyāna] adv. gram. as has been said.
yathāgatam |āgata| adv. thus come.
yathātattvam [tattva] adv. in accordance with reality.
yathādarśanam [darśana] adv. in accordance with perception.
yathānirdista [nirdista] amnf yathānirdistā as specified.
yáthānyāyam [nyāya] adv. gram. according to the rule; properly. yathānyayam vṛttim vartasva mātṛṣu behave properly towards your mothers.
yáthānyāsam [nyāsa] adv. gram. as specified in the sūtra.
yáthāpūrva [pūrva] amnf yathāpūrvā as before. yathāpūrvam adv. as before | in reverse order; opp. yathottaram. dhātā yathāpūrvam akalpayat [TkS.] The demiurge fashioned (the World) as it was before.
yathāpūrvatva [tva] n. state of being the same as before.
yáthābalám |bala| adv. according to his power.
yathābhagam [bhaga] adv. according to the lot (proper to each).
yáthāyatham [red.] ind. respectively.
yáthāyogam [yoga] adv. according to the circumstances; as appropriate; as required.
yáthāyogena [yogena] ind. as required; according to custom; as usual.
yáthāyogya [yogya₂] amnf yathāyogyā conve nable. yathāyogyam suitably; appropriately.

yáthārtha | artha| amnf yathārthā authentic, true, in accordance with reality | suitable, ap proper, deserved. yathārtham adv. suitably; appropriately; willingly | in fact; in reality; in accordance with the facts. yathārthatattvam adv. in accordance with the facts. yathārthaśāstre in accordance with the scriptures.
yathārthajñāna [jñāna] n. phil. [NN.] correct knowledge.
yathārthajñānakaraṇa | karaṇa | n. phil. cause of correct knowledge.
yathārthajñānasādhana |sādhana| n. phil. instrument of correct knowledge.
yathārthatā |tā| f. the state of being suitable or ap proper.
yathārthānubhava [anubhava] m. phil. [nyāya] authentic knowledge; cf pramāṇa.
yáthārha [arha] amnf yathārhā deserving, worthy of respect | according to its merit; appropriate. yathārham adv. in an appropriate manner; suitably.
yathālakṣaṇam [lakṣaṇa] adv. as indicated | gram. according to the rule, in accordance with the rules (of Pānini).
yáthāvakāśam [avakāśa] adv. at the appropriate place; depending on the available space | when the opportunity arises.
yathāvat [vat] adv. precisely, exactly; appropriately.
yathāvaśám |vaśa| adv. at will; according to his own pleasure.
yáthāvasaram [avasara] adv. according to the circumstances | if the opportunity arises.
yáthāvastu | vastu₁ | adv. according to the circumstances; precisely.
yáthāvastham |avasthā₂| adv. according to the circumstances | in this case, if the same circumstances arise.
yáthāvidhi [vidhi] adv. according to the rule. yathāvidhi devān pūjayet We must honor the gods )1 in accordance with the rule.
yáthāvṛddham [vṛddha] adv. according to seniority. yathāvrddham brāhmanān āmantrayasva Bring in the brahmins according to their seniority.
yáthāvṛddhi |vṛddhi| adv. according to the phase of the Moon.
yathāśakti |śakti| adv. as much as possible, as far as one can; according to one's abilities.
yathāśīlam [śīla] adv. (each) according to his character.
yathāśraddhám | śraddhā₂ | adv. according to his beliefs; by conviction; according to his inclination.

yáthāśruta [śruta] amnf yathāśrutā as it has been heard; corresponding to the information n. local tradition. yathāśrutam adv. as it has been heard; according to the information; as we know | according to the Vedic prescriptions.
yáthāśruti [śruti] adv. according to the Vedic prescriptions.
yathāsukham [sukha] adv. according to one's pleasure; with joy. yathāsukhamākṛḍya after having had a good time.
yathāsthānam [sthāna] adv. each in his place.
yathestam [iṣta₁] adv. at choice, according to one's desire, wherever one sees fit; freely.
yathokta [ukta] amnf yathoktā as it is said | (ifc.) as already mentioned. yathoktam adv. as it has been said (by (i.)); as already mentioned.

yathottara [uttara₁] amnf yathottarā ordered, in order, in succession, one after the other — n. chronology; hierarchy. yathottaram adv. in order; progressively. yathottaram munīnām prāmāṇyam gram. The more recent the sage, the greater his authority (gives priority to Patañjali₁ over Kātyāyana, and to the latter over Pāṇini).
yathodita [udita₂] amnf yathoditā as mentioned. yathoditam adv. as previously stated.
yathoddeśa [uddeśa] amnf yathoddeśā as prescribed. yathoddeśam adv. according to the instructions.
yathoddeśapaksa | paksa | m. gram. viewpoint according to which the operations [sūtra] are explicitly self-sufficient; opp. kāryakālapakṣa.
yathopadiṣṭam [upadiṣṭa] adv. gram. in the measure of usage by a cultivated speaker.

yad pn. relative nm ya₁ f. yā who, that — conj. so that, in order that, so that, because, therefore | [suppl. of tad] namely; if, when. yadapi conj. although, even if. yena because, since; so that, in order that.

yadvat |suppl. tadvat| conj. in the manner that. yat kimca any, anything. yat kimcit any thing, whatever it may be. yat satyam in truth, in fact, to tell the truth. yad astu tad astu come what may. yad vā otherwise, otherwise, however. yo yah any one. yā yā any one. yad vā nah tad vā nah what is ours is ours. yad yad vadati tat tad bhavati everything he says is true. yasyai kasyai ca devatāyai to any deity whatsoever. yah kaścit anyone. yat kimcit var. yat kimcana anything. yāvantah kiyantah however many (among (loc.)). It doesn't matter much. Anything, anyone. All friends without exception. In any country. Come what may. Whatever I do, O Shiva, is entirely at your service.
yádartha [artha] amnf yadarthā which has such an object; which has such a use. yadartham var. yadarthe adv. for what use? why? | because of, since, while.
yádrūpa [rūpa] amnf yadrūpā which has the shape or color.
yadā [ya₁dā] adv. [suppl. of tadā] if, when, while, since. yadā ... kadā ca as many times as possible. yadā ... tadā ... when ... then ...
yadāyadā [suppl. tadātadā] conj. as long as, whenever.

yadi [yad] adv. [suppl. of tarhi] if, in case. yadi kila maybe. yadi ced if. yadi ... tadā ... if ... then ... yadi ... tarhi ... if ... then ... yadi tavad what if? yadi tavad evam kriyate if we did this? yadi nāma if ever. )2 yadi ... vā unless, or rather; however.
yadyapi [api| adv. |suppl. of tathāpi| even if, notwithstanding; although, admitting that.

Yadu m. myth. np. of the Kshatriya hero Yadu, eldest son of Yayati and Devayani, half-brother of Puru and brother of Turvasu; he received the southern Dravidian land as his inheritance; through his son Sahasrajit he is the ancestor of Ekavira and thus of the Haihaya people, and notably of Kartavirya; he is therefore also the ancestor of the Vrishni people and notably of Krishna; his other sons are Krosta, Nala, and Ripu | pl. yadavas myth. np. of the yadavas, descendants of Yadu; notably subjects of Krishna | hist. name of a dynasty of the Deccan; cf. yadavas. yaduvamsha vamsha m. the Yadu lineage.
yádrccha [yadrcchā] amnf yadrcchā spontaneous; accidental; occurring unexpectedly — f. cf. yadrcchā.

yadrcchā [f. yadrccha] f. spontaneity; accident, chance — adv. by chance. yadrcchayā spontaneously; of his own accord by chance, by accident; unexpectedly. yadrcchātas adv. by chance; by accident. kinnaramithunam yadrcchayādrākṣīt He happened upon a pair of kinnarās.

yadrcchāśabda [śabda] m. gram. ["accidental word such"] proper noun, obtained by convention. catustayī śabdānām pravṛttiḥ jātiśabdā guņašabdāh kriyāśabdā yadrcchāśabdāś ca turthāḥ | [MB.] There are 4 word-formation processes: Species nouns, Quality nouns, Verbal forms, and Proper nouns.
yadryác var. yadryañc [yadac] amnf
yadrīcī [m. nom. yadryan; n. nom. yadryak] turned in which direction?
yádvat |yadvat| adv. |suppl. by tadvat| in the way that.

yantṛ [agt. yam] amnf yantrī that restricts, that limits; that prevents access to (loc.) | that establishes; that grants, that bestows — m. that rides (a horse, an elephant); that drives a chariot | driver; guide; chief.

Yantra [instr. yam] n. barrier, lock; reins, guide | tool, machine, device, apparatus, instrument, constraint, force | puppet theater | soc. [Tantra] mystical diagram (serving as a support for meditation, worship, or magic); cf. śrīyantra — v. [11] pr. (yantrayati) pp. (yantrita) pf. (ni) to restrict, repress; to bind. yantrena by force; violently. yantracintāmaņi |cintāmaņi| m. lit. np. from the Yan tracintāmaņi of Dāmodara₁ Bhatta; it describes the magical rites [abhicāra] using the diagrams; also called Kalpacintāmaņi.
yantradhārāgṛha [dhārā₁gṛha] n. bathroom.
yantradhārāgṛhatva [tva] n. act of serving in the bath.
yantrapurusa | purusa | mr. puppet.
yantraprakāra | prakāra | m. lit. np. of the Yantra prakāra, descriptive work of astronomical instruments established at the request of Jayasimha₆.
yantramandira [mandira] n. geo. np. of the Yantra mandira "Instrumental Palace", observatory established by King Jayasimha₆ at Jayapura in 1728 for his astronomer Jagannātha₄.
yantramātṛkā | mātṛkā | f. phil. mystical alphabet associated with a Yantra | soc. association of mystical syllables with a Yantra, one of the 64 arts |kalā|.
Yantrarāja | rāja | mr. astr. n.p. from Mahendra₂ Sūri's treatise Yantrarāja on the astrolabe (1370).
yantrāgāra [agāra] n. mod. workshop, factory.
yantrālaya |ālaya| mr. mod. printing; presses of (iic.).
yantraka [Yantraka] ifc. mf yantrikā instrument, device, tool | link; control; coercion | bandage; attachment.
yantrana |Yantrana| n. restriction, limitation, constraint | guard, protection.
yantrita [pp. Yantra] amnf yantritā res treint, controlled; attached, confined | subject to, obliged by, dependent on (i. abl. iic.).
yantrin [Yantrain] amnf yantriṇī gar dien; oppressor, binder.
√ yabh v. [1] pr. (yabhati) pf. (pra) copulate; fuck; seduce.

√ yam [related to yat₁] v. [1] pr. (yacchati) pft. (yayāma) pft. r. (yeme) pp. (yata) pf. (ā, ut, upa, ni, pra, sam) to hold, brandish; to support, carry; hand to hold, preserve, procure; to restrain, restrain — pr. r. (yacchate) to restrain; to control, restrain, subjugate, master; to control oneself | to offer, confer, grant to (dat. loc.) | to give in exchange for (pratiabl.) — ca. (yāmayati) ca. (yamayati) pp. (yamita) to restrain, restrain, restrain. mārgam yam to open the way to (g.). yatih agnaye balim yacchati the ascetic offers the oblation in the fire.

yáma₁ [act. yam] m. self-control; moral duty, rule, observance; penance; social restraint. Self-control, the first stage of yoga, consists of observing the commandment to practice five virtues: loving-kindness and non-violence [ahiṃsā], sincerity [satya], integrity [asteya], the
Chastity [brahmacarya], and the absence of lust [aparigraha]; cf. astāngayoga. Vācamyamo bhava, hold your tongue!
yámavat |vat| amnf yamavatī in control of his passions — f. yamavatī phon. name of a meter.

yamá₂ [Yama₁] amnf yamā forming a pair — m. twin | myth. np. of Yama "twin", epithet of ManuVaivasvata, son of Vivasvān and Saraṇyū, the first man who became god of Death upon his death; he is depicted red, crippled, holding the noose, the staff, the axe and the dagger; |RV.| he guards the sky of the dead with two dogs with piercing eyes [caturakṣa], Syāma the black one, and Sabala with spotted fur; later, he is judge of

actions [Dharmarāja], and king of the underworld [Yamarāja], where he inflicts torments [yātanā] on the spirits of the dead; Citragupta is his assistant, accountant of the actions of men; the buffalo is his vehicle |vāhana|; he is the guardian |dikpāla| of the direction of the South; astr. he presides over the nakṣatra Bharaṇī (Fly); cf. Dharma, Vaivasvata, Samana | du. yamau myth. the two Aśvinau — f. yamī myth. np. of yamī "Twin", Twin sister of Yama, and his śakti; she became the Yamunā at his Death | math. symb. the number 2 || lat. gemellus; fr. jumeau.

yamaka [ka] amnf yamakā paired — n. bed. [alaṃkāra] gemination, figure of speech of repetition of homophones; Bharata₃ describes 10 kinds: pādānta, kāñcī, samudgata, vikrānta, ca kravāla, sandastaka, pādādi, pādāntāmredita, ca turvyavasita, and mālā — m. of. Yamakau myth. n.p. of Yamakau "the Gemini" (Castor and Pollux), epith. of the nakṣatra of the Punarvasū. yamakam prathamādhuryamādhuryavacaso vidhih |Candrāloka| The yamaka prescribes the repetition of pleasant words in poetic speech. śāradā śāradāmbhojavadanā vadanāmbuje | sarvadā sarvadāsmākam sannidhim sannidhim kriyāt || (Sa rasvatī stotra) that śāradā, with a face like the autumn lotus, who bestows all gifts, always comes to us, to create treasures in the lotus of our mouth.
yamaja [ja] amnf yamajā twin; born twin — m. twin.

yamadaṃṣṭra [daṃṣṭrā] m. lit. [KSS.] np. from the rākṣasa Yamadaṃṣṭra "Bite of Death", who reigned in Sailapura after devouring the legitimate king Vīrabhuja and taking his wife Madanadamstrā; Indīvarasena killed him with his magic sword, and married his sister, the beautiful Khadgadaṃṣṭrā.
yamadarśana [darśana] n. soc. (ceremony of the) vision of Yama.

yamadarśanatrayodaśī [trayodaśī] f. soc. 13th lunar day of celebration of this rite. yamadarśanatrayodaśīvrata n. soc. religious observance of this day; it is said that those who observe it are exempt from appearing before Yama to be judged.
yamadūtá | dūta | m. myth. np. of Yamadūta, mes sager of Yama; he guides the Dead to his judgment throne to decide his fate | myth. class of such assistants.
yamadvitīya | dvitīya | m. soc. second day of the clear fortnight of kārttika, fourth day of the Dīpāvali festival, where sisters invite their brothers to their homes.
yamadhānī |dhānī| f. myth. abode of Yama, underworld.
yámayātanā [yātanā] f. myth. suffering inflicted by Yama on the spirits of the deceased.
yámasmṛti [smṛti] f. bed. n.p. of the Yamasmṛti, code of laws.
yamāntaka | antaka | m. myth. np. of yamāntaka "Yama (god of) Death" | myth. epith. of Shiva as destroyer of Death | bd. np. of the vidyārāja yamāntaka₁ "who kills Death".
yamālaya [ālaya] mn kingdom of the dead.
yámana [agt. yam] amnf yamanī who re straint, who governs — m. myth. epith. of Yama — act. n. restriction; bond, hindrance; cessation.
yamala [Yama₂la] amnf Yamalā twin, doubled, paired — m. singer of a duo | math. symb. the number 2 | du. yamalau twins; pair, couple, duo — f. Yamalā myth. np. of Yamalā, tantric divinity.
yamalārjuna [arjuna] m. du. lit. the two arjuna trees that Kṛṣṇa as a child uprooted because they blocked his passage; they embodied Nalakūbara and Manigrīva cursed by Nārada, and were thus freed.
yamalārjunabhañjana [bhañjana] m. lit. [Pañcarātra] "destroyer of the two trees ar juna", epith. of Kṛṣṇa.
yamalārjunahan [han₂] m. id.
yamita [pp. That. yam] amnf yamita controlled; restrained; restrained. )4

Yamunā [Yama₂] f. geo. np. of the Yamunā River (mod. Jumnā); it joins the Gangā at Prayāga; it is Kālindī "sister of Mount Kalinda"; [Mah.] it parted its waters to allow Vasu deva to save Kṛṣṇa at his birth by carrying him to Yaśodā | myth. np. of the goddess Yamunā who personifies her, eternal form of Yamī; her mount is the tortoise |kūrma|; she is depicted holding a vase of prosperity |pūrṇakumbha|; she is often associated with Gangā; cf. Varuṇa.
yamunācārya |ācārya| m. hist. np. of Ya munācārya, born around 906, second guru of Rāmānuja; cf. Yāmunācārya.
yamunāmuni [muni] m. hist. n.p. from yamunāmuni, epith. of Yāmunācārya.
yamunāstaka [astaka] n. lit. np. of the Yamunāstaka, devotional hymn to the Yamunā of Rūpa Gosvāmī, included in the Stavamālā; Baladeva₁ Vidyābhūsana made a comment on it.
Yamunotrī [uttṝ] f. geo. n.p. from Yamunotrī, a place of pilgrimage in Uttarakhanda, at 3225 m, near the source of the Yamunā.
yamya [pfp. [1] yam] amnf yamyā to control; which must be restricted.
yayā [i. yā₂] ind. by which.

Yayāti [red. yat₁] m. myth. np. of the Yayāti king Nāhuṣa, 5th king of the lunar lineage [somavaṃśa], son of Nahuşa; he is the father of Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru through Sarmişthā and of Yadu and Turvasu through Devayānī; he divided his kingdom into 5 parts for his 5 sons; the youngest, Pūru, received the āryāvarta land in the Center, Yadu received the drāvida land in the South, Turvasu received the homeland of the pure [arya] in the West, Anu received the North, and Druhyu received the land of the enne

mis [druh₂] of the East; hymns of the Rigveda are attributed to him; [VP.] he was fickle, and his infidelities to Devayānī with his servant Sarmiṣṭhā earned him the curse of his father-in-law Śukra to endure old age and decrepitude; he nevertheless obtained permission to transfer the curse to any consenting son; decrepit, he asked his sons to give him their youth; he obtained it from his youngest son Pūru, lived a thousand years in pleasures, then, weary but not satisfied, gave his youth back to his son and ended his time as a hermit; [PP.] he was invited to heaven [svarga] by Indra, who sent his charioteer Mātali to fetch him; He taught him wisdom, and upon his return to earth he reigned so well that his subjects were free from decrepitude; Yama complained of no longer receiving mortals, and Indra asked Kāma to send his daughter Aśruvindumatī to seduce him; to regain the necessary virility he asked his sons to give him theirs, and obtained it from his ca det Pūru; Mādhavī was his daughter | myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā yayāti₁, son of Nahuṣa₁, father of Nābhāga | hist. np. of the yayāti₂ king Kesar₁, who seized power from Kalinga in the 5th century.

yarvāṇa m. gram. [Paspaśā] np. of the fictitious ṛṣi yarvāṇa, who with his alter ego Tarvāṇa pronounced yarvānah tarvānah instead of yad vā nah tad vā naḥ; Patañjali₁ explains that they did not incur demerit, because grammatical correction is only required for sacrificial formulas.
yárhi [yad] adv. [suppl. of etarhi] while, whereas | (followed by tadā, tatra, atha) at that time, as long as, whenever.
yalambara m. myth. np. of the yalambara king of Nepal; he conquered the Kathmandu valley and founded the Kirātās dynasty; he is assimilated to bar barīka.
yáva |agt. yu₂| m. bot. Hordeum vulgare, barley grain; weight measure (= 12 sarṣapa, there are 2 in a guñjā seed).
yávakrīta | krīta | m. myth. np. of Yavakrīta "Bought with barley", son of Bharadvāja; he was killed by Raibhya.
Java Island |dvīpa| m. geo. Java Island. Java Island. The incomparable Java Island.
yávanāla | nāla | m. bot. Sorghum bicolor, sorghum, Indian millet.
yávamat [mat] amnf yavamatī containing barley, mixed with barley — n. ved. abundance of grains.
yavamaya [maya] amnf yavamayī (broth) made from barley.

yavana [agt. yu₂] m. Ionian; Greek; foreigner, barbarian | mod. Persian; Turkish; Arabic; Muslim | pl. yavanās the Greeks, the Persians, the foreigners; not. the Greek astrologers — f. yavanī Greek; woman bar bare.

yavanajātaka [jātaka] n. lit. np. from yavanajātaka, the first work of astrology in Sanskrit; the original (lost) was the translation of a Greek work made by Yavaneśvara in Alexandria in 149; in 269 Sphujidhvaja made a versification of it in 4000 verses; it contains instructions on the making of horoscopes.
yavanadeśa [deśa] m. geo. n.p. from yavanadeśa “land of the yavanās”; Greece, Persia, Bactria; Arabia.
yavanapura [pura] n. geo. Alexandria.
yavanamunda [munda] m. bald Persian (inverted compound).
yavaneśvara [īśvara] m. hist. np. of yavaneśvara "the Greek lord", translator of the Yavanajātaka; he lived in Alexandria at the time of the satrap Rudra karmā₁ (2nd century).
yavanānī [yavanaānī] f. the Greek language, Greek writing.
yavanikā [yavanaika] f. theater curtain.
yavanīya [yavanaīya] amnf yavanīyā relating to foreigners — f. yavanīyā the Persian language.
yavarga [(ya)varga] m. phone. the class of semivowels.
yavāgū [yava] f. barley or rice porridge; it is the food of choice of the kṣatriya .
yavānī [yavaānī] f. inferior quality grains | bio. bot. Trachyspermum ammi, bee-bearing umbel used in medicine.
yaviṣṭha [super. yuvan] amnf yaviṣṭhā cadet; the youngest, lastborn | myth. epith. of Agni (brought to the altar last).
yavīyas [compar. yuvan] amnf yavīyasī cadet, younger | inferior.
yáśas [abstr. aś₁] n. praise, eulogy; glory, fame — amnf yaśás ved. splendid, ex cellent; respected, revered; honored; glorious.

yaśaḥketu [ketu] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of King Yaśahketu "of the glorious standard"; occupied with pleasures, he leaves the charge of the kingdom to his minister Dīrghadarśī; the latter goes on a pilgrimage, meets at sea the vidyādharī Mṛgāṅkavatī secluded in an underground palace by the curse of her father; Yaśahketu joins her, ends her spell, and marries her.

yáśaskara [kara₁] amnf yaśaskarā Who gives glory, Who makes famous — ifc. glorious of, famous for (iic.) — m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the rich brahmin Yaśaskara₁ | hist. np. of the king Yaśaskara₁ (3rd century).

Yaśastilaka [tilaka] m. bed. n.p. from the Yaśastilaka "Mark of Glory", poem in campū style, written by Somadeva₁ Sūri in 959; it narrates the pathetic legend of Yasodhara, king of Avanti, the machi nations of his wife, his death, his rebirths and his final conversion to Jainism; it gives a picture of the cultural life of the medieval Deccan.
yaśastilakacampū | campū| f. bed. n.p. yaśastilakacampū; cf. Yaśastilaka.
yaśasvat [vat] amnf yaśasvatī glorious, famous.
yaśasvin |wine| amnf yaśasvinī glorious.

Yaśoda |da| amnf Yaśodā Who gives glory — f. Yaśodā myth. |Mah.| np. of Yaśodā "Who gives glory", wife of Nanda king of the shepherds; she raised Kṛṣṇa as a child in Gokula; her daughter Yogakanyā was substituted for her.

Yaśodhara |dhara| amnf Yaśodharā bearer of glory | lit. np. of Yaśodhara "Glorious", king of Avanti in the Yaśastilaka hist. np. of Yaśodhara₁, Brahmin of the Bengale of the 13th century, author of the Ayurveda treatise Rasaprakāśasudhākara; he is also credited with the Jayamangalā, commentary on the Kāmasūtra — f. Yaśodharā bd. np. of Yaśodharā, cousin and wife of Prince Siddhārtha.

Yaśodharman [dharman] m. hist. np. of the king of Mālava Yaśodharmā (early 6th century); ally of the emperor Narasimhagupta, he defeated the hūṇa king Mihirakula in 528, and drove the Huns out of India; his son Šīlāditya succeeded him.
yaśodhā [dhā₃] amf That which confers glory.
yaśomitra [mitra] m. hist. n.p. by yaśomitra "Friend of glory", comic philosopher. author of the Abhidhar makośavyākhyā, commentary [tīkā] on the Abhidhar makośa of Vasubandhu.
yaśovat [vat] amnf yaśovatī Who possesses glory; famous.

yaśovarman [varman] m. hist. np. of the emperor Yaśovarmā₁, who reigned over the Ganges valley in the 8th century; his capital was KanyākubjāGādhipura; he was defeated by Lalitāditya at Prayāga in 733; we owe him the drama Rāmābhyudaya | hist. np. of the Khmer king Yaśovarmā₁, son of Indravarmā₁; first king of Angkor, he established his state temple at the summit of Phnom Bakheng; his son Harṣavarmā₁ succeeded him.
yaṣṭāyaṣṭi [red. yaṣṭi] adv. "stick against stick" in unarmed combat.

yaşti f. stick, club; pole; post, pillar, shaft; cane | tree trunk, branch, twig, stem; sugar cane; licorice stick | trunk, human body | thread, rope; necklace — ifc. stem of (2nd century); row of (2nd century) (not. beads) | var. yaṣṭī id. yaştika [ka] m. ["stick-bearer"] brahmin — ifc. row of so many (2nd century) beads — f. yaṣṭikā stick, club. yastikām bhojaya Feed a brahmin.
yastigraha [graha] m. ["stick bearer"] ascetic.
yaştr | agt. yaj₁ | amnf yaştrī sacrificer.

√ yas v. [4] pr. (yásyati) pp. (yasta, yasita) pf. (ā, pra) to heat, to get hot, to boil; to make an effort, to tire oneself — ca. (yāsayati) ca. r. (yāsayate) to make, to strive to | gr. o ; all. gähren.
yasmāt [abl. ya₁] adv. [suppl. of tasmāt] since, because, for, hence, as a result of which; so that.
yasmin [loc. yad] ind. in whom; as long as.
yasmai [dat. yad] ind. to whom.
yasyā [abl. yā₂] ind. of which.
yasyām [loc. yā₂] ind. in which.
yasyai [dat. yā₂] ind. to what.
yáhu amnf ved. quick, agile; strong — m. offspring, child; syn. apatya.

√ yā₁ [connected to i] v. [2] pr. (yāti) pft. (yayau) aor. [6] (áyāsīt) pp. (yāta) fut. péri. (yātā) pf. (anu, apa, abhi, ā, ut, upa, nis, pra, prati, sam) to go, walk, travel, move | to set out, leave, depart; to flee; to spend (time), to pass; to reach, attain, succeed — ps. (yāyate) to be moved — ca. (yāpáyati) to cause to leave, to make go (towards (acc.)) — des. (yiyāsati) to desire to leave. karņau yā to be heard; to be learned. gatim yā to undertake a journey, to walk. diśo yā to go in all directions. dveşyatām yā to be hated. nidrām yā to fall asleep. nidhanam yā to die. patham yā to fall into the domain of. prakṛtiṃ yā to return to one's natural state. śamam yā to calm down. udayam yā to rise (as a celestial body). hastam yā to fall into the hands of. vācyatām yā to incur blame. karnau yā to come to one's ears. utsavād utsavam yā to go from festival to festival. idamapi yāsyati phil. this too will come to pass. yāhi yāhi iti yāti phil. he goes from time to time.
yā₂ [f. yad] pn. relative f. who, that.
yā forms adverbs of manner.
yāga [act. yaj₁] m. soc. oblation, sacrifice; of frande, gift; consecration. yāgāya gacchati he goes to perform the sacrifice.
yāgakantaka [kantaka] m. soc. ["thorn in his crifice" incompetent reciter.

√ yāc v. [1] pr. (yācati) pr. r. (yācate) aor. [5] (ayācīt) pp. (yācita) to ask, to pray, to beg, to petition acc. de acc. abl. | to ask for marriage. sarvalokapitāmaho devārtham visnumupakāram ayācat The ancestor of the Universe prayed to Viṣṇu to help the gods.
yācaka [agt. yāc] amnf yācikā solicitor, petitioner; beggar.
yācana [act. yāc] nf yācanā solicitation, request; marriage proposal; begging. yācanam kṛ to honor a request.
yācanaka [ka] m. solicitor, petitioner; men diant.
yācñā [act. yāc] f. request, demand, solicitation; prayer, supplication | request for alms, begging | soc. marriage proposal.
yāj₁ [ca. yaj₁] v. [10] pr. (yājayati) to make a proud sacrifice; to offer the sacrifice to (acc.).
yāj₁ [agt. yāj₁] ifc. amnf [sg. nom. yāt] who sacrifices to (iic.).
yājaka |agt. yāj₁| amnf yājikā who sacrifices (for (iic.)) — act. f. yājikā sacrifice. brāhmaṇayājakaḥ who sacrifices for a brahmin.

yājana |act. yāj₁| n. soc. performance of the sacrifice (for the benefit of a sacrificer (g. iic.)), one of the 6 duties of a brahmin |saṭkarmāni|. yājanapratigraha m. du. soc. the execution of the sacrifice and the reception of gifts (the two privileges of the brahmins).
yāji [agt. yāj₁] m. sacrificing — act. f. sacrifice.

yājin [agt. yaj₁] ifc. amnf yājinī who sacrificed by (iic.). agnistomayājī who performed the sacrificial rite by agnistoma (to ensure salvation). haviryājī who performed the sacrificial rite with a vegetable offering.
yājuṣa [*yajusa] amnf yājuṣī relating to yajus and yajurveda.
yājña [*yajña] amnf yājñā relating to his sacrifice.

yājñavalkya [*yajñavalkaya] m. hist. np. of the sage |ṛṣi| yājñavalkya Vājasaneya; he is credited with the white yajurveda [vājasaneyin] and the Satapatha brāhmaṇa, and notably the esoteric lesson [upaniṣad] Bṛhadāraṇyaka; it is said that the yajurveda was taught to him by his master Vaisampāyana, but that the latter, feeling offended, asked him to vomit it up so that his other students, transformed into partridges, would regurgitate this "blackened" text [Taittirīya]; he won 1000 cows, each with 10 gold pieces between the horns, by winning the tournament of knowledge organized by King Janakarāja; His wives are Maitreyī and Kātyāyanī₁; cf. Taittirīya, Madhyandina. )7

yājñavalkyasmrti [smrti] f. lit. np. of the Yājñavalkyasmrti, code of laws attributed to Yājñavalkya; it comprises more than 1000 verses in 3 chapters; it dates from the Gupta period; Aparārkayājñavalkīyadharmaśāstranibandha, cf. Bālakrīdā, Mitākṣarā₁.
yājñasenī [*Yajñasena] f. myth. n.p. of yājñasenī, patr. of Draupadī "(daughter) of Yajñasena".
yājñavalka [Yājñavalkya] amnf yājñavalkā composed by Yājñavalkya.

yājñavalkīya [īya] amnf yājñavalkīyā composed by Yājñavalkya — n. lit. epith. of the code of laws [dharmaśāstra] yājñavalkyasmṛti. yājñavalkīyadharmaśāstranibandha [dharmaśāstranibandha] cf. m. Aparārkayājñavalkīyadharmaśāstranibandha.
yājñiká [*yājñaika] amnf yājñikī soc. relating to sacrifice; sacrificial — m. soc. priest expert in sacrifice, ritualist | plant used in sacrifice.

yāta [pp. yā₁] amnf yātā gone, departed; fled; who is (in a place), who has fallen (into such a state) |followed (path); past, elapsed (time) — n. walk, journey, race; pace | place where someone has gone | the past; opp. anāgata.
yātana |act. yat₁| n. revenge; revenge — f. cf. Yātanā.
Yātanā [f. yātana] f. vengeance | torment, torture | myth. sufferings inflicted on the spirits of the dead by Yama | myth. their personification Yātanā "torture". yātanām dā to take revenge.
yātanāgṛha [gṛha] m. torture chamber.
yātu [yā₁tu] m. traveler | ved. sorcerer | pl. yātavas ved. demons/sorcerers causing diseases.
yātr₁ [agt. yā₁] ifc. amnf yātr that goes to (iic.); that seeks (iic.) | that goes in (iic.) (vehicle, horse).
yātr₂ f. [acc. yātaram] wife of a brother of her husband | lat. janitrices.
yātrā [instr. yā₁] f. march, journey, expedition; procession, feast, festival; pilgrimage subsistence way of life, custom; practice, usage; manner, expedient | lit. category of astronomical work.

yātrika [yātrāika] amnf yātrikā relating to a march or expedition — m. traveler; pilgrim — n. march, military campaign | provisions, supplies; stewardship | lit. category of astronomical work; syn. yātrā.
yāthā iic. yathā.

yāthātathya [tathya] n. true condition, fact, truth. yāthātathyam var. yāthātathyena adv. in truth; in fact. yāthātathyatah adv. by the force of circumstances. adhigatayāthātathyāh (sages) having acquired complete knowledge of the true nature of things.

yādava [*Yadua] amnf yādavī myth. of the race of Yadu — m. pl. yādavas myth. mythical royal family of the descendants of Yadu; cf. Kārtavīrya, Vasudeva, Kṛṣṇa | hist. n.p. from the yādavās dynasty to the Mahārāṣṭra, initially a subsidiary of the Western Cālukyās, then independent in the 13th century; their capital was Devagiri; cf. Bhillama, Rāmacandra₁ | hist. epith. of the Hoysala dynasty of Karṇāṭaka in the 13th century | mod. shepherd caste of Bihāra || hi. Yadav.

yādavaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. hist. np. of yādavaprakāśa, advaitavādin master; he lived in Kāñcīpura in the 11th century, and was the first guru of Rāmānuja; he taught the svābhāvika version of the bhedābhedavāda doctrine; he wrote a monistic |advaita| commentary on the Brahmasūtra, and the manual of ascetic rules Yatidhar masamuccaya; he is also the author of the lexicon Vaijayantīkośa; when Rāmānuja broke with him, he converted to his doctrine, came to throw himself at his feet to receive the sacraments, and took the name Govindadāsa.
yādavasūri [sūri] m. hist. n.p. by the astrologer yādavasūri (Gujarat, early 17th century), author of Tājikayogasudhānidhi.

yādavācala [acala] m. geo. np. of yādavācala or Yādavagiri "Mount of the yādavās" 40 km northeast of modern Mysore in Karṇāṭaka; the fort of Melukote was established there in the 12th century by the Hoysala kings; Rāmānuja settled there, founded the Tirunārāyaṇa temple, and the place became a great Vaishnava center of pāñcarātra doctrine; cf. Nārāyaņasvāmī.
yādavācalamāhātmya [māhātmya] n. lit. np. from yādavācalamāhātmya "Greatness of Yādavagiri", chapter of the Iśvarasamhitā praising the sacred site of yādavācalaMelukote.

yādavābhyudaya [abhyudaya] m. bed. n.p. from the yādavābhyudaya "Triumph of the prince of the yādavās", an emotional poem dedicated to Viṣṇu in his avatar Kṛṣṇa, due to Vedāntadeśika; Appayya Dīkṣita commented on it.
yādavīya |īya| amnf yādavīyā relating to the yādavās or to Kṛṣṇa.
yādas m. myth. sea monster; the yādasas are governed by Varuna. yādasām patiḥ myth. Varuṇa. yādasām nāthah myth. Varuna.
yādaspati | pati | m. myth. np. of yādaspati, epith. of Varuna "Master of the oceans".
yādrcchika [*yadrcchaika] amnf yādrcchikī spontaneous; accidental, unforeseen; arbitrary | acting randomly; acting as one pleases.
yādṛś [ya₁dṛś₂] amnf [suppl. of tādṛś] in such a way, similar to, like, just like — amn yādṛśa f. yādṛśī id. — amn yādṛkṣa f. yādṛkṣī id. yādṛśa tādṛśa whoever, the first one who comes along.
yādo iic. yādas.
yādonātha |nātha| m. myth. np. of yādonātha, epith. of Varuna "Master of the oceans".

yāna [agt. yā₁] amnf yānī that leads, that conducts (at the g. rangle angle) (not. route) — act. n. march, journey, expedition; way | phil. soteriological way; cf. devayāna, pitṛyāna | vehicle, act of going (on such mount) | bd. mode of knowledge, path of liberation, doctrine; cf. Hīnayāna, Mahāyāna, Mantrayāna, Vajrayāna | mod. bus — f. yānī che min — f. yānā ifc. journey || pkt. jāṇa.
yāni [nom. pl. yad] ind. which ones.
yāpya [pfp. [1] ca. yā₁] amnf yāpyā that one must get rid of, that one must get rid of med. to cure, that one must relieve (disease) | useless; bad (action).
yām [acc. yā₂] ind. which one.
yāma [act. yam] m. control, coercion; abstinence, asceticism; suppression | Night watch, vigil; third of the night.
yāmala [*yamala] n. pair | lit. category of tantric texts; cf. Jayadrathayāmala, Brah mayāmala, Rudrayāmala.
yāmin [agt. yam] m. ifc. control of (iic.) — f. Yāminī night | myth. np. of Yāminī "Night Watch", daughter of Prahlāda.
yāmuna [*yamunā] amnf yāmunī relating to the river yamunā.
yāmunācārya [ācārya] m. hist. np. of yāmunācārya, grandson of Nāthamuni (11th century); nicknamed Ālavandār ("Conqueror" in Tamil), he preached the doctrine of non-duality

distinguished [viśiṣṭādvaita]; he brought Rāmānuja to Srīranga to continue his work and succeed him as pontiff of the Vaishnava order; he expounded the foundations of viśiṣṭādvaita philosophy in his work Siddhitraya; he is also the author of the Āgamaprāmāṇya, the Mahāpuruṣanirṇaya and the Gītārthasaṃgraha₁; he is also called Yamunācārya and Yamunāmuni.

yāmya [*Yama₂ya] amnf yāmyā relating to Yama | of the South, in the South | to the right; opp. savya — m. right hand — n. astr. epith. of the naksatra Bharaṇī, presided over by Yama | myth. messenger of Yama — f. yāmyā southern region. yāmye var. yāmmyena adv. in the South; to the right. yāmyatas adv. coming from the South.
yāyā [intens. yā₁] f. Wandering | myth. n.p. from yāyā "Wandering".
yāyāvará [vara] amnf yāyāvarā wandering, not made; opp. śālin — m. wanderer | hist. n.p. of Yāyāvara or Yāyāvarīya, patr. of Rājaśekhara — n. soc. state of wandering monk.
yāyin [agt. yā₁] amnf yāyinī ifc. who goes, who walks, who travels to (iic.) | who goes to war against (iic.) | astr. in opposition (planets).
yāva [*yava] amnf yāvā relating to barley, barley-based — m. barley gruel.
yāvaka [ka] n. barley grains.

yāvat [*ya₁vat] amnf yāvatī (as great) as, (as numerous) as, (as much) as — adv. as long as, while, as soon as |during, until (abl.); however, in the interval [suppl. of tāvat] (as long) as, as; (as soon as); (fut. pr.) indicates that the action will take place. yāvatā adv. as long as; as far as. yāvati adv. as long as; as far as. iti yāvat be, that is to say. yāvat ... na as long as ... not, before, until. na yāvattāvat scarcely, as soon as. sūryodayam yāvat until dawn. kiyantamavadhim yāvat until when? yāvajjīvam adhīte he studies his whole life. sarpavivaram yāvat to the snake hole. kārttikāccaitram yāvacchītam Winter lasts from kārttika to caitra.
yāvacchakyam |śakya| adv. as far as possible; as much as can be done.
yāvajjīvam [jīva] adv. throughout one's entire life. )9
yāvatkāmam |kāma| adv. as long as one wants, for as long as desired.
yāvattāvat [tāvat] amnf yāvattāvatī math. unknown, algebraic variable (abbreviated as yā) | linear equation, rule of three.
yāvallayanam |layana| adv. within the limits of available cells.
yāvana [*yavana| amnf yāvanī of the land of the yavanās.
yāvanāla [*yavanāla] m. bio. bot. Andro pogon sorghum; sorghum, Indian millet — f. yāvanālī sorghum sugar.
yāśu n. ved. embrace; not. sexual embrace.
Yāska m. hist. patr. of Yāska, ancient author of the Nirukta, commentary on the Nighanțu (between the 6th and 4th centuries BC); he taught the Yajurveda to his student Tittiri.
yitnu forms a. with an active meaning.
yiyās [des. yā₁] v. pr. (yiyāsati) to want to go.
yiyāsā [act. des. yā₁] f. desire to leave.
yiyāsu [agt. des. yā₁] amnf who wishes to leave or go (towards (dat. acc.)).
√ yu₁ [reli 'e à yuj₁] v. [2] pr. (yauti) pr. r. (yute) v. [6] pr. (yuváti) pr. r. (yuvate) v. [9] pr. (yunāti) pr. r. (yunīte) pp. (yuta₁) pf. (ā, ni, sam) ved. join, unite; hold, attach, bind.
√ yu₂ v. [3] pr. (yuyoti) v. [1] pr. (yucchati) pp. (yuta₂) pf. (ava, pra) to set aside, repel; to separate, exclude — ca. (yāvayati) to cause to exclude | lat. juvo.
yu₃ | yā₁ | ifc. amnf ved. that goes towards (iic.).
yu is a secondary suffix forming agent names.

yugápad [pad₂] adv. ["going hand in hand"] simul tanément (with (i.)). darśanam ganitam caiva yugapad yogasādhakam jn. Observation and calculation used together are effective.

yugam [acc. yuga] iic.

yuj₂ [agt. yuj₁] amnf ifc. harnessed to, which harnesses (iic.); equipped with, joined to, united to (iic.) | math. pair (number) — m. companion, associate | of the. yujau the pair of (iic.).

Yuddha [pp. yudh₁] amnf yuddhā com beaten; conquered, subdued, Vanquished — m. myth. n.p. of Yuddha "Defeated", son of Ugrasena — b. fight, battle | attack (opp. defense [sthāna]) | armed; cf. pancayuddha | astr. opposition of planets — f. yuddhā ifc. attack of; victory over. yuddhīkṛ to give battle, to engage in combat. meşakukkutakurarakapiñjalalāvakavartikāyuddham K. Fights of rams, cocks, birds of prey, pheasants, partridges and quails.

(ā, pra, prati) to fight, to struggle with (i.saha₂) | to attack, to assail | to conquer — des. r. (yuyutsate) to want to fight, to want to conquer. yoddhukāmaḥ who wants to fight. na yotsye |BhG.| (Arjuna) I will not fight.

yudhāmanyu [manyu] m. lit. [Mah.] np. of yudhāmanyu "furious fighter", Pañcāla warrior who protected the wheels of Arjuna's chariot with his brother Uttamaujas; they both perished in the burning of the camp after the victory.
yudhi [loc. yudh₂] iic.

Yudhisthira [sthira] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Yudhisthira "Firm in battle", eldest of the 5 Pandavas, son of the god Dharma and Kuntī; also named Dharmaputra, Dharmarāja, Dharmasuta; he lost his kingdom at dice against the treacherous Sakuni, and went into exile for 12 years with his brothers and their common wife Draupadī; in the 13th year, he hid under the identity of Kanka at the court of King Virāta; he led the army of the Pandavas during the great battle of Kuruksetra; he possessed the nanda and upananda drums; his charioteer was In drasena; he is Ajātaśatru₁ "whose enemy is yet to be born"; After his royal reinstatement, he made a great horse sacrifice [aśvamedha] to subdue all the kings; then he decided to abdicate and renounce the world [tyāga]; he set out for the North, dressed in bark, with his brothers and their common wife; they all died on the way, except him, and he alone obtained permission to go to Heaven with his own body [svargārohaṇa]; a dog accompanied him, which he called his devotee [bhakta]; when Indra came to meet him, he refused to abandon it; the dog revealed itself to be Dharma come to test him | gram. np. from the grammarian mīmāṃsaka Yudhiṣṭhira₁ (20th century). yudhişthirārjunau yudhişthira and Arjuna (dvandva of brothers in order of primogeniture).
yuyu m. horse.
yuyuts [des. yudh₂] v. pr. r. (yuyutsate) to want to fight, to desire to conquer.
yuyutsā |act. des. yudh₂| f. desire to fight, combativeness, pugnacity.

yuyutsu [agt. des. yudh₂] amnf bel liqueux, combative, pugnacious; aggressive, who wants to fight | myth. [Mah.] np. from the karaṇa yuyutsu "Fighter", 101st son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, bastard of Vaishya mother; at the beginning of the war he defected at the call of Yudhisthira and rallied to the cause of the Pāndavās.

Yuyudhāna |related to yuyuts| m. myth. |Mah.| np. of Sātyaki Yuyudhāna "Inclined to battle", friend vrșni of Krșna, and driver of his chariot; he was a student of Drona and a comrade-in-arms of Arjuna; the latter saved his life in battle: when Bhūriśravā had him at his mercy, Arjuna pierced his arm with an arrow, and Yuyudhāna beheaded him; he survived the war, but 36 years later fought with Krtavarmā in the fratricidal battle that ended the yādava line, fulfilling the curse of Gāndhārī.
yuva iic. yuvan.
yuvakhalati |khalati| m. young bald man.
yuvatā [tā] f. youth.
yuvatva [tva] n. youth.
yuvadvandva [dvandva] n. myth. the young divine couple of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vraja.
yuvamahārāja [mahārāja] m. soc. crown prince.
yuvarāja |rāja| m. soc. crown prince.

yúvan amnf yūnī young | strong, well for so much; adult; vigorous — m. young man; young animal | myth. epith. of gods (not. Indra, Agni, the marutas) | soc. patronymic name of a younger son (e.g., Gārgyāyaṇa for the gotra of Garga); opp. vrddha astr. np. of Yuvā "Juvenil", personifying the 9th year of a life cycle [samvatsara] — f. yuvati young girl, young woman | var. yuvatī id. || lat. juvenis; all. jung; ang. young; fr. Juvenil, young.

Yuvanāśva m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Yuvanāśva, son of Prasenajit of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa] (or [Rām.] son of Dhund humāra); he performed many sacrifices [yāga]; having renounced meat, he had the gift of being

extrasensory [parāvaratattva]; he had one hundred wives, but remained childless; he visited the sages in the forest, who organized a sacrifice [yāga] to Indra; they blessed a pot of water intended for his wives with a fertility mantra; the king, being thirsty, drank unintentionally, and ten months later gave birth to a son, Māndhātā, who emerged from his side. )2
yuvayos [g. du. tvad] ind. to the two of you; at the two of you're at your place.
yuvābhyām [i. du. tvad] ind. by you two; for you two; of you two.
yuvām |nom. du. tvad| ind. you two.
yuṣmat [abl. pl. tvad] ind. of you | var. yuşmad gram. pronominal theme of 2nd person. yuşmadīya [īya] amnf yuşmadīyā yours — m. one of yours; compatriot, country.

yuṣmān [acc. pl. tvad] ind. you.
yūka mf yūkā pou.
yūkālikṣa [likṣā] n. sg. (collective) lice and their nits.

yūthanātha |nātha| m. leader of a horde (not. of elephants).
yūthapa |pa₂| m. id.
yūthaśas [śas] adv. in a band; in a herd.
yūthikā f. bio. bot. Jasminum auriculatum, white-flowered jasmine with a sweet scent, used in medicine; syn. sūcimallikā.
yūn cf. yuvan.
yūna |yu₁| n. band, bandage; rope, string.
yūni [yu₁] f. connection; union.
yūpa m. ved. sacrificial post | pillar, post; pal.
yūpadāru |dāru| n. ved. wood of the sacrificial post.

yūparohaṇa [rohaṇa] n. ved. ceremony of ascension of the sacrificial pole [sthānu] during the vājapeya ritual by the sacrificer [yajamāna] and his wife, symbolizing their ascent to heaven; on the pole is placed a dough wheel representing the sun.
