yoktavya [pfp. [3] yuj₁] amnf yoktavyā to unite; which must be concentrated (mind) | which must be practiced, used, prepared | to inflict (punishment).

yoga [act. yuj₁] m. vehicle, equipment; means, method; suitability | contact; union, joining; zeal, care; concentration of mind | soc. mystical experience of divine fusion, enstasis soc. spiritual discipline, practice of yoga; integral yoga [rājayoga] comprises a frugal way of life ensuring self-control [yama₁] through a discipline of spiritual exercises [niyama], and the practice of exercises for mastering the body [hathayoga] and meditation [dhyāna] in order to attain liberation in enstasis [samādhi]; it was codified in the Yogasūtra in 8 disciplines

plines |aṣṭāṅgayoga| | phil. philosophical system of yoga, attributed to Patañjali₂, one of the 6 viewpoints [saddarśana] of orthodox Hinduism; it deals with the inner universe of man or microcosm; it is a theistic version of sāṃkhya |seśvarasāṃkhya| |soc. devotion, a pañcopāsana according to Rāmānuja | gram. etymological meaning of a word (opp. rūdhi conventional meaning) | astr. conjunction | pl. yogās astr. constellation, asterism; there are 12 khayogās, and including the moon 13 cāndrayogās phil. np. of yoga as a viewpoint or

thodoxe [darśana]; cf. saddarśana | astr. the time taken by the sun and moon to travel a longitude of 13° 20'; there are 27 such yogās in a lunar month, corresponding to the nakṣatrāṇi || fr. joug; ang. yoke. yogam i to agree, to lend oneself to. yogatas adv. as is fitting | assiduously. yogāt in accordance with, according to (iic.). yogena adv. as is fitting | in accordance with, according to (iic.). kathāyogena during the conversation. pūrņena yogena adv. with all one's might.

yogakanyā [kanyā] f. myth. [HV.] np. of yoga kanyā, daughter of Yaśodā; she was substituted for Krsna as daughter of Devakī, was therefore put to death by Kamsa, and ascended to heaven as a beautiful young girl.

yogakṣemá |kṣema| mn ved. period of peace )3 (opp. period of war) | well-being, prosperity; security of property, assurance; subsistence | phil. peaceful enjoyment of the fruits of action | of. yogakṣemau acquisition and preservation of property. yogakṣemam vah to provide for, to furnish subsistence for (dat.).
yoga |ja| amnf yogajā produced by yoga or meditation.
yogatārā [tārā] f. astr. main star of a nakṣatra; syn. tārakā.
Yogatārāvalī | tārāvalī | f. bed. n.p. from the Yogatārāvalī of Sankara₁, which deals with amanaskayoga.
yógadanda |danda| m. soc. ascetic staff, given to the brahmacārin during the upanayana.
yogananda [nanda] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of yoga nanda "False king nanda", which was replaced by In dradatta.

yoganidrā [nidrā₂] f. phil. ["yogic sleep"] intermediate state between meditation and sleep; state of consciousness without mental fluctuation | myth. refers to the sleep of VișnuAnantaśāyin between two manifestations | myth. refers to the sleep of Brahmā during pralaya.
yogapatta | patta | m. soc. meditation strap, passed between the knees and back of a meditating yogi | var. yogapattaka id.
yogapattavidhi | vidhi | mr. soc. yogapatta ordination rite.
Yogabīja [bīja| m. lit. np. of the Yogabīja, a treatise on yoga attributed to Gorakṣanātha.
yogabhāṣya [bhāṣya] n. lit. np. of the yogabhāṣya, first commentary on the yogasūtra of Patañjali₂, attributed to Vyāsa₁; cf. Vyāsabhāsya.
yogabhāṣyavivarana [vivarana] n. bed. n.p. from Yo gabhāsyavivaraņa, commentary on the previous one, attributed to Sankara₁.
yogabhraṣṭa [bhraṣṭa] amnf yogabhraṣṭā phil. who has lost yogic grace — m. fallen yogi.
yogamāyā [māyā] f. myth. n.p. of yogamāyā, the divine Illusion resulting from the yoga of Viṣṇu; |BhP.| she made note. the magical transfer of Samkarşana Balarāma.
yogayājñavalkya [yājñavalkya] n. bed. n.p. from Yo gayājñavalkya, haṭhayoga text.
yogayukta [yukta] amnf yogayuktā absorbed in meditation — m. warrior.
yogaratnamālā [ratnamālā] f. bed. n.p. from the yogaratnamālā, tantric work of magic by Nāgārjuna₁ (Gujarat, 12th or 13th century).
Yogarāja [rāja] m. hist. np. of Yogarāja, śaiva scholar of the 11th century, disciple of Kṣemarāja; we owe him a gloss |vivṛtti| of the Paramārthasāra.
yogarūdha [rūdha] amnf yogarūdhā gram. is said of a word which has a fixed conventional meaning preferable to its etymological meaning; (e.g. pańkaja for lotus, goghna for guest).
yogavārttika [vārttika] n. bed. n.p. of the yogavārttika, commentary on the yogasūtra by Vijnānabhikṣu.

yogavāsistha [vāsistha] n. lit. np. of the Yogavāsistha "The yoga according to Vasistha", a phil. [Vedānta] work in the form of a dialogue between Vasistha and his student Rāma, dealing with the means of attaining happiness through liberation [mokṣopāya]; considered as an anexe of the Rām., it is attributed to Vālmīki; it is prior to the 10th century and inspired by the Moksopāya; it contains more than 30000 strophes |śloka|; Abhi nanda made an abridged version of it, the Laghuyogava sishta.
yogavāsiṣṭhasāra [sāra] m. bed. n.p. from Yo gavāsisthasāra, attributed to Vālmīki.
yogavāha [vāha] m. phon. phonemes not dependent on context; opp. ayogavāha.
yogavāhin [vāhin] amnf yogavāhinī who cor pore to oneself — n. solvent; not. soda, mercury.
yogavāhitva [tva] n. (alchemy) quality of soil.
yogavid |vid₃| amnf who knows the right method, who knows what is appropriate | expert in yoga — m. myth. epith. of Śiva.
yogavibhāga [vibhāga] m. dissociation of what has been unified gram. division of a sūtra into two (in order to reinterpret it).
yogaśakti [śakti] f. phil. the power of yoga or divine union.
yogaśata | śata | n. lit. np. of yogaśata, a medical treatise attributed to Nāgārjuna₁.
yogaśataka [ka] n. lit. id.
Yogaśāstra [śāstra] n. science of yoga | lit. np. of the Yogaśāstra, work attributed to Dattātreya.
yogasāra [sārasamgraha] m. lit. np. from the Yo gasārasamgraha "Compendium of the mind of yoga", work of Vijñānabhikṣu explaining the Yo gasūtra and the Vyāsabhāsya.

yogasūtra [sūtra] n. phil. [yoga] np. of the Yo gasūtra, a collection of aphorisms by Patañjali₂ expounding the theory and practice of yoga; it comprises four sections [pāda], the last of which, hostile to Buddhism, is undoubtedly later than the first three; Bhojadeva made the commentary on it Rājamārtaņda | Bhojavrtti |.
yogastha |stha| amnf yogasthā absorbed in yoga. yogasthaḥ kuru karmaṇi [BhG.] Act absorbed in yoga.
yogāgni |agni| m. ardor of yoga.
yogāgnimaya [maya] amnf yogāgnimayī filled with the ardor of yoga.

Yogācāra [ācāra] m. practice of yoga | bd. idealist Buddhist school of Yogācāra using yoga; it developed not. in Nālandā, in reaction to the nihilistic doctrine | śūnyavāda | of Nāgārjuna; cf. vijñānavāda.

yogācārabhūmi [bhūmi] f. lit. np. of the yogācārabhūmi "Foundation of the practice of yoga", detailed bd. text on meditation (4th century); it was composed by Maitreya₃ or by his student Asanga; it has 5 divisions, of which the 1st has 17 sections, the 15th being the Bodhisattvabhūmi.
yogācārabhūmiśāstra [śāstra] n. id.
yogācārin [in] amnf yogācārinī bd. adept of Yogācāra.

yogānanda [ānanda] m. mod. np. of the Bengali mystic Mukunda Lal Ghosh (1893–1952); he became Svāmī yogānanda "Joy of Yoga" in 1914, settled in the United States in 1920, and received the title of paramahamsa in 1935; he is the author of the memoir "Autobiography of a Yogi".
yogānubhūti [anubhūti] f. experience of yoga.
yogāyoga [ayoga] m. of. more or less great adequacy | coincidence.
yogāsana |āsana| n. yoga posture.
Yogeśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Yogeśvara, epith. of Shiva or Krishna "Master of yoga".
yogi iic. yogin.
yogitā [tā] f. the state of being connected with (iic.) connection, relationship.
yogitva [tva] n. fid.
yogipratyakṣa | pratyakṣa | n. phil. yogic perception.
yogīndra | indra | m. "king of yogis", honorific title; cf. Cintāmani₁.
yogīśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of yogīśvara "Lord of the yogi ", epith. of Skanda.
yogin [agt. yuj₁] amnf yoginī [nom. yogī] yogī, practitioner of yoga — f. cf. yoginī. acintyā yoginām gatih The powers of a yogi are unimaginable.
yogini [f. yogin] f. phil. [Tantra] power

divine [śakti]; initially 8 are listed: Mangalā, Pingalā₁, Dhanyā, Bhrāmarī, Bhadrikā, Ulkā, Sid dhi and Samkaţā; later, 64 are listed; cf. mātrkā. ʻyoginīkaula [kaula] m. phil. [Tantra] follower of SaktiBhairava and of the fierce powers [yoginī].

[Ratnāvalī₁] Patr. of Yaugand harāyaṇa, prime minister of King Udayana; full of cunning, he hatched complex intrigues; [Svapnavāsavadatta] he presented Queen Vāsavadattā to Padmāvatī₂ as his sister to ask her for shelter, while spreading the rumor that the queen had perished in a fire; [Pratijñāyaugandharāyaṇa] when King Udayana was tricked into being captured by hunting a fake elephant, he pledged to free him and restore him to the throne in Ujjayinī; Marubhūti is his son.

raktamarica | marica | mr. organic. bot. Capsicum an nuum, chili pepper; syn. katuvīra.
raktamālā [mālā] f. garland of red flowers.
Raktamukha [mukha] m. bed. [PT.] np. of the monkey Raktamukha "with a red snout", victim of the cro codile Karālamukha.
Raktākṣa [akṣa] amnf raktākṣī with bloodshot eyes | horrible, frightening — m. bio. pi geon (with red eyes) | astr. np. of Raktākṣa "Decrepit", personifying year 58 of a life cycle |samvatsara|.

direction | dik|.

raghú [raṃhu] amnf raghvī swift, light, agile — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Raghu "agile", king of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa], son of Dilīpa₂ and Sudakṣiṇā; he is father of Aja, great-grandfather of Rāma; or [Rām.] he is said son of Kakutstha and ancestor of Rāma through his son Pravrddha; he had a lotus-shaped halo [prabhāmaṇḍala] above his head; [raghuvamśa] he conquered the Uni vers, then renounced all his possessions; The young brah mane Kautsa came to ask him for alms to pay his master the exorbitant sum he demanded as gurudakṣiṇā; he went to fight Ku bera to raise the sum, fell asleep dreaming that he would subdue him, and in the early morning was informed that Kubera had made the gold coins rain down into his coffers.
Raghudeva [deva] m. hist. np. of Raghudeva Nyāyālamkāra, logician of the 17th century; we owe him the Padārthakhandanavyākhyā.

raghunandana [nandana] m. myth. np. of Raghu nandana "Joy of (the race of) Raghu", epith. of Rāma | hist. np. of raghunandana₁ Bhatṭācārya, Bengali author of works of dharmaśāstra of the 16th century, born in Navadvīpa; we owe him notably the Smrtitattva and the Tithitattva.

raghúnātha [nātha] m. myth. np. of Raghu nātha "Lord of (the race of) Raghu", epith. of Rāma as ruler of Ayodhyā | geo. np. of the great temple of Raghunātha at Jammu (19th century) | hist. np. of Raghunātha₁ Siromani (1475–~1550), principal Bengali logician of the Na vyanyāya; child prodigy, one-eyed, and arrogant, he was a pupil of Vāsudeva₃ Sārvabhauma and then of Pakṣadhara at Mithilā; he then settled at Navadvīpa, and trained many pupils; we owe to him not. the Guṇakiraṇāvalīprakāśadīdhiti, the Tatt vacintāmaņidīdhiti, the Akhyātavāda, the Nañvāda, the Padārthatattvanirūpana/Padārthakhandana, the Atmatattvavivekadīdhiti, the Kiranāvalīprakāśadīdhiti, and the Dīdhiti hist. np. of Raghunātha₂ Nāyaka, son of Acyutappa, enlightened regent of Thanjavur (1600–1633); scholar, he was poet, composer of pieces in Sanskrit and Telugu, musician, teacher; his master was Govinda₁ Dīkṣita | hist. np. of Raghunātha₃ Pandita, 17th century Maratha scholar, author of the Rājavyavahārakośa | hist. np. of Raghunātha₄ Sarmā, author of the Ambākartrī, commentary on the Vākyapadīya (1980) | hist. np. of the rājput Raghunātha₅ Varmā, author of the collections of popular maxims Laukikanyāyasamgraha and Laukikanyāyaratnākara (19th century).

raghunāthadāsa [dāsa] m. hist. np. of the poet ben gali raghunāthadāsa "Servant of Rāma", (1495– 1586); at the age of 19 he left his merchant family to receive teaching from Caitanya in Purī, before settling in Vṛndāvana; he is one of the six pastors |Gosvāmī|; he composed the Muktācarita and the Manaḥśīkṣā.
raghupañcikā |pañcaka| f. bed. n.p. of the Rag hupañcikā, commentary by Vallabhadeva on the raghuvamśa.
raghúpati | pat | mr. cf. Raghunatha.

rangapūjana [pūjana] n. [nāṭya] consecration of the scene.
Rangarāja [rāja] m. myth. n.p. of Rangarāja, epith. of Rāma or other aspects of Viṣṇu.
rangarāmānuja [rāja] m. hist. np. of rangarāmānuja, phil. śrīvaiṣṇava of the 17th century, author of commentaries on the esoteric lessons |upanisad|.
rangaśāyin [śāyin] m. geo. np. of Rangaśāyī "God of colors resting (on Śesa)", principal idol of Ranganātha; he is represented lying down facing South.
rangāvali |āvali| f. soc. row of colored drawings on the ground in front of a house, not. on the occasion of a festival like Dīpāvali || hi. rangoli.
raṅgita [raṅgaita] amnf raṅgitā colorful; pretty; beautiful.
rangin [agt. rañj] amnf rangiṇī which colors — m. dye; dyeing.

rangoji [rangajī] m. hist. np. of rangoji Bhatta, younger brother of Bhattoji Dīkṣita, scholar ad vaitin of the court of King Venkaṭappā Nāyaka (early 17th century); he engaged in a three-month oratorical contest against the dvaitin Vidyādhīśa, disciple of Madhva.

rátnakīrti [kīrti] m. hist. n.p. from the philosopher bd. Ratnakīrti (1st half of the 11th century), student of Jñānaśrīmitra, specialist in epistemology and logic; he taught at the Vikramaśīla monastery the doctrine of exclusion [apohavāda]; we owe him not. Apohasiddhi, Ksanabhangasiddhi, Iśvarasādhanadūṣaṇa, Santānāntaradūṣaṇa, Citrādvaitaprakāśavāda and Sthirasiddhidūṣaṇa.

rátnakūṭa [kūṭa] n. bd. n.p. of the Ratnakūṭa “Multitude of Jewels”, collection of 49 works of the Mahāyāna tradition.
ratnakośa [kośa] m. bed. ["collection of pearls"] anthology.
ratnakhaṇḍamañjūṣā [khaṇḍamañjūṣā] f. bed. an thology.
ratnakheta [kheta] m. hist. n.p. by the scholar Ratnakheṭa Srīnivāsa Dīkṣita (Tamil Nadu, 16th century); cf. Śrīnivāsa₁.

Ratnagiri [giri] m. geo. n.p. from Ratnagiri hill in Orissa; cf. Puspagiri.
ratnaguna | guna | mr. bd. n.p. of the Ratnaguna or Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagātha, text of 302 verses precursor of the Astasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā in hybrid dialect bd. from Sanskrit.

ratnagotravibhāga [gotravibhāga] m. bd. n.p. of the ratnagotravibhāga, which expounds the Mahāyāna doctrine of tathāgatagarbha; also called Ut taratantra, it is attributed by Tibetan tradition to Maitreya.
ratnacakra [cakra] n. ["jewel wheel"] wheel of sovereignty, attribute of the universal monarch [cakravartin] | bd. not. wheel of the Law, symbolizing the Teaching of Buddha; cf. dharmacakra.
rátnatraya [traya] n. bd. the three jewels of Buddhism: buddha, dharma and sangha | jn. the three jewels of Jainism: samyagdarśana, samyagjñāna and samyakcāritra.
Ratnadvīpa [dvīpa] m. geo. np. of Ratnadvīpa, epith. of Ceylon "the island of jewels".
ratnaparīkṣā [parīkṣā] f. soc. Appraisal of gems | lit. np. of the ratnaparīkṣā "Appraisal" of gems", treatise on gemology [ratnaśāstra] by Buddhabhatta.
Ratnapurī | purī | f. geo. np. of the City of Ratnapurī "City of Jewels", capital of a small princely state of the AvantiMālava country; mod. Ratlam in Madhya Pradesh.
rátnaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. gram. np. of Rat naprakāśa "Splendor of jewels", commentary on the Mahābhāsya by Šivarāmendra Sarasvatī₂ (17th century).

ratnaprabhā [prabhā₂] f. lit. np. of the Rat naprabhā, commentary on the Bhāsya due to Go vindānanda | lit. [KSS.] np. of ratnaprabhā₁, daughter of King Hemaprabha and his favorite Alamkāraprabhā, destined to become the second wife of Naravāhanadatta.
ratnabhāndāgāra [bhāndāgāra] n. treasure of jewels lit. anthology.

rátnamālā [mālā] f. necklace of jewels, necklace of pearls — ifc. lit. title of works.
ratnaśāstra [śāstra] n. gemology.
ratnaśrī [śrī] amnf which has the splendor of a jewel — f. [ratnaśrīṭīkā] lit. np. of the ratnaśrī, commentary [tīkā] by Ratnaśrījñāna on the Kāvyādarśa. .1
ratnaśrījñāna [jñāna] m. hist. of np. Ratnaśrijñāna, Buddhist monk from Ceylon, author of the Ratnaśrī tīkā (10th century).

ratnasabhāpati [sabhāpati] m. soc. np. of the Ratna sabhāpati "Jewel Lord of the sanctuary", image of Shiva Națarāja in ruby from the sanctuary of Cidam baram; it is said to have come from a sacrifice of Brahmā.

ratnākaraśānti [śānti] m. hist. np. of ratnākaraśānti (11th century), bd philosopher teaching in Vikramaśīla; he maintained that consciousness was without object |nirākāra|; he is the author of the prosody work Chandoratnākara.
ratnādhipati [adhipati] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the king ratnādhipati of the island Ratnakūṭa; satisfied with his asceticism, Vișnu gave him the magical elephant Svetaraśmi as a mount.

Ratnāvalī₂ |āvalī| f. pearl necklace | lit. ifc. title of works | myth. np. of Ratnāvalī₂ "River of diamonds", a wife of Citrasena; cf. Gālava | lit. np. of Ratnāvalī₂, court comedy of Harṣa, in the nāṭikā style; it relates a gallant episode from the life of King Udayana | lit. np. of Ratnāvalī₂, heroine of the eponymous poem, daughter of the king of Ceylon; the minister Yaugamdharāyana, having learned from a prophecy that the man she will marry will become the master of the world, persuaded her father to give her hand to King Udayana; She was shipwrecked, and was taken in at her court as a lady-in-waiting to Queen Vāsavadattā₂ under the name Sāgarikā; at the spring festival, she fell in love with King Udayana, was caught by the queen in his company, and after many adventures was able to marry him.

Ratnodbhava [udbhava] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Rat nodbhava "From the Jewel", son of the minister Pad modbhava; he traveled to trade; arriving at the island of Kālayavana, he married Suvrttā; on the return voyage they were shipwrecked; 16 years later, in despair, he threw himself from the top of a cliff, and was rescued by Puspodbhava; nearby, a woman was preparing to throw herself into the fire; an old woman explained that she was Suvrttā who had survived the shipwreck, then given birth to a boy who was taken by an elephant; a siddha₁ had told her that she would find her husband and son after 16 years; Puspodbhava then realized that he had found his parents.
ratni [aratni] m. cubit; unit of length, from elbow to closed fist | closed fist.

[11] pr. (rasáyati) to taste, appreciate, feel | lat. ros; fr. raisin. suputrali saptamo rasali A good son is like a 7th delight.

rasaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. bed. [āyurveda] np. of Ra saprakāśa; cf. Rasaprakāśasudhākara. .5
Rasaprakāśasudhākara | sudhākara₁ | m. lit. np. of the Rasaprakāśasudhākara, a medical treatise by Yaśodhara₁.
Rasapradīpa [pradīpa] m. lit. np. from the Rasapradīpa, treatise on poetics by Prabhākarabhaṭṭa (16th century).
rásabodha | bodha | m. phil. knowledge of aesthetic taste | lit. poetic science.
rásamañjarī [mañjarī] f. bed. n.p. from the Ra samañjarī "Bouquet of aesthetic emotion", work by Bhānudatta on aesthetics in Sanskrit poetry.
rásamaya [maya] amnf rasamayī full of sap; fluid, liquid | (alchemy) made of sea cure | tasty; delicious; charming.
rasaratna | ratna | n. lit. np. of the rasaratna, medical work | of. ["metals and minerals"] alchemy.
Rasaratnasamuccaya [samuccaya] m. lit. np. from the Rasaratnasamuccaya "Compendium on gems and metals", a 13th century alchemical work traditionally attributed to Vāgbhaṭa.
rasaratnākara [ākara] m. bed. n.p. from Ra saratnākara “Mine of alchemy”, work by Nāgārjuna₃.

rasavat |vat| amnf rasavatī full of juice, succulent; tasty | graceful, pleasant; charming, elegant, tasteful; witty | passionate, moved | moist, well-watered, irrigated | lit. [Udbhaṭa] rhetorical figure of the completed development of a mode
aesthetic [Rasa] through the use of dramatic situations [vibhāva]; opp. preyasvat.
rasavid [vid₃] amnf who tastes good.
rásaviddha [viddha] n. (alchemy) transmutation of copper into gold by mercury | phil. [śaiva] irreversible transformation of the soul into śivatva by initiation.
rasavidyā [vidyā] f. ["knowledge of mercury"] alchemy.

rasavaiśesika [vaiśesika] n. lit. np. of the Rasa vaiśeṣika, a medical work in sūtra style, by the Buddhist Bhadanta Nāgārjuna (5th century?), with a commentary by Narasimha (7th century?); only one manuscript in Malayalam is known, preserved by the Astavaidya community of Kerala.
rásaśāstra [śāstra] n. alchemy.
rasājñāna [ajñāna] n. med. loss of the sense of taste, ageusia; syn. arasajñatā.
Rasādhyāya [adhyāya] m. lit. np. from the Rasādhyāya, 6th chapter of the Nāṭyaśāstra.
rasānubhava [anubhava] m. experience of Rasa, essence of drama according to Bharata₃.
rasābhāsa [ābhāsa] m. phil. [aesthetics] illusion of an aesthetic emotion; appearance, false expression of feelings.

rasābhyantara | abhyantara | amnf rasābhyantarā full of water; filled with feeling; filled with love. vīcikṣobhastanitavihagaśreṇikāñcīguṇāyāḥ samsarpantyāh skhalitasubhagam darśitāvartanābheḥ | nirvindhyāyāḥ pathi bhava rasābhyantaraḥ sannipatya strīnām ādyam pranayavacanam vibhramo hi priyeşu | | [MD.] You will find Nirvindhyā on your path; the flights of birds in the thunder of its surge form a belt around it; meandering indecisive and joyous, it reveals its navel in its whirlpools; You will fall in love immediately; women's coquettishness is the first expression of love for their beloved.
rasāyana [ayana] n. [Ayurveda] elixir of youth | alchemy — m. alchemist | med. vermifuge — f. rasāyanī med. channel of bodily fluid; vein, artery.
rasāyanatantra | tantra | n. med. the science of elixirs, a section of Ayurveda. rasārņava [arṇava] m. lit. np. from rasārṇava "Ocean of humors", a work of alchemy.
rasāsvāda [āsvāda] m. action of sipping juice | phil. perception of pleasure, enjoyment of Rasa.
rasoddīpana | uddīpana | n. stimulation of a feeling.
rasoddīpanasāmarthya [sāmarthya] n. lit. aptitude to stimulate a poetic feeling.
rasana₁ [act. ras] n. act of shouting | shout; noise.
rasana₁ [Rasana] m. saliva — act. n. taste, flavor | gustation; perception | bio. bot. Allium as calonicum, shallot — f. cf. rasanā.
rasanā [f. rasana₁] f. tongue (organ of taste) | [raśanā] corset; belt.
rasā [f. Rasa] f. moisture; dew | myth. np. of the celestial river rasā or Milky Way; |RV.| in one of its islands was the cavern Vala | hell; ground.
rasātala [tala] n. myth. np. of the world [loka] rasātala, fourth subterranean hell; |Rām.| the sons of Sagara sought there the horse of his sacrifice.
rasāla [rasāla] m. mango tree | sugar cane — f. rasālā curdled milk with sugar and spices | tongue.
rasika [Rasaika] amnf rasikā aesthete, raf refined, who has taste; elegant; dilettante | amateur, .6 devoted to, passionate about (loc.) — f. rasikā passionate woman.
rasikajīvana [jīvana] n. bed. n.p. of the rasikajīvana, anthology of subhāṣita |subhāṣitasaṃgraha| composed around 1660 by Gadādhara₂ Bhaṭṭa.
Rasikapriyā [priyā] f. bed. n.p. from the Rasikapriyā, erotic work by Keśavadāsa (1591).
rasikasāmājika [sāmājika] amnf rasikasāmājikī soc. member of an assembly of aesthetes.

rasita₁ [pp. ras] amnf rasitā shouted; resonated — n. cry; noise; not. trumpeting of the elephant — ifc. wedding song of (iic.). mṛgapatinakhabhidyamānakumbhakuñjararasitam [K.] trumpeting of the elephant when the lion lacerates its temples.
rasita₁ [pp. rasa] amnf rasitā tasted,
appreciated | tasteful | plated, gold-plated.
rasín [agt. rasa] amnf rasinī juicy, li quide | which tastes good.
rasendra [rasaIndra] m. mercury ["sperm of Indra". rasendracūdāmaņi [cūdāmaņi] m. bed. n.p. of the Ra sendracūḍāmaṇi "Diara of mercury", compendium of alchemy due to Somadeva (12th century).
rasona [rasaūna] m. garlic ["which has (bad) taste"]; syn. laśuna | var. rasuna id.
rasya [pfp. [1] rasa] amnf rasyā juicy; tasty, good-tasting — n. blood.
√ rah v. [1] pr. (rahati) ca. (rahayati) pp. (ra hita) pf. (vi) leave, abandon.
rahas [abstr. rah] n. deserted place, retreat; solitude, secret — acc. adv. in secret. rahasi adv. in secret.
rahasya |ya| amnf rahasyā secret, clandes tin — n. secret | phil. esoteric doctrine (not. āraņyaka or upaniṣad). rahasyam adv. clandestinely.
rahasyanikṣepa [nikṣepa] m. secret received in confidence. api raksyate tvayā rahasyaniksepah astu kept the secret that was entrusted to you?

rahita [pp. rah] amnf rahitā left, abandoned given, forsaken; solitary | deprived or exempt from, Without i. iic. ; opp. sahita₂. alankārarahitā vidhaveva sarasvatī Without ornaments, sarasvatī is like a widow.
ráhūgaṇa m. lit. np. of the ṛṣi Rahūgaṇa, to the hymn-writer of the RV., father of Gotama, a singer |āṅgirasa| | pl. clan āṅgirasá.
rā₂ |agt. rā₁| ifc. mf that gives, that grants (iic.).

rākā f. scar | girl having her first menstruation | astr. np. of rākā, goddess personifying the full moon day |pūrnimā| | myth. |Rām. | np. of the ogress [rākṣasī] rākā₁, mother of Khara and Sūrpaņakhā.
Rākeśa |īśa| mr. myth. n.p. of Rākeśa, epith. of Siva.

Rākṣasa₁ [*rakṣasa] amnf rākṣasī myth. relating to the rakṣas — m. myth. an ogrevampire of the rakṣas; The rākṣasās descend from Nirṛti |nairṛta|; these giants wander at night in deserted places, they have terrifying forms, sharp fangs and a lolling tongue; they eat raw flesh; their leader is Rāvaṇa; their preferred direction is the West; they watch for errors in the execution of mortal rites; cf. Kirmīra, Kumbhakarņa, Baka₁, Hidimba | astr. np. of Rākṣasa₁ "Undead", personifying the 49th year of a life cycle |samvatsara| hist. n.p. from the minister Rākṣasa₁ of the Nanda to the Ma gadha; he favored Candragupta's coup d'état under the influence of Cāṇakya; cf. Mudrārākṣasa — f. rākṣasī myth. female ogrevampire; cf. Karkaṭī, Kaikasī, Jarā₁, Tāṭakā, Dīrghajihvī, Sūrpaṇakhā, Hidimbā, Holikā.
Rākṣasakāvya | kāvya | n. bed. n.p. of Rākṣasakāvya; cf. Kāvyarākṣasa.
rākṣasagraha | graha | mr. phil. | Tantra | possession by a vampire.
Rākṣasāntaka | antaka | m. myth. | Rām. | np. of Rākṣasāntaka, epith. of Hanuman "Slayer of vam pires".

rāga [act. rañj] m. coloration, redness; intensity of red; color, dye | passion, love towards (loc.); opp. virāga₁ | mus. melody; musical mode (appropriate to a particular mood) seasoning; condiment | bd. np. du vidyārāja rāga "Reddening" — f. rāgī bot. Eleusine cora cana, eleusine, red millet. cakṣūrāgaḥ kokileṣu na parakalatreṣu [K.] The cuckoos have red eyes (fall in love), and no one has loving glances towards another's wife.
rāgadvesa [dvesa] m. of. attachment and aversion.

Rāgamañjarī [mañjarī] f. lit. [DKC.] np. of Rāgamañjarī "Bouquet of melodies", younger sister of Kāmamañjarī; despite the remonstrances of her mother, she decided to choose her husband on his virtues and not on his wealth; she fell in love with Apahāravarmā.

rāgamālā [mālā] f. lit. association of musical modes [rāga] with hours, seasons, animals, plants, emotions, etc. | style of rājput paintings with motifs of flowers, fruits and animals evoking perfumes.

rāgavibodha [vibodha₂] m. lit. from the np. rāgavibodha, versified music manual by Somanātha₁ (1609); it describes the kinds of lutes [vīṇā] and explains how to play them; it deals with musical modes [rāga] which it classifies into progenitors [janaka] and derivatives [janya₁]; it gives melodies.

rāgin [agt. rañj] amnf rāgiṇī red | passionate for, enamored of, loving (loc.) — ifc. who charms (iic.) — m. lover — f. rāgiņī modification of a musical mode, personified as his lover; there are 35 or 36 of them | myth. np. of Rāgiņī "lover", eldest daughter of Himavān and Menā.

rāghava |*Raghua| mr. myth. n.p. rāghava “descendant of Raghu”; patr. not. of Dasaratha, Rāma and his brothers | hist. n.p. of rāghava₁ or Rāghavadeva, rājaguru of King Hammīra (13th century) | hist. n.p. of rāghava₂ or Rāghavabhaṭṭa, author of a commentary on the Abhijñānaśakuntalā | pl. Rāghavās myth. |Rām. | Rāma, his brothers and their followers.
rāghavapāṇḍava | pāṇḍava | mr. the Rāghavās and the Pāndavās.

rāghavapāṇḍavīya |īya| n. lit. du np. rāghavapāṇḍavīya de Kavirāja₁, composed around 1175; it is a masterpiece of ślesa literature, telling in parallel the Rāmāyana and the Mahābhārata; it was the subject of more than 12 commentaries.
Rāghavayādavīya [yādavīya] m. bed. n.p. from the Rāghavayādavīya “Story of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa”, a poem with two interpretations by Venkaṭādhvarī; cf. Dvisandhānakāvya.

Rāghavendra [indra] m. hist. np. of the mystic Rāghavendra Svāmī (1595–1671); Telugu Brahmin born Venkanna Bhatta in Bhuvanagiri, he studied the dualistic doctrine of Madhva at the matha of Kumbhakoṇa; he became sannyāsin in 1614 under the name of Rāghavendra Tīrtha; he is said to be the incarnation of Prahlāda and miracles are attributed to him; he is also named Venkaţācārya; his cenotaph [samādhi] in Mantrālāya is a place of pilgrimage.
rāghavīya [rāghavaīya] amnf rāghavīyā relating to Rāma.
rāj₂ [agt. rāj₂] amnf ifc. brilliant (iic.) — m. |sg. name. rāt| ved. King, leader; kṣatriya | mod. n.p. of rāj₂, the British regime of India | lat. rex; all. Reich; eng. rich; fr. King, rich.
rāja iic. rājan.
rājaka |ka| m. wren.
rājakartr | kartr | m. soc. organizer of the coronation of a King.

rājakarma | karman | n. soc. royal destiny | pl. rājakarmāṇi soc. rituals of reinstatement of an exiled King (election of the purohita, war preparations, consecration of the King, game of dice establishing his superiority).
rājakula | kula | n. royal family | royal palace; King's court of justice | main street, royal road.
rājakulamahāmantrin [mahāmantrin] m. soc. title of palace majordomo, principal royal minister.
rājakośa | kośa | m. royal dictionary.
rājakośanighantu [nighantu] m. bed. n.p. from the Rājakośanighaṇṭu "Royal Glossary"; cf. rājavyavahārakośa.
rājaguru | guru | mr. soc. spiritual guide of the King.

rājagṛha [gṛha] n. royal palace | hist. np. of the city of Rājagrha "Royal Residence", ancient capital of Magadha (before the 5th century BC); it is said to have been founded by Jarāsandha as Giri vraja; it was an important center of Buddhism, close to Nālandā; Buddha and Mahāvīra₁ taught there; it was the site of the first Buddhist council; mod. Rājgīr in Bihāra — amnf rājagrhī inhabitant of Rājagrha — f. rājagrhī np. of Rājagrhī, ancient name of the city || pali rājagaha.
Rājagopāla [gopāla] m. myth. n.p. of Rājagopāla "Herdsman King", aspect of KṛṣṇaViṣṇu worshiped not. in Mannargudi in Tamil Nadu.

rājaghātaka [ghātaka] m. regicide. rājacūdāmaņi [cūdāmaṇi] m. hist. n.p. of the scholar Rājacūdāmaņi Dīkṣita, son of Ratnakheta Srīnivāsa Dīkṣita (Tamil Nadu, 16th century); he is the author of the poem Rukminīkalyāna.

rājataraṃgiṇī [taraṃgiṇī] f. bed. n.p. from the Rājataramgiņī "River of Kings", a historical epic in 8000 verses by Kalhana recounting the exploits of kings Lalitāditya and Jayāpīda, in an emotional but historically reliable personal Sanskrit style (1148); it was completed by the Dvitīyarājatarangiņī of Jonarāja then by the Jai narājatarangiņī of Srīvara.
rājatā [tā] f. kingship; sovereignty.
rājatva [tva] n. id.
rājadanda [daṇḍa] m. soc. scepter.

rājadattā [datta] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of rājadattā, younger sister of the virtuous Silāvatī; she embodies the gandharvī Rājavatī; King Ratnādhipati married her, believing that she would be faithful to him; cf. Svetaraśmi.
rājadanta [danta] m. ["main tooth"] front tooth | gram. generic example of a compound with inverted dependency, exception to sūtra (2,2, 30): upasarjanam pūrvam.
Rājadeva [deva] m. hist. n.p. of Rājadeva, King of Kaśmīra (13th century); cf. Jayadratha₂.
rājadroha [droha] m. oppression, tyranny rebellion, sedition.
rājadrohin [in] m. rebel; traitor.
rājadharma [dharma] m. duty of the King | lit. [Mah.] np. of the rājadharma section of the Sāntiparva dealing with the duties of a King | mod. political.
rājadhānī [dhānī] f. ["King's residence"] capital.
rājadhurā [dhurā] f. soc. royal office.
rājanighantu [nighantu] m. lit. from the np. Rājanighaṇṭu, dictionary due to Narahari; it is also called Nighanturāja and Abhidhānacūdāmaņi.
rājaputrá [putra] mf rājaputrī ["son of King"] member of the kṣatriya caste; prince, noble hi. rājput.
Rājaputrīya |īya| m. np. of the Rājaputrīya, a medical treatise on the treatment of elephants; tradition attributes it to Budha (son of CandraTārakārāja).
Rājapura [pura] n. geo. np. of the "city of the King" Rājapura, in Kūrmāncala it was founded in 1578 by King Kalyāṇa₁ Canda; mod. Almora in Uttarakhanda.
rājapuruṣa [puruṣa] m. the person of the King | servant of the King | gram. [generic] compound which can be interpreted either as a descriptive compound [karmadhāraya] or as a determinative compound
casual [tatpurusa]; in the first case the left component (here rājan) is principal [pradhāna] and the right one (here purușa) is auxiliary [upasarjana]; in the second case it is the reverse.
rājabhoja [Bhoja₁] m. hist. np. of the King of Mālava Bhoja₁; cf. Bhojadeva.
rājamaṇi [maṇi] m. royal jewel | precious stone.
rājamahita [mahita] amnf rājamahitā honored by the King.
rājamahendra [mahendra] m. hist. cf. Narendra₁.

rājamahendrapura [pura] n. geo. np. of the city of rājamahendrapura or Rājamahendravara of the country of Andhra, in the delta of the Godāvarī; it was the capital of King Rājarāja₁ Narendra₁ in the 11th century, then of the nāyaka Kāpaya in the 14th; mod. Rajahmundri.

rājamārga [mārga] m. royal way. rājamārtaņda [mārtaņda] m. lit. np. of the Rājamārtanda "Royal Light (on yoga)", commentary on the Yogasūtra of Patanjali₂ [Pātañjalavṛtti] due to King Bhojadeva; cf. Bhojavrtti.
Rājamṛgānga [mṛgaanga₁] m. bed. n.p. from the Rājamrgānga karaņa work of astronomy in verse dated 1042, attributed to King Bhojadeva.
Rājayakṣman [yakṣman] m. med. disease of the King; not. drought due to a royal sin | consumption, queen of diseases | lit. np. from the Rājayakṣman, chapter of the cikitsā of Caraka.
rājayoga [yoga] m. soc. integral yoga, spiritual discipline; it leads to liberation [kaivalyamukti]; cf. astāngayoga.
rājayogabhāṣya [bhāṣya] n. lit. np. of the rājayogabhāṣya, commentary on the Mandalabrāhmanopanisad attributed to Sankara₁, but rather due to a certain Sadānandāvadhūta.

Rājarāja₁ [rājan] m. myth. np. of Rājarāja₁ "King of kings", a title of Kubera | hist. np. of King Cola Rājarāja₁ (reign 985–1012); his capital was Tan javūr (mod. Tamil Nadu); his son Rājendracola succeeded him; cf. bṛhadīśvara.
rājarājeśvara [īśvara] m. myth. n.p. from rājarājeśvara, epith. of Śiva “Emperor” — f. Rājarājeśvarī myth. n.p. of Rājarājeśvarī, terrible aspect [daśamahāvidyā] of the Goddess; cf. Ṣoḍaśī.
Rājarāṇī [rāṇī] f. geo. n.p. from the temple of Rājarāṇī of Bhuvaneśvarī₁ (11th century), pañcaratha plan, sanctuary of IndresvaraSiva, in pink Rājarānīya sandstone.
rājarṣabha | ṛṣabha | m. best among kings.
rājarṣi [ṛṣi] m. myth. sage [ṛṣi] of royal origin; cf. Janakaraja.
rājalakṣman [lakṣman] m. bearing the insignia of royalty.
rājalīlā [līlā] f. relaxation of the King.
rājalīlāsana [āsana] n. seated posture of royal ease, one leg bent horizontally, the other bent vertically, the feet touching. .9

rājavat |vat| adv. like a king — amnf Rājavatī possessing a king — f. Rājavatī lit. [KSS.] np. of the gandharvī Rājavatī with the enchanting voice, wife of Devaprabha, whose jealousy caused her downfall into the mortal Rājadattā; cf. Švetaraśmi. rājavati adv. in the presence of kings.

Rājavāhana [vāhana] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Prince Rājavāhana "Bearer of Kingship", son of Rājahaṃsa and Vasumatī; he leads the group of 10 princes whose adventures are recounted in the Daśakumāracarita; he went with them to the forest of the Vindhya Mountains; there they met Mātaṅga₂, a repentant Brahmin brigand; Rājavāhana left his sleeping companions, followed him, and disappeared; his friends separated to try to find him; he himself found the cave with the inscription indicated by Mātanga₂, and went to the Rasātala hell; there, Mātanga₂ uttered formulas [mantra], threw himself into the fire, and obtained a divine body; immediately the celestial Kālindī₂ appeared to whom he united and from became the king of Rasātala; he gave a magical jewel to Rājavāhana, who went to Ujjayinī where he met Somadatta₂ who told him about his adventures, then Puspodbhava who did the same; he then went to Avantikā, where he met Avan tisundarī₁ in a park, and they remembered their previous life as Samba and Yajñavatī; The Brahmin magician Vidyeśvara helped them, by a trick of illusion before Candavarmā allowing Rājavāhana to enter the women's quarters and unite with his beloved; after a night of love he awoke with a silver chain on his feet; Candavarmā imprisoned him, and on the order of Dar pasāra condemned him to death; but his silver chain came to life like the divine apsaras Suratamañjarī₁ whose curse had ended, like his own; at that moment, it was learned that Candavarmā had just been killed by none other than Apahāravarmā; Shortly after, Rājavāhana reunited with his other companions Dhanamitra, Upahāravarmā, Arthapāla, Pramati, Mitragupta, Mantragupta, Viśruta, as well as Prahāravarmā, Kāmapāla, and Siṃhavarmā.
rājavidyā [vidyā] f. science of government; royal politics | reason of state.
rājavihāra [vihāra] m. Royal monastery | geo. not. np. of the bd. rājavihāra monastery of Angkor, consecrated by King Jayavarmā VII in 1186; mod. Ta Prom.
rājavyavahāra [vyavahāra] iic. of Royal patronage.

rājavyavahārakośa [kośa] m. lit. np. from rājavyavahārakośa "Dictionary commissioned by the king", due to Raghunātha₃ Pandita; it was commissioned by the Maratha king Chattrapati Sivajī around 1675; it gives the Sanskrit equivalents of common words borrowed from Arabic and Persian; also called Rājakośanighantu.
rājaśāsana [śāsana] n. soc. Royal edict; not. deed of donation of land | lit. instruction on Royal duty.

rājaśekhara [śekhara] m. hist. np. of rājaśekhara "Royal Diadem", poet of the 10th century, chaplain [upādhyāya] at the court of Kings Mahendrapāla₁ then Mahīpāla in Kanyākubjā; he is named by his patron Yāyāvarīya or Yāyāvara; he is the author of the treatise on poetics Kāvyamīmāmsā, a sum of knowledge for the use of apprentice poets; he is also credited with the drama Karpūramañjarī of the sattaka type in 4 acts in Prakrit and the plays Bālarāmāyaṇa and Vid dhaśālabhañjikā in Sanskrit; His mahāprabandha Haravilāsa earned him the title of Mahākavi; he is also credited with the Bhuvanakośa | hist. np. of rājaśekhara₁, king of Pandalam in Kerala, descendant of the Pāṇdya dynasty; myth. he found the child Ayonija on the banks of the Pampā and adopted him as his heir; this is the origin of Ayyappā, object of an important cult at the temple of Sabarimala in Kerala.
rājasakha |sakhi| mr. friend of the king | var. rājasakhi of which the king is a friend.
rājasūya |sūya| m. soc. solemn rite of royal consecration, imperial coronation; it was performed upon return from a victorious military expedition.
Rājasūyacampū [campū] f. lit. np. of the Rājasūyacampū, mixed prose/verse poem by Bhatta Nārāyaṇa₃, recounting the rājasūya of Yudhişthira.
rājasthāna [sthāna] n. mod. ["land of the Rajputs"] np. of the territory of rājasthāna.

rājahaṃsa [haṃsa] m. bio. zoo. Cignus Cignus, Swan | lit. [DKC.] np. of the king of Magadha rājahamsa "Swan among kings"; he fought his enemy Mānasāra, king of Mālava, was victorious, but kept him on his throne; the latter invoked Shiva, who gave him a magical mace which enabled him to destroy the army of Magadha; rājahamsa, wounded, took refuge in the forest of the Vindhya Mountains with his harem; he surrendered to the sage Vāmadeva₂, who told him that his son Rājavāhana (of his wife Vasumatī) would avenge him.
rājādhikṛta [adhikṛta] m. soc. Royal official.
rājādhirāja [adhirāja] m. soc. title of king of kings.
rājābhiṣeka | abhiṣeka | m. soc. solemn ceremony of the coronation of the King on his throne.
rājāmātya [amātya] m. soc. minister of the King.
rājāvarta [āvarta] m. lapis lazuli.
Rājāvali |āvali| f. bed. n.p. from Jonarāja's dynastic epic Kaśmīra Rājāvali (or Rājāvalī) (1412); cf. Dvitīyarājataranginī.

rājāvalipatākā [patākā] f. lit. np. of the dynastic epic of Kaśmīra rājāvalipatākā by Prājya Bhatta, sequel to the Rājataraṃgiṇī (1513), now lost; it stops at the conquest of Kaśmīra by the emperor Akbar.
rājāsandī [āsandī] f. soc. ["royal throne"] braided stool bearing the soma stems in solemn Vedic rites.
Rajendra | Indra | m. King of kings, emperor.

Rājendracola |Cola| m. hist. np. of the emperor Cola Rājendracola, son of Rājarāja₁ (reign 1012–1044); the Cola empire reached its zenith, extending to the Ganges, and including Ceylon, the Maldives, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; cf. Gangaikonda | hist. np. of Rājendracola₂, son of the former, who succeeded him (reign 1045–1063).
rājendravarman [varman] m. hist. np. of the Khmer emperor Rājendravarmā, founder of the temple of Pre Rup (10th century).
rājaka [agt. rāj₁] m. King.
rājat [ppr. rāj₁] amnf rājant reigning.

rājan [agt. rāj₁] m. [sg. nom. Rājā, acc. rājānam, i. rājñā; en comp. rāja| King, chief, god; kṣatriya, noble | soc. np. of Rājā, title of King | the King in chess [caturangā]; syn. nrpa | epithet of various sovereign gods such as Varuna, Indra, or somaCandra — f. rājāī queen — m. rāja ifc. King of — v. [11] pr. (rājīyati) to wish for a King | to behave like a King — v. [11] pr. r. (rājayate) to reign | to claim to be King || pkt. rāya . rājatas adv. (originating) from the King; by order of the King.
rājana |*rājana| amnf rājanī from a royal family.
rājanya |rājanya| amnf rājanyā royal — m. man of kṣatriya caste, noble; lord, prince; not. prince of the royal circle |ratnin|.
rājanyaka |ka| amnf rājanyikā inhabited by nobles — m. soc. person of royal rank — n. as assembly of lords.
rājanyabandhu | bandhu | m. soc. prince of the second rank.
rājasa [*rajasa] amnf Rājasī [“whose predominant guna is rajas” enterprising, active, energetic; passionate, animated by passion — f. Rājasī myth. np. of Rājasī, epith. of Durgā “Passionate”.
rājasika |ika| amnf rājasikā id.
rājānaka [rājan] m. wren | soc. title rājānaka of royal courtier; cf. Abhinavagupta, Kuntaka, Jayaratha.
rāji [related to rañj] f. line, stroke; row, series | parting in the hair; line of hair | var. rājī id.
rājīva [iva] amnf rājīvā striped, with stripes — m. bio. striped antelope — n. blue lotus flower. smerarājīisovanayane (woman) smiling with lotus eyes.
rājika [rāj₂ika] amnf rājikā royal — n. black mustard grain; minimum weight measure (1/3 sarṣapa) — f. rājikā bio. bot. Sinapis ramosa, black mustard.
rājīya [rāj₂īya] amnf rājīyā royal.

Rājya [pfp. [1] rāj₁] amnf rājyā princely, royal — n. royalty, empire, government | kingdom — m. hist. np. of Prince Rājya vardhana₁, eldest son of King Prabhākara₁ of Sthāneśvara; he succeeded his father on his death in 605; he fought the Huns [hūṇās] in the North and exterminated them; and fought King Devagupta of Mālava who had imprisoned his sister Rājyaśrī after killing her husband Grahavarmā; he was treacherously killed by Saśānka King of Gauda; his younger brother Harşa succeeded him in 606 and established himself as emperor.

Rājyadhara [dhara] m. regent | lit. [KSS.] np. of Rājyadhara, younger brother of Prānadhara, skilled in making automata; he fled from Kāncī on a flying chariot, and discovered a magical city created by Kumāra for him, and without inhabitants; he became its regent and populated it with automata.
Rājyavardhana [vardhana] amnf rājyavardhanī who makes the kingdom prosper — m. hist. np. of King Rājyavardhana, elder brother of King Harṣa; cf. Rājya.
rāḍhā var. rārā f. beauty, splendor | geo. the region of Bengal.
rāṇā [pkt. rājan] m. King — f. rāṇī Middle Indian title of queen.
rāṇāyana [*raṇaāyana] m. patr. of rāṇāyana "descendant of raṇa", founder of a school of Vedic chanting.
rāṇāyanīya [īya] amnf rāṇāyanīyā refers to the Sāmaveda school of chanting of rāṇāyana; it uses a syllabic notation for tones.
rātá |pp. rā₁| amnf rātā given, granted, conferred — ifc. given by (iic.).
rāti [act. rā₁] f. gift, favor; grace — agt. amnf generous; favorable; gracious, benevolent.
rātra ifc. rātri.

rātri f. [en comp. rātra] night | var. rātrī cosmic night — m. rātra ifc. night of (2nd century). rātrau var. rātrim adv. of the night; during the night. rātryām adv. of the night. navarātram festival of the 9 nights of Durgā; cf. na varātra.
rātribhojana | bhojana | n. night meal (forbidden in Jainism).
rātrika [rātrika] amnf rātrikā nocturnal — cl. after num. which lasts so many days — f. rātrikā night. pañcarātrika which lasts 5 days.
rātrim [acc. rātri] adv. of the night; during the night.
rātrindivam | diva | adv. night and day.
rātrau [loc. rātri] adv. of the night; during the night.
rātraubhava | bhava | amnf rātraubhavā which takes place at night.
rāddhá |pp. rādh| amnf rāddhā accom pli, accomplished, prepared; ready; due to (acc.) | fortunate, crowned with success | initiated — n. (impers.) it has been accomplished by (i.).
rāddhi [act. rādh] f. accomplishment; success, fortune.
rādhana |act. rādh| n. act of reconciling; prayer.
rādhas [abstr. rādh] n. success, achievement; to see.

Rādhā [act. rādh] f. prosperity, success | myth. [GG.] np. of Rādhā "Success", shepherdess [gopī] fa vorite of the young Gopālakṛṣṇa to Vṛndāvana; she was the wife of the cowherd Ayanaghoşa; Vṛṣabhānu was her father; she was deified as Srī Rādhā, symbol of Divine Love, by the devotional movement [bhakti] of Caitanya; cf. rādhikā, Vṛndā, Hlādinī | myth. [Mah.] np. of Rādhā₁, nurse of Karna, wife of Adhiratha | astr. np. of Rādhā₂ "Success", 14th lunar asterism [naksatra], also called Viśākhe.
Rādhākāntadeva |kāntadeva| m. hist. np. of Rādhākāntadeva, Bengali scholar and conservative politician (1784–1867); he edited the Sabdakalpadruma.
Rādhākuṇḍa [kuṇḍa] n. myth. np. of the Rādhākuṇḍa, pond where Rādhā bathed at Vṛndāvana.
Rādhākṛṣṇa [kṛṣṇa] m. soc. np. of Rādhākṛṣṇa, combination of Rādhā and kṛṣṇa considered as supreme deity in the gaudīyavaiṣṇava movement.
rādhātantra | tantra | n. lit. np. of the rādhātantra, a 17th-century Bengali text presenting the story of Rādhā and kṛṣṇa from a śākta point of view.
rādhāramana [ramana] m. soc. n.p. of rādhāramaṇa, form of Rādhākṛṣṇa whose cult was initiated by Gopāla₃ Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī; its main temple is at Vṛndāvana.
rādhikā [Rādhāika] f. myth. n.p. from rādhikā, diminutive of Rādhā.
rādheya [Rādhāīya] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Rādheya, epith. of Karņa "raised by Rādhā₁".
rādhya [pfp. [1] rādh] amnf rādhyā to undertake, to accomplish; to succeed, to obtain | that which must be honored.

rāma [agt. ram] amnf rāmā pleasant, Charming; agreeable, beautiful — m. pleasure | myth. [Rām.] np. of King rāma "the Charming", 7th avatar of Vișnu in the tretāyuga; son of Daśaratha king of Ayodhyā of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa] and of Queen Kausalyā, he was born at noon on the 9th day of the month caitra under the nakṣatra punarvasu; his guru was Viśvāmitra, with whom he went to Mithilā; he married Sītā, daughter of King Janakarāja, by winning an archery contest, where he strung, and broke, the Ajagava bow of Siva; Paraśurāma, indignant that he had disrespected his guru Shiva, defied him and snatched Vishnu's bow; Daśaratha, in his old age, made Rama his heir; but his second wife, Kaikeyī, reminding him of his promise to grant a vow, forced him to leave the kingdom to his son, Bharata₁; Rama voluntarily went into exile with Sītā and his brother Lakṣmaṇa, with Bharata₁ assuming the regency; Rama lived with them as a hermit in the Daṇḍaka forest, in a hermitage on the banks of the Godāvarī, where he killed many demons, notably the ogress Tāṭakā and her sons; the ogre | rākṣasa | Rāvaṇa, king of Lankā, decided to avenge them, and disguised as an ascetic, abducted Sītā and transported her to Lankā in his flying chariot [vimāna₁]; rāma and Lakṣmaṇa went in search of her with the help of the monkey king Sugrīva and his faithful general Hanuman, who flew across the strait and found Sītā; the monkey army built a stone jetty |setu| to cross the ocean, and after a great battle Rāvaņa was defeated by rāma; this victory is celebrated at the festival of daśāha; Sita, repudiated by Rama, threw herself onto the funeral pyre, but Agni spared her, and she was reunited with Rama, who resumed his throne at Ayodhya for a long reign of justice; Sita bore him Kusha and Lava as sons; Rama is the archetype of the Just King by Divine Right; cf. Karunasagara, Kakutstha, Dasharatha, Raghunan Dana, Raghunatha, Raghava, Ramacandra, Marica | [parasurama] myth. np. of the Bhargava parasurama "Rama with the axe"; cf. Jamadagnya | |Balarama| myth. np. from kṛṣṇa's elder brother "rāma₂ the strong"; cf. Balarāma | math. symb. the number 3 — f. rāmā charming woman. rāmo rājamaṇiḥ sadā vijayate rāmaṃ rameśaṃ bhaje rāmeṇābhihatā niśācaracamūḥ rāmāya tas mai namah | rāmānnāsti parāyanam parataram rāmasya dāso'smyaham rāme cittalayassadā bha vatu me bho rāma māmuddhara || (grammatical memory aid) rāma, jewel among kings, is always victorious; I revere Rama, lord of Sri; I honor this Rama, who destroyed the armies of the night demons; there is no better refuge than Rama; I am a humble servant of Rama; may Rama always be present in my mind; O Rama, save me.

Rāmakaṇṭha [kaṇṭha] m. hist. np. of Rāmakaṇṭha Bhatta, theologian of Kaśmīra of the 10th century (~950~1000); he is the author of the Paramokṣanirāsakārikavṛtti, the Kiranavṛtti and a commentary on the Mataigaparames varāgama.

Rāmakathā [kathā₁] f. myth. Deed of rāma; it is recounted not. in the Rāmāyana, the rāmacaritamānasa, the Rāmacarita₁, and the Rāmopākhyāna, as well as in the Rāmakathā section of the Vahnipurāņa; the Bālarāmāyaņa is an irreverent satirical play freely inspired by the earlier stories.

rāmakṛṣṇa [kṛṣṇa] m. mod. np. of the Bengali saint Srī rāmakṛṣṇa paramahaṃsa, born Ṭhākūr (1836– 1886); he preached a syncretic doctrine combining vedānta and bhakti; he founded an āśrama in Belūr near Calcutta; his principal disciple was Vivekānanda, who founded the rāmakṛṣṇa mission in 1897 | [Rāmakṛṣṇakāvya] lit. np. of the poem Rāmakṛṣṇakāvya, due to Sūryadāsa; it is a vi lomākṣarakāvya of 36 verses; each verse has 4 feet [carana], the first two have rāma as their subject, and the following two, obtained by reversing the order of their syllables, have kṛṣṇa as their subject | du. rāmakṛṣṇau myth. rāma and kṛṣṇa.
rāmagiri [giri] m. geo. np. of the hill of rāmagiri, near Nāgapura in Vidarbha (mod. Ramtek in Mahārāṣṭra) | lit. [Meghadūta] place of the āśrama where the yakṣa hero of the poem was exiled.

rāmagupta [gupta] m. hist. np. of rāmagupta, eldest son of the emperor Samudragupta; he reigned briefly (375–~380); according to the play Devīcandragupta, he had cowardly abandoned his wife Dhruvadevī who had been captured by an enemy Saka prince; his younger brother Kumāra Candra gupta, disguised as a woman, infiltrated the enemy camp, punished the rival, freed Dhruvadevī, then to marry her assassinated rāmagupta, and ascended the throne under the name of Candragupta₂ (around 380).

Rāmacandra₁ | Candra | m. myth. np. of the divine King Rāmacandra₁, son of Daśaratha; cf. rāma hist. np. of King Rāmacandra₁, of the Yādavās dynasty; he reigned in Devagiri from 1271 to 1309; he was defeated by Alauddin Khalji; his first minister was the scholar Hemādri₁ | hist. np. of the Mairian grammarian Rāmacandra₁ of the 15th century, author of the Prakriyākaumudī.

Rāmacandrapura [pura] n. geo. np. of Rāmacandrapura, city of Andhra north of the delta of the Godāvarī; there is the temple of Somārāma; it is a pañcārāmakṣetra, it is said that the śivalinga Someśvara was installed there by Candra.

Rāmacarita₁ [carita] n. lit. np. of the Rāmacarita₁ "Deeds of rāma", in 40 cantos, composed by Abhinanda₁ in the vaidarbhī style; it is based on the Rāmāyana, but introduces variants; it begins with the sojourn of rāma and Lakṣmaṇa in the Mountains Mālyavān₁ | lit. np. of the Rāmacarita₁, a poem without krit with double meaning by Sandhyākaranandī; it glorifies both the god rāma and King Rāmapāla; it is also called Rāmapālacarita; this poem anticipates the Rāghavayādavīya style.
rāmacaritamānasa [mānasa] n. lit. np. from rāmacaritamānasa "Sacred Collection of the Deeds of rāma", epic of rāma due to Tulasīdāsa; it is composed in avadhī, an eastern dialect ancestor of Hindu.
rāmatāpin [tāpin] amnf rāmatāpinī soc. re nunciating devotee to rāma — f. rāmatāpinī lit. n.p. from the lesson Rāmatāpinyupanisad.
rāmanavamī [navamī] f. soc. birthday festival of Rāma, the 9th day | tithi | of the clear fortnight of the month caitra.
rāmanātha [nātha] m. geo. np. of the rāmanātha, jyotirlinga of Rāmeśvara; cf. rāmalingeśvara.
rāmapaṭṭābhiṣeka | paṭṭābhiṣeka | mr. bed. | Ram. | coronation of Rama.
Rāmapāla |pāla| m. hist. np. of King Rāmapāla of Puṇḍravardhana (Bengal) (11th century); Sandhyākaranandī wrote his panegyric rāmapālacarita; he founded the monastery bd. Jagaddala.
rāmapālacarita [carita] n. lit. np. of the rāmapālacarita, praise of King Rāmapāla; it is one of the readings of the double-meaning poem Rāmacarita₁.

Rāmabhadra | bhadra | m. myth. np. of Rāmabhadra, epith. of Rāma dear to Daśaratha hist. np. of the logician Rāmabhadra₁ Sārvabhauma, son of Janakīnātha Cūdāmaņi (16th century); he is author of the Padārthatattvavivecanaprakāśa | hist. np. of many other characters.
rāmarājya [rājya] n. mod. just government, social justice.
rāmarudrī [rudra] f. bed. [Nyāya] np. of the rāmarudrī, commentary on the Dinakarī.
rāmalalla | lala | m. myth. np. of Rāmalala, epith. of the divine hero Rāma as a child.

rāmalingeśvara | lingaīśvara | m. myth. np. of rāmalingeśvara, one of the 12 radiant signs of Shiva [jyotirlinga], established on the island of Rāmeśvara; Rāma consecrated it [lingapratiṣṭhā] on his return from Lankā with Sītā, on the way to Ayodhyā; there he expiated the crime of brahmahatyā, committed by having killed Rāvaṇa; Hanumān was charged with finding the linga on Mount Kailāsa; as he was delayed, at the time fixed by the jyotisa Sītā made a linga of sand which Rāma consecrated, and which became indestructible; This is the rāmanātha jyotirlinga while the Himalayan linga is the subordinate Viśvanātha; other sources say that Rāma consecrated an earth linga [pārthiva] before his departure for Lankā, in order to obtain the blessing of Siva.
rāmalīlā [līlā] f. soc. representation of the exploits of the god Rāma and his fight against Rāvaṇa; it is performed during the festival of navarātra (durgāpūjā in Bengal).
Rāmaśataka | śataka | n. bed. n.p. from Rāmaśataka, a hymn in 100 verses to the glory of Rāma, by Someśvaradeva.

rāmasetu |setu| m. geo. line of rocks forming a natural jetty between Ceylon and India (known in English as Adam's Bridge) | myth. [Rām.] it was by this bridge, built by monkeys, that Rāma invaded Lankā.

Rāmānanda |ānanda| m. hist. np. of Rāmānanda "Joy of Rāma", vaiṣṇava brahmin (~1380–1450), born in Prayāga; he popularized the bhakti doctrine; he attempted to reconcile Islam and Hinduism, and to abolish caste distinctions; the saint Kabīr was his disciple, and continued his work of reform; the poet Tulasīdāsa belonged to his movement; Guru Nānaka Shah, founder of the Sikh religion, was inspired by him | hist. np. of Rāmānanda₁ Svāmī, born Ajaya Sarmā in Ayodhyā in 1738; considered an incarnation of Uddhava₁, he led an ascetic life; he met his master Rāmānujācārya in a dream; he founded the religious order [sampradāya] Uddhava₁ in Gurjara; his successor was his student Svāminārāyaṇa | hist. np. of Rāmānanda₂ Sarasvatī₂ Svāmī (1867–1936), author of the Maniprabhā.
rāmānandin [in] m. soc. renunciant [tyāgin] disciple of rāmānuja; practicing hathayoga; Rāmānanda created their sampradāya Rāmānandī; they worship RāmaViṣṇu, but also Śiva; cf. Rāmatāpinyupaniṣad.

rāmānuja [anuja] m. myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa as younger brother of Balarāma | phil. np. of the master [ācārya] rāmānuja "Rāma junior", Vaishnava philosopher and mystic (~1050–1137) born Ilaya Per umal in Tamil Nadu; married young, he settled in Kāñcīpura, where he met his first Guru, the advaitavādin Yādavaprakāśa; he left him for Yamunācārya, who preached the doctrine of distinguished non-duality [viśiṣṭādvaita] which refined the simple non-duality [advaita] of Sankara₁; He sent his wife back to her family to become a sannyāsin, and he lived in Sriranga where he preached liberation through devotion [bhakti] in submission [prapatti]; he became the Master Ramanujacarya, and had many disciples, notably Nathamuni; he admitted outcasts into his order; he founded 700 monasteries in Karnataka, established the Venkata temple in Tirupati, and the Tirunarayana temple in Melukote near modern-day Mysore, where he settled, to escape the hostility of the Shaiva kings in Tamil Nadu; he wrote many works [navaratna] on Vedanta, notably the Śrībhāṣya, the Vedāntasāra₁, the Vedāntadīpa and the Vedārthasaṃgraha; he is also credited with the Tan trarahasya and the Nityagrantha; cf. śrīvaisnava.
rāmābhyudaya [abhyudaya] m. lit. np. of the play | nāṭaka | Rāmābhyudaya "Triumph of Rāma", due to King Yaśovarmā; this 8th century classic praised by critics is now lost.
Rāmāyaṇa [ayana] n. lit. np. of the Rāmāyaṇa, or Deeds of Rāma, great epic poem | itihāsa | at attributed to Vālmīki; its composition dates back to the 7th century BC.
rāmāyaṇacampū [campū] f. lit. np. from the rāmāyaṇacampū, a classical poem by Bhoja deva in campū style.
rāmāyaṇāmañjarī [mañjarī] f. lit. np. of the poem Rāmayaṇamañjarī, version of the Rām. due to Ksemendra.
rāmāvatara [avatara] n. lit. np. of the rāmāvatara, Tamil version of the Rāmāyaṇa in 6 chapters, by Kamban (12th century); it comprises 11000 stanzas.

Rāmeśvara [īśvara] m. the charming Lord Rāma (karmadhāraya), the god worshipped by Rāma (sasthītatpurusa), or who has Rāma as their chosen deity (bahuvrīhi), generic example of compound word am biguity | geo. np. of the island of Rāmeśvara, south of Tamil Nadu, important place of pilgrimage; cf. Rāmalingeśvara | geo. temple of Rāmeśvara₁ at Bhuvaneśvara (11th century).
Rāmopākhyāna [upākhyāna] n. bed. n.p. from the Rāmopākhyāna, “Gesture of Rāma”, recounted by Mārkandeya to Yudhisthira in the 3rd book of the Mah.
rāmaṇīyaka [*ramaṇīyaka] n. charm, beauty.
rāmyā [related to ram] f. night.
rāya [pkt. rājan] ifc. mr. soc. rāya, Middle Indian royal title; cf. Kṛṣṇadeva.

rāyacūru [telugu] n. geo. np. of the citadel city of rāyacūru (mod. Raichur), in the Northeast of Karṇāṭaka, on the border of the Andhra country; it controls the rich plain of the doab of confluence of the Krsnā and the Tungabhadrā; the district was part of the possessions of the Cālukyās of Badāmi, then of the Rāstrakūtās, then of the Cālukyās of Kalyāņī; its fort was built by Rudrāmbā, queen of the Kākatīyās, in 1294; the city was sacked by the troops of the Delhi Sultanate in 1312; It was conquered by King Krishnadeva of Vijayana Gara in 1520, and taken over by the Sultanate of Bijapur after the Battle of Talikota in 1565; it was captured by Aurangzeb in 1686, then passed to the Nizam of Hyderabad in 1724.
rāyas [g. rai] iic.
rāyaspoṣa | poṣa | m. increase of wealth, good fortune | myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa "that which makes prosper".
rāla var. rāli m. bio. resin of the śāla tree, used as lacquer.
rāva [*rava] m. cry, piercing noise.

rāvaṇa [*ravaṇa] amnf rāvaṇā who cries out — m. myth. [Rām.] np. of rāvaṇa "Hur leur", brahmin son of Viśravā and Keśinī₂, vampire king | rākṣasa | of Laṅkā, chief of the rakṣas; by his penances |tapas| he obtained from Brahmā that he could not be killed by the gods |deva|, nor by the genies [gandharva], nor by the trolls [yakṣa], nor by the ogres [rākṣasa]; Brahmā gave him 10 heads [Daśāsya] to govern the 10 directions; he became an impious tyrant, and wanted to dominate the Universe; He went to Mount Kailāsa to fight the yakṣās of his elder half-brother Kubera; he knocked the latter unconscious and stole his flying chariot Puspaka; arriving near Shiva, he mocked Nandi who came to arrest him, calling him a monkey, provoking his curse that he perish by the monkeys; he embraced Mount Kailāsa, making it tremble, hoping to carry it to Lanka as an altar for his aged mother, and even Parvati became afraid; Shiva crushed his arms with his toe for 1000 years, which he spent weeping and begging him; then Shiva forgave him, gave him an increase in life and the sword Candrahāsa; in the woods he met the beautiful Vedavati, betrothed to Vishnu, living as an ascetic; He defiled her by touching her hair, and she threw herself into the fire, vowing to be reborn in the Tretayuga like Sita to bring about his downfall; he defiled the sacrifice of King Marutta, to which the gods were invited, and where Samvarta officiated; the gods hid in the wombs of animals for shelter; he then fought all the kings; Pururava, Gaya, Gadhi, Su Ratha, and Dusyanta admitted defeat; Anaranya, king of Ayodhya, fought him in vain and perished cursing him for being defeated by his descendant Rama; Narada reminded him that killing men was beneath him, and that he should instead measure himself against Yama; He descended into the underworld to fight Yama, Mṛtyu and their hordes of tormenting demons, but Brahmā intervened, for his word could not be doubted; Ravana then went to Bhogavatī to subdue the nāgās, then to Maṇimatī to fight the nivātakavacās, who made peace with him after a long war; he then went to the kingdom of the waters to fight Varuṇa's army; then he returned to Lankā, abducting women and pillaging everything in his path; he then attacked the gods; he abducted and raped Rambhā, the most beautiful woman in Indra's paradise, although she was the wife of his nephew Nalakūbara; the latter cursed him so that he could not seduce a non-consenting woman, under penalty of his head bursting into seven pieces; His son Meghanada subdued Indra and became Indrajit; Prajapati came to ask for mercy, and Indra was released in exchange for Indrajit's immunity; he fought Arjuna Kartavirya, but was taken prisoner by his 1000 arms, and was only freed through the intervention of his grandfather Pulastya; he attacked the monkey king Vali, who was engaged in his evening rites, but Vali seized him and tied him to his belt, going around the four oceans; then Vali released him and took him to Kiskindha where he accepted his offer of alliance; During Rama's exile in the forest, thanks to the trick of Marica, who was transformed into a golden deer [hemamrga] to lure Rama away, Ravana abducted his wife Sita and took her prisoner to Lanka; he locked Sani in a cistern to escape his influence, but Hanuman freed him, and with a glance Sani blackened his golden palace; he was defeated and killed by Rama, aided by Hanuman, at the end of a long war in which monkeys and bears were their allies; he has a monstrous body, with ten heads [Daśagrīva] and twenty arms; he is sometimes depicted with an eleventh donkey head symbolizing his madness; His first queen was Mandodarī, who gave him as sons Meghanāda Indrajit, Prahasta, Atikāya and Akṣakumāra; cf. Dūṣaṇa, Sūrpaṇakhā, brahmāstra.

rāvaṇavadha [vadha] m. lit. np. of the rāvaṇavadha "Defeat of rāvaṇa", mahākāvya due to Bhatti (7th century); also called Bhattikāvya, this poem serves as a collection of grammatical composition according to Pāṇini and a compendium of stylistic figures [alamkāra], and therefore belongs to the śāstrakāvya genre. latānupātam kusumānyagrhņāt sa nadyavaskan dam upāspṛśac ca kutūhalāc cāruśilopaveśaṃ kākutsthesatsmayamānāsta | Often, Rama would bend branches and pluck their blossoms, descend to streams to purify himself, sit upon charming rocks, and remain seated, attentive, with a slight smile (illustrious Pan (III, 4, 56), with 3 compounds formed on an absolutive namulanta with a frequentative meaning: latānupātam, nadyavaskandam and cāruśilopaveśam). vyākhyāgamyam idam kāvyam [Bhaṭṭi] This poem is only accessible with a commentary/This poem is inaccessible even with a commentary.

Rāvaṇavaha [vaha] m. bed. n.p. from Rāvaṇavaha (for rāvaṇavadha), poem on the gesture of Rāma in prākṛtī attributed to Pravarasena₂; also called Setubandha₁. rāvaņaśiras [śiras] n. myth. head of rāvaṇa (there are 10) | math. symb. the number 10. rāvaņahrada [hrada] m. geo. n.p. of Rāvaņahrada, lake of rāvaṇa, in the Himalayas; cf. Anavatapta.
Rāvaṇi [rāvaṇa] m. myth. patr. of Rāvaṇi "son of rāvaṇa", with the voice of thunder [Meghanāda]; he subdued Indra, and thus became Indrajit.

rāśí m. heap, pile, stack; mass, quantity; group, multitude; set | astr. group of stars indicating a sign of the zodiac (Greek); their use dates back to 400 BC in India; there are 12 of them, associated with the constellations: meşa (Aries), vrsa (Taurus), mithuna (Gemini), karkata (Cancer), siṃha (Leo), kanya (Virgo), tula or vaṇija (Libra), vrścika (Scorpio), dhanus (Sagittarius), makara (Capricorn), kumbha (Aquarius) and mīna (Pisces) | math. by extension. angle or arc of 30° math. set of arguments of an arithmetic operation. rāśīkṛ to accumulate. rāśīkṛta amn accumulated. rāśībhū to accumulate. rāśībhūta amn formed into a heap; accumulated. rāśībhūtadhanaḥ m. who has accumulated wealth.

rāṣṭrá [instr. rāj₁] mn kingdom, empire; people, subjects | pali rattha. rāṣṭreṣu soc. under the jurisdiction of.

Rāṣṭrakūṭa [kūṭa] m. hist. n.p. of the Rāstrakūta dynasty of northern Karņātaka (810th century), founded by king Dantidurga in 733; their capital was Mānyakheta; they sponsored the construction of the cellars of Ellora; the Rāṣṭrakūṭās cultivated Sanskrit culture, not. in the court of King Kṛṣṇa₃; cf. Trivikrama₁.
rāṣṭrapa [pa₂] m. king ["protector of the kingdom"].
rāṣṭrapati [pati] m. sovereign | mod. government.
Rāṣṭrapāla [pāla] m. king ["protector of the royal me"] | bd. [Mahāyāna] np. of the venerable [āyuṣmat] Rāstrapāla.

rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā [paripṛcchā] f. lit. np. of the work [sūtra] bd. rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā "Questions of Rāṣṭrapāla"; the monk Rāṣṭrapāla questions the Buddha on the duties [dharma] of an accomplished [bodhisattva]; this text is earlier than the 6th century.
rāṣṭrabhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. language of the kingdom | mod. partisan designation of Hindi as the language of the Indian Union.
rāṣṭrabhṛt |bhṛt| m. soc. ved. ritual episode of the "support of the kingdom" during the sacrifice of the agnicayana; the adhvaryu priest pronounces the ya jus consecrating the 4 classes.
Rāṣṭrasenā [senā] f. myth. np. of Rāṣṭrasenā, falcon goddess of the Mewar mountains.
rāṣṭríya |iya| amnf rāṣṭriyā royal | mod. national — mr. var. rāṣṭrīya f. rāṣṭrīyā provincial governor. rāṣṭriyasaṃskṛtasthāna n. mod. National Sanskrit Center.
rāsa |*rasa| m. name of a round dance, not. that danced by Kṛṣṇa and the cowherds |gopī|.
rāsakrīdā [krīdā] f. myth. [BhP.] Kṛṣṇa's dance with the cowherds.
rāsabha [bha| mf rāsabhī bio. zoo. donkey; syn. khara, gardebha.

rāsāyana [*rasāyana] amnf rāsāyanā concerning the elixir of youth or remedies.
rāsāyanatantra [tantra] n. med. the science of elixirs, a section of Ayurveda.

Rahu [*rahu] m. myth. np. of influence [graha] Rahu, the daitya dragon who devours the Sun or the Moon during eclipses; he is the son of Vi pracitti and Simhikā [Saimhikeya]; he was beheaded by Vișnu while drinking the amrta he had stolen during the kṣīrodamathana, and only his head is immortal; his tail became the 9th graha Ketu; he is represented by a large head with an open mouth; his perishable body Ketu is represented as a serpent; he is Dānavapati, king of the
merfolk [dānavās]; cf. Jalandhara, Svarbhānu.
rāhuketu [Ketu] m. du. Rāhuketū myth. np. of Rāhuketū, the two influences [graha] Rāhu and Ketu together; cf. kṣīrodamathana.
rāhugama | gama | amnf rāhugamā eclipsed; as somber.
Rāhula₁ m. hist. np. of Rāhula₁, son of Prince Siddhārtha Gautama (future Buddha) and Yaśodharā; he is one of the 16 meritorious | arhat | hist. np. of the scholar bd. Rāhula₁; cf. Saraha.

Rivālasara n. geo. np. of Rivālasara, small pilgrimage town in the district of Mandī in Himachal Pradesh (mod. Rewalsar), also called Trisangam, and Tso Pema in Tibetan; it is situated on the edge of a lake, at an altitude of 1360; it is a sacred place for Hindus, Sikhs, and Buddhists, who revere Padmasambhava there.

Lit. literary style; mode of poetic composition; diction, manner of pronunciation; there are three principal ones: vaidarbhī, gaudī and pāñcālī, to which are added lāṭikā, āvantikā and māgadhī | bronze; brass; rust, oxidized metal. rasabhāvarītigaticatura amn skilled in tastes, feelings, turns of phrase and manners. rītirātmā kāvyasya |Vāmana₃| Style is the soul of poetry.

rukmin [ruc₁min] n. myth. [Mah.] np. of Rukmī "Gold-adorned", son of Bhīsmaka, adversary of Kṛṣṇa, defeated by Balarāma — f. Rukmiṇī myth. [Mah.] np. of Rukmiņī, his sister; promised by her father to Siśupāla, she secretly loved Kṛṣṇa, who abducted her at her request with the help of Balarāma; by him she bore Pradyumna; she is identified with Lakşmī.

(abhi, pra, vi) to shine, to gleam; to be beautiful | to seem beautiful or good, to be desirable, to please (to (dat. g.)) — ca. (rocayati) to make shine, to illuminate; to like, to prove || gr. λευκος; lat. lūceo; ang. light; all. Licht; fr. luciole. yadbhavate rocate as you please. mahyam madhuram rocate I like sweets. tasmā upakhyānam na rocate the story doesn't please him. Nāradāya rocate kalahaḥ The quarrel pleases Nārada.

Rudra [rud₁ra] m. myth. Vedic np. of Rudra "Tormentor" ["one who makes weep"], or "Furious" ["whose nature is raudra"]; savage chief of the breaths [marut], terrible deity; also epithet of Agni and Vedic prototype of Shiva; as Mṛgavyādha he pierced Prajāpati with his arrow during the primordial incest, and pinned him to Heaven as Mṛgaśiras; astr. himself presides over the nakṣatra Ardrā (Betelgeuse) — n. lit. hymn of the Kṛṣṇayajurveda | phil. he embodies metaphysical Wrath; at the end of the World [kalpānta] he emanates from the heads of the eternal dragon Ananta to destroy the degraded Universe | math. symb. the number 11; cf. ekādaśarudrās | pl. rudrās myth. np. of the rudrās, aspects of Rudra, son of Surabhī; cf. ekādaśarudrās — f. rudrā myth. [Mah.] np. of rudrā, one of the 7 "mothers (dangerous) of children" [śiśumātaras] associated with Skanda.
rudraganikā [ganikā] f. soc. sacred prostitute of a śaiva temple.
rudrádāman₁ [dāman₁] m. hist. np. of King Śaka Ru dradāmā; he reigned, with the title of mahākṣatrapa, from 120 to 150, and conquered the Mālava country from the Sātavāhanās.
Rudradeva | deva | mr. hist. n.p. of King Rudradeva of the Kākatīyās (1259–1289), actually Queen Rudrāmbā Rudradevī.
rudrabhatta | bhatta | m. hist. np. of Rudrabhatta, poet of the 12th-13th century, author of the Śrigāratilaka₁.
rudramuhūrta [muhūrta] m. astr. period of a laps [muhūrta] (48') preceding sunrise.

Rudrayāmala [yāmala] n. [rudrayāmalatantra] lit. np. of the Rudrayāmala tantra; this ancient (mythical?) text contains not. medical and chemical teachings, but also esoteric kaula liberation techniques; another homonymous text dates from the 14th century; cf. Parātrimśikā, Vijñānabhairava.
rudravīṇā [vīṇā] f. lute [vīṇā] from North India. rudrasāvarņa [sāvarņa] m. myth. n.p. of Ru drasāvarņa, 12ᵉ Manu of the kalpa.
rudrahrdayopanisad [hrdayaupanisad] f. bed. n.p. of the Rudrahrdayopanisad.

rudrākṣa [akṣa] m. bio. bot. Elæocarpus sphæri cus, small tree with lanceolate leaves, with grouped white flowers; its fruit, a brown and wrinkled seed, is used in medicine — n. ["eye of Rudra"] its seed, from which rosaries are made; myth. it is sacred to Shiva, because it came from the tears that Rudra shed when he had to destroy Tripura; syn. mālāphala.
rudrākṣamālā [mālā] f. rosary of rudrākṣa, also worn as a necklace or on the bun by the devotees of Shiva; it is said to warm the body.
Rudrādhyāya [adhyāya] m. lit. np. of the Rudrādhyāya, chapter of the Taittirīya saṃhitā.
rudrābhiṣeka [abhiṣeka] m. soc. rite of continuous sprinkling of the linga in a Shaivite sanctuary.

Rudrāmbhā [ambā] f. hist. np. of Rāṇī Rudrāmbā Rudramadevī, daughter of the king of the Kākatīyās or Ganapatideva who reigned in Ekasilā (mod. Waran gal); he having no male heir, he organized a putrikā ceremony to name her crown prince under the name of Rudradeva; she succeeded him at the age of 14, and reigned from 1259 to 1289; she married the prince Cālukya of the East Vīrabhadra₁; her reign was a succession of wars; she died fighting the rebellious kāyastha Ambadeva; her grandson Pratāparudra₁ succeeded her.
Rudrața m. hist. np. of the poet Rudrața; he lived in Kaśmīra in the 9th century; he is credited with the treatise on poetics Kāvyālamkāra₂; cf. turagabandha.

Ruma m. myth. |RV.| np. of Ruma, companion of Indra | geo. name of a mountain containing salt mines — f. Rumā geo. np. of the Rumā river geo. name of a salt lake.
rumanvat |vat| m. myth. np. of Rumanvān, eldest son of Jamadagni | lit. [KSS.] np. of Rumanvān₁, minister of King Udayana; he had a son named Hariśikha.

ruyyaka m. hist. np. of ruyyaka, a 12th-century Kashmiri scholar specializing in literary aesthetics; he is notably credited with the Alamkārasarvasva, the Sahṛdayalīlā, and the Saṃketa commentary on the Kāvyaprakāśa; his Vyaktivivekavyākhyāna is a critique of the Vyaktiviveka. হহ rúru |ruru| m. bio. zoo. Cervus duvauceli, barasingha deer | myth. [Mah.] np. of the hermit Ruru₁, son of Pramati and Pratāpī; at the hermitage of Sthūlakeśa he fell in love with the nymph Pra madvarā; on their wedding day, she died from a snake bite; Ruru₁ resurrected her by offering her half of his life; Sunaka is their son; Ruru₁ had become the enemy of the snakes which he wanted to exterminate; one day he met a dundubha snake, which was Sahasrapāda cursed by Kha gama, and which took on human form to dissuade him | myth. np. of the undine [dānava] Ruru₁ "Deer Demon"; he was defeated by the Goddess.
rurukrama [krama] m. ved. ["who jumps like an antelope"] epith. of Viṣṇu Trivikrama.

rúśama m. myth. |RV.| np. of Ruśama, companion of Indra — f. Ruśamā myth. np. of Ruśamā, who made a bet with Indra on who would circle the Earth the fastest; while Indra circled the Earth, Rusamā circled Kuruksetra and won.
