ruha [agt. ruh₁] ifc. amnf ruhā that makes rise, that makes spring forth (iic.) | that grows in (iic.).
rūkṣá amnf rūkṣā dry, arid; emaciated | harsh; rough | rough, brutal, cruel — v. [11] pr. (rūkṣayati) to be rough; to treat roughly; to insult, to offend.
rūkṣatā [tā] f. roughness; brutality; cruelty.
rūḍhá [pp. ruh₁] amnf rūḍhā mounted, climbed; pushed, developed | widespread, notorious; traditional, conventional | gram. idiomatic.
rūḍhārtha [artha] m. gram. conventional meaning of a word; opp. yaugikārtha.

rūdhi [agt. ruh₁] f. rise, development; progress | notoriety; usage, convention, tradition [rūdhilakṣaṇā] gram. traditional meaning of a word, fixed meaning (opp. yoga etymological meaning). yogād rūḍhir balīyasī gram. the traditional meaning prevails over the etymological meaning.
rūp [vn. rūpa] v. [10] pr. (rūpayati) pp. (rūpita) pf. (ni, Pra, prati) to figure, to represent (not. on the stage), to express by gestures.
rūpá [agt. rūp] n. figure, form; sign | appearance, exterior; aspect; image; color; species; nature | grace, beauty | phil. |Sāṃkhya| the

perception [tanmātra] of sight [cakṣus]; its regent [niyantr] is Aditya | phil. [Vaiśesika] the property [guṇa] of form or aspect | bd. form, one of the 5 aggregates [skandha] of the ego | math. symb. the number 1 | hist. np. of rūpa Gosvāmī, one of the six pastors of the Vṛndāvana, disciple of Caitanya (16th century); the Stavamālā is attributed to him. rūpaṃ kṛ taking the form of (nom.). kṛṣṇo rūpaṃ kṛtvā having taken a black form.
rūpakāra [kāra] m. sculptor.
rūpacandrikā |candrikā| f. gram. n.p. from the rūpacandrikā “Light on the form (of the word)”, a work of morphology from 1947 giving the inflection paradigms of Sanskrit.
rūpajīva [jīva] amnf rūpajīvā soc. ["who lives by her charms"] who prostitutes herself — f. rūpajīvā [rūpajīvanā] prostitute.
rūpatā [tā] f. act of taking form; manifestation.
rūpatva |tva| n. id.
rūpadhara | dhara | ifc. amnf rūpadharā which has the shape of iic. ; of the color of iic. . gorūpadhara amn in the shape of a cow.
rūpadhārin | dhārin | amnf rūpadhārinī qui as sume la forme de.
rūpadhṛt [dhṛt] amnf [sg. nom. rūpadhṛk] which has the form of (iic.). kapirūpadhṛk in the form of a monkey.
rūpadheya [dheya] n. colour; shape, appearance.
rūpábheda [bheda] m. phil. the science of forms and colors, a ṣaḍaṅgaśilpa.
rūpámañjarī [mañjarī] f. gram. np. from the Rūpamanjarī, a work listing morphological forms.
rūpámaṇḍana [maṇḍana] n. lit. du np. detailing Rūpamandana, the canonical iconographic representations.
rūpalatā [latā] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the beautiful princess rūpalatā, daughter of King rūpadhara and Queen He malatā on the island of Muktipura; she married King Pṛthvīrūpa.
rūpaśikhā [śikhā] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the beautiful rākṣasī rūpaśikhā, daughter of Agniśikha; she married Prince Śrigabhuja.
rūpásamṛddha [samṛddha] afmn rūpásamṛddhā soc. of perfect form; excellent in appearance.
rūpasamṛddhi [samṛddhi] f. soc. formal perfection (not. of a ritual act).
rūpasiddhi |siddhi| m. gram. mod. treatise giving the parameters of morphological generation of roots.
rūpasena [senā] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara rūpasena, younger son of King Muktāsena; he followed his elder Padmasena on Earth as Anicchāsena; cf. Parityāgasena.
rūpahāni |hāni| f. loss of form.
rūpārūpa | arūpa | amnf rūpārūpā phil. both with form and without form; said of Candra maulīśvara.
Rūpāvatāra [avatāra] m. lit. np. of the Rūpāvatāra, grammar of Sanskrit due to Dharmakīrti₁; it rearranges the rules of Pāṇini into functional blocks, inaugurating the prakriyā tradition.
rūpāvali [āvali] f. gram. list of inflected forms of Sanskrit | var. rūpāvalī id.
rūpa sf. form of flattering comparatives: sem blable à (like the French: sūryarūpa solar). paţurūpaḥ very skillful. pacatirūpam he cooks very well.

rūpaka [agt. rūp] amnf rūpikā allegorical, figurative — f. rūpakā ifc. which has the form of (iic.); similar to (iic.) — m. coin (of gold or silver), money — n. lit. [alaṃkāra] metaphorical identification, where the upameya is compared to the upamāna; metaphor, allegory | image; white resemblance; sign; symptom | lit. one of the 10 major genres of theatre, the most esteemed being the nāṭaka; cf. Daśarūpaka | mus. rhythmic cycle [tāla] comprising 1 druta and 1 laghu.
rūpakasamāsa [samāsa] m. gram. metaphorical compound, like mukhacandra "moon face".
rūpakātiśayokti [atiśayokti] f. bed. figure of speech of emphatic comparison; cf. sādhyavasānā.
rūpakotsava [utsava] m. theater festival.
rūpaṇa [act. rūp] n. illustration; metaphor investigation, examination.
rūpavat [rūpavat] amnf rūpavatī which has form, incorporated | beautiful, pretty — ifc. having the form or features of (iic.).
rūpavattara |compar. rūpavat| amnf rūpavattarā more beautiful than.
rūpi iic. rūpin.
rūpidāraka [dāraka] m. pretty boy.
rūpita [pp. rūp] amnf rūpitā represented; exhibited; imagined.

rūpin [agt. rūp] amnf rūpiṇī bodily; having such a form, beautiful, pretty — ifc. having the form of, characterized by (iic.) — f. rūpiņī [kāmaśāstra] one of the 4 types of women. rūpiņikā [ika] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of rūpiņikā, a courtesan of Mathurā, daughter of Makaradaṃṣṭrā; she fell in love with the poor Brahmin Lo hajangha.

rūpya [pfp. [1] rūp] amnf rūpyā which has a beautiful shape, pretty | printed, engraved — n. silver (metal) | minted coin | "bearing an effigy" | ; rupee — ifc. which was the possession of (iic.) ; from (iic.) || fr. roupie.
rūpyaka [ka] amnf rūpyakī of silver.
rūpyamaya |maya| amnf rūpyamayī in silver; containing money.
rūpyaratnaparīkṣā [ratnaparīkṣā] f. the examination of coins and jewels, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
Rūmā f. myth. |Rām.| np. of Rūmā, wife of Sugrīva then Vālī. ₹ re interj. (contemptuous) peuh! bah! re re interj. marks contempt and disrespect
rékṇas [abstr. ric] n. ved. inheritance; riches; or. rekņasvat |vat| amnf rekņasvatī rich.

rekhā [lekhā] f. line, row, series | sketch; drawing, painting; not. painted idol | math. straight line of the hand | small quantity | arch. temple style characteristic of Madhyadeśa and Kalinga; cf. pīdā, khākhārā — v. [11] pr. (rekhāyati) to approach. rekhīkṛ to align; to put in rows. rekhām na labh not to approach, not to come close to. rekhāgaņita [gaņita] n. lit. np. of the Rekhāgaņita, translation of Euclid's Elements from Arabic into Sanskrit by Jagannātha₄ (1728, Jaipur).
rekhāmātram [mātra] adv. not by a hair. kṣuṇṇādvartmano rekhāmātramapi na vyatīyuḥ he did not deviate by an iota from the path laid out.
rekhāśāstra [śāstra] n. phil. science of the lines of the hand.
reca [act. ric] m. expiry.

recaka [agt. ric] amnf recikā that empties, that purges — m. expiration | phil. [yoga] slow complete expiration through the nose; opp. pūraka | soc. oscillatory movements in dance [nartana] | syringe.
recana [agt. ric] amnf recanā which purges — act. n. act of emptying, purging, exhaling | med. purge.
recita [pp. ca. ric] amnf recitā emptied, purged, cleaned | abandoned — f. recitā name of a hand position in dancing.
Renu₁ [ri] m. grain or particle of sand, Dust, pollen; powder — f. myth. np. of Renu₁ "Dust", wife of Viśvāmitra | myth. np. of Renu₁, wife of Prasenajit, mother of Renukā.

reņuka m. soc. magic formula (used to bless weapons) — f. renukā myth. np. of Renukā, daughter of King Prasenajit and Renu₁; she married the sage | rṣi | Jamadagni; guilty of lust at watching the erotic frolics of King Kārtavīrya taking his bath (var. falling in love with the gandharva Citrasena at seeing his reflection in the river), she was cursed by Jamadagni and condemned to wander as a leper; recovering her beauty through her devotion to Shiva, she returned to Jamadagni who ordered his sons to behead her; Only the youngest, Paraśurāma, obeyed, and obtained as a vow to resurrect her, to be washed clean of the sin of matricide, and to restore the senses of his brothers who had been made stupid by their father's curse for disobeying him; it is said that at the time of her execution, she embraced an untouchable named Ellammā, to thank her for her sympathy, and they were beheaded together; when Jamadagni forgave her, he put the heads back on the bodies by his magical powers, but made a mistake; Reņukā returned to life with an untouchable's body as Māryammā, "Mother Rain", who brings disease (not. smallpox) and death, but also healing and resurrection; a shrine is dedicated to her at Māhūr, in the Mahārāṣṭra; It is the object of a cult pilgrimage to Saundatti, north of Karṇāṭaka, in common with Ellammā; goats and roosters are offered as sacrifices to Māryammā, and buffaloes to Ellammā; cf. Konkanā.

retas [abstr. ri] n. flow, current, libation | var. retana sperm | mercury (semen of Indra or Śiva). retah sic ejaculate. reto dhā (r.) to conceive. retahseka var. retasseka [seka] m. ejaculation; carnal relationship.

repha m. phon. guttural rolling of the sound 'r' gram. the letter 'ra'. ਨੇਮ rebha m. panegyrist, author of praises | myth. np. of the rṣi rebha, thrown into a well by the asurās; he remained there 10 nights and 9 days until he was saved by the Aśvinau.

revát [raivat] amnf revatī rich, prosperous; abundant; splendid — n. abundance, wealth, prosperity — f. revatī astr. 26th lunar asterism | nakṣatra|, corr. to the star of Pisces; Pūṣā presides over it; its symbol is a timpani | woman born under the sign of this asterism | myth. np. of revatī "Abundance", daughter of Revata; |BhP.| born in the era of the tretāyuga, she went with her father to the court of Brahmā and when they returned to Earth it was the dvāparayuga; men had become smaller, and to marry this giantess her father found only Balarāma of her size.
Revata [revata] m. myth. np. of the king Revata "prosperous", son of Anarta; he established his capital at Kuśasthalī; he is father of revatī.

revanta [revat] m. myth. np. of revanta "Splendid", son of Sūrya and Sañjñā; he is the leader of the hidden spirits | guhyakās | ; his stunning beauty bewildered Lakṣmī; cf. Ekavīra; in southern India he is identified with AyyanārSāstā.
Revā f. geo. np. of Revā, name of the Nar madā river.

Revākhanda |khanda| min reads. from np. Revākhanda, SP chapter. ₹ rai [obj. rā₁] m. [sg. name. voc. rās, acc. rāyam, i. rāyā, dat. striped; abl. g. rāyas, loc. rāyi; of. name. acc. voc. rāyau, i. dat. abl. rābhyām, g. loc. rāyos; pl. name. acc. voc. rāyas, i. rābhis, dat. abl. rābhyas, g. rāyām, loc. rāsu wealth — f. id. (rare). ₹ਮ raibha [*rebha] m. soc. patr. descendants of rebha.
Raibhya [*rebhaya] m. soc. clan of descendants of rebha | myth. | Mah. | n.p. of Raibhya, who killed Yavakrīta.

raivatá [*revata] amnf raivatī rich — m. myth. np. of Raivata₁ "the rich one", 5th Manu of the kalpa | myth. epith. of one of the 11 marutas, or of Siva myth. np. of Raivata₁ "born of revatī", giant who torments young children | myth. |Mah. | np. of Mount Raivata₁, east of Kuśasthalī; Ekala vya lived there; cf. raivataka — n. epith. of various hymns |sāman|.

raivataka [ka] m. geo. np. of Mount Raivataka "Opulence", in Surāṣṭra; it is celebrated as a place of pleasure and occult practices in the Siśupālavadha; mod. range of Girnar mountains in Gujarāt, sanctuary of the last Asiatic lions.
raivatika [*revatīika] m. myth. (matr.) son of revatī.
róga [act. ruj₁] m. disease.
rogaghna [ghna] amnf rogaghnā that heals — n. medicine.
rogada |da| amnf rogadā which makes one sick.
rogamukta [mukta] amnf rogamuktā [“freed from illness” | convalescent, cured.
rogalakṣaṇa | lakṣaṇa | n. med. symptom; pathology.
rogaviniścaya [viniścaya] m. med. n.p. from the Roga viniścaya of Mādhava₂; cf. Mādhavanidāna.
rogaśama [śama] m. med. convalescence.
rogita [Rogaita] amnf rogitā sick.
rogin [agt. ruj₁] amnf roginī sick.
rocaka [agt. ruc₁] amnf rocakā which illuminates, which stimulates | which gives appetite; pleasant, agreeable — m. stimulant; aperitif.
rocakin [agt. ruc₁] amnf rocakinī who appreciates, who takes pleasure in (loc.).

rocaná [agt. ruc₁] amnf rocanā bright, luminous; beautiful, charming; enchanting | tonic; stimulating the appetite — n. daytime sky; firmament | awakening of desire to (iic.) — f. cf. rocanā. rocanākr to please.
rocana [f. rocana] f. red lotus | pretty woman | [gorocanā] yellow pigment.
rócas [abstr. ruc₁] n. light, splendor.
rocís [abstr. ruc₁] n. brilliance, splendor; grace.
roṭī f. mod. bread, pancake | var. roṭikā id. | hi. roast.
rod [ca. rud₁] v. [10] pr. (rodayati) to make cry.
rodana [act. rud₁] n. lamentation, tears.
rodha₁ [agt. rudh₁] ifc. amnf rodhā (iic.) that which pushes, that which grows; that which rises to (iic.).
rodha₁ [act. rudh₁] m. act of restraining or closing; obstruction, blockade, siege; hindrance; dike.

rhodhra [contr. rudhira] m. bio. bot. Symplocos racemosa, a shrub with yellow flowers; it is used in medicine; its bark is used to make the red powder thrown at holī | var. lodhra id.. nītā rodhraprasavarajasā pāṇḍutām ānanaśrīḥ [MD.] The pollen from the rhodhra gives a golden sheen to the beauty of their face.
rop [ca. ruh₁] v. [10] pr. (ropayati) pp. (ropita) to raise, to grow; to plant.
ropa [act. ca. ruh₁] m. act of raising; planting.
ropaṇa [agt. ca. ruh₁] amnf ropaṇā who fixes; who plants — act. n. plantation.
ropita [pp. ca. ruh₁] amnf ropitā raised; planted.
roma₁ iic. roman.
roma₂ m. geo. the city of Rome, the Roman state.

romakūpa [kūpa] mn skin pore; syn. ro marandhra. Romapāda var. lomapāda | pāda | m. myth. | Rām. | np. of Romapāda "hairy-footed", king of the Angās, friend of Daśaratha; his capital was Campā; he was cursed by Indra for having lied to a brahmin, and the country suffered a long drought causing a famine; to stop these evils he gave his daughter Sāntā in marriage to the ascetic Rsyasriga.
romarandhra | randhra | n. skin pore; syn. romakūpa.
romarāji |rāji| f. fine line of hair on the belly of women, below the navel | var. romarājī id.

romavallī [vallī] f. organic. bot. Mucuna pruriens, velvet pea; syn. kapikacchu; cf. atmaguptā. romaharșa [harșa] m. piloerection (from pleasure, fear or cold); excitement. romaharșita [harșita] amnf romaharșitā which has the hairs that stand up (from pleasure, from fear); excited. [añca] m. piloerection, romāñca a sāttvikānubhāva — f. romāncā ifc. id.
romāvalī [āvalī] f. vertical line of hair above the navel; lit. it is evoked in erotic poetry.
romaka |ka| m. pl. romakās the Romans.
novel [related to loman] n. hair; antenna; you, sound, wool; fur | plumage (of a bird); scales (of a fish).
rómanvat |vat| amnf romanvatī hairy. śepo romanyantau bhedau icchati véd. [RV.] The penis desires the hairy vagina.
romaśa [śa] amnf romaśā hairy, shaggy; disheveled — m. sheep; pig, boar; various hairy plants.
romantha m. act of ruminating, of chewing — v. [11] pr. r. (romanthāyate) ruminate | lat. rumi nare; fr. ruminer.
romanthana [na] n. rumination.
rolamba m. bee.
rolambakadamba [kadamba] n. swarm of bees.
roṣ₁ [ca. ruṣ₁] v. [10] pr. (roṣayati) pp. (roṣita) to exasperate, irritate.
roṣ₂ [agt. roṣ₁] ifc. amnf [sg. nom. roṭ] that makes one angry, that enrages (iic.).
roṣa [act. ruṣ₁] m. anger; rage, passion, fury. rosena adv. with anger. roṣaṃ kṛ to be angry (against (g. loc. prati)).
roṣaṇa [agt. ruṣ₁] amnf roṣaṇā who is irritated, choleric; passionate (about or against g. iic. ).
rosita [pp. ros₁] amnf rositā irritated, exasperated, overheated.
roha [agt. ruh₁] amnf rohā that rises, that climbs — ifc. that has as a mount (iic.) — act. m. ascension; elevation | increase, growth; germination | bud; shoot.
Rohasena |senā| m. lit. |Mṛcchakaṭikā| np. of the young boy Rohasena "Army in the making", son of Cārudatta and Dhūtā.
rohaka [agt. ruh₁] amnf rohakā that rises, that ascends — ifc. that is mounted on, that rides (iic.) — m. myth. spirit, specter.

Rohaṇa [act. ruh₁] n. means of ascension | healing (of an injury) | sperm — ifc. act of mounting or riding (iic.) — m. bd. np. of rohana, master of Nāgasena | [rohanaparvata] geo. np. of Mount Rohaṇa₁, mod. Adam's Peak in Lankā.

Rohini [f. rohita] f. myth. np. of Rohini "Radiant One", epithet of Usha the Dawn, daughter of Prajapati, with whom he committed primordial incest at Creation; cf. mrgaśiras myth. np. of Rohini₁ "(Aldebaran the star) red", daughter of Daksha, favorite wife of SomaCandra; astr. its cosmological symbolization as the 2nd lunar asterism [nakshatra], corr. to the star Aldebaran; Prajapati presides over it; its symbol is the wheelbarrow. myth. np. of Rohini₂ "the (Red) Cow", daughter of Kashyapa and Surabhi, mother of Kamadhuk and cattle | myth. [Mah.] np. of Rohinī₃, 2nd wife of Vasudeva, who raised Balarāma in secret; [HV.] she embodies Surabhī on Earth.
Rohinīkunda [kunda] n. myth. np. of the Rohinīkunda liberation fountain, located near Nīlagiri Hill, in Purusottamaksetra.
rohiṇīvallabha [vallabha] m. myth. ["lover of rohiṇī₁"] the Moon god.
rohit [rohita] red amnf — m. the Sun — f. red deer.
rohitaśva [aśva] m. myth. np. of rohitaśva, epith. of Agni "who has red horses".

rohita [related to lohita] amnf rohiṇī red — m. the color red | blood | bio. zoo. Cyprinus ro hita, goldfish | ved. np. of rohita "The red", form of the Sun as creator of the world | myth. np. of Indra's bow "red" | myth. np. of Prince Rohitāśva — f. cf. rohinī | gr. ερυθρος; lat. ruber; ang. red; all. roth; fr. rouge. Rohitaka var. rohītaka [ka] m. bio. bot. Aphana mixis polystachya (or Andersonia Rohitaka), tree whose bark and seeds are used in medicine, notably for spleen ailments | geo. np. of the city of Rohitaka, mod. Rohtak in Hariyāṇa | rohītaka id.

Rohitāśva [aśva] m. myth. np. of King Rohitāśva “of the Red Horse”, son of Hariscandra of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa]; he bought Sunaḥśepa from his father to sacrifice him to Varuna in his place; Cuncu is his son.
rohin [agt. ruh₁] amnf rohinī that rises | that ascends towards (iic.) | that grows on (iic.) | that increases; that grows in number.
raukṣya [*rūkṣaya] n. dryness, harshness; from reté, harshness.
raucanika [*rocanāika] amnf raucanikī yellowish; bile color — n. dental tartar.
Raucya [*rucya] m. myth. np. of Raucya "who holds a bilva staff", 13th Manu of the kalpa.
raudhīya [*rūdhiīya] amnf raudhīyā np. of the Raudhīya grammar treatise | pl. members of the Raudhīya school. ghṛtarauḍhīya (pej.) grammar student for the benefit of meals.

Raudra [*Rudra] amnf raudrā f. raudrī violent, furious, savage, terrible; fatal — n. ferocity, savagery | lit. [aesthetics] the furious one, one of the 9 artistic modes [rasa]; it evokes the feeling of aggression; it is associated with the color red and the divinity Rudra — m. astr. np. of Raudra "furious", personifying the 54th year of a life cycle [saṃvatsara] — f. raudrī myth. np. of raudrī, śakti of Rudra.
raudrakāla [kāla₁] n. soc. "Rudra time", morning time (variable) considered inauspicious for starting an undertaking.

raudradhyāna [dhyāna] n. jn. harmful meditation; it is of four kinds: thinking about violence [himsā], thinking about a lie, thinking about stealing, thinking about getting rich; it is harmful, and leads to rebirths in hell; it characterizes the first five stages of spiritual development [guṇasthāna].
raupya [*rūpya] amnf raupyā silvered; in silver — n. silver.
raupyapītha |pītha| n. geo. np. of the Raupyapītha "Silver Base", pilgrimage center of the South Ka nara at Udupī.
raumaka [*romaka] amnf raumikā roman — m. Latin.
raurava [*ruru] amnf rauravā made from the skin of the ruru antelope | wild; frightening | bd. np. of raurava, one of the 8 burning hells, where the damned scream in pain.
rauravatantra [tantra] n. bed. n.p. of Rauravatan tra.
rauravāgama [āgama] m. lit. np. of the Rau ravāgama; it describes not. the gaurīpūjā.
la [contr. laghu] nota. phon. notation for a short syllable of one meter; opp. ga₃.

lagakriyā [ga₃kriyā] f. phon. number of meters having a given number of long and short syllables (binomial coefficients); cf. meruprastāra. °ল the form of the a. and secondary sn in the sense of matup

lakāra [(la)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'la' | gram. index of time or mood of a verb, whose endings are noted by an indeclinable abbreviation in the grammar of Pāṇini; their name begins with 'la': lat present, lan impar fact, lot imperative, lin optative/potential, lrt future, lut periphrastic future, lui aorist, lit perfect, lrn conditional (preterite of the future), lyap absolute tive, and let subjunctive/injunctive; āśīrlin denotes the precative/benedictative (optative of the aorist).
lakuṭa var. laguḍa m. club. lakuțin [in] amnf lakuținī who holds a mas sue.

lakuli iic. lakulin. lakulīśa var. lakulīśvara [īśa] m. myth. np. of La kulīśa, epith. of Šiva in the form of the "Lord La kulī"; he is represented as an ascetic meditating in the forest, and holding a club in his left hand | hist. ancient ascetic (2nd century?), founder of the pāśupata doctrine.

lakulin [related to lakuțin] m. hist. np. from muni Lakulī, ascetic of the 2nd century, considered as the last of the 28 manifestations [avatāra] of Shiva; his attribute is the club [lakuta]; he founded the pāśupata sect.

√ lakş v. |1| pr. r. (lakṣate) pp. (lakṣita) pfp. (laksya) pf. (ā, upa, vi) perceive — v. [1] pr. (lakṣati) recognize — ca. (lakṣayati) ca. r. (laksayate) indicate, designate; aim — ps. (lakṣyate) appear, show oneself. punarapi vaktukāma ivāryo laksyate Your honor seems to want to speak again.

lakṣá [agt. lakṣ] mn mark, sign | goal, target, prize, prey; wager (game) | appearance | 100000 || hi. lakh. lakṣīkr to make a mark or sign; to point at, aim, designate. iyam kathā māmeva lakṣīkaroti this story alludes to me. lakṣībhū to become a target or sign. ākāśe lakṣam bandh to stare into space. lakşasupta who appears to be sleeping.

lakṣaṇa [act. lakṣ] n. sign; favorable sign; mark, attribute; designation, name, description bd. one of the 32 canonical signs of an accomplished bodhisattva or buddha | gram. figurative or metaphorical meaning of a word; opp. abhidhā₂ phon. |śikṣā| traditional teaching of the meaning of syllables and their correct intonation in the Veda | phil. |Nyāya| definition; opp. lakṣya | gram. grammatical rule | [mus.] musical theory | lit. one of the 5 subjects treated by the mythological collections [pañcalakṣaṇa] | med. symptom — ifc. characterized by (2nd ed.); possessed by (2nd ed.) — f. cf. lakṣaṇā || Pali Lakkhana.

lakṣaṇalakṣaṇa | red. | n. phil. | Nyāya | definition of the term "definition": linguistic description of a concept free from the three faults [dosa₂] of excessive generality [ativyāpti], incompleteness [avyāpti] and inapplicability [asambhava].

lakṣaṇasaptamī |saptamī | f. gram. locative absolute.
Lakṣaṇāvalī [āvalī] f. bed. n.p. from the Lakṣaṇāvalī "Garland of definitions", philosophical work by Udayana₁.
lakṣaṇaika [eka] iic. gram. only the grammar rule.
lakṣaṇaikacakṣuṣka [cakṣuṣka] afmn lakṣaṇaikacakṣuṣkā gram. who only looks at the rules (of Pāṇini); opp. lakṣyaikacakṣuṣka.

lakṣaṇā [f. lakṣaṇa] f. purpose, object; indication; aim | gram. figurative meaning, metaphor; Mukula distinguishes 3 types: śuddhā, sāropā, and sādhyavasāna. śakyasambandho lakṣaṇā [Nyāya] The figurative meaning is close to the literal meaning. svabodhyasambandho lakṣaṇā |Mīmāṃsā| The figurative meaning is close to the literal meaning.
lakṣaṇāvṛtti | vṛtti | f. gram. figurative extension of the meaning of a word.
lakṣita [pp. lakṣ] amnf lakṣitā indicated, distinguished; noticed, examined, recognized | perceived; evident.
lakṣin [agt. lakṣ] amnf lakṣiṇī provided with good marks.
lakṣī iiv. lakṣá.
lakṣīkṛta |kṛta| amnf lakṣīkṛtā targeted, designated, marked.
lakṣīkṛtanāsa [nāsā] amnf lakṣīkṛtanāsī who fixes her gaze on the tip of her nose.

Lakṣmaṇa |lakṣmana| m. myth. |Rām.| np. of Laksmana "Happy omen", son of Dasaratha and Sumitrā, younger half-brother of Rāma, twin of Satrughna; he is the symbol of loyalty; he is said to be the incarnation of Seșa; he married Urmilā; cf. Meghanāda | myth. [Mah.] np. of Lakṣmaṇa₁, son of Duryodhana, killed in battle by Abhimanyu.

Lakṣmaṇagupta [gupta] m. hist. np. of Lakṣmaṇagupta, scholar of Kaśmīra (10th century), student of Utpaladeva; Abhinavagupta was his student. lakşmanadeva [deva] m. hist. np. of Lakṣmaṇadeva, king of Kaśmīra (1273–1286); Simhadeva succeeded him. lakşmanarekhā [rekhā] f. myth. [Rām.] "line of Lakṣmaṇa", which he drew around Sītā, leaving her alone in the forest; she was in no danger if she did not cross it; Rāvaņa, disguised as an ascetic, deceived her and made her cross it, so that he could abduct her | by extension, a line not to be crossed, a red line.
lakṣmaṇavatī [vat] f. geo. n.p. from the town of lakṣmaṇavatī to Gauda, capital of Laksmanasena; mod. Lakhnauti.

lakṣmaṇasena [Sena] m. hist. n.p. of king Laksmanasena, who ruled Bengal [Gauda] from 1179 to 1203, succeeding his father Vallālasena; its capital was Navadvīpa; his court included many Bengali Renaissance literati, including Jayadeva, Govardhana₁, Dhoyī, Halāyudha₁ and Saranadeva; his defeat by Turkish general Muhammed Bakhtiyar Khilji marked the end of the Sena dynasty.
lakṣman [lakṣman] n. mark, sign; favorable sign; stain.

Lakṣmī [lakṣman] f. [sg. nom. lakṣmīḥ, nom. Lakṣmī] beauty, radiance, splendor | prosperity, success; wealth, Fortune; royal dignity | myth. np. of Lakṣmī "Fortune", goddess of prosperity and luck, wife of Vishnu; she was born from a lotus churned from the primordial sea of milk [kṣīrodamathana]; she is depicted on a lotus pedestal, holding a lotus symbolizing abundance, often ruffled by two

elephants [gajalakṣmī]; she notably adorns the lintel of the sanctuary of temples |garbhagrha|; her mount is the owl [ulūka]; Thursday [guruvāra] is dedicated to her, and it is an auspicious day for marriages; she symbolizes the wife in the home; modernly, merchants invoke her when collecting money from a transaction; cf. Śrī, Padmā, Indirā, Bhagavatī, Ramā, Rukmiņī.
lakṣmīka [Lakṣmīka] ifc. m. whose Fortune is (iic.). putrasankrāntalaksmīkāh having devolved their fortunes among their sons.
lakṣmīdhara [dhara] m. hist. np. of lakṣmīdhara, sandhivigrahika minister of king Govindacandra of Kanyākubjā (12th century); he is the author of the Krtyakalpataru.
lakṣmīnārāyaṇa |Nārāyaṇa| n. myth. Lakṣmī and Nārāyana.

lakṣmīnṛsiṃha [nṛsiṃha] m. hist. np. of the scholar Lakṣmīnṛsimha, son of Kaundabhaṭṭa, and therefore great-nephew of Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita (17th century); he is the author of the advaita commentary Abhoga of the Kal pataru; Hari₂ Dīkṣita is his son.

Lakṣmīpati [pati] m. soc. ["Bridegroom of Fortune"] princely title | myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa | hist. np. of the renunciant Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha (15th century); he took Nityānanda at age 13 as his disciple and traveling companion. lakşmīpūjana [pūjana] n. soc. homage to Lakşmī paid by the young couple returning to the husband's house after their marriage.
lakṣmīpūjā [pūjā] f. soc. great festival of Lakṣmī, celebrated on the second day of the festival of dīpāvali, at the new moon.
lakṣmībhārya [bhāryā] m. ["who has Lakṣmī as a wife" Visnu.
lakṣmīvat [vat] amnf lakṣmīvatī prosperous, fortunate, rich; lucky | pretty, splendid.

[Nyāya] term to be defined; opp. lakṣaṇa | gram. object of a grammatical rule | lit. usage of language, literature | | mus. | practice of an instrument. laksyam labh to succeed. laksyam bandh to set oneself as a goal (loc.). laksyīkr to set oneself as a goal (iic.). lakṣyībhū to become a target. lakşyamūlam lakşanam [Kṣīrasvāmī] The rule is supported by the example.
lakṣyatā |tā| f. state of being visible; state of being the goal phil. [Nyāya] state of being definable. laksye laksyatā vartate phil. [Nyāya] Definability resides in the definable.
laksyabheda [bheda] m. act of striking the target.
lakṣyalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. of. gram. concept and its definition; word and its derivation. laksyalaksane vyākaranam gram. |Kātyāyana| Grammar combines words and rules.
laksyalaksanabhāva | bhāva | m. relation between a concept and its definition | lit. relation between rasa and kāvya.

lagna |pp. lag| amnf lagnā attached to, ac hooked to, stuck to; that which permeates; permanently fixed, attentive to, absorbed in (loc.) | that which began to (inf.); that which immediately follows | past, elapsed (time) — mn math. point of intersection of two curves astr. conjunction of the planets or stars with the horizon; not. entry of the sun into a zodiac sign | by extension, favorable moment to enter; critical time. sa pathane lagno'sti he is absorbed in his studies. anāvrstih sampadyate lagnā a period of drought is imminent.

laghumasūrikā [masūrikā] f. med. chickenpox.

stanzas [śloka] of the Yogavāsiṣṭha, due to Abhi nanda; a Persian translation of 1597 contributed to its dissemination.

√ lap v. [1] pr. (lapati) pp. (lapita) inf. (la pitum) pf. (ā, ut, pra, vi, sam) to talk, to chatter; to whisper, to babble; to murmur | to lament; to cry — ca. ( lāpayati ) to make someone talk.

labdhalakṣa [lakṣa] amnf labdhalakṣā who hit the target; who won the prize |tried, tested; skilled; who has proven himself in loc. .

√ lubh v. [4] pr. (lubhyati) pft. (lulobha) pp. (lubdha) pfp. (lobhanīya) pf. (vi) to desire, covet ter (g. loc.); to experience a violent desire — ca. (lobháyati) ca. r. (lobhayate) to seduce, attract — in tens. r. (lolubhyate) to covet intensely lat. lubet , libido ; ang. to love; all. lieben.
√ lul v. [1] pr. (lolati) pp. (lulita) to waver, to sway, to tremble; to become agitated.
lulita [pp. lul] amnf lulita agitated; shaken, swayed | undone, disordered (hair) | damaged, destroyed — n. movement, swaying.

√ ; lū₁ ; v. ; [9] ; pr. ; (lunāti) ; pr. ; r. ; (lunīte) ; pp. ; (lūna) pfp. (lavya) pf. (ati) to cut, split; to pluck, tear off — intens. r. (lolūyate) to cut with force | gr. v ; lat. solūtus; all. los, lösen; ang. less, to lose. lolūyāṃcakre he cut with force. dātreņa lūnavān having cut with the sickle.
lū₂ [agt. lū₁] ifc. amnf that cuts, that divides (iic.) | that picks (iic.).
lūtā f. bio. spider. lūtātantu | tantu | m. spider web.
lūna [pp. lū₁] amnf lūnā cut, sliced; picked, plucked; harvested.
lūnapakṣa |pakṣa| amnf lūnapakṣā with clipped wings. লু <u>ङ্</u> lṛṅ note. gram. conjugation suffix [lakāra] of the conditional |kriyātipatti|.
lṛṭ nota. gram. conjugation suffix |lakāra| of the future | bhavisyantī].
lekh [ca. likh] v. [10] pr. (lekhayati) to write.
lekha [act. likh] m. writing, letter — f. cf. lekhā. lekhakāra | kāra | m. scribe; writer.
lekhāvali [āvali] f. line of writing.
lekhaka [agt. likh] amnf lekhikā who writes — m. act of transcribing | copyist, scribe; writer — f. lekhikā woman who writes
lekhana [act. likh] n. writing, copy; article — f. lekhanā f. lekhanī quill, reed pen, brush | mod. pen, pencil.
lékhā [f. lekha] f. writing | line; drawing; painting.
Let nota. gram. lakāra of the subjunctive/injunctive. patāti vidyut véd. May lightning strike!
lep [ca. lip] v. [10] pr. (lepayati) to coat with (i.); to cover, to re-cover.

lepa [act. lip] m. act of coating, plastering, varnishing, painting | coating, plaster, varnish; layer of paint | impurity, grease | soc. rinse of frande to the three ancestors | tripindī|, used as an offering to the manes [pitaras] of degrees 4, 5 and 6.
lepana [act. lip] n. act of coating, plastering, varnishing | coating, plaster, mortar, varnish.
lelā v. [10] pr. (lelāyati) to tremble. lelāyamāṇā f. myth. ["trembling"] epith. of one of the 7 languages of Agni.
lesa [obj. liś] m. particle, small piece.

leha [agt. lih₁] m. that which licks; that which suckles, laps, gathers nectar | ast. one of the 10 ways of producing oneself from an eclipse — obj. n. (to lick, to suckle) syrup. madhuno lehah bee. kṣīráleham adv. in order to suckle the milk.
lehana [act. lih₁] n. action of licking, suckling, lapping.

loká [act. lok] m. place, location | the World, the universe; the earth, here below | the people; the people | pl. lokās humanity, society; the people; affairs | myth. the 7 worlds: Bhū the earth, where men [nara] dwell, Bhuvar the Between-heaven-earth, where the accomplished [siddha₁] dwell, Svar the sky, where Indra and the gods | deva| dwell, Mahar or Ma harloka, above the pole star, where Bhrgu and the sages [rsi] who survive the dissolution of the World dwell, Janaloka, where Sanatkumāra and other sons of Brahmā dwell, Taparloka, where the renunciant ascetics |vairāgin| dwell, and Satyaloka where Brahmā dwells, and where those who are freed from rebirths are transported; These worlds correspond to 7 levels of consciousness; there are also 7 subterranean worlds: Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Rasātala, Talātala, Mahātala, and Pātāla | math. symb. the number 7 — ifc. which went to heaven from (iic.) | lat. locus; ang. location; fr. place, local. loke adv. in place of (g.) | here below. ihaloke adv. here below. trīmlokāh the three worlds. tasya lokah sa u loka eva phil. [BU.] The World belongs to him; he is the World itself.
lokakṣaya [kṣaya₂] m. phil. destruction of the world.

lokakṣayakṛt [kṛt₂] amnf destroyer of the World. kālo'smi lokakṣayakṛt pravṛddho lokān samāhartum iha pravrttah [BhG.] I am Time having reached its end as destroyer of the World, put to the task of annihilating the World here below.
lokátraya | traya | n. myth. the 3 worlds: bhūr, bhuvar, svar₃; a brahmin makes the ritual proclamation [vyāhṛti] — f. lokatrayī id.
lokádvaya | dvaya | n. phil. the 2 worlds: Heaven and Earth.
Lokanātha | nātha | m. myth. np. of Lokanātha "Protector of the worlds", epith. of various gods king, sovereign | bd. epith. of Buddha.
lokanyāya | nyāya | amnf lokanyāyā known by common sense or by common usage; customary.
lokanyāyasiddha |siddha₁| amnf lo kanyāyasiddha gram. refers to rules of common sense that are not explicit in Aştādhyāyī.
lokapakti [pakti] f. ved. ["cooking of the World"] the perfection of the World, a duty of brah mane.
lokápāla [pāla] m. king ["guardian of the World"] | myth. cf. dikpāla. Lokapurușa [purușa] m. jn. np. of the cosmic Man Lokapurușa, the World personified.
Lokaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. bed. n.p. of Lokaprakāśa, didactic work by Vyāsadāsa Kṣemendra (11th century).
lokayātrā [yātrā] f. the profane world; the world as it is, affairs.
lokavākya |vākya| n. bed. proverb; syn. lokokti.
lokávārttā [vārttā] f. local customs; folk stories, rumors.

lokáVigraha [Vigraha] m. hist. np. of the king of Kalinga, Lokavigraha, of the Vigraha dynasty; he reigned around 600. lokáviśruta viśruta amnf lokaviśrutā re named throughout the world. lokávrtta vrtta n. customary practice; usual behavior | social interactions; banal conversation.

lokávyavahāra [vyavahāra] m. current events, everyday affairs | gram. usage (of the language). lokásamgraha var. lokasangraha | samgraha | m. the good of the World, the happiness of humanity | phil. [BhG.] the cohesion of the World.
lokasabhā |sabhā| f. mod. chamber of deputies.
lokasāt |sāt| adv. for the common good; for the public.
lokasātkṛta |kṛta| amnf lokasātkṛtā intended for the public.
lokasāmānya |sāmānya| amnf lokasāmānyā generally common.
lokasundarī | sundarī | f. (woman) "whose beauty is famous throughout the world".
lokahita [hita₂] amnf lokahitā beneficial to the World — n. well-being of the World. lokahitāya for the well-being of society.
lokācāra |ācāra| m. social behavior; my life.
lokānanda [ānanda] m. lit. np. of the lokānanda "Joy of the World", play [nāṭaka] at tribuée to Candragomī; the heroes of it are Maṇicūḍa and his wife Malayavatī.
lokānukṛti [anukṛti] f. conformity to traditional usage.
lokāyata [āyata] amnf lokāyatā materialist — n. phil. materialism; cf. Cārvāka | phil. more gen. positivism (e.g. nyāya and vaiśesika).
lokāyatika |ika| mr. phil. materialist.
lokāloka | aloka | m. myth. np. of the chain of mon tagnes lokāloka surrounding the universe and separating the visible world from darkness.
lokāśraya |āśraya| amnf lokāśrayā conforms to usage | gram. attested in common usage.
lokāśrayatva [tva] n. quality of being in common use. lingam aśisyam lokāśrayatvāl lingasya gram. [Patañjali₁] Gender does not need to be taught, as it is based on common usage.
Lokeśvara [īśvara] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] np. of the perfect [bodhisattva] Lokeśvara "Master of the world of" | myth. np. of Lokeśvara₁ "Master of the World", epith. of SivaVirūpākṣa.
lokokti [ukti] f. bed. proverb; syn. lokavākya.
lokottara [uttara₁] amnf lokottarā extraordinary, which transcends the material world; supernatural — m. phil. being which has attained divine realization.
lokottaratva [vat] n. supernaturality, transcendence.
lokottaravādin [vādin] m. pl. lokottaravādinaļi followers of the Lokottaravādī school of the bd. Mahāsāmghikās; their language is called "Buddhist Sanskrit"; cf. Mahāvastu.
lokottarāhlāda [āhlāda] m. transcendent pleasure.

lokátas [adv. loka] adv. of the people, of the common folk by common usage. siddhe śabdārthasambandhe lokataḥ arthaprayukte śabdaprayoge śāstrena dharmaniyamah yathā laukikavaidikesu gram. [Kātyāyana] The exact relationship between the word and its meaning being established by common usage, in the use of language in accordance with its meaning, (grammatical) science restricts For the purposes of dharma, in common usage as in the Veda.
lokana [act. lok] n. act of looking; vision, contemplation.
lokanīya [īya] amnf lokanīyā visible; to look at.
lokam [acc. loka] iic.

lokamprna [pṛṇa] amnf lokampṛṇā that fills the space; hole-filler — f. lokampṛṇā ved. brick |iṣṭakā| hole-filler of the agnicayana. lokamprna chidramprna ved. [SB.] Fill the space, Fill the hole (said while placing a hole-filler brick).
lokya [pfp. [1] lok] amnf lokyā real, of this world, earthly; usual, ordinary; widespread throughout the world | which leads to a better world — n. free space | sphere.
lokyatā [tā] f. improvement of the world | phil. materialism; cf. cārvākās.
loga m. clod of earth or clay.
logākṣa [akṣa] m. ["With bulging eyes"] man's name.
√ loc [related to lok] v. [1] pr. r. (locate) pp. (lo cita) pf. (to have.
locaka [agt. loc] amnf locikā [“who has a fixed gaze” idiot; inanimate — m. pupil of the eye frown.
Locana [agt. loc] amnf locanā qui illu mine, qui éclaire — n. eye; gaze | lit. comment; not. np. du Locana, commentaire du Dh vanyāloka par Abhinavagupta.
loṭ noted. gram. lakāra of the imperative [vidhi].
Lota m. tears | Aries.
lodhra cf. rodhra.
lopa [act. lup] m. loss, disappearance; interruption; destruction, pillage; violation, transgression | gram. elision; elision, loss of a suffix perplexity — f. cf. lopā.
lopana [act. lup] n. violation, transgression omission.
lopā [f. lopa] f. organic. quail.

Lopāmudrā [mudrā] f. myth. np. of Lopāmudrā, wife of the sage [ṛṣi] Agasti; it is said that she was made by Agasti from the most beautiful parts of various animals, and secretly brought into the palace of the king of Vidarbha to be raised as his daughter; she incited Agasti to conquer the riches of the daitya Ilvala; he gave her the choice between 1000 ordinary sons, or 100 sons with tenfold strength, or 10 sons of one hundredfold strength, or a single son 1000 times nobler; she chose to have only one son, and 7 years after her conception gave birth to Drdhadasyu, who recited the Veda from his birth; cf. Vaidarbhī.
lopin [agt. lup] ifc. amnf lopinī who sup prime; who offends, who transgresses (iic.).
loptra [instr. lup] n. stolen goods, booty. loptragṛhīta caught in the act of plundering.

lobha [act. lubh] m. perplexity, confusion; im patience | envy, desire, covetousness (of (g. loc. iic.)); concupiscence, greed; avarice, avarice | myth. np. of lobha "the Miser", personifying avarice, son of Dambha and Pușți. lobhamūlāni pāpāni Greed is the root of all vices. lobhāt krodhaḥ prabhavati Anger stems from avarice.
lobhana [agt. lubh] amnf lobhanā desirable, seductive — act. n. seduction; temptation.
lobhanīya [pfp. [2] lubh] amnf lob hanīyā desirable, coveted | that which seduces, that which attracts.
lobhin [agt. lubh] amnf lobhinī who desires, who covets ((iic)); greedy, avaricious | who charms, who seduces.
loma iic. loman.
lomaghna | ghna | n. hair loss.

lomapāda [pāda] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Lo mapāda "Hairy-feet", king of the Anga country; cf. Romapāda. lomaharșana [harșana] n. horripilation; goosebumps — amnf lomaharṣaṇā exciting; that which gives chills, terrifying — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of
herald [sūta₂] Lomaharṣaṇa "who makes the hair stand on end"; Ugraśravā is his son; the original collection of mytho-logical books [purāṇa], or mūlasaṃhitā, is attributed to him.
loman n. hair (of the body) — m. loma f. lomā ifc. that has hair (iic.). lomatas adv. (skin) of the hairy side; opp. māmsatas.

lomaśa [lomanśa] amnf lomaśā hairy, hairy — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the venerable [devarși] lomaśa "With long hair"; he met Arjuna in the Svarga heaven of Indra; Indra explained to him that Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa were Nara and Nārāyaṇa, and sent him to Kāmyaka to report to Yudhişthira and help the Pāṇdavās; he traveled with them to many sacred places [tīrtha], and told them many stories of olden times.
lola [agt. lul] amnf lolā mobile; qui fris sonne, qui frémit, qui flitte; inconstant agité, qui ne tient pas place desirant, greed de (loc. inf. iic.).
lolajihva | jihva | amnf lolajihvā | “tongue-waving” greedy, insatiable — f. lolajihva myth. epith. of Kālī or of Tārā₁.
lolita [pp. ca. lul] amnf lolitā agitated, shaken.
lolupa [agt. intens. lup] amnf lolupā avid — act. f. lolupā avidity, ardent desire for loc. .
lolupatā [tā] f. greed, avarice.
lolupatva |tva| n. id.
loluva [intens. lū₁] amnf loluvā which cuts with force.
lolūya [intens. lū₁] amnf lolūyā that cuts with force — f. lolūyā determination to cut.
lolūyavat [vat] amnf lolūyavatī determined to cut.
loṣṭá mn clod of earth or clay — n. rust. samátrnamanilostakāñcana amn ["who attaches the same value to a blade of grass, a jewel, earth or gold" | indifferent to wealth.
lostághāta [ghāta] m. blow struck by a clod of earth. lostaghātam han to stone. sa lostaghātam hatah he was stoned.
lostághna [ghna] m. harrow.
lostra cf. losta.
Loha [related to lū₁] n. copper; iron; metal in general.
lohakāra [kāra] m. black-smith.
lohakumbhī [kumbhī] f. bd. n.p. from hell Loha kumbhī "Metal urn".

lohajangha [janghā] m. lit. [KSS.] np. du brah mane sans le sou lohajangha "Iron Leg"; the courtesan Rūpinikā fell in love with him, and her mother Makaradamṣṭrā had him beaten; he arrived by accident in Lankā, where King Vibhīṣaṇa procured for him a bird of the race of Garuda which he used as a mount to pass himself off as Vișnu in the eyes of his beautiful woman; he took revenge on Makaradamstrā and was honored by the king.
lohamaya |maya| amnf lohamayī in iron; metal.
Lohara [ra] m. geo. n.p. from the Lohara country to Kaśmīra and the dynasty of its princes (11th to 13th centuries); cf. Saṃgrāmarāja, Ananta₁, Jayasiṃha₇.
lohavedha | vedha | mr. (alchemy) transmutation of copper (into gold).

lóhita [Lohaita] amnf lohitā f. lohinī red | made of copper — m. the color ruby red astr. the planet Mars | red rice; red lentil | np. of man "The Red" | pl. his descendants — n. red substance; ruby; blood — f. lohitā myth. one of the 7 languages of Agni [saptajihva] — f. lohinī woman red with anger — v. [11] pr. (lohitāyati) v. |11| pr. r. (lohitāyate) to become red, to blush. lohitam kr to shed blood.
lohitaka [ka] amnf lohitikā dyed or painted red; turned red (with anger, etc.) — m. ruby.
lohitagangam [gangā] adv. where the Ganges is red.
lohitākṣa |akṣa| amnf lohitākṣī who has red eyes.
lohitāyanī [āyana₁] f. phil. [Tantra] np. of Lohitāyanī, infanticidal influence said to be one of the "mothers" of Skanda; she is associated with the ka damba tree.
laukāyata [*lokāyata] n. phil. materialism, professed by Cārvāka.
laukāyatika [*lokāyataika] amnf laukāyatikī phil. materialist.

laukika [*lokaika] amnf laukikī ter restre; ordinary, common; temporal, profane; uneducated | gram. said of classical Sanskrit, opp. Vaidika — m. common man | pl. laukikās the people, humanity — n. profane thing, ordinary occupation. laukikī vivakṣā [Patañjali₁] language conforming to common usage.
laukikadevatā [devatā] f. soc. popular deity.
laukikanyāya [nyāya] m. popular maxim | gram. |Patanjali₁| maxim illustrating the use of language.
Laukikanyāyaratnākara [ratnākara] m. lit. np. from the Laukikanyāyaratnākara "Mine of popular maxims", by Raghunātha₅ Varmā.
laukikanyāyasamgraha [samgraha] m. lit. np. du laukikanyāyasamgraha "Collection of popular maxims", by Raghunātha₅ Varmā.
laukikavigrahavākya [vigrahavākya] n. gram. canonical Sanskrit rapphrase of the meaning of a compound word; opp. alaukikavigrahavākya.
laugākṣi [*logākṣa] m. hist. patr. of laugākṣi Bhāskara₂, logician of the 14th century, author of the Tarkakaumudī. [9
laulya [*lolaya] n. greed, avarice; passion for (loc. iic.) | phil. [gaudīya] ardent desire for redemption through divine love.
laulyatā [tā] f. ardent desire; greed.
lauhitya [*lohitaya] n. red color — m. variety of red grain rice | geo. np. of the lauhitya river "reddish", epith. of the Brahmaputra.
lyap noted. gram. lakāra of the absolutive in ya.
lyu nota. gram. primary affix [krt₂] forming the agent of the action after certain roots, such as nandana.
lyut nota. gram. primary suffix [kṛt₂] of the verbal noun in ana denoting the activity associated with the verb (ex. bhojana).

√ v. [4] pr. r. (styāyate) pp. (styāna) dur cir; se congeler; augmenter, s'étender | répercuter (un son).

vamśá m. bamboo, reed, or sugarcane cane; beam | spine | flute (in bam bou) | soc. lineage, race, family, dynasty; multitude | lit. chronicle (of a dynasty) | soc. caste; cf. trivamsa | lit. the genealogy of the gods and sages, a pañcalakṣaṇa — ifc. collection, assemblage of, multitude of (ii.) — f. cf. vaṃśī. sūryavamśa myth. solar lineage; cf. Vivasvān, Manu, Ikṣvāku, Daśaratha, Rāma. somavamśa myth. lunar lineage; cf. Budha, Pūru, Duşyanta, Purūravā, Bharata, kuru, Sāmtanu. nṛpavaṃśadīrgham nāsāvaṃśam dadhānaḥ (said of King Skandagupta by Bāṇa₂) Sporting a nose as long as his dynasty.
vaṃśabrāhmaṇa |brāhmaṇa| mr. bed. n.p. of Vamsabrāhmana of Sāmaveda; Sāyana commented on it.
vamśastha [stha] m. phon. name of a homosyllabic meter of 12 syllables per pada, of jata jara pattern. vamśānkura ankura m. bamboo shoot, used in medicine.
vamśānucarita [anucarita] n. lit. the history of the dy nasties, a pañcalakṣaṇa.
vamśāvalī [āvalī] f. bed. dynasty chronicle.
vaṃśin [vaṃśain] amnf vaṃśinī appar tenant à une famille.
vaṃśī [f. vaṃśa] f. flute (bamboo) | myth. not. the flute of Kṛṣṇa Gopāla.
vaṃśīya [vaṃśaīya] amnf vaṃśīyā of the family | of good family.

vaṃśya [vaṃśaya] amnf vaṃśyā which relates to the dynasty | originating from the spine (said of bones of the limbs) — m. soc. member of the lineage; prince of blood — n. collegiality | pl. soc. members of a lineage; descendants of a dynasty.
vaka m. cf. baka.
vakāra |(va)kāra| m. the sound or letter 'va'.
vaktavya [pfp. [3] vac] n. that which must be said, that which has to be said. sarvaih satyam vaktavyam the truth must be told by all.
vakti [act. vac] f. speech.
vaktu [inf. vac] iic. to speak.
vaktukāma [kāma] amnf vaktukāmā who wants to speak.

vaktṛ [agt. vac] amnf vaktrī who speaks, who says, who proclaims (g.); eloquent | wise; honest; sincere | loquacious; talkative — m. speaker, articulate; orator || pali vattā. samskrtavaktārah the speakers of Sanskrit.
vaktṛtā |tā| f. ease of speech; eloquence; ba vardage.
vaktrtva |tva| n. id.
vaktrvivakṣā [vivakṣā] f. gram. speaker's desire to communicate. vaktṛvivakṣādhīnam gram. under the control of the speaker's desire to communicate.
vaktra |instr. vac| n. mouth; face.

vaktrāgama [āgama] amnf vaktrāgamā trans mis orally. śivavaktrāgamodita reputed to come from the mouth of Shiva himself. বক্ষ vakrá [vañcra] amnf vakrā curved, sinuous, tortuous, twisted; oblique, crooked | ambiguous, disloyal, false. vakrībhū to twist, to bend | astr. (planet) to retrograde.
vakrátā [tā] f. curvature; the state of being twisted or tortuous | ambiguity; perversity; falsehood, mzl honesty | lit. oblique quality of poetry, Kuntaka's aesthetic criterion.

vakrátunda [tunda] m. myth. np. of Vakratunda, epith. of Ganesa "with the curved trunk". Vakratunda mahākāya sūryakoṭisamaprabha nirvighnam kuru me deva sarvakāryeşu sarvadā || (invocation to Ganesa for the success of an undertaking) O Lord with the curved trunk, with the mighty body and the radiance of a million suns, may you remove the obstacles from all the actions that I undertake.
vakrabhanita | bhanita | n. ambiguous remark.
vakrarekhā [rekhā] f. math. curve.
vakrokti [ukti] f. lit. ["oblique speech"] veiled, metaphorical or double entendre language, genre
poetic | kāvya | cryptic; Kuntaka distinguishes 6 processes at different linguistic levels: phonetic composition [varṇavinyāsa], the choice of nominal themes [padapūrvārdha], the use of suf
fixed [pratyayāśrita], the allusive discourse [vākya], the arrangement of chapters | prakarana | and the whole composition | prabandha | | charade, rebus, word games; cf. ślesa.
vakroktijīvita [jīvita] m. lit. np. from Vakrok tijīvita "Vitality of the oblique word", a work on poetics by Kuntaka; he argues that the genre
oblique | vakrokti | Is the essence of poetry. vakroktiķ kāvyajīvitam lit. [Kuntaka] Poetry finds its Vitality in suggestion.
vakroktipañcāśikā [pañcāśaka] f. bed. n.p. from the vakroktipañcāśikā, poem of 50 rebus verses by rājānaka Ratnākara₂ forming a loving dialogue between Siva and Pārvatī.
vakrolaka m. [vakraloka] lit. [KSS.] np. from the town of vakrolaka, capital of king Sūryaprabha.
√ vakṣ [related to ukṣ] v. pft. (vavakṣa) to grow, to increase; to be strong — ca. (vakṣayati) to make grow, to strengthen, to invigorate | ang. wax.
vákṣaṇa [agt. vakṣ] amnf vakṣaṇī that which refreshes, that which invigorates — n. invigorating | chest; breast — f. vakṣáṇā stomach; entrails; belly; fertile ground.
vákṣas [abstr. vakṣ] n. (sg. and pl.) chest, rib cage; breast — m. ved. ox.
vakṣaḥsthala |sthala| n. chest.

vaksoja [ja] m. breast ["born from the breast"]. vakṣojapānakṛt kāṇa ["little one-eyed man who still suckles at his mother's breast" insult of the logician Pakṣadhara towards his insolent student Raghunātha₁ Siromaṇi.
vakṣu [vakṣu] m. geo. np. of the river vakṣu (Oxus), which descends from the Pamir to the Aral Sea; mod. AmouDaria.

Vagalā f. phil. [Tantra] np. of Vagalā or Va galāmukhī, one of the 10 powers [mahāvidyā] of the Goddess [Sakti], later called Bagalā or Ba galāmukhī; she is also Pītāmbarā "clothed in yellow"; she holds a club in her hand with which she strikes men to destroy their ignorance; her gaze is hypnotic; she transcends opposites and her knowledge destroys dualities; her yantra is a 6-pointed star with hrī om in its center.
vagāha |avagāha| mr. bath, ablution; immersion.
vagāhya |avagāh| ind. having plunged into. বহু vanka [agt. vanc] m. vagabond | meander (of a river) — f. vankā saddle pommel.

vaṅkú [vañcu] amnf ved. one who goes by roundabout means; one who hurries; impulsive. vankuḥ kaviḥ myth. "Obscure poet", epithet of Ru dra. বন্ধ Vanga m. myth. np. of King Vanga, son of Dīrghatamā and Sudeṣṇā; he is said to be the ancestor of the ben galis | geo. his kingdom, one of the five countries of North India | pañcagauḍa | ; mod. East Bengal | pl. vangās the land of Bengal and its people | |vangana| bio. bot. Solanum melongena, eggplant || bengali bafga; fr. Bengal.
vangasenā [senā] f. Bengal Army.
vangasenāka [ka] m. bio. bot. Sesbania grandi flora or Agati tree, legume that can reach 10 in height, with scarlet flowers.
vangana [Vangana] m. organic. bot. Solanum walked alongside me, eggplant; syn. vārttāka || Persian baaden jaan; fr. eggplant; hi. baimgan.

√ vac v. [2] pr. (vakti) imp. (voci) v. [3] pr. (vi vakti) pft. (uvāca) pft. r. (ūce) aor. [2] (avocat) aor. ps. (avāci) aor. ps. (avoci) subj. (vocati) pp. (ukta) ppft. (ūcivas) inf. (vaktum) fut. péri. (vaktā) pfp. (vaktavya, vacanīya) abs. (uktvā, ucya) pf. (adhi, anu, ni, nis, pra, prati, vi) to speak; to say something to someone (2 acc.); to express; to call | to recite, to invoke — ps. (ucyáte) to be said, to be spoken | to be addressed, to be informed, to be called — ca. (vācáyati) ps. (vācyate) pfp. (vācya) to make speak | to utter, to read aloud ["to make a written text speak"] — des. (vivakṣati) to ask the word; to mean | lat. vocare, vox; ang. voice; all. erwähnen; fr. voix, vocal. yad ucyate it is said that, it is said that. kathām vakti he tells a story. tvām vakti he speaks to you. devyuvāca lit. [āgama] the Goddess asked (Shiva) | phil. [Abhinavagupta] I, who am the Goddess, ask myself.
vaca |agt. vac| amnf vacā who speaks — m. parrot — act. n. act of speaking; speech — f. vacā mainate; syn. sārikā.
Vacaknu |vacasnu| eloquent amnf; ba vard — m. lit. np. of the sage Vacaknu, father of Gargī Vācaknavī.
vácana |act. vac| n. speech, language; discourse,

enunciation | saying | lit. devotional words addressed to Shiva | edict, order, advice | gram. number (ekavacana singular, dvivacana dual, bahuvacana plural). vacanaih by words; verbally. madvacanāt adv. in my name.
vacanajyāyas |jyāyas| amnf vacanajyāyasī best for speaking.
vácanajyestha | jyestha | amnf vacanajyesthā the most eloquent, the best in words.
Vacanamālā [mālā] f. bed. n.p. of the Vacanamālā "Garland of words", gloss [vyākhyā₂] of the Bālakrīdā, due to Sureśvara.
vacanavyakti [vyakti] f. gram. specific denotation of an utterance.
vacanāśanka [āśankā] n. fear of speaking.
vacanīya [pfp. [2] vac] amnf vacanīyā to say; about which it is necessary to speak | about which there is cause for complaint, blameworthy — n. blame, reproach; censure.
vácas [abstr. vac] n. speech; discourse. vacasām patiḥ myth. "Master of speech", epith. of Bṛhaspati; cf. Vācaspati, Vāgīśa.
√ vaj v. to be strong ∥ lat. vigeo; fr. vigor.

vajra [vajra] mn lightning | diamond |vajrayuddha| myth. the lightning missile, weapon of Indra (represented by a trident with three points, then four points curved at the two ends of a scepter); syn. kuliśa | myth. np. of vajra "Diamond", son of Aniruddha and Uṣā₁; he was the last of the yādavās.
vajrakaṭhina | kaṭhina | amnf vajrakaṭhinā hard as diamond. dhātrā sṛṣṭaṃ hṛdayaṃ vajrakaṭhinam the creator has endowed you with a heart as hard as diamond.
vajrakandara | kandara | n. med. urogenital canal.
Vajrakarma [karman] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of the vajrabodhisattva Vajrakarma "to the destiny adamant tin"
vajrakāya [kāya] m. bd. the "essential body" ["of diamond"], symbolizing the absolute Being present in the spiritual nature of every man; syn. dhar makāya.
vájrakīla [kīla] m. lightning — v. [11] pr. r. (vaj rakīlayate) to act like lightning | bd. to practice Vajrayāna.
vajraketu [ketu] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of the vajra bodhisattva vajraketu "Adamantine meteor". vajracūrņa [cūrņa] n. mod. cement.
vajracchedaka | chedaka | amnf Vajracchedikā who cuts the diamond.

Vajracchedakaprajñāpāramitā | prajñāpāramitā| f. bd. n.p. of the Vajracchedakaprajñāpāramitā or Vajracchedikā "Wisdom that cuts the diamond" or "Diamond Sūtra", founding work of Mahāyāna Buddhism, in the form of a dialogue between Buddha and his disciple Subhūti on the fate and impermanence of the world; it was translated into Chinese by Kumārajīva in 401, a printed version of 868 is known.
Vajratīkṣṇa [tīkṣṇa] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of the va jrabodhisattva Vajratīkṣṇa aspect of Mañjuśrī "with the adamantine sword".
vajratejas | tejas | mr. bd. | Mahāyāna | n.p. of the vajra bodhisattva Vajratejā “Adamantine Power”.
Vajradhara [dhara] m. myth. epith. of Indra "Holding the thunderbolt" | bd. [Vajrayāna] np. of the perfect [bodhisattva] Vajradhara "Bearing the thunderbolt ada mantin", also called Vajrapāni.
Vajradharma [dharma] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of the vajrabodhisattva Vajradharma, "Adamantine Law", aspect of Avalokitesvara.
vajranābha | nābhi | mr. myth. n.p. of vajranābha, epith. from Sudarsana, cakra of Vișnu "with the diamond hub"; Agni gave it to Kṛṣṇa.

vajrapāṇi [pāṇi] m. myth. np. of Vajrapāṇi, epith. of fierce Indra "With thunderbolt in hand" | bd. |Vajrayāna| epith. of an accomplished |bodhisattva| in incorporating Indra into the Mahāyāna pantheon; cf. Vajradhara.

Vajrabodhi [bodhi] m. hist. np. of the monk bd. Vajrabodhi "Diamond Wisdom" (671–741), Brahmin from southern India; at 10 years old he entered Nalanda, to study linguistics [śabdabodha]; then he studied the work of Candrakirti and became a master of Mahayana; after a pilgrimage to Lanka he left for China where he arrived in 719; there he taught Vajrayana and translated sit into Chinese many sutranis; he is considered the patriarch of the Chinese school of bd. tantric.

vajrabodhisattva [bodhisattva] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] one of 16 accomplished [bodhisattva] associated 4 by 4 with the guardian jina Aksobhya, Amitābha, Amo ghasiddhi and Ratnasambhava; they are called Va jrasattva, Vajrarāja, Vajrarāga, Vajrasādhu, Va jraratna, Vajratejā, vajraketu, Vajrahāsa, vaj radharma, Vajratīkṣṇa, Vajrahetu, Vajrabhāṣa, Va jrakarma, Vajrarakṣa, Vajrayakṣa, and Vajrasandhi.
vajrabhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. geo. prakrit of the Mathurā region — m. Vajrabhāṣa bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. from the vajrabodhisattva Vajrabhāṣa “To the word adamantine”.
vajramani | mani | mr. diamond.
Vajrayakṣa [yakṣa] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of the vaj rabodhisattva Vajrayakṣa “Adamantine Genius”.
Vajrayāna [yāna] n. bd. n.p. of the Vajrayāna "Path of the diamond", tantric form of bd. Mahāyāna; cf Amoghavajra, Abhayākaragupta, Buddhaśrījñāna, Vajrabodhi.
vajrayuddha | yuddha | mr. myth. Indra's lightning diamond weapon.
Vajrayoginī [yoginī] f. myth. n.p. from Vajrayoginī, yoginī “to lightning”; cf. Vajreśvarī.
Vajrarakṣa [rakṣa] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of the vajrabodhisattva Vajrarakṣa “Protector adamant tin”; it is a vidyārāja.
Vajraratna [ratna] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of the vaj rabodhisattva Vajraratna "Adamantine Jewel".
Vajrarāga [rāga] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of the vajra bodhisattva Vajrarāga “Adamantine taste”.
vajrarāja [rāja] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of the vajra bodhisattva vajrarāja "Adamantine King".

vajralepa [lepa] m. mortar (of lime, sand, oil, and cotton); plaster | strong glue; not. buffalo hide glue used for plastering. dharmakşetre krtam pāpam vajralepam bhavişyati In this time of justice, let the sin committed be pilloried. Vajrasattva var. vajrasatva [sattva] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] np. of vajrabodhisattva Vajrasattva "Adamantine Being" | bd. [Tantra] epithet of Hevajra.
Vajrasandhi [sandhi] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. from va jrabodhisattva Vajrasandhi “Twilight adamant tin”.
vajrasādhu [sādhu] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] np. du va jrabodhisattva vajrasādhu "Adamantine Blessing".
Vajrasāra [sāra] n. bed. [KSS.] np. from the city of Vajrasāra, capital of King Rambha.

vajrasūcī [sūcī] f. bd. np. of the vajrasūcī "Diamond Point", verse text attributed to Aśvaghoṣa, probably later (6th century); it is a sa draw of Brahmanical ideals and a critique of the caste system; also called Vajrasūci, vaj rasūcikā and Vajrasūcyupanisad.
vajrahāsa [hāsa] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. from the vajra bodhisattva vajrahāsa “Adamantine laughter”.
Vajrahetu [hetu] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] n.p. of the vajra bodhisattva Vajrahetu "Adamantine Agent", aspect of Maitreya.
vajrācārya [ācārya] m. bd. master of the Vajrayāna doctrine; cf. Abhayākaragupta.
vajrābha [ābhā₂] m. ["like a diamond"] precious stone | arch. dovetail joint.
Vajrāvalī [āvalī] f. bed. n.p. of the Vajrāvalī of Abhayākaragupta, which codifies the rituals of the bd. Tantric Vajrayāna.
vajrāsana |āsana| n. phil. |yoga| posture with legs crossed in lotus, soles of feet facing upwards | bd. "diamond throne" of the Buddha, at the foot of the bodhitaru.

Vajreśvarī [īśvarī] f. bd. np. of the goddess bd. Va jreśvarī | myth. form of Durgā "of the thunderbolt"; her main temple is in mod. Kangra (Himachal Pradesh); it was very rich, was looted by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1009 and by Tughluk Shah in 1360, and destroyed by an earthquake in 1905; another temple is in Vajreśvarī, on the banks of the Tansā in Mahārāṣṭra; it is a śaktipīṭha, the pīṭhasthāna of a breast of Satī.
vajrin [vajrain] m. myth. np. of Vajrī, epith. of Indra "who holds the thunderbolt".
vajrolī [related to vajra] f. cf. vajrolīmudrā.
vajrolīmudrā [mudrā] f. phil. [Tantra] re-aspiration of sperm by the penis.
√ vañc v. [1] pr. (vañcati) pfp. (vaṅkya, vañcya) to walk crookedly; to stagger, to stagger — ca. (vañcayati) pp. (vañcita) to deceive | lat. vacillo; fr. vaciller.

vañcaka [agt. ca. vañc] amnf vañcikā deceitful, fraudulent — n. bio. jackal. hṛdayavihīno dhūrtaḥ saṃgraharahitaḥ sa vaṃcako vaidyaḥ | vakti na doṣān doṣī carakaś carakaṃ na jānāti || [Deśopadeśa] A quack doctor is a heartless swindler (he does not know the Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya) lacking concentration (and ignores the Aṣṭāṅgasaṃgraha); being guilty, he does not diagnose the humors; he is nomadic, but does not know Caraka.
vañcana [act. ca. vañc] n. deception, deception | illusion, hallucination — f. vancanā id. vañcanām kṛ to cheat, to deceive. vañcanām labh to be deceived.
vañcita [pp. ca. vañc] amnf vañcitā deceived, disappointed; who misses (the goal (i.)).
vañcitaka [ka] m. id.

vața [Dravidian] m. organic. bot. Ficus indica, banyan tree; syn. nyagrodha, śunga | soc. pawn in chess | thread, rope. vațapattra pattra n. geo. n.p. from the town of Vațapattra, on the banks of the Viśvāmitrī, to Gu jarāt (mod. VadodarāBaroda); it was formerly called Candravatī, then Vīravatī; this Maratha stronghold was wrested from the Mughal empire in 1721 by the Gāyakavāda clan.
vaṭapūrṇimā | pūrṇimā | f. soc. full moon of the month jyaistha; in western India, vatasāvitrīpūjā is celebrated.

vaṭasāvitrīpūjā [sāvitrīpūjā] f. soc. celebration of sāvitrī₁ during the vaṭapūrṇimā; the women fast there while praying for the health of their husbands; they circle | parikrama | a sacred banyan tree 7 times, which they surround with cotton threads.
vaṭaka mn globule, boulette; not. fried lentil dough ball.
vatu cf. batu.
vaḍabá m. cf. vaḍava — f. váḍabā cf. Vaḍavā.
vadavá m. horse attracting the stallion | var. vadabá id. — f. cf. vadavā.
vadava | f. vadava | f. mare | myth. n.p. from vadavā, epith. of the nymph Aśvinī | var. vádabā id.

vádavāgni | agni | mr. myth. n.p. of Vadabāgni or Vadavāgni "Fire of the mare", inextinguishable fire coming out of an underwater cavern in the southern regions, coming from the ardor of Aurva's penance; its smoke is said to be the source of lightning; variants Badavāgni, Vādavāgni.
vádavānala [anala] m. cf. vadavāgni.
vadavāmukha [mukha] n. myth. from the np. Vadavāmukha or Vadabāmukha "Mouth" of the mare", one of the gates of the infernal regions, located at the South Pole.
vaníj var. banij m. [nom. vanik] merchant, trader — f. commerce. vanikputrah son of a merchant.
vaṇija [vaṇija] m. merchant — n. astr. zodiacal sign of Libra | astr. sixth lunar halfday [karaṇa] (mobile) — f. vaṇijā traffic, com merce.
vaṇḍa var. baṇḍa, vaṇṭha amnf vaṇḍā mutilated, crippled; castrated, impotent.

vat var. mat (form of the a.) like, similar to, which is | which has, which possesses; which produces transforms a passive sense into an active sense, not. a pp. into a ppa. (cf. ktavatu) | forms the noun. acc. voc. sg. of a ppft. n. (cf. vas) | (acc. used as an adv.) according to, in the manner of, such. ghațo ghațatvavān |Nyāya| A pot is that which possesses the quality of a pot. tattvavat tadeva [Nyāya] The possession of the characteristic property of a notion is that notion itself (axiom of possession). tadvattvam tadeva |Nyāya| The extension of belonging to a notion is that notion itself (axiom of extension).
vatanda m. np. of a man | pl. his descendants — f. vatandī one of his descendants.
vatup noted. gram. secondary training
daire [taddhita] of adjectives in vat, meaning "possessing"; cf. matup.
vatūla cf. vātula.
vattva phil. [NN.] "that which possesses the quality of" (combines vat and tva). sāsnāvattvam phil. |Vaiśeṣika| universal of cattle; syn. gotva.

vatsá m. calf, young animal | [vatsabhūmi] name of the vatsa country, in the lower valley of the Ya munā, with capital Kauśāmbī | myth. np. of vatsa₁, son of King Pratardana | myth. np. of vatsa₂, cousin of Sārasvata; he founded the Vātsyāyana lineage | pl. vatsās the inhabitants of the vatsa country; its princes — voc. adr. my child, my son, my darling — f. vatsā heifer, young female | dear — voc. vatse adr. my daughter, my darling.
vatsátará |tara| m. young bovine — f. vatsatarī young cow.
vatsánābha | nābha | m. bio. bot. Aconitum napel lus, aconite napel, ranunculaceae toxic — n. poi son violent prepared with aconite root.
vatsábhūmi [bhūmi] f. geo. land of the vatsās, from ca pitale Kauśāmbī.
vatsarāja | rāja | mr. hist. king of the vatsa country; not. title of King Udayana.
vatsala |la| amnf vatsalā tender towards his children, affectionate.

Vatsāsura [asura] m. myth. np. of the demon calf Vatsāsura; he had slipped, disguised as a calf by cunning, into the herd that Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma children were guarding at Vṛndāvana; Kṛṣṇa noticed him and killed him; to expiate this crime of goghāta, he purified himself in the waters of the Manasigangākunda, where he conjured the Ganges by thought.
vatsará [vatsara] m. year of a 5-year cycle; year in gen.

√ vad v. [1] pr. (vadati) pr. r. (vadate) fut. (vadisyati) imp. (vada) impft. (avadat) opt. (va det) pft. (uvāda) aor. [5] (avādīt) pp. (udita₂, va dita) pfp. (udya, vadya) abs. (udya) pf. (anu, apa, abhi, ut, upa, pari, pra, prati, vi, sam) to speak; to say something to someone (2 acc.); to call | to state, to explain — ca. (vādáyati) ca. r. (vādayate) ps. (vādyate) to make someone speak, to make someone say | to play a musical instrument (i.) — ps. (udyáte) to be spoken, to be said; to be said — intens. (vāvadīti) to speak loudly; to chatter, to talk too much | Latin: vates; French: vaticiner. satyam vad to tell the truth. samskrtena vad to speak in Sanskrit. kim vadeyam what should I say?
vada [agt. vad] ifc. amnf vadā which says (iic.).

vádana |act. vad| n. act of speaking; speech | mouth; face, visage; mug | math. first term of a sequence; vertex of a triangle — f. vadanā ifc. act of talking about (ii.). vadanam kr to make a face. vadanībhū to become a face.
vadānya | vad | amnf vadānyā eloquent; affable | generous; donor — m. myth. | Mah. | np. du rṣi vadānya.
vadi adv. during the dark fortnight (of a lunar month); opp. śudi | badi id.
vaditṛ [agt. vad] amnf vaditrī who says; who speaks, who tells (acc.) — m. orator. viruddham vaditā who is inclined to say contradictory things.

vadya |pfp. |1| vad| amnf vadyā that which can or should be said | that which should be spoken of; that which deserves praise, praiseworthy — n. that which is said, that which is recounted; that which can or should be said.
√ vadh v. aor. [5] (avadhīt) pfp. (vadhya) pf. (ā) to strike, to kill (substitute for han₁ for the aor.) — ps. (vadhyate) to be killed, struck down, defeated.

vadha [agt. vadha] amnf vadha that kills, murderer — act. m. murder, killing; truction | soc. corporal punishment; capital punishment erasure, disappearance; frustration; defect, im perfection | math. multiplication. vadham kr to kill.
vadhabhūmi | bhūmi | f. place of execution, gallows.
vadhasná [sna] mn deadly weapon.
vadhodyata | udyata | amnf vadhodyatā ready to kill — m. murderer, assassin.
vadhopāya |upāya| m. instrument of murder, means of killing.
vádhaka [agt. vadhā] amnf vadhikā who kills, murderer — m. assassin | soc. executioner; executioner.
vadhin [agt. vadh] ifc. amnf vadhinī put to death by (iic.).
vadhu | vadhu | f. young wife; young woman.
vadhū [vah₁] f. fiancée, young bride; woman, wife; daughter-in-law; female | female animal (not. cow and mare).
vadhūpraveśa | praveśa | m. soc. rite of the wife's entry into her husband's house.
Vadhūsarā [sara] f. myth. np. of the river Vadhūsarā "Out of the beautiful one", formed from the tears of Pulomā₂ mourning the loss of Cyavana.
vadhūṭī [vadhū] f. young woman.

vádhya [pfp. [1] vadhyā] amnf vadhyā that which must be struck; that which must be punished | that which must or will be killed, that which deserves death; condemned; that which must be destroyed — m. enemy — f. vadhyā ifc. murder, killing of.
vadhyatā [tā] f. the state of deserving to be killed. vadhyatām gam to deserve death.
vadhyatva [tva] n. id.
vadhyamālā [mālā] f. soc. rose laurel garland |karavīra| that a condemned man wore around his neck.
vádhri [vadhri] amn ["whose testicles have been crushed" | emasculated, castrated; opp. vṛṣan — m. eunuch.
√ van v. [1] pr. (vánati) v. [8] pr. (vanóti) pr. r. (vanity) pp. (vanita) to love, to desire | lat. Venus, veneror; all. Wahn; fr. venerate.
van forme des a. mas. (f. en varī).

vána n. wood, natural forest; nature, vegetation, thicket; tree | ornamental garden, grove; orchard | multitude, abundance — iic. bio. (animal) (ifc.) wild. vanamahisavrndam herd of wild buffalo. vánacara var. vanecara [cara] amnf vanacarī one who lives in the woods; one who roams in the woods — m. anchorite; aboriginal | wild animal.
vánaja [ja] amnf vanajā from the woods; wild — m. woodsman; elephant.
vanaparvan | parvan | n. lit. np. from Vanaparva, 3rd book of Mah., "of the forest".
vanamānusa [mānusa] m. bio. ["man of the woods"] orangutan.
Vanarāja | rāja | mr. hist. n.p. of king Vanarāja, of the Cāpa dynasty in Gujarat; in 746 he founded his capital Anahilapātaka.

vanavāsa [vāsa₁] m. stay in the forest | myth. [Mah.] pilgrimage; 12-year exile of the five Pāṇḍavās; myth. [Rām.] 14-year exile in the forest of Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa — f. vanavāsi geo. np. of the city of Vanavāsī, a very ancient city of Karņāṭa, mentioned in the Mah. as the capital of the Va navāsikās, on the Varadā River (mod. town of Ba navāsī); it was the capital of the Kadamba dynasty in the 4th century; also called Vaijayantī.
vanavāsin |in| amnf vanavāsinī who dwells in the forest — m. anchorite | mod. member of a tribal community.
vanaspati | pat | mr. tree | "wood master" |.
vanaspativana [vana] n. timber harvesting forest.
vanānta | anta | m. edge of a wood; wood, forest.
vanausadhi [osadhi] m. pl. plants.
vanauṣadhivarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Bhūmyādikānda, dealing with woods and flora.
vanita [pp. van] amnf vanitā solicited; desired; loved — f. cf. vanitā.
vanitā [f. vanita] f. lover; beloved wife woman; female animal.
vanitādvis [dvis₂] m. misogynist.
vanín₁ [agt. van] amnf vaninī ved. who desires | who grants, who bestows.
vánin₂ [vanain] m. ved. tree; soma plant that inhabits the woods; hermit.
vániṣṭha [super. vanin₁] amnf vaniṣṭhā the most generous.
vane [loc. vana] iic.
vanecara [cara] amnf vanecarī who travels in the woods — m. tribal hunter; syn. kirāta.

√ vand [related to vad] v. [1] pr. r. (vandate) pft. (vavande) pp. (vandita) pf. (abhi) to welcome, to greet with deference; to pay homage to, to show respect; to praise, celebrate, honor; to offer respectfully to; dat. lat. vendo; fr. vanter. bhagavatpadau śirasā vanditvā bd. having honored with his head the feet of Buddha. vande mātaram mod. "Long live the mother (country)", patriotic poem by the Bengali Bankim Chandra Chatterji (1875), recited by children at the beginning of classes. vandemahi ca tām vāṇīm amṛtām ātmanaḥ kalām |Kālidāsa| Let us praise the voice, the immortal part of the soul.
vanda |agt. vand| amnf vandā who honors.
vandana [act. vand] n. adoration, homage, worship; veneration — f. vandanā id.
vandāru [agt. vand] amnf ved. qui ho nore, qui célèbre | respectful, polite.
vandita [pp. vand] amnf vanditā res pecté; praised, celebrated.
vanditavya [pfp. [3] vand] amnf vandi tavyā that one must honor, to whom one must show respect.
vanditṛ [agt. vand] amnf vanditrī who celebrates, who praises.
vandin var. bandin₁ [agt. vand] m. soc. bard (singing the praises of the prince); herald (declaiming in battle).
vándya [pfp. [1] vand] amnf vandyā that one must honor; respectable; venerable; ado rable.
vándyatā [tā] honorability.
vandrá [vandra] amnf vandrā who honors; who adores — m. worshipper; disciple — n. prosperity, abundance.
vandhúra var. bandhura n. front part of the chariot, where the driver sits.
vandhya var. bandhya amnf vandhyā sterile, unproductive, vain | lacking (iic. i.) — f. vandhyā sterile woman.
vandhyāsuta [suta₂] m. ["son of a barren woman"] absurdity, paradox.

ványa [vanaya] amnf vanyā product or existing in the forest; wild | occurring in the woods; myth. epith. of Agni — m. wild animal or plant — n. product of the woods; fruit or root of a wild plant — f. vanyā great forest.
vanyāśana [aśana₂] amnf vanyāśanā [“who feeds on the products of the forest” | hermit.
√ vap₁ v. [1] pr. (vapati) pp. (upta) shave — v. [1] pr. r. (vapate) shave.
√ vap₂ v. [1] pr. (vapati) pft. (uvāpa) pp. (uptá) pf. (ā, ni, nis, pra, prati) to sow, to sow, to spread, to disperse — ps. (upyate) to be spread — ca. (vāpayati) to sow, to plant.
vapa₁ [act. vap₂] m. shaving.
vapa₁ [agt. vap₂] m. sower — f. cf. vapā.
vapana [act. vap₁] n. shaving | razor — f. vapaṇī shaving salon.
vapā [f. vapa₁] f. anthill | ved. peritoneum, omentum (used during oblation) | marrow; syn. medas.
vapāmārjana [mārjana] n. separation of the omen tum.
vapāvat |vat| amnf vapāvatī wrapped in omentum.
vapāśrapaṇī [śrapaṇī] f. ved. fork for frying omentum.
vapus iic. vapus.

vapuṣmat |mat| amnf vapuṣmatī Beautiful | myth. [MkP.] np. of Prince Vapuṣmān "the Beautiful", son of Sankrandana, king of Vidarbha; King Dama Dișta having abducted Sumanā, Vapuṣmān took revenge by killing his father Narisyanta, whose wife threw herself into the funeral pyre; to avenge his parents, Dama raised an army, and killed Vapuṣmān; with his flesh he made the pinda offerings to honor his parents, with his blood as a libation.

vapus [abstr. vap₂] n. body; syn. śarīra | Beautiful body; form, beauty; marvel | gram. stage of speech manifestation |v bar{a}c|; Bhartrhari distinguishes three: paśyantī, madhyamā, and vaikharī; Somānanda adds the ultimate form parā at the beginning; Abhinavagupta adds the form sūksmā second in the Krama, then returns to the three stages, each subdivided into 3 levels: parā, sūkṣmā, and sthūlā — amnf vapuṣī who has a lovely form; pretty; marvelous. martyavapuṣā in human form. sā pupoṣa manoharaṃ vapuḥ she has developed a ravishing body.
vapra |vap₂ra| mn rampart, mound, buttress | high bank (river, canal) | slope (hill) | rice paddy — f. vaprā flowerbed, cultivated land — f. vaprī mound; anthill.
vaba m. phon. 'va' and 'ba'. vabayor abhedaḥ 'va' and 'ba' are allophones.
√ vam v. [1] pr. (vamati) pp. (vanta) pfp. (va mitavya) pf. (ut) vomit; expectorate | reject | lat. vomere; fr. vomir; ang. to vomit.
vama [agt. vam] amnf vamī who vomits.
vamata |imp. vam | ind. vomit!
vamana [act. vam] n. vomiting.
vamitavya [pfp. [3] vam] amnf vami tavyā to vomit.
vayaḥ iic. vayas₁. vayaḥsaṃdhi var. vayaḥsandhi [saṃdhi] m. puberty.
vayaḥstha |stha| amnf vayaḥsthā in the prime of life; adult; vigorous | of the same age group; contemporary.
vayam [noun. pl. aham] ind. We.
vayaṃvayam [red.] ourselves.
váyas₁ [abstr. vī₁] n. vigor, youth | age the age, an āyādi ; syn. āyus . prathamavayasi adv. in childhood. parinatavayasi adv. in the age of decline. tasmin vayasi adv. at that age.
váyas₂ [abstr. vi₁] n. winged kind; flock of birds
vayahparināmapānduraśirasā [K.] with hair whitened by the weight of years.
vayasvat |vat| amnf vayasvatī vigorous.
vayovrddha | vrddha | amnf vayovrddhā advanced in age, aged; old.
vayasá₁ [vayas₁a] ifc. mr. of age (iic.).
vayasá₂ | vayas₂a| mr. bird.
vayaska |vayas₁ka| ifc. amnf vayaskā of age (iic.).
Vayasya [vayas₁ya] m. companion, comrade, friend (of childhood or of the same age) | myth. np. of Vayasya "Buddy", son of Angirā.
vayúna [vī₁] amnf vayunā rapid, mo bile, quick; agitated, turbulent — m. path; rule, or giving; ritual arrangement — f. vayunā mark; purpose; knowledge, wisdom.
vára₁ [agt. vr₁] m. circumference; space that surrounds, surrounding room, thing that envelops.

vará₂ [obj. vṛ₂] amnf varā chosen, preferred; excellent, very good, very beautiful; elite, choice; elder; better than (abl.); the best of (g. abl. loc.); the strongest — agt. ifc. he who chooses (iic.) (not. a husband, a wife, with (acc.)) | princely, royal — m. chosen, suitor, fiancé; spouse, son-in-law — act. n. vára choice, desire; gift, offering; dowry; pri vilège, favor, reward; blessing | saffron — ind. varam rather, preferably, better (than (abl. acc.); cf. varamā. varam adv. rather, preferably. varam gacchāmi it is better that I leave. varam varam adv. at one's own discretion, at choice. varam ... na rather ... than; better ... than. ... varaṃ na ca rather ... than; better ... than. na hi ... varam not ... but rather varam dā to grant a gift, to grant a wish, to bestow one's blessing. varam labh to obtain the object of one's desire. varam tat kuryāt it would be better if he did it. varaṃ mṛtyur na cākīrtiḥ rather death than infamy. varam buddhir na tu vidyā [PT.] Intelligence is better than knowledge. varam eko gunī putro na ca mūrkhaśatair api [PT.] One gifted son is better than a hundred fools.
varatanu [tanu] amnf varatanū who has a Beautiful body — f. varatanū pretty woman.
varatantu [tantu] m. bed. [Ragh.] np. of varatantu, tutor of Kautsa "of good lineage".
varadāna |dāna| n. granting of a favor or a vow, blessing.
varanārī [nārī] f. excellent woman.
varamālā [mālā] f. soc. garland used to designate the chosen spouse during a svayamvara.

Vararuci₂ [ruci] m. myth. epith. of Shiva "who takes pleasure in offerings" | hist. np. of the grammarian Vararuci₂, expert in rhetoric |alamkāra|; he is the author of the Prākṛtaprakāśa and the Lingaviśeṣavidhi; tradition gives him as one of the nine jewels | navaratna | of the court of King Vikramāditya | lit. [KSS.] Vararuci₂, also identified with Kātyāyana, is said to be the incarnation on Earth of the gana Puspadanta banished by Pārvatī for having listened to the story of the magicians that Shiva told him; he was born brah mane in Kauśāmbī; at his birth, a voice from heaven said that he had the gift of remembering any text heard once; As a young boy, his gift was recognized by the Brahmins Vyādi₂ and Indradatta, thus identifying the student destined for Varsa; he went with them to Pāṭaliputra, where Varsa sang the Veda and all the sciences to him; to pay his exorbitant gurudakṣiṇā, Indradatta used magic to possess the dying king; the false Yogananda gave the sum to Vararuci₂, and appointed him minister; he fell in love with Upakośā and married her; one day, Pāṇini, a student banished from Varsa's school, having learned the grammar of Shiva's grace, challenged him to a grammar debate, and he realized his ignorance; He went to the Himalayas, where Shiva revealed to him the grammar of Pāṇini, which he improved; he went to honor Vindhyavāsinī who told him where to find the piśāca Kāṇabhūti to whom he told the story of the magicians, remembering his existence as Puspadanta, and thus obtaining his liberation; he retired to Badarī, where he self-consumed | hist. np. of Vararuci₂, astronomer of Kerala (4th century), inventor of a redundant coding technique for mnemonic purposes |kaṭapayādi| | hist. np. of Vararuci₂, astronomer of Tamil Nadu (13th century), author of the Vākyakaraņa hist. np. of other authors of various periods. I bow before the three sages: Pāṇini the author of the rules, Vararuci₂ the grammarian and Patanjali the commentator.
vararucivākya [vākya] n. cf. candravākya.
varavarnin [varnin] amnf varavarninī of fair complexion — f. varavarninī beautiful woman with fair complexion.
varaśāpa [śāpa] m. du. varaśāpau blessing and curse.
varānga [anga₁] n. ["the best part of the body"] head | vagina | pretty body — amnf varāngā who has a beautiful body.
varānganā [anganā] f. pretty woman. virile varānganāsusamartha.
varānanā [ānana] f. (woman) with a pretty face | myth. np. of the nymph | apsaras | varānanā "Plump".
varārohā [āroha] f. (woman) who has beautiful hips.
