varendra [Indra] m. chief, king | myth. np. of Va will make "Indra the Valiant" — mn geo. np. of the varendra₁, region of northern Bengal; it included the Pundravardhana.
vará gram. expresses "the one who does" after a verb.
varaka₁ [agt. vṛ₁] m. coat — n. fabric | cover, tarpaulin; lid | thin film of silver or gold covering sweets | bio. variety of millet.
varaka₂ | agt. vr₂ | m. wish, request | soc. man who asks for marriage.

varaṇa₁ [act. vṛ₁] m. rampart, mound; causeway; bridge | bio. bot. Crataeva magna, shrub growing along rivers, with trifoliate leaves, greenish flowers, used in medicine; also called varuna, it is supposed to possess magical virtues | soc. magical formula recited to increase the power of weapons — n. enclosure — f. Varaṇā geo. np. of the small river Varaṇā near Benares (mod. Barnā).
varaṇa₁ [act. vṛ₂] n. act of choosing | soc. act of giving one's hand to one's future husband. varanam kṛ to choose. varaņīya [īya] amnf varaņīyā that which must be chosen or selected.
varaṇāsī [asī] f. du. geo. the Varaṇā and asī rivers cf. vārāṇasī.
varanda [vr₂] m. veranda, gallery, porch || pt. verandah; fr. veranda.

varada [vara₂da] amnf varadā auspicious; one who grants wishes, who bestows gifts — m. myth. np. of varada "Benefactor", auspicious aspect of Vișnu; he is represented as padmanābha — f. varadā maiden | geo. np. of the river varadā, tributary of the Godāvarī (mod. Wardha).
varadamudrā [mudrā] f. bd. gesture of giving (horizontal forearm, hand extended towards the ground, palm forward).

Varadarāja₁ | rāja | mr. myth. n.p. of Varadarāja₁ "Master of Abundance", auspicious aspect of Vișņu; its main temple is in Kāñcīpura | hist. n.p. of the grammarian Varadarāja₁, student of Bhaṭṭoji, author of the Laghukaumudī | hist. [Nyāya] np. of the logician Varadarāja₁ Miśra, author of the Tārkikarakṣā (12th century).
varadarājastava [stava] m. bed. n.p. from the vara darājastava, a hymn in praise of Vișnu Varadarāja₁, commissioned from Appayya Dīkṣita by the Vaisnava King Venkata II (around 1590).
varamā [varamā] ind. better than. ajātamṛtamūrkhāṇām varamādvau na cāntimaḥ lit. [Hit.] Unborn, stillborn or idiotic. The first two are still better than the last.
varāka amnf varākī miserable; wretched, pitiable | impure, dirty (money).
varāṇasī f. geo. np. of the varāṇasī river, north of Vārānasī; cf. Varanā.

varāha m. bio. zoo. boar, pig myth. np. of varāha, cosmic boar, 3rd avatar of Vishnu, who plunged into the waters to save Bhumi the Earth which had been plunged into them by the dai tya Hiranyaksha at the beginning of the present kalpa; from their union was born Naraka; cf. Emūṣa — f. Varāhī myth. np. of the yoginī Varāhī; she is represented with a boar's head, holding in her hand a fish and a cup of blood | lat. glasses; fr. boar. varāhakarņa [karņa] m. kind of arrow "in the shape of a boar's ear".
varāhapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. bed. from np. varāhapurāṇa; cf. vārāhapurāṇa.

Varāhamihira [mihira] m. hist. de np. Varāhamihira, astrologer, naturalist and mathematician of Magadha (6th century), author of the encyclopedia Bṛhatsaṃhitā; he is also credited with the treatise on astrology Bṛhajjātaka; he lived in Kāmpilyā and Ujjayinī; tradition includes him among the nine jewels |navaratna| of the court of King Vikramāditya.

varāhopaniṣad [upaniṣad] f. lit. np. of the varāhopaniṣad "Lesson of varāha". om saha nāvavatu saha nau bhunaktu saha vīryam karavāvahai | tejasvināvadhītamastu mā vidviṣāvahai | [KU.] Om, may He protect us together, (the teacher and the student), may He nourish us together, may we together feel vigor, may our study prove effective, and may no enmity arise between us.

várivas [related to uru] n. room, space | ease, comfort — v. [11] pr. (varivasyáti) to allocate space, to make room (for (dat.)); to concede, to honor; to serve, to help; to cherish. varivas kṛ to make way for, to open the way for. varivas dhā id.
váriṣṭha₁ [super. uru] amnf variṣṭhā the widest, the largest, the most extensive.
váriṣṭha₂ [super. vara₂] amnf variṣṭhā the best, the most eminent; better than (abl.) | (pej.) the worst of the g. .
várīyas₁ [compar. uru] amnf varīyasī wider (than (abl.)) | freer — ind. further — n. larger space (than (abl.)) | free space; freedom; comfort, ease.
várīyas₂ [compar. vara₂] amnf varīyasī best, excellent; best of the g. .

váruṇa [vṛ₁una] m. myth. np. of Varuṇa "(the sky) that surrounds us", Vedic asura of the starry sky; eldest of the radiant ones [āditya], he represents the dark side of the divine, in opposition to his double Mitra; he is the universal King |adhipati|, severe but just, and celebrated for himself the first royal consecration [rājasūya] whose rite he established; Varuna is Pracetā₁, the all-hearing one; he is the guarantor of oaths, and binds men with his magic noose [pāśa]; he symbolizes the true Word, and is the god of Commandments; by confessing one's faults to Varuna, one burns one's sins in the fire of repentance [paścāttāpa]; he is the guardian [dikpāla] of the direction of the West; later he is the sovereign god of the celestial waters or of the
terrains |Ambhaḥpati| and master of creatures

marines [Yādaspati]; astr. he presides over the nakṣatra Satabhişak (of Aquarius); phil. [Sāṃkhya] he is the regent [niyantr] of the sense of taste [jihvā]; he is the guardian of celestial order [rta], aided by Gandharva; his mount is the makara; he is depicted flanked on his right by Gangā and on his left by Yamunā; his weapon is the rope or the lace, he is the master of knots; his wife Carṣaṇī raised his son Bhṛgu, born of sacrificial fire; [Mah.] the river Parṇāśā gave him as a son Srutāyudha, to whom he gave a magical mace to make him invincible; cf. Śunaḥśepa | myth. one of the 10 regions [dvīpa] forming Jambudvīpa | cf. varaņa₁ || gr. ουρανος; lat. ūrīna.

varuṇapraghāsa [praghāsa] m. pl. varuṇapraghāsās soc. 2ᵉ rite of cāturmāsya at the full moon of the month āṣāḍha; there one sacrifices to Varuna to be delivered from his snare; it is so called because a barley feast is held there in his honor.
varunasava [sava₂] m. myth. ["coronation of Varuna"] coronation, royal consecration; syn. rājasūya.
varuṇasenā |senā| f. bed. |KSS.| n.p. of Princess Varunasenā, daughter of Kumbīra, third wife of Sūryaprabha₁.
varuṇya [Varuṇaya] amnf varuṇyā from Varuna, belonging to Varuna. Varuņyā rajjuh |SB.| The rope is in Varuṇa.
váreṇya [pfp. [2] vṛ₂] amnf váreṇyā va lable, désirable; excellent; best among the g. .

várga [agt. vṛj] amnf Vargā ifc. that which discards, that which eliminates; that which selects (iic.) | group of (iic.) math. square of (iic.) — m. category, group of ment; association, band, party | not. class of words, category of notions, list of subjects | phon. place of articulation of a consonant; family of consonants sharing it (kavarga gutturals, cavarga palatals, tavarga cerebrals, tavarga dentals, pavarga labials, yavarga semivowels, śavarga sibilants) section of a book; not. subdivision of an adhyāya (the Rigveda has 2006) | math. class of quadratic equations — f. Vargā myth. [Mah.] np. of the nymph [apsaras] Vargā; She and her companions Budbudā, Latā, Saurabheyī, and Samīcī were on their way to Kubera's palace when they saw a hermit doing penance, whom they tried to tempt; he cursed them to become crocodiles until they met a hero; Arjuna, bathing in a lake during his pilgrimage, was snatched by the crocodile embodying Vargā, freed himself, and delivered them all from their spell. (pañcavargah math. five squared)
vargamūla [mūla] n. math. square root.
vargin [agt. vṛj] ifc. amnf varginī of the party of, devoted to (iic.) — m. pl. varginas partisans of, members of the party of, devoted to (iic.).
vargīya [vargaīya] ifc. amnf vargīyā of the category of, of the party of (iic.) | phone. from the series of (iic.) phonemes. kavargīya phon. (phoneme) guttural.
vargya [vargaya] amnf vargyā ifc. of the category of, of the party of (iic.) — m. colleague, fellow member; member of the same society; student of the same class; party or class comrade.

varcas [abstr. ruc₁] n. vital force, vigor, energy; not. the radiant power of fire and sun | brilliance, splendor; color | excrement, hard gold, dung | arch. latrines — m. myth. np. of Varcā "Resplendent", son of SomaCandra; the gods had decided to send him to Earth as an avatar to defend the dharma; his father Candra agreed to separate from him for no more than 16 years, provided that he was born as the son of Arjuna; he was therefore incarnated as Abhimanyu, condemned to die at 16 — n. varca ifc. color or brilliance of — n. varcasa ifc. luster, brilliance of.
varcogeha | geha | n. arch. latrines.
varj [ca. vrj] v. [10] pr. (varjayati) pp. (varjita) pfp. (varjya) abs. (varjayitvā) to set aside, avoid; aban to give, renounce, abstain from acc. | exclude.
varja [agt. vṛj] ifc. amnf varjā free of, rid of; without, except (iic.) | with the exception of (iic.).
varjaka [agt. vṛj] amnf varjikā which avoids; which excludes; excepted.
varjana [act. vṛj] n. exclusion; avoidance; abandonment.
varjayitvā [abs. ca. vṛj] ind. having given, having avoided | with the exception of (acc.).
varjita [pp. ca. vṛj] amnf varjitā excluded, avoided, abandoned | without, devoid of, except for (iic. i.).
varjya [pfp. [1] ca. vṛj] amnf varjyā to be avoided, to be excluded — ifc. with the exception of (iic.). varjyam adv. excepted (iic.).

√ varṇ [vn. varṇa] v. [10] pr. (varṇáyati) pp. (varnita) pf. (upa, nis) to paint; to describe, to depict, to expose. varņayāmāsa he described. apūrne pañcame varse varnayāmi jagattrayam (Śaṃkara₂ Miśra) At not even 5 years old I can describe the three Worlds.

várṇa [instr. vṛ₁] m. cloak, covering; appearance, aspect | color, tint; pigment, paint color; skin color, complexion | kind, species, category | quality, property | soc. Vedic social category, major class or caste; tradition distinguishes 4 [caturvarna] brāhmana, kṣatriya, vaiśya and śūdra, which are subdivided into hereditary corporations [jāti] or minor castes of trades and regions | math. symb. the number 4 gram. phoneme; letter, vowel | note, sound, music, melody, poem. varnatas adv. according to color.

varṇakrama [krama] m. soc. order of gram classes. alphabet. varnakramena according to the order of classes. nārāyaṇād udbhūto'yaṃ varṇakramaḥ gram. |Harināmāmṛtavyākaraṇa| This alphabet comes from Nārāyaṇa.
varnacitra [citra] n. lit. learned poetry with constraints on the phonemes used; cf. sthānacitra, svaracitra.
varṇatā |tā| f. fact of being the color of (iic.).
varnatva |tva| n. state of being the color of (i.e.) class condition, division into classes. anyavarnatvam state of being of another color.
Varṇadeśanā | deśanā | f. lit. np. de la Varṇadeśanā, dictionary en prose de Purusottamadeva, indi quant la variant orthographique correct pour des alternations telles ba/va, śa/ṣa, etc.
varnaparāmarśa [parāmarśa] m. gram. phonemic manifestation | phil. [Trika] verbal origin of
Creation [sṛṣṭi].
várnaparicaya [paricaya] m. study of music, knowledge of a tune, musical talent.
várnapātha [pātha] m. alphabet.

várṇamālā [mālā] f. alphabet as a table of phonemes arranged according to their points of articulation |sparśa|. varņavakratā [vakratā] f. lit. [Kuntaka] oblique quality of the use of sounds; syn. śabdālaṃkāra.
varṇavikāra [vikāra] m. the change of complexion, a sāttvikānubhāva | phon. phonetic change of a text.

varṇavid | vid₃ | m. gram. phonetician. iti varņavidah prāhurnipuņam tam nibodhata gram. [Pāṇinīyaśikṣā] Thus said the phoneticians; learn this exactly. varņavinyāsa [vinyāsa] m. lit. [alaṃkāra] the arrangement of phonemes, or phonetic composition.
várnavrtta [vrtta] n. phone. class of meters defined by the number of syllables; opp. mātrāvṛtta.
varṇavyavasthā [vyavasthā₂] f. soc. caste system. varņaśas |śas| adv. soc. to each class.

varṇasaṃkara [saṃkara] m. soc. mixing of castes through intermarriage | myth. [Mah.] accidental confusion of castes arising from the inversion of ritual foods during the marriage of Satya vatī₁; she consumed the food intended to give her a Kṣatriya son (an error transferred to her grandson Paraśurāma), while his mother consumed the Brahman food (thus later allowing her son Viśvāmitra to transcend his Kṣatriya destiny to become a Brahman). varņasamāmnāya [samāmnāya] m. phon. alpha bet, sequence of Sanskrit phonemes in canonical order; it does not include anusvāra, visarga, and their variants [ayogavāha].
varṇasamūha |samūha| m. gram. aggregate of phonemes. varņasāmya [sāmya] n. phon. phonetic similarity.
varnasthiti |sthiti| f. preservation of phonemes | maintenance of social order.
varnasphota |sphota| m. gram. evocative power of a phoneme.
varṇāgama |āgama| m. phon. superposition of one phoneme on another, augmentation.
varṇāpatti |āpatti| f. phon. transformation of one phoneme into another, substitution.
varṇāvara [avara] amnf varṇāvarā soc. lower caste.
varṇāśrama [āśrama] n. soc. ["social class and way of life" conformity to the traditional Brahmanical social organization.
varṇāśramaguru [guru] m. soc. the king as guardian of Brahmanical orthodoxy.
varṇāśramadharma [dharma] m. soc. ["duties of caste and way of life"] rights and duties of Brahmanic society.

varṇaka [agt. varṇ] amnf varṇikā that represents, that depicts | that colors, that pigments — mn model; specimen | painting, pigment — n. lit. section of a work — f. varnikā mask; makeup; tattoo | soc. not. colorful decoration of spouses by each other.

varṇana [act. varṇ] n. act of painting, coloring — f. varnanā painting, coloring | description; decoration | praise. varņanavisayātikāmtam tatsthānam This place defies description. moghavarnanaprayatnam tatsthānam id.
varṇanīya [pfp. [2] varṇ] amnf varṇanīyā to depict, to describe; to paint — n. lit. subject of a work.
varṇika [varṇaika] m. writer, scribe; secretary | color for painting.
varnikabhanga [bhanga] m. phil. the science of colors, a sadangasilpa.
varnita [pp. varn] amnf varnitā painted, described, explained.
varṇin [agt. varṇ] amnf varṇinī colorful | of high caste — mn varni gold.
vart [ca. vṛt₁] v. [10] pr. (vartayati) pp. (vartita) pfp. (vartitavya, vartya) to turn, roll something; to accomplish, produce; to expose, to tell.
varta [act. vṛt₁] ifc. m. ["place of deployment"] country, region, stay | means of subsistence.
vartaka [agt. vṛt₁] amnf vartikā that exists; living — ifc. devoted, attached to (iic.) — mf vartakī f. vartakā quail.

vartana [agt. vṛt₁] amnf vartanā that sets in motion, that uses (iic.) | that is found — act. n. movement, the act of going around | pastime, stay (in loc. ); occupation; means of subsistence | behavior, conduct | soc. technical of rendering shadows in painting — f. vartanī stay; existence; course of life | path, journey.
vartanaka [ka] n. [Mayamata] area measure, quarter of 4 lots [māṣa]; (approximately 40 ares); there are 5 in a vātikā .
vartaní [vṛt₁] f. circumference of a wheel; rim | footprint of a wheel; path, route; course (river) — m. geo. region of eastern India.

vartamāna [ppr. mo. vṛt₁] amnf var tamānā current, in action; that which happens, that which takes place, occurring, contemporary; popular, in vogue — n. the present | gram. the present tense; cf. lat — f. vartamānā gram. the present tense conjugation suffixes. vartamānakāle gram. (conjugated) in the present tense.
vartamānasāmīpya [sāmīpya] n. gram. proximity of the present; one can use the Latin tense there.
varti [act. ca. vṛt₁] f. roll; bandage; gauze; ointment, eye drops; cosmetic; suppository | wick of a lamp; fringe of a fabric; edge, rim (vase) | vartī id.
vartikā [f. vartaka] f. quail | bio. bot. Lannea coromandelica, Coromandel ash; its bark is used in medicine as an antibacterial [varṇikā] pencil, charcoal; brush.
vartita [pp. ca. vṛt₁] amnf vartitā turned, rolled; rounded | produced, created, accomplished; prepared — n. gram. (the time of the) past — f. vartitā ifc. conduct to observe visàvis.

vartitavya [pfp. [3] vṛt₁] amnf varti tavyā to practice, to observe; which must be taken care of — n. (impers.) it must be observed; one must practice; which must be applied to (loc.). asmadvaśe vartitavya according to our instructions; out of obedience to us.

vartin [agt. vṛt₁] ifc. amnf vartinī that which dwells, which is found, which occurs, which exists at (iic.) | that which turns, which moves around (iic.) | engaged in (iic.); that which obeys, which practices (iic.) | that which makes turn (iic.) — m. gram. meaning of a suffix; syn. pratyayārtha.
vartula [vṛt₁] amnf vartulā round; circular; globular — m. ball — n. math. circle | organic. bulb.
vártman [vṛt₁man] n. wheel trace, furrow; track, path.
vardh [ca. vṛdh₁] v. [10] pr. (vardhayati) pr. r. (vardhayate) pp. (vardhita) to increase; to make grow, to raise. mānam vardh to honor.
várdha [act. vṛdh₁] m. increase.

várdhana [agt. vṛdh₁] amnf vardhanī that grows, that prospers — ifc. that makes grow, that makes prosper, that multiplies (iic.); that increases the power of (iic.) — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Vardhana "prosperous", son of Kṛṣṇa and Mitravindā | myth. epith. of Siva "that makes prosper" | hist. np. of the Vardhana₁ dynasty of kings of North India, after the fall of the Gupta empire in the 6th century; It was founded by Prabhākara₁, of the Puşyabhūti family, who was succeeded by his eldest son Rājya in 605, then after the latter's murder a year later by his son ca det Harşa at the age of 16 — f. vardhanī broom, brush | [vārdhanī] soc. ritual water pot — act. n. growth, prosperity, progress | expansion, strengthening, promotion; education.

Vardhamāna [ppr. mo. vṛdh₁] amnf vardhamānā growing, prosperous; figuratively, one who rises spiritually — m. jn. np. of Vard hamāna "prosperous", ascetic of the 6th century BC, founder of Jainism; he is the 24th and last tīrthankara; he is represented with a golden-yellow body, his animal is a lion; cf. Mahāvīra, Jina | hist. np. of the grammarian-logician Vard hamāna₁ or Vardhamānopādhyāya (14th century), son of Gangesa, author of the Ganaratnamahodadhi and the Kiraṇāvalīprakāśa | hist. np. of Vard hamāna₂, scholar of Mithilā (16th century), author of Dandaviveka — b. [vardhamānapura] lit. [KSS.] np. from the town of Vardhamāna₃; cf. Virabhuja. śatam jīva śarado vardhamānah | śatam he mantānchatam u vasantān | [RV.] live a hundred autumns in prosperity, a hundred winters and certainly a hundred springs.

vardhamānaka |ka| m. earthenware dish covered with another dish, forming an oil lamp; cf. samputa jn. sacred Jain symbol representing him, associated with VardhamānaJina and symbolizing the light of his teaching; cf. aṣṭamaṅgala | ritual gesture [mudrā] of the pot (fingers joined towards the palm, thumb protruding) posture of the two hands, one turned over the other | lit. [Pañcatantra] np. of Vardhamānaka, son of a merchant | lit. [Mṛcchakaṭikā] np. of Vardhamānaka₁, servant of Cārudatta.
vardhamānapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. bed. n.p. from Vard hamanapurāṇa, work jn. of Jinasena.
vardhita [pp. vardh] amnf vardhitā increased, grown; completed.
vardhin [agt. vṛdh₁] amnf vardhinī increasing, growing, increasing — f. vardhinī ifc. which increases.
vardhiṣṇú [agt. vṛdh₁] amnf that grows, that pushes | expanding.
vardhman [vṛdh₁man] m. med. hernia | var. vardhma id.
várdhra m. leather strap; leather — n. id. — f. vardhrī tendon; strap.
varpas n. form, figure, image, aspect | artifice; disguise; stratagem.
varma iic. varman.
varmavat [vat] amnf varmavatī armed; cui rassed.
varmahara | hara | amnf varmaharā who receives his weapons; of fighting age | who takes up arms.
varmana m. orange tree.
varman [vṛ₁man] n. cuirass, mail; armor; shelter, defense, protection | bark — m. ifc. soc. protector of (2nd century); form of princely titles [kṣatriya] Varmā "protector".

várya [pfp. [1] ca. vr₂] amnf varyā va lable, eligible; that which can be sought in marriage | excellent, eminent; principal; best among (g. iic.) — f. varyā that which cannot be prevented | soc. girl who chooses a husband (of her own free will).
vars [ca. vṛṣ] v. [10] pr. (varṣayati) to make it rain or fall as rain | to rain on acc. ; to water (from ⟨i.⟩).

varsá [agt. vṛṣ] m. rain | catchment basin, division of the world between two mountain ranges (tradition divides the world into 9 slopes: kuru, kiṃnara, ketumāla, bhārata, bhadrāśva, ramyaka, hari₂, hiraņmaya, ilāvṛta) | lit. [KSS.] np. of the idiotic Brahmin Varṣa; he lived in Pāṭalika in great poverty; by praying to Kārttikeya he obtained knowledge of all the sciences, charged to him to reveal them to a student who learns everything by heart on the first reading; the Brahmins Vyādi₂ and Indradatta brought Vararuci to him for this purpose; after teaching him everything, he asked for a gurudakṣiṇā of 10 million gold pieces; cf. Vyādi₂ — n. year — f. cf. varṣā || pali vassa; fr. downpour, pouring. āvarsāt adv. within a year. varṣāt adv. after a year. varșena adv. in one year. vasse adv. every year. varşartumāsapakṣāhovelādeśapradeśavat indicating the date and place. varşakundalī [kundalī] f. astr. horoscope of the year.

varsákrtya | krtya | amnf varsakrtyā to do during the year. varşakrtyakaumudī | kaumudī | f. lit. np. of the Varsakrtyakaumudī "Light on the ceremonies throughout the year", text by the Bengali scholar Go vindānanda (16th century).
varsátra [tra] n. umbrella.
varsáphala [phala] n. astr. [Tājika] annual horoscope. varşabhogya | bhogya | amnf varşabhogyā to last (punishment) for one year. śāpena varṣabhogyeṇa |Meghadūta| as a punishment of one year.
varsávara | vara₂ | m. eunuch (harem attendant).
varsávrddhi [vrddhi] f. ["increase of one year" | anniversary.
varṣaka [agt. vṛṣ] amnf varṣakā falling like rain.
varṣaṇa [agt. vṛṣ] amnf varṣaṇā that makes it rain (astra) — act. n. act of raining, downpour; watering | act of covering someone (iic.) with gifts.
varṣat [ppr. vṛṣ] amnf varṣantī in the process of raining. varşati adv. while it is raining.
varṣasu [loc. pl. varṣā] ind. at the rainy season.
varṣasuja |ja| amnf varṣasujā born in the rainy season.
varṣā [f. Varṣa] f. ifc. rain of | pl. varṣās rainy season (month of śrāvaṇa₁ and bhādrapada), monsoon | year.
varṣākāla |kāla₁| m. rainy season.
varṣābhū [bhū₂] mf varṣābhvī bio. ["produced by rain" | frog | earthworm.
varṣāmada [mada] m. ["rain drunk"] peacock.
varşin [agt. vṛṣ] amnf varṣiṇī who pours, who waters, who makes it rain | who cries copious tears — ifc. who distributes (iic.) | of (iic.) years. sastivarsī aged 60 years.
vársistha [super. vṛddha] amnf varsisthā the greatest, the longest, the best; excellent | the oldest; very old.
varṣīṇa [varṣaīna] ifc. amnf varṣīṇā de tant d'années.
varṣīya [varṣaīya] ifc. amnf varṣīyā of so many years. trivarṣīyah aged 3 years.
várṣīyas [compar. vṛddha] amnf varṣīyasī higher, longer, better than (abl.) considerable, important; prosperous | pkus older, more ancient.
várṣuka [varṣauka] amnf varṣukā plus vieux.
varṣyá [pfp. [1] vṛṣ] amnf varṣyā concerning rain; rainy | that which must be watered — f. varsyā pl. rainwater.

√ val [related to vr₁] v. [1] pr. r. (valate) v. [1] pr. (valati) pft. (vavale) pp. (valitá) to turn towards, to lean; to be attached to (loc.) | to return, to come back; to go home | to manifest | to cover; to be covered with — ca. (valayati) to turn. বল valá [obj. val] m. enclosure; cave, cavern | cloud | ved. | RV. | np. of the Vala cavern, which Indra, aided by the luminous | angirasas | and the breaths | marutas |, opened to release the Dawn |Uṣā| on the first morning of the World; its nourishing rays were confiscated by the avaricious demons [pani] like their cattle; this cave, discovered by the dog Saramā, was located on an island in the celestial river Rasā | ved. np. of the asura Vala "Mighty", brother of Vṛtra, killed by Indra (later called bala) — ifc. fort en (iic.); cf. bala || hi. Vala.
Vala provided with, abundant in ⟨iic.⟩.
valabhi [Valabhid₂] f. roof ridge, pinnacle; turret; terrace | var. valabhī id. | cf. Vallabhi. kasyāmcid bhavanavalabhau suptapārāvatāyām [MD.] on some palace terrace where doves sleep.

valaya [Valaya] mn bracelet; circle herd, horde; crowd — f. valayā ifc. id. | encircled by (iic.). valayīkṛ to wear as a bracelet. valayīkṛta used as a bracelet. valayībhū to form a circle, to encircle.
valayita [valayaita] amnf valayitā en circled, surrounded; surrounded by (i. iic.) | worn like a bracelet | wrapped; turning.
valayin [valayain] amnf valayinī who wears a bracelet — ifc. encircled, surrounded by (iic.).
valava cf. balava.
valāka var. balāka m. bio. zoo. type of heron.
valāhaka cf. balāhaka.
vali [act. val] mf fold, wrinkle; not. fold of the belly | curl (of hair) | wave | var. valī id.
valimat [mat] amnf valimatī wrinkled. valimukha var. valīmukha | mukha | amnf goes
limukhī | "with a wrinkled face" | monkey.
valita [pp. val] amnf valitā pleated, wrinkled; curved; curled — ifc. connected with, accompanied by (iic.) — n. black pepper.
valī iic. vali.
valīmukha [mukha] amnf valīmukhī ["with a wrinkled face" | monkey.
valka m. tree bark — n. bark garment | fish scales.
valkala [la] n. bark | garment made of bark fibers (for the use of ascetics).
√ valg v. [1] pr. (valgati) pp. (valgita) to move the limbs, to fidget; to jump, to leap, to dance.
valgā |valg| f. flange; rein.
valgānka [anka] amnf valgānkā who holds the bridle.
valgita [pp. valg] amnf valgitā that which has twitched; that which has throbbed — n. jump; movement, agi tation. bālavalgitam childish words.
valgú |valgu| amnf pretty, graceful; beautiful, charming, attractive — m. bio. goat — adv. prettyly, gracefully — v. [11] pr. (valgūyati) to become graceful or kind; to honor.
valguka [ka] amnf valgukā pretty; pleasant — m. sandalwood — n. sandalwood.
valmīka mn fourmilière.
valmīkopari | upari | adv. perched on an anthill; said of Vālmīki.
valla m. variety of wheat | its grain, unit of weight (between 2 and 4 grains [yava]).
vallatama [tama] amnf vallatamā super. the best loved.
vallatara |tara| amnf vallatarā compar. most loved.
vallatā |tā| f. state of being loved; popularity; favoriteness.
vallatva |tva| n. id.

vallabha amnf vallabhā loved, desired, preferred; dear to (g. loc. iic.); preferred to (abl.) — m. beloved, lover, husband, favorite; supreme | myth. n.p. of Vallabha, epith. of Kṛṣṇa “beloved” | hist. n.p. of Vallabha₁, founder of a Vaiṣṇava sect; cf. vallabhācārya | hist. n.p. of the logician Vallabha₂, author of the Nyāyalīlāvatī | hist. n.p. of Vallabha₃, son of Anandadeva, śaiva philosopher of Kaśmīra; cf. Vallabhadeva — f. vallabhā wife, beloved, favorite; mistress — f. vallabhī geo. n.p. from the city of Vallabhi in southern Gujarat, ancient Maitraka capital (5th to 8th centuries); it housed a bd. university and an important Jain center; in the 5th century, a council was held there to fix its canon |āgama|; cf. Dharasena, Bhatti.
Vallabhadeva | deva | mr. hist. n.p. of Vallabhadeva, śaiva author of the Kaśmīra (between the 12th and 15th centuries); we owe him not. the Subhāṣitāvalī, the Rag hupańcikā, and the Viśausadhi.

vallabhācārya [ācārya] m. hist. np. of Val labhācārya "Beloved Master", Brahmin te lugu (1479–1531) born into a family from Benares; with Caitanya he preached devotion [bhakti] to Kṛṣṇa and created the doctrine of purified monism [śuddhādvaita] realized by the way of Kṛṣṇa's grace [puṣṭimārga], and rejected asceticism; he wrote notably. the Anubhāsya, commentary on the Brahmasūtra, the Subodhinī, commentary on the Bhāgavatapurāņa, the teaching text Tattvārthadīpa nibandha , and the devotional poem Madhurāṣṭaka; he is also credited with 16 texts [Sodasagranthās] explaining the pustimārga path; he is said to be the reincarnation of Agni; he is celebrated at gurudvādaśī; the main center of his Kumāra₁ sampradāya is at Nāthadvārā; his followers are called Mahārāja.
vallabhendra [indra] m. hist. np. of the physician Val labhendra, author of the Vaidyacintāmaņi.
vallarī f. liana, climbing plant | (in fig.) curly hair | var. vallari id. — mr. vallarīka ifc. id.
vallāla m. hist. n.p. de vallāla, late 16th century poet, author of Bhojaprabandha | cf. Vallālasena.
Vallālacarita | carita | n. bed. n.p. from Anandabhaṭṭa's Vallālacarita "life of king Vallālasena" (16th century).

Vallālasena [sena] m. hist. np. of King Pāla Vallālasena or Ballālasena, son of Vijayasena; he reigned in Bengal from 1158 to 1178; he instituted the kulīna caste system and persecuted Buddhism; his son Laksmanasena succeeded him; he composed the Dānasāgara; his life was recounted in the Vallālacarita.

Valli f. liana, climbing plant; not. sweet potato | myth. np. of Valli "vine", second wife of Skanda; she is honored at Vellamalai, in Kerala lit. chapter of an esoteric lesson | upanisad | | var. valli id.
vava cf. bava.

√ vaś v. [2] pr. (váṣṭi) pft. (uvāśa) pp. (uśita) to be favorable to; to desire, to want, to wish | to impose one's will, to command; to affirm, to rule — ca. (vāśayati) to make desired; to take under one's power gr. ; ang. to wish.

vása | act. vas | m. will, desire | order, authority; influence; control, power, empire — obj. amnf vaśā submissive, obedient; dependent on, under the power of (g. iic.). vaśāt by the will, by the effect of. vaśīkr var. vaśe kr to submit to one's will, subjugate. vaśībhū to be subject to the will of another, to be subjugated. vaśam nī id. vase labh id. vaśam i var. vaśam gam to fall under the sway of. rosavasam gatah fallen under the sway of anger.
vaśaga [ga₁] amnf vaśagā subject to the will of, dependent on.
vaśam [acc. vaśa] iic.
vaśamvada | vada | amnf vaśamvadā submissive, obedient.
vaśā [f. vaśa] f. [govaśā] cow (sterile or not yet having calved) | female animal; woman lat. vacca; fr. vache.
vaśí [act. vaś] m. subjugation; fascination; under spell; power to subject others to one's will — n. subjection.
vaśi₁ iic. vaśin.

vaśitā [tā] f. subjugation, domination; power to subject others to one's will | phil. [yoga] the irresistible will, or power to impose one's will on others, an astasiddhi; this power allows one to tame wild beasts, but also to subject the sky or the water to one's will.
vaśitva [tva] n. self-control | the power to subjugate others; syn. vaśitā.
vaśin [agt. vaś] amnf vaśinī who imposes his will, who is authoritative; lord (of (g.)) | master of himself — m. ruler | wise master of his
passions | parasitic plant | phil. [Vedānta] the supreme controller of the Universe — f. vaśinī mistress.
vasistha cf. vasistha.
vaśiṣṭhī [f. vaśiṣṭha] f. woman's name | hist. not. np. of a wife of the emperor Śālivāhana, mother of the princes Śrīpulamāvi and Śātakarņī.

vaśiṣṭhīputra [putra] m. hist. matr. of Vasisthīputra₁ Srīpulamāvi, son of the emperor Śālivāhana, whom he succeeded in 102 as king of the line of Sātavāhanās | hist. his younger brother Vasisthīputra₂ Sātakarnī, who succeeded him in 130.
vaśī iiv. vaśa.
vaśīkaraṇa [karaṇa] n. phil. [Tantra] subjugation (by mantra or yantra).
vaśīkāra | kāra | m. id.
vaśīkṛta [kṛta] amnf vaśīkṛtā dependent; under the influence of — f. vaśīkṛtā submission, dependence; state of being under the control or power of; bewitchment.

vaśya [pfp. [1] vaś] amnf vaśyā who must be subjugated, to be tamed | subdued, docile; in the power of, in the service of g. iic. — m. servant; slave — f. vaśyā wife, docile woman | soc. magical power to subdue to one's will; rite of subjugation. yam brāhmaṇam devī vāg vaśyaiva anuvartate [Bhavabhūti] This Brahmin whom the goddess of speech follows everywhere like a servant.
vaśyatā |tā| f. subjugation, docility; obedience; modesty.
vaśyatva [tva] n. id.

vaṣaṭ [vah₁] interj. Vedic. let come ⟨dat.⟩ (invocation of a deity by the hotr at the end of the recitation of a ritual, after which the adhvaryu pours the oblation into the sacrificial fire). pūṣṇe vaṣaṭ invocation to Pūṣā. vasatkr soc. pronounce the vasat invocation. vașațkāra | kāra | m. soc. performance of the vasat invocation. anavarataśravaṇagṛhītavaṣaṭkāravācālaśukakulam K. a flock of parrots loudly repeating the vașat invocation, learned from hearing it repeated endlessly.

vasati var. vasatī [act. vas₁] f. night stop, overnight stay; encampment, stay | dwelling, residence; hideout, lodging | jn. monastery — amnf who resides at (loc.) || pkt. vasahi, vasadi, basadi. vasatim kr to spend the night; to take refuge at (loc.). vasatim grah id. usitāh smo ha vasatim we spent the night. tisro vasatīr usitvā having spent three nights.
vasatha [related to vasati] m. house.
vasana₁ [act. vas₁] n. stay, residence.
vásana₂ [act. vas₁] n. clothing; fabric — f. vasanā ifc. clothed in | wholly devoted to, infatuated with (doc trine).
vasantá [vas₁] m. the season [rtu] of Spring (month of caitra and vaiśākha) | myth. np. of Vasanta, Spring personified as servant of Kāma. vas₁ántā adv. in Spring.
Vasantaka [ka] m. Spring | lit. [Ratnāvalī₁] np. of the jester [vidūṣaka] Vasantaka, pleasure companion of King Udayana.
vasantatilaka [tilaka] nf vasantatilakā phon. “grace of Spring”, name of a homosyllabic poetic meter, 4 feet of 14 syllables; cf. Cau rapañcāśikā.

vasantapañcamī [pañcamī] f. soc. festival in honor of Sarasvatī, on the 5th day of the clear fortnight of the month māgha; books and writing instruments are honored there; this festival is also called śrīpañcamī.
Vasantabhānu [bhānu] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of the king of Aśmaka Vasantabhānu "Spring Light"; Indrapālita is his minister.
Vasantarājīya | rājīya | n. bed. n.p. of Vasantarājīya, treatise on nātyaśāstra due to king Kumaragiri Reddy (14th century).
vasantartu | rtu | m. the Spring season; it includes the months of caitra and vaiśākha.
Vasantasenā |senā| f. lit. np. of the courtesan Vasantasenā "army of Spring", heroine of the Mṛcchakaṭikā; she is in love with the brahmin Cārudatta.
vasantotsava | utsava | mr. soc. spring festival, celebrated in phālgunī; cf. dolāpūrnimā, gau rapūrņimā, Kumaragiri.
vasántā |vasanta| adv. |vasante| in springtime.
vasā [agt. vas₄] f. fat, lard; marrow, brain.

vasiṣṭha [super. Vasu₁] amnf vasiṣṭhā the richest; the most eminent; the best — m. myth. np. from the saptarși Vasistha "The richest" or Vasistha "whose every wish is granted", to whom hymns of the Rigveda are attributed; he is a brahmarși of Great purity, born from the breath [prāṇa] of Brahmā; he died at the sacrifice of Dakṣa but was reborn in the sacrificial Fire of Brahmā; he was the chaplain [purohita] of King Ikṣvāku and of all his lineage; he cursed his son Nimi for not waiting for him to undertake his 500-year crucifixion, condemning him to lose his body; in return Nimi cursed him likewise, and his body disappeared again; [MP.] He was born again from the sperm spilled by Mitra and Varuna [Mitrāvaruṇau] at the sight of the nymph Urvaśī; he has perfect knowledge of brahman | brahmanistha |; his wishes are granted by his cow of plenty NandinīSabalā; [Rām.] his rival King Viśvāmitra tried to steal her from him, but his army was routed by his humbhā bellowing which produced countless armies; [Mah.] his son Sakti₁ having refused to give way to King Kalmāṣapāda, the latter struck him with his whip; in turn, Vasistha cursed him, condemning him to become a vampire [rākṣasa]; the vampire successively devoured his 100 sons; In despair, Vasistha tried in vain to take his own life, then delivered the king from his fate after 12 years; astrologically, he is associated with the star Mizar of the Great Bear; his wife is Arundhatī, his companion star; he had 100 sons, all accomplished ascetics, the eldest of whom was Sakti₁, who fathered the ascetic Parāśara; it is said that he meditated for 90,000 years in the Himalayas, where Rāma visited him, and there created a hot spring by striking the ground with a fiery arrow so that he could bathe in it; near this spring, a temple honoring Vasistha can be seen a few kilometers from mod. Manali.

Vasu₁ [vas₄u] amnf good, excellent ["that which shines"] — n. wealth, riches, money, treasure | gold, jewel, precious stone | excellent, beneficial object — m. myth. np. of Vasu₁ "the rich one", epithet of Agni; Fire; the Sun; various deities | myth. np. of Vasu₁, 3rd son of Jamadagni | myth. [Mah.] np. of Vasu₁ "the Excellent one" king of the land of Cedi, son of Kṛtī, father of Satya vatī and Brhadratha; cf. Uparicara | myth. |Rām.| np. of King Vasu₁, son of Kuśa₁; he founded the city of GirivrajaRājagṛha | pl. vasavas myth. |aṣṭavasu| the group of the 8 Natural Treasures, a class of Vedic deities assisting Indra in the heaven of the 33 gods [trayastriṃśa]; they include [BU.]: Agni the Fire, Vāyu the Wind, Antarikṣa the Space, Aditya the Sun, Dyau the Sky/Light (husband of Prthivī the Earth), Candra the Moon god, and nakṣatrāṇi the set of constellations or lunar mansions; or

well [VP.]: Apa the Water (or Ahar the Day), Dh ruva the Fixed (Polar Star) or Space, Soma the Moon god, Dhara the ground of the Earth (or Prthu), Anila the Wind, Anala the Fire, Pratyūṣa the Dawn of the Sun, and Prabhāsa/Sāvitra the Light; they were born of Kasyapa and Aditi |Rām.| or of Prajāpati |Mah.|; the treasures represent the visible forms of natural laws; astr. they preside over the nakṣatra Sraviṣṭhā (beta of the Dolphin); later, they form a class of the gana; [Mah.] they visited the hermitage of Vasistha with their wives; Prthivī fell in love with the cow Nandinī, and asked Dyau to steal her; Vasistha in return cursed the vasavas to be reincarnated as men; in response to their supplications, he granted them to be reborn only very briefly, except for the one who had stolen Nandinī, condemned to a very long existence; they were reincarnated as sons of Gangādevī and King Sāntanu, all drowned at their birth except Devavrata/Bhīṣma | math. symb. the number 8.

vasugupta [gupta] m. hist. [Trika] np. of the phil. Va sugupta of Kaśmīra (end of 8th century); he received from Śiva in a dream the revelation of Śivasūtra; his student Kallata wrote the Spandakārikās, which expound the pratyabhijñādarśana doctrine.

vasudeva [deva] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Vasu₁ deva "Prolific Divine", king of Mathurā of the lunar yādava lineage, son of Śūra, brother of Kuntī; his birth was greeted by a celestial drum roll [Anakadundubhi]; he embodies Kaśyapa re returned to Earth by a curse of Varuna; imprisoned by the tyrant Kamsa, he had 8 sons by his wife Devakī, including Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, the previous ones having been killed at birth on the order of Kamsa; his other wives are Rohin₃ and Vaiśalī.
vasudevahindi [hindi] f. lit. np. of the vasudevahindi, jaina version of the Bṛhatkathā where Vasudeva takes the place of the prince Na ravāhanadatta.
vásudharā [dharā] f. bd. np. of the goddess Vasud harā "who brings wealth".
vásudhā |dhā₃| f. the earth | the earth, the soil; the kingdom. vasudhaiva kuṭumbakam |Hitopadeśa| The earth is our home.
vasunemi | nemi | mr. myth. n.p. from the nāga Vasunemi “Wheel of Fortune”; saved from a hunter by King Udayana, he showed him the underwater city Bhogavatī, and gave him the magical vīṇā Ghoṣavatī.
vasupālita [pālita] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Va supālita "Protected by wealth", rich merchant of Campā; very ugly, he was nicknamed Virūpaka; he was ruined by Kāmamañjarī, but avenged by Apahāravarmā.
vásupūjya | pūjya | m. jn. np. of the mythical king Va supūjya or Vasupūjyarāj "Venerable Jewel", father of the 12th arhat.

Vásubandhu [bandhu] m. hist. np. of Vasubandhu, Buddhist scholar of the 5th century, born to a brah mane father from Purușapura, of gotra Kauśika; he is the author of numerous philosophical works, including the Abhidharmakośa bhāsya, summa of the Theravāda doctrine; he is also credited with the grammar work Vyākhyāyukti, the Viṃśikā "20 verses on manifestation alone" and the Trimśikā "30 verses"; the Tarkaśāstra is also attributed to him; his brother Asanga converted him to the Mahāyāna doctrine.
vásumat [mat] amnf vasumatī rich; full of treasures — mr. myth. n.p. of Vasumān, son of Manu Vaivasvata | epith. of Kṛṣṇa and other gods or kings — f. cf. vasumatī.
vásumanas [manas] m. myth. np. of Vasumanā, king of Ayodhyā of the solar lineage, son of Haryaśva and Mādhavī; he is father of Tridhanvā.

vasumitra [mitra] m. hist. np. of the scholar Vasu mitra, a Sarvāstivādin monk from Gandhāra (2nd century); he presided over the 4th bd. council in Kaśmīra under Kaniska₁; he classified the doctrines in his Samayabhedoparacanacakra. vasurakșita [rakșita] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of vasurakṣita, wise advisor to King Anantavarmā; after the ruin of the kingdom, he took vasumdharā and his children to Māhiṣmatī.
vásurocis [rocis] n. rite [yajña] honoring the natural principles [vasavas].
vasum [acc. Vasu] iic.

vasumdhara [dhara] amnf vasumdharā generous, prolific — f. vasuṃdharā the land ["which bears treasures"] | the land, the soil; the kingdom lit. [DKC.] np. of Vasuṃdharā, queen of Vidarbha, wife of Anantavarmā and mother of Mañjuvādinī and Bhāskaravarmā; she is daughter of King Kusu madhanvā₁ and Sāgaradattā.

vasumatī [f. vasumat] f. the earth; syn. Bhū | region, terrain, soil | lit. [DKC.] np. of Va sumatī "rich as the earth", wife of King Rājahamsa; she took in Arthapāla, brought by his mother Tārāvalī, to serve as a companion to her son Rājavāhana.
vasumatīsnāna |snāna| n. SOC. np. of Vasu matīsnāna, ritual bath for the purification of the earth, on the 4th day of Rajā (Orissa).
vasos [g. Vasu] iic. . vasoșpati [pati] m. ved. np. of Vasoșpati "Master of riches", god of prosperity.
vastavya [pfp. [3] vas₁] amnf vas₁ tavyā who must stay or live (at (loc.)) | to spend (time). vastavyam one must stay.
vastavyatā [tā] f. residence.

vastí [act. vas₁] m. bladder | med. enema | med. [Ayurveda] laxative treatment with oil [anuvāsana] or herbal decoction [nirūha] — f. vastī | yoga | urinary tract cleansing exercise | | lat. vesica; all. Wanst; fr. bladder, vesicle.

vastu₁ [vas₁tu] n. goods, riches | thing; matter, substance | phil. concrete reality; fact | (in fig.) property, nature, character | gram. literal meaning (opp. alankāra figurative meaning) | that which is in question tion; theme; subject; matter; factual content | lit. plot of a story; scenario; musical composition substance, essence.
vastutas |tas| adv. in accordance with the nature of things | in substance, in reality; in fact; indeed; essentially. vastutas tu adv. in fact, yet; but in truth.
vastutaḥsattā [sattā] f. state of affairs.
vastutā [tā] f. ifc. state of being the object of (iic.) reality.
vastutva [tva] n. reality.
vastudharma [dharma] m. phil. the true nature of things | pl. id.
vastudharmin |in| amnf vastudharminī phil. which depends on the nature of a thing; objective.
vastudhvani [dhvani] m. lit. suggestion of a fact.

vastupāla [pāla] m. hist. n.p. of vastupāla, Jaina minister of king Vāghela Vīradhavala, born in Aņahilapāṭaka in Gujarat, died in 1240; he was appointed governor of Stambhatīrtha; with his brother Tejapāla he built temples in Śatruñjaya; he patronized the poet Someśvaradeva, who praised him in the Kīrtikaumudī.
vastubheda | bheda | m. lit. change of theme; break in event.
vastuvakratā |vakratā| f. lit. |Kuntaka| oblique quality of the subjects addressed.

vastuvidyā [vidyā] f. soc. science of the consecration of habitation or cult sites, of favorable installation rites, of technical processes of architecture and iconography; cf. matsyapurāṇa; syn. vastuśāstra.
vastuvṛtta |vṛtta| n. the facts (substance of what has occurred). vastuvrttena in fact; to tell the truth.
vastuśāstra | śāstra | n. cf. vastuvidyā.
vástu₂ [vas₁tu] f. dawn; Morning. vástoh in the morning. vástor vastoh adv. every morning. vástor asyāḥ adv. This morning. práti vástoh adv. towards the morning.
vastra |instr. vas₁| n. garment, fabric — amnf vastrā clothed in (iic.) — v. [11] pr. (vastráyati) to put on a garment — v. [11] pr. (vastrīyati) to desire a garment || fr. jacket, garment.
vastrakala | kalā | f. the art of embroidery.
vastragopana | gopana | n. the art of concealing in one's clothes, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
vastracīra | cīra | n. ragged garment.
vastrapūta [pūta₁] amnf vastrapūtā filtered through a cloth. vastrapūtam jalam purified water.
vastrayuga [yuga] n. pair of clothes | var. vas₁ trayugala id.
vastrayugin |in| amnf vastrayuginī who wears a pair of clothes.

vastraharana [harana] n. myth. episode from the Mah. where Duḥśāsana humiliates Draupadī in front of her husbands by undressing her | episode from the BhP. where Kṛṣṇa steals the clothes of the cowherds [gopī] when they take their bath.
vasná [vas₁na] mn ved. wealth; selling price; salary | lat. vendo; fr. vendre.
vasnika |ika| amnf vasnikā employee.

√ vah₁ v. [1] pr. (vahati) pft. (uvāha) pp. (ūdha) pf. (apa, ā, ut, upa, ni, nis, pari, pra, vi, sam) to carry, bring, take; to drive, lead, transport, drag, pull (said of a horse harnessed to a chariot, of a draft animal harnessed to a cart) | to advance, go; to flow (river), to blow (wind) | to carry, to have — ps. (uhyate) to be carried, to be taken, to be transported — ca. (vāhayati) to drive, to diri ger, to use a vehicle | to have carried, to have pulled (by (i.)) | lat. veho; all. Wagen; ang. wagon; fr. véhicule. aśvena vah to go on horseback. plavena vah to go by boat. bhrtyo bharam vahati the servant carries the burden. nadī vahati the river flows.
vah₂ [vah₁] ifc. amnf that goes (on horseback, etc).

vaha [agt. vah₁] amnf vahā ifc. that which leads, that which carries, that which transports (iic.); charged with, provided with (iic.) | that which bears the name of (iic.) — ins. m. vehicle; chariot; boat | wind, current | myth. one of the 7 Winds of Heaven | marut | ; the Devīpurāṇa lists: Parāvaha, Nivaha, Udvaha, Samvaha, Vivaha, Pravaha, and Parivaha; they are associated with the 7 languages of Agni |saptajihva| | bearer; transport animal; shoulder — n. collar of a draft animal — f. vahā watercourse, river || lat. via; fr. wave, way.
vahat [ppr. vah₁] amnf vahantī flowing.
vahadgu |gu| adv. at the time when cattle are being herded.
vahatú |vahatu| m. soc. procession of my marriage; wedding.
vahana [agt. vah₁] amnf vahanā ifc. who goes, who drives, who carries — act. n. driving (by car, etc.); vehicle. vahanīkṛ to use as a vehicle.

vahitra [instr. vah₁] n. boat. kimārdrakavanijo vahitracintayā A ginger merchant has no business dealing with navigation (this maxim mocks people who concern themselves with things for which they are incompetent).
vahin [agt. vah₁] amnf vahinī who pulls — m. draft animal.

váhni [vah₁ni] m. draft animal | fire [“that which carries the offerings”] | myth. np. of Vahni, epith. of Agni guardian [dikpāla] of the Southeast | phil. masculine divine principle, opp. śakti | phil. mystical fire — n. |vahnipurāṇa| lit. np. of the Vahni₁ purāṇa.
vahnitrikona [trikona] n. phil. [Tantra] fiery triangle, point upwards, symbolizing the male principle in geometric | yantra | diagrams.
vahnitva [tva] n. phil. nature of fire. vahnitvāvacchinna phil. delimited by the fiery nature.
Vahnipurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. of the Vahnipurāṇa, also called Agneyapurāna; the Rāmakathā is a section of it.
vahnimat [mat] amnf vahnimatī which contains fire. parvato vahnimān dhūmavattvāt var. parvato vah nimān dhūmāt | Tarkasaṃgraha | The mountain contains fire, because it carries smoke.

vā₁ conj. cl. or, or else, either; supposing that, as | or rather, or better | really | however, yet | even supposing that the future angle ranges | the interr. angle ranges therefore; isn't it; is it that? | optional gram. ly; preferably na vā otherwise; optionally | rather than. na ... vā neither ... nor. na vā ... vā id. vā ... vā either ... or. yadi vā ... vā id. vā na vā yes or no | rarely. vā na ... vā either we don't have ... or. yadi ... vā unless. atha vā or else; but. ke vā (followed by a negation) all.

√ vā₂ v. [2] pr. (vāti) pp. (vāta) pf. (nis, pra) to blow, to wind; to blow on or towards (acc.) | to exhale; to emit (odor) — ca. (vāpayati) to cause to blow | gr. alpha opi ; lat. aer; all. wehen; ang. air; fr. air.
vāṃśa [*vaṃśa] amnf vāṃśā f. vāṃśī re latif made from sugar cane | made from bamboo.
vāk iic. vāc.
vākkovida [kovida] amnf vākkodiā expert in speech — m. myth. epith. of Hanuman, who possesses the science of language.
vākpati | pati | m. hist. np. of vākpati "Master of Sanskrit", epith. of the poet-king Muñja.
vākpatirāja [rāja] m. hist. np. of vākpatirāja, prakrit author (early 8th century).
vākpatha | patha | m. turn of speech | range of voice.
vākpathātita | atīta| amnf vākpathātitā out of earshot.
vākpārusya [pārusya] n. vulgar, abusive or insulting language; verbal violence.
vāká [agt. vac] amnf vākā ifc. who says, who recites, who expresses (iic.) — act. m. recitation.
vākovākya [vākya] n. dialogue.

Vākāṭaka m. pl. hist. np. of the dynasty of the Vākāṭakās princes; they reigned in Mahārāṣṭra from the 3rd to the 5th century, succeeding the Sātavāhanās; their capital was Nandivardhana₁; they were patrons of religion and the arts; cf. Pravarapura, Pravarasena₁, Sarvasena.

vākya [pfp. [1] vac] n. speech, discourse, language, declaration, edict, utterance | gram. proposition, sentence (opp. word [pada]) | gram. analytic expression (opp. synthetic expression [vrtti]); not. paraphrase of a compound word — f. vākyā ifc. speech of (iic.). samānavākye adv. gram. in the same sentence. pade na varņā vidyante varņesvavayavā na ca | vākyāt padānām atyantam praviveko na kaścana gram. [Bhartrhari] There are no phonemes in words, nor subparts in phonemes; outside the sentence, the complete isolation of independent words is meaningless. padānāmabhidhitsitārthagranthanākarah san darbho vākyam [KM.] A sentence is the arrangement of a set of words articulating a meaning that one wishes to express. ākhyātam sāvyayakārakaviśesanam vākyam gram. [MB.] The sentence consists of the verb with its adverbs, its complements, and its determiners.
vākyakarana [karana] m. astr. np. of the Vākyakarana or Vākyakaraṇasiddhānta, astronomical work by Vararuci₂ (circa 1282), origin of the Vākyapañcānga almanac popular in South India.
vākyakarman [karman] n. gram. indirect discourse.
vākyakāṇḍa |kāṇḍa| n. lit. np. from the vākyakāṇḍa, 2nd section of the Vākyapadīya, dealing with the sentence; cf. Trikāndī.
vākyadarśin [darśin] amnf vākyadarśinī gram. adhering to the theory that the sentence is the unit of meaning; opp. padadarsin.

Vākyapadīya [padaīya] n. lit. np. of the Vākyapadīya "of phrases and words", an important linguistic treatise by Bhartrhari, dealing with the semantic and cognitive aspects of language; cf. ha rikārikās, Trikāṇḍī; there is a gloss [vrtti] by Harivṛṣabha (probably Bhartṛhari himself), a commentary [tīkā] by Puņyarāja for the 2nd section, and the Prakīrņaprakāśa by Helārāja for the 3rd; more recently, see the Ambākartrī by Raghunātha₄ Sarmā.

vākyabheda | bheda | m. gram. segmentation of an utterance into sentences | phil. [Mīmāmsā] ambiguity of interpretation of an injunction as to aim at a single purpose; opp. viśiṣṭavidhāna | gram. ["sentence break"] lack of unity of the communicative purpose of an utterance | pl. contradictory sentences; dis incoherent course. sākṣī vākyabhedān bahūnakathayat the witness made many contradictory statements.
vākyayojanā [yojanā] f. gram. structural analysis of the sentence.
vākyaracanā [racanā] f. taking of the floor; the act of speaking | gram. syntax.
vākyavakratā [vakratā] f. lit. [Kuntaka] oblique quality of sentences; tortuousness of speech.
vākyavajra [vajra] n. pl. ["words that fall like lightning" thunderous words; cho quants.
vākyavara | vara₁ | n. wish, vow.
vākyavidyā [vidyā] f. lit. interpretation of the phrase in poetry.
vākyaśeṣa [śeṣa] m. gram. ellipsis; implied | meaning given by the context.
vākyasaṃskāra [saṃskāra] m. gram. sentence development; opp. padasaṃskāra.
vākyasaṃcāra [saṃcāra] m. manner of expressing oneself.
vākyasphoṭa [sphoṭa] m. gram. evocative power of a sentence.
vākyādhyāhāra [adhyāhāra] m. gram. paraphrase supplementing the omitted terms of an elliptical sentence.

vākyārtha [artha] m. gram. meaning of a sentence; semantics. vākyārthībhāva m. gram. establishment of the meaning of a sentence | phil. [Mīmāṃsā] transmission of the speaker's communicative intention; syn. tātparya.
vākyārthatva [tva] n. gram. quality of being the overall meaning of the sentence; syn. vākyārthībhāva.
Vākyārthamātṛkā [mātṛkā] f. lit. np. from the Vākyārthamātrkā of Śālikanātha, a work on semantics (9th century).
vākyārthamātṛkāvṛtti [vṛtti] f. bed. n.p. of the Vākyārthamātrkāvrtti, his commentary.
vākyaikatva [ekatva] n. gram. principle of the uniqueness of the verb in the sentence | syntactic integrity.
vāg iic. vāc.
vāgīśa [īśa] amnf vāgīśā eloquent, good orator; title of poet — m. myth. np. of vāgīśa, epith. of Brhaspati "Master of the word".
vāgīśatva [tva] n. eloquence.
vāgīśvara |īśvara| m. eloquent orator | bd. deified sage; qualifies not. Mañjughoșa — f. vāgīśvarī myth. epith. of Sarasvatī "the Eloquent One".

Vāgīśvarakīrti [kīrti] m. hist. np. of the tantric master bd. Vāgīśvarakīrti who taught at Vi kramaśīla (1011th century) with the title of "Master of the Western Gate" [dvārapaṇḍita]; he is the author of the Mrtyuvañcanopadeśa.
vāgrṣabha [rṣabha] m. eloquent man, with eminent speech.

vāgrṣabhatva [tva] n. eloquence. pathan dvijo vāgrsabhatvam īyāt syāt ksatriyo bhūmipatitvam īyāt | vanigjanah panyaphalatvam īyāt janaś ca śūdro'pi mahattvam īyāt | [Rām.] May a Brahmin acquire eloquence through reading (the Rām.), may a Kṣatriya acquire a kingdom, may a merchant acquire wealth, and even may a śūdra attain eminence. vāgdaņda [daņda] m. rebuke | du. insults and blows.
vāgdāna |dāna| n. soc. engagement of a fiancée with a view to marriage.
vāgdusta | dusta | amnf vāgdustā who uses bad, vulgar language.

Vāgbhaṭa [bhaṭa] m. hist. np. of Vṛddha Vāgbhata the Elder, a 7th-century physician; he is credited with the Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya saṃhitā, a synthesis of Indian medical knowledge [Ayurveda]; the Aṣṭāṅgasaṃgraha, a related work in prose, is also attributed to him, but its authenticity is disputed. hist. np. of the physician Vāgbhata₁ the Younger, a descendant of the former, who is said to have lived a century later | hist. np. of Vāgbhaṭa₂, a 12th-century poet, author of the Vāgbhaṭālaṃkāra | hist. np. by Vāgbhaṭa₃, a 13th-century poet and author of the Kāvyānuśāsana₁.
vāgbhatālamkāra [alamkāra] m. lit. np. of the Vāgbhatālamkāra, a work of poetics by Vāgbhata₂.
vāgbhava [bhava] n. [vāgbhavabīja] phil. [Tantra] the bījamantra 'aim'. vāgmin var. vāggmin [min] amnf vāgminī eloquent — m. ["master of the word"] intellectual, scholar.

vāgyoga | yoga | m. correct use of the tongue. yastu prayunkte kuśalo viśese śabdān yathāvad vyavahārakāle | so'nantamāpnoti jayam paratra vāgyogavid dusyati cāpaśabdaiḥ | [Mahābhāsya] He who knows how to use words with discernment to communicate correctly, this connoisseur of the correct use of the tongue will obtain eternal success in the hereafter, but he commits a sin if he speaks incorrectly.
vāgvajra [vajra] n. ["word of thunder"] violent words | lit. np. from the Vāgraja, a polemical work.
vāgvardhinī [vardhinī] f. [vāgvardhinīsabhā] soc. grammar improvement class.
vāgvaśin [vaśin] amnf vāgvaśinī who masters the language. tam vāgvašyevānuvartate he has mastery of the language.
vāgvid | vid₃ | amnf eloquent | learned; educated, wise.
vāgvin |vin| amnf vāgvinī eloquent.
vāgvyavahāra [vyavahāra] m. oral discussion.

vāghela m. hist. n.p. of the Vāghela dynasty of Gujarat, first vassal of the Solankī kings then independent in 1243 with king Vīradhavala; its capital was Dholka; it ended with the defeat of Karnadeva in 1299 by Alauddin Khilji.
vān iic. vāc.
vānmatī [mat] f. geo. np. of the vānmatī "where the word flows", sacred river of Nepal; mod. Bāgmatī.
vānmanasa [manas] n. du. vānmanase speech and thought.

vānmáya |maya| amnf Vānmayī concerning speech; whose nature is speech — n. language; eloquence, rhetoric; literature — f. Vānmayī myth. np. of Vānmayī "Made of speech", epith. of Sarasvatī. vānmaye (attested) in language; in literature.

vāc [act. vac] f. [nom. Vāk] voice, speech, sound; verb, language, discourse; holy word phil. |Sāṃkhya| the faculty |karmendriya| of speech, whose regent | niyantr | is Agni; its predominant element [bhūta] is ākāśa the ether; the associated perception [tanmātra] is sound [śabda] which excites the sense [buddhīndriya] of hearing [śrotra] | myth. np. of Vāk, the personified word, epith. of Saras vatī; she is the wife of Prajāpati, and represents his power of creation — v. [11] pr. (vācyati) to want to speak.
vācāṭa [āṭa] amnf vācāṭā chatterbox | boastful; grandiloquent.

vācaka [agt. vac] amnf vācikā who speaks, who recites; who speaks of (g. iic.) — m. phil. sonorous essence of a divinity (svarūpamantra) | gram. denoting word; opp. dyotaka | soc. vācaka title of Reader.
vācakatā [tā] f. gram. power of expression; meaning.
vācakatva |tva| n. id.
Vācaknavī [*Vacaknu] f. bed. n.p. of Vācaknavī, patr. of the philosopher Gārgī “daughter of Vacaknu”.
vācana |act. ca. vac| n. |"that which makes one recite"| recitation, reading aloud — f. vācanā lesson; chapter.
vācanaka [ka] n. recitation; not. of blessing |svasti|.
vācanārtha [artha] m. lit. (text) for public recitation; opp. paṭhanārtha.
vācanika [*vacanaika] amnf vācanikī gram. expressly mentioned, explicitly taught; opp. svābhāvika — n. verbal message; syn. vācika.
vācas [g. vāc] iic.

vācaspáti [pati] m. myth. np. of Vācaspati₁ "Master of speech", epith. of various gods, not. Brhaspati; he presides over the human faculty of speech | soc. title of scholar [paṇḍita] | hist. np. of the philosopher Vācaspati₁ Miśra (10th century), of monistic [advaita] tradition; he is the author of the Bhāmatī exegesis of the Brahmasūtrabhāsya₁ commentary of Sankarācārya, and of the Tātparyaṭīkā gloss of the Nyāyabhāsya; He is also credited with the Tattvabindu, the Nyāyasūcīnibandhana, the Tattva vaiśāradī commentary on the Pātañjalayogaśāstra, the Sabdārņava dictionary, and the Sāmkhyatattvakaumudī; his Tatt vasamīkṣā is a commentary on the Brahmasid dhi of Mandana Miśra; for his erudition, he was awarded the title of sarvatantrasvatantra | hist. np. of the scholar Vācaspati₁ Miśra (15th century), author of the Anumānanirnaya, the Khandanoddhāra, the Nyāyasūtroddhāra, the Vārdhamānendu, the

comments [prakāśa] of the Tattvacintāmaņi of Gangesa and of the Nyāyaratna of Manikantha Misra [tarkavācaspati] hist. np. of Tārānātha Tar kavācaspati, (1812–1885), Bengali scholar, lexicographer, author of the Vācaspatya encyclopedia and of the Aśubodha grammar.

Vācaspatya [*Vācaspati₁a] amnf vācaspatyā relating to Vācaspati₁ — n. eloquence | lit. np. of the Vācaspatya, encyclopedia in Sanskrit due to the paṇḍita Tārānātha Tarkavācaspati (1884, Cal cutta); it includes not. 151 maxims |nyāya|.
vācoyukti [yukti] f. appropriate words | turn of phrase, idiomatic form.
vācā | related to vāc | f. word; speech; text.
vācāla [la] amnf vācālā chatterbox; noisy (oi bucket) | boastful — ifc. filled with the din of (iic.).
vācika [*vacika] amnf vācikā verbal; communicated orally — n. speech; oral message; news, rumors; proclamations. pāruṣye daṇḍavācike the two forms of violence: physical and verbal.
vacin [agt. vac] f. vacinī ifc. that asserts (iic.); that presumes (iic.); that signifies (iic.).

vācya [pfp. [1] ca. vac] amnf vācyā to say, to state; about which one must speak; which deserves to be said | to whom one must or can address the word | to denounce; reprehensible, blameworthy — n. blame, reproach; that which must be denounced | gram. that which is expressed; literal sense, connotation | gram. voice; there are three voices: the active, where the verb denotes the agent | kartr|, the passive, where the verb denotes the patient or the goal [kartṛ], and the impersonal, where the verb denotes only the process; the other semantic roles |kāraka| necessitated by the paraphrase must be provided to the corresponding cases.
vācyatā [tā] f. enunciation; predication | that in saying; the act of blaming; infamy. sa kātara iti vācyatām gataḥ he exposed himself to being called a coward.
vācyatva [tva] n. id. | that which must be said; signified — ifc. that which is signified by (iic.).
vācyavācaka [vācaka] n. gram. the signified and the signifying.
vācyavacakabhāva [bhāva] m. gram. relation between the signified and the signifier.

vācyāvacana [avacana] n. lit. not mentioning what is to be expressed, an aesthetic defect of poetry. বাস Vāja [act. vaj] m. Strength; vigor, energy | soc. ritual food | myth. np. of the rbhu Vāja "Strength" — n. food; offering | ved. not. wild rice broth prepared by the priest for the vājapeya as a sacrifice to Brhaspati.

vājapeya [peya] n. soc. ["drink of vigor"] Vedic royal rite of sacrifice of the soma consecrated to Indra and the centaurs [gandharvās]; it celebrates the virility of a king of mature age, and replaces the rājasūya for the emperors [samrāj]; a race of 17 chariots on a course marked by 17 arrows ends ritually with the victory of the king; in the center of the course a brahmin, perched on a pole |sthāṇu|, spins a chariot wheel and chants verses from the Rigveda; cf. yūparohaņa.
vājapeyin |in| amnf vājapeyinī who drinks the soma of sacrifice — m. soc. n.p. of a high caste Vājapeyī man.
vājavat |vat| amnf vājavatī vigorous, strong.
vājaśravas | śravas | m. np. of Vājaśravā "Famous for its vigor".
Vājaśravasa [a] m. lit. [KU.] patr. of Vājaśravasa "son of Vājaśravā"; he made the sacrifice of all his
possessions [viśvajit], and sent his son Naciketā to Death [Yama].
Vājapyāyana m. hist. patr. du grammai rien antique Vājapyāyana.
vājayú [Vājayu] amnf eager to conquer.
vājasaneyá m. myth. n.p. of Vājasaneya, patr. by Yājñavalkya | pl. soc. Vājasaneya school of white Yajurveda.

Vājasaneyasamhitā [samhitā] f. lit. np. of the Vājasaneyasamhitā, recension of the white Yajurveda, established by Yājñavalkya, and distributed to his 15 disciples; [AP.] it alone is authorized in the kaliyuga.
vājasaneyin [in] amnf vājasaneyinī who ap partent à l'école de VājasaneyaYājñavalkya | pl. hist. school of the white Yajurveda; opp. taittirīya.
vājasaneyi iic. vājasaneyin.
vājasaneyiprātiśākhya [prātiśākhya] n. bed. the prātiśākhya collection of the white Yajurveda.
vājasaneyisaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. bed. n.p. of the vājasaneyisamhitā or white Yajurveda; we distinguish two recensions [śākhā]: the mādhyamdinīya and the kāṇva .
vājin [agt. vaj] amnf vājinī valiant, heroic, manly; strong, effective, prolific — m. horse (symbol of Strength) | arrow. pragrhyantām vājinah I restrain my arrows.
vājī iiv. Vāja. vājīkaraņa | karaņa | n. aphrodisiac substance.
vājīkaraṇatantra | tantra | n. med. the science of aphrodisiacs and sexual vigor, a section of Ayurveda.
√ বাস্প্ত vāñch v. [1] pr. (vāñchati) pp. (vāñchita) pf. (abhi) to desire, to wish, to aspire to acc. ang. to wish; all. wunsc.
vāñchā [act. vāñch] f. desire, longing for (loc. iic. vānchām kṛ to aspire to (loc.).
vāñchita [pp. vāñch] amnf vāñchitā desired, loved — n. desire, longing.
vāṭa [*vaṭa] mf vāṭī enclosure; fence; garden, park; hut; village.
vāṭaka [ka] mf vāṭikā id.
vāḍaba var. vāḍava [*vaḍaba] m. standard.
Vāḍabāgni [agni] m. myth. n.p. of Vāḍabāgni or Vādavāgni “Equine Fire”; cf. Vadavāgni.

vāṇa m. sound; music; harp | |bāṇa | reed; arrow — f. Vāṇī sound; music | speech, voice, dictation; good diction; eloquent speech | myth. np. of Vāṇī "speech", epith. of Sarasvatī | pl. orchestra; choir. sapta vāṇyaḥ the 7 notes of the scale.
vāṇijá var. bāṇija [*vaṇija] m. merchant || hi. banya.
vāṇijaka [ka| m. merchant, trader.
vāṇijika [*vaṇijika] m. merchant, merchant.
vāṇijya [*vaṇijya] nf vāṇijyā commerce.
vāṇijyaka |ka| m. merchant, trader.

Vāta [pp. vā₂] m. wind, air, breath; vital breath myth. np. of Vāta, epith. of the god Vāyu “who breathes” | med. the breath, one of the 3 humors | tridoșa|; syn. Vāyu | lat. ventus; ang. Wind; all. Wind; fr. vent. prativātam adv. against the wind.
vātaramha [raṃhas] amnf vātaraṃhā swift as the wind.
vātavarṣá | varṣa | m. (collective) wind and rain.
vātāṇḍa |aṇḍa| n. med. swollen testicle — m. who has swollen testicles.

Vātāpi |āpī| m. myth. |Mah.| np. of the ogre |rākṣasa| Vātāpi "Flatulence", who with his brother Ilvala han ait the Daṇḍaka forest; he disguised himself as a sacrificial ram to be eaten by the brahmins, whose belly he would burst open when Ilvala called him; he met his fate by being digested by Agasti; cf. Mahākūteśvara | geo. np. of the city of Vātāpi₁ in Karņāṭa, capital of the Cālukyās (540–757); captured by the Pallavās in 642, it remained under their control for 13 years, until the restoration of the kingdom by Vikramāditya₁; mod. Badāmi. vātāpijīrno bhava [Agasti] Let the digestion of Vātāpi be accomplished.
vātāyana [ayana] amnf vātāyanā that moves through the air | swift as the wind (said of a horse) — n. window; balcony; terrace. niruddhavātāyana with closed windows.
avaniśayanāsannavātāyanasthah [MD.] Standing at the window near his bed on the floor.
vātāma var. bādāma m. almond.
vāti [agt. vā₂] m. vent.

vātika [Vātaika] amnf vātikī windy | rheumatic — m. talkative; smooth talker, flatterer — f. vātikā [Mayamata] area measure of 5 quarters [vartanaka] (about 2 ha); it is a quarter of the land needed to feed a family in a village.
vātula [Vātala] amnf vātulā windy | flatterer | loquacious, talkative | var. vātūla f. vātūlā madman afflicted with gout or rheumatism || hi. baul.
Vātulāgama [āgama] m. bed. n.p. of the Vātulāgama, a mūlāgama of the śaiva Siddhānta doctrine.
vātsa [*vatsa] amnf vātsī np. patr. “descendants of vatsa” | vātsi soc. son of vatsa — f. cf. vātsī.
vātsalya [*vatsalaya] n. parental affection towards children | tenderness towards g. loc. iic. .
vātsī [f. vātsa] f. soc. wife of a vātsya.
Vātsīputra [putra] m. hist. np. of Vātsīputra, philosopher founder of a bd. heterodox doctrine.
Vātsīputrīya [īya] m. pl. bd. np. of the Vātsīputrīyās school, considered heretical by Va subandhu.
vātsya [*vatsaya] amnf vātsyā relating to the country vatsa — m. soc. n.p. patr. from vātsya “of the cendants of vatsa”.

Vātsyāyana [*vatsaāyana] m. soc. n.p. from gotra Vātsyāyana "descendant of vatsa" | bed. n.p. by Vātsyāyana₁, 5th century philosopher, author of the Kāmasūtra | bed. n.p. by Pakṣilasvāmī Vātsyāyana₂, philosopher from 4th century Bihāra, author of Nyāyabhāsya.
vād [ca. vad] v. [10] pr. (vādayati) pp. (vādita) pfp. (vādya) ppr. ps. (vādyamāna) to make speak, to make say | to play a musical instrument (i.).

vāda [agt. vad] amnf vādā ifc. who speaks of, who makes heard, who proclaims — act. m. word, declaration, discussion; statement, narration; thesis, theory | argumentation; debate | phil. [Nyāya] intellectual debate; Akṣapāda distinguishes honest debate [vāda] where the opponents seek to establish the truth, specious debate [jalpa] whose sole purpose is to win the argument, and offensive debate [vitandā] whose purpose is to demolish the opponent by all means | controversy; dispute, quarrel | sound (of an instrument); song (of a bird) — ifc. discussion of, mention of, doctrine of (ii.). ādau vāda āsīt |John| In the beginning was the Word.
vādakathā [kathā₁] f. phil. intellectual debate.
vādanyāya [nyāya] m. phil. epistemological doctrine bd. of the logic of argumentation of Dharmakīrti.
vādaka [agt. vad] amnf vādikā musician.

vādana [agt. vad] m. musician — act. n. noise — f. vādanā ifc. sound of, music of; playing of (instrument) — loc. vādane ifc. mod. at (such) hour. saptavādane adv. mod. ["when 7 o'clock strikes"] at 7 o'clock.
vādavidyā [vidyā] f. phil. [nyāya] rhetoric; Akṣapāda theorized it.
vādi iic. vādin.

vādirāja [rāja] m. hist. n.p. of the scholar Dvaita Vādirāja, born in southern Kanara (16th century); he was the 20th pontiff of the mațha of Udupī; we owe him not. the Yukti mallikā, the Nyāyaratnāvalī the Srutitattvaprakāśikā and the Bhāvaprakāśikā tīkā .
vādin [agt. vad] amnf vādinī ifc. who speaks, who says, who states, who affirms (iic.) | phil. arguer of a thesis; opp. prativādin — m. (law) plaintiff | myth. np. of Vādī, son of King Pṛthu.
vādya | pfp. | 1 | vād | n. music (instrumental) — m. musical instrument.
vādyavidyā | vidyā | f. knowledge of music.
vādyamāna [ppr. ps. vād] amnf vādyamānā being played.
Vādhūla m. patr. of Vādhūla — n. bed. n.p. of the Vādhūla śrautasūtra .
vāna₁ |*vana| amnf vānī relating to the woods; inhabitant of the woods — n. thick forest.
vāna₁ [act. vā₃] n. braiding; weaving; quilt sewing. vānadaņda | daņda | m. loom, shuttle.

vānaprastha [prastha] m. soc. brahmin in the 3rd stage of brahmanic life |āśrama|, hermit withdrawn in the forest; the vānaprastha must have secured his offspring (by the birth of a son of his son) but may withdraw into the forest with his wife; the associated puruṣārtha is dharma.
vānara [vāna₁ra] m. monkey — f. vānarī guenon || hi. bandar.
vānaraketana [ketana] m. myth. np. of vānaraketana, epith. of Arjuna "who has the monkey as his emblem".
vānaraketu | ketu | m. myth. np. of vānaraketu, epith. of Arjuna "who has the monkey as his emblem".
vānarasenā |senā| f. myth. |Rām.| monkey army, ally of King Rāma; it helped him to conquer Lankā.
vānaspatyá [*vanaspatiya] amnf vānaspatyā coming from a tree; sylvan; woody — m. tree, shrub — m. fruit of a tree | group of trees.
vānta |pp. vam| amnf vāntā vomi. vāntam samskritam sanskrit to vomit (bad sans krit, to question sentences ending in 'vā').
vānti [act. vam] f. vomiting.
vapa₁ |act. vap₁| n. the act of shaving.
vāpa₁ |agt. vap₂| m. sower | seed — ifc. sown with (iic.).
vāpana₁ [act. vap₁] n. the act of shaving.
vāpana₁ [act. vap₂] n. sowing.
vāpi [act. vap₂] f. pond (formed by dikes) | vāpī id. | reservoir, cistern.
vāpin [agt. vap₂] ifc. amnf vāpinī who sows (iic.). māṣavāpin who sows beans.
vāma₁ amnf vāmā left | left, curved | low, dwarf, vile. vāmena var. vāmatas adv. left. vāmād dakṣiṇam adv. from left to right.
vāma₃ |act. vam| m. vomiting.
vāmatā [tā] f. annoyance; disfavor; resistance.
vāmatva |tva| n. id.
vāmabhuja [bhuja] m. left arm.
vāmācaraṇa |ācaraṇa| n. soc. practice of the tantric path.
Vāmācaraṇabhaṭṭācārya | bhaṭṭaācārya | m. hist. np. of Vāmācaraṇabhaṭṭācārya, logician of the early 20th century, precursor of the use of diagrams for the Navyanyāya.
vāmācāra [ācāra] m. phil. [Tantra] the tan way
trique [śākta] "of the left hand", who practices impure prohibitions; cf. makārapañcaka; opp. dakṣiṇācāra.
vāmācārin [in] amnf vāmācāriņī soc. [Tantra] adept of "left-hand" practices.
vāmetara [itara] amnf vāmetarā right ["other than left".
vāmá₂ |obj. van | amnf vāmī f. vāmā char mant, beautiful.

vāmadeva | deva | m. phil. | śaivasiddhānta | np. of vāmadeva, protective face of SadāśivaUmā, turned towards the North, associated with the world of stability | pratisthā₂|, with the element of water and the color red; he is represented with feminine features | myth. np. of the hermit vāmadeva₁ Gautama "whose god is charming", who composed the essential part of the 4th mandala of the Rigveda; [Mah.] he had splendid horses which King Sala₁ borrowed from him; when he came to claim them in vain, giants appeared to kill him lit. |DKC.| np. of the sage Vāmadeva₂, who advised King Rājahaṃsa | lit. [KSS.] np. of the wise vidyādhara Vāmadeva₃, who keeps the jewels of the vidyādharās in his hermitage at Ma laya.

vāmalocanā [locana] amnf vāmalocanā with the pretty gaze — f. vāmalocanā lit. [DKC.] np. of the princess vāmalocanā "with the beautiful gaze", daughter of King Vīraketu; she was abducted by King Mattakāla, then freed by Somadatta₂ whom she married.
vāmoru [ūru] amnf vāmorū who has beautiful thighs.
vāmaka₁ |agt. vam| amnf vāmikā who vomits.
vāmaka₂ |vāma₁ka| amnf vāmikā ad verse, cruel, harsh — f. vamika myth. n.p. from vāmikā, epith. from Durgā “Cruel”.
Vāmakeśvaratantra |īśvaratantra| n. lit. np. of the Vāmakeśvaratantra, work of tantric rites; cf. Setubandha₂.

Vāmana m. dwarf | myth. np. of Vāmana "the dwarf", son of Aditi, conceived according to the milk vow |payovrata| as the 5th descent |avatāra| of Viṣṇu, the first in human form; he descended to earth to fight the daitya Bali, tyrant king who had appropriated the three worlds; coming to a festival in Bali as a dwarf brahmin, he requested 3 strides of land; when Bali granted it to him (disobeying his guru Sukra who had recognized Viṣṇu, and thus losing his protection) he transformed into the Cosmic Giant [Trivikrama] to cover the three worlds; he is depicted as a dwarf holding the para sol of the brahmin | myth. np. of the celestial elephant [gajapati] Vāmana₁, guardian [diggaja] of the South | hist. np. of the grammarian Vāmana₂, second author of the Kāśikā vṛtti (7th century) | hist. np. of Vāmana₃ or Vāmanācārya, minister to King Jayāpīda, poet and grammarian of Kaśmīra from the late 8th century; he is credited with the manual of poetics Kāvyālamkāravṛtti; hist. np. of Vāmana₄ Bhatta Bāna, court poet of Peda Komați Vema in Kondavīdu, Andhra (14th century); he is the author of the Nalābhyudaya. [purāna] n. lit. Vāmanapurāṇa from the np. Vāmanapurāṇa, a relatively recent mixed mythological text.
Vāmanācārya |ācārya| m. hist. np. of the literary critic Vāmanācārya; cf. Vāmana₃.
vāmanika [ika] m. dwarf — f. dwarf vamanikā.
vāmin [agt. vam] amnf vāminī qui vo mit — f. vāminī (with yoni) (vulva) qui ev le sperme.
vāya [act. vā₃] m. weaving — agt. amnf vāyī ifc. who weaves (iic.) — m. weaver. tantuvāyaḥ mf tantuvāyī weaver.
vāyava [*vāyua] amnf vāyavī concerning the Wind, relating to vāyu — f. vāyavī the Northwest.
vāyavīya [īya] amnf vāyavīyā which relates to the Wind; aerial.
Vāyavīyapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. of the Vāyavīyapurāṇa, one of the oldest texts
mythoritualists [purāna], of Shaivite tradition [śaiva]; also called Vāyupurāṇa, Śivapurāṇa, śaivapurāņa.
vāyavīyasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. np. of the vāyavīyasamhitā, collection of texts concerning the Shaivite doctrine and rite.

vāyasa [*vayas₂a] mf vāyasī bio. zoo. cor beau, coreille | arch. the raven, a matrix [yoni] of the āyādi system — n. multitude of ravens. narāṇām tāpito dhūrtah pakṣiṇām caiva vāyasah The raven is the tormentor of men and a scoundrel among birds.
vāyasavidyā [vidyā] f. science (of divination by observation) of crows.
vāyu [*vā₂u] m. Wind; Air | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] the

substance [dravya₁] of Wind or Air; [Sāṃkhya] one of the 5 elements [bhūta]; his pañcabhūtasthala is Kālahastīśvara | med. breath, one of the 3 humors [tridoṣa]; syn. vāta | myth. ved. np. of the god vāyu, the personified Wind, messenger of the gods, son of Tvașțā, or born from the breath of Purușa; he is Mu khyaprāṇa, the Supreme Breath; his pro energy comes from the force leaving Indra after his murder of the brāhmaņa Vṛtra; he is friend of Agni, servant of Indra, father of Hanuman; He is the guardian [dikpāla] of the Northwest direction, and the king of the gandharvās; phil. [Sāṃkhya] he is the regent [niyantr] of the sense of touch [tvak]; he is the essence of Speech [Vāk]; first to drink the soma, he is the strongest of the gods; one day in anger, he created Lankā by blowing the top of Mount Meru into the sea; under the name of Anila, he is one of the 8 Treasures |vasu|; he is invoked at the beginning of rituals; he is represented as a white man, riding a gazelle; astr. he presides over the nakṣatra Svāti (Arcturus); cf. Pavana, marut, Vāta | math. symb. the number 5 (cf. prāṇās).

Vāyupatha [patha] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Vāyupatha "who follows the Wind", president of the Court of the vidyādharās kings; he is summoned on the complaint of Mānasavega against Naravāhanadatta, accusing him of being the lover of his sister and of wanting to become emperor; a terrible god intervenes and takes Naravāhanadatta to Mount Ŗṣyamūka; in the war that Mānasavega waged against Naravāhanadatta, Vāyupatha allies himself with the latter who becomes emperor; Vāyupatha has a younger sister Vāyuvegayaśā whom he wants to give to the emperor as a wife; but the pact of the latter with 4 other princesses obliges them to marry all 5 simultaneously.
vāyupurāṇa [purāṇa] n. bed. n.p. of vāyupurāṇa; cf. Vāyavīyapurāna.
vāyubhakṣa | bhakṣa | amnf vāyubhakṣā who feeds on air (said of a hermit).
vāyuvat |vat| adv. like the Wind.
vāyuvega [vega] amnf vāyuvegā swift as the Wind.

Vāyuvegayaśas [yaśas] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī princess Vāyuvegayaśā, younger sister of King Vāyupatha; she concludes with four other lovesick princesses not to marry Naravāhanadatta separately, under penalty of suicide of the others in the widows' fire; when Vāyupatha wants to marry her to the new emperor, she rebels and demands the collective marriage, saving her friends from the pyre.
vāyvagni |agni| mr. of. vāyvagnī ved. Vāyu and agni.
vār [agt. vṛ₁] n. ved. water; pool, stagnant water | gr. ουρον; lat. ūrīna; fr. urine. vāram nidhih the ocean | "receptacle of waters" |.

vārāśi |rāśi| m. ocean. goṣpadīkṛtavārāśim maśakīkṛtarākṣasam rāmāyaṇamahāmālāratnam vande'nilātmajam [dhyānaśloka] I honor you, Son of the Wind, great jewel in the garland of stories of the Rām., you who crossed the ocean like a puddle of hoof and treated the demons like mosquitoes.
vārdhanī [dhanin] f. soc. ritual water pot symbolizing the Goddess.

vāra | agt. vṛ₁ | m. that which restricts, that which obstructs; cover; door, barrier | determined place or event; agreed place | suitable or appropriate location, chosen place | favorable moment; chosen instant, appointed hour; agreed period opportunity, occasion — cl. after num. time | day of the week (dedicated to a deity (i.c.): sūrya (di manche), soma (Monday), mangala (Tuesday), budha (Wednesday), guru (Thursday), śukra (Friday), śani (sa medi)) | the solar day, an āyādi — f. vārā courti sane, prostitute | gr.; lat. hora; fr. heure. vāram adv. often, many times. ekavāram adv. only once. bahuvāram adv. many times, very often. vāramvāram adv. sometimes. kativāram kathayeyam how many times should I say it?
vārakanyakā [kanyakā] f. soc. ["girl (taken) in turn"] prostitute.
vāranārī [nārī] f. soc. prostitute, easy woman.
vāraka [agt. vṛ₁] amnf vārikā that which restrains, resists, opposes — m. obstacle | turn of a person. vārakeņa adv. in turn.

vāraņá [agt. vṛ₁] amnf vāraṇā that which resists, that which resists | dangerous; invincible — m. protection, armor | elephant — act. n. resistance; op position, obstacle — f. vāraņā geo. small river, tributary of the Ganges north of Benares — f. vāraņī female elephant.
vāraṇasī f. geo. Benares; cf. vārāṇasī.

vāraṇāvata n. myth. [Mah.] np. of the resort of Vāranāvata, located on the Ganges a week's walk from Hastināpura; Duryod hana exiled Kuntī and the Pāṇḍavās there in a very flammable lacquer palace [lākṣāgrha], in order to make them perish in a fire; the plot was foiled by Vidura, who had a tunnel dug through which the Pāṇḍavās escaped.
vāraruca [*vararucia] amnf vārarucā lit. composed by vararuci.
vārarucasaṃgraha [saṃgraha] m. lit. complete works of vararuci.
vārānasī [*varānasī] f. geo. np. of the city of vārāṇasī or vāraṇasī (Benares) "near Varāṇasī"; it is one of the 7 sacred cities [saptapurī]; cf. Kāśi | var. vāraņasī id.
vārāṇasīmāhātmya [māhātmya] n. lit. glorification of Benares; there are several versions of it, not. in the Matsyapurāņa and the Skandapurāņa.

vārāha [*varāha] amnf vārāhī relating to the wild boar, to the avatar varāha — f. vārāhī myth. n.p. of vārāhī, śakti of varāha, a saptamātṛkā | organic. bot. Tacca integrifola, perennial taccaceous plant, with spectacular flower reminiscent of bats, equipped with thick rhizomes, used medicinally.
vārāhapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. of the Vārāhapurāņa, mythological collection of Vaishnava obedience; cf. sāttvika.
vāri var. vār n. water; rain | fluid; fluidity.
vārija [ja] n. lotus ["born in water"].
vāridhi [dhi] m. sea, ocean. vedavāridhih soc. scholar's title "Ocean of knowledge".
vārinātha [nātha] m. myth. np. of vārinātha, epith. of Varuna "Master of the waters".
vārivarga [varga] m. bed. section of the Svargādikānda, dealing with water.
