vārita [pp. ca. vṛ₁] amnf vāritā set aside, avoided, restrained; forbidden | covered, hidden.
vāritavāma [vāma₁] amnf vāritavāmā who revels in the forbidden.

vāruņa [*Varuņa] amnf vāruņī relating to Varuna; aquatic; western | wet, cool; syn. saumya — m. aquatic animal | myth. np. of Vāruņa "son of Varuņa", patron of Bhṛgu | pl. myth. the vāruņās "children of Varuņa", warrior race | var. vāruņi myth. np. of Vāruņi "descended from Varuna", patron of Bhrgu, Agastya, Vasistha — f. vāruņī myth. np. of Vāruņī, śakti of Varuņa, a yogini; wife (or daughter) of Varuṇa, she personifies the wine produced during the churning of the sea of milk | kṣīrodamathana | and she "rolls her eyes in intoxication"; cf. Surādevī | astr. 13th day of the dark fortnight of the month caitra | soc. alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation of hogweed macerated in palm juice.
vārunāstra | astra | n. myth. magical weapon of Varuna.
vāruņya [*Varuņaya] amnf vāruņyā re related to Varuna.

vārkarin m. soc. np. of the bhakti Vārkarī movement of the Mahārāṣṭra of devotees of Paṇḍharpur, founded by Jñānadeva in the 13th century; the sect is open to all; a vārkarin must make the pilgrimage to Paṇdharpur twice a year, to the ekādaśī of āṣādha and to that of kārttika ; he wears the tulasīmālā rosary; cf. Nāmadeva.
vārṇika [*varṇaika] m. writer; scribe.
vārtā cf. vārttā.
vārtika cf. vārttika.
vārtta [*vṛttia] amnf vārttā who has resources, who has a trade; in good health — act. n. health, state — f. cf. vārttā. kā vārttā what's happening? what's new?

vārttā [f. vārtta] f. profession, occupation; not. commerce, economy | the science of economics (what is happening) information, news, rumors (about (g. iic.)) | vārtā id. — ifc. living off (iic.); (iic.) by profession; speaking of (iic.).
vārttāka |ka| mf vārttākī bio. bot. Solanum walked alongside me, eggplant; syn. vangana — m. its fruit — m. vārtāka id. | var. vārtāku id. —n. its fruit.

vārttika [*vṛttika] amnf vārttikā who practices a profession; professional | informant, messenger, spy — ifc. who practices the trade of, who lives off (iic.); who thinks only of (iic.) — n. explanation; elaboration | gram. explanatory annex to a sūtra, critical remark; not. aphorism forming a supplementary commentary on the Aṣṭādhyāyī of Pānini by Kātyāyana.
vārttikakāra [kāra] m. gram. author of rule commentary [vārttika]; not. epith. of Kātyāyana.
vārttikasūtra [sūtra] n. gram. aphorism of Kātyāyana commenting on the Aṣṭādhyāyī.
vārttikasūtriká [ika] m. (grammarian) who studies the aphorisms of Kātyāyana.
vārddhakya [*vrddhakaya] n. old age; senility.
vārdhra [*vardhra] amnf vārdhrā [“which is used to make straps”] leather — f. cf. vārdhrī.
vārdhrī [f. vārdhra] f. leather; leather strap.
vārdhrīṇasa [nasa] m. organic. ["leather nose"] rhi noceros | var. vārdhrīnasa id.
vārṣá [*varṣa] amnf vārṣā concerning the monsoon | annual.
vārsaganya [gaṇya] m. hist. np. of the sage Vārṣagaṇya, ancient philosopher, precursor of the sāṃkhya system cited in the Vyāsabhāsya.
vārṣika [*varṣaika] amnf vārṣikī older; rain-related | annual — ifc. aged (iic.) years.
vārṣṇeya [*vṛṣṇiīya] amnf vārṣṇeyā myth. descendant of vṛṣṇi.

vāla [agt. val] m. hair, mane; not. of the tail of a horse or a yak. vālakhilya var. bālakhilya [khilya] m. pl. vālakhilyās lit. collection of 11 apocryphal stanzas from the Rigveda | myth. [VP.] name of a class of sages [rsi] of very small stature, sons of Kratu and Santati; or descended from the hair of Prajāpati who did penance to obtain the creation of living beings; there are 60000 vālakhilyās, who surround the chariot of the Sun.
vālavyajana [vyajana] n. yak tail fly swatters; syn. cāmara. বালক vālaka [vālaka] m. animal tail (horse, yak, elephant) — n. horsehair ring.

Vālin var. Bālin [Vālain] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of Vālī or Bālī "hairy tail", monkey-king son of Indra; he humiliated Ravana, who had attacked him, by carrying him around the world on his belt, before making him his ally; he killed the asura Dun dubhi; he fought his younger brother Sugrīva, whose wife Rūmā he took; he was killed by an arrow shot in his back by surprise by Rama, who installed Sugrīva on his throne; cf. Tarā₂. rāmeņa bāņena Vālī hataḥ (grammatical example exhibiting agent/instrument ambiguity) Rama killed Vālī with an arrow.
vāluka amnf vālukā sandy — f. vālukā (in gen. pl.) sand, gravel — f. vālukī sandbank.

vālmīki [*valmīka] m. myth. np. of the sage | rṣi | vālmīki "(Penitent) of the anthill", born Ratnākara₁; renouncing a life of brigandage, he meditated so long on the word 'death' |māra| that his body was covered with ants; he is said to be the son of Garuda; the composition of the Rāmāyaṇa is attributed to him, and for this purpose the invention of the epic śloka meter; cf. Adikavi, Kuśīlava.
vālmīkīya |īya| amnf vālmīkīyā concerning vālmīki; composed by vālmīki.
vāvad [intens. vad] intens. (vāvadīti) to speak loudly; to chatter, to talk too much.
vāvadūka [vāvadūka] amnf vāvadūkā talkative; eloquent.
vāvāta | red. van | amnf vāvātā dear, beloved; favorite — f. vāvātā soc. favorite royal wife.
√ vās [related to vasā] v. [4] pr. r. (vāsyate) pp. (vāśita) to bellow, to bellow; to howl, to shout; to moan || fr. cow.
vāṣpa [bāṣpa] m. tear, tears — v. [11] pr. r. (vāspāyate) to cry.
vās₁ [ca. vas₁] v. [10] pr. (vāsayati) pp. (vāsita) pfp. (vāsya₁) to lodge, to house, to shelter.
vās₂ [ca. vas₁] v. [10] pr. (vāsayati) pp. (vāsita) pfp. (vāsya₁) to clothe, dress; to wrap with acc. .
√ vās₃ v. [10] pr. (vāsayati) pr. r. (vāsayate) pp. (vāsita) to perfume, incense.
vāsa₂ [act. vas₁] m. stay, dwelling; stop, stage | (in fig.) situation, condition.
vāsa₂ [agt. vas₁] m. clothing.
vasa₂ | agt. vās₃ | mr. perfume, pleasant smell | print, Illusion | myth. n.p. from asura vāsa₂ “Illusion”; cf. Kirti.
vāsamat |mat| amnf vāsamatī scented | hi. bāsmatī.
vāsayoga | yoga | m. perfumed powder; not. red powder used at the Holī festival.
vāsaka₁ [agt. vās₃] amnf vāsakā f. vāsikā that perfumes — m. perfume — n. mus. recurring melody, refrain; cf. dhruvā.
vāsaka₂ |agt. vas₁| ifc. m. habit, clothing of (iic.).
vāsana₁ [act. vās₃] n. act of perfuming — f. cf. vāsanā.
vāsana₂ [act. vas₁] n. garment, clothing, cover | envelope, box, cassette.
vāsana₃ |act. vas₁| n. habitation, residence.

vāsanā [f. vāsana₁] f. memory; desire, inclination, tendency; Illusion | phil. impregnation; residual trace; impression of a previous sensation, subconscious memory; emotion, association of feelings with the reading or hearing of a work | math. proof, demonstration; syn. upapatti.
vāsanākṣaya [kṣaya₂] m. phil. [Tantra] the destruction of impressions or impulses, goal of the kaula ritual.
vāsanta [*vasanta] amnf vāsantī prin tanier | ["in the spring of life"] young — m. young man; young animal — f. vāsantī soc. fes spring tival | bio. bot. Gaertnera racemosa, jasmine.
vāsantaka [*vasantaka] amnf vāsantikā relating to spring; spring-like.

vāsantika [*vasantaika] amnf vāsantikā relating to spring; spring-like — m. soc. spring festival — f. vāsantikā bio. bot. Hiptage benghalensis, climbing shrub with fragrant white flowers; syn. mādhavī. madhuśca mādhavaśca vāsantikāvṛtuḥ The spring season includes the months of madhu and mādhava.
vāsantikaspapna [svapna] n. lit. np. from vāsantikaspapna "A Midsummer Night's Dream", translation of Shakespeare's play "Midsummer Night", by R. Krishnamacharya (1892).
vāsará [vas₁] amnf vāsarī early morning, clear — mn day (opp. night); day of the week | time, turn, succession.
vāsareśa |īśa| m. astr. regent of a day of the week: sūrya (Sunday), soma (Monday), mangala (Tuesday), budha (Wednesday), guru (Thursday), śukra (Friday) and śani (Saturday).
vāsava [*vasua] amnf vāsavī myth. relating to vasavas; relating to Indra — m. myth. n.p. from vāsava, epith. of Indra "Chief of the vasavas".

vāsavadatta [datta] m. np. vāsavadatta "given by Indra" — f. Vāsavadattā₁ lit. np. from the romance Vāsavadattā₁ by Subandhu | lit. its eponymous heroine, Princess Vāsavadattā₁ "Gift of the Gods", daughter of King Sringārasekhara; after opposing her parents who wished to arrange her marriage by svayamvara, she met in a dream the charming Prince Kandarpaketu₁; he himself had met her in a dream, and with the help of a parrot he found her and abducted her; they hid in the Vindhya mountains, where a tribal battle separated them; in her flight she disturbed an irascible sage, who turned her to stone; Despairing of finding her again, Kandarpaketu₁ threw himself into the ocean, but a voice from heaven told him that they would be reunited; when he found the stone, touching it brought Vāsavadattā₁ back to life, and they lived happily in their mutual love | lit. [KSS.] np. of Princess Vāsavadattā₁, daughter of King Caṇḍamahāsena and Queen Angāravatī; her father abducted King Udayana from the Vatsa country to serve as his daughter's music teacher; he escaped with the beautiful princess and married her; Bhāsa dramatized their love in the Svap navāsavadatta.
vāsavi [vāsavai] m. myth. [Mah.] np. from vāsavi, patr. of Arjuna "son of Indra" | myth. [Rām.] patr. of Valī.
vāsas [abstr. vās₂] n. garment (for the lower body); costume; fabric, cloth | du. vāsasī two pieces of fabric forming a complete garment.
vāsita [pp. vās₃] amnf vāsitā fragrant; spicy | affected by, under the influence of (i. ifc.).
vāsin₁ [agt. vas₁] amnf vāsinī inhabitant.
vāsin₂ [agt. vas₁] ifc. amnf vāsinī dressed in (iic.).
Vāsiṣka m. hist. np. of King Kuṣāṇa Vāsiṣka₁; he reigned around 150 | hist. np. of King Vāsiska₂; he reigned around 230.
vāsiṣṭha [*Vasiṣṭha] amnf vāsiṣṭhā derived from, related to, descendant of, composed by Vasistha.
Vāsiṣṭhadharmasūtra [dharmasūtra] n. bed. n.p. of the Vāsisthadharmasūtra, a text of laws attributed to Vasistha.
Vāsu [vās₁u] m. myth. np. of Vāsu, epith. of Vișnu "the Immanent" ["who remains in all things"|.

vāsuki m. myth. np. of vāsuki, dragon king | nāga | used as a rope encircling Mount Man dara, resting on the tortoise Akūpāra, to churn the sea of milk | kṣīrodamathana | in order to extract amrta at the dawn of the world; he is brother of Ananta Śesa.
vāsukeya [vāsukiīya] m. myth. vasuki.
vāsukeyasvasṛ [svasṛ] f. myth. epith. of Manasā "Sister of vāsuki".

Vāsudeva [*vasudeva] amnf vāsudevā myth. relating to Kṛṣṇa — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Vāsudeva, patr. of Kṛṣṇa, son of vasudeva; but also "(God) in whom all resides", i.e. Nārāyaṇa; phil. |pañcarātra| He is the first emanation [vyūha] of Viṣṇu; in the spiritual heaven he is the direction of the East | jn. eminent person [śalākāpuruṣa] of an epic, in the role of the hero; not. Kṛṣṇa, opposite his sworn enemy | prativāsudeva | Jarāsandha, and Laksmana, opposed to Rāvana | myth. np. of the impostor Srīgālava Vāsudeva₁, king of Karavīrapura; he was killed by Kṛṣṇa | hist. np. of King Vāsudeva₂ who created the Kanva dynasty in Magadha by overthrowing the last of the śungās around 71 ante. | hist. np. of Vāsudeva₃ Sārvabhauma, Bengali logician of the late 15th century; he studied logic at Mithilā, where he memorized the Tattvacintāmani; breaking the monopoly of Mithilā, he established himself as a logician at Navadvīpa, where he converted to the teachings of Caitanya in 1510; He is credited with the Sārvabhaumanirukta; it is said that Raghunātha₁ Siromaṇi was his student before his departure for Mithilā | hist. np. of Vāsudeva₄ Dīkṣita, author of the Bālamanoramā (18th century). om namo bhagavate vāsudevāya [vaiṣṇava] Om, I worship God in the son of Vasudeva.
vāsudevaka [ka] m. myth. KṛṣṇaVāsudeva | soc. devotee of Kṛṣṇa.
vāsudevāśrama [āśrama] m. hist. n.p. by vāsudevāśrama, author of the Yatidharmaprakāśā.
Vāsupūjya [*Vasupūjya] m. jn. patr. of Vāsupūjya, son of King Vasupūjya, 12th mythical tīrthankara; his body is red, his symbol is a buffalo.
vāstava [*vastu₁a] amnf vāstavī real, substantial; true, authentic; characteristic, representative | fixed, determined; established, proven — n. rendezvous. vāstave truly, assuredly; syn. vastutas.
vāstavatva [tva] n. reality; substantiality.
vāstavika [ika] amnf vāstavikā real, substantial; syn. vāstava — m. realistic.
vāstavya [*vastu₁ya] amnf vāstavyā left as a remnant | myth. said of Rudra, to whom the remains of the sacrifice are left | resident, inhabitant.
vāstu [vās₁tu] n. place, location; site; land; estate, house, home; hall | [vāstuśāstra] architecture — m. myth. syn. vasu.
vāstuka [ka] amnf vāstukā soc. (remains) of the sacrifice — m. bio. bot. Chenopodium album, white goosefoot, used in medicine.
vāstuja | ja | amnf domestic vāstujā.

vāstupurusa [purusa] m. arch. personification of the ideal plan of a building; it symbolizes the feeling of integrity of the peaceful space in which the building is situated; its plan integrates the gods; Brahmā occupies the central square; 4 principal gods occupy a central cross: Pṛthvīdhāra in the East, Savitā in the South, Vivasvān in the West and Mitra in the North; around a square supports 32 minor deities; the diagram is completed by the guardians of the directions |dikpāla|: Sūrya, Agni, Yama, Nirṛti₁, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kubera and Isāna.
vāstupuruṣamaṇḍala [maṇḍala] cf. mn vāstumaņdala. vāstumaņdala | maṇḍala | mn architectural ritual plan, not. of temple.
vāstuvidyā [vidyā] f. architecture, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.
vāstuśamana [śamana] n. soc. rite of "appeasing the ground", ritual preparation of the ground for a construction.
vāstuśāstra [śāstra] n. architecture; there is a Northern school, which claims its origins from Viśvakarmā, and a Southern school, which claims its origins from Maya; cf. Mayamata.

Vāstusūtropanisad [sūtraupanisad] f. bed. n.p. of the vāstusūtropaniṣad, late text (18th century) of Silpaśāstra in 6 chapters, treating not. of the making of sacred images; it was attributed to Pippalāda.
vāstos [g. vāstu] ind. of the hearth || lat. vesta.
vāstospati | pat | mr. ved. god lare.
vāsya₁ [pfp. [1] vas₁] amnf vāsyā to host.
vāsya₁ [pfp. [1] vas₁] amnf vāsyā to clothe, to cover, to wrap | wrapped; covered, carried.
vāh [ca. vah₁] v. [10] pr. (vāhayati) to drive, to direct, to use a vehicle | to carry — ps. (vāhyate) to carry, to transport (2 acc.) to guide (horse); to drive (chariot).
vāha [agt. vah₁] amn ifc. that which carries, that which transports, that which leads, that which flows (iic.) — m. wind mount, vehicle; beast of burden, not. horse.
vāhaka [agt. vah₁] amnf vāhikā who transports, who brings.

vāhana [agt. vah₁] amnf vāhanī that pulls, that transports, that brings — act. n. driving | vehicle | mount | myth. animal associated with a god as his follower; cf. Garuda, Nandī, Paravāni, Makara, Hamsa — ifc. that transports (11th century); trans port of (11th century). vāhanīkṛ to make a vehicle of. vāhanībhū to become a vehicle.

vāhanāyudhavartana [āyudhavartana] n. lit. np. from the vāhanāyudhavartana "Use of mounts and weapons", 9th chapter of the Pratisthālakṣaṇasārasamuccaya, which deals with the identification of deities by their attributes.
vāhanika [*vāhanaika] amnf vāhanikī who subsists by trading in draft animals; horse dealer.
vāhika [vāhaika] m. vehicle; transporter.
vāhin [agt. ca. vah₁] amnf vāhinī who transports, who leads — f. vāhinī army; not. ba taillon of 3 companies [gaṇa], comprising 81 (3⁴) elephants and chariots, 243 horsemen and 405 infantrymen.
vāhīka m. geo. cf. Bāhlīkās.
vāhya [related to bāhya] amnf vāhyā external, situated outside of (abl. loc.); opp. ābhyantara external, foreign to, contrary to excluded, excom munited, horscaste — m. foreigner.
vāhli m. geo. country of Bactria; cf. bāhli
vāhlika [ka] amnf vāhlikī geo. balkhi, habi tant or prince of Bactria | var. vāhlīka id.
vāhlija [ja] amnf vāhlijā born in Bactria | from Bactria; not. breed of renowned horses. ājighrati praņatamūrdhani vāhlije'sve lit. [ZPV.] While a Balkhi horse lowered its head to sniff the ground.
vi pf. (privative, dispersion) far from, outside of, deprived of, separated from, distinct from; in opposition
vi₁ m. bird | to be swift (not. horse, arrow, wind) | lat. avis; fr. aviaire.
with | (pej.) badly | (intensive) varied; intensified; very.
viṃśá [contr. viṃśati] amnf viṃśī twentieth | in 20 parts.

viṃśaka [viṃśaka] amnf viṃśikā in 20 parts | accompanied or augmented by 20 entities — n. period of 20 days | (with śata ) 20 percent — f. viṃśikā lit. collection of 20 verses | bd. not. np. of the Vimśikā of Vasubandhu.
viṃśakakārikāprakaraṇa | kārikāprakaraṇa | n. lit. np. of the Vimśakakārikāprakaraņa "Treatise explaining 20 stanzas" by Vasubandhu, also known as Vimśikā; it explains the vijñānavāda doctrine.

viṃśatí [contr. dvidaśat] num. f. sg. the number twenty; about twenty — iic. var. vimśat id. | lat. viginti; fr. twenty. vimsatítama var. vimsa, vimsatī [tama] amnf vimśatitamī ord. twentieth. vimsatísata sata num. n. 120.
viṃśatísāhasra [sāhasra] amnf viṃśatisāhasrā f. vimśatisāhasrī 20000.
víkankata [vikankata] m. bio. bot. Flacour tia jangomas, small tree with round purple fruits; its wood is used to make sacrificial instruments; cf. sruvavrksa.
víkaca₁ [vikaca] amnf vikacā bald.
vikaca₂ amnf vikacā open, blooming (flower) | spread out; scattered | manifest; shining brightly — v. [11] pr. (vikacayati) pp. (vikacita) to bloom. vikacīkṛ to bloom.
víkaṭa [vikaṭa] amnf vikaṭā f. vikaṭī immense, huge, enormous | extraordinary, monstrous; Hideous, horrible — m. myth. np. of Vikața, epith. of Ganeśa "Enormous". vikatīkr to enlarge; to extend.
vikaṭakavi | kavi | m. bad poet (palindrome of syllables).
vikaṭanitamba | nitamba | amnf vikaṭanitambā who has a big behind.

Vikaṭavadana [vadana] m. lit. [KSS.] np of Vikatavadana "with the horrible face", gaṇa of Am bikā; he coveted the daughter Cāpalekhā of the hermit Kapilajața, and was cursed by him to be reborn on Earth as Jīvadatta.
vikatavarman [varman] m. bed. [DKC.] np of Vikațavarmā “Hideous”; he usurped the throne of Vi deha in the absence of king Prahāravarmā; he was killed by Upahāravarmā.
vikatth [vikatth] v. [1] pr. r. (vikatthate) pp. (vikatthita) abs. (vikatthya) to boast (of (i.)); to boast — ca. (vikatthayati) to make fun of, to humiliate.
vikatthā [act. vikatth] f. boasting.
vikamp [vikamp] v. [1] pr. r. (vikampate) pp. (vikampita) to tremble violently | to be frightened; to hesitate.
vikampa [agt. vikamp] amnf vikampā trembling, panting; unsteady, hesitant; frightened.
vikampana [act. vikamp] n. trembling; movement (Sun).
vikampita [pp. vikamp] amnf vikam pitā trembling, agitated; unstable.
vikampin [agt. vikamp] amnf vikam pinī trembling, agitated.
víkaraṇa₁ [vikaraṇa₁] amnf vikaraṇā deprived of sensations — n. phil. abandonment of acts; deprivation of sensations.

vikarana₂ [agt. vikr] m. gram. ["that which triggers a transformation"] modifier marker, used as a suffix to a root to form a conjugation stem; not. śap₂, luk, ślu, śyan, śnu, śa, śnam, u, śnā for the present stems of gana verbs 1 to 9; nic for the present stems of gana verbs 10 and causatives; also yak for the passive stem [karman], cli for the ao
riste [him], tāsi for the future [lṛt], sya₁ for the future
periphrastic | lut|, sip for the subjunctive | let|, san₂ for the desiderative, and yan for the intensive.
Vikarāla [vikarāla] amnf Vikarālā hor rible; frightening, dreadful — f. Vikarālā myth. epith. of Durgā or Kālī | lit. [Kuṭṭanīmata] np. of Vikarālā, old decrepit prostitute.
víkarālatā [tā] f. state of being dreadful.
vikarṇa [vikarṇa] amnf vikarṇī without ears | with long ears — m. myth. [Mah.| np. of Vikarņa, one of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; he defends Draupadī.
vikartana [agt. vikṛt] amnf vikartanā that separates, that tears apart — m. the Sun (that separates the clouds).
vikarman [vikarman] n. bad action.

vikala [vikalā] amnf vikalā mutilated, infirm; lacking, deficient in (i. iic.) | confused, agitated; depressed; in pain — f. vikalī soc. woman at the beginning of her period. dvyangavikalah mutilated in both legs.
vikalita [vikalita] n. math. subtraction.
vikalp [ca. viklp] v. [10] pr. (vikalpayati) to pose a dilemma; to present a choice | to conjecture.

vikalpa [act. viklp] m. option, alternative, choice; distinction, discrimination; dilemma, hesitation, indecision, doubt; imagination, illusion, mental image; mental state | phil. abstention from action; opp. samkalpa | phil. [Yoga] conceptualization, a cittavṛtti | phil. [Nyāya] logical analysis of a concept, classification | phil. [Mīmāmsā] set of alternative instructions, to be executed at will; opp. samuccaya | math. combinatorics | gram. alternative of a grammatical rule, option | lit. rhet. antithesis. vikalpena adv. optionally.
vikalpavāsanā [vāsanā] f. phil. [Dinnāga] constructive force of reason.
vikalpaka [agt. viklp] m. distributor; dispatcher | composer; transformer.
vikalpana [agt. viklp] m. arranger; composer — act. n. alternative, option; distinction | diversity of opinion; confusion; imagination; indecision.
vikalpita [pp. ca. viklp] amnf vikalpitā prepared, arranged | imagined | doubtful; optional.
vikalpitatva [vat] n. optionality.
vikas [vikas] v. [1] pr. (vikasati) pp. (vi kasita) to open, to bloom; to flourish | to rejoice | to spread, to grow, to increase — ca. (vikāsayati) to cause to bloom; to make grow.
vikasita [pp. vikas] amnf vikasitā fulfilled.
vikār [ca. vikṛ] v. [10] pr. (vikārayati) to change (not. mood).

vikāra [act. vikr] m. formation; transformation, change; deformation, alteration, perversion | culinary preparation | play of physiognomy, grimace | bodily disorder, illness; injury | emotion; anguish; agitation, passion | gram. application of sandhi to pass from the isolated form [padapāṭha] to the continuous form [saṃhitāpāṭha] phil. [Sāṃkhya] element [tattva] product of prakṛti; 7 are themselves producers: buddhi, ahaṃkāra, and the 5 subtle elements |tanmātra|; the other 16 are only productions: the 5 gross elements [bhūta], and the 11 organs, including the 10 faculties of perception and action [indriya] and the mind [manas] | gram. Morphological derivative of a word. vikāro yauvanam youth is quick to passion. vikārasya gamanīyāsmi saṃvṛttā I feel the awakening of an emotion.
víkāraṇa [vikāraṇa] amnf vikāraṇā without cause.
vikārin [agt. vikr] amnf vikārinī subject to change; fickle, unfaithful — m. astr. n.p. of Vikārī "inconstant", personification of the year 33 of a life cycle [samvatsara].
vikārya [pfp. [1] vikār] amnf vikāryā to transform; intended to change, variable | gram. qualifies an object [karman] transformed.
vikāś [vikāś] v. [1] pr. r. (vikāśate) pp. (vikāśita) to appear, to become visible | to shine, to splendify — ca. (vikāśayati) to make appear; to make bright.
víkāśa₁ [vikāśa] m. absence of demonstration; solitude.
vikāsa₂ [agt. vikās] m. brilliance, splendor; ma nifestation.
vikāśin [agt. vikāś] amnf vikāśinī ra gods, bright; that illuminates, that explains (iic.) — f. vikāśinī myth. np. of vikāśinī "Radiant", one of Skanda's nurses [mātr].

vikāsa [act. vikas] m. blossoming, unfolding; flowering | phil. [Trika] descending phase of spiritual realization where the disciple reintegrates the phenomenal world, and transgresses prohibitions to attain supreme consciousness [Anuttara]; it succeeds the phase of retraction [samkoca].
vikāsita [pp. ca. vikas] amnf vikāsitā épanoui.
vikāsin [agt. vikas] amnf vikāsinī blooming, flowering; developed, extended.

vikira [act. vikr] m. dispersion | soc. portion of rice scattered to ward off beings hostile to the offering | dripping water; water filtered drop by drop; not. water obtained by digging a hole in the sandy bank of a river.

vikukşi [vikukşi] m. myth. np. of Vikukşi "Glutton", eldest son of Ikṣvāku, founder of the Ayodhyā dynasty of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa]; when his father Ikṣvāku wanted to celebrate the mahāpralaya śrāddha, he went into the forest to hunt the sacrificial beasts; on the return, hungry, he took a hare from the game to eat; the purohita Vasistha refused to perform the ritual sprinkling [prokṣaṇa] on a remnant, unworthy of a sacrifice; Ikṣvāku banished Vikukşi, who under the name of Saśāda lived as a hermit; upon the death of his father he returned to Ayodhyā to reign; his son is Kakutstha, or [Rām.] Bāṇa₁.
vikuṇṭh [vikuṇṭh] [unused without pf.].

vikuṇṭha [vikuṇṭha] amnf vikuṇṭhā sharp; penetrating, irresistible — m. myth. np. of Vikuntha, epith. of Vișnu "the Immanent" ["who pervades all"] — f. vikuṇṭhā myth. np. of Vikunțhā, wife of Subhra and mother of Vaikunțha.
víkuṇṭhita [vivikuṇṭhita] amnf vikunthitā blunt; obtuse.

vikṛ [vikṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (vikaroti) pp. (Vikṛta) to change, alter, deform | ruin; to act treacherously, to be unfaithful to (g. loc.) — pr. r. (vikurute) to become deformed, to undergo a change — ps. (vikriyate) to change mood, to experience sudden joy or fear; to change form — ca. (vikārayati) to transform; to cause to change (not. mood).
vikṛt [vikṛt₁] v. [6] pr. (vikṛntati) to cut, slice, chop, tear.

Vikrita [pp. vikr] amnf Vikrita changed, transformed; adorned; deformed, altered; disfigured, mutilated | strange, ugly; incongruous; deformed; sick | unfulfilled, incomplete, aborted | decorated, embellished; adorned with, inlaid with (iic.) — m. soc. tortures, mutilation astr. np. of Vikrita "transformed", son of Naradi personifying the 24th year of a life cycle [saṃvatsara] — n. alteration; disgust, aversion | soc. silence of embarrassment | abortion, monster — f. Vikrita myth. np. of the yogi Vikrita || pkt. vikata. vikrtavadhah m. soc. capital execution with mutilation. Vikṛtā vāk f. incongruous or foul language.

víkṛti [act. vikṛ] f. change, evolution, transformation; modification, distortion; degradation, decline; incongruity | change of mood, emotion; disturbance | alienation; hostility; defection | specter, phantom | gram.

derived | lit. dialect | lit. variations in the recitation of a Vedic verse, using redundancy to avoid errors; there are 8 of them [aṣṭavikṛti] | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the degradation by transformation of the phenomenal world (opp. prakṛti the Original Nature) | phil. [Mīmāṃsā] injunction adapted to the context, modified rite; opp. prakrti. maranamprakṛtih vikṛtirjīvitamucyate Death is said to be natural, and life accidental. prakṛtivad vikṛtiḥ kartavyaḥ [Mīmāṃsā] The injunction must be made according to the original mantra.
Vikṛtikaumudī [kaumudī] f. bed. n.p. of the Vikṛtikaumudī, commentary on the Vikṛtivallī by Gangādharabhattācārya.

vikṛtipāṭha [pāṭha] m. phon. particular recitation of the Veda, for mnemonic use, where the order of the words | krama | is not preserved; cf. jaṭā, mālā, śikhā, rekhā, dhvaja, daņda, ratha, ghana; opp. prakṛtipāṭha.
vikrtivallī [vallī] f. lit. np. of the Vikrtivallī, listing 28 stanzas [kārikā] attributed to Vyāḍi, giving the 8 modes of Vedic recitation |vikṛti|.

vikṛṣ [vikṛṣ] v. [1] pr. (vikarṣati) pp. (vikṛṣṭa) to stretch (not. the bow); to draw, to drag. বিকু vikṛ [vikṛ] v. [6] pr. (vikirati) pp. (vikīrṇa) to throw, to cast; to spread, to scatter, to scatter; to strew, to cover with (i.).
viklp [viklp] v. [1] pr. r. (vikalpate) pp. (vikļpta) to be undecided, to hesitate; to be doubtful or fa optional — ca. (vikalpayati) to pose a dilemma; to present a choice | to conjecture.
Vikka M., young elephant.
vikram [vikram] v. [1] pr. (vikrāmati) pp. (vikrānta) to walk, advance, stride over | to rise to (acc.) | to show courage; to attack, fight, subdue.

vikramá [act. vikram] m. walk, gait; step, stride | gait (not. majestic); valor, courage, heroism; prowess; power | military campaign | myth. np. of Vikrama "Hero", epithet of King Purūravā; he personifies year 14 of a life cycle [saṃvatsara] | cf. vikramāditya | hist. np. of the era [saṃvat] Vikrama, beginning in 57 ante. astr. calendar used in North India; the festival of Dīpāvali marks its last day. vikramāt by force, through force.

vikramácarita [carita] n. lit. np. from the Vikra macarita, a collection of 32 marvelous tales in praise of Vikramāditya, told by the magical statues of his throne to King Bho jadeva; they celebrate his legendary magna nimité; four versions are known; syn. Siṃhāsanadvātriṃśikā, Dvātriṃśatputtalikā.
vikramácālukya [cālukya] m. hist. [saṃvat] Vikramacālukya dynasty of the Deccan, founded in 1075 by Vikramāditya₆.

vikramátunga [tunga] n. lit. [KSS.] np. of King Vi kramatunga of Pātaliputra; he met a brahman making an offering of bilva fruits in the hope that Agni would turn them into gold; the king promised Agni his head, and obtained from him the golden fruits, and for the brahman great riches; a young brahman had obtained from his master a magic powder that turned copper into gold; he informed the king of it, but did not succeed in the magic, an invisible yakṣa stealing the powder; the king, who saw the yakṣa, succeeded and obtained the riches.
vikramápattana | patana | n. geo. n.p. of the city of Vikramapațțana "capital of Vikramāditya₁", epith. of Ujjayini.
vikramápura | pura | n. geo. np. of Vikramapura "city of Vikramāditya₁"; cf. Vikramapaṭṭana — f. vikramapurī id.

Vikramasīla [śīla] m. geo. np. of the monastery bd. of Vikramasīla (mod. Antichak, 50 km east of Bha galpur, Bihāra); King Dharmapāla₁ founded a University there at the end of the 8th century, in reaction to a presumed decline of Nālandā; about a hundred professors taught a thousand students there; the site was destroyed in 1198 by the Muslim army of Bakhtiar Khiliji fighting the Sena dynasty.

Vikramasimhapurī [simhapurī] f. geo. np. of the city of Vikramasimhapurī, on the coast of Andhra; it has existed since the time of the Maurya empire; it was part of the kingdom of the Pallavās from the 4th to the 6th century; mod. Nellore.
vikramasena [senā] m. bed. [KSS] np. of King Vikra masena of Ujjayinī; he is father of Tejasvatī.
Vikramānkadeva [ankadeva] m. hist. n.p. of King Cālukya Vikramānkadeva; cf. Vikramāditya₁.

Vikramānkadevacarita [carita] n. lit. np. of the Vikramānkadevacarita "Exploits of King Vi kramānkadeva", panegyric of the Cālukya dynasty of Kalyāṇa₁, composed for King Vikramāditya₁ by the court poet Bilhaṇa.

Vikramāditya₁ [āditya] m. hist. np. of King Vikramāditya₁ "Sun of Heroism", epith. of Candragupta₂ (380–415), who defeated the Sakās; he conquered the satrapy of AvantiUjjayinī, which he made his capital Puramdarapurī; the poet Bhartrhari₁ was his brother; he encouraged the arts, and tradition says that nine treasuries of learning | navaratna | lived at his court; his golden legend is recounted in the Vikramacarita and the Kathāsaritsāgara added other fantastic tales about him; tradition wrongly attributes to him the founding of the Vikrama era. of King Cālukya Vikramāditya₁, son of Pulakeśī₂ and a daughter of Durvinīta; he reigned at Vātāpi₁ (mod. Badāmi) from 655 to 681; he established the chronicles of the dynasty in 658; he captured Kāncīpura in 671 | hist. np. of King Cālukya Vikramāditya₁; he reigned at Vātāpi₁ from 733 to 746 | hist. np. of King Cālukya Vikramāditya₁; he reigned at Kalyāṇī in the 11th century; He intrigued against his elder brother Someśvara₂, dethroned him in 1076, and then founded the Vikramacālukya era [saṃvat]; he controlled a vast empire from Kāverī to Narmadā; he patronized the arts and letters; cf. Bilhana; after his death in 1126 the Cālukya empire disintegrated.

Vikramorvaśī [Urvaśī] f. lit. np. from the Vikramorvaśī, a drama by Kālidāsa recounting the love of Purūravā and Urvaśī "conquered by his worth"; believing that she is leaving him out of jealousy, he is mad with grief at the separation from the beloved [vipralambhaśṛṅgāra].
vikramorvaśīya [ya] n. bed. n.p. from the drama Vikra morvaśīya; cf. Vikramorvaśī.
vikramaṇa [act. vikram] n. stride, step; not. cosmic stride of Vișnu | heroism, bravery; power | [pāśupata] supernatural power soc. recitation step by step according to the rules of the kra mapātha.
vikrayá [act. vikrī] m. sale.
vikrayaka [agt. vikrī] amnf vikrayikā seller — m. vikrayika id.
vikrayapattra [pattra] n. Invoice.
vikrayaśālā [śālā] f. shop, trade.

vikrayin [agt. vikrī] ifc. amnf vikrayinī who has sold (iic.) | who traffics in (iic.) (not. māmsa, soma). somavikrayī who has sold soma (blameworthy). rasavikrayī who traffics in alcohol. māṃsavikrayī who has sold meat. vedavikrayiņaścaiva vedānām caiva dūsakāh vedānām lekhakaścaiva te vai nirayagāminah [Mah.] Those who sell the Veda, like those who defile the Veda, like those who write the Veda, all in truth will go to Hell.
vikrayya [pfp. [1] vikrī] amnf vikrayyā for sale.

víkrānta [pp. vikram] amnf vikrāntā who takes long strides | gram. exceeded (said of a sandhi preserving the visarga) | valiant, brave, powerful — n. gait, bearing; valor, boldness | lit. [alamkāra] variety of yamaka where the repetition occurs at the end of each hemistich of a stanza. tasminnavasare tena dhīram vikrāmtam he behaved bravely on this occasion.

vikriyā [act. vikr] f. transformation, change, modification; alteration of the natural state | deterioration; deformity | indisposition, affection; illness | disturbance; perplexity | hostility; rebellion, defection, alienation | injury, damage; misfortune. vikriyām yā to suffer a setback; to be injured; to fail. vikriyā na khalu kāladosajā nirmalaprakrtisu sthi
rodayā [KuS.] In those whose nature is pure, alteration due to an occasional fault certainly never has a lasting consequence.
vikrī [vikrī₁] v. [9] pr. (vikrīṇāti) pr. r. (vikrīnīté) pp. (vikrīta) pfp. (vikrayya, vikretavya, vikreya) sell (at the price of (i.)); barter for i. . vikretum for sale.
vikrīḍ [vikrīḍ] v. [1] pr. (vikrīḍati) pp. (vikrīdita) to play, to have fun; to play with (saha₂).
vikrīḍa [obj. vikrīḍ] m. playground; toy.
vikrīḍita [pp. vikrīḍ] amnf vikrīḍitā toy; used as a game — n. game; sport | easy task ("like child's play").
vikrita [pp. vikrī] amnf vikrītā sold — n. sale.
vikruś [vikruś] v. [1] pr. (vikrośati) pp. (vikrusta) to cry out, to call for help; to call out to someone. acc. .
vikretavya [pfp. [3] vikrī] amnf vikre tavyā for sale.
vikretṛ [agt. vikrī] amnf vikretrī who sells — m. merchant.
vikreya [pfp. [1] vikrī] amnf vikreyā for sale, sellable — n. selling price.
viklav [viklav] v. [1] pr. r. (viklavate) pp. (viklavita) to become troubled, confused; to be agitated.

viklava [agt. viklav] amnf vik lavā troubled, agitated; confused, perplexed; hesitant, indecisive, uncertain; timid | upset, frightened, in timid; discouraged, faltering | unsteady (in speech, gait); weakened (faculty) — ifc. disgusted with, unwilling to (iic.) — act. n. agitation, disturbance; discouragement. viklavam kr to discourage. viklavam bhū to become troubled, discouraged.
viklavatā [tā] f. trouble, agitation, confusion; timidity; fear, discouragement; indecision.
viklavatva [tā] n. id.
viklitti [act. viklid] f. moistening; softening (of rice in water, of food by cooking, etc.).
viklid [viklid] v. [4] pr. (viklidyati) will soften. odano viklidyati the rice softens.
vikṣar [vikṣar] v. [1] pr. (vikṣarati) pp. (vikṣarita) to flow, to spread; to dissolve, to permeate.

vikṣará [agt. vikṣar] amnf vikṣarā which flows — m. emanation, effluence | myth. np. of Vikṣara₁, epith. of Viṣṇu "permeating the Universe" | myth. np. of the asura Vikṣara₁, son of Danāyu and Kaśyapa.
vikṣita [vikṣita] amnf vikṣitā destroyed, annihilated; miserable.
vikṣip [vikṣip] v. [6] pr. (vikṣipati) pp. (vikṣipta) throw, scatter; eliminate (pain) extend, pull, stretch (not. the bow); drag, pull out of, retain.
vikṣipa [agt. vikṣip] amnf vikṣipī who agitates; who causes trouble; agitator.
vikṣipta [pp. vikṣip] amnf vikṣiptā thrown, scattered; refuted | agitated; distracted — n. dispersion.
vikṣiptacitta [citta] amnf vikṣiptacittā à l'es pris distré.
vikṣubh [vikṣubh] v. [4] pr. r. (vikṣubhyate) pp. (vikṣubdha) to be upset, to be agitated — ca. (vikṣobhayati) pp. (vikṣobhita) to agitate, to disturb; to rout.
viksepa [act. viksip] m. act of scattering, throwing; refutation | act of agitating | inattention; confusion, perplexity.
vikṣobha [act. vikṣubh] m. agitation, feverishness; disturbance, worry; mental disturbance.
vikṣobhita [pp. ca. vikṣubh] amnf vikṣobhitā agitated, worried, troubled.
vikhaṇḍita [vikhaṇḍita] amnf vikhanditā torn to pieces, dismantled; destroyed.
vikhan [vikhan] v. [1] pr. (vikhanati) to dig up.
Vikhānasa [vikhan] amnf vikhānasā that digs up (roots) — m. hist. np. of the er
mite [muni] Vikhānasa, who establishes the rule of the ana
chorites [vaikhānasa].
vikhyā [vikhyā] v. [2] pr. (vikhyāti) pp. (vikhyāta) to look, see, contemplate — ca. (vi khyāpayati) to make known, say, announce, proclaim mer.
vikhyāta [pp. vikhyā] amnf vikhyātā well known; famous, celebrated | known as, called.
vikhyāti [act. vikhyā] f. renown, celebrity.
vikhyāpana [act. ca. vikhyā] n. announcement, proclamation; explanation; exposition | avowal, ad mission; confession.

vigaṇ [vigaṇ] v. [10] pr. (vigaṇayati) pp. (viganita) abs. (viganayya) to count, calculate, deliberate, consider | to consider (acc.) as (acc.); to estimate — ps. (viganyate) to be esteemed, to be held in high regard. aviganayya without giving consideration to.
vigata [pp. vigam] amnf vigatā gone, disappeared; absent — iic. without, from which we removed — ifc. who abstains from (iic.). vigatāsurbabhūva he lost his life.
vigatacetana | cetana | amnf vigatacetanā ab feels, distracted. ānandena vigatacetana iva bhūtvā overcome with joy.
vigatāmbara | ambara | amnf vigatāmbarā without clothes, naked.
vigatāśanka [āśankā] amnf vigatāśankā fearless; confident.
vigam [vigam] v. [1] pr. (vigacchati) pp. (vi gata) to go away, to leave, to disappear; to die; to pass (time).
vigama [act. vigam] m. departure; disappearance; end; absence — ifc. act of avoiding or abstaining from (iic.).
vigarh [vigarh] v. [1] pr. (vigarhati) v. [10] pr. (vigarhayati) pp. (vigarhita) accuse, blame; censor.
vigarhaṇa [agt. vigarh] n. blame, reproach; censure — f. vigarhaṇā id. vigarhaṇāṃ kṛ to reproach.
vigarhaṇīya [pfp. [2] vigarh] amnf vigarhanīyā blameworthy; reprehensible.
vigarhita [pp. vigarh] amnf vigarhitā blamed, prohibited (by (ig loc. iic.), because of (iic.)).
vigal [vigal] v. [1] pr. (vigalati) pp. (vigalita) to fall, to flow away; to vanish, to disappear.
vigalita [pp. vigal] amnf vigalitā fallen, flowed away; dissolved, dried up; vanished, lost; fallen from abl. | undone (knot, hairstyle).
vigā [vigā₂] pp. (vigīta) ps. (gīyate) to be blamed, to be contradicted.
vigāḍha [pp. vigāh] amnf vigāḍhā plunged, immersed, absorbed | where one plunges, where one has penetrated; which one has seized.
vigāh [vigāh] v. [1] pr. r. (vigāhate) pp. (vigādha) to plunge into, bathe, be immersed in (loc. acc.); to penetrate, to be absorbed in.
vigīta [pp. vigā] amnf vigītā incoherent, contradictory | blamed.

viguṇa [viguṇa] amnf viguṇā deficient, imperfect; faulty, ineffective, unfit; of poor quality | without merit; bad; disordered (health); adverse (fate) | without a string (bow). vigunīkr to remove the string from a bow.
vigunatā [tā] f. inaptitude; uselessness; disorder.
vigṛhya [pfp. [1] vigrah] amnf vigṛhyā which must be separated or isolated | gram. independent (padapātha) | hostile, aggressive, unfriendly — abs. ind. having separated; having quarreled.
