vigrhyavāda [vāda] m. dispute.
vigrhyasambhāṣā [sambhāṣā] f. dispute; opp. samdhāyasambhāsā.
vigna [pp. vij] amnf vignā agitated, ball poured.
vigrah [vigrah] v. [9] pr. (vigṛḥṇāti) pr. r. (vigrhnīté) pp. (vigrhīta) to seize, grasp; com to beat | to recognize, separate, divide, isolate. keśe vigrah to seize by the hair.

Vigraha [act. vigrah] m. separation, isolation; individual form, figure, silhouette, body; ornament; in the form of (iic.) | gram. analysis of a compound word [samāsa] into its constituents; morphological analysis of an inflected word [pada]; paraphrase of a construction [vṛtti] in prose [vākya] | struggle, conflict | hist. np. of the Vigraha dynasty of Kalinga (6th century). vigraham grah take shape. vigraham kr take shape | to wage war. vigraham upādā assume a form. latāntaritavigrahah var. latāvyavahitavigrahah ca singing his body behind a bush. iti vigrahah gram. this is the literal analysis of the compound.
vigrahavat |vat| amnf vigrahavatī having taken form; incarnate. vigrahavān dharmaḥ phil. Duty incarnate; said not. of Rāma.
vigrahavākya | vākya | n. gram. canonical paraphrase of the meaning of a compound word.
Vigrahavyāvartanī [vyāvartana] f. lit. np. of the Vigrahavyāvartanī, "(Method) to avoid sterile discussions", epistemological treatise due to Nāgārjuna.
vigrahin [agt. vigrah] amnf vigrahinī who makes war — m. soc. minister of war.
vigrahika [ka] m. id.
vighat [vighat] v. [1] pr. r. (vighatate) pp. (vighațita) to separate; to disperse; to interrupt, to stop — ca. (vighaṭayati) to separate, to disperse; to interrupt, to destroy.
vighaṭṭ [vighaṭṭ] v. [1] pr. r. (vighaṭṭate) pp. (vighattita) to break, destroy — v. [10] pr. (vighaṭṭayati) to break (door); scatter; shake, rub.
vighațțana [act. vighațț] nf vighațțanā act of rubbing, friction; act of agitating; act of untying | act of tearing, of breaking into pieces — amnf vighattanā That which opens.
vighasa [vighasa] mn leftover food (offered as an oblation, or to a guest).
vighasāśa |āśa₂| amnf vighasā Who eats the leftovers.
vighasāśin [āśin] amnf vighasāśinī Who eats the leftovers (of the guest), is said of the masters of the house.
vighāt [ca. vihan] v. [10] pr. (vighātáyati) to destroy, to beat (not. an army); to torment.
vighāta [act. vighāt] m. act of repelling, pushing back someone. (g. iic.) | obstruction, obstacle, impediment; interruption, rupture; suppression.
vighūrṇ [vighūrṇ] v. [6] pr. (vighūrṇati) pp. (vighūrnita) to be overturned, to be agitated.
vighūrṇita [pp. vighūrṇ] amnf vighūrnitā agitated, overturned. বিঘ্ন vighna [agt. vihan] m. obstacle; impediment; interrupt — ifc. Who pushes back, Who breaks (iic.); destroyer, switch of (iic.).
vighnakara [kara₁] amnf vighnakarā obstructor; Who blocks, Who pushes back.
vighnakārin [kārin] amnf vighnakārinī obs constructor; That which blocks, That which repels.
vighnakṛt [kṛt₂] amnf Who interferes, Who obs true.
vighnajit [jit] amnf Who overcomes obstacles — m. myth. np. of Voghnajit, epith. of Ganesa.
vighnāntaka [antaka] m. myth. np. of vighnāntaka, epith. of Gaņeśa "He who removes obstacles"

vighneśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of vighneśvara, epithet of Ganesa "Master of Obstacles"; he triumphs over obstacles for those who invoke him, but can also create them for others. namo ganeśāya vighneśvarāya lit. (preliminary invocation of a work) Glory to you, Ganesa, who removes obstacles.

√ vic [related to vij] v. [7] pr. (vinakti) pr. r. (vinkte) pp. (vikta) pf. (vi) to discriminate, to discern; to separate; not. the grain from the chaff, to winnow | to deprive of i. — ca. (vecayati) cf. vivic — des. (vivikṣati) to wish to separate.
vicakṣ [vicakṣ] v. [2] pr. r. (vicaṣṭe) to see clearly; to discern, to perceive.

vicaksaná [agt. vicaks] amnf vicaksanā perceptible; visible, evident; radiant, splendid intelligent, clairvoyant, perceptive; cunning | wise, prudent, prudent; circumspect | expert in, versed in (loc. iic. | not. title of graduate of advanced Sanskrit — f. vicakṣaṇā myth. np. of vicakṣaṇā "Clairvoyance", throne of Brahmā.
vicatura [vicatura] amnf vicaturā having varied verses [pāda].
vicaya [act. vici] m. collection, enumeration investigation, research, examination.

vicar [vicar] v. [1] pr. (vicarati) pp. (vicarita) pfp. (vicārya) to circulate, wander, travel; to spread; to live; to practice | to make a mistake, to deviate from the rule — ca. (vicārayati) to mislead, to lead astray; to seduce — ca. r. (vicārayate) ["to turn around" to reflect, hesitate, have doubts about loc. . kim vicārayate what's the point of procrastinating?
vicarṣaṇi [vicarṣaṇi] amnf very active; talented | var. vicarṣaṇa f. vicarṣaṇā id.

vical [vical] v. [1] pr. (vicalati) pp. (vicalita) pf. (pra) to move, to stir, to be agitated; to leave, to deviate, to withdraw from (abl.) — ca. (vicālayati) to make move; to agitate, to shake, to stir | to turn away from abl. .
vicalita [pp. vical] amnf vicalitā parti; rebié; dévié de (abl.) | troubled, obscured, blinded. vācā vicalitā yasya sukṛtaṃ tena hāritam |VC.| He who denies his word loses all his merit here below.

vicāra [act. vicar] m. procedure; deliberation, reflection; introspection; reasoning, rational investigation | doubt, hesitation; prudence | probable conjecture | intellectual debate; controversy, dispute | phil. opinion as a criterion of moral judgment; opp. ācāra — ifc. considerations relating to (iic.). vicāram kṛ to hesitate, to procrastinate.
vicāravat [vat] amnf vicāravatī prudent; prudent, Who acts after reflection.
vicārasāgara [sāgara] n. bed. n.p. of the vicārasāgara, Vedānta text in Hindi due to Niścaladāsa muni (1844), translated into Sanskrit by śrī Vāsudeva Brah mendra Sarasvatī₂ Svāmī (1964).
vicāraṇa [act. vicar] n. consideration, reflection; deliberation, discussion; doubt, hesitation — f. vicāraņā id. | phil. [YV.] introspection, 2nd level of knowledge [jñānabhūmikā].
vicāraṇīya [pfp. [2] ca. vicar] amnf vicāranīyā which deserves reflection.
vicārita [pp. ca. vicar] amnf vicāritā considered, discussed, evaluated | doubtful, uncertain | decided, established — n. doubt, hesitation; deliberation, discussion.
vicārin [agt. vicar] amnf vicāriṇī who moves; who wanders — ifc. who considers, who discusses, who judges (iic.).
vicārya₁ [pfp. [1] ca. vicar] amnf vicāryā debatable; that which must be debated; doubtful.
vicārya₁ [abs. vicar] ind. having discussed, having deliberated.
vicālin [agt. vical] amnf vicalinī changing, variable.
vici [vici] v. [5] pr. (vicinóti) pr. r. (vicinuté) pp. (vicita) pf. (pra) separate by thought, distinguish; select | divide (not. hair); lift, disperse | investigate; examine carefully search.
vicit [vicit₁] v. [1] pr. (vicetati) pp. (vicitta) to perceive, discern, understand — pr. r. (vicetate) to appear.
vicitta [pp. vicit] amnf vicittā perceived, observed; manifest.
vicitra [vicitra] amnf vicitrā varied; mul ticolore, variegated | astonishing, singular, surprising; strange, marvelous; rare | pleasant, amusing.

vicitravīrya [vīrya] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Vi citravīrya "Wonderful Hero", of the lunar kaurava lineage; younger son of King Sāmtanu and his wife Satyavatī, he is half-brother of Bhīşma; after the death of his elder brother Citrāngada he became heir to the throne; to ensure his lineage, Bhīsma abducted Ambikā₁ and Ambālikā₁ to serve as his wives; When he died of phthisis without an heir, Satyavatī asked her secret son Vyāsa, whom she had from her encounter with the ascetic Parāśara, to return from his hermitage to marry his two widows, Am bikā₁ from whom he fathered Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Ambālikā₁ from whom he fathered Pāndu.
vicitraśākayūṣabhakṣya [śāka₁yūṣabhakṣya] n. variety of vegetarian dishes. vicitraśākayūṣabhakṣyavikārakriyā vikāra kriyā] f. soc. the art of preparing food, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
vicitrita [vicitraita] amnf vicitritā painted, decorated, adorned, embellished.

vicint [vicint] v. [10] pr. (vicintáyati) pp. (vicintita) abs. (vicintya) to consider, examine; to reflect upon, to concern oneself with (acc.) | to invent, to invent. rātrirgamisyati suprabhātam bhāsvān udesyati hasisyati pankajaśrīh | ittham vicintayatikośagate dvirephe hā | hanta hanta nalinīm gaja ujjahāra || The night will pass, in the morning the Sun will rise, and the beauty of the lotus will bloom; thus the bee, imprisoned in a bud, imagines its future; alas, boom, boom, an elephant uproots the lotus plant. vicintya ind. reflecting.
vícetana [vicetana] amnf vicetanī in conscious; distracted | inanimate; deceased | idiot — f. vicetanī charm rendering unconscious.
vícetas [vicetas] amnf distracted; perplexed | ignorant; stupid.

viceṣṭ [viceṣṭ] v. [1] pr. (viceṣṭati) pp. (viceștita) to gesticulate, to fidget; to struggle; to be in convulsions | to act, to strive, to exert oneself. kam api nikṛttapāṇipādakarṇanāsikam avanipṛṣṭhe vicestamānam purusamadrāksīt [DKC.] He saw a man fidgeting on the ground, with his hands, feet, ears, and nose amputated.
viceṣṭita [pp. viceṣṭ] amnf viceṣṭitā performed — n. action, behavior.

vícchiti [act. vicchid] f. action of breaking or cutting or tearing; break | interruption; cessation | lit. poetic flourish, surprising twist (figure of speech) | decoration of the body by ointments, makeup | [nāṭya] the rearrangement of clothing or jewelry for erotic purposes, one of the 10 means of seduction [hāva] of the woman.
vicchid [vichid₁] v. [7] pr. (vicchinátti) pr. r. (vicchintté) pp. (vicchinna) abs. (vicchidya) to split, destroy; to separate, interrupt.
vicchidya [abs. vicchid] ind. having separated separately from (abl.).
vicchindat [ppr. vicchid] amnf vic chindatī separating, interrupting. বিভিন্তম vicchinna [pp. vicchid] amnf vicchinnā split, separated, interrupted.
viccheda [act. vicchid] m. fracture, interruption, separation; destruction, cessation; difference, distinction | gram. segmentation.
vicchedaka [agt. vicchid] amnf vicche dikā that cuts, that slices; that separates.
vicchedana [act. vicchid] m. separation; cutting | cancellation, suppression, destruction.
vicchedin [agt. vicchid] amnf vic chedinī that cuts, that slices; that destroys, having intervals, segmented.
vicyuta [vicyuta] amnf vicyutā fallen, banished; expelled, diverted from (abl.) | med. removed (you die).
vicyuti [vicyuti] f. forfeiture; expulsion, separation; abortion.
√ vij v. [6] pr. r. (vijáte) v. [6] pr. (vijati) pp. (vigna) pf. (ut, sam) to rush | to flee; to tremble, to be afraid — ca. (vejayati) pp. (vegita) to accelerate,
intensify | worry, alarm | ang. vigour, weak; fr. vigor.
vijana [vijana] amnf vijanā without men, solitary.

vijayá [act. viji] m. victory, conquest over (g. iic.); triumph; success | booty | myth. [Mah.] np. of vijaya "the Victorious", name of exile of Arjuna in the kingdom of Virāta | myth. np. of vijaya₁, one of the two dvārapāla of Viṣṇu | hist. np. of vijaya₂, Sinhalese founding prince, around 500 ante; cf. Anurādha | ved. np. of vijaya₃ "Victory", javelin of Rudra | myth. [Mah.] vijaya₄ bow that Viśvakarmā had made for Indra, and that Jāmadagnya gave to Karṇa; cf. bhārgava | astr. np. of vijaya₅ "Victorious", personifying the 27th year of a life cycle [samvatsara] | geo. np. of the principality of vijaya₆ of the Hinduized kingdom of Campā₁ in southern Vietnam — n. royal tent — amnf vijayā which leads to victory; Victorious — f. cf. vijayā.
vijayacandra [candra] m. hist. np. of the vijaya candra king of Kānyakubja; he is son of Govindacan dra, whom he succeeded (1155–1169); he patronized Srīharsa.

vijayadatta [datta] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Vi jayadatta, younger son of the brahmin Govindasvāmī who went to Vārāṇasī; seized by a freezing fever, he warmed himself in a crematorium field where by accident he transformed into the rākṣasa Kapālasphota.

vijayádaśamī [daśamī] f. soc. 10th tithi of the festival of durgāpūjā, just after navarātra; it coincides with the festival of Daśaharā, on the 10th tithi of the clear fortnight of the month āśvina (mod. Dassera); the birthday [jayantī] of Madhva is also celebrated there.

vijayánagara [nagara] n. geo. np. of Vijayana gara "City of Victory", capital of the Karnata Empire, on the south bank of the Tugabhadra (mod. Hampi, near Hospet); its mythical origins are associated with Kişkindhā; during the conquest of Warangal by Malik Kafur in 1323, the brothers Harihara₁ and Bukka₁, ministers of King Pratāparudra₁, fled to Kampili; during its invasion in 1327 by the army of Sultan Tughluk of Delhi, they were taken prisoner, converted, and sent back there as governors; they then founded the City of Vijayanagara, and Harihara₁ became its first emperor in 1336, inaugurating the Sangama dynasty; It was sacked and destroyed after the Battle of Tālīkoṭa in 1565; the empire would die out in 1678 | geo. np. of Vijayanagara₁, City of the Gajapati empire south of the Kalifga, on the east coast of the Deccan; mod. Viśakhapatnam, north of the country of Andhra [Uttarāndhra].

Vijayapura [pura] n. geo. np. of Vijayapura "City of Victory", capital of the Cālukya kingdom; mod. Bījāpur in Karņāṭa — f. vijayapurī geo. np. of vijayapurī, capital of the Ikṣvāku₁ dynasty in the Andhra country; it became an important monastic university center, later called Nāgārjunakunda.

vijayabhaṭṭārikā [bhaṭṭārikā] f. hist. np. of Queen Vijayabhatţārikā, who ensured the regency of the Cālukya throne of Vātāpi₁ (mod. Badāmi) between 649 and 655; Vikramāditya₁ succeeded her, upon the death of her minor son; she was literate, and composed the poem Kaumudīmahotsava.
Vijayasena [sena] m. hist. np. of King Vijayasena, son of Hemantasena; he reigned over Bengal from 1096 to 1159; his son Vallasena succeeded him.
vijayanta [vijayanta] m. myth. np. of Vi jayanta "Most Victorious", epith. of Indra.
vijayā [f. vijaya] f. soc. [Tantra] drink of crushed hemp [bhangā] drunk during rituals.

vijayākalpa [kalpa] m. lit. np. from the vijayākalpa, chapter of the Anandakanda dealing with the use of cannabis. śakrāsanam tu tīkṣṇoṣṇam mohakṛt kuṣṭhanāśanam balamedhāgnikrc chlesmadoṣahāri rasāyanam | It is truly the food of Indra; stimulating, hallucinogenic, it fights leprosy, gives strength and mental acuity, reduces phlegm, and gives long life.
vijayi iic. vijayin.

vijayīndra [Indra] m. hist. np. of the ascetic philosopher vijayīndra Tīrtha (1514–1595), disciple of Madhva, whom he defended against Appayya Dīkṣita; he had as his patron Sevappa Nāyaka of Tanjavūr; we owe him notably the Madhvādhvakantakoddhāra, and the polemic Appayyakapolacapeţikā, as well as the Upasaṃhāravijaya; he also fought that Nṛsiṃhāśrama in his Bhedavidyāvilāsa.

vijayin [agt. viji] amnf vijayinī vain queur — m. adversary conqueror; we distinguish the dharmavijayin respecting the laws of war, the lobhavijayin, conqueror greedy for lands and goods, and the asuravijayin, demonic conqueror, who takes sons, wives and life.
vijānat [ppr. vijñā₁] amnf vijānatī sa vant, scholar.
viji [viji] v. [1] pr. r. (vijayate) pp. (vijita) to overcome, conquer; to win, beat, prevail over (acc.) — des. (vijigīṣati) des. r. (vijigīṣate) to want to conquer.
vijigīṣ [des. viji] v. pr. (vijigīṣati) v. pr. r. (vijigīṣate) to want to conquer.
vijigīṣā [act. des. viji] f. desire to conquer.
vijigīṣu [agt. des. viji] amnf who wants to conquer; ambitious | soc. "ambitious of conquest", royal title of conqueror; Kauţilya bestows it upon Prince Bindusāra.
vijigīṣutā [tā] f. desire for conquest; ambition.
vijigīṣutva [tva] n. id.
vijigīṣuvāda [vāda] m. phil. debate where victory is sought (rather than truth).
vijighra [vijighra] ifc. amnf vijighrā who sniffs.
víjita [pp. viji] amnf vijitā conquered; beaten, dominated, vanquished — mn conquered country; conquest, victory.
vijṛmbh [vijṛmbh] v. [1] pr. r. (vijṛmbhate) pp. (vijṛmbhita) open the mouth; yawn | develop, spread out; appear; have an erection; be at ease.
vijṛmbha [act. vijṛmbh] m. frown — f. vijṛmbhā yawn.
vijṛmbhaṇa [act. vijṛmbh] n. yawn; frown | blossoming, flowering; extension, spreading.
vijṛmbhita [pp. vijṛmbh] amnf vijṛmbhitā yawned; open; extended, spread out; stretched (bow) — n. yawn; manifestation.
vijetṛ [agt. viji] amnf vijetrī conqueror, victorious. বিরা vijña [agt. vijñā₁] amnf vijñā instructed, learned — m. learned, scholar, wise.
vijñatā [tā] f. wisdom; skill; knowledge.
vijñatva |tva| n. id.

vijñap [ca. vijñā₁] v. [10] pr. (jñapayati) pp. (vijñapta) to make known, to inform; bring to the attention or judgment of a superior — pr. r. (vijñapayate) to inform oneself. বিহ্নম vijñaptá [pp. vijñap] amnf vijñaptā dif fusé, published; informed
vijñapti [act. vijñap] f. information; report (to a superior) | request (about (g.)). vijñaptikṛ to report (to a superior) | to submit a request (about g.).
vijñaptimātra [mātra] n. bd. doctrine of nothingness as representation, of the idealist school of bd. Mahāyāna; it teaches that the World is only an idea; cf. cittamātra.
vijñaptimātratā |tā| f. bd. idealist thesis of bd. Yogācāra, denying the absolute reality of perceived objects.
vijñaptimātratāsiddhi [siddhi] f. bed. n.p. of the vijñaptimātratāsiddhi, commentary on the Trimśikā of Vasubandhu.

vijnā₁ [vijnā₁] v. [9] pr. (vijānāti) pp. (vijñāta) pfp. (vijñeya) pf. (sam) to recognize, to recognize, to distinguish, to understand; to recognize something (acc.) as something (acc.); to recognize oneself in (loc.) to learn something (acc.) from someone (g.); to inform oneself, to cultivate oneself — ca. (vijñapayati) ca. (vijñāpayati) pp. (vijñapta) to make known, to inform; to bring to the knowledge or judgment of a superior — ps. (vijñāyate) to be known; to be understood | (impers.) it is known that, it being understood that; it is prescribed that. বিরা vijñā₂ [act. vijñā₁] f. knowledge, understanding.
vijñāvāda [vāda] m. phil. Buddhist idealism.
vijñāta [pp. vijñā₁] amnf vijñātā dis surrounded, understood, known | famous; celebrated.

vijnāna [act. vijnā₁] n. cognition; discernment, understanding, intellect | knowledge, wisdom, science | phil. sacred knowledge, science in fuse | bd. discriminating knowledge, one of the 5 aggregates [skandha] of the ego; it is the 3rd cause of suffering [pratītyasamutpāda] | bd. consciousness as absolute reality — ifc. knowledge of, understanding of (iic.) | pali viññāṇa. vijñānamātram bd. nothing other than consciousness. śāstram śabdavijñānādasannikṛṣṭe 'rthe vijñānam phil. [Sabarasvāmī] Knowledge of sacred texts, arising from the word, is produced without any contact with the object.
vijñānanidhi [nidhi] m. mod. cultural treasure (not. ancient manuscripts).

vijñānabhikṣu [bhikṣu] m. hist. n.p. of the philosopher Vijñānabhikṣu (16th century); He fought against the monistic [Advaita] interpretation of Vedanta and strove to reconcile a theistic interpretation with Samkhya; he reinterpreted Patanjali's Yoga Sutra to situate it within the Vedanta perspective; we owe him, notably, the Yogavarttika, the Yogasarasamgraha, the Samkhya Ravanabhasya, the Samkhyasara, and the Vijñanamrṛta. [bhairava] Vijñanabhairava n. [vijñanabhairavatantra] lit. np. of the Vijñanabhairava Tantra, an ancient esoteric text of Kashmira Shaivism; it is a chapter of the Rudrayāmala tantra; it describes 112 spiritual techniques of liberation.
vijñānamaya [maya] amnf vijñānamayī phil. made of pure intellect, of the nature of knowledge.
vijñānamayakośa [kośa] m. phil. [Vedānta] the sheath of discernment, forming with manomayakośa the subtle or intellectual body [sūkṣmaśarīra].
vijñānavāda [vāda] m. bd. ["way of full awareness" idealist phil. doctrine of the Yogācāra Buddhist school; opp. śūnyavāda; cf. Asanga, Va subandhu.
vijnānavādin [in] amnf vijnānavādinī bd. proponent of the path of knowledge, idealist; he affirms that the phenomenal world is made up only of psychic representations.
Vijñānāmṛta [amṛta] n. bed. n.p. of the Vijñānāmṛta, or Vijñānāmṛtabhāṣya, commentary on the Brahmasūtra due to Vijñānabhikşu.
vijñānāstitvavāda [astitvavāda] m. bd. vijñānāstitvavāda school professing the doctrine that only consciousness is real; it is said to have been founded by Rāhula₁.
vijñānāstitvavādin [in] amfn vijñānāstitvavādinī bd. holding to this doctrine; syn. vijñānavādin; opp. sarvāstitvavādin, śūnyavādin.
vijñānin [agt. vijñā₁] amnf vijñāninī scholar; specialist.
vijñāp [ca. vijñā₁] v. [10] pr. (vijñāpayati) pp. (vijñāpita) to make known, to inform; to bring to the knowledge or judgment of a superior.
vijñāpana [act. That. vijñā₁] n. information, communication; request — f. vijñāpanā id.
vijñāya [abs. vijñā₁] ind. having recognized, having discerned.
vijñeya [pfp. [1] vijñā₁] amnf vijñeyā re recognizable, discernible, perceptible | to be known; to be considered as (nom.).
vijvara [vijvara] amnf vijvarā devoid of anxiety, serene.
vijval [vijval] pf. (abhi) [unused without pf.].

vița m. epicurean, bon vivant; wit; libertine, debauchee; lover | pimp; matchmaker; darling, giton | lit. (theatre) companion in debauchery of a prince; flatterer, courtier; not. Vița in the Mṛcchakaṭikā.
vitapriya [priya] m. jasmine.

viṭaṅka [viṭaṅka] amnf viṭaṅkā [“made without being chiseled”] is said of a primordial linga [svayaṃbhū] | pretty, graceful; excellent — mr. geo. not. n.p. of Vitanka, emerald linga [marakata] of the Tyāgarāja temple.
viṭapa mn branch, twig; bush | shoot.

vitthala [pkt. viṣṇu] m. myth. np. of viṭṭhala or Vițhobā "brick", aspect of VișnuKṛṣṇa; while visiting the city of Pandharpur he breathed his essence into a young Brahmin named Puṇḍarīka (or Puṇḍalīka or Puṇḍaraṅga) who was renowned for his filial piety; he is depicted as a white adolescent standing on a brick, his fists on his hips, awaiting the return of Pundarīka who had gone to take care of his parents; his cult gave rise to the Haridāsa sect in the 13th century; his pilgrimage is celebrated in Pandharpur, not. at āṣāḍha ekādaśī; The saint Nāmadeva celebrated him; a large temple of vitthala is located at Vijayana gara; his cult gave rise to the [sampradāya] Vārkarī movement | hist. np. of the grammarian viṭṭhala₁, commentator of Rāmacandra₂. বিতহ্ন viṭhaṅka amnf viṭhaṅkā dissolute; debauched, frequenting prostitutes.
viṭhobā cf. viṭṭhala.
vid iic. vis₂.
vidja [ja] amnf vidjā produced by garbage — m. mushroom.

vida mn salt of solution deposition | med. medicinal salt obtained from the fruit of the myrobalan. বিভদ্ধ vidanga amnf vidangā intelligent, gifted — m. bio. bot. Embelia Ribes, a primrose shrub with reddish-black fruits; it is an important medicinal plant — n. its fruit, used as a vermifuge.
vidamb [vidamb] v. [10] pr. (vidambayati) pp. (vidambita) imitate, mock, make fun of.
vidambana [act. vidamb] n. imitation; ca ricature — f. vidambanā id.
viḍambita [pp. viḍamb] amnf vidambitā imitated, copied; disguised, deformed | deceived; frustrated, mortified | inferior; abject — n. object of ridicule or mockery; object of contempt.
viḍambin [agt. viḍamb] amnf vidambinī who imitates, imitator; who mocks, who ridicules | cheat; impostor | forger; profaner.
viḍāla var. biḍāla m. cat — f. viḍālā f. vidālī female cat.
vitaḍ [vitaḍ] ca. (vitāḍayati) pp. (vitāḍita) to defend oneself, to strike back; to crush | to fight against (loc.).

vitaṇḍa [act. vitaḍ] m. three-lever lock — f. vitandā sterile objection, quibbling; derision; sophistry, obstruction, nitpicking; controversy | phil. rhet. criticism or mockery of the opposing thesis; opp. vāda, jalpa.
vitata [pp. vitan] amnf vitatā extended, spread out; that which covers | under tension (bowstring); stretched (bow) | covered; filled | wide; clear (road).
vítatadhanvan [dhanvan] amn who has drawn his bow.
vitati [act. vitan] f. dimension, length extension, expansion; diffusion | quantity, collection; group.

Vitatha [vitathā] amnf vitathā false, incorrect; futile, irrelevant | myth. np. of Vitatha "Bastard", name given by Bharata to his adopted son Bharadvāja₁ found in the forest; he became the hermit Dīrghatamā. vitathena adv. falsely. vitatham kr revoke, annul.
vitathatā [tā] f. falsehood; lie. vitathatām gam to tell a lie.
vitathātmadṛṣṭi [ātmadṛṣṭi] f. bd. false conception of the Self.
vitathya [ya] amnf vitathyā false, erroneous.

vitan [vitan₁] v. [8] pr. (vitanóti) pr. r. (vita nuté) pp. (vitata) to extend, spread out; to extend; to go on; to stretch (bow, rope, fabric) | to execute, to accomplish (a sacrifice); to deploy | lat. tendo; fr. tendre.

vitap [vitap] v. [1] pr. (vitapati) pp. (vitapta) to give off heat | to force, to penetrate — pr. r. (vitapate) to warm up; to be burning hot, to be consumed — ca. (vitāpayati) to warm, to heat. vitapate svam prstham his back is burning.
vitara [vitara] amnf vitarā which leads further (said of a path).
vitaraṇa [agt. vitr़] amnf vitaraṇā that crosses — act. n. crossing | transfer; donation.
vitark [vitark] v. [10] pr. (vitarkayati) pp. (vitarkita) to think.
vitarka [act. vitark] m. reflection; supposition, conjecture, probability | discussion, argument
tation | doubt, suspicion | pali vitakka.
vitarkamudrā [mudrā] f. bd. gesture of argumentation, or of teaching (originally as abhayamudrā, then thumb and index finger of the hand joined).
Vitala [vitala] n. myth. np. of the world [loka] Vitala, second subterranean hell. বিবস্থ vitaṣṭa [vitaṣṭa] amnf vitaṣṭā hollowed, sculpted; flattened.

vitástā f. geo. np. of the Vitastā river, which originates in the southeast of the Kaśmīra valley, flows at Śrīnagara and empties into the Chenāb at Puñjab; it is the Hydaspes of the Greeks which Alexander reached; mod. Jhelum.
vitasti f. span; unit of length, equal to 12 inches [aigula] (approximately 23 cm); syn. tāla.
vitāna [agt. vitan] mn extension, expansion; large volume, multitude, mass accomplishment | soc. oblation; not. solemn rite with the 3 sacred fires | canopy, dais.
vitāla [vitāla] amnf vitālā out of step.
vitṛṣ₁ [vitṛṣ₁] v. [4] pr. (vitṛṣyati) to be thirsty — ca. (vitarṣayati) to thirst.
vitṛṣ₁ [vitṛṣ₁] amnf freed from thirst or desire.
vitṛṣa [vitṛṣā] amnf vitṛṣā freed from thirst or desire.

vitṛṣṇa [vitṛṣṇā] amnf vitṛṣṇā freed from all desire; who does not covet — f. vitṛṣṇā absence of desires. mūdha jahīhi dhanāgamatṛṣṇām kuru sadbuddhim manasi vitrsnām | yallabhase nijakarmopāttam vittam tena vinodaya cittam || [Bhajagovinda] Poor fool! Abandon your thirst for wealth, and with your mind fixed on truth, manage to free yourself from all desire, and limit yourself to the fruit of your past actions.
vitṛṣṇatā [tā] f. absence of covetousness, satisfaction.
vitṛṣṇā [act. vitṛṣ₁ɪ] f. violent desire.

vitr [vitr] v. [1] pr. (vitarati) v. [1] pr. (viti rati) pp. (vitīrņa) to cross, to permeate | to carry out, to remove | to give, to grant | to produce, to accomplish, to realize — ca. (vitārayati) to sort, to filter, to comb; to accomplish. āsanam vitr to offer a seat. uttaram vitr to grant an answer. darśanam vitr to permit sight; to grant audition. dvāram vitr to grant passage.
vittá [pp. vid₂] amnf vittā acquired, obtained — n. property, goods; wealth, fortune; money.
vittakosa | kosa | mr. mod. bank.
Vittama [vid₂tama] ifc. amnf Vittamā super. Best connoisseur of (iic.). Yogavittama best practitioner of yoga.
vittavat [ppa. vid₂] amnf vittavatī who acquired; rich.
vitti [act. vid₂] f. consciousness | understanding; intelligence.
vitras [vitras] v. [4] pr. (vitrasyati) pp. (vi trasta) to be terrified — ca. (vitrāsayati) to frighten.
vitrasta [pp. vitras] amnf vitrastā ter rified.

√ vid₂ v. [2] pr. (vetti) pft. (veda) aor. [5] (avedīt) pp. (viditá) ppft. (vidvas) pfp. (veditavya, vedya) abs. (viditvā) pf. (ā, ni, pra, prati, sam) to know, to be familiar with; to know as (2 acc.); to take | to experience, to feel, to be aware of; to see — ps. (vidyate) to be known, to be recognized — ca. (ve dayati) ps. (vedyate) to inform someone (dat.); to show, to demonstrate, to communicate something (acc.); to teach someone something (2 acc.) — dés. (vividisati) to want to know, to desire to know; to investigate — dés. (vivit sati) id. — intens. (vevidīti) intens. r. (vevidyate) to know well | Lat. video; All. wissen, weise; Eng. wit, wise, wisdom. vidyāt one must understand that; one must know that. vidāmāsa he knows this. viddhi yathā know this. ya evam veda who knows this (use of the perfect tense in the present). tam sthaviram viduh they consider him old. rājarṣir iti mām viduḥ they take me for a rājarsi. uttamānām api strīņām viśvāso naiva vidyate One should not trust, even the best of women. tad idam sarvam āpnoti ya evam veda [CU.] He who knows this gets everything he desires. He knows all the sciences and yet does not boast; he discusses the law with the wise and attains glory among them (illustrates the use of the roots vid₂ ₁ and vid₂ ₂). What pleases me, I do; what the wife knows, I am not sure, she does what pleases her.

√ vid₂ [related to vid₂] v. [6] pr. (vindati) pft. (viveda) aor. [2] (avidat) v. [2] pr. r. (vitte) pp. (vittá, vinna) ppr. ps. (vidyamāna) pf. (nis) to find, discover, acquire, obtain | procure for someone. (dat.) — v. [6] pr. r. (vindate) to obtain in marriage, to marry — v. [7] pr. r. (vintte) to discuss, to consider — ps. (vidyate) to be found, to exist, to be. vidyate there is (a) | (with na) there is not. vidyante there are (some).
vid₂ [agt. vid₂] amnf ifc. who knows, who is familiar with (iic.); knowing, connoisseur of (iic.); cf. vit tama — m. learned, scholar.
vida [agt. vid₂] ifc. amnf vidā id.
vídagdha [pp. vidah] amnf vidagdhā burned, inflamed; consumed, digested | spoiled, corrupted, sour; matured | subtle, intelligent, learned, scholarly; Skillful, cunning — m. learned, erudite; syn.
pandita | intriguing | lit. np. of Vidagdha, title of Sākalya "Skilled scholar", eminent linguist and author of the Padapāṭha — f. vidagdhā soc. learned woman.
vídagdhatā [tā] f. intelligence, erudition; skill in (loc.).
vídagdhatva |tva| n. intelligence, erudition; habi leté en loc. .
vid₂átha m. wisdom, expertise; spiritual authority | assembly, council; congregation.

Vidarbha [vidarbha] m. geo. n.p. from the Vidarbha country "devoid of kuśa grass", south of the Vindhya mountains (mod. Berar, northeast of Mahārāṣṭra); its capital was Kundina₁; cf. Da mayantī, Bhīṣmaka | pl. vidarbhās his people, the vidarbhās || hi. Berar. vidarbheșu loc. adv. in Vidarbha.
vidal [vidal] v. [1] pr. (vidalati) pp. (vidalita) to burst, to burst; to split, to open suddenly.
vidala [agt. vidal] amnf vidalā split, cracked — n. fragment, piece, portion | split bamboo; cane | split pea.
vidalana [act. vidal] n. act of splitting.
vidalita [pp. vidal] amnf vidalitā split, cracked, burst.
vidas [vidas] v. [4] pr. (vidasyati) pp. (vi dasta) to run out, to exhaust oneself; to be exhausted, to run out.
vidah [vidah₁] v. [1] pr. (vidahati) pp. (vi dagdha) to burn, to destroy by fire. )4
vidāra [act. vidr] m. action of splitting, tearing | war ; catastrophe — f. organic vidārī. bot. Ipomoea digitata, sweet potato.
vidāraņa [agt. vidr] amnf vidāraņā splitting, breaking; that which bursts — act. n. act of splitting, piercing, opening (not. the mouth).
vidāsin [vidasin] amnf vidāsinī that is exhausted; that dries up.
vidāhin [vidāhin] amnf vidāhinī burning.
vidāhitva [tva] n. state of being very hot.
viditá [pp. vid₁] amnf viditā known, re known; learned, understood.
viditaveditavya [veditavya] amnf viditavedi tavyā who knows all that must be known.
vidiś [vidiś₂] f. intermediate point of the com not (like Northeast).

Vidiśā [vidiśā] f. northeastern region | geo. np. of the city [nāgara] of Vidiśā, on the Vetra vatī, 10 km from Sāñcī, in Madhya Pradesh; it was an important center of trade and worship in the 6th and 5th centuries BC; it was abandoned in the 6th century, destroyed and then rebuilt as Bhilsā, capital of the Daśārnās (modern Besnagar) in the 9th century; the Pillar of Heliodorus and the Caves of Udayagiri₃ are found there; cf. Pingalā₂ | lit. [K.] capital of King Sūdraka₁.
vidu [vid₁u] amnf Intelligent; wise.

vidura [vid₁ura] amnf vidurā Intelligent, clever — ifc. connoisseur, specialist (in (iic.)) — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of vidura "the Intelligent One", born (from the gaze) of Vyāsa upon a servant disguised by Ambikā₁; he was born Intelligent because his mother understood the fertilizing gaze of Vyāsa; he embodies Dharma cursed by Māṇḍavya; half-brother of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu, he is the wise advisor of the Pāṇḍavās; at the end of the war he became a wandering ascetic, ceased to eat, and died uniting with Yudhisthira by the gaze.
viduranīti [nīti] f. lit. [Mah.] np. of the viduranīti "Wisdom of vidura", episode of book 5, where vidura vainly offered advice to Dhṛtarāṣṭra to try to avoid war.
viduraprajāgara [prajāgara] m. cf. viduranīti.
viduṣ [viduṣ] v. [4] pr. (viduṣyati) to sin, to commit a fault, to transgress ca. (vidūṣayati) cf. vidūṣ.
vidusī cf. vidvas.

vidūra [vidūra] amnf vidūrā distant, very far away | that which cannot be reached by g. . vidūrāt var. vidūratas adv. from afar; far away. vidūraja var. vidūraja |ja| n. blue beryl, aquamarine | gem, precious stone (cat's eye, lapis lazuli, etc.).
vidūratha | ratha | mr. myth. | Mah. | n.p. of prince vrsni vidūratha, son of Vasudeva.
vidūṣ [ca. viduṣ] v. [10] pr. (vidūṣayati) pp. (vidūṣita) to defile, corrupt, dishonor. upahāsaih vidūs to ridicule, mock.

vidūṣaka [agt. ca. viduṣ] amnf vidūṣikā ifc. who dishonors, who ridicules — m. soc. jester, burlesque theatre role of childhood companion of the prince-hero; he plays the corrupter, and serves as a scapegoat; he must be a brahman, or of a caste superior to the prince, and speaks Sanskrit; he carries a twisted staff | kuṭilaka |, and he himself is crippled and bald; he is gluttonous, and cowardly, but acts the braggart; he is symbolically associated with Varuna and Brahmā; cf. Gautama₁, Cārāyaṇa₁, Māṇavaka, Mādhavya, Maitreya₂, Va santaka, Vaikhānasa, Santusta.
vidūṣaṇa [agt. ca. viduṣ] amnf vidūṣaṇā that defiles, that soils; vile, corrupter — act. n. its tire; insult; defamation.
vidūṣita [pp. ca. viduṣ] amnf vidūṣitā defiled; slandered, outraged, insulted — n. lit. rhet. slander, insult; ad hominem attack.
vidṛ [vidṛ] ca. (vidāráyati) pp. (vidīrṇa) to split, tear, lacerate.
videśa [videśa] amnf videśī foreign; exotic — m. foreign country — f. videśī foreign language | hi. videś. videśagata gone abroad. videśagamana departure abroad.
videśin [videśain] amnf videśinī foreign || hi. videśī.
videśyá [videśaya] amnf videśyā foreigner; opp. samdeśya.

videha [videha] amnf videhā incorpo rel; mort ["deprived of body"] — m. phil. absence of consciousness of one's body in the experience of identity with the Absolute [brahman] | myth. np. of videha, epith. of the king Mithi Janaka, born from the lifeless body of Nimi | geo. by ext., country north of the Ganges, kingdom of the Janaka dynasty; its capital was Mithilā.
videhamukta [mukta] amnf videhamuktā phil. [yoga] which frees itself from the consciousness of its body.
videhamukti [mukti] f. phil. liberation through absence of consciousness of one's body.
videhin |in| amnf videhinī phil. to be accomplished [siddha₁] reduced to one's causal body [kāraṇaśarīra], in a state of asamprajñāta samādhi.
viddhá [pp. vyadh] amnf viddhā pierced; struck, beaten; wounded — ifc. filled with, affected by, transformed by (iic.) — m. arch. (jointing) tenon. śūlāyām viddhaḥ impaled.
viddhaśālabhañjikā [śālabhañjikā] f. bed. n.p. from the viddhaśālabhañjikā, nāṭikā style drama of Rājaśekhara.
vidyamāna [ppr. p.s. vid₂] amnf vi dyamānā which is found, which exists; existing, real.

vidyā [vid₂ya₂] f. science, knowledge, wisdom | sacred tradition; the Veda, revealed knowledge | soc. magical formula; not. mantra associated with a female deity phil. |śaivasiddhānta| aspect of the bindu associated with SadāśivaAghora. vidyām prapad to access knowledge.

Vidyākara [kara₁] m. hist. np. of the Bengali Buddhist scholar Vidyākara (early 12th century); he was abbot of the monastery [vihāra] of Jagaddala in Varendra₁ (modern Bangladesh); he is the compiler of the Subhāsitaratnakośa.
vidyādāna [dāna] n. instruction; teaching of sacred knowledge.

vidyādhara [dhara] mf vidyādharī myth. ["bearer of wisdom"] class of aerial genies, magicians in Shiva's retinue, considered demides [upadeva]; eternally young, of great beauty, they change their appearance at will [kāmarūpin]; they are depicted carrying garlands in the sky; cf. Kandarpa ketu, Jīmūtavāhana, Mānasavega, Sudarśana₁ | pl. myth. np. of the vidyādharā genies; [KSS.] Na ravāhanadatta became their emperor | hist. np. of the poet Vidyādhara, author of the poetic treatise Ekāvalī (13th-14th centuries) | bd. title of Tibetan lamas.
vidyādharamalla [malla] lit. mr. [viddhaśālabhañjikā] np. of King Vidyādharamalla of the country Karpūravarsa.
vidyādhikārin [adhikārin] afmn vidyādhikāriņī soc. "in charge of knowledge", title of cultural advisor to the prince, court poet with ministerial rank; cf. Srīnātha.

vidyādhīśa [adhīśa] m. hist. np. of vidyādhīśa, 16th pontiff of the Uttarādi matha (1619–1631); expert in debate, he travelled around India to fight opponents of Madhva; at Ikkeri he engaged in a three-month oratorical contest against the advaitin Rangoji Bhatta.
vidyānanda [nanda] m. hist. np. of the Jain logician vidyānanda (circa 750); we owe him the Aptaparīkṣā with his own commentary.
Vidyānātha [nātha] m. hist. np. of the scholar Vidyānātha, author of the Pratāparudrīya (early 14th century).
vidyānidhi [nidhi] m. soc. scholar's title Vidyānidhi "Treasury of knowledge". vidyānipuņa |nipuņa| amnf vidyānipuņā who succeeds in their studies.
vidyāpati [pati] m. "master of knowledge", title of

scholar [paṇḍita] | myth. np. of vidyāpati, mi nistre of King Indradyumna, sent as a scout to Purușottamakșetra | hist. np. of the poet vidyāpati₁, important court poet of Mithilā (1352–1448); he is notable author of Vaishnava devotional poems in the Maithilī language which he helped to fix, such as the Kīrtilatā and the Kīrtipatākā; he also composed many smṛti works in Sanskrit, such as the Puruṣaparīkṣā.
vidyāpīṭha [pīṭha] n. ["seat of knowledge"] school, college, university | soc. throne for the presentation of a Shaivite manuscript [āgama] to be consecrated.
vidyāpravīna [pravīna] amnf vidyāpravīnā "versed in knowledge", holder of a university master's degree.
vidyābhūṣaṇa [bhūṣaṇa] n. soc. np. of vidyābhūṣaṇa, title of scholar.
vidyāmandira [mandira] n. school.

Vidyāmādhava [mādhava] m. hist. np. of Vidyāmādhava, poet of the 14th-15th century, expert in double-meaning poetry [śleṣa]; we owe him notably the Pārvatīrukminīya. vidyāraņya [raṇya] amnf vidyāraṇyā who takes pleasure in knowledge — m. hist. np. of Vidyāranya, name of ascetic of Mādhavācārya.

vidyārambha [rambha] m. soc. ceremony marking the beginning of a boy's primary education, around the age of five; the teacher presents a stick of chalk [khadī] to the pupil and begins to teach him to write. sarasvatī namastubhyam varade kāmarūpiņī vidyārambham karişyāmi siddhirbhavatu me sadā O goddess sarasvatī of enchanting aspect, I worship you; as I begin my studies, grant me always knowledge.

vidyārāja [rāja] m. bd. King of brightness, wrathful deity of the esoteric bd. of Tibet, China and Japan; he protects the pure (buddha, bodhisattva); the principal ones are Acala, Rāga, Hayagrīva₂, Ucchuṣma, Trailokyavijaya, Kundalī, Yamāntaka₁, Vajrayakṣa; they are depicted furious, with many arms bearing weapons, carrying skulls, and surrounded by flames — f. vidyārājñī bd. partner of a king of brightness; cf. Mahāmayūrī. vidyārthin var. vidyarthin [arthin] amnf vidyārthinī who desires to learn — m. student.
vidyālaya |ālaya| mn school, college.
vidyāvat [vat] amnf vidyāvatī who possesses knowledge; scholar.
vidyāvāridhi | vāridhi | amnf soc. | “ocean of science” | holds a doctorate.
vidyāvṛddha [vṛddha] amnf vidyāvṛddhā superior in science; advanced in knowledge.
vidyāṣaḍakṣarī [ṣaḍakṣara] f. bd. formula in 6 syllabes; cf. om.
vidyāsāgara |sāgara| m. np. Vidyasāgara "Ocean of knowledge", scholar's title in Sanskrit.
vidyāsthāna [sthāna] n. phil. ["seat of knowledge"] branch of knowledge; tradition distinguishes 14: The 4 Knowledges [Veda], The 6 subsidiary disciplines [vedānga], and The 4 disciplines
secondary [upānga]: logic [Nyāya], exegesis [Mīmāṃsā], law [dharmaśāstra] and Ancient Tales [purāṇa].
vidyāsnātaka | snātaka | m. soc. returning home at the end of his Vedic studies; if he has also completed his vows |vrata|, he is vidyāvratasnātaka.
vidyeśvara [īśvara] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Vi dyesvara "Master of science", brahmin endowed with magical powers.
Vidyuc iic. Vidyut₂.

Vidyucchikhā [śikhā] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the rākṣasī Vidyucchikhā "Crowned with lightning", widow of King Lambajihva killed by Kapālasphota; she lured her brother Vijayadatta into a crematorium field and left him an ankle ring; when he came back to her to get the second one, she offered to marry him to her daughter vidyutprabhā in Trighanta.
Vidyut₁ [vidyut₁] v. [1] pr. r. (vidyotate) to shine (like lightning) — ca. (vidyotayati) to illuminate.

Vidyut₂ [agt. Vidyut₁] f. lightning; thunder | phil. [ChU.] np. of Vidyut, the Lightning personified as a quarter [kalā] of the radiant aspect [jyotiṣmat] of the brah man | [vidyucchakti] mod. electricity || pali vijju.
vidyutkanda [kanda] m. mod. electric light bulb.
vidyutprabhā [prabhā₂] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of Vi dyutprabhā "Illumination of lightning", daughter of the rākṣasī Vidyucchikhā; she married Vijayadatta.
vidyutvat [vat] amnf vidyutvatī equipped with lightning; charged with lightning.
vidyuddūta | dūta | m. mod. electronic message.
vidyudvallī | vallī | f. flash.
vidyúnmat |mat| amnf vidyunmatī accom accompanied by lightning.
vidyunmālā [mālā] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the princess vidyunmālā, daughter of Suroha, fifth wife of Sūryaprabha₁.
vidyunmālā |mālā| f. crown of lightning | phon. variety of meter anuştubh₂.
vidyunmālin [mālin] m. myth. np. of the asura Vi dyunmālī "Crowned with lightning", son of Tāraka; cf. Tripura.
Vidyullatā | latā | f. branched lightning | lit. np. of a commentary Vidyullatā of the Meghasandeśa of Kālidāsa.
Vidyota [agt. Vidyut₁] amnf vidyotā sparkling — m. lightning | myth. np. of Vidyota, son of Dharma, personifying lightning.
vidru [vidru₁] v. [1] pr. (vidravati) to run here and there, to flee, to run away — ca. (vidrāvayati) to chase, to put to flight.
vidruma [vidruma] n. coral.
vidrumamaya [maya] amnf vidrumamayī in coral.
vidvaj iic. vidvat.
vidvajjana [jana] m. wise; learned.
vidvat iic. vidvas.
vidvattama [tama] amnf vidvattamā super. who knows best; the best scholar.
vidvattara |tara| amnf vidvattarā compar. who knows better; better scholar.
vidvattā [tā] f. science; expertise, knowledge, erudition.
vidvattva |tva| n. id.
vidvatpravara [pravara₃] m. soc. scholar's title.
vidvatpriyatā [priyatā] f. love of science.
vidvatsabhā [sabhā] f. assembly of scholars; scientific colloquium.
vidvadgoṣṭhī [goṣṭhī] f. scholastic debate among scholars.

vidvás [ppft. vid₁] amnf vid₁úṣī scholar, wise, learned; intelligent; expert, versed in (acc. loc. iic.) — m. soc. np. of Vidvān, title of scholar. vidvāmso vaiyākaraņāḥ prathame [Anandavardhana] The first scholars are The grammarians. udyantu śatamādityā udyantu śatamindavah | na vinā viduṣām vākyairnaśyatyābhyantaram tamah )7 that 100 Suns rise, that 100 Moons rise, yet the inner darkness cannot be dispelled without the word of the wise. viduṣītarā var. viduṣitarā |tara| f. a more learned woman.
vidvis₁ [vidvis₁] v. [2] pr. (vidvesti) pp. (vidviṣṭa) ppr. (vidviṣat) to hate, to detest — pr. r. (vidviște) to hate each other.
vidviṣ₂ [agt. vidviṣ₁] m. enemy.
vidviṣat [ppr. vidviṣa] amnf vidviṣatī ennemi — m. id.
vidviṣṭa [pp. vidviṣṭā hated, detested, odious; hostile to (loc.) — ifc. contrary to (iic.).
vidveṣa [act. vidviṣ₁] m. hatred, hostility; aversion towards (loc.). vidveşam kr to be hostile towards (loc.). vidveṣaṃ gam to be odious towards (loc.).
√ vidh₁ v. [6] pr. (vidhati) to worship, to honor a god (dat. loc. acc.) (with (i.)) | to offer, to dedicate. kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema [RV.] To which god should we offer the oblation?
vidh₁ [agt. vyadh] ifc. amnf [sg. nom. vit] that stings, that pierces (iic.). ਕਿੰਘ vidha cf. vidhā₂.
vidhama [vidhama] amnf vidhamā who blows or beats against (iic.).

vidh₁áraṇa [agt. vidhṛ] amnf vidharaṇī that maintains, that supports | that controls, that restrains.
vidharma [vidharma] amnf vidharmā evil, unjust; illegal, illicit; contrary to duty — m. illegality, injustice.
vidhavā [vidhava₂] f. widow eng. widow.
vidhavātā [tā] f. state of widowhood.

vidhā₂ [vidhā₁] v. [3] pr. (vidádhāti) pr. r. (vidhatté) pp. (vihita) pf. (anu, abhi, prati, sam) to make, produce, effect; to determine, assign; to join; to establish, fix, decree; to regulate, distribute; to install, place, arrange, put; to fix upon, direct towards (dat. loc.) | to show in itself — ps. (vidhīyate) to be. Intended for, to be considered as [nom.] — des. (vidhitsati) to seek to procure. vidhīyamānah gram. being established. yo vidhīyate gram. that which is enjoined. kāmān vidhā₂ to grant wishes. pūjām vidhā₂ to perform devotions. maitryam vidhā₂ to make friends. mano vidhā₂ to think about, to meditate on (loc. dat. prati inf. mantram vidhā₂ to hold counsel. veṣaṃ vidhā₂ to put on clothing; to assume the appearance of. upāyam vidhā₂ to devise a means. lajjam vidhā₂ to be timid; to show modesty. rājyam vidhā₂ to rule. simhatvam vidhā₂ to transform into a lion. saṃdhim vidhā₂ to make peace. kalaham vidhā₂ to pick a quarrel. vairam vidhā₂ to declare war. kolāhalam vidhā₂ to cause a commotion. cumbanam vidhā₂ to give a kiss.
vidhā₂ [act. vidhā₂] f. manner of being, behavior | kind — mn vidha ifc. similar to | (num.) occurring so many times. evamvidha amn tel ["whose kind is thus"]. tathāvidha tel ... (that).
yathāvidha | correl. tathāvidha | conj. (such) ... that. bahuvidha amn diverse ["of many kinds"]. bhavadvidha like you. saptavidha math. on a scale of 7.

vidhātṛ [agt. vidhā₂] amnf vidhātrī or giver, Dispenser; creator of (g. iic.) — m. myth. np. of Vidhātā "Dispenser", epith. of Brahmā "the Ordainer of the World", personifying Destiny with his wife Ayati | myth. son of Bhṛgu by Kyāti, associated with his brother Dhātā as masters of Destiny. bhāgya vidhātṛ Destiny savior (not. of India).

vidhāna [act. vidhā₂] n. arrangement, order; disposition (not. of sacred fires) | prescription, rule; act of enjoining | that which is prescribed, that which must be accomplished | application of rules, execution; means, manner | mod. constitution. vidhānatas adv. according to the rules, in accordance with the prescriptions.
vidhanavid | vid₃ | amnf who knows the prescriptions.

vidhāv [vidhāv₁] v. [1] pr. (vidhāvati) to cease flowing, to dry up; to disperse, to disappear.

vidhi [act. vidhā₁] m. rule, ordinance, instruction; precept, law, authority; affirmation; injunction; exhortation | rite, ceremony; manner of acting, conduct | phil. [Mīmāmsā] ritual injunction; syn. codanā; cf. utpattividhi, viniyoga vidhi, prayogavidhi, adhikāravidhi, niyamavidhi, parisaṃkhyāvidhi, phalavidhi | lit. instruction text of the ritual in brāhmaṇa literature; opp. arthavāda | gram. prescriptive rule of a grammatical operation; prescription of a tense/aspect for conjugating a verb; cf. lakāra; not. imperative, cf. lot | creator, ordainer; destiny | myth. np. of vidhi the Regulator, epith. of Brahmā.
vidhipūrvakam | purvaka | adv. according to his duty; duly.

vidhivat |vat| adv. according to the rule or rite; as is proper. vidhivat pūjyate he receives worship according to the rule.
vidhiviveka [viveka] m. bed. n.p. of the vidhiviveka, work of Mīmāmsā of Maṇḍana Miśra; Vācaspati₁ Miśra commented on it Nyāyakaṇikā.
vidhisūtra [sūtra] n. gram. rule prescribing an operation in Asṭādhyāyī.
vidhī cf. vidhā₁.
vidhú [vindhu] m. the Moon; in poetry she afflicts those who are far from the beloved.

vidhura [vidhura] amnf vidhurā [“without stretchers” damaged | separated (from the beloved object); sad, depressed | unsympathetic — ifc. deprived of, lacking (iic.); full of longing for (iic.). saṃskṛtagandhavidhura devoid of the fragrance of Sanskrit.
vidhū [vidhū₁] v. [5] pr. (vidhunóti) pp. (vidhūta) to shake, agitate | to chase away, disperse.

Vidhūma [vidhūma] amnf vidhūmā smokeless — m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vasu Vidhūma; having fallen in love with the nymph [apsaras] Alambuṣā, he was punished by Indra to be reborn on Earth as King Sahasrānīka.
vidhṛ [vidhṛ] pft. (vidadhāra) pp. (vidhṛta) to hold; to carry; to transport | to arrange; to seize; to bind.
vídhṛta [vidhṛta] amnf vidhṛtā kept separate; divided | avoided; stopped; controlled, restricted | possessed, held; carried.
vídhṛtāyudha [āyudha] amnf vidhṛtāyudhā who holds weapons.
vídhṛti [vidhṛti] f. separation; division, partition | regulation; exclusion | border; barrier.
vidheya [pfp. [1] vidhā₁] amnf vidheyā obedient, submissive, docile | prescribed | gram. predicate (opp. subject [uddeśya]) | gram. refers to the number [vacana] prescribed to a word.

vidhvaṃs [vidhvaṃs] v. [1] pr. r. (vidhvaṃsate) pp. (vidhvasta) to fall into pieces, to crumble to dust; to perish, to disappear — ca. (vidhvamsayati) pp. (vidhvamsita) to cause to collapse, to destroy; to annihilate, to obliterate.

wine which has, which possesses (sf. secondary possess sif, form of the a.).

vinata [pp. vinam] amnf Vinatā inclined, bent, arched | humble, humiliated — f. Vinatā myth. np. of Vinatā "the humble", daughter of Prajāpati, and of Nalā, wife of Kaśyapa; [Mah.] she wished to have two sons stronger than those of her sister Kadrū; she gave birth to Aruna and Garuda, who stole the amrta to deliver her from death — n. vinati the act of bowing (before (loc.)).

vinayá [act. vinī] m. teaching (of moral values), discipline; regulation | education, conduct | good conduct, obedience; decency, modesty | bd. disciplinary code (of a monastic order) | myth. np. of Vinaya "modest", son of Dharma and Kriyā. gunesu vinayah śresthah The best quality is modesty. guṇā vinayena śobhante virtues are enhanced by modesty.
vinayatā [tā] f. good conduct; modesty.
vinayadhara [dhara] m. bd. master of moral teaching.
vinayapiṭaka | piṭaka | n. bd. collection of discipline manuals.

vinayavat [vat] amnf Vinayavatī who has good conduct; modest — f. Vinayavatī lit. [DKC.] np. of Vinayavatī "modest"; she adopted the baby born of the love of Śūdraka₂ and Aryadāsī, developing the maternal love of her future incarnation Kāntimatī towards her son Arthapāla.
Vinayasūtra [sūtra] n. bd. n.p. of the Vinayasūtra, disciplinary code bd.
vinayana [vinayana] amnf vinayanā that removes, that takes away — n. education, discipline.
vinaś [vinaś₁] v. [4] pr. (vinaśyati) pp. (vinașța) pf. (anu) to perish, disappear | to be lost, to be ruined; to be destroyed — ca. (vināśayati) to cause the ruin of.
vinaśana [act. vinaś] n. complete disappearance; ruin | geo. place where the Sarasvatī₁ dis appears in the sands of the Thar desert.

vinaśvaratva [tva] n. id. ਰਿਜਣ vinaṣṭa [pp. vinaś] amnf vinaṣṭā lost, ruined; destroyed, perished, disappeared | corrupted, tainted — n. carrion.
vinastatejas [tejas] amnf who has lost his energy; weak, anemic.
vinaști [act. vinaś] f. ruin, destruction.

vināyaka [agt. vinī] amnf vināyikā who leads, who guides — m. chief, guide | myth. np. of vināyaka "guide", epith. of Gaņeśa | myth. Garuda "King of the birds" | hist. np. of vināyaka₁ Dīkṣita, Tamil śaiva mystic (1520–1593); he is the author of many texts on Vedānta and other subjects; he was the second guru of Bhațțoji Dīkṣita; he is better known as Appayya Dīksita | hist. np. of vināyaka₂ deva, son of Kāpaya nāyaka; he was defeated by Bahadur Khān, sent by Sultan Muhammad Shah (14th century).

vinigraha [vinigraha] m. restriction, control, limitation.

vinipāt [ca. vinipat] v. [10] pr. (vi nipātayati) to cut down, destroy. )()
vinipāta [act. vinipat] m. blows; fall, ruin.

viniyata [pp. viniyam] amnf viniyatā restricted, repressed; controlled, regulated. yadā viniyatam cittam ātmanyevāvatisthate nihsprhah sarvakāmebhyo yukta iti ucyate tadā | BhG. viniyogamantra [mantra] mn lit. formula which attributes a sage [ṛṣi] as visionary author to each hymn of the Rigveda, and indicates their meter and tone.
viniyogavidhi [vidhi] m. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] auxiliary ritual injunction, for example specifying an instrument.
vinirgata [pp. vinirgam] amnf vinirgatā parti; product | released (from (abl.)).
vinirgam [vinirgam] v. [1] pr. (vinirgac chati) pp. (vinirgata) to leave, to go out of; to disappear | to escape (from (abl.)); to be out of oneself.

vinirṇī [vinirṇī] pp. (vinirṇīta) to determine precisely.
vinirṇīta [pp. vinirṇī] amnf vinirṇītā determined precisely; fixed; certain.
vinirdiś [vinirdiś] v. [1] pr. (vinirdiśati) pp. (vinirdista) to indicate, designate something (acc.) as (acc.); to destine for (loc.) | to determine, specify, define; to resolve.
vinirdiṣṭa [pp. vinirdiś] amnf vinirdistā indicated; designated, specified; entrusted to (loc.). 9(
vinirdeśya [pfp. [1] vinirdiś] amnf vi nirdeśyā to determine, to define | math. to solve; statement of a problem (find ... such that).

vinirmita [pp. vinirmā] amnf vinir mitā made, constructed, fashioned, created | intended for, designated for.

vinirmukta [pp. vinirmuc] amnf vinir muktā made free; freed (from (i. iic.)) | abandoned; discharged, cast. śrnoti śrāvayedvā'pi satatam caiva yaḥ naraḥ sarvapāpavinirmuktah vaisnavam padamāpnuyāt || [Mah.] The man who listens or even better who recites perpetually (the Mah.) is freed from all his sins, and attains the position of Vișnu.
vinirmukti [act. vinirmuc] ifc. f. liberation, deliverance from (iic.).
vinirmuc [vinirmuc] v. [6] pr. (vi nirmuñcati) pp. (vinirmukta) abandon (one's body, die) — ps. (vinirmucyate) to be released (from (i.), to be rid of (i.).
vinivid [vinivid₁] ca. (vinivedayati) to make known, to inform.
viniviś [viniviś] ca. (viniveśayati) pp. (nivesita) install; introduce; appoint to (loc.); erect (statue); found (city) | fix the eyes or the taken upon (loc.).
viniviṣṭa [pp. viniviś] amnf viniviṣṭā residing at (iic.); placed on or in (loc.).
vinivṛt [vinivṛt] v. [1] pr. r. (vinivartate) v. [1] pr. (vinivartati) pp. (vinivrtta) to go back, to return; to turn around | to withdraw, to cease.

viniveśita [pp. ca. viniviś] amnf viniveśitā erected; installed (on or in (loc.)) installation, arrangement. sarvopamādravyasamuccayena yathāpradeśam vinivesitena | sā nirmitā visvasrjā prayatnād ekasthasaundaryadidṛkṣayeva || [KuS.] The Creator endeavored to fashion her by arranging in every appropriate place on her body the totality of objects of praise, as if he desired to contemplate all beauty in one place.
viniveśin [agt. viniviś] ifc. amnf vi niveśinī located on (iic.) or in (loc.).
viniścaya [act. viniści] m. decision (about (g. iic.), determination; firm opinion, 1( certainty.

viniści [viniści] v. [5] pr. (viniścinóti) pr. r. (viniścinuté) pp. (viniścita) abs. (viniścitya) inf. (viniscetum) to deliberate, discuss; to take into consideration; to decide, to conclude. viniścetum śakyo na sukhamiti vā duḥkhamiti vā prabodho nidrā vā kimu visavisarpah kimu madah |Uttararāmacarita| One is not capable of making a decision, neither when one is joyful, nor when one is in sorrow, nor when one is waking from sleep, nor, a fortiori, when one is poisoned or drunk.
viniśvas var. viniḥśvas [viniḥśvas] v. [2] pr. (viniśvásiti) pp. (viniśvásita) to sigh, to pant, to hiss; to utter sighs.

vinihata [pp. nihata] amnf vinihatā struck; struck down | dissipated (darkness) | ignored (order) afflicted, defeated (mood) — m. disaster, calamity; stroke of luck | comet, meteor.
vinihan [vinihan] v. [2] pr. (vinihanti) pp. (vinihata) to flatten, to destroy.

vinīya [vinī] m. related; syn. kalka.
vinud [vinud] v. [6] pr. (vinudati) pp. (vi nunna) to strike, to injure — ca. (vinodayati) to drive away (not. worries); entertain, distract. বিনুম vinunna [pp. vinud] amnf vinunnā injured.
vinod [ca. vinud] v. [10] pr. (vinodayati) pp. (vinodita) to chase away (not. worries); to entertain, to distract — ps. (vinodyate) to amuse oneself (i.).

vinodavat |vat| amnf vinodavatī pleasant, fun, entertaining.

vinodita [pp. vinod] amnf vinoditā distracted, entertained.
vinda [agt. vid₂] ifc. amnf vindā qui ac quiert, qui acquis (iic.); qui trouve (iic.).
vindu₁ var. bindu m. drop.
vindu₁ [vid₂u] ifc. m. who seeks (iic.); who finds (iic.); familiar with (iic.).
√ vindh v. [6] pr. r. (vindháte) to lack of.
vindhya m. [vindhyagiri] geo. name of the Vindhya mountain range | myth. np. of his personification Vindhya; he bowed before the ṛṣi Agasti.

vindhyamāhātmya | māhātmya | n. lit. np. of the Vind hyamāhātmya, glorifying the vindhya mountains.

vindhyavāsin [vāsin₁] amnf vindhyavāsinī who dwells in the vindhya mountains — f. vindhyavāsinī myth. np. of vindhyavāsinī, epith. of Durgā "who dwells on Mount Vindhya"; her temple is in Vindhyācala; [KSS.] Vararuci went there, and the goddess showed him in a dream where to find Kāṇabhūti; she did the same for Guṇāḍhya, allowing the transmission of the history of the magicians.

Vindhyācala [acala] m. geo. the range of the vindhya mountains; syn. vindhyagiri |soc. np. of Vindhyācala, pilgrimage site on the Ganges upstream from Vārānasī (far from the vindhya mountains, near mod. Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh); the temple of vindhyavāsinī is located there.
Vindhyācalavāsinī [vāsin₁] f. geo. n.p. of Vindhyācalavāsinī; cf. vindhyavāsinī.
vindhyāvalī [āvalī] f. myth. np. of vindhyāvalī "chain of the vindhya", wife of the daitya king Bali, mother of Bāṇa.

Vibhāṇḍaka [vibhāṇḍaka] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the ṛṣi Vibhāṇḍaka, son of Kāśyapa; he lived as a hermit and practiced penances; Rśyaśrnga is his son, born of an antelope that drank the water of the river where its seed had flowed in the sight of the apsaras Urvaśī; the antelope was a daughter of the gods to whom Brahmā had promised to regain human form if she gave birth, as an antelope, to a great saint; a son was born to her with a horn on his forehead [Ráyaśrnga]; Vibhāndaka raised him in ignorance of women; In adulthood, he was abducted by courtesans sent by King Lomapāda to marry him to his daughter and alleviate the drought in his country; Vibhāndaka consented, provided that his son returned to the hermitage after having a son of his own.

vibhūti [act. vibhū₂] f. manifestation of force, deployment of energy, power; superhuman power; syn. siddhi | abundance, wealth; success, splendor | phil. [vaiṣṇava] divine manifestation; being possessing a portion of divine creative energy | soc. ashes (of cow dung) with which ascetics smear themselves, not. Shiva.

vibhūtipañjara [pañjara] n. soc. ["cage of divine manifestations"] recitation of the 100 syllables of 10 series of invocations of the daśāksaramantra, followed by its installation [vibhūtipañjaranyāsa], successively in 100 places of the body.
vibhūtipāda [pāda] m. phil. [yoga] np. from the vibhūtipāda, section of the Yogasūtra dealing with the Way of power.
vibhūtimat [mat] amnf vibhūtimatī powerful; superhuman | covered in ashes.
vibhūṣ [vibhūṣ] v. [10] pr. (vibhūṣayati) pp. (vibhūṣita) to adorn, to decorate.
vibhūṣaṇa [act. vibhūṣ] n. ornament.
vibhūṣita [pp. vibhūṣ] amnf vibhūṣitā ornate, decorated. mundamālāvibhūṣitā adorned with the garland of skulls (called of Kālī).
vibheda [act. vibhid] m. act of breaking; division, separation; distinction | frowning | change, alteration | divergence of opinion, dissension.
vibhedaka [agt. vibhid] amnf vibhedikā which distinguishes one thing (g.) from another (abl.) — m. cf. vibhīdaka.

vibhraṃś [vibhraṃś] v. [1] pr. r. (vibhramsate) pp. (vibhrasta) to fall into info rune; to fall from, to be separated from (abl.) — ca. (vibhramśayati) pp. (vibhramśita) to cause to fall or decline, to make disappear; to cause the loss of.
vibhraṃśa [act. vibhraṃś] m. decline; loss, ruin; end | disturbance — ifc. state of being deprived of, loss of (iic.).
vibhraṃśita [pp. That. vibhraṃś] amnf vibhraṃśitā that has been dropped.
vibhraṃśitajñāna [jñāna] amfn vibhramśitajñānā who has lost his mind; who lost consciousness.
vibhraṃśin [agt. vibhraṃś] amnf vibhramśinī that falls (from (iic.)); detached from iic. that falls into pieces.
vibhram [vibhram] v. [1] pr. (vibhramati) v. [4] pr. (vibhrāmyati) pp. (vibhrānta) to wander, to circulate, to move about in all directions, to become confused to scatter, to stir, to frighten.

Vibhrama [act. vibhram] m. agitation, confusion; vehemence, violence, excess, intensity | disturbance, illusion, appearance; error of perception | error; fault | feminine charm, coquetry; erotic play, art of the courtesan | [nāṭya] state of amorous confusion, one of the 10 means of seduction [hāva] of the woman.

vibhramaviveka [viveka] m. lit. np. from Vibhrama viveka, work of Mandana Miśra. ਕਿਸ਼ੲ vibhraṣṭa [pp. vibhraṃś] amnf vibhraṣṭā fallen, sunk | disappeared, gone; lost; useless — ifc. deprived of (iic.); which fails at (iic.).
vibhrāj [vibhrāj] v. [1] pr. r. (vibhrājate) to shine, to sparkle.
Vibhrāja [agt. vibhrāj] amnf vibhrājā very bright — m. lit. [HV.] np. of King Vibhrāja.
vibhrānta [pp. vibhram] amnf vibhrāntā who wandered | confused, troubled; bewitched.
vibhrāntanayana [nayana] amnf vibhrāntanayanā who rolls their eyes | who looks out of the corner of their eye, who casts sideways glances.
vibhrāntamanas [manas] amnf with a confused mind; bewildered, troubled. )8
vibhvan [vibhū₂] amnf vibhvanī penetrating, which permeates — m. myth. np. from rbhu Vibhvā "Penetrating".
vímati [vimati] amnf [“of poor in intelligence” | limited | of a different opinion — m. difference of opinion; disagreement — f. ["which inspires bad thoughts" | antipathy, aversion.
vimatitā [tā] f. state of being narrow-minded, foolishness, stupidity.
vímatsara [vimatsara] amnf vimatsarā not envious, without jealousy; altruistic.
vímada [vimada] amnf vimadā sobre; calm; without arrogance.
viman [viman] ca. (vimānayati) pp. (vimata) pfp. (vimānya) to disrespect, humiliate, treat with disdain, with contempt; to dishonor.
vimanas [vimanas] amnf discouraged, dejected, desolate, depressed | mentally disturbed; stu pide | ill-disposed; hostile.
vimanaska [ka] amnf vimanaskā discouraged, dejected; inconsolable.
vimanā [vn. vimanas] v. [11] pr. r. (vi manāyate) to be dejected, to be discouraged.
vimarda [act. vimrd] m. crushing, grinding | devastation, destruction | interruption | astr. total eclipse.
Vimardaka [agt. vimṛd] amnf vimardikā who grinds; who destroys — m. grinding; destruction l lit. [DKC.] np. of Vimardaka "Grinder", brute in the pay of Apahāravarmā.
vimardana [act. vimṛd] n. grinding; destruction — f. vimardanā id.

vimarśa [act. vimṛś] m. consideration, examination; discussion, reflection; awareness; understanding | lit. [theatre] knot of the plot in a drama; this episode follows the germ [garbha] and precedes the denouement [nirvahaṇa] | phil. [Tantra] Nature, emanation of Śakti, mirror of the universal consciousness of Śiva [prakāśa].
vimarśana [act. vimṛś] n. discussion ; investigations — m. vimarșana lit. n.p. of vimarșana, king of the Kirātās.

vimarśin [agt. vimṛś] amnf vi marśinī who considers, who examines — f. vimarśinī lit. n.p. from the Vimarśinī₁, "Exegesis" of the Śivasūtra by Kṣemarāja; cf. Śivasūtravimarśinī | bed. n.p. of Jayaratha's Vimarśinī₂, commentary on Ruyyaka's Alamkārasarvasva.

vimala [vimala] amnf vimalā pure, immaculate; clear, limpid, transparent; bright | astr. lunar year (opp. mātula, solar year) | hist. 9( np. of vimala Shah, commander-in-chief of King Bhīmadeva; he built at Arbuda₁ the eponymous monastery [vasati], the first of 5 Jain marble temples at Dilwara, dedicated to Rṣabhanātha (1031) — f. cf. vimalā. vimale adv. at daybreak. himavimalamuktāguņah necklace of pearls as pure as snow.

Vimalakīrti [kīrti] m. bd. np. of Vimalakīrti, a wealthy merchant of Vaiśālī₁ "of impeccable reputation", an expert in dharma and a lay disciple of the Buddha, who according to tradition sent Mañjuśrī to debate with him.
vimalakīrtinirdeśa [nirdeśa] m. bed. n.p. from the Vima lakīrtinirdeśa “Instruction of Vimalakīrti”.
vimaladyu |dyu| m. fine weather day.
Vimalanātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of Vimalanātha "Master of Purity", 13th mythical tīrthankara; his body is golden yellow, his symbol is a bloody lion.
vimalaprabhā [prabhā₁] f. bd. n.p. of the Vima laprabhā “Immaculate Light”, gloss [tīkā] of the Kālacakratantra in 12000 stanzas [śloka]; it is attributed to king Kalkī Puṇḍarīka₄.
vimalākṣa [akṣa] amnf vimalākṣī who has light eyes.
Vimalādri |adri| m. geo. np. of Mount Vimalādri "Pure Mountain", highest peak in Gujarāt (1031 m); cf. Girinagara, Satruñjaya.
vimalāpa [āpa₁] amnf vimalāpā whose waters are pure.
vimalā [f. vimala] f. myth. np. of Vi malā, tutelary goddess of the hill of Nīlagiri; she has a shrine in the temple of Ja gannātha at Purī, and the offering [prasāda] is offered to her first.
vimā [vimā₁] v. [2] pr. (vimāti) pp. (vimita) to measure, to count; to cross.
vimātṛ [vimātṛ] f. stepmother, stepmother (wife of one's father).
vimātrja [ja] m. half-brother; syn. vaimātra.

vimāna₁ [agt. vimā] amnf vimānā that travels from one end to the other — mn myth. aerial chariot (of a god), celestial throne; palanquin for transporting a mobile idol [mūrti] | royal palace; sanctuary of a temple | med. sense of proportion (between the humors of the body); relationship between illnesses and remedies. vimānīkṛ to transform into an aerial chariot. )9
vimāna₂ [vimāna₁] amnf vimānā hu milié, outragé — m. disdain, contempt; humiliation.

Vimānasthāna [sthāna] n. lit. np. of the Vimānasthāna, section of the Carakasamhitā dealing with risk factors of diseases, the relationship between doctor and patient, and the acquisition of medical knowledge.
Vimānārcanakalpa [arcanakalpa] m. lit. np. from the Vimānārcanakalpa "Rules for venerating humilia tion" work of vaikhānasa tradition attributed to Marīci.
vimānya [pfp. [1] viman] amnf vimānyā despicable.
vimārga [vimārga] m. path which is not the right one, wrong road.
vimukta [pp. vimuc] amnf vimuktā Freed, liberated, delivered from (abl. i. iic.); deprived of (i.); abandoned.

vimukti [act. vimuc] f. Liberation, deliverance; the act of dismissing; the act of getting out of trouble | disconnection; opp. yukti | bd. Liberation — ifc. abandonment of (iic.) || pali vimutti. sā vidyā yā vimuktaye Knowledge leads to freedom (motto of the University of Hyderabad).
vimuktimārga [mārga] m. bd. Liberation Way.

vimukha [vimukha] amnf vimukhī who turns away, who turns their back; who turns away from (g.) | ill-disposed, hostile | headless or faceless. vimukham kr to put to flight. vimukhīkṛ to dismiss, send away. vimukhībhū to turn their back, to flee; to turn away from abl. .
vimukhatā [tā] f. act of turning away from the angle loc. pratiacc.

vimuc [vimuc₁] v. [6] pr. (vimuñcati) pp. (vi mukta) pf. (pra) to release, to throw; to unharness, to free; to separate, to deprive of (i.) | to lay — ca. (vimokṣayati) To release from (abl.). vimucyantām śvānah release the dogs!
vimuh [vimuh] v. [4] pr. (vimuhyati) pp. (vimūdha) to be lost, to be unconscious; to be stupid to go astray, to be mistaken — ca. (vimohayati) pp. (vi mohita) to panic, to mislead.
vimūḍha [pp. vimuh] amnf vimūḍhā stu pide; lost.
vimūḍhātman |ātman| amnf vimūḍhātmanī with a deranged mind; demented.
vimṛd [vimṛd₁] v. [9] pr. (vimṛdnāti) v. [1] pr. (vimardati) reduce to powder; destroy — ca. (vimardayati) grind; destroy.

vimṛś [vimṛś] v. [1] pr. (vimṛśati) pp. (vimṛṣṭa, vimṛṣita) pf. (pra) to touch, to recognize by touch, to pass one's hand over | to consider, to examine — v. [1] pr. r. (vimṛśate) to wonder, to question — ca. (vimarśayati) to consider, to reflect upon. śāstre prayoge ca mām vimṛśa put me to the test in theory and in practice.
vimṛṣa [act. vimṛś] m. consideration, reflection.
vimṛṣṭa var. vimṛṣita [pp. vimṛś] amnf vimṛṣṭā considered, examined, weighed.
vimoká [act. vimuc] m. unharnessing, dismantling; termination | abandonment; deliverance (from (abl. ii.) | phil. Liberation from the world of the senses. vimókam adv. in order to change the horses.
vimokṣ [ca. vimuc] v. [10] pr. (vimokṣayati) To free from (abl.).
vimokṣa [act. vimokṣ] m. Liberation; abandonment; act of dismissing | phil. deliverance, salvation.
vimokṣaṇa [act. vimokṣ] n. Liberation, delivery; childbirth | the act of releasing (an arrow).

vimocana [agt. vimuc] amnf vimocanī that dismantles, that loosens; that liberates — m. myth. np. of vimocana, epith. of Shiva "Liberator" — act. n. act of unharnessing; rest; help | deliverance; Liberation (not. from sin) | abandonment.
vimoh [ca. vimuh] ca. (vimohayati) pp. (vi mohita) to drive mad, to lead astray.
vimoha [act. ca. vimuh] m. trouble, stupor.
vimohana [act. ca. vimuh] n. confusion, perplexity.
vimohita [pp. ca. vimuh] amnf vimo hitā troubled, distraught.
viyát [ppr. vī₃] amnf viyatī dispersing; evanescent — n. sky, air, ether; syn. vyoman | math. symb. the number zero.
viyukta [pp. viyuj] amnf viyuktā detached, separated; freed from, deprived of (i.e.) | separated (husband and wife) | deficient. prānairna viyuktah He was not deprived of life.

viyuj [viyuj₁] v. [7] pr. (viyunákti) pr. r. (viyunkté) pp. (viyukta) to separate, to deprive of (i. abl.) to separate oneself from (i) — ps. (viyujyate) to be deprived of, to lose (i.) — ca. (viyuyayati) to separate, to deprive of (i. abl. | math. to subtract. .0 mitrairviyujyate he loses his friends.
viyoga [act. viyuj] m. separation; separation from (i. abl. iic.) | the act of getting lost, of missing. viyogena var. viyogatas in the absence, for want of g. ic. . viyogam gam to get lost.
viyogi iic. viyogin.
viyogitā [tā] f. separation.

viyogin [agt. viyuj] amnf viyoginī separated; absent from (i. iic.) — f. viyoginī woman separated from her lover | phone. name of a meter varnavrtta, of motifs sa sa la ga, sa bha ra la ga; the corresponding mātrāvṛtta meter is the syn. vaitālīya.
virakta [pp. virañj] amnf viraktā in different, no longer taking an interest in, not feeling interest or love for (abl. loc. iic.). viraktaceștā [ceṣṭā] f. type of woman who has lost her passion.
virakti [act. virañj] f. change of mood; lack of interest; indifference to (loc. upari g. pratiacc. | indifference to worldly affairs.
viraktimat [mat] amnf viraktimatī indifferent to (loc.).
virac [virac] v. [10] pr. (viracayati) pp. (vira cita) to form, arrange; to shape, construct, erect, invent, compose | to bear, display.

Viracita [pp. virac] amnf viracitā constructed, arranged; erected; invented, composed; borne | composed by, author (i. iic.) — f. viracitā lit. KSS. np. of viracitā, follower of Vāsavadattā₂ with whom King Udayana was cheating on her.
viracitapada [pada] amnf viracitapadā (dis cours) to elaborate words, poetic.

viraja [virajas] amnf virajā clean, pure, unpolluted | (figuratively) free from passions — m. np. viraja "Immaculate" — f. virajā freed from mens trues | np. virajā "Immaculate". virajīkr to free (from dust or passions). virajībhū to free oneself (from dust or passions).

virajānanda [ānanda] m. hist. np. of Svāmī Vi rajānanda Sarasvatī₂ (1757–1868), born in Pañjāb, blind at the age of 5; master of Vedic Sanskrit, he taught notably in Mathurā; Svāmī Dayānanda₁ Sa rasvatī₂ was his student.
virajas [virajas] amnf cf. viraja — m. np. from virajā "Pure"; myth. name of many sages.
virañj [virañj] v. [4] pr. (virájyati) pp. (vi rakta) to fade, to change color; to renounce passions, to become indifferent, to lose interest in (abl. loc.).
virata [pp. viram] amnf viratā stopped (of his own free will), finished | who gives up (abl. loc. iic.) — n. (impers.) that which is stopped. viratam vācā the voice stopped.
virati [act. viram] f. stop; pause; end | phon. end of a caesura in a verse [pada] | resignation; abstention from (abl. loc. iic.) — ifc. finally (iic.).
viram [viram] v. [1] pr. (viramati) pp. (vi rata) abs. (viramya) to stop, cease, end | to put an end to, to cease, to give up (abl.) — ca. (vi ramayati) pp. (viramita) to stop, to make cease.
virama [act. viram] m. cessation, stop; abstention | sunset — ifc. renunciation of (iic.).
viramita [pp. ca. viram] amnf viramitā arrested (by force).
viramya [abs. viram] ind. having stopped.
virala amnf viralā spaced out, sparse; rare; poor in (loc.).
virasa [virasa] amnf virasā insipid.
virah [virah] ca. (virahayati) pp. (virahita) to leave, abandon, desert.

viraha [act. virah] m. separation from, absence of (i. 1ic.) | lit. pain of separation from the loved one — ifc. lack of, suffering from the absence of (iic.) | with the exception of (iic.). virahīkṛ separate.
virahaśayana [śayana] n. [MD.] solitary layer.

virahānka [anka] m. hist. np. of virahānka, prosody theorist and mathematician (between 6th and 8th centuries), commented on by Gopāla₂; he is the author of the Vṛttajātisamuccaya (around 600) (in prākṛta); he found the Fibonacci numbers from the meru prastāra.
virahotkaṇṭhikā [utkaṇṭhaka] f. lit. theatrical heroine who suffers from separation from her lover.
virahita [pp. virah] amnf virahitā aban given — ifc. separated or deprived of (iic.). virahitāt except for (g.).

virahin [agt. virah] amnf virahinī aban given; desert, solitary; alone | separated from, delivered from, deprived of (ig iic.) | absent | who abstains from (iic.) — f. virahiṇī woman separated from her husband or lover.
vírāga₁ [virāga₁] amnf virāgā who is without passion, who has renounced the world; indifferent .1 — m. disgust, aversion (towards (loc. abl. iic.)); opp. rāga | indifference towards the world.
vírāgatā [tā] f. indifference to the world; stoicism.
virāga₂ [act. viranj] m. change or loss of color | excitement, irritation | aversion, disgust, indifference towards (loc. abl. iic.).
virāgin |in| amnf virāgiņī indifferent (inverted (loc.)).
virāj₁ [virāj₁] v. [1] pr. (virājati) pr. r. (virājate) pp. (virājita) to shine, to gleam | to reign over (g. acc.), to govern; to excel in (abl.) — ca. (virājayati) to illuminate.

virāj₁ [agt. virāj₁] amnf [sg. nom. virāt] sovereign — m. king, prince, sovereign | myth. np. of virāt, the Creative Power or Divine Food personified, epith. of Prajāpati, or first creation of Brahmā from his male half, giving birth by his female half Satarūpā to ManuSvāyambhuva, who begat the 10 progenitors |Prajāpati| |phil. the manifested Cosmos, physical support of the Universe; macrocosm — f. phon. name of a meter | chandas | Vedic.
virāṭ iic. virāj₁.
virātpurusa [purusa] m. phil. the Cosmic Being.

virāṭa [virāṭa] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of virāṭa "sovereign", king of the matsyās; his court was at Upaplavya; he possessed many hides; Sudeṣṇā₁ was his queen, whose brother Kīcaka commanded his army; Uttara and Uttarā are his children; he sheltered the Pāndavās under various disguises during their 13th year of exile (cf. Brhannadā, Kanka, Ballava, Granthika, Tan tipāla); he was killed in the great battle by Drona.
virāṭanagara [nagara] n. myth. [Mah.] np. from Virātanagara, capital of Virāta, where the Pāndavās hid during their 13th year of exile; it was Upaplavya, on the banks of the Vetravatī.
virāṭaparvan [parvan] n. bed. n.p. of Virāṭaparva, 4th book of the Mah., "of king virāṭa".
virāddha [pp. virādh] amnf virāddhā contré; blessé, insulté.
virādh [virādh] v. [4] pr. (virādhyati) pp. (Virādha) to counter, to prevent; to hurt — ca. (virādhayati) to disapprove, to disassociate oneself from.

Virādha [act. virādh] m. obstruction, opposition | myth. [Rām.] np. of Virādha "Obstruction", first rākṣasa encountered by Rāma in the Dandakā forest, of frightful appearance; he tried to lift Sītā from it; Rāma and Laksmaņa cut off his hands and buried him alive; he revealed to them that he was the gandharva Tumburu cursed by Kubera; Rāma freed him, he regained his celestial form, and showed the princes the way to the hermitage of Sarabhanga.

virāma [act. viram] m. cessation, stop; pause; rest | gram. sign indicating that a syllable ends in a consonant; cf. halanta abstention; the act of withdrawing; disinterestedness gram. middle of a stanza, indicated in writing by the danda 1. virāmam yā var. virāmamprayā to stop, to rest.
virāva [act. viru] m. noise, buzzing; cry, howl.
virikta [pp. viric] amnf viriktā evacuated, emptied, purged.
viric [viric] v. [4] pr. r. (viricyate) pp. (vi rikta) to empty, to purge — ca. (vireciyati) to empty, to evacuate; to purge.
Viriñca m. myth. n.p. from Viriñca, a name of Brahmā.

viru [viru] v. [2] pr. (virauti) pp. (viruta) to make noise (chirp, buzz, neigh, etc.); to shout, to yell. ūrdhvabāhurviraumyeşa na ca kaścicchṛṇoti mām I shout it very loudly, but nobody listens to me.
viruc [viruc₁] v. [1] pr. r. (virocate) pp. (virūcita) to shine, to illuminate; to excel — ca. (viro cayati) to make shine.
viruca [agt. viruc] m. soc. magic formula to be pronounced over a weapon.
viruj [viruj₁] v. [6] pr. (virujati) to tear to pieces, to destroy.
viruta [pp. viru] amnf virutā cried | filled with the din of (i. iic.) — m. din; call, cry; neighing, warbling, rustling.
viruda var. biruda m. panegyric or glorious nickname of a prince; cf. Mahāmalla | proclamation.

viruddha [pp. virudh] amnf vi ruddhā opposed, obstructed, hindered, blocked; inter said, prohibited; excluded (from (gi iic.)) | uncertain, dangerous, doubtful; incoherent, incompatible contrary; hostile, adverse, enemy | unpleasant, repugnant; disagreeable, odious, hateful (from (iic.)) | gram. (sense) privative — n. opposition, hostility, repugnance | lit. rhet. [alaṃkāra] figure attributing to its likeness properties contrary to its nature. viruddham in an incongruous or perverse manner. viruddham vaditā who is inclined to say contradictory things.
viruddhatā [tā] f. opposition, hostility; interdict tion, prohibition.
viruddhatva |tva| n. id.
viruddhārtha [artha] amnf viruddhārthā of opposite meaning; antonym | contradictory.

virudh [virudh₂] v. [7] pr. (virunáddhi) pr. r. (virunddhé) pp. (viruddha) to obstruct, prevent, oppose (acc.) — ps. (virudhyate) to be opposed, to be hostile to, to fight against (ig loc. pratiacc.) | to contest; to be repressed — ca. (virodhayati) to make hostile, to cause a quarrel.
viruh [viruh₁] v. [1] pr. (virohati) pp. (virūdha) to mount, germinate, sprout — ca. (viro hayati) to make grow; to plant.
virūḍha [pp. viruh] amnf virūḍhā mounted, sprouted, sprouted | climbed, ascended.

vírūpa [virūpa] amnf virūpā multicolored; multiform; varied, different | deformed, disfigured; ugly; deformed, monstrous | myth. np. of the aigiras virūpa "Cripple", son of Angirā — ifc. different from (iic.).

Virūpākṣa₁ [akṣa] amnf virūpākṣī who has deformed eyes; who has many eyes | myth. np. of Virūpākṣa₁, epithet of Shiva "three-eyed"; he was the tutelary deity of the Karnāta empire of Vijaya nagara where his main temple is located; the Pampā River is his wife | geo. temple of Virūpākṣa₁ Lokeśvara₁ built in the 8th century by the Cālukyās of Vātāpi₁ at their coronation capital (mod. village of Pattadakal 20 km from Badāmi) | myth. np. of Virūpākṣa₁, fortunate demon king; The vulture Nādijangha is his friend | myth. [Rām.] np. of Virūpākṣa₁, diśāgaja of the East | myth. np. of numerous supernatural beings | hist. np. of Virūpakṣa₃ Rāya, emperor of Vijayanagara (1404–1405) | hist. np. of Virūpakṣa₄ Rāya, emperor of Vijayanagara (1465–1485) | lit. [KSS.] np. of the yakşa Virūpakşa₅, guardian of the treasures of Kubera; he was punished by being reborn on Earth for having treasure-seeking Brahmins killed.
virūpita [ita] amnf virūpitā disfigured.
virūpin [in] m. ["having several appearances"] chameleon.

virūpaka [virūpaka] amnf virūpikā ugly, hideous; deformed | lit. [DKC.] np. of virūpaka "hideous", epith. of the rich merchant Va supālita; after being ruined by the prostitute Kāmamañjarī, he became a renunciant digambara.
vireka [act. viric] n. act of purging; intestinal evacuation.
virecana [act. viric] n. med. purge.
virecin [agt. viric] amnf virecinī that purges.
viroc [ca. viruc] v. [10] pr. (virocayati) to make shine.
