Conflict with (iic.). virodhīkṛ to oppose, revolt, object; obstruct; pick a quarrel. virodhāvirodhau nirūpayet We must examine whether or not there is a contradiction. virodhah so'virodhe'pi viruddhatvena yad vacah [Kāvyaprakāśa] The virodha is a contradictory statement, although there is no contradiction (by another interpretation).
Virodhakṛt [kṛt₂] amnf provoking revolt, sowing discord — m. enemy | astr. np. of Virodhakṛt "Conflict", son of Nāradī personifying year 45 of a life cycle [samvatsara].
virodhaparihāra [parihāra] m. withdrawal of an incom

vivarta [act. vivṛt] m. change, transformation; evolution; deviation | phil. [Vedānta] divine manifestation in the phenomenal world phil. [Bhartrhari] illusory appearance, emanation of the śabdatattva bringing forth the phenomenal world
apparent [asatya] without affecting the unity of reality
ultimate |satya|.

vivādārthin | arthin | amnf vivādārthinī pleading; procedural.

["abduction (of the bride from the paternal home)" ceremony [saṃskāra] of marriage, nuptial rite; 8 forms of marriage are recognized [astavivāha] | soc. marriage with (i.saha₂) | arch. np. of Vivāha, epith. of Shiva "celebrating marriage"; it is one of the 16 aspects of Shiva.

vivāhavidhi | vidhi | mr. soc. marriage rite.

viveka [act. vivic] m. separation, distinction, discrimination; Discernment, reasoning: discussion, investigation | myth. np. of Vi veka "Discernment", personifying Intelligence, son of Manas and Nivrtti | lit. np. of viveka₁ "Elucidation", advanced commentary of Hemacan dra to his Alamkāracūdāmaņi. iti vivekah gram. this is how one should distinguish. vivekacūdāmaņi [cūdāmaņi] m. phil. np. of Vivekacūdāmaņi "Supreme Flower of Discernment", philosophical work of Vedānta; it is attributed to Sankarācārya or later to Śaṃkarānanda; It comprises 580 verses in śārdūlavikrīdita meter.

viśas [viśas] v. [1] pr. (viśasati) pp. (viśasta) to cut up, dissect; to immolate, kill, destroy.
viśásana [agt. viśas] amnf viśasanā that causes death; mortal — m. sword — act. n. cutting, dissection | combat, carnage, murder, destruction | cruel treatment.

Viśākha [viśākhā] amnf viśākhā that forks, that branches | branchless; man chot — m. myth. np. of Viśākha "Horned", ram-headed being that sprang from Skanda's right side when Indra struck him with his thunderbolt [vajra]; this aspect of Skanda is associated with fertility, but considered dangerous for children; its symbol is the banyan tree; cf. Naigameșa — f. viśākhā bd. np. of viśākhā, a wealthy woman from Magadha who found enlightenment by listening to Buddha at the age of 7; she put her fortune at his service | du. viśākhe astr. np. of viśākhe "fork", 14th lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to a pair of stars in Libra; Indra and Agni together [Indrāgnī] preside there; its symbol is the arch decorated with a garland; also called viśākhā and later Rādhā₂.

viśākhadatta | datta | m. hist. np. of viśākhadatta, author of the historical drama Mudrārākṣasa; he was of royal family (of Bihāra) and lived around the 6th century; also known as Viśākhadeva, he is credited with the dramas Devīcandragupta and Abhisārikāvañcitaka.
Viśākhadeva | deva | mr. cf. viśākhadatta.
viśāya [act. viśī] m. turn to rest (alternating with a watch). tavādya viśāyaḥ it's your turn to sleep today. mama viśāyah it's my turn to sleep.
viśārada [viśāradā] amnf viśāradā gifted, skillful; Expert in, gifted in, skilled in (g. loc. iic.) | soc. n.p. from viśārada "Expert", scholar title. yuddhaviśāradaḥ skilled in combat.

Viśālā [viśāla] amnf Viśālā vast, spacious, great; important, eminent, Illustrious; then sant | myth. [Rām.] np. of King Viśāla "Illustrious", son of Ikṣvāku and Alambuṣā; he founded the city of Viśālā; Hemacandra₁ is his son — ifc. rich in, full of (iic.) — f. Viśālā myth. [Rām.] np. of the city of Viśālā, capital of King Viśāla, on the Gangā geo. np. of Viśālā₁, epith. of Ujjayinī the Illustrious. viśālam extensively; in abundance.

viśālākṣa [akṣa] amnf viśālākṣī who has large eyes — m. bio. owl | myth. epith. of Śiva | ventilating wall hollowed out in a checkerboard pattern, mou charabieh | arch. not. grid diagram with sides of 28, with 784 squares — f. viśālākṣī myth. np. of viśālākṣī "with large eyes", epith. of Kāśī devī, tutelary goddess |adhiṣṭhātrī| of Kāśī, who is his
pedestal | devīpītha |.

viśikha [viśikhā] amnf viśikhā without wick; bald | without tip, blunt (arrow) | flameless (fire) | astr. without tail (comet) — m. arrow — f. viśikhā small arrow; needle | bed. n.p. of viśikhā, confidante of Satyabhāmā.

viśiṣ [viśiṣ] v. [7] pr. (viśináṣṭi) pp. (viśiṣṭa) pfp. (viśesya) pf. (prati) to distinguish, to distinguish among (i.); to particularize; to place above (i.) | to distinguish oneself, to surpass — ps. (viśisyate) to be distinguished by (i.); to be distinguished from (abl. i.); to be superior to, to surpass, to excel. বিशিষ্ট viśiṣṭa [pp. viśiṣ] amnf viśiṣṭā dis tinct; distinguished, remarkable; noble, preeminent, excellent | phil. (object) specified by a word.
viśiṣṭajñāna [jñāna] n. phil. [NN.] qualifying cognition.
viśiṣṭatā [tā] f. particularity, specificity; distinction; excellence, superiority.
viśistatva [tva] n. id.
viśiṣṭanāmasūcī [nāma₁sūcī] f. name index.
viśiṣṭavidhāna [vidhāna] n. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] in distinguished interpretation of an injunction allows its interpretation as aiming at a single goal; opp. vākyabheda.
viśistavaiśistya [vaiśistya] n. phil. [Nyāya] the distinguished and the distinction. visistavaišistyāvagāhi [avagāhi] f. phil. [Nyāya] knowledge of the distinguished and the distinction.
viśiṣṭādvaita [advaita] n. phil. [vedānta] "distinguished non-duality", metaphysical position opposed to the undifferentiated non-duality of Sankara₁.
viśiṣṭādvaitavāda [vāda] m. phil. doctrine of "distinguished nonduality", preached by Rāmānuja; it affirms the supremacy of Kṛṣṇa over the impersonal brahman.
viśī [ viśī ₁] v. [2] pr. r. ( viśete ) v. [1] pr. r. (śayate) to be stretched out; to remain lying down | to doubt.
viśīrṇa [pp. viśṛ] amnf viśīrṇā broken, torn, crushed; scattered, destroyed; fallen (tooth).
viśuddha [pp. viśudh] amnf viśuddhā very pure; perfectly purified | completed — ifc. that has completed (iic.).

viśuddhacakra [cakra] n. phil. [Tantra] 5th cakra of tantric yoga, located at the level of the larynx; it is represented by a lotus of 16 mauve petals; a white circle in a triangle symbolizes the ether, and bears the bījamantra 'haṃ'; this cakra controls the sense of hearing; it is the psychic center of the Sacred Word.
viśuddhi [act. viśudh] f. purification; pu reté; virtue, holiness | rectification, correction | retribution, reimbursement | math. quantity to be subtracted.
Viśuddhimārga | mārga | mr. bd. the correct way | bed. n.p. of the Viśuddhimārga “path of purification” (Pāli Visuddhimagga) of Buddhaghoşa.
viśudh [viśudh] v. [4] pr. (viśudhyati) pr. r. (viśudhyate) pp. (viśuddha) to become perfectly pure — ca. (viśodhayati) to purify; justify, discul per.
viśuṣ [viśuṣ₁] v. [1] pr. (viśuṣyati) pr. r. (viśusyate) pp. (viśuska) to dry out completely; waste away — ca. (viśosayati) dry out completely.
viśṛ [viśṛ] ps. (viśīryate) pp. (viśīrṇa) to break, to wither, to fade | to be damaged, to be destroyed.

viśeṣa [act. viśiṣ] m. discrimination, difference; distinction, advantage; opp. sāmānya specification, particularity, characteristic species, category, type | phil. [Vaisesika] the category |padārtha| of discriminative substrates | frontal mark (indicating sect) | distinguished case, special case | gram. word specifying or limiting the meaning of another — f. viśeṣā ifc. difference between something (g. loc. i.) and something (g. loc. i.). viśeṣāt var. viśeṣeṇa adv. particularly, singularly; par excellence. viśesatas adv. singularly, extremely; principally, particularly, especially; rather — ifc. in proportion to, according to (iic.). giriviśesah a certain mountain. pușpaviśeșah a kind of flower. maṇiviśeṣaḥ a variety of jewel. rūpaviśesah distinguished beauty. atithiviśesah a distinguished guest. asti me viśeso'dya I feel better today. tasya narasya viśesam brūhi gives the description of this man.
viśeṣaguṇa | guṇa | m. phil. specific quality.
viśeṣajña [jña] amnf viśeṣajñā instructed ["who knows how to distinguish"].

viśeṣatantra [tantra] n. lit. teaching reserved for initiates; designates the saura, śaiva and pāñcarātra texts, those of the atimārga tradition, the Atharvaveda, the treatises of sāṃkhya and yoga, Buddhist and Jain scriptures, etc. the śaiva tradition distinguishes a more esoteric level, the viśeṣataraśāstra; opp. sāmānya.
viśeṣatara [tara] amnf viśeṣatarā compar. very distinguished; restricted.
viśeṣataraśāstra [śāstra] n. lit. esoteric śaiva teaching; it can only be transmitted by an initiate bound by the vows of his tradition | bd. set of texts of the Vajrayāna tradition.
viśeṣavat |vat| amnf viśeṣavatī which has special merits; excellent, eminent; superior to (abl.) | which pursues a particular goal.
viśeṣavidhāna [vidhāna] n. gram. prescription par ticular to a rule.
viśeṣasūtra [sūtra] n. gram. particular rule (opp. to general rule [utsargasūtra]).
viśesastava [stava] n. bed. n.p. of the Viśesastava, a hymn of glorification of the Buddha.
viśeṣārtha [artha] amnf viśeṣarthā whose object is particular — m. distinction; difference.
viśeṣārthatva [tva] n. fact that its object is particular.

viśesokti [ukti] f. lit. [alaṃkāra] A figure of speech in which the excellence of an object is indicated by its comparison with a prestigious object, while also highlighting the difference. dyūtamnāma purusasyāsimhāsanam rājyam lit. [MK.] The game of dice is truly to a man like sovereignty without a throne.

viśeṣaka [agt. viśiṣ] amnf viśeṣikā ifc. which specifies, which distinguishes (iic.); which characterizes (iic.) | gram. which determines, specifying (iic.) — n. distinction, difference; specification | distinctive mark; not. sectarian mark on the forehead [tilaka] | lit. figure of rhetoric, where the differences between two similar objects are detailed | lit. triplet of stanzas [śloka] syntactically connected.
viśesakacchedya [chedya] n. the ornamentation of the face by a tilaka, one of the 64 arts [kalā].

viśeṣaṇa [agt. viśiṣ] amnf viśeṣaṇā that distinguishes, that specifies — act. n. specification; distinctive mark, (sign of) distinction; excellence | phil. attribute, qualifier; predicate, specifier | gram. predicative attribute (epithet adjective or subordinate noun (about it [viśesya])); adjective, apposition; permanent qualifier (opp. upalakṣaṇa). viśeṣaṇīkṛ gram. to perform a predication.
viśeṣaṇatā [tā] f. phil. particularity; individuality; fact of being a specifier.
viśeṣaṇatāviśeṣa [viśeṣa] m. phil. [Nyāya] relation [sambandha] of specific qualification between the qualifier and the qualified; syn. svarūpasambandha.
viśeṣaṇatāsambandha [sambandha] m. gram. relation between the predicate and the subject.
viśeṣaṇatva [tva] n. cf. viśeṣaṇatā | gram. nature of adjective.
viśeṣaṇapūrvapada [pūrvapada] amnf viśeṣaṇapūrvapadā gram. qualifies karmadhāraya compounds whose left constituent is predicative (like dīrghakanthah). nīlotpalam blue lotus.
viśesanaviśesyabhāva | viśesyabhāva | m. relation between the qualifier and the qualified.
viśeṣaṇottarapada [uttarapada] amnf viśeṣaṇottarapadā gram. compound of the kar madhāraya type whose right constituent is predicative. vaiyākaranakhasūcih an incompetent grammarian.
viśeṣaṇobhayapada [ubhayapada] amnf viśeṣaṇobhayapadā gram. qualifies compounds kar madhāraya whose two constituents are coordinated adjectives (like snātānulipta). nīlalohitah purple.
viśeṣin [agt. viśiṣ] amnf viśeṣiṇī dis tinct, individual — ifc. who seeks to surpass (iic.).
viśeṣya [pfp. [1] viśiṣ] amnf viśeṣyā phil. (object) to be specified, to be determined — n. gram. substantive | gram. subject of a predication by an attri
but [viśesana].
viśesyatā |tā| f. the act of being specified, qualified or distinguished | gram. nature of noun.
viśesyatva [tva] n. id.
viśesyanighnavarga [nighnavarga] m. lit. section of the Sāmānyakānda, dealing with adjectives.
viśesyaviśesanabhāva [viśesanabhāva] m. gram. relation of subordination; dependence.
viśesyaviśesanabhāvavat |vat| amnf viśesyaviśesanabhāvavatī (phrase) exhibiting a dependency.
viśesyaka [agt. viśis़] ifc. amnf viśesyakā phil. [Nyāya] qualified by, determined by.
viśodh [ca. viśudh] v. [10] pr. (viśodhayati) to purify; to justify, to exonerate.
viśodhana [agt. viśudh] amnf viśodhanī that purifies, that cleanses — act. n. purification, cleansing (of (iic.)) | med. laxative.
viśodhanīya [pfp. [2] viśudh] amnf viśodhanīyā to purify; to clean; to rectify.
viśodhi iic. viśodhin.
viśodhitva |tva| ifc. n. purification, cleansing of (iic.).
viśodhin [agt. viśudh] amnf viśodhinī that cleans.
viśoṣa [act. viśuṣ] m. drought.
viśoṣaṇa [agt. viśuṣ] amnf viśoṣaṇā which dries out; drying — act. n. desiccation.

viśya [viś₂ya] amnf viśyā belonging to the community — m. soc. man of the 3rd class. विশ্বতথ viśrabdha [pp. viśrambh] amnf viśrabdhā confident; fearless, serene; calm, tranquil | trusting in (with prati) | inspiring confidence. viśrabdham adv. confidently; without reservations.

viśram [viśram] v. [4] pr. (viśrāmyati) v. [1] pr. r. (viśramate) pp. (viśrānta) to rest, to stop; to rely on (loc.) | to trust, to be at ease — ca. (viśrāmayati) to cause to rest, to stop — ps. (viśrāmyate) to be rested. viśramasva rest. viśrāmyatām (ps. imp.) enough! stop!
viśrama [act. viśram] m. rest, ease, relaxation.
viśrambh [viśrambh] v. [1] pr. r. (viśrambhate) pp. (viśrabdha, viśrambhita) to have confidence, to trust (loc.) — ca. (viśrāmbhayati) to inspire confidence, to reassure. viśrabhya ind. confident.

viśrambha [act. viśrambh] m. trust (in (loc. g. iic.) | familiarity; intimacy | relaxation, relaxation, loosening | relaxation posture, used by Vedic reciters for the grave accent |svarita| — f. viśrambhā ifc. trust in (iic.). viśrambhāt var. viśrambhena with complete trust. viśrambham kr to gain the trust of g. . viśrambhasthāne man to have complete trust in. kasmai viśrambham kathayāmi Whom should I trust? viśvāsaviśraṃbhabhūmiḥ sa mama He has my complete trust.
viśrambhatā [tā] f. confidence. viśrambhatām gam to gain the trust of.
viśrambhaṇa [act. viśrambh] ifc. n. the act of gaining the trust of (iic.). viśrambhanam gam to gain the trust of.
viśrambhaṇīya [pfp. [2] viśrambh] amnf viśrambhaṇīyā trustworthy; which inspires confidence in (l.).
viśrambhin [agt. viśrambh] amnf viśrambhiṇī who trusts (iic.) | who inspires confidence | confidential.
viśravaṇa [viśravaṇa₁] m. cf. viśravas.

viśravas [viśravas] m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Viśravā "the Most Glorious", son of Māninī by Pulastya angry to see his son Kubera neglect him in favour of his father Brahmā; Viśravā is Pulastya reincarnated to give birth to Kubera by Idavidā but also Rāvaņa, Kumbhakarņa, Khara and Vibhīsaņa by Keśinī₂.
viśrānta [pp. ca. viśram] amnf viśrāntā that rests, that has rested | stopped, finished.
viśrānti [act. That. viśram] f. rest; stop, cessation, end.
viśrām [ca. viśram] v. [10] pr. (viśrāmayati) to make rest, to stop.
viśrāma [act. viśram] m. rest, relaxation; calm, tranquility; vacation | catching one's breath after an effort | phon. silence at the end of a pāda (syn. yati₃).
viśrāmakāla | kāla₁ | m. mod. holiday period, vacation.
viśri [viśri] v. [1] pr. (viśrayati) pr. r. (viśrayate) ved. open, spread.
viśru [viśru] v. [5] pr. (viśṛṇóti) pp. (Viśruta) to hear distinctly, to understand — ps. (viśrūyate) to be renowned.

Viśruta [pp. viśru] amnf viśrutā well known, renowned — n. renown | good understanding; knowledge, wisdom — m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Viśruta "Expert", son of the minister Padmodbhava and Sindhudattā, one of the 10 heroes of the Daśakumāracarita; after their separation, he saw a young boy near a well into which an old man had fallen; the latter, Nālījangha, told him of the ruin of King Anantavarmā₁, and that the boy was Prince Bhāskaravarmā; he realized that the prince's mother and his own father had the same paternal grandfather, and he took him under his protection; he restored him to his father's throne, and married Princess Mañjuvādinī. damayantī iti viśrutā It is called damayantī.
viśrutavat [vat] amnf viśrutavatī very learned, erudite.
viśruti [act. viśru] f. fame, celebrity. viśrutim gam to achieve celebrity.
viśliṣ [viśliṣ] ca. (viśleṣayati) pp. (viśliṣṭa) separate from (abl.); deprive of (i.). ਕਿਲਿੲ viśliṣṭa [pp. viśliṣ] amnf viśliṣṭā separated, disjointed; set aside; dislocated; dissolved.
viślisya [abs. viślis] ind. having separated from.
viśleṣa [act. viśliṣ] m. separation, dissolution [sandhiviślesa] gram. hiatus; absence of |sandhi| connection.
viśleṣaka [agt. viśliṣ] amnf viśleṣikā that separates; that dissolves — f. viślesikā gram. morphological analysis.

viśleṣaṇa [agt. viśliṣ] amnf viśleṣaṇā dissolved, separated — act. n. separation; dissolution gram. analysis of sandhi. বিষ্য víśva pn. mnf viśvā all, total, in thirds; universal | omnipresent, which contains all | phil. [Vedānta] np. of viśva, awakened aspect of consciousness; cf. Vaiśvānara — n. viśva the World — f. viśvā the Earth.

viśvakarman [karman] m. myth. np. of the god Viśvakarmā "who made everything", architect of the universe, craftsman of the gods, form of Agni, also called Tvaștā (or considered as a son of Tvașțā); he is father of Sañjñā; he shaved off one-eighth of the Sun's brightness to lessen it, and from it made the discus [cakra] of Vișnu, the trident [triśūla] of Shiva, and the spear [śakti] of Skanda; he made the marvelous chariot Puspaka for Kubera; he made two marvelous bows; he gave the first [Pināka] to Shiva to destroy Tripura, and the second [Sāraṅga] to Viṣṇu; The gods wanted to test their supremacy, and Brahmā arbitrated a duel between Shiva and Vishnu, from which the latter emerged victorious thanks to his war cry hum | soc. artisan.

Viśvaguṇādarśa [guṇaādarśa] m. lit. np. from Viśvaguṇādarśa "Mirror of all qualities", a satirical poem in campū style by Venkaṭādhvarī; it features the two gandharvās Kṛśānu and Viśvāvasu crossing the Tamil country aboard a celestial chariot.

viśvajit [jit] amnf who conquers all | myth. sacrifice of omnipotence; the magician Sukra performed it for the benefit of the king of demons [asura] Bali to give him sovereignty over the three worlds soc. expiatory sacrifice (gift of all his possessions); cf. sarvamedha. viśvajitā yajeta the viśvajit sacrifice must be accomplished (by one who aspires to Heaven [svargakāma]).
Viśvanagara [nagara] m. lit. np. of the beggar Viśvanagara "Urban prowler" in the comedy Dhūrtasamāgama.

viśvanātha [nātha] m. geo. np. of viśvanātha "Universal Lord", one of the 12 radiant signs of Shiva [jyotirlinga]; he is associated with his śakti An napūrņā; his shrine at Vārāṇasī was destroyed by Aurangzeb in 1669; the modern temple dates from 1780, it is covered in gold | geo. np. of the secondary linga of Rāmeśvara; cf. rāmalingeśvara | hist. np. of Viśvanātha₁ Kavirāja, poet of the Kalinga, son of a court dignitary in the early 14th century; he is the author of the poetic treatise Sāhityadarpaṇa; He defined poetry as the art of seasoning the sentence with taste [rasa]; he wrote a commentary on the Kāvyaprakāśa | hist. np. of the Bengali logician Viśvanātha₂ Pañcānana Bhaṭṭācārya (17th century); he is the author of the Bhāṣāpariccheda, also called Kārikāvalī, and its commentary the Muktāvalī; he is also credited with the customary treatise |smṛti| Māṃsatattvaviveka | hist. np. of the scholar Viśvanātha₃ of the Vidarbha (17th century); he is responsible for the eulogies Satruśalyacarita and Jagatprakāśa, as well as the dictionary Koşakalpadruma | hist. np. of the Telugu scholar Viśvanātha₄ (early 17th century), theorist of the mystical rasa.
viśvapā [pā₃] m. myth. np. of viśvapā "Universal Protector", epith. of Vișnu.
viśvaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. np. from viśvaprakāśa, important dictionary of mononyms due to Maheśvarakavi (1112); cf. Sabdabhedaprakāśa.

Viśvamitra [mitra] amnf viśvamitrā friend of all — m. myth. n.p. from Visvamitra; cf. Viśvāmitra. viśvamitrasya raksati brahmedam bharatam janam [RV.] This word of Viśvamitra protects the nation of Bharata.

Viśvarūpa [rūpa] amnf Viśvarūpā Multiform, universal | changing, multicolored (said of multicolored jewels by diffraction) — m. ved. np. of Viśvarūpa, epithet of the three-headed monster Triśirā Tvāṣṭra | myth. np. of Viśvarūpa₁, epithet of the cosmic form of Vișnu "Multiform"; he is represented with 3 heads of man, lion and boar, and 10 arms, or with a multitude of heads BhG. cosmic form of Kṛṣṇa revealing himself to Arjuna | hist. np. of Viśvarūpa₂ Miśra, elder brother of Caitanya; renouncing the arranged marriage by his parents, he became sannyāsin under the name of Sankararanya Svāmī; he ended his life in Pandharpur; in the bhakti tradition, he embodies Balarāma | hist. np. of Viśvarūpa₃, author of the Bālakrīdā, commentary on the Yājñavalkyasmṛti (9th century).
víśvarūpadarśana [darśana] n. phil. vision of the Multiform God; divine vision granted by Kṛṣṇa to Arjuna in the 11th chapter of the Gītā.
víśvarūpamahotsava [mahotsava] m. soc. day an nversary of the vow of renunciation |sannyāsin| of Viśvarūpa₂.

víśvalocanakośa [locanakośa] n. lit. np. from the dictionary Viśvalocana "Complete Examination" by Srīdharasena (late 12th century); it includes a section of synonyms and another of homonyms; it was translated into Tibetan; also called Muktāvalī₁.
víśvavasu | vasu | mr. myth. n.p. of Viśvavasu, 4th son of Jamadagni.

víśvavāra | vāra | amnf viśvavārā which grants all treasures | beloved of all — f. viśvavārā expo sition, exhibition. sa prathamā saṃskṛtirviśvavārā [SB.] This is the first consecration (of soma), which grants all benefits.
viśvavidyālaya [vidyālaya] m. university.
viśváścandra [ścandra] amnf viśvaścandrā which shines from everywhere.
viśvasaṃskṛtadina [saṃskṛtadina] n. soc. "day of Sanskrit", celebrated at the full moon śrāvaṇī.

viśvāntara [antara] m. bd. [VJ.] np. of the king viśvāntara "Close to all" (pāli Vessantara), in previous incarnation of the Buddha; prince banished from his kingdom, he abandoned all his possessions, including his wife and two children, in order to free himself from all ties; but Indra intervened, reunited them, and reinstated viśvāntara at his father's court.
Viśvāntarajātaka [jātaka] n. bed. [bd.] np. of the Viśvāntarajātaka, which tells the story of viśvāntara as a previous manifestation of the Buddha.

Viśveśvara₁ [īśvara] m. myth. n.p. of Viśveśvara₁ "Universal God", epith. by Viśvanātha | hist. n.p. of Viśveśvara₁, court poet of Singabhūpāla II in Telangāna (14th century); he is the author of the Camatkāracandrikā, the Aryāsaptaśatī and the Alamkārakaustubha.
viśvaksena m. cf. vișvaksena.
viśvátas [adv. viśva] adv. from all sides; universellement. viśvato bhayāt out of all danger.
viśvátomukha [mukha] amnf viśvatomukhā oriented in all directions; universal. viśvatomukham adv. in all directions.

viśvam [acc. viśva] iic. viśvaṃbhara var. viśvambhara [bhara] amnf viśvambharā who supports all (qualifies not. the Supreme Being) — m. hist. np. of viśvambhara Miśra, birth name of Caitanya — f. viśvaṃbharā the Earth.
viśvas [viśvas₁] v. [2] pr. (viśvásiti) pp. (viśvásita) to have confidence in (g. loc.); to be reassured — ca. (viśvāsayati) to reassure, to inspire confidence in (acc.); to console, to encourage.
viśvasana [act. viśvas] n. act of trusting.
viśvasanīya [pfp. [2] viśvas] amnf viśvasanīyā trustworthy; reliable; credible — n. (impers.) he must be trusted.
viśvasanīyatā [tā] f. confidence; reliability; credibility.
viśvasanīyatva [tva] n. id.
viśvasita [pp. viśvas] amnf viśvasitā full of assurance; without fear; without suspicion | of confidence; credible, believed.

viśvasta [related to viśvasita] amnf viśvastā full of assurance; without fear; without suspicion | trustworthy; reliable, faithful — f. viśvastā widow. viśvastam confident; without apprehension. বিশ্বা viśvā [viśva] iic. (ifc.) of All.
viśvānara [nara] amnf viśvānarā common to all men | np. of an ascetic.
viśvāpuṣ [puṣ₂] amnf ved. at the origin of everything.

viśvāmitra [mitra] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of viśvāmitra "Friend of All", one of the seven sages [saptarși], son of King Gādhi, of gotra Kauśika; when his elder sister Princess Satyavatī₁ married the Brahmin Rcīka, she asked her father-in-law Bhrgu for a rite to allow her and her mother to have a son; these would be Jamadagni and viśvāmitra respectively, but a ritual error caused confusion of castes [varṇasaṃkara]; kṣatriya of the descendants of Purūravā, of the race of bharatās, he ruled over Kanyākubja when his father retired to the hermitage of Rcīka; He married Madhavi, with whom he had a son, Aṣṭaka; he opposed the brāhmaṇa Vasistha, from whom he attempted to abduct Nandinī; in order to become a brāhmaṇa himself, for the sake of power, he performed penances for thousands of years; he then realized the destiny of brahmarși that the ritual error had allowed, and he became the guru of Rāma; he allowed himself to be seduced by the nymph [apsaras] Me nakā, who bore him Sakuntalā, but resolved to resume his penances; the essential part of the Rigveda is attributed to him; he symbolizes will, perseverance, and longevity; cf. Kauśika, Gālava, Jāhnava, Triśańku, Śālańkāyana, Śunaḥśepha, Hariścandra — f. viśvāmitrī geo. np. of the viśvāmitrī river, north of the Narmadā; it is renowned for the
banyan trees [vata] from its banks; cf. Vatapattra.
viśvārāj | rāj₂ | mr. | sg. name. viśvārāt | emperor.

viśvāvasu [vasu] amnf universal benefactor, said of Viṣṇu — m. myth. n.p. of viśvāvasu, giant Gandharvadānava king of prodigious beauty; Pramadvarā is his daughter by Menakā; |Rām.| he challenged Indra to fight, who transformed him into the monstrous ogre | rākṣasa | Kabandha; Rāma killed him, and freed him from his spell by burning him | astr. n.p. of viśvāvasu "Colossus", personifying year 39 of a |samvatsara| life cycle.
viśvās [ca. viśvas] v. [10] pr. (viśvāsayati) abs. (viśvāsya) to reassure, to inspire confidence in acc. .
viśvāsa [act. viśvas] m. trust (in (loc.); faith in (loc. i. iic.) | confidential communication, secret.
viśvāsaghāta |ghāta| m. breach of trust, betrayal of one's.
viśvāsaghātaka | ghātaka | amnf viśvāsaghātikā traitor.
viśvāsaprada | prada | amnf viśvāsapradā which gives confidence.
viśvāsasthāna | sthāna | n. | "place of trust" | ga rantie; hostage. caturah śaśakān viśvāsasthāne dhṛtvā having held 4 hares hostage.
viśvāsin [agt. viśvās] amnf viśvāsinī in confidence | trustworthy; reliable; honest.
viśvāsya [pfp. [1] viśvās] amnf viśvāsyā trustworthy | who should be reassured — abs. ind. having put in confidence.
viśve [nom. pl. viśva] iic.
viśvedeva [deva] m. pl. myth. np. of the collective Viśvedevās, "All the gods"; astr. they preside over the nakṣatra of the Uttarāṣāḍhās (sigma of Sagittarius).

√ ₁ v. [3] pr. (vivesti) pf. (pari) to be active, to act; to do, to accomplish — v. [1] pr. (véșati) to be rapid, to flow; to flow (water); to serve (servant) — ca. (vesayati) to serve — intens. (vevesti) to impregnate.
viş₂ f. [nom. vit] excrement, garbage.
víṣa [agt. viṣ₁] m. ved. servant — n. [“that which acts quickly”] poison, venom — v. [11] pr. r. (viṣāyate) to act like a poison || gr. o ; lat. virus. viṣībhūta poisoned (not. food).
víṣakanyā [kanyā] f. soc. bait girl, causing the death of whoever succumbs to her charms.
vísakrta | kṛta | amnf viṣakṛtā poisoned.

víṣaghna [ghna] amnf viṣaghnā which fights poison; antidote. vișacikitsita | cikitsita | n. med. n.p. of the Vișacikitsita, section of the Carakasamhitā dealing with poisons. vișapuccha [puccha] mf vișapucchī bio. ["whose tail carries poison" | Scorpio.
visávat [vat] amnf visavatī poisonous, poisoned — adv. like poison. viṣayān viṣavattyaja rejects sense objects like poison.
viṣavidyā [vidyā] f. science of poisons and antidotes.
visavega [vega] m. effect of the poison.
vísavaidya [vaidya] m. snakebite healer; seller of poison antidote; syn. jāngulika | lit. poison treatment book.
viṣaśāstra [śāstra] n. science of poisons and venoms; toxicology.
viṣahīna |hīna| amnf viṣahīnā non-venomous (not. snake).
viṣādin₁ |ādin| amnf viṣādinī who eats poison.
viṣānna | anna | n. poisoned arrow.
viṣāpaha [apaha] amnf viṣāpahā that cures from poison — m. antidote | myth. epith. of Garuda. mantrair viṣāpahaiḥ by antidote charms.
viṣāpahāra [apahāra] m. antidote — f. viṣāpahārā f. viṣāpahārī myth. epith. of Manasā "that which protects from poison".
viṣāpahāradaṇḍa |daṇḍa| m. soc. magic wand to destroy poison.
viṣāpahārastotra [stotra] n. bed. from np. Jain viṣāpahārastotra devotional poem by Dhanañjaya₁.
viṣāstra | astra | n. poisoned food. vișin |in| amnf vișinī poisoned. vișaușadhi [oṣadhi] f. organic. toxic plant | bed. n.p. of the Viśauṣadhi, commentary by Vallabhadeva of the Siśupālavadha.
viṣakta [pp. viṣañj] amnf viṣaktā sus hanging from ; attached to (loc.) | directed towards (loc. iic.) supported on, dependent on (iic.).

viṣañj [visañj] v. [1] pr. (viṣajati) pp. (viṣakta) to hang from | to head towards (loc.) — pr. r. (viṣajjate) to be attached to, to be suspended from (loc.) phil. to be attached to the phenomenal world | to be held by; to have on one's heels (i.).
viṣaṇṇa [pp. viṣad] amnf viṣaṇṇā sad, downcast, depressed.
viṣaṇṇatā [tā] f. weariness, sadness, depression.
viṣaṇṇatva |tva| n. cf. viṣaṇṇatā.

viṣad [visad₁] v. [1] pr. (viṣīdati) pft. (viṣasāda) pp. (viṣaṇṇa) to be exhausted, to be dejected; depress — ca. (viṣādayati) pp. (viṣādita) to despair, to despair. viṣīdantam adv. dejected, depressed. viṣīdan idam abravīt While lamenting, he said this.
viṣama [visama] amnf viṣamā rough, harsh; uneven, irregular; crude, harsh | different; inconsistent | difficult, awkward, painful; incongruous; unpleasant, bad; painful; angry,

dangerous | math. odd | that which does not divide (like a living animal) | adverse; inadequate, incomprehensible, erroneous; partial, dishonest — n. roughness; irregularity; difficulty, misfortune; difficult situation; wrong path, danger. visamena adv. unequally. viṣamapādāntalaghu phon. poetic license allowing a short syllable at the end of an odd-numbered line in certain meters.
āśīviṣaviṣavegaviṣamaḥ [K.] painful like the effect of the poison of a venomous snake (describes the arrows of Kāma, torments of love).
visamakālīna [kālīna] amnf viṣamakālīnā asynchronous; opp. samakālīna.
viṣamanetra [netra] m. myth. ["with an odd number of eyes"] epith. of SivaTrilocana.
viṣamapada [pada] amnf viṣamapadā (che min) difficult to progress | lit. (stance) having irregular feet. viṣamapadavimarśinī ṭīkā commentary explaining the difficulties.
visamalocana [locana] m. myth. epith. by Siva Trilocana.
viṣamavṛtta [vṛtta] amnf viṣamavṛttā phon. (meter) heterosyllabic; opp. samavrtta.
viṣamastha [stha] amnf viṣamasthā ["who lives in difficult conditions"] unhappy; opp. samastha.
viṣamākṣara [akṣara] m. lit. refers to a form of vilomakāvya in which the verse and its mirror image are different; opp. samākṣara. vişamānka [anka] m. math. odd number; opp. samānka.

viṣaya [act. viṣi] m. domain, territory, space; field of perception, sphere of influence; scope | object, purpose, matter | that which is accessible to the senses; perception; enjoyment, pleasure | phil. rhet. tangible material object opposed to its figurative representation; object opposed to the subject; not. one of the five objects of the senses | pañcaviṣayāh|: śabda sound, sparśa tactile sensation, rūpa form, rasa taste and gandha smell | object proper to (dat. g. 11th century) | phil. subject of a comparison; opp. viṣayin | phil. [NN.] the perceived; object of cognitive perception — f. viṣayā ifc. that which concerns, that which pertains to (11th century). viṣaye with regard to (11th century). viṣayīkṛ to seize, to grasp ⟨acc.⟩. viṣayībhū to become the domain of (g.). alpavisaya amn of limited scope. atra vişaye adv. in this respect. yathāyam ghaṭa iti jñāne ghaṭatvam viṣayaḥ Thus, for a pot, its perception consists in the knowledge one has of its quality as a pot.
viṣayaka |ka| ifc. amnf viṣayakā which concerns (iic.) | phil. [Nyāya] (knowledge) concerning (iic.).
viṣayakatā [tā] f. phil. [Nyāya] quality of knowledge of (iic.). vişayakatva [tva] n. phil. id.
viṣayatā [tā] f. phil. rhet. relation between an object and the knowledge one has of it | phil. [NN.] state of perception, semantics; fact of being understood.
Viṣayatāvāda [vāda] m. bed. [Nyāya] np. of Vișayatāvāda, treatise on cognitives by Harirāma Tarkālankāra, philosopher of the 16th century.
viṣayatva [tva] n. cf. viṣayatā — ifc. restriction to, fact of appearing only in (iic.). vișayapati [pati] m. soc. governor, territorial official.

viṣayabhoga | bhoga₂ | m. pleasure of the senses | phil. enjoyment of the phenomenal world. vişayavişayibhāva [vişayinbhāva] m. phil. [Nyāya] relation between an object and the perception one has of it.
viṣayasaptamī [saptamī] f. gram. locative in a spatial sense; opp. parasaptamī.

viṣayasūcī [sūcī] f. lit. table of contents. vișayin [in] amnf vișayinī (man) sensual ["attached to the pleasures of the senses"]; materialist | lit. figurative meaning; object of a comparison; opp. visaya phil. cognitive subject figurative representation (opp. real object) — n. ifc. phil. [Nyāya] knowledge [jñāna] of an object (iic.). vișayaișin [eșin] amnf vișayaișinī given to the pleasures of the senses | occupied with worldly affairs.
vişayi iic. vişayin.
viṣayitā [tā] f. phil. [navyanyaaya] cognitive state, the act of perceiving.
visayitva [tva] n. id.
viṣah [visah₁] v. [1] pr. r. (visahate) to conquer, dominate, surpass | to be able to, to be capable of (inf.) | to resist, to bear, to endure.
vişahya [pfp. [1] vişah] amnf vişahyā bearable, tolerable; which can be resisted possible, feasible (av. kartum).
viṣāṇa n. horn; tusk (of the elephant); claws (of a crab) | summit, peak (of a mountain) | nipple | best of its class — f. viṣāṇā ifc. horn of (iic.).
viṣāṇin |in| amnf viṣāṇinī (animal) horned.
viṣāda [act. viṣad] m. dejection, discouragement, weariness, depression; desolation, despair | disgust, aversion. viṣādena with discouragement. viṣādaṃ kṛ to show aversion.
viṣādana [agt. viṣad] amnf viṣādanā depressing, desolate — act. n. desolation, despair.
viṣādaśalya [śalya] mn suffering of despair. uddhrtavisādaśalya amn having plucked out the thorn of despair.
viṣādita [pp. That. viṣad] amnf viṣāditā that one despaired.
viṣādin² [agt. viṣad] amnf viṣādinī depressed, discouraged; desperate.
viṣāditā [tā] f. discouragement; despair.
viṣāditva [tva] n. id.
viṣi [visi] pp. (viṣita) to untie, to loosen.
víṣita [pp. viṣi] amnf viṣitā released; freed relieved (said of the Sun just before its dear neck).
vișu [related to viśva] iic. on both sides, in all directions; also, in equal parts.

vísuna [na] amnf visunā varied; multiple; different | changing; not. said of the Moon | unfavorable to (abl.) — m. astr. equinox. a separate view; as an aside. vișuvat [vat] amnf vișuvatī which shares, median, central — m. soc. central day of great sacrifice [sattra] | equinox | phil. [Tantra] point of balance of breathing between exhalation [prāṇa] and inspiration [apāna]; opp. abhijit | var. vișuva f. vișuvā id.
viṣūcī [f. viṣvac] f. cholera.

viṣūcīkā [ka] f. cholera | myth. his personification Visūcīkā; cf. Karkatī. vişūcīke tvam himavantam gaccha (cholera healing hymn) O Mother of Cholera, go to the Himalayas. বিষ্কান্থ viṣkabdha [pp. viṣkambh] amnf viskabdhā fixed, supported.
√ viṣkambh [viskambh] v. [5] pr. (viṣkabhnoti) v. [9] pr. (viṣkabhnāti) pp. (viṣkabdha) to support; to throw; to escape — ca. (viṣkabhāyati) to attach firmly.

viskambha [agt. viskambh] m. support; pi to bind; post, column | bar of a door; obstacle math. diameter of a circle | lit. (theatre) interlude, introductory prologue to a scene explaining the progress of the action in the interval.
viṣkambhaparvata [parvata] m. chain of my tagnes.
viṣkambhaka [agt. viṣkambh] amnf viṣkambhikā who supports — m. lit. (theatre) in interlude, introduction.
viṣkambhaṇa [act. viṣkambh] n. obstruction.
viṣkambhin [agt. viṣkambh] amnf viṣkambhinī that prevents, that forms an obstacle — m. lock or bar of a door.

viṣkira [agt. vikṛ] amnf viṣkirā that scatters, that scatters; that scratches the ground — m. bio. zoo. gallinaceous bird; quail, partridge, fowl. vișkirarasa [rasa] m. chicken broth. বিষ্ট viṣṭá [pp. viś₁] amnf viṣṭā entered into, contained in (acc. loc.) | into which one has entered | filled or accompanied by (i.). brāhmaņena devālayo vistah var. brāhmaņo devālayam viṣṭaḥ the Brahmin entered the temple.
viṣṭapa [viṣṭambh] n. summit; World, sky. vistape to the sky. বিষ্টভথ viṣṭabdha [pp. viṣṭambh] amnf vistabdhā fixed, rigid | stopped, restricted; paralyzed.

viṣṭambh [vistambh] v. [9] pr. (viṣṭabhnāti) pp. (vistabdha) consolidate, strengthen, fortify; stiffen | stuff something (acc.) with (i.) — ca. (viṣṭambhayati) pp. (viṣṭambhita) stop, immobilize, fix.
viṣṭambha [act. viṣṭambh] m. consolidation, strengthening; fixation | support | immobilization; suppression, obstruction | med. ischuria; constipation; paralysis.
viṣṭambhakara |kara₁| amnf viṣṭambhakarā that stops, that obstructs.

viṣṭambhita [pp. ca. viṣṭambh] amnf vistambhitā stopped, immobilized, fixed. বিষ্টি viṣṭi [act. viṣɪ] f. service, work; forced labor, slavery | (collective) class of servants, slaves | astr. seventh lunar half-day | karana | (mobile). বিষ্ঠা viṣṭhā₁ var. viṣṭā [related to viṣ₁] f. excrement, filth. visthām kr var. visthām dhā to defecate. বিষ্ঠা viṣṭhā₂ [visthā₁] v. [1] pr. r. (vitiṣṭhate) pp. (visthita) to be distant; to be diffuse or dispersed; to be separated from (i.).
viṣṭhita [pp. viṣṭhā₂] amnf viṣṭhitā distant; scattered.
Viṣṇu [agt. viṣ₁] m. myth. Vedic. aspect of the sun, radiant younger son of Aditi [āditya]; later, noun referring to the supreme god Viṣnu "the Immanent"; his 10 ma

The avatars [daśāvatārās] are traditionally Matsya the Fish who saved Man from the flood, Kūrma the Tortoise, the foundation of Creation, Varāha the Boar, savior of the Earth, Narasimha the Lion-Man, Vāmana Trivikrama the Brahman, Dwarf and Cosmic Giant, Parasurāma Rāma the Axe-Warrior, the perfect King Rāma, Ba larāma Rāma the Strong, the Black God Kṛṣṇa his brother, and Kalkī the future Horseman of the Apocalypse; sometimes Buddha is included as an avatar; the Eagle Garuda is his mount, Lakṣmī and Bhūdevī his wives; he dwells in the Vaikuntha heaven; its 24 aspects [upavyūha] carry with their 4 arms the 24 per mutations of 4 attributes: the fire disk |cakra|, the conch [śaṅkha], the mace [gadā] and the lotus [padma]; [Rūpamaṇḍana] they are named Keśava, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava, Govinda, Mokṣada, Madhu sūdana, Trivikrama, Vāmana, Srīdhara Hṛṣīkeśa, Varada, Dāmodara, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Vāsudeva, Pra dyumna, Aniruddha, Purusottama, Adhoksaja, Narasimha, Acyuta, Janārdana, Upendra, Hari and Kṛṣṇa; other aspects are named Cakrapāṇi, Jagannātha, Padmanābha, Pītavāsā, Prajāgara, Pratardana, Bhagavān, Mohinī, Vikuntha, Vibhu, Viśvarūpa₁, Venkateśvara, Śrīnivāsa; [BhP.] its manifestation is white in kṛtayuga, red in tretāyuga, yellow in dvāparayuga and black in ka liyuga; its attributes are the jewel Kaustubha, the mace scepter Kaumodakī, the disc Sudarśana, the conch Pāñcajanya, the bow Śṛṅga, the sword Nandaka, the curl of hair Śrīvatsa; The sacred basil [tulasī] is consecrated to him, as is the ammonite [śālagrāma]; depicted as an emperor, he wears the tiara of glory [kīrtimukuṭa]; he is dressed in yellow [Pītāmbara]; astrologically, he regents the nakṣatra Śravaṇā (Altaïr); philosophically, [Sāṃkhya] he is the regent [niyantr] of the faculty of
walk [pāda]; Viṣṇu amazes the world by the
play [līlā] of his Magic [Māyā]; he obtained from Siva to in carner Sakti; cf. tejolinga. vișnūyate dvijam he treats the Brahmin like Visnu.
vísnukavaca | kavaca | mn myth. np. of the shield of invincibility Vișnukavaca; cf. Sankhacūda.
Visnukhanda | khanda | min reads. n.p. of Viṣṇukhaṇḍa, section of Skandapurāṇa.
visnugupta | gupta | mr. hist. n.p. of Visnugupta, minister of Candragupta Maurya; he is often identified with Kautilya Cānakya. víșnutva [vat] n. essence of Vișnu.
viṣṇudūta [dūta] m. myth. emissary of Viṣṇu, class of beings in the service of Vișnu.
viṣṇudharma [dharma] m. soc. rite of śrāddha | bed. n.p. of viṣṇudharma; cf. Viṣṇudharmottara.

Viṣṇudharmottara | uttara₁ | n. |viṣṇudharmottarapurāṇa| lit. of the noun visnudharmottara, an upapurāṇa; it discusses the sciences and arts [śilpaśāstra] and notably gives the rules for celebrating Hindu festivals; it contains a chapter on poetics |alamkāra|, and a Citrasūtra section on painting; it was compiled between 450 and 650. vișnupada | pada | n. foot of Vișnu | geo. np. of the temple of Vișnupada at Gayā; cf. Gayāsura. vișnupura | pura | n. geo. np. of Vișnupura "City of Viṣṇu" — f. Viṣṇupurī geo. np. of Viṣṇupurī, third of the Omkāreśvara site.

viṣṇupurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. of the viṣṇupurāṇa [VP.], mythological collection of Vaishnava obedience, one of the six virtuous books |sāttvika|; similar to the model pañcalakṣaṇa, it comprises 6 parts: creation of the universe, royal genealogies, Veda and duties of the castes, chronicles of the dynasties, life of Kṛṣṇa, and dissolution of the worlds, according to the teaching of Parāśara.

viṣṇubali [bali] m. soc. ["offering to Viṣṇu"] rite performed in the 8th month of pregnancy, allowing the birth of the child as a vaikhānasa. mahāpurāṇa cf. vișnumahāpurāņa n. vișņupurāņa. vișnumitra | mitra | m. np. Vișnumitra "Friend of Vișnu", prototype character used in rhetoric, like Devadatta and Yajñadatta.

Viṣṇuvardhana [vardhana] m. hist. np. of the Hoysala king Viṣṇuvardhana (12th century); he reigned from 1108 to 1152, fought the Western Cālukya Empire and broke free from it by creating the Hoysala Empire; of Jaina origin, he converted to the worship of Viṣnu under the influence of Rāmānujācārya and commissioned many temples in Belūr, Halebidu, Melukote and Pandharpur; his son Narasimha₁ succeeded him.
viṣṇuśarman [śarman] m. hist. np. from the Brahman Vișnuśarmā "in the joy of Vișnu", narrator and presumed author of the Pañcatantra (6th century).
viṣṇusahasranāman [sahasranāman] n. myth. the thousand names of Vișnu — iic. vișnusahasranāma of the thousand names of Vișnu.
Viṣṇusahasranāmastotra |stotra| n. bed. n.p. of the Viṣṇusahasranāmastotra or litany of the thousand names of Viṣṇu; |Mah.| Bhīṣma revealed it to Yudhiṣṭhira during his agony

viṣṇusūkta |sūkta| n. ved. hymn 1. 154 of the Rgveda establishing the primacy of Vișnu. vișnusena [senā] m. hist. n.p. of King Vișnusena of the Maitraka dynasty in Gujarat (around 600). vișnusmrti [smrti] f. bed. n.p. of the Vișnusmrti, collection of Vishnuite laws [dharmaśāstra] of Kaśmīra.
Viṣṇvardha [ardha] m. arch. np. of Viṣṇvardha, epith. of Shiva "half Viṣṇu"; it is one of the 16 aspects of Shiva.
vişvak iic. vişvac.

Visvaksena [senā] m. myth. np. of Visvaksena or Viśvaksena, epithet of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa "who makes his powers felt everywhere" | myth. np. of Vișvaksena₁, guard of Viṣṇu's palace; Shiva killed him with his three teeth after cutting off Brahmā's head, in order to meet Vișnu to ask his forgiveness. [HV.] np. of Visvaksena₁, son of Brahmadatta.
viṣvaksenasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. np. of the Vișvaksenasamhitā, work of the pāñcarātra doctrine.
viṣvac var. viṣvañc [viṣuac] amnf viṣūcī [m. nom. vișvai; n. nom. vișvak] turned in all (or both) directions; which goes in all directions — f. cf. viṣūcī. vișvak adv. in all directions, everywhere.
viṣvadryac var. viṣvadryañc [viṣuac] amnf vişvadrīcī [m. nom. vişvadryan; n. nom. visvadryak in all directions; everywhere present. visvadryak adv. in all directions, everywhere.

visaṃvad [visaṃvad] v. [1] pr. (visamvadati) pp. (visamudita) to go back on one's promise, to break one's word | to contradict, to raise an objection. phale visamvadati it fails to bear fruit. tasyācaraṇam vacasā na visamvadati His conduct does not contradict his words.
visaṃvāda [act. visaṃvad] m. breach of one's word; contradiction; objection to (i. loc. iic.).
visamvādaka [agt. visamvad] amnf visaṃvādikā who breaks his word; who contradicts.
visaṃvādita [pp. ca. visaṃvad] amnf visamvāditā disappointed, dissatisfied | disagreeing; contradicting. ramanīyo'vadhirvidhinā visamvāditah a satisfactory conclusion was contradicted by fate.
visaṃvādin [agt. visaṃvad] amnf visamvādinī who does not keep his word, perjurer; who deceives; deceiver | contradictor.
visaṃvāditā [tā] f. breach of one's word, by oath.
visaṃvāditva |tva| n. id.
visaṃjña [visaṃjñā₂] amnf visaṃjñā unconscious, outside of oneself.
vísaṃdhi var. visandhi [visaṃdhi] amnf without euphonic juncture — m. gram. absence or error of sandhi.
vísamdhika [ka] amnf visamdhikā gram. (text) where the sandhi has not been performed.
visara [act. visr] m. flow, emission; dispersion, spreading | quantity, multitude, abundance dance.

visargá [act. visṛj] m. emission, launching (not. of arrow); liberation, repudiation; procreation phil. creation of the world of rite | phon. alteration of 's' and 'r' before voiceless consonants and in finals, into a muffled breath followed by a vowel resonance; it is represented by 'h' in transcription; sometimes a distinction is made between the guttural form [jihvāmūlīya] before 'k' and 'kh' and the bilabial form [upadhmānīya] before 'p' and 'ph' | phil. [Abhinavagupta] creation in three modes: emergent [kunda] identified with Shakti, quiescent or reabsorbing [linga] identified with Shiva and their supreme union [saṃghāṭa] arising from their indescribable mixture [melaka].

visarjana [act. visṛj] n. cessation, end | evacuation, discharge; dismissal | abandonment, desertion; setting cattle free to pasture; soc. aban; offering of an idol to the river at the end of a festival; not. at Mahārāṣṭra, during the anantavrata.
visarjanīya [pfp. [2] visṛj] m. phone. old name of visarga.
visarpa [act. visṛp] m. creeping; diffusion; extension | med. eruption; infectious disease causing cutaneous edema | lit. (in the theatre) action having a harmful consequence by chain reaction.

visarpin [agt. visrp] amnf visarpinī that creeps; that arises; arising from (iic.) | that prowls, that circles around | that spreads, that extends, that grows | sick with a tumor — m. malignant tumor.
visāra [act. visr़] m. spreading, extension, dif fusion | fish.
visārin [agt. visr़] amnf visāriņī that comes out, that spreads, that leaps out (from (iic.)) — m. fish its.
visr [visr] v. [1] pr. (visarati) pp. (visrta) to spread, to extend — ca. (visārayati) to send.
visrj [visṛj₁] v. [6] pr. (visṛjati) pp. (visṛṣṭa) to throw, to release; to spread, to emit | to throw at (loc. dat. pratiacc. ca. (visarjayati) to cause to spread.

visṛp [visṛp] v. [1] pr. (visarpati) pp. (visrpta) to creep; to fly (said of arrows) | to disperse; to spread, to extend | to prowl; to steal — ca. (visarpayati) to extend, to disperse — inf. (visrpas) to spread out.
visṛṣṭi [act. visṛj] f. emission, creation; of lineage.
viskhal [viskhal] v. [1] pr. (viskhalati) to stumble.

viskhalat [ppr. viskhal] amnf viskha lantī stumbling; leaping forth in fits and starts. bhinnakarikumbhaviskhalan mauk yena tikāvalibhirañcitā mahī | adya tena hariṇāntike katham kathyatām nu harinā parākramah || [Bhāminīvilāsa] How could this lion, he who adorned the Earth with strings of pearls dripping from the split temples of elephants, now in the presence of deer, express his glory?

vistara [act. vistr] m. extension, expansion, enlargement, development | multitude; assembly; intensity, detailed description; amplification — f. vistarā ifc. lit. extensive treatise on, complete history of (2nd century). vistarena var. vistarāt adv. exhaustively; in detail; in extenso. vistaratas id. vistarena kāryam give all the details. alam ativistarena enough of the length; enough of the idle details.
vistaratā [tā] f. extension, completeness.
vistaraśas [śas] adv. cf. vistaratas.
vistār [ca. vistr़्] v. [10] pr. (vistārayati) pp. (vistārita) to extend, spread out, unfurl.
vistāra [act. vistr] m. extension; breadth, width | detailed exposition.
vistārita [pp. ca. vistr़] amnf vistāritā extended, spread out, deployed.
vistārin [agt. vistr़] amnf vistāriņī which extends; vast.
vistīrņa [pp. vistr] amnf vistīrņā green neck of (i. iic.) | extended, wide, numerous; extensive; long (history). śatayojanavistīrņa extending for hundreds of leagues around.
vistṛta [pp. vistṛ] amnf visṛtā covered with (i. iic.) | extended, open; wide, developed; extensive; long (history). vistrtam completely.

vistṛ [vistṛ] v. [9] pr. (vistṛṇāti) v. [5] pr. (vistṛṇoti) pp. (vistīrṇa, vistṛta) pf. (pra) to stretch; to extend, to spread — pr. r. (vistṛṇīté) to extend, to spread — ca. (vistārayati) to extend, to spread out, to unfurl. vacanam vistr to speak at length.
vispaṣṭa [vispaṣṭa] amnf vispaṣṭā clear, evident, manifest; intelligible. vispastam adv. clearly.
vispaṣṭārtha | artha | amnf vispaṣṭārthā whose meaning is clear | gram. to aid understanding.
visphuṭ [visphuṭ] v. [6] pr. (visphuṭati) v. [1] pr. (visphotati) to burst, to explode.
visphuțita [pp. visphuț] amnf visphutitā exploded.
visphur [visphur] v. [6] pr. (visphu rati) v. [6] pr. (visphurati) pp. (visphurita) abs. (visphūrya) to tremble, vibrate, quiver, throb (eye, lip) | to sparkle, glitter; to appear.
visphurita [pp. visphur] amnf visphu ritā trembling, vibrant, throbbing; sparkling.
visphota [agt. visphuṭ] m. blister; ampoule.
visphotaka [agt. visphuṭ] mf visphotikā blister; ampoule.
vismaya₁ [act. vismi] m. astonishment, surprise, stupefaction; wonder.
vismayānvita [anvita] amnf vismayānvitā struck with astonishment.
vísmaya₂ [vismaya] amnf vismayā who is not proud; humble, modest.
vismayin [agt. vismi] amnf vismayinī astonished, surprised.
vismaraṇa [act. vismṛ] n. forgetfulness.
vismi [vismi] v. [1] pr. r. (vismayate) pp. (vismita) to be surprised.
vismita [pp. vismi] amnf vismitā astonished.

vismṛ [vismṛ] v. [1] pr. (vismarati) pp. (vismṛta) forget. na vismaratu do not forget. na kadāpi kutrāpi kasyāncidavasthāyāmapi bhaga vantam tasya kṛpām ca vismaret At all times, in all places, in all circumstances, one must not forget God and His grace.
vismṛta [pp. vismṛ] amnf vismṛtā forgotten who has forgotten. adyāpi sā na mayā vismṛtā even today, I do not forget it.
visraṃs [visraṃs] v. [1] pr. r. (visraṃsate) to fall; to break; to come undone (hair) — ca. (visramsayati) to cause to fall.
visramsa [act. visrams] m. fall; the act of breaking when falling; release.
visramsana [act. visrams] n. fall; loosening, the act of loosening (clothing) — agt. amnf visraṃsanī that which drops, that which releases, that which throws.
visramsita [pp. That. visrams] amnf visramsitā that has been dropped; loosened, relaxed, untied.
visraṃsin [agt. visraṃs] amnf visramsinī that falls, that detaches (garland, garment).
visrambha [viśrambh] m. cf. viśrambha.
visvan [visvan] v. [1] pr. (visvanati) to make noise; to shout, to yell; to roar — v. [1] pr. (vișvanati) to eat noisily, to smack one's lips.
viha [vihā₂] iic. air, space, sky.
vihaga [ga₁] m. ["that moves in the air"] arrow bird.
vihata [pp. vihan] amnf vihatā struck, beaten; beaten | touched or visited by (i. iic.) | repelled; rejected; prevented.
vihati [act. vihan] f. blow; injury | prevention, arrest; the act of being repelled, defeat.
vihan [vihan₁] v. [2] pr. (vihanti) pp. (vi hata) to prevent, repress, stop, restrain, hold in check — ca. (vighātáyati) to destroy, defeat (not. an army); to torment.
viham [acc. viha] iic.
vihamga [ga₁] m. ["that which moves in the air"] bird; syn. vihaga | arrow.
viharana [act. vihr] n. removal; change, transposition; expansion | exit from a walk or exercise.
viharaṇīya [pfp. [2] vihṛ] amnf viharanīyā to be removed | which is suitable for walking or exercise.
vihavá [act. vihū] m. invocation.
vihavya [pfp. [1] vihū] amnf vihavyā which must be invoked.
vihas [vihas] v. [1] pr. (vihasati) pr. r. (viha sate) pp. (vihasita) laugh, burst out laughing; make fun of acc. g. . vihasya reads. (theater) laughing.
vihasita [pp. vihas] amnf vihasitā laughing, who laughs | who is mocked (i.) — act. n. the small laugh, not very noisy, where the cheeks redden and the eyes crinkle.
vihā₁ [vihā₁] v. [3] pr. (vijáhāti) pp. (vihīna) pf. (pra) to abandon, forsake, reject; to renounce (acc.) | to get rid of (acc.) — ps. (vihīyate) to lose oneself, disappear.
vihā₁ [vihā₂] v. [3] pr. r. (vijihīte) to move aside, to extend, to spread out; to open wide; to yawn.
vihāya [abs. vihā₁] ind. lassant behind (acc.) | ignorant (acc.) | in spite of, despite (acc.) | except, with the exception of (acc.).
vihāyas [vihā₁] mn space, air; sky — m. bird. vihāyasā i. adv. across the sky.
vihāra [act. vihṛ] m. promenade; pastime, amusement; place of pleasure | bd. convent,
monastery | jn. jain temple | pali Bihāra; hi. Bihar.
vihārabhadra [bhadra] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of vihārabhadra, pleasure advisor to the young king Anantavarmā₁.
vihārabhūmi | bhūmi | f. bd. stage of perfection of a bodhisattva.
vihāraka [agt. vihṛ] amnf vihārikā who takes pleasure in (iic.) | serving the pleasures of (iic.) concerning a bd. monastery or a Jain temple.

vihārin [agt. vihṛ] amnf vihāriṇī who walks, who visits | who enjoys himself, who is entertained — ifc. who appreciates, who is a follower of, who has a passion for (iic.) — f. vihāriņī fickle girl. mṛgayāvihārin who is passionate about hunting.
vihāsa [act. vihas] m. laughter; the act of laughing, of mocking.

víhita [pp. vidhā₁] amnf vihitā attributed, prescribed, instituted, ordained, fixed; destined | accomplished, performed; provided, furnished with (i. iic.) — n. prescription, ordinance, attribution; remedy. vihitāñjali amnf that does the añjali.
víhitatva [vat] n. prescription. 9:
víhitapratijña [pratijñā₂] amnf vihitapratijñā resolved.
víhitapratisiddha [pratisiddha] amnf vihitapratisiddhā prescribes and prohibits.
víhitāśis [āśis₁] amnf having given his blessing.
víhiti [act. vidhā₁] f. procedure, program | performance: accomplishment.

vihīna [pp. vihā₁] amnf vihīnā aban given, rejected | low, inferior; vulgar, vile | lacking, deprived of, free from (abl. i. iic.) — ifc. math. less (num.). vidyāvihīnām kanyām tyaja Abandons a young girl devoid of knowledge.
vihīnatā [tā] f. deprivation; lack of (iic.).
vihīnayoni [yoni] amnf of vile origin, of inferior race.
vihū [vihū] v. [1] pr. r. (vihvayate) to invoke.

vihṛ [vihṛ₁] v. [1] pr. (viharati) pp. (vihṛta) pf. (pra) to take away, to snatch, to distribute | to pass the time, to stroll, to circulate; to amuse oneself, to play. mṛgayāṃ vihṛ to go hunting. talāt talam vihr to pass from hand to hand.
vihṛta [pp. vihṛ] amnf vihṛtā removed, dis tribué — n. promenade | [nāṭya] the silence imposed by modesty, one of the 10 means of seduction |hāva| of the woman.
vihval [vihval] v. [1] pr. (vihvalati) pr. r. (vihvalate) pp. (vihvalita) to stumble, to stagger | (in fig.) to be troubled, to doubt.
vihvala [agt. vihval] amnf vihvalā troubled, agitated; anxious, bored; who is not in control of himself. vihvalā hi rājaprakṛtiḥ [K.] For it is in the nature of kings to be restless.
vihvalita [pp. vihval] amnf vihvalitā who stumbles, who staggers | troubled, perplexed.
√ vī₁ v. [2] pr. (veti) pp. (vīta₂) pf. (pra) to move; to approach; to accept; to seize, to take advantage of; to attack, to take possession of; to punish | to initiate, to incite.
vī₂ [agt. vī₁] ifc. mf inclined to, desirous of, ready to (iic. g.) | propelled by (iic.) — act. m. act of going, movement.

vī₃ [vii] v. [2] pr. (vyeti) pp. (vīta₂) ppr. (viyat) to separate, to disperse; to spread out into; se dissi per, to disappear, to cease. sam ca vi caiti sarvam véd. everything here below is made and unmade.
vīkṣ [viīkṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (vīkṣate) pp. (vīkṣita) abs. (vīksya) pf. (abhi, ut) to see, look, observe, consider, contemplate | to perceive, distinguish, recognize.
vīkṣaṇa [act. vīkṣ] n. observation, consideration, contemplation; examination, inquiry, investigation | phil. [yoga] meditation; cf. astāngayoga.
vīkṣita [pp. vīkṣ] amnf vīkṣitā contemplated.
vīci m. wave, swell, swell.
√ v ī j v. [1] pr. (v ī jati) to fan, to ventilate, to cool by blowing.
vīja cf. bīja.
vīṭa mf vīṭā piece of wood carried in the mouth by ascetics as penance.
vīṭamukha [mukha] amnf vīṭamukhī who has the vīta in the mouth.
vīṭī f. organic. bot. Piper betel, betel.
√ vīd v. [10] pr. (vīdayati) strengthen — v. [10] pr. r. (vīḍayate) to be strong, to be tough.
vīḍu [vīḍu] amnf strong, firm, hard — n. support.

vīṇā f. mus. a type of lute made of jackfruit wood, with 2 bodies and 7 strings (4 on top for the melody, 3 on the sides for the rhythm); it is played flat, resting on the knees, legs in a cross-legged position; the variants rudravīņā (North India), sarasvatīvīņā (South India) are found.
vīṇāḍamaruvādya |ḍamaruvādya| pl. n. vīṇāḍamaruvādyāni lute and tambourine performances, one of the 64 |kalā| arts.
vīṇin [vīṇāin] amnf vīṇinī equipped with a lute; playing the lute.
vītá₁ [pp. vī₁] amnf vītā desired, appreciated; pleasing — n. desire, wish — f. vītā line, row.
vītá₃ [pp. vyā] amnf vītā surrounded by, surrounded by (i. iic.).

vītahavya [havya₁] amnf vītahavyā whose offering is pleasing — m. myth. np. of the king vītahavya, epith. of Ekavīra "who pleases the gods with his offerings", ancestor of the Haihayās; |Mah.| he persecuted Divodāsa, and his son Pratardana followed him; he took refuge with Bhrgu, became a sage, and was raised to the rank of brahmin; Gṛtsamada₁ is his son.
vīta₂ [pp. vī₃] amnf vītā gone, disappeared; past, over; destroyed — ifc. devoid of, free from, without (iic.).
vītaghṛṇa |ghṛṇā| amnf vītaghṛṇā merciless, ruthless.
vītacinta |cintā| amnf vītacintā indifferent; without worry about (loc.); at ease. 9: adhunāham vītacintaḥ now it doesn't matter to me.
vītabhī [bhī₂] amnf fearless, intrepid.
vītabhīti [bhīti] amnf without fear, emboldened.
vītamanyu | manyu| amnf appeased.
vītasūtra [sūtra] n. sacred cord of the dvija; cf. upavita.
vīti [act. vī₃] f. feast, bounty; profit.

vītihotra [hotra] amnf vītihotrā who invites to the feast | myth. invited to the feast (of the gods); epith. of Agni | myth. np. of vītihotra, eldest of the 100 sons of King Tālajangha; when his father was defeated by Paraśurāma, he took refuge in the Himalayas, from which he descended when the latter left as a hermit to Mount Mahendra₁ | pl. myth. np. of the Vītihotrās, his descendants.
vīthi f. line, row; street; alignment of shops, bazaar | art gallery | lit. name of the dramatic style "in garland"; cf. gaṇḍa | var. vīthī id.
vīthika [ka] mf vīthikā id.
vīthyanga [anga₁] n. lit. one of the 13 stages of the
prologue [pūrvaranga] to the theater, not. the trigata.
vidhra amnf vidhrā clear, pure — n. clear sky; wind; fire. vidhr on a sunny day.
vīps [des. vyāp] v. pr. (vīpsati) pp. (vīpsita) to desire to spread.

vīpsā [act. des. vyāp] f. distribution, repetition, succession | gram. repetition of words to signify the repetition or distribution of an action. vrksam vrksam siñcati he waters one tree after another. nityavīpsāyoh gram. Pan (8,1, 4): A word is re doubled to signify repetition or distribution.

vīrá [vī₁ra] m. male, warrior, hero, chief; husband, son | lit. [aesthetics] heroism, one of the 9 artistic modes [rasa] | myth. [Mah.] np. of the asura Vīra₁ "Hero", son of Danāyu and Kasyapa hist. np. of Vīra₁ Narasimha₆, son of Narasa Nāyaka, regent of Vijayanagara; upon his father's death in 1503 he continued the regency; the legitimate heir Immadi having been assassinated in 1505, Vīra₁ Narasimha₆ became king, creating the Tuluva dynasty; in 1509 his brother Kṛṣṇadeva Rāya succeeded him — v. [11] pr. r. (vīráyate) to be strong, to be brave — v. [11] pr. (vīrayati) to conquer, to subjugate || lat. vir; fr. viril. vīrapuruṣa man who is a hero.
vīraká |ka| mr. myth. |Haracaritacintāmaṇi| n.p. of Vīraka "little hero", epith. of Nandī.
vīraketu [ketu] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of the vīraketu "with the emblem of heroes"; besieged by Mattakāla, king of the Lātās, he had to give him his daughter Vāmalocanā.
vīrakerala | kerala | mr. hist. n.p. of king vīrakerala₁ Varmā of Venad (mod. Quilon in Kerala), reign (1125–1145); he had the Pad manābhasvāmī rebuilt.

Vīradhavala |dhavala| mr. hist. n.p. of king Vīradhavala, first of the Vāghela dynasty in Gujarat, who supplanted the Solankīs (1243–1262); its capital was Dholka, in the Mod district. Ahmedabad; his ministers Vastupāla and Te japāla financed the Jain monastery Lūna vasati in Arbuda₁, dedicated to the Jain saint Neminātha in memory of their brother Lūna (1230).
vīrápatnī | patnī | f. wife of a hero.
vīrápuruṣa [puruṣa] m. hero.
vīrapuruṣaka |ka| m. village famous for its heroes.
vīrabhaṭa [bhaṭa] m. bed. [KSS.] np. of king Vīrabhaṭa of Tāmraliptī, father of Madanasenā and Vilāsinī.

Vīrabhadra | bhadra | m. myth. np. of Vīrabhadra, terrible aspect of Shiva "Ready for war", which he took to destroy the sacrifice of Daksha; he has 1000 heads, 1000 eyes, 1000 arms carrying a club and 1000 legs; he wears a linga in his hair; he is often depicted with his right arm holding an upright sword, his left arm carrying the severed head of Daksha, and behind him a wolf waiting to gnaw on the head; he transformed into śarabha to end the incarnation of Narasimha | hist. np. of Prince Vīrabhadra₁ of the Eastern Cālukya dynasty; he married Queen Rudramadevī | hist. np. of Vīrabhadra₂ Prabhu, gaudīya mystic, son of Nityānanda Prabhu | hist. np. of Prince Vīrabhadra₃ Reddi, king of Rājamahendrapura from 1423 to 1434; he patronized Śrīnātha.
Vīrabhadratantra [tantra] n. lit. of the np. Vīrabhadratantra, a Shaivite text dealing with magic and enchantment.

vīrabhuja [bhuja] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of vīrabhuja, king of Vardhamāna₃; he had 100 wives, and Gunavārā was his favorite; distressed at not having a son, he asked the physician Srutavardhana for a remedy; the latter made a stew with a wild goat mixed with magical powders; all the women drank the broth, except Guṇavārā oc 9: cut off to pay homage to the gods with her husband; when she returned, only the horns remained; the marrow was extracted to give to her; all the women gave birth to a son, but Srigabhuja, son of Guṇavārā, surpassed them all.
vīrámitrodaya | mitrodaya | mr. bed. n.p. from Mitra₁ Miśra's Vīramitrodaya, a vast collection of dharmaśāstra (1610–1640).
vīramelāpa [melāpa] m. SOC. ["virile meeting"] secret krama ritual of collective orgy; syn. cakrame Iaka, cakrakrīdā.
vīrarasa | rasa | m. lit. the heroic feeling, one of the 9 artistic modes [rasa]; it is associated with the color light orange and the deity Indra.
vīrarāghava [rāghava] m. myth. np. of vīrarāghava, epith. of Rāma "Hero of the rāghavās"; he is worshipped at Kingrhapura (mod. Tiruvallur, near Chennai in Tamil Nadu).
vīrávrata [vrata] amnf vīravratā who shows courage, who takes a vow of heroism.

Vīraśekhara [śekhara] m. lit. [DKC.] np. du vidyādhara Vīraśekhara "Crowned with heroism", son of Mānasavega; King Darpasāra had promised him his sister Avantisundarī in marriage; he found the silver chain that embodied Suratamañjarī₁ mau said by Mārkaņdeya; he used his magical powers to spy on Avantisundarī in the women's quarters, where he surprised her in the company of Rājavāhana, whom during her sleep he bound with the chain.

vīraśaiva [śaiva] m. pl. name of a śaiva sect of Karņāta founded by Basava; its members wear a small linga around their necks, hence their name lingāyat; their dead are buried rather than burned; cf. jangama .

vīrasena [senā] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of vīrasena "to the army of heroes", king of the Niṣadhās, father of Nala | hist. n.p. of the master ācārya vīrasena₁, mathematician, geometer and Jain poet of the 9th century; Jinasena was his disciple.
vīrastambha [stambha] m. SOC. stele commemorating the prowess of a hero; they are found in the Deccan and Bengal || kannara viirakkal.
vīrāsana |āsana| n. phil. |yoga| seated posture with the left foot on the right thigh, the right leg hanging down.
vīreśvara [īśvara] m. hist. n.p. of vīreśvara, son of Bhattoji Dīkṣita, father of Hari₁ Dīkṣita.
vīrut iic. virudh.
vīruttṛṇa |tṛṇa| n. straw.
vīruttṛṇamaya |maya| amnf vīruttṛṇamayī made of straw.
vīruttṛṇmayapuruṣa | puruṣa | m. scarecrow.
vīrudh [agt. viruh] f. [nom. vīrut] plant, herb; not. vine or bush.

vīryá [vīraya] n. valor, heroism; prowess | energy, vigor, virility, strength | bd. vigor, one of the 6 perfections |pāramitā| of an accomplished [bodhisattva] | sperm — f. vīryā vigor; energy; virility. vīryabuddhisampanna endowed with vigor and intelligence.
vīryavat |vat| amnf vīryavatī energetic, valiant, vigorous; capable of prowess; effective.

vīryaśulka [śulka] n. prize of heroism — amnf vīryaśulkā obtained at the price of bravery. imāh kāśipateh kanyā mayā nirjitya pārthivān vicitravīryasya kṛte vīryaśulkā upārjitāḥ | [Mah.] (Bhīṣma) By subjugating the princes in battle I won these daughters of the king of Kāśi on behalf of Vicitravīrya at the price of my bravery.

√ vr₁ v. [5] pr. (vrnoti) pr. r. (vrnute) v. [1] pr. (várati) v. [5] pr. (ūrņóti) aor. [3] (avīvarat) aor. [5] (avārīt) aor. [1] (avṛta) pp. (vṛta₁) pf. (anu, abhi, ā, ni, nis, pari, pra, vi, sam) cover, envelop, surround; hide; obstruct, prevent | close (a door) — ca. (vārayati) prevent (from the abl. inf. angle), stop — intens. r. (ūrṇonūyate) (av. pra) prevent continually.

√ vr₂ v. [9] pr. (vṛṇāti) pr. r. (vṛṇīté) aor. [4] (avārṣīt) aor. r. [1] (avṛta) aor. r. [4] (avṛṣṭa) pp. (vrta₂) pfp. (vrtya, varenya) pf. (abhi, pra) to choose, to take for (dat. loc. i.); to ask for in marriage — ca. (varáyati) to choose, to solicit, to favor — ca. r. (varáyate) to choose, to select, to solicit | lat. volo; ang. to will; all. wollen; fr. vouloir, volonté.
vṛṃh cf. bṛh₁.
vrk cf. vraśc.
vṛka [agt. bulk] m. organic. zoo. wolf, jackal; cf. śālāvṛka | ved. plow — f. organic vṛkī. she-wolf | gr. λυκος; lat. lupus; all. wolf; eng. wolf; fr. wolf.
vrkabhaya |bhaya| n. fear of the wolf.
vṛkabhīta [bhīta] amnf vṛkabhītā who is afraid of the wolf.
vṛkodara [udara] m. myth. [Mah.] np. from vṛkodara "Wolf's belly", epith. of Bhīma.
vṛkṇá [pp. vraśc] amnf vṛkṇā torn, cut up, torn to pieces — n. cut, incision.
vṛktá [pp. vṛj] amnf vṛktā twisted; turned. 9:
vrkṣá | related to vraśc | m. tree.
vrksaka [ka] m. shrub — f. vrksakā myth. dryad.
vrksakotara | kotara | n. hollow of a tree.
vrkṣamūla [mūla] n. tree root.
vṛkṣavat [vat] amnf vṛkṣavatī covered with trees.
vrksásākhā | śākhā | f. tree branch.
vrkṣasthala |sthala| n. soc. sacred temple tree.

vrkṣāmla [amla] m. bio. bot. Spondias pinnata, tree with compound leaves, thick bark, numerous flowers in panicles, green then yellow fruits; it is used in medicine — n. bio. fruit of the tamarind tree, used as an acidic condiment syn. tintidīka.
Vṛkṣāyurveda [āyurveda] m. treatment of trees lit. np. from the Vṛkṣāyurveda, a treatise on botany and horticulture by Surapāla.
vrkṣāyurvedayoga [yoga] m. soc. the practice of horticulture, one of the 64 arts | kalā|.
vṛkṣāropaṇa [āropaṇa] n. orchard, tree plantation.

√ vrj v. [7] pr. (vrnakti) aor. [7] (avrksat) pp. (vṛktá) pf. (apa, ā, pari, pra, vi) bend, twist; pull up; pick (not. of the sacrificial herb) | turn away from, divert from (abl. g.); exclude, alienate — pr. r. (vṛṅkte) choose, select; reserve — ca. (varjayati) turn away, avoid; abandon, renounce, abstain from (acc.) | exclude.
vrjána [act. vrj] n. ved. fort; camp; colony; town | deception; intrigue; sin.
vṛji [vṛji] f. geo. n.p. of the vṛji country, mod. Braj; cf. Vraja || pali vajji .
vṛjiná [obj. vṛj] amnf vṛjinā twisted,
curved | deceptive, false | disastrous — m. hair lure, curl — n. vice; wickedness; bad faith | distress, misfortune — f. vṛjinā deception, intrigue; calamity.
vrjyá [pfp. [1] vrj] amnf vrjyā which must be excluded or diverted.

√ vrt₁ v. [1] pr. r. (vártate) v. [3] pr. (vavartti) pft. (vavrte) aor. [2] (avrtat) aor. [3] (avrīvrtat) pp. (vṛtta) ppr. r. (vartamāna) pf. (ati, anu, apa, abhi, ā, ut, upa, ni, nis, parā, pari, pra, vi, sam) turn, roll | be, take place, occur, be accomplished; proceed to (acc.); proceed from (abl.), originate from (loc.) | remain, maintain; continue to (ind. abs.); pass, flow (time) | act as, turn out to be (i. acc. adv.) (towards someone (loc. dat. prati)); to serve (dat.) — ca. (vartáyati) to turn, to rotate something; to operate | to exist, to live off (i.); to be occupied with (loc.) | to accomplish, to produce; to explain, to relate — intens. (varīvartti) ved. to roll; to exist; to predominate — des. (vívrtsati) to want to turn | lat. verto; all. werden. kim vartate what is he doing, how is he? | what is happening? āgacchan vartate he is arriving. kā velā vartate what time is it? priyam vrt to act kindly. svāni vrt to mind one's own business. mūrdhni vṛt₁ to be in the lead, to be important. mrtyormukhe vartate he is in the clutches of death. ehisvāgatā vartate "come in and be welcome" is the custom here.
vrt₂ |agt. vrt₁| ifc. amnf (iic.) which turns, which exists | (after number) (iic.) times.
vṛt₁á₁ [pp. vṛ₁] amnf vṛtā covered, hidden gram. qualifies a closed class [gaṇa]; opp. ākṛti; syn. paripūrņa.
vṛt₁á₂ [pp. vṛ₂] amnf vṛtā chosen, elected. vrte adv. the choice having been made.
vṛti [act. vṛ₁] f. environment | cultivated enclosure; garden.

vṛttá [pp. vṛt₁] amnf vṛttā accomplished, produced, arrived; maintained, remained | which took place, which existed; over, finished, dead | round ["that rolls"] — ifc. that behaves like; derived from (iic.) — n. event, adventure, affair ["that which happened"]; procedure, action; manifestation | conduct, behavior, customs; course, race | math. circle; sequence — f. vṛttā phon. meter (counted by syllables); opp. jāti. kim tasyā vṛttam What's wrong with her? sītādevyāḥ kiṃ vṛttam What happened to Queen Sītā?
vrttacūda [cūdā] amnf vrttacūdā soc. having received the ritual tonsure.
vrttajātisamuccaya [jātisamuccaya] m. math. np. from the Vṛttajātisamuccaya, a work on prosody and combinatorics by Virahānka (around 600, in prākṛta).
vrttaphala [phala] m. ["round fruit"] pomegranate; ju jube — f. organic vṛttaphalā. bot. Solanum melongena, eggplant.
vṛttamālāstuti [mālāstuti] f. lit. np. of the Vrttamālāstuti, a hymn of praise to Mañjuśrī by Jñānaśrīmitra, each of whose 150 stanzas illustrates a meter. 9:
vṛttamālāstutivivṛtti [vivṛtti] f. bed. n.p. of the Vṛttamālāstutivivṛti or Vṛttamālāvivṛti, commentary on the vṛttamālāstuti by Sākyarakṣita.
vṛttamuktāvalī [muktāvalī] f. bed. n.p. from the Vrttamuktāvalī, a grammar work by Srīkṛṣṇabhaṭṭa (18th century).
vṛttaratnākara [ratnākara] n. lit. np. from the Vrttaratnākara "Mine of metrics", a work of prosodic combinatorics, due to Kedāra₁ Bhaṭṭa; it describes 136 meters.
vrttasampanna [sampanna] amnf vrttasampanna of good conduct, virtuous.

vṛttānta [anta] m. [“that which has as its object what has happened” event, adventure; episode; situation | course, turn, manner | narrative, story, news; information. kastasyā vṛttāntaḥ what is happening to him? kah vrttāntastatrabhavatyāh how is Madam? anabhyamtarā vayam madanagatasya vṛttāntasya We are not competent in matters of sexuality.
vṛttin [in] amnf vṛttinī phil. [Nyāya] occur rent; present in (iic.).

vṛtti [act. vṛt₁] f. circular movement, rolling; flow (tears); development; occurrence; dynamic | way of being or acting, behavior; lifestyle, conduct | means of subsistence, activity, occupation; profession, trade gram. function of a word; use of a word in a given sense; morphological formation; style, genre; cf. pañcavrtti | gram. synthetic expression (opp. analytic expression [vākya]) | phil. divinity attached to a function | phil. fluctuation, movement of thought; cf. cittavṛtti | phil. [Nyāya] relation between a word and its meaning [padārtha] | phon. mode of recitation; alliteration | lit. (mode of composition) commentary, gloss on an aphorism [sūtra] — ifc. occupied with, engaged in, whose profession is (ii.). vrttim kr live from (i. iic.); bring to life (g.). kuru priyasakhivṛttim sapatnījane behave as a friend towards your rivals. parārthābhidhānam vṛttiḥ gram. |Patañjali₁| The vrtti (of a sentence) is the expression of the meaning (according to the meaning of its constituents).
vṛttika [ka] ifc. amnf vṛttikā which has the function of (iic.); which has the meaning of (iic.).
vṛttitā |tā| f. conduct, mode of subsistence — ifc. devotion to (iic.).
vrttitva [tva] n. state of subsistence; occupation — ifc. phil. [Nyāya] presence of (g.) in (iic.); residence in (iic.).
Vṛttidīpikā [dīpikā] f. bed. n.p. from the Vṛttidīpikā, a grammar work by Śrīkṛṣṇabhaṭṭa (18th century).

vrttiniyāmaka [niyāmaka] amnf vrttiniyāmikā phil. [Nyāya] is said of a factual relation |sambandha|; opp. vṛttyaniyāmaka. sambandho dvividhah vṛttiniyāmakah phil. vrttyaniyāmakaśceti [Pāribhāṣipadārthasaṃgraha] relations are of two kinds: factual and conventional.
vṛttyaniyāmaka |aniyāmaka| amnf vrttyaniyāmikā phil. [Nyāya] is said of a relationship
conventional [bhāva]; opp. vṛttiniyāmaka.

vṛttyanuprāsa [anuprāsa] m. lit. [alaṃkāra] repetition of one or more consonants resulting in a specific emotion, contributing to the flavor [rasa] of the text. বুর vṛtrá |vṛt₁ra| m. resistance, obstruction; hostile influence; darkness | myth. ved. np. of Vrtra "the Obstructor", celestial dānavadragon |ahi| created by tvașțā as his son (and therefore brāhmaṇa) to avenge his elder TvāṣṭraViśvarūpa killed by In dra; Tvaṣṭā made a sacrifice to have a son "victorious over Indra" [indraśatrú] but made a mistake and asked instead that he be "defeated by Indra" | índraśatru | ; symbol of drought, Vrtra held the waters captive; he was killed by Indra armed with his vajra, releasing the waters and creating the rivers; [Mah.] ViṣṇuTrivikrama had opened the space for battle by taking his three steps; because of this crime of brahmicide, Indra lost his strength which gave birth to Vāyu; other texts say Vrtra son of Danāyu and Kaśyapa — n. pl. vrtrāņi ved. the forces of obstruction, hostile influences of Chaos resisting the creation of the Cosmos.
vrtrátará |tara| mr. ved. Vrtra only worse.
vrtráhátya [hatya] n. myth. murder of Vrtra by Indra — f. vṛtrahatyā id.
vrtráhán [han₂] m. myth. np. of Vrtrahan, epith. of Indra "Dragon Slayer".

vṛthā [vṛ₁thā] adv. at random; at will, abundantly, lavishly | vainly, uselessly | falsely, improperly, wrongly. vṛthā kṛ to render useless. vṛthā bhū to be useless, to be frustrated, to be disappointed. kālam vṛthā na gamayet one must not waste one's time.

vṛddha | pp. vṛdh₁ | amnf vṛddhā augmented, 9: increased, grown; adult, aged; aged, ancient, old; in ruins | instructed, expert, learned, eminent; wise — m. old man, senior | soc. patronymic name of a senior (e.g., Gārgya for the gotra of Garga); opp. yuvan — ifc. the eldest of; superior in, advanced in (iic.) — f. vṛddhā old woman.
vṛddhakumārī [kumārī] f. old maid.

vṛddhakumārīvākyavaranyāya [vākyavara Nyāya] m. lit. saying of the wish of the old maid, to whom Indra had granted a wish, and who deceived him by making a convoluted request; it illustrates the power of presupposition, which allows one to ask for the impossible; in grammar it is used for a sentence with multiple meanings. putrā me bahukṣīraghṛtam odanam kāñcanapātryām bhuñjīran lit. [Mahābhāṣya] May my sons eat their rice with cream in abundance from golden vessels.
vrddhakṣatra [kṣatra] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Vrddhakṣatra "Venerable lord", father of Jaya dratha.
vrddhagarga [Garga] m. hist. n.p. from the astro nome Vrddhagarga or Garga₁ the ancient; his work [Vrddhagargasamhitā] is the Gārgīyajyotişa. vṛddhatā [ tā ] f. old age.
vrddhatva [tva] n. id.

vrddhapranaptr | pranaptr | m. great-great-grandson; the son of a great-grandson is said vrddhaprapautra, that of a great-granddaughter is said vrddhapradauhitra — f. vrddhapranaptrī great-great-granddaughter; the daughter of a great-grandson is said vṛddhaprapautrī, that of a great-granddaughter is said vrddhapradauhitrī.
vrddhaprapitāmaha [prapitāmaha] m. paternal great-great-grandfather — f. vṛddhaprapitāmahī paternal great-great-grandmother.
vṛddhapramātāmaha [pramātāmaha] m. maternal great-great-grandfather — f. vrddhapramātāmahī maternal great-great-grandmother.

vṛddhayavanajātaka [yavanajātaka] n. astr. np. of the Vrddhayavanajātaka of Mīnarāja, also called Mīnarājajātaka; it is the summary in 8000 verses of a lost work on Greek astronomy. vrddhokşa [ukşan] m. old bull.
vṛddhaka [agt. vṛdh₁] amnf vṛddhikā old.

vṛddhi [act. vṛdh₁] f. growth, increase | prosperity; wealth, fortune | phon. increase of a vowel in the 2nd degree: the vṛddhi of ('a', 'i', 'u', 'r') is resp. ('ā', 'ai', 'au', 'ār') | rising tide; waxing moon | soc. interest, usury rate; cf. kāyikā, kālikā, kāritā, śikhā, cakravṛddhi, bhogalābha, dharmavṛddhi, anyāyavrddhi, paramavrddhi | bio. bot. Habenaria intermedia, an orchid whose tubers are used in medicine. vrddhikṣayau astr. waxing and waning of the moon. vṛddhikara | kara₁ ₁ | amnf vṛddhikarī which causes the increase of (iic.).
vrddhikaratva |tva| n. act of causing the increase of (iic.).
vṛddhimat [mat] amnf vṛddhimatī s'accrois sant.

√ vrdh₁ [related to brh₁] v. [1] pr. r. (vardhate) pft. (vavardha) pp. (vṛddha) ppr. r. (vardhamāna) pf. (abhi, ā, pra, vi, sam) to grow, prosper; to increase, to grow | to be inspired or excited or joyful by (i. loc. g.), concerning (dat.) — ca. (vardháyati) ca. r. (vardhayate) pp. (vardhita) to increase; to make grow, to raise. distyā vṛdh₁ | "to wish prosperity" | to congratulate for (i.).
vrdh₂ [agt. vrdh₁] ifc. amnf which increases, which augments (iic.).
vrnta m. small crawling animal, not. caterpillar — n. peduncle of a leaf, flower or fruit; stem.
vṛntāka |related to vṛnta| mf vṛntākī auber gine (plant) — n. its fruit.
vṛndá n. multitude, crowd, gathering; troop | aggregate; bouquet, sheaf; choir, chorus | a very large number; 100 billion — f. cf. vṛndā. vrndam adv. in groups, in a crowd. ... vṛnda long live ...
vṛndā [f. vṛnda] f. sacred basil; syn. tulasī myth. np. of vṛndā "Prolific", epith. of Rādhā.
vrndāvat [vat] f. vrndāvatī soc. 3-tiered square pyramid housing a culture of holy basil, established near shrines; simpler forms adorn houses.

vṛndāvana [vana] n. myth. np. of vṛndāvana, the grove of vṛndāRādhā, near the Yamunā, where the young KṛṣṇaGopāla grazed the flocks with the cowherds [gopī]; it was here that the love affair of Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā took place; mod. Vrin daban/Brindaban | soc. place of memory, where the ashes of Madhva's disciples rest; cf. Navavṛndāvana. 9:
vṛndāra |vṛndāra| amnf vṛndārā cf. vrndāraka.
vṛndāraka |ka| m. the best, the most eminent, the leader, the most beautiful of a troop — f. vṛndārakā f. vṛndārikā the best of its kind.
vṛścat [ppr. vraśc] amnf vṛścantī tearing, cutting.
vṛścádvana [vana] amnf vṛścadvanā that destroys the forest — m. myth. epith. of Agni. বৃশ্বন vṛścana |agt. vraśc| m. bio. zoo. Scorpion; syn. vrścika.
vṛścika [vraścika] m. bio. zoo. Scorpion |astr. zodiac sign [rāśi] of Scorpio. gomayād vṛściko jāyate The Scorpion is born from cow dung.

√ vṛṣ [related to ṛṣ] v. [1] pr. (varṣati) pft. (vavarṣa) pp. (vṛṣṭa) pf. (abhi, pra) to rain, to fall as rain; to spread rain (god, cloud), to water, to spread as rain | (figuratively) to cover with riches or evils — ca. (varṣayati) to make it rain or fall as rain; to water (with (i.)) || gr. ; fr. to pour. vavarșa rudhiram | Rām. | It was raining blood.

vṛṣa [agt. vṛṣ] m. male (animal); Bull; sperm ["that which fertilizes"] | astr. zodiacal sign |rāśi| of Taurus; symbol of justice | virtue, meritorious act | myth. [Rām.] np. of vṛṣa, mountain in the Himalayas facing Kailāsa, where Nandī meditates; there is the herb-covered mountain Mahodaya where the herb of resurrection |samjīvanī| grows; cf. Hanuman — v.
