[11] pr. (vṛṣasyati) to desire the bull (said of the cow) — v. [11] pr. (vṛṣīyati) to wish to have a Bull | lat. verres.
vṛṣaka |ka| m. small tree, shrub.
vṛṣatā [tā] f. virility; creative power. vrşaparvan [parvan] m. myth. np. of the dānava Vṛṣaparvā "with powerful limbs"; he is father of Sarmisthā.

vṛṣabhá | bha| amnf vṛṣabhā vigorous; viril — m. myth. n.p. of Vṛṣabha, Bull mount [vāhana] of Siva; later, epith. from Nandī “Like the Bull”; cf. Rsabha | myth. n.p. of Vṛṣabha₂, son of Arjuna₁ Kārtavīrya.
vrsabhadeva [deva] m. hist. n.p. of the philosopher Vrsabhadeva, author of the Sphuṭākṣarā (8th century).
vṛṣabhadhvaja [dhvaja] m. myth. epith. of Shiva "who has the Bull as her banner".
vṛṣabhavāhana [vāhana] m. "Led by the bull", epith. of Shiva accompanied by Nandi.
vṛṣabhānu [bhānu] m. myth. np. of the vaiśya vṛṣabhānu, father of Rādhā.
vṛṣavāhana |vāhana| mr. cf. vṛṣabhavāhana.
vṛṣaśaila |śaila| m. geo. bull hill; cf. cf. venkatādri.
vṛṣasaṅga [saṅga] m. myth. epith. of Shiva “associated with the bull”.

vṛṣasena [senā] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of vṛṣasena son of Karna "with the manly arm"; in the great battle he faced all the heroes of the army of the Pāṇḍavās; Arjuna killed him before the eyes of his father, before killing the latter.
Vṛṣārūḍha [ārūḍha] m. arch. np. of Vṛṣārūḍha epith. of Shiva "having the bull as a mount"; it is one of the 16 aspects of Shiva.
vṛṣaṇ iic. vṛṣan.
vṛṣaṇaśvá [aśva] amn drawn by male horses (chariot) — m. ved. [RV.] np. of King Vṛṣaṇaśva "Stallion", Virile hero of very great vigor.
vṛṣaṇa [agt. vṛṣ] amnf vṛṣaṇī that fertilizes — m. of the. testicles.

vṛṣan [vṛṣ] m. Vedic. fertile; male, etc. | myth. np. of vṛṣā "Prolific", epithet of Indra | astr. np. of vṛṣā₁ "Pubescent", son of Nāradī, personifying the 15th year of a life cycle |samvatsara| — ifc. best among the (iic.). বৃষ্প vṛṣala |vṛṣala| m. man of low caste (syn. śūdra); despicable man — f. cf. vṛṣalī.
vṛṣalī [f. vṛṣala] f. woman vṛṣala | unmarried pubescent woman; menstruating woman | sterile woman; mother of a stillborn child.
vṛṣalīsevana |sevana₁| n. soc. sexual commerce with a śūdrā woman.
vṛṣā |noun. vṛṣan | iic.

vṛṣākapi [kapi] m. myth. [RV.] np. of vṛṣākapi "Male Monkey", friend of Indra; he sexually harassed Indrāṇī, who rejected his advances and corrected him — f. Vṛṣākapāyī myth. np. of Vṛṣākapāyī, wife of vṛṣākapi.
vṛṣī cf. bṛṣī. ਕੁਣ vṛṣṭa |pp. vṛṣ| amnf vṛṣṭā fell in rain. vrstam it rained.
vṛṣṭí [act. vṛṣ] f. rain | pl. vṛṣṭayas id. — ifc. rain of (iic.). puspavṛṣṭi f. rain of flowers. dhārāsarairmahatī vṛṣṭirbabhūva torrents of water were falling.

Vṛṣṇi [vṛṣni] m. ram | myth. np. of King Vṛṣṇi "Viril", of the Yadu dynasty; he is the eldest of the 100 sons of Madhu, and therefore grandson of Kārtavīrya; or he would be the eldest of the 7 sons of Sātvata, descendant 9: of Krostā | myth. dynasty of princes descended from Vṛṣṇi [vārṣṇeya]; to which belong not. Bhoja, Sūrasena, Kṛṣṇa, Sātyaki, Yuyudhāna and Ugrasena; Mathurā was their capital.
vṛṣṇya [a] amnf vṛṣṇyā ved. vigorous, then healthy; Viril — n. virility.

vṛṣya [pfp. [1] vṛṣ] amnf vṛṣyā med. tonic; sexual stimulant, aphrodisiac — m. bio. legume bot. Vigna radiata; its seed, comes tible, (mungo bean, green soybean) is used in many culinary preparations.
vṛṣyatā [tā] f. virility.
vrsī cf. brsī.
√ vṛh [related to bṛh₂] v. [6] pr. (vṛháti) pp. (vṛḍhá) to tear, to rip.
vṛhat cf. bṛhat.

vega [agt. vij] m. stream of water; torrent; figuratively, torrent of tears | rapidity, velocity; momentum, impulse, surge | vehemence, impetuosity; violent effect (not. poison); paroxysm | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] speed acquired by a body. vegāt adv. impetuously.

Vegavat [vat] amnf Vegavatī agitated (not. ocean); impetuous; vehement, violent; rapid (not. torrent) | lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara king Vegavat, husband of Prthivīdevī, father of Vegavatī and Mānasavega — f. Vegavatī lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī Vegavatī, sister of Mānasavega; she helped Prince Naravāhanadatta find Mada namañcukā and is counted among his wives.
vegasara [sara] m. mule — f. vegasarī mule.
vegita [vegaita] amnf vegitā agitated by waves, turbulent | rapid, swift; impetuous.
vegin [agt. vij] amnf veginī rapid, swift; impetuous.
veňka m. pl. name of a people of South India.

venkața [pkt. vyankața] m. geo. name of the sacred hill of venkața, in Tirumala, South Andhra Pradesh, important place of pilgrimage var. vyankata id. (uncorrupted form) | hist. np. of the Vaishnava king venkata₂ of the Aravidu dynasty he reigned in Vijayanagara from 1586 to 1614.
venkatanātha [nātha] m. bed. n.p. of Venkatanātha "Master of venkața", epith. of the phil. vaișnava Vedāntadeśika.
venkatācārya [ācārya] m. hist. n.p. of the mystic Venkatācārya; cf. Raghavendra.
venkaṭādri [adri] m. geo. Tirupati hill.
venkaṭādhvarin [adhvarin] m. hist. n.p. by Venkațādhvarī, campū style satirical poet (South India, 17th century), author of Rāghavayādavīya and Viśvaguṇādarśa.
venkateśa [īśa] m. myth. np. of Venkateśa the "Lord of Venkata", epith. of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu; cf. Venkatesvara.
venkateśānanda [ānanda] m. mod. n.p. of Svāmī Venkateśānanda (1921–1982), disciple of Śivānanda.

venkateśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Venkațeśvara, the "Lord of Venkața", as pect of Vișnu venerated at the temple of Venkata; he has his eyes hidden (because his gaze would burn the universe), and is often covered with garlands of flowers which only reveal his feet.
Vengī f. geo. np. of the city of Vengī or Vengi, capital of the Śālankāyanās, then of the Cālukyās of the East; it was close to modern Eluru in Andhra.
vej [ca. vij] v. [10] pr. (vejayati) pp. (vejita) to accelerate, intensify | to worry, alarm.
vejita [pp. ca. vij] amnf vejitā frightened, terrified | increased, intensified.
veṭ [vā₁iṭ] nota. gram. refers to roots ad putting an optional intercalated 'i'.
veṇi f. braid, plait | soc. not. hair in a single plait worn by a widow | confluence of two rivers.
venivedhanī | vedhanī | f. comb.

veṇika [veṇika] m. pl. np. of the Veṇikā people — f. veṇikā lock of hair | stream (river); track (forest). baddhavenikayā godāvarya parigatam |K.| Surrounded by the uninterrupted flow of the Godāvarī. veņikavāhin [vāhin] amnf veņikavāhinī which carries a continuous stream.

veṇī [veṇi] f. braid, plaited hair | stream, brook. veņīdatta | datta | m. hist. np. of the poet Veņīdatta | (17th century); he is the author of the Padyavenī and the dictionary Pañcatattvaprakāśa. veņīsamhāra [saṃhāra] m. lit. of the np. Venīsamhāra, a drama by Bhattanārāyana, which evokes the episode in the Mah. where Duḥśāsana insults Draupadī by undoing her plaits |veṇīsaṃhāra| and dragging her by her undone hair, inciting Bhīma to swear to avenge her by drinking her blood.
veņu [vā₃] m. reed, bamboo; pipe, transverse flute. 9: veņugopāla [gopāla] m. myth. Kṛṣṇa adolescent playing the flute (to delight the cowherds [gopī]).
venudanda [danda] m. myth. bamboo stick, planted in the ground to celebrate the festival of Indra [indrotsava], instituted by King Uparicara Vasu₂.
vetana [related to vartana] n. wages, remuneration; salary.
vetasa [related to vetra] m. bio. bot. Calamus ro tang, a type of reed, rattan; cane, rod — n. med. lancet — f. vetasī reed, rattan.
vetasvat [vetasavat] amnf vetasvatī covered with reeds.
vetāla m. myth. demon that seizes corpses, vampire, ghost, specter; revenant, living dead; syn. pūtana — f. vetālā f. vetālī myth. aspects of Durgā.

vetālapañcaviṃśatikā | pañcaviṃśatika | f. lit. np. from the collection of fables Vetālapañcaviṃśatikā "25 tales of the undead" (VeP.); there are four versions of it; not. it forms part of the Kathāsaritsāgara (fixed in the 11th century); King Trivi kramasena carries on his shoulder an undead who tells him stories, ending with riddles.
Vetālabhaṭṭa [bhaṭṭa] m. hist. np. of Vetālabhaṭṭa, one of the nine jewels [navaratna] of the court of King Vikramāditya.
vettr [agt. vid₁] amnf vettrī who knows, connoisseur of (g. iic.) | witness | who experiences (iic.) who will know.
vetra [instr. vā₃] m. organic. bot. Calamus fascicu latus, a type of bamboo; cane, stick; cf. veņu lat. vīmen.
vetralatā |latā| f. bamboo cane.
vetralatāvat [vat] amnf vetralatāvatī equipped with a bamboo cane.

vetravat [vat] f. Vetravatī geo. n.p. from the Vetravatī River “Covered with Bamboos”; mod. Betvā, tributary of the Yamunā; cf. Virāṭanagara | bed. [Abhijñānaśakuntalā] np. of Vetravatī₁ "who carries the cane", female usher of the palace of Dusyanta.

ved [ca. vid₁] v. [10] pr. (vedayati) pfp. (ve dayitavya) abs. (vedayitvā) to inform someone (dat.) of (acc.); to make known, to proclaim; to show, to communicate (acc.) (to something (dat.)); to teach something to someone. 2 acc. . Veda [obj. vid₁] m. knowledge, science; pa sacred role, revealed knowledge | phil. np. of the Veda or "Knowledge", a set of sacred texts including the Rigveda, the Samaveda, the two Yajurvedas and the Atharvaveda | math. symb. the number four — v. |11| pr. (vedāpayati) to make known. trayo vedā eta eva vāg evargvedah mano yajurvedah prāṇah sāmavedah [BU.] There are three Vedas: the Rgveda is speech, the Yajurveda is mind and the Sāmaveda is breath.
Vedajñāna [jñāna] m. hist. n.p. by Vedajñāna, Shaivite theologian of the 16th century, author of the Dīkṣādarśa.
vedatraya | traya | n. lit. the three Vedas.
Vedadīpa |dīpa| m. lit. np. from the Vedadīpa "Light on the Vedas" by Mahīdhara.
vedapāṭhaka [pāṭhaka] amnf vedapāṭhikā reciter of the Veda.

Vedapriya [priya] m. myth. np. of the pious brah mane Vedapriya, who lived with his 4 sons at the hermitage of Sāndīpani; they were persecuted by the asura Dūṣaṇa₁; they established a linga of earth | pārthiva |; ŚivaMahākāla emerged from it to kill the demon; cf. Mahākāleśvara.
vedabāhya | bāhya | amnf vedabāhyā soc. outside the Vedic tradition; unorthodox, heretic. vedabāhyavratalingadhārin who bears the outward signs of a heretic.
vedabāhyatara [tara] amnf vedabāhyatarā compar. soc. excluded from Brahmanical orthodoxy.
vedabhraṣṭa | bhraṣṭa | amnf vedabhraṣṭā soc. fallen from the Veda.

vedavat |vat| amnf vedavatī which is familiar with the Veda | myth. [Bhavişyapurāṇa] np. of King Vedavān, son of Pradyota₁ — f. vedavatī myth. [Rām.] np. of the beautiful vedavatī, incarnation of Vāk, daughter of Kuśadhvaja, who would not marry her to anyone except Vișnu; she lived as an ascetic in the woods, where Rāvaṇa met her and disrespected her; she threw herself into the fire cursing it, and vowing to be reborn out of all misery, a pious daughter of a righteous man; at the tretāyuga she was reborn as Sītā.
vedavādin [vādin] amnf vedavādinī who celebrates the Veda.
Vedavicāra [vicāra] m. lit. np. of the Vedavicāra, work of Sāmaśāstrī Dravida Dvivedī; it deals not. with the observances of the drāvidās.
vedavid [vid₃] amnf poured into the Veda.
vedavidyā [vidyā] f. knowledge of the Veda.
vedavirodha [virodha] amnf vedavirodha in contradiction with the Veda.
vedavyāsa [vyāsa] m. bed. n.p. of vedavyāsa "Composer of the Veda", epith. of vyāsa or Bādarāyaṇa.
vedaṣaḍaṅga |ṣaḍaṅga| n. cf. vedāṅga.

vedānga [anga₁] n. phil. ["appendix of the Veda"] ancillary discipline of the Veda; there are 6 of them [vedaṣaḍaṅga]: phonetics [śikṣā], ritual | kalpa|, grammar | vyākaraṇa|, hermeneutics [nirukta], the metrics prosody of hymns |chandas| and astronomy astrology |jyotiṣa|; these six members of the Veda are compared to resp. his nose, his hands, his mouth, his ears and his eyes.
vedāngajyotisa | jyotisa| n. astr. np. from the Vedāngajyotisa, a very ancient astronomical treatise, attributed to Lagadha.
vedādhikāra | adhikāra | m. authority of the Veda.
vedādhyayana [adhyayana] n. soc. reading, personal study of the Veda, one of the 6 duties of a brah mane [saţkarmāni].
vedādhyāpaka [adhyāpaka] m. soc. teacher of the Veda.
vedādhyāpana [adhyāpana] n. soc. teaching of the Veda, one of the 6 duties of a brahmin |satkarmāni|.
vedādhyāya [adhyāya] amnf vedādhyāyī who recites the Veda; reciter.

Vedānta [anta] m. phil. np. of the Vedānta "culmination of the Veda", one of the 6 points of view [saddarśana] of orthodox Hinduism, doctrine attributed to vyāsa, developed in the esoteric teachings [upaniṣad] and by Śaṅkarācārya; it deals with the metaphysics of nonduality [advaita].
Vedāntadīpa [dīpa] m. bed. n.p. from the Vedāntadīpa of Rāmānujācārya.

Vedāntadeśika [deśika] m. lit. np. of the Vaishnava poet and philosopher Vedāntadešika (1268–1369); nephew and successor of Rāmānuja, he lived in Śrīranga; he is credited with two philosophical works on the pañcarātra tradition: the Pañcarātrarakṣā and the Saccaritraraksā; his Tattvatīkā is a commentary on Rāmānuja's Śrībhāsya, his Tātparyacandrikā is a commentary on the Gītā; his Seśvaramīmāṃsā unifies the mīmāmsā viewpoint; He is credited with numerous other works, such as the Hamsasandesa, the Nyāyasiddhāntajana, the Pādukāsahasra, the Dayāśataka, the Hamsasandeśa, the Yādavābhyudaya and the Saṃkalpasūryodaya; he is also called Venkatanātha.
Vedāntaparibhāṣā [paribhāṣā] f. bed. n.p. of the Vedāntaparibhāṣā.
Vedāntasāra₁ [sāra] m. bed. n.p. of Vedāntasāra₁ "Essence of Vedānta", work by Rāmānuja explaining the viśiṣṭādvaita doctrine | bed. n.p. of Vedāntasāra₂, work of Sadānanda.

Vedāntasūtra |sūtra| n. pl. lit. np. of the collections of Vedāntasūtra; cf. Brahmasūtra. vedāntādhikaraṇaratnamālā | adhikaraṇa ratnamālā] f. lit. np. of the vedāntādhikaraṇaratnamālā, first work of Mādhavācārya, dealing with the Vedānta system in prose.
vedāntin |in| mr. phil. holder of Vedānta. jainagandhivedāntin "vedāntin with a par fum jaina", qualification of Bhāskara₁ by Vedāntadeśika.
vedārtha | artha | mr. phil. meaning of Veda.
vedārthaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. np. from the vedārthaprakāśa "Explanation of the meaning of the Veda", commentary by Sāyaṇa on the Veda.
vedārthavid [vid₂] amnf who knows the meaning of the Veda.
vedārthasamgraha [samgraha] m. bed. n.p. from the vedārthasamgraha of Rāmānuja.
vedaka [agt. vid₂] amnf vedikā qui an nonce, qui proclame.
vedana₁ [agt. vid₂] amnf Vedanā who announces, who proclaims — act. n. perception, knowledge | proclamation — f. cf. Vedanā.
vedana₁ [agt. vid₂] amnf Vedanā who finds; who procures — act. n. act of finding, discovery; encounter | soc. marriage (not. of a woman of class śūdra with a man of class dvija).

Vedanā [f. vedana₁] f. pain; torture; agony | myth. np. of Vedanā, pain personified, daughter of Anrta | bd. sensation, one of the 5 aggregates [skandha] of the ego; it is the 7th cause of suffering [pratītyasamutpāda].
vedanāvat |vat| amnf vedanāvatī who suffers painfully.
vedanīya [pfp. [2] vid₂] amnf ve danīyā ifc. which must be understood as; which must be expressed by; which must be felt as | to know; to make known.
vedaya [agt. That. vid₂] amnf vedayā which informs.
vedayat [ppr. That. vid₂] amnf veddantī by making it known.
vedayitavya [pfp. [3] ca. vid₂] amnf vedayitavyā that must be made known, of which one must inform.
vedayitr [agt. ca. vid₂] amnf vedayitrī who perceives; who knows.
vedayitvā [abs. ca. vid₂] ind. having in former.
vedas₁ [obj. vid₂] n. ved. science, knowledge.
vedas₂ [obj. vid₂] n. ved. possessions, riches.
vedi₁ [vid₂] f. sacrificial space; altar, sacrificial pit; bench, terrace | ved. sacrificial area, leveled ground where the altar, rectangular hollow, is surrounded by three fires | var. vedī id.
vedi₁ iic. vedin.
vedika [ka] m. seat; bench — f. vedikā ved. sacrifice area; altar of sacrifice | balcony; arch balustrade. not. balustrade surrounding a stūpa.
veditā [tā] f. knowledge of, familiarity with (iic.).
veditva [tva] n. id.
veditavya [pfp. [3] vid₂] amnf veditavyā namely, that which deserves to be known, that which must be learned.
vedin [agt. vid₂] ifc. amnf vedinī who knows, who is familiar with (iic.).
vedya [pfp. [1] vid₂] amnf vedyā who must be known | famous, illustrious. vedaiśca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ BhG. I am known by all the Vedas.
vedha [act. vyadh] m. action of piercing, of wounding; penetration, perforation | wound | depth (of an excavation, etc.) | (alchemy) transmutation.
vedhaka [agt. vyadh] m. perforator (not. of gems) — n. coriander | unwinnowed grain.
vedhana [act. vyadh] n. act of piercing, of reaching with an arrow | penetration, perforation — f. vedhanī perforator; drill, auger | not. elephant ear perforator.
vedhanīya [pfp. [2] vyadh] amnf ved hanīyā suitable for being pierced; penetrable, vulnerable.
vedhás [vidh₁] amnf pious, virtuous, brave — m. myth. np. of Vedhā, creator or ordering god; epith. of Brahmā, Prajāpati, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Daksa, etc.
√ ven v. [1] pr. (venati) pp. (venita) to desire, to wait impatiently, to long for.

vená [agt. ven] amnf venī anxious, desirous — m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Vena "Desire", son of Anga₁ and Sunīthā; under the bad influence of his mother, he committed sacrileges which caused his downfall; the brahmins churned his body, to extract Evil in the form of the niṣāda race, then created PṛthuViṣṇu from Good.
vep [ca. vip] v. [10] pr. (vepayati) to make tremble, to agitate.
vepa [act. vip] m. trembling, shivering.
vepáthu [vepathu] m. trembling.
vepana [act. vip] n. trembling, shivering; palpitation.
vepas [abstr. vip] n. trembling, shivering; agitation.
vepita [pp. That. vip] amnf vepitā trem blant.
vema [vā₃] m. loom — n. veman id.
vera mn corps || lat. cadaver; fr. cadavre.

velā f. border, limit, edge; shore, bank; coast, seaside; time limit; epoch, hour, time; last hour, hour of death | tide; current; gum. velāyām at the right time; in season. kā velā vartate what time is it? velā bhoktum it is time to eat. kā velā prāptāyāḥ how long has it been here? velopalakṣaṇārtham determining the time.
velākula | kula | n. seaside, coast — amnf velākulā situated on the coast; agitated by the waves.
velātikrama | atikrama | m. exceeding the time limit, delay. velātikramah kṛtah you are late.
veśá [agt. viś₁] m. farmer, tenant; neighbor, resident; vassal | tent, dwelling; business brothel; prostitution | |veṣa| clothing, costume.
veśana [act. viś₁] n. act of entering, admission; habitation — f. veśanī entrance, vestibule.
veśma iic. veśman.
veśmabhū | bhū₂ | f. land, site of a dwelling.
véśman [viś₁man] n. house, dwelling; ap. apartment; palace | astr. constellation.
veśya [pfp. [1] viś₁] amnf veśyā ifc. ⟨iic.⟩ where one must enter — n. neighborhood; vassal territory prostitution — f. veśyā courtesan, prostitute. veśyam vāh to engage in prostitution.
veśyālaya [ālaya] mn house of prostitution; in the right of perdition.

veṣa [act. viṣ₁] m. work, activity | costume, attire; appearance. veṣaṃ kṛ to put on a costume; not. to take on the (orange) habit of a renunciant [sannyāsin]. veṣaṃ dhā to disguise oneself, to put on the air of.
veṣaṇa [act. viṣɪ] n. service, function — f. veşanā id.
√ vest v. [1] pr. r. (vestate) pp. (vestita) pf. (ā, pari, vi) to coil; to molt (serpent) — ca. (veṣṭayati) to wrap, to surround, to cover; to coil (not. tur ban).
vesta [agt. vest] m. enclosure, envelope | noose.
vestaka [agt. vest] m. enclosure, enclosure wall gram. delimitation by the indirect speech particle iti — n. turban.

vestana [act. vest] n. act of encircling, surrounding, wrapping | bandage; belt | tiara, diadem, enclosure, fence; casket. dukūlapaṭapallavena kṛtaśiroveṣṭanaḥ |K.| he wrapped a silk turban around his head.
vestitá [pp. vest] amnf vestitā surrounded, wrapped; enclosed; besieged, encircled; captured covered, veiled (by (i.)) | twisted (rope) — n. in a circle | turban.
vesya [pfp. [1] vis₁] amnf vesyā costumed, disguised; made up (not. like an actor).
vesara mf vesarī organic. zoo. mule |geo. designates the country south of the Kṛṣṇā₁ as far as Cape Comorin.
vai conj. cl. certainly, in truth, indeed, really, precisely. yadi ... vai ... si ... on the contrary ...
Vaikartana [*vikartana] amnf vaikar tanā relating to the Sun — m. myth. np. of Vaikartana "the Flayed One", epith. of Karna after he tore off the golden breastplate with which he was born.
vaikalpa [*vikalpa] n. doubt, indecision; am biguity | the fact of being optional.
vaikalpika [*vikalpaika] amnf vaikal pikī optional; subject to discussion.
vaikalpikatā [tā] f. fact of being optional.
vaikalpikatva [tva] n. id.
vaikalpikasamāsa [samāsa] m. gram. compound word analyzable by paraphrase [vigrahavākya]; opp. nityasamāsa.
vaikalya [*vikalaya] n. imperfection, defect, incompetence, insufficiency; confusion.

vaikuntha [*vikutha] amnf vaikuntha myth. relating to Viṣṇu "the Immanent" — mn myth. np. of the Vaikuntha "(sky) of Viṣṇu"; cf. vaikunthasvarga — m. myth. ["of the sky of Viṣṇu"] epith. of various gods, not. Indra and ViṣṇuKṛṣṇa.
Vaikunthagadya [gadya] n. bed. n.p. from Vaikunthagadya, devotional poem by Rāmānuja.
vaikunthacaturdaśī [caturdaśī] f. soc. fourteenth day of the clear fortnight of the month kārttika, sacred [2 to Viṣṇu, also called narakacaturdaśī; it begins the festival of Dīpāvali.
vaikunthacaturmūrti [caturmūrti] m. myth. form of Vișnu with 4 faces, representing Varāha, Narasimha, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa; cf. caturānana₁.
vaikunthasvarga [svarga] m. myth. Heaven of Viṣṇu; neither fear nor obstacles exist there; it is symbolized by an umbrella, whose axis is Mount Meru.
vaikunthaikādaśī | ekādaśī | f. soc. eleventh day of the clear fortnight of the month pausa; it is sacred to Vișnu, and fasted | vrata | ; it is an important festival in South India.

vaikṛta [*vikṛtia] amnf vaikṛtā modified; derivational, secondary | changing; subject to modification | deformed; artificial; opp. prākṛta | phil. sound [dhvani] in the form of a spoken word — n. change, modification; alteration, deformation — f. vaikṛtā ifc. change, modification of (iic.).
vaikṛtadhvani [dhvani] m. phon. sound emitted by a spoken word (with phonetic variations, tone, ac cent); opp. prākṛtadhvani.
vaikṛtika [*vikṛtika] amnf vaikṛtikā subject to change | modified.
vaikṛtya [*vikṛtiya] amnf vaikṛtyā changed — n. change; alteration; disfigurement | aversion, disgust.
vaiklava [*viklava] n. perplexity; dejection.
vaiklavya [*viklavaya] n. perplexity; dejection | weakness; discouragement; mental deficiency. vaiklasyam māvalambasva do not give in to discouragement. jarāvaiklavyapralapitam senile babble.
vaikharī f. [vaikharīvāc] articulated discourse, understandable speech | faculty of speech | phil. [Bhartrhari] intelligible speech, 3rd stage [vapus] of the manifestation of the word.

vaikhānasá [*Vikhānasa] mf vaikhānasī soc. anchorite according to the rule of the hermit |muni| Vikhānasa; it is an extreme form of hermit [vānaprastha]; he must eat only roots and wild berries | soc. hereditary caste of Vaishnavite priests of South India [arcaka] descended from these ascetics; they replaced Vedic sacrifice with temple rites; they bear a brand on the shoulder; one becomes Vaikhānasa through the prenatal rite viṣṇubali | lit. np. of Vaikhānasa, vidūṣaka of the Kaumudīmahotsava.
Vaikhānasamantrapāṭha | mantrapāṭha | mr. bed. n.p. from Vaikhānasamantrapātha, collection of Vish Nouit hymns.

vaicakṣaṇya [*vicakṣaṇaya] n. experience, competence, expertise in (loc.). dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu vaicakṣaṇyaṃ kalāsu ca | karoti kīrtiprītim ca sādhukāvyanibandhanam || [Bhāmaha] Competence in morals and art, as well as the requirement to preserve one's reputation, are obstacles to good poetry.
vaicārika [*vicāraika] amnf vaicārikī rational.
vaicārikatā [tā] f. rationality.
vaicitrya [*vicitraya] n. diversity, variety; multiplicity.
vajayanta [*vijayanta] m. flag, banner; banner; not. banner of Indra — f. cf. vaijuantī — n. vajayanta np. from the town of vaijayanta; cf. vajayantī.

vaijayantī [f. vajayanta] f. victory banner or garland | myth. not. Vișnu neck adornment | geo. n.p. from the city of vaijayantī "Victo rieuse", epith. of Vanavāsī, very ancient city of Karnāta, secondary capital of the Sātavāhanās, then capital of the Kadamba dynasty in the 4th century | bed. n.p. vaijayantī₁ from the lexicon of Yādavaprakāśa; cf. vajayantīkośa.

vaijayantīkośa [kośa] m. lit. np. of the vaijayantīkośa, lexicon due to Yādavaprakāśa; it includes a Paryāyabhāga section of synonymous words, and a Nānārthabhāga section of polysemous words; it explains the underlying concepts in greater detail than the Amarakosa.
vaijayantīmālā [mālā] f. myth. magic garland protecting from injury, given by Indra to King Uparicara Vasu₂; eternally fresh, it does not fade.

vaijayika [*vijayaika] amnf vaijayikī that confers or predicts victory — f. vaijayikī strategy, one of the 64 arts [kalā]. vaijayikīnām vidyānām jñānam the knowledge of the knowledge that brings victory.
vaijñānika [*vijñānaika] amnf vaijñānikā scholar, learned; scientist.
vaiḍāla var. baiḍāla [*viḍāla] amnf vaidālī relating to the cat, characteristic of the cat; hypocritical feline, impostor.
vaidālavratina [vratin] m. hypocritical ascetic, false ascetic.
vaidūrya cf. vaidūrya.
vaitaṇḍika [*vitaṇḍāika] amnf vaitandikā phil. champion of sophistry; who supports an arbitrary thesis for the simple pleasure of bringing up the debate — m. sophist.
vaitathya [*vitathya] n. falsehood, error.
vaitanika [*vetanaika] amnf vaitanikī who lives on his wages; salaried worker — m. worker, day laborer.

vaitaraṇa [*vitaraṇa] amnf Vaitaraṇī who wants to cross (the river) — n. phil. transport of souls on the river leading to the infernal regions — f. Vaitaraṇī myth. np. of the underground river Vaitaraņī, leading the dead to the kingdom of Yama; it is the Indian Styx; the Pāṇḍavās bathed in it during their exile, on the way to Mount Mahendra | geo. river of the Kalinga (mod. Baitaranī, which passes through Jajpur in Orissa).
vaitasa [*vaitasa] amnf vaitasī made of reed, rattan — mn wicker basket. vaitasī vṛtti ["action of reed"] the act of adapting to circumstances. vaitasīm vṛttim āśri to yield to a superior force.
vaitāna [*vitāna] amnf vaitānā soc. concerning the 3 sacred fires — n. soc. great rite, performed with the 3 sacred fires.
vaitānakuśala [kuśala] amnf vaitānakuśalā lit. able to perform the great rite.
vaitānasūtra [sūtra] n. lit. np. of the vaitānasūtra; it describes the ritual of the Atharvaveda.
vaitāla [*vetāla] amnf vaitālā relating to the undead.
vaitālika [*vetālaika] m. man possessed by an undead; sorcerer | soc. court herald-poet; he proclaims the hour poetically, including a panegyric of the King.
vaitālīya [*vetālaīya] amnf vaitālīyā relating to the undead — n. phone. name of a meter mātrāvṛtta; it corresponds to the varṇavṛtta syn meters. viyoginī and aparavaktra.

vaidarbha [*Vidarbha] amnf vaidarbhī re latif au Vidarbha | lit. poetic style [rīti] of the Vi darbha; opp. gauḍa — m. man or prince of the Vi darbha — f. vaidarbhī princess of the Vidarbha | lit. poetic style [rīti], avoiding long compounds in verse, but favoring them in prose; it was used not. by Daṇḍī₁ and Kālidāsa; opp. gauḍī | myth. np. of vaidarbhī, epith. of Lopāmudrā, of Damayantī, of Rukminī.
vaidarbharīti | rīti | f. lit. style of poetic composition of the Vidarbha.
vaidala [*vidala] m. grain vegetable, not. split pea | wicker container.

vaidalya [*vidalaya] n. [vaidalyaprakaraṇa] lit. np. of the Vaidalyaprakaraņa "Dismantling of the categories", a phil. bd. treatise by Nāgārjuna refuting the 16 categories [padārtha] classifying the methods of argumentation of the Nyāya doctrine.

vaidika [*Vedaika] amnf vaidikī Vedic; in accordance with the Veda, prescribed by the Veda | gram. refers to the Vedic language; opp. laukika | knowing the Veda — m. soc. Brahmin versed in the Veda — n. Vedic injunction; extract from the Veda.
vaidiśa [*vidiśā] amnf vaidikī geo. country of vaidiśa, capital vidiśā; cf. Daśārṇās.
vaidusa [*vidvasa] amnf vaidusī scholar — f. vaiduṣī science; expertise, erudition.
vaidusya [*vidvasya] n. science; expertise, erudition.
vaidūrya [*vidūraya] n. blue beryl, aquamarine; astr. it is the jewel associated with Ketu | semiprecious stone (cat's eye, lapis lazuli, etc.) | var. vaidūrya id.
vaideśika [*videśaika] amnf vaideśikī non-native — mf vaideśikī foreigner.

Vaideha [*Videha] m. soc. man or prince of Videha | man of mixed caste (not. of vaiśya father and brāhmaṇī mother) — f. Vaidehī woman of Videha | myth. [Rām.] np. of Vaidehī, epith. of Sītā "princess of Videha".
vaidya [*Vedaya] amnf vaidyā scholar, learned person — m. learned man, expert; physician — f. vaidyī wife of a physician.

vaidyanātha [nātha] m. geo. np. of vai dyanātha, one of the 12 radiant signs of Šiva [jyotirlinga], established in Devagarh (mod. Deogarh in Bihāra/Jharakhanda); it is also one of the 51 holy places of the Goddess [śaktipīṭha].

Vaidyarāj [rāj₂] m. myth. np. of Vaidyarāj "King of physicians", epith. of Dhanvantari | var. vai dyarāja id. vaidyarāja namastubhyam yamarājasahodarah yamastu harati prāṇān tvam tu prāṇān dhanānyapi I salute you, O physician, you are the brother of Yama; while Yama takes our life, you take both life and money from us.
vaidyavidyā [vidyā] f. science of medicine.
vaidyaka [*vidyāka] amnf vaidyakā medical — m. doctor — n. medicine, medical science.
vaidyuta [*vidyut₂a] amnf vaidyutā concerning lightning; similar to thunder — mn (fire) of lightning.
vaidyutaka [*vidyut₂aka] amnf vaidyu tikā mod. electronic.
vaidha [*vidhi] amnf vaidhā prescribed; legal.
vaidharmya [*vidharmaya] n. illegality; difference in treatment, injustice | difference; heterogeneity.
vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta |dṛṣṭānta| mr. phil. |Nyāya| example in negative support of a syllogism, falsifying both the cause | hetu| and the thesis | sādhya|; opp. sadharmyadrstānta.

vaidhasa [*vedhasa] amnf vaidhasī pro duit par le destin | composed by Brahmā — m. myth. AB. patr. de Hariścandra "son of Vedhā". hariścandro ha vaidhasa aikṣvāko rājāputra āsa | tasya ha śatam jāyā babhūvuḥ || Hariścandra himself, son of Vedhā, of the line of Ikṣvāku, was a king without sons; he, however, had a hundred wives.

vaidhātra [*vidhātṛa] amnf vaidhātrī from Brahmā | myth. refers to the 4 (or 7) sages [ṛṣi] from the mind of Brahmā [vaidhātra] to populate the World; cf. Sana, Sanaka, Sanatkumāra, Sanandana; they inhabit the sky [loka] Janaloka.
vaidheya [*vidhieya] amnf vaidheyā ["struck by fate"] idiot, fool.
vainateya [*vinatāeya] mf vainateyī myth. n.p. from vainateya, epith. of Garuda "son of vinatā".
vainayika [*vinayaika] amnf vainayikī relating to discipline or good conduct — f. vainayikī military discipline, one of the 64 arts [kalā]. vainayikīnām vidyānām jñānam soc. aptitude for command.
vainītaka [*vinītaka] mn litter; horse-drawn carriage; sedan chair.
vaiparītya [*viparītaya] n. contrariety; op position; inverse | counterpart; incoherence. brhaspatir ayam mūrkhah This fool is a true Brhaspati (ironic metaphor).
vaiphalya [*viphalaya] n. uselessness. vaiphalyād vakti nānṛṇam [Dharmakīrti] He (Bud dha) does not speak for nothing.
vaibudha [*vibudha₁] amnf vaibudhī concerning the gods; divine.
vaibhava [*vibhava] n. power; notoriety, grandeur; glory.
vaibhāṣika [*vibhāṣāika] amnf vaibhāṣikā optional | bd. follower of an externalist doctrine; 4 varieties are recognized; cf. sarvāstivāda.
vaibhrāja [*vibhrāja] m. bed. [HV.] patr. by Visvaksena₁.
vaimatya [*vimatiya] n. difference of opinion aversion.
vaimanasya [*vimanasya] n. sadness, discouragement.
vaimala [*vimala] amnf vaimalā lit. is said of sacred texts śaiva , of the atimārga tradition.
vaimalya [*vimalaya] n. purity; cleanliness.

vaimātra [*vimātṛa] m. half-brother; syn. vimātrja — f. vaimātri var. vaimātrkā half-sister. vaimātra bhrātṛ half-brother; brother-in-law. vaimātṛkā bhaginī half-sister; sister-in-law (opp. svakasvakā bhaginī).
vaimānika [*vimāna₁ika] amnf vaimānikī myth. born in a celestial aeronautical chariot.
vaiyadhikaraṇya [*vyadhikaraṇaya] n. gram. non-agreement in case | in relation to different subjects.
vaiyarthya [*vyarthaya] n. uselessness.
vaiyasa [*vyāsa] amnf vaiyasā derived from vyāsa.

vaiyākaraṇa [*vyākaraṇa] amnf vaiyākaraṇī relating to grammar | one who studies/knows grammar — mf vaiyākaraņī grammarian. prathame hi vidvāmso vaiyākaranāh vyākaraṇamūlatvāt sarvavidyānām [Dhvanyāloka] grammarians are first among scholars, for grammar is at the root of all studies.

vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇa [bhūṣaṇa] n. lit. np. from vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇa "Ornamentation of Grammar", copious treatise on the philosophy of language by Kaundabhatta, also called Vaiyākaraņasiddhāntabhūṣaṇa; it is a commentary on the Vaiyākaraṇamatonmajjana.
vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra [sāra] m. bed. n.p. from the Vaiyākaraņabhūṣaṇasāra “Linguistic quintessence”, summary of the previous one, also by Kaundabhatta.
vaiyākaranamatonmajjana [mataunmajjana] n. bed. n.p. from the Vaiyākaraṇamatonmajjana of Bhaṭṭoji Dīksita.
vaiyākaraṇasiddhānta [siddhānta] m. treatise on grammar.
vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntabhūṣaṇa [bhūṣaṇa] n. cf. vaiyākaraṇabhūsaṇa.

Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntamañjūṣā [mañjūṣā] f. bed. n.p. from the Vaiyākaraņasiddhāntamañjūṣā “Treasure of Grammatical Knowledge”, a linguistic treatise by Nāgeśa Bhaṭṭa; it was summarized in the Vaiyākaraņasiddhāntalaghumañjūṣā, and condensed even further in the Vaiyākaraṇa siddhāntaparamalaghumañjūṣā; Durbalācārya made the Kuñcikā commentary on it, Bālambhaṭṭa made the Kalā commentary on it.
vaiyāghra [*vyāghra] amnf vaiyāghrā relating to the tiger | covered with a tiger skin — n. tiger skin.
vaiyāghrapadya [*vyāghrapadya] amnf vaiyāghrapadyā composed by Vyāghrapād — m. patr. of muni vaiyāghrapadya; gotra name.
vaiyāsika [*vyāsaika] amnf vaiyāsikī relating to, composed by vyāsa.
vaiyāsīya [*vyāsaīya] amnf vaiyāsīyā relating to vyāsa.
vaiyuṣṭa [*vyuṣṭa] amnf vaiyuṣṭā to be performed at dawn.

vaira [*vīra] amnf vairā hostile, unfriendly — n. hostility, enmity; quarrel; hostility towards (i.) — f. vairā ifc. hostility towards — v. [11] pr. r. (vairāyate) pp. (vairāyita) to do a hostile act, to start hostilities, to attack (pratiacc. i. rangle.
vairabhakti | bhakti | f. phil. hatred turned into devotion; it results from the common essence of the
hatred [dveṣa] and love [rāga] as forms of envy [saṅga]; syn. dveṣabhakti.
vairabhāva [bhāva] m. hostile attitude.
vairayātanā [yātanā] f. revenge.
vairasādhana [sādhana] n. reason for enmity | revenge; syn. niryātana.
vairāga [*virāga₁] n. absence of passion, liberation of desires.
vairāgin [in] amnf vairāgiṇī who has freed himself from all passion and all desire — m. soc. ascetic, not. vaisnava.
vairāgya [*virāga₁ya] n. renunciation of the world, cessation of passions; self-denial.
vairāgyaprakarana [prakarana] n. bed. n.p. of Vairāgyaprakaraņa, 2nd section of Moksopāya.
vairāgyaśataka [śataka] n. lit. du np. vairāgyaśataka, collection of 100 poems on renunciation due to Bhartrhari₁.
vairi iic. vairin.

vairisimha |simha| mr. hist. n.p. of king vairisimha "Lion among the heroes", of the Paramāra dynasty; he reigned in Mālava in the 9th century; he transferred his capital from Ujjayinī to Dhārā; he is ancestor of Bho jadeva.
vairin [vairain] amnf vairiṇī hostile, in friendly — m. enemy | hero.
vairudhya [*virudhya] m. hostility, obstruction, opposition.
vairudhyavāda | vāda | m. dialectic.
vairūpa [*virūpa] m. myth. descendant of virūpa | pl. vairūpās myth. syn. aigirasas.
vairūpya [*virūpaya] n. multiplicity of forms, diversity | deformity, ugliness.
vairūpyatā [tā] f. condition of deformity.
Vaireśvari [*vīreśvara] m. hist. np. of Vairesvari "Son of Vīresvara", patr. of Hari₁ Dīkṣita.

vairocana [*Virocana] amnf vairo canā solar — m. bd. np. of vairocana "the Light", dhyānibuddha of the Centre in the mahāyāna pantheon, represented in gen. in dharmacakra mudrā | myth. np. of vairocana₁, patr. of Bali "Son of Virocana".
vaila [*vila] amnf vailī rupestre.
vailasthāná [sthāna] n. rock habitat, cavern; ruins, cemetery.

vailakṣya [*vilakṣaya] n. absence of mark or distinctive sign | failure to achieve one's goal: disappointment, annoyance | strangeness, absence of naturalness, discomfort, embarrassment; feeling of shame.
vaivarṇya [*vivarṇaya] n. change of color | the change of complexion, a sāttvikānubhāva | soc. expulsion from one's caste or tribe | heterogeneity; diversity.
vaivarta [*vivarta] n. cf. brahmavaivarta purāna.

vaivasvata [*vivasvata] amnf vaivas vatī relating to Vivasvān; of the solar lineage | myth. np. of vaivasvata, patr. of Satyavrata Son of Vi vasvān, 7th Manu of the kalpa ; he is the ManuYama of the current era; he was saved from the flood by a giant fish, to whose horn he hung his boat; cf. Satyavrata — f. Vaivasvatī myth. np. of Vaivasvatī, patr. of Yamī || pkt. Vaiśvata.
vaivāhya [*vivāhaya] amnf vaivāhyā nuptial — n. nuptial pomp.
vaiśadya [*viśadaya] n. clarity; purity; freshness; intelligibility.

Vaiśampāyana [*Viśampaāyana] m. myth. [Mah.] patr. of Vaiśampāyana "Son of Viśampa", disciple of vyāsa; at his request he recited the Mah. at Janamejaya | lit. [K.] np. of Vaiśampāyana₁, son of Sukanāsa and Manoramā₁, companion of Prince Candrāpīda₁; he is the reincarnation of the hero Puṇḍarīka₂; sent by Candrāpīda₁ to declare his love to Kādambarī, he falls in love with Mahāśvetā, but she curses him to be reborn as the narrating parrot at the court of King Sūdraka₁; He dies, which will (apparently) cause Candrāpīḍa₁ to die of grief.
Vaiśalī cf. Vaiśālī.
vaiśasa [*viśasa] amnf vaiśasā destruc teur — n. destruction, dismemberment, massacre; calamity, war, butchery — f. vaiśasā ifc. des truction de (iic.).
Vaiśākha [*viśākha] m. month of Vīśākhe (April-May), 2nd lunar month, and 1st solar month | soc. festival of Vīśākha, celebrating the anniversary of the Bud
dha [buddhajayantī] — f. vaiśākhī its full moon [pūrnimā]; cf. buddhapūrnimā || Sinhala vesak; pali vesākha.
vaiśārada [*viśārada] amnf vaiśāradī scholar, expert; infallible — n. erudition, expertise — f. vaiśāradī lit. title of scholarly works.
vaiśāradya [*viśāradaya] n. great experience, wisdom; expertise (in (loc.)); infallibility | bd. not. sureness of judgment of Buddha.

Vaiśālī [*viśāla] f. myth. np. of Vaiśālī (or Vaisalī), a wife of Vasudeva | geo. np. of the city [nagara] of Vaiśālī₁ in Bihāra (mod. Ba sarh, Muśannarpur district, 50 km north of mod. Paṭnā); it was the capital of the Licchavi clan and of the Vrji republican confederation, in the 5th century BC; its regent Cetaka fought Ajātaśatru₂; Mahāvīra was born there, Buddha gave his last sermon there, Vimalakīrti lived there, Śiśunāga reigned there; it was the site of the second Buddhist council.
vaiśiṣṭa [*viśiṣṭa] n. distinction; difference.
vaiśiṣṭya [*viśiṣṭaya] n. phil. possession of a distinctive property; distinction; qualification | singularity; difference | preeminence, excellence, superiority.

vaiśeṣika [*viśeṣaika] amnf vaiśeṣikā particular, specific; distinguished, excellent — n. phil. np. of the Vaiśesika "systematic", a discriminative philosophical doctrine dating back to the 1st century, traditionally attributed to Kaṇāda; it deals with discerning the characteristic differences [viśeṣa] between things; it is one of the 6 points of view | saddarśana | of orthodox Hinduism, of ontological and systematic concern; it classifies concepts into 6 ontological categories [padārtha]: substances [dravya₁], properties [guna], activities [karman], universals or generic substrates [sāmānya] or discriminative substrates [viśeṣa], and inherences [samavāya].
vaiśeṣikasūtra [sūtra] n. lit. np. of the Vaiśeṣikasūtra, exposition of the discriminatory doctrine [Vaiseșika] in ten books [adhyāya], attributed to Kaṇāda.
vaiśeṣikasūtravṛtti [vṛtti] f. bed. n.p. of the vaiśeṣikasūtravṛtti, a gloss of the Vaiśeṣikasūtra due to Candrānanda.
vaiśeṣya [*viśeṣya] n. particularity, specificity; generic distinction | difference; superiority, preeminence.

vaiśya [*viś₂ya] m. soc. ["man of the people"] member of the 3rd class, Who lives by his labor; farmer, breeder, merchant, craftsman, banker | pl. vaiśyās soc. the class of workers — f. vaiśyā soc. woman of this class — n. subordination, dependence.
vaiśyavarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Bhūmyādikānda, dealing with merchants.

vaiśravaṇa [*viśravaṇa] m. myth. np. of Vaiśravana "Descendant of Viśravā", father of Ku bera, but also of Rāvaņa and his brothers | bd. king of the north (also called Jambhala in Tibet); he is often depicted with a mongoose [nakula] cra song of jewels | lit. [DKC.] np. of vaiśravaṇa₁, merchant of Pāṭaliputra, father of Sāgaradattā and Sindhudattā || pali vessavana.

vaiśvadevá [*viśvedeva] amnf vaiśvadevī relating to all the gods [Viśvedevās]; sacred to all the gods — n. soc. 1st rite of cāturmāsya at the full moon of the month māgha, where sacrifices are made to all the gods, and not. to Agni Who brings them the offerings — f. vaiśvadevī soc. variety of fire altar brick | soc. 8th day of the dark fortnight of the month māgha.
vaiśvadevabali [bali] m. offering (thrown) to all the gods.

Vaiśvānara [*viśvānara] amnf vaiśvānarī common to all men, universal, general; applying to all | venerated by all — m. myth. np. of Vaiśvānara, invocation of Agni "That which belongs to all men", in his aspect of the Sun, of light or of fire āhavanīya | phil. [Vedānta] awakened aspect of consciousness, knower of material reality, associated with the Sun, residing in the right eye.

vaisamya [*visamaya] n. irregularity (ter rain) | inequality; diversity; disproportion | difficulty; distress; calamity | impropriety, incorrectness; fault error (about (loc. iic.)) | solitude | med. imbalance of bodily humors.
vaiṣṭra [viṣ₁tra] n. phil. Heaven, paradise.

vaiṣṇava [*Viṣṇua] amnf vaiṣṇavī rela tif to, dedicated to, addressed to, belonging to Viṣṇu — m. vaishnuite, devotee of Viṣṇavāstra| myth. |Mah.| name of a missile |astra| that King Bhagadatta used against Arjuna; his father Naraka had obtained it from Viṣṇu — f. vaiṣṇavī myth. np. of vaiṣṇavī, śakti of Viṣṇu, a saptamātṛkā; she is worshipped in the cave of Vaisno Devī in the district of Jammu, 12 km above Katra; cf. Trikūţa.

Vaiṣṇavacāpa [cāpa] m. myth. np. of the Vaisnavacāpa bow that Viśvakarmā made for Vișnu; after his victorious duel with Siva, Vișnu gave it to Ŗcīka, who gave it to Jamadagni, who gave it to his son Parasurāma, who used it to confront Rāma on the return of the svayaṃvara from Sītā; cf. Śrnga.
Vaisnavadīkṣā [dīkṣā] f. soc. Vishnuite initiation; cf. taptamudrā.
voc [aor. vac] subj. (vocat) (peremptory) that he speaks. maivam vocah do not speak like that!
Vopadeva m. hist. n.p. from Vopadeva, poet and grammarian of the court of Hemādri₁ to Deva giri in Mahārāṣṭra (13th century); we owe him not. Mugdhabodha grammar and dhātupāṭha Kavi kalpadruma.
vauṣaṭ [vaṣaṭ] interj. soc. sacrificial formula with an offering to the fire.
vyáṃsa [viáṃsa] amnf vyaṃsā with broad shoulders — m. ved. cobra.
vyamsaka m. cheater; swindler.

Vyakta [pp. vyañj] amnf vyaktā clear, lim pide; visible, perceptible; manifest, evident — m. np. of Vyakta "Manifested", epithet of Viṣṇu — n. phil. [Sāṃkhya] the Manifested, evolution of Nature from the unManifested [avyakta]. vyaktam adv. manifestly, evidently. vyaktīkṛ to make manifest, to make evident. vyaktīkaraņa explication; making evident. vyaktībhū to become manifest or evident; to distinguish oneself.

Vyakti [act. vyañj] f. Manifestation; evidence; emergence | individuality; individual | phil. singular larity, particularity; index, discriminatory characteristic; opp. jāti | distinction, difference; syn. viśeṣa; opp. ākṛti | gram. grammatical gender.
vyaktitva [tva] n. phil. [Nyāya] individuality, by particularity. ghatavyaktitvam phil. fact of being a particular pot; distinguishes the pot in question from an arbitrary pot.

vyaktiviveka [viveka] m. lit. np. from Vyakti viveka "Analysis of Manifestation", a work of literary aesthetics by Mahimabhatta (circa 1025) questioning suggestion; it borrows from Dharmakīrti and criticizes the theory of dhvani of Anandavardhana.
Vyaktivivekavyākhyāna [vyākhyāna] n. lit. np. of the Vyaktivivekavyākhyāna of Ruyyaka, which is covered with commentary is an attack against the Vyakti viveka.
vyaktiśakti |śakti| f. gram. individual meaning of a word; opp. jātiśakti.
vyaktiśaktivāda [vāda] m. phil. doctrine of the particularism of meaning.
vyakṣa [viakṣa] m. astr. ["without latitude"] equator.
viagra |viagra| amnf viagra distracted, inat tentif | "who does not direct his attention to any particular point" | agitated; obsessed, preoccupied with (i. iic.).
vyagratā [tā] f. intense occupation (at (iic.)); concentration | perplexity, confusion.
vyagratva [vat] n. distraction | confusion, agitation — ifc. concentration on (iic.).
vyankața m. geo. np. of the hill of Vyankata, cf. venkata.
vyánga₁ [vianga₁] amnf vyangā without limbs; mutilated; lame; infirm — m. infirm.
vyáṅga₂ [agt. vyañj] amnf vyaṅgā ta cheté, mottled; marked with freckles — m. freckles | spot, imperfection.

vyaṅgya [pfp. [1] vyañj] amnf vyaṅgyā manifest, perceptible | gram. (meaning) suggested, in sinuate; implied — m. mod. satire. gunībhūtavyangya lit. (poetry) where the suggested meaning is secondary; opp. dhvani.
vyangyakarana [karana] n. satire, derision.
vyangyacitra [citra] n. mod. humorous drawing; comic strip.
vyangyārtha | artha | m. gram. suggested meaning; implied meaning.
vyangyokti [ukti] f. insinuation; implied.
√ vyac v. [3] pr. (vivyakti) to encompass; to take, to contain.
vyácas |abstr. vyac| n. extent, capacity; open space; degree of freedom. vyacas kṛ to dilate, extend, open.
vyaja [instr. vīj] m. fan.
vyajana [act. vīj] n. act of fanning | fan | mod. fan — f. vyajanā ifc. id. vyajanīkṛ to use as a fan. vyajanībhū to serve as a fan.

vyañj [viañj] v. [7] pr. (vyanakti) pp. (vyakta) pf. (abhi) ved. to anoint completely | to decorate, to beautify | to make visible, to reveal, to manifest — pr. r. (vyankte) to manifest itself — ps. (vyajyate) to be revealed, to be expressed — ca. (vyañjayati) to reveal, to manifest.

vyañjana [act. vyañj] n. sign, indication; in dice, symptom; badge, mark; sexual character | condiment, sauce, curry | disguise | suggestion; figurative expression; pointed remark, irony — m. phon. consonant; cf. hal — f. vyañjanā gram. suggestive meaning of a word or phrase; implicature; allusion, innuendo; opp. abhidhā₂; cf. dhvani. tapasvivyamjanopetāh disguised as ascetics.
vyañjanabhakti [bhakti] f. phone. epenthesis by intercalation of a consonant; opp. svarabhakti.
vyati pf. verbal prefix used for mutual or reciprocal action.
vyatikara [act. vyatikr] m. mixture | disturbing or astonishing resemblance.
vyatikaravat [vat] amnf vyatikaravatī mixed | unnatural.
vyatikarita |ita| amnf vyatikaritā mixed with (i. iic.).
vyatikīrņa [pp. vyatikr] amnf vya tikīrṇā mixed; scattered; upset.
vyatikṛ [viatikṛ] ps. (vyatikīryate) pp. (vya tikīrna) to be mixed with.
vyatikram [viatikram] v. [1] pr. (vya tikrāmvyati) to cross; overstep; overstep; transgress;
surpass | pass (time) | neglect, omit.
vyatikrama [act. vyatikram] m. overstepping; transgression; crime, vice | flow (time) | reverse, contrary order.
vyatikrámana [act. vyatikram] ifc. n. act of transgressing; sin.
vyatigam [viatigam] v. [3] pr. (vyatigac chati) pp. (vyatigata) to confront each other.
vyatijalp [viatijalp] v. [1] pr. (vyatijal pati) to gossip; to exchange rumors.
vyatitṛ [viatitṛ] fut. (vyatitariṣyati) on mounting completely.
vyatipath [viatipath] v. [3] pr. (vyatipathati) to recite mutually.

vyatirikta [pp. vyatiric] amnf vyati riktā excessive, immoderate; in excess; free | distinct from, other than (abl. iic.) — ifc. abundantly provided with (iic.) | free from; remainder of | having exceeded. vyatiriktam adv. excepted; with the exception of, without. svaravyatiriktam without accent.
vyatiric [viatiric] v. [4] pr. r. (vyatiri cyate) pp. (vyatirikta) surpass, dominate (acc. abl.); to be separated from (abl.).

vyatireka [act. vyatiric] m. distinction, separation; mutual exclusion; difference; incompatibility | gram. incompatibility of co-occurrence; opp. anvaya | lit. [alamkāra] figure of speech contrasting two concepts or objects — i.e., unlike, with the exception of, without (i.e.). vyatirekāt var. vyatireņa unlike, with the exception of (i.e.). vyatireke otherwise. vyatirekah sādhyabhāvahetvabhāvayoḥ
sāhacaryam [Nyāyakośa] Incompatibility is the association of the non-existence of a cause and the existence of a thesis.

vyatirekavyāpti [vyāpti] f. phil. [Nyāya] proof by contradiction; opp. anvayavyāpti. yatra sādhyābhāvah tatra hetvabhāvah iti vyati rekavyāptih The negation of the thesis implies the negation of the cause.
vyatirekālankāra [alankāra] m. lit. rhet. figure of speech where a metaphor is reversed.
vyatirekin [agt. vyatiric] amnf vyatirekiṇī that distinguishes, that differentiates; that ex clue; negative | different, inverse.
vyatilū [viatilū] v. [9] pr. (vyatilunāti) pr. r. (vyatilunīte) to cut each other off.
vyatişakta [pp. vyatişañj] amnf vyatisaktā interconnected; intertwined; mixed.
vyatiṣaṅga [act. vyatiṣañj] m. mutual connection; reciprocal relationship, mutual bond.
vyatisaigavat [vat] amnf vyatisaigavatī in interconnected; having a mutual connection.

vyatiṣañj [viatiṣañj] v. [1] pr. (vyatiṣajati) pr. r. (vyatisajate) pp. (vyatisakta) interconnect; intertwine; mix. [9 vyatisajati padārthān āntarah ko'pi na khalu bahi rupādhīn prītayah saṃśrayante [Uttararāmacarita] It is an internal reason that interconnects things, affinities certainly do not depend on external attributes.
vyatihas [viatihas] v. [1] pr. (vyatihasati) to laugh at each other. vyatihasanti they laugh at each other.
vyatihāra [act. vyatihr] m. exchange, trans position; alternation; reciprocity | soc. barter | exchange of blows or insults.
vyatihṛ [viatihṛ] v. [1] pr. (vyatiharati) to exchange, to transpose.
vyatī [viatī] v. [2] pr. (vyatyeti) pp. (vyatīta) to pass, to flow (time) | to deviate, to stray from [abl.] | to pass over; to surpass, to dominate, to overcome; to conquer, to omit, to neglect.

vyatīta [pp. vyatī] amnf vyatītā past, bygone (time); abandoned | that which deviates from [abl.] omitted, neglected; that which comes too late. sa śrutipatham vyatītah he was too far away to reach it.
vyatītakāla |kāla₁| amnf vyatītakālā out of season; past its prime; inopportune.

vyatyaya [act. vyatī] m. transposition, change; inversion, inverse relation. vyatyaye adv. in the opposite case; conversely. vyatyayam adv. alternatively. vyatyayāt var. vyatyayena adv. as an exception to the rule. vyatyayo bahulam often reversed.
vyatyas [viatyas] v. [4] pr. (vyatyasyati) pp. (vyatyasta) throw over, cross; exchange reverse.
vyatyasta |pp. vyatyas| amnf vyatyasta put upside down, reversed, turned over; crossed (hands) incoherent (words); perverse.
vyatyastapada | pada| amnf vyatyastapadī with legs crossed.
vyatyastabhuja | bhuja | amnf vyatyastabhujī with arms crossed.
vyatyāsa [act. vyatyas] m. exchange, barter | inversion, opposite; confusion. vyatyāsena adv. conversely, reciprocally.

√ vyath v. [1] pr. (vyathati) pp. (vyathita) pf. (pra) to be moved, to tremble, to stagger — pr. r. (vya thate) to grieve, to be afraid; to suffer — ca. (vya thayati) to torment, to afflict, to frighten, to cause suffering.
vyathā |act. vyath| f. anguish, torment; pain, sorrow; suffering; fear. vyathām kṛ to make (someone) (g.) suffer.
vyathākara [kara₁] amnf vyathākarā that causes suffering; painful; atrocious.
vyathāpaha [apaha] amnf vyathāpahā which removes pain.
vyad [viad₁] v. [2] pr. (vyatti) to gnaw.

√ vyadh v. [4] pr. (vidhyati) pft. (vivyādha) aor. [3] (avīvidhat) aor. [4] (avyātsīt) pp. (viddha) pf. (anu, apa, ā, ni) to pierce | to pierce, to wound; at to sting (with (i.) an arrow) | to goad, to stimulate | to inflict something (i.) on someone. (acc.) — ps. (vidhyate) to be pierced, to be wounded — ca. (vyādhayati) to pierce. dhanuṣāvidhyati he pierces with (the arrow from) his bow.
vyadha [act. vyadh] m. action of piercing, of wounding | blow; wound — f. vyadhā bleeding.
vyadhana [act. vyadh] n. injury; perforation (vein) — ifc. massacre of, hunt for (iic.).
vyadhikarana [viadhikarana] amnf vyadhikaranā gram. not congruent to; which does not have the same denotation as; put in a different case than; opp. samānādhikarana.
vyadhikaraṇabahuvrīhi [bahuvrīhi] m. gram. com posed heterodenotational determinative, like kanthekāla.
vyan [vian₂] v. [2] pr. (vyaniti) to breathe.
vyanunad [vianunad] ca. (vyanunādayati) pp. (vyanunādita) to make a racket, to fill with noise or shouts.
vyanunāda [act. vyanunad] m. reverberation; uproar.
vyantara [viantara] n. lack of distinction | interval — m. cf. vyantaradevatā.
vyantaradevatā [devatā] f. jn. ["intermediate divine being" | class of subordinate deities, including the piśācās, bhūtās, yakṣās, rakṣās, kin narāskimpuruṣās, mahoragās and gandharvās.
vyapagata [pp. vyapagam] amnf vya pagatā gone.
vyapagam [viapagam] v. [1] pr. (vyapagac chati) pp. (vyapagata) to move away, to go away, to dissipate; to flee, to disappear.
vyapadiś [viapadiś] v. [1] pr. (vyapadiśati) pp. (vyapadista) to name, designate | to pretext, to claim that, to pass off (acc.) as (acc.).

vyapadeśa [act. vyapadiś] m. designation, name, title; family name, race | summons, mobilization | pretext, appearance. tadvyapadeśanyāyaḥ "maxim of the so-called"; it justifies, in particular, that the śyenayāga , rite of cursing an enemy, is not the sacrifice of a falcon, but is so named by analogy with the falcon that swoops down on its prey.
vyapadeśin [agt. vyapadiś] ifc. amnf vyapadeśinī who disguises himself under, who takes as a pretext (iic.). dharmakañcukavyapadeśin hypocrite | "who takes as a pretext the garb of duty".
vyapadeśya [pfp. [1] vyapadiś] amnf vyapadeśyā to designate, to name; to blame; which deserves a title | phil. expressible.
vyapāśraya [obj. vyapāśri] m. refuge, shelter, support — agt. ifc. one who has recourse to, who has faith in, who has confidence in (iic.).
vyapāśri [viapāśri] v. [1] pr. (vyapāśrayati) pr. r. (vyapāśrayate) pp. (vyapāśrita) to seek refuge in, to have recourse to, to adhere to (doctrine), to put.
vyape [viape] v. [2] pr. (vyapaiti) pp. (vya peta) to disappear, to cease.
vyapekṣ [viapekṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (vyapekṣate) pp. (vyapekṣita) to consider, to pay attention to, to take regard to, to expect; to have in mind, to desire.

vyapekṣā [act. vyapekṣ] f. consideration; expectation | gram. grammatical agreement; collocation; opp. ekārthībhāva — ifc. with regard to; in accordance with (iic.). vyapekṣāyām gram. when there is mutual dependence.
vyapekṣita [pp. vyapekṣ] amnf vyapekṣitā expected, conforming; mutually related.
vyapeta [pp. vyape] amnf vyapeta dis paru; cesse.
vyapodha [pp. vyapoh] amnf vyapodhā chased away, repelled; destroyed | shown, exhibited | opposed; contrary; inverse. vyapoḍhābhra that repels the clouds.

vyapoh [viapoh] v. [1] pr. (vyapohati) pp. (vyapodha) to set aside, repel, send away; to destroy, expiate (fault); to cure (disease) — pr. r. (vyapo hate) id. kṣudhā nirṇudati prajñām dharmyām buddhim vyapohati | kṣudhāparigatajñāno dhṛtim tyajati caiva ha | [Mah.] Hunger banishes wisdom and repels virtuous thought; he whose understanding is afflicted by hunger abandons all resolution.
vyapoha [act. vyapoh] m. act of removing, repelling, suppressing; destruction | denial; negation.
vyabhicar [viabhicar] v. [1] pr. (vyabhi carati) pp. (vyabhicarita) to behave badly towards ⟨acc. g.⟩; to offend, to insult | to practice witchcraft; to transgress; to sin.
vyabhicarita [pp. vyabhicar] amnf vyabhicaritā phil. [Nyāya] incorrect.

vyabhicāra [act. vyabhicar] m. deviance, debauchery; sin, vice; infidelity | violation, transgression; irregularity, anomaly | disturbance; change, mutation; deviation, divergence | phil. [Nyāya] nonconcomitance in a syllogism; opp. sahacāra.
vyabhicāri iic. vyabhicārin.

vyabhicāribhāva [bhāva] m. deviant feeling phil. transient state of mind, unwise mood (opp. sthāyibhāva); there are 34 of them: indifference [nirveda], weariness [glāni], apprehension [śaṅkā], envy [asūyā], drunkenness [mada], weariness [śrama], sloth [ālasya], the
discouragement [dainya], worry [cintā], bewilderment [moha], memory [smṛti], the
resolution [dhṛti], timidity [vrīḍā], inconsistency
tance [capalatā], pleasure [harṣa], excitement [āvega], stupidity [jaḍatā], pride [garva], despair [viṣāda], impatience [autsukya], the
drowsiness [nidrā₂], possession [apasmāra],
lethargy [supta], inattention [vibodha₁], impa
concealment [amarṣa], dissimulation [avahitthā], the
anger [ugratā], wisdom [mati], rebuke [upālambha], illness [vyādhi], madness [unmāda], agony [maraṇa], fear [trāsa] and reflection [vitarka].
vyabhicāribhāvana [bhāvana] n. id.
vyabhicārin [agt. vyabhicar] amnf vyabhicāriņī deviant, debauched; sinner, vicious; unfaithful | inconstant; opp. sthāyin — ifc. who transgresses (iic.).
vyabhra [viabhra] amnf vyabhrā cloudless. vyabhre adv. in fine weather.

Vyaya [agt. vī₃] amnf vyayā chan geant, transient; variable, mutable; degradable, alterable — act. m. expenditure; opp. āya | expenditure for (loc. iic.); sacrifice of (g. iic.) | prodigality, wastefulness; disappearance, ruin, loss; opp. udaya gram. inflection, declension astr. np. of Vyaya "Prodigal", personifying year 20 of a life cycle |samvatsara| | arch. expenditure in the āyādi system; syn. rṇa — v. [11] pr. (vyayati) v. [11] pr. r. (vyayate) to spend; to waste. vyayena ind. ifc. at the cost of (iic. g.). vyayīkr to spend. āyādhikam vyayam karoti he lives beyond his means.
vyayin [agt. vī₃] amnf vyayinī which declines, which deteriorates; which disappears.
vyartha [viartha] amnf vyarthā useless, vain; absurd; pointless | poor, ruined.
vyalīka [vialīka] amnf vyalīkā false, deceitful, hypocritical — m. giton, darling — n. falsehood, lie, cheating.

vyavacchid₁ [viavacchid] v. [7] pr. (Vya vacchinatti) pp. (vyavacchinna) to cut, to slice off; to separate | to tear, to open; to split, to divide. prajātantum mā vyavacchetsīḥ [TU.] You must not break the chain of descent.
vyavacchid₁ [act. vyavacchid₁] f. limitation.
vyavacchinna [pp. vyavacchid₁] amnf vyavacchinnā cut out, removed, separated | distinguished, discriminated; distinct.
vyavaccheda [act. vyavacchid₁] m. separation; interruption; exclusion | separation, delimitation; distinction, discrimination — ifc. rejection of (iic.).
vyavacchedaka [agt. vyavacchid₁] amnf vyavacchedikā discriminant | exclusive. vyavacchedakalakṣaṇam discriminating sign.
vyavacchedakatva [tva] n. the act of being discriminatory or exclusive.
vyavacchedya [pfp. [1] vyavacchid₁] amnf vyavacchedyā to exclude.
vyavadāna [viavadāna₂] n. cleaning; purification.
vyavadhā [viavadhā] v. [3] pr. (vyava dadhāti) pp. (vyavahita) interpose, separate, interrupt.
vyavadhana |act. vyavadhana| n. intervention; obstruction (sight); interruption | gram. occurrence of a blocking phoneme | interval. vyavadhana indirectly.

vyavasā [viavasā] v. [4] pr. (vyavasyati) pp. (vyavasita) pf. (anu) to decide, to resolve to acc. inf. | to accept, to be persuaded to | to strive to; to apply oneself to (inf.) | to consider, to determine; to decide. pātum na prathamam vyavasyati jalam she doesn't want to drink the water first. gantum āśu vyavasyet resolve to leave without delay.
vyavasāya [act. vyavasā] m. determination, resolution.
vyavasāyin [agt. vyavasā] amnf Vya vasāyinī resolved.

vyavasita [pp. vyavasā] amnf vyavasitā decided, resolved, undertaken; of which one is sure | resolved, decided to (loc. dat. inf.); who has become convinced — n. decision; undertaking; resolution, determination. vyavasitam (impers.) it is certain that; it is decided that. tena jīvotsargāya vyavasitam he resolved to end his life.

vyavasthā₁ [viavasthā₁] v. [1] pr. r. (vyavatisthate) pp. (vyavasthita) to stop, halt; to prepare to (dat.) | to be logically established — ca. (vyavasthāpayati) pp. (vyavasthāpita) to establish, determine; fix upon, direct towards (loc.); charge with; arrange. vācam vyavasthāpya having decided what to say.

vyavasthā₁ [act. vyavasthā₁] f. particularity, singularity, characteristic; distinction, separation | constancy; conviction, firm opinion | soc. not. edict of a scholar [śāstrin] concerning an observance | state, circumstance. varṇavyavasthā soc. the notion of caste as a characteristic of Hinduism.
vyavasthārṇava [arṇava] m. lit. np. du Vya vasthārṇava "Flow of observances", title of work.
vyavasthāna [act. vyavasthā₁] n. perseverance, firmness; condition.
vyavasthāpita [pp. ca. vyavasthā₁] amnf vyavasthāpitā established, determined; arranged, prepared. vyavasthāpitavak prepared discourse.
vyavasthita [pp. vyavasthā₁] amnf vyavasthita placed, situated; being at, included in (iic.) | dependent on, decided at (loc.); defined, well established; constant, invariable.

vyavasthiti [act. vyavasthā₁] f. distinction, difference | constancy; perseverance; determination. व्यवहरण vyavaharana [act. vyavahr] n. the act of betting or doing business | legal dispute, litigation.

vyavahāra [act. vyavahr] m. action, activity, affair, use, custom; procedures, practice, profession, traffic, commerce | contract, legal act; legal proceedings, trial, judicial procedure; civil law | everyday language | mod. management. vyavahāratas adv. according to procedure; in practice; by convention. vyavahāreşu adv. gram. in everyday conversation.
vyavahāragocara [gocara] m. domain of current affairs.
vyavahāragocaratva |tva| n. phil. nature of the domain of current affairs.
vyavahārajña [jña] amnf vyavahārajñā soc. who knows business, who understands the law — mr. 16 years old, adult; opp. bāla.
vyavahārapada | padah | n. soc. title of law; legal citation, statement of a dispute.
vyavahārapāda [pāda] m. soc. one of the 4 stages of a trial: complaint, defense, evidence and sentence.
vyavahāramayūkha [mayūkha] m. bed. n.p. of the Vya vahāramayūkha, summary of laws due to Nīlakaṇṭha₅ Bhatta.
vyavahāravat [vat] amnf vyavahāravatī who carries out a transaction; who does business — m. merchant, businessman.
vyavahārasaukhya [saukhya] n. bed. n.p. of the Vya vahārasaukhya, criminal procedure code, Țodarānanda section.

vyavahārika [ika] amnf vyavahārikā phil. contingent, material; conventional; of the domain of empirical experience; opp. paramārthika. vyavahārikasat phil. conventional reality. व्यवहारक vyavahāraka [agt. vyavahr] m. businessman — f. vyavahārikā servant. vyavahārikayā bhāṣayā vada who speaks a kitchen Sanskrit.
vyavahārin [agt. vyavahr] amnf Vya vahārinī trader — m. merchant (of (iic.)). surākiņvavyavahārī trader in alcohol and fermented bran woods.
vyavahāritā [tā] f. legal majority.
vyavahārya [pfp. [1] vyavahr] amnf vyavahāryā which can be the subject of a transaction with whom one can associate.
vyavahita [pp. vyavadha] amnf vyava hitā interrupted, separated; prevented, hindered.

vyavahr [viavahr] v. [1] pr. (vyavaharati) pp. (vyavahṛta) pf. (sam) to exchange, to have activities, to behave; to communicate | to do business (of the amount of (g. acc.) | to have sexual relations with (i. loc.) | to confront (the enemy); to fight with (i.); to measure oneself against (sārdham (i.)) | to act, to take care of (loc.); to work | to plead, to go to court | to bet on the game (the sum of (g. acc.)).
vyavahṛta [pp. vyavahṛ] amnf vyavahṛtā named, designated — n. activity, business, commerce.
vyavahṛti [act. vyavahṛ] f. practice, conduct, action | sexual intercourse | affairs; com merce; dispute, legal action | discourse; rumor lit. (poetry) treatment of a subject.

vyavāya [act. vyave] m. intervention, in interposition | the act of being separated by (i. iic.) | penetration; change, transmutation | gram. separation (said of vowels in hiatus); interposition (of a phoneme); opp. samavāya | immodesty; sexual act.
vyavāyin [agt. vyave] amnf vyavāyinī that intervenes, that separates | penetrating; diffuse | lascivious — m. libertine.
vyave [viave] v. [2] pr. (vyavaiti) pp. (vyaveta) to intercalate; to separate.
vyaveta [act. vyave] amnf vyavetā separated, divided gram. not. (words) separated by the insertion of a phoneme.
vyas [vias₂] v. [4] pr. (vyasyati) pp. (vyasta) to separate, reject, disperse; to throw away | to tear to pieces | to expend effort on, to throw one's strength into.

vyasana [act. vyas] n. assiduity, attachment, devotion | mania, whim; passion, obsession, vice, addiction | misfortune, disaster; misfortune, bad luck, bad fate. vyasanodayau var. pātotpātau the ups and downs. sa suhrd vyasane yaḥ syāt it is in times of need that one recognizes one's true friends.
vyasanakara [kara₁] amnf vyasanakarī who indulges in vice.
vyasani iic. vyasanin.
vyasanitva [tva] ifc. n. the act of having an addiction (to ⟨iic.⟩).

vyasanin [vyasanain] amnf vyasa ninī who works hard, who makes an effort — ifc. passionately attracted to; who adores (iic.) | slave to a vice (gambling, alcohol, sex); dissolute | unfortunate, who suffers from his addiction to (iic.).

vyásta [pp. vyas] amnf vyastā torn to pieces, dismembered; ripped, divided, scattered, dispersed; separated | multiplied; varied, multiple disorganized; changed, altered. vyastam separately; partially. vyaste kāle at different times, from time to time.
√ vyā v. [1] pr. (vyayati) pr. r. (vyayate) aor. [2] (ávyat) pp. (vītá) pf. (upa, sam) to wrap, to cover; to protect, to hide. vovyāt may he protect you.

vyākaraņa [act. vyākr] n. separation, distinction; analysis, description, development, revelation, communication; creation | phil. Grammar, one of the six supplementary treatises of the Veda [vedānga]; grammatical analysis. pradhānam ca ṣaṭsvaṅgeṣu vyākaraṇam [MB.] Grammar is the first among the six auxiliary sciences. dvādaśabhirvarṣair vyākaraṇaṃ śrūyate [PT.] One must study grammar for 12 years. rājan varṣairdvādaśabhiḥ sadā jñāyate sarva vidyānām mukham vyākaraņam naraih [KSS.] Sire, it takes men 12 years to learn grammar, the first of all sciences.
vyākaraṇacūḍāmaṇi [cūḍāmaṇi] m. diploma of expert grammarian.
vyākaraṇatīrtha [tīrtha] n. certificate of Sanskrit studies.
vyākaraṇamahābhāṣya [mahābhāṣya] n. bed. cf. Mahābhāsya.
Vyākaraṇāgama [āgama] n. gram. n.p. of the Vyākaraṇāgama, epith. of Mahābhāsya.
vyākaraṇācārya [ācārya] m. professor of grammar. vyākaraņottamā [uttama] f. higher diploma in Sanskrit studies.
vyākīrṇa [viākīrṇa] amnf vyākīrṇā scattered in all directions | disturbed, troubled; frantic — n. confusion.
vyākula [viākula] amnf vyākulā troubled, agitated; upset, moved; confused, disordered; in a trance — ifc. full of; occupied with, ab absorbed by, under the influence of (iic.).
vyākulatā [tā] f. pain, emotion, distraction; trouble, anxiety; perplexity, confusion | agitation, elation; nervousness, impatience.
vyākulatva |tva| n. pain, emotion, trouble.
vyākṛ [viākṛ] v. [8] pr. (vyākaróti) pp. (vyākṛta) to develop, to explain.

vyākṛta [pp. vyākṛ] amnf vyākṛtā developed, unfolded; analyzed, explained | transformed, changed; translated (from the (1st century)) | phil. manifest. ibrīyabhāṣāto vyākṛta translated from Hebrew. vyākṛtā vāg udyate gram. [Bhaṭṭoji] The language is spoken in accordance with the formations (of the grammar).
vyākhyā₁ [viākhyā₁] v. [2] pr. (vyākhyāti) pp. (vyākhyāta) to explain, to set forth in detail, to comment.
vyākhyā₁ [act. vyākhyā₁] f. explanation, commentary; elaboration | lit. gloss.
vyākhyāprajñapti [prajñapti] f. lit. 5ᵉ text of the ca non jaina, the legends and dialogues concerning the dogma; also called Bhagavatī₁.
vyākhyāyukti [yukti] f. lit. np. of the vyākhyāyukti (or Vyākhyāyuktiśāstra), a grammar work by Vasubandhu; only a Tibetan translation is known.
vyākhyāta [pp. vyākhyā₁ ₁] amnf vyākhyātā narrated, expounded; detailed; explained, commented, discussed.
vyākhyātṛ [agt. vyākhyā₁] amnf vyākhyātrī glossator.

vyākhyāna [agt. vyākhyā₁] amnf vyākhyānā who explains, who glosses | who resembles (g.) — act. n. narrative, exposition | gram. interpretation, semantics; detailed explanation; cf. bhāṣya | narration; recitation. lakṣyānusāri vyākhyānam [Nāgojibhaṭṭa] The interpretation conforms to the rules (of Pāṇini). padacchedah padārthoktir vigraho vākyayojanā ākṣepo'tha samādhānam vyākhyānam sadvidham matam | Segmenting and giving meaning to words, performing morphological and structural analysis of the sentence, raising objections and responding to them, these are the 6 goals prescribed for a textual interpretation.
vyākhyānadakṣiṇāmūrti [dakṣiṇāmūrti] m. myth. epith. of Shiva explaining sacred texts.
Vyākhyānamālā [mālā] f. bed. n.p. from the Vyākhyānamālā "Garland of Commentaries".
vyākhyānarūpa [rūpa] n. lit. (text) having the appearance of a commentary.

vyāghāta [act. vyāhan] m. strike, blow; act of beating, of wounding | agitation, disorder; obstacle, impediment | phil. contradiction, incoherence | lit. rhetorical device [alaṃkāra] of describing opposite effects of the same causes.
vyāghātaka |agt. vyāhan | amnf vyāghātikā that strikes; that opposes, that resists.
vyāghr [viāghr] ca. (vyājigharti) pp. (vyāghṛta) ved. asperger alentour.
vyāghrá [viāghra] m. bio. zoo. tiger; myth. tigers descend from Sārdūlī (or Damstrā) | hero ("a tiger among men") — f. vyāghrī bio. tigress || hi. bāgha.
vyāghránakha [nakha] m. tiger claw | hand weapon, comprising a series of steel blades; Sivajī used it to disembowel the Bijapuri general Afzal Khan in 1656.
vyāghrapad |pad₂| amnf who has a tiger's foot — m. lit. np. of Vyāghrapād, author of hymns of the RV.

Vyāghrapāda [pāda] m. myth. epith. of the rsi Vyāghrapāda, to whom tiger paws grew so that he could pick flowers from the tops of trees undefiled even by bees, in order to offer them to ŚivaNaṭarāja; he is represented in the company of Patañjali₁ with the body of a serpent | hist. grammai rien eponyme of the 2nd century ant., accomplished [siddha₁], to whom the Daśaka is attributed.
vyāghrabhaya [bhaya] n. fear of the tiger.

vyāghramukha [mukha] amnf vyāghramukhī which has a tiger's head. vyāghramukhī gauh ["tiger-headed cow"] overestimated difficulty; said not. of the Aṣṭādhyāyī, which, frightening at first glance, reveals itself to be clear.
vyācakṣ [viācakṣ] v. [2] pr. r. (vyācaṣṭe) explain.

vyāja |act. vyañj| m. appearance, imitation, plagiarism; deception, fraud; pretext, dissimulation — agt. f. vyājā ifc. that which has the appearance of (iic.); that which passes itself off as, pretending to be (iic.); false (iic.). vyājena var. vyajāt adv. falsely; treacherously.
vyājaguru | guru | m. self-proclaimed master.
vyājasupta [supta] amnf vyājasuptā who feigns sleep.
vyājastuti [stuti] f. feigned or ironic praise.
vyājokti [ukti] f. lit. rhet. (figure of speech) deceptive roles, dissimulation; the concealed fact must be suggested but denied; syn. apahnuti.
vyāḍa amnf vyāḍā wicked, cruel; cf. vyāla — m. wild beast.

Vyāḍi₁ [vyāḍai] m. hist. np. of the ancient grammarian Vyāḍi₁; he is credited with the grammar Samgraha, and the Paribhāṣāsūcanā (or Vyādīyaparibhāṣāvrtti) | hist. np. of the grammarian Vyādi₁, author of the Utpalinī | lit. [KSS.] np. of the Brahmin Vyādi₂; he went with his friend Indradatta to see the Brahmin varșa who taught them that he knew everything, and could transmit it to the disciple who could remember any text heard only once; they brought Vararuci to him for this purpose; When he had learned everything, Varșa asked for a koți of gold rupees as gurudakṣiṇā; they went to solicit King Nanda, but he died; Indradatta entered his body by magic, becoming Yoga Nanda; Vararuci received the sum, and became a minister.
vyādīya [īya] amnf vyādīyā produced by Vyādi.

vyādīyaparibhāṣāvṛtti | paribhāṣāvṛtti | f. gram. np. of the Vyādīyaparibhāṣāvṛtti, which deals with the meta-rules of Pāṇini's grammar, also called Paribhāṣāsūcanā; it is traditionally attributed to Vyādi, but is probably more recent.
vyātta [contr. vyāditta] amnf vyāttā wide open, vast — n. open mouth or maw.
vyāttānana [ānana] amnf vyāttānānā with open mouth | myth. [BhG.] said of Viṣṇu ready to destroy the universe.

vyādā [viādā] v. [3] pr. r. (vyādatte) pp. (vyātta, vyādita) to open wide, not. the mouth [mukha] | to accept; to receive (from (loc. i. abl.)). व्यादाय vyādāya [vyādāya] amnf vyādāyā having opened (not. the mouth). vyādāyaḥ svapiti he sleeps with his mouth open. व्यादित vyādita [pp. vyādā] amnf vyāditā wide open, vast.
vyāditāsya |āsya| amnf vyāditāsyā who has her mouth wide open.
vyādha [agt. vyadh] m. hunter.
vyādhapataiga [pataiga] m. organic. dragonfly.
vyādhā [viādhā] ps. (vyādhīyate) pp. (vyādhita) to be indisposed.
vyādhi [act. vyādhā] m. disease; not. leprosy | pain, suffering; torment, worry — ifc. plague of (iic.).
vyādhita [ita] amnf vyādhitā malade, souf frant, maladif.
vyādhū [viādhū] v. [5] pr. (vyādhunóti) pp. (vyādhūta) to agitate, stir; to disperse (not. wind).
vyāna [obj. vyan] m. phil. [Yoga] the vital breath, synthesis of the 4 other breaths [prāṇa].
vyāp [viāp] v. [5] pr. (vyāpnóti) pp. (vyāpta) to penetrate, fill; to spread into, impregnate; to reach — des. (vīpsati) to desire to spread.

vyāpaka [agt. vyāp] amnf vyāpikā that fills; penetrating, diffusing, pervading; inclusive; comprehensive | phil. [Nyāya] concomitant, inherent, inevitable; involved | soc. [law] comprehensive, including all the arguments of a trial.
vyāpakatā [tā] f. diffusion, impregnation | phil. [Nyāya] implication.
vyāpakatva |tva| n. id.
vyāpad [viāpad₁] v. [4] pr. r. (vyāpadyate) pp. (vyāpanna) to perish, to go to one's ruin — ca. (vyāpādáyati) pp. (vyāpādita) to cause to perish, to destroy, to kill.
vyāpanna [pp. vyāpad] amnf vyāpannā who perished.
vyāpād [ca. vyāpad] v. [10] pr. (vyāpādáyati) pp. (vyāpādita) to cause to perish, to destroy, to kill.
vyāpādana |act. vyāpād| n. destruction, death; murder.
vyāpādita [pp. vyāpād] amnf vyāpāditā annihilated, killed, that which has been put to death. asau vyāghrena vyāpāditah khāditaśca The tiger killed and devoured it.

vyāpāra [act. vyāpr] m. occupation, activity; function, employment, profession | phil. [Gangeśa] operation resulting from a causality | gram. action associated with a verb; intermediate factor between the instrument of an action and its goal — f. vyāpārā ifc. function of, employment of (i.e., occupation of (i.e., loc. vyāpāram kṛ to help. vyāpāram yā to care for. vyāpāram vraj to take care of (loc.). phalaviśiṣṭavyāpāra gram. [vyākaraṇa] activity with a view to a goal (denotation of a verb).
vyāpāravat [vat] amnf vyāpāravatī effective, active.
vyāpārin [agt. vyāpṛ] amnf vyāpāriṇī occupied, active; whose occupation is (iic.) — m. merchant; commercial agent; professional.

vyāpin [agt. vyāp] amnf vyāpinī widely spread, which penetrates everywhere, omnipresent — ifc. which reaches (iic.). snānaśaṅkhānām bhuvanavivaravyāpī āpūryamāṇām atimukharo dhvaniḥ |K.| The deafening sound of conch shells sounded for bath time penetrates all the crevices of the Earth.

vyāpṛ [viāpṛ] ps. (vyāpṛiyate) pp. (vyāpṛta) to be occupied with loc.; to be employed — ca. (vyāpārayati) to occupy someone with (loc.); to employ, to make work | to fix one's eyes, to direct one's gaze towards. hastam vyāpr to use the hand; to wave the hand.
vyāpṛta [pp. vyāpṛ] amnf vyāpṛtā oc cupé à, employé à, concernant par (loc. iic.) — m. soc. officiel; ministre.
vyāpṛtaka |ka| m. soc. officer; superintendent of (iic.). hastyaśvostranaubalavyāprtakah soc. superintendent of elephants, cavalry, camels and ships.

vyāpta [pp. vyāp] amnf vyāptā by run, filled; which has been taken possession of; penetrated, impregnated (by (i.)) | phil. [Nyāya] understood as an instance of a universal fact conceived as an inevitable inherent property; implying | gram. covered (by an understanding). dhūmo vahninā vyāptaḥ ["fire impregnates the smoke" | there is no smoke without fire.
vyāpti [act. vyāp] f. accomplishment, success | inherence, impregnation, interpenetration | phil. [Nyāya] validity of the inference between the hy

hypothesis [hetu] and conclusion [sādhya]; it is established that the hypothesis implies the conclusion by showing that the conclusion is inherent in the nature of the hypothesis; inference is distinguished
positive [anvayavyāpti] and that by contradiction [vyatirekavyāpti] | phil. [NN.] inevitable concomitance, correlation. sāhacaryaniyamaḥ vyāptiḥ [Nyāya] Inherence is an obligatory association.
vyāptijñāna [jñāna] n. phil. [Nyāya] knowledge of an inevitable concomitance.
vyāptidhī [dhī₂] n. phil. [Nyāya] understanding of an inevitable concomitance.
vyāptipañcaka [pañcaka] mn phil. [NN.] the series of 5 definitions of inevitable concomitance according to Gangesa, prelude to the correct definition [siddhāntalakṣana].
vyāptipañcakarahasya [rahasya] n. phil. [Nyāya] np. of the vyāptipañcakarahasya, commentary by Mathurānātha₁ of the vyāptipañcaka.

vyāptipratipādaka [pratipādaka] amnf vyāptipratipādikā phil. [Nyāya] which sets forth the law of concomitance; said of the clause of example in support [udāharaṇa] in the quintuple syllogism pañcāvayava.

vyāpya [pfp. [1] vyāp] amnf vyāpyā permeable, penetrable; impregnated with (iic.) | gram. (word) to be covered by a notion; (verb) made transitive by | phil. [Nyāya] qualifyable; which can serve as a predicate — n. substrate of a hypothesis. vahnivyāpyo dhūmah ["the smoke is impregnated with fire"] There is no smoke without fire.
vyāpyatā [tā] f. permeability; qualifiability.
vyāpyatva [tva] n. permeability; qualifiability.

vyāpyavyāpakabhāva |vyāpakabhāva| m. phil. [Nyāya] relation between implying and implied; logical consequence. vyāpyavyāpakabhāvo hi bhāvayoh yādrk isyate tayoḥ abhāvayos tasmāt viparītaḥ pratīyate | [SIV.] If the relation of logical implication exists between two propositions, the inverse relation exists between their negations.
vyāma m. length measurement (fathom, fathom).

vyāmiśra [viāmiśra] amnf vyāmiśrā mixed; combined | mixed with, accompanied by, provided with (i.e.) | of various kinds, varied | confused. vyāmiśre gram. when both cases are combined. vyāmiśrena vākyena buddhim mohayasīva me [BhG.] by a profusion of words you sow confusion in my mind.
vyāmiśratā [tā] f. state of being a mixture; heterogeneity, variety.
vyāyata [pp. vyāyam] amnf vyāyatā long, extended; exceptional — iic. that goes far, that comes from afar. vyāyatam adv. extremely.
vyāyam [viāyam] v. [1] pr. (vyāyacchati) pp. (vyāyata) to extend — pr. r. (vyāyacchate) to force oneself to, to struggle for (loc.) — ca. (vyāyamayati) to practice.
vyāyāma |act. vyāyam| m. competition, struggle | effort, exercise; mastery, maintenance — ifc. exercise of, effort for (iic.).
vyāyāmavidyā [vidyā] f. gymnastics.
vyāyāmika [ika] amnf vyāyāmikī relating to physical culture; athletic — f. vyāyāmikī athletics, one of the 64 arts | kalā|. vyāyāmikīnām vidyānām jñānam knowledge of physical culture.
vyāyoga [viāyoga] m. lit. form of heroic dramatic play in one act.

vyāla [related to vyāḍa] amnf vyālī cruel, wicked, ferocious; extravagant — m. ferocious beast, wild beast; serpent; ferocious wild animal (opp. mṛga) myth. griffin, horned lion; it is often depicted overpowering an elephant, symbol of the victory of Hinduism over Buddhism; syn. śarabha — f. vyālī female serpent | myth. serpent of the cycle of rebirths.
vyālamb [viālamb] v. [1] pr. r. (vyālambate) pp. (vyālambita) to hang from; to descend on.
vyālup [viālup] v. [6] pr. (vyālumpati) to rise — ps. (vyālupyate) to be destroyed, to disappear.
vyālola [viālola] amnf vyālolā that is agitated, that is swaying. vyālolakuntalakalāpavatī with hair flowing in disorder.
vyāvarta [act. vyāvṛt] m. turning, separation, bifurcation; approx.
vyāvartaka [agt. vyāvrt] amnf vyāvartikā that separates, that excludes; that distinguishes phil. [Nyāya] discriminator.
vyāvartana [agt. vyāvrt] amnf vyāvartanī which excludes, which removes — ifc. which turns away from (iic.) — act. n. turning (of a road); ring (of a snake); spool.
vyāvahārika [*vyavahāraika] amnf vyāvahārikī phil. contingent of human affairs, worldly; pragmatic, empirical, current; opp. pāramārthika (real), opp. prātibhāsika (illusory).
vyāvahārī [*vyavahāra] f. exchange | soc. exchange of sexual relations.

vyāvṛt [viāvṛt₁] v. [1] pr. r.
