(vyāvartate) pp. (vyāvṛtta) to separate from (i.); to divide, to bifurcate | to be distinct from, incompatible with (abl.) | to turn away from, to get rid of (i. abl.) | to go away, to leave; to end, to disappear; to lie down (not. so leil) — ca. r. (vyāvartayate) to separate, to divide; to isolate from (i.); to set aside; to take back; to retract | to disperse, to repress; to annihilate, to cancel.
vyāvṛtta [pp. vyāvṛt] amnf vyāvṛttā divided, split; diverted, turned over; rid of (i. abl. iic. | incompatible (with (iic.)); disappeared, gone, ceased.
vyāvṛttatva [tva] n. incompatibility | phil. state of being isolated or exceptional; syn. alpadeśavṛttitva.
vyāvṛttaśiras [śiras] amnf who turns his head away.
vyāvṛtti [act. vyāvṛt] f. act of getting rid of (abl.); act of being excluded or frustrated from.
vyāsa [viāsa₁] m. separation, division | diffusion, extension; exposition, detailed report gram. analytical form; opp. samāsa | width, thickness,
diameter | compiler | myth. [Mah.] np. of the sage [rsi] vyāsa "compiler (of the Mah.)", son of the ascetic Parāśara and Kālī₁Satyavatī, and thus half-brother of Bhīşma and Vicitravīrya; born mid

Raculously [Dvaipāyana₁] on an island of the Ya munā, an adult from his conception, he lived there as a hermit; his mother brought him back to the world by the sight of niyoga to marry (by the lightning of his gaze) the 2 widows of Vicitravīrya, Ambikā₁ to conceive Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Ambālikā₁ to conceive Pāṇḍu; when he wanted a 3rd child, Ambikā₁ disguised one of his servants as a substitute, from whom he begot Vidura; he is credited with the compilation of the Mahābhārata and the ancient tales | purāṇa | ; he is also called the composer of the Veda [Vedavyāsa]; he is celebrated at gurupūrnimā; He is one of the seven immortals [ciramjīvin]; he performed great penances to pray to Shiva to grant him a son; having obtained his wish, he returned to his hermitage |āśrama| where the nymph [apsaras] Ghṛtācī appeared to him in the form of a

parrot [śuka]; before its beauty he lost his se, from which was born the sage Suka; Vaisampāyana, Jaimini, Paila, Sumantu and Suka were his disciples. historical noun of Vyāsa₁ the "Analyst", author of the Yo gabhāṣya, first commentary on the Yogasūtra; he could be Patañjali₂ himself, and is said to have lived between the 4th and 7th centuries. Vyāsocchistam jagatsarvam Vyāsa regurgitated the whole Earth (in the Mah.).

vyāsatīrtha [tīrtha] m. hist. np. of vyāsatīrtha, learned mystic of the Madhva Dvaita order (~1460–1539); born Yatirāja in Mysore, he was initiated by Brahmanyatīrtha as the renunciant vyāsatīrtha; he studied at Kāñcī and then at Mulba gal; he headed the Tirupati temple from 1486 to 1498; he joined Vijayanagara at the request of Saluva Narasimha₄; he was the rājaguru of Emperor Kṛṣṇadeva Rāya; he was an unparalleled dialectician in debates and an accomplished scholar; he defended the Madhva Dvaita doctrine; He is credited with the Nyāyāmṛta, the Tarkatāṇḍava, the Tātparyacandrikā₁, and the Bhedojjīvana.
vyāsadasa [dāsa] m. hist. n.p. by Vyāsadāsa Ksemendra (Kaśmīra, 11th century).
vyāsapītha [pītha] n. mod. throne of the reciter of a saptāha.
Vyāsabhāsya | bhāsya | n. lit. np. of the Vyāsabhāsya, commentary on the Yogasūtra of Patañjali₂, attributed to Vyāsa₁; cf. Yogabhāsya.
vyāsarāja | rāja | mr. hist. n.p. of the holy vyāsarāja; cf. vyāsatīrtha.

vyāsakta [pp. vyāsañj] amnf vyāsaktā devoted to, attached to; connected with; dependent on engaged in, busy with (loc. iic.) | embraced, embraced detached, disjointed from | distracted, confused; perplexed.
vyāsaṅga [vyāsañj] m. excessive attachment, strong adherence | devotion to, addiction to (loc. iic.) | distraction, straying | detachment, separation.
vyāsajya [pfp. [1] vyāsañj] amnf vyāsajyā to connect with, to attach, to stick | which must be associated with.
vyāsajyaceta | cetas | amnf vyāsajyacetā at taché en pensée à.
vyāsajyavṛtti |vṛtti| amnf phil. |Nyāya| (quality) residing in several objects.
vyāsañj [viāsañj] v. [1] pr. (vyāsajati) pp. (vyāsakta) to attach excessively; to adhere strongly; to fix oneself on (loc. iic.).
vyāhan [viāhan] v. [2] pr. (vyāhanti) pp. (vyāhata) to strike, to trample; to repel, to prevent.
vyāhita cf. vyādhita.
vyāhṛ [viāhṛ] v. [1] pr. (vyāharati) pp. (vyāhṛta) pf. (abhi, pra) to pronounce, say, speak. nāmabhir vyāhr to call by their names. praśnān vyāhr to answer questions.
vyāhṛta [pp. vyāhṛ] amnf vyāhṛtā pro noncé, dit — n. conversation.

vyāhṛti [act. vyāhṛ] f. enunciation, declaration, proclamation | ved. ritual exclamation, not. during libations; proclamation of the name of the 7 celestial worlds [loka], or only of the first 3 [vyāhṛtitraya].

vyāhṛtitraya | traya | n. myth. ritual proclamation of the 3 celestial worlds [lokatraya]: bhūr bhuvar svar₃ (cf. bhū₂).<mark> व्युत्क्रम्</mark> vyutkram [viutkram] v. [1] pr. (vyutkrāmati) pp. (vyutkrānta) to stray from the right path, to go in another direction; to go astray, to ignore, to neglect; to transgress. <u>ञ्युत्क्रम</u> vyutkrama [act. vyutkram] m. the act of straying; inversion | transgression; offense.
vyutkramana [act. vyutkram] n. the act of straying; separation.
vyutkrānta [pp. vyutkram] amnf vyutkrāntā astray; gone in another direction | gone; finished | transgressed, ignored — f. vyutkrāntā kind of riddle.

vyutthā [viutthā] v. [1] pr. (vyuttiṣṭhati) pr. r. (vyuttiṣṭhate) pp. (vyutthita) to rise up; to turn away from, to deviate from (abl.) — ca. se (vyutthāpayati) to set aside, to distance oneself; to disagree about (acc.). dharmāt vyutthā to deviate from duty.
vyutthāna [act. vyutthā] n. awakening | abandonment; the act of turning away from one's duty | phil. [yoga] return to the world of perceptions, yogic awakening.
vyutthita [pp. vyutthā] amnf vyutthitā agitated, excited | phil. [yoga] that awakens from the state of samādhi — n. divergence of opinion.

vyutpatti [act. vyutpad] f. production, origin, mode of formation | gram. derivation, etymology | development, improvement, growth | training; learning, increase of knowledge | expertise, science, erudition; culture.
vyutpattinimitta | nimitta | n. gram. strict etymological meaning of a word.
vyutpattipakṣa [pakṣa] m. gram. dogma insti tuing that every nominal is derived from a verbal root; it is defended by Yāska and Śākaṭāyana; opp. avyutpattipaksa.
vyutpattipakṣin [pakṣin] afmn vyutpattipakṣiṇī gram. holding from the point of view that every nominal is derived from a verbal root; opp. avyutpattipakṣin.
vyutpattivāda [vāda] m. lit. np. of the Vyutpat tivāda, a treatise on semantics by Gadādhara Bhaṭṭācārya, in terms of Navyanyāya.

vyutpad [viutpad] v. [4] pr. r. (vyutpa dyate) pp. (vyutpanna) to occur, to arise | gram. to derive etymologically from (abl.) — ca. (vyutpādayati) to cause to occur, to create, to cause | gram. to derive from; to trace back to a root.

vyutpanna [pp. vyutpad] amnf vyutpannā issu, derivative | gram. explicable by etymology; not. derived from a verbal root gram. derived by the grammar of Pāṇini | learned in, accomplished in, versed in (i.) | gram. not. who knows how to use the grammar of Pāṇini.
vyutpannasamketa [samketa] amnf vyutpannasamketā gram. by whom grammar is understood.
vyutpādaka [agt. vyutpad] amnf vyutpādikā gram. that produces; productive.
vyutpādana [act. vyutpad] n. gram. etymological explanation; derivation from (abl.); grammatical analysis.
vyudas [viudas] v. [4] pr. (vyudasyati) pp. (vyudasta) scatter; emit | reject, expel; abandon.
vyudasta [pp. vyudas] amnf vyudastā scattered; rejected, abandoned.
vyudita [pp. vivad] amnf vyuditā dis cuté, debated; disputed, contradicted.
vyus [vius] v. [4] pr. (vyusati) pp. (vyusita, vyusta) burn.
vyuṣṭa [pp. vyuṣ] amnf vyuṣṭā became clear; appeared (day) — n. dawn, daybreak.
vyuṣṭi [act. vyuṣ] f. first glimmer of dawn | reward, fruit (from g. loc. iic. ).
vyūdha [pp. vyūh] amnf vyūdhā set aside, distributed; arranged in battle order.
vyūh [viūh] v. [1] pr. (vyūhati) pr. r. (vyūhate) pp. (vyūdha) pf. (nis) to spread out, divide; to spread out, rearrange | to arrange in battle order.

vyūhá [act. vyūh] m. distribution, disposition; rearrangement, transposition | order of size; cf. cakravyūha | phil. |vaiṣṇava| divine emanation; there are 4 principal manifestations of Vișnu: Purusottama, Samkarsana, Pradyumna and Anirud dha, and 24 secondary manifestations |upavyūha| reasoning, speculation.
vyeka [vieka] amnf vyekā math. minus one | predecessor.
vyoma iic. vyoman.
Vyomakeśa [keśa] m. myth. np. of Vyomakeśa, epith. of Shiva "whose hair is in the sky".
vyomacārin [cārin] amnf vyomacārinī that moves in the air — m. bird; divine being; celestial body.
vyomacāripura | pura | n. myth. np. of Vyo macāripura, the "Flying City" of King Hariścandra.
vyomadigvarga [digvarga] m. air and space.
vyomamāya [māya] amnf vyomamāyī ["who measures the sky" | who reaches the heavens.
vyomamārga [mārga] m. the way of the air. vyomamārgeņa by way of the air.
vyomayāna [yāna] n. myth. celestial chariot carrying a god through the air; syn. vimāna₁.
vyomavat [vat] amnf vyomavatī like the sky — f. vyomavatī lit. np. of the vyomavatī, commentary on the Padārthadharmasamgraha due to Vyomaśiva.
Vyomaśiva [śiva] m. hist. np. of the philosopher Vyomaśiva (~900–960), author of the vyomavatī, treatise on discriminative doctrine [Vaiseșika].

vyoman [vyāman] m. sky, air, ether; es space; syn. viyat | math. symb. the number zero. yo asyādhyakṣaḥ parame vyomaniso aṅgá veda yádi vā na veda [RV.] (Nāsadīyasūkta, Hymn of Creation) He, the spectator of this (creation) in the highest heavens, undoubtedly knows it; or perhaps, even He does not know it?

√ vraj v. [1] pr. (vrájati) aor. [5] (avrājīt) pp. (vrajita) pf. (anu, pari, pra) ved. to graze (livestock) | to go, to walk, to advance, to move about; to wander; to go away; to follow the course of one's life. antam vraj to go to the end. jarāṃ vraj to grow old. jīvan vraj to have one's life spared. padbhyām vraj to walk. punar vraj to be reborn; to come back to life. mṛtyum vraj to die. vyāpāram vraj to take care of (loc.). sukham vraj to feel well, to be at ease. bhojako vrajati he is going to eat.

vrajá [agt. vraj] m. troop, flock — loc. m. pasture, cattle pen, sheepfold | myth. [BhP.] np. of the place called Vraja "Pasture", near Mathurā, where the shepherd Nanda lived, and where Kṛṣṇa spent his youth with the cowherds [gopī]; mod. Braj; cf. Vrji, Vrndāvana, Gokula | route, path — act. n. wandering, journey.
vrajákiśora [kiśora] m. myth. "boy of Vraja", epith. of Kṛṣṇa.
vrajánātha [nātha] m. myth. "lord of the pastures", epith. of Kṛṣṇa.
vrajábhū [bhū₂] amnf derived from Vraja — f. region of Vraja; idyllic place ["Land of cattle"].
vrajámohana | mohana | m. myth. "enchanter of Vraja", epith. of Kṛṣṇa.
vrajendra | indra | m. myth. "the best of Vraja", epith. of Kṛṣṇa.
vrajaka |agt. vraj| m. ascetic mendicant no made.
vrájana |act. vraj| n. the act of traveling; wandering, exile. anyatra vrajana on the move elsewhere.
Vrajas iic. Vraja.
Vrajaspati | pati | m. myth. np. of Vrajaspati "Master of the stable", epithet of Kṛṣṇa echoing Brhaspati.
vrajita [pp. vraj] amnf vrajitā parti — n. wandering. anyena vrajita parti by another route.
vrajyā |act. vraj| f. journey; travel; al
lure | march; invasion | lit. thematic division of an anthology.

vrana m. wound, injury; scar — v. [11] pr. (vranayati) pp. (vranita) to wound, ulcerate | lat. vulnus; fr. vulnerable. Vraņaviropaņa [viropaṇa] amnf vraṇaviropaṇā that heals wounds, that heals sores — n. healing of wounds. vranaviropanam tailam ointment for treating sores.
vranita [pp. vrana] amnf vranitā wounded.

vratá [act. vr₂] n. rule, observance; sphere of action; way of life, conduct; individual duty; commitment | vow, oath; commandment, obligation | religious practice, chastity | jn. Jain ritual observance; cf. mahāvrata | ritual fasting day | Vedic. boiled milk as a dīkṣita diet; cf. prāṇāgnihotra — f. vratā ifc. one who eats or drinks only (iic.) — v. [11] pr. (vratáyati) to observe a vow or oath; not. to observe a ritual fast | Lat. verbum; Eng. word; Fr. verbe. vratāt as a result of a vow. vratam car to observe a vow (not. of chastity). vratam dhr to observe a vow.
vratabandha [bandha] m. soc. ceremony of investiture of the sacred cord [upavīta]; syn. upanayana soc. restriction related to the observance of a vow.
vratasnātaka |snātaka| m. soc. returning home after fulfilling his vows; if he has also completed his Vedic studies, he is vidyāvratasnātaka .
vratopāyana [upāyana] n. ved. np. of the Vra topāyana, first ceremony of the full moon sacrifice [pūrṇamāsa]; there one swears to tell the truth.
vratáti [obj. vṛt₁] f. liana — act. f. expansion; act of covering.
vratín [vratain] amnf vratinī who observes vows — ifc. who follows, who venerates (iic.) — m. ascetic; faithful, pious man.
vratyá |vrataya| amnf vratyā obedient; pious; faithful (to (g.)) — m. vrátya soc. in accordance with a religious observance — n. soc. food appropriate for a day of fasting.
√ষ্ vrasc v. [6] pr. (vrscati) pp. (vrkna) aor. [5] (avraścīt) aor. [4] (avrākṣīt) aor. [3] (avivraścat) to tear, to cut — ca. (vraścayati) to cause to tear.
vraścana [agt. vraśc] amnf vraścanā (that or the one) who cuts | to cut — n. saw; chisel — act. n. cut, incision; wound | sap, latex flowing from the incision in the bark of a tree.
vrāta |*vrata| m. multitude, crowd; group, company; troop | attendance at a wedding — n. manual labor; occasional day labor. vrātam in numbers, in crowds; in troops. pañcavrātāḥ the 5 races of men.
vrātika [vrātaika] n. soc. vow [vrata] taken by a student before beginning the study of esoteric texts [āranyaka].
vrātīna [vrātaīna] m. manual laborer; or nomadic laborer working by the day.

vrātya [*vrataya] amnf vrātyā no made; wanderer; heretic — m. Vedic. member of a brotherhood of magician-shamans, associated with the rudrās; they performed a 12-day ceremony at the winter solstice to bring back the Sun, with a sacrifice of dogs, and used dice made of polished sheep bones. SOC. member of a non-Brahmanic community; outcast, pariah; person deposed from their caste, pariah | SOC. not. Brahmin who has gone abroad without compelling reason; man of the ārya caste who does not observe Vedic ritual observances | vagabond; seasonal worker, migrant. SOC. Brahmanic student on holiday, who begs for cows in a group.
vrātyakāṇḍa | kāṇḍa | n. lit. section of the Atharva veda glorifying the vrātya .
vrātyastoma [stoma] n. SOC. ceremony of reintegration or integration of a vrātya into the brahmanic community.
√ vrī [related to vr₂] v. [9] pr. (vrīnāti) v. [4] pr. r. (vrīyate) pp. (vrīṇa) choose.
√ vrīd v. [1] pr. r. (vrīdate) pp. (vrīdita) to be ashamed.
vrīḍā [act. vrīḍ] f. modesty, timidity; shame. vrīdām kṛ to be ashamed; to be intimidated; to be perplexed. vrīdām upagam id.
vrīdāvat [vat] amnf vrīdāvatī ashamed, inti midé, confused.
vrīḍita [pp. vrīḍ] amnf vrīḍitā shameful, confused; timid — n. shame, confusion.
vrīṇa [pp. vrī] amnf vrīṇā chosen, elected.

vrīhi m. rice (plant, before winnowing) | pl. grains of rice. bahuvrīhih m. rich | gram. exocentric possessive compound. odanam bubhukşur vrīhīn prokṣati who wants to eat a dish of rice must soak the grains. vrīhika [ika] amnf vrīhikā who has rice.
vrīhin [in] amnf vrīhiṇī ["rich in rice"] rice paddy.
vrīhimat [mat] amnf vrīhimatī id.
√ vrud var. brud v. [6] pr. (vrudati) pp. (vrudita) to cover, to conceal; to submerge.
vruḍita [pp. vruḍ] amnf vruḍitā dissi mulé; plunged, sunk.
√ vlī var. blī v. [9] pr. (vlīnāti) pp. (vlīna) to crush — ps. (vlīyate) to succumb.

vlīna [pp. vlī] amnf vlīnā crushed, sunk, collapsed. s ম śa nota. gram. modifier | vikaraṇa₂ | of formation of the present of gaṇa 6 | tudādi|, thematic without affix to reduced degree. °ম śa (for śaya) extended over | to whom belongs, in whom Is.
śaṃyú [śam₁yu] amnf benevolent, benevolent | myth. np. of Śamyu "Benevolent", son of Brhaspati and Tārā; he presides over the Vedic sacrifice; he is sometimes said to be the father of Agni.

√ śaṃs v. [1] pr. (śaṃsati) pft. (śaśaṃsa) pp. (śasta) pfp. (śaṃsya, śasya, śastavya) pf. (ā, pra) to indicate, show | to relate, say; to proclaim, reveal; to pronounce (not. an oath) | Vedic to recite (as hotr) | to praise, celebrate — ca. (śaṃsayati) pp. (śaṃsita) id. || Lat. carmen. nivacanam śaṃsati he makes a speech.

sáṃsa |act. saṃs| m. recitation; proclamation Vedic not. recitation of the Rigveda | incantation; invocation; promise, vow; imprecation; blessing, curse — f. śaṃsā praise; eulogy; announcement, proclamation; enunciation.
śaṃsita [pp. ca. śaṃs] amnf śaṃsitā declared, said; celebrated, praised.
śaṃsin [agt. śaṃs] amnf śaṃsinī who indicates; who announces, who proclaims; who recites.
śáṃstṛ [agt. śaṃs] m. Vedic hymn reciter; syn. praśāstṛ | praise singer, panegyrist.
śáṃsya [pfp. [1] śaṃs] amnf śaṃsyā to
recite | praiseworthy | desirable — m. SOC. fire its Eastern criticism.

√ śak v. [5] pr. (śaknóti) v. [4] pr. (śakyati) aor. [2] (akaśat) pp. (śakta) pfp. (śakya) pf. (pra, sam) to be able to, to be capable of (inf.) — ps. (śakyate) to be able to (inf.) — des. (śikṣati) des. r. (śikṣate) pp. (śikṣita) cf. śikṣ. śaknoti kartum he can do it. tatkartum śaknomi I can do it. śakyate bhavitum var. śakyam bhavitum It is possible; it can be done. tacchakyate kartum var. tatkartum śakyate that can be done. rāṣṭraṃ bhoktuṃ śakyasi pālayan |Mah.| You will be able to enjoy the kingdom while protecting it. স্থাক Śaka₁ m. hist. np. of the Scythian Śaka people who arrived from Bactria in northwestern India in the 1st century BC to found the kuṣāṇa kingdom | pl. śakās geo. the Šakās or Indo-Scythians; myth. it is said that their kings are the kṣatriyās born from the sweat of Vasistha's cow, in order to destroy the army of Viśvāmitra; King Sagara fought them in vain | [śakakāla] hist. the Saka era, beginning in the year 78. śakavarsesu catuhśatesu pañcasastiyutesu ["in the saka₁ four hundred and sixty-five" era] In 543.
śakakāla [kāla₁] m. hist. the era [saṃvat] saka₁, beginning in the year 78 with King Śālivāhana.
Śakāyanya [āyanya] m. phil. np. of the sage Śakāyanya, who taught wisdom to King Bṛhadratha₁ in the Maitrī.
śáka₂ |śakan| n. excrement, garbage; droppings, dung.
sákadhūma |dhūma| m. smoke from a cow dung fire. śakadhūmaja ved. born in the dung fire.
śakandhu | andhu | n. manure pit.
śakāśa |āśa₂| amnf śakāśā who eats excrement.
Śaka₃ [act. śak] ifc. amnf śakā possibility.
śakaṭa mnf śakaṭī char, chariot — m. myth. np. of the asura Sakata, killed by Kṛṣṇa.
śakaṭikā [ika] f. small pull-along cart (child's toy) | floral decoration cart. Śakațin |in| amnf Śakaținī who owns a cart.

śakaṭāla m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the minister Sakatala of King Nanda; when Indradatta magically entered the king's body to restore him to life as Yogananda, he ordered all the corpses to be burned, causing Indradatta's body to disappear; for burning the body of a living Brahmin he was thrown into a dungeon with his 100 sons, with only one ration for all per day; Vararuci had him released and reinstated; Vararuci fell into disgrace, but sakaṭāla did not execute him, knowing his powers, and secretly sheltered him; he was pardoned by freeing Prince Hiranyagupta from his curse; Saka₁țala then conspired with Cāṇakya to kill Yogananda and his son, and install Candragupta, the son of the true king Nanda, on the throne; the latter appointed Cāṇakya minister; Śakaṭala became er mite, and Vararuci left for Vindhyavāsinī.
śakan [related to śakṛt] n. [nom. acc. śakṛt] excrement, filth | gr. o.

śakam [acc. Śaka₁] iic. sákambhará var. sakambhara |bhara| amnf śakambharā that carries excrement. সকল śákala mn piece, portion, end; fragment, shard, shard; scale; bark | hist. np. of Sakala, author of a sāman — n. half; not. half-moon, hemistich, etc. | cinnamon | a type of black pigment used in dyeing. śakalam kṛ to separate, divide.

śakāra [(śa)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'śa' | lit. [Mṛcchakaṭikā] np. of Sakāra, brother of a wife of King Pālaka; he is frivolous, arrogant, fan faron and cruel | by extension conventional theatrical character of the brother of the royal concubine; he wears luxurious clothes, is proud and arrogant.

śakita [pp. śak] amnf śakitā capable of (inf.); incapable of (inf.) (with na, passive). na śakitam chettum it could not be cut. na śakitam tena (impers.) he was not capable of it. স্কুন śakuna m. (large) bird; bird of prey, kite, vulture, eagle | soc. bird of omen — n. omen, augury; good omen; bad omen — f. Śakunī female bird | myth. np. of Śakunī, female demon who makes children sick; cf. Pūtanā.
śakunaka |ka| mf śakunikā sort of big oi bucket.
śakunajña |jña| amnf śakunajñā who knows omens. śakunaśāstra | śāstra | n. science of omens.

śakuni [śakunai] m. (large) bird; not. mi lan, vulture, crow | myth. [Mah.] np. of the Gāndhāra prince Sakuni "vulture"; he is Saubala, son of King Subala, brother of Gāndhārī, and treacherous advisor to Duryodhana; he won for him the kingdom of Yudhişthira by cheating at dice (the dice were made from his father's thigh bone, and obeyed him); he personifies the dvāparayuga; Ulūka is his son; at the end of the great battle, he was beheaded by Sa hadeva | astr. second fixed lunar halfday [karana].
śakunta | related to śakuna | m. bird; not. oi bucket of prey.

śakuntalā [śakuntala] f. myth. [Mah.] np. of Sakuntalā "Protected by the birds", daughter of Viśvāmitra and the nymph [apsaras] Menakā; abandoned in the woods at her birth, she was "Protected by the birds", then found by the sage Kanva, who raised her in his hermitage as his daughter; lit. she is the heroine of the drama Abhijñānaśakuntalā by Kālidāsa; King Dusyanta having married her in the gāndharva fashion, she gave birth to Bharata; by the curse of Durvāsā that she would have poorly received the king forgot her, and only recognized her later thanks to the magic ring he had given her.
śákṛt n. excrement; filth. śákṛtkari [ kari₁ ₁] m. [“that which makes manure”] calf.
śakta [pp. śak] amnf śaktā capable of (inf. g. dat. i.); powerful, strong.

śákti [act. śak] f. power, strength, force | spear, shaft; iron javelin | myth. Skanda's spear, made by Viśvakarmā by planing the Sun's brilliance | myth. the energy of fire, Agni's weapon phil. divine feminine principle, opp. vahni; power of a personified god | myth. np. of Sakti₁ "the Force" (of Shiva), Supreme Goddess, epithet of Durga in her aspect of cosmic energy | phil. [śaiva] the trident [triśūla] of the three powers comprises will [icchā], knowledge [jñāna], and action [kriyā]; Somānanda adds to them aesthetic pleasure |nirvṛti| and creative tension |aunmukhya| | phil. [Trika] the supreme creative energy, which has three aspects: parāśakti the transcendent energy, parāpara śakti the intermediate energy, and aparā śakti the immanent energy | phil. [Nyāya] evocative power of a word | lit. [KM.] poetic talent — m. myth. np. of Sakti₁, eldest son of the rși Vasistha and Arund hatī; walking one day on a narrow path, he found himself facing the king Kalmāṣapāda, and asked him to step aside, having priority as a brahmin; the king struck him with a stick, and cursed him; his father Vasistha had the king possessed by the vampire [rākṣasa] Kimkara; Kalmāṣapāda himself became a worse vam, and he devoured Sakti₁ and her 100 brothers; after Sakti₁'s death, his wife Adráyantī gave birth to Parāśara, who was already chanting the Veda in her womb. śáktigraha [graha] amnf śaktigrahā who carries a spear gram. who understands the meaning (of a word or phrase) — m. soldier | myth. epith. of Skanda gram. evocative power of a word. śaktigraham vyākaraņopamānakośāptavākyād vya vahāratas ca vākyasya sesād vivrter vadanti sāṃnidhyataḥ siddhapadasya vṛddhāḥ || gram. [Muktāvalī] The ancient masters say that the evocative power of a word can be understood from grammar, analogy, the dictionary, the speech of a competent person; but also from common usage, the rest of the sentence, a paraphrase, or proximity to a known word.
śaktigrahopāya [upāya] m. gram. means of knowing the meaning of a word. śáktitā [ tā ] f. ifc. power, capacity, faculty of.
śaktitrikona [trikona] n. phil. [Tantra] aqueous triangle, point downwards, symbolizing the female principle in geometric [yantra] diagrams.
sáktitva [tva] n. ifc. power, capacity, ability to.

śaktideva [deva] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the brahmin Saktideva of Vardhamāna₃; a gambler and debauchee, he claimed to have visited the city of Kanakapurī; after many adventures, he arrived there and met Candraprabhā; a horse threw him into a lake, from which he magically emerged in Vardhamāna₃; he informed Kanakarekhā, who was freed from her curse, and returned to Kanakapurī; Saktideva then went to Utsthala, where Bindumatī₁ fell in love with him; then he met Bindurekhā whom he also married; he became the vidyādhara king Saktivega.
sáktipāta [pāta] m. phil. ["fall of power"] spiritual initiation by a master [guru]; trans mission of spiritual energy from a master to a disciple theorized in the Trika philosophy of Abhina vagupta.
śaktipītha [pītha] n. cf. pīthasthāna.
śaktibhadra [bhadra] m. hist. np. of śaktibhadra, 9th century playwright (South India); he is credited with the Aśrayacūḍāmaṇi; some works attributed to Bhāsa are attributed to him by others.
sáktibhrt [bhrt] amnf powerful | np. of Saktibhrt, epith. of Skanda "who carries the javelin".

śáktimat [mat] amnf śaktimatī who can; powerful, strong | competent; capable of (inf. loc.) | armed with a spear | myth. (god) accompanied by his consort, personifying his power. śáktimattva [tva] n. power.

śaktiyaśas [yaśas] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of Princess Saktiyaśā, daughter of King Vidyādhara Sphatikayaśā and Queen Hemaprabhā; she became the wife of Na ravāhanadatta. śáktivāda [ vāda ] m. lit. np. of the Śaktivāda "power of speech", a treatise on semantics by Gadādhara.
śaktyāviṣkaraṇa [āviṣkaraṇa] n. phil. [Trika] revelation of the power [Sakti₁] of Siva.

śaktivega [vega] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara king Šaktivega, born a brahmin like Saktideva in Vardhamāna₃; he visited King Udayana to contemplate the young Na ravāhanadatta, his future emperor.
śaknuvat [ppr. śak] amnf śaknuvatī ca pable (from (inf.)).

śakya [pfp. [1] śak] amnf śakyā feasible, practicable, which can be put into effect | capable of (inf.) | explicit | gram. (sense) literal | phil. [Nyāya] referent, denotation — n. (impers.) it is possible to (inf.) — ifc. which can be obliged to, which can be subject to (iic) | capacity to (iic.).
śakyatā [tā] f. phil. [Nyāya] quality of referent; meaning.
śakyatāvacchedaka | avacchedaka | phil. m. [Nyāya] reference delimiter.
śakrá [śakra] amnf śakrā ved. powerful, strong — m. ved. np. of the radiant [āditya] Sakra, epith. of Indra "the powerful" || pali sakka.
śakrágopa [gopa] m. bio. cochineal; insect used to make a red dye, crimson.
śakrágopaka | gopaka | mr. id.
śakradhanus [dhanus] n. myth. the rainbow, attribute of power of Indra.
śakrāvatāra [avatāra] m. myth. n.p. from Sakrāvatāra, place called the “Descent of Indra”; cf. śacītīrtha.
śákvan [śakvan] amnf śakvarī powerful, capable — f. śakvarī phon. Vedic meter of 7 feet of 8 syllables | meter of 4 times 14 syllables; cf. va santatilakā.

v. [1] pr. r. (kate) pp. (kita) pfp. (śańkya, śańkitavya) pf. (ā, pari, vi) to suspect, to distrust (acc.); to fear something from someone. (abl.) | to hesitate, to doubt; to suspect, to conjecture | lat. cunctor. śańke adv. I suppose; in my opinion, probably; it seems, perhaps | it may be feared.

śamkará var. śankara [śam₃kara₁] amnf śaṃkarā benevolent, who brings good fortune or prosperity (np.) — m. myth. np. of Sankara or Samkara, epith. of Shiva "granting his blessing" | hist. np. of Sankara₁ or Adi Sankarācārya "Benevolent Master" (∼700– 750) philosopher born in Kālaṭi (near modern-day Kochi in Kerala); he was a disciple of Govindanātha; he lived in Vārāṇasī, where he preached Vedānta based on Advaita doctrine; he is credited with numerous works, notably. Vivekacūdāmaņi, Digvijaya, Prapancasāra, Aparokṣānubhūti, Mo hamudgara, Upadeśasāhasrī, Brahmasūtrabhāsya₁ Śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣya, Cidānandadaśaślokī; he founded 4 monasteries [matha], resp. in Purī Govardhana₃, Śrigerī, Dvārakā and Badarīnātha (jyotirmațha); their superiors are the pontiffs [jagadguru] of the daśanāmīdaṇḍin order of the advaita doctrine; he founded the system of the 6 doctrines [Ṣanmatasthāpakācārya] | hist. np. of Sankara₂ or Samkara₂ Miśra, poet, playwright and scholar of the 15th century; to him is the Kaṇādarahasya, which describes the categories of Vaiseka with the methods of Navyanyāya — f. śaṃkarī myth. np. of Śaṃkarī "Wife of Samkara", epith. of the Goddess | hist. np. of Samkara₃, scholar of Kaśmīra around the 10th century, author of the Samketa₁, commentary on the Harsacarita | hist. np. of Samkara₄, logician [naiyāyika] of the 7th century, author of the Sthirasiddhi — f. śaṃkarā bio. zoo. Sturnia pagodarum "Pagoda Starling" or Brahman Myna, a pretty beige bird with a black hood and a serene appearance; it is compared to wandering renunciants | parivrājikā|. śamkarā nāma śakunikā the bird called Brahman Myna. śańkararanya [ranya] m. hist. np. of the renunciant Svāmī Sankararanya "Pleasure of Benevolence", elder brother of Caitanya; cf. Viśvarūpa₂. śańkaravarman [varman] m. hist. np. of the king of Kaśmīra Sankaravarmā (883–902); cf. Agamadambara.

śankaravijaya [vijaya] m. lit. np. of the Sankaravijaya₁ "Decisive Victory of Sankara₁", work by Anandagiri refuting heresies | lit. np. of the Sankaravijaya₁, biography of Sankara₁ by Vyāsācala, also called Vyāsācalīya. śańkarasena [senā] m. med. np. of the physician Śamkarasena, author of the Nāḍīprakāśa (18th century?). śańkarasvāmin [svāmin] m. hist. np. of Śaṅkarasvāmī, logician and author of the Nyāyapraveśa. śańkarācārya [ācārya] m. hist. Master Saṃkarānanda, one of the superiors of the four monasteries [matha] founded by him. śańkarānanda [ānanda] m. hist. np. of the philosopher Saṃkarānanda; he was the guru of Sāyaṇa; he is credited with the Atmapurāṇa and numerous commentaries on the esoteric teachings [upaniṣad]. সঙ্কা śańkā [act. śańk] f. worry, apprehension, fear | suspicion, mistrust, dread; suspicion of (abl. loc. pratiacc.) | doubt, hesitation — ifc. belief in; the act of supposing that; suspicion of, presumption of (iic.) — iic. id. brahmahatyākṛtā śaṅkā fear of having caused the death of a brahmin. pāpaśankā na kartavyā [KSS.] There is no reason to suspect that a sin has been committed. śańkāsthāna [sthāna] n. cause of fear; object of suspicion.
śańkita [pp. śańk] amnf śańkitā preoccupied, worried, alarmed; distrustful, fearful; fearful; doubtful, uncertain.
śańkitavya [pfp. [3] śańk] amnf śankitavyā to be feared, to be wary of. śankitavyam (impers.) it is to be feared.

śaṅkin [agt. śaṅk] amnf śaṅkinī anxious, suspicious; distrustful; jealous; timid — ifc. one who fears, who believes (iic.) | one who arouses concern. kākaśańkī as suspicious as a crow. atisnehaḥ pāpaśaṃkī excessive affection makes one fear the worst.

śańkú [śańku] m. stake, post; tree trunk | peg, nail; arrow, point | astr. gnomon of a sundial | phil. the sting of remorse | astr. sine of altitude | math. one billion (a thousand billion) [hist. np. of Sanku, one of the nine jewels [navaratna] of the court of King Vikramāditya | myth. [Mah.] np. of Prince Vṛṣṇi Śaṅku₁, son of Ugrasena; he is one of the 7 famous Yādavās archers. śańkuka [ka] m. small peg; nail | hist. np. poet and playwright śrī Sankuka at the court of King Ajitapīda (circa 850); He is the author of the Bhuvanābhyudaya, commentaries on literary aesthetics; he is also credited with comedies, such as the Citrotpalāvalambitaka. śańkúkarṇa [karṇa] amnf śańkukarṇī who has pointed ears — m. donkey.
śaṅkulā [śaṅkula] f. scalpel | scissors; cutting pliers (not. for cutting areca nut). śańkulākhaṇḍa [khaṇḍa] mn (fragment, piece) cut with scissors or pliers.

śańkya [pfp. [1] śańk] amnf śańkyā to be feared, to be wary of | to be anticipated, to be anticipated. śańkyam (impers.) it is to be feared. সাহ্ব śańkhá mn conch; shell, seashell myth. conch attribute of Vișnu, symbolizing the divine call; cf. Pāncajanya — m. med. frontal bone; forehead of the elephant, between the tusks | myth. np. of the demon [daitya] Sankha; he hid the Veda at the bottom of the ocean; VișnuMatsya fished it out — n. math. ten billion | lat. concha; fr. conque.

śankhacūḍa [cūḍā] amnf śankhacūḍā wearing a conch shell — m. myth. np. of the asura Sankhacūda, born of a curse from Rādhā to the dear vagrant Sudāmā₁; through his penances at Badarīnātha he obtained from Brahmā the shield Viṣṇukavaca which assured him of invincibility; he married Tulasī and committed many sins; Vișnu asked Shiva to fight him, and assumed his identity to present himself to Tulasī and bring her back to Vaikuntha as Lakshmi. śańkhadvāra [dvāra] n. arch. sanctuary threshold adorned with two conch shells. śańkhanāda [nāda] m. noise produced by sounding a conch shell, not. to call to battle.
Śankhanidhi [nidhi] m. myth. n.p. of Sankhanidhi, one of the 9 treasures of Kubera | navanidhi |.

śankhápāla [pāla] m. myth. np. of the nāga Sankhapāla. śańkhapuspī [puspa] f. bio. bot. Clitoria terna tea, legume with purple flowers, also called aparājitā; it is sacred to Shiva | bio. bot. Canscora alata, gentian with white flowers like the conch.

śankhámuktā [muktā] f. mother-of-pearl. śańkhálikhita [likhita] amnf śańkhalikhitā im peccable, perfect; without defect, irreproachable. śańkhalikhitavṛtti [ vṛtti ] f. irreproachable conduct. śańkhavat |vat| amnf śańkhavatī who has the conch in hand. śańkhāsura [asura] m. myth. np. of the sea demon Sankhāsura "Genius of the conch"; cf. Pancajana.
śankhana m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā Sankhaṇa, son of Pravṛddha, father of Sudarśana₂.
śaṅkhin [śaṅkhain] amnf śaṅkhinī who possesses a conch | myth. relating to the demon Sankha — m. ocean | myth. epith. of Viṣṇu — f. cf. śankhinī.
śaṅkhinī [f. śaṅkhin] f. mother-of-pearl | soc. [kāmaśāstra] one of the 4 natures of women (with citrinī, padminī, and hastinī).
śacī [related to śak] f. assistance, help, grace | dexterity; eloquence | myth. np. of Sacī "Grace", daughter of Pulomā₁, wife of Indra.
śacītīrtha [tīrtha] n. myth. place called the pilgrimage site of Sacī, where Sakuntalā stopped on the way to the palace of Dușyanta; it is also called Sakrāvatāra.
śacīpati [pati] m. myth. np. of Sacīpati "Master of Grace", epith. of Indra.
śaṭha amnf śaṭhā false, deceitful; per fide, traitor; adultery — m. wicked; traitor; unfaithful husband.
śaṭhatā |tā| f. wickedness, vice; deceit, per fidie. śathatva |tva| n. id.

śaṭhāri | ari | m. enemy of traitors | soc. Vaishnava bell-shaped cult instrument in silver bearing the imprint of Vishnu's feet; it is used by the priest to bless the faithful at the temple by placing it on their heads.
śaṇá m. organic. bot. cannabis sativa, hemp || lat. cannabis; fr. hemp. সাত্ত śaṇḍa m. curdled milk, fresh cheese | myth. n.p. of Saṇḍa, son of Sukra, priest of the asurās.
śatá num. n. sg. A hundred, a hundred — f. śatī ifc. id. || gr. o ; lat. centum; fr. Hundred. dve sate var. quoted two hundred. trīņi śatāni 300. śatāni trīni 103. astāni satāni 800.
śatakarna [karna] m. n.p. of man. śatakṛtvas | kṛtvas | adv. 100 times.
śatakratu [kratu] m. myth. np. of Satakratu, epithet of Indra "He who has performed 100 sacrifices". śatakrato | vivardhasva || Prosperous, O Indra.
śatajit [jit] m. myth. np. of the king śatajit "of the Hundred Victories", son of Sahasrajit; he is father of Ekavīra.
śatatamá [tama] amnf śatatamī ord. 100ᵉ. tricatvārimsottaradvisatatamo'dhyāyah 243° chapter.

śatada [da] amnf śatadā Who gives 100 (cows) (to a Brahmin). śatadru [dru₂] f. geo. np. of the Satadru or Śutudrī river "That which flows in 100 (branches)"; it descends from the Himalayas towards the Pañjāb to flow into the Indus (mod. Sutlej); cf. Anavatapta.

śatadhanvan [dhanvan] m. myth. np. of the yādava king Satadhanvā "of the Hundred Bows"; at the instigation of Akrūra and Kṛtavarmā he assassinated Satrājit to seize the magic jewel Syamantaka; Kṛṣṇa and Balabhadra pursued him and killed him.

śatapatha [patha] amnf śatapathā ["Having 100 paths"] Having many aspects. śatapathabrāhmaṇa [ brāhmaṇa ] n. lit. np. of the Satapatha brāhmaṇa "the Hundred Ways of Ritual", attached to the White Yajurveda; it comprises 14 books [khaṇḍa], divided into 100 lessons [adhyāya]; cf. Yājñavalkya.
śatapad [pad₂] amnf śatapadī [nom. śatapāt] Who has One Hundred Feet.

śatabhiṣaj [bhiṣaj] f. astr. np. of Satabhiṣak "He who heals a hundredfold", 23rd lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the star of Aquarius [kumbha]; Indra (or Varuna) presides over it; its symbol is a circle.

śatarūpā [rūpa] f. myth. np. of śatarūpā "Multiform", feminine cosmological emanation of Brahmā, both creator (through her masculine double Virāţ) and wife of ManuSvāyaṃbhuva. śataśas [ śas ] adv. by hundreds; One hundred times. śataśāstra [ śāstra ] n. lit. np. of Sataśāstra "treatise in 100 verses" by Aryadeva.

śataśriga |śriga| amnf śataśrigā Who has a Hundred Peaks — n. myth. [Mah.] np. of Sataśriga, the mountain "of the Hundred Peaks", where King Pāṇḍu withdrew when he became a hermit. śatásahasra | sahasra | n. One hundred thousand.
satasahasrasas |sas| adv. by hundreds of thousands.

śatasahasraka | sahasraka | amnf śatasahasrikā consisting of One hundred thousand. śatasāhasra | sahasra | amnf śatasāhasrā f. śatasāhasrī consisting of One hundred thousand — n. One hundred thousandth share | pl. One hundred thousand. gavām śatasahasrāni One hundred thousand cows. śatasāhasraka [ sāhasraka ] amnf śatasāhasrikā consisting of One Hundred Thousand. śatasāhasrikā prajñāpāramitā bd. long version of the prajñāpāramitā, in 100,000 verses [sūtra].

śatānanda [ānanda] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the ascetic Satānanda₁ "joy a hundredfold", eldest son of Gautama and Ahalyā; he was chaplain [purohita] of King Janakarāja | hist. np. of Šatānanda₁, disciple of Svāminārāyaņa, author of the Satsangijīvana.

Śatānīka [anīka] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Satānīka₁ "of the army of One Hundred brave men", son of Nakula and Draupadī; during the great war he was killed by Aśvatthāmā; Sahasrānīka is his son; cf. Jayat sena | myth. [BhP.] np. of Satānīka₁, son of Ja namejaya, father of Adhisīmakṛṣṇa | lit. [KSS.] this king of Kauśāmbī had Viṣṇumatī as his queen; The hermit Sāṇdilya gave her a consecrated food, and she gave birth to Sahasrānīka whom the king made crown prince, before fighting the demons [asura] at Indra's side.
śatāvadhānin [avadhānin] amnf śatāvadhāninī ["Who can pay attention to 100 different things"| champion of astāvadhāna capable of prodigies of memorization.
śatāvara [avara] mn soc. fine of 1 OO (paṇa) — f. Organic śatāvarī. bot. Asparagus racemosus, wild perch; its tuberous roots are used medicinally.

śataka [śataka] amnf śatikā in One Hundred parts | hundredth — n. hundred; set of 100 stanzas; century | lit. collection of One Hundred poems; cf. śatakatraya. sūryaśatakam One Hundred hymns to the Sun.
śatakatraya [traya] n. bed. n.p. from Satakatraya “Triple collection of Hundred poems” by Bhartrhari₁; it includes the Nītiśataka, the Śrṅgāraśataka, and the Vairāgyaśataka.
śatika [śataika] amnf śatikā numbering one hundred; containing one hundred; at the price of one hundred; relating to one hundred.
śatr nota. gram. primary affix [kṛt₂] marking the active present participle, indicating simultaneity with the main action.
śatya |śataya| amnf śatyā consisting of a hundred | Which can be acquired for 100 (rupees).

śátru [śadru] m. (He who attacks, He who overthrows, He who vanquishes) enemy, rival, aggressor, invader; not. hostile neighboring king — ifc. hostile towards; He who conquers, He who vanquishes (iic.) | (a. bahuvrīhi) defeated by (iic.) || gr. κοτος; ang. hate. śatrughna [ghna] m. myth. np. of śatrughna "He who conquers the enemy", son of Daśaratha and Sumitrā, twin brother of Laksmana, companion of his half-brother Bharata₁; he killed the asurās Madhu₂ and Lavana; he is credited with the founding of the city of Mathurā, which he gave to his son Subāhu₁.
śatrutā [tā] f. hostility, enmity. śatrutva [tva] n. id. śatrunibarhana | nibarhana | afmn śatrunibarhaṇā He who exterminates his enemies. śátruvat [vat] adv. like an enemy.

śatruśalya [śalya] m. hist. n.p. from Satruśalya, epith. of king Jām Sattarsāl of Navanagara (15691608). śatruśalyacarita [carita] n. bed. n.p. of the Satruśalyacarita, eulogy of Satruśalya due to Viśvanātha₃.

śatrum [acc. śatru ] iic. śátrumjaya var. Śatruñjaya [ jaya ] m. Satruñjaya "Victory over the enemy", np. of man, king, elephant | geo. epith. of Mount Vimalādri; it is a sacred place [tīrtha] and an important pilgrimage of Jainism; it is said that Ŗṣabhanātha gave his first sermon there.
śatrumjayamahātmya [mahātmya] n. bed. n.p. from Satrumjayamahātmya, work jn. by Candra gacchīya Dhaneśvara Sūri (Gujarat, 391).

√ śad v. [1] pr. r. (śīyate) fut. (śatsyati) pft. (śaśāda) pp. (śanna) to fall — ca. (śātayati) to knock down; to destroy — ca. (śādayati) to drive cattle (in front of oneself). bilvam bilvena śātaya | Mah. | Break the bel shell with the bel shell.

Śani [śam₁] m. myth. np. from the graha Sani "(Slow) Star", regent of the planet Saturn; he is the son of Sūrya and Chāyā, and is thus Divākarasuta; astr. his astral influence is feared, he has the evil eye; he is said to be lame |Pangu|, flatulent and lazy; [Rām.] Rāvaṇa, fearing his influence, enclosed him in a cistern, from which his friend Hanuman freed him; his first glance fell upon the golden palace of Rāvaṇa, which became black; he is represented as a black mass with shining eyes, or as a black man dressed in black; his mount is the donkey, or sometimes the vulture, the crow, the buffalo or the tortoise; cf. Krūradṛṭ, Krūralocana, Kroda, Nīlānjanagiri, Manda, Saura.
śanivāra [vāra] m. Saturday.
śanais [śam₁] adv. very gently, slowly; little by little, gradually var. śanakais id. śanaihśanais adv. little by little, gradually.
śanaiścara | cara | amnf śanaiścarā That which moves slowly — m. astr. np. of Sanaiścara, epith. of the planet Saturn and of the graha Sani.
śáṃtanu n. cf. śāṃtanu.
śantu [śam₃tu] amnf happy.

√ sáp v. [1] pr. (sápati) pft. (sásāpa) pft. r. (śepe) pp. (śapta, śapita) pfp. (śapya) pf. (abhi) to curse, pronounce a curse, utter an imprecation | to insult (acc.) — pr. r. ( śapate ) to swear; to take an oath to (dat.) upon (i.) | to insult, to curse (dat.) — ca. (śāpayati) pp. (śāpita) to make swear by (i.). śape I swear. śap yadi ... to promise not to ... anrtam sap to make a false oath. satyena vai sape truly I swear it. svayamupagatā śrīstyajyamānā śapati Fortune in espérée qu’on fuit devient malèche.
sap₁ part. prefix of assent. śap karoti he agrees.
√ sap₁ v. [1] pr. (sapati) to follow, honor, serve | to caress; to love — ca. (sāpayati) to pay homage to, to serve.
śap₂ nota. gram. modifier [vikaraṇa₂] of present formation of gaṇa 1 [bhvādi], with thematic a, full degree | guna |.
śapa |act. śap| m. curse, imprecation | oath.
śapatha | śapatha | m. curse, imprecation, anathema | resolution, oath, vow. śapatham kr to swear, to take an oath.
śapita [pp. śap ] amnf śapitā cursed.
sapta [pp. sap] amnf saptā cursed | conjured, adjured — n. oath.
śaptavat [ppa. śap] amnf śaptavatī Who has cursed.
śaphá m. hoof; not. horse hoof | claw; hook | not. wooden hook for removing a pot from the fire | ang. hoof.
śaphavat [vat] amnf śaphavatī (animal) with hooves.
śaphara m. organic. zoo. Cyprinus sophora, small shiny fish; carp.

sábara m. tribal people of the Deccan; chas seur; savage, barbarian | myth. np. of Sabara, epithet of Shiva "Savage Hunter" | hist. np. of Sabara₁ Svāmī or Sabarasvāmī, 5th century philosopher of language, author of the Mīmāṃsābhāṣya; his work served as the foundation for the systems of Kumārila and Prabhākara — f. śabarī tribal woman | myth. [Ram.] np. of Sabarī, tribal woman who gave Rāma jujubes [badara]; she tasted each fruit before giving it to him, to be sure that it was tasty; she personifies the devotion that liberates from sins.
śabarabhāsya [bhāṣya] n. bed. n.p. of the Sabarabhāsya, commentary by Sabarasvāmī of the Mīmāṃsāsūtra; cf. Mīmāmsābhāsya.

Śabala amnf śabalā f. Śabalī variegated, spotted; tinged with (iic. i.) | myth. ["with variegated fur"] np. of Sabala, guardian dog of the underworld of Yama, with a piercing gaze [caturakṣa]; he was born of Saramā, like his brother the black Syāma; he symbolizes the Sunday, as his brother the Moonnight; du. they are collectively designated as the pair śabalau; cf. Kālakañjās | changed, altered — f. cf. śabalā | gr. κερβερος; fr. Cerberus. śabalau m. du. myth. Sabala and Syāma, the two dogs of the sky of Yama.

śabalā var. Śabalī [f. Śabala] f. myth. np. of Sabalā or Sabalī "variegated", the abundant cow of Pṛthu | myth. [Rām.] epith. of Nandinī, the abundant cow of Vasistha. স্থাব্দ śábda m. noise, sound; word, speech; discourse, language | name, title, appellation | oral tradition | gram. articulated element of language: morpheme, word, phrase | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the perception [tanmātra] of hearing [śrotra]; this subtle element is governed [niyantr] by the Diśas | phil. [Mīmāṃsā] it is the specific quality [viśeṣaguṇa] of space [ākāśa] phil. [Nyāya] the Word, authority of sacred speech, a means of knowledge [pramāṇa] | gram. [Bhartrhari] language, in the two forms of articulated sound signal [dhvani] and meaning [artha] gram. denoting word; Patañjali₁ distinguishes 4 categories: jātiśabda common noun (denoting a species), gunasabda adjective (denoting a property), kriyāśabda Verb (denoting an action) and yadrcchāśabda proper noun (denoting an individual) | gram. [Patañjali₁] sound production enabling the recognition of a known object | (music) note of the tempered keyboard, dividing an octave into 12; by adding 10 quarter tones, one obtains the 22 notes | śruti| of the natural keyboard — ifc. gram. the word "(iic.)" — v. [11] pr. r. (śabdāyate) v. [11] pr. (śabdayati) pp. (śabdita) to make noise. śabdam kr to call out loudly. śabdam dā to raise one's voice, to call. saśabdam adv. loudly. śabdam kuru make noise. mā śabdam kārṣīḥ do not make noise. śabdapūrvena yogena phil. yoga based on speech

imperishable [śabdatattva]. kvaśabdah m. gram. the word "kva". dvitīyagāmī na hi śabda eşa nah this is our title and does not apply to anyone else. yenoccāritena sāsnālāngūlakakudakhuravisāninām sampratyayo bhavati sa śabdaḥ [Patañjali₁] The śabda is what, when pronounced, allows one to identify a horned, hoofed, humped, tailed, and dewlapped animal. śabdakalpa | kalpa | amnf śabdakalpā gram. proper to treating the tongue.
śabdakalpataru [taru] m. gram. lexicon.

śabdakalpadruma [druma] m. gram. encyclopedia lit. np. of the Sabdakalpadruma, encyclopedic lexicon of Sanskrit with grammatical indications from several Bengali scholars, at the initiative of Rājā Rādhākāntadeva. śábdakāra | kāra | amnf śabdakārī noisy; sonorous.
śábdakārin [kārin] amnf śabdakāriṇī noisy; sonorous.
śábdakośa [kośa] m. dictionary. śábdakaustubha [kaustubha] mn gram. np. from the Sabdakaustubha "Jewel of Linguistics", work by Bhattoji Dīkṣita, commentary on the Kāśikā.
śabdakaustubhadūṣaṇa [dūṣaṇa] n. gram. n.p. of the Sabdakaustubhadūṣaṇa, critique of the Sabdakaustubha by Bhāskara₃ Dīkṣita.
sábdaguna [guna] m. quality of sound.

śabdagunaka [ka] amnf śabdagunikā phil. [Vaiśeṣika] which has sound as its specific quality (said of ether [ākāśa]). śábdacāturya [ cāturya ] n. use of the right word; good diction; eloquence. śábdacaurya [caurya] n. act of plagiarism. śábdatattva [ tattva ] n. phil. ["essence of word"] the imperishable and creative word of the world | the Word constituting the symbolic universe. śabdatva |tva| n. phonetic nature.
śabdanityatva [nityatva] n. phil. [Mīmāmsā] doctrine of the eternity of sound.
sábdabodha | bodha | m. phil. knowledge induced from an oral testimony.

Śabdabrahman | brahman | n. phil. np. of Śabdabrahma, the Veda as revealed Word, erected as Supreme Being. śabdabrahmavivarta | vivarta | m. phil. aesthetic theory of transformation through linguistic acts.
śábdabhāvanā [bhāvanā] f. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] realization of speech; linguistic faculty.
sábdabheda [bheda] m. gram. spelling variant of a word.
śabdabhedaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. np. from the Sabdabhedaprakāśa, supplement to the Viśvaprakāśa dealing with orthographic variants and gender.
sábdamañjarī [mañjarī] f. bed. n.p. from the Śabdamañjarī “Linguistic Bouquet”, a glossary of inflected forms due to KLV Sāstrī (1961).

sábdamaya |maya| amnf sabdamayī made up of sound; act of speaking — ifc. formed from the word (iic.). śabdaratnākara [ratnākara] m. lit. np. from Sabdaratnākara, dictionary of synonyms by Mahīpa (14th century) | lit. np. from Sabdaratnākara₁, dictionary of words with several spellings, by Sādhusundara Gaṇī (17th century).
śabdarūpa [rūpa] n. nature or quality of a grammatical sound. [Kāśikā] structure of the signifier; grammatical word.
sábdavat |vat| amnf sabdavatī that emits a sound; noisy — adv. loudly.
śábdavidyā [vidyā] f. grammar; linguistics; philology.

sábdavrtti | vrtti | f. lit. linguistic modality; opp. cittavrtti. śabdavyāpāra | vyāpāra | m. use of speech. śabdavyāpāravicāra [ vicāra ] m. lit. np. from Sabdavyāpāravicāra "Investigation of the Use of Speech", a work on semantics by Mammata.

sábdasakti [sakti] f. phil. lexical, pragmatic semantics; power of speech | gram. power to evoke the meaning of a word; four levels are distinguished: the literal meaning [abhidhā₂], the figurative meaning | lakṣaṇā|, the suggestive meaning | vyañjanā|, and the meaning the speaker wishes to convey [tātparya]. śábdaśaktiprakāśikā [ prakāśikā ] f. phil. np. of the Sabdaśaktiprakāśikā "Revelation of the Power of Speech," a work of semantics [Navyanyāya] by Jagadīśa₁.

sábdasaktimūla | mūla | amnf sabdasaktimūlā gram. ["which has its origin in the power of words"] refers to a suggested meaning [dhvani] derived from the signifier; opp. arthaśaktimūla. śábdaśaktisvābhāvya | svābhāvya | n. gram. autonomy of the power of speech (justifying idiomatic meanings).
śábdaśesa [śesa] ifc. amnf śabdaśesā who is (iic.) only in name. prabhuśabdaśesah who is king only in title.
sábdasamjñā [samjñā₁] f. gram. technical word of grammar.
śabdasiddhi [siddhi] f. gram. morphology.
śabdādvaitavāda [advaitavāda] m. phil. doctrine expressing that all concepts are associated with a linguistic signifier.
śabdādhyāsavāda [adhyāsavāda] m. gram. doc trine expressing that the words are superimposed on their meaning, postulating the identity of śabda and artha .

śabdānukṛti [anukṛti] f. gram. onomatopoeia. kāka iti śabdānukṛtiḥ tadidam śakuniṣu bahulam [Nirukta] The word kāka is an onomatopoeia, like several bird names. śabdānuśāsana [ anuśāsana ] n. gram. language teaching, grammar rules; Treatise on Grammar | lit. np. of grammar Sabdānuśāsana "Treatise on Language" by Śākaṭāyana₁; it includes a commentary Amoghavṛtti. bhagavatā pāṇininā sādhuśabdānām vyutpādanārtham śabdānuśāsananāmakam śāstraṃ viracitam gram. The science called śabdānuśāsana, which aims at the derivation of correct speech, was established by the blessed Pāṇini.
śabdānaucitya [anaucitya] n. (literary criticism) inappropriate linguistic usage; the Vyaktivi veka distinguishes 5 kinds: lack of syn
tax [vidheyāvimarśa], incompatibility with the
context [prakramabheda], lack of sequencing [kramabheda], redundancy [paunaruktya] and failure to mention what should be expressed [vācyāvacana].
śabdābdhi [abdhi] m. gram. n.p. from the Śabdābdhi lexicon “Ocean of words”. śabdārņava [arṇava] m. bed. n.p. from the Sabdārṇava, dictionary due to Vācaspati₁ Miśra.

śabdārtha [artha] m. gram. meaning of a word; analytical meaning of a sentence broken down into words (preliminary to the gloss [bhāvārtha]) | phil. magical power of speech |du. śabdārthau gram. the linguistic sign (of Saussure), pair of sound and meaning (of a word, of a sentence). siddhe śabdārthasambandhe gram. [Kātyāyana] The relationship between speech and meaning being established. śabdārthacintā [cintā] f. gram. np. of the Sabdārthacintā, commentary on the grammar of Candragomi due to Ratnamati.
śabdārthavicāra [vicāra] m. gram. determination of the link between the signifier and the signified.
śabdālaṃkāra [alaṃkāra] m. lit. ["phonetic embellishment" | euphonic stylistic figure: rhythmic balance, repetition [yamaka], alliteration [anuprāsa]; opp. arthālamkāra.
śabdālaṃkāravicāra [vicāra] m. bed. n.p. Sabdālaṃkāravicāra, chapter of the Kāvyālamkāravrtti of Vāmana₃.
śabdāśraya [āśraya] amnf śabdāśrayā gram. Which is based on form; opp. arthāśraya.

śabdenduśekhara [induśekhara] m. gram. from the Śabdenduśekhara, commentary np. of Siddhāntakaumudī due to Nāgoji Bhaṭṭa; distinguishes it between the complete commentary on Brhaccabdenduśekhara and its summary, the Laghuśabdenduśekhara.
śabdana [śabdana] n. noise, sound; made of speaking | phil. [Bhartrhari] verbal expression, where the signifier and the signified are superimposed [adhyāsa].
śabdita [pp. śabda] amnf śabditā (noise) emitted; uttered, shouted; communicated; taught; invoked — n. noise, tumult; braying.

√ sam₁ v. [4] pr. (sāmyati) pft. (sasāma) pp. (śānta) pf. (upa, pra) to work, to tire oneself; to perform ritual acts | to calm oneself; to be calm, to be appeased, to be at peace | to rest, to withdraw, to renounce; to die out — ca. (śamayati) ca. (śāmayati) ps. (śāmyate) to calm, to appease; to reconcile (not. by a rite of conjuration) | to render immobile; to kill | German hemmen; English to hem.
√ śam₂ ca. (śamayati) ps. (śamyate) ca. (śāmayati) pf. (ni) [unusual without pf.].
śam₃ [act. śam₁] part. blessing, happiness; well-being; joyfully, happily, well.
śamyoh | yos | ved. peace and prosperity. sam₁ ca yoś ca ved. id.
sámvat |vat| amnf samvatī of good omen, favorable; prosperous.

śama [act. śam₁] m. appeasement, tranquility; peace of heart; tranquility; pacification | indifference, apathy; abandonment, renunciation, extinction | phil. |Vedanta| tranquility, one of the 6 cardinal virtues
nales |satsampad| | lit. the feeling of impassivity phil. emancipation from the illusions of existence. śamam kṛ to calm down; to be tranquil.
śamatha |śamatha| m. phil. tranquility of mind, Quietude.

śamana [agt. śam₁] amnf śamanā That which calms, That which soothes, That which softens | That which extinguishes — m. myth. np. of Samana, epith. of Yama "That which extinguishes (life)" — act. n. appeasement; extinction.
sámi [act. sam₁] n. work, labor, exercise — f. cf. śamī.
śamika [ka] m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Samika "Worker", father of Mātali.
śamita [pp. ca. śam₁] amnf śamitā appeased, calmed; extinguished | destroyed, killed | cut (nail).
śamitṛ [agt. śam₁] amnf śamitrī Who calms his mind | killer — m. ved. officiant in charge of the killing of sacrificial victims | butcher.
śamin [agt. śam₁] amnf śaminī Who is calm.

śamī [f. śami] f. bio. bot. Prosopis spici gera, Indian mimosa, leguminous tree of arid regions, with very hard wood; Vedic. its wood is used to light the sacred fire by friction, because "Agni hides there"; its fire symbolizes the anger [manyu] of the warrior; it is also used for the stake [yūpa]; [Mah.] when they spent their 13th year of exile at the court of King Virāta, the Pāṇḍavās hid their weapons in a śamī; the tree is honored at vijayadaśamī.
śamīmivābhyantaralīnapāvakām [Ragh.] she was like the śamī, Who hides in her bosom the purifying fire.
śamīka m. myth. [Mah.] np. of śamīka, son of Śūra, hero vrsni.

sámba m. myth. Indra's weapon; sometimes identified with the synonym vajra | iron chain around the belt, worn by some ascetics | furrow plowed on the way out | lit. [DKC.] np. of King Samba, son of Krishna; one day, his wife Yajñavatī asked him to capture a swan; this swan was a sage who cursed him to be chained and to suffer separation from his beloved for two months in a future reincarnation; he was reincarnated as Rajavahana.

śámbara m. bio. zoo. Cervus unicolor, sambar deer; it lives in the forest | ved. [RV.] np. of the demon [dānava] Sambara₁ (or Saṃvara); he had 99 fortresses in which he hid the soma and kept DivodāsaAtithigva prisoner; he personifies drought; Hiranyakasipu used him to persecute Prahlāda; Indra destroyed his forts and killed him to free the soma | myth. np. of the asura Sambara₁ who abducted Pradyumna as a child; the latter escaped, and as an adult returned to kill him, and marry his wife the sorceress Māyāvatī.
śambu m. bio. bivalve shell; oyster, mussel, cockle | var. śambuka id.

Śambūka [related to śambu] m. bio. shell | myth. [Rām.] np. of the śūdra Śambūka, who wrongfully practiced asceticism [tapasya] at the dvāparayuga without initiation; this offense caused the death of the son of a brahmin who reproached Rāma for it; the cause of the disorder having been explained by Nārada, Rāma cut off his head, and the young brahmin returned to life.

Sambhala m. bd. [Kālacakra] np. of the mythical subterranean kingdom of Sambhala; it is a fabulous pure land, and a spiritual realm, that of the Buddha of the future Maitreya; the Vajrayana tradition gives it a succession of 32 kings since the Buddha; the first 7 are saints | dharmarāja | transmitting the teaching of the Wheel of Time [Kālacakra]; the 25 most recent are prophesied as announcing Kalki | myth. [VP.] supposed place of Kalki's birth at the Apocalypse.
śambhu var. śaṃbhu [śam₃bhu] m. myth. n.p. of sambhu "Dispenser of blessings", name of an auspicious aspect of Siva | myth. [Rām.] np. of the daitya sambhu₁, murderer of Kuśadhvaja.
śambhukrpā [krpā] f. myth. mercy of benevolent Shiva.
śambhukṛpāmanoharastava [manoharastava] m. bed. n.p. from Sambhukṛpāmanoharastava "Hymn to the miracle of Siva's mercy", work by Ratnakantha.

śambhunātha [nātha] m. geo. np. of śambhunātha, epith. of Śiva “Blessed lord”, he is worshipped not. at the eponymous temple in Nepāla | hist. np. of Sambhunātha₁, guru of Abhinavagupta for the kaula doctrine.
śambhupuṣpāñjali [puṣpāñjali] m. bed. n.p. from Śambhupuṣpāñjali, a śaiva personal devotional manual by Saundaranātha (17th century).
śambhubhaṭṭa [bhaṭṭa] m. hist. n.p. of Śambhubhaṭṭa, mīmāṃsaka of Kāśī (~1675–1710), commentator of Khandadeva.
śaya [agt. śī₁] amnf śayā ifc. lying, prostrate, stretched out on (iic.); sleeping on (iic.) — act. m. som meil | bed, couch — f. śayā resting place. guhāśayaḥ who lies in a hiding place.
śayana |act. śī ₁| n. bed, layer |sleep, rest. śayanīkr to make a layer of. śayanāya icchati he wants to lie down to sleep.
śayanagrha [grha] n. bedroom. śayanaracana [racana] n. the arrangement of the bed, one of the 64 arts |kalā|.

śayanaikādaśī [ekādaśī] f. soc. festival of the beginning of Viṣṇu's sleep, on the 11th day [ekādaśī] of the bright fortnight of the month āṣāḍha (around the beginning of July); it is the occasion of a great festival [yatra] in Pandharpur.
śayanīya [pfp. [2] śī₁] amnf śayanīyā used for sleeping or resting — n. bed, couch. śayanīyam adv. (impers.) one must sleep.
śayāna [ppr. śī₁] amnf śayānā lying down, resting; lying down; sleeping — m. lizard. śayānena bhuktam it eats lying down.
śayita [pp. śī₁] amnf śayitā lying, stretched out, lying down; resting, sleeping; asleep.

śayitavya [pfp. [3] śī₁] amnf śayitavyā who must sleep or rest — n. (impers.) one must rest. rātrāvapi nikāmam śayitavyam nāsti I cannot sleep to my heart's content, even during the night. mayā hutavahe śayitavyam I must pour it into the fire.
śayú [śī₁u] m. bio. ["which is elongated"] boa.
śayyā [act. śī₁] f. bed, couch | rest, sleep bed. (poetic) the right word. śayyotthāyam bhunkte As soon as he gets out of bed he eats.

śará [act. śr̩] m. bio. bot. Saccharum sara, reed (from which arrows are made) | arrow | math. symb. the number 5 (for the 5 puṣpabāṇa) | math. complement to 1 of the cosine | [sara] skin of milk, cream; cf. saras | gr. o ; lat. calamus; all. halm; ang. halm; fr. chalumeau.
śaraja | ja | amnf śarajā born in the reeds.
śaradhi [dhi] m. quiver.
śarápunkha [punkha] m. fletching of an arrow bio. bot. Tephrosia purpurea, wild indigo, bushy legume with purple flowers.
śarábandha [bandha] m. lit. geometric poem [citrakāvya] in the shape of an arrow.

śarábhaiga [bhaiga] m. myth. [Rām.] np. from the er mite Sarabhanga "Arrow Breaker"; he welcomed Rāma in the Daṇḍakā forest after receiving a visit from Indra; he sent Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā to the ascetic Sutīkṣṇa, then immolated himself in the fire to join the heaven of Brahmā in the guise of a shining angel.
śarábhinna [bhinna] amnf śarabhinnā trans pierced by an arrow.
śaráyantraka | yantraka | n. string used to bind the palm leaves of a manuscript. śaralāva [ lāva ] amnf śaralāvī cutter of reeds; brush cutter.
śarávana [vana] n. thicket of reeds.
śaravat [vat] amnf śaravatī filled with arrows. śarávarṣa | varṣa | n. rain of arrows.
śarávarṣin [in| amnf śaravarṣiṇī who throws a rain of arrows.
śarástamba [stamba] m. clump of reeds. śarāgni | agni | m. fire arrow. śarāsana [ āsana ] n. ["that which shoots arrows"] bow.
śarāhata [āhata] amnf śarāhatā struck by an arrow.
śarac iic. śarad . śaraccandra | candra | m. autumn moon.
śaracchikhin [śikhin] m. bio. peacock (in autumn, having stopped calling).

śaraṇá |agt. śri| amnf śaraṇā that protects, that defends — act. n. shelter, sanctuary, refuge | asylum, protection | bd. The three refuges of Buddhism are the Buddha, his Law | dharma |, and the community [sangha]; cf. triratna. śaranam gam var. śaranam yā to seek refuge with (acc. g.). śaraṇīkṛ (r.) to seek refuge with acc. . kimanyaccharaṇam I cannot help.
śaraṇagamana | gamana | n. bd. first vow of a disciple bd. to "take refuge in the Buddha". buddham śaranam gacchāmi bd. I take refuge in the Buddha (first vow of a disciple bd.).
śaraṇáda [da] amnf śaraṇadā who grants his protection.
śaranadeva [deva] m. hist. np. of Saranadeva, poet bd. of the court of King Laksmanasena of Bengal, of the end of the 12th century; we owe him the Durghatavrtti (1172).
śaranalaya [laya] m. place of asylum; refuge, shelter.
śaraṇāgata [āgata] amnf śaraṇāgatā who comes seeking refuge or protection; who asks for asylum, refugee; fugitive.
śaraṇāgati |āgati| f. request for asylum or protection | phil. act of placing oneself under the protection of a deity.
śaraṇāgatigadya [gadya] n. lit. np. from the śaraṇāgatigadya, a devotional poem by Rāmānuja.
śaraṇārthin | arthin | amnf śaraṇārthinī who seeks refuge; who asks for protection.
śaranya [śaranaya] amnf śaranyā who offers asylum, who grants protection (to (g. iic.)); protector | who seeks asylum with (iic.) — n. refuge.
śaranyatā |tā| f. act of giving protection.
śarat iic. śarad. śaratkāla [ kāla₁ ₁] m. autumn season. śaratkālam var. śaratkāle adv. in autumn.
śarád f. autumn season (month of āśvina and kārttika) | year | pl. śaradas of the years (poetic). śaracchatam adv. for 100 years. śatam jīva śaradah May you live to 100 years.

śaradvat [vat] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the sage Saradvān "(born in) autumn", son of Kṛpa Gau tama, born with arrows [sara] in his hand; he was drawn to weapons, which he obtained through his penances as a brahmacārin; Indra tried in vain to dissuade him from them by seducing the nymph Jānapadī; his seed fell into a clump of
reed [śarastamba], where two twins, a boy and a girl, were born; King Sāmtanu took them in and adopted them under the names Kṛpa and Kṛpī.

śarabhá m. bio. Ram Markhor with spiral horns | myth. śarabha, a fabulous animal created by Brahmā; this 8-legged griffin [astapad], with large horns, is stronger than the lion and the elephant, and runs at prodigious speed; it lives in the forest, in Kashmir, under the snow; it notably adorns the columns of temples in South India, where it is called yālī; the theme of the śarabha dominating the elephant represents the victory of Hinduism over Buddhism; syn. vyāla; Shiva had to transform into śarabha to end the wrath of Narasimha. astapādah śarabhah siṃhaghātī The śarabha has 8 legs and kills the lion.
śarabheśvara [īśvara] m. myth. [SP.] np. of śarabheśvara, form of ŚivaVīrabhadra who puts an end to the incarnation of Narasimha.
śarabhopaniṣad [upaniṣad] f. lit. np. of the śarabhopaniṣad, also called Paippalādopaniṣad.
śaravya |śaru| amnf śaravyā capable of wounding — f. śaravyā arrow shot; deluge of arrows — n. target; goal.
śaravyatā [tā] f. the act of becoming a target; exposure to danger.
sáras [related to saras] n. cream, skin of milk | thin layer of ashes.
sárogṛhīta |gṛhīta| amnf sarogṛhītā covered with a skin (milk); covered with a crust or a film.

śarāru amnf dangerous, toxic, vicious — m. ferocious animal. śarārucakracārabhīṣaṇāyāṃ mahāṭavyām ekakasya me prasuptasya |DKC.| I sleep alone in the deep forest where terrifying hordes of ferocious beasts roam.
śarāva mn plate, bowl, dish; earthenware dish or pot | tray; dish lid | grain measure equal to two prastha (approximately 3 l).
śarāśari [red. śara] adv. arrow for arrow (in com bat).

śarīra [śṛīra] human body, person; life | phil. [Vedānta] the perishable physical body, one of the 3 bodies formed by the 5 sheaths |kośa| of the soul; cf. kāraṇa, sūkṣma, sthūla — f. śarīrā ifc. body of (iic.). śarīrībhū to take on a body, to incarnate. śarīram ādyaṃ khalu dharmasādhanam One fulfills one's duty, in truth, by taking care of one's body.
śarīraka |ka| n. small body | phil. "this vile body".
śarīrakastūpa [stūpa] m. bd. reliquary of bodily remains of Buddha.
śarīrasattā [sattā] f. phil. bodily existence.
śarīrasthāna [sthāna] n. lit. np. from the Sarīrasthāna "Book of the Body", section of the Carakasamhitā.

śarīrin [śarīrain] amnf śarīriṇī corpo rel — ifc. having a body (iic.) — m. creature; man. jānakī karuņasya mūrtirathavā śarīriņī virahavya theva Sītā is the pain incarnate, the pain of separation itself.
śáru [śṛu] f. dart, lance, arrow | myth. mis sile divin, weapon of Indra and the genies of the winds [marutas] — f. myth. this personified weapon.
sare [loc. sara] iic.
śareja [ja] amnf śarejā cf. Saraja.

śarkarā f. pl. śarkarās gravel, sand; calculus, plug | sugar (candi or granulated) | lat. saccha rum; ang. sugar; fr. sucre; pali sakharā. śarkarāmaricopetam mixed with sugar and pepper. śarkariká [ika] amnf śarkarikī granular.
śarngadhara m. hist. n.p. by śarngadhara, author of the work Sarigadharasamhita (14th century).
śarngadharasamhita [samhita] m. lit. np. from the medical compendium Sarngadharasamhita, a very popular manual of Ayurveda to this day.
śardhat [ppr. śṛdh] amnf śardhantī insolent.
śarma ifc. śarman.
śárman [śriman] n. [en comp. śarma] shelter, refuge, protection; security — m. ifc. soc. joy of, happiness of | soc. title Sarmā forming np. of brahmins.
śarmin [śarmanin] amnf śarmiṇī heu reux, Fortuné, heureux.
śarmiṣṭhā [super. śarmin] f. myth. np. of Śarmisthā "the Most Fortunate", daughter of Vṛṣaparvā, wife of Yayāti and mother of Puru, Druhyu, and Anu.
śárya [śara] m. arrow; missile — f. śaryā cane; rod, arrow; finger.
sáryaṇa [na] m. pl. reed thicket | ved. np. of a region of Kuruksetra.
śáryaṇāvat [vat] m. ved. n.p. of Śaryaṇāvān, high altitude region of Kuruksetra where the soma is found.
śaryāta m. ved. n.p. of śaryāta; cf. Śaryāti.

Śaryāti m. myth. np. of King Śaryāti, son of ManuVaivasvata; he lived at the court of Yama; he founded the Sāryātās dynasty; he was the father of the beautiful Sukanyā, whom he had to marry to the old blind ascetic Cyavana, whom she had disturbed in his penances; it was for Śaryāti that Cyavana performed the yajña during which the Aśvinau drank the soma, in disobedience to Indra; he had as sons Uttānabarhis and Anarta.
Sarva [saru] m. myth. np. of Sarva, epith. of RudraŚiva “(who kills) with his arrow” | ved. one of the 11 rudrās.

śarvavarman [varman] m. hist. np. of the grammar Śarvavarmā; he lived in the 2nd century in South India, under the Sātavāhanās; he is the author of the Kātantra | lit. [KSS.] Guṇāḍhya having declared to King Sātavāhana that he could teach him grammar in 6 years rather than the required 12, Sarvavarmāl made a bet that he could teach it to him in 6 months; he won his bet through the favor of Kārttikeya satisfied with his penances.

śarvara [śarvara] amnf śarvarī spotted; starry — f. śárvarī night (starry) | twilight | myth. np. of śarvarī, wife of Doṣa, mother of Śiśumāra | pl. śarvarās myth. epith. of the horses (or an tilopes) of the winds [marutas] "with a starry coat".
Śarvilaka m. lit. np. from the Brahmin Śarvilaka, cynical thief in the play Mṛcchakaṭikā; he revolts against the injustice of the king, and helps Aryaka₁ to overthrow him.
√ śal v. [1] pr. (śalati) pp. (śalita) pf. (ut) saut (avec uc).

śalá m. point, spike, spear | porcupine quill myth. [Mah.] np. of Sala "He who pierces", one of the 100 sons of Dhrtarāstra | myth. np. of King Sala₁ "Skewered", eldest son of King Parīkṣit; he refused to return the horses he had borrowed from the hermit Vāmadeva₁; during their quarrel, giants attacked him and pierced him with a trident. śalala [ la ] m. bio. porcupine — n. porcupine quill — f. śalalī id.
śalabha m. bio. zoo. moth | bio. grasshopper, locust — v. [11] pr. r. (śalabhāyate) al ler to certain death (like a moth throwing itself into the fire).

śalākā |śalaāka| f. stick, rod, twig; piece of wood; ruler; bar; pawn | parasol rib; cage bar | porcupine quill; thorn; shoot | cylindrical die of quadrangular cross-section, of ivory or bone | arrow; needle, pointed instrument; scalpel; brush; not. eyeliner applicator — m. śalāka id. (rare). śalākāpari [pari] ind. unfavorable roll of the dice | missed roll of a die.
śalākāparīkṣā [parīkṣā] f. traditional method of examination: the student must comment on a page chosen at random by a needle in a work [grantha] of the subject of the examination.

śalākāpurusa [purusa] m. jn. eminent person; tradition counts 63: 24 emancipatory saints [tīrthaṅkara], 27 epic heroes (divided into 9 groups of triplets consisting of a saint [baladeva], hero [vāsudeva] and an antihero of a [prativāsudeva]), and 12 emperors [cakravartin].

śalātura [śalaātura] n. geo. np. of the village of śalātura, presumed place of origin of Pāṇini, at the confluence of the Kabul River and the Indus, near modern-day Peshāwar. মলালু śalālu n. perfumed substance. śalāluka [ ka ] amnf śalālukī One who sells śalālu . श ল্ক śálka [śalaka] mn end, piece, splinter, portion — n. fish scale | bark.

śalya [śalaya] mn arrowhead or spearhead | thorn, splinter, prickle — m. porcupine | myth. [Mah.] np. of Salya "Spearman", king of the madras, brother of Madrī; he embodies the asura Saṃhrāda; his emblem is the furrow [sītā]; he assembled a great army, promised Duryodhana to be his commander-in-chief, and at the request of Yudhişthira agreed to serve as Karna's charioteer in his fight against Arjuna; after Karna's death he commanded the army of the Kauravās; he killed Uttara with a javelin, was attacked by his brother Sveta, and was saved by Bhīṣma; after a long inconclusive battle with clubs against Bhīma, he was killed by Yudhiṣṭhira armed with the celestial missile Kālarātrī; cf. Artāyani — f. śalyā ifc. id.
śalyaka |ka| m. bio. zoo. Hystrix indica, porcupine. śalyatantra [Tantra] n. manual of surgery.
śalyaparvan [parvan] n. bed. n.p. of Śalyaparva, 9th book of the Mah., "of Salya".
śallā var. śallakī [related to śalya] f. organic. bot. Bos wellia serrata, tree whose resin is used to make censer.
śallaka |ka| mr. organic. porcupine — f. śallikā f. śallakī cf. śallā .
śava |agt. śū| mn corpse.
śavārūdha [ārūdha] amnf śavārūdhā myth. refers to a deity whose mount is a corpse.

śavāsana [āsana] n. phil. [yoga] relaxation posture, lying on the floor, palms of hands upwards, back adhering to the floor | soc. [Tantra] coupling posture "like a corpse", where the female partner is the only active partner.
śavarga [(śa)varga] m. phone. the class of si-balates.
śávas [abstr. śū] n. strength, vigor; prowess, valor, heroism. śavasā adv. powerfully, with vigor.
śavasāná [śavas] amnf śavasānā ved. strong, powerful, vigorous; violent — m. road.
śavya [śavaya] n. soc. cremation; funeral.
√ সংস্ śaś v. [1] pr. (śaśati) pp. (śaśita) to leap, to jump; to dance.

śaśa [agt. śaś] m. hare, rabbit | hare-shaped spot on the moon | type of man; cf. pañcamanusyavibhāga — f. śaśī rabbit. śaśīsarpanyāya maxim of the rabbit and the snake: the rabbit whose young are attacked finds the strength to kill the snake.
śaśaka |ka| m. (small) hare, rabbit | hare-type man.

śaśadhara [dhara] m. epith. of the moon "that carries the hare" | hist. np. of Saśadhara (1275– 1325), philosopher of knowledge; he investigated the notion of concomitance [vyāpti]; his work Nyāyasiddhāntadīpa influenced Gangeśa.
śaśadharamauli [mauli] m. myth. epith. of Śiva "wearing the moon as a diadem".
Śaśabindu [bindu] m. moon ["which has a hare-shaped spot"] | myth. np. of King Śaśabindu, son of Citraratha, father of Bindumatī₁.
śaśaviṣāṇa [viṣāṇa] n. ["hare's horn"] thing in existence; cf. gaganāravinda.
śaśaśriga [śriga] n. ["hare's horn"] non-existent object; cf. aprasiddha.

śaśānka [anka] m. the moon ["which bears the image of a hare"] | hist. np. of King Saśānka of Gauda (late 6th century); secret ally of King Devagupta of Mālava, he treacherously assassinated King Rājya Vardhana₁ in 606.
śaśānkavat [vat] amnf śaśānkavatī sem blable to the moon — f. śaśānkavatī lit. [KSS.] np. of Śāśānkavatī, princess of Ujjayinī; Mṛgānkadatta married her after many trials.
Śaśāda [ada] m. myth. np. of Śaśāda, epith. of Vikukṣi "Hare eater (destined for sacrifice)".
śaśi iic. śaśin.
śaśikalā [kalā] f. moon phase; the moon | bed. n.p. of Princess Saśikalā of whom Bilhana sang of her love in the Caurapañcāśikā.

śaśikhanda [khanda] m. bed. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara Sasikhanda or Sasikhandapada, king of Kanakapurī, father of Candraprabhā, Candra rekhā, śaśiprabhā, Śaśirekhā; he granted their hand to Śaktideva, and named him his successor Śaktivega.

śaśiprabhā [prabhā₂] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī śaśiprabhā, sister of Candraprabhā, cursed to become human in the form of Princess Bindurekhā; she married Šaktideva like her three sisters [lit. [KSS.] np. of Princess Sasiprabhā₁, daughter of King Yasaḥketu of Sivapura; Manaḥsvāmī fell in love with her | lit. [KSS.] np. of Sasiprabhā₂, wife of King Mahāsena₁, mother of Sundarasena.
śaśimauli [mauli] m. myth. epith. of Śiva “wearing the moon as a diadem”.

Śaśirekhā [rekhā] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī Saśirekhā, sister of Candraprabhā, cursed to become human in the form of the fisherman’s daughter Bindumatī₁ of Vardhamāna; she married Saktideva first, before her three sisters.

śaśivadanā [vadanā] f. lit. poetic meter samavṛtta of 21 syllables "at the rhythm of the hare", with caesura [yati₃] after the 11th syllable. śaśivarna m. myth. epithet of Ganesha "who has a complexion of the moon".
śaśin [śaśain] m. moon [“that which carries a hare”].
śáśvat adv. always; perpetually; continuously, constantly | right away, on the spot — amnf śaśvatī perpetual, continuous, without end; incessant; recurrent, frequent; numerous.

śaṣkuli f. ear opening | sweet rice cake cooked in oil | var. śaṣkulī id. dīrghaśaskulībhaksananyāyah maxime dde l'inges tion de la longue śaṣkulī; it illustrates the effect of such multanéity of various sensations (texture, appearance, taste, smell), which are in fact perceived separately.
śáṣpa n. tender grass | pubic hair.
√ śas v. [1] pr. (śasati) pp. (śasta) pfp. (śasya) pf. (vi) to cut, to slaughter, to kill.
śas forms adv. of manner (like fr. ment) | iterates the numeral iic. (fois).
śasana |act. śas| n. slaughter, killing.
śastá₁ [pp. śaṃs] amnf śastā said, recited praised, celebrated, approved; beautiful.
śasta₂ [pp. śas] amnf śastā cut, slaughtered; killed.
śasta₃ |pp. śās | amnf śastā punished.
śastrá₁ |śaṃstra| n. Vedic invocation, hymn to be recited; opp. stotra. মাধ্য śástra₂ |śastra| n. sword, knife; dagger; ra soir; weapon in gen. — f. cf. śastrī || Latin castrāre; French castré.
śastrakarma [karma] n. surgery. śastraśāstra [ śāstra ] n. bed. n.p. of Sastraśāstra or science of weapons, an upaveda.
śastrāśastri [red. śastra₂] adv. “dagger against dagger” in single combat.
śastrin [śastra₂in] amnf śastriṇī who carries a weapon; armed with a sword.
śastrī [f. śastra₂] f. dagger, knife.
śastrīśyāma [śyāma] amnf śastrīśyāmā blue
steel ["blue like a knife blade"].
śasya [pfp. [1] śas] amnf śasyā to cut; to harvest; to kill — n. grain, wheat; grain harvest, reaping; cf. sasya.
√ his v. [3] pr. (sisati) pr. r. (sisat) pp. (sita, śāta) v. [4] pr. (śyáti) pf. (nor, sat) ved. sharpen || lat. catus; eng. hone.
śāka₁ n. vegetable, plant — m. |śākavṛkṣa| bio. bot. Tectona grandis, teak tree | [śākadvīpa] myth. one of the 7 continents | dvīpa|.
śāka₃ [*śaka₁] amnf śākā relating to the Sakās — mn cf. śākakāla — m. pl. people of the Sākās.
śākadvīpa [dvīpa] m. myth. np. of the Sākadvīpa "Continent of teak", surrounded by an ocean of milk.
śākadvīpīya [īya] amnf śākadvīpīyā myth. belonging to the Sākadvīpa | soc. qualifies a class of brahmins of Scythian [Saka] origin.
śākapārthiva [pārthiva] m. vegetarian | king dear to the śākās.
śākaprati | prati | adv. a little bit of vegetables.
śākabhakṣa [bhakṣa] amnf śākabhakṣā vegetarian. śākika | ika | amnf śākikī who gathers vegetables.
Saka₂ | act. sak | m. power, strength; help, aid, friend.
śākakāla [kāla₁] m. era of the Śakās, beginning in year 78
śākaṭa |*śakaṭa| amnf śākaṭī relating to the chariot, to the cart | that which goes in a chariot; that which pulls a chariot; that which fills a chariot — m. draft animal; cartload.

śākaṭāyana [*śakaṭaāyana] m. hist. patr. of the ancient grammarian Sākaṭāyana, mentioned by Pāṇini; the uṇādisūtrāṇi are attributed to him; he professed that every noun derives from a root [vyutpattipakṣa] | hist. patr. of the Jain grammarian Sākatāyana₁ or Abhinavaśākatāyana; he lived at the court of the Rāṣṭrakūṭa kings at the end of the 9th century; he wrote the grammar Sabdānuśāsana and its gloss.
śākaṭika [*śakaṭaika] m. carter.

śākam [acc. śāka₁] iic. Śākambharī var. Śākambharī [bhara] f. myth. np. of Sākambharī "the Vegetable Gardener", epith. of Durgā who grew vegetables from her own body to save the world from a 100-year drought; [Mah.] her sanctuary is located near the ford Triśulakhāta geo. np. of Śākambharī₁ "Rich in Cultures", capital of the Cāhuvāṇa princes; cf. Hammīra.

śākala [*śakala] amnf śākalā dyed with śakala | concerning a portion, a shard, etc. | inhabitant of śākala | which follows śākalya — mn mor ceau, portion; fragment, shard, sherd; scale — n. lit. text of śākalya — m. geo. np. of the city of Sākala, city of the Madra country (mod. Sialkot in the Pañjāb of Pakistan), capital of King Milinda; its tutelary goddess was Sāvitrī | pl. śākalās the inhabitants of śākala.
śākalasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. np. of the Śākalasamhitā, compilation of the Ŗgveda due to śākalya.

śākalya [*śakalaya] m. hist. patr. of the Scholar [Vidagdha] śākalya, ancient grammarian who lived in northern Bihāra around 800 BC; first compiler of the Rigveda, he fixed the text segmented into words [Padapāṭha]; his recension includes the Ai tareya brāhmaṇa; the other recension [śākhā] is due to Bāṣkala.
śākārī [*śaka₁] f. dialect of the Sakās | speaking prākṛta of the vulgar type.
śākin [agt. śak] amnf śākinī powerful — f. śākinī myth. [Tantra] female demon assistant to Durgā; cf. hākinī.
śākuntala [*śakuntalā] n. lit. np. of the śākuntala, drama by Kālidāsa, also called Abhijñānaśakuntalā.

śākta [*śakta] amnf śāktā relating to power or energy | phil. relating to divine power, to the Goddess [Sakti] — m. soc.
