[Tantra] follower of the Goddess, adept of Tantrism, who follows the teachings of the canonical texts [Tantra]; a distinction is made between those who follow the orthodox or proper ritual [dakṣiṇācāra] and those who follow the impure ritual or
left | vāmācāra|.
śāktaśarīra [śarīra] mn phil. [Trika] the power body, which envelops the causal body |paraśarīra|.
śākya [*śaka₁ya] amnf śākyā which concerns the people of the Sakās | soc. n.p. of fa

thousand [jāti] identifying the Indo-Scythian [Saka] origin; this clan was assimilated to the [varna] kṣatriya class; tradition says of a śākya prince that he descends from Ikṣvāku | bd. not. np. of family of the Buddha || pali sākiya.
śākyabhikṣu | bhikṣu | m. bd. Buddhist monk.
śākyabhikṣuka [ka] m. bd. Buddhist monk — f. śākyabhikṣukī bd. Buddhist nun |soc. (in lit.) matchmaker.
Śākyamuni [muni] m. bd. n.p. of Śākyamuni, epith. of the Buddha “Sage of the Sakās”.
Śākyarakṣita [rakṣita] m. hist. np. of Sākyarakṣita, author of the Vrttamālāvivrti; he lived between 1050 and 1150.
śākyasiṃha [siṃha] m. bd. n.p. from Śākyasiṃha, epith. of the Buddha "Lion among the Sakās".
śākra [*śakra] amnf śākrī relating to śakra Indra — n. astr. the nakṣatra Jyeṣṭhā, presided over by Indra — f. śākrī np. of Sākrī, epith. of Indrāṇī.
śākravarmaṇa [varmaṇa] m. hist. np. of Śākravarmana, ancient grammarian mentioned by Pāṇini.
śākhā f. branch, twig, division; species; extremity, finger | soc. ved. ritual school, sect; edition of a sectarian text.
śākhāgrapakva [agrapakva] famn śākhāgrapakvā ripened at the end of the branch.
śākhānagara [nagara] n. suburb.
śākhāmṛga [mṛga] m. organic. monkey ["branch animal".
śākhin [in] amnf śākhinī which has branches divided into schools (Veda) | which adheres to a Vedic school — m. tree ["which has branches"] | soc. member of a Vedic school.
śāṃkara var. śāṅkara [*śaṃkara] amnf śāṃkarā relating to ŚaṅkaraŚiva | relating to Sankarācārya.
śāṃkaradarśana [darśana] n. phil. philo-sophical system of Sankarācārya.
Śānkarabhāṣya [bhāṣya] n. bed. from np. Śāṅkarabhāṣya, commentary by Saṅkara₁ on the Brahmasūtra.
śāṅkha [*śaṅkha] amnf śāṅkhā relating to the conch; made of shell, of mother-of-pearl — n. sound of the war conch.

śāṅkhāyana [*śaṅkhaāyana] m. hist. patr. of Śānkhāyana "son of śankha", composer of the ritual formulary [brāhmaṇa] Kauṣītaki — amnf śāṅkhāyanī relating to Śāṅkhāyana — n. lit. his work, not. the Sānkhāyanabrāhmana. śānkhāyanagṛhyasūtra [ gṛhyasūtra ] n. lit. np. of a collection of instructions for domestic ritual attributed to Sāṅkhāyana.
śāṅkhāyanabrāhmaṇa [brāhmaṇa] n. bed. n.p. from Śāṅkhāyanabrāhmaṇa, epith. of the Kauṣītaki brāhmaṇa “owed to Sānkhāyana”.
śāṅkhāyanāraṇyaka [āraṇyaka] n. bed. n.p. of Sānkhāyanāranyaka.
śāṭa m. piece of cloth, dress, skirt; sari — f. śāṭī id. — f. śāti id.
śātaka [ka] mnf śātikā id.
śāṭhya |*śaṭhaya| n. deception; falsehood, fraud, dishonesty.
śāḍvala [śādvala] amnf śāḍvalā worm covered with grass — mn (sg. or pl.) meadow — m. bull. sharpen.
śānottejana | uttejana | n. act of sharpening on a grinding wheel; (fig.) criticism.
śāṇa₂ [*śaṇa] amnf śāṇā made of hemp.
śāṇḍilya m. soc. clan name [gotra] | hist. np. of Śāṇḍilya, patronymic of an author of aphorisms
devotional [bhaktisūtra], of unknown date.
śāṇḍilyabhaktisūtra [bhaktisūtra] n. bed. n.p. from the bhaktisūtra of Sāndilya.
sāta₁ [pp. sā] amnf sātā sharp, cutting | thin, lean, emaciated; weak.
śātātapa [ātapa] m. hist. np. of the jurist Sātātapa₁, composer of smrti , of uncertain date | myth. [YV.] np. of the sage Sātātapa₁, who in the paradise of Indra told Vasistha the story of Bhusunda.
śātātapasmṛti [smṛti] f. bed. n.p. of the śātātapasmṛti, collection of laws due to śātātapa.
śātodara [udara] amnf śātodarā thin, with a thin waist.
śātodaratva |vat| n. slimness, slenderness.
sata₂ [act. sad] m. fall, loss (nails, hair).

śātakarṇin [*śatakarṇain] m. hist. np. of Sātakarņī, patriarch of a line of the Sātavāhanās; notable of an emperor of the Sātavāhanās, who performed two horse sacrifices [aśvamedha] and conquered large territories in the 2nd century BC; his capital was Amarāvatī₁ | hist. np. of Gautamīputra Sātakarnī, who reconquered the empire in 78 under the name of Śālivāhana.
śātana₁ [act. śā] n. act of sharpening | acuity, fineness; thinness.
satana₂ |act. sad| n. act of making fall; cutting, polishing; tearing, destruction.
śātrava [*śatrua] amnf śātravī concerning an enemy; hostile — m. enemy — n. hostility | enemy multitude.
sāda m. ved. grass — f. sādā brick. śaraśādam of reed and grass.
śādvala var. śāḍvala [related to śāda] amnf śādvalā green, covered with grass — mn (sg. or pl.) meadow — m. bull.
śādvalin |in| amnf śādvalinī covered with grass.
c nota. gram. primary affix [krt₂] mar as in the middle or passive present participle.

śāntá [pp. śam₁] amnf śāntā calm, se rein; appeased, tranquil | kind, favorable; propitious | harmless; dead — m. lit. the peaceful one, one of the 9 artistic modes |rasa|; it is associated with the color jasmine and the deity Nārāyaṇa; it was added by Mammața to the eight modes of Bharata₃ — f. cf. śāntā — v. |11| pr. (śāntayati) to appease. śāntam interj. peace! calm down! be quiet! | God forbid (said to ward off a bad omen). śāntam pāpam vade retro, satanas. yac cakṣuṣā dṛṣ́yate tan mithyā | yacchāntena ma nasā jñāyate tat satyam || What is seen by the eyes is erroneous, what is understood by a serene mind is the truth.

śāntarakṣita | rakṣita | m. hist. np. of the paṇḍita bd. Sāntarakṣita, born in Rivālasara in Himachal Pradesh (~725–788); he was abbot of Nālandā, where he synthesized the Yogācāra and the Madhyamaka with the epistemological tools of Dharmakīrti in his phil. Madhyamakālamkāra work; he introduced the bd. to Tibet around 767 at the invitation of King Trisong Detsen, and created the first monastery at Samye, where he spent the rest of his life, and where he brought Pad masambhava; he is also credited with the philosophical compendium Tattvasamgraha; his student Kamalaśīla made an analytical commentary on it, the Pañjikā; cf. daśakuśala, pratītyasamutpāda.
śāntarasa [rasa] m. phil. feeling of peace; [Abhinavagupta] the peaceful as a liberating aesthetic experience.
śāntavilāsa [vilāsa] n. lit. np. from the Sāntavilāsa, 4th section of the Bhāminīvilāsa, of a devotional nature; it comprises 36 verses in 12 meters.
śāntātman [ātman] n. phil. [KU.] the true self at peace.

śāṃtanu var. śāntanu [*śam₃tanū] amnf healthy, wholesome for the body — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the mythical king Sāmtanu or Sāntanu "Well-healthy", 21st king of the lunar lineage [somavamśa], descendant of Bharata through Kuru and son of Pratīpa; he usurped the throne of his elder brother Devāpi when the latter became a hermit; by the goddess Gangā he fathered Devavrata, the future Bhīsma, patriarch of the Mahābhārata; he fell in love with the beautiful Sa tyavatī, whose adoptive father demanded that he promise her royal offspring, and who fathered Citrāngada and Vicitravīrya with him.
śāntā [f. śānta] f. myth. [Rām.] np. of Sāntā "peaceful", daughter of King Romapāda; she married the ascetic Rśyaśrnga.

śānti [act. śam₁] f. peace, calm, rest; peace of heart | prosperity, blessing, happiness | satisfaction of a desire [ākānkṣā] | soc. propitiatory rite prior to a sacrifice; rite of appeasement of a possessing demon; power [siddhi] of elimination of dangers | destruction, end, death; eternal rest | phil. [śaivasiddhānta] peaceful aspect of the bindu, associated with SadāśivaTatpuruṣa | myth. np. of Sānti "peace", daughter of Dakṣa, wife of Dharma — m. myth. np. of the angiras Sānti₁ "peaceful", son of Angirā | myth. np. of many other characters.

śāntideva [deva] m. hist. np. of the philosopher and poet Sāntideva (~685–763), bd. of the mādhyamika obedience; according to tradition, having received the apparition of Mañjuśrī, he renounced his princely destiny, fled from his palace and received ordination at Nālandā; he is credited with the Bodhicaryāvatāra and the Śiksāsamuccaya; he is particularly revered in Tibet.
śāntinātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of Sāntinātha "Master of Peace", 16th mythical tīrthankara; his body is golden yellow, his symbol is a deer or a tortoise.
śāntiparvan [parvan] n. lit. np. from the Śāntiparva, 12th book of the Mah., "of peace".
śāntipāṭha [pāṭha] m. lit. Vedic hymn “of the peaceful way”.
śāntivacana [vacana] n. lit. invocation of appeasement, placed at the beginning of a work.
śāntyatīta [atīta] n. phil. [śaivasiddhānta] transcendent principle [tattva], supreme aspect of the bindu as associated with SadāśivaIśāna.
śāntyadhyāya [adhyāya] m. lit. np. from the Sānty adhyāya "book of propitiations", 6th chapter of the Šivadharmaśāstra.
śāntyudaka | udaka | n. soc. consecrated water, used in the śānti rite.
śāntyudakavidhi [vidhi] m. soc. [Atharvaveda] prescriptions concerning the water of the śānti rite.
śāṃtva var. śāntva [śām₁tva] n. consolation, comfort | pl. śāntvāni soothing words, kind words.
śāp [ca. śap] v. [10] pr. (śāpayati) pp. (śāpita) to make swear by (i.).

sāpa [act. sāp] m. curse, imprecation, anathema. śāpam dā to utter a curse against (loc. g. dat. pratiacc.). śāpam vac id. kuberaśāpena adv. by the curse of Kubera. |mokṣa| śāpamokṣa m. deliverance from a curse.
śāpita [pp. śāp] amnf śāpitā that one made swear.
śābara [*Śabara₁] amnf śābarā wicked | related to Sabara₁ — m. offense, insult — f. śābarī tribal language.
śābarabhāsya [bhāṣya] n. bed. n.p. of the Śābarabhāsya, commentary on the Mīmāṃsāsūtra due to Sabara₁; cf. Mīmāṃsāsūtrabhāṣya.
śābaleya [*śabalaīya] amnf śābaleyā variegated — f. śābaleyā “variegated”, n.p. cow.

śābdá [*śábda] amnf śābdī sonorous | concerning sound | oral, verbal; based on the authority of the Veda — m. grammarian | gram. the signifier (opp. ārtha the signified) — f. śābdī myth. np. of Sābdhī "Significant", epith. of Sarasvatī.
śābdanirṇaya [nirṇaya] m. lit. np. from the Sābdanirņaya "Inquiry into Verbal Knowledge", work of Prakāśātmā; Anandabodha commented on it.

śābdabodha [bodha] m. gram. understanding the meaning of an utterance; logical analysis of a sentence | gram. communicative semantics; there are 3 methods of language analysis, following the vyākaraņa, nyāya and mīmāmsā schools.
śābdabodhīya [īya] amnf śābdabodhīyā phil. (meaning) obtained by understanding a sentence.

śābdika [*śabdaika] amnf śābdikā sonorous; noisy | relating to sounds or words; verbal — m. ["word expert"] grammarian, lexicographer. upa govardhanam śābdikāḥ Govardhana is better than the grammarians.
śābdikābharaṇa [ābharaṇa] n. gram. np. from the śābdikābharaṇa, grammar and lexicon of roots [dhātuvṛtti] due to Dharmakīrti.
sam₁ [ca. sam₁] v. [10] pr. (sam₁ ayati) ps. (śāmyate) to calm, appease; to reconcile (not. by a conjuration rite) | to render immobile; to kill.
sam₁ [ca. sat₁] v. [10] pr. (sat₁) observe.
śāma [agt. śam₁] amnf śāmā that soothes; that heals.

śāmana [agt. śam₁] amnf śāmanā that extinguishes, that destroys — act. n. tranquility, peace | sedative | destruction, death; massacre | end — m. myth. epith. of Yama — f. śāmanī the direction of the South, of which he is the guardian. śāmanam yā to go to one's ruin.
śāmitra [*śamitra] amnf śāmitrā relating to the sacrificer — m. soc. sacrificial fire — n. its location | slaughterhouse; place of execution.
śāmba cf. sāmba.
śāmbhava [*śambhua] amnf śāmbhavī myth. relating to or deriving from Siva; sacred to Siva.
śāmbhavopāya [upāya] m. phil. [Abhinavagupta] path of salvation according to Shiva, by which one attains the state of jīvanmukti.
śāmya [*śamaya] amnf śāmyā relating to peace; peaceful — n. peace; reconciliation.
say [ca. si₁] v. [10] pr. (sayayati) to make sleep, to send to sleep.
saya | agt. si₁ | m. who sleeps, who rests.
śāyaka [agt. śī₁] amnf śāyikā who sleeps, who rests — f. śāyikā sleeping posture | resting tower.
śāyin [agt. śī₁] amnf śāyinī lying down, stretched out; resting.
śāra m. piece, pawn (in dice games).
śāraṅga m. cf. saraṅga.
śāradá [*śarada] amnf śāradī autumnal; ripe | shy, modest — m. year; cloud — n. grain, fruit (autumn produce) — f. cf. Śāradā.
Śāradacandrikā [candrikā] f. bed. n.p. from the Sāradacandrikā "Autumnal Moonlight", a piece in nāṭaka style by Bāṇa₂, of which only isolated verses remain.

Śāradā [f. śārada] f. type of lute [vīṇā] | hist. script used in Kaśmīra from the 8th century, evolved from the brāhmī script; the gurmukhī script is derived from it | myth. np. of Sāradā, incarnation of Sa rasvatī, personifying knowledge and joy; she is depicted carrying the vīṇā; she is celebrated at the Navarātra festival; she is venerated notably in Śṛṅgerī; in her sanctuary Śāradāsthāna in Kaśmīra she had a miraculous idol which was destroyed by Zainulābidīn for having refused her darśana geo. np. from an important ancient university in Kaśmīra, located in the valley of the Nīlum river.

śāradātanaya [tanaya] m. hist. n.p. of śāradātanaya "Son of Śāradā", originating from North India (between the 12th and 14th centuries); he is the author of Bhāvaprakāśa. śāradātilaka [ tilaka ] m. bed. n.p. from the śāradātilaka tantra, a late Kaula text by Laksmanadesika (15th century).
śāradābhujaṃga [bhujaṃga] n. bed. n.p. from Śāradābhujaṃga, a devotional poem of 8 stanzas by Samkara₁.
śāradāmāhātmya [māhātmya] n. lit. np. from the śāradāmāhātmya, text of praise of the Sāradāsthāna shrine, chapter of the Bhṛṅgīśasaṃhitā.
śāradāmbā [ambā] f. myth. the Goddess Sāradā Sarasvatī.
Śāradāsthāna [sthāna] n. geo. n.p. of the Śāradāsthāna sanctuary of Kaśmīra.
śāradīya [*śaradīya] amnf śāradīyā autumnal.
śāradīyākhyanāmamālā [ākhyā₂nāmamālā] f. bed. n.p. from the Sāradīyākhyanāmamālā dictionary of synonyms by Harşakīrti Sūri.
śāradvata [*śaradvata] m. myth. n.p. of śāradvata, disciple of Kaṇva.

śāravatī [*śaravat] f. geo. np. of the Sāravatī river, which flows from East to West in Karņāṭa for 128 km; it originates in the Western Ghats at Ambutīrtha; it is said that Rāma shot an arrow to make it spring forth, in order to quench the thirst of Sītā.
śāri f. organic. zoo. Gracula religiosa, myna — m. pawn in chess or checkers; dice. śārikā var. sārikā [ka] f. organic. zoo. Gracula reli giosa, myna. pṛcchantī vā madhuravacanām śārikām
pañjarasthām [MD.] Perhaps by questioning the caged myna bird, with the sweet voice.

śāriputra [putra] m. hist. np. of Sāriputra "son of Sāri", one of the chief disciples of the Bud dha, with Mahāmaudgalyāyana; he established the foundations of Abhidharma; he was the first disciple authorized to enthrone other monks; he bore the title of Dharmasenāpati; he is frequently mentioned in the Jātakamālā; he is the hero of the Sāriputraprakaraņa.
śāriputrakaraṇa [prakaraṇa] n. lit. np. from Sāriputrakaraņa "gesture of Sāriputra", play by Aśvaghosa.
śāribā f. organic. bot. Hemidesmus Indicus, Indian separilla, gentian creeper; the root of this sarmentose shrub is used medicinally; cf. anantamūla.
śārīrá [*śarīra] amnf śārīrā corporeal — n. med. physiology, anatomy. śārīrah dandah corporal punishment.

śārīraka [*śarīraka] amnf śārīrakā cor porel — n. phil. the embodied spirit | doctrine about its nature. śārīrakamīmāṃsā [ mīmāṃsā ] f. bed. n.p. from the Śārīrakamīmāmsā “Investigation into the spirit in carné”, phil. study. of the Brahmasūtra.
śārīrakamīmāmsābhāsya [bhāsya] n. lit. np. of the Śārīrakamīmāmsābhāṣya of Saṅkara; cf. Brah masūtrabhāṣya₁ | lit. epith. of the Bhāskarabhāṣya, another gloss of the Brahmasūtra due to Bhāskara₁.

śārkará [*śarkarā] amnf śārkarā like gravel. খার্ক্ন śārṅga [*śṛṅga] amnf śārṅgā made of horn; horn-shaped; pointed — mf śārngī bio. zoo. Merops apiaster, bee-eater; it feeds mainly on hymenoptera; in flight it resembles a bow with its arrow — n. myth. np. of the Sāriga bow of Vișnu; cf. Srnga.

śārngaka [ka] mf śārngikā bio. bird Merops, bee-eater | pl. śārṅgakās myth. [Mah.] the four little bee-eaters Jaritāri, Sārisrkta, Stambamitra and Drona₁, sons of the ascetic Mandapāla and the śārngikā Jaritā; still unable to fly when the Khāndava forest was on fire, they were spared by Agni, satisfied with their recitation of the Veda; he granted them a wish, and they asked that all cats be burned.
śārngadhanus [dhanus] m. myth. epith. of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa "armed with the Sārṅga bow".
śārngadhara [dhara] m. hist. np. of the poet Śārṅgadhara; he compiled the anthology Sārngadharapaddhati in 1363 | hist. np. of the physician Sārngadharācārya (1314th century); cf. Sārngadharasamhitā.

śārngadharapaddhati [paddhati] f. lit. np. from the Śārngadharapaddhati, an anthology of sayings [subhāṣita] due to Śārṅgadhara (1363); it also contains practical recipes, such as the preparation of fertilizer with carrion manure [kunapa].
śārngadharasamhitā [saṃhitā] f. med. np. of the Sārngadharasamhitā, a compendium of knowledge from the 14th-century Ayurvedic pharmacopoeia.
śārṅgarava [rava] m. myth. np. of a disciple of Kanva "who chirps like a wasp-eater".
śārngin [in] m. myth. epith. of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa "armed with the Śārṅga bow".

śārdūla m. bio. zoo. tiger — ifc. the best among the (iic.) — f. śārdūlī bio. tigress | myth. np. of Sārdūlī, daughter of Kaśyapa and Krodhavaśā; she gave birth to the race of tigers. muniśārdūlah m. best among the wise. śārdūlakarņa [karņa] m. bd. np. of Sārdūlakarņa "tiger ear", son of the candāla chief Triśanku₁, whom the latter wanted to marry to the daughter of the brahmin Puşkarasārī. śārdūlakarṇāvadāna | avadāna₂ | n. bd. np. from Sārdūlakarņāvadāna "Tale of Sārdūlakarņa", comic strip text refuting the natural existence of classes and castes.

śārdūlavikrīdita [vikrīdita] n. lit. poetic meter samavrtta of 19 syllables "at the rhythm of the tiger's game", with caesura [yati₃] after the 12th syllable; its rhythm evokes the march of the tiger; it is used not. for wishes to newlyweds.
śāryāta [*śaryātia] amnf śāryātī myth. descendant of Saryāti — m. myth. king of his dynasty; cf. Haihaya, Talajangha | pl. myth. the people of the Sāryātās.
śārva [*Śarva] amnf śārvā relating to Śiva/Śarva. śārvā dik direction of the East.
śārvarin [*śarvarain] m. astr. n.p. of Śārvarī "Twilight", personifying year 34 of a |samvatsara| life cycle.
Śārvarī [*śarvarī] amnf nocturnal | pernicious; gloomy — f. night — n. darkness.

śālá [related to śri] amnf śālā who stays at home — m. bio. bot. Shorea robusta or Sāl, a large tree used in carpentry; its resin |rāla| is used as lacquer, for incense, and for medicine; from its kernel is extracted illipe butter used in cosmetics; its leaves are used to make disposable plates; the śāla is sacred to Viṣṇu; bd. it was against this tree that the mother of Buddha leaned to give birth to him, and it was under this tree that he passed into parinirvāṇa — f. cf. śālā. śālam adv. at home; at one's own place.

Śālagrāma [grāma] m. geo. np. of Śālagrāma, sacred village of the devotees of Vișnu [vaișnava], located on the Gaṇḍakī river | soc. (often from Sālagrāma) fossil ammonite shell, used as a devotional image of the chakra of Vișnu; magical virtues are attributed to it; cf. tulasī. śālaparņī [parṇī] f. bio. bot. Pseudarthria vis cida, shrub of the Papilionaceae family, trifoliate, with pink flowers; it is one of the 5 minor medicinal roots [hrasvapañcamūla].
śālabhañjikā [bhañjikā] f. bed. woman or nymph

sylvestre [yakṣī] of such beauty that she makes a tree bloom when she touches it with her foot; in sculpture she is represented swaying in front of a śāla tree, touching a flowering branch with her hand | bd. representation in painting or sculpture of Queen Māyā₁ | (art) more gen. statue | courtesan.

śālaṅkāyana m. myth. patr. of the ṛṣi Śālaṅkāyana or Sālaṅkāyana, son of Viśvāmitra soc. name of gotra | pl. hist. np. of the dynas tie brāhmana of the Sālankāyanās; they reigned in Andhra over the region of Vengī from 300 to 440; they were vassals of the Pallavās.
śālā [f. śāla] f. hut, house; apartment; workshop; stable | room, hall; study room — n. śāla ifc. house of (iic.) || fr. hall.
śālāvṛka [vṛka] m. jackal ["stable wolf"].
śālākya [*śalākāya] m. med. surgeon; not. oculist — n. med. eye and ear surgery, a section of Ayurveda.
śālāluka [*śalāluka] amnf śālālukī qu sells śalālu .
Śāli m. rice | pl. śālayas grains of rice | myth. n.p. of the yakṣa Sāli.
śālika [ka] amnf śālikā derived from rice; rice-based.
śālikanātha [nātha] m. hist. np. of Sālikanātha, 7th century mīmāṃsaka philosopher of prābhākara obedience, author of the Prakaraņapañcikā and the Vākyārthamātṛkā.

śālikapiṣṭa [piṣṭa] n. rice flour. śālicūrņa [cūrṇa] n. rice flour. śālivāhana [ vāhana ] m. hist. śālivāhana “who has Śāli as a mount”, title of the Indoscythian [Saka] king Gautamīputra Sātakarņī (78–102); he was kṣatrapa of Ujjayinī; he founded the Saka era; he is credited as the first prākṛtī poet, and is attributed the Prākṛtacandrikā | myth. [VC.] np. of the mythical king Sālivāhana₁; he reigned in Pratisthāna; He is associated with King Vikramāditya in the stories of the Vikrama carita as his enemy or rival | pl. śālivāhanās hist. np. of the Andhra people and dynasty of the Sālivāhanās; cf. Sātavāhanās.

śālihotra [hotra] m. lit. "who receives the rice in frande", name of horse in poetry | hist. np. of Sālihotra, ancient author of an eponymous veterinary treatise; he lived in Śrāvastī — n. lit. his work; cf. Sālihotrasamhitā.
śālihotrasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. np. of the Sālihotrasaṃhitā, veterinary work of Sālihotra; it deals not. with horses and elephants.

śālin [*śālāin] amnf śālinī who owns a house, owner | sedentary (opp. yāyāvara) — ifc. who possesses; full of, endowed with, furnished in abundance with (iic.) — f. śālinī phon. meter of 4 times 11 syllables, variety of tristubh.
śālīnā [ śālāīna ] f. [“who deserves to enter the bridal chamber” | new wife.
śālu [*śalu] m. frog — n. cade nutmeg | med. throat tumor. शালুক śālūka [*śalūka] mf śālūkā frog — n. nutmeg | med. throat tumor.

śālmala m. bio. bot. Bombax heptaphyl lum or Salmalia malabarica, cotton tree or kapok tree, with red flowers; it is said that the thorns of its trunk are used to torture the damned in iron | myth. one of the 7 continents [dvīpa] — f. śālmalī id. | myth. np. of the śālmalī, one of the rivers of the iron | var. śālmali id.

śālva m. pl. name of the people of the Sālvās (west of the Aravalli) | myth. [Mah.] np. of śālva, king of Saubha, who unsuccessfully opposed Bhīsma's abduction of the daughters of the king of Kāśi whom he was to marry; Bhīṣma returned to him the eldest, Ambā, who had promised herself to him, but he repudiated her; [BhP.] Sālva, friend of Siśupāla, swore an oath at the latter's death to eliminate the Yādavās; through his penances he obtained from Shiva the construction by Maya of an indestructible citadel of magical iron; He attacked Dvārakā, defended by Pradyumna, but only Kṛṣṇa was able to kill him with his chakra.
śālveya [śālvaīya] amnf śālveyā pl. geo. np. of the Śālveyās, people of the Śālvās | their king.
sava₁ m. small animal. śāvaka | ka | mr. id.
śāva₁ [*śava] amnf śāvā cadaveric; re latif to the corpse.

śāśvatá [*śaśvata] amnf śāśvatī eternal, perpetual; continuous, incessant, uninterrupted; all imminent — n. continuity; eternity — f. śāśvatī the Earth || pali sassata. śāśvatam eternally, perpetually. śāśvatīḥ samāḥ adv. forever ["for an uninterrupted succession of years"]. mā Niṣāda pratiṣṭhāṃ tvaṃ agamaḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ [Rām.] Niṣāda, may you never have rest.
śāśvatadṛṣṭi [dṛṣṭi] f. phil. doctrine of eternalism; cf. śāśvatavāda.
śāśvatavāda [vāda] m. phil. doctrine of eternalism, postulating not. that an individual has an invariable and eternal self; it was denied by Buddha, as well as its opposite materialism |ucchedavāda|.
śāśvatika [śāśvataika] amnf śāśvatikī eternal, permanent; constant. śāśvatikatā | tā | f. eternity.
śāsa₁ |act. śās| m. order, command — agt. m. śāsá commander, governor; punisher | myth. np. of the ṛṣi śāsa Bhāradvāja, author of Vedic hymns.
śāsa₂ [instr. śas] m. butcher's knife.
śāsáhasta [hasta] amnf śāsahastā who holds a butcher's knife in hand.
śāsaka |agt. śās| m. master, tutor.

śāsana [agt. śās] amnf śāsanī who punishes; who commands; who teaches, tutor — n. pu nition, punishment; order, royal edict, decree | written contract; title deed; authoritative writing, sacred book | teaching, instruction; doctrine, religion lit. not. teaching of Shiva to the Goddess in his
revelations [śaivāgama] — ifc. power over (iic.). śāsanāt karaṇaṃ śreyaḥ example is better than precept.
śāsanadevatā [devatā] f. jn. protective yakṣī deity associated with a Jain saint [arhat]; cf. Ca kreśvarī.
śāsita [pp. śās] amnf śāsitā directed, governed; instructed | controlled, restricted | reprimanded, punished.
śāsitavya [pfp. [3] śās] amnf śāsitavyā to teach, to prescribe | which must be directed or instructed.
śāsitṛ [agt. śās] amnf śāsitrī who punishes; who directs; who instructs | governor, commander, instructor, teacher.
śāsti [act. śās] f. correction, punishment; rule; command, order; command | scepter.

śāstṛ [agt. śās] amnf śāstrī [sg. nom. śāstā, acc. śāstāram who punishes, chastises, commands; who instructs | master, teacher, governor | myth. np. of śāstā "Justiciar", epith. of HariharaputraAyyanār bearing the sword and the whip; Puṣkalā and Pūrṇā₁ are his wives.

śāstrá [śāstra] n. order, law; precept, rule, imperative teaching, instruction; commandment | rule, theory (opp. prayoga, practice); doctrine, science; knowledge [["instrument of instruction" | prescriptive treatise, teaching work, book of precepts; sacred text | ang. chas tise. anantamśāstram alpamjīvitam Knowledge is endless, but life is short.

śāstrakavi | kavi | m. lit. didactic poet, exegete of instructional texts. bhavati prathayannartham līnam samabhiplutam sphuṭīkurvan | alpamanalpaṃ racayannanal pamālyam ca śāstrakaviḥ | [KM.] It is by unfolding the hidden meaning, by revealing what is submerged, by lengthening what is brief, that the didactic poet weaves his long garland.
śāstrakāvya [kāvya] n. bed. ["instructive poetry"] cf. Rāvaṇavadha, Hitopadeśa.
śāstracarca [carca] m. discussion on sacred texts.
śāstracarcasadas | sadas | n. debate, discussion on sacred texts.
śāstracūḍāmaṇi |cūḍāmaṇi| m. SOC. title of scholar in learned texts.
śāstradīpikā [dīpikā] f. bed. n.p. of the Sāstradīpikā, work of Mīmāṃsā of Pārthasārathi₁ Miśra (13th century); he teaches the systems of Kumārila Bhaṭṭa and Prabhākara Miśra.
śāstradṛṣṭa |dṛṣṭa| amnf śāstradṛṣṭā recognized by scholarly texts.
śāstrapaddhati [paddhati] f. phil. canonical interpretation of sacred texts.
śāstraprameyapariccheda [prameyapariccheda] m. bed. n.p. of Rāmānujācārya's śāstraprameyapariccheda, part of his Tantrarahasya.
śāstraratnākara [ratnākara] m. SOC. title Sāstraratnākara of scholar in sacred texts.
śāstrávid | vid₃ | amnf who knows the sacred texts.
śāstravihita [vihita] amnf śāstravihitā prescribed by the sacred texts.
śāstrasiddha [siddha₁] amnf śāstrasiddhā conforeme aux textes sacrés.
śāstrārtha [artha] m. scholastic, erudition; traditional scholarly debate gram. interpretative dialectic of the Pāṇini system.
śāstri iic. śāstrin.
śāstripariṣad [pariṣad₂] f. SOC. scientific community.
śāstrin [śāstrain] amnf śāstriņī versed in scriptures; learned, scholar; scholar — m. SOC. np. of Śāstrī "Master", title of a scholar.
śāstrīya [śāstraīya] amnf śāstrīyā conforms to the teachings, prescribed by the texts; legal, correct. śāstrīyatva [tva] n. the state of being prescribed by the texts.
śāstrīyalinga [linga] n. gram. grammatical gender.
śāsya [pfp. [1] śās] amnf śāsyā punishable; that which must be punished | that which must be governed or directed.
śāha m. geo. np. of the śāha, region of Kaśmīra.
śāhin [in] m. hist. np. of the Sāhī dynasty, originating from Tibet, last Hindu dynasty of the Northwest (3rd to 10th century), ruling over the Kabul valley and Gandhāra; cf. Anandapala.

śimśápā f. bio. bot. Dalbergia sissoo, large Sissou tree, with pale yellow flowers; it is used in medicine; its wood, dense and pink veined, is used in quality joinery; lit. the corpse/vampire of the Vetālapañcavimsatikā resided on a Sissou; Ha numān observed Sitā imprisoned in Lankā from the top of a Sissou.
śiṃśumāra m. organic. zoo. Platanista gange tica, Ganges dolphin.
śikyá n. rope suspended at its two ends to carry a load; sling; rope court.

śikṣ [des. śak] v. pr. r. (śikṣate) v. pr. (śikṣati) fut. (śayiṣyati) pft. (śiśikṣa) pp. (śikṣita) pf. (anu, upa) to study, learn (from (abl.)) | to train in (loc.) | to want to help, to show friendship towards (dat.); to enter the service of (acc.) — ps. (śiksyate) to be learned or practiced — ca. (śikṣayati) to instruct, to teach something to someone (2 acc.). guruh śisyam śiksayet śaucam the guru must teach purity to his student.
śikṣaka [agt. śikṣ] amnf śikṣikā who instructs — m. instructor; teacher.
śikṣaṇa [act. śikṣ] n. study; acquisition of knowledge | instruction, teaching (in loc. iic.)).
śikṣaṇīya [pfp. [2] śikṣ] amnf śikṣaṇīyā which must be taught.

śikṣā [act. des. śak] f. desire to accomplish | learning, study; knowledge, art; science in (loc. iic.) phil. recitation or phonetics, one of the 6 supplementary treatises of the Veda [vedānga]; cf. Apiśaliśiksā | gram. cf. pāṇinīyaśikṣā — m. śikṣa myth. np. of Sikṣa "scholar", a gandharva king.
śikṣāguru [guru] m. master who teaches (opp. dīkṣāguru, who initiates). śikṣāprakāśa [ prakāśa ] m. lit. np. from the phonetics manual Sikṣāprakāśa.
śikṣāvat |vat| amnf śikṣāvatī instructive; instructive scholar.
śikṣāvallī [vallī] f. lit. 1st chapter of the TU.

śikṣāvrata [vrata] n. jn. disciplinary vow, spiritual exercise of a Jain renunciant; there are four of them: the practice of meditation |sāmāyika|, the avoidance of certain places [deśāvakāśika], the experience of an ascetic day's life |poṣadhopavāsa| and sharing with a guest |atithisamvibhāga|. śikṣāṣṭaka [ aṣṭaka ] n. lit. np. of the śikṣāṣṭaka, an 8-line poem of four stanzas attributed to Caitanya, summarizing his teachings.

śikṣāsamuccaya [samuccaya] m. lit. np. from the Sikṣāsamuccaya "Didactic Compendium", a philosophical work by Sāntideva: in it he discusses the path of progress of the accomplished [bodhisattvamārga].
śikṣita [pp. śikṣ] amnf śikṣitā learned, studied | who has learned (acc.); instructed, trained in (acc. loc. iic.) — n. teaching, instruction.
śikhaṇḍa [śikhā] m. tuft of hair; lock of hair on the top of the head | crest; plume, aigrette | peacock's tail.
śikhaṇḍaka [ka] m. id. | lock of hair; group of 3 or 5 locks reserved in the hairstyle of warriors.

śikhandin [in] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Sikhandī "Wearing the Lock of Hair", hero of the Pañcālās, in whom Ambā was reincarnated as a transsexual [klība]; he faced Bhīṣma in combat; the latter refusing to fight a woman, he served as a shield for Arjuna who dealt the fatal blow to his ancestor; thus he avenged the humiliation of Ambā; he was attacked in his sleep and killed by Aśvatthāmā — f. śikhaṇḍinī myth. np. of Sikhandinī, daughter of King Drupada who became the transsexual Śikhaṇḍī by exchanging her sex with the yakşa Sthūnakarna; epith. insulting term used by Ulūka to refer to Sikhandī.

śikhara [śikhāra] amnf śikharā pointed, jagged — mn summit, peak; point; summit, pinnacle; crest | arch. main tower above the sanctuary of a temple | ritual gesture [mudrā] of the crest (index and middle fingers in a V, ring finger folded over the thumb) | ruby.

śikharin [in] amnf śikhariṇī pointed; rounded neck; endowed with a crest — m. mountain — f. śikharinī lit. name of a complex 17-syllable kāvya meter with a caesura [yati₃] after the 6th syllable and often the 11th; it is used by Bhavabhūti in the Uttararāmacarita; the Saundaryalaharī consists of 100 verses of this meter.

śikhā f. point | plume, tuft, crest; tuft of hair | soc. lock reserved during the shearing of a brāhmaṇa; it is worn notably by the disciples of Caitanya; syn. cūḍā | phil. [Tantra] the śikhā represents the intermediate space between the brahmarandhra and the dvādaśānta | nipple; tip of the foot | flame of a lamp; ray of light soc. ["growing like a lock of hair"] interest [vṛddhā] payable daily at a usurious rate.
síkhāmaṇi [maṇi] m. jewel worn on the head — ifc. splendor of iic. (title not. of works).

śikhāmuṇḍa [muṇḍa] amnf śikhāmuṇḍā who has a shaved head, except for a lock of hair. śikhāmūla [ mūla ] n. ["root with a tuft"] ca rotte, turnip. śikhāvat [vat] amnf śikhāvatī pointed; burning, blazing — m. fire, lamp | astr. comet — adv. crest-like.

śikhin [śikhāin] amnf śikhinī who has a tuft or a crest | burning — m. bio. zoo. peacock | fire. yatnād api kaḥ paśyec chikhinām āhāraniḥsaraṇamārgam | yadi jaladadhvanimuditās ta eva mūḍhā na nṛtyeyuḥ | [PT.] No matter how hard you try, you'll never see a peacock's rear end, unless that idiot is displaying his tail, excited by the rumble of thunder.
śigrú m. bio. bot. Moringa oleifera, Moringa tree; its leaves, rich in protein, are used in medicine | āyurveda| — n. its seeds.
śiṅghāṇa mn nasal mucus | rust. śinghāṇaka [ ka ] mn id.
√ সিল্ল্ j v. [2] pr. r. ( kte) pft. ( ije) pp. (śiñjita) to jingle, ring; to vibrate, buzz; to make a chain noise — ca. (śiñjayati) to resound.
śiñjat [related to śiñj] amnf śiñjatī emitting chimes; resonating.
śiñjadvalaya [valaya] amnf śiñjadvalayā who clinks his bracelets. śiñjadvalayasubhagaih lit. [MD.] to the sound of the chariot ringing its bracelets.
śiñjadṣaḍaṅghri [ṣaḍaṅghri] amnf lit. [BhP.] full of buzzing bees. ā [act. j] f. tinkling, vibration; not. rustling of silver anklets.
śiñjāvat [vat] amnf śiñjāvatī which rings.
śiñjin [agt. śiñj] amnf śiñjinī which rings, which vibrates — f. śiñjinī bowstring.
śitá [pp. śā] amnf śitā sharp, cutting, thin, lean, emaciated; weak.
śiti amnf white | blueblack — m. organic. birch; syn. bhūrja . śitiratna | ratna | n. sapphire. śitivāsas | vasas | amnf dressed in dark — mr. myth. epith. of Balarāma.

śithilá [śrathira] amnf śithilā loose, slack, loosened, untied, unbound, free | flabby, soft — n. untied knot; slackness, negligence — v. [11] pr. (sithilayati) pp. (sithilita) to make loose, slack, loosen; to undo (one's clothes) — v. [11] pr. r. (sithilayate) to neglect — v. [11] pr. r. (śithilāyate) to become slack; to soften, weaken. śithilīkṛ to loosen, loosen; to relax, unwind. śithilībhū to become relaxed, untied; to be at ease | to abandon, to withdraw from (abl.). śithilátā [tā] f. laxity; negligence, laxity; indifference. śithilatām gam var. śithilatām vraj to be neglected. śithilátva [tva] n. id. śithiladvitva [dvitva] n. lit. poetic license.
śithilita [pp. śithila] amnf śithilitā relaxed, defeated, cowardly, flabby.
śithilī iiv. śithila .
śithilīkaraṇa [karaṇa] n. phil. [yoga] relaxation.
Śini m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the prince vṛṣṇi Sini, father of Satyaka, grandfather of Sātyaki.

Śibi m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the royal sage [rājarṣi] Śibi or Śivi, descendant of Uśīnara and Mādhavī, king of the Uśīnarās; he is the symbol of selfless altruism and superhuman devotion; to save Agni transformed into a dove from the blows of Indra transformed into a falcon, he offered equal weights of his own body; one day a brahmin came to his palace to beg for food; at his request, Sibi killed his only son Brhadgarbha to prepare the meal for him; although the brahmin set fire to his palace, he put on a brave face and served him; when the brahmin asked that he share this meal, even though he was a vegetarian, he agreed; Brahmā, who had come to test him, then revealed himself, and gave him back his son and his palace | pl. śibayas myth. his descendants; cf. śaibya | myth. np. of the asura Sibi₁, son of Samhrāda. śibicarita [carita] n. lit. story of Śibi, episode from book 3 of the Mah. | var. śibicaritra id.
śibikā f. palanquin; litter | platform.
śibira n. royal residence; royal camp; royal tent | tent; fortified camp | mod. ["study camp" | workshop, seminar. sambhāṣaṇaśibira mod. study camp of spoken Sanskrit.
śimba mf śimbā pod, pod.
śimbi [śimba] f. pod, pod | śimbī id. | bio. bot. Phaseolus Trilobus, legume used for fodder and in medicine to cure hepatitis.

śíras n. head; skull | upper part, summit, pinnacle; vanguard; beginning (of a verse) lit. np. of the verse Sirā "āpo jyotir āpo 'mṛtam" [Baudhāyana] — ifc. head of, first of (iic.) gr. ; lat. cerebrum; fr. brain, cerebral. uṣā vā aśvasya medhyasya śiraḥ |BU.| The head of the sacrificial horse, in truth, is Dawn. śirodā | "to give one's head" | to renounce life. śirodhr var. śirovah | "to hold one's head high" | to be proud. śiropasthā | "to hold one's head high" | to acknowledge one's guilt. śirasā grah var. śirasādhā, śirasādhṛ, śirasāvidhṛ, śirasābhṛ, śirasāvah, śirasākṛ: to place on the head, to receive with deference. śirasā gam var. śirasāpragrah, śirasādhṛ, śirasāyā, śirasāpraṇam, śirasānipat, śirasāpraṇipat: to touch with the head | to prostrate oneself before. śirasi kṛ var. śirasinidhā : to place on the head. śirasi sthā | "to stand on the head of" | to be far superior to (g.). śiro'rtiḥ: headache.
śiraḥpīdā [pīdā] f. med. headache.

śiracchada [chada] m. bonnet. śiraska [ka] ifc. amnf śiraskā who has the head (iic.). avanataśiraskah who has bowed the head. śiromani [mani] m. headdress or turban jewel; diadem | lit. title of a work, literary or scientific summa; principal work on a subject | soc. np. of Siromani, scholar's title [pandita]; cf. Rag hunātha₁.
śiroruha [ruha] m. ["that grows on the head"] che veux | corne.
śirorekhā [rekhā] f. top line of the devanāgarī script. śirorti | arti | f. med. headache.
śirovrata [vrata] n. soc. [MO.] vow of renunciation, marked by the shaving of the head.

śirīṣa [śṛīṣa] m. bio. bot. Acacia sirissa or bot. Albizia lebbeck, a tree with black wood and fragrant white flowers; it attracts parrots — n. its flower; women make earrings from it; the softness of its petals evokes tenderness in poetry. śirīṣavaṇa | vana | n. acacia wood.

śila m. gleaning (of ears of corn). Śilāhāra [āhāra] amnf śilāhārā gleaner; one who feeds by gleaning — m. hist. np. of the Śilāhāra dynasty of the north of the West Deccan; it claimed descent from the vidyādhara Jīmūtavāhana; in the 13th century, it established itself in the Konkana as a maritime power regulating trade in the West with the Arabs, to the detriment of their neighbors [samanta] Rāṣṭrakūṭa; cf. Aparārka. śilāhārin [āhārin] amnf śilāhārinī gleaner.
śiloñcha [uñcha] m. du. śiloñchau gleaning of ears and grains | subsistence by means of fortune.
śilottha [uttha] amnf śilottthā which grows on stones; product of rock — n. bitumen.
śilā f. stone, rock | lower stone of a millstone; syn. drsad. śilībhū to become stone; to harden.
śilākuṭṭa |kuṭṭa| m. grinding in a mortar. śilākṣara [ kṣara ] n. lithography. śilācārika [ cārika ] m. epigraph.
śilānyāsa [nyāsa] m. arch. laying the first stone of a building.
śilāpatta | patta | m. flat stone, slab; millstone.
śilāyantra [yantra] n. mod. lithographic stone.
śilāvatī [vat] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the virtuous Silāvatī, servant of the merchant Harşagupta of Tāmraliptī, elder sister of Rājadattā. śiloccaya [uccaya] m. ["pile of rocks"] mountain.
śilodbhava [udbhava] amnf śilodbhavā produced by stones — n. bitumen; benzine | or.
śilī f. kind of vermin | female frog | dart; arrow.
śilīmukha [mukha] m. lit. ["frog-headed"] is said of a sword, an arrow, a bee, a hare.
śilīndhra n. mushroom. সিলুষ Śilūṣa m. organic. bot. Ægle marmelos; syn. bilva myth. n.p. of rṣi Śilūṣa, ancient master of the art of dance.
śilpa n. decoration; work of art | plastic art; craft, trade; talent, skill; tradition lists 64; cf. kalā | soc. oblation spoon.
Śilpaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. np. from the Śilpaprakāśa, treatise on architecture, not. for the construction of temples.
śilparatna [ratna] n. bed. n.p. of Śilparatna, work of śilpaśāstra of Srīkumāra (16th century).
śilpaśāstra [śāstra] n. lit. np. from the upaveda silpaśāstra "Science of the arts", discipline defining the rules of artistic representation; cf. Abhilaşitārthacintāmaņi.
śilpin [in] amnf śilpinī craftsman, artist, or wrier; not. sculptor. śilpirāja | rāja | m. king among the artists.

śivá amnf śivā benevolent; favorable, propitious, salutary, auspicious — m. myth. euphemistic epithet of the Vedic god Rudra; later elevated to the supreme god Śiva, transcendent form of the divine; his first wife, Satī daughter of Dakṣa, immolated herself by fire out of humiliation at not being invited to the solemn sacrifice that he made to Vishnu; Shiva, mad with grief, carried her corpse throughout the universe, scattering her limbs into as many parts as there are

shrines [pīṭhasthāna]; later he married his reincarnation, the mountain girl [Pārvatī], who embodies his Inaccessible [Durgā] power [Sakti]; their sons are Gaņeśa and Skanda; Shiva is the patron of ascetics, he wears his hair braided into a topknot [Jaṭādhara] and meditates on the summit of Mount Kailāsa; he is adorned with serpents [nāgabhūṣaṇa]; omniscient, he possesses the third eye [trinetra] in the middle of his forehead, from which emanates the Fire that destroys desire (Kāma); his mount is the bull Nandī, his symbol the linga; he carries the bow Ajagava, and is the archer Pinākin who destroyed the City of the Three Demons Tripura; he killed the

elephant demon [gajāsura]; in his terrible Bhairava form he roams the crematorium fields with his scepter of bone and skull [khatvānga]; he manifested as a pillar of Fire [Aruṇācaleśvara] to show his supremacy to Brahmā and Vișnu; cf. Ardana, Ardhanārīśvara, Iśa, Iśāna, Umāpati, Kapardī, Kālāri, Kṛttivāsā, Kedāra, Gangādhara, Candramukuta, Candraśekhara, Tripuraghna, Dhanvin, Dhūrjati, Natarāja, Nirañjana, Paśupati, Puramathana, Batu, Bhagālin, Bharga, Bhava, Bhikṣāṭana, Manthāna, Mahākāla, Mṛtyumjaya, Lakulīśa, Vīrabhadra, Vyomakeśa, Sankara, Sabara, Sambhu, Sarva, Hara | soc. the worship of Shiva elevates the destructive power of Rudra to the supreme transcendent divine principle [Maheśvara]; his temples bear his sign [linga] in the sanctuary of the Lord [Iśvara], guarded by Nanda and Sunanda; the tree of Bael [bilva] is sacred to him, its trilobed leaves |tryambaka| are given to him as an offering, but the ketakī is odious to him | arch. [Mayamata] the 16 aspects of Siva are: Sukhāsana, Vivāha, Umāskanda, Vṛṣārūḍha, Purāri, Nṛtta, Candraśekhara, Ard hanārī, Viṣṇvardha, Caṇḍeśānugraha, Kāmāri, Kālanāśa, Dakṣiṇāmūrti, Bhikṣāṭana, Mukhalinga, and Lingasambhūta — n. well-being, prosperity, happiness. śivāya var. śivena happily; by chance. śivāya gamyatām have a good trip! śivās te panthānah santu have a good trip!
śivakara [kara₁] amnf śivakarī which causes happiness, prosperity; beneficial, auspicious.
Śivakāmasundarī [kāmasundarī] f. myth. np. of sivakāmasundarī "Beautiful of Shiva's desire", epith. of Pārvatī companion of Națeśvara; her main sanctuary is at Cidambaram.
śivakeśava [keśava] m. of. Śiva and keśava.
śivagiri [giri] m. geo. n.p. from the hermitage [matha] of Sivagiri "Mount Siva", hill near Varkala on the Kerala coast; mod. śrī Nārāyaṇa Guru (1855–1928) preached the abolition of castes there.
śivagītā [gītā] f. myth. [PP.] sermon preached by Śiva to Rāma. śivajñāna [ jñāna ] n. phil. gnosis revealed by Shiva in an āgama .
śivajñānabodha [bodha] m. lit. np. of the śivajñānabodha, synthetic work of the śaivasiddhānta movement of South India.
śivatattva [tattva] n. bed. n.p. of śivatattva, or vrage of śaivasiddhānta . śivatama [tama] amnf śivatamā great. the most favorable. śivatara |tara| amnf śivatarā compar. more favorable than (abl.).
śivatāṇḍava [tāṇḍava] mn myth. cosmic dance of Shiva.

Śivatāṇḍavatantra [tantra] n. lit. np. of the Sivatāṇḍavatantra, ancient tantra (1st century?); this dialogue between Siva and Pārvatī describes magical practices with diagrams [yantra] and magic squares; it notably contains the perfect magic square (1,8, 13,12); (14,11, 2,7); (4,5, 16,9); (15,10, 3,6).
śivatāṇḍavastotra [stotra] n. lit. np. of the devotional poem sivatāṇḍavastotra, traditionally attributed to Rāvaṇa.
śivátva [vat] n. essence or nature of Śiva.
śivadatta [datta] m. hist. np. of śivadatta Karpūra, author of the dictionary of homonyms Sivakoșa and of his commentary Sivaprakāśa (1677, Vāraņasī).
Śivadṛṣṭi [dṛṣṭi] f. bed. n.p. from the Śivadṛṣṭi "Vision of Siva", basic work of the śaivasiddhānta doctrine of Recognition [pratyabhijñāśāstra], by Somānanda (end of the 9th century).
śivadviṣṭā [dviṣṭa] f. bio. flower of the pandanus tree, bot. Pandanus odoratissimus; it is odious to Šiva; cf. ketakī.
śivadhanus [dhanus] n. myth. bow of Siva; cf. Bhīmasena.

Śivadharma [dharma] n. bed. n.p. from the Śivadharma or Sivadharmaśāstra "Religion of Siva", anonymous Shaivite ritual text from the 5th or 6th century; it is part of the Nandikeśvarasamhitā; cf. Santyadhyaya.
śivapura [pura] n. geo. n.p. of śivapura, epith. of Vārāṇasī “City of Siva” — f. śivapurī id. | geo. n.p. of sivapurī, third of the Omkāreśvara site.
śivapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. bed. n.p. from śivapurāṇa; cf. Vāyavīyapurāņa.
śivapuspaka | puspaka | mr. organic. bot. Calotropis gi gantea; cf. jambhana₁.
śivámahiman [mahiman] m. myth. majesty of Siva. śivamahimnah stavah m. bed. hymns of praise of Siva.
Śivayogadīpikā [yogadīpikā] f. bed. n.p. from the sivayogadīpikā, late śaiva text.
śivarāja [rājan] m. hist. cf. Shivajī.

śivarātri [rātri] f. soc. festival of the night of Šiva, the 14th day [caturdaśī] of the dark fortnight [kṛṣṇapakṣa] of the month of māgha; it is a day of fasting [vrata]; the marriage of Shiva and Parvati and Shiva's cosmic dance [tāndava] are celebrated; in the shrines the linga is wafted with pañcagavya; the faithful spend the night at the temple singing hymns, and the wives pray for the longevity of their husbands. Śivarātrimāhātmya [ māhātmya ] n. lit. np. from Śivarātrimāhātmya, poem by Śrīnātha glorifying śivarātri ; cf. Sukumāra₁.
śivalinga [linga] n. cf. linga | soc. gesture [abhinaya] of the raised thumb symbolizing the śivalinga .
śivavallabha [vallabha] amnf śivavallabhā dear to Śiva — f. śivavallabhā epith. of Gangā “dear to Siva”.
śivaśaraṇa [śaraṇa] amnf śivaśaraṇā "protector of Shiva", qualifies Shaivite proselytes such as Basava.

Śivasūtra [sūtra] n. lit. np. of the Šivasūtra, a Shaivite collection [āgama] consisting of 77 stanzas [sūtra]; it is the basis of the Trika system of Kaśmīra; it is said to have been revealed in a dream to Vasugupta; Bhāskara₁ made its exegesis in the sivasūtravārttika; Kallaṭa composed the Spandakārikās as a commentary under the direction of Vasugupta; Kṣemarāja made the vimarśinī₁ commentary | pl. śivasūtrāni gram. 14 formulas describing the families of phonemes useful to Aṣṭādhyāyī; cf. pratyāhārasūtra. jayatyekapadākrāntasamastabhuvanatrayah dvitīyapadavinyāsavyākulābhinayaḥ śivaḥ | [SS.] Glory to Shiva, who with a single step traversed the entirety of the three worlds, and whose second step, upon landing, transformed their theater. Śivasūtravārttika [ vārttika ] n. lit. np. from the sivasūtravārttika of Bhāskara₁.
śivasūtravimarśinī [vimarśinī] f. bed. n.p. of the Sivasūtravimarśinī, commentary on the Sivasūtra due to Kşemarāja.
Śivasoma [soma] m. hist. n.p. of sivasoma, disciple of Samkara₁, guru of king Indravarma₁. śivastotra [ stotra ] n. bed. n.p. from the devotional hymn Sivastotra, attributed to Rāvaṇa.
śivasmāmin [svāmin] m. hist. np. of Sivasvāmī, bd. poet of Kaśmīra, in the 9th century; he was court poet of King Avantivarmā (855–883); we owe him the mahākāvya Kapphiṇābhyudaya.
śivādityamiśra [ādityamiśra] m. hist. n.p. of the logician Sivādityamiśra (12th century), author of the Sap tapadārthī.
śivādvayaśāsana [advayaśāsana] n. phil. non-dualistic Shaivite doctrine.
Śivānanda [ānanda] m. hist. np. of Šivānanda "Joy of the Lord", name of various persons; not. mod. Svāmī Sivānanda₁ (1887–1963), physician, sage and writer, founder of the "Divine Life Society".
śivānandanātha [nātha] m. hist. of np. śivānandanātha, phil. śaiva of the Krama school of Kaśmīra (8th century).
śivārkamaṇidīpikā [arkamaṇidīpikā] f. bed. n.p. of the Sivārkamanidīpikā “Sparkle of the solar jewel of śiva”, work of Appayya Dīkṣita in honor of the Vedānta śaiva of Srīkantha.

śivajī [śivajī] m. hist. np. of the Maratha king Chattrapati śivajī (1627–1680); he was the son of the mercenary Sahjī, of the Bhonsle family, general of the Sultanate of Ahmednagar, then of the Sultanate of Vijayapura (Bi japur) in Pune; he fought the Mughal emperors and created a powerful Hindu kingdom in the Deccan in the 17th century.
śivi cf. śibi.
śiś cf. śā .
śiśira [śyāira] amnf śiśirā fresh, cold — mn cold, freshness, frost | cold season (month of māgha and phālguna). śiśirīkṛ to cool, refresh. śiśirībhū to cool down.
śiśirapathika [pathika] m. lit. ["winter traveler nal" | category of verse in anthologies; syn. hemantapathika.
śiśiravasanta [vasanta] m. du. śiśiravasantau the cold and the heat; winter and spring.
Śiśireśvara [īśvara] m. myth. np. of Siśireśvara, epith. of Shiva "Master of the cold"; he has a temple at Bhuvaneśvarī₁.

śiśirita [śiśiraita] amnf śiśiritā re froidi | trembling; crenellated (said notably of the outline of a linear yantra forming right-angled recesses). সিয়ু śiśu m. child, young boy; syn. kumāra, bāla | young of an animal — v. [11] pr. r. (śiśūyate) to behave like a child. śiśūyate vṛddhaḥ the old man regresses to childhood.
śiśuká [ka] m. little child.
śiśukranda | kranda | m. moans, cries of young children.
śiśukrandīya |īya| m. (text) relating to the crying of young children. śiśutva [tva] n. childhood.

śiśunāga [nāga] m. hist. np. of śiśunāga, prince of the Licchavi clan, minister [amātya] of Magadha, viceroy of Vārāṇasī (5th century BC); he ended the Haryańka dynasty and became emperor of Magadha; he established his capital at Vaiśālī₁; he conquered Avanti and ended the power of the Pradyota kings.

Śiśupāla [pāla] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Šiśupāla "Protector of Children", prince of the Cedayas, son of Damaghosa and Srutaśravā (and therefore paternal cousin of Kṛṣṇa); when he was born, he had 3 eyes and 4 arms, and he brayed like a donkey; it was predicted that he would lose his 3rd eye and his 2 extra arms at the sight of the man destined to kill him; one day when Kṛṣṇa was visiting the Cedi country, he took the child in his arms and the miracle occurred; his mother then made him promise that if her son offended him, he would forgive him; Kṛṣṇa swore that he would not harm him unless he insulted him a hundred times; He grew up and became a powerful king; Rukmiņī was promised to him, but she was in love with Kṛṣṇa who abducted her on the day scheduled for their wedding; during the solemn sacrifice [rājasūya] of Yudhişthira, Bhīşma proposed to honor Kṛṣṇa as the honored guest receiving the arghya first, but Siśupāla began to insult him; at the hundredth insult Kṛṣṇa decapitated him with his discus [cakra] Sudarśana; Siśupāla, the last avatar of the third rebirth of the cursed dvārapālau, was then able to free himself by merging with Kṛṣṇa "like a meteor striking the Earth".

śiśupālagaḍha [gaḍha] m. geo. of np. Siśupālagadha or Kalinganagarī, ancient and medieval capital of Kalinga, on the site of ancient Toşalī; mod. the ruins of its fortifications are 5 km south of Bhubaneśvar.

śiśupālavadha [vadha] m. lit. np. from the Siśupālavadha "Murder of Siśupāla", a great epic poem [mahākāvya] in 20 chapters [sarga] by Māgha, very mannered; at the request of the gods, Nārada asks Kṛṣṇa to kill his own cousin Sisupāla, reincarnation of Hiranyakasipu and Rāvaņa; during the rājasūya of Yudhisthira, Kṛṣṇa, insulted 100 times, carried it out without denying the oath he had made to his mother; cf. Viśausadhi, Sarvankasā.
śiśumātṛ [mātṛ] f. pl. śiśumātaras myth. [Mah.] the 7 "mothers (dangerous) to children" associated with Skanda; cf. Aryā, mātrgaņa.

śiśumāra [māra] mf śiśumārī bio. zoo. Platanista gangetica, Ganges river dolphin | bio. crocodile ["child killer"] | myth. [VP.] np. of Siśumāra, celestial creature, microcodile half-man; the human half evokes Vishnu and the divinity latent in man, the crocodile devours time, while the universe revolves around the pole star Dhruva which bears its tail | astr. constellation of the Little Bear, bearing Siśumāra.
śiśná mn tail; penis. śiśnam bharah given to lust. śiśnodaraparāyaṇaḥ hedonist, libertine | "who thinks only of his penis and his stomach"].
śiśnadeva |deva| amnf śiśnadevā véd. qua lifie les barbares "worshippers of the penis" | libertine, debauched, depraved.

√ সিষ্ śiṣ v. [7] pr. (śináṣṭi) pp. (śiṣṭa) pf. (ava, ut, pari, vi) leave — ps. (śisyate) remain — ca. (śesayati) make remain; spare. na śisyate it is missing (nom.). সিষ্ট śiṣṭá₁ [pp. śiṣ] amnf śiṣṭā left, remained — n. residue, remainder. সিষ্ট śiṣtá₂ [pp. śās] amnf śiṣṭā chastised, punished ordered, commanded; taught, prescribed; normative educated, instructed; polite, well-mannered; cultured, eminent grammarian (speaker) of high register.

śistaprayoga | prayoga | m. correct practice (not. of grammar | vyākarana | ) | gram. correct usage of language. śiṣṭācāra | ācāra | amnf śiṣṭācārā polite, well-mannered — m. good manners; (formulas of) politeness | phil. virtuous practice of well-mannered people. সিষ্টি śiṣṭi [act. śās] f. correction, punishment | refined language, correct speech, authorized teaching.
śisya [pfp. [1] śās] amnf śisyā who must be educated — m. pupil, apprentice, disciple || Punjabi Sikh.
śisyahitā [hita₂] f. gram. n.p. of the Sisyahitā, gloss
grammatical [vrtti] due to Ugrabhūti Bhaṭṭa (around 1000).
sī₂ [agt. sī₁] ifc. amnf which rests on (iic.) — act. f. repose of, tranquility of (iic.).
√, sik, v. , [1], pr. ,r. , (sikate) , pft. , (sisike), drizzle — ca. (śīkayati) ca. r. (śīkayate) to speak.
śīkara [śīk] m. pl. śīkarās light rain, drizzle
śīkṣā cf. śikṣā .
śīghra amnf śīghrā Rapid; opp. manda — n. astr. conjunction — v. [11] pr. r. (sīghrāyate) to accelerate. śīghram var. śīghreṇa adv. rapidly, quickly, swiftly.
śīghrakavi [kavi| m. poet expert in improvisation; syn. āśukavi .
śīghraga |ga₁| m. myth. |Rām.| np. of the king of Ayodhyā Sīghraga "Fast", son of Agnivarṇa, father of Maru₁.
śīghratara |tara| amnf śīghratarā compar. Faster.
ś īt cf. sīt.
śītkāra | kāra | m. the "pschitt" sound; not. the sound of splashing water | bravo | sounds of amorous pleasure or pain.

śīta [pp. śyā] amnf śītā cold, cool — n. the cold, frost, winter. śītāḥ f. pl. cold water (ellipsis of āpas). śītīkṛ to cool. śītīkaraṇam n. action or means of cooling. śītībhū to cool down. śītībhūta cooled | calmed. śītībhāva the act of cooling down.
śītaka [ka] amnf śītikā lazy; opp. usnaka.
śītápitta [pitta] n. med. skin disease; not. urticaria.
Śītapūtanā [pūtanā] f. myth. np. of Sītapūtanā "Icy Stink", horrible piśācī that steals fetuses.
śītāṃśu [aṃśu] m. epith. of the Moon “with cold rays”; opp. gharmāṃśu.
śītālú [ālu] amnf who cannot stand the cold; sensitive to the cold.
śītoṣṇa |uṣṇa| amnf śītoṣṇā hot and cold — n. hot and cold.
śītala [śītala] amnf śītalā cold, fresh, refreshing | icy; freezing | passionless, calm — m. Moon | camphor — f. cf. śītalā.
śītalanātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of Sītalanātha "Master of the cold", 10th mythical tīrthankara; his body is golden yellow, his symbol is the swastika or a pipal leaf.
śītalamudrādhāraṇa [mudrādhāraṇa] n. soc. wearing the seal of Vișnu cold-printed with the gopīcandana, mādhva religious rite performed daily.
śītalā [f. śītala ] f. smallpox | myth. np. of the goddess Šītalā "Frosty", personifying smallpox; one prays for her protection; her mount is a donkey.

śītalāṣaṣṭhī [ṣaṣṭhī] f. soc. festival of śītalā, on the 6th day of the clear fortnight [śuklapakṣa] of the month of māgha; women pray there to conceive a child | soc. festival of Sambalpur (Orissa), celebrating the marriage of Siva and Pārvatī, on the 6th day of the clear fortnight of jyaistha.
śītalāsaptamī [saptamī] f. soc. festival of the 7th day of the clear fortnight [śuklapaksa] of the month of māgha, dedicated to the goddess Sītalā; only cold foods should be consumed there.
śīdhu [related to sīdhu] m. rum.
śīra m. bio. zoo. python.
śīrna [pp. śṛ] amnf śīrṇā broken, torn, crushed; faded, destroyed; fallen (tooth) | rotten, spoiled. śīrnīkr to damage, to injure. śīrṇatva [tva] n. rot.
śīrṣá [śiras] n. head, skull; upper part, forehead; anterior part, beginning | var. śīrṣán ved. id.
śīrṣaṇya [ya] amnf śīrṣaṇyā phon. [“from the skull” cerebral (phoneme); syn. mūrdhanya. śīrṣaṇyāḥ mane.
śīrṣāvaśeṣa [avaśeṣa] amnf śīrṣāvaśeṣā of which only the head remains.

śīrṣaka [śīrṣaka] amnf śīrṣakā superior, at the head | phil. who knows the verse Širā — m. myth. np. of Sīrṣaka, epith. of Rāhu "reduced to a head" — n. head, skull | summit; helmet, hat; guir heath carried on the head | soc. judgment, verdict, sentence.
√ śīl v. [1] pr. (śīlati) pp. (śīlita) pf. (pari) to serve, to revere; to practice, to act — ca. (śīlayati) to be accustomed to doing; to practice intensely; to engage in; to exercise, to cultivate.

śīla [act. śīl ] mn habit, character, disposition, nature | moral practice; good conduct, morality, piety, virtue | bd. virtue or moral discipline, one of the 6 perfections |pāramitā| of an accomplished [bodhisattva] — agt. f. śīlā ifc. accustomed to, practicing, devoted to (iic.). kalahaśīla quarrelsome. māṃsaśīla who usually eats meat; carnivore. duḥkhaśīla accustomed to hardship | ill-tempered, irritable. pañcaśīla mod. the five founding principles of the Indonesian state. yuvāno vismaraṇaśīlāḥ young people tend to forget.
śīlagunopeta [guṇaupeta] amnf śīlagunopetā bd. ["who possesses the quality of virtue"] virtuous.

śīlavat [vat] amnf śīlavatī of good morality, virtuous — f. śīlavatī myth. np. of śīlavatī "the Pious One", wife of Ugraśravā; to save him from the curse of Māndavya, she prevented the Sun from rising; she was appeased by Anasūyā.
śīlākṣara [akṣara] n. lithograph.
śīlāditya [āditya] m. hist. np. of the king of Mālava śīlāditya "Sun of virtue", son of Yaśodharmā (6th century); virtuous Buddhist, he emigrated to Kaśmīra, where he became king again in 540.
śīlana [act. śīl ] n. assiduous practice, incessant study (not of knowledge [śāstra]); devotion.
śīlita [pp. śīl] amnf śīlitā practiced | frequented — n. practice; conduct.

śúka [agt. śuc₁] m. bio. zoo. parrot; in poetry, it acts as a matchmaker and confidant myth. [Mah.] np. of Suka "parrot", mythical sage son of Vyāsa who spilled his seed at the sight of the nymph [apsaras] Ghṛtācī who appeared to him in the form of a parrot; Shiva himself came to officiate at the ceremony [upanayana] of investiture of his sacred cord [upavīta]; he was exceptionally intelligent, and was educated by Brhaspati; he wanted to become a renunciant [sannyāsin]; his father sent him to gather the wisdom of King Janaka, who taught him the duty of a Brahmin; he returned to his father, and took the beautiful Pīvarī as his wife, who bore him four sons and one daughter; His father Vyāsa told him the Mah., which he recited to the gandharvās, yakṣās, and rakṣās; he told the Bhāgavatapurāna to Haridvāra, to King Parīkṣit, who desired to receive wisdom before dying; following a visit from Nārada, he went to meditate on Mount Kailāsa, where he attained perfection [siddha₁] and was raised like a star to Heaven; full of grief, his father Vyāsa ascended Kailāsa, where he inquired of his son from Shiva; Shiva allowed him to have an image of Suka accompany him henceforth; at the place where he appeared to him, Shiva can still be invoked successfully — f. śukī bio. female parrot | myth. [Mah.] np. of Sukī, daughter of Kaśyapa and Tāmrā; she gave birth to Nalā | myth. [Mah.] np. of Sukī₁, daughter of Kaśyapa and Dhṛtarāṣṭrī₁; she gave birth to Natā.

śukatīrtha [tīrtha] n. myth. np. of Sukatīrtha, hermitage of the sage Suka, where the latter told the Bhāgavatapurāṇa to King Parīkṣit for 7 days at the foot of a kalpavrkṣa; it is identified with the mod. Sukratal near Muzaffarnagar.
śukatunda [tunda] m. parrot's beak | soc. ritual gesture [mudrā] of the hand "in parrot's beak" (fingers closed, except the index finger half-bent).
śukadeva [deva] m. myth. n.p. from śukadeva "Parrot Lord", a name from Suka.
śúkanāsa [nāsā] m. lit. [K.] np. of the minister Śukanāsa "with a parrot's beak nose", father of Pundarīka₂ — f. śukanāsī arch. tower of the vestibule of a temple, forming the "nose" of the vimāna₁.

śukanāsopadeśa [upadeśa] m. bed. n.p. from the Sukanāsopadeśa "Teachings of Śukanāsa", episode of the Kādambarī. śúkanāsikā [ nāsikā ] f. nose in the shape of a parrot's beak | arch. tower of the vestibule [antarāla] of a temple.
śukapura [pura] n. geo. n.p. from Sukapura village, near Edappal, 10 km east of Ponnani, Kerala; its temple, dedicated to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, faces the South.
Śukavāha [vāha] m. myth. np. of Šukavāha, epith. of Kāma "who has the parrot as a mount".

śukasaptati [saptati] m. lit. np. from the Sukasaptati "the 70 tales of the parrot", a collection of tales in Sanskrit from the 12th century by an unknown author; there are 3 recensions of it; cf. Prabhāvatī. śukasārikāpralāpana [ sārikapralāpana ] n. the art of teaching parrots and mai nates to speak, one of the 64 arts |kalā|.
śuktá [pp. śuc₁] amnf śuktā sour; sour | putrid, foul; stinking | hard (words) — m. sourness — n. sour thing or liquid; sour drink.
śuktapāka [pāka] m. gastric fluid; digestion.
śukti [act. śuc₁] f. ["that shines"] pearl | mother-of-pearl; shell. oyster | skullcap.

śuktimat [mat] amnf Śuktimatī full of shells | geo. np. of Mount Suktimān, a kula giri — f. Śuktimatī myth. np. of the Cedi river Suktimatī₁ "which produces pearls" (mod. Kena); lit. it was diverted by Mount Kolāhala which was in love with it; from their union was born Queen Gi rikā | myth. np. of Suktimatī₁, capital of the Cedi kingdom, on the banks of the Suktimatī₁; it was founded by King Uparicara Vasu₂ || pali sotthivati. য়ুক śukrá [śuc₁ra] amnf śukrā Bright, splendid res | clear, pure, white — m. [śukragraha] myth. np. from the graha Sukra "Brilliant", son of Bhrgu, regent of the planet Venus; he is also Šukrācārya, the chaplain [purohita] of the demons [asura]; [PP.] through his penances (by breathing smoke for a thousand years with his head upside down) he obtained from Śiva invincibility; he possesses the science of resurrection [samjīvanī] with which he restored Bali to life after he was killed in battle by the gods; he gave sovereignty over the three worlds to Bali by performing the sacrifice of omnipotence |viśvajit|; he tried unsuccessfully to dissuade Bali from granting his vow to Vāmana; to punish him for trying to hinder a charitable gift, Viṣṇu blinded him (and his name is synonymous with one-eyed); He possesses the secret of immortality, which he shared with his student Kaca; he fought his rival Bṛhaspati who impersonated him; Jayantī is his wife; father of Devayānī, he cursed his son-in-law Yayāti with decrepitude for his infidelities; cf. Uśanā, Kavi, Kāvya | astr. the planet Venus; a journey undertaken in its direction is considered inauspicious | Vedic. name of the 3rd Vedic month (May June, Jyaistha), personified as guardian of the treasures of Kubera — n. splendor, clarity, light | semen. śukravisarjayati he spills his seed.
śukranīti [nīti] f. lit. np. from the Šukranīti, a treatise on political science attributed to the sage Sukrācārya, actually from the 19th century.
Śukranītisara [sara] m. bed. n.p. of Sukranītisara, variant of the previous one.
śukravāra [vāra] m. Friday, the day of Venus [śukra].
śukravisṛṣṭi [visṛṣṭi] f. emission of sperm; mas turbation.
śukla [related to śukra] amnf śuklā Brilliant,

resplendent | white | clear, pure, immaculate — m. the color white | [śuklapakṣa] fortnight of the waxing moon | astr. np. of śukla "Bright", son of Nāradī personifying year 3 of a life cycle | myth. epith. of various gods, beings or objects | not. Sukra. śuklībhū to whiten (become white). śuklīkṛ to whiten (make white).
śuklakṛṣṇa [kṛṣṇa] m. du. śuklakṛṣṇau the white and the black. śuklatā |tā| f. whiteness, property |jāti| of being white. śuklatva |tva| n. id.
śukladhyāna [dhyāna] n. jn. pure meditation; syn. sitadhyana | pkt. sukkajjhāna.
śuklapakṣa [pakṣa] m. astr. "clear fortnight", (favorable) period between a new moon [amāvāsyā] and a full moon [pūrņimā]; opp. kṛṣṇapakṣa.
śuklapratipad | pratipad₂ | astr. day | tithi | following a new moon; it is a day of celebration; not. caitraśuklapratipad marks the Hindu New Year |yugādi|.
śuklayajurveda [yajurveda] m. bed. n.p. of śuklayajurveda; opp. Kṛṣṇayajurveda.
śuklāpānga [apānga] m. ["having white corners of the eyes"] peacock.

śunga m. bio. bot. Ficus indica, banyan; syn. nyagrodha, vata | myth. np. of King Sunga, son of Dīrghatamā and Sudeṣṇā | hist. the Sunga dynasty at the beginning of the Kuṣāṇa period which succeeded the Maurya dynasty in 185 ante; it was established by Pusyamitra Sunga₁, commander-in-chief of King Brhadratha₃, the last of the Mauryas, whom he assassinated; Sunga₁ was a Brahmin, and this era favored the decline of Buddhism | pl. śungās hist. the 10 kings of this dynasty; the founder Puşyamitra was succeeded by his son Agnimitra; The Kanva dynasty succeeded the śuṅgās around 71 BC.

√ śuc₁ v. [1] pr. (śocati) pft. (śuśoca) aor. [2] (aśucat) pp. (śukta) pf. (anu, abhi) to burn, shine, gleam | to weep, groan, grieve, be distressed; to be in pain, suffer | to suffer about (loc. i. pratiacc.) | to pity; to complain about; to regret, to mourn someone. (acc.) — ca. (śocáyati) ps. (śocyate) to afflict — ca. r. (śocáyate) to grieve, to lament — intens. r. (śośucyate) to shine or burn intensely. mā śucaḥ do not grieve; do not worry.

súc₂ [act. suc₁] amnf ifc. that shines, that illuminates (iic.) — f. flame; radiance; brilliance, splendor — ifc. pl. sorrows, griefs, regrets for (iic.) tears. śuco vaśam mā gamaḥ do not let yourself go to the cha grin.

śuci [śuc₁i] amnf Bright, shining | white, immaculate, clear; pure, clean, virtuous, purified — m. purification, purity, virtue — n. Vedic. 4th Vedic month of the hot season (June-July); hot season. śucībhū to purify oneself. śucitā [tā] f. clarity; purity; virtue.
śucitva [tva] n. id..
śuṇṭhī f. dry ginger; opp. ārdraka || hi. soth.
śuṇḍā f. rum | tavern.
śundaka [ika] m. tavern.
Śutudrī f. geo. np. of the Śutudrī river which flows from the Himalayas towards the Pañjāb (mod. Sutlej); cf. Satadru.
śudi [śukladina] adv. during the clear fortnight (of a lunar month); opp. vadi | sudi id.

śuddhá [pp. śudh] amnf śuddhā pure, clear, purified; immaculate, unaltered; irreproachable, spotless | correct, just | phon. said of a simple vowel, short or long — iic. astr. normal month following an intercalary month [adhika] — f. śuddhā lit. [Mukula] metaphor [lakṣaṇā] where the figurative meaning is completely distinct from the literal meaning. śuddhīkṛ to purify. śuddhībhū to purify oneself. śuddham udakam pure water.
śuddhatā [tā] f. purity; integrity; correctness, justice. śuddhatva [tva] n. id. )2
śuddhavikalpa | vikalpa | m. phil. technique of purifying the mind, due to Abhinavagupta: one exorcises a negative obsession by repeating its opposite as a mantra.
śuddhavidyā [vidyā] f. phil. |Tantra| Pure Knowledge, a category of existence [tattva].

śuddhādvaita [advaita] n. phil. [Vedānta] purified monism, vaisnava phil. doctrine taught by Vallabhācārya; it affirms the reality of the phenomenal world, and thus opposes the advaita doctrine of Sankara₁.
śuddhādhvan [adhvan] n. phil. [siddhānta] pure world of the accomplished, who can grant deliverance.
śuddhānta | anta | m. gynaeceum, harem | "the inviolate interior" |.
Śuddhodana [odana] m. hist. np. of the king śākya Śuddhodana, father by his wife Māyā₁ of the prince Siddhārtha Gautama, the future Buddha; he reigned in Nepal at Kapilavastu in the 6th century BC.

śúddhi [act. śudh] f. purification, purity | soc. purification rite | innocence; acquittal; discharge, the act of settling one's debts | correction, revision (text, rite) | precision; sincerity; certainty. śuddhim kṛ to ascertain, to verify. śuddhim i math. to be correct.
śuddhipattra [pattra] n. bed. errata.

√ śudh v. [4] pr. (śudhyati) pr. r. (śudhyate) pft. (śuśodha) aor. [2] (aśudhat) pp. (śuddha) pfp. (śodhanīya) pf. (vi, pari, sam) to purify | to purify oneself, to be purified; to become clear | to see one's doubts dispelled — ca. (śodhayati) to purify; to perform a ritual purification — ps. (śudhyate) to be excused, to be cleared of an accusation. m. myth. np. of Śuna "the Auspicious," epith. of Vāyu or Indra — n. prosperity; success.
śunahotra [hotra] m. myth. np. of the sage [rsi] śunahotra "of the Propitious sacrifice", a Bhāradvāja, author of hymns of the Rgveda; Grtsamada was his son.
sun a₂ iic. svan₁.
śunaka [ka] m. young dog; dog | myth. [BhP.] np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Sunaka "Canine"; cf. Kumāravana — f. śunakī female dog. श्रुन: śunaḥ [g. śvan₁] iic.

śunahpuccha [puccha] m. myth. from np. Sunappuccha "Dog's Butt", elder brother of Sunahsepa. Śunaḥśepa var. śunaḥśepha [śepa] m. lit. [AB.] np. from the Brahmana Sunahsepa or Sunahsepha "Dog's Penis", sold for 100 cows by his father Ajīgarta to King Hariścandra to serve as a substitute for his son Rohitāśva as a sacrifice to Varuṇa; by praying to all the gods, and especially by instituting the rājasūya in honor of Varuna, he had his life spared, and was adopted by Viśvāmitra [śaunaḥśepa] | lit. [Rām.] In this variant, Sunahsepha₁ is the son of Rcīka; King Ambarīṣa had undertaken a yāga, in which Indra, out of jealousy, stole the sacrificial cow; the priest advised him to replace it with a Brahman, and Rcīka sold Sunahsepha for 100,000 cows; Viśvāmitra wanted to save him and asked his own sons to replace him, but upon their refusal, he cursed them to become cannibals; he gave Sunahsepha two prayers to Agni which allowed him to be saved; cf. Devarāta.
śunahśepākhyāna [ākhyāna] n. lit. account of the history of Sunaḥśepa in the Aitareyabrāhmaṇa.
śunolāngūla [lāngūla] m. myth. n.p. of Sunolāngūla "Dog's Tail", younger brother of Sunahsepa.
śunī cf. śvan₁.
śundhyu var. śundhyū [śudh] amnf pure; brilliant; radiant — m. myth. epith. of Agni.

√ śubh₁ v. [1] pr. r. (śobhate) v. [1] pr. (śobhati) pft. (śuśobha) pp. (śobhita) pf. (upa) to shine, to splendor | to be distinguished, to present well, to have a beautiful appearance; to be eminent — ca. (śobhayati) to adorn, to decorate; to make shine. vidyā vinayena śobhate One displays one's knowledge with modesty.
súbh₂ |act. subh₁| f. ved. splendor, beauty; decoration | rise; flight.

śubha [agt. śubh₁] amnf śubhā bright, ornate, beautiful, pretty, pleasing, splendid; useful, good, appropriate; favorable, propitious, auspicious, happy, prosperous; eminent, distinguished; excellent | honest, virtuous — act. n. beauty, charm; luck, happiness, prosperity, good, virtuous action. śubham adr. good luck. śubhamastu var. śubhambhūyāt adr. all my best wishes! śubharātrī good night!
śubhakara [kara₁] amnf śubhakarī that causes prosperity; fortunate.
śubhakaradeva [deva] m. hist. np. of the king subhakaradeva; Buddhist, he reigned in Orissa at the end of the 8th century.

śubhakarasiṃha [siṃha] m. hist. np. of the monk bd. subhakarasimha "Lion of Happiness" (637–735); a kṣatriya by birth, he inherited the Oḍra throne at age 13, then ceded it to his elder brother to become a monk; in Nālandā he met his master Dhar magupta who initiated him into Vajrayāna; he departed for Tibet and then China, which he reached in 714; there he translated the sūtrāņi and trained disciples; he is considered the 1st patriarch of bd. Japanese Shingon. śubhakṛt | kṛt ₂| amnf cf. śubhakara — m. astr. np. of Subhakrt "Fortunate", personifying year 36 of a life cycle [samvatsara].

śubhagupta [gupta] m. hist. np. of Subhagupta, phil. bd. externalist of the 8th century, author of the Bāhyārthasiddhikārikās; he supported the existence of external objects, contrary to the nirākāravāda doctrine.
śubhacintaka [cintaka] amnf śubhacintikā which makes good wishes. śubhadina [dina] n. blessed day, lucky day.
śubhanāma [nāman] n. soc. name in use of a person.
śubhalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. sign or mark fa vorable, good omen; their study constitutes the sāmudrakavidyā — m. bearer of favorable signs.
śubhasūcanī [sūcana] f. myth. np. of Subhasūcanī "She who brings good news", a deity invoked by women in times of calamity.

śubhānga [anga₁] amnf śubhāngī who has a beautiful body; graceful — m. myth. epith. of Shiva — f. śubhāngī beautiful woman | myth. epith. of many wives of gods and kings. śubhānana [ānana] amnf śubhānanā who has a radiant face.
śubhārambha [ārambha] m. inaugural session.
śubhāśaya [āśaya] m. favorable occasion. navavarşasya śubhāśayāh adr. Happy New Year!

śubhāśubha [aśubha] amnf śubhāśubhā more or less good; pleasant and unpleasant; good and bad — n. good and bad. yadbhāvi tadbhavatu śubhamaśubham vā come what may, for good or for bad. nābhuktam kṣīyate karma kalpakoṭiśatair api avaśyam eva bhoktavyam kṛtam karma śubhāśubham | The unrewarded act is not lost, even in billions of eons; it is quite certain that every action performed, good or bad, will eventually bear fruit.

śubhāśubhasvapnaparīkṣā [svapnaparīkṣā] f. med. [Śārngadharasamhitā] examination of precognitive dreams. śubhecchā | icchā | f. phil. righteous desire | phil. | YV. | the desire for liberation, 1st level of knowledge |jñānabhūmikā|.
śubham [acc. śubh₁] iic.
śubhamyā |yā| amf which flies away quickly.
śubhamyú | yu₃ | amnf elegant, splendid; happy.

śubhrá [śubh₁ra] amnf śubhrā bright; beautiful, splendid | white; Immaculate — m. the color white | myth. np. of Subhra "the Immaculate", husband of Vikunthā. śubhratā | tā | f. whiteness. śubhratva [tva] n. whiteness. śubhrádat [dat] amnf who has white teeth.
śubhrí [śubh₁ri] amnf brilliant; splendid.
√ śumbh v. [1] pr. (śumbhati) pf. (ni) to wound, to kill.
śumbha [agt. śumbh] m. myth. [Devīmāhātmya] np. of the asura śumbha "Slayer", son of Gavesthī, killed with his brother Nisumbha by Kālī emerging from the front of Durgā.
śulka mn price, value; prize of a competition | tax, toll, customs duty | soc. dot — f. śulkā ifc. value of (iic.).
śulba var. śulva n. rope.

śulbadīpikā [dīpikā] f. lit. np. of the Sulbadīpikā, commentary on the Baudhāyana śulbasūtra by Dvārakānātha. śulbasūtra [ sūtra ] n. math. mathematical formulary | lit. collections of formulas [sūtra] describing geometric constructions for ritual purposes, not. for building altars; some date back to Vedic times, and are among the oldest mathematical texts; cf. Baudhāyana, Apastamba, Kātyāyana₁.
śulva var. śulba n. rope. য়ুসুষ্ śuśrūṣ [des. śru] v. pr. r. (śuśrūṣate) to be attentive to obey.

Śūdraka₁ [ka] m. hist. np. of Sūdraka₁ Rājā "King of Servants", presumed author of the play Mṛcchakaṭikā, dating from before the 6th century; in it he gives a sharp critique of the society of princes, brahmins and courtesans of his time, from a Buddhist perspective | lit. [K.] np. of Śūdraka₁, King of Vidiśā, hero of the frame story of the Kādambarī; he had all the qualities, but did not know love; A beautiful woman named Caṇḍālā brought him the parrot Vaisampāyana₁, who revealed to him that he was in fact CandraCandrāpīda₁ reincarnated, that he himself was Puṇḍarīka₂ punished for his sins by being born in animal form, and that the Caṇḍālā was in fact Lakṣmī his creator, all this labyrinth of wondrous events having been revealed to him by the sage Jābāli₁ | lit. [DKC.] np. of Sūdraka₁, lover of Aryadāsī, who conceived by him a boy who was abandoned, taken in by Vinayavatī, and who was reborn as Arthapāla. nāmnaiva yo nirbhinnārātihṛdayo viraci tanārasiṃharūpāḍambaramekavikramākrāntasakalabhuvanatalo vikramatrayāyāsitam ca jahāseva vāsudevam K. (describing Sūdraka₁) The mere mention of his name pierces the hearts of his enemies and he conquers the whole world by his sheer bravery (with a single step), as if to humiliate Viṣṇu/Vāsudeva who had to create the thunderous form of Narasimha and tire himself out taking three strides (to conquer the Universe in the form of Trivikrama).

śūdrávarga [varga] m. SOC. class of servants |lit. section of the Bhūmyādikāṇḍa, dealing with servants.
Śūdrācāraśiromaṇi [ācāraśiromaṇi] m. lit. np. du Sūdrācāraśiromaņi "Treasury of the good conduct of the servant", work of śūdradharma de Kṛṣṇa Sesa₂.
śūdrāryá [ārya] m. du. śūdrāryau a servant and a nobleman.
śūna [pp. śū] amnf śūnā swollen; hollow — n. void, absence.

śūnyatva [vat] n. cf. śūnyatā.

Śūra [śūra] amnf śūrā courageous, brave, Bold, warrior — m. hero | myth. [Mah.] np. of the yādava king Śūra "the Bold", or Śūrasena₁ "of the army of brave men", son of Hṛdika; he conceived 10 sons and 4 daughters by his wife Māriṣā₂; his younger brother Vasudeva is the father of Kṛṣṇa; he gave his eldest daughter Pṛthā to his cousin Kunti to be adopted as Kuntī hist. np. of Sūra₁ or Aryaśūra, bd. monk. From the 1st century, author of a campū-style version of the Jātakamālā, recounting 34 previous lives [jātaka] of the Buddha; some of these stories are illustrated in the Ajanta frescoes; 33 of these births are depicted in the 135 panels of the basilisk in the first gallery of the Borobudur stupa. sā te gatir yā śūrāṇām (recited at the avabhṛtha) Your path is that of heroes.
śūrapadma [padma] m. myth. [SkP.] np. of the asura Sūrapadma, elder brother of Tāraka; he fought Skanda, and defeated begged for mercy; he became his
peacock mount | vāhana|.

Śūrasena₁ [senā] m. geo. np. of the country and people of Śūrasena₁; its capital was Mathurā | myth. np. of King Sūrasena "to the army of brave men"; cf. Sūra | myth. np. of King Sūrasena₁, son of Kārtavīrya; he killed Ja madagni to avenge his father.
śūram [acc. Śūra] iic.

śūramgamasamādhi [samādhi] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] Complete awakening, with wisdom through
done [prajñāpāramitā], and attainment of Buddha nature [buddhasvabhāva]; also called simhanādasamādhi and vajrasamādhi.
Śūramgamasamādhinirdeśa [nirdeśa] m. bed. n.p. from Sūramgamasamādhinirdeśa “Complete Manual of Awakening”; cf. Suramgamasūtra.
Śūramgamasūtra [sūtra] n. lit. np. of the Sūramgamasūtra, ancient text of the bd. Mahāyāna, also called Sūramgamasamādhinirdeśa.
śūrpa n. wicker basket; fan; sieve; wicker basket.

Śūrpaṇakhā [nakha] f. myth. [Rām.] np. of Sūrpaṇakhā "She with fan-like claws", vampire [rākṣasī] sister of Rāvaṇa; she lived in Janasthāna with her brother Khara; she fell in love with Rāmacandra who rejected her, and was mocked by Sītā; taking on a horrible form she wanted to devour her, but Lakshmana disfigured her by cutting off her nose and ears; to take revenge she incited Rāvaṇa to abduct Sītā. সূল śūla m. pike, spear, skewer | myth. trident of Śiva | acute pain, colic; impalement — f. śūlā stake | prostitute — ifc. sale of (iic.). śūle niksip condemn to the stake. śūlāyām viddhah impaled. śūlā kuryāt can be cooked on a spit.

śūlaghna [ghna] amnf śūlaghnā med. (remedy) for colic. śūlapāṇi [ pāṇi ] amnf who has the spear in hand — m. myth. epith. of Rudra/Siva | hist. np. of the Mahāmahopādhyāya Sūlapāni, author of Smrti literature from Bengal (15th century); he is also credited with the chess treatise Caturangadīpikā. স্লিক śūlika [śūlaika] amnf śūlikī roasted on a spit | who carries a spear or pike — m. executioner impaling criminals | bastard of a brah mane or kṣatriya and a śūdrā woman — n. roast meat — f. śūlikā roasting spit.

śṛṅkhalatā [tā] f. state of being linked by a chain; connection; series. śṛṅkhalatva |tva| n. id. মৃহ্বলা śṛṅkhalā [f. śṛṅkhala] f. chain; irons.

śṛṅgī [f. śṛṅga] ifc. f. bio. name of various plants.
