Śeṣa [obj. śiṣ] mn residue, remainder | soc. not. remainder of the offerings to the gods of the pākayajña, eaten by the master of the house | end, conclusion; memory | myth. np. of Śeṣa "Vestige", son of Kaśyapa and Kadrū, king of dragons | nāga | symbolizing the residue of the Universe between two kalpas and the germ of creation; during the kalpa he supports the world; at the pralaya, he vomits the fire that destroys everything; during cosmic sleep, ViṣṇuNārāyaṇa rests upon him; he incarnated on earth as Lakṣmaṇa and Balarāma; it is also said that he incarnated as Caraka to heal men, and as Patañjali to bring Sanskrit and yoga; cf. Ananta, Anantaśīrṣā, Adiśesa, Phanindra, Vāsuki onyx; soc. this stone is considered malevolent | lit. [K.] np. of Seșa₁ "Residual", a necklace of pearls of unparalleled brilliance, the last treasure from the primordial churning; it was given by Varuna to Citraratha; Kādambarī offered it to Candrāpīda₁ | hist. np. of the pandita Kṛṣṇa Śesa₂, grammarian and poet of the 16th century; he is the author of the Kamsavadha and the Śūdrācāraśiromaņi hist. np. From the pandita Krishna Shesha, 16th-century grammarian and poet. Shesha is an adverbial in grammar. In other cases, iti Shesha is a grammar. To be completed by this. There is nothing left.

śaibya [*śibiya] amnf śaibyā relating to the śibayas ; descendant of Sibi — m. myth. [PP.] np. of Saibya, one of the 4 horses of Kṛṣṇa's chariot, of green color — f. śaibyā myth. np. of Princess Saibyā, niece of the impostor Vāsudeva₁; Svetaketu₁ and Uddhava fell in love with her; the latter made Kṛṣṇa intervene on his behalf. খীল śaila [*śilā] amnf śailā of stone, stony — m. hill, mountain | myth. chain of mountains separating the earthly regions; there are seven of them | math. symb. the number 7.

śailūṣá [*śilūṣa] m. dancer, mime; actor, entertainer; conductor, one who beats the beat | thug, pimp — f. śailūṣī actress, dancer. śailūṣa iva mām Rāma parebhyo dātum icchasi [Rām.] (Sītā) Like a entertainer, O Rāma, you want to give me to others. śaiva [*śiva] amnf śaivī relating to shiva phil. [Tantra] qualifies the Shaivite doctrine, which is developed in the divine dialogues (āgama and ni gama); Kashmiri Shaivism developed the Tantric doctrine. Trika — m. Shaivite, worshipper of Šiva | myth. [BhP.] np. of Saiva, friend of Šiśupāla; to avenge him, he attacked Kṛṣṇa at Dvārakā; the latter cut off his head with his discus, and Saiva thus attained liberation through dvesabhakti.
śaivacāpa [cāpa] m. myth. np. of the magic bow Saivacāpa that Viśvakarmā made for shiva in order to destroy Tripura; cf. Ajagava.
Śaivatantra [Tantra] n. bed. n.p. of the Saivatantra.
Śaivapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. bed. n.p. from Śaivapurāṇa; cf. Vāyavīyapurāna.

śokavaśa | vaśa | amnf śokavaśā who gives himself over to Sorrow — n. empire of Sorrow. śokavaśam mā gamah one must not give oneself over to Sorrow. śokasamtapta var. śokasantapta |samtapta| amnf śokasaṃtaptā tortured by Sorrow.
śokāpanuda | apanuda | m. | "who takes away the punishment" | son.
śokārta |ārta| amnf śokārtā afflicted by sorrow. śokārtasya pravṛtto me śloko bhavatu nānyathā [Rām.] Being afflicted by sorrow, the śloka and no other imposed itself upon me.
śokārti |ārti| f. affliction; Grief.
śoc [ca. śuc₁] v. [10] pr. (śocáyati) pfp. (śocya) inf. (śocitum) to afflict | to grieve, to lament — ps. (śocyate) to be afflicted. na tvam śocitum arhasi you must not lament.
śocanīya [pfp. [2] śoc] amnf śocanīyā lamentable, déplorable — n. (impers.) it is necessary to deplore.
śocis [abstr. śuc₁] n. flame; radiance; light | splendor — amnf bright; radiant.
śocya [pfp. [1] śuc₁] amnf śocyā which one must grieve over; lamentable, deplorable, miserable — n. (impers.) one must deplore. gatam na śocyam One must not regret the past.

śoṇa amnf śoṇā f. śoṇī red, blood-colored — m. redness — n. blood; minium — f. śoṇā geo. np. of the Soṇā River, which rises near the Amarakantaka peak of the Vindhya Mountains and flows into the Ganges upstream from Pāṭaliputra; it marks the western boundary of Magadha, south of the Ganges. śoṇīkṛ to dye red. śoṇanarmadam n. sg. (collective) the Soṇā and the Nar madā.
śoṇita [śoṇaita] n. blood. bahūśonitaliptaśarīra amn who has her body covered in blood. śonitārdrayeva dṛṣṭyā with a bloodshot gaze.
śonitapa | pa₁ | amnf śonitapā who drinks blood.
śonitapura [pura] n. myth. no. of Sonitapura "City of blood", capital of the asura Bāṇa.
śodh [ca. śudh] v. [10] pr. (śodhayati) pp. (sod hita) to purify.
śodha [act. śudh] m. purification; cleaning; correction. śodhapattra | pattra | n. lit. erratum.
śodhaka [agt. śudh] amnf śodhikā which purifies, purificatory — m. purifier | math. quantity to be subtracted from a number so that the remainder is a square.
śodhana [act. śudh] amnf śodhanā cleansing, purifying — n. means of purification | justification; proof | math. subtraction — f. śodhanī broom; brush.
śodhanaka [ka] m. soc. court attendant, in charge of its cleanliness and proper functioning.
śodhanīya [pfp. [2] śudh] amnf śodhanīyā to purify; to justify | to pay.
śodhita [pp. śodh] amnf śodhitā purified.
śodhin [agt. śudh] amnf śodhinī that which cleanses, that which purifies.
śopha [related to śū] m. tumescence; swelling | tumor — f. śophā ifc. swelling of (iic.).
śobh [ca. śubh₁] v. [10] pr. (śobhayati) to adorn, decorate; to make shine.
śobha [agt. śubh₁] amnf śobhā bright; pretty, graceful — m. luster — f. cf. śobhā.
śobhakṛt [kṛt₂] amnf that makes shine; that makes it bright.

śobhana [agt. śubh₁] amnf śobhanā brilliant; beautiful, pretty; excellent, glorious, magnificent — ifc. superior to, better than (iic.) — n. good, virtue, prosperity | astr. np. of sobhana "Fullness", personifying the 37th year of a life cycle [saṃvatsara] — f. śobhanā pretty woman. śobhane voc. adr. my beautiful one. śobhanā kṛtiḥ [Patanjali₁] an excellent work (the Aştādhyāyī).
śobhā [f. śobha] f. beauty, grace; splendor; luster; color, appearance — ifc. excellence of (iic.). śobhām na kṛ to be ugly.
śobhita [pp. śubh₁] amnf śobhitā splen dide — ifc. adorned with, decorated with (iic.).
śobhin [agt. śubh₁] amnf śobhinī that shines; resplendent | beautiful, pretty — f. śobhinī ifc. adorned with, that shines with, that is distinguished by; ornament of (iic.).
śoṣ [ca. śuṣ₁ɪ] v. [10] pr. (śoṣayati) to dry, to desiccate | to cut down, to destroy.
śoṣa [agt. śuṣ₁ɪ] amnf śoṣā which dries out — act. m. drying out; desiccation | med. tuber culose.

śosana [agt. śuṣ₁ɪ] amnf śoṣaṇā that dries, that desiccates; that absorbs, that dries out | myth. epith. of the burning of love [dahana], arrow of Kāma — ifc. that removes, that destroys (iic.) — m. myth. np. of Śoṣaṇa, aspect of Agni — act. n. desiccation, drying out | dry ginger.
śauká [*śuka] n. flight of parrots.
śauca [*śuc₁a] n. purity, cleanliness; honesty; purification | soc. not. separation of untouchables phil. purity, one of the disciplines | niyama | of yoga.
śauṇḍa [*śuṇḍā] amnf śauṇḍā drunk, intoxicated — ifc. dependent on; intoxicated by; familiar with, gifted at (iic.) — m. drunkard | peacock — f. śauṇḍā alcohol, liquor. aksaśaundah skilled at dice.
śauṇḍi [śauṇḍai] ifc. amnf amateur of, slave of, devoted to (iic.).
śaundika [*śuṇḍāika] amnf śauṇḍikī relating to rum — m. manufacturer or seller of al cool — f. śaundikī proprietor of an alcohol outlet.
śaudra [*śūdra] amnf śaudrā relating to the class śūdra.
śauna [*śūna] amnf śaunī relating to the dog.
śaunaḥśepa [*śunaḥśepa] n. myth. [AB.] story of Śunahśepa.

śaunaka [*śunaka] m. myth. [Mah.] patriarch of the clan chief [kulapati] Ŝaunaka "from Ŝunaka", descendant of Bhrgu; he is credited with the system of the 4 classes [varna]; he presided over the sacrificial session at which Ugraśravā Sauti₂ recounted the Mah.; Gṛtsamada and Paramāra are said to be his sons | lit. [MO.] np. of a wealthy householder in search of knowledge; he questioned Angirā about supreme knowledge | hist. np. of Saunaka₁, grammarian of the 4th century BC; He established an eponymous recension of the Atharvaveda with his padapāṭha [Caturādhyāyikā], and the prātiśākhya of the Ŗgveda; also the Anuvākānukramaņī; it is said that Kātyāyana was his student; tradition identifies him with the previous lit. his recension of the Atharvaveda lit. [DKC.] np. of Saunaka₂, who married Aryadāsī; Kāmapāla is a reincarnation of him.
śaunakin |in| mr. pl. śaunakinah followers of the Veda promulgated by Saunaka.
śaunakīya [īya] amnf śaunakīyā composed by Śaunaka₁ — n. bed. review of the Atharvaveda by Saunaka₁; syn. śaunakīyasamhitā.
śaunakīyasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. bed. n.p. of the Saunakīyasaṃhitā, recension of the Atharvaveda due to Saunaka₁; cf. Caturādhyāyikā.
śaubhreya [*śubhraeya] amnf śaubhreyā descendant of Subhra.
śaura [*śūra] amnf śaurī heroic.

śaurasena [*Śūrasena] amnf śaurasenī geo. relating to the Śūrasena people — f. śaurasenī their language, prākṛta of the Mathurā region; it is used in Sanskrit theatre for high-ranking women; it is the ancestor of Hindi.
śauri [*śūrai] m. myth. n.p. of Sauri, patr. of Vasudeva "son of Sūra" | myth. by ext. epith. of Krsna or Baladeva.
śaurya [*śūraya] n. heroism; valor; prowess.
śaulkika [*śulkaika] m. soc. customs officer, responsible for collecting customs duties.
śauva [*śva] amnf śauvī relating to dogs; canine — n. pack of dogs | dog nature.
śauvana [*śvana] amnf śauvanī re latif aux chiens; canin — n. pack of dogs; offspring of a dog | nature of a dog.
ścandra [related to candra] ifc. amnf ścandrā that shines.
√ scut₁ var. scyut v. [1] pr. (scotati) aor. [5] (aścotīt) aor. [2] (aścutat) pp. (śscutita) to ooze; to drip; to distill | to pour; to sprinkle; to water — ca. (ścotayati) to make flow.
scut₂ [agt. scut₁] ifc. amnf that oozes, that exudes, that distills (iic.); that waters (iic.).
ścutita [pp. ścut₁] amnf śscutitā oozed, exuded; poured; sprinkled.
ścota [act. ścut₁ ₁] m. act of oozing; leak; ar rosage.
scotana [act. scut₁] n. oozing, flowing.

cyut [related to scut₁] v. [1] pr. (scyotati) pp. (śscyutita) to ooze; to flow; to distill | to pour; to sprinkle; to water — ca. (ścyotayati) to cause to flow. স্বৃদ্ śnam nota. gram. modifier [vikaraṇa₂] of present tense formation of gaṇa 7 [rudhādi], athematic with infix n/na. স্বা śnā nota. gram. modifier |vikaraṇa₂| of present tense formation of gaṇa 9 [kryādi], athematic with infix nī/nā.
śnu nota. gram. modifier |vikaraṇa₂| of the present tense of gaṇa 5 [svādi], athematic with affix nu/no.
śmaśāna |aśmaśayana| n. cemetery, cremation ground.
śmaśāru [śmaśru] n. beard; mustache | pl. śmaśrūni id. hárismasāru véd. with a blond or red beard (called Indra).
śmáśru n. beard; mustache. Bearded śmáśrudhara . śmaśru dhr wear a beard. śmaśrula | the | amnf śmaśrulā bearded. śmaśruvardhana | vardhana | mr. barber.
śyan nota. gram. modifier [vikaraṇa₂] of present formation of gana 4 [divādi], theme with affix y.
√ syā v. [1] pr. (syāyati) pp. (sīta) to freeze; to freeze, to cool — pr. r. (śyāyate) to coagulate, to solidify; to cool; to dry out — ps. (śīyate) to freeze, to be cold.
śyāna [agt. śyā] amnf śyānā which dries out; which solidifies, which coagulates | viscous; sticky; dried out.

śyāma |śyāma | amnf śyāmā black; brown, dark, dark-complexioned (used in praise) | myth. epith. of Kṛṣṇa, Barbarīka, etc. | myth. np. of Syāma, black dog of Yama's hell, with a piercing gaze [caturakṣa]; he was born of the bitch Saramā, like his brother the spotted Sabala; the two symbolize the gnawing away at human life by the alternation of days and nights | bio. np. of numerous black animals or plants — n. black pepper — f. śyāmā woman in her prime | bio. np. of many black plants, not. priyangu | night myth. epith. of Durgā, Yamunā, etc. — v. [11] pr. r. (śyāmāyate) to become dark, to darken.
śyāmakarṇa [karṇa] amnf śyāmakarṇī who has the black ear.
śyāmakarṇāśva [aśva] m. myth. horse (white) with black ear; cf. Ŗcīka, Gālava.
śyāmakuṇḍa [kuṇḍa] n. myth. n.p. of the Syāmakunda, pond where GopālaKṛṣṇa bathed in Vṛndāvana.
śyāmagaura [gaura] m. [Viṣṇudharmottara] (painting) tone; syn. śyāmojjvala . śyāmatā [ tā ] f. darkness. śyāmatva |vat| n. id.

śyāmavarṇa | varṇa | amnf śyāmavarṇā of their dark neck. ś yāmāyas | ayas | n. iron ; syn. kṛṣṇāyas. śyāmāruņa | Aruna | amnf śyāmāruņī dark red; is said of the secretion of the temples of the elephant | mada|. śyāmojjvala [ ujjvala ] m. (paint) tone; syn. śyāmagaura.
śyāmaka var. śyāmāka [śyāmaka] amnf śyāmakā of dark color — m. organic. bot. Pani cum frumentaceum, millet.

śyāmala [śyāmala] amnf śyāmalā of dark color. śyāmalatā [ tā ] f. blackness. śyāmalatva [tva] n. blackness. Śyāmalika [ika] m. hist. np. of Syāmalika, author of the play Pādatāditaka; he lived between the 1st and 10th centuries. śyāmalīkṛ to darken, to blacken.
śyāmalī iiv. śyāmala .
śyāmalīkṛta [kṛta] amnf śyāmalīkṛtā blackened, darkened.
śyāya [act. śyā] m. cold.
śyāla [related to syāla] mf śyālī cf. syāla.

śyená m. bio. zoo. eagle; falcon; hawk myth. the hawk into which Indra had transformed himself to reclaim the elixir of immortality [amṛta] stolen by Susna | soc. ved. altar [uttaravedi] in the shape of a hawk built for the sacrifice of the soma [agnicayana] — f. śyenī myth. np. of śyenī, daughter of Kaśyapa, mother of birds of prey, wife of aruna; Sampāti and Jaṭāyu are her sons — v. [11] pr. r. (śyenāyate) to behave like an eagle — v. [11] pr. (śyenayati) to act like an eagle. śyenácit [cit₃] amnf stacked in the shape of a falcon (said of the Vedic altar) — amn śyenácita id. śyenacitam cinvīta (inj.) the altar must be built in the shape of a falcon. śyenapāta [ pāta ] m. fall of a falcon in attack.
śyenayāga [yāga] m. ved. falcon sacrifice, rite of cursing an enemy; it is so named by analogy with the falcon that swoops down on its prey.
śyai cf. śyā.
śyainampātā [*śyenapātaa] f. (hunting [mrgayā]) falcon.

śyonāka m. bio. bot. Bignonia indica or bot. Oroxylum indicum, Indian trumpet vine, a vine with red trumpet-shaped flowers; it is one of the 5 major medicinal roots | bṛhatpañcamūla|. স্বর śrat [related to hrd] pf. ved. in accordance with its aspi
rations | faith | Latin cord, credo; French croire.
√ শ্বথ śrath var. śranth v. [9] pr. (śrathnāti) pr. r. (śrathnīte) to be free; to sag — ca. (śratháyati) to untie, release, free.
śraddádhāna [ppr. mo. śraddhā₁] amnf śraddadhānā having faith; believing; having confidence.
śraddadhānatā [tā] f. belief; faith.

śraddadhānavat |vat| amnf śraddadhānavatī trusting; believing. স্থারা śraddhā₁ [śratdhā₁] v. [3] pr. (śraddádhāti) pr. r. (śraddhatté) to have faith, to trust, to believe; to be faithful; to believe someone (dat. g.); to believe in something (g. loc.); to approve, to consent. সন্ধা śraddhā₂ [act. śraddhā₁] f. faith, trust, belief, devotion; fidelity, loyalty phil. [Vedānta] faith, one of the 6 cardinal virtues [satsampad] | desire, curiosity | The act of being attentive | myth. np. of Sraddhā "Devotion", wife of Angirā; she is the mother of Utathya, Bṛhaspati, Vayasya, Sānti₁, Ghora, Virūpa, Saṃvarta and Sudhanvā; she is also the mother of Kāma by Dharma — agt. amn śraddha f. śraddhā believer; faithful; trusting | lat. credo. śraddhayā adv. with pleasure, gladly. śraddhām ākhyāhi nas tāvat just out of curiosity, tell us.
śraddhālú [ālu] amnf ready to believe; faithful, trusting — ifc. who ardently desires (iic.) — f. pregnant woman experiencing desires. śraddhāvat [vat] amnf śraddhāvatī who has faith; believer.
śraddhita [śraddhā₂ita] amnf śraddhitā believed, trusted | agreed; approved | gladly accepted.
śraddhin [agt. śraddhā₁] amnf śraddhinī faithful; trusting; believing.
śraddheya [pfp. [1] śraddhā₁] amnf śraddheyā credible, trustworthy.
śranthana [act. śrath ] n. act of loosening, untying | arrangement (flowers).
śrápaṇa [agt. ca. śrā] n. act of boiling, of cooking — m. ved. cooking fire (hearth of the offering fire |āhavanīya| or domestic fire [gārhapatya]) — f. śrapaṇī grilling fork.

śrapita [pp. ca. śrā] amnf śrapitā that has been cooked; cooked — n. boiled meat — f. śrapitā rice porridge. jāmātrartham śrapitasya sūpāderatithyupakārakatvam popular maxim |nyāya|: food prepared for the son-in-law can also help the passing guest.

√ শ্বদ্ śram v. [4] pr. (śrāmyati) v. [1] pr. (śramati) pr. r. (śramate) pft. (śaśrāma) aor. [2] (áśramat) pp. (śrānta) pf. (pari, vi) to be weary, to be tired; to tire oneself | to practice asceticism; to be exhausted by penances — ca. (śrāmayati) to tire; to subjugate, to dominate. ná mā śramat may my determination not weaken!

śráma |act. śram| m. fatigue, exhaustion, lassi tude | labor, exercise; pain, aches, troubles | var. śrāma id. — f. śramā ifc. exercise of, fatigue of (iic.). śramam vinā na kimapi sādhyam (motto of the Roorkee IIT) Without effort there is no success.
śramasahiṣṇu [sahiṣṇu] amnf tireless, hardworking.
śramaṇa [agt. śram] m. manual laborer; inferior, vile ascetic, mendicant religious; not. monk bd. — n. labor, toil — f. śramaṇā f. śramaṇī bd. religious. śramanagautamah m. bd. the Buddha.
śramin [agt. śram] amnf śraminī who works hard.
√ śrambh v. [1] pr. r. (śrambhate) pp. (śrabdha) pf. (vi) [unused Without pf.].
śraya [act. śri] m. protection, refuge.

śrayaṇa [act. śri] n. seeking protection from, recourse to (ii.); refuge, asylum. শ্বৰ śravaka [agt. śru] m. bd. personal disciple of Sākyamuni. স্বৃবৃত্য śravana₁ [act. śru] n. hearing, the act of listening; attentive hearing of the master's word | thing heard, teaching, oral tradition | phil. [Vedānta] determination of the true doctrine of the unity of Being — m. ear | math. hypotenuse; diagonal of an astral quadrilateral.

asterism [nakṣatra] in the shape of a triangle; not. śravana₂ | [śramana] ascetic, mendicant religious; not. renunciant bd. or jn. avaisnavamukhodgīrnam pūtam harikathāmṛtam śravanam naiva kartavyam sarpocchistam yathā
payah [PP.] We should not listen to any praise of the Lord from the fetid mouth of a nonvaisnava; it is poison, like milk defiled by a serpent.

śravaṇakumāra [kumāra] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the young boy Sravanakumāra, only help of his blind parents, whom King Dasaratha accidentally killed while hunting by shooting an arrow at the sound of the jug he was filling at the Sarayū; as punishment, his father cursed Daśaratha with the curse of losing his son |putraśoka|, and the latter died while his son Rāma had gone into exile; cf. Yajñadatta₁.
śravaṇakṣetra [kṣetra] n. geo. place presumed where Daśaratha killed śravaṇakumāra, on the banks of the Sa rayū.

śravaṇa₂ [related to sru] amnf śravaṇā boi teux — f. śravaṇā myth. np. de śravaṇā “(the) Lame Cow”, 21st lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the star Altair of the Eagle; Vișnu presides over it; his symbol is three footprints, symbolized by the Eagle.

śrávas |abstr. śru| n. Vedic. noise, uproar, cries of praise | praise, fame, glory. স্ববিষ্ট śraviṣṭha amnf Śraviṣṭhā very glorious — f. śravisthā astr. np. of Sravisthā "the very glorious one", 22nd lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the star β Delphinus; the treasures [vasavas] preside there; its symbol is a tambourine; later called Dhanisthā.
śravya [pfp. [1] śru] amnf śravyā audible | worthy of being heard; which must be listened to — n. obligation to listen | lit. story, poetry (opp. dréya).
śravyakāvya [kāvya] n. lit. praiseworthy poetry, poetry of Prakrite literature; opp. drśyakāvya.
śravyatva [tva] n. the state of being worthy of praise.

√ srā v. [4] pr. (śrāyati) v. [9] pr. (śrīṇāti) pp. (śrāta) to boil; to cook, to ripen — ca. (śrapáyati) ca. r. (śrapayate) pp. (śrapita) to cook, to boil, to roast | to heat; to sweat. স্বাদ্ধ śrāddha |*śraddhā₂| amnf śrāddhā believer; faithful; loyal; truthful — n. soc. ved. funeral rite, offering to the manes | pitaras | ; it is a pākayajña; cf. Gayā, ābhyudayika, nāndīmukhās, ekoddista.
śrāddhabhuj |bhuj₃| amnf who eats the of frandes to the manes.
śrāddhin [śrāddhain] amnf śrāddhinī who performs the funeral rite.
śrāntá [pp. śram] amnf śrāntā tired, exhausted | in pain, depressed; hungry — n. fatigue, exhaustion | mortification, practice of penances.
śrāntácitta [citta] amnf śrāntacittā in a depressed mood.
śrāntámanas [manas] amnf of depressed mood.

śrānti [act. śram] f. fatigue; weariness; exhaustion. ūrdhvordhvamāruhya yadarthatattvam dhīḥ paśyati śrāntimavedayantī | phalam tadādyaih parikalpitānām vivekasopānaparamparāṇām || [Abhinavabhāratī] If the mind perceives the truth of things by rising higher and higher without ceasing, it is through the successive rungs of investigations carried out by the chain of illustrious pioneers.
śrām [ca. śram] v. [10] pr. (śrāmayati) to tire; to subjugate, to dominate.

śrāma cf. śrama. শ্বাৰ্ śrāv [ca. śru] v. [10] pr. (śrāváyati) to tell, recite, proclaim to (acc.). শ্বাবক śrāvaka [agt. śru] amnf śrāvikā audible — m. listener; student | bd. not. disciple of the Buddha having heard the doctrine from the mouth of the Master | jn. Jain disciple; not. renunciant (syn. śravaṇa₁).

śrāvakācāra [ācāra] m. jn. behavior required of a Jain disciple. স্বাবিদ śrāvaṇa₁ [*śravaṇa₁] amnf śrāvaṇā pres crit in the Veda. স্বাবিদ śrāvaṇa₁ [*śravaṇa₂] amnf śrāvaṇā astr. relating to the nakṣatra Sravaṇā — m. month of Sravaṇā (August-September) — f. śrāvaṇī full moon day [pūrṇimā] of this month; SOC. a pākayajña is practiced there; Sanskrit [viśvasaṃskṛtadina] is celebrated there; this festival which follows tantupar van is the occasion to renew the upavīta, and the sisters put a rakṣābandhana on the wrist of their brothers; mod. hi. rakhīpūrņimā.
śrāvam [abs. śru] ind. having listened.

Śrāvasta [*śravasta] m. hist. n.p. of king Srāvasta “the Glorious” — f. śrāvastī geo. n.p. from the city of śrāvastī "the Glorious", capital of king Śrāvasta, located in Kosala (pāli Savatthi, mod. SāhetMāhet near Faizabad in northern Bihāra); bd. Buddha performed a miracle there in the presence of King Prasenajit₂: he walked in the air and multiplied his image endlessly. স্বাত্য śrāvya [pfp. [1] ca. śru] amnf śrāvyā to the dible | worthy of being heard; who must be listened to, who must be proclaimed.

√ śri v. [1] pr. (śrayati) pr. r. (śrayate) aor. [3] (aśiśriyat) pp. (śrita) pf. (ā, ut, pari, vi, sam) to lean on, to be near, to take refuge with (acc.) | to assume a condition, to occupy a place | gr. ; lat. inclino; all. lehnen; ang. to lean; fr. incliner. vatsatarah mahokṣabhāvam śrayati the little calf became a big bull.

śrita [pp. śri] amnf śritā attached to, clinging to, connected with, that which is in (loc. acc. iic.) approached, sought, served, honored; occupied (place) that which has recourse to; that which has gone to, taken refuge with, fallen into (acc.) | subordinate, auxiliary. vān mayyastu śritā vāgghyojisthā devatānām Let the Word be in me, for the Word is the most powerful divinity.
śritákṣama [kṣama] amnf śritakṣamā who has taken patience; tranquil.

śritásattva [sattva] amnf śritasattvā who took courage; resolute. স্থা śrī f. luck; prosperity, Fortune, happiness; Glory | beauty | myth. np. of Srī "Fortune", epithet of Lakṣmī, goddess of prosperity, wife śakti of Vișnu; she is said to have come from the churning of the primordial sea of milk [kṣīrodamathana], or daughter of Bhṛgu and Kyāti; she is the patroness of commerce — iic. [śrīmat] (before proper names or works) excellent, splendid; honorable, eminent; famous, celebrated, illustrious; holy, venerated, sacred.

śrīkantha [kantha] m. myth. epith. of Siva Nīlakaṇṭha₁ "with the splendid throat" | hist. n.p. of Srikantha, an 11th century philosopher; he developed the Shaivite doctrine of “distinguished nonduality” [viśiṣṭādvaita] in his commentaries on the Brah masūtra and in his Sivārkamaņidīpikā | hist. n.p. of Srīkaṇṭha₁ Nīlakaṇṭha₁; cf. Bhavabhuti | hist. n.p. of śrīkantha₂ Kavi, court poet of Śatruśalya, student of Puṇḍarīka₅ Viṭṭhala; We owe to him the Ra sakaumudī (circa 1600) | lit. [KSS.] np. of the country Srīkantha₃ where King Kāntisena reigns.

śrīkanthacarita [carita] n. lit. np. from the mahākāvya Srīkanthacarita, a poem by Mankha in 25 cantos; its theme is the destruction of Tripura by Śiva. śrīkalāpūrņa [kalāpūrņa] m. SOC. title of śrīkalāpūrṇa "Glory of artistic plenitude".

Śrīkālahasti [kāla₂hasti] m. geo. np. of Srīkālahasti, a sacred city in southern Andhra Pradesh, 36 km from Tirupati on the Svarnamukhī River; there one finds the great temple of the Wind Kālahastīśvara.
śrīkṛcchra | kṛcchra | m. soc. penance of three days consisting of eating only cow excrement.
Śrīkṛṣṇa [Kṛṣṇa] m. phil. the Divine Kṛṣṇa hist. n.p. by Srīkṛṣṇa Trakālankāra, author of the Dāyabhāgaprabodhinī | hist. cf. Śrīkṛṣṇabhaṭṭa.
śrīkrsnabhatta [bhatta] m. hist. n.p. by Srīkṛṣṇabhaṭṭa, 18th century author; we owe him not. the Vṛttidīpikā and the Vṛttamuktāvalī.

Śrīkṛṣṇamaṭha [maṭha] m. geo. np. of the temple Srīkṛṣṇamaṭha of Uḍupī, founded by Madhva in the 13th century, a great center of philosophical debates; it is dedicated to Bālakṛṣṇa; [Madhvavijaya] it is said that its idol comes from Dvārakā.
śrīkṛṣṇavilāsa [vilāsa] n. [śrīkṛṣṇavilāsakāvya] lit. n.p. from śrīkṛṣṇavilāsa, poem by Sukumāra.
śrīkhaṇḍa [khaṇḍa] mn sandalwood, sandalwood.
śrīcakra [cakra] n. cf. Sriyantra.
śrīcakrapūjā [pūjā] f. soc. tantric rite of union with Lalitā.
Śrīḍāmara [ḍāmara] n. bed. n.p. from the Śrīḍāmara tantra “extraordinary book”.

Śrītattvanidhi [tattvanidhi] m. lit. np. of the Srītattvanidhi "Illustrious Treasury of Reality", iconographic treatise of the Mahārāja of Mysore Kṛṣṇarāja₁; it contains illustrations of the different deities, in 9 treasuries [nidhi] of illustrations: Šakti, Viṣṇu, Šiva, Brahmā, graha, vaiṣṇava, śaiva, āgama, kautuka.
śrītāla [tāla] m. variety of palm leaf.
śrīdurgāsaptaśatī [Durgāsaptaśatī] f. lit. np. of the śrīdurgāsaptaśatī "700 hymns to Durgā", section of the Mārkandeya purāna, also called Devīmāhātmya.

Śrīdhara [dhara] m. myth. np. of Srīdhara "Di vin support", epith. of ViṣṇuKūrma, supporting the primordial churn; cf. kṣīrodamathana | hist. np. of Śrīdhara₁ bhaṭṭa, Bengali philosopher of the 10th century; he is credited with the Nyāyakandalī | hist. np. of the philosopher Srīdhara₂ Svāmī (14th century, Val labhī) he is credited with the Bhāvārthadīpikā commentary on the Bhāgavatapurāṇa and commentaries on the Vișnupurăna and the Bhagavadgītā | hist. cf. śrīdharācārya.
śrīdharadāsa [dāsa] m. hist. de np. Srīdharadāsa, compiler of the collection of proverbs Saduktikarņāmṛta (1205).

Śrīdharasena [sena] m. hist. np. of Śrīdharasena, Jain scholar of the late 12th century; he is credited with the lexicon Viśvalocana, also called Muktāvalī₁. śrīdharācārya [ ācārya ] m. hist. np. of śrīdharācārya (~870~930); mathematician, he is credited with the arithmetic treatise Pāṭīgaṇita; he gave the rule for solving quadratic equations in the algebra treatise Bījaganita, now lost.

Śrīnagara [nagara] n. geo. np. of Śrīnagara "Rich city", capital of Kaśmīra, on the banks of the Vi tastā (mod. Jhelum); this very ancient city was a bd. center in the time of the Maurya empire then of the kuṣāṇa period; King Pravarasena II made it his capital PravarasenapuraPravara; it was taken by the Huns in the 6th century, became Muslim under the Mughals, then was annexed by the Sikhs in 1820.

Śrīnātha [nātha] m. hist. n.p. of Śrīnātha, Telugu poet (~1365–1441), he popularized the style of versified narration [prabandha], in Sanskritized Telugu; we owe him not. the Naisadhamu, te lugu version of the Naisadhīya of Srīharsa, the Kaśīkhandamu glorifying Benares, the Bhīmakhandamu glorifying the Dakṣārāma temple, the Haravilāsamu celebrating Siva, and the Sivarātrimāhātmya glorifying the śivarātri .

Śrīnāthajī [jī] m. soc. np. of Śrīnāthajī, idol of Krsna as a child; originally installed in Vrndāvana in the 14th century, it was moved to Nāthadvārā in Rājasthāna in the 17th century to protect it from Aurang zeb; it is the object of veneration of the [sampradāya] Kumāra₁ movement founded by Vallabhācārya.

Śrīnivāsa [nivāsa₁] m. myth. residence of Srī | myth. np. of Srīnivāsa "Refuge of Srī", epith. of Vișnu | hist. np. of the Tamil poet and grammarian Ratnakheta Srīnivāsa₁ Dīkṣita (early 16th century); he was the prolific court poet of Sūrappa Nāyaka of Senji; he is notably credited with the play Bhāvanāpurusottama, and the treatise on accents Svarasiddhāntacandrikā; he bore the titles of Şadbhāsācatura "who masters 6 languages" and Pra tidinaprabandhakartā "who writes a book a day".
śrīnivāsakalyāṇa [kalyāṇa] n. soc. celestial marriage ceremony between VișnuSrīnivāsa and Srī Padmāvatī; its festival is celebrated not. at Tirumala.

śrīpañcamī [pañcamī] f. soc. festival in honor of Sarasvatī, on the 5th day of the clear fortnight of the month māgha; books and writing instruments are honored there; this festival is also called va santapañcamī.

Śrīpati₁ [pati] m. "master of fortune", name of prince | myth. np. of Srīpati, epith. of Viṣṇu "the husband of Srī" | hist. np. of the ma rathe mathematician Śrīpati₁, author of the Ganitatilaka (11th century).
śrīpatidatta [datta] m. hist. np. from the grammarian śrīpatidatta, author of the Kātantrapariśiṣṭa, of unknown date.
Śrīparvata [parvata] m. geo. n.p. from the Śrīparvata mountain range, south of the Śrīśaila plateau; mod. Nallamala.
śrīpādasaptati [pādasaptati] f. lit. np. of the śrīpādasaptati "70 verses at the sacred feet of the Goddess", poem by Nārāyaṇa₃ Bhaṭṭa celebrating the defeat of the buffalo demon Mahişa.
śrīphala [phala] n. fruit of the bilva, large yellowish berry, which contains an orange pulp which the priests squeeze to drink the juice.
śrībīja [bīja] n. phil. [Tantra] bijamantra 'śrīm', evocation of Śrī.
Śrībhāgavata [bhāgavata] n. bed. from np. Śrībhāgavata mahāpurāṇa; cf. Bhāgavatapurāṇa.
Śrībhāṣya [bhāṣya] n. bed. n.p. of Rāmānujācārya's Śrībhāṣya, commentary on the Brahmasūtra.

śrīmat [mat] amnf śrīmatī beautiful, amiable, charming, pleasant; splendid, glorious | eminent, famous, illustrious | well-established; rich, fortunate, prosperous — m. person of quality — iic. adr. (honorific) Venerable (np.). śrīman adr. Sir! śrīmatī adr. Madam! (married woman whose husband is still alive). śrīmān bhūyāt may he be happy! śrīmadrāmānujāya namah Glory to the Venerable Rāmānuja.
śrīmattā |tā| f. splendor, beauty; Glory; for tune.
śrīmadbhagavadgītā [bhagavadgītā] f. lit. np. of the Srīmadbhagavadgītā, qualifying the "Holy Bha gavadgītā".
śrīmadbhāgavata [bhāgavata] lit. n. n.p. of Srimadbhāgavata, the “Venerable Bhāgavatapurāṇa”.

Śrīmadbhāgavatamāhātmya | māhātmya | n. lit. np. of Srīmadbhāgavatamāhātmya "Glorification" of the venerable Bhāgavatapurāṇa"; this supplement to the Padmapurāṇa gives instructions on the organization of a saptāha; it predates the 18th century.
śrīmukha [mukha] amnf śrīmukhī who has a pretty face — m. astr. np. of Srīmukha "who has a pretty face", personifying year 7 of a life cycle |samvatsara|.
śrīmus | mus₂ | ifc. amnf which delights the beauty at (iic.).
śrīyantra | yantra | n. phil. tantric meditation diagram, formed of 9 interlocking triangles; syn. śrīcakra ; cf. śrīvidyā .

Śrīranga [ranga] m. myth. np. of Srīranga "Master of the assembly", aspect of Vișnu, also called Ranganātha Svāmī — n. geo. np. of the temple of Srīranga, great sanctuary established on the banks of the Kāverī by Rāmānuja near Trichi in Tamil Nadu, to the Glory of Ranganātha.
śrīraṅgagadya | gadya| n. lit. np. from the Srīrangagadya, a devotional poem by Rāmānuja.

śrīrangapaṭṭana [paṭṭana] n. geo. np. of the city of Srīrangapaṭṭana, on an island in the Kāverī River, 15 km north of Mysore in Karṇāṭa; it is named in honor of Ranganātha, whose temple was built in the 12th century; it was fortified in the 15th century, and served as the capital of the kings and sultans of Mysore | ang. Seringapatam.

śrīrāghavayādavīya [rāghavayādavīya] n. lit. np. of the Srīrāghavayādavīya "Golden Legend of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa", boustrophedon [vilomakāvya] double-meaning [dvyarthakāvya] poem relating the story of Rāma in one direction, and that of Kṛṣṇa in the other; the mirror [pratiloma] of the sequence of syllables of its nominative form yamvidayāvagharāśrī "with which Lakṣmī sprinkled the residence with knowledge".

śrīrāma [Rāma] m. myth. np. of Srīrāma "Divine Rāma", respectful invocation of King Rāmacandra as incarnation [avatāra] of Vișnu | adr. soc. vaișnava salutation | soc. invocation of Rāma; its repetition is a merit; a tradition sets the goal of doing 10 million (1 koți) during one's lifetime.
śrīrāmanavamī [navamī] f. cf. rāmanavamī.
śrīrāmodanta [udanta] m. lit. poem in 200 śloka s, summary of the Rām., of unknown author; it was used in Kerala as the first Sanskrit reading book.

śrīvatsa [vatsa] m. myth. np. of śrīvatsa "Dear to Śrī", a loop of golden hair that adorns the left breast of Vișnu; this attribute is represented by a symbol in the shape of a fleur-de-lis | jn. frequent symbol on the chest of a tīrthankara | bd. arch. symbol associated with the triratna and the cakra, endless knot in the shape of a lattice or flower.

Śrīvara [vara] m. hist. n.p. of the pandita of Kaśmīra Śrīvara, student of Jonarāja (15th century); he continued his Rājāvali with the Jainarājataranginī, called the third [tṛtīyā] Rājataraṃgiṇī; it covers the period 1459 to 1486.
śrīvāstu |vāstu| f. geo. np. of the valley of the Srīvāstu river "Holy Residence", later became the Suvāstu.

Śrīvijaya [vijaya] m. hist. np. of the maritime empire of Śrīvijaya, based on the island of Sumatra; the ruling Sailendra dynasty had its capital at modern Palembang; it dominated maritime trade with China from the 7th to the 11th centuries.
śrīvidyā [vidyā] f. SOC. [Tantra] worship of Tripura sundarī using the śrīyantra; cf. Saundaryalaharī.
Śrīvidyānityapaddhati [nityapaddhati] f. bed. n.p. of the Śrīvidyānityapaddhati, guide to tantric ritual.
śrīvaiṣṇava [vaiṣṇava] m. SOC. follower of Rāmānuja.

Śrīśaila [śaila] mn geo. np. of Śrīśaila, plateau south of the Krsna River, in Andhra Pradesh, im bearing place of pilgrimage; in the temple of Mal likārjuna Mahālinga one of the 12 radiant signs of Shiva [jyotirlinga] is venerated; the temple of Bhra marāmbikā is a śaktipītha.

Śrīsūkta [sūkta] n. lit. np. of the Śrīsūkta, a devotional poem praising Lakṣmī; its hymns are found in the khilāni. śrīsūktāvalī [ āvalī ] f. lit. np. of the śrīsūktāvalī, a subhāṣitasamgraha of 192 verses, of unknown author and date.

śrīharṣa [harṣa] m. hist. np. of the poet and philosopher śrīharṣa (12th century), son of Hīra; he is the author of the mahākāvya Naisadhacarita and the treatise on advaita philosophy Khandanakhandakhādya | honorific name of King Harşa.
Śrīka [śrīka] amnf śrīkā fortune, prosperity; beauty.
śrīm part. phil. [Tantra] sound of the kamalābīja or śrībīja, bījamantra of evocation of the Goddess.
Śrīla [śrīla] amnf śrīlā prosperous, happy; eminent | SOC. np. of Śrīla "Blessed", Vaishnava title of respect.

√ śru v. [5] pr. (śrnóti) pr. r. (śrnuté) pft. (śuśrāva) aor. [3] (aśuśruvat) aor. [2] (aśravat) aor. ps. (aśrāvi) pp. (śruta) pfp. (śravya, śrotavya) abs. (śrutvā, śruya, śrāvam) inf. (śrotum) pf. (anu, ā, upa, prati, vi, sam) to hear | to learn something (acc.) from someone (g. abl. i.) | to listen, to learn, to study — ps. (śrūyate) to be heard; to be known; to be learned from a master — ca. (śrāvayati) pfp. (śrāvayitavya) to tell, recite, proclaim to (acc.) — des. (śuśrūṣati) des. r. (śuśrūṣate) to obey | gr. κλυω; lat. clutus; all. laut; ang. loud. śrūyatām interj. silence! listen! (ps. imp. "may it be heard"). śravat (inj.) he will have heard. śrosat véd. (subj.) may He hear us! śrnu me [Mah.] learn from me. śrnudhvam samāhitāh listen attentively. samprativārtāh śrūyantām please listen to the information. sa śuśruvāṃstadvacanam having heard these words.
śrut [agt. śru ] ifc. amnf who listens (iic.).
śrutkarṇa [karṇa] amnf śrutkarṇī ved. who is listening.

śruta [pp. śru] amnf śrutā listened to, heard, taught; known, famous, renowned; known as being | called (iti nom.) — n. act of hearing; knowledge, science | sacred science, revelation. śrutam tu sarvān atyeti | na śrutam atīyād adhi daivam athādhyātmam adhiyajñam iti trayam mantreșu brāhmaņe caiva śrutam ity abhidhīyate Revelation surpasses all; revelation must not be transgressed; it concerns the divine, but also the Self and sacrifice, the threefold (subject); only the hymns and their brāhmaṇa supplements are called revelation.
śrutakarman [karman] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Srutakarmā "of the famous exploits", son of Saha deva and Draupadī.

śrutakīrti [kīrti] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Srutakīrti "whose glory is famous", son of Arjuna and Drau padī — f. myth. [Rām.] np. of Srutakīrti₁, daughter of the king Kuśadhvaja₁; she married Satrughna.
śrutakevalin [kevalin] m. exceptional scholar.
śrutádeva [deva] m. "god of erudition", np. of man — f. śrutadevā myth. [Mah.] np. of Srutadevā, daughter of King Sūra, sister of Vasudeva.
Śrutanābha [nābha] m. myth. np. of Srutanābha "who possesses knowledge in the navel", king of Ayodhyā, son of Bhagīratha, father of Sind hudvīpa, ancestor of Raghu and therefore of Rāma.

śrutapañcamī [pañcamī] f. jn. festival commemorating the sacred texts of the jaina tradition, also ap pelée gurupañcamī, celebrated in the di gambara tradition on the 5th day of the month jyaistha; in the śvetāmbara tradition this festival is called jñānapañcamī, it is celebrated on the 5th day of the month kārttika; the sacred books are carried in procession.
śrutapāla [pāla] m. hist. np. from the grammarian śrutapāla "Guardian of knowledge".
Śrutabodha [bodha] m. phon. np. from the Śrutabodha, elementary manual of prosody; it is attributed to Kālidāsa or Vararuci.
śrutámaya [maya] amnf śrutamayī bd. fact of knowledge; concerning sacred tradition.
śrutaśarman [śarman] m. bed. [KSS.] np. of Srutaśarmā, king of geniuses [vidyādhara], protégé of Indra, adversary of Sūryaprabha.
śrutaśravas [śravas] m. "Glory of knowledge", np. of man — f. myth. [Mah.] np. of Srutaśravā, daughter of King Sūra, sister of Vasudeva; she married Damaghoșa, and gave birth to Śiśupāla.
śrutasena [senā] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of śrutasena "of the famous army", son of Sahadeva and Draupadī, also called Śrutakarmā | np. of many princes.
Śrutasoma [soma] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Srutasoma, son of Bhīma and Draupadī.
śrutānvita | anvita | amnf śrutānvitā endowed with Vedic knowledge.
Śrutāyudha [āyudha] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Śrutāyudha "armed with knowledge", son of the great

river [mahānadī] Parṇāśā and the god Varuṇa; at Parṇāśā's request, Varuṇa had given him a magical mace with the power to be invincible and immortal as long as he did not throw it at an unarmed man; he became king of Kamboja and took the side of the Kauravās; on the 14th day of the great battle, when Arjuna wanted to kill Jayadra tha, he intervened; his old age caused him to make the mistake of throwing his mace at the unarmed Kṛṣṇa, who took the mace on his chest, nullifying the magical power, and thus allowing Arjuna to kill him.

śrutārthā [artha] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of Srutārthā, daughter of the brahmin Somaśarmā; she embodies a nymph [apsaras] who descended to Earth as a result of a curse, like her brothers Vatsa and Gulma; seen bathing by the nāga Kīrtisena, and married in the gandharva fashion, she gave birth to Guṇāḍhya, ending the curses.
śrutārthāpatti [arthāpatti] f. phil. [Kumārila] implication from an ellipse; opp. dṛṣṭārthāpatti.
śrutavat [ppa. śru] amnf Śrutavatī who knows; scholar, who possesses knowledge — f. Śrutavatī myth. np. of Srutavatī "Scholar", wife of Bha radvāja; she devoted her life to the study of the Veda.

śruti [act. śru ] f. audition; ear | tradition, doctrine, knowledge; sacred teaching; revelation lit. the revealed word (opp. smṛti, the corpus of traditional texts) | soc. (mus.) division of the octave, quarter tone; 22 are listed, personified as nymphs.
śrutikrama | krama | m. phil. | Mīmāṃsā | series of instructions to achieve the goal.
Śrutitattvaprakāśikā [tattvaprakāśikā] f. lit. np. of the Srutitattvaprakāśikā, work of Vādirāja reinterpreting the aphorisms of the esoteric lessons |upanisad| according to the dvaita doctrine.
śrutidhara [dhara] amnf śrutidharā expert in Veda | able to memorize instantly.
śrútimat [mat] amnf śrutimatī endowed with ears | scholar | soc. conforming to the Veda.
śrútimaya [maya] amnf śrutimayī soc. according to the Veda.
śrutya [pfp. [1] śru] amnf śrutyā which must be listened to. সূবো śrutvā [abs. śru] ind. having heard; having learned.
średhī [related to śreni] f. math. progression; series.

śreņi [śrini] f. line, row, queue; series, group, class; troop, multitude | swarm (bees) guild (merchants), company (artists), corporation (craftsmen) | var. śrenī id. śrenibhū to queue, to line up. śreniky to line up. śrenikrtāh arranged in series.
Śrenika [ka] m. incisor (tooth) | hist. n.p. of Srenika, epith. of King Bimbisāra.
śrenya [śrenia] m. hist. [Buddhacarita] np. of King śrenya of Magadha, contemporary of Prince Siddhārtha; cf. Bimbisāra.
średdhī f. sequence of different objects | math. arithmetic progression.
średdhīphala [phala] n. math. sum of an arithmetic progression.
śremán [śrīman] m. distinction, superiority; splendor. sūryasya paśya śremāṇam yo na tandrayate caran [AB.] Admire the splendor of the Sun which never tires of turning.

śréyas [compar. śrī] amnf śreyasī more beautiful, better, preferable; excellent; propitious, favorable — adv. better — n. better condition, well-being, happiness; salvation | phil. [KU.] the preferable path, which leads to salvation; opp. preyas the path of pleasures, which leads to perdition — f. śreyasī good wife. śreyas ... na ... better ... than ... śreyaśca preyaśca the best and the agreeable. satyād apyanṛtaṃ śreyas [Ve.] The lie is still better than the truth. śreyaśca preyaśca manusyametastau samparītya vi vinakti dhīraḥ | śreyo hi dhīro'bhi preyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yogakṣemādvṛṇīte | [KU.] Both good and pleasure present themselves to man; having examined them, the discerning man distinguishes them; the intelligent man prefers good; the fool prefers pleasure for his well-being.
śréyaskara [kara₁] amnf śreyaskarī which improves; which makes excellent.
śreyasa [śreyasa] ifc. n. well-being, happiness, salvation from (iic.).
śreyāṃsa [śreyasaṃsa] m. jn. n.p. of Śreyāmsa; cf. Śreyāmsanātha.

śreyāṃsanātha [nātha] m. jn. of np. Sreyāṃsanātha "Best of Masters", 11th mythical tīrthankara; his body is golden yellow, his symbol is an eagle, a deer, or a rhinoceros. শ্বষ্ট śreṣṭha [super. śrī] amnf śreṣṭhā Best, excellent at something (loc.) | the first, the Best, the most beautiful among (g. iic.) | the eldest — m. king; brahmin | myth. epith. of Kubera or Viṣṇu — n. cow's milk — f. śreṣṭhā excellent woman. dhanvinām śrestha the Best of Archers. munisrestha Best among the wise.
śresthatama |tama| amnf śresthatamā super. The best, the supreme.
śreṣṭhatara |tara| amnf śreṣṭhatarā compar. Best. na hi mānuṣācchreṣṭhataraṃ hi kiñcit [Mah.] There is nothing superior to man.

śreṣṭhin [śreṣṭhain] m. the Best (craftsman), head of a guild [śreni] | merchant, craftsman bd. treasurer; banker, lender. শ্বীষ্ট্রয śraiṣṭhya [*śreṣṭhaya] n. superiority | supremacy, preeminence, preeminence (among g. iic.)).
śroṇi [śruni] f. of. śroṇī cf. śroṇī.
śroṇī f. hip, buttock; cf. suśroṇī | du. hips, buttocks | gr. κλονις; lat. clūnis.
śrotavya [pfp. [3] śru] amnf śrotavyā worthy of being heard; which must be listened to — n. time to listen; obligation to listen | (imp.) one must listen.

śrotṛ [agt. śru] amnf śrotrī who listens — m. gram. listener; (opp. prayoktr speaker). শ্বীস śrótra [instr. śru] n. ear | phil. [Sāṃkhya] the sense [buddhīndriya] of hearing; it is governed [niyantr] by the Diśas; the associated perception [tanmātra] is sound [śabda]. śrotradywa dwaya n. pair of ears.
śrotrānupātin | anupātin | m. phon. (utterance) object of listening.
śrótriya [śrotraiya] amnf śrotriyā scholar, expert in Veda — m. soc. brahmin versed in the Veda; cf. anūcāna.
śrauta [*śrutia] amnf śrautā phil. in accordance with revealed knowledge; correct with regard to doctrine; said not. of solemn Vedic rites.
śrautasūtra [sūtra] n. phil. text of aphorisms summarizing the brāhmana texts for solemn rites; cf. Aśvalāyana, Baudhāyana, Vādhūla, Jai mini.
śrauṣaṭ [śru] ind. soc. ["may he (god, ancestor) hear us" ritual exclamation during the offering of the oblation in the fire.
śryartham [śrīartha] adv. for the purpose of prosperity.

ślakṣṇá [śliṣsna] amnf ślakṣṇā slippery, smooth, polished | tender, kind, delicate; small, thin, slender | honest, sincere — v. [11] pr. (ślakṣṇayati) to make slippery; to polish; to thin. ślakṣṇam adv. gently, delicately, kindly. ślakṣṇīkṛ to polish.
ślakṣṇátara [tara] amnf ślakṣṇátarā compar. very slippery; very smooth. ślakṣṇátā [tā] f. softness; the state of being smooth or slippery.
√ স্থে ślath [related to śrath] v. [1] pr. (ślathati) pr. r. (ślathate) to be free; to slump — ca. (ślathayati) ca. (ślathayati) to untie, release, free.

ślatha [agt. ślath] amnf ślathā free, loose, unbound; relaxed; disordered (hair); detached; soft, weak — f. ślathā type of tall, thin, fair-skinned woman, not very sexually active; opp. ghanā. ślathatva |tva| n. relaxation; slackening.
√ ślāgh v. [1] pr. r. (ślāghate) pp. (ślāghita) to praise, to celebrate (dat.). nṛpāya ślāghate bandī the bard praises the king.

√ śliş v. [4] pr. (ślisyati) pr. r. (ślisyate) pp. (śliṣṭa) abs. (śliṣṭvā, śliṣya) pf. (ā, pra, vi, sam) to cling, adhere, be fixed to (loc. acc.) | to surround, embrace — ca. (ślesayati) to unite, join. puṣkarapalāśa āpo na ślisyanta yathā evamevamvidi pāpam karma na ślisyate [ChU.] Just as water does not adhere to the lotus leaves, so too does sin not adhere to one who knows this.
śliṣā [act. śliṣ ] f. adhesion. ਇਲਾ ślista [pp. ślis] amnf ślistā surrounded, embraced, embraced | attached, adherent; that embraces, that embraces.
ślistapriya [priya] amnf ślistapriyā who embraces his beloved.
ślīla var. śrīra amnf ślīlā prosperous; rich; lucky; happy.
slu nota. gram. modifier |vikaraṇa₂| of formation of the athematic present of gana 3 | juhotyādi|, with reduplication.

ślesa [act. ślis] m. union, junction, embrace; amalgamation; coalescence | lit. rhet. double meaning, verbal ambiguity, wordplay; paronomasia; oronym; multiple interpretation of a text; three types are distinguished: sabhangaślesa, abhangaślesa, and ubhayaślesa. śabdaih svabhāvādekārthaih ślese'nekārthavācanam In ślesa style, multiple meanings are expressed by words that naturally have a single meaning.
ślesakāvya [kāvya] n. bed. double meaning poetry; cf. vilomakāvya. ślesana [na] ifc. n. mixture, alloy of (iic.).
ślesarūpaka [rūpaka] n. bed. syn. ślesopamā.
ślesopamā [upamā₁] f. lit. comparison using ślesa for the respective meanings of the compared and the comparator.
śleşma iic. śleşman.
ślesmāntaka | antaka | amnf ślesmāntakā which removes phlegm — m. cf. ślesmātaka.
śleṣmán [śleṣaman] m. med. mucus; phlegm, one of the 3 humors [tridoṣa]; syn. kapha — n. cord, band, thread.
ślesmātaka [ślesmāntaka] m. bio. bot. Cor dia dichotoma, tree with lanceolate leaves, white flowers, brown clusters with viscous pulp; its bark and fruits are used in medicine.

śloka [related to śru] m. stanza, heroic verse (not. couplet of two hemistichs, forming 4 pādās of 8 feet); its invention is attributed to Vālmīki; its meter is a variety of anustubh₂ | unit of text length, worth 32 syllables.
ślokatva [tva] n. poetry. śokah ślokatvam āgatah [Rām.] The sorrow (of Vālmīki at the sight of the despair of the krauñca bird losing its companion killed by a hunter) of vint poetry.
ślokadvaya [dvaya] n. couple of stanzas.

Ślokavārttika | vārttika | n. bed. kind of vārttika; cf. Kātyāyana | bed. n.p. from the Slokavārttika or Tan travārttika, the mīmāmsā work of Kumārila; Su carita Miśra glossed it Kāśikā₁. ষ śva iic. śvan₁.
śvagana | gana | m. pack of hunting dogs.
śvaganika |ika| amnf śvaganikī who uses a pack — m. huntsman.
śvaghnin |ghna| m. Vedic. chief of a Vrātya clan, chosen by the game of dice; he must produce a ti
rage |glaha| whose remainder modulo 4 is 1 |kali|; he embodies kaliRudra and leads the group.
śvacaryā | caryā | f. | "dog's life" | slavery, servitude; this way of life is unsuitable for the brahmin |satkarman|.
śvajana [jana| m. canine gent | dog.
śvadamstrā [damstrā] f. dog tooth.
śvapaca | paca | amnf śvapacī soc. horscaste; he is employed as an executioner, and cremates the corpses.

śvapada | pada | n. dog's foot | soc. brand of a dog's foot, applied with an iron to the forehead of thieves. śunah pādam ayomayam branding iron with a dog's foot. śvapāka | pāka | amnf śvapākī soc. | "dog eater" (pej.) outcaste; cf. śvapaca.
śvaphalka | phalka | m. myth. np. of the Yādava prince Svaphalka, son of Pṛṣṇi, father of Akrūra.
śvavat [vat] amnf śvavatī accompanied by a dog — m. dog breeder; dog owner. svarge loke śvavatām nāsti dhiṣṇyam [Mah.] There is no room in heaven for someone with a dog.

śvavrtti [vrtti] f. ["dog's life"] slavery, servitude; this way of life is unsuitable for the Brahmin |satkarman|. śváśarīra | śarīra | n. his own body — amnf śvaśarīrā (in heaven) with his own body. ষ্ব্ śvan₁ m. [fb. śun; obl. śvān; nom. śvā, acc. śvānam dog arch. the dog, a yoni matrix of the āyādi system — f. śunī bitch || gr. κυον; lat. canis; all. Hund; ang. hound; fr. chien. ষ্বন্ śvan₂ [śū] ifc. m. that swells, that grows. ষ্ঠা śvábhra mn crevasse, trough, well, abyss — m. myth. hell.
śvábhramat |mat| amnf śvabhramatī that makes holes; perforated, hollow — f. śvabhramatī geo. np. of the śvabhramatī river in Gurjara; mod. Sabarmatī.

śvayathu [śūathu] m. swelling, tumors cence. ষ্মুং śváśura m. father-in-law (father of one’s spouse) | of. śvaśurau au parents-in-law || lat. soccer. ষসু śvaśrū [related to śvaśura] f. mother-in-law (mother of one's partner) | lat. socrus. śvaśrūśvaśura | śvaśura | mr. of. in-laws. śvaśrūsnuṣā [ snuṣā ] f. of. mother-in-law and daughter-in-law.
√ষ্ব ধ্ śvas₁ v. [2] pr. (śvásiti) v. [1] pr. (śvásati) pr. r. (śvasate) pp. (śvásita) pf. (ā, ut, ni, nis, pra, vi) breathe, pant; blow, whistle — ca. (śvāsayati) to blow.

śvás₂ adv. tomorrow | in the future. śvah śvah day after day; further and further away. śvo bhūte the next day. śvaḥ kartā it will be done tomorrow. nakaścidapi jānāti kim kasya śvo bhavişyati | ataḥ śvaḥ karaṇīyāni kuryādadyaiva buddhimān || No one knows what tomorrow will bring; therefore, the wise person does not put off until tomorrow what they can do today.

śvástana |tana| amnf śvastanī du lende main — n. tomorrow; the next day; the future — f. śvastanī the next day | gram. periphrastic future tense; cf. luț | lat. crastinus; fr. procras tiner. śvastane 'hani the next day.
śvasana |agt. śvas₁| amnf śvasanā that whistles; that blows; that pants — n. breath; respiration; sigh | hiss; not. hiss of a snake — m. air; wind; bodily flow.
śvasanabhuj [bhuj₃] m. snake ["that feeds on air"]; syn. pavanāśana.
śvasita [pp. śvas₁] amnf śvasitā res piré, sighed | full of life, vivified — n. breathing, breathing; sigh. ষ্বা śvā [noun. śvan₁] iic.
śvāpada | pada | m. carnivorous quadruped | "dog-footed"; wild beast. siṃhaḥ sarvaśvāpadeṣu baliṣṭhaḥ The lion is the strongest of animals.
śvāvidh [vidh₂] m. ["spiky dog"] porcupine | var. śvāvidha id.
śvāna [*śvan₁a] mf śvānī dog.
śvānanidrā [nidrā₁] amnf śvānanidrā who has a light sleep — f. śvānanidrā ["dog sleep"] light sleep.

śvānamāra | māra | m. bio. | "tuechien" | bot. Cer bera odollam, an apocynaceae tree of the Western Ghats, with white flowers with 5 petals, and a fruit resembling a mango; its latex and seeds are deadly poisons.
śvāvit iic. śvāvidh.
śvāviccharaṇa [śaraṇa] n. porcupine's den.
śvāsa [act. śvas₁] m. whistling; panting, sniffling | breathing; inspiration | sigh | med. difficulty breathing, asthma.
śvāsatā |tā| f. act of being sucked in | respiration, aspiration.
śvāsin [agt. śvas₁] amnf śvāsinī who is worse; who whistles | asthmatic | gram. aspirated (letter) — m. vent.
śvit₁ [śvit₁] ifc. n. (iic.) white. ষির śvitra [śvit₁ra] mn med. leukoderma, viti ligo (white leprosy).

śveta [agt. śvit₁] amnf śvetā f. śvenī white, clear — m. white horse | myth. [Mah.] np. of Sveta "the white one", invincible brother of Uttara; he attacked King Salya, but Bhīsma annihilated him with the brahmāstra weapon | myth. [Rām.] np. of Mount White Sveta₁, formed from the sperm of Shiva penetrated by Agni; at its foot is the bamboo grove where Skanda was born — f. śvetā myth. np. of Sveta, daughter of Kaśyapa and Krodhavaśā; she gave birth to the race of horses.
śvetakāka [kāka] m. ["white crow"] (fig.) extraordinary thing.
śvetakākīya [īya] amnf śvetakākīyā rare, exceptional; extraordinary, incredible.

śvetaketu [ketu] m. phil. [ChU.] np. of śvetaketu "of the white standard", young brahmin who, returning from his guru at the end of his Vedic studies, learned from his father Uddālaka Aruņi that he knew nothing, but that it was enough to understand "you are that" (tat tvam asi); [KB.] he became a maharși, master [ācārya] of the rules of sacrifice [yajña]; [Mah.] he instituted the rules of marriage, after an old man wanted to borrow his mother from his father in order to have such a beautiful son | myth. np. of Svetaketu₁, first disciple of Sāndīpani; he fell in love with the beautiful princess Śaibyā.
śvetadvīpa [dvīpa] m. myth. np. of Švetadvīpa the "White Island", place where Vișnu resides in the middle of the ocean of milk [kṣīrodadhi].

śvetaraśmi [raśmi] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the magical white elephant Svetaraśmi, endowed with supernatural powers, such as moving through the air; very intelligent, he remembered his previous existences; Vișnu gave him as a mount to King Ratnādhipati; wounded by an eagle, he lost consciousness; a heavenly voice told the king that he would only recover if he was touched by a woman faithful to her husband; the test failed for the 80,000 women of the gycenaeum, then for all the women of the island; only the slave Silāvatī of the merchant Harşagupta from Tāmraliptī made him rise again; the king decided to marry his sister Rājadattā; he neglected the advice of his astrologers to wait three months, and installed her on a deserted island; A shipwrecked man took refuge there, and took advantage of Rājadattā's drunkenness to possess her; the king, grieved, renounced his kingdom, which he left to the Brahmin Pāpabhanjana; he wanted to become a hermit, called Švetaraśmi, but the latter transformed into a man of divine beauty, and revealed that he was the gandharva Somaprabha, that the king was his elder brother Devaprabha, whose wife Rājavatī had seduced an ascetic with her song; suspected of evil thoughts, he had cursed all three of them in their present conditions, and the term having arrived, all ended well.
śvetavāhana [vāhana] m. myth. de np. Svetavāhana, epith. of Arjuna "to the white of the sorting".
śvetāmbara | ambara | amnf śvetāmbarā jn. "clothed in white", epith. of the Jain sect of the śvetāmbarās (opp. digambara).
śvetārka [arka] m. bio. botanical variety of Calatropis gigantea with white flowers; these are borne by Siva.
śvetāśva |aśva| m. white horse — amnf śvetāśvā who has white horses — m. lit. |Mah.| epith. of Arjuna "to the chariot drawn by white horses".
śvetāśvatara [aśvatara] m. hist. np. of the sage Švetāśvatara "of the white mules", presumed author of the Svetāśvataropaniṣad.
śvetāśvataropaniṣad [upaniṣad] f. lit. np. of the esoteric lesson Svetāśvataropaniṣad "Lesson of (the man with) white mules"; it questions the ultimate nature of reality.
Śvetāśvataropaniṣadbhāṣya [bhāṣya] n. bed. n.p. of the Śvetāśvataropaniṣadbhāṣya, commentary on the śvetāśvataropaniṣad; tradition attributes it to Sankara₁.
śvetaka [śvetaka] amnf śvetakā whitish; white — m. cowrie shell; syn. kaparda — n. money.

śvetaki m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the overly pious King Švetaki, who exhausted his priests by demanding incessant sacrifices; on the orders of Shankara, Durvāsā performed a great sacrifice for him lasting 12 years, causing Agni to suffer indigestion; Brahmā advised Agni to cure himself by burning the Khāṇḍava forest; cf. khāṇḍavadahana. s
Ṣakāra [(ṣa)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'ṣa'.
sat iic. sas.
saṭka |ka| amnf ṣaṭkā consisting of 6 com posantes, of symmetry 6 | which has learned after 6 repetitions — n. half-dozen; category of 6 ob jets | lit. not. poem in 6 verses.
saṭkasampatti [sampatti] f. pl. phil. [Vedānta] the 6 perfections, or aptitudes required of the aspi

rant [adhikārin]: control of one's mind [śama], control of one's senses [dama], renunciation of the world [uparama], endurance [titikṣā], faith [śraddhā₂] and stability of mind [samādhāna]; syn. satsampad.

satkarman | karman | m. soc. brahmin who practices the ṣaṭkarmāni — n. pl. ṣaṭkarmāni soc. the 6 duties of a brahmin: adhyayana the recitation of the Veda, adhyāpana the teaching of the Veda, ya jana the celebration of sacrifice (for oneself), yājana the performance of sacrifice (for others), dāna the giving of alms, and pratigraha the acceptance of offerings; a brahmin of lower rank [trikarmin] may only perform adhyayana, yajana and dāna | The six daily religious duties: snāna (ritual bath), saṃdhyājapa (prayer at the three sacred times [saṃdhyā]), brahmayajña (worship of Brahman), tarpana (libation to the spirits), homa (offering at the hearth), devapūjā (rite of divine worship) | The six means of subsistence suitable or unsuitable for a Brahmin: rta (gleaning), amrta (unsolicited almsgiving), mrta (solicited almsgiving), karṣaṇa or anrta (farming), satyānrta (trade), and śvavrtti (servitude) | The six mortifications of yoga: dhautī, vastī, netī, trāṭaka, naulika, and kapālabhātī | Phil. | Tantra | the 6 evil rites: śānti, vaśya, stambhana, vidvesa, uccāṭana, and māraṇa.
satkrtvas [krtvas] adv. six times.
satkona [kona] n. hexagon | myth. the vajra of In dra.
satkhanda [khanda] amnf satkhandā consisting of 6 parts.
satkhandāgama |āgama| n. jn. np. of the Satkhandāgama, the oldest sacred script of the digambarās; it is attributed to the ascetic Dharasena₁.

satcakra [cakra] n. phil. [Tantra] the 6 centers of psychic energy: mūlādhāra, svādhiṣṭhāna, manipūra, anāhata, viśuddha, and ājñā₂. satcakranirūpaņa [nirūpaṇa] n. lit. np. from tan tra Şatcakranirūpaņa "Investigation of the 6 psychic centers", esoteric text dealing with mystical anatomy.
satcatvārimsa [catvārimsa] mnfa satcatvārimšī ord. 46°.
satcatvārimsat | catvārimsat | f. 46.
satcarana [carana] amnf satcaranī with 6 legs — m. insect; not. bee.
sattrimsa | trimsa | amnf sattrimsī ord. 36e consisting of 36 parts. şattrimásat | trimásat | f. 36.
sattrimśattama |tama| amnf sattrimśattamī ord. 36ᵉ.
sattrimśati | trimśati | f. 36.
satpañcāśa | pañcāśa | amnf satpañcāśī ord. 56^ e.
satpañcāśat | pañcāśat | f. 56.
satpañcāśattama |tama| afmn satpañcāśattamī ord. 56ᵉ.
satpada | padah | amnf satpadā f. 6-legged satpadī — m. insect; not. bee.
satpadajya | jyā₃ | m. myth. epith. of Kāma "with a bow whose string is made of bees".
satpala | pala | m. pl. med. the six peppers and salt, including the five spices |pañcakola| and rock salt; cf. indukāntaghṛta.
satsasti |sasti| f. 66.
satsaptata |saptata| amnf satsaptatī ord. 76°.
satsaptati |saptati| f. 76.
satsaptatitama |tama| amnf satsaptatitamī ord. 76ᵉ.
satsampad [sampad₂] f. phil. [Vedānta] the 6 cardinal virtues: śama tranquility, dama self-control, uparati contemplation, titikṣā patience, śraddhā ₂ faith and samādhāna stability of mind.
sad iic. sas. șadanga |anga₁| amnf șadangā composed of 6 parts.
sadangayoga [Yoga] m. bed. n.p. of Ṣaḍangayoga, treatise bd. by Anupamaraksita.

sadangaśilpa | śilpa | n. phil. The plastic art judged in 6 aesthetic canons: rūpabheda the science of forms, pramāņa the sense of proportions, bhava the expression of feeling, lāvaṇyayojana the sense of grace, sadrsya the sense of resemblance, and varnikabhanga the science of colors.
sadanghri | anghri | m. lit. | "having 6 legs" | bee.
sadasīta |asīta| amnf sadasītī ord. 86°.
sadaśīti |aśīti| f. 86.
ṣaḍaśītitama |tama| amnf ṣaḍaśītitamī ord. 86^ e.
sadāmnāya |āmnāya| m. soc. |Kaula| association of the śākta deities with the 6 directions of space.
sadāyatana |āyatana| n. bd. the 6 sensory perceptions, including the 5 senses and thought |manas|; they form the 5th cause of suffering |pratītyasamutpāda|.
sadrtu | rtu | m. pl. sadrtavah the 6 seasons.

sadguna [guna] m. pl. the 6 qualities, perceived by the 5 senses and the mind [manas] | the 6 personal excellences | soc. the 6 royal means of action in foreign policy: alliance [samdhi], war [vigraha], expedition/invasion [yāna], the
seat [āsana], division of forces [dvaidhībhāva] and allegiance to a more powerful king [samśraya].
sadja [ja] m. (mus.) ["derived from 6 (organs)"] 1st note of the Indian octave, with ṛṣabha, gāndhāra, madhyama, pañcama, dhaivata and niṣāda.
saddhotr [hotr] m. pl. saddhotāras ved. the 6 priests who sacrificed for whom? (classic question of a ritual riddle [brahmodya]).

saddarśana [darśana] n. phil. [Mādhava] encompasses the 6 orthodox doctrinal viewpoints of Hinduism: logic or dialectic [Nyāya] which studies the means of knowledge, systematics [Vaisesika] which classifies concepts, the evolutionary discrimination of substances [sānkhya], the practice of ritual spiritual communion |Yoga|, hermeneutics or exegesis of Vedic ritual [Mīmāṃsā] and the culmination of the Veda [Vedānta] or non-dualistic philosophy — amnf saddarśanī who is competent in the 6 doctrines.

saddarśanasamuccaya [samuccaya] m. bed. n.p. from the Ṣaḍdarśanasamuccaya "Compendium of the 6 points of view", doxographic work by Harib hadra; he gives the list of 6 orthodox systems |āstika| : bauddha, Nyāya, sānkhya, jaina, vaišesika and mīmāṃsā, contrasted with atheistic materialism |lokāyata|.

saddharma [dharma] m. bd. [Mahāyāna] the 6 stages of the practice of Tantric Yoga: caṇḍālī or Yoga of ardent fervor, prabhāsavara or Yoga of radiance, svapnadarśana or Yoga of lucid dreaming, māyākāya or Yoga of the illusory nature of the phenomenal world, antarābhava or Yoga of the intermediate state, and saṃkrānti or Yoga of the transfer of consciousness where one reaches the state of awakening [buddha]; its teaching was transmitted from Tilopa to Nāropa, then to Marpa who added karmamudrā, and through Milarepa and Gampopa gave birth to the Kagyūpa school of Tibetan yoga.
saddhātusamīkṣā [dhātusamīkṣā] f. gram. n.p. from the Ṣaḍdhātusamīkṣā "Examination of 6 Roots", a work by Bhartrhari now lost.

sadbhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. pl. bed. the 6 languages of India; to the original triad | bhāṣātraya | including samskṛta, prākṛta and apabhraṃśa, Rudraṭa added śaurasenī, māgadhī and paiśācī. prākṛtasaṃskṛtamāgadhapiśācabhāṣaś ca sūrasenī sastho 'tra bhūribhedo deśaviśesād apabhramśah [Kāvyālaṃkāra₂] Prakrit, Sanskrit, māgadhī, paiśācī and śaurasenī, with apabhraméa, are here the 6 main subdivisions of the language according to the country of origin.

Sadbhuja [bhuja] amnf sadbhujā which has 6 arms math. which has 6 sides; hexagon — m. myth. np. of Sadbhuja, which combines three incarnations of Vișnu: Rāma with the bow and arrow, Kṛṣṇa with the flute and a branch, and Caitanya with the staff and the water pot of the ascetics.

sadbhujagaurānga [gaurānga] myth. m. deified representation of Caitanya with the two arms of Rāma holding the bow and arrow, the two arms of Kṛṣṇa playing the flute, and the two arms of the ascetic carrying the water pot |kamaṇḍalu| and the staff [yogadanda]. şadripu | ripu | m. pl. phil. the 6 sins that are enemies of man: lust [kāma], avarice [lobha], anger [krodha], pride [mada], attachment to the phenomenal world [moha], and envy [matsara].
ṣaḍvaktra [vaktra] amnf ṣaḍvaktrī which has six mouths or six heads — m. myth. epith. of Skanda "with 6 heads".
sadvarga [varga] m. the 6 categories; cf. arişadvarga, āyādişadvarga.

sadvimsat [vimsat] f. 26.
sadvimsati [vimsati] f. 26.
ṣaḍvidhāna [vidhāna] amnf ṣaḍvidhānā of order 6; in rank by 6.
san iic. sas.

√ san₁ v. [8] pr. (sanoti) pp. (sāta) to acquire, obtain, possess | to procure, give, distribute — ps. (sanyate) ps. (sāyate) to succeed, obtain — ca. (sānayati) to cause to obtain — des. (sisānayiṣati) to desire to obtain.
sannavata [navata] amnf sannavatī ord. 96°. şannavati [navati] f. 96.
ṣaṇṇavatitama |tama| amnf ṣaṇṇavatitamī ord. 96ᵉ.

ṣaṇmata [mata] n. soc. system of "6 doctrines", founded by Sankara₁ as a syncretistic religion of 6 principal deities: Śiva, Viṣṇu, Durgā, Gaṇeśa, Sūrya and Skanda; the first 5 are offered the pañcāyatana pūjā.
ṣaṇmatasthāpaka [sthāpaka] m. soc. founder of the system of 6 doctrines, said of Sankara₁, called thus Sanmatasthāpakācārya. saņmāsa | māsa | m. semester.

sanmukha [mukha] m. myth. np. of Sanmukha, epithet of Skanda "with 6 heads". şanmukhakalpa [kalpa] m. lit. np. of the Sanmukhakalpa "Treatise of Skanda", teaching the art of the thief [cauryaśāstra]. প্ত sanda ifc. mn ifc. group, heap, collection, bouquet, quantity of (iic.) | not. bush, grove, wood — m. free-roaming bull. প্ত Sandha m. eunuch; impotent; so-called hermaphrodite; syn. klība, paṇḍa | myth. [Mah.] np. of Ṣaṇḍha "Hermaphrodite", a son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra | arch. the eunuch, a part [aṃsa] of the āyādi system — n. gram. neuter gender — f. ṣaṇḍhī refers to the
vulva [yoni] of an immature woman — v. [11] pr. (sandhayati) to castrate, emasculate.
satva [(sa)tva] n. phon. retroflexion of the letter 's'.

satvanatva [natva] n. phone. retroflection of the letter 's' or the letter 'n'. airlock number. pers. pl. [name. acc. ṣaṭ, i. ṣaḍbhis, dat. abl. ṣaḍbhyas, g. ṣaṇṇām, loc. ṣaṭsu; in comp. ṣaṭ, sad, san the number six | lat. sex; all. dried; eng. six; fr. six. sat ind. 6 times. প্ত sasta [ṣaṣta] ifc. amnf ṣaṣṭī sixty (iic.) th. প্তি saṣṭi [ṣaṣti] num. f. sg. sixty.

sastika [ka] amnf sastikā relating to 60 — f. şaştikā variety of rice that is harvested after 60 days. şaştyabda | abda | m. astr. 60-year cycle of Jupiter [Guru] (actually of the conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn); the years are named in 60 saṃvatsarās — f. ṣaṣṭyabdī soc. life cycle, of 60 years, aligned with the previous one | soc. rite of departure in
retirement [vānaprastha] at age 60. পষ্ট saṣṭha [ṣaṣtha] amnf ṣaṣṭhī ord. sixth — f. cf. sasthī. ekaşaştha 61ᵉ (after num. id. dvāşaştha etc.).
saṣṭhāṃśa [aṃśa] m. the 6th part; the tax of the sixth.

sasthī [f. sastha] f. 6th day of a lunar month gram. genitive (6th case of declension) myth. tantr. np. of Ṣaṣṭhī, goddess protecting newborns; she is honored on the 6th day after a birth, notably in Bengal; she is associated with Skanda; she is represented as a wet nurse carrying children |sūtikā|, often with 6 heads, sometimes with
wings [pakṣaṣaṣṭhī]; his mount is a cat.
sasthītatpurusa [tatpurusa] m. gram. compound possessive determiner word, the first member of which has the value of a genitive.

ṣāḍjguṇya [*ṣaḍguṇaya] n. soc. the 6 royal means of action in matters of foreign policy; cf. sadguna. পাষ্ট ṣāṣṭha [*ṣaṣṭha] amnf ṣāṣṭhā (fraction) one sixth. পিদ্ধ sidga amnf sidgā lascivious, lewd — m. debauched; pimp.
sodaśá [sodaśan] amnf sodaśī ord. sixteenth — f. sodaśā ifc. id. — n. 1/16 — f. sodaśī myth. np. of Ṣoḍaśī "the sixteenth", a terrible [mahāvidyā] aspect of Durgā; also called Rājarājeśvarī.

sodaśagrantha | grantha | m. pl. lit. np. of the Sodasagranthas, a collection of 16 texts by Val labhācārya explaining the pustimārga devotional path; it is also called Vallabhagītā. sodaśadhā [dhā] adv. of 16 ways | in 16 parts.
sodaśādhāra [ādhāra] m. phil. [yoga] the "sixteen supports" of meditation or points of fixation [dhāraṇā] of thought: the toes [aṅguṣṭha], the
ankles [gulpha], knees [jānu], thighs [ūru], perineal raphe [sīvanī], penis [linga], navel [nābhi], heart [hṛd], the
nape of the neck [grīvā], the throat [kaṇṭha], the veil of the pa
lais [lambikā], the nostrils [nāsikā], the space between the eyebrows |bhrūmadhya|, the forehead |lalāṭa|, the head [mūrdhan], and the fontanelle or opening of Brahmā [brahmarandhra].
ṣoḍaśaka [ṣoḍaśaka] amnf ṣoḍaśikā in 16 parts — n. aggregate of 16.
ṣoḍaśan [ṣaṣdaśan] num. pers. name. sodaśa] sixteen.
ṣoḍaśin [ṣoḍaśan] amnf ṣoḍaśinī which has sixteen parts.
soddhala m. hist. n.p. by the kāyastha poet Şoddhala of Lāṭa, author of the Udayasundarīkathā in campū style (around 1000).
sodhā [ṣaṣdhā] adv. in 6 ways | 6 times.
√ sthīv var. sthiv v. [1] pr. (sthīvati) v. [4] pr. (sthīvyati) pp. (sthyūta) pf. (ni) spit, expecto rer | eng. spew.
sthīvana [act. sthīv] n. spit; saliva | the act of spitting on (loc.). ষ্থ্র sthyūta [pp. sthīv] amnf sthyūtā spat out, expectorated — n. spit. S

sa₁ pf. (for saha₂) with, having, equipped with, including | (for samāna₂) similar to. sakṣatram adv. as befits a kṣatriya. sacakram adv. simultaneously. sataddhitam adhīte adv. he studies up to (chapter of the) secondary suffix. salakşmi adv. behaving like Lakşmī. savīņam adv. like a vīņā.

sa₂ [m. tad] pn. 3rd pers. m. [sg. nom. sas, acc. tam; du. nom. acc. tau; pl. nom. te, acc. tān; other cases cf. tad | he; this, that; that ... there, that ... there, that one | (with personal pronoun) oneself | [correl. of ya₁] (he who) ... he. so'ham myself. sa tvā pṛcchāmi it is I who ask you. sa tvam yourself. sa vai no brūhi tell us really yourself. sa ... ābhara yourself ... bring (demonstrative agreement sa with 2nd pers.).
saka |ka| amnf sakā him who.
saṃyát [samyat₂] amnf coherent; contiguous; continuous, uninterrupted — f. convention, agreement | conflict, battle, war.
saṃyata [pp. saṃyam] amnf saṃyatā restricted, constrained, repressed, subjugated; restrained, in a strait, chained.
saṃyatātman [ātman] amnf saṃyatātmanī who controls his mind.
samyatendriya [indriya] amnf samyatendriyā who controls his senses.
saṃyam [samyam] v. [1] pr. (saṃyacchati) pp. (samyata) to restrain, restrain, repress, control; to attach, chain.

saṃyama [act. saṃyam] m. bond; restricted, discipline, abstinence, self-control | suppression, annihilation; abstention from (loc. abl.) | phil. [yoga] concentration and contemplation, combining dhāraṇā, dhyāna, and samādhi.
samyamat [agt. samyam] amnf
saṃyamantī [BhG] who disciplines (like Yama the judge of the dead).
saṃyamana [act. saṃyam] n. restricted, discipline | self-control, self-discipline. mayā raśmisaṃyamanād rathasya mandīkṛto vegaḥ the chariot slowed down because I tightened the reins.
saṃyamin [agt. saṃyam] amnf samyaminī who has ties; who disciplines himself | who has tamed his senses; master of himself.
samyā [samyā₁] v. [2] pr. (samyāti) pp. (saṃyāta) to go, to advance towards.
saṃyu [samyu₁] v. [2] pr. (saṃyauti) pp. (saṃyuta) ved. to join to oneself, to take into oneself | to join with, to unite with (i.); to unite with.

sáṃyukta [pp. saṃyuj₁] amnf saṃyuktā united, bound; joined, joined, combined; married to (i.); placed, assigned to (loc.) | accompanied by, provided with, possessing (i. iic.) | phon. (vowel) compound ('e', 'ai', 'o', 'au'); contiguous consonants — ifc. connected to (iic.); related to, concerning (iic.).
saṃyuktasvara [svara] m. diphthong.
samyuktākṣara [akṣara] n. gram. ligature.
saṃyuktāgama [āgama] m. bed. n.p. from Sa myuktāgama, comic text. of Sarvāstivāda tradition
samyuktābhidharmahrdaya [Abhidharmahrdaya] from Saṃyuktābhidharmahṛdaya, lit. n.p. mr. bd. of Dharmatrāta, which extends the work of Abhidharmahrdaya₂.
saṃyuga [act. saṃyuj₁] mn union, conjunction | confrontation; combat, battle, war.

saṃyuj₁ [samyuj₁] v. [7] pr. (saṃyunákti) pp. (samyukta) to unite, join, combine, bind — ca. (saṃyojayati) to gather; to bring into contact, to unite; to harness, equip; to dominate, to subdue (one's senses); to provide with (i.); to entrust (acc.) to (g.); to accomplish — pr. r. (saṃyuṅkté) to meditate.
saṃyuj₂ [obj. saṃyuj₁] amnf joint; unified; connected, linked — act. m. relation — f. union, connection.
saṃyuta [pp. saṃyu] amnf saṃyutā bound together, joined | var. saṃyutta f. saṃyuttā id. — ifc. in conjunction with (iic.). samyutta hastau joined hands.
saṃyutamudrā | mudrā | f. posture with two joined hands; cf. añjali.
saṃyutahasta | hasta| amnf saṃyutahastā refers to a symbolic gesture | mudrā| with two hands; opp. asamyutahasta.
samyoga [act. samyuj₁] m. union, combination, association; opp. vibhāga | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] the

property [guṇa] of union | phil. [Nyāya] conjunction | gram. group of contiguous consonants; ligature | gram. association between two notions, allowing the mutual disambiguation of their signifiers; syn. samsarga. dravyayoreva saṃyogaḥ [Nyāya] The contact relation exists only between two substances.
saṃyogavibhāga [vibhāga] m. of. samyogavibhāgau (dvandva of opposites) union and separation.
samyogin [agt. samyuj₁] amnf saṃyoginī in contact with, connected to (i. iic.) | united (with a loved object); opp. virahin | married | gram. consonant in a group of consonants.
saṃrakta [pp. saṃrañj] amnf saṃraktā became red, excited, amorous; furious, charming, pleasant.
samraktanayana [nayana] amfn samraktanayanā with eyes reddened by passion or anger.
saṃraktalocana |locana| afmn samraktalocanā id.
samrakṣ [samrakṣ] v. [1] pr. (saṃrakṣati) pp. (samraksita) to protect, to guard, to defend; to preserve, to save from (abl.).
