samrañj [samrañj] v. [4] pr. r. (samrajyate) pp. (samrakta) to blush | to be passionate; to be in love — ca. (samrañjayati) to color red; to please.
saṃrabdha [pp. saṃrabh] famn samrabdhā excited, irritated.
samrabh [samrabh] v. [1] pr. r. (samrabhate) pp. (samrabdha) to be excited.
samrambha [act. samrabh] m. emotion, ex inner citation; impulse, enthusiasm, zeal, eagerness | agitation, vehemence; anger, fury (against upari (loc. g.)) — iic. excessively, in intensely (ifc.).
samrambhamārga [mārga] m. phil. [vaiṣṇava] path of redemption through hatred; cf. Sisupāla, Pūtanā.
saṃrāj [samrāj₁] v. [1] pr. (saṃrājati) to reign universally (over g. ).
samruddha [pp. samrudh] amnf samruddhā completely stopped; blocked, hindered, prevented, held back | surrounded, besieged (by (iic.)) | covered, hidden; refused.

saṃrudh [samrudh₂] v. [7] pr. (saṃruṇaddhi) pr. r. (saṃrunddhé) pp. (saṃruddha) to stop completely; to block, to hinder; not. to block a road | to obstruct, to prevent, to enclose; to close one's mind to the outside world | to besiege, to surround; to invest, to oppress.
saṃrodha [act. saṃrudh] m. complete obstruction; stoppage, impediment, suppression; in hindrance, confinement.
samrodhana [act. samrudh] n. complete obstruction; act of stopping, preventing; suppression; hindrance, confinement.
samlagna [samlagna] amnf samlagnā in contact with; attached to, adhering to (iic. loc.) of the hand-to-hand combatant.
saṃlap [samlap] v. [1] pr. (saṃlapati) to converse, to converse.
saṃlāpa var. saṃllāpa |act. saṃlap| m. conversation, friendly discussion; dialogue.

saṃvat [contr. saṃvatsara] adv. in the year; not. in the year of the Vikrama era | hist. designates the date according to a dynastic era, not. Mālava or Vikrama (57 antecedent), Šaka (78), Cedi or Kalacuri (249), Gupta (319-320), Harşa (606), Vikramacālukya (1075) — ifc. the year of the reign of (11th century). ... samvat lit. postcolophon of dating.

saṃvatsara [samvatsara] m. year, an astr. year of a life cycle [sastyabda]; there are 60 samvatsarās, named: Prabhava, Vibhava, Šukla, Pramoda₃, Prajāpati, Aṅgīrasa, Srīmukha, Bhāva, Yuvā, Dhātā₁, Iśvara, Ba hudhānya, Pramāthī, Vikrama, Vṛṣā₁, Citrabhānu, Subhānu, Tāraṇa, Pārthiva, Vyaya, Sarvajit, Sarvadhārī, Virodhī, Vikṛta, Khara₁, Nandana, Vijaya₅, Jaya₃, Manmatha, Durmukha, Hema lamba, Vilamba, Vikārī, Sārvarī, Plava, Subhakṛt, Sobhana, Krodhī, Viśvāvasu, Parābhava, Plavanga, Kīlaka, Saumya, Sādhāraņa, Virodhakṛt, Pa ridhāvī, Pramādī, Ananda₁, Rākṣasa, Anala, Pingala₁, Kālayukta, Siddhārthī, Raudra, Dur mati, Dundubhi₁, Rudhirodgārī, Raktākṣa, Krod hana and Kṣaya; the first 20 are dedicated to Brahmā, the next 20 to Visnu, the last 20 to Siva; these 60 years correspond to the conjunction of Jupiter (with a period of 12 years) and Saturn (with a period of 30 years); They are personified as the 60 sons of Nāradī. samvatsarena adv. in the year.

saṃvad [samvad] v. [1] pr. (saṃvadati) pp. (samudita) pfp. (samvaditavya) pf. (vi) to converse, to talk, to chat (with someone (i.), about something (loc.)); to speak to, to address (acc.) | to agree, to come to terms — ca. (saṃvādayati) to make someone (i.), talk about something (loc.) | to invite someone to speak | to play a musical instrument. samvādya ind. having declared sincerely. sāmvatsarikaih samvādyatām that the astrologers be consulted.
samvadana | act. samvad | n. conversation; examination; message — f. samvadanā act of submitting to magic; charm, amulet.
saṃvara [agt. saṃvṛ] amnf saṃvarā that restricts, that stops, that repels — m. barrier | cf. śambara — act. n. bd. restriction; abstention (of a ritual observance).

saṃvaraṇa [agt. saṃvṛ] amnf saṃvaraṇā that covers, that contains, that hides — m. myth. np. of Samvarana "Sanctuary", king of the lunar lineage, 6th descendant of Bharata, son of Rkṣa; [Mah.] attacked by a king Pāncāla, he appealed to Vasistha to regain his kingdom; he was a devotee of Sūrya, whose daughter Tapatī he married; King Kuru is their son — act. n. secrecy, hidden act; Sanctuary | soc. enclosure of sacrifice | soc. choice of a husband.
saṃvaraṇasraj |sraj| f. soc. crown given by a young girl to the husband of her choice at her svayamvara.
samvart [ca. samvrt] v. [10] pr. (samvartayati) to roll, to throw; to accomplish.

saṃvartá [act. saṃvṛt] m. encounter, com combat; destruction, end of the world [ "that which is rolled"] ball; clod; crowd | myth. np. of Samvarta "Apo calypse", son of Angira and Śraddha, younger brother of Brhaspati, his rival; he went to the forest naked, to devote himself to penances; King Marutta asked him to be his chaplain [purohita]; he officiated for him at a great soma sacrifice where Indra and all the gods attended; |Rām.| he officiated at a sa crifice of King Marutta, profaned by Rāvaņa.
samvartaka [agt. samvrt] amnf samvartikā that destroys everything (at the apocalypse) — m. destructive fire; clouds of the end of the world | pl. samvartakās the flames of hell.
saṃvardh [ca. saṃvṛdh] v. [10] pr. (samvardhayati) pp. (samvardhita) to enlarge, increase, strengthen; to raise, nourish, prosper; to grant (i.), to fulfill.
samvardhana [agt. samvrdh] amnf samvardhanā which increases, which makes prosper; strengthening — act. n. growth, prosperity; care, maintenance, nurse; increase, growth.
samvardhita [pp. samvardh] amnf samvardhitā nourished, raised, cared for.
saṃvas [samvas₁] v. [1] pr. (saṃvasati) pp. (samvasita) to live or stay together, to cohabit with; to associate with (i. acc.); to assemble.

saṃvah [samvah₁] v. [1] pr. (saṃvahati) to carry with oneself; to bring; to transport | to load (chariot, carriage) to take a wife, to marry massage, to caress — ca. (saṃvāhayati) to cause to bring | to guide, to drive (chariot, carriage).
samvaha [agt. samvah] m. myth. np. of samvaha "that which carries", wind of one of the 7 ways of heaven [mārga], above Udvaha; it propels the Moon | myth. np. of one of the 7 languages of Agni.

samvādá [act. samvad] m. conversation, dialogue; discussion | soc. not. in-depth discussion among scholars | ved. dialogued hymn | agreement, understanding; meeting, colloquium | legal matter | agreement, conformity; correspondence, similiarity; opp. vivāda | information, news — f. saṃvādā ifc. conversation with (i.c.). samvādam kr to converse, to converse with (i.).
saṃvādana [act. saṃvad] n. agreement, accord.
saṃvāra [act. saṃvṛ] m. closure, covering, contraction | phon. contraction of the organs of the voice, compression of the throat; opp. vivāra — f. saṃvārā ifc. closure of, contraction of (iic.).
saṃvāsa [act. saṃvas] m. cohabitation; union with | the act of settling down; dwelling association, company.
saṃvāha [agt. ca. saṃvah] amnf saṃvāhā that transports — act. m. transport | massage, caress.

saṃvāhaka [agt. saṃvah] amnf samvāhikā who massages — m. lit. [Mṛcchakaṭikā] np. of Saṃvāhaka, masseur in the service of Cārudatta; he loses at gambling, is persecuted for his debts which Vasantasenā will repay, and thus humiliated becomes a renunciant.
saṃvāhana [act. saṃvah] n. transport; driving | caresses; massage, shampoo.
saṃvigna [pp. saṃvij] amnf saṃvignā agitated; terrified; timid.

saṃvijñā [samvijñā₁] v. [9] pr. (saṃvijānāti) pp. (saṃvijñāta) to approve; to recommend; to advise (a person (g.)) — ca. (saṃvijñāpayati) to make known, to proclaim; to recite.
saṃvijñāta [pp. saṃvijñā] amnf samvijnātā well known | gram. not. proper noun common.

saṃvid₁ [samvid₁] v. [2] pr. (saṃvetti) pp. (samvidita) to consult, to agree; to approve | to know; to recognize; to perceive.

saṃvíd₂ [act. saṃvid₁] f. knowledge, consciousness, perception | understanding, agreement, convention tion; meeting; conversation | custom, usage — ifc. discussion on (iic.). samvid₁ eşa svayam prabhā phil. consciousness is its own light.
saṃvidita [pp. saṃvid₁] amnf samviditā learned, known; recognized, understood, approved.
samvidhā₁ [sam extvidhā₁] v. [3] pr. (saṃvidadhāti) pp. (saṃvihita) to determine, establish, fix, resolve; to rule, order.

saṃvibhāga [act. saṃvibhaj] m. sharing with others, pooling; distribution.

saṃviś [samviś₁] v. [6] pr. (saṃviśati) pp. (saṃviṣṭa) pf. (abhi) to approach; to associate with (acc. i.) | to settle, to rest; to sleep with (i. dat.) to cohabit with, to have sexual relations with acc. — ca. (samveśayati) to settle together, as seem.
saṃviṣṭa [pp. saṃviś] amnf saṃviṣṭā approached, entered; who rests; seated with (i.).

saṃvīta [pp. saṃvyā] amnf saṃvītā green neck; dressed; in armor; wearing the sacred cord surrounded by, covered with, clothed in, equipped with, hidden by (i. iic.) | obscured; hidden; invisible, disappeared n. garment.

saṃvṛ [samvṛ₁] v. [5] pr. (saṃvṛṇóti) pr. r. (saṃvṛṇuté) pp. (saṃvṛta) to cover, to wrap, to enclose; to hide | to enclose, to obstruct; to repel. mā vama samvṛṇu viṣam idam [Govardhana₁] Do not vomit this poison, enclose it within yourself (Brahmā to Shiva having swallowed the poison Halāhala).
saṃvṛt [samvṛt₁] v. [1] pr. r. (saṃvartate) pp. (samvrtta) to begin, to occur, to become; to be realized — ca. (samvartayati) to roll, to throw; ac complir.
saṃvṛta [pp. saṃvṛ] amnf saṃvṛtā green neck, closed; wrapped in (loc.); hidden, guarded, secret | repressed, restricted, withdrawn | phon. (sound) closed; opp. vivrta.
saṃvṛti [act. saṃvṛ] f. closure, obstruction |dissimulation, the act of keeping secret; hypocrisy |bd. level of conventional or concealed truth, as opposed to the level of supreme truth pa ramārtha.
samvṛtisat [sat] amnf samvṛtisatī bd. which exists by convention; opp. paramārthasat.
samvṛtisatya [satya] n. bd. conventional or concealed truth (opp. paramārthasatya) | phil. ["contingent real" plane of ordinary reality.
saṃvṛtta [pp. saṃvṛt] amnf saṃvṛttā which takes place, which occurs | happened, occurred; become; accomplished, realized.
saṃvṛtti [act. saṃvṛt] f. usual occupation, routine | accomplishment, realization; existence, state | cf. samvrti.
samvrddha [pp. samvrdh] amnf samvṛddhā increased, augmented, grown, well developed; prosperous.
saṃvṛdh [samvṛdh₁] v. [1] pr. r. (saṃvardhate) pp. (saṃvṛddha) to grow, to gran dir, to gain strength — ca. (samvardhayati) cf. samvardh.
saṃvega [act. saṃvij] m. disturbance, agitation, excitement; impulse, vehemence.
saṃvegin [agt. saṃvij] amnf saṃveginī agitated, excited.
samveda [act. samvid₁] m. perception; awareness.
samvedana [act. samvid₁] n. act of perception or sensation; perception; sensation communication; announcement; information.
samvedita [pp. ca. samvid₁] amnf samveditā communicated; informed; instructed.
saṃvedya [pfp. [1] saṃvid₁] amnf samvedyā which must be known or understood or ap
taken | intelligible | to be communicated to (loc.).
samveśá [act. samviś] m. arrival, entrance | rest; sleep; dream — obj. m. bedroom; seat.
saṃveśana [agt. saṃviś] amnf saṃveśanā which makes one lie down — act. n. rest;
entrance | sexual union | seat, bench.
saṃvyavaharaṇa [act. saṃvyavahṛ] n. business, commerce.
samvyavahāra [act. samvyavahr] m. ifc. exchange, trafficking, business, sexual relations with occupation with, addiction to.
saṃvyavahāravat [vat] m. businessman.
samvyavahr [samvyavahr] v. [1] pr. (saṃvyavaharati) pp. (saṃvyavahṛta) to have (sexual or professional) relations with (i. loc.).
saṃvyā [samvyā] v. [1] pr. (saṃvyayati) pp. (saṃvīta) to wrap, to cover — pr. r. (saṃvyayate) to cover oneself with acc. .
saṃśak [samśak] v. [5] pr. (saṃśaknóti) pp. (saṃśakta) to be able, to be capable of (inf.).
saṃśakti [act. saṃśak] f. power; not. to see the supernatural (syn. siddhi).

saṃśaya [act. saṃśī] m. doubt, hesitation, uncertainty; risk, danger | doubt towards (loc. prati acc. iic. | (with opt.) it is doubtful that | phil. [Nyāya] not contestable, one of the 16 categories [padārtha]. na saṃśayaḥ without a doubt. atra na samśayah that is beyond doubt.
samśayocchedin [ucchedin] amnf samśayocchedinī which dispels doubts.
samśayika [samśayaika] amnf samśayikī in a precarious state.
saṃśayita [pp. saṃśī] amnf saṃśayitā doubted, contested | irresolute; one who doubts (iic.). samśayitajīvitah one who risks his life.
saṃśā [samśā] v. [3] pr. (saṃśiśāti) pp. (saṃśita) to sharpen | prepare; to exhort, to push, to press — v. [3] pr. r. (saṃśiśīte) to sharpen one's weapons.
saṃśita [pp. saṃśā] amnf saṃśitā ai guisé; pointed, cutting | prepared; decided, resolved to (loc.); zealous.
saṃśitavrata [vrata] amnf saṃśitavratā fer mement determined to keep his commitments; honest, virtuous.
saṃśī [samśī₁] v. [2] pr. r. (saṃśayate) pp. (saṃśayita) to hesitate, to doubt | to lose hope in (loc.) — v. [2] pr. r. (saṃśayati) to dispute, not to believe in (acc.).
saṃśuddha [pp. saṃśudh] amnf samśuddhā pure, clean | paid, expiated; acquitted.
saṃśuddhi [act. saṃśudh] f. perfect purification, perfect purity | complete innocence; absence of debts | correction; rectification.
saṃśudh [samśudh] v. [4] pr. (saṃśudhyati) pp. (samśuddha) to purify oneself perfectly, to acquit oneself of — ca. (samśodhayati) to purify completely | to acquit oneself of; to secure.
saṃśodhana [act. saṃśudh] n. purification; acquittal | amendment, correction.
saṃśodhita [pp. ca. saṃśudh] amnf samśodhitā purified | lit. corrected edition and ap proven.
saṃścat m. juggler, illusionist; rogue — n. juggling; illusion, trickery; deception.

samśraya [act. samśri] m. refuge, stay, residence; shelter, support, protection — ifc. associated with, relating to, devoted to (iic.). saṃśrayāt adv. with the help of, by means of; as a consequence of.
saṃśravaṇa [act. saṃśru] n. act of hearing or listening | within earshot — ifc. hearsay of (iic.). samśravane within earshot; aloud. asaméravane beyond earshot.
saṃśri [samśri] v. [1] pr. (saṃśrayati) pr. r. (saṃśrayate) pp. (saṃśrita) to join, to take refuge with, to ask for protection from (acc.); to depend on, to rely on (acc.).
saṃśrita [pp. saṃśri] ifc. amnf saṃśritā associated, attached, in relation with; devoted to; who chooses, who serves.

saṃśru [samśru] v. [5] pr. (saṃśṛṇoti) pp. (saméruta) to hear from; to listen attentively; to consent to, to promise (dat. loc.) — pr. r. (saṃśṛṇute) to be heard distinctly — ca. (saṃśṛāvayati) to make heard, to proclaim, to announce cer. mukhāt saṃśru to learn from someone's mouth.
saṃśruta [pp. saṃśru] amnf saṃśrutā clearly understood; learned; instructed in (loc.) consented, promised (to the angle g. rangle).
saṃśliṣ [samśliṣ] v. [4] pr. (saṃśliṣyati) pp. (saṃśliṣṭa) to embrace, to hug, to press against — ca. (samślesayati) to unite.
samślesa [act. saṃślis] m. union, embrace; at stain, link.
saṃsakta [pp. saṃsañj] amnf saṃsaktā stuck together; met; united, pressed close | directed towards, busy with, devoted to, lover of (loc. iic.) near, contiguous | compact, dense, continuous.
samsañj [samsañj] v. [1] pr. r. (samsajate) pp. (saṃsakta) ps. (saṃsajjate) to adhere, to cling to; to stop | to meet in hand-to-hand combat an enemy (i.).
samsad₁ [samsad₁] v. [1] pr. (samsidati) pp. (saṃsanna) to sit together.
saṃsad₂ [act. saṃsad₁] f. assembly, court of a prince.
saṃsaraṇa [act. saṃsṛ] n. promenade, the act of wandering | phil. changes of state; wandering towards transmigrations; earthly condition | the marching of an army; a military campaign
laughing | highway | soc. resting place for travelers at the gates of a city.

samsarga [act. samsrj] m. union, junction; association, connection, contact | encounter, frequentation, mingling with (i. loc. iic.); commerce with the world; familiarity | gram. association between two notions, allowing the mutual disambiguation of their signifiers; syn. saṃyoga | math. point of intersection | pl. samsargās carnal commerce, sensual pleasures. saṃsargatas adv. in contact.
samsargaka [ka] ifc. amnf samsargakā associated with; brought into contact with; who frequents.
samsargadoṣa [doṣa₂] m. poor attendance.
samsargamaryādā [maryādā] f. gram. agreement of words in the sentence to determine its meaning.
samsargavidyā [vidyā] f. knowledge of human relations; sociology.

samsargābhāva [abhāva] m. phil. [NN.] negation of a predication; non-existence, one of the senses of negation |na|; opp. anyonyābhāva; we distinguish 3 kinds of it: absence of birth, present destruction, and necessary ultimate annihilation.
saṃsargin [agt. saṃsṛj] amnf saṃsargiṇī mixed; related to, connected, in contact with (iic.) | familiar, associated — m. companion, as socié.
samsargitā |tā| f. connection, contact; combination, association.
samsargitva |tva| n. id.
saṃsarjana [act. saṃsṛj] n. mixture; encounter against; association, combination (with (i.)) reconciliation.
saṃsava [act. saṃsu] m. pressing of soma competing by competition [samṛtayajña].
saṃsah [samsah₁] v. [1] pr. r. (saṃsáhate) pp. (samsodha) bear.

samsādh [ca. samsidh] v. [10] pr. (saṃsādhayati) pfp. (saṃsādhya) to accomplish completely; to procure; to dominate, to master; to prepare (food) | to enforce, to apply (a promise); to recover (a debt) — ps. (saṃsādhyate) to be completely accomplished or provided. marum samsādh to abstain from drinking.
saṃsādhana [act. saṃsādh] n. accomplishment; realization, execution — f. saṃsādhanī work.
saṃsādhya [pfp. [1] saṃsādh] amnf samsādhyā that can or must be accomplished; that can or must be executed | controllable; that can be put under control.
saṃsār [ca. saṃsr̩] v. [10] pr. (saṃsārayati) phil. to cause to undergo transmigrations.

samsāra [act. samsār] m. transition | phil. transmigration; current of successive rebirths | here below, the human condition; the phenomenal world | secular life; the flow of life | mod. family life; personal journey. āsaṃsārāt adv. from the beginning of the world. samsārakatuvrksasya dve phale hy amrtopame subhāṣitarasāsvādah saṅgatih sujanaih saha || From the bitter tree of existence two fruits are like the divine nectar: the delight of proverbs and the company of the righteous. citte calati saṃsāro niścale mokṣa eva tu When thought is in motion, one feels the phenomenal world; when it stops, one is liberated.
saṃsāracakra [cakra] n. phil. the cycle of rebirths | bd. the wheel of existence | bhavacakra |.
saṃsārasaṅga |saṅga| m. phil. attachment to the world.
samsārasāra [sāra] m. the salt of existence.
saṃsārika [saṃsāraika] amnf samsārikī worldly.
samsiddha [pp. samsidh] amnf saṃsiddhā completely accomplished; successful; prepared (food) | ready, firmly resolved (to (dat.)); ha bile to loc. | who has achieved the goal (not. of liberation).
saṃsiddhi [act. saṃsidh] f. total accomplishment; success; perfection | bliss; final emancipation | last word, definitive opinion.
saṃsidh [samsidh₁] v. [4] pr. (saṃsidhyati) pp. (samsiddha) to succeed perfectly; to attain bliss — ca. (saṃsādhayati) cf. saṃsādh.
saṃsu [samsu₂] v. [5] pr. (saṃsunoti) ved. to press the soma together.
saṃsūc [samsūc] v. [10] pr. (saṃsūcayati) pp. (samsūcita) to make known, to indicate clearly, to inform; to confirm | to reveal.

saṃsṛ [samsṛ] v. [1] pr. (saṃsarati) pr. r. (saṃsarate) pp. (saṃsṛta) to circulate, to travel, to wander phil. to pass through successive rebirths — ca. (saṃsārayati) phil. to cause to undergo transmigrations.
saṃsṛj [samsṛj₁] v. [6] pr. (saṃsṛjati) pp. (saṃsṛṣṭa) to unite.
saṃsṛp [samsṛp] v. [1] pr. (saṃsarpati) pp. (samsrpta) to advance by crawling; to slide towards ved. (ritual) to perform a series of 10 offerings at different distances.

saṃsṛṣṭa [pp. saṃsṛj] amnf saṃsṛṣṭā ras seemed, collected; united, combined, mixed, fused | from the same litter; associated, partner — ifc. connected with, belonging to (iic.) — n. friendship; intimacy. samsṛṣṭam because becoming intimate with.
samsṛṣṭatva |tva| n. association, mixture.
samsṛṣṭārtha [artha] amnf saṃsṛṣṭārthā gram. is said of a compound word not composed nel, like aśvakarna.

sámsrsti [act. samsrj] f. union, combination, association; promiscuity, sexual act | common life in the same family | collection, assembly | lit. association of two different metaphors in the same sentence.
samskarana [agt. samskr] n. preparation, getting ready | soc. cremation.
saṃskartṛ [agt. saṃskṛ] amnf saṃskartrī who prepares; who decorates, who arranges; who arranges (meal, rite).

saṃskāra [act. saṃskṛ] m. preparation, ar. arrangement; dressing, decoration; impression | dressing of a thing giving it the aptitude for a function culinary dressing, seasoning acquired disposition; residual subconscious tendencies soc. ritual dressing; consecration; religious ceremony, private rite; sacrament, initiation, rite of purification; cf. garbhādhāna, puṃsavana, Sīmantonnayana, jātakarman, nāmakaraņa, annaprāśana, karṇavedha, cauḍacūḍākaraṇa, vidyārambha, upanayana, godāna, keśānta, snāna samāvartana, vivāha, antyeṣṭi | purification of the body; grooming; good education; The state of being correct; predisposition, innate impulse | phil. [Vedānta] acquired disposition; emotional nature; residual mental formation, impression composing personality; liberation is attained by sublimating them phil. [Vaisesika] faculty of regeneration, 24th quality [guna] | bd. mental formation, one of the 5 aggregates [skandha] of the ego; it is the 2nd cause of suffering [pratītyasamutpāda] | Gram. correct formation of a word; correct usage — f. samskārā ifc. id. || pali sankhāra. jananāt jāyate śūdraḥ saṃskārāt dvija ucyate by birth one is born śūdra; by the sacrament one becomes dvija. samskāras trividhah vego bhāvanā sthi tisthāpakaśceti phil. [TkS.] The faculty of regeneration is of 3 kinds: velocity, imagination and elasticity.
saṃskāraprayogaratna [prayogaratna] n. lit. [Atharvaveda] np. of the Saṃskāraprayogaratna, manual of prenatal rites and concerning young children.
Samskāravidhi [vidhi] m. bed. n.p. of Saṃskāravidhi, versified form of the Aśvalāyanagrhyasūtra.

saṃskṛ [samkṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (saṃskaróti) pp. (saṃskṛta) pf. (prati) to prepare, arrange; to decorate, adorn, embellish; to consecrate; to perfect. vācam hyevaitām samskurute [SB.] It is the word that thus he perfects.

saṃskṛtá [pp. saṃskṛtā amnf saṃskṛtā consecrated, purified, clean; refined, neat; adorned; regular; perfect — n. Sanskrit, refined language, correct language; perfect language; sacred language | bd. [Mahāyāna] the conditioned, or phenomenal existence; it is unsatisfactory, impermanent, and illusory; opp. asamskrta | pali sankhata; fr. sans krit.
samskṛtavāc [vāc] f. [name. saṃskṛtavāk] Sanskrit language.

saṃskṛtavyākaraṇa [vyākaraṇa] n. grammar of Sanskrit | lit. np. of the Saṃskṛtavyākaraṇa, "Grammar of Sanskrit" by the Jesuit missionary Johann Ernst Hanxleden (1681–1732); he lived in Kerala, not. in Velur.
samskṛtaśūnyatā [śūnyatā] f. bd. [Mahāyāna] emptiness of the conditioned; unreality of phenomenal existence.
saṃskṛtoccaraṇa | uccaraṇa | n. phone. pronunciation of Sanskrit.
saṃskṛti [act. saṃskṛ] f. preparation, perfection; consecration | var. saṃskṛtī mod. Sanskrit cosmopolitan culture. samskṛtiḥ saṃskṛtāśritā Sanskrit culture is transmitted through Sanskrit.
saṃskṛtrima [saṃskṛtrima] amnf samskrtrimā very refined; precious, artificial; am poulé — f. samskṛtrimā Sanskrit refined.

√ saṃstambh [samstambh] v. [9] pr. (saṃstabhnāti) pp. (saṃstabdha) to consolidate, strengthen; to encourage | to freeze, immobilize, paralyze (notably by magic); to obstruct — ca. (saṃstambhayati) pp. (samstambhita) to invigorate; to regain courage. sa nādyāpi saṃstambhayati ātmānam he has not yet recovered.
saṃstambhá [act. saṃstambh] m. obstination tion, tenacity; endurance | support; firmness | enchantment, paralysis.
saṃstava [act. saṃstu] m. collective praise; praise in common | intimate familiarity with (i. iic.) | pl. praises.
saṃstavāna [agt. saṃstu] amnf saṃstavānā eloquent — m. orator | soc. priest reciting the Sāmaveda.
saṃstu [samstu] v. [2] pr. (saṃstauti) pp. (saṃstuta) to praise with (i.); to celebrate together or simultaneously | to praise abundantly, to celebrate with great pomp.
sáṃstuta [pp. saṃstu] amnf saṃstutā celebrated, praised.
sáṃstuti [act. saṃstu] f. praise, celebration | lit. figurative expression.
saṃstyāna [samstyāna] amnf samstyānā coagulated, frozen — n. state of being condensed or compact (not. fetus).
saṃstha [agt. saṃsthā₁] ifc. amnf saṃsthā which stands in or on (iic.); founded on, dependent on (iic.) — f. cf. saṃsthā₂.

samsthā₁ [samsthā₁] v. [1] pr. r. (samtisthate) pp. (samsthita) to stop, to finish, to come to an end; to be accomplished, to succeed | to be ruined, to die — ca. (saṃsthāpayati) to establish, to complete, to accomplish.

samsthā₁ [f. samstha] f. abode in iic. | manifestation, appearance; form; fact of appearing as (iic.) | established rule, order | quality, property; nature | conclusion, termination, completion; end, death; cremation | phil. destruction of the world; syn. pralaya soc. liturgical sequence during a sacrifice.
saṃsthāna [act. saṃsthā₁] n. existence, presence; form, aspect, appearance; nature, condition, state | phil. structure | mod. institute, institution.
saṃsthānaka [ka] m. lit. np. of the odious prince Saṃsthānaka, brother-in-law of King Pālaka in the play Mrcchakatikā.
saṃsthāpaka [agt. ca. saṃsthā₁] amnf saṃsthāpakā that establishes, that strengthens (iic.); that accomplishes (iic.).
saṃsthāpana [act. ca. saṃsthā₁] n. establishment, foundation; regulation — f. samsthāpanā encouragement; restoration.

samsthita [pp. samsthā₁] amnf saṃsthitā that stands there, that is manifest, that is being discussed | standing; available; instituted | concerning (i.e., loc.); familiar with (loc.) | that lasts, that persists; surviving | finished, completed, accomplished; ready; arrived | frequented (place); near, contiguous — n. behavior; appearance.
saṃsparśa [act. saṃspṛś] m. contact; touch, sense of touch; the act of touching or being touched.
saṃspṛś [samspṛś₁] v. [6] pr. (saṃspṛśati) pr. r. (samsprśate) pp. (samsprṣṭa) touch; put in contact; reach, seize abl. .
saṃspṛṣṭa [pp. saṃspṛś] amnf saṃspṛṣṭā touched, reached.
saṃsphur [samsphur] v. [6] pr. r. (saṃsphuráte) to leap together | to sparkle, to glitter.
saṃsmṛ [samsmṛ] v. [1] pr. (saṃsmarati) pp. (saṃsmṛta) pf. (abhi) to remember, to recall (acc. g.) — ca. (saṃsmārayati) to remind someone of something (acc.) (acc. g.).
saṃsrāvá |act. saṃsru| mf saṃsrāvā seepage; flow; confluence | liquid residue; sediments.
saṃsru [samsru] v. [1] pr. (saṃsravati) to flow around, to ooze | to merge — ca. (saṃrāvayati) to make flow together; to mix remnants of liquid.
saṃsveda [samsveda] m. sweat, perspiration.
saṃsvedaja [ja] m. ["born of sweat"] vermin.
saṃhata [pp. saṃhan] amnf saṃhatā united, bound, associated; combined; compact, dense, firm,
hardened | bound to (i.) | compound, composite; complex.
saṃhatatā [tā] f. union, association.
samhatatva [tva] n. union, association; amalgamation | compactness, firmness; complexity.
saṃhatamūrti [mūrti] amnf of compact appearance; firm.

samhati [act. samhan] f. solidity, compactness, firmness | collection, accumulation | alliance; junction; common effort; contact with (i.) | compact mass; heap; collection; gathering; multitude. saṃhatiḥ kāryasādhikā unity makes strength.
saṃhatya [pfp. [1] saṃhan] amnf saṃhatyā to combine (with (i.)).

samhatyakāritā [kāritā] f. gram. cumulative effect of the meaning of words to produce the meaning of the sentence containing them; Jayanta attributes it to the power of words to account for the speaker's intention [tātparyaśakti].
saṃhan [samhan₁] v. [2] pr. (saṃhanti) pp. (saṃhata) to unite, to associate; to close.
samhanana [agt. samhan] amnf samhananī solid, compact, firm | that kills, that destroys — act. n. hardening, solidification solidity, firmness; robustness, strength.
samhara [act. samhr] m. collection, contraction; destruction.
samharana [act. samhr] n. collection, contraction, gathering, arrangement | taking | destruction.
saṃharṣ [ca. saṃhṛṣ] v. [10] pr. (saṃharṣayati) to excite, to rejoice; to give pleasure.
samharṣa [act. samharṣ] m. excitement; joy, sexual arousal, ardor; emulation, rivalry. samharṣāt adv. carried away by excitement.

saṃhāra [act. saṃhṛ] m. contraction; destruction; resorption; end, conclusion (of a drama, etc.) lit. summary, compendium | annihilator; epith. of Shiva | phil. cosmic dissolution (opp. sṛṣṭi), one of the 5 divine manifestations [pañcakṛtya] | myth. destruction of the world at the end of a kalpa | myth. return of a magical weapon to its possessor.
saṃhita [pp. saṃdhā₁] amnf saṃhitā united to, associated with; followed by, provided with; conforming to — f. cf. samhitā.

samhitā [f. samhita] f. conjunction, union; proximity | [saṃhitāpāṭha] continuous enunciation; text in continuous form where the connection [sandhi] applies | phil. collection of texts (notably from the Veda), collection of works, compilation, compendium. samhitāyām gram. in continuous sentence (where the sandhi is performed). parah samnikarşah samhitā gram. [Pāṇini] Mutual contact (between signifiers) is called samhitā. samhitaikapade nityā nityā dhātūpasargayoh | nityāsamāse vākye tu sā vivakṣāmapekṣate || Continuous enunciation is obligatory within a word, obligatory between a preverb and a verb form, obligatory within a compound, but in the sentence it must respect the communicative intention of the speaker.
samhitāpātha [pātha] m. soc. recitation of the Veda by continuous reading applying sandhi; opp. padapāṭha; cf. Sākalya | gram. written form where the linking between words [sandhi] is carried out.

saṃhṛ [samhṛ₁] v. [1] pr. (saṃharati) pr. r. (samharate) pp. (samhrta) pf. (upa, prati) to concentrate, tighten; to repress, suspend, stop; to absorb, make disappear; to remove, appropriate — ps. (samhriyate) to be arrested. rūpam samhr to abandon one's form. samhriyatāmiyam kathā let us forget this matter. tava mahīmānamutkīrtya vacaḥ saṃhriyate words fail to describe your greatness.

saṃhṛta [pp. saṃhṛ] amnf saṃhṛtā concentrated, pressed; repressed, arrested; disappeared — iic. form with object acc. ifc. an adverb signifying the end of the process concerning it. samhrtayavam adv. after the barley harvest.
saṃhṛtarūpa [rūpa] amnf saṃhṛtarūpā com pressed, shrunk.
samhṛti [act. saṃhṛ] f. contraction; act of concentrating, of abbreviating | conclusion, end | phil. of the construction of the Universe.

saṃhṛṣ [samhṛṣ] v. [4] pr. (saṃhṛṣyati) pp. (samhṛṣita, samhṛṣṭa) to bristle, to stiffen; to stand up (hairs); to quiver; to be excited | to rejoice, to appreciate; to enjoy — ca. (saṃharṣayati) to excite, to rejoice; to give pleasure.
saṃhṛṣṭa [pp. saṃhṛṣ] amnf saṃhṛṣṭā bristling; joyful, happy, delighted | feeling pleasure | erect.
saṃhṛṣṭin [agt. saṃhṛṣ] m. excited; erect.
saṃhrād [samhrād] v. [1] pr. r. (saṃhrādate) pp. (saṃhrādita) to rattle and collide ca. (saṃhrādáyati) ppr. (saṃhrādayat) to click.

saṃhrāda [agt. saṃhrād] m. noise (not. of chains) | myth. np. of the asura samhrāda "Noisy" son of Hiranyakaśipu; his sons are Ayuşmat, Sibi₁, Bāṣkala₁ and Pañcajana (by Kṛti); he incarnated in Salya.
saṃhrādayat [ppr. That. saṃhrād] amnf samhrādayantī by clicking.
saṃhlāda m. cf. saṃhrāda.

sakantaka [sa₁kantaka] amnf sakantaka thorny; prickly | irritating; dangerous with bones (fish) | bio. bot. Guilandina bonduc, a seaside legume forming bushes with thorny fruits; the seeds are used in medicine.
sakapi [sa₁kapi] amnf accompanied by a monkey.
sakarunam [sa₁karunam] amnf sakarunam compassionate | pitiable. sakarunam adv. with compassion | piteously.
sakarmaka [sa₁karmaka] amnf sakar mikā effective, which acts | gram. (verb) transitive; opp. akarmaka.
sakala |sa₁kalā| amnf sakalā whole, integral, complete, total, intact | formed of portions, divisible — m. everyone — n. all. pratijñām sakalam kṛ fulfill one's promise.
sakalakathā [kathā₁] f. lit. complete story (a literary genre).
sakalārtha | artha | amnf universal sakalārthā.
sakalārthaśāstra [śāstra] n. universal knowledge. sakalārthaśāstravid amnf that possesses knowledge of all things. sakalārthaśāstrasāra amn that contains the essence of all knowledge.
sakalakala |sa₁kalakala| amnf saka lakalā tumultuous.
sakalpavṛkṣa [sa₁kalpavṛkṣa] amnf sakalpavrkṣā possessing the tree of abundance.
sakalmaṣa [sa₁kalmaṣa] amnf sakalmasā defiled.

sákāma [sa₁kāma] amnf sakāmā who satisfies desires | whose desires are satisfied; satisfied, fulfilled | who has given their consent; consenting (not. girl) | desirous of (i.e.) | of their own free will, voluntarily | filled with desire; in love. sakāmam adv. with pleasure; for the pleasure of (acc.).
sakāra [(sa)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'sa'.
sakārānta [anta] amn gram. which ends with the letter 'sa'.
sakāla |sa₁kāla₁| amnf sakālā at the appropriate time, opportune; in season. sakālam adv. in season; at the right time, on time; the time having come | early in the morning.

sakāsa [sa₁kāsa] amnf sakāsā visible; present; near — m. visibility, presence, proximity. sakāśam adv. towards, near (vb. of movement). sakāśe adv. in the presence of, near. sakāśāt adv. from, on behalf of, from the side of; from the point of view of.
sakiśora [sa₁kiśora] amnf sakiśorā accompanied by her young. sakiśorā dhenuḥ mare with her foal.
sakula [sa₁kula] amnf sakulā having a family; belonging to a good family; from the same family | accompanied by his family.
sakulaja |ja| amnf sakulajā born in the same family as (g.).

sakṛt [sa₁kṛt₂] amnf simultaneous — adv. all at once, at the same time, simultaneously; suddenly | only once; formerly; once and for all; forever. sakrd bhunkte he eats once. sakrjjagāma he left suddenly. sakṛcchrutam ayaṃ bālaḥ sarvaṃ vai
dhārayeddhṛdi [KSS.] This boy memorizes any text after a single listening.
sakṛpa [sa₁kṛpa] amnf sakṛpā compatis sant.
sáketa [sa₁keta] amnf saketā of the same intention.
saketu [sa₁ketu] amnf with a banner.
sakopa [sa₁kopa] amnf sakopā angry, angry. sakopam adv. angrily.

saktá [pp. sañj] amnf saktā adherent, at stained; belonging to, equipped with (g.) | attentive; ab absorbed in, devoted to, given to, preoccupied with (loc. acc. iic. | hindered, hampered, embarrassed (opp. asakta). manmukhāsaktadṛṣṭiḥ with his gaze fixed on my face.
sakti [act. sañj] f. adherence, attachment; ad diction | phil. attachment to the world and to passions.
saktú [sañjtu] mn gruel; porridge, not. of barley; orgeat.
saktvādhaka |ādhaka| n. measure of barley grains.
sakthán var. sakthi n. thigh.
sakrodha [sa₁krodha] amnf sakrodhā angry, furious. sakrodham with anger.
sakṣīra [sa₁kṣīra] amnf sakṣīrā milky; with latex, succulent.
sakha cf. sakhi.
sakhaṇḍa |sa₁khaṇḍa| amnf sakhaṇḍā composite; divisible; opp. akhaṇḍa.
sakhaṇḍopādhi [upādhi] f. phil. [Nyāya] particular composite qualification.

sakhi [agt. bag] m. [sg. name. sakhā, acc. sakhāyam, i. sakhyā, dat. sakhye, g. abl. sakhyus, loc. sakhyau, voc. sakhe; of. name. sakhāyau, i. sakhibhyām, g. sakhyos; pl. name. sakhāyas, acc. sakhīn, i. sakhibhis; in comp. sakha] friend, comrade, companion | ally by ritual, sworn friend | soc. brother-in-law (husband of a sister of the wife) — mr. sa kha ifc. friend of (iic.) | accompanied by (iic.) — f. cf. sakhī — v. [11] pr. (sakhīyati) to seek the friendship of (i.) | lat. socius.
sakhī [f. sakhi] f. friend, confidante; mistress — ifc. friend of (iic.). sakhīmukhenoce spoke through the voice of her friend.
sakhījana | jana | m. circle of friends.
sakhya [sakhia] n. friendship, intimacy.
sagaṇa [sa₁gaṇa] amnf sagaṇā accom accompanied by servants or troops; accompanied by (i.) — m. myth. Shiva with his followers.
sagandha [sa₁gandha] amnf sagandhā similar, related | "which has the same smell" |.

Sagara [sa₁gara] amnf sagarā which contains poison; Poisoned — m. myth. np. of King Sagara "(born) Poisoned", of the solar lineage [sūryavaṃśa], son of Bāhu (or [Rām.] of Asita); he came into the world with the poison given to his mother by his father's other wife; thanks to the help of the sage [rṣi] Aurva who gave him the āgneyāstra, he defeated the Haihayās to regain his throne; it is said that his reign lasted 3000 years; he married Keśinī₁ and Sumati₂, but could not have offspring; [Rām.] After 100 years of penance in the Himalayas, Bhṛgu gave his wives the choice between begetting the heir of the lineage or having 60,000 renowned sons; he begot the good-for-nothing Asamañjā by Queen Keśinī₁ and had 60,000 sons [sāgarās] by Sumati₂; he made 100 horse sacrifices [aśvamedha] to increase his kingdom; on the 100th, he was to gain the kingdom of Indra himself; the latter deceived the vigilance of his sons, and stole the sacrificial horse; King Sagara, angry at their negligence, ordered them to go and get it, even in hell |pātāla|; They dug (the Ocean pit), and found him there not far from the sage Kapila, sitting in meditation, whom they took for the thief, and attacked; Kapila, disturbed, reduced them to ashes with a look; so that they could have the funeral rites and return to heaven, later Bhagīratha brought down the celestial Ganges to Earth in order to purify the Ocean "dug on the order of Sagara" [sāgara].
saguṇa [sa₁guṇa] amnf saguṇā with a cord | endowed with qualities, virtues | phil. that has attributes, differentiated (opp. nirguna). saguna brahman phil. the immanent divine or mani festé.
saguṇātmavādin |ātmavādin| amnf sagunātmavādinī phil. holder of a doctrine
positivist [āstika] believing in an immanent manifestation; opp. nirgunātmavādin.
sagunopāsanā [upāsanā] f. soc. veneration of the divine [brahman] in the form of a particular deity.
sagotra [sa₁gotra] amnf sagotrā soc. ["of the same gotra"] related; not. not eligible for marriage by exogamy — m. soc. distant relative — m. pa rented.
sagdhi [sa₁ad₁ti] m. common meal.

saṃkaṭá [samkaṭa] amnf saṃkaṭā contracted; narrow; crowded; dense; impassable — ifc. crowded with, full of (iic.) — n. difficult or dangerous passage | trouble; (figuratively) difficult situation, misery; calamity | affliction; not. mental illness — ifc. dangerous for; that which is threatened with (iic.) — f. saṃkaṭā phil. [Tantra] np. of Saṃkaṭā “An goisse”, one of the 8 divine powers [yoginī] — v. [11] pr. r. (saṃkaṭāyate) to become narrow; to shrink, to contract.
samkaṭahara [hara] amnf samkaṭaharā which facilitates passage — m. myth. np. of Samkatahara, epith. of Ganesa "which removes difficulties".
saṃkath [samkath] v. [10] pr. (saṃkathayati) pp. (kathita) to tell completely; to converse with (i.).
saṃkathā [act. saṃkath] f. discussion, conversation with (iic. i.) | agreement, understanding — ifc. conversation about (iic.).

saṃkara [act. saṃkṝ] m. mixture, confusion soc. not. mixture of castes |varnasamkara|; mixed caste | soc. illicit action; impurity, defilement | filth, excrement; dust, dirt | lit. rhet. mixture of incoherent metaphors; opp. samsṛṣṭi phil. ambiguity of ontological class.
samkarşa [agt. samkrş] amnf samkarşā near, neighbor.
saṃkarṣakāṇḍa [kāṇḍa] m. bed. from np. Samkarşakānda of Jaimini; cf. Samkarşanakānda.

saṃkarṣaṇa [act. saṃkṛṣ] n. extraction | reunion — m. myth. [BhP.] np. of Samkarşana, epith. of Balarāma "Subtracted" (from the womb of Devakī to be transferred into that of Rohinī₃) by the magic of Yogamāyā; he is the incarnation of AnantaSesa, and represents the destructive aspect of Vișnu; phil. as cosmic emanation [vyūha], he is the prakrti aspect of Purusottama, as Vāsudeva is the puruṣa aspect; Pra dyumna is the manas aspect, and Aniruddha is the ahamkāra aspect; in the spiritual heaven he is the direction of the West | lit. [Agamadambara] np. Samkarṣaṇa₁, a young snātaka brahmin, is scandalized by the bad behavior of the bd. and other heretics; tasked with policing religions, he must compromise his principles for political reasons.
saṃkarṣaṇakāṇḍa [kāṇḍa] m. bed. n.p. of Jaimini's Samkarşanakānda, in 4 chapters, basic work of mīmāṃsā, appendix to the Mīmāmsāsūtra.
saṃkal [samkal] v. [10] pr. (saṃkaláyati) pp. (samkalita) pf. (anu) to group, add.
saṃkalana [act. saṃkal] n. addition — f. samkalanā addition.
saṃkalita [pp. saṃkal] amnf saṃkalitā accumulated, added; mixed | included — n. math. addition — f. saṃkalitā math. sum of an arithmetic progression.

samkalpá var. sankalpa [act. saṃklp] m. vo will; desire, intention; conviction; commitment; determination; resolution (to (loc. dat. 11th century)) | lit. imagination; creativity | phil. the decision to act; opp. vikalpa | soc. solemn introductory act of the pūjā by which a sacrificer states their desire for the fruit of the sacrifice; this mental preparation includes meditation on the gods, the statement of the time and place of the ceremony | soc. solemn oath to fulfill a vow; not. for a widow to throw herself onto her husband's funeral pyre | myth. np. of Samkalpa, the personified "will" — 11th century. intentionally, of one's own volition; expressly — f. Samkalpā myth. np. of Samkalpā, mother of Samkalpa, daughter of Dakşa. samkalpamkr to resolve to, to decide to.
samkalpaja [ja] amnf samkalpajā produced by his will; willed, intentional — m. desire, wish; intention.
samkalpasūryodaya [sūryodaya] m. bed. n.p. from Saṃkalpasūryodaya, an allegorical drama by Vedāntadeśika; he rejects the worship of gods other than Vișnu and opposes the atheism of SāṃkhyaVaiśeṣika.
saṃkāś [samkāś] v. [1] pr. r. (saṃkāśate) pp. (saṃkāśita) to become visible, to manifest — ca. (saṃkāśayati) to look, to contemplate.
samkāśa [agt. samkāś] m. appearance, aspect — f. saṃkāśā ifc. resembling, having the appearance of (iic.).
saṃkāśya [pfp. [1] saṃkāś] amnf saṃkāśyā to contemplate, to admire.

saṃkīrṇa [pp. saṃkṝ] amnf saṃkīrṇā mixed, mingled; varied; confused, muddled, disordered; adulterated, defiled | soc. born of a mixed marriage — ifc. full of (iic.). samkīrņavarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Sāmānyakāṇḍa, dealing with various subjects.
samkīrt [samkīrt] v. [10] pr. (saṃkīrtayati) to announce, proclaim; to celebrate; to glorify.
samkīrtana [act. samkīrt] n. narration, saga, epic; praise | soc. recitation, not. by a congregation, of devotional songs, not. of litanies of the names of God; cf. mahāmantra, Caitanya.
saṃkuc [samkuc] v. [1] pr. r. (saṃkucati) pp. (samkucita) to contract, compress; to absorb — ca. (samkucayati) to decrease — ca. r. (samkocayate) to withdraw.
saṃkuñc [samkuñc] v. [6] pr. r. (saṃkuñcate) pp. (saṃkuñcita) to close (flower), to tighten.

saṃkula [samkula] amnf saṃkulā filled, crowded; thick, intense | troubled, confused; hindered, routed — ifc. full of, abundant in, infested by (iic.) — n. throng, crowd, melee; trouble, distress. samkulīkī to press in a crowd.
saṃkusumita [samkusumita] amnf saṃkusumitā covered with flowers | bd. manifest (in names of awakened ones [buddha]).
saṃkṛṣ [samkṛṣ] v. [6] pr. (saṃkṛṣati) to extract, to take away.
saṃkṝ [samkṝ] v. [6] pr. (saṃkirati) pp. (samkīrņa) to mix, to mingle; to confuse; to defile — ps. (saṃkīryate) to mix; to be defiled.

saṃklp [samklp] v. [1] pr. r. (saṃkalpate) pp. (samklpta) to realize; to be ready; to desire — ca. (samkalpayati) ca. r. (samkalpayate) to arrange; to imagine, to conceive; to intend to; to decide, to determine, to convince oneself of.

samketa [samketa] m. convention, agreement, agreed signal; appointment | gram. conventional meaning of a word; Bhartrhari distinguishes the original, permanent etymological meaning [ājānika], and the modern meaning, adopted as a technical definition [ādhunika] | lit. np. from the Saṃketa, commentary on the aesthetic treatise Kāvyaprakāśa, by Ruyyaka (Kaśmīra, 12th century) | lit. np. from the Saṃketa₁, commentary on the Harșacarita by Śaṃkara₃. samketīkṛ to set an appointment. samketam anurudhyasva keep your appointment. samketam anupālaya id.
saṃketasthāna [sthāna] n. meeting point.

samkoca var. sankoca [act. samkuc] m. contraction, compression, narrowing, abbreviation | reduction, restriction; retraction; drying up (of a pond or lake) | the act of closing (the eyes) | phil. [Trika] ascending phase of spiritual realization where the disciple purifies himself by performing the retraction of the phenomenal world; it is followed by a phase of expansion [vikāsa].
samkocana var. sankocana [agt. samkuc] amnf samkocanī astringent — act. n. contraction, narrowing, restriction; abbreviation — f. organic samkocanī. bot. Mimosa Pudica, sensitive.

saṃkram [samkram] v. [1] pr. (saṃkrāmati) pp. (saṃkrānta) to meet, approach, travel, cross, pass from (abl.) to (loc. acc.) astr. (Sun) to enter a sign of the zodiac — ca. (saṃkrāmayati) to lead towards (acc.); to transfer, transmit.

saṃkramá [act. saṃkram] m. encounter | journey; transition (towards (loc.)) | astr. journey of the Sun in the zodiac | fall of a meteorite gram. encounter of two words in the text in krama mode | access staircase to a well | difficult access path.

saṃkrámaṇa [act. saṃkram] n. encounter; entry into (loc. dat. 2nd century) | beginning (not. old age) astr. entry of the Sun into a sign of the zodiac astr. solstice | passage into the other world, death. makarasamkramanam astr. date of entry into the sign of Capricorn, January 15.

saṃkrānta [pp. saṃkram] amnf samkrāntā met, reunited; transferred (from (abl.) to (loc.) | represented in image; reflected — n. lit. [KM.] transfer from a conventional meaning to a new meaning, poetic quality authorizing the borrowing of a phrase; figure of speech of reflection of a borrowed phrase.

samkrānti var. sankrānti [act. samkram] f. encounter, passage | transmission, transfer (not. from master to disciple) | bd. yoga of the transfer of consciousness, where one reaches the state of awakening [buddha], a saddharma | astr. passage of the sun (or a star) into a new sign of the zodiac [rāśi]; there is one per month, between the 13th and the 17th; this day is unfavorable and traditionally fasted [upavāsa] | [makarasamkrānti] astr. Indian new year, cf. makarasamkrānti.
saṃkrīḍ [samkrīḍ] v. [1] pr. r. (saṃkrīḍate) to play together; to play with (i.) — v. [1] pr. (saṃkrīḍati) to creak (char).
saṃkrudh var. saṅkrudh [samkrudh₁] v. [4] pr. (saṃkrudhyati) pp. (saṃkruddha) to be irritated; to get angry.
saṃkliś [samkliś] v. [9] pr. (saṃkliśnāti) pp. (saṃkliṣṭa) to afflict, torment, to cause suffering, to pain — ps. (kliśyate) to be soiled.
saṃkliṣṭa [pp. saṃkliś] amnf saṃkliṣṭā crushed; bruised | soiled; moldy; tarnished.
saṃkleśa [act. saṃkliś] m. contusion; souf france | soiling, loss of shine.
saṃkṣaya [act. saṃkṣī] m. exhaustion, destruction, annihilation, ruin; twilight.
saṃkṣip [samkṣip] v. [6] pr. (saṃkṣipati) pp. (saṃkṣipta) to pile up, to overturn; to tighten, to compress, to reduce, to diminish.
saṃkṣipta [pp. saṃkṣip] amnf saṃkṣiptā compressed, abbreviated, concise, brief.
samkṣī [samkṣī] ps. (saṃkṣīyate) to diminish, to perish, to exhaust oneself, to vanish, to die out; to decrease (moon).
saṃkṣubdha [pp. saṃkṣubh] amnf saṃkṣubdhā violently agitated, shaken.
saṃkṣubh [samkṣubh] pp. (saṃkṣubdha, samkṣubhita) ca. (samkṣobhayati) pp. (saṃkṣobhita) to shake violently, to agitate.
saṃkṣubhita [pp. saṃkṣubh] amnf samksubhitā violently agitated, shaken.
saṃkṣepa [act. saṃkṣip] m. abbreviation, concise statement, summary, summary; the essentials. samksepena var. samksepāt adv. in short, in summary. samksepatas adv. briefly.
saṃkṣobha [act. saṃkṣubh] m. violent shock, reversal, upheaval | commotion; agitation, excitement | arrogance.
saṃkṣobhita [pp. ca. saṃkṣubh] amnf samkṣobhitā violently agitated, shaken.
saṃkṣṇu [samkṣṇu] v. [2] pr. r. (saṃkṣṇute) to sharpen well | to stimulate, excite, intensify. samksnute śastram he sharpens his weapon.
saṃkhya [agt. saṃkhyā₁] amnf saṃkhyā ifc. who adds, who counts (iic.) — act. n. com bat, battle — f. cf. samkhyā₁. gosamkhya he who counts the cows.
saṃkhyā₁ [samkhyā] v. [2] pr. (saṃkhyāti) pp. (samkhyāta) pf. (pari, pra) count, calculate.

samkhyā₁ [f. samkhya] f. count, calculation, arithmetic; number, quantity, total | gram. number (neuter form used for counting, such as ekam, dve, trīṇi, catvāri, etc.) | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] the property [guṇa] of number | math. symb. the number 9.
samkhyāpari | pari | ind. unfavorable roll of the dice.
samkhyāvakratā [vakratā] f. lit. [Kuntaka] oblique quality of the use of grammatical number.
saṃkhyāvat [vat] amnf saṃkhyāvatī equipped with a number; numbered | intelligent — adv. like a number.
sáṃkhyāta [pp. saṃkhyā₁] amnf samkhyātā enumerated, counted, measured; countable; estimated at (i.) — n. math. ordinal number; multitude.
samkhyāna var. sankhyāna [act. saṃkhyā₁] n. estimation, count; calculation, enumeration.
saṃkhyeya [pfp. [1] saṃkhyā₁] amnf saṃkhyeyā enumerable, countable; cardinal (number) | to be considered.
samkhyeyavācaka [vācaka] m. ordinal number.

saṅga [act. sañj] m. adherence, contact (with (loc. iic.)); association, meeting; society attachment, affection, inclination, attraction (towards (loc.); desire, envy, greed. mrgā mrgaih sangamanuvrajanti gāvaśca gobhis turagāsturangaih | mūrkhāśca mūrkhaih sudhiyah sudhībhiḥ | [PT.] does gather with does, cows with cows, horses with horses, fools with fools and wise men with wise men.
saṃgaṇaka var. saṅgaṇaka [samgaṇaka] m. abacus, calculator.
samganakayantra | yantra | n. mod. computer.

saṃgata var. saṅgata [pp. saṃgam] amnf saṃgatā That which has met, That which has come together; contracted | put together, assembled | conform, suitable — m. alliance, peace — n. meeting, accord, association, union; association, intimacy with (ig iic.).
saṃgatārtha | artha | amnf saṃgatārthā gram. (compound) whose meaning is conventional.

samgati var. sangati [act. samgam] f. encounter, company of (g. ii.); association with (i.) | league, alliance, society, association | accident, chance; becoming aware | applicability, conformity, adequacy | gram. [Mīmāmsā] relation of discourse coherence; we distinguish: śāstrasangati coherence of the subject of a work, adyāyasangati coherence at the level of the chapter or book, padasangati at the level of the section, adhikaranasangati coherence of the articulation of the discourse. saṃgatyā adv. by chance, by accident.

saṃgam var. saṅgam [samgam] v. [1] pr. r. (samgacchate) pp. (samgata) pf. (upa) to meet, to gather, to enter into relations with (i.) | to come to an understanding, to agree — ca. (saṃgamayati) abs. (saṃgamayya) to gather, to unite; to bring into contact with (i.); to lead someone towards 2 acc.; to transmit to loc. . samgacchadhvam gather together. ratnam ratnena samgacchate Birds of a feather flock together.

saṃgama var. saṅgama [act. saṃgam] m. encounter; collision; meeting, contact; union; team | confluence of two tivières | frequentation; pen song, attraction; carnal union | hist. np. of sangama, father of Harihara₁ and Bukka₁, who founded the eponymous Vijayanagara dynasty (14th century); the dynasty died out in 1485 and was followed by the Saluva dynasty.
saṃgamanātha [nātha] m. geo. np. of the temple of Sangamanātha at Kudālasangama, of Cālukya style (12th century); Basavanna and Siva are identified there as the svayambhūlinga Aikya.
samgameśvara [īśvara] m. myth. of np. samgameśvara, epith. of Siva "Master of river confluences".
saṃgamana var. saṅgamana [act. saṃgam] n. meeting, gathering (with (iic.)) | participation in (i.).
saṃgara₁ [act. saṃgr₁] m. act of swallowing, devouring; engulfment | [Kāmasūtra] mode of fellatio [auparistaka] where the penis penetrates completely — n. poison | calamity.
samgara₂ [act. samgr₁] m. consent, agreement, accord | conflict, fight; battle (for (g.), with (i.) | transaction.
saṃgava var. saṅgava [samgava] m. ["gathering of cows (for milking)"] period of the day [kāla₁] of the morning, Which follows the prātastana; it begins 2 h 24 after sunrise, and lasts 2 h 24.
saṃgā [samgā₂] v. [1] pr. (saṃgāyati) pp. (saṃgīta) to sing in chorus; to celebrate by singing together.

saṅgin [agt. sañj] amnf saṅginī Who is attached to, Who adheres to, in contact with (iic.) | given to, devoted to, connected with (g. loc. iic.) | phil. attached to the world; filled with desires; given to the pleasures of this world.
samgīta var. sangīta [pp. samgā] amnf saṃgītā sung in chorus — n. choir, song, sung theatre; music, concert.
Samgītamakaranda [makaranda] m. bed. n.p. from Saṃgītamakaranda, a Carnatic musicology text attributed to Nārada.
samgītaratnākara [ratnākara] m. lit. np. from samgītaratnākara, a 13th-century musicological text.
saṃgītaśālā |śālā| f. music room.
samgītasudhā [sudhā] f. lit. np. of the Saṅgītasudhā "Nectar of Music", a treatise on musical theory composed by Govinda₁ Dīkṣita for King Rag hunātha₂ Nāyaka.
saṃgīti [act. saṃgā] f. choral, concert, symphony; song combined with music and dance.
saṃgṛhīta [pp. saṃgrah] amnf saṃgṛhītā seized, caught; received, collected, seemed; well received | contracted, abbreviated; restrained, constrained, mastered; governed.
saṃgṛhīti [act. saṃgrah] f. mastery, control.
saṃgṝ₁ [samgṝ₁] v. [6] pr. (saṃgirati) pp. (saṃgīrṇa) to swallow, to devour — v. [6] pr. r. (samgirate) to promise. satam samgirate he promises (to pay) one hundred (coins).
saṃgṝ₂ [samgṝ₂] v. [9] pr. (saṃgṛṇāti) pr. r. (samgrnīte) to agree, to accept; to promise | to praise, to celebrate.

saṃgrah var. saṅgrah [samgrah] v. [9] pr. (saṃgrhṇāti) pr. r. (saṃgrhṇīté) pp. (saṃgrhīta) pf. (upa) to seize, take possession of, appropriate; to heap up, accumulate | to govern, constrain, hold in one's power; to master, understand | to protect, receive, marry.

Samgraha var. sangraha [act. samgrah] m. the act of seizing, taking possession of; appropriation | accumulation, collection, gathering; complete enumeration, totality | understanding, summary; catalogue, compendium | gram. np. of the Samgraha, Vyādi's ancient grammar to which the Mahābhāṣya refers | protection, government; guardian, protector | cohesion; concentration, discipline of mind | clenched fist | mod. management || Pali samgaha. samgrahāt adv. in summary, briefly. samgrahena adv. in summary, briefly; completely.
samgrahaśloka |śloka| m. lit. summary verse of a passage (in prose mixed with aphorisms |sūtra|).
Samgrahasūtra [sūtra] n. lit. from the np. Samgrahasūtra, a collection of traditional aphorisms.
saṃgráhaṇa [agt. saṃgrah] amnf samgrahaṇī that takes, that seizes — act. n. sai sie, taking, gain; reception, acquisition incrustation, act of setting (jewel) | sexual act (with (iic.)); adultery.
saṃgráhaṇīya [pfp. [2] saṃgrah] amnf samgrahaṇīyā which one must seize | which one must take as a remedy.
saṃgrahin [agt. saṃgrah] amnf samgrahinī that assembles, that accumulates, that procures; that masters, that understands.
saṃgrahītṛ [agt. saṃgrah] amnf saṃgrahītrī who seizes, who acquires — m. soc. high royal official, in charge of war chariots; he is part of the royal circle |ratnin|.

saṃgrāmá var. saṅgrāma [samgrāma] m. soc. gathering, assembly of a people; troop, army | confrontation, conflict; combat, battle; war; hostile encounter with (i. iic.) — v. [11] pr. r. (saṃgrāmayate) impft. r. (asaṃgrāmayata) com to fight, to wage war. bahusamgrāmakarsita very emaciated by fighting.
samgrāmájit [jit] amnf victorious in combat.
samgrāmábhūmi [bhūmi] f. battlefield.

saṃgrāmarāja [rāja] m. hist. np. of the king samgrāmarāja of Kaśmīra, founder of the Lohara dynasty in 1003; he was installed by his aunt Diddadevī, whose lover Tunga, prime minister, was plundering the kingdom; at his death in 1028 his son Harirāja succeeded him, was assassinated, and his younger son Ananta₁ succeeded him.
saṃgrāhin [agt. saṃgrah] amnf samgrāhiņī that collects, that accumulates, that seems | astringent; constipating.
saṃgha var. saṅgha [act. saṃhan] m. collection, quantity; multitude, crowd; association, company, assembly | bd. congregation of Buddhist monks | soc. republic.
samghabheda [bheda] amnf samghabhedā bd. which causes division in the congregation (one of the 5 unforgivable sins).
samghabhedavastu [vastu₁] n. bd. n.p. of the samghabhedavastu, text of the comic canon.
samghārāma [ārāma] m. bd. convent, monastery; syn. vihāra.
saṃghaṭ [samghaṭ] v. [1] pr. r. (saṃghaṭate) pp. (saṃghaṭita) to assemble; to meet — ca. (saṃghaṭayati) to assemble, to join.
saṃghaṭa [obj. saṃghaṭ] amnf saṃghaṭā piled up, heaped.
saṃghaṭana [act. saṃghaṭ] ifc. n. union with (iic.).

saṃghaṭanā [f. saṃghaṭana] f. gram. combination of words or morphemes | lit. Anandavardhana texture, lexical style; not. density of compounds; there are three types: asamāsā (absence of compounds), madhyamasamāsā (short compounds), dīrghasamāsā (long compounds).
samghaṭṭ [samghaṭṭ] v. [10] pr. (samghattayati) to rub together; to knead; to crush | to gather; to meet.

saṃghaṭṭa [act. saṃghaṭṭ] m. friction, friction; collision, conflict | encounter; coitus | phil. [Trika] conflict in the central psychic path [Suṣumṇā] between the Sun and the Moon representing all dualities.
samgharsa [act. samghṛṣ] m. friction; trituration | rivalry | jealousy (reverse (acc.prati iic.)).

samghāṭá [act. samghat] m. act of crushing; destruction | compression, compaction; assembly, aggregate; heap; syn. samūha | not. wood assembly; carpentry, joinery | collection, gathering, crowd; mass, multitude; horde; caravan gram. syllable; compound word; phrase.
samghāṭasūtra [sūtra] n. bd. np. of the samghāṭasūtra, text of the Mahāyāna originally in Sanskrit, prior to the 5th century.
samghāti [act. samghat] f. bd. monastic garment for winter, draped, exposing the right shoulder and forming folds on the left arm; cf. tricīvara | var. samghātī id.

saṃghātá [act. saṃhan] mn com combat, battle, confrontation; encounter, opposition | compression, condensation, hardening | collection, heap; gathering, mass, multitude, crowd; caravan | gram. compound word | phon. syllable (vowel accompanied by the preceding consonants); opp. varņa | bd. np. of Saṃghāta, one of the 8 burning hells, overhung by falling rocks to crush the damned — f. saṃghātā ifc. collection of (iic.).
saṃghātavat [vat] amnf saṃghātavatī com pact, dense.
saṃghātaśilā |śilā| f. hard stone used as an anvil to crack coconuts.
saṃghṛṣ [samghṛṣ] v. [1] pr. (saṃgharṣati) pp. (saṃghṛṣṭa) to rub against each other | compete with (i.).
saṃghṛṣṭa [pp. saṃghṛṣļ amnf saṃghṛṣṭā rubbed with; confronted with.
sac₁ iic. sat.

√ sac [reli 'ea sa ~nj] v. [1] pr. r. (s 'acate) to be united with, to unite with (i.) | to be possessed by, to participate in, to undergo (i.) | to serve, to follow, to accompany, to seek, to assist (acc.) | to reach | lat. sequitur.
sacakita [sa₁cakita] amnf sacakitā trembling, fearful, intimidated. sacakitam trembling, with fear.
sacarācara |sa₁carācara| amnf sa carācarā including all creatures — n. the uni vers.
sáci [saci] conj. ved. with.
sacitra [sa₁citra] amnf sacitrā forné of paintings | illustrated.
saciva [saciva] m. friend, companion | advisor to the king, minister; syn. amātya — ifc. aided by, provided with (iic.) — f. sacivī companion, friend.
sacivatā [tā] f. soc. quality of minister.
sacivatva [vat] n. soc. rank of minister.
sacivālaya [ālaya] mn mod. ministry (building).
sacī cf. śacī.
sacetana [sa₁cetana] amnf sacetanī conscious, sensitive, animated, living; opp. acetana.
sacetanatā [tā] f. state of being alive; sensitivity.
sacetas [sa₁cetas] amnf of the same opinion, unanimous | rational, intelligent, sensitive — m. man of heart.
sajala |sa₁jala| amnf sajalā moist; containing water.
sajalatva |tva| n. humidity.
sajalanayana | nayana | amnf sajalanayana with moist eyes (said notably of peacocks).
sajāta [sa₁jāta] amnf sajātā born together of the same family; of the same origin — m. cousin, relative; country.
sajātīya [īya| amnf sajātīyā soc. of the same family, clan or class | homogeneous; similar; res resembling.
sajāti [sa₁jāti] amnf of the same class or species; similar; homogeneous.
sajīva [sa₁jīva] amnf sajīvā living, animated.
sajus |sa₁jus₂| amnf that accompanies; associate, companion — ind. sajūs at the same time; moreover | with i. .
sajj cf. sañj.

sajja [sa₁jyā₃] amnf sajjā prepared, equipped, ready (not. bow ready to fire) | armed; fortified — f. sajjā equipment; armor — v. [11] pr. r. (sajjīyate) to be ready. sajjīkr to prepare. sajjībhū to prepare; to get ready, to prepare oneself; to be ready.
sañca m. sheets for writing; notebook, notepad.
sañcaka |ka| mr. seal — f. sañcikā notebook.
saṃcaya var. sañcaya [act. saṃci] m. collection; accumulation, heap | pile, multitude; wealth.

saṃcar var. sañcar [samcar] v. [1] pr. (samcarati) pp. (samcarita) to go together, to meet; to travel, to journey, to cross | to live, to exist, to occur — ca. (saṃcārayati) to make go, to set in motion, to shake, to agitate. āsane śayane yāne samparke sahabhojane sañcaranti mahāghore narake kālamakṣayam | Those who sit, lie down, walk, or share a meal (with an outcaste) will go for an interminable time to the most horrible of hells.

saṃcara var. sañcara [loc. saṃcar] m. passage difficult passage; defile, pass; crossing of torrent soc. space of movement, path to follow in a rite | phil. |Sāṃkhya| evolution, development; emanation.
samcarana var. sañcarana [act. saṃcar] n. act of gathering; assembly; convergence passage, way, path; motion; crossing from (abl.), in (loc.), by means of (iic.).
samcal [samcal] v. [1] pr. (samcalati) pp. (samcalita) to sway about; to oscillate, to tremble — ca. (saṃcālayati) to agitate, to shake | to expel (from (abl.), to drive away.
saṃcalana [act. saṃcal] n. agitation, trembling.
samcār var. sañcār [ca. samcar] v. [10] pr. (samcārayati) to make go, to set in motion, to shake, to agitate.

saṃcāra var. sañcāra [act. saṃcar] m. circulation, movement, displacement, course; frequentation, passage, crossing; transition | course of life; existence, career | path of passage of an animal, traces | transmission (disease), contagion — loc. m. path, route.

saṃcārin var. sañcārin [agt. saṃcar] amnf samcāriņī that circulates, that walks; mobile | that spreads, that passes from one to another; contagious; hereditary | contiguous; bordering — ifc. at (iic.).
saṃcālana var. sañcālana [act. ca. saṃcal] n. agitation, setting in motion | putting into application.
saṃci var. sañci [samci] v. [5] pr. (saṃcinóti) pr. r. (samcinuté) pp. (samcita) to pile up, accumulate, gather, acquire.
samcita var. sañcita [pp. samci] amnf samcitā accumulated, piled up, assembled, collected; ac
quis | dense, full | phil. part of the accumulated karma which will bear fruit in due time.
samcint var. sañcint [samcint] v. [10] (saṃcintáyati) pp. (saṃcintita) ppr. r. pr. (saṃcintayāna) pfp. (saṃcintya) to think about, to be concerned about (acc.).
saṃcintayāna var. sañcintayāna [ppr. mo. samcint] amnf samcintayānā who reflects, who thinks.
saṃcintya var. sañcintya [pfp. [1] saṃcint] amnf saṃcintyā which deserves reflection, to consider, something to think about.
saṃcud [samcud] ca. (saṃcodáyati) pp. (samcudita) ppr. (samcodayat) to incite, to push, to lead; to excite, to stimulate; to order.
samchad var. sañchad [samchad₁] pp. (saṃchanna) ca. (saṃchādayati) to cover completely, to wrap; to cover, to hide.
saṃchanna var. sañchanna [pp. saṃchad] amnf sañchannā entirely covered; hidden, concealed; obscure, unknown.

saṃchid var. sañchid [samchid₁] v. [7] pr. (samchinatti) pr. r. (samchintté) to cut into pieces; to pierce, to slice | to resolve (doubt); to decide (decision) — ps. (samchidyate) to be cut into pieces.
samchinna [pp. samchid] amnf samchinnā cut into pieces; sliced.

√ sañj var. saj v. [1] pr. (sájati) pft. (sasañja) pp. (sakta) pf. (ati, anu, ā, ni, pra, vi, sam) to adhere — v. [1] pr. r. (sajjate) to be attached to, to be suspended from (loc.) | to be devoted, to be attached, to care for (affectively); to think constantly about (loc.) — ca. (saj jayati) to make adhere; to engage in (loc.), to become attached to (loc.) | to prostitute, to deliver (one's wife) to others | lat. segnis.

samjan var. sañjan [samjan] v. [4] pr. r. (samjāyate) pp. (samjāta) ["to be produced simultaneously"] to be born, to occur — ca. (samjanayati) to conceive, to engender; to produce, to create, to form; to cause, to bring about. tasya samjanayan harsam [BhG.] to rejoice.

samjaya var. Sañjaya [agt. samji] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Sañjaya, "who masters his senses", bard of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; he knows the past, present and future by his divine vision [divyacakṣus]; he made an embassy to Yudhisthira at Upaplavya to try to avoid war; he told Dhṛtarāṣṭra about the great battle.

saṃjāta var. sañjāta [pp. saṃjan] amnf samjātā produced, born, grown; appeared, became | past (time). tasya smrtilopah samjātah his memory failed him. iti tasya buddhau na samjātam that did not occur to him.
saṃji var. sañji [samji] v. [1] pr. (saṃjayati) pp. (samjita) to overcome together | to conquer completely; to master (one's senses).
saṃjīv var. sañjīv [samjīv] v. [1] pr. (samjīvati) pp. (samjīvita) to return to life.

saṃjīvá var. sañjīva [agt. saṃjīv] amnf samjīvā vivifying; that which restores life — m. return to life | bd. np. of Samjīva, one of the 8 burning hells, with a floor of burning iron; it owes its name to the fact that, as soon as a damned person dies of suffering, he is immediately brought back to life.
samjīvakaranī [karanī] f. cf. samjīvanī.
samjīvaka [agt. samjīv] amnf samjīvikā which brings back to life — m. lit. [PT.] np. of the bull samjīvaka, friend of the lion Pingalaka₁; he will be lost by the jealousy of the jackal Damanaka.

samjīvana var. sañjīvana [agt. samjīv] amnf samjīvanī vivifying; that which animates or restores life — act. n. resurrection, life — f. saṃjīvanī myth. [Rām.] resurrection herb samjīvanī or saṃjīvakaraṇī , brought back by Hanuman from the Himalayas to heal Rama's army | myth. [BhP.] the science of resurrection, possessed by Sukra; he used it to bring Bali back to life after he died in battle against the gods; he transmitted its secret to Kaca | lit. np. from the Sañjīvanī, commentary on the epic poems [mahākāvya] Raghuvaṃśa, Kumārasambhava and Meghadūta of Kālidāsa by Mallinātha₁.
samjñaka [agt. sañjñā₁] ifc. amnf samjñikā which is called, known as (iic.).

samjnā₁ var. sanjnā₁ [samjnā₁] v. [9] pr. (samjānāti) pp. (samjñāta) to assign; to understand, to have awareness of | to remember sadly g. — v. [9] pr. r. (saṃjānīte) to know well, to understand — ca. (samjñāpayati) ved. ["to make consent" | to kill (the sacrificial animal) | to make understood; to communicate; to instruct.

samjnā₂ var. sanjnā₂ [act. samjnā₁] f. harmony, consent; Consciousness; perception, common understanding | sign, signal; name, reference, designation, appellation; signifier gram. word evoking an entity specific to the context, memorized, not morphologically analyzable; not. proper noun; autonym (denoting its own form); technical term, metanotion; neologism; terminology; opp. abhidhā₂ | gram. word whose gender or number is conventional, such as dāra | phil. individual Consciousness | bd. perception, one of the 5 aggregates [skandha] of the mythic ego. [HV.] np. of sañjñā₁ "Consciousness", daughter of Viśvakarmā, wife of Sūrya, with whom she bore ManuVaivasvata, Yama, and Yamī; unable to bear her husband's ardor, she had her servant, the Shade [Chāyā], take her place and transformed herself into a mare to devote herself to meditation; Sūrya Vivasvān followed her, and they gave birth to the Aśvinau and Revanta; Viśvakarmā then reduced the Sun's brightness by one-eighth so that she could bear it; cf. Saraṇyū | pali saññā. samjñāyām loc. adv. gram. when used as a proper noun. samjñām kṛ to beckon. samjñām dā to give a sign. samjñām cetanām labh to regain one's senses. ekadravyopaniveśinī samjñā₁ a samjñā₁ refers to a unique object.
samjñāsūtra [sūtra] n. gram. [Pāṇini] rule [sūtra] defining a technical term or a proper name.
samjñāta var. sañjñāta [pp. samjñā₁] amnf samjñātā well known, understood — ifc. for the purpose of (iic.).
saṃjñāna [agt. saṃjñā₁] amnf saṃjñānī ved. that produces harmony or unanimity — act. n. full Consciousness | correct perception, good conception.
samjñānasūkta [sūkta] n. lit. final hymn of the Rigveda (10.191), advocating brotherhood.
saṃjñita var. sañjñita [saṃjñā₁ita] amnf samjñitā communiqué — ifc. called, named (iic.).
saṃjñin [agt. saṃjñā₁] amnf saṃjñinī conscious; conscious of (iic.) | named, defined | gram. defined notion.
samjvar var. sañjvar [samjvar] v. [1] pr. (samjvarati) to have a high fever, to be very ill | to be very sad, to be afflicted.
saṃjvara [act. saṃjvar] m. high fever; great agitation.
saṃjvārin [agt. saṃjvar] amnf samjvāriņī feverish.
saṭā f. braid.
satta n. arch. chamranle.
sattaka |ka| n. bed. minor form of drama; cf. Karpūramañjarī.

sat [ppr. as₁] amnf satī existing, present; real, true | good, just, virtuous, suitable, honest bd. just, correct; wonderful; profound, subtle | qqf. added as a pleonasm of an a. — n. phil. Being; the real | good, virtue — m. (man) just, good, virtuous; virtuous man | pl. satas the just; learned people — f. cf. satī. tatraivam sati that being so. tathā sati if it is so. nāmni kṛte sati the name having been given. saccidānanda phil. [Vedānta] existenceConsciousness joy, formula evoking ecstasy in the fusion brahmanātman. nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ |BhG.| From nothingness nothing comes, from Being nothing is destroyed.
saccaritra | caritra | n. good conduct — amnf saccaritrā virtuous.
sacchūdra |śūdra| amnf sacchūdrā soc. servant | sūdra | of good conduct, not. vegetarian and abstinent.
sajjana | jana | amnf sajjanī virtuous — m. good man.
sátkartr | kartr | amnf satkartrī that does good.
sátkarman | karman | n. good action; virtue — amnf satkarmaṇī that does good actions; killing, pious worm.
sátkriya [kriyā] amnf satkriyā that does good; virtuous — f. satkriyā preparation, putting in order | good action; virtue | pious action; purificatory ceremony; funeral rite.
sattā [tā] f. existence.
sattāsamavāya |samavāya| m. phil. |vaišesika| inherence of universal reality; characterizes existence | sattva |.
sattāsāmānya [sāmānya] n. phil. generality.
satpakṣa [pakṣa] amnf satpakṣā useful, favorable; opp. pratipakṣa.
satpuṣpa | puṣpa | amnf satpuṣpā in bloom.
satpustaka [pustaka] mn lit. (manuscript) authentic.
satsanga | sanga | m. association with good; good company; assembly for spiritual purposes | soc. proximity to the master [guru] | gram. group of consecutive consonants.
satsangin [sangin] amnf satsanginī which associates itself with good.
satsangijīvana [jīvana] n. lit. np. of the satsangijīvana, a work explaining the life and teachings of Svāminārāyaṇa, by his disciple Satānanda₁.
satata [sa₁tata₁] amnf satatā perpetual. satatam adv. always. nasatatam adv. never.
satatayukta [yukta] amnf satatayuktā phil. in perpetual communion (with God).
satarka [sa₁tarka] amnf satarkā rai ringer; good at argumentation | careful; attentive.

Satī [f. sat] f. woman of quality, lady | faithful wife, virtuous and chaste woman | soc. widow who commits suicide on her husband's funeral pyre; cf. sahamarana | myth. np. of Satī "Virtuous", daughter of Dakṣa and Asiknī, first wife of Śiva; after SivaVīrabhadra destroyed Dakṣa's sacrifice to which he had not been invited, she threw herself into the sacrificial fire; her corpse was carried across the world by Shiva in a state of madness, torn to pieces by the disk of Viṣṇu; cf. pīṭhasthāna; she was reborn as Pārvatī; cf. Jagadamba | ang. suttee.
satīrtha [sa₁tīrtha] amnf satīrthā geo. who possesses a holy place — m. soc. who shares the same master of studies.
satīrthya |ya| m. soc. disciple of the same master; fellow student.
satṛṇa |sa₁tṛṇa| amnf satṛṇā with grass — iic. (ifc.) stuffing and chaff. satṛṇam adv. stuffing and chaff.
satṛṇābhyavahārin [abhyavahārin] amnf satṛṇābhyavahāriṇī who swallows everything without discernment; credulous.
satkāra |act. satkṛ| m. hospitality, respectful welcome | pl. satkārās honors (rendered to a guest).
satkārya [pfp. [1] satkṛ] amnf satkāryā which is well done | to whom the last homage (of cremation) is paid — n. phil. [Sāṃkhya] ef fet necessarily inherent in a cause.

satkāryavāda [vāda] m. phil. [Sāṃkhya] theory of causality, doctrine affirming the necessary pre-existence of an effect in its cause, as the pot pre-exists in the clay with which it was made; opp. asatkāryavāda.
satkṛ [satkṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (satkaróti) pp. (satkṛta) to offer hospitality, to welcome with respect. gurūn satkṛtya gataḥ he left after having honored the masters.
satkṛta [pp. satkṛ] amnf satkṛtā arranged, adorned with | honored, well received; welcome.
sattama [super. sat] amnf sattamā the best, excellent, very fair — ifc. the best of (iic.).

sattrá [instr. sad₁] n. soc. ["session"] grand sa crifice de soma (solemn Vedic ceremony lasting from 13 to 100 days) | soc. meritorious pious act; offering of food, boiler, hospice | false appearance, disguise | soc. ambush | var. satra id. sattrībhū to offer meals as alms. gavo vai sattram āsata Vedic. the cows performed a great sacrifice (to obtain horns).
sattragrha [grha] n. hospice.
sattrādhikāra [adhikāra] m. soc. priest in charge of a charity.
sattrin [sattrain] amnf sattriṇī soc. who celebrates or attends a sattra; meritorious | disguised; spy.

Sattva |sattva| n. being, creature; fetus; existence, reality, nature; Essence | strength, energy; courage, strength of character | spirit, vital breath, vital principle | intelligence, consciousness, truth; purity [phil. [Sāṃkhya] the Good or Pure Essence of Being, the first quality [guna] of nature, quintessence of purity and truth; its efficacy [arthakriyā] is clarity [prakāśa] | [dravya₁] gram. substance — m. living creature, animal; fetus, embryo | phantom, demon, monster | myth. np. of Sattva, a son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra | var. satva id. abhivyaktasattvalakṣaṇā manifestly pregnant. āpannasattvā f. (woman) pregnant.
sattvaguṇa [guṇa] m. phil. [Sāṃkhya] the quality of Good, Essence of purity and truth.
sattvagunamaya |maya| afmn sattvaguṇamayī which has the quality of Good.
sattvapariplava [pariplava] m. med. instability of thought.
sattvavat [vat] amnf sattvavatī firm, energetic; brave, courageous.
sattvastha |stha| amnf sattvastha inherent in its own nature; in accordance with its state | established in its own nature; resolute; energetic | phil. established in truth; dedicated to the Good.
sattvāpatti [āpatti] f. phil. [YV.] the attainment of the state of Pure consciousness, 4th level of knowledge [jñānabhūmikā].

satyá [satya] amnf satyā true, truthful | Vedic accomplished; promised to fulfillment — n. reality; truth, veracity | promise, oath | phil. sincerity, one of the virtues [yama₁] of yoga | cf. sa tyaloka — f. satyā sincerity, veracity — v. [11] pr. (satyāpayati) to tell the truth. satyam var. satyena adv. truly, really, in truth, it is true that. satyátas adv. in truth; really. yatsatyam adv. certainly. tenasatyena conj. as true (as ... previously expressed by yathā). satyam vac to tell the truth. sātyā kṛ to make true | to conclude an agreement. satyāt nāsti parodharmaḥ There is no law higher than truth. satyameva jayate nānrtam satyena panthā vitato devayānaḥ | yenākramantyrṣayo hyāptakāmā ya tra tat satyasya paramam nidhānam || |MO.| Only truth triumphs, not sin; only truth unfolds the royal road traveled by the wise who control their desires, and which is the supreme reservoir of truth.
satyaka [ka] amnf satyikā truthful — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of king vṛṣṇi satyaka "Truthful", son of Sini, father of Sātyaki.

satyákāma [kāma] amnf satyakāmā who loves truth; sincere — m. phil. [ChU.] np. of the boy Satyakāma "sincere"; seeking to become a brah macārin, he asked his mother Jabālā for her gotra name; she replied that when she was young she worked as a servant, and that in this way she brought him into the world; if he were asked for his gotra name, and he was sincere and she was Jabālā, he should say that his name was Satyakāma Jābāla; when he repeated these words to Hāridrumata Gautama, the latter told him that he accepted him as a student, for only a true brāhmaṇa could be so sincere; The guru entrusted him with 400 lean cows, which he took to graze in the high pastures; when the cows had prospered to a thousand, the bull told him to bring them back to the stable; on the way, it taught him the four parts [kalā] of the quarter |pāda| of Brahman constituted by Space [prakāśavat]; the next day, the fire taught him the four parts of the quarter of Brahman constituted by the Illi
mite [anantavat]; then the swan [hamsa] taught him the 4 parts of the quarter of Brahman constituted by the

Radiant [jyotismat]; finally, the plunge [madgu] taught him the four parts of the quarter of Brahman constituted by the Cognitive [āyatanavat]; he then found his master, who completed his instruction; having become a teacher himself, Satyakāma took on students; he neglected his student Upakosala Kāmalāyana for 12 years without giving him any instruction, then went on a journey; his sacrificial fires instructed the student of the
Soi [Atmā], and Satyakāma returned to teach him Liberation.
satyákriyā [kriyā] f. ["act of truth"] promise, oath | pali saccakiriyā.
satyajit [jit] amnf who conquers through truth.
satyátā [tva] f. veracity; truth, reality.
satyátva [tva] n. id.
satyadeva [deva] m. myth. "God of truth", epithet of Varuna.
satyanāman [nāman] amnf satyanāmnī Well named, justly named — m. satyanāma f. sa tyanāmā id.
satyanārāyaṇa [nārāyaṇa] m. phil. np. of Sa tyanārāyaṇa, aspect of Viṣṇu to whom one addresses oneself to make a solemn resolution.
satyanārāyaṇakathā | kathā₁ | f. lit. np. of the Sa tyanārāyaṇakathā, description of the ritual and its consequences, part of the Revākhanda of the SP.
satyanārāyaṇapūjā [pūjā] f. soc. ceremony by which a resolution is publicly declared or an important event such as the birth of a child is celebrated.
satyanārāyaṇavrata | vrata | n. soc. public resolution.
satyapratiśrava | pratiśrava | amnf satya pratiśravā faithful to his vows.

satyabhāmā [bhāmā] f. myth. np. of satyabhāmā "Passionate about truth", daughter of Satrājit, one of the 8 wives of Kṛṣṇa, by whom she had 10 sons; she was an incarnation of Bhūmi; she helped Kṛṣṇa to defeat Naraka by driving his chariot, and by shooting a fatal arrow; she was of a jealous nature, notably towards Rukminī; Kṛṣṇa took her to Indra's paradise, and she incited her to steal the pārijāta tree there, as a result of Nārada's indiscretions; cf. Muktācarita.
satyáyuga | yuga | n. phil. the first yuga, the golden age; syn. krtayuga.
satyáloka | loka | m. myth. np. of Satyaloka "Heaven of Brahmā", supreme 7th celestial world, where those who are delivered from rebirths are transported.
satyávacana [vacana] n. sincerity; truthfulness | promise, oath.

satyávat |vat| amnf Satyavatī₁ truthful, sincere — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of King Satyavān "the sincere one", husband of Sāvitrī₁, who saved him from death — f. Satyavatī₁ myth. [Mah.] np. of satya vatī "sincerity"; born from the sperm of King Uparicara fallen into the Yamunā, she was found with her twin brother in the belly of the mermaid Adrikā caught by the chief of the fishermen Dāsarāja; the king adopted the boy who became King Matsya₁, named the girl Matsyagandhī because of her fishy smell, and gave her back to Dāsarāja who raised her as Kālī₁ because of her complexion, but she came to be known as Satyavatī₁; she ferried people across the Yamunā on her ferry; the sage [ṛṣi] Parāśara, while crossing, fell in love with her; he caused clouds to rise, hiding their love, from which Vyāsa was born immediately, who was left on an island [Dvaipāyana₁] where he grew up alone; Parāśara restored her virginity, and changed her fishy smell into a musky perfume; she thus became Kastūrīgandhī or Gandhavatī; Attracted by her perfume, King Śāṃtanu, who was hunting near his fisherman's hut, fell madly in love with her; Dāsarāja gave her his hand, on the condition that he disinherit his dolphin Bhīṣma in favor of the sons she bore him, Citrāngada and Vicitravīrya; after their death without heirs, she summoned Vyāsa to fulfill his niyoga duty and continue the lineage by fathering Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu, whose descendants would fight in the great fratricidal battle of the Mah. myth.
