[Mah.] np. of Satyavatī₁, daughter of King Gādhi, married to the Brahmin Ŗcīka; at her marriage, she obtained from Bhrgu a rite intended to give her a Brahmin son; She was to kiss a banyan tree and eat a broth [caru] containing a magical substance; her mother, who celebrated the corresponding ksatriya rite, was to kiss a pippal tree and eat a different caru, but this caused the exchange of rites, causing confusion of castes | varṇasaṃkara | ; she conceived Jamadagni, but obtained that the ritual error be transferred to a grandson (this would be Paraśurāma).
satyávadana [vadana] n. the act of telling the truth.

satyavarman [varman] m. lit. [DKC.] np. of Sa tyavarmā "Protector of the truth", son of the minister Sitavarmā; he went on a pilgrimage; he married Kālī₁, daughter of a brahmin, but not obtaining any children from her he married his younger sister Gaurī₂ who gave him a son; Kālī₁, jealous, threw him into the river with his nurse; the king collected the child, whom he named Somadatta₂ and entrusted to his uncle Sumati₃.
satyavaha [vaha] m. myth. [MO.] np. of Bhāradvāja satyavaha "who transmits the truth"; he learned from Atharvā the brahmavidyā which he taught to Angirā; he is also called Satyavāha.
satyávākya [vākya] n. true words.
satyavāc [vāc] amnf who speaks the truth, sincere.
satyavādin [vādin] amnf satyavādinī who speaks the truth.
Satyavāha [vāha] m. myth. np. of the sage [rsi] Sa tyavāha; he received the sacred knowledge [brahmavidyā] from Angī and transmitted it to his student Angirā; he is also called satyavaha.

Satyavrata | vrata | amnf satyavratā who practices sincerity — n. vow of truthfulness — m. myth. np. of Satyavrata "Devoted to Truth", 7th Manu of the kalpa, Manu of the present time; cf. Vaivasvata myth. np. of Satyavrata₂, birth name of King Triśańku | lit. | KSS. | np. of Satyavrata₃, king of the fishermen of Utsthala.
satyaśīla |śīla| amnf satyaśīlā who follows the right path.
satyasaṃdha [saṃdhā₂] amnf satyasaṃdhā ["who keeps his promises"] true to his word, loyal.
Satyasoma [soma] m. bed. n.p. of Satyasoma, kāpālika of the play Mattavilāsa.

satyānanda [ānanda] m. phil. joy of truth hist. np. of Svāmī satyānanda Sarasvatī₂, born in India in 1923, of British education; disciple of Sivānanda₁, he took as his mission to make Yoga known in the West; he founded the "Bihāra School of Yoga" in Munger in Bihāra in 1963 and the "International Yoga Fellowship" in 1964; he received the title of paramahamsa in 1974 and retired as sannyāsin.

satyānṛta [anṛta] amnf satyānṛtā both true and false; true/false — n. du. satyānṛte truth and falsehood | sg. soc. (in fig.) commerce, business; it is an unsuitable means of subsistence for a brahmin | saṭkarmāni|.
satyārtha [artha] m. phil. duty of truth.
satyārthaprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. np. from satyārthaprakāśa "Explanation of the duty of truth", principal work of Svāmī Dayānanda₁ Sarasvatī₂ (1875).
satyā [f. satya] iic. truth.

satyāgraha [graha] m. mod. ["claim for truth"] civil disobedience movement founded by Gandhi in 1907 to resist the English occupation | np. of the āśrama satyāgraha, on the banks of the Sabarmatī, from where Gandhi started the salt march in 1930.
satyāgrāhin | grāhin | amnf satyagrāhinī mod. which makes civil disobedience.
satra cf. sattra.
satrā adv. together; all together; in a bundle (not. palm leaves) | with (i.).

satrājit [jit] amnf always victorious — m. myth. np. of the prince satrājit "always victorious", son of Nighna, king of the Yādavās; to reward him for his devotion, Sūrya gave him the magic jewel Syamantaka; his brother Prasena seized it before being devoured by a lion; Kṛṣṇa, suspected of the theft, went in search of the jewel, found it at Jāmbavān and returned it to him; in exchange satrājit gave him his daughter Satyabhāmā as a wife; satrājit was assassinated by Satadhanvā who seized the jewel.
satva cf. sattva.
satvát m. pl. geo. name of a people of South India; syn. vṛṣṇi, yādava; cf. satvata.
satvan |satvan| amnf satvarī living; energetic; valiant; strong, powerful — m. living being warrior | pl. satvānas warriors; guards; partisans.
satvara |sa₁tvarā| amnf satvarā who hastens, hastened, lively. satvaram adv. in haste.
sad₁ |agt. sad₁| ifc. amnf seated on, residing at (iic.).
sad₁ iic. sat.
sadaśva |aśva| m. good horse — amnf sádaśvā who owns a good horse.
sadasat | asat | amnf sadasatī true and false; real and unreal; good and evil — n. phil. Being and Nothingness; the true and the false; the real and the illusory.
sadasadrūpa | rūpa | amnf sadasadrūpā phil. that which seems to exist and not to exist.
sadasadrūpatā |tā| f. phil. quality of both existing and not existing; said of the phenomenal world.
sadasadviveka | viveka | m. phil. discrimination between true and false, or good and evil.
sadasadvivekabuddhi | buddhi | f. phil. ability to discern good from evil, or truth from falsehood.
sadāgama |āgama| m. correct teaching; orthodox triune doctrine.
sadācāra |ācāra| m. virtuous conduct; Good practice — amnf sadācārā who practices virtue; just, honest.
sadukti [ukti] f. ["Good word"] proverb. saduktikarņāmṛta [karṇāmṛta] n. lit. np. from saduktikarṇāmṛta "Nectar for the ear", a collection of proverbs by Srīdharadāsa (1205).
sadgati [gati] f. good outcome; happy outcome phil. way of the righteous; eternal rest; liberation. sadgatiprāptirastu may he rest in peace.
sadguru [guru] m. authentic master.
saddharma [dharma] m. bd. correct law | bd. wonderful law.

saddharmapuṇḍarīka [puṇḍarīka] n. [saddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtra] pl. bd. np. of the aphorism text [sūtra] saddharmapuṇḍarīka "Lotus of the Good Law"; it is the essential teaching of the bd. Mahāyāna doctrine propagated notably by Nichiren in Japan. saddharmasmṛtyupasthānasūtra |smṛtiupasthānasūtra| n. lit. np. of the Saddharmamṛtyupasthānasūtra, a bd. work from the 4th century.
saddhetu | hetu | m. phil. proof of existence.
sadbhāva | bhāva | m. existence, reality | truth; inclination, affection (for (prati)) | sincerity, loyalty, kindness.
sadvāda | vāda | m. orthodox doctrine; truthful discourse.
sadvidya [vidyā] amnf sadvidyā well-formed; having correct knowledge — f. sad₁ vidyā correct knowledge.
sadvṛtta [vṛtta] n. good conduct, virtuous behavior — amnf sadvṛttā virtuous.

sádana [agt. sad₁] amnf sadanī that which makes dwell — act. n. seat; dwelling, residence; sojourn | act of settling, of resting; rest — ifc. that which resides in, that which inhabits (iic.). patnīnām sadana gynaeceum.
sadaya |sa₁dayā| amnf sadayā compassionate (in reverse (loc.)). sadayam adv. with compassion, gently.
sadarpa [sa₁darpa] amnf sadarpā proud; haughty, arrogant. sadarpam adv. proudly; with arrogance.

sadas [abstr. sad₁] n. seat, residence; place of meeting, assembly; advice | ritual assembly; doctrinal debate among scholars | pandita|. sadasi in public. sadaspati var. sadasaspati [pati] m. president of the assembly.
sadasyá [ya] amnf sadasyā participant in a ritual or scholarly assembly; spectator; jury |soc. priest assessor of a solemn rite.
sadogata | gata | amnf sadogatā participant in an assembly.
sadogrha [grha] n. meeting room.
sádā adv. always; constantly, every time. na sadā never.
sádānanda [nanda| m. perpetual joy — amnf sadānandā always joyful — m. hist. np. of Sadānanda, philosopher of the 15th or 16th century, author of the Vedāntasāra₂.
sádāpuspa | puspa | amnf sadāpuspā always in bloom.
sadāphala | phala | n. organic. bot edible fig. Ficus glometara or Gulār |udumbara| fig tree.

sádāśiva [śiva] m. phil. [śaivasiddhānta] np. of Sadāśiva, supreme form of Shiva; he has 5 faces: Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpurusa and Isāna, respectively associated with 5 aspects or worlds of the bindu, 5 elements, 5 colors and 5 directions of space | hist. np. of Sadāśiva₁, emperor of Vijaya nagara (1542–1576); he succeeded his uncle Acyu tadeva Rāya.
sádāna [sa₁dāna] amnf sadānā that gives; generous | (elephant) in rut (whose temples exude ichor).

sadṛśa [samāna₂dṛś₂] amnf sadṛśī sem blable to, resembling, similar to, like (gi loc. iic.) | suitable, decent, correct, deserved; worthy; regular. sadrśam adv. as is fitting, decently, well. pitrsadrśah like the father. na jñānena sadṛśam (motto of the University of My sore) Nothing is worth more than knowledge.
sadrśya |ya| n. phil. the sense of resemblance, a sadangasilpa.
sadman [sad₁man] n. seat, residence, dwelling, stay; place, location, shelter | palace, temple.
sadyah iic. sadyas.
sadyaḥkṛta [kṛta] amnf sadyaḥkṛtā done immediately, done quickly; done the same day.
sadyaḥkrī [krī₂] amnf bought the same day — m. soc. rite of dīkṣā abbreviated in one day |ekāha|.
sadyaḥprāṇahara [prāṇáhara] amnf sadyaḥprāṇaharī which kills instantly.

sadyás [sa₁div] adv. the same day; at once, immediately; instantly; suddenly | every day. sadyaskāla var. sadyaḥkāla [kāla₁] m. the same day; the present time — amnf sadyaskālā which falls on the same day. sadyaskrī var. sadyaḥkrī [krī₂] amnf bought on the same day | soc. Vedic ceremony of libation of soma bought on the same day, rite performed in one day | ekāha |.
sadyoja [ja] amnf sadyojā newborn.

Sadyojāta [jāta] amnf sadyojātā newborn | born instantly (said of the gods) — m. newborn calf; young calf | phil. [śaivasiddhānta] np. of Sadyojāta, face of bliss of SadāśivaNandi, turned towards the West, associated with the world of cessation of activity [nivrtti], with the element earth and the color white — f. sadyojātā young woman who has given birth.

sadyojyoti [jyotis] m. hist. np. of the Kashmira philosopher sadyojyoti (~675~~725), founder of the Mantramārga school; he wrote the Paramokṣanirāsakārikās "Stanzas rejecting other views on liberation", refuting 20 conceptions of the state of liberation | mokṣa|; Bhatta Rāmakantha made the commentary Paramokṣanirāsakārikavṛtti.
sadvandva [sa₁dvandva] amnf sadvandvā quarrelsome.
sadha var. saha₂ |sa₁dhā₁| iic. with.
sadhana |sa₁dhana| amnf sadhanā rich; opp. daridra.
sadhanatā [tā] f. wealth.
sadharma [sa₁dharma] amnf sadharmā of the same nature, having the same duties; equal to, similar to (gi).
sádhūma [sa₁dhūma] amnf sadhūmā enveloped in smoke; emitting smoke.
sadhūmavarṇā [varṇa] f. myth. epith. from one of the 7 languages of Agni.
sadhaumya [sa₁Dhaumya] amnf sadhaumyā accompanied by Dhaumya.
sadhri [saha₂] iic. with, likewise.

sadhryác [ac] amnf sadhrīcī turned in the same direction; associated, convergent | well directed; correct — mf sadhrīcī friend, companion. sadhryak adv. together, in concert, in common; opp. prthak | in the right way.
san₂ noted. gram. suffix [pratyaya] of the desiderative.
sanādi |ādi| m. gram. secondary conjugation marker of verbs: desiderative [san₂], intensiv/frequentative [yan], or causative/nominal [nic]; also the denominative variants kyac, kāmyac, kvip.
sanādyanta | anta | iic. gram. is said of a secondary verbal theme.
sanādyantadhātuvṛtti [dhātuvṛtti] f. gram. formation of a secondary verbal theme.
sanantadhātu [antadhātu] m. gram. desiderative form of a root, carrying the indicator san₂.
sana₁ [act. san₁] m. gain, acquisition | don, of france.

sána₂ amnf sanā old; which lasts a long time; Elder — mr. myth. n.p. of the wise |rsi| sana₁ "the Elder", one of the 4 eternal |sanakādi| from the mind of Brahmā | lat. senex, senior; fr. senile. sanam adv. formerly.
sanaká [sana₁ka] amnf sanikā old; Ancient myth. np. of the sage rsi Sanaka "the Ancient", one of the 4 eternals |sanakādi| from the mind of Brahmā.

sanakādi |ādi| m. pl. myth. The 4 eternal sages |ṛṣi|; they emanated from the mind of Brahmā |vaidhātra| to populate the World; they are called Sanaka, sanatkumāra, sanandana and Sanātana or sana₁; being the incarnation of purity [sattva], they refused to procreate; eternally young, abstinent, experts in Veda, they travel the World together; visiting Vaikuntha one day, they cursed Jaya₁ and Vijaya₁ who had disrespected them; they dwell in Heaven [loka] Janaloka; they are depicted listening to the teachings of Shiva dakṣiṇāmūrti, who taught them, notably, the 14 phonemic intervals |śivasūtra|.
sanat [sana₁] adv. always, since forever, eternally.

sanatkumāra [kumāra] m. myth. np. of sanat kumāra "Eternally young", one of the 4 eternals [sanakādi] from the mind of Brahmā; in the Chāndogyā upaniṣad, sanatkumāra debates with the sage Nārada about the conditions for attaining good fortune.
sanatkumāracarita [carita] n. bed. n.p. of the sanat kumāracarita, section of the Nemināthacarita of Ne minātha.
sanatsujāta [sujāta] m. myth. np. of sanatsujāta "Eternally beautiful", epith. of the eternal [sanakādi] sanatkumāra.
sanatsujātīya [īya] n. lit. np. of the sanatsujātīya, philosophical episode of the Mah.
sanandana [sa₁nandana] m. myth. np. of the sage [rsi] sanandana "Joyful", one of the 4 eternals [sanakādi] from the mind of Brahmā.
sanáya var. sānaya [sana₁ya] amnf sa nayā old; Ancient; sustainable.
sanayanajala [sa₁nayanajala] amnf sanayanajalā with tear-filled eyes. śuklāpāngaih sanayanajalaih svāgatīkṛtya |MD.| welcomed by the peacocks with moist eyes.
sanā [related to sana₁] adv. always; perpetually | var. sanāt id.

sanātána |tana| amnf sanātanī eternal, perpetual, imperishable | ancient, antique — m. myth. np. of the sage [ṛṣi] Sanātana "Eternal", one of the 4 eternals [sanakādi] from the mind of Brahmā | hist. np. of Sanātana₁ Gosvāmī |1488–1558|, eldest son of Mukunda, secretary to the Sultan of Ben gale; he became treasurer of the Sultan, but renounced the world to become a disciple of Caitanya; with his brother Rūpa he is one of the six pastors of Vṛndāvana; we owe him the Bṛhadbhāgavatāmṛita and the Haribhaktivilāsa || fr. seneschal.
sanātanadharma [dharma] mn phil. "Eternal Law", neologism to designate the Hindu religion, due to Annie Besant and popularized by Auro bindo.
sanātánatama [super. Sanātana] m. phil. the Eternal One, epith. of Vishnu.
sanātha [sa₁nātha] amnf sanāthā having a protector; protected by (i. iic.) | provided with, possessing (i. iic.) — f. sanāthā married woman whose husband is still alive.
sánābhi [sa₁nābhi] amnf of the same center | connected by blood; syn. sapinda | who has a navel — m. uterine brother | var. sanābha f. sanābhā id. — f. uterine sister.
sanābhya [a] m. consanguinity (in the 7th degree).
sanidra [sa₁nidrā₂] amnf sanidrā in slept.
sanirveda [sa₁nirveda] amnf sanirvedā discouraged; dejected, depressed.
sánemi [sa₁nemi] amnf equipped with a rim (wheel) | complete; perfect — adv. completely; all the time; always.
saṃtata var. santata [pp. saṃtan] amnf saṃtatā extended; continuous, uninterrupted, dense repeated, continual, lasting, perpetual. samtatam adv. continually.

samtati var. Santati [act. samtan] f. extent, continuation, Continuity | lineage, descendants | myth. np. of Santati "Continuity", daughter of Daksa, wife of Kratu. samtativicchedah interruption of lineage.
saṃtan var. santan [samtan₁] v. [8] pr. (samtanoti) pr. r. (samtanute) pp. (samtata) pf. (anu) to extend; maintain Continuity, join.

samtap var. santap |samtap| v. |1| pr. (saṃtapati) pr. r. (saṃtapate) pp. (saṃtapita, samtapta) to heat, burn, torment — v. [4] pr. r. (saṃtapyate) to suffer; to be sad — ca. (samtāpayati) to cause suffering; to make sad.
samtapta var. santapta [pp. samtap] amnf samtaptā very hot, burning; burned | melted; red-hot | tormented, oppressed; in distress — n. pain, torment; sorrow, grief.
saṃtaptāyas [ayas] n. iron heated to red heat.

saṃtāná var. santāna |act. saṃtan| m. continuous succession; not. continuous flow, series of thoughts; Continuity, succession, continuation, series | bd. series of cognitions of the conscious being | cohesion, connection, alliance | myth. kalpavrksa tree, one of the 5 trees of Indra's Svarga paradise; cf. pañcavṛkṣa — mn progeny, descendants; lineage, race — f. santānā ifc. offspring of, flow of, series of (2nd century). samtānāntara var. santānāntara [antara] n. bd. interruption of the flow of thoughts | series of cognitions of others.
samtānāntaradūṣana [dūṣana] m. bed. n.p. of the Santānāntaradūsana of Ratnakīrti.

samtānāntarasiddhi [siddhi] f. bed. n.p. of the Santānāntarasiddhi of Dharmakīrti, developing the doctrine bd. of impermanence, and establishing the existence of cognitive series other than one's own consciousness.

samtānaka var. santānaka [agt. samtan] amnf samtānikā that extends, that continues — m. myth. kalpavrksa tree, its flower — amnf samtānikā cobweb | cream, coagulated milk | scum. samtānakataru var. santānakataru | taru | m. myth. celestial kalpavrksa tree, which grants wishes. samtānakatarucchāyāsuptavidyādharādhvagam | yasya copavanam bāhyam gandhavad gand hamādanah | [KuS.] Its outer park is the fragrant Gandhamādana, where traveling celestial magicians slumber in the shade of the wishing tree. samtānakamaya var. santānakamaya [maya] amnf saṃtānakamayī made of flowers from the tree of desires.

saṃtāpa [act. saṃtap] m. burning in tense, furnace | torment, pain, distress | self-mortification, asceticism, penance; remorse — f. saṃtāpā ifc. who suffers from (iic.). samtāpam kṛ to be afflicted with (g.) | to inflict torments. dhanavişaye samtāpo na kāryaḥ [PT.] One should not grieve over material possessions.
saṃtāra var. santāra [agt. ca. saṃtr̩] m. that which crosses, that which traverses.

saṃtuṣ var. santuṣ [samtuṣ] v. [4] pr. (saṃtuṣyati) pp. (saṃtuṣṭa) to be satisfied with something or someone; to take pleasure in something (i.) | to be fulfilled — ca. (saṃtoṣayati) to satisfy, to rejoice, to content.
saṃtuṣṭa var. santuṣṭa [pp. saṃtuṣ] amnf saṃtuṣṭā content (with little), content with (i.); satis done, rejoiced — m. lit. np. of santuṣṭa, vidūṣaka of the Avimāraka.
saṃtuṣṭacitta [citta] amnf saṃtuṣṭacittā d'hum meur joyeusee.
saṃtṛd var. santṛd [samtṛd] v. [7] pr. (saṃtṛṇatti) pp. (saṃtṛṇṇa) to pin together, to staple; to punch.
saṃtṛ var. santṛ [samtṛ] v. [1] pr. (saṃtarati) pp. (saṃtīrṇa) to cross.
saṃtoṣ var. santoṣ [ca. saṃtuṣ] v. [10] pr. (samtosayati) pp. (samtosita) satisfy, delight, content.

saṃtoṣa var. santoṣa [act. saṃtuṣ] m. satis faction, contentment (with little); serenity; frugality phil. moderation, one of the disciplines [niyama] of yoga | myth. np. of samtoşa "Frugal", son of Dharma and Tuşţi. samtosam kr to be content with.
saṃtoṣita [pp. saṃtoṣ] amnf saṃtoṣitā satisfied.
saṃtyakta [pp. saṃtyaj] amnf samtyaktā abandoned.
saṃtyaj var. santyaj [samtyaj₁] v. [1] pr. (saṃtyajati) pp. (saṃtyakta) to abandon.
saṃtyajya var. saṃtyājya [pfp. [1] saṃtyaj] amnf samtyajyā that which must be banished, which must be rid of | that which must be renounced; said not. of worldly desires.
samtras var. santras [samtras] v. [4] pr. (samtrasyati) pp. (samtrasta) to tremble, to be frightened.
saṃtrāsa [act. saṃtras] m. terror, dread (from (abl. iic.)).
saṃdaṃś var. sandaṃś [samdaṃś] v. [1] pr. (saṃdaśati) pp. (saṃdaṣṭa) to bite, to seize with the teeth; to squeeze, to compress, to pinch.
saṃdaṃśa [act. saṃdaṃś] m. pinching (lips) | pinch; gesture of grasping with one's fingers; grasping, compression | myth. hell where one is tortured with pincers.
saṃdarbha var. sandarbha [samdarbha] m. formation of sheaf, bouquet, wreath or rosary; floral arrangement, composition, bouquet — f. samdarbhā ifc. bouquet of, sheaf of (iic.).
saṃdarbhavat [vat] amnf saṃdarbhavatī ar tificiellement composé.
saṃdarśa var. sandarśa [act. saṃdṛś] m. vision; appearance.

samdarśana [act. saṃdṛś] n. act of staring, of contemplating; vision | act of being seen by or in the company of g. . samdarsane in the presence of (g. iic.). svapne samdarśanam gam to be seen (by (g.)) in a dream. samdarśanam prayam to appear to (g.).
saṃdaṣṭa var. sandaṣṭa [pp. saṃdaṃś] amnf saṃdaṣṭā bitten; squeezed, compressed, crushed.
samdaştaka var. sandaştaka [samaştaka] n. lit. [alaṃkāra] variety of yamaka where the repetition occurs at the beginning of each half-hemistich.
saṃdā var. sandā [samdā₁] v. [3] pr. (samdadāti) to gather gifts; to grant, oc to troyer.
saṃdāya var. sandāya [agt. saṃdā] ifc. amnf saṃdāyī that grants, that bestows (iic.). gosaṃdāyaḥ m. that confers a cow.
saṃdāyin [agt. saṃdā] amnf saṃdāyinī id.
saṃdāva [samdāva] m. fire.

samdigdha var. sandigdha [pp. samdih] amnf samdigdhā covered with, anointed with, smeared with (i. iic.) | obscure, doubtful, questionable; uncertain, troubled; ambiguous, hazardous | gram. ambiguous | hesitant, doubting; confused — n. uncertainty, doubt; confusion. tad etad atyantasandigdham vartate ācāryānām vibhāṣā anuvartate na veti gram. [Patañjali₁] Thus we are in constant uncertainty as to whether the Master's option is followed or not. vacanagamyasyārthasya saṃdigdharūpatvāt gram. Because of the ambiguity of the meaning of a word understood by speech alone. samdigdheşu vākyaśeṣāt lit. [MI.] In case of doubt, (the meaning is determined) by the rest of the text.
saṃdiś var. sandiś [samdiś₁] v. [1] pr. (samdisati) pp. (samdista) to indicate, signal, in form, make known; to give a message; to explain, demonstrate | to order.
samdista var. sandista [pp. saṃdiś] amnf samdistā shown, stipulated; promised — n. communication, information; news.
saṃdih var. sandih [satdih] v. [2] pr. (samdegdhi) pp. (samdigdha) to smear, to dirty, to boil, to blur — ca. (samdehayati) to confuse — ca. r. (samdehayate) to hesitate, to doubt; to confuse.
saṃdīp var. sandīp [samdīp] v. [4] pr. r. (samdīpyate) pp. (samdīpta) to blaze, to blaze; to ignite, to become excited — ca. (saṃdīpayati) to ignite; (figuratively) to excite.
saṃdīpaka var. sandīpaka [agt. saṃdīp] amnf sandīpikā which excites, which inflames | which makes jealous.
samdīpana var. sandīpana [agt. saṃdīp] amnf saṃdīpanā which excites, which inflames — m. myth. name of a flower arrow of Kāma — n. act of exciting (envy, etc).
saṃdīpanavat [vat] amnf saṃdīpanavatī which contains flammable materials.
saṃdīpta var. sandīpta [pp. saṃdīp] amnf saṃdīptā lit, blazing, inflamed, flamboyant excited.
saṃduṣ var. sanduṣ [samduṣ] v. [4] pr. (sāṃduṣyati) pp. (saṃduṣṭa) become corrupt or impure; defiled — ca. (saṃdūṣayati) to corrupt, defile, defile | to tarnish; to cover with shame or infamy.
saṃduṣṭa [pp. saṃduṣ] amnf saṃduṣṭā corrupted, tainted; bad | ill-disposed towards (g.).
saṃduh var. sanduh [samduh₁] v. [2] pr. (samdogdhi) pp. (samdugdha) to milk together — pr. r. (saṃdogdhe) ved. to soak up, to revel in | to give (milk) — ca. (saṃdohayati) to milk.
saṃdṛbdha [samdṛbdha] amnf saṃdṛbdhā braided; plaited; arranged in a tuft; composed | crossed, corroborated; confirmed — n. braid.

saṃdṛś var. sandṛś [samdṛś₁] abs. (saṃdṛśya) to see at the same time; to contemplate, to observe — ps. (saṃdṛśyate) to be observed; to show oneself; to resemble — ca. (samdarśayati) to show, to display; to pretend to be | to expose, to explain. nikṛtamivātmānaṃ saṃdarśya affecting an air of feigned innocence. ātmānam mṛtavatsaṃdarśayāmāsa he played dead.
saṃdeśa var. sandeśa [act. saṃdiś] m. indication tion, information, communication, information; message; explanation | mission; instruction, order — f. saṃdeśā ifc. information on (iic.).
samdeśakāvya [kāvya] n. lit. genre of messenger poetry; the messenger can be a cloud [Meghadūta], the wind [Pavanadūta], a bee [Bhṛṅgasandeśa], a bird [Haṃsasandeśa], etc.
saṃdeśaka var. sandeśaka [agt. saṃdiś] mn information; news.
samdeśya var. sandeśya [pfp. [1] samdiś] amnf samdeśyā which must be directed; which must receive instructions | done according to instructions; done on purpose | foreign; opp. videśya.
samdestavya var. sandestavya [pfp. [3] saṃdiś] amnf saṃdeṣṭavyā which must be informed; which must receive instructions | which must be transmitted as instruction — n. instruction; injunction, order.
samdeha var. sandeha [act. saṃdih] m. doubt, hesitation, confusion; ambiguity | uncertainty (concerning (g. loc. iic.)) | risk, danger. nāsti saṃdehaḥ without a doubt.
saṃdehatva [tva] n. state of doubt.
samdehadolā [dolā] f. perplexity.
saṃdoha var. sandoha [act. saṃduh] m. milking | milk produced by milking the herd | multitude, mass; abundance.
samdohana var. sandohana [agt. samduh] amnf saṃdohanā which produces (milk, reward).
saṃdrāva [samdrāva] m. act of running together | confluence.

samdhā₁ var. sandhā₁ [samdhā₁] v. [3] pr. (saṃdadhāti) pp. (saṃhita) pf. (anu, abhi, prati) to unite, bring together, combine; adjust; place, fix (not. the arrow on the bowstring) | form an alliance with — pr. r. (saṃdhatté) to reconcile with, to ally oneself with. śatrunā na hi samdadhyāt suślistenāpi samdhinā lit. [PT.] One should never make an alliance with an enemy, even if he is very close to you.
samdhā₁ [act. samdhā₁] f. agreement, convention, alliance; promise | mixture | border, limit. samdhābhāṣā var. sandhābhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. phil. [Tantra] enigmatic language; cf. saṃdhyābhāṣā.

saṃdhāna var. sandhāna [act. sandhā₁] n. meeting, gathering; assembly; union | reconciliation, agreement, alliance (with (i.saha₂)) | point of contact, junction | the act of aiming with the arrow in contact with the bow | gram. combination of words; linking; syn. sandhi | preparation, mixture (drink); spirits — f. saṃdhānī distillation | myth. [Rām.] herb saṃdhānī "that mends amputated limbs," brought back by Hanuman from the Himalayas to heal Rama's army. saṃdhānam āyā to be admitted (into an assembly). śarasamdhānam kurvan aiming with his arrow.
samdhāya [abs. samdhā₁] ind. having formed an alliance, having made peace.
saṃdhāyasaṃbhāṣā [saṃbhāṣā] f. dialogue friend cal; opp. vigrhyasambhāṣā.
saṃdhār var. sandhār [ca. saṃdhṛ] v. [10] pr. (saṃdhārayati) pp. (saṃdhārita) to carry, sup to carry; to support, to hold.
saṃdhāraṇa [act. saṃdhṛ] n. act of supporting, bearing, maintaining | med. act of being pregnant — f. saṃdhāraṇā attitude, position | direction (thoughts).

saṃdhi var. sandhi [act. saṃdhā₁] m. union, association, combination; alliance | junction, articulation | phon. liaison, euphonic combination; a distinction is made between internal sandhi |antaranga| for forming words and external sandhi [bahiranga] effecting the euphonic liaison of words in the sentence; sandhi can be agglutinative by juxtaposition
taposition [āgama] or combining by substitution

euphonious [ādeśa] | bed. articulation of a story; cf. pancasandhi. saṃdhikārya var. sandhikārya | kārya | n. gram. making the euphonic connection. samdhirahita var. sandhirahita [rahita] amnf samdhirahitā gram. is said of a text whose sandhi has been analyzed in isolated words. saṃdhivigrahika var. sandhivigrahika [vigrahika] m. soc. minister of alliances and war; cf. Lakşmīdhara. samdhiviccheda var. sandhiviccheda | viccheda | mr. gram. sandhi analysis, segmentation. samdhiviślesana var. sandhiviślesana [viślesana] n. id. samdhivelā var. sandhivelā [velā] f. twilight | astr. articulation of the time of day (morning, evening) or of the month (new moon, full moon). saṃdhisthāna var. sandhisthāna [sthāna] n. arch. junction of two parts of a building. saṃdhyakṣara var. sandhyakṣara [akṣara] n. phon. diphthong; includes e, o, ai and au. samdhyanga var. sandhyanga [anga₁] n. lit. (theatre) component of the plot.
saṃdhita var. sandhita [pp. saṃdhā₁] amnf saṃdhitā tied together; braided (hair) | joined, attached (arrow) | united to; allied | mixed.
saṃdhiteṣu |loc. pl. saṃdhita| adv. having armed his bow with an arrow.
saṃdhukṣ var. sandhukṣ [samdhukṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (saṃdhukṣate) kindle, inflame, stir up — ca. (saṃdhukṣayati) id.
samdhr var. sandhr [samdhr] v. [1] pr. (samdharati) pp. (samdhrta) to carry, to bear; endure; support, retain — ca. (saṃdhārayati) id.
saṃdheya var. sandheya [pfp. [1] saṃdhā₁] amnf saṃdheyā which must be joined or attached | to be reconciled, which must make an alliance with. samdheyam (impers.) it must be reconciled with (i. loc.
saṃdhya [saṃdhia] amnf saṃdhyā at the point of junction | gram. based on the euphonic combination — f. cf. saṃdhyā.

samdhyā var. sandhyā [f. saṃdhya] f. junction, transitional period, notably twilight; there are three, at dawn, at noon, and at sunset [saṃdhyāvandana] soc. prayer at the time of a sandhyā | phil. twilight that precedes or follows a yuga | myth. np. of sandhyā "Twilight", a wife of Citrasena; cf. Gālava — v. [11] pr. r. (saṃdhyāyate) to resemble a twilight. saṃdhyām ās var. saṃdhyāmanvās, saṃdhyāmupās soc. to perform the rite of saṃdhyā, notably by reciting the gāyatrī. samdhyākaranandin var. sandhyākaranandin [kara₁nandin] m. hist. np. of the poet Sandhyākaranandī, author of the Rāmacarita₁; he lived in the 11th century at the court of King Rāmapāla in Pundravardhana (Bengal).
samdhyājapa [japa] m. soc. recitation of a prayer at the time of a sandhyā.

samdhyābhāṣā [bhāṣā] f. phil. esoteric language, teaching by enigma. saṃdhyāvandana var. sandhyāvandana [vandana] n. soc. morning rite [prātaḥsaṃdhyā] (before the Sun's disk has risen) and evening rite [sāyaṃsaṃdhyā] (after half of the solar disk has disappeared below the horizon, and before the stars are visible); it is performed after the ritual bath, sitting in the evening facing Northwest, and standing in the morning facing East; It includes the purification of the mouth [ācamana], the regulation of breath [prāṇāyāma], sprinkling while reciting mantras [mārjana], the absolution of sins [aghamarṣaṇa], the ritual welcoming of the Sun [arghya], and the recitation [japa] of the sāvitrī preceded by om and the ritual exclamation [vyāhṛti]; one may also celebrate Mitra in the morning and Varuna in the evening; a third rite is practiced at noon, when the Sun is at its zenith [madhyāhnasaṃdhyā]; these three rites | trikāla | are part of the obligations of a brahmin [nityakarman]; syn. sandhyopāsana. saṃdhyāvandanādini soc. ritual obligations of a brahmin: the saṃdhyāvandana etc. saṃdhyopāsana var. sandhyopāsana | upāsana | n. cf. saṃdhyāvandana.
sanna [pp. sad₁] amnf sannā sitting | weak; depressed.

sámnaddha [pp. samnah] amnf samnaddhā attached, bound, fixed | equipped, harnessed, armed; ready | ready to burst (storm); ready to bloom (bud) | that adheres to, that permeates (loc.). yuddhāya saṃnaddhāh they prepared themselves for battle.
sámnaddhakavaca [kavaca] amnf
saṃnaddhakavacā ["who has donned his breastplate"] ready for battle.
samnaya var. sannaya [agt. saṃnī] amnf saṃnayā who leads, who brings together — act. mr. collection; assembly | rearguard of an army.

saṃnah var. sannah [samnah] v. [4] pr. (samnáhyati) pp. (samnaddha) to attach, bind, fix; to clothe, gird, equip — pr. r. (saṃnahyate) to dress, equip, harness. yuddhāya saṃnahyate he prepares for battle.

samnikarṣa var. sannikarṣa [act. saṃnikṛṣ] act of bringing together; proximity, contact m. [indriyasamnikarṣa] phil. relation between the organ and the object of meaning | gram. contiguity of phonemes — amnf samnikarṣā near, close. samnikarse adv. in the vicinity of (g.). samnikarṣam adv. (to go, ...) near. saṃnikarṣāt adv. (to come, ...) from near.
saṃnikṛṣ var. sannikṛṣ [samnikṛṣ] v. [6] pr. (saṃnikṛṣati) pp. (saṃnikṛṣṭa) bring together.
samnikṛṣṭa var. sannikṛṣṭa [pp. samnikṛṣ] amnf samnikṛṣṭā approached; close; opp. viprakṛṣṭa.
saṃnikṛṣṭārtha [artha] m. phil. [Sabara₁] closest meaning of a Vedic statement; opp. viprakṛṣṭārtha.
saṃnigrah var. sannigrah [samnigrah] v. [9] pr. (samnigṛḥṇāti) pr. r. (saṃnigṛḥṇīté) pp. (samnigrhīta) to master, subjugate, tame; to repress, restrict; to stop.

saṃnidhā var. sannidhā [samnidhā] v. [3] pr. (saṃnidadhāti) pp. (saṃnihita) pfp. (samnidheya) to place in or on (loc.); to deposit; to amass, to collect — pr. r. (saṃnidhate) to appoint to the office of (loc.); to be in (loc.) | to be imminent; to be near — ps. (saṃnidhīyate) to be present; to be close — ca. (samnidhāpayati) to bring near; to make manifest, to represent. dṛṣṭiṃ saṃnidhā to fix one's eyes on. samnidhāpyate it manifests itself in the presence of g. .

samnidhāna var. sannidhāna act. samnidhā n. receptacle; neighborhood, presence. ākānkṣā sannidhānam ca yogyatā ceti ca trayam sambandhakāraṇatvena klptam nānantaraśrutih | Kumārila It is said that dependence, proximity and compatibility are the three factors of production of a semantic relation (between words); simple contiguity is not one of them.

samnidhi var. sannidhi [act. samnidhā] m. proximity, presence; neighborhood | gram. contiguity (between constituents). samnidhau adv. in the presence of (g. iic.). samnidhim kr realize one's presence. samnidhim prāp come near (g. iic.). śabdasyānyasya saṃnidhiḥ m. gram. proximity of another word, collocation allowing disam biguer.
samnidheya var. sannidheya [pfp. [1] samnidhā] amnf samnidheyā to bring closer.

samnipat var. sannipat [samnipat] v. [1] pr. (samnipatati) pp. (samnipatita) to descend, to swoop down on, to throw oneself upon (loc.); to fall; to fall with (i.) | to present oneself, to appear among (loc.) | to perish — ca. (samnipātayati) to bring down, to strike down | to assemble, to summon.
saṃnipatita var. sanniparta [pp. samnipat] amnf samnipatitā descended; met | appeared, arrived.
saṃnipatya [abs. saṃnipat] ind. being cendu; having stolen | immediately, directly.
saṃnipatyakārin [kārin] anfm samnipatyakārinī which acts immediately.
saṃnipāt [ca. saṃnipat] v. [10] pr. (saṃnipātayati) to bring down, to strike down | to assemble, to summon.
saṃnipāta var. sannipāta [act. saṃnipat] m. descent, fall; collapse; downfall, ruin; death | conjunction, combination, mixture; sexual intercourse with (loc.) | astr. conjunction of planets.
saṃnipātana [act. saṃnipāt] n. act of causing a common fall.
saṃnipātita var. sannipātita pp. saṃnipāt] amnf saṃnipātitā overturned, struck down, sent back | gathered.
samnibarhana var. sannibarahana [act. samnibrh] n. action of overthrowing, of defeating; repression.
saṃnibṛh var. sannibṛh [samnibṛh] v. [6] pr. (samnibṛhati) to bring down; repress.
samnibha var. sannibha [nibha] ifc. amnf saṃnibhā similar to, like (iic.).
saṃniyam var. sanniyam [samniyam] v. [1] pr. (samniyaccati) pp. (samniyata) to restrain.
saṃniyukta var. sannyiukta [pp. saṃniyuj] amnf saṃniyuktā attached to, connected with (iic.) employee.
samniyuj var. sannyuj [samniyuj] v. [7] pr. (saṃniyunakti) pp. (saṃniyukta) connect with, place at (loc.) | load with — ca. (samniyojayati) id.
samniyoga var. sannyoga [act. samniyuj] m. connection with; employment | gram. injunction, prescription.
samniyogaśiṣṭa |śiṣṭa₂| amnf samniyogaśiṣṭā gram. specified in conjunction.
samnirudh var. sannirudh [samnirudh] v. [7] pr. (samnirunaddhi) pr. r. (samnirunddhé) pp. (samniruddha) to obstruct, block; confine, hell sea; repress (not. one's senses).
samnirodha var. sannirodha act. samnirudh m. obstruction, suppression.

samnilī var. sannilī [samnilī] v. [4] pr. r. (samnilīyate) to take refuge; to crouch, to hide. upariṣṭācca vṛkṣasyabalākā sannyalīyata | tayā purīṣamutsṛṣṭam brāhmaṇasya tadopari | [Mah.] a crane had perched at the top of a tree; it dropped excrement on a brahmin who was below.

saṃniviś var. sanniviś [samniviś] v. [6] pr. r. (samniviśate) pp. (samniviṣṭa) to sit with; to associate with, to have dealings with (i.) — ca. (samniviśyati) to make sit together; to install, to lodge, to make camp; to establish, to fix in; to found (a city).

samnivṛt var. sannivṛt [samnivṛt] v. [1] pr. r. (samnivartate) pp. (samnivrtta) to return, to come back from (abl.) (towards (acc.)) | to stop (abl.) | to cease, to disappear, to stop; to die — ca. (samnivartayati) to make return, to send back; to prevent (abl.); to suppress, to stop.
saṃnivṛtta var. sannivṛtta [pp. saṃnivṛt] amnf samnivṛttā returned | removed; stopped, finished.
samnivṛtti var. sannivṛtti [act. saṃnivṛt] f. return | avoiding, stopping; abstention from abl. . asannivrttyai gatah gone without return; syn. atyan tagata.
saṃniveśa var. sanniveśa [act. saṃniviś] m. meeting, crowd.
samnisad var. sannişad [samnişad₁] v. [1] pr. (sanniṣīdati) to sit.

samnihita var. sannihita [pp. samnidhā] amnf samnihitā placed beside; near, present; within reach; contiguous, neighbor | ready, prepared to (dat.). yadi so'tra sannihitah syāt tarhi aho śobhanam bhavet I wish he were among us.
samnī var. sannī [samnī₁] v. [1] pr. (samnayati) to lead, to conduct together; to connect, to join | to mix, to amalgamate.
saṃnyas var. sannyas [samnyas] v. [4] pr. (samnyásyati) pp. (samnyasta) to deposit, abandon; to renounce (acc.) | to entrust to (g. loc.), to leave, to throw away | phil. to renounce the world.
samnyasana var. sannyasana [act. samnyas] n. phil. renunciation of the world.
samnyasta var. sannyasta [pp. samnyas] amnf saṃnyastā thrown away; put aside; abandoned consigned.
samnyāsa var. sannyāsa [act. saṃnyas] m. renunciation, abandonment | soc. ascetic life, 4th stage of brahmanical life |āśrama|.
saṃnyāsin var. sannyāsin [agt. saṃnyas] amnf samnyāsinī soc. renunciant ascetic, wandering ascetic; man in the state of sannyāsa; syn. bhiksu.
sanmātra [satmātra] amnf sanmātrā phil. whose existence alone can be affirmed (said of brahman).
sanmātradravya [dravya₁] n. phil. [Yādavaprakāśa] brahman as substance, efficient cause [kāraṇa] of its effect the phenomenal world [kārya].
sap₁ [agt. sap₁] ifc. amnf which pays homage to, which serves (iic.).
sapa |śepa| m. penis.

sapakṣa [sa₁pakṣa] amnf sapakṣā winged feathered (arrow) that has supporters; of the same side, of the same party | phil. in support (example); opp. vipakṣa — m. ally, companion; companion of fortune | phil. [Nyāya] subject validating the predicate. niścitasādhyavān sapakṣaḥ phil. [Nyāya] The valid subject satisfies the predicate.
sapañcāla [sa₁pañcāla] amnf sapañcālā accompanied by the Pañcālās.
sapatāka |sa₁patāka| amnf sapatākā supplied with standards | lit. full of twists and turns (theater).
sapatnī [sa₁patnī] f. co-wife; rival — m. sapatna rival, adversary, enemy. kuru priyasakhīvṛttim sapatnījane [AS.] Plays the role of good friend towards co-wives.
sapatnīka |ka| m. with his wife.
sapatnīmātā |mātā| f. soc. co-wife of the mother.
sapadi [sa₁pad₂] adv. immediately, at once.
saparicchada [sa₁paricchada] amnf saparicchadā with stewardship.
saparivāra [sa₁parivāra] amnf sapa rivārā accompanied by an escort or a court.
saparivāraka [sa₁parivāraka] amnf saparivārakā id.
saparyā f. adoration, homage. saparyām kṛ var. saparyām kṛ to pay homage to, to worship.
sapāda [sa₁pāda] amnf sapādā f. sapādī which has feet | augmented by a quarter; augmented by a word, by half a stanza.
sapādasaptādhyāyī [saptādhyāyī] f. gram. first seven books of the Aṣṭādhyāyī, plus the first section of the eighth book; syn. siddhakāṇḍa; opp. tripādī.

sapiṇḍa [sa₁piṇḍa] m. soc. ["who has in common a piṇḍa"] close relative, member of a family unit (same great-grandfather) | distant relative at most 6 — v. [11] pr. (sapindayati) to perform a śrāddha rite. sapiṇḍīkṛ to perform a śrāddha rite.
sapiṇḍatā [tā] f. soc. kinship (with 3 ascendants and 3 descendants).
sapindana [na] n. soc. [Garudapurāṇa] rite of
dead [pretakalpa] by which a deceased [preta] becomes a mane [pitr]; the son of the deceased offers three pinda to his close ancestors, plus a fourth for his father.
sapiṇḍīkaraṇa [karaṇa] n. soc. rite of śrāddha of a son at the death of his father; syn. sapindana.
sapidhāna [sa₁pidhāna] amnf sa pidhānā with its lid (container).
saputra [sa₁putra] amnf saputrā who has a son | accompanied by a son or a young (animal).
saputrakalatra [sa₁putrakalatra] am with (his) wife and (his) son (and not with the wife of (his) son).
sapuṣpa [sa₁puṣpa] amnf sapuṣpā fleuri, en fleurs.
sapaura [sa₁paura] amnf sapaurā ac companion of citizens.
sapta iic. saptan.
saptaka |ka| amnf saptikā with 7 components seventh — n. collection of 7 objects | week.
saptagodāvara [godāvarī] n. geo. all 7 tributaries of the Godāvarī delta, in Andhra.
saptacatvārimsa | catvārimsa | amnf sapta catvārimśī ord. 47°.
saptacatvārimsat [catvārimsat] f. 47.
saptacchada [chada] m. bio. bot. Alstonia scho laris, Indian cinchona; large tree with greyish bark and glossy leaves grouped in green
ticilles ["7 leaves"]; the bark and its latex are used in medicine; syn. saptaparna; (poetry) the acrid scent of its flowers causes headaches to those who breathe them in.

saptacchadapāṃsupāṇḍu [SPV.] pallor of the cinchona pollen. saptacchadatarava iva kusumarajovikārair āsannavartinām śiraḥśūlam utpādayanti K. They create headaches in those who approach them, like the affliction caused by the pollen of the cinchona flower.
saptájihva [jihvā] amnf saptajihvā myth. ["who has 7 tongues"] epith. of Agni.
saptajñānabhūmikā [jñānabhūmikā] f. pl. saptajñānabhūmikās phil. [YV.] the series of 7 levels of knowledge: śubhecchā, vicāraņa, tanumānasa, sattvāpatti, asaṃśakti, parārthabhāvinī, turyagā.
saptatí [ti] num. f. sg. seventy; sixty
ten | 70 years | bed. cf. Sāṃkhyakārikās.
saptatítama |tama| amnf saptatitamī ord. 70^ e.
saptatrimśa [trimśa] amnf saptatrimśī ord. 37ᵉ | made up of 37 parts.
saptatrimśat [trimśat] f. 37.
saptatrimśattama |tama| amnf saptatrimśattamī ord. 37ᵉ.
saptatrimśati [trimśati] f. 37.
saptadaśa [daśa] amnf saptadaśī ord. 17ᵉ made up of 17 elements; having 17 attributes — m. lit. stoma in 17 parts.
saptadaśan [daśan] num. pers. 17.
saptanadī [nadī] f. geo. the 7 sacred rivers of India: Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī₁, Godāvarī, Nar madā, Kāverī and Sindhu.
saptanadījala [jala] n. soc. mixed water from the 7 sacred rivers; it is used in rites of
lustration | abhiseka |.
saptanavata [navata] amnf saptanavatī ord. 97^ e.
saptanavati | navati | f. 97.
saptanavatitama |tama| amnf saptanavati tamī ord. 97ᵉ.
saptapañcāśa | pañcāśa | amnf saptapañcāśī ord. 57ᵉ.
saptapañcāśat [pañcāśat] f. 57.
saptapañcāśattama [tama] amnf sap tapañcāśattamī ord. 57ᵉ.

saptapada | pada | amnf saptapadā soc. who took the 7 steps consecrating the marriage — f. saptapadī soc. rite of the 7 steps taken by the bride and groom north of the consecrated fire in the direction of the Northeast during the wedding ceremony, to consecrate their union; the bride must walk with her right foot on 7 small piles of rice.

saptapadārthī [padārtha] f. lit. np. from the Sapta padārthī, a work of logic by Sivādityamiśra (12th century). saptaparņa | parņa | amnf saptaparņī which has 7 leaves — m. bio. bot. Alstonya scholaris, Indian quin quina; tree of the Apocynaceae family, which can reach 40 m, with a brown trunk, emitting a white latex; its glossy leaves are in corollas of 4 to 7 leathery elliptical leaves; small greenish-white flowers in umbels, very fragrant; it is used in medicine; syn. saptacchada — n. its flower — f. saptaparņī bio. bot. Mimosa pudica; syn. lajjā.
saptapātāla [pātāla] n. myth. the 7 hells under the earth; [PP.] they are called Taptavāluka, And hatāmisra, Krakaca, Argala, Kūṭaśālmalī, Rak tapūya and Kumbhīpāka.
saptapurī [purī] f. pl. saptapuryas geo. the 7 sacred cities of India: Ayodhyā, Mathurā, Haridvāra, Vārāṇasī, Kāñcī, Ujjayinī and Dvārakā.
saptabhangī [bhangī] f. pl. jn. the seven aspects of reality (or modality of assertion) accounting for the diversity of philosophical viewpoints

sophiques [nayavāda]: syād asti affirmation of existence, syān nāsti negation of existence, syād asti nāsti existence conditioned on circumstances, syād avaktavyam indescribable inquali reliable, syād asty avaktavyam indescribable with existence, syād nāsty avaktavyam indescribable with non-existence, syād asti nāsty avaktavyam indescribable with existence and non-existence if multanées.

saptama |ma| amnf saptamī ord. seventh — f. saptamī gram. locative (7th case of declension); it can concern time |parasaptamī| or space [viṣayasaptamī] | soc. cf. śītalāsaptamī. sati saptamī gram. locative absolute.

saptamātrkā [mātrkā] f. pl. saptamātrkās myth. the 7 aspects of Mātā the Mother; the Shivaite [śaiva] tradition names them: Brāhmī (śakti of Brahmā), Māheśvarī (śakti of Siva), Kaumārī (śakti of Skanda), Vaisṇavī (śakti of Viṣṇu), Vārāhī (śakti of Varāha), Indrāṇī/Aindrī (śakti of Indra) and Cāmuṇḍā or Cāmuṇḍī or Raudrī (śakti of Rudra).

saptaratna [ratna] n. pl. saptaratnāni the 7 jewels of the cakravartin: the wheel, the elephant, the horse, the gem, the woman, the treasurer, and the general. saptarși [ṛṣi] m. [n. pl. nom. saptarṣayas] myth. the 7 Vedic sages or patriarchs; they are the

progenitors [prajāpati] from the mind of Brahmā to give birth to the world; they are associated with the stars of the Great Bear; [Mah.] those of the era [manvantara] of Svāyambhuva are: Marīci, Vasistha, Angirā, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu; [SB.] those of the era [manvantara] of Vaivasvata are: Vasistha, Kaśyapa, Atri, Jamadagni, Gau tama, Viśvāmitra and Bharadvāja; sometimes Agastya, Kanva and Bhrgu are also listed; they were saved from the flood by clinging to the horn of VișnuMatsya. saptarṣīnu ha sma vai pura_rkṣā ityācakṣate [SB.] (The constellation of) the seven sages was in fact also called, formerly, the Bears.
saptarṣimaṇḍala [maṇḍala] n. astr. the Great Bear.
saptavimsá [vimsa] amnf saptavimsī ord. 27e made up of 27 parts.
saptávimásti [vimásti] f. 27.
saptaśata [śata] amnf saptaśatī 700 — n. 700; 107 — f. saptaśatī 700 | lit. collection of 700 verses, like the Gāthāsaptaśatī.

saptaśataka [śataka] n. bed. n.p. saptaśataka or Sattasai, collection of 700 erotic verses in prākṛta by King Hāla, dealing with romantic relationships in a pastoral setting; cf. Gāthāsaptaśatī — f. saptaśatikā bd. n.p. from the saptaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā in 700 verses.
saptasasti [sasti] f. 67.
saptasaptata |saptata| amnf saptasaptatī ord. 77ᵉ.
saptasaptati |saptati| f. 77.
saptasaptatitama |tama| amnf saptasapta titamī ord. 77ᵉ.
saptahotr |hotr| m. pl. saptahotāras ved. the 7 priests who sacrificed for whom? (classic question of a ritual riddle |brahmodya|).
saptāṅga [aṅga₁] n. soc. [Arthaśāstra] the set of the 7 bodies of the State: the king, the territory, the administration, the treasury, the capital, the coercive power [danda], and the allies.
saptādhyāyī [adhyāyī] f. gram. first seven books of the Aştādhyāyī.
saptāśīta |aśīta| amnf saptāśītī ord. 87°.
saptāśīti [aśīti] f. 87.
saptāśītitama [tama] amnf saptāśītitamī ord. 87ᵉ.
saptāśva |aśva| m. pl. myth. the 7 horses of Sūrya, symbolizing the 7 days of the week.
saptāha [aha] m. ["7 days"] week | soc. recitation of a text over 7 days, not. of the Bhāgavatapurāņa.
saptata |saptati| ifc. amnf saptatī ord. 70^ e.
saptan num. pers. pl. |name. sapta| the number seven | gr. ; lat. septem; all. sieben; eng. se fri; fr. seven; pkt. satta.
sapraṇava [sa₁praṇava] amnf sapraṇavā accompanied by the sacred syllable om 3.
sapratigha [sa₁pratigha] amnf sapra tighā which encounters resistance; which has an opposition.
sapratighatva |tva| n. bd. impenetrability of matter.
sapratibha [sa₁pratibhā₂] amnf sapra tibhā intelligent; who demonstrates the presence of mind.
saprayojana [sa₁prayojana] amnf sa prayojanā with a pattern; intentional.
sapraharṣa [sa₁praharṣa] amnf sapraharṣā in joy, experiencing pleasure.
saprema [sa₁preman] amnf sapremā af fectioné; tender.

saphala [sa₁phala] amnf saphalā that bears fruit ["having testicles"] uncastrated productive; successful; crowned with success, advantageous with the result — v. [11] pr. (saphalayati) to make profitable; to cause to succeed; to benefit from. saphalam kr to make profitable, to make fruitful | to keep one's promise; to satisfy. saphalībhū to be profitable, to succeed. saphalībhūta become profitable; having succeeded. saphalīkṛ to make profitable; to cause to succeed; to benefit from. saphalīkṛta made profitable or useful; successful, ac compli. saphalīkaraṇam the act of making profitable or useful; success.
saphalatva [tva] n. the state of being profitable; the state of being successful.
saphalya |saphalaya| n. the act of bearing fruit, utility, profit.
sábandhu [sa₁bandhu] amnf of the same family, relative | accompanied by a friend or a parent.
sabar n. iic. milk; nectar | eng. sap; fr. sap.

sabarmat [mat] amnf sabarmatī which emits milk or nectar — f. sabarmatī geo. np. of the river sabarmatī or Svabhramatī, river of Gurjara; it flows into the Gulf of Khambhāta to the East of the mouth of the Indus; on its bank is the hermitage [āśrama] Satyāgraha.
sábala |sa₁bala| amnf sabalā powerful, strong | accompanied by an escort or an army | myth. accompanied by Balarāma. of the seeds; fertile; opp. nirbīja.
sabījatva [tva] n. fertility.
sabrahmacārin [sa₁brahmacārin] m. soc. fellow Vedic scholar.
sabhanga [sa₁bhanga] amnf sabhangā gram. with division (of a word).

sabhangaślesa [ślesa] m. lit. figure of speech of double meaning in which the ambiguity lies in a different division into words; opp. abhangaslesa. śvetodhāvati The (white) horse runs/The dog runs towards here (paradigmatic example of segmentation ambiguity leading to multiple meanings).

sabhā f. house, common room; at the inn, inn | assembly, meeting; society, congregation | court of a prince, good society; circle of poets | audience hall; court of justice, council chamber | [lokasabhā] mod. chamber of deputies | [paṇditasabhā] symposium of scholars | [citrasabhā] art gallery | [dyūtasabhā] dice room — n. sabha ifc. hall of (2nd century); meeting of (2nd century) (chiefs, demons) | all. Sippe.

sabhāpati [pati] m. soc. superior of a society; president of an assembly; master of an academy; deity of a shrine | keeper of a gambling hall, responsible for procuring the dice and organizing the gambling tables.
sabhāparvan [parvan] n. lit. np. from the Sabhāparva, 2nd book of the Mah., "of the assembly".
sabhāsiṃha |siṃha| m. hist. np. of Sabhāsiṃha, king in Bundelkhand, son of Chattrasāla (18th century).
sabhāga [sa₁bhāga] amnf sabhāgā com mun, universal.
sabhāja |sa₁bhāja| amnf sabhājā with a person of great merit — v. |11| pr. (sabhājayati) abs. (sabhājayitvā) to show respect to (acc.), to pay homage to; to serve, to honor; to venerate.
sabhājana [act. sabhāja] n. civility, courtesy (not. when welcoming or leaving a friend).
sabhājita [pp. sabhāja] amnf sabhājitā served, honored, rewarded.
sabhājya [pfp. [1] sabhāja] amnf sabhājyā which must be honored.
sabhārya [sa₁bhāryā] amnf sabhāryā accompanied by his wife.
sabhika [ika] m. soc. supervisor of the hall of
Paris [dyūta]; he keeps track of gambling winnings, under royal authority. sabhikam varjayitvaikam rudro'pi na raksitum ta
rati [MK.] Only the dealer (can save you), not even Rudra can protect you.

sábhya [sabhāya] amnf sabhyā suitable for an assembly; appropriate in society | courteous, polite, civilized; decent; not. noble language | soc. ap belonging to the court of (g.) | soc. refers to a solemn fire for royal use; it is one of the pañcāgni — m. member of the council; assessor; judge; honorable person.
sabhyatā [tā] f. savoir-vivre; honorability; civili sation.
sabhyatva |tva| n. id.
sabhrukuṭīmukha [sa₁bhrukuṭīmukha] amnf sabhrukuṭīmukhī who frowns.
sabhrūbhaṅga [sa₁bhrūbhaṅga] amnf sabhrūbhangā who frowns. sabhrūbhangam adv. frowning.
sám [related to sa₁] pf. (intensive, convergence) completely, totally, perfectly | with; in accordance with, in agreement with; together, in com
mun | conversely | lat. sem.

samá amnf samā equal, even, flat | similar, alike, identical to (ig); as expensive as (i.); at the same level as; parallel to | normal, ordinary, common; mediocre, neither good nor bad; indifferent — n. even surface, plain | fairness; equality, identity | math. equation — f. cf. samā | gr. οὐς; lat. si milis; all. zusammen; ang. same; fr. similar. samam adv. in the same way, likewise, equally | at the same time, simultaneously, together; at the same time as, with (i.); syn. saha₁, sākam exactly, precisely, in accordance with (iic.). samena adv. in the same way, equally exactly. samam kr equalize, balance; put in order. samīkṛ equalize, level; adjust, fine-tune; shave. samīkaraņa math. equation. samībhū to be balanced; to be placed in the same way to become indifferent.
samákāla [kāla₁] amnf samakālā simultaneous. samakālam adv. simultaneously.
samakālaprāpta [prāpta] amnf sa makālaprāptā gram. (rule) applicable simultaneously.
samákālīna [kālīna] amnf samakālīnā syn chrone; opp. viṣamakālīna.
samacitta [samacitta] amnf samacittā of equal humor, balanced, serene.
samacittatva [tva] n. balance of mood, equanimity; phlegm; serenity.

samatā [tā] f. similarity; equality, identity; balance; symmetry; equity | lit. uniformity of diction, a poetic quality. doṣāṇāṃ samatā med. balance of humors. samatām nī to share equitably; to balance, to regulate.
samatāvasthā [avasthā₂] f. phil. psychological state of equilibrium; syn. samādhi.
samatva [tva] n. equality, identity | equality of mood, balance; regularity, uniformity.
samaduḥkha [duḥkha] amnf samaduḥkhā who shares the pain; compassionate. vihagāḥ samaduḥkhā iva cukruśuḥ the birds cried as if in sympathy.
samaduhkhasukha [duhkhasukha] amnf samaduhkhasukhā who shares joys and sorrows | indifferent to joys and sorrows — m. companion for better or for worse.
samabhanga [bhanga] m. rigid standing posture, knees locked.
samabhāva | bhāva | m. equality; equity — ifc. equitable treatment of (iic.) — amnf samabhāvā of the same kind.
samarūpya | rūpya | amnf samarūpyā who was partenait to an honest man.

samavṛtta [vṛtta] amnf samavṛttā phon. homosyllabic, said of a meter whose 4 feet [pada] have the same structure; this class includes the Vedic meters gāyatrī, uṣṇih, anuṣṭubh₂, bṛhatī, paṅkti, triṣṭubh and ja gatī (from 6 to 12 syllables per foot) and the classical meters upajāti, vamsastha, vasantati lakā, mandākrāntā, śārdūlavikrīdita, śaśivadanā, and sragdharā.
samasamskrta [samskrta] n. bed. pure and simple Sanskrit.
samastha [stha] amnf samasthā ["who lives normally" | happy; opp. viṣamastha.
samānka [anka] m. math. even number; opp. visamanka.
samāntara₁ [antara] amnf samāntarā in pro portion of (with num.) | parallel. trisamāntara of size three times greater than that of.
samaka |samaka| amnf samikā equal to, the same as.
samakṣa |samakṣa| amnf samakṣā vi sible, present, manifest ["under his own eyes"]. samakṣam adv. manifestly; under his eyes; in front of, in the presence of g. .
samagra [samagra] amnf samagrā com complete, whole, integral; all, each; (pl.) all | well provided with (i.); who has everything he needs. plavagāḥ samagrāḥ |Rām.| all the monkeys.
samaj [samaj] v. [1] pr. (samajati) to gather, to assemble.
samajyā |samajya| f. assembly.
samañj [samañj] v. [7] pr. (samanakti) pp. (samakta) to anoint; to adorn | to unite by anointing; in general, to unite with.
samañjasa [samañjasa] amnf samañjasā appropriate, correct, regular; excellent, virtuous, just. samañjasam adv. as is fitting.
samatikram [samatikram] v. [1] pr. (sa matikrāmati) pr. r. (samatikrāmate) to transgress, neglect; to surpass | to let pass (time). dvau māsau samatikramya two months having passed.
samatī [samatī] v. [2] pr. (samatyeti) pp. (samatīta) to pass completely, to cross; to leave behind.
samatīta [pp. samatī] amnf samatītā past, elapsed; crossed.

samadhika [samadhika] amnf sa madhikā superabundant, excessive; superfluous, redundant | abundant; intense; extraordinary | greater than, exceeding (iic.). samadhikam in quantity. māsasamadhika greater than a month.
samadhikatara [tara] amnf samadhikatarā compar. even more abundant | more than necessary; excessive. usņocchvāsam samadhikatarocchvāsinā |MD.| To the burning sighs (respond) even deeper sighs.
samadhigata [pp. samadhigam] amnf samadhigatā came very close, approached.
samadhigam [samadhigam] v. [1] pr. (sa madhigacchati) pp. (samadhigata) to approach together; to get closer to obtain, acquire, surpass, exceed.
sámana [samana] n. meeting; assembly, festival | embrace; amorous exchange.
samanantara [samanantara] amnf samanantarā immediately contiguous to; which follows immediately (abl. g.) | continuous.
sámanas [sa₁manas] amnf of the same opinion; unanimous | endowed with reason.
samanā [f. samana] adv. together; at the same point; at the same time | likewise; united formerly.

sámanta [samanta] amnf samantā voi sin, contiguous, adjacent; whole | universal; forming a whole — m. limit, boundary — f. samantā pl. sa mantās neighborhood. sámantam var. samantāt adv. on all sides, from every angle, all around; everywhere, in every direction, entirely | in conjunction with; together. samantena adv. on all sides | (with na) nowhere. samantāt adv. from every angle | completely. samantatas adv. on all sides, from every angle, all around; everywhere, in every direction, entirely | in conjunction with.
samantapañcaka [pañcaka] n. myth. [Mah.] np. of the ford [tīrtha] samantapañcaka at Kurukṣetra, where Paraśurāma made three lakes of the blood of the kṣatriyās he had killed.
Samantabhadra [bhadra] m. hist. np. of the Bengali prince Samantabhadra, (1016–1100); gifted in studies, he was sent at age 8 to study at Ca

Kashmir [Kaśmīra]; returning home, his parents married him to the Brahmaṇī Vimaladīpī, but after a few years he went back to Kashmir where he was ordained a Buddhist monk; At 28 he went to study in Nālandā, where he became abbot; a dākinī appeared to him, telling him to go in search of his master Tilopa with whom he spent 12 years of trials; he transmitted his teachings to Pullahari near Nālandā; his student Marpa brought his teachings to Tibet, translated the doctrine there and founded the Kagyūpa lineage; he is one of the 64 accomplished [mahāsiddha]; cf. Nādaprada, Nāropa | bd. his idealization Samantabhadra "the Generous Everywhere", accomplished [bodhisattva] embodying Total Compassion; Its 64 representations of Borobudur in Java welcome the pilgrim at the 5th balustrade.
samanyu [sa₁manyu] amnf filled with anger, furious | pained.
samanvaya [act. samanvi] m. succession, sequence; causal sequence; correlation. samanvayāt adv. therefore.
samanvi [samanvi] v. [2] pr. (samanveti) pp. (samanvita) to follow, to accompany | to ensue.
samanvita [pp. samanvi] amnf saman vitā accompanied by, in relation to, associated with; endowed with (i. iic.) — ifc. which corresponds to (iic.). caturbāhusamanvita endowed with 4 arms.
samabhigam [samabhigam] v. [1] pr. (sa mabhigacchati) to go together towards, to approach to have sexual relations with (i.).
samabhidhāv [samabhidhāv] v. [1] pr. (samabhidhāvati) pp. (samabhidhāvita) to throw oneself on.
samabhiplu [samabhiplu] v. [1] pr. r. (sa mabhiplavate) pp. (samabhipluta) to flood.
samabhipluta [pp. samabhiplu] amnf samabhiplutā overwhelmed, flooded | eclipsed (said of the Moon) | overwhelmed by, drowned under (i.).
samabhiruh [samabhiruh] v. [1] pr. r. (sa mabhirohati) pp. (samabhirūḍha) to climb together.
samabhirūḍha [pp. samabhiruh] amnf samabhirūḍhā gravi together — n. jn. one of the seven argumentative points of view [naya].
samabhivyāhāra [act. samabhivyāhr] m. common mention, association.
samabhivyāhr [samabhivyāhr] v. [1] pr. (samabhivyāharati) pp. (samabhivyāhṛta) to mention together, to associate.
samabhihāra [samabhihāra] m. gram. (in the sense of) repetition | well-executed action.
samabhyas [samabhyas₂] v. [4] pr. (sa mabhyasyati) pp. (samabhyasta) to practice; practice; to study.
samabhyasa [act. samabhyas] m. practice, exercise; study.

samayá [act. sami] m. meeting, frequenting; convention, agreement; occasion, event, circumstance, appropriate time | current time; hour | rule, practice, doctrine, authority; rite. samayam kṛ to agree with someone (i.); to commit oneself. samayam grah to subscribe to an agreement. samayam tyaj to break an agreement. samayam raks to keep a commitment. samayo'sti there is time. samayāt adv. subject to agreement. samayena adv. according to the agreement. tena samayena adv. at that time. iha samaye adv. under those circumstances. samayīkī to stipulate, to make necessary. samayākṛ to pass the time; to waste time; to drag things out. namaskārasamaye adv. soc. during the offering to the deity. iti samayaḥ kṛtaḥ the deal was struck. śrīman kṛpayā kaḥ samayaḥ Sir, what time is it, please? madhyāhnaprāyaḥ samayaḥ It's about noon. samayam anurudhyasva Keep your appointment. samayam anupālaya id. samayo bhoktum It's time to eat.
samayakāra [kāra] m. making an appointment.
samayábheda [bheda] m. act of breaking an agreement phil. division into classes.
samayabhedoparacanacakra [uparacanacakra] m. bed. n.p. from the samayabhedoparacanacakra "Classification of the divisions of the doctrinal tradition", treatise bd. of Vasumitra.
samayamātṛkā [mātṛkā] f. lit. np. from the Sa mayamātrkā "Encounters of a Matron", satirical work by Kşemendra; it narrates in a pi caresque manner the adventures of a prostitute at the Cache mire.
samayasāra [sāra] n. bed. n.p. from samayasāra, phil text. prakrit of Acārya Kuṇḍakuṇḍa, phil. Digambara Jain (3rd century or later).
samayācāra [ācāra] m. phil. the way consistent with doctrine; syn. dakṣiṇācāra; opp. vāmācāra.
samayācārin |in| amnf samayācāriņī soc. who follows the path in accordance with the doctrine.
samayānurūpa [anurūpa] amnf samayānurūpā in accordance with the circumstances, appropriate.
Samayocitapadyamālikā | ucitapadyamālikā| f. bed. n.p. from the Samayocitapadyamālikā, collection of verses | śloka | popular.
samáyā [samayā] adv. through, in the middle of, among (acc. i.) | in the vicinity of (acc. ig) | completely, thoroughly.
samara [act. samr] m. conflict, fight, war.
Samarasimha [simha] m. hist. np. of Samarasimha, 13th century astrologer, author of the Tājikatantrasāra and the Prcchoddeśa.
samarānganasūtradhāra [anganasūtradhāra] m. lit. np. from the Samarāngaņasūtradhāra, an encyclopedic work attributed to Bhojadeva; it deals notably with architecture [vāstu] and theatre.
samarth [samarth] v. [10] pr. r. (sa marthayate) pp. (samarthita) prepare; finish | consider; contemplate; judge | perceive; understand; determine; approve | encourage, comfort.

samartha [agt. samarth] amnf samarthā conforming, appropriate, adequate; useful; powerful, vi gourous | competent; capable, able to (inf. loc. dat.); intelligent | gram. (word) contributing to the meaning of a sentence | (words) of the same meaning, of comparable meaning

tibles [ekārthībhāva], or semantically connected — m. soc. ability; title of assistant to priests in a temple; e.g., instrumentalist or person in charge of fixing the flag to the temple spire (non brah mane) — n. capacity, skill | gram. syntax. samarthah padavidhih gram. [Pāṇini] The instructions concerning words apply insofar as they are semantically compatible together. 'tibhārah samarthānām kim krūram ko vya vasāyinām ko videšah savidyānām kah parah priyavādinām || What is too difficult for a wise person? What danger exists for a bold person? What is foreign to a scholar? What is unattainable for a flatterer?
samarthatara [compar. samartha] amnf sa marthatarā very intelligent; better than.
samarthita [pp. samarth] amnf samar thitā taken into account, considered; determined; approached prayed; established.

samarp [ca. samṛ] v. [10] pr. (samarpayati) pp. (samarpita) to send, to throw at (acc.); to reach, to wound | to deliver; to offer; to entrust — pr. r. (samar payate) to surrender, to give oneself up, to abandon oneself. samarpayāmi I offer (said especially at the temple). haste samarp to entrust (task).

samarpaṇa [act. samarp] n. gift, transmission, communication; act of dedication; dedication, surrender. samskṛtasya sevanam samskṛtāya jīvanam | lokahitasamṛddhaye bhavatu tanusamarpaṇam || Let us serve Sanskrit, let us dedicate our lives to Sanskrit, let us devote ourselves to improving the well-being of the world.
samarpita [pp. samarp] amnf samarpitā delivered; offered; entrusted; transmitted. ayam janah kasya haste samarpitah into whose care this person has been entrusted.
samala [sa₁mala] amnf samalā dirty, soiled; impure — n. excrement, filth. samalīkṛ to soil, stain, pollute.

samalamkr [samalamkr] v. [8] pr. (samalamkaroti) to adorn, decorate; embellish. vāņyekā samalamkaroti purusam yā samskṛtā dhāryate | kṣīyante khalu bhūṣaṇāni satataṃ vāgbhūṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇam || Only language used with refinement (Sanskrit) is the ornament of a person; truly mere adornments are fleeting, while the distinction of language alone is a lasting ornament.
samalaṃkṛta var. samalaṅkṛta pp. samalamkṛl amnf samalamkṛtā completely decorated.
samavakāra [samavakāra] m. lit. genre of heroic drama in 3 acts.
samavakṣip [samavakṣip] v. [1] pr. (samavakṣipati) pp. (samavakṣipta) to push back with force.
samávatta [pp. samavadā] amnf sama vattā cut into pieces — m. pieces together.
samavadā [samavadā₁] v. [4] pr. (samava dyati) pp. (samavatta) cut into pieces and rasp.
samavadhā [samavadhā] v. [3] pr. (sama vadadhāti) to gather together.
samavadhāna [act. samavadhā] n. gathering | phil. [Nyāya] simultaneous presence.
samavanata [samavanata] amnf sama vanatā completely curved; deeply inclined bent (not. to drink water).
samavasthā [samavasthā₁] v. [1] pr. (samavatisthati) pp. (samavasthita) to be stable, to be firm.
samavasthita [pp. samavasthā] amnf samavasthitā unshakable.
samavasrava [act. samavasru] m. flow of water; drain.
samavasru [samavasru] abs. (samavasrutya) flow downwards.

samavāya [act. samave] m. encounter, union, meeting, assembly | concomitance; collision, conflict; conjunction (of celestial bodies) | phil. [Nyāya] inseparability between notions | phil. [Vaiseṣika] the category [padārtha] of inherences: indissociable relation of coexistence between subject and predicate, between the whole and its parts, between quality and the qualified, between movement and the moving, between the individual and the genus, between property and substance. Gram. combination of phonemes; substance inherent in an action (such as pāka, cooking). samavāyāt var. samavāyena in combination. samavāyam kr to gather, to group, to ally. samavāyo hi dustaraḥ unity is strength. gunaguninoh samavāyah [Nyāya] inherent relationship between quality and the qualified.
samavāyasaṃbandha [saṃbandha] m. phil. |Nyāya| relation of inherence | gram. inseparable relation of meaning between a compound and its members.
samavāyasūtra |sūtra| n. bed. n.p. from Sa mavāyasūtra, a Jain text.
samavāyānga [anga₁] n. lit. 4th text of the jaina canon, developing the 10 doctrinal subjects.
samavāyi iic. samavāyin. samavāyikāraņa [kāraņa] n. phil. [Nyāya] inherent cause.
samavāyin [agt. samave] amnf sa mavāyinī met; close, linked; united | concomitant — ifc. inherent in; aggregated to (iic.) — m. partner phil. individual soul linked to the body [puruṣa].
samave [samave] v. [2] pr. (samaiti) pp. (samaveta) to come together.
samaveta [pp. samave] amnf samavetā gathered, assembled; gathered; inherent — ifc. included in; inherent in (iic.).
samaś [samaś₁] v. [5] pr. r. (samaśnuté) pp. (astá) to attain, to reach (acc.) | to obtain, to enjoy (acc.) | to fulfill (a vow). atra brahma samaśnute phil. [BU.] Here he enjoys brahman.
samaṣṭi [act. samas] f. attainment | phil. [Vedānta] totality, aggregate; the cosmic. samașticitta | citta | m. phil. | Vedānta | cosmic thought.
samas [samas₂] v. [4] pr. (samasyati) pp. (sa masta) to combine, compose, unite — ps. (sama syate) to form a compound; to be united.
samasana [act. samas] n. gathering, combination, composition; unification | gram. formation of a compound word |samāsa|.
sámasta [pp. samas] amnf samastā com combined, gathered; condensed; united, whole; total, forming a whole | gram. compound (word) | phil. inherent; penetrating, pervading — m. totality, aggregate.
samastapada [pada] n. gram. compound word; syn. samāsa.
samastaloka [loka] m. the whole world. samastalokāh sukhino bhavantu Let us work for the happiness of the world.
samasya |samasya| amnf samasyā to gather, to complete — ifc. set of (iic.) — f. cf. samasyā.
samasyapūrti |pūrti| f. soc. competition of scholars to complete a beginning of verse.

samasyā [f. samasya] f. meeting; the act of remaining together | [avadhāna] problem in the form of a sentence or poem to be completed — ifc. meeting with, family of (iic.). samasyāpūraņa | pūraņa | n. lit. exercise in poetic improvisation, consisting of completing a stanza whose 4th line (or 1st) is provided.
samasyāpūrti [pūrti] f. cf. samasyāpūraņa.
sámā [f. sama] f. year | season; weather, weather conditions | all. Sommer; ang. summer.
samānta | anta | m. end of the year | | samanta | neighbor. samānte adv. at the end of the year.
samāntara₂ [antara] n. interval of one year. samāntare adv. within a year.
samāṃsa [sa₁māṃsa] amnf samāṃsā accompanied by meat, containing meat.
samākṣara [samakṣara] m. bed. palindrome; syn. tulyākṣara.
samākṣip [samākṣip] v. [1] pr. (samākṣipati) pp. (samākṣipta) to repel forcefully.
samāgata [pp. samāgam] amnf samāgatā approached, met; gathered | went in company to (prati acc.).
samāgam [samāgam] v. |1| pr. (samāgacchati) pp. (samāgata) to meet, to confront, to come together (with (i.saha₂)); to assemble, to come towards, to approach.

samāgama |act. samāgam| m. encounter, meeting; collision; junction; union, assembly, association; sexual union (with (ig loc.)) | astr. conjunction (of planets) — f. samāgamā ifc. encounter with; meeting of (iic.).
samāgamana |act. samāgam| n. meeting, union.
samācakṣ [samācakṣ] v. [2] pr. r. (samācaṣṭe) to tell, relate, say.
samācar [samācar] v. [1] pr. (samācarati) pp. (samācarita) to conduct oneself, to behave (towards (loc.)) | to do, to practice, to exercise, to accomplish. āhāraṃ samācar to feed on (i.).
samācāra [act. samācar] m. conduct, way of life; not. virtuous conduct; monastic rule | practice, custom, usage — amnf samācārā who is regular in his conduct.
samācchad [samācchad₁] pp. (samācchanna) ca. (samācchādayati) to cover, to wrap.
samāja [act. samaj] m. gathering; assembly, meeting, convention; club, company, society, party.
samājika [ika| amnf samājikī participant; spectator; cf. sāmājika.

samādiś [samādiś] v. [1] pr. (samādiśati) pp. (samādiṣṭa) to assign, to allocate | to show, to indicate; to declare, to announce, to designate, name sea | to prescribe, to command (dat. inf.) — ca. (samādeśayati) to order, to command.
samādiṣṭa [pp. samādiś] amnf samādiṣṭā informed, instructed; enjoined, commanded.
samādeśa [act. samādiś] m. informatopn; instruction, command, injunction.

samādhā [samādhā] v. [3] pr. (samādadhati) pr. r. (samādadhate) pp. (samāhita) to place, set, fix, install; establish; bring together; combine, arrange; restore, repair. cittam samādhā to concentrate on, to become absorbed in loc. . kopaṃ samādhā [r.] to become angry. dṛṣṭiṃ samādhā to fix one's gaze on (loc.).

samādhāna [act. samādhā] n. arrangement; establishment; the act of feeding (not. the fire with logs) | the act of settling; resolution; reconciliation, arrangement | lit. [bhāṣya] dispelling doubts (in the argumentation of a commentary) | concentration of the mind; meditation | phil. [Vedānta] stability of the mind; its practice is one of the 6 cardinal virtues [satsampad] | phil. [Nyāya] answer to an objection; justification lit. rhet. the act of planting the seed of the plot.

samādhi [act. samādhā] m. union, totality; accomplishment, completion | concentration of the mind; contemplation, accomplished religious meditation; identification with the object of meditation; spiritual trance, ecstasy; (Eliade) enstasis | phil. state of psychic arrest, allows one to feel objective divine reality; [yoga] spiritual communion, 8th stage and accomplishment of rājayoga (cf. aṣṭāṅgayoga); [Vedānta] several qualities [guna] of samādhi are distinguished: tāmasika samādhi, the contemplation of emptiness, in the state of śūnyabhāva; rājasika samādhi, which includes 3 stages: savikalpa samādhi, identification with the object while remaining conscious of its identity, sa vitarka samādhi, reasoned identification ["with distinction", and savicāra samādhi, knowledge of the purpose of the identified object ["with reflection"]; finally sāttvika samādhi (syn. nirvicāra samādhi), total and impersonal identification with the object ["without reflection"], which comprises 3 stages: ānandānugata samādhi, the state of grace, asmitā samādhi, self-realization, where one says tingue purușa de prakrti (sabīja), and asamprajñāta samādhi, the cessation of thought, where one attains liberation [kaivalya] by suppression of personal impressions [saṃskāra], without the support of citta (in dharmamegha, nirbīja) | bd. extinction [nirvāṇa] or absorption into the void [śūnyatāsamādhi] | lit. (poetic) intuition of meaning | mod. death; ashes; mausoleum, cenotaph.
Samādhipāda [pāda] m. phil. [yoga] np. of the Samādhipāda, section of the Yogasūtra dealing with the Way of Union.
samādhimat |mat| amnf samādhimatī ab sorbé en méditation | attentive.
samādhimudrā [mudrā] f. bd. meditation gesture, in lotus posture, hands palms towards the sky one on top of the other at the level of the navel; syn. dhyānimudrā.
Samādhirājasūtra [rājasūtra] n. lit. np. of the Samādhirājasūtra "Discourse on the king of contemporaneity", very ancient text of the bd. Mahāyāna.
samāná₁ m. med. the vital flow |prāṇa| of management.

samāná₂ [samaana] amnf samānā f. samānī same, identical, equal, homogeneous, uniform form; similar; of the same age | common, average, median; moderate | current; general; universal | math. (number) integer — m. even, equal; ami. samānam as, just as (i.).
samānátā [tā] f. equality (with (g. iic.)). strīśūdrasamānatā soc. equality of status between women and servants.
samānátra [tra] adv. in the same place.
samānátva [tva] n. equality (with (i. iic.)).

samānadharma [dharma] amnf samānadharmā which has the same qualities, similar to (i.) | which shares the same interests, colleague — m. lit. [Nyāya] common property of the subject [upameya] and the object [upamāna] of a comparison.

samānamudrā [mudrā] f. hand gesture evoking several associated words. samānādhikaraņa [adhikaraņa] n. gram. congruence, coindexation; agreement; coreference; opp. vyadhikaraṇa — amnf samānādhikaraṇā gram. in the same case; coindexed (with (i. i. ic.)); codenoting; coreferent, which refers to the same object. kartṛṣamānādhikaraṇam gram. coindexation with the agent.
samānādhikaraṇatā [tā] f. gram. agreement; co-indexing.
samānādhikaraṇatva |tva| n. id.
samānādhikaraṇabahuvrīhi [bahuvrīhi] amnf gram. is said of descriptive exocentric compounds, adjectival forms of appositional compounds |karmadhāraya|.
samānādhikaraṇaviśeṣaṇa [viśeṣaṇa] n. gram. re lation of coreference, agreement of predication.
samānādhikaraṇya [adhikaraṇya] n. gram. CO indexing; agreement.
samānārtha [artha] amnf samānārtha having the same purpose | gram. having the same meaning; synonym — m. math. equivalence.
samānārthaka [ka] amnf samānārthakā of the same meaning | lit. qualifies dictionaries of synonyms; opp. anekārthaka.
samānārthatā [tā] f. equivalence; not. same social status.
samānārthatva [tva] n. fact of having the same purpose identity of meaning, synonymy.

samānodaka [udaká] amnf samānodikā soc. ["who shares the water (of the libation to the deceased)"] distant relatives, up to the 14th degree; closer relatives, up to the 7th degree, are called sapinda.
samāna₃ [sa₁māna₂] amnf samānā es timé, honored (of (l.)) | proud.
samāna₄ |sa₁māna₂| amnf samānā of the same measure.
samānikā [ika] f. phone. variety of meter anustubh₂.
samānī [samānī] v. [1] pr. (samānayati) to bring, to gather; to bring, to offer. hastau samānīya with joined hands.
samāp [samāp] v. [5] pr. (samāpnoti) pp. (samāpta) pf. (pari) to attain, accomplish, complete; to obtain fully, win — ca. (samāpayati) to finish, complete; to put an end to, destroy.
samāpaka [agt. samāp] amnf samāpikā that completes, that finishes, that supplements. samāpikākriyā f. gram. verb having the perfect aspect.
samāpat [samāpat] v. [1] pr. (samāpatati) pp. (samāpatita) to fly together | to rush upon, to fall upon, to attack; to reach; to have sexual relations with (i. saha₂).

samāpatty [act. samāpad] f. encounter, meeting | accident; chance; occurrence | attainment; completion, conclusion | phil. [Yoga] contemplation bd. subdivision of the 4th stage of meditation (there are eight). samāpattyā by chance; by accident.
samāpattidrsta [drsta] amnf samāpattidrstā seen by chance. sa mayā samāpattidrstah I saw him by chance.
samāpad [samāpad₁] v. [4] pr. r. (samāpadyate) pp. (samāpanna) to attack, assail; to undertake; to realize; to accomplish, complete.
samāpana [act. samāp] n. completion; conclusion | accomplishment; destruction.
samāpanna [pp. samāpad] amnf samāpannā arrived; undertaken; done, accomplished; concluded, finished.
samāpita [pp. ca. samāp] amnf samāpitā accomplished, finished, completed, done.
samāpta [pp. samāp] amnf samāptā at teint, obtained, completed; accomplished, finished — ifc. lit. here it ends (iic.) (colophon at the end of a work). iti ... samāptam lit. colophon.
samāpti [act. samāp] f. completion, fulfillment; perfection | closure; destruction, dissolution.
samāplu [samāplu] v. [1] pr. r. (samāplavate) pp. (samāpluta) to bathe, to immerse oneself | to overflow; to flood; to submerge.
samāmnā |samāmnā| v. |1| pr. (samāmanati) pp. (samāmnāta) mention together, enumerate; transmit as tradition.
samāmnāta |pp. samāmnā| amnf samāmnātā transmitted; traditional.
samāmnāya [pfp. [1] samāmnā] m. enumeration, catalogue; tradition, sacred text.
samāya [act. same] m. visit; meeting.
samāyā [samāyā] v. [2] pr. (samāyāti) pp. (samāyāta) to come to this very place; to approach, to come from (abl.), to go towards (acc. loc.); to arrive at acc. .
samāyin [agt. same] amnf samāyinī which occurs with or simultaneously.
samāyukta |pp. samāyuj| amnf samāyuktā prepared; ready; decided | met; put in contact | provided.
samāyuj [samāyuj] v. [7] pr. (samāyunakti) pr. r. (samāyunkte) pp. (samāyukta) join, attach together | prepare; confront, encircle — ca. (samāyojayati) provide (i.).

samāyoga [act. samāyuj] m. conjunction, union, connection; contact with (i. ii.) preparation; adjustment; not. of an arrow to a bow cause, origin; motive, object. samāyogāt adv. as a consequence of; by means of.
samārabdha [pp. samārabh] amnf samārabdhā taken in hand; undertaken, begun that which has begun; that which has taken place.
samārabh [samārabh] v. [1] pr. r. (samārabhate) pp. (samārabdha) to take in hand; to undertake; to begin (at (inf.)).
samārambha [act. samārabh] m. undertaking; entrepreneurial spirit | beginning, commencement.
samārambhaṇa [act. samārabh] n. taking in hand.
samārambhin [agt. samārabh] amnf samārambhinī entrepreneur.
samārādh [samārādh] ca. (samārādhayati) to win, to be reconciled; to give thanks to.
samārādhana [act. samārādh] n. conciliation, thanksgiving | soc. not. common feast on return from pilgrimage, or on the occasion of a wedding.

samāruh [samāruh] v. [1] pr. (samārohati) pp. (samārūḍha) to go up on or towards (acc. loc.); to ascend (acc.) | to reach, to advance towards (acc.) — ca. (samāropayati) to raise, to set up, to erect; to raise up on (acc.).
samāropa [act. samāruh] m. rising, as cension | putting an arc under tension.
samāropaṇa [act. samāruh] n. id. | phil. internalization.
samālamb [samālamb] v. [1] pr. r. (samālambate) pp. (samālambita) to hang from, to be suspended from; to keep (such a state) | to rely on, to depend on, to trust in acc. .
samālok [samālok] abs. (samālokya) to consider, to note.
samāvarta [act. samāvrt] m. half-turn; re-turn (at loc. ).
samāvartana [act. samāvrt] n. act of returning soc. not. return home of a brahmin having finished his studies with his master and taken his ritual bath |snāna|; the corresponding |saṃskāra| ceremony.
samāvas [samāvas] v. [1] pr. (samāvasati) to dwell | to stop at — ca. (samāvāsayati) pp. (samāvasita) to stop; to settle at.
samāvāsa [act. samāvas] m. residence; camp.
samāvāsita [pp. ca. samāvas] amnf samāvāsitā stayed; established; lodged, settled.
samāvāsitakaṭaka [kaṭaka] amnf samāvāsitakaṭakā who camped.
samāviś [samāviś] v. [6] pr. r. (samāvisate) pp. (samāvista) to approach; to enter, to visit | to penetrate; to fill, to invade; to settle.
samāvṛ [samāvṛ] v. [5] pr. (samāvṛṇoti) pr. r. (samāvṛṇuté) pp. (samāvṛta) completely re cover, hide; impregnate.
samāvrt [samāvrt₁] v. [1] pr. r. (samāvartate) pp. (samāvrtta) to return, to go home | soc. not. to return to one's parents after one's studies with one's guru.
