samāvṛta [pp. samāvṛ] amnf samāvṛtā covered; wrapped, concealed (by (i. iic.)) protected by (i.); filled with (iic.). mohajālasamāvṛta caught in the nets of illusion.
samāvṛtta [pp. samāvṛt] amnf samāvṛttā who has turned around; who has returned; said not. of a brahmin who has completed his studies of brahmacārin — ifc. returned from (iic.).
samāveśa [act. samāviś] m. penetration; invasion; coexistence; cohabitation | gram. co-occurrence; accord — ifc. absorption into, immersion into (iic.).
samāvešana [act. samāviś] n. soc. consummation of marriage.
samāśri [samāśri] v. [1] pr. r. (samāśrayate) pp. (samāśrita) to rely on, to count on, to draw upon, to stick to (acc.) | to practice; to experience, to undergo.
samāśrita [pp. samāśri] ifc. amnf samāśritā which resorts to, which depends on (loc.); which practices | relating to; afflicted with; endowed, provided with (i.).

samāśvas [samāśvas] v. [2] pr. (samāśvasiti) pp. (samāśvasta) to catch one's breath; to regain courage | to have confidence in (loc.) — ca. (samāśvāsayati) to revive; to comfort; to console. samāśvasihi regain courage! | come to your senses!
samāśvasta [pp. samāśvas] amnf samāśvastā revived, comforted, restored; calmed, consoled.
samāśvāsa [act. samāśvas] m. recovery, catching one's breath; relief, ease.
samāśvāsana [act. ca. samāśvas] n. act of bringing help, of reviving; encouragement, consolation.
samāśvāsita [pp. ca. samāśvas] amnf samāśvāsitā revived, brought back to life, restored to shape.
samās [samās₂] v. [2] pr. r. (samāste) pp. (samāsita) to sit together, to be assembled around acc.; to agree with acc. .

samāsa [act. samās] m. meeting, conjunction, combination | gram. compound noun; it can be copulative [dvandva] or determinative [tatpurusa], or possessive and used as an exocentric adjective [bahuvrīhi] or as an adverb in

variable [avyayībhāva]; the codenotative apposition [karmadhāraya] is a special case of tatpuruṣa, and dvigu a special case of karmadhāraya; the first term is called pūrvapada, the second uttarapada; when the first term retains its ending, the compound is called aluk. samāsatas adv. succinctly, in summary. dvandvo dvigurapi cāham madgehe nityama vyayībhāvah | tatpuruṣa karma dhāraya yenāham syām bahuvrīhiḥ | gram. (mnemonic verse of varieties of compound words) I am married, and I have two cows; (yet) at home there is nothing to spend; thus, O servant, work hard so that I may become rich.
samāsagarbhita | garbhita | afmn samāsagarbhitā gram. is said of a compound word containing a compound word as a sub-component (this being said garbhasthasamāsa).
Samāsacakra [cakra] n. lit. np. from the Samāsacakra "Round of compound words", a grammar treatise on the formation of compound words (1901).
Samāsacandrikā [candrikā] f. bed. n.p. from the Samāsacandrikā “Clarification of compound words”, a grammar treatise classifying compound words.
samāsapūrvapada [pūrvapada] n. gram. first term of a compound word; opp. uttarapada.
samāsavigraha [vigraha] m. gram. analysis of a compound word into its constituents.
samāsavṛtti [vṛtti] f. gram. formation of a nominal theme by composition of two words [pāda].
samāsavyāsa [vyāsa] m. gram. compounds and analytical forms.
samāsānta | anta | m. gram. refers to a terminal suffix of a compound word.
samāsokta [ukta] amnf samāsoktā expressed concisely | gram. contained in a compound.
samāsokti [ukti] f. lit. figure of speech of metaphorical parallelism.
samāsad [samāsad] v. [1] pr. (samāsīdati) abs. (samāsadya) to approach, go to, head towards (acc.); to reach, find — ca. (samāsādáyati) to approach, reach; to meet, attack. samāsadya that is near.
samāsīna [ppr. mo. samās] amnf samāsīnā sitting together.
samāsthā [samāsthā₁] v. [1] pr. (samātisthati) pr. r. (samātisthate) pp. (samāsthita) to go up, to go towards; to stop, to stand, to halt | to undertake, to accomplish; to undergo, to assume.
samāsyā [samāsyā] f. session, assembly; colloquium.
samāhan [samāhan] v. [2] pr. (samāhanti) pp. (samāhata) abs. (samāhatya) to strike, to graze; to strike together; to collide with (i.).
samāhartṛ [agt. samāhṛ] amnf samāhartrī soc. governor, royal administrative agent of the region; royal tax collector.
samāhāra [act. samāhṛ] m. combination, assembly, aggregate, gathering; collective value | gram. semantic aggregate; class of linguistic structures grouped collectively.

samāhāradvandva [dvandva] n. gram. compound dvandva copulative collective; it denotes the whole (n. sg.) of its members; opp. itaretaradvandva. hastapādam n. the hand and the foot (sg.). brāhmaṇaśramaṇam n. the orthodox brahmins and the Buddhists/Jains (prototype of dvandva collective of opposites).
samāhāradvigusamāsa [dvigusamāsa] m. gram. compound dvigu collective denoting an aggregate (n. sg.), like tribhuvanam.

samāhita [pp. samādhā] amnf samāhitā attentive, absorbed; given, devoted to arranged, combined, reunited; fixed | raised, dismissed (said of a doubt) | phil. [Udbhaṭa] rhetorical figure of cessation of an emotion without evocation of a new emotion.
samāhū [samāhū] v. [1] pr. (samāhvayati) pp. (samāhūta) to assemble, to summon together — pr. r. (āhvayate) to challenge (in combat or in play).
samāhūta [pp. samāhū] amnf samāhūtā assembled | challenged.
samāhṛ [samāhṛ] v. [1] pr. (samāharati) pp. (samāhṛta) to assemble, to bring together, to combine; to contract | to put back in its place (loc.) | to remove, to take away; to destroy, to annihilate.
samāhṛta |pp. samāhṛ| amnf samāhṛtā gathered, collected gram. assembled, united, ren contré; taken collectively, combined.
samāhva |act. samāhū| m. collective call; challenge.
samāhvaya [act. samāhū] m. challenge; conflict | wager (not. on animal fights); opp. dyūta.
samāhvāna [act. āhū] n. call to arms
blement | challenge | bet (notably on animal fights).
sami [sami] v. [2] pr. (saméti) pp. (samita) pf. (abhi) to gather, to meet, to assemble; to rejoin, to visit (i.).
Samit IIc. Samidh.
samidādhāna [ādhāna] n. soc. arrangement of logs to feed the sacred fire.
samita [pp. sami] amnf samitā reunited, assembled | united with, combined with (i. iic.).
samiti [act. sami] f. meeting, gathering, assembly | var. samit combat, battle.
samitim [acc. samiti] iic.
samitimjaya [jaya] amnf samitimjayā vic torious in combat — m. myth. |Mah.| n.p. of samitimjaya, famous vṛṣṇi warrior.
samiddha [pp. samindh] amnf samiddhā which has been set on fire; lit, ablaze.
samidh [obj. samindh] f. log, bundle, firewood | soc. not. wood to feed the sacred fire.
samindh [samindh] v. [7] pr. r. (saminddhé) pp. (samiddha) to light, to set ablaze — ps. (sa midhyate) to light up, to catch fire.
samī iiv. sama. samīkaraņa | karaņa | n. equalization, leveling; assimilation; bringing up to the level of (i.) | math. algebraic equation.
samīkāra | kāra | m. equation.
samīká [samyac] n. ved. conflict, battle.

samīkṣ [samīkṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (samīkṣate) pp. (samīkṣita) to perceive; to contemplate; to examine, consider, reflect upon, investigate | to discover, to discover; to make a considered choice. mitrasya caksusā samīksāmahe [Yajurveda] We examine with the gaze of friendship.

samīkṣa [act. samīkṣ] n. "complete investigation", epith. of sāṃkhya philosophy — f. samīkṣā investigation; complete inspection; perception; understanding | desire to see; glance opinion (concerning prati), view orchestration; effort explanation of Vedic ritual; not. mīmāṃsā.
samīkṣaṇa [act. samīkṣ] n. complete inspection, thorough investigation; research — amnf samīkṣaṇā that makes one perceive.
samīkṣita [pp. samīkṣ] amnf samīkṣitā perceived; considered; investigated, sought.
samīkṣitavya [pfp. [3] samīkṣ] amnf samīkṣitavyā to investigate.
samīkṣya [pfp. [1] samīkṣ] amnf samīkṣyā to investigate — n. phil. philosophy sāmkhya.
samīcī [f. samyac] f. doe | myth. n.p. of the apsaras samīcī, companion of Vargā.

samīcīná [na] amnf samīcīnā that goes in the same direction, that accompanies; connected; reunited; complete | correct, exact; suitable. samīcīnam interj. very good, exactly! tat samīcīnam bhavati it's good; I approve.

samīpa amnf samīpā near (space, time), neighbor, contiguous, adjacent, imminent | close to, near, in the vicinity of (g. 1ic.); immediately after (iic.) — n. proximity, vicinity, neighborhood; imminence; syn. antika. samīpe adv. near, in the vicinity of. samīpatas adv. in the presence of, near (g. 1ic.) | towards (g.) | immediately. asmatsamīpatas in our presence.
samīpatara |tara| amnf samīpatarā compar. closest.
samīpataravartin | vartin | anfm samīpataravartinī which is the closest; neighbor, adjacent.
samīpamaraṇacihna | maraṇacihna | n. warning signs of death.
samīpasaptamī | saptamī | f. gram. locative of proximity.
samīpastha |stha| amnf samīpasthā located nearby, neighbor.
samīr [samīr] ca. (samīrayati) pp. (samīrita) to set in motion, to send forth; to animate, to create, to accomplish — pft. (sameriré) (3rd pers. pl.) to establish (an act), to institute.
samīra [agt. samīr] m. wind.
samīraṇa [agt. samīr] amnf samīraṇā that stirs, that sets in motion; that stimulates — m. wind; syn. vāyu — n. setting in motion — f. samīranā ifc. wind, breath of (iic.).
samīrita [pp. samīr] amnf samīritā agitated, displaced, overturned, thrown | emitted (sound).
samīh [samīh] v. [1] pr. r. (samīhate) pp. (samīhita) to aspire to, to desire, to seek to obtain; to strive to.
samuc [samuc] v. [4] pr. (samucyati) pp. (sa mucita) to rejoice in, to appreciate the company of (i.).
samucita [pp. samuc] amnf samucitā appreciated; appropriate.

samuccaya [act. samucci] m. aggregate, collection, assembly | gram. conjunction, coordination; accumulation, cumulative value gram. coordination (marked by ca) | lit. figure of rhetoric (association of two different actors in the same action) | phil. |Mīmāṃsā| set of instructions to be executed obligatorily; opp. vikalpa.
samuccayaprāyaścitta [prāyaścitta] n. pl. ved. np. of the Samuccayaprāyaścittāni, collection of expiations for errors of ritual, appendix [parisista] of the Athar vaveda.
samucci [samucci] v. [5] pr. (samuccinoti) pr. r. (samuccinute) pp. (samuccita) to gather, to assemble; to collate, to put in order; to pile up, to accumulate | gram. to join cumulatively.
samuccita [pp. samucci] amnf samuc cita accumulated, collected; put in order.
samuttha [agt. samutthā] ifc. amnf sa mutthā erected, raised, sprung from, produced by (iic.).

samutthā [samutthā] v. [1] pr. (samuttisthati) pr. r. (samuttisthate) pp. (sa mutthita) to rise, to stand up; to get up, to rise again; to appear, to emerge — ca. (samutthāpayati) to cause to rise, to set up, to raise up | to excite, to awaken, to stimulate, to incite.
samutthāna [act. samutthā] n. act of raising it; act of erecting (standard) | healing; care, cure | increase; enlargement, swelling | effort, undertaking, industry.
samutthita [pp. samutthā] amnf sa mutthitā which rises, which stands up, which emerges; pro coming from abl. iic. | ready for loc. .
samutpat [samutpat] v. [1] pr. (samutpa tati) pp. (samutpatita) to fly simultaneously, to dart, to leap; to rise, to ascend | to leave, to disappear.
samutpad [samutpad] v. [4] pr. r. (sa mutpadyate) pp. (samutpanna) to occur (simultanément), to take place; to arise, to emerge, to appear — ca. (samutpādayati) to produce, to cause.
samutpanna [pp. samutpad] amnf sa mutpannā produced, begotten (of mother (loc.), of father (abl.); occurred, arrived.
samutpād [ca. samutpad] v. [10] pr. (sa mutpādayati) pp. (samutpādita) to produce, to cause.
samutpāda [act. samutpād] m. advent, origin, production.
samutsarga [act. samutsṛj] m. evacuation (not. of urine); emission (not. of semen). samutsargam kṛ to have sexual relations with loc. .

samutsrj [samutsrj] v. [6] pr. (samutsrjati) pp. (samutsṛṣṭa) to pour; to throw; to send (arrow) to emit (urine, sperm); to shed (tears); to utter (imprecation, insult) | to abandon; to release; to renounce.
samutsṛp [samutsṛp] v. [1] pr. (utsarpati) to rise together towards; to rise (up to (acc.)); to settle (darkness).
samutsedha [samutsidh] m. height, size; thickness; obesity — f. samutsedhā ifc. height of (iic.).
samudaya [act. samudi] m. union, junction, meeting | combination, connection, assembly, aggregation.
samudācar [samudācar] v. [1] pr. (sa mudācarati) pp. (samudācarita) to treat, to act in verse, to behave towards.
samudācāra [act. samudācar] m. apostrophe, manner of addressing speech | relations with, behavior towards (i.); good practices.

samudāya var. samudaya [act. samudi] m. collection, conglomerate, set; multitude; totality; opp. avayava | thing taken collectively (opp. pratyeka) | bd. set of the constituent elements of existence; by ext., Noble Truth [āryasatya] of the origin of suffering | gram. compound word considered as a single word |pada|.
samudāyaśakti [śakti] f. gram. creative capacity of a compound word, producing a meaning [parārthābhidhāna] from that of its compounds.
samudi [samudi] v. [2] pr. (samudéti) to rise together; to gather.
samudita [pp. saṃvad] amnf samu ditā interlocutor | that which is understood, that which is agreed.
samudīr [samudīr] ca. (samudīrayati) an noncer, to declare.
samudga mn round basket | arch. round temple.
samudgayamaka [yamaka] n. lit. [alaṃkāra] figure of speech of repetition of homophones.
samudgata [pp. samudgam] amnf sa mudgatā repeated — m. lit. [alaṃkāra] variety of ya maka where the first hemistich is repeated in the second.
samudgam [samudgam] v. [1] pr. (samud gacchati) pp. (samudgata) to rise together; to repeat.
samuddiś [samuddiś] v. [1] pr. (sa muddiśati) pp. (samuddiṣṭa) abs. (samuddiśya) indicate completely; declare, communicate designate, name (2 acc.).
samuddiśya [abs. samuddiś] ind. having fully informed | in reference to, on behalf of, in honor of (acc.); according to, verse.
samuddeśa [act. samuddiś] m. complete exposition, precise description; theory, doctrine.
samuddhata [samuddhata] amnf sa muddhatā raised; risen; swollen (waters); violent, intense; imposing | proud, vain, haughty; arrogant — ifc. abundant in, overflowing with, full of (iic.).
samuddhāra [act. samuddhṛ] m. act of withdrawing, removing, annihilating; rescue discernment, choice, selection; deduction; redemption.
samuddhāralāngūla [lāngūla] m. organic. animal with raised tail.
samuddhū [samuddhū] v. [5] pr. (samuddhu noti) pp. (samuddhūta) to shake, stir, agitate.
samuddhṛ [samuddhṛ] v. [1] pr. (samuddha rati) pp. (samuddhrta) to pull, extract, extirpate; to snatch | to snatch from danger; to save, deliver; to raise up, straighten.

samuddhṛta [pp. samuddhṛ] amnf samuddhṛtā erected, drawn; extracted, extirpated; taken, deduced | saved, delivered; raised up. sadasajjñānasamudrāt samuddhṛtam de vatāprasādena | sajjñānottamaratnam mayā nimagnam svamatināvā | [Aryabhaṭa] From the ocean of true and false knowledge, by divine grace, I extracted the supreme jewel of exact knowledge which is submerged therein, thanks to the vessel of my own judgment.
samudbhava [act. samudbhū] m. production, origin, birth; resurrection — ifc. coming from, having as its origin (iic.) | source of — f. sa mudbhavā ifc. id.
samudbhū [samudbhū] v. [1] pr. (samudbha vati) pp. (samudbhūta) to arise from; to be born from, to originate from | to increase, to grow.
samudbhūta [pp. samudbhū] amnf sa mudbhūtā born, produced, derived | existing.
samudyata [pp. samudyam] amnf sa mudyatā raised, lifted up | ready to (inf. dat.); engaged in, busy with (loc.).
samudyam [samudyam] v. [1] pr. (samu dyaccati) pp. (samudyata) to lift.
samudyama [act. samudyam] m. act of raising | great effort; zeal, preparation for (loc. dat. iic.
samudyamin [agt. samudyam] amnf samudyaminī committed, striving; zealous.
samudyoga [samudyoga] m. complete preparation; the act of putting oneself to (g.) | employment, use. samudyogam kār to undertake (g.) against (acc.).

samudrá₁ [samudra] m. sea, ocean | phil. [ChU.] np. of Samudra, the Ocean personified as a quarter [kalā] of Brahman | myth. [VP.] celestial ocean; there are seven of them, concentric: lavana the ocean of salt water, ikṣu the ocean of syrup, surā the ocean of wine, ghṛta the ocean of clarified butter, dadhi the ocean of yogurt, dugdha the ocean of milk, and jala, the ocean of fresh water; other sources mention 4 main oceans | math. symb. the number 4 — n. math. one hundred billion — f. samudrā ifc. ocean of (iic.) — v. [11] pr. (samudrāyati) to become ocean — v. [11] pr. r. (samudrāyate) to be like the ocean | pali samudda.

samudrágupta | gupta | m. hist. np. of the king samu dragupta, son of Candragupta₁; he reigned from 335 to 375; his empire extended over the whole valley of the Ganges, and he even subdued part of the Deccan; he celebrated an aśvamedha; his eldest son Rāmagupta succeeded him, then his younger son Candragupta₂ Vikramāditya seized the throne; he was a poet, and patronized poets like his minister Harisena; Kālidāsa was inspired by his exploits to write the Raghuvamśa; cf. Candramā.
samudrágrha [grha] n. pool.
samudráculuka [culuka] m. myth. epith. of the sage Agastya "who made short work of the ocean".
samudrátīra [tīra] n. seaside, shore; beach.
samudrámathana [mathana] n. myth. churning of the ocean (of milk); cf. kṣīrodamathana.

samudráyāna [yāna] n. transport by sea; ship. samudrasamgama var. samudrasangama [saṃgama] m. lit. np. of the Samudrasaṅgama "Meeting of two oceans", translation into Sanskrit of the Majma'alBahrain in Persian by Dārā Shikoh; it explains the compatibility of the Sufi traditions of Islam with the Vedānta of the esoteric lessons | upanisad |.
samudrasetu [setu] m. myth. [Rām.] bridge built by monkeys between India and Lankā to allow the army of Rāma to pass.

samudrayānagamana [gamana] n. travel by sea. samudrayānagamanadosamīmāmsā [doṣa₂mīmāṃsā] f. lit. np. of the samu drayānadoṣamīmāṃsā, ritual treatise on the sin of traveling abroad, of the paṇḍita Bhaṭṭācārya Tārānātha Tarkavācaspati (1870, Calcutta).
samudrasena [sena] m. bed. [Mah.] np. of king Sa mudrasena.
samudrāyana [ayana] n. travel by sea.
samudra₂ [sa₁mudrā] amnf samudrā tam ponné, sealed, marked.
samudvīkṣ [samudvīkṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (sa mudvīkṣate) pp. (samudvīkṣita) to look around, to consider, to observe.
samunnata [pp. samunnam] amnf sa munnatā raised, erect, high, prominent.
samunnati [act. samunnam] f. elevation, height; high position. manasah samunnati lofty thought. cittam samunnatim asnute The mind takes on a higher plane.
samunnaddha [pp. samunnah] amnf samunnaddhā unleashed, excessive; arrogant, or rebellious.
samunnam [samunnam] v. [1] pr. (samun namati) pp. (samunnata) to rise — ca. (samunna mayati) to raise, to raise, to erect, to erect.
samunnah [samunnah] v. [4] pr. (samunna hyati) pr. r. (samunnahyate) pp. (samunnaddha) to free oneself, to rise.
samunmīl [samunmīl] v. [1] pr. (sa munmīlati) pp. (samunmīlita) to manifest, to flourish — ca. (samunmīlayati) to open (eyes); to manifest, to unfold.
samupagata [pp. samupagam] amnf samupagatā occurred; suffered.
samupagam [samupagam] v. [1] pr. (samu pagacchati) pp. (samupagata) to go together towards, to resort to | to fall into, to undergo. hastābhyām samupagam to fall into the hands of.
samupaviś [samupaviś] v. [6] pr. (samu paviśati) pp. (samupaviṣṭa) to sit with or next to, to sit on (loc. upari g.) | to lie down on — ca. (samupaveśayati) to make sit.
samupaviṣṭa [pp. samupaviś] amnf samupavistā sitting.
samupavṛt [samupavṛt] v. [1] pr. r. (samu pavartate) pp. (samupavrtta) to behave, to behave like (acc.).
samupasr [samupasr] v. [1] pr. (samupasa rati) pp. (samupasṛta) to go towards, to approach acc. .
samupasthā [samupasthā] v. [1] pr. (samupatisthati) pr. r. (samupatisthate) pp. (sa mupasthita) to stand beside, to be in the service of; to rely on (acc.) | to be found, to arrive; to plague.
samupasthita [pp. samupasthā] amnf samupasthitā approached, arrived; gathered | opportune, seasonal; occurred; obtained, acquired.
samupāgata [pp. samupāgam] amnf samupāgatā occurred, happened; suffered, incurred. sa brahmaśāpo niyatam adya mām samupāgatah |Rām.| The curse of the brahmin falls upon me today.
samupāgam [samupāgam] v. [1] pr. (sa mupāgacchati) pp. (samupāgata) to go together towards; to approach, to meet; to resort to | to fall into, to undergo.
samupārj [samupārj] v. [1] pr. (sa mupārjati) pp. (upārjita) ca. (samupārjayati) acquire together.
samupārjita [pp. samupārj] amnf samupārjitā acquired together, brought together.
samupāś [samupāś] v. [5] pr. (sa mupāśnóti) pr. r. (samupāśnuté) to obtain, acquire, receive.
samupāśri [samupāśri] pp. (samupāśrita) to rely on, to depend on | to seek refuge in, to surrender to.
samupāśrita [pp. samupāśri] amnf samupāśritā who relies on, who has recourse to, who takes refuge in (acc.).
samupe [samupe₁] v. [2] pr. (samupéti) pp. (samupeta) to gather, to meet; to go towards, to approach sexually (acc.) | to occur, to happen.
samupeta [pp. samupe] amnf samupetā reunited; arrived | accompanied by, provided with, furnished with, rich in (i. iic.).

saṃbodhiprāpti [prāpti] f. bd. attainment of Enlightenment by Buddha in Gayā.
sambodhya var. sambodhya [pfp. [1] sambudh] amnf sambodhyā to understand.
saṃbhará var. Sambhara [agt. saṃbhṛ] amnf saṃbharā gatherer; that which supports, that which acc cord — m. geo. np. of the salt lake Sambhara, in Rājasthāna.
sambharabhava [bhava] n. salt “from Lake Sambhara”.

saṃbhavá var. sambhava [agt. saṃbhū] m. origin, birth, source; cause, reason for existence; possibility, eventuality; alternative phil. equivalence — f. sambhavā ifc. origin of, cause of (iic.). sambhave adv. as much as possible. sambhavatah adv. probably.
sambhavanātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of sam bhavanātha "Causal Master", 3ᵉ tīrthankara mythique; his symbol is a horse.

saṃbhārá var. sambhāra [act. saṃbhṛ] m. collection; preparation, equipment | provision; necessary material, ingredient | completeness; mul titude, number, quantity; excess | wealth; support, food | bd. quality necessary for liberation; not. punyasambhāra meritorious acts, jñānasaṃbhāra knowledge, śamathasaṃbhāra tranquility, and vidarśanasaṃbhāra foresight — f. sambhārā id.
saṃbhāv var. sambhāv [ca. saṃbhū] v. [10] pr. (saṃbhāvayati) pfp. (saṃbhāvya) to produce, ef

to perform | to honor, to esteem | to suppose, to admit; at to attribute to loc. g. ; to consider as 2 acc. . sarvam sambhāvyate anything can happen. mānyathā saṃbhāvaya do not misunderstand. pāpakarma tasya saṃbhāvyate a bad deed is attributed to him.

saṃbhāvana var. sambhāvana |agt. sambhū] amnf sambhāvanā ifc. who has a high opinion of — act. nf saṃbhāvanā rap proximity, assembly; encounter (with g.) honor, respect, esteem; high opinion of (loc.) imagination, supposition, hypothesis; possibility gram. subjunctive mood, rendered notably by the potential/optative; cf. Lin. ātmani saṃbhāvana high opinion of oneself. sambhāvanam bhaj to make a hypothesis. sambhāvanāyām lṛṭ gram. hypothetical future.

saṃbhāvanapūrvapada [pūrvapada] n. gram. refers to a compound word of the karmadhāraya type in which the first component is a specific species and the second a universal genus, such as amravṛkṣaḥ or ayodhyānagarī .
saṃbhāvanīya [pfp. [2] ca. saṃbhū] amnf saṃbhāvanīyā in which one must participate; which must be honored or respected | possible; probable.

sambhāvita [pp. ca. sambhū] amnf sambhāvitā gathered; grasped, understood | esteemed, respected, honored | considered; conjectured | adapted, adequate; possible, probable — n. conjecture, supposition, hypothesis.
sambhāvya var. sambhāvya [pfp. [1] ca. sambhū] amnf sambhāvyā to suppose; which can be admitted; possible.

saṃbhāṣ var. sambhāṣ [sambhāṣ] v. [1] pr. r. (sambhāṣate) pp. (sambhāṣita) to greet, address (acc.); to join the conversation | discuss with (i.); to speak, say, recite | persuade; prevail. sambhāṣamāṇah priyah haiva bhavati one is appreciated by a fine speech.
saṃbhāṣa var. sambhāṣa act. saṃbhāṣ m. conversation — f. sambhāṣā id. cf. tadvidya, vigrhya, saṃdhāya.
saṃbhāṣaṇa [act. saṃbhāṣ] n. conversation (with (i. iic.)).
sambhid var. sambhid [sambhid₁] v. [7] pr. (sambhinatti) pr. r. (sambhintte) pp. (sambhinna) to break into pieces, destroy | combine, mix; to associate with (acc.).
saṃbhinna var. sambhinna [pp. saṃbhid] amnf saṃbhinnā completely destroyed; inter broken, abandoned | joined, combined, mixed — ifc. brought into contact with (iic.).
saṃbhinnapralāpa | pralāpa | m. vain chatter; bd. it is one of the 10 sins.
saṃbhu var. sambhu [saṃbhū] m. phil. the Being manifesting; it emits the bindu Which becomes śakti then om | myth. np. of sambhu, the peaceful aspect of Shiva — ifc. produced by, from (iic.).
saṃbhuj var. sambhuj [sambhuj₂] v. [7] pr. r. (sambhunkté) v. [7] pr. (sambhunakti) pp. (smb hukta) to have a meal together.

saṃbhū var. sambhū [sambhū₁] v. [1] pr. (saṃbhavati) pp. (saṃbhūta) to meet, unite, combine | to become, arise from; to occur, manifest; to develop, exist, be — ca. (saṃbhāvayati) cf. saṃbhāv. samabhhut there was. vikramāditya rājye Puramdarapurī nāma na garī samabhūt [VC.] There was a city called Puramdarapurī in the kingdom of Vikramāditya.
saṃbhūta var. sambhūta [pp. saṃbhū] amnf saṃbhūtā uni ou combined avec | product, derived from ; compound of (abl. iic.).
saṃbhūti var. sambhūti [act. saṃbhū] f. origin, birth, manifestation | phil. the Divine Manifestation.
saṃbhṛ var. sambhṛ [sambhṛ] v. [3] pr. (saṃbibharti) v. [1] pr. (saṃbhárati) pr. r. (sambharate) pp. (sambhrta) to gather, amass; to prepare (not. the sacrifice); to equip.
sambhṛta var. sambhṛta [pp. saṃbhṛ] amnf sambhrtā gathered, assembled; provided, equipped; prepared, composed | imaginary.

sambheda var. sambheda [act. sambhid] m. destruction | dislocation; fall | division, separation, dissension (friends, allies) | junction, mixture | confluence (rivers); estuary — ifc. contact with (iic.).
sambhoga var. sambhoga [sambhoga₂] m. pleasure, passion, mutual enjoyment; sexual pleasure.
sambhogakāya [kāya] m. bd. the "body of bliss", symbolizing the form of Being present in the state of meditation.
sambhogaśringāra [śringāra] m. phil. [aesthetics] artistic mode [rasa] of consummated eroticism.
saṃbhram var. sambhram [sambhram] v. [1] pr. (saṃbhramati) v. [4] pr. (saṃbhrāmyati) pp. (sambhrānta) to be confused, perplexed, agitated, excited; to be moved, to become troubled.
saṃbhrama var. sambhrama [act. saṃbhram] excitement, eagerness, haste; m. emotion, disturbance, dread; misunderstanding | that which frightens. alamalam sambhramena enough emotions!
saṃbhrānta var. sambhrānta pp. sambhram] amnf sambhrāntā confused, perplexed, agitated, excited; troubled, moved, startled.

sammata var. sammata [pp. samman] amnf sammatā consented, agreed; of the same opinion; authorized (by (g. iic.)) | esteemed, appreciated; celebrated | considered as (nom.) — ifc. in agreement with, with the approval of (iic.) — n. opinion, impression; consent, authorization. sammate with the consent of, according to the opinion of g. . sammatena according to the opinion of g. . bahupustakasammata lit. (text) based on numerous manuscripts. śāstrasammatasāhitya lit. literature in agreement with scholarly texts.
sammati var. sammati [act. samman] f. accord, approval, agreement, harmony | opinion, point of view | homage; desire; affection; command. maunam sammatilakṣaṇam Silence gives consent.
saṃmada var. sammada [sammada] m. great joy, happiness.

saṃman var. samman [samman] v. [4] pr. (sammanyati) pp. (sammata) to honor, respect; to appreciate, esteem | to approve, consent, authorize — ca. (saṃmānayati) to honor, treat with respect; to bestow (i.). sammānanīyāh adr. respectful greetings.
sammantr var. sammantr [sammantr] v. [10] pr. (sammantrayati) pp. (sammantrita) se consul ter; to take advice from (i.) | to deliberate; to advise; to express an opinion | to greet; to welcome.
saṃmantraṇīya var. sammantraṇīya [pfp. [2] sammantr] amnf sammantraṇīyā to consult | which one must greet.
sammantrita var. sammantrita pp. sammantr] amnf sammantritā deliberate; considered.
sammarda var. sammarda [act. sammrd] m. friction; the act of pressing together; crushing; trampling | surging (waves) | encounter (armies); battle.

sammā₂ var. sammā₂ [sammā₁] v. [3] pr. r. (saṃmimīte) v. [2] pr. (saṃmāti) pp. (saṃmita) to measure; to compare with (i.); to equalize; to distribute to be of the same capacity; to be contained in (loc.) — ps. (sammīyate) to be of the same capacity; to be contained in (loc.).
saṃmā₂ var. saṃmā₂ [act. saṃmā₁] f. equality in number or size; symmetry.
saṃmān var. sammān [ca. saṃman] v. [10] pr. (saṃmānayati) to honor, to treat with respect; to reward with i. .
saṃmāna var. sammāna [act. saṃmān] m. respect, homage | pl. saṃmānās honors. sarasvatī sammāna mod. Indian literary prize.
saṃmānya var. sammānya [pfp. [1] saṃmān] amnf saṃmānyā (address) very honorable; res pecté.
saṃmārjana var. sammārjana [act. saṃmṛj] n. cleaning; purification | soc. cleaning and preparation of idols — f. saṃmārjanī broth-based meal [sūpa] to cleanse the stomach | mod. broom.

sammita var. sammita [pp. sammā₂] amnf saṃmitā measured; which measures exactly | of the same measure, of the same number | corresponding to, resembling, passing for (ig iic.) intended for (iic.) | symmetrical — n. distance. sammite adv. at a distance of (iic.).

saṃmiti var. sammiti [act. saṃmā₁] f. equalization; comparison. saṃmitīya var. sammitīya [īya] m. pl. bd. n.p. of the Sammitīyās school, which admits the theory of the permanence of the pudgala individual.

saṃmukhá var. sammukha [sammukha] amnf saṃmukhī face to face; opposite (g. iic.) | ready to begin; at the start of (iic.) | favorable to (g. iic.) | suited to the circumstances, adequate. sammukham adv. toward, near; opposite; face to face in the presence of g. . sammukhe adv. opposite; opposite, face to face | in the presence of, at the start of (g. iic.). sammukhīkr to stand opposite; to face; to aim for. sammukhībhū to be face to face; to confront.
saṃmugdha var. sammugdha [pp. saṃmuh] amnf saṃmugdhā lost; stunned.
saṃmud var. sammud [sammud₂] f. joy.
saṃmuh var. sammuh [sammuh] v. [4] pr. (saṃmúhyati) pp. (saṃmugdha, saṃmūḍha) to be stunned; to be confused, to be bewildered; to be unconscious — ca. (saṃmohayati) pp. (saṃmohita) to mislead.
saṃmūḍha var. sammūḍha [pp. saṃmuh] amnf saṃmūḍhā stunned; astonished; unconscious — f. sammūdhā enigma.
saṃmūḍhatva [tva] n. stupefaction.

saṃmūrch var. sammūrch [sammūrch] v. [1] pr. (sammūrchati) pp. (sammūrchita) to solidify, harden, thicken; to coagulate | to strengthen; to grow, to increase; to become powerful | to become stupid; to lose consciousness — ca. (sammūrchayati) to cause to form into a mass; to take shape. sammürchat var. sammürchat increasing the effect, magnifying.
saṃmūrchita var. sammūrchita pp. sammūrch] amnf sammūrchitā coagulated; frozen; thickened; intensified | stunned; fainted, unconscious.
saṃmṛj var. sammṛj [sammṛj] v. [2] pr. (saṃmāṛṣṭi) pp. (saṃmṛṣṭa) to clean.
saṃmṛta var. sammṛta [sammṛta] amnf sammṛtā completely dead.
saṃmṛd var. sammṛd [sammṛd₁] v. [9] pr. (sammṛdnāti) v. [1] pr. (sammardati) to press together; to grind, to reduce to powder — ca. (sammar dayati) to press, to crush | to rub, to clean.
saṃmṛṣṭa var. sammṛṣṭa [pp. saṃmṛj] amnf sammṛṣṭā cleansed.
saṃmelana var. sammelana [sammelana] m. meeting, gathering | soc. not. symposium of scholars [pandita].
sammoda var. sammoda [act. sammud] m. joy | scent. sammodika var. sammodika [ika] m. friend, old friend.
saṃmodana var. sammodana [agt. saṃmud] amnf sammodanī friendly; kind.

sammoha var. sammoha [act. sammuh] m. stupefaction; confusion, bewilderment; illusion, ignorance, madness. krodhād bhavati sammohāh sammohāt smrtivibhramah smrtibhramád buddhināáo buddhināśāt praṇaśyati | [BhG.] From anger comes error, from error the loss of memory, from the loss of memory the ruin of reason, from the ruin of reason one perishes.
sammohaka var. sammohaka [agt. ca. saṃmuh] amnf saṃmohikā stupefying; bewitching, fascinating.
sammohana var. sammohana [act. ca. sammuh] n. confusion, bewilderment; fascination; enchantment — agt. amnf sammohanī stupefying; fascinating — m. myth. np. of an arrow of Kāmadeva.
sammohita var. sammohita [pp. ca. saṃmuh] amnf saṃmohitā bewildered; stunned; fascinated.

samyak [n. samyac] adv. together, so simultaneously, at the same time | well, suitably, properly, wisely, as is appropriate | justly, correctly, exactly; completely, truly, absolutely. samyan na adv. absolutely not.
samyakkarmānta [karmānta] m. bd. the right course, one of the 8 steps of the path of abolition of suffering [aṣṭāṅgamārga].
samyakcāritra [cāritra] n. jn. correct behavior; it is one of the three Jain treasures [ratnatraya].
samyaktā [tā] f. moral rectitude, uprightness, ethical behavior.
samyaktva [tva] n. correctness, accuracy; perfection jn. behavior in accordance with Jain ethics.

samyakprayoga [prayoga] m. proper use; suitable practice; correct procedure. samyakprayogena adv. by the proper means. samyaksamkalpa var. samyaksankalpa [samkalpa] m. good intention | bd. right intention, one of the 8 steps on the path of abolishing suffering [astāṅgamārga].
samyaksamkalpaja [ja] afmn samyaksamkalpajā phil. which comes from a good intention.
samyaksamādhi [samādhi] f. bd. correct meditation, one of the 8 steps on the path of abolishing suffering [aṣṭāṅgamārga].
samyaksmrti |smrti| f. bd. Right attention, one of the 8 steps on the path to the abolition of suffering |aṣṭāṅgamārga|.
samyagājīva |ājīva| m. bd. the right way of existence, one of the 8 stages of the path to the abolition of suffering | aṣṭāṅgamārga |.
samyagjñāna [jñāna] n. phil. right knowledge; it is one of the three Jain treasures |ratnatraya|.
samyagdarśana [darśana] n. phil. [Nyāya] true knowledge of reality | jn. correct point of view; it is one of the three Jain treasures | ratnatraya |.
samyagdṛṣṭi |dṛṣṭi| f. bd. the right understanding, one of the 8 steps on the path to the abolition of suffering france | astāngamārga |.
samyagvāc |vāc| f. bd. right speech, one of the 8 steps on the path to the abolition of suffering [astāngamārga].
samyagvidya [vidyā] amnf samyagvidyā phil. who has perfect knowledge.
samyagvyāyāma [vyāyāma] m. bd. the correct effort, one of the 8 steps on the path to the abolition of suffering
samyac var. samyañc [samac] amnf
samīcī [m. nom. samyan; n. nom. samyak] turned in the same direction, convergent, united; correct, conforming — m. companion — f. samīcī praise.

samrāj [agt. saṃrāj] m. [nom. samrāt] sovereign, absolute monarch, emperor | myth. ved. universal sovereignty of Mitra and Varuna; opp. svarāj of Indra | hist. np. of the mathematician Samrāt Jagannātha₄; he lived in Amber at the court of King Jayasimha₆; he is credited with the Rekhāganita, a translation of Euclid's Elements from Arabic to Sanskrit | astr. np. of the Samrāt Yantra, sundial of the Yantra mandira of Jayapura, established by King Jayasimha₆ in 1728; the largest sundial in the world, it has an accuracy of 15 s.
samrādāsandī [āsandī] f. soc. ["imperial throne"] ta bouret tresse portant les plats de l’pravargya dans les rites véd. solemn rites.
sayatna [sa₁yatna] amnf sayatnā who makes an effort; zealous; who strives to (inf.). sayatnam adv. by making an effort, by applying oneself.
sayúj [sa₁yuj₂] amnf united with — m. companion, comrade.
sayujya [sa₁yujya] amnf sayujyā very close, intimate; united with.
sayujyatā [tā] f. privacy; union.
sayoga [sa₁yoga] amnf sayogā who has tinted yoga — n. jn. penultimate step towards emancipation.
sayogakevalin [kevalin] amnf sayogakevalinī jn. to be accomplished [arhat], in a state of active omniscience, at the 13th stage of spiritual development [gunasthāna]; opp. ayogakevalin.
sará [agt. sṛ] amnf sarā fluid, liquid; purgative, laxative — f. sarī ifc. that goes to (iic.), that moves — act. m. movement, gushing | rope; cord (of a necklace) | cascade.
saraka |agt. sr| amnf sarikā that moves, that crawls, that slides, that flows — ins. mn goblet | alcohol, rum; action of drinking (an alcoholic beverage).
saraghā f. bee.
saraṅga [sa₁raṅga] amnf saraṅgā colorful.
sarajasa |sa₁rajas| amnf sarajasā dusty; dirty. sarajasam adv. ["even with the dust"] in totality, down to the last drop.
sarața m. lizard; chameleon | var. sarațu id. bhattasya karane saratah pravistah A lizard entered the master's ear (false pretext of a teacher's lady to test the intelligence of his students).
saraṇa |act. sr | n. course, movement Rapid; pursuit.
saraṇi [sṛani] f. path, way, road | straight line.

saraṇyú [related to saraṇa] amnf Swift, swift, agile — m. storm cloud — f. Saraṇyū myth. [RV.] np. of Saranyū "Swift", daughter of tvaștā, wife of the Sun Vivasvān; exhausted by her ardor, she fashioned a woman in her own image [Savarṇā] and transformed herself into a mare; Vivasvān followed her and they gave birth to the Aśvinau and Revanta; cf. Sañjñā.
saratna |sa₁ratna| amnf saratha with a precious stone.
saratha |sa₁ratha| m. chariot companion.

sarámā [sarama] f. myth. np. of Saramā "Swift", Indra's dog; she is the mother of Syāma and Ŝabala, Yama's hellhounds; [RV.] she discovered on an island in the celestial river Rasā the cave Vala where the Sun was hidden, thus allowing its return at the winter solstice | paritakmyā|; [Mah.] she cursed Janamejaya for having driven away one of her young during a sacrifice; she steals fetuses from her hands; she is associated with the karañja tree, which is honored by women desiring a son.

saráyu [sṛyu] m. air, wind — f. geo. n.p. of the Sarayu, Kosala river flowing to Ayodhyā, tributary (or downstream section) of the GhargharaGogra (mod. Surjū), tributary of the Gangā | var. sarayū geo. n.p. of the sarayū (later id.).

Sarala [sarala| amnf saralā [“who runs him” | right; direct, frank; spontaneous | (morally) honest, upright, loyal, sincere; just, correct; to the thentic — m. organic. bot. Cedrus deodara, deodar cedar; syn. devadāru | hist. n.p. of Sarala, an Oriya poet of the 15th century; he wrote (in Oriya) the Sārala Mahābhārata — n. organic. pine resin.
saraśana |sa₁raśanā| amnf saraśanā who wears a belt.
sáRas [abstr. sṛ] n. water | lake, pond, reservoir.

Sarasvat₁₁ |vat| amnf sarasvatī like a lake; forming ponds | elegant; sentimental; delighting in (loc.) — m. river, sea | myth. np. of Sa rasvān, guardian god of waters and fertility — f. cf. sarasvatī.

sarasa |sa₁rasa| amnf sarasā full of sap, juicy, moist; tonic; vigorous, powerful fresh, new; succulent, tasty; charming, graceful, elegant | passionate, amorous, full of desire — ifc. having the taste of (iic.). sarasam adv. passionately.
sarasatā [tā] f. state of being full of sap; vigor.
sarasatva [vat] n. id. | freshness.
sarasi [loc. saras] iic.
sarasija [ja] amnf sarasijā produced by a lake or pond; not. fish — n. lotus; syn. saroja.

sarasvatī [f. Sarasvat₁₁] f. myth. np. of Sa rasvatī "Gracious", wife śakti of Brahmā and goddess of wisdom, sacred speech and knowledge; she is represented dressed in white and playing the vīṇā, and holding a book or a sword symbolizing knowledge; her mount is the swan [haṃsa]; she is sometimes said to be the daughter of Shiva; she is celebrated at the śrīpañcamī/vasantapañcamī festival: cf. Irā, Kuṭilā, Go, Vāk, Vāṇī, Sāradā, Brāhmī | geo. np. of the sarasvatī₁ river "which forms numerous lakes", formerly a tributary of the Indus [Sindhu] or parallel river flowing into the Kutch marsh; it is thought to subsist like the Sarsutī and the monsoon river Ghaggar which disappear into the sands of Rājasthāna; myth. it is a celestial river [divyagangā]; cf. Brahmanadī — m. saras vatī soc. sarasvatī₂ title of renunciant of one of the 10 temples founded by Śańkara₁; cf. Dayānanda₁, Brahmānanda, Madhusūdana₁, Satyānanda | soc. expiation ceremony for a speech error during a ritual. sarasvatīvandanam soc. homage to sarasvatī, pronounced during the inauguration ceremonies of places of knowledge or education.

sarasvatīkanthābharana | kanthābharana | n. lit. np. of the Sarasvatīkaņṭhābharaṇa₁ "Necklace of saras vatī", treatise on poetic style [alaṃkāra] by King Bhojadeva | lit. np. of the Sarasvatīkanthābharana₂, Sanskrit grammar by the same king; it was intended to supplant the Astādhyāyī; it influenced Hemacandra's Siddhahemaśabdānuśāsana. sarasvatīkaņṭhābharaṇaprāsāda | prāsāda | m. hist. palace of King Bhojadeva.
sarasvatīvilāsa |vilāsa| mr. bed. n.p. from saras vatīvilāsa “Entertainment of Sarasvatī”, precise from
Pratāparudradeva's right [smrti]; it has two sections, the Vyavahārakānda and the Acārakānda. sarasvatīvīņā [vīṇā] f. South Indian lute [vīṇā].

Saraha m. hist. np. of the perfective [mahāsiddha] Saraha or Sarahapā; brahmin born Rāhula₁ in the 8th century in Sarolī near the city of Rājī in East India, he studied Buddhism in Nālandā; he is considered the first sahajīya, and one of the creators of Vajrayāna; he was a wandering yogi , of free morals [avadhūta], it is said that he frequented succubi [dākinī]; a collection of mystical poems and chants is attributed to him; he is represented holding the arrow of nonduality.
sarāga |sa₁rāga| amnf sarāgā colorful;
blushed | kind, pleasant | passionate; in love. sarāgam adv. with love; passionately.
sarāgatā [tā] f. passion; love.
sarāgatva [tva] n. id.
sarāghava [sa₁rāghava] amnf sarāghavā myth. accompanied by rāghavās (said from Viśvāmitra).
sarājaka [sa₁rājaka] amnf sarājikā ac accompanied by the king, with the king.
sarit [sṛit] f. river, stream; spring. saritām varā ["The best of rivers"] the Ganges.
sarudita [sa₁rudita] amnf saruditā san glant. saruditam adv. with blood.
saruṣ [sa₁ruṣ₂] amnf saruṣā furious.
sarūpa [sa₁rūpa] amnf sarūpā of the same form, like, similar to, in the image of (g. iic.) in the graceful form, beautiful.
saro iic. saras.
saroja | ja | amnf sarojā produced by a lake or pond — n. lotus.
saroruh |ruh₂| n. |"that grows in a lake" | lotus var. saroruha id.
sarovara | vara₂ | n. large pond (deep enough for lotus), lake.
saroga [sa₁roga] amnf sarogā sick.
sarogatā [tā] f. state of illness.
saroṣa [sa₁roṣa] amnf saroṣā irritated. saroşam adv. angrily.

sárga [act. srj₁] m. emission, creation, emanation, production; creature, offspring the world | phil. cycle of creation of the world; cf. prākṛtasarga, pratisarga; pañcalakṣaṇa | phil. [Sāmkhya] the natural evolution of matter; cf. tattva | book, chapter, section | nature, disposition; effort, will — f. sargā ifc. id. sarge adv. herebas.

sargabandha [bandha] m. lit. division of a mahākāvya into thematic sections. sargabandho mahākāvyam mahatām ca mahac ca yat [Bhāmaha] The composition in songs Is called great poetry because it Is ample, and deals with lofty subjects.
sarp [ca. sṛp] v. [10] pr. (sarpayati) pp. (sarpita) to make crawl.

sarpá [agt. sṛp] amnf sarpī that crawls — m. serpent | myth. np. of Sarpa "serpent", one of the 11 divine breaths [marut] | pl. sarpās myth. category of mythical beings; astr. they preside over the nakshatra Aśleṣās (Hydra) | math. symb. the number 8 | fr. serpent. na hi godhā sarpantī sarpaṇādahirbhavati (maxim) A lizard that crawls does not thereby become a serpent.
sarpagandhā [gandha] f. bio. bot. Rauvolvia ser pentina, apocynaceae shrub with small red flowers and black berries; its roots are used in medicine; syn. candrikā.
sarpadevajana [devajana] m. myth. the race of gods and serpents.
sarpadevajanavidyā [vidyā] f. phil. the science of divine beings, a literary genre.
sarpapankti [pankti] f. knot of (more or less 5) snakes.
sarpabandha [bandha] m. lit. ["ser pentin diagram"] serpent sculpture in the Mahākāleśvara temple in Ujjayinī, which illustrates the inflectional morphology of Sanskrit.
sarpabali [bali] m. soc. snake sacrifice.
sarpamauli [mauli] m. style of representation of Shiva's hair with snakes.

sarpavara [vara₂] n. geo. n.p. from sarpavara, a sacred place near Kākināda in the Godāvarī delta; his temple Bhāvanārāyaṇa Svāmi Is said to be built at the place of the sarpasattra sacrifice of Ja namejaya.
sarpavivara [vivara] mn snake hole.
sarpásiras [siras] m. ritual gesture [mudrā] of the snake's head (fingers curved in the shape of a cobra's hood).
sarpasattra [sattra] n. myth. [Mah.] great sacrifice of snakes, carried out by the emperor Janamejaya to avenge his father Parīkṣit; it was interrupted by Astika.
sarpasattrin |in| amnf sarpasattrinī myth. [Mah.] np. of Sarpasattrī, epith. by Janamejaya "Who celebrated the sacrifice of the serpents".
sarpana [act. srp] n. action of crawling, of escaping | soc. ved. procession where the officiants throw the prastara into the air.
sarpita [pp. ca. sṛp] amnf sarpitā de na ture serpentine; ophidian — n. snake bite.
sarpin [agt. sṛp] amnf sarpiṇī Who crawls.
sarpis [abstr. srp] n. clarified butter; fat.
sarpiḥkuṇḍikā [kuṇḍikā] f. jar of clarified butter.
sarpirmadhu [madhu] n. du. sarpirmadhuni butter and honey.
sarpiṣka |ka| f. sarpiṣkā ifc. Who has the butter (iic.).

sárva pn. mnf sarvā all; whole, universal — m. myth. epith. of Shiva "That which permeates all" | gr. ολος; lat. sollus. sarvam adv. completely. sarve'pi all together. sarvah ko'pi all without exception. te sarve them all. gavām sarvam all that which comes from the cow. sarveṣāṃsvastirbhavatu sarveṣāṃśāntirbhavatu sarveṣāmpūrṇambhavatu sarveṣāmmaṅgalambhavatu Good luck to all, peace to all, abundance to all, happiness to all.

sarvakarman [karman] amnf sarvakarmanī Who performs all the acts — m. myth. np. of King Sar vakarmā, descendant of Kalmāṣapāda; Parāśara saved him from the extermination of the kṣatriyās by Paraśurāma — n. pl. all kinds of work.
sarvakarmaphalatyāga [karmaphalatyāga] m. phil. ["renunciation of all fruit of action"] disinterestedness.
sarvakarmaphalatyāgin [in] amnf sarvakar
maphalatyāginī ["Who renounces all fruit of his actions" selfless; Who acts without interest.
sarvakāma [kāma] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā sarvakāma "Who wants everything", son of Rtuparna, father of Sudāsa₁.
sárvakratu | kratu | m. pl. soc. sacrifices of all kinds.
sárvaga [ga₁] amnf sarvagā omnipresent; im manent — n. phil. qualifies the brahman.
sárvagata [gata] amnf sarvagatā omnipresent; immanent; That which pervades everything — n. everything that moves.
sárvagatatva |tva| n. omnipresence.
sárvagāmin [gāmin] amnf sarvagaminī om niprésent; immanent; permanent; absolu — n. phil. qualifies brahman. sarvagāmī ayam niyamah this rule is universally valid.

sárvajit [jit] amnf Who succeeds at everything, victorious all; excellent — m. death | astr. np. of Sarvajit "victorious", personifying the 21st year of a life cycle [samvatsara] | soc. ritual ved. ekāha; not. rājasūya.
sárvajña |jña| amnf sarvajñā Who knows everything; opp. alpajña.
sarvajñatā [tā] f. omniscience.
sarvajñatva |tva| n. id. | bd. not. omniscience of the Buddha.
sárvajñāna |jñāna| n. bed. |Tantra| n.p. of the Sar vajñāna or Sarvajñānatantra.
sárvajñānottama [uttama] n. bed. [Tantra] n.p. of the Sarvajñānottama or Sarvajñānottamatantra.
sárvajyāní [jyāni] f. loss of all one's possessions.
sárvatanu [tanu] amnf sarvatanū whose body is intact — m. sarvatanū phil. ved. Who is reborn with his own body.
sárvatantra [Tantra] n. pl. sarvatantrāṇi phil. all doctrines — amnf sarvatantrā phil. universally admitted by all doctrines phil. learned in all doctrines.
sarvatantrasvatantra [svatantra] m. phil. "learned in all doctrines, without being a slave to any", honorific title of erudition; cf. Vācaspati₁ Miśra.
sárvatā [tā] f. totality.
sárvatvá [tva] n. totality; completeness.
sárvada [da] amnf sarvadā Who grants all — m. myth. epith. of Shiva.

sarvadamana [damana] n. myth. np. of Sarvada mana "He who can tame all", son of Sakuntalā repudiated by Dusyanta; he lived at the hermitage of Kanva, and earned his name by his courage, by taming wild beasts; his mother presented him to King Dusyanta to be recognized as the heir; |Mah.| the latter complied after hearing a heavenly voice; in the Abhijñānaśakuntala, it is a magic ring that reminds him of his promise, forgotten by a curse; he was then enthroned as rājaputra, and became the emperor [cakravartin] Bharata.
sarvadarśana |darśana| amnf sarvadarśanī ecumenical, universal.

Sarvadarśanasamgraha | samgraha | m. lit. np. of the Sarvadarśanasamgraha "Panorama of Viewpoints", a work classifying the various philosophical schools into 16 systems; it is attributed to Mādhavācārya or to his brother Sāyaṇa or to his nephew Māyana (mid-14th century).
sarvadarśanasiddhānta [siddhānta] m. bed. n.p. from the sarvadarśanasiddhānta "Compendium of all dogmas", philosophical text attributed to Sankara₁.
sarvadāna [dāna] n. donation of all one's possessions.
sárvadrá [drá2] amnf who sees everything.
sarvadharma [dharma] amnf sarvadharmā re latif to all laws — m. pl. all laws. sarvadharmān parityaja māmekam śaraṇam vraja [BhG.] Abandon all rules and take refuge in me.
sarvadharmasamabhāva [samabhāva] m. SOC. tolerance towards all religions.
sarvadhātu [dhātu] m. gram. root with its suffix [pratyaya]; cf. sārvadhātuka.
sárvadhārin [dhārin] m. n.p. of Sarvadhārī “who possesses everything”, personifying the 22nd year of a life cycle [samvatsara] | myth. epith. of Siva.
sarvanāman [nāman] n. gram. ["generic name"] pronoun or a. with pronominal inflection — amnf sarvanāmnī which bears all names.
sarvanāśa [nāśa] m. total destruction, complete ruin. sarvanāśam kṛ to lose everything.
sarvanāśin [in] amnf sarvanāśinī which destroys everything.

sarvapathīna [pathīna] amnf sarvapathīnā which goes in all directions; celebrated everywhere | which occupies the whole road — f. sarvapathīnā lit. np. of the sarvapathīnā, commentary on the Bhaṭṭikāvya by Mallinātha₁.
sarvapārṣada [pārṣada] n. gram. linguistic doctrine agreed upon by all schools.
sarvaprada [prada] amnf sarvapradā who gives everything.
sarvaprabhuguṇa [prabhuguṇa] m. ["all good qualities"] excellence.
sarvaprasanga | prasanga | mr. gram. total application.
sárvapriya | priya | amnf sarvapriyā who loves everything | dear to all.
sárvabāhya | bāhya | amnf sárvabāhyā the outermost.
sárvabhakṣa [bhakṣa] amnf sarvabhakṣā who eats everything; omnivorous.
sarvabhaksaka [bhaksaka] amnf sarvabhakṣakā who eats everything | myth. said of Agni condemned by Bhṛgu to eat anything and everything for having revealed Pulomā₁ to Pulomā₁.
sarvabhakṣin [bhakṣin] amnf sarvabhakṣiṇī who eats everything; omnivorous.
sárvabhāva [bhāva] m. the complete being; body and soul | pl. all beings. sarvabhāvena var. sarvabhāvais with all his heart; body and soul.

sárvabhūtá |bhūta| amnf sarvabhūtā which exists everywhere, universal — n. pl. all creatures. yac cāpi sarvabhūtānām bījam tad aham |BhG.| (Kṛṣṇa addressing Arjuna) This very source of all beings is me.
sarvabhūtātman |ātman| m. phil. the essence of all beings, the universal soul | myth. epith. of Śiva.
sárvabhūmi [bhūmi] f. the whole Earth — amnf who possesses the whole Earth.
sarvabhoga [bhoga₂] m. full enjoyment (of a good).
sarvabhogasamanvita | samanvita | amnf sar vabhogasamanvitā SOC. endowed with full enjoyment (of a good).
sarvabhogin | bhogin₂ | amnf sarvabhoginī who has full enjoyment.
sarvabhauma [bhauma] m. SOC. ["possessor of all the Earth" | royal title.
sarvamangalā [Mangalā] f. myth. np. of sar vamangalā "Favorable to all", form of Devī; cf. Mangalā.
sarvamatasaṃgraha | matasaṃgraha | m. lit. np. from the Sarvamatasamgraha, an anonymous doxographic work presenting 10 schools.
sárvamáya [maya] amnf sarvamayī which contains everything, which includes everything.
sarvamūla [mūla] amnf sarvamūlā lit. qualifies the philosophical work. of Madhva collected in collections | grantha|, serving as the foundation of the dvaita tradition.
sárvamedhá [medha] m. ved. 10-day soma sacrifice; on the last day of this total sacrifice, the soma giving all his possessions [viśvajit].
sárvarasa [rasa] amnf sarvarasā of all tastes; of all perfumes | containing all juices pl. all kinds of drops or perfumes.
sárvarūpa [rūpa] amnf sarvarūpā multiform; multicolored | of all kinds.
sárvarūpin [rūpin] amnf sarvarūpinī which takes all forms.
sárvaloká | loka | m. the whole world; everyone, all.
sárvavarna [varna] amnf sarvavarna of all colors | soc. of all social classes.
sárvavarman [varman] m. hist. n.p. of Sarvavarmā "all-Protector", Sanskrit grammarian of the 1st century.
sárvavidya [vidyā] amnf sarvavidyā who knows everything; omniscient — f. sarvavidyā all knowledge | pl. all the sciences.
sarvavidyāviśārada [viśārada| amnf sarva vidyāviśāradā expert in all knowledge.
sárvavedas [vedas₂] amnf who gives away all his possessions — m. sarvavedasa véd. his sacrifice of all his possessions.
sárvavedin [vedin] amnf sarvavedinī omni scient | who knows the whole Veda.
sárvavyāpin [vyāpin] amnf sarvavyāpinī om nipresent.
sarvaśūnyatvavādin [śūnyatvavādin] amnf sarvaśūnyatvādinī bd. holding to the doctrine that everything is empty; syn. śūnyavādin.
sárvaśveta [śveta] amnf sarvaśvetā entirely white | var. sarvásveta the whitest of all.
sarvasaṃmataśīkṣā [saṃmataśīkṣā] f. lit. np. from the phonetic treatise Sarvasammata "agreed upon by all".
sarvasāra |sāra| n. phil. universal essence.
sarvasiddhāntarāja [siddhāntarāja] m. hist. n.p. from sarvasiddhāntarāja, a mathematics text by Nityānanda₁ (17th century); cf. Golādhyāya₁.
Sarvasena [senā] m. hist. n.p. of King Sarvasena of the Vākāṭakās (end of 4th century); we owe him the court epic Harivijaya in prākṛtī .
sárvasauvarna [sauvarna] amnf sarvasauvarnā entirely in gold.
sarvasāropaniṣad | upaniṣad | f. bed. n.p. from the Sar vasāropaniṣad “Lesson on the Universal Essence”.
sarvasva [sva] n. the whole, the entire. jīvitasarvasvam balance sheet of a whole life.
sarvasvāmiguna [svāmiguna] m. bed. n.p. of king Sar vasvāmiguņa "who possesses all the qualities of a leader", hero of Hitopadesa.
sarvānga | anga₁ | n. the whole body — amnf sarvāngī complete, which has all its parts; total; perfect | Indonesian sarong. sarvāngam adv. entirely, totally; in all its aspects.
sarvāngāsana [āsana] m. phil. [yoga] candle posture.
sarvāc [ac] amnf sarvācī which goes in all directions.
sarvātman |ātman| m. the whole person phil. the universal Soul. sarvātmanā adv. entirely, completely | with all one's heart.
sarvādi |ādi| m. phil. the beginning of all things — amnf whatever the beginning may be.

sarvānukrama [anukrama] m. lit. complete index of a work, not. of the Rigveda. sarvānukramaņa [anukramaņa] nf sarvānukramaņī lit. complete index or concordance of a text, not. of the Rigveda | lit. np. of the sarvānukramaņī, concordance of the Rigveda attributed to Kātyāyana; Sadguruśisya made a commentary on it.
sarvānukramaṇaka [ka] amnf sarvānukramaņikā lit. which gives a complete index.
sarvānurakta [anurakta] amnf sarvānuraktā towards whom all are devoted.
sarvānuraktaprakṛti [prakṛti] m. object of devotion of all his subjects (said of Rāma).
sarvāpahāra [apahāra] m. act of taking everything.
sarvāpahāralopa [lopa] m. gram. elision of all markers of a suffix | pratyaya |.
sarvāstitvavādin [astitvavādin] amnf sarvāstitvavādinī cf. sarvāstivādin.

sarvāstivāda [astivāda] m. bd. sarvāstivāda school of Kaśmīra, professing the doctrine that everything is transient; it is one of the 4 schools of optional Buddhism [vaibhāṣika]; it is said to have been founded by Rāhula₁.
sarvāstivādin |in| m. bd. follower of this doctrine; opp. vijñānāstitvavādin, śūnyavādin. sarvāhna var. sarvāhņa [ahna] n. the whole day.
sarvottama | uttama | amnf sarvottamā best of all.
sarvausadha [osadhī] amnf sarvausadhā made up of various herbs.
sarvauṣadhī [oṣadhī] f. pl. various herbs | combination of 10 herbs — m. sarvausadhi id.
sarvaká [sarvaka] amnf sarvikā tout, total; entire; universal. sarvake adv. everywhere.
sarvatas [adv. sarva] adv. from all sides, in all directions | everywhere; completely. sarvato bhayāt out of fear of everyone.

sarvatobhadra [bhadra] amnf sarvatobhadrā favorable on all sides — m. [Mah.] name of an army formation | square temple having an entrance at the 4 cardinal points | open courtyard of a palace | mystical square diagram painted on a cloth | lit. double palindrome, variety of geometric poem |citrakāvya| in which each demistance is mirrored.
sarvatomukha | mukha | amnf sarvatomukhī ["that which faces on all sides"] multiple, multiform; complete, absolute, perfect | valid in all respects, without limitation.
sarvatra [sarvatra] adv. everywhere; in everything | always.
sarvatragā |ga₁| amnf sarvatragā that goes everywhere; omnipresent — m. air; wind.
sarvatragata [gata] amnf sarvatragatā univer sel, everywhere present.
sarvatragāmin [gāmin] amnf sarvatragāminī that penetrates all — m. air; wind.
sarvathā [sarvathā] adv. in every way, in any case, whatever the case may be; in every respect absolutely, completely; to the highest degree as far as possible.
sarvadā [sarvadā] adv. always; all the time.
sarvam [acc. sarva] iic.

sarvamsaha [saha₁] amnf sarvamsahā which patiently bears all — f. sarvaṃsahā the Earth. sarvamkasa var. sarvankasa [kasa] amnf sarvamkasā very irritating — f. sarvankasā lit. np. of the Sarvankaṣā, commentary on the Siśupālavadha of Māgha by Mallinātha₁.
sarvaśas [sarvaśas] adv. completely; entirely | all together, collectively; universally | gram. indicates that a collective noun can be used in all cases or i.e. | always, in all cases, everywhere.
sarvātmaka [sarvātmanka] amnf sarvātmakā which contains everything | contained in everything. sarvātmakena with all his heart. sarvam sarvātmakam [Sivadṛṣṭi] everything is in everything.
sarvātmakatva [tva] n. phil. interconnection of all things.
sarvāhṇa [sarvāhna] the whole day. sarvāhņam adv. all day.
sarṣapa m. bio. bot. Sinapis dichotoma, mou tarde | mustard grain; minimum weight measure (= 3 rājika, there are 12 in a yava, and 8 in a taṇḍula).
sala m. myth. np. of the young sala, who saved his Jain master Sudatta by killing a lion; he became the founding hero of the Hoysala dynasty, the lion symbolizing the Colās defeated by Viṣṇuvardhana.
salakṣaṇa [sa₁lakṣaṇa] amnf salakṣaṇā of the same character, similar; homogeneous. सল্জ salajja [sa₁lajjā] amnf salajjā embarrassed, ashamed; modest.
salavi cf. apasalavi.
salāja [sa₁lāja] amnf salājā accompanied by fried rice grains.
salila [sṛila] n. fluid, water; tears. salilam kṛ soc. to offer a libation of water to the shades.
salīla [sa₁līlā] amnf salīlā who plays; who makes graces, coquettish — acc. salīlam adv. playfully; making graces. salīlam iva as if playing, easily.

saluva m. hist. np. of saluva Narasimha₄, king of Vijayanagara (1486–1491); he founded the eponymous dynasty; he fought unsuccessfully against Gajapati Purusottamadeva₁, king of Kalinga, was taken prisoner, and released against the surrender of the citadel of Udayagiri; at his death the minister Narasa Nāyaka assumed the regency; his eldest son having been assassinated, his younger son Narasimha₅ succeeded him.
saloka [sa₁loka] amnf salokā sharing the same world, in the same country | on the same footing as g. loc. .
sallakī [related to śallā] f. bio. bot. Boswellia serrata, a tree whose resin is used to make incense.
savá₁ |act. su₂| m. pressing (not. of soma); libation — n. juice; sap, nectar.
sava₂ |agt. sū₁| m. instigator; instigator — act. m. incitement, impulse, order | ved. inaugu ration, solemn consecration | myth. np. of Sava, epith. of the Sun Savitā the instigator.
savayajña | yajna | mr. ved. rite of consecration.
savatsa [sa₁vatsa] amnf savatsā accompanied by her little one. savatsā dhenuḥ cow with her calf. s ildeavana₁ [act. su₂] n. action of pressing (not. the soma) | soma juice; soma libation.
sávana₁ |act. sū₁| n. incitement, instigation; command — ifc. soc. prayer to obtain (iic.).
savayas [sa₁vayas₁] amnf of the same age — m. comrade, friend — f. friend, confidante.
savara cf. sabara.

savarṇa [sa₁varṇa] amnf Savarṇā which is of the same color or class as; identical, of the same appearance | homogeneous, uniform | phon. (consonants) of the same group [varga] | soc. offspring of a brahmin and a kṣatriyā — f. Savarṇā myth. np. of Savarṇā "Identical (to Saranyū)", made by Saranyū to replace her with her husband Vivasvān; she is the mother of ManuYama.
savarṇana |na| n. math. reduction to a common denominator.
savastha [sa₁Vasistha] amnf savasistha accompanied by Vasistha.
savikalpa [sa₁vikalpa] amnf savikalpā differentiated | phil. [yoga] qualifies the samādhi where identification with the object is done while remaining conscious of one's identity; opp. nirvikalpa.
savikalpaka [ka] amnf savikalpakā phil. |Nyāya| is called discriminating knowledge; opp. nirvikalpaka.
savikalpapratyaksa [pratyaksa] n. phil. [Nyāya] conceptualized perception.
savicāra [sa₁vicāra] amnf savicārā with reflection, with introspection; with hesitation; opp. nirvicāra.

savitarka [sa₁vitarka] amnf savitarkā reasoned, with reflection | phil. [yoga] qualifies the first stage of samādhi, where the yogi continues to reason about the subject of his meditation. savitarkam adv. reflecting, upon reflection.

savitṛ [agt. sū₁] amnf savitrī stimulator, instigator; producer, creator myth. ved. np. of the creator god Savitā, radiant [āditya] of the rising Sun, "the instigator" with golden hands [Hiranyahasta]; he symbolizes the magical power of the Word identified with the procreative power of the Sun [Sūrya]; astr. he presides over the naksatra Hasta (Raven); he is celebrated in the gāyatrī.
savidya [sa₁vidyā] amnf savidyā scholar who pursues the same studies.
savinaya [sa₁vinaya] amnf savinayā modest, well-mannered. savinayam adv. modestly, politely, respectfully.
savibhīṣaṇa [sa₁vibhīṣaṇa] amnf sa vibhīṣaṇā accompanied by vibhīṣaṇa.
savibhrama [sa₁vibhrama] amnf sa vibhramā (especially in the feminine) languorous, sensual; erotic, provocative. savibhramam adv. sensually; casting provocative glances.

saviśeṣa [sa₁viśeṣa] amnf saviśeṣā endowed with specific properties | singular, particular; extraordinary | who knows how to discriminate — n. math. square root of two. savisesam with all the details | especially; excessively.
saviśeṣaśītala [śītala] amnf saviśeṣaśītalā very fresh; completely refreshing.
saviśrambha [sa₁viśrambha] amnf saviśrambhā confidential; intimate. saviśrambham adv. confidentially.
saviṣa [sa₁viṣa] amnf saviṣā poisonous, venomous.
saviṣaya [sa₁viṣaya] amnf saviṣayā gram. which admits an object, transitive (Verb); opp. nirvisaya; syn. sakarmaka.
savistara [sa₁vistara] amnf savistarā complete. savistaram var. savistarena in detail; completely, exhaustively | bed. (the Veda) with related texts.
savismaya [sa₁vismaya₁] amnf savis mayā with astonishment, with surprise.
savailaksya [sa₁vailaksya] amnf savailakṣyā awkward, embarrassed; clumsy; a little ashamed | unnatural; forced. savailakṣyam in a forced; unnatural manner.

savyá amnf savyā left; to the left; opp. daksina | opposite, contrary — m. left hand, left arm, left foot — n. soc. sacred cord worn over the left shoulder. savyatas adv. to the left; on the left side; with the left hand | on the wrong side. savyam kr to wear the sacred cord |yajñopavīta| over the left shoulder.
savyaṣṭhā |sthā₂| m. warrior standing to the left of a chariot.

savyasācin [sācin] amnf savyasācinī adroit ["who reaches (even) with the (left) hand"]; am biextre — m. left-handed | myth. np. of Savyasācī, epith. of Arjuna "the skillful one" (who can draw the Gāṇḍīva bow even with the left hand).
savyapekṣa [sa₁vyapekṣā] ifc. amnf savyapekṣā which requires, which presupposes, which depends on (iic.). nimittasavyapekṣa amn which requires a cause.
savyabhicāra [sa₁vyabhicāra] amnf savyabhicārā of doubtful validity; whose proof is incorrect — m. phil. [Nyāya] use of an overly general argument.
savyāpāra [sa₁vyāpāra] amnf savyāpārā occupied, employed, active.
savyāhṛti [sa₁vyāhṛti] amnf soc. ac accompanied by the three ritual exclamations.
saśańkha [sa₁śańkha] amnf saśańkhā carrying a conch shell — m. Vishnu carrying the conch shell. saśańkhacakro harih myth. Vishnu carrying the conch shell and the discus.
saśatrughna |sa₁śatrughna| amnf saśatrughnā accompanied by Satrughna.
saśabda [sa₁śabda] amnf saśabdā noisy. saśabdam adv. with a crash.
sáśarīra [sa₁śarīra] amnf saśarīrā with his body; said not. of heavenly visits. saśarīrasvargārohaṇam ascent to Heaven with his own body.
saśākhānagara |sa₁śākhānagara| amnf saśākhānagarā (city) surrounded by suburbs.
saśaila [sa₁śaila] amnf saśailā (my tagne) surrounded by hills.
saśoka [sa₁śoka] amnf saśokā filled with sadness, in pain; opp. aśoka. saśokam sadly.
saśmaśru [sa₁śmaśru] amnf bearded.
saśrīka [sa₁śrīka] amnf saśrīkā pretty, splendid | fortune.
saśrīkatā [tā] f. splendor.
saśrīkatva |tva| n. id. sas [nom. sa₂] ind. he, that, that one. anyasas another, that other one.

sasamdeha [sa₁sasamdeha] amnf sasamdehā who has doubts, who hesitates; with confusion | lit. poetic figure [alaṃkāra] where the speaker pretends to confuse the upameya with the upamāna of a simile [rūpaka].
sasaṃbandhi [sa₁saṃbandhi] amnf related to, connected with.
sasambandhika [ka] ifc. amnf sasambandhikā phil. [Nyāya] which is related to (iic.).
sasarpa [sa₁sarpa] amnf sasarpā with snakes; infested with snakes.
sasīta [sa₁Sītā] amnf sasītā accompanied by Sītā.
sasīma [sa₁sīman] amnf sasīmā of the same border; contiguous; neighbor.
sasuta [sa₁suta₂] amnf sasutā with his son; with his children.
sastrīka [sa₁strīka] amnf sastrīkā ac accompanied by women; married.
sasneha [sa₁sneha] amnf sasnehā onc killer, oily | with affection. sasneham affectionately.
saspṛha [sa₁spṛhā] amnf saspṛhā filled with desire; envious; desirous (loc. inf.). sasprham adv. lovingly | in an old manner.
sasmita [sa₁smita] amnf sasmitā sou riant. sasmitam adv. with a smile.
sasyá [related to śasya] n. cereal, wheat, grains | harvest, reaping | merit, virtue; good qualities. sasyam iva ājāyate martyaḥ [KU.] Just like the grain, the mortal is reborn.
sasyaka [ka] amnf sasyakā abundantly endowed with good qualities; perfect — m. (jewel) of very high quality. sasyapūrņa [pūrṇa] amnf sasyapūrṇā abundant in grain.
sasyabhuj [bhuj₃] amnf [nom. sasyabhuk] vegetarian.
sasyámālin [mālin] amnf sasyamālinī girded with harvests; fertile.
sasyáveda [veda] m. agronomy.
sasyáśālin [śālin] amnf sasyasālinī abundant in grain. kāle varsatu parjanyah prthivī sasyaśālinī That in the rainy season the monsoon covers the Earth with abundant harvests.
sasvara [sa₁svara] amnf sasvarā noisy, resounding | gram. stressed (text). sasvaram adv. loudly; in a loud voice.

√ sah₁ v. [1] pr. r. (sáhate) v. [1] pr. (sáhati) pft. (sasāha) pp. (sodha, sādha, sahita₁) pfp. (sa hya) inf. (sodhum) pf. (ut, pra, vi, sam) to be able to, to be capable of | resist, bear, endure, sustain | master, overcome; repress — ca. (sāhayati) to bear, endure. sahasva māsadvayam wait two months. na vāspam ašakat sodhum he could not hold back his tears.
sah₁ [agt. sah₁] ifc. mf Who prevails over, Who is master of (iic.) | Who supports, Who endures (iic.).

sah₁á₁ [agt. sah₁] amnf sahā powerful; capable; enduring — ifc. Who prevails over, victor over (iic.); capable of (iic. inf.) | Who bears (pa timentily), Who endures, indulgent towards (iic.) | Who stands up to, Who defies, on par with, Who triumphs over g. iic. .
sah₁á₂ [related to sadha] adv. together, at the same time; si multanély; opp. vinā | with, in company with (i.) (cl.) — iic. accompanied by, provided with, including — ifc. id. (rare).
sah₁ákāra₁ |kāra| m. cooperation; assistance | bio. variety of very fragrant mango — n. its fruit.
sahakāravṛkṣa [vṛkṣa] m. mango tree.
sah₁ákārin [kārin] amnf sahakāriņī Who assists, Who cooperates — m. assistant; accessory; expedient.
sahakṛtvan [kṛtvan] amnf sahakṛtvarī Who acts with.
sahagamana [gamana] n. common departure | soc. suicide of a widow on the funeral pyre of her husband; syn. sahamarana; cf. satī.

sahacara [cara] amnf sahacarī ["That which goes with"] That which accompanies, That which associates with; similar to — m. companion; servant | bio. bot. Nilgirianthus ciliatus (or bot. Strobilanthus kunthiana), shrub with violet flowers, flowering every 12 years in the Western Ghats; it gave its name to the Blue Mountains [Nīlagiri₁]; its honey is renowned — f. sahacarī companion, wife, lover.
sahacāra [cāra] m. agreement, harmony; congruence, concomitance | phil. [Nyāya] conco mitance in the syllogism [pañcāvayava] of the premises of cause [hetu] and conclusion [sādhya]; opp. vyabhicāra.
sahacārin [cārin] amnf sahacārinī Who coha bite; associate, colleague; companion, close friend, comrade.

sahajá [ja] amnf sahajā simultaneous (at (g.)) spontaneous; innate, hereditary, of birth; natu rel, easy — m. natural disposition | blood brother natural philosophy, developed by the saints (Caitanya, Nāmadeva, Tukārāma, Kabīr, Mīrabai, Nānaka, etc.); it advocated love and natural life.
sahajakīrti [kīrti] m. hist. np. from the Jain scholar (śvetāmbara) sahajakīrti (first half of the 17th century, Rajasthan); he is the author of the dictionary of synonyms Siddhaśabdārnava.
sahajakumbhakasthiti | kumbhakasthiti | f. phil. [yoga] "natural state similar to a jar", without breathing.
sahajadeśa [deśa] m. place of birth; place of origin of the family.
sahajayāna [yāna] n. bd. late doctrine of Mahāyāna in Bengal; its sacred texts were mystical chants [caryāgīti] composed by par
facts [siddha₁] of the movement.
sahajānanda [ānanda] m. hist. n.p. of Svāmī sahajānanda (1781–1830), non-renouncer of Svāminārāyaņa; cf. Šatānanda₁.
sahajāvasthā [avasthā₂] f. natural condition.
sahajīya [īya] amnf sahajīyā soc. follower of natural philosophy, tantric derivative of the vaiṣṇava gaudīya sect advocating the satisfaction of the senses and not. sexual.

Sahadeva [deva] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Sahadeva "He who has the gods with him," one of the 5 Pāṇḍavās, son of the Aśvinau and Mādrī, twin brother of Na kula; he conquered Kalinga so that it would pay tribute to Yudhiṣṭhira; he killed the treacherous Sakuni; cf. Tantipāla myth. [Mah.] np. of Sahadeva₁, son of Jarāsandha; he succeeded him as king of Magadha; he died in the Mah. war and his son Somādhi succeeded him | myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Viśālā Sahadeva₂, son of Sṛñjaya, father of Kuśāśva | lit. np. from the rhetorician sahadeva₃, student of Mukula (10th century) — f. sahadevā myth. np. of sahadevā "Companion of the gods", epith. of Devakī.
sahadharma [dharma] m. common duty.
sahapāthin [pāthin] m. schoolmate.
sahabahuvrīhi [bahuvrīhi] m. gram. exocentric compound comitative determinative.
sahabrahmacārin [brahmacārin] m. du. sahabrah macārinau study companions.
sahamaraṇa [maraṇa] n. soc. suicide of a widow on the funeral pyre of her husband; syn. sahaga mana; cf. satī.
sah₁ámāna₁ [māna₁] amnf sahamānā arrogant.
sahādhyāyin [adhyāyin] amnf sahādhyāyinī study companion; fellow student.
sahokti [ukti] f. cacophony | lit. figure of speech comparing objects using saha₂; opp. vinokti. samam dviṣām dhanuṣām ca jīvākṛṣṭim
yodhāścakruḥ [Subandhu] the warriors together drew the strings of their bows and took the lives of their enemies.
sahodara | udara | amnf sahodarā f. sahodarī couterin — m. brother — f. sahodarā var. sahodarī sister.
sahopalambha | upalambha | mr. simultaneous perception.
sahopalambhaniyama [niyama] m. phil. observation of simultaneous perception of two entities.
sahakāra₁ [sa₁hakāra] amnf sahakārā which includes the letter 'ha' | with call.
sahana [agt. sah₁] amnf sahanā powerful | patient; who supports, who endures — act. n. patience; resistance; longanimity.
sáhamāna₁ [ppr. mo. sah₁] amnf sa hamānā conqueror; victorious | tolerant.
sáhas [abstr. sah₁] amnf Vedic. powerful; victorious — n. Vedic. power, strength; combat, victory; booty — m. name of a Vedic month (mārgaśīrṣa, November-December).
sáhasvat |vat| amnf sahasvatī strong, powerful, victorious.
sahasa |sa₁hasa| amnf sahasā who laughs — n. laughable thing.
sáhasā | i. Sahas | adv. intensely, powerfully, with force | rapidly, precipitately; all at once, suddenly; in an unexpected way.
sahasya [Sahasya] amnf sahasyā then sant, strong — m. name of a Vedic month (pauṣa, December-January).
sah₁ásra [Sahasra] num. n. sg. thousand, one thousand ∥ gr. χιλιοι .
sahasracandradarśana [candradarśana] n. SOC. celebration on the occasion of an 80th birthday (corresponding to 1000 lunar months).
Sahasrajit [jit] m. myth. np. of King Sahasrajit "of a thousand victories", eldest son of King Yadu; he is father of Satajit.
sahasrada |da| amnf sahasradā which gives 1000 (cows) (to a brahmin).
sahasranāman [nāman] amnf sahasranāmnī who has a thousand names — n. pl. sahasranāmānas the thousand names (of a deity).
sahasrapad | pad₂ | amnf sahasrapadī | nom. sahasrapād which has a thousand feet; which has a thousand columns — m. ved. said not. of Purușa.

Sahasrapāda [pāda] m. Sun ["which has 1000 rays"] myth. np. of the Brahmin Sahasrapāda; having playfully placed a fake straw snake in the neck of his friend Khagama, the latter cursed him to become a snake |dundubha| and to regain human form only at the sight of the ascetic Ruru | sahasrapād var. Sahas rapāt.
sahasraphaṇa | phaṇa | m. representation "with a thousand cobra hoods".
sahasrabāhu |bāhu| m. who has a thousand arms | myth. epith. of king Arjuna₁ Kārtavīrya "of the thousand arms".
sah₁ásramarīci [marīci] m. myth. np. of Sahasra marīci, epith. of the Sun "with a thousand rays".
sah₁ásramarīcimālin [mālin] m. myth. np. of Sa hasramarīcimālī, epith. of the Sun "crowned with a thousand rays".
sah₁ásramukha [mukha] amnf sahasramukhī which has a thousand heads.
Sahasramukhāsura [asura] m. myth. np. of the asura Sahasramukhāsura "Hydra with a thousand heads".
sahasramukhāsuracaritra [caritra] n. bed. n.p. from the sahasramukhāsuracaritra, text attributed to Jaimini.
sah₁ásralingī [linga] f. the feminine form of Sahas ralinga "adorned with a thousand representations of the linga".
sah₁ásralocana [locana] amnf sahasralocanā who has a thousand eyes — m. myth. epith. of Indra.
sahasraśas [śas] adv. by the thousands.

sahasrākṣa [akṣa] amnf sahasrākṣī who has 1000 eyes | who sees all | myth. epith. of Indra Netrayoni cursed to have to bear 1000 vagina marks on his body (later changed into 1000 eyes) | myth. epith. of several gods.

Sahasrānīka [anīka] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of King Sahasrānīka "of the thousand armies", son of Satānīka, first king of the Vatsa dynasty; he is the reincarnation of the vasu Vidhūma; Šakra gave him a magic chariot to travel in the air; he married the princess of Videha Mṛgāvatī; she was taken away by a bird, and found by Jamadagni in his hermitage where she gave birth to Udayana; a gold ring engraved with his name allowed them to be found; feeling old age coming, he abdicated in favor of Udayana, and retired with his wife and his advisors to the Himalayas.

sahasrāra | ara | m. [sahasrāracakra] phil. [yoga] "(Circle with) a thousand rays", 7th chakra of tantric yoga, located at the brahmarandhra, at the top of the occiput; it opens in the ultimate stage of kundalinīyoga; it is represented by a lotus of 1000 golden petals bearing all the letters of the devanāgarī; it is the psychic center of Divine Union.
sahasrāragranthi [granthi] m. med. pineal gland.
sahasraka [sahasraka] amnf sahasrikā ifc. having a thousand — amnf sahasrakā with a thousand heads — n. sahasrika a thousand — f. sahasrikī ifc. which lasts a thousand years (year, with varsa, abda).
sahāya [saha₂aya] m. traveling companion; comrade, ally; colleague, associate; helper, assistant | soc. royal servant || lat. socius; fr. associé.
sahāyatā |tā| f. camaraderie; friendship | pl. group of companions.
sahāyatva |tva| n. camaraderie; friendship.
sahāyavat |vat| amnf sahāyavatī who has a (true) companion.
sahāva |sa₁hāva| amnf sahāvā libertine; shameless, licentious.
sahita₁ [pp. sah₁] amnf sahitā endured, borne.

sahita₂ [saha₂ita] amnf sahitā united; united with, accompanied by, with (i. iic.) | provided with, endowed with | astr. in conjunction with (i. iic.) | pl. sa hitāh all together | du. sahitau the two together. sahitam adv. ifc. near (iic.) | together; with, in the company of (iic.).
sahiṣṇu [agt. sah₁] amnf patient; who bears (acc. g. iic.) | humble.
sahiṣṇutā [tā] f. patience, tolerance; resignation | humility.
sahiṣṇutva |tva| n. patience, tolerance; resignation | humility.

sahṛdaya |sa₁hṛdaya| amnf sahṛdayā ["who has a heart"] affectionate; sensitive, not. to beauty; intelligent — m. wise; kind-hearted man phil. enlightened amateur, who appreciates the emotion expressed during an aesthetic experience [rasa].
sahrdayatā [tā] f. phil. aesthetic appreciation.
Sahṛdayalīlā [līlā] f. bed. n.p. of the Sahṛdayalīlā, or literary aesthetic work of Ruyyaka (Kaśmīra, 12th century).
sahṛdayāloka [āloka] m. lit. np. from sahṛdayāloka "Illumination on Literary Emotion", a work on aesthetics by Anandavardhana.
sahya [pfp. [1] sah₁] amnf sahyā to last; tolerable | able to bear, enduring; strong, powerful — m. geo. np. of sahya or sahyādri, chain of Western Ghats — n. assistance; healing.
sahyādri [adri] m. geo. np. of the sahyādri mountain range "powerful", piedmont of the Western Ghats rate.

sahyādrikhanda [khanda] mn lit. np. of the Sahyādrikhanda, late section of the Skandapurāna; it tells of, in particular, the exploits of Parasurāma in creating the Konkana by throwing his axe from Mt sahyādri; followed by an often hostile description of the various Brahmanical clans that populated the region.

√ sā₁ v. [4] pr. (syati) pp. (sita) pf. (ava) to stop; to end | to dispute | to determine, to decide; to be convinced or persuaded of; to take for (acc.) — ca. (sāyáyati) to cause to stop; to incite to (inf.). brāḥmasya ved. O brahmin, tue.

sā₂ [f. tad] pn. 3rd person. f. [sg. name. sā, acc. tām, i. tayā, dat. tasyai, abl. g. tasyās, loc. tasyām; of. name. acc. te, i. dat. abl. tābhyām, g. loc. tayos; pl. name. acc. tās, i. tabhis, dat. abl. tābhyas, g. tāsām, loc. tāsu she, this, that one.
sāṃyogika [*saṃyogaika] amnf sāṃyogikā connected | gram. (meaning) figurative or metaphorical; opp. auddeśika.
sāṃvatsara [*saṃvatsara] amnf annual sāṃvatsarā | which takes a year — m. astrologer — f. sāmvatsarī soc. funeral rite one year after death.
sāmvatsarika [*samvatsaraika] amnf sāṃvatsarikā annual; produced in one year; due annually — m. astrologer.
sākám adv. at the same time, simultaneously, together | at the same time as, in concert with, in common with (i.); syn. samam, saha₂.
sākamedha [edha] m. pl. sākamedhās soc. 3rd rite of cāturmāsya at the full moon of the month kārttika, where "the fires are all lit at once".

sākāṅkṣa [sa₁ākāṅkṣa] amnf sākāṅkṣā gram. possessing a syntactic-semantic dependency. arthaikatvāt ekam vākyam sākānkṣam cet vibhāge syāt gram. [Jaimini] When analyzing a sentence, every word must be connected to obtain a unique meaning.
sākāra [sa₁ākāra₁] amnf sākārā which has a shape; definite | which has a pretty shape, beautiful.
sākāravāda [vāda] m. bd. doctrine teaching the reality of the object of consciousness; opp. nirākāravāda; cf. Jñānaśrīmitra.
Sāketa n. geo. np. of the city of Sāketa, near Ayodhyā; it was renamed Faizabad as the capital of the Nawab of Avadh in 1722.
sākṣa iic. sākṣāt.

sāk, sāt [sa₁ak, sa₁ adv. visu, with one's own eyes; before one's eyes; visibly, truly, directly | in reality, in person, in the flesh, in bodily form. sākṣātkṛ to see with one's own eyes; to realize. sākṣātkṛtya ind. having placed before his eyes. sākṣādbhū to appear in person, to materialize, to become visible. sākṣātkāvyārtha literal meaning of a poem.
sākṣātkāra [kāra] amnf sākṣātkārī phil. of which we have direct experience.
sākṣātkṛta [kṛta] amnf sākṣātkṛtā placed before the eyes; evident.
sākṣādupāya [upāya] m. direct route.
sākṣāddṛṣṭa [dṛṣṭa] amnf sākṣāddṛṣṭā seen with his own eyes.
sākṣi iic. sākṣin.
sākṣicaitanya [caitanya] n. phil. ["witness consciousness"] pure consciousness.
sākṣivat [vat] adv. as a witness.
sākṣika [sākṣaika] amnf sākṣikā who observes; spectator, eyewitness.
sākṣin [sākṣain] m. spectator, eyewitness; disinterested witness | phil. thinking subject; ego. sākṣīkr to cite as a witness; to call to witness. sākṣībhū to be a witness.
