sākṣiptam [sa₁ākṣipta] adv. in a careless, distracted manner.
sākṣya [sākṣaya] n. testimony; evidence; attestation — amnf sākṣyā visible by (iic.). sākṣyaṃ kṛ attest. agnim sākṣye ādhāya in the presence of fire.

Sāgara [*Sagara] m. sea, ocean | (figuratively) immensity | myth. np. of Sāgara the Ocean; it was dug by the 60,000 sons of King Sagara to find the horse of his sacrifice lost in the underworld, then filled by the Ganges descending from the heavens; cf. Bhagīratha | pl. sāgarās myth. the 60,000 sons of Sagara.

sāgaraka [ka] amnf sāgarikā who lives by the sea — f. sāgarikā lit. [Ratnāvalī₁] np. of sāgarikā "Oceanic", borrowed name of Ratnāvalī₁, daughter of the king of Ceylon, shipwrecked, rescued and introduced to the court of King Udayana as a lady-in-waiting to Queen Vāsavadattā₂.

sāgaradatta | datta | amnf sāgaradattā given by the ocean — f. sāgaradattā lit. [DKC.] np. of sāgaradattā, daughter of Vaiśravaṇa₁ and sister of Sind hudattā; wife of King Kusumadhanvā, she is mother of Vasumdharā.
sāgnika [sa₁Agnika] amnf sāgnikā ac companion of Agni.
sāgra |sa₁ agra| amnf sāgrā with the tip or the peak | [samagra] whole, in its entirety | in excess of. sāgram adv. for a longer period; for all of life.

sāmkāśya [*samkāśaya] nf Sāmkāśyā myth. [Rām.] np. of the city of Sāṃkāśyā "Ad mirable", on the banks of the Ikṣumatī River; it was conquered by Janakarāja, and offered as a capital to his younger brother Kuśadhvaja₁.
sāṃketika [*saṃketaika] amnf sāmketikā conventional; relating to an agreement.
sāṃketya [*saṃketaya] n. convention; agreement; appointment.

sāmkhya var. sānkhya [*saṃkhya] n. np. from sāmkhya "Theory of Substances", a philosophical doctrine based on discrimination, and attributed to Kapila; it is one of the 6 viewpoints |saddarśana| of orthodox Hinduism; it deals with universal structures, or macrocosm; it postulates a supreme principle [āstika] although atheistic [nirīśvara]; cf. tattva, purusa, prakṛti, Iśvarakṛṣṇa.

sāṃkhyakārikā [kārikā] f. pl. lit. np. of the Sāṃkhyakārikās or Sāṃkhyasaptati, a collection of 72 stanzas by Iśvarakṛṣṇa, the first systematic elaboration of the doctrine of sāmkhya; it teaches how man can liberate himself by eliminating the three kinds of suffering |tapatraya|:
psychic [ādhyātmika], material [ādhibhautika], and supernatural [ādhidaivika]; Gauḍapāda commented on it [vṛtti], as did Māṭhara; the Yuk tidīpikā is considered its major exegesis [Rājavārttika].
sāmkhyatattvakaumudī | tattvakaumudi | f. bed. n.p. of the sāmkhyatattvakaumudī, exposition of the sāṃkhya doctrine due to Vācaspati₁ Miśra.

sāṃkhyapravacanabhāṣya [pravacanabhāṣya] n. lit. np. of the Sāṃkhyapravacanabhāṣya, commentary on the Sāmkhyasūtra by Vijnānabhikṣu; he elaborates the theory of the balance of the three qualities [trigunasāmya].
sāmkhyasāra |sāra| mr. bed. n.p. of sāmkhyasāra, philosophical work. of Vijñānabhikṣu.
Sāmkhyasūtra [sūtra] n. pl. lit. np. of the Sāṃkhyasūtra or Sāṃkhyapravacanasūtra, foundational work of sāṃkhya, attributed to Kapila; the current text is late (14th century).
sāṃgrahasūtrika [*saṃgrahasūtraika] amnf sāmgrahasūtrikī soc. who studies the aphorisms of the Samgrahasūtra.
sāṃghika [*saṃghaika] amnf sāṃghikī bd. which concerns the community of monks.
sācí [sa₁ac] adv. sideways, obliquely; at an angle (look). sācīkṛ to turn away; to act furtively. sācīdṛś to avert one's gaze.
sācivilokita [vilokita] n. furtive glance; (theatre) oblique (lingering) look.
sācin [agt. sac] amnf sācinī which reaches; cf. savya.
sācivya [*sacivaya] n. companionship, friendship, assistance | office of minister or advisor to a prince.
sācī iiv. sāci.
sācīkṛta [kṛta] amnf sācīkṛtā diverted, furtive — n. dissimulation, distortion; perversion. sācīkṛtam in a diverted manner.
sācīsūtra |sūtra| n. med. frenulum of the foreskin.
sāñcī f. geo. np. of Sāñcī, in Madhya Pra desh, site of construction of an important stūpa (1st century BC); it is 12.80 high and 32.20 in diameter.
sāñjali [sa₁añjali] amnf who has her hands joined (in greeting).
sādha |pp. sah₁| amnf sādhā conquered, defeated.
sāt reduces to (form of adverbs for liaires auxiliaries). sātkṛ var. sātbhū reduce to (iiv.). bhūmisātkṛ raze (building).

Sāta |pp. san₁| amnf sātā ved. obtained, given — n. Pleasure, delight — m. lit. [KSS.] np. from yakṣa Sāta "Pleasure"; guilty of having seduced the daughter of a sage, he was transformed into a lion; che vauched by his son, he recovered his nature when King Dīpakarni struck him with his arrow; cf. Sātavāhana.

Sātavāhana [vāhana] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of King Sātavāhana, son of the yakṣa Sāta who was transformed into a lion as punishment; he was adopted by King Dīpakarņi and succeeded him; mocked for his poor knowledge of Sanskrit, he learned Sarvavarmā's grammar in 6 months, causing Guṇāḍhya to lose his bet | pl. Sātavāhanās hist. np. of the Andhra people and dynasty of the Sātavāhanās, who ruled over the Deccan after the fall of the Maurya empire, and until around the year 200; their capital was Pratisthāna; cf. Sālivāhana.
sātanka |sa₁ātanka| amnf sātankā ef frayé, terrifié.
sātatya [*satataya] n. continuity; permanence. sātatye gram. without hiatus. sātatyena continuously; permanently.
sāttva |*sattva| amnf sāttvā concerning the sattva quality.

sāttvika [*sattvaika] amnf sāttvikī who has character, firm; vigorous, energetic phil. | "whose predominant guṇa is sattva" | virtuous, pure; natural; honest, authentic soc. qualifies a vegetarian food without garlic or onions, and a virtuous way of life | lit. qualifies 6 mythological collections [purāṇa] of vaiṣṇava obedience: Padmapurāṇa, Visnupurāna, Nāradapurāna, Bhāgavatapurāna, Garudapurāņa and Vārāhapurāņa — m. [theatre] expression | cf. sāttvikānubhāva.
sāttvikabhāva [bhāva] m. lit. involuntary symptom of emotion.

sāttvikānubhāva [anubhāva] m. [aesthetics] physiological state resulting from an emotion; there are 8 of them: a broken voice [svarabheda], fainting [pralaya], goosebumps [romāñca], pallor [vaivarṇya] (or a change of complexion [varṇavikāra]), paralysis [stambha], sweating [sveda], trembling [vepathu], and the
tears [aśru].
sātma |sa₁ ātma| amnf sātmā with one's own person; of one's own nature. sātmīkṛ to become accustomed to (acc.). sātmībhū to become a habit; to become appropriate.
sātmatā |tā| f. fact of being of the same essence as (gi iic.).

sātmya [sātmaya] amnf sātmyā appro prié; natural — n. community of nature; appropriation | soc. conformity to the norm | med. appropriate treatment; habit of life in accordance with the organism; regimen.
sātyá [*satya] amnf sātyā whose nature is truth; of trust.
Sātyaki [*satyakai] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Sātyaki, patr. of the vṛṣṇi Yuyudhāna "son of satya ka", friend and driver of the chariot of Kṛṣṇa; he is also called Saineya.

sātvata [*satvata] amnf sātvatī geo. concerning the Satvat people; who belongs to this people | myth. np. of King Sātvata, descendant of Madhu; he is said to have had 7 sons, of whom vṛṣṇi is the eldest myth. [Mah.] epithet of Kṛṣṇa, prince vṛṣṇi — f. sātvatī lit. noble, serene style; opp. ārabhaṭī.
sād |ca. sad₁| v. |10| pr. (sādayati) pp. (sādita) to seat, to make sit; to place in or on (loc.) to ruin, to overthrow, to destroy, to cause to perish, to reduce to nothing.
sāda |act. sad₁| m. ved. horsemanship slump, bogged down; fatigue, weakening; discouragement, despair.
sādana [act. ca. sad₁] n. exhaustion; wear and tear | arrangement (of utensils) | the act of getting bogged down.
sādara [sa₁ādara] amnf sādarā respec tueux | who shows consideration or devotion towards (iic.). sādaram respectfully.
sādita [pp. ca. sad₁] amnf sāditā as sis, installed; in the saddle | tired, depressed, discouraged; destroyed.
sādin [agt. sad₁] m. horseman; driver of
char | destroyer | var. sādi id.
sādṛśya [sa₁dṛśya] n. resemblance, simila rité | phil. the fact of being in the image of God; one of the goals of karmayoga .
sādya [pfp. [1] ca. sad₁] amnf sādyā saddled, harnessed — m. horse to ride.
sādyaḥkra [*sadyaḥkrī] amnf sādyaḥkrā cf. sādyahskra.

sādyaḥskra [*sadyaḥkrī] amnf sādyaḥskrā SOC. (solemn rite) performed with soma purchased on the same day — n. SOC. ceremony abbreviated to one day | myth. during a competition between the radiant [ādityās] and the lu

The miners [angirasas] for the possession of Heaven, the latter proposed to the former to officiate at the solemn ritual in which they themselves would be sacrificers [yajamāna]; the ādityās then invented the accelerated ritual sādyaḥskra in which they invited the angirasas to officiate, thus winning the competition.

sādh [ca. sidh₁] v. [10] pr. (sādhayati) pp. (sādhita) pfp. (sādhya) to arrange, settle; to accomplish, perform, realize; to set out (to do what one has to do) | to practice, train oneself to, strive to achieve | to get straight to the point; to obtain, win, acquire | to win over, conjure, seize; to subjugate; to prevail over acc. | to demonstrate, prove — ps. (sādhyate) to be subject, to be dominated — des. (siṣādhayiṣati) to want to prevail. mantram sādh to recite a mantra. marum sādh to abstain from drinking. vākyam sādh to keep one's word, fulfill a promise. idānīm sādhaya you may dispose. tatkāryam sādhayitumalam saḥ he is up to the task.

sādhaka | agt. ; sidh₁ | ; a. ; m. ; n. ; f. ; sādhikā ; one who operates, who performs, who influences, who masters | effective, useful; rational — m. phil. practitioner of yoga | SOC. spiritual practitioner established in a path of salvation | magician.
sādhakatā |tā| f. usefulness, relevance.
sādhakatva [tva] n. act of convincing | magic, illusion, Zionism.

sādhakatama [super. sādhaka] amnf sādhakatamā most effective | gram. means which characterizes the main cause of the action, associated with the semantic role [kāraka] of instrument [karaṇa]; it is marked by the instrumental [tṛtīya] |phil. [Nyāya] causal factor of maximum effectiveness generating correct knowledge | pramā₂|.

sādhana [agt. sidh₁] amnf sādhanā effective — ifc. that performs, that produces, that procures (iic.) | that conjures (spirit) — act. n. execution, realization, accomplishment; acquisition, obtaining; result | means, instrument, factor; effective proof, cause | army; military forces; means of punishment | source of comfort or pleasure | genital organ (male or female) | SOC. spiritual practice gram. formative, factor of realization of a suffix kṛt₂; it expresses an actor [kāraka] of the action such as its agent [kartr] or its object/purpose [karma] or the action itself [bhāva] | (adj.) that realizes the factor (iic.) (said of a suffix krt₂ or a krdanta) — f. sādhanā phil. mastery of yoga; spiritual quest. sādhanīkṛ to employ as a means to (loc.). sādhanībhū to become a means or an instrument. karmasādhana gram. that expresses the object of the action (expressed by the verb). bhāvasādhana gram. that expresses the completed action (like the kṛt₂ ap).
sādhanaka [ka] ifc. amnf sādhanikā carried out by means of (iic.).

sādhanacatustaya [catustaya] n. phil. [Vedānta] the four qualifications of the aspirant to liberation: to know how to distinguish in reality between the permanent and the ephemeral [nityānityavastuviveka], to be indifferent to the benefit of the fruits of one's action [arthaphalabhogavirāga] here and in the hereafter [ihāmutra], to have accomplished the 6 perfections beyond tions [satkasampatti], and to desire liberation |mumukṣutva|.
sādhanatā [tā] ifc. f. fact of being a means of (iic.).
sādhanatva [tva] n. efficacy [the fact of being a means or a proof.
sādhanapañcaka [pañcaka] n. lit. np. from the sādhanapañcaka "Five verses on spiritual discipline", where Śaṃkara₁ gives 40 pieces of advice to his disciples to achieve Enlightenment.
Sādhanapāda [pāda] m. phil. [yoga] np. of the Sādhanapāda, section of the Yogasūtra dealing with the Way of realization.

sādhanamālā [mālā] f. lit. np. of the sādhanamālā "Garland of spiritual realization", work [tantra] bd. giving 300 instructions for the visualization of the deities and the formulas [mantra] which are appropriate to them, composed between the 5th and 11th century.
sādhanīna [īna] ifc. amnf sādhanīnā proper to perform (iic.).
sādhanīya [sādhanaīya] amnf sādhanīyā that must be accomplished or executed | gram. that must be formed (word) | phil. that be to be acquired (knowledge); to be demonstrated.
sādharmya [*sadharmaya] n. equality of attributions; identity of nature | phil. participation in the works of God, one of the duties of the karmayoga.
sādharmyadṛṣṭānta [dṛṣṭānta] m. phil. [Nyāya] example in positive support of a syllogism, verifying both the cause [hetu] and the thesis [sādhya]; opp. vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta.
sādhāra |sa₁ādhāra| amnf sādhārā which has support.

sādhāraṇa [sa₁ādhāraṇa] amnf sadhāraṇā f. sadhāraṇī ["having a common base" ordinary, general, generic; collective; shared; common to (g. dat. i. ii.); common to all, universal | having the same base as, analogous to, similar to (i. ii.) | average, temperate (between two extremes, hot and cold, etc.); not. intermediate terroir between dry lands [jāngala] and marshy lands [anūpa] | phil. [Nyāya] characterizes ordinary perception [pratyakṣa], by the 5 senses and the mind; opp. asādhāraṇa | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] which belongs to more instances than the one presented, part of the paradox anaikāntika — n. generic property — m. astr. np. of Sādhārana "Solidarity", personifying the 44th year of a life cycle [samvatsara]. sādhāraṇīkṛ to pool; to share. kena vānyena saha sādhāranīkaromi duhkham With whom else shall I share my sorrow? sādhāraṇībhū to become the equal of; to identify with.
sādhāraṇadharma [dharma] m. phil. the universal moral duty, superior to that of one's own condition | svadharma|.
sādhāraṇī iiv. sādhāraṇa.
sādhāraṇīkaraṇa [karaṇa] n. pooling; generalization | phil. [aesthetics] universalization of human emotions; this concept, due to Bhatṭanāyaka, was developed by Abhinavagupta.
sādhāraṇīkṛta [kṛta] amnf sādhāraṇīkṛtā pooled, shared, collective.
sādhita [pp. ca. sidh₁] amnf sādhitā accomplished; carried out; provoked; completed | mastered, subdued; punished, forced to pay a fine
appointed | phil. demonstrated | ordered (punishment, fine).
sādhibhūta [sa₁adhibhūta] amnf sādhibhūtā phil. in accord With the spirit pervading nature.
sādhibhūtādhidaiva [adhidaiva] amnf sādhibhūtādhidaivā phil. [BG.] in accord With the spirit pervading nature and With the divine.

sādhiyajña [sa₁adhiyajña] amnf sādhiyajñā phil. in accord with the spirit of sacrifice. sādhibhūtādhidaivam mām sādhiyajñañca ye viduh | prayāṇakāle'pi ca mām te viduryuktacetasah || [BG.] Those who know me as pervading nature, as divine, and as the spirit of sacrifice, until their last hour have their minds engaged in my correct knowledge.
sādhiṣṭha [super. sādhu] amnf sādhiṣṭhā the most upright, the most direct; the most effective (sacrifice); the most appropriate; the best.
sādhīyas [compar. sādhu] amnf sādhīyasī better; more appropriate; more agreeable — ind. more willingly | to a higher degree; excessively.

sādhú [*sādhu] amnf sādhvī good, benevolent; honest, virtuous, excellent; capable, able, competent, effective; accomplished | skilled in, able to (loc.) — m. good man, holy man, saint; mod. wandering ascetic — n. goodness, honesty. sādhu acc. adv. good | excl. good! sādhu man to approve. sādhu kṛ to do well. sādhu sādhu very well! sāmasu sādhu skilled in Vedic chanting.
sādhukarman [karman] amnf sādhukarmaṇī who acts well.
sādhukāritva | kāritva | amnf sādhukāritvā who does something well.
sādhúkārín |kārin| amnf sādhukāriņī who acts well; gifted, intelligent.
sādhutama |tama| amnf sādhutamā super. excellent; the best.
sādhutara |tara| amnf sādhutarā compar. better than (abl.).
sādhutā [tā] f. correctness, validity; goodness; excellence.
sādhutva |tva| n. correctness, validity; excellence.
sādhutvajñana [jñāna] n. gram. knowledge of correct forms (through grammar).
sādhúmata [mata] amnf sādhumatā held in high esteem.
sādhúvāda | vāda | m. exclamation "bravo!" |sādhu|. sādhuvādam dā to applaud.
sādhuvṛtta [vṛtta] amnf sādhuvṛttā who behaves well; virtuous — n. good conduct, virtuous behavior.
sādhvanuśāsana [anuśāsana] n. correct teaching (not. of language use, purpose of grammar).
sādhvācāra |ācāra| m. good conduct; virtuous behavior — amnf sādhvācārī who behaves well.

sādhyá [pfp. [1] ca. sidh₁] amnf sādhyā to submit, that which can or must be won | to accomplish, to achieve, to realize; that which must be realized; capable of being executed | med. (disease) curable | to deduce, to demonstrate — m. goal, objective | phil. |Tantra| part of a formula |mantra| expressing the desired goal | phil. [Nyāya] logical proposition to be established; thesis; cf. pratijñā₂ | pl. sādhyās Vedic. the "perfectibles", class of divine beings who preceded the gods; what is superabundant [atirikta] is offered to them in the sacrifice; the sādhyās are associated with the zenith [upariṣṭāt]; opp. āptyās.
sādhyaka [ka] ifc. amnf sādhyakā which must attain (iic.).
sādhyatā |tā| f. feasibility, realizability, attainability | gram. unfulfilled character of an action; opp. siddhatā.
sādhyatāvacchedaka [avacchedaka] phil. mr. [Nyāya] characteristic of the fact to be established.
sādhyatva [tva] n. curability; the state of being improvable or successful.
sādhyanāma | nāman | n. soc. "name" of a mantra, expressing its purpose.
sādhyanirdeśa | nirdeśa | mr. phil. | Nyāya | evidence of the thesis.
sādhyavat |vat| amnf sādhyavatī who takes the goal to be achieved | phil. [Nyāya] who verifies the predicate — m. soc. party in a trial which is responsible for making the proof.

sādhyavasāna [sa₁adhyavasāna] amnf sādhyavasānā lit. with ellipsis to be filled in — f. sādhyavasānā lit. [Mukula] figurative sense [lakṣaṇā] totally obscuring the literal sense; it expresses the figure of speech rūpakātiśayokti. ayam candrah this (face) is like the Moon (criterion of beauty).
sādhyāvasthāpanna [avasthāpanna] n. gram. im perfective; opp. siddhāvasthāpanna.
sādhyāvasthāpannabhāva [bhāva] m. gram. meaning of a root as an action in progress.
sādhyīya [sādhyaīya] amnf sādhyīyā phil. [Nyāya] concerning the thesis.
sādhvasa [sādhuasa] n. alarm, terror; fear of (g. iic.) | (theatre) false alarm, sudden fear, panic. sādhvasam gam to be seized with terror.
sānanda [sa₁ānanda] amnf sānandā happy, joyful; one who takes joy in (iic.). sānandam adv. joyfully.
sānaya [*sana₂ya] amnf sānayā old; ancient; durable.
sānu mn summit, ridge, mountain range; plateau; forest.
sānumat |mat| amnf Sānumatī mountainous; having a plateau or a summit — f. Sānumatī reads. [Abhijñānaśakuntalā] np. of the nymph [apsaras] Sānumatī, friend of Sakuntalā.
sānuja [sa₁anuja] amnf sānujā accom accompanied by the younger brother.
sānunāsika [sa₁anunāsika] amnf sānunāsikā phon. refers to nasalized semivowels, marked in writing by the candrabindu; opp. ni ranunāsika.
sānurodha [sa₁anurodha] amnf sānurodhā who shows consideration. sānurodham adv. with consideration.
sāntara [sa₁antara] amnf sāntarā having an interval or gaps | multiform, non-uniform (opp. ekarūpa); non-compact, discontinuous gram. not within the scope of the rule by an additional clause.
sāntāpika [*santāpaika] amnf sāntāpikā fit to do penance.

sāntva [*satva] amnf sāntvā kind, comforting — n. consolation, conciliation | phil. conciliation, the first means of overcoming a recalcitrant person; syn. sāman | pl. sāntvāni good words, words of appeasement or comfort — v. [11] pr. (sāntvayati) pfp. (sāntvya) pf. (pari) to console, to comfort; to soothe, to calm. sāntvatas adv. with words of comfort; lovingly. sāntvameva tu bālesu pradhānam prathamo nayah [HV.] The principal means of educating children is first and foremost kindness.
sāntvana [act. sāntva] n. act of appeasement or reconciliation; consolation of g. iic. pl. sāntvanāni id. — f. sāntvanā id.

sāṃdīpani var. Sāndīpani [*saṃdīpana] m. myth. [VP.] np. of the sage Sāndīpani "the Illuminator", preceptor of Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma, Sudāma, Uddhava and Švetaketu₁; his āśrama was located near Uj jayinī; he demanded from Kṛṣṇa as a price for his service the release of his son, imprisoned under the waters of the demon Pañcajana; cf. Ankapāta.

sāndra amnf sāndrā viscous, unctuous, oily; tender; oozing with (i. ic.) | solid, compact, dense; continuous; grouped | strong, robust; intense; vehement; excessive, abundant — i. ic. furnished with, crowned by, full of (i. i. ic.) — n. copse, wood; heap, bunch.
sāmdhya var. sāndhya [*saṃdhyā] amnf sāṃdhyā relating to dawn or dusk; vesperal.

sāṃnidhya var. sānnidhya [*saṃnidhia] n. vicinity, proximity, neighborhood | gram. co-occurrence, collocation. sāmnidhyatas adv. by proximity. sāmnidhyam kṛ appear, present oneself | (causative) cause to come closer. sāmnidhyam yā approach. sāmnidhyam vraj approach. sāmnidhyapakṣe jan take the place of (g.).
sāmnidhyatā [tā] f. proximity, proximity, neighborhood.
sānvaya [sa₁anvaya] amnf sānvayā with the family; with the descendants | relative, close | sensible | of the same occupation.
sāpatna [*sapatna] m. son of a rival wife — f. sāpatnī daughter of a rival wife.
sāpatnya [*sapatnaya] amnf sāpatnyā based on rivalry; born of another wife — m. half-brother; rival, enemy — n. enmity between wives of the same husband | relationship between half-brothers.

sāpavāda [sa₁apavāda] amnf sāpavādā that insults, that contradicts | that causes scandal gram. that has exceptions. sāpavādam adv. reproachfully, with blame. utsargāh sāpavādah the rules have exceptions.
sāpiṇḍya [*sapiṇḍaya] n. degree of consanguinity.

sāpekṣa [sa₁apekṣā] amnf sāpekṣā concerned with, having respect for (iic. loc.) attentive; interested; partial; opp. nirapekṣa | gram. having a dependency or presupposition — f. nirapekṣā interest. sāpekṣam adv. with interest; intentionally.
sāpekṣatā [tā] f. interest | gram. dependence.
sāpekṣatva [tva] n. id.
sāphalya [*saphalaya] n. fertility; profitability; advantage; good result; success.
sābhinaya [sa₁abhinaya] amnf sābhinayā making gestures. sābhinayam by gestures.
sābhra [sa₁abhra] amnf sābhrā cloudy.
sābhramatī [mat] f. geo. np. of the sābhramatī river, which descends from the Arāvalī Mountains in Rājasthāna and crosses Ahmedābād before flowing into the Gulf of Khambhāta; mod. Sābaramatī.
sāma iic. sāman.
sāmaga |ga₂| m. ved. cantor, brāhmaṇa who sings the Sāmaveda | var. sāmagā id. — f. sāmagī wife of a cantor.
sāmagāna |gāna| amnf sāmagānā chantre — n. soc. sung recitation of a hymn, not. from the Sāmaveda; opp. ekaśruti.

sāmavat [vat] amnf sāmavatī related to a hymn — m. lit. [Brahmottarakhanda] np. of the young brah mane Sāmavān who disguised himself as a woman to present himself with his comrade Sumedhā₁ as a couple seeking the favors of Queen Sīmantinī.

Sāmaveda [Veda] m. lit. np. of the Sāmaveda (SV.) or Veda of hymns [sāman], collection of songs, one of the 4 parts of the Veda; there are three schools of singing: kauthuma, rānāyanīya and jaiminīya.

sāmagrī [*samagra] f. totality, wholeness; completeness; not. complete collection, complete equipment, totality of luggage, effects or furniture | phil. set of causal factors of an effect | available means | soc. means required for a ritual. kā te sāmagrī what means do you have at your disposal?

sāmagrya [*samagraya] n. cf. sāmagrī. watchful | conciliation, amicable negotiation | phil. negotiation, one of the stratagems | upāya | to win over an adversary soc. hymn of praise; not. Vedic chant, liturgical melody for the Rigveda, sung by the udgātṛ; syn. stoma | pl. sāmāni cf. sāmaveda. sāmnā i. adv. with kindness, willingly | pl. sāmabhis by friendly means.
sāmanta |*samanta| m. neighbor | soc. vassal, count; district chief (paying tribute to a king) captain, leader | soc. not. prince held hostage by an enemy king — n. neighborhood, surroundings.

sāmayika [*samayaika] amnf sāmayikī usual, customary, conventional | of the same opinion, in agreement | who complies with his commitments | precise, exact; on time, punctual; recurring, periodic; temporary. devi sāmayikā bhavāmaḥ [MAl.] Your Majesty, let us be punctual for the appointment.
sāmayikatva [tva] n. the fact of being conventional. sāmayikatvācchabdārthasampratyayasya gram. [Nyāyasūtra] It is by convention that one associates its meaning with the word.

sāmarthya [*samarthaya] n. conformity, adequacy | that which conforms | sufficient grounds for (loc. iic.) | power, effectiveness; aptitude; capacity to (inf. dat. loc. iic.) | gram. uniqueness of object (syn. ekārthībhāva); agreement (syn. vyapekṣā); co-reference; ability to evoke a specific meaning from the context | bd. [Sarvāstivāda] capacity for causal interaction of a moment of consciousness [dharma] with moments of the past or future; it is distinct from internal activity [kāritra] at a moment of the present. sāmarthyāt according to the circumstances; due to the situation; for this reason | by virtue of the fact that (iic.); as a result of (iic.). sāmarthyatas adv. as the situation requires — ifc. following, in accordance with (iic.). sāmarthyam kṛ to do one's best. sāmarthyam bhaj to strive.
sāmarthyavat |vat| amnf sāmarthyavatī ca pable, puissant.
sāmācārika [*samācāraika] amnf sāmācārikā concerning the rules of good conduct.
Sāmācārī [*samācāra] f. lit. np. of the Sāmācārī, section of the Jaina Kalpasūtra, dealing with monastic discipline.
sāmājika [*samājaika] amnf sāmājikī who is part of an assembly — m. participant; spectator.

sāmānādhikaranya [*samānādhikaraṇaya] n. gram. congruence, agreement; apposition; correlation; coreference, the fact of denoting the same object | phil. [NN.] inherence in the same substrate or receptacle, colocation.

sāmānya [*samāna₂ya] amnf sāmānyā similar, alike; common to several or all common, ordinary, usual — n. identity, similarity; common trait; type, species | phil. [Vaiśeṣika] category [padārtha] of universals or generic substrates; such a substrate can be superior | para | if it is general, like existence [sattā] or inferior [apara₂] if it is less so, like substance

tialité [dravyatva]; cf. anuvrttipratyayahetu | lit. common collection of sacred texts, freely accessible to the 4 social classes; it includes the two epics Mah. and Rām., and the mythological collections |purāṇa|; opp. sāmānyaviśesa. sāmānyatas adv. in a similar way; by analogy in general.
sāmānyaka |ka| ifc. amnf sāmānyakā which is similar to (iic.).

sāmānyakāṇḍa [kāṇḍa] n. lit. np. from the Sāmānyakānda, 3rd volume of the Amarakoşa; it comprises five sections [varga]: viśesyanighnavarga dealing with adjectives, samkīrņavarga dealing with various subjects, nānārthavarga dealing with homonymous words, avyayavarga dealing with indeclinables, and lingādisaṃgrahavarga dealing with the gender of nouns and other miscellaneous subjects.
sāmānyakriyā [kriyā] f. gram. use of a verb in the impersonal voice.
sāmānyalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. phil. [Nyāya] specific perception of recognition of a universal type by its sign (analogy); opp. svalakṣaṇa.
sāmānyaviśeṣa [viśeṣa] n. lit. sacred texts reserved for the 3 classes dvija, including the revealed texts [śruti] (Veda and associated texts) and the collections of law [smṛti] (dharmaśāstra).
sāmānyaspanda [spanda] m. phil. [Trika] universal creative pulse.
sāmānyābhāva [abhāva] m. phil. [Nyāya] inequality, negation; generic absence.
sāmānyatama [super. sāmānya] amnf sāmānyatamā extremely similar, the same.
sāmānyatara [compar. sāmānya] amnf sāmānyatarā more common; very common, banal.
sāmānyatas [adv. sāmānya] adv. in a similar manner; by analogy | in general.
sāmānyatodṛṣṭa [dṛṣṭa] n. phil. [Nyāya] mode of
reasoning [anumāna] by analogy or induction.
sāmānyīya [sāmānyaīya] amnf sāmānyīyā phil. [Nyāya] which concerns the substrate
generic [sāmānya].
sāmāyika [*samayaika] n. equanimity, serenity | [sāmāyikavrata] jn. the practice of meditation, a śikṣāvrata .
sāmāsika [*samāsaika] amnf sāmāsikī concise, succinct, brief | gram. concerning compound words.
sāmí adv. too early; prematurely, in completely | halfway (with pp. ifc.) | lat. semi.
sāmíkṛta [kṛta] amnf sāmikṛtā half finished.
sāmípīta [pīta₁] amnf sāmipītā half drunk.

sāmīpya [*samīpaya] amnf sāmīpyā neighbor, adjoining, connected — n. neighborhood, proximity | gram. time connected to that of the narration | phil. the proximity of God, one of the goals of bhaktiyoga; one of the 4 states of liberation | mukti|; cf. sālokyādicatustaya.
sāmudra₁ [*samudra₁] amnf sāmudrā relating to the sea, maritime, marine — m. marine, na vigator | bio. sea fish; opp. nādeya — n. sea salt.
sāmudra₂ [*samudra₂] n. body mark.
sāmudraka [ka] m. interpreter of bodily signs, diviner.
sāmudrakavidyā [vidyā] f. science of the interpretation of signs and omens [śubhalakṣaṇa].
sāmudrika [ika] amnf sāmudrikā relating to bodily signs — m. soothsayer; syn. samudraka.
sāmudrikalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. definition of bodily signs.
sāmudrikaśāstra [śāstra] n. science of corporeal signs; physiognomy.
sāmūhika [*samūhaika] amnf sāmūhikā gathered en masse, put in ranks — m. gram. suffix forming collective nouns.
sāmprata var. sāmprata [*sampratia] amnf sāmpratā appropriate, adequate, suitable, cor rect | contemporary. sāmpratam var. sāmpratam acc. adv. currently, at present, now; immediately.
sāṃpradāyika var. sāmpradāyika [*sampradāyaika] amnf sāmpradāyikī tra ditionnel; in accordance with tradition — m. SOC. traditionalist; opp. svatantra — n. lit. (text) received; syn. āgata.

Sāmba m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Sāmba or Sāmba, son of Kṛṣṇa and Jāmbavatī; he led a dissolute life in Dvārakā and mocked the devotions of Viśvāmitra, Durvāsā and Nārada; he disguised himself as a pregnant woman and asked them to predict whether he would give birth to a girl or a boy; they condemned him to give birth to an iron stake which would be the downfall of the race of Yadu; Ugrasena had it ground to powder and thrown into the sea, but a piece was found in a fish by a fisherman who sold it to the hunter Jarā₂ who used it to make the point of the arrow with which he killed Kṛṣṇa; Mau, as Durvāsā said, became a leper; he was cured by Sūrya, to whom he built a temple on the banks of the Chenāb.
sāmbadaśamī [daśamī] f. SOC. 10th day of the clear fortnight of the month pausa; on this day we celebrate the sūryapūjā, which celebrates the cure of Sāmba’s leprosy by Sūrya.
Sāmbapurāṇa | purāṇa | n. lit. np. of the Sāmbapurāṇa, a minor tale of olden times [upapurāṇa].
sāmbopapurāṇa [upapurāṇa] n. cf. Sāmbapurāṇa.
sāmmitīya [*sammitiīya] amnf sāmmitīyā hist. community of monks bd. of Sindhu.
sāmmukhya [*sammukhaya] n. the act of being face to face | favor, attraction to g. iic. . sāmmukhyam ādhā to go towards (g.).

sāmya [*samaya] n. equality, identity; perfect agreement (with (i. loc. iic.)) | balance; normal state; evenness of temper, composure; impartiality (towards [pratiloc.]) — amnf sāmyā ordinary, average, normal; impartial. sāmyam i to become identical to, to be one with. sāmyaṃ kṛ to render justice to (loc.). sāmyam nī to calm.
sāmyatā [tā] f. equality.
sāmyatva [tva] n. equality.
sāmrājya [*samrājya] n. sovereignty, universal kingship; empire | supreme power (on g. loc. iic. ).
sāya | act. sā₁ | n. evening, night.

sāyám [acc. sāya] adv. the evening. hyah sāyam adv. last night. sāyam prātar adv. evening and morning, morning and evening. sāyam sāyam adv. every evening. abhi sāyam adv. towards evening. sāyam kr to spend the night.
sāyāhan |ahan| n. in the evening — m. sāyāhna id.
sāyaka m. projectile, arrow. his laksyacyutasāyako'bhūt his arrow missed its mark.

Sāyaṇa m. hist. np. of Sāyaṇa or Sāyaṇācārya, younger brother of Mādhavācārya, minister of King Harihara₂ of Vijayanagara, student of Samkarānanda, scholar and commentator of Vedic texts, and notably of the Rigveda, (~1315–1387); cf. Mādhavīyadhātuvrtti, Vedārthaprakāśa, Bhāratītīrtha, Subhāṣitanidhi.
sāyana [sa₁ayana] n. astr. tropical zodiac | "with movement" |, related to the terrestrial year; opp. nirayana.
sāyam [acc. sāya] adv. The evening.
sāyaṃsaṃdhyā |saṃdhyā| f. sunset rite.
sāyantana [tana] amnf sāyamtanī evening.
sāyantanasnāna |snāna| n. evening bath.
sāyamaśana [aśana₂] n. evening meal.

sāyujya [*sayujya] n. union, communion with, absorption into (g. loc.) | phil. absorption into the Divine Essence, union with God; ultimate goal of jñānayoga; one of the 4 states of liberation | mukti|; cf. sālokyādicatustaya.

sāra [agt. sṛ] amnf sārā precious, excellent; essential; solid, strong — act. mn kernel, Essence; mælle, quintessence; the best of something | solid part of a body | sap; cream, ointment; nectar | resin; serosity; flow, effusion, pus; excrement | med. one of the 7 constituents of the body, whose proportion determines the temperament: sattva intelligence, śukra sperm, majjan marrow, asthi bones, medas fat, māmsa flesh, and rakta blood | fortune, wealth; strength, vigor, power; energy; firmness, hardness; resistance; solidity | pawn in the game of chess | lit. som mayor; summary; extract — f. sārī ifc. constituted essentially of, which has the Essence of (iic.); full of (i.) || lat. serum. candanasāra Sandalwood essence. khadirasāra Essence of cachou. sārāt sāram the cream of the crop. tūṣṇīm sāraḥ essentially silent. dharmasāram jagat The World rests on Justice.
sāratā [tā] f. solidity.
Sāranātha [nātha] m. geo. np. of Sāranātha, a place north of Vārāṇasī, where Buddha revealed his teachings through his first sermon, in the gazelle park.
sārabhāṇḍa | bhāṇḍa | n. precious thing, treasure.
sārabhāṇḍabhūmigṛha [bhūmigṛha] n. soc. ca chot where the queen imprisons her rivals.

sārabhūta [bhūta] amnf sārabhūtā essential; excellent — n. essential thing, quintessence. anantaśāstram bahuveditavyam alpaśca kālo ba havaśca vighnāḥ | yatsārabhūtam tadupāsitavyam hamso yathā kṣīramivāmbumiśram | | Uttaragītā| The works worth studying are innumerable, life is short and obstacles are many; what one needs to know is the essential, like the hamsa who knows how to separate milk from water.
sāravat [vat] amnf sāravatī strong, solid; resilient | substantial; nourishing; full of sap | containing the essential (teaching) | precious.
sāravattā [tā] f. strength, vigor, resilience | solidity (not. arrow).
sārasaṃgraha |saṃgraha| mr. bed. |Tantra| n.p. of the Sārasaṃgraha, compendium of Vaiṣṇava ritual.
sarasamuccaya |samuccaya| mr. bed. n.p. of the Sārasamuccaya Tantra, collection of Nārāyaṇa rituals.
sārāvalī |āvalī| f. lit. title of works.
sārāsāra [asāra] amnf sārāsārā relatively substantial; more or less strong — n. relative strength; more or less good quality.
sāroddhāra | uddhāra | m. receptacle of flow; collection of the Essence of a matter — ifc. lit. "quintessence of" | title of works.

Sāranga [*saranga] amnf sārangī speckled, mottled | bio. Jacobin cuckoo; syn. cātaka — m. myth. np. of Sāranga or Sāranga, bow of Viṣṇu, fashioned by Viśvakarmā; cf. cf. pañcayuddha, hum bio. zoo. Cucculus melanoleucus or zoo. Clama tor jacobinus, Jacobin cuckoo, black and white bird; always thirsty, it is said to feed on raindrops; syn. cātaka — f. sārangī mus. stringed instrument (sarangi).
sārangabaka | baka | m. bio. zoo. Ardea sarunga, great black-necked crane.

Sāraṇa [agt. sṛ] amnf sāraṇī cracked, split; that which leaks — act. m. diarrhea, dysentery; leak autumn wind myth. [Mah.] np. of the prince vṛṣṇi Sāraṇa "Swift", son of Vasudeva — amnf sāranī stream. sāraņika |ika| mf sāraņikā traveler; peddler.
sārathi [*sarathai] m. coachman — ifc. one who guides, who directs (iic.).
sārathya [*sarathaya] n. condition of co-cher; act of driving like a coachman.
sāramaya |sāramaya| amnf sāramayī very firm, very solid | consisting of the best part of g. .
sārameya [*saramāīya] m. ["son of His ramā" | dog.
Sārala [*Sarala] amnf sāralā relating to Sa rala — m. bed. n.p. of the Sārala Mahābhārata, due to Sarala.
saraśana |*saraśana| mr. cf. sarasana.
sārasa [*sarasa] mf sārasī bio. zoo. Grus antigone, large crane from northern India.
sārasana [related to sāraśana] mn sheath, cor set; belt (not. military); chest armor.

sārasvatá [*sarasvata] amnf sārasvatī relating to Sarasvān, Sarasvatī, or Sarasvatī₁ | of the land of the Sārasvatās | eloquent; learned — m. bilva wood staff | lit. poetic inspiration, literary creativity | myth. |Harṣacarita| np. of the sage | ṛṣi | Sārasvata, son of Dadhīci and Sarasvatī; he was raised by his aunt Akṣamālikā with his own son Vatsa₂; he transmitted his knowledge to Vatsa₂, and established him in Prītikūṭa where he gave rise to the Vātsyāyana race | pl. Sārasvatās geo. np. of the Sārasvatās people, who lived on the banks of the saras vatī₁ | soc. tribe of brahmins originating from this region; they claim to be descendants of Sārasvata; the learned brahmins [paṇḍita] of Kaśmīra are Sārasvatās | mod. community of brahmins from the region of Goa and the northern coast of Karṇāṭaka; they follow the dvaita doctrine of Madhvācārya; cf. Citrapura.
sārasvatīprakriyā [prakriyā] f. gram. the sārasvatīprakriyā grammar of np. of Anubhūtisvarūpācārya, also called Sārasvatavyākarana.
sārika [sāraika] mf sārikā bio. zoo. Turdus salica, blackbird | organic. zoo. Gracula religiosa, mynah; syn. śārikā — f. sārikā confidante.
sārin [agt. sr] amnf sārinī who runs, who hurries — ifc. who pursues (iic.) — f. sāriņī stream; canal.
Sārisṛkta m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Sārisṛkta one of the śārngakās; hymns of the Rgveda are attributed to him.

sārūpya [*sarūpaya] n. the fact of having the same form as, similarity, resemblance to (g.) phil. conformity with the Divine Essence, the fact of being in the image of God; one of the 4 states of liberation [mukti]; cf. sālokyādicatustaya.

sāropa [sa₁āropa] amnf sāropā lit. el liptic, requiring an additional argument — f. sāropā lit. [Mukula] metaphor [lakṣaṇā] with superimposition of the figurative meaning on the literal meaning; it expresses the figure of speech rūpaka . mukham candrah face (similar to) the Moon (criterion of beauty).
sārtha [sa₁artha] amnf sārthā rich; profitable; significant, sensible; successful — m. cara vane; company, troop, enterprise.
arthasārthaḥ ["caravan of ideas"] the train of thoughts.
sārthaka |ka| amnf sārthakā useful; significant | successful | gram. that makes sense.
sārthakaśabda [śabda] m. gram. meaning linguistic; it includes the lexical bases [prakṛti], the affixes [pratyaya] and the particles [nipāta].
sārthavat [vat] amnf sārthavatī intensional; significant.
sārthavāha | vāha | mr. caravanner; merchant.

sārdha [sa₁ardha] amnf sārdhā increased by half. sārdham adv. by half, with, in the company of (i.); together. sārdham ādā to take with oneself. brāhmaṇaiḥ sārdham with the priests. dveśate sārdhe 250.
sārpa [*sarpa] amnf sārpā relating to serpents.
sārva [*sarva] amnf sārvā good for all; general, universal.

sārvadhātuka [*sarvadhātuka] amnf sārvadhātukā gram. ["proper to any root"] refers to the verbal endings of the tenses of the present system (present, imperfect, imperative and optative); also of the aorist, future and conditional; opp. ārdhadhātuka.

Sārvabhauma [*sarvabhūmia] amnf sārvabhaumā universal — m. ["king of all the earth" Emperor; cf. Lalitāditya | myth. np. of the celestial elephant Sārvabhauma "Emperor", dig gaja of the north, in the service of Kubera | hist. np. of the logician Vāsudeva₃ Sārvabhauma, Bengali master of the 15th century, author of the Sārvabhaumanirukta | hist. np. of the logician Rāmabhadra₁ Sārvabhauma; to him we owe the Padārthatattvavivecanaprakāśa — n. universal sovereignty.
Sarvabhaumanirukta | nirukta | n. bed. | Nyāya | n.p. of the Sārvabhaumanirukta, work of Vāsudeva₃ Sārvabhauma.
sārvalaukika [*sarvalokaika] amnf sārvalaukikī phil. in accordance with usual experience; of common, universal use.
sārvalaukikapratyaya [pratyaya] m. everyday experience; common sense.
sārvavarņika [*sarvavarņaika] amnf sārvavarņikā soc. which is suitable for the entire population.
sārṣṭi [sa₁ārṣa] amnf of the same rank or condition.
sārṣṭitā [tā] f. equality of rank or value | phil. attainment of Divine rank, attainment of Divine Power, one of the 4 states of liberation | mukti|; cf. sālokyādicatustaya.
sārstya [ya] n. id.
sāla [śāla] m. organic. bot. Shorea robusta, Sāl tree; syn. śāla.
sālagrāma [grāma] m. cf. śālagrāma.
sālaka |sa₁alaka| amnf sālakā adorned with locks of hair.
sālaṅkāyana m. myth. patr. of ṛṣi Sālankāyana or Śālankāyana, son of Viśvāmitra.
sālasa [sa₁alasa] amnf sālasā languid, indolent; lazy; without energy, weary, tired.

sālokya [*salokaya] n. cohabitation with, the state of being in the same world, the same country, in the same place as (gisaha₂ iic.) | phil. immersion in the Supreme Being [brahman]; cohabitation with the Divine Essence, the state of being in the presence of God, one of the goals of bhaktiyoga; one of the 4 states of liberation |mukti|; cf. sālokyādicatustaya.

sālokyādicatuṣṭaya [ādicatuṣṭaya] n. phil. the 4 stages of liberation [mukti]: the proximity of God [sāmīpya], the being in the presence of God [sālokya], the being in the image of God [sārūpya], the absorption in the Divine Essence [sāyujya]; sometimes the attainment of Divine Power |sārstitā| is added.
sāva [act. su₂] m. ved. libation of soma.

sāvadhāna [sa₁avadhāna] amnf sāvadhānā attentive (to (loc.)), vigilant, prudent | who intends to (inf.) — v. [11] pr. (sāvadhānayati) to pay attention, to be on one's guard. sāvadhānam adv. attentively; prudently. sāvadhānībhū to pay attention (to (loc.)). sāvadhānīkī to warn, to put on one's guard.
sāvadhānatā |tā| f. attention, caution.
sāvana [*savana₁] amnf sāvanā soc. which determines the 3 daily libations of soma — m. patron of a sacrifice — n. true solar time.
sāvayava [sa₁avayava] amnf sāvayavā composed of parts | phil. of limited extension; not eternal.
sāvarņa [*savarṇa] amnf sāvarṇā which is of the same colour or caste as phon. homophone (said of phonemes of the same position of articulation) — m. cf. sāvarni.
sāvarni [*savarṇai] m. myth. n.p. of sāvarṇa or Sāvarņi, son of Sūrya and Chāyā, 8ᵉ Manu of the kalpa.
sāvarṇya [*savarṇaya] n. identity of colour or caste | phon. homophony of phonemes.
sāvaśesa [sa₁avaśesa] amnf sāvaśesā incomplete, unfinished — n. remainder, residue. sāvaśeṣam adv. to the end. śrnu me sāvaśeṣam vacah listen to my speech to the end.

Sāvitrá [*savitṛa] amnf Sāvitrī₁ related to the Sun; descendant of the Sun (designates various celestial beings) — m. myth. [Rām.] not. np. of Sāvitra, epithet of the Light Prabhāsa, eighth vasu; he pulverized the rākṣasa Sumāli with his club — f. Sāvitrī₁ lit. one of the most sacred hymns of the Rigveda, praising Savitā; syn. gāyatrī | myth. np. of Sāvitrī₁ the Instigator, wife of Savitā; she is the muse personifying inspiration and intuition myth. [Mah.] np. of Sāvitrī₁, wife of Satyavān; She asked Surya not to get up so that Yama wouldn't come and take her husband, who had been bitten by a deadly snake; she represents the model of marital love; she is celebrated on the full moon of
jyaistha [vaṭapūrṇimā] with the vaṭasāvitrīpūjā.
sāsru [sa₁asru] amnf in tears; shedding tears — adv. in tears.
sāśrunetra [netra] amnf sāśrunetrā with eyes filled with tears.

sāṣṭāṅga [sa₁aṣṭāṅga] amnf sāṣṭāṅgī ["with the eight limbs"] at full length (describes the prostration where the hands, feet, knees, chest and forehead touch the ground). sāṣṭāṅgam adv. in prostration at full length.
sāṣṭiká [*ṣaṣṭika] amnf sāṣṭikā aged 60 years.
sāsnā f. dewlap (characteristic sign |lakṣaṇa| of cattle).
sāsnāvat |vat| amnf sāsnāvatī phil. | "belly-bearer"] qualifies the cattle by its characteristic sign | lakṣaṇa|.
sāsnāvattva [vat] n. phil. [Vaiśeṣika] universal of cattle; syn. gotva.
sāh [ca. sah₁] v. [10] pr. (sāhayati) to bear, to endure.
sāhaṃkāra |sa₁ahaṃkāra| amnf sāhaṃkārā selfish; vain; self-satisfied, arrogant.
sāhaṃkāratā [tā] f. vanity; arrogance.
sāhaṃkṛta [sa₁ahaṃkṛta] amnf sāhaṃkṛtā smug, arrogant.

sāhacarya [*sahacaraya] n. company, society, association (with (i. iic.)) | gram. disambiguation by colocation of an associated word; e.g. in rāmalakṣmaṇau, Lakṣmaṇa allows Rāma to be identified without confusion with Paraśurāma or Balarāma.
sāhaya |agt. ca. sah₁| amnf sāhayā who supports, who endures.

sāhasa [*sahasa] amnf sāhasā hasty, thoughtless; bold, reckless; imprudent — n. audacity, recklessness; haste; violence, aggression, cruelty; hatred. mā sāhasam no imprudence. sāhase śrīḥ prativasati fortune smiles on the bold.
Sāhasānka | anka | m. np. of Sāhasānka "Intrepid", epith. of King Vikramāditya.
sāhasika [sāhasaika] amnf sāhasikī au dacieux, réméraire; impétueux, fiergueux | brutal, féroce, cruel.
sāhasrá [*sahasra] amnf sāhasrā f. sāhasrī composed of a thousand parts; very numerous — n. thousand. sāhasreņa adv. by thousands.
sāhasraka [sāhasraka] amnf sāhasrikā consisting of a thousand.
sāhāyaka [*sahāyaka] n. aid, help.
sāhāyya [*sahāya] n. help, aid. sāhāyyam kṛ to give assistance. sāhāyyam sthā id.
sāhāyyārtha [artha] m. occupation to carry one's course.
sāhitya [*sahita₂ya] n. state of being together, union, unity | rhetoric; poetic art; literary composition, literature.
sāhityadarpaṇa |darpaṇa| m. lit. np. from sāhityadarpaṇa, a work of poetics by Viśvanātha₁ Kavirāja (14th century).

Sāhityaratnākara [ratnākara] m. lit. np. of the Sāhityaratnākara "Mine of jewels of poetic art", work of poetics due to Dharmasūri (15th century), in 10 chapters [taranga]; also called Sāhityaratnākaramīmāmsā.
sāhityotsava [utsava] m. mod. festival.
√ si v. [9] pr. ( āti) pp. ( āt) pf. (vi) v. [5] pr. (sinoti) to bind, to attach; to hinder — ca. (sāyáyati) to cause to be attached.
simhá [related to himsa] m. Lion | astr. sign zo

diacal [rāśi] of the Lion | myth. [Mahāvaṃśa] np. of Simha "the Lion", mythical ancestor of the Singhalais [Siṃhalās]; it is said that he married Suppadevī, prince of Vanga; he lived in a cave closed by a rock; Suppadevī escaped from it with his son and daughter; later his son Siṃhabāhu returned to kill him with an arrow | arch. the Lion, a matrix | yoni | of the āyādi system | lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādhara king Simha₁, husband of Dhanavatī — ifc. the first, the best of (iic.) ("a Lion among the") — f. siṃhī lioness.
Simhaghosa | ghosa | m. roar | lit. | DKC. | np. of Prince Simhaghosa, son of King Candasimha; cf. Kāmapāla.
siṃhatā [tā] f. leonine nature.

Simhatilaka | tilaka | mr. hist. n.p. of the Jain mathematician and astronomer Simhatilaka Sūri; he lived in Vijāpur in Gujarat in the 13th century; he is the author of commentaries on the Ganitatilaka and the Bhuva nadīpaka.
simhatva [vat] n. leonine nature
simhadeva | deva | mr. hist. n.p. of simhadeva, king of Kaśmīra (1286–1301); he succeeded Lakṣmaṇadeva (1273–1286); his Damara dynasty replaced the Lo hara; Sūhadeva succeeded him.
siṃhanāda | nāda | m. roar | bd. teaching of the Dharma by the Buddha.

Simhapura [pura] n. geo. np. of Simhapura "Lion City"; several ancient cities bear this name, not. in Lāṭa and Kalinga | mod. np. of Simhapūr or Singapore, the "Lion City" — f. siṃhapurī cf. vikramasimhapurī.

siṃhabāhu [bāhu] m. myth. np. of King Siṃhabāhu "with the Lion's arms", son of the Lion Simha; he killed his father for a reward, and was offered the throne of Vanga, but created his own capital Simhapura in Kalinga; he married his own sister, with whom he had 32 children; he banished his eldest son dis solu Vijaya₂, who went to sea with 700 companions to become simhala the founder of Ceylon |Simhaladvīpa|.
siṃhabhūpāla [bhūpāla] m. hist. n.p. of king Siṃhabhūpāla of the Recarla Velama dynasty of Rācakoṇḍa in the Andhra country (14th century); he is the author of the play Ratnapañcālikā.
simhavarman [varman] m. hist. np. of king Siṃhavarmā₁ Pallava (275–300) | hist. np. of the Buddhist king Simhavarmā₁ Pallava (436–477) | lit. |DKC.| np. of king Siṃhavarmā king of Campā.

Simhastha |stha| m. astr. said of Jupiter entering the sign of Leo | soc. np. of the festival of Simhastha, pilgrimage to Ujjayinī of kumbhamela, with bathing in the Ksiprā; it begins at the full moon of caitra and ends at that of vaiśākha.
siṃhādivarga |ādi| m. pl. | "lions, etc." | animals.
simhādivarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Bhūmyādikānda, dealing with animals.
simhāvalokana [avalokana] n. retrospective look (not. on the work of a lifetime); re-examination.
simhāvalokananyāya ["maxim of the Lion's gaze"] which looks back to see what it has left behind.

siṃhāsana [āsana] n. royal throne (with armrests decorated with Lion heads) | phil. [yoga] "Lion" posture: seated cross-legged, each ankle under the opposite testicle, hands placed on the knees, fingers spread, mouth wide open, tongue hanging out, in eye concentration [nāsāgradṛṣṭi].

simhāsanadvātrimśikā [dvātrimśikā] f. lit. np. of the Siṃhāsanadvātriṃśikā or Siṃhāsana dvātrimsikakathā, a collection of 32 prose tales in praise of King Vikramāditya; each exploit is recounted by one of the nymphs supporting his magic throne, which emerged from the earth when Bhoja₁ sat upon it; the work expresses that only a king possessing all the virtues of Vikramāditya deserves the throne; the original is lost; one recension is by the author Ksemendra, another is attributed to Vararuci; syn. Vikramacarita, Dvātrimsatputtalikā.
siṃhāsanabhraṣṭa [bhraṣṭa] afmn simhāsanabhrastā dethroned.

simhala [simhala] m. bd. np. of simhala "of the race of the Lion", father of the merchant Vijaya₂, grandson of simha; he had gone to sea in search of precious stones with 700 noble companions; they were shipwrecked, and landed on the island of Ceylon [Tāmradvīpa] on the day that Buddha passed into parinirvāṇa ; they were welcomed there by the ogresses [rākṣasī] who transformed themselves into pretty nymphs to seduce them; the accomplished [bodhisattva] Lokesvara came to save them in the form of the flying horse Balāha; they had to fly away with him, with their eyes closed, without yielding to the calls of the nymphs; only simhala had faith and was saved; the island of Ceylon bears his name in his honor | |simhādvīpa | geo. Ceylon | pl. Simhalās np. of the Simhalās, the Singha lais.
siṃhaladvīpa | dvīpa | m. geo. np. of Siṃhaladvīpa, the island of Ceylon.
siṃhikā [siṃhaika] f. myth. np. from the Asurī simhikā "Lioness", sister of Hiranyakaśipu, wife of Vipracitti, mother of Rāhu.
sikatā f. pl. sikatās sand || lat. siccus.
sikatila [sikatāila] amnf sikatilā sa blond.
siktá |pp. sic| amnf siktā spread, poured; watered, moistened.
siktasammṛṣṭa [saṃmṛṣṭa] amfn siktasammṛṣṭā mixed by pouring.
siktha [related to sikta] mn cooked drained rice; rice ball — n. wax.
sikthavartinī | vartin| f. mod. candle.
Singhana m. hist. np. of King Singhana, of the Yādavās dynasty, grandson of Bhillama; he reigned in Devagiri from (1210–1247).

√ (ásicat) pp. (sikta) pf. (abhi, ava, ā, ut, upa, ni) to pour, to spread, to make flow (not. jala, retas) | to water, to sprinkle, to moisten (with (i.)) — ps. (sicyate) to be poured, to flow — ca. (secayati) to spread, to water || all. seichen. payasā siñcati he waters with water.
sitá₁ [pp. si] amnf Sitā bound, tied, chained; captive | accompanied by (i.).

sita₂ [related to asita] amnf Sitā white, clear, bright; limpid — m. the color white | astr. the "clear fortnight" [śuklapakṣa] — f. Sitā myth. np. of the Sitā, a divyagangā; it is a branch of the Milky Way or celestial Ganges [Mandākinī].
sitadhyāna [dhyāna] n. jn. pure meditation; syn. śukladhyāna.
sitavarman [varman] n. lit. [DKC.] np. of Si tavarmā, hereditary minister of King Rājahamsa; Sumati₃ and Somadatta₂ are his sons.
sitotpala | utpala | n. organic. bot. Nelumbium specio sum, white day lotus.
sitopala | upala | mn | "white stone" | chalk; rock crystal — f. sitopalā refined sugar.
siti [act. si] f. act of binding, attaching.

Siddha₁ [pp. sidh₁] amnf siddhā Accomplished, realized; earned, obtained; perfect | who has achieved their goal, realized their objective, accomplished their mission | finished, on time, ready; not. rice | stable, immutable, eternal; syn. nitya; opp. kārya | phil. who has attained the supreme goal | endowed with supernatural virtues, marvelous, magical — m. who has attained perfection; saint, blessed | magician; expert phil. Accomplished, human being who has become immortal and omniscient after attaining liberation | mokṣa|, and endowed with magical powers | siddhi|; the siddhās inhabit Bhuvar, the Between Heaven and Earth gram. (rule) mutually applicable soc. effi cace (mantra, rite) — n. magic, supernatural | hist. writing derived from brāhmī; cf. siddhamātṛkā. iti siddham fin; j'en ai fini | phil. [Nyāya] QED. arthaprāptiśca pratyakṣasiddhā [Viśvanātha₁] Only the acquisition of wealth is evidence of success.
siddha₂ [pp. sidh₂] amnf siddhā prevented, set aside, repelled.
siddhakāṇḍa |kāṇḍa| n. gram. part of the Aştādhyāyī preceding the second section of the eighth book; the order of application of its rules depends on criteria of priority; opp. asiddhakānda.
siddhagraha [graha] m. phil. [Tantra] possession by an Accomplished.

siddhatā [tā] f. perfection | phil. condition of a being Accomplished [Siddha₁] | validity (of a doctrine, a rule) | fact of being recognized or understood | gram. character Accomplished of an action; opp. sādhyatā.
siddhatva [tva] n. id.
siddhapada [pada] n. gram. word whose meaning is known.
siddhapadasāmnidhya [sāmnidhya] n. gram. the act of disambiguating a word by collocation.
siddhapura [pura] nf siddhapurī myth. np. of siddhapura or siddhapurī, city of the accomplished; it is often located in the far North.
siddhaprāya [prāya] amnf siddhaprāyā almost Perfected.

siddhamātṛkā [mātṛkā] f. syllabic script derived from brāhmī; it is at the origin of the writing of maithilī, then of Bengali, Burmese and Tibetan; it was exported to China in the 8th century with Buddhism; from there it passed to Japan where it gave rise to the kana phonetic alphabet.
siddhayoga [yoga] m. phil. [Tantra] realization of miraculous acts through the practice of yoga.
Siddhayogeśvaratantra [īśvaraTantra] n. bed. n.p. from the Siddhayogeśvaratantra, tantr work. about yoga.
Siddhayogeśvarīmata [īśvarīmata] n. bed. n.p. of the Siddhayogeśvarīmata, a work of the Kaula doctrine.
siddharasa | rasa | m. mercury | alchemist; magician.

Siddharāja [rāja] m. hist. n.p. of king Jayasimha Sid dharāja "Accomplished", of the Caulukya dynasty (12th century); he reigned at Anahilapāṭaka in Gurjara; he made a military campaign on Avantī in Mālava to bring back as booty the Sanskrit library founded by king Bhojadeva. Siddharşi [rṣi] m. hist. n.p. by the Jain poet and philosopher Siddharși Gaṇī, author of the Upamitibhava prapañcakathā (10th century).
siddhaśabdārṇava [śabdaarṇava] m. lit. np. from the siddhaśabdārṇava, dictionary of synonyms of Sahajakīrti; only fragments of it are known.
siddhasāra [sāra] mn lit. np. from siddhasāra "Knowledge of the humors", a medical treatise [āyurveda] attributed to Ravigupta (circa 650).

Siddhasiddhāntapaddhati [Siddhāntapaddhati] f. bed. n.p. from the Siddhasiddhāntapaddhati "Manual of Accomplished Doctrine", an ancient hathayoga text, attributed to Gorakṣanātha; he describes the renunciant [avadhūta] as capable of embodying all social roles, from king to ascetic.
Siddhahemacandra | hemacandra | mr. bed. n.p. from Siddhahemacandra or Siddhahemasabdānusāsana “(grammar of) hemacandra (dedicated to) Sid dharāja”.
siddhahemaśabda [hemaśabda] iic. lit. grammar of hema (candra) dedicated to Siddha (rāja).

Siddhahemaśabdānuśāsana [anuśāsana] n. lit. np. of the Siddhahemaśabdānuśāsana, synthesis of the grammars of Sanskrit due to hemacandra, on the command of King Siddharāja, who had it copied by 300 scribes; it is also called siddhahaima and Siddha hemacandra; its first 7 chapters [adhyāya] concern Sanskrit, the 8th is a grammar of prākṛta.
siddhahaima [haima₂] m. cf. Siddhahemacandra.
siddhācārya [ācārya] m. bd. [Vajrayāna] magician.

Siddhānta [anta] m. supreme goal; conclusion axiom, truism; dogma, doctrine; knowledge; teaching | generic name of certain treatises (not. math. ast. and gram.) phil. ["conclusive argumentation"] tantric texts. Shaivite Siddhānta respecting Brahmanical purity, of dualistic tendency; Shiva reveals in it the Knowledge which leads to liberation; cf. Kāmika.

siddhāntakaumudī [kaumudī] m. bed. n.p. from the siddhāntakaumudī “Elucidation of the doctrine” (from the grammar of Pāṇini); its author is Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita (17th century); his student Varadarāja₁ made a simplified version for students, the Laghu siddhāntakaumudī; cf. Laghukaumudi, Tattvabod hinī, Sabdenduśekhara.
siddhāntabindu [bindu] m. lit. du np. siddhāntabindu de Madhusūdana₁ Sarasvatī₂, also called Siddhāntatattvabindu; it is a commentary on the Daśaślokī de Saṃkara₁.
Siddhāntamuktāvalī [muktāvalī] f. n.p. of the Siddhāntamuktāvalī; cf. bed. Nyāyasiddhāntamuktāvalī.
siddhāntalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. phil. [Nyāya] exact definition; accepted definition.
siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi [śikhāmaṇi] m. bed. n.p. from Siddhāntaśikhāmani, a vīraśaiva text from the 8th century, due to Sivayogī Sivācārya.

siddhāntaśiromaṇi [śiromaṇi] m. math. np. from the Siddhāntaśiromani "Coronation of Science", treatise on mathematics and astronomy by Bhāskarācārya₂; it comprises 4 parts: Līlāvatī (arithmetic calculation), Bījagaņita (algebra), Grahaganitādhyāya (calculation of the planets) and Golādhyāya (spherical trigonometry applied to the terrestrial and celestial globes).
siddhāntasārāvalī [sārāvalī] f. bed. n.p. of siddhāntasārāvalī, metrical treatise of the śaivasiddhānta due to Trilocanaśiva Acārya.
siddhāntasundara [sundara] m. math. n.p. from the siddhāntasundara, treatise by Jñānarāja (around 1500).
siddhāntin [in] amnf siddhāntinī expert (in science, grammar or sacred texts) | soc. adept of the siddhānta doctrine.
siddhāyatana |āyatana| n. soc. sanctuary serving as a place of penance.

siddhārtha [artha] amnf siddhārthā who is successful, who succeeds, effective; who has achieved the goal — m. bd. np. of the Nepalese prince siddhārtha Gautama "the Accomplished", who would become the Buddha.
siddhārthin [arthin] m. astr. n.p. of Siddhārthī "who seeks Perfection", personifying year 53 of a life cycle [samvatsara].
siddhāvasthāpanna [avasthāpanna] n. gram. per fective; opp. sādhyāvasthāpanna.
siddhāvasthāpannabhāva | bhāva | m. gram. meaning of an action noun as a completed action.
siddhāsana [āsana] n. [Yoga] Perfect posture.
siddheśvara [īśvara] m. bio. bot. Delonix regia, gulmohar tree, legume, with large red/orange flowers.

Siddhi₁ [act. sidh₂] f. accomplishment, acquired perfection, skill; making, preparation (of food) | efficiency, success, achievement | phil. [Nyāya] demonstration, proof, conclusion, validity | perfect science, knowledge | chance, advantage,

prosperity | phil. | Yoga | supernatural power, then magical power; one of the 8 canonical supernatural powers; cf. astasiddhi | phil. | Tantra | noun of Siddhi₁ "Perfect", one of the 8 divine powers [yoginī] | phil. [Sāṃkhya] means of Perfection of the scholar; there are 8 of them | math. symb. the number 8 | myth. noun of Siddhi₁, Perfection personified, daughter of Prajāpati | myth. [SP.] noun of Siddhi₁, wife of Ganesha, by whom she bore Ksema. siddhir astu (blessing formula concluding an edict) so be it. ūhaḥ śabdo 'dhyayanam duḥkhavighātās trayaḥ suhrtprāptihdānam ca siddhayo 'ṣṭau [Sāṃkhya] the eight means of Perfection are reflection, speech (of the master), study, suppression of the three aspects of misery, discussion with relatives, and giving.

Siddhicandra [candra] m. hist. np. of the Jaina renunciant Siddhicandra "Full Moon" (1587–1666); this scholar of Sanskrit, of great intelligence and beauty, a pupil of Bhānucandra, was an intimate of the court of the Mughal emperors.
siddhitraya [traya] n. lit. np. of the Siddhi₁ traya "Triple knowledge", phil. work of Yāmunācārya (10th century); it had a great influence on his student Rāmānuja.
siddhida [da] amnf siddhidā which confers happiness — m. myth. form of Bhairava.
Siddhidātrī [dātrī] f. myth. np. of Siddhidātrī, epith. of Durgā "who gives Perfection".
siddhiprāya [prāya] amnf siddhiprāyā almost perfect.
siddhimat |mat| amnf siddhimatī who has achieved Perfection.
siddhilakṣmī [lakṣmī] f. myth. [kaula] np. of siddhilakṣmī, terrible aspect [mahāvidyā] of the Goddess [Sakti], also called Kamalā; main Newar deity in Nepal, its main temple is in Bhaktapura.
siddhivināyaka [vināyaka] m. myth. np. of Siddhi vināyaka, epith. of Gaņeśa "Master of powers".

√ ; sidh₂ ; v. ; [4] ; pr. ; (sidhyati) ; pft. ; (sisedha) ; pp. (siddha₁) pf. (pra, sam) to succeed, to achieve, to reach the goal | to have value, to be demonstrated, to be valid, to follow — ca. (sādháyati) cf. sādh. ișavah sidhyanti lakșye cale the arrows reach the moving target. vinā puruṣakāreṇa divam na sidhyati help yourself, Heaven will help you.
√ sidh₂ v. [1] pr. (sedhati) aor. [5] (asedht) pp. (siddha₂) pf. (apa, ut, ni, prati) to push, to drive away, to repel, to remove, to prevent.
sidhmá amnf sidhmā which has white spots; leper — m. leprosy; there are 18 cases — n. leprosy spot — f. sidhmā med. leprosy lesion.
sidhmalá |la| amnf sidhmalā med. leper — f. sidhmalā med. type of leprosy.
Sidhya [act. sidh₂] m. astr. np. of Sidhya "Deliverance" or "Success", one of the names of the nakşatra Pusya the Cancer.
Sinīvālī f. ved. np. of Sinīvālī, a goddess of fertility; she presides over the first day of the new moon.

sinduvāra [sindhuvāra] m. bio. bot. Vitex negundo, aromatic shrub, labiate with opposite leaves in 5 leaflets, with violet flowers in long panicles; used in medicine; syn. nirguṇḍī — n. its berry, ovoid, black.

sindūra n. minium; vermilion | soc. its color is symbolic of the brahmacārin; images of Hanuman and Gaņeśa are painted with it; this lead salt is also used in medicine, not. to heal wounds — f. sindūrī red garment.
sindūrita [ita] amnf sindūritā covered with mini nium, vermilion red.

Sindhu f. river, stream (in gen.) — mf the Indus; it is a sacred river [divyagangā] — m. the sea, the ocean | geo. np. of Sindhu, Indus valley | pl. sindhavas the inhabitants of Sindhu || fr. Indus, India, Hindu.

sindhudatta | datta | amnf sindhudattā given by the river — f. sindhudattā lit. [DKC.] np. of sindhudattā, daughter of the merchant Vaiśravaṇa₁, sister of Sāgaradattā; she married the minister Padmodb hava; Viśruta is their son.

sindhudvīpa [dvīpa] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Sind hudvīpa, king of Ayodhyā, son of Srutanābha, father of Ayutāyu, ancestor of Raghu and therefore of Rāma | myth. np. of sindhudvīpa₁, son of Jahnu, also called Aja₁; by his penances at the pilgrimage of Pṛthūdakatīrtha he is said to have attained the status of brah mane; he is father of Balākāśva.

sindhurāja |rāja| m. hist. np. of sindhurāja, king Paramāra who reigned in Dhārā at the end of the 10th century; he succeeded his elder brother Muñja; Bhojadeva and Udayāditya are his sons; cf. Padmagupta.
sindhulipi [lipi] f. comic writing. sāṃmitīya monks; syn. sandhavī.

sindhuvāra [vāra] m. bio. bot. Vitex negundo, ar aromatic shrub with opposite leaves in 5 leaflets, with purple flowers in long panicles; used in medicine; syn. nirguṇḍī, sinduvāra — n. its berry, ovoid, black.
sip nota. gram. modifier [vikaraṇa₂] of subjunctive formation [let].
sipra m. sweat, perspiration — f. cf. sipra.
siprā [f. sipra] f. geo. np. of the river siprā, flowing at Ujjayinī; cf. Kṣiprā.
sirā [sr] f. watercourse; drain, narrow channel | med. body vessel; vein, artery, nerve; tendon.
siṣaṃgrāmayiṣu var. sisaṃgrāmayiṣu [agt. des. saṃgrāma] amnf who wants war, eager to fight.
siṣādhayiṣ [des. sādh] v. pr. (siṣādhayiṣati) to want to prevail.
siṣādhayiṣā [act. des. sādh] f. desire to convince | phil. [Nyāya] intention to make an inference.
siṣādhayiṣu [agt. des. sādh] amnf desirous of accomplishing, aiming (acc.) | phil. [Nyāya] who desires to make a proof.
sisaṃgrāmayiṣu var. siṣaṃgrāmayiṣu [agt. des. saṃgrāma] amnf who wants war, eager to fight.
sisṛkṣ [des. sṛj₁] v. pr. (sisṛkṣati) to desire to create, to want to emit.
sisṛkṣā [act. des. sṛj₁] f. desire to create.
sisṛkṣu [agt. des. sṛj₁] amnf desirous of creating, who wants to emit; prolific; not. said of Brahmā. sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ Desirous of creating the various creatures.
sīt var. śīt [onomatopoeia] ind. sigh expressing pleasure. sītkāra var. śītkāra |kāra| m. act of uttering a sigh | not. sighs of pleasure during orgasm | act of blowing with one's trunk (elephant).

sītkārasīkara | śīkara | m. pl. sprinkling by an elephant blowing its trunk. saṃdhyānuttotsave tārāḥ karenoddhūya vighnajit sītkārasīkarairanyāḥ kalpayanniva pātu vaḥ | | lit. KSS. During the festival of the invincible twilight, Ganesha raises the stars by raising his trunk, as if to create new ones with his sprinkling; may he protect you!

Sītā [related to sīra] f. furrow (of the plow); field, cultivated land | myth. Vedic np. of Sītā, personifying the cultivated land and its vegetation, Indian Pomona, symbol of fertility | myth. |Rām.| her incarnation Sītā, born in Mithilā from a ritual furrow traced by her father, the just king Janakarāja, desiring posterity, thus fulfilling the vow of Vedavati; she married the divine king Rāma by

choice [svayaṃvara], During a festival at which as sista Paraśurāma was present; she was abducted by the rākṣasa Rāvaṇa; freed by Rāma with the help of Hanuman, she was repudiated, then forgiven after undergoing the ordeal of fire [agniparīkṣā]; at the end of her life she was reabsorbed by her mother the Earth |Bhūmi|; cf. Jānakī, Vaidehī. jaya Sītā rāmah mod. "glory to Sītā and Rāma", salutation formula.
sītādravya [dravya₁] n. plow.
sītāphala [phala] n. custard apple; syn. ātṛpya.
sītārāma |Rāma| mr. of. myth. Sītā and Rāma. jayasītārāma mod. (greeting) glory to Sītā and Rāma.
sītārāmakalyāṇa | kalyāṇa | n. myth. marriage of Sītā and Rāma.
sīdhu var. śīdhu m. rhum. sīdhumāmsapaśupriyā f. myth. "fond of rum, meat and sacrificial animals", epith. of Durgā Mahiṣāsuramardinī.
sīdhupa [pa₁] amnf sīdhupā f. sīdhupī who drinks liquors; drinker, drunkard.
sīma iic. sīman.
sīmánta [anta] m. ray (splitting the hairs) | med. joints of the human body; there are 14 of them, corresponding to the joints [asthisamghāta].

Sīmantin [in] amnf Sīmantinī by tagé (hair) | having parted hair (like a pregnant woman) — f. Sīmantinī lit. [Brahmottarakhaṇḍa] np. of Queen Sīmantinī of the Niṣadha country, devotee of Śiva; every Monday, she invited a sage and his wife, treated them like Shiva and Umā, and covered them with gold; two young Brahmins from Vidarbha having finished their studies went to ask the king for alms to finance their marriages; on his order one of them disguised himself as a woman so that the couple could enjoy the favors of Sīmantinī, but Sīmantinī made the change of sex irreversible.
sīmantonnayana [unnayana] n. soc. rite of dividing a woman's hair by her husband in the 3rd (or 6th) month of her 1st pregnancy, a saṃskāra; the comb is a branch bearing a green fruit.
sīmán [related to Sītā] m. parting (dividing the hair) — fn border, boundary, extremity, limit; margin | horizon; summit; nec plus ultra. sīmānaḥ borders.
sīmā [f. sīman] f. border; village boundary (figuratively) delimitation.
sīmānta | anta | mr. edge; border; terminal | boundary of a village — amnf sīmāntā delimited (by iic. ).
sīmāntabhūpāla | bhūpāla | mr. king of a bordering country.
sīmāntara | antara | n. boundary of a village.
Sīyaka m. hist. np. Sīyaka of a family of Paramāra kings in the 10th century; cf. Harṣa₁.
sīra [related to Sītā] m. plow | plough ox.

Sīradhvaja [dhvaja] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the king Sīradhvaja Janaka "whose standard bears the chariot", also called Janakarāja; son of Hrasvaromā, he descends from Mithi Janaka; by plowing the sacrificial ground with his plow, he caused his daughter Sītā to emerge from the furrow.
sīrin |in| m. myth. np. of Sīrī, epith. of Balarāma "who holds the plow".
sīvaka [agt. sīv] m. fashion designer — f. sīvikā neck turret.
sīvana [act. sīv] n. seam — f. sīvanī raphe of the perineum.
sīvanayantra [yantra] n. mod. sewing machine.
sīvya [pfp. [1] sīv] amnf sīvyā to sew.
su₁ pf. good, well; beautiful, pretty, pleasant; very. susiktam tvayā you watered well.

√ su₂ v. [5] pr. (sunóti) pr. r. (sunute) pp. (suta₁) pf. (adhi, abhi, ā, pra, sam) ved. to squeeze, to express; squeeze (not. the soma for sacrifice) — ca. (sāvayati) to press. icchanti devāh sunvantam na svapnāya sprhayanti [RV.] the gods love the one who presses (the soma); they are not attracted to sleep.

súkanyā [su₁kanyā] f. beautiful young girl |myth. np. of Sukanyā "Pretty girl", daughter of King Śaryāti who gave her in marriage to the old sage |rsi| Cyavana in expiation for his mistreatment; after he had taken his rejuvenating bath she gave him a son Pra mati.
súkára [su₁kara₁] amnf sukarī easy to do; easy for (g.); easy to (inf.) | that succeeds easily | docile (animal) — m. docile horse — f. sujarā docile cow — n. sukara good deed; charity.
súkarman [su₁karman] n. good work — amnf sukarmanī who works well; active, efficient who does good deeds, virtuous — m. craftsman, artist, architect.
sukavitā [su₁kavitā] f. poetic talent.

sukumāra [su₁kumāra] amnf sukumārī tender, delicate, slender; in the grace of youth — m. hist. np. of the poet sukumāra, author of the Srīkṛṣṇavilāsa | lit. [Sivarātrimāhātmya] np. of sukumāra₁ "good boy", young brahmin who indulged in women, alcohol, meat, theft; he was banished to the country of Hūṇa, where he met an untouchable woman with whom he fell in love, and he united with her while she was menstruating; she bore him two daughters before dying, and then sukumāra₁ committed incest with her daughters; The Brahmins banished him, but he entered by chance the Shiva temple Adimadhyāntanāgeśvara on Shivarātri night, and when the gong sounded at midnight all his sins were abolished; at his death, Yama's emissaries wanted to lead him to hell, but Shiva opposed it, because he had stayed awake on Shivarātri . sukumāracaraṇayugalam a pair of delicate feet.
sukumāratā [tā] f. delicacy, finesse | lit. sweetness, poetic quality.
sukṛt [su₁kṛt₂] amnf who acts well; good;
virtuous | fortunate; wise | skillful — mn sukṛtas pl. soc. the manes (rewarded for their virtue in the afterlife).

súkṛtá |su₁kṛta| amnf sukṛtā well done, successful; well conducted; pretty, just, useful — n. benefit; spoils; help, favor | good deed, beneficence, meritorious act | reward; happiness, luck. sukrtam good! bravo!
súkṛti [su₁kṛti] f. good conduct, virtue; kindness, goodness — amnf virtuous, just.

Suketu [su₁ketu] amnf very bright | myth. |Rām.| np. of Suketu, the "Most Bright" king of the genies [yakṣa]; after a long asceticism, Brahmā granted him to father a daughter Tāṭakā strong as 1000 elephants; he married her to Sunda₁ | myth. [BhP.] np. of King Suketu₁ Janaka, son of Nandivardhana, father of Devarāta.
sukeśa [su₁keśa] amnf sukeśī who has beautiful hair — m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the ogre |rākṣasa| sukeśa.
sukṣatra [su₁kṣatra] amnf sukṣatrā who reigns well; powerful.
sukṣatriya [su₁kṣatriya] m. good warrior; good prince.
sukhá |su₁kha| amnf sukhā easy, pleasant; joyful, happy; good for (dat.) — n. joy, happiness, pleasure; comfort, prosperity; opp

duḥkha | phil. | Vaiśeṣika | quality | guṇa | of pleasure | chance — f. cf. sukhā — v. [11] pr. (sukhyati) to make happy — v. [11] pr. (sukhayati) to give pleasure — v. [11] pr. r. (sukhāyate) to experience pleasure. sukhám adv. happily; easily, comfortably; readily, at ease; willingly, with pleasure. kadalīsukham as easily as (catching) a banana. sukham ... na punar rather ... than. sukhena var. sukhāt adv. easily, conveniently. mahatā sukhena with great pleasure. sukham kṛ to please (g.). sukham dā to give pleasure. sukhā kr to make happy. sukhībhū to rejoice. sa bhavişyati sukham hantum he will be easy to kill. sukham duḥkham jayati Happiness surpasses misfortune. sukham asūn api saṃtyajanti na punaḥ pratijñām They prefer to renounce life rather than an oath. sukhārthinah kṛto vidyā kuto vidyārthinah sukham Knowledge attained by one who seeks pleasure is not worth the joy of one who seeks knowledge.
sukhákara [kara₁] amnf sukhakarā that gives pleasure, that makes happy | var. sukhakāra f. su khakārā id.
sukhákārin [kārin] amnf sukhakārinī which causes joy; which gives pleasure.
sukhátara [tara] amnf sukhatarā compar. easier. sukhataram adv. more easily.
sukháda |da| amnf sukhadā which gives happiness or joy — m. myth. epith. of Visnu.
sukhaduḥkha [duḥkha] n. du. sukhaduḥkhe (dvandva of opposites) pleasure and pain. sukhaduhkhada amn that causes pleasure and pain.
sukhadhana [dhana] m. bed. [KSS.] np. of Su khadhana, a rich merchant from Kāñcī; cf. Artha lobha.
sukhaprati [prati] ind. a piece of pleasure.
sukhápratīkṣa [pratīkṣa] amnf sukhapratīkṣā which anticipates pleasure | of an optimistic nature.
sukhábuddhi [buddhi] f. easy understanding.
sukhábodha [bodha] m. easy understanding | sensation of pleasure. bālānām sukhabodhāya for the easy understanding of children | [Tarkasamgraha] for the use of beginners.
sukhábhāj [bhāj] amnf happy, joyful.
sukhábhuj [bhuj₂] amnf happy, joyful.
sukhámaya [maya] amnf sukhamayī makes joy; filled with joy; that brings joy.
sukhásayana [sayana] n. pleasant sleep.

sukháśayita [śayita] amnf sukhaśayitā having had a pleasant sleep — n. pleasant rest. tām sukhaśayitam prccha asks him if she slept well. sukhásambodhya var. sukhasambodhya [saṃbodhya] amnf sukhasaṃbodhyā fa cile to understand; easy to explain or teach.
sukhasupta [supta] amnf sukhasuptā who has a pleasant sleep.
sukhāpanna [āpanna] amnf sukhāpannā who has attained happiness.
Sukhāsana [āsana] n. posture of ease (seated with left leg folded, right leg hanging down) — m. arch. np. of Sukhāsana, epith. of Šiva "in posture of ease"; it is one of the 16 aspects of Śiva.
sukhocita [ucita] amnf sukhocitā accustomed to comfort.
sukhā [f. sukha] f. happiness, bliss | phil. effort to gain merit, piety.

sukhāvat [vat] amnf Sukhāvatī₂ who procures happiness — f. Sukhāvatī₂ bd. np. of Sukhāvatī₂ "Land of happiness", paradise of the West of Amitābha | lit. np. of Sukhāvatī₂ "Beneficent", wife of Sūryaprabha.
Sukhāvatīvyūha [vyūha] m. bd. np. of the Sukhāvatīvyūha "Emanation of Amitābha", a work which describes the splendor of Amitābha's paradise in an extravagant manner.
sukhāhara [āhara] amnf sukhāharā who indulges in pleasure.
sukhita [pp. sukha] amnf sukhitā heu reux; satisfied.
sukhin [sukhain] amnf sukhiniī who loves pleasure; happy. sarve bhavantu sukhinaḥ Let us work for the happiness of all. sukhinaste panthānah santu May the journey be pleasant for you.
sugata |su₁gata| amnf sugatā who is well | well-off; who has a good life — m. bd. Buddhist; Buddhist master | bd. np. of sugata "Welcome", epith. of Buddha.
sugati [su₁gati] f. beautiful life; pleasant existence; happiness | safe refuge — amnf that is in a favorable position (star).

sugandha [su₁gandha] m. good smell; by fum — amnf Sugandhā Perfumed; fragrant — m. sulfur — f. Sugandhā myth. np. of the nymph [apsaras] Sugandhā "Perfumed" | bio. di verses fragrant plants, not. the tulasī.
sugandhavat [vat] amnf sugandhavatī by smoked.
sugandhi [su₁gandhi] amnf Perfumed.
sugandhitā [tā] f. Perfume.
sugandhimūla [mūla] n. organic. bot. Vetiveria ziza nioides, vetiver; syn. uśīra.
sugandhin [su₁gandhin] amnf sugand hinī Fragrant, sweet — f. organic sugandhinī. bot. Pan danus odoratissimus, pandana tree; its flower; syn. ketakī.
sugama [su₁gama] amnf sugamā easy to cross; practicable, easy to access | easy to understand; obvious.
sugamānvaya [anvaya] amnf sugamānvayā gram. easy to analyze — f. sugamānvayā lit. n.p. of the sugamānvayā vṛtti, commentary on the Meghadūta by the Jain Muni Sumati Vijaya.
sugātra [su₁gātra] amnf sugātrī slender, who has a pretty body.
suguṇin [su₁guṇin] amnf suguṇinī full of good qualities, very virtuous.
suguru [su₁guru] amnf sugurvī very serious, abominable (crime) — m. good tutor.
sugrhīta [su₁gṛhīta] amnf sugrhītā held firmly; Well caught, Well received; Well understood.
sugṛhītanāman |nāman| amnf sugṛhītanāmnī soc. whose name is invoked favorably.

Sugrīva [su₁grīvā] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of Sugrīva "with the beautiful throat", king of the monkeys, ally of Rāma against Rāvaṇa; he is said to be the son of Sūrya |Ravinandana|, and capable of changing his form at will; he fought his elder brother Vālī, who dethroned and exiled him, but was reinstated in his capital of Kişkindhā by Rāma upon the latter's death; he was defeated by Kumbhakarna; cf. Rūmā | myth. |PP.| np. of Sugrīva₁, "with the beautiful neck", one of the 4 horses of Kṛṣṇa's chariot, of yellow color.
sugrīṣma [su₁grīṣma] m. beautiful summer.
sugrīṣmaka [ka] m. soc. np. of the summer festival Sugrīṣmaka, celebrated in Konkana on the 5 days preceding the full moon phālgunī; mod. Sigmo (koṅkaṇī) || pkt. suggimaho.
sugla |su₁gla| amnf sugla very tired.
sughaṭa [su₁ghaṭa] amnf sughaṭā easy to accomplish. sughațatva |tva| n. ease of accomplishment.
sughațita [su₁ghațita] amnf sughațitā Well planned, Well foreseen; Well accomplished, successful.
sughoṣa [su₁ghoṣa] amnf sughoṣā very noisy | which has a pleasant sound — m. myth. |Mah.| np. of sughosa, conch of Nakula.
sucakṣus |su₁cakṣus| amnf sucakṣuṣī who has good eyes.
sucatura [su₁catura] amnf sucaturā which has 4 beautiful ...
Sucandra |su₁candra| m. myth. |Rām.| np. of the king of Viśālā Sucandra, son of Hemacandra₁, father of Dhūmrāśva.

Sucarita [su₁carita] amnf sucaritā Well accomplished, correct | who behaves Well, virtuous — n. benefit, good work; good conduct — m. hist. np. from the grammarian Sucarita Miśra (early 11th century), author of a Kāśikā₁ of the Slokavārttika.
sucira [su₁cira] amnf sucirā very long — acc. suciram adv. iic. for a long time — g. sucirāya adv. iic. id. — loc. sucireņa adv. iic. id. — abl. sucirāt adv. iic. a very long time later.
sucirāyus |āyus| amnf who lives very long (said of a deity).
sujana [su₁jana] amnf sujanā good, benevolent, kind, helpful, charitable; virtuous — mf sujanā good person; benevolent person; virtuous person.
sujanatā |tā| f. kindness, benevolence.
sujanatva [tva] n. kindness, benevolence.

sujāta [su₁jāta] amnf Sujātā Well-born; Well-made, beautiful — n. birth under happy circumstances — f. Sujātā bd. |Buddhacarita| np. of Sujātā "Well-born", young girl who offered the future Buddha his first meal after his 6 years of penance on the banks of the Nīlāñjanā.

Sujāti [su₁jāti] amnf of good race, of good tribe, of good family, of good class; noble — m. bd. np. of Sujāti "the Well-Born", legendary hero; as a child, he offered his flesh to feed his starving parents.
sujita [su₁jita] m. “who easily conquered”, man's name — n. easy victory.
sujña [su₁jña] amnf sujñā Well informed; competent; knowledgeable (iic.).
sujñāna [su₁jñāna] amnf sujñānā who has good knowledge | easy to understand — n. good understanding; intelligence | good knowledge.
sujñānatva |tva| n. state of being well informed; competence.
sujyotis [su₁jyotis] amnf Well lit.
suț nota. gram. increment of 's' before the forms of kṛ₁ (e.g. saṃskṛta).
sut [agt. su₂] ifc. amnf véd. who pressed the soma; who sacrifices — m. sacrificing.
suta₁ [pp. su₂] amnf sutā pressed — mn pressed soma juice, libation.

suta₁ [pp. sū₁] amnf sutā brought into the world — m. son, child | math. symb. the number 5 (for the 5 Pāṇḍavās) | du. sutau boy and girl — f. sutā girl. sutamukhadarśanasukham the joy of seeing the face of a son.
sutapa₁ [pa₁] amnf sutapā who drinks soma.
sutanu [su₁tanu] amnf thin, slender; who has a beautiful body — f. var. sutanū pretty woman | myth. np. of sutanu, daughter of Ahuka, wife of Akrūra.
sutapa₁ [su₁tapa] m. myth. ["who practices great penances" | class of gods.
sutápas [su₁tapas] amnf that heats a lot, that warms; epith. of the Sun | that practices great penances — m. soc. ascetic; er mite.
