sútapta [su₁tapta] amnf sutaptā burning; stinging; very hot | very severe (penance) — f. sutaptā bio. bot. Mucuna pruriens, velvet bean; this climbing legume is very stinging. sutaptamapi pānīyam śamayatyeva pāvakam |PT| Even scalding, water extinguishes fire.
sutarām [su₁tarām] adv. very good; more in cor. na sutarām adv. not very good. mā sutarām adv. not at all.
sutala |su₁tala| n. myth. np. of the world |loka| sutala, third subterranean hell.
sutīkṣṇa [su₁tīkṣṇa] amnf sutīkṣṇā Well sharpened — m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the ascetic sutīkṣṇa "Very virulent", who received Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā in the Dandakā forest.
sutrp |su₁trp₂| amnf easy to satisfy.
sutya [su₂] n. ved. (day of) pressing of soma | var. sūya id. — f. sutyā ved. pressing so lennel of soma.
Sutrāman [su₁trāman] amnf sutrāmaṇī who protects Well — m. myth. np. of Sutrāman, epith. of Indra "Good protector".

Sudakṣiṇa [su₁dakṣiṇa] amnf Sudakṣiṇā skillful | courteous, polite; sincere, frank | generous towards the priests — m. myth. [BhP.] np. of Sudakṣiṇa, son of Pauṇḍraka; to avenge his father, he implored Shiva, who gave him the mantra to create the monster Dakṣiṇāgni, who failed to defeat Krishna, and ended up turning against him — f. Sudakṣiṇā myth. np. of Sudakṣiṇā "Generous in verse to the priests", wife of Dilīpa₂, mother of Raghu.
sudat [su₁dat] amnf sudat ī who has beautiful teeth.
sudatta |su₁datta| amnf sudattā Well done.
sudanta [su₁danta] amnf sudantā f. su dantī who has beautiful teeth.

sudarśana [su₁darśana₁] amnf su darśanī beautiful, Graceful, pleasing ["pleasing to the eye"] — mn myth. np. of sudarśana "Magnificent", personifying the cakra or flaming disk, solar weapon of Vishnu; also called Vajranābha or Cakrapurușa; it comes from the churning of the ocean of milk [kṣīrodamathana]; or [VP.] Vishvakarma fashioned it with the shavings obtained by planing the radiance of the Sun; [Mah.] Agni gave it to Krishna after the khāṇḍavadahana | myth. epith. of Shiva "the Graceful" | myth. [BhP.] np. of the Vidyādhara Su Darśana₁, a celestial genius of great beauty, but very vain; for having mocked the ugliness of Angirā, the latter cursed him to be reborn as a serpent demon on the banks of the Yamunā; one day he attacked Nanda, but Kṛṣṇa touched him with his foot and he regained his celestial form, freed from his curse | myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā Sudarśana₂, son of Sankhana, father of Agnivarna | lit. [Hitopadesa] np. of the (fictional) king Sudarśana₃.

Sudāma [su₁dāman₁] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of Sudāma "Well rewarded", young brahmin study companion [gurukula] and close friend of Kṛṣṇa during his youth in Vṛndāvana, at their master Sāndīpani; he was poor, married, and lived with his family in poverty; his wife Suśīlā urged him to visit Kṛṣṇa, who had become king in Dvārakā; he was ashamed to bring him only a few flakes of rice | pṛthuka | as a gift, but the latter honored him as a distinguished guest, washed his feet and covered him with presents; upon his return his modest hut had become a palace; cf. Kucela | pl. name of a people — f. Sudāmā₁ myth. np. of Sudāmā₁, one of Skanda's nurses.

sudāman [su₁ extdāman₁] amnf sudāman₁] generous, who gives in abundance — m. myth. np. of the cowherd Sudāmā₁ "Generous", companion of the young Kṛṣṇa at Gokula; for having defended the fickle Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā cursed him to be reborn like the asura Sankhacūḍa | np. of many other characters.
sudāruņa [su₁dāruņa] amnf sudāruņā very cruel; severe, terrible — n. myth. |Mah.| terrifying celestial weapon.
Sudāsa [su₁dāsa] m. hist. [RV.] np. of King Sudāsa of the Tṛtsu people, son of Divodāsa₁, of the Bharatās tribe; victor of the Battle of the Ten
kings |dāśarājña|, he allowed the Bharatās to settle in Kurukṣetra | myth. [Mah.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā Sudāsa₁, son of Sarvakāma, father of Kalmāṣapāda.
sudi cf. śudi.
sudina [su₁dina] n. beautiful day; happy occasion — v. [11] pr. r. (sudināyate) to return to good (weather).
sudurācāra [su₁durācāra] amnf su durācārā hardened criminal.
sudurlabha [su₁durlabha] amnf sudur labhā very difficult to reach; very rare | very diffi cult to (inf.).
súdṛḍha [su₁dṛḍha] amnf sudṛḍhā very firm; very hard; very strong | very resistant, very good (memory) | Safe, well protected. sudrdham very intensely.
sudṛś [su₁dṛś₂] amnf with a piercing gaze | pleasing to the eye, pretty. sudrk f. pretty woman.
sudṛśya [su₁dṛśya] amnf sudṛśyā easy to see | pleasant to look at.
sudṛṣṭa [su₁dṛṣṭa] amnf sudṛṣṭā well seen; easy to see; obvious.
sudṛṣṭi [su₁dṛṣṭi] amnf who has keen eyesight — m. vulture.
sudevá [su₁deva] m. good king | myth. np. of King Sudeva "the good king", of the solar lineage |sūryavaṃśa|, son of Cuñcu; Bharuka is his son.
sudeśa [su₁deśa] m. good place; suitable location.
sudeśika [su₁deśika] m. good guide.

Sudeṣṇa [su₁deṣṇa] amnf Sudeṣṇā₁ generous — m. myth. np. of Sudeṣṇa "Generous", a son of Kṛṣṇa — f. Sudeṣṇā₁ myth. np. of Sudeṣṇā₁ "Generous", wife of King Bali; she bore by the ascetic Dīrghatamā the kings Anga₁, Vanga, Kalinga₁, Pundra, Sunga and Suhma, who gave their names to the kingdoms corr. [myth. [Mah.] np. of Queen Sudeṇā₁, wife of King Virāṭa; her brother Kīcaka was the commander of the army; during his last year of exile, Draupadī was in his service, disguised as the sairandhrī Mālinī₁.
suddhyupāsya [sudhīupāsya] amnf suddhyupāsyā adored by the wise (said of God).

sudyumna [su₁dyumna] m. myth. np. of Su dyumna "the Splendid", son of Manu, obtained by the sex change of Idā by Vasistha; having gone hunting in the Kumāravana forest, he became the beautiful Idā again. sudyumnah strīmayaivābhavat lit. [VAD.] Su dyumna became a woman.
Sudhana [su₁dhana] amnf sudhanā very rich — m. bd. np. of Prince Sudhana "Fortunate", exemplary disciple, who after a long initiatory journey, received Enlightenment thanks to Samantabhadra.
sudhanāvadāna [avadāna₂] n. lit. np. from the Sudhana vadāna, "Golden Legend of Sudhana", comic work.

sudhanvan [su₁dhanvan] m. myth. np. of Sudhanvā₁ "Skilled with the bow", son of Angirā; [Mah.] Vi rocana and he fell in love with the same woman; they sent to Prahlāda to arbitrate between them; Sudhanvā₁, fearing that the latter would favor his son, reminded him of the terrible punishment for a liar (Indra bursts their skulls open); after consulting Kaśyapa, Prahlāda declared that Sudhanvā₁ was of nobler origin and thus had precedence | myth. |Rām. | np. of King Sudhanvā₁, who reigned in Sāṃkāśyā; He attacked Mithilā to take the Ajagava bow from King Ja nakarāja, but the latter killed him and gave his capital to his brother Kuśadhvaja₁.
sudharma [su₁dharma] m. good law; justice; duty — amnf sudharmā that renders good justice — m. jn. one of the 10 disciples of Mahāvīra — f. sudharmā myth. assembly hall of the gods.
sudhárman [su₁dharman] amnf sudhármanī who practices justice; who does his duty well — m. family provider | myth. assembly hall of the gods | np. of various kings and deities.
sudhā su₁ dhā₂ f. nectar of flowers; milk<math></math> myth. drink of the gods, nectar; syn. amrta | plaster, stucco.
sudhākara |kara₁| m. nectar receptacle.
sudhākalaśa [kalaśa] m. hist. n.p. by Sudhākalaśa Gaņī author of the Ekākṣaranāmamālā₁.
sudhānidhi [nidhi] m. ["nectar receptacle"] epith. of the Moon.
sudhālaharī | laharī | f. lit. np. of the sudhālaharī "Wave of nectar", poem of praise to the Sun of Ja gannātha₁.
sudhāman [su₁dhāman] m. ved. np. of the ṛṣi Sudhāmā — m. sudhāma pl. sudhāmās myth. np. of a class of celestial beings.
sudhārmika [su₁dhārmika] amnf sudhārmikī very pious.
sudhī [su₁dhī₂] f. intelligence — amnf intelligent, wise, pious — m. tutor | expert.
sudhyupāsya [upāsya] amnf sudhyupāsyā which must be venerated by the sage.
sudhūmravarṇā [su₁dhūmravarṇa] f. myth. epith. from one of the 7 languages of Agni.
sudhṛti [su₁dhṛti] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of the sudhṛti king Janaka "the very resolute", son of Mahāvīrya, father of Dhrstaketu₁.
sunakṣatra [su₁nakṣatra] n. astr. refers to a favorable lunar constellation.

sunanda [su₁Nanda] amnf sunandā plai sant, agreeable — m. myth. np. du dvārapāla Su Nanda (his double being called Nanda) — f. su nandā geo. np. de la montagne sunandā devī, som met de 7816 de l'Himālaya, pic est de nandā devī.
sunaya [su₁naya] amnf sunayā of good conduct — m. correct conduct; wise policy.
sunāman [su₁nāman] amnf sunamnī who has a pretty name.
suniścita [su₁niścita] amnf suniścitā firmly resolved. suniścitam adv. with complete certainty.
suniṣaṇṇa [su₁niṣaṇṇa] m. organic. bot. Mar silea quadrifolia, water clover; syn. catuṣpatrī.
sunta [su₁nta] amnf sunta well conducted, well executed — n. wisdom, prudence, skill; so lution, good execution.
sunīti [su₁nīti] amnf who behaves well; virtuous — f. good conduct | myth. np. of sunīti "Virtuous", wife of Uttānapāda and mother of Dhruva.

Sunītha₁ [su₁nītha] amnf sunīthā who leads well | who is well led — m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the dānava Sunītha₁, son of Maya, reincarnated on Earth as King Candraprabha — f. sunīthā myth. np. of sunīthā, eldest daughter of MṛtyuYama, mother of Vena.

sunda m. myth. np. of the demon |daitya| sunda; |Mah.| sunda and his brother Upasunda were demons who had obtained from Brahma the promise that they could only be killed by each other; the gods saw Tilottamā seduce them into killing each other; [Hit.] after venerating Shiva with their great penances, he granted them a vow; they chose Parvati, but could not agree on how to divide her; they asked for the arbitration of an old Brahmin, whom Shiva impersonated; he told them that being of a warlike nature, it was their duty to fight, and they slaughtered each other myth. |Rām.| np. From the gandharva sunda₁, he married the powerful yakṣī Tāṭakā, by whom he had sons Mārīca and Subāhu; one day, drunk, he attacked the hermitage of Agastya, and the latter reduced him to ashes; Tāṭakā and his sons wanted to avenge him, and Agastya cursed them to become ogres [rākṣasa].

sundara amnf sundarī beautiful, pretty; pleasant, kind, charming — f. sundarī beautiful woman; cf. lokasundarī | lit. [KSS.] np. of sundarī, daughter of the asura Bali who gave her as a wife to Sūryaprabha. sundaram very good; exactly; agreed. sundarī nārī a beautiful woman. sundare sundaro ramaḥ sundarī kathā sundarī Sītā sundare sundaram vanam sundare sundaram kāvyam sundare sundaraḥ kapiḥ sundare sundaram mantram sundare kim na sun daram || in the pleasant book, Rāma is pleasant, in this pleasant book, the story is pleasant; In the pleasant book, Sita is pleasant, in this pleasant book, the wood is pleasant; in the pleasant book, the poem is pleasant, in this pleasant book, the monkey is pleasant; in the pleasant book, the mantra is pleasant, in this pleasant book, what is not pleasant?

sundarakāṇḍa [kāṇḍa] n. lit. np. from the sunda rakāṇḍa, 5th "pleasant" book of the Rām.; it describes the visit of Hanuman to Lankā, his meeting with Sitā, his capture by Indrajit, and his setting fire to the palace of Rāvaṇa.
sundaramūrti [mūrti] m. hist. np. of the Swami sun daramūrti "Pretty boy", Shaivite saint.
Sundaravarada [Varada] m. geo. n.p. of the Sundaravarada temple, dedicated to VișnuVarada, in Utti ramerur (Kāñcīpura district in Tamil Nadu), built in 750 by the Pallavās, renovated by the Colās.

Sundarasena [senā] m. lit. np. of Sundarasena, hero of the Kuṭṭanīmata | lit. [KSS.] np. of the Beautiful Prince Sundarasena₁, son of King Mahāsena₁ and Sasiprabhā₂; he lived celibate in his father's palace with five companions; while hunting, he met an elderly ascetic who described to him the incomparable beauty of Mandāravatī, and showed him his portrait; he fell in love with her, and his father proposed marriage to Mandāradeva, sending his portrait; Mandāravatī fell in love with her, and the marriage was agreed upon, set at 3 months by the astrologers; Mandāravatī, impatient, crossed the ocean to join him, and was shipwrecked; Sundarasena₁ did the same on his side, and was shipwrecked with his 5 companions; He finds Mandāravatī, is separated from her again, and they are finally reunited.
sundareśvara |īśvara| m. myth. np. of sun dareśvara "pleasant Lord", aspect of Śiva worshipped especially at the great temple of Mīnākṣī sundareśvara in Madurai, Tamil Nadu.
sunva [su₂va] amnf sunvā ved. who presses (the soma for sacrifice); who dedicates to the gods.
sup var. sub nota. gram. ending of the loc. pl.; in general, case ending of a nominal form; opp. tin. supsupā gram. [Mahābhāṣya] (a tatpurusa compound is formed) by two (consecutive) nominal forms.
subluk [luk] noted. gram. [Pāṇini] drop of the nominal suffix in composition.
supakva |su₁pakva| amnf supakvā well cooked; well ripe.
supațiman [su₁pațiman] amnf supațimā very skillful. supaṭimāṇaḥ var. supaṭimāḥ (women) very skillful.
supattra [su₁pattra] amnf supattrā who has beautiful leaves or beautiful wings — m. myth. epith. of Garuda.
supathin [su₁pathin] m. [sg. nom. su panthās good path, good road — amnf supathī which has good roads.
supad [su₁pad₂] amnf supad who has good or pretty feet | with fast feet.
supadya [su₁padya] amnf supadyā lit. in good verses.
supayas [su₁payas] amnf to the beautiful waters | which permeates well.
supayovin [vin] amnf supayovinī abundant in milk.

Suparṇa [su₁parṇa] m. bird; not. falcon, eagle | myth. [RV.] np. of suparna, watchful sea bird that snatches the divine soma from heaven | myth. epith. of Garuda "with beautiful plumage" — f. suparņī myth. epith. of Vinatā | epith. of Vāk as mother of meters | pali supanna. suparņākhyāna [ākhyāna] n. lit. np. of the suparṇākhyāna "Story of Suparṇa".
suparṇādhyāya [adhyāya] m. lit. np. of the suparṇādhyāya, a piece in verse relating to suparna.
suparvan [su₁parvan] amnf suparvā who has graceful limbs. suparvāṇaḥ var. suparvāḥ (women) with graceful limbs.
supārśva [su₁pārśva] amnf supārśvā who has a beautiful side, a beautiful torso.
Supārśvanātha [nātha] m. jn. de np. 7^e Supārśvanātha "Master with the beautiful torso", mythical tīrthankara; his body is green, his symbol is a swastika and a 7-headed cobra.
supu [su₁pū₂] ifc. amnf that which purifies well, that which cleans well; that which clarifies.
suputra [su₁putra] m. good son.
supta [pp. svap] amnf suptā asleep | immobile, latent — n. sleep; lethargy. nahi suptasya simhasya praviśanti mukhe mṛgāḥ |Hit.| Gazelles do not enter the mouth of a sleeping lion on their own.
supti [act. svap] f. sleep; deep sleep numbness; paralysis.
supratistha [su₁pratistha] amnf supratișthā that stands firm | that endures well | famous — f. supratisthā firm position | good reputation, glory | establishment (temple, idol); consecration.

Supratiṣṭhita [su₁pratiṣṭhita] amnf supratisthitā which stands firm | well established | completely rooted in (loc.) | famous; prosperous celebrated; well consecrated — n. lit. [KSS.] np. of the quarter of supratisthita in Pratisthāna.

Supratīka [su₁pratīka] amnf su pratīkā of beautiful appearance, pretty; admirable — m. myth. np. of the celestial elephant Supratīka₁ "with the broad forehead", diggaja of the North | myth. | Mah. | np. of Su pratīka₂, war elephant of King Bhagadatta; he crushed Bhīma's chariot and nearly swore him to death | lit. [KSS.] np. of the yakşa Supratīka₃; for having befriended the rākṣasa Sthūlaśirā, he was condemned by Kubera to incarnate as the piśāca Kāṇabhūti.

suprabha [su₁prabhā₂] amnf suprabhā magnificent, splendid; glorious — m. myth. np. of the dānava suprabha — f. suprabhā myth. np. of Su prabhā, daughter of Dakṣa; she married Kṛśāśva, by whom she had 50 very powerful sons, magical missiles in
fallibles | samhāra |.
suprabhāta [su₁ extprabhāta] amnf su prabhātā illuminated by the light of dawn — n. dawn of a happy day | morning prayer. suprabhātam adr. good morning. suprabhāte at the first light of dawn.

suprayukta [su₁prayukta] amnf suprayuktā well used; well designed, well planned; well administered, well organized | well sent (arrow). ekah śabdah samyak jñātah śāstrānvitah suprayuktah svarge loke kāmadhuk bhavati
iti [Patañjali₁] A word used wisely and correctly understood produces knowledge as the celestial cow grants our wishes.
suprayoga [su₁prayoga] m. good application, good use; good management | dexterity; competence; expertise.
suprasāda [su₁prasāda] amnf su prasādā very favorable; easy to reconcile — m. myth. epith. of Shiva — f. suprasādā myth. np. of Su prasādā, one of the nurses [kṛttikā] of Skanda.
súpriya [su₁priya] amnf supriyā very dear, beloved — m. myth. np. of the gandharva Su priya — f. cf. supriyā.
supriyā [f. supriya] f. pretty woman; favorite wife | myth. np. of the apsaras supriyā.
suphala [su₁phala] amnf suphalā which gives good fruit or many fruitful fruits | bio. describes many fruit trees.
sub iic. sup.
subanta [anta] n. gram. declined form of a nominal stem; syn. nāmapada; opp. tinanta.
subdhātu [dhātu] m. gram. denominative verb.

subvibhakti [vibhakti] f. gram. suffix marking the case of a nominal inflection; the following cases are distinguished: prathamā nominative, dvitīyā accusative, tṛtīyā ins strumental, caturthī dative, pañcamī ablative, ṣaṣṭhī genitive, and saptamī locative.
subaddhá [su₁baddha] amnf subaddhā firmly bound | tightly closed; tight. dvibandhah subaddho bhavati that which is doubly bound is well bound.

subandhu |su₁bandhu| amnf close parent or friend — m. hist. np. of subandhu, poet prior to Bāṇa₂; he is the author of the famous prose novel Vāsavadattā, a masterpiece of śleṣa figures, studded with erotic images and scabrous comparisons.
subala [su₁bala] m. myth. [Mah.] np. from sub ala "Very Strong", king of Gandhāra, father of Sakuni and Gāndhārī; from his thigh bone were made the dice with which Sakuni cheated.
subahu [su₁bahu] amnf subahvī very numerous; in very large quantity — adv. many, enormously; very often, frequently.
subahudhā [dhā] adv. often, frequently.
subahuśas |śas| adv. id.

Subāhu [su₁bāhu] amnf who has beautiful arms; with powerful arms — m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the rākṣasa Subāhu, son of Sunda₁ and Tāṭakā, who became a rākṣasa through the curse of Agastya; with his brother Mārīca they disrupted the sacrifice of Viśvāmitra; he was killed by Rāma | myth. [Rām.] np. of Subāhu₁, son of King Satrughna, who gave him the city of Madhurā | myth. [Mah.] np. of Subāhu₂, son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, king of the Cedayas.
subuddhi [su₁buddhi] amnf who understands quickly; intelligent — f. good understanding.
subodha [su₁bodha] m. good understanding — amnf subodhā easy to understand, easy to teach.
Subodhinī [in] f. introductory manual, didactic work, commentary | bed. n.p. of the Subodhinī, commentary by Vallabha₁ on the Bhāgavatapurāna.

Subrahmanya [su₁brahmanya] m. myth. np. of Subrahmanya, epith. of Skanda "Devoted to the Brahmins". rable; happy, favored; lucky, fortunate — VOC. adr. my dear. subhagam with happiness; to the highest degree.
subhagatvá [tva] n. chance.
subhagam [acc. subhaga] iic.
subhagamkarana | karana | afmn subhagaṃkaraṇī which makes one happy.
subhagammanya [manya] amnf subhagam manyā who thinks he is lucky.
subhaṭa [su₁bhaṭa] m. hero; champion | hist. n.p. by the poet Subhaṭa, author of the drama Dūtāṅgada (13th century) | bed. |KSS.| n.p. of king Subhaṭa₁, king of the West, father of Candrikāvati.
subhadra |su₁bhadra| amnf subhadrā excellent, glorious, magnificent — f. cf. subhadrā.

subhadrā [f. subhadra] f. myth. [Mah.] np. of subhadrā "the Glorious", beloved daughter of Vasu deva and Devakī, sister of Kṛṣṇa; she became Arjuna's second wife who abducted her with the consent of her brother; to overcome the jealousy of Drau padī, she presented herself to her at Indraprastha dressed as a cowherd; she gave birth to Abhimanyu; cf. Citrā₁.
subhadrādhanañjaya [dhanañjaya] n. bed. n.p. from the nāṭaka subhadrādhanañjaya of the Chera king Kulase khara (Kerala, 10th century).
subhava |su₁bhava| m. |"who has a noble origin" | king.
Subhānu |su₁bhānu| amnf which res plendit — m. astr. n.p. by Subhānu "Resplendent", personification of the 17th year of a life cycle [saṃvatsara] | myth. [BhP.] np. of Subhānu₁, a son of Kṛṣṇa.
subhāṣa [su₁bhāṣā] amnf subhāṣā who speaks well.
subhāṣita [su₁bhāṣita] amnf subhāṣitā well said; eloquent — n. fine words, praise; moral stance, saying, proverb. bālādapi subhāṣitam One can benefit from good advice, even from a child.
subhāṣitakaustubha [kaustubha] m. bed. n.p. from subhāṣitakaustubha, collection of proverbs.
subhāṣitatriśatī [triśatī] f. bed. n.p. of the subhāṣitatriśatī of Bhartrhari₁; cf. Satakatraya.
subhāsitanidhi [nidhi] m. bed. n.p. Subhāṣitanidhi of Sāyaṇa; cf. of Subhāṣitasudhānidhi.
Subhāṣitamañjūṣā [mañjūṣā] f. bed. n.p. from the anthology of dictators Subhāṣitamañjūṣā.
Subhāṣitamuktāvalī [muktāvalī] f. bed. n.p. from Jalhaṇa's anthology of sayings Subhāṣitamuktāvalī (1257), also called Sūktimuktāvalī.
subhāṣitaratnakośa | ratnakośa | mr. bed. n.p. from the collection of subhāṣitaratnakośa court poetry, collected by the poet Vidyākara (around 1050).
Subhāṣitaratnabhāṇḍāgāra [ratnabhāṇḍāgāra] lit. n.p. of Subhāṣitaratnabhāṇḍāgāra n. (SRBh.), modern anthology of proverbs due to Nārāyaṇa Rāma ācārya; also called Subhāṣitaratnakhandamañjūṣā.
subhāṣitaratnākara [ratnākara] m. bed. n.p. from the anthology of subhāṣitaratnākara maxims.
subhāṣitasaṃgraha [saṃgraha] m. bed. collection of sayings; cf. Subhāṣitāvalī, Sūktimuktāvalī, Saduktikarņāmṛta, subhāṣitaratnakośa, Subhāsitaratnabhāndāgāra.
Subhāṣitasudhānidhi [sudhānidhi] m. lit. np. from the Subhāṣitasudhānidhi "Treasury of nectar of beautiful words" of Sāyaṇa, also called Subhāṣitanidhi; it borrows from the Sūktiratnahāra.
Subhāṣitāvalī [āvalī] f. bed. n.p. from the Subhāṣitāvalī "Garland of Proverbs", an anthology of sayings compiled by Vallabhadeva (15th century).
subhāṣin [su₁bhāṣin] amnf subhāṣiṇī who speaks kindly, who says pleasant words, who speaks well.
subhūtá [su₁bhūta] amnf subhūtā (nour riture) well prepared — n. well-being.

súbhūti [su₁bhūti] f. well-being — mr. bd. n.p. of Subhūti, disciple of the Buddha; cf. Vajrac chedika | hist. n.p. by the lexicographer Subhūti₁ or Subhūticandra, author of the Kavikāmadhenu, commentary on the Amarakoșa.
subhoja [su₁bhoja] amnf subhojā easy to eat.
subhrātṛ |su₁bhrātṛ| amnf who has a good brother.
subhru |su₁bhrū| amnf who has beautiful eyebrows — f. subhrū pretty woman | "with beautiful eyebrows and eyelashes"].
sumangala [su₁mangala] amnf sumangalā f. auspicious sumangalī; which brings luck.
sumangalavilāsinī [vilāsinī] f. bed. n.p. from the sumangalavilāsinī of Buddhaghosa, commentary on the Dīgha nikāya .

súmati [su₁mati] amnf wise, wise; versed in (g.) — m. myth. [Rām.] np. of King Sumati "the wise," son of Kakutstha₁; he received Viśvāmitra, Rāma, and Lakṣmaṇa in his capital of Viśālā | hist. np. of the Jain philosopher Sumati₁ (9th century) | hist. np. of the Buddhist grammarian Sumati₂ (10th century) lit. [KSS.] np. of Sumati₃, eldest son of the minister Sitavarmā, and father of Pramati₁ — f. benevolence,

favor | pleasure to (loc.) | myth. | Rām. | np. of Sumati₂ "the wise one", daughter of Aristanemi, of incomparable beauty; second wife of Sagara, she gave him 60000 sons who, in search of the horse of their father's sacrifice, were reduced to ashes by Kapila.
sumatinātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of sumatinātha "Benevolent Master", 5th mythical tīrthankara; his body is golden yellow, his symbol is a bird or a wheel.
sumatipañjikā [pañjikā] f. lit. np. of the Su matipanjika, analytical commentary of the Cāndravyākaraņavrtti by Sumati₂.
sumadhyamā [su₁madhyamā] f. woman with a slender waist.
sumana |sumanas| amnf Sumanā char mant, pretty, graceful — m. wheat; syn. godhūma.

sumánas [su₁manas] amnf pleasant, agreeable; benevolent, amiable, well-disposed | content, joyful, at ease; even-tempered, wise; intelligent — m. wise man | lit. np. of King Sumanā, whose story is told in the Bṛhatkathā; he is transposed as King Śūdraka₁ in the Kādambarī novel by Bāna₂ which is inspired by him — n. flower — f. pl. sumanasas flowers — v. [11] pr. r. (su manāyate) to become benevolent. sumanīkṛ to make well-disposed. sumanībhū to be well-disposed.
sumanastā [tā] f. gaiety; opp. durmanastā || pali sumanassa.
Sumanottara | uttara | f. myth. n.p. of Sumanottarā, heroine of a tale [ākhyāyikā].
sumántu [su₁mantu] amnf well known | of good advice — m. friendly feeling | hist. np. of Sumantu, disciple of Vyāsa, author of a dhar ma'śāstra.

sumantra [su₁mantra] amnf sumantrā who advises well — m. myth. [Rām.] np. of Su mantra "of good counsel", advisor and charioteer of Daśaratha; he took Rāma into exile to the banks of the Gangā | lit. [DKC.] np. of Sumantra₁, son of the minister Dharmapāla₂; he is father of Mantragupta.
sumantrita [su₁mantrita] amnf su mantritā well advised; wisely planned — n. good advice. sumantritam (impers.) that is good advice.
sumantrin [su₁mantrin] amnf sumantriņī which is well recommended.
sumahat [su₁mahat] amnf sumahatī very large; vast, immense; numerous | very glorious.
sumahā iic. sumahat.
sumahātapas [tapas] amnf who practices great penances.

Sumāgadhī [su₁māgadhī] f. myth. [Rām.] np. of the Sumāgadhī river, which flows at the foot of Girivraja towards Magadha | geo. mod. Sonanadī, important tributary of the south of the Ganges, which joins it upstream of PāṭaliputraPaṭnā.
sumāli var. sumālin [su₁mālin] m. myth. np. du rākṣasa sumāli, father of Kaikasī by Ketu matī₁, grandfather of Rāvaṇa; he was killed by Sāvitra.

Sumitrā [su₁mitra] amnf Sumitrā who has good friends — m. myth. [JB.] np. of Sumi tra "good friend", who helped Indra kill Dīrghajihvī lit. [DKC.] np. of Sumitra₁, son of Dharmapāla₂, elder half-brother of Kāmapāla | lit. np. of many other characters — f. Sumitrā myth. [Rām.] np. of Sumitrā "Good friend", secondary wife of King Daśaratha, mother of the twins Lakshmana and Satrughna | lit. [KSS.] np. of the splendid yakṣiṇī Sumitrā₁, cursed to live on Earth until she unites with a human; this will be the ascetic Nāgasvāmī.
sumista [su₁mista] amnf sumistā very sweet, very sugary.

Sumukha [su₁mukha] n. pretty mouth; pleasant face — amnf sumukhī who has a pretty face; who smiles | pleasant, amiable; joyful | in good humor; well-disposed, favorable; kind towards (g.) — amnf sumukhā well-aimed (arrow); who has a wide aperture — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the Naga prince Sumukha "with the beautiful face"; he is the son of Cikura, put to death by Garuda; Vișnu gave him the amrta to protect him; he married Gunakeśī "with the beautiful hair". sumukhena adv. joyfully.
Sumuṇḍīka [su₁muṇḍaīka] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the dānava Sumuṇḍīka, son of Maya, reincarnated on Earth as King Sūryaprabha.

sumedhas [su₁medhā] m. myth. np. of the ṛṣi Sumedhā "Very wise" | lit. [Brahmottarakhaṇḍa] np. of the young brahmin Sumedhā₁, who went to see Queen Sīmantinī with his comrade Sāmavān disguised as a woman.
sumeru [su₁Meru] m. myth. n.p. from sumeru, epith. beautiful Mount Meru; KSS. he gave his daughter Kāmacūdāmaņi in marriage to Sūryaprabha.
sumná [su₁mna] amnf sumnā pleasant, gracious; kind, agreeable; favorable — n. goodness; grace, favor; devotion, prayer | peace, joy, happiness.
sumla [su₁mla] amnf sumlā very downcast, severely depressed.

suyantrita [su₁yantrita] amnf suyan tritā who controls himself correctly. sāvitrīmātrasāro 'pi varam viprah suyantritah | nāyantritas trivedo 'pi sarvāśī sarvavikrayī | [MS.] A brahmin who controls himself correctly, even if he only knows sāvitrī, is better than one who does not control himself, even if he knows the three Vedas, eating everything and dealing in everything.
suyaśa |suyaśas| amnf suyaśā very fa meux.
suyaśas [su₁yaśas] amnf very famous — n. glory, celebrity.
suyudh |su₁yudh₂| amnf who fights well.
suyodhana [su₁yodhana] m. myth. [Mah.] np. from suyodhana "great warrior", epith. by Du ryodhana.
sura [agt. sur] m. god, divinity; syn. deva.
suragaja [gaja] m. myth. np. of suragaja, epith. of Airāvaṇa "the divine elephant".
suragana [gana] m. myth. class of deities | a group of gods.
Suraguru [guru] m. myth. np. of Suraguru, epith. of Brhaspati "Preceptor of the gods".
surataru [taru] m. myth. tree of the gods; cf. pañcavrksa. suradviş var. suradvişa [dviş2] m. enemy of the gods; demon | asura |.
surapati | pati | m. myth. epith. of Indra, chief of the gods.
surapāla |pāla| m. hist. np. of surapāla, physician of the court of Rāmapāla; we owe him not. the Vrkṣāyurveda; we give him the title of Sureśvara₁.
suraśrestha [śrestha] m. myth. "the best of the gods", epith. of Viṣṇu, of Shiva, of Indra, of Dharma, of Ganesha, etc.
surasundara | sundara | mf surasundarī celestial beauty, a theme of temple sculpture.
surānganā [anganā] f. myth. divine wife; celestial beauty, syn. apsaras.
Sureśa |īś₂| m. myth. np. of Sureśa "lord of the gods", epith. of Shiva or ViṣṇuKṛṣṇa or (ved.) of Indra — f. sureśī myth. epith. of Durgā "who commands the gods".

Sureśvara |īśvara| mr. hist. n.p. of the scholar |ācārya| Sureśvara "Divine lord", renunciant name of Mandana Miśra, philosopher of the 9th century; champion of the pūrvamīmāṃsā doctrine, he lost a debate with Śaṃkara₁, became his student and converted to the advaita doctrine; we owe to him in particular the Sphotasiddhi, the Brahmasiddhi, the Naiskarmyasiddhi the Vidhiviveka, and the Vacanamālā | hist. n.p. of Sureśvara₁, epith. from Surapāla
Surottama [Uttama] amnf surotamā super. Best of the gods.
surakta [su₁rakta] amnf suraktā well co loré, well dyed | very moved, passionate | charming dark red.
surakṣita [su₁rakṣita] amnf surakṣitā well protected, well guarded. surakṣitām tām preṣaya send him (fem.) a good escort.
surata |su₁rata| n. enjoyment, sexual pleasure; copulation.

Suratamañjarī [mañjarī] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī princess Suratamañjarī "Bouquet of Pleasure", born on Earth as the daughter of the candāla Matangadeva as a result of his curse; Prince Avantivardhana fell in love with her; King Pālaka asked for her hand, Matangadeva asked him to invite 18,000 brahmins to eat at his house to end his curse | myth. np. of the apsaras Sura tamañjarī₁; she was cursed by Mārkaṇḍeya, and transformed into a silver chain; the chain was found by Vīrasekhara, to whom Darpasāra had promised his sister Avantisundarī in marriage; Taking advantage of his magical powers, he entered the women's quarters to contemplate her, and surprised her with Rajavahana, whom he bound with the chain.
suratarasa | rasa | m. sexual pleasure, passion, lust.
Suratha [su₁ratha] m. np. of Suratha “with the beautiful chariot”, epith. of various kings and heroes.

surathostava | stava | m. lit. np. of the surathostava, great poem [mahākāvya] in gaudī style due to Someśvaradeva; it tells the story of the mythical king Suratha, inspired by the life of King Bhīma₂.
surabhí [su₁rabhi] amnf Surabhi₁ f. sur abhī ["which affects pleasantly"] fragrant, by smoky; agreeable, charming — m. Perfume; spring weather; jasmine — n. Perfume — f. cf. surabhī.
Surabhidattā [datta] f. lit. [KSS.] np. of the nymph [apsaras] Surabhidattā, deposed from Indra's paradise for seducing a vidyādhara; she was condemned to incarnate on Earth as Kalingasenā.
surabhita [Surabhi₁ta] amnf surabhitā rendered Perfumed (by (i.)).

surabhī [f. Surabhi₁] f. myth. np. of Surabhi₁ or surabhī "the Perfumed One", celestial cow created by Dakṣa, wife of Kaśyapa, mother of the Rudrās, of Rohinī₂ and of Gandharvī; she incarnated on Earth as Rohinī₃ | myth. np. of surabhī₁, daughter of Kaśyapa and Krodhavaśā; she gave birth to the breed of cows. surabhīkṛ to perfume.

surasa [su₁rasa] amnf Surasā juicy, full of juice | tasty, delicious — f. Surasā bio. bot. Ocymum sanctum, holy basil; syn. tulasī | myth. np. of Surasā, daughter of Kaśyapa and Krodhavaśā; she is the mother of the herons [kanka] | myth. epith. of Kadrū, daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Kaśyapa; she is the mother of the race of snakes |nāga|.

súrā [su₂] f. spirit drink, alcohol; not. rice beer | myth. liquor produced during the churning of the sea of milk [kṣīrodamathana]; np. of Surā or Surādevī, her personification, daughter of Varuņa; cf. Vāruņī.
surāpa [pa₁] amnf surāpā who drinks liquors; drinker, drunkard.
surāpāna [pāna] n. drunkenness, alcoholism | var. surāpāņa id.
surājan [su₁rājan] m. good king; opp. kimrājan.
surātri [su₁rātri] f. beautiful night. surātri bhavatu adr. good night.
surāṣṭra [su₁rāṣṭra] m. geo. np. of surāṣṭra, country in western India (mod. Kațhiyāvār peninsula and Surāt coast in Gujarāt) | pl. its inhabitants.
suruc [su₁ruc₂] amnf with a vivid shine; very beautiful.
suruci [su₁ruci] amnf who has much pleasure in loc. — f. myth. np. of suruci, favorite of Uttānapāda and mother of Uttama.
surūpa |su₁rūpa| amnf surūpā well formed, beautiful.
suroha [su₁roha] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of suroha, emperor of China, father of Vidyunmālā.
sulakṣaṇa [su₁lakṣaṇa] amnf sulakṣaṇā which carries auspicious signs.

sulabha [su₁labha] amnf Sulabhā fa cile to find, to obtain, to acquire — f. Sulabhā lit. |Mah.| np. of Princess Sulabhā, daughter of King Pradhāna; having become a wandering ascetic, she conversed in thought with King Janaka. mānuṣatāsulabho laghimā the natural lightness of humankind.
sulalāṭa [su₁lalāṭa] amnf sulalāṭā who has a pretty neck.
sulalita [su₁lalita] amnf sulalitā gra cieux; charming | seductive — f. sulalitā easy woman. sulalitam adv. in a graceful manner; with ease, playfully.
sulalitavistara [su₁lalitavistara] m. bd. n.p. of the charming lalitavistara.
sulavaṇa [su₁lavaṇa] amnf sulavaṇā very salty — f. sulavaṇā bio. bot. Chionachne gigan tea, a grass.

sulaimat m. bed. n.p. of Sulaimān, king Sa lomon; its fictionalized story, the Sulaimaccaritra, was written in Sanskrit by Kalyāṇa₂ Malla at the request of Prince Lāḍkhān, of the Afghan line of Lodī, around 1500.

Sulocana [su₁locana] amnf Sulocanā who has pretty eyes — m. bio. deer | myth. np. of Sulocana, one of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; he was killed by Bhīma — f. Sulocanā lit. [KSS.] np. of the princess Sulocanā, daughter of Paurava₁, fourth wife of Sūryaprabha₁ | lit. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī princess Sulocanā₁, daughter of King Amitagati, who gave her as a wife to Naravāhanadatta.
suvaktra [su₁vaktra] amnf suvaktrī who has a beautiful face, a beautiful mouth; epith. of Shiva — n. pretty face.
suvakṣas [su₁vakṣas] amnf who has a pretty chest.
suvakṣoja [su₁vakṣoja] m. pretty breast — f. suvaksojā who has a pretty breast.
suvarga cf. svarga.
suvarcas [su₁varcas] amnf vigorous; ardent; splendid.

suvárṇa var. svarṇa [su₁varṇa] amnf suvarṇā bright, golden, gold-like — m. weight of gold (a gold coin, about 25 g, or 16 māṣa); syn. karṣa — n. gold; gold coin || pali suvanna. kuṇḍalāya suvarṇam gold suitable for jewelry.
suvarṇakaraṇī | karaṇī | f. myth. | Rām. | herb suvarṇakaraṇī "which restores a golden complexion", rap carried by Hanuman of the Himalayas to heal Rāma's army.
suvarṇakāla |kāla₁| mr. golden age.
Suvarṇadvīpa | dvīpa | m. geo. np. of Suvarṇadvīpa, peninsula of Sumatra; syn. Suvarṇabhūmi.
suvarnapura [pura] n. myth. np. of the mythical city of Suvarṇapura, inhabited by the Kirātās.
Suvarṇabhūmi [bhūmi] f. geo. np. of Suvarṇabhūmi "Land of Gold", Su matra peninsula; syn. Suvarṇadvīpa | mod. np. of Suwannaphum Airport in Bangkok.
suvarṇavaṇij [vaṇij] m. gold trader | soc. mixed caste, resulting from the marriage of an ambastha man and a vaiśya woman.
suvárṇavat [vat] amnf suvarṇavatī which contains or possesses gold | pretty, graceful — adv. like gold.
suvarnavarna | varna | amnf suvarnavarnā golden color, golden — f. suvarṇavarṇā turmeric.
suvarṇaka [su₁varṇaka] amnf suvarṇakā golden | of a pretty color — m. bio. break shower of gold; cf. āragvadha — n. or.
suvasana₁ [su₁vasana₂] n. pleasant residence.
suvasana₂ [su₁vasana₂] amnf suvasanā well dressed.
suvastra [su₁vastra] amnf suvastrā well dressed.
suvāsa |su₁vāsa₃| m. pleasant fragrance or illusion.
suvāsakumāra [kumāra] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Suvarṇakumāra, son of Kaśyapa endowed with magical powers, charged with helping Sūryaprabha.

suvāstu [su₁vāstu] f. geo. np. of the valley of the river suvāstu "Good Residence", which descends from the Hindukush mountains to flow into the Kabul River, near modern Peshawar; modern Swat — m. pl. suvāstavas the inhabitants of this valley; cf. śrīvāstu.
suvikrama [su₁vikrama] amnf suvi kramā with a pretty gait | courageous, brave — m. high exploit | hero.
suvikrānta [su₁vikrānta] amnf su vikrāntā very valiant, heroic; bold; cheva leresque — m. hero.
suvikrāntavikramaṇaparipṛcchā [vikramaṇa pariprechā] f. bed. n.p. from the Su vikrāntavikramaņaparipṛcchā, comic work.
suvicāra [su₁vicāra] m. good thought — amnf suvicārā animated by good thoughts.
suvida [su₁vida] m. soc. ["who knows everything"] attendant of private apartments.
súvidita [su₁vidita] amnf well-known suviditā; well understood.
suvidha [su₁vidha] amnf suvidhā of good sort, suitable. suvidham adv. easily.
suvidhi [su₁vidhi] m. good rule, correct procedure. suvidhinā adv. as is proper; in the right way.
suvidhinātha [nātha] m. jn. np. of suvidhi nātha "Master of favorable rites", epith. of Puspadanta, 9th mythical tīrthankara.
suvirūḍha [su₁virūḍha] amnf su virūdhā completely grown or developed | well mounted.
suvistara [su₁vistara] amnf suvistarā extensive; strong, intense, complete — m. abundance, fullness. suvistaram var. followed in great detail, exhaustively.
suvismita [su₁vismita] amnf suvis mitā very surprising; very wonderful.
suvīra [su₁vīra] m. great hero | geo. people of the mouths of the Indus [Sindhu]; syn. saindhava.
suvīrya [su₁vīrya] amnf suvīryā very powerful; very effective — n. heroism; abundance of heroes.
suvṛkti [su₁ṛc₂] f. soc. hymn of praise.

suvṛtta [su₁vṛtta] amnf Suvṛttā well-turned; well-rounded | who behaves well, virtuous | lit. well-composed, well-versed — f. Suvṛttā lit. [DKC.] np. of Suvṛttā "Virtuous", daughter of the merchant Kālagupta from the island of Kālayavana; she married Rat nodbhava, but they were separated during a shipwreck; she gave birth to Puspodbhava, who was taken by an elephant; 16 years later the three of them were reunited.
suvrttatilaka | tilaka | mr. bed. n.p. from the Suvrttatilaka “Treasure of Versification”, a poetic work by Kşemendra.
suvrata |su₁vrata| amnf suvratā worm killer, chaste | docile.
suśabda [su₁śabda] amnf suśabdā which sounds good (flute); correct (word).
suśarman [su₁śarman] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Suśarmā "good protector", king of the Trigartās.
suśānta [su₁śānta] amnf suśāntā tota ly extinct | very calm, placid (waters).
suśānti [su₁śānti] f. perfect tranquility — m. myth. np. suśānti, Indra of the 3rd Manu.

suśikṣita [su₁śikṣita] amnf suśikṣitā well-educated; well-trained. nahi suśiksito 'pi natabatuh svaskandhamārodhum patuh However well-trained an acrobat may be, he will never be able to hoist himself onto his own shoulders.
suśiras [su₁śiras] amnf who has a pretty face.
suśītala [su₁śītala] amnf suśītalā ra refreshing. koțicandrasuśītala refreshing like a million moons.

Suśīla [su₁śīla] amnf Suśīlā₁ well-disposed; good, kind; virtuous | well-made, well-formed — f. Suśīlā₁ myth. [BhP.] np. of Suśīlā₁ "Virtuous", wife of Sudāma | myth. [HV.] np. of Suśīlā₁, a wife of Kṛṣṇa | myth. [MP.] np. of Suśīlā₁, daughter of the king of Kāśī, into whom Nārada found himself transformed when he asked Vișnu for the secret of his Māyā; she married the king of Vidarbha, lived happily, had many children; but her father and her husband fought each other, and all her family perished; She threw herself onto her husband's funeral pyre, and became the mystified Narada once more.
suśobhita [su₁śobhita] amnf suśobhitā brilliant; splendid — ifc. embellished by (iic.).
suśrávas [su₁śravas] amnf glorious, fa best, renowned | well-intentioned, kind.

Suśruta [su₁śruta] amnf suśrutā famous, renowned | well understood; learned with pleasure — m. hist. np. of Suśruta, famous ancient physician; he wrote the Suśrutasamhitā, presented as a summation of the teachings of Dhanvantari₁; the original text is earlier than the 3rd century BC, the definitive text was fixed around 500 | lit. [DKC.] np. of Suśruta₁, son of the minister Padmodbhava and Sindhudattā, father of Viśruta.
suśrutapāthaśuddhi [pāthaśuddhi] f. bed. n.p. of the suśrutapāṭhaśuddhi “Correction of the variants of Suśruta”, due to Candrața (end of 10th century).
Suśrutavyākhyā [vyākhyā₂] f. bed. n.p. the Suśrutavyākhyā, anonymous commentary on the suśrutasamhitā.
suśrutasaṃhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. np. of the suśrutasamhitā, basic work of medicine and surgery of Ayurveda, attributed to Suśruta.
suśroņi [su₁śroni] f. (woman) who has beautiful hips, callipygian; syn. nitambinī — f. suśronī id.
suślakṣṇa [su₁ślakṣṇa] very tender, very smooth | graceful, elegant (speech).
suślista [su₁ślista] amnf suślistā which adheres well; well bound; tight. suślistametat this is well suited.
suṣāman [su₁sāman] amnf suṣāmā which has a pretty song.
suṣikta [su₁sikta] amnf suṣiktā bien ar rosé; syn. susikta.
suṣira [su₁sirā] amnf suṣirā [“well drained” pierced, hollow — m. bamboo, reed, cane — n. vessel, tube; hollow, hole, cavity | flute.
suṣupta [su₁supta] amnf suṣuptā pro fundamentally asleep — n. deep sleep.
suṣupti [su₁supti] f. the state [avasthā₂] of deep sleep | phil. the third stage of consciousness; cf. māṇdūkyopaniṣad.

suṣumna var. suṣumṇa [su₁sumna] amnf suṣumnā very kind, very good — f. Suṣumṇā phil. [yoga] the central psychic path [mārga] Suṣumṇā "Good prayer", representation of Sarasvatī₁ in the microcosm; the apānavāyu is raised there by means of mūlabandha; its encounter with prāṇavāyu brings about the awakening of Kuṇḍalinī; cf. Iḍā, Pingalā.
suṣṭhú [su₁stha] adv. well, as it should be; excellently; extremely; opp. duḥṣṭhu | excl. well! susthu khalu most certainly.
susthuprayoga [prayoga] m. good usage, correct use | gram. not. correct use of a word.
susaṃvāda [su₁saṃvāda] m. lit. gospel.
susaṃvīta [su₁saṃvīta] amnf susaṃvītā well dressed; well covered; well har naché — ifc. richly provided with (iic.).
susakthan [su₁sakthan] amn who has beautiful thighs.

susaṃgata [su₁saṃgata] amnf Susamgatā good friend, pleasant companion — f. susaṃgatā lit. [Ratnāvalī₁] np. of Susaṃgatā, "Good friend", confidante of Sāgarikā; she makes his portrait on that of King Udayana.
Susandhi [su₁sandhi] m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Ayodhyā Susandhi, son of Māndhātā, father of Dhruvasandhi and Prasenajit₁.
susamāhita [su₁samāhita] amnf su samāhitā very attentive, intensely absorbed in | well-ornamented; perfectly suited to.
susamiddha [su₁samiddha] amnf su samiddhā well inflamed — m. ved. n.p. of Susa middha, an aspect [āprī₂] of Agni.
susampanna [su₁sampanna] amnf susampannā well equipped, well supplied fully developed.
susaha [su₁saha₁] amnf susaha easy to bear | that bears well.
susikta [su₁sikta] amnf susiktā well watered; syn. susikta.
susūkṣma [su₁sūkṣma] amnf susūkṣmā very fine, very small; very delicate | very subtle; very difficult to grasp.
sustambha [su₁stambha| mr. good pillar; nice post.
sustrī [su₁ strī] f. virtuous woman.
sustha [su₁stha] amnf susthā who is at ease, content, happy; in good condition; opp. duḥstha. sustho'sau he is in good health.

susthita [su₁sthita] amnf susthitā well established; at ease; in good condition, in good health; prosperous, rich | firm, resolute; on the right path — n. house with a gallery on all sides. susthit (vocative f.) address to a woman.
susthirā [su₁sthira] amnf susthirā firm, stable; at ease | determined, resolute.
susthirāsana [āsana] amnf susthirāsanā [yoga] who is comfortable in the position.
susnāta [su₁snāta] amnf sausnātikā who performed the ritual bath.
susnigdha [su₁snigdha] amnf sus nigdhā very tender, unctuous; loving | (food) unctuous, rich in fats.
susmita [su₁smita] amnf susmitā who has a pretty smile; person's name.
susvadha [su₁svadhā] m. pl. soc. spirits to be honored particularly — f. susvadhā prosperity.
susvara [su₁svara] amnf susvarā harmo nieux. susvaram adv. harmoniously | aloud.
súhita [su₁hita₂] amnf suhitā appropriate, well suited; wholesome | fulfilled, satiated | friendly, affectionate — n. satiety, abundance.
suhṛd [su₁hṛd] mf ["who has a good heart"] friend, ally — amnf ifc. who loves, who is devoted to, who pleases (iic.). suhrdo janāh friends. nayanasuhrdo vrksah a tree pleasing to the eye.
suhrdbandhu | bandhu | mr. relative who is a friend.
suhrdbheda | bheda | m. separation of friends | lit. title of the 2nd chapter of the Hitopadesa.
suhṛnmitra | mitra | n. (sg. collective) friends and allies.
suhṛdaya [su₁hṛdaya] amnf suhṛdayā "who has a good heart" | friendly; affectionate.
Suhotra₁ [su₁hotra] m. myth. np. of Suho tra "who sacrifices abundantly", son of Vitatha, ancestor of Gādhi and Jahnu; Brhatputra is his son myth. np. of Suhotra₁, 2nd son of Jamadagni.
Suhma m. myth. np. of King Suhma, son of Dīrghatamā and Sudeṣṇā | geo. np. of the land of Suhma, in western Bengal (mod. district of Ban kura) | pl. the Suhmās, its inhabitants.

√ sū₁ v. [1] pr. (savati) v. [6] pr. (suvati) v. [2] pr. (sauti) v. [2] pr. r. (sūte) pp. (sūta₁, suta₂, sūna) pf. (pra) incite; impart an impulse, set in motion; create | conceive, give birth; produce || gr. vios; all. Sohn; ang. son.
sū₂ |agt. sū₁| ifc. mf that produces, that creates, that gives birth (iic.) — m. birthing, delivery lat. sus; ang. sow.
sūkará var. śūkara, ṣūkara |(sū)kara₁| mr. pork, pig; wild boar — f. sūkarī sow, sow.

sūkta [su₁ukta] amnf sūktā ved. well said, well recited | eloquent — n. lit. prayer, blessing, pious recitation; Vedic hymn; not. division of a maṇḍala of the Ḥgveda; cf. śrīsūkta | pali su vutta. rsih sūktam paśyati The sage has the vision of the hymns.
sūkti [su₁ukti] f. lit. well-turned poetry; dic ton; syn. subhāṣita.
sūktimuktāvalī [muktāvalī] f. bed. n.p. from the sūktimuktāvalī, collection of proverbs due to Jalhaṇa (1257), also called Subhāṣitamuktāvalī.
sūktiratnahāra [ratnahāra₁] m. bed. n.p. from the anthology of sūktiratnahāra dictators (South India, 13th-14th century, prākṛta); the Subhāṣitanidhi comes from it.

sūkṣma [related to sūci] amnf sūkṣmā fine, small, thin; small, narrow; weak, insignificant; sub til, acute; atomic | phil. subtle (opp. sthūla) — mn atom — f. sūkṣmā phil. subtle stage of manifestation of speech; cf. vapus.
sūkṣmatā [tā] f. finesse, subtlety.
sūkṣmatva [tva] n. id.
sūkṣmabhūta | bhūta | n. phil. |Sāṃkhya | subtle substance, perception; syn. tanmātra; opp. sthū labhūta.
sūkṣmamati [mati] f. subtle perception.
sūkṣmaśarīra [śarīra] n. phil. [Vedānta] subtle body of the soul, formed of manomayakośa and vijñānamayakośa.
Sūkṣmāgama |āgama| n. lit. np. of the Sūkṣmāgama, manual of Shaivite ritual [śaivāgama]; it is considered one of the 28 revealed scriptures of the śaivasiddhānta.
√ sūc v. [10] pr. (sūcayati) pp. (sūcita) pf. (sam) to announce, to make known; to indicate, to designate | to suggest; to represent (not. in the theatre).
sūca [agt. sūc] amnf sūcā ifc. which indicates, which designates (iic.) | which pierces (iic.) — m. blade of grass (cutting) kuśa; syn. darbhānkūra — act. f. sūcā indication | theatrical performance.
sūcaka ; [ agt. ; sūc] ; a. ; m. ; n. ; f. ; sūcikā ; who; in dique, who designates — m. indicator; informant; denouncer.
sūcana [agt. sūc] amnf sūcan indicator — act. n. indication, information — f. sūcanā indication; heading.
sūci [sūci] f. needle, point; pointer; pointed object; not. scalpel | bd. arch. horizontal crossbar of balustrade [vedikā] of a stūpa | var. sūcī id.
sūcikaṭāha [kaṭāha] iic. the needle and the cauldron.
sūcikaṭāhanyāya [nyāya] m. lit. maxim of the knife and the cauldron; it says that simple things should be done before complicated things.
sūcipatra | patra | n. lit. table of contents; index.

sūcibhedya [bhedya] amnf sūcibhedyā [“that one could pierce with a needle” dense, palpable. sūcibhedyam tamah thick darkness. gacchantīnām ramaṇavasatim yoṣitām tatra naktam ruddhāloke narapatipathe sūcibhedyais
tamobhih [MD.] There, at night, on the royal road, in the darkness of knife-cut darkness, women go to their lovers.
sūcimallikā [mallikā] f. bio. bot. Jasminum auri culatum, jasmine with sweet-smelling white flowers, used in medicine; syn. yūthikā.
sūcīvāna [vāna₂] n. sewing and weaving.
sūcīvānakarman [karman] n. pl. sūcīvānakarmāṇi sewing and weaving, one of the 64 arts |kalā|.
sūcikā [sūcika] f. needle | elephant tusk.
sūcikāmukha [mukha] m. ["pointed end"] shell; conch | ritual gesture | mudrā | of the index finger pointing (index finger pointing, other fingers folded).
sūcita [pp. sūc] amnf sūcitā indicated; designated; announced; suggested.
sūt |onomatopoeia| ind. snort.
sūtkāra | kāra | mr. sound production; grunt lies.
sūtkṛta [kṛta] n. bio. grunt (not. of elephants).
Sūta₁ [pp. sū₁] amnf sūtā born, engendered | incited; emitted | that engendered — m. mercury.

sūtaka [ka] n. birth | soc. impurity related to birth impurity in gen. phil. Tantra impurity of a mantra by contamination of its context, remedied by encapsulation [sampuṭa] — f. sūtakā f. sūtikā parturient, young woman who has given birth.

sūtá2 m. herald, messenger | charioteer, chariot driver, chariot fighter | soc. royal charioteer or herald, high office; its holder was often of Kṣatriya father and Brāhmaṇī mother | bard; minstrel | myth. np. of the sage Sūta₁, who recited the Bhāgavatapurāṇa to the sages of the Naimișa forest; he had heard it recited by Suka to King Parīkṣit | myth. np. of Sūta₁ Gosvāmī, who gave his vision of the kaliyuga to Vyāsa to compose the Bhavişyapurāna. duhsūta bad driver.
sūti [act. sū₁] f. birth, childbirth; production; cf. punaḥsūti.
sūtyāśauca [āśauca] n. soc. impurity linked to childbirth; it lasts 10 days for a birth, and a number of days equal to the number of months since conception in case of miscarriage.
sūtikā [f. sūtaka] f. woman in labor | (cow) having recently given birth.
sūtikāṣaṣṭhī [ṣaṣṭhī] f. myth. tantr. Ṣaṣṭhī “to the infant”.

sūtra [instr. sīv] n. thread, cord, cord | soc. sacred cord; cf. anantasūtra, brahmasūtra, yajñasūtra | phil. aphorism, condensed formula; ritual treatise; cf. Yogasūtra | gram. formula, rule (of Pāṇini's grammar) | pl. sūtrāṇi bd. canonical teaching treatise | gram. rules of grammar; formulary — v. [11] pr. (sūtrayati) to compose a sūtra — v. [11] pr. r. (sūtrayate) to shape into a sūtra || fr. suture; pali sutta. alpākṣaram asaṃdigdhaṃ sāravad viśvatomukham astobham anavadyam ca sūtram sūtravido viduh Scholars of aphorisms assert that an aphorism should be condensed, unambiguous, substantive, universal, stated without pause, and not be faulted. laghūni sūcitārthāni svalpākṣarapadāni ca | sarvatah sārabhūtāni sūtrāny āhur manīṣiṇaḥ || Scholars say that aphorisms should be succinct, precise, use short words, and get to the point. samjñā₁ ca paribhāṣā ca vidhirniyama eva ca | atideśo'dhikāraśca ṣaḍvidhaṃ sūtralakṣaṇam || gram. The rules (of Pāṇini's grammar) are of 6 kinds: technical definition [samjñā₁], metalinguistic rule [paribhāṣā], prescription of an operation [vidhi], restriction of an operation [niyama], extension of property [atideśa] and rule of scope |adhikāra|.
sūtrakartṛ [kartṛ] m. author of sūtra.
sūtrakāra [kāra] m. gram. epith. of Pāṇini, author of the rules (of the Aştādhyāyī).
sūtrakṛt [kṛt₂] m. sutra author.
sūtrakṛtāṅga [aṅga₁] n. lit. 2ᵉ text of the jaina canon, intended to give novices the good to the authors, and to refute heretical arguments | pkt. sūryagada.
sūtrakrīdā | krīdā | f. soc. the art of puppetry, one of the 64 arts [kalā].
sūtragraha | graha | amnf sūtragrahā who grasps the meaning of the sūtra | who wears the sacred cord.
sūtradhāra [dhāra₁] m. architect | soc. director of a theatrical company; he presents the prologue of
plays [pūrvaranga] | puppeteer. nāndyantepraviśati sūtradhāraḥ The theatre director enters the stage after the blessing stanza.
sūtradhārakṛtārambha | kṛtaārambha | n. refers to a play [nāṭaka] where the theatre director himself pronounces the blessing stanza.
sūtrapāṭha |pāṭha| m. gram. np. du sūtrapāṭha "(Collection of) recitation of the rules (of Pānini's grammar)"; syn. Astādhyāyī.
Sūtrasthāna |sthāna| n. lit. general section (not. of a medical work) | not. the Sūtrasthāna "Book of Principles", first section of the Carakasamhitā.
sūtrātman |ātman| mr. phil. |Vedānta| the link of consciousness that threads the Universe.
Sūtrānta [anta] m. bd. np. of the Sūtrānta, doctrine bd. defined by aphorisms.
sūda [agt. sūd] m. ved. well | mud; remaining liquid; sauce | to cook.
sūdadohas [dohas] amnf ved. that gives milk like a well — f. soc. sacrificial formula "source of milk".
sūdaśālā |śālā| f. kitchen.
sūdana |act. sūd| n. destruction, the act of killing — agt. f. sūdanā ifc. that which kills, that which destroys (iic.).
sūna [pp. sū₁] amnf sūnā produced, born | blossomed (flower) — m. son — f. sūnā daughter.
sūnā [related to sūd] f. slaughterhouse; butcher shop; sacred mas | gallows, place of execution.
sūnu [agt. sū₁] m. (solemn) son, child, offspring | younger brother — f. daughter || ang. son; lat. sūnus; all. Sohn.
sūnútā |tā| f. condition of son.
sūnumát |mat| amnf sūnumatī who has sons.
sūpa m. sauce, soup; broth, vegetable curry; stew | lat. suppa; fr. soupe.
sūpaprati [prati] adv. with a little sauce.
sūpasarpaṇa [su₁upasarpaṇa] amnf sūpasarpaṇā easy to approach.

sūpāyana [su₁upāyana] amnf sūpāyanā easy to approach, accessible. sa naḥ piteva sūnave 'gne sūpāyano bhava | sa casvā nah svastaye | [RV.] be accessible to us, O Agni, as the father is to the son; always be present for our well-being.
sūma |su₂| m. milk; water.
sūya cf. sutya.
sūra [related to sura] m. the Sun.
sūrasena [sena] m. pl. geo. the sūrasena people — f. sūrasenī its language, śaurasenī.
sūrata [su₁rata] amnf sūratā well-disposed towards, tender | of good disposition, calm.

Sūri [sur] m. scholar, learned; sage | jn. Sūri title of superior of a monastic order [gaccha] of śvetāmbara obedience; cf. Uddyotana₁, Padma sundara, Mahendra₂, Simhatilaka, Somadeva₁, Ha ribhadra, Harşakīrti, Hemacandra.
sūrmī f. anvil.

sūrya [svar₂ya] m. the Sun | myth. np. of the "Di vin" sūrya, Sun god; he is the Radiant [Aditya] son of Aditi and Dyau (or [Rām.] Kaśyapa); he is Resplendent [Vivasvān], dark in color [śyāmavarṇa]; at his rising in his aspect as Incitator [Savitā] he inspires thoughts; he is represented holding 2 lotuses; |VP.| his chariot is drawn by 7 horses symbolizing the 7 days of the week, and named after Vedic meters: Gāyatrī₁, Brhatī₁, Ja gatī, Usnik, Tristup, Anustup and Pankti; his co-sister is Aruna the Dawn; he is the guardian [dikpāla] of the Southwest direction; |HV.| From his wife Conscience [Sañjñā] he begot ManuVaivasvata Yama and Yamī; from his substitute [Savarṇā] the Shade [Chāyā] he begot Sani (Saturn) and Tapatī (Ca nicule); from SañjñāSaraṇyū transformed into a mare he begot the Aśvinau and Revanta; Viśvakarmā shaved off one-eighth of his splendor so that Sañjñā could bear it, and from his shavings fashioned Su darśana and the other weapons of the gods; Dandī and Pingala are his servants; his principal temples are at Koṇārka (modern-day Orissa) and Modhera (modern-day Gujarat); cf. Arka, Khaga, Citraratha, Ta pana, Dinakara, Bhānu, Bhāskara, Ravi | math. symb. the number 12 — f. Sūryā myth. np. of Sūryā, daughter of sūrya; she accompanies the Aśvinau in their chariot; her marriage with Soma is the mythical proto-type of the Vedic wedding ceremony | gr. o; lat. sol; fr. Soleil.
sūryakānta [kānta] m. myth. ["beloved of the Sun"] crystal with marvelous properties; in poetry, it emits fire in the rays of the Sun, while the can drakānta emits water in the rays of the Moon.
sūryagraha [graha] m. astr. Sun (as an astral influence) | solar eclipse (as a phenomenon); syn. sūryagrahaṇa | myth. epith. of Rāhu, demon of eclipses.
sūryagrahaṇa [grahaṇa] n. solar eclipse.
sūryatā [tā] f. solar quality.
sūryatejas [tejas] amnf which possesses the brightness of the Sun — n. sūryatejás brightness of the Sun.

Sūryadāsa [dāsa] m. hist. np. of the poet Sūryadāsa "Servant of the Sun" (16th century); he composed the vi lomakāvya Rāmakṛṣṇakāvya around 1580; he is undoubtedly the inventor of this literary genre.
sūryanamaskāra [namaskāra] m. soc. [yoga] her wrestling in the Sun; she begins a session of exercise
cices [hathayoga].
sūryanādī [nādī] f. cf. pingalā.
sūryapūjā |pūjā| f. soc. festival celebrating the cure of Sāmba’s leprosy by sūrya; it is celebrated at the sāmbadaśamī, to wish good health to children; cf. dhanuyātrā.

Sūryaprabha₁ [prabhā₂] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the good king Sūryaprabha₁ "Resplendent Sun"; he reigned in Vakrolaka; his wife was Sukhāvatī₂ | lit. KSS. np. of Prince Sūryaprabha₁, son of King Candraprabha₁ of Śākala, destined by Śiva to become emperor of the vidyādharās ; the dānava Maya took him to Pātāla to acquire magical powers, and to build the aerial chariot Bhūtāsana; He abducted the princesses Madanasenā, Candrikāvati, Varunasenā, Sulocanā, Vidyunmālā, Kāntimatī, Parapuṣṭā, Tārāvalī₁ and Vilāsinī, then married them to conclude alliances; Maya revealed to him that in a previous life he had been her younger son Sumundīka; he led with the dānavās a fight with his rival Śrutaśarmā supported by the gods, which concluded with their sharing of the empire of the vidyādharās.
sūryabhakta [bhakta] amnf sūryabhaktā soc. worshiper of sūrya.
sūryamandala [mandala] n. disk of the Sun.

sūryamat [mat] amnf sūryamatī sunny — f. sūryamatī hist. np. of the queen sūryamatī of Kaśmīra, wife of the prodigal king Ananta₁, whom she forced to abdicate in favour of their son Kalaśa in 1063; Somadeva Bhatta composed the Brhatkathā for her.
sūryavaṃśa [vaṃśa] m. myth. solar lineage; cf. Vivasvān, Manu, Ikṣvāku, Daśaratha, Rāma, Hariścandra.
sūryavaṃśin |in| amnf sūryavaṃśinī myth. is said to be of the Sūryavaṃśī solar lineage.
sūryavat [vat] amnf sūryavatī sunny.
sūryavāra [vāra] m. Sunday, the day of the Sun.
Sūryaśataka [śataka] n. lit. np. from the Sūryaśataka, a collection of 100 poems in praise of the Sun by Mayūra.
Sūryasiddhānta [siddhānta] m. lit. np. of the Sūryasiddhānta "Solar Treatise", astronomical text of the 6th century in 14 chapters; it is attributed to Lātadeva by alBiruni.
sūryāṣtaka [aṣtaka] n. lit. np. of the sūryāṣṭaka hymn of devotion to the Sun.
sūryodaya [udaya] m. sunrise. sūryodaye adv. at sunrise.
sūryam [acc. sūrya] iic.
sūryampaśya [paśya] amnf sūryampaśyā who sees the Sun; cf. asūryampaśya.
sūryā iic. sūrya.
sūryāgni |Agni| mr. of. sūryāgnī myth. sūrya and Agni.
sūryācandramasa | candramas | mr. of. myth. sūrya and Candra.

√ sr v. [1] pr. (sarati) v. [3] pr. (sísarti) pft. (sasāra) pp. (sṛta) pf. (ati, anu, apa, abhi, ā, ut, upa, nis, pari, pra, prati, vi, sam) to flow, run, move quickly; flee running; slip; blow (wind) | advance quickly, on, to turn; pursue, attack; impose oneself | cross — ca. (sārayati) to set in motion | grant a
lute |vīṇā| | to put away a set | dyūta | | to set aside, to remove.
sṛká [sṛka] m. arrow. ধূক srkva n. corner of the mouth, commissures of the
lips | var. sṛkvan id. | var. sṛkvi id. — f. sṛkviṇī id.
srgāla var. śrgāla m. bio. zoo. jackal — f. srgālī bio. female jackal.

√ srj₁ v. [6] pr. (srjati) pft. (sasarja) pp. (srṣṭa) aor. |1| (asarji) pf. (ati, ava, ut, upa, pra, vi, sam) to release, let escape, spread | to create, give birth, emit, launch — ps. (sṛjyate) to be created, to be launched — ca. (sarjayati) to release, spread; to create — des. (sisrkṣati) to desire to create | fr. source; ang. surge.
srj₁ [agt. srj₁] ifc. amnf that emits, that discharges (iic.); that produces, that creates (iic.).
sṛñjaya m. myth. [Rām.] np. of the king of Viśālā Srñjaya, son of Dhūmrāśva, father of Sahadeva₂ | myth. |MS.| name of a people who abused sacrifices and were punished for it.
sṛṇi [sṛ] m. elephant tusk | the Moon.
sṛtá [pp. sṛ] amnf sṛtā ran away; fled, gone away, escaped — n. course, race; flight.
sṛti [act. sṛ] f. path; journey, wandering; transmigration.

√ srp v. [1] pr. (sarpati) pp. (srpta) pf. (apa, ava, ut, upa, pari, vi, sam) crawl; slip towards | ved. (ritual) to advance while hovering, the body leaning, hand in hand, (not. from sadas to bahiṣpavamāna) — ca. (sarpayati) to make crawl || gr. ερπω; lat. serpo; fr. snake.
srpta |pp. srp| amnf srptā creeped, slid (out of (abl.), into (loc.)) — n. place through which to slip.
srprá |srpra| amnf srprā slippery; oily; smooth — m. the Moon ["that slips in the Sky"].
sṛmará [sṛmara] amnf sṛmarī fast | organic. deer, gazelle.
sṛṣṭá |pp. sṛj₁| amnf sṛṣṭā issued, created, produced | provided with (i. iic.) | resolved to (loc. dat.).
sṛṣṭānna [anna] amnf sṛṣṭānnā who brings food.

sṛṣṭi [act. sṛj₁] f. emission, creation, production; nature | phil. cosmic creation, one of the 5 divine manifestations [pañcakṛtya]; opp. samhāra | lit. np. of the section | khanda | Sṛṣṭi of a purāṇa dealing with creation myths.
seka [act. sic] m. sprinkling, watering, action of pouring | emission of liquid; ejaculation, sperm.
dry [ca. sic] v. [10] pr. (secayati) to spread, to rose.
secana [act. sic] n. watering, sprinkling. vrksasecanam watering of trees.
seț [sa₁iṭ] nota. gram. se dit des racines se conjugate avec un 'i' intercalaire (opp. anit).
setu [situ] m. dike, dam; bridge; border; impassable limit | (figuratively) norm to be respected, taboo.

setubandha [bandha] m. construction of a bridge, dam or dike | myth. [Rām.] construction of the rock jetty linking Rāmeśvara to the island of Lankā, built by Hanuman with his monkey army to allow access to Rāma's army | lit. np. of the setubandha₁, poem on the deeds of Rāma in prākṛta attributed to Pravarasena₂; also called Rāvanavaha | lit. np. of the setubandha₂, commentary on the Vāmakeśvaratantra due to Bhāskararāya.
setubandhāsana [āsana] n. “bridge-shaped” yoga posture.
sena iic. senā.

senakula [kula] n. hist. family of the Sena dynasty, originating from the Kannada country, which ruled in Bengal in the 11th and 12th centuries; its founder Hemantasena took its independence from the Pāla Empire in 1095; Vaishnava Hinduism was promoted, and Buddhists persecuted.
senajít | jit | amnf ["who conquers armies (ad verses)"] np. of various characters.

senā f. dart, javelin, missile | army; army in battle formation | [senāmukha] troop of 3 elephants and chariots, 9 cavalry, 15 infantry — n. sena ifc. id. — m. sena ifc. hist. form of the names of princes of the Sena dynasty. sinoti śatrumiti senā the army is what hinders the enemy.
senāgra | agra | n. front of an army.
senāgraga |ga₁| amnf senāgragā who marches at the head of an army; general.
senājit [jit] amnf "to the victorious army", name of princes | var. senajit id.
senādhinātha | adhinātha | m. commander-in-chief of the royal army.
senādhipati |adhipati| m. commander-in-chief of an army corps.
senānī |nī₂| m. SOC. army commander; general; he is part of the royal circle | ratnin |. senānigrāmaņī [grāmaņī] m. of. senānigrāmaņyā SOC. the head of the army and the village chief.
senāpati | pati | m. army general | myth. np. of senāpati "leader of the army (of the gods)", epith. of Skanda.
senāmukha | mukha | n. army section formed of 3 troops [patti]; cf. gulma.
sendra [sa₁indra] amnf sendrā myth. ac accompanied by Indra.

ev v. [1] pr. r. (sevate) fut. (sevisyate) pft. (siṣeve) pp. (sevita) pfp. (sevanīya) pf. (ā, upa, ni) to serve, honor, pay homage to; to cherish, raise (child); to have sexual relations with (acc.) to inhabit, live in (acc.); to live near (loc.) | to cultivate, practice, devote oneself to — des. (sisevisate) to want to be vir. etāvānme vibhavo bhavantam sevitum that's all I can do for you.
seva [act. sev] n. var. sevi mod. apple.

sevaka [agt. sev] amnf sevikā who serves — ifc. who takes care of, who honors, who reveres, who obeys (iic.) — m. servant | helper, courtier, follower, volunteer | SOC. not. temple worker | mod. official — f. sevikā servant.

sevana₁ [act. sev] n. service; homage, reverence (not. of the guru) | sexual commerce — ifc. service of, homage of (iic.), etc. assiduous practice of, act of devoting oneself to (iic.) — f. sevanā homage.
sevana₁ [act. sīv] n. sewing — f. sevanī ai guille | suture.
sevanīya [pfp. [2] sev] amnf sevanīyā that must be served, honored or courted.
sevā [act. sev] f. homage, service; servitude; courtship (loc. g. iic.); flattery | worship — ifc. assiduous practice of; sexual commerce with (iic.).
sevi iic. sevin.
sevitā [tā] f. service.
sevitva [tva] ifc. n. act of resolving to (iic.) service of, deference to (iic.) | residence at (iic.).
sevita [pp. sev] amnf sevitā inhabited; served, honored — ifc. provided with, full of.
sevin [agt. sev] amnf sevinī ifc. who serves, who honors (iic.); who lives in (iic.); who practices (iic.) | respectful; courtier.
sevya [pfp. [1] sev] amnf sevyā that must be inhabited (by (g.)); that must be followed (path); that must be used | that must be honored; that must be served or guarded — m. master (of a servant).

sevyatā [tā] f. usability; service (of (g.)); the state of being honored or revered. prayā sevyatām to render servile, to be useful (to the g. rangle angle). hemantakāle gurūņi vastrāņi prayānti janasya se vyatām In winter, thick clothing is useful to people.
sevyatva |tva| n. id.
sevyasevaka | sevaka | m. du. master and servant — n. gram. relationship between master and servant (one of the meanings of the genitive).
sevyasevakopadeśa [upadeśa] m. bed. n.p. from Se vyasevakopadeśa, work by Ksemendra.
seśvara [sa₁īśvara] amnf seśvarā phil. theist; opp. nirīśvara.
seśvarasāṃkhya |sāṃkhya| n. phil. theistic form of sāmkhya; cf. yoga.
saiṃhala [*siṃhala] amnf saiṃhalī concerning Ceylon; produced in Ceylon; inhabitant of Ceylon.
saiṃhika [*siṃhaika] amnf saiṃhikā similar to a lion; leonine — m. myth. np. of Saimhika, matr. of Rāhu "son of simhikā".

Saimhikeya [*simhikāīya] m. myth. np. of Saimhikeya "son of simhikā", matr. not. of the graha Rāhu. dhriyate yāvadeko 'pi ripustāvatkutaḥ śivam | purah kliśnāti somam hi saimhikeyo 'suradruhām [Māgha] How could there be peace as long as a single enemy remains? Rāhu torments the Moon under the gaze of the powerless gods.
saiddhāntika [*siddhāntaika] amnf saiddhāntikā SOC. concerning the śaiva siddhānta doctrine, its ritual, its followers.
sainika [*senāika] amnf sainikā military — m. soldier, warrior | pl. Sainikās troops.

saindhava [*sindhua] amnf sandhavī relating to sindhu, originating from sindhu | fluvial — m. inhabitant, prince of sindhu; horse of sindhu | myth. | Mah. | n.p. from sablehava, epith. by Jayadra tha “king of sindhu” | pl. sandhavās inhabitants of sindhu — f. sandhavī language of sindhu | comic writing. of sāṃmitīya monks — n. rock salt (from Sindhu); salt in gen. sandhavam ānaya gram. (depending on the context) pass the salt; bring the horse.
saindhavaka [ka] amnf saindhavikā proper to the inhabitants of Sindh. saindhavácūrņa | cūrņa | n. fine salt.
sainya [*senāya] amnf sainyā military — m. soldier — n. army. adhisainyam adv. in the middle of the army.

saira [*sīra] amnf sairī which relates to the cart street. sairamdhra var. sairandhra |dhara| m. SOC. ["ploughman"] man of lower caste; not. son of a dasyu and an āyogavī SOC. free servant — f. sairandhrī SOC. wife of a sairandhra; free servant of the gynaeceum, lady-in-waiting | myth. |Mah.| borrowed role of Draupadī hidden at the court of King Virāța as lady-in-waiting and headdress of the queen.
socchvāsa [sa₁ucchvāsa] amnf SOC chvāsā who sighs; who exhales forcefully | out of breath. socchvāsam adv. with a sigh of relief.
sodha [pp. sah₁] amnf sodhā supported, endured; tolerated — v. [11] pr. r. (sodhāyate) to support, to endure.
sotka [sa₁utka] amnf sotkā with an ardent desire.
sotkantha [sa₁utkantha] amnf sotkanthā who has a strong desire (for (prati)) | who regrets, who laments (iic.). sotkantham adv. with sorrow, with regret.
sotkampa [sa₁utkampa] amnf sot kampā trembling, shivering.

sotsāha [sa₁utsāha] amnf sotsāhā who makes an effort; resolute, energetic, courageous. sotsāham adv. with energy, with determination; putting one's whole heart into it. kāṣṭhād agnir jāyate mathyamānādbhūmistoyam khanyamānā dadāti | sotsāhānām nāstyasādhyām nārāṇām mārgārabdhāḥ sarvayatnāḥ phalanti || [Pratijñāyaugandharāyaṇa] The fire overcomes the logs, by its agitation the water carves channels in the earth; For courageous men nothing is impossible; all efforts on the path of their undertakings will be rewarded.
sotsāhatā [tā] f. energy, zeal; determination, courage.
sodara [sa₁udara] amnf sodarī (brother/sister) cousin; blood relative; close, of the same family. narmaikasodaram navam vayah |KSS.| Youth knows only one ally, and that is pleasure.
sodarya [ya] amnf sodaryā id.
sopasarga [sa₁upasarga] amnf sopa sargā gram. is said with a compound verb, preceded by a preverb [upasarga].
sopāna n. staircase, steps; ladder | degree, level.
sopānakūpa [kūpa] m. stepwell.
sopānatva [tva] n. function of staircase. sopānatvam kuru sukhapadasparšam ārohaņesu [MD.] Become a staircase which, to climb the slope, will be gentle on the feet.
sobhari m. ved. np. of sobhari, author of hymns of the Rigveda.

sóma [su₂ma] m. Vedic. stimulating juice extracted by pressing and filtering the stems of the soma plant, whose identification is controversial (bot. Cannabis sativa or Sarcostema viminalis or Asclepias acida or Ephedra distachya), sacred beverage drunk by priests during Vedic sacrifice; cf. amśu, adri, pavitra, sutya | myth. its personification the god soma, to whom the 9th mandala of the Rigveda is dedicated; later identified with amrta, beverage of the gods and source of immortality; the king of the gods Indra is drunk in myth. epithet of the god Candra personifying the moon as "(vessel of) soma", one of the 8 Treasures [vasu]; he is the guardian [dikpāla] of the Northeast direction; His marriage to Surya is mentioned in the Vedic marriage rites; astr. he presides over the nakshatra Mgaśiras; his excessive amorous passion for Rohini (the star Aldebaran) causes his regular consumption [snehaksaya]; cf. Tara, Varca | phil. [Ayurveda] the cold principle, opp. to the hot principle [agni] | camphor | Vedic the male principle, opp. to the female principle [sura] | math. symb. the number 1 || Avestan Haoma.
somakānta [kānta] amnf somakāntā dear to the moon | charming like the moon — m. lit. moonstone; cf. candrakānta.
somakrayaṇī [krayaṇa] f. soc. young cow serving as purchase price for the soma of the sacrifice.

Somadatta₁ [datta] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the Kaurava prince Somadatta₁ "Lunar Gift", son of Bāhlīka, father of Bhūriśravā | myth. [Rām.] np. of the Viśālā king Somadatta₁, son of Kuśāśva, father of Kakutstha₁ | lit. [DKC.] np. of Somadatta₁, one of the 10 heroes of the Daśakumāracarita, son of Satya varmā and Gaurī₂; he found a jewel, gave it to an old Brahmin, then was arrested by the soldiers of Mattakāla; He freed himself, and thanks to Mānapāla who gave him weapons, he killed Mattakāla and freed the princess Vāmalocanā whom his father gave him as a wife.
sómadā [dā] f. myth. [Rām.] np. of the gandharvī Somadā; she conceived King Brahmadatta of ṛṣi Cūlī.

somadeva | deva | m. hist. np. of somadeva Bhatta, śaiva brahmin, court poet of King Ananta₁ and his son Kalaśa in Kaśmīra; for Queen Sūryamatī he composed the Kathāsaritsāgara between 1063 and 1082, allegedly from the paiśācī version of Guṇāḍhya which is doubtless fictitious | hist. np. of somadeva₁ Sūri, 10th century Jain scholar during the reign of King Rāstrakūta Kṛṣṇa₃; to him are attributed the masterpieces Yaśastilaka and Nītivākyāmṛta; he was considered a very great sage, scholar and poet | hist. n.p. by somadeva₂, alchemist from Gujarāt of the 12th century, author of Ra sendracūdāmaņi.

somanātha [nātha] m. geo. np. of somanātha "Master of soma", first among the 12 radiant signs of Shiva [jyotirlinga]; it is said that he was established in a golden temple by soma at Somanāthapattana, to thank Shiva for softening the curse of Daksa; his linga was suspended in the air by magnetism; somanātha was the tutelary deity of the Solankī dynasty; the temple was destroyed by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1025; a modern temple was rebuilt at the independence of India | hist. np. of somanātha₁, 17th century musicologist, author of the Rāgavibodha hist. np. of somanātha₂, phil. of Kaśmīra, author of the Ajñānadhvāntadīpikā.

Somanāthapattana [pattana] n. geo. np. of So manāthapattana "city of Šiva Master of the Moon", famous for its magnificent gates and the many treasures of its temple; it was sacked by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1025, sacked again in 1297 and 1394, and finally destroyed by Aurangzeb in 1706; mod. Somnath Patan on the coast of Gujarāt.

Somanāthapura [pura] n. geo. np. of the city of Somanāthapura, near Mysore in Karņāṭaka, site of the splendid temple of Keśava; it was founded in 1269 by Somadaṇḍanāyaka, vassal of King Hoysala Narasimha III.
somapa [pa₁] amnf somapā soc. who drinks soma — mr. soc. priest celebrating the sacrifice of soma var. somapā id.
somapāna | pana | n. soc. soma drink.

somapura | pura | n. geo. np. of the great monastery bd. of somapura in Bengal (mod. Paharpur) established by King Dharmapāla₁ in the 8th century; it burned down in a war in the 11th century, was rebuilt, and abandoned in the 13th century during the Muslim invasions.

somaprabha [prabhā₂] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the great harva Somaprabha, younger brother of Devaprabha, cursed by an ascetic to incarnate as the magical elephant Svetaraśmi — f. somaprabhā lit. [KSS.] np. of somaprabhā, daughter of the asura Maya; she became friends with Kalingasenā.
somayāga [yāga] m. soc. ved. soma sacrifice; cf. pravargya.
somayājin |yājin| amnf somayājinī soc. who performs a soma sacrifice | hist. n.p. by the mathematician and astronomer Nīlakantha₃ So mayājī, author of the Tantrasaṃgraha (1445–1545).
sómarasa [rasa] m. ved. juice of the soma plant.
somavamśa [vamśa] m. myth. lunar royal lineage; cf. Budha, Puru, Dusyanta, Purūravā, Bha rata, Kuru, Sāmtanu.
somavamśin [vaṃśin] amnf somavaṃśinī myth. prince of the Lunar royal line | hist. n.p. of the Somavamśī dynasty, which ruled in Orissa in the 10th century.
somavat |vat| amnf somavatī which contains soma | Lunar — adv. similar to the Moon.
somavarcas | varcas | n. light of the Moon.
somavāra [vāra] m. Monday, the day of the Moon.
Somaśambhu [śambhu] m. hist. np. of Somaśambhu, śaiva author of the 11th century born in Kaśmīra; he is credited with an important manual of ritual |paddhati|.
Somaśambhupaddhati | paddhati | f. bed. n.p. from the Somaśambhupaddhati, manual of śaiva ritual due to Somaśambhu; Trilocanaśiva commented on it Somaśambhupaddhatiţīkā.
Somaśravas [śravas] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Somaśravā "Glory of the Moon," son of a hermit and a female serpent who had absorbed some of his seed; King Janamejaya took him as his cha
pelain | purohita |.
somasūtra [sūtra] n. arch. gutter draining libations poured on the linga in a śaiva sanctuary.
Somādhi [ādhi₁] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Somādhi or somāpi, son of Sahadeva₁, king of Magadha.

somānanda [ānanda] m. hist. n.p. by somānanda "Lunar Joy", śaivasiddhānta philosopher of Kaśmīra from the end of the 9th century, precursor of the doctrine of Recognition | Pratyabhijñā | which was developed by his disciple Utpaladeva; he is the author of the Sivadṛṣṭi; he was perhaps Vasugupta's student.
somāpi |āpi| mr. myth. cf. Somadhi.
somāpīdā [āpīda] f. myth. [DKC.] np. of Somāpīdā "Horned by the Moon", a form of Durgā that Kandukavatī was to honor with a ball game.
somārāma [ārāma] m. geo. np. of somārāma, a major Shaivite pilgrimage site in Rāmacandrapura; it is one of the five shrines
gardens [pañcārāmakṣetra]; it is said that the śivalinga Someśvara was installed there by Candra.

Someśvara [īśvara] m. geo. np. of the śivalinga Someśvara, established in somārāma by Candra | hist. np. of King Someśvara₁, of the Western Cālukyās dynasty, son of Jayasimha₃; he reigned from 1042 to 1068; he fought unsuccessfully against the Colās emperors; he founded the city of Kalyāṇī, which he made his capital; he committed suicide by drowning in the Tungabhadrā | hist. np. of King Someśvara₂, eldest son of the preceding; he reigned in Kalyānī from 1068 to 1076, when he was dethroned by his younger brother Vikramāditya₆ | hist. np. of King Cālukya Someśvara₃, son of Vikramāditya₆; he reigned in Kalyāṇī from 1126 to 1138; the encyclopedic work Mānasollāsa is attributed to him, probably composed by his court poets; Jagadhekamalla₂ succeeded him | hist. np. of the scholar Someśvara₄ Bhatta, author of the Nyāyasudhā₁ | cf. someśvaradeva.

Someśvaradeva [deva] m. hist. np. of the Brahmin śaiva Someśvaradeva, purohita and court poet of King Cālukya Bhīma₂, then of King Vāghela Vīradhavala (Gujaraat, 13th century); the minister Vastupāla was his patron and friend; he is the author of two great poems [mahākāvya], the Kīrtikaumudī and the Surathostava; he is also credited with the Rāmaśataka, the Karṇāmṛtaprapā and numerous
praises | praises|.
somodbhava [udbhava] amnf somodbhavā produced by the Moon — f. somodbhavā geo. epith. of the Narmadā "from the Moon".
soma₁ [sa₁Umā] amnf somā accompanied by Umā (not. Śiva).

somaskanda [Skanda] m. myth. np. of somaskanda "(Shiva) with Umā and Skanda", group representing the family of Shiva, traditional bronze idol of South India; it is associated with the cult of Tyāgarāja; syn. umāskandasahita.
somyá [somaya] amnf somyā who offers soma; inspired by soma | made of soma — VOC. adr. [saumya] my dear.

solanka m. name of a Rajput clan of the Gur Jara, of Jaina obedience — f. solankī hist. np. of the Solankī dynasty; it was created by King Mūlarāja at Aṇahilapāṭaka in 940; Bhīmadeva I succeeded him; the tutelary deity Solankī was Somanātha.
sollāsa [sa₁ullāsa] amnf sollāsā rejoiced, delighted. sollāsam adv. with joy; cheerfully.
soṣṇīṣa [sa₁uṣṇīṣa] amnf soṣṇīṣā in a turban.
soṣman [sa₁uṣman] amnf soṣmaṇī hot; burning | phone. sucked — m. phone. his ace worse. सौ: sauḥ interj. phil. mystical syllable [bījamantra] of Trika.
saukarya [*sukaraya] n. ease of operation or preparation; ease | skill; dexterity; agility.
saukumārya [*sukumāraya] n. beauty, elegance, slenderness; tenderness, delicacy — f. sau kumāryā ifc. beauty of (iic.).
saukṣmya [*sūkṣmaya] n. state of being tiny | finesse, subtlety.
saukha [*sukha] iic. about good.
saukhayānika [yānaika] m. soc. bard charged with wishing the king success in an expedition.
saukharātrika [rātrika] m. soc. title of the person charged with asking the king if he slept well.
saukhaśāyika [śāyikā] m. syn. saukharatrika.
saukhya [*sukhaya] n. well-being, happiness, bliss.
saugandha [*sugandha] amnf saugandhī fragrant, sweet — m. perfumer — n. scent.
saugandhika [*sugandhaika] amnf saugandhikā fragrant, perfumed — m. perfumer — n. sulfur | variety of ruby | variety of fragrant lotus cf. kalyāṇasaugandhika.
saucika [*sūcika] m. tailor.
saujanya [*sujanaya] n. kindness, goodness, benevolence, obligingness, charity | mod. gratuity; patronage.

Sauti [*sūta₁] m. patr. Sauti "Son of charioteer" | myth. [Mah.] np. of Sauti₁, patr. of Karna "raised by the charioteer [sūta₁]" (Adhiratha) | myth. [Mah.] np. of Sauti₂, patr. of Ugraśravā, Son of the
messenger [sūta₁] Lomaharṣaṇa, who told the sages [ṛṣi] of the forest Naimiṣa gathered by Saunaka the poem [kāvya] of Mah. which he had heard from Vaiśampāyana at the sacrifice of Janamejaya.
sautra [*sūtra] amnf sautrī made of thread; fabric | lit. relating to aphorisms | gram. unattested form justified by a sūtra.
sautradhātu [dhātu] m. gram. root mentioned in a grammar rule for the derivation of a nominal stem, but not admitting conjugated verbal forms.
sautrāntika [*Sūtrāntaika] m. bd. adherent of the Sūtrānta | pl. bd. externalist doctrine of the sautrāntikās, school attached to the sarvāstivāda.
