sautrāmaņá [*sutrāmana] amnf sautrāmanī myth. relating to Indra the Protector — f. sautrāmaṇī ved. solemn rite in honor of Indra; an offering of alcohol is made; |surā|; |SB.| which is consecrated with this sacrifice is reborn among the gods "with his own body" [sarvatanū]. sautrāmaņika [ika] amnf sautrāmaņikī soc. concerning the sautrāmaņī rite.
sautsukya [sa₁autsukya] amnf saut sukyā full of desire; with anxiety.
saudāmanī [*sudāman] f. [resplendent] (lightning) with multiple branches. vidyut saudāmanī yathā like a lightning bolt with multiple branches.
saudāminī f. cf. saudāmanī.
Saudāsa [*Sudāsa₁] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Saudāsa, patr. of Kalmāṣapāda “(Son) of Sudāsa₁”; he became a cannibal by the curse of Vasistha.
saudha [*sudhā] amnf saudhā plastered; plastered, covered with stucco — mn villa, palace.
Saundarananda [*sundaraNanda] m. lit. np. of the Saundarananda, epic of the gracious Nanda₂, bd. poem due to Aśvaghoṣa.
saundarya [*sundaraya] n. beauty, grace, elegance | goodness, generosity | phil. aesthetics.

saundaryalaharī [laharī] f. lit. [Tantra] np. of the saundaryalaharī "Wave of Beauty", devotional poem to the glory of beauty by Pārvatī Tripurasundarī, in 100 verses of śikhariṇī meter; it gives instruction [śrīvidyā] on the śrīyantra; it is wrongly attributed to Sankara₁, but its author is thought to be a śańkarācārya from South India (12th century?).
sauparṇeya [*suparṇīeya] m. myth. n.p. of sauparṇeya, matr. of Garuḍa — f. sauparṇeyī of the female cendant of Garuda.
saupika [*sūpaika] amnf saupikā drizzled with sauce.
sauptika [*suptaika] amnf sauptikā related to sleep; nocturnal.
sauptikaparvan [parvan] n. lit. np. from the sauptika parva, 10th book of the Mah., "of (the nocturnal) attack"; it recounts the carnage of the camp of the Pāṇḍavās in dormis.
Saubala [*subala] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Saubala, son of king Subala, patr. of Sakuni.
Saubha m. myth. np. of Saubha, aerial city of Hariścandra; cf. Vyomacāripura | myth. [Mah.] np. of Saubha₁, capital of King Sālva, indestructible magical citadel.
saubhaga [*subhaga] amnf saubhagā auspicious, favorable.
saubhagatva [vat] n. happiness; chance.
saubhadra [*subhadrā] amnf saubhadrā relating to subhadrā — m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Saub hadra, matr. of Abhimanyu.

Saubhari [*sobhari] m. myth. np. of the sage [muni] Saubhari; he lived in Vṛndāvana, and had forbidden Garuda to come there, under penalty of death; the nāga Kāliya took refuge there, and was only driven out by Krsna.
saubhāgya [*subhagaya] n. happiness, luck, fortune; felicity; not. marital happiness.
saubhāgyavat [vat] amnf saubhāgyavatī for tuné; which brings good luck — f. saubhāgyavatī young bride (not. at the wedding |pāṇigrahaṇa|).
saubhrātra [*subhrātṛa] n. brotherhood.
Saumadatti [*somadattai] m. myth. [Mah.] np. of Saumadatti, patr. of Bhūriśravā "son of somadatta".
saumanasa [*sumanasa] amnf sau manasī pleasant, agreeable | flowery — m. Well-being; good humor | myth. [Rām.] np. of saumanasa, diśāgaja of the West — n. pleasure, satisfaction.
saumanasya [*sumanasya] amnf sau manasyā which gladdens the mind — n. satisfaction of the mind; joy, good humor | understanding cor recte soc. offering of flowers to the priest of a śrāddha .
saumanasyavat [vat] amnf saumanasyavatī joyful, cheerful.

Saumitra [*sumitra] n. friendship — mr. var. sau mitri myth. matr. of Saumitra or Saumitri, matr. by Lakṣmaṇa | of. saumitrī myth. n.p. from saumitrī "the (2) sons of Sumitrā" (Lakṣmaṇa and Satrughna).

saumyá [*somaya] amnf saumī myth. relating to soma, to the moon | northern; cool and moist; of a cold character (opp. āgneya) | astr. qualifies the cooler half of the year | amiable, gentle, kind; placid; agreeable; benevolent, Benevolent — m. myth. one of the 10 regions [dvīpa] forming the Jambudvīpa | astr. np. of Saumya "Benevolent", personifying the 43rd year of a life cycle |samvatsara| |myth. patr. of Buddha (Mercury), son of soma (moon) — voc. adr. my dear, honorable (polite term of address to a brahmin).
saumyagraha | graha | m. astr. planet beneficence sante; opp. krūragraha.
saumyátā |tā| f. humidity; freshness | kindness, benevolence.
saumyátva [tva] n. id.
saumyádarśana [darśana] amnf Saumya darśanī pleasant to look at.
Saura [*sura] amnf saurā solar — m. myth. np. of Saura, patr. of Sani "(son) of the Sun" | [sauraja] coriander — n. lit. collection of hymns to the Sun, extracted from the Rigveda | cf. saurapurāṇa.
saurapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. bed. n.p. of saurapurāṇa.
sauramāna [māna₁] amnf sauramānā (calen drier) solar (opp. cāndramāna).
sauramānayugādi [yugādi] m. mod. New Year's Day according to the sauramāna calendar.
saurasamhitā [saṃhitā] f. lit. tantric text on the worship of the Sun (10th century).
saurata [*surata] amnf sauratā relating to sexual pleasure — n. sexual enjoyment.
saurabha [*surabhia] amnf fragrant saurabhā — m. coriander — n. perfume, good smell | saffron; myrrh | memorial, souvenir gifts; of france.
saurabheya |īya| amnf Saurabheyī myth. ap belonging to surabhi — m. bull leader of herd — f. Saurabheyī myth. np. of the apsaras Saurabheyī, companion of Vargā.
saurāṣṭra [*surāṣṭra] amnf saurāṣṭrī geo. inhabitant of Surāstra (mod. Kāthiyāvāda in Gu jarāt).
saurāṣṭranagara [nagara] n. geo. n.p. from the city of saurāṣṭranagara (mod. Surāt).
sauvarga [*svarga] amnf sauvargā who is in Heaven.
sauvarṇa [*suvarṇa] amnf sauvarṇā in gold — n. gold — m. gold coin; gold jewelry.
sauvarnika [*suvarnaika] amnf sauvarnikā which is worth a gold coin — ifc. (after num.) which is worth (iic.) gold coins — m. goldsmith — f. sauvarnikā venomous insect.
sauvastika [*svastikaika] amnf sau vastikā salutary — m. Swastika symbol turned upside down.
sauvīra [*suvīra] m. relating to the suvīra people; its king; syn. saindhava | pl. sauvīrās population suvīra — n. sour porridge (fermented boiled rice water).
sauvīraka [ka] m. man of the people will survive.
sauśabda [*suśabda] m. grammatical correction.
sauśabdya [*suśabdaya] m. id.
sauśravasa [*suśravasa] amnf sauśravasā of good reputation — n. celebrity, re name.
sauṣṭhava [*suṣṭhua] n. excellence; supreme good; extreme beauty; superior intelligence; excellent posture of the body (not. dance).
sausnātika [*susnātaika] amnf sausnātikī Who asks if one had a pleasant bath.
sauhārda [*suhṛda] n. friendship, affection (in verse (g. loc.).
sauhārdya [*suhṛdya] n. friendship, affection.
sauhṛda [*suhṛda] amnf sauhṛdā relating to a friend — m. friend — n. friendship, affection (reverse iic. ).
sauhṛdya [*suhṛdya] n. friendship, affection.

√ skand v. [1] pr. (skandati) pft. (caskanda) pp. (skanna) pf. (ava, ā, pra) to rise, jump, gush | to descend, fall, flow — ca. (skandayati) to spread, emit (not. retas); to neglect | lat. scando; fr. scander, to descend.

skandá [act. skand] m. jet, gushing; ef fusion, leap; act of overflowing | mercury; sperm | ved. |ChU.| np. of Skanda for the sage Skandakumāra "Gushing Boy", son of Brahmā, eternally young, unsurpassed scholar of the Veda; he taught Shiva the power of the praņava mantra [om]; cf. Svāminātha | myth. later evoked as Skanda "He Who Gushes (from the fertilization of the Ganges by the Fire of Shiva's sperm)"; he is said to have been born from a spurt of Shiva's sperm penetrated by Agni in the Ganges; [Rām.] ShivaRudra having united with UmāPārvatī, the gods were inquisitive about the birth of a son whose power the Earth could not bear; They begged him to devote himself to asceticism; his already spilled sperm, penetrated by Agni, gave birth to the White Mountain [Śveta₁]; the gods, desiring to have a leader for their army, asked Agni to fertilize Gangā; the golden embryo that sprang from it was Skanda; [Mah.] (variant) Agni fertilized the wives of the seven sages [saptarsi] (except the faithful Arund hatī) into whom Svāhā had successively transformed, who collected his sperm to throw it [skanna] 6 times into a golden pool of Mount Sveta₁; Skanda was entrusted to the 6 Pleiades [Kṛttikās], his nurses, who raised him in secret; he is thus often represented with 6 heads [Şanmukha], and called Kārttikeya and Guha; Worried about his powers, the gods sent Indra, who declared war on him but was defeated; the impact of his vajra on Skanda's side only gave birth to his double, Vishākha; Indra bowed, but Skanda only asked to become the commander-in-chief of the army of the gods [Senāpati]; he carries the magic javelin [śakti] which is in his hand; many exploits are attributed to him; he killed the demon Taraka, who had obtained the right to die only by a son of Shiva; he killed the daitya Bana hidden in the Krauñca mountain; his mount is the peacock Paravāṇi, into which his defeated enemy Śūrapadma was transformed; he carries a rooster on his banner; he is identified with the Dravidian deity Murugan of youth, beauty, and war; He is evoked as the abstinent adolescent [brahmacārin] Kumāra, avoiding contact with women, who are not admitted into his sanctuaries; he nevertheless retained from Murugan a loving and dissipated character, and his cult is inappropriate for young girls; he is also the patron of thieves and bandits; in his ram-headed aspect Naigameșa Viśākha, he ensures fertility, and he is implored for a son; but in his Skandagraha aspect, he harms children; in the South, Devasenā and Vallī are attributed to him as wives, who personify his army and his javelin; he is also called Subrahmanya "Favorable to Brahmins" and Yogīśvara "Lord of the Yogin"; he is Saktibhrt "He who carries the javelin" (Velan en ta mil); It is sometimes associated with the planet Mars.
Skandakumāra [Kumāra] m. ved. [ChU.] np. of the sage Skandakumāra, son of Brahmā, eternally young [Sanatkumāra], eternally
handsome [Sanatsujāta], unsurpassed scholar of the Veda; later evolves into Skanda, born of Shiva and Agni.
skandagupta [gupta] m. hist. np. of King Skanda gupta, last of the great emperors of the gupta line; he defeated the Puşyamitrāh and stopped an invasion of the Hūṇās in 455; he died in 467.
Skandagraha [graha] m. myth. np. of Skanda graha, aspect or companion of Kumāra Who harms children; cf. Nejamesa.

skandapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. lit. np. of the Skan dapurāṇa or Skāndapurāṇa, immense mythological śaiva text, composed between the 6th and 9th centuries; it comprises 7 sections: Maheśvarakhanda, Visnukhanda, Brahmakhanda, Kāśīkhanda, Avantyakhanda, Nāgarakhanda, Prabhāsakhanda; the later Sahyādrikhaṇḍa (14th century) is also attached to it; it gives the sacred śaiva geography of India in panegyrics of the places of pilgrimage |māhātmya|.
skandāpasmāra [apasmāra] m. myth. np. de skandāpasmāra "Skanda's Epilepsy", a demon emerging from Skanda's body to harm children.
skandana | act. skand | n. gushing; ef
fusion | abortion | purging, defecation | formation of a clot.
skandin [agt. skand] ifc. amnf skandinī that springs forth (from (iic.)) | flow, loss.

skandhá m. shoulder, trunk, body; tree trunk | sacrificial post; syn. stambha | troop, division of an army; multitude | lit. section, division (of a work) | bd. aggregate or constituent factor of the ego; there are 5 [pañcaskandhī]: material form [rūpa], sensation [vedanā], cognitive perception [samjñā₁], mental formation (emotion, thought, opinion, compulsion) [saṃskāra] and active awareness [vijñāna]; Buddha taught that one must be freed from them, by realizing their emptiness | pali khandha. tanmūlatvāt prajānām rājā skandhah The king is the trunk of the people, because the people are its root.
skandhasaṃtāna [saṃtāna] m. bd. suite of aggregates.
skandhāvāra |āvāra| m. royal camp; army headquarters.
skandhaka [skandhaka] n. lit. āryā poetry meter used for certain epic court narratives.<del> ংকর</del> skanna |pp. skand| amnf skannā thrown; emitted (not. sperm).
√ skambh [related to stambh] v. [9] pr. (skabhnāti) pf. (vi) to strengthen; to support; to fix; to establish.
skambhá [agt. skambh] m. support, prop; pi to tie; post, column; syn. stambha | phil. np. of Skambha, "Pillar of the Universe"; it is identified with Brahmā, or with Purusa.
skānda [*Skanda] amnf skāndā myth. relating to Skanda.
skāndapurāna [purāna] n. cf. skandapurāna.

√ skhal v. [1] pr. (skhalati) pft. (caskāla) aor. [5] (askhālīt) pp. (skhalita) pf. (vi) to stumble; to hesitate; to stutter | to make a mistake — ca. (skhalayati) ca. (skhālayati) to cause to stumble; to stop. na skhal not to hesitate, to remain firm; to succeed.
skhala [act. skhal] m. the act of stumbling, of wavering; stuttering, hesitation.
skhalat |ppr. skhal | amnf skhalantī stumbling.
skhaladvākya [vākya] amnf skhaladvākyā who stutters, who pronounces badly.
skhalana |act. skhal| n. stumbling, instability; drunkenness; stuttering, speech error | jerky discharge | error (in (iic.)). manusyāḥ skhalanaśīlāḥ To err is human. skhalanam manusyāṇām dharmaḥ id.

skhalita [pp. skhal] amnf skha litā jerky; unstable; hesitant, insecure; imperfect; deficient (language) | wavering; drunken | obstructed, hindered, interrupted; frustrated, perplexed | erroneous in (loc.) — n. error, fault, clumsiness. gotraskhalitam naming error of gotra.
√ stan [related to tan₂] v. [1] pr. (stanati) aor. [5] (astānīt) aor. [2] (atiṣṭanat) pp. (stanita) to thunder — ca. (stanáyati) (impers.) he thunders.
stána mn breast, udder, udder. stanakoți |koți| f. breast nipple.
stanacūcuka | cūcuka | n. nipple of the breast.
stanadaghná [daghna] amnf stanadaghnā f. stanadaghnī who has (water) up to her chest.
stánapa [pa₁] mf stanapā infant.
stánapāna | pāna | n. act of drinking from the breast. stanayitnú var. tanayitnu |yitnu| amnf ton nant — m. thunder | pl. ved. thunderclaps, personified as sons of Vidyota the Lightning.
stanayuga [yuga] n. pair of breasts. stánavinta vinta n. "breast stem" nipple.
stánaśikhā [śikhā] f. ["top of the breast"] nipple.
stanita [pp. stan] amnf stanitā which thunders — n. thunder; rumor, cries; applause; grunt; cries of pleasure during coitus | rumbling vibration (not. of a bowstring).
stabaka var. stavaka mn tuft, bouquet, bunch (flowers); flowerbed | lit. literary tribute; not. suite of 25 stanzas | śloka |
stabdha [pp. stambh] amnf stabdhā fixed, rigid; frozen | paralyzed; unconscious; dull | slow; obstinate | lit. laborious style in kāvya | proud; arrogant.
stabdhadrsti [dṛṣṭi] amnf ["with a fixed gaze"] is said of the gods (whose eyes do not blink).
stambá m. clump (not. of grass), clod; sheaf (not. of rice); stem; stubble; bouquet, bundle | cf. stambha.
stambaka |ka| m. id.
stambamitra | mitra | m. myth. | Mah. | np. of Stam bamitra, one of the śārngakās; hymns of the Rgveda are attributed to him.
stamba [loc. stamba] iic.
stamberama [rama] m. ["who plays in the grass"] elephant.

√ stambh v. [9] pr. (stabhnāti) v. [5] pr. (stabhnoti) v. [1] pr. r. (stambhate) pp. (stabdha, stabhitá) pf. (abhi, ava, ut, vi, sam) fix, support, prop up, consolidate, strengthen | stop, freeze, immobilize, paralyze — ca. (stambhayati) pp. (stambhita) fix, prop up; stop, immobilize.

stambha |agt. stambh| m. pillar, post, column, upright; tree trunk | soc. sacrificial post; syn. skandha [[dhvajastambha] soc. flagpole of a temple | obstacle; obstruction, suppression; rigidity; solidification | obstinacy; stupefaction, stupefaction | phil. |Tantra| paralysis by magic — f. stambhā ifc. pillar of (iic.).
stambhaka [agt. stambh] amnf stamb hikā act of stopping, immobilizing — m. pillar, post | lit. [KSS.] np. of the gaṇa stambhaka in charge of the security of Naravāhanadatta.
stambhakara [kara₁] amnf stambhakarī that obstructs; that paralyzes — m. fence; balustrade.
stambhakari [kari₁] m. ["which forms tufts"] rice.
stambhatā [tā] f. rigidity; paralysis.
stambhatīrtha | tīrtha | n. geo. n.p. from the port city of stambhatīrtha in Gujarat (mod. Khamb hat); cf. Vastupāla.
stambhana |agt. stambha| amnf stamb hanā that freezes, that immobilizes; paralyzing — act. n. paralysis; arrest by magic.
stambhita [pp. stambh] amnf stamb hitā fixed, paralyzed; suppressed, annihilated (not. by ma gie).
staraṇa [act. str] n. act of strewing or scattering | soc. not. arranging the sacrificial grass [kuśa] | act of coating or plastering.
starī [stṛ] f. heifer; barren cow || lat. sterilis; fr. sterile.
starya [pfp. [1] stṛ] amnf staryā to extend, to spread out.

stáva |obj. stu| m. lit. praise, eulogy; not. hymn of praise. sūryastavaḥ soc. hymn of worship of the Sun. stavacintāmaņi [cintāmaṇi] m. lit. [Trika] np. of the Stavacintāmaņi "Jewel of Praises", devotional stotra of worship of Shiva due to Bhatta Nārāyaṇa₆ (late 9th century); Kṣemarāja commented on it.
Stavamālā |mālā| f. bed. n.p. from the Stavamālā, a collection of devotional hymns by Rūpa Gosvāmī; cf. Yamunastaka.
stavarāja [rāja] m. lit. ["sovereign hymn"] va riante de la gāyatrī de Viśvāmitra.
stavaka [agt. stu] amnf stavikā who gives praise — obj. m. praise, eulogy.
stavana |act. stu| n. praise | pl. songs of praise.
stāva [obj. stu] m. praise, eulogy — agt. m. one who gives praise — f. stāvā myth. np. of the nymph [apsaras] stāvā.
stāvaka [agt. stu] amnf stāvikā who praises; who sings praise — m. eulogist, singer.
stāvya [pfp. [1] stu] amnf stāvyā to be praised, which should be praised.
√ stim v. [4] pr. (stimyati) pp. (stimita) to be stiff; to be fixed; to be wet.
stimita [pp. stim] amnf stimitā fixed, immobile | calm, tranquil; gentle, kind; moist — n. moisture; immobility, stiffness. stimitalocanah with a fixed gaze.
stīrṇá [pp. stṛ] amnf stīrṇā extended; strewn, scattered, strewn about.

√ stu v. [2] pr. (stauti) v. [5] pr. (stunoti) pft. (tuṣṭāva) was. (stoṣyati) aor. [3] (atuṣṭavat) aor. [4] (astauṣīt) aor. [5] (astāvīt) aor. p.s. (astāvi) pp. (stuta) pfp. (stutya, stāvya) ppr. p.s. (stūyamāna) abs. (stutvā, stutya) pf. (abhi, pra, sam) praise, celebrate, glorify — ps. (stūyate) to be praised — ca. (stāvayati) to praise; celebrate — ca. r. (stāvayate) to celebrate — dice. (tuṣṭūṣati) pp. (tuṣṭūṣita) to want to celebrate or glorify.
stúkā [related to stoka] f. lock, braid (of che veux); tuft, braid (not. of wool).
stut [agt. stu] amnf ifc. who praises, who celebrates (iic.) — f. hymn of praise.
stuta [pp. stu] amnf stutā praised, celebrated, glorified — n. praise; anthem; chanting of udgātṛ; cf. stotra.
stuti [act. stu] f. praise, panegyric; flattery.
stutyarthavāda [arthavāda] m. phil. [Mīmāṃsā] speech with a positive aim; opp. niṣedharthavāda.
stubdha [pp. stubh] amnf stubdhā sung, celebrated.
√ stubh v. [1] pr. (stobhati) pp. (stubdha) pf. (anu) to celebrate; to sing (not. a sāman).
stubh₁ [stubh] ifc. f. phon. variety of meter (according to the pause).
stūpa m. head; summit | heap, mound; mountain | bd. earthen mound or dome brick monument, conical in shape serving as a reliquary or commemorating an event in the life of the Buddha.
stūyamāna [ppr. ps. stu] amnf stūyamānā being praised.
stṛta [pp. stṛ] amnf stṛtā covered, strewn.

√ stṛ v. [9] pr. (stṛṇāti) pr. r. (stṛṇīté) v. [5] pr. (stṛṇóti) pr. r. (stṛṇuté) pp. (stīrṇa, stṛta) pf. (anu, ā, upa, pari, pra, vi) to extend, spread, scatter; to strew, cover with i. | to spread on the ground, to kill | lat. sterno; ang. to strew.
stená m. thief — v. [11] pr. (stenayati) to steal, to rob.
steya [related to stena] n. theft, robbery; stolen thing.
steyin [in] m. thief.

stoká amnf stokā small, brief, short, thin — m. drop; spark. stokam adv. a little; hardly; little by little — ifc. of the kind of (iic.). stokena muktah var. stokānmuktah just released. stokam pākah cooking a little. stokah pākah a little cooking. stokena na adv. not in the least. na stokāṃśenāpi not in the least.
stokátā [tā] f. smallness; insignificance.
stokátva [tva] n. id.
stokāt [abl. stoka] iic.
stokānmukta [mukta] amnf stokānmuktā just released.
stotrá [instr. stu] n. lit. praise, eulogy; hymn, ode | soc. hymn to be sung (opp. śastra₁ hymn to be recited); it consists of 5 parts: the
virtue [prastāva], the song [udgītha], the voices
lises [pratihāra], the attack [upadrava] and the finale [nidhana].
stotrīya [stotraīya] amnf stotrīyā re related to a stotra | var. stotriya f. stotriyā id.
stobha [obj. stubh] m. ved. syllable without meaning, interjection sung in a sāman lit. modulation of a stanza [rc₂] by non-meaningful phonetic additions | lack of respect, insolence; insult.
stóma [stuma] m. ved. praise; anthem | ritual singing; cf. prastāva, udgītha, pratihāra, upadrava, nidhana | mass, cluster, multitude — n. grain, riches.
styāna |pp. styā| amnf styānā coagulated, frozen — n. intensity, increase, extension | its reverberated.
styena [related to stena] m. thief.

strī f. [sg. acc. striyam strīm, i. striyā, dat. striyau, abl. g. striyās, loc. striyām; du. nom. striyau, i. strībhyām, loc. striyos; pl. nom. striyas, acc. striyas strīs, i. strībhis, g. strīṇām] woman; wife; female | [strīlinga] gram. feminine gender.
strīka [ka] amnf strīkā feminine.
strītā [tā] f. state of being a woman; femininity.
strītva |tva| n. feminine state | gram. state of being of the feminine gender.
strīdhana | dhana | n. soc. woman's property; dowry.
strīdharma [dharma] m. female condition; rights and duties of women.
strīnāman [nāman] amnf strīnāmnī which has a feminine name.
strīparvan | parvan | n. bed. n.p. from Strīparva, 11th book of the Mah., "of (lamentations of) women".
strīpumsa | pums | mr. of. male and female strīpumsau.
strīpuruṣa | puruṣa | m. of. man and woman; humanity.

strīpuruṣasāmānya [sāmānya] n. human type; the kāmaśāstra recognizes 4 types of woman: padminī, citrinī, śankhinī and hastinī and 4 types of man: śaśa, mṛga, vṛṣa and turaga; same classification in the Anangaranga and the Ratiramana. strīpurusasāmānyasāmudrikalaksaņa [sāmudrikalakṣaṇa] n. lit. section of chapter 8 of the Anangaranga dealing with the recognition of signs classifying the types of men and women.
strīpratyaya [pratyaya] m. gram. suffix for forming a feminine stem, affixed to a nominal base |prātipadika|. strīpratyayaprakaraṇam gram. formation of the feminine stem.
strībhāva [bhāva] m. state of being a woman; feminine state.
strīmaya [maya] amnf strīmayī of a feminine nature | effeminate.
strīvat [vat] amnf strīvatī like a woman.
straiṇa [*strīna] amnf straiṇī feminine; fe melle |concerning women; directed by women — n. the female sex | feminine nature.
stha [agt. sthā₁] ifc. amnf sthā who stands, who remains, who is (in, on, among, at) (iic.) occupied with, who practices, who does (iic.) | stay of (iic.) | lat. stabulum; fr. étable.
√ sthag v. [1] pr. (sthagati) pp. (sthagita) to cover; to conceal — ca. (sthagayati) to cover, to hide, to make disappear.
sthaga |agt. sthag| amnf sthagā clandes tin; fraudulent | eng. thugs.
sthagana |act. sthag| n. concealment.
sthagita [pp. sthag] amnf sthagitā hidden, disappeared.
sthandila [related to sthala] n. soc. sacrificial area, Vedic ritual site | earthen floor; field — amnf sthandilā who sleeps on the bare ground (in penance). śrīmadādyākālikāyāḥ devatāyāḥ sthaṇḍilāya
namah [Mahānirvāṇatantra] Honor to the sacred area of the Goddess, the revered primordial Kālikā.
sthaṇḍilaśayyā [śayyā] f. soc. act of lying down on the ground (as penance).
sthandilaśāyin [śāyin] amnf sthandilaśāyinī spread out on the ground.
sthapáti [sthapati] m. chieftain; governor, administrator | architect, builder | chamberlain, butler.

sthala [sthala] n. dry land, continent; eminence, plateau; dry ground, soil | surface; dear plan; terrace; place, location, spot; temple — m. chapter, section of a work — f. sthalī virgin ground | eminence; plateau — f. sthálā heap; pile of earth, tumulus || lat. locus; all. Stelle; fr. lieu.
sthalakamala | kamala | n. organic. red hibiscus flower; cf. sthalapadma.
sthalakamalinī [kamalinī] f. organic. bot. hibiscus mu tabilis, red hibiscus; cf. sthalapadminī. sābhre 'hnīvasthalakamalinīm na prabuddhām na
suptām [MD.] She neither sleeps nor watches, like the hibiscus flower on a cloudy day.
sthalapadma | padma | n. bio. flower of the hibiscus red, white in the morning and purple in the evening; it is offered to Surya and Kali.
sthalapadminī [padminī] f. organic. bot. hibiscus mu tabilis, red hibiscus.
sthalapurāṇa | purāṇa | n. lit. collection of stories and legends concerning a temple or other sacred place.
sthalamāhātmya [māhātmya] n. lit. work of glorification of a holy place; cf. talapurāṇa.
sthalavrksa [vrksa] m. soc. sacred tree of a temple.
sthavira [sthā₁ira] amnf sthavirā com pact, thick, dense | Ancient, antique, venerable — m. bd. Ancient (said of the oldest monks [bhikṣu]); cf. theravāda.
sthavirāvalī |āvalī| f. bed. n.p. of the sthavirāvalī, section of the Kalpasūtra jaina, dealing with homage to the ancient masters.
sthā₁ cf. stha₁.

√ sthā₁ v. [1] pr. (tiṣṭhati) pr. r. (tiṣṭhate) pft. (tasthau) pft. r. (tasthe) aor. [1] (asthāt) pp. (sthita) ppr. (tisthat) ppft. (tasthivas) pf. (adhi, anu, abhi, ava, ā, ut, upa, ni, pari, pra, prati, vi, sam) to stand; to remain motionless | to stay, to remain; to persist, to subsist, to last; to stop, to tend | to be present, to exist; to be in a certain place | to be available to; to rely on, to occupy oneself, to be busy with, to practice; to adhere to, to follow | to conform to (loc.) | to offer oneself to (dat.) — ps. (sthīyate) to remain motionless; to submit — ca. (sthāpayati) aor. [3] (atiṣṭhipat) to put, place; to appoint, establish; to stop; to offer the presidency | gr. ; lat. sto; all. stehen; ang. to stand; fr. stable. tistha stop! sthāpaya stop (acc.). vrksastisthati the tree rises. vrksam sthāpayati he sets the tree upright. anyathā sthā to behave differently. maunena sthā to keep silent. samam sthā to treat someone (loc.) as an equal. sukham sthā to feel at ease; to be happy. mayā sthīyatām I submit. svadharme sthā to do one's duty. svakarmani sthā to mind one's own business. saṃśaye sthā persist in one's doubts. tisthatu bhoh please stay. tisthatu tisthet let's leave it at that! svam ratham sthāpaya stop your chariot. śāsane tiṣṭha bhartuḥ follow the master's instructions. chāttrāya tiṣṭhate kanyā the young girl offers herself to the student. dhanibhyas tisthate veśyā the prostitute offers herself to the rich. nrpatau tisthate janah the man takes the king as his arbiter. tvayā tatraiva sthīyatām stay here, I beg you.
sthānu [agt. sthā₁] amnf firm, fixed, immutable | tree trunk, pillar, post, column | soc. ritual pole of the vājapeya — m. myth. np. from sthā₁ņu "pillar (of fire)", one of the 11 breaths of
wines [marut]; epithet of Shiva; his sign [tejolinga] is worshipped as Arunācaleśvara. sthāṇuṃ vande I pay homage to ShivaSthānu.
sthāṇvīśvara |īśvara| m. geo. np. of sthāṇvīśvara "Lord of the burning pillar", foundation linga of sthāneśvara.
sthāṇḍilá [*sthaṇḍila] amnf sthāṇḍilā soc. who sleeps on the bare ground as a result of a religious vow.
sthātṛ [agt. sthā₁] m. guide, driver (of horses, etc.) | authority — amnf sthātrī immo bile; opp. jagat.

sthāna [act. sthā₁] n. posture, position; state, rank, function, dignity, grade; condition of stay, residence, abode, seat; sanctuary; throne | room, chamber | continuation, status quo (as long as (i.) | site, locality, location, place, spot, place; province, region, domain, sphere | suitable place; fortress | defense of the position by a troop (opp. charge [yuddha]) | occurrence, case, section; occasion, cause phon. position of articulation; cf. utpattisthāna | med. [Ayurveda] medical act; cf. astasthāna — ifc. in place of, which stands in for, which plays the role of; represented by (iic.). sthāne adv. appropriately, rightly; judiciously, in a suitable manner | in place of, instead of (g. iic. sthāne sthāne everywhere, in all places. sthānesthāne var. sthānesthānesu at different rights, here and there. yathāsthānam adv. each to his place.

sthānacitra |citra| n. lit. learned poetry |varnacitra| with constraints on the families of phonemes used. gāngāngakākākagāhakāghakakākahā agā ahāhānka khagānkāgakankāgakhagakākaka (all in gutturals) O traveler, who bathes in the winding current of the Ganges waves; you do not know the sad sound of the world's sufferings; you can go as far as Mount Meru; you are not under the sway of deceiving senses; you, who dispel sins, have come to this land.
sthānaniyama [niyama] m. bed. lipogram.
sthānapati [pati] m. soc. head of an institution; not. superior of a monastery.
sthānānga [anga₁] n. [Sthānāngasūtra] lit. np. of the Sthānāngasūtra, 3rd text of the jaina canon, treatise on the set of the 10 doctrinal subjects (ard hamāgadhī, 3rd century).
sthānādhipati [adhipati] m. cf. sthānapati.

sthāneśvara [īśvara] n. geo. np. of the pilgrimage city sthāneśvara (mod. Thāneswar in Ha riyāṇa); it was the capital of King Harṣa, dedicated to Sthānvīśvara; it was sacked by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1011.
sthānaka [sthānaka] n. position, situation; rank, dignity | place; locality.
sthāni iic. sthānin.
sthānivat |vat| adv. such as the original element | gram. said of the substitute if it is subject to all the rules applicable to the original element.
sthānyāśraya [āśraya] amnf sthānyāśrayā gram, which depends on the original form (during substitution).

sthānin [sthānain] amnf sthāninī in its place; permanent; appropriate — m. gram. original form; positional marker to be substituted (opp. ādeśa the substitute); e.g. ktvā is the sthānī of lyap, which is its ādeśa.

sthāp [ca. sthā₁] v. [10] pr. (sthāpayati) pp. (sthāpita) pfp. (sthāpya) abs. (sthāpayitvā) to put, place; to name, establish; to stop; to erect | to make continue, to strengthen; to confirm; to support; to maintain— ps. (sthāpyate) to be placed. kim dosapakse sthāpayāmi who should I declare guilty?
sthāpaka [agt. ca. sthā₁] amnf sthāpikā who places, who fixes, who establishes; who erects (not. an idol) | arch. priest officiating at the foundation of a building — ifc. founder of (iic.).
sthāpatya [*sthapatia] m. guardian of the women's quarters — n. office of district governor architecture, building construction.
Sthāpatyaveda [veda] m. bed. n.p. of the Sthāpatyaveda or science of architecture, an upaveda.

sthāpana [agt. ca. sthā₁] amnf sthāpanā that places, that fixes; that maintains, that preserves — act. nf sthāpanā establishment, maintenance; ins institute, fixing; definition | regulation, management; preservation, reinforcement.
sthāpayitvā [abs. ca. sthā₁] ind. having placed, having established, having stopped.
sthāpita [pp. ca. sthā₁] amnf sthāpitā fixed, established, named; deposited; placed in reserve.
sthāpya [pfp. [1] ca. sthā₁] amnf sthāpyā to install, to establish (not. idol) | to place on or in (loc) | which must be made immobile | to enclose (not. in the house | veśmani|).
sthāma iic. sthāman. neighing.
sthāyi iic. sthāyin.
sthāyitā [tā] f. stability, invariance; durability; permanence.
sthāyitva |tva| n. id.

sthāyibhāva | bhāva | m. enduring state of mind; stable feeling | phil. |Nāṭyaśāstra| stable mood, emotion; Bharatamuni in list 8: erotic desire [rati], humor [hāsa], sorrow [śoka], anger [krodha], courage [utsāha], fear [bhaya], disgust [jugupsā] and astonishment [vismaya₁]; these emotions are conveyed in the theater by 8 modes
aesthetics [rasa]; Udbhaṭa added tranquility [śama] to them; opp. vyabhicāribhāva.
sthāyin [agt. sthā₁] amnf sthāyinī stable, persistent, lasting; stubborn. sthāyībhū to become permanent. rāgaḥ śuklapaṭe sthāyībhavatī the color red leaves indelible marks on white fabric.
sthāla [*sthala] n. container, receptacle; dish, pot, cauldron; cooking utensil (in metal) — f. cf. sthālī.
sthālavrkṣa [vrkṣa] m. ["site tree"] sacred tree of a temple.
sthālī [f. sthāla] f. container, dish; saucepan, cauldron, pot. randhanāya sthālī cauldron for cooking. sthālyāmodanam pacyati he/she cooks rice in the cauldron.
sthālīpakva | pakva | amnf sthālīpakvā cooked in a dish.
sthālīpāka [pāka] m. soc. oblation of a dish of rice or barley cooked in milk; it is consumed during the mahāvrata.
sthālīpulāka [pulāka] m. rice cooked in a cauldron.
sthālīpulākanyāya [nyāya] m. phil. maxim of inference of the property of an object from that of one of its parts, as we know that rice is cooked by tasting a grain | significant example.

sthāvará [sthā₁vara] amnf sthāvarā that stands upright; immobile; stable; constant, invariable | not capable of movement — n. the plant kingdom; opp. trasa, jangama, cara | stability; permanence | soc. inalienable family properties — m. pl. sthāvarās plants.
sthāvaraka [ka] m. lit. np. of sthāvaraka, servant of Saṃsthānaka in the Mṛcchakaṭikā.
sthāvarajangama [jangama] amnf sthāvarajangamā mobile and immobile — m. of. animals and plants.
sthāvaratā |tā| f. immobility, permanence | state of being vegetable or mineral.
sthāvaratva |tva| n. id.
sthāvaralinga [linga] n. soc. linga fixes, not. in a sanctuary; opp. istalinga.
sthāvira [*sthavira] amnf sthāvirā old; senile — n. old age.
sthāsnu [agt. sthā₁] amnf firm; stationary; fixed | durable, permanent; eternal.
sthāsnutā [tā] f. firmness; stability; permanence.

sthitá [pp. sthā₁] amnf sthitā standing, motionless; waiting | busy with, doing; firm, constant | conforming, following, in charge; resolute, convinced | present, ready, available; settled, established, admitted, fixed | belonging to (g.); dependent on (loc.); leading to (dat.) — n. action of stopping, of remaining | gr. o; lat. sta tus; fr. statut. evam sthite adv. that being; thereupon. purah sthite in this imminence. sthitam tena he waited. upaviśya sthitah he remains seated. katham sthitāsi how vastu?
sthitátā [tā] f. the state of being established.

sthitáprajña [prajña] amnf sthitaprajñā firm in his convictions; who agrees his actions and his ideals; whose behavior is ethical; wise, calm, just; enlightened; reliable, sincere; respectful, kind, modest.
sthitalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] amnf sthitalakṣaṇā gram. (meaning) stable in nature; opp. apoddhārapadārtha.

list [advaita]; they were composed by Kallața (9th century) under the direction of his master Vasu gupta; his son Mukula made a commentary on them; Rāmakantha made the gloss |vivṛtti|.

sphotavāda [vāda] m. phil. thesis of Bhartrhari postulating the existence of an indivisible unit of meaning |abheda| inherent in a word or phrase | lit. np. of the Sphotavāda "Doctrine of Evocative Power", work of Nāgeśa.
sphotaśataka [śataka] n. gram. n.p. from the sphotaśataka, treatise by Kṛṣṇaśāstrī Arade.

sphotasiddhi [siddhi] f. lit. np. of the Sphotasiddhi "Knowledge of the cognitive process", work of Maṇḍana Miśra refuting Kumārila Bhaṭṭa and establishing the Doctrine of the evocative power (9th century); Rsiputra Paramesvara made the commentary Gopālikā.
sphotāyana [āyana₁] m. hist. np. of Sphotāyana, ancient grammarian prior to Pāṇini.
sphotaka [agt. sphut] amnf sphotikā med. eruption (not. smallpox); abscess, tumor.

sphotana [agt. sphut] amnf sphotanā that bursts; that breaks, that destroys — m. myth. np. of sphotana, epith. of Shiva "Destroyer" — f. sphoṭanī drill — act. n. act of beating, tearing, bursting | threshing (grain) | act of waving the arms or cracking one's fingers.
sphotita [pp. ca. sphut] amnf sphotitā burst, torn, split; revealed — n. fissure.
sphotya [pfp. [1] sphut] amnf sphotyā to break, to split.

sphotyābhujanga [bhujanga] n. organic. bot. Raphi dophora laciniata, variety of philodendron, liana climbing along tree trunks; its stems are used medicinally; its leaves are reminiscent of a split cobra's cap, hence its name.
sphya n. ved. wooden sword used in rituals | oar.

The past participle *sma*, used to express assertion, gives the present tense an imperfective aspect and the tense of a narrative, progressive, or habitual past (imperfective aspect, whereas the imperfect is only a preterite) | slightly reinforces, notably after *iti*, *na*, *mā₂* | with the imperative for a polite request. *mā sma śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ* do not give in to grief. *balamadhyāpaya sma* please instruct the child.
smaya [act. smi] m. pride.
smayitvā [abs. smi] ind. having smiled; smiling.
smar [ca. smṛ] v. [10] pr. (smarayati) pp. (smārita) to remind someone of something (acc.); to make someone remember; to make someone regret.
smara [act. smr] m. memory, recollection; ob session | amorous desire; sexual love | myth. np. of smara "Obsession (of love)", epithet of the god Kāma. smarasi smara | KuS. | love, you remember.
smarakūpa [kūpa] m. vulva; syn. bhaga.
smarakūpaka [kūpaka] m. ["little well of love"] (poetry) female sexual organ.
smaragrha [grha] n. id.
smarageha [geha] n. id.
smarachattra [chattra] n. ["umbrella of love"] clitoris.
smaradhvaja | dhvaja | m. male sexual organ — n. female sexual organ.
smaramandira [mandira] n. ["temple of love"]; cf. smaragrha.
smarastambha [stambha] m. ["pillar of love"] or male sexual gane.
smarānkuśa [ankuśa] m. ["fang of love"] nail.
smarānala [anala] m. fires of love.
smarana [act. smr] n. invocation in thought; thought, memory; reminiscence; memory | phil. tradition [Yoga] meditation by mental recitation of the name of a deity.
smartavya [pfp. [3] smṛ] amnf smar tavyā that which can or should be remembered, memorable — f. smartavyā memory. smara yat smartavyam remember that which you should remember.
smartṛ [agt. smṛ] amnf smartrī who remembers (of (iic. g.)) — m. recorder.
smartṛtva [tva] n. memory; the act of remembering.
smarya [pfp. [1] smṛ] amnf smaryā to remember; memorable.
smāra [obj. smr] ifc. mr. memory of (iic.).
smārita [pp. ca. smṛ] amnf smāritā recalled; remembered — n. action of remembering.

smārta [*smṛtia] amnf smārtā relating to memory | phil. based on smṛti ; traditional, legal; that which follows tradition [smṛti] — m. jurist | soc. Brahmin performing domestic rites (as opposed to a priest officiating in a temple) | soc. designates certain Brahmins who worship both Shiva and Vishnu | soc. Brahmin who follows only śruti and smṛti (opp. vaiṣṇava also following the pañcarātrās). smārtavyavasthārņava | vyavasthārņava | m. lit. np. of the Smārtavyavasthārņava, treatise by Raghunātha Sārvabhauma.
smārtasūtra |sūtra| n. pl. soc. collection of injunctions
rituals [kalpasūtra] concerning domestic rites; cf. gṛhasūtra, dharmasūtra.

√ smi v. [1] pr. (smayati) pr. r. (smayate) pp. (smita) pf. (ut, vi) to smile; to bloom; to laugh softly | to blush; to bloom (flower) | to show pride; to be arrogant — ca. (smāyayati) ca. (smāpayati) to make smile; to mock — des. (sismayiṣati) to desire to smile | gr. μειδαω; lat. mi rus, miror; ang. smile.
smita [pp. smi] amnf smitā who smiles; blossoming, flowering — n. smile.
smitavat [ppa. smi] amnf smitavatī who smiled. buddhaḥ smitavān Buddha smiled (mod. coded message announcing the first Indian atomic test).

√ smr v. [1] pr. (smarati) fut. (smarisyati) pft. (sasmāra) pp. (smṛta) pf. (anu, vi, sam) to remember; to recall (acc. g.) | to think of (acc.); to teach — ps. (smaryate) to be kept in memory (impers.) it is said that, tradition teaches — ca. (smārayati) pp. (smārita) to remind someone of something (acc.); to make someone remember; to make someone regret | gr. μερμερος; lat. memor; ang. memory; fr. mémoire. aham mātaram smarāmi var. aham mātuh smarāmi I remember my mother.

smṛta |pp. smṛ| amnf smṛtā recalled, remembered; what or whom one thinks of | taught, prescribed (by the smṛti ); that which is declared by tradition to be, that which is considered to be, legal. smṛtaṃ mayā I remember.

smṛti [act. smṛ] f. faculty of memorization; memory lit. tradition, epic; body of traditional sacred and legal texts (opp. śruti, revealed knowledge) | phil. | yoga | the call to memory, a cittavrtti | myth. [VP.] np. of Smrti, wife of Angirā; she is mother of Anumati. smṛtīnāmm nāśaḥ loss of memory.
smṛtikaraṇḍikā [karaṇḍikā] f. bed. n.p. of the Smrtikarandika.
smṛtikalpadruma | kalpadruma | mr. bed. n.p. of smṛtikalpadruma.
Smṛtikaumudī [kaumudī] f. bed. n.p. of the Smrtikaumudī.
smrtikaumudītīkā [tīkā] f. bed. n.p. of the Smṛtikaumudītīkā.
smrtigītā [gītā] f. bed. n.p. of Smrtigītā.
smrtitattva [tattva] n. lit. np. of the Smrtitattva, of collections of dharmaśāstra together of Raghunandana₁ Bhattācārya.
smṛtinibandhakāra | nibandhakāra | m. author of smṛti literature.
smrtipāthaka [pāthaka] m. lawyer, judge.
smrtibhramśa [bhramśa| m. memory loss.
smrtirodha [rodha₂] m. memory loss, forgetfulness.
smṛtilopa [lopa] m. id.
smṛtivibhrama [vibhrama] m. false memory.
smṛtiviruddha [viruddha] amnf smṛtiviruddhā illegal; unjust.
smṛtivirodha | virodha | m. illegality; injustice | disagreement over the interpretation of the law.
Smṛtiviveka [viveka] m. lit. np. of the text of laws Smrtiviveka. smṛtisammata sammata amnf smṛtisammatā approved by law.
smṛtisādhya [sādhya] amnf smṛtisādhyā which can be justified by law.
smṛtisiddha [siddha₁] amnf smṛtisiddhā conforming to the law.
smṛtimat [smṛtimat] amnf smṛtimatī who remembers; who has a good memory | versed in sacred tradition | who enables one to remember.
smera [smira] amnf smerā smiling, friendly, calm; blossoming, open (not. flower); proud | evident — ifc. full of, joyful of (iic.) — m. smile; laughter. smerīkī smile. smerīkṛta smiling.
smeramukha | mukha | amnf smeramukhī with a smiling face.
syá [m. tyad] pn. start. mr. [sg. name. syas, acc. tyam ved. this, the ; that one.
sya₁ nota. gram. modifier | vikarana₂ | of formation of the periphrastic future | lut|.
syáda [act. syand] m. speed.
√ syand v. [1] pr. r. (syandate) pf. (abhi, ni) to run, to rush; to flow, to trickle, to gush — ca. (syandayati) to flow, to run; to make flow, to make run.
syanda [act. syand] m. the act of flowing, trickling, seeping.

syandaná |agt. syand| amnf syandanī swift (chariot, wind) | flowing (river); that ripples saddle, that waters — m. chariot (of war) — act. n. flow, stream; rapid movement; circulation; leak, outpouring; water — f. syandanī saliva.
syandin [agt. syand] amnf syandinī that flows, that runs; that runs; that emits a liquid, that leaks; that drops (iic.) — f. syandinī saliva.

syamantaka m. myth. [VP.] np. of the jewel [mani] syamantaka, favorable to the righteous and harmful to the wicked; it gives gold to those who worship it with devotion, and protects from diseases; Sūrya gave it to Satrājit who gave it to his brother Prasena, who was killed by a lion, killed in turn by Jāmbavān; Kṛṣṇa, wrongly suspected of theft, fought the latter for twenty-eight days and obtained the jewel, which he wears on his wrist | bd. np. of an actor from a previous life of the Buddha, model of filial piety, to be compared with sravaņakumāra.
syā [f. tyad] pn. dem. f. [sg. nom. syā, acc. tyām] ved. this, the.
syāt [opt. as₁] adv. perhaps, it may be | provided that, may it happen that | may it come to pass. sāyamprātarāśyeva syāt One can eat only two meals a day, in the morning and in the evening.

syādvāda [vāda] m. phil. [jn.] Jain agnosticism; it postulates the relativity of truth according to the point of view [nayavāda] by proposing a modal logic according to different modes of predication which allows one to account for the multiform nature of reality | anekāntavāda | and can accommodate different ontological presuppositions, notably the seven aspects of reality [saptabhangī].
Syādvādamañjarī [mañjarī] f. jn. n.p. from the Syādvādamañjarī “Bouquet of Agnosticism”, work by Mallisena.

syāla var. śyāla m. brother-in-law (brother of his wife) | favorite of the king | scoundrel, rogue (insult) — f. syālī var. śyālī sister-in-law (sister of his wife) hi. sālā. syālajāyā var. śyālajāyā [jāyā] f. wife of a brother of his wife.
syū [instr. sīv] f. thread; string.
syūtá [pp. sīv] amnf syūtā woven; sewn; assembled (clothing) — m. jute sack.
syūna [sīvna] m. jute sack.
syota [syūta] m. bag.
syoná [sīvna] amnf syonā pleasant, comfortable, soft (not. for walking or sitting) | tender, soft — n. soft layer, comfortable seat; pleasant situation | happiness.
syonáśī [śī₂] amnf who rests comfortably.
√ sraṃs v. [1] pr. r. (sraṃsate) pp. (srasta) pf. (vi) to fall; to collapse — ca. (sraṃsayati) to cause to fall. sramsate dehabandhah the whole body collapses.
sraṃsana |act. sraṃs| n. fall; relaxation, the act of loosening — agt. amnf sraṃsanī laxative.
sramsita [pp. ca. srams] amnf sramsitā that one has dropped; loosened, slackened.
sraṃsin [agt. sraṃs] amnf sraṃsinī that falls, that detaches.
srag iic. sraj.
sragdāman [dāman₂] n. garland thread | garland. sragdāma kṣip to throw a garland at.
sragdhara | dhara | amnf sragdharā who wears a garland — f. sragdharā lit. syllabic poetic meter, of 4 feet of 21 syllables, with caesuras after the 7th and 14th.
sragvat [vat] amnf sragvatī crowned, who wears a garland.
sragvin |vin| amnf sragviņī crowned, who wears a garland.
sráj [act. srj₁] f. [nom. srak] garland of flowers, wreath; rosary worn on the head; ring, chain | series, suite.
sraja [act. srj₁] m. ifc. garland of, suite of [iic.] — v. [11] pr. (srajayati) to decorate with a garland.
srajas [abstr. sṛj₁] ifc. n. garland of, sequence of (iic.).
srava |agt. sru| m. current, flow — ifc. course of (iic.) | that spreads.
sravaṇa |act. sru| n. current, flow, stream.
sravat |ppr. sru| amnf sravantī flowing — f. river.
sravas [abstr. sru] ifc. n. flow of (iic.).
sraṣṭṛ [agt. sru] amnf sraṣṭrī [sg. nom. sraṣṭā, acc. sraṣṭāram] ["that which makes flow"] producer, creator | myth. np. of sraṣṭā, epith. of Brahmā "the Creator".
sras |agt. sraṃs| ifc. amnf |sg. nom. srat| that falls from (iic.). ukhāsrat that falls from the pot.
srasta [pp. sraṃs] amnf srastā fallen, dropped, escaped (from (abl. iic.)) | released; pen
tooth | sunken (eyes) | dislocated.
srastatā |tā| f. state of being cowardly or flabby.
srāv [ca. sru] v. [10] pr. (srāvayati) to flow, to pour.
srāva [agt. sru] m. flow (not. of blood), discharge.

√ sru v. [1] pr. (sravati) pp. (sruta) pf. (ā, ava, pari, pra, sam) to flow, to run, to spread; to gush from, to emanate from (abl.) | to leak (from a container), to disappear; to come prematurely, to abort — ca. (srāvayati) to cause to flow, to pour || gr. ρεω; all. Strom; ang. stream.
sruk cf. sruc.
Srughna n. geo. n.p. from the town of Srughna, north of Hastināpura.
sruc [related to sru] f. [sg. nom. sruk] soc. large wooden spoon (used in oblation) — m. srukka ifc. id. — f. srukkā ifc. id.
srut [related to sru] ifc. amnf that emits, from which flows.
sruta |pp. sru| amnf srutā which flows, which spreads, which gushes forth; which flees; emptied — n. flow.
srutí [act. sru] f. flow, effusion (of (iic.)) | fall (of snow).
sruva [related to sru] m. soc. small wooden spoon, used in the oblation to pour the butter |ghṛta|.
sruvataru | taru| mr. cf. sruvavṛkṣa. sruvavrksa vrksa m. organic. bot. Flacourtia jango mas, small tree with round purple fruits; its wood is used to make sacrificial instruments; syn. vikankata.
srota [srótas] mn current, flow — f. srotā ifc. flow of || pali sota.
srotāpatti |āpatti| f. bd. entry into the flow (of the noble path |āryamārga| leading to nirvāṇa); it is the first of the four stages of enlightenment.

srotāpanna [āpanna] amnf srotāpannā bd. title of spiritual qualification: ["one who has entered the flow"] (which leads to nirvāṇa) by freeing himself from the three fetters: belief in the reality of the self, skepticism and attachment to rites; he conducts himself well in deeds, words and thoughts pali sotapanna.
srótas [abstr. sru] n. flow, current, course; river, torrent; surge, rush of (iic.) | spout of a jug | med. canal or opening (of the human body); or gane of the senses | lineage, heredity.
srotaḥpati [pati] m. ocean.
sraughna [*Srughna] amnf sraughṇī geo. originating from or inhabiting the town of Srughna | born in, located in, coming from, leading to, found especially in, inhabiting Srughna, etc.
sva pn. mnf svā his, her, his | (reflexive pronoun, in oblique cases) cf. ātman — amnf svā own, personal — m. man of his own family, of his

people ["one of his own"]; relationship, friend, ally — n. his own self, his ego — mn his own property, his fortune — f. svā soc. woman of his own caste || lat. sūs; fr. soi. svīkr to appropriate. svam nāma kathaya say your name.
svákarman [karman] n. his own act; his own affair (opp. the affairs of others).
svakārya [kārya] n. his own occupation.
svakāryārthin [arthin] amnf svakāryārthinī selfish.
svakuśala [kuśala] n. his own well-being.
svakuśalamaya [maya] amnf svakuśalamayī concerning his own well-being.
svakṛta |kṛta| amnf svakṛtā done by oneself spontaneous — n. personal accomplishment.
svakṛtya [kṛtya] n. his own duty, his responsibility.
svagata | gata | amnf svagatā in one's own words; in private | came to mind. svagatam adv. to oneself; (theatre) aside.
svagrāma [grāma] m. his own village of origin.

svacchanda [chanda] amnf svacchandā who follows his own pleasure | independent; spontaneous — m. his own will, his own pleasure; free will. svacchandāt var. svacchandena adv. following his own pleasure; freely; spontaneously; independently. svacchandatas adv. id.
svacchandatantra [tantra] n. bed. n.p. from the Svacchan datingra, kaula text; Kṣemarāja commented on it.
svacchandabhairava | Bhairava | mr. phil. Spontaneous Bhairava, kaula concept.
Svacchandabhairavatantra [tantra] n. bed. n.p. from the Svacchandabhairavatantra, kaula text.
svájana [jana] m. compatriot; relative | his own people; his clan — f. svajanā ifc. of the clan (iic.).
svájāti [jāti] amnf of his own kind — f. his own kind, caste, family or race.
svajātīya [īya] amnf svajātīyā ["which is of its own kind" | similar, equal, alike.

svatantra [tantra] amnf svatantrā ["which is subject only to its own rule" free, independent, autonomous — m. gram. the autonomous actor; its semantic role [kāraka] is that of agent [kartr]. svatantrah kartā gram. |Pāṇini| the agent is the independent actor.
svatantratā |tā| f. freedom, independence, autonomy.
Svatantrika [ika] m. bd. n.p. of the doctrine bd. Svatantrika or Svātantrika.
svatva |tva| n. possession, ownership (of (loc.)) | independence.
svatvatvat |vat| amnf svatvatvat having property rights.
svadeśa | deśa | mr. homeland, country of origin | pl. com patriots.
svadeśin [in] amnf svadeśinī national, in native language.

svadharma [dharma] m. specific role of the individual; personal duty | soc. duty of one's social class; opp. sādhāranadharma. svadharma labh to have one's rights recognized. svadharma viguņaļ śreyān paradharmāt
svanusthitāt [BhG.] It is better to do one's own duty badly than to excel in that of others.

svadhā [dhā₃] f. personal power, natural authority | natural state; usage, custom, cultural environment; law; ethics | place of origin; home. Soc. sacrifice to the gods; not. offering of water or clarified butter as a libation to the ancestors in the pitryajña — interj. invocation of blessing by offering the libation to the ancestors | śrāddha|. svade of the. his two residences: on Earth and in Heaven. anusvadhām var. svadhāmanu adv. of his own accord; naturally, easily, freely. svadhākṛ soc. to perform the ritual invocation svadhā. svadhāstu interj. soc. that the libation be beneficial.
svanāman [nāman] n. his own name.
svapada [pada] n. his own place or rank.
svapadavigraha [vigraha] amnf svapadavi grahā gram. said of a compound word whose para phrase can be expressed with its subcomponents. svaparņaśālā [parṇaśālā] f. his own hut.
svapitr [pitr] m. his own father.
sváprakāśa [prakāśa] amnf svaprakāśā evident in itself.
svaprakāśatva |tva| n. self-evidence; the act of manifesting oneself.

svábhāva [bhāva] m. natural disposition, innate or spontaneous nature; own nature; character | bd. [Yogācāra] atemporal determinant of ontological status; cf. trisvabhāva — f. svabhāvā ifc. own existence of (iic.). svabhāvāt adv. by nature. nāsti svabhāvo bhāvānām bd. [Nāgārjuna] Nothing has its own nature.
svábhāvakṛta [kṛta] amnf svabhāvakṛtā done naturally; natural.

svabhāvaja [ja] amnf svabhāvajā né spon tanément; inné — n. [svabhāvajavarṇa] refers to a primary color: white, red, yellow and blue [nīla]; by mixing, secondary colors |samyogajavarna| and auxiliary colors |upavarna| are obtained. svabhāvajam dhāma natural energy | inner light.
svábhāvatā [tā] f. natural state.
svábhāvatva |tva| n. id.
svábhāvadaurjanya [daurjanya] n. natural wickedness.
svábhāvadveṣa [dveṣa] m. natural aversion.
svábhāvabhāva [bhāva] m. natural disposition.

svabhāvavat [vat] ifc. amnf svabhāvavatī which has the nature of (iic.). devo'smi nacānyo'smi | brahmaivāham na śokabhāk | saccidānandarūpo'ham | nityamuktasvabhāvavān | | Nityakarmā| I am neither God nor other; unlike Brahman, I feel no pain; I am existence, consciousness, and joy; my own nature is to be eternally liberated.
svabhāvaśūnya [śūnya] amnf svabhāvaśūnyā phil. empty of being clean.
svabhāvasamsiddha [samsiddha] amnf svabhāvasaṃsiddhā accomplished spontaneously; innate. svabhāvasamsiddhalakṣaṇāt according to the laws inherent in nature.
svabhāvasiddha |siddha₁| afmn svabhāvasiddhā phil. naturally true, flowing from its nature; innate | obvious.
svabhāvasiddhatva [vat] n. natural disposition. svabhāvasiddhatvāt due to their natural disposition.
svabhāvasaukumārya [saukumārya] n. bed. natural beauty.
svabhāvahetu [hetu] m. phil. reason of essential nature, concept. bd. due to Dharmakīrti.
svabhāvika [ika] amnf svabhāvikā phil. spontaneous | gram. is said of an indeclinable having neither gender nor number.
svabhāvikatva |vat| n. phil. |Vedānta| spontaneous state.
svabhāvokta [ukta] amnf svabhāvoktā declared spontaneously.

svabhāvokti [ukti] f. spontaneous declaration; natural expression | naturalistic description, faithful description of the properties of something. lit. ["expression of inherent nature"] poetic method [alamkāra] of picturesque description, using miniature poems inspired by nature, with few figures of speech.
svábhū [bhū₂] self-generated amnf — m. myth. differs from Brahmā, from Viṣṇu, from Siva.
svábhūmi [bhūmi] f. his own country.
svamedhā [medhā] f. own intelligence.
sváyoni [yoni] f. own origin — consanguineous amnf | coming from oneself.
svárasa | rasa | m. his natural taste | his natural inclination.

svarāj [rāj₂] amnf [sg. nom. svarāt] autonomous, independent — m. autonomy; independence; to determination | phil. principle of self; microcosm; opp. virāj₂ | myth. Indra's own sovereignty; opp. samrāj.
svarūpa | rūpa | n. proper nature, natural, essence of (g. iic.) | phil. essential property of an object — ifc. which has the form of (iic.). svarūpeņa adv. in reality; in itself.
svarūpapadārthaka [padārthaka] amnf svarūpapadārthikā gram. autonym.
svarūpamantra | mantra | mn phil. so nore essence of a divinity.
svarūpavācin [vācin] amnf svarūpavācinī gram. is said of words in self-referential use.
svarūpavimarśa [vimarśa] m. phil. [Trika] self-reflexive Reality.
svarūpasambandha [sambandha] m. phil. [Nyāya] relation of particular qualification; it is specific to a qualifier-qualified pair.
svarūpasthiti [sthiti] f. ["maintenance of its essence" sincerity, naturalness, authenticity.
svarūpāsiddhi [asiddhi] f. phil. lack of proof, not established by the intrinsic nature of the subject.
svarūpin [rūpin] amnf svarūpinī which has its natural form — ifc. which appears in the form of (iic.).
svarocis [rocis] n. its own light — amnf that illuminates by itself.

sválakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] amnf svalakṣaṇā which has its own characteristics — n. particular sign; opp. sāmānyalakṣaṇa | phil. [Dinnāga] the thing-in-itself, unique particular event constituting reality; interpreted by a yogācārin as a moment of consciousness, by a sautrāntika as an external temporal point | bd. real particular event, object of perception [pratyakṣa]; as opposed to a universal |sāmānya|, object of inference |anumāna|.
sválikhita [likhita] n. document written in one's own hand.
svávrtta [vrtta] n. his own occupation.
svávrtti [vrtti] f. his own way of life | his own existence | lit. his own commentary.
svaśākhā [śākhā] f. soc. personal Vedic affiliation of a Brahmin.
svasamvid [samvid₂] f. self-awareness.
svasamvedana [samvedana] n. phil. autonomous awareness.
svastha |stha| amnf svasthā natural, healthy; fit, at ease; content | independent; confident; resolute. svastham calmly, composedly.
svasthatā [tā] f. ease, well-being, comfort, satisfaction.
svasthāna | sthāna | n. home, proper dwelling — amnf svasthānā who stays at home; who stays in her place — f. Svasthānī myth. np. of Svasthānī, goddess of her own residence.
svasva [red.] iic. his own (ifc.) | (ifc.) mutual; his (ifc.) respective.

svasvāmibhāva [svāmibhāva] m. gram. relation between the one who possesses and that which is possessed (one of the uses of g.) | phil. [Vedānta] relation between the Self and the Soul; cf. bimbabimbībhāva.
sváhasta [hasta] m. one's own hand | one's own handwriting; signature, autograph. svahastam dā to offer one's hand for (loc.). svahasto mama (inscription, colophon) in my own hand.
sváhita [hita₁] amnf svahitā directed towards oneself, which benefits oneself — n. one's own interest. svahitaparāthaņo mā bhūḥ that your own interest is not your primary goal.
sváhitaisin | eṣin | amnf svahitaisinī who seeks his own advantage.
svānga [anga₁] n. member of one's own body; one's own body.
svādhīna [adhīna] amnf svādhīnā which depends only on itself; independent; free | which is in its own power.
svādhīnatā |tā| f. autonomy, independence; freedom.
svādhīnatva |tva| n. id.

svādhīnapatikā [pati] f. soc. woman whose husband is under her control. svapne'pi samareșu tvām vijayaśrīrna muñcati | prabhāvaprabhavam kāntam svādhīnapatikā yathā [Kāvyaprakāśa] in battle, victory will not abandon you, for even in a dream, even an independent woman does not abandon her husband, the source of her splendor.
svādhīnabhartṛkā [bhartṛ] f. id.
svānubhava [anubhava] m. personal experience.
svānubhāva [anubhāva] m. personal feeling.
svānubhūti [anubhūti] f. personal experience.
svānusthāna [anusthāna] n. personal action.
svāśrama [āśrama] mn soc. rule of conduct specific to one's own stage of life.
svah iic. svar₃.
svaḥsad [sad₂] amnf myth. who resides in the heavens (said of the gods).
svaka [svaka] amnf svakā his; his own; of his entourage — m. ally, friend | pl. svakās his own; his people.
svakasvaka | red. | amnf svakasvakā id. svakasvakā bhaginī his own sister (opp. vaimātṛkā bhaginī).
svakīya |īya| amnf svakīyā id. (opp. parakīya) — f. svakīyā his own wife. svakīya bhava own nature.
svagā interj. soc. prosperity! (ritual exclamation).
svánga |su₁anga₁| amnf svangā who has a beautiful body; with a pleasing physique — n. graceful body.

svaccha [su₁accha₁] amnf svacchā very clear, crystalline, transparent | clear, limpid; clean, pure — m. rock crystal — n. pearl | |svacchadhātuka| alloy of silver and gold — f. svacchā white variety of dūrvā grass.
svacchatva [tva] n. clarity, limpidity, transparency; purity, cleanliness.
√ svañj v. [1] pr. r. (svajate) pp. (svakta) pf. (abhi, pari) to embrace, encircle, press in one's arms — ca. (svañjayati) to cause to be embraced.
svátas [adv. sva] adv. by nature; intrinsically; of its own accord; on its own funds; opp. paratas.
svataḥprāmāṇya [prāmāṇya] n. phil. [Sabara₁] va intrinsic lidity of a cognition.

√ svad v. [1] pr. (svádati) pf. (ā) to taste, to savor, to eat with pleasure — pr. r. (svádate) to be sweet; to be agreeable to the taste, to please dat. g. — ca. (svādáyati) ca. (sādáyati) to make agreeable to the taste, to season, to cook || gr. v ; lat. suāvis; all. süss; ang. sweet; fr. suave.
svadita [pp. svad] amnf svaditā well seasoned, tasty — n. soc. ["good appetite"] invocation during the śraddhā₁ ₂ at the time of the presentation of the oblation to the ancestors | pitaras |.
√ svan v. [1] pr. (svanati) pp. (svanita) ca. (sva nayati) pf. (vi) ring, resonate, resound, emit a noise | lat. sonar; fr. ring.
svana |agt. svan| mr. sound, noise, speech || lat. sonus; fr. her.
svanuṣṭhita [su₁anuṣṭhita] amnf svanusthitā well done, well executed; well observed.
svanta [su₁anta] amnf svantā which ends well. svantam bhavisyati this will end well.
svapat [ppr. svap] amnf svapatī sleeping.
svapaná [agt. svap] amnf svapanā som nolent — act. n. drowsiness; falling asleep, sleep; dream.
svapitṛ [agt. svap] amnf svapitrī en dormi; dormeur.

svápna [act. svap] m. the state [avasthā₂] of sleep; dream | phil. the second stage of consciousness; cf. māṇḍūkyopaniṣad || lat. somnus; fr. sommeil. svapne en songe. svapnam dṛś ["to see in a dream"] to dream.
svapnakṛt | kṛt₂ | amnf somniferous; soporific.
svapnagata [gata] amnf svapngatā asleep.
svapnadarśana [darśana] n. dream | bd. [Vajrayāna] practice of lucid dreaming, a saddharma; cf. mahāmāyātantra.
svápnadrá [drá2] amnf who dreams.
svápnadosa [dosa₂] m. nighttime pollution.
svápnanidarsana [nidarsana] n. med. premonitory dreams and visions.
svápnanidarśanīya [īya] amnf svapnani darśanīyā med. which deals with visions and premonitory dreams.
svápnanirdeśa [nirdeśa] m. bd. np. du Svapna nirdeśa, text bd. on dreams.
svápnaparīkṣā | parīkṣā | f. med. examination of dreams.
svapnavat [vat] adv. as in a dream.

Svapnavāsavadatta [vāsavadattā] n. lit. np. of the Svapnavāsavadatta "vāsavadattā₂ seen in a dream", play [nāṭaka] by Bhāsa, inspired by legends of the Brhatkathā, and not. of King Udayana; his minister Yaugandharāyaṇa plots an alliance with the king of Magadha by having him marry his daughter Padmāvatī₂; to this end, he spreads the rumor of the death of Queen vāsavadattā₂, and convinces Padmāvatī₂ to shelter the latter for the time of the marriage.
svapnotthita [utthita] amnf svapnotthitā just woke up.

svayám [svaya] ind. oneself, himself, myself, in person — adv. of oneself, by oneself; of one's own free will; Spontaneously, voluntarily. manuḥ svayam Manu in person. svayamevāgata amn came Spontaneously. gramo gacchati svayam eva the village is easily accessible.
svayamvara |vara₂| mr. SOC. mode of marriage by choice of the young girl — f. svayamvarā chosen wife siding her husband.
Svayamvaramantra [mantra] n. SOC. n.p. of the Svayamvaramantra, in homage to Pārvatī.
svayaṃvyakta [vyakta] amnf svayaṃvyaktā appeared by itself; says not. of a spontaneous linga; syn. svayambhu.
svayamjāta [jāta] amnf svayamjātā Spontaneous; produced Spontaneously.
svayámjyotis [jyotis] amnf luminous of itself.
svayaṃjyotiḥsvabhāva [svabhāva] amn phil. whose own nature is to be self-luminous (called brahman).
svayaṃdatta [datta] amnf svayaṃdattā refers to a child who is being offered for adoption.
svayamātṛṇṇa [ātṛṇṇa] amnf svayamātṛṇṇā pierced with natural holes — f. svayamātṛṇṇā SOC. "naturally pierced" brick of the agnicayana altar.
svayamindriyamocana [indriyamocana] n. masturbation.

svayampākin [pākin] amnf svayampākinī SOC. who prepares their own meals. svayámbhu var. svayambhu |bhu| mr. myth. n.p. from svayambhu, epith. of Brahmā, the “self-begotten” demiurge | cf. svayaṃbhū. svayámbhuva var. svayambhuva |bhuva| amnf svayambhuva cf. svayambhu — m. myth. n.p. of svayambhuva, first Manu.

Svayambhuvasūtrasamgraha [sūtrasamgraha] m. bed. n.p. from the Svayambhuvasūtrasamgraha "Collection of the aphorisms of Siva", Shivaite tantra. svayámbhū var. svayambhū [bhū₂] amnf ["self-begotten"] independent, autonomous, spontaneous; primordial — m. myth. n.p. from svayambhū, epith. of Brahmā, the “Spontaneous” demiurge | myth. epith. of Śiva or Viṣṇu or Vyāsa, etc. | bed. n.p. of svayambhū₁, 9th century apabhramśa poet and meter theorist (Puṇe) svayambhūpurāṇa var. svayambhūpurāṇa | purāṇa | n. bed. n.p. of svayambhūpurāṇa.

svayambhūlinga [linga] n. SOC. primordial or Spontaneous linga; there are 12 of them in India, corresponding to places of pilgrimage; cf. jyotirlinga | phil. |yoga| support of the Kundalini asleep in the mūlādhāra.
√ Svar₁ var. svṛ v. [1] pr. (svárati) pp. (svarita) to rustle; to make a sound, to resound | to ring; to sing praises | gr. ; lat. susurrus.
√ Svar₂ [related to on] v. [1] pr. (svarati) to shine — ca. (svarayati) to make shine || gr. ηλιος.

Svar₃ var. súvar [agt. Svar₂] ind. sky | [svarloka] myth. np. of Svar or Svarga, the sky or Paradise of Indra, highest of the 3 celestial worlds |lokatraya|, inhabited by the gods |deva|, Paradise of the blessed; cf. vyāhṛti | excl. sky! (pronounced between om and la gāyatrī). bhūr bhuvar Svar by the earth, the worlds, and the sky (ritual exclamation [vyāhṛti]). svah prayātah deceased (gone to heaven). svaḥkāmaḥ one who loves heaven. svaricchati he desires Paradise.
svarbhānu [bhānu] m. myth. np. of svarbhānu, asura causing solar eclipses; later assi milé to Rāhu | var. svarbhāņu id.
svarloka [loka] m. myth. cf. Svarga.
svarlokadrśvan [drśvan] amnf svarlokadrśvarī who saw the sky.

svára |agt. Svar₁| m. sound, noise; cry; accent, tone; musical note | phil. [Abhinavagupta] music as a rediscovery of the self | math. symb. the number 7 (for the 7 notes) | phon. vowel | gram. intonation.

svaracitra [citra] n. lit. learned poetry [varnacitra] with constraints on the vowels used. urugum dyugurum yutsu cukruśustustuvuh puru lulubhuḥ pupuṣurmutsu mumuhurnu muhurmuhuḥ ('u' single vowel) the gods took refuge in Brhaspati, lord of speech, chaplain of the gods in the heavens, when they went into battle; they prayed again and again that he would remain happy and strong, and that his mind would not wander.
svárabhakti [bhakti] f. phon. vowel break, epenthesis by intercalation of a vowel in a consonant group (e.g. varisa for varsa); opp. vyañjanabhakti.
svárabheda [bheda] m. loss of voice | counterfeit voice | gram. difference in accent | the broken voice, a sāttvikānubhāva.
svárabhedabhaya [bhaya] n. fear of being betrayed by one's voice.
sváravat |vat| amnf svaravatī phon. voiced | stressed | containing a vowel.
svaravarna | varna | n. phon. accent and timbre. svaravarnatas adv. phon. due to the accent and timbre.
svarasaṃyoga [saṃyoga] m. musical chord.
svarasiddhāntacandrikā [siddhāntacandrikā] f. bed. n.p. from the svarasiddhāntacandrikā, manual of Paninean phonetics due to Srīnivāsa₁.
Svarodaya [udaya] amnf svarodayā phon. followed by a vowel — mn lit. np. from the Svarodaya tantra, which deals with divinatory arts.
svarita [pp. svar₁] amnf svaritā that is made to resonate, grave (sound) — mn gram. grave accent (opp. udātta).

svargá var. suvarga [svar₁ga₁] amnf svargā who goes to Heaven; celestial — m. [svargaloka] myth. np. of Svarga the Heaven of Light, paradise of Indra; cf. vaikuntha | phil. [Mīmāmsā] celestial bliss as the legitimate fruit of sacrifice; ac supreme fulfillment of man's desire for happiness, happiness in its pure state | lit. np. Svarga from the section [khaṇḍa] of a purāṇa dealing with creation myths.
svargakāma | kāma | amnf svargakāmā who has worse in Heaven.
svarganaraka | naraka | n. pl. paradises and irons.
svargapatita | patita | amnf svargapatitā fallen from Heaven.
svargáparvan | parvan | n. lit. np. from the Svargaparva or Svargārohanaparva, 18th book of the Mah.; it describes the journey of the 5 Pāṇḍavās princes to the Heaven of Indra on Mount Meru.
svargavarga [varga] m. lit. section of the Svargādikānda, dealing with Heaven.

Svargādikāṇḍa [ādikāṇḍa] n. lit. np. from the Svargādikānda, 1st volume of the Amarakosa; it comprises 9 sections [varga]: Heaven [svargavarga], air and space [vyomadigvarga], time [kālavarga], intellect [dhīvarga], mountains [śailavarga], the
dramaturgy [nātyavarga], the underworld [pātālabhogivarga], hell [narakavarga], and water [vārivarga].
svargārohaṇa [ārohaṇa] n. myth. Ascent to Heaven; [Mah.] not. Ascent to Heaven of Yudhisthira with his own body.
svargārohanaparvan | parvan | n. bed. n.p. of Svargārohaṇaparva, 18th book of the Mah., "of the ascent to Heaven".
svargin [in] amnf svarginī residing in Heaven deceased — m. myth. occupant of Heaven, god.
svargīya |īya| amnf svargīyā concerning Heaven; leading to Heaven; celestial.
svargyá [ya] amnf svargyā id.
svarṇa [contr. suvarṇa] n. gold. svar₁ņakāra [kāra] m. goldsmith, jeweler.
svarṇacūḍa [cūḍā] m. bio. ["with a golden crest"] blue jay.
svarṇadvīpa [dvīpa] mn geo. n.p. from svarṇadvīpa, the Golden Island, mod. Ceylon | eng. serendipity. svar₁ņamaya |maya| amnf svar₁ņamayī golden; in gold.
svarṇaroman [roman] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of the king svar₁ņaromā "with golden hair", son of Mahāromā, father of Hrasvaromā.
svalamkṛta var. svalankṛta [su₁alamkṛta] amnf svalamkṛtā well prepared; well decorated.
svalpa [su₁alpa] amnf svalpā very small, tiny; brief; insignificant, negligible. svalpena adv. in a flash.
svalpaka [ka] amnf svalpakā very small, half a nutlet. svalpakena adv. very quickly.
svalpaśilā [śilā] f. very small stone — v. [11] pr. r. (svalpaśilāyate) to become an insignificant stone.
svásṛ f. [sg. name. svasā, acc. svasāram] sister || lat. soror; eng. sister; fr. sister.
svasrīya [īya] m. nephew (son of a sister); syn. bhāgineya — f. svastrīyā niece.

svasti [su₁asti] f. well-being; good fortune, success — ind. excl. long live (dat.)! | adr. good luck! to your health! | greetings (polite formula to begin a letter). svastirastu adr. all my best wishes for success. yūyam pāta svastibhih sadā nah |Vasiṣṭha| May you always protect us with your blessings.
swastika |ka| m. bard (responsible for pronouncing the swastika) | soc. swastika or swastika cross, mystical sign of good omen, of solar origin.
svastikāsana [āsana] n. phil. [yoga] seated posture, with the sole of each foot between the opposite thigh and calf.

svāgata |su₁āgata| amnf svāgatā welcome — n. greeting (of welcome); welcome | soc. not. formula of welcome to the deity during the pūjā — f. svāgatā phon. meter of 11 syllables in each pada, with a pause after the 3rd and last syllable. svāgatam var. susvāgatam adr. welcome! svāgatīkṛ to welcome, to greet.
svāgama [su₁āgama] m. greeting.
svādhyamkarana [su₁ādhyamkarana] amnf svādhyamkaranī which makes one rich easily.
svātantrika [*svatantraika] amnf svātantrikā bd. tradition of the mādhyamaka school founded by Bhāvaviveka.

svātantrya [*svatantraya] n. freedom, independence, autonomy | phil. free will | phil. [Trika] freedom of the Divine. svātantryāt var. svātantryena adv. of oneself, of one's own free will; naturally; freely, voluntarily. pitā rakṣati kaumāre bhartā rakṣati yauvane | rakṣanti sthavire putrā na strī svātantryamarhati [MS.] Her father protects her in her childhood, her husband protects her in her youth, and her sons protect her in her old age; woman does not deserve independence.
svātantryavāda [vāda] m. phil. doctrine of autonomy (of the self), developed by the non-dualistic Shaivism [advaita] of Kaśmīra [Trika]; it is a theory of freedom through Recognition [Pratyabhijñā].
svātí var. Svātī f. astr. np. of Svāti or Svātī, regent of the 13th lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corr. to the star Arcturus of Boötes; Vāyu presides over it; Its symbol is coral.
svātma iic. svātman.
svātmanisthita [nisthita] amnf svātmanisthitā phil. autonomous; confined within itself.
svātmavijñāna [vijñāna] m. self-knowledge.
Svātmārāma [ārāma] amnf svātmārāmā who is content with the self — m. hist. n.p. of Svātmārāma, religious name of the nāthayogin Cintāmaṇi₁.
svātman [svaātman] m. self, own nature; one's own person.
svāda [obj. svad] m. taste, flavor — ifc. taste, interest in (iic.); cf. brahmāsvāda, rasāsvāda.
svādana [agt. svad] amnf svādanā that seasons, that gives taste — act. n. act of tasting | act of appreciating (a poem).
svādi [(su₂)ādi] m. gram. ["which begins with su₂" | qualifies the fifth class |gaṇa| of present of verbs; Its characteristic marker [vikarana₂] is śnu.
svādiṣṭha [super. svāda] amnf svādiṣṭhā the best, the tastiest; delicious | sweeter than (abl.).
svādu [*svadu] amnf tasty, sweet, pleasant; delicious, pleasing to the taste — n. sweetness, sweet flavor; syrup.
svādurasa [rasa] amnf svādurasā with a pleasant, succulent taste.
svādhikāra [svaadhikāra] m. His own employment, office entrusted to him personally.
svādhikārapramatta [pramatta] amnf adhikārapramattā negligent in his charge.

svādhiṣṭhāna [svaadhiṣṭhāna] n. phil. “the Seat of the Self”, 2nd chakra of tantric yoga. Located at the level of the genitals; it is represented by a lotus of 6 red petals; a crescent moon symbolizes the element of water, and bears the bijamantra vam; it controls the sense of taste; it is the psychic center of the enjoyment of the self.

svādhyāya [svaadhyāya] m. soc. private recitation (not. of sacred texts, of the Vedas); it is a pañcopāsana according to Rāmānuja | phil. knowledge (acquired through the reading of sacred texts), one of the disciplines [niyama] of yoga | phil. not. discipline of self-knowledge [adhyātmajñāna]. satyam vada dharmam cara svādhyāyānmā
Pramadah [TU.] Speak the truth, do your duty, do not neglect your studies.
svānta [svaanta] m. his own end, his own death | His own domain; his province, his country — n. mind, heart (seat of emotions).
svāpa [act. svap] m. sleep, dream; drowsiness, numbness; stupidity.

svābhāvika [*svabhāvaika] amnf svābhāvikī natural, native; proper to its nature; to the tonome; spontaneous | med. said not. of diseases related to old age | gram. irregular (said of spontaneous forms not provided for by the rule); opp. vācanika | phil. [Vedānta] variant of the bhedābhedavāda doctrine professing that brahman is both different and not different from the phenomenal world by its own nature (opp. aupādhika); cf. Yādavaprakāśa | pl. bd. name of a bd. school — n. proper nature.
svābhāvya [*svabhāvaya] amnf svābhāvyā self-existing, spontaneous (said not. of Viṣṇu) — n. own nature | gram. autonomy of the connotative power of the word; it justifies irregular forms.
svāmi iic. svāmin. svāmiguņa [guṇa] m. ability to command.
svāmitā [tā] f. ownership, control, governance of (iic. g.).
svāmitva [tva] n. ownership, control, governance of (iic. g.).

Svāminātha [nātha] m. myth. np. of Svāminātha "Master Preceptor", epith. of SkandaMurugan teaching Shiva the power of the pranava mantra [om]; he is honored at the temple of Svāmimalai near Kumbakonam in Tamil Nadu.

Svāminārāyaṇa₁ [nārāyaṇa] m. hist. np. of Svāminārāyaņa, born Ghansyam Paņde (1781–1830), founder of the eponymous religious order [sampradāya]; he left his family at age 11 to become the wandering ascetic Nīlakantha Varnī; he was initiated as Sahajānanda Svāmī by Rāmānanda₁ Svāmī and settled in Gadhada in Gujarāt; he advocated non-violence, a vegetarian diet, the prohibition of alcohol, the education of women, the abolition of caste segregation and widow suicide [satī]; he was deified as an incarnation at the kaliyuga of nārāyaṇa; cf. Satsangijīvana | mod. n.p. of the Svāminārāyana₁ Akṣaradhāman temple, inaugurated in Delhi in 2005. Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā [siddhāntasudhā] f. bed. of np. the Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā, text expounding the doctrine of Svāminārāyaņa.
svāmibhāva [bhāva] m. domination; ownership.

svāmin [*svamin] m. [nom. Svāmī] owner, master; lord, chief; King, prince (of g. loc.) | husband, lover | soc. spiritual preceptor, enlightened brahman; title Svāmī in various religious orders — ifc. master (honorary) — f. svāminī mistress, princess; favorite. svasvāmibhāva gram. relation between possessor and possession. Svāmī title Svāmī in various religious orders.

Svāyambhuva var. Svāyambhuva [*svayaṃbhua] amnf svāyaṃbhuvā myth. relating to BrahmāSvayaṃbhu — m. myth. n.p. of Svāyaṃbhuva, "(Issuing) from the self-begotten", 1st Manu of the kalpa; he begat the 10 progenitors [prajāpati].
svāyaṃbhuvatantra | tantra | n. bed. n.p. of the Svāyambhuvatantra.
svārasika [*svarasaika] amnf svārasikā which has its own aesthetic (poetry) | natural; easy to appreciate.
svārāj [svar₃rāj₂] m. [sg. name. svārāt] epith. of Indra "King of Heaven".
Svārociṣa [*svarocisa] m. myth. n.p. of Svārociṣa “Issuing from his own grace”, 2nd Manu of the kalpa.

svārtha [svaartha] m. (one's) own destiny, (one's) own affairs, (one's) cause, (one's) purpose | one's own interests; selfish work; opp. paramārtha own substance; end in itself, proper meaning | phil. pleonasm — amnf svārthā selfish intended for its own use gram. which does not add meaning (said of certain suffixes forming endocentric derivatives); opp. anya padārtha. svārtham adv. for oneself. svārthe adv. gram. in the proper sense (of the rac cine); said of class 10 roots (curādi gaṇa) as opposed to causative verbs. svārthe ka gram. pleonastic suffix 'ka'.
svārthatā [tā] f. selfishness.
svārthānumāna [anumāna] n. phil. [Nyāya] use of reasoning for one's own use. svārthānumānaparicchedasvavṛtti [paricchedasvavrtti] f. bed. n.p. of the Svārthānumānaparicchedasvavrtti of Dharmakīrti.
svārthika [ika] amnf svārthikā gram. refers to endocentric suffixes, which do not contribute any meaning external to the theme.

svāsthya [*svasthaya] n. autonomy; comfort; good health; good condition (physical or mental); satisfaction. labdham svāsthyam mayā I am at ease. śīghreṇaiva svāsthyalābho bhaviṣyati Health will return very soon.

Svāhā (ind. excl. soc.) Glory to dat.! (accompanies the offering to a deity); Vedic, pronounced when offering wood in the fire in the devayajña — f. myth. np. of Svāhā "Oblation", wife of Agni; she took the form of the wives of the 7 sages to unite with him and thus procreate Skanda. śivāya Svāhā (glory to Shiva!) Agnaye svāhāgnaya idam na mama (glory to Agni!) This is for Agni, not for me.
svāhāra [su₁āhāra] amnf svāhārā easy to obtain — m. succulent food | priest cook charged with preparing the offerings [prasāda].
svid₁ [su₁id] part. cl. Do you think? Really? Maybe? Anywhere. āho svid Or. kim svid What then? kva svid Anywhere. kaḥ svid Anyone.
√ svid₂ v. [1] pr. r. (svedate) pp. (svinná) to sweat, to perspire — v. [4] pr. (svidyati) to be sweaty — ca. (svedayati) to make sweat | lat. sudor; ang. sweat; fr. sueur.
svī iiv. sva.
svīkarana [karana] n. claim; acquisition, appropriation, taking | marriage ["to make (his wife) his own"|.
svīkaraṇīya | karaṇīya | amnf svīkaraṇīyā ac ceptable; which one can agree to; which one can appropriate.
svīkartavya [kartavya] amnf svīkartavyā that one must accept; to which one must give one's ac cord.
svīkāra | kāra | m. appropriation, claim | consent, agreement; promise.

svīkṛ [kṛ₁] v. [8] pr. (svīkaroti) pp. (svīkṛta) s'ap to appropriate, claim. sarve bhāgam svīkurvantu (formal greeting) Please accept all my blessings. vācā dattā mayā kanyā putrārtham svīkṛtā tvayā soc. Please receive my daughter for your son (at the wedding).
svīya [svaīya] amnf svīyā sien, propre; characteristic.
sveccham [svaicchā] adv. [en comp. svec cha] at his own pleasure, according to his fancy; of his own will, voluntarily.
svecchā [svaicchā] f. desire, free will, good pleasure. svecchayā at his own discretion. svecchatas of his own free will.
svecchācāriṇī [cārin] f. woman of loose morals.
svétavya [su₁etavya] n. (impers.) it is easy to leave.
sveda [obj. svid₂] m. sweat, perspiration.
svedaja [ja] m. ["born of sweat"] vermin.
svedana [agt. svid₂] amnf svedanā that sweats, that tends to sweat | that makes sweat | med. sudorific — act. n. sweating.
svedin [agt. svid₂] amnf svedinī who sweats.

svaira [svaīra] amnf svairā autonomous, independent; free, without constraint — acc. svai ram adv. at one's own pleasure, freely, of one's own accord, without obstacle | without reservation, in complete confidence. svairam upaviśyatām sit quietly.
independent svairi [svairin].
svairitā [tā] f. free will; autonomy, independence.
svairin [svairain] amnf svairiṇī free of movement, independent — f. svairinī soc. free woman | bio. bat. ह h ha part. cl. |affirmation| indeed, certainly, truly interjection of appeal.

hamsa m. bio. zoo. anser indicus, wild goose; swan; cf. rājahaṃsa, kalahaṃsa | phil. mythical bird; tradition says that it has the gift of separating milk from water (i.e., discerning truth from error) [nīrakṣīraviveka], and it embodies the power to discern the essential substance of things; cf. Mānasasarovara | myth. np. of hamsa, the goose mount of Brahmā | lit. [K.] np. of the great king harva hamsa₁, father of the apsaras Mahāśvetā by Gaurī₁ | lit. [Mah.] messenger swan informing Nala of Damayantī's love | phil. the rhythmic breath mantra 'hamsa'; cf. ajapā | type of man; cf. pañcamanusyavibhāga || gr. ; lat. anser; all. Gans; ang. gander, goose. haṃsaḥ so 'ham [Tantra] I am that divine bird.
