haṃsagāminī [gāmin] f. ["who has the bearing of a hamsa"] graceful young woman.
haṃsádvāra [dvāra] n. geo. Niti pass in the Himalayas, "goose path" which goes to Lake Mānasa; cf. krauñcarandhra.
hamsánāda [nāda] m. cry of geese; it has a sacred character; in poetry, it is compared to the tinkling of anklets worn by women.
hamsapakṣa [pakṣa] m. wild goose wing | ritual gesture [mudrā] of the goose wing (fingers joined upwards, thumb spread).
hamsavat [vat] amnf hamsavatī like a swan — f. hamsavatī myth. np. of hamsavatī "(Beautiful) like a swan", first wife of King Duşyanta.
hamsavidyā [vidyā] f. phil. esoteric knowledge of the hamsa mantra, leading to brahmavidyā.
hamsasamdeśa [samdeśa] m. lit. from the np. Hamsasandesa, devotional poem of the samdeśakāvya type by Vedāntadeśika; it evokes the goose sent as a messenger from Rāma to Sītā held prisoner in Lankā.
hamsāsya [āsya] m. ritual gesture [mudrā] of the wild goose face (index finger pinching the thumb, other fingers raised).
hamsopanisad [upanisad] f. lit. np. of the esoteric lesson hamsopanisad; it is part of the Suklayajurveda; Sanatkumāra teaches the hamsavidyā to Gautama.
hamsaka [hamsaka] m. bio. goose; little goose — f. hamsikā female goose.
hamho interj. hey!
hakāra [(ha)kāra] m. the sound or letter 'ha'.
hatta m. market; fair — f. hattī small market.
hattacauraka [cauraka] m. market robber, cutthroat.
√ hath v. |1| pr. (hathati) to harm, oppress.
hatha |act. hath| m. violence; stubbornness, obstinacy; perseverance, effort | necessity, urgency. hațhāt var. hațhena adv. by force, through violence | inevitably. hathāt kṛ to be stubborn.
haṭhapradīpikā [pradīpikā] f. bed. n.p. from Hathapradīpikā "Enlightenment of hathayoga", 15th century text by Svātmārāma.

hathayoga [yoga] m. soc. yoga of effort; it is mainly concerned with the control of the body and the maintenance of its health by correct postures [āsana] and breath discipline [prāṇāyāma]; it leads to the meditation techniques [dhyāna] of rājayoga; it is taught in the Hathayogapradīpikā.
Hathayogapradīpikā [pradīpikā] f. lit. np. of the Hathayogapradīpikā "Elucidation of the hathayoga", work of the nāthayogin Cintāmani₁ (around the 15th century).
haṭhavidyā [vidyā] f. phil. science of effort yoga.

haṭhaśarman [śarman] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of the rich brahmin Hathaśarmā; he demanded the hand of the beautiful princess Aśokamālā, but she fled, for he was hideous; he pursued and persecuted her; thus he fulfilled the curse of the vidyādhara prince Sthūlabhuja.
hathābhyāsa |abhyāsa| mr. soc. practice of hathayoga.

haṭhābhyāsapaddhati | paddhati | f. lit. np. of the Hathābhyāsapaddhati, a manual of yoga postures (18th century), in crude Sanskrit; it is at the basis of modern yoga teaching, and not. of Srītattvanidhi.

hata |pp. han₁| amnf hatā struck, beaten; killed, felled; destroyed, lost; defective, unusable | ruined, lost, miserable; cursed | tormented by (i. iic.) | deprived of, without (ifc.) — n. blow, strike — f. hatā raped woman. caurahata killed by a thief. mūle hate hatam sarvam When the root is destroyed, everything is destroyed.
hatajñāna | jñāna | amnf hatajñānā deprived of consciousness; unconscious.
hatádaiva |daiva| amnf hatadaivā struck by fate; unlucky — n. bad luck.
hatadvis | dvis₂ | amnf who slaughtered his enemies.
hataprabha | prabhā₂ | amnf hataprabhā which has lost its luster.
hatávidhi | vidhi | m. bad luck — amnf marked by bad luck.
hatávīrya | vīrya | amnf hatavīryā who has lost his virility or vigor.
hatavat |ppa. han₁ | amnf hatavatī who killed. cauram hatavān he killed the thief.
hati [act. han₁] f. blow (delivered by (iic.)); murder; destruction, ruin; disappearance, absence | math. multiplication.
hatya [act. han₁] n. murder (of (iic.)) — f. hatyā id.
√ had v. [1] pr. (hadati) pr. r. (hadate) pp. (hanna) to defecate.

√ han₁ v. [2] pr. (hanti) imp. (jahi) fut. (hanisyati) pft. (jaghāna) pft. r. (jaghne) pp. (hata) ppr. (ghnat) pfp. (hantavya, ghnya) abs. (hatya, hatvā) pf. (apa, abhi, ava, ā, ut, upa, kaņe, ni, nis, pari, pra, prati, manas, vi, sam) to strike, to beat; to beat a drum | to kill, to destroy, to cause to perish — ps. (hanyate) to be struck, to be killed — ca. (ghātáyati) to put to death; to cause to be killed — des. (jighāṃsati) des. r. (jighāṃsate) to desire to kill — intens. (jáṅghati) mas to consecrate — intens. r. (janghanyate) Vedic. to be struck (by the vicissitudes of life). áhannáhim Vedic. ["you/he killed the serpent"] evocation of the murder of Vrtra. carmani dvīpinam hanti he kills the tiger for its skin.
han₁ [agt. han₁] ifc. amnf ghnī [fb. ha; obl. ghna; sg. nom. hā] who killed (iic.). brahmahā who killed a brahmin. bhrūṇahā who killed a fetus.
vṛtrahā | "who killed Vṛtra" | epith. of Indra. mātṛhā saptamam narakam praviśet ved. that he who killed his mother go to the 7th hell.
hana [agt. han₁] ifc. amnf hanā murderer, Destroyer of (iic.) — act. n. murder, destruction of (iic.).
hanana [agt. han₁] amnf hananī who kills, murderer — act. n. murder, act of killing; act of striking; destruction | math. multiplication.
hánu |han₁u| f. jaw | var. hanū id. | eng. chin; all. Kinn; lat. gena.

hanumat var. hanūmat [hanumat] m. [nom. hanumān] myth. [Rām.] np. of the god hanumān "Prognathus", advisor to the monkey king Sugrīva, ally of Rāma; he is the son of the wind Pavana and the nymph | apsaras | Añjanā transformed into a monkey; endowed with immense strength, he has the power to fly through the air; as a child, he leaped to seize the Sun when Rāhu came to eclipse it; the latter complained to Indra, who broke the child's jaw with his

lightning |vajra|; he killed many rākṣasās and helped Rāma to free Sītā; he leaped in a single bound from the Himālaya to Lankā, which he set ablaze with his flaming tail; he is an expert in speech [vākkovida], his van and healer; on the order of Jāmbavān he went in search of the herbs of resurrection and healing (samjīvanī, viśalyakaranī, suvarņakaranī, saṃdhānī); he brought back from the Himālaya the summit of Mount VṛṣaMahodaya where they grew, to bring Lakshmana back to life; he is abstaining |brahmacārin|, and therefore often depicted with a green neck of vermilion paste [sindūra]; His attributes are the mace [gadā] and the banana tree [kadala]; in the presence of Rama, he is depicted in the posture of devotion [mastakāñjali]; he symbolizes devotion and faithful friendship, as well as physical strength in the service of good; due to a curse, he is unaware of his great powers, which are revealed to him by others; Rama having granted him to live as long as the Ramayana would be told, he is one of the seven immortals [ciramjīvin]; his birthday (Ha numān jayantī) is celebrated on the full moon of the month of Cai
tra [caitrī]; cf. Añjaneya, Ghanasāravilepa, Marut putra, Mahāvīra, Māruti, Rākṣasāntaka.
hanumaddhvaja |dhvaja| amnf hanumaddh vajā hist. ["who has hanumān on his banner"] title of the dynasty of Malla kings of the Kath mandu valley in Nepal.
hanūmat cf. hanumat.
hánta interj. (exhortation) come on! well! let's see! hey! quickly! | alas. hanta na gatah Oh! he hasn't left.
hantavya |pfp. |3| han₁| amnf hantavya that must be put to death | that must be transgressed. hantavyo 'smi I am struck dead.
hantu [inf. han₁] m. murder.
hantukāma [kāma] amnf hantukāmā who wants to kill | soc. qualifies a hostile possession demon of ardent character [āgneya]; opp. ratikāma.
hantr [agt. han₁] amnf hantrī [sg. nom. hantā, acc. hantāram who strikes, who kills, who harms (g.); Destroyer — m. murderer, assassin.
Hammīra m. hist. np. of the Rajput king Hammīra "Amir" of Sākambharī₁, of the Cāhuvāṇa dynasty, reigning (1301–1365); he encouraged the arts, and pa tronna not. his chaplain Rāghavadeva.
haya [agt. hi₂] m. horse, racehorse — f. hayā mare.

hayagrīva [grīvā] m. myth. np. of the asura hayagrīva "horse neck", son of Naraka; he cast the Veda into the waters, from where Vișnu incarnated by Matsya saved him; through his penances he had obtained from Devī that he could only be defeated by a hayagrīva; Viṣṇu gave himself a horse's head to become hayagrīva₁ and be able to kill him; it was in this form that Vișnu killed Madhu₁ and Kaițabha |bd. [Mahāvairocanasūtra] np. of hayagrīva₂, vidyārāja close to Avalokiteśvara.
hayagrīvavadha [vadha] m. lit. no. of the mahākāvya hayagrīvavadha of Bhartrmentha, highly esteemed, but of which only a few quotations remain.
hayaśīrṣa |śīrṣa| amnf hayaśīrṣī who has a horse's head — m. myth. epith. of Visnuhayagrīva₁.
Hayaśīrṣapañcarātra [pañcarātra] n. lit. np. of the Hayaśīrṣapañcarātra, collection of vaiṣṇava rituals relating to the erection of temples, initiation, and the consecration of idols.

Hara [agt. hṛ₁] amnf harā ifc. one who takes, who seizes, who removes; one who has taken away | one who destroys, who suppresses | one who receives, who obtains | given to (iic.) old enough to take care of (iic.) — m. myth. np. of Hara, epithet of Shiva "the Destroyer" | math. divi seur; division. sukhāhara m. given to pleasure. kavacahara m. (kṣatriya) old enough to wear leather. asthihara m. (dog) old enough to gnaw a bone. Hara Hara Hara mahādeva Śiva Śiva Śiva Śiva Supreme God (Maratha war cry).

haracarita [carita] n. lit. gesture of Shiva. haracaritacintāmaņi |cintāmaņi| m. lit. np. of the Haracaritacintāmaņi, long mythological poem by Jayadratha₂ recounting the exploits of Shiva and featuring the pilgrimage sites of Kaśmīra.
Haradatta [datta] amnf haradattā "given by Śiva" — m. hist. np. of the grammarian Haradatta, composer of the Padamañjarī (circa 1100).
haradattācārya [ācārya] m. hist. n.p. by Hara dattācārya, author of the Gaṇakārikās.

Haravijaya [vijaya] m. lit. np. of the Haravijaya "Triumph of Shiva", mahākāvya in 50 songs due to rājānaka Ratnākara₂; it recounts the destruction of the demon Andhaka by Shiva, and brings the style of Māgha to a paroxysm of complexity; in its chapter 43, verses 145 and 146 describe a Hamiltonian circuit on the chessboard [turagabandha].
haravilāsa [vilāsa] m. lit. np. from the mahāprabandha haravilāsa "Entertainment of Šiva", due to Rājaśekhara (now lost).
Harasakhi [sakhi] m. myth. n.p. from Harasakhi, epith. of Kubera the “friend of Siva”.

Harasiddhi [siddhi] f. myth. np. of Harasiddhi, an aspect of Kālī; she is the tutelary deity [kuladevī] of Rajput communities not. in Gujarāt; her main temple is at Miyani, on top of a hill, where it is said that Kṛṣṇa prayed to overcome Jarāsandha; another temple is at Ujjayinī, on the banks of the Ksiprā; it is said to have been built by Vikramāditya; it is one of the holy places of the Goddess [śaktipīṭha]; the ceiling of one of its domes bears a large śrīyantra; two large lamp-bearing pillars in the Maratha style are at the entrance.
haraṇa [agt. hṛ₁] amnf haraṇī ifc. who takes, who transports (iic.); who contains (iic.) — m. ["who takes"] hand — act. n. action of taking; theft; abduction | present (for wedding or initiation).
hari₁ [agt. hṛ₁] ifc. amnf who takes, who transports (iic.).
hari₂ ind. excl. alas!

hári₂ amnf tawny, bay; blond, red; yellow-green-brown ("color of young leaves in spring") | phil. an indefinable color | tawny color — m. Lion | myth. np. of hari₁, epithet of Vishnu "the Lion" (or glossed as hari₁ "He who takes away (sins)") | myth. epithet of Indra and other per

sonnages | bay horse | monkey | hist. np. of the grammai rien hari₁ Dīkṣita, son of Vīreśvara |Vaireśvari|, and therefore grandson of Bhațțoji Dīkșita (17th century); he is the author of the Brhacchabdaratna | hist. np. of the grammai rien hari₁ Dīkṣita, born Lakṣmīnaraharisūrisūnu, son of Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, and therefore great-grandnephew of Bhațțoji Dīkṣita; he is the author of the Brah masūtravṛtti — f. harī myth. np. of harī, daughter of Kaśyapa and Krodhavaśā; she gave birth to the race of monkeys. hare voc. O hari₁! cf. mahāmantra. hariḥ om adr. May God be with you | mod. First writing exercise with grains of rice taught to a child in South India in a private religious ceremony. saśańkhacakro harih myth. Vishnu carrying the conch and discus.
harikathā [kathā₁] f. soc. oral recitation of traditional stories from Vișnu or Krșna.
harikārikā [kārikā] f. pl. harikārikās lit. stanzas of the Vākyapadīya.
Harikṛṣṇa |Kṛṣṇa| mr. hist. n.p. of the logician [navyanyāya] Harikṛṣṇa Paṇḍita, author of the Upasarganipātadyotakatvavācakatvavicāra (Kūrmāñcala, 17th century).
hárikeśa [keśa] amnf harikeśī with blond or red hair | ved. qualifies gods of ardent nature (Agni, SūryaSavitā, Indra).
haricandana | candana | mn yellow sandalwood tree myth. one of the 5 trees of paradise Svarga of Indra; cf. pañcavrksa.
Haricandra [candra] m. hist. np. of Haricandra, Jain poet, author of the Dharmaśarmābhyudaya, of unknown date.
harijana [jana] m. mod. untouchable ("people of God", mod. term due to Gandhi).
haritāla [tāla] m. yellow color of the orpiment | bio. zoo. yellow pigeon.
Haridāsa |dāsa| m. soc. "Servant of Viṣṇu", np. of the Haridāsa sect of the worshippers of Vitthala; cf. Nāmadeva.
haridīkṣita [Dīkṣita] m. hist. np. of haridīkṣita, grammarian of the 17th century; cf. hari₁.
haridrā [related to haridru] f. organic. bot. curcuma longa, turmeric (plant and powder from its rhizome). haridrācūrņa [cūrṇa] mn turmeric powder, common spice.

Haridru |dru₂| amnf tending to yellow — m. organic. bot. curcuma Aromatica, turmeric; syn. haridra | ved. n.p. of Haridru, student of Kalāpī. hāridraviṇaḥ ved. students of Kalāpī studying the text promulgated by Haridru.
haridrumat [mat] m. bed. [chu.] np. of Haridru mat, father of Hāridrumata Gautama.

haridvāra [dvāra] n. geo. np. of haridvāra "Divine Gate", mod. Hardwar, in Uttar Pradesh, on the Ganges, also called Gangādvāra; it is a place of pilgrimage, and not. of kumbhamela; it is one of the 7 sacred cities | saptapurī |.
hárināman | nāman | n. name of Hari: cf sahas ranāman.
harināmāmṛtavyākaraṇa [amṛtavyākaraṇa] n. lit. np. from harināmāmṛtavyākaraṇa "grammar of the nectar of the names of Visnu", a grammar treatise by Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī.
háripriya [priya] amnf haripriyā who loves bay horses — m. myth. epith. of Indra.
haribhaktivilāsa [bhaktivilāsa] m. lit. np. from the Ha ribhaktivilāsa "Practice of devotion to Viṣṇu", treatise on Vaishnava worship written by Sanātana₁ Gosvāmī.
háribhaṭṭa [bhaṭṭa] m. hist. n.p. of Haribhaṭṭa, name of a bd scholar. contributor to Jātakamālā.
háribhadra [bhadra] m. hist. n.p. of the Jain philosopher Haribhadra Sūri (8th century); he is the author not. Şaddarśanasamuccaya and Anekāntajayapatākā; we also owe him the Ne mināthacarita.
harimat [mat] m. myth. np. of Harimān, epith. of Indra "who possesses bay horses".
harimán |man| m. yellow color | med. form of jaundice.
hariyāṇa [yāna] n. mod. n.p. from the State of Ha riyāṇa “Viṣṇu Passage”, separated from Pañjāb in 1966, west of Delhi; its capital is Chandi garh.
harirāma [rāma] m. phil. [Nyāya] np. by harirāma Tarkālankāra, 16th century philosopher, author of Visayatāvāda.
harivamśa [vaṃśa] m. bed. n.p. from Harivaṃśa "Lineage of Hari", epic poem in 16375 stanzas [śloka], supplement [Khilaparva] of the Mah.; it tells the story of Kṛṣṇa Gopāla’s youth.
harivamśapurāṇa [purāṇa] n. bed. n.p. from the harivamśapurāṇa, a Jaina text by Jinasena describing not. the Lineage of Yādavās princes. harivarşa varşa n. myth. one of the 9 worm pools
sants [varşa] of the world.
Harivijaya [vijaya] m. lit. np. from the Harivijaya "Triumph of Hari", court epic in prākṛtī due to King Sarvasena.
harivṛṣabha |vṛṣabha| m. hist. np. of the philosopher of the harivṛṣabha language, author of a gloss |vṛtti| of the Vākyapadīya; it is probably Bhartrhari himself.
háriśamkara | śamkara | m. geo. np. of the temple of Hariśamkara, in the west of Orissa, at the foot of the Gandhamardana Mountains, an important place of pilgrimage, famous for its waterfalls.

Hariśikha [śikhā] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Hariśikha, son of Rumanvān₁, companion of Naravāhanadatta; after a fight with Mānasavega, he meets at the burial field the bhūta Tālajaṅgha₁ who reassures him; by praying to Siva he found his companions; he became chief of staff of Naravāhanadatta.

Hariścandra [ścandra] m. myth. np. of the mythical king of Ayodhyā Hariścandra "Bright as gold", son of Triśanku, 28th of the Solar Lineage [sūryavaṃśa] in the tretāyuga; he conquered all the Earth; to satisfy Viśvāmitra he renounced his kingdom, his wife, his son, his life, and was raised to heaven [svarga]; having no son from his 100 wives, on the advice of Nārada he asked Varuna for a son, promising to sacrifice him to him; but he substituted for his son Rohitāśva the young Brahmin Sunahsepa whom he had bought from his father; Narada having thus induced him to make a false promise, he was cast down from heaven to dwell in the at
mosphere [antarikṣa], in his aerial city Saubha Vyomacāripura. hariścandrasamo rājā na bhūto na bhaviṣyati A king such as Hariścandra did not exist nor will exist.
hariścandraghaṭṭa [ghaṭṭa] m. geo. np. of Hariścandraghatta, cremation place in Benares on the banks of the Ganges.
hariśmaśāru [śmaśāru] m. with a blond or red beard (said notably of Indra).
harisvāmin [svāmin] m. hist. np. of Harisvāmī, commentator of the white Yajurveda, and not. of the Satapatha brāhmaṇa; he lived at the court of Vi kramāditya.

Harihara₁ [hara] m. sg. myth. np. of Harihara₁, syncretistic god combining Vishnu and Shiva; he is abundantly depicted at Angkor | hist. np. of Harihara₁; elder brother of Bukka₁, both ministers of King Prataparudra₁; they fled to Kampilī; during its invasion in 1327 by the army of the Sultan of Delhi, they were taken prisoner, converted, and sent back there as governors; the saint Vidyāranya inspired them to revolt; they then founded the city of Vijayanagara, and Harihara₁ became its first emperor in 1336, inaugurating the Sangama dynasty; he died in 1356, and Bukka₁ succeeded him | hist. np. of Harihara₁ Rāya, Emperor of Vijayanagara (1377–1404) | hist. n.p. not. of various other kings of Vijayanagara or Angkor | of. hari₂ harau myth. Visnu and Siva.

hariharaksetra [kṣetra] n. geo. np. of Hariharaksetra, ancient Buddhist site and important place of pilgrimage at the confluence of the Gaṇḍakī and the Gaṅgā; there is the temple of hariharanātha; an important pilgrimage [melā] is held there at kārttikapūrņimā; it celebrates gajendramokṣa, victory of the elephant Gajendra over the crocodile with the help of Kṛṣṇa; it is the occasion of an important fair of cattle, camels and elephants; mod. Sonapur in Bihāra.
hariharanātha [nātha] m. geo. np. of the temple of hariharanātha at Hariharakṣetra; it is said that this is where the gajendramoksa took place.

Hariharaputra [putra] m. myth. np. of Harihara₁ putra "Son of Vishnu and Shiva", Brahmanized form of the Dravidian deity Ayyanār or Ayyappa, protector god of villages and patron of hunters, associated with his servant Karuppan; he is presented as the offspring of Shiva and Mohinī, created to destroy the demoness Mahiṣī; he is then represented as the Justiciar [Śāstā] as a rider equipped with a hook or whip, riding a tiger; he is more often represented as a slender adolescent sitting in a yoga posture, his knees held by a meditation strap; he is then the model of celibacy, and is inaccessible to women; his main temple is at Sabarimala, in central Kerala, the object of an important pilgrimage forbidden to women of menstruating age; his worshippers are dressed in black; cf. Ayonija, Revanta, Sāstā, Manikantha.
Hariharālayapura |ālayapura| n. geo. np. of the ancient Khmer capital Hariharālayapura (mod. Roluos).
haryanka [anka] m. lion emblem, symbol of the solar royal family | hist. np. of the haryanka dynasty of Magadha (5th century BC).
haryankakula [kula] amnf haryankakulā hist. prince of the haryanka dynasty; said not. of Bim bisāra.

harina [hari₂na] amnf harinī bai; tawny, reddish-brown — m. bio. deer, roe deer; gazelle, antelope; not. zoo. black antelope, black antelope (young or female); cf. eṇa — f. hariṇī lit. poetic meter of 4 feet of 17 syllables, with caesura after the 6th and 10th e.

hariṇākṣī [akṣa] f. pretty woman ["with doe-like eyes"]; said by Rādhā. vipine mṛgīm bhramantīmavalokya kuto'nudhāvasi mukunda | hariṇākṣī tava nikaṭe mādhava mā dhāva mā dhāva || Having seen a doe wandering in the forest, O mukunda, why do you pursue her? (Rādhā) with doe-like eyes is near you, O mādhava, cease running, cease running.
harinekṣaṇā [īkṣaṇa] f. pretty woman ["with gazelle eyes" |.
harít [hari₂] amnf brown, bay, fawn; yellowish, greenish — m. the pale yellow color — f. bay-colored mare | myth. not. horses of Soma, Indra, or Sūrya. saptaharitas myth. the 7 horses of Sūrya.
harinmani [mani] m. ["green jewel"] emerald.
harinmaṇimaya [maya] amnf harinmaṇimayī made of emeralds.

hárita [hari₂ta] amnf haritā brown, tawny; green, yellow — m. the color green | myth. np. of the rājarsi Harita, Son of Yuvanāśva (or of Rohitāśva or of Cyavana) | soc. gotra of his descendants, the Hāritās | lit. [K.] np. of the young ascetic Harita₁, Son of the sage Jābāli₁.
haritaśāka [śāka₁] n. green vegetable.
hari₂șeṇa m. hist. np. of hari₂șeṇa, minister and court poet of King Samudragupta (circa 350); he composed his panegyric in kāvya style which he had engraved on a pillar of Aśoka (now at Allaha bad).
harītakī f. bio. bot. Terminalia chebula, chebulic myrobalan tree; its fruit, a small astringent plum, is used for its medicinal virtues, not. to treat breath [vāyu]; cf. triphalā | this fruit.
hartṛ [agt. hṛ₁] amnf hartrī who takes away; thief. hártā manaḥ who knows how to steal the soul.
harmikā f. arch. stepped pole, at the upper part of a stūpa, equipped with a well to receive the pole of the parasol.
harmya n. palace; dwelling, house. bāhyodyānasthitaharaśiraścandrikādhautaharmyā [MD.] (Alakā) whose palaces are bathed by the moonlight from the head of Hara, Who stands in the outer gardens.
haryatá amnf haryatā desired, pleasing; precious — m. prize horse.

Haryaśva [hari₂aśva] m. Vedic. bay horse; not. horse of Indra — amnf haryaśvā Who possesses a bay horse — m. Vedic. epith. of Indra | myth. np. of Haryaśva "of the bay horse", king of Ayodhyā, son of Anaranya of the solar line |sūryavamśa|; after long penances to have a son, he married Mādhavī; their son Est Vasumanā; cf. Gālava myth. |BhP.| np. of the king Haryaśva₁ Janaka, son of Dhrstaketu₁, father of Maru.
harṣ [ca. hṛṣ] v. [10] pr. (harṣayati) pp. (harṣita) to excite, to rejoice.

harṣa [act. hṛṣ] m. horripilation (of pleasure or fear) | pleasure, happiness; joy, ardent desire; erection hist. np. of the king harşa Vardhana₁ or harşadeva, son of Prabhākara₁; after the death of his elder brother Rājya he ascended the throne at 16 years old; he reigned (606–647) in Sthāneśvara and then in Kanyākubjā (mod. Kannauj) after its annexation; he was the most powerful king of North and East India, and bore the title of emperor | parameśvara|, but was thwarted by Pulakesī₂ in the South; he protected Buddhism, patronized Nālandā and encouraged the arts; He is said to be the author of the court comedies Nāgānanda, Priyadarśikā, and Ratnāvalī₁; at his court were the poets Bāṇa₁ (who wrote his panegyric in the harşacarita), Mayūra and Divākara, and the philosopher of the language Bhartrhari; he died without an heir and his empire disintegrated | hist. np. of the king Pa ramāra harşa₁ Sīyaka; he defeated Khoṭṭiga, the last king Rāṣṭrakūṭa, in 972 and sacked his capital Mānyakheta | hist. np. of the king harṣa₂ of Kaśmīra; this iconoclast was the Nero of Kashmir; he reigned from 1089 to 1111; cf. Campaka. saharşam adv. with joy.

harṣakīrti [kīrti] m. hist. np. from the Jain scholar śvetāmbara harṣakīrti Sūri (late 16th century); he is the author of the synonym dictionary Sāradīyākhyanāmamālā. harşagiri [giri] m. geo. np. from Mount Harşagiri in Rajasthan; a temple to SivaHarṣadeva was built there in the 10th century, and destroyed by Aurangzeb in 1679. harșacarita [carita] n. lit. np. from the harșacarita "Deeds of King Harsa", a mythologico-historical prose novel by Bāna₂ Bhatta, in the ākhyāyikā style, in 8 chapters [ucchvāsa]; After a eulogy of famous poets and a manifesto of literary aesthetics, he first devotes two chapters to his own biography; after some founding myths of the dynasty, he describes the reign of Prabhākaravardhana, father of harşa, the expedition of his brother Rājyavardhana against the Huns [hūṇās], and the principal events of his reign, ending with the miraculous rescue of his sister Rājyaśrī. bānasya harsacarite niśitām udīksyaśaktim na ke'tra kavitāstramadam tyajanti [Ṣoḍḍhala] Whoever has beheld the sharpened spear of Bāṇa₁ in his harșacarita, can no longer now take pleasure in the weapons of poetry.
harsacaritavārtika [vārtika] n. lit. np. of the harşacaritavārtika, commentary on the harşacarita due to Ruyyaka (lost).

harṣajanana [janana] amnf harṣajananī med. aphrodisiac. sarvātankavināśaharsajananī vijayā [Paryāyaratnamālā] Marijuana is an aphrodisiac and makes all worries disappear. harşadeva [deva] m. hist. np. of King Harşadeva of Kannauj (7th century); he is venerated as a form of Shiva in Harşagiri; cf. Harşa. harşavardhana [Vardhana₁] m. hist. np. of King Harşavardhana "Source of Joy"; cf. Harşa.

Harṣaṇa [agt. hṛṣ] amnf harṣaṇā f. harṣaṇī That which causes joy, pleasure — m. myth. np. of Harsana "Enjoyment", one of the five arrows of Kāma | puṣpabāṇa | — act. n. joy, delight, pleasure, Enjoyment; erection; cf. śephaharṣaṇa .
harșita [pp. ca. hṛṣ] amnf harșitā excited, delighted.
harsin [agt. hṛṣ] amnf harsiṇī rejoiced; excited at the idea of, taking pleasure in (iic.).
harşula [hṛṣ] m. lover.
hal nota. gram. pratyāhāra listing all the consonants.
halanta | anta | amnf halantā phon. (word) ending in a consonant; cf. virāma.
hala mn araire; charrue; syn. lāṅgala — v. |11| pr. (halayati) to hold the plow.
Haladhara | dhara | m. myth. np. of Haladhara, epith. of Balarāma "He who holds the plow".
halabhrt [bhrt] m. myth. np. of Halabhrt, epith. of Balarāma "He who holds the plow".

Halāyudha |āyudha| m. myth. np. of Halāyudha, epith. of Balarāma "Armed with the plow" | hist. np. of Halāyudha₁, court poet of King Rāṣṭrakūṭa Kṛṣṇa₃ (10th century); his Kaviraha sya is a panegyric [praśasti] of the king also serving as a manual of the forms and meanings of the verbal roots of Sanskrit; his Brāhmaṇasarvasva is a compendium of Brahmanical practices; his Abhidhānaratnamālā is a lexicon of Sanskrit; his Mṛtasamjīvanī is a commentary on the Pingalachandahsūtra.
halā interj. (friendly address to a woman of equal rank) Dear!
halāhala mn myth. np. of the poison halāhala produced during the churning of the sea of milk [kṣīrodamathana]; Šiva drank it to save the world, and his throat turned blue [nīlakanṭha]; syn. Kālakūta.
hali [halai] m. large plow.
hali₁ iic. halin.
halipriya [priya] amnf halipriyā dear to Ba larāma — m. organic. bot. Nauclea cadamba, cf. ka damba — f. halipriya wine, alcohol.
halíkṣṇa m. kind of wild beast — mn hálīkṣṇa part of the intestine.
halin [halāin] amnf halinī SOC. labour reur; peasant | myth. epith. of Balarāma "equipped with the plow".
halimā f. myth. [Mah.] np. of halimā, one of the 7 "mothers (dangerous) to children" [śiśumātaras] associated with Skanda.
halīma m. organic. bot. Pandanus odoratissimus, pandana tree.
halīmaka |ka| m. id. | med. form of jaundice; cf. hariman.
halya [pfp. [1] hala] amnf halyā ploughed — m. ploughing, agriculture — n. ploughed field.
hava [act. hu] m. oblation, sacrifice.
havana [act. hu] n. act of offering a sacrifice — f. havanī oblation spoon. हवि: havih iic. havis.
haviḥśeṣa [śeṣa] m. SOC. remains of the sacrifice.
havir iic. havis.
havirdāna [dāna] n. SOC. offering of an oblation.

havirdhāna [dhāna] n. SOC. oblation | ved. ["receptacle of the oblation"] vehicle used to bring the soma to be pressed | hut in which its pressing takes place during the jyotistoma — m. myth. [VP.] np. of the prajāpati havirdhāna, son of An tardhāna and Dhiṣaṇā; Prācīnabarhi is his son.
havirbhuj [bhuj₃] m. ved. epith. of sacrificial fire "that consumes the oblation".
haviryajña [yajña] m. ved. solemn non-animal sacrifice offered in the fire; syn. ișți₂.
haviryajñanivāpa [nivāpa] m. SOC. scattering of the ashes of a deceased person.
haviş iic. havis.
havísmat [mat] amnf havismatī who possesses or offers an oblation.
havisyá |ya| amnf havisyā ved. adequate as the oblation; not. cereals | which deserves the oblation; epith. of not. Shiva.
havís [abstr. hu] n. SOC. ritual oblation (offering in the fire). havişki to make an offering of (acc.).
havya₁ [pfp. [1] hu] amnf havyā intended for sacrifice — n. ritual oblation; offering for sacrifice.
havya₂ [pfp. [1] hū] amnf havyā which must be invoked.

havyavah [vah₂] m. [sg. nom. havyavāt] fire ["that which bears the offerings" | myth. np. of havyavah, epith. of Agni | var. havyavāha id. talavad drśyate vyomā khadyoto havyavādiva naiva cāsti talam vyomni na khadyote hutāśanah || |Vākyapadīya| The sky is perceived as having a surface, and the firefly as having fire; yet there is no surface in the sky, nor fire in the firefly.

√ has v. [1] pr. (hasati) pr. r. (hasate) pp. (ha sita) pfp. (hāsya, hasanīya) abs. (hasya, hasitvā) pf. (ati, apa, upa, pari, pra, vi) laugh, smile | mock, ridicule, laugh at (i. acc.) | bloom (flower) — ca. (hāsayati) make laugh; make fun of (acc.).
hasa [act. has] m. laughter, smile; gaiety — f. hasā ifc. joy of (iic.).
hasat |ppr. has| amnf hasantī smiling; mocking.
hasanmukha [mukha] amnf hasanmukhī who jokes.
hasana [agt. has] amnf hasanā who laughs, who jokes — m. myth. np. of hasana "Jester", companion of Skanda — act. n. laughter; burst of laughter — f. hasanā exclamation of encouragement.
hasanīya [pfp. [2] has] amnf hasanīyā which one should mock | which one should amuse with (g.).

Hasita [pp. has] amnf hasitā who laughs | mocked — act. n. laughter, the act of laughing | (impers.) one laughed | myth. np. of Hasita "laughter", bow of Kāma | SOC. [Bharata₃] we distinguish 6 levels of laughter: smita the smile expressing joy, raising the cheekbones, without opening the mouth; hasita the broad smile, showing the teeth, but silently; vihasita the small laugh, with a sneer, the cheeks redden and the eyes crinkle; upahasita the burst of laughter, with movement of the shoulders and widening of the nostrils; apahasita the roar of laughter with tears in the eyes; and atihasita the uncontrolled hysterical laughter; the first two are suitable for well-bred people, the two in the middle are common to the people, and the last two are vulgar and reserved for people of bad reputation. hasitam bhikṣoḥ the laughter of the monk.
hasitavya [pfp. [3] has] amnf hasitavyā who must smile. devadattena hasitavyam Devadatta should smile.

hastá m. Hand; forearm; trunk (of an elephant); syn. kara₁, pāṇi | handwriting; signature; (figuratively) proof | astr. np. of Hasta "the Hand", 11th lunar asterism [nakṣatra], corresponding to the constellation of the Crow; its symbol is the (golden) Hand of Savitā, which presides over it | cubit, a measure of the length of a forearm, from the elbow to the fingertips, equal to 24 inches |angula| (approximately 45 cm); there are 4 in an arc [dhanus] Hand gesture in the theater [nāṭya]; 67 are recorded. hastīkr deliver. haste kr take in Hand; lay Hand on; marry.
hástaga |ga₁| amnf hastagā which is in its pos session.
hastagata |gata| amnf hastagatā fallen into his possession; obtained, procured. parahastagata fallen into the hands of another.
hástagamin [gamin] amnf hastagaminī in his possession; possessed; delivered. vasudhām tasya hastagāminīmakarot He delivered the Earth to him.
hastamudrā [mudrā] f. sign of the Hand | soc. sign made with the right Hand of a reciter of the Rigveda to disambiguate the padapāṭha.
hastalakṣaṇa [lakṣaṇa] n. symbolic gesture.

hastalakṣaṇadīpikā [dīpikā] f. bed. n.p. from the Hastalakṣaṇadīpikā "Light on Gestures", a Kerala text listing the 24 basic ritual gestures [mudrā], particularly for Kūṭiyāṭṭam theatre: patāka (banner), mudrākhya (seal), kataka (bracelet), musti (fist), kar tarīmukha (scissor blades), śukatuṇḍa (parrot's beak), kapitthaka (monkey tree), hamsapaksa (wild goose wing), śikhara (crest), hamsāsya (wild goose face), añjali (salutation), ardhacandra (half-moon), mukura (mirror), bhramara (bee), sūcikāmukha (point), pallava (shoot), tripatāka (triple banner), mṛgaśīrṣa (antelope head), sarpaśiras (snake head), vardhamānaka (pot), arāla (curve), ūrṇanābha (spider), mukula (bud), patāka (banner), and kaṭakāmukha (bracelet clasp).

hastalāghava [lāghava] n. manual skill, dexterity | sleight of hand, one of the 64 arts [kalā]. hastavālaprakaraņa |vālaprakaraņa| n. lit. np. of the Hastavālaprakaraņa, bd. work of Aryadeva, also called Mustiprakarana "Explanation of the closed fist".
hastābhinaya [abhinaya] m. [Abhinavabhāratī] actor's play with his hands.
hastāhasti [red. Hasta] adv. in unarmed combat.
hasti iic. hastin.
hastipá [pa₂] m. elephant driver or groom.
hastipaka | paka₂ | m. id.
hastipada | pada | n. elephant footprint.
hastivana [vana] n. elephant forest.
hastisnāna [snāna] n. elephant bath; (figuratively) non-lasting purification, like the elephant which covers itself with dust after its bath.
hastyāyurveda [āyurveda] m. lit. np. from hastyāyurveda, treatise on the veterinary science of the elephant, due to Pālakāpya Muni.

hastin [Hastain] m. bio. zoo. elephant ["having a trunk" | ; syn. dvipa, gaja, karabha | piece corr. to the bishop in chess [caturaigā] | myth. np. of King Hastī "Elephant", prince of the lunar lineage, founder of Hastināpura; Ajamīdha₁ is his son arch. the elephant, a matrix [yoni] of the āyādi system — f. hastinī elephant | [kāmaśāstra] one of the 4 types of women; cf. ratimañjarī || pkt. hāthī.
hastinā [i. hastin] iic. .

Hastināpura [pura] n. geo. np. of the city of has tināpura "founded by King Hastī", in the Ganges Valley, 90 km from modern Delhi | myth. [Mah.] capital of the lunar lineage, of the Kauravās, and not. of Dusyanta and Yudhisthira, who was crowned there after his triumphant return.
hasrá [hasra] amnf hasrā who laughs | stupid, stupid.

√ hā₁ v. [3] pr. (jahāti) pft. (jahau) aor. [1] (ahāt) aor. [3] (ajījahat) ppr. (jahat) pp. (hīna, hāta, hāna₁) pfp. (heya) abs. (hitvā) inf. (hātum) pf. (apa, pari, pra, vi) to leave, abandon, let go; to get rid of; to release, emit | to let go; to avoid; to neglect, disdain, ignore; to abstain from; to return to; to lose — ps. (hīyate) to be left, to be aban given, to be set aside; to be excluded from or deprived of (abl. i.) | to fail; to wither; to detach, to fall — ca. (hāpayati) to cause to be abandoned; to omit, to neglect — ca. r. (hāpayate) to abandon; to lose (time) — des. (jihāsati) to want to abandon or neglect; to want to escape. prāṇairahīyata he lost his life.
hā₃ interj. of sorrow or astonishment; alas! oh! hā dhik what misfortune! what shame! hā hā misfortune!
√ hā₂ [related to hā₁] v. [3] pr. r. (jihīte) aor. [4] (ahāsta) ps. (hāyate) pp. (hāna₁) abs. (hātvā) pf. (ut, vi) start; leap; give way to (dat.).
hākinī [related to śākinī] f. myth. [Tantra] female demon, harpy assistant to Durgā.
hāta [pp. hā₁] amnf hātā abandoned.
hātavat [ppa. hā₁] amnf hātavatī aban given by, deprived of (acc.).
hātavya [pfp. [3] hā₁] amnf hātavyā to abandon, to leave.
hāthī [pkt. hastin] m. elephant.
hāthīgumpha [gumpha] m. geo. "Elephant Cave", at the Jain hermitage on Udayagiri Hill₂ in Kalinga (8 km north of mod. Bhubaneśvar, Orissa); it bears an inscription of King Khāravela.

hāthīveśa [veśa] m. soc. decoration of the idols of Jagannātha and Balabhadra in elephants (resp. by black/silver and white/gold costumes), on the occasion of the ritual bathing festival [snānayātrā] at Purī during the festival of snānapūrņimā.
hāna₁ [pp. hā₁] amnf hānā gone, disappeared.
hāna₁ |pp. hā₂| amnf hānā abandoned — n. abandonment.
hāni [hāni] f. cessation.
hāyana |agt. hā₁| mn an, year |pl. hāyanās variety of rice — f. hāyanī ifc. (after num.) aged (iic.) years. dvihāyanī aged two years.
Hāyanaratna | ratna | n. lit. np. of the Hāyanaratna | "Jewel of ephemerides", a work of astronomy
PersoArabic [tājika] of Balabhadra₁ (1649).
hāyanasundara | sundara | n. astr. n.p. from the hāyanasundara treatise on Jain astrology by Padmasundara Sūri (late 16th century).
hār [ca. hṛ₁] v. [10] pr. (hārayati) pp. (hārita) to cause to be taken away, to cause to be taken; to be deprived of, to lose.

hāra₁ |agt. hṛ₁| amnf hārī ifc. who carries, who takes away, who steals; who imposes taxes | who charms, who delights — act. m. theft, confiscation — obj. m. ("that which is worn (around the neck)") necklace; not. collar of pearls (descending between the breasts); chain, garland — f. hārā f. hārī pearl | loose girl.
hāra₁ [*hari₂a] amnf hārā myth. relating to hari/Visnu.
hāramuktā [muktā] f. pl. pearls from a necklace.
hāravarṣa | varṣa | m. hist. np. of the prince | yuvarāja | hāravarṣa, epith. of Rājyapāla, son of King De vapāla; this lover of poetry was the patron of Abhinanda₁.
hārāvalī [āvalī] f. bed. n.p. of the hārāvalī, dictionary due to Puruşottamadeva.
hāraka [agt. hṛ₁] amnf hārikā who takes, who steals (iic.) | who captivates (iic.) — m. thief; cheat; cheat; rogue.
hārita₁ [pp. ca. hṛ₁] amnf hāritā taken, carried off, taken away; stolen; lost; deprived of (acc.) captivated, fascinated — m. thief | theft; fraud.
hārita₂ [*harita] amnf hāritā descendant of harita — m. pl. hāritās soc. the people of the hāritās.
hāridra [*haridrā] amnf hāridrā colored by turmeric; yellow — m. the yellow color | kadamba tree. hāridrapatākah with the yellow banner.
hāridratva [tva] n. state of being yellow.
Hāridrumata [*haridrumata] m. bed. [ChU.] np. of Hāridrumata Gautama, master [guru] of Satyakāma.
hārin [agt. hṛ₁] amnf hārinī carrying; one who brings, who carries; one who delights, who charms; ra screwing | one who takes, who carries off; one who steals, thief who wears a necklace.

hārīta [related to haritāla] m. yellow dove; syn. haritāla | hist. np. of the scholar hārīta, ancient author of a legal text [dharmasūtra], known only through quotations | lit. [K.] np. of the young Brahmin hārīta₁, who takes in the young quet dove Vaisampāyana₁ that has fallen from its nest and brings it to his father Jābāli₁ — f. Hārītī myth. np. of the yakṣī Hārītī, child-devouring ogress; later, goddess of smallpox; bd. [Gandhāra] converted to Buddhism, she protects children; she is the wife of JambhalaPāñcika, Kubera's chief general; It is said that she had 500 children by him.
hārda [*hṛda] amnf hārdā relating to the heart; coming from the heart, cordial, friendly — n. inclination, friendship; affection; love.
hārya [pfp. [1] hṛ₁] amnf hāryā to transport; to seize; that which can be stolen | to delight, captivating — m. math. dividend — f. hāryā variety of sandalwood.

Hāla [*hala] mn araire; plow — m. [haladhara] myth. epith. of Balarāma "at the char rue" | hist. n.p. of king Hāla, of the Śālivāhanās dynasty; he reigned around the 1st century in Pratișțhāna; the Sattasai collection of 700 verses in prākṛtī from the Mahārāṣṭra, taken as a model by Govardhana₁, is attributed to him; cf. Gāthāsaptaśatī — f. hālā wine (provincial).
hālika [*halaika] amnf hālikā concerning the plow — m. plowman.
hāva [act. hū] m. act of calling; flattery, banter, flirting | [nātya] feminine manifestation of seduction; 10 are listed: amorous agitation

reuse [kilakiñcita], feigned anger [kuṭṭamita], feigned indifference [bibboka], absorption in the lover's thoughts when his name is mentioned |moțțāyita|, languid behavior |lalita|, imitation of the lover [līlā], rearranging one's clothing or jewelry for erotic purposes [vicchiti], a state of amorous confusion [vibhrama], a thrill of pleasure [vilāsa], and silence imposed by modesty, |vihṛta|.
hāvaka [agt. hū] m. soc. page boy calling the bride to the wedding ceremony.
hās [ca. has] v. [10] pr. (hāsayati) to make laugh; to mock acc. .
hāsa [act. has] m. laughter; gaiety; joke; cf. aṭṭahāsa | phil. humor, a stable emotion [sthāyibhāva].
hāstika [*hastaika] amnf hāstikā concerning elephants — m. elephant driver — n. herd of elephants.
hāsya [pfp. [1] has] amnf hāsyā laughable, ridiculous; amusing, comic — n. laughable thing; amusement; laughter | lit. the comic, one of the 9 modes artis
ticks [rasa]; it is associated with the color white and the deity Shiva.
hāsyakathā [kathā₁] f. funny story.
hāsyakāra [kāra] amnf hāsyakārī that makes one laugh — m. jester, comic.
hāsyakṛt |kṛt₂| amnf jester, comic.
hāsyatā |tā| f. laughable, ridiculous condition.
hāsyatva |tva| n. id.
hāsyavyangya [vyangya] m. mod. comic satire; humor.
hāsyābhāsa |ābhāsa| mr. apparent humor.
Hāsyārṇava | arṇava | mr. bed. n.p. from Hāsyārṇava “Ocean of laughter”, farce | prahasana | by Jagadīśvara₁ Bhaṭṭācārya (14th century).

hāhā m. myth. np. of the Gandharva hāhā "Laughter", son of Kaśyapa and Pradhā; Mah. he received Arjuna when the latter visited the Devaloka | math. ten thousand billion. mahāhāhā math. one hundred thousand billion.

hi₁ part. cl. affirmative; yes, certainly, assuredly; for, indeed, precisely, in fact | (interr. imp.) therefore. tathā hi likewise, for example, that is how. na hi no, not at all, not by any means. tena hi if that is the case, agreed.
√ hi₂ [related to hā₁] v. [5] pr. (hinóti) pp. (hita₁) pf. (apa, pra) to send, to throw, to emit; to set in motion; to incite — pr. r. (hinute) to dart forth.

√ hiṃs [related to han₁] v. [7] pr. (hinásti) v. [1] pr. (himsati) aor. [5] (ahimsīt) pp. (himsita) pfp. (himsya) to harm or injure (acc.); to strike, to wound; to kill, to destroy — ca. (himsayati) to wound; to kill, to destroy — dés. (jíhiṃsiṣati) to want to wound. na himsyāt one must not harm.
himsa [agt. hims] amnf Himsā that does harm; that wounds; that kills — act. f. cf. Himsā.
hiṃsaka [agt. hiṃs] amnf hiṃsikā id. |jn. (practice) forbidden by its violence towards life— m. phil. [Netratantra] sorcerer (practicing black magic).
himsana [act. hims] m. bad action; act of wounding, killing — agt. m. enemy.

hiṃsā [f. hiṃsa] f. action of causing damage, violence; offense, nuisance, wrongdoing | damage caused; injury, murder | phil. will to injure; hatred | myth. np. of Himsā, hatred personified, wife of Krodha from whom she bore Duruktī. tyaja himsām bhaja dharmam Renounces violence, practices justice.
himsita [pp. hims] amnf himsitā injured, wronged; wounded; damaged, devastated, destroyed — n. damage.
hiṃsitavya [pfp. [3] hiṃs] amnf himsitavyā who must be hurt. daridro na kenāpi himsitavyah one must never do violence to a poor person.
hiṃsya [pfp. [1] hiṃs] amnf hiṃsyā that must be destroyed.
hiṃsra [hiṃsra] amnf hiṃsrā cruel, savage, malevolent. himsraih sahacaritānyamrgāni kānanāni |Kir.| the forests where ferocious beasts accompany peaceful animals.
√ hikk v. [1] pr. (hikkati) pr. r. (hikkate) to have the hiccups.
hikkā var. hekkā [act. hikk] f. hiccups || eng. hiccup.
hikkita [act. hikk] n. hiccup.
Hikmat iic. (import).
hikmatprakāśa [prakāśa] m. lit. np. from the Hikmat prakāśa, a medical treatise translated from Arabic by Māhadeva₂ Pandita.
hingu m. bio. bot. Assa fætida, umbellifer; a resin is extracted from the root used as a condiment and in medicine — n. bio. spice extracted from the root of Assa fætida.
hingula mn preparation of mercury and sulfur, vermilion | orange color.
hingulaka [ka] n. id.
hidimba m. myth. [Mah.] np. of the giant vampire [rākṣasa] hidimba, killed by Bhīma — f. hiḍimbā myth. his sister hiḍimbā, who bore Ghatotkaca with Bhīma.
Hidimbavadha [vadha] m. bed. n.p. from Hidimbavadha “Killing of hidimba”, episode from Mah.
Hindi f. [jaina] peregrination; journeys, adventures.
hiṇḍira m. organic. cuttlefish bone — n. grenade.
hitá₁ [pp. hi₂] amnf hitā sent, launched, emitted.

hitá₂ [pp. dhā₁] amnf hitā placed, set, arranged | suitable, advantageous; useful, appropriate to, good for (dat. g. loc.); beneficial | friendly, benevolent; that which does good — n. advantage, profit, benefit; good, useful thing; well-being. hitam (blessing) that ... be granted to (dat. g.). tasmai hitam gram. |Pāṇini| for the benefit of this (nominal base). jagaddhitāya (dat.) to the benefactor of the world. kṛṣṇāya hitaṃ bhūyāt May it be beneficial to Kṛṣṇa.
hitakara [kara₁] amnf hitakarī that helps, that benefits (g.); favorable, useful, beneficial.

Hitopadeśa | upadeśa | m. lit. np. of the Hitopadeśa "Healthy Instruction", a collection of fables for the education of princes [nītiśāstra] attributed to Nārāyaṇa₁; it is a revised version in 4 chapters of the Pañcatantra, used as a manual for teaching Sanskrit.
hitvā [abs. hā₁] ind. having abandoned, having left.
hintāla m. bio. bot. Cycas circinalis, elegant palm with a robust ringed trunk; its bark and seeds are used in medicine.
Hindī [hindu] f. the Hindī language, a nacular worm language of Sindh, evolved from the prākṛta dialects.
Hindu m. (from Persian) who lives in Sindh | mod. Hindu.
Hindusthāna [sthāna] n. geo. Hindustan, India.
hindola [related to dolā] mf hindolā ba lançoire; hamac | not. gondola for presenting the image of Kṛṣṇa during the spring festival [holākā].

Hima m. cold; cold season, winter | myth. np. of King Hima; his 16-year-old son was to die from a snake bite on the 4th day of his wedding; his wife saved him by leaving the lamps lit all night, with gold and jewels; Yama came in the form of a snake, but was dazzled by the light, charmed by the music of the princess, and left; this legend is commemorated at the festival of dhanatrayodaśī — n. snow | gr. ; lat. hiems, hibernus; fr. hiver.
himákanin [kanin] m. blizzard. himakanini kanan konatah konam eti [Bāna₂] He walks through the blizzard, back and forth, squinting his eyes.
himakara [kara₁] amnf himakarā that cools — m. the Moon "with cold rays"; opp. ahimakara the Sun | camphor.
himágarbha [garbha] amnf himagarbhā neck green with snow.
himagiri | giri | m. | "snow mountain" | a name from the Himalayas.
himádīdhiti [dīdhiti] m. "in the cold light", epith. of the Moon; opp. ahimadīdhiti the Sun.
himadhāman [dhāman] m. "of cold splendor", epith. of the Moon.
himaraśmi |raśmi| m. the Moon "with cold rays"; opp. ahimaraśmi the Sun.
himaruci [ruci] m. (poetry) the star Moon, “cold splendor”; opp. ahimaruci the Sun.

himavat [vat] amnf himavatī cold, snowy — m. | "snowy" | a name from the Himalayas | myth. | Rām. | np. of Himavān, the Himalayas personified, husband of Menā, father of Gaṅgā and UmāPārvatī. himavrști | vrști | f. snowfall.
himaśiśira [śiśira] amnf himaśiśirā glacial, cold as ice.
himásubhra [subhra] amnf himasubhra white as snow.
himālaya [ālaya] m. geo. ["abode of snows"] mountain range of the Himalayas.
himānī [himaānī] f. piles of snow.
himya [himaya] amnf himyā snowy; covered with snow.
hiraṇmaya [contr. hiraṇyamaya] amnf hiranmayī golden, gold-colored, made of gold — m. [hiranmayavarṣa] myth. one of the 9 watersheds varșa] of the world.
hiraṇya n. gold | currency, money, wealth — amnf golden hiranyā — f. hiranyā myth. n.p. from one of the 7 languages of Agni.
hiranyaka [ka] m. greed for gold | lit. [PT.] np. of hiranyaka "Greedy", king of rats; he helps Ci tragrīva and makes a friend of Laghupatanaka.

Hiranyakaśipu [kaśipu] m. myth. [BhP.] np. du dai tya Hiranyakaśipu "Golden Cushion", Asura king who, through his penances, obtained from Shiva sovereignty over the three worlds for a million years, and from Brahma the gift of invincibility, neither day nor night, neither indoors nor outdoors, neither by man nor beast; he persecuted his son Prahlāda, who worshipped Vishnu; the latter incarnated as Narasimha, the lion-man, and sprang from a pillar on the veranda of his palace at
twilight |sandhyā| to gut him; his other sons are Anuhrāda, Saṃhrāda and Hrāda; his brother is Hiraņyākṣa, his sister Siṃhikā or Holikā, his wife Kayādhu.
híranyakeśa | keśa | amnf hiranyakeśī aux che veux d'or; à la crinière d'or — m. myth. epith. de Vișnu.
hiranyakeśin |in| mr. bed. n.p. by Hiranyakeśī, author of aphorism texts [sūtra], not. the Hiranyakeśiśrautasūtra and the Hiranyakeśigrhasūtra.
hiranyagarbhá [garbha] m. myth. n.p. of Hiranyagarbha "Golden Embryo", epith. of Brahmā who generates the Universe | myth. a name of Sūrya | phil. the Spirit manifested.

Hiranyagupta₁ [gupta] m. lit. [KSS.] np. of Prince Hiranyagupta₁, "who hides his gold", son of King Yogananda; while hunting, he slept in a tree, joined by a bear being pursued by a lion; the lion ordered the bear to throw it to him; he refused, saying that he was his friend; then the lion asked the prince to throw the bear to him, which he wanted to do, but the bear cursed him to become an idiot until the day the story of his betrayal became known; Yogananda, despairing at having an idiot son, mourned Vararuci whom he thought dead; Sakațala brought Vararuci out of his hiding place, and the latter invoked Sarasvatī to tell the story and free the prince from his curse | lit. [KSS.] np. of the rich chief of the merchants Hiranyagupta₁; He abducted Sudarsana's wife, Anangaprabhā, who had come to him for help.
Hiranyanābha [nābha] m. myth. de np. Hiranyanābha, epith. of Viṣṇu "with the golden navel" | princely name.
hiranyabāhu [bāhu] amnf with golden arms — m. myth. epith. of Siva — f. geo. epith. from the Sonā River; syn. hiranyavāha.
hiranyamaya [maya] amnf hiranmayī in gold.
hiranyaretas [retas] m. myth. ["with golden sperm"] epith. not. of Agni, of Sūrya, of Siva.
hiranyavat [vat] amnf hiranvatī containing gold; made of gold.
hiranyavarman [varman] m. myth. n.p. of the king of the Daśārṇās Hiraṇyavarmā "with the golden breastplate"; his daughter was married to Sikhandī.
hiranyavāha [vāha] m. geo. epith. of the river Soṇā "that which carries gold"; syn. hiraṇyabāhu.
Hiranyahasta [hasta] amnf hiranyahastā with golden hands — m. myth. n.p. of Hiranyahasta, epith. of the divine Savitā "with golden hands".

hiranyākṣa [akṣa] m. myth. np. du dai tya Hiraṇyākṣa "Golden Eye", asura brother of Hiranyakasipu; he is said to be the eldest of the sons of Kasyapa [kaśyapasūnujyestha]; he suppressed gravity, folded the Earth to make a carpet [kaṭa] for himself, and plunged it into the primordial waters; Vișnu killed him and incarnated as Varāha, the divine Boar, to save the Earth by lifting it out of the waters.
hī interj. of surprise, horror, sorrow or joy; ah! oh!
hīná [pp. hā₁] amnf hīnā left, abandoned deficient, insufficient, mediocre without, deprived of, lacking (i. iic.) — n. lack, absence; deficiency. velāhīne before the proper time; out of season.
hīnákośa [kośa] amnf hīnakośā whose coffers are empty.
hīnája | ja | amnf hīnajā of low extraction.
hīnájāti [jāti] amnf of low class; out of caste; vile.

hīnátara |tara| amnf hīnátarā compar. worse, inferior. iṣṭāpūrtam manyamānā variṣṭham nānyacchreyo vedayante pramūḍhāḥ | nākasya prsthe te sukṛte'nubhūtvemam lokam hīnataram vā viśanti | [MO.] The fools who believe that the Vedic rites are superior cannot understand the other preferable path (of liberation); having enjoyed the blessings in the highest heavens, they return to this world or to a worse one.
hīnátva [tva] n. deprivation, the state of being deprived of.
hīnáyāna [yāna] n. bd. np. of the Hīnayāna "mediocre (way) of liberation" or "small vehicle", pejorative term for the original Theravāda doctrine by the proponents of the reformed Mahāyāna doctrine.
hīnávādin [vādin] amnf hīnavādinī who gives defective testimony; contradicts | deprived of speech; who is silent; mute.
hīnásevā | sevā | f. service of bad people; bad company.
hīyamāna [ppr. ps. hā₁] amnf hīyamānā being abandoned; deserted inferior; yielding.
Hīra m. diamond; lightning | hist. np. of Hīra, pandita at the court of King Vijayacandra; he lost a debate with Udayana₁, and trained his son Srīharṣa to avenge him.

√ hu v. [3] pr. (juhóti) pr. r. (juhuté) pft. (juhāva) aor. [4] (ahauṣīt) pp. (huta) pfp. (havya₁) pf. (ā, upa, pra) to sacrifice (to (dat.)), to pour into the fire; to offer an oblation (to dat.); to shower with offerings — ps. (hūyate) to be offered as an oblation — des. (juhūṣati) to desire to sacrifice — intens. (johavīti) to crif repeatedly | gr. ; lat. fundo; all. giessen.
√ huṇḍ v. [1] pr. r. (huṇḍate) collect, accumulate || hi. huṇḍī.
huta [pp. hu] amnf hutā sacrificed, poured in oblation | to whom an oblation is offered — n. oblation, offering.
hutabhuj |bhuj₃| m. |nom. hutabhuk| fire | myth. np. of hutabhuk, epith. of Agni "who eats the oblation".
Hutavaha | vaha | m. fire | "who carries the offerings" | myth. np. of Hutavaha, epith. of Agni "who carries the offerings (to the gods)".
hutāgni |Agni| amnf who offered an oblation to the fire — m. soc. the sacrificial fire.
Hutāśa |āśa₂| m. fire | myth. np. of Hutāśa, epith. of Agni "who eats the offering".
hutāśana [aśana₂] m. fire [“that which consumes the oblation”] | myth. np. of hutāśana, epith. of Agni “that which consumes the oblation”.
huti [act. hu] f. sacrifice.

hum interj. not. of anger, reproach, insult or question, doubt, etc. ah! | var. hūm id. | var. hum var. hūm phil. mystical syllable [bījamantra] used in certain rituals, not. of divine invocation | lit. [Rām.] (Paraśurāma) the gods having wished to arbitrate supremacy between Viṣnu and Shiva, Brahmā organized a competition between the two, armed respectively with Śāranga and Pināka; by his war cry hum, Viṣṇu para lysa all the gods and won. hum kār to let out one's anger.

huṃkāra [kāra] amnf huṃkārī [“who says hum”] in anger; said notably of Indra — m. cry of anger; trumpeting, roaring; vibration of the bow. ekahumkāranipātitanahusaprakataprabhāvasya [K.] (Agastya) whose power was revealed when he made Nahusa fall from the heavens by uttering a single hum.
humbhā [bha] f. myth. [Rām.] bellowing of anger of the abundant cow Nandinī of Vasistha; it produced armies which routed those of King Viśvāmitra who wanted to appropriate it.
hulahulī f. soc. ululations of joy of women, not. during a wedding ceremony; syn. mukhaghantā.

huhu m. [nom. huhūs] myth. np. of the great king Harva Huhu or Hūhū; he was transformed into a crocodile by the curse of Rși Devala; he attacked the elephant Gajendra and was decapitated by the discus [cakra] of Vișnu, attaining liberation; cf. Gaja
graha | var. huh id. | var. Hūhū id.

√ hū var. hve v. [1] pr. (hváyati) pr. r. (hvayate) pft. (juhāva) aor. [2] (áhvat) pp. (hūta) pf. (ā, upa, vi) to call | summon, invite; invoke | challenge — ps. (hūyate) to be called, to be summoned — ca. (hvāyáyati) to summon, to cause to be called.

hūṇa m. geo. np. Hūṇa of the Hun people; leader of the Huns | pl. hūṇās hist. the Hūṇās, Hun invaders; they plundered Gandhāra in the 5th century, then conquered the Indus basin and plundered northern India in the 6th century; they were defeated around 530.
hūta [pp. hū] amnf hūtā called, invoked; summoned.
hūti [act. hū] f. call, invocation; summons.
hūm cf. hum.
hūya [act. hū] ifc. n. invocation of iic. .
hūhū cf. huhu.

√夏 hṛ₁ [related to bhṛ] v. [1] pr. (hárati) pr. r. (ha rate) v. [3] pr. (jiharti) fut. (hariṣyati) pft. (jahāra) pft. r. (jahāre) pp. (hṛta) pfp. (hārya) inf. (har tum) pf. (ati, apa, abhi, ava, ā, ut, upa, nis, pari, pra, prati, vi, sam) to carry, bring, transport; to present | to take (with oneself), to seize; to carry off, to lift | to steal, to rob ((acc.) of (abl.)) | to plunder; to remove, to cut off (an arm, the head) — pr. r. (harate) to appropriate; to win, to conquer; to charm, to delight — ps. (hriyate) to be taken, to be seized, to be removed — ca. (hārayati) to cause to be taken, to cause to be taken; to be deprived of, to lose — des. (jihīrṣati) to want to remove. balim hr to present the offering. amāṣaṃ haramāṇam not even taking a len tille.
√ hr₂ v. [9] pr. r. (hṛṇīté) ppr. r. (hṛṇāná) ved. to be angry.
hṛcchayá |hṛdśaya| amnf hṛcchayā which stands in the heart — m. love.
hṛcchayapīḍita |pīḍita| amnf hṛcchayapīḍitā tormented by love, sick with love.
hṛcchayavardhana |vardhana| amnf hṛcchayavardhanā which awakens or increases love.
hrcchayāvista [āvista] amnf hrcchayāvistā filled with love.
hrcchayāvistacetana [cetana] amfn hṛcchayāviṣṭacetanā whose mind is filled with love.
hṛṇāná |ppr. mo. hṛ₂ | amnf hṛṇānā véd. angry.
hrt iic. hrd.
hrtkampa [kampa] m. palpitation.
hṛta |pp. hṛ₁| amnf hṛtā taken, carried; taken, seized, stolen; delighted, charmed — iic. deprived of, stripped of, who has lost.
hrd n. [except noun. acc. voc. hrdaya] heart; in breasts, chest | phil. the spiritual Heart | gr. ; lat. cor; ang. heart; fr. cœur.
hrdgata | gata | amnf hrdgatā dear, pleasant, agreeable — n. meaning, purpose, intention.
hṛdaya [hṛdya] n. heart; entrails, chest (figuratively) heart; feelings; thought, mind, intelligence — ifc. understanding of, expertise in (iic.), title of works gr. ; fr. cardiac.
hṛdayacaura | caura | amnf hṛdayacaurī | "who steals the heart" | person with whom one falls in love — n. love at first sight.
Hṛdayadarpaṇa [darpaṇa] n. lit. np. from the Hṛdayadarpaṇa "Mirror of Feelings", a treatise on aesthetics by Bhaṭṭanāyaka, now lost.
hṛdayanyāsa | nyāsa | m. soc. | Tantra | transfer of the power of a mantra into the heart by ritual gesture.
hṛdayabīja [bīja] n. phil. [Trika] (seed of the heart) epith. of the mystical syllable sauh.

hṛdayamantra [mantra] n. lit. there are several versions of the Hrdayamantra "mantra of the heart" in various devotional currents, in honor of various deities (Heruka, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, Sūrya, etc.) | bd. cf. Hṛdayasūtra.
hrdayamarman [mantra] n. sensitive heart.
hṛdayamarmabhida [bhidā] amnf hrdayamarmabhidā which breaks the heart.

hrdayasūtra [sūtra] n. bd. n.p. of the Hhrdayasūtra, mantra of the Prajñāpāramitāhṛdaya "Heart of the perfection of wisdom", ancient text of the Mahāyāna tradition. gate gate pāragate pārasamgate bodhi svāhā bd. gone, gone, gone to the other side, gone completely beyond, the spirit of the accomplished awake; so be it.
hṛdayālu [ālu] amnf who has a good heart; warm; affectionate.
hṛdayam [acc. hṛdaya] iic.
hrdayamgama [gama] amnf hrdayamgamā that touches the heart | that comes from the heart. na hṛdayaṃgamagāminī gīḥ [Abhinavagupta] There is no better messenger of the heart than speech.
hrdi [loc. hrd] iic. hrdi enām bhāratīm upadhātumarhasi learn these words by heart.
hṛdistha [stha] amnf hṛdisthā which is in the heart; dear, adored.
hṛdika [hṛdika] m. myth. np. of the yādava hrdika or Hrdīka "of the Great Heart", son of Bhoja, father of Kṛtavarmā and Sūra.
hrdya [hrdya] amnf hrdyā of the heart; central, internal | dear, pleasant, agreeable.
hrdyagandha [gandha] amnf hrdyagandhā with a pleasant scent — m. organic. Bæl tree; syn. bilva — f. hṛdyagandhā organic. jasmine; syn. cetakī.

√ hṛṣ v. [4] pr. (hṛṣyati) v. [1] pr. (hárṣati) pp. (hṛṣita, hṛṣṭa) pf. (pra, sam) to bristle (hairs), to stand up, to stiffen; to have an erection | to tremble, to quiver; to ring (with joy, with fear); to be excited or impatient; to feel sexual desire ["to tremble with joy"] to rejoice, to be joyful, to be happy; to feel pleasure — ca. (harşayati) to excite, to rejoice; to make love, to give pleasure | lat. horreo, horror; fr. horripiler, horror.
hṛṣi [act. hṛṣ] f. joy.
hṛṣivat |vat| amnf hṛṣivatī joyful, happy; who feels pleasure.
hṛṣita var. hṛṣṭa [pp. hṛṣ] amnf hṛṣitā joyful, happy, delighted | bristling; erect (hairs) | surprised, astonished.
hṛṣīka [hṛṣīka] n. sense organ.
hṛṣīkeśa |īśa| m. myth. np. of Ḥṛṣīkeśa "Master of his senses", epith. of Kṛṣṇa | geo. np. of the hermitage, then of the city of hṛṣīkeśa₁, in the upper Ganges valley.
hṛṣu |hṛṣu| amnf happy, joyful — m. fire.
hṛṣṭa |pp. hṛṣ| amnf hṛṣṭā cf. hṛṣita.
he interj. call eh! | (invocation) O (voc.).
heti mf projectile weapon, javelin.

hetú [hi₂tu] m. impulse; agent, cause, means, condition | cause of, reason for (loc. dat. g.) | phil. [Nyāya] logical cause, reason for the syllogism |pañcāvayava| | gram. the role |kāraka| of cause (agent of the causative) — ifc. caused by (2nd ed.). hetau var. hetunā, hetoh, hetave adv. because of, due to (g. 2nd ed.). mama hetoh var. maddhetoh because of me. kam hetum var. ko hetuh hence, why? kuto hetoh for what reason? yato hetoh because mrtyuhetave in order to kill. hetur alaukikah supernatural cause. karmahetu amnf caused by the acts (of past existences). māṃsahetu amnf attracted by (the smell of) meat. pañcamyantam trtīyāntam vā lingavacanam hetuh gram. |Padakṛtya| The reason is expressed by the characteristic sign declined in the ablative or instrumental case.
hetuka |ka| amnf hetukī ifc. which causes, intended for (iic.) | which has as its cause — m. cause, instrument; agent.
hetucakradamaru [cakradamaru] m. bed. n.p. from Hetucakradamaru, Dinnāga's work of logic.
hetutā |tā| f. causality; motive | phil. |Nyāya| causal dependence.
hetutva |tva| n. id.
hetúdṛṣṭi |dṛṣṭi| f. investigation of causes; skepticism.
hetubindu [bindu] n. lit. np. from the hetubindu "Pearl of Causality", a work of logic by Dharmakīrti (circa 600).
hetúmat |mat| amnf hetumatī having a cause; justified, argued; accompanied by proof | reasonable.
hetuvāda | vāda | m. argumentation; dialectic.
hetuvidyā [vidyā] f. dialectic.
hetuśāstra [śāstra] n. phil. dialectical science.
hetuhetumadbhāva [hetumatbhāva] m. phil. relation of cause and effect.
hetvābhāsa [ābhāsa] m. phil. [Nyāya] fallacious argument; logical error, inconsistency; cf. virud dha, asiddha, anaikāntika, savyabhicāra.
hema iic. heman₁.

hemakūṭa [kūṭa] m. myth. np. of the Mount of Gold hemakūṭa, mountain range delimiting the Kimpuruşavarşa; there dwell the gandharvās, the apsarasas and the kimpuruṣās | geo. Hampi hill where King Kampilideva built a temple of Shiva in 1309.

hemagarbha [garbha] m. myth. np. of hema garbha "golden embryo", epith. of Brahmā who engenders the Universe; syn. Hiranyagarbha | arch. ceremony of the golden embryo, consecrating the foundation deposit of a building.
hemaghna | ghna | m. ["destroyer of gold"] lead.

hemacandra [candra] amnf hemacandrā decorated with a golden crescent — m. hist. np. of the Jain master Hemacandrācārya or hemacandra Sūri (1089–1173); born Cāṅgaveda in Dhandhukā in Surāṣṭra of Jain merchants, he studied with the monk Devacandra, and received the initiation name Somacandra; in 1110 he received the title of Sūri and took the name hemacandra; he settled in Anahilapātaka to work at the court of the Caulukya kings; there he served King Jayasimha₄ Siddharāja, then his successor Kumārapāla; He is the author of numerous works, and received the title of Kalikālasarvajña "Omniscient of the Kali era"; he is notably credited with the Kāvyānuśāsana, a work of poetics in condensed formulas [sūtra], glossed by his commentaries Alamkāracūdāmaņi and Viveka₁; his Siddhahemaśabdānuśāsana is a synthesis of the Sanskrit grammars existing at the time; he is credited with four lexicons: the Abhidhānacintāmaņi (synonyms), the Anekārthasamgraha (homonyms), the Nighanțuśeșa (botanical terms) and the Deśīnāmālā (barbarisms and neologisms); He is also the author of the encyclopedia of meters Chandonuśāsana and the grammatical appendices Uṇādigaṇasūtra and Liṅgānuśāsana; finally, at the request of King Kumārapāla, he composed the Trișașțiśalākāpurușacaritra "Lives of the 63 illustrious persons (of Jainism)", which was followed by the Pariśiṣṭaparva or Sthāviravalī "Lives of the patriarchs" | myth. [Rām.] np. of King Hemacandra₁, son of Viśāla, father of Sucandra.
hemacandrācārya [ācārya] m. hist. n.p. of hema candrācārya; cf. Hemacandra.

hemaprabha [prabhā₂] m. bed. [KSS.] np. of prince vidyādhara hemaprabha, king of Kāncanaśrnga, devotee of Siva; of his wife Alamkāraprabhā na leaves his daughter Ratnaprabhā | bed. [KSS.] np. of the vidyādharī Hemaprabhā, mother of Sphatikayaśā.
hemamrga [mrga] m. myth. [Rām.] golden deer, into which Mārīca metamorphosed to attract Rāma; syn. māyāmrga, kanakamrga.
hemalamba [lamba] m. astr. n.p. of hemalamba, personifying year 31 of a life cycle [saṃvatsara].

hemānga | anga₁ | amnf hemānga f. hemāngī with golden limbs; formed of gold — m. bio. bot. Mi chelia champaka, shrub with bright yellow flowers; cf. campaka | myth. np. d'hemānga "Golden Mountain", epith. of Meru | epith. of various gods.
hemāngada | angada | mr. myth. n.p. from gandharva hemāngada "wearing a golden bracelet" | bed. region north of the Vindhya Mts.

hemādri [adri] m. myth. np. of hemādri, epith. of Mount Meru "Golden Mountain" | hist. np. of the scholar hemādri₁ Paṇḍita, prime minister of Kings Māhadeva₁ then Rāmacandra₁ in Devagiri (13th century); he was a diplomat, architect, poet, physician and theologian; he is credited with numerous encyclopedic works, notably the treatise Caturvar gacintāmaņi; he protected artists and scholars, such as Vopadeva.

Heman₁ [related to hiraṇya] n. gold (refined); gold coin; gold object — f. hemā myth. np. of the apsaras hemā "golden", wife of Maya; their sons are Māyāvī and Dundubhi; they adopted Mandodarī as their daughter — m. hema weight of gold; syn. māṣaka.
Heman₂ [hima] adv. in winter.
hemanta [hima] m. winter season [rtu] (month of mārgaśīrṣa and pauṣa).
hemantapathika | pathika | mr. cf. śiśirapathika.
hemantasena [sena] m. hist. np. of King Heman tasena, who seceded from the Pala Empire in 1095 to found the Sena dynasty in Bengal; his son Vijayasena succeeded him in 1096.

heya [pfp. [1] hā₁] amnf heyā that which must be avoided | to be left, to be rejected, that which must be gotten rid of, that which must go away. heyam duḥkham anāgatam Misfortune must be avoided before it happens.
hayamedha | medha | mr. cf. aśvamedha.
heramba m. myth. np. of heramba, form of Ganesa from Nepal, represented with 5 heads, riding a lion.
herambanarasimhanyāya | narasimhanyāya | m. lit. maxim of heramba and narasimha; it evokes two contrary notions united in the same creature.
Herika M., spy.
helā f. play; mockery, ridicule; contempt | frivolity; ease. trnahelayā adv. as if by chance; (easy) as a child's game.
Helārāja [rāja] m. hist. np. of the grammarian Helārāja of the 10th century; we owe him the commentary Prakīrņaprakāśa of the Vākyapadīya.

Hevajra [heVajra] m. bd. [Tantra] np. of hevajra "O Diamond", a fierce deity with 8 heads, 4 legs, and 16 arms; he wears a necklace of strung heads; he dances, sometimes entwined with his consort Prajñānairātmyā; he utters the mantra hūm; he represents Awakening here and now; cf. Vajra sattva — n. cf. hevajratantra
hevajratantra [Tantra] n. lit. np. of the hevajratantra, work of the esoteric bd. Vajrayāna, originating from East India (8th-9th century).
hehaya [hehaya] m. myth. np. of the king hehaya "O horse", epith. of Ekavīra born of a horse; cf. Haihaya.
hai interj. of call or vociferation: eh!
haituka [*hetuka] amnf haitukī motivated, caused — ifc. caused by, dependent on (iic.) — m. reasoner, rationalist; skeptic, heretic; syn. tārkika.
haima₁ [*hima] amnf haimā snowy; icy; misty, cold — n. frost.

haima₁ [*Heman₁] amnf haimī in gold; gilded; of golden yellow color — m. myth. np. of haima₁, epith. of Shiva "Golden" — f. haimā₂ bio. yellow jasmine — f. haimī id. | bio. flower of the bot. Pandanus odora tissimus; syn. ketakī. haimībhū to become gold, to turn into gold.
haimalingānuśāsana | anuśāsana | gram. n. Lingānuśāsana of Hemacandra.
haimaná [haima₁na] amnf winter haimanī | epith. of the month mārgašīrṣa (November December).
haimavatá [*himavata] amnf haimavatī from the Himālaya; snowy — f. haimavatī myth. n.p. of haimavatī, patr. of Pārvatī “daughter of Himavān”.
haiyaṃgavīna [*hyasgo] n. [“made from yesterday’s milk”] fresh butter.

Haihaya m. myth. np. of King Haihaya or He haya; cf. Ekavīra | pl. myth. name of the Hai hayās people, descendants of Yadu through Ekavīra; they were rival conquerors of the śakās; they were divided into 5 tribes: Tālajaighās, Vītihotrās, Avantyās, Tuṇḍikerās, and Jātās; they drove Bāhu out of his kingdom; his son Sagara reconquered it with the help of Aurva; cf. Kārtavīrya, Mahismatī.
ho interj. of appeal, challenge or surprise; oh!
hotā [nom. hotr] iic.
hotāpotr | potr | m. du. hotāpotarau ved. the two priests hotr and potr.
hotāpotānestodgātr [nestodgātr] pl. m. hotāpotānestodgātārah ved. the four priests of sacrifice.

hotṛ [agt. hu] amnf soc. who sacrifices, his criifiant — m. ved. function of the priest who recites the hymns of the Rigveda prescribed for a sacrifice; he is the first of the 7 priests of the solemn rites, before the potr, the nestr, the agnīdh, the adhvaryu, the praśāstr and the brahman; he has three assistants: the maitrāvaruņa, the achāvāka and the grāvastut.
hotrpotrnestodgātāra | potrnestrudgātr| m. pl. hotrpotrnestodgātārah ved. the four priests of sacrifice.
hotra [instr. hu] n. soc. offering to the fire, liba tion, sacrifice; ved. rite of the yajña performed by the hotr.

Hotravāhana | vāhana | m. myth. | Mah. | np. du rși Hotravāhana "who carries the offering"; his daughter is the wife of the king of Kāśi; he came to the hermitage where Ambā had taken refuge after her repudiation, and advised her to ask Parasurāma to avenge her by killing Bhīsma.
hóma [huma] m. soc. ved. oblation to the fire, his crucifixion; not. oblation in the fire āhavanīya.
homadhenu | dhenu | f. cow (that provides the milk) of the offering.
Hoy iic. (import).

hoysala [sala] m. hist. np. of the Hoy sala dynasty "sala strikes (the Cola lion)" of Karnaka; they formed a great empire in the 13th century; their capital was Belur, then Halebidu; cf. Vișnuvardhana.
horā f. hour; horoscope, zodiac sign | gr. ωρα; lat. hora; ang. hour; fr. heure.
horāśāstra [śāstra] n. bed. n.p. from the horāśāstra, or astronomy work of Bhattotpala (10th century).

holākā var. holī f. soc. festival of holī, dedicated to Kṛṣṇa, at the full moon phālgunī; also called phālgunotsava; the spring harvest is celebrated with a carnival where social transgressions are tolerated, and where colored powders and pastes are thrown (cf. raṅgapañcamī, madanamahotsava); in the evening bonfires are lit to celebrate the defeat of Holikā.

Holikā f. cf. holākā | myth. np. of the rākṣasī Holikā, sister of Hiraṇyakaśipu; she obtained from Brahmā the power to be insensitive to fire; she tried to use it to burn her nephew Prahlāda by taking him on a pyre, but it was she who burned there, because Brahmā forbids using his powers to harm a bhakta || hi. holī.

holikādahana [dahana] m. myth. destruction by fire of the witch Holikā | soc. her annual commemoration, on the evening of phālgunī ; her straw effigy is burned there, as a prelude to the festival of holākā.
holī cf. holākā.
hautra [*hotṛa] amnf hautrā soc. relating to the priest hotr; sacerdotal — m. soc. function of the hotr.
hauterika |ika| amnfhautrikā id.
√長 hnu v. [2] pr. r. (hnuted) pp. (hnuta) pf. (apa) to hide; hide from (dat.).
hnutá [pp. hnu] amnf hnutā concealed, hidden.
hyas adv. yesterday | lat. herī; fr. yesterday; eng. yester day.
hyaskṛta |kṛta| amnf hyaskṛtā done yesterday.
hyastana |tana| amnf hyastanī of yesterday; which happened yesterday — f. hyastanī gram. imperfect tense; cf. lan.
hyastanadina | dina | n. yesterday.
hrada [related to hlād] m. body of water, pond, lake.
hradagraha | graha | mr. organic. crocodile.
√ hras v. [1] pr. (hrasati) pft. (jahrāsa) pp. (hrasita) to decrease, diminish, lessen — ca. (hrāsayati) to make decrease, shorten.
hrásiṣṭha [super. hrasva] amnf hrasiṣṭhā the shortest, the smallest; very short, very small.
hrásīyas [compar. hrasva] amnf hrasīyasī shorter, smaller; very short, very pe tit.
hrasvá [hrasva] amnf hrasvā short, pe tit, shortened; brief, low | phon. (phoneme) brief; opp. dīrgha | insignificant — m. dwarf | bad person. hrasvam adv. very near, close by.
hrasvatā |tā| f. the state of being small.
hrasvatva [tva] n. id.
hrasvapañcamūla [pañcamūla] n. med. the 5 minor medicinal roots: śālaparņī, pṛśni parņī, kaṇṭakārī, bṛhatī and gokṣura; opp. bṛhat pañcamūla; cf. daśamūla.
hrasvaroman [roman] m. myth. [BhP.] np. of King Hrasvaromā "with short hair", son of Svarnaromā, father of Janakarāja and Kuśadhvaja₁.
hrād v. [1] pr. r. (hrādate) pp. (hrādita) pf. (nis, sam) to make noise; to resound (drum); tam to thump, to thunder — ca. (hrādayati) to make noise.
Hrāda |act. hrād| m. noise, tumult; rumble (thunder) | phon. sound | myth. np. of Hrāda "Thunderer", son of Hiranyakaśipu.
hrādin [agt. hrād] amnf hrādinī noisy, deafening — f. hrādinī thunder.
hrādúni [hrād] f. hail, hailstone || lat. grando.
hrām leaves. phil. [Tantra] bijamantra.
hrās [ca. hras] v. [10] pr. (hrāsayati) to make di minuer, to shorten.
√ hrāsin [agt. ca. hras] amnf hrāsinī which makes decrease, which shortens.
√ Hrī₁ v. [3] pr. (jihréti) pp. (hrīta, hrīṇa) to be ashamed, to be ashamed (of (abl.)) | to be modest, to be timid — ca. (hrepayati) to shame.
Hrī₂ [act. Hrī₁] f. shame; modesty; modesty; timidity | myth. np. of Hrī "Prude", daughter of Dakṣa, wife of Dharma.
hrīmat [mat] amnf hrīmatī who feels shame, ashamed | shy, modest.
hrīkā [act. Hrī₁] f. timidity, modesty; modesty | hlīkā id.
hrīṇa [pp. Hrī₁] amnf hrīṇā modest, ti mide, chaste | ashamed.
hrīṇamukha [mukha] amnf hrīṇamukhī who has red cheeks; with a face filled with shame.
hrīta [pp. Hrī₁] amnf hrītā modest, timid, modest; ashamed.
hrīm part. phil. [Tantra] sound of the māyābīja, bījamantra of evocation of Durgā.
hrūm leaves. phil. [Tantra] bijamantra.
hrep [ca. Hrī₁] v. [10] pr. (hrepayati) to shame.
hrepaṇīya [pfp. [2] hrep] amnf hrepaṇīyā capable of causing shame, of which one should be ashamed.
hraim leaves. phil. [Tantra] bijamantra.
hraum leaves. phil. [Tantra] bijamantra.

√ hlād v. [1] pr. r. (hlādate) pp. (hlādita) pf. (ā, pra) to rejoice, to be joyful | to cool down, to refresh — ca. (hlādayati) to rejoice, to amuse, to enchant | to cool down, to refresh | ang. glad.
hlāda [act. hlād] m. fun, joy.
hlādaka [agt. hlād] amnf hlādikā ra refreshing; pleasant.
hlādikāvat |vat| amnf hlādikāvatī which cools well.
hlādana |act. hlāda| n. refreshment; well-being, joy.
hlādayat [ppr. That. hlād] amnf hlādayantī refreshing.
hlādi iic. hlādin.
hlāditva |tva| n. joy.
hlādita [pp. hlād] amnf hlāditā fresh; rejoiced, joyful.
hlādin [agt. hlād] amnf Hlādinī who rejoices, distracts, amuses — f. Hlādinī myth. np. of Hlādinī, epith. of Rādhā "who rejoices".
hvaraka [agt. hvr] amnf hvarikā who goes astray; deviant; renegade.
√ hval v. [1] pr. (hvalati) pr. r. (hvalate) pp. (hvalita) pf. (vi) to walk crookedly; to stagger, to faint; to fail — ca. (hvālayati) ca. (hvalayati) to cause to stagger.
hvala [agt. hval] amnf hvālā who stumbles; who staggers.
hvalana [act. hval] n. wavering; the act of stumbling, of fainting.
hvāy [ca. hū] v. [10] pr. (hvāyáyati) to summon, to call.
hvāya |agt. hū| ifc. amnf hvāyī who calls, who invokes (iic.). svargáhvāyaḥ mf svargahvāyī who invokes Heaven.
√夏 hvṛ [related to hval] v. [1] pr. (hvárati) to deviate from the right path; to go astray — ca. (hvārayati) to cause to deviate from the right path, to pervert.

√ ad₁ v. [2] pr. (átti) fut. (atsyáti) inf. (áttum) pfp. (attavya) pf. (vi) to eat, consume; devour — ps. (adyate) to be eaten — ca. (ādayati) to nourish | gr. ; lat. edo; ang. to eat; all. essen. ad₂ [agt. ad₁] ifc. amnf who eats (iic.). matsyāt who eats fish. āmāt who eats raw food. sasyāt who eats grains. kravyāt who eats meat.

√ an₂ v. [2] pr. (ániti) fut. (anisyáti) pp. (anita) pf. (pra, vi) to breathe, to blow, to exhale | to live, to be alive; to move — ca. (ānayati) to give life; to animate — des. (aninisati) to want to breathe; to want to live | gr. ανεμος; lat. anima; fr. soul, animal. ana cf. ayam. ana form of verbal nouns of action n. and a. sometimes having the value of agent; cf. yuc.

√ as₁ v. [5] pr. r. (asnute) pp. (asta) pf. (abhi, ā, upa, sam) to reach, arrive at, attain (acc.) | to obtain, acquire, gain; to feel; to enjoy | to permeate, penetrate, fill — des. r. (asisisate) to wish to obtain — intens. r. (aśāśyate) to obtain much or often. vidyayā'mṛtamaśnute through knowledge one gains immortality (motto of the Hindu University of Benares).

√ as₂ v. [9] pr. (asnāti) pr. r. (asnīte) pft. (āsa) pp. (aśitá) abs. (aśitvā, áśya) pf. (pra) to eat, devour; to taste, enjoy | to destroy, lose — ca. (āśayati) pp. (āśita) to feed, to make someone eat — intens. r. (aśāśyate) to eat incessantly | lat. esca.

√ in [related to i] v. [5] pr. (inóti) ved. to lead; to force. ^72 in var. vin, min like, similar to, which is (form of the a.) | which does like (form of the agt. ifc.) which has, which possesses (sf. possessive, form of the a.) which makes the vow of | which is in the habit of doing (iic.) | which does repeatedly.

√ is v. [6] pr. (iccháti) pr. r. (icchate) pft. (iyeṣa) fut. (eṣiṣyáti) aor. [5] (aiṣīt) pp. (iṣṭa₁) inf. (eṣṭum) abs. (iṣya) pfp. (eṣṭavya) pf. (adhi, anu, abhi) to desire, want, wish (inf.) — v. [1] pr. r. (eṣate) (av. adhi) to seek — v. [4] pr. (iṣyati) (av. anu) to seek — ps. (isyate) to be desired, to be prescribed, to be approved | to be recognized; to pass for — ca. (eṣayati) pp. (eṣṭa) to cause to be desired. etadicchāmyaham śrotum I would like to hear that. yathecchasi tathā kuru [BhG.] Do what you wish. gantum icchāmi tatra aham yatra me bhrātarah

(pari, pra) send, throw, pour; impul ser, incite, animate | dispatch; discharge; announce, proclaim — ca. (iṣayati) cf. pres. is₃ [agt. is₁] ifc. amnf who seeks, who desires (iic.).

√ nr v. [2] pr. r. (nrte) pp. (nrna) pf. (ā, ut, pra, sam) to go, to advance, to move, to rise — ca. (īráyati) pp. (īritá) to provoke, to engender; to raise (voice) | to resound, to announce, to proclaim — ca. r. ( īráyate ) to rise — ps. ( īryate ) to be called | lat. ira; fr. irascible.

√ rc₁ v. [1] pr. (arcati) fut. (arcisyati) pft. (ānarca) aor. [5] (ārcīt) pp. (arcita) pfp. (arcya, ar canīya) abs. (arcitvā, arcya) pf. (abhi) ved. to shine l to praise, venerate, honor — ca. (arcayati) opt. (ar cayet) to make shine; to honor — dés. (arcicisati) to want to honor. nādevo devam arcayet no one but God should worship God. nārudrastu spṛśedrudram nārudro rudram arcayet [Lingapurāna] no one but Rudra should undulate Rudra, no one but Rudra should worship Rudra. rc₂ [agt. rc₁] f. sacred verse, stanza or verse of the Rigveda | pl. rcas the stanzas (of the Rigveda).

√ zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz zzzzzzzzz (kuñcita) pf. (sat) to contract, to tighten; curl — ca. (kuñcayati) to bend; frown. কুষ্মক kuñcaka [agt. kuñc] amnf kuñcikā which curves — f. kuñcikā key | bed. n.p. of the kuñcikā, commentary on the Vaiyākaraņasiddhāntamañjūṣā due to Durbalācārya.
√ to chirp, cackle; to hum; to warble, coo; to sing (bird) | to grunt, moan; to murmur. কুজ kūja [act. kūj] m. chirping, cooing | gurgling; murmur.

√ kr v. [6] pr. (kiráti) pr. r. (kirate) pft. (cakāra) pft. r. (cakare) pp. (kīrṇa) pf. (ati, anu, apa, ava, ā, ut, upa, pra, prati, vi, sam) to throw, to cast, to spread, to water; to scatter, to scatter; to strew, to cover with (i.); to fill — ps. (kīryate) to be spread, to be scattered.

√ khād v. |1| pr. (khādati) pft. (cakāda) fut. r. (kādisyate) pp. (khādita) to bite, chew; to feed on; to eat, devour. khāda khādeti khādati eat! eat! he said to himself while eating (he stuffed himself).
√ to take place; to be found; to reach, to fall to, to hang from loc. .

(abhi, ava, ā, ut, upa, nis, parā, vi, sam) conquer, conquer win at the game, beat var. jināti to surpass, to undermine; cf. jyā₁ — imp. (jaya) victory at (noun.) — ca. (jāpayati) ps. (jāpyate) to defeat — dice. (jigīṣati) dice. r.
